Dawn.t: The Dawnish assembly sent Ser Ancél Watcher with troubadours and questing knights to track down Druj miasma pillars in Ossium, and condemned the use of cruel armies. It also honoured the houses that raised the Gates of Adamant and called House Minos nobles to inquisition over aiding Asaveans against rebelling slaves.

Druj.t: An enacted Dawnish mandate set questing knights hunting the Druj miasma pillars in Ossium. Mandates from Highguard and Urizen found homes for Urizeni refugees displaced by the Druj.

Grendel.t: After the Imperial raid on Dubhtraig, the Synod moved to help the slaves freed there reach the Empire. It also thanked the Asaveans at Feroz for protecting Freeborn citizens from the Grendel.

Highguard.t: Highborn priests stood at the centre of the Grey Pilgrims controversy, and Sister Lilith of the Chantry was called to inquisition. The Highborn assembly enacted a mandate offering Urizeni refugees sanctuary in Reikos and urged its commanders to liberate Tamarbode from the Eternal Llofir.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs enacted a mandate rewarding those who bring freed Dubhtraig orcs home to Skarsind, at a cost to the nation's production. Their assembly also urged engagement with the Sand Fishers and praised the Coven of Crows.

Jotun.t: Wintermark's assembly declared that becoming a Jotun thrall is not heroic, urged that thralls be spared so they could come home, and lamented the Jotun occupation of Sermersuaq. The Marches urged Mournwold orcs who were formerly Jotun thralls to become Marcher citizens.

Navarr.t: The Navarr assembly rejected the Grey Pilgrims' critique of national faith and called for a new army to strike at the vallorn. The General Assembly urged action in Liathaven and Brocéliande and recognised Seren in Miaren as a city of worth.

The League.t: The League assembly narrowly called for Imperial Bourse seats in League territory to become national seats again, and invited study of the Giselle frogs of Sarvos. A mandate consecrated the Colossus of Sarvos to Pride, and the Senator for Temeschwar was called to inquisition over the Oktístis idols.

The Marches.t: An enacted Marcher mandate lets any Imperial army billet in Marcher territory with access to the Imperial Breadbasket. The assembly also invited Mournwold orcs to become Marchers, urged folk to shun the Grey Pilgrims and vindicated Will Talbot, General of the Drakes.

Urizen.t: Refugees from Zenith are to settle in Redoubt and Morrow under an enacted Urizeni mandate, while Highguard offered others sanctuary in Reikos. The Synod also funded a School of War honouring Morrow's defenders and vindicated Tolamy for saving the injured at Atheneum Spire.

Varushka.t: Varushka enacted a mandate urging its people towards the riches of mines and forests, and welcomed the Ketsov and others in Ossium as Varushkans. It named Father Drakov Tender of the Hearth and recognised Zoria's original shrine in the Vale of Gniejezdo.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's assembly cautioned against narrowing Heroism to Steinr 'honour' and called Krampus subservience idolatry. It also encouraged pilgrimage to Isenbrad's tomb in Runegrott and appointed Ursa Hendel Hearth Crow Keeper of the Rest.

383YE Spring Equinox Synod judgements.o: At the Spring Equinox 383YE summit the Imperial Synod raised 126 judgements, agreeing to pause recognitions and doctrinal changes while differences with Sumaah are resolved. It also enacted mandates ranging from removing Almodin Oktístis's idols to sheltering Urizeni refugees, amid bitter debate over the Grey Pilgrims.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind is the intended new home of the slaves freed from Dubhtraig, and an enacted mandate rewards those who guide them there. Preachers from Skarsind were urged to travel with the Great Forest orcs to aid the liberated.

383YE Spring Equinox winds of fortune.d: Navarr defenders, aided by Dawn, Highguard, forest orcs and Tharim, struggled to hold Elerael and Boar's Dell against the vallorn. Ossium joined Varushka but faced unresolved threats. Urizen thanked its allies and weighed what to do with those rescued from Zenith. The Druj threatened to slaughter yeofolk children in Dawnguard if the Empire kept invading the Mallum. Refugees from Dubhtraig were stranded across the Empire. Grendel pirates of Attar raided shipping. Wardens smashed Janon's statue in Temeschwar. Further entries covered the Liberty Pact sanctions, Sarcophan trade proposals, a Wintermark rune forge proposal and orc diplomacy. Sixteen Synod mandates were upheld, and Frederick di Sarvos faced inquisition.

Dawn.t: Dawn faced a Druj threat to slaughter the yeofolk children held in Dawnguard, with a possible rescue foray into the Barrens. Its national assembly also sent Ranae de Rondell with liao to rally knights and witches to Brocéliande, and Weirwater suffered a subtle curse.

Druj.t: The Druj issued an ultimatum to kill the Dawnish prisoners in Dawnguard if the Empire continued invading the Mallum. They still held Zenith and were pressing into Spiral.

Grendel.t: The Grendel armada was focused on invading Feroz while Attar pirates raided Imperial shipping. Enraged by Imperial raids, the Salt Lords reportedly offered bounties on Imperial vessels, perhaps overreaching enough to give the Empire an opening in the Bay.

Highguard.t: Highguard was thanked by Urizen for its aid and its congregations were urged to help defend Brocéliande. Several Highborn mandates shaped the grey pilgrimage, while its citizens were urged to withhold white granite from the Bourse auction until the Cinderpath Exchange is built.

Imperial Orcs.t: Some two thousand slaves freed from Dubhtraig were offered homes in Skarsind among the Imperial Orcs, but were stranded across the Empire after a harsh winter. Skywise Tulva's mandate urged them to settle there and in time become Imperial Orcs.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the Empire's orc neighbours, alongside a reference to former Jotun thralls and some details about Jotun-held Liathaven.

Navarr.t: The Navarr faced an ever-stronger vallorn assault on their liberated lands in Brocéliande, with allies rallying and Tharim and the General of Day offering further help. Grey pilgrims walking the trods also aided the Navarr's great quest.

The Brass Coast.t: Feroz faced a Grendel invasion and Brass Coast merchant shipping was threatened by Attar pirates. The nation was also tied to Sarcophan trade proposals and to the Cinderpath developments.

The League.t: Urizen urged its people to thank League generals. Sarcophan families proposed a trading enclave in Sarvos, wardens destroyed the idolatrous statue of Janon in Temeschwar, and ships from Tassato and Sarvos faced pirate raids.

The Marches.t: Marchers worked out practical ways for farms to billet and feed armies, Marcher or not, if the Synod approved. The Landskeepers also showed their support for keeping Rivers Run Red under interdiction.

Thule.t: Relations with the Thule of Otkodov suffered a sudden frost. Otkodov was also among the slaving nations placed under sanctions by the Liberty Pact.

Urizen.t: Urizen's National Assembly thanked Varushka, Highguard and the League and controversially welcomed would-be Urizen, even orcs. The nation must also decide whether those rescued from Zenith should wait to return or resettle, depending on whether it consolidates Morrow or tries to retake Zenith.

Varushka.t: Varushka absorbed Ossium, becoming the largest Imperial nation, and was presented with prosperity opportunities. Belakov, the Wolf of Karsk, was sent to examine the freed slaves of Ossium, and a Sarcophan enclave was proposed in Karsk.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark had the chance to build a new rune forge to reclaim the runesmiths' lost prestige, and the hylje offered gifts including crystal mana. Severi Jarlmarison's mandate let Winterfolk turn congregations into military units.

383YE Spring Equinox winds of fortune.o: The Spring Equinox 383YE Winds of Fortune gathered the season's news for the Empire. Headlines included the vallorn's mounting assault on Brocéliande, Ossium's absorption into Varushka, a Druj ultimatum over the children held in Dawnguard, the plight of refugees freed from Dubhtraig and many trade, faith and foreign opportunities.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Navarr defenders and their allies continued to hold Boar's Dell against the vallorn's strengthening assault.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Elerael remained on the front line as the vallorn brought ever more power against its Navarr defenders.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dawn mandate reminded the people of Semmerholm and Astolat of the Navarr's sacrifices against the vallorn.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Jorma Steelhail's mandate urged that Bastion and the Sumaah city of Timoj be seen as equals in the Way.

Bay of Catazar.t: Attar pirates kept raiding Imperial shipping in the Bay and the Salt Lords claimed mastery of it. Their overconfidence may have given the Empire an opportunity to dominate the Bay.

Brocéliande.t: The vallorn threw more and more of its power against the Navarr-liberated lands of Brocéliande. Dawn, Highguard, forest orcs and Tharim aided the defence, and Synod mandates rallied further support.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel armada was noted to be focused on its invasion of Feroz.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: some details about Hercynia were given alongside the Brocéliande news.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's guilds, free companies and Holberg itself were tagged as interested in trade opportunities and the Ossium situation.

Karsk.t: Sarcophan families proposed turning a ruined location in Karsk into a large trading enclave, and the Wolf of Karsk was charged with vetting the freed slaves of Ossium.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: some details about Liathaven were given alongside the Brocéliande news.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: a recent Imperial raid on Mareave was among those that enraged the Salt Lords.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's recent gains in restoring Morrow were one option it might choose to consolidate.

Ossium.t: Newly conquered Ossium became part of Varushka, with settlers arriving and the egregore finding new citizens. The Ketsov, the Sand Fishers, the Crawling Depths and a miasma of terror remained unresolved.

Otkodov.t: Imperial relations with the Thule of Otkodov frosted over and the territory was placed under Liberty Pact sanctions. Otkodov is also where Wintermark's captured runesmiths were taken long ago.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: residents of Reikos were tagged as concerned by the season's Winds of Magic.

Sarvos.t: Sarcophan families proposed turning a ruined location in Sarvos into a large trading enclave, and merchant ships out of Sarvos faced Grendel pirate raids.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dawn mandate reminded the people of Semmerholm and Astolat of the Navarr's sacrifices against the vallorn.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind was offered as a home for slaves freed from Dubhtraig, and Skywise Tulva's mandate urged them to settle there, though many were stranded across the Empire.

Spiral.t: Spiral remained a grim, contested land facing a Druj advance. Urizen had to choose whether to blunt that advance or commit to retaking Zenith.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: merchant vessels from Tassato were listed among those threatened by Attar pirates.

Temeschwar.t: Inspired by the Cardinal of Pride's condemnation of idolatry, a warden fellowship reduced Temeschwar's statue of Janon to rubble.

Weirwater.t: A subtle curse fell on the Dawnish folk of Weirwater, as covered in the Winds of Magic.

Zenith.t: Imperial heroes rescued more than half of the Urizen imprisoned by the Druj in Zenith, which remained under Druj control as Urizen weighed an attempt to retake it.

383YE Spring Equinox winds of war.d: Freed slaves left for Skarsind, and the Broken Shore orcs cannot raise an army in Mareave for a year. Morrow was retaken without casualties, and the Citadel Guard stopped declining. Raiders rescued two-thirds of Zenith's captives. Dawn, Varushka and five Thule armies took Nearweald and the Drownbark Forest. Navarr, aided by Dawn, Highguard and Tharim, held the vallorn in Brocéliande. The Quiet Step and Strong Reeds blunted the Lasambrian Jotun in Segura. Imperial armies took the Ford of Berusen and reached four-tenths of Stark, where the Jotun finished the Tusks of the Lion. The Druj took Ossuary, Screed and the Legacy. Four Sentinel Gate conjunctions were identified.

Dawn.t: Dawnish soldiers stormed Beoraidh's garrison towers, and four Dawnish armies completed the conquest of Ossium alongside the Thule without the aid of the Fields of Glory. Questing knights helped hold the vallorn in Brocéliande, and Dawnish warbands freed captured Highborn soldiers in Zenith.

Druj.t: The Druj abandoned Morrow and were driven entirely out of Ossium, losing Orieb. In return they poured some thirty thousand orcs into Spiral, seizing Ossuary, Screed and the Legacy and nearly retaking Apulus, while keeping their grip on Zenith.

Grendel.t: The Grendel lost their half-built Beoraidh fortress and their coliseum, and cannot raise an army in Mareave for a year. Their armada, however, conquered the Cazar Straits and Oranseri, captured Bramar, looted widely and enslaved Freeborn citizens.

Highguard.t: Highborn soldiers took Beoraidh's towers after the raid set out from Necropolis, and congregations sent warriors and supplies to Brocéliande. The Zenith raid returned 250 troops to each of the Granite Pillar, the Valiant Pegasus and the Seventh Wave.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Winter Sun marched home to Skarsind while three thousand furloughed reavers led the Beoraidh raid. About 2,500 freed orcs will settle in Skarsind and could one day form the core of a third army. The Summer Storm lost many soldiers beneath the ice of the Atkonaroq.

Jotun.t: The Bear Who Swims came nine-tenths of the way to conquering West Ranging. In Segura the Lasambrian Jotun held Anduzjasse but fell back around Anduz. In Sermersuaq the Jotun lost Atalaq, Sealtoq and the Ford of Berusen, but completed the Tusks of the Lion castle in Stark.

Navarr.t: With help from Dawn, Highguard and Tharim, Navarr bands saved the Broch and held back the vallorn in Brocéliande, though Tharim's feasting costs Miaren, Therunin and Hercynia. Bonering striding was driven from Liathaven, while the Quiet Step and Black Thorns fought in Segura and Stark.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn corsairs spearheaded the landing at Beoraidh, but the Grendel conquered the Cazar Straits and Oranseri, looting and enslaving Freeborn and seizing two Bourse offices. Segura was defended by Imperial armies, and the Red Wind Corsairs and Fire of the South won the Ford of Berusen with a charge across the ice.

The League.t: League soldiers smashed Beoraidh's catapults and League saboteurs fired its towers. The Towerjacks and Wolves of War helped clear Morrow, and the League helped pay for Winter's Mantle. Sarvos was alarmed when the Grendel armada sailed from its waters.

The Marches.t: Marcher soldiers captured Beoraidh's towers, and bounders and yeofolk repelled the Jotun from Bregasland. The Strong Reeds anchored the defence of Segura, while the Tusks and Drakes fought honourably in Stark.

Thule.t: Five Thule armies, nearly thirty thousand orcs under Grand Warlock Fljajokull, fought beside the Empire to clear Ossium and caused most of the Druj deaths. The Shard of Winter mysteriously broke ranks to destroy a fleeing Druj column.

Urizen.t: Caeli and Peregro were liberated and the Citadel Guard no longer declines, while thousands were rescued from Zenith, including 250 sentinels who joined the Citadel Guard. In Spiral, however, the Druj took Ossuary, Screed and the Legacy and threaten Apulian.

Varushka.t: Ossium, now Varushkan, was fully cleared of Druj with the Golden Axe and the Thule, and settlers are moving in from Karsk. The Northern Eagle and Iron Helms fought in Morrow, and Varushkan warriors guarded the saboteurs at Beoraidh.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark soldiers smashed Beoraidh's catapults. The Green Shield, Fist of the Mountain and Bloodcloaks retook Atalaq and Sealtoq and broke through at the Ford of Berusen, fighting honourably. Debate over Suaq who swore oaths as Jotun thralls bred some dissension in the ranks.

383YE Spring Equinox winds of war.o: In the Spring of 383YE the Empire raided Beoraidh, burning the Grendel fortification and coliseum and freeing about 2,500 orc slaves, and liberated Caeli and Peregro in Morrow. It also rescued thousands from Zenith and completed the conquest of Ossium alongside the Thule. Elsewhere the Druj seized much of Spiral, the Grendel conquered the Cazar Straits and Oranseri, and the Jotun swept into West Ranging.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Bone-armoured knights of Tharim fought here alongside Navarr and Dawnish defenders, and the region was saved from the vallorn.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Tharim's baron Poena led bound dead in its defence, and the Broch's survival kept the vallorn from surging into Elerael.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The Grendel overran Cazar and Shantarim, looted the corsair families and enslaved many, and seized the Broken Shore Bounty office. A conjunction to the Pillars of the Osseini is on offer.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Bramar fell in a day and its wines were plundered. Most of the region remains Imperial, but the Grendel are three-tenths of the way to taking it.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Joharra and Oran fell, Lord Rahab rules from the Scorrero Nets office, and Imperial refugees are trapped inside the Asavean temple of Balo.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: The Bear Who Swims is nine-tenths of the way to conquering the region and camps at Silent Stand, which is offered as a Sentinel Gate conjunction.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: The Jotun advance likely ends Navarr hopes of uprooting the vallorn here before the Summer Solstice.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Imperial forces burned the nearly complete castle and the coliseum, freed thousands of slaves, and caught a Tarquinius ship trading granite and slaves.

Morrow/Altis.t: Mentioned in passing: giant hounds summoned into its hills ranged across Morrow hunting the Druj.

Morrow/Caeli.t: Liberated by the Citadel Guard and its allies, with new heliopticon towers, including a central replacement, being raised.

Morrow/Operus.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj had already been denied their foothold here before the Winter Solstice.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Its spires were liberated, though at the Spire of the Red Sun the Druj killed as many captives as they could.

Necropolis/Hedrossan.t: Mentioned in passing: the Beoraidh raid departed from Necropolis's quaysides and returned there.

Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand.t: Mentioned in passing: Sanctuary was among the ports straining to launch the armada.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish armies advanced east from Bittershore.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule armies marched south from their domain in the Bonewood, which remains theirs.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Taken by the allies after Orieb and its serpent-carved palace fell. Here the Shard of Winter cut down a fleeing Druj column, aided by mysterious hooded Druj.

Ossium/Galath Fields.t: Mentioned in passing: the allied pincer advanced south from Galath Fields.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: It fell first to the allied pincer, its abandoned settlements full of traps, and fleeing Druj scattered south and east.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt's quaysides launched the Beoraidh raid and welcomed back the armada and Zenith refugees.

Redoubt/Optarion.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt's ports launched the armada and received rescued Urizen from Zenith.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel armada anchored off Sarvos set sail, causing alarm on the quaysides.

Sarvos/Foracci.t: Mentioned in passing: frightened people fled north to Foracci when the Grendel armada stirred.

Segura/Anduzjasse.t: It remains wholly Lasambrian Jotun, and their forces rallied around Anduz and the Golden Terraces at season's end.

Segura/Anozeseri.t: Most of the fighting took place here, with a command post at Anozel. The Jotun foothold neither grew nor shrank.

Segura/Burnish.t: Mentioned in passing: losing its Tower of Anduz would cost the entire great work's benefit.

Segura/Lucksprings.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial armies could not defend Segura from here and moved south-west.

Segura/Sobral Grasses.t: The Lasambrians burned the ancient Sobral Stand, revealing a recently broken burial mound with smashed spiral-carved stones.

Segura/Yellow Chase.t: Mentioned in passing: losing its Tower of Anduz would cost the entire great work's benefit.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Atalaq was retaken intact and Sealtoq liberated, but Suaq who swore thrall oaths face shame and division.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: The Empire won the Ford of Berusen after the Freeborn charged across the frozen Atkonaroq and is four-tenths of the way to taking Stark. The new Tusks of the Lion castle now bars further progress.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: There was talk of pushing here instead, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction to Lansipari Head, a hub of thrall supply activity, is offered.

Spiral/Ankra.t: The new central heliopticon tower in southern Ankra is effectively complete, and the Druj have not interfered with it.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Ten thousand Druj retook almost all the liberated land and are halfway to claiming the region, camped miles from Apulian.

Spiral/Cinion.t: The Block here is effectively complete, though Druj scouts have watched it without attacking.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: The Druj took the region and the Legacy mithril mine, and a conjunction along the Twilight Way through Ossuary is offered.

Spiral/Screed.t: The Druj seized the Black Plateau, suffering its madness, and are working Spring curses on the territory there.

The Barrens/Farweald.t: Mentioned in passing: some Druj fleeing Nearweald retreated south into Farweald.

Zenith/Iteri.t: Spire Calator has become a Druj weapon-forge and dragonbone work-camp; some slaves were freed, but the spire was too well defended to attack.

Zenith/Lustri.t: Druj magic makes its forests hostile, but Spring and Night heralds aided fugitives, and only the bravest raiders went this deep.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Only the bravest warbands ventured here, finding fewer Druj and captives but long escape routes to safety.

Zenith/Proceris.t: The Druj retreated from Morrow along the trods into Proceris. There Highborn, Dawnish and Urizen raiders freed a camp of captured Highborn soldiers from its marsh farms.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: its noble houses and villages are said to support Dawnish champions who fought the vallorn in Brocéliande.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Imperial armada gathered and sailed across the bay to Beoraidh and back, while the Grendel armada left its anchorage off Sarvos to strike Feroz.

Bregasland.t: Jotun pursuing the survivors of Bonering out of Liathaven were met by Marcher bounders and yeofolk and fell back across the border.

Brocéliande.t: Navarr, Dawnish knights, Highborn congregations and Tharim's servants held back the vallorn and saved the Broch. The miasma is thickening and larger horrors are emerging, however.

Feroz.t: The Grendel conquered the Cazar Straits and Oranseri and are three-tenths of the way to taking Fontargenta. Their pillaging will cost characters based there production next season.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: a Druj column fleeing Ossium towards it was destroyed by the Shard of Winter.

Hercynia.t: Tharim's servants are devouring its forests and herb gardens, which lose a rank of production for a year in exchange for his aid in Brocéliande.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun army that struck West Ranging crossed the border from Hordalant.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: settlers and wagon raiders are travelling east from Karsk into newly Varushkan Ossium.

Liathaven.t: The Bear Who Swims has nearly conquered West Ranging, ending Navarr hopes of driving the vallorn from the Westwood, while the Feni roam the northern woods.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: there were fears the departing Grendel armada would strike Trivento and the Spider's Dream, but it sailed on.

Mareave.t: The Imperial raid destroyed the Grendel fortification and coliseum at Beoraidh, so the Broken Shore orcs cannot raise an army here for a year.

Miaren.t: Its forests and herb gardens are being devoured by Tharim's servants, losing a rank of production for a year to pay for his aid in Brocéliande.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes' general promised to return the Jotun dead in cloths of Mitwold linen.

Morrow.t: The Druj fled and the Empire retook Caeli and Peregro unopposed, rooting out stragglers. Some spires had been left empty by massacre or by the gift of Kaela.

Necropolis.t: The Beoraidh raid launched from its overstretched quaysides, and the freed orcs returned here before heading north to Skarsind.

Ossium.t: Imperial and Thule forces took Nearweald and the Drownbark Forest, including Orieb. The whole territory apart from the Thule-held Bonewood is now Imperial.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: it is the homeland of the Thule armies that fought in Ossium, said to have few woodlands.

Redoubt.t: Its quaysides launched the Beoraidh raid and received the returning armada, and rescuers struck into Zenith from here and brought refugees back.

Sarvos.t: The Grendel armada anchored offshore set sail, causing panic before it headed south-west. Ships from Oran later brought refugees to its docks.

Segura.t: The Quiet Step and Strong Reeds held the Lasambrian Jotun in Anozeseri. Subtle Autumn magic thwarted the Corazón raids, though it fades with the Equinox.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: its nobles have ties to Boar's Dell and support Dawnish champions who fought in Brocéliande.

Sermersuaq.t: The Empire retook Atalaq and Sealtoq and pushed four-tenths of the way into Stark, where the new Jotun castle will make further progress harder.

Skarsind.t: The Winter Sun returned home, and about 2,500 freed orc warriors, plus others, are settling here to begin new lives as Imperial Orcs.

Spiral.t: A huge Druj army took Ossuary, Screed and the Legacy and nearly reclaimed Apulus. They have so far left the Block and the new heliopticon alone, and are cursing the territory with Spring magic.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: some Druj fleeing Nearweald retreated south into Farweald.

Therunin.t: Tharim is feasting on its forests and herb gardens, which lose a rank of production for a year in return for his support in Brocéliande.

Tsirku.t: Mentioned in passing: harsh winds blowing down from Tsirku brought hail and snow to Sermersuaq.

Zenith.t: The Druj still control the whole territory, but a three-month rescue raid freed two-thirds of the trapped Urizen, including soldiers who rejoined the armies.

383YE Summer Solstice interlude.d: Military captains could Slow the Vallorn in Brocéliande, serve either side of the Asavean uprising, escort lost orcs to Skarsind, or join a Mission of Mercy into the Barrens. Fleets could join Dominate the Bay against the Grendel. The Guerdon of 175 Thrones went to four named armies. Trade was hit by Grendel piracy, sanctions on Asavea, turmoil in Axos, the closure of Robec and Jarmish tariffs, while the Commonwealth offered bonuses. Synod mandates, Tharim's feast on Navarr lands, Varushkan prosperity and the Wondrous Forests enchantment altered production, and Tithe of Bats entered Imperial Lore.

Dawn.t: Dawnish characters received extra rewards for helping Slow the Vallorn in Brocéliande, and captains could join a Mission of Mercy to rescue captured children of Dawn from the Barrens.

Druj.t: The Mission of Mercy opportunity offered Imperial captains a secretive foray into the Barrens to free captured children and other slaves and frustrate the Druj.

Grendel.t: Grendel pirates continued raiding Bay of Catazar shipping and pillaging Feroz, while Imperial fleets were offered a counterattack, Dominate the Bay, to challenge their dominance there.

Highguard.t: Highborn congregations lost two votes and one liao through the Blade of the Pilgrims fighting in Brocéliande, and Highborn fleets trading in the Bay suffered a rank penalty from Grendel piracy.

Imperial Orcs.t: Allies could escort lost orcs to Skarsind for a reward, funded by an Imperial Orc assembly mandate that imposed a one-rank penalty on every orc-owned farm, business, herb garden, forest, mine, mana site and fleet.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: any Lasambrian Jotun plunder after the Spring Equinox would have no effect on personal resources because protective magic persisted over Segura.

Navarr.t: Every Navarr herb garden lost two random herbs per season under the Blood and Gold mandate, and Tharim's feast reduced herb gardens and forests in Miaren, Therunin and Hercynia until the Winter Solstice 383YE.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast fleets suffered a rank penalty from Grendel pirates, and all personal resources in Feroz faced a two-rank penalty from Grendel pillaging, though Segura remained protected.

The League.t: Fleets from Tassato and Sarvos suffered a rank penalty from Grendel piracy, while congregations in Temeschwar and Tassato gained votes and liao under Rafael Barossa di Tassato's Reject False Gods mandate.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr's Blood and Gold mandate supported Good Leaf Gardens in Upwold in recognition of the Marcher sacrifice fighting the vallorn of Liathaven.

Urizen.t: Urizen fleets trading in the Bay suffered a rank penalty from Grendel piracy, while congregations in Redoubt gained two votes and one liao for as long as the Synod opposes idolatry.

Varushka.t: Varushkan mines and forests gained a rank of production, potentially for a year if Raskylov provided a suitable story, and Karsk congregations gained four extra votes and two liao for a year.

Wintermark.t: Congregations in Hahnmark gained two votes and one liao under the Reject False Gods mandate while the Synod maintains its anti-idolatry stance.

383YE Summer Solstice interlude.o: Ahead of the Summer Solstice, a temporary interlude set out the downtime opportunities, trade conditions and large-scale effects following the Spring Equinox 383YE, pending the full Winds of Fortune.

Bay of Catazar.t: Grendel pirates continued harassing shipping in the Bay, and Imperial fleets could join a damaging counterattack to challenge Grendel dominance there for a share of seized goods.

Brocéliande.t: The vallorn continued to expand in Brocéliande; captains could help the steadings Slow the Vallorn, while Highborn congregations and the eternal Tharim also aided its defence.

Feroz.t: Every character based in Feroz faced a two-rank penalty to personal resource production from Grendel pillaging, though the Asavean temple there still boosted Imperial trade with Nemoria.

Hahnmark.t: Congregations in Hahnmark gained two votes and one liao after builders forcibly redesigned the Asavean-designed buildings there.

Hercynia.t: Tharim was permitted to feast on Hercynia's herb gardens and forests, each losing two herbs or resources until the Winter Solstice 383YE.

Karsk.t: Karsk congregations received four extra votes and two liao for a year under the Reject False Gods mandate, then the lesser bonus given elsewhere.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher sacrifice in fighting the vallorn of Liathaven was the reason Good Leaf Gardens were supported in Upwold.

Miaren.t: Herb gardens and forests in Miaren were fed upon by Tharim, losing two herbs or resources each until the Winter Solstice 383YE.

Redoubt.t: Congregations in Redoubt gained two votes and one liao as the Asavean-designed buildings there were forcibly redesigned.

Sarvos.t: Fleets from Sarvos trading out of the Bay suffered a one-rank production penalty from Grendel pirate raids.

Segura.t: The magic that protected Segura from Corazón raids persisted, so any Lasambrian Jotun plunder would not affect personal resources there.

Skarsind.t: Lost orcs across the Empire sought to reach Skarsind, and Imperial captains could escort them there to safety.

Tassato.t: Tassato's fleets suffered a rank penalty from Grendel piracy, while its congregations gained two votes and one liao under the Reject False Gods mandate.

Temeschwar.t: Congregations in Temeschwar gained two votes and one liao after the Asavean-designed buildings there were forcibly redesigned.

Therunin.t: Therunin's herb gardens and forests lost two herbs or resources each to Tharim's feast until the Winter Solstice 383YE.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr's Blood and Gold mandate was a consequence of supporting Good Leaf Gardens in Upwold.

383YE Summer Solstice winds of fortune.d: All six eternals agreed to some form of parley with the archmages, and new opportunities opened at Anvil. The Sand Fishers left Bittershore for Misericorde in Holberg and began trading with the League. Brocéliande faced a building vallorn onslaught, while Westwood was liberated and a pristine weirwood forest found there. The Brass Coast, Navarr, the Marches, Varushka, Wintermark and several assemblies were each offered opportunities. The Basilica of Seven Doors was restored. Two miasma pillars were found in Ossium. Mobs stripped Almodin's commissions, and magistrates are now investigating. Vengeful Feni sacked the Singing Caves, and as many as fourteen wains of mithril are missing. Frederick di Sarvos threatened to leave the Empire.

Dawn.t: Dawn was named among those holding Brocéliande against the swelling vallorn, and its national assembly was invited to answer the grey pilgrims' questions. The Dawnish Cardinal of Ambition, Viviane de Coeurdefer, is tied to Frederick di Sarvos's stalled offer.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are listed as one of the Empire's orc neighbours. They once ruled the Sand Fishers and left behind the miasma still choking Ossium.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are listed as one of the four orc nations bordering the Empire, and orc slaves recently rescued from them are noted.

Highguard.t: The Basilica of Seven Doors in Bastion was restored and the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly reinstated. Highborn statements guide the grey pilgrims, and Highguard is also tagged in the Brocéliande defence and magical developments.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc assembly was tagged in the Sand Fishers' settlement of Holberg, the integration of the Mournwold thralls and wider orc affairs, where the many orc peoples are described as being in states ranging from war to uneasy truce with the Empire.

Jotun.t: Thralls the Jotun left behind in the Mournwold may be drawn into the Marcher nation. The Brass Coast offered a bounty to any Imperial who would fight the Lasambrian Jotun, and the Stormcrows declared Suaq who became Jotun thralls to be Frayed.

Navarr.t: The Navarr could raise a new vallorn-fighting army, with or without the Queen of Scorpions, and weighed three visions for Seren. They also held Brocéliande through another season and celebrated the vallorn's defeat in Liathaven.

The Brass Coast.t: Barbarians threaten every Brass Coast territory except Madruga. The Freeborn were offered a mithril exchange towards restoring the Burning Falcon, proposals to strengthen Segura, a salvage port, the Broken Shore Bounty and a bounty against the Lasambrian Jotun, and a Freeborn could become captain of the Passion of the Flame.

The League.t: League burghers gained a trade in herbs, delicacies and hides with the Sand Fishers in Holberg, and bishops proposed reinvigorating Capodomus Cathedral. Someone could also become leader of the Revelry, and a mandate under Rafael Barossa di Tassato sent mobs against Almodin's works.

The Marches.t: The Marcher assembly and the Senate examined bringing the Mournwold thralls into the Marcher nation. Feni sacked the Singing Caves, leaving Abbot Thomas Arch only seven wains of mithril, and Abbot Matilda of Becktunn championed Marcher common sense and a lost exemplar of Ambition.

Thule.t: Thule forces are currently the only defenders of Ossium, and few of the territory's people have any reason to trust them. An Ambassador to Otkodov is among those concerned with orc affairs.

Varushka.t: The Varushkans could raise a memorial to the paragon Zoria with true liao, and wise ones weighed the role of the Tender of the Hearth. In newly conquered Ossium, two miasma pillars were found, but defence and the many resident orcs remain pressing problems.

Wintermark.t: The Stormcrows' celebration of heroism opened opportunities for a daring raid, a mystical rookery and a chronicle of heroes. Their declaring Jotun-thralled Suaq Frayed provoked a very different reaction, and the Crows highlighted the parlous state of the Hall of Rund.

383YE Summer Solstice winds of fortune.o: The Summer Solstice 383YE winds of fortune gathered the Empire's developments after the Spring Equinox. They included the Sand Fishers settling Misericorde, victory over the vallorn in Westwood, a Feni attack on the Singing Caves and mobs stripping the works of Almodin Oktístis.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Boar's Dell is one of the footholds of civilisation threatened by a coming tidal wave of vallorn malice that must be endured for one more season.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Elerael is one of the footholds of civilisation threatened by a coming tidal wave of vallorn malice that must be endured for one more season.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: The Sand Fishers prefer roaming the marshes of Ennerlund to visiting the city of Holberg.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Ceded to the Sand Fishers, Misericorde quickly gained small orc villages that exploit its abundant wildlife.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: The Sand Fishers range into the marshes of Rebeshof rather than the city of Holberg.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: The Sand Fishers are wary of Utterlund's deep woods, fearing the bandits there and perhaps reminded of the Druj.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: Imperial forces drove the vallorn out of Westwood, claiming the region and discovering a pristine weirwood forest.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: Vengeful Feni crossed the Ore Hills to sack the Singing Caves. They slaughtered miners and left as many as fourteen wains of mithril missing, though the mine should return to full production next season.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: The Sand Fishers abandoned Bittershore with civil service help and crossed the Semmerlak to settle Misericorde.

Bastion.t: The Senate-commissioned refurbishment of the Basilica of Seven Doors was quickly completed with the Custodes Clavium's help, and the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly was reinstated.

Brocéliande.t: The vallorn's attacks have grown for nine months and are expected to crest next season. If the Empire holds for three more months the threat should end for now, possibly with new opportunity.

Holberg.t: The Sand Fishers settled Misericorde as recognised foreigners, founding villages and trading rare goods with League citizens. They shun the city itself and the bandit-haunted woods of Utterlund.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold Marchers are said to have more in common with the Jotun thralls than with people across the border in Kahraman.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: Karsk is not named on the page. The Varushkan matters discussed are Zoria's claimed resting place in the Vale of Gniejezdo and the situation in Ossium.

Liathaven.t: Imperial forces won a decisive victory over the vallorn, claiming Westwood and an unlooked-for pristine weirwood forest ripe for development.

Madruga.t: Madruga is the only Brass Coast territory not threatened by barbarians, and there is an opportunity to build a salvage port there.

Mournwold.t: Marchers and Jotun thralls who stayed behind have become neighbours after thirty years of shared labour. Both the Senate and the Marcher assembly sought their integration, and Feni raided the Singing Caves in the Ore Hills.

Ossium.t: Ser Ancél Watcher's work uncovered the first two miasma pillars, likely one per region. The territory is defended only by the distrusted Thule and holds many orcs less tractable than the Sand Fishers.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov is tagged as having an interest in the season's orc affairs.

Segura.t: The Senate signalled it would not abandon Segura to the western invaders, and the architect Angelina i Duarte i Riqueza put forward proposals to strengthen it.

Sermersuaq.t: The Stormcrows declared the Suaq who became Jotun thralls to be Frayed, a judgement that has provoked a strong reaction among the people of Sermersuaq.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral itself is not discussed. The nearest reference is the Spiral Sword runeforge, one of Almodin's works stripped by mobs.

Tassato.t: League citizens, especially those of Tassato, are flagged as concerned by the season's magical developments. Rafael Barossa di Tassato enacted the mandate that sent mobs against Almodin's works.

The Semmerlak.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers crossed the Semmerlak from Bittershore to reach their new home in Misericorde.

Upwold.t: Nearly a gross of Feni gathered in a copse near the Old Pig before splitting. Those heading northeast into the Silver Chase were quickly dealt with by Marcher heroes arriving through the Sentinel Gate.

383YE Summer Solstice winds of war.d: Two Highborn armies narrowly held Segura against the Lasambrian Jotun. In Feroz, Marcher and Navarr armies were pushed back and Bramar fell, leaving the Grendel nine-tenths of the way to taking the territory. The vallorn was held in Brocéliande, though it is expected to crest next season. League armies destroyed Llofir's Castle of Ruin, and Tamarbode was restored without its Spring regio. Imperial and Axou captains sank hundreds of Grendel ships and raided Gainmeachdubh. The Jotun took two-thirds of Serra Damata. The Druj threw back the Barrens invasion and executed prisoners, but the Mission of Mercy freed the Drycastle children and many slaves. Six armies cleansed Westwood, confining Liathaven's vallorn to Liath's Heart. Five Sentinel Gate conjunctions were identified.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Hounds of Glory, Eastern Sky, Golden Sun and Gryphon's Pride invaded Dawnguard and were driven back to Semmerholm with nearly a thousand dead, after which the Druj executed hundreds of Dawnish prisoners. The Mission of Mercy freed the Drycastle children and about two-fifths of the missing Dawnish citizens.

Druj.t: The Druj, prepared with traps, Spring and Night magic and the White Lion's coordination, repelled the invasion of Dawnguard and slaughtered prisoners in reprisal. They nonetheless lost the Drycastle children and many slaves to the Mission of Mercy, while their forces in Spiral fell quiet.

Grendel.t: The Grendel armada took Bramar and nearly all of Fontargenta, holding Feroz's coast and ilium offices. At sea, however, hundreds of their ships were sunk or crippled, Gainmeachdubh was raided, and their supply convoys will struggle to resupply for a year.

Highguard.t: The Granite Pillar and Seventh Wave held Segura at a cost of some fifteen hundred Highborn. Highguard's Remember Exile garrison was key to liberating Tamarbode, Highborn ships sank many Grendel supply convoys, and Highborn priests and a national mandate aided Brocéliande.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Summer Storm fought in the Westwood, where one of its patrols found an untouched weirwood grove, while orc defenders repelled Jotun raiders in Skarsind. Imperial Orc captains also joined raids on Grendel ports, though they were absent from the Mission of Mercy.

Jotun.t: The Lasambrian Jotun failed to advance in Segura but kept Anduzjasse, while the Bear-Who-Swims and Skjalderborn took two-thirds of Serra Damata. The Jotun still hold all of Sermersuaq except Sealtoq and four regions of Liathaven.

Navarr.t: The Black Thorns led the cleansing of the Westwood, confining the Liathaven vallorn to Liath's Heart, and the vallorn was held in Brocéliande with many allies. The Quiet Step harried the Grendel in Feroz, while Tharim continues to feed on Navarr forests and herb gardens.

The Brass Coast.t: Three of the four Freeborn territories are now invaded: Segura narrowly held, Feroz nearly lost to the Grendel, and Serra Damata in Kahraman two-thirds taken by the Jotun. Freeborn corsairs were prominent in the campaign that broke Grendel control of the Bay.

The League.t: The Towerjacks and Wolves of War, with Holberg siege engineers, stormed the Castle of Ruin and liberated Tamarbode. League captains hunted Grendel pirates in the Bay, and League citizens captured in Holberg years ago were freed from the Druj.

The Marches.t: The Strong Reeds and Bounders fought the Grendel in Feroz but were forced to abandon Bramar. The Drakes helped cleanse the Westwood of Liathaven.

Urizen.t: The Citadel Guard defended Elerael in Brocéliande and studied the vallorn's magic, and Urizen ships sank many Grendel supply convoys. Around a hundred Urizen captives taken from Zenith were freed from Druj slavery.

Varushka.t: The Golden Axe joined the failed invasion of Dawnguard, liberating smaller settlements before the retreat, and captured Varushkan soldiers were among those executed by the Druj. Varushkan ships preyed on Grendel merchant vessels.

Wintermark.t: The Bloodcloaks and Fist of the Mountains left Sermersuaq to help cleanse the Westwood, while the Beacons of Wintermark turned back Jotun raiders in Kallavesa and Hahnmark. Wintermark has by far the largest force weight for the Solstice conjunctions.

383YE Summer Solstice winds of war.o: Across the Empire, Imperial armies narrowly held Segura and Brocéliande, liberated Tamarbode from the eternal Llofir, cleansed the Westwood of Liathaven, and broke Grendel dominance of the Bay of Catazar. Elsewhere the Grendel took Bramar and nearly all of Feroz, the Jotun invaded Kahraman again, and the Dawnish-Varushkan invasion of the Barrens was repelled, though a covert mission freed the children of Drycastle and many slaves.

Ayereed/Gainmeachdubh.t: Imperial captains raided this prosperous Grendel port under the gaze of Salt Lord Azshur, damaging the harbour and burning over two dozen pirate ships at anchor.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Mentioned in passing: a captain 'of North Fens' is listed in the naval campaign.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Boar's Dell was defended against the vallorn's push, helped by the destruction of the North Weaver Wood herald. Great Forest orcs born here returned to fight for it.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: The Citadel Guard and their husks stood ready to defend Elerael, freeing other defenders to concentrate on Boar's Dell.

Brocéliande/Vale's Lament.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though the vallorn of Brocéliande is described pressing outward into Boar's Dell and Elerael.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: Imperial troops remain billeted near Afar and the borders of Afarjasse, and Grendel looters raided Afar. The armada cannot push inland here without land forces.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The Grendel have uncontested control of the region, including Cazar and its ilium office, halting ilium collection.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Bramar fell after a three-day stand and was looted, leaving the Grendel nine-tenths of the way to taking the region and with it the territory.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: The nearly finished Mora's Rock served as the Imperial base of operations, and Grendel looters raided Mora. The Bounders arrived here via the Cinnabar Hills.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The Grendel hold Oranseri and the southern ends of the Scorrero bridges, and the Strong Reeds' push here was driven back. The Scorrero Bluffs are a Sentinel Gate conjunction for the Solstice.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Mentioned in passing: the armies marched through the woods of northern Holberg, where poisonous plants no longer grow.

Holberg/The Morass.t: Mentioned in passing: the armies trudged through the stinking mud of the Morass on their way south.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Mentioned in passing: the armies passed through its woods, now free of the poisonous plants that once grew there.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: The Fort Braydon garrison slowed the Jotun, but many of its soldiers are in precarious positions as the Solstice nears.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named and is touched only by the wider Jotun invasion of Kahraman.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: Dhomiro of Serra Briante sent warriors west to resist, and Jotun raiders pushed toward Rojota. The Rojota Road is a Sentinel Gate conjunction for the Solstice.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: The Jotun overran two-thirds of Serra Damata, but defenders held Damata and its white granite cliffs.

Liathaven/Liath's Heart.t: The vallorn of Liathaven is now confined to Liath's Heart around the ruined Terunael city, and it is more dangerous than ever.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: The Jotun had withdrawn, so West Ranging stayed Imperial and carried the supply lines for the Westwood campaign. It can now be reached on foot from Western Scout.

Liathaven/Western Scout.t: It is now possible to walk from Western Scout to West Ranging. Fallen Thorn Stead, a Jotun meeting point here, is a Sentinel Gate conjunction.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: Westwood was cleansed of the vallorn and conquered by the Empire, and a healthy weirwood grove was found here. The Heartway is a Sentinel Gate conjunction for the Solstice.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: the earlier Imperial raid on Beoraidh is recalled, and Gainmeachdubh is compared to it in size.

Reikos/Broken Ride.t: The garrison of Remember Exile, the fortification here, was a major factor in liberating Tamarbode.

Reikos/Grey Charge.t: Mentioned in passing: the League armies gathered beneath its boughs, hosted by its chapters, before entering Tamarbode.

Reikos/Haros Water.t: Mentioned in passing: veterans recall the horror of its liberation when facing Druj traps in Dawnguard.

Reikos/Longshire.t: Mentioned in passing: the League armies gathered here as guests of its rebuilt chapterhouses.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Tamarbode was liberated and is now forested and Springtouched. Its Spring regio and Tamar's Toes are gone, and the Sign of Tamar is being reclaimed by the forest.

Segura/Anduzjasse.t: Anduzjasse remains wholly in Lasambrian Jotun hands, and refugees continue to flee east from it.

Segura/Anozeseri.t: The Jotun foothold in Anozeseri was neither expanded nor reduced. Losing any of its Towers of Anduz would end the great work's benefits.

Segura/Burnish.t: If the orcs take any Towers of Anduz in Burnish, the great work's entire benefit will be lost.

Segura/Iron Plains.t: A force of Escuta led by a pale-skinned shaman shadowed Granite Pillar troops escorting refugees across the Iron Plains, the site of an old slaughter, but largely avoided battle.

Segura/Yellow Chase.t: Its Towers of Anduz are at risk should the orcs advance. The Ambergris Valley here is a Sentinel Gate conjunction for the Solstice.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: The invading armies regrouped in Axmure, and the Druj raised a forest of spiked heads in sight of its forests.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Sealtoq is the only region not held by the Jotun, whose rulers are keeping their oath not to march into it for a year.

Spiral/Apulus.t: The Druj push into Apulus was halted last season, and no further Druj movement has been reported.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: Ossuary and the Legacy remain under Druj control, though no further activity has been seen.

Spiral/Screed.t: Screed and the Black Plateau remain under Druj control after their rites there, though no Druj movements are reported.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: The invasion of Dawnguard was driven back and the Druj executed hundreds of prisoners, but the Drycastle children and many slaves were freed.

The Barrens/Farweald.t: Mentioned in passing: savage beasts from Farweald followed the Druj into Dawnguard.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: Heroes struck slave camps here, freeing Urizen captives working the weirwood forest, and some freed children escaped through Peytaht to Reikos.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: Three hundred freed orc children were brought to the sanctuary at Hope's Rest before being taken on to Therunin.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Heroes of the Mission of Mercy struck against slave camps in Murderdale.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: Malignant marsh creatures from Saltmarsh harried Imperial soldiers, and orc children taken from Saltmarsh were among those rescued.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: Mentioned in passing: savage beasts out of the Bleaks fought in the Druj's wake in Dawnguard.

The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth.t: Orc children were rescued from the Plains of Teeth, and freed slaves report thriving Druj towns there.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: Most of the freed Drycastle children reached freedom by travelling south through the Lower Tarn Valley.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: its noble houses and villages support Dawnish champions in Brocéliande, and many Astolat citizens are listed among those taking part.

Ayereed.t: Ayereed suffered lightning raids by Imperial captains culminating in the attack on Gainmeachdubh, contributing to a bounty of mithril and ilium.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Bastion captains are listed among those who sailed against the Grendel.

Bay of Catazar.t: Imperial and Axou captains sank or crippled hundreds of Grendel ships, ending the Grendel hunt of Imperial traders and halving their resupply for a year. They were not strong enough to disrupt the Rites of Spring, however.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the armies bound for Liathaven marched through its marshes, and Bregasland captains are listed in the naval campaign.

Brocéliande.t: Defenders held back the vallorn for a third season with the Citadel Guard, Great Forest orcs and other allies, but their reserves are taxed and the vallorn's wave has yet to crest.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea citizens are listed among those aiding Brocéliande and the naval campaign.

Feroz.t: The Grendel now hold Oranseri and the Cazar Straits and nine-tenths of Fontargenta after taking Bramar, along with the ilium offices and the Temple of Balo. Over fifteen hundred Imperial soldiers were lost, and residents continue to suffer raids.

Hahnmark.t: Jotun raiders from Sermersuaq met stiff resistance at the lit Beacons of Wintermark and were turned back.

Hercynia.t: Tharim continues to feast on Hercynia's forests and herb gardens, costing each a rank of production for a year in return for his aid in Brocéliande.

Holberg.t: The armies bound for the Barrens passed through Holberg, its university supplied siege engineers for Tamarbode, and masked boatmen carried liberators and freed children along the river.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bear-That-Swims earlier crossed from Hordalant to attack West Ranging.

Kahraman.t: The Jotun invaded again from the west and took two-thirds of Serra Damata, held back from Damata and the white granite cliffs only by the Fort Braydon garrison.

Kallavesa.t: Jotun raiders were repelled at the borders, and the armies bound for Liathaven marched through Kallavesa's marshes.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Karov citizens are listed among the captains who sailed against the Grendel.

Liathaven.t: Six Imperial armies cleansed the Westwood, leaving the vallorn confined to Liath's Heart, at a cost of over three thousand lives. The Jotun still hold the territory, and the Paths of Lan Thúven are gone.

Madruga.t: With the Grendel holding the southern ends of the Scorrero bridges, armies can no longer enter Feroz from Madruga without fighting. A few Freeborn refugees are being smuggled there.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: earlier Imperial raids on Mareave and Beoraidh are said to have enraged the Salt Lords.

Miaren.t: Tharim continues to feed on Miaren's forests and herb gardens, costing each a rank of production for a year.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova citizens are listed in the naval campaign and the Mission of Mercy.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: a Mitwold captain is listed in the naval campaign.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard came to Brocéliande fresh from fighting the Druj in Morrow, bringing husks raised from the fallen there.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bounders came to Feroz from furlough in the Mournwold, which Fort Braydon overlooks.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis citizens are listed among the captains who sailed against the Grendel.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: with the fighting in Ossium over for now, the five armies that conquered it marched south to invade the Barrens.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt citizens are listed among those aiding Brocéliande and the naval campaign.

Reikos.t: Tamarbode was liberated, Llofir vanished and the region was restored as forest, though its Spring regio and Tamar's Toes were destroyed.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: some Freeborn refugees are smuggled out of Feroz to Sarvos, and ships sailed from its docks to hunt the Grendel.

Segura.t: Highborn armies narrowly held the line against the Lasambrian Jotun at a cost of some fifteen hundred dead. The protective Autumn magic is fading, seven Towers of Anduz remain in orc hands, and destitute refugees strain the eastern towns.

Semmerholm.t: The armies gathered at Axmure before invading the Barrens and retreated there in defeat, and the Druj raised a field of heads on spikes in sight of its forests. Semmerholm yeofolk also guided liberators into Dawnguard.

Sermersuaq.t: The Jotun rule all of Sermersuaq except Sealtoq, which they are keeping their oath not to enter for a year. Their raids south and east are being repelled.

Shayeel.t: Imperial captains made lightning raids on Grendel pirate settlements in Shayeel, contributing to a bounty of 12 wains of mithril and 6 rings of ilium.

Skarsind.t: Jotun raiders from Sermersuaq crossed into Skarsind and clashed with its Imperial Orc defenders.

Spiral.t: There has been no news of Druj movements since they took Ossuary and Screed, and it is unclear whether any major Druj force remains. Roughly a third of Spiral is still under their nominal control.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the gentler route through Tassato into Feroz is closed to Marcher armies while the Grendel hold Oranseri.

Tathar.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel trade ships avoid the channel between the Iron Confederacy and Tathar.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar citizens are listed in the naval campaign and the Mission of Mercy.

The Barrens.t: The Dawnish-Varushkan invasion of Dawnguard was repelled and prisoners were executed in reprisal, but the Mission of Mercy freed the Drycastle children, many slaves and 10 wains of weirwood. Freed slaves report that the Towers of Dusk have been rebuilt as a great citadel.

Therunin.t: Tharim continues to feed on Therunin's forests and herb gardens. A thousand freed orcs and three hundred orc children joined the Great Forest orcs here, with liberators and Navarr scouts using it as a route into the Barrens.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: an Upwold captain is listed in the naval campaign.

Volodmartz.t: Mentioned in passing: a Volodmartz captain is listed in the naval campaign.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: many Weirwater citizens are listed among those aiding Brocéliande and the Mission of Mercy.

Zenith.t: Around a hundred Urizen citizens taken north from Zenith were found enslaved in Peytaht and the Carmine Fields and were freed.

383YE Winter Solstice Imperial elections.d: Senators were chosen for Astolat, Bregasland, Hercynia, Kallavesa, Madruga, Miekarova, Mitwold, Necropolis, Ossium, Skarsind, Temeschwar and Therunin. The Senate appointed three ambassadors (to Axos, Jarm and the Iron Confederacy), ten generals and several other titles. The Synod returned cardinals, inquisitors and other religious positions, led by Leonora van Holberg as Patron of the Pavilion with 177 votes. Bourse auctions placed great forests and wayleaves, the largest bid being 510 thrones for the Golden Trees of Seren. Bourse votes filled further posts. The Conclave chose four grandmasters, and candidates declared for several titles, including the Archmages of Night and Winter and the Imperial Seer.

Dawn.t: Dawn's senate seat for Astolat went to Bohemond De Rondell, and Tancred was appointed General of the Hounds of Glory.

Highguard.t: Highguard returned Eli as Senator for Necropolis, and Asenath was appointed General of the Granite Pillar.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs chose Rurik as Senator for Skarsind, and Zerk was appointed General of the Summer Storm.

Navarr.t: Navarr filled two senate seats, Rhisiart Dancewalker for Hercynia and Travid Longest Path for Therunin, and Iron Osric was appointed General of the Green Shield.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast returned Chiara Zayden Riqueza as Senator for Madruga.

The League.t: The League chose Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar as Senator for Temeschwar, and Natalia "The Falcon" Barossa was appointed General of the Towerjacks.

The Marches.t: The Marches filled two senate seats, Orrick for Bregasland and William Lowther for Mitwold, and Jack Flint was appointed General of the Strong Reeds.

Varushka.t: Varushka returned Yulia Kasimirova Voronov for Miekarova and Vesna (Sparrow) Borkovna for Ossium. New generals were appointed for the Golden Axe, the Iron Helms and the Northern Eagle.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark chose Rane Sherarding as Senator for Kallavesa, and Rykana was appointed General of the Winter Sun.

383YE Winter Solstice Imperial elections.o: At the 383YE Winter Solstice summit, the Empire filled a wide range of Imperial titles, from twelve national Senate seats to Senate-appointed generals, Synod and Bourse positions and Conclave grandmasterships.

Astolat.t: Bohemond De Rondell was elected Senator for Astolat.

Bregasland.t: Orrick was elected Senator for Bregasland.

Hercynia.t: Rhisiart Dancewalker was elected Senator for Hercynia.

Kallavesa.t: Rane Sherarding was elected Senator for Kallavesa.

Madruga.t: Chiara Zayden Riqueza was elected Senator for Madruga.

Miekarova.t: Yulia Kasimirova Voronov was elected Senator for Miekarova.

Mitwold.t: William Lowther was elected Senator for Mitwold.

Necropolis.t: Eli was elected Senator for Necropolis.

Ossium.t: Vesna (Sparrow) Borkovna was elected Senator for Ossium.

Skarsind.t: Rurik was elected Senator for Skarsind.

Temeschwar.t: Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar was elected Senator for Temeschwar.

Therunin.t: Travid Longest Path was elected Senator for Therunin.

383YE Winter Solstice Senate sessions.d: The treasury stood at 1994 thrones. The Senate funded Marcher military resupply and the enlargement of the Drakes, and set the magistrates on Brass Coast smuggling and on followers of Yaw'nagrah, which costs every mana site one crystal while the investigation runs. It renamed the Imperial Orc Wayleave as Legion Engineer and raised Holberg's upkeep to educate the Sand Fisher orcs. Commissions included works in Casinea, Hahnmark, Kallavesa, Kahraman, Sarvos, Tassato, Semmerholm and Hercynia, and a schloss ceded to the Commonwealth. Title-holders announced a spy network in Feroz, a ward against the trogoni and the decommissioning of Ossium's spy network. Three ambassadors were appointed and two deferred.

Dawn.t: Semmerholm gained the Arbor of the Twin Roses, a sinecure honouring the exemplar Elayne Silverlark whose Voice is chosen by the Dawnish National Assembly. The proposed Manor of the Greenwood failed.

Grendel.t: A spy network was announced for Grendel-held Feroz, and the Broken Shore Mithril Market in Cargo was commissioned to buy Grendel mithril in exchange for weirwood.

Highguard.t: The College of Maykop was commissioned in Casinea, and Britta's Shrine is to become a memorial for pilgrims of Courage, following a Highborn National Assembly judgement. A first version of that motion from Reikos was withdrawn.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc Wayleave was renamed Legion Engineer and given power to build spy networks. Ka'bal used the title to announce a spy network in Feroz.

Navarr.t: The Tenebrous Path sinecure was commissioned in Hercynia to inspire the Thorns of Navarr, as the anti-vallorn army Isaella's Dance prepares to muster at Miaren. Navarr senators also launched the magistrates' hunt for followers of Yaw'nagrah.

The Brass Coast.t: The Parador of Dust in Kahraman was refurbished as a mithril ministry for the Freeborn. A schloss off Madruga was ceded to the Commonwealth, and magistrates were tasked with stopping smuggling across Brass Coast borders.

The League.t: League territories gained the Sweetwater Springs in Sarvos, an Imperial Consulate in Tassato and an expanded Georgie's House in Holberg. Holberg's upkeep also rose to educate the Sand Fisher orcs.

The Marches.t: The Senate disbursed 300 thrones to Orrick of Bregasland for military resupply and 230 thrones to complete the enlargement of the Drakes, the first Marcher army. Upwold's senator proposed the Thule treaty.

Thule.t: The ratified treaty ceded the regions of Miechernya in Miekarova and Webwood in Ossium to the Thule. Appointing an Ambassador to Otkodov was deferred to the Spring Equinox.

Urizen.t: The Senate commissioned an appraisal of fortifications in Urizen territory, to be delivered before Spring 384YE. Octavius of Damakan's Forge also announced the Broken Shore Mithril Market in Cargo, with its Broker chosen by Urizen mana site holders.

Varushka.t: Varushkan senators now appoint the five Ossium spoils-of-war positions, but Varushka lost Miechernya and Webwood to the Thule under the treaty. Ossium's spy network was decommissioned.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's runesmiths were confirmed as heirs of the Gildenheim Runeforge, and its ruins are to go to Runegrott. The Senate also commissioned the Kauppahall in Hahnmark and the Healing House of Wittal Grove in Kallavesa.

383YE Winter Solstice Senate sessions.o: At the Winter Solstice 383YE the Senate ratified a treaty ceding Miechernya and Webwood to the Thule, made the Ossium spoils of war Varushkan national positions and created six Champions of Virtue. It also passed a long slate of commissions, disbursements and investigations, though no Throne was elected.

Holberg/Holfried.t: The Kennels of Holfried, Georgie's House, were expanded to sell across the Empire, raising the sinecure's revenue.

Kallavesa/Wittal Grove.t: The Healing House of Wittal Grove, a great work to benefit herb garden owners, was commissioned along with a title meant for a grimnir. A motion allowing the Senate to abrogate that title failed.

Miekarova/Miechernya.t: Miechernya was ceded to the Thule under the ratified treaty.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Webwood was ceded to the Thule under the ratified treaty.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Urizen fortifications appraisal and seconded the Britta's Memorial motion.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Gildenheim Runeforge motion and seconded the Sweetwater Springs.

Bregasland.t: Orrick of Bregasland received 300 thrones for military resupply. The Quartermaster General's instruction to apply the Guerdon to Bregasland was ignored because it is not an army or military opportunity.

Casinea.t: A campus for the Halls of Maykop, the College of Maykop, was commissioned in Casinea.

Feroz.t: The Legion Engineer Ka'bal announced the construction of a spy network in Feroz.

Hahnmark.t: The Kauppahall trading hall was commissioned in Hahnmark, and the Runeforge excavation will cut the cost of a runeforge at Runegrott. The Runic Hearth of Adamant is meant to stop trogoni threatening Hahnmark.

Hercynia.t: The Tenebrous Path sinecure, which produces mana crystals, was commissioned in Hercynia's Old Ranging. The Guerdon instruction naming Hercynia was ignored, and its senator's second seconding was referred to the magistrates.

Holberg.t: Holberg's upkeep rose by 14 thrones a season to educate the Sand Fisher orcs, and Georgie's House there was expanded. Two von Holberg citizens donated thrones to the treasury.

Kahraman.t: The Parador of Dust in the Jade Range was commissioned as a mithril ministry, with its Mistress appointed through the Bourse.

Kallavesa.t: The Healing House of Wittal Grove was commissioned in Kallavesa at 328 thrones, and its senator seconded the Runeforge excavation.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Ossium positions motion and seconded the Lyceum Schloss.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Champions of Virtue titles and seconded the Silver Chalice manifesto amendment.

Madruga.t: The Commonwealth may build a schloss for Lyceum visitors on the island east of Siroc, and the structure is ceded to them.

Miaren.t: Isaella's Dance is to muster at Miaren in the coming summer, and the Runic Hearth of Adamant is meant to protect Miaren from the trogoni. Its senator proposed the Yaw'nagrah investigation.

Miekarova.t: The Thule treaty ceded Miekarova's region of Miechernya to the Thule.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: its senator William Lowther proposed, and received, 230 thrones for materials to enlarge the Drakes.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: its senator seconded the Urizen fortifications appraisal and proposed an Ambassador to the Thule.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the smuggling investigation, receiving 25 thrones for it, and proposed the Ambassador to Axos.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: its senator seconded the withdrawn Britta's Shrine motion and proposed the Ambassador to Jarm.

Ossium.t: Ossium's spoils of war became Varushkan national positions and its Webwood region was ceded to the Thule. Its spy network was decommissioned and emergency repair of the Tower of the Scorpion was allowed.

Redoubt.t: The Architects of Stone at Delving in Redoubt prompted the appraisal of fortifications in Urizen territory, due before Spring 384YE.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the withdrawn Britta's Shrine motion and seconded the Arbor of the Twin Roses.

Sarvos.t: The Sweetwater Springs, a great work of wells and fountains to protect Sarvos against fire, was commissioned at 150 thrones.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy.

Semmerholm.t: The Arbor of the Twin Roses sinecure was commissioned in Semmerholm, but the Manor of the Greenwood and its Greenforest Market expansion failed.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the successful Britta's Memorial motion and seconded the Kauppahall.

Tassato.t: An Imperial Consulate was commissioned in Tassato with 250 thrones.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar is among the territories the Runic Hearth of Adamant is meant to shield from the trogoni. Its senator proposed the Cathedral of the Navigators.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: its senator seconded the Yaw'nagrah investigation and proposed an Ambassador to the Commonwealth.

Upwold.t: Upwold's senator proposed the Thule treaty, and the Runic Hearth of Adamant is meant to protect Upwold from the trogoni.

Volodmartz.t: Mentioned in passing: its senator seconded the Ossium positions motion and proposed the College of Maykop.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Arbor of the Twin Roses and seconded the failed Manor of the Greenwood.

383YE Winter Solstice Synod judgements.d: Rafael Barossa di Tassato's mandate chastising the Wisdom assembly passed, but rival mandates from the Wisdom, Loyalty and Courage assemblies left the matter of mandate opposition unresolved. Several weaker mandates were enacted only because of the ongoing pilgrimage in Imperatrix Lisabetta's name. Other mandates backed the Brass Coast's abandonment of Feroz, Sarvos becoming the City of Masks, wardens and wagon-raiders in Ossium, a Marcher raid on Skallahn, and cooperation with the Grendel in Spiral. Many Whittlefolk were condemned for blasphemy. Yulia was revoked as senator for Miekarova. Finna i Fijadoz i Guerra was vindicated and became High Exorcist, and the virtue fund closed at 60 Thrones.

Dawn.t: Dawnish mandates challenged other nations to a race for the Barrens, rewarded knights fighting to reclaim Dark Ranging, sent knights-errant to join the Varushkan wagon raiders in Ossium, and invited Marracossan refugees to the House of the Proffered Hand in Astolat.

Druj.t: The Druj were the target of crusade calls from League and General Assembly priests, of a contest between Dawn, Highguard and the Imperial Orcs to seize the Barrens, and of mandates to hunt their guerrillas and their Webwood temple in Ossium.

Grendel.t: Urizen urged its citizens to extend the mithril block's protection to Grendel settlements without revealing its workings, and a mandate strengthened by Loyalty told the Urizeni of Spiral to cooperate and trade with the Salt Lord. The Freeborn were urged to abandon Feroz, which had been surrendered to the Grendel.

Highguard.t: Highguard's assembly unanimously accepted Dawn's challenge to race for the Barrens and passed mandates to preserve the Sign of Tamar and to honour Empress Britta's memorial. Isaac of the Silent Tide was appointed Speaker of the Highborn Assembly.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orc priests sent Bloodcrow Udoo to Ossium, reassured the neighbours of the Illarawm, rallied Skarsind's settlers and marked 60 years since Thrace's rebellion. Other assemblies sent orc remains and black lotus potions to the nation, funded mithril for Ethengraw's Armoury, and called for orcs to be admitted to the virtue assemblies.

Jotun.t: The Marches, backed by Wintermark and Navarr mandates and a virtue fund reward for captains to map the territory, prepared a raid on Skallahn. Wintermark priests rejected Jotun honour and Blood on the Snow's bargain, and the Marches urged Mournwold orcs to heed ancestors who did not fight.

Navarr.t: Navarr priests invited the Sand Fishers to walk the trods, sent aid for the Marcher strike against the Jotun and urged Navarr guides to help the Varushkan wardens in Ossium. Harwyn Eternal was appointed Voice of Barbs and vindicated over the Arhallogen deal.

The Brass Coast.t: A Freeborn mandate urged the people to abandon Feroz, while others called refugees to enlist in a new army and sought a new celebration inspired by Zemress. Santana of the Kohan was condemned for heresy, and Finna i Fijadoz i Guerra was inquisited, vindicated and appointed High Exorcist.

The League.t: A League mandate made Sarvos the City of Masks and averted the doom threatening it, and both the League and Wisdom assemblies backed consecrating the gallery above Holberg's Holmauer Gate to Wisdom. Tassato was urged to root out Hatred, and Leonora van Holberg was appointed Patron of the Pavilion.

The Marches.t: Many Whittlefolk, including Little Mournwold's Margret Steward, were condemned for blasphemy in following Hatred. A Marcher mandate prepared a raid on Skallahn, Bregasland fisherfolk were urged to crew raids on Hordalant, and Friar John of the Mourn replaced the revoked Friar of Honour's Rest.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Yulia was revoked for allegedly helping the Thule enslave Jotun thralls, and a later Varushkan statement clarified that the Thule are not enemies of the Empire.

Urizen.t: Urizeni mandates fostered cooperation with the Grendel in Spiral, urged civil debate rather than armed conflict over Sulemaine i Taziel, and encouraged commerce in Redoubt. An intelligence campaign in Zenith was encouraged, but consecrating the Academy of Arms on Mount Siluri failed for want of true liao.

Varushka.t: Varushkan mandates backed the wardens, wagon raiders and native Ossians in Ossium, and the assembly urged the return of enslaved orcs' remains to Skarsind. It also revoked Yulia as senator for Miekarova, condemned the Cabal of the Green Mother and the Heirs of Terunael, and vindicated Nack over the Iron Helms' merciless assault.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark priests commended Isolde Tempest-Shield's work on a sinecure for the nation's armies, praised the heroes fighting the Jotun in Bregasland, and refused support to those who accepted Blood on the Snow's bargain. A mandate sent aid to the Marcher raid, and Maarit Suvidottir became Inquisitor of Courage.

383YE Winter Solstice Synod judgements.o: At the Winter Solstice 383YE summit the Synod raised 127 judgements, chiefly a General Assembly mandate rebuking the Wisdom assembly for urging opposition to Synod mandates, calls for a crusade against the Druj and a contest to claim the Barrens, and the condemnation of the Whittlefolk for following Hatred.

Reikos.t: A Highguard mandate urged chapters near the Sign of Tamar in Reikos to clear the encroaching forest and commit to preserving the historic sigil.

383YE Winter Solstice interlude.d: The Imperial Guerdon of 350 thrones was shared among units supporting the Fist of the Mountain, Tusks, Valiant Pegasus, Winter Sun, Wolves of War and Protect Hercynia. Selling liao to the Axou now earned a full crown. Trade with Asavea suffered under sanctions. Issyk in Axos opened to Imperial traders but under a penalty, and the Kantor penalty was lifted. Robec was closed by the Iron Confederacy, Jarm imposed double tariffs, and the Commonwealth gave extra goods. National mandates affected Highguard, Dawn, Navarr, Varushka, Wintermark, the Brass Coast and anti-idolatry congregations. Four mandates failed because of the Wisdom assembly and the sword scholars.

Dawn.t: Dawnish congregations gained one liao and two votes until the end of the Spring Equinox 384YE. Highborn statements of principle could now come to their attention, under a Highborn mandate seeking understanding between priests and troubadours.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: a failed judgement encouraging citizens to travel to Druj-held Zenith and offer aid there.

Grendel.t: In conquering Feroz, the Grendel claimed the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull. Imperial traders lost the benefit that symbol of Asavean cooperation had given them.

Highguard.t: Highborn could upgrade military units for one less wain of mithril, and their congregations gained liao and votes through closer ties with Dawn. They also lost liao and votes to the call to fight the vallorn, and their businesses lost a rank of production to support purifying Holberg's waters.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark units that raided the Jotun-held Pride of Ikka's Tears were rewarded with a morale bonus.

Navarr.t: Every Navarr herb garden lost two herbs a season for a year to support Good Leaf Gardens in Upwold. Herb gardens and forests in Miaren, Therunin and Hercynia were also fed upon by Tharim after the Conclave accepted his aid.

The Brass Coast.t: After the national assembly backed Efenia i Maristela i Riqueza's mandate urging privateering, Freeborn fleet captains who trade suffer a one-rank production penalty for at least two seasons.

The League.t: Under Rafael Barossa di Tassato's anti-idolatry mandate, congregations in Temeschwar and Tassato gained votes and liao. Highborn businesses, meanwhile, were urged to help purify the cursed waters of Holberg.

The Marches.t: Navarr support created Good Leaf Gardens in Upwold, recognising the Marchers' sacrifice against the vallorn of Liathaven. A mandate encouraging Marcher pilgrims to visit Holberg failed.

Urizen.t: Congregations in Redoubt gained votes and liao for as long as the Synod opposes idolatry. Several rituals were also added to Urizen lore.
