The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast contributed force weight 16. Madruga, which it partly held, saw conjunctions to aid a stranded ship from Sumaah and to claim the Snapping Face.

The League.t: The League contributed force weight 26. Its territories saw conjunctions to intercept mercenaries' pay in Spiral and to kill heralds of Siakha in Tassato.

The Marches.t: The Marches contributed force weight 26. Marcher armies cannot Give Ground but gain extra strength in their home territories, any Imperial army may Billet in Mitwold, Mournwold or Upwold, and conjunctions sought to protect the Maiden Stone and Golden Fields in Mitwold.

Urizen.t: Urizen contributed force weight 13. Herminius's mandate set citizens patrolling the borders of Morrow and Zenith, Urizen armies gain bonuses attacking Zenith from Morrow, and a conjunction in Redoubt sought to leave no more than a dozen Grendel alive.

Varushka.t: Varushka contributed force weight 18. Velko's mandate set citizens patrolling Ossium, where Varushkan armies may take Hospitality of the Boyars, and conjunctions aimed to prevent the cursing of Ossium and destroy the Sumisev Peegel in Volodmartz.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark contributed force weight 65. Its armies may Fight with Honour and gain modifiers against the Jotun, and conjunctions in Kallavesa sought to consecrate the Meeting Place and defeat the Grendel at Frithstan's Fen.

388YE Summer Solstice winds of war.o: The Summer Solstice 388YE Winds of War summarised Imperial military activity, pointing to fuller Winds for Madruga, Mareave, Sarangrave and the Forest of Ulnak. It also set out three possible Sentinel Gate battles, many smaller conjunctions across the Empire and the special rules affecting Imperial armies.

Astolat/Withy.t: A small, low-combat conjunction was to investigate and resolve Igraine's Regio repeatedly shifting back to Spring.

Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest.t: The Fetid Heart was the site of a possible battle opportunity to raid the Druj.

Forest of Ulnak/Gloomsea.t: The Archmage of Day was tasked with stopping the Eyes of the Dragon from using a boon of Kimus at the Islet of Calm.

Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire.t: The Warmage was tasked with exploiting a recent scouting discovery at Moss End.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: Erlend was tasked with consecrating the Meeting Place in a low-combat conjunction.

Kallavesa/Wittal Grove.t: The Grimnir of Wittal Grove was tasked with defeating the Grendel at Frithstan's Fen and possibly rescuing the Iontach.

Madruga/Crucible.t: The Champion of Vigilance was tasked with claiming the Snapping Face at Talpses Plat.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: The Hand of Guerra was tasked with aiding a stranded ship from Sumaah at Hart's Cove.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: The Ruins of Sinat were the site of a possible Sunday battle to open the vaults against the Grendel.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: The Grandmaster of the Silver Chalice was tasked with poisoning the Grendel from a Spring regio near Golden Wind's Encampment.

Mitwold/Maiden Downs.t: Conjunctions aimed to stop Jyll Longleys cursing the Maiden Stone and Dusty Cobb setting Golden Fields alight.

Necropolis/Coursmouth.t: The Guardian of Britta's Memorial was tasked with spilling the waters of Siakha at the Veiled Garden.

Ossium/Echofell.t: The Shadowed Torchbearer was tasked with preventing the cursing of Ossium at the Burned Glade.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Telemachus of the Lighthouse-That-Was was to leave no more than a dozen Grendel alive at Isaac's End.

Reikos/Haros Water.t: Nekoda of the Shattered Tower was to save Professor Gelberg from Grendel assassins at Couros Field.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: Conjunctions were set to drive the vallorn from the Spring Regio and to cast Dance of Navarr and Thorn there.

Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh.t: Theodora and the Spear of the Seven were tasked with casting permanent wards at the Eastern and Western Wards.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: The Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path was tasked with preventing the cursing of Sarangrave at Slow Worm's Hill.

Sarangrave/Turan Flats.t: The Fens of Varreth were the site of a possible battle to contain the dead, and the General of the Eastern Sky was to recover treasure at the Breakteeth dais.

Sarangrave/Whisperwood.t: Conjunctions were set to destroy heralds of Surut at Halfweir Grove and to investigate the Depths of the Hungry Earth.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: The Custodian of the Legacy was tasked with intercepting mercenaries' pay at Alba's Lea.

Tassato/Cascatas.t: The Keeper of the Sapphire Stair was tasked with killing heralds of Siakha at Campo Verdenta.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: The Merchant of the Fangs was tasked with answering General Utmar's call for aid at Saltshore.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Caladain de Renard was to kill the Druj het Prilak Gutdredger. Success would win the knights-errant of The Deepest Vintage to a nominee, while failure would cost the Reeve of Drycastle 10 crowns a season until repaired.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: Lady Aletheia was charged by Skathe's herald with killing the Servants of the Burnt, for a boon or a curse. A separate conjunction sought to stop Druj kidnapping Lenna Karass.

The Barrens/The Untrod Groves.t: The Knight-protector of Winter was tasked with thwarting Ser Gawain Amboise's schemes at the Glade of the Good Knight.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: A newly raised Druj miasma pillar threatened to blanket the region. Andronikos was to destroy it, and Chimes of Annulment, Dreadful Ending or a strength 15 consecration could also end the threat.

Volodmartz/Livardz.t: Auntie Armand Mariyavich Remislav was tasked with destroying the Sumisev Peegel.

Astolat.t: The Senator for Astolat was tasked with a conjunction to discover why Igraine's Regio in Withy kept shifting back to Spring, and to resolve it.

Bregasland.t: The Strong Reeds receive an additional 1000 strength when fighting in Bregasland, then held by the Jotun.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj band threatening Dawnguard burst out of Brocéliande.

Forest of Ulnak.t: The Forest of Ulnak had its own Wind, a possible battle to raid the Druj at the Fetid Heart, and conjunctions in Grimfen Mire and Gloomsea.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa saw conjunctions to consecrate the Meeting Place in West Marsh and to defeat the Grendel in Wittal Grove.

Madruga.t: Madruga had its own Wind, Phantasms and foam, plus conjunctions to aid a stranded Sumaah ship at Free Landing and to claim the Snapping Face in the Crucible.

Mareave.t: Mareave had its own Wind, Mithril and rope, and a possible Sunday battle against the Grendel at the Ruins of Sinat. A conjunction in Fleisardh aimed to poison the Grendel.

Mitwold.t: Conjunctions in Maiden Downs sought to stop the cursing of the Maiden Stone and the burning of Golden Fields. Imperial armies may Billet there, and the Drakes gain strength fighting in Mitwold.

Morrow.t: Citizens patrol Morrow's borders, so the Druj need 25 victory points for a beachhead. Highborn and Urizen armies gain bonuses attacking Zenith from Morrow or defending Morrow against attacks from Zenith.

Mournwold.t: Any Imperial army may Billet in Mournwold, and the Tusks receive an additional 1000 strength when fighting there.

Necropolis.t: The Guardian of Britta's Memorial was tasked with spilling the waters of Siakha at the Veiled Garden in Coursmouth.

Ossium.t: A conjunction sought to prevent the cursing of Ossium. Citizen patrols mean the Druj need 25 victory points for a beachhead, and Varushkan armies may take Hospitality of the Boyars there.

Redoubt.t: Telemachus of the Lighthouse-That-Was was tasked with leaving no more than a dozen Grendel alive at Isaac's End in Naris.

Reikos.t: Nekoda of the Shattered Tower was tasked with saving Professor Gelberg from Grendel assassins at Couros Field in Haros Water.

Sarangrave.t: Sarangrave had its own Wind, Thorn and bone, a possible battle to contain the dead in Turan Flats, and the most conjunctions of any territory, including wards, cursing and the vallorn.

Skarsind.t: An Imperial Orc army may take the Forge Hammers order while in Skarsind.

Spiral.t: The Custodian of the Legacy was tasked with intercepting mercenaries' pay at Alba's Lea in Apstrus.

Tassato.t: The Keeper of the Sapphire Stair was tasked with killing heralds of Siakha at Campo Verdenta in Cascatas.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens faced several conjunctions against Druj raiders, Surut's servants, failed knights-errant and Ser Gawain Amboise. Citizen patrols mean the Druj need 25 victory points to claim a beachhead there.

Therunin.t: A Druj miasma pillar was located in Lower Tarn Valley, and Andronikos of the Lighthouse-That-Was was tasked with destroying it.

Upwold.t: Any Imperial army may Billet in Upwold, and the Bounders receive an additional 1000 strength when fighting there.

Volodmartz.t: Auntie Armand Mariyavich Remislav was tasked with destroying the Sumisev Peegel in Livardz.

Zenith.t: Citizens patrol Zenith's borders, so the Druj need 25 victory points for a beachhead. Highborn and Urizen armies attacking Zenith from Morrow gain bonuses to territory captured.

388YE Winter Solstice interlude.d: The Quartermaster General limited the 350-throne Imperial Guerdon to units supporting the Golden Axe in the Salt Flats of Sanath, the Seventh Wave in Mareave, and the search for the Drakes lost in Crucible. Military units were offered ventures to ward Kroll, aid the Commonwealth and Jarm against Cold Sun, support the Suranni Black Eagle Banner in Reinos, scout or sabotage the scouting of Tsirku, and fight in Spiral. Navarri could treasonously join Agramant's heralds in Therunin. Jakhalsmarkt closed to Imperial fleets after its 70-throne investment went unpaid. The Calvos docks were completed, and enchantments and curses touched Segura, Ossium, Weirwater, Semmerholm, Upwold, Casinea, Spiral and Mareave.

Dawn.t: Dawnish units could protect the vales of Varushka, gained bonuses fighting for Jarm and an extra two ingots of green iron with the Black Eagle Banner, and could fight in Spiral. At home Weirwater was enchanted with Night magic and Semmerholm was cursed.

Druj.t: Navarri allied with Agramant's heralds sought to retake the nominally Druj-controlled regions of Therunin, while Imperial units earned Guerdon shares supporting the Golden Axe in the Druj-held Salt Flats of Sanath.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but it shares Mareave, where the Seventh Wave fought and where Rivers of Life and other rituals were cast.

Highguard.t: Highborn units received a one-rank bonus for aiding the Commonwealth against Cold Sun. Pilgrims were urged to travel to Bastion to help build the Grand Inspiration, and Casinea was enchanted with a song spreading across the trods.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orc-held Mareave was blessed with Rivers of Life and protected by Frozen Citadel rituals in three regions and Ramparts of Ashlar at Rucraic's Redoubt. Units supporting the Seventh Wave there shared the Guerdon.

Jotun.t: Imperial units were invited to support the Suranni Black Eagle Banner in a wider effort to conquer Jotun-held Reinos. The Tsirku scouts also sought details of any significant Jotun presence in the wastes.

Navarr.t: Navarri could join Dochas Weeping Glade and Agramant's heralds to reconquer Therunin, an act of treason, and Navarr units faced no penalty searching for the Drakes. Navarr forests in Ossium also suffered the Dubik's bloody harvest.

The Brass Coast.t: The completed Municipal Docks of Calvos gave every Freeborn seven extra rings a season, cheaper fleet upgrades and stronger fleets in Madruga. Freeborn fleets could hunt the Free Landing kraken, and Segura was enchanted towards becoming the City of Wonders.

The League.t: League units were sought by both the Commonwealth and Jarm and could fight in Spiral, which was also enchanted with Hand of the Dhomiro. Temeschwari congregations could preach Pride for their city, and Leaguers could convert resources to businesses for free.

The Marches.t: Marchers rallied to rescue the Drakes lost in Crucible. Mournwold suffered disruption from the Rebellion's Ridge consecration, Upwold's forges were enchanted to speed a new army, and Marchers could convert resources to farms for free.

Thule.t: A Thule coven performed a Summer ritual on Ossium at the Lord of the Aurorae's offer to improve the Jaws of Winter Lightning. The Imperial scouts of Tsirku sought details of any significant Thule presence and links to Otkodov.

Urizen.t: Urizen could send units to secure Kroll's lair so the creature could be warded with ilium and later called to defend the region. Urizen units were also favoured by Jarm and fought in Spiral, and the Walls of Cargo in Limus were strengthened.

Varushka.t: Varushkans protecting the vales received potions of the deep wood, while Ossium's forests were plagued by the Dubik and the territory was enchanted with Summer magic. Varushkan units escaped the cold penalty in Tsirku.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark units faced no cold penalty scouting Tsirku, where the Mediator of Hyljehal had secured the hylje's aid. Hahnmark herbalists could cultivate Draaikolkbloem, and West Marsh in Kallavesa was enchanted by the Sussivari Frost Coven.

388YE Winter Solstice interlude.o: The interlude after the Autumn Equinox 388YE set out the downtime opportunities and effects for the coming season. These included new ventures for military units, fleets and congregations, the completion of the Calvos docks, the closure of Jakhalsmarkt, and a range of enchantments and curses across the Empire.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: Ottermire received Dripping Echoes of the Fen twice, including once from the Circle of Zulgan-Tash.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: West Marsh was enchanted with Dripping Echoes of the Fen by the Sussivari Frost Coven.

Madruga/Crucible.t: The Drakes remained lost in Crucible's transformative marshes. The strength of the rescue would decide whether they escaped by the Winter Solstice and how many soldiers they lost, from 2,000 strength down to none.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Freeborn fleets could hunt Free Landing's juvenile kraken for money and ambrellic, with the Magpies earning extra treasure through the Wraith King's crew.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: Clisearn was protected with Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae by the Ashen Flame coven.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: Rucraic's Redoubt in Eoradal was strengthened with Ramparts of Ashlar by the Concordium of Pallas.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Icarion was protected with Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae by the Ashen Flame coven.

Mareave/Nadir.t: Nadir was protected with Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae by the Phoenix Rising coven.

Necropolis/Coursmouth.t: Reumah's Rest in Coursmouth received Ramparts of Ashlar from the Concordium of Pallas.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Mentioned in passing: a ritual named Arc of Sküld was raised and funded for Imperial Lore by Yarvi Swiftwind for the Silver Chalice.

Redoubt/Limus.t: The Walls of Cargo in Limus received Ramparts of Ashlar from the Concordium of Pallas.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: Urizen units needed 7,500 strength to secure Kroll's lair so that seven rings of ilium could seal the creature until Urizen magicians called it to defend the region.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: Nesustak Forest was enchanted with Forge the Wooden Fastness by the Coven of the Horned Hare.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: The Tower of the Skink in Thornfen received Bells of Silver and Brass from the Concordium of Pallas.

Spiral/Screed.t: Three seasons of fighting removed the penalty that Screed's malignancy had imposed on military units.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: Members of the Apothecaries' Guild with physick or apothecary skills could help cleanse the valley's poison, needing at least 30 to make headway. The Gardens of High Chalcis covered the cost this season.

Bastion.t: Congregations across the Empire could encourage pilgrims to travel to Bastion and contribute labour towards completing the Grand Inspiration of the Way.

Bregasland.t: Ottermire in Bregasland received Dripping Echoes of the Fen twice, one casting by the Circle of Zulgan-Tash.

Casinea.t: Casinea was enchanted with a magnitude 40 Night ritual, spreading dreams of the song Founders' Dance, especially among those walking or camping near the trods.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark's herb garden owners could work with the Zuredruiven vintners to grow two drams of Draaikolkbloem at the cost of other herbs.

Kallavesa.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven cast Dripping Echoes of the Fen on West Marsh in Kallavesa.

Madruga.t: The Drakes remained lost in Crucible awaiting rescue, Freeborn fleets could hunt the Free Landing kraken, and the completed Calvos docks gave Freeborn fleets in Madruga an extra rank.

Mareave.t: Rivers of Life infused Mareave's waters with Spring power and reduced army casualties. Frozen Citadel was cast on Icarion, Clisearn and Nadir, Ramparts of Ashlar was cast on Rucraic's Redoubt, and units supporting the Seventh Wave there shared the Guerdon.

Mournwold.t: With Rebellion's Ridge consecrated to Pride, all personal resources in the Mournwold suffered a two-rank penalty, but its mine owners would elect the next senator.

Necropolis.t: Reumah's Rest in Coursmouth was strengthened with Ramparts of Ashlar by the Concordium of Pallas.

Ossium.t: Ossium's forests suffered a one-rank penalty from the Dubik but yielded blackblood thorns or bloodvine liquor, though Kurstrozi's Lumbermill was safe. A Thule coven's magnitude 80 Summer ritual made Summer encounters more common there.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tsirku scouts hoped to learn of any connections between Tsirku and Otkodov.

Redoubt.t: The Walls of Cargo in Limus were strengthened with Ramparts of Ashlar by the Concordium of Pallas.

Reinos.t: The Suranni Black Eagle Banner under General Hendrick marched into Reinos as part of a larger effort to conquer it, inviting Imperial units to join. Sending purely magical troops would cause a diplomatic incident.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Military units supporting the Golden Axe in the Salt Flats of Sanath were among those sharing the Imperial Guerdon this season.

Sarangrave.t: Urizen could secure Kroll's lair for warding, the Coven of the Horned Hare cast Forge the Wooden Fastness on Nesustak Forest, and the Tower of the Skink in Thornfen received Bells of Silver and Brass.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the scouts suspected the western region of Tsirku might connect to the Sea of Snow, allowing sea beasts to reach the Grave of the Giants.

Segura.t: A magnitude 80 Night ritual infused the fountain of Anduz and aligned the old city's three great structures into the City of Wonders. The Firebrand, Hawker and Trailblazer archetypes would soon become available.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm was cursed with a magnitude 27 Autumn ritual embodying Things Go Awry, with effects obvious to all in the territory.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is not named, though the Mediator of Hyljehal secured the hylje's aid for the Tsirku scouts.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tsirku scouts hoped to learn of any connections between Tsirku and Skallahn.

Spiral.t: Sustained attacks by Urizen, League and Dawnish units beat back the horrors of the Black Plateau and removed the Screed malignancy penalty, and the venture continued indefinitely. Hand of the Dhomiro also guided those fleeing or travelling past enemy patrols.

Temeschwar.t: With Virtue's Respite remade and the Pride of Temeschwar standing by a river gate, Temeschwari congregations could preach Pride in the city's honour for extra Synod votes.

Therunin.t: With the Golden Axe gone, Dochas Weeping Glade and Agramant's heralds offered Navarri a treasonous chance to retake Druj-held regions. Apothecaries could also work to cleanse the poison of the Lower Tarn Valley.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Spymaster directed the Tsirku scouts westwards towards Tromsa and sought any connections to it.

Tsirku.t: Scouts were sent to explore Tsirku's western region with the hylje's help, needing 2,400 strength for any useful findings. The Whisper Gallery paid units to sabotage the effort.

Upwold.t: The Cabal Lyktan invoked the Hammers of Fury to speed mustering a new army in Upwold, cutting each mine's ingots by two in exchange for warm ashes.

Weirwater.t: A magnitude 80 Night ritual filled Weirwater with mysterious twilight music that stirs memories of love and friendship, making Night encounters and heralds of Sung and Janon more common.

A Blight in Miaren.d: Navarr walking the trods of Miaren reported sudden blights of Armillaria, a white, furry fungus suspected of being altered by the realm of Spring. It aggressively attacks marrowort, harming herb gardens, but acts as a natural medicinal for livestock, improving farm productivity. The fungus is fragile, lasting only until the Summer Solstice and unlikely to spread beyond adjacent territories, and worldblood (ambergelt) is toxic to it. The civil service set out several options: Senate motions to harvest the fungus for livestock or deliberately spread it to neighbouring territories, a Conclave gambit of ambergelt to kill it, approaching the Eternal Llofir, or using the ritual Ruthless Vigilance, Healthy Crop. Mari, Archmage of Day, rallied the Conclave to gather ambergelt and destroy the infestation.

Navarr.t: Navarr trod-walkers first reported the blight in their territory of Miaren, threatening Navarr herb gardens' marrowort while offering a temporary boon to their farms before the Conclave's ambergelt destroyed the fungus.

A Blight in Miaren.o: In Spring 379YE a blight of Armillaria, a Spring-touched parasitic fungus that attacks marrowort but benefits livestock, broke out across the herb gardens of Miaren. The Conclave, rallied by Mari, Archmage of Day, gathered ambergelt to destroy the fungus.

Miaren.t: Armillaria fungus spread through Miaren's herb gardens, threatening marrowort yields while potentially benefiting local livestock, until the Conclave gathered ambergelt to eliminate the blight and both its harms and benefits.

A Crown in Winter.d: Raised on a pumpkin farm in Srodkoja, Vesna joined the Wardens of the Grateful Hearth and served two terms as senator for Ossium, extending the Iron Roads. She faced inquisition over the Winter 383YE treaty with the Thule, without further resolution. No veto was sought in time, so the Constitutional Court confirmed she would take the Throne at the first Senate session, first ratifying her own election. Planned celebrations included a timed tour of the nations, national presentations, a dedication to Prosperity by Ophelia Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato, and a crowning by Belakov Zakharovich Prochnost. The Commonwealth, Faraden, Axos, Otkodov and Sarcophan said they would send representatives with gifts.

Dawn.t: The Empress's tour would reach the Dawnish at 14:50, and Dawn would make the second formal presentation at the coronation ceremony.

Highguard.t: Highguard would be the second nation visited on the tour, at 13:40, and would give the third presentation to the new Throne.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs would welcome the Empress at 14:20 and present fourth. Emperor Ahraz's coronation during the Orc Rebellion was recalled as a precedent for celebrating even in wartime.

Navarr.t: The Navarr would welcome the Empress at 14:30 and give the seventh formal presentation.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast would be the final stop on the tour, at 15:00, and would open the national presentations at the ceremony.

The League.t: The League would welcome the Empress at 14:10 and present fifth, and Ophelia Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato of the League would perform the coronation's dedication to Prosperity.

The Marches.t: The Marches would receive the Empress at 14:00 and give the sixth presentation at the ceremony.

Thule.t: Vesna's part in the Winter 383YE treaty with the Thule led to her being called before an inquisition, and Thule-held Otkodov planned to send a representative to acknowledge her accession.

Urizen.t: Urizen would be the third nation on the tour, at 13:50, and would give the eighth presentation.

Varushka.t: A Varushkan from Srodkoja and former senator for Ossium became Empress-elect, crowned by Belakov Zakharovich Prochnost with an anthem by Kalina Jadwigowna Piosnkowa Prochnost. Her tour would begin in Varushka at 13:30, and Varushka would give the ninth presentation.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark would welcome the Empress at 14:40 and give the final national presentation at the ceremony.

A Crown in Winter.o: The Senate elected Varushkan senator Vesna Borkovna Prochnost as the twenty-first Empress in Autumn 385YE, and an Assembly of Nine veto was unanimously voted down. Her coronation was set for the Winter Solstice summit, with a tour of the nations, national presentations and gifts from foreign dignitaries.

Miekarova/Srodkoja.t: Srodkoja was Vesna's home: the youngest of seven children, she grew up on a pumpkin farm in its woods before joining the Wardens of the Grateful Hearth.

Miekarova.t: The new Empress-elect was raised in Miekarova, on a pumpkin farm in the woods of its region of Srodkoja.

Otkodov.t: The government of Otkodov, then held by the Thule, said it would send a representative to Anvil to acknowledge the new Empress.

A Miracle in Hahnmark.d: Miners in Hahnmark's weltsilver mines reported warm, enjoyable sensations when working the ore, greatly increasing productivity. Religious zeal and congregation attendance rose, but other businesses complained of losing workers to the mines. Some speculated the auras stemmed from a forgotten Wintermark Paragon of Prosperity, sparking debate over whether they were Kallavesi, Steinr or Suaq. The civil service offered options including a recruitment subsidy for businesses, spreading the effect to all mines, missionary work to an adjacent territory, or a controversial exorcism. A General Assembly judgement of Rewarding sent Jorma Steelhail to spread word to Skarsind, and a Prosperity Assembly judgement sent Soratio Seseer Del Toro so that all mines in the affected territories would benefit.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: a historical Cardinal of the Way, an Urizen Illuminate suspected of Lucidianism, is cited as having once called for the exorcism of a spontaneous aura of Ambition.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's mining territories gained a miraculous boost to mine output and congregational influence, and the auras prompted speculation about a forgotten Wintermark Paragon of Prosperity, with debate over whether they were Kallavesi, Steinr or Suaq.

A Miracle in Hahnmark.o: In spring 379YE, weltsilver mines in Hahnmark spontaneously generated auras of Prosperity that made mining feel deeply rewarding, boosting mine output and congregations while drawing labour away from other businesses. The Synod responded by spreading the miracle to Skarsind and extending its benefit to all mines.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark's weltsilver mines became the source of spontaneous Prosperity auras, raising mine productivity and congregation attendance, though local businesses complained of losing labour to the mines; a Prosperity Assembly judgement sought to extend the benefit to all mines there.

Skarsind.t: Through a General Assembly judgement of Rewarding, Jorma Steelhail was charged with spreading word of the miracle to neighbouring Skarsind so that it too would share in the effect.

A Sparrow in Spring.d: The Senate could name one person, by a single motion, to organise celebrations with Imperial funds, Synod Virtue fund money and private donations. Grand celebrations cost 80 thrones, breath-taking ones 250 and wondrous ones 500. The scale set the benefit, while the Throne's short celebratory message set its nature, as when Empress Lisabetta's 500-throne festivities and her plea to stem the tide of Imperial blood let every army launch a steady conquest. Empress Vesna also had to ratify her own election and the creation of the Citizen's Voice. She could appoint the Captain of the Throne Guard and the Queen's Rose, and had to decide whether to seek the vacant title of Monarch of Dawn.

Dawn.t: Dawnish weavers were booked up with orders for fine garments, the new Empress could appoint the long-vacant Queen's Rose, and she had to decide whether to claim the vacant title of Monarch of Dawn. Any such claim would rely wholly on Dawnish nobles fighting for her in the tourney.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League's cities were recalled as transformed into wonderlands during Empress Lisabetta's coronation celebrations.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: breath-taking celebrations would include magical lights imported from Urizen, and past festivities had linked its spires with bridges of magical glass.

Varushka.t: The new Empress was a Varushkan, and wealthy Varushkans were determined that her celebrations would be as magnificent as those of the Merchant Prince of Holberg. The page noted the recent closeness between Varushka and Dawn, whose armies fought side by side to conquer Ossium.

A Sparrow in Spring.o: After the Senate chose Senator Vesna Borkovna Prochnost as the new Empress, citizens across the Empire, especially in Ossium, began preparing to celebrate. The Senate had the opportunity to fund coronation festivities that, with a clear inaugural address, could leave a lasting legacy.

Bay of Catazar.t: Merchants on the Bay of Catazar had begun importing consignments of wine, beer, brandy and mead in anticipation of the festivities.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushkans hoped to match the Prosperity shown for Empress Lisabetta, the Merchant Prince of Holberg.

Ossium.t: Excitement ran highest in Ossium, where every town and vale was preparing to celebrate the new Empress. The territory had been conquered by Varushkan and Dawnish armies fighting side by side.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: donations after Emperor James's coronation went much of the way towards repairing the Tower of the Dawn in the Barrens.

A banner of Thorns.d: With the Black Thorns fighting alone in southern Liathaven, the wind offered four opportunities. The Senate could enlarge the army using arriving volunteers. A Synod statement could grant supporting warbands a bonus if both the Black Thorns and the Quiet Step attacked in Liathaven. Navarr generals could issue the ruthless 'An Enduring Example' order. A strike on a gate could open the hidden Paths of Lan Thúven through the vallorn. At the Summer Solstice the Navarr liberated the Paths. Corey Brackensong led the Navarr Assembly's call for unity, but the two armies fought in different territories. The Senate began the two-season enlargement, with 50 mithril and 10 thrones still owed. General Ulric Y'Basden ordered the Black Thorns to become the dark beneath the trees.

Jotun.t: The Jotun, who had purged the Navarr of Liathaven, faced a growing resistance. They lost control of the Lan Thúven gates and suffered General Ulric Y'Basden's merciless 'Enduring Example' campaign, though fleeing warriors reinforced Jotun armies beyond Liathaven.

Navarr.t: The Navarr rallied to the Black Thorns and seized the Paths of Lan Thúven, giving their armies passage across the vallorn. The Senate began enlarging the Black Thorns, and the National Assembly issued a call for unity to retake Liathaven.

A banner of Thorns.o: In Summer 380YE the Black Thorns' fight to liberate Liathaven from the Jotun drew Navarr survivors and volunteers to their banner, and the nation was offered several opportunities to press the campaign. The Navarr seized the hidden Paths of Lan Thúven, began enlarging the Black Thorns and waged a merciless campaign against the orcs.

Liathaven/Liath's Ring.t: Mentioned in passing: there was no news from Liath's Ring in northern Liathaven.

Liathaven/Liaven's Glen.t: Mentioned in passing: there was no news from Liaven's Glen in northern Liathaven.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: West Ranging holds the northern Gate of Lan Thúven near the destroyed Silent Stand steading, once guarded by a Jotun warband. With the Paths liberated, Navarr armies could treat it as adjacent to Western Scout.

Liathaven/Western Scout.t: Western Scout, on the edge of the vallorn, holds the southern Gate of Lan Thúven by the ruins of Hidden Walk steading, once guarded by an isolated Jotun warband. It became the southern end of the Navarr route through the vallorn.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: Mentioned in passing: the Hidden Walk Navarr once used the hidden path to travel deep into the Westwood.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: Hordalant, to the west, was noted as holding unknown numbers of orcs who might strike at the Black Thorns.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman was noted as hosting major Jotun forces to the east that might be sent against the Black Thorns.

Liathaven.t: Liathaven was the focus of the Navarr liberation campaign. The Black Thorns fought ruthlessly in the south, began their enlargement there, and gained the hidden Paths of Lan Thúven linking the territory's north and south across the vallorn.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step was fighting in the Mournwold, which was noted as holding major Jotun forces, while many Navarr urged that army to turn to Liathaven instead.

A beacon of smoke.d: Treachery from within Siroc and Naguerro battle-magic brought down the Salt Guard's chains and twin keeps, despite Autumn enchantments, a Freeborn warband and the Commonwealth Embassy garrison. The Grendel looted Siroc, then the Asaveans burned it and murdered captured priests. Friends of the Prince of a Thousand Foes led many people, including the Kindled Flame's orphans, to safety. Quzar, the Parador of Salt and Sand, Atalaya, Midport and the Shining Pillar fell, and the Lyceum came under siege. Madruga lost its Senator and several titles lost their ministries. Solstice opportunities were offered to raise the Lyceum's wards, save the Shining Pillar and counter Grendel raids elsewhere.

Grendel.t: Their armada of four navies and several armies, including the Iron Gulls, Black Eels, Bone Nautilus and Governor Rahab's troops, took Siroc Plains, Lightsea and Free Landing, looting the Sapphire and besieging the Lyceum. Their captains also launched probing raids across the Bay.

Highguard.t: Grendel Sky Mage Ranald, who escaped the purge of an espionage ring in Necropolis, was moving through Coursmouth to uncover a secret guarded by the chapter of Ethan's Respite. The Champion of Courage, Thomir, Son of Astion, was charged with stopping him.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn lost Siroc, Lightsea and Free Landing, along with the Shining Pillar, the Freeborn Flame Marina and several ministries, and Madruga's Senate seat. Short of the prosperous coastal regions, their armies would begin to decline after the Winter Solstice.

The League.t: The Salt Guard, designed by Menno van Ritsjhof, was destroyed. Grendel raiders under Quartermaster Ewan threatened Glass Point Cove in Sarvos, and the Sarvos Shipwrights Syndicate offered fleet deeds in return for salvaging defeated Grendel ships.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marches are not named on the page. The nearest related matter is the destruction of the Commonwealth Embassy in Siroc and the Ambassador to the Commonwealth losing their ministry.

Urizen.t: Maistir Dorcas landed in Naris to threaten the Great Harbour of Elos, and the Elosian Architect, Talia Seaboar, was offered the fleet deed to The Impulse for stopping them. A recovered Final Dance of the Immobile could also be added to Urizen lore.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the iron chains and nets that guarded Siroc's harbour had been imported centuries ago from the forges of Wintermark.

A beacon of smoke.o: When the two-year peace treaty expired, the Grendel armada, backed by Asavean warships, broke the Salt Guard and sacked and burned Siroc. It went on to seize Lightsea and Free Landing, leaving Madruga contested and the Brass Coast unable to supply its armies.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Mentioned in passing: it is listed as one of the prosperous coastal regions, two of which the Freeborn would need to regain to supply their armies again.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Mentioned in passing: it is listed as one of the prosperous coastal regions whose recovery would help restore Freeborn army supply.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Mentioned in passing: it is listed as one of the prosperous coastal regions whose recovery would help restore Freeborn army supply.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: It remained in Freeborn hands, as the Salt Guard's resistance slowed the armada too much to attack it. Holding Calvos is essential to the Brass Coast's hopes of resupplying its armies.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: The Grendel seized Atalaya, Midport and the Shining Pillar, whose beacon went out, and besieged the Lyceum. Battles were offered to raise the Lyceum's wards, rescue the Beacon's Watch and stop an Asavean sacrifice.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: Grendel forces overran Lightsea, taking Quzar and looting the Parador of Salt and Sand. Sand Mage Nechtan waited at Ezmara's Thicket to escape with a stolen hakima heirloom.

Madruga/Torres.t: Mentioned in passing: Torres is noted as one of only two Madrugan regions still under Freeborn control.

Necropolis/Coursmouth.t: Sky Mage Ranald's company was moving through Coursmouth towards Ada's Plain, with the Sentinel Gate opening to Hedra's Meadow.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Maistir Dorcas landed on the Naris coast and left a guard at the ships while hurrying toward Elos. The Sentinel Gate was to open to the Elosian Grove.

Sarvos/Uccelini.t: Quartermaster Ewan landed on a wooded Uccelini island with servants of the Salt-born Devourer, sending a vanguard ahead to Glass Point Cove. The Sentinel Gate was to open to the Isle of Quiet.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Grendel armada and Asavean warships swept across the Bay to strike Madruga, and individual Grendel captains raided targets around its shores. With the Shining Pillar dark, the Bay lost its familiar beacon.

Feroz.t: Governor Rahab's honour guard sailed from Grendel-held Feroz to join the assault and looted the Glass Parador. The earlier loss of Feroz helped leave the Brass Coast unable to supply its armies.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is not named; Wintermark appears only as the source of Siroc's old harbour chains.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Iñez i Azul-Mar i Erigo of Kahraman, captain of the Bloodgold Jackals, is listed in the Freeborn force table.

Madruga.t: Siroc was razed and left in ruins, and the Grendel took three of the territory's six regions. Madruga became contested and lost its Senator, though the Lyceum's wards and the Shining Pillar might yet be saved.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is not named anywhere on the page.

Necropolis.t: With its defenders watching the coast, Sky Mage Ranald's reduced company was heading for Ada's Plain and the Courspan Bridge. The Champion of Courage was asked to intercept them.

Redoubt.t: Grendel under Maistir Dorcas, accompanied by heralds of the Mother of Wrecks, were marching on the shipyards and warehouses of Elos.

Sarvos.t: Grendel raiders threatened Glass Point Cove and its mithril netting. The Sarvos Shipwrights Syndicate agreed to salvage captured Grendel ships in return for granting fleet deeds.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: refugees from Siroc, including the orphans of the Parador of the Kindled Flame, fled west across the Scorrero toward Segura.

A better future.d: The Prince Mila School of the Belligerent Art, a Maykop–Jarm collaboration, was closed after Fintan Nighthaven's protest. Axos blamed Maxatios, though the civil service judged him a scapegoat and Skopos a likely ally of Grand Ilarch Kyther's unity movement. Several sects formed a Unified Convocation at Solokha. Kantor now trades Sable and Blackened Key instead of orichalcum, and Issyk has reopened to Imperial fleets with Axou esoterica. Maykop offered the Conclave a chance to codify a Winter ritual. Further items were a request for students to visit the Great Library of Hacynian, a visiting memory-doctor, two missing merchants, and an Ipotavo emissary seeking General Gabriel Barossa.

Druj.t: The Druj had captured the Axou agema Menoetius of Issyk to make him a tortured soul, but Imperial heroes rescued him. Fintan Nighthaven's assurance that the Empire means to destroy the Druj was warmly received in Axos.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the House of Spirits in Highguard-held Casinea is run by Mistress Isephenia of Maykop and Rinnah of the Shattered Tower, the Bursar of the House of Spirits.

Navarr.t: Fintan Nighthaven of Navarr, the Ambassador to Axos, exposed the treaty breach and was publicly thanked by the Grand Council for his advice. He also promised that Therunin would be recovered from the Druj.

A better future.o: In Summer 387YE Ambassador Fintan Nighthaven exposed an Axou war-magic school run with Jarm in breach of the Liberty Pact. Axos forced Ilarch Maxatios to resign as their ambassador, formed a formal Grand Council and appointed Ilarch Kario Skopos of Solokha in his place.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is home to the House of Spirits, run by Mistress Isephenia and the Bursar Rinnah, whose students now seek a season at the Great Library of Hacynian.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Mentioned in passing: Fintan Nighthaven assured Axos that the Salt Flats of Sanath would one day be freed from the Buruk Tepel.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Fintan Nighthaven assured Axos that the Sarangrave would one day be freed from the Buruk Tepel.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Fintan Nighthaven told Axos that the Empire would recover Therunin from the Druj.

A big sleep.d: Interrogations after the Summer Solstice raid led to warrants against lower-tier vyig agents and sympathisers, and within weeks vyig operations in Sarvos, along with other criminal enterprises, were shut down. Militia recruitment surged as fear of the vyig waned. Only Livueta Garovich di Sarvos, a brutal lieutenant of "Uncle Sarvos", escaped and remains wanted. Seized assets, two businesses, a farm and a forest, were offered to League citizens. The Vigilance assembly then named Vladimir von Temeschwar (Holberg), Valimir von Temeschwar (Tassato) and Irada von Temeschwar (Temeschwar) to lead campaigns funded with liao. All three chose active opposition, which significantly damages the vyig but cuts business production in those cities by a quarter.

The League.t: League heroes and magistrates broke the vyig in Sarvos and launched a campaign against them in the other three cities, though at the cost of disrupted trade in Holberg, Tassato and Temeschwar.

A big sleep.o: After League citizens struck at a vyig gathering in Sarvos during the Summer Solstice, the magistrates and a swelling militia dismantled vyig operations in the city, and at the Autumn Equinox the Vigilance assembly appointed three priests to lead active opposition to the vyig in Holberg, Tassato and Temeschwar.

Holberg.t: Vladimir von Temeschwar of the Brotherhood of the Ashen Tower was appointed to lead active opposition to the vyig in the city, significantly damaging vyig activity while cutting all business production there by a quarter.

Sarvos.t: Vyig operations in the Jewelled City were brought to a close, militia enthusiasm surged, and seized vyig assets were put up for auction. Livueta Garovich di Sarvos remains at large under an outstanding warrant.

Tassato.t: Valimir von Temeschwar of the Red Tower was appointed to lead active opposition to the vyig in Tassato, significantly damaging vyig activity but disrupting business production there by a quarter.

Temeschwar.t: Irada von Temeschwar was appointed to lead active opposition to the vyig in Temeschwar, where the vyig were expected to be hardest to dislodge, and businesses there lost a quarter of their production through the disruption.

A bit of peace.d: About a dozen Jotun, led by the old Jarl Ustigar with the Hierro orcs Kenza and Juevar, travelled openly to Anvil as guests of Liissá of Sigehold, bound for a meeting with Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra. Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-United would return to negotiate before the Thule peace treaty ended, refusing to discuss surrendering the Silver Peaks or Krevsaty. He complained that Thule archaeologists had been ordered out of Hercynia and that a Navarr deal over Sküld was imperilled. The Great Forest orcs, still settling Therunin, planned an informal visit bearing gifts. With unnamed allies, they and briar humans freed Dawnish prisoners from the Barrens and led them through Peytaht to Reikos.

Druj.t: Dawnish captives escaped from a Druj labour camp in the Barrens, and the Druj did not follow them into the Great Forest of Peytaht. The freed prisoners told harrowing tales of Druj cruelty and back-breaking work under malicious overseers.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Reikos took in more than a hundred and fifty freed Dawnish captives at Remember Exile. The senator for Reikos was to receive gifts from the Great Forest orcs in thanks for herbs provided to them.

Jotun.t: Having invaded Sermersuaq, the Jotun sent a delegation of about a dozen under a flag of truce to Anvil, led by Jarl Ustigar with the Hierro orcs Kenza and Juevar. They came as guests of Liissá of Sigehold to meet the Jarl of the Golden People.

Navarr.t: Rak said the Dragons were disappointed that Thule archaeologists had been told to leave Hercynia, which imperilled an agreement allowing the Navarr to dance the Dance of Navarr and Thorn in Sküld. He urged the Navarr to send a good-faith negotiator, naming Merel. Meanwhile the Navarr in Therunin were learning to live alongside the Great Forest orcs.

Thule.t: Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-United was to return to Anvil to seek a new treaty before the existing one ended at the Summer Solstice. The Dragons refused to discuss giving up the Silver Peaks or Krevsaty, and had recalled their archaeologists from Hercynia.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk watchers in Hahnmark let the Jotun truce delegation pass unmolested, honouring the law protecting delegations. This was despite the Jotun having invaded Sermersuaq.

A bit of peace.o: In spring 382YE a Jotun delegation under a flag of truce walked south from Sermersuaq towards Anvil, while the Thule, the Great Forest orcs and their briar allies all announced visits of their own. The Great Forest orcs also delivered more than a hundred and fifty Dawnish captives freed from a Druj labour camp to Reikos.

Hahnmark/Southridge.t: From a tower in Southridge, a Winterfolk captain stopped a young warrior from shooting at the passing Jotun envoys. She upheld the law and the spirit of truce.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: The Dragons' agreement to let the Navarr perform the Dance of Navarr and Thorn in a suitable regio in Sküld was left severely imperilled.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The Thule declared the Silver Peaks ancestral land that they would not surrender. They warned that any demand to quit them would wreck the negotiations.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: More than a hundred and fifty yeofolk and a handful of nobles from the houses of Dawnguard were freed from Druj captivity. Most hoped to rejoin their houses-in-exile.

Casinea.t: The Thule declared that Krevsaty, ancestral land returned to them under the earlier treaty, was not up for negotiation. Any Imperial demand that they quit it would end the talks in failure.

Hahnmark.t: The Jotun delegation walked openly south through Hahnmark under a flag of truce. Its Winterfolk watchers chose to let them pass and report to their Thane.

Hercynia.t: At the Empire's request, all Thule visitors to Hercynia were recalled to Otkodov. They had believed they had leave to recover culturally significant items there.

Otkodov.t: The Dragons of Otkodov sent Rak back to Anvil to continue peace negotiations. They expressed disappointment at the revoked Hercynia agreement.

Reikos.t: Over a hundred and fifty freed Dawnish yeofolk and some nobles arrived at Remember Exile in Reikos, escorted by Great Forest orcs and briar humans. Its senator was due to receive Great Forest gifts at Anvil.

Sermersuaq.t: The Jotun had invaded Sermersuaq, and their truce delegation set out south from there. The Thule insisted they would not give up the Silver Peaks.

The Barrens.t: Dawnish captives were liberated from a Druj labour camp in the Barrens during the Winter Solstice and led away through Peytaht.

Therunin.t: The Great Forest orcs continued settling in Therunin alongside the Navarr, settling occasional problems by arbitration. Their work on the Holt of the Oak was slow for lack of weirwood and money, and about two dozen freed yeofolk went back with them.

A blessing in disguise.d: Lilith of the Chantry carried the mandate across Highguard, and thousands prepared to walk the trods. The civil service estimated that every Highborn farm and business would lose 72 rings of income and every military unit two ranks, with the penalties lasting at least ten years. Any nation except Highguard could pass a mandate, with 50 liao (25 for Navarr and Urizen), to offer pilgrims food, shelter and protection. Each supporting nation would take half the penalty, and each additional nation would shorten the adjustment period, down to one season with eight or more. The planned fourth Highborn army had to be abandoned, but veterans could enlarge one existing army for 100 mithril and 25 thrones if the Senate approved. All options were valid only at the Autumn Equinox 382YE.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, but the page notes Highborn armies recently bled defending Urizeni lands in Zenith and Morrow.

Highguard.t: Highborn citizens set out on a vast pilgrimage at a ruinous projected cost of 72 rings per farm and business and two ranks per military unit, and their planned fourth army was abandoned. They could instead enlarge an existing army with eager veterans if the Senate approved it that season.

Navarr.t: Navarr, who understand the vallorn and migratory life better than anyone, could endorse the support mandate for only 25 liao, with wayhouses welcoming the pilgrims, at the cost of 36 rings per farm and business and one rank per military unit.

Urizen.t: Urizen, grateful for Highborn armies bleeding in defence of Zenith and Morrow, could endorse the support mandate for only 25 liao, with stargazers finding safe routes for pilgrims, at the cost of 36 rings per farm and business and one rank per military unit.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark, like any non-Highborn nation, could pass the support mandate, and its halls are suggested as places that might take pilgrims in and offer them seats by the fire.

A blessing in disguise.o: After the Highborn Assembly upheld Kerem, Daughter of the Chantry's mandate calling citizens to an extended pilgrimage on the trods against the vallorn, the civil service judged the cost ruinous. Other national assemblies were offered the chance to share the burden by supporting the pilgrims, and Highguard was offered a cheaper way to enlarge an existing army.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is cited as a land where Highborn armies recently bled defending Urizen, which inclines some Urizeni to support the pilgrims.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Zenith is cited as a land where Highborn armies recently bled in defence of Urizen.

A box for a sword.d: The Waning Circle bought out the Street of Grains and will buy weirwood, mithril and white granite through Ephisis' Scale, with prices dropping as more wains are offered. Ilium prices are withheld until after the ilium seat auction. At Vossk's request, the Sovereign-Lord of the City of Chains offered the Argent Sword, a raiding army costing 300 mithril and 900 crowns with 50 thrones upkeep. It can only be raised if Callidus has amity, a Senate motion authorises it and it is placed under the Military Council. The city would pay its upkeep if the Canterspire Circle were ceded to it. Immaculate Architect costs 77 rings of ilium. The Silent Market offers Vermillion Heart spice for cow bonds.

Highguard.t: Arlais of Highguard asked about having the Autumn realm build fortifications in Highguard, which Crown could not make profitable. Instead Crown offered the Immaculate Architect ritual text to the first citizen to send 77 rings of ilium.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are named as having taken possession of the Immaculate Architect ritual text and refusing to return it to the Empire.

Urizen.t: Vossk of the Concordium of Pallas obtained an offer for an Autumn mercenary army to fight under an Urizen banner. It would need Callidus to have amity, Senate authorisation and a general chosen through constitutional means under the Military Council. Her request to buy an Ephisis box was refused.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the description of raiding armies notes that some Wintermark armies find fighting alongside foraging armies distasteful, given their dislike of "maggots".

A box for a sword.o: In Spring 387YE the City of Lead and Gold's herald Crown, now working for the Waning Circle, set out falling prices for wains and brokered an offer from the City of Chains to sell Urizen an Autumn mercenary army, the Argent Sword. He also put the Immaculate Architect ritual text up for sale and passed on a foreign client's bid for cow bonds.

Redoubt.t: The proposed Argent Sword mercenary army would be raised at Wilstone in Redoubt if the opportunity is commissioned before the end of the Summer Solstice 387YE.

A bridge too far.d: The Kongegőr was damaged by an Imperial raid in 384YE, but the Jotun have since rebuilt and heavily fortified it, so a repeat raid by fleets and military units cannot succeed. One option is for an army to take full control of Alsterbo or Bjarkey and then destroy the bridges in a season. The alternative depends on the Marcher and Wintermark assemblies each enacting a mandate urging fleets to support the Red Wind Corsairs. The Corsairs would then take to the sea from Mitwold, Kallavesa or Bregasland, backed by at least 5,000 points of fleets. After that they could launch a shore offensive on Alsterbo. Graciana warned that a Jotun counter-attack was likely.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Graciana considered and rejected enlisting the Grendel, expecting them to betray the plan to the Jotun, and she recalled her earlier appraisal on disrupting Grendel activity in the Bay of Catazar.

Jotun.t: Destroying the Kongegőr's bridges would stop Jotun armies moving between Narkyst and Kalsea. The Jotun have heavily fortified the causeway against fleets and raids, though they would not expect an attack by a navy.

The Marches.t: The Marcher assembly would need to enact a mandate urging its fleets to support the Red Wind Corsairs. Mitwold is one of the possible launch points, though the Marches have nowhere near enough fleets on their own.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark assembly would also need to enact the mandate, and Wintermark has at least twice the required fleet strength. Its lands offer Kallavesa as a launch point and Sermersuaq as a route into Skallahn.

A bridge too far.o: In Spring 387YE the prognosticator Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra delivered her appraisal on destroying the Kongegőr, the bridged chain of islands linking the Jotun territories of Skallahn and Hordalant. She found that it could only be done with armies, and proposed a risky naval assault by the Red Wind Corsairs.

Hordalant/Alsterbo.t: Alsterbo anchors the southern end of the Kongegőr and is protected by a small fortification at Dalvi. It is the target of the proposed naval shore offensive, which would have to capture the region before the bridges could be destroyed.

Hordalant/Ashahon.t: The Fortress of the Pale Queen in Ashahon, a rank two fortification of cultural significance to the Jotun, would make any Imperial capture of Alsterbo harder.

Skallahn/Bjarkey.t: Bjarkey anchors the northern end of the Kongegőr and is guarded by the level two walls of Kierheim, seat of the Jarl of Kierheim. An army in full control of the region could destroy the bridges.

Skallahn/Greenwall.t: Imperial armies would have to seize Greenwall first, possibly within a single season, before they could reach Bjarkey.

Bay of Catazar.t: Warships built on the Bay to let the Red Wind Corsairs put to sea were due for completion by the coming summit. Without local fleet support, the Corsairs could only sail in these waters.

Bregasland.t: Now in Jotun hands, Bregasland is one of the territories the Empire would have to fight through to reach Hordalant. It is also named as one of the places the Red Wind Corsairs could take to the sea from.

Hordalant.t: Hordalant anchors the southern end of the Kongegőr and is heavily fortified. The Empire's information about it rests on a spy network several years old.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa is one of the three territories where the Red Wind Corsairs could take to the sea, with Wintermark fleet support, to begin an assault on the Kongegőr.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a Jotun-held territory the Empire would need to pass through to reach Hordalant overland.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold is one of the three territories where the Red Wind Corsairs could take to the sea with Marcher and Wintermark fleet support.

Sermersuaq.t: As firmly Imperial territory bordering Skallahn, Sermersuaq is the starting point for any overland push on Greenwall and then Bjarkey.

Skallahn.t: Skallahn anchors the northern end of the Kongegőr. It looks the easier overland target, but it is defended by the walls of Kierheim and a smaller fortification at Ulfsmoor.

A bright cerulean flame.d: Accompanied by nearly five thousand mostly Navarr soldiers, the Pilgrim's Defiance swept aside Druj traps and defenders, encountered heralds of the Agramant slaughtering Druj, and reached Mudlark's Haven, where failed Druj warding obelisks left the orcs besieged by vallornspawn. Two dozen volunteers died destroying a unique abomination fused with a miasma pillar that spread terror. The army then withdrew to Lustri. The vallorn is now quiescent; East Ashes is infested but unclaimed, Mudlark's Haven remains Druj, and Therunin is nominally Druj. Highborn congregations may support the army until Summer 389YE. Separately, refugees freed by the Agramant's servants have overwhelmed the hospital at High Chalcis, offering a relief opportunity.

Druj.t: Druj forces in East Ashes were routed by the Pilgrims and ravaged by the vallorn and Agramant's heralds, yet clung on to Mudlark's Haven and keep nominal but feeble control of Therunin; their failed warding stones and a possible Buruk Tepel hand in the pillar-abomination raise questions.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Pilgrim's Defiance lost around 1,500 soldiers but halted the vallorn in East Ashes, an inspiring feat that lets Highborn congregations keep supporting the army until Summer 389YE.

Navarr.t: Navarr soldiers and vates marched alongside the Pilgrims to save their homeland, though centuries of Navarr work reclaiming the marshes were partly undone and Navarr refugees freed by the Agramant's servants fled to Reikos.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the army marched across Urizen's Zenith, past memorials to the Highborn armies that defended Urizen from the Druj.

A bright cerulean flame.o: In Spring 388YE the Highborn army the Pilgrim's Defiance marched through Zenith into East Ashes in Therunin, broke Druj defences and fought the risen vallorn at Mudlark's Haven, stopping it from claiming the region at the cost of some 1,500 dead.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj obelisks at Mudlark's Haven were modelled on the Terunael warding stones of Bendol.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: Mentioned in passing: Nesustak rebels' spears await any Druj fleeing into Sarangrave.

Therunin/East Ashes.t: East Ashes was saved from being claimed by the vallorn but is now infested, with vallornspawn equivalent to a 4,000-strong force in its western and northern reaches, while the Druj still hold Mudlark's Haven.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Eastring, already lost to the vallorn, poured vallornspawn husks onto Mudlark's Haven and now blocks safe passage between East Ashes and the Lower Tarn Valley.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Lower Tarn Valley cannot be reached from East Ashes without crossing the vallorn and suffering casualties, and it remains poisoned.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj at Mudlark's Haven were battling the abomination of the Sweetglades.

Zenith/Clypion.t: The Pilgrims marched through Clypion past the Three Watchers, where many soldiers were anointed with liao donated by Highborn congregations.

Zenith/Iteri.t: The Pilgrims passed through Iteri beneath the Three Watchers memorial, where many took anointings before the campaign.

Zenith/Lustri.t: The army crossed Lustri past the ruins of the Stork's Gaze, then fell back to its Night-haunted woods to regroup and keep watch northward.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Mentioned in passing: the army marched through Proceris, where the Golden Cascade flows once again.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Three Watchers memorial stands over the pass into Morrow.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: other Imperial soldiers were pressing south in Redoubt while the Pilgrims marched east.

Reikos.t: Refugees led out of Therunin by the Agramant's servants overwhelmed the hospital at High Chalcis, whose healers asked the Medical Officer of the Pegasus Respite to bring a team of physicks through the Sentinel Gate.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Mentioned in passing: trapped Druj could only flee upriver to the Salt Flats by passing through another vallorn.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Druj fleeing across the Feverwater would find only Imperial steel or Nesustak rebel spears in Sarangrave.

Therunin.t: Therunin saw the Pilgrims check the vallorn's expansion, which has now subsided into quiescence; the territory remains nominally Druj but largely belongs to the beasts of the marsh.

Zenith.t: The Pilgrim's Defiance marched through Zenith, taking anointings beneath the Three Watchers, and afterwards regrouped in Lustri to count its losses.

A broken frame.d: Three conjunctions targeted marshwalker threats in Holberg, Therunin and Kallavesa. In Ossium, the Druj miasma pillars at Red Lizard Point and the twin stones of Scorpion Glades could be broken, and a Druj and tortured-soul force at Korlack Marsh could be engaged. In Holberg, a Druj warband threatening the Legacy of Courage stelae and a Tepel apothecary's potion convoy could be struck. Rescue missions were offered for captured priests in Feroz, the Urizen engineer Minicia in Spiral and Grey Pilgrims in Segura and Therunin. Other conjunctions targeted vallorn incursions, a Jotun thrall camp, a Jotun blockade of the Gullet, mysterious Jotun lumbering in Liathaven, and sewer disappearances in Sarvos. These were opportunities, not outcomes.

Dawn.t: Dawnish priests and Day ritualists were called on to help break the Druj miasma pillars in Ossium, where consecration or the Chimes of Annulment could dispel the pall of dread.

Druj.t: Druj interests were targeted on several fronts: their miasma pillars in Ossium, the war party at Korlack Marsh, a warband destroying stelae in Holberg and a Tepel apothecary's escorted potion shipment in Utterlund.

Grendel.t: The Grendel held captive priests at the Fahran Wood Siegework near Mora and were taking the engineer Minicia south through Apstrus. Both offered the Empire chances to strike at their slave-taking.

Highguard.t: Highborn were drawn in by rescues of Grey Pilgrims held by Corazon orcs at Brejah Crag and trapped by vallorn in Greenheart. Highguard unconquered also reported husks threatening the Valiant Pegasus hospital, and Highborn soldiers were credited with protecting Feroz refugees.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orcs, alongside Wintermark, were invited to attack Varki's Camp so that Jotun thralls could escape into the wilds.

Jotun.t: Jotun positions faced Imperial attack at Varki's Camp in Sermersuaq and at their Cocklegullet base blockading the Gullet. Their unexplained mass felling of timber along Fallen Thorn Trail in Liathaven was also open to investigation.

Navarr.t: The Navarr were central to the vallorn and Heirs of Terunael threats in Brocéliande, Therunin and Hercynia, including a stranded band of trackers and a vate. They were also called to help against the marshlings in Therunin, to investigate Jotun lumbering in Liathaven, and were praised for protecting Feroz refugees.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn faced the aftermath of losing Feroz, with refugees fleeing inland and priests held by the Grendel near Mora. They were also concerned in the pilgrims' captivity in Segura, whose Corazon captors demanded 20 wains of mithril.

The League.t: The League faced threats to Holberg's mithril pumps from marshwalkers, to the Legacy of Courage stelae from a Druj warband, and to Druj supply lines in Utterlund. Its citizens were urged to explore the sewers of Sarvos for missing people.

The Marches.t: Marcher fleet-owners risked a one-rank profit penalty unless the Jotun base at Cocklegullet was removed. Marchers were also among those with an interest in the captive pilgrims in Segura.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the location of the pillar in Thule-held Bonewood was unknown, and it was unclear whether the mystics of Otkodov had already cleansed it.

Urizen.t: Urizen were offered a rescue mission for Minicia of the Illuminated Circle of Bloodsilver Twilight, the engineer behind the Block great work, before the Grendel could learn its secrets.

Varushka.t: Varushkan settlers in Ossium could see the miasma pillars broken and the Druj force plaguing Korlack Marsh destroyed, ending whispers that it might become the territory's first wolves. Varushka was also listed among those invited into the Sarvos sewers.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark faced a marshwalker attack around Raimo's Fast in Kallavesa. It was also invited to raid Varki's Camp so that Jotun thralls could escape to Hahnmark or Kallavesa.

A broken frame.o: Ahead of the Autumn 383YE summit, the civil service listed the Sentinel Gate conjunctions its prognosticators had found. They offered chances to fight marshwalkers, break Druj miasma pillars in Ossium, rescue captives from the Grendel and Jotun, help Jotun thralls escape, counter the vallorn and the Heirs of Terunael, and explore the sewers of Sarvos.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: The Jotun base outside Cocklegullet on the Gullet's southern shore was targeted by a conjunction; if it was not removed, Marcher fleets would lose profits.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Vallorn husks and Heirs of Terunael threatened the Valiant Pegasus hospital at Swift Watch Woods, even though the vallorn's expansion into Elerael had already been stopped.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: Mentioned in passing: refugees fleeing the Grendel were making for Afarjasse.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: Captured priests were held at the Fahran Wood Siegework among the Grendel lines around Mora, and a rescue conjunction was offered.

Hercynia/Deer's Folly.t: Navarr trackers and a vate were isolated in miasma on the Bont Goch Trail, surrounded by husks.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: Converging marshwalker colonies threatened the South Wastes Drain pumps of the Great Pits, and a Druj warband stalked the Uitgang Road seeking more stelae to destroy.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: The Druj presence there raised alarm, and a conjunction to the Barrens Trail offered a chance to ambush a Tepel apothecary's escorted potion shipment.

Kallavesa/Rundhal Marsh.t: A marshwalker destroyed structures and injured locals around Raimo's Fast, and those wounded needed aid.

Liathaven/Western Scout.t: Jotun and thralls left felled timber strewn along miles of Fallen Thorn Trail, and Navarr could investigate why.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: Mentioned in passing: the location and status of the Bonewood pillar in Thule-held land were unknown.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Conjunctions offered the chance to break the pillar at Red Lizard Point and to fight the Druj and tortured souls plaguing the Korlack Marsh settlers.

Ossium/Echofell.t: Two miasma stones in the Scorpion Glades had to be depowered within about a minute of each other, amid tortured souls, to lift the dread.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Mentioned in passing: a pillar remained at Fang Tree, but no conjunction to it was detected.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Ten small conjunctions led into the unmapped Sewers of Sarvos to search for missing performers, a debutante, cadavers, a free company and lost ingots.

Segura/Anduzjasse.t: Highborn pilgrims were held by Corazon orcs at Brejah Crag, and a ransom of 20 wains of mithril was demanded.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: An attack on Varki's Camp could sow disruption among the Jotun and let many thralls escape before winter.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: Minicia was being taken south through the Forest of Xanthi, and a rescue could be mounted there.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: Grey Pilgrims left by the Heirs of Terunael at the ruins of Heart's Watch Steading held back advancing husks with a failing ward.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: Marshlings emerging from the swamps advanced on Holt Outpost, the Great Forest Orcs' watchpost guarding the Holt of the Oak.

Bregasland.t: Jotun forces based outside Cocklegullet threatened to choke shipping on the Gullet, offering a conjunction to drive them out.

Brocéliande.t: A horde of vallorn husks, accompanied by suspected Heirs of Terunael, moved on the Valiant Pegasus field hospital at Swift Watch Woods in Elerael.

Feroz.t: With Feroz lost to the Grendel, refugees fled inland and captured priests were held at the Fahran Wood Siegework near Mora, awaiting possible rescue.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark was named as a possible refuge for Jotun thralls escaping Sermersuaq.

Hercynia.t: Navarr trackers and a vate were trapped by vallorn miasma and husks on the Bont Goch Trail, offering a chance to relieve them.

Holberg.t: Holberg faced a marshwalker threat to the Great Pits' mithril pumps, a Druj warband attacking the Legacy of Courage stelae, and a Druj potion convoy that could be ambushed.

Kallavesa.t: A marshwalker attacked the watchtowers around Raimo's Fast, injuring locals, though the Beacons network itself was not at risk.

Liathaven.t: Jotun warriors and thralls were felling timber on a massive scale along Fallen Thorn Trail for no clear purpose, and Navarr were invited to investigate.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: Minicia's Grendel captors were thought possibly to be taking her to slave camps in Mareave.

Ossium.t: The Druj miasma pillars at Red Lizard Point and Scorpion Glades could be broken, and the Druj force terrorising the settlers of Korlack Marsh could be engaged.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the mystics of Otkodov might already have tried to cleanse the Bonewood pillar.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Reikos campaign was cited as the bitter lesson that clustered miasma pillars are harder to remove.

Sarvos.t: Disappearances and unease beneath the city, after a Winter curse and the arrival of the Iron Helms, prompted ten conjunctions into the unmapped sewers.

Segura.t: Highborn pilgrims preaching to Corazon orcs were held captive at Brejah Crag, and the Corazon demanded 20 wains of mithril for their return.

Sermersuaq.t: Many thralls had been moved to Varki's Camp, and an attack there could let large numbers escape Jotun rule.

Spiral.t: After the Grendel annexed Apstrus, the captured engineer Minicia was being taken south, and a rescue conjunction was offered.

Therunin.t: Marshlings threatened the Great Forest Orcs' Holt Outpost, and Grey Pilgrims were trapped by vallorn at Heart's Watch Steading.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: clashes in Zenith were cited as showing that clustered miasma pillars are harder to dispel.

A business like any other.d: With Kantor's port open, Axou traders brought spices, narcotics, orichalcum and bone carvings, with a few closed-mouthed Skouran passengers. They sought metalwork, dragonbone, green iron and liao, so liao sold for 20 rings instead of 12 this season. The Synod or Senate could encourage or restrict that trade. Jarm lifted its last sanctions, giving bonuses at Kavor, Vezak and Rigia if relations held through the Solstice. A Suranni faction offered to open Robec for a bribe. Faraden caravans flourished. Sarcophan stayed neutral while a white granite dock began at Cargo. Sumaah still held the Imperial Crown and remained at war, the Commonwealth stayed chilly and Thule showed cautious interest in trade.

Dawn.t: Adventurous Axou captains braved the Semmerlak to trade in Dawn. Starac Sijed Orzel of House Orzel, Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy, was expected to learn the details of the Robec proposal first.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel vessels were regular visitors to the Sarcophan Delves' southern port, which kept open diplomatic relations with them.

Highguard.t: Axou merchants on the Bay of Catazar favoured other nations' ports over those of Highguard. The skeletal Sumaah embassy in Necropolis continued its quiet business.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: a binding treaty with the Faraden let their caravans pass through the northern Lasambrian hills unmolested by the Jotun.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast ports were among those Axou merchants favoured, and Feroz mazzarine was on sale in Sarvos. Reports from southern Feroz revealed a Suranni fortification being built in Kalino.

The League.t: League ports drew Axou trade, and a Sarvos shopkeeper was shown selling liao to Axou buyers. There were rumours of Jarmish interest in the Tassato Mana Exchange.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Senator Henry Ward of Upwold was quoted for the Senate statement welcoming trade with Jarm.

Thule.t: The Thule orcs expressed cautious interest in establishing an embassy and opening trade routes with the northern Empire.

Urizen.t: Urizen ports were favoured by Axou merchants. Work began on a loading dock at Cargo that, once completed, will let a chosen minister purchase Sarcophan white granite.

Varushka.t: Axou captains crossed the Semmerlak to trade in Varushka, and Volodmartz bladeroot featured among the herbs sold in Sarvos.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sarvos shopkeeper in the story offered 'special' herbs supposedly shipped from Kallavesa.

A business like any other.o: In Winter 380YE, black-sailed Axou merchants began visiting Imperial ports in large numbers for the first time in decades, and their appetite for liao briefly drove up its price. Imperial relations with Jarm, the Iron Confederacy, Faraden, Sarcophan, Sumaah, the Commonwealth, Asavea and Thule also shifted.

Bay of Catazar.t: Black-sailed Axou merchants plied the Bay in significant numbers, favouring Brass Coast, League and Urizen ports over those of Highguard.

Feroz.t: Mazzarine from the Feroz Spice Gardens was traded abroad. Reports from southern Feroz told of a significant Suranni fortification going up across the border in Kalino.

Kalino.t: The Suranni began work on a significant fortification in Kalino, overlooking a main route through the southern Lasambrian Hills to the Iron Confederacy heartland.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: a shopkeeper in the story claimed a shipment of 'special' herbs from Kallavesa.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the skeletal staff of the Sumaah embassy in Necropolis conducted their little business with a minimum of fuss.

Redoubt.t: Work began on a loading dock at the international trade port of Cargo, under a treaty with a Sarcophan Bedelaar-Huisbaas, to allow purchases of white granite once completed.

Sarvos.t: In the story, a Sarvos herb shop was visited by Axou necromancer and guard seeking to buy as much liao as the shopkeeper had, a sign of the city's new Axou trade.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: there was a rumour of Jarmish interest in the Tassato Mana Exchange.

The Semmerlak.t: Adventurous Axou captains were reported braving the Semmerlak to reach Varushka and Dawn.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the quoted Senate statement on trade with Jarm was attributed to Senator Henry Ward of Upwold.

Volodmartz.t: Mentioned in passing: a shipment of Volodmartz bladeroot was on sale in the Sarvos shop in the story.

A challenging time.d: Barien could not respond to Challenge the Iron Duke because of an ongoing conjunction, so his heralds offered alternatives. Citizens without Imperial titles gathered favours by fighting one another in Anvil. Twenty-four competitors then fought a grand melee at Goldenoak Circle in Serenael, Miaren, for the sword Pinnacle. The sword may be borne until the holder dies or gains an Imperial title. Jacques Flayer of Dawn won. Past victors of Dawn and Wintermark were summoned to the Grove of the Thousand in Axmure, Semmerholm, where a year-long challenge between the two nations was set, to end the following Autumn. Brynell Goldengrove, acting for the Archmage of Summer, raised a declaration of amity naming the Clattering Curtain's performing arts competition at the Winter Solstice to receive Barien's prize.

Dawn.t: Dawn's past victors of the Iron Duke's challenges were invited to a year-long contest against Wintermark, and Jacques Flayer of Dawn won the Pinnacle Tourney and the sword Pinnacle.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Pinnacle Tourney was held via conjunction at Goldenoak Circle in Serenael, a region of the Navarr-held territory of Miaren.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the in-character story follows a League street gang, the Mudskippers, racing across the Sarvos docks.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's past victors, including Artis Greyholm and Tarik of Ashenhall, were summoned to receive a year-long challenge pitting them against Dawn, to be concluded at the following Autumn Equinox.

A challenging time.o: With his ritual Challenge the Iron Duke unable to be cast, Barien, the Iron Duke, announced a grand tourney for the sword Pinnacle, a year-long Victor's Challenge between Dawn and Wintermark, and an offer to patronise a contest chosen by the Archmage of Summer. Jacques Flayer of Dawn won the Pinnacle Tourney.

Miaren/Serenael.t: Goldenoak Circle in Serenael was the site of the Pinnacle Tourney, which was open to spectators and won by Jacques Flayer of Dawn.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: At the Grove of the Thousand in Axmure, Barien's heralds set the year-long Victor's Challenge for the invited victors of Dawn and Wintermark.

Miaren.t: Miaren hosted the Pinnacle Tourney, a grand melee fought via conjunction at Goldenoak Circle in Serenael.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the in-character story is set at the Sarvos docks, where the Mudskippers hold their annual Buskin's Day race.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm's Grove of the Thousand hosted Barien's usual rewards ceremony and the setting of the Victor's Challenge between Dawn and Wintermark.

A circle sewn with fate.d: After being rebuffed at Redoubt, the Children of Wrecks sent their Gathered Storm navy, led by the flagship Storm's Child and backed by carcharodons and a guardian of Siakha, south from Madruga to sack Oran. At the same time Commander Gallum Fiersach and Wind Lord Saoirse led almost the entire garrison of Mora's Rock towards the town. Both forces arrived together. The Grendel broke the western gate, ignored the Freeborn and slaughtered the pirates, aided by Grendel sleeper agents and the corsairs. After three hours the Children fled into the Cazar Straits. Saoirse explained the intelligence that made this possible had come from a 'ghost of the sea' and a now-burned spy ring. She urged the Freeborn to prepare their own defences or seek an accord with Mora's Rock. Fiersach and Saoirse will accept winged messengers.
