Grendel.t: The Mora's Rock garrison under Commander Fiersach and Wind Lord Saoirse defeated the Children of Wrecks at Oran out of contempt for them as traitors, then returned to Morajasse. They lost the use of part of their espionage ring and now invite Imperial messengers.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the fortifications in Necropolis are among the few coastal defences, and the Highborn traitor Ezhabbenar of Hedrossan is confirmed dead.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the closest Imperial forces to Oran had already crossed into Reinos, too far away to help.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn of Oran were saved from a Children of Wrecks sack by the Grendel and their own corsairs. They were warned to prepare their defences or persuade their leaders to reach an accord with Mora's Rock.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: fortifications in Sarvos and Spiral are named among the few protections against surprise attack from the sea.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the recap recalls the Grendel and Children of Wrecks attacks on Elos and Visten, and the Gyre coven's magical storms over Redoubt.

A circle sewn with fate.o: In spring 387YE the Grendel garrison of Mora's Rock marched out of Morajasse and, together with Oran's corsairs, routed a Children of Wrecks assault on Oran before returning to their holdfast. Commander Gallum Fiersach's forces spared the Freeborn defenders.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: Some citizens of Oran fled south-east on foot across the grasslands towards Afarjasse to escape the coming battle.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Corsair refugees from the Cazar Straits fought hard against the Children at Oran, and the beaten Gathered Storm retreated into the Straits' waters.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Mentioned in passing: fleeing citizens chose not to go south into Fontargenta, fearing the Children of Wrecks would follow them.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: The Grendel garrison of Mora's Rock marched out of Morajasse to fight at Oran, then returned there with their dead and injured.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The Children of Wrecks tried to conquer Oranseri and pillage Oran, but the Grendel and local corsairs drove them off after three hours of fighting in the town.

Madruga/Siroc Bayou.t: Mentioned in passing: a band of youths set out through the Siroc Bayou to seek help from Quzar.

Necropolis/Hedrossan.t: Mentioned in passing: the traitor Ezhabbenar of Hedrossan is confirmed dead after the Winter Solstice battle.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Mentioned in passing: the recap recalls the Children of Wrecks' attempt to devastate the spires of Visten.

Segura/Lucksprings.t: Mentioned in passing: refugees dared not take the road to Lucksprings with a Grendel force crossing the grasslands.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: anxiety gripped the whole bay as the Grendel armada and the Children of Wrecks' fleets remained at large.

Feroz.t: Oran was attacked by the Children of Wrecks and saved by the Grendel garrison of Mora's Rock. The Empire still controls three regions, while the Children and the Grendel hold one apiece.

Madruga.t: The Gathered Storm sailed south from Madruga to attack Oran. The territory remains uncontrolled, with three regions held by the Empire, one by the Children of Wrecks and three uncontrolled.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: named as the eastern edge of the Bay of Catazar, where the air was thick with anticipation.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: its fortifications are one of the few defences against a surprise attack from the sea.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the recap notes the failed Grendel and Children of Wrecks attacks on Elos and the Gyre coven's storms that struck Redoubt.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the nearest Imperial forces were already across the border into Reinos.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: its fortifications help guard the southern coast against sea raids.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Oran's garrison sent desperate messages west to Segura for help.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: its fortifications help guard the southern coast against sea raids.

A dark and stormy night.d: Imperial magistrates, aided by League bravos, sentinels and magicians, arrested the Grendel ringleaders in Apulian. Holdouts were executed and informants exiled, revealing operations in Sarvos, including Trivento, and in Cargo. The Vigilant found Grendel spies who had stayed behind in the closed embassy, using a secret tunnel, and paid Urizeni captains for reports. The spies were executed. Each jewel needs a Grendel navy to spend a season offshore, or Grendel control of the territory. The Senate could commission Spymaster's offices to run counter-espionage operations, or the Conclave could pursue a Shuttered Lantern grand lodge. Navarr prognosticator Eilian Sweetwater is missing, feared captured.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Bell is described as focused on the Druj in the east, where it is suffering heavy losses, leaving it unable to hunt the remaining Grendel spies.

Grendel.t: The Grendel lost their espionage outposts in Spiral and in the old Cargo embassy, with many agents executed. Their methods were exposed: each jewel costs a navy a season offshore and a heavy purse.

Highguard.t: Necropolis was confirmed clear of Grendel espionage. Captured spies revealed that the Grendel had planned a new outpost in the Black City but lacked the resources to establish it.

Navarr.t: The Navarr Imperial Prognosticator Eilian Sweetwater vanished after sailing from Elos just before the Grendel attack on Naris. There are fears that Grendel spymasters hold him and will extract his knowledge of Imperial plans.

The Brass Coast.t: A Grendel espionage jewel was confirmed in Madruga, and one is suspected in Feroz. The Brass Coast is left with spy operations still to root out.

The League.t: League bravos raised as militia helped arrest the Grendel spies in Apulian, ending operations in Spiral. However, two Grendel jewels remain confirmed in Sarvos, including one in Trivento.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Marcher bounders in Mitwold are cited as an example of national units that could only support counter-espionage within their own nation.

Urizen.t: Grendel spies were found hiding in the old embassy in Cargo and were executed alongside Urizeni captains who had sold them information. Disgruntled Urizeni were also among those arrested in Spiral.

A dark and stormy night.o: In Autumn 387YE the Military Council shut down the Grendel espionage outpost in Spiral, and the intelligence gathered let the followers of Berechiah uncover and destroy a second Grendel spy cell hidden in the old embassy building in Cargo, Redoubt. Further Grendel 'jewels' remain in Sarvos and Madruga, with one suspected in Feroz.

Redoubt/Naris.t: The Grendel armada swept into Naris and laid siege to Elos the day after prognosticator Eilian Sweetwater sailed from there. He has not been heard from since.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: Mentioned in passing: Bocche is not named, but the page confirms two Grendel espionage jewels in Sarvos, one of them in Trivento.

Feroz.t: Feroz is suspected of hosting a Grendel espionage jewel, a suspicion reinforced by Commander Gallum Fiersach's response to the Wrecker attack there.

Madruga.t: Madruga is confirmed as hosting a Grendel espionage jewel that has yet to be dealt with.

Mareave.t: Mareave is listed as clear of Grendel espionage. It is also noted as the site of the completed grand lodge of the Golden Pyramid.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is used as an example of where Marcher bounders could effectively support counter-espionage.

Necropolis.t: Necropolis is confirmed clear. Grendel plans for a new outpost in the Black City were never realised for lack of resources.

Redoubt.t: The followers of Berechiah uncovered Grendel spies operating from a secret tunnel in the old Cargo embassy, and magistrates arrested and executed them. Redoubt is now clear of espionage.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos is confirmed to host two Grendel espionage jewels, one of them in Trivento, despite efforts to root them out two years earlier.

Spiral.t: The Military Council shut down the Grendel outpost in Apulian through dawn raids. Holdouts were executed, informants exiled, and Grendel operations in Spiral ended.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the former ambassador to the Grendel who ordered the embassy staff out signed himself Abel of Zenith Ascendant.

A dream that can last.d: After abandoning Ossium and crossing the Semmerlak, the Sand Fishers built simple villages in Misericorde and roamed Holberg's marshes. Their wanderings onto farmland were settled by agreement: in return for access they tithe herbs, so every Holberg farm now yields two random herbs each season. Cultural friction, including an incident at the Imperial Menagerie, led to calls for a market outside the city. Tristan Exile's End used an Imperial Wayleave to commission Misericorde Market. The Synod sent Kaspar Yakovitch von Holberg to teach the Virtues, Leonora Van Holberg to rally Holberg's citizens, and Skywise Rykana to rally the Imperial Orcs. Each mandate carried costs for those it called upon.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as the Sand Fishers' former enslavers, whose miasma crushed their spirit, and as the one-time masters of Ossium's forests.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc assembly sent Skywise Rykana to rally support for the Sand Fishers. Under the mandate, Imperial Orc-owned resources were to produce one rank less from the Summer Solstice until the Winter Solstice 383YE, with the Sand Fishers gaining what the orcs gave up.

The League.t: Holberg's citizens gained herb tithes on their farms and a new market for Sand Fisher goods. In return, Leonora Van Holberg's mandate called on them to support their new neighbours at a cost to Holberg's production, and Kaspar Yakovitch von Holberg was sent to teach the Sand Fishers the Virtues.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is not named directly, but the Sand Fishers' departure took place from Ossium, which Varushka held.

A dream that can last.o: In Summer 383YE the Sand Fishers finished settling Misericorde in Holberg, which the Senate had ceded to them, and began a thriving trade in herbs and marsh goods with the League. During the Summer Solstice a covered market was commissioned for them, and the Synod passed three mandates to support them and teach them the Virtues.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: Sand Fishers range into Ennerlund's marshes hunting and gathering herbs, and they tithe a share of the herbs they find to the owners of the farmland they cross.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: The Sand Fishers completed their claim on Misericorde and built small reed-and-wood villages near the Semmerlak. A covered market, Misericorde Market, was commissioned for trade between them and Holberg's citizens.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: Sand Fishers wander Rebeshof's marshes in search of herbs, and they share a portion of their finds with local landowners in exchange for passage across their farms.

Holberg.t: The Sand Fishers settled in Misericorde and roam its marshes. Every farm in Holberg now gains two random herbs each season, Misericorde Market was commissioned beside the city, and a passed mandate called on Holberg's citizens to support the orcs at a temporary cost to production.

Ossium.t: With the civil service's help, the Sand Fishers abandoned Ossium and crossed the Semmerlak to their new home in Misericorde.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: a statement by the preachers of Skarsind urging Imperial Orcs to engage with the Sand Fishers is quoted, and the orcs' development of Skarsind is cited as an example.

A fine and private place.d: The new regio counts as a strong Winter regio but cannot target rituals beyond its own territory. Those who linger there take on draughir-like thoughts. From the fourth hour of the afternoon until midnight on the Saturday of the Winter Solstice, its portal led to a Winter Chamber that Tharim and the other Winter eternals declared neutral ground. There they would grant each prepared boon to whichever nation offered the most dragonbone. Until Sunday sunrise the Imperial regio lost its Winter component entirely. The heralds addressed many nations, most of them long gone. Tharim's heralds revealed the winners before the Spring Equinox 380YE.

Dawn.t: The royal houses of the Dawn were among the peoples Tharim's heralds named, inviting them to choose a representative to offer dragonbone tribute in the Winter Chamber for the eternals' boons.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the travelling actors recalled reducing the dour Highborn of Necropolis to tears of laughter during an earlier performance.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: news of the battle for the Mournwold was beginning to reach the Marches as the actors performed.

A fine and private place.o: In Winter 379YE a second regio, strongly aligned to Winter, appeared at Anvil, foreshadowed by actors across the Empire unaccountably setting their plays in the Tomb. Heralds of the eternal Tharim announced that it opened onto a Winter Chamber where invited nations could offer dragonbone to the sovereign-lords of the Wasteland in return for boons.

Casinea.t: The new Winter regio appeared at Anvil in Casinea. Winter rituals performed there were strengthened but could target only Casinea, and its portal to the Winter Chamber was open for one night of the Winter Solstice.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the first stories of the battle for the Mournwold were filtering north to the Marches at the time.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the mummer troupe had once performed their comedy in Necropolis to great acclaim.

A force to be reckoned with.d: The Sumaah had reopened Zemeh and invited pilgrims to Timoj, but still held the Imperial Crown and rejected the Synod. Asavea's civil war continued, and Almodin Oktístis faced trial for idolatry. The Senate ended Jarm's favoured trader status, while the Lantir question pushed Jarm and the Commonwealth towards war. The Sarcophan Kruidenkenner offered to build herb warehouses. Faraden trade suffered from Lasambrian Jotun incursions and an iridescent gloaming blight. The Iron Confederacy, angry over liao smuggling and Imperial maps, later received a treaty sharing territorial knowledge and criminalising the liao trade. Tsark remained enigmatic. The summit agreed sanctions on Jarm, Asavea, Faraden, Thule and the Iron Confederacy.

Dawn.t: Dawnish citizens served as ambassadors to Asavea and the Iron Confederacy. The Kruidenkenner were interested in building a herb warehouse in Dawn, and Faraden merchants wanted access to Dawnish luxuries, though their hopes were fading.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Druj-held Zenith is named only as lying west of the Mountains of the Moon, where Tsark was discovered.

Grendel.t: Under the treaty ratified with the Iron Confederacy, the Empire agreed to share its knowledge of Grendel territories with the Suranni.

Highguard.t: The Sumaah Houses of Virtue declared they no longer recognised Bastion as the heart of the Way, and a Highborn, Accalon of Felix's Watch, served as Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.

Jotun.t: The Lasambrian Jotun's attack on Segura disrupted Faraden caravans: they refused to let western travellers trade in the land they had claimed, though they would not breach their treaty with Faraden.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Faraden merchants concluded that the success of Moonwater Hall was unlikely to be repeated elsewhere in the Empire.

The Brass Coast.t: The Lasambrian attack on Segura disrupted Faraden trade, the Suranni accused the Empire of letting liao be smuggled through Feroz, and the Brass Coast's Gonzalo i Riqueza served as Ambassador to Faraden.

The League.t: League citizen Guillamo de Tassato was alleged to have stolen the Imperial Crown for the Sumaah. Jarmish magicians traded through the Tassato Mana Exchange, and engineer Menno van Ritsjhof left to visit the Commonwealth with the League Assembly's blessing.

The Marches.t: The Sarcophan Kruidenkenner expressed interest in building a herb-trading warehouse in the Marches, an opportunity open until the end of the Spring Equinox 383YE.

Thule.t: Thule was explicitly named among the slaving nations against which the Empire agreed to enact trade sanctions after the summit.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's Tarquinius Ankarien is named as the Imperial Ambassador to Axos.

Varushka.t: Sarcophan merchants were travelling in growing numbers through Varushka's forests and hills, and Faraden merchants wanted Varushkan timber and ore through an enclave in Volodmartz, though the Empire showed little interest.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark citizens served as ambassadors to Jarm and the Sarcophan Delves, Kallavesa proposed the motion ending Jarm's favoured trader status, and the Kruidenkenner considered building a warehouse in the nation.

A force to be reckoned with.o: Ahead of the Winter Solstice 382YE, this Wind of Fortune surveyed the Empire's relations with the great powers and its smaller neighbours, centred on the planned Imperial Slavery Summit. The summit proved a resounding success and committed the Empire to trade sanctions against slaving nations.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Mentioned in passing: Sanctuary Sands is listed among the places along the Bay of Catazar where Sarcophan merchants were a common sight.

Astolat.t: Faraden merchants hoped for a trading enclave in central Astolat to reach Dawnish luxuries, but admitted the Empire seemed to have little interest in the idea.

Bastion.t: The Sumaah Houses of Virtue formally declared that they no longer recognised the White City of Bastion as the heart of the Way, urging pilgrims to look to Timoj instead.

Bay of Catazar.t: Sarcophan merchants were common in the towns around the bay, and Imperial captains' earlier mapping of it led to Suranni accusations of espionage, later answered by a treaty sharing that knowledge.

Feroz.t: The Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz kept bringing profit from Asavean trade, while the Suranni insisted that liao was being smuggled into the Iron Confederacy through Feroz.

Karsk.t: The Kruidenkenner enclave at chill Ivarsgard had brought a marked rise in Sarcophan merchants travelling through the eastern territories and more herbs reaching the auction at Anvil.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Siroc is listed among the places where Sarcophan merchants and traders were a common sight.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: the success of Moonwater Hall is cited as something Faraden merchants no longer expected to see repeated elsewhere in the Empire.

Mountains of the Moon.t: After the spy network into the mountains was completed and the nation of Tsark revealed, there were no further developments, and Tsark remained enigmatic.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Sanctuary Sands is listed among the places where Sarcophan merchants were a common sight.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is listed among the smaller neighbours known to practise slavery, with no sign of its representatives attending the summit.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named directly. Its only link to the page is Urizen's Tarquinius Ankarien, named as Ambassador to Axos.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is noted for the sea fortifications Menno van Ritsjhof designed for it and as a place where Sarcophan traders were common.

Segura.t: The Lasambrian Jotun's attack on Segura left them barring Faraden travellers from the land they had claimed, disrupting western trade with the Empire. The page warned this could worsen if they took more Brass Coast land.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is named only as lying west of the Mountains of the Moon, where Tsark was discovered.

Tassato.t: An enclave of Jarmish magicians continued to work through the Tassato Mana Exchange, importing Beloye zerno for sale to Imperial citizens with mana sites.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is not named directly; the Marches as a whole are among the nations where the Kruidenkenner considered building a herb warehouse.

Volodmartz.t: Faraden merchants wanted a trading enclave in Volodmartz to reach Varushkan timber and ore, but conceded the Empire seemed to have little interest.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Zenith is named only as lying west of the Mountains of the Moon, where Tsark was discovered.

A fork in the path.d: The mystics revealed that the Raven's Dream, a shared vision, needs a dose of true liao. They withdrew support for the Parliament of Owls, which can no longer be cast, and will instead let the Witan choose one new Wintermark problem for them to appraise each year, starting at the Winter Solstice. They warned that no new Champion should take the Crown of Three Tears until Wemba the Bloody and Kaarina White-Eye are dealt with. After that, a Witan will choose a cause and the nation's mystics will choose and crown its Champion. Answering the Raven Seer's question about the Gullet, they reported that Rook's Feather has offered a proposal to defend the marshes. Sung offered to enfold the Aviary at Ishal if the Archmage of Night formally asks before the end of the Summer Solstice 389YE.

Jotun.t: The Jotun are named as one of the two known threats from the Gullet, having apparently called up allies from Fjorknae able to sail in and raid its shores. The aid offered to Wintermark is partly aimed at guarding against them.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Night Singer's apparent protection of the City from the Whisper Gallery after the Chamber of Euphony was built in Apulian is cited as a hopeful precedent.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are recalled as having captured the Crown of Three Tears about a decade ago and used fell magic on it.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark loses the Parliament of Owls but gains a yearly Witan-chosen appraisal by the mystics and a way to experience the Raven's Dream if it can supply true liao. The Crown of Three Tears is held back until Agramant's servants are slain, after which the nation's mystics will choose a Champion for a Witan-chosen cause. The Raven Seer may also accept Sung's offer to enfold the Aviary at Ishal.

A fork in the path.o: Returning from their exploration of Tsirku, the Mystics of Ishal reorganised the help they give Wintermark and the Raven Seer. They ended the Parliament of Owls, offered the Raven's Dream in exchange for true liao, set out new rules for crowning a Champion of Wintermark, and brought offers of aid against threats from the Gullet.

Fjorknae.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun appear to have called up allies from Fjorknae who can sail into the Gullet.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Hahnmark is used as an example of how the Crown's doom might fall on a territory if its senator became Champion.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa is named as the territory most endangered by threats from the Gullet, both Jotun raiders and coral-encrusted creatures. Rook's Feather has offered a proposal to help defend its marshes.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the page refers only to the mystics returning from their labours in the far frozen north.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Witan's exploration was of the wastes north of Sermersuaq, and the page notes the Jotun would attack Sermersuaq if they came overland.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Night Singer's apparent intervention to protect the City from the Whisper Gallery after the Chamber of Euphony was built in Apulian is cited as a precedent.

Tsirku.t: The Mystics of Ishal have finished their part in exploring Tsirku and will not return to it. Further exploration, likely years of work, now falls to others.

A friend like you.d: Meraud offered to help build the Highgrove Trail in Axmure, and Prospero agreed to patronise a Dawnish college, the Tower of the Loom. Estavus's architects proposed rebuilding Binding Oak Spire in Proceris. Roshanwe offered to swear an oath against the Cold Sun if the Throne swore the same, and proposed a Frozen Beacon in Suaq Fount. Zakalwe challenged the Hanuri Garrison's Quartermaster to defeat a yegarra warband in Bregasland and announced a symposium questioning the future of their pact. Janon, still under enmity, sent heralds threatening curses on Bregasland, the Barrens and Kahraman. Tharim offered a replacement for the Clarion Call ritual on conditions, Skathe set a bounty on cursing the Knight-protector of Winter, and the illegal Whisper Gallery offered Druj ritual texts.

Dawn.t: Dawn was offered Meraud's Highgrove Trail in Semmerholm and Prospero's patronage of the Tower of the Loom in Astolat, while Janon's heralds targeted the Barrens to test the Dawnish Maestro of the Cat's Graces and Skathe set a bounty on cursing Lady Aletheia, the Knight-protector of Winter.

Druj.t: The Whisper Gallery claimed the Druj gave it the Palace of the Sleepers to keep it from the Empire during the invasion of Sarangrave, and Zakalwe's heralds planned to discuss the war with the Druj, whose defeat they called imminent.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the reward for beating Cathan Canae's warhost was likened to the boon offered to the Unshackled in Mareave.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Polemarch of Highwatch was among those specifically invited to Zakalwe's symposium on the Empire's wars.

Jotun.t: A yegarra warband led by Abby the Feller, accompanied by heralds of Eleonaris, was marching across Bella's Bluff in Bregasland, and Zakalwe's herald challenged the Empire to defeat it or see her favour pass to the yegarra.

The Brass Coast.t: Janon's heralds crossed into Braydon's Jasse to test Freeborn passion, and the Azure Sutannir, João i Cabral i Riqueza, was charged with stopping them before they cursed Kahraman.

The League.t: Zakalwe's herald Telephysius spent the season in Temeschwar and offered prismatic ink to the Quartermaster of the Hanuri Garrison, Erikas Van Temeshwar, if he defeated the yegarra, while Jaheris noted that no League citizen had yet met the Argent Preceptor.

The Marches.t: Janon's heralds threatened to curse Bregasland from Gravenmarch, and Tharim sought the last artefact from a cave in Oddmire, Mitwold, entrusting its recovery to William Guildenstern.

Urizen.t: Urizen was offered plans to rebuild Binding Oak Spire in Zenith, with any cut to Zenith's business investment subject to the Urizen Assembly's veto, and was warned of consequences if Prospero-aided rituals entered Urizen lore.

Varushka.t: Tharim's legion of Ashen Knights remained camped outside Vorota and began fortifying its encampment with palisades and black-iron chains, still refusing to explain its presence.

Wintermark.t: Roshanwe proposed a Frozen Beacon in Suaq Fount to aid the Winterfolk quest to scout Tsirku, and Tharim demanded an apology from Eevi of the Gadrai as a condition of his ritual offer.

A friend like you.o: In Autumn 388YE a host of eternals sought to influence the Empire, offering great works, a Dawnish college of magic and an oath against the Cold Sun, while laying down challenges and threatening curses in several territories.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: Janon's heralds occupied the Graven Commons in Gravenmarch and called out Aracelis I Erigo, General of the Burning Falcon, to face them.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: Janon's heralds set themselves in Uthman's Field in Braydon's Jasse, less than a day from the Azure Chorus, to test the Freeborn.

Karov/Wieliczka.t: Tharim's Ashen Knights remained encamped outside Vorota and began fortifying the camp with palisades and black-iron chains.

Mitwold/Oddmire.t: A four-person conjunction opened to a cave in Oddmire where the last of Tharim's sought-after artefacts lay with its dead bearer.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: Meraud's herald surveyed Axmure for the Highgrove Trail, whose statues would also animate to defend the region at House D'Fauntine's command, each with an effective strength of 300.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: Suaq Fount was chosen as the site for Roshanwe's proposed Frozen Beacon, a lighthouse watching the storm of Sydanjaa.

Temeschwar/Hanuri.t: Telephysius spent much of the season talking with the Hanuri garrison before challenging its Quartermaster to defeat the yegarra in Bregasland.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: Janon's heralds planted their flag at the Glade of the Rising Sun in Saltmarsh, awaiting Lady Ralphine Sepulchre, the Maestro of the Cat's Graces.

Zenith/Proceris.t: The ruined Binding Oak Spire in Proceris could be rebuilt to house quarry workers, raising the Arch of the Sky's output to twenty wains a season and allowing extra white granite to be bought.

Astolat.t: Prospero asked that the Tower of the Loom, a proposed Dawnish college of magic, be built beside Silver Lake just outside Weaving, and requested dominion over its reflection in the water.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the name only appears in the title of Cathan Canae's herald, the Thane of the Enduring Bastion; nothing happened in the territory.

Bregasland.t: Janon's heralds threatened to curse Bregasland with violent emotions, and a yegarra warband with heralds of Eleonaris was marching across Bella's Bluff, where the Hanuri Garrison's Quartermaster was challenged to defeat it.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Roshanwe's herald searched Hahnmark, among other Wintermark territories, for a suitable regio before choosing Sermersuaq.

Kahraman.t: A band of Janon heralds entered Kahraman and threatened to curse it with violent emotions unless the Azure Sutannir defeated them.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: Roshanwe's herald searched Kallavesa, among other Wintermark territories, for a suitable regio before choosing Sermersuaq.

Karov.t: Tharim's Ashen Knights remained camped outside Vorota and began fortifying their camp, giving no reason for being there.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the boon for beating Cathan Canae's warhost was compared to that offered to the Unshackled in Mareave.

Mitwold.t: A conjunction opened to a cave in Mitwold, where the bearer of the last artefact sought by Tharim died trapped, and William Guildenstern was made responsible for recovering it.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Roshanwe first offered a prismatic ink site in Operus, Redoubt, before the Archmage of Day steered it towards Wintermark.

Sarangrave.t: The Whisper Gallery revealed that the Druj handed it the Palace of the Sleepers to keep it from the Empire during the invasion of Sarangrave, and it offered some of the Palace's ritual texts to Night magicians.

Semmerholm.t: Meraud offered to enchant a Highgrove Trail of heraldic beast statues, raising mana site investment in Semmerholm and giving Dawnish mana sites an extra crystal each season, if the materials were provided and the Senate approved it.

Sermersuaq.t: Roshanwe proposed a Frozen Beacon on Sermersuaq's northern border, creating the Keeper of the Northern Light with an income of prismatic ink.

Temeschwar.t: Zakalwe's herald Telephysius stayed in Temeschwar and offered to remain, providing prismatic ink each season to the Hanuri Garrison's Quartermaster, if he defeated the yegarra.

The Barrens.t: Janon's heralds crossed into the Barrens, seen as the easiest Dawnish territory to enter, threatening to curse it unless the Maestro of the Cat's Graces defeated them.

Tsirku.t: The proposed Frozen Beacon would peer into the storm of Sydanjaa to aid the Winterfolk quest to scout Tsirku and guide those returning home.

Zenith.t: Estavus's architects offered plans to rebuild Binding Oak Spire to boost the Arch of the Sky's white granite, optionally redirecting Bridge of the Air profits by permanently cutting Zenith's business investment.

A fundamental struggle (Trade Winds).d: Sumaah diplomats kept denouncing the Synod as heretics, slowly souring foreign views of the Imperial Way. An Ambassador to the Sumaah was to be appointed. Asavean relations had recovered after the trade-ban law was abrogated, though the Tarquinius family still sought retribution. An Imperial embassy opened in Leerdam, but the Commonwealth, troubled by Imperial ambiguity on slavery, searched ships, ended crystal mana sales and cheapened Artisan's Oil. Jarm's House of Princes lifted its crystal mana embargo, and Rigia became a fully functioning port offering good green iron deals. Sarcophan stayed neutral. Regario Dossier agents became active in Robec, Issyk, Kantor and Faraden.

Dawn.t: A Dawnish captain, Gerralt, illustrates the new Commonwealth regime, enduring a search for slaves and contraband in Leerdam while carrying Dawnish wood, wine, brandy and true vervain.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sarcophan Delves are said to welcome even the Grendel to their port.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the completed Sumaah embassy in Necropolis has not ended the Republic's war with the Empire.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Meade and Siroc are named among the ports from which Imperial captains set sail.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos and Tassato are named as ports for Imperial captains, and the Commonwealth embassy stands in the City of a Thousand Sails.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Lacre is named among the Imperial ports from which fleets sail.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Korotny is named among the Imperial ports from which fleets sail.

Wintermark.t: Stormcrow Beodun Snowlock of Wintermark, sent by the Synod at Prince Barbara Radz's invitation, countered Sumaah anti-Imperial preaching in the Eastern Principalities of Jarm with some success, helping win the princes' goodwill.

A fundamental struggle (Trade Winds).o: In Spring 380YE Imperial fleet captains brought back news of shifting foreign relations: the Sumaah remained at war with the Empire, Asavea and the Eastern Jarmish princes were friendly, and the Commonwealth imposed strict searches, tariffs and restrictions on Imperial ships.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: wine and brandy from Astolat's vineyards form part of Captain Gerralt's cargo searched in Leerdam.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan ships are regular visitors to the ports of the Bay of Catazar, where trade remains healthy.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: its port of Korotny is listed among those from which Imperial captains set sail.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named directly, but Brass Coast ports such as Siroc are listed among those from which Imperial captains sail.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: its port of Lacre is listed among those from which Imperial captains set sail.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sumaah embassy here has been completed, yet the Republic remains at war with the Empire.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is named as a sailing port, and the Commonwealth embassy in the City of a Thousand Sails has been completed.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; it is at most implied among the smaller Imperial ports from which captains sail.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is named among the ports from which Imperial captains set sail.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: hardwood from Weirwater's forests is part of Captain Gerralt's cargo inspected in Leerdam.

A glorious victory.d: Fayres, tourneys and mass ennoblements of yeofolk swept Dawn, and most Summer eternals were pleased, though the dethroned herald Hayaak raged. The Dawnish National Assembly was offered competing mandates: either turn towards prosperity at home or press the war against the remaining Druj. A second set of competing mandates would encourage settlement of the Barrens, urge caution, or support its factions instead. The Druj still held parts of the Barrens, the Karass and Vendarri remained hostile, the Montanians defiant, and the Rahvin had seized the Fangs. Most of the Barrens was unknown, so no regular commissions could be raised there for now. A Sentinel Gate conjunction would reach the Shrine of Hope.

Dawn.t: Dawn realised its centuries-old dream at the cost of the Hounds of Glory. Its National Assembly now faced competing choices over prosperity or war, and over settling the Barrens or holding back.

Druj.t: The Druj armies in the Barrens were shattered, though they still clung to the Heart of Peytaht and half of Murderdale. As they retreated they lashed out with curses, summoned defences and ancient trees.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: their custom of carrying torches on the Day of the Dead was cited as a model for the torchlit procession through the Sentinel Gate.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the rebellious Rahvin were noted as still willing to speak with the Imperial Orcs of the Winter Sun.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the liberation of Ossium was noted as an earlier step in the war against the Druj.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: their torchlit journey to the Kallavesa marshes was cited as an example for the Sentinel Gate conjunction.

A glorious victory.o: Dawn and its allies shattered the Druj armies and conquered the Barrens, at the cost of the Hounds of Glory, who were broken storming the Spires of Dusk. The Senate granted Dawn dominion over the territory, setting off nationwide celebration and a set of choices about how to secure the victory.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, and covered only as part of the wider Barrens, much of which remained unknown to the Empire.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Dawnguard bore the scars of occupation, with the Towers of the Dawn ruined and Drycastle pillaged. The Empire could rebuild the towers (60 white granite, 15 thrones, nine months) or restore Drycastle as a sinecure creating a Knight of Dawnguard and a Reeve of Drycastle.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: The Heart of Peytaht remained under Druj control, and Imperial armies were urged to remove this last vestige of their authority.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: Dozens of ghosts were converging on the Shrine of Hope, said to hold the grave of Ser Guineve. A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered all of Dawn the chance to visit and create a permanent aura there.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Half of Murderdale was still held by the Druj, who continued to strike at the Empire from what remained to them.

Astolat.t: Astolat's people joined the nationwide jubilation, with fayres, tourneys and celebrations held in honour of the conquest.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's earlier torchlit journey to the Kallavesa marshes was cited as an example for this conjunction.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: its liberation from the Druj was cited alongside the freeing of the Barrens.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: named among the lands the Druj still held, which a war-focused Dawnish mandate might open new fronts against.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm celebrated the victory with fayres and tourneys. The ruined Towers of the Dawn that once kept the Druj out of it could now be rebuilt.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens was conquered and granted to Dawn, but it remained largely unknown, scarred by Druj pillage and home to hostile septs. No regular commissions could be raised there for now, and mandates on whether and how to settle it were on offer.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater shared in the elation across Dawn, hosting celebrations of the long-awaited conquest.

A greater darkness.d: The Druj had threatened to kill every enslaved Great Forest Orc unless the orcs of Peytaht betrayed the Empire. Led by Ioan Longshadow and Skywise Rykana, the raiders took watchtowers in Upper Saarnath, stormed the Grove of Woe, where a Buruk Tepel burned herself to death after her death fog failed, and escorted several hundred former slaves down the Lidless Stair to Imperial lines. In Deathsgate they broke Winter-bound guardians and stopped Nimon Rue's het from burning the slaves alive. The Karass then slipped away, claiming they would mount a diversion, and the fleeing column met a retreating Druj army. A Sentinel Gate conjunction to Grimfen Mire offered Anvil a chance to delay the Druj and save them.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Envoy to the Karass, Reynard of De Gauvin, persuaded the Karass to join the raid, and some of the humans freed from the Grove of Woe were Dawnish yeofolk taken in Druj raids.

Druj.t: The Druj lost the Grove of Woe and its enslaved tree-tenders, saw a Buruk Tepel and Nimon Rue's het killed, and lost the Lidless Stair gate. Their Amber Scorpion sept is now retreating towards the column of refugees fleeing the Sacred Grove.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Ioan Longshadow is described as a survivor of Grendel chains, and Grendel-held Mareave is named among the places whose Unshackled septs answered the call.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc Assembly sent Skywise Rykana, seconded by Bloodcrow Meep, to lead its warbands, whose orcs used Druj disguises and fought for their ancestors at both groves. Rykana shares a dozen wains of liberated weirwood with the Navarr commander.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr gathered for the raid in hidden glens in Liathaven, beneath the blind eyes of the Jotun.

Navarr.t: The Navarr Assembly sent Ioan Longshadow to honour its oaths to the Great Forest Orcs, and Navarr from across their lands joined the raid. Their words broke the freed slaves' fear and their Spring magicians breached the Lidless Stair.

Thule.t: The Thule of Otkodov unwittingly shaped the raid: their curse on Ulnak weakened the Winter guardians, but their seizure of Bonewall drove a Druj army into the path of the fleeing refugees.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named; the page refers only to the Imperial campaign from Sarangrave and the earlier conquest of Whisperwood.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Great Forest Orcs in Ossium were previously liberated, Bloodcrow Meep of Ossium's Yerende sept went on the raid, and Varushka's Hunt of Alderei the Fair is the only weirwood forest named as larger than the Grove of Woe.

A greater darkness.o: In Autumn 388YE Navarr and Imperial Orc warbands, aided by heralds of Irra Harah and the Karass sept, raided the Mallum to free the Great Forest Orcs enslaved in the Druj weirwood groves. Those freed from the Grove of Woe reached the Empire, but about four hundred freed from the Sacred Grove were left trapped in the Forest of Ulnak.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Mentioned in passing: only as part of a participant's name, Aldred Boar's Dell.

Forest of Ulnak/Deathsgate.t: Beneath Cassad Ûln the raiders shattered the binding stones of Winter guardians, killed Nimon Rue's het and freed the Great Forest Orcs penned in wooden pyres at the Sacred Grove.

Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest.t: The raiders avoided crossing Gul'thak but marched along its border with Bonewall, destroying a retreating Deadly Blade cohort and other Druj stragglers.

Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire.t: The raiders crossed the cursed mire unopposed but unwelcomed, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction to the Reeth Plain offers the chance to delay the Amber Scorpions so the refugees can escape.

Forest of Ulnak/Oerwealt.t: Navarr covens permanently gave Oerwealt the woodward quality, letting heralds of Irra Harah enter there more easily to aid those who fear oppression.

Forest of Ulnak/Shifting Basin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Karass proposed escaping south through it, but the route was rejected because it holds one of Ulnak's largest Druj settlements.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Leen Rarckan.t: Mentioned in passing: a Druj force approaching the Grove of Woe may have come up from Leen Rarckan.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Lower Saarnath.t: With the Imperial armies fighting in Lower Saarnath, the rescued slaves descended the Lidless Stair to safety behind the victorious Imperial lines.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Upper Saarnath.t: Raiders captured watchtowers, stormed the Grove of Woe, killed its Buruk Tepel and broke through the Lidless Stair's gate to lead several hundred freed slaves out.

Sarangrave/Whisperwood.t: Mentioned in passing: its conquest by the Empire is cited as having freed the Great Forest Orcs held there.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: The Great Forest Orcs here had defied the Buruk Tepel's ultimatum, and the Heart of Peytaht is the intended refuge for their rescued kin.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: Mentioned in passing: the Karass proposed fleeing south to Saltmarsh, but the plan was rejected.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish envoy who recruited the Karass deals with the sept of the Bleaks and the Untrod Groves.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr moved even in the tangled depths of Brocéliande to join the raid.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Raiders crossed Grimfen Mire into Deathsgate and freed some four hundred slaves from the Sacred Grove, but the refugees are now trapped between pursuers from Cassad Ûln and a retreating Druj army.

Hercynia.t: Navarr and Great Forest Orc steadings in Hercynia supported the raid with warriors and supplies, and some of the freed servants of the Druj may find a home there.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr in the lost lands of Liathaven gathered for the raid in secret.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: Unshackled septs in Mareave heard the call to fight the Druj, and its businesses and farms provided supplies.

Miaren.t: Miaren's Navarr and Great Forest Orc steadings gave warriors and supplies to the raid, and some freed servants of the Druj may settle there.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs of Ossium were freed from the Druj in earlier years, and Imperial forces rallied there.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of Otkodov were considered as uncertain allies on the northern route, and the fleeing refugees headed towards their front line.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Raiders scaled Upper Saarnath, liberated the Grove of Woe and fought their way down the Lidless Stair to the Imperial armies in Lower Saarnath.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial forces rallied in northern Sarangrave, and the earlier conquest of Whisperwood had freed the orcs held there.

Skarsind.t: Unshackled septs of Skarsind answered their ancestors' call with warriors and supplies, and some freed servants of the Druj may find a welcome there.

The Barrens.t: The raid was mounted to rescue the kin of the Barrens' Great Forest Orcs, and the Barrens is the intended refuge for those freed. A hundred Karass hunters joined the Imperial forces on its borders.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr in Therunin answered the call, and memories of the Druj atrocities there spurred the raiders on.

A habit I can't break.d: The rakshasa gifted in 380YE died in Holberg, ending the Keeper of the Imperial Menagerie's supply of Winter vis and rare consumables. Claude of Holberg will preserve it for the Sculpture Garden unless the Conclave accepts the Thrice-Cursed Court's offer of 8 vials of heart's blood. Agramant also asked for it, which would be illegal while he is under enmity. The hakima sent *Dust, Glass and Flame* to Anvil because the City of Wonders was finished early. The Ode to Blood and Sacrifice song ended. The two Rivers rituals now replace each other permanently rather than cancelling out. Three skirmishes against coral husks were offered, each with a crown reward.

Dawn.t: Kay Griffinsbain of Dawn, Keeper of the Imperial Menagerie, lost the Winter vis and rare consumables the rakshasa once provided. Kay would receive 8 vials of heart's blood if the Conclave let the Thrice-Cursed Court take the body.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Agramant offered to animate the rakshasa's corpse with a winter spirit to run amok in the Salt Flats eating Druj. The offer is illegal while he remains under enmity.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: drakes from Mareave, held by the Grendel, are among the newer Menagerie attractions that eclipsed the rakshasa.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun are not named, but the coral husk skirmish takes place in Ottermire in Bregasland, which they held alongside the Marches.

Navarr.t: The magical song carried along the trods from Brocéliande finally faded. Navarr wayhouses debated whether it echoed Nathair Autumngale's judgement, spoke to the coming final battle against the vallorn, or needed no meaning at all.

The League.t: Claude of Holberg is set to receive the rakshasa's body for the Sculpture Garden unless the Conclave chooses otherwise. Doing so would raise the Financier of Holberg's Phantasmagorical Mementoes' income by two crowns a season.

The Marches.t: Beaters from Sallow went missing hunting coral husks in Ottermire. Biggest Peter asked the Keeper of the Dour Fens, Bill of Middleton, to find them and offered four crowns if he succeeds.

Wintermark.t: Two coral husk threats arose in Kallavesa. The scop Seaxwulf asked the Raven Seer Elena to investigate strangely huddled husks, and the thane of Freja's Rest asked Remembrancer Hodwyn Aevardson to destroy husks lurking near the village.

A habit I can't break.o: An Autumn 388YE roundup of strange events: the Imperial Menagerie's rakshasa died of old age and three parties sought its body, the hakima sent the City of Wonders' arcane projection to Anvil, Navarr's dream-song faded, Rivers of Life and Rivers Run Red changed their relationship, and coral husks stirred in Bregasland and Kallavesa.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: Beaters who went looking for coral husks in Ottermire were ambushed and have not returned. Biggest Peter asked Bill of Middleton to find out what happened, warning that husks are likely in the area.

Bregasland.t: Coral husks set upon a band of beaters from Sallow in Ottermire. This led to a combat-likely skirmish for the Keeper of the Dour Fens.

Brocéliande.t: The song raised in Brocéliande by *An Ode To Blood And Sacrifice* a year earlier finally came to an end, leaving only faint echoes.

Holberg.t: The rakshasa died in Holberg's Imperial Menagerie, and its body may be preserved for the city's Sculpture Garden or claimed by the heralds of the Thrice-Cursed Court.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa hosts two coral husk skirmishes: strangely huddled husks for the Raven Seer to investigate, and a lurking gaggle near the fishing village of Freja's Rest for the Remembrancer of Blood and Salt to destroy.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: drakes from Mareave are cited as Menagerie attractions that eclipsed the rakshasa.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: beasts captured in northern Sermersuaq are cited as Menagerie attractions that eclipsed the rakshasa.

A health to the company.d: The College of Engineering, using improved versions of Frederick di Sarvos's sketches, needed only a Senate motion to expand. If League Senators began a commission of at least 30 wains in each of Sarvos, Tassato, Temeschwar and Holberg by the Winter Solstice 384YE, a Chair of the Wolf, chosen by Tally of the Votes, could commit the Guild of Engineers to League construction without using up Imperial commissions. In Holmauer Park the waters were being cleansed, and a Loyalty mandate could make the Memorial Garden a shrine. Georgie's House could expand for 23 crowns, which the Senate approved. Mellfort's sorrow-easing aura could support either a Synod shrine or the Emerald Magpie Guild's Palace of Rest, but not both.

Highguard.t: The Highborn National Assembly upheld Lina of Felix's Watch's mandate urging Highborn business owners to cleanse the befouled waters of Holmauer, and that work was well underway.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim is listed among the places whose citizens know the trouble rats cause, as demand grows for Holberg's trained ratters.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Siroc is named among the cities troubled by rats, where interest in dogs from Georgie's House was growing.

The League.t: The League was challenged to begin an impressive commission in each of its four cities by Winter 384YE to win the Chair of the Wolf and the services of the Guild of Engineers. It also faced choices over Holmauer Park and Mellfort, and saw the Senate approve the expansion of Georgie's House.

The Marches.t: Aureliana di Sarvos's statement honoured the untouched Marcher apple grove in Holmauer Park as a symbol of Marcher Loyalty, though the Marcher Assembly's own pilgrimage mandate was not enacted. A Loyalty mandate could now make the Memorial Garden of General Flowers a shrine.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Gildenheim is listed among the cities all too aware of rats, as demand for Holberg's trained ratters spreads.

A health to the company.o: In Winter 383YE the Holberg University College of Engineering sought Senate permission to expand and challenged the League to begin an impressive commission in each of its four cities, offering a Chair of the Wolf in return. The page also set out opportunities in Holmauer Park, at Georgie's House and at Mellfort; the Senate approved the expansion of Georgie's House.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: The Pavilion was inspiring efforts to reclaim the cursed Holmauer Park and its waters were being cleansed, but the Blood Orchard, Sculpture Garden and Duelling Fields opportunities were due to lapse after the Winter Solstice. The Duelling Field Menhirs would count towards the College's challenge, and the Memorial Garden could become a Loyalty shrine.

Temeschwar/Locul.t: At Mellfort, the Synod judged the aura of a cavern beneath the mountain to be neither virtuous nor unvirtuous but able to ease sorrow. It could become either a shrine with a Synod title or the Emerald Magpie Guild's Palace of Rest, but not both, and neither opportunity was time-limited.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Bastion is named among the places where rats are a fact of urban life and interest in Georgie's House dogs was growing.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Gildenheim is named among the cities troubled by rats that were taking an interest in Holberg's ratters.

Holberg.t: The College of Engineering in Holberg sought Senate permission to expand, and a commission begun in the city would count towards the Chair of the Wolf challenge. The Senate approved the expansion of Georgie's House kennels, which was set to bring its Custodian an additional 100 rings each season.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Siroc is named among the cities whose citizens know the problem of rats and were looking to Holberg's kennels.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Meade is listed among the cities where rats are a problem and demand for Georgie's House ratters was growing.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos was one of the four cities needing an impressive commission for the Chair of the Wolf, and the College suggested refurbishing Capodomus Cathedral, which some faculty consider long overdue.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim is named among the places plagued by rats, where Holberg-trained ratters were becoming sought after.

Tassato.t: Tassato needed an impressive commission within its walls for the Chair of the Wolf challenge. The Imperial Consulate qualified, but the Tagliano market and the Mestran Hills Mutual Association, built outside the walls, did not.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar needed a qualifying commission for the Chair of the Wolf challenge, and the College said turning Ratibor's Gate or the Red Tower into a shrine blessed with true liao would count. Mellfort's aura offered a choice between a Synod shrine and a Palace of Rest.

A heap of broken images.d: Synod missionaries restored the Hierro's Ambition, Courage and Pride, but the orcs bent the Virtues to excuse raiding and mocked the Labyrinth. The Senate paid them 75 thrones a season, and they asked for 100 mithril or weirwood to rebuild an army of fewer than three thousand fighting-fit orcs. They demanded admission as an eleventh nation with their own homeland, Madruga or Segura, and offered to conquer one if needed. The General Assembly backed Duke Ferrero, who quelled Seguran tensions for the season but could not secure resupply. It also backed Elka Nadyanova Gremani, who drew the Hierro towards orthodoxy with 100 liao. A third judgement inviting them to Holmauer, made without liao, had no effect.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: level-headed Freeborn suggested Reikos, then held by Highguard and up for allocation, as a distant homeland for the Hierro, though it cannot legally be given to foreigners.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Hierro refused point-blank to join the Imperial Orcs, yet cited their homeland as a precedent. Freeborn fears drew on the Senate's earlier transfer of Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs.

Jotun.t: The Hierro named the Jotun to the west as a threat to their exposed camp in south-western Segura, and promised to reclaim Jotun-held Reinos if they became an Imperial nation.

Navarr.t: The Navarr priest Taryn of Exile's End led the Synod's missionary work among the Hierro. His teaching revived their spirit but also produced near-heretical interpretations of the Virtues.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn in Segura and Madruga were alarmed that the Hierro demanded one of their territories as a homeland, and some talked of driving them out. Duke Ferrero's preaching kept the peace in Segura for the season.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn compared Hierro honesty unfavourably to a 'League mountebank', and an unfunded judgement invited the Hierro to visit Holmauer in Holberg.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Freeborn cited the Senate taking Skarsind from Wintermark for the Imperial Orcs as a reason to fear losing Segura.

A heap of broken images.o: In Winter 379YE the displaced Hierro clan of Lasambrian orcs, camped in Segura and taught the Way by Imperial missionaries, grew bolder, formally asked to join the Empire as a new nation with a homeland, and strained relations with their Freeborn neighbours. The Synod answered with judgements urging tolerance and orthodox instruction.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: An unfunded Synod judgement invited the Hierro to come to Holmauer to marvel at its agriculture and wildlife, but it had no immediate effect.

Holberg.t: A General Assembly judgement urged the Hierro to visit Holmauer in Holberg to see more of the Empire, but without liao behind it, it had no immediate effect.

Kalino.t: Mentioned in passing: the Hierro declared they would recover Kalino, then held by the Iron Confederacy, for their new nation if admitted to the Empire.

Madruga.t: The Hierro named Madruga as their preferred homeland because it does not border their enemies, and offered to conquer it if that helped. Locals who knew of the demand were far from pleased.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: some Freeborn suggested Reikos as a distant homeland for the Hierro, though assigning it to foreigners is not legal.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Hierro listed Reinos, held by the Jotun, among the lost territories they would reclaim once established in the Empire.

Segura.t: The Hierro camp south of Anduz grew more permanent as tensions with Freeborn farmers mounted. Duke Ferrero's liao-backed preaching of tolerance quelled the troubles for the Winter, but not enough to let the orcs resupply.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the earlier transfer of Skarsind from Wintermark to the Imperial Orcs was cited by worried Freeborn as a precedent for losing Segura.

A hero's welcome.d: Crowds in Siroc, Necropolis, Sarvos and elsewhere greeted the returning fleets. Inspired by Eska Crowspeaker's mandate, the people housed the freed slaves wherever there was space. Nearly two hundred humans, mostly foreigners, were given the means to go home, as were a handful of Jotun, Thule, Druj and other foreign orcs. The great majority, orcs of the Broken Shore, hate the Grendel, are grateful to the Empire and wish to stay. The civil service suggested Skarsind, the Brass Coast or a League city as homes. The General Assembly upheld Skywise Tulva's mandate for Skarsind by a greater margin than Arno von Leche's competing mandate for the League. It also upheld Eska Crowspeaker's mandate to spread the Way to them.

Druj.t: A few freed Druj were among the rescued orcs and left for home almost at once, despite some concern about returning sworn enemies of the Empire.

Grendel.t: The Grendel lost treasure and nearly two thousand slaves taken from Dubhtraig, and the freed orcs of the Broken Shore now burn with hatred for their former masters.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: crowds in Necropolis were among those welcoming the returning fleets.

Imperial Orcs.t: Skywise Tulva's winning mandate invites the freed orcs to settle in Skarsind, fight their former enslavers or support the legions, and in time become Imperial Orcs by adopting their ways.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: a handful of the freed orcs were Jotun, who returned home quickly despite some unease.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the welcome of the Great Forest orcs into Therunin is cited as a precedent for settling newcomers.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn corsairs rescued many of the slaves, and settling them in the Brass Coast was proposed, but no Freeborn mandate was upheld.

The League.t: The League was proposed as a home for the more ambitious former house slaves, and Arno von Leche's mandate to settle them in League cities was upheld but lost to the Skarsind mandate on margin.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: stalled attempts to bring the thralls of the Mournwold to the Way are cited as a warning about converting the freed orcs.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: a handful of the freed orcs were Thule, who sought to return home.

A hero's welcome.o: Imperial fleets returning from the raid on the Grendel at Dubhtraig were welcomed as heroes, bringing treasure and nearly two thousand freed slaves, most of them orcs of the Broken Shore with nowhere to go. At the Winter Solstice the Synod's General Assembly upheld a mandate settling the freed orcs in Skarsind and another bringing them the Way.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: not named on the page, though the fleets returning from the Broken Shore landed at Imperial ports.

Holberg.t: Holberg was suggested as a possible home for the freed orcs if the Senate funded 15 thrones of travel support, but the League mandate did not prevail.

Madruga.t: Crowds in Siroc welcomed the returning fleets and about a third of the freed slaves were already there, making it a ready option for settling them in the Brass Coast, though this was not chosen.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: attempts to bring the Mournwold's thralls to the Way have stalled, a cautionary example.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: crowds lined the docks of Necropolis to welcome the victorious fleets.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos welcomed the returning fleets and could have taken the freed orcs at no cost, with the College of the Liberated to help them, but the League mandate lost to the Skarsind mandate.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the settlement of the Zemress islanders in Segura is cited as a precedent for welcoming newcomers.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind will receive the freed orcs of the Broken Shore under Skywise Tulva's winning mandate, a long journey the Senate could ease with 20 thrones of support.

Tassato.t: Tassato was named as a League city where the freed orcs could have settled at no cost, but the League mandate did not prevail.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar was suggested as a possible home if the Senate funded 15 thrones of travel support, but the League mandate did not prevail.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the earlier welcome of the Great Forest orcs into Therunin is cited as a precedent.

A horn blast of victory.d: Vesna praised the knights who fought for her against the manticore and pledged to end the Druj. Until the Summer Solstice 389YE, all Dawnish armies could make a triumphant charge against Druj-held regions, but could not take a steady conquest against them. The Northern Eagle had spent the season isolating Lower Saarnath for an Imperial beachhead. Vesna's oath of office was inscribed in the Forge of Bonds. The manticore's surviving vassals and die-hard supporters caused three crises in the Barrens, each offered as a conjunction. The Earl's Council recognised Earl Temperance of the Groves' claim to the manticore's manse, which brings its holder extra materials each season.

Dawn.t: Dawn's pride was stirred by its new queen, letting the Eastern Sky, Golden Sun, Gryphon's Pride and Lions of Adelmar make triumphant charges against the Druj for a year, though not steady conquests. The nation also faced trouble in the Barrens from the manticore's vassals and followers.

Druj.t: The Druj were named as Dawn's ancient enemy, to be destroyed. Their remaining lands in the Salt Flats, Forest of Ulnak and Therunin faced triumphant charges from Dawnish armies for the coming year.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Vesna commended a list of citizens for taking the first successful steps towards diplomacy with the Jotun.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Druj-held regions of Therunin, a territory Navarr shared with the Druj, were among those Dawnish armies could charge.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule push into the Forest of Ulnak was noted as being supported by Imperial mercenaries.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Vesna commended Andronikos of the Lighthouse-That-Was for his victory in Bloodwater Marsh and Arsenio Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato for his service as Grandmaster of the Golden Pyramid.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium was listed among the lands taken from the Druj, and Varushkans were noted as understanding the danger of broken oaths.

A horn blast of victory.o: In Summer 388YE Emperor Vesna, newly crowned Queen of Dawn after the manticore's defeat, addressed the Empire and called the Dawnish to destroy the Druj. Her words filled Dawn's armies with eagerness for glorious charges against the orcs.

Forest of Ulnak/Deathsgate.t: Held by the Druj, Deathsgate was a valid target for Dawnish triumphant charges until Summer 389YE.

Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest.t: Ghul'thak Forest was among the Druj regions Dawnish generals could order triumphant charges against for the coming year.

Forest of Ulnak/Gloomsea.t: Gloomsea was open to Dawnish triumphant charges against its Druj holders, and steady conquests there were barred to Dawn.

Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire.t: Grimfen Mire was named as a Druj region where Dawnish armies could make a triumphant charge.

Forest of Ulnak/Shifting Basin.t: Shifting Basin was listed among the Druj-held regions open to Dawnish triumphant charges for the year.

Forest of Ulnak/The Bonewall.t: The Bonewall was a valid target for Dawnish triumphant charges while it remained in Druj hands.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Lower Saarnath.t: The Northern Eagle had spent three months isolating Lower Saarnath from the Druj garrisons, so that an Imperial beachhead could be claimed with little resistance.

Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh.t: Mentioned in passing: Vesna commended Andronikos of the Lighthouse-That-Was for his monumental victory in Bloodwater Marsh.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: Mentioned in passing: some Gryphon's Pride deserters had left the army when asked to defend Nesustak Forest.

Therunin/East Ashes.t: East Ashes was named among the Druj-held regions where Dawnish armies could make triumphant charges.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: Lower Tarn Valley was open to Dawnish triumphant charges against the Druj until Summer 389YE.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Peakedge Song was a Druj-held region Dawnish generals could target with a triumphant charge.

Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley.t: Upper Tarn Valley was listed as a valid target for Dawnish triumphant charges against the Druj.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Its Druj-held regions became targets for Dawnish triumphant charges, alongside the existing Thule push supported by Imperial mercenaries.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as one of the territories wrested from Druj control, leaving the Mallum smaller than ever.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Described as the last great Druj territory, heavy with miasma and guarded by ancient fortifications. All its regions were open to Dawnish triumphant charges.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: named as newly wrested from Druj control, with a commendation for the victory in Bloodwater Marsh.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Vesna recalled how Dawn's forebears drove the Ulvenkin from Semmerholm.

Therunin.t: East Ashes, Lower Tarn Valley, Peakedge Song and Upper Tarn Valley, held by the Druj, were open to Dawnish triumphant charges for the year.

A horn resounding.d: Believing Wintermark faced its darkest hour, Kirsa and Summer magicians at Rundhal magnified the horn with a ritual. It gave a single note and broke, and no Summer heroes appeared. Later, children under sixteen experienced month-long Summer-driven growth spurts that aged them mentally and physically, prompting emergency citizenship tests. The Seers of the Barren Tree in Woodbury claimed many past heroes had been reborn, and offered a dose of true liao for a young citizen chosen by the Gatekeepers, who duly selected one. The herald Elioe collected children's accounts for the Great Library, and many eternals, even the enemy Agramant, offered boons to Summer Children.

Highguard.t: The Highborn chapter of the Seers of the Barren Tree claimed the Summer Children proved great heroes were being reborn, and supplied a dose of true liao for a young citizen chosen by the Gatekeepers.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Kirsa cites the orcs holding Skarsind as a sign of Wintermark's darkest hour.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Kirsa cites the Jotun holding the ice floes as part of Wintermark's plight.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the legendary Marjatta of the Three Spears is said to have defeated Agramant's champion Jedza Toothunger in the forests of Hercynia.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Marjatta of the Three Spears is remembered as Field Marshal at the Battle of the Golden Groves during the conquest of Karsk.

Wintermark.t: A Wintermark scop judged her nation, reduced to half of what it once was, to be at its darkest hour and spent its long-guarded Horn of Hope, which shattered as it sounded.

A horn resounding.o: Kirsa Wordsmith, a scop of Hahnmark, sounded the century-old Horn of Hope at Rundhal during the Summer Solstice, shattering it, and months later a wave of Summer magic caused many Imperial children to age suddenly by one to three years. The phenomenon drew the interest of the Academy, a Highborn chapter and numerous eternals.

Bastion/Woodbury.t: Woodbury houses the Seers of the Barren Tree's chapter house, from which their stored true liao will go to a young citizen chosen by the Gatekeepers.

Hahnmark/Wood Heath.t: Wood Heath is the home of Kirsa Wordsmith, the scop who bore and sounded the Horn of Hope.

Bastion.t: The Seers of the Barren Tree, founded in Bastion in 317YE, had kept a dose of true liao in their chapter house there awaiting this moment.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Tarsus of Casinea, whose past-life vision inspired the Seers, lived out his days tending fruit trees in his chapter house there.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark is home to Kirsa Wordsmith and the line of scops who guarded the Horn of Hope for over a century.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the forests of Hercynia are where Marjatta of the Three Spears is said to have defeated Jedza Toothunger.

Kallavesa.t: At Rundhal in Kallavesa a coven of Summer magicians helped Kirsa perform the Solstice ritual before she sounded and shattered the horn.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: Marjatta served as Field Marshal at the Battle of the Golden Groves in the conquest of Karsk.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Marjatta is said to have destroyed the Crimson Artok in the mountains above Sermersuaq.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the orcs holding Skarsind is cited by Kirsa as evidence of Wintermark's darkest hour.

A job worth doing.d: Before the Autumn Equinox a powerful Winter curse had raised the Castle of Thorns' upkeep and damaged its structure. Shortly afterwards, koboldi emissaries of King Adamant, summoned by the Spire of the Auric Horizon, appeared overnight. Supernaturally strong, resilient and swift expert masons and engineers, they repaired all structural damage and many minor faults within two days, then departed. The castle was left at full strength and in its best repair since completion. Dawnish enchanters confirmed the koboldi were intelligent Summer beings. Their chief engineer said King Adamant, who admires impressive stonework, would likely send emissaries, and asked about the Conclave and archmages. At the Winter Solstice koboldi visited Anvil, encouraging fortification-building and asking about mines.

Dawn.t: Dawn's great fortress was fully restored at no apparent cost to its people, and Dawnish enchanters gained first-hand knowledge of King Adamant's servants and the eternal's admiration for grand stone structures like the Castle of Thorns.

A job worth doing.o: After the Autumn Equinox 379YE, a band of scaled, lizard-like Summer creatures calling themselves koboldi arrived at the Castle of Thorns in Astolat and, within two days, repaired all the damage left by a recent Winter curse before vanishing. They claimed to serve King Adamant, a Summer eternal previously unknown in the Empire, and had been summoned by the Urizeni Spire of the Auric Horizon.

Astolat.t: The Castle of Thorns in Astolat was cleansed of every lingering effect of the Winter curse and left cleaner and in better repair than at any time since it was completed, after koboldi workers swarmed its walls and thorny battlements for two days.

A knock at the door.d: Ehsan, Lord of Sand, welcomed the Senate's choice of an ambassador (Melkior of Balthazar's Vineyard) without an embassy, which helps protect Beoraidh's neutrality. He appointed his great-nephew Rubhart Kaltrin in return. Beoraidh renewed its offer of land for a temple or basilica of the Way, with halved labour costs if an orc commissions it. It also renewed a dock investment and proposed a salt-for-beef trading post with the Unshackled. It offered to arrange a meeting with the Brine Turtles if the Senate facilitated an introduction to Skoura, and refused to spy for either side. Warlord Bikk proposed a mandate enabling reaver ventures against the Brine Turtles, though Unshackled voices disagreed.

Grendel.t: Beoraidh refuses to spy on the Grendel for the Empire, insisting on strict neutrality. Ehsan offered to spend his favours with his former Grendel peers to arrange talks with their Brine Turtles sept.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Beoraidh, Melkior of Balthazar's Vineyard, is Highborn.

Imperial Orcs.t: Orcs were offered cheaper construction of a temple or basilica of the Way in Beoraidh, and the Unshackled a salt-for-beef trading post. The national assembly was asked to back Warlord Bikk's mandate for reaver raids on the Brine Turtles, amid disagreement among the Unshackled.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark maggots would be welcome to join the proposed raids on the Brine Turtles, and Bikk hoped Winterfolk reavers would attend the discussion at Anvil.

A knock at the door.o: In Spring 388YE the independent city-state of Beoraidh, now under Sarcophan Delves protection, named Rubhart Kaltrin as its ambassador to the Empire and renewed offers of trade, temple-building and diplomacy. Separately, a coalition of reavers proposed raiding the Brine Turtles sept in Mareave, seeking a mandate from the Imperial Orc assembly.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: The city-state appointed Rubhart Kaltrin as ambassador and renewed offers to sell land for a temple of the Way and to take dock investment. It ruled out spying for either side and left any formal colosseum invitation to Imperial warbands on hold.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: Mentioned in passing: refugees from wealthy Clisearn swelled Beoraidh's population during the war.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: Eoradal was offered as a site for the Unshackled trading post on the Sinfoyard border. Beoradhi access to its Grand Aqueduct reportedly requires Skouran agreement.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: The Brine Turtles sept of Fleisardh is the proposed target of reaver raids. If enough force joined the plunder venture, many of the sept would withdraw south to Grendel-protected lands.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Warlord Bikk moved his Legion to Icarion to coordinate the proposed raids, and Icarion was offered as a site for the salt-for-beef trading post.

Mareave/Sinfoyard.t: Sinfoyard forms part of Ehsan's planned neutral state, and Beoraidh proposed building its matching trading post on the Sinfoyard side of the border. A temple of the Way would preach to its orcs.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: with the Children of Wrecks apparently on the way out, Beoraidh may be able to fish the bay's waters again.

Mareave.t: Beoraidh balances between the Empire, the Grendel and the Sarcophan Delves while fighting continues across the territory. Reavers proposed raiding the Brine Turtles sept to cut army supplies or drive them out.

Skarsind.t: If the proposed salt-for-beef trading post were built, the Shepherd of the Great Herd in Skarsind would gain 5 extra crowns each season from access to Beoradhi salt.

A lasting commitment.d: Rafael Barossa's statement, upheld with a greater majority, invoked the Hallowing of the Patron. A Synod mandate could spread word that the Grand Inspiration would open as 388YE turned to 389YE; success would inspire the faithful, and failure carries no penalty. The Highborn Assembly proposed seven gardens for the Voices of Virtue, giving each five liao a season and creating the Annals of Virtue. Highborn benefactors also offered the Guildmaster of the Artisans four thrones a season to arrange regalia for the Voices. Further options were residentiary canons or national speakers housed in the edifice, and a choristers balcony if a mandate drew Highborn cantors to Bastion.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly's highest calling now sets the shape of the Grand Inspiration, and a Highguard mandate could revive the nation's cantor tradition with a choristers balcony at its heart, while Nicodemus's Speaker role is proposed as a model for other nations.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the Archbishop of Capodomus, Estella Lucati, is listed among existing national titles that could take up offices in the Grand Inspiration.

A lasting commitment.o: In Summer 388YE the Ambition Assembly declared completing the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion within a single year to be its highest calling, while the Highborn Assembly began deciding how the vast edifice should be laid out and who should occupy it.

Bastion.t: Bastion is where the Grand Inspiration is being built. If it is completed by the start of 389YE, all eyes will be on the construction and Bastion could become the heart of the Way, with possible new gardens, offices and a choristers balcony within the edifice.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the great walls of Holberg are cited as smaller than the Grand Inspiration, the largest commission ever undertaken in the Empire.

A long December.d: Snowstorm Henk will still complete Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti's research into the orcs who guarded Emperor Ahraz's tomb. A skeleton crew will keep aiding the Great Library of Hacynian, delaying its vallorn investigation to Summer 386YE while allowing one research commission per season. The Department can now support only one of three titles: the Minister of Historical Research, the Advisor on the Vallorn or the Imperial Advisor for the Feni. An administrative motion will decide which, or none. Gerard La Salle proposed auctioning the right to direct research through the Bourse. Ris Steelfist's patron-funded plan replaces the Senate's 22-throne bodyguard payment, and military units can now take on the War of Whispers adventure.
