Highguard.t: Highguard's scholars are helping to speed the vallorn research, and wealthy Highborn chapters are among the patrons funding heroes to protect scholars from the Whisper Gallery.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Archivist remarks that one of his scholars would quickly be caught by the Jotun if he became a war scout.

Navarr.t: The Department will still give skeleton support to assembling the Navarr archives at the Great Library of Hacynian, but the vallorn investigation will now finish at the Summer Solstice 386YE. The Whisper Gallery's agents tried to set fire to the library.

The League.t: The League's support is helping the vallorn research. The Lepidean University was targeted by Whisper Gallery arsonists, and League scholarship faces the same threat that the new protection fund is meant to counter.

Urizen.t: Urizen spires are among the patrons funding heroes to protect scholars. Octavia of Stream's Source Spire now leads one of the Department's three research teams.

A long December.o: Following the Winter Solstice, the Department of Historical Research was left badly stretched after staff were retrained as prognosticators and assigned to vallorn research, while the Whisper Gallery renewed its murderous campaign against Imperial scholars. The Imperial Archivist set out changes to the Department and a plan to fight back.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: information recovered from Brocéliande is helping to shorten the vallorn research for the Great Library.

Holberg.t: The opportunity that came with consecrating the Walls of Holberg led the Senate to retrain Department researchers as prognosticators, which helped leave the Department short of scholars.

A long good-bye.d: Following the Sarvos raids, three priests named by the Synod rallied citizens, militia and magistrates against the vyig. Vladimir von Temeschwar led the effort in Holberg, Valimir von Temeschwar in Tassato and Irada von Temeschwar in Temeschwar, where the vyig fought back with arms and fire. Their operations in Tassato and Holberg were ended, and their Temeschwar ring was smashed. The leader Bollek was believed dead, though questions remained about his fate. The upheaval reduced business income in the four cities by a quarter. Five confiscated vyig assets were to be auctioned at the Winter Solstice, but bad weather prevented this and the auction was rescheduled for Spring 380YE.

Dawn.t: Several dozen Dawnish questing knights and knights-errant joined the sweep of Holberg alongside Vladimir von Temeschwar.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the vyig are said to have mostly deserted Holberg during the earlier Druj siege.

Navarr.t: Wily Navarr thorns helped uncover a trade in stolen goods passing between Mestra and Regario in Tassato.

The League.t: League citizens led the fight against the vyig in their cities, freeing Holberg and Tassato of the criminals and smashing their Temeschwar operations, at the cost of a quarter of their business income for the season.

Varushka.t: Varushkan schlacta and volhov joined the hunt for vyig in Temeschwar, and goods stolen from Varushka were found being smuggled south through Bartelli's Bolt.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: goods stolen from Wintermark were among those smuggled through Bartelli's Bolt for sale to overseas buyers.

A long good-bye.o: In the autumn of 379YE, priests of vigilance led a League-wide campaign against the vyig in Holberg, Tassato and Temeschwar that broke the criminal conspiracy, although the disruption cut business incomes in those cities for the season.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Several armed clashes took place in the ruins of Holmauer, where the vyig had been trying to build criminal dens among the rubble.

Semmerholm/Estmure.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial orc camp at Estcastle sent thief-takers to help in Holberg.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: The vyig enforcers of Auntie Vivian fled Mestra after murdering Uncle Uzo, and the merrow Carta de Fimi Nacoso, forced into ferrying stolen goods after its head was blackmailed, was seized for auction.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: Pressing Matters, a Regario printworks secretly used by confidence tricksters who had tried to counterfeit Bourse certificates, was seized, and Regario lost Callista di Tassato Regario of the Charitable Chain of Andromeo.

Temeschwar/Hanuri.t: The militia shut down Auntie Bimber's Palinka, a Hanuri tavern used as neutral ground by vyig factions, and offered its largely intact premises for auction.

Temeschwar/Locul.t: Mentioned in passing: Locul is not named directly and is covered only as part of the wider Temeschwar campaign.

Holberg.t: Holberg was searched with help from orc thief-takers and Dawnish knights, ending vyig operations there, and the seized Tunnel Snakes smuggling network was earmarked for sale to an honest owner.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the summer raids in Sarvos are named as the start of the campaign, and the opening story tells of a vyig Uncle driven out of the city.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: thief-takers from the Imperial orc camp at Estcastle came to help hunt the vyig in Holberg.

Tassato.t: Valimir von Temeschwar brokered a temporary truce between rival Princes, and by winter the vyig were no longer a force in the twin city, though Callista di Tassato Regario and several allies died in the fight.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar saw a week of open battles in the city and nearby forests, weapon caches and plans for insurrection were uncovered, and the vyig ring was smashed with help from the Vardstein Voyi bravos.

A lost king.d: The Black Forge in Gildermark began slowly arming the Ethengraw, who also bought paper to rebuild their Epic. The Senate could now raise a new Imperial Orc army from the Ethengraw for 200 mithril and 50 thrones over a year, but it must bear a Proud name and must not be called a third legion. The Illarawm Ossuary in Southpine opened, and its mystagogues began collecting ancestors' names, stories and bones across Skarsind. The Yerende garden is paid for and expected by the Equinox. Following Archmage Gralka's judgement, the Assembly could adopt the name Sunstorm Sept by mandate. Apulian, Mournwold and Great Forest orcs may join other nations.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: they are named as the former overlords who broke the Ethengraw, destroyed every copy of their Epic and scattered the Illarawm's ancestral bones.

Imperial Orcs.t: The nation stands to gain the Ethengraw, Illarawm and Yerende as septs at the Autumn Equinox. It may also raise a new Ethengraw army and was invited to adopt the name Sunstorm Sept for the descendants of Thrace.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: there are signs that some Great Forest Orcs might one day join the Navarr.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the Apulian orcs look set to join the League, and Tassato is used as a comparison of scale.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold orcs have been looking to join the Marchers for years.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bone Temple's modest exterior is likened to a tiny Urizen temple.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium, now Varushkan-held, is where the Ethengraw once ruled and which the three septs left together.

A lost king.o: The Imperial Orcs completed two of the three great follies promised to the orc septs from Ossium: the Black Forge for the Ethengraw and the Bone Temple ossuary for the Illarawm. The septs resolved to join the Imperial Orcs together at the Autumn Equinox, once the Yerende garden is finished.

Skarsind/Gildermark.t: The Black Forge was completed here, its dozen forges running night and day to arm the Ethengraw, who also bought paper and blank books traded from Gildermark.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: The Illarawm Ossuary, a vast bone-lined crypt beneath a modest temple, was completed here, and its mystagogues set out into southern Skarsind to record ancestors and collect bones.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: its orcs are noted as having long sought to join the Marchers.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ethengraw recall once ruling all of Ossium, and the three septs left it together.

Skarsind.t: The Black Forge and the Illarawm Ossuary were completed here, the Yerende garden is under way, and Illarawm mystagogues toured local villages gathering ancestors' names, stories and bones.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: comparing the Ossuary with the Black Forge is likened to comparing Tassato with a hamlet.

A mountain of vipers.d: After the Axou rejected slavery and Maximillian Ankarien's mandate urged trade, the new Grand Ilarch Andronicus opened Issyk's port and invited the Empire to build Imperial docks there for 30 wains of weirwood and 60 crowns. Issyk and Maykop traders added streams to the Quaymaster of the Black Sails and the Eastern Broker. The Purple Sails and the Sarvos and Tassato Chambers of Commerce asked the Synod whether selling liao to Axos was acceptable, and two competing mandates were proposed. Hesychia of Elos proposed the Elosian Docks in Redoubt to trade dragonbone for white granite. Maykop offered a student exchange and ilium through a proposed House of Spirits. All offers would lapse after Winter Solstice 383YE.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat and Semmerholm are listed among the Blood Red Roads territories where the proposed House of Spirits could be built.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Tanwyn Ankarien is recalled as having led Imperial mercenaries to help Ipotavo fight off a Druj invasion.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Issyk's former alliance with the orcs of the Broken Shore is recalled, and the new Grand Ilarch is critical of Issyk's dealings with the Grendel.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is a candidate site for the House of Spirits, and the Litharge in Necropolis is named as a place Axou students might attend.

Navarr.t: If the Eastern Broker's offices survive the vallorn, the Navarr title would gain a third stream to buy cerulean mazzarine, ambergelt and green iron from Issyk. A Navarr scholar's account of Maykop is cited, and Miaren is a candidate site for the House of Spirits.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn Fellowship of Purple Sails helped put the question of the liao trade to the Synod, hoping to profit from Axou demand. Madruga is a candidate site for the House of Spirits.

The League.t: League merchants were central to the push: the Chambers of Commerce of Sarvos and Tassato put the liao question to the Synod, and Issyk sent ships to Sarvos. Four League cities are candidate sites for the House of Spirits, and the University of Holberg might receive Axou students.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is listed among the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.

Urizen.t: Urizen citizen Hesychia of Elos proposed refitting the docks at Elos in Redoubt to trade dragonbone for Axou white granite. Urizen's places of learning would also welcome Axou students if the Senate opened its universities to them.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Karov is listed among the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is listed among the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.

A mountain of vipers.o: Following a Summer Solstice Synod mandate urging trade with Axos, a series of time-limited Axou trade and diplomatic opportunities opened to the Empire in Autumn 383YE. They included a new port at Issyk, a liao market, white granite for dragonbone and a student exchange with Maykop.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Mentioned in passing: the Litharge of Necropolis is named as a likely destination for Axou students; no specific location within the territory is given.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.

Holberg.t: Holberg is a candidate site for the House of Spirits, and its University is named among the institutions Axou students would seek to join if the Senate opened its universities to them.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Karov is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the prestigious Litharge in Necropolis is named among the places Axou students would seek to attend if the student exchange went ahead.

Redoubt.t: Hesychia of Elos proposed refitting the old docks at Elos to welcome Axou traders, exchanging dragonbone for white granite. The work would need a Senate motion and commission, 30 wains of weirwood and 60 crowns, and would create a Quaymaster of the Elosian Docks title.

Sarvos.t: Issyk sent ships to Sarvos announcing that its port was open to Imperial trade. The Sarvos Chamber of Commerce joined the delegation asking the Synod to rule on the liao trade, and Sarvos is a candidate site for the House of Spirits.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.

Tassato.t: The Tassato Chamber of Commerce helped bring the liao question to the Synod, prompted by merchants such as Mariana di Tassato. The city is also a candidate site for the House of Spirits.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is one of the Blood Red Roads territories where the House of Spirits could be built.

A murder of one.d: Three kinds of Spring boggart appeared: crow-like Corbs that unmake crafted things, Greenteeth that lure rescuers to stagnant water and kill them, and Grimmelkint that feed on forests and curse anyone who harms them. Unless they are dealt with, every forest faces a two-rank production penalty. Professor Beatrice of Holberg suggested herding those heading for Anvil back through the Hall of Worlds portal. Arhallogen proposed a Navarr Synod mandate urging merciless war on the Jotun; Corey Wayfarer and Nathair Autumngale offered competing alternatives. High Priestess Shivaarn asked the Conclave to lift Siakha's enmity, promising only a half-dozen observing heralds and no attack on the Conclave for two seasons.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Arhallogen's open patronage of the Druj orcs is cited as what makes the eternal a problematic ally.

Grendel.t: Three rough Grendel orcs from the Temple of Tempest Jade carried High Priestess Shivaarn's offer on Siakha's behalf, hinting at the imminent shattering of the Grendel treaty. Shivaarn may care more for her goddess than for the Salt Lords' concerns.

Jotun.t: Arhallogen wants the Navarr to stop sparing Jotun lives. If the mandate passes, Navarr armies would inflict 10% more casualties on the orcs of Narkyst, Kalsea and Lasambria for a year, and the slaughter would be plain to every force in the territory.

Navarr.t: The Navarr assembly could enact Arhallogen's mandate, gaining 10% more casualties against the Jotun at the cost of 20% fewer victory points and earning an arcane projection from the eternal. Alternatively it could take Corey Wayfarer's version without the projection, or Nathair Autumngale's rejection, which would keep thorns to balanced attack or solid defence.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Segura is named among the places whose forests the Grimmelkint are swarming, and a Freeborn corsair's boastful letters drew Siakha's attention.

The League.t: Greenteeth caused unpleasant incidents in Holberg, and Professor Beatrice of Holberg proposed herding the Grimmelkint back through the Hall of Worlds portal. She also speculated that they might one day coexist with forest owners.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen marks one edge of the Grimmelkint swarms descending on Imperial forests.

Varushka.t: Small groups of Greenteeth were sighted in Ossium, and Varushkan forests fall within the Grimmelkint swarms' reach. The tale's Varushkan heroine, Sasha, fights the beasts in Inga Tarn's name.

Wintermark.t: Greenteeth struck in Kallavesa, and Sermersuaq's forests face Grimmelkint swarms. Wintermark's 381YE mandate urging honourable war against the Jotun is what Arhallogen scorns.

A murder of one.o: In Spring 385YE, Hallow of the Green World pried open Spring regio across the Empire. Boggarts spilled out, Grimmelkint swarms threatened every Imperial forest, Arhallogen urged the Navarr to slaughter the Jotun, and Siakha offered a short truce through a Grendel high priestess.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Temple of Tempest Jade that sent Siakha's message lies on the far side of the Bay of Catazar.

Holberg.t: Greenteeth lurking in stagnant water caused unpleasant incidents here, and Holberg's Professor Beatrice led the study of the boggarts.

Kallavesa.t: Greenteeth ambushed travellers in Kallavesa's marshes by mimicking cries for help, as in the tale of Ulf Unmelten and Sasha, and there were real incidents here.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Ulf jokes that monsters belong in Karov, not Kallavesa.

Ossium.t: Small groups of Greenteeth were sighted in Ossium.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Segura is named as one extent of the Grimmelkint swarms threatening Imperial forests.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is named as one extent of the Grimmelkint swarms threatening Imperial forests.

A peerless sacrifice.d: Peerless kinship had let Highguard aid the Freeborn in Kahraman, the Dawnish in the Barrens, the orcs of Skarsind and the Marches in the Mournwold, with Therunin to follow. After a Greater Majority statement by Nicodemus of Balthazar's Vineyard, the faithful proved unable to sustain both kinship and crusade, so competing mandates were offered. The Assembly upheld Judgement 116, sending Brother Olyvar of Esther's Sanctum to urge embracing peerless kinship. The Assembly may now choose any nation to aid, though not the same nation two seasons running. Highborn armies will no longer automatically generate mandates. The Benefactors' Council, which could have redirected Highguard's ten wains each season to any civilian commission, kept them going to the Grand Inspiration of the Way.

Dawn.t: Dawn had earlier received Highborn peerless kinship to help contact the factions in the Barrens, and its people could be chosen again under the retained power.

Highguard.t: Highguard chose peerless kinship over crusade, so its armies no longer automatically generate mandates. Its benefactors kept donating ten wains a season of white granite towards the Grand Inspiration of the Way.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs had been helped through peerless kinship to better understand the Ossium septs, and remain eligible for future Highborn aid.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: a renewed crusade power would likely have taken the form of the recent call for an ongoing crusade against the Jotun, but this option was not chosen.

Navarr.t: The Navarr were named as the next recipients of Highborn peerless kinship in Therunin, and the Highborn were preparing for war with the vallorn alongside the returning grey pilgrims.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn had received Highborn peerless kinship in Kahraman, and the retained power means the Brass Coast could be aided again in future.

The Marches.t: The Marches had been helped by Highguard to deal with threats in the Mournwold, and Highborn armies rested and resupplied in Upwold this season.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not discussed, though Highborn benefactors from a group called Reumah's Redoubt are listed.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn kinship helped the Imperial Orcs understand the septs of Ossium, a Varushkan territory.

A peerless sacrifice.o: Highguard was forced to choose between keeping its power of peerless kinship towards other nations and its armies' power of crusade. The Highborn Assembly enacted a mandate retaining peerless kinship, and the Benefactors' Council chose to keep supporting the Grand Inspiration of the Way.

Astolat.t: Highborn armies took a much-needed rest in Astolat this season, resupplying rather than campaigning.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman was one of the places where Highguard's peerless kinship had helped the Freeborn.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: an in-character vignette notes that a listed benefactor is a corsair from Madruga.

Mournwold.t: Highguard's peerless kinship had helped the Marches deal with threats in the Mournwold.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn kinship had helped the Imperial Orcs better understand the Ossium septs.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory itself is not discussed, though benefactors of Reumah's Redoubt appear in the list.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind was where Highborn kinship had helped the Imperial Orcs better understand the Ossium septs.

The Barrens.t: Highguard's peerless kinship had aided the Dawnish in contacting the factions of the Barrens.

Therunin.t: Therunin was named as the next place where Highguard would offer peerless kinship in the weeks to come.

Upwold.t: Highborn armies rested and resupplied in Upwold this season instead of campaigning.

A pillow of winds.d: Faraden asked what non-military help it could give against the Jotun, and suggested capturing Flareizo, Chaveiro and Cimeira. High Lord Ganzorig Muhnkhabat asked for a Rod and Shield honour guard to escort his war-wizards to Anvil through Reinos, while Mistress Karadragha proposed that the Celestial Arch soften the visit's political impact. Caitun now offered luxury goods in place of weltsilver. The Hakhandra family offered to buy Marcher cattle bonds, and the Tseriyn offered mithril for gloaming. The Parador of Wind and Flame was completed at the Azure Chorus. A Holberg trading enclave awaited the Chamber of Commerce's choice of goods. Conservative Faraden priests invited Imperial preachers, and the Ember Blossoms sought Freeborn passage to Asavea.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: described as the opportunistic Asavean ally already in the Empire's back yard.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as one of the nations a Faraden caravan could trade with along the Blood Red Roads.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Faraden ambassador said any Sand Fishers visiting Holberg would be welcomed as Imperial Orcs are.

Jotun.t: The Faraden treaty with the Jotun stopped Faraden aiding the Imperial invasion of Reinos. The civil service warned that this peace holds only while the Jotun focus on the Empire, and the proposed Muhnkhabat journey through Reinos risked provoking them.

The Brass Coast.t: The Azure Sutannir completed the Parador of Wind and Flame in Kahraman and gained added weight with the Faraden. Separately, the Ember Blossoms sought the Freeborn National Assembly's help in reaching Asavea.

The League.t: Faraden remained keen on a trading enclave in Holberg but needed the Holberg Chamber of Commerce to choose cloth, spice, iron or none. The ambassador also answered League concerns about orcs, the Holberg Gate and the Bishops' judgement.

The Marches.t: The Hakhandra offered to buy up to 16 Marcher cattle bonds and would back Yakholme Grange, and the Tseriyn offered the Alder of Meade mithril for iridescent gloaming. Faraden appetite for Marcher food and Upwold confectionery remained strong.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as a nation a Faraden caravan could trade with on its way across the Empire.

A pillow of winds.o: In Spring 387YE the Civil Service reported on relations with Faraden. The Court of the Five Winds welcomed the Imperial invasion of Reinos but could not give military aid because of its treaty with the Jotun, and the report set out trade, magical and religious opportunities.

Holberg/Holfried.t: Mentioned in passing: not named on the page, which is linked here through the wider Holberg enclave plans, including a Firewind Market in the upper city.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: The parkland of Holmauer was favoured for the Faraden caravan enclave, and a small Hall of Five Flames temple there was described as a deal-breaker for the merchant families.

Reinos/Chaveiro.t: Faraden named the capture of Chaveiro as one of three conquests that would best secure a safe land trade route between the two nations.

Reinos/Cimeira.t: Faraden named the capture of Cimeira as one of three conquests that would best secure a safe land trade route between the two nations.

Reinos/Flareizo.t: Faraden named the capture of Flareizo as one of three conquests that would best secure a safe land trade route between the two nations.

Holberg.t: Faraden proposed the Firewind Market and a caravan enclave with a Hall of Five Flames in Holberg, pending the Chamber of Commerce's choice of trade goods. Faraden merchants might avoid the Holberg Gate because of its False Flame aura.

Kahraman.t: The Parador of Wind and Flame was completed at the Azure Chorus, drawing Faraden entertainers to celebrate alongside Imperial pilgrims, though their journey still meant paying Jotun tolls in Reinos.

Mitwold.t: Faraden merchants were waiting to see whether Mitwold or Upwold became the leading cattle market before choosing where to trade, and the Hakhandra sought cattle bonds from both markets.

Reinos.t: The Court of Five Winds welcomed the Imperial invasion but could not send troops. It sought other ways to help drive out the Jotun, and the Muhnkhabat planned a provocative journey through the Lasambrian Hills.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Faraden ambassador called the sea of snow too dangerous for safe commerce, which is why Faraden merchants will not take to ships.

Upwold.t: The Marcher ambassador proposed reviving Moonwater Hall in Upwold as Yakholme Grange, and Upwold's liquorice confectionery was in fashion among wealthy Faraden. Faraden merchants were still weighing Upwold against Mitwold as a cattle market.

A pinch of salt.d: After Aliss Thorn's mandate sent artisans to Oakwood, the recovered smiths revealed their lost art was forging bargains, not crafting. A friar proposed the Stone Smith's Workshop sinecure, costing 8 white granite, 8 mithril, 8 ilium and 6 thrones, built at the Woldstone (Ashbrook, Upwold) or the Maiden Stone (Maiden Downs, Mitwold). The Stone Smith, appointed by the Tally of the Votes, would receive 1 throne each season; if a smith, they would also gain a pauper's key each Spring and, through Renna Whitesmith's ancient bargain with the herald Gull, an annual plenipotentiary-like invitation to an eternal each Autumn. Upwold and Mitwold smiths dispute the site. The opportunity ends if not commissioned by the Winter Solstice 387YE.

The Marches.t: The Marches may revive the smiths' lost art of bargaining by commissioning a workshop and electing a Stone Smith, though rival Upwold and Mitwold smiths have left the choice of site to the nation.

A pinch of salt.o: The smiths freed from the Woldstone in Summer 386YE, having recovered with the monks of Oakwood, offered the Marches the chance to commission a Stone Smith's Workshop at either the Woldstone in Upwold or the Maiden Stone in Mitwold, creating the title of Stone Smith.

Mitwold/Maiden Downs.t: The Maiden Stone on the Maiden Downs, a site echoing with magic, is proposed as a possible home for the Stone Smith's Workshop.

Upwold/Ashbrook.t: The Woldstone at Ashbrook, the regio where the smiths were trapped for centuries, is proposed as a possible home for the Stone Smith's Workshop.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold is one of two candidate locations for the Stone Smith's Workshop, and its returned smiths insist the Maiden Stone should be chosen.

Upwold.t: Upwold is one of two candidate locations for the Stone Smith's Workshop, with its smiths, including Jack Hammersmith, arguing for the Woldstone.

A place on a map.d: Gerard La Salle chose the frugal Escovitch for the appraisal. He proposed a fortification at Willstone guarding the Crow Road (70 wains of white granite, 140 crowns, one year, upkeep cut to 5 thrones). In Morrow he proposed four citadels at the Three Watchers (140 wains, 280 crowns, two years, or one with a Synod mandate). In Spiral, Fort Mezudan could be rebuilt (60 wains, 130 crowns, three seasons) if Ateri were Imperial. For Zenith, old records suggest help from Meraud or the tulpa Phellem, or permanent magical citadels with eternal approval. Escovitch then retired, and Lutomysla Niegoslava replaced him.

Druj.t: The Druj hold Zenith and recently attacked Morrow. The proposed Morrow citadels would exploit their evident fear of the Three Watchers, and any Zenith fortification options depend on wresting regions back from them.

Grendel.t: The Grendel's Crow Road from Cinion is identified as an undefended invasion route into Redoubt. Their control of Spiral bars any building there unless Ateri is retaken or Salt Lord Kaliact can be persuaded to cede a rebuilt Fort Mezudan.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: securing Therunin is named alongside liberating Zenith as necessary to end the Druj threat to Morrow.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule's permanent Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae, conjured in the Silver Peaks in 379YE, is cited as a precedent for magically created fortifications in Zenith.

Urizen.t: Urizen received a costed plan for fortifying each of its territories, from Willstone and the Three Watchers to Fort Mezudan. One option calls on the Urizen Assembly to uphold a mandate sending liao to speed garrisoning of the Morrow citadels.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Varushkan Mladen Escovitch wrote the appraisal before retiring to Miekarova, and his successor Lutomysla Niegoslava is a cabalist from Karov.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark is not named, though the Silver Peaks in Sermersuaq are cited as the site of an earlier permanent Frozen Citadel.

A place on a map.o: In Spring 384YE, the civil servant Mladen Escovitch delivered the Senate-requested appraisal of how each Urizen territory might be fortified, including Druj-held Zenith and Grendel-held Spiral. He named fortification opportunities, and their costs, for each.

Redoubt/Optarion.t: Mentioned in passing: Optarion lies at the Redoubt end of the Onyx Path to Ateri, which a rebuilt Fort Mezudan would help defend.

Redoubt/Willstone.t: Willstone's existing citadel could be expanded to guard the Crow Road. The fortification would deter orc bandits troubling visitors to the Grand Conservatory of Music, and charging merchants to store wagons in its courtyard would halve its upkeep.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Mentioned in passing: a permanent Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae was conjured here by the Thule in Winter 379YE, costing an estimated 240 rings of ilium.

Spiral/Ateri.t: The ruined Fort Mezudan in Ateri could be rebuilt in three seasons for 60 wains and 130 crowns if the Empire controlled the region. While the Onyx Path and the Court of the White Fountain stayed Imperial, the fort would qualify for automatic repair.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Mentioned in passing: Cinion is the Spiral end of the undefended Crow Road, by which Grendel armies could strike at Willstone.

Zenith/Clypion.t: Clypion is named as suitable for a permanent Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae, created instantly once the region was held, given ilium and the eternal's consent.

Zenith/Lustri.t: An ancient record tells of the tulpa Phellem in Lustri's forests offering to help "secure" them; finding it would need a scouting army and then negotiating magicians. A permanent Wooden Fastness is also feasible, though which eternal to approach is unknown.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Occursion is named as suitable for a permanent Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae if the region were held and the eternal agreed.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Proceris could host a permanent Basalt Citadel if Sorin's approval were secured. A permanent Dripping Echoes of the Fen is also possible, though which eternal to ask is unclear.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Escovitch's replacement, Lutomysla Niegoslava, is a cabalist from Karov.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: Escovitch is retiring to spend his remaining years with his family in Miekarova.

Morrow.t: Morrow, unfortified and recently attacked by the Druj, could gain four citadels around the Three Watchers forming a fortification of strength six thousand. Other options include fortified sword scholar temples and perhaps codifying Phaleron's crystal-sheathing ritual used at Canterspire.

Redoubt.t: Already guarded by the Walls of Cargo and the Court of the White Fountain, Redoubt could close its undefended Crow Road with a new fortification at Willstone. The eternal Adamant has also offered to strengthen the Court of the White Fountain.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the permanent Frozen Citadel conjured by the Thule in the Silver Peaks is cited as a precedent.

Spiral.t: Ceded to the Grendel by treaty, Spiral cannot host Imperial construction. Fort Mezudan could be rebuilt cheaply if Ateri were retaken or Salt Lord Kaliact agreed to cede it.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: securing Therunin is named as necessary, with liberating Zenith, before the Druj threat to Morrow ends.

Zenith.t: Too dangerous to survey, Zenith was assessed from old records instead. Options include Meraud's century-old offer of Summer basalt in return for a thousand pieces of tempest jade, and help from the tulpa Phellem. Permanent magical citadels conjured with an eternal's approval are another possibility.

A pleasing and deceptive face.d: Eleonaris refused a parley but invited named courtiers to meet her diplomats in the Hall of Fellowship. Surut offered parley to the Winter Archmage and asked to meet several named groups. Estavus proposed a veilingmarkt auction of goods and enchantments for materials. Lashonar opened the Caucus Forum to the Archmage of Night and the Imperial Consul. Kimus agreed to parley with the Archmage of Day, the Imperial Seer, Spymaster and Penumbral Watcher, but rejected a general meeting on magic. A briar emissary told Navarr vates at the Broch that Yaw'nagrah would grant no audience. A Jarmish magician delivered Ter Andzrev's request; the Imperial Archivist found the name may belong to Ossegrahn, an eternal once declared an enemy by the Conclave.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish Archmage of Spring, Ser Fabienne De Miel, was refused a parley by Yaw'nagrah, told the favour shown to last year's Dawnish archmage would not be repeated, and was asked by "Lord Rain" to attend a formal parley; Urien Novarion of Dawn was also invited to meet Eleonaris's diplomats.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Yaw'nagrah's briar emissary accused the Navarr of preferring to embrace the Druj over the gifts of the Green Mother.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the page closes with a quotation on the deceptive faces of eternals from Saul of Cantiarch's Hold, a Highborn magister writing in 27YE.

Imperial Orcs.t: Skywise Gralka of the Imperial Orcs, Archmage of Day, was invited by Kimus to bring the Imperial Seer, Spymaster and Penumbral Watcher to meet two senior heralds, though her request for a general meeting on magic was refused.

Navarr.t: Navarr vates and thorns at the Broch received and passed on Yaw'nagrah's hostile message, then turned their backs on the briar emissary mid-speech; separately, Syn Truth-Walker Returned of Navarr, Archmage of Winter, was offered a midnight parley with Surut.

Urizen.t: Two Urizen archmages received answers: Edmundo of Damakan's Forge, Archmage of Autumn, was offered Estavus's veilingmarkt and talks on construct use, and Elyssiathain, Archmage of Night, was granted entry to Lashonar's Caucus Forum.

A pleasing and deceptive face.o: Following the Summer Solstice, six eternals answered the Imperial archmages' plenipotentiary messages for the Autumn Equinox 383YE: five agreed to meetings of some kind, Yaw'nagrah declined, and a little-known Spring eternal calling itself "Lord Rain" unexpectedly requested a formal parley.

Brocéliande.t: A briar emissary of Yaw'nagrah, flanked by two towering tree-creatures, delivered the Green Mother's refusal of parley at the Broch amid the Navarr's muted celebration of the vallorn's defeat, before withdrawing into the trees without violence.

A question of loyalty.d: The Urizen Assembly's mandate urging Urizen to stay apart from Apulian until a reckoning was supported by the Loyalty Assembly, whose Eyes of Loyalty turned simmering resentment into open secession. Three factions now stand together. Tiborion wants the Imperial Mint moved from Tassato to Cargo as an Urizen seat. Caela demands that Spiral be returned to Urizen. Actius seeks a Treasury-funded office paying 35 thrones a season for Vale of Shadows, using Sung's boon. Sung's shrouds make the rebels nearly impossible to bring to heel. Further mandates could spread the rebellion across Spiral or into Urizen, and the Black Plateau may stir.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's earlier cession of Spiral and Feroz is described as buying time to defeat the Druj, and Spiral's Urizen are noted as having endured Druj attacks.

Grendel.t: If the Senate returned Spiral to Urizen, Kaliact's followers would turn on her, and Apulian, Apulus and Apstrus would revert to Grendel control. Many in Apulian are still legally Grendel.

The League.t: The League's new hold on Spiral faces armed secession, and its Assembly's pledged reckoning is tested by demands such as giving up the Mint at Tassato. Its Assembly may propose mandates to influence its own people in Spiral.

Urizen.t: Urizen citizens in Spiral split by loyalty: some are moving to Zenith and Redoubt, while others have taken up arms. Further mandates could spread the rebellion across Spiral or, if the Empire uses force, into the rest of Urizen.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the rebels recall the Wintermark thane Dogri Thulebane, who was dragged to Anvil for execution after an earlier secession.

A question of loyalty.o: In Autumn 385YE, Urizen spires in Spiral rebelled against the Empire and seized Ankra and Cinion, after the Loyalty Assembly's Eyes of Loyalty amplified Hector's Urizen Assembly mandate. Naomi of Virtue's Rest set out the rebel factions' demands and possible remedies.

Spiral/Ankra.t: Rebels have seized Ankra and declared it part of Urizen. It is home to Tiborion of the Endless Horizen, who leads the faction seeking the Mint's move.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: Apstrus would fall back under Grendel control alongside Apulian if the Senate returned Spiral to Urizen.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Apulus would revert to Grendel control if Spiral were restored to Urizen and Kaliact's followers turned on her.

Spiral/Ateri.t: Rebels in Ateri could rise and seize the region if a further Synod mandate urges the remaining Spiral Urizen to take up arms, unless an Imperial army stops them.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Rebel spires have seized Cinion, declared it Urizen and rejected the authority of the Imperial Senate.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: Outraged spires here are preparing for rebellion, and a further mandate could see them seize the region unless an Imperial army intervenes.

Spiral/Screed.t: The Black Plateau at Screed's heart may stir again if the situation escalates, and rebels here could seize the region under a further mandate.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: it was given to the Grendel along with Spiral in the peace treaty that Urizen loyalists resent.

Redoubt.t: Empire-loyal Urizen are relocating here, and Tiborion's faction proposes a Senate commission to build a new Imperial Mint in Cargo as an Urizen national seat.

Spiral.t: Rebel spires have seized Ankra and Cinion and declared them Urizen. Sung's Vale of Shadows hides them from Imperial armies, and unrest risks rousing the Black Plateau.

Tassato.t: Tassato would lose the Imperial Mint, decommissioned there and re-established in Cargo, if the Senate accepted Tiborion's proposed reckoning.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Senate's earlier motion asking Naomi to appraise the septs of the Barrens failed.

Zenith.t: Many Spiral Urizen loyal to the Empire are moving here, and mithril statues on the passes from Spiral are to link the spires with Zenith and Redoubt.

A question of provenance.d: As Spring magic transformed Reikos, eerie fungi spread through vinum, grain and produce. They spoiled crops but proved tasty and nourishing, and their mulch helped herb gardens. The Synod could issue an exclusionist judgement, boosting congregations but reducing production, or an inclusionist one, increasing production and sending curious materials to the congregations. Magisters also warned that such widespread effects should not have been possible without a Declaration of amity for Llofir, and urged the Conclave to investigate. With Highborn Assembly support, Gravus of the Shattered Tower carried an exclusionist message into Reikos. The congregations there were reinforced while businesses, farms, forests and herb gardens lost output. The Conclave also stripped the herald Gilean of her amity.

Highguard.t: The Highborn of Reikos were guided by their own Assembly to shun Llofir's influence in the name of Vigilance, renewing their attendance at congregation but destroying suspect goods and losing production across their businesses, farms, forests and herb gardens.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard of Urizen moved to Reikos after the Solstice to try to capture Tamarbode from Llofir's forces.

A question of provenance.o: Spring magic tied to the eternal Llofir left strange, nourishing but unsettling mushrooms and plants across Reikos, and the Synod was asked to guide the Highborn on whether to shun or use them. The Highborn Assembly backed an exclusionist message, strengthening the congregations of Reikos at the cost of its production.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Mentioned in passing: Tamarbode was named as the region the Citadel Guard of Urizen sought to capture from the forces of Llofir.

Reikos.t: Weird Spring-born fungi spread across the territory, and after the exclusionist judgement its congregations gained votes and liao while its businesses, farms, forests and herb gardens produced less as people discarded suspect materials.

A season of mushrooms.d: Fungus, mould and ivy consumed corpses, ruins, timber and roads, erasing the Druj's poisons but also centuries of Highborn history. Chapters fought daily to save prized buildings, helped by Lucifer Son of Cyrus's auras of Courage and by a dozen captains supporting a great ossuary. Together with Llofir's power they located and destroyed many Druj miasma pillars, reducing the survivors to small zones of terror. A dark new forest engulfed the Sign of Tamar in Tamarbode, guarded by myconoid soldiers, and its Druj camps vanished. By the Autumn Equinox the magic had faded, leaving Reikos verdant and possibly better able to support a fourth Highborn army.

Druj.t: Their foul legacy in Reikos was washed away and many of their miasma pillars were destroyed, while the Druj remnant camps in Tamarbode disappeared without trace once the new forest appeared.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Sister Hepzibah's voice is said to have cut through battlefields from Karsk to Spiral, the latter a Grendel-held territory.

Highguard.t: The Highborn of Reikos saw the Druj taint erased but lost much of their centuries-old legacy, labouring daily to save their chapter houses, while Highborn captains and Lucifer Son of Cyrus helped destroy Druj miasma pillars.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Skywise Kray of the Imperial Orcs is named among the captains who brought retinues to Reikos to support the great ossuary.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: some speculate the force in Tamarbode crept out of Brocéliande, and the apothecaries of Peakedge Song are noted as interested in new medicinal plants.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Karsk is named as one of the battlefields where Sister Hepzibah once fought.

A season of mushrooms.o: In Summer 380YE a surge of Spring magic, believed by magisters to be directed by the eternal Llofir and heightened by the Hallow of the Green World, swept Reikos, devouring the dead, the ruined and the Druj taint and leaving a wild, natural landscape in its place.

Reikos/Broken Ride.t: The existing opportunity to build a fortification here became of even greater interest to the Vigilant, as it would also allow watch over events in Tamarbode.

Reikos/Grey Charge.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial forces destroyed several orc camps in Tamarbode during the earlier cleansing of Grey Charge.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Something unknown seized the region, raising a dense dark forest around the Sign of Tamar patrolled by myconoid soldiers who turn back armed intruders, and the Druj camps there vanished.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not directly discussed; the page's great ossuary is a project in Reikos, and Spiral is named only in a vignette.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Mentioned in passing: its apothecaries are keen to see what new medicinal plants the Spring magic and Druj domination might reveal for the Garden of High Chalcis.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: some suggest the thing that seized Tamarbode may have snuck out of Brocéliande to the north-west.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: named in a vignette as one of the battlefields where Sister Hepzibah's voice was heard.

Reikos.t: The territory was transformed in a single season from a Druj-blighted ruin into wild meadow, forest and marsh, losing most of its ruins and much Highborn history while its villages, towns and key resources were kept clear.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: named in a vignette as one of the battlefields where Sister Hepzibah's voice was heard.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the apothecaries of Peakedge Song are said to be keen to see what new medicinal plants the magic reveals.

A spiritual prism.d: After the Synod failed to uphold the Doctrine of the Beyond, Wintermark, Varushka, Navarr, Urizen and the League rejected Yael by greater majority. Their military support to and from Dawn, Highguard, the Marches and the Brass Coast was halved. The Imperial Orcs declared the matter one for humans only and were freed from the turmoil. Undecided Highguard saw its armies lose 10% of victory points and break below 1200 strength. Dawn's assembly backed Yael without a greater majority, opening optional mandates: a song bringing resource bonuses, inducting the Congregation into the Gryphon's Pride, and a possible tourney making Yael Queen of Dawn. The Courage assembly could also turn the Congregation into an independent army.

Dawn.t: Dawn's assembly praised Yael as First Empress Reborn, opening the chance of a song mandate, of the Congregation joining the Gryphon's Pride and of a Grand Tourney to make her Queen of Dawn, though Dawnish armies now get only halved support from the five rejecting nations.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Congregation's call to conquer the barbarians alongside the Gryphon's Pride is implicitly aimed at orcs such as the Druj.

Highguard.t: Without a clear judgement from its assembly, division among the faithful weakened every Highborn army, imposing a 10% penalty to victory points and making them break below 1200 strength until a greater-majority statement resolves it.

Imperial Orcs.t: Having declared Yael's revelation a matter for humans alone, the Imperial Orcs were freed from the turmoil, and their armies may support and be supported by any nation.

Navarr.t: Navarr's decisive rejection of Yael settled the question at home but halved its military support to and from Dawn, Highguard, the Marches and the Brass Coast; its assembly may also mandate a priest with liao to bring Navarri pilgrims home.

Urizen.t: Urizen's rejection of Yael ended debate among its citizens but halved effective military cooperation with Dawn, Highguard, the Marches and the Brass Coast; its assembly may mandate liao to recall Urizeni pilgrims.

Varushka.t: Varushka's rejection of Yael brought clarity at home but halved effective military support between Varushkan armies and those of the four undecided or supportive nations; a mandate could recall Varushkan pilgrims from the Congregation.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's decisive rejection of Yael settled doubts among its people, at the cost of halved military support to and from Dawn, Highguard, the Marches and the Brass Coast; its assembly may send a priest with liao to reclaim converted pilgrims.

A spiritual prism.o: In Spring 381YE the Synod's rejection of Yael's Doctrine of the Beyond split the Empire along lines of faith: nations whose assemblies decisively rejected her could no longer fight effectively alongside those that had not, Highborn armies began to falter, and new opportunities opened for Yael's supporters.

Casinea.t: Makeshift camps of pilgrims from across the Empire gathered in Casinea to praise Yael, enduring the elements without shelter while swelling the Congregation of the First Empress.

Reikos.t: Reikos hosted makeshift camps of pilgrims seeking the First Empress Reborn, part of the Congregation that could be recalled, sent to fight for Dawn or turned into an army.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: rumours claimed that one or more pieces of the Dawnish regalia had been seen in the Barrens, taken by some as a sign of the Dawnish monarch's return.

A star is born.d: Acting on Synod judgements, the expedition found the freed slaves thriving in Leerdam. Rachensgrab's surviving common folk were living in poverty, warned by the Commonwealth never to resume slaving. Nearby, the Viyerda, humans and orcs ruled by a reincarnating Winter Queen and Summer King, hold metals and ilium but refused trade and contact. Diplomacy could be attempted through a Senate appraisal by Naomi of Virtue's Rest (60 thrones) or a Celestial Arch declaration (100 mana), but not both. Either risks angering the Commonwealth, whose ambassador objects to Imperial activity there. A judgement of rewarding could recompense the unrewarded participants. The expedition closed early.

Dawn.t: Five Dawnish fleets, including those of Caspian Du Marin and Purnelle, sacrificed their own prosperity to join the voyage. Like all participants, they went unrewarded unless the Synod or Senate chooses to recompense them.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only in an out-of-character note citing a television show as visual inspiration for the Viyerda, and no Grendel participants are listed.

Highguard.t: Highguard sent a modest contingent to the expedition: the military unit of Thomas and the fleet of Creed.

Navarr.t: Navarr contributed Farren Silver Streams' military unit and six fleets, among them Cadfael Silentwatch and Wyllen Blood Oak, to the voyage to the northern Sea of Steel.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast was one of the largest contributors. It sent thirteen fleets and Guillermo i Ezmara i Erigo's military unit to bring Prosperity to Rachensgrab's former slaves.

The League.t: Eight League fleets, several of them from Sarvos, and Othello di Severio von Holberg's military unit joined the expedition.

The Marches.t: The expedition answered a judgement by the Marcher Creighton Blackewater, who also sailed with his own fleet alongside four other Marcher fleets and Tom Appleseed's unit. The page closes on a Marcher proverb counselling caution.

Urizen.t: Urizen sent Hugh Ravenspire's military unit and four fleets, including Bacauda Netherwatch and Xenia, to the Sea of Steel.

Varushka.t: Varushka provided eleven fleets and Fania Vessely-Vanek's military unit, one of the larger national contributions to the flotilla.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark sent the largest contingent of any nation, with eight military units and eighteen fleets committing to the voyage.

A star is born.o: An Imperial expedition of fifteen military units and seventy-one fleets sailed to the Sea of Steel to aid the former slaves of Rachensgrab. It found them prospering in the Commonwealth, and instead discovered the guarded island kingdom of the Viyerda, whose bay yields ilium from falling stars.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the main Viyerda island is described as half the size of Sarvos, and several participating League fleets bear the name 'di Sarvos'.

A stone for a stone.d: Naomi consulted Marcher orcs, studied past wars and crossed under truce to speak with the Jotun in Mournwold. She traced their enmity to the abrogated ceasefire and the Mournwold curses, after which the Jotun refused peace until every dishonoured warrior, above all Jarl Haakon, was dead. Her suggested steps were to kill Haakon, avoid further atrocities, start another war or inflict a major defeat, agree terms for war, build a new Meeting Place, echo Jotun gests, and resolve Jotun hatred of the Navarr. The Lasambrians offered a 'Little Sibling' ceasefire in exchange for Gambit and Serra Damata, or a 'Big Sibling' secession. Their delegation came to Anvil, but no treaty went before the Senate.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is cited as an example of land a nation regards as its own, and the Lasambrians are likened to the Dawnish in their keenness for adventure.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun insult the Navarr as 'human Druj', and the Druj are named among the enemies who would exploit any Imperial weakness.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named among the foes who would press a weakened Empire, and as having helped a third of the Lasambrians flee to the Broken Shore.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian envoys are likened to the Highborn in spirituality, and travelled with Naomi along the road towards Casinea.

Jotun.t: The appraisal found the Jotun bound by faith to seek worthy war and unwilling to make peace until Jarl Haakon and the other warriors dishonoured in the Mournwold are slain. Even then, any peace would likely be used to rebuild or to attack the Faraden, while the Lasambrian Jotun pursued their own deals.

Navarr.t: The Jotun despise the Navarr as 'human Druj' and give them no quarter. Naomi suggested either improving that view through diplomacy or keeping Navarr armies away from Jotun campaigns, which would be hard if war reached Liathaven.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn have won Jotun respect, notably for raising a barrow over the dead of Fort Braydon and through Avisena, the 'Golden Jarl'. The Lasambrian Little Sibling deal would cede two Kahraman regions in return for keeping all Jotun armies out of Freeborn territory for two years.

The Marches.t: Naomi consulted Marcher orcs, and noted lingering Marcher resentment over the Mournwold curses. She also found that the Jotun respect the Marchers to a lesser degree than Wintermark and the Freeborn.

Thule.t: Starting a war with the Thule was put forward as something that might prompt the Jotun to grant a temporary peace, though Naomi warned it could be cataclysmic without other steps. Guntherm's past alliance with the Jotun against the Thule was recalled as a precedent.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's choice to fight with honour, as in retaking Sermersuaq, earned the Jotun's respect but no interest in a ceasefire. Naomi advised that at least one Wintermark army fight honourably in every Jotun campaign to avoid accidental dishonour.

A stone for a stone.o: Commissioned by the Imperial Senate, Naomi of Virtue's Rest appraised what might make peace more appealing to the Jotun. She concluded that a lasting peace was near impossible, but set out steps that could make a temporary ceasefire achievable, and reported two Lasambrian peace offers.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: Gambit was one of the two regions the Lasambrians asked the Empire to cede to them under the proposed Little Sibling ceasefire. No treaty was brought before the Senate.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: Serra Damata was proposed for cession under the Little Sibling deal, which would have handed the Lasambrians the Damatian Cliffs and the Red Depths. No treaty was brought before the Senate.

Tromsa/Majastind.t: Mount Majastind, believed to hold Ulven's bones and at least three powerful artefacts, is the Jotun's most sacred site. The Imperial decision to spare it may have been the most important step in changing Jotun views.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: used as an analogy for how deeply the Jotun regard their claimed lands as their own.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the bay is not named; the page notes only the Jotun dislike of open water and dread of drowning.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: resentment over the Mournwold curses is said to linger in Bregasland.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian delegation travelled with Naomi along the road to Casinea before turning off for Anvil.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrians are noted to have attacked Feroz in the past.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the territories the Jotun claim, at least in part, as their own.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: a sept in Tromsa claims Hercynia's woods and peaks were its domain before the Terunael came.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman, where the Jotun were defeated at Fort Braydon, is claimed by both Jotun and Lasambrians. It was the subject of the Little Sibling offer to cede Gambit and Serra Damata, and Naomi met the Lasambrians near its border on the Scorrero River.

Kalino.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the lands the Lasambrians lay claim to.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the territories the Jotun claim as their own.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Naomi warned that keeping the Navarr from fighting the Jotun would be fraught if the war moved to Liathaven.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among Jotun-claimed lands, and as an example of land the Marchers see as theirs.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold curses, which killed nearly one in six inhabitants, left the Jotun dishonoured and committed to war until Jarl Haakon, its former ruler, is dead. Naomi made her truce visit to the Jotun there.

Reinos.t: Reinos is claimed in part by the Lasambrians, and Naomi met them where its border meets Kahraman and Segura. Under the Little Sibling offer, no Imperial army would enter Reinos for two years.

Segura.t: Segura is claimed by both Jotun and Lasambrians, and its former senator Avisena is revered by the Jotun as the Golden Jarl. It would be covered by the Little Sibling ceasefire barring Jotun armies from Freeborn lands.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq is claimed by the Jotun. Wintermark's honourable campaign to retake it saw the Jotun allow Imperial forces to recover their wounded and dead.

Tromsa.t: Imperial generals chose not to attack Mount Majastind during their invasion of Tromsa, which may have been pivotal in improving Jotun views of the nations involved.

A strange land.d: The Varushkan egregore made steady progress in Ossium, especially among the Ketsov, who erased Bone Scorpion symbols and sought Varushkan ways. They feared a Druj return and the loss of their weapons trade, so they proposed walls, a barracks and a Trading Exchange, which the Thule offered to build if the Empire would not. The Sand Fishers' coastal lands could support Varushkan settlers and help towards a fourth army. Options were to cede Misericorde, move them to Skarsind, or let the Thule offer sanctuary in Sküld. Dawnish and Varushkan statements opened opportunities for mandates. The Senate ceded Misericorde and the Pride assembly mandated preaching in Ossium. The other opportunities lapsed by Winter 383YE.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish National Assembly urged troubadours to bring tales of glory to Ossium, opening the opportunity for a mandate sending Dawnish knights to hunt the Druj miasma pillars. The civil service judged that the Ketsov and Sand Fishers had little interest in glory.

Druj.t: The Druj were in retreat but still contested Ossium, were expected to try to retake it within a year or two, and had left miasma pillars poisoning the land with dread.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: veterans of the Reikos campaign are said to remember the Druj miasma pillars well.

Imperial Orcs.t: Moving the Sand Fishers to Skarsind was considered, but they would add nothing to Imperial Orc strength or taxes, and ceding any region would disrupt the orcs living there.

The League.t: The Senate ceded Misericorde in Holberg to the Sand Fishers, so the region was no longer part of the League. In return Holberg's merchants were expected to profit from trade in fish, hides and timber.

Thule.t: The Thule offered to build and run the Ketsov Trading Exchange if the Empire would not. They also offered sanctuary in Sküld to the Sand Fishers and other Ossium orcs, but said they would approach them only with Senate or ambassadorial permission.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not discussed; the only related reference is a production table for Knightly Redoubts.

Varushka.t: Varushka received Ossium, where its egregore sought new citizens among the receptive Ketsov. The barracks and coastal resettlement were offered as a path to a fourth Varushkan army, and the Varushkan Assembly welcomed the Dawnish troubadours.

A strange land.o: After the Senate assigned newly conquered Ossium to Varushka, a series of opportunities arose for the territory: fortifying and arming the town of Ketsov, resettling the Sand Fishers, upgrading the Crawling Depths mines and preaching the Way to its people. The Senate ceded Misericorde in Holberg to the Sand Fishers, and the Pride assembly passed a mandate to preach in Ossium.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: The Senate ceded Misericorde, a bandit-haunted forest with few citizens, to the Sand Fishers, who were expected to thrive on its marshy Semmerlak coast and possibly aid magistrates hunting fugitives there.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: The Thule offered homes on the banks of the Luhguren in Sküld to the Sand Fishers and other Ossium orcs, who would join the Thule nation.

Holberg.t: Holberg lost its region of Misericorde, ceded to the Sand Fishers, with the trade they would bring expected to raise the territory's taxation by 8 thrones by year's end.

Ossium.t: Ossium's Ketsov embraced Varushkan ways and proposed walls, a barracks and a Trading Exchange. Its Crawling Depths mines could be upgraded to double mithril output, and the Pride assembly mandated preaching the Way to its people.

Otkodov.t: The Thule proposed resettling the Sand Fishers and other Ossium orcs in Otkodov's region of Sküld, as part of the Thule nation.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory itself is not discussed; 'Knightly Redoubts' appear only as an item in a production table.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Reikos campaign is recalled as the Empire's earlier encounter with Druj miasma pillars.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind was considered as a new home for the Sand Fishers, but they would struggle in its harsh mountains, ceding land would disrupt its Imperial Orcs, and a region next to Crows Ridge would fall outside the Thule pacts.

A tale told.d: Wintermark's Bloodcloaks and Green Shield, the Imperial Orc Summer Storm, the Marcher Strong Reeds, Tusks and Bounders, and the Freeborn Fire of the South gathered at Kalant in Stark. About seventy thousand troops took Icewood, Skyfall Waste and Rikskog. At Viheltavathorn, Jarls Olgaf and Klarra died holding the gates, and Mathilda Fisher was mortally wounded. Around fifteen hundred Imperial soldiers died. Igya Olgafsdottir, now Jarl, held Oksenesfestsal. She offered an honour battle at Crows Field for Mathilda's Blue Eel Banner. The Jotun formed three fyrds. A huge Kalsean host retook Skallahn and threatened to cut the Imperial line of retreat.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Oksenesfestsal is compared to Astolat's Castle of Thorns and Semmerholm's Adamant Gate, and the Bound King is noted to have aided the Dawnish in the past.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Summer Storm, joined by Summer heralds and emissaries of the Shadowed Fire, helped conquer Skyfall Waste and flank the Jotun at Viheltavathorn. Its orcs found the voices of warlike ancestors such as Sjöfn of the Bittenblade clearer in Tromsa.

Jotun.t: The Jotun lost three regions of Tromsa, Viheltavathorn and Jarl Olgaf, while Igya Olgafsdottir took up the jarldom and held Oksenesfestsal. Meanwhile all the armies of Kalsea retook Skallahn and stood ready to strike north or into Sermersuaq.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bound King is said to have sent his court to aid the Navarr in the past.

The Brass Coast.t: The Fire of the South force-marched from Kahraman to fight in Rikskog, suffering in the northern cold. The Bound King's knights who accompanied the Freeborn ignored their general's orders by executing the fallen, cutting down fugitives and targeting healers.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the unscalable walls of Holberg are cited as an example of defences that could not hold off seventy thousand troops.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the adamant in Oksenesfestsal is compared to that of the Court of the White Fountain in Redoubt.

Wintermark.t: The Bloodcloaks and Green Shield led the invasion from Stark, and the Jotun repaid their honourable fighting by holding back from killing, which reduced Winterfolk casualties. Igya addressed the Winterfolk at the parley and entrusted General Osric with a knife for Mathilda Fisher.

A tale told.o: In Autumn 385YE seven Imperial armies, backed by elite warbands and Summer, Winter, Autumn and Shadowed Fire allies, invaded the Jotun territory of Tromsa from Sermersuaq. They conquered Icewood, Skyfall Waste and Rikskog, killed Jarl Olgaf, and then stalled before the adamant-reinforced fortress of Oksenesfestsal in Tromsdalen.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: The Imperial armies and their realm allies mustered at the Fortress of Kalant in Stark before crossing the Lansipari into Tromsa.

Skallahn/Eyrarfell.t: Mentioned in passing: the mountains of Tromsdalen are part of the same range as Eyrarfell.

Skallahn/Iron Stand.t: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm, Bloodcloaks and Green Shield withdrew out of Iron Stand into Sermersuaq before the invasion.

Tromsa/Icewood.t: Icewood was the first region conquered, as Jarl Bjørnda Bearcrusher retreated west with her warriors and thralls. In the north, a fane of Wise Rangara was found and left under watch by a hundred Imperial soldiers.

Tromsa/Majastind.t: Mentioned in passing: thralls describe Mount Majastind at the heart of Tromsa as the throne of the gods, but the region was not reached.

Tromsa/Rikskog.t: Rikskog was taken after the Battle of Viheltavathorn, where the fortified tower was destroyed, Jarls Olgaf and Klarra died and Mathilda Fisher was mortally wounded. Jotun remain at Fniskard's Palisade, and a Jotun recapture of the region could cut off the Imperial retreat.

Tromsa/Skyfall Waste.t: Jarl Hodne Hodnesson's hall, Hodnesshal, fell and the storm-swept tundra was conquered. This gave the Empire Lake Karnakadatha, an ilium source the Senate could allocate if the region is held.

Tromsa/Tromsdalen.t: The Imperial advance stalled before the adamant-reinforced Oksenesfestsal, held by Igya Olgafsdottir, leaving the region one tenth captured. Jotun reinforcements were moving through the Nordbotn pass to resupply the fortress.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Oksenesfestsal is described as a match for Astolat's Castle of Thorns.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Mathilda Fisher fled north to Tromsa after her defeat in Bregasland, and the Strong Reeds' general boasts of running the Jotun and Fisher out of it.

Fjorknae.t: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Igya threatened to spirit Mathilda Fisher away to Fjorknae and bury her there if the Empire failed to take her banner.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: its unscalable walls are cited as defences that could not long withstand seventy thousand troops.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fishers did not return to their lands in Hordalant, and Jotun embassies to the realms like the Icewood fane have been seen there.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South marched north from Kahraman, where the Bound King was allowed to slake his hunger in return for his aid.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the Court of the White Fountain in Redoubt is cited as another adamant construction.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: what little the Empire knew of Tromsa came largely from the recent expedition to map the Sea of Snow.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Oksenesfestsal's adamant is compared to the Adamant Gate in Semmerholm.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq was the staging ground where the seven armies gathered before crossing into Tromsa. It now faces a possible Jotun raid from the Kalsean host massed in Skallahn.

Skallahn.t: Three Imperial armies withdrew from Skallahn to join the invasion, and an immense Jotun force including all the armies of Kalsea then recaptured all the territory the Empire had claimed there. That force is poised to march north into Tromsa or raid Sermersuaq.

Tromsa.t: The Empire captured Icewood, Skyfall Waste and Rikskog of the presumed seven regions, destroyed Viheltavathorn and besieged Oksenesfestsal, while Jarl Olgaf fell and his daughter Igya succeeded him. Three Jotun fyrds rallied in the west.

Tsirku.t: Mentioned in passing: Tsirku lies north of the Skyfall Wastes, Lake Karnakadatha sits on its border, and its proximity may explain Tromsa's strangeness.

A thousand steps.d: Only Highguard, the League and Varushka agreed that the time was right to fight the vallorn. With the treasury empty, the Navarr had to fund their Hercynian army themselves, using mithril or various ingots and measures. The options were these: send Navarr military units into Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, boosted by Feast of Heroes and three Heroes Helms made by Treji artisans. Other nations could pass Synod mandates committing their artisans. Marrowort could be sold to the City of Gold and Lead at one wain per sixty, at this summit only. Citizens across the Empire could simply be asked for donations. Restless Terunael ghosts were slowing work on the Seren temple.

Dawn.t: Dawn remained broadly unconvinced that now was the time to fight the vallorn, despite clear enthusiasm for a glorious battle against long odds. Its Assembly could commit Dawnish artisans to the Navarr army, worth ten wains, at the cost of being unable to begin a runeforge for four seasons.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: named among the barbarian threats on the Empire's borders that keep the Empire's attention away from the vallorn.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the barbarian threats on the Empire's borders that keep the Empire's attention away from the vallorn.

Highguard.t: Highguard was one of three nations to agree with the Navarr that the time to fight the vallorn had come. Catrin urged the Navarr to court its wealthy benefactors and the Council of Benefactors, whose ten wains a season could indirectly free funds for the army or support the City of Dreams.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc Assembly could mandate the Ethengraw of the Black Forge to help raise the Navarr army. This would let the Navarr substitute other resources for mithril more efficiently, but Orc armies would lose the forge hammers order until the army was complete.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: named among the barbarian threats on the Empire's borders, and Jotun-held Liathaven is cited as a place where the vallorn war will not be won.

Navarr.t: With the stridings home and Isaella's Dance sacrificed, the Navarr had only two armies and needed to fund a new one in Hercynia and win allies in the Senate, Military Council and Conclave. Every Navarr was urged to mine Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, sell herbs and marrowort, and beg support from other nations.

The League.t: The League was one of three nations to agree that the time to fight the vallorn was right. Its merchant-princes were named as wealthy targets for Navarr appeals, and Holberg's civic pride as something that might be used to win donations.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the barbarian threats on the Empire's borders that keep the Empire's attention away from the vallorn.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Urizeni raising of an army with three hundred wains of mithril in a single season is cited as an example of wealth the Navarr might tap.

Varushka.t: Varushka agreed that the time to fight the vallorn had come. Its Assembly could commit Varushkan artisans to the Navarr army, worth ten wains, at the cost of a year without a new runeforge, and its boyars and wealthy vales were singled out as potential donors.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark Assembly could mandate the Runegrott artisans to arm the Navarr army, halting new artisan items until the army was complete. However, its upheld statements suggested it saw the vallorn war as ill-timed and a low priority.

A thousand steps.o: Having committed to war against the vallorn, the Navarr faced the urgent problem of paying for the new army being raised in Hercynia, and this wind set out several ways to fund it and win allies. It also revealed ghostly hauntings at the Seren temple site and announced a conjunction there.

Miaren/Serenael.t: Ghosts of the Terunael city were haunting the Seren temple building site and slowing construction. A conjunction there at 22:45 on the Friday of the Summer Solstice, for a hundred people under Tanwen, the Eternal Flame of Miaren, would let musicians and dancers help the ghosts celebrate and pass into the Labyrinth. Weapons and bloodshed were to be avoided.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Catrin, the broker who urged the Navarr simply to ask every citizen at Anvil for help, came from Brocéliande.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is not named on the page; its only link is through the Wintermark Runegrott, whose artisans could be mandated to help arm the Navarr army.

Hercynia.t: The new Navarr army capable of fighting the vallorn was being raised in Hercynia. It could be paid for with mithril or with ingots and measures of weltsilver, orichalcum, green iron, tempest jade, beggar's lye or iridescent gloaming.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Catrin suggested Holberg's claim to be the greatest city in the world could spur it to outgive other League cities.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: named in the opening story as one of the places where the vallorn war will not ultimately be won.

Miaren.t: Lorenzo's Deep Pockets on the edge of Miaren offered a seemingly limitless supply of tempest jade and weltsilver for Navarr warbands. The vate Ffion of Parting Ways in Miaren had arranged the marrowort deal with the City of Gold and Lead.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: named in the opening story as a place where the vallorn war will not ultimately be won.

A thousand years of longing.d: With contributions from the League, Highborn pilgrims, the Department of Historical Research, the eternal Phaleron, papers seized from the Heirs of Terunael and Thule scholars from Otkodov, the library confirmed and extended Siân Eternal's work. It traced the vallorn to Terunael rituals meant to channel Spring magic into their armies. Scholars set out three futures: centuries more trod-walking, the Heirs' spreading of the vallorn, or connecting the last unlinked hearts, Béantal Dol in Sarangrave and Cavan in Visokuma, to provoke a final war that the Empire might win but could not easily halt. Opportunities included spying on Béantal Dol, approaching eternals and Assembly statements. Spymaster Bernard Dugdale funded the Sarangrave expedition.

Druj.t: The Druj are thought to have studied and contained the vallorn of Béantal Dol, possibly from the Palace of the Sleepers, and may be researching magic to rouse it, so liberating Sarangrave from them is seen as the likely first step towards the final trod.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: in the opening story a Navarr scholar expects the Senate to say the time is not right until the Druj and the Grendel have been dealt with.

Highguard.t: Highborn pilgrims supplied books and priceless journals dating back to landfall, their grey pilgrims are credited with speeding the weakening of the vallorn, and the Highborn Assembly is one of two assemblies whose mandates on the findings other nations' priests could answer.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, though Liathaven, which they hold, is noted as having one remaining vallorn region and disrupted trods.

Navarr.t: The Navarr now hold everything there is to know about the vallorn and face an existential choice: keep walking the trods for centuries or complete the network and fight the final battle that Navarr and Thorn foresaw, which would also end their trapped ancestors' lives.

Thule.t: Otkodov's orc warlocks and their Dragons shared ancient records and are enthusiastically in favour of completing the trod network, promising to deal with Sküld's vallorn themselves, apparently hoping to restore Sküld and reach the treasures of Emrys.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Terunael used ilium taken from the Urizen to power their rituals, and a scattering of Urizen arcane scholars agreed that a roused vallorn would take years to subside.

A thousand years of longing.o: The expanded Great Library of Hacynian completed its research into the vallorn years ahead of schedule, gathering everything known about its creation and concluding that linking every remaining vallorn heart to the trods would rouse it fully and make it vulnerable to final defeat.

Brocéliande/Dark Ranging.t: Mentioned in passing: Dark Ranging is cited, alongside West Ranging, as becoming vulnerable within the same decade thanks to the trods' wider reach and more travellers.

Brocéliande/Terunael.t: The vallorn of Terunael, the first and most potent, is where Navarr and Thorn led their final expedition and where they seem to remain alive at the heart, keeping the vallorn from healing so the trods can bleed it.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: The fight to clear the vallorn from West Ranging is cited as showing how a weakened vallorn rises in frenzy yet can then be defeated.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Site of the Terunael city of Emrys, Sküld's vallorn is constrained and weakened under Thule Winter magic; the Thule offer to destroy it themselves if it is roused, which would let them restore the region's fertility and perhaps reach Emrys.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: The Dance of Navarr and Thorn would have to be cast in Bendol to link Béantal Dol to the trods, and the Spymaster's 6 wains of weirwood funded a season's outpost there to scout the vallorn heart, leading to the Into Béantal Dol report.

Brocéliande.t: Brocéliande remains the gravest threat with five vallorn regions, an ancient vallorn whose heart holds Navarr and Thorn, and papers from the Heirs of Terunael stronghold there shaped the library's findings; Wither the Seed's restraint would fail once its curse ends or the vallorn is roused.

Hercynia.t: Home of the Great Library, whose work went on undeterred by the threat of Cold Sun, Hercynia has one vallorn region left; its recently disrupted trods let the vallorn recover, and its heart is thought likely the next to become vulnerable in perhaps fifty years.

Liathaven.t: Liathaven has one vallorn region left, but its disrupted trods let the vallorn recover quickly, its reclamation was projected at a century beyond Hercynia, and it would return to full force once Wither the Seed runs its course.
