Miaren.t: Miaren holds the only vallorn heart ever destroyed, and its records show the vallorn lashing out when exposed and decades of clearing afterwards, which is why it is so lightly forested.

Otkodov.t: A contingent of orc warlocks from Otkodov joined the Great Library's faculty, bringing Thule scrolls never seen by human eyes and warning that a fully roused vallorn could not quickly be stopped.

Sarangrave.t: Sarangrave contains Béantal Dol, one of only two unconnected vallorn hearts, so its liberation is likely needed for the final trod; Imperial Spymaster Bernard Dugdale backed the spy network there to scout the vallorn heart.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Therunin is listed as still holding two vallorn regions, among the smaller vallorn that would fight savagely if roused.

A throne of blood.d: A Navarri messenger was told by Dogri's Crowskeepers that Dogri would talk, but only at Crowskeep in Crow's Ridge. Kali of the Saker had to attend, accompanied only by Skarsind folk, and a former senator was barred. Breaking the terms would end the meeting, and Dogri would defend his borders against anyone. The Wintermark national assembly's Winter Solstice statement urged Winterfolk not to join Dogri. Some stubborn Winterfolk left Skarsind, but die-hards went north to him. The Four Seasons Market stayed in Wintermark hands because no Imperial Orc came to claim it. The civil service confirmed a Sentinel Gate conjunction to Crowskeep at the Spring Equinox.

Imperial Orcs.t: While the orcs build their nation in southern Skarsind, the Four Seasons Market remains in Wintermark hands, because its owner says no Imperial Orc came to take it over.

Wintermark.t: The assembly's call to come home persuaded some Winterfolk to leave Skarsind, but die-hards joined Dogri, who demanded that Kali of the Saker and Skarsind folk meet him at Crowskeep.

A throne of blood.o: With spring easing the harsh winter, Dogri Thulebane, still occupying Crow's Ridge in northern Skarsind, sent word that he would meet Imperial representatives at Crowskeep on strict terms, as die-hard Winterfolk continued to rally to his banner.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Dogri's forces still held Crow's Ridge, and he named Crowskeep as the only place he would meet, reachable through a Sentinel Gate conjunction at the Spring Equinox.

Skarsind.t: The territory remained divided, with the Imperial Orcs building in the south and Dogri's Winterfolk rebels holding the north as spring brought new recruits to his banner.

A tide in the affairs.d: Welcomed at Ballaghadruh by Kaliact's garrison commander Rhababahrúns, the Wolves followed Kaliact's proposed itinerary through Ossuary, Ankra, Cinion, Ateri, Screed, Apstrus and finally Apulus. Fighting was limited to scattered loyalist orcs and miasma-maddened wretches in Screed, but the Black Plateau drove many soldiers to desert. Kaliact had used forged orders to send the Black Eels and Brine Turtles to Mareave, then used the procession to buy time to crush loyalists in the City of Nets. By season's end Spiral was part of the Empire, but Kaliact's supporters held control only narrowly, and Paymaster Muireall led a peaceful holdout camp in southern Apstrus.

Grendel.t: Spiral's Grendel split between Kaliact's conspirators, bewildered bystanders and loyalists to Dubhtraig, who fought and lost at Apulian's docks and palace. Two Grendel armies were sent to Mareave by forged orders.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Hercynian Navarr scouts, skilled at moving unseen through Spiral's broken terrain, accompanied the Wolves of War.

The League.t: The League's Wolves of War brought Spiral into the Empire as a new League territory, losing soldiers mainly to desertion under the Black Plateau's influence and to a few skirmishes.

Urizen.t: Urizeni met in Ankra and Cinion gave the Wolves a mixed welcome, some feeling betrayed and some preparing to leave Spiral for Redoubt, Morrow or Zenith.

A tide in the affairs.o: In Summer 385YE the League's Wolves of War crossed through the Twilight Gate and secured all of Spiral in a single season under Salt Lord Kaliact's treaty with the Senate, making it a League territory of the Empire. They met little organised resistance but lost soldiers to the Black Plateau's miasma.

Spiral/Ankra.t: In Ankra the Wolves met their first Urizeni, whose welcome was mixed and some of whom were preparing to leave Spiral.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: Apstrus, site of the Battle of Solen's Doubt, saw a little more resistance, and Paymaster Muireall established a non-violent holdout camp of anti-Imperial orcs on its southern borders.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Kaliact's supporters won a bloody fight against loyalists in the City of Nets, especially at the docks and palace, leaving Apulian tense and only narrowly under her control.

Spiral/Ateri.t: At Ateri Rhababahrúns returned to Ballaghadruh and was replaced as escort by Captain Chevahn of Kaliact's guard and two Circle of Black Sand magicians.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Urizeni in Cinion greeted the Wolves with barely concealed anger and a sense of betrayal, and some made ready to leave.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: At the Legacy mithril mine Kaliact's orcs had seized control after fighting off the Lamhaich family, whose Overseer Seàrlas Lamhaich fled, and here the Wolves first felt the Black Plateau's miasma again.

Spiral/Screed.t: Screed, where the Black Plateau is strongest, was secured after fighting miasma-maddened killers that cost a score or so of soldiers, and Oblivion's Edge sentinels warned of increased activity near the Plateau.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is not named; the only maritime element is the loyalists' attempt to seize or burn ships at Apulian's docks.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Hercynian Navarr scouts were recruited to help the Wolves of War move through Spiral.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Eels and Brine Turtles left Spiral for Mareave on forged orders, and Kaliact had expected Paymaster Muireall to retreat there.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: some Urizeni in Spiral prepared to leave for Morrow.

Mountains of the Moon.t: Mentioned in passing: Paymaster Muireall was almost ruined by a disastrous venture into the Mountains of the Moon.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: some Urizeni in Spiral prepared to leave for Redoubt.

Spiral.t: Spiral was secured by the Wolves of War and became a League territory of the Empire, though Kaliact's hold on its orcs remained fragile and the Black Plateau's miasma persisted.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: some Urizeni in Spiral were even preparing to leave for Zenith.

A time of plenty.d: Backed by the Prosperity Assembly (152-0), Gilah consecrated the Kraken's Bane, drawing more pilgrims to Calvos Sound and prompting new paradors and plans to expand the dock. Gabriela's seminary would stand on a wharf, with a library and an etched mithril floor depicting Zemress' life. It would cost 15 wains each of weirwood, white granite and mithril plus 45 crowns. The Zemress islanders offered to build it and pay the crowns. The Sumaah Republic offered all the granite or the weirwood and copies of its records of Zemress, if the seminary stayed open to all followers of the Way. The offers lapse unless work begins by the Summer Solstice 383YE.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Gilah's statement of principle hoped the consecrated shrine would bolster those who follow Zemress' example in raiding the Grendel.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gained a newly consecrated shrine to their exemplar Zemress, with growing pilgrim trade and an Imperial commission for her seminary. The Zemress islanders pledged to build it and pay its 45 crowns themselves.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named on the page; the only link is a section heading, 'What the Morrow Holds'.

A time of plenty.o: After Gilah of the Chantry consecrated Zemress' ship, the Kraken's Bane, with true liao at Calvos Sound, the architect Gabriela i Matez i Riqueza i Zemress proposed a seminary built on a wharf beside it. The Senate commissioned the seminary, and Sumaash support was secured provided work began on time.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: Calvos Sound, Zemress' birthplace, saw her ship consecrated and a rising flood of pilgrims, with new paradors opening and plans to expand the dry dock. The Senate commissioned a wharf-top seminary to be built beside the Bane.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is recalled as the waters Zemress cleared of pirates from the deck of the Kraken's Bane, earning her the title Blade of the Isles.

Madruga.t: Madruga hosts the consecrated Kraken's Bane, and the Senate commissioned a seminary to Zemress there, drawing pilgrims from across the Empire and from Sumaah.

A victory for diplomacy.d: Ambassador Tethros i Zuhri i Erigo's treaty gave the Iron Confederacy Free Trade status and criminalised the export of narcotics to it for three years. In response, Duke Helen Gerradin of Veroigne allowed Imperial fleets at Robec to receive Kobol's Vigour, a metallic elixir, in place of luxuries. The Dukes declined a joint campaign against the Children of Wrecks, recalling that their offer to invade Feroz had been rebuffed. They also urged the Empire to disband the Conclave and Synod to oppose Dumon, which the Empire declined. Ser Marquette Lavasse, Temple of the Veiled King priests and Baron de Bestel's kin visited Anvil. Afterwards Robec granted Imperial merchants mercantilist status, though scrutiny and some delays remained.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named as believed members of the Freedom Accord and fellow victims of the Children of Wrecks, and the Suranni asked for evidence of the claim that the pirates were brought by 'the Asaveans and their Grendel pawns'.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast's Tethros i Zuhri i Erigo, as Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy, drove the treaty and hosted the Suranni delegations. Suranni merchants mostly travel overland through the Brass Coast, so they benefit from the tariff-free trade.

A victory for diplomacy.o: In Autumn 386YE the Iron Confederacy accepted the Senate's Free Trade and narcotics-ban treaty and stayed out of the Freedom Accord. After three Suranni delegations visited Anvil, the Iron Dukes lifted their sanctions on Imperial merchants trading at Robec.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name the Bay. It describes the Children of Wrecks' piracy against the Empire and the Grendel, and the Suranni intention to guard only their own territorial waters.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Feroz, and particularly the town of Bramar, was once a favoured Suranni market before it was lost. The Empire's rebuff of a Suranni offer to invade Feroz is cited as the reason the Dukes refused a military alliance.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Segura is where Iron Confederacy merchants most often sell their goods, now without tariffs on their imports.

Veroigne.t: Duke Helen Gerradin welcomed the narcotics ban for her port of Robec and allowed Imperial fleets there to receive Kobol's Vigour. After the delegation's visit, sanctions on Imperial merchants at Robec were lifted, though some delays and scrutiny remained.

A walk in shadow.d: The Urizeni Citadel Guard led the crossing with the Irresistible Spear. Summer knights fought alongside the Dawnish and Urizeni armies, and the Iron Helms waged a merciless onslaught of terror. Five Druj armies under the White Lion, reinforced from the city of Leen, pushed the Empire back. Over fifteen hundred Imperial soldiers died, and perhaps twice as many Druj. Imperial forces were a tenth of the way to capturing the Fens. A potent miasma and a Night shroud lay over the territory. The page also set out three opportunities: intercepting the captive former governor Sarra Grubfeast at the Brineways, warding the Well of Tears against Skathe, and stopping a Druj band heading into Brocéliande.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Gryphon's Pride, under Archavion Wolfborne, marched into the Mallum for the third time with Summer knights at its side. Dawn's Barrens faced Winter husks raised against it, and its Knight-protector of Spring was charged with slaying the Lady of the Dappled Trees.

Druj.t: The Druj defended their heartland under White Lion command and pushed the Empire back to the river at heavy cost. They hold Grubfeast captive for judgement in Leen and are plotting with Skathe and Yaw'nagrah from Murderdale and the Heart of Peytaht.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Valiant Pegasus, under Jack Flint, gathered intelligence from the surrendered Vendarri and fought in the Fens. Highguard's leaders could see Grubfeast handed to the Rahvin to improve relations with that sept.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr had been hunting Sarra Grubfeast in the Sarangrave before she resurfaced in the Salt Flats.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Druj veterans of the fighting in Holberg were among Leen's warriors, and Holberg mercenaries once fought alongside House Bettencourt.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Citadel Guard, under Nicassia Avicia, spearheaded the assault and built the fortified camp that let the Empire cling to the Salt Flats despite the Druj counter-attack.

Varushka.t: The Iron Helms, under Alderei the Fair, were unleashed in a merciless onslaught that spread terror through the Fens. The Leen veterans focused much of their wrath on the Varushkans.

A walk in shadow.o: In Autumn 385YE the Citadel Guard, Valiant Pegasus, Gryphon's Pride and Iron Helms crossed the Nameless River from Saltmarsh into the Druj heartland of the Salt Flats of Sanath. Stiff Druj resistance in the Sydathian Fens drove them back to their first fortified camp, but the Imperial armies held on.

Brocéliande/Dark Ranging.t: Druj warriors with the Lady of the Dappled Trees were seen by yeofolk making their way towards Dark Ranging.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Sydathian Fens.t: The Fens were the battlefield, a miasma-cloaked marsh ruled by the Razorbird clan, where over fifteen hundred Imperial soldiers died. The Empire ended the season a tenth of the way to capturing the region.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the page refers only to the wider Barrens, which Winter spirits could overrun if the Well of Tears is not warded.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: It remains in Druj hands, and some of its Druj joined the band heading for Brocéliande. The page notes it holds no regio linked to Skathe.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Still Druj-held, Murderdale could be fortified by Skathe's hungry ghosts, equivalent to a 2000-strength fortification, if the Well of Tears is not warded. The Sentinel Gate was to open to Hugh's Sward there.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: The four armies gathered at Saltmarsh to ford the Nameless River. Its Vendarri sept, nominally surrendered to the Highborn, briefed the Valiant Pegasus on what lay beyond.

Brocéliande.t: A band of Druj led by the Lady of the Dappled Trees, a herald of Yaw'nagrah, was seen heading through Brocéliande towards Dark Ranging.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: the Gryphon's Pride were repulsed there almost two years earlier, and the Empire had no map of it, as with the Salt Flats.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: many Druj from Leen were veterans of past battles in Holberg, and Holberg mercenaries once fought beside House Bettencourt.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Gryphon's Pride conquered it three years earlier, and its miasma was compared with the stronger one in the Salt Flats.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Druj veterans of Reikos fought in the Fens, and accounts of Grubfeast's cruelty made even veterans of Reikos blanch.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Imperial armies invaded for the first time in many decades and were forced back to their riverside camp, but not out. The territory lies under an ancient miasma and a Night shroud, and Grubfeast is being taken across it to Leen.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr hunted Grubfeast there, and the ghulai Tankath Seveneyes left its Palace of the Sleepers carrying notes on a ritual text being codified there.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: its claiming for the Empire preceded House Bettencourt's ill-fated push into the Barrens.

The Barrens.t: The armies staged from the Barrens, where Druj-held regions threaten to use the Well of Tears to raise Winter spirits. That would leave the whole territory contested unless the regio is warded.

The Semmerlak.t: Mentioned in passing: the Nameless River connects the Semmerlak to the Barren Sea, the Feverwater and the open sea.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the page notes only that the Nameless River links to the Feverwater and on to the sea.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the miasma in the Salt Flats was noted as more potent than the one Imperial armies met in Zenith.

A wandering fire.d: The Bloodcloaks, Green Shield, Drakes, Bounders and Tusks, with three Thule armies and hylje aid, besieged Olgafsdottirshal. The Drakes breached its gates in the second week, though Eisa Winterborn's yegarra held long enough for hundreds of Jotun to escape to Kalant. The Golden Sun then arrived by forced march, and on the fourth day of the Kalant siege Thule warlocks blasted open the gates. Around fifteen hundred alliance soldiers fell. The Shard of Winter seized wealth and thralls, later ransoming them back to the Jotun. The Thule outlawed slavery and asked for help stopping a Jotun ritual to Hayaak at Jaelwif's Mound.

Dawn.t: The Golden Sun crossed the Empire by Autumn-enchanted forced march and arrived at Kalant, lifting Imperial spirits and helping to bring down the last Jotun refuge in Sermersuaq.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Tusks fought in the conquest of Sermersuaq, expecting Wintermark to repay them in Bregasland. Jarl Snekmar also demanded that Imperial Orcs join the warriors sent to face him in a final battle.

Jotun.t: The Jotun lost both great citadels and every region of Sermersuaq, falling back to Skallahn. Some fought on, with a ritual to Hayaak against the Thule, Jarl Snekmar's death-seeking warband, and a pursuit of Wintermark raiders.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm withdrew east to Skarsind through the forests of Hercynia.

Thule.t: Three Thule armies fought alongside the Empire, and their warlocks opened Kalant's gates. The Shard of Winter angered Imperial soldiers by seizing wealth and thralls and ransoming them to the Jotun. The Dragons then outlawed slavery and pleaded for help against Hayaak's heralds.

Wintermark.t: The Bloodcloaks and the Green Shield, who paid heavily for leading the assault on Olgafsdottirshal, helped make Sermersuaq fully Imperial again. Wintermark now has opportunities to recover Tuuli's Eye and to answer Jarl Snekmar's challenge.

A wandering fire.o: In Autumn 384YE an Imperial and Thule alliance stormed the Jotun citadels of Olgafsdottirshal in Tanikipari and the Fortress of Kalant in Stark, driving the Jotun entirely out of Sermersuaq. Afterwards the Thule warned of a Jotun plot to unleash Hayaak's heralds on their warlocks, and several further opportunities arose in the territory.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Mentioned in passing: the garrison of the Thule Citadel of Silver and Bone, which dominates the Silver Peaks, supported the alliance armies.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: The Fortress of Kalant fell on the fourth day of the siege, ending Jotun control of Stark. Conjunctions to Avointaivas and the Flat Hills offer the chance to recover Tuuli's Eye and to intercept a creature pursuing Wintermark raiders.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: Olgafsdottirshal fell after the Drakes breached its gates and is now an Imperial bastion. Tanikipari also hosts the Jotun ritual at Jaelwif's Mound and Jarl Snekmar's raiding camp above Kilpailuala Bay.

Skallahn/Iron Stand.t: Mentioned in passing: the surviving Jotun forces retreated into Iron Stand after Kalant fell.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun had collapsed the western end of the pass, forcing the Summer Storm to take a longer route.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher armies had just left Bregasland, and the Bounders and Tusks expected their northern allies to help retake it in return.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm had to travel through Hercynia's rugged forests because the western end of Pakaanan's Pass had been collapsed.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: more than twenty thousand Thule warriors came out of Otkodov, and the Ambassador to Otkodov received the Thule plea for help.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq was entirely retaken, with the rank two fortifications Olgafsdottirshal and Kalant now in Imperial hands. Jotun remnants, a ritual threat and a mysterious pursuer still trouble the territory.

Skallahn.t: The defeated Jotun retreated into Skallahn, while a successful Wintermark raid there brought back much wealth but left one group pursued back to the border.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm withdrew east to Skarsind.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: Igya Olgafsdottir, builder of the Sermersuaq citadels, is named as eldest child of the Jarl of Tromsa.

A wild night and a new road.d: Imperial access to the Jakhalsmarkt in Betovering was extended, despite the risk of angering the Commonwealth over Jarmish star jewels. The deBruin offered 1,500 effective strength for an attack on Free Landing for 12 Thrones, provided the force receives the Imperial guerdon. Burgemeester Vandersaar invited the League, Highguard and the Brass Coast to celebrate five years of the Alivetti enclave, with assemblies able to encourage or discourage attendance. The Senate might fund magistrates or build the Walls of Liberty to stop smuggling, which would anger the Sarcophan. An administrative motion would settle who may disseminate herbals. The Cathedral of the Navigators kept losing prestige.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but the page discusses Sarcophan entrepreneurs developing a presence in the city-state of Beoraidh in western Mareave.

Highguard.t: Highborn businesses and mines kept earning an extra 18 rings a season from Sarcophan demand for Highborn funerary sculpture, while the Cathedral of the Navigators lost further ministry production and prestige. Highborn citizens were also invited to the Alivetti celebrations, and their assembly could encourage or discourage attendance.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun capture of Meade has put the Master of the Root and Stem trade on hold, which the Delves regard as a minor aberration.

The Brass Coast.t: Ambassador Dino i Riqueza handled Sarcophan relations, and Madruga's senator could hire deBruin mercenaries to help retake Free Landing. Freeborn businesses were invited to the Alivetti festivities, which offered trade diversification, and the Freeborn assembly could back or discourage the event.

The League.t: The Sarcophan enclave in Sarvos marked five prosperous years, and League citizens were invited to its festival. The Senate might fund Sarvosan magistrates or build the Walls of Liberty with a new League title, the Alivetti Gatekeeper. The League assembly had already restricted the Community of Silence to the enclave.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark captains, especially Bron Mordssen, drew praise for their dealings at the Jakhalsmarkt in Betovering.

A wild night and a new road.o: The Civil Service's Winter 387YE report on relations with the Sarcophan Delves covered continued Imperial access to the Jakhalsmarkt and a Sarcophan offer of mercenaries against the Children of Wrecks. It also covered the five-year anniversary party at the Alivetti estates in Sarvos, proposals to police that enclave, herbal trade with the Apothecaries' Guild and the Highborn monument trade.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: The deBruin offered 1,500 effective strength for the next attack on the Children of Wrecks at Free Landing before Summer, for 12 Thrones and on condition that the force receives the Imperial guerdon. They would continue each season until it is back in Imperial hands.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Partly through Sarcophan influence, representatives of Beoraidh planned to visit Anvil at the Winter Solstice, supported by Delves merchants. Diplomatic matters with the city-state fall to the Imperial Consul.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: an earlier wind of fortune on growing Sarcophan influence in the Bay of Catazar is listed in the further reading.

Casinea.t: Casinea's neighbours were invited to the Alivetti anniversary, and every business owner there was due to receive Sarcophan consumables after the Solstice, some of which might be illegal in the Empire.

Madruga.t: Madruga's senator, Eulàlia i Phovas i Riqueza, was one of those who could enlist deBruin aid against the Children of Wrecks. Local business owners were also due to receive consumables from the Alivetti festivities.

Mareave.t: Sarcophan entrepreneurs were eager to develop a presence in Beoraidh in western Mareave, while promising not to antagonise the Empire. Delves merchants were supporting a Beoraidh delegation to Anvil.

Necropolis.t: Necropolis was invited to the Alivetti celebrations, and its business owners were due to receive Sarcophan consumables afterwards, possibly including proscribed goods.

Sarvos.t: The Alivetti enclave at Caricomare celebrated five years with a week-long festival, but magistrates struggled to stop smuggling of illegal goods. The Senate weighed extra funding or the Walls of Liberty in response. A magical mask schema was promised to the Mirrored Maschieri if all three invited nations took part.

Tassato.t: Tassato was invited to the Alivetti anniversary, and its business owners were due to receive Sarcophan consumables, some possibly illegal, after the Solstice.

A wisdom of questions.d: At the Summer Solstice, Herminius's statement that sword scholars should no longer venerate Sulemaine passed the Urizen Assembly 374-16. A 75-liao mandate carried by a known sword scholar could now separate the teachings from the woman. That would shatter the Temple of the Four Winds, drive Sulemainists such as Severus away, and cost every Urizen congregation 2 votes and 1 liao for a year, because it reverses the Assembly's 383YE praise of her. Sulemaine's tomb was not consecrated, to Highborn relief, but some Highborn proposed a writ of consecration needing Synod approval. Cato and Clytemnestra will teach at Laroc, and a Dawnish mandate could spread their questioning ethos there.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish Assembly could send 50 liao to urge the faithful to learn at Laroc. Over time this would mean Synod mandates only affect Dawn if passed by a greater majority, but it would also bring questioning of the noble houses and a threat to the discipline of Dawnish armies.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn histories describe their triumph over Sulemaine's creed in the same terms as victories over the Druj.

Highguard.t: Highborn histories treat those Sulemaine killed as martyrs, and Highguard was relieved that her tomb was not consecrated. Some Highborn priests proposed a writ of consecration that would require approval by a Virtue assembly and the General Assembly.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: sword scholars already teach at the Scholars of the Sword Academy in Holberg.

Urizen.t: The Urizen Assembly could send a known sword scholar to separate the movement from Sulemaine. Doing so would cause an irreversible schism, close the Temple of the Four Winds and weaken all Urizen congregations for a year.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Synod's influence, weakened by earlier sword scholar campaigns, is still diminished in Varushka.

A wisdom of questions.o: After the Urizen Assembly called on sword scholars to stop venerating Sulemaine, several opportunities followed. A Urizen mandate could split the sword scholar movement, Highborn priests proposed a law requiring Synod approval to consecrate tombs, and Dawn's Assembly could embrace sword scholar teaching at Laroc.

Astolat.t: Cato and Clytemnestra of the House of the Wanderer accepted Ser Dindrane de Cantharos's invitation to teach at the small Cathedral of Laroc. A Dawnish mandate could make Laroc a source of sword scholar ideas for the whole nation.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: sword scholars were previously invited to teach in Holberg, at the Scholars of the Sword Academy.

A wizard did it.d: The Imperial regio still cannot enhance ritual lore, and territory-scale rituals at the Summer Solstice risk pronounced side effects. Covens of the same nation can still cooperate freely. A Rivers of Life on Mareave turned its northern regions green until the growth died, leaving rare Spring-realm donahorti that could be preserved if Spring magic is cast on Mareave at the Solstice. The same growth destroyed old ruins and the lighthouse above the Bay of Catazar. The mists over Miekarova's Painted Caves are now permanent, angering the Thule. Seers dreamed of Serenus Starsong, Queen Igraine's regio reverted towards Spring, the Navarr song began fading and northern merchants grew suspicious of coins.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: old Grendel and Skoura ruins in northern Mareave were swallowed by the Spring-infused growth and collapsed with it.

Imperial Orcs.t: Their territory of Mareave briefly turned verdant, breeding cattle and drakes, and now offers a chance to preserve valuable donahorti if Spring magic is cast there again at the Summer Solstice.

Navarr.t: The magical song by Idwynn Splitroot that echoed along the trods began to fade, though Navarr who embrace it may still feel fierce pride in their oaths and tattoos. Some Navarr merchants have also started demanding coins be laid out before accepting them.

Thule.t: The Thule were angered that the mists over the Painted Caves, in a region ceded to them by treaty, became permanent, and the orcs of Otkodov intend to raise it with Ambassador Kindra Surefoot.

Urizen.t: Abandoned Urizen spires in Icarion were reduced to rubble by the dying growth. Seers also dreamed of Serenus Starsong in a Urizen-style gown, and the Citadel Guard can still channel rituals through the Imperial regio.

Varushka.t: The Painted Caves in Varushkan-held Miekarova are now permanently shrouded, removable only by a magnitude-60 Piercing Light of Revelation with sixty rings of ilium. Some Varushkan merchants have grown suspicious of cash.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark merchants were heard whispering of soot in their purses and insisting on seeing coins before payment, a habit spreading to other northern traders.

A wizard did it.o: A roundup of strange magical happenings in Summer 388YE: the astronomantic chaos continued, Mareave briefly bloomed under a wayward Rivers of Life, the Painted Caves enchantment became permanent, and odd dreams, songs and superstitions spread across the Empire.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: Eoradal's scarce waters filled and greenery briefly spread around lakes and wells, before dying back and dragging nearby ruins down with it.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Icarion saw the worst damage, with its abandoned spires left as rubble covered in scrubby grass and odd yellow and orange flowers.

Mareave/Nadir.t: The fertility surge bred hungry young drakes, and Nadir's hunters did a roaring trade killing them before they could prey on farms and the Great Southern Herd.

Mareave/Sinfoyard.t: Sinfoyard briefly turned green as Rivers of Life filled its waters, bringing unfamiliar fruit and livestock fertility before the growth withered and pulled down old ruins.

Bay of Catazar.t: The ruined lighthouse that had stood for centuries on the cliffs above the bay was torn down by the Spring-infused vegetation, the greatest loss among Mareave's ruins.

Mareave.t: A wayward Rivers of Life made the arid north green for a few months before the growth died, destroying old ruins but leaving short-lived donahorti that farms, herb gardens, mana sites and businesses could harvest if Spring magic is cast on the territory at the Summer Solstice.

Miekarova.t: The enchanted mists around the Painted Caves were bound with ilium and became permanent, requiring a magnitude-60 Piercing Light of Revelation plus sixty rings of ilium to lift.

Otkodov.t: The orcs of Otkodov are deeply unhappy about the permanent shrouding of the Painted Caves and plan to raise it with Ambassador Kindra Surefoot.

A yellow star hung.d: Fortifications rose in Ossium's Drownbark Forest and in Operus, Caeli, Serra Briante and Clypion, and Penumbral Veils lingered over Ossium, Madruga, Kahraman, the Barrens and Zenith. The Navarr and the Citadel Guard restored Zenith's trods. Regrow the Land's Heart aided Iteri and western Clypion, but a curse cut Zenith's herb harvests. Storms blamed on the Archmage of Spring battered the Barrens. Weirwater's horse-lovers shared a stormy dream, and artists dreamt of Farren Silver Streams. The Key grew ascendant. Conjunctions were identified to Kephalos' Delve in Screed, where Grendel sky mages were exploring, and to Udoli's Fall in Brez. Olic gave Urizen the Concordance of Earthbound Stars, and Treacher's Quill also entered Urizen lore.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Weirwater saw everyone with an affinity for horses dream of riding a galloping horse along a storm-lashed shore. They woke exhilarated, though the dream taught them nothing new about horses.

Druj.t: Veils still shroud the Druj-held Barrens and Zenith, but the Barrens were battered by storms. The Zenith herb curse hurt the orcs most, and their hold in Iteri and western Clypion was described as weakened.

Grendel.t: A group of Grendel sky mages with mercenary escorts pressed deep into the Black Plateau in Screed and has not returned. A conjunction offers Imperial heroes the chance to discover what they are doing.

Navarr.t: Working with the General of the Citadel Guard, the Navarr successfully performed the Dance of Navarr and Thorn, restoring the trods of Zenith.

The Brass Coast.t: A Frozen Citadel was summoned in Serra Briante, and Penumbral Veils continue to hang over the Freeborn territories of Madruga and Kahraman.

Urizen.t: Urizen gained Frozen Citadels in Morrow and Zenith, restored trods and rejuvenating rains that gave hope to its people in Zenith, though Zenith's herb gardens were cursed. Five new rituals entered Urizen lore, including the Concordance of Earthbound Stars and Treacher's Quill.

Varushka.t: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen now protect Ossium from the Druj, and a veil still hangs over that territory. A conjunction to monster-haunted ruins in Brez was entrusted to the Boyar of the Sovereign's Head.

A yellow star hung.o: In the Autumn of 384YE, magical fortifications, veils and restored trods followed the Summer Solstice. Rejuvenating rains fell on Zenith while savage storms struck the Barrens, and assorted curses, dreams, conjunctions and new Urizen lore emerged across the Empire.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: One of the Frozen Citadels was summoned from the Summer realm in Serra Briante.

Morrow/Caeli.t: A Frozen Citadel was summoned in Caeli during the Summer Solstice.

Morrow/Operus.t: A Frozen Citadel was raised in Operus.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen rose in the Drownbark Forest, helping protect Ossium from the Druj.

Spiral/Screed.t: A group of Grendel sky mages pushed into Kephalos' Delve on the Black Plateau, and Imperial heroes may travel there by conjunction to investigate.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: Bitter Strand bore some of the worst of the storms, with thunder, lightning, mighty waves and even waterspouts.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: Saltmarsh was among the hardest-hit regions in the storms and is likely to have been flooded.

Volodmartz/Brez.t: A conjunction to Udoli's Fall in Brez at 20:45 on Saturday will take heroes to ruins sheltering travellers, where the risk from monsters is high.

Zenith/Clypion.t: A Frozen Citadel was raised in Clypion with the Citadel Guard's aid. The restorative rains encouraged new growth and hope in western Clypion, where the Druj hold has weakened.

Zenith/Iteri.t: The rejuvenating rains were felt most strongly in Iteri, encouraging healthy growth and giving the remaining Urizen hope as the Druj hold weakened.

Zenith/Proceris.t: The enchantment brought a burst of growth to the marshes of Proceris, with bright flowers springing up between octopus-haunted pools and ruined cisterns.

Kahraman.t: A Frozen Citadel was raised in Serra Briante, and a Penumbral Veil continues to hinder divination into the territory.

Madruga.t: A Penumbral Veil still hangs over Madruga, so rituals scrying into it must first overcome the veil.

Morrow.t: Frozen Citadels were summoned from the Summer realm in both Operus and Caeli.

Ossium.t: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen rose in the Drownbark Forest to help protect Ossium from the Druj, and a Penumbral Veil remains over the territory.

Spiral.t: Grendel sky mages were tracked exploring the Black Plateau in Screed, and a conjunction to Kephalos' Delve was identified for an Imperial expedition.

The Barrens.t: Dreadful storms and waves pummelled every region bordering the Barren Sea, likely blunting the Fangs and flooding Saltmarsh. A veil also still shrouds the territory.

The Semmerlak.t: Mentioned in passing: some Weirwater horse dreams involved diving beneath its waters to sunken ruins, possibly linked to strange treasures left on its shores.

Volodmartz.t: A conjunction to Udoli's Fall, among long-forgotten ruins in the far north of the territory, was identified. Travellers there face early snows and monsters.

Weirwater.t: Everyone in Weirwater with an interest in horses dreamt vividly of riding on a stormy, moonless shore, and woke full of wonder.

Zenith.t: Zenith gained a Frozen Citadel, restored trods and muted rejuvenating rains, while its herb gardens suffered a curse that cut their yields. A veil still hangs over it.

About today.d: No public report followed Ambassador Kindra Surefoot's talks with Rak on extending the peace, and the Thule appear to expect a heavy price. If the treaty lapses, war follows in six months, with Thule fortifications and stockpiled mana threatening the north. Warlock Hoosfa Mek arranged for Thule skuldyr to swap non-military tales with Wintermark scops and offered a shared book of stories. The Five Fang Consortium will repay its bonds in full from its mithril mine. Two conjunctions were announced: Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn to find the missing Chosen of Samkǒma, and Halvind Brinegold to calm rogue Thule threatening Wreck's food caravans. Rak deferred talks on Suaq hunting rights until the treaty is settled.

Thule.t: The Thule hold the treaty's fate in their hands, while showing a gentler side through skuldyr storytelling and the Five Fang Consortium's full repayment of Imperial bonds. Some of their people also face trouble: the Chosen of Samkǒma are missing and a rogue band of Volham threatens trade.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan Custodian of the Gift of the Dwindling Star, Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn, was asked to find the missing Chosen of Samkǒma. Void's cabalists warned that the orcs may have made a deal with Fly-the-light.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Kindra Surefoot leads the treaty talks as Ambassador to Otkodov, and Wintermark scops were invited to swap five tales with Thule skuldyr at the Moot Circle. Mediator of Wreck Halvind Brinegold was asked to calm rogue Thule.

About today.o: In Winter 386YE the Civil Service reported on relations with Otkodov, with the peace treaty due to expire at the Summer Solstice 387YE. The report also covered a planned cultural exchange, a Thule consortium repaying its bonds, and two conjunctions involving troubled Thule bands.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Mieriada is the likely setting of the Miekarova conjunction to find the missing Chosen of Samkǒma, though the page names only the territory.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: Mentioned in passing: Warlock Askja dropped vague hints about incidents in Urdur when suggesting the rogue Thule were under some malign influence.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: A Thule band crossed into northern East Floes and is threatening the Wreck food caravans. A combat-likely skirmish is expected there.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The rogue Thule are threatening caravans on the East Floes border with the Silver Peaks.

Verthandi/Askja.t: Mentioned in passing: only Warlock Askja appears, disavowing the rogue band and asking the Mediator of Wreck to calm them.

Verthandi/Hengill.t: Mentioned in passing: Hengill is not named on the page; it is covered only through the wider treaty situation with the Thule.

Miekarova.t: A conjunction was announced for Miekarova to search for the Chosen of Samkǒma, who vanished after leaving the Red Lantern in Void. Combat is possible, and innocents may be present.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov's peace with the Empire runs out at the Summer Solstice 387YE, and the Thule fortifications and mana stockpiles there make war a serious threat. Hunting-rights talks wait on the treaty.

Sermersuaq.t: Rogue Thule crossed into Sermersuaq and threatened the food caravans from Wreck. Rak put off Suaq hunting rights negotiations until the peace treaty is settled.

Verthandi.t: Mentioned in passing: Verthandi is not named directly; Warlock Askja, who oversees the Wreck trade, disavowed the rogue band.

Volodmartz.t: Mentioned in passing: Volodmartz is not named on the page; its only Varushkan links are the Gift of the Dwindling Star and its Custodian.

Abrogate Moonwater Hall.d: Moonwater Hall had been commissioned in Summer 381YE and built with the help of the Faraden merchant families. It provided the benefits of a great work in Upwold, adding income to the territory's farms and businesses. The Senate voted to abrogate it, and the motion passed. Most of the buildings were pulled down, and the Faraden were informed that the Senate no longer wished them to congregate there. The Faraden reacted with some anger. They asked for, and were granted, a week to put their affairs in order, make preparations and send messengers to Faraden merchants visiting the Empire. The hall no longer provides any benefit to Upwold.

The Marches.t: Marcher farms and businesses in Upwold lost the extra income Moonwater Hall had provided, and the Faraden merchant presence in their land was dismissed.

Abrogate Moonwater Hall.o: In Summer 384YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Reikos and seconded by Semmerholm, to abrogate Moonwater Hall, the Faraden trade hub in Upwold. The hall was largely demolished and the Faraden were told to stop gathering there.

Upwold.t: Moonwater Hall was largely torn down, ending its trade benefits to Upwold's farms and businesses, and the Faraden were given a week to leave.

Abrogate motion to construct the Signori.d: Earlier in the Summer 381YE summit the Senate had passed a motion to construct a vineyard in Sarvos, the Signori d'Argento Vineyards, as a sinecure providing money. Later in the same summit Kahraman proposed abrogating that motion, Zenith seconded it, and the abrogation passed, cancelling the commission. The vineyard did not stay cancelled: it was later recommissioned by Brother Dagon of the Shattered Tower, acting as holder of an Imperial Wayleave.

The League.t: The League lost, then regained, a planned Imperial vineyard sinecure in its territory of Sarvos when the Senate's commission was abrogated and the project was later recommissioned through an Imperial Wayleave.

Abrogate motion to construct the Signori.o: In Summer 381YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Zenith, to abrogate its earlier decision that same summit to construct the Signori d'Argento Vineyards sinecure in Sarvos.

Sarvos.t: The Signori d'Argento Vineyards planned for Sarvos were cancelled by this abrogation, though the vineyard was later recommissioned by Brother Dagon of the Shattered Tower.

Accept Barrens peace treaty.d: A delegation from the Barrens negotiated a treaty governing the movement of troops through their lands, and the terms were put to the Senate in a motion proposed by Upwold and seconded by Therunin. The motion stated that it did not cover the Navarri army of the Black Thorns moving through the Barrens into Brocéliande, which was to happen whatever the terms. The motion was defeated and the treaty was not accepted. The Barrens delegation had already left Anvil before the vote, and it is unclear whether they know their treaty has been declined.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named. The treaty came from the orcs and humans of the Barrens, a territory listed as held by the Druj that season.

Accept Barrens peace treaty.o: In Summer 379YE the Senate defeated a motion to accept a treaty negotiated by a delegation of Barrens orcs and humans, which would have set terms for Imperial troops moving through the Barrens.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: the motion excluded the Black Thorns' march through the Barrens into Brocéliande, stating that it would go ahead regardless of the treaty.

The Barrens.t: The treaty offered by the Barrens orcs and humans to let troops pass through their lands was rejected by the Senate, and the delegation may not yet know it was declined.

Accept Grendel proposal.d: An ambassador from the Grendel Salt Lord of Dubhtraig brought an agreement before the Imperial Senate. Proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Feroz, the motion accepted it: one Grendel army would leave Spiral in return for the Empire refraining from raiding Dubhtraig for one year, with further negotiations possible afterwards with this Salt Lord or others. The motion changed no law and was a statement of principle by the Senate. The Grendel remained barbarians, and raiding their fleets remained entirely legal.

Grendel.t: The Salt Lord of Dubhtraig secured the Senate's acceptance of a deal under which Dubhtraig would be spared Imperial raids for a year in return for withdrawing one Grendel army from Spiral, though Grendel fleets remained lawful targets for raiders.

Accept Grendel proposal.o: In Winter 378YE the Senate formally accepted a proposal from the Grendel Salt Lord of Dubhtraig: the Grendel would withdraw one of their armies from Spiral if the Empire did not raid Dubhtraig for a year.

Spiral.t: Under the accepted agreement, the Grendel occupiers of Spiral were to remove one of their armies from the territory in exchange for a year without Imperial raids on Dubhtraig.

Accept Jotun ceasefire.d: Proposed by Upwold and seconded by Mitwold, the motion agreed a ceasefire running from the start of the Spring Equinox 377YE until the start of the Spring Equinox 379YE. Imperial armies were barred from entering territories claimed by the Jotun, including Liathaven and Mournwold, while Jotun campaign armies would not enter Imperial territory. Subsidiary motions to outlaw raiding on the Jotun during the ceasefire and to declare them foreigners for its duration were defeated. At the Spring Equinox 378YE the Senate extended the treaty to the start of the Spring Equinox 380YE, but at the Summer Solstice 379YE it abrogated the ceasefire early in order to give military aid to the Lasambrian orcs against the Jotun.

Jotun.t: The Jotun's offer of peace was accepted, so their campaign armies would stay out of Imperial territory while their claimed lands were spared Imperial attack, until the Senate broke the truce in Summer 379YE to aid the Lasambrian orcs against them.

Accept Jotun ceasefire.o: In Summer 377YE the Senate accepted the Jotun offer of a two-year ceasefire, passing the motion by 27 votes to 0, so that neither the Jotun nor the Empire would make war on the other.

Liathaven.t: As a territory claimed by the Jotun, Liathaven was closed to Imperial armies for the duration of the ceasefire, leaving it in Jotun hands without Imperial challenge.

Mournwold.t: The ceasefire barred Imperial armies from entering Jotun-held Mournwold, halting any Imperial campaign to retake it while the truce held.

Accept Orcs of the Great Forest treaty.d: Proposed by Holberg and seconded by Feroz, the motion passed and survived Constitutional Court scrutiny. The treaty, negotiated at the Spring Equinox summit by Miroslav di Sarvos and the Speaker of Totems, lets the Great Forest live as guests of the Navarr in the Lower Tarn Valley for five years, hunting, building and trading. In return they will defend Therunin and fight alongside Navarri armies in the Barrens under their own warchief, sharing knowledge of the Druj through a Military Liaison. They may practise their religion privately but not proselytise. Should the Barrens fall to the Empire, the valley returns to Imperial control and the Heart of Peytaht is ceded to the Great Forest.

Druj.t: The treaty binds the Great Forest to make common cause against Druj attack and to share their knowledge of the Druj with the Empire, though they may take no action against the Druj while the Empire is at peace with them, save in self-defence.

Navarr.t: The Navarr host the Great Forest orcs as guests in Therunin for five years, gaining allies who will fight alongside any Navarri army in the Barrens; Navarri may walk the trods freely through the leased land but may not hunt there.

Accept Orcs of the Great Forest treaty.o: In Summer 381YE the Senate passed a motion ratifying a peace treaty with the Orcs of the Great Forest, recognising them as a sovereign foreign nation. The orcs, formerly of the Barrens, became officially foreigners and were granted residence in the Lower Tarn Valley of Therunin.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Lower Tarn Valley becomes the leased home of the Great Forest orcs for five years, where they may hunt, build and trade, and where Imperial citizens may stay under the Way or leave with guaranteed safe passage.

Therunin.t: Therunin gains orc defenders sworn to protect the territory for the duration of the treaty, while its Imperial residents keep their right to live and gather resources there.

Accept Sarcophan Delves treaty.d: The treaty, signed by Imperial Consul Aureliana Perpetua Nicasia Saverio di Sarvos, Ambassador Thanmir Hrafn and Edwin Vandersaar, offered 24 wains of white granite a season at 32, 29 and 26 crowns for successive batches of eight. It would hold while neither party was at war with the other, with quantity and price open to renegotiation after a year. A Senate-appointed minister would oversee purchases. Proposed by Miaren and seconded by Zenith, the motion passed. The Bedelaar-Huisbaas ratified it, and work on the docks in Redoubt could begin after the Winter Solstice 380YE. Construction would cost 40 wains of weirwood, 10 of white granite and 12 thrones 4 crowns, and take three months. The civil service sought the proposing Senator's guidance on whether the overseeing title would be national or Imperial.

Urizen.t: Urizen was to host the new cargo dock and ministerial offices in its territory of Redoubt. If the overseeing title were made national, Urizeni citizens might appoint the minister using their traditional methods.

Accept Sarcophan Delves treaty.o: In Autumn 380YE the Senate passed a motion ratifying a trade treaty with the Sarcophan Bedelaar-Huisbaas Vandersaar, under which the Empire could buy 24 wains of white granite each season. A cargo dock and ministerial offices were to be built in Redoubt to receive it.

Redoubt.t: The Senator intended to build the cargo docks and ministerial offices for unloading Sarcophan white granite in Redoubt, with work able to begin after the Winter Solstice 380YE.

Accept Thule peace treaty.d: Under the recorded terms, the Thule would withdraw from Branoc and Crowslook and would not harm any Varushkan, with Varushkans likewise not harming the Thule. The Thule would receive the Silver Peaks, the Empire would withdraw all its forces from there, and the Thule would leave the rest of Sermersuaq. Hostilities would cease for three years, and neither side would invade the other's other controlled regions or raid the other. After a year of the treaty holding, information about the Enemies of the Empire and further trade opportunities would be negotiated. The Thule would also receive a usable ritual script for Crystalline Focus of Aesh, chosen from an approved list.

Thule.t: The Thule gained the Silver Peaks, a usable ritual script for Crystalline Focus of Aesh and three years of peace with the Empire. In return they agreed to leave Branoc, Crowslook and the rest of Sermersuaq and to refrain from invasion and raids.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark lost the Silver Peaks in Sermersuaq to the Thule, with all Imperial forces to withdraw from there. In return, the Thule would leave the rest of the territory and hostilities would cease for three years.

Accept Thule peace treaty.o: In Summer 379YE the Senate considered a motion, proposed by Volodmartz and seconded by Morrow, to accept a peace treaty negotiated by a Thule delegation. The recorded outcome set out a three-year cessation of hostilities between the Thule and the Empire.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The Silver Peaks were ceded to the Thule, and the Empire was to withdraw all its forces from the region.

Sermersuaq.t: Under the treaty, Sermersuaq was partitioned: the Silver Peaks passed to the Thule, while the Thule agreed to leave the rest of the territory.

Accomplices.d: The heralds mocked the Synod, the Empress and the Military Council, complaining that only Towlen Nighthaven (Deadfall) and Mirella of the Twisted Rose (Amber Lance) had backed the Golden Axe, and that no guerdon was paid. Agramant offered two pawns of heart's blood to every unit supporting an Imperial army in Therunin, although accepting it is illegal while it remains under enmity. If no army attacked, it would again offer a Reconquer Therunin venture, allowing pseudonyms on its roll. Dochas, summoned to inquisition by Eskah Swift Hart, refused to surrender until the work was done. He offered a conjunction to the Weeping Glade and the recovered Iron Helms standard as a gift. The Chief Magistrate ruled that lawful cooperation with him was permitted.

Druj.t: The Druj still held Peakedge Song, Upper Tarn Valley and East Ashes in Therunin, where their remnant leadership continued to oppress the Navarri, but they had lost Lower Tarn Valley to the Golden Axe.

Navarr.t: Agramant's heralds urged the Navarri to question whether the Empire truly cared about Therunin, despite the Navarr National Assembly's repeated rejections of its offer. Meanwhile, Dochas Weeping Glade pressed on with his own plan to liberate the territory.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the heralds jeered that four Imperial armies were 'having a holiday' in the Urizen territory of Zenith.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: a quoted Navarr Assembly statement directed people to the Stormcloaks of Wintermark for help against Blood on the Snow.

Accomplices.o: Agramant's heralds in Therunin derided the Empire for sending only the Golden Axe and two military units to retake Lower Tarn Valley. The Bloody Ally offered heart's blood to any unit supporting an Imperial attack there, while the outlaw Dochas Weeping Glade invited Imperial representatives to a Sentinel Gate meeting to plan the territory's liberation.

Therunin/East Ashes.t: The region remained under Druj control, but a Sentinel Gate conjunction opened for four people to the Weeping Glade there, where Dochas and his allies would meet Imperial representatives.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as completely dominated by the vallorn.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as completely dominated by the vallorn.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Golden Axe, supported by Deadfall and Amber Lance, made progress in retaking this region from the Druj.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Mentioned in passing: noted as still under Druj control.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as completely dominated by the vallorn.

Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley.t: Mentioned in passing: noted as still under Druj control.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Mentioned in passing: the heralds noted that six Imperial armies were fighting there, and Dochas lamented that the crushing of Sanath seemed to come before Therunin.

Therunin.t: Heralds of Agramant worked throughout the territory, aiding the fight against the Druj and the vallorn while spreading propaganda. Agramant offered heart's blood to units supporting any Imperial army attacking there, and Dochas sought Imperial help to retake the rest of the territory.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the heralds mocked the four Imperial armies stationed there as being on holiday.

According to principle.d: The Commonwealth remained locked in war with Jarm over Lantir. Moved by Gisli Baerson's donation, Professor Gelberg's academics arrived offering him a first Beurteilung (appraisal). They proposed auctioning further appraisals from Spring 387YE, which would need a Senate motion welcoming them. Engineer Poldi Hellebrant continued building the diplomatenschloss in Necropolis, uneasy about the nearby Jarmish embassy. Commonwealth ports now offered war goods such as Soul Honey, War Amulets, Bloodclay and Hero Stone instead of herbs, ingots and measures. The Asavean bounty curtailed Commonwealth shipping. The Empire assured the Commonwealth it would not contact Viyerda. Holberg's 250th anniversary drew Commonwealth interest, and the League Assembly could issue a supportive statement of principle.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Commonwealth soldiers joke that enough Soldatentrunk on the breath could drive the orcs of the Mallum away.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the new diplomatenschloss replaces the embassy destroyed during the Grendel attack on Madruga.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Ingenieurin Hellebrant oversees the embassy's construction from quarters in the Highborn town of Hedra.

The Brass Coast.t: The Commonwealth appreciated Freeborn efforts to protect trade in the Bay of Catazar, and recalled Commonwealth soldiers fighting beside the Freeborn at the fall of Siroc. It was also kept informed about events in Madruga.

The League.t: The Commonwealth showed keen interest in Holberg's 250th anniversary. The League Assembly was offered the chance to uphold a statement of principle welcoming Commonwealth guests and endorsing Commonwealth ideals, which could lead to closer ties.

Urizen.t: The Commonwealth was reassured that the Conclave had worked with Sadogua to extend the wards protecting the Lyceum and its Commonwealth Schloss until Winter 387YE, though it wants its magicians brought home.

Wintermark.t: Gisli Baerson of Wintermark, "the Provider", received a commendation from the Commonwealth generals for donating mana and coin. He was offered the first appraisal by Professor Gelberg's scholars.

According to principle.o: The Civil Service's Winter 386YE summary of relations with the Commonwealth reported that a party of Commonwealth scholars under Professor Immanuel Gelberg had arrived in Sarvos to offer appraisals in return for donations to their war against Jarm. It also covered sweeping changes to trade at Leerdam and Volkavaar.

Necropolis/Hedrossan.t: Poldi Hellebrant oversaw construction of the new Commonwealth embassy from her quarters in the town of Hedra.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Professor Gelberg was based at the General Benbow Inn in Cigno, where Gisli Baerson could send a winged messenger to commission the first appraisal.

Bay of Catazar.t: Freeborn efforts to protect trade in the bay were welcomed, but the Asavean bounty kept the long journey from the Sea of Steel treacherous for Commonwealth merchants.

Holberg.t: Holberg's 250th anniversary drew interest from Commonwealth historians. Professor Gelberg's expedition planned to visit its walls, markets and university, though the Militärattache could not attend.

Madruga.t: The old Commonwealth embassy destroyed in the Grendel attack on Madruga is being replaced, and the Commonwealth was pleased to be kept informed of the situation there.

Necropolis.t: Construction of the fortified diplomatenschloss continued in Necropolis; most of the weirwood had been supplied but much white granite was still needed. Its engineer worried about Jarmish vessels sharing the Couros river.

Redoubt.t: The Lyceum and the Commonwealth Schloss on the island remain protected by Sadogua's wards until Winter 387YE, and the Commonwealth wants a way found to bring its magicians home.

Sarvos.t: The Commonwealth warship Bemühen landed Professor Gelberg's party of scholars at the Sarvos docks. They engaged a Sarvos printing house to publish their findings.

Across the Abyss.d: Freed from Druj slavery and settled in Misericorde, the Sand Fishers were transformed by the Imperial victory and by Bartimaeus of the Shattered Tower's Prosperity mandate. They came to believe the Way had beaten the Druj miasma. They asked for Imperial education and access to Holberg University, for Imperial lore through the Conclave, and for a Senate appraisal of Holberg's forests. They also arranged to trade herbs for mithril or weirwood at the planned Misericorde Market, saying it was 'for next time'. Troubled by the tenet to despise those who take without giving, they asked what they could do for the Empire. The Synod raised statements of advice, and the Senate raised Holberg's funding to support their study at the university.

Druj.t: The Druj risked everything on an attack into Holberg to punish the Sand Fishers' 'rebellion', but Imperial heroes intercepted them and their armies fled back into the Barrens. Their former slaves now say their ancestors urge them to wipe out every last Druj.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Eliza recalls reading that Imperial Orcs often hear conflicting things from their ancestors, which proves a poor guide to the Sand Fishers.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: a recent misunderstanding in Therunin is cited as an example of the risks of sharing Imperial lore with outsiders.

The League.t: Holberg's people were urged to trade fairly with the Sand Fishers and did so. The territory's merchants and the coming Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market stood to gain herb trades for mithril or weirwood, and Holberg University was opened to the orcs through extra Senate funding.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's free basic education for citizens is described as a legacy of Urizen joining the Empire.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers were first encountered when Imperial armies invaded Ossium, the land they fled.

Across the Abyss.o: After Imperial forces drove a Druj army out of Holberg in Winter 383YE, the Sand Fishers embraced the Virtues, especially Prosperity, with new fervour and began petitioning the Empire for education, lore and development. They also asked what they could give the Empire in return.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: The Sand Fishers' new home in the forests of Misericorde was the Druj army's target before it was stopped. The orcs there now consecrate round houses, await the Misericorde Market and are eager to develop the largely undeveloped land.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Mentioned in passing: the forests of Utterlund are noted as having only sporadic farms and herb gardens, as part of the case for an appraisal of Holberg's wilds.

Holberg.t: The Druj invasion of Holberg was repelled. The Sand Fishers living there grew in Prosperity and Ambition, and they won Senate funding, raised through Holberg's upkeep, to study at Holberg University. A planned market there is set to trade their herbs for mithril and weirwood.

Ossium.t: Ossium was where the Sand Fishers were enslaved and brutalised by the Druj for decades and where the Druj kept herbal places of study. The Druj took heavy losses there, and its defeat is held up as proof that their hoarding failed them.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: a recent misunderstanding in Therunin is cited as a warning about how shared ritual lore might be used unexpectedly.

Across the seven seas.d: The in-character story has the Freeborn painter Mirkala, at Siroc, telling children about the seven seas: Sighs, Teeth, Storms, Salt, Steel, Snow and a mysterious seventh sea of starlight. Enchanted fleets ran into mist-shrouded islands with unliving courtiers, a pig-obsessed Night magician, helpful dolphins, an angry pirate, a ghost ship of dead Sarcophan to be beaten in a rhyming contest, dodos guarding tempest jade, an ambergris-spewing whale and a giant sea turtle mistaken for an island. Overcoming these challenges brought extra wealth and tales to tell in Anvil. Rhianos appears to be a Summer eternal. Imperial scholars know little of them, and the Empire has had no significant dealings with them for centuries.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: in Mirkala's story, sailors returning through the Sea of Sighs are relieved to be nearly home, provided they can get past the Grendel.

Navarr.t: All fleets owned by Navarr characters were enchanted, so captains who traded abroad or went privateering met strange maritime adventures and earned additional booty.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Mirkala describes the Sea of Snow stretching past Otkodov, 'where the wicked Thule live', and claims no ships sail it because of ice and the dark magic of the dragon princes.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Mirkala jokes that the Sea of Storms is deep enough to swallow the mountains of Urizen, with wizards bobbing up complaining about their ruined silk robes.

Across the seven seas.o: Through the past season, every fleet belonging to Navarr and Varushkan captains carried a potent Summer enchantment, so those who went privateering or traded with foreign ports met strange adventures at sea and came home with extra booty. The magic came from scrolls delivered at the Winter Solstice by heralds of Rhianos, Regent of the Eternal Ocean.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Mirkala describes the Bay as only the northernmost part of the Sea of Sighs.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Mirkala's tale has the Sea of Snow stretching past Otkodov, home of the Thule.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: in Mirkala's story it is the ice-filled sixth sea, rumoured to hold strange beasts such as horned whales and giant tusked seals, and said to be shunned by ships because of the ice and the Thule's magic.

Address boggart infestation in Morrow.d: The motion set out to trap the boggarts plaguing Morrow, which had been causing the loss of mana from the territory's mana sites. It passed at a cost of 25 thrones, and the Synod passed a statement of principle saying it had no intention of vetoing it. The 25 thrones were disbursed to Senator Sarvos. Together with a successful quest by the Academy, the traps prevented further loss of mana from Morrow's mana sites. In an unexpected side benefit, boggart faeces was harvested and used to enhance the herb gardens of Morrow. The wider campaign outcome is recorded as unknown.

Urizen.t: Urizen's senator Sarvos proposed the motion and received the 25 thrones, and with the Academy's successful quest the nation stopped boggarts draining mana from its sites in Morrow.

Address boggart infestation in Morrow.o: In Winter 378YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Sarvos and seconded by Necropolis, to trap the boggarts infesting Morrow and stop them damaging its mana sites.

Morrow.t: Boggarts infesting Morrow were trapped, ending the loss of mana from the territory's mana sites, and their droppings were put to use enriching Morrow's herb gardens.

After the gold rush.d: Steinr thane Cenred Xunhand, inspired by Alfmund Forwinsson's Synod judgement, planned to offer a prize to the scop who told the best story of non-martial heroism; his Suaq daughter Erna died defending Skarsind. Vulpius, herald of Ephisis, was to hold a silent auction of curios in the Hall of Worlds. Something that arrived after the surge of Night magic invited visitors to a chamber beyond a night regio in Miaren, offering rewards for new experiences. Marquis Joueur was to auction an invitation to Prospero's Threadweaver game. Alejandro i Galiano i Erigo's ship, the Passion of Flame, was to be sold on the Bourse. The Revelry, former bandits of Holberg, sent Finn von Holberg to seek a new patron.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Cenred's daughter Erna is said to have died defending Skarsind, the Imperial Orc territory, alongside Britta of the Green Shields.

Navarr.t: An unknown entity has settled beyond a night regio used by local vates in Miaren, inviting people to perform for it and bring it new experiences in return for rewards.

The Brass Coast.t: A Galiano dhomiro, sickened by the slavery seen in Maragladia, was retiring to farm olives and putting their weirwood-reinforced ship up for sale, while Marquis Joueur intended to hold his auction at the Brass Coast camp.

The League.t: The Revelry, a Holberg military unit of former bandits, was seeking a new patron among Holberg-based guilds and free companies, with its quartermaster planning to report to a League egregore.

Wintermark.t: Thane Cenred Xunhand challenged the scops of Wintermark to tell the best tale of heroism that does not involve battle, offering a prize in the spirit of Alfmund Forwinsson's Synod judgement.

After the gold rush.o: Ahead of the Summer Solstice 383YE, a series of opportunities arose at Anvil: a Wintermark thane's storytelling contest, two auctions by heralds of Autumn, a mysterious presence in a Navarr night regio, a Brass Coast fleet offered for sale, and a Holberg military unit seeking a new patron.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: The Revelry had been operating in the forests of Misericorde, fighting the bandits still infesting the woods, but found the work too poorly paid to continue without a patron.

Holberg.t: The Revelry, awarded as spoils after Holberg's liberation in 379YE, had fallen on hard times guarding caravans and hunting bandits, and sought a new patron from Holberg's guilds and free companies.

Madruga.t: The Passion of Flame, a swift fleet based in the town of Calvos, was offered for sale on the Bourse as its owner retired from trade.

Miaren.t: Since the recent surge of Night magic, something new has made its home in a chamber beyond a night regio in a forest near the ruins of Seren, sending tendrils to invite visitors.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Erna, daughter of Cenred Xunhand, was killed defending Skarsind as adjutant of the Green Shields.

Against the Jotun.d: After capturing Mathilda Fisher, the Empire retreated into Sermersuaq, and Yrsa Jansdóttir's forces retook Tromsa. The Bloodcloaks, Green Shield, Red Wind Corsairs, Summer Storm and Tusks, with over sixty captains, attacked the Iron Stand but met four southern Jotun armies. After a pre-battle toast with Bjorgthorn Hammerhand, three days of fighting left a stalemate. The Empire is a quarter of the way to taking the Iron Stand, and honourable Wintermark fighting reduced its casualties by a tenth. Summer Storm orcs heard a new ancestral voice in their fighting pits. In Kahraman, Lasambrian raids halted road restoration, delayed the Red Depths and left Gambit three-fifths conquered. Three Sentinel Gate opportunities were also announced.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Mouse of Dawn, Sebastián Fawnwood and Urien Novarion are listed among the captains who fought in Skallahn.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Summer Storm fought in the Iron Stand, and many Skarsind captains joined the campaign. Sunstorm orcs who tested themselves in the army's fighting pits heard an unnamed ancestral voice urging them to fierce loyalty to family and vengeance on traitors.

Jotun.t: Under Yrsa Jansdóttir, the Jotun reclaimed Tromsa. Four southern armies with local fyrds held the Iron Stand to a stalemate, and the Lasambrian Jotun raided Kahraman and pressed towards the conquest of Gambit.

The Brass Coast.t: The Red Wind Corsairs fought with notable restraint in Skallahn, helping to bury an old Winterfolk slur against the Freeborn. Meanwhile, Kahraman suffered a fresh Lasambrian invasion that halted its great Senate projects.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Viktor von Temeschwar is listed among the captains, and an unnamed League general is quoted on contingency planning.

The Marches.t: Marcher armies led the vanguard in Tromsa, and the Tusks fought in the Iron Stand. The Imperial Advisor for the Feni was offered a chance to atone for the Alderly killings by saving a Feni enclave in Liathaven.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Aulus Warcaster of Zenith is listed among the captains and named by the Bloodcloaks' general.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Maria Alexandrovna Kabanova of Ossium is listed among the captains fighting in Skallahn.

Wintermark.t: The Bloodcloaks and Green Shield fought with honour in the Iron Stand, earning Jotun respect and mutual quarter that cut Wintermark casualties by a tenth. The Imperial Seer was asked to lead a strike on Jarl Ebbe.

Against the Jotun.o: In Winter 385YE the Imperial armies withdrew from Tromsa after defeating the new Jarl and taking Mathilda Fisher, and a vast Jotun force swiftly reclaimed the territory. Most of the remaining armies then invaded the Iron Stand in Skallahn and fought to a bloody stalemate below Oversgaard, while the Lasambrian Jotun invaded Kahraman again.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: Lasambrian soldiers reached the region and paid respects at the Fort Braydon burial mound. A Jotun warband also seized a Bataguin caravan there and took Erdene Bataguin as a thrall.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: The Lasambrians camped in Gambit, taking villages and estates, and are over three-fifths of the way to conquering it. The Sentinel Gate is to open at the Path of Idina.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: Lasambrian warbands were sent east to harry the people of the Jade Range.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: A magical citadel was raised in the mountains above Serra Briante, helping to deter the Lasambrians.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: A magical citadel garrisoned by lion-headed ogres stood above Serra Damata and turned back probing Lasambrian scouts.

Liathaven/Liath's Heart.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named; the threatened Feni enclave is described only as lying in the depths of Liathaven.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Mentioned in passing: the earlier killings of the Feni of Alderly are what the Marchers are invited to atone for.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: Mentioned in passing: Halka, a herald of the Ancient One, was first spotted near the Old Pig in Freemoor.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: The Imperial armies camped briefly at Olgafsdottirshal in Tanikipari, waiting for the Red Wind Corsairs before crossing into Skallahn.

Skallahn/Greenwall.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Seer is named as responsible for stopping 'the Jarl of Greenwall', though the opportunity concerns Jarl Ebbe of the Iron Stand.

Skallahn/Iron Stand.t: Three days of fighting below Oversgaard and the fallen Iron Banner ended in stalemate, leaving the Empire a quarter of the way to taking the region. Jarl Ebbe is calling up its fyrd.

Skallahn/Ulfrsmoor.t: The Imperial plan to besiege Ulfrsborg was blocked by the Southern Bear and the Iron Host, with skirmishes fought across eastern Ulfrsmoor.

Tromsa/Icewood.t: The Imperial armies withdrew through the forested borders of the Icewood into Sermersuaq.

Tromsa/Majastind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun response may have been driven by fear that the Empire would despoil Mount Majastind and the graves of the ancestors.

Tromsa/Rikskog.t: An immense Jotun force under Yrsa Jansdóttir entered Rikskog from the south to catch the invaders, arriving too late.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Mouse of Dawn, a captain from Astolat, fought in the Skallahn campaign.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Marcher captains from Bregasland are listed among those in Skallahn, and scions of Cold Sun are said to have been seen there.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: many Hahnmark captains are listed, including Lofyn Blood-cloak and the warriors of Dunhearth Hall.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: Hordalant is not named in the page and is linked only through the wider Jotun campaign.

Kahraman.t: The Lasambrians invaded again, seizing about ten wains of white granite and halting road restoration. Work on the Red Depths is delayed until the Spring Equinox, and a Sentinel Gate opportunity was announced to rescue a captured Faraden architect.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: several Kallavesa captains are listed among those fighting in Skallahn.

Liathaven.t: A warband under Urse Longarm is moving to breach the wards of a hidden Feni enclave in Liathaven. The Imperial Advisor for the Feni was charged with stopping them via the Sentinel Gate.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold captains are listed among those in Skallahn, and heralds of the Mother of Wrecks are recalled as having appeared there.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold captains are listed, the dour Mournish are quoted, and Halka was sighted in Freemoor.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Maria Alexandrovna Kabanova of Ossium is listed among the captains.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun warband holding Erdene Bataguin is heading back towards the border with Reinos.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: those fighting alongside the Burning Falcon in Segura are referenced for comparison.

Sermersuaq.t: The Imperial armies retreated from Tromsa into Sermersuaq and rested briefly before invading Skallahn. Several Sermersuaq captains, including Iron Osric, joined the campaign.

Skallahn.t: The Imperial invasion of the Iron Stand met four southern Jotun armies and stalled below Oversgaard after three days of heavy fighting. The Empire is a quarter of the way to taking the region, and Jarl Ebbe is calling up a fyrd.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: numerous Skarsind captains are listed, and the page muses on a possible new understanding between Jotun and Skarsind.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Viktor von Temeschwar is listed among the captains.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: Sebastián Fawnwood of the Barrens is listed among the captains.

Tromsa.t: The Empire defeated Igya Olgafsdottir's warriors and took Mathilda Fisher before withdrawing. The Jotun then swiftly reconquered every region the Empire had taken.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold captains of the Hartell Household are listed among those in Skallahn.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: Urien Novarion of Weirwater is listed among the captains.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Aulus Warcaster, called the Dragon of Zenith, is listed among the captains.

All I ask of you.d: The mystagogues learned the little left to know of Great Forest beliefs. The sept also confided two fears: that the Synod might proscribe their faith, and that the Montanian orphans they shelter will one day seek answers from the Empire. Nimon Rue of Cassad Ûln had twice threatened to execute the orcs enslaved at the Sacred Grove and the Grove of Woe. Vallack says he has not replied. The Navarr and Imperial Orc assemblies could each appoint a leader for a venture to Rescue the Great Forest Orcs. Its success would depend on the strength committed, possibly boosted by the Northern Eagle, Winter Sun, Gryphon's Pride, Irra Harah or the Karass, though Karass treachery would weaken it.

Dawn.t: The Gryphon's Pride could station themselves in the Barrens as a logistics hub for the raid, exposed to heavier casualties, as a tangible gesture that might soften Great Forest hostility to the Dawnish. Lady Gwendoloena de Ordraig and Reynard of De Gauvain could also appeal to the Karass for help.

Druj.t: Nimon Rue threatened to impale the enslaved Great Forest Orcs, and the planned raid could strip the Druj of these slaves and of weirwood from the Sacred Grove and the Grove of Woe.
