Imperial Orcs.t: The Unshackled Assembly's delegation uncovered the Druj threat. The nation could now appoint a raid leader and commit military units, personal resources and the Winter Sun to rescuing their Great Forest 'cousins'.

Navarr.t: The Navarr, sworn to protect the Great Forest Orcs, could appoint a raid leader and commit units and personal resources to the rescue. Young Great Forest Orcs from Hercynia were also due to visit their camp to offer support for the new armies.

Thule.t: The Thule would allow Imperial armies to join their fight in Ulnak from Oerwealt, but only if they acknowledged Tathenon the Gyre's strategy. Their war has put Cassad Ûln's garrison on high alert.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun was stationed in the Urizen territory of Zenith.

Varushka.t: The Northern Eagle could order a Strike at the Grove of Woe to aid the raid, though the Great Forest Orcs blame the Varushkans for slaughtering the Montanians at Hope's Rest.

All I ask of you.o: An Imperial Orc delegation under Skywise Rykana, sent to learn about the Great Forest Orc ancestors, found that the Druj were threatening to impale thousands of enslaved Great Forest Orcs unless Chief Vallack collaborated. This opened an opportunity for the Navarr and Imperial Orcs to organise a rescue raid into Druj lands.

Forest of Ulnak/Deathsgate.t: Hundreds of Great Forest Orcs are enslaved at the Sacred Grove near the Deathsgate fortification, and were the main target of the Ulnak raid along with its weirwood.

Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire.t: A Sentinel Gate conjunction to the strong Spring regio of Moss End, guarded by Druj, offered a chance to cast Forge the Wooden Fastness and bring Irra Harah's forces into the raid.

Forest of Ulnak/Oerwealt.t: The Thule-held Oerwealt could serve as a launch point for the Winter Sun, and casting Forge the Wooden Fastness there, possibly with Woodward, would bolster the Thule and let Irra Harah aid the raid.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Lower Saarnath.t: The Northern Eagle had isolated Lower Saarnath, fuelling rumours of a planned Imperial invasion, which gave the army a fleeting chance to strike at the Grove of Woe.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Ûrinth.t: A Northern Eagle strike at the Grove of Woe would trade casualties with the garrison of The Witness in Ûrinth, at an estimated cost of 900 Imperial casualties.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: Mentioned in passing: Ser Guy of the Twisted Rose aided the anti-Druj insurgents of Nesustak Forest and built trust there.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: Mentioned in passing: the Northern Eagle slew the Montanians at Hope's Rest, a deed that colours Great Forest attitudes to Varushka.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the page refers only to the Barrens generally as the destination for rescued orcs and a staging area.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: used to compare how hard it is for Bramblepatch to enter Ulnak with how hard Astolat is for Agramant's heralds.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Hundreds of Great Forest Orcs enslaved at the Sacred Grove faced execution by Nimon Rue of Cassad Ûln, whose huge garrison patrols the territory. The raid, the Winter Sun and a Spring ritual offered ways to free them.

Hercynia.t: Great Forest Orc youths living in Hercynia planned to visit the Navarr camp to discuss supporting the nation and its new armies.

Miaren.t: Small Great Forest Orc communities live in Miaren, and some of their younger members feel less wary of the Empire than their elders.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not named in the text; its only link is indirect, through the involvement of Varushka's Northern Eagle.

Otkodov.t: The Thule invasion of Ulnak was launched from Otkodov, and the Winter Sun could only order Break the Chains by joining that attack.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Several thousand Great Forest Orcs enslaved at the Grove of Woe faced execution. Three massive fortifications make the territory hard to raid, though the Northern Eagle was already operating there.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Ser Guy of the Twisted Rose built trust by aiding the anti-Druj insurgents of Nesustak Forest.

The Barrens.t: Rescued Great Forest Orcs would be brought back to the Eaves of Peytaht in the Barrens, where the Gryphon's Pride could stage the raid and the Northern Eagle could retreat to cover the refugees.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Great Forest Orc communities lived there and suffered heavily fighting beside the Navarr before the Druj conquered it.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun was in Zenith and would need Find the Best Path to reach the Forest of Ulnak.

All I can do.d: Beoraidh, a neutral free port under Sarcophan protection, offered to halve the basilica's 27-Throne labour cost if an orc commissioned it. Elsbeth di Sarvos noted that an army enchanted with Bound by Common Cause on a defensive order could supply 108 crowns of labour. The Weavers of Culwich offered tapestries of weltsilver and iridescent gloaming in place of mithril. Tibisi of Shelah's Bounty suggested redirecting the Grand Ossuary of Reikos's donations to provide 10 wains of white granite. The Aghnayadh Apothecaries offered to fund the land if the Senate devolved drug legality to the Imperial Apothecaries Guild. Ambassador Kaltrin also tacitly welcomed discreet Imperial spies, through a proposed 12-Throne Regario Dossier motion.

Dawn.t: The Weavers of Culwich, a Dawnish cabal, offered to replace the basilica's mithril with tapestries depicting moments of Virtue, at a cost of 400 ingots of weltsilver and 400 measures of iridescent gloaming. The Cat's Graces could reduce this cost.

Grendel.t: Beoraidh had broken from the Grendel but welcomed their merchants. Proposed Imperial agents there could gather intelligence on the Grendel, and any Grendel shift to aggression in Mareave would stop an Imperial army from helping with construction.

Highguard.t: Highborn ambassador Melkior championed the basilica, and the Benefactors Council was urged to pause the Grand Inspiration to fund it. Reikos's Grand Ossuary donations were offered as an alternative source of funds.

Imperial Orcs.t: Beoradhi investors offered to cover half the basilica's labour costs if an orc commissioned it. Bloodcrow Rasp, Senator for Skarsind, co-funded the land purchase after the Equinox.

All I can do.o: The General Assembly's backing for a Basilica of the Way in the independent city-state of Beoraidh brought forward several offers to help fund and build it, alongside a chance for the Senate to extend the Regario Dossier's spies into the city. After the Autumn Equinox 388YE, Bloodcrow Rasp and Herminius of the House of the Wanderer provided the twenty Thrones needed to buy the land.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: The city-state was the site of the planned Basilica of the Way, and its land was paid for after the Equinox. Its Aghnayadh Apothecaries sought influence with the Imperial Apothecaries Guild, and its docks were proposed as a listening post for Imperial spies.

Mareave/Sinfoyard.t: Mentioned in passing: Sinfoyard is recognised by the Senate, together with the city of Beoraidh, as part of the neutral state.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name the Bay directly. It is linked only through the maritime trade and docks of nearby Beoraidh.

Mareave.t: Mareave was the proposed site of a grand Basilica of the Way in Beoraidh, with Imperial soldiers potentially labouring there under defensive orders. Any campaign in Mareave would halt that help.

Reikos.t: The Steward of the Ossuary could divert the Grand Ossuary's donations from Reikos's congregations for six months to supply white granite for the basilica. In return, the Steward would receive four doses of liao each season.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's Senator, Bloodcrow Rasp, had earlier pushed through investment in Beoraidh's docks and helped pay for the basilica's land.

Weirwater.t: Culwich in eastern Weirwater, famed for its flax and wool, is home to the Weavers of Culwich, who offered tapestries for the basilica. Artists may have been drawn to Dawn to help them.

All along the watchtower.d: Imperial troops in the Mourn were shunned or driven off with rough music. Locals accused the Empire of caring only about killing Jotun. A landskeeper plan to have Rivers of Life cast failed when the Empire lost access to Spring regio. The Marcher assembly's statement on punishments was undercut when the Conclave added another Spring curse to lore. The civil service identified several options. One was a proposed Declaration of Remorse, costing 25 thrones per ritual, to destroy every text of Rivers Run Red and Mountain Remembers its Youth. Others were making the Singing Caves a Marcher national seat, a no-retreat mandate, and 75 thrones a season to feed orc thralls. A harsher alternative was a Senate law letting armies Lay Down the Law. In the end the Marcher assembly passed the mandate, and Mel of Mourn spread it with liao.

Jotun.t: Jotun forces in the Mourn were falling back in terror before the Iron Helms' onslaught. The orc thralls they had brought with them were left trapped, short of food and in growing danger from Imperial armies.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman is named as a neighbouring territory, and the Hierro clan is cited as an example of the risks of encouraging virtue.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Mournwolders assumed a League prince would end up holding the Singing Caves. Holberg is cited as land that joined the League only after Dawnish conquest.

The Marches.t: Marchers in the Mourn grew deeply alienated from the Empire over the curses and the war. The Marcher assembly then passed a mandate that no Marcher army can ever again give ground, a gesture of solidarity with the Mournwolders.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher assembly's statement notes that the Urizen General was rebuked by the Synod over the cursing of the Mourn.

Varushka.t: The Iron Helms under General Akstis Eigulys used visible, merciless tactics against Jotun warriors and spared civilians, yet left Mournwolders fearful of what fresh orders might bring. Empress Varkula's letter to a Karsk senator is also quoted.

All along the watchtower.o: In Summer 381YE the people of the Mournwold turned bitterly against the Empire after Imperial Spring curses killed a sixth of the population and the Iron Helms waged a campaign of terror against the Jotun. The civil service set out several partial remedies, and the Marcher assembly answered by mandating that no Marcher army would ever give ground.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Overton in Greensward had held out against the Jotun. The Singing Caves mithril mine near Overton was proposed as a Marcher national seat, after the Senate's earlier allocation to the Marchers had been vetoed by the Throne.

Tassato/Madeiras.t: Mentioned in passing: a tinker reports that the failure of Spring regio was being felt in Madeiras as well.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: named alongside Upwold and Mitwold as Marcher lands whose shared resolve to defend their land the no-retreat mandate would show.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as an example of a land that joined the Empire only after Dawnish armies conquered the surrounding territory.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a territory across the border with whose people some Mourn thralls have less in common than with their orc neighbours.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: a letter from Empress Varkula to a Karsk senator is quoted.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Harry Archer, a thresher from Mitwold, devised the proposed Declaration of Remorse, and Mitwold is named among the Marcher lands the mandate would align with the Mourn.

Mournwold.t: With Imperial armies driving out the Jotun, the Mournwold seethed with anger over the curse deaths and the Iron Helms' brutality. Imperial soldiers were shunned and orc thralls were left hungry, leaving the territory close to rebellion once the armies depart.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a territory across the border with whose people some Mourn thralls have less in common than with their orc neighbours.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: named alongside Mitwold and Bregasland as Marcher lands whose shared resolve to defend their land the no-retreat mandate would show.

All at sea.d: Asavea is hosting a summit that excludes the Liberty Pact, and Jarm has closed its ports to Imperial captains. The Alivetti estates in Sarvos were ceded to the Sarcophan Vandersaar, who are building an enclave there and offering land for a Temple of the Way in the Delves. Asavean exiles in Trajadoz are sending envoys to Anvil. Smuggling rings into Faraden lands were confirmed in Kahraman and Segura. A Sentinel Gate conjunction allows a meeting with the Great Forest Orcs. The Thule released almost all remaining Imperial slaves. At the Solstice the magistrates were sent to investigate the smuggling, and the College of Maykop and Lyceum Schloss were commissioned.

Dawn.t: The Free Folk exiles were invited by troubadours to discuss moving to Dawn, and Dawnish envoys could meet the Great Forest Orcs, who hold enduring grudges against Dawn.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Axou scouts aided the Imperial spy network completed in the Druj-held marshes of Sarangrave.

Grendel.t: Now treated as foreigners, the Grendel hold the Temple of the Black Bull in Feroz and let Asavean merchants dock there, drawing to themselves the goodwill Imperial fleets once enjoyed. They are also rumoured to be sending a delegation to the Nemoria gathering.

Highguard.t: Highborn ambassadors handle Jarm and Sumaah, while Necropolis saw an expanded Sarcophan herb warehouse, a dispute over the Black Sails Quay, and a Free Folk pilgrimage to Empress Richilde's tomb.

Imperial Orcs.t: Chainbreaker Pakt serves as Ambassador to Asavea, and the orc-controlled Steel Fist Bourse seat permanently gains 4 extra rings of ilium each season from the new Sarcophan enclave.

Jotun.t: The Jotun hold the Faraden embassy, smuggled goods flow into their territory of Reinos, and a Thule delegation was coming to Anvil to propose an alliance with Wintermark against them.

Navarr.t: Their Great Forest Orc allies will only meet through a delegation that includes a Navarr, and twenty Navarr artisans taken by the Thule at Treji were returned home.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn host Asavean exiles at Trajadoz and were found to be running smuggling rings into Faraden lands. Rival Synod mandates could oppose or back the smugglers, and at the Solstice the magistrates were sent to investigate.

The League.t: The ruined Alivetti estates in Sarvos were ceded to the Sarcophan for a trading enclave, Empress Giselle's tomb became a guided landmark, and League ambassadors handle the Commonwealth and Faraden.

Thule.t: The Thule released what they say are all their remaining Imperial slaves under the Sungold treaty, apparently put down trouble in Sküld, and planned to send envoys to Wintermark about an alliance against the Jotun.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Tarquinius Ankarien is Ambassador to Axos, and Commonwealth magicians are studying at the Lyceum. The Redoubt senator's motion for the Elosian docks has made no progress.

Varushka.t: Commonwealth zauberer visited the Icy Crag in Miekarova, and groups of freed Imperial slaves were handed over in Miekarova and at Ivarsgard in Karsk.

Wintermark.t: A Thule delegation was coming to court Wintermark for an alliance against the Jotun, Thanmir Hrafnar is Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves, and about a dozen Winterfolk artisans remain held by the Thule.

All at sea.o: Ahead of the Winter Solstice 383YE, this Wind of Fortune surveyed the Empire's relations with foreign powers. Relations with Asavea and Jarm worsened, ties with the Sarcophan Delves, Commonwealth and Axos grew warmer, smuggling across the Brass Coast's western border was confirmed, and the Thule freed their last Imperial slaves.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Rumours tell of conflict here, possibly involving the vallorn around the lost city of Emrys, which the Thule appear to have suppressed.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: A Sentinel Gate conjunction at 2pm on the Sunday lets six people reach the Chief's Contemplation Glade to meet Chief Vallack and the elders, now guarded by the completed Holt of the Oak.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the bay is not named directly, though the page covers the overseas trade and diplomacy carried by the Empire's southern sea routes.

Feroz.t: The Temple of the Black Bull still stands under Grendel control, and Asavean merchants dock there by order of the Salt Lords. The Wisdom Assembly wanted the temple destroyed, but the Empire cannot do so.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: twenty Navarr artisans taken during the Thule conquest of Treji in Hercynia were among the freed slaves.

Kahraman.t: Several smuggling rings were found moving goods from Kahraman into Faraden lands, with one route running on into the Marches. One proposed mandate would give its businesses extra ingots.

Karsk.t: One of three large groups of freed Imperial slaves was delivered by the Thule to Ivarsgard in Karsk.

Madruga.t: The empty town of Trajadoz now houses the Marracossan and Free Folk exiles from Asavea, who are seeking recognition of their settlement and a temple to their gods.

Miekarova.t: A Commonwealth professor and students studied Summer lore at the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, and a group of freed Imperial slaves was delivered here.

Mountains of the Moon.t: Mentioned in passing: a copy of the Empire's map of the mountains was shared with Axos under the treaty.

Necropolis.t: The Kruidenkenner Magazijn at Crown's Quay was expanded, Axou traders petitioned to change how the Black Sails Quaymaster is appointed, and Free Folk pilgrims decorated Empress Richilde's tomb.

Otkodov.t: The Thule homeland sent back almost all remaining Imperial slaves across its border, and there was apparently conflict in Sküld that the Thule appear to have contained.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the senator of Redoubt raised a motion to build the Elosian docks, but no progress has been made.

Reinos.t: Goods smuggled from the Brass Coast pass into the Lasambrain Hills of Reinos, west of the Freeborn border.

Sarangrave.t: Axou scouts and Toxatai supported the Imperial spy network completed in the marshes and will share any intelligence it gathers, including a possible map.

Sarvos.t: The Alivetti estates were ceded to the Sarcophan Vandersaar, who are raising an enclave there and giving guided tours of Empress Giselle's ruined tomb. Asavean backers of the Cavabiance Docks fear being forced to stop trading.

Segura.t: Smuggling rings operate here despite the war with the Jotun, and members of the Hand of Dumon were executed crossing from Segura into the Confederacy. One proposed mandate would give its businesses extra ingots.

Skarsind.t: One of three groups of freed Imperial slaves was delivered here, and visiting Thule merchants brought vague word of trouble in Sküld.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the situation in Grendel-held Spiral is covered in a separate wind of fortune.

Therunin.t: The Great Forest Orcs and their Navarr neighbours came through the clash with the Heirs of Terunael largely unscathed, the Holt of the Oak was completed, and the new senator is expected to lead the delegation through the Sentinel Gate.

All in red.d: After Moonwater Hall in Upwold was abrogated and torn down, the Court of Five Winds asked for recompense for the 20 wains of white granite and 20 crowns Faraden families had invested. Six weeks later Modnos agents set fires in Tassato and Redoubt. There were no deaths. Five arsonists were arrested, refused to pay their fines and face likely execution, and Chief Magistrate Stanislav Karkovich was asked for advice. The Modnos lifted their bounties on Livia and Astrid but raised the bounty on Colwynn de Rondell to 30 Thrones. Tchinua Ganbatar then deposed the Lady of the Five Winds, and an envoy is promised for the Autumn Equinox to discuss the Liberty Pact, sanctions and religious attitudes.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial help to Faraden against the Jotun is cited as one reason some Faraden families value the Empire.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tsagaan grudge over the execution of the Brass Coast's Honradez sisters is noted, and the new Faraden ambassador has arrived at the embassy in Segura.

The League.t: Tassato's Blood Red River Museum was badly burned and three arsonists were held there. The Senate may now repair or grandly expand the museum, the printing houses of Tassato and Sarvos could take over publishing Echoes of the Labyrinth, and League ambassador Erasmo di Tassato faces a delicate diplomatic task. Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato is no longer under a Modnos bounty.

The Marches.t: Moonwater Hall in Upwold was closed and torn down by Marcher militia and magistrates. It no longer benefits Marcher farms and businesses, and the Faraden want payment for their lost investment.

Urizen.t: Spider's Vantage Spire was nearly gutted, losing its printing press and warehouses. Its torchbearers plan to rebuild themselves, which halts widespread publication of Echoes of the Labyrinth for about six months. Livia of the Celestial Cascade is no longer under a Modnos bounty.

All in red.o: In Summer 384YE, Faraden anger at the Senate's abrogation of Moonwater Hall boiled over: Modnos arsonists burned the Blood Red River Museum in Tassato and Spider's Vantage Spire in Redoubt, and a bloodless coup soon put the Ganbatar family in charge of Faraden.

Redoubt.t: Modnos arsonists nearly gutted Spider's Vantage Spire, destroying its printing press and warehouses. Two Faraden were arrested and face likely execution.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: its printing houses are named as a possible alternative publisher of Echoes of the Labyrinth if the Senate amends its motion.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the Faraden embassy is in Segura, where the new ambassador Arban Tuvalk arrived with letters from the new Liege.

Tassato.t: The Blood Red River Museum was gutted in one wing and many artworks were lost, so its Pride congregation benefits are suspended. The Senate can repair it or rebuild it on a grander scale before the Autumn Equinox 384YE, or lose the site.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the damaged museum was paid for by Temeschwar's Bloody Butchers Guild and built on foundations laid by Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar.

Upwold.t: Moonwater Hall was abrogated and most of its buildings demolished, ending its benefits to Upwold's farms and businesses and sending Faraden merchants away aggrieved.

All laudable qualities.d: Following a Winter 387YE call, the Assembly of Nine appointed Wulfric of the Marches as Symposiarch after he swore an oath in their presence. Sessions on heresy, idolatry, blasphemy, abuse of powers, desecration and other matters were scheduled in Anvil's sodality chamber. Magistrates advised that debating what should be a religious crime is legal, but actually committing a proscribed act would be prosecuted. Magistrate Abraham may attend the opening and two Chief Magistrates will try to be available. The Marcher Assembly invited the Mournwold orcs, whose heretical belief in orc reincarnation the Synod can no longer ignore; Hap the Soft will try to attend. The Assembly of the Way invited the Raboviches of False Hopes and the Hall of the Newborn Sun to represent Lucidianism.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: False Hopes was built from the bones of an old Druj logging camp, and the Hall of the Newborn Sun once rewarded efforts to rid Urizen lands of the Druj miasma.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold orcs are noted as having once been Jotun before becoming Marchers.

The Marches.t: Wulfric of the Marches leads the Symposium, and the Marcher Assembly unanimously invited the Mournwold orcs, forcing the Synod to confront the unresolved clash between their reincarnation belief and the Doctrines of Faith that the Marchers promised would be settled later.

Urizen.t: Lucidianism, founded in the spires of Urizen, is to be represented at the Symposium, with the Urizen citadel of the Hall of the Newborn Sun invited and Phocas planning to arrive for the start.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan banner the Raboviches of False Hopes was invited to represent Lucidianism, though they had not yet said whether they would accept.

All laudable qualities.o: In Summer 388YE the civil service published the timetable for the Proscription Symposium led by Wulfric of the Marches, alongside magistrates' guidance on religious crimes and details of invited guests: the Constitutional Court, the Mournwold orcs and two Lucidian groups.

Morrow.t: Morrow is home to the Hall of the Newborn Sun, the Urizen Lucidian citadel invited to address the Symposium, whose arbiter Aphroias previously secured recognition that Lucidian views were not heretical.

Mournwold.t: The orcs of the Mournwold, whose belief in reincarnation is plainly heretical under the Doctrines, were formally invited to speak, with Hap the Soft intending to attend; a proscription of their belief could only end in bloodshed.

Ossium.t: The Raboviches of False Hopes, an outpost in south-east Drownbark in Ossium, were invited to represent Lucidianism at the Symposium.

All lift together.d: Pahkina's statement of principle passed 223-0 at the Autumn Equinox 383YE. It confused many, as few outside Anvil knew of Asny's role as 'head healer'. The healers offered four routes. Existing herb sinecures in Hahnmark could become annual titles with a duty to supply Wintermark's heroes, gaining a ministry. The Healing House of Wittal Grove could be rebuilt in Kallavesa (56 wains of weirwood, 112 crowns) with a Grimnir of Wittal Grove title. An Assembly mandate could let warriors work for herbs. Hufi's Garden near Masi could be commissioned as a Woundbinder of the Mark sinecure. The Senate commissioned the Healing House, but its motion had significant problems.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: raids against the Druj in the Mallum are named as one way warriors could earn herbs if the proposed Wintermark mandate were enacted.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn of Liathaven, which the Jotun then held, is named as a place warriors might raid for herbs under the proposed mandate.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn of Hercynia is named as a place warriors might raid for herbs under the proposed mandate.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's grimnir and healers rallied to the Assembly's call. They offered to sell spare herbs to titles that serve the nation's heroes and proposed new great works, titles and a mandate. The Senate commissioned the Healing House of Wittal Grove, though the motion ran into legal trouble.

All lift together.o: The Wintermark National Assembly's call for more healing herbs to support Asny of Storm Spire and the nation's warriors stirred debate among the grimnir, who put forward several ways to secure herbs. The Senate went on to commission the Healing House of Wittal Grove at the Winter Solstice, though problems with the motion left the Constitutional Court to resolve them.

Hahnmark/Kalpamark.t: Kalpamark hosts the hot-spring Garden of Falling Snow and the Master Apothecary's Garden. The page suggests the Gatekeeper of Falling Snow title could be reshaped to serve Wintermark's warriors, as the Master Apothecary already does.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: The overgrown, Spring-touched ruins of Hufi Villesdottir's estate near Masi were proposed as Hufi's Garden. This sinecure, for a Woundbinder of the Mark, would cost 16 wains of white granite and 32 crowns, and its commissioning is not recorded here.

Kallavesa/Wittal Grove.t: Elina of Redleaf's Hall proposed rebuilding Sigrid the Redleaf's old Healing House at Wittal Grove under a Grimnir of Wittal Grove. The Senate commissioned it at the Winter Solstice, but the Constitutional Court is resolving problems with the motion.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark's existing herb sinecures and Freya's Garden were pointed to as resources. The sinecures could be amended into annual titles obliged to supply Wintermark's warriors and able to buy herbs.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: its vallorn is listed as somewhere military units might raid for herbs if the Wintermark mandate were enacted.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa was singled out by the Assembly's call. Proposals followed for the Healing House of Wittal Grove, which would add a shared bounty of 90 herbs a season to Wintermark herb gardens there, and for Hufi's Garden near Masi. The Senate commissioned the Healing House at the Winter Solstice.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: its vallorn is listed as somewhere military units might raid for herbs if the Wintermark mandate were enacted.

All my magic friends.d: A Winter curse over Casinea made still water freeze and show viewers the spectres of those they had wronged. Highguard's inquisition routed followers of the Whisper Gallery, though three cultists escaped. The Alders-Baart family were struck by sickness. The dead village of Wilkza rose to celebrate Vesna's coronation. Day boggarts plagued Casinean archivists. Odd portents followed Madruga's tragedies. The Lictors praised Ashborn Trosk and promised contracts for the Autumn Hammers. Arhallogen sought a Navarr fane, and the Azoth demanded profound change of the Navarr. Sanvar Isk denied slaving. Kaela challenged Orc and Wintermark banners. Challenge the Iron Duke became uncastable. Tharim offered his knights to the new Throne.

Dawn.t: Scringol the Hunter, a herald of Jaheris, sought representatives of House de Gauvain and Thanàte Sangwine in the Dawnish camp, and Barien's heralds asked for Aldwyn Wyldrose of Dawn and held a challenge scroll for Rillian de Gauvain.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel and their Asavean allies are named as the cause of the brutality visited on Siroc, and their conquest of Feroz as one of Madruga's woes.

Highguard.t: The Highborn endured the Casinea curse and a plague of Day boggarts, while their inquisition exposed dozens of Whisper Gallery dealers and arrested two covens, with three cultists' details passed to Brother Aemon.

Imperial Orcs.t: Heralds of the Lictors praised Ashborn Trosk and planned to offer contracts granting qualities to the new Autumn Hammers at the Spring Equinox, and Kaela challenged Orc banner-bearers to bind their banners for a year.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun Lasambrians are listed among the troubles afflicting Madruga.

Navarr.t: Arhallogen sought a fane creating a Huntsmaster of the Spider King for a Navarr vate, the Wolf Spider brought a hunting challenge for the thorns, and the Azoth said it could transform the Singing Stone only if the nation fundamentally changed.

The Brass Coast.t: In the wake of Siroc's fall, the Three Sisters constellation shone unnaturally bright to the Freeborn, even at Anvil, while the personae of Death and Fortune wandered Madruga laying curses on those who lingered near them.

The League.t: Sanvar Isk, operator of the Loom of Spells in Tassato, sought out League bishops to quash rumours that he used slave labour before auctioning access to the Loom again.

Varushka.t: The dead villagers of Wilkza rose to celebrate Vesna Borkovna Prochnost's coronation and local boyars asked Varushkans to see them back to their barrow, while a herald of Tharim brought an offer of his knights to the new Throne.

Wintermark.t: Kaela's grim legion came to the Tree of Names to bind Wintermark banners to a year-long challenge, and Barien's heralds summoned Ishka and Jaska about their challenges.

All my magic friends.o: A Winter 385YE Wind of Fortune gathered many smaller magical happenings across the Empire, from a fading Winter curse over Casinea and a risen dead village in Miekarova to offers, challenges and complaints from eternals including Arhallogen, the Azoth, Kaela, Barien, Jaheris and Tharim.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Brianna Black Blood identified a suitable regio in Elerael for Arhallogen's proposed fane, the Centipede General's preferred site.

Madruga/Torres.t: The last eyewitness reports placed the wandering personae of Death and Fortune in Torres.

Miekarova/Perumaki.t: The dead village of Wilkza in Perumaki rose to offer twisted hospitality in celebration of the coronation, shrouded in plaguewulf miasma.

Therunin/Eastring.t: A suitable regio in Eastring was identified as the alternative site for Arhallogen's proposed fane.

Brocéliande.t: Arhallogen preferred his proposed fane to be built in Brocéliande, the Singing Stone the Azoth offered to transform came from there, and one suggested change for the Navarr was abandoning settlements in its vallorn.

Casinea.t: A Winter curse froze Casinea's still waters into mirrors showing the spectres of those the viewer had wronged, and a swarm of Day boggarts harried its archivists and filled its newspapers with rambling articles.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the conquest of Feroz is listed among the troubles the Three Sisters portent was first thought to reflect.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is named as one of the more civilised places the Navarr might settle if they abandoned the vallorn.

Kahraman.t: After Siroc's fall, the unnaturally bright Three Sisters constellation was also observed over Kahraman.

Liathaven.t: The Azoth suggested the Navarr could fully abandon Liathaven and formally renounce their claim to it as one way to bring about the change it required.

Madruga.t: Scarred by blight and the burning of Siroc, Madruga saw the Three Sisters shine ever brighter and the personae of Death and Fortune roam the land, cursing those who spent long with them.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is named as one of the more civilised places the Navarr might settle if they abandoned the vallorn.

Miekarova.t: The long-dead village of Wilkza rose from its barrow to celebrate the new Throne, and the Sentinel Gate opened so Varushkans could attend and see the dead returned to rest.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Tharim's black-clad knights are said to be resting in Sarvos.

Segura.t: After Siroc's fall, the unnaturally bright Three Sisters constellation was also observed over Segura.

Skarsind.t: Heralds of the Lictors visited Skarsind to observe the mustering of the Autumn Hammers and were pleased by what they saw, and Janon's heralds sought out the Skarsind College of Pitfighting.

Tassato.t: Broadsheets around the Loom of Spells regio in Tassato insisting Sanvar Isk was not a slaver instead set the salons and taverns gossiping about abductions.

Therunin.t: Therunin was offered as the acceptable alternative site for Arhallogen's fane, and was also named as a civilised place the Navarr might settle if they left the vallorn.

All the news from Twin Town.d: Merchant-Prince Benjamin of the Featherwick Guild proposed refurbishing his great aunt's derelict building in Regario as an Imperial Consulate, requiring a Senate motion, weirwood, white granite and 80 crowns. He also suggested the Consul appoint ambassadors, an option later withdrawn. After Alfredo Barossa's statement inviting Seren to become the fifth League city, Tassatans proposed markets at Tagliano and Holt, and a Mestran Hills Mutual Association trading ore for Navarr herbs. Merchant-Prince Mariana von Mestra drafted a Synod mandate offering the Whittle folk sanctuary in Little Mournwold, at the cost of their green iron. Rumours of murder, sabotage or rioting surrounded the Arratan Gamble quarries.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are said to have preferred dealing with the Imperial Fleet Master over the Consul, and Prince Benjamin does not count the Fleet Master as a proper ambassador whatever they say.

Highguard.t: Gossips claimed the incident at the Arratan Gamble quarries was the work of a secret society seeking to remove the Highborn holder of the seat, Ames of Reikos.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun advance is recalled as having driven the Whittle villagers from their homes to Tassato in 380YE.

Navarr.t: The League statement inviting Seren to join it got a mixed reception among the Navarr. In response, Tassatans proposed joint markets at Tagliano and Holt and a trading association giving Navarr herb garden owners their own Imperial title overseeing a metal ministry.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Siroc is named among the cities that could only join the League if Madruga seceded, something pundits called inconceivable.

The League.t: Tassato offered several proposals: an Imperial Consulate, trade works with Navarr, a League Bourse title overseeing a herb ministry, and a possible Synod mandate granting the Whittle folk sanctuary. Sarvos, Holberg and Temeschwar remained preoccupied with curses and attacks.

The Marches.t: The Little Mournwold enclave of Marchers in Tassato Mestra is troubled by the Marcher assembly's ultimatum to the Whittle folk. A proposed League mandate would offer the Whittle folk sanctuary away from orcs.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are noted as preferring to deal with the Varushkans rather than the Consul, even after agreeing to embassies between Otkodov and the Empire.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim is named among cities that could not join the League without Hahnmark seceding, and the Feni are said to have ignored the Consul during trouble in Hahnmark.

All the news from Twin Town.o: In Autumn 383YE the twin cities of Tassato, enjoying relative peace while other League cities suffered, put forward several proposals: an Imperial Consulate in Regario, two trade projects with Navarr prompted by a statement inviting Seren to join the League, and sanctuary for the Whittle folk. A rumoured incident also struck the Arratan Gamble quarries in Enterio.

Miaren/Holtford.t: The town of Holt was proposed as the Navarr half of the Road to Seren markets, with warehouses to channel lumber trade towards Tassato.

Tassato/Enterio.t: A week before the Autumn Equinox, rumours spread of an incident at the Arratan Gamble's white granite quarries, with talk of murder, sabotage and rioting likely exaggerated.

Tassato/Madeiras.t: Gemma Stewart's Forge and Furnace Fellowship proposed building a trading post at the base of the hills in western Madeiras, where mining guilds would sell ore to the Navarr in exchange for herbs.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Little Mournwold in Mestra hosts a thriving Marcher enclave and could take in returning Whittle folk under a proposed mandate. They might then help revive the old mine workings above the city.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: A derelict four-storey building near the University of Tassato in Regario, with its own dock, was proposed for refurbishment as the Imperial Consulate.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: some Marchers settled in Little Mournwold in Tassato come from as far afield as Bregasland.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is cited as a territory that would have to secede for Kalpaheim to join the League, and as a scene of recent unpleasantness involving the Feni.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's people are described as dealing with curses that withered their gardens.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is named as a territory that would need to secede for Siroc to join the League, which was deemed inconceivable.

Miaren.t: Miaren could gain a market at Holt as part of the proposed Road to Seren, giving its forest owners a seasonal share of 54 crowns. Its herbalists could also trade with Tassatan miners through the proposed Mutual Association.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is named as a territory that would need to secede for Meade to join the League.

Mournwold.t: The Whittle folk of the Mournwold faced the Marcher assembly's ultimatum. A proposed League mandate would let many of them leave for sanctuary in Tassato, ending the green iron from the Whittle Hill mine.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is named as the site of grudgingly agreed embassies between the Thule and the Empire.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Arratan Gamble seat is held by Ames of Reikos, whom rumour named as the target of the quarry incident.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos's people are described as dealing with curses that shattered their mirrors.

Tassato.t: Tassato enjoyed relative peace and became the source of proposals for an Imperial Consulate, trade works with Seren, and sanctuary for the Whittle folk. Meanwhile rumours of trouble swirled around its Arratan Gamble quarries.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar's people are preparing for further attacks, and the city is cited as a historical example of a city joining the League.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: some Marchers settled in Little Mournwold in Tassato come from Upwold.

All the night-tide.d: The Delves warned the Grendel Salt Lords to stop attacking vessels trading with the Empire, and announced talks to gain a trading enclave in Beoraidh in return for backing its neutrality. They offered discounted white granite for a fortified lighthouse at Oranseri if the Senate ceded an enclave there. Highborn art sales to the Collectors sect cost the Cathedral of the Navigators prestige. The Silent Manse in Sarvos was completed. The Jakhalsmarkt opened selling partly Jarmish goods, and the House of the Buidelrat offered Moeraskriden access in exchange for two rituals. The Kruidenkenner made proposals to the Apothecaries' Guild, and Sarcophan merchants sought Hahnmark farmers about strange flowers.

Dawn.t: Ser Rosalynn Redgrave, a renowned Dawnish artist, is expected to begin decorating the completed Silent Manse, and Poortwachter Farber has written to confirm the agreement.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: their invasion and the spreading vallorn are blamed for putting Thornsong House out of action.

Grendel.t: The Sarcophan have warned the Salt Lords to stop attacking independent vessels in the Bay under the Pax Sarcophan, and their planned treaty with Beoraidh could complicate Grendel ambitions in Mareave.

Highguard.t: The art and stone deal with the Collectors raised Highborn production, but it backfired on the faith: the Cathedral of the Navigators lost prestige, and its Low Ministry and Merchant Ministry are set to decline.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn were offered Sarcophan white granite and DeBruin warships to help build and defend a fortified Celesti Lighthouse at Oranseri. Speaker Esmé i Estrico i Erigo's approach to the Kruidenkenner opened new herbal proposals.

The League.t: With the Silent Manse complete in Sarvos, the League Assembly urged polite disinterest, and a mandate was proposed to discourage citizens from visiting the temple.

The Marches.t: The Kruidenkenner proposed that the Apothecaries' Guild, rather than the Tally of the Votes, appoint the Master of the Root and Stem, which would gain extra herb purchases. The position would still go to a Marcher unless the Senate opened it to all citizens.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen traders' term "Triumph Vis" is cited, and its magicians are noted as having some knowledge of Jarmish star jewellery.

Wintermark.t: Sarcophan merchant Florian Kraft and vintner Renaten Zuredruiven sought to meet Hahnmark farmers at the Wintermark Tree of Names about the strange draaikolkbloem flowers.

All the night-tide.o: Sarcophan relations with the Empire in Autumn 387YE centred on the Pax Sarcophan against piracy, a planned treaty with Beoraidh, and an offer to invest in a new Celesti Lighthouse. The season also brought new trading opportunities, proposals for the Apothecaries' Guild, and fallout from the trade in Highborn art.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Mentioned in passing: hostile, supernaturally strengthened forces controlling the Cazar Straits make sea access to Oran challenging.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Oranseri is the proposed site of the fortified Celesti Lighthouse citadel, where the Sarcophan want a docks enclave and offered DeBruin warships and a defensive venture and voyage.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Mentioned in passing: Free Landing is held by hostile, supernaturally strengthened forces that hinder access by sea to Oran.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Sarcophan is negotiating with former Salt Lord Ehsan for a trading enclave in exchange for supporting Beoraidh's neutrality. The Empire might yet influence or oppose the treaty.

Mareave/Sinfoyard.t: The Civil Service judged the proposed Sarcophan treaty would likely help protect Sinfoyard, alongside Beoraidh, from the Grendel.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Mentioned in passing: the page discusses the Kruidenkenner Magazijn at Crown's Quay in Necropolis, without naming Longbeach.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Ser Rosalynn Redgrave, the artist hired for the Silent Manse, is from Astolat.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Pax Sarcophan is meant to protect independent shipping in the Bay from Grendel piracy, though not Imperial ships. The Delves also seek a port on the Bay at Beoraidh.

Feroz.t: The Sarcophan offered cheap white granite and naval help for a fortified Celesti Lighthouse at Oranseri in return for a trade enclave, but the lighthouse had not yet been commissioned.

Hahnmark.t: Mysterious spiral draaikolkbloem flowers keep appearing among the vlinderbloem grown for Sarcophan merchants, prompting visitors from the Delves to seek out Hahnmark's farmers.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: hostile, supernaturally strengthened forces holding Free Landing make sea access to Oran difficult.

Mareave.t: A Sarcophan treaty with Beoraidh could shield the city-state and Sinfoyard from the Grendel and boost local prosperity. It would also mean either side needs four of the remaining regions to control the territory, and would limit Imperial influence in Beoraidh.

Mitwold.t: The Kruidenkenner Magazijn at Meade, overseen by the Master of the Root and Stem, would gain extra herb trade if the Apothecaries' Guild took over appointing the title.

Necropolis.t: The Kruidenkenner Magazijn at Crown's Quay would let the Kruidenkenner Trademaster buy marrowort and true vervain if the Apothecaries' Guild took over appointing the title.

Sarvos.t: The Silent Manse was completed in the Alivetti Estates, prompting League calls for disinterest. The Gold Leaf Gardeners kept trading there under Luca Beekhof.

All the way.d: The Red Wind Corsairs, Winter Sun and Quiet Step advanced on Anduz to find the Lasambrians gone. They had stripped the area of food and wine, and the Corsairs raided their supply lines, taking wagons and prisoners. Segura is wholly Freeborn again. The Hierro, Corazón and Escuta, newly intensified by the relics, entered Gambit with Steven of Sarcombe's Yegarra and offered locals loyalty or exile. Corazón raids threatened white granite and mithril caravans, and the Fort Braydon garrison slowed their advance. A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered a chance to stop the Yegarra-led push on Rojota, and the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills was asked to recover goods looted from Redhill Pastures.

Jotun.t: The Lasambrian families quit Segura with their recovered relics, largely without support from other Jotun, then invaded Kahraman more driven and daring than before, vowing one day to reclaim the Brass Coast.

Navarr.t: The Quiet Step joined the campaign to liberate Segura under Brennos Brackensong, while the Black Thorns marched north to Miaren.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn regained all of Segura and saw Anduz celebrate its liberation, but now face a Lasambrian invasion of Kahraman that threatens Gambit, its people and its precious mining caravans.

The Marches.t: Humans of the Mournwold, the Yegarra under Steven of Sarcombe, travelled south through Jotun lands to fight beside the Corazón and led the vanguard against Rojota.

All the way.o: In Spring 384YE the Lasambrian Jotun abandoned Segura after recovering ancestral relics from the Caida, letting Imperial armies liberate Anduz, then promptly invaded Kahraman through western Gambit alongside the Yegarra of the Mournwold.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: The Fort Braydon garrison rallied and made the long march south-west to engage the invaders, slowing their advance at the cost of exhaustion.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: The orcs and Yegarra overran western Gambit, offering loyalty or exile and looting Redhill Pastures, and threatened Rojota, whose fall would give them a beachhead; a conjunction offered a chance to intercept them.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: Corazón raids targeted the mithril caravans from the Great Mine of Briante, and losing Rojota would make such raids considerably easier.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: The Jotun bypassed Damata's hills this time, but Corazón raiders struck caravans carrying white granite from the Damatian Cliffs.

Segura/Anduzjasse.t: The Winter Sun advanced across the plains of Anduzjasse to find Anduz's gates open and its people cheering their liberation.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun forces in Bregasland are noted as having been on the defensive.

Kahraman.t: The Lasambrian Jotun invaded through Gambit, raiding caravans from the Damatian Cliffs and Great Mine of Briante; if they stay another season, white granite and mithril supplies will fall.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: a slow trickle of Freeborn exiles from Gambit flowed east through Rojota and down into Madruga.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns marched north to Miaren after the Winter Solstice.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Yegarra who joined the Lasambrian invasion of Kahraman come from the Mournwold.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian Jotun withdrew from Segura across the border into the hills of Reinos.

Segura.t: The Lasambrian occupation ended and the whole territory returned to Freeborn hands, though Anduz and its villages had been stripped of food and wine before the orcs left.

All the way to Anvil.d: Alexandre Sortilega di Apulian, who fronts the Company of the Venturesome Harrier's tours of the Black Plateau, came with a reckoner to confront the League assembly over its denunciation. Isaziah, a Highborn merrow, returned with an incense made from Tamarbodian mushrooms. The Sagrado sutannir offered up to 50 people a glimpse of a past life through true liao infused by Sung. A grieving Highborn pilgrim sought tombola participants. Rahuun Amahuz, a former Grendel magician now in Apulus, sought a 'friend of Melissa'. An Axou merchant sought discreet physicks for three patients. A herald of Tharim was to address the Navarr about the vallorn. Valja Nikodemin Kopec sought volunteers to cleanse Bulgakov, and Megan Brownblood came to question the vines.

Grendel.t: Rahuun Amahuz, a former Grendel orc magician, had defected with half the Black Sand Circle to the League, and boasted of ties to a Grendel Wind Lord he was careful not to contact for fear of treason accusations.

Highguard.t: Two Highborn visitors were expected: the merrow Isaziah, bringing a mushroom incense to test and sell, and the grieving grey pilgrim Tamar, who blamed the tombola's mountebanks for the loss of a brother.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: their egregore received no invitation to the Sagrado true liao offering, as Imperial Orcs cannot benefit from liao in any form.

Navarr.t: The Autocrator of the Sheathed Armoury was due at the Navarr camp to explain how Tharim, Surut or Skathe might aid the campaign against the vallorn, while Megan Brownblood came to demand the vines' answers on their oath.

The League.t: The League assembly faced an incensed Alexandre Sortilega di Apulian, who threatened a defamation suit over its denunciation of the Black Plateau tours, and Apulus had gained Rahuun Amahuz's Circle of Black Sand as a new guild.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the astronomancers of the Circle of Black Sand now rub shoulders with Urizen students of the stars, and Zenith's spires were once visited by Axou seeking medicine.

All the way to Anvil.o: Ahead of the Autumn Equinox 386YE, word spread of a number of visitors heading to Anvil, each with their own business: grievances, experiments, magical opportunities, offers from the realms and a plan to reclaim the ruined Vale of Bulgakov.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: Beoraidh is home to the Black Sand Circle half led by Mannun Amahuz, who took the coven's ritual library there.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Odd mushrooms harvested in Tamarbode underpin Isaziah's continuing experiments and the incense she planned to test and sell at Anvil.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Rahuun Amahuz had settled in Apulus, set up the Circle of Black Sand as a guild in the League city and styled himself its Merchant-Prince.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: Mentioned in passing: its learned halls were among the places Axou once visited for medicine, a practice not resumed since contact was restored.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Beoraidh half of the Black Sand Circle, under Mannun Amahuz, kept the coven's ritual library after the split.

Miaren.t: The Thrice-Cursed Court's message arrived through a straining winter regio near Seren, from which a vate returned bearing the Bound King's scroll.

Reikos.t: The peculiar mushrooms of Tamarbode were the source of Isaziah's distilled substance and her new incense, brought to Anvil for testing and sale.

Spiral.t: The Company of the Venturesome Harrier's walking tours across benighted Spiral and the Black Plateau, branded a scam by the League's priests, were at the centre of Alexandre's dispute.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the learned halls of Tassato Regario were once a destination for Axou seeking medical knowledge.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the high spires of Zenith were once visited by Axou seeking medical learning.

All the wind.d: Mistress Karadragha offered condolences for the Asavean raid on Meade but no reparations, and declined any joint resistance to Asavea or Imperial help against dissidents. Celestial Arch visitors found the Muhnkhabat hostile to the Jotun and respectful of Asavea, the Jokhi warning that Asavea was arming Faraden extremists, and the Altantsetseg fearing Faraden could be crushed between two empires. Caitun's trade shifted towards giant blood whelks, and yak goods were offered in place of weltsilver. The Holberg Chamber of Commerce was asked to vote on an enclave including a Hall of Five Flames in Holmauer. The Gloaming Road was abrogated, and Mina i Yashum i Riqueza later funded the Parador of Wind and Flame.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is named as one of the nations a Faraden caravan would trade with along the Blood Red Roads to Holberg.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Muhnkhabat treated Imperial Orc visitors with polite disdain until convinced they were nothing like the Jotun.

Jotun.t: The Muhnkhabat bear a particular dislike for the Jotun, especially the Lasambrians, and fear a Jotun turn against Faraden, while Asavea dangles support for reclaiming Menendram and Talemas. Lasambrian tolls on Faraden caravans also helped end the Gloaming Road.

The League.t: Building on a statement of principle from the League National Assembly, the Faraden sought a trading enclave in Holberg, with Holberg's Chamber of Commerce to choose whether it would focus on cloth, spice, iron or nothing at all.

The Marches.t: The Marcher ambassador Ebenezer received sympathy but no reparations for the Asavean attack on Meade, and was offered yak products from Caitun rather than live yaks for the Marches.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Blue Silk Scarf guild showed interest in meeting Varushkan artisans to discuss fabrics and trade.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark is named as a nation a Faraden caravan might trade with on its way along the Blood Red Roads.

All the wind.o: In Winter 386YE the Faraden ambassador rebuffed Imperial approaches over the Asavean attack on Meade, while Celestial Arch emissaries toured Faraden wizard families and found Asavean influence spreading. The Court of Five Winds also proposed a Faraden trading enclave in Holberg and a parador at the Azure Chorus.

Holberg/Holfried.t: Mentioned in passing: Holfried is not named; it is linked only through the wider proposal for a Faraden trading enclave in Holberg.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: The Faraden wanted land in the parkland of Holmauer for a caravan enclave that would include a Hall of Five Flames, a shrine with resident Faraden priests, which could prove a sticking point.

Holberg.t: The Faraden proposed a Firewind Market in the upper city and a caravan enclave in the lower city, with the Chamber of Commerce due to vote on which goods the market would focus on or whether to reject it.

Mitwold.t: Faraden offered only condolences for the Asavean warships' attack on Meade, launched from a Faraden port, and accepted no responsibility. No more mithril had yet reached the Alder of Meade after the Gloaming Road ended.

Sea of Snow.t: Giant blood whelks native to the Sea of Snow, potted along the Pelabuhan coast, were to be supplied in greater number to Imperial fleets at Caitun at the cost of some orichalcum.

Upwold.t: Mistress Karadragha warned against introducing yaks to Upwold, as they are suited to high altitudes, and the civil service confirmed that past attempts had all failed expensively.

All those moments.d: The Great Forest Orcs returned to the Heart of Peytaht and sheltered about a hundred survivors from Hope's Rest, but they now feel betrayed and their trust in the Navarr is fraying. The Karass, newly recognised as foreigners, settled old scores and now eye the Rahvin. The Rahvin, sustained by Imperial Orc supplies, expect destruction and secretly seek weapons through the Imperial Orcs. Black Wind prisoners revealed that their army of over four thousand under Alakath the Torn is marching to the Barrens under duress. Many Dawnish welcomed these events. In Sanath, Imperial curses weakened the Druj, who used the Vendarri's fate to rally their subjects. The clash between Synod and Military Council undermined faith in both.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish occupants of the Barrens were broadly pleased by the destruction of the Montanians and the Black Wind, and Dawnish settlement of Hope's Rest could bring chances to develop the area if the Dawnish Assembly encourages it.

Druj.t: Driven from the Barrens and battered by curses in Sanath, the Druj grew fearful but turned the Vendarri's fate into propaganda to recruit warriors, and they were deeply shaken to see the Empire adopt their own ruthless methods.

Grendel.t: The Druj pinned their hopes on the Grendel's war against the Empire, trusting that it would draw Imperial armies away and let them survive and later retake their lost lands.

Imperial Orcs.t: Their Assembly's gift of 75 thrones of supplies kept the Rahvin alive through winter and won their appreciation, and a secret Rahvin delegation is coming to Anvil to seek weapons from them, although arming declared barbarians would risk a charge of treason.

Navarr.t: The Great Forest Orcs, their closest orc allies, felt betrayed and confronted the Navarr who had accompanied them; it falls to the Navarr to rebuild that trust or watch the orcs leave Therunin and abandon trade in weirwood.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold Orcs were named in the Wintermark Assembly's statement as an example of non-Imperial peoples the Empire has long accepted.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan armies were at the heart of the bloodshed: the Northern Eagle slaughtered the Montanians and the Iron Helms executed the Black Wind's leaders, frightening the sept into compliance, which many Dawnish praised and which rattled the Druj.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark Assembly's statement urging the Empire to accept the Barrens peoples rather than put them to the sword was the only one of the Synod's statements of caution to pass with a greater majority, and it was overshadowed by the Military Council's actions.

All those moments.o: In Winter 385YE a dark wind swept the Barrens after the Druj were driven out: the Montanians were slaughtered by the Northern Eagle, the Black Wind's leaders were executed by the Iron Helms, and the Karass all but wiped out the Vendarri. The surviving orc factions were left in shock, the Druj spread the news to deepen fear of the Empire, and the Synod's authority suffered.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: The page places the Rahvin, still occupying the mithril mine on Bittershore, gathering mithril to arm themselves for a fight they expect to lose.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Sydathian Fens.t: Mentioned in passing: after the Summer Solstice the Valiant Pegasus had fought to secure a foothold in the Sydathian Fens.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: The Rahvin in Bitter Strand received the Imperial Orcs' food and supplies, which ensured they would survive the winter.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: The Great Forest Orcs reclaimed the Heart of Peytaht and its weirwood grove, sheltered survivors from Hope's Rest, and their elders weighed using the weirwood to fortify against the Dawnish.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: About a hundred survivors of the attack on Hope's Rest fled to the Heart of Peytaht, and the area offers development opportunities if the Dawnish Assembly encourages settlement there.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: The Dawnish occupants of Murderdale were broadly pleased by the destruction of the Montanians and the Black Wind.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the Valiant Pegasus withdrew from the Salt Flats to Astolat while Imperial magicians cursed Sanath.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs were recalled as having fought alongside the Navarr against the vallorn in Brocéliande.

Hercynia.t: Great Forest Orcs who were encouraged to settle in Hercynia now find their new steadings, and their Navarr friends, in the firing line if relations with the Empire collapse.

Miaren.t: Great Forest Orcs who were encouraged to settle in Miaren now find their new steadings, and their Navarr friends, in the firing line if relations with the Empire collapse.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold Orcs were cited in a Synod statement as a non-Imperial people the Empire had treated well.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish commentators pointed to Ossium as an earlier victory of the Dawn–Varushka alliance, and the Druj mourned it as ancestral land they had lost.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Imperial curses ravaged Sanath's settlements and herb fields, and the Druj gathered a major force there and spread tales of the Vendarri to recruit, making local orcs increasingly unwilling to speak with Imperials.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens was soaked in blood as the Montanians, the Black Wind leadership and the Vendarri were destroyed, while the Great Forest Orcs returned home and the Black Wind army marched back under Imperial threat.

Therunin.t: Great Forest Orcs in Therunin had begun to discuss asking to stay among the Navarr, but those talks faltered and they may leave unless the Navarr restore their trust.

All too well.d: None of the three follies that would reassure the septs (Ethengraw Armoury-Smithies, Illarawm Ossuary, Yerende Gardens) had been started. In Gildenheim, Stonecliff Brakkalo denounced the Empire's neglect and urged Imperial Orc armies to stay in Skarsind and raise the money themselves. The Imperial Orc assembly could silence her or endorse her with a Synod mandate; otherwise dissent would grow. The Illarawm offered to teach shaman a meditation that quiets intrusive ancestors. The Yerende offered orcsroot to the House of the Broken Shield in exchange for alpine cultivation lore. Inspired by Thanmir Hrafnar's statement, the Ethengraw approached Wintermark, offering to move to Hahnmark if forges were built, possibly alongside the planned runeforge.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are remembered as the cruel former masters of the Ossium septs, whose oppression shaped their traditions and fears.

Imperial Orcs.t: The nation faced growing dissent from Stonecliff Brakkalo, who urged its armies to withdraw to Skarsind, and its assembly could answer her by Synod mandate. It also had open offers from the Illarawm to help its shaman quiet troubled ancestors.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr stridings carried Great Forest Orcs through Skarsind, took a few Yerende away with them, and escorted Ethengraw emissaries through Hercynia.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Brakkalo complained of white granite going to Marcher canals, and the Mournwold was cited as a precedent for questions about orcs joining a nation.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs' earlier refusal to fight while the Empire was allied with slave-owning Otkodov inspired Brakkalo, and the Thule Dragons have since decreed an end to the practice.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Brakkalo complained that Ossium was freed and handed to the Varushkans, and a Varushkan trader told the Illarawm of Bloodcrow Udoo's efforts.

Wintermark.t: Moved by Thanmir Hrafnar's welcome to heroes of any origin, the Ethengraw asked the Winterfolk to build them forges, possibly adding 45 wains of mithril to the planned runeforge. In return they would come to work there and one day seek to join the nation.

All too well.o: A year after the Ossium septs settled in Skarsind, the Ethengraw, Illarawm and Yerende still stood apart from the Imperial Orcs. A fiery preacher, Stonecliff Brakkalo, urged the nation to withdraw from the Empire's wars, while each sept made its own overture.

Skarsind/Gildermark.t: Brakkalo preached in Gildenheim, where the Ethengraw are mostly settled and where their proposed Armoury-Smithies would be built.

Skarsind/Solvihill.t: The Yerende in Solvihill struggled with alpine soil and offered 8 doses of orcsroot to the House of the Broken Shield in exchange for lore on growing Cerulean Mazzarine.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: The Illarawm in Southpine, site of their proposed Ossuary, offered to teach visiting Imperial Orc shaman a meditation for quieting angry or fearful ancestors.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs suggested the Yerende might one day settle beneath the boughs of the Heart of Peytaht.

Hahnmark.t: Ethengraw emissaries led by Amadi Thunderstone came to Kalpaheim, and thousands of Ethengraw would move to Hahnmark if Wintermark built them forges.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ethengraw emissaries travelled through Hercynia with a Navarr striding on their way to Hahnmark.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: earlier questions about orcs joining a nation in the Mournwold, settled by a Senate appraisal, were cited as a precedent.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is the homeland the three septs left behind, freed from the Druj and now held by Varushka.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's alliance with slave-owning Otkodov prompted the Imperial Orc generals' earlier withdrawal, which inspired Brakkalo.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the new Hall of the Unbroken in Sermersuaq is named among the Empire's efforts to help new citizens.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind was home to the three unintegrated Ossium septs and to Brakkalo's preaching, which risked pulling the nation's armies home and stirring dissent if left unanswered.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs, a Barrens sept, appear to be distant kin of the Yerende.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs suggested the Yerende might be happier in Therunin, though the sept as a whole showed no wish to move again.

All work together.d: Nina's Summer 381YE judgement implied a mandate, but the civil service treated it as a statement of principle and sent it to every priest. Five mandates followed, each sending a priest with 100 liao to preach. Nina's and Bartimaeus's orthodox mandates would have strengthened the Highguard, Varushkan and League congregations at the expense of the Marches, Brass Coast and Wintermark. Bartimaeus's and Jorma Steelhail's also risked vigilante persecution of heretics, foreigners or the unvirtuous. Brother Orchard's would have reversed the orthodox balance. Several were upheld, but Severin's unity mandate won. It favoured no congregation and strongly inhibits attempts to stir religious conflict for a year.

Dawn.t: Past doubts about Dawn's orthodoxy were said to be somewhat eased by Viviane de Couerdefer's statement that glory lies through true Virtue. Dawn's congregations would not have been affected by any of the proposed mandates.

Highguard.t: Highguard was named among the most orthodox nations, and Bartimaeus of the Shattered Tower proposed the strident anti-heresy mandate. Because the unity mandate prevailed, Highborn congregations gained none of the liao or votes the orthodox mandates would have brought.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs were described as having found a place in the Way through the recent doctrinal changes of the Yaelian Schism. They would not have been affected by any of the mandates.

Navarr.t: The Navarr were described as accepting Virtue through their own Great Dance, a philosophy not greatly at odds with the Way. Their congregations were unaffected by the mandates.

The Marches.t: The Marches were named among the least orthodox nations, for beliefs such as rebirth as apple trees or rats and passing unvirtuous acts to others. Brother Orchard's heterodox mandate would have boosted Marcher congregations, but the unity mandate's success spared them both loss and gain.

Urizen.t: The Urizen were described as approaching Virtue through the Net of the Heavens, which is not particularly at odds with the Way. Their congregations were unaffected by the mandates.

Varushka.t: Varushka was counted among the most orthodox nations and would have gained congregation strength under the orthodox mandates, or lost it under Brother Orchard's. The unity mandate left its congregations unchanged.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's heroic veneration and swamp burials put it among the least orthodox nations, which the orthodox mandates would have weakened. Jorma Steelhail of Wintermark proposed the mandate to persecute the unvirtuous, but the unity mandate prevailed instead.

All work together.o: In Winter 381YE the Synod weighed rival mandates arising from Nina of Cantiarch's Hold's statement of principle urging the Empire to follow the Way more closely. Severin Teyhard von Holberg's mandate calling for unity around the seven Virtues passed by the largest margin.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the historical Abbot Robin of Upwold is cited for his rejected early-Empire claim that the Labyrinth of Ages was a metaphor for a soul's time as a tree.

Allocate Crawling Depths.d: The motion assigned the Crawling Depths, a mithril mine in Ossium, as an Imperial Bourse seat, and it passed. As a result the position is Imperial, and any Imperial citizen is eligible to hold the associated title. The page notes that this allocation is permanent: even once Ossium is conquered and assigned to an Imperial nation, the Crawling Depths will remain an Imperial position, and there will be no further opportunity to allocate it to that nation or any other.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj held Ossium when the Senate allocated the Crawling Depths there as an Imperial Bourse seat; they are not otherwise named.

Allocate Crawling Depths.o: In Autumn 382YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Tassato and seconded by Holberg, making the mithril mine known as the Crawling Depths in Ossium an Imperial Bourse seat.

Ossium.t: The mithril mine of the Crawling Depths in Ossium was made an Imperial Bourse seat, and it will stay Imperial even if Ossium is conquered and given to an Imperial nation.

Allocate Great Forest.d: Proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by the senator for Astolat on the virtue of Prosperity, the motion sought to make the Great Forest, a bourse seat in Reikos, a national position appointed by Highguard. The Senate rejected it. A later motion to allocate the Great Forest as an Imperial position was passed, so the seat was not reserved for Highguard.

Highguard.t: Highguard failed to secure the Great Forest as a national bourse position, and the seat instead became an Imperial position under a subsequent motion.

Allocate Great Forest.o: A Senate motion to allocate the Great Forest at Reikos bourse seat as a national bourse position for Highguard failed in Spring 380YE. A subsequent motion allocating it as an Imperial position passed instead.

Reikos.t: The Great Forest bourse seat in Reikos was not made a Highborn national position. It was allocated as an Imperial position by a later motion.

Allocate Great Forest II.d: Proposed by the senator for Bastion and seconded by Necropolis, the motion assigned the Great Forest of Peythat, the bourse seat in Reikos, as an Imperial Bourse Seat. It followed a previous motion to allocate the seat as a national position, which had failed. With this motion passed, the Great Forest became an Imperial seat and was due to be auctioned, for a reduced term, at the Summer Solstice 380YE.

Highguard.t: Highguard senators for Bastion and Necropolis proposed and seconded the motion, settling the bourse seat in Highguard-held Reikos as an Imperial position open to auction rather than a national one.

Allocate Great Forest II.o: The Senate passed a motion in Spring 380YE allocating the Great Forest bourse seat in Reikos as an Imperial position, following an earlier failed attempt to make it a national seat.

Reikos.t: The Great Forest bourse seat in Reikos became an Imperial position, due for auction for a reduced term at the Summer Solstice 380YE.

Allocate Great Pits of Ennerlund.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by the senator for Therunin, the motion passed. The Great Pits of Ennerlund, a mithril mine wrecked by the Druj, were under repair at the time. Repairs were expected to be finished after the Summer Solstice 380YE, with the first mithril reaching the holder of the seat at the Autumn Equinox 380YE. The bourse seat tied to the Pits was to be auctioned at that same Autumn Equinox 380YE, opening the restored mine's output to whoever won the position.

Druj.t: The Druj are named as having destroyed the Great Pits of Ennerlund, the damage that made the repairs and this allocation necessary.

The League.t: The League's Holberg senator proposed the motion, which secured the restored mithril mine in League-held Holberg as an Imperial bourse seat to be auctioned at the Autumn Equinox 380YE.

Allocate Great Pits of Ennerlund.o: The Senate passed a motion in Winter 379YE to allocate the Great Pits of Ennerlund in Holberg as an Imperial bourse position, while the mithril mine was still being repaired after its destruction by the Druj.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: Ennerlund is home to the Great Pits, which were being rebuilt after Druj destruction and were expected to yield their first mithril for the new bourse seat at the Autumn Equinox 380YE.

Holberg.t: Holberg's Great Pits of Ennerlund were set to become an Imperial bourse position once repairs to the mine were finished after the Summer Solstice 380YE.

Allocate Legacy.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Spiral and seconded by the senator for Sermersuaq. It allocated the Legacy bourse seat, located in the Ossuary region of Spiral, as a national bourse position. The motion passed. The Legacy therefore became a national position, due for its first appointment at the Autumn Equinox 380YE.

Grendel.t: With Grendel holding Spiral at the time, it was Spiral's senator who proposed making the Legacy a national bourse position, with appointment due at the Autumn Equinox 380YE.

Allocate Legacy.o: In Summer 380YE the Senate passed a motion allocating the Legacy, a bourse seat in Ossuary in Spiral, as a national position.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: The Legacy bourse seat in Ossuary was allocated as a national position and was due for appointment at the Autumn Equinox 380YE.

Spiral.t: Spiral's senator proposed the motion, which turned the Legacy, a bourse seat within the territory, into a national position.

Allocate The Brilliant Shore.d: The procedural motion proposed making the Brilliant Shore a National Bourse position assigned to Wintermark. It passed the Senate by 21 votes to 4 at the Autumn Equinox 377YE, but the General Assembly of the Imperial Synod vetoed it, leaving the resource unassigned. The Civil Service noted that naming Wintermark was legally extraneous, because a national Bourse position is only open to citizens of the nation that controls the territory. At the Winter Solstice the question was raised again and passed 21 to 3. The Brilliant Shore became a National Bourse position, and production stockpiled since Autumn 377YE was held for the first citizen elected to operate it.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule is not named on the page. It appears here only because Skarsind, where the Brilliant Shore lies, is recorded as held by Thule that season.

Wintermark.t: The Brilliant Shore's White Granite became a National Bourse position under Wintermark's control, open to election only by Wintermark citizens, though the Synod's veto delayed this by a season.

Allocate The Brilliant Shore.o: In Autumn 377YE the Senate voted 21 to 4 to make the Brilliant Shore, a White Granite source in Skarsind, a National Bourse position for Wintermark, but the Imperial Synod vetoed the motion. The question was raised again automatically at the Winter Solstice 377YE, passed, and the Brilliant Shore became a National Bourse position.

Skarsind.t: The Brilliant Shore White Granite source in Skarsind stood unassigned after the Autumn veto and became a National Bourse position at Winter, with its Autumn production stockpiled for its first elected operator.

Allocate the Great Mine of Briante.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Kahraman and seconded by the senator for Feroz. It allocated the Great Mine of Briante, a bourse seat located in Kahraman, as an Imperial position, and the Senate passed it. As a result, the Great Mine of Briante remained Imperial and was due to be auctioned for a reduced term at the Winter Solstice 380YE.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast senators for Kahraman and Feroz proposed and seconded the motion, which kept a bourse seat on Brass Coast land under Imperial control, to be auctioned rather than appointed by the nation.

Allocate the Great Mine of Briante.o: In Autumn 380YE the Senate passed a motion to allocate the Great Mine of Briante, a bourse seat in Kahraman, as an Imperial Bourse position.

Kahraman.t: The Great Mine of Briante in Kahraman remained an Imperial Bourse position, to be auctioned for a reduced term at the Winter Solstice 380YE.

Allocate the Pride of Ikka's Tears.d: The motion allocated the mithril mine that had been under construction in Sermersuaq since Winter 379YE, naming it the Pride of Ikka's Tears and making it a national position. It passed in Autumn 380YE. The seat became a national Bourse position of Wintermark, allocated by secret vote of Wintermark's military captains. Unlike the Stonefield Ice Caves, the actions a military unit has been engaging in have no bearing on the vote. The first election was set for the Winter Solstice 380YE; after that the seat is elected each Autumn, like all other mithril seats.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gained a new national Bourse seat controlling a mithril mine, to be awarded by secret ballot of its military captains, first at the Winter Solstice 380YE and then each Autumn.
