Allocate the Pride of Ikka's Tears.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by Madruga and seconded by Bastion, allocating the new mithril mine in Sermersuaq as a Wintermark national Bourse position named the Pride of Ikka's Tears.

Sermersuaq.t: The mithril mine built in Sermersuaq since Winter 379YE was formally allocated as the Pride of Ikka's Tears, a Wintermark national Bourse position.

Allocate the Singing Caves.d: The Singing Caves in the Mournwold had recently been liberated by the heroes of the Empire, and this Autumn 380YE motion sought to make them a national position. The Marches and the League were the nations proposed, and the record states the position was assigned to the Marches. The motion was subject to the veto of the Throne. The constitutional note is written conditionally, recording that had the motion passed, the national status of the associated Bourse seat would have followed the Mournwold to whichever nation the territory was eventually assigned. This suggests the allocation may not have taken final effect.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, but they held the Mournwold at the time the Imperial Senate debated the newly liberated caves.

The League.t: The League was one of the two nations proposed to receive the Singing Caves, but the record names the Marches as the nation it was assigned to.

The Marches.t: The Marches, whose senator for Mitwold proposed the motion, were recorded as the nation assigned the Singing Caves, subject to the Throne's veto.

Allocate the Singing Caves.o: The Senate considered a motion, proposed by the senator for Mitwold and seconded by Hahnmark, to allocate the recently liberated Singing Caves in the Mournwold as a national position, with the Marches and the League put forward as candidates.

Mournwold.t: The Singing Caves within the Mournwold, recently liberated by Imperial heroes, were the subject of the allocation, even though the territory itself was held by the Jotun at the time.

Allocate the Singing Caves II.d: After the Empire recovered the Singing Caves in Mournwold, an earlier motion to allocate them fell to the veto of Empress Lisabetta. This second motion, proposed by the senator for Upwold and seconded by the senator for Mitwold, was raised in Winter 380YE and passed as an Imperial motion. As a result, the Singing Caves became an Imperial bourse position, and the seat was auctioned at the Winter Solstice 380YE for a reduced term.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named on the page; they are linked only because they held Mournwold, where the caves lie, that season.

Allocate the Singing Caves II.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by Upwold and seconded by Mitwold, allocating the Singing Caves in Mournwold, which the Empire had recovered, as an Imperial bourse position.

Mournwold.t: The Singing Caves in Mournwold, recovered by the Empire, became an Imperial bourse position and were auctioned for a reduced term at the Winter Solstice 380YE.

Allocate the Singing Caves III.d: The Singing Caves, a Bourse seat in Mournwold, had been recovered by the Empire, and Senator Holberg proposed a motion to allocate it, seconded by the senator for Bregasland. During the Senate's discussion a motion of curtailment was passed, but The Throne vetoed it. Senator Holberg then withdrew the motion. As a result the Singing Caves were not allocated that season and the seat remained vacant.

The Marches.t: Senators for two Marcher territories, Holberg and Bregasland, proposed and seconded the motion to allocate a Bourse seat in Marcher-held Mournwold, but Holberg's withdrawal left it unallocated.

Allocate the Singing Caves III.o: In Autumn 381YE Holberg proposed, with Bregasland seconding, a Senate motion to allocate the Bourse seat for the Singing Caves in Mournwold, recently recovered by the Empire. The motion was withdrawn and the seat was left unallocated.

Mournwold.t: The Singing Caves in Mournwold had been recovered by the Empire, but their Bourse seat went unallocated this season after the motion was withdrawn.

Allocate the Singing Caves Spring 382YE.d: In Spring 382YE the Senate considered a motion to allocate the Singing Caves, a mithril mine in the Mournwold. The senator for Bregasland proposed it and the senator for Astolat seconded it. The motion passed, making the Singing Caves a Marcher national Bourse position rather than one open to the whole Empire. The position was to be filled at the Summer Solstice by Marcher citizens who own farms.

The Marches.t: The Singing Caves became a Marcher national position, to be appointed by Marcher farm-owners at the Summer Solstice, putting control of a mithril mine in Marcher hands.

Allocate the Singing Caves Spring 382YE.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by Bregasland and seconded by Astolat, to allocate the Singing Caves mithril mine in the Mournwold as a national Bourse position.

Mournwold.t: The Singing Caves mithril mine in the Mournwold was formally allocated as a national Bourse position, to be filled at the Summer Solstice.

Allocate the Vigilant Swan.d: The Vigilant Swan in Reikos had recently been liberated by Imperial troops. A motion proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by the senator for Casinea sought to allocate the bourse seat. Highguard and the Imperial Orcs were both proposed, and the Senate passed it as a national position assigned to the Imperial Orcs. The General Assembly of the Imperial Synod then vetoed the motion, so it could not be raised again that summit. The Swan remained unassigned, with production from Spring 379YE stockpiled for the first Imperial citizen elected to operate it. Had the motion stood, the seat's national status would have followed whichever nation Reikos was eventually assigned to.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, though the Vigilant Swan is described as recently liberated by Imperial troops in Reikos, a territory they held.

Highguard.t: Highguard was proposed as a nation to receive the Vigilant Swan, and the motion was put forward by the senators for Necropolis and Casinea, but the seat was assigned to the Imperial Orcs before the Synod's veto overturned it.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Senate assigned the Vigilant Swan to the Imperial Orcs as a national position, but the Synod's veto denied them the seat, leaving it unassigned.

Allocate the Vigilant Swan.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate passed a motion to assign the newly liberated Vigilant Swan bourse seat in Reikos as a national position for the Imperial Orcs, but the General Assembly of the Synod vetoed it.

Reikos.t: The Vigilant Swan bourse seat in Reikos, recently liberated by Imperial troops, was left unassigned after the veto, with its output stockpiled for its first elected holder.

Alongside the Earthquake Drummers.d: At the invitation of the dragon Tathenon the Gyre, Imperial captains mustered in the southern Webwood with the Earthquake Drummers under Saemundr Elvirsbairn and four other Thule armies. The drummers' loud advance drew the Druj to battle in the haunted, miasma-shrouded woods of Oerwealt, where the Thule and over two thousand Imperial troops defeated a Druj ambush of perhaps ten thousand. The Thule then turned toward the Great Pit in the Bonewall but were slowed in the hills. The Jaws of Winter Lightning laid a sickness curse across Ulnak and awakened Oerwealt's trees. Imperial units were paid in crystal mana, and the same pay of seven crystal mana per unit was offered for further service.

Druj.t: The Druj lost Oerwealt and most of the Bonewall, and their garrisons at Cassad Ûln and the Thistle of Barbs took heavy losses, though both bastions remain untouched. Unless their armies respond, the Great Pit is expected to fall by the Summer Solstice.

Thule.t: Otkodov's armies, guided by the Dragons, claimed Oerwealt and are poised to besiege the Great Pit. The Eyes of the Dragon, who serve Hinodir of the Bright Orb, were seen searching the forest for something unknown.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is not named; it is linked only through Ossium, where the Thule armies mustered.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule recalled their role in liberating Sermersuaq, and the Banner of the Rime Hound's war rhinos were remembered from the Battle of Ikka's Tears.

Alongside the Earthquake Drummers.o: In Spring 388YE Imperial warbands fighting as mercenaries alongside the Thule army the Earthquake Drummers helped Otkodov's forces conquer Oerwealt in the Druj-held Forest of Ulnak and push three-quarters of the way through the Bonewall. The Great Pit remained untaken.

Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest.t: Mentioned in passing: Ghul'thak Forest is not named; the campaign concentrated on Oerwealt and the Bonewall.

Forest of Ulnak/Oerwealt.t: The Thule conquered Oerwealt's haunted woods after defeating a large Druj ambush. Spring magic awakened its trees to protect the Thule and harry any Druj attempt to retake it.

Forest of Ulnak/The Bonewall.t: The Thule took about three-quarters of the Bonewall but were slowed by Druj fighters using caves and tunnels. They are ready to besiege the Great Pit, which scouts expect to fall by the Summer Solstice unless the Druj respond.

Ossium/Webwood.t: The armies mustered in the southern Webwood, where Thule warlocks have woven a Spring ward that makes the trees attack intruders. Many old Druj traps and deadfalls remain uncleared in its deeper parts.

Forest of Ulnak.t: The Thule conquered Oerwealt and pushed deep into the Bonewall. Ritual magic now curses the coming season with a sickness that will raise casualties among armies and garrisons fighting there.

Ossium.t: Ossium served as the mustering ground for the invasion. The Thule noted that they had sent warriors to help conquer it and had hoped the Empire would return the favour.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the invading Thule are identified as the orcs and armies of Otkodov, whose astronomancers name the Wanderer "the Eye of Chaos".

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the main Druj armies were concentrated to the south in the Salt Flats and Sarangrave rather than in Ulnak.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule pointed to their part in Sermersuaq's liberation as a reason the Empire might aid them.

Verthandi.t: Mentioned in passing: Verthandi is not named on the page; it is linked only as Thule-held land.

Alter the works of Almodin Oktístis.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Redoubt, the motion targeted the Pallas Docks and Runeforge in Redoubt, Lorenzo's Great Game and Lorenzo's Legacy of Loyalty in Temeschwar, Lorenzo's Legacy of Ambition in Tassato and Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance in Hahnmark. Its text gave a cost of six Senate commissions and either 92 thrones 4 crowns or 185 thrones, depending on Synod decisions. Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar provided the 92 thrones and 4 crowns after the Spring Equinox. The Great Game, the three Legacies, the Pallas Docks and the Spiral Sword were all to have their heretical elements removed. This worked alongside Synod Mandate 14: Synod-inspired mobs tore out the idolatrous statues and decorations as a message to the Asaveans, then Senate-employed craftspeople repaired the damage.

Grendel.t: The Spiral Sword was listed among the Oktístis works that would have their heretical elements removed.

The League.t: The League drove the motion: Temeschwar's senator proposed it, Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar paid the full cost, and three League works were cleansed of heretical elements.

Urizen.t: Redoubt's senator seconded the motion, and the Urizen works at Redoubt, including the Pallas Docks, were to be stripped of their heretical elements.

Wintermark.t: Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance, standing in Wintermark's Hahnmark, was among the works to have its heretical elements removed.

Alter the works of Almodin Oktístis.o: The Senate passed a motion in Spring 383YE to remove the heretical elements from several Imperial works built by the Asavean architect Almodin Oktístis, at a cost of 92 thrones and 4 crowns.

Hahnmark.t: Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance in Hahnmark was to have its heretical elements removed.

Redoubt.t: The motion named the Pallas Docks and the Runeforge in Redoubt, and the outcome confirmed that the Pallas Docks would lose their heretical elements.

Spiral.t: The Spiral Sword appears in the outcome among the works whose heretical elements would be removed.

Tassato.t: Lorenzo's Legacy of Ambition in Tassato was to have its heretical elements removed.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar's senator proposed the motion, a Temeschwar noble funded it, and Lorenzo's Great Game and Legacy of Loyalty there were to be cleansed of their heretical elements.

Ambassadors of death.d: Kaela offered to discuss patronage of a new Navarr army against the vallorn, but declared the Clarion Call of Ivory and Dust void because the Synod had proscribed joining her Grim Legion. Prospero called in a favour from the Imperial ambassadors and offered Dawn a hearing on founding a magical college. Meraud would meet Ser Drayvana and the Golden Chalice, allowing From the Mouths of Babes one final, altered casting. Roshanwe proposed a chosen title, Beachcomber, a Necropolis edifice and a prismatic ink commission at Starstep. Irra Harah reported aiding the Nesustak rebels, condemned Imperial policy in Sarangrave, and offered a Woodward boon through Forge the Wooden Fastness.

Dawn.t: Prospero offered Earl Galahad Du Besté and up to four Dawnish enchanters a parley on creating a college of magic in Dawn, and Dawnish citizens were expected at Meraud's meeting during the Arcane Colloquium.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Nesustak rebels are described as having thrown off the Druj yoke, and Irra Harah offered to protect the folk of the Barrens from war with the Mallum.

Highguard.t: Roshanwe proposed that the Senate build the House on the Shore, apartments for her proposed Beachcomber, at Sanctuary Sands in the Highborn territory of Necropolis, near the proposed Grand Lodge of the Sevenfold Path.

Navarr.t: Kaela invited the Archmage of Winter to parley alongside the General of the Black Thorns, the Senator of Miaren and up to three other Navarr about her patronage of a new Navarr army against the vallorn, with the Grim Legion fighting at its side.

The League.t: League citizens were among those expected at Meraud's informal meeting during the Arcane Colloquium on Saturday.

The Marches.t: Irra Harah offered to help protect Marcher orcs and yeofolk from the Synod if Alderly or Tower March gained the Woodward quality, but warned that the assurance on Forge the Wooden Fastness, tied to the Hare Stone, is deliberately fragile after the destruction of the Protectors Stone he gave the landskeepers.

Urizen.t: Irra Harah condemned the Empire for giving Sarangrave to Urizen rather than its inhabitants, while Roshanwe proposed a prismatic ink commission at Starstep in the Urizen-held territory of Morrow.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Irra Harah's herald delivered the message by sitting beside Jorgen of Wintermark at an Anvil food vendor.

Ambassadors of death.o: In Summer 388YE five eternals answered the plenipotentiary messages of the Imperial archmages, while no Night parley took place because Archmage Bella Vicente d'Apulian resigned amid treason rumours without sending one. Kaela, Prospero, Meraud, Roshanwe and Irra Harah each set out terms, offers or grievances.

Morrow/Operus.t: Starstep in Operus was proposed by Roshanwe as the site of a prismatic ink commission, earlier plans having been ruined by damage from the Scions' invasion.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Casting Forge the Wooden Fastness with eight rings of ilium on Alderly would grant the Woodward quality, empowering future wards and bringing Irra Harah's aid to Marchers fearing oppression.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: Irra Harah's heralds held the wards against the Doom of Terunael in Nesustak Forest, aiding the rebels and Imperial soldiers, though the eternal remains distrustful of Imperial intentions there.

The Barrens/Farweald.t: Farweald was named as a forest where the Woodward quality would see Irra Harah protect the folk of the Barrens from war and the vallorn.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: The Bleaks were named as a forest where the Woodward quality would bring Irra Harah's protection to the human and orc folk of the Barrens.

Upwold/Tower March.t: If Tower March gained the Woodward quality, Irra Harah would be ready to help defend the Marcher orcs and yeofolk of Upwold against the Synod should it become necessary.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is not named directly; the nearest link is the Dawnish involvement and Irra Harah's offer of the Woodward boon for forests near the Barrens.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Richard of Holberg had earlier suggested Starstep as a site for a similar construction.

Miaren.t: Kaela understands that a new Navarr army will be raised in Miaren and invited its senator to her parley on patronage of that army and ending the vallorn.

Morrow.t: Roshanwe offered to draw up a proposal for a prismatic ink commission at Starstep in Morrow, its scale to be guided by a Conclave declaration of acceptance.

Mournwold.t: If Alderly gained the Woodward quality, Irra Harah would be ready to help protect the Marcher orcs and yeofolk of Mournwold from murder at the hands of the Synod.

Necropolis.t: Roshanwe proposed the House on the Shore at Sanctuary Sands, a regio near an abandoned fishing village, giving the Beachcomber three prismatic ink a season if the Conclave approves the title.

Sarangrave.t: Irra Harah's heralds had helped the Nesustak rebels and Imperial soldiers survive the vallorn, and the eternal demanded the Empire return Sarangrave to its native people rather than giving it to Urizen or the Victorious Axis.

The Barrens.t: Irra Harah recalled past Imperial 'liberation' of the Barrens ending in bloodshed, and offered to protect its human and orc folk from war and the vallorn if Farweald or The Bleaks gained the Woodward quality.

Amend Memorial Gardens of Treji.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Skarsind, the motion amended the Keeper of the Memorial Gardens of Treji so that it became an Imperial Orc national title, appointed by the Imperial Orc senators and revocable by the Imperial Orc national assembly. The motion's text framed it as a gesture of friendship, honouring those who fell in the costly liberation of Hercynia. The motion passed, though its outcome remained pending scrutiny. The incumbent was likely to keep the title until they died, stepped down or were revoked. The motion is only constitutional if the title is now revocable by the Imperial Orc national assembly rather than the Navarr one.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs gained the Keeper of the Memorial Gardens of Treji as a national title, to be appointed by their senators and revocable by their national assembly, in recognition of their part in liberating Hercynia.

Navarr.t: Navarr gave up the Keeper of the Memorial Gardens of Treji as a national title, with its Hercynia senator proposing the transfer to the Imperial Orcs as a gesture of friendship.

Amend Memorial Gardens of Treji.o: The Senate passed a motion in Summer 382YE transferring the Keeper of the Memorial Gardens of Treji from a Navarr national title to an Imperial Orc national title, as a gesture of friendship after the two peoples jointly liberated Hercynia.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia's senator proposed the motion, which honours the costly joint Navarr and Imperial Orc liberation of the territory by placing the Memorial Gardens of Treji title in orc hands.

Amend Spires of Dusk.d: Proposed by the senator for the Barrens and seconded by Redoubt, the motion amended the Spires of Dusk as described in the Three Keys Wind of Fortune. No commission was needed, because Mortarion Carver, Castellan of Spiral Castle, paid for it himself. The work cost 50 thrones and 10 wains of white granite, which he provided after the Spring Equinox, and took three months. Once it was finished, the Spires of Dusk, also called Houndsgate, had been remade. The last traces of Druj power were gone, replaced by an imposing symbol of Imperial rule. It signals to the Empire and to every sept in the Barrens that the territory is Dawnish, now and in the future.

Dawn.t: The remodelled Houndsgate honours the sacrifice of the Hounds of Glory and proclaims to the Empire and the Barrens septs that the territory is Dawnish, now and for the future.

Druj.t: The last traces of Druj power were removed from the Spires of Dusk and replaced with a symbol of Imperial rule.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the work was paid for by Mortarion Carver, who holds the title Castellan of Spiral Castle.

Amend Spires of Dusk.o: In Spring 386YE the Senate passed a motion to remodel the Spires of Dusk, a fortification in the Barrens, stripping away its Druj elements and making it a monument to the sacrifice of the Hounds of Glory.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the work was funded by Mortarion Carver, Castellan of Spiral Castle.

The Barrens.t: The territory's fortification, the Spires of Dusk, was rebuilt over three months as Houndsgate, a monument to the Hounds of Glory and a clear statement of Dawnish rule over the Barrens.

Amend Virtue's Respite.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Tassato, the motion amended an existing sinecure in Hanuri at a cost of 30 crowns in labour and three months of work. The title, appointed annually by the League National Assembly and providing four liao and seven crowns each season, was renamed from Guardian of Giselle's Tomb to the Bloody Custodian of Pride. Funds came from several citizens, chiefly Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar, who gave 2 thrones 6 crowns. On completion, citizens of Temeschwar with congregations could take the Preach Pride - Pride of Temeschwar lecture until the Winter Solstice 388YE. It produces no liao but grants two extra Synod votes.

The League.t: The League National Assembly gained an annually appointed title, the Bloody Custodian of Pride, worth four liao and seven crowns a season. League citizens of Temeschwar paid for most of the work.

Amend Virtue's Respite.o: In Spring 388YE the Senate passed a motion to amend Virtue's Respite in Hanuri, Temeschwar, into the "Bloody Massive Pride of Temeschwar", an opportunity arising from The concisest tenant Wind of Fortune. Once complete, its title was renamed the Bloody Custodian of Pride.

Temeschwar/Hanuri.t: Virtue's Respite in Hanuri was reworked into the Bloody Massive Pride of Temeschwar, and its guardian's title was renamed the Bloody Custodian of Pride.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar's senator proposed the amendment to the city's monument. Its citizens with congregations could then preach the Pride of Temeschwar lecture for two extra Synod votes until the Winter Solstice 388YE.

Amend conditions of Brock's Buffet.d: Brock's Toll, a National Bourse position (a sinecure) in Miaren, is held by whoever wins Brock's Buffet, an annual competition of arms between yeomen of Dawn and the Marches. The senator for Miaren proposed changing the conditions so that the Navarr could field contestants and potentially win custodianship of the toll bridge themselves. The motion was seconded by the senator for Therunin. It was put to the Senate at the Spring Equinox 378YE and was defeated in principle by 6 votes to 22, leaving the contest open only to Dawnish and Marcher yeomen.

Dawn.t: Dawnish yeomen kept their place as one of only two contenders for Brock's Toll, with no new Navarr rivals admitted to the contest.

Navarr.t: The Navarr attempt, led by the senators for Miaren and Therunin, to win a place in Brock's Buffet and a chance at the toll bridge in their own territory was defeated.

Amend conditions of Brock's Buffet.o: In Spring 378YE the Senate rejected a motion to let the Navarr compete in Brock's Buffet, the annual contest of arms between Dawnish and Marcher yeomen that decides custodianship of Brock's Toll in Miaren.

Miaren.t: Although Brock's Toll lies in Navarr-held Miaren, the failed motion meant its custodianship would still be decided solely between Dawnish and Marcher yeomen.

Amend motion to construct runeforge in R.d: Kahraman proposed, and Necropolis seconded, an amendment to the existing motion to construct a runeforge in the Urizen territory of Redoubt. The amendment directed that the work make use of the Asavean architect. The recorded outcome is that the architect's services were engaged for building the runeforge. The page gives no further details of cost, timescale or the runeforge's completion.

Urizen.t: Urizen's planned runeforge in its own territory of Redoubt was to be built with the Asavean architect's help, with the amendment proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Necropolis.

Amend motion to construct runeforge in R.o: In Spring 381YE the Senate amended its earlier motion to build a runeforge in Redoubt so that the construction would use the services of the Asavean architect.

Redoubt.t: The runeforge to be constructed in Redoubt had the Asavean architect engaged for its construction.

Amend motion to fortify Karsk.d: Proposed by Therunin and seconded by Reikos, the motion amended the previously agreed plan to construct a fortification in the Lestasny region of Karsk. The amendment directed that the services of the Asavean architect be used for the work. The motion passed, and as a result the Asavean architect was engaged to carry out the construction of the fortification.

Varushka.t: The fortification planned for Varushka's territory of Karsk will be built using the Asavean architect, an outside expertise engaged on the Varushkans' behalf by the Senate.

Amend motion to fortify Karsk.o: In Spring 381YE the Senate passed an amendment to its earlier motion to build a fortification in Lestasny, Karsk, so that the work would use the Asavean architect.

Karsk/Lestasny.t: Lestasny is the site of the fortification, and its construction is now to be carried out under the Asavean architect.

Karsk.t: The planned fortification in Karsk will now be built with the services of the Asavean architect, who has been engaged for the work.

Amend powers of Dredgemaster of Feverwat.d: Proposed by Miaren and seconded by Hercynia, the motion amended the powers of the Dredgemaster of Feverwater, the sinecure dedicated to dredging lake Feverwater in Therunin. The Senate set no upper limit on improving the sinecure. The Dredgemaster may announce one historical research request each season to the Civil Service, which presents it to the Senate without a vote, though the Synod may veto it. The Empire's overall seasonal limit on historical research still applies. Because similar titles are appointed annually, the Constitutional Court recommended the title's tenure become annual. This power was later removed by the Senate at the Winter Solstice 381YE.

Navarr.t: The improved sinecure is based in Navarri-held Therunin, and its holder gained the power to direct a share of the Empire's historical research each season, until the Senate removed that power in Winter 381YE.

Amend powers of Dredgemaster of Feverwat.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate passed a motion improving the Feverwater Lake sinecure and granting the Dredgemaster of Feverwater the power to commission one piece of historical research each season.

Therunin.t: The sinecure dredging lake Feverwater in Therunin was to be improved, and the Dredgemaster overseeing it gained the power to commission one piece of historical research each season.

Amend the use of the Gardens of High Cha.d: Passed in Autumn 381YE, the motion took up an opportunity to use the Gardens of High Chalcis great work in Reikos to support the Great Forest orcs then resident in Therunin. As a result, the herb garden owners of Reikos receive no benefit from the Gardens for the following year, until after the Autumn Equinox 382YE. The Great Forest orcs instead receive a generous supply of herbs. This exceptional act of generosity creates an unrivalled opportunity for a closer relationship between the people of Reikos and the orcs of the Great Forest.

Highguard.t: Highborn herb garden owners in Reikos give up the Gardens' benefit for a year, but in return gain an unrivalled chance to build closer ties with the Great Forest orcs.

Navarr.t: The Great Forest orcs living in Navarri-held Therunin receive a generous supply of herbs.

Amend the use of the Gardens of High Cha.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by Necropolis, to redirect the herbs produced by the Gardens of High Chalcis to the orcs of the Great Forest living in Therunin.

Reikos.t: The Gardens of High Chalcis in Reikos stop benefiting local herb garden owners until after the Autumn Equinox 382YE, with their bounty sent to the Great Forest orcs instead.

Therunin.t: The Great Forest orcs resident in Therunin receive a generous supply of herbs from the Gardens of High Chalcis.

Amend the use of the Imperial breadbaske.d: The motion changed the entire function of the Imperial Breadbasket great work to providing food for the people of the Mournwold. While it stands, the work provides no funds to farmers in the Marches, and its granaries no longer reduce the effects of natural decay on the armies of a single nation. The change took three months to take effect. If the motion is abrogated, the money for Marcher farms would be restored immediately, but restoring the protection against natural decay for a nation's armies would take a further three months, during which all armies would suffer the full effect of decay.

Jotun.t: The Jotun-held Mournwold became the beneficiary of the Imperial Breadbasket, which would now supply food to the people living under Jotun rule there.

Amend the use of the Imperial breadbaske.o: In Summer 381YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Bregasland and seconded by Skarsind, repurposing the Imperial Breadbasket to supply free food to the people of the Mournwold who were not in an army.

Mournwold.t: The Imperial Breadbasket was redirected to provide free food to the people of the Mournwold who were not in an army, at a time when the territory was held by the Jotun.

Amend the use of the Imperial breadbaske.d: Proposed by the senator for Bregasland and seconded by Skarsind in Autumn 381YE, this motion sought a further amendment to the use of the Imperial Breadbasket. Had it passed, the benefits of the breadbasket would have spread to the Mournwold and grown more effective. The cost would have been the permanent loss of the breadbasket's ability to support additional Imperial armies. The Senate did not pass the motion, so the Imperial Breadbasket remained unchanged.

The Marches.t: A Marcher senator from Bregasland put forward the attempt to bring the Mournwold under the Imperial Breadbasket's benefits, but the Marches gained nothing from it because the motion failed.

Amend the use of the Imperial breadbaske.o: A Senate motion proposed by Bregasland and seconded by Skarsind sought to permanently change the Imperial Breadbasket to include the Mournwold. The motion failed.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold, then held by the Marches, would have been permanently added to the Imperial Breadbasket's reach. The motion's failure left it outside the breadbasket's benefits.

An affirming flame.d: Urizen's national assembly thanked the generals of the League, Highguard and Varushka. Narses, a refugee from Zenith, worked with Zakalwe to propose a library in Tassato Regario, or a larger Barossa School of Imperial Strategy, to house Zakalwe's quill. Either commission would need a Senate motion and would supply Prismatic Ink to one or both League generals. Furia Severia called in Adamant's favour so that koboldi would carve three giant Highborn soldiers from the Three Sorrows near the Weave, and this was done. Aurum consecrated the shrine with true liao. Varushka received no thanks because the Iron Helms had awakened the Black Plateau. A second statement explained that orcs could join Urizen only as an entire like-minded population.

Druj.t: The Druj had taken Zenith, spread a miasma there and invaded Morrow before being driven from the Caeli hills, and Menos holds that they could never be bonded to the Urizen nation.

Grendel.t: The Black Plateau killed Grendel soldiers on a horrifying scale and broke their armies in Spiral, though they are expected to rebuild. The blight may deter them from invading again, and they could never be bonded to Urizen.

Highguard.t: Highguard's three armies were honoured for three seasons of costly rearguard fighting in Zenith that let countless Urizeni escape. The Three Watchers now stand in their memory and are expected to draw Highborn pilgrims.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs were cited as proof that orcs can choose a different path, having been taught to read by Urizeni teachers. Their own gregarious, martial culture means they are not seen as suitable candidates to join Urizen.

The League.t: The League generals Natalia and Gabriel Barossa were praised for helping turn back the Druj in Morrow. A proposed library or school in Tassato Regario would reward them with Prismatic Ink if the Senate commissioned it.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the slaughter caused by the Black Plateau was compared, uneasily, with what happened in the Mournwold.

Urizen.t: The Urizeni honoured their allies with a monument to the Highborn and a proposed gift for the League generals, but remained divided over Varushka's role. They also learned that orcs could join the nation only as a whole like-minded population.

Varushka.t: The Northern Eagle was credited for its role in Morrow, but the Iron Helms' awakening of the Black Plateau killed thousands of Imperial soldiers and Urizeni and left Spiral blighted. As a result, Urizen would not unite in thanking Varushka.

An affirming flame.o: Urizen took stock of the foreign help it had received against the Druj and Grendel, and was offered ways to thank the League generals and the Highborn armies. Furia Severia's Three Watchers, colossal statues of Highborn soldiers, were created by ritual and consecrated with true liao.

Morrow/Caeli.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were driven out of the Caeli hills during the Winter Solstice.

Morrow/Operus.t: Furia Severia's spire, the Weave, is in Operus, and her koboldi carved the Three Watchers into the Three Sorrows nearby. The shrine at the base of the central statue was consecrated with true liao.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: Tassato Regario was proposed as the home of a library or school, built with Zakalwe's quill, that would provide Prismatic Ink to the League generals.

Zenith/Occursion.t: The Spire of the Silver Chimera, a school of military study guarding a high pass in Occursion, burned when the Druj captured the region. Narses saved Zakalwe's quill from it.

Morrow.t: Morrow was saved from collapse when League, Varushkan and Urizen forces drove the Druj back. The Three Watchers were carved near the Weave, overlooking a pass to Zenith.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: its suffering was compared with the slaughter caused by the Black Plateau, though its people reacted differently.

Spiral.t: Spiral remains blighted by the awakened Black Plateau and may not recover for decades. The Block keeps its connected spires habitable, but those outside them suffer, and some blame Varushka.

Tassato.t: Tassato was proposed as the site of a Library or School of Imperial Strategy honouring the League generals, subject to a Senate motion.

Zenith.t: Zenith, lost to the Druj, suffers under their miasma. Highborn armies were overwhelmed there while covering the flight of Urizeni citizens.

An angry blade.d: The motion, proposed by Miaren and seconded by The Barrens, followed the attack on Madruga. Graciana, a former corsair, found that only a new Imperial navy would let fleets fight the Grendel's four known navies directly. She proposed a shipyard at Elos, new cranes at Cargo and docks at Nostos; if all three were built, Urizen could support a navy alongside the Citadel Guard. She also proposed the Free Docks, a fortification in Free Landing that fleets could support. Smugglers coves, spy networks for fleets, became a standard commission. Finally, the Red Wind Corsairs could be upgraded to the Forayer quality, letting them switch between army and navy. The Elos and Free Docks opportunities have since expired.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the senators for Miaren and The Barrens proposed and seconded the motion that ordered the appraisal.

Grendel.t: The appraisal was aimed squarely at the Grendel and their four known navies. Graciana judged it debatable whether the Empire could ever fully defeat them without a substantial navy of its own.

The Brass Coast.t: Graciana warned that any navy raised on the Coast would be dangerously exposed after the Grendel burned and then captured the Atalaya shipyards. She proposed fortified Free Docks to protect Madruga and an upgrade letting the Red Wind Corsairs put to sea as a navy.

Urizen.t: Urizen was offered the chance to commission its own navy alongside the Citadel Guard through a shipyard at Elos, cranes at Cargo and docks at Nostos. The Penumbral Watcher's Night mages could shroud the Elos works from Grendel spies.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that many Wintermark heroes prefer ransoming defeated enemies to butchering them, so they have no reason to dislike fighting alongside a daring army like the Red Wind Corsairs.

An angry blade.o: Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra, instructed by the Senate to find ways for Imperial fleet captains to disrupt Grendel naval and logistical operations in the Bay of Catazar, concluded that fleets cannot directly oppose a Grendel navy without an Imperial navy to support. She offered four alternative proposals instead.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Graciana proposed the Free Docks, fortified jetties and docks across Free Landing's islands. Imperial fleets could support them as a basic fortification against attacks from the sea, though this opportunity has since expired.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Bay was the focus of the appraisal. The proposed Forayer quality would let the Red Wind Corsairs switch between army and navy only in its coastal regions, and fortifying the Bay was judged a very sheer cliff to climb.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mora's Rock fortification in Feroz is recalled as having been traded to the Grendel years ago, and an earlier fleet spy network there is cited as the model for smugglers coves.

Madruga.t: The recent Grendel attack on Madruga ruined the Salt Guard and drove the appraisal. The proposed Free Docks would make Madruga harder to attack from the sea, but could not sensibly be built while the Grendel held it.

Morrow.t: Graciana proposed new docks at the Conscious River near Canterspire. They would create the Architect of the Conscious River sinecure and raise Canterspire's weirwood output by four wains to 26 each season.

Redoubt.t: Graciana's plans included upgraded cranes at Cargo, costing 25 mithril and 75 crowns, which would raise the level of investment for businesses in Redoubt. They formed one of the three commissions needed for a Urizen navy.

An apple that falls.d: Food from the Marcher Breadbasket, 75 thrones for orc thralls and casualty-limiting advances by Marcher and Imperial Orc armies won some goodwill. Warmage Heilyn Bronwen's Rest undid much of it by backing his predecessor's curse and refusing to rule out repeating it, sparking riots. The Mourn sought protection from Conclave magic, the Singing Caves as a Marcher national resource, the rebuilding of Sarcombe, fortifications held by locals, and acceptance of the Hatred-revering Whittlefolk. Mel Greenhill, Long Tom and Edda Counter would come to Anvil, and a wicker man was being built to burn at the Solstice as a reckoning. Outcomes were deferred to the Winter Solstice winds.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orc armies, like the Marchers, made a steady advance meant to minimise casualties, helping to blunt claims that the war was simply a slaughter of Jotun.

Jotun.t: Jotun forces were nearly routed but still held two Mournwold regions, including a garrison at Hillstop castle, and had pulled back to Liathaven, where Mournwolders feared they were resupplying for a return.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Mournwolders complained it was apparently fine for the Navarr to hate the Jotun while Marchers who Hate them faced condemnation.

The League.t: Senator Cesare and citizens of the twin cities had helped the Whittlefolk settle in Tassato, and the League Assembly could choose to urge Tassatans to report blasphemy among them.

The Marches.t: Marchers won respect for sharing their granaries and limiting casualties, but the Mourn remained close to rebellion. The Marcher Assembly's shunning of the Whittlefolk and its lack of its own Bourse seat both fed the unrest.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: a Marcher judgement noted that the Urizen General had been rebuked by the Synod for the ritual slaughter, which Mournwolders felt was not enough.

An apple that falls.o: In Autumn 381YE the Mournwold stood on the brink of sedition despite the Jotun being nearly driven out, angry over the Empire's ritual slaughter and the new Imperial Warmage's address. The wind set out the Mourn's grievances and a range of possible Imperial responses.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: Whittle Hill in Freemoor had been liberated, and the Whittlefolk hoped to return there despite fears over their open devotion to Hatred.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Green March was suggested as a site for one of the fortifications the Mourn wanted built against a Jotun return.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: The Greensward's fields had been the scene of the ritual deaths the Mourn demanded a reckoning for, and some who fled the region chose to remain in Tassato.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Southmoor still had a Jotun garrison at Hillstop castle. Once it was liberated, the ruined mining town of Sarcombe could be rebuilt, and the region was suggested as a fortification site.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: The Whittlefolk enclave in Tassato Mestra, known as Little Mournwold, would remain home to other Mournwolders even if the Whittlefolk returned to Freemoor.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland shared in the Marcher Breadbasket supplies sent to the Mourn, and Sister Meredith's mandate there urged Marchers to shun the Whittlefolk.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun had withdrawn to Liathaven, where Mournwolders feared they were resupplying for a renewed attack.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold's fertile farms helped feed the Mourn through the Breadbasket, and Sister Meredith's mandate there urged Marchers to shun the Whittlefolk. Its senator's earlier bid to make the Singing Caves national had been vetoed.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold was seething after the Warmage's address. Riots broke out and couriers were beaten, and its people sought protection, a share of the mithril, fortifications and acceptance of the Whittlefolk, while a wicker man was raised for a Solstice reckoning.

Tassato.t: Tassato sheltered the Whittlefolk, whose green iron would keep flowing to the Chamber of Commerce. Assemblies might urge Tassatans to give evidence of blasphemy among them.

Upwold.t: Upwold's granaries helped feed the Mourn through the Breadbasket, and Sister Meredith's mandate there urged Marchers to shun the Whittlefolk.

An arrow nocked and in flight.d: The Protectorate holds Mora's Rock with veteran orcs and Wind Lord Saoirse, a master of Sand lore. Its attempts to buy supplies from the Freeborn of Feroz and Segura have largely failed because of memories of Governor Rahab's tyranny. Gallum agreed to meet at the Summer Solstice after Garviel i Abrira i Erigo and Khalil i Carno i Guerra offered safe passage. His proposal, open until the end of that Solstice, would return the Spice Gardens to Imperial control and restore the Keeper of the Spice Gardens as a Freeborn national title appointed by the Imperial Apothecaries Guild. An optional appraisal could use the Protectorate's engineers to help Feroz. The civil service warned of possible espionage risks, and noted the Freeborn assembly could support or sink the deal.

Grendel.t: The Protectorate is treated as foreign and separate from the Grendel for as long as it stays independent, though the civil service suspects some contact with the Salt Lords. The Silent Bell is also preparing a report on Grendel espionage rings around the Bay.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn could regain the Spice Gardens and a restored Keeper title, but only if their farmers agree to feed the orc garrison. Their national assembly holds the power to encourage or effectively sink the arrangement.

An arrow nocked and in flight.o: In Spring 388YE Commander Gallum Fiersach of the Protectorate of Morajasse, recognised by the Senate as foreign and distinct from the Grendel, asked to deal with the Empire through the Imperial Consul. He offered to concede the Spice Gardens of Feroz in return for Freeborn-grown food for his garrison at Mora's Rock.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: Morajasse remains held by Gallum's Protectorate from the fortress of Mora's Rock, with its borders largely closed. Under the proposal its supply troubles would ease and travel restrictions on Imperial citizens would be relaxed.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Mentioned in passing: the battle at Oran is cited as the point after which the Senate recognised the Protectorate.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Bell is investigating Grendel espionage rings across the wider Bay, and the Spice Gardens are noted for growing some of its finest Cerulean Mazzarine.

Feroz.t: The long-fallow Spice Gardens of Feroz could return to Freeborn hands, and an appraisal might help rebuild the territory's prosperity, its bridges across the Scorrero or its defences. However, its people remain wary of the orcs who once enforced Rahab's rule.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Gallum expects the Iron Confederacy matter concerning the islands of Madruga to be settled by the Summer Solstice.

Segura.t: Some Freeborn of Segura are prepared to trade food with Mora's Rock despite widespread suspicion. Any appraisal could look for ways for the orcs to work with the people of Segura.

An eagle in song.d: Lady Kaywenn de Orzel's writ of consecration was upheld by the Pride Assembly at the Spring Equinox 386YE. The civil service proposed an academy of music and oration with monthly martial tournaments, costing 30 wains of white granite and 90 crowns over three months, then consecrated with true liao. It would also house the High Bard and give them two thrones a season. Possible sites were Gnijezdo in Miekarova, the Pits of Ennerlund in Holberg, or Belletain in Weirwater. At the Summer Solstice the General Assembly backed Starac Sijed Orzel's mandate for Sandling (1234-248). The true liao is ready, but no work has been commissioned. The crisis of faith over Vardas blocks any extra benefits until it is resolved. The High Bard sent the Culwich Witches eighty-one names to receive gifts once the consecration is complete.

Dawn.t: The memorial honours a Dawnish troubadour and knight, and its chosen site in Weirwater would inspire pilgrims, especially the Dawnish, to look to their future and value Dawnish music. Weirwater's Culwich Witches also plan gifts for the Empire's musicians.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Ozren de Orzel is noted as having ultimately died to the Druj.

The League.t: The Pits of Ennerlund in Holberg was offered as a site that would have inspired pilgrims with League music and paid Holberg's congregations extra income, but the General Assembly chose Weirwater instead.

Varushka.t: Gnijezdo in Miekarova, where Ozren had served as a stzena and priest before his house moved to Dawn, was offered as a site honouring Varushkan music and heritage, but it was not chosen.

An eagle in song.o: After the Assembly of Pride called for a memorial to the Dawnish troubadour and exemplar Ozren de Orzel, the civil service offered three sites for an inspirational academy. The General Assembly chose Belletain in Sandling, Weirwater, though the academy had not yet been commissioned.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: Ennerlund, home of the Great Pits left by spirits Ozren exorcised, was proposed as a monument to his Pride as a cardinal, but it was passed over.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Mieriada, site of Ozren's first congregation at Gnijezdo, was proposed for an academy that would turn pilgrims towards their past, but the mandate was not enacted.

Weirwater/Sandling.t: Belletain in Sandling, where Ozren led his congregation and the Children of the Crow, was chosen for the academy. True liao is held ready, but construction has yet to be commissioned or paid for.

Holberg.t: Had the academy been built at the Pits of Ennerlund, every congregation in Holberg would have gained 36 extra rings each season, but another site was chosen.

Miekarova.t: An academy at Gnijezdo would have given every congregation in Miekarova two extra doses of liao each season, but the General Assembly chose a different site.

Weirwater.t: Chosen as the academy's site, Weirwater's congregations would each gain a Philtre of Strength every season once it is built and consecrated, though only if the crisis of faith is resolved in favour of the exemplars.

An ideal for living.d: A month after the Spring Equinox, half a dozen sword scholar sects, including the Five Blade Fellowship, the Steel Crane and the Red Scroll Bearers, met amid fractious debates and duels. They had been nearly bled dry fighting Grendel and Druj invaders on their own, and shared reverence for Sulemaine forged a consensus. Rebuilding the temple would need a Senate motion or Wayleave, 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns. It would create a sinecure worth 8 liao and 16 Synod votes, but only if the Urizen Assembly appointed the holder and granted the mysterious Labyrinth Sword. Follow-up mandates could make mandates depend on greater majorities. Some priests instead condemned the scholars as followers of a false paragon.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: in the in-character story, a Dawnish knight named Leo duels the sword scholar Talitha of the Tempests in Morrow, watched by a crowd of his companions.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the sword scholar sects had been nearly bled dry fighting Druj invaders, and Zenith is described as being in enemy hands.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named alongside the Druj as invaders whom the sword scholars had exhausted themselves fighting.

Urizen.t: Urizen's sword scholars returned to the fold after the National Assembly's judgement, and Urizen was offered the chance to rebuild the Temple of the Winds. If the Assembly also appointed the envoy and secured the Labyrinth Sword, mandates from any assembly would struggle to affect Urizen without a greater majority in the Synod.

An ideal for living.o: Following an Urizen National Assembly judgement, Urizen's rival sword scholar sects gathered at the ruined Temple of the Winds in Peregro, Morrow, and agreed to unite under the Disciples of the Tempest Jade Maiden and return to the Imperial fold. They offered the chance to rebuild the temple, which would come with mandates able to blunt religious influence over Urizen and potentially the whole Empire.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Peregro hosted the sword scholar gathering at the ruined Temple of the Winds, once the Disciples of the Tempest Jade Maiden's largest temple, which could be reconstructed as a symbol of reconciliation.

Morrow.t: The sword scholars gathered in Morrow at the ruins of the Temple of the Winds, which could be rebuilt there as a new centre for the Wisdom sects.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: a Urizen healer in the story says no life may be squandered while Zenith is still in the hands of the enemy.

An iron feast.d: Only those who receive the Challenge the Iron Duke ritual may enter, and victors must wait a year before competing again. Nine covens cast the ritual the previous season. In the Eternal Banquet, challengers cook two vegetarian dishes using a secret ingredient revealed that morning, judged by Barien and chosen judges in a Summer chamber, with an extra prize for the best dish. In the Noble Hunt, held through a conjunction to Gazelle Park in Weirmoor, Weirwater, unarmed and unarmoured challengers must gather enough trophies while Jaheris' hunters pursue them with bow and spear. Death is unlikely but possible, and a second may scout for them but cannot collect trophies.

Dawn.t: Dawn is home to the Noble Hunt, held in a Summer chamber linked to Gazelle Park in the Dawnish woods of Weirmoor, and four Dawnish covens (Phoenix Rising, The Cabal of Nevezamzer, The Coven of Golden Wings and Unicorn's Glorious Charge) were among those who cast Challenge the Iron Duke last season.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr coven The Eternal Family is listed among those who cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Brass Coast covens The Glass Mantle and The Tempest Flame are listed among those who cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Urizeni coven Ashen Flame is listed among those who cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wintermark coven Voices of the Unbound Storm is listed among those who cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season.

An iron feast.o: Barien's heralds announced two new challenges for the Autumn 387YE summit: the Challenge of the Eternal Banquet, a cooking contest built around a secret ingredient, and the Challenge of the Noble Hunt, in which unarmed challengers seek hidden trophies while being hunted by Jaheris' heralds.

Weirwater/Weirmoor.t: Gazelle Park in the woods of Weirmoor is the site linked to the Iron Duke's hunting chamber, where a conjunction at 1:30pm on the Saturday carries challengers into the Noble Hunt.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater hosts the conjunction for the Challenge of the Noble Hunt, through which challengers reach a Summer chamber linked to Gazelle Park to be pursued by Jaheris' hunters.

An old sodality.d: Founded with the Throne's backing, the Sun Chamber was crippled when nearly all its members died fighting beside Empress Britta. Prompted by Zoria and Luca of the Zulgan Tash, the civil service found its powers were never abrogated. A magnitude 20 Autumn arcane projection was given to Zoria to help members join through Mark of Fellowship, and the Senate chamber was reserved for three sessions covering joining, electing the Counsel and assigning bequests, and using one of the Doors of the Chamber. The court warned that a sodality limiting its membership in this way would struggle to pass scrutiny today. Roshanwe sent three Tempest Jade ammonites so worthy magicians could submit theses to its herald, the Empty Page.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening vignette shows a Marcher-style steading, the Tall Oaks, receiving a letter asking whether their old bequest to the Sun Chamber still stands.

An old sodality.o: The Constitutional Court confirmed that the Sun Chamber, an ancient sodality founded under Empress Richilde to help young citizens gain high office, still legally exists. It was revived at Anvil with civil service support, and the eternal Roshanwe offered its members gifts and an audience with a herald.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: The Eaves, an abandoned woodcutter's hut on the edge of Alderly, was prepared by Roshanwe as the meeting place where its navigators would bring magicians to put their theses to the Empty Page.

Mournwold.t: Roshanwe's herald, the Empty Page, was to receive the magicians who used the ammonites, along with their guests, in a chamber prepared by the eternal on the edge of Alderly in Mournwold.

An unexpected alignment.d: With the Empire clinging to Sealtoq and the year-long Jotun truce there nearly expired, the Thule, whose own peace with the Jotun had lapsed, offered the Talons of the Wind, the Banner of the Rime Hound and the Earthquake Drummers for up to a year. Their conditions were that Imperial armies always outnumber Thule armies, that the campaign be pursued seriously, that no territory-wide slaughter curses be used, and that their Rivers of Life curse go unhindered. The price was one region per army, chosen from Skogei Glens, Miechernya, Branoc or the Webwood, or alternatively Opascari or Brez in place of three. They also wanted the right to take captured orc thralls to Otkodov as slaves. An envoy would negotiate at Anvil.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Thule named the Skogei Glens in Skarsind, held by the Imperial Orcs, as one of the regions they would accept as payment. Their demand to enslave captured orc thralls also bore directly on orcish people.

Jotun.t: The Jotun were the intended target of a joint Imperial and Thule campaign to drive them from Sermersuaq. Their truce over Sealtoq was nearly at an end, and the Thule rebuffed their envoys' attempts to extend their own peace.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the deaths of Jotun thralls in the Mournwold were cited as the reason Jotun diplomacy had failed, and the Thule cited them again as grounds for their ban on slaughter curses.

Thule.t: Emboldened by their success in Ossium and urged on by the Eternal Dragons, the Thule offered three armies against the Jotun. They sought new Imperial regions and orc slaves as their price, and the Senate ultimately ratified a treaty securing their aid.

Varushka.t: Most of the regions the Thule demanded were Varushkan, including Miechernya, Branoc, the Webwood, and the prized Opascari and Brez. These could be ceded or simply left for Thule armies to conquer.

Wintermark.t: The offer gave Wintermark a chance to retake the Suaq homeland of Sermersuaq with Thule help. When told the regions demanded were not Wintermark's, Hoosfa Mek shrugged and treated that as Wintermark's problem to solve.

An unexpected alignment.o: In Winter 383YE a Thule delegation led by the general Hoosfa Mek arrived at Sealtoq under a flag of truce, offering up to three Thule armies to support an Imperial reconquest of Sermersuaq from the Jotun in exchange for Imperial regions and captured orc thralls. The Senate went on to ratify a treaty with the Thule securing their aid in Sermersuaq.

Karsk/Branoc.t: Branoc was one of the four regions the Thule named as acceptable payment of one region per army.

Miekarova/Miechernya.t: Miechernya was named as an acceptable region for the Thule to receive, whether by cession or by unopposed conquest.

Ossium/Webwood.t: The Webwood was listed among the regions the Thule would take as the price of one army's support.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule delegation travelled to Sealtoq through the Jotun-controlled East Floes.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Sealtoq was the Empire's last foothold in Sermersuaq, and the Jotun's year-long agreement not to fight there was nearly over. It was here that the Thule delegation arrived under a white flag to make its offer.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The Thule, who had held and magically fortified the Silver Peaks since 379YE, abandoned their silent watch. They insisted that no slaughter curses endanger the people of the Silver Peaks.

Skarsind/Skogei Glens.t: The Skogei Glens were one of the regions the Thule would accept in exchange for an army.

Volodmartz/Brez.t: Brez, home of the Granites of Veltsgorsk, was offered as an alternative payment worth three regions.

Volodmartz/Opascari.t: Opascari, with its Hunt of Alderei the Fair, was offered as an alternative payment worth three regions.

Karsk.t: Karsk's region of Branoc was one of the regions the Thule would accept as payment for each army they committed.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova's region of Miechernya was offered as one possible region the Thule would take in exchange for an army.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the killing of Jotun thralls in the Mournwold was cited as the source of continuing Jotun hostility and of the Thule's refusal to tolerate slaughter curses.

Ossium.t: The Thule called their invasion of Ossium a success that had whetted their appetite for conquest. The Webwood in Ossium was among the regions they would accept as payment.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov was named as the beneficiary of Thule conquest. Captured orc thralls would be taken there as slaves to serve the Dragons.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq was the focus of the proposed year-long joint campaign to reconquer the territory from the Jotun. The Thule planned to cast Rivers of Life over it and forbade territory-wide slaughter curses there.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind's Skogei Glens was listed among the regions the Thule would accept in return for committing an army.

Volodmartz.t: The Thule would accept either Opascari or Brez in Volodmartz as worth three regions, because of the valuable bourse resources each holds.

Anarchy in Miekarova.d: The civil service reported a coordinated campaign of anarchy auras and sabotage in Miekarova aimed at the infrastructure that supports smaller military units, leaving soldiers demoralised and cut off from letters and supplies. No cult claimed responsibility, though the incidents followed the Senate building's consecration to anarchy and at least one Synod-condemned individual remained at large. Left unchecked, the units would suffer a massive loss of effectiveness while businesses enjoyed a moderate, unsustainable rise in demand. The options set out were militia funding, a military sweep relocating anarchists to a neighbouring territory, exorcism, auras of Vigilance, or disrupting the cult's leadership. The Assembly of Vigilance chose the auras, naming Vitomir Vardov to coordinate them, which limits the disruption while leaving the business boost intact.

Varushka.t: Varushkan military units operating out of Miekarova faced sabotage and demoralisation. The Varushkan National Assembly was one body that could have named someone to lead exorcisms, but the response came instead from the Vigilance Assembly through Vitomir Vardov.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's territory of Skarsind was listed as a possible destination if the Senate had ordered anarchists swept out of Miekarova and relocated.

Anarchy in Miekarova.o: In Winter 378YE an organised anarchy cult spread malign auras and sabotaged supply lines for military units based in Miekarova, threatening their effectiveness while briefly boosting local trade. The Vigilance Assembly responded by naming Vitomir Vardov to raise virtuous auras across the territory.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Karov was named as a neighbouring territory to which anarchists could have been forcibly relocated under a Senate-approved military sweep.

Miekarova.t: Anarchy auras and sabotage across Miekarova threatened a massive loss of effectiveness for military units based there, while impulse spending gave local businesses a temporary boost. Vitomir Vardov was named to raise auras of Vigilance throughout the territory in response.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind was named as a neighbouring territory to which anarchists could have been forcibly relocated under a Senate-approved military sweep.

Volodmartz.t: Mentioned in passing: Volodmartz was named as a neighbouring territory to which anarchists could have been forcibly relocated under a Senate-approved military sweep.

Another verse.d: Isaella's Dance, the Fist of the Mountains, the Tusks and the Valiant Pegasus fought in Kahraman, while a tower of black ice raised by Imperial magicians guarded Serra Damata. The Hierro, Corazón and Escuta, with the Skjaldirborn and Yantan Thetrason's warband, were pushed back from Rojota, though over five hundred Imperial soldiers died there. The Bear who Swims and Roaring Thunder then struck from Liathaven into Braydon's Jasse, but the Tusks' defence gave warning in time. The western Jotun withdrew into Reinos and the northern force fell back into Liathaven. Corazón raids cost several mines resources, and the roads and kamkrags project is close to completion if Jade Range holds.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs marched south and east to join the fight against the Grendel in Madruga.

Jotun.t: The Lasambrian armies and the reinforcing Bear who Swims and Roaring Thunder were all driven out of Kahraman, falling back into Reinos and Liathaven with losses estimated at almost as many as the Empire's. The Bear who Swims was weakened by its new general's lost banner.

Navarr.t: Cadwell Waystone's Isaella's Dance pressed west against the Lasambrians, helping to win the bloody battle west of Rojota alongside a single Navarr contingent of Imperial captains.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn territory of Kahraman was liberated again, though Corazón raids cost its mines resources; the Red Wind Corsairs left to fight the Grendel in Madruga.

The Marches.t: Stanley of Chalkdown's Tusks anchored the defence, blunting the Corazón raids and giving warning of the Jotun advance from Liathaven, with a furlough in the Mournwold promised to the soldiers.

Wintermark.t: Ivar Dunning's Fist of the Mountains split its forces between the west and the Tusks in the north, and by fighting with honour saw its casualties reduced by a tenth as the Jotun offered and accepted quarter.

Another verse.o: In Summer 386YE, four Imperial armies backed by the Knights of Glory and Imperial captains drove the Lasambrian Jotun and two further Jotun armies out of Kahraman, liberating the territory at a cost of nearly three and a half thousand Imperial soldiers.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: Two Jotun armies with magical and allied warriors came down from Liathaven into the Jasse and fought near the site of Fort Braydon, but were held and driven back.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: The Lasambrian attempt to complete the conquest of Jade Range failed as they were pushed back, and the kamkrag project's completion depends on it staying in Imperial hands.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: Corazón raiders struck some caravans passing through Serra Briante but could not rob the grassland folk or threaten the kamkrag labourers.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: A tower of black ice garrisoned by warriors from the realm of the Mistress of Ice and Darkness protected the peaks of Serra Damata, though the Damatian Cliffs still lost five wains of white granite to raiders.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman was liberated after a season of hard fighting on two fronts, at a cost of nearly three and a half thousand Imperial dead or unable to fight, and its roads and kamkrags are nearly finished.

Liathaven.t: The Bear who Swims and Roaring Thunder marched out of Liathaven to seek a second beachhead in Kahraman, only to be pushed back into it.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs marched here to join the fight against the Grendel.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: the Valiant Pegasus came to Kahraman straight from fighting the scions of Cold Sun in Miaren.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tusks paraded south through the Mourn and were promised a furlough there by their general.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the defeated Lasambrian armies retreated through the woods back into Reinos.

Any dream will do.d: The Assembly's judgement passed 404-0 and cited Holberg and Apulian as cities that chose to join the League. From the Summer Solstice 388YE until the Summer Solstice 389YE, the Assembly may each season pass one of two competing mandates, each costing 25 liao. One names a non-citizen group within the Empire and a League archetype to lead the approach, with a different group and archetype each time. The other has one League city approach a significant foreign town or city on the Empire's continent. Neither guarantees anyone joins, but each creates closer ties. If both pass in one season, the one with the higher margin applies. No other known species could plausibly join at present.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the League is cautioned that courting Dubhtraig would mean benefiting a Grendel city in the middle of the Empire's war with them.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos and Tassato were once Highborn cities that broke away by declaring themselves free cities rather than by rebellion, keeping reasonable relations with their former kin.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: in the accompanying fiction a Navarr named Alcuin rejects a Sarvos bishop's comparison of the League's courtship to the Great Dance.

The League.t: The Assembly's judgement gives the League a year of seasonal mandates to court non-citizen groups within the Empire, led by its archetypes, or foreign cities, led by one of its own cities, in pursuit of new partners. It also stakes a lasting claim to welcome any other sapient species should one ever become available.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the hylje are noted as a sapient people who, if they could join any Imperial nation, would surely join Wintermark, though their fluid nature may put them beyond the egregore bond.

Any dream will do.o: After the League Assembly declared it their highest calling to bring sapient beings of every kind into the Empire, the Way of Virtue and the League, the League gained a year-long opportunity to court new partners for the Great Game.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Mentioned in passing: some describe Tassato Mestra and Tassato Regario as a pair of lovers bound in fractious matrimony, as a model for the bonds a League city might forge with a foreign one.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato Regario is paired with Tassato Mestra as lovers in fractious matrimony, an illustration of the marriage-like bonds the League hopes to form.

Holberg.t: Holberg is held up as proof of the League's success, a city with its own history that joined through friendship with its burghers and is now called the greatest city in the world. It is one of the five cities that could lead an approach to a foreign city.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos is shown as a former Highborn outpost that won independence through diplomacy, and as the founding city of the nation through Aldones di Sarvos. The accompanying scene features one of its bishops eager to recruit new partners.

Spiral.t: Spiral's city of Apulian is cited alongside Holberg as a city that joined the League without being conquered, though not without rancour, and is described as a city of wondrous secrets.

Tassato.t: Tassato is recalled as a former Highborn city that declared itself free without military rebellion, and Barell of Tassato as a founding partner of the League. It is one of the cities that could lead an approach to a foreign city.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar is remembered as joining the League peacefully when Maria Ivanova allied with Tassato. The sovereign King Rat, who claims the city's underbelly, is rumoured to be seeking to join the League, a prospect the nation is urged to weigh exceptionally carefully.

Any port in a storm.d: The proposed Great Work would cost 75 white granite, 50 weirwood and 375 crowns over a year. It would raise investment in Holberg, boost taxation around the Semmerlak by 15 thrones a season, found a new town, add a ferry to Ossium and create a League Merchant-Prince post. It would also raise Varushkan dock prices by a tenth. The Lijkkever offered materials and marsh expertise in exchange for fifteen years' exclusive Sarcophan access, which would cut the tax gain to 10 thrones. The Sand Fishers offered weirwood in return for their own trade enclave. The Prognosticators' Office was short of appraisers, with Eilian Sweetwater missing in Redoubt.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: past ideas to expand Lacre never emerged, and ships might sail on to Lacre if the new port were too small.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: their retreat from Holberg's outlying regions made the port feasible, and some Sand Fishers now call them 'those who take without giving'.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a major Grendel offensive in Redoubt coincided with Eilian Sweetwater's lighthouse investigation, and he has been missing since.

The League.t: Holberg stood to gain a great port, a new town, cheaper business upgrades, wain purchases and a new League post, the Merchant-Prince of the Imperatrix Docks, if the Senate commissioned the work.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Eilian Sweetwater vanished while investigating the destroyed Lighthouse of Nikephoros in Urizen-held Redoubt.

Varushka.t: The new port would draw trade from Korotny Docks and Kostjyas Respite, raising prices for the Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore and the Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak by a tenth.

Any port in a storm.o: In Autumn 387YE Naomi of Virtue's Rest completed a Senate-ordered appraisal of building a great port, the Imperatrix Docks, in Utterlund on Holberg's coast, with offers of help from the Sarcophan Lijkkever family and the Sand Fisher orcs. The Senate could now commission it.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: Mentioned in passing: the creeping waters of the Morass have been expanding to claim Ennerlund.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Once the proposed port site at the end of the Lakesedge Highway, it was passed over for Utterlund, though its Sand Fishers still offered weirwood and labour.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: Mentioned in passing: the Morass is spreading into Rebeshof, and Professor Gelberg is exploring Sand Fisher farms there.

Holberg/The Morass.t: Mentioned in passing: its expanding waters were why Misericorde was once thought the only practical port site.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: The marshy coast was the chosen site for the proposed Imperatrix Docks and the new town expected to grow around them.

Karov/Malimorzi.t: Korotny Docks would lose trade to the new port, raising the Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak's prices by a tenth.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: The Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore would pay a tenth more for purchases as trade shifted to Holberg.

Semmerholm/Lacuve.t: Mentioned in passing: proposals to expand Lacre never came to anything, and ships might sail on to Lacre instead.

Holberg.t: The Imperatrix Docks were proposed for its Utterlund coast, promising a new town, more investment, a ferry to Ossium and an extension of the Lakesedge Highway.

Karov.t: Varushka's Korotny Docks would see trade fall and the Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak's prices rise by a tenth if the port were built.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, though Varushkan ports on the Semmerlak would lose trade to the proposed docks.

Ossium.t: A ferry across the Nameless River would ease travel and trade with Holberg, though Kostjyas Respite and the Bittershore ministry would face higher prices.

Redoubt.t: Eilian Sweetwater went missing while investigating the destroyed Lighthouse of Nikephoros during a major Grendel offensive.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers modelled their request for a trade enclave on the Alivetti Enclave in Sarvos.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: earlier ideas to expand the port of Lacre never emerged.

The Semmerlak.t: The docks would boost taxation in territories bordering the lake and shift shipping away from Varushkan ports.

Anyone but you.d: Directed by the Assembly of Nine, the Silent Bell helped magistrates arrest and execute most of the cult ringleaders, but Kaarina White-Eye, Maarik the Golden Tongue and Wemba the Bloody fled with their followers. Under a Wintermark Assembly mandate, backed by the Loyalty Assembly, priests and Stormcrows saved nearly half of those who took Agramant's bargains; more than two score confessed, were fined and became Frayed, possible recruits for Wintermark's new army. Theodric Irontongue's unrepentant Walkers of the Wastes are now Averil Olsen's responsibility. The Shuttered Lantern recovered boons, vis and texts, found the Bleeding Ice, a Heart's Blood source the Conclave must endow or see destroyed, and tracked the herald Ender of Virtue.

Dawn.t: Tyburn of House De Rondell, the Dawnish Grandmaster of the Shuttered Lantern, will receive the boons recovered from the cultists and is responsible for intercepting Ender of Virtue in Stark.

Jotun.t: The escaped cult leaders are all driven by hatred of the Jotun and vow bloody vengeance on them, with Kaarina White-Eye believed to have fled west towards the Jotun border; a maimed Jotun orc, Harla, testified against Theodric Irontongue.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Cardinal of Vigilance, Gaelen Embercast of Navarr, raised the Assembly of Nine motion that sent the Silent Bell to Sermersuaq.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Maarik the Golden Tongue grew wealthy mediating trade deals with the Thule in the Silver Peaks, where she is now believed to be hiding.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: two recovered ritual texts would be recognisable to any Urizen who had studied the ceremonies of the Black Drop Society.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's priests and Stormcrows saved many of the Sermersuaq Winterfolk who bargained with Agramant, leaving a body of Frayed warriors and others who could form the core of the nation's new army. Three Winterfolk cult leaders remain at large and Averil Olsen must deal with Theodric Irontongue's cult.

Anyone but you.o: In spring 385YE the Empire's efforts to root out Agramant's cults in reclaimed Sermersuaq bore fruit: the Silent Bell exposed the ringleaders, Wintermark's priests and Stormcrows won clemency for remorseful cultists, and the Shuttered Lantern recovered the Howler's boons. Three notorious cult leaders escaped, and new threats were uncovered.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: Mentioned in passing: Maarik the Golden Tongue was a Suaq mediator from the north of the East Floes before her hall was burned and she turned to Agramant.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Maarik the Golden Tongue and her followers are believed to be hiding in the Silver Peaks, sheltered by several allies.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: Ender of Virtue and its cultists were tracked in Stark heading towards Kallavesa, with an opportunity to confront them at Nestori's Lament.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: Theodric Irontongue is preaching to the Walkers of the Wastes, who will remain a threat here unless stopped, with an opportunity to strike at them at Ardith's Rest.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: The Bleeding Ice, a boulder near the Hot Springs weeping four pawns of winter vis each season and linked to Wemba the Bloody, was found here, and the Conclave must endow it or see it destroyed.

Kallavesa.t: The herald Ender of Virtue is heading for the Kallavesa border carrying something from the Winter realm believed capable of blighting the Kallavesi herb gardens.

Sermersuaq.t: The territory was purged of most of Agramant's cultists through executions and clemency, though three ringleaders fled, the Walkers of the Wastes remain unrepentant and the Bleeding Ice awaits the Conclave's decision.

Apparently with no surprise.d: Bastiaan van Krommemuil's procession for the late Hester van de Moerassen expected to reach the Highguard Chapel on Friday and asked for Whispers through the Black Gate. Unsettling travellers planned to visit the Rod and Shield and the Unfettered Mind. Gelder Kraft and Bramme van Zuredruiven had both arranged to meet Hahnmark farmers at the Tree of Names at the same hour, which risked trouble. Mitwold alders sought defence oaths after the Jotun took Meade. The Spire of the Stallion's Volition sought divinatory exchange with Wintermark. Nicodemus was asked to send Naga to rescue Garev. Highborn herbalists sought a Spring alternative to Ruthless Vigilance, Healthy Crop. Battlefed's envoys sought eternal-powered magic items. Sular's Spyglass agreed to attend Abreya de Lagriffe's inquisition.
