Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: assembly statements honour the Fist of the Mountains for halting a Grendel assault on Urizen, and Urizen vows not to be cowed by the Grendel.

Highguard.t: Several Highborn concerns arose. A Sarcophan funeral was to be hosted at the Highguard Chapel, the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly was asked to send Naga to rescue the mendicant Garev, and Highborn herbalists offered ten thrones towards a new herb-garden ritual.

Jotun.t: Their sudden, overwhelming assault left Mitwold on the brink of falling into Jotun hands, with Meade itself captured.

The Marches.t: Alders of Mitwold travelled to the Community Hall seeking oaths of aid, fearing for the Marches' most valuable territory after the loss of Meade.

Urizen.t: The Spire of the Stallion's Volition, inspired by the Fist of the Mountains' sacrifice at Redoubt, came to meet Urizen seers and illuminates before seeking exchange with Wintermark.

Varushka.t: Boyars received word that the Charnel Lord had sent envoys to the Feast of the Loom in the Varushkan camp, seeking magic items to consume for the benefit of Karsk.

Wintermark.t: Rival Sarcophan merchants sought Hahnmark farmers at the Tree of Names, and Urizen astronomancers hoped to share divinatory methods with stormcrows and mystics after the Fist of the Mountains' sacrifice.

Apparently with no surprise.o: Ahead of the 387YE Winter Solstice, word arrived of visitors travelling to Anvil to meet citizens. They included a Sarcophan funeral procession, rival merchants seeking Hahnmark farmers, alders from Jotun-assailed Mitwold, Urizen seers, Highborn herbalists, envoys of the Charnel Lord and a Freeborn sect answering an inquisition. A Highborn mendicant was also trapped in caves beneath Casfall.

Casinea/Casfall.t: The injured mendicant Garev was trapped in a treacherous, lightless cave system beneath Casfall, and up to four Naga were sought to reach and treat him without triggering a collapse.

Casinea.t: Strange, off-putting travellers were reported across the territory, and the mendicant Garev lay injured in caves beneath Casfall awaiting rescue.

Hahnmark.t: Farmers growing crops for viezesmaak were sought by both Gelder Kraft and Bramme van Zuredruiven at the same time. Experts warned that a meeting between the rival merchants would go badly for everyone.

Karsk.t: The Charnel Lord sought to reassure Karsk's people, especially those near Broken Barrow, that he remained their protector, promising to turn eternal-powered items into something to benefit them.

Mitwold.t: With the territory teetering on the brink of Jotun control and Meade captured, alders travelled to Anvil to learn of defence plans, especially from the Drakes' general.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Charnel Lord disparaged Karsk folk who left for Ossium seeking riches.

Redoubt.t: The Fist of the Mountains' final charge defending Redoubt, witnessed by the Spire of the Stallion's Volition from their homes, inspired the spire's journey to Anvil.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mitwold alders reckoned that even losing Upwold would not be as bad as the Jotun assault on Mitwold.

Apples from a tree.d: Suaq icewalker Artja Fivefeet proposed the Kauppahall, a twinned trading hall in Valashal costing 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns, with a Wintermark title, the Talon of Kauppahall, to buy white granite and some ilium. Varushkan boyars under Oksana Lyava Pinavora proposed enlarging Korotny's docks for 18 wains of white granite and 36 crowns, creating a Harbour Master of Semmerlak to buy weirwood and ilium. Each project would end public auction supply of a resource. The Senate commissioned the Kauppahall, though the appointment method it named was unconstitutional, and the Parador of Dust. The Blackfield Market lapsed. The Korotny opportunity remains until Summer 384YE. Bartimaeus then enacted a Prosperity mandate for Redoubt.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish declined to build the Star Metal Market in Lacre, which prompted the Varushkan boyars' alternative plan, and Dawn is named as a trading partner of Korotny.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is named as one of the partners in Korotny's substantial trade across the Semmerlak.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the ever-present threat of the Thule is described as the only check on Korotny's ambitions.

Urizen.t: After the Solstice, Bartimaeus of the Prosperity Assembly enacted a mandate urging the citizens of Redoubt to seek ways to increase their prosperity, which could lead to a new commercial opportunity there.

Varushka.t: Wealthy Varushkan boyars led by Oksana Lyava Pinavora proposed enlarging the Korotny docks, which would create a Harbour Master of Semmerlak chosen by Varushkan mine and forest owners. The Senate did not commission it, but the opportunity remains until the end of the Summer Solstice 384YE.

Wintermark.t: The Senate commissioned the Kauppahall in Valashal, which would give Wintermark a national title, the Talon of Kauppahall, to buy white granite and ilium. However, the appointment method the Senators named was unconstitutional; the civil service had advised a tally of votes among Wintermark military unit leaders.

Apples from a tree.o: In Winter 383YE the civil service set out new and lingering chances to build national markets that divert Bourse resources from the public auction: the Kauppahall in Valashal, expanded docks at Korotny, the Blackfield Market and the Parador of Dust. Abbess Jenny Stock also proposed that the Cardinal of Prosperity use Synod mandates to seek commercial opportunities in named territories.

Hahnmark/Valasmark.t: Valashal, built on the site of the razed and supposedly cursed Runehall, is to gain the commissioned Kauppahall, a trading hall meant to enrich Valasmark through trade in white granite and ilium from the surrounding hills.

Hahnmark.t: The Kauppahall, a rune-shaped twinned trading hall at Valashal, was commissioned to draw merchants from southern Hahnmark and northern Kallavesa and trade stone and ilium from the nearby hills.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is noted as a partner in Korotny's lake-trade on the Semmerlak.

Karov.t: A plan was put forward to enlarge Korotny's docks on the Semmerlak, making them the outlet for weirwood and lake ilium. It was not commissioned this season, but it remains available until the end of the Summer Solstice 384YE.

Redoubt.t: Following the Solstice, Bartimaeus enacted a Prosperity mandate encouraging Redoubt's citizens to seek new ways to increase their prosperity, which could give rise to a commercial opportunity at the next summit.

Appoint Ambassador to Otkodov Spring 382.d: The motion to appoint a new Ambassador to Otkodov was proposed by the senator for Karsk and seconded by the senator for Karov. It passed, and the resulting election was held at the Sunday afternoon session of the Senate. Yvengi Katzev was appointed Ambassador to Otkodov.

Thule.t: Thule, which held Otkodov at the time, saw the Senate appoint Yvengi Katzev as the Empire's Ambassador to Otkodov.

Appoint Ambassador to Otkodov Spring 382.o: The Senate passed a motion to appoint an Ambassador to Otkodov in Spring 382YE, and Yvengi Katzev was elected to the post.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov gained a newly appointed Imperial ambassador, Yvengi Katzev, while the territory was held by Thule.

Appoint Ambassador to Otkodov Spring 383.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Miekarova and seconded by the senator for Karov, called for the election of an Ambassador to Otkodov. The page records only the outcome: Yevgeni Katzev, who already held the position, was reappointed. It gives no further details about the ambassador's duties or about how the vote went.

Thule.t: Thule's senators for Miekarova and Karov proposed and seconded the motion, which kept Yevgeni Katzev in place as Ambassador to Otkodov, a Thule territory.

Appoint Ambassador to Otkodov Spring 383.o: In Spring 383YE the Senate passed a motion to elect an Ambassador to Otkodov, and the incumbent, Yevgeni Katzev, was reappointed to the post.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov kept its incumbent ambassador, Yevgeni Katzev, who was reappointed to the post.

Appoint Commonwealth ambassador.d: This administrative motion created the first appointment of an Imperial Ambassador to the Commonwealth. The holder is responsible for the Commonwealth Embassy and represents the Empire in its dealings with the Commonwealth. The motion was carried, and Beatrix Amalia Novarian Zu Holberg was appointed to the position, becoming the Empire's first envoy to the Commonwealth.

The League.t: A citizen bearing the name Zu Holberg, Beatrix Amalia Novarian, became the Empire's first Ambassador to the Commonwealth, placing the League's diplomatic voice at the forefront of Imperial dealings with that nation.

Appoint Commonwealth ambassador.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate made the first appointment to the new post of Ambassador to the Commonwealth, choosing Beatrix Amalia Novarian Zu Holberg.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg appears only in the name of the newly appointed ambassador, Beatrix Amalia Novarian Zu Holberg.

Appoint Dean of the Academy Summer 382YE.d: The motion to appoint the Dean of the Academy was proposed by the senator for Mitwold and seconded by Mournwold. Mitwold escalated the vote so that the election was held immediately. The candidate was elected by constitutional vote and the appointment was ratified by the Throne. As a result, Morana was appointed Dean of the Academy.

The Marches.t: Marcher senators for Mitwold and Mournwold proposed and seconded the motion, and Mitwold's escalation brought about the immediate election of a new Dean of the Academy.

Appoint Dean of the Academy Summer 382YE.o: In Summer 382YE the Senate passed a motion to appoint a new Dean of the Academy, and Morana was elected to the post.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold's senator proposed the motion and escalated the vote so that the election of the Dean was held at once.

Appoint Dean of the Liberated.d: The College of the Liberated is a great work in Sarvos, and it carries an associated ceremonial title, the Dean of the Liberated. In Autumn 381YE the Senate considered a motion to appoint someone to the post. Miaren proposed the motion and Feroz seconded it. The outcome was that Venturo de Sarvos was appointed as Dean of the Liberated.

The League.t: A League citizen, Venturo de Sarvos, took up the ceremonial title tied to a great work in one of the League's own territories.

Appoint Dean of the Liberated.o: In Autumn 381YE the Senate considered a motion, proposed by Miaren and seconded by Feroz, to appoint a Dean of the Liberated, the ceremonial title attached to the College of the Liberated in Sarvos. Venturo de Sarvos was appointed to the position.

Sarvos.t: The College of the Liberated, a great work in Sarvos, gained a Dean when Venturo de Sarvos was appointed to the title.

Appoint Feverwater Dredgemaster.d: This procedural Senate motion assigned a person to the position of Dredgemaster of Lake Feverwater, with the nomination falling to the Navarr senators. The position was a sinecure in Feverwater lake in Therunin, created by an earlier Senate motion that permitted the dredging of Feverwater. The election was a national one, run by the master of elections and involving only the Navarr senators. There was a single nominee, Corey Brackensong, who was appointed by unanimous decision of the Navarri senators.

Navarr.t: Navarr's senators held the right to nominate the Dredgemaster and unanimously chose Corey Brackensong, placing the new Feverwater sinecure in Navarri hands.

Appoint Feverwater Dredgemaster.o: In Spring 378YE the Navarr senators unanimously appointed Corey Brackensong as Dredgemaster of Lake Feverwater, a procedural appointment to the position created by an earlier motion permitting the dredging of Feverwater.

Therunin.t: Therunin's Lake Feverwater gained its first Dredgemaster, Corey Brackensong, to hold the sinecure created when the Senate permitted the lake's dredging.

Appoint Sumaah ambassador.d: The motion was raised at the last Senate session of the Autumn Equinox summit. Under the Senate's rules for elections, the vote was therefore held at the first session of the Winter Solstice 379YE. No candidate received enough support, and the title of Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic remained unfilled. With the Sumaah Embassy in Necropolis completed, the Senate was expected to have another opportunity to appoint an ambassador in Spring 380YE.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named, but the Sumaah Embassy that offers the next chance to fill the post stands in Necropolis, a Highguard territory.

Appoint Sumaah ambassador.o: In Autumn 379YE the Senate raised a motion, proposed by Miaren and seconded by Zenith, to appoint an Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic. When the election was held at the Winter Solstice no candidate won the Senate's backing, so the post stayed vacant.

Necropolis.t: The completed Sumaah Embassy in Necropolis was expected to give the Senate a fresh opportunity to appoint an ambassador in Spring 380YE.

Appoint Throne IV.d: Proposed by Upwold and seconded by Therunin, the motion sought to elect an Imperial Citizen to the Throne. Three nominees stood: Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason, Senator for Sermersuaq; General Vanhe Korppi of the Fist of the Mountain; and Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, the Conscience of the Senate. The campaign ended without a result because no single candidate gained sufficient votes, so the Throne remained unfilled after this attempt.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Senator for Sermersuaq, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason, stood for the Throne but did not win enough votes to be elected.

Appoint Throne IV.o: In Autumn 379YE the Senate attempted to elect a new Throne, but no single candidate received enough votes and no one was appointed.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory's senator, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason, was one of the three nominees for the Throne.

Appoint Throne V.d: The motion sought to elect a citizen to the Throne. Four nominees stood: Lisabetta von Holberg; Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason, Senator for Sermersuaq; Cyrus son of Felix, of Felix's Watch, the Imperial Magus; and Olle Markusson, Senator for Kallavesa. The campaign ended with Lisabetta von Holberg elected to the Throne, and the motion was afterwards ratified by Empress Lisabetta herself in Spring 380YE.

Wintermark.t: Two of Wintermark's senators, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason and Olle Markusson, stood for the Throne but lost to Lisabetta von Holberg.

Appoint Throne V.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate held an election for the Throne, proposed by Volodmartz and seconded by Therunin, and Lisabetta von Holberg was elected Empress.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa's senator, Olle Markusson, was nominated for the Throne but was not elected.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq's senator, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason, was nominated for the Throne but was not elected.

Appoint Thule Ambassador.d: The motion elected an Imperial citizen as ambassador to the Thule, empowered to deal with them on behalf of the Empire. The recorded outcome is that Juha, the Cave Spider was appointed as ambassador, described as Ambassador to Otkodov, the territory then held by the Thule. The page gives no further detail on the ambassador's instructions or on any negotiations that followed.

Thule.t: The Thule now had a named Imperial representative, Juha, the Cave Spider, authorised to treat with them on the Empire's behalf.

Appoint Thule Ambassador.o: In Spring 381YE the Senate passed an administrative motion creating the post of Imperial ambassador to the Thule, and Juha, the Cave Spider was appointed to it.

Otkodov.t: Juha, the Cave Spider was appointed Ambassador to Otkodov, the Thule-held territory with which the Empire now had a formal envoy.

Appraisal of Feni dispersion.d: The motion sought a civil service appraisal of what it would cost to deal with the Woods-that-Fell Feni, who were causing disruption in northern Hercynia, either by dispersing them or arresting them using the militia or private citizens. It was proposed by Hercynia and seconded by Hahnmark. Only one appraisal may be commissioned each season. The motion failed, so no appraisal was made and the Senate was given no costed option for removing the Feni by these means.

Navarr.t: Navarr's senator for Hercynia brought the motion to get a costed plan for handling the Feni in Navarr-held land, but its failure left the nation with no Senate-backed appraisal of the problem.

Appraisal of Feni dispersion.o: In Winter 382YE the Senate considered a motion, proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Hahnmark, to have the civil service appraise the cost of using the militia or private citizens to disperse or arrest the northern Woods-that-Fell Feni in Hercynia. The motion failed.

Hercynia.t: The disruption caused by the Woods-that-Fell Feni in northern Hercynia remained without a costed plan to disperse or arrest them, because the appraisal motion failed.

Appraisal of integration of Mournwold Or.d: Proposed by the Senator for Mournwold and seconded by the Senator for Sarvos, the motion asked the civil service to appraise how the Mournwold Orcs might be integrated into the Marches. Only one appraisal may be carried out each season. The motion passed, and the civil service was to deliver its report to the Empire before the Summer Solstice 383YE. The Speaker noted that this was the second motion the Senator for Sarvos had seconded at that Equinox, and the matter was passed to the magistrates as a possible case of subverting the agencies of state.

The Marches.t: The appraisal examines how the orc thralls of the Mournwold might be brought into the Marcher nation, with findings due before the Summer Solstice.

Appraisal of integration of Mournwold Or.o: In Spring 383YE the Senate passed a motion commissioning a civil service appraisal into integrating the orc thralls of the Mournwold into the Marcher nation, with a report due before the Summer Solstice.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold's senator proposed the appraisal, which focuses on the future of the territory's orc thralls and their integration into the Marches.

Appraise Sign of Tamar.d: Proposed by the senator for Weirwater and seconded by the senator for Sarvos, the motion directed Graciana i Lopez i Guerra to carry out the appraisal. It asked two questions: how the Sign of Tamar could be kept from being swallowed by the encroaching forest, and what uses the Empire could make of it once it was preserved. The motion passed, and the appraisal was due to be delivered before the Winter Solstice. The motion itself committed no work or resources to preserving the site. It only commissioned the study.

Highguard.t: Highguard held Reikos at the time, so this appraisal concerned a site within Highborn-held land whose preservation and future use the Senate had chosen to investigate.

Appraise Sign of Tamar.o: In Autumn 383YE the Senate passed a motion to appraise how the Sign of Tamar in Tamarbode, Reikos, might be saved from being reclaimed by the forest, and how the Empire might use it once preserved.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Tamarbode is home to the Sign of Tamar, which faced being reclaimed by the forest. The appraisal was commissioned to find ways to save it and put it to Imperial use.

Reikos.t: The Senate commissioned a study into preserving the Sign of Tamar in Reikos from the forest and making use of it for the Empire, with the report due before the Winter Solstice.

Archive:376YE Winter Solstice Imperial t.d: Each Imperial territory's senator and each army's general were listed. League bishops took four cardinalships (Ambition, Loyalty, Prosperity and The Way), and Gralka of the Imperial Orcs became Conscience of the Senate. Six archmagi were declared, and the order grandmasters were to serve with fixed voting strengths until the Spring Equinox 377YE. Because of concerns about economic stability in a time of Imperial crisis, Bourse seats won at this summit were to run until Winter 377YE. The Brilliant Shore, the Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund were held by Thule and the Druj and would not be auctioned until their territories were Imperial again.

Dawn.t: Dawn's three senators were listed, along with Generals Floree de Rondell, Eryk Rykker and Frederick Novarion of the Hounds of Glory, Golden Sun and Eastern Sky.

Druj.t: The Druj held the Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund, and neither would be auctioned until Reikos and Holberg were Imperial again.

Highguard.t: Highguard's senators and Generals Matthias and Ruth were listed, alongside gatekeepers Asher (Courage) and Abraham (Vigilance), Grandmaster Jessica of the Sevenfold Path and Obediah holding the Vigilant Swan.

Imperial Orcs.t: Generals Klor of the Winter Sun and Braka of the Summer Storm sat on the Military Council, and Gralka was appointed Conscience of the Senate.

Navarr.t: Alongside its senators and two generals, Navarr provided the Cardinals of Courage and Wisdom, the Pride gatekeeper, Grandmaster Meir Pathfinder of the Rod and Shield and the holder of the Thimble.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn senators were listed, with Madruga's seat later proxied by Yalda i Ezmara i Erigo. Generals Yasmina and Deigo were also listed, and Darius i Esmara i Erigo became gatekeeper of the Prosperity Assembly.

The League.t: The League dominated the Synod with four cardinalships and held many Imperial Bourse seats, the Regario Dossier and the Mastery of the Imperial Mint. Its senators and General Stanislav Krieger of the Wolves of War were also listed.

The Marches.t: Marcher Langdon Tor became Cardinal of Pride, and Silent John and Alan Young were made gatekeepers. William Bolholt led the Golden Pyramid with a voting strength of 76, and the Marches' senators and three generals were listed.

Thule.t: Thule held the Brilliant Shore, which would not be auctioned until Skarsind was once again an Imperial territory.

Urizen.t: Urizen's three senators were listed, along with General Decius Cascade of the Citadel Guard and Valerion of Phoenix Reach, who held the Legacy.

Archive:377YE Autumn Equinox Imperial ti.d: The record lists every senator, general, cardinal, gatekeeper, archmage, grandmaster and Bourse holder after the Autumn Equinox. Several seats changed hands: senators were claimed in Casinea, Tassato, Morrow and Volodmartz, and new generals took the Fire of the South, Winter Sun, Wolves of War and Quiet Step. Septima of Shatterspire died, leaving the Warmage vacant until elections at the Winter Solstice. Bourse seats were extended to Winter 377 amid the Imperial crisis. The Brilliant Shore was reclaimed from the Thule, but the Synod's General Assembly vetoed its allocation. The Vigilant Swan, the Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund remained in Druj hands.

Dawn.t: Dawn kept its three senators, with Ywain De Gauvain retaining Semmerholm, and General Frederick Novarion kept the Eastern Sky. Agnetha De Rondell was appointed Cardinal of Wisdom and Maurice de Gauvain was declared Archmage of Autumn.

Druj.t: The Druj held the Great Forest at Reikos, the Great Pits of Ennerlund and the Vigilant Swan, none of which will be auctioned while they remain in orc hands.

Highguard.t: Zephram of Cantiarch's Hold claimed the Casinea seat, and Highguard took four of the eight cardinalships, with Asher at Courage, Samson at Pride and Jared at Loyalty. The nation lost the Vigilant Swan to the Druj with the fall of Reikos.

Imperial Orcs.t: Bloodcrow Martok replaced Klor as general of the Winter Sun, a change marked as yet to be confirmed, and Braka kept the Summer Storm. Stormcrow Gralka remained Conscience of the Senate, Kessek served as Advisor on Orc Affairs and Bruk held the Steel Fist.

Navarr.t: Caerwyn Summer Crow kept Therunin and General Cerunnos kept the Black Thorns, while Gwai replaced Kale Vigil at the Quiet Step. Hywel Summercrow became Gatekeeper of the Wisdom Assembly and Meir Pathfinder led the Rod and Shield with a voting strength of 22.

The Brass Coast.t: Rauul i Jannat i Requiza kept Kahraman, and Anwar i Covas i Erigo replaced Yasmina as general of the Fire of the South. Edmundo I Jannat I Riqueza became Grandmaster of the Golden Pyramid, and Tabib i Eldaha i Riqueza held the Broken Shore Bounty.

The League.t: Cesare claimed the Tassato seat and Gabriel Barossa replaced Stanislav Krieger at the Wolves of War. Ynez became Cardinal of Prosperity alongside Olek and Bishop Antonnio Vanzetti, and League citizens held many Bourse seats as well as the Regario Dossier and the Imperial Mint.

The Marches.t: Henry Ward retained Upwold and General William Tanner kept the Bounders, and Friar Alan Young stayed Gatekeeper of Loyalty. The Marcher William Bolholt lost the Golden Pyramid grandmastership.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Brilliant Shore is noted as having been reclaimed from the Thule.

Urizen.t: Lucius of Quicksilver Spire claimed Morrow from Ioseph, and Hector kept Zenith after his re-election, protecting him from revocation for now. Darius of Auric Horizon replaced Callisius Quicksilver as Archmage of Day, and Valerian of Phoenix Reach held the Legacy.

Varushka.t: Valentin Ivarovich Severy claimed Volodmartz from Maxim, and Petra Petrivna Melikov remained Cardinal of Vigilance. Dimitri Ivanovich Ionescu took the Shuttered Lantern with a strength of 35, Alexei led the Unfettered Mind and Simargl remained Dean of the Lyceum.

Wintermark.t: Hengest Dun retained Hahnmark and Triva of Tyrshalt was listed as Senator for Skarsind, with that seat next up at the Spring Equinox 378YE. Wyrda Bjornadottir was replaced as Grandmaster of the Shuttered Lantern, and Joakim held the Stonefield Ice Caves.

Archive:377YE Spring Equinox Imperial ti.d: Each nation's senators and generals were recorded. Senator Hector of Zenith had been revoked by the Synod but was re-elected, so he cannot be revoked again until his seat next falls due. Gralka served as Conscience of the Senate and Septima of Shatterspire was appointed Warmage. New cardinals were appointed for Ambition, Courage, Pride and Vigilance. Six archmagi and six grandmasters, with their voting strengths, were named, and Simargl became Dean of the Lyceum. Imperial Bourse seats gained at Winter 376YE run until Winter 377YE. The Brilliant Shore, the Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund remain in Thule or Druj hands and will not be auctioned until those territories are reclaimed.

Dawn.t: Dawn's senators were Bohemond De Rondell (proxied), Ywain De Gauvain and Marek, and its generals were Floree de Rondell, Eryk Rykker and Frederick Novarion. Josephine became Cardinal of Pride and Agnetha de Rondell became Gatekeeper of Wisdom.

Druj.t: The Druj held the Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund, which will not be auctioned as Bourse seats until Reikos and Holberg are Imperial again.

Highguard.t: Highguard held three senatorships and two generalships, under Matthias and Ruth. Lazarus became Cardinal of Courage, Asher and Silas became gatekeepers, Jessica was Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path and Obadiah held the Vigilant Swan.

Imperial Orcs.t: The orc Gralka remained Conscience of the Senate. Klor and Braka led the Winter Sun and Summer Storm, and Bruk held the Steel Fist.

Navarr.t: Navarr's senators were Cei Windstrider, Bledri Eternal and Caerwyn Summer Crow, and Cerunnos and Kale Vigil were its generals. Tockryn Nighthaven remained Cardinal of Wisdom, Meir Pathfinder led the Rod and Shield and Idris Eternal held the Thimble.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn senators were Sallur, Rauul and Avisena, and Yasmina and Deigo were the generals. Darius remained Gatekeeper of Prosperity and Tabib held the Broken Shore Bounty.

The League.t: The League held three senatorships, Stanislav Krieger's Wolves of War and four cardinalships, with Olek newly made Cardinal of Ambition. Leaguers also held many Imperial Bourse seats, the Regario Dossier and the post of Master of the Imperial Mint.

The Marches.t: The Marches' senators were Richard of Bourholt, Bridget Talbot and Henry Ward, and Bjorn, Edwin de Warrene and William Tanner were its generals. Alan Young's status as Gatekeeper of Loyalty was unresolved, and William Bolholt was Grandmaster of the Golden Pyramid.

Thule.t: The Thule held the Brilliant Shore, which will not be auctioned until Skarsind is an Imperial territory again.

Urizen.t: Urizen's senators were Ioseph, Probus and Hector, who was re-elected after the Synod revoked him. Decius Cascade led the Citadel Guard and Valerian of Phoenix Reach held the Legacy.

Varushka.t: Varushka's senators were Constantin, Yelislaveta and Maxim, and Zakhar the grim and Stanislav Borodin Havel were its generals. Petra became Cardinal of Vigilance, Alexei led the Unfettered Mind and Simargl became Dean of the Lyceum.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's senators were Hengest Dun, Uskolli and Atte, and Merrick and Erkenbrand were its generals. Wyrda Bjornadottir was Grandmaster of the Shuttered Lantern and Joakim held the Stonefield Ice Caves.

Archive:377YE Summer Solstice Imperial t.d: Several Senate seats changed hands. Lady Adia took Weirwater and Gideon took Bastion. In Hercynia, Rhain replaced Cei Windstrider, whom the Navarr National Assembly had revoked. Hector kept Zenith after being revoked by the Synod and re-elected. New generals included Estana, Skayde, Richard Talbot, Tanwyn Ankarien, Olaf Gregorson and Vahne, and Septima of Shatterspire became Warmage. In the Synod, Jared, Epaph and Agnetha De Rondell became Cardinals of Loyalty, Pride and Wisdom, and six Archmagi were declared. White Granite Bourse seats were not re-elected because of concerns over economic stability in a time of crisis. Seats in Druj- and Thule-held lands were withheld from auction.

Dawn.t: Lady Adia of House Arwood claimed Weirwater's Senate seat from Marek, and Skayde replaced Eryk Rykker as general of the Golden Sun. Agnetha De Rondell became Cardinal of Wisdom and Maurice de Gauvain was declared Archmage of Autumn.

The Brass Coast.t: Sallur kept Feroz's seat, and Estana replaced Yasmina as general of the Red Wind Corsairs. Yasmina was listed as taking the Fire of the South from Deigo, pending confirmation.

The League.t: Mirislav kept Sarvos and League clergy held three Cardinalates: Ambition, Prosperity and The Way. League merchants held many Imperial Bourse seats, along with the Regario Dossier and the Mint.

The Marches.t: Richard Talbot replaced Bjorn as general of the Drakes. Friar Alan Young remained Gatekeeper of Loyalty and William Bolholt was Grandmaster of the Golden Pyramid.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule held the Brilliant Shore, which would not be auctioned until Skarsind was Imperial again.

Urizen.t: Hector kept Zenith despite his Spring revocation and could not be revoked again before the next normal election, while Probus kept Redoubt. Tanwyn Ankarien replaced Decius Cascade at the Citadel Guard and Cyrus Cascade became Gatekeeper of Courage.

Varushka.t: Constantin kept Karov, and Olaf Gregorson Strascovichlaf replaced Zakhar 'the grim' as general of the Northern Eagle. Petra Petrivna Melikov remained Cardinal of Vigilance and Simargl was appointed Dean of the Lyceum.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark National Assembly revoked General Merrick in his absence, and Vahne replaced him at the Green Shield. Atte kept Sermersuaq, Erkenbrand kept the Fist of the Mountain and Wyrda Bjornadottir was Grandmaster of the Shuttered Lantern.

Archive:378YE Autumn Equinox Imperial ti.d: The record listed senators for each Imperial territory, the generals of every Imperial army, the cardinals and gatekeepers of the virtue assemblies, the six archmagi and the grandmasters of the Conclave's orders, and the holders of Imperial and national Bourse seats with their winning bids. Other offices included Gideon of the Suns of Couros as Conscience of the Senate, Sendero i Hazana i Guerra as Admiral and Vaan of Auric Horizon as Warmage. The Senate selected Syn Nighthaven as Wisest Senator. The Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund were held by the Druj and would not be auctioned until those territories were Imperial again.

Dawn.t: Dawn's senators were Bohemond De Rondell, Escalados deCarsenere and Valentin Ivarovich Orzel. Its generals led the Hounds of Glory, Golden Sun and Eastern Sky, and Agnetha and Tancred De Rondell held Synod seats in Wisdom and Loyalty.

Druj.t: The Druj held the Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund, so neither Bourse seat would be auctioned until Reikos and Holberg were Imperial territories again.

Highguard.t: Highguard had three senators and three generals, including those of the Seventh Wave, Granite Pillar and Valiant Pegasus. Its citizens held the Courage, Loyalty and Pride cardinalships, two gatekeeper roles and the grandmastership of the Order of the Sevenfold Path.

Imperial Orcs.t: Generals Bloodcrow Martok and Braka led the Winter Sun and Summer Storm. Irontide Bruc was Advisor on Orc Affairs, Irontide Rad was Quartermaster General and Irontide Vio held the Steel Fist.

Navarr.t: Navarr's senators were Rhain, Syn Nighthaven, who was also chosen as Wisest Senator, and Caerwyn Summer Crow. Its generals led the Black Thorns and Quiet Step, Meir Pathfinder led the Order of the Rod and Shield, and Idris Eternal held the Thimble.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast had four senators and two generals, of the Red Wind Corsairs and the Fire of the South. Sendero i Hazana i Guerra was Admiral and Edmundo I Jannat I Riqueza led the Order of the Golden Pyramid, and several Freeborn held mercantile posts and sinecures.

The League.t: The League's senators were Mirislav, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato and Drogon Morosini, and Gabriel Barossa commanded the Wolves of War. Leaguers held the Ambition and Prosperity cardinalships, the Conclave bursar and Senate liaison roles, and many Bourse seats.

The Marches.t: The Marches had senators Orrick, Bridget Eastville and Henry Ward. Its generals Furious Fin, Jack Flint and Brianna of King's Stoke led the Drakes, Strong Reeds and Bounders.

Urizen.t: Urizen's senators were Ariadne, Marissa Shatterspire and Cato, and Tanwyn Ankarien led the Citadel Guard. Livia Cascade was Gatekeeper of Wisdom, Solas was High Exorcist and Sibella held the Legacy.

Varushka.t: Varushka had senators Constantin, Radomir and Irina Kardaova Arkady, and generals of the Northern Eagle and Golden Axe. Varushkans also held the Auditor of Senatorial Accountability, the Imperial Inquisitor, the Dean of the Lyceum, the grandmastership of the Shuttered Lantern and two national Bourse seats.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's four senators were Hengest Dun, Uskolli, Atte and Jorma Steelhail. Its generals Vahne and Erkenbrand of Tyrsholm led the Green Shield and Fist of the Mountain, and Wintermarkers held the Stonefield Ice Caves, the Brilliant Shore and the trade envoy post to the Sumaah Republic.

Archive:378YE Spring Equinox Imperial ti.d: The list named the senators for each territory, Senate appointees such as the Conscience of the Senate, Gideon, and the sinecure holders. It also named the Military Council's generals, the Warmage Vaan of Auric Horizon and the Quartermaster General. The Synod's cardinals and gatekeepers, the High Exorcist and the Auditor of Senatorial Accountability appeared, as did the six Archmagi and the Grandmasters of the Orders. Bourse seats were listed with their winning bids. New generals took command of the Fire of the South, the Winter Sun, the Wolves of War and the Quiet Step. The Mitwold Senate seat was vacant. The Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund remained in Druj hands and would not be auctioned until those territories were Imperial again.

Dawn.t: Dawn's senators were Bohemond De Rondell, Ywain De Gauvain and Lady Adia of House Arwood, and its generals were Floree de Rondell, Clarence Oswald and Frederick Novarion. Dawn also held the Vigilance and Wisdom cardinalships, and Maurice de Gauvain was Archmage of Autumn.

Druj.t: The Druj were recorded as holding the Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund, which would not be auctioned while those territories remained in their hands.

Highguard.t: Highguard's senators were Solomon, Zephram and Adamah, and its generals were Matthias, Ruth and Tyrus. Highguard also held the Courage, Loyalty and Pride cardinalships, and Gideon of the Suns of Couros was Conscience of the Senate.

Imperial Orcs.t: General Bloodcrow Martok replaced Klor as commander of the Winter Sun, and Braka continued to lead the Summer Storm. The Steel Fist was held by Irontide Vio.

Navarr.t: Navarr's senators were Rhain, Rhys and Caerwyn Summer Crow, and General Gwai replaced Kale Vigil in command of the Quiet Step. Meurig Tystwarden remained Gatekeeper of the Pride Assembly, and Meir Pathfinder was Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast's three senators were listed, and General Anwar i Covas i Erigo replaced Yasmina i Ezmara i Erigo at the head of the Fire of the South. Freeborn also held the Prosperity gatekeepership and the Grandmastery of the Golden Pyramid.

The League.t: The League's senators were Mirislav, Cesare Sanguineo and Drogon Morosini, and General Gabriel Barossa replaced Stanislav Krieger in command of the Wolves of War. League citizens also held the Prosperity cardinalship, the post of Quartermaster General and many Bourse seats.

The Marches.t: The Marcher senators were Orrick for Bregasland and Henry Ward for Upwold, while the Mitwold seat stood vacant. Its generals were Richard Talbot, Jack Flint and William Tanner.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule is not named; its only link is Karsk, which it held, though the page still listed a senator for Karsk among Varushka's senators.

Urizen.t: Urizen's senators were Lucius, Probus and Cato, and General Tanwyn Ankarien led the Citadel Guard. Urizeni also held the Courage and Wisdom gatekeeperships, the post of High Exorcist and the Legacy.

Varushka.t: Varushka's senators were listed for Karsk, Karov, Miekarova and Volodmartz, and its generals were Olaf Gregorson Strascovich and Stanislav Borodin Havel. Varushkans also served as Auditor of Senatorial Accountability, Dean of the Lyceum and Grandmasters of two Orders.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's four senators were listed, and its generals were Vahne and Erkenbrand of Tyrsholm. Eofric Sammersund Miksa was Cardinal of Ambition, and Wintermark held the Stonefield Ice Caves and the Brilliant Shore.

Archive:379YE Autumn Equinox Imperial ti.d: The roster named the senators for each territory, the generals of every Imperial army, the cardinals, gatekeepers and virtue inquisitors of the Synod, the Conclave's archmagi and grandmasters, and the holders of Imperial, national and minor Bourse positions. Several posts stood vacant, including the Imperial Master of Works, the Minister of Historical Research, the Admiral and the Virtue Inquisitor of Prosperity. The Great Forest at Reikos and the Vigilant Swan were back under Imperial control and awaited Senate allocation. The Great Pits of Ennerlund were being repaired and could be allocated now that Holberg was Imperial again. The Legacy remained in Grendel hands until Spiral was retaken.

Dawn.t: Dawn held the Senate seats of Astolat, Semmerholm and Weirwater and fielded three generals: Tancred de Rondell, Starac Sijed Orzel and Richard Vandale. Its nobles also held the cardinalships of Pride and Wisdom and the Archmage of Autumn's seat through Maurice de Gauvain.

Grendel.t: The Grendel held Spiral and with it the Bourse seat of the Legacy, which could not be allocated until the territory was Imperial once more.

Highguard.t: Highguard's senators Solomon, Zephram and Adamah sat for Bastion, Casinea and Necropolis. Generals Cuth, Mathayus and Jericho led its armies, and Highborn held the cardinalships of Courage, Loyalty and Vigilance as well as the post of Imperial Magus.

Imperial Orcs.t: Morgur Bloodcrow commanded the Winter Sun and Irontide Skar the Summer Storm, while Irontide Kul held the national Bourse seat of the Steel Fist.

Navarr.t: Navarr's senators were Rhain, Llewellyn Leafstalker and Caerwyn Summer Crow, and its generals were Carr Foxden of the Black Thorns and Merryn Farkas of the Quiet Step. Hywel Summercrow served as Chaplain Consular and Idris Eternal held the Thimble.

The League.t: The League sat four senators, including Rossalyn Jordan for a newly restored Holberg, and General Gabriel Barossa led the Wolves of War. Leaguers held the Conscience of the Senate, the Imperial Inquisitor's post, the Ambition cardinalship and the Master of the Imperial Mint.

Urizen.t: Urizen's senators were Ariadne, Probus and Cato, and General Nicassia Avicia led the Citadel Guard. Urizeni also held the post of High Exorcist and the gatekeeperships of Loyalty and Wisdom.

Varushka.t: Varushka sat four senators and fielded generals Valentin Brossa of the Northern Eagle and Magnus Anatolyvich Prochnost of the Golden Axe. Its people also held the Eternal Shafts of Time, the Granites of Veltsgorsk and the post of Dean of the Lyceum.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's senators sat for Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq, and Generals Marius Fjellrevening and Vanhe Korppi led its armies. Its people also held the cardinalships of Prosperity and the Way, the post of Imperial Consul and two national Bourse seats.

The Imperial and national Bourse seats were listed with their holders and, where recorded, the price paid in thrones. Two seats were not allocated. The Great Forest at Reikos remained in Druj hands and would not be auctioned until Reikos was Imperial again. The Great Pits of Ennerlund needed repair before allocation, now that Holberg was once more an Imperial territory.

Archive:380YE Autumn Equinox Imperial ti.d: The list named the senators for each territory, the generals of every national army, the Synod's cardinals, gatekeepers and inquisitors, the Archmagi and Grandmasters of the Conclave, and the holders of Imperial and national Bourse seats, commissions and sinecures. Several gaps stood out. The Great Mine of Briante was vacant and due to be auctioned at the Winter Solstice for a reduced term, and the Pride of Ikka's Tears was due to be elected then. The Singing Caves were back in Imperial control and awaited allocation by the Senate. The Damatian Cliffs were held by the Jotun and the Stonefield Ice Caves by the Thule. The Sheriff of Overton post was vacant after the town's loss and recovery, and the Gatekeeper of Wisdom was also vacant.

Archive:380YE Spring Equinox Imperial ti.d: The record lists the Empress, every territorial senator, Senate appointees, commissioners and sinecures, the generals of each nation's armies, the Synod's cardinals, gatekeepers and virtue inquisitors, the Conclave's archmagi and grandmasters, and the Bourse seats with their winning bids. It notes that Senator Dušan of Miekarova was revoked by the Synod but re-elected. The Civilian Commissioners of Urizen and Wintermark, the Dean of Pilgrims and the Imperial Fleet Master were vacant. The Great Pits of Ennerlund were being repaired, with mithril expected shortly after the Summer Solstice. The Great Forest at Reikos was due for auction at that Solstice. The Legacy was held by the Grendel, and the Stonefield Ice Caves by the Thule.

Archive:380YE Winter Solstice Imperial t.d: The list names the senator for every Imperial territory, along with Senate appointments such as the Conscience of the Senate, Ingrid Sigeing, and ambassadors to foreign nations. It notes that the Senate abrogated the Civilian Commissioners at this Solstice, so those titles no longer exist. It records each nation's generals; the General of the Gryphon's Pride post was vacant after Soldier Akella died at the Solstice, and the Imperial Fleet Master post was also vacant. It also lists the Synod's cardinals and other religious posts, the six Archmagi and Grandmasters, and Bourse seats. The Damatian Cliffs were back under Imperial control and awaited allocation by the Senate.

Dawn.t: Dawn held three Senate seats and several titles, including Cardinal of Wisdom Agnetha de Rondell and Warmage Barthol de Rondell. Its army the Gryphon's Pride was left without a general after Soldier Akella died at the Winter Solstice.

The League.t: The League held the Throne through Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, four Senate seats and four cardinalships. Its citizens held numerous Bourse seats, including the Great Pits of Ennerlund and the Master of the Imperial Mint.

The Marches.t: The Marches held three Senate seats and four generalships. Robert Shanks served as Operator of Brock's Toll, and Tobias Shanks held the Fortress of Salt.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Stonefield Ice Caves of Wintermark are noted as held by the Thule.

Urizen.t: Urizen held four Senate seats and a single general, Nicassia Avicia of the Citadel Guard. Its people also held posts including High Exorcist Solas and Cardinal of Courage Levitia of Endsmeet.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark held three Senate seats and two generalships, and Ingrid Sigeing served as Conscience of the Senate. Its national Stonefield Ice Caves were recorded as held by the Thule.

It also listed Senate advisors, ambassadors, sinecures and ministries, and the generals of the Military Council. Varushka's Army of the Golden Axe had no general after the death of Volk Kunzetsov Strascovih, so his adjutant was carrying out the general's duties. The Synod section covered the cardinals, gatekeepers, virtue inquisitors and other religious posts. The Conclave section named the archmagi and grandmasters. The Bourse section gave seat holders with their bids, though the Damatian Cliffs awaited allocation. The Senate auctioned three Imperial wayleaves that season.

Dawn.t: Dawn held the senatorships of Astolat, Semmerholm and Weirwater, fielded four generals including Tancred de Rondell of the Hounds of Glory, and held the Ambition and Courage cardinalships.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page; it is linked only through Spiral, for which the record still lists a senator, Tanwyn Ankarien, among Urizen's seats.

Highguard.t: Highguard held four senatorships, three generals including Brother Lucifer of the Valiant Pegasus, the Wisdom cardinalship and numerous Synod and Conclave posts.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs held Skarsind's senatorship through Irontide Vio, the generalships of the Winter Sun and Summer Storm, and the Cardinal of the Way through Atla.

Navarr.t: Navarr held three senatorships, the Warmage post and the generalship of the Black Thorns, while the League of the Quiet Step was commanded by the Empress as Defender of the Empire.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast held all four of its senatorships and the generalships of the Red Wind Corsairs and Fire of the South, and Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra served as Imperial Fleet Master.

The League.t: The League provided the Empress, four senators and two generals, and held the Pride, Prosperity and Vigilance cardinalships.

The Marches.t: The Marches fielded four generals and held senators for Bregasland, Mitwold and Mournwold, but Upwold's seat stood vacant.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wintermark national Bourse seat of the Stonefield Ice Caves is recorded as held by the Thule.

Urizen.t: Urizen was listed with senators for Morrow, Redoubt and Spiral, and Nicassia Avicia of Phoenix Reach commanded the Citadel Guard.

Varushka.t: Varushka held four senatorships, three generals including Magnus Prochnost of the Iron Helms, and the post of High Bard of the Empire.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark held the senatorships of Hahnmark and Kallavesa, three generals including Lofyn Bloodcloak, and the Loyalty cardinalship, though its Stonefield Ice Caves seat was held by the Thule.

Archive:382YE Summer Solstice Imperial t.o: The record of Imperial titles at the Summer Solstice 382YE listed the holders of offices across the Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave and Bourse, with Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg of the League on the Throne.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Pits of Ennerlund Bourse seat is listed as held by Vasiliy Krenyenkov Valeskai Strascovich for 370 Thrones.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Bohemond de Rondell is listed as Senator for Astolat.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Sammual, of the Cohort of the Winter Bear, is listed as Senator for Bastion.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Orrick Bolholt is listed as Senator for Bregasland, and Bill of Middleton as Keeper of the Dour Fens.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Nira, of Cantiarch's Hold, is listed as Senator for Casinea.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza is listed as Senator for Feroz.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Hengest Dun is listed as Senator for Hahnmark.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Rhisiart Dancewalker is listed as Senator for Hercynia.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Caerwyn von Holberg of the Feasting Crow is listed as Senator for Holberg.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Qusay i Kalamar i Guerra is listed as Senator for Kahraman.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: Edythe Dunne is listed as Senator for Kallavesa.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Vuk the Wolfeater is listed as Senator for Karov.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: Maarit is listed as Senator for Karsk.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Adan i Del-Toro i Riqueza is listed as Senator for Madruga.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Llewellyn Leafstalker is listed as Senator for Miaren, and Tanwen Snowstep holds the Eternal Flame of Miaren sinecure.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: Father Nikolovich Drakov is listed as Senator for Miekarova.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: William Guildenstern is listed as Senator for Mitwold.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Ariadne of Auric Horizon is listed as Senator for Morrow.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Robert Dunlain is listed as Senator for Mournwold.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Jeconiah, of Raven's Watch, is listed as Senator for Necropolis.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Andronikos is listed as Senator for Redoubt.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Cadeus, of the Shattered Tower, is listed as Senator for Reikos, and Issachar holds the Great Forest at Reikos Bourse seat.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Magdelena Alagna di Sarvos is listed as Senator for Sarvos, and the Steward of the Sarvos Mana Exchange is listed as vacant.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra is listed as Senator for Segura.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Lady Ailliena Devereux is listed as Senator for Semmerholm.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Irontide Vio is listed as Senator for Skarsind, and the Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting is listed as vacant.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Tanwyn Ankarien is listed as Senator for Spiral among Urizen's senators, and Maryc of House Orzel is named Castellan of Spiral Castle.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato is listed as Senator for Tassato, and Edwin Rogerius Sanguineo as Steward of the Tassato Mana Exchange.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Giuseppe Sanguieno is listed as Senator for Temeschwar.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Cybi Farkas is listed as Senator for Therunin.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the senatorship of Upwold, the Silver Chase, is listed as vacant.

Volodmartz.t: Mentioned in passing: Alexei Volostra is listed as Senator for Volodmartz.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: Lady Eve Orzel is listed as Senator for Weirwater, and Rada holds the Weirwater Vales Bourse seat.

Archive:Paid Work Autumn Equinox 384YE.d: The page is a roster rather than an account of events. It sets out three unlabelled tables of citizens, each entry giving a name and an Imperial nation. Dawn, Highguard, the Imperial Orcs, Navarr, the Brass Coast, the League, the Marches, Urizen, Varushka and Wintermark all appear. The first table is dominated by Brass Coast and Navarr names. The second is overwhelmingly Navarr, with sizeable Dawn and Wintermark contingents. The third is a short list of a few Dawn, League, Marcher and Wintermark citizens. The page does not explain what distinguishes the three tables, nor what work was done or what was paid.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish citizens appear in all three tables of those who took paid work, including a sizeable group in the second.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named on the page; the only link is Zenith, which appears in the names of Urizen citizens.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn citizens are listed in the first and second tables, among them Lazarus of the Necropolis.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: a group of Imperial Orc citizens, including several Bloodcrows, appears in the first table only.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr citizens make up a large share of the first table and the great majority of the second.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Brass Coast citizens form the largest group in the first table, with one more listed in the second.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: League citizens, many styled after Sarvos, Temeschwar, Tassato or Holberg, appear in all three tables.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Marcher citizens are listed in all three tables, most numerously in the second.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen citizens are listed in the first and second tables, including two named as being of Zenith Ascendant.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan citizens appear in the first and second tables.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark citizens appear in all three tables, with many Dunning and Dunwolf names in the second.

Archive:Paid Work Autumn Equinox 384YE.o: This archive page recorded the citizens who took paid work at the Autumn Equinox 384YE, listing each by name and nation across three separate tables.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory appears only in the name of the Highborn citizen Lazarus of the Necropolis.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos appears only in the names of several League citizens, such as Achille di Sarvos.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar appears only in the names of several League citizens, such as Aleksei Dukov van Temeschwar.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Zenith appears only in the names of two Urizen citizens styled 'of Zenith Ascendant'.

Archive:Roll of Honour Spring Equinox 38.d: The roll lists each supporter's name, nation, home territory and banner against the force or operation they backed. Armies and fleets supported included the Argent Sword, Black Thorns, Boyar's Hasta, Citadel Guard, Drakes, Golden Axe, Granite Pillar, Northern Eagle, Red Wind Corsairs, Strong Reeds, Summer Storm, Wolves of War and the Will of the Wintermark. Spy networks were also supported: Defence of the Broch, the Forest of Ulnak and, most heavily, Tsirku. Fifty Wintermark citizens from Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq, among them many of Dunhearth Hall and the Shield Wolves, plus one Navarr, backed the Tsirku network. The Drakes and Black Thorns drew especially broad support.

Dawn.t: Dawn's nobles gave widespread support, above all to the Drakes, where House Orzel and House Mortére of Weirwater stood out, and to the Black Thorns. Others backed the Boyar's Hasta, Granite Pillar, Argent Sword, Red Wind Corsairs and Summer Storm.

Highguard.t: Highborn citizens backed the Drakes, among them members of The Steel Tide from Necropolis, as well as the Argent Sword, Granite Pillar, Summer Storm, Black Thorns and Northern Eagle. Silus of The Sentinels Tower supported the Forest of Ulnak spy network.

Imperial Orcs.t: Orcs of Mareave and Skarsind threw their weight behind the Summer Storm and the Argent Sword. Bands such as the Irontide, Bloodcrows, Sand Vipers, Pathfinders and Stonesworn were prominent among them.

Navarr.t: The Navarr overwhelmingly supported the Black Thorns, with many striders from Hercynia, Miaren and Brocéliande, and also backed the Argent Sword, Drakes, Boyar's Hasta and Summer Storm. Powell Open-Skies also aided the Tsirku spy network.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast citizens from Feroz, Kahraman, Madruga and Segura supported the Red Wind Corsairs, including members of the Bloodgold Jackals and Flames of the Coast.

The League.t: A handful of League citizens contributed. Two from Temeschwar backed the Argent Sword, Gunter Von Holberg supported the Drakes, and Pierra di Sarvos of the Crimson Reaper Cartel supported the Wolves of War.

The Marches.t: Marchers from Upwold, Mitwold, Mournwold and Bregasland mainly supported the Drakes, notably The Talbots, The Fire of the Marches and the Applewood Levy. Rowan Gotts backed the Strong Reeds and Bradwin Barlymaine the Red Wind Corsairs.

Urizen.t: Urizeni citizens supported the Argent Sword and the Citadel Guard, including members of the Scythe of The Sarangrave. Others backed the Summer Storm and the Red Wind Corsairs.

Varushka.t: Varushkan citizens backed the Drakes, largely through the Grimhold Guard, as well as the Argent Sword and Summer Storm. Kazimiera Radovna Suvretzska was the sole listed supporter of the Golden Axe.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark dominated the roll. Fifty of its citizens supported the Tsirku spy network, Siegfried Eofogar backed the Defence of the Broch network, and Mandrake Lightfoot supported the Will of the Wintermark. Many Dunhearth Hall members also backed the Drakes.

Archive:Roll of Honour Spring Equinox 38.o: The Roll of Honour for the Spring Equinox 388YE recorded the Imperial citizens who lent their support to armies, fleets and spy networks that season. It is notable for a large Wintermark effort behind a spy network in Tsirku.

Tsirku.t: Tsirku was the focus of the season's largest spy network effort, supported by fifty Wintermark citizens from Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq and one Navarr.

Archive:Roll of Honour Summer Solstice 3.d: The roll lists each contributing citizen with their nation, home territory and, where given, their banner. The largest entries were for the Citadel Guard and Eastern Sky, drawing heavily on Dawn, Highguard, Urizen, Varushka, Wintermark and the Imperial Orcs. Burning Falcon drew support across Wintermark, the Marches, the Brass Coast, Highguard, Dawn, Navarr and Varushka. More than two dozen citizens, nearly all Wintermark with two Varushkans, backed the Tsirku spy network. Smaller numbers supported the Forest of Ulnak spy network, the three Wintermark beacons, and Bounders, Drakes, Fire of the South, Golden Axe, Gryphon's Pride, Lions of Adelmar, Red Wind Corsairs, Sparrows Reckoning, Star Forged, Strong Reeds and Tusks.

Dawn.t: Many Dawnish nobles from Astolat, Semmerholm, the Barrens and Weirwater were honoured, chiefly for the Citadel Guard and Eastern Sky, alongside Burning Falcon, Gryphon's Pride, Lions of Adelmar, Golden Axe, Drakes and the Forest of Ulnak spy network.

Highguard.t: Highborn from Bastion, Casinea, Necropolis and Reikos were honoured for the Citadel Guard and Eastern Sky, including the Cohort of the Winter Bear and the Steel Tide, with a few from Reikos supporting Burning Falcon.

Imperial Orcs.t: Orcs from Mareave and Skarsind, among them Pathfinders, Sand Vipers, Stonesworn and Bloodcrows, were honoured for supporting Eastern Sky.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: a handful of Navarr from Therunin, Miaren, Hercynia and the Barrens are listed supporting Burning Falcon, the Citadel Guard and Golden Axe.

The Brass Coast.t: Citizens from Feroz, Kahraman, Segura and Madruga were honoured for Burning Falcon, Red Wind Corsairs, Star Forged, Fire of the South, Drakes and Eastern Sky.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: a few League citizens from Tassato, Sarvos and Temeschwar are listed supporting the Citadel Guard, Eastern Sky and Sparrows Reckoning.

The Marches.t: Marchers from Bregasland, Upwold, Mitwold and Mournwold were honoured, notably for Burning Falcon, alongside the Tusks, Strong Reeds, Bounders, Drakes, Eastern Sky and the Citadel Guard.

Urizen.t: Urizeni from Morrow, Redoubt, Zenith, Sarangrave and Spiral were honoured in numbers for the Citadel Guard and Eastern Sky, with Tropaion and Urizen, Whole prominent among the banners.

Varushka.t: Varushkans from Karov, Karsk, Miekarova, Ossium and Volodmartz were honoured for the Citadel Guard and Eastern Sky, with two from Ossium backing the Tsirku spy network and one Burning Falcon.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark dominated support for the Tsirku spy network and the Beacons of Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq, and many of its citizens were also honoured for Burning Falcon, Eastern Sky, Fire of the South and the Citadel Guard.

Archive:Roll of Honour Summer Solstice 3.o: The Roll of Honour for the Summer Solstice 388YE recorded the Imperial citizens who lent their support to named efforts that season, including the Tsirku spy network, the Beacons of Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq, and forces such as the Citadel Guard, Eastern Sky and Burning Falcon.

Tsirku.t: More than two dozen citizens, overwhelmingly from Wintermark's Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq with two from Varushka's Ossium, were honoured for supporting a spy network in Tsirku.

Arranging grace.d: The Court judged the manifesto 'elegant and concise' but ruled that the Maestro could represent the sodality, not lead it. Approval would move titles such as the High Bard of the Empire and the Dean of the First Voice Glade to election by the sodality. The Mistress of Monuments would follow unless the Senate redefined it around the inspirations. No existing powers would transfer automatically, and the sodality would be singular. The songbirds offered to fund the refinement of commissions. League princes and Highborn benefactors pledged grants to a patrons' fund. Some artists criticised the name. The Senate established the sodality with power to refine a commission and to preserve chosen artworks in First Voice Glade. It set a one-throne stipend, creating a Patron's Fund of five thrones a season.

Highguard.t: Highborn benefactors joined League merchant-princes in pledging three thrones a season to the sodality's fund and in matching any Senate stipend, provided grants were disbursed openly.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the walls of Damata are cited as an example of a historical commission the sodality might refine.

The League.t: League merchant-princes, led by Genia Bourné di Sarvos, pledged funding to the sodality. Diora University was named as a possible repository for honoured art, and il Volpe's League galleries and theatres were held up as a model of arts patronage.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the scops' halls of Kalpaheim were listed among possible central repositories for the sodality's honoured artworks.

Arranging grace.o: At Empress Vesna's request, the Civil Service and Magistrate Abraham appraised the constitutional implications of making the Cat's Graces, a proposed sodality for promoting the arts, an Imperial sodality, while several patron groups offered support if it were approved. The Senate later established the sodality.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: Mentioned in passing: the walls of Damata are cited as an example of a historical commission the sodality could refine.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the many basilicas of Bastion are cited as historical commissions the sodality could ask artists to refine.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim's scops' halls were suggested as a possible repository for the sodality's art, though First Voice Glade was ultimately chosen.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the walls of Damata are given as an example of a historical commission open to refinement by the sodality.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Genia Bourné di Sarvos, merchant-prince of the Bourné fashion house, acted as spokesperson for the patrons pledging funds to the sodality.

Arrows and clay.d: Entry required being the target of the Summer ritual Challenge the Iron Duke; ten covens cast it the previous season. Winners in the past year may not compete again. In the Challenge of the Black Web, challengers and one attendant each had thirty minutes to gather glowing lights from hedge-lined glades at Widowsglade while avoiding venomous spider heralds of Jaheris. One hit ended a challenger's attempt, and the top half by lights collected would win. In the Challenge of the Painted Gallery, Barien posed for artists, who then had until evening to create any form of art for judging by his heralds and Ralphine, Maestro of the Cat's Graces, with a grand prize for the favourite piece.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: five of the ten covens listed as having cast Challenge the Iron Duke last season were Dawnish.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Eternal Family, a Navarri coven, was listed among last season's casters of Challenge the Iron Duke.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Glass Mantle and the Tempest Flame, both Freeborn covens, were listed among last season's casters of Challenge the Iron Duke.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Prosperous Pigs, a Marcher coven, was listed among last season's casters of Challenge the Iron Duke.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Voices of the Unbound Storm, a Wintermark coven, was listed among last season's casters of Challenge the Iron Duke.

Arrows and clay.o: For the Autumn 388YE summit, the heralds of the Iron Duke issued two new challenges to Imperial citizens: a stealth contest among the spider heralds of Jaheris at Widowsglade in Weirmoor, and an art contest with Barien himself as the subject.

Weirwater/Weirmoor.t: Widowsglade in Weirmoor was the site of the stealth challenge, reached by a conjunction from the Sentinel Gate for up to a hundred people at 22:30 on Saturday.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater hosted the Challenge of the Black Web, with a conjunction opening to Widowsglade where challengers stalked glades patrolled by spider heralds of Jaheris.

As above, so below.d: The Door, the Stork, the Web and the Great Wyrm aligned around the Wanderer, the eye of change, which burned crimson in the sky. Out of season, the winter lights shone brighter than any mystic or volhov could remember. Magicians and others reported a distant chord, vertigo, dreams of history branching and merging, an overwhelming sense of interconnection, and ideas that challenged their deepest beliefs. During the equinox no new ritual effect could be improvised. Mastered rituals, Imperial lore, non-Imperial texts, messages to eternals and gifts to their realms still worked. Covens could draw on their bond for three rituals a day, and making enchantments or curses permanent needed less ilium.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule is not named, but the lights stretched across Karsk, part of which Thule held, as far as Crowslook.

Varushka.t: Varushkan volhov were among those astonished by lights brighter than any of them remembered, and Varushkan ritualists shared in the conjunction's limits on improvised magic and its strengthened coven bonds.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's mystics saw the winter lights blaze in autumn over Sermersuaq, brighter than they had ever known, and its ritualists felt the conjunction's effects on their magic.

As above, so below.o: Six days before the Autumn Equinox 378YE a once-in-a-lifetime Grand Conjunction began, filling the northern night sky with winter lights from Tanikipari in Sermersuaq to Crowslook in Karsk and unsettling magic across the Empire.

Karsk/Crowslook.t: Crowslook was named as the eastern limit of the region where the brilliant winter lights could be seen.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: Tanikipari was named as the western limit of the region where the winter lights blazed during the conjunction.

Karsk.t: Karsk marked the eastern edge of the spectacle, where the out-of-season winter lights coiled across the night sky as far as Crowslook.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq marked the western edge of the display, where the great winter lights shone over Tanikipari in autumn.

As it is when it was.d: A magnitude-50 Summer enchantment showed a glowing winged figure over Casinea, drawing complaints of waste and idolatry. Valasheim's forgemistress sought an apprentice from twelve runesmiths. Thornsong House was completed in Therunin, and its first Thornsinger was to choose a potion for research. The last trods were restored, and Liathaven's Wither the Seed curse was found to have ended. Senate-commissioned Journeymage Towers let the Wavewatchers contain Dho'uala. The Thule enchanted their forts in Imperial lands ahead of an ambassadorial meeting. Lashonar's feathers would carry letters to the Night realm. Conjunctions arose at Tilly's Howe and in the Choked Forest. Sanvar Isk was humiliated by Tassato's orphans.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: pessimistic Navarr note that Thornsong House would be moot if the Druj conquered Therunin, which seems very unlikely.

Highguard.t: Highborn in Casinea largely disliked the winged sky-figure, complaining of lost sleep and wasted mana. Some priests questioned whether it was idolatry and suggested the Imperial Censor consider a Conclave interdiction.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Thule fort of Crow's Keep, on Crow's Ridge in Skarsind, now burns night and day with a pale red-green flame.

Jotun.t: The curse on Liathaven, which they call Ashvale, has ended, and some vates suspect northern Jotun who heed Wise Rangara of helping the Feni. The Jotun will likely need their own plans to deal with the Feni and the reawakened vallorn.

Navarr.t: Thornsong House was completed, and Navarr herb garden owners would choose the first Thornsinger by Tally of the Votes. The trods were fully restored, but the curse their nation placed on Liathaven has been lifted.

The League.t: In Tassato, Sanvar Isk was fooled and fined after the Church of the Little Mother's orphans tricked him. League mountebanks are also being recruited into the Wavewatchers around the Semmerlak.

The Marches.t: Marchers left behind in Jotun-occupied Mournwold report disappearances and hooded figures near Tilly's Howe, where a conjunction was found. Marchers bordering Liathaven also suggested the Spymaster Bernard Dugdale rebuild a spy network there.

Thule.t: The Thule laid powerful enchantments on all their forts in Imperial regions: ice giants, pale flame, white wolves from Sorin's court and Autumn runes. This appeared to be a show of strength before talks with the Ambassador to Otkodov.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the nationwide efforts of the Urizen, overseen by the Doyen of the Spires, are listed as one of the Empire's colleges of magic.

Varushka.t: Volhov joined the new Wavewatchers with the Wise assembly's blessing, and the trods in Volodmartz and Karov had been restored. The wolves of Nadezhdikov have risen in Volodmartz, and Thule forts in Varushkan lands now bear striking enchantments.

Wintermark.t: Valasheim's forgemistress Ursula Starhammer invited twelve egregore-divined runesmiths to compete to become her apprentice. Meanwhile the Thule citadel in Sermersuaq's Silver Peaks has been reinforced by ice giants.

As it is when it was.o: A Wind of Fortune gathered mortal and uncertain magical happenings across the Empire as Autumn 386YE approached. They included a winged figure enchanted into Casinea's sky, the completion of Thornsong House, the restoration of the trods, the lifting of Liathaven's curse, the containment of Dho'uala and showy Thule enchantments on their forts.

Hahnmark/Valasmark.t: The Aflhal forge at Valasheim will host a challenge to choose Ursula Starhammer's new apprentice, reached by conjunction during the summit.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: The Thule fort of Krevsatyzmei is now attended by great white wolves from Sorin's court.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: Mentioned in passing: last summer's giant sky-miner over the Ore Hills, which Marchers treated as an excuse for a picnic, is cited as an earlier comparison.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: Flajajokep bears glowing Autumn runes, and unusual numbers of Autumn heralds attend its markets.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The garrison of the Citadel of Silver and Bone has been reinforced by ice giants.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Crow's Keep now burns night and day with a pale red-green flame.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr warn that if the Greenheart is triggered, vallornspawn could threaten Thornsong House and Peakedge Song.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr are urged to consider how Peakedge Song, along with Thornsong House, will be protected if the Greenheart is triggered.

Tromsa/Icewood.t: Mentioned in passing: it is not named on the page; the only link is the note about northern Jotun seeking Wise Rangara's counsel.

Casinea.t: A glowing winged figure resembling Umbar i Elba Stardo i Guerra appeared in the sky, clearest above Anvil, and faded over the season. It provoked complaints of noise, waste and possible idolatry.

Hahnmark.t: At Valasheim in Valasmark, the forge of the Aflhal sought a new apprentice through a conjunction challenge during the summit.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: its trods, rent by the Cold Sun's servants, are noted as having been restored at the Spring Equinox.

Karsk.t: The Thule fort of Krevsatyzmei in Krevsaty is now attended by great white wolves, apparently gifts from Sorin's court.

Liathaven.t: The Wither the Seed curse has ended, so humans and orcs there can bear children again. It also means nothing now holds the vallorn quiescent, and citizens suggested rebuilding an Imperial spy network.

Miaren.t: The trods torn apart by the Cold Sun's scions were repaired at the Summer Solstice, though some paths have shifted slightly.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: it is not named; the link is the Wavewatchers' recruitment of Varushkan volhov from around the Semmerlak.

Mournwold.t: A conjunction to Tilly's Howe in the Chalk Downs, contested with the Jotun, was found after reports of disappearances and robed figures near a dolmen. It appears to call for investigation and magic rather than violence.

Ossium.t: The Thule fort of Flajajokep in the Bonewood is covered in glowing Autumn runes, and heralds of two Autumn cities attend its markets.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are named as masters of Otkodov, and its Imperial ambassador Kindra Surefoot is due to meet the Thule Ambassador.

Sermersuaq.t: The Thule Citadel of Silver and Bone in the Silver Peaks has been reinforced by ice giants, presumably called from Cathan Canae.

Skarsind.t: The Thule fort of Crow's Keep on Crow's Ridge now burns night and day with a pale red-green flame.

Tassato.t: Sanvar Isk was tricked by the Church of the Little Mother's orphans, then fined and thrown out by a magistrate. The Church planned to meet interested parties at Anvil before he auctions access to the Loom of Spells.

The Semmerlak.t: The completed Journeymage Towers let the Wavewatchers counter the sovereign Dho'uala's threat to shipping. Dho'uala is still awake, and the lake's ilium and fish remain an open problem.

Therunin.t: Thornsong House, the college of herbalism, was completed, and its Thornsinger will direct a year-long potion research project. Navarr worry about protecting the house from the vallorn.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: it is not named; the closest link is the note that some northern Jotun seek Wise Rangara's counsel.

Volodmartz.t: The wolves of Nadezhdikov have risen in the Choked Forest near the Gardens of the Grim, and the Grim Gardener is responsible for soothing them. Its trods were also restored in Spring.

Asavean Factor.d: The Loyalty Assembly, which values the Asavean project above the grand construction in Bastion, could raise one of two competing year-long mandates. One would arrange a face-to-face meeting between a named individual and one of the six identified Asavean factions. The other would press the heralds of a named eternal for aid. Whichever wins forecloses the other path. The Senate might also commission an appraisal into how Loyal citizens could support the project, though its backing is uncertain and the choice of prognosticator would matter greatly. Through his herald Zand, Callidus offered white granite in exchange for items of profound significance, such as pilgrim shields, true liao, the liberty pact pen or even the Imperial Crown, negotiated through the Archmage of Autumn's plenipotentiary.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Asaveans' support for the Grendel in their war on the Empire is cited as a reason the Senate may be cool towards the project.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the grand construction in Bastion is referred to only as the project the Loyalty Assembly values less than anchoring the Way in Asavea.

Asavean Factor.o: In Summer 388YE the Loyalty Assembly, frustrated that only 34 of the 750 wains of white granite needed to Anchor the Way in Asavea had been delivered, sought new ways to advance the project. Several opportunities arose: two competing Synod mandates to find allies, a possible Senate appraisal, and an offer from the eternal Callidus.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Bastion is named as the site of the Empire's other grand construction, which the Loyalty Assembly ranks below its Asavean effort.

Ashes.d: The Golden Sun and Gryphon's Pride watched the Black Wind army in Saltmarsh but did not engage it, and the sept fled east across the Nameless River. At least thirty-five thousand Druj poured from the Nesustak Forest into Therunin. They slaughtered Navarr defenders, seized the Thimble and the Feverwater Docks, and burned the Holt of the Oak, where almost two thousand Great Forest Orcs and Navarr died. The Arrow Vipers destroyed the Sarangrave spy network. Navarr lost control of Therunin, which is now contested, and its senator lost their seat. The Rivers of Life curse risks rousing the vallorn. A battle opportunity at Tarn Bend offered the Empire a chance to shield fleeing refugees and stop the Sephals Cauldron poisoning the land.

Dawn.t: The Golden Sun and Gryphon's Pride held the Barrens without fighting the Black Wind, and earlier Dawnish senators had urged the Throne to veto the Rahvin treaty.

Druj.t: Seven Druj armies overran eastern Therunin with brutal efficiency, while the Arrow Vipers crushed Imperial spying in the Sarangrave. They now hold two regions of the territory and the captured Thimble and Feverwater Docks.

Navarr.t: The Navarr suffered terrible slaughter in Therunin and lost control of the territory and its Senate seat. Their survivors fled north to the Barrens, and the Holt of the Oak was lost alongside their Great Forest Orc allies.

Urizen.t: Urizen feared the Druj would press on into Lustri, where the fortification was far from complete. A Druj band also captured a Sunspire stargazer in Morrow, threatening the spire itself.

Ashes.o: In Summer 386YE the Black Wind sept crossed the Barrens without incident and withdrew into the Mallum. Meanwhile a vast Druj host of seven armies invaded Therunin, conquering Eastring and East Ashes, destroying the Holt of the Oak and the Sarangrave spy network, and laying the Rivers of Life curse over the territory.

Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest.t: Black Wind bands led their fleeing people north into the Ghul'thak Forest on their way to the Mallum.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: Seven Druj armies poured out of the Nesustak Forest to launch their invasion of Eastring.
