The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: The Great Forest Orcs offered sanctuary to fleeing refugees, and success at Tarn Bend would see the refugees reach the protection of the Heart of Peytaht.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: The Gryphon's Pride resupplied here. The region risked becoming Poisoned if the Sephals Cauldron's contents were poured into the Tarn.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: The Black Wind sept abandoned its homes in Murderdale to join its warriors and escape destruction.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: The Black Wind army camped in sodden Saltmarsh all season until the last refugees arrived, then crossed the Nameless River into the Mallum.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: The Karass remained in the Bleaks, and a Druj band with heralds of Surut marched on the Hollow Tree regio to claim it for the Charred Prince.

Therunin/East Ashes.t: East Ashes fell to the Druj, and the Feverwater Docks were captured after holding for four days. A few refugees escaped south to Zenith before an eerie silence fell.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Eastring's well-defended steadings were overwhelmed one after another, and their defenders were swiftly executed; the region is now under Druj control.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: Greenheart remains vallorn-held, and the Rivers of Life curse threatens to rouse the vallorn here as refugees flee its danger.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Flame Beetle burned the Holt of the Oak and the Druj are two fifths of the way to conquering the region. Tarn Bend offered a chance to halt them and stop the region being poisoned.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Peakedge Song remains in Navarr hands, but Druj forces were gathering to sweep up the Tarn Valley towards it.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: Sweetglades remains vallorn-held, and the vitality of the Rivers of Life curse risks rousing the vallorn here.

Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley.t: The Upper Tarn Valley is still held by the Navarr but lies in the path of the expected Druj advance up the Tarn Valley.

Zenith/Lustri.t: Urizen feared a Druj push into Lustri, whose fortification is incomplete, and the last survivors of the Sarangrave spy network emerged here.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: rumours of an arrangement protecting Therunin and Brocéliande from the Druj are clearly no longer true, at least for Therunin.

Forest of Ulnak.t: The fleeing Black Wind people were ushered north into the Forest of Ulnak as they left the Barrens for the Mallum.

Morrow.t: Druj raiders captured the stargazer Megaris and threatened to loot Sunspire, and the Advisor on the Vallorn was charged with stopping them.

Sarangrave.t: The invasion of Therunin was launched from the Sarangrave. There the Arrow Vipers and the Tower of the Skink garrison destroyed the Imperial spy network and ended Imperial exploration.

The Barrens.t: The Black Wind sept crossed the Barrens peacefully under the watch of two Dawnish armies. Afterwards the territory began receiving Navarr and Great Forest Orc refugees from Therunin, and Druj with heralds of Surut moved on the Hollow Tree.

Therunin.t: The Druj conquered Eastring and East Ashes, captured the Thimble and Feverwater Docks, and destroyed the Holt of the Oak. They laid the Rivers of Life curse across the land, leaving the territory contested and the vallorn stirring.

Zenith.t: About a hundred refugees fled from East Ashes into northern Zenith, and Urizen feared a Druj push south that has not yet come.

Assign Breadbasket Spring 383YE.d: The Keeper announced that because the Citadel Guard did not need the Bread Basket that season, and no other army was eligible or had asked for its help, its surplus and the prosperity it provides would go to Bregasland to ease its citizens' suffering. The surplus was welcomed by the inhabitants, but it made no material difference there. The Jotun invasion had not caused widespread famine. The Jotun were not destroying farms and instead wanted the Bregas to keep working them, albeit as thralls. The page notes that the Bread Basket could make a real difference only if a famine struck a Marcher territory, and that any such opportunity would be set out in a Wind of Fortune.

Jotun.t: The Jotun invaders were not destroying Bregas farms and wanted the conquered Bregas to keep working them as thralls. As a result, no famine arose for the Bread Basket to relieve.

The Marches.t: The Marchers' sacrifices were formally recognised by the Keeper's allocation. However, the surplus brought only welcome comfort, not material relief, because the occupied lands were not starving.

Assign Breadbasket Spring 383YE.o: In Spring 384YE the Keeper of the Breadbasket allocated the Bread Basket's surplus to the Marcher territory of Bregasland, in recognition of the sacrifices made by the Marchers and especially by Bregas farmers and citizens.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland received the Bread Basket's surplus to ease its citizens' suffering under the Jotun invasion. Its inhabitants welcomed it, but it changed little because there was no famine there.

Assign Spiral.d: The motion, proposed by Morrow and seconded by Mitwold, sought to assign Spiral to an Imperial nation. The Senate assigned the territory to Urizen. As a result, Spiral became a Urizen territory and elected its own Senator, gaining representation in the Senate.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page. Spiral, listed as held by Grendel that season, was assigned to Urizen.

Urizen.t: Urizen gained Spiral as one of its territories and with it a new Senator in the Imperial Senate.

Assign Spiral.o: In Summer 380YE the Imperial Senate passed a motion assigning the territory of Spiral to Urizen, after which Spiral elected a Senator.

Spiral.t: Spiral was formally assigned to the nation of Urizen and elected a Senator to represent it.

Assignment of Holberg.d: The motion that Holberg be allocated to the League was proposed by the senator for Semmerholm and seconded by the senator for Astolat. An alternative was put forward that Holberg instead be assigned to the Imperial Orcs. The Senate passed the motion in favour of the League by 19 votes to 11. As a result, Holberg was assigned to the League and gained the right to elect a Senator to represent it.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs were the subject of a rival proposal to receive Holberg, but the Senate voted against them, so the territory did not pass into orc hands.

The League.t: The League was awarded Holberg by 19 votes to 11, adding a territory to its lands and gaining the right to elect a Senator for it.

Assignment of Holberg.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate voted to allocate the territory of Holberg to the League, choosing it over an alternative proposal to assign it to the Imperial Orcs.

Holberg.t: Holberg was formally assigned to the League rather than the Imperial Orcs and became entitled to elect its own Senator.

Assignment of Karsk.d: Karsk was conquered after a heroic opportunity in the region of Lestasny, so the Senate had to decide which Imperial nation would take it. The procedural vote went 26 to 0 in favour of Varushka over the Imperial Orcs, and Karsk became part of Varushka. The Senate recorded that the hold was not secure. The Thule still controlled three of Karsk's seven regions, and losing a single further region would mean the Empire lost the territory.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs were the other nation put forward to receive Karsk but received no votes, so the territory went to Varushka.

Thule.t: The Thule lost Karsk as a territory but still held three of its seven regions, enough to threaten the Empire's grip on it.

Varushka.t: Varushka gained Karsk unanimously, 26 votes to 0, but took on a fragile territory that would be lost if a single further region fell.

Assignment of Karsk.o: In Spring 378YE the Senate held a procedural vote assigning the newly conquered territory of Karsk to an Imperial nation, and Varushka won it 26 votes to none over the Imperial Orcs.

Karsk/Lestasny.t: Lestasny was where the heroic opportunity took place that led to the conquest of Karsk.

Karsk.t: Karsk was formally made part of Varushka, though the Thule still held three of its seven regions and the Imperial claim remained precarious.

Assignment of Karsk II.d: Karsk had been retaken by Imperial forces during the Autumn of 378YE, and this motion before the Senate sought to assign the territory to one of the Imperial nations. It was proposed by Mitwold and seconded by Karov. As a result, Karsk became part of the nation of Varushka. The territory was noted to remain insecure, however, as the Thule still controlled three of its seven regions, leaving the reconquest incomplete.

Thule.t: The Thule lost Karsk to the Empire but still held three of its seven regions, keeping the territory insecure.

Varushka.t: Varushka gained Karsk as part of its nation following the Imperial reconquest, though the territory was not yet fully secure.

Assignment of Karsk II.o: In Winter 378YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Mitwold and seconded by Karov, allocating the reconquered territory of Karsk to an Imperial nation; Karsk became part of Varushka.

Karsk.t: Karsk was formally allocated to Varushka after its reconquest, but the Thule still controlled three of its seven regions.

Assignment of Mournwold.d: The motion to assign Mournwold to the Marches was proposed by the senator for Bregasland and seconded by the senator for Mitwold, and it passed. As a result Mournwold formally became part of the Marches, which meant the territory could elect a senator to represent it in the Senate.

The Marches.t: The Marches formally gained Mournwold as one of its territories, at the instigation of its own senators for Bregasland and Mitwold.

Assignment of Mournwold.o: In Autumn 381YE the Senate passed a motion assigning the territory of Mournwold to the Marches.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold was assigned to the Marches and could now elect its own senator.

Assignment of Ossium.d: The motion, proposed by Karov and seconded by Volomartz, sought to assign the territory of Ossium to Varushka, and it passed in Winter 382YE. As a result Ossium became a Varushkan territory and went on to appoint a Senator, giving it representation in the Imperial Senate as part of Varushka.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named in the motion, though Ossium was recorded as theirs that season; its assignment to Varushka treats it as an Imperial territory.

Varushka.t: Varushka gained Ossium as one of its territories, and the territory appointed a Senator to sit for it.

Assignment of Ossium.o: In Winter 382YE the Senate passed a motion assigning the territory of Ossium to the nation of Varushka.

Ossium.t: Ossium was formally assigned to Varushka by the Senate, became a Varushkan territory and appointed a Senator.

Assignment of Reikos.d: The motion to assign Reikos as an Imperial territory was proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by the senator for Casinea. It passed, and Reikos was assigned to Highguard. As a result, Reikos became entitled to elect its own senator to sit in the Imperial Senate.

Highguard.t: Highguard gained Reikos as one of its territories, with the motion proposed and seconded by the Highborn senators for Necropolis and Casinea.

Assignment of Reikos.o: In Winter 379YE the Senate passed a motion assigning Reikos as an Imperial territory under Highguard, allowing it to elect a senator.

Reikos.t: Reikos was formally assigned to Highguard as an Imperial territory and became able to elect a senator of its own.

Assignment of Segura.d: After a long military campaign, Segura was conquered and a motion was brought to assign it to the Brass Coast. The motion was proposed by the senator for Segura and seconded by the senator for Kahraman. As a result, Segura became part of the Brass Coast nation. The territory was noted to be far from secure, however: Lasambrian orcs still controlled three of its seven regions, and the loss of just one more region would mean the loss of Segura as an Imperial territory.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast gained Segura as a new territory, though its hold was precarious, with Lasambrian orcs still holding three of the seven regions.

Assignment of Segura.o: In Summer 378YE the Senate assigned the newly conquered territory of Segura to the Brass Coast, following an extended military campaign to take it.

Segura.t: Segura was formally assigned to the Brass Coast after its conquest, but it remained insecure, with Lasambrian orcs controlling three regions and the loss of one more threatening its Imperial status.

Assignment of Skarsind.d: In Autumn 377YE the Senate held a procedural vote on which Imperial nation should receive the newly conquered territory of Skarsind. The motion assigned it to Wintermark and passed unanimously. As a result, Skarsind formally became part of the nation of Wintermark.

Thule.t: Skarsind, recorded as held by the Thule that season, was formally treated as conquered land and assigned to an Imperial nation, confirming that the territory had passed out of Thule hands.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark received Skarsind by unanimous Senate vote, adding the conquered territory to its lands.

Assignment of Skarsind.o: The Senate assigned the conquered territory of Skarsind to the nation of Wintermark in Autumn 377YE, in a procedural vote that passed unanimously.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind was formally assigned to Wintermark as conquered territory and became part of that nation.

Assignment of Skarsind II.d: The motion allocated Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs, making it their territory and entitling it to elect a Senator. Skarsind ceased to be a Wintermark territory, with significant implications for any Winterfolk still living there. Constitutionally, a method was settled by which the Imperial Orcs appoint a senator, and this directly affected how they appoint their Generals and similar titles.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs gained Skarsind as their own territory and the right to a Senator, and the method settled for that appointment reshaped how they choose their Generals and similar titles.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark lost Skarsind as one of its territories, with significant implications for any Winterfolk still living there.

Assignment of Skarsind II.o: In Autumn 379YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Hahnmark and seconded by Temeschwar, assigning the territory of Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind passed from Wintermark to the Imperial Orcs and could now elect a Senator to represent it.

Assignment of Spiral Spring 382YE.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Redoubt and seconded by the senator for Segura, simply resolved that Spiral be assigned to Urizen. It passed. As a result, Spiral became a Urizen territory and went on to elect a senator, giving it representation in the Senate once more. The page records only the assignment and the election of a senator, not who held the territory on the ground.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named in the motion; the map records Grendel as holding Spiral that season, while the Senate assigned the territory to Urizen.

Urizen.t: Urizen formally gained Spiral as one of its territories, and with it a new Senate seat, since Spiral went on to elect a senator.

Assignment of Spiral Spring 382YE.o: In Spring 382YE the Imperial Senate passed a motion assigning the territory of Spiral to the Urizen nation.

Spiral.t: Spiral was assigned to Urizen by the Senate and elected a senator, restoring its representation in the Senate even though the map records it as held by Grendel that season.

At the dog and eel show.d: After three Marcher national assembly statements, from Edward Greenfriar, Bryce Tanner and Sister Meredith, the yeofolk, backed by the alders of Meade and Sarcombe, asked the civil service to hold a tally of votes among those with farms. Feed the Wizards would send seed, livestock and cuttings to Zenith for a year in return for mana, letting Urizen support the Citadel Guard without the Golden Cascade and afford a navy at Elos. Beat the Bounds would add 1,000 force to Imperial campaigns in Mitwold, Mournwold and Upwold, and to the Strong Reeds in Bregasland. Tend the Hearth would give farms extra rings and cheaper upgrades. Separately, orc leaders led by Hap the Soft met at Golden Hoof amid heated argument, and about fifty orcs walked out.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr traveller described the venomous Druj creatures now infesting Zenith's marshes and lakes, which Bregas listeners thought might be farmed like eels.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Marcher farmers asked whether cargo bound for Zenith would travel quicker through Highguard or Therunin.

Jotun.t: The Jotun were out in force in Bregasland and massing in Liathaven, which drove the Beat the Bounds option, while the gathering of their former thralls near the border made Marchers uneasy.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr traveller Lindir told the Dog & Eel's taproom about Zenith and was teased for not knowing the difference between poisonous and venomous.

The Marches.t: Marcher farm-holders were to decide in a tally of the votes how their farms would spend the next year, whether aiding Zenith, supporting the beaters against the Jotun, or improving their own farms, while beaters watched an unexplained orc gathering in the Mournwold.

Urizen.t: If the yeofolk chose Feed the Wizards, Marcher farms would help rebuild Zenith's agriculture for a year, letting Urizen sustain the Citadel Guard without rebuilding the Golden Cascade and become prosperous enough to support a navy at Elos.

At the dog and eel show.o: In Winter 384YE the yeofolk of the Marches were offered a choice, settled by a tally of votes among farm-holders, between aiding Zenith's recovery, supporting the beaters against a Jotun threat, or tending their own farms for the coming year. Meanwhile around five hundred former Jotun thralls held a secretive gathering at Golden Hoof farm in the Mournwold.

Mournwold/Green March.t: About five hundred former Jotun thralls camped around Golden Hoof farm in Green March at Hap the Soft's call, turned Marchers away, and argued for days until about fifty walked out before the rest dispersed in silence.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj creatures in Zenith were likened to the octopuses of the Bay of Catazar.

Bregasland.t: Held by the Jotun, Bregasland was the source of Marcher worry, and under Beat the Bounds the Strong Reeds would gain 1,000 strength while fighting there; under Tend the Hearth even Bregas farms would gain the extra rings.

Liathaven.t: The Jotun were massing in force in Liathaven, recalling to Marchers the build-up before the Mourn fell, and news of it coincided with the thralls' gathering.

Mitwold.t: Under the Beat the Bounds option, any campaign in Mitwold would see 1,000 additional force added to the Imperial side for a year.

Mournwold.t: Beat the Bounds would add 1,000 force to Imperial campaigns in Mournwold, and the territory's orcs, the former Jotun thralls, gathered there in a tense and secretive meeting.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Marcher farmers asked whether the roads through Therunin or Highguard were the quicker route to Zenith.

Upwold.t: Under the Beat the Bounds option, any campaign in Upwold would see 1,000 additional force added to the Imperial side for a year.

Zenith.t: Newly recovered by Urizen and facing serious problems, including Druj creatures in its marshes and lakes, Zenith stood to receive a year of Marcher seed, livestock and fruit cuttings if the yeofolk chose Feed the Wizards.

Authorise Ambassador to Axos.d: Proposed by the senator for Weirwater and seconded by the senator for Necropolis, the motion allowed the Ambassador to Axos to offer Axos access to the spy network in the Mountains of the Moon, inviting Axou troops to support it. The motion passed, giving the Ambassador the Senate's backing in issuing the invitation to Axos. The page records only the authorisation and says nothing of whether Axos accepted.
Authorise Ambassador to Axos.o: In Summer 382YE the Senate passed a motion authorising the Ambassador to Axos to invite Axou troops to support the Imperial spy network in the Mountains of the Moon.

Mountains of the Moon.t: The Imperial spy network in this Tsark-held territory was the focus of the motion, with the Senate backing an invitation for Axou troops to support it.

Authorise ambassador to Iron Confederacy.d: Proposed by the senator for Feroz and seconded by Upwold, the motion passed in Winter 381YE. It authorised the Imperial Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy to invite Duke Guiscard, identified on the page as the Duke of Kalino, to bring his troops into Feroz to deal with rebels from the Iron Confederacy there, on the understanding that they would withdraw immediately afterwards. The motion did not itself bring foreign troops into the Empire: the ambassador still needed to issue the invitation to the Duke for anything to happen.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast's senator for Feroz sought foreign help against Iron Confederacy rebels on Brass Coast soil, opening the way for Duke Guiscard's troops to enter one of the nation's territories.

Authorise ambassador to Iron Confederacy.o: The Imperial Senate passed a motion authorising the Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy to invite Duke Guiscard to send his forces into Feroz to deal with Iron Confederacy rebels and then immediately withdraw.

Feroz.t: Feroz was named as the territory into which Duke Guiscard might be invited to send his forces to deal with the Iron Confederacy rebels before withdrawing, though the ambassador still had to issue the invitation.

Kalino.t: Kalino's Duke Guiscard was the ruler the ambassador was authorised to invite to send forces into Feroz against Iron Confederacy rebels.

Authorise targets of the Imperial Guerdo.d: Dan Brackensong, Quartermaster General of the Imperial Armies, used the power the Senate granted his office to name the season's targets of the Imperial Guerdon. He named the Liathaven Spy Network, the Black Thorns, the Hounds of Glory and the Wolves of War, and closed with a call for a moment of silence for the dead. As a result, owners of military units who supported one of the named armies received a share of the Imperial Guerdon. The motion was approved under the Quartermaster General's own authority, not by a Senate vote.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named. The motion only directs the Guerdon to a spy network in Liathaven, a territory the Jotun held at the time.

Authorise targets of the Imperial Guerdo.o: In Winter 380YE the Quartermaster General of the Imperial Armies, Dan Brackensong, directed the Imperial Guerdon to the Liathaven Spy Network and three Imperial armies: the Black Thorns, the Hounds of Glory and the Wolves of War.

Liathaven.t: The Liathaven Spy Network was named as a target of the Imperial Guerdon, so Imperial support was directed to the spy operation in this Jotun-held territory.

Authority and acceptance.d: The Senate's Summer renunciation of six northern regions satisfied Rak, who invited Ambassador Kindra Surefoot to a private parley on the Thule treaty, which expires in Summer 387YE. A conjunction to a Five Fang Consortium site in Otkodov opened. Skoura welcomed the new treaty and sent delegations about a schema and the Eoradal aqueduct. Tsark returned memory-stripped Urizeni prisoners through Occursion and sent envoys to Anvil. Asavea's bounty on Imperial-bound shipping cost the treasury 62 thrones. Thirty Asavean priests surrendered at Oran. Jarm welcomed the ban on mercenaries aiding the Commonwealth, but the Conclave refused Brotherhood of Tian, so Measure was lost. Speaker Morna of the Grendel declined to attend Anvil.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Consul who handles Skoura and Tsark, Lord Jarrigk Orzel, is of Dawn.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as a bordering orc nation, a past target of Thule cooperation, and invaders whose attack shocks the returning Urizeni.

Grendel.t: The Grendel remain at war with the Empire, with Asavean support, and are pressing hard in Feroz and Ayereed. Speaker Morna declined to attend Anvil until there is something of substance to discuss, such as the Children of Wrecks.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tsark delegation travels west toward Casinea to reach Anvil.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orc interest in rebuilding the Skouran aqueduct in Eoradal prompted a Skouran delegation, which asked to meet Legion Engineer Groza and Senator Gaddak of Mareave about the water it would carry.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are named as a bordering orc nation and a past target of Imperial–Thule cooperation.

Navarr.t: The Tsark sages Apollion and Kristoph particularly hoped to meet Navarr guides during their visit to Anvil.

The Brass Coast.t: The three Freeborn generals had to decide whether to execute or repatriate around thirty Asavean priests who surrendered to them at Oran. Freeborn ambassadors handled both Asavea and the Grendel.

The League.t: The Tsark envoys were especially keen to meet the League, whom they understood now to rule Spiral, home to some of the returned prisoners.

Thule.t: Satisfied by the Senate's renunciation of claims, Rak invited the Empire's ambassador to negotiate the expiring treaty, expecting a further price for peace. He also confirmed that Gisli Baerson funded Otkodov's famine relief.

Urizen.t: Urizeni long held prisoner on Zabor returned to Zenith with their memories of Tsark removed, bringing the body of Ursula. Quinta, who chose to stay in Tsark, travelled to explain that choice to the Urizeni at Anvil.

Varushka.t: Varushkan ambassador Nikita Teanga Volkov handled the frosty relations with Jarm. The Senate's renunciation recognised Miechernya, Krevsaty, Bonewood and Webwood as part of Otkodov.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Kindra Surefoot was invited to a private parley with Rak on the treaty's future, and the Tsark envoys hoped to meet Wintermark mediators.

Authority and acceptance.o: In Autumn 386YE the Empire's foreign relations shifted on several fronts. The Thule agreed to reopen peace treaty talks, Skoura and Tsark planned delegations to Anvil, Asavea put a bounty on shipping trading with the Empire, Jarm pressed its offer over the shield Measure, and the Grendel stayed away.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: Krevsaty was among the regions the Senate recognised as part of Otkodov, the statement the Thule demanded before reopening talks.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: The ruined Skouran aqueduct in Eoradal, which the Imperial Orcs hope to rebuild, prompted Skoura to send engineers to discuss how much water arid Eoradal would need.

Miekarova/Miechernya.t: Miechernya was recognised by the Senate as part of Otkodov, now and forever.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: Bonewood was recognised by the Senate as part of Otkodov.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Webwood was recognised by the Senate as part of Otkodov.

Otkodov/Nithoggir.t: The Sentinel Gate opened to Shaft #3, Skarlans, in Nithoggir, apparently linked to the Five Fang Consortium venture, with violence considered possible but unlikely.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The Silver Peaks were recognised by the Senate as part of Otkodov.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Crow's Ridge was recognised by the Senate as part of Otkodov.

Zenith/Lustri.t: Mentioned in passing: the Stork's Gaze was built in Lustri two years earlier after the Senate declined Tsark's offer of help.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Returning Urizeni and Tsark cuvari came through Mislitel Pass into Occursion and were received at Cato Hypation's Temple of the Wanderer, carrying Ursula's body.

Ayereed.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are reported to be heavily engaged in Ayereed.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Asavean vessels will not enter the Bay, where Imperial and Grendel ships skirmish amid the Children of Wrecks.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tsark delegation sets off west toward Casinea on its way to Anvil.

Feroz.t: The Grendel have struck decisively into Feroz, and Asavean priests who surrendered after the siege of Oran are held under guard there while the Freeborn generals decide their fate.

Karsk.t: The Senate's renunciation recognised Krevsaty in Karsk as part of Otkodov, now and forever.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: a major Grendel force of armies and navies is believed still to be in Madruga, though scrying there is difficult.

Mareave.t: A Skouran schema found in Mareave was to be collected by a Skouran representative. Skoura weighed whether to supply water through a rebuilt aqueduct in Eoradal.

Miekarova.t: The Senate's renunciation recognised Miechernya in Miekarova as part of Otkodov.

Mountains of the Moon.t: Tsark released Urizeni prisoners from Zabor and, after debating its isolation, sent Sage Apollion, Sage Kristoph and Quinta to Anvil to learn about the Imperial nations.

Ossium.t: Ossium, conquered with Thule cooperation, saw its Bonewood and Webwood recognised by the Senate as part of Otkodov.

Otkodov.t: A conjunction opened to a Five Fang Consortium venture in Otkodov while treaty talks loomed. Rak confirmed Gisli Baerson's funds had eased Otkodov's famine.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Stork's Gaze fortification stands in Lustri on the border between Zenith and the Sarangrave.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq, liberated with Thule help, had its Silver Peaks recognised by the Senate as part of Otkodov.

Skarsind.t: The Senate's renunciation recognised Crow's Ridge in Skarsind as part of Otkodov.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: some returned prisoners originally came from Spiral, and the Tsark know it is now ruled by the League.

Zenith.t: Former Urizeni prisoners and Tsark envoys came down into Zenith and were received at the Temple of the Wanderer, where the returnees were sheltered while they reconnected with the world.

Axe-bite and ploughshare.d: Three Wintermark armies, the Autumn Hammers, the Drakes, the Bounders and the Seventh Wave mustered in Green March. Using siege engines leased from Estavus, the Hammers breached Schogsfestnir, and Jarl Sederholm retreated west and began raising a fyrd. The Feni of the Moon-That-Sings supplied maps but insisted Liathaven is now their home. Roughly three thousand Jotun and more than fifteen hundred Imperial soldiers fell. The Wither the Seed curse is gone. Several conjunctions followed, along with a solstice opportunity to destroy an Autumn mechanism hastening the West Ranging fort. Offers from Skathe, Surut and Tharim were also on the table.

Highguard.t: The Seventh Wave scouted ahead, pinned the Schogsfestnir garrison with arrow fire and swept the Glen's flanks. Its general, Melkior of Balthazar's Vineyard, was charged with killing the Jotun champion Halbera Strongarm.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Autumn Hammers brought siege engines leased from the City of Fire and Stone and battered Schogsfestnir open, and Imperial Orc soldiers are now taking up residence there. Ashborn Vana was asked to recover a damaged construct of Estavus.

Jotun.t: The Jotun lost Liaven's Glen, Liath's Ring and Schogsfestnir, with perhaps three thousand dead, but still control Liathaven. Jarl Sederholm is raising a fyrd while a new fortification rises in West Ranging.

Navarr.t: The Empire found the old Navarr steadings gone and the Glen's ancient forest cleared, and Liaven's Dance turned into a guarded Jotun camp, though the earthworks themselves are intact. The vallorn of Liath's Heart remains untouched.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman is named as one of the lands bordering Liaven's Glen.

The Marches.t: The Drakes and the Bounders formed the cautious core of the host, joined for the first time by Marcher orc healers on a major campaign abroad. The Bounders received the Feni envoys and their vital maps.

Wintermark.t: The Green Shield, the Bloodcloaks and the Narwhal's Spear fought with conspicuous honour and kept the wounded alive. Champion of Ambition Eldrid Vestardottir was tasked with stopping heralds escorting a construct of Estavus to Westwood.

Axe-bite and ploughshare.o: In Spring 387YE seven Imperial armies marched from the Mournwold into Jotun-held Liathaven, stormed the fortified town of Schogsfestnir and seized Liaven's Glen and Liath's Ring. The Jotun still hold the rest of the territory and are racing to finish a new fortification in West Ranging.

Liathaven/Liath's Heart.t: The vallorn heart remains outside both sides' control, ringed by Jotun effigies and rune-poles meant to contain it.

Liathaven/Liath's Ring.t: Using Feni intelligence, Imperial forces cleared the Jotun from the Ring within weeks and consolidated their hold. The armies halted on its western border with West Ranging.

Liathaven/Liaven's Glen.t: The Empire stormed and captured the fortified town of Schogsfestnir, the seat of Jarl Sederholm, and took the whole Glen. Many uncertain thralls remain, and Liaven's Dance was found intact.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: The Jotun fell back here and are hurrying to build a new granite fortification, aided by an Autumn mechanism at Far Steading. Imperial heroes have a solstice opportunity to destroy the device, or Surut offers to burn the region.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: The retreating Jotun are escorting a construct of Estavus to Westwood, where it would resupply the Shield of the Mountain unless Wintermark's Champion of Ambition stops it.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Mentioned in passing: the Autumn Hammers hauled wagonloads of lumber harvested from its woods.

Mournwold/Green March.t: All seven Imperial armies mustered here before marching west into Liaven's Glen.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Host may have been guarding against incursions from Bregasland, Bounders beat its border, and events there prevented a direct attack into Liath's Ring.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: its deep woods are compared with the wilder forests of old Liathaven.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: its rugged splendour is compared with the once-untamed Liaven's Glen.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: it is named as bordering Liaven's Glen.

Liathaven.t: The Empire took Liaven's Glen, Liath's Ring and the fortified town of Schogsfestnir, but the Jotun still control the territory. A new Jotun fortification is under construction in West Ranging, and the Feni claim the land as their home.

Mournwold.t: The seven armies mustered in Green March before the invasion, and the Autumn Hammers carried lumber harvested from Alderly.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: its deep woods are compared with the wilder forests of old Liathaven.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; it appears only as part of the wider Jotun lands whose armies defended Liathaven.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Autumn mechanism at Far Steading resembles the contraptions once found at the Well of Whispers in Skallahn.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: its alpine peaks are contrasted with the woodlands of Liathaven.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: Igya Olgafsdottir, who built Schogsfestnir, is now Jarl of Tromsa.

Back in the same place.d: Temeschwar's existing faculties of metallurgy, mining and warding did not suit the Senate's brief, but its merchant princes backed a grander plan. A new university building (60 wains of white granite, 30 of weirwood, 180 crowns, six months, in Hanuri) would create the Master of Rings. This national League title, appointed by the Bourse, could announce one extra civilian commission each season and would be charged with enriching the League. Separately, if the Synod recognised La Volpe as an exemplar of Ambition (or Pride), the Senate could build his tomb, creating the Blood Red Builder to commission great works or tombs. Both opportunities lapse after the Summer Solstice 385YE. Graciana would be on leave for the following season.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the prognosticator Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra is granted leave to travel home to Madruga for her niece's wedding, so she will be unavailable until the Winter Solstice 384YE.

The League.t: The League stands to gain a national title, the Master of Rings, charged with generating wealth for the League, and the Blood Red Builder could also become a League national position appointed by its National Assembly.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: materials passing through Temeschwar from Varushka are one source of the white granite, mithril and weirwood the Master of Rings would receive.

Back in the same place.o: Prognosticator Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra reported on the Senate's appraisal of a university in Temeschwar to raise the number of commissions the Empire could undertake each season. She set out two opportunities: a new University of Temeschwar creating a League title, the Master of Rings, and an inspirational tomb for Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar creating the Blood Red Builder.

Temeschwar/Hanuri.t: Hanuri would host both proposed commissions: the new University of Temeschwar, built on demolished slums on the city's north side, and Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar's inspirational tomb bearing the Butchers' Bank symbol.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's university is described as the Empire's foremost centre of engineering learning, the standard a new Temeschwar university would seek to rival.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Graciana returns home to Madruga to oversee arrangements for her niece Ailande's wedding.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is named as a city whose university prestige, and whose supposed condescension towards Temeschwar, the new university would answer.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwari believe folk in Tassato look down on them, a resentment the proposed university is meant to address.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar's merchant princes offered endowments and contributions to back a new university and the Master of Rings, and its citizens called for a tomb honouring La Volpe, both to establish the city as the equal of its League rivals.

Back in town.d: Meraud declined parley but offered Enchantress Areloe Larmallevés plans for the Flame of the Phoenix, a mana-producing sinecure in Astolat. It must be commissioned by the end of the Winter Solstice and ceded to him. Zakalwe arranged a parley with Skywise Gralka, and his myrmidons began aiding the fight against Cold Sun. Prospero responded privately and offered a Runesmith's Law schema in return for ten rings of ilium and a ritual text. Tharim sent courtiers to speak with named citizens and agreed to empower a Throne-linked ritual. Janon arranged a parley and proposed an Imperial title. Arhallogen, angered by the Spring Archmage's tone, would receive only five Navarr vates.

Dawn.t: Meraud offered Enchantress Areloe Larmallevés plans for the Flame of the Phoenix in Astolat, and its Tender would gain extra powers and a ministry if they were a Dawnish noble Enchanter. Enchantress Armand Remys was among those Tharim's courtiers would visit.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Arhallogen's herald acknowledged that the eternal continues to aid the Druj.

Highguard.t: Zakalwe's three myrmidon messengers joined the garrison of the Silent Sentinel to support Highguard's defence of Casinea against Cold Sun.

Navarr.t: Arhallogen would receive only Navarr vates, no more than five, and claimed his role in their treaty with the Mallum orcs had spared Therunin. Prospero was watching whether the Navarr would keep Thornsong House's apothecary lore for themselves.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Meraud suggested that Marsello Givello Cellini di Sarvos speak to the Warlocks of Otkodov.

Urizen.t: Zakalwe's myrmidons were especially common in Urizen, citing a debt to the mountain people who saved them from extinction. The Urizen Archmages of Winter and Night secured meetings with Tharim's courtiers and Janon.

Wintermark.t: Prospero offered a schema for inclusion in Runesmith's Law, to be given to the smiths of Runegrott, and approved of Wintermark artisans keeping their own unique lore.

Back in town.o: In late Summer 385YE six eternals answered the plenipotentiary messages sent by the Empire's archmages at the Summer Solstice. Zakalwe and Janon offered parleys, Arhallogen called a meeting of uncertain status, Tharim agreed to send courtiers, and Meraud and Prospero made other arrangements.

Astolat.t: Meraud proposed building the Flame of the Phoenix at a regio near the Larmallevés estate. Prospero's minotaur herald also appeared at the Castle of Thorns.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Arhallogen declared that nothing at the Heart of the Tempest is any longer of interest to eternals of the Endless Forest.

Casinea.t: Three of Zakalwe's myrmidons joined the garrison at the Silent Sentinel to help defend Casinea against Cold Sun.

Hahnmark.t: Prospero's schema for Runesmith's Law would be given to the smiths at Runegrott if the Archmage of Autumn met his terms.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Meraud suggested consulting the Warlocks of Otkodov on a matter raised by Marsello Givello Cellini di Sarvos.

Therunin.t: Arhallogen claimed that his involvement in the Navarr treaty with the Mallum orcs saved Therunin from despoilment like Zenith's. He also scorned the 'cowards of the Great Forest' sheltering there.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Arhallogen cited Zenith's despoilment as the fate Therunin had escaped.

Bad blood.d: Jenny Arbor's Marcher assembly statement named six Urizeni casters, including Archmage of Spring Ibiss of Netherwatch, Imperial Inquisitor Galene and the once-declared sorcerer Aquillian, plus two facilitators and a person of interest. Rafael Barossa di Tassato's Concord was ruled equivalent to an endorsement, so the magistrates and militia dropped their case, though priests and magicians may still act. Alisoun Bathwater urged threshers to investigate those involved through the Assemblies and the Conclave. The proposed title, appointed by Declaration of Candidacy, could raise one Declaration of Sorcery per session. Depending on its remit, Marcher threshers offer four Thresher's Cudgels a season, Necropolis's Umbral Shroud the Lantern Ring, and Miaren's Lost Lore Steading a yearly Thornpath Sash. The offer lapses at the end of the Spring Equinox 385YE.

Highguard.t: Highborn magisters, who believe magical study should be paired with the study of virtue, want the proposed title to watch closely over anyone dealing with eternals. A dwindling group from Necropolis has offered the Lantern Ring as regalia on that condition.

Navarr.t: Navarr vates, mindful of Terunael's fall and the creation of the vallorn, want the title to keep watch over all powerful magicians before hubris leads them astray. Lost Lore Steading has offered a yearly Thornpath Sash if the title investigates Conclave-appointed title holders.

Urizen.t: All six named casters of Thunderous Deluge are prominent Urizeni, including the Archmage of Spring, the Imperial Inquisitor and Aquillian of Urizen, and some suspect Urizen's mountain-dwelling economic interests behind the flooding. They are safe from the magistrates but face possible investigation by threshers, the Assemblies and the Conclave.

Bad blood.o: After the magical tempest that broke the drought, the Marcher assembly named the Urizeni magicians behind Thunderous Deluge, but the Constitutional Court treated the Conclave's Concord as an endorsement and ended the magistrates' investigation. Threshers, Highborn magisters and Navarr vates then called on the Senate to create a Conclave-appointed title to lead declarations of sorcery, offering regalia if it acts in time.

Miaren.t: The vates of Lost Lore Steading in Miaren have offered a Thornpath Sash each year, a focus for several investigative rituals, if the new title is charged with ensuring Conclave-appointed title holders are not corrupted by their power.

Necropolis.t: The Umbral Shroud, a once-powerful order of Necropolis magisters from Empress Giselle's reign, has offered the Lantern Ring, which can reveal whether someone has recently visited a chamber between worlds, if the title watches those dealing with eternals.

Banners and bells.d: Jacob, Benefactor of Regalia, presented banners to the generals of the Granite Pillar, Seventh Wave and Valiant Pegasus, while Ever Forward awaits the new army's general, who could be appointed at the Autumn Equinox. The senator who raised the army must choose a quality: Devoted, Fast or Righteous. For a year, Highborn congregations may forgo liao to support the army against the vallorn. With the crusading storm over, Asher of the Seven Pools proposed a mandate, worded by Exarch Luke, letting Highborn armies Protect the Innocent in the Sarangrave. The Assembly may also invoke peerless kinship each season. The Assembly of Nine appointed Ardeniel of the Woodwych Harts to record the Seven Bells pilgrimage for the Stone Library.

Druj.t: Having lost a large swathe of the Sarangrave to a new Imperial assault, the Druj have spread word of the Barrens slaughter through the Mallum's septs, leaving their oppressed subjects more afraid of the Empire than of their masters.

Highguard.t: Highguard's fourth army can now be raised for 80 mithril around the grey pilgrims and their Ever Forward banner. Its Assembly may also adopt a Protect the Innocent mandate, invoke peerless kinship each season and support the new army against the vallorn.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the hallowed bells are described as what the Imperial Orcs would call "items of worth".

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the grey pilgrims learned to travel the trods alongside the Navarr, which could make the new Highborn army fast like the Black Thorns.

Banners and bells.o: Four relic banners hallowed with true liao were created for the Highborn armies, cutting the cost of raising Highguard's fourth army, built around the returning grey pilgrims, to 80 mithril. The page also set out new opportunities for the Highborn Assembly and the Synod's plan to hallow seven bells for a pilgrimage around the Empire.

Bastion.t: The Stone Library chapter in Bastion, led by Librarian Seth, challenged the Assembly of Nine to record the Seven Bells pilgrimage. Ardeniel of the Woodwych Harts was appointed, and the chapter's archivists will copy and distribute the account.

Sarangrave.t: The Empire has captured a large swathe of the Sarangrave, with the Granite Pillar ordered to spare the Druj's oppressed subjects. A proposed Highborn mandate would let armies fight there to protect the innocent, though winning over the local septs would be a hard struggle.

Battle cries.d: Captains of the League, Varushka and the Imperial Orcs crushed the vyig, ending the bite trade but leaving a vacuum of disorganised crime. Three groups remained: Uncle Tassato carrying a stolen copy of the Regario Dossier, Miekarovan vyig with a mysterious patron bound for the Butterfly Holt, and Aunt Alina's gang in Vardstein Vale after a bloody raid on the Assayer's Guild. Magistrates confiscated vyig-linked businesses in Tassato, Sarvos and Karov. The Silver Rook Carta sought a League Assembly mandate to publish the names of the vyig-hunters. A Lantern Wolf office could be built in one of the four League cities before the end of Winter 385YE.

Druj.t: Evidence marked bite as a Druj product, and the vyig who escaped fled into the Mallum, where they almost certainly learned how little the Druj can be trusted.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the fleeing Tassatan vyig were preparing a final leg of their journey to Grendel-held Feroz.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial Orc captains were among those who directly opposed and helped break the vyig.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun were expected simply to enslave any Varushkan vyig who reached their border.

The Brass Coast.t: The Tassatan vyig were reportedly hiding in the Renewal Grove in Brass Coast-held Madruga, so the fight to recover the stolen Regario Dossier would take place on Freeborn land.

The League.t: The League saw its ancient criminal syndicate destroyed, gained confiscated businesses and fee-free business opportunities in Tassato and Sarvos, and was offered a mandate to honour the vyig-hunters and the chance to create a Lantern Wolf to guard against a new syndicate.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule were considered unlikely to offer the fleeing Varushkan vyig shelter.

Varushka.t: Varushka's vyig were all but destroyed, with Orel the Bondbreaker slain, though the last Miekarovan band threatened the Butterfly Holt and a vyig-owned mine and business in Karov were seized for Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti to dispose of.

Battle cries.o: By Summer 385YE the vyig had been broken in the League and Varushka, leaving three desperate bands trying to flee the Empire, each of which could be intercepted through a Sentinel Gate conjunction. The page also covered seized vyig businesses, a proposed Synod mandate honouring the vyig-hunters, and an opportunity to create a League office of the Lantern Wolf.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered the chance to intercept Uncle Tassato's band at the Renewal Grove in Calvos Sound and recover the stolen Regario Dossier before they left for Feroz.

Miekarova/Srodkoja.t: The last Miekarovan vyig were set to attack the Butterfly Holt in southern Srodkoja, threatening significant damage that would cut its production of iridescent gloaming unless the Gloaming Sentinel's allies intercepted them.

Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale.t: Aunt Alina's gang held an abandoned fort in the Broken Wilds of Vardstein Vale, having slaughtered the Green Torch bravos, and the Custodian of the Assayer's Guild was charged with ending them and taking her head for House de Courcey.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Feroz was the intended final destination of Uncle Tassato's escape.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: a few groups of vyig were reported slinking through Ossium into the Forest of Ulnak.

Holberg.t: The garrison of the Walls of Holberg supported the city against the vyig, and Holberg was one of the cities where a Lantern Wolf office could be built, implying a pragmatic, ingenious investigator.

Karov.t: Magistrates recovered a vyig-owned mine and business in Karov, both legitimate enterprises, whose deeds were given to Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti to deal with at the summit.

Madruga.t: The last Tassatan vyig were believed to be hiding in Madruga's Renewal Grove, located with help from a Mestran herb seller's sighting in the markets of Calvos, awaiting interception by the Custodian of the Regario Dossier.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova saw running skirmishes and the death of vyig leader Orel the Bondbreaker near the vale of Olodny, but his surviving band regrouped in the woods to strike at the Butterfly Holt.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: a few groups of vyig were reported slipping through Ossium into the Forest of Ulnak.

Sarvos.t: Swift ships left Sarvos carrying suspiciously wealthy passengers, a vyig-linked business there was confiscated and its deed given to Irada von Temeschwar, and the city was a possible site for an elegant, sophisticated Lantern Wolf's office.

Tassato.t: Tassato suffered running skirmishes and the burning of the vyig lair at the Jarmish Lodge; two confiscated businesses passed to Irada von Temeschwar, League citizens could take new businesses there without the usual fee, and it was a possible site for a diplomatic Lantern Wolf.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar endured skirmishes and a bloody vyig heist on the Assayer's Guild that killed and captured clerks and angered House de Courcey, and it was a possible site for a ruthless, hard-nosed Lantern Wolf.

Beat of your drum.d: Schöningen praised outgoing ambassador Lucia Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato. She said that once the diplomatenschloss is built, merchants would send seasonal cultural tokens to the ambassador rather than offering "special deals". The Commonwealth is struggling against Jarmish magic in Lantir. It offered Soldatentrunk, Blutlehm, Würzpaste and Heldenstein in return for 200 crystal mana sent by the end of the Summer Solstice. Magicians trapped in the Lyceum improved Rule of Risk and Reward and Sum of the Parts. Professor Gelberg's faculty will auction appraisals at Anvil. The University of Volkavaar asked to acquire a sungold tablet from the Great Library of Hacynian. Schöningen formally questioned whether Suranni serfs are slaves under the Liberty Pact. Teo Freid described orc beliefs about the Raging Storm and reincarnation.

Imperial Orcs.t: Ambassador Pridetalker's enquiry on behalf of some Imperial Orcs drew a reply from Teo Freid. He described a sizeable sect of Commonwealth orcs who believe orcs reincarnate if they resist the Raging Storm through disciplined service to the Common Good.

Navarr.t: Navarr hosts at the Great Library of Hacynian, invited by Advisor on the Vallorn Nathair Autumngale, welcomed the Commonwealth faculty and debated true consecrations with them. They now face a formal request from the University of Volkavaar to name a price for the sungold tablet.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Freeborn are recalled as having fought alongside Commonwealth soldiers in the fall of Siroc. The Liberty Pact questions arose after a Commonwealth scholar met Iron Confederacy merchants in Madruga.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: League ambassador Lucia Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato was praised on leaving the post, and the visiting faculty passed through Sarvos, Tassato and Temeschwar.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the city of Seren was among the places the Commonwealth faculty visited on their journey north.

Wintermark.t: Finn Pridetalker of Wintermark was welcomed as the new Ambassador to the Commonwealth. Pridetalker was offered the mana exchange and asked to address the problem of shipping on the Couros.

Beat of your drum.o: The Civil Service's seasonal report on the Commonwealth recorded Militärattache Ludkhannah Schöningen welcoming new Imperial ambassador Finn Pridetalker. It also covered the Lantir War, a one-off mana-for-goods offer, ritual breakthroughs from the Lyceum, the Beurteilung auction, interest in a sungold tablet, Liberty Pact concerns over the Iron Confederacy, and an account of Commonwealth orc spirituality.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: Mentioned in passing: the bustling town of Torfast was visited by the Commonwealth faculty on their travels.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is named as the northern end of the Commonwealth faculty's journey from Sarvos.

Madruga.t: While discharging an obligation to Gisli "Provider" Baerson in Madruga, a Commonwealth scholar met Iron Confederacy merchants. That meeting led to the formal Liberty Pact questions about Suranni serfs.

Miaren.t: The Great Library of Hacynian received the Commonwealth faculty and let them study a cracked tablet on making sungold. The University of Volkavaar has now asked what price the Library would accept for it.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the city of Seren was visited by the Commonwealth faculty on their travels.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Commonwealth faculty were travelling north from Sarvos when the news reached them.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the town of Torfast was among the stops on the Commonwealth faculty's journey.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the city of Tassato was visited by the Commonwealth faculty, and the former ambassador bears its name.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the city of Temeschwar was visited by the Commonwealth faculty on their way north.

Because they must.d: The Tusks advanced methodically south, while the Burning Falcon, joined by Summer Knights of Glory, charged the strongest Jotun positions and smashed the defenders of the Singing Caves. The outnumbered Jotun fought hard, but Farstrider's Watch fell. The Tusks' general had ordered that none be left to contest the Marcher claim, and the garrison was wiped out. Surviving warbands are now hunted as outlaws. A Summer enchantment kept the ruined castle standing, but it will collapse unless repaired before the enchantment fades near the Summer solstice 388YE. The Singing Caves mithril mine returned to Imperial control for the Senate to allocate. Units supporting each army gained inspiration or a Summer boon.

Jotun.t: Jarl Haakon's last champions were destroyed at Farstrider's Watch, ending thirty years of Jotun domination in the Mournwold, and any surviving warbands are now hunted as outlaws.

The Brass Coast.t: The Burning Falcon marched to the aid of the Marches, smashed the defenders of the Singing Caves at the head of the assault, and earned a Summer boon for the units that fought alongside them.

The Marches.t: The Tusks kept their oath and completed the liberation of the Mournwold at little Marcher cost, earning the people's lasting trust and inspiration for those who supported them.

Because they must.o: In Autumn 387YE the Tusks and the Burning Falcon conquered the Greensward, storming Farstrider's Watch and the Singing Caves and destroying the last champions loyal to the dead Jarl Haakon. The Mournwold was left entirely in Marcher hands.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Mentioned in passing: the green woven wards of the Prince of a Thousand Foes persisted in Alderly for another season.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: The Greensward was conquered. The Singing Caves returned to Imperial control and Farstrider's Watch was emptied of Jotun, though it stands only through a Summer enchantment and must be repaired before that fades.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Burning Falcon's general notes they had fought on the coast in previous seasons before coming to aid the Marches.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: surviving Jotun warbands may try to escape to Liathaven, though Sarcombe and the Bounders Hall lie in their way.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold is once again wholly Imperial and part of the Marches, with the Singing Caves mithril mine available for the Senate to allocate.

Bedight in veils.d: The Otkodov treaty became law, although the formal signing was delayed until Winter. The Thule bought large quantities of food in the Marches and Navarr and took Mieriada, while leaving the Empire half the Night Quarry's output and access to the Maze of Zoria. They also asked to use the Imperial spy network in Ulnak. The Suranni clarified the status of serfs, said the curse on Kalino had lifted and planned a visit to the Marcher Wassail. The Jotun mourned Jarl Ustigar while a meeting hall rose on Gull Island, and a smidr sought help over murdered thralls. The Grendel offered Hearts Blood for black pearls. The Karass demanded the removal of the Last Battle Wayhouse, Tsark proposed low-key diplomacy, and Morajasse pledged to guard Feroz.

Dawn.t: The Karass accepted Dawnish rule of the Barrens but begged that the Last Battle Wayhouse be removed from their woods. They were also baffled by a Dawnish noble's demand for love poetry and sent three doses of true vervain instead. Finna of Dawn, Ambassador to the Grendel, received Speaker Morna's missive.

Druj.t: The Thule said they would rather the folk of the Vore did not take the Forest of Ulnak should the Druj collapse. They sought to scout Ulnak, but the Dragons will not consider helping the Empire fight the Druj without far greater rewards.

Grendel.t: The Grendel remained at war. They attacked Mareave and seized Elos in Redoubt, and claimed to have destroyed the Children of Wrecks' temple in Raineach. Their Saltbinder Grekodh offered Hearts Blood for black pearls, while Speaker Morna insisted that peace talks go only through the Ambassador to the Grendel.

Jotun.t: The Jotun honoured the fallen Jarl Ustigar of Kierheim, whose successor is unclear, and recognised Igya Olgafsdottir as their representative to the Empire. They are likely to respond to an invitation to the new Gull Island meeting hall, and a smidr planned to come to Anvil under truce over two murdered thralls.

Navarr.t: Heavy Thule food purchases reduced Navarr's ability to support armies, but the trade boom raised taxation in Hercynia and Miaren. The Karass objected strongly to Navarr scouts from the Last Battle Wayhouse, and Rak showed interest in Dylan Thornweaver's Legacy Accords.

The Brass Coast.t: The Grendel Protectorate of Morajasse pledged to guard Feroz's coast against the Children of Wrecks, many of whom had moved to islands off the Brass Coast. The Freeborn of Feroz and Segura proved suspicious of trading with the garrison, and Freeborn-linked assemblies could urge them either way.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Speaker Morna remarked that the Children of Wrecks seemed bent on looting Sarvos, and the Morajasse missive arrived at the Imperial Consulate in Tassato.

The Marches.t: Thule buying of herds and provisions reduced the Marches' ability to support armies, but the trade boom raised taxation in Mitwold and Upwold. A Suranni delegation planned to attend the Marcher Wassail, and the Jotun were noted as still fighting the Marchers in the south.

Thule.t: Otkodov's treaty became law, the Thule took Mieriada and laid enchantments in Ossium, and Thule warlocks joined the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun. They stalled on tariffs, warned against restricting hollows and sought access to the Ulnak spy network. They also explained what they knew of the 'face peelers'.

Urizen.t: The Grendel seized Elos in Redoubt, which was saved from destruction only by the sacrifice of the Fist of the Mountains. Tsark asked to station two sages at the abandoned Spire of the Night Sun in Zenith, and Zenith Ascendant agreed to host Sage Kristoph at Anvil.

Varushka.t: Varushka lost Mieriada, including the Night Quarry, the Painted Caves and the Tolvoli Slaughterhouse, to the Thule. The Slaughterhouse could keep operating only if a Varushkan took the reduced post of Tolvoli Butcher and kept supplying the Thule with beasts. The Thule suggested people in Ossium or Karsk might know more about the face-stealing creatures.

Wintermark.t: The Gull Island meeting hall off Kallavesa neared completion under Wintermark naval guard, and a national mandate was proposed to invite the Jotun there. The Fist of the Mountains was commended by the Grendel for its costly stand at Elos, and the scholar Marko Siwarsbairn remained a guest of the Suranni.

Bedight in veils.o: A seasonal round-up of the Empire's dealings with lesser foreign powers: Otkodov, the Iron Confederacy, the Jotun, the Grendel, the people of Tsark, the Karass of the Barrens and the new Protectorate of Morajasse. It covered a newly binding Thule treaty, Thule control of Mieriada, and several diplomatic openings and requests.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: Morajasse remained held from Mora's Rock by Commander Gallum Fiersach and Wind Lord Saoirse, now recognised as a foreign protectorate that Imperial generals may not attack. Saoirse offered to raise Ramparts of Ashlar over the fortress for 75 crystals of mana.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Before the Spring Equinox, Gallum and Saoirse led their troops into Oranseri to fight the Children of Wrecks.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: The Thule took Mieriada along with the Night Quarry, the Heart of the Tempest, the Maze of Zoria, several Painted Caves and the Tolvoli Slaughterhouse. The Night Quarry's Imperial output was halved to 14 wains.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: The Thule castle of Fljajokep in the Bonewood bore a forge-bright enchantment of brass sigils this season.

Ossium/Webwood.t: A Thule ward of Night magic seethed in the Webwood, whose border with Ulnak gives Thule scouts easy access to the Forest.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Mentioned in passing: human labourers in the forests of Sküld once called the face-stealing creatures 'face peelers'.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr scouts based at the Last Battle Wayhouse are exploring the Nesustak Forest.

Segura/Anozeseri.t: Folk of Anozeseri were unwilling to sell their limited supplies to the Grendel garrison at Mora's Rock.

Segura/Lucksprings.t: Folk of Lucksprings were unwilling to trade with the Grendel of Morajasse, whom they associate with Governor Rahab's tyranny.

Skallahn/Fareskov.t: Two thralls, Vigdis and Toki, were murdered in Fareskov last season in a case linked to an eternal interest in its dark forest. The smidr Harald Fourforge suspects the Hungry Beast.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Mentioned in passing: a Karass emissary travelled to Dawnguard to deliver Anka Karass's missive for the Imperial Consul.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: Mentioned in passing: the Karass suggested the wayhouse might be moved to Saltmarsh instead.

The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth.t: Mentioned in passing: the Karass have largely abandoned their villages on the Plains of Teeth, which they suggested as an alternative wayhouse site.

The Barrens/The Untrod Groves.t: The Karass want the Last Battle Wayhouse removed from the Untrod Groves, fearing it has woken the Manticore Earl. Replacing it would mean abrogating it and losing its special striding benefits.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Tsark asked to house two sages and their staff at the abandoned Spire of the Night Sun near the border of Occursion as a trial diplomatic post.

Bay of Catazar.t: Black pearls appeared in the bay's waters, and the Grendel said they had prepared against any threat from the depths. Saltbinder Grekodh offered a pawn of Hearts Blood for each pair of pearls.

Feroz.t: Most of Feroz had been liberated, but Grendel under Commander Gallum still held Morajasse as a recognised protectorate pledged to defend the coast against the Children of Wrecks. Local Freeborn refused to trade with the garrison.

Forest of Ulnak.t: The Thule asked to use the Imperial spy network here to map the forest and investigate magical sites, or would spy independently if refused. They would not share what they know of the Vore to the north.

Hercynia.t: Thule buying under the new treaty brought a trade boom that raised taxation here, though Navarr's ability to support armies fell.

Kalino.t: The curse that blighted the harvest in the Suranni province of Arbonne, known to the Empire as Kalino, appeared to have abated. The Suranni credited the priests of Farod, while civil servants thought it had simply run its course.

Kallavesa.t: A meeting hall for Jotun diplomacy neared completion on tidal Gull Island off Kallavesa, despite attacks by coral husks. Some locals feared the Jotun might use it as a springboard for renewed attacks.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule suggested people in Ossium or Karsk might answer questions about the face-stealing creatures once known to their human slaves.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; Speaker Morna noted that many Children of Wrecks had shifted to the islands off the Brass Coast.

Mareave.t: The Grendel launched a land offensive here, 'liberating' the Brine Turtles and threatening the mithril mine.

Miaren.t: Thule purchases under the treaty brought a trade boom that raised taxation here, though Navarr's ability to support armies fell.

Miekarova.t: A Thule army took control of the Mieriada region and its notable resources. The Empire kept half the Night Quarry's stone and conditional access to the Maze of Zoria.

Mitwold.t: Trade with Thule merchants buying food and herds brought money and higher taxation to Mitwold, at the cost of the Marches' ability to support armies.

Mountains of the Moon.t: The Council of Sages of Tsark agreed to trial restrained diplomacy with the Empire, but no Imperial citizen will be allowed to enter the Mountains.

Ossium.t: The Thule enchanted the Bonewood castle of Fljajokep and laid a ward of Night magic in the Webwood. They also confirmed that face-stealing 'face peelers' once preyed on humans in these woods.

Otkodov.t: Food, herds and supplies bought in the Marches and Navarr were shipped north to Otkodov, presumably increasing its ability to support armies. Rak insisted any remaining shortfall was well in hand.

Raineach.t: Speaker Morna said Grendel soldiers had dealt with the Temple of Tempest Jade, a Children of Wrecks fane on Raineach's shores.

Redoubt.t: A Grendel naval attack seized the port of Elos, and only the sacrifice of the Fist of the Mountains prevented its destruction and the reshaping of the coast.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr scouts from the Last Battle Wayhouse are exploring the Nesustak Forest across the border in Sarangrave.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Speaker Morna remarked that the Children of Wrecks seemed hell-bent on looting Sarvos.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: some say the terrible monsters of the Sea of Snow are why the Jotun avoid sea travel.

Segura.t: Freeborn in Lucksprings and Anozeseri, like those in Feroz, were reluctant to sell supplies to the Grendel garrison at Mora's Rock.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule bought meat and produce from Sermersuaq, and the old Meeting Place once lay just beyond its borders.

Skallahn.t: Jarl Ustigar was buried at Kierheim, where both claimants to Jarl of Jarls reportedly attended. A smidr of Skallahn's Skroh of the Locked Door is investigating murders he links to the Hungry Beast.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Wind Lord Saoirse's magical missive was delivered to the Imperial Consulate in Tassato.

The Barrens.t: The Karass accepted Dawnish rule but demanded the removal of the Last Battle Wayhouse, fearing it had stirred the Manticore Earl. They offered nothing in return.

Tromsa.t: Igya Olgafsdottir, Jarl of Tromsa, was acclaimed the Jotun representative to the Empire. Tromsa is among the lands a proposed mandate would send messengers to.

Upwold.t: Trade with Thule merchants brought money and higher taxation to Upwold, at the cost of the Marches' ability to support armies.

Veroigne.t: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni ambassador's seat, Chaubrette, apparently lies to the west of Veroigne.

Zenith.t: Sage Apollion of Tsark visited Zenith to announce a trial of restrained diplomacy. He asked that two sages reside at the abandoned Spire of the Night Sun.

Before the sunrise.d: A magnitude fifty Spring curse, apparently Rivers of Life, infused Therunin's waters with healing power, but threatened to stir its vallorn; the counter-ritual Rivers Run Red is interdicted. The Suaq Qimmiq Swiftblade and Nukilik Adamantine, who attacked the Krampus, agreed to face inquisition at Anvil. The Spiral Sword runeforge was finished near Cargo in Redoubt, with its Seer title to be auctioned through the Bourse. Irra Harah offered boons for the hearts of Zadkiel de Coeurdefer, Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza and Henry Ward. Stars stayed hidden over Semmerholm and the Barrens and vanished over Zenith, strengthening naga secrecy. Penumbral veils covered Urdur, Necropolis and Redoubt, and the Sussivari Frost Coven raised the Citadel of Fog in the Morass.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish naga Zadkiel de Coeurdefer had a bounty placed on his heart by Irra Harah, and the stars remained hidden over Dawn's territory of Semmerholm, impeding scrying and heightening naga secretiveness there.

Druj.t: The stars remained absent over the Druj-held Barrens and vanished over Druj-occupied Zenith, whose proximity left the new runeforge vulnerable to any Druj move against Redoubt.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but cats in Spiral, which Grendel partly held, suffered a Night curse of nightmares.

Highguard.t: A ritual shroud warped the stars over Necropolis and shielded it from scrying, bringing heavy dark fog, while the runeforge stood on the road to the Highborn trading-port of Hedra.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Krampus-beast linked to Skarsind was attacked and slain at the Winter Solstice, though its spirit was reportedly banished to the Krampushall in Pakaanan's Pass and reformed there.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun advance into Liathaven thirty years ago was recalled as a time when using Rivers of Life near a vallorn was cautioned against, and Liathaven's vallorn remained a source of uncertainty.

Navarr.t: Rivers of Life settled over Navarr Therunin, healing wounds but thickening the vallorn's miasma and making giant insects restive, with attacks on isolated steadings reported.

The League.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven again raised a misty fortress in Holberg's Morass, and masked strangers in its fogs sometimes aided hunters and travellers against orc ambushes.

The Marches.t: Henry Ward of Upwold was one of three citizens whose hearts Irra Harah sought, and Thomas of Upwold was among the benefactors who funded the Spiral Sword.

Thule.t: Thule appeared to have drawn the penumbral veil over Urdur in Otkodov, filling its night sky with strange phenomena; whether Nithoggir, Sküld or Verthandi were similarly veiled was unclear.

Urizen.t: The Spiral Sword runeforge was completed in Redoubt, which was also shrouded against scrying, and Spiral's cats were tormented by a Night curse, prompting two magicians to leave for Redoubt.

Wintermark.t: Many Winterfolk were troubled by the assault on the Krampus, and the stormcrow Baena Stormsdottir, injured in a fall, urged other Wintermark priests to inquisit the Suaq perpetrators Qimmiq Swiftblade and Nukilik Adamantine at Anvil.

Before the sunrise.o: In the run-up to the Spring Equinox 382YE, several strange magical events touched the Empire: a Rivers of Life curse settled over vallorn-haunted Therunin, the Spiral Sword runeforge was completed in Redoubt, and the eternal Irra Harah set bounties on three Imperial citizens. Star-shrouds persisted or appeared over several territories, the Citadel of Fog rose again in Holberg, the Krampus's attackers awaited possible inquisition, and Spiral's cats suffered cursed nightmares.

Holberg/The Morass.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven's dripping castle of mud, reeds and roots rose again from the Morass, wreathed in vision-limiting mists.

Necropolis/Hedrossan.t: Mentioned in passing: Hedrossan is not named, though the runeforge's road leads to the Highborn port of Hedra and Necropolis as a whole was shrouded.

Otkodov/Nithoggir.t: Mentioned in passing: it was unknown whether the penumbral veil over Urdur also lay over Nithoggir.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Mentioned in passing: it was unknown whether the penumbral veil over Urdur also lay over Sküld.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: Merchants at Thule trading posts in Urdur reported misplaced constellations, a randomly shifting moon and eerie lights, suggesting a penumbral veil.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: The Krampus's spirit was reportedly banished to the Krampushall in Pakaanan's Pass and reformed there, though its return to full strength was uncertain.

Spiral/Screed.t: Mentioned in passing: the curse on Spiral's cats seemed unconnected to the thing in Screed.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: Stories told of the vallorn miasma thickening in Greenheart as the Spring curse took hold.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: Stories told of the vallorn miasma thickening in Sweetglades as the Spring curse took hold.

Holberg.t: The Citadel of Fog rose again in the Morass, its mists spreading across the territory with masked figures who sometimes helped travellers, before dissipating shortly before the Equinox.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: questions over the active status of Liathaven's vallorn added to fears about Therunin, and its stars were among those missing during 381YE.

Necropolis.t: A ritual shroud warped Necropolis's stars, protected it from scrying for the coming year and brought heavy, dark fog.

Otkodov.t: Urdur appeared to be under a Thule penumbral veil, with misplaced constellations and eerie lights; whether other regions were veiled was uncertain.

Redoubt.t: The Spiral Sword runeforge was completed on the road between Cargo and Hedra, dangerously close to Zenith, and a shroud now hid Redoubt from scrying behind warped stars and dark fog.

Semmerholm.t: The stars remained absent over Semmerholm under a magnitude fifty Night shroud, impeding scrying and strengthening naga secretiveness.

Skarsind.t: The Krampus-beast associated with Skarsind was attacked at the Winter Solstice, its spirit reportedly reforming in the Krampushall.

Spiral.t: Every cat in Spiral suffered a Night curse of nightmares for three months, and many residents' cats went missing, apparently having fled.

The Barrens.t: The stars remained hidden over the Barrens, impeding scrying and heightening naga secrecy, with the shroud expected to last until shortly before the Winter Solstice 382YE.

Therunin.t: Rivers of Life infused all of Therunin's waters with healing magic, but risked stirring its vallorn, with miasma thickening and giant insects attacking isolated steadings.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Henry Ward of Upwold was targeted by Irra Harah's bounty and Thomas of Upwold helped fund the runeforge.

Verthandi.t: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the penumbral veil over Urdur also covered Verthandi.

Zenith.t: The stars vanished over Druj-occupied Zenith shortly before the Spring Equinox, and its nearness to Redoubt left the new runeforge exposed.

Beg, steal, or borrow.d: Jules i Conzara i Guerra, a Siroc trader acting for the Asavean Lord Magnus Tullis, sought relics of paragons and exemplars and asked to meet the Cardinal of Prosperity. Oswald the Red, a battlefield looter enriched by the Grendel rout in Spiral, offered mostly artisan magic items plus one supposedly Eternal artefact. Lani of the Red Hills coven sought authentication of a letter about a lost tomb linked to the divining crystal of Riqueza. Loud Pat of Beech Hill brought a Feni letter to fund repairs after a raid. A survivor of burnt Torvaldshall brought a jar said to hold a spirit. Two Navarr of Fabledwing Striding called a meeting of bestiary compilers.

Grendel.t: Following their crushing defeat in Spiral, Grendel dead and fallen have been widely looted, and many of their magic items are now being sold on, including by Oswald the Red at Anvil.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named, though the summit visitors gather at Anvil in Casinea.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Kallavesi hunters in the accompanying fiction briefly suspect the Jotun before finding the Torvaldshall survivors.

Navarr.t: Two Navarr of Fabledwing Striding arranged a Friday evening meeting in the Forge for bestiary compilers, zoologists and veterans of beast-hunting to share knowledge and plan future hunts, rescues and studies.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn feature prominently: Jules i Conzara i Guerra came to buy relics for an Asavean lord, and Lani of the Red Hills coven brought a letter tied to the fabled divining crystal of Riqueza, with a possible auction if it proves authentic.

The Marches.t: Beech Hill's alder Matt of Redston sent Loud Pat to Anvil with a captured Feni letter, hoping to sell its news to alders, beaters and other Marchers to fund repairs after the Feni raid.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: a Kallavesi warrior in the fiction compares the looting in Spiral to fighting alongside the Thule.

Wintermark.t: Torvaldshall, a small mostly Suaq hall, burned down and one survivor travelled to Anvil to sell a haunted jar, while the looter Oswald the Red planned to seek out fellow 'maggots' in the Wintermark camp, a term many Winterfolk despise.

Beg, steal, or borrow.o: Several traders, envoys and petitioners announced through the Civil Service that they would come to Anvil for the Spring Equinox 382YE, offering or seeking relics, battlefield loot, an antique Freeborn letter, a haunted jar, Feni secrets and bestiary knowledge.

Upwold/Ashbrook.t: The market town of Beech Hill in Ashbrook was raided by Feni, leaving its people mostly unharmed but its property wrecked, goods stolen and its reputation as a safe trading town damaged.
