Casinea.t: Anvil in Casinea drew all these sellers and petitioners for the Spring Equinox summit, with meetings arranged at the Forge and the Anvil Library.

Hahnmark.t: Torvaldshall, a hall on the border of Hahnmark and Kallavesa, burned to the ground and its survivors took to the floes to hunt.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fabledwing fiction recalls a successful hunt of vallorn-infested Mandowla near Twr Uchel and Bont Goch, with help from the Pride of Hercynia.

Kahraman.t: Lani's antique letter was found in a rotting attic on a Kahraman goat farm the Red Hills coven once visited.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the relic-buyer Jules i Conzara i Guerra is a trader from Siroc.

Spiral.t: After the Grendel defeat in Spiral, the plain below Solen's Doubt became an open graveyard drawing looters from many armies, and some looted items appear to be Urizeni, with murkier legal standing.

Upwold.t: A Feni band extending its raids southwards has troubled households throughout eastern Upwold, prompting Beech Hill to seek funds and sell information about them at Anvil.

Begin to speak.d: Azoth declined a parley but sent its servants to hold another night market in the Hall of Worlds on Friday night. Jaheris invited the Archmage of Summer to a parley in the grove of sighs and asked for representatives of House de Rondell. Roshanwe accepted the Archmage of Day's parley with a set guest list. Estavus declined a parley but, with the City of Gold and Lead, offered mystic scrolls for four war rituals and some warm ashes in exchange for Ephisis' Scales bargains. Tharim agreed to parley with the Archmage of Winter. Siakha demanded that the Empire, bearing the Staff of Spring, take the Stone of Storms from her Druj favoured in the Stormwood before she would send any message. Her herald then attacked citizens in Anvil.

Dawn.t: Jaheris specifically asked for representatives of House de Rondell of Dawn to attend his parley in the grove of sighs. The Archmage of Spring, Ser Fabienne De Miel, faces Siakha's challenge to bring the Staff of Spring to the Stormwood.

Druj.t: A band of Druj favoured by Siakha holds the Stone of Storms in the Stormwood, possibly supported by Siakhan heralds. The Empire is expected to fight them to the death to claim it.

Urizen.t: Two Urizen archmages were involved. Elyssiathain, Archmage of Night, was refused a parley by Azoth but offered a night market, while Ematius, Archmage of Winter, secured a parley with Tharim.

Begin to speak.o: Ahead of the 384YE Summer Solstice, six eternals answered the plenipotentiary messages sent by the Imperial archmages at the Spring Equinox. Jaheris, Roshanwe and Tharim agreed to formal parleys, while Azoth, Estavus and Siakha made other arrangements.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: The Stormwood in the Bleaks was named as the place where Siakha's Druj favoured await the Spring Archmage's force with the Stone of Storms. The conjunction was set for five o'clock on the Saturday.

The Barrens.t: A conjunction through the Sentinel Gate offered the Empire a way into the Druj-held Barrens to face Siakha's favoured and take the Stone of Storms.

Begins where it ends.d: Cathan Canae sent a castellan to parley, offering one of three generals a boon for the conquests of Ossium, Sermersuaq and Zenith, and a beacon boon to Wintermark warriors. Zakalwe declined but backed his Polemarch in Skallahn. Ephisis proposed a mutual ban on looting Grendel property in exchange for Grendel restraint, and offered Ogila's Tower in Kalpaheim. Surut agreed to parley but refused to abandon the Druj. Sadogua, furious that Varushkans took the Whistling Strand from his realm, suspended all aid and named three possible reparations. The Azoth offered boons against Cold Sun in exchange for amity. Irra Harah would discuss only the Barrens, barring titled Imperials and Varushkans.

Dawn.t: Cathan Canae's herald recalled her warriors fighting Oblivion in Dawn, while Irra Harah's parley will focus solely on what Dawn's forces did in the Barrens.

Druj.t: Surut refused the Winter Archmage's request to withdraw his aid from the Druj, saying their desperation pleases him and he will feast on their fall if they are destroyed.

Grendel.t: Ephisis offered to persuade the Grendel to stop looting and destroying Imperial wealth if the Senate outlawed robbing or destroying Grendel property, while Surut and Cathan Canae both declined to involve themselves against the Grendel.

Jotun.t: Zakalwe's Polemarch marches with the Bloodcloaks against the Jotun in Skallahn, and Zakalwe hopes his herald can discuss the war against the Jotun with the Imperial Seer.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae's herald noted that the Spears of the Pines conquered their homeland in the Barrens with Navarr aid.

The Brass Coast.t: Irra Harah was helping the Freeborn at Madruga, and Surut spoke of the inferno of bitterness the Broken Shore orcs and their allies created there; Ephisis also named the Red Wind Corsairs as looters.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua's herald suggested he could take a League city in recompense, and Ephisis cited the Wolves of War as looters and Sarvos as a city the Grendel might invade.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae's herald noted the Thule had already received a similar boon for fighting the Jotun and Druj.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua's herald recalled his boons used to move things around in Urizen, and the conquest of Zenith was among those Cathan Canae will hear about.

Varushka.t: Sadogua is furious that the Circle of Zulgan-Tash moved the Whistling Strand to Varushka and suggested the Senate cede the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, while Irra Harah barred any Varushkan from his parley.

Wintermark.t: Cathan Canae will grant a boon to two Wintermark warband leaders who fought Cold Sun at the beacons, and Ephisis offered Ogila's Tower in Kalpaheim, whose Merchant title could become a Wintermark national position.

Begins where it ends.o: Ahead of the Winter Solstice 385YE, six eternals answered plenipotentiary messages from the Imperial archmages. Cathan Canae, Surut and Irra Harah agreed to parley, Ephisis replied with offers, Zakalwe and Sadogua declined to meet, and The Azoth requested a parley of its own.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua's herald idly imagined trapping the Castle of Thorns in an hourglass as one of several reprisals he chose not to pursue.

Bay of Catazar.t: Ephisis's proposed law against robbing Grendel property would ban Imperial privateering in the bay.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: as Grendel-held land it falls only within Ephisis's general discussion of conquering territory without looting it.

Hahnmark.t: Cathan Canae praised the Winterfolk victories at the beacons here and will grant a boon to the warrior who led their warband against Cold Sun in Hahnmark.

Kallavesa.t: Cathan Canae praised the Winterfolk victories at the beacons here and will grant a boon to the warrior who led their warband against Cold Sun in Kallavesa.

Madruga.t: Irra Harah had been aiding the Freeborn at Madruga, and Surut described the bitterness kindled there by the Broken Shore orcs and their allies as a conflagration hard to outmatch.

Ossium.t: The conquest of Ossium is among the triumphs the commended generals will present to Cathan Canae's castellan for the chance of the Fist of the Black Glacier boon.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Ephisis used a possible Grendel invasion of Sarvos to illustrate that conquest would still be allowed under her proposal, but not burning or looting.

Sermersuaq.t: The conquest of Sermersuaq is among the triumphs the commended generals will present to Cathan Canae's castellan for the chance of her boon.

Skallahn.t: Zakalwe's Polemarch marches with the Bloodcloaks in Skallahn, and Zakalwe wishes to discuss the invasion's timing and challenges with the Imperial Seer at the Spring Equinox.

The Barrens.t: Cathan Canae considers the matter of ceding Barrens land to the Spears of the Pines settled, while Irra Harah will parley only about events there, citing Dourfell Keep, the Black Wind and the Vendarri.

Zenith.t: The conquest of Zenith is among the triumphs the commended generals will present to Cathan Canae's castellan for the chance of her boon.

Below the red rock.d: Four Jotun armies (the Escuta, Hierro, Skjalderborn and Corazón) faced two Imperial armies. The fortresses of Cathan Canae's heralds kept the orcs out of the mountains, so they focused on Gambit and Jade Range. They are now four-fifths of the way to conquering Gambit. The Empire won the battle west of Rojota, but lost nearly fifteen hundred soldiers over the season. No building materials were stolen, but the road project made no progress. Corazón raiders took 6 wains of mithril and 7 of white granite. Spring-magic rain fell, and the Red Depths were completed. A raiding warband, accompanied by heralds of Cathan Canae, must be stopped by the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs' general refers to the Marches answering 'the Grendel atrocities'.

Jotun.t: The Lasambrian Jotun pushed to within a fifth of conquering Gambit and stripped mithril and granite from the hills, despite their defeat at Rojota. New forces joined them, including Yantan Tethrasson's young warband and Fisher-reinforced yeggara, and there were rumours of a new Jarl of Briante.

Navarr.t: Isaella's Dance, under General Ioan Longshadow, advanced cautiously into Kahraman. It helped win the battle for Rojota but shared in losses of nearly fifteen hundred Imperial dead.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn's own territory was invaded again. The Red Wind Corsairs helped save Rojota, but their mines lost mithril and granite, road-building stalled, and the completion of the Red Depths brought a symbolic flowering to Serra Damata.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: a handful of League free warriors fought alongside the Red Wind Corsairs.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Corsairs' general praises Marcher allies, and traitorous Mournwold humans fight among the Jotun.

Below the red rock.o: In Spring 386YE the Lasambrian Jotun, reinforced by the Skjalderborn, pressed their invasion of Kahraman, while Isaella's Dance and the Red Wind Corsairs, backed by three magical fortresses in the northern peaks, held them back at heavy cost. The Empire won the battle for Rojota, but the orcs pushed deeper into Gambit and raided the territory's mines.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: The Hierro ground down resistance in Gambit, which is now four-fifths conquered. Imperial forces won the major battle west of Rojota, and the town remains in Imperial hands.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: The orc armies focused their raids and probes on Jade Range's plains. Without the Imperial armies and fortresses they would have made significant headway here, and the Blightheart threatens to spill over into the region.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: An enchanted fortress looms over Briante and kept out all but cursory raids. Corazón raiders still stole 6 wains of mithril from the Great Mine, and Chana Aran is rumoured to have been recognised as Jarl of Briante.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: Jotun scouts were repulsed from the foothills, and the Damatian Cliffs lost 7 wains of white granite to raiders. Work on the Red Depths was completed and red and gold flowers bloomed across the scarred mountains.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman remained a battleground. The Jotun advanced in Gambit and raided mines and builders, while the defences of two Imperial armies and three magical fortresses kept Rojota and the mountains in Imperial hands.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the Spring-magic rains were assumed to be an attempt to contain the Blightheart of Madruga.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the yeggara of Mournwold, bolstered by Fishers under Stephen of Sarcombe, fought with the Hierro in Kahraman.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Corsairs' general calls on the Freeborn to take the fight to the tribes of Reinos.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: an enchantment helped the Red Wind Corsairs march from Skallahn to Kahraman.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Corazón raiders targeted caravans carrying stone from Serra Damata down into Tassato.

Below the thunders.d: Seven Imperial armies, including the newly raised Narwhal's Spear, fought perhaps forty thousand Grendel and Asavean mercenaries, with Governor Rahab of Feroz present in person. Curses empowered by Siakha caused floods, monster attacks and lightning that killed around fifteen hundred and halted fighting for two weeks. The Seminary of Zemress was destroyed, the House of Guerra and Zemress Naval Academy were flooded, but the Kraken's Bane endured. Heralds of Janon helped transform the Burning Falcon, while Tharim's Winter knights left their mark on the Fire of the South. A battle opportunity at Sabadellano offered chances to kill Rahab, seize Asavean orders, rescue a defecting orc and recover a mithril map and the Star of Attar.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish Eastern Sky marched west out of Dawn with the aid of the Lord of the Crossroads, resting near Summer regio that strengthened its knights and yeofolk, and arrived fit to fight in Madruga.

Grendel.t: The Grendel, supported by their armada and Asavean mercenaries, fiercely defended Siroc Plains but were slowly pushed back towards the ruins of Siroc, and their armies and navies suffered heavily from Siakha's storm. Governor Rahab was exposed to a possible assassination at Sabadellano, and his counsellor Questioner Polh was marked for death.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs left Kahraman trusting their Imperial allies to deal with the Lasambrian Jotun.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn armies fought to reclaim Madruga as their homeland was flooded and battered, losing the Seminary of Zemress and lives at the House of Guerra. The Burning Falcon was transformed by heralds of Janon, and killing Rahab offered to halve the seasonal losses of Freeborn armies for a year.

The League.t: The Wolves of War under Marcus Derivian di Sarvos fought in Madruga, and only units supporting them received shares of the Imperial Guerdon. The Apulian magnate Leann Dubh sought to bring the defecting orc Rígbarddán to Spiral, which would boost its businesses.

Wintermark.t: The new Wintermark army, the Narwhal's Spear, marched from Sermersuaq to Madruga with the help of Suaq hunters, arriving ready to fight and bolstered by Day magic.

Below the thunders.o: In Summer 386YE the Imperial armies pressed the Grendel in Madruga's Siroc Plains while a cataclysmic storm, empowered by the eternal Siakha, ravaged the territory. The Empire made two-fifths progress towards claiming the region despite heavy losses on both sides.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: Calvos was flooded and attacked by sea monsters, sending hundreds of refugees inland, and the Seminary of Zemress was smashed to rubble by the waves.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Siakha's fane and monsters cut Free Landing off from armies unless carried by a navy, and the Freeborn Flame Marina there likely suffered major damage.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: Imperial armies advanced from Lightsea into Siroc Plains, while the flooding Aleatorio and monsters from the sea struck the region during the storm.

Madruga/Torres.t: The stream beside the Crimson Drummers shrine flooded, causing lesser damage, but the Crimson Sutannir will provide no liao or money after the Summer Solstice as they support rebuilding.

Spiral/Apulus.t: A recently arrived Apulian family and magnate Leann Dubh hoped to recover their relative Rígbarddán, whose logistics skill would improve trade in and out of Apulus for a year.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Bay rose during the storm, battering coastal towns and bringing forth monsters and storm-marked pirates. A fabled map, the Dùthcha-Éadrom, was said to show a mithril mine somewhere on its shores, which the Empire might seize before Rahab claims it.

Feroz.t: Feroz's tyrannical governor Rahab left his fortified palace to fight in Siroc Plains, and the Empire was offered a chance to kill him, though he would quickly be replaced. Losing his advisor Questioner Polh would make him more unpredictable and lead him to squeeze his subjects harder.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs left Kahraman to fight in Madruga.

Madruga.t: Madruga was ravaged by Siakha's storms, which flooded its coastal settlements, killed many and destroyed the Seminary of Zemress, while the Empire advanced two-fifths of the way towards retaking Siroc Plains.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the great thunderclap over Madruga was heard as far north as Caricomare in Sarvos.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Narwhal's Spear marched from Sermersuaq to the southern coast of the Empire.

Spiral.t: If the Stone Born commander Rígbarddán defects and reaches Anvil, businesses in Spiral will be able to diversify without charge until the Summer Solstice 387YE.

Beneath a moonless sky.d: The festival celebrates the victory over the Cult of the Falconer and years of good relations fostered by Raal Dunn, Mediator of Hyljehal. Koskinen warned that the orcs of Fjorknae, paid with Meade's plundered gold, had sent a warband to aid the Lasambrians, raising the risk of piracy. Rebuilding a smuggler's cove in Tromsa would open the voyage Sail into the Cold, and later Raid into the Cold. He asked for a Wintermark story performance, offering hylje tales of Sermersuaq and the Rusalka in return. Given three measures of stardust, the hylje could aid exploration of Tsirku, with more help possible if the Empire took Skyfall Waste and the Icewood.

Jotun.t: The orcs of Fjorknae give fealty to a Jarl of Jarls, though nobody knows which. The hylje would offer their fullest help with Tsirku only if the Empire seized Skyfall Waste in Tromsa from the Jotun.

Wintermark.t: Up to fifty Wintermarkers were invited to an unprecedented hylje festival, with the Mediator of Hyljehal asked to arrange a story performance and to bring stardust. Wintermark fleets were also offered a scouting voyage against Fjorknae.

Beneath a moonless sky.o: Koskinen, son of one of the Palliko who lead the hylje, invited up to fifty Wintermarkers, explicitly including Steinr and Kallavesa, to the hylje Festival of Autumn's Easing at the coming Autumn Equinox. He also raised three matters to prepare for beforehand: a threat from Fjorknae, an exchange of stories, and hylje help exploring Tsirku.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: Holding the Fount alongside the Suaq Wastes, Skyfall Waste and the Icewood would give the Empire control of access to Tsirku's southern lakes. Hylje-aided scouts would cross Nutjuitoq rather than head north-west from the Fount.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: The hylje would aid scouts crossing Nutjuitoq into Tsirku from the Suaq Wastes. Keeping the Wastes is part of controlling access to Tsirku's southern lakes.

Tromsa/Icewood.t: If the Empire held the Icewood along with Skyfall Waste and the Suaq lands, it would control access to Tsirku's southern lakes, letting the hylje move freely between them.

Tromsa/Skyfall Waste.t: Seizing Skyfall Waste from the Jotun would let the hylje also aid exploration of Karnakadatha's region and raise their help to two fifths for both regions.

Fjorknae.t: Its little-known orcs had been paid by the Lasambrians to send a large warband, might stay or even send a navy, and were once close to the violent akhlut. A Wintermark voyage could reveal who they are and whom they serve, then turn to raiding their settlements.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Koskinen believed some smiths of Hahnmark know how to make the stardust the hylje need.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Kallavesa are named as good friends of the hylje and expressly included in the festival invitation.

Sea of Snow.t: Koskinen warned of a heightened risk of piracy for those sailing the Sea of Snow, given the activity of the Fjorknae orcs.

Sermersuaq.t: Home of the Hyljehal and the Suaq, the hylje's close kin, Sermersuaq was to be enchanted by a hylje ritual of Autumn magic during the festival. The hylje would also tell their tale of the legendary Sermersuaq herself.

Tromsa.t: Re-establishing a smuggler's cove in Tromsa would restore intelligence gathering there and open the Sail into the Cold voyage. Taking Skyfall Waste and the Icewood from the Jotun would greatly increase hylje help in Tsirku.

Tsirku.t: With three measures of stardust to protect them from the Northern Lights, the hylje offered to aid exploration of the region containing Nutjuitoq, cutting the scouting needed by a fifth. With Skyfall Waste in Imperial hands, they could also aid with Karnakadatha's region, cutting it by two fifths for both.

Beneath mithril spires.d: Commonwealth siege engineer Poldi Hellebrant praised the new embassy and docks under construction at Hedra in Necropolis, though she worried about Jarmish and Commonwealth ships sharing the Couros river. The war with Jarm over Lantir is expected to be long. Militärattache Ludkhannah Schöningen regretted the Senate's refusal to let captains fight Jarm, thanked the Empire for gifts of mana, and dismissed concerns about the Freedom Accord. The Commonwealth tactfully declined to approve contact with the Viyerda. The Asavean bounty has cut Commonwealth shipping, which boosts Imperial fleets trading there. The Senate raised no motions on the Viyerda or on exploring the Sea of Steel, and enthusiasm for exploration faded.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: their armies are used as a yardstick for the scale of the Jarmish war, and they are named among the slaving neighbours the Commonwealth thinks the Empire should focus on.

Grendel.t: The Grendel invasion of the Brass Coast destroyed the old embassy. The Commonwealth doubts it could stop the Grendel accepting Asavean help, and the trapped Lyceum magicians ask whether to prepare for another Grendel attack.

Highguard.t: The replacement Commonwealth embassy is being built at Hedra in Highguard's territory of Necropolis, and a Commonwealth siege engineer praised its land, progress and modern docks.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: their armies help illustrate the scale of the Jarmish war, and they are listed among the slaving neighbours the Empire is urged to fight.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn Assembly's call for captains to explore eastwards fed interest in a Sea of Steel expedition. The page also recalls Freeborn and Commonwealth soldiers fighting together at Siroc and the loss of the old embassy to the Grendel invasion.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the page names no Urizen people or deeds directly. Its link is through the Lyceum, whose Dean the Ambassador is asked to consult about the Commonwealth magicians sheltering behind its misty wards.

Beneath mithril spires.o: In Autumn 386YE the Civil Service reported on relations with the Commonwealth, the Empire's closest great-power ally. Topics included a new embassy at Hedra, the Commonwealth's war with Jarm, polite opposition to Imperial contact with the Viyerda, a possible Sea of Steel expedition, and Asavean pressure on trade.

Necropolis/Hedrossan.t: The town of Hedra is the site of the new Commonwealth embassy, where engineer Poldi Hellebrant reported favourably on the land, the construction and the modern docks.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Mentioned in passing: Longbeach is not named directly; it is linked through the embassy works in Necropolis and concerns about Commonwealth and Jarmish ships sharing the Couros river.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's detailed charting of the Bay is cited as something impossible to repeat across the vast Sea of Steel.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the Commonwealth magicians trapped on the Lyceum isle ask whether Madruga is still in enemy hands.

Necropolis.t: Work on the new Commonwealth embassy is under way at Hedra, praised for its modern docks. Its closeness to Cargo and the Jarmish embassy raises concerns about rival ships sharing the Couros river.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named on the page and is linked only through the Lyceum and the Commonwealth magicians sheltering there.

Benevolence, inspiration, and legacy.d: The General Assembly upheld Severin von Holberg's mandate (886–232), which sent him with liao to remind citizens of their shared belief in the virtues. His sermon argued that Benevolence, Inspiration and Legacy are the signs that should guide everyday action. Its effect is that attempts to stir religious conflict are strongly inhibited for a year, muting outrage over the Suranni enslaving rebels in Feroz, the Iron Helms' deadly strike in Spiral, the Zemress Islanders, the Yaelites and the Asavean Architect. In response, moderates under Teodora Bezavina proposed stripping the National Assemblies of statements of principle, while radicals under Bishop Orlando di Holberg proposed abolishing them. Scholars suggested cutting the paragon signs to three, which reopened debates about miracles, exemplars and the Sumaah.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; the page refers only to the Iron Helms' strike on the Black Plateau in Spiral, which Grendel held that season.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly's rejection of Yael is noted, and a Highborn movement is pressing to undo Atuman's demotion. The radicals' plan would also change Highguard's senators to be chosen by its priests rather than a National Assembly.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the nation's founding is cited as a Legacy, and Bloodcrow Ergot's statement urging the orcs to ignore some ancestors is given as a potential source of division that the sermon helped suppress.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn shock at the Suranni enslaving rebels in Feroz and anger at the deaths caused by the Iron Helms have been kept from erupting by the sermon. Religious differences with the Zemress Islanders have also been set aside for now, though hostility to Varushka endures.

The League.t: The League's Severin von Holberg, Bishop of Ambition, authored the mandate and sermon. Bishop Orlando di Holberg of the University of Holberg leads the radicals calling for the National Assemblies to be disbanded.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the sermon reached congregations in Sarcombe, and the Mournwold slaughter is said to remain fresh in people's minds.

Varushka.t: Western anger at the Iron Helms' brutal tactics has been stifled, so no one is openly denouncing Varushka, but the Coast and Wintermark remain hostile, and that hostility now seems set to endure. Varushkans also feature in the debate: Teodora Bezavina of Delev speaks for the moderates and Vera Runova Helgrod faces the Sumaah question.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark remains openly hostile to the Varushkans after rejecting their cruel ways, though the sermon has kept that hostility from becoming active agitation. The sermon was also preached in Gildenheim.

Benevolence, inspiration, and legacy.o: In Spring 382YE, Severin von Holberg's General Assembly mandate urging unity around the Seven Virtues was spread across the Empire as a sermon on the signs of Benevolence, Inspiration and Legacy. It damped religious conflict for a year and prompted proposals to curb the National Assemblies and revise the Doctrine of the Paragons.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Mentioned in passing: Holmauer is named as one of the places where congregations heard Severin's sermon.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: some theologians argue that true followers of the Way, the Sumaah included, take their instruction from Bastion.

Feroz.t: The Senate's invitation to the Suranni ended with the rebel camp's occupants enslaved, which deeply shocked the Freeborn. Only Severin's sermon has kept people from speaking out and appealing to the Synod.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is home to the sermon's author, Severin von Holberg, and to the radical Bishop Orlando di Holberg of the University of Holberg.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory's only link is the constitutional scholar Teodora Bezavina of Delev, who speaks for the moderates seeking to curb the National Assemblies.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold slaughter is cited as still fresh in the minds of many in the West.

Spiral.t: The Iron Helms struck the heart of the Black Plateau, killing hundreds of Imperial soldiers through magical whiplash and madness. Severin's sermon has stifled calls for the Synod to act over it.

Best beware my sting.d: Writing to the Castle of Thorns, the Earl of the Groves voiced 'deep concern' that some in Dawn reject his nobility, and invited sixteen nobles to a feast at the Red Hall, reached by a conjunction during the Autumn summit. Guests are protected by hospitality, but yeofolk are not, apart from the two knights-errant who accepted his test of mettle. He staked his remaining favour, a gift from Penni the White, against the favours taken from him, with Clevis, a herald of Tharim, judging. Yeofolk followers led by Tristan Seneschal planned to attend the Guising Fayre. Hugh de Veran's Throne Room restoration was finished, and the National Assembly may urge him to research Penni the White, the First Empress or another monarch.

Dawn.t: Dawnish nobles were invited to the manticore's feast and wager, and holders of its favours were given the final say over who attends. The National Assembly also had the chance to direct Hugh de Veran's research, perhaps towards how Penni the White avoided the manticore's sting.

Best beware my sting.o: The manticore calling itself the Earl of the Groves invited sixteen Dawnish nobles to a feast in the Untrod Groves, where it offered its last favour from Penni the White in a wager of oratory. Separately, some of its yeofolk followers planned to visit Anvil, and the historian Hugh de Veran could be steered towards researching a particular pre-Imperial monarch.

The Barrens/The Untrod Groves.t: A conjunction was due to open to the Red Hall, the Earl's home in the Untrod Groves, admitting sixteen guests to the feast and wager.

The Barrens.t: The self-proclaimed Earl continued to press its claim to Dawnish nobility within the newly conquered Barrens, now hosting a feast for Dawn's nobles on its lands there.

Better world.d: At the Autumn Equinox 381YE Barbara Radz made it a crime in Rigia to kill or mistreat slaves, required them to be fed and watered, and told eastern princes to match her laws or leave her alliance, leaving her position precarious. The Synod was offered mandates urging Imperial captains to trade with Rigia rather than Vezak or Kavor, and the General Assembly passed one. Soon after, Soreana of Borașova, Tuernin of Limitu and other northern princes, after consulting Anton Trescher, supplied white seed through the Jarmish lodge in Tassato. It increases mana site yields for a season with steep diminishing returns, cannot be made in the Empire, and its price rose by about a fifth after the Winter 382YE sanctions on Jarm.

The League.t: League mana site owners gained the chance to buy white seed from the Jarmish merchants trading out of Tassato, and League alchemists such as Jaffo were among those examining the substance on behalf of figures like Prince Maria.

Better world.o: Magician-Prince Barbara Radz of Rigia reformed the treatment of slaves in her principality and demanded the eastern alliance follow. Weeks later Prince Soreana of Borașova and other northern princes began selling beloye zerno, or "white seed", a Jarmish mineral that boosts crystal mana production, to Imperial citizens through the Jarmish traders in Tassato.

Tassato.t: The Jarmish lodge in Tassato, already known for its work with the Tassato Mana Exchange, became the sole point of sale for white seed in the Empire after a heavily armed Jarmish vessel delivered the first shipment shortly before the Winter Solstice.

Between peace and hate.d: The Thule delivered about 150 human slaves freed from the Bonewood to Ivarsgard, postponed ransom talks and rejected the Imperial claim to Sungold Pass. The Great Forest orcs described the Mallum and offered scouts to map it. The Thralls in the Mournwold refused to cooperate with magistrates. Grendel pirates continued to penalise trading fleets. The Jotun were angered by undead and the destruction of the Meeting Place, while the Lasambrians demanded Segura and Feroz. Druj envoys offered Urizen a ceasefire bound by Sorin's oath. Afterwards the Conclave agreed to share a ritual with Otkodov, the Varushkan assembly sent Belakov to examine the slaves, and the Senate declined the mapping but resumed the Holt of the Oak.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: a handful of the freed slaves at Ivarsgard have links to Dawn.

Druj.t: Druj envoys, backed by a herald of Sorin, offered the leaders of Urizen a ceasefire covering Morrow and adjacent territories, sealed by a sanguine oath. Meanwhile the Great Forest orcs revealed what they knew of the Mallum's lands, fortresses and slave labour.

Grendel.t: The Grendel armada stayed anchored off Sarvos, while independent pirates, some serving Siakha, raided Imperial shipping. Innevia, daughter of Salt Lord Moorvain, and fifty other prisoners were released after negotiations with General Talbot.

Highguard.t: Highguard trading fleets faced a one-rank production penalty from Grendel piracy. The Great Forest orcs offered their scouts to their Highguard and Navarr allies, and a few of the freed slaves have Highborn links.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thralls prefer to deal directly with representatives of the Imperial Orcs and the Marchers, and Marchers noted the travelling Thralls were clearly not from Skarsind.

Jotun.t: The northern Jotun held all of Sermersuaq and were enraged by risen dead and the destruction of the Meeting Place, yet Queen Yrsa Jansdóttir sent a message to the Military Council. The Lasambrian Jotun demanded Segura and Feroz in exchange for a ceasefire.

Navarr.t: Around two hundred Great Forest orcs now walk the trods with Navarr stridings, and the Thule were bringing a dragon-made ritual text for the vate Merel. The Senate approved resuming work on the Holt of the Oak.

The Brass Coast.t: The Lasambrian Jotun claimed Segura and Feroz as ancestral lands and offered peace only if both were ceded or conquered, promising that Freeborn who stayed could join their nation. Brass Coast fleets also faced the Grendel trade penalty.

The League.t: Fleets from Tassato and Sarvos suffered the Grendel piracy penalty as the armada stayed anchored off Sarvos. The senator for Sarvos had seconded the motion claiming Sungold Pass.

The Marches.t: Marchers struggled to adjust to the Thralls of the Mournwold as brawls broke out and the orcs refused to help magistrates, following Anna Pernn's statement of principle. A trio of Thralls clashed with Faraden in Hay.

Thule.t: The Thule held the Bonewood, freed its human slaves to Karsk, denied using forced cannibalism, delayed ransom talks and rejected the Imperial claim to Sungold Pass. Grand Warlock Fljajokull's visit led the Conclave to agree to share a ritual with Otkodov.

Urizen.t: The Druj insisted on presenting ceasefire terms only to Urizen's leaders, offering an oath enforced by Sorin. Urizen fleets also faced the Grendel trade penalty.

Varushka.t: Most of the 150 freed slaves at Ivarsgard were Varushkan or of Varushkan descent, and the national assembly sent Belakov the Wolf of Karsk to examine their true nature. Imperial and Thule forces were also in a standoff at Sungold Pass.

Wintermark.t: An emissary of the Queen of Kalsea approached Wintermark's armies near Sealtoq. The Jotun blamed Imperials for smashing the Meeting Place stone but saw a contradiction with Wintermark's honourable conduct, leaving a chance to restore trust.

Between peace and hate.o: In Winter 382YE, the Empire's orc neighbours stirred on several fronts. The Thule freed Druj-held slaves into Karsk and disputed Sungold Pass, the Great Forest orcs offered intelligence on the Mallum, the Lasambrian Jotun issued an ultimatum over Segura and Feroz, Grendel pirates harried the Bay of Catazar, and the Druj sought a ceasefire with Urizen.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: A Thule warband emerged from the hills of Krevsaty to deliver the freed slaves to Ivarsgard.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thralls seemed reluctant to cross the Greensward south into Kahraman.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: Thule warriors conquered and held the Bonewood and freed all of its roughly 150 human slaves, while the fate of its far more numerous orc slaves remained unknown.

Otkodov/Nithoggir.t: Mentioned in passing: in the opening tale, a dragon ordered a merchant to send word to Nithoggir after surveying the mine.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: Mentioned in passing: new Thule towers at Crow's Keep overlook the passes into Urdur.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: The Queen of Kalsea's emissary approached the Wintermark armies camped south of the ancient town of Sealtoq.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule fortifications at Crow's Keep overlook the passes into the Silver Peaks.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: Small groups of Jotun raiders were sighted as far east as Pakaanan's Pass.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Senate approved resuming work on the Holt of the Oak fortification in the Lower Tarn Valley.

Volodmartz/Opascari.t: Sungold Pass, claimed by the Senate as part of Opascari, remained in an Imperial–Thule standoff, with a historical research investigation of the ruins commissioned.

Bay of Catazar.t: Independent Grendel pirates, including bloodthirsty Siakha worshippers with sharks and unnatural weather, stepped up raids on Imperial trading ships in the Bay.

Bregasland.t: Jotun scouting parties were reported in Bregasland's marshes, and some adventurous Thralls travelled there from the Mournwold.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest orcs offered support against the vallorn here, with details given elsewhere.

Feroz.t: The Lasambrian Jotun claimed Feroz as ancestral land and demanded it be ceded or conquered before they would make peace.

Forest of Ulnak.t: The Great Forest orcs described a huge slave-worked mine, rich weirwood groves and an immense fortress said to house a powerful buruk tepel master of poisons.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thralls seemed oddly reluctant to travel south into Kahraman.

Kallavesa.t: Jotun scouting parties were reported tentatively exploring the marshes of Kallavesa.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: the senator for Karov, Vuk the Wolfeater, had proposed the motion claiming Sungold Pass.

Karsk.t: Nearly 150 freed slaves were delivered to Ivarsgard, leaving the town unsure whether to welcome them, and Belakov the Wolf of Karsk was sent to examine them for interlopers.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: some Thralls travelled north into Mitwold after the harvest.

Morrow.t: Druj envoys and a draughir herald approached the Imperial position in Morrow under a flag of truce to propose a ceasefire.

Mournwold.t: The Thralls brought in their harvests and went to fairs, but brawls followed and they refused all cooperation with the magistrates, while doubts about their faith persisted.

Ossium.t: Thule warriors conquered and held the Bonewood and freed its human slaves, while the Great Forest orcs, never sent there by the Druj, sought to walk the trods into it.

Otkodov.t: Peace with the orcs of Otkodov held, though they pressed their claim to Sungold Pass. The Conclave declared it would share a ritual with them.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: The Great Forest orcs described watery plains and the port of Leen, which they believe is the Mallum's largest settlement and a place where the Grendel trade.

Sarangrave.t: The Great Forest orcs described the Sarangrave as fertile slave plantations with an ancient white-granite fortress and a malignant presence in the marsh.

Sarvos.t: The Grendel armada remained anchored off Sarvos, and its trading fleets faced the piracy penalty.

Segura.t: Three Lasambrian Jotun armies made inroads into Segura and demanded the whole territory, offering a Spring Equinox summit if the remaining regions were ceded.

Sermersuaq.t: The Jotun still held all of Sermersuaq after undead rose from its battlefields, and Wintermark's armies camped there received the Queen of Kalsea's emissary.

Skarsind.t: Thule work on Crow's Keep continued apace, with completion expected before Summer 383YE, and Jotun raiders were sighted at Pakaanan's Pass.

Tassato.t: Tassato's trading fleets suffered the Grendel piracy penalty, and some Thralls travelled there from the Mournwold.

The Barrens.t: The Great Forest orcs described the Barrens as the Druj's coveted hub for moving armies. The Imperial spy network there had been destroyed but could be rebuilt.

Therunin.t: The Great Forest orcs remained in Therunin, dealing with Senator Cybi Farkas, and the Senate approved resuming work on the Holt of the Oak there.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: some Thralls travelled north into Upwold after the harvest.

Volodmartz.t: Imperial and Thule forces watched each other over Sungold Pass, which Otkodov refused to concede, and the Minister of Historical Research commissioned further investigation of the mine.

Between stone and salt.d: More than twenty-five thousand Imperial soldiers, joined by fey warriors of the Queen of the Pennants, invaded Mareave. The Brine Turtles and Salt Lord Ehsan's soldiers were badly outnumbered. Icarion fell, and the walled town of Rathmonna in Nadir held out for a fortnight. The defenders then rallied at the Gate of Storms in Eoradal, leaving the Empire a fifth of the way to taking that region. The Brine Turtles lost perhaps five for every Imperial casualty. The page also sets out opportunities for the coming battle: slaying drake warbeasts, bribing the Dracaild of Rathmonna and the Red Ibis, buying Sannite contracts, finding a map to Rucraic's Aerie, and hiring the Gaineamh Tine.

Grendel.t: The Grendel lost Icarion and Nadir, and the Brine Turtles suffered heavy casualties largely alone. Soldiers openly asked where the rest of the Grendel were, while locals voiced resentment at the Council that had sent no reinforcements.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Winter Sun fought in the invasion, and some Sannites found lost family in Eoradal, with mixed results. There was friction with the Sunstorm over how to treat Mareave's orcs, and a deal was offered to free hundreds of enslaved orcs for the Sannite sept.

The League.t: The Towerjacks broke Rathmonna's walls and the Seventh Wave located the Gate of Storms, as the League went to war for the first time as five cities. Apulian's new orc citizens welcomed the armies warmly, and the Red Ibis offered paid intelligence.

Urizen.t: Many of the Imperial captains' warbands with the Golden Axe were Urizen, and some Urizen eagerly explored the Skouran ruins of conquered Mareave. Meanwhile Apulian's citizens feared the Urizen rebels in Ankra and Cinion.

Varushka.t: The Golden Axe led the invasion with almost seven thousand Varushkans, in the spirit of the Vard, and were the first to set foot in Mareave. Their general was offered the chance to hire the Gaineamh Tine to ransack the region.

Between stone and salt.o: In Winter 385YE four Imperial armies, the Golden Axe, Towerjacks, Seventh Wave and Winter Sun, marched from Apulian in Spiral into Grendel-held Mareave. They conquered Icarion and Nadir and began pushing into Eoradal.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: the seat of Salt Lord Ehsan, whose garrison soldiers fought alongside the Brine Turtles but were disliked by the locals.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: The Empire is about a fifth of the way to conquering this ruin-strewn hill region, where the Brine Turtles hold the Gate of Storms. Slaying the Grendel drakes or finding a hidden map to the Aerie could tip the balance.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Icarion was the first region to fall, conquered by Imperial troops after the outnumbered defenders fell back, and some slaves were freed from its mines.

Mareave/Nadir.t: Nadir was conquered after Rathmonna fell to the Towerjacks within a fortnight. The Dracaild of Rathmonna now threatens to loose drakes on Imperial supply lines unless paid sixty thrones.

Spiral/Ankra.t: Mentioned in passing: Apulian's citizens feared what the Urizen rebels in Ankra might work against them.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Mentioned in passing: Apulian's citizens feared what the Urizen rebels in Cinion might work against them.

Spiral/Screed.t: Mentioned in passing: the grim oppression emanating from Screed made the march miserable and tormented the soldiers' dreams.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the Winter Sun's general speaks only of striking the Grendel before they can set the Imperial coast ablaze.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks' engineers from Holberg drew interest in Apulian, and Holberger immigrants there spread fearful tales of the Blight.

Mareave.t: Imperial armies conquered the northern hills of Icarion and Nadir and made inroads into Eoradal. The Brine Turtles held out from the Gate of Storms, and the territory's free, independent orcs took to the hills.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the armies gathered at the Court of the White Fountain as guests of the sentinels before marching into Spiral.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvosi immigrants in Apulian fuelled local fears with stories of the Doom that befell their former homes.

Skarsind.t: A few orcs from Eoradal resolved to come north to Skarsind with Sannite relatives. A proposed deal with the North Mareave Trading Consortium could free hundreds more to join the Sannite sept there.

Spiral.t: The armies marched through Spiral under Screed's oppressive aura to Apulian, where citizens cheered them south while fearing Grendel reprisals and the Urizen rebels.

Between the lines of ages.d: Irra Harah agreed to send a herald for a second parley with the Spring archmage on Friday at eight. Sinokenon, saying nothing had changed, will still send a mandarin to hear the Day archmage and invited cardinals at ten. The Lictors accepted a formal parley at eleven, with three questions and three answers. Rhianos's heralds will hear tales of adventure, especially against the Grendel, on Saturday at two. A gloomy Sadogua, mourning Richard of Holberg, will attend at half past eight and asked for a named group to gather by nine for a task. Skathe will meet the Winter archmage and the Wisest Senator about Zephaniah's Lament on Saturday at eleven, but only if the Conclave first grants her amity.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Ser Fabienne De Miel, Archmage of Spring, secured a second parley with Irra Harah's herald, and Sadogua asked for the most glorious witch-adept of Night lore in Dawn to join his gathering.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Irra Harah is credited with helping to free prisoners held by the Druj in the Barrens.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Rhianos helped the Empire secure the chance to attack the Grendel stronghold of Beoraidh, and wants to hear tales of the Empire's ventures against the Grendel.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Brother Luke of the Shattered Tower, Archmage of Summer, will host Rhianos's heralds, who expect him to gather storytellers with tales of daring adventure.

Imperial Orcs.t: Skywise Gralka, Archmage of Day, secured a formal parley with Sinokenon's mandarin alongside Synod cardinals, while Sadogua sought a representative of the Circle of Zulgan Tash, and Irra Harah was credited with resettling orcs freed from Dubhtraig.

Navarr.t: Navarr's Syn Truth-Walker Returned, Archmage of Winter, was invited with the Wisest Senator to meet Skathe about Zephaniah's Lament, provided the Conclave grants her amity first.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua's gloomy mood stems from the recent death of his long-time friend Richard of Holberg, the magical architect.

Urizen.t: Two Urizen archmages secured meetings: Edmundo of Damakan's Forge a formal parley with the Lictors, and Elyssiathain a parley with Sadogua, who asked for help gathering a special group.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua named Sovica of Varushka, or someone she appoints, among those he wants gathered for a task.

Between the lines of ages.o: Following the Spring Equinox of 383YE, six eternals (Irra Harah, Sinokenon, the Lictors, Rhianos, Sadogua and Skathe) answered the Imperial archmages' plenipotentiary messages and agreed to meetings at the Summer Solstice, one of them conditional on amity.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the death of the magical architect Richard of Holberg is the reason given for Sadogua's dark mood.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Irra Harah is credited with helping bring the lost orcs liberated from Dubhtraig to new homes in Skarsind.

Between two mounds.d: After the Freeborn raised a mound over the Jotun champions who died at Fort Braydon, a ghodi speaking for King Gudmundur of Narkyst sought leave to build a fire-filled bowl from nine wains of mithril honouring the Freeborn. The Assembly could allow it, turn her back, guard her, or let the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills raid Liathaven to seize her and the mithril. She also asked why the Freeborn fight alongside servants of the King in Chains. In Tromsa, Jarl Ustigar asked Generals Iron Osric and Lofyn Blood-Cloak to swear that no ally would loot Majastind, resting place of Ulven. Any of the seven armies there could loot it this season. Meanwhile almost a thousand Sermersuaq thralls were freed.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun King asks why the Freeborn fight 'like the Druj' and march alongside corrupted knights bound to the King in Chains.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Jarls fear that the Imperial Orcs, who grow ever closer to their own ancestors, might seek out Mount Majastind to steal the Jotun ancestors. Their army in Tromsa is one of those that could choose to loot it.

Jotun.t: The Jotun reached out on two fronts. The King of Narkyst sought to honour his fallen champions and questioned Freeborn honour, while the Jarl of Kierheim pleaded for the safety of Mount Majastind, where Ulven and many ancestors lie with great treasures and artefacts.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn had to decide whether to permit, refuse, guard or plunder the ghodi's mithril monument. They were also challenged by the King of Narkyst to explain why they raise barrows for Jotun dead yet fight beside servants of the King in Chains.

The Marches.t: The Jarls distrust the Marchers in Tromsa despite their recent efforts to reclaim their honour, because they unleashed curses on their own people in the Mournwold barely half a decade before.

Wintermark.t: Generals Iron Osric and Lofyn Blood-Cloak were asked to swear an oath before the egregores that their allies would not despoil Mount Majastind. Separately, the thralls taken from Sermersuaq were returned under a deal struck with the General of the Green Shield.

Between two mounds.o: In Autumn 385YE the Jotun sent envoys to the Empire. A ghodi asked the Freeborn's permission to crown the burial mound at Braydon's Jasse with an ever-burning mithril bowl, while in Tromsa the Jarl of Kierheim asked Wintermark's generals to swear that their allies would not despoil the sacred Mount Majastind.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: The burial mound of the Jotun champions stands here, and it is where the ghodi proposed to raise her ever-burning mithril bowl honouring the Freeborn.

Tromsa/Majastind.t: Mount Majastind holds Ulven's bones, many other ancestors, great wealth and at least three artefacts. An Imperial army fighting in Tromsa that targeted the region this season could loot it, unless Wintermark's oath prevented this.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: some Sermersuaq thralls had been made to work Jotun estates in Hordalant before their release.

Kahraman.t: The Freeborn raised a burial mound over the Jotun dead here. An unarmed ghodi then studied it and announced plans to return after the Autumn Equinox to build a burning mithril monument, unless the Assembly mandated otherwise.

Kallavesa.t: The Jarl of Kierheim compared Majastind to the sacred marshes of Kallavesa and implied that the marshes could face Ulvenwar reprisals if the Jotun tombs were looted.

Liathaven.t: The ghodi was expected to carry nine wains of mithril through Liathaven, where the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills could order a lightning raid to capture her and the metal.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the deaths of thralls in the Mournwold are cited as the stain on Jotun honour that keeps the King from making peace.

Sermersuaq.t: Almost a thousand thralls taken from Sermersuaq during the Jotun conquest were released and escorted in good health to Olgafsdottirshal, to great celebration.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: some Sermersuaq thralls had been made to work Jotun estates in Skallahn before their release.

Tromsa.t: With Imperial armies invading, the new Jarl Igya Olgafsdottir refused to yield and offered battle to capture Mathilda Fisher. The Jarl of Kierheim came north to plead for Mount Majastind.

Between wind and water.d: The Thorns of a Rose, a weaver cabal in Culwich, prepared three bondrings for Claude Cutter, Roland Singer and Tristaine Tiller, to be hallowed by Dawnish priests. Earl Mathilde Courcillon offered to rebuild a chapel in Ferrond near Elayne Silverlark's empty tomb, which would create the Troubadour of Auvanne. Earl deGramont proposed Greenwood Manor and an expanded Greenforest Fair at Racqueen in Elvette, creating the Knight of the Greenwood and the Reeve of Greenforest Fair. Lady Eleanor Novarion drafted a mandate inviting Marracossan refugees in Trajadoz to the House of the Proffered Hand, and proposed it at the Winter Solstice. The Senate did not support Greenwood Manor, but it was later built under an Imperial Wayleave and both titles became active.

Dawn.t: Dawn's troubadours, knights and priests were offered several opportunities: bondrings for its prize-winning storytellers, a chapel and the Troubadour of Auvanne title, Greenwood Manor with titles for both a noble and a yeofolk, and a mandate to draw Asavean followers of the Way into Dawnish life.

Navarr.t: Navarr thorns had found succour at the deGramont estate during the struggle against the Heirs of Terunael, and Navarr stridings leaving Brocéliande regularly stop at Racqueen, where an expanded fair was expected to draw still more of their traffic.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marracossan refugees whom Dawn hoped to invite to Astolat were then living in Trajadoz in Madruga.

Between wind and water.o: In Winter 383YE, three Dawnish statements of principle from the Autumn Equinox inspired offers to Dawn: a weaver cabal's gifts to award-winning storytellers, a proposed troubadours' chapel in Semmerholm, a proposed manor and fair for knights questing against the vallorn of Brocéliande, and a possible Synod mandate to welcome Marracossan followers of the Way to Astolat.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Mentioned in passing: the in-character tale of a poisoned Argent Dawn knight and her retainer takes place in a storm on the edge of Boar's Dell.

Semmerholm/Elvette.t: The deGramont estate near Racqueen in Elvette was the site of the proposed Greenwood Manor and expanded Greenforest Fair, which were later built under an Imperial Wayleave.

Semmerholm/Ferrond.t: Earl Mathilde Courcillon offered to rebuild her chapel in Ferrond, overlooking Endric's Hill and Elayne Silverlark's empty tomb, as a ministry and venue for the Troubadour of Auvanne; the page records no outcome for this offer.

Astolat.t: The House of the Proffered Hand in Astolat, overseen by Lady Eleanor Novarion, was proposed as the new home for Marracossan refugees who follow the Way, with any resulting problems falling to her to resolve.

Brocéliande.t: The roused vallorn of Brocéliande was the main target of the proposed Greenwood Manor, which was eventually built to encourage Dawnish knights to quest against it and to trade the treasures recovered from its ruins.

Madruga.t: A community of Marracossan former slaves living in Trajadoz was the subject of a proposed Dawnish mandate to persuade them to resettle at the House of the Proffered Hand.

Semmerholm.t: Two Semmerholm noble houses made offers: Earl Mathilde Courcillon a troubadours' chapel in Ferrond, and Earl deGramont Greenwood Manor and an expanded Greenforest Fair in Elvette, the latter eventually completed.

Weirwater.t: The Thorns of a Rose, a weaver cabal from Culwich led by Sibylla, offered three bondrings to Dawn's prize-winning storytellers and promised a yearly Fireglass to any troubadour who holds the Troubadour of Auvanne title.

Beware my power.d: Freeborn magicians raised storms off Spiral that battered shipping in the north-eastern Bay of Catazar and may have hampered Asavean granite shipments to their orc allies. Magical fortifications rose in Kallavesa and Necropolis, though neither was attacked. Sentinel Gate conjunctions behaved oddly, apparently because of the fallen red star. Spring magic healed Cinion and its fire-scarred soldiers, but the overgrowth tore apart ruined spires and damaged Damakan's Forge; one Winter-tainted grove resisted the healing. A surge of healthy, mostly green-eyed babies followed last year's Hallow of the Green World. The Silver Mask persona emerged among the Dawnish. Tamarbode remains under Llofir's control, and the Semmerlak is calm again.

Dawn.t: Dawnish guiser troupes created the Silver Mask, a new minor persona of the Captain, and some Dawnish actors claim it is a real, masked Dawnish figure behind tales of spies and hidden justice.

Grendel.t: Grendel's orcs in the ruins of Apulian may have lost Asavean deliveries of white granite to the storms, and it is unclear whether any Grendel navies in the Bay were battered.

Highguard.t: Magical fortifications rose in the woodlands of Necropolis, and Highborn magisters judged that the Llofir occupying Tamarbode in Reikos is playing a long game.

Navarr.t: Navarr vates agreed that Llofir is interested in the long game, and its servants showed no sign of entering Elerael. Some of the most traditional Navarr voiced concern that the many new green-eyed babies carry the briar lineage.

The League.t: League guisers spread wild tales of an incarnated Silver Mask, and a vindictive play by an anonymous Tassato playwright imagined horrible fates for Guillermo di Tassato.

Urizen.t: Urizen citizens spent three months cutting back the overgrowth that threatened Damakan's Forge in Cinion and saved its central parts. However, the damage means any runeforge project there needs a new costing from the civil service.

Wintermark.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven and Sherard Hunters kept wielding powerful magic for the Empire, and magical castles rose in the marshes of Kallavesa.

Beware my power.o: In the run-up to the Winter Solstice of 380YE, a scattering of magical effects was felt across the Empire. Freeborn storms struck the Bay of Catazar, Spring magic rejuvenated Cinion, a new Silver Mask persona emerged, the Semmerlak grew calm, and a hidden conjunction of the Key, Lock and Spider with the Wanderer appeared.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Llofir's servants in neighbouring Tamarbode showed no interest in poking around Elerael.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Tamarbode remains under Llofir. Only the mana site of Tamar's Toes is accessible, where gatherers report watchful creatures and mould-infested clothes, and a living fungal castle reportedly still stands at the Sign of Tamar.

Spiral/Apulus.t: The storms probably stymied Asavean vessels carrying white granite to their orc allies in the ruins of Apulian.

Spiral/Ateri.t: A story circulating in Ateri claims at least one Asavean galley was caught by the storm and smashed against the southern cliffs.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Spring magic healed Cinion's fire damage and its injured, but overgrowth destroyed ruined spires including Ossen's Spire and damaged Damakan's Forge. One small burnt grove, infused with Winter magic and possibly a nascent regio, is being watched by illuminates.

Bay of Catazar.t: Freeborn storms battered ships in the north-eastern Bay, and astronomancers sailed out onto its open waters to see the hidden stars.

Brocéliande.t: The servants of Llofir showed no interest in crossing from Tamarbode into Brocéliande's region of Elerael.

Kallavesa.t: Magical fortifications rose in Kallavesa's marshes and would have hindered any attacking army, though no barbarian attack came this season.

Necropolis.t: Magical castles rose in the woodlands of Necropolis, ready to impede attackers, though the territory was not attacked this season.

Reikos.t: Reikos's region of Tamarbode remains under Llofir's control, but its servants showed no interest in exploring the rest of Reikos.

Spiral.t: Massive storms off Spiral's coast hampered shipping from the war-torn territory and Asavean supply runs. Meanwhile, Spring magic healed the fire damage in Cinion but wrecked ruined spires and parts of Damakan's Forge.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: an anonymous Tassato playwright wrote a vindictive Silver Mask play about Guillermo di Tassato, and the page recalls Piero of Both Banks in first-century Tassato.

The Semmerlak.t: The Semmerlak's troubles ended. Its waters turned placid and warm, fisherfolk landed bumper hauls, and its odd folk apologised after the Lady of the Semmerlak was reportedly rescued from a curse.

Beyond the light.d: Ossium remained under-developed, underpopulated and under threat from lingering Druj, while bandits and roused wolves preyed on settlers crossing Karsk. Military units could take one of three independent actions. Wagon raiding meant fighting Druj and seizing caches. Sellswords would protect settlers and vales. Wardens would explore the territory and contact isolated humans and non-Druj orcs. The combined strength committed would decide overall success, and the strongest action would shape the Spring opportunities. Each action also risked trouble: with the eternal Arhallogen, with the bandits of Karsk, or with the Thule. Several mandates were enacted to back all three approaches, including Varushkan, Imperial Orc, Dawnish and Navarr ones.

Dawn.t: Dawn's armies had done most of the fighting to conquer Ossium. Pelleas Montrose enacted the mandate urging Dawnish knights-errant and questing knights to join the wagon raiders against the Druj, which promised Dawn a Spring opportunity to tackle the under threat problem if the effort succeeded.

Druj.t: Druj guerrillas, holdfasts and the Arhallogen-linked temple in the Webwood were the targets of the wagon raiders and their allies, and the Druj still threatened to return through Ossium's eastern forests.

Imperial Orcs.t: Skywise Tulva's statement of principle was followed by Bloodcrow Udoo enacting a mandate sending Imperial Orc preachers to reach out to Ossium's remaining orcs and support the wardens. This promised an opportunity to deal with the territory's independent orcs.

Navarr.t: Nathair Autumngale enacted a Navarr mandate encouraging guides to help Varushkan wardens reach isolated settlements in Ossium, adding its strength to the wardens' action on top of the Varushkan support.

The League.t: The League had already given a home in Holberg to former Druj-ruled orcs. Its assembly was offered a mandate to send mercenaries and towerjacks to support the settlers, though the page does not record it being enacted.

Thule.t: The Thule of Otkodov held Bonewood and still resented being refused the chance to recruit Ossium's orcs. Explorers straying into their lands risked giving them grounds to seek reparations from the Empire.

Varushka.t: Varushka's assembly drove the effort to secure its new territory. Varushkan mandates were enacted backing wagon raiders, wardens, and sellswords who would seek out former Druj slaves to found new vales. Meanwhile the boyar of Isember planned to visit Anvil amid concerns over banditry in Karsk.

Beyond the light.o: In Winter 383YE, following calls from the Varushkan National Assembly, military units, armies and national assemblies were offered the chance to help secure the newly conquered territory of Ossium. They could do so through wagon raiding, supporting settlers, or venturing into the unknown.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers of Bittershore had been offered a new home in Holberg by the League.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: The Thule held Bonewood, and enthusiastic wardens or adventurers risked straying into it, prompting delicate negotiations and possible demands for reparations.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: If the wardens' action led a major victory, the Drownbark Forest would lose its underpopulated quality as former Druj subjects joined Varushka and founded new vales there.

Ossium/Echofell.t: If wagon raiding led a major victory, Echofell would lose its under threat quality, with the Tower of the Scorpion becoming the centre of a garrison keeping the woods clear of orcs and dangerous insects.

Ossium/Galath Fields.t: Mentioned in passing: explorers from northern Galath Fields might easily stray across the forest border into Thule territory.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: If supporting the settlers led a major victory, Nearweald would lose its under-developed quality as its vales received vital support and supplies.

Ossium/Webwood.t: The spider-haunted Webwood held the worst Druj enclaves, a miasma pillar and Arhallogen's temple, which the Conclave had declared the eternal's property. Wagon raiders might take charge of the region but risked clashing with Arhallogen's followers, and settlement there was excluded under the settlers' action.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as the place where Arhallogen secured Druj warriors to aid the Navarr during recent troubles.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: noted as the territory Dawn's armies were invading while the Dawnish knights were urged to fight in Ossium.

Holberg.t: The League had offered Holberg as a new home to the Sand Fishers of Bittershore, with the Senate ceding a region of it to these former Druj subjects.

Karsk.t: Bandits were preying on settlers and supply wagons heading for Ossium, and the violence had stirred up undead and monstrous wolves along the roads. Supporting the settlers risked making the Karsk bandits bolder, while the boyar of Isember sought talks over concerns about his vale.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova is not named directly on the page.

Ossium.t: Ossium was the focus of the opportunity, under-developed, underpopulated and under threat from the Druj. A major victory could strip one of these qualities from a region, and success would bring further Spring opportunities.

Otkodov.t: The Thule of Otkodov, whose ambassador was Yevgeni Katzev, could seek reparations if Imperial adventurers trespassed into their lands in Ossium.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: many former orc subjects of the Druj had left Ossium to seek new homes in Skarsind.

Beyond this dark house.d: The Gryphon's Pride, Northern Eagle and Iron Helms pushed into the Echofell while two Thule armies from Otkodov held defensive positions alongside the garrison of Flajokep. The Druj had already gone. The Imperial forces, helped by magical defences in the Drownbark Forest, mopped up the remaining raiders, though the region stayed under threat. The Thule then returned to the Bonewood. Druj damage to the Bone Hives during the Summer Solstice means the Keeper of the Bonehives receives no production until Spring 385YE. Lise de Lionsgate has proposed rebuilding the ruined tower as the Tower of the Manticore. A conjunction on Petka's Path offers a chance to stop Druj sappers before the Drownbark Forest becomes contested.

Druj.t: The Druj armies abandoned Ossium after destroying the Tower of the Scorpion and retreated into the Forest of Ulnak. Their raiders still lurk in the Drownbark and Echofell, and a band of sappers is tearing up roads and bridges along Petka's Path.

Thule.t: Two Thule orc armies marched out of Otkodov to defend Ossium alongside the garrison of Flajokep, aiding the humans as the Dragons willed. They then returned to the Bonewood once the territory was secured.

Varushka.t: The Northern Eagle and Iron Helms helped restore Imperial control of the Echofell, but Varushkan hold on the Drownbark is threatened by Druj sabotage. The Keeper of the Bonehives will receive no production until Spring 385YE because of the earlier Druj attack on the hives.

Beyond this dark house.o: In Autumn 384YE, Imperial armies and Thule forces arrived in Ossium to confront the Druj, only to find that the orcs had already withdrawn into the Forest of Ulnak, leaving the Tower of the Scorpion in ruins. The Echofell was quickly brought back under Imperial control, but a Druj sabotage raid in the Drownbark Forest created a new threat.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule returned to the Bonewood once Ossium was as secure as it could be.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Magical defences here helped Imperial forces deal with raiders, but Druj sappers are now wrecking roads and bridges on Petka's Path. A conjunction offers a chance to stop them; if they are not stopped, the region will become contested.

Ossium/Echofell.t: The Imperial armies found the Druj gone from the Echofell and quickly brought it back under Imperial control, though it remains under threat. The proposed Tower of the Manticore would permanently remove that threat.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: Mentioned in passing: Petka's Path, the road being sabotaged by the Druj, links the southern coast through to the Nearweald.

Forest of Ulnak.t: The Druj armies withdrew from Ossium back into the shadowed depths of the Forest of Ulnak, from where they continue to threaten Ossium's eastern borders.

Ossium.t: With the Druj armies gone, Ossium was largely secured, though raiders remain in its eastern regions. A proposal to rebuild the ruined tower as the Tower of the Manticore would add a fortification on its eastern border.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the two Thule orc armies that went to defend Ossium marched out of Otkodov.

Bills or bows.d: Inspired by popular love for their generals and Friar John's mandate, all Marcher armies may now fight shoulder to shoulder, holding the line with bill blocks and archers. For one year, the Senate could commission the Drakes' enlargement for 125 wains of mithril or weirwood, with wealthy yeomen covering the money. A motion to do so was brought, but the page does not record its outcome. The Bounders and the Strong Reeds could each change quality for 25 wains. Abbot Thomas Arch supplied 44 wains of mithril and 6 of weirwood, so the Bounders became watchful and the Strong Reeds secretive. The Tusks' general appointment will move to the Spring Equinox from 384YE.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: a pair of Jotun orcs are seen meeting a poacher at the edge of the Mourn in the opening story, and the Strong Reeds are noted for their history of resisting Jotun aggression.

The Marches.t: Every Marcher army can now fight shoulder to shoulder. The Bounders became watchful and the Strong Reeds secretive, the Drakes were offered an enlargement, and the Tusks' general appointment is being moved to the Spring Equinox.

Bills or bows.o: Following Friar John of the Mourn's Autumn mandate, which urged Marchers to defend their land without drowning it in blood, every Marcher army gained the defensive order to fight shoulder to shoulder, and several Marcher armies were offered new ways to fight during Winter 382YE.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Mentioned in passing: in the opening story, a poacher from Alderly Edge is seen secretly meeting Jotun at the edge of the Mourn.

Bregasland.t: The Strong Reeds, long tied to Bregasland's people, turned back to old fen-honed stratagems and became a secretive army able to lay low in marsh, forest and mountain regions.

Mitwold.t: The Drakes, many of whose soldiers come from Mitwold, were offered the chance to be enlarged and armed with bills or bows, funded by wealthy Marcher yeomen and 125 wains of mithril or weirwood.

Mournwold.t: The Mandate came from Friar John of the Mourn, and recruits from the Mournwold have swelled the Drakes' ranks. Its barren mountains are named as the kind of terrain where the newly secretive Strong Reeds can lay low.

Upwold.t: The Bounders, built around Upwold beaters and landskeepers, gave up their slaughtering tactics to become a watchful army able to harry the flanks or watch the passes.

Birds.d: Much of Zoria's story was lost when Nicovar burned the great libraries. At the Spring Equinox, the Varushka and Wisdom Assemblies recognised her maze in Gniejezdo as her original shrine. The maze, whose most recent guardian Domagoj Gnietzen vanished over two years ago, had languished. A rival site, a cave beneath Black Hill in the Opascari mountains, was looted by Thule raiders over a century ago. A shrine would cost 18 wains of white granite and 36 crowns at the maze. Its guardian would gain 9 liao and 18 Synod votes and might collect tales of Zoria. The Senate commissioned the shrine at the maze.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Starac Sijed, the maze's former guardian, gave up that charge when he and his family left Varushka for Dawn.

Thule.t: A Thule raiding party attacked and looted Zoria's Cave over a century ago, carrying off whatever was kept there. No one has ever been able to ask them what they took.

Varushka.t: Varushka gains a renewed focus on its patron of wise ones, with the Senate commissioning a shrine at Zoria's Maze. Its guardian might be elected by the Varushkan National Assembly and could gather the vales' scattered tales of her.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the stone tablet at the heart of Zoria's Cave is carved with hundreds of Wintermark runes.

Birds.o: Following two Synod judgements naming the Vale of Gniejezdo in Miekarova as the first shrine of Zoria, the Varushkan Paragon of Wisdom, an opportunity arose to build a great shrine in her honour. During the Summer Solstice the Senate commissioned Zoria's Maze to be transformed into such a shrine.

Miekarova.t: The neglected maze in the Vale of Gniejezdo, Miekarova, was chosen as the site of the new shrine to Zoria. Its nearby chapel was to be greatly enlarged to welcome pilgrims.

Mountains of the Moon.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial scouts found the territory guarded by a twisting maze known locally as the Maze of Zora, almost certainly unconnected to Zoria.

Birds and bats.d: Lashonar's herald delivered a sonnet proposing a contest of real love letters, open to anyone whose name was placed in a vessel in the Hall of Worlds; Rossignol would visit those named at Anvil. Sadogua, distressed at losing the Empire's amity, sent Neora of Spiral, a young girl with a potent naga lineage, to request a parley under the Archmage of Night. He wished to discuss saving the Halls of Knowledge from the Druj, offer to reforge or restore rare items he had given Imperial magicians, ask about a certain weirwood tree, and discuss the Dark Moon legacy. The parley took place on Saturday night; its content stayed private, but after the Winter Solstice the Halls of Knowledge vanished from Zenith, whether through a deal with Sadogua or Druj machinations.

Druj.t: Sadogua framed his parley around saving the Halls of Knowledge from the Druj, and their later disappearance may have been the result of some Druj machination.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua's young naga-blooded messenger gave her name as Neora of Spiral, a territory held by the Grendel.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the in-character fiction features Richard of Holberg, a Leaguer, trying to explain to Sadogua why the Conclave was displeased with him.

Urizen.t: The Halls of Knowledge in Urizen's territory of Zenith, which Sadogua claimed he could help save from the Druj, vanished mysteriously shortly after the Winter Solstice.

Birds and bats.o: Two eternals of the Night realm approached the Imperial Conclave: Lashonar announced a love-letter writing contest run by his herald Rossignol, and Sadogua, the Brother of Wizards, sent a herald to request a formal parley. The parley was granted, and shortly after the Winter Solstice the Halls of Knowledge vanished from Zenith.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg appears only in the name of Richard of Holberg, a character in the opening fiction.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua's messenger introduced herself as Neora of Spiral.

Zenith.t: The Halls of Knowledge vanished from Zenith under mysterious circumstances shortly after the Winter Solstice, possibly through an arrangement with Sadogua or Druj machinations.

Bits and bobs.d: Bourse prices appeared to be falling: the Canterspire Circle sold for 260 thrones, down from 405, and mithril, weirwood and white granite were cheapening. After letters from Else Van Temeschwar and Laurencio di Sarvos and a Vigilance judgement, several options were laid out. The Senate could let the Master of the Mint publish summaries of treasury reports (+5 thrones upkeep). It could commission an appraisal to find tax opportunities. It could relinquish national Bourse seats, though any affected national assembly could veto this. It could abrogate or freeze all ministries, or turn tenured sinecures into annual Bourse auctions. Auditor Gerard La Salle offered to attend Senator Miaren's economics forum.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposal to build a grand lodge for the Golden Pyramid in Grendel's Mareave is cited as an example of an opportunity that raised tax revenue.

Navarr.t: Llewellyn Leafstalker, the Navarr Senator for Miaren, booked the Senate chamber for an economics forum, which the Imperial auditor Gerard La Salle offered to attend to answer questions.

The League.t: League citizens drove the concern, with Else Van Temeschwar and Laurencio di Sarvos writing to the Constitutional Court. The League-held Master of the Mint might gain the power to publish treasury summaries, though any reduction in its status could lower what League citizens pay for the seat.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the focused appraisal previously carried out on Wintermark's Sermersuaq is cited as an example of how a narrow appraisal can uncover every opportunity.

Bits and bobs.o: Amid falling Bourse seat prices and dropping wain values, concerned League citizens and the Vigilance Assembly pressed for action on the Empire's finances, and the Civil Service set out options open to the Senate, from publishing the Mint's reports to reallocating Bourse seats, curbing ministries and auctioning sinecures.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposal for a Golden Pyramid grand lodge in Mareave is given as an example of an opportunity that boosted a territory's taxation.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Miaren, Llewellyn Leafstalker, is hosting an economics forum in the Senate chamber at Anvil.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the economist Laurencio di Sarvos raised questions with the Constitutional Court, including the estimate of seventy-two tenured sinecures that might be auctioned.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the earlier appraisal of Sermersuaq is held up as a model of a focused appraisal.

Temeschwar.t: A League Assembly judgement called for trading posts across Temeschwar to turn the Empire's surplus metal into coin, but the page notes such ministries would require an appraisal or extensive diplomacy to achieve.

Bitter and absolute.d: Having raised former slaves only to serf status, the Suranni had played the Empire and the Asavean-backed Freedom Accord against each other for concessions. The Ducal Council would now befriend anyone friendly to them, though it left the door open to a stronger stance later.
