The Senate's Free Trade treaty and narcotics ban, meant to last three years, had boosted Suranni trade, mostly via the Brass Coast. Sarcophan vessels had become a regular presence at Robec. Separately, Suranni salvagers asked Golden Fleet Salvagemaster Caleb of the Cenotaph to clear ghosts from the sunken Singing Riqueza, a deep-water task only merrow could undertake.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a Suranni count recalls a former Imperial ambassador hiring a duke's orcs to fight the Grendel, and wonders whether there were any Grendel to fight.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast merchants benefited from the rise in Suranni trade, which flowed mostly through their lands, and Tethros i Zuhri i Erigo of the Brass Coast was still serving as Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy pending the Senate's Winter decision.

Bitter and absolute.o: The Iron Confederacy's Ducal Council declared strict neutrality between the Liberty Pact and the Freedom Accord, refusing to sign either and offering to deal with any nation on an issue-by-issue basis. The Civil Service's seasonal briefing also covered growing Suranni trade through the Brass Coast and a haunted Golden Fleet ship.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is not named on the page; the link appears to be the underwater salvage of the haunted Golden Fleet ship Singing Riqueza.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: although Feroz was described as largely back in Imperial hands, Suranni caravans still preferred to trade through Segura instead.

Madruga.t: The unnatural marshes spreading across southern Madruga frightened Suranni merchants, who called them Dumon's Sump and spread tales that they were full of infernal forces.

Segura.t: Segura became the favoured route for Suranni caravans trading with the Empire, even with Feroz largely back in Imperial hands.

Veroigne.t: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni ambassador's seat, the Tour Lavasse in Chaubrette, apparently lies to the west of Veroigne.

Black and white.d: While searching for troll artefacts, Peter of Hintown's party found unworked mithril near where the glacier meets the sea, and experts confirmed a significant deposit. Exploiting it needed a Senate motion: 100 Thrones for a mine producing 10 wains a season, or 200 Thrones for deeper workings producing 15. The find would create a Bourse seat, either Imperial or national to Wintermark. Advisers warned that the site lies close to Jotun and Thule lands and to whatever might emerge from Tsirku or the glacier, and urged a fortification. At the Winter Solstice Senator Atte provided 200 Thrones and work began, with completion projected for Autumn 380YE. No fortification was built. Prospectors were sent in Spring 382YE.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: a Winterfolk expedition member grumbles that the Senate might take the find away and give it to the orcs.

Jotun.t: The Empire was already at war with the Jotun, and the mine's closeness to Jotun lands was named as a serious threat to the new resource.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the discoverer, Peter of Hintown, is a Marcher who longs to be back home in Bregasland.

Thule.t: The mine lies close to Thule lands and would come under immediate threat if hostilities with the Thule were renewed. Peter is also investigating a possible link between the Thule invasion and the trolls.

Wintermark.t: The mithril was found in Wintermark's Sermersuaq, so a national Bourse seat would fall to Wintermark, normally appointed by its captains. Senator Atte funded the mine's construction.

Black and white.o: Peter of Hintown's expedition to the Face of Ikka in Sermersuaq, sent to research troll ruins, found a sizeable vein of raw mithril in caves near the great glacier on the border with Tsirku. The Senate went on to commission a mine there.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: The new mithril mine is being built on the edge of Suaq Fount. Advisers urged a fortification there to protect it and the Face of Ikka artefacts, but none was commissioned.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Peter of Hintown remembers its Feni-haunted drowned ruins with unexpected nostalgia.

Sermersuaq.t: A significant mithril deposit was found at the Face of Ikka, and the Senate commissioned a 200-Throne mine there, projected to be ready by Autumn 380YE.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: not named on the page; the only link is an expedition member's fear that the find might be handed to the orcs.

Tsirku.t: The mithril find lies on the glacier border between Tsirku and the Empire, and any horror emerging from Tsirku would likely fall straight on the mine.

Blackest night.d: Scholars at Iteri's Observatory of the Blazing Mirror built a device with Camillius of Endsmeet to study the star. Rumour says their spire fell and its magicians died. The star is visible only in parts of the north, which suggests powerful magic. Its impact would devastate the region it struck, and every resource in Miekarova improved beyond level one would lose a level. Day and Night magic might divine where it will fall, and Autumn magic might shift its path, but no Imperial ritual exists and any working would need to be done in Miekarova or at the Anvil regio. The empty skies spread to Necropolis, Bregasland and Segura. By the resolution the star had grown further, but the Phoenix was plainly visible again.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star could be seen over Wickmoor and Sandling in Weirwater.

Highguard.t: The empty-sky phenomenon spread over Necropolis, leaving only the moon and clouds visible at night and unsettling those who studied it.

Imperial Orcs.t: The skies over Skarsind stayed empty of stars except for the crimson star, and naga who spent long periods there found their secretive urges greatly strengthened.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star could be seen in the northern sky over Hercynia.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast astronomancers were among the first to report the new star, and the empty skies spread over Segura.

The League.t: Holberg remained under the empty, starless skies, and naga who spent long periods beneath the city's inky black sky found it hard to speak openly about their intentions.

The Marches.t: The empty-sky phenomenon spread to Bregasland, leaving its night skies bare of stars.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the star appeared to hover above the mountains separating the northern Empire from the lands of the Thule.

Urizen.t: Scholars of the Observatory of the Blazing Mirror in Iteri tried to study the star closely, and rumour says their spire fell and all its magicians died as a result.

Varushka.t: The star was visible over all of Varushka, and divinations warned that it would strike Miekarova, with devastating loss of life and resources if it hit an important region.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible over Sermersuaq and over Northspires and Bruckland in Hahnmark.

Blackest night.o: In summer 380YE the nameless red star, now detached from the Wanderer, grew brighter in the northern sky, and every divination agreed it would fall on the Empire, almost certainly somewhere in Miekarova. Meanwhile the starless 'empty skies' spread to new territories and the Phoenix constellation faded almost from sight.

Hahnmark/Bruckland.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible in the night sky over Bruckland.

Hahnmark/Northspires.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible in the night sky over Northspires.

Karsk/Moresvah.t: A cabal charged with the vales of Moresvah confirmed through observation and Night magic that the star would fall in Miekarova, but its elders decided it was not their concern.

Weirwater/Sandling.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star could be seen over Sandling.

Weirwater/Wickmoor.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star could be seen over Wickmoor.

Zenith/Iteri.t: Iteri's Observatory of the Blazing Mirror built a device to view the star, and its spire is rumoured to have fallen, with all its magicians dead.

Bregasland.t: The empty skies spread to Bregasland, so that by night nothing but the moon and clouds could be seen.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star could be seen low in the northern sky over Northspires and Bruckland.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible in the northern sky over Hercynia.

Holberg.t: Holberg's night skies stayed empty of stars, and naga who lingered there found their secretiveness markedly intensified.

Karsk.t: A Karsk cabal tracked the star's approach and foresaw its fall in Miekarova, but its elders chose to leave the problem to the cabals of Miekarova.

Miekarova.t: Divinations pointed to Miekarova as where the star would fall: one region would be utterly devastated, and every resource improved beyond level one would permanently lose a level. Any ritual to divert it would have to be performed there or at the Anvil.

Necropolis.t: The empty-sky phenomenon spread over Necropolis, leaving its nights starless and unsettling to those who studied them.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the page refers only to the mountains that separate the northern Empire from the lands of the Thule.

Segura.t: The starless empty skies spread over Segura, and naga who spent long there found their urge towards secrecy greatly strengthened.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible in the northern sky over Sermersuaq.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind's night sky remained empty of stars, yet the crimson star was clearly visible there, the only thing besides the moon that could be seen.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star could be seen over Wickmoor and Sandling.

Zenith.t: The Observatory of the Blazing Mirror in Iteri attempted to study the star, and rumours say its spire fell and its magicians perished.

Blood and gold.d: The General Assembly had declared the vallorn the greatest spiritual threat to the Empire, but the Empire's wars took precedence and the opportunity in Liathaven was likely to pass. Morgan of Brock Bottom Steading argued that a testimony was poor thanks for Marcher losses. He proposed a Navarr-built wayhouse in Upwold, stocked by a national mandate, to give the Marches a permanent herb sinecure. He also suggested ceding the Treji Memorial Gardens to the Imperial Orcs. Weirwood from the Thimble might resupply the Black Thorns if emergency resupply were permitted. Proposed mandates could pressure Imperial and Urizen units to fight in Liathaven. The Constitutional Court rejected Magistrate Abraham's challenge to the testimony judgement.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Urizen Assembly said reclaiming Zenith from the Druj must not come at the expense of fighting the vallorn.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step had once aided the Highborn in plague-stricken Reikos, and a Highborn magistrate unsuccessfully challenged the Navarr testimony judgement.

Imperial Orcs.t: Morgan suggested the Senate make the Keeper of the Memorial Gardens at Treji an Imperial Orc appointment, as real thanks for the Summer Storm's help in retaking Hercynia and to win orc support against the vallorn.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: neither the Military Council nor the Throne seemed inclined to campaign in Liathaven, even to retake it from the Jotun.

Navarr.t: The Navarr lacked the support to exploit the vallorn's weakness, with the Quiet Step under the Empress's command and the Black Thorns close to breaking. They were offered ways to win allies, including herb sacrifices, ceding the Treji gardens and pushing a General Assembly or Assembly of the Nine mandate.

The Marches.t: The Marchers had borne most of nearly fifteen hundred deaths in Liathaven. Their armies had withdrawn, and Morgan proposed a Navarr-built Upwold wayhouse to give Marcher farmers a permanent sinecure of 30 herbs a season.

Urizen.t: The Urizen Assembly declared that the fight against the vallorn in Liathaven should take precedence over liberating Zenith. A proposed mandate would cost Urizen units two ranks of morale if they did not support an Imperial army in Liathaven.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as an example of gratitude for giving Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs in thanks for the Crown of Three Tears.

Blood and gold.o: In Summer 382YE, with no Navarr army in Liathaven and the Marcher armies withdrawn, the Navarr faced losing a rare chance to strike at the weakened vallorn. Several proposals arose from recent Navarr and Urizen Assembly judgements to win allies and support for the fight.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Morgan's steading lies deep in Hercynia, and the Summer Storm's help in retaking the territory was cited as a debt poorly repaid.

Liathaven.t: A rare window to fight the vallorn in Liathaven was closing, with no Navarr army there and the Marcher armies withdrawn. Proposed mandates sought to draw Imperial and Urizen forces back to fight there.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step had fought in Reikos when it was plague-stricken, to help the Highborn.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as Wintermark's gift to the Imperial Orcs in thanks for the return of the Crown of Three Tears.

Therunin.t: The Thimble weirwood forest in Therunin, still producing 20 wains a season under Idris Eternal, was suggested as the source for resupplying the Black Thorns and funding Morgan's proposals.

Upwold.t: Morgan proposed a Navarr wayhouse in Upwold, costing 15 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns. Backed by a Navarr mandate, it would become a Marcher-appointed sinecure producing 30 herbs a season.

Zenith.t: The Urizen Assembly judged that liberating Zenith from the Druj should wait while the chance to fight the vallorn in Liathaven was seized.

Blood and mire.d: After the Druj invasion and the spilling of the Sephals Cauldron, roughly thirty thousand Imperial soldiers advanced, led by the Black Thorns. They were joined by twelve thousand Navarr-led warbands, a thousand Spears of the Pines and six thousand Knights of Glory serving Eleonaris. The Druj were cleared from the Lower Tarn Valley, which is now poisoned, and nine-tenths of the way out of Eastring. Nearly two thousand Imperial soldiers died in Eastring, which became haunted. The Towerjacks built temporary forts in Peakedge Song. A battle opportunity at Ashborder in Sweetglades offered a chance to stop two plans: a Siakha-empowered deluge that would flood East Ashes and destroy the Docks, and Cintra Blackstaff's ritual to rouse the vallorn.

Dawn.t: The Golden Sun and the Gryphon's Pride marched from the Barrens to secure land and root out hidden Druj. Dawn's Knight-protector of Spring, Doctor Henri, was charged with stopping Druj ritualists from cursing the Barrens with storms.

Druj.t: The Druj brought in at least three more armies and fought a cautious, venomous campaign. Even so, they lost the Lower Tarn Valley and nearly all of Eastring, though they kept uncontested hold of East Ashes and the Feverwater Docks, where their ghulai prepared a 'cataclysm'.

Navarr.t: Navarr warbands formed the bulk of the twelve thousand who rallied to the Black Thorns to reclaim their homeland. Their steadings were left ruined, their dead haunt Eastring, and the vallorn now threatens to be woken against them.

Urizen.t: Druj ritualists threatened the Churnspire in Peregro. A flooded East Ashes would also cut army movement from Therunin into Morrow's Peregro and Zenith's Lustri.

Varushka.t: The Northern Eagle and the Iron Helms marched from Ossium to aid their Navarr cousins, with Ser Gaspare's Knights of Glory fighting beside the Northern Eagle.

Blood and mire.o: In Autumn 386YE six Imperial armies, alongside Navarr warbands, Great Forest Orcs and Knights of Glory, drove the Druj out of Therunin's Lower Tarn Valley and broke most of their hold on Eastring at a terrible cost. The Druj kept East Ashes and the Feverwater Docks and began preparing a magical cataclysm.

Morrow/Altis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks pushed up through Altis on their way into Peakedge Song.

Morrow/Peregro.t: The Shuddering Wrast advanced into Peregro to raze the Churnspire, and its Adjutor, Sejanus of the Scarlet Guard, was charged with stopping them. Flooding in East Ashes would cut Peregro off from Therunin for a year.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: The Sephals Cauldron's poison had been meant to taint the lake at Hope's Rest, but overturning it in the Tarn Valley left Hope's Rest safe for now.

Therunin/East Ashes.t: East Ashes stayed under uncontested Druj control, ringed with walls of poison thorns, while ghulai gathered at the Feverwater Docks. An empowered Thunderous Deluge would make the region impassable for a year and sink the Docks.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Eastring saw the most brutal fighting, amid Night-magic wards, and nearly two thousand Imperial soldiers died there. Druj control is almost broken, but the region is now haunted by Navarr and Druj dead.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Druj were driven out entirely, but the cauldron's spilled poison has left the valley poisoned, killing trees and fouling the waters.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Druj scouts reached its eastern steadings, and the Towerjacks raised temporary forts there, including a spiked palisade around Peakedge Stand. If Blackstaff wakes the vallorn, at least fifteen thousand vallornspawn could pour into the region.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: The Druj pushed into the vallorn woods at Ashborder, where a battle opportunity offered the chance to stop the Blood Drainers' deluge and Cintra Blackstaff's ritual to rouse the vallorn. The ground is thick with vallorn miasma and Druj-driven giant insects.

Zenith/Lustri.t: If East Ashes floods, armies could no longer move between it and Lustri. Lustri's forests are also the only escape for Druj trapped in East Ashes.

Morrow.t: The Towerjacks advanced through Morrow into Therunin, while the Shuddering Wrast moved into Peregro to destroy the Churnspire. If East Ashes floods, the route between Peregro and Therunin would be closed, leaving only Peakedge Song open.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Northern Eagle and Iron Helms marched into Therunin from Ossium, and veterans of the war in Ossium served among them.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Mentioned in passing: the Blood Drainers, the Druj coven favoured by Siakha, were believed to hail from the far east of the Salt Flats.

Sarangrave.t: The invasion was launched from the marshes of Sarangrave, and the defeated Druj fell back through Eastring towards it. Cintra Blackstaff has strong ties to the Palace of the Sleepers there.

The Barrens.t: Two Dawnish armies and the Spears of the Pines marched south from the Barrens, and Hope's Rest was spared the cauldron's poison. Druj ritualists headed for the Swirling Cavern regio in the Untrod Groves to curse the territory with Thunderous Deluge.

Therunin.t: The Empire retook the Lower Tarn Valley and most of Eastring, leaving one poisoned and the other haunted, while the Druj kept East Ashes and the Feverwater Docks. Druj plans threatened to flood East Ashes and wake the vallorn, and Black Wind raiders were attacking Axou traders in the west.

Zenith.t: A flooded East Ashes would block army movement to Lustri. Any Druj trapped in Therunin might try to break south into Zenith's forests, and the Druj fear a repeat of their losses during the liberation of Zenith.

Blood makes noise.d: Sellswords, wagon raiders, wardens, Dawnish knights, Navarr scouts and Imperial Orc preachers poured into Ossium. Thanks to Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov's mandate, the effort focused on freed slaves, who established vales in every region except the Thule-held Webwood and Bonewood. Ossium is now firmly Varushkan, and Nearweald lost its under-developed quality. On offer are several opportunities: sharing the Crawling Depths with local boyars; Lise de Lionsgate's proposed Tower of the Manticore; Ketsov or Senate use of the Mir Mozga in Karsk; and a military assault on Isember, whose bandits attacked Kosti. The Menrothat sept offer black lotus for Farweald, and a conjunction could rescue soldiers trapped at Beetle Tree in Ulnak.

Dawn.t: Dawnish knights and yeofolk flocked to Ossium alongside the Hounds of Glory, and Lise de Lionsgate proposed rebuilding the Tower of the Scorpion as the Tower of the Manticore. The Dawnish Assembly may also urge glory-seekers into Ossium and Ulnak, and a few hundred Ossium natives are petitioning to join Dawn.

Druj.t: The Druj lost their former slaves to Varushka's new vales. They have a force waiting at Beetle Tree to trap Imperial survivors fleeing the Forest of Ulnak, and they still hold Menrothat orcs under their yoke.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a Varushkan mandate would penalise units taking part in the land-based evacuation of Grendel-held Feroz.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: several Highborn are listed among those who ventured into the unknown or went wagon raiding in Ossium.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orc preachers led by Bloodcrow Udoo drew more Ossium orcs to Skarsind and made contact with the Menrothat. The sept offers them a dose of black lotus, and knowledge of its use, if the Empire cedes Farweald.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: a Varushkan mandate would make Varushka opt out of the raid on Jotun-held Skallahn described in another wind.

Navarr.t: Navarr scouts sent by Nathair Autumngale's mandate helped the settlement, escorted orcs to Skarsind and helped Ossium natives who wished to join the Great Dance.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: a couple of Brass Coast characters are listed among those who aided Ossium.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: several League characters are listed among those who supported the settlement, ventured into the unknown, or went wagon raiding in Ossium.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: a handful of Marchers are listed among those who aided Ossium.

Thule.t: A disciplined Thule force was claiming the land the Senate had ceded to them in Ossium, and no new Varushkan vales were founded in the Thule-dominated Webwood and Bonewood. The Ketsov are courting Thule merchants, and Isember's bandits trade with Thule-held Oloy.

Varushka.t: Varushka gained many new, fervently orthodox citizens and vales across Ossium. It now faces choices over the distrusted Ketsov and the Mir Mozga, and may pass a Synod mandate rallying Varushkans to destroy the bandit haven of Isember.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: two Wintermark characters are listed among those who aided Ossium.

Blood makes noise.o: In Spring 384YE, with Synod backing and the support of the Golden Axe and the Hounds of Glory, former Druj slaves joined Varushka and founded new vales across Imperial Ossium. The wind also set out several opportunities: sharing the Crawling Depths, rebuilding the Tower of the Scorpion, the Ketsov claim on the Mir Mozga, an assault on bandit-held Isember, and a Menrothat offer of black lotus.

Karsk/Kopevnost.t: Bandits from Isember raided the town of Kosti, but its walls and some vigilant local children foiled them. Kosti's wise ones, led by Valya Sofyn Kosteva, are now calling for Isember's destruction.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: Mentioned in passing: Isember's boyar is said to trade with the town of Oloy in Thule-controlled Krevsaty.

Karsk/Lestasny.t: The ruins of Isember, ruled by the outlaw boyar Alexi Iskandrova Isembrioch, are the target of a proposed assault. The untamed Mir Mozga nearby is sought by the Ketsov for a new vale.

Karsk/Moresvah.t: Miners from Moresvah help work the Crawling Depths in Ossium, and Moresvah families would assist if the mine were shared with Ossium's boyars.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: Bittershore remains under-developed and gained new vales; some of its former residents chose to petition Dawn instead.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: The Bonewood remains Thule-dominated with no new Varushkan vales, though the Ketsov have begun forestry south of it.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Konstantin's outpost near Marshstand Skerry shelters natives wary of the settler-boyars, and Menrothat orcs live in the east. Sharing the Crawling Depths would remove the region's under-populated quality.

Ossium/Echofell.t: The Tower of the Scorpion stands here, and rebuilding it as the Tower of the Manticore would remove the region's under threat quality. The Menrothat also tend the Bone Hives here.

Ossium/Galath Fields.t: The Galath Fields remain under-developed, and some former residents sought to join Dawn. A crushing success against Isember, or the Crawling Depths arrangement, could remove a negative quality here.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: Nearweald lost its under-developed quality thanks to the settlement effort and is home to Menrothat settlements.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Webwood remains Thule-dominated, with no new Varushkan vales founded there.

The Barrens/Farweald.t: The Menrothat ask the Empire to cede Farweald to them in exchange for a dose of black lotus and knowledge of its use, provided it will not simply fall back to the Druj.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the evacuation of Feroz is cited as one of the actions a Varushkan mandate would discourage.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Druj forces wait at Beetle Tree to trap Dawnish and Varushkan survivors, whom a conjunction could save; success would allow a half-price spy network here. The forest is also proposed as a hunting ground for glory-seeking knights.

Karsk.t: The bandit haven of Isember threatens Karsk; military units and armies here could assault it. The Senate must also decide whether the Ketsov or local vales should harvest the dragonbone of the Mir Mozga.

Ossium.t: Ossium is now firmly Varushkan, with new vales founded by former Druj slaves and settlers, and Nearweald has lost its under-developed quality. Opportunities over the Crawling Depths and the Tower of the Scorpion await the Senate.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of Otkodov invaded Karsk in 368YE, helped by some of Isember's inhabitants.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos appears only in the names of League characters listed as supporting Ossium.

Semmerholm.t: Some of the few hundred Ossium natives who chose Dawn over Varushka seek new lives here as yeofolk.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: a Varushkan mandate on Isember would make Varushka opt out of a raid on Skallahn.

Skarsind.t: More orcs left Ossium for Skarsind, often with Navarr escorts along the Varushkan roads.

The Barrens.t: Menrothat orcs live in the northern Barrens under Druj rule, and the sept asks the Empire to cede the Barrens region of Farweald to them.

The Semmerlak.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish knights crossed the Semmerlak on their way to Ossium, many stopping to visit the Golden Causeway.

Weirwater.t: Ossium natives who petitioned to join Dawn seek to start new lives here as yeofolk.

Blood will thicken.d: Commissioned by the Senator for Necropolis, the appraisal found that pilgrims lacked a reason to come, not the means. Eilian proposed that artists submit designs to the Assembly of Nine at the Summer Solstice. Pharos' Water offered the Dragonbone Symbol Wayfarers Guide to the winner if the Senate builds the design. The full commission would need 1000 wains of white granite, 250 Thrones and three years, and would make Bastion the undisputed centre of the Way. National assemblies could pass mandates committing citizens' granite and coin, at the cost of supporting other causes. Highguard could give 25 wains and 50 crowns each season. Alternative League and Varushkan mandates, and an Urizen refusal, were also proposed.

Dawn.t: Dawn's assembly could pass a mandate pledging its citizens' spare resources, worth 12 wains of white granite and 24 crowns a season for a year. Doing so would stop Dawn backing other causes through mandates during that time.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Urizen's proposed refusal calls for the repatriation of Grendel-held Spiral.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly could redirect the nation's building zeal to the holy city, giving 25 wains of white granite and 50 crowns each season until it is complete. This would sacrifice its earlier mandate's benefits and any other financial mandates, and abandoning the work later would deeply wound Highborn Pride and Ambition.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs could mandate support for the holy city, contributing 4 wains of white granite and 8 crowns a season for a year. That would block other financial mandates for the nation during that time.

Navarr.t: The appraisal was carried out by the Navarr historian Eilian Sweetwater, chosen for his insight into travellers. Navarr could also pledge 12 wains and 24 crowns a season by mandate.

The Brass Coast.t: The Senate's separate appraisal into restoring Kahraman's infrastructure went to Naomi. The Brass Coast could pledge 8 wains of white granite and 16 crowns a season to the holy city by mandate.

The League.t: The League could pledge 20 wains and 40 crowns a season by mandate. Rafael Barossa d'Apulian proposed an alternative mandate appealing to League Pride to outdo the other nations.

The Marches.t: The Marches could pass a mandate giving 16 wains of white granite and 32 crowns a season for a year towards the holy city.

Urizen.t: Urizen could pledge 12 wains and 24 crowns a season by mandate. Aspar instead proposed a refusal that would bar any Urizen aid to Bastion and prioritise rebuilding Zenith and repatriating Spiral.

Varushka.t: Varushka could pledge 20 wains and 40 crowns a season by mandate. Vasilmir Radovanovna Esskivic proposed a Vigilance-themed alternative to pave the holy city with Varushkan stone and line it with wards.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark could pass a mandate contributing 12 wains of white granite and 24 crowns a season for a year towards the holy city.

Blood will thicken.o: Navarr prognosticator Eilian Sweetwater appraised how foreign pilgrims of the Way could be drawn to the Empire. He proposed an artistic contest and a vast folly, the Grand Inspiration of the Way, to remake Bastion's White City into a holy city to supplant Timoj.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the Castle of Thorns is cited as a grand fortification that, unlike the proposed holy city, exists for defence rather than faith.

Bastion.t: The White City of Bastion, birthplace of the Way, is the only place the Grand Inspiration of the Way could be built. If completed, it would become the indisputable centre of the Way and draw pilgrims from across the known world.

Bay of Catazar.t: Completing the holy city would bring a vast influx of foreign pilgrims to the Bay of Catazar, fulfilling the aim of raising its territories to the challenge of Timoj.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Walls of Holberg are cited as a grand defensive work, unlike a monument dedicated purely to faith.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Senate also commissioned Naomi of Virtue's Rest to appraise how Kahraman's infrastructure might be restored.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Necropolis raised the motion that commissioned the pilgrim appraisal.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Aspar's proposed Urizen mandate names the repatriation of Spiral as a priority above funding Bastion.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bloody Great Theatre is cited as a site that draws visitors from across Temeschwar and the Empire but is too small to attract foreign pilgrims.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Aspar's proposed Urizen mandate would put the rebuilding of Zenith ahead of any support for the holy city.

Blood-red blooms.d: The Black Eels, Bone Nautilus and Hamsin, backed by Grendel navies and Asavean mercenaries, seized Mount Siluri and stormed the conjured Keep of Azure Ice. The Imperial armies, aided by Autumn and Summer allies and Spring healing magic, then fell back to Limus. Cathan Canae repelled a Black Eels thrust into Tomari. In Naris, the Sempronia are fortifying Elos, the Tower of Light and Shadow was looted and its Night magic wrecked, and the Pinnacle was sent to Salt Lord Garbhan. Losing Siluri's central heliopticon tower weakens the Doyen of the Spires. Sentinel Gate conjunctions threaten the Academy of Arms, the Brilliant Star and the Abbey of Reconciliation.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns marched to Redoubt out of Astolat.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Argent Sword arrived fresh from helping secure victory against the Druj in Zenith.

Grendel.t: The Grendel took Siluri, its mines and the central heliopticon tower, fortified Naris with Asavean help, and looted Urizen libraries and the Pinnacle. Their land armies, especially the Bone Nautilus and Hamsin, were disproportionately weakened in the fighting.

Highguard.t: The newly mustered Pilgrim's Defiance fought alongside the Navarr in Siluri, and the Highborn were enraged to see Grendel bearing looted Wintermark arms. A Grendel mercenary company threatens the Abbey of Reconciliation in Necropolis.

Navarr.t: The Black Thorns, under Cadwell Waystone, marched with the Grey Pilgrims to defend Redoubt and fought in Siluri. Summer goblin warbands joined them, and they withdrew in good order to the hills around Cargo.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: many of the Winter spirits haunting Naris were raised from League cadavers in Tassato, and the Prelate of Adelmar's Shrine bears a Tassato name.

Urizen.t: Urizen lost Siluri and its central heliopticon tower, and the Tower of Light and Shadow was stripped of its Night magic and its library. Its conjured citadels and the Argent Sword nonetheless helped stop the Grendel taking Tomari and pushing on to Cargo.

Wintermark.t: Grendel warriors carried weapons and shields looted from the Wintermark dead who fell saving Elos. The Pinnacle, a relic of the Fist of the Mountains, was carried off to the Salt Lord of Deinath.

Blood-red blooms.o: In Winter 387YE the Grendel armies of the Broken Shore fought the Black Thorns, Argent Sword and Pilgrim's Defiance across Redoubt and took Siluri, adding it to Naris. Imperial magic and cautious tactics stopped them advancing further, and the Imperial armies withdrew in good order to the hills around Cargo.

Casinea/Woodwych.t: Mentioned in passing: the Pilgrim's Defiance's general is Nathaniel of the Woodwych harts.

Necropolis/Fishguard.t: A Grendel mercenary company carrying its pay is travelling through Fishguard towards the Abbey of Reconciliation, intent on looting it.

Redoubt/Limus.t: The Imperial armies retreated into Limus and dug in around Cargo, where the Grendel only harried and probed the north-western hills. A small Grendel embassy in Cargo raises fears of espionage.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Naris stays in Grendel hands. The Sempronia are building makeshift walls around Elos, the Tower of Light and Shadow has been ruined and looted, and the Winter spirits there appear to have been contained by the Grendel.

Redoubt/Siluri.t: The Grendel conquered Siluri, taking Mount Siluri, the Keep of Azure Ice, rich mines and Redoubt's central heliopticon tower. A conjunction also threatens the Academy of Arms with siege and burning.

Redoubt/Tomari.t: The Black Eels' push into Tomari was repelled by the conjured bastion of Cathan Canae and the White Fountain garrison. A conjunction warns of a Grendel raid on the Brilliant Star mithril mine.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns set out from Astolat to join the defence of Redoubt.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel and Asavean fleets crowd its coast, and seers fear stolen lore could produce a Grendel magical navy able to strike anywhere along the bay.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Pilgrim's Defiance had only recently mustered in Casinea before marching to Redoubt.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Salt Council's navies and armies are massing in Redoubt and Mareave.

Necropolis.t: A Grendel mercenary company sent by maistir Eilidh is heading through Fishguard to loot the Abbey of Reconciliation, and Abbess Sister Rosa is responsible for stopping it.

Redoubt.t: The Grendel now hold both Siluri and Naris, and Elos is being fortified against recapture. Libraries and spires have been looted, and conjunctions threaten the Academy of Arms and the Brilliant Star.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the page names only the forges of the Spiral Sword in Limus as a site that would have been threatened had the fighting reached Limus earlier.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: many of the Winter spirits in Naris were raised from League cadavers of Tassato, buried with grave goods the Grendel covet.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns' general lamented their home in Therunin falling to the sway of the vallorn.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Argent Sword came to Redoubt after helping secure victory against the Druj in Zenith.

Bloody murder.d: Calladan of Widow's Walk was killed travelling to Sybella; veteran Douglas Wyrdwatcher was found dead in Canterspire in Morrow; Suaq pacifist Bridget Windsdottir was also slain; and Arnaud di Sarvos, trained at the School of Epistemology in Tassato and a long-serving Synod aide, was found with his throat cut. Each was attacked alone with edged weapons, the scenes deliberately drenched in blood, with no sign of forced entry. With retirements compounding the losses, the Senate's capacity to commission historical research fell permanently from five to two per season, forcing the Minister of Historical Research, the Advisor on the Vallorn and the Dredgemaster of Feverwater to compete with senators. Magistrates continue to investigate; the Senate raised a motion to protect the remaining researchers.

The League.t: Arnaud di Sarvos, a scholar trained at Tassato's School of Epistemology and twenty years an aide to the Synod, was among the slain, and the Empire's research capacity that League senators draw on was sharply cut.

Urizen.t: Douglas Wyrdwatcher was murdered while visiting Canterspire in Urizen-held Morrow, bringing the killings into the nation's lands.

Bloody murder.o: Four more civil servants of the department of historical research, all studying the origins of the vallorn, were bloodily murdered in the three months after the Spring Equinox 379YE, following earlier killings of their colleagues.

Morrow.t: Veteran researcher Douglas Wyrdwatcher, said to be a man not easily killed, was found murdered while visiting Canterspire in Morrow.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the murdered Arnaud di Sarvos had honed his eye for detail at the School of Epistemology in Tassato.

Blossoms a rose in the deeps of my heart.d: A woodsman in the darkening Rosered Woods, south-east of Laroc, met a herald of Janon and the first of its knights, who charged him to carry an invitation. Janon intended to open the night-aligned regio at the heart of the woods, known as the Snowdrop Glade, so that non-magicians could attend. Night magicians, artists and priests were specifically invited. Performers, food and drink, contests and petitioners seeking boons were welcomed. The 'prince of toads', likely Sadogua, was expected to attend. A magician still had to open the Sentinel Gate, and visitors who could not open portals themselves would leave the chamber only at the eternal's sufferance.

Dawn.t: Janon's court was to be held within a Dawnish territory near Laroc, and the eternal's call for artists, performers and passionate petitioners offered Dawn's people a chance to seek its favour.

Blossoms a rose in the deeps of my heart.o: The night eternal Janon, the Shadowed Flame, invited the people of the Empire to an audience in the Rosered Woods of Astolat on the third night of the Spring Equinox, opening the regio and chamber there to visitors who came by way of the Sentinel Gate.

Astolat.t: Strange fires and a deepening gloom were reported in Astolat's Rosered Woods, where Janon planned to open the night regio to visitors arriving through the Sentinel Gate.

Blue flowers in the snow.d: Most Empire-loyal Urizeni left Spiral for Zenith and Redoubt. The Senate passed Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian's motion spending 35 thrones a season on mana for Vale of Shadows over Urizen interests, meeting the demands of Actius of the Deathless Cave. Rebels under Tiborion and Caela still held Ankra and Cinion. Aurum's mandate warned that if any army moved against them before Autumn 386YE, all Urizen would rise. Tiborion sought a powerful political position, perhaps a national War Mage title. The League's Lorenzo's Legacies could be redirected to cut the cost, and an Urizen mandate could shape Apulian's culture. The Icy Maw curse halved mana in Morrow and Redoubt.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is cited as having held the War Mage title in recent memory.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named among those whose attacks left Urizen exposed, and the curse does not appear to be their work.

Grendel.t: There is a feared but unproven danger that the rebel spires might reach a secret agreement with the Salt Lords. The Silent Bell or the Shuttered Lantern could investigate this.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr are cited as having held the War Mage title in recent memory.

The League.t: The League kept settling into Spiral, buying former spire buildings and calling with Urizen for Apulian to embrace Urizeni culture. It was offered the chance to redirect Lorenzo's Legacies to fund the shrouds, while some voices like Ludwig Bassilo von Temeschwar urged exploiting Spiral's resources.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Assembly backed the Spiral rebels, and Aurum's mandate threatens a nation-wide rising if the Empire sends troops against them. Meanwhile the Icy Maw curse on Morrow and Redoubt, blamed on another Imperial nation, deepened Urizeni resentment.

Blue flowers in the snow.o: In Winter 385YE Spiral remained divided between the League and Urizen rebels. The Senate funded mana to shroud the spires that chose to stay, while a Winter curse struck Morrow and Redoubt and hardened Urizeni sympathy for the rebels.

Spiral/Ankra.t: Ankra remains under the control of the Urizen rebel spires.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: Mentioned in passing: Apstrus is listed among the regions still controlled by the League.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Apulus remains in League hands, and the former bishop Ludwig Bassilo von Temeschwar has newly arrived there calling for the exploitation of Spiral's resources.

Spiral/Ateri.t: Mentioned in passing: Ateri is listed among the regions still controlled by the League.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Cinion remains under the control of the Urizen rebel spires.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossuary, home of the mithril mine, is listed among the regions still controlled by the League.

Spiral/Screed.t: Mentioned in passing: Screed is listed among the League-held regions, with the remark that the less said about it the better.

Holberg.t: Holberg's Legacy of Courage is one of four great works whose mana a Senate motion could redirect to shroud Spiral's spires, ending its extra mana for League sites.

Morrow.t: The Icy Maw curse halved mana production in Morrow and afflicted its magicians with malaise and ill temper. The Citadel Guard's arcane consolidation there yielded only half the expected crystals, and worse effects loom if the curse continues.

Redoubt.t: Departing Urizeni from Spiral founded new spires in Redoubt, which also suffered the Icy Maw curse that halved its mana sites. Worse effects loom if the curse is renewed.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos's Legacy of Pride could have its mana redirected to Spiral under a Senate motion, as urged by Isaia Pavone di Sarvos.

Spiral.t: Spiral remained split: the League held most regions while rebel spires held Ankra and Cinion. The Senate funded Vale of Shadows over all Urizen interests there, which blocks other rituals on them and new mana-producing Senate projects in the territory.

Tassato.t: Tassato's Legacy of Ambition is one of the great works whose mana could be redirected to support Spiral's spires if the Senate so chose.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar's Varushkan heritage was held up as a model for Apulian absorbing Urizeni culture. Its Legacy of Loyalty could be redirected to fund the Spiral shrouds.

Zenith.t: Urizeni loyal to the Empire left Spiral to establish new spires in Zenith, and the shrouds aim to keep Spiral's spires linked with those of Zenith.

Blue seas, white stone.d: Alonso Tarquinius, of the powerful Tarquinius family and agent of Lady Madrianna of the Blue Stones, trade advisor to the Asavean Plenum, arrived at Sarvos aboard Tarquinius trading ships crewed by free sailors. A Plenum galley escorted them and anchored half a mile out, reportedly because its oars were worked by slaves. Alonso stayed at the Asavean embassy before visiting Anvil, seeking to meet the Imperial Ambassador to Asavea and perhaps representatives of the Synod. With peace between the Archipelago and the Empire, he was protected by and bound to Imperial law. His experiences could sway the Plenum for or against the Empire. In the event, his visit was marred by curses from Imperial citizens, leaving future relations uncertain.

The League.t: The League's great port received the Asavean envoy and his cargo of white granite, its free guilder dockworkers unloading the stone and collecting dock fees, while Alonso formed an unflattering first impression of the League folk as industrious but uncouth.

Blue seas, white stone.o: Two Asavean trading vessels laden with white granite docked at Sarvos, bringing Alonso Tarquinius, a nobleman and agent of Lady Madrianna of the Blue Stones, who intended to visit Anvil during the Summer Solstice. A Plenum warship, rumoured to be rowed by slaves, waited offshore.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Asavean ships and their Plenum warship escort sighted an orc vessel as they rounded the coast into the Bay of Catazar, but completed their passage safely.

Sarvos.t: Two Tarquinius trading vessels unloaded white granite on the Sarvos docks, Alonso Tarquinius lodged at the Asavean embassy in the City of Jewels, and a reputedly slave-rowed Asavean galley lay at anchor half a mile offshore.

Boggarts in Morrow.d: A Spire's mana site in Morrow was found raided by boggarts, which camouflage themselves and feed on pooled magic. Left alone, they would massively cut Morrow's mana site output, though their potent but short-lived faeces would moderately boost herb gardens and farms. The civil service set out historical responses: Academy boggart hunts, relocating the swarm by lures to an adjacent territory as in Empress Mariika's reign, Nicovar's boggart traps protecting mana while harvesting the manure, or seeking Sadogua's uncertain intervention. The Senate chose to trap the boggarts and reduce the impact on mana sites, the response that preserves both the mana supply and the boost to herb gardens.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the boggarts are likened to naga yeomen far from Dawn, and Dawn's Astolat is cited as a past infestation.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr's Miaren is cited as the territory that once received boggarts relocated from Astolat.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: a First Interregnum tale tells of Sadogua moving boggarts from Kahraman to Madruga, both now Brass Coast territories.

Urizen.t: Urizen's mana sites in Morrow faced a massive loss of production to boggarts, which the Senate's trapping response was chosen to reduce while its herb gardens and farms stood to benefit from the boggarts' manure.

Boggarts in Morrow.o: In Winter 378YE boggarts, mana-eating vermin from the realm of Night, infested the Urizen territory of Morrow and threatened its mana sites. The Senate chose to trap the boggarts to reduce the damage to mana production.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named on the page, which refers only to Kahraman as a whole in the tale of Sadogua's removal of boggarts.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: boggarts were once lured from Astolat to Miaren under a scheme from Empress Mariika's reign.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: in a possibly apocryphal First Interregnum story, Sadogua removed boggarts from Kahraman at an Archmage of Night's request.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the same story claims Sadogua relocated Kahraman's boggarts to Madruga with their numbers swollen.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren once received boggarts relocated from Astolat, gaining herb production while being mana poor at the time.

Morrow.t: Boggarts infested Morrow's mana sites, threatening a massive fall in mana production; the Senate chose to trap them, protecting the mana supply while the creatures' manure could enrich local herb gardens and farms.

Bones in the ocean.d: A contract between Finna i Fijadoz i Guerra and Speaker Morna allowed up to a hundred justicars to settle on the Isle of the Osseini. Visiting Freeborn found that Saltbinder Grekodh's Grendel coven had built a white granite and mithril tower over the regio, destroyed the ghost-binding pillars and killed the justicars left behind. The priests were permitted an enclave on the northern coast. The Senate could commission a Sanctuary of the Justicars for 15 wains of white granite and 30 crowns, on the Isle or elsewhere in the Brass Coast. Shantarim's corsairs proposed a fleet-powered spy network; Ka'bal, Bearer of the Imperial Wayleave, built it during the Winter Solstice.

Grendel.t: A Grendel coven under Saltbinder Grekodh now holds the heart of the Isle, having destroyed the pillars and killed the justicars there. They grudgingly accepted a Freeborn enclave, while a corsair spy network was built to watch them in Feroz.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the justicars are described as a legacy of the Brass Coast's Highborn roots, comparable in skill to a Highborn Steward of the Dead, and Highguard is named as a nation where ghosts are more common.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun orcs are noted as a risk to any sanctuary built on the battlefields of the Iron Plains in Segura.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn priests regained a foothold on the Isle of the Osseini, and the nation was offered a sanctuary to gather its few exorcists under an appointed Justicar. The corsairs of Shantarim got the chance to strike back at the Grendel through a new spy network.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is named as a nation where ghosts and hauntings are far more common than in the Brass Coast.

Bones in the ocean.o: After the Grendel conquest of the Isle of the Osseini in Feroz, a treaty contract let Freeborn justicars return there, opening opportunities for the Senate to commission a sanctuary for exorcist priests and a fleet-supported spy network. During the Winter Solstice the Imperial Wayleave was used to build that spy network in Feroz.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The Isle of the Osseini lies here, now shared uneasily between Saltbinder Grekodh's coven and a Freeborn enclave on its northern coast, with Grendel escorts requested for visiting ships.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Mentioned in passing: the Spring 383YE briefing records the Grendel landing pushing down into Fontargenta.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Mentioned in passing: the Spring 383YE briefing records Grendel landings and pillaging along the Oranseri coast between Oran and Joharra.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: The peaks of Braydon's Jasse were suggested as an isolated but reachable site for the Sanctuary of the Justicars.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: The windswept plains of the Jade Range were suggested as an isolated but accessible site for the sanctuary.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: Uninhabited islands in Calvos Sound were suggested as a sanctuary site that would strengthen the justicars' bond with the sea.

Segura/Iron Plains.t: The haunted battlefields of the Iron Plains were proposed as a sanctuary site for studying the dead, though at some risk from Jotun orcs.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the ghosts adrift in the Bay were once drawn to and trapped by the Isle's pillars, and with the pillars gone nothing now calls them there.

Feroz.t: Under Grendel rule, Feroz now hosts a small Freeborn priestly enclave on the Isle of the Osseini beside an orc coven's tower. During the Winter Solstice a fleet-supported spy network was built there to watch Lord Rahab's Grendel.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman was put forward as a safer possible site for the Sanctuary of the Justicars, offering isolated but reachable locations.

Madruga.t: Madruga was proposed as a possible site for the sanctuary, and its corsairs, idle since the peace treaty voided the Broken Shore Bounty, were noted as eager to act against the Grendel.

Segura.t: Segura's Iron Plains were proposed as a sanctuary site, being perhaps the most haunted place in the Brass Coast.

Born with insight.d: Nearly five hundred votes opposed the General Assembly's mandate, many probably from the Wisdom Assembly backing Cardinal Silas of the Cenotaph. The Varushkan Assembly could enact Jaromir Ostrovyn Kostka's call to move against those spreading blasphemy, though Varushkans would then expect their leaders to show no tolerance either. In Wintermark, Rafe's mandate brought rumours that Valdr Grieversonn's family farmstead in Hahnmark bears a strange aura and that he has shown interest in the Sungate. The Assembly could confront or talk to him. Vigilance could urge Varushkan–Wintermark cooperation, and Wisdom could defy the General Assembly at risk of a crisis of faith. Magistrates will ignore Judgement 42 and Nekoda's inquisition proposal.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr are named among those who embraced false auras, alongside Highborn and Dawnish.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is named as one of the nations most prone to question the Synod, where the General Assembly's narrowly backed mandate has less effect.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan Assembly could enact a mandate rallying schlacta and wardens to confront false Virtues head-on, though this would create an expectation that Varushkan leaders at Anvil show no tolerance either. The Vigilance Assembly could also urge Varushkans to cooperate with Wintermark against false Virtues.

Wintermark.t: Rafe's mandate urging people to report malign auras to the stormcrows has surfaced suspicions about Valdr Grieversonn, and the Wintermark Assembly must choose whether to confront him or invite him to talk. Wintermark could also be encouraged to join Varushka in a northern bulwark against false Virtues.

Born with insight.o: After the General Assembly's mandate against false Virtues passed without a greater majority, its authority was weakened in Urizen, Varushka and Wintermark. This Wind of Fortune set out options for the Varushkan, Wintermark, Vigilance and Wisdom Assemblies to respond.

Hahnmark.t: A farmstead in Hahnmark, home of the Grieversonn family, is rumoured to bear a strange aura, and Valdr Grieversonn has been seen near the Sungate half a dozen times in six months. The Wintermark Assembly may send magistrates to confront him or seek talks.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Karov is cited as one of the territories where the Firestarters once attacked.

Both cut alike.d: Druj reconnaissance bands from Zenith were scouting Redoubt, Morrow and Spiral. The Jotun were closing on Atalaq in Sealtoq, and four conjunctions to the Nuajaat Shore could protect fleeing Suaq refugees. Strange Navarr-like warriors travelling with heralds of Yaw'nagrah threatened a Spring regio at Eleri's Paths in Brocéliande. Warriors in Kallavesa were dragging Suaq captives beneath the Gullet. Feni raiders troubled Hahnmark. Navarr vates could attempt high-magnitude rituals at the Verdant Maw in Westwood, which Surut wished to see turned into a Winter regio. Two storm-damaged Grendel ships had come aground in Sarvos and Necropolis, and their marines were pillaging the coast.

Druj.t: Elite Druj bands bearing beetle banners crossed from Zenith to scout Redoubt, Morrow and Spiral, avoiding citadels and fights, and five conjunctions offered the chance to stop them reporting back.

Grendel.t: Two storm-damaged Grendel ships came aground at Haven Rocks and White Sands. Their marines pillaged farms, smelters and woodmills while gathering repair materials, and they could now be intercepted.

Highguard.t: Highguard was named as interested in the Druj incursions into Redoubt. Grendel marines had pillaged the land around White Sands in Necropolis, offering Highborn a chance for revenge.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs were named as interested in countering the Druj scouts in Redoubt and Spiral, where they had campaign armies.

Jotun.t: Jotun forces were tightening their ring around Atalaq, offering everyone the Choice and taking children as thralls. Four conjunctions offered the chance to intercept their warbands on the Nuajaat Shore.

Navarr.t: Navarr vates had chances to defend a Spring regio at Eleri's Paths and cast the Dance of Navarr and Thorn there. They could also attempt planned high-magnitude rituals at the Verdant Maw in Westwood, where a herald of Surut would await them.

The League.t: Grendel marines pillaged near Orphan's Haven in Sarvos, and the League was named among the nations with campaign armies in Spiral facing the Druj scouts.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Marchers of the North Fens were telling tales of shapeshifting beasts in the Gullet that devour fisherfolk.

Urizen.t: Druj scouts roamed the Urizen territories of Redoubt, Morrow and Spiral that neighbour Zenith. Sentinels were readied against them, and conjunctions offered the chance to deny the Druj knowledge of the terrain.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka was named among the nations with campaign armies in Spiral with an interest in the Druj scouts.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark faced several threats: Jotun closing on Atalaq's refugees in Sealtoq, warriors dragging Suaq captives into the Gullet from Kallavesa, and Feni raiders damaging farms, businesses and herb gardens in Hahnmark.

Both cut alike.o: The Wind of Fortune for the 382YE Summer Solstice listed the conjunctions found by the war scouts and prognosticators. They offered chances to intercept Druj scouts, Jotun warbands, Feni raiders, Grendel pirates and mysterious kidnappers, and to reach Spring regios in Brocéliande and Liathaven.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Mentioned in passing: Marchers of the North Fens were already telling tales of shapeshifting Gullet beasts.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: At Eleri's Paths, near Brackensong Steading, two conjunctions led to a Spring regio that the Courageous Bough were warding against heralds of Yaw'nagrah.

Hahnmark/Southridge.t: The Frayed Talons of Dusk were fleeing pursuing Feni after a failed ambush, and a conjunction to Whitethorn Gulch offered a chance to intervene.

Hahnmark/Valasmark.t: A Feni warband beaten back from a Steinr hall was camped near the ruins of Eafshal, where a conjunction allowed it to be defeated.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: A conjunction to Hval Beach offered a chance to stop the warriors who had been dragging Suaq captives into the Gullet.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: Mentioned in passing: the withdrawal of Imperial armies from West Ranging made intelligence on the Verdant Maw hard to obtain.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: Two conjunctions led to the Verdant Maw, a Spring regio where Navarr vates could cast rituals and a herald of Surut would wait to receive it if it became a Winter regio.

Morrow/Operus.t: Druj scouts were active in the Weaving Wood and near the Green Road Citadel by Canterspire, where Saturday conjunctions opened.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: A Grendel ship ran aground at White Sands, and its marines pillaged the area before trying to refloat their vessel.

Redoubt/Limus.t: A conjunction to the Trees on the Mountain of Aquina, across a valley from the Granite Pillar's camp, offered a chance to intercept Druj scouts.

Redoubt/Willstone.t: A conjunction to the Beggar's Trail, near the Winter Sun's camp, offered a chance to intercept Druj scouts.

Sarvos/Riposi.t: A Grendel ship foundered at Haven Rocks, east of Orphan's Haven, and its marines raided local farms and works.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: Druj scouts were active near the Twilight Gate, with a conjunction to the Wooden Rest of Dusk.

Zenith/Iteri.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj bands crossed the open plains of Iteri on their way out of Zenith.

Bay of Catazar.t: Two Grendel vessels, apparently battered by a storm in deeper water, made landfall on the northern coast of the bay.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Marchers from Bregasland spoke of shapeshifting beasts in the Gullet.

Brocéliande.t: Courageous Bough vates were defending a Spring regio at Eleri's Paths against strange Navarr-like warriors and heralds of Yaw'nagrah. Conjunctions there offered a chance to repair the territory's trods.

Hahnmark.t: Feni raiding troubled Hahnmark, and two conjunctions offered the chance to halve or wholly remove the harm to Winterfolk farms, businesses and herb gardens.

Kallavesa.t: A band of warriors attacked wandering groups along the coast and dragged Suaq captives into the Gullet, and a conjunction offered a chance to stop further kidnappings.

Liathaven.t: Conjunctions reached the Verdant Maw, a Spring regio deep in vallorn-infested Liathaven, where visitors risked Green Lung and Surut sought to claim the regio.

Morrow.t: Druj scouts were active in Morrow, and conjunctions to the Weaving Wood and Green Road Citadel offered chances to stop them.

Necropolis.t: Grendel marines from a ship aground at White Sands pillaged nearby farms, smelters and woodmills and were trying to refloat their vessel.

Redoubt.t: Druj reconnaissance parties moved through eastern Redoubt, with conjunctions to the Beggar's Trail and the Trees on the Mountain of Aquina.

Sarvos.t: A Grendel ship foundered at Haven Rocks, and its marines raided the surrounding area for supplies.

Spiral.t: Druj scouts were active near the Twilight Gate, and a conjunction to the Wooden Rest of Dusk offered a chance to intercept them.

Zenith.t: The Druj reconnaissance bands set out from Zenith to scout the Urizen territories bordering it.

Briar liar.d: Tobin, accompanied by his sister, told crowds that the Carstokes had tried to murder him for being a Briar, displaying his Briar patches as proof. Margary Bolholt of the militia exposed him: he had blamed the Trammels at Tower March, the Bolholts elsewhere and, by a report from Anvil, the Talbots. She arrested him and his sister on suspicion of stealing a Carstoke sheep. In the chaos that followed, accounts differed over who drew a knife, but Margary was stabbed twice and killed, and the siblings fled. Magistrates asked law-abiding citizens to watch for the suspect. His rhetoric urging Briars to stand together against an oppressive system has found some acceptance, and the longer he remains free, the more dangerous he may become.

The Marches.t: A Briar demagogue is stoking resentment between Briars and the Marcher establishment with lies against families such as the Carstokes, Trammels, Bolholts and Talbots, and he killed or fled the killing of a young Bolholt militia member. He remains a small but growing threat to the nation's stability.

Briar liar.o: A young Briar calling himself Tobin travelled the Marches spreading false tales that powerful Marcher families had beaten him and tried to drown him, stirring Briars to "fight back". Confronted in Birchland by fifteen-year-old militia member Margary Bolholt, he fled after she was stabbed to death, and he remains at large.

Upwold/Birchland.t: Tobin was tracked to Birchland and confronted before a crowd. Young Margary Bolholt was stabbed to death there, and he and his sister fled.

Upwold/Tower March.t: Mentioned in passing: Tobin had earlier appeared at Tower March, claiming there that the Trammels had beaten him.

Upwold.t: Upwold saw the firebrand stir crowds in several places and the death of militia member Margary Bolholt, and its magistrates are now asking citizens to report sightings of the fugitive.

Bricks and boards.d: Entrants must be the target of the Summer ritual Challenge the Iron Duke; four covens, three Dawnish and one Wintermarker, cast it the previous season. The Challenge of the Boards was a four-round tourney of fifteen-minute two-player strategy games, each round a different game, with at least one Summer herald competing and the top half of the table victorious. It was held at the House of the Wanderer camp in Urizen at 16:00 on Saturday. The Challenge of the Oaken Bricks pitted Imperial teams of up to four against a foreign team from Otkodov, Kalsea and Narkyst at kubb in the Anvil arena at 14:00, with each game winner-takes-all.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: three of the four covens that cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season, Phoenix Rising, the Cabal of Nevezamzer and the Coven of Golden Wings, were Dawnish.

Jotun.t: Jotun kubb players from Kalsea and Narkyst were to come to Anvil under escort of Barien's heralds, as part of a foreign team taking on Imperial challengers at a game played in their winter homelands.

Thule.t: Thule players from Otkodov were to join the foreign kubb team at Anvil, competing in their own challenge of the Iron Duke against Imperial teams at a game the Thule play in their homelands.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the strategy games tourney was to be held at the House of the Wanderer camp in Urizen, arranged through Revel.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Voices of the Unbound Storm, a Wintermark coven, was one of four that cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season.

Bricks and boards.o: In Spring 388YE the heralds of Barien, the Iron Duke, announced two challenges for the Spring summit: a tourney of abstract strategy games and a team game of kubb against challengers from the Thule and the Jotun.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov, held by the Thule, supplied players for the foreign kubb team that was to travel to Anvil to challenge Imperial competitors in the arena.

Bright yellow blooms.d: After meeting Heilyn Bronwen's Rest at the Summer Solstice, Gethyn Blood-And-Sweat's Rising Tide settled at the Spire of the Golden Wood, famed yellow dye-makers limited by scarce iridescent gloaming. They offered two opportunities. The Senate could commission the Gloaming Forum (12 white granite, 36 crowns, three months, a Bourse seat commission slot) near the spire, creating an Urizen national title, the Gloaming Merchant, chosen by Tally of the Votes, who could trade gloaming for pooled local weirwood and would be charged with improving Morrow's Prosperity. Separately, for the coming year the Mirrored Maschieri may buy one mask a season from the spire for gloaming; buying two or more would see the Tide seek to make the arrangement permanent.

Navarr.t: The Navarr Basilisk of the Bourse, Heilyn Bronwen's Rest, set the initiative in motion by asking the Rising Tide to draw up proposals for improving the Canterspire Circle.

Urizen.t: Urizen stands to gain a new national title, the Gloaming Merchant, chosen by its mana site owners, while the Spire of the Golden Wood and neighbouring spires could profit from trade in dyes, masks and weirwood despite tensions with the League.

Bright yellow blooms.o: At the request of the Navarr Basilisk of the Bourse, the would-be sodality the Rising Tide visited the Canterspire Circle in Operus, Morrow, and proposed ways to spread its Prosperity, chiefly by helping the dye-making Spire of the Golden Wood obtain iridescent gloaming.

Morrow/Operus.t: In Operus the Rising Tide met the Canterspire Circle's lumberjack crews without disrupting their work and took up residence at the Spire of the Golden Wood, where any forum would be built.

Morrow.t: Morrow is the focus of the proposals: a possible Gloaming Forum near the Spire of the Golden Wood, whose Merchant would be bound to use weirwood for Morrow's Prosperity, and a mask trade bringing gloaming to its dye-makers.

Brightness long ago.d: Commissioned by Sagua i Ezmara, Master of the Koboldi, the warded seal was carried down through natural caverns, unstable Terunael mineworkings, vast runecarved trollworkings and finally the trogoni burrows, facing trogoni hulks, strange new trogoni breeds, constructs, unliving spirits and runic traps. The seal was set just as an immense trogoni rose up the shaft, and the swarms fled; a brief Deepest Feast followed. The koboldi shared the principles of the ward so similar seals can protect mines and mana sites across the Empire. Participants won orichalcum, weltsilver, tempest jade, crystal mana, mithril and ilium rings, the Delver of the Depths gains deeper access, and a new Explore the Depths action opened.

Dawn.t: Urged on by their assembly, dozens of Dawnish captains joined the delve, their reckless knightly inspiration greatly increasing the treasure won, and Dawnish units may now take Explore the Depths as freely as bordering nations despite not neighbouring the sinkhole.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: two Highborn captains appear on the list of expedition participants.

Navarr.t: Answering their assembly's call, Navarr sent the largest contingent, uncovered hidden Terunael chambers on the edge of Miaren, and earned a report on their ancestors' work there for the Advisor on the Vallorn; Navarr units may also now Explore the Depths.

The League.t: Numerous League captains, many from Temeschwar, joined the expedition, and League military units can now take the Explore the Depths action to recover metals and crystal mana.

The Marches.t: A few Marcher captains and a unit of shadowy warriors raised from beneath the trees of the Marches joined the delve, and Marcher units may now Explore the Depths.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: a single Urizen captain is listed among the expedition's participants.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: a single Varushkan captain is listed among the expedition's participants.

Wintermark.t: Having declared the endeavour heroic, Wintermark sent many captains and a unit of shadowy warriors; its runesmiths identified the ancient tunnels as remarkably preserved trollworkings, yielding runic secrets for future opportunities at the Runegrott Runeforge, and its units may now Explore the Depths.

Brightness long ago.o: In Autumn 384YE a great expedition of 170 independent captains escorted the koboldi and their red iron door, the Runic Hearth of Adamant, to the bottom of Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, sealing the great shaft and ending the threat of a trogoni swarm erupting onto the surface.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark is now safe from a trogoni host pouring out of the sinkhole, and explorers believe the vast ancient trollworkings may stretch beneath its mountains.

Miaren.t: Miaren is spared the threatened trogoni devastation, and newly found Terunael chambers on its edge shed light on what the ancient Navarr dug for there.

Temeschwar.t: With the seal in place, Temeschwar no longer faces a swarm of trogoni rising from the neighbouring sinkhole to ravage its mines and mana sites.

Upwold.t: Upwold is freed from the threat of trogoni bursting out of Lorenzo's Deep Pockets to devastate its lands.

Bring you jewels.d: The Golden Pyramid's Grand Lodge was completed in Clisearn, granting prestige that ended the region's uncooperative stance, and closed the order's year of investigations. These produced two proposals: funding an expansion of Savurn Marr's mine in Nadir, creating a Patron of Nadir who could buy cheap ingots and mithril, and the Stallion's Reward sinecure in Clisearn, yielding mana and seasonal vis. Ruicraic's Redoubt now guards Eoradal, but some septs still doubt the Unshackled will stay. Vranitas, herald of the Immovable One, proposed a Tower of the Immovable at the Redoubt. It would grow a settlement over time and give the Strategos 216 rings a season.

Grendel.t: Their attempt to recapture Mareave faltered and was driven back, with Imperial armies holding the upper hand, though Grendel forces remained in Fleisardh. Their mishandling of the former Grendel orcs there helped reconcile some septs to the Unshackled.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Unshackled saw their hold on Mareave strengthened, with the Redoubt garrisoned and local septs warming to them. They were offered a Patron of Nadir title, the Stallion's Reward sinecure and a tower that would fund their Strategos.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen does not appear in the page; the only link is the name of Ruicraic's Redoubt, a fortification in Mareave.

Bring you jewels.o: In Winter 387YE Mareave was thriving under the Imperial Orcs: Grendel efforts to retake it had faltered, Ruicraic's Redoubt and the grand aqueduct were complete, and the Golden Pyramid finished its Grand Lodge in Clisearn. Several new commission opportunities were offered across the territory.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: the independent city-state still prizes its neutrality but is facing the realities of life under Imperial "new management".

Mareave/Clisearn.t: The completed Grand Lodge brought prestige that ended Clisearn's uncooperative stance, and its three major families made informal approaches about trade. The Stallion's Reward sinecure was proposed here to channel the territory's magical flows.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: Ruicraic's Redoubt was completed and garrisoned here, though some septs still doubted the Unshackled would stay. Vranitas proposed the Tower of the Immovable, which would draw a growing settlement around the Redoubt.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel armies were still present in Fleisardh and had yet to be dealt with.

Mareave/Nadir.t: Golden Pyramid diviners found a rich new vein, including some mithril, in Savurn Marr's mine. If the Empire funds an expansion, the Imperial Orcs could buy its output cheaply through a Patron of Nadir.

Mareave.t: The territory prospered as Grendel attacks were repulsed, the aqueduct and Redoubt were completed and the Grand Lodge stood in Clisearn. New opportunities for mines, magical sinecures and a landmark tower were laid out across its regions.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the page concerns Ruicraic's Redoubt in Eoradal, Mareave, not the Urizen territory of Redoubt.

Broken arrow.d: Henriika Ikkasbane devised a stealthy raid across Atkonaroq into Suaq Fount to strike the Pride of Ikka's Tears, recover mithril and free Suaq thralls. The raid would liberate 50 thralls per thousand strength committed, and Jotun patrols would then prevent further raids. The Assembly named Raknar Ravenstorm, Eyes of the North, to lead it, and Kindra Edasdottir sent half the Fist of the Mountains. The page does not record the raid's result. The Senate voted to rebuild the Ishal aviary, creating the Raven Seer title, and to create the Chronicle of Heroism. A controversial judgement declared Suaq thralls Frayed. Usko Argonning raised a follow-up mandate but withdrew it without it being enacted.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: a Wintermark statement praises Aethelric the Grounded's work at the field hospital in Zenith, without naming the Druj.

Jotun.t: Their Pride of Ikka's Tears mine and the halls of their jarls in Sermersuaq became the target of a Wintermark raid to free Suaq thralls and recover mithril. Wintermark statements also set their notion of honour apart from Wintermark heroism.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: most Wintermarkers are said to reject the brutal tactics of the Navarr as unheroic.

Wintermark.t: The Assembly named Raknar Ravenstorm to lead the raid, the Fist of the Mountains committed half its warriors, and the Senate commissioned the Ishal aviary and a Chronicle of Heroism for the nation. A judgement declaring thralls Frayed stirred controversy among stormcrows.

Broken arrow.o: After the Wintermark National Assembly's Spring 383YE statements on heroism, opportunities arose for a stealthy Suaq raid on the Jotun-held Pride of Ikka's Tears, a rebuilt aviary at Ishal and a Chronicle of Heroism. In Summer the raid was launched and the Senate commissioned both the aviary and the Chronicle.

Kallavesa/Skymark.t: Ishal, in southern Skymark, was chosen as the site of the Senate-commissioned aviary, where mystics would read omens for the Raven Seer through the Parliament of Owls ritual.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: The raid crossed Atkonaroq into Suaq Fount to reach the Pride of Ikka's Tears. A large enough force could have blocked the mine and prepared the region for an Imperial assault without the usual beachhead penalty.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: freed Suaq thralls and recovered wealth were to be escorted back to Hahnmark and Kallavesa.

Kallavesa.t: The Senate voted to rebuild the aviary at Ishal, which would create the Raven Seer title for a Kallavesi-backed mystic. The territory was also to receive freed thralls.

Sermersuaq.t: Wintermark raiders struck at the Jotun-held lands to free Suaq thralls and reach Ikka's Tears, after which the Jotun were certain to tighten their patrols. The Assembly's judgement declaring those who took the choice to be Frayed caused controversy among Wintermarkers.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Aethelric the Grounded is praised for saving hundreds of lives at a field hospital in Zenith.

Broken sword.d: Herminius of the House of the Wanderer's mandate (284-10) shattered the Temple of the Four Winds. Unrepentant scholars renamed themselves the Disciples of Sulemaine and rejected the Assembly and the Arbiter, who lost their bounty of liao. Having reversed its 383YE praise of Sulemaine, the Assembly lost authority: Urizen congregations give 2 fewer votes and 1 fewer liao until Winter Solstice 386YE. The Assembly upheld a mandate, raised by Herminius and enacted by Clytemnestra, urging loyal scholars to carry Sulemaine's teachings across the Empire. There will be no new sword scholars in Urizen, and the last of them may found a sodality. Galene Netherwatch's judgement keeps Urizen bound only by greater-majority mandates.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the sword scholars' earlier links with the yeofolk of Dawn are cited as a step towards forming a sodality.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Sulemaine is recalled as having taken up the sword against the Highborn missionaries who came to Urizen.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Harwyn Eternal of the Navarr Assembly is named among those whose statements encouraged the departing sword scholars to settle in their lands.

The League.t: Departing sword scholars are expected to inspire the League's bravos to seek Wisdom, though the influence will be slow and subtle.

Urizen.t: Urizen loses its sword scholar tradition, sees its Assembly's authority and congregations weakened for a year, and is left with an abandoned Temple of the Four Winds and an Arbiter without a clear role.

Broken sword.o: After the Urizen Assembly repudiated Sulemaine i Taziel, the sword scholar movement split. Loyal scholars, urged by a new mandate, scattered across the Empire, and the unrepentant Disciples of Sulemaine withdrew into the mountains of Zenith.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the sword scholars' earlier links with the bravos of Holberg are cited as progress towards a sodality.

Zenith.t: The Disciples of Sulemaine have largely withdrawn to reclusive temples deep in Zenith's mountains, where a few vow revenge on those they feel betrayed Sulemaine.

Budded roses.d: The Druj had taken Axmure and destroyed the Gate, but four Dawnish generals united their armies and reconquered almost all of it. The Dawnish assembly sent Lady Caewyn of the Gryphon's Quill, with a song, to spur herb garden output for a year. Weirwater weavers and Queen Eleonaris gave gifts and favours to chosen champions at the Winter Solstice. The Senate commissioned the Harps of Astolat and accepted King Adamant's help to rebuild the Gate as the Adamant Gate. Sandro Visconti di Sarvos commissioned the Rose Towers at Lacuve by wayleave, with the Throne appointing their custodian.
