The Lady of the Semmerlak's Golden Causeway was completed before the Summer Solstice 382YE.

Dawn.t: Dawn's reconquest of Semmerholm stirred unprecedented national pride, and the nation gained a year-long boost to herb gardens, magical gifts for its champions, and several new great works and fortifications.

Druj.t: The Druj were routed from most of Semmerholm after their conquest of Axmure. They were defeated but not broken, and now face a rebuilt Gate and a hidden causeway that Dawnish armies could use to invade.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the unliving horrors that threatened Weirwater are described as coming out of Varushka, and wise Varushkan allies helped free the Lady of the Semmerlak from her curse.

Budded roses.o: After Dawn's armies drove the Druj back through Semmerholm in a single season and reconquered almost everything lost, a wave of patriotic fervour offered the nation and its Summer allies a series of opportunities. Most were taken up: a national mandate, magical gifts, the Harps of Astolat, the Rose Towers, the Adamant Gate and the Golden Causeway.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: Axmure had been conquered by the Druj, who destroyed the Gate there. It was swept up in the Dawnish counter-offensive that reconquered almost everything lost, and the Gate's rebuilding as the Adamant Gate has begun.

Semmerholm/Lacuve.t: Lacuve, home to Semmer's Rose and Lacre, is to see its minor defences turned into the Rose Towers, a place of pilgrimage commissioned by wayleave. The Golden Causeway lets Dawnish armies march from here across the Semmerlak.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the fall of Dawnguard is cited as a source of uncertainty among the yeomanry, and it is named as a land the Dawnish expect to drive the Druj from after Semmerholm.

Astolat.t: Enchanters and weavers gathered at Weaving to plan great aeolian harps. The Senate commissioned the works, which were due shortly before the Spring Equinox 382YE and would share 45 extra crystal mana among Dawnish-owned mana sites.

Semmerholm.t: Dawn retook almost all of the territory from the Druj. The Senate accepted King Adamant's aid to rebuild the Gate, and the Rose Towers monument and the Golden Causeway were also commissioned here.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens is named as the Druj's completed conquest from which they struck into Semmerholm, and as a land the Dawnish now expect to drive them from.

The Semmerlak.t: The Lady of the Semmerlak called young Pelleas of Lacre to her court and offered to raise a magical causeway across the lake for Dawnish armies alone. Its gate on the shore below Lacre was completed before the Summer Solstice 382YE.

Weirwater.t: Having seen the nobility defend them against the unliving, the weavers of Hawthorn, Applefel and Culwich crafted the Crown of Glorious Fire, the Belt of Knighthood and the Shield of the Seeker as year-long gifts for Dawnish champions.

Build up my body.d: Sophus of the Guiding Lights proposed expanding the Academy of Arms in Siluri with a gymnasium, palaestra, accommodation and auditorium, costing 25 wains of white granite and 50 crowns over three months. It would create the Prelate of Adelmar's Shrine (10 liao, 20 Synod votes, appointed annually by the Assembly of Ambition) and let one starting military unit train there each season for a free upgrade. The Circle of the Shimmering Forge invited citizens to donate materials to Provost Lord Florette Griffinsbane so artisans could craft up to five magic items each season for Anvil's Academy students. The Senate could also commission Academy great works in Astolat, Hercynia, Holberg and Sarvos, each giving 30 Synod votes and 15 liao. The pilgrimage opportunities last until the end of the Spring Equinox 385YE.

Dawn.t: A Dawnish priest, Ranae de Rondell, raised the consecration mandate that sparked this interest, and House de Kucant is among the artisans offering to craft items for Anvil's Academy; Dawn's Astolat Academy could also be expanded as a great work.

Navarr.t: The Steading of Evergreen Tears joined the artisans supporting Anvil's Academy, and Navarr-held Hercynia hosts one of the four Academies the Senate could expand into a great work.

The League.t: The League holds two of the four territories, Holberg and Sarvos, whose Academies of Arms could be expanded into great works for Ambition's congregations, and the Guild of Good Grapes joined the artisans supporting Anvil's Academy.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Academy of Arms in Redoubt, Adelmar's own and now consecrated, drew rising pilgrim numbers and could be expanded into a grand pilgrimage site with a new Synod title, while the Citadel of Shining Quartz joined the artisans aiding Anvil's Academy.

Build up my body.o: Following the Assembly of Ambition's endorsement of Ranae de Rondell's mandate to consecrate the Academy of Arms in Redoubt, a wave of interest in Academies of Arms across the Empire created three opportunities: expanding the Siluri Academy into a place of pilgrimage, funding magic items for the Academy in Anvil, and commissioning great works at four other Academies.

Redoubt/Siluri.t: Reached by a treacherous mountain path, the Siluri Academy of Arms could gain a gymnasium, palaestra, pilgrim lodgings and auditorium, creating the Prelate of Adelmar's Shrine and letting one starting military unit train there each season for an upgrade.

Astolat.t: The Academy of Arms in Astolat could be expanded by Senate commission into a great work providing 30 Synod votes and 15 liao to its congregations of Ambition.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia's Academy of Arms is one of four large enough to be expanded into a great work granting 30 Synod votes and 15 liao to Ambition congregations there.

Holberg.t: Holberg's Academy of Arms could be enlarged into a great work to house pilgrims, providing 30 Synod votes and 15 liao for its congregations of Ambition.

Redoubt.t: The newly consecrated Academy of Arms in Redoubt saw growing crowds of pilgrims and could be expanded into a major place of pilgrimage with its own Synod title.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos's Academy of Arms could be expanded by Senate commission into a great work providing 30 Synod votes and 15 liao to local congregations of Ambition.

Burning.d: Imperial heroes, joined by Commonwealth, Sumaah and Axou ships, used charts seized at Chalonsio to reach Rachensgrab. Abel, Bursar of Conclave, was recognised by the General Assembly as Admiral of the Great Fleet. The armada overwhelmed the docks, where crews of many foreign ships fought alone and were sunk, captured or fled. Champions slew the herald Pharam Vex and burned his temple, while Ajakstu of the Many Masks leapt to their death from the Sacrificial Tower. A blockade sank or seized most fleeing ships. Guided by freed slaves through hidden tunnels, the attackers stormed the aerie, killing the slave lords and their leader Feetla. The vaults were looted, and Jarm and Asavea must now adapt.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: several Grendel cogs were among the foreign vessels at Rachensgrab's docks, which were overwhelmed, sunk or forced to flee.

Urizen.t: Abel of Zenith Ascendant, Bursar of Conclave, was recognised as Admiral of the Great Fleet, pledged mana to captains joining the raid, and gained the captured fleets and Autumn ritual texts to distribute.

Burning.o: In Winter 384YE a Liberty Pact armada sailed from Volkavaar to the Tears of the Moon and destroyed the slave lords' aerie on Rachensgrab, freeing thousands of slaves and shattering the international slave trade.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Zenith appears only in the name of Zenith Ascendant, the group to which the Admiral Abel belongs; nothing happened in the territory itself.

Bury the hatchet.d: Meraud agreed to discuss a ritual with Archmage Solomon and asked to meet Enchantress Vandale, Carlos Guerra, the Eternal Family and the Concordium of Pallas. The Whisper Gallery, though enmitied and still at war, would treat with Night Archmage Elyssiathain only if Ancel Watcher met the Cardinals of the Sanguine Icon privately. Callidus charged for its message, fixed a trade-focused agenda and summoned Estana i Mestiere i Guerra. Sinokenon required a representative of the Throne. Llofir warned of retribution if its herald Pah Rashet were harmed. Skathe would discuss cursing those who despoiled Spiral, her home, and awaited a gift. A timetable set each parley.

Dawn.t: The Whisper Gallery addressed the Night Archmage as a "sweet witch of Dawn" and demanded the witch Ancel Steward meet their Cardinals alone, while Meraud asked to speak with Enchantress Vandale of House Vandale about a gift.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Skathe's parley concerns cursing those responsible for despoiling Spiral, which Grendel held at the time.

Urizen.t: Skathe of the Thrice-cursed Court agreed to discuss with the Winter Archmage laying a vengeful curse on those who despoiled her home, the Urizen territory of Spiral, and offered to speak with a Highborn chapter with a red torch if the archmage supported them.

Bury the hatchet.o: Six eternals (Meraud, the Whisper Gallery, Callidus, Sinokenon, Llofir and Skathe) answered plenipotentiary messages from the Conclave's archmages, each agreeing to a formal parley at the summit. Several set conditions, fixed agendas or requests to meet particular citizens.

Spiral.t: Spiral is named as Skathe's home, and her parley with Winter Archmage Emilia Ankarien was to concern a vengeful curse on those responsible for despoiling it while it was held by Grendel.

Burying the lede.d: The Asavean Plenum, angered by the Synod's missionaries, discussed sending the Grendel more warships, coin, mithril or weirwood. That aid was stalled until "the Sanguinosa Incident" was resolved. Some Plenum members blamed the Empire for the Tarquinius murders and called for assassins, so Imperial ambassadors were warned. The Duke of Arbonne auctioned salvage rights to Golden Fleet wrecks, offering either weirwood for up to four years or relics. The Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy controlled a 20-person conjunction to the auction. Grenehal Chusciorzi would visit Anvil to meet the kraken-slayers. The Bedelaar Huisbaas offered blight help once the Dry Patricians were defeated. Ehsan's sibling would discuss peace, and the Golden Sugar Cartel made its free ambassadorial message service permanent.

Grendel.t: Asavean warships and marines already backed the Grendel, and the Plenum weighed further aid that was blocked until the Sanguinosa Incident was settled. The Grendel were also invited to the Golden Fleet auction, and Ehsan's sibling was coming to Anvil to discuss Beoraidh, Sinfoyard and peace declarations.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule is not named on the page; its only link is Otkodov's appearance in the list of the Empire's smaller neighbours.

Burying the lede.o: A collection of foreign news for Spring 386YE reported that Asavea remained at war with the Empire and was considering more aid to the Grendel. It also covered an Arbonne auction for salvage rights to the sunken Golden Fleet, a Caitun merchant's visit over a slain Sea of Snow kraken, and several diplomatic developments.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is not named directly; the page recounts Asavean warships aiding the Grendel, including the destruction of the Isle of Osseini settlement and the burning of Siroc.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is listed among the smaller neighbouring nations that exert unexpected influence over the Empire.

Sea of Snow.t: News of the first kraken killed in the Sea of Snow in living memory reached Faraden. A scion of the Caitun Chusciorzi merchant family was coming to Anvil to meet those responsible.

Butterfly in reverse.d: High Lord Mukhali Tchemetzi offered to supply 60 wains of white granite and Faraden builders if the Empire provided 15 wains of weirwood and 45 crowns for transport. Once complete, any Imperial fleet could trade at Caitun for orichalcum, weltsilver, green iron and blood whelks, with Wintermark and Marcher fleets profiting most. Winterfolk, Marcher and Freeborn fleets could also hunt Sea of Snow monsters for oil, whale horn or kraken's ink. Separate proposals, which the page does not record as enacted, would dredge the Westmere near Meade, raising taxes and opening mithril trade with the Tseriyn and ilium trade with the rival Salagiin, provided dredging finished before Spring 386YE.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the shipwrecked sailors in the story fear being caught on the Jotun side of the Faraden border, and note that the Jotun shun the sea there.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn fleets, swift enough to base themselves at Caitun, gained the chance to hunt the monsters of the Sea of Snow once the port opened after the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

The Marches.t: Marcher fleets would earn a bonus to their production trading at Caitun and could hunt Sea of Snow monsters. Dredging the Westmere at Meade was also proposed, which would create a possible Alder of Meade buying Tseriyn mithril in exchange for Marcher farm produce.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named directly and shares only in the general opportunity for Imperial fleets to trade at Caitun.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk fleets would gain a production bonus trading at Caitun and could hunt Sea of Snow monsters. Dredging the Westmere was proposed to benefit Fisk, with a possible Mediator of Fisk buying Salagiin ilium for coin and beggar's lye.

Butterfly in reverse.o: After a great Imperial flotilla charted part of the Sea of Snow and reached the Faraden coast, the Faraden of Menendram offered to expand the docks at Caitun if the Empire contributed weirwood and coin. The Senate backed the expansion in Spring 385YE, and the port opened to Imperial fleets after the Autumn Equinox.

Kallavesa/Wittal Grove.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named on the page, which instead discusses Kallavesa's port of Fisk and its prospects if the Westmere were dredged.

Mitwold/Meade March.t: The proposed dredging of the Westmere would give Meade March the coastal quality, potentially allowing a future shipyard at Meade and easing passage for ships trading with Caitun.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the sailor Hoepel regrets swapping the shark-filled Bay of Catazar for the Sea of Snow.

Bregasland.t: The proposed dredging of the Westmere would raise taxation from Bregasland by 2 thrones each season, though the page does not record the dredging as carried out.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa's port of Fisk stood to gain from the proposed Westmere dredging, which would add 2 thrones of tax each season, and from a possible ilium-buying Mediator of Fisk based there.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Meade's docks are compared unfavourably with major Imperial ports such as Cargo, Siroc and Atalaya.

Mitwold.t: Dredging the Westmere near Meade was proposed as a ministry commission costing 50 weirwood, 30 white granite and 20 thrones, which would raise Mitwold's taxation by 5 thrones each season and enable a mithril trade.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named on the page and is linked only through the wider Imperial opportunity at Caitun.

Sea of Snow.t: The flotilla's voyage reached the Faraden coast, and with Caitun opened to Imperial ships, fleets could now hunt the seahemoths, cambion-whales and kraken that haunt these waters.

By fountains, by fishes.d: Bregasland and Odd's End fishing boats and Westerhal's fishing fleet would smuggle Imperial warriors across the Gullet, and any Imperial fleet could also help. Navarr guides would lead the raiders back through Jotun-held Sermersuaq. Hitting forges such as the Steelweaver's Crucible would stop Jotun armies being raised or resupplied. Attacking Kierheim would halt Jotun fortification work. Striking kirkja and Ulfrskelf would recall Jotun orc champions. Raiders could win metals, natural materials and possibly Bourse resources. If more than 20,000 strength took part, every Imperial military unit would suffer a penalty. National assemblies could opt out by mandate. Three Sentinel Gate conjunctions offered ways to strengthen the raid, ease the return or protect the Skallahn spy network.

Dawn.t: Tobias Field proposed a Dawn Assembly mandate urging Dawnish captains to stay out of the Skallahn raid and turn instead to conquering the Barrens. This would spare Dawn the raid's penalty at the cost of weaker Dawnish participation.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are cited as far easier to raid than the Jotun, and a proposed Dawn mandate calls for death to the Druj.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named as easier raiding targets than the Jotun, and alternative mandates propose rescuing people escaping Grendel-held Feroz.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Dawn mandate speaks of standing with Highguard against the Druj, and the Highborn unconquered are compared to Navarr guides.

Jotun.t: The Jotun faced an Imperial raid on Skallahn that could cripple their army resupply, halt their fortification work or force their orc champions home to guard their temples. A Jotun warband near Starkmarsh threatened to expose the Empire's spying, which would put every jarl on alert.

Navarr.t: The Navarr Assembly pledged scouts and pathfinders to lead the raiders out of Skallahn through Jotun-held Sermersuaq. Nathair Autumngale also proposed an alternative mandate steering Navarr captains towards rescuing people fleeing Feroz instead.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Kierheim is described as almost as famous as the League cities of Sarvos and Tassato.

The Marches.t: The Marcher Assembly led the raid and urged Bregasland fisherfolk to lend their boats. It had to choose the raid's targets by statement of principle, and Marcher fleets could join without the penalty other nations' fleets faced.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are named as far easier to raid than the Jotun.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: a special alternative mandate was available to the Varushkan Assembly to focus the nation on the Ossium problem instead of the raid.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark Assembly urged Winterfolk to aid the raid, and Westerhal pledged its fishing fleet to smuggle warriors into Skallahn. Wintermark fleets could join without penalty, and hylje kin could ease the raiders' return.

By fountains, by fishes.o: In Spring 384YE the Marcher Assembly called its people to raid the Jotun territory of Skallahn after the Spring Equinox, with Wintermark and Navarr pledging to help get raiders in by fishing boat and out overland through Sermersuaq. The Marcher Assembly could choose whether the raid struck military, economic or spiritual targets.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: At Starkmarsh on West Marsh's northern coast, Navarr scouts warned of a Jotun warband that had to be wiped out to keep the Skallahn spy network secret.

Mitwold/Oddmire.t: Steward's Landing near Odd's End was a staging post where small boats were being readied for the raid. Jotun raiders threatened it, and Jarvey Oddsboy asked for warriors and a Vale of Shadows ritual to hide it.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: If the Empire took Stark by the end of the season, the penalty on Imperial military units from the raid would fall by one rank.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: Taking the Suaq Wastes by the end of the season would ease the raiders' return and cut the raid's penalty by one rank.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: At the Lansipari Pines, hylje threatened by a Kirkland unit would help returning raiders if the orcs were driven off. Taking Tanikipari by season's end would also cut the raid's penalty by one rank.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Freeborn and other Bay of Catazar nations' fleets are noted as being far from the Gullet.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland's fisherfolk and eel farmers were called on to lend boats for the raid. Jotun warriors had been seen coming ashore on the salt flats at Bregasland's edge.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: proposed Brass Coast and Navarr mandates would redirect captains towards liberating or rescuing people held in or escaping Feroz.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: an earlier Marcher judgement spoke of raiding Hordalant, and the Hordalant spy network's loss is cited as a warning.

Kallavesa.t: Two conjunctions led to Kallavesa's Gullet shore, where boats and supplies were being readied for the raid. At Starkmarsh a Jotun warband threatened to expose the Skallahn spy network.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: if the Starkmarsh warband escaped, spying in Jotun territory, including Liathaven, would become twice as hard for a year.

Mitwold.t: The Odd's End fishing fleet would carry raiders, and at Steward's Landing near Odd's End Jarvey Oddsboy sought help to drive off Jotun raiders and hide his preparations. Success would let him send up to 1,500 strength on the raid.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: a special mandate let the Varushkan Assembly focus on the Ossium problem instead of the raid.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Kierheim is compared in fame to Sarvos.

Sermersuaq.t: The raiders' route home ran through Jotun-held western Sermersuaq, where most Imperial losses were expected. Retaking border regions there would reduce the raid's penalty on Imperial forces.

Skallahn.t: Skallahn was the raid's target: a rich territory and seat of Jarl Ustigar of Kierheim. Its forges, its wealth and its sacred kirkja, including Ulfrskelf, were all potential targets, with metals and Bourse resources to be looted.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Kierheim is compared in fame to Tassato.

By northern shores.d: Around six thousand soldiers of the Gryphon's Pride, joined by fourteen Dawnish captains and one each from the Marches and Wintermark, attacked the Rahvin at the Fangs. Magistrates confirmed the order was illegal, but the Military Council's generals have full discretion. More than thirty Dawnish captains, with forces from Varushka, Navarr, the Imperial Orcs and every other nation, defended the suspicious Rahvin and covered their retreat east. The mine fell, at a cost of about 750 Dawnish dead. The Senate may now allocate it as an Imperial or Dawnish Bourse seat. The Rahvin vow to retake it this season, and will be wiped out if an Imperial army defends it.

Dawn.t: A Dawnish army and general carried out an illegal attack that took the Fangs, and its supporters face murder trials. More than thirty Dawnish captains, the largest contingent, fought their own nation's army to save the Rahvin, though the sept was most hostile to them.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: named as the enemy Navarr and the Great Forest Orcs march to fight in Therunin, and as the former masters who taught the Rahvin to mine.

Highguard.t: Highborn captains defended the palisades and worked hardest, alongside the Imperial Orcs, to convince the Rahvin that their defenders were sincere.

Imperial Orcs.t: Significant Imperial Orc forces came to defend the Rahvin and led the diplomacy that persuaded the sept to accept Imperial help and survive.

Navarr.t: Isaella's Dance passed through the Barrens as guests of the Great Forest Orcs, gaining nearly a thousand Spears of the Pines for the defence of Therunin. Significant Navarr forces also harassed the Pride's flanks at the Fangs.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast captains joined the defence of the Rahvin, harrying the Gryphon's Pride's flanks with hit-and-run tactics across the broken terrain.

The League.t: League captains helped hold the palisades around the mine against the Gryphon's Pride while the Rahvin withdrew.

The Marches.t: One Marcher captain joined the Gryphon's Pride and now faces prosecution, while Hartell Household captains stood with the Rahvin on the palisades.

Urizen.t: Urizen captains harassed the flanks of the Gryphon's Pride, pinning down its reserves to cover the Rahvin.

Varushka.t: Significant Varushkan forces defended the Rahvin despite deep suspicion rooted in the memory of the Iron Helms and the Northern Eagle.

Wintermark.t: One Wintermark captain supported the Gryphon's Pride and faces prosecution, while other Winterfolk captains reinforced the palisades in the Rahvin's defence.

By northern shores.o: The Dawnish army the Gryphon's Pride, acting on an illegal order from General Archavion Wolfborne, marched on the Bitter Strand and seized the Fangs mithril mine from the Rahvin sept, who were legally foreigners under Imperial protection. Imperial captains from every nation fought to defend the orcs, and most of the sept escaped.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: The Gryphon's Pride stormed the Rahvin's fortified village and took the Fangs mithril mine intact. The surviving Rahvin withdrew east along the coast, planning a counterattack this season.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Mentioned in passing: named as the region the Mallum once threatened from Houndsgate, and its Imperial citizens are among those waiting to see what happens next.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Mentioned in passing: its Imperial citizens are listed among those awaiting the outcome in the Barrens.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: Mentioned in passing: the Gryphon's Pride turned north-west at the edge of the Saltmarsh, former home of the Vendarri, onto the Bitter Strand.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: The Gryphon's Pride cut straight through the forests of the Bleaks, home of the Karass and other septs, meeting neither orcs nor beasts.

The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth.t: The Gryphon's Pride marched north through the region, avoiding Houndsgate, and met the garrison's messengers with stony silence. Its Imperial citizens now await what happens next.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Mentioned in passing: Isaella's Dance moved south into Eastring to join the defence of Therunin.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the battle is described as the first time since before the Empire that the people of the Bay of Catazar have fought each other on this scale.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Isaella's Dance entered the Barrens from Semmerholm.

The Barrens.t: The Fangs mithril mine passed into Imperial hands through an illegal attack, and the Rahvin retreated east vowing to retake it. The territory's other septs and Dawnish inhabitants wait uneasily for what comes next.

Therunin.t: The Gryphon's Pride abandoned the fight against the Druj here to march north, while Isaella's Dance and nearly a thousand Great Forest Orcs moved into Eastring to join the desperate defence.

Can you hear me?.d: Hayaak, now a wandering Outlaw Prince, will parley without boons over whether he has any future with the Empire. The City of Locks offers three meetings through the Conspirator's Congress, chosen by a Declaration of Acceptance, plus a chance to steal the Manticore's favour and an Autumn Market. Janon sends heralds to the Shadowed Torchbearer, the Sun Chamber and others, and offers two ways to inflame Imperial armies. Tharim sends Lord-Captain Catenatus as a formal embassy over Obligatus's murder; his knights are already in Upwold. Kimus aids the Sarvos lighthouse project and the Magpies. Irra Harah will parley but refuses further aid in Therunin and Asav, and sides with the people of the Mallum.

Dawn.t: Irra Harah invites the new general of the Gryphon's Pride to argue for a boon, noting that more Dawnish fought against tyranny than marched on the Rahvin. Dawnish seeking to transform a boon of the Slaughterbeast may also plead their case.

Druj.t: The Empire's campaign in the Sarangrave is Irra Harah's chief concern, and he declares himself on the side of the Mallum's people rather than the Empire's. Imperial armies attacking Kroll face the Lake Beast, and Tharim offers one general protection against it.

Imperial Orcs.t: Janon's heralds wish to discuss the Skarsind College of Pit Fighting with Stonesworn Crix and see Anvil's fighting pit. The Kindling Cadre, last seen fighting alongside the former slaves during the Orc Rebellion, return to court the Sun Chamber.

Jotun.t: Janon's herald refuses to discuss the boons the eternal grants the Jotun, calling them gifts for its friends in the west that would be cheapened if handed out to all.

Navarr.t: Irra Harah refuses any further aid in Therunin, accusing the Empire of abandoning the weak, young and elderly there. Hayaak's emissary is described as looking like a Navarr or Suaq changeling.

The League.t: A League briar delivers Irra Harah's message, and freelance troublemaker Rafael Barossa d'Apulian is summoned by Janon to fan the flames against Asavea. Kimus sends the herald Fotismos to advise Eilian Sweetwater's Sarvos lighthouse symposium.

The Marches.t: Tharim's knights reached Upwold shortly before the Solstice. Tharim demands a Declaration of Acceptance for Marcher magicians to help his knights hunt Obligatus's killers, and the Civil Service warns this could badly disrupt the Marches.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the framing story follows the Wintermark civil servant Jorgen, and Janon's emissary wears a mix of Winterfolk and Imperial Orc garb.

Can you hear me?.o: Six eternals answered the Imperial archmages' plenipotentiary messages ahead of the 387YE Summer Solstice. Hayaak and Irra Harah agreed to parleys, Janon, Tharim and Kimus sent heralds or emissaries instead, and the City of Locks declined parley but offered meetings, opportunities and a market.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: Imperial armies invading Kroll have encountered the Lake Beast. Generals may beseech Tharim for aid, and he will shield the most deferential general's army from the beast's casualties.

Bay of Catazar.t: Tharim wishes to discuss the Sunken Rope's attention being drawn to the Bay of Catazar, and offers protection against the Deep and the Dark to any territory whose senator humbles themselves before his Lord-Captain.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is not named on the page, and is at most touched by Tharim's demand to scour the Marches and nearby lands.

Sarangrave.t: Irra Harah names the Sarangrave as the Empire's next test after the Barrens. He will help its orcs and humans run, hide or kill to survive, whoever bears down on them.

Sarvos.t: Kimus has sent her herald Fotismos to the Sarvos lighthouse symposium to advise Eilian Sweetwater. Records recall that the Kindling Cadre aided the former slaves in Sarvos during the Orc Rebellion.

Skarsind.t: Janon's warriors want to discuss the Skarsind College of Pit Fighting with Stonesworn Crix.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the Kindling Cadre are recorded as having fought alongside the former slaves in Tassato during the Orc Rebellion.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: Irra Harah calls the Barrens the first test the Empire faced, before the Sarangrave.

Therunin.t: Irra Harah will give no further aid in Therunin, saying the Empire abandoned its weak, young and elderly. He has already helped protect those who remain and said what more is needed.

Upwold.t: Tharim's knights have arrived in Upwold and trouble is brewing. Tharim demands a memorial edifice in the Copse of the Bone Birch where Obligatus was murdered, which might also serve as a fane to him.

Can't give everything away.d: Ambassador Bedelaar Huisbaas Annike delivered the ultimatum to the Empire and every other nation. Asavea, facing war with the Empire, Sumaah and the Delves, dropped its bounty, so Sarcophan ministry prices should return to normal by the Autumn Equinox. The Delves hoped to keep free trade but accepted the Senate might end it. The wind also set out several openings: Kruidenkenner talks with the Apothecaries Guild, a possible port in Holberg or the draining of the Great Pits of Ennerlund, Hyena investment in the Brass Coast, and market research for Annike. It also covered a strange flower in Hahnmark, a controversial Highborn funerary-goods deal, research into sea eternals, and an offer for black pearls.

Highguard.t: The Council of Benefactors endorsed a deal selling Highborn granite and funerary art to the Sarcophan Collectors, giving every Highborn business and mine 18 extra rings a season until Spring 388YE. The deal also damaged the Cathedral of the Navigators and the Assembly's standing, and two competing mandates were offered to end it.

The Brass Coast.t: After Ignacio i Zuhri i Erigo declared the Coast open for business, the Hyena seat showed interest in selling mithril and artisan metals to Freeborn markets. That interest was held back by the threat of the Children of Wrecks, and appraisals, ambassadorial proposals, Autumn magic or private letters were suggested as ways to win investment.

The League.t: Sarcophan interest in a port in Holberg and in draining the Great Pits of Ennerlund remained alive, with Schuyler Koopman staying with the Kleists. If free trade ended, the Delves would focus on the Alivetti estate in Sarvos.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Custodian of the Concordium Dock is listed among the ministries whose Sarcophan prices had risen by a fifth and should now return to normal.

Wintermark.t: A mysterious spiralling flower, draaikolkbloem, began growing among the vlinderbloem cultivated for the Kraft brothers on Hahnmark farms. A Sarcophan vintner offered to brew viezesmaak from any blooms brought to Anvil.

Can't give everything away.o: Having seen the Free Seas Pact founder without Imperial backing, the Sarcophan Delves declared the Pax Sarcophan in Summer 387YE. They threatened war on any nation that blockades neutral trade or sponsors piracy, which led Asavea to withdraw its bounty on ships visiting the Empire.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: Koopman was staying with Bernhard and Lula Kleist von Ennerlund, and the Hyena families were interested in a joint effort to drain the Great Pits of Ennerlund, pending an appraisal.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fisher orcs of Misericorde were said to share Holberg's enthusiasm for a Sarcophan trading port.

Holberg/The Morass.t: Mentioned in passing: the Morass is cited as the kind of marshy terrain where Sarcophan engineers have unmatched experience, which supports the idea of draining the Great Pits.

Bay of Catazar.t: Annike dismissed the idea of an eternal physically beneath the Bay but offered to host Imperial historical research into a dangerous Winter eternal tied to the sea. A Sarcophan coven also offered a Mask of the Seven Seas for twelve of the strange black pearls found by captains crossing the Bay.

Hahnmark.t: Farms growing vlinderbloem found a new flower, draaikolkbloem, growing among the crop. Some blamed the Penumbral Veil or the territory's mineral-rich soil, and the Kraft brothers and a Sarcophan vintner were keen to test its worth.

Holberg.t: Koopman remained hopeful of a joint Sarcophan-Imperial port in Holberg, even though the Senate had dropped the appraisal in favour of lighthouses. Hyena families were also interested in helping to drain the Great Pits of Ennerlund if Naomi of Virtue's Rest were asked to appraise it.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan houses were said to be eager to access the Brass Coast's wealth of metals from Kahraman.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the Custodian of the Concordium Dock is named among the Sarcophan-supplied ministries hit by the one-fifth price rise, which was expected to ease.

Sarvos.t: The Alivetti estate remained the Delves' foothold in the Empire, and would become their main focus if the Senate abandoned free trade. Freeborn senators had pointedly claimed the Kruidenkenner were not prospering in Sarvos.

Carnival of rust.d: Under the Druj miasma and their Rivers of Life curse, the Empire fought slow, grinding engagements in Clypion against the White Lion, Hidden Snake and Red Lizard. The Highborn crusade drove the orcs back, at a cost of about 1,500 Imperial casualties. Unliving Urizen sentinels made by Karvor Eyepeel left Zenith Terrorised, so weakened Imperial armies there now disband. The Citadel Guard's Glass Labyrinth hampers the Druj armies' ability to leave. Two battle opportunities were offered. One was to destroy the Bulwark of Lutum miasma pillars with help from Zakalwe's myrmidons and free key tormented souls. The other was to intercept a caravan from the Palace of the Sleepers bound for the Tainted Basilisk's working in Proceris. Two further conjunctions targeted tormented souls.

Dawn.t: The Eastern Sky made a magically hastened forced march from Holberg to join the Zenith campaign. Its general, Vincent Vexille, pledged to aid Urizen.

Druj.t: The Druj lost about half of Clypion to the Imperial advance and their armies in Zenith are snared by the Glass Labyrinth. They have unleashed tormented sentinels, and the Tainted Basilisk is preparing to poison Proceris.

Highguard.t: The Granite Pillar, Seventh Wave and Valiant Pegasus led a costly virtuous crusade that broke the Druj in Clypion. They are the only armies with enough priests to exorcise the tormented souls, and some of those souls are former Highborn.

The League.t: The Wolves of War, bolstered by warbands and heavily armoured free companies from Holberg and Temeschwar, led a grinding advance into Zenith.

Urizen.t: The Citadel Guard's Autumn magic crippled Druj command in Zenith. However, the Druj have turned fallen Urizen sentinels, sword scholars, warrior-wizards and the seer Yoland into tormented souls that are hostile to their own people.

Carnival of rust.o: In Spring 384YE seven Imperial armies, including the Dawnish Eastern Sky and three Highborn armies, invaded Druj-held Zenith again and took roughly half of Clypion. The Citadel Guard's Autumn magic trapped the Druj armies in a Glass Labyrinth, while the Druj unleashed tormented Urizen sentinels and planned to poison the Proceris marshes.

Bastion/The Elms.t: Mentioned in passing: the fallen exarch Benedictian of the Children of the Elms, a Sybella-based chapter, is enslaved as a tormented soul, and the chapter has pledged support if he is laid to rest.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Mentioned in passing: its forests were once poisoned by a Druj poison beast, a precedent for the planned taint of Proceris.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Mentioned in passing: its forests were once poisoned by a Druj poison beast, a precedent for the planned taint of Proceris.

Zenith/Clypion.t: The Empire conquered roughly half of Clypion and is close to a beachhead. A battle opportunity was offered to destroy the Bulwark of Lutum miasma pillars, and the seer Yoland is held at Eridemia's Isolation.

Zenith/Iteri.t: An Imperial beachhead in Clypion would cut Iteri off. Destroying the Clypion pillars would also collapse the miasma over Iteri for at least a year.

Zenith/Lustri.t: Lustri remains a magically defended Druj stronghold with shadows and many-legged guardians, and the Tainted Basilisk gathered resources there. The Sarangrave caravan travels through its woods.

Zenith/Occursion.t: The Tainted Basilisk harvested arcane resources in Occursion, and its miasma will endure for now. It can only be reached through Proceris or from outside Zenith.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Proceris is the heart of Druj power, where the Tainted Basilisk plans to permanently poison the marshes and strengthen its wards. A conjunction to the Fields of Resplendent Twilight offered a chance to intercept the caravan.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky marched through Astolat on its way to Zenith.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky marched through Bastion en route to Zenith.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks and Northern Eagle withdrew to Casinea to recover from their wounds, and the Eastern Sky marched through it.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky came fresh from rooting out the Druj in Holberg's marshes, free companies from Holberg joined the Wolves of War, and the Druj once poisoned its forests.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky marched through Morrow, and the Druj could not force the Empire back into Morrow this time.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: two years earlier the Highborn armies were forced back out of Iteri into Redoubt.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: similar tormented abominations were fought and some freed during the liberation of Reikos, where Isaa and Bakah were once torn apart.

Sarangrave.t: A caravan of Druj warriors and ghulai from the Palace of the Sleepers was heading to Proceris. It carried components that represent more than a year of work in the caverns beneath the palace.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky marched through Semmerholm on its way to Zenith.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: free companies from Temeschwar were recruited to fight with the Wolves of War.

Zenith.t: Zenith saw a seven-army Imperial invasion and the conquest of about half of Clypion. It is now Terrorised by tormented souls, still under the miasma and Rivers of Life, and its Druj armies are trapped by the Glass Labyrinth.

Carved in stone.d: The hallows sworn to by Silas of the Cenotaph and Iniska Ashwood were removed, breaking their oaths, and a doom settled on the Wisdom and Prosperity assemblies. Their preachers became quarrelsome and resentful for a year, though a sincere public oath can lift the curse. Pride was spared, apparently because Zadkiel de Coeurdefer stepped down promptly. Viviane Barossa kept her oath to the end, and Vigilance congregations gained two extra votes. Following complementary judgements by the Wintermark and Loyalty assemblies, the Forge of Bonds could be commissioned at Wood Heath in Hahnmark before the end of Winter 387YE. It would create a Keeper of Oaths to carve one important oath a season into its walls, though some warned that this would make breaking such oaths far more perilous.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: in a scop's tale, Gulnar's wife is said to have died long ago fighting the Thule.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark Assembly's judgement helped prompt the proposed Forge of Bonds, an oathing place at the Fingers that echoes the stormcrow's role and that many Wintermarkers feel is right. Some scops, however, warn that carving oaths in stone tempts fate.

Carved in stone.o: Broken oaths sworn by members of the Assembly of Nine to bear auras of Peace brought a year-long curse of discord on the Wisdom and Prosperity assemblies, while Viviane Barossa's steadfast keeping of her vow strengthened the Vigilance Assembly. The Empire also gained the opportunity to build the Forge of Bonds, an oathing place at the Fingers in Hahnmark.

Hahnmark/Wood Heath.t: The Fingers in Wood Heath, where the formation of Wintermark is celebrated, is the proposed site for the Forge of Bonds. It would cost 11 white granite and 33 crowns in labour, with oaths cut into its white granite walls.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark could become the home of the Forge of Bonds, an edifice where a Keeper of Oaths would record important vows, if it is commissioned by Senate motion before the end of Winter 387YE.

Castle of wind and sky.d: Since the solstice, heavy snow-laden clouds have hung over the Crag, and vindictive winds strike any magician who steps outside, while the people of the vale walk through the storms untouched. Inside, the stone protects the occupants. Ritual research continued, but magicians grew reluctant to travel there, so the Empire had to pay far higher wages than planned, doubling the college's running costs for as long as the curse lasts. Rumour held that Cathan Canae was angered because Meraud's banner hangs in the Crag's halls instead of hers, after she had been promised patronage. Possible remedies included careful diplomacy, which risked angering Meraud, or a Conclave declaration of enmity, which would break the curse.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan vale of Volchitrava now hosts a college besieged by an eternal's wrath, with a stream of strangers visiting. Its own people remained untouched by the storms and walked freely through them.

Castle of wind and sky.o: Cathan Canae, the Summer eternal known as the Mistress of Blizzards, placed a curse on the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, the new magical college at the edge of the vale of Volchitrava, assailing anyone who leaves the castle with snow and targeted gales. The college kept working, but its upkeep doubled because of the higher wages needed to persuade magicians to come.

Miekarova/Srodkoja.t: The vale of Volchitrava's fortress was wrapped in snow clouds and capricious gales aimed only at outsiders, with strange effects such as washing drying within an hour in falling snow.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova's Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun lay under Cathan Canae's curse, and storms battered any magician who ventured outside the fortress walls.

Cede Trajadoz.d: Proposed by the senator for Madruga and seconded by Segura, the motion passed at no cost to the Empire. Trajadoz now belongs to the Marracossan exiles, who may run the town as they please, including constructing buildings such as the temple they had previously requested, provided they have the materials. The motion created the title of Marracossa Sendito, a Brass Coast national position appointed annually at the Spring Equinox by Tally of the Votes of the fleet owners. The Sendito represents the Empire to the Marracossans and vice versa, and holds a ministry allowing the purchase of magic items made by the émigré artisans, some of them unknown in the Empire.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast gained a new national Bourse title, the Marracossa Sendito, chosen each Spring Equinox by its fleet owners, which acts as the link to the Marracossan exiles and gives access to their artisans' unusual magic items.

Cede Trajadoz.o: The Senate passed a motion in Winter 384YE ceding the town of Trajadoz in Madruga to the Marracossan exiles, former Asavean citizens who fled to the Empire after the short-lived Asavean civil war. It also created a new Brass Coast national position, the Marracossa Sendito.

Madruga.t: The town of Trajadoz in Madruga was handed over to the Marracossan exiles, who are now free to govern it and build there, including the temple they had asked for.

Cede region of Misericorde to Sand Fishe.d: The motion ceded the Holberg region of Misericorde to the Sand Fishers, an orc nation in Ossium. It was proposed by the senator for Holberg, seconded by the senator for Karsk, and passed. As a result the region was ceded and the Sand Fishers settled there. The page notes that overall tax revenue for the territory of Holberg would rise by 8 thrones by the end of 383YE as a consequence of the arrangement.

The League.t: The League gave up direct control of Misericorde to the Sand Fishers at the proposal of Holberg's own senator, gaining a promised increase of 8 thrones in Holberg's tax revenue by the end of 383YE.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Karsk's senator seconded the motion, and the Sand Fishers are described as an orc nation in the Varushkan territory of Ossium.

Cede region of Misericorde to Sand Fishe.o: In Spring 383YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Holberg's senator and seconded by Karsk's, ceding the region of Misericorde in Holberg to the Sand Fishers, an orc nation based in Ossium.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Misericorde was ceded outright to the Sand Fishers, who settled the region.

Holberg.t: One of Holberg's regions was handed to the Sand Fishers, with the territory's overall tax revenue set to rise by 8 thrones by the end of 383YE.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is identified as the home of the Sand Fishers, the orc nation receiving Misericorde.

Chain and anchor.d: The Buidelrat and deBruin accepted that the Empire did not want their offers. Jakhalsmarkt access continues until the Autumn Equinox 388YE. Sarcophan visitors were warned to respect Imperial law after the Hester van de Moerassen affair. League and Freeborn citizens attended the Alivetti celebration, but Highguard stayed away, so the Delves will make no approaches to Highguard for a year. After the Senate limited the Apothecaries' Guild to Imperial citizens, the Kruidenkenner withdrew most offers and proposed a cooperation appraisal. The Highborn stone trade ended and the Cathedral of the Navigators lost most of its ministries. Marieke of the House of the Maggot offered 140 Thrones for it, available only at the Spring Equinox.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; the page notes only that the Sarcophan have extended protection to the independent city-state of Beoraidh in Mareave.

Highguard.t: Highborn heeded Exarch Aemon's statement and stayed away from the Alivetti celebration, so the Delves will make no approaches to Highguard for at least a year. The lucrative stone trade has ended and the Cathedral of the Navigators has lost all but one rank of its merchant ministry, with an offer made to buy the building.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn attended the Alivetti revels in numbers, and their business owners gained a free diversification. Ambassador Dino i Riqueza was praised for his patience, and Freeborn figures such as Estrella and Guild Leader Esmé i Estrico i Erigo are tied to the cooling Kruidenkenner relationship.

The League.t: League citizens attended the Alivetti celebrations openly and in good numbers, and their business owners gained a free diversification from deals struck during the revelry.

Chain and anchor.o: In Spring 388YE the Sarcophan Delves stayed friendly to the Empire and keen on trade, but reset several dealings. The Alivetti estate's five-year celebration ended without Highborn attendance, the Kruidenkenner withdrew most offers, and the Highborn stone boom ended. An entrepreneur offered to buy the Cathedral of the Navigators.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: Beoraidh is named as an independent city-state now under Sarcophan protection to help guarantee its neutrality.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Mentioned in passing: Longbeach is not named; the page refers only generally to Highborn mines and businesses losing their stone-trade income.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the bay appears only in a further-reading link to an earlier wind about growing Sarcophan influence there.

Madruga.t: Business owners in Madruga received consumables from the Alivetti estates, some possibly illegal in the Empire, as goods flowed out of the celebration.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the overview notes that the Sarcophan have extended their protection to Beoraidh in Mareave, apparently to guarantee its neutrality.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis is not named; the page refers only generally to Highborn businesses and mines losing their stone-trade profits.

Sarvos.t: The Sarcophan enclave at the Alivetti estate in Sarvos held its week-long five-year celebration, and local business owners received consumables from it. Selling the Cathedral would have no implications for the enclave.

Tassato.t: Business owners in Tassato received consumables from the Alivetti estates after the celebration, and magistrates will struggle to stop illegal goods entering the Empire.

Chain around my leg.d: At the Autumn Equinox a Day ritual devised by the Skywise and woven by Urizen's magicians, using the slave-made skull Defiance as its focus, was laid on general Mor'gur. While the Summer Storm resupplied, the Winter Sun spent the season in Casinea seeking their ancestors. They heard mostly enslaved orcs from Varushka, Temeschwar and Wintermark, including Skarsind, demanding freedom and vengeance on humans. A few older Thule and Jotun voices raged at their descendants. Affected orcs were haunted until the Winter Solstice, and Defiance became a mundane skull. Some soldiers swore oaths against slavery and wore hammer totems. Morg'ur's weirwood permanently changed the army's quality, granting the Break the chains order.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named, but the events took place in its territory of Casinea, where the orc armies rested.

Imperial Orcs.t: Both orc armies rested in Casinea, and the Winter Sun endured a harrowing revelation of their ancestors' slavery that haunted many soldiers and shaman until the Winter Solstice. The army was permanently transformed into Freedom Fighters able to launch the Break the chains order.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: some of the older, pre-slavery ancestors the orcs heard seemed to be Jotun, angry that their descendants serve unworthy humans.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: in the accompanying fiction, a Freeborn merchant selling herbs from Feroz was nearly attacked by a haunted orc.

The League.t: Many Winter Sun soldiers descend from slaves held in Temeschwar, so their shaman felt strong urges to flee or attack Temeschwari. The transformed army will be less comfortable alongside League armies, though discipline should prevent serious incidents.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: some of the oldest ancestral voices the orcs heard seemed to be Thule, raging at and disappointed in their descendants.

Urizen.t: Urizen's magicians wove the Day magic enchantment on general Mor'gur, the ritual behind the season's revelation.

Varushka.t: Most of the Winter Sun descend from orcs enslaved in Varushka, whose mines their ancestors worked. Shaman felt strong urges to flee from or attack Varushkans, and the army will remain uneasy alongside Varushkan forces.

Wintermark.t: Many of the ancestral voices were those of slaves held in Wintermark, which then included Skarsind. Shaman felt strong hostility towards Winterfolk, and the reformed army will be less comfortable fighting beside Wintermark's armies.

Chain around my leg.o: In Winter 381YE the Winter Sun, resting in Casinea under an enchantment meant to help orcs hear their ancestors, were flooded with the angry voices and visions of orcs once enslaved by the Empire. The army's general, Bloodcrow Morg'ur, then paid 25 wains of weirwood to permanently remake the army as Freedom Fighters.

Casinea.t: Both Imperial Orc armies spent the season resting in Casinea, where the Winter Sun held drumming, meditation and fighting pits that brought on the revelation. Any orc who spent time there may have shared in the haunting.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the fiction refers to herbs from the Spice Gardens of Feroz offered by a Freeborn merchant.

Skarsind.t: The revelation reminded the orcs that Skarsind's mines, in the homeland they now claim, were dug and worked by orc slaves when it was part of Wintermark, and many soldiers wept at the knowledge.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar was one of the places where the Winter Sun's ancestors lived and died as slaves, and orc shaman felt a powerful urge to flee from or attack Temeschwari.

Chains from the deep.d: A Synod mandate sending a named individual with true liao this season would create an aura of Vigilance over the Great Chain, permanently doubling the benefit of wains spent on emergency resupply, repairing the bastion or replenishing the garrison. If consecrated, the League could within a year build the Cathedral of Links in Cigno, creating a Bishop of the Links with 18 liao a season; Sarvosi would match wains spent on its grandeur. A fortification commission could also let fleets guard the Chain. Skathe offered, if the League National Assembly declared her a worthy player of the Great Game and 500 tempest jade and 500 beggar's lye were provided, to curse the Chain to inflict extra casualties on attackers.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named as the likely besiegers of Sarvos while Imperial armies are stretched east and west.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: competitive Sarvosi do not want to be outdone by the Highborn next door in defending the Bay, and Skathe recalls a troublesome Highguard coven.

The League.t: The League was offered a chance to sanctify Sarvos's Great Chain, build a grand cathedral to restore the city's prestige against Holberg, strengthen its harbour defences, and decide whether to court Skathe, whose earlier attack on Sarvos many still resent.

Chains from the deep.o: After the Vigilance Assembly upheld a Writ of Consecration for the Great Chain of Sarvos, an opportunity arose to consecrate it with true liao from the Sun Chamber, opening the way to a new cathedral, expanded defences and a spiteful offer from Skathe.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Both the proposed Cathedral of Links on the main dock and the commission to expand the Great Chain would be built in Cigno, provided the Chain is first consecrated.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos is called the most stunning cathedral outside Bastion.

Bay of Catazar.t: Expanding the Chain would let Imperial fleets help guard Sarvos the next time pirates from the Bay of Catazar attack the city.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is the current greatest city in the League, and Sarvosi hope a new cathedral could give them an edge in a future rematch.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos could gain a consecrated Great Chain that strengthens resupply of its defences, a new cathedral funded partly by its own merchant princes, fleet-guarded fortifications, and possibly a curse from Skathe on its defences.

Change.d: Until the Summer Solstice, every Imperial mine and forest produced six ingots or measures of random materials in place of part of its usual yield. Scholars judged the effect to be neither curse nor enchantment. Casting Wondrous Forests of the Night or Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths across the Empire could intensify it, and the Eight-spoked Wheel and Retrograde Wheel were more potent at the Equinox. The heralds Centimani and Alkahest vanished, and the old eternals could no longer be contacted. Their sealed regio reopened with altered magic. Azoth's herald promised that its spirits would come to Anvil at the Summer Solstice. Distil the Serpent's Stone was permanently changed so that it produced shadow eggs.

Dawn.t: A glade of night-blooming flowers in Semmerholm, once tied to the old eternals, now gives anyone who sleeps there vivid dreams of living wildly different lives. Dawn's mines and forests are also affected by the strange yields.

Imperial Orcs.t: Orc miners share in the upheaval: a liberated orc in Skarsind struck what looked like copper and found ambergelt gushing out instead.

Navarr.t: Navarri lands were changed twice over: dragonbone clay in Miaren crystallised into tempest jade, and the Senate's alchemical tower at Holtford vanished, leaving a strange pool in its place.

The Marches.t: Marcher mines such as the Green Iron mines beneath Whittle Hill produced swarms of insects and cocoons, and the earlier harvesting of corpses in the Mournwold is named among the signs of the old eternals' work.

Wintermark.t: A beggarwood grove in Kallavesa, where mystics once met heralds of Murit, now comes alive at night with drifting lights whispering in unknown tongues.

Change.o: In Spring 382YE the eternals Murit and Soghter ceased to exist and a new Night eternal, Azoth, claimed to be their alchemical recreation. Mines and forests across the Empire began yielding strange, random materials, and the regio and works tied to the old eternals were transformed.

Miaren/Holtford.t: The Senate-built white granite tower dedicated to Murit collapsed and vanished, leaving a painfully cold pool. It shows visitors who they might have been and reflects stars unlike the real sky, and locals say a creature rises from it at half moon to speak with Night scholars.

Kallavesa.t: The Kallavesa beggarwood grove once used for meetings with Murit's heralds now fills at night with iridescent lights that whisper in a dozen unknown tongues.

Miaren.t: Soft dragonbone clay beneath Miaren's trees crystallised into crimson tempest jade, and the Holtford alchemical workshop was transformed.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the harvesting of corpses in the Mournwold is cited as one of the signs of Murit and Soghter's activity over the previous months.

Semmerholm.t: A night-blooming glade in Semmerholm, its regio reopened, now gives sleepers incredibly vivid dreams of living wildly different lives.

Skarsind.t: A liberated orc mining in Skarsind struck what seemed a copper vein, only for thick ambergelt to gush out, one example of the transformed mine yields.

Change to Imperial Breadbasket.d: Rowan Merrick, Keeper of the Imperial Breadbasket, announced that the Breadbasket would now be distributed to the Citadel Guard army rather than supporting the Mournwold, returning the commission to its role of contributing to the upkeep of Imperial armies. The change was approved by the Keeper and passed. It would take three months for the Breadbasket to begin supporting the Citadel Guard. At the same time, the money received by farms in the Marcher territories of Upwold, Mitwold and Bregasland was restored immediately.

The Marches.t: Marcher farms in Upwold, Mitwold and Bregasland had their Breadbasket income restored at once, while Breadbasket support for the Mournwold came to an end.

Change to Imperial Breadbasket.o: In Winter 381YE the Keeper of the Imperial Breadbasket, Rowan Merrick, redirected the Breadbasket away from supporting the Mournwold and towards the upkeep of the Citadel Guard army, a change that passed.

Bregasland.t: The money received by farms in Bregasland was restored immediately when the change passed.

Mitwold.t: Farms in Mitwold had the money they receive restored immediately as a result of the change.

Mournwold.t: The Imperial Breadbasket ceased to support the Mournwold, its resources being redirected to the Citadel Guard.

Upwold.t: The money received by farms in Upwold was restored immediately once the Breadbasket stopped supporting the Mournwold.

Changing of the guards.d: Tamain Sepulchre's Statement of Principle, upheld 158–20, inspired the advocate Melusine of Tanner's Bar to propose that Dawn's senatorial tourneys be judged by the Queen or her representative, who would pick the winning house. Lady Griffinsbain, speaking as egregore, said support was real but not universal. Melusine therefore sought a mandate with 100 doses of liao, which would give the Empress's seasonal words the weight of a greater-majority Statement in Dawn. Weirwater's Five Rings cabal would then surrender the Staff of the Archmage schema, and Castle Spiral would kneel to her. Separately, Earl du Chailly sought a potentially heretical mandate urging glory above virtue. Both were opportunities available only during the Summer Solstice 381YE.

Dawn.t: Dawn faced a choice between partially restoring the monarchy, with the Queen judging senatorial tourneys and her words carrying national authority, and a riskier call to put glory before virtue. The latter would bolster Dawnish military units but weaken congregations and risk Synod condemnation.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel are not named on the page; their only connection is that they held Spiral, whose castle residents offered fealty to a ruling Queen of Dawn.

Changing of the guards.o: After Empress Lisabetta won the tourney to become Monarch of Dawn and the Dawnish National Assembly declared her the ultimate authority in Dawn, two Dawnish movements sought Synod mandates: one to make her Queen in truth, the other to place glory above virtue.

Spiral.t: The residents of Castle Spiral pledged to acknowledge Lisabetta as their liege if she became the ultimate authority in Dawn. At her command they would pass the castle's resources to the Castellan of Spiral Castle, either to keep resupplying Imperial armies or to dispose of its weirwood directly.

Weirwater.t: The secretive Five Rings weaver's cabal of Weirwater offered to hand the Queen the six schema for the Staff of the Archmage, held in trust since King Rodric, if she became Queen in truth. This could cost the Archmages a symbol of their office.

Chaos, and the stillness of it.d: The force needed to stop the vallorn doubled again. Military units could take the Slow the Vallorn action, paid in herbs by the Navarr. With 10,000 strength the Broch would survive another season. With 8,000 both regions would hold but the Broch would fall, though its people could escape. With 4,000 only Boar's Dell would hold, and below that the vallorn would claim about half of each region. Armies sent to Boar's Dell (via Semmerholm) or Elerael (via Reikos) could add up to 5,000 each. Highborn congregations, the Great Forest orcs and Tharim kept up their aid. Zakalwe gave a Find the Best Path boon to the Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield, and Llofir withdrew his offer.

Dawn.t: At Ranae de Rondell's urging Dawnish knights went to the greenwood, and Dawnish military units continued to receive additional rewards for fighting the vallorn.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Druj presence made a route into Boar's Dell through Drycastle far less feasible, and the Great Forest orcs feared Druj malice while away.

Highguard.t: Highborn congregations answered Josephine of Adina's Charge with at least 500 strength. Tharim offered to add 2,000 force if allowed to feed on Highguard's herb gardens and forests.

Imperial Orcs.t: The opening story follows two Imperial Orc soldiers sent by Ziek to hold the wall beside the Navarr, one of them sickened by the vallorn and urged to seek bladeroot treatment.

Jotun.t: A significant Jotun force invaded Liathaven, threatening the Imperial foothold in West Ranging and making any reclamation of Westwood far harder.

Navarr.t: The Navarr faced a vallorn that doubled in strength again, threatening the Broch, Boar's Dell and Elerael. Their steadings paid defenders in herbs while Tharim's feeding withered herb gardens in three Navarr territories.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe suggested moving an army into Sermersuaq to free the Black Thorns, and the Kallavesi mystic Tremont of Cundahl took back his projections.

Chaos, and the stillness of it.o: The vallorn heart in Brocéliande grew stronger again in Spring 383YE, doubling the force needed to hold back its spread into Boar's Dell and Elerael and to save the steading of the Broch. Elsewhere, the Jotun invaded Liathaven and the Feni raiding Hercynia vanished.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Boar's Dell could be held with at least 4,000 strength or an army there; below that the vallorn would claim roughly half the region.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Elerael needed at least 8,000 strength or an army arriving via Reikos; otherwise the vallorn would push into it.

Hahnmark/Southridge.t: Mentioned in passing: Feni of Southridge had swollen the ranks of the band that raided Hercynia.

Hercynia/Deer's Folly.t: There was speculation that the vanished Feni might have gone into Deer's Folly, the vallorn heart of Hercynia, though surely not by accident.

Hercynia/Old Ranging.t: The Feni raiders retreated into the deepest woods of northern Old Ranging and then disappeared, and Navarr scouts found no sign of them.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though Tremont of Cundahl was said to have returned to his home in Kallavesa.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: The Jotun invasion threatened the Imperial foothold in West Ranging, which the Empire would need to conquer in a single season against orc opposition.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: With a significant Jotun force in Liathaven, any attempt to reclaim Westwood from the vallorn became even more difficult.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the nobles and yeofolk of Astolat continued to cheer those seeking glory against the vallorn.

Brocéliande.t: The vallorn heart in Brocéliande grew stronger again, and the fate of Boar's Dell, Elerael and the Broch hung on how much military strength the Empire committed.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: some Feni of Southridge had joined the Woods-that-Fell band that raided Hercynia.

Hercynia.t: Tharim's black frost withered Hercynia's herb gardens, and the Feni raiders who had stolen food, supplies and crystal mana there abruptly vanished.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: Tremont of Cundahl was presumed to have returned home to Kallavesa with his reclaimed arcane projections.

Liathaven.t: The Jotun invaded Liathaven while time ran short to exploit its vallorn, and the eternal Surut would not help because the Conclave had not granted him amity.

Miaren.t: Tharim's black frost struck Miaren's herb gardens and forests as payment for his 1,000 strength against the vallorn.

Reikos.t: Reikos was almost certainly the only practical route for an army to reach Elerael without fighting through aggressive vallorn.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm offered the only safe route for an army to reach Boar's Dell, and its nobles and yeofolk continued to cheer Dawnish volunteers.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe suggested using Find the Best Path to move an army into Sermersuaq so the Black Thorns could go to Brocéliande.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, though Druj presence was cited as making the Drycastle route to Boar's Dell much less feasible.

Therunin.t: Therunin's herb gardens suffered Tharim's black frost, and its Senator Cybi Farkas brought about 1,000 Great Forest orcs to fight the vallorn.

Charter Sarcombe market town.d: The motion awarded charter town status to Sarcombe, a Marcher town being rebuilt in the Mourn, so that if rebuilt it will be recognised as a market town across the Empire. The charter requires the townsfolk to form a council of aldermen that elects a Mayoress annually. She speaks for the town to the Senator for the Mourn, who agrees to give her a fair hearing. The council controls the town budget and appoints a Town Clerk who reports to the Imperial Civil Service. Sarcombe may hold a monthly market and run a permanent trading post for mined goods, both funded by levies. It must also host an outpost of the Imperial Militia.

The Marches.t: The Marcher town of Sarcombe gains Imperial recognition as a market town once rebuilt, with its own elected council and Mayoress, and the right to profit from its people's mining expertise through a trading post.

Charter Sarcombe market town.o: In Winter 381YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Mournwold and seconded by Sermersuaq, granting an Imperial Charter that recognises Sarcombe in the Mournwold as a market town.

Mournwold.t: Sarcombe, a town being rebuilt in the Mournwold, is chartered to hold a monthly market and a mined-goods trading post and to host a Militia outpost, with its Mayoress keeping the Mourn's senator informed.

Chasing you home.d: In Kahraman, the Jotun had taken Fort Braydon, helped by large elite warbands. Three of these warbands sent their banners to Morogvejo, where the ghodi Alok Surefoot would cast runes and issue orders. The Empire could intercept those orders, seize the banners, and kill Alok to take the Spear of Bounty. If he kept it, Hayaak's heralds would inflict 250 casualties a season on Imperial armies in Kahraman. In Bregasland, the defeated Mathilda Fisher was gathering her followers at Rock Foot Wood to retreat to Hordalant. The Empire could have her executed by a Marcher to prevent her becoming a martyr, and could deal with the Loyalty priest Bushel Sykes.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish enchanters are given as an example of how a captured Spear of Bounty might be offered to a Summer court in return for patronage of the Eastern Sky.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that Alok Surefoot regards the Navarr as no better than human Druj.

Jotun.t: The Jotun had taken Fort Braydon in Kahraman and were gathering warband banners and orders at Morogvejo under the ghodi Alok Surefoot. Meanwhile their allies in Bregasland were retreating towards Hordalant, which left them exposed to an Imperial strike at either site.

Navarr.t: Alok Surefoot hates the Navarr, so any Navarr armies in Kahraman would be the first target of Hayaak's heralds if the Spear of Bounty was not taken from him.

The Brass Coast.t: Fort Braydon, a long-standing Freeborn stronghold in Kahraman, had fallen to the Jotun. The Morogvejo opportunity offered a chance to blunt the Jotun warbands operating there.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the ruined Morogvejo watchtower once kept watch over Tassato.

The Marches.t: The rebellion in Bregasland was near collapse, and only a proper execution of Mathilda Fisher by a Marcher would kill the dream of Free Bregas. Dealing with Bushel Sykes would let the Marcher Assembly root out remaining traitors.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Alok Surefoot's earlier boon from Hayaak sent heralds to slaughter many of the Thule Dragon's prized warlocks in Sermersuaq.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: vengeful Summer heralds summoned by Alok Surefoot had earlier stalked the tundra of Sermersuaq.

Chasing you home.o: Ahead of the Spring Equinox 385YE, prognosticators identified two major conjunctions on the Saturday morning, one to the Morogvejo valley in Kahraman and one to Graven Rock in Bregasland. The Military Council was to choose between them, and which nations would take part, at the Friday muster.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the regions Imperial forces had liberated from the Jotun.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: Imperial forces had made gains into Ottermire, the home of the rebel priest Bushel Sykes.

Bregasland/The Rushes.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the regions liberated by Imperial forces.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: Fort Braydon had fallen and the Jotun banners now flew from its walls. The Kahraman strike opportunity, against the warbands and Alok Surefoot gathered at Morogvejo, was set out under this region's heading.

Bregasland.t: Imperial forces had liberated much of the territory, and Mathilda Fisher was preparing to flee from Graven Rock. Her execution by a Marcher would end Free Bregas, while her escape or an unceremonious death risked future unrest.

Hordalant.t: Hordalant was the intended refuge of Mathilda Fisher and her followers, some of whom were levies from its fens. If she escaped, the Fishers would withdraw there and resurface later.

Kahraman.t: The Jotun held Fort Braydon and were gathering warband banners at Morogvejo. Imperial armies in the territory faced 250 casualties a season from Hayaak's heralds unless Alok Surefoot lost the Spear of Bounty.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the old Morogvejo watchtower once kept watch over Madruga.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Morogvejo watchtower once overlooked it, and recent unrest in the Mournwold is cited as a warning about rebellion taking root in the Marches.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Alok's earlier boon from Hayaak saw heralds hunt and slaughter Thule warlocks on its tundra.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the ruined watchtower on Morogvejo hill once kept watch over Tassato.

Children in bloom.d: The enchantment touched only territories that were Imperial at the end of Winter 384YE. Strange blooms spread everywhere, briars felt invigorated, and herds, harvests and perhaps births all increased. For a season, farms and forests could be diversified for free, and citizens could exchange their resources for farms. The trods surged with power, and Navarr Spring magicians with mana sites could harvest vis. Chaos fruit from Brocéliande could be cultivated in forests until the end of the Spring Equinox, prompting Navarr calls for vigilance and possible Navarr and Highborn mandates. A resonance of ruin badly damaged the Blood Red Roads and Sunset Roads. The civil service would spend 26 Thrones a season maintaining them unless the Senate instructed otherwise.

Dawn.t: Magical blooms were in great demand ahead of the Dawnish Festival of the Net. Astolat and Semmerholm stood to lose Blood Red Roads income if maintenance stopped.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens, which the Druj held, was excluded from the enchantment's benefits.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral and Feroz, held by the Grendel, were excluded from the enchantment's benefits.

Highguard.t: Highguard's new White Roads suffered only minor erosion. The Highborn assembly had the opportunity to raise a mandate, with the grey pilgrims searching out chaos fruit forests.

Imperial Orcs.t: Swelling herds boded well for the Shepherd of the Great Herd and for the orcs raising their own herds in Skarsind.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland and Liathaven, which the Jotun held, were excluded from the enchantment, and the winter fighting with the Jotun in Liathaven is recalled.

Navarr.t: The trods, newly extended by the Voice of the Quiet Forest, surged with power, and Navarr Spring magicians with mana sites each gained vis. Enfys Larksong urged openness about chaos fruit cultivation, and a Navarr mandate to track it was proposed.

The Brass Coast.t: The Sails of the First Flame cast the enchantment, but the Sunset roads in Segura and Madruga were damaged by the resulting Spring magic.

The League.t: A fashion for wearing unique flowers swept the League. The late La Volpe's Blood Red Roads, which enrich Temeschwar, Sarvos, Tassato and Holberg, bore the brunt of the ruinous damage.

The Marches.t: The blooms added grandeur to Marcher spring festivals. Marcher farms could build landskeeper menhirs without the usual diversification cost, and Upwold's road income depended on maintenance.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: new Navarr trods in Sküld, in Thule-held Otkodov, are noted as part of the enlarged network.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the magical blooms were in demand ahead of the Urizen Night of Flowers.

Varushka.t: The newly completed Iron Roads were untouched, which Varushkan builders attributed to their protections. Karov's Blood Red Roads benefits were still at risk.

Wintermark.t: Growing herds boded well for Winterfolk returning to Sermersuaq and for the proposed Hunt of the North. The Pilgrim's Trail in Kallavesa weathered the season through hard work.

Children in bloom.o: In Spring 385YE the Brass Coast's Sails of the First Flame cast the Hallow of the Green World, flooding the Empire with Spring magic. It brought flowers, fertility and healing herbs, but also wild side effects, including serious damage to the Empire's roads.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, the briar Amwell and his comrade Bruna recall having fought at Rebeshof.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Mentioned in passing: Sküld's new trods are part of the Navarr network through which the Spring magic surged.

Astolat.t: Astolat's farms and businesses risked losing their Blood Red Roads income, and its vallorn-plant farms would be listed if both Navarr and Highborn mandates passed.

Bastion.t: The White Roads linking Bastion sustained less damage than other roads, though they showed some erosion in wilder places.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: as a Jotun-held territory, Bregasland's resources gained none of the enchantment's benefits.

Brocéliande.t: Excluded from the enchantment, Brocéliande was the source of the chaos fruit, and there were concerns that cultivating the fruit near its vallorn could be dangerous.

Casinea.t: Casinea's Blood Red Roads income was at risk, and its vallorn-plant farms would be listed if both mandates were enacted.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: as a Grendel-held territory, Feroz was excluded from the enchantment's benefits.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark's extra farm and business income from the Blood Red Roads would erode unless the roads were maintained.

Hercynia.t: Concerns were raised that cultivating chaos fruit in Hercynia could be dangerous because of the vallorn there.

Holberg.t: Holberg's Blood Red Roads income was threatened by the damage, and the city's streets bloomed with lilac.

Kallavesa.t: The Pilgrim's Trail was less affected than other roads, though its mystics and priests had a challenging season keeping the paths clear of marsh growth.

Karov.t: Karov benefits from the Blood Red Roads, which stop short of Delev, and that income was at risk if maintenance lapsed.
