Liathaven.t: Jotun-held Liathaven was excluded from the enchantment. Its newly restored trods joined the Navarr network, and cultivating chaos fruit there was seen as dangerous.

Madruga.t: Madruga's Sunset roads were damaged by the Spring magic, and its Blood Red Roads income depended on Senate-funded maintenance.

Miaren.t: Miaren's Blood Red Roads income would slowly erode if the roads were not maintained.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the war in Mitwold is used as an example of where a Bregasland briar might have spent the season.

Necropolis.t: The White Roads connecting Necropolis held up better than most, showing only minor erosion.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: new trods in Ossium are noted as part of the enlarged Navarr network.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: new trods in Sküld, within Otkodov, are noted as part of the enlarged Navarr network.

Reikos.t: The granite White Roads serving Reikos suffered only light erosion.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos's Blood Red Roads income was at risk, and its fashionable citizens led the craze for wearing spring flowers.

Segura.t: Segura's Sunset Roads were badly worn by the Spring magic, and their benefits would fade unless the Senate allowed maintenance to continue.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm's Blood Red Roads income was at risk, and its vallorn-plant farms would be listed if both mandates were enacted.

Sermersuaq.t: The surge in herds boded well for the Winterfolk returning to Sermersuaq.

Skarsind.t: Imperial Orcs raising herds in Skarsind could expect them to grow significantly.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: as a Grendel-held territory, Spiral was excluded from the enchantment's benefits.

Tassato.t: Tassato's Blood Red Roads income would decline by a Throne a season if maintenance stopped.

Temeschwar.t: The Blood Red Roads built by Temeschwar's late La Volpe bore the brunt of the damage, putting the territory's road income at risk.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj-held Barrens was excluded from the enchantment, and recent fighting there had left some soldiers disillusioned.

Therunin.t: Concerns were raised that cultivating chaos fruit in Therunin could be dangerous because of the vallorn there.

Upwold.t: Upwold's Blood Red Roads income would slowly erode unless the roads were maintained.

Children of Wrecks.d: After Shivaarn's followers destroyed the Shining Pillar and betrayed the Asaveans, the Salt Lords denounced them. Free Landing then rejected Salt Lord rule, and the wreckers made Atalaya a haven for Siakha's worshippers. They seized Cazar Straits under Azzura di Cazarri and stormed Axiom Prison in the Iron Confederacy, freeing rogue magicians. They now raid Imperial and Grendel lands alike and are at war with the Grendel. Some Imperial citizens have defected to them. The page set out conjunctions in Madruga and Sarvos, backed by boons from Rhianos, along with opportunities to strike Jotun, Grendel and Druj holdings weakened by Siakha-blessed raids.

Druj.t: The Varnalis family of Grimfen Mire, unsettled by raids in the east of the Forest of Ulnak, were moving stores of herbs and potions. This gave Imperial heroes a chance to defeat them and take their goods and white granite.

Grendel.t: The Grendel lost Free Landing's allegiance and Cazar Straits to the Children of Wrecks, who are now at war with them. Raids have also left their resupply isle of Dunreagh vulnerable to Imperial attack.

Jotun.t: Raids along the Skallahn coast drew most of the garrison away from Augaard's Bluff, leaving its weirwood stores open to an Imperial strike.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn lands in Madruga bore the brunt of the wreckers' activity. Some corsair families were rumoured to keep hidden shrines to Siakha, and the reclusive Tabhorios family appealed to Strategos Gael i Guerra for protection from a pursuing mob.

The League.t: Wreckers slipped into Sarvos to curse the territory with deadly storms from a Spring regio, threatening Aversa and the Wellspring of Jade. Stopping them fell to the Jade Custodian, Giacomo Corvinoscuro.

Varushka.t: Wagon raiders trading at the market in Ossium reported the Varnalis' movements. They offered to loot the Druj family's white granite if the Champion of Prosperity defeated them.

Wintermark.t: The icewalker Kaija Headstrong of the Narwhal's Spear scouted the wrecker mob in Madruga. Finn Vertering of Vertering Hall offered the Champion of Ambition, Eldrid Vestardottir, a share of weirwood taken from Augaard's Bluff.

Children of Wrecks.o: Followers of Siakha in the Bay of Catazar formed a loose coalition, the Children of Wrecks, under High Priestess Shivaarn, broke decisively from the Grendel and claimed Free Landing and Cazar Straits. Several conjunctions arose to confront them or to exploit savage raids they had inspired.

Ayereed/Gainmeachdubh.t: The Isle of Dunreagh, a Grendel cache of herbs, mana crystals and mithril, was left under-defended and open to assault.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The Children of Wrecks claimed the region from the Grendel and turned its grand lighthouse into a shrine to Siakha under Azzura di Cazarri.

Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire.t: The Varnalis family were travelling through the mire with a chest of herbs and potions, making them the target of the Champion of Prosperity, Hugh Farrier.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: A mob of wreckers and heralds plundered the pomegranate orchards, slaughtered corsairs and pursued the Tabhorios family.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: The region rejected Salt Lord rule and was held by the Children of Wrecks, who made Atalaya a haven for Siakha's worshippers. A mysterious, Lock-shrouded conjunction to Baleen Cove fell to the Champion of Vigilance.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named. It is touched only by general references to wrecker activity on the Madruga coast.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn corsair was visiting the new foreigners of Beoraidh when he learned of Dunreagh's vulnerability.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: Wreckers slipped into Bocche to work storm curses at the Spring regio Ferocity's Stand, endangering the hamlet of Aversa and the Wellspring of Jade.

Skallahn/Iron Stand.t: Augaard's Bluff, near the Sermersuaq border, was left with a reduced garrison guarding weirwood, fine arms and herbs.

Ayereed.t: Raids have left the Grendel resupply isle of Dunreagh weakly garrisoned, offering a chance to plunder 12 wains of mithril, with Asaveans expected to arrive there too.

Bay of Catazar.t: High Priestess Shivaarn claimed the whole bay for Siakha, and her ships stalk its waters, preying on Empire, Grendel, Suranni and foreign shipping alike.

Feroz.t: The Children of Wrecks seized Cazar Straits from the Grendel, leaving the southern Jewelled Isles under their control. Little more is known, since few Freeborn remain in the territory.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Raids in the east of the territory prompted the Druj Varnalis family to move their stores, exposing them to an Imperial skirmish.

Madruga.t: Free Landing now answers to the Children of Wrecks rather than the Salt Lords, and wrecker mobs roam Calvos Sound. Two conjunctions here offered chances to confront them.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the corsair Juan i Macabeo i Erigo learned of Dunreagh's weakness while visiting the new foreigners of Beoraidh.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: wagon raiders who trade at the stinking market in Ossium supplied the intelligence on the Varnalis.

Sarvos.t: Wreckers infiltrated the territory to unleash deadly storms that could kill people across Sarvos, though Caricomare's flood defences would limit the harm there.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: it is named as the distant, cold refuge of Howl-in-the-Night, and as the border Vertering Hall would cross to reach Augaard's Bluff.

Skallahn.t: Coastal raids drew Jotun forces away, leaving Augaard's Bluff and its weirwood stores lightly guarded.

Chilled to the bone.d: After defeating a force of pressed Druj farmers on the Galath Fields, Imperial forces spread across Ossium without maps. At Lomaa, seat of the Bone Serpent clan, the Dawnish took the Crawling Depths and freed about five hundred slaves born underground. The mine produces 14 wains of mithril a season; a 300-throne Senate commission taking two seasons would double that, and the Senate may allocate it as Imperial or national. The trapped weirwood hall of the Bitter Vats produces herbs and Oil of Blackthorn, a spoil of war for the Military Council to assign. The hopeless Sand Fishers orcs and the calculating Varushkan-like townsfolk of Ketsov both submitted to Imperial rule.

Druj.t: The Druj were caught completely unprepared, with their elite troops absent and only pressed farmers and labourers in the field. The Bone Serpent clan lost its clan seat at Lomaa, its mithril mine and its poison workshop, and Ketsov's Druj-allied leaders fled east with what wealth they could carry.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: soldiers who fought in the Reikos campaign are noted as having seen slaves before, though none had seen people reduced to the state of the Crawling Depths slaves.

Chilled to the bone.o: In autumn 382YE, Dawnish and Varushkan armies invaded Ossium in the Mallum, catching the Druj by surprise. They captured the Crawling Depths mithril mine and the Bitter Vats, freed slaves, and met the territory's orc and human inhabitants.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: The Bittershore was where the Empire first met the Sand Fishers. Bone Snake symbols are painted everywhere there to mark the clan's ownership, and the Sand Fishers quietly keep their sashes in case the Druj return.

Ossium/Galath Fields.t: The Empire won a great battle here against a far larger force of conscripted Druj labourers. Control of the Bitter Vats depends on holding the region, and would be lost if the Druj reconquered it.

Ossium.t: Imperial forces seized much of Ossium, including the Crawling Depths and the Bitter Vats at Lomaa. Without maps, though, they struggled to work out exactly what they had conquered, and the Sand Fishers and Ketsovs waited to learn who would now rule them.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: veterans of the Reikos campaign are cited as having encountered slaves there before.

The Semmerlak.t: The Sand Fishers fish, catch crabs and hunt eels in the lake's shallow waters. Its violent storms and turbulent river leave them feeling unable to flee Druj rule, and their oral history says they once controlled the lands all round it.

Chime the sound.d: The warlock Lirk, speaking for Tathenon, offered a ritual text unknown to Imperial lore in exchange for the original herbal almanac the Imperial Orcs took from the Druj. The trade would be completed over several summits, starting with a winged messenger to Rak. Freynir offered the ancient mask Strágríma, whose wearers hear whispering voices, if Thule warlocks could study the Shepherd of the Great Herd for a season, halving its output. With the Thule short of food, a Senate motion could create a charitable caravan, needing at least 50 Thrones to help and 200 to help greatly. Two Freeborn mandates would send priests to Otkodov, either urging freed slaves south or urging virtue on the Thule; either would provoke a diplomatic incident.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the almanac the Thule seek was taken from the Druj, and the freed humans sent south were former Druj slaves.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs received two Thule offers: a ritual text in exchange for their original Druj herbal almanac, and the mask Strágríma in exchange for hosting warlocks studying the Shepherd of the Great Herd. Both the Preceptor and Shepherd positions were vacant at the time.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn Synod statement noted that the Thule sought Imperial help because they are in danger from the Jotun.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn could encourage the Thule's abolition of slavery by sending a charitable food caravan north. Their priests could also travel to Otkodov under either of two prepared mandates, both of which would risk a serious diplomatic incident.

Thule.t: Facing a food shortfall after freeing their slaves, the Thule sought Imperial knowledge through offers by Tathenon and Freynir. They might receive charitable food, or Freeborn preachers they would strongly resent.

Varushka.t: Thule merchants appeared in Varushka after the tariffs were lifted. Its national assembly urged preparation for travellers, and some of the freed human slaves arrived in northern Karsk.

Wintermark.t: Thule merchants were trading in Wintermark, which had already received two Thule offers. Freed human slaves arrived in eastern Seremersuaq, and Thule diplomats told Wintermarkers of Otkodov's food shortage.

Chime the sound.o: After the Thule Dragons outlawed slavery and the Senate lifted tariffs on Thule trade, the Thule offered the Imperial Orcs two knowledge-for-reward exchanges. Meanwhile the Brass Coast was given the chance to send charitable food to a hungry Otkodov, or to send priests north at the risk of a diplomatic incident.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Mentioned in passing: Mieriada is where Rak's Embassy to Otkodov stands, the destination for winged messengers accepting the Thule offers.

Otkodov/Nithoggir.t: The Thule hoped to reproduce the Imperial Orcs' fenceless herding techniques in Nithoggir's open lands if Freynir's warlocks were allowed to study them.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: Urdur was named alongside Nithoggir as land where the Thule hoped to apply the herding methods learned from the Shepherd of the Great Herd.

Verthandi/Askja.t: Mentioned in passing: the region itself is not discussed; the name appears only through the Thule diplomat Askja of Volham, who hinted at Otkodov's food shortage.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn Synod statement contrasted aiding the Thule with travelling to Kahraman to kill wounded Lasambrians.

Karsk.t: Some of the roughly eight hundred freed human slaves of the Druj were returned into northern Karsk, where priests and others worked to house them and find them work.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: a Synod statement declared that the House of Guerra in Madruga will always welcome refugees.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule ambassador Rak dwells at the Embassy to Otkodov in Miekarova, where messages about both offers must be sent.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the slaves the Thule liberated from the Druj in Ossium and sent into Varushka were all human.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov faced short-term starvation after its slaves were freed. It could receive a charitable Imperial food caravan, or Freeborn priests preaching to its people at the risk of a major diplomatic incident.

Skarsind.t: The Thule offers were aimed at Skarsind's orcs: the senator for Skarsind or the Preceptor of its College of Warcasting would need to answer Lirk's proposed trade of a ritual for the Druj almanac.

Verthandi.t: Mentioned in passing: Verthandi was noted as the only part of Otkodov the Empire knows much about.

Chords.d: The Apulian Orcs endorse Ambition, Prosperity and Vigilance, but also prize audacity, cunning, fidelity and retribution, viewing all virtues as pathways to power. Their questioners petitioned the Synod to rule on each quality before anyone fell foul of the law. The General Assembly could deem a quality a noble ideal like honesty or glory, condemn it as a malign spiritual force, or, with a doctrinal change, name it an eighth Virtue. Any Virtue assembly could instead claim one as an expression of its Virtue. Retribution in particular resembles the forbidden aura of Vengeance. The Apulians accept they may need to compromise, and Graime the Questioner was expected at Anvil to answer priests' questions.

Grendel.t: The Grendel orcs who defected in Spiral brought their own creed, built on the pursuit of power and four virtues outside Imperial doctrine, and now await the Synod's verdict on which they may keep preaching.

The League.t: The League's egregores Harlequin and Innamorata were weighing whether to accept the Apulian Orcs as citizens, while the Synod's rulings would decide which of the orcs' ideals might spread through the League.

Chords.o: After the Grendel of Spiral under Salt Lord Kaliact switched allegiance to the Empire and sought to join the League, their priests asked the Imperial Synod to rule on four non-Imperial virtues they follow: audacity, cunning, fidelity and retribution.

Spiral.t: Spiral's Apulian Orcs, now part of the Empire after the territory passed to the Wolves of War, were asking the Synod to rule on their beliefs, so the outcome would shape how their questioners may preach there.

Church of your heart.d: While the Granite Pillar defended the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion from the Winnowers, veterans awaited Synod confirmation before leaving their chapters. A Vigilance mandate costing 50 doses of liao would grant Highborn armies Bring Virtue to the Scions: more casualties inflicted on scions, more casualties suffered. A Loyalty mandate would grant Defence of the Virtuous: stronger defence against scions, at the same cost in casualties. Neither competes with the other. Enacting either would stop Highborn armies generating opportunities until every Cold Sun army in the Empire is destroyed. Kalina Jadwigowna Piosnkowa Prochnost and Sławomir Rabovich Bolotstrazh offered Varushkan versions using Partner of Greatness.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly could send veterans to the Granite Pillar, Seventh Wave and Valiant Pegasus, gaining offensive or defensive orders against the scions. The price would be that its armies generate no further opportunities until Cold Sun is driven from the Empire.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is named as one of the territories where scions caused suffering that the Loyal hope never to see repeated.

Varushka.t: Alternative mandates were offered to the Varushkan Assembly that would give its armies either new order, usable only in Varushkan territories. Enacting one would bar the Assembly from further mandates until the Cold Sun armies in Varushka are defeated.

Church of your heart.o: In Winter 385YE, Highborn veterans answered calls from Ira of the Flame Beneath the Earth and General Asenath to return to arms against the scions of Cold Sun. This gave the Highborn Assembly two mandate opportunities for new army orders, with alternative versions offered to the Varushkan Assembly.

Karov/Duzekani.t: Mentioned in passing: Sławomir's proposed Varushkan mandate declares that what happened in Livardz and Duzekani will not be repeated.

Bastion.t: The Granite Pillar under General Asenath was defending the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion against the Winnowers, and the veterans' first aim was to make the Highborn homeland safe.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Karov is cited as a territory where scion horrors befell civilians, a fate the Loyal want to prevent elsewhere.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is cited alongside Karov as a place where scions brought harm that Highborn dedicates of Loyalty vow will not be repeated.

Cities of the Iron Labyrinth.d: Estavus made mystic scrolls of Accoutrements of War, Ramparts of Ashlar and Hammers of Fury available through Before the Throne of Estavus, each requiring a rune of Lann and costly materials. Her Architects of Iron and Stone offered, for a rising price, to assess mithril or white granite bourse seats if the Conclave asked. Her herald Illia sold limited magical items at the Anvil regio, and Hand of the Maker was eased to magnitude six with warm ashes at the Imperial regio. Varushkans remained barred from Before the Throne of Estavus. Ephisis reported gluts of mana crystals and mithril and dearer beggar's lye and tempest jade, and withdrew last season's Grendel deal. The Lictors' agent Oathsmith would meet Ashborn Trosk's representative, while the City of Locks remained in turmoil.

Grendel.t: The deal between the Grendel and the Empire, brokered by the City of Gold and Lead the season before, was declared no longer available.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: a League reckoner described the transformed Lictors as "smart", and the opening fiction likened the haggling herald to a Sarvos street urchin.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the City of Gold and Lead's glut of mana crystals was attributed to sales by warlocks of the Frozen North.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction showed Urizeni magicians of a spire selling tempest jade to a herald of Ephisis, and the page noted the scroll rituals could not be added to Urizen lore.

Varushka.t: Estavus's year-long injunction still stood, so Varushkan magicians could not use Before the Throne of Estavus to take up any of her offers; their mana would be spent and their goods returned.

Cities of the Iron Labyrinth.o: In Spring 386YE the Autumn cities answered the Archmage of Autumn's call for aid in the Empire's wars. Estavus offered mystic scrolls, bourse surveys, magical items and a cheaper Hand of the Maker, Ephisis reported volatile prices, and the Lictors arranged to meet Ashborn Trosk's representative.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is not named on the page, and its only possible link is the reference to warlocks of the Frozen North selling mana crystals to Ephisis.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named on the page, which features Urizeni spire magicians only in its opening fiction.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction compared the herald's banal patter to that of a Sarvos street urchin.

City folk and country folk.d: Whittle's thirty-year truce with the Jotun ended after the villagers aided the Empire, and young, old and infirm alike fled to Tassato. Margaret Steward offered green iron for the Rua da Madeira and the Avenida da Penha, a run-down hilltop quarter of Mestra, to house their dependants apart from city life. The fighters would go on to Overton. An enclave was estimated to yield 50 ingots of green iron a season for a year to Tassato's businesses. It also carried the risk of Synod censure, because the Whittlers openly embrace Hatred. The Sheriff of the Mournwold must decide whether Overton accepts their fighters. Friar Robin was travelling to Anvil to face his accusers and to seek an accommodation with the Marcher Assembly.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: a few orcs at the Mestra docks claimed to be Imperial Orcs, though onlookers doubted it.

Jotun.t: The Jotun ended their long, uneasy truce with Whittle after the villagers aided the Empire, driving the Whittlefolk from their land. The Whittlers now vow to fight them from Overton and to return if their land is retaken.

The League.t: Tassato's Chamber of Commerce, which unites Mestran and Regarian merchants, had to decide whether to sell Mestran streets to the Whittlefolk. It weighed the green iron profit against the risk of Synod condemnation and the spread of Hatred.

The Marches.t: Whittle Marchers were made refugees by the Jotun, and the Sheriff of the Mournwold must decide whether to take their fighters into the Overton garrison. Friar Robin was seeking an accommodation with the Marcher Assembly over the Whittlers' belief in Hatred.

City folk and country folk.o: In Winter 380YE about a hundred Whittlefolk fled their Jotun-held village in Freemoor and camped outside Tassato Mestra. Their steward, Margaret Steward, asked the Tassatan Chamber of Commerce to sell them two streets for a closed enclave, and the Chamber postponed its decision to a meeting at Anvil.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: The Marcher village of Whittle in Freemoor lost its thirty-year truce with the Jotun, and its people fled south along the old road to Tassato.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: The Whittlers' fighters offered to join the garrison at Overton, though they did not wish to settle their families in the Greensward. Their arrival could spread their Hatred among the garrison.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: The Whittlefolk camped outside Mestra's walls and worked its short-handed docks. They sought to buy the run-down Rua da Madeira and Avenida da Penha as a closed enclave for their dependants.

Mournwold.t: The Whittlefolk were forced out of their village in the Mournwold. Their fighters proposed to return to the territory to join the garrison at Overton, pending the Sheriff's approval.

Tassato.t: The refugees camped outside Tassato Mestra and worked its docks. The territory's businesses were offered about 50 green iron ingots a season if the Chamber agreed to an enclave, but the deal carried religious and social risks.

City lights.d: Gains from the newly finished Blood Red Roads lifted almost every citizen's income, but League bravos and mountebanks lost their income to bite, whose price and violence were rising; the Senate could outlaw it and fund magistrates with 25 thrones a season. In Siroc, Safya i Kalamar i Guerra of the Glass Parador refused the Full Sails Carta's offer to buy out fleeing Freeborn, boosting Madrugan production. Siroc merchants offered to help fund a new shipyard until the Summer Solstice. Ambassador Mila Eisenfalke believed the Commonwealth would garrison a Siroc fortification, and Menno Van Ritsjhof might design coastal defences. Suaq and Steinr merchants proposed the Kalpaheim Runehall, needing 60 wains of white granite.

Grendel.t: The Grendel, holding Atalaya and all of Free Landing and raiding Lightsea, are the threat Siroc is defying, and the proposed shipyard and sea defences are aimed squarely at resisting them.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as one of the westward routes from Kalpaheim made easier by the Blood Red Roads.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is named as a neighbour that trades with Hahnmark and lies on a road from Kalpaheim.

The Brass Coast.t: Madrugan businesses gain an extra rank of production thanks to the Mistress of the Glass Parador's call to stand firm, and Siroc's merchants offer to help fund a new shipyard to replace the one burned at Atalaya.

The League.t: League bravos and mountebanks lose their income to bite as drug violence spreads through the cities, the Full Sails Carta's opportunistic offer in Siroc was rebuffed, and the League National Assembly could urge Menno Van Ritsjhof to design Siroc's sea defences.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Little Whittle carries Mournwold green iron to Tassato, and Upwold and Marcher neighbours are named as Hahnmark's established trade routes.

Wintermark.t: Suaq and Steinr merchants, aided by the runesmith-engineers Hurik and Manun, propose a Kalpaheim Runehall to exploit the Blood Red Roads, offering either extra coin or mine resources to Hahnmark businesses if commissioned and built.

City lights.o: In Spring 382YE the Blood Red Roads brought a short-lived boost to incomes across the Empire, while the addictive drug bite fuelled violence among League bravos and mountebanks. Madruga's defiance of the Grendel raised trade and opened opportunities for a shipyard and sea defences at Siroc, and Hahnmark merchants proposed a runehall at Kalpaheim.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Free Landing, including Atalaya where the Grendel burned the shipyard, is described as wholly in Grendel hands.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel raiders are described looting north and south along the Lightsea coast, with Quzar already looted.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Mestran bravos, enraged by a rumour that Regarians had intercepted their bite shipment, crossed the river by boat and fought deadly clashes, and many Mestrans still blame the thieving Regarians.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: Regario mountebanks were rumoured to have intercepted a bite shipment, drawing armed Mestran bravos across the river; Regarians dismiss the anger as proof the Mestrans are drug-addled.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes the Commonwealth could not feasibly move an army to the Bay of Catazar.

Hahnmark.t: Merchants propose the Kalpaheim Runehall, which would take six months and 60 wains of white granite and grant Hahnmark businesses either 1060 coins a season (Bargains) or a share of 60 mine resources (Wealth); the opportunity lasts until the end of the Autumn Equinox.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is named as a trading neighbour of Hahnmark and a route west from Kalpaheim.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is named as a destination Wintermark merchants can now reach quickly on the Blood Red Roads.

Madruga.t: Every business in Madruga gains an extra rank of production this season, and Siroc is offered a cheaper new shipyard until the end of the Summer Solstice plus possible Commonwealth-garrisoned or Van Ritsjhof-designed defences against the Grendel.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Little Whittle is noted as bringing green iron from the Mournwold to Tassato.

Sarvos.t: Bite has become so sought after that a dose fetches three or four crowns in parts of Sarvos, amid violence against dealers; the city's Colossus and markets are also noted as drawing foreign visitors.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Segura is not named; it shares only in the general Empire-wide trade boost described.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the northern borders of Sermersuaq are used to compare travel times from Kalpaheim.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a westward route from Kalpaheim eased by the Blood Red Roads.

Tassato.t: A rumour about stolen bite sparked armed clashes across the river between Regario and Mestra that left two dead and dozens seriously injured, and resentments continue to simmer.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is named as the road south from Kalpaheim that was once hard going for wagons.

Civil tongue.d: Sumaah, still at war, sent Envoy Azcan and Tipoa the Insightful back to request a formal Senate reception from Ambassador Accalon of Felix's Watch, with Tarquinius of Ankarien present; otherwise they would leave. Asavea stayed warm but faced provincial revolts and sought mercenaries. Jarm's Rigia stayed closed, and the Kobarid offered star jewels through a proposed fortified exchange, with a deadline of the Autumn Equinox. Faraden trade grew with Segura's new roads. Axos offered 500 scouts for the Mountains of the Moon spy network, which needs a Military Council or Senate vote. The Suranni demanded an end to liao smuggling and spoke of reparations. Cargo's fortification against the Druj was half complete.

Dawn.t: Faraden merchants remained keen on a trade enclave in central Astolat, ideally at Laroc or Oldheart, to reach Dawnish luxuries, though nothing had yet been arranged.

Druj.t: Cargo, home to three embassies, was under immediate threat of Druj invasion, and its foreign-aided fortification was half built to resist them.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan discontent over the Delves' agreement with the Grendel continued, though it was muted by the magic protecting Imperial ships.

Highguard.t: With the completion of the Necropolis warehouses, more Sarcophan merchants came to Highguard, and the Kruidenkenner herbalists' guild sought new markets through its enclave there.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Sumaah delegate Tipoa the Insightful was noted as best known for work on doctrine changes concerning the Imperial Orcs.

The Brass Coast.t: New roads brought prosperity to Segura and wealth to Madruga through Faraden trade, while Asavean merchants grew common on the coast. Kalino's troops left Feroz after the slave rebellion was crushed, but the Suranni accused the Empire of smuggling liao through Feroz.

The League.t: Asavean merchants were increasingly seen across Sarvos, the new Faraden road reached Tassato, and the Kobarid, hosted by Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato, proposed an exchange modelled on Tassato's Mana Exchange.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the civil service Secretary to the Diplomatic Corps, John Cooper of Upwold, double-checked Sumaah's request for Tarquinius of Ankarien to attend.

Urizen.t: Axos sought a land route to the spires of eastern Urizen and offered to help map the Mountains of the Moon, an offer that would need Military Council or Senate approval.

Varushka.t: Faraden traders remained eager for an enclave in Volodmartz, most likely Triosk, to gain access to Varushkan timber and ore, though there had been no movement on it.

Civil tongue.o: In Summer 382YE the Empire's foreign relations were surveyed nation by nation: a Sumaah envoy returned seeking a formal Senate reception, Axos offered scouts to help map the Mountains of the Moon, Jarmish jewellers proposed a trading exchange, and the Iron Confederacy made fresh demands.

Astolat.t: The Faraden hoped for a trade enclave in central Astolat, at Laroc or Oldheart, but nothing had yet been agreed.

Bay of Catazar.t: The recent Imperial effort to map the Bay angered the Iron Confederacy, which talked of reparations for the incursion into its coastal waters.

Feroz.t: Kalino's troops withdrew from Feroz after the slave rebellion was crushed, and the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull prospered. The Suranni, however, demanded an end to alleged liao smuggling through the territory.

Kalino.t: The Duke of Kalino's troops returned south across the border after helping crush the slave rebellion in Feroz.

Madruga.t: The new road through Siroc linked Segura's network to the Blood Red Roads, and the influx of Faraden merchants brought more wealth into Madruga.

Mountains of the Moon.t: Axos offered 500 Agema and Toxatai scouts to support the Imperial spy network mapping the territory, provided the Military Council or Senate approved. Any maps produced would be shared with the Axou.

Necropolis.t: The completed warehouses drew more Sarcophan merchants, including the Kruidenkenner herbalists, who were keen to exploit their new Highguard enclave.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Asavean merchants were described as increasingly common across Sarvos.

Segura.t: The completed south-western road network, linking Anduz to Tassato via Siroc, brought increased prosperity to Segura through Faraden trade.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Zana noted that no map showed any mountain pass from Spiral towards Axos.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato was named as an endpoint of the new Faraden road and as the model for the Kobarid's proposed exchange.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: only as the home of civil servant John Cooper of Upwold.

Volodmartz.t: The Faraden remained keen on a trade enclave in Volodmartz, most likely at Triosk, for timber and ore, though nothing had progressed.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Zana observed that no map showed any pass from Zenith through the eastern mountains.

Claim Sungold Pass.d: Proposed by the senator for Karov and seconded by the senator for Sarvos, the motion reasserted the Empire's claim that the Sungold Pass belongs to Opascari in Volodmartz rather than to neighbouring Otkodov. It also declared that foreigners exploiting resources in Imperial land without the Empire's direct invitation is not acceptable. The motion passed. It had implications for the Thule, who may also have laid claim to the mine there. The claim did not last: at the Summer Solstice 383YE the Senate chose to cede Sungold Pass to the Thule, effectively abrogating this motion.

Thule.t: The Senate rejected any Thule right to exploit the Sungold Pass mine without Imperial invitation, challenging their possible claim. A year later the Senate ceded the pass to them.

Varushka.t: Varushka's claim to the Sungold Pass as part of its territory of Volodmartz was formally upheld by the Senate, though the pass was ceded to the Thule a year later.

Claim Sungold Pass.o: In Summer 382YE the Senate passed a motion declaring that the Sungold Pass and the mountain called the Traveller lie within Opascari in Volodmartz, and that foreigners exploiting resources on Imperial land without the Empire's direct invitation is unacceptable.

Volodmartz/Opascari.t: Opascari was named as the region containing the Sungold Pass and the mountain called the Traveller. That claim was effectively abandoned when the pass was ceded to the Thule in Summer 383YE.

Otkodov.t: The Thule-held territory of Otkodov was explicitly denied possession of the Sungold Pass, which the Senate insisted lay within the Empire.

Volodmartz.t: The Senate declared the Sungold Pass and the Traveller part of Volodmartz and condemned unsanctioned foreign exploitation of its resources there.

Clarification on the Brilliant Shore.d: In Winter 379YE an administrative motion asked the Senate to clarify the status of the Brilliant Shore, a national bourse resource in Skarsind. The question was whether the position should remain with the current seat holder until next up for election, or pass immediately to the Imperial Orcs to elect. The Senate decided the seat should remain with the current holder. As a result, the Brilliant Shore bourse seat would become available for election by the Imperial Orcs at the Summer Solstice 380YE.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs were not given the Brilliant Shore seat at once, but gained the right to elect its holder at the Summer Solstice 380YE.

Clarification on the Brilliant Shore.o: The Senate ruled that the Brilliant Shore, a national bourse seat in Skarsind, should stay with its current holder until it next came up for election rather than passing at once to the Imperial Orcs to elect.

Skarsind.t: The Brilliant Shore, a bourse resource in Skarsind, kept its current seat holder until the Imperial Orcs could elect a new one at the Summer Solstice 380YE.

Climb every mountain.d: The Disciples of Sulemaine, cast out when the sword scholars were sundered, hid in heterodox temples in Zenith, rebellious citadels in Cinion and iconoclastic spires in Operus. Herminius' mandate, upheld 234-20, was welcomed by pro-Imperial spires but not by those actually sheltering the Disciples. The Urizen Assembly could pass a mandate (two competing wordings were offered) creating a raiding venture, Drive out the Disciples. Committing a combined strength of at least two thousand would kill dozens and force the Disciples to respond. Such raids would be illegal unless the Senate outlawed membership of the Disciples, letting magistrates lead the raids at no cost to the Senate.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: rebellious citadels in Cinion shelter the Disciples partly because their people blame the Empire for the League taking the territory.

Urizen.t: Urizen faced the choice of driving the Disciples of Sulemaine out by force, either through illegal raids by its military units urged by a Synod mandate or lawfully alongside magistrates if the Senate outlawed the fraternity, with many sentinels keen to join any such campaign.

Climb every mountain.o: Herminius' Urizen Assembly mandate calling on Urizeni to turn out the Disciples of Sulemaine failed to move the spires sheltering them, since they harbour in places that reject the Synod's authority. The wind set out two further options: an illegal Synod mandate to hunt the Disciples down by force, or a Senate motion criminalising their fraternity.

Morrow/Operus.t: Disciples dwelt in the highest peaks of Operus, in iconoclastic spires where followers of Abraxus seek ways to breach the Labyrinth, and these spires would face raids if Urizen moved to drive them out.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Rebellious citadels in Cinion, whose people blame the Empire for the League's seizure of the territory, sheltered Disciples of Sulemaine.

Zenith/Clypion.t: Clypion's highest peaks were among the places where the Disciples found safe harbour in spires sympathetic to their philosophy, unmoved by Herminius' mandate.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Proceris was among the mountain refuges of the Disciples, sheltered by spires that question the Synod and would not expel them voluntarily.

Morrow.t: The Disciples were sheltering in iconoclastic spires of Morrow, where Herminius' call to expel them had no effect, making them potential targets of any raids to drive them out.

Spiral.t: Disciples of Sulemaine were found in rebellious Urizeni citadels in Spiral's Cinion region, where resentment of the Empire over the loss of the territory gave them shelter.

Zenith.t: Zenith, home of Senator Herminius, held heterodox temples long sceptical of the Synod that sheltered the Disciples in its high peaks and refused to turn them out.

Cloud waves break.d: The mist eroded or altered less vital memories but left names, loyalties and ambitions intact. Hearth-magic wards kept it at bay, and citizens were urged to renew friendships, receive anointings, renew oaths and share stories of modern heroes in the Navarr manner. Some embraced the forgetting to begin new lives. Arcane Mark, Cast Off The Chain of Memory, Infant Starts with a Blank Slate and Transmogrification of the Soul's Echo worked differently during the Solstice. Red-masked tulpas traded memories with willing people everywhere except Varushka. Records suggest similar episodes in 346YE and 296YE. The Thule sought the eternal Sadogua's counsel and were told the mist meant nothing and would pass.

Highguard.t: Devorah of Twin Suns, a Highborn magister from Syrene, discovered that washing the hands in pure water while rejecting it within ten minutes dispels the false memory created by Cast Off The Chain of Memory.

Navarr.t: The Navarr practice of Songs and Stories was held up as a model for resisting the fog, Navarr blood mages found blood and water refusing to mix, and stridings reported record numbers walking away from lives in which they felt trapped.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: sutannir are among the storytellers encouraged to gather and share tales of modern heroes at the Solstice.

The League.t: In Temeschwar, troupe magicians performing The Lament of the Shepherd fell silent together and recited strange, sorrowful lines during a ritual for the cicisbeo Guild of the Steel Quill.

Thule.t: The fog plagued Thule lands, and the warlock Urnamost, emissary of Tathenon the Gyre, paid Sadogua four measures of dragonbone only to be told the mist portends nothing and will pass.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: learned magicians 'from Urizen to Wintermark' suggested covens, sects and banners renew their binding oaths at the Solstice.

Varushka.t: Varushkans sleeping in warded homes reported no fog in their dreams, the tulpas did not manifest there at all, and Varushkan blood mages saw blood and water refuse to mix while cabalists distrusted the tulpas for refusing hospitality.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark is named among the lands whose magicians urged oath-renewal, and skalds are among the storytellers encouraged to share tales.

Cloud waves break.o: In Winter 383YE an Empire-wide supernatural fog clouded and subtly altered memories and invaded dreams, accompanied by masked tulpas of the Door that offered to take unwanted memories. The phenomenon, tied to a conjunction of the Wanderer with the Lock and the Door, abated after the Winter Solstice.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the eerie glowing fog that shrouded the Bay in late 379YE and early 380YE is contrasted with this Empire-wide mist.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named, though Lyceum scholars are credited with discovering the empowered Arcane Mark.

Hercynia.t: The Hercynian blood-magic coven Tears Unshed Shall Dry discovered that adding Beggar's Lye to Infant Starts with a Blank Slate strips all knowledge from a willing subject, freeing them to learn anew.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is not named; it is touched only by the fog that spread to every corner of the Empire.

Temeschwar.t: At the Bloody Great Theatre, performers of The Lament of the Shepherd simultaneously began reciting unsettling lines that no one could afterwards recall beyond a sense of past sorrow.

Colourblind.d: Investigation found the blight was a Winter curse from the Wasteland, spread by the Parched or Ashwalkers and sustained by a handful of powerful Dry Patricians, members of the Aldea di Tutamen who sought physical immortality. Dry Patricians can be destroyed only by Words of Ending at magnitude 18. Ashwalkers can be dispersed with Turns the Circle, though some are slowly becoming Dry Patricians. Exorcism and Insight fail against them. Heralds of Ossegrahn supplied pure Spring water that lures the creatures. A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered the Silver Chalice's Grandmaster a chance to destroy some. Regrow the Land's Heart only holds the blight in check, and its origin remained unexplained.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Aldea di Tutamen traced their roots to the exodus from Highguard, and their robes recalled pre-Highguard patricians.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr members of the Silver Chalice drew unsettling parallels between the blight and the vallorn, while stressing it was not an equivalent threat.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn hakima and kohan died investigating the blight on their own lands. The Sails of the First Flame coven's Regrow the Land's Heart and Hallow of the Green World kept it from worsening. The source was a Freeborn family, the Aldea di Tutamen, cursed into Dry Patricians.

The League.t: League magicians and archers fought alongside the effort. A Holberg doctor who came with Lord Rain's heralds declared that the Parched were a sickness that must be fought.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni sentinels appear guarding the edge of the blight, and a Urizen stargazer suggested the desiccated land might be an extrusion of the Winter realm.

Colourblind.o: The Silver Chalice, working with Freeborn hakima and kohan and friends of Lord Rain, uncovered the nature of the Winter blight on Madruga's Great Grasses. It was spread by desiccated monsters, led by the cursed Aldea di Tutamen family, and an opportunity arose to destroy some of them through the Sentinel Gate.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: The Sentinel Gate was to open on the edge of the blight deep in the Great Grasses. There, heroes could lure out and fight the Dry Patricians, though the battleground would likely be destroyed even in victory.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: a League doctor from Holberg, Doctor von Holberg, rescues a hakima in the story and joins the effort alongside Lord Rain's heralds.

Madruga.t: The Great Grasses in Madruga were being consumed by a Winter blight that only ritual magic was holding back. Failure to destroy the Dry Patricians would mean the Grasses could never be restored and would need constant magical containment.

Come back to stay.d: Research circulated at Lord Armand Remys's request claimed that Varkula's tomb has three doors, two reportedly opened when Holberg and Skarsind fell, and that the third might now open. People sleeping in Casinea dreamt of a wolf-toothed woman in a crown of black ice berating the Empire for losing Zenith. The Senate interior gained an aura of suspicion and paranoia, blamed by some on Varkula's ghost. An i Tamazir i Riqueza scribe of the House of Quills, whose family executed her will, was seen travelling cagily to Anvil. In Necropolis an unfamiliar bell tolled at midnight, a former tomb guard began preaching that the tomb had been torn open, and the tomb was found barred from outside with the ground before it consecrated to Vigilance.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: a Necropolis citizen grumbles that the Imperatrix should bring Dawn and Navarr to heel.

Druj.t: The Druj conquest of Zenith is the loss that supposedly stirred Varkula's spirit, and the dreams demand that the Druj-held territory be reclaimed immediately.

Highguard.t: The Highborn face unrest at home: Varkula's tomb in Necropolis was found barred and consecrated to Vigilance, and a former tomb guard preaches that her spirit was woken by the defeat of the joined Highborn armies at Zenith.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: some Varushkans darkly suggest Varkula might not regard Skarsind, now held by the Imperial Orcs, as truly in Imperial hands.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the House of Quills scribe was spotted at the Navarr wayhouse of Myfanwy's Rest, and a citizen grumbles that Navarr should be brought to heel.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn House of Quills, the i Tamazir i Riqueza family who executed Varkula's will, are drawn into the rumours after one of them was seen travelling secretively to Anvil.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the earlier fall of Holberg is recalled as the time one of the tomb's doors supposedly opened.

Urizen.t: Many in Urizen see the dreams as proof that losing their territory of Zenith has called Varkula back, and that it must be retaken at once to avert her vengeance.

Varushka.t: Varushkans reportedly experience the Casinea dreams more often, and some suggest the Winterborn might not consider Skarsind truly Imperial.

Come back to stay.o: After Zenith fell to the Druj, rumours spread across the Empire that the spirit of Empress Varkula, whose first conquest was Zenith, was stirring in her tomb in Necropolis, accompanied by shared nightmares, a haunted Senate and strange events at the tomb itself.

Necropolis/Fishguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Fishguard is not named; it is attached as part of Necropolis, where Varkula's tomb and the preaching are found.

Casinea.t: People sleeping in Casinea suffered dreams of a crowned, wolf-toothed woman condemning the loss of Zenith, waking confused and weakened.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: stories recall loud noises from the tomb when Holberg fell to the orcs, though it has since been liberated.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: most relatives of the i Tamazir i Riqueza family of the House of Quills still live in Madruga.

Necropolis.t: In the Black City an unfamiliar bell tolled at midnight, preachers proclaimed Varkula's return, and her tomb was found barred from outside with the ground before it consecrated to Vigilance.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's fall supposedly opened a door of the tomb, and no closing was heard when it returned to the Empire.

Zenith.t: Zenith's fall to the Druj, as the first territory Varkula added to the Empire, is the trigger for all the omens of her return.

Come together.d: Survivors of Thornsong House, lost when Therunin fell to the Druj, inspired the proposal. Commissioned by Senate motion before the end of Summer Solstice 389YE, the Gardens would cost 90 weirwood, 40 white granite, 20 mithril and 450 crowns, take a year, and have a 10-throne upkeep. Each Miaren herb garden would gain two true vervain and one cerulean mazzarine a season, and the Apothecaries Guild would vote on which of three research options to pursue, or four if all four nations helped. Reassigning four great works for a year could remove the need for wains entirely. New sinecures were also offered in Holberg, Ossium and Skarsind. This supersedes the Winter 387YE opportunity.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: their conquest of Therunin destroyed Thornsong House, the loss that inspired the proposal.

Highguard.t: The Benefactor of High Chalcis, Enoch of Atun's Sanctuary, could redirect the Gardens of High Chalcis for a year with a Senate announcement, cutting the weirwood needed by 50 wains. The skilled apothecaries of Reikos would also broaden the college's research if they took part.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Yerende sept is eager to help: redirecting the Red Blade Memorial would remove the need for mithril. A House of the Lost sinecure could create Rhyv's Blade to support Unshackled warriors with herbs and potions, and the earlier Yerende opportunity has lapsed.

Navarr.t: The proposal comes from Navarr dreamspeakers seeking to restore the herbal expertise lost with Thornsong House, though its great cost and the Guild's control of research are clear drawbacks. Bronwen urges the nation to embrace the Apothecaries Guild and use its wayhouses to win support from other nations.

The League.t: Holmauer Park could be redirected for a year to remove the need for white granite, and League doctors could widen the college's research. The League could also build a Holmauer Watchhouse to create the Holmauer Watchcaptain.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Doyen of the Spires is cited as a justified exception to Imperial bodies directing college research, because it relies on unique Urizen magic.

Varushka.t: Krustrozi's Lumbermill could be redirected to cut the weirwood needed by 40 wains, and Varushkan wise ones would broaden the college's research. A Darkwoods Wagonhouse could create the Kurstrozi Lumberjack title to serve Ossium's forest owners.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the accompanying story recalls an old Wintermark scholar, Topi, who moved his books to Gildenheim with the help of beavers.

Come together.o: Inspired by the completion of the City of Dreams, the dreamspeaker Bronwen of the Silver Falls proposed the Gardens of the Heart, a great work in Serenael that would boost Miaren's herb gardens and let the Imperial Apothecaries Guild direct new potion research. The cost could be cut sharply if great works in Reikos, Holberg, Ossium and Skarsind were redirected to help.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: A Holmauer Watchhouse could be built at the Gates of Holmauer Park for 10 white granite and 30 crowns. It would create the Holmauer Watchcaptain, who would receive 9 crystal mana a season, guard against threats from the cursed park and could redirect its funds.

Miaren/Serenael.t: The proposed Gardens of the Heart would be built here in Seren, the City of Dreams, drawing masters of the natural sciences to research new potions under the Apothecaries Guild.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: A Darkwoods Wagonhouse could be built at Kurstrozi's Lumbermill for 10 weirwood and 36 crowns. It would create the Kurstrozi Lumberjack, who would receive 11 crowns a season and could redirect the mill's bounty.

Reikos/Chalcis Mount.t: Mentioned in passing: some survivors of Thornsong House stayed on Chalcis Mount after fleeing to Reikos.

Skarsind/Gildermark.t: A House of the Lost, a school of field medicine at the Red Blade Memorial, could be built for 10 weirwood and 30 crowns. It would create Rhyv's Blade, who would receive weltsilver, ambergelt and beggar's lye each season and could redirect the memorial's bounty.

Holberg.t: The Gates of Holmauer Park could be redirected for a year to cover the white granite needed, and a sinecure could be commissioned there to oversee the park's safety and funds.

Miaren.t: The Gardens of the Heart would raise the investment in Miaren's herb gardens, giving each two extra true vervain and one extra cerulean mazzarine a season, and would make Seren a centre for potion research.

Ossium.t: Krustrozi's Lumbermill could be redirected for a year to supply tools and materials for the Gardens, and the territory was offered a sinecure to support its forest owners.

Reikos.t: Many Thornsong House survivors fled here. The Gardens of High Chalcis could be redirected for a year to cut the weirwood needed for the Gardens of the Heart by 50 wains.

Skarsind.t: The Red Blade Memorial could be redirected for a year so its bonesetters' contributions remove the need for mithril, and the territory was offered a sinecure to support Unshackled field medicine.

Therunin.t: Thornsong House, the Navarr herbmastery college here, was burned when the territory fell to the Druj, and the proposal seeks to restore what was lost.

Comes a time.d: Corey Wayfarer's greater-majority judgement urged a third Navarr army to fight the vallorn. The eternal Arhallogen offered to train it at a hall in Brocéliande, in exchange for Conclave amity or a precise declaration of concord, giving it the Silent Hunters quality. Critics instead proposed a costlier Thornbound army trained through Navarr herb lore and Spring magic. Enis's judgement on Seren inspired three mutually exclusive proposals: the Gardens of the Heart, the Temple of Waking Dream and the great library Isaella's Legacy. The Navarr raised Isaella's Dance with the Thornbound quality. The redesigned temple was completed in Autumn 388YE, creating the dreamspeaker archetype and a new title.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Bastion is named among the Empire's cities, Highborn cathedrals are a yardstick for the temple, and the Highborn's destruction of Llofir's fortress in Reikos is cited as a reason for Conclave caution.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Gildenheim in Skarsind is named among the recognised cities of the Empire.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the weakening of the vallorn in Liathaven, which the Jotun now hold, is cited as a sign that the vallorn can be beaten.

Navarr.t: The nation faced a choice between accepting Arhallogen's help or training its own vallorn-fighting army, and between three wonders for Seren. It raised the Thornbound army Isaella's Dance and later built the Temple of Waking Dream, which gave rise to the dreamspeaker archetype.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Siroc is named among the Empire's recognised cities.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Meade is held up as the city Seren equals, and Marcher monetary wealth is contrasted with the Navarr's.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim is named among the Empire's cities, the scop Topi appears in the opening tale, and the Wintermark Fight with honour order would affect both new army orders.

Comes a time.o: After the Navarr Assembly called for a new army to strike at the vallorn and the General Assembly recognised Seren as a city equal to those of other nations, two sets of opportunities opened: raising a vallorn-fighting army, with or without Arhallogen's aid, and three rival great commissions to raise Seren's standing. The Navarr later raised the Thornbound army Isaella's Dance and built the redesigned Temple of Waking Dream.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Boar's Dell was named as a likely site for Arhallogen's proposed training hall for the new Navarr army.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Elerael was named as a likely site for Arhallogen's proposed training hall for the new Navarr army.

Miaren/Serenael.t: Serenael was the site of the redesigned Temple of Waking Dream, completed in Autumn 388YE, which established the dreamspeaker archetype and a new Navarr title.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Bastion is named as one of the cities people think of before Seren.

Brocéliande.t: Arhallogen offered to raise a training hall for the new Navarr army around a regio in Brocéliande, needing no materials or Senate commission, if the Conclave approved. Some hope the territory's vallorn might be weakened if it can be withstood long enough.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim is listed among the Empire's recognised cities.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Library of Hacynian is cited as an example of Navarr scholarship.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: the weakening of Liathaven's vallorn is cited as encouragement for a dedicated vallorn-fighting army.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Siroc is named among the Empire's recognised cities.

Miaren.t: Seren in Miaren became the focus of three proposed great commissions meant to make it the Garden City, the City of Dreams or the City of Leaves. The Temple of Waking Dream was built, and every congregation in Miaren now receives an extra dose of liao and Goosewhisper Infusion each season.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Meade is named as the city Seren is said to equal.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn's forced destruction of Llofir's fortress in Reikos is cited as a reason the Conclave might refuse an eternal's commission.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Gildenheim is named among the Empire's cities and as the place where the scop Topi carried his books.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: it is one of the Navarr territories through which the Assembly's judgements were spread.

Coming home.d: The civil service could find no military purpose for the conjunction, which opened near the bridge of Guthwulf of the Red Embrace. Kallavesi mystics said it was meant for a pilgrimage to the marsh's dead, last seen in Emperor Guntherm's reign. Only one nation could pass through. The Masi prepared to receive the host, and stormcrows were asked to choose three recent fallen heroes and three speakers. Consecrating the marsh grove to Pride with true liao would raise Wintermark's ability to support armies to four, honouring Inga Tarn and Isenbrad. Gunnbrand's mandate was enacted, so Wintermark armies fighting the Jotun gain victory but inflict fewer casualties, and the Fist of the Mountains and Green Shield may each update their army's quality once.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Emperor Guntherm's body lies in state in Bastion rather than in the marsh, which some Wintermark folk quietly resent.

Jotun.t: Wintermark's enacted mandate means its armies will now fight the Jotun as honourable equals, gaining more victory but inflicting a fifth fewer casualties. The change will be visible to everyone in any territory where such a campaign is fought.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mourne is cited as the point when relations between Wintermark and the Jotun took a darker turn.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: in Guntherm's reign, Wintermark and Jotun warriors briefly joined forces to fight the Thule.

Wintermark.t: The whole nation was offered a pilgrimage to inter and honour its dead in the Kallavesa Marsh, with the chance to win permanent extra army capacity by consecrating the grove to Pride with true liao. Its Assembly's heroism mandate was enacted, permanently changing how its armies fight the Jotun and giving two of its generals a chance to update their armies.

Coming home.o: A major conjunction opened into the heart of the Kallavesa Marsh, letting the whole Wintermark nation make a rare pilgrimage to honour and inter its heroic dead. The Wintermark Assembly also sent Gunnbrand Ironwill with 50 doses of liao to make its call to fight the Jotun as heroes permanent.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: The marsh, resting place of Empress Britta, Inga Tarn and Isenbrad, was the pilgrimage destination. A Pride consecration of its central grove with true liao would be guarded by the Masi and lost only if an enemy conquered and despoiled the region.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun armies in Stark are too far away to explain the conjunction.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Emperor Guntherm's body lies in state here, not in the Kallavesa swamp.

Kallavesa.t: The conjunction opened into the heart of Kallavesa's great swamp, where the Masi readied a traditional welcome and song for the Wintermark pilgrims and any fallen heroes brought to be interred.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mourne is named as the turning point after which Wintermark's battles with the Jotun grew more threatening.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun armies in Stark are noted to be far from the conjunction's destination, ruling out a military purpose.

Commission report on Morrow evacuation.d: Proposed by the senator for Morrow and seconded by the senator for Spiral, this Autumn 382YE motion asked the Imperial Civil Service to investigate whether evacuating the civilian population of Morrow was feasible and, if so, to set out how it could be done. The motion passed. The Civil Service was expected to present its findings at the Winter Solstice 382YE. The motion itself commissioned only a report; it did not order or begin any evacuation.

Urizen.t: Urizen's senator for Morrow proposed the motion, seeking a civil service study into how the nation's civilians in that territory might be evacuated.

Commission report on Morrow evacuation.o: The Senate passed a motion directing the civil service to determine possible routes for evacuating civilians from Morrow, and to present proposals on how this might be achieved if feasible.

Morrow.t: Morrow's civilians were the subject of the commissioned study, with the civil service tasked to find possible evacuation routes and report back at the Winter Solstice 382YE.

Concede territory of Segura to Lasambria.d: The motion, proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Feroz, called for the Empire to concede the territory of Segura to the four tribes of the Lasambrian Jotun. It was put before the Senate in Spring 383YE and failed, so no concession of Segura was made. The page records no further details of the debate or the reasons for the motion's defeat.

Jotun.t: The four tribes of the Lasambrian Jotun would have received Segura had the motion passed, but its failure meant the Empire made no concession of the territory to them.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast faced a proposal to give up one of its territories, Segura, to the Lasambrian Jotun, but the motion's failure left the Empire's claim to it unconceded.

Concede territory of Segura to Lasambria.o: In Spring 383YE a Senate motion proposed conceding the Brass Coast territory of Segura to the four tribes of the Lasambrian Jotun; the motion failed.

Segura.t: Segura was the subject of a proposed concession to the Lasambrian Jotun, which the Senate did not pass.

Concord and accord.d: Four candidates stood in the latest Throne election (Bohemond De Rondell, Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza, Sir Claude Vyse Videre and Veikko Bondforger), but none won the required two-thirds. Æsa Sigeling's declaration met near-universal agreement. Magicians will now assume a Throne lacks Conclave support unless it has been explicitly given beforehand. The Conclave can approve any number of candidates, prefer a single one, or denounce candidates, and declarations passed after an appointment have no effect. A minority urges the Conclave to step back, which would weaken political Concords and the Imperial Magus for a year. Others suggest magicians stand as candidates or lobby their senators instead.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: an Imperial magician wistfully compares his coven's evening to the wine-and-cake salons held in Holberg.

Concord and accord.o: On the second anniversary of Imperatrix Lisabetta's disappearance, with the Throne still unfilled, Imperial magicians broadly accepted the Imperial Magus's Spring Equinox Declaration of Concord that Throne candidates must engage with the Conclave.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's salons are held up in the fiction as the model of a refined evening of political discourse.

Conduit to destiny.d: A runeforge needed 60 wains of mithril, white granite and weirwood, 45 thrones and a year's work. Building it at Runegrott offered savings. If the Imperial Orcs returned the Gildenheim ruins in Skarsind and the Senate confirmed Wintermark's runesmiths as heirs, moving them would cost 12 thrones but save 30 wains of white granite and 60 crowns. Runesmiths enslaved by the Thule in 373YE might be ransomed. Hallowing Isenbrad's tomb with true liao would bring fifteen wains of weirwood. Recovering the lost Rime Hammer would see Runegrott fund the labour. Barien offered ice-walkers a Summer challenge. The Gildenheim ruins were moved to Runegrott in 383YE.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish weavers at work in Weirwater are cited as a famous example of Imperial magic.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Spiral Sword is named as the runeforge a new Wintermark forge would aim to rival.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sentinel's Tomb in Casinea is cited as a precedent for an inspirational tomb having effects across the Empire.

Imperial Orcs.t: As owners of Skarsind, the Imperial Orcs held the Gildenheim runeforge ruins and could return them to Wintermark, having already refused significant Thule offers to buy them.

Thule.t: The Thule were believed to still hold the runesmiths and artisans enslaved at Gildenheim in 373YE, and had said they would return them only if paid what they were worth.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark was given a path to rebuild its runesmithing tradition with a new runeforge at Runegrott, possibly paired with a Runesmith title advising the Thane's Council, and the Gildenheim ruins were moved there to cut the cost.

Conduit to destiny.o: Wintermark was offered the chance to build a new runeforge at the Runegrott beneath Northspires to reclaim its lost prestige in crafting magic items, with several ways to reduce the enormous cost. By the resolution, the ruins of the Gildenheim runeforge had been dismantled and moved to Runegrott, allowing a new forge to be built there at a significant discount.

Hahnmark/Northspires.t: The Runegrott ice caves beneath Northspires, guarded by runesmiths and the Eyes of the North, became the destination of the Gildenheim ruins and the proposed home of a new runeforge and a tomb to Isenbrad.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the creation of the Sentinel's Tomb here is cited as the model for the wider inspiration an Isenbrad tomb might bring.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark's Runegrott was proposed as the site of a new runeforge, a possible hallowed tomb to Isenbrad, and the home of the lost Rime Hammer, and it received the dismantled Gildenheim runeforge in 383YE.

Otkodov.t: The runesmiths captured at Gildenheim were taken to Otkodov and are likely still kept as slaves serving its undying masters.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind held the ruins of the Gildenheim runeforge, conquered by the Thule in 373YE, which were dismantled and moved out of the territory to Runegrott in 383YE.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Spiral Sword runeforge is named as the forge a new Wintermark runeforge would rival.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish weavers of Weirwater are cited as an example of the Empire's renowned magic.

Construct A Fair Price.d: Announced by Groza, Legion Engineer, at the Winter Solstice 385YE, the commission cost 10 wains of weirwood, 30 crowns and standard costs, and took three months to build. Because the Legion Engineer could not amend a title to grant custodianship of a sinecure, the Senate voted at the Summer Solstice 386YE to amend the Champion of Prosperity title to include it. Funding came in instalments from Serenus Starsong, Rhys Nighthaven, Thiaga i Pérez i Riqueza, Tethros i Zuhri i Erigo and finally Bartimaeus, who supplied the remaining money and the weirwood after the Autumn Equinox 386YE. Once complete, the Champion of Prosperity was to receive 216 rings each season from the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Urizen.t: The new sinecure was built on Urizen land in Zenith, bringing a farm and a seasonal income to an Imperial title within the nation's territory.

Construct A Fair Price.o: The Legion Engineer Groza announced the commission of 'A Fair Price', a farm sinecure in Iteri, Zenith, intended to fund the Champion of Prosperity so they could pay deserving citizens for their work.

Zenith/Iteri.t: Iteri was chosen as the site of 'A Fair Price', a farm sinecure attached to the Champion of Prosperity and completed after funding finished in late 386YE.

Zenith.t: Zenith gained a new farm sinecure, 'A Fair Price', which yields 216 rings each season for the Champion of Prosperity from the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Construct Abbey of Reconciliation.d: Proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by Bastion, the motion created the Abbey of Reconciliation, overseen by the Abbess of Reconciliation. The Abbess is charged with supporting ex-slaves and refugees, bringing them into the Way, and giving them the opportunity to work and recover in the Empire. The title is elected by the Highborn National Assembly and revocable by the Highborn, General and Assembly of the Nine. Construction cost 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns in labour on top of standard costs, and took three months. Sister Rosa, Fintan Nighthaven and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov supplied the funds and weirwood. With the abbey complete, the first Abbess was to be appointed at the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

Highguard.t: Highguard gained a new national title, the Abbess of Reconciliation, elected by the Highborn National Assembly and charged with caring for ex-slaves and refugees and bringing them into the Way.

Construct Abbey of Reconciliation.o: In Summer 385YE the Senate passed a motion to construct the Abbey of Reconciliation in Necropolis, a sinecure producing 10 weirwood herbs and forming part of the Network of the Proffered Hand.

Necropolis.t: The Abbey of Reconciliation was built in Necropolis as a 10 weirwood sinecure, making the territory a centre for aiding ex-slaves and refugees within the Network of the Proffered Hand.

Construct Academy Religious Studies sine.d: Proposed by Casinea and seconded by the Conscience of the Senate, the motion created a sinecure, described as the "Custodian of the Academy Religious Studies", producing 18 liao each season for the Academy's use. It passed at a cost of 30 thrones. Construction required 10 wains of white granite, 2 thrones 4 crowns and three months; Zephram of Cantiarch's Hold supplied the materials and money after the Winter Solstice 378YE. On completion it creates the Imperial title of Dean of Pilgrims, a lifetime appointment open to any Imperial citizen and appointed by the Senate. It can be revoked by the General Assembly or the Assembly of the Nine.

Urizen.t: A Urizen territory hosts the new Academy sinecure, and the granite and coin to build it came from Zephram of Cantiarch's Hold.

Construct Academy Religious Studies sine.o: In Autumn 378YE the Senate approved the construction of a sinecure at Canterspire in Morrow to supply liao to the Academy, requested by the Academy Junior Council.

Morrow.t: The sinecure is built at Canterspire in Morrow and will produce 18 liao each season for the Academy.

Construct Adelaarskade.d: The Holberg College of Engineering was called upon to plan the dykes, which were costed at 30 wains of weirwood and 90 crowns in labour and would take three months to build. Once the land was suitable, the Rebeshof Roadwarden, Lia Adelaar van Holberg, was to fund pig markets in the Marches and encourage the Sand Fishers to farm Rebeshof and Utterlund as foreigners. Otmar van Holberg, members of the Kleist von Ennerlund family, Cees Van Holberg, Morlock and others contributed money and weirwood after the Autumn Equinox and Winter Solstice. On completion, the penalty to farms in Holberg would be removed, and a year later both regions would lose their marsh quality.

The League.t: League citizens, led by Otmar von Holberg and the Adelaar family, drove and largely funded a project to make Holberg's marshy land fit for farming.

Construct Adelaarskade.o: In Autumn 387YE the Chair of the Wolf announced the construction of Adelaarskade, a series of dykes in Holberg meant to drain the wetlands of Rebeshof and Utterlund, commissioned at the behest of Otmar von Holberg of Adelaarsgilde.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: Rebeshof's wetlands were to be drained by the dykes, losing their marsh quality a year after completion, with its Roadwarden pledged to encourage Sand Fishers to farm the land.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Utterlund's wetlands were also to be drained, losing their marsh quality a year after completion and becoming more appealing for farming, including by Sand Fishers.

Holberg.t: Completion of Adelaarskade would remove the penalty affecting farms across Holberg and reshape the landscape of two of its regions.

Construct Alchemical Workshop in Miaren.d: In Winter 380YE the Senate approved the construction of an alchemical workshop, a potion lab dedicated to Murit, in the Navarr territory of Miaren. The motion was proposed by Miaren and seconded by Hercynia, and it passed; the page records the cost as unknown. After the Winter Solstice 380YE, Llewellyn Leafstalker provided 5 wains of white granite and 10 crowns towards the work. The workshop was subsequently completed and stands in Holtford in Miaren.

Navarr.t: The Navarr territory of Miaren gained a completed alchemical workshop dedicated to Murit, built at the request of its own senator.

Construct Alchemical Workshop in Miaren.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Miaren and seconded by Hercynia, to build a potion laboratory in Miaren dedicated to Murit.

Miaren/Holtford.t: Holtford is the site of the completed alchemical workshop dedicated to Murit.

Miaren.t: Miaren's senator proposed the potion lab, and the workshop dedicated to Murit was duly built within the territory.

Construct Angelica Memorial House of Hea.d: The motion called for a self-funded sinecure in Riposi, a garden of tailored and peaceful grounds intended to heal the malign and mental maladies of war and to grow herbs for producing cerulean mazzarine, specifically for the use of the League national block. Its custodian is to hold the Imperial title of Mistress of Medicine, a tenured position appointed by the generals of the League. No costs were specified, so the civil service assumed the minimum size of 10 wains. Shauni di Vergo provided 2 thrones, 4 crowns and 10 wains of weirwood after the Summer Solstice 384YE. Once completed, the sinecure will create the title.

The League.t: The League gains a herb garden whose produce is reserved for its national block, together with a new title, the Mistress of Medicine, to be appointed by the League's generals.

Construct Angelica Memorial House of Hea.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by Skarsind, to commission a herb garden sinecure in Riposi called the Angelica Vergo di Sarvos Memorial House of Healing.

Sarvos/Riposi.t: Riposi is the site chosen for the sinecure's healing gardens. These will grow herbs for cerulean mazzarine and tend to those suffering the maladies of war.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos is to host the memorial house of healing, which honours Angelica Vergo di Sarvos and was proposed by the territory's own senator.

Construct Anvil Library Scriptorium.d: Using the Second Imperial Wayleave, Claus Friedrich von Holberg announced a sinecure costing 12 wains of white granite and three thrones in labour, taking three months to build. The Scriptorium will provide liao and votes in the Imperial Synod. It and the sodality of the Anvil Library will be governed by the Armarius of the Anvil Library, an Imperial title appointed and revoked by the Wisdom Assembly, with tenure until death, resignation or revocation. Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided the three thrones and twelve wains of white granite after the Spring Equinox 385YE. Once complete, the Wisdom Assembly may appoint the Armarius.

The League.t: The League gains a new Imperial sinecure in one of its cities, Rodez in Sarvos, whose holder will control liao and Synod votes tied to the Anvil Library.

Construct Anvil Library Scriptorium.o: The Bearer of the Second Imperial Wayleave, Claus Friedrich von Holberg, announced the construction of the Anvil Library Scriptorium, a self-funded sinecure in Rodez, Foracci, Sarvos, providing liao and Synod votes.

Sarvos/Foracci.t: The Scriptorium is to be constructed in Rodez in Foracci, taking three months to complete before the Armarius can be appointed.

Sarvos.t: The Anvil Library Scriptorium is to be built in Sarvos, funded after the Spring Equinox by Giacomo Corvinoscuro's donation of money and white granite.

Construct Apstrus Dam.d: Firesong Arachas, the Legion Engineer, commissioned the dam described in the Million miles of water and Damming the Doubt winds of fortune. The work required 30 wains of white granite and the labour of an Imperial army. It also cost 5 thrones to carve the names of the dead into the stones and 5 thrones to relocate the books of Solen's Doubt. The Towerjacks supported the motion after the Winter Solstice. Bloodcrow Rasp supplied the granite, and Raine Tealeaf, Halkyon of the Myriad Stream, Callista and Rhys Nighthaven contributed money. Once complete, the dam made Icarion an oasis and raised the territory's taxation by 6 thrones a season.
