Grendel.t: Grendel held Mareave during this season, so it was among the holders of the territory whose region of Icarion received the dam's diverted water.

Imperial Orcs.t: For the Imperial Orcs, who held Mareave, the dam turned Icarion into an oasis and increased the taxation the territory produces by 6 thrones a season.

The League.t: The dam was built on League-held land in Apstrus, Spiral, and the books of Solen's Doubt had to be relocated as part of the work.

Construct Apstrus Dam.o: In Winter 387YE the Legion Engineer, Firesong Arachas, announced the construction of a dam in Apstrus, Spiral, to divert water into Icarion in Mareave. The motion was self-funded and later completed, turning Icarion into an oasis.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Water redirected from Apstrus transformed Icarion into an oasis.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: The dam was raised in Apstrus by the labour of an Imperial army, and the books of Solen's Doubt were moved to make way for it.

Mareave.t: Mareave received the diverted water in Icarion, which became an oasis, and the territory's taxation rose by 6 thrones a season.

Spiral.t: Spiral became the site of the new dam in Apstrus, built from 30 wains of white granite with the names of the dead carved into its stones.

Construct Arbor of the Twin Roses.d: Proposed by Weirwater and seconded by Reikos, the self-funded motion commissioned a sinecure as described in the Draw strength from vulnerability Wind of Fortune. It created the Voice of the Twin Roses, elected annually by the Dawnish National Assembly and revocable by it. Non-standard costs applied: 8 wains of white granite, 8 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns in labour, with three months to construct. After the Winter Solstice, Claude Deeds provided 4 thrones along with the weirwood and white granite. Once completed, the Dawnish National Assembly will be able to appoint the Voice of the Twin Roses.

Dawn.t: Dawn gains a monument to its exemplar Elayne Silverlark and a new title, the Voice of the Twin Roses, which its National Assembly will elect annually and may revoke once the Arbor is complete.

Construct Arbor of the Twin Roses.o: In Winter 383YE the Senate passed a motion to commission the Arbor of the Twin Roses, a sinecure in Ferrond, Semmerholm, honouring the exemplar Elayne Silverlark and creating the position of the Voice of the Twin Roses.

Semmerholm/Ferrond.t: Ferrond is the site of the new sinecure honouring Elayne Silverlark, built from white granite and weirwood.

Semmerholm.t: The Arbor of the Twin Roses is to be built in Semmerholm, with materials supplied by Claude Deeds after the Winter Solstice and three months needed to construct it.

Construct Archives of the Advisor.d: Proposed by Merari Navigators of Virtue, Senator for the Bastion, and seconded by Pathfinder Gaddak, Senator for Mareave, the motion commissioned a sinecure in Solvihill and amended the title of Advisor on Orc Affairs to hold it. The construction required standard costs, 10 wains of white granite and 30 crowns in labour, and took three months. After the Summer Solstice Frith provided 3 thrones 6 crowns and the 10 wains of white granite. With the Archives complete, the Advisor on Orc Affairs receives 12 measures of iridescent gloaming each season, starting at the Winter Solstice 388YE.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs' homeland of Skarsind gained a new sinecure, and the Advisor on Orc Affairs, the title tied to their affairs, now draws 12 measures of iridescent gloaming each season.

Construct Archives of the Advisor.o: The Senate passed a motion in Summer 388YE to commission the Archives of the Advisor in Solvihill, Skarsind, a sinecure producing 12 measures of iridescent gloaming each season, attached to the existing title of Advisor on Orc Affairs.

Skarsind/Solvihill.t: The Archives of the Advisor were built in Solvihill using white granite and labour paid for by Frith, and were completed in time to yield gloaming from the Winter Solstice 388YE.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind, held by the Imperial Orcs, became home to the Archives of the Advisor, a newly completed sinecure.

Construct Arsenal in Sarvos.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by the senator for Kahraman, sought Senate approval to build a Great Work in Sarvos. It was believed to relate to the opportunity to build the Sarvos Dockyard and Arsenal. The proposed construction would have enriched the port fleets by 900 rings, shared equally among them, and would have given the League the possibility of raising a Navy in future. The work was to be self-funded rather than paid for from the Imperial treasury. The Senate did not pass the motion, so the arsenal was not commissioned that season.

The League.t: The League lost, for now, a self-funded route to enriching its port fleets and to the possibility of raising a League Navy, after a motion backed by its own senators for Sarvos and Kahraman failed.

Construct Arsenal in Sarvos.o: In Winter 381YE the senator for Sarvos proposed a self-funded Great Work, an arsenal in Sarvos, to enrich the port fleets and give the League the option of raising a navy. The motion failed.

Sarvos.t: The proposed dockyard and arsenal in Sarvos was not approved, so the territory's ports did not gain the Great Work or the promised enrichment of its fleets.

Construct Art Museum of Tassato.d: The motion authorised a great work in Tassato at a cost of 15 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones in labour, taking three months to construct. After the Spring Equinox 381YE Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar provided all the required materials and money. The completed great work, the Blood Red River Museum, provides 15 liao and 30 votes in the Imperial Synod each season. These are spread among citizens of Tassato dedicated to Pride who own congregations, following attendance at the Anvil Summit.

The League.t: The League gained a great work in one of its cities, the Blood Red River Museum, which strengthens Pride-dedicated League congregations with additional liao and Synod votes.

Construct Art Museum of Tassato.o: In Spring 381YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Tassato's senator and seconded by Astolat's, to build a great work in Tassato dedicated to the virtue of Pride, taking advantage of a recent surge of inspiration in Pride and the arts.

Tassato.t: Tassato became home to the Blood Red River Museum, funded by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar, which each season gives its Pride-dedicated congregation owners 15 liao and 30 Synod votes between them.

Construct Asavean Embassy.d: The motion passed in principle by 22 votes to 2 and at 35 Thrones by 18 to 6, but failed at 40 Thrones. The commission carried an unusual cost of 20 white granite and 20 weirwood, which Mirislav, Senator for Sarvos, supplied after the Spring Equinox 378YE. An amendment proposed by Miaren and seconded by Weirwater disbursed a further 5 Thrones to Senator Miaren to buy white granite. The completed embassy became a ministry, allowing its appointed citizen to purchase Cerulean Mazzarine, Orichalcum, Iridescent Gloaming, Tempest Jade and True Vervain. The title of ambassador to the Asavean Archipelago was created automatically.

The League.t: The League gained a formal embassy to the Asavean Archipelago in one of its cities, along with a ministry trading in rare Asavean materials. Sarvos's own senator, Mirislav, supplied the stone and timber needed to build it.

Construct Asavean Embassy.o: In Winter 377YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by Temeschwar, to construct an embassy to the Asavean Archipelago in Sarvos, approving it at 35 Thrones.

Sarvos.t: The Asavean embassy was built in Sarvos, making the city the site of the Empire's diplomatic and trading link with the Archipelago. Its senator, Mirislav, proposed the motion and provided the 20 wains of white granite and weirwood.

Construct Asavean Temple.d: Proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Madruga, the motion passed and the Asaveans began building the temple in the port-town of Oran on Feroz's northern coast, with six months expected for construction. When complete, the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull will create a non-Imperial title responsible for liaising with its priests. The Asaveans said they would be guided in that appointment by the Senator for Feroz. The Imperial Synod cannot revoke the title, though the priesthood may refuse to deal with a liaison. Completion was first expected before the Autumn Equinox 380YE, but significant delays fostered by Synod interference pushed it back to shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE.

The Brass Coast.t: A Brass Coast territory became host to a foreign major temple, and the Senator for Feroz was given the say over who would serve as the temple's liaison.

Construct Asavean Temple.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate passed a motion granting Asavea permission to build a major temple to their gods in Feroz, on the understanding that it would be used only by non-Imperial citizens.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The Asaveans began building the temple in Oran, the bustling port-town on Feroz's northern coast, though Synod-fostered delays put its completion back to shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE.

Feroz.t: Feroz is the site of the Asavean Temple of Balo and the Black Bull, and its Senator will guide the Asaveans in appointing the temple's liaison.

Construct Ashen Tears Wayhouse.d: Firesong Arachas, the Legion Engineer, announced the construction of a wayhouse named the Ashen Tears in Skogei, Skarsind. The commission called for 16 wains of white granite and 6 thrones (listed among the costs as 16 white granite and 48 crowns), with three months to complete. After the Summer Solstice 387YE, "Grim" Grimmeth Ashen-Tear provided the full 6 thrones and 16 wains of white granite. The wayhouse is now complete, and the title of Keeper of the Ashen Tears becomes available to be appointed by unanimous vote of the senators of Navarr, for the first time at the Autumn Equinox 387YE.

Imperial Orcs.t: A new wayhouse stands within the Imperial Orc territory of Skarsind, announced by the Legion Engineer and funded by Grimmeth Ashen-Tear, though its keeper is chosen by Navarr rather than by the orcs' own senators.

Navarr.t: The Navarr senators gain the right to appoint the Keeper of the Ashen Tears by unanimous vote, first at the Autumn Equinox 387YE, giving Navarr a role at a wayhouse in Skarsind.

Construct Ashen Tears Wayhouse.o: In Summer 387YE a Senate motion commissioned the Ashen Tears wayhouse in Skogei Glens, Skarsind, and it was completed, with its keeper to be appointed by the senators of Navarr.

Skarsind/Skogei Glens.t: Skogei Glens is the site of the newly completed Ashen Tears wayhouse, whose keeper will be named by the senators of Navarr.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind gains the completed Ashen Tears wayhouse, built in Skogei with 16 wains of white granite and 6 thrones.

Construct Atalaq Tradehall.d: Fedelmidd Sydanjaa's Heart Floer, Senator for Sermersuaq, proposed the motion and Mel Bleak, Senator for Mournwold, seconded it. The tradehall had recently resurfaced during an appraisal of non-coin trades that ministries could make, which strayed into past opportunities to bring more money into the Anvil economy. The motion passed. After the Autumn Equinox, Jambert Wulfgar provided the 50 wains of weirwood with 4 thrones 2 crowns, and Kanute Adelaar van Holberg gave 14 thrones. Four others each added a crown. Once complete, the tradehall would raise business investment and taxation in Sermersuaq, add 7 crowns to the Custodian of the Bloody Great Sausage's income, and give Wintermark fleets extra income when trading abroad.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark fleet owners stood to earn an extra 36 rings for a year whenever they traded with foreign nations, and Wintermark's senator for Sermersuaq led the motion.

Construct Atalaq Tradehall.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 388YE, proposed by Sermersuaq's senator, to build the Atalaq Tradehall, a great work in Sealtoq meant to boost business investment in Sermersuaq. It required 50 wains of weirwood and 150 crowns and was seeking funds.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Sealtoq was chosen as the site of the Atalaq Tradehall, a great work taking three months to build once the weirwood and labour costs were met.

Sermersuaq.t: Once built, the tradehall would increase business investment in Sermersuaq by one and raise the territory's taxation by 4 thrones.

Construct Atalaya Harbour.d: Proposed by Segura and seconded by Kahraman, the motion built the harbour described in the wind of fortune The power behind our moves, at a cost of 10 wains of weirwood, 20 wains of white granite and 60 crowns in labour, with upkeep of 5 thrones a season. Gancio di Catazar supplied the money and materials after the Winter Solstice. Once complete, any Freeborn fleet based in Madruga can be upgraded each season for one less weirwood. The Grendel cannot legitimately claim it breaches the existing treaty, though they recognise the threat. The docks could later be expanded cheaply into a full shipyard. The discount lasts only while the new arrivals stay in Madruga, and many would likely go home if Feroz is reclaimed.

Grendel.t: The Grendel cannot legitimately claim the new docks breach the existing treaty, but they are aware of the threat the harbour poses as a possible future shipyard.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn fleets based in Madruga gain cheaper upgrades from the harbour, which relies on shipwrights among the new arrivals, many of whom would return home once the Brass Coast reclaims Feroz.

Construct Atalaya Harbour.o: In Winter 384YE the Senate passed a motion to rebuild Atalaya Harbour in Madruga, letting Freeborn fleets based there be upgraded more cheaply without the harbour counting as a shipyard.

Feroz.t: Feroz, held by the Grendel, is home to many of the new arrivals now working in Madruga, and its reclamation by the Brass Coast would draw them home and end the harbour's upgrade discount.

Madruga.t: Atalaya Harbour is rebuilt in Madruga, letting fleets based there upgrade for one less weirwood each season, with the option of later expanding it into a full shipyard.

Construct Aurelie's Garden.d: Proposed by the senator for Weirwater and seconded by the senator for Sarvos, the motion created a self-funded herb garden sinecure near the hospital Aurelie's Rest in Grovesyard, Miaren. Its holder is to be decided by an annual contest of ten Dawnish against ten Navarr, using all skills until one team remains standing, with any further rules agreed between the teams. The motion passed. Construction was underway, with 10 weirwood and 20 crowns spent by Nym after the Spring Equinox. When complete it will create the Imperial title Keeper of Aurelie's Garden. The size of the sinecure, the term of the title and which Synod assemblies may revoke it were left for the senator to decide.

Dawn.t: Dawnish champions will field a team of ten in an annual contest against the Navarr to win control of the new herb garden sinecure.

Navarr.t: The Navarr gain a herb garden within their own territory of Miaren, but must defend control of it each year in a ten-against-ten contest with Dawn.

Construct Aurelie's Garden.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate passed a motion to build Aurelie's Garden, a herb-producing sinecure in Grovesyard, Miaren, beside the hospital Aurelie's Rest, to be contested each year between Dawn and Navarr.

Miaren.t: A herb garden sinecure was ordered to be built in Grovesyard, beside the hospital Aurelie's Rest, and construction had begun with materials and funds committed.

Construct Autumn's Boon.d: Proposed by Kallavesa and seconded by Casinea, the motion commissions a mana sinecure named Autumn's Boon, to be built in Wood Heath in Hahnmark at standard cost. Its holder, the Collector of Prosperity's Boon, is to be selected by the Senators of Wintermark. The motion passed in principle but left the size of the sinecure unspecified, a necessary detail for the senator to determine. After the Summer Solstice 382YE, Tyr Brennan provided 12 wains of mithril and 24 crowns towards construction. Once complete, the sinecure will create the Imperial title.

Wintermark.t: The Senators of Wintermark are to select the Collector of Prosperity's Boon, giving the nation control of a new mana sinecure on its own land in Hahnmark.

Construct Autumn's Boon.o: In Summer 382YE the Senate passed in principle a motion to construct a mana sinecure called Autumn's Boon in Wood Heath, Hahnmark, creating the Imperial title Collector of Prosperity's Boon.

Hahnmark/Wood Heath.t: Wood Heath is the chosen site for the Autumn's Boon sinecure, which on completion will create the title of Collector of Prosperity's Boon.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark is to gain a mana sinecure, Autumn's Boon, towards which Tyr Brennan supplied 12 wains of mithril and 24 crowns after the Summer Solstice.

Construct Axos Embassy.d: Proposed by Zenith and seconded by Sarvos, the self-funded motion called for an Embassy to Axos in Redoubt. It required 25 wains of weirwood, 25 wains of white granite and 12 thrones in labour, with three months to build and an upkeep of 5 thrones per season from the Senate's budget. After the Summer Solstice, Tanwyn Ankarien supplied all the materials and labour, and construction began in Limus, Cargo, Redoubt, near the Jarmish embassy. Once complete, the embassy will create a new Imperial title, Ambassador to Axos, appointed by the Senate.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Senate seats proposed and seconded the motion through Zenith and Sarvos. The Empire's new diplomatic link with Axos is being built on Urizeni soil in Redoubt.

Construct Axos Embassy.o: In Summer 380YE the Senate passed a motion to build an embassy to Axos in Redoubt, with the ambassador to be appointed by the Senate. Construction began in Limus after the materials and labour were privately supplied.

Redoubt/Limus.t: Construction of the Axos embassy began in Cargo, Limus, near the existing Jarmish embassy, after Tanwyn Ankarien supplied the materials and labour.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt will host the Empire's embassy to Axos once the three months of building are finished, adding to the diplomatic presence already there near the Jarmish embassy.

Construct Bakers' Bowl.d: The commission, announced in Autumn 388YE, required 20 wains of weirwood and 60 crowns in labour and took three months to build. Lula and Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund each provided 10 wains of weirwood and 2 thrones. Morlock and several Holbergers, along with Emilio Marsana Saverio di Sarvos, contributed further coin. Once complete, the Senators of the League can appoint the Sponsor of the Holberg Hammers, a lifetime position with an income of at least 216 rings per season, responsible for the well-being of the stadium and the team. The position is revocable by the Assembly of Nine, the General Assembly and the League National Assembly. Calcio and Foot-the-Ball teams from towns without their own stadiums were invited to train and play fixtures there.

The League.t: The League gains a new lifetime national sinecure, the Sponsor of the Holberg Hammers, appointed by League Senators, along with a stadium for its calcio and foot-the-ball teams.

Construct Bakers' Bowl.o: Lula Kleist von Ennerlund announced, under an Imperial Wayleave, the commissioning of the Bakers' Bowl, a stadium in Holmauer, Holberg, as a sinecure creating the League national position of Sponsor of the Holberg Hammers.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: The Bakers' Bowl stadium was to be built in Holmauer, where teams from towns without their own stadiums were invited to train and play fixtures.

Holberg.t: Holberg was to host the Bakers' Bowl stadium and its team, the Holberg Hammers, with several Holbergers contributing coin to the construction.

Construct Barossa University of Dramatur.d: The university would act as a college of magic with the unique power to codify rituals itself or to work with the Doyen of Spires to achieve unprecedented codification. It also creates the League title of Reapers Gift, appointed by auction, responsible for promoting dramaturgy, overseeing the university and facilitating collaboration between Urizen and League magicians. Construction requires 70 white granite, 60 weirwood, 70 mithril and 75 thrones in labour, takes 12 months and carries 12 thrones upkeep. Many citizens donated materials and money between Summer 387YE and Autumn 388YE. The project stemmed from the wind of fortune The play that came to Apulian.

The League.t: The League would gain a new college of magic in Apulian and a new national title, the Reapers Gift, appointed by auction to oversee the university and promote dramaturgy; League citizens supplied much of the material and coin.

Urizen.t: The university is meant to foster collaboration between Urizen and League magicians and may work with the Urizen Doyen of Spires to achieve unprecedented ritual codification.

Construct Barossa University of Dramatur.o: In Summer 387YE the Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, announced a Senate motion to construct the Barossa University of Dramaturgical Arts, a college of magic in Apulian dedicated to the study of dramaturgy.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Apulus is the site of the planned university in Apulian, with donated weirwood, white granite, mithril and coin flowing in towards its construction.

Spiral.t: Spiral is to host the new Barossa University of Dramaturgical Arts in the city of Apulian, adding a college of magic to the territory.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the motion was announced by the Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, who bears the territory's name.

Construct Barrens Spy Network.d: The motion to create a spy network in The Barrens passed in principle by 23 votes to 2. The commission cost 10 wains of weirwood, took three months to build, and carried an upkeep of 2 thrones per season from the Senate budget. Hector de Rondell provided the 10 wains of weirwood after the Spring Equinox 378YE, and the network was completed, giving the Empire a means of gathering intelligence in the Druj-held territory. It survived for several years before the Druj destroyed it following the Summer Solstice 382YE.

Druj.t: The Empire planted a spy network in Druj-held lands to watch their movements, and the Druj eventually found it and destroyed it after the Summer Solstice 382YE.

Construct Barrens Spy Network.o: In Spring 378YE the Senate approved the construction of a spy network in The Barrens, proposed by the Volodmartz senator and seconded by the Skarsind senator; it was later destroyed by the Druj after the Summer Solstice 382YE.

The Barrens.t: An Imperial spy network was built in The Barrens while the Druj held it, and it operated there until the Druj destroyed it following the Summer Solstice 382YE.

Construct Basilica of the Seven Doors.d: Proposed by the senator for Casinea and seconded by the senator for Bastion, the motion commissioned the restoration of the Basilica of the Seven Doors as a sinecure. The project used non-standard costs: 15 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns in labour, taking three months to complete. Thanks to the Custodes Clavium it needed no civil service commission slot and was entirely self-funded. Bartimaeus supplied the granite and weirwood after the Spring Equinox, and the Custodes Clavium met the labour costs. The restoration re-created the title Speaker of the Highborn Assembly, granting a congregation to its holder, who is appointed by the Highborn National Assembly at the Winter Solstice.

Highguard.t: Highguard gained a restored Basilica of the Seven Doors and a new national title, the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly, chosen by the Highborn National Assembly at the Winter Solstice and holding a congregation; the work was funded by the Custodes Clavium and the Benefactors of Highguard.

Construct Basilica of the Seven Doors.o: The Senate passed a motion in Spring 383YE to restore the Basilica of the Seven Doors in Bastion with the aid of the Custodes Clavium, re-creating the title of Speaker of the Highborn Assembly as a sinecure.

Bastion.t: The Basilica of the Seven Doors was restored in Bastion, with Bastion's senator seconding the motion and the construction taking three months to complete.

Construct Beacon of Sermersuaq.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by Madruga, the motion commissioned the last of the Beacons of Wintermark. It invoked a boon granted by Cathan Canae in recognition of Wintermark's resilience against two armies of Oblivion. The work cost 30 wains of white granite, 25 wains of weirwood and 165 crowns in labour, and took six months. Garth supplied nearly all the materials, while Otmar van Holberg, Fedelmidd Sydanjaa's Heart Floer and several others contributed money. Once completed, military units could guard the beacons, and Cathan Canae undertook to send the ritual text of Drums of the Iron Harpoon to the General of the Narwhal's Spear at the Summer Solstice 388YE.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark completed the final set of its Beacons, with the work commissioned in recognition of its resilience against two armies of Oblivion. The General of the Narwhal's Spear was to receive the ritual text of Drums of the Iron Harpoon from Cathan Canae.

Construct Beacon of Sermersuaq.o: The Senate passed a motion in Winter 387YE to construct the Beacons of Sermersuaq in Sealtoq, completing the final set of the Beacons of Wintermark and drawing on a boon from the eternal Cathan Canae.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: The beacons were raised in Sealtoq, built from white granite and weirwood over six months.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq gained the Beacons of Sermersuaq, which military units were able to guard once construction was complete.

Construct Bears Rest.d: The commission required ten wains of mithril and 30 crowns of labour on top of the standard costs, and would take three months to build. After the Summer Solstice 388YE, Bjorn provided the ten wains of mithril and 3 thrones 5 crowns, and Rhys Nighthaven gave a further crown. Once complete, the title of Steward of Bears Rest is to be appointed by unanimous decision of the Wintermark senators. The steward is responsible for collecting the mana carried down the river from the melting glacier upstream.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a new mana sinecure in its own lands, and its senators must agree unanimously on who holds the title of Steward of Bears Rest.

Construct Bears Rest.o: In Summer 388YE the Legion Engineer, Firesong Arachas, announced the construction of Bears Rest, a mana sinecure in Northspires, Hahnmark, whose steward collects mana flowing down the river from a melting glacier upstream.

Hahnmark/Northspires.t: Bears Rest was to be built in Northspires, where its steward would collect mana flowing down the river from the melting glacier upstream.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark is the site of the Bears Rest commission, a sinecure gathering mana from a glacier-fed river in the territory.

Construct Beneficiary of the Golden Casc.d: Proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by Zenith's, the motion built a sinecure arising from the Forwards and Rewards wind of fortune, at a cost of 8 weirwood, 8 white granite and 6 thrones, taking three months to complete. Abel the Rounder of Sarangrave Reforged provided the thrones and materials after the Spring Equinox. The title, appointed by the Urizen Assembly, requires its holder to use the proceeds to aid and reward other nations to build international friendship and cooperation. Each season the holder receives 20 random herbs, 3 elixir vitae, 3 ossean solutions, 3 philtres of heavenly lore and 10 crowns, while the Virtue Fund gains an additional 10 crowns.

Urizen.t: Urizen gained a new title whose holder, appointed by the Urizen Assembly, is charged with using its herbs, potions and crowns to aid and reward other nations and foster international friendship.

Construct Beneficiary of the Golden Casc.o: The Senate passed a motion in Spring 387YE to construct the Beneficiary of the Golden Cascade, a sinecure in Proceris, Zenith, which was completed and became available for appointment by the Urizen Assembly from the Summer Solstice 387YE.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Proceris became home to the Beneficiary of the Golden Cascade, built with weirwood and white granite supplied by Abel the Rounder of Sarangrave Reforged.

Zenith.t: The sinecure was built in Zenith, with Zenith's senator seconding the motion, and was complete in time for its first appointment at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

Construct Beoraidh Trading Post.d: The commission followed the A knock at the door Wind of Fortune and was described as fully funded. It cost 10 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns in labour, plus standard costs, and took three months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Sandviper Nid supplied 3 thrones, 5 crowns and the 10 wains of weirwood, and Farren Silver Streams gave 1 crown. Once finished, the Beoraidh Trading Post raised the income of the Shepherd of the Southern Herd by 10 crowns each season and that of the Shepherd of the Great Herd in Skarsind by 5 crowns each season. It also secured trade between the Unshackled and Beoraidh.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page; it is attached only because it held part of Mareave, where the trading post was built.

Imperial Orcs.t: The trading post, built in Icarion in Mareave and commissioned on the Mareave senator's proposal, increased the seasonal incomes of the Shepherd of the Southern Herd and the Shepherd of the Great Herd in Skarsind.

Construct Beoraidh Trading Post.o: In Spring 388YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Mareave and seconded by The Barrens, to build a trading post in Icarion, Mareave, so that salt could be traded for beef with Beoraidh. The trading post was later completed.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Beoraidh became the trading partner for the new post, supplying beef in exchange for salt, and its trade with the Unshackled was secured.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Icarion was chosen as the site of the Beoraidh Trading Post, which was built there with weirwood and crowns from Imperial donors.

Mareave.t: A new trading post was built in Mareave's Icarion region to exchange salt for beef with neighbouring Beoraidh, adding 10 crowns a season to the Shepherd of the Southern Herd's income.

Skarsind.t: The Shepherd of the Great Herd in Skarsind gained 5 extra crowns each season from the completed trading post.

Construct Black Canal.d: Proposed by Upwold's senator and seconded by Bastion's, the motion passed at no cost in thrones; the canal followed the Light upon the water Wind of Fortune. It required 60 wains of white granite, 40 wains of weirwood, 200 crowns and nine months, all met through many private donations from 384YE to 386YE. The Mournwold orcs supplied half the labour costs (100 crowns) through money, food and work, and grew more familiar to the northern Marches. The canal raised investment in Mitwold's farms and businesses and the Mournwold's businesses and mines. After the Jotun conquest of the Mourn in Summer 386YE, the Mournwold half gave no benefit and Mitwold's yield fell to 18 rings.

Jotun.t: The Jotun conquest of the Mourn after the Summer Solstice 386YE stripped away the Mournwold half of the canal's benefit and sharply cut the return to Mitwold.

The Marches.t: The Marches gained a canal joining its two most prosperous settlements, Meade and Sarcombe, funded by many Marcher donors and built alongside the Mournwold orcs, who became better known to the northern Marches.

Construct Black Canal.o: In Autumn 384YE the Senate commissioned the Black Canal, a great westward waterway named for Gerraint Black and linking Meade in Mitwold with Sarcombe in the Mournwold, built with the help of the Mournwold orcs.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: Chalkdowns must be reclaimed from the Jotun before the canal's Mitwold half can return to its full benefit.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Southmoor's recovery is, alongside Chalkdowns, a condition for the canal again yielding its full benefit.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold's farms and businesses gained greater investment from the canal starting at Meade, though after the Mourn's loss its half yields only 18 rings until Chalkdowns and Southmoor are reclaimed.

Mournwold.t: The canal reached Sarcombe and raised investment in the Mournwold's businesses and mines, with the local orcs paying half the labour, but the Jotun conquest left its Mournwold half providing no benefit.

Construct Black Obelisk.d: Proposed by Casinea and seconded by Zenith, the motion commissioned an edifice called "The Black Obelisk" in Stockmarch, Upwold, describing it as fully self-funded. It would commemorate the herald Obligatus and Geraint Black, a landskeeper, leader of the Unbound Union and Keeper of the Prosperity of Afal, in the wake of cultist activity in the territory. The construction required standard costs plus 10 wains of white granite and 30 crowns in labour, and would take three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice, Edgar Guildenstern provided the 10 wains of white granite and Ehud provided 3 thrones 6 crowns. The page records no outcome for the completed work.

The Marches.t: The Marches would gain a memorial in its own lands to the Marcher landskeeper Geraint Black, leader of the Unbound Union, and to the herald Obligatus, marking the losses caused by cultists in Upwold.

Construct Black Obelisk.o: In Winter 387YE the Senate passed a motion to build "The Black Obelisk" on the Guildenstern estate in Stockmarch, Upwold. It was to be a memorial to the herald Obligatus and the landskeeper Geraint Black after cultist activity in Upwold.

Upwold.t: The Black Obelisk was commissioned for the Guildenstern estate in Stockmarch, Upwold, in response to cultist activity there, and Edgar Guildenstern supplied the white granite for its construction.

Construct Blackfield Market.d: Proposed by the senator for Bregasland and seconded by the senator for Mitwold, the motion sought to disburse Senate funds to construct the Blackfield Market in Mitwold. It would have created the title of Blackfield Bailiff, appointed annually through the Imperial Bourse by a vote of the farm owners of the Marches, to oversee the market. The motion was framed as taking advantage of a recent proposal to construct a ministry for purchasing white granite. It failed, so the market was not commissioned and the Bailiff title was not created.

The Marches.t: Marcher senators for Bregasland and Mitwold put forward a market and a Bailiff title to be chosen by the nation's farm owners, but the motion failed and the Marches gained neither.

Construct Blackfield Market.o: A Senate motion in Autumn 383YE proposed spending Imperial funds to build the Blackfield Market in Mitwold, with a new Blackfield Bailiff title to oversee it, but the motion failed.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold was the proposed site of the Blackfield Market, but the motion to fund its construction failed, so nothing was built there.

Construct Blade of Thorn.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Miaren, the motion commissioned a great work in Old Ranging to produce mana. Its spiral is to include stones honouring those who gave their lives in defence of others, and it was framed as a gesture of goodwill from Achilles of Damokan's Forge to the Navarr and a reminder that the Empire stands united even in its darkest days. It cost 40 wains of mithril and 10 thrones in labour. Both sums were received from Rhisiart Dancewalker after the Spring Equinox 382YE. The great work does not create an Imperial title.

Navarr.t: The Navarr received a mana-producing great work in their territory of Hercynia, offered as a gesture of goodwill from Achilles of Damokan's Forge and paid for by Rhisiart Dancewalker.

Construct Blade of Thorn.o: In Spring 382YE the Senate passed a motion to commission Llafndrián, the Blade of Thorn, a self-funded great work in Old Ranging in Hercynia that produces mana for the owners of mana sites.

Hercynia/Old Ranging.t: Old Ranging is the site of the Blade of Thorn, whose spiral bears memorial stones to those who died defending others.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia's senator proposed the commission, and the territory gained Llafndrián, a great work that supplies mana to the owners of mana sites.

Construct Bladeroot Sinecure.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by the senator for Mitwold, the motion commissioned a sinecure for the production of bladeroot, to be built in Old Ranging. The motion called it self funded and did not define its costs, so the civil service assumed the minimum size of 10 wains, with standard costs applying. After the Summer Solstice 384YE, Radic Splinterovich Schaslyvyy provided 2 thrones, 4 crowns and 10 wains of weirwood. Once completed, the sinecure will create the Imperial title of Steward of the Nabarr, appointed by the senators of Navarr.

Navarr.t: Navarr's senators will appoint the new Steward of the Nabarr once the sinecure is completed, giving the nation control of a bladeroot-producing Imperial title within its own lands.

Construct Bladeroot Sinecure.o: In Summer 384YE the Senate passed a motion to commission a bladeroot-producing herb garden sinecure in Old Ranging, Hercynia, which will create the Imperial title of Steward of the Nabarr, appointed by the senators of Navarr.

Hercynia/Old Ranging.t: Old Ranging is the chosen site for the bladeroot sinecure, with materials and money already supplied towards its construction after the Summer Solstice.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia's senator proposed the motion, and the territory will be home to the new bladeroot herb garden sinecure once construction is completed.

Construct Bleak Tower.d: Proposed by Spiral and seconded by Reikos, the motion took up an opportunity presented at the Spring Equinox. The commission used non-standard costs: 30 wains each of weirwood and white granite, 120 crowns in labour, and six months to complete. Edmundo of Damakan's Forge supplied 10 wains of weirwood, 22 wains of white granite and 8 thrones after the Summer Solstice 382YE. Thalia of Netherwatch provided 20 wains of weirwood, 8 wains of white granite and 7 thrones after the Spring Equinox 383YE. Once complete, the tower spreads a share of 80 random herbs through Morrow's herb gardens. It also creates the title Custodian of the Bleak Tower, appointed by Urizen senators, which receives six doses of heart's blood each season.

Urizen.t: Urizen gains a great work that shelters Pallas's displaced herbalists and enriches its herb gardens in Morrow. Its senators appoint the new Custodian of the Bleak Tower.

Construct Bleak Tower.o: In Summer 382YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Bleak Tower, a self-funded great work in Ravion, Morrow, to house the refugees of the herb garden of Pallas and their herbalist researchers.

Morrow/Ravion.t: Ravion is the site of the Bleak Tower, which houses the refugees and researchers of the herb garden of Pallas.

Morrow.t: Morrow becomes home to the Bleak Tower, which distributes a share of 80 random herbs through the territory's herb gardens.

Construct Boar's Market.d: Proposed by the senator for Weirwater and seconded by the senator for Casinea, the motion took up an opportunity set out in the Good old smooth red wine Wind of Fortune. It passed at 50 thrones. The commission cost 12 wains of weirwood and 24 crowns and would take three months. After the Autumn Equinox 384YE, Bertrand provided 3 thrones and 12 wains of weirwood towards it. Once complete, the market-fayre would be overseen by a new Imperial title, the Reeve of Boar's Market. The title was intended for a yeofolk and appointed by Tally of the Votes, though the motion's own text described election by well worn path.

Dawn.t: Dawn would gain a market through which it could buy weirwood, mithril and white granite. It would also gain a new Dawnish title, the Reeve of Boar's Market, intended for one of its yeofolk.

Construct Boar's Market.o: In Autumn 384YE the Senate passed a motion to fund and construct the Boar's Market, a market-fayre at Boar's Hollow in Astolat where Dawn could purchase weirwood, mithril and white granite.

Astolat.t: The Boar's Market was to be built at Boar's Hollow in Astolat. Bertrand supplied the thrones and weirwood after the Autumn Equinox to begin its construction.

Construct Botanical Gardens of First Voi.d: Rhisiart Heartsbane, Senator for Miaren, proposed the restoration of the gardens, and Bronimir Ranedzkah Pinewheel, Senator for Ossium, seconded it. The project was to be self-funded. Its cost was 30 wains of weirwood and 90 crowns in labour, and it would take three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox, several donors began contributing: Vick Dagger gave 8 wains of weirwood and Mharen Splitroot gave 2 wains. Others gave thrones and crowns, including Drysfa Broken Bough, Merewen Splitroot and Lady Mercy Goldvein. Once complete, the Dean of the First Voice Glade would again receive 27 drams of herbs each season. The Dean could also upgrade one basic herb garden belonging to a member of the Vallornguard each season.

Navarr.t: The gardens would restore a seasonal supply of herbs to the Dean of the Navarr First Voice Glade school. They would also let the Dean improve herb gardens belonging to members of the Vallornguard, and Navarr donors were among the first to contribute weirwood and money.

Construct Botanical Gardens of First Voi.o: In Autumn 388YE the Senate passed a motion to restore the Botanical Gardens at the First Voice Glade School in Oakways, Miaren. The gardens would support the study of herb-lore with the Navarr and strengthen the Empire's prosperity and health.

Miaren/Oakways.t: The restored gardens were to be built in Oakways, with materials and funds still being gathered after the Autumn Equinox.

Miaren.t: Miaren's own senator proposed restoring the botanical gardens of the First Voice Glade School in the Navarr-held territory, and the motion passed.

Construct Bounders Hall in Bregasland.d: Announced by James Forrester, Bearer of the Second Imperial Wayleave, and sponsored by the Prosperity of Morgan Townsend and Thomas Oak, the motion followed the Kith and Kin Wind of Fortune. It would have cost 12 white granite and 36 crowns, taking three months to complete. Once built, it would create the national title Bailiff of the Fens, appointed annually by unanimous decision of the Marcher senators. It would also extend the protection of the Beating the Bounds military unit action to Bregasland once Sarcombe was reclaimed from the Jotun. Thomas Oak provided 4 thrones 4 crowns after the Summer Solstice 386YE. The project lapsed, and 3 thrones 3 crowns were returned to him after the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Jotun.t: The Jotun conquest of Bregasland was one of the reasons the planned Bounders Hall lapsed, and the hall's Beating the Bounds benefit depended on reclaiming Sarcombe from them.

Construct Bounders Hall in Bregasland.o: A Senate motion commissioned a Bounders Hall in Ottery, Bregasland, to create the Marcher title Bailiff of the Fens. The construction later lapsed for lack of funds and because the Jotun conquered Bregasland.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland was to gain a Bounders Hall at Ottery and a Bailiff of the Fens, but the project lapsed after the territory fell to the Jotun and funding proved insufficient.

Construct Bounders Hall of Meade.d: Following the Kith and Kin Wind of Fortune, Protectorate Thenrik, Legion Engineer, announced the construction of a Bounders Hall in Meade. It cost 12 white granite and 36 crowns and took three months to complete. The funding is credited in character to the houses of Talbot and Mudd of Mitwold. Matthias Talbot provided 12 wains of white granite and Thomas Oak provided 4 thrones 4 crowns after the Autumn Equinox. With the hall complete, the senators of the Marches could appoint the Bailiff of Meade by unanimous vote for the first time at the Winter Solstice 386YE. Marcher beaters can now send their military units to defend Mitwold.

The Marches.t: The Marches gained a new national title, the Bailiff of Meade, appointed by unanimous vote of Marcher senators. Marcher beaters can now send their military units to defend Mitwold.

Construct Bounders Hall of Meade.o: The Legion Engineer announced the commissioning of a Bounders Hall in Meade, Mitwold, at Autumn Equinox 386YE. The hall was built and created the Marcher national title of Bailiff of Meade.

Mitwold.t: A Bounders Hall was built in Meade in Mitwold with backing credited to the local houses of Talbot and Mudd. It allows Marcher beaters' military units to defend the territory.

Construct Brenna’s Gift.d: Raised in Spring 382YE through Jorgen Brenna's Imperial Wayleave, the motion proposed a great work in Hahnmark to boost farming income, and it passed. Beyond standard costs, it required 40 wains of weirwood and 80 crowns in labour. Jorgen Brenna supplied both the weirwood and the crowns after the Spring Equinox 382YE. Once completed, the work will provide money split between the owners of farms in Hahnmark. The page notes that the region of Hahnmark in which the great work will stand has still to be settled.

Wintermark.t: A Wintermark-held territory gains a work meant to enrich its farmers, funded entirely by Jorgen Brenna's own weirwood and coin.

Construct Brenna’s Gift.o: The Senate passed a motion, raised by Imperial Wayleave by Jorgen Brenna, to construct a great work in Hahnmark called Brenna's Gift that increases farming revenue.

Hahnmark.t: Brenna's Gift is to be built in Hahnmark, and once complete it will share extra money among the territory's farm owners, though its exact region is still to be decided.

Construct Bright-Threads Brass Works.d: Announced by Groza, the Legion Engineer, in Autumn 385YE, the Bright-Threads Brass Works was a sinecure to be built in Valasmark in Hahnmark, providing orichalcum. Construction cost 10 wains of mithril and 30 crowns on top of standard costs, and took three months. After the Autumn Equinox, Deorlaf Bright Thread supplied the 10 wains of mithril and 3 thrones 6 crowns. With the work completed, the tenured position of Bright Threadweaver was created, elected by unanimous decision of Wintermark's senators, and was first filled at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gained a new tenured title, Bright Threadweaver, chosen by the unanimous decision of its senators, after the Wintermark citizen Deorlaf Bright Thread funded the works.

Construct Bright-Threads Brass Works.o: The Legion Engineer Groza announced the construction of the Bright-Threads Brass Works, a sinecure producing orichalcum in Valasmark, Hahnmark. Once completed, it created the Wintermark title of Bright Threadweaver, first appointed at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Hahnmark/Valasmark.t: The Bright-Threads Brass Works was built in Valasmark, giving the region a working source of orichalcum attached to the Bright Threadweaver title.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark became home to a new orichalcum-producing sinecure, the Bright-Threads Brass Works, completed after three months.

Construct Bulgakov Memorial.d: Announced in Autumn 387YE, the memorial was designed by Triska Markova of the Druzhba Karova. It required 4 wains of weirwood, 1 wain of white granite and 15 crowns in labour, alongside standard costs, and took three months to build. Triska Markova supplied 1 throne 5 crowns and all of the weirwood and white granite. Rhys Nighthaven and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov each gave 1 crown. All of these contributions were made after the Autumn Equinox. The finished monument takes the form of warding stakes standing around Bulgakov in Duzekani, Karov.

Varushka.t: The memorial honours Varushkan citizens slain by the Cold Sun and the knights-errant who sacrificed themselves to save them, and a Varushkan of the Druzhba Karova designed it and largely paid for it.

Construct Bulgakov Memorial.o: Ada Droon, Mistress of Monuments, announced a memorial in Bulgakov, Duzekani, to commemorate the Varushkan citizens killed in the Cold Sun's attacks and the knights-errant who died fighting the scions so that many people of the vale could escape. The work was funded and completed, and warding stakes now stand around Bulgakov.

Karov/Duzekani.t: Warding stakes now stand around Bulgakov in Duzekani, a memorial to the vale's dead and to the knights-errant who held back the scions.

Karov.t: Karov gained a completed monument at Bulgakov marking the losses its people suffered in the Cold Sun's attacks.

Construct Carmine Fields Trading Post.d: Proposed by the senator for the Barrens and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion arose from the Little Mercy Wind of Fortune. It cost 12 wains of weirwood and 36 crowns and took three months to build. After the Summer Solstice Reynard of De Gauvain provided 4 thrones, 2 crowns and 12 wains of weirwood, and Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven gave a crown each. With construction complete, the Envoy to the Karass became available to appoint for the first time at the Autumn Equinox 387YE. The holder is chosen by a Tally of the Votes of Dawnish military unit captains and serves a shortened first term of three seasons.

Dawn.t: Dawn gains a new title, the Envoy to the Karass. It is chosen by the captains of Dawnish military units and was first appointable at the Autumn Equinox 387YE, and a Dawnish noble, Reynard of De Gauvain, supplied most of the funds and all the weirwood.

Construct Carmine Fields Trading Post.o: In Summer 387YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Wordes, Numbers, Figures and Knotes Trading Post, a ministry at Carmine Fields in the Barrens, and to create the title of Envoy to the Karass.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens' senator proposed the motion, and the new trading post ministry now stands at Carmine Fields in the Barrens, under Dawnish control.

Construct Cascade of Living Flame.d: The Crystal Architect of the Spires, Tiberius Echostorm, announced the commission of a self-funded mana sinecure in Peregro, Morrow (named "Cascade of Living Fire" in the announcement), to produce mana crystals. It cost 10 wains of mithril and 30 crowns and took three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox 386YE, Rhode provided the 10 wains of mithril and 3 thrones 6 crowns. With the work complete, the position of Custodian of Living Flame can be appointed by unanimous vote of the senators of Urizen, for the first time at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

Urizen.t: Urizen's senators gain the power to appoint the new Custodian of Living Flame by unanimous vote, starting at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

Construct Cascade of Living Flame.o: In Autumn 386YE a mana sinecure, the Cascade of Living Flame, was commissioned in Peregro, Morrow, and has since been completed, creating a new Urizen-appointed position.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Peregro is the site of the newly completed Cascade of Living Flame, a mana-producing sinecure.

Morrow.t: Morrow gains a new sinecure producing mana crystals, built with mithril and crowns supplied by Rhode.

Construct Cathedral of Courage.d: Proposed by the senator for Weirwater and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion called for a cathedral dedicated to Courage in Astolat as a sinecure providing Synod votes, with its Dean to be chosen by the National Assembly of Dawn. It passed at a cost of 25 thrones, which were disbursed to Senator Weirwater. Valentin Ivarovich Severyan contributed 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns after the Summer Solstice. Because some necessary details were missing from the motion, Senator Weirwater was left to decide them. The result was a small cathedral close to the tourney grounds of Laroc in The Chase, overseen by the Dean of Laroc Cathedral.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish gained a cathedral meant to strengthen their Courage against malign influences, with its Dean, the Dean of Laroc Cathedral, chosen by the National Assembly of Dawn and holding Synod votes.

Construct Cathedral of Courage.o: In Summer 380YE the Senate passed a motion to raise a Cathedral of Courage in Astolat, a sinecure granting votes in the Synod, to fortify the virtue of the Dawnish people against malign influences and auras. A small cathedral was subsequently built near the tourney grounds of Laroc in The Chase.

Astolat/The Chase.t: The new Cathedral of Courage stands in The Chase, close to the tourney grounds of Laroc.

Astolat.t: Astolat became home to a new small cathedral to Courage, raised with Senate funding and donated white granite.

Construct Celestial Library at Canterspi.d: Proposed by Redoubt and seconded by Tassato, the commission came from an agreement between the people of Urizen and Phaleron, following proposals from the library's archivists. It aimed to secure the library in perpetuity against harm or invasion. The civil service set non-standard costs after talking with Novus, herald of Phaleron: 40 wains of mithril, 80 crowns and three months of work. After the Summer Solstice 383YE, Spyridonakes provided 10 thrones. Marcus gave 20 wains of mithril, and Thalia and Edmundo of Damakan's forge gave 10 wains each, covering the mithril required. When construction is complete, Canterspire will be ceded to Phaleron.

Urizen.t: Urizen gains the institution of Urizen Lore, a lasting monument to its magical Ambition and Pride, in return for giving up the Grand Library of Canterspire to the eternal Phaleron.

Construct Celestial Library at Canterspi.o: The Senate passed a motion to transform the Grand Library of Canterspire into a Celestial Library and cede it to the eternal Phaleron, creating the institution of Urizen Lore as a monument to the nation's magical Ambition and Pride.

Morrow.t: The Grand Library of Canterspire is to be transformed and, once the work is complete, ceded to Phaleron so that it is protected in perpetuity against harm or invasion.

Construct Cerulean Balmhouse.d: Proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Zenith, the commission created the Cerulean Balmhouse, a herb sinecure whose holder is elected by the Freeborn National Assembly and has tenure. The motion drew on the aid of the Sumaah Republic offered through the Forging Links wind of fortune, as part of ongoing co-operation. Construction required standard costs, 20 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns in labour, reduced because Fontargenta was impoverished, and took three months. After the Spring Equinox, Mont i Sawa i Erigo provided 1 throne 2 crowns and the 20 wains of weirwood, and Sumaah citizens provided a further 1 throne 2 crowns. The Freeborn Assembly would appoint the first Herb Tender at the Summer Solstice 388YE.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named in the motion and is linked to it only because it held part of Feroz that season.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gained a new tenured herb sinecure in Feroz, with the Herb Tender of the Cerulean Balmhouse to be elected by their National Assembly from the Summer Solstice 388YE.

Construct Cerulean Balmhouse.o: In Spring 388YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Cerulean Balmhouse, a fully funded herb sinecure in Fontargenta in Feroz, with help sought from the Sumaah Republic. It was completed, with its first Herb Tender to be appointed by the Freeborn Assembly at the Summer Solstice 388YE.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Fontargenta became the site of the Cerulean Balmhouse, and its impoverished state lowered the labour cost of the construction to 20 crowns.

Feroz.t: Feroz gained a new herb sinecure, the Cerulean Balmhouse, built in Fontargenta with Sumaah support while control of the territory was divided between Grendel and the Brass Coast.

Construct Challenger in Waiting.d: Announced in Summer 385YE under an Imperial Wayleave, the Challenger in Waiting is a sinecure granting liao and a vote in the Synod, with a congregation based in Weirwater. The title is appointed by the Dawnish National Assembly, which expects the holder to appoint tourneys, and like the High Bard it may be held only once in a lifetime; regalia is to be provided. Construction cost 10 wains of white granite, 20 crowns in labour and standard costs, taking three months. Valentin Ivarovich Orzel supplied 2 thrones 4 crowns and the granite after the Summer Solstice. The first holder was elected at the Autumn Equinox 385YE, though the announcement remained subject to further scrutiny.

Dawn.t: Dawn's National Assembly gained a new once-per-lifetime title to appoint, its holder expected to call tourneys and given a vote in the Synod, with the first Challenger in Waiting elected at the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

Construct Challenger in Waiting.o: Valentin Ivarovich Orzel, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction of the Challenger in Waiting, a liao sinecure without tenure based in Weirwater, appointed by the Dawnish National Assembly. Construction was completed and the first Challenger in Waiting was elected at the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

Weirwater.t: The Challenger in Waiting was built in Weirwater, where its holder's congregation is based, using 10 wains of white granite.

Construct Chamber of Euphony.d: Proposed by the senator for Spiral and seconded by Tassato, the motion followed the opportunity described in the Wind of Fortune 'The play that came to Apulian'. It cost 15 mithril, 12 ilium and 5 thrones and took three months to build. Funding came from private donors across 387YE, including Sofonisba Amilcara of the City Below, Rafael, Genoveva and Dagon Barossa, Rhys Nighthaven, Gideon of the suns of Couros and Farren Silver Streams. The Map to the City Below is appointed annually by the League National Assembly. It is revocable by the League or General Assemblies or the Assembly of Nine, and oversees the fane while encouraging magic, music and mystery in Apulian. With the work complete, the title became available to appoint for the first time.

The League.t: The League gained a new Imperial title, the Map to the City Below, which its National Assembly appoints each year. Much of the funding came from League citizens such as members of the Barossa family and Sofonisba Amilcara of the City Below.

Construct Chamber of Euphony.o: The Senate passed a motion in Spring 387YE to build and cede the Chamber of Euphony, a fane to Sung in Apulus, Spiral, along with a new Imperial title, the Map to the City Below. It was funded through donations over the following year and completed.

Spiral/Apulus.t: The Chamber of Euphony was built in Apulus, and its titleholder is charged with spreading magic, music and mystery in the city of Apulian.

Spiral.t: Spiral's senator proposed the motion, and the territory gained the Chamber of Euphony, a fane dedicated to Sung.

Construct Church of the Roads.d: Diego i Del Toro i Erigo, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the commission in Winter 386YE. The Chaplain of the Roads is a tenured position, appointed by and revocable by the Highguard National Assembly, and comes with a supply of liao. Construction required 10 white granite and 30 crowns and took three months. Asael provided 3 thrones 6 crowns and 10 wains of white granite after the Winter Solstice. With the work complete, the Highborn Assembly was set to appoint the first Chaplain of the Roads at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly gained the power to appoint and revoke a new tenured liao sinecure charged with protecting the souls of travellers on Highguard's roads, with the first appointment due at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Construct Church of the Roads.o: A commission was announced to build the Church of the Roads in Woodbury, Bastion, creating a liao sinecure, the Chaplain of the Roads, responsible for protecting the souls of those travelling on Highguard's roads.

Bastion/Woodbury.t: The Church of the Roads was built in Woodbury using white granite and crowns provided by Asael.

Bastion.t: Bastion became home to the Church of the Roads, a completed commission providing liao to the Chaplain of the Roads.

Construct Churnspire.d: Proposed by Bastion's senator and seconded by Morrow's, the motion passed at 100 thrones and followed an opportunity described in The Net of the Realms wind of fortune. The tower, designed by Megaris of Glowspire to stand taller than Pakaanan's Pass, required 20 wains of white granite, 10 wains of mithril, 60 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Baal provided the mithril, granite and 7 thrones 4 crowns. The proposed Churnspire Adjutor would receive regalia and a regular gift of mana from Meraud. On scrutiny, the Constitutional Court ruled the title could not be filled by a vote of all Urizen magi. It asked for an administrative motion making it a national title appointed by the Senate.

Urizen.t: Urizen gains a new national title, the Churnspire Adjutor, which carries Meraud's regalia and mana. The Court ruled that the Senate, not a vote of Urizen's magi, must appoint it.

Construct Churnspire.o: In Spring 384YE the Imperial Senate passed a motion commissioning the Churnspire, a magical tower in Peregro in Morrow, built with the help of the eternal Meraud and ceded to her. Once complete, it creates the national position of Churnspire Adjutor.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Peregro is where the Churnspire is to be raised, a tower designed to stand taller than Pakaanan's Pass and then be ceded to Meraud.

Morrow.t: Morrow is the site of the Churnspire, and its senator seconded the motion to build the tower.

Construct Cinderpath Exchange.d: Proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by Redoubt, the motion would have created the Cinderpath Exchange and the Imperial title 'Cinderpath Benefactor', an opportunity presented by the benefactors of Highguard. It was rejected. Scrutiny found that Abraham had given incorrect information in the Senate about its effect on white granite at public auction. With the Highborn assembly mandate supporting it, the ministry would have removed 6 wains of white granite each season from the auction, rising to 8 if the General Assembly mandate were later passed. The civil service raised an administrative motion to reconsider, but it also failed. A constitutional challenge confirmed the title would have been appointed by vote of Highborn congregations, not the Highborn assembly.

Highguard.t: Highguard lost the chance to control a white granite ministry through the Cinderpath Benefactor title, which a constitutional challenge confirmed would have been chosen by Highborn congregations rather than their National Assembly.

Construct Cinderpath Exchange.o: A Senate motion to construct the Cinderpath Exchange, a self-funded ministry in Mareholm, Casinea, allowing the purchase of white granite, failed in Summer 382YE. A follow-up administrative motion to reconsider it also failed.

Casinea/Mareholm.t: Mareholm was the proposed site of the Cinderpath Exchange, but no ministry will be built there.

Casinea.t: The Highborn-held territory of Casinea will not gain the Cinderpath Exchange, after both the original motion and the reconsideration failed.

Construct Cinderpath Exchange II.d: Proposed by the senator for Bastion and seconded by the senator for Miekarova, the motion sought to commission the Cinderpath Exchange as a ministry in Mareholm, Casinea. The project drew on an opportunity presented by the benefactors of Highguard. It would have cost White Granite, been self-funded, and created the title 'Cinderpath Benefactor', to be appointed once a year by a vote of the congregation leaders of Highguard. The motion followed an earlier, unsuccessful attempt to build the same ministry, and this second motion also failed, so the Exchange was not commissioned.

Highguard.t: The Highborn missed a second chance to secure a ministry built on an opportunity from their own benefactors, along with a new title that their congregation leaders would have appointed each year.

Construct Cinderpath Exchange II.o: In Spring 383YE the Senate considered a motion to build the Cinderpath Exchange, a self-funded ministry in Mareholm, Casinea, and the motion failed. It was a second attempt, following an earlier motion that had also failed.

Casinea/Mareholm.t: Mareholm was the proposed site of the Cinderpath Exchange, but it remained unbuilt after this second motion also failed.

Casinea.t: The Highguard territory of Casinea would have gained a new ministry, but the motion failed and no construction was commissioned.

Construct Cinderpath Exchange III.d: Issachar of the Unbound, proxy to Caleb of Reumah's Redoubt and bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction of the Cinderpath Exchange, drawing on an opportunity offered by the benefactors of Highguard. The ministry used non-standard costs: 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns in labour, with three months to construct. It was self-funded, and Rhesa provided the materials and money after the Spring Equinox 383YE. When complete, it will create a Highguard national position, the Cinderpath Custodian, chosen as a bourse position by Highborn owners of congregations, a method adopted on advice from the Constitutional Court.

Highguard.t: Highguard gains a white granite ministry and a new national title, the Cinderpath Custodian, chosen by Highborn congregation owners once construction is complete.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named; the only link is the word Redoubt in the proposer's title, Caleb of Reumah's Redoubt.

Construct Cinderpath Exchange III.o: In Spring 383YE a bearer of an Imperial Wayleave announced the commissioning of the Cinderpath Exchange, a white granite ministry in Mareholm, Casinea. It followed two earlier failed motions for the same project.

Casinea/Mareholm.t: Mareholm is the site of the new Cinderpath Exchange ministry, funded with 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns provided by Rhesa.

Casinea.t: The Cinderpath Exchange is being built in Casinea, with materials supplied and three months set for its completion.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not involved; Redoubt appears only in the name Caleb of Reumah's Redoubt.

Construct Circo del Topo.d: The commission required 10 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns in labour costs and took three months to complete. The resulting sinecure provides an income of 216 rings per season and is supervised by the Temeschwari Topolino. This Imperial title is appointed by unanimous decision of the League senators and is held with tenure until death, resignation or revocation. The holder works with the Temeschwar Rat Catchers guild to find wider business uses for captured rats, beginning with training them for entertainment. The project was organised by Red Raven Holdings. Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided 3 thrones 6 crowns and the weirwood after the Winter Solstice 387YE.

The League.t: The League gains a new tenured Imperial title, the Temeschwari Topolino, which its senators appoint by unanimous decision and which carries an income of 216 rings per season.

Construct Circo del Topo.o: In Winter 387YE the Chair of the Wolf, Lucrezia Corvinascura, announced the construction of the Circo del Topo, a self-funded sinecure in Hanuri, Temeschwar. It was completed after the Winter Solstice, and the Temeschwari Topolino title became available for appointment at the Spring Equinox 388YE.

Temeschwar/Hanuri.t: The Circo del Topo was built in Hanuri and completed after the Winter Solstice 387YE.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar gains the Circo del Topo, which ties its Rat Catchers guild to new business ventures, starting with rats trained for entertainment.

Construct City of Dreams.d: The motion framed the project as an answer to what Navarr would become once the vallorn it marches against is destroyed. It was to be self-funded through donations, costing 90 wains of weirwood, 30 wains of white granite and 360 crowns, with nine months to complete. Many citizens contributed materials and money from Summer 386YE through to Summer 388YE, with Rhys Nighthaven, Geraint Bronwen's Rest and Asthore Autumngale among the most frequent donors. Once complete, the City of Dreams will raise investment in Miaren's congregations by one, providing a vial of liao and a dose of Goosewhisper Infusion each season. It will also establish the Dreamspeaker archetype in Navarr and create the title of Dreamer's Guide.

Navarr.t: Once the city is complete, Navarr gains the Dreamspeaker archetype, and its National Assembly can appoint a Dreamer's Guide, offering the nation a vision of its future beyond the war with the vallorn.

Construct City of Dreams.o: In Summer 386YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Miaren's senator and seconded by Bastion's, to commission the City of Dreams in Serenael, Miaren, using the opportunity set out in the Comes a Time wind of fortune.

Miaren/Serenael.t: Serenael is the site chosen for the City of Dreams, a great weirwood and white granite project funded by donations over two years.

Miaren.t: Miaren's senator proposed the motion, and once complete the city will increase investment in the territory's congregations by one, yielding liao and Goosewhisper Infusion each season.

Construct City of Wonders.d: The edifice cost 50 wains of white granite, 35 of weirwood, 5 of mithril, 30 rings of ilium and 270 crowns in labour, and takes six months to build. Brass Coast citizens supported it through mandates enacted by Ignacio i Zuhri i Erigo, Isario i Riqueza and Val, and the Cat's Graces provided the foundational artwork, created by Karrak. Many contributors supplied materials and money after the Spring Equinox and Summer Solstice. Once complete, it creates the Burning Agora, a new southern propylaeum, a restored Market of a Thousand Sails and an enchanted Fountain of Wonders. It also adds the Firebrand, Hawker and Trailblazer Freeborn archetypes and changes Anduz's fate to become the City of Wonders.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn citizens backed the project with mandates and contributed most of the materials and coin. The completed edifice gives the Brass Coast three new archetypes, the Firebrand, the Hawker and the Trailblazer, and promises wealth, adventure and new ideas.

Construct City of Wonders.o: Firesong Arachas, the Legion Engineer, announced the construction of the City of Wonders edifice in Anduzjasse, Segura, following the example of Dust, Glass, and Flame and taking up the opportunity of the On the road ahead wind of fortune.

Segura/Anduzjasse.t: Anduzjasse is the site of the six-month construction. Once complete, it gains the torchlit Burning Agora, a southern propylaeum, the restored Market of a Thousand Sails and the enchanted Fountain of Wonders at the city's centre.

Segura.t: Segura's city of Anduz is to be transformed into the City of Wonders, with a restored Market of a Thousand Sails, a new propylaeum and the Burning Agora for the exchange of ideas.

Construct Clattering Curtain Theatre.d: Proposed by Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato, Senator for Tassato, and seconded by Vasilmir Radovanovna Esskivic, Senator for Miekarova, the motion authorised a theatre in Tassato Mestra. It created the tenured title of Martim de Tassato's Clattering Curtain Theatre Champion, to be appointed by unanimous vote of the League's senators. Construction required 12 wains of white granite and 36 crowns in labour on top of standard costs, and would take three months. After the Summer Solstice, Esme Beatrix de Holberg provided 4 thrones 4 crowns and the 12 wains of white granite. Once complete, the League senators may appoint the Champion.

The League.t: The League gains a new tenured, money-producing sinecure whose Champion its senators must appoint by unanimous vote once the theatre is complete.

Construct Clattering Curtain Theatre.o: In Summer 388YE the Senate passed a motion to build Martim de Tassato's Clattering Curtain Theatre in Mestra, Tassato, a money-producing sinecure with its own Imperial title.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Mestra is to host the new Clattering Curtain Theatre, built from white granite over three months with materials and funds supplied by Esme Beatrix de Holberg.

Tassato.t: Tassato's senator proposed the theatre, which honours Martim de Tassato and will stand in the territory's capital region.

Construct College of Engineering and Arc.d: Proposed by Tassato and seconded by Astolat, the motion arose from an opportunity offered by the eternal Adamant. The college required at least 60 wains of white granite and 120 crowns and six months to build, and had to stand in a hilly region, which in Temeschwar meant Locul. The Master of the Koboldi, appointed through the Conclave, would be Adamant's representative to the Empire and vice versa. Adamant intended the title to announce one extra commission each season using at least 30 wains of white granite, but only if its holder could freely choose what to build. The original wording failed this and was amended at Winter Solstice 382YE. Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato later provided white granite and thrones in 383YE.

The League.t: A League senator, Tassato, proposed the motion, and the college would stand in League-held Temeschwar, with a Tassatan magnate, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato, providing white granite and thrones towards its construction.

Construct College of Engineering and Arc.o: In Summer 382YE the Senate passed in principle a motion to commission a college of engineering and architecture in Temeschwar, to be ceded to the eternal Adamant and creating the Imperial title of Master of the Koboldi.

Temeschwar/Locul.t: As the only hilly region in Temeschwar, Locul was required by Adamant's stipulation to host the college of engineering and architecture.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar was chosen as the site of the new college, which would be ceded to the eternal Adamant once complete.

Construct College of Maykop.d: The motion, proposed by Volodmartz and seconded by Ossium, authorised construction of the College of Maykop in Casinea at a non-standard cost of 20 wains of white granite, 10 wains of mithril and 60 crowns in labour, taking three months to build. It passed. After the Winter Solstice 383YE, Dagon Barossa supplied the 10 wains of mithril, the 20 wains of white granite and 6 thrones 4 crowns, and Richardo Glostari di Sarvos added a further throne. Once completed, the work creates the title of Bursar of the House of Spirits, a Highborn national Bourse position appointed annually through the Tally of the Votes.

Highguard.t: Highguard gains a new national Bourse position, the Bursar of the House of Spirits, once the college is complete, with the holder appointed each year through the Tally of the Votes.

Construct College of Maykop.o: In Winter 383YE the Senate passed a motion to build a campus for the Halls of Maykop in Casinea, as set out in the A mountain of vipers Wind of Fortune.

Casinea.t: Casinea is the site of the new College of Maykop campus for the Halls of Maykop, a three-month project built from white granite and mithril.

Construct College of Summer Magic.d: Proposed by Miaren, the motion sought permission, but no funding, to build a College of Magic dedicated to Cathan Canae. Because it followed the Eternal's designs, its cost differed from a standard college: 90 wains of white granite, 30 of mithril and 30 of weirwood, 35 Thrones of labour and a year to build, with upkeep of 25 Thrones. Llewellyn Leafstalker supplied all of the materials and labour between Autumn 379YE and Spring 380YE. The college was built at Volchitrava in Miekarova and named The Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun. Its completion created the title of Master of Ice and Darkness, which the senator made an Imperial position assigned by declaration of the Conclave.

Varushka.t: Varushka gained an Imperial College of Summer Magic on its soil, along with the Master of Ice and Darkness title, which is assigned by Conclave declaration.

Construct College of Summer Magic.o: In Summer 379YE the Senate was asked to approve a College of Summer Magic in Miekarova, built to designs provided by the Eternal Cathan Canae. Once completed, it became The Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun and created the Imperial title of Master of Ice and Darkness.

Miekarova/Srodkoja.t: The map attaches the college to Srodkoja; the page itself gives the site as Volchitrava in Miekarova, where The Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun was completed.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova became home to The Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, a Summer college built at Volchitrava to the designs of Cathan Canae.

Construct College of the Liberated.d: Proposed by Casinea and seconded by Sarvos, with wording help from Senator Miaren, the motion passed at 100 thrones and 4 crowns, disbursed to Senator Casinea. Ferrero Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato supplied 40 wains of white granite and 10 thrones after the Winter Solstice. The College was built in the town of Trivento and, once complete, enhances the earnings of Sarvos businesses whose owners attended the previous Anvil summit. The Constitutional Court found it legal, provided the Jarmish newcomers are told they need not stay or study there; spare places could go to Sarvos orphans and poor. The Senate appoints the Dean of the Liberated for life.

The League.t: A League senator proposed the College and a League merchant supplied its materials, giving the League a new Senate-appointed title and greater prosperity for Sarvos businesses whose owners attended the Anvil summit.

Construct College of the Liberated.o: In Winter 379YE the Senate passed a motion to build the College of the Liberated in Sarvos, a great work to help former Jarmish slaves integrate into the Empire through education and apprenticeships, and created the title of Dean of the Liberated.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: The map places the College here; the page records it as built in the town of Trivento, where former Jarmish slaves may receive education and apprenticeships.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos gained the College of the Liberated in Trivento, which educates willing former Jarmish slaves and could also take in local orphans and poor, while boosting the earnings of eligible Sarvos businesses.

Construct Commonwealth embassy.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by the senator for Kallavesa, the motion called for an embassy to the Commonwealth to be constructed in Madruga. It passed in principle, but no money was set aside for it. The commission required 25 wains each of weirwood and white granite, 12 thrones of labour and one season to build, with upkeep of 5 thrones. After the Winter Solstice of 379YE, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason supplied the full materials and the labour cost. Completing the embassy automatically creates the Imperial title of Ambassador to the Commonwealth.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast was to host the Empire's embassy to the Commonwealth on its own soil in Madruga, giving the nation a direct diplomatic stake in relations with the Commonwealth.

Construct Commonwealth embassy.o: In Summer 379YE the Senate passed in principle a motion to build an embassy to the Commonwealth in Madruga, though no funds were allocated at the time.

Madruga.t: Madruga was chosen as the site of the Commonwealth embassy, with the materials and labour for it supplied after the Winter Solstice of 379YE.

Construct Compassion Without Expectation.d: The monument was to be a restful garden celebrating Lady Eleanor Novarion's virtuous work in founding the Proffered Hand network. It required 4 white granite, 4 weirwood, 1 mithril and 27 crowns, with three months to complete. Contributions came in from many citizens over the following year, from Winter Solstice 386YE to Autumn Equinox 387YE.
