Construction began after a suitably inspiring design was chosen at the Summer Solstice 385YE. Mandates brought seasonal contributions from the citizens of the Marches, the Brass Coast, Highguard, Wintermark, Navarr, the League and Dawn. Many individuals also donated over the following years. Highguard's support continues under the Benefactors Council. In 388YE the design was amended to add seven great bells, gardens for the Voices of Virtue and a choristers' balcony.

Dawn.t: Through a mandate enacted by Darian Numbers at the Winter Solstice 385YE, Dawn's citizens gave 16 wains of white granite and 32 crowns each season until the Winter Solstice 386YE.

Highguard.t: The edifice rises in Highguard's territory of Bastion. Its citizens have supported it since Eli of the Cenotaph's mandate, and they now give 12 wains of white granite and 36 crowns each season under the Benefactors Council's direction until it is completed.

Navarr.t: After Fintan Nighthaven's mandate at the Autumn Equinox 385YE, Navarr's citizens contributed until the Autumn Equinox 386YE. Their seasonal share fell from 12 wains of white granite and 24 crowns to 8 wains and 16 crowns because Navarr did not control Therunin.

The Brass Coast.t: After Sufyan i Zuhri i Erigo's mandate at the Summer Solstice 385YE, Brass Coast citizens contributed until the Summer Solstice 386YE. Their share fell from 12 wains of white granite and 24 crowns to 8 wains and 16 crowns because the Brass Coast did not control Madruga.

Wintermark.t: Through Eldrid Vestardottir's mandate at the Autumn Equinox 385YE, Wintermark's citizens gave 12 wains of white granite and 24 crowns each season until the Autumn Equinox 386YE.

Construct Grand Inspiration of the Way.o: The Senate passed a motion in Summer 385YE to commission the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion, a great temple-city edifice arising from the Blood will thicken wind of fortune. Once complete, it is meant to establish the Empire as the undisputed source of spiritual guidance for all followers of the Way in the known world.

Bastion.t: Bastion is the site of the Grand Inspiration of the Way, a temple-city whose construction began after its design was chosen in Summer 385YE. Its design was later enlarged with great bells, gardens for the Voices of Virtue and a choristers' balcony.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the Brass Coast's contribution to the project was reduced because the nation did not control Madruga.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr's contribution to the project was reduced because the nation did not control Therunin.

Construct Grand Lodge of Sevenfold Path.d: The grand lodge was first presented shortly before the Winter Solstice 387YE. It required 65 wains of weirwood, 45 of white granite, 15 of mithril and 375 crowns in labour, with five thrones of upkeep and nine months to build. Several individuals made small crown donations after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete it will add 15 mana crystals to the Conclave font each season, house a grand basilica to the Way, cut the Grandmaster's mana costs, and supply true liao and liao to the order. It will also raise congregation investment in the territory, let Highguard support an additional navy, and add the Voice of the Paragons to Imperial lore while Net of Gossamer Chains is interdicted.

Highguard.t: Once complete, the grand lodge will allow Highguard to raise and support one additional navy beyond current limits, and will raise the investment level of congregations in its Necropolis territory by one.

Construct Grand Lodge of Sevenfold Path.o: In Autumn 388YE Galene Netherwatch announced the construction of the Grand Lodge of the Sevenfold Path, with an extended basilica, in Sanctuary Sands, Necropolis, built with the aid of the eternal Adamant, the Shaper of Mountains, through a personal boon.

Necropolis.t: The Grand Lodge of the Sevenfold Path and its extended basilica are being built in Sanctuary Sands, Necropolis, and on completion will raise the investment level of congregations in the territory by one.

Construct Grand Lodge of the Golden Pyra.d: Proposed by the senator for Mareave and seconded by Reikos, the commission cost 50 mithril, 50 white granite and 60 crowns, and took six months to build. Its proposer stated that 60% was already funded. Irontide Flax supplied all 50 wains of mithril, and many citizens donated granite and money over three seasons, Arsenio Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato chief among them. Once complete, the Lodge added 15 mana crystals to the Conclave font each season, housed and aided the order's Grandmaster, and gave the order mithril and income. It raised investment, Fundindelve output and taxes in Mareave and removed Clisearn's Uncooperative quality. The new title was first appointed at the Autumn Equinox 387YE.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel are not named on the page; their only connection is that they held Mareave alongside the Imperial Orcs when the commission was passed.

Imperial Orcs.t: The commission created the Imperial Orc title Bonesetter of the Delving Market, appointed by the Tally of the Votes and first available at the Autumn Equinox 387YE. The Lodge also strengthened the Mareave lands they held through higher investment, taxes and Fundindelve output.

Construct Grand Lodge of the Golden Pyra.o: In Winter 386YE the Senate passed a commission to build the Grand Lodge of the Golden Pyramid, a great work in Clisearn, Mareave, as set out in the Lit up Wind of Fortune. It also created the Imperial Orc title Bonesetter of the Delving Market.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: Clisearn is where the Grand Lodge of the Golden Pyramid was built. Its completion removed the region's Uncooperative quality.

Mareave.t: The completed Lodge raised the investment level of mines, businesses and mana sites in Mareave by one. It also boosted the Fundindelve's production by 2 wains and the territory's taxation by 10 thrones each season.

Construct Great Aqueduct of Eoradal.d: The commission cost 12 white granite, 4 weirwood, 4 mithril and 15 crowns, the crowns arising from the underdeveloped nature of Icarion. It carried 12 thrones upkeep and took three months to build. After the Winter Solstice several citizens donated money, including Pathfinder Gaddak, Fedelmidd Sydanjaa's Heart Floer, Karrak, Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven. After the Spring Equinox 387YE Bloodcrow Rasp provided all the required materials. The completed aqueduct uses water bought from the Skourans of Jadefall to supply fresh water to Eoradal's main settlement and removes the region's arid quality while operational. Once Curstag's Way is also completed, Eoradal can support a large town, raising taxation by 4 thrones a season.

Grendel.t: Grendel held part of Mareave at the time, but the page does not mention Grendel or say which Mareave regions it controlled. The aqueduct was built and paid for through Imperial commission and citizens' donations.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Legion Engineer commissioned the aqueduct for Mareave, a territory the Imperial Orcs held in part. Once complete, it brought fresh water and the prospect of greater prosperity to Eoradal.

Construct Great Aqueduct of Eoradal.o: In Winter 386YE the Legion Engineer, Protectorate Thenrik, commissioned the Great Aqueduct of Eoradal in Mareave, an edifice built in Clisearn to bring water to Eoradal under the Million Miles of Water Wind of Fortune. The aqueduct was later completed.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: The Great Aqueduct of Eoradal was constructed as an edifice in Clisearn.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: The aqueduct supplies fresh water to Eoradal's main settlement and removes the region's arid quality while operational. Once Curstag's Way is also completed, the region can support a large town, raising taxation by 4 thrones a season.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Mentioned in passing: Icarion's underdeveloped nature added 15 crowns to the cost of the commission.

Mareave.t: Mareave gained a great aqueduct built in Clisearn that carries water bought from the Skourans of Jadefall to Eoradal. It removed that region's aridity and opened the way to a large town and higher taxes once Curstag's Way is finished.

Construct Great Hall of Fabric Arts.d: Announced by Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, Master of the Koboldi, with the backing of the Varushkan Assembly through a mandate enacted by Anatolij Paukov Zorkin, the commission cost 80 white granite and 240 crowns and took six months to complete. Funding came over several seasons into Spring 387YE: Varushkan citizens provided granite and thrones each season, alongside donations from Triska Markova, Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov, Kostjya, Farren Silver Streams, Rhys Nighthaven, a large contribution from Yakov "Yasha" Bjelovuk, and small gifts. Once complete, the hall would spark a renaissance in the fabric arts, reminding Varushkans of their traditional heritage and restoring these skills to prominence in the nation's culture.

Varushka.t: The hall was meant to start a renaissance in Varushkan fabric arts, restoring these traditional skills to prominence in the nation's culture. The Varushkan Assembly backed the motion and Varushkan citizens supplied much of the granite and money.

Construct Great Hall of Fabric Arts.o: In Summer 386YE the Master of the Koboldi announced the construction of a Great Hall of Fabric Arts in Delev, Karov, celebrating Varushka's industry as set out in The Deer in the Sun wind of fortune.

Karov.t: The Great Hall of Fabric Arts was to be built in Delev in Karov, making the territory home to the centre of Varushka's revived fabric arts.

Construct Great Harbour of Elos.d: Proposed by Volodmartz and seconded by Sarvos, the motion disbursed funds for the Great Harbour of Elos, an opportunity set out in the To see what you sell Wind of Fortune. The harbour was described as a great work yielding prosperous returns to the territory and the tax budget. Construction required 35 wains of weirwood, 35 wains of white granite, 140 crowns in labour and six months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Radomir Ivanovic Volkov provided 5 wains of weirwood and 35 of white granite, and Gancio di Catazar gave 17 thrones 4 crowns and 30 wains of weirwood. On completion, the Elosian Architect, appointed by Imperial Bourse auction with the right to purchase foreign herbs, would become available.

Urizen.t: The restored harbour at Elos promised prosperous returns for Urizen's territory of Redoubt, with the materials and labour largely supplied by citizens of other nations.

Construct Great Harbour of Elos.o: In Spring 384YE the Senate passed a motion, at a cost of 300 Thrones, commissioning the restoration of the Great Harbour of Elos in the Naris region of Redoubt. The great work was to be overseen by a new Imperial title, the Elosian Architect.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Elos in Naris was the site of the Great Harbour, whose restoration required weirwood, white granite and labour and would create the Elosian Architect title on completion.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt was to gain the restored Great Harbour of Elos, a great work meant to bring prosperity to the territory and the Imperial tax budget once its six-month construction was complete.

Construct Great Library of Hacynian.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Therunin, the motion commissioned the expansion of the Library of Hacynian into the Great Library, leaving the title 'Advisor on the Vallorn' unchanged. Navarr asked the Senate to disburse funds for the commission, which cost 50 wains of white granite, 40 of weirwood, 30 of mithril and 240 crowns, and takes a year to complete. The motion passed. After the Autumn Equinox most materials and much of the money came from Nemae Splitroot, with further contributions from many others. Once complete, the library would allow research into a way to finally defeat the vallorn, and League and Highguard mandates were passed to support it.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: a Highguard mandate (Mandate 50) was passed to support the vallorn research the library would enable.

Navarr.t: Navarr requested Senate funding for a library its people had waited generations for, and many Navarr contributed materials and coin, chiefly Nemae Splitroot, in hope of finding a way to finally defeat the vallorn.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the senator for Therunin seconded the motion, and Edric of Urizen donated a crown towards it.

Construct Great Library of Hacynian.o: The Senate passed a motion to expand the Library of Hacynian in Hercynia into a Great Library collating the world's lore on the vallorn, taking up an opportunity from the Wind of Fortune 'The bones of what you believe'.

Hercynia.t: The Library of Hacynian in Hercynia was commissioned to be expanded into the Great Library, a year-long construction intended to collate vallorn lore from across the world.

Construct Greenwood Manor.d: The commission was announced by Bertrand under an Imperial Wayleave rather than raised in the usual way. It cost 10 wains of white granite, 10 wains of weirwood and 40 crowns in labour, and would take three months to build. After the Summer Solstice Bertrand supplied 5 thrones, 10 wains of weirwood and 10 wains of white granite. Once complete, the commission would create two Imperial titles, the Knight of the Greenwood and the Reeve of the Greenwood Fair. Both would be elected annually by the Dawnish National Assembly and could be revoked by the General Assembly or the Dawnish National Assembly.

Dawn.t: Once the manor is complete, the Dawnish National Assembly gains the power to elect, and to revoke, the new Knight of the Greenwood and Reeve of the Greenwood Fair each year.

Construct Greenwood Manor.o: In Summer 384YE Bertrand, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the commission of Greenwood Manor in Elvette, Semmerholm, together with the renovation of the Greenwood Market, a unique opportunity drawn from a Wind of Fortune.

Semmerholm/Elvette.t: Elvette is the site of the commission, where Greenwood Manor was to be built and the Greenwood Market renovated over three months.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm is to gain Greenwood Manor and a renovated Greenwood Market, funded with materials and money provided by Bertrand after the Summer Solstice.

Construct Grendel Embassy.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Redoubt and seconded by Kahraman, amended the title of Imperial Fleetmaster by commissioning an embassy to the Grendel in Cargo. It passed at no cost in thrones. The Senate chose a standard embassy rather than the large one outlined in the Everything has a price wind of fortune. The embassy required 25 wains of weirwood, 25 wains of white granite, 100 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Summer Solstice 384YE, Sejanus of the Scarlet Guard provided 10 thrones and all the weirwood and white granite, and Ehud gave 2 thrones 4 crowns. Once completed, the Imperial Fleetmaster gains the standard benefits of an embassy.

Grendel.t: The Empire committed to a formal embassy to the Grendel at Cargo, giving the Imperial Fleetmaster a standing diplomatic presence with them, though not the grander embassy the Grendel's offer had proposed.

Urizen.t: Urizen's senator for Redoubt proposed the motion, and the new embassy was to be built at Cargo within Urizen's territory.

Construct Grendel Embassy.o: In Spring 384YE the Senate passed a motion to build an embassy to the Grendel at Cargo in Redoubt, attached to the title of Imperial Fleetmaster. It declined the larger embassy offered in the Everything has a price wind of fortune.

Redoubt.t: An Imperial embassy to the Grendel was commissioned at Cargo in Redoubt, with its materials and much of its labour cost provided after the Summer Solstice.

Construct Guildhouse of the Artisans.d: Proposed by the senator for Hahnmark and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion created a guildhouse with a sinecure producing materials for artisans of the guild. The title of Guildmaster of the Artisans is appointed with tenure by the Senate, with the expectation that the guild will present its own chosen candidate. The motion credited the guild's ambition, prosperity and hard work with funding the work, and asked that any additional funds make the guildhouse grander and the envy of foreign nations. After the Summer Solstice, Xanthius Storm's End provided 8 wains of mithril, 4 thrones and 8 wains of white granite. Once complete, the guildhouse will create the Imperial title of Guildmaster of the Artisans.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains an Imperial guildhouse for the Artisans Guild beside its own Runegrott and Runeforge, proposed by the senator for Hahnmark, which will give the nation's artisans a recognised sodality, a Guildmaster and a supply of materials.

Construct Guildhouse of the Artisans.o: The Senate passed a motion in Summer 385YE to build a guildhouse for the Artisans Guild near Runegrott and the Runeforge in Hahnmark, creating a sinecure, an Imperial title and a sodality.

Hahnmark.t: The guildhouse is to be built in Hahnmark, close to Runegrott and the Runeforge, and the territory's senator proposed the motion.

Construct Hall of Rund.d: Proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by Kahraman, the motion took up the opportunity presented by the Old Ways Wind of Fortune. The Hall of Rund is a sinecure that produces liao, and its holder, the Speaker of the Crows, is to lead and guide Wintermark's National Assembly. Construction required 10 wains of weirwood, 6 wains of white granite and 48 crowns, and took three months. After the Winter Solstice, Veikko Bondforger supplied the weirwood and white granite, and Gisli i Phovas i Guerra provided 6 thrones. With the work complete, the National Assembly of Wintermark can appoint the first Speaker of the Crows at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a new national position, the Speaker of the Crows, appointed by and charged with leading and guiding its National Assembly. The Assembly can make its first appointment at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

Construct Hall of Rund.o: In Winter 385YE the Senate passed a motion to commission the Hall of Rund in Rundhal, Kallavesa, a sinecure granting liao, to be held by a new Speaker of the Crows chosen by the Wintermark National Assembly.

Kallavesa.t: The Hall of Rund was built at Rundhal in Kallavesa as a liao-giving sinecure, on a motion proposed by Kallavesa's own senator.

Construct Hall of the Hunters.d: Announced in Spring 385YE under the Legion Engineer's authority, the Hall of the Hunters is a sinecure arising from the Watching my mistakes wind of fortune. It required 12 wains of white granite, 3 thrones in labour and three months to build, plus standard costs. Liv Tidgaring provided the 3 thrones and 12 wains of white granite after the Spring Equinox. Once complete, the Wintermark National Assembly may appoint the Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq by judgement. The hall will also open a new adventure, Hunt the Suaq Wastes, to military units from Dawn and Wintermark.

Dawn.t: Dawn's military units will gain access to the new Hunt the Suaq Wastes adventure once the hall is complete.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark National Assembly will gain the right to appoint the Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq, and Wintermark military units can take part in the Hunt the Suaq Wastes adventure; Liv Tidgaring supplied the granite and labour costs.

Construct Hall of the Hunters.o: The Legion Engineer Groza announced construction of the Hall of the Hunters, a sinecure at Lake Atkonaroq in the Suaq Wastes of Sermersuaq, creating the title Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: The hall is to stand at Lake Atkonaroq in the Suaq Wastes, which become the setting for the new Hunt the Suaq Wastes adventure.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq, held by Wintermark, is to gain the Hall of the Hunters at Lake Atkonaroq, a new sinecure tied to hunting in its wastes.

Construct Hall of the Krampus.d: The motion called for a hall for the Krampus to be constructed in Skarsind as a folly, following recent events. It passed in Winter 380YE. The cost was 13 wains of white granite and 26 crowns in labour, with three months needed to build. After the Winter Solstice 380YE, Irontide Vio provided both the granite and the crowns. The campaign outcome records that the Krampushall has been constructed in Skarsind.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs, who held Skarsind, gained the Krampushall in their territory, a folly proposed by Skarsind's senator and honouring the Krampus.

Construct Hall of the Krampus.o: In Winter 380YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by Karsk, to build a folly honouring the Krampus in Skarsind, which was subsequently completed as the Krampushall.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind became home to the Krampushall, a folly for the Krampus built from white granite and crowns supplied by Irontide Vio.

Construct Hall of the Seven.d: Announced by Bertrand, Bearer of the First Imperial Wayleave, the commission followed the wind of fortune "The bones of what you believe". It cost 10 wains of weirwood, 10 wains of mithril and 5 thrones in labour, and took three months to build. The mithril was given in memory of Amaan Embercast, and weirwood and coin came from many Navarr donors, including Corwyn Heartsbane, Nathair Autumngale and several of the Eternal and Nighthaven lines. Corwyn added a further 6 wains of weirwood after the Summer Solstice. Once the hall was finished, the Spear of the Seven became available for annual election by the Navarr senators, and could be revoked by the National or Imperial Synod. The hall also opened an adventure for Navarr military units exploring the ruins of Terunael.

Navarr.t: Navarr gained a new national position, the Spear of the Seven, elected each year by its senators. Its military units also gained the chance to explore the ruins of Terunael.

Construct Hall of the Seven.o: In Spring 385YE the Senate commissioned the Hall of the Seven in Miaren, a ministry creating the post of Spear of the Seven, a military counterpart to the Advisor on the Vallorn. Construction was completed with materials and money donated by many citizens.

Miaren.t: The Hall of the Seven was built in Navarr-held Miaren and became the seat of the new Spear of the Seven.

Construct Hall of the Soturi.d: Proposed by Rane Shardbearer, Senator for Kallavesa, and seconded by Delara of the House of the Wanderer, Senator for Zenith, the motion commissioned the Hall of the Soturi as a self-funded project. First suggested by the Mystics of Ishal in answer to a call to action from the Raven Seer, it required 20 wains of white granite, 20 wains of weirwood and 15 thrones in labour, and would take three months to complete. Early contributions after the Autumn Equinox included two wains of white granite and two crowns from individual donors. Once complete, Wintermark can raise a single new army based on the Kallavesi tradition with the fearless quality.

Wintermark.t: Once the hall is complete, Wintermark will be able to raise one new army rooted in the Kallavesi tradition and bearing the unique fearless quality.

Construct Hall of the Soturi.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 388YE to commission the Hall of the Soturi, an edifice in the Kallavesa Marsh that would allow Wintermark to raise a new army with the unique fearless quality.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: The Hall of the Soturi is to be raised in the Kallavesa Marsh, with construction taking three months once the white granite, weirwood and labour costs are met.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa's own senator proposed the edifice, which is to be built on Kallavesi soil and will shape a new army in the territory's mystic tradition.

Construct Hall of the Unbroken.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by Astolat, the motion commissioned a mana sinecure as part of the Proffered Hand Network. Its stated purpose is to provide physical and emotional healing to former slaves and to rehabilitate them into the Way and the Empire. Construction requires 12 wains of mithril, 3 thrones in labour and three months. After the Autumn Equinox, Lady Eleanor Novarion provided the 12 wains of mithril and 2 thrones 6 crowns, and Ergot Di Cevia and Fintan Nighthaven each gave a crown. Once complete, it is intended to provide mana to the Hearthtender of the Unbroken, a title appointed by unanimous decision of Wintermark's senators.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a new sinecure title, the Hearthtender of the Unbroken, which its senators will appoint by unanimous decision and which is intended to receive the Hall's mana once it is built.

Construct Hall of the Unbroken.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 384YE to commission the Hall of the Unbroken, a mana sinecure in the East Floes of Sermersuaq intended to give sanctuary and healing to those who have endured slavery.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: The East Floes is the chosen site for the Hall of the Unbroken, which is due to take three months to build once its materials and labour are supplied.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq's senator proposed the motion, and the territory is to host a sanctuary for former slaves within the Proffered Hand Network.

Construct Happiston Mana Exchange.d: Using the authority of the First Imperial Wayleave, Vivane Knotes announced a 16-wain ministry in Happiston that allows the purchase of mana crystals. Its cost was 16 wains of mithril and 48 crowns, with three months to complete. Morgan Townsend von Holberg met the cost in full after the Spring Equinox 386YE, providing 16 wains of mithril and 6 thrones through the prosperity of Happiston Bakes. With the ministry complete, the new title of Reeve of the Happiston Mana Exchange was to be elected for the first time at the Summer Solstice 386YE by a Tally of the Votes of Marcher farm owners. This first term was a short one, running until the Winter Solstice 386YE.

The Marches.t: The Marches gained a new national title, the Reeve of the Happiston Mana Exchange, chosen annually by a Tally of the Votes of Marcher farm owners. A Marcher, Morgan Townsend von Holberg, funded the whole construction.

Construct Happiston Mana Exchange.o: Vivane Knotes, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, commissioned a mana ministry at Happiston in the Chalkdowns of Mournwold, creating a new Marcher national title, the Reeve of the Happiston Mana Exchange.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: The Happiston Mana Exchange was built in the Chalkdowns and paid for out of the prosperity of Happiston Bakes.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold, held by the Marches, gained a ministry at Happiston where mana crystals can be bought.

Construct Haros Riverpatrol.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by Mournwold, and it passed. The commission cost 15 wains of weirwood and 45 crowns in labour, and would take three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice 387YE, money was donated by Kish of the Flame Beneath the Earth, Triska Markova, Farren Silver Streams, Rhys Nighthaven and others. Caleb of the Cenotaph supplied the 15 wains of weirwood after the Autumn Equinox 388YE, when Kish gave a further throne and seven crowns. Once complete, the sinecure creates the Coursguard title, appointed by a Tally of the Votes of the owners of Highborn congregations.

Highguard.t: Highborn congregation owners will choose the Coursguard by Tally of the Votes once the sinecure is complete, giving Highguard's faithful a new appointed position in Reikos.

Construct Haros Riverpatrol.o: In Winter 387YE the Senate passed a motion to commission the Haros Riverpatrol, a sinecure in Haros Water, Reikos, tied to the opportunity described in the Wind of Fortune "The price is great".

Reikos/Haros Water.t: Haros Water is the site of the Haros Riverpatrol, built with 15 wains of weirwood and 45 crowns of labour over three months.

Reikos.t: The commission placed a new Imperial sinecure, the Haros Riverpatrol, in Highguard-held Reikos, and private donors funded and supplied its construction.

Construct Harps of Astolat.d: The motion took advantage of an existing opportunity to raise a powerful great work in Astolat. Besides the 150 thrones, it required 35 wains of weirwood, 15 wains of mithril and 100 crowns, and took three months to complete. Bohemond De Rondell supplied all of the materials and crowns after the Winter Solstice 381YE. The finished great work means every mana site in Astolat owned by a Dawnish citizen shares an additional 45 crystal mana each season, provided the central harp at Weaving remains unmolested.

Dawn.t: Dawnish citizens who own mana sites in Astolat gain a share of 45 extra crystal mana each season, a project funded through the materials and crowns supplied by Bohemond De Rondell.

Construct Harps of Astolat.o: In Winter 381YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Astolat and seconded by Sarvos, to build the Harps of Astolat, a mana great work in Astolat costing 150 thrones.

Astolat.t: The Harps of Astolat were built here, and every Dawnish-owned mana site in the territory now benefits from them so long as the central harp at Weaving stays unmolested.

Construct Hartford Brewery.d: Using an Imperial Wayleave, Edmund Forster announced in Autumn 386YE that a sinecure called the Hartford Brewery would be built in Hartford in the Stock March region of Upwold. Its holder, the Hartford Brewmaster, would receive 16 wains each season and hold the post in tenure, appointed by the senators of the Marches. Construction required 16 white granite and 48 crowns and took three months. Forster provided 6 thrones after the Autumn Equinox 386YE and 16 wains of white granite after the Winter Solstice 386YE. With the brewery complete, the Brewmaster was due to be appointed for the first time at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

The Marches.t: The Marcher senators gained the right to appoint the Hartford Brewmaster in tenure, a post worth 16 wains a season, with the first appointment due at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

Construct Hartford Brewery.o: Edmund Forster, bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction of the Hartford Brewery, a money-producing sinecure in Hartford, Stock March, Upwold, whose holder is appointed by the Marcher senators.

Upwold/Stock March.t: The Hartford Brewery was built at Hartford in Stock March and was completed after the Winter Solstice 386YE.

Upwold.t: Upwold gained a new money-producing sinecure, the Hartford Brewery, built at Hartford with materials supplied by Edmund Forster.

Construct Healing House of Wittal Grove.d: Proposed by the Senator for Kallavesa and seconded by Mitwold, the motion passed at 328 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Kallavesa. Non-standard costs applied: 56 wains of weirwood and 14 thrones in labour. Vauraus Korppitkotka and Rane Shardbearer each provided 7 thrones and 28 wains of weirwood after the Spring Equinox 384YE. Once completed, the great work will provide a shared bounty to all herb gardens in Kallavesa. The motion omitted the optional Imperial title, Grimnir of Wittal Grove, which was intended to be held by a grimnir. The constitutional court let the commission proceed and raised an administrative motion allowing the Senate to abrogate the title. That motion failed.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a healing great work in its territory of Kallavesa, and its grimnir, who have committed time and resources to the House, keep the intended title Grimnir of Wittal Grove after the Senate declined to abrogate it.

Construct Healing House of Wittal Grove.o: In Winter 383YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Healing House of Wittal Grove, a great work in Wittal Grove, Kallavesa, arising from the All life together wind of fortune and intended to benefit herb garden owners.

Kallavesa/Wittal Grove.t: Wittal Grove is the site of the new Healing House, which was funded through donations of weirwood and thrones after the Spring Equinox 384YE.

Kallavesa.t: Proposed by Kallavesa's own Senator, the Healing House will provide a shared bounty to every herb garden in Kallavesa once it is completed.

Construct High Path to Otkodov.d: Proposed by the senator for Volodmartz and seconded by Karsk, the motion commissioned the high path described in the Pride and Prejudice Wind of Fortune. It required 8 wains of white granite, 2 thrones in labour costs and three months to build. After the Summer Solstice, Kostjya supplied the granite, while Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov contributed money towards the labour. Once the path was completed, the resulting ministry allowed the custodian of the Gift of the Dwindling Star to trade food to the Thule for additional rings of ilium.

Thule.t: The Thule became the Empire's trading partner through the new ministry, receiving food from the custodian of the Gift of the Dwindling Star in exchange for additional rings of ilium.

Construct High Path to Otkodov.o: In Summer 385YE the Senate passed a motion to build a high path through the mountains to Otkodov, opening a ministry through which food could be exchanged for ilium and strengthening northern trade.

Otkodov.t: A new high path was cut through the mountains to Thule-held Otkodov, creating a route for exchanging Imperial food for ilium.

Construct Highwatch Citadel.d: The commission followed a Wind of Fortune offer from a herald of Zakalwe. The offer had expired the previous season, but after the Conclave thanked Zakalwe and voted to accept it, a one-season extension was granted. The work cost 20 wains of white granite, 40 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Summer Solstice Ka'bal provided five thrones and five wains of granite, and fifteen other contributors gave one wain each. Once complete, the expansion would create a new Imperial title, the Polemarch of Highwatch, appointed annually by Urizen's senators. The announcement said it would provide vis and pearls to enchant an army attacking the Druj.

Druj.t: The expanded citadel was promised to supply vis and pearls to enchant an Imperial army attacking the Druj.

Urizen.t: Urizen's senators would gain the power to appoint a new Polemarch of Highwatch each year once the citadel expansion in their territory of Morrow was complete.

Construct Highwatch Citadel.o: In Summer 384YE the Legion Engineer Ka'bal commissioned the expansion of Highwatch Citadel in Altis, Morrow, to make room for heralds of Zakalwe. This took up a time-limited offer from Zakalwe that had been given a one-season extension.

Morrow/Altis.t: Altis is the site of Highwatch Citadel, where three months of construction were commissioned to add rooms for Zakalwe's heralds.

Morrow.t: Highwatch Citadel in Urizen-held Morrow was to be expanded to house heralds of Zakalwe. The work needed 20 wains of white granite, all of which were provided after the Summer Solstice.

Construct Holberg's Melodious Cascade.d: The sinecure cost 10 wains of mithril and 30 crowns of labour and took three months to build. It was self-funded by Bernhard and Lula Kleist von Ennerlund and other League citizens, whose names were to be inscribed near the cascade's entrance; the commission credited Abigail Ashill and Theodora von Holberg as inspiration. Lula Kleist von Ennerlund provided 9 wains of mithril and 3 thrones 6 crowns, and Otmar van Holberg the final wain. The cascade created the post of Director of Holberg's Melodious Cascade, appointed annually by the League's senators and revocable by the Assembly of Nine, the General Assembly and the League National Assembly. The first appointment was due at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

The League.t: The League gained a new national position, the Director of Holberg's Melodious Cascade, appointed annually by its senators and first available at the Winter Solstice 385YE, with League citizens paying for the work themselves.

Construct Holberg's Melodious Cascade.o: In Autumn 385YE the Master of Rings, Laughlan vi Temeschwar, announced the commission of Holberg's Melodious Cascade, a sinecure in Holmauer producing nine mana per season. Funded by League citizens, it was completed with a new League national position attached.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: The Melodious Cascade was built in Holmauer, with the names of the League citizens who supplied its mithril to be inscribed near its entrance.

Holberg.t: Holberg gained a new sinecure, the Melodious Cascade, producing nine mana each season and celebrated by its builders as a tribute to their great city.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the commission was announced by Laughlan vi Temeschwar, the Master of Rings, whose name references the territory.

Construct Holberg's Phantasmagorical Mem.d: As part of completing the restoration of Holmauer Park, Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund used his Imperial Wayleave to announce that the entrepreneurial souvenir stall run by Claude of Holberg, formerly known as 'The Rickety Stall', would become a standard business sinecure. The Kleists of Holberg invested coin and wains in the work. The project cost 5 thrones, beyond the costs set by the opportunity, and took three months to complete. Lula Kleist von Ennerlund provided the 5 thrones after the Winter Solstice 385YE. With the work complete, the title of Financier of Holberg's Phantasmagorical Mementoes can now be appointed by unanimous decision of the League's senators.

The League.t: The League's senators gained a new business title to award, the Financier of Holberg's Phantasmagorical Mementoes, which they must appoint by unanimous decision.

Construct Holberg's Phantasmagorical Mem.o: Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the legitimisation of a souvenir stall in Holmauer Park as "Holberg's Phantasmagorical Mementoes", a new business sinecure created under the In the Garden of Defiance Wind of Fortune.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: In Holmauer Park, Claude of Holberg's makeshift Rickety Stall was turned into the established souvenir business Holberg's Phantasmagorical Mementoes, completing the park's restoration.

Holberg.t: Holberg gained a new business sinecure, built through investment by the Kleists of Holberg as part of the restoration of Holmauer Park.

Construct Home of the Broken Shield.d: Announced in Winter 380YE under the power to commission constructions delegated to the Civilian Commissioner by the Senate, the Home of the Broken Shield is a sinecure producing herbs, sited in Skogei's Glen in Skarsind. It costs 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns in labour, and takes three months to build. Bloodcrow Yargol provided the full weirwood and crowns after the Winter Solstice. Once completed, it will create a new Imperial Orc national title, Broken Shield Guardian. Certain necessary details still had to be settled before construction could begin.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs gain a planned communal home for those of the Broken Shield and, once it is built, a new national title, Broken Shield Guardian, with Bloodcrow Yargol supplying the materials and labour costs.

Construct Home of the Broken Shield.o: The Civilian Commissioner of the Imperial Orcs commissioned the Home of the Broken Shield, a communal home for Imperial Orcs of the Broken Shield, as a herb-producing sinecure in Skogei's Glen, Skarsind.

Skarsind.t: The Home of the Broken Shield is to be built in Skogei's Glen, Skarsind, as a sinecure producing herbs, though some necessary details remained to be settled before work could start.

Construct Honour's Rest.d: Proposed by Kallavesa's senator and seconded by Volodmartz's, the motion would construct the congregational sinecure Honour's Rest in Overton, in the Greensward region of the Mournwold. Once completed it would create the title Friar of Honour's Rest, appointed by the Marcher National Assembly and revocable in the usual way. Wintermark was to fund the work itself as a gift, and Olle Markusson provided 16 wains of white granite and 4 thrones after the Autumn Equinox 381YE. The motion passed in principle, but no construction progress is recorded.

The Marches.t: The Marcher National Assembly would gain the right to appoint the Friar of Honour's Rest once the sinecure in their Mournwold territory is completed.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's people undertook to fund the sinecure themselves as a gift to the Mournwold. Olle Markusson supplied the white granite and thrones, and the senators of Kallavesa and Volodmartz proposed and seconded the motion.

Construct Honour's Rest.o: The Senate passed in principle a motion to build Honour's Rest, a congregational sinecure in Overton in the Mournwold, funded by the people of Wintermark as a gift to the people of the Mournwold. It was meant as a reminder that the Empire makes mistakes and should acknowledge them.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Honour's Rest was to be built at Overton in the Greensward, though no progress on its construction is recorded.

Mournwold.t: The Marcher-held Mournwold was to receive a new congregational sinecure in Overton, given by Wintermark as an acknowledgement that the Empire makes mistakes.

Construct Hordalant spy network.d: The motion called for a spy network in Hordalant, costing 10 weirwood, taking three months to construct and requiring 2 Thrones a season in upkeep from the Senate budget. Caerwyn supplied the 10 wains of weirwood after the Summer Solstice 379YE, and the network was finished shortly before the Autumn Equinox. Imperial citizens could assign military units to it: five units would reveal a map of settlements, ten the armies, naval routes and trading partners, and fifteen the location and size of fortifications. Contributors received the information and a share of the Imperial guerdon. Historical research on Emperor Guntherm's reign recorded a Marcher attempt to capture Hordalant.

Jotun.t: The spy network was built in Jotun-controlled Hordalant, so Imperial units supporting it could uncover the territory's settlements, Jotun armies, naval routes, trading partners and fortifications.

The Marches.t: The motion recalled historical research showing that Marcher forces under Emperor Guntherm once tried to capture Hordalant from the border of Bregasland but stalled after taking Blutgahn and Ashahohn.

Construct Hordalant spy network.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate considered a motion, proposed by Therunin and seconded by Mitwold, to build a spy network based in Jotun-held Hordalant to explore the lands west of the Empire. The network was completed shortly before the Autumn Equinox 379YE.

Hordalant/Blutgahn.t: Mentioned in passing: the historical account notes that Marchers once overran the marshes of Blutgahn during Emperor Guntherm's reign.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Hordalant is described as lying on the border of Bregasland in the historical account cited by the motion.

Hordalant.t: Hordalant became the site of an Imperial spy network, completed before the Autumn Equinox 379YE, through which units could gather intelligence on its settlements, armies, trade and fortifications.

Construct Hounds Hall.d: The motion arose from an opportunity described in the Here comes the night Wind of Fortune. It commissioned the Hounds Hall in Lestasny, Karsk, at a cost of 15 wains of white granite and 45 crowns in labour, with three months needed to complete it. After the Autumn Equinox, Sirka Parakgoosier Bashnya provided 5 thrones, 3 crowns and the full 15 wains of white granite. Anastasiya Lukashovna Volkov contributed a further 2 crowns. Once the hall was finished, the Boyar's Hasta gained the sellsword quality.

Varushka.t: Varushkan citizens funded and supplied the hall, and its completion gave Varushka's new army, the Boyar's Hasta, the sellsword quality.

Construct Hounds Hall.o: In Autumn 387YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Karsk's senator and seconded by Bastion's, to build the Hounds Hall edifice in Ivarsguard, Karsk. The hall let the newly raised Varushkan army, the Boyar's Hasta, use its sellsword quality.

Karsk/Lestasny.t: The Hounds Hall edifice was built in Lestasny from white granite, and its completion granted the Boyar's Hasta the sellsword quality.

Karsk.t: Karsk's senator proposed the motion, and the Hounds Hall was raised in Ivarsguard as a base for the Boyar's Hasta.

Construct House Bourné School of Couture.d: Proposed by the Senator for Sarvos and seconded by Weirwater, the motion drew on an opportunity presented by House Bourné. It was to be funded by the Looking Glass and prosperous Sarvos citizens with help from the Highborn Benefactors, at a non-standard cost of 6 wains of weirwood, 6 wains of white granite and 45 thrones. Magdelena Alanga Di Sarvos provided almost all of it (44 thrones 7 crowns plus all the materials), with Lieselotte van Holberg giving the final crown. The Senator confirmed the Mirrored Maschieri would be a Senate appointment, championing fashion and design across the Empire while a vice-chancellor runs the school day to day.

The League.t: League senators for Sarvos and Weirwater proposed and seconded the folly, and League citizens almost entirely funded it, giving the nation a new Imperial institution of couture and a Senate-appointed champion of fashion.

Construct House Bourné School of Couture.o: In Autumn 383YE the Senate passed a motion to construct the House Bourné School of Couture in Sarvos, a folly creating the Imperial title of the Mirrored Maschieri and opening the way for Sarvos to be rebuilt as the City of Masks.

Sarvos.t: The House Bourné School of Couture is to be built in Sarvos, paid for by its prosperous citizens, offering the chance to rebuild the city as the City of Masks.

Construct House of Barbs.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Miaren, the motion passed at 1 ring. Construction required 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns in labour, with no upkeep. Bloody Trees Rhain Winters Vigil supplied the materials and money after the Autumn Equinox 379YE, and the House of Barbs was completed, leaving the Voice of Barbs to be appointed. The title is normally held for life and grants Synod membership, including the relevant assemblies. In Summer 382YE, after an earlier false start, the Senate commissioned an extension that increased the liao and votes the sinecure provides. The Constitution notes also warned senators against motions of similar verbosity.

Navarr.t: The Navarr national assembly gains the right to elect the Voice of Barbs, a title carrying 12 Synod votes, and the building was funded by the Navarr Bloody Trees Rhain Winters Vigil.

Construct House of Barbs.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate passed a motion to construct the House of Barbs in Hercynia, a sinecure whose title, the Voice of Barbs, is elected by the Navarr national assembly and carries 12 votes in the Imperial Synod.

Hercynia.t: The House of Barbs was built in Hercynia, using white granite and crowns supplied after the Autumn Equinox 379YE, and was later extended in 382YE.

Construct House of Guerra.d: Proposed by the senator for Madruga and seconded by Kahraman, the motion commissioned a great work in Madruga to take advantage of a special opportunity, linked to supporting refugees, to construct a ministry for purchasing liao. It used non-standard costs of 20 wains of white granite and 40 crowns of labour, was self-funded, and takes three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox 383YE, Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra provided 5 thrones and 20 wains of white granite. On completion it will create the Hand of Guerra, a Freeborn national title appointed yearly by the Brass Coast National Assembly and revocable by the National and General Assemblies.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gain a new national position, the Hand of Guerra, appointed yearly by their National Assembly, and Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra personally supplied the white granite and funds for the work.

Construct House of Guerra.o: The Senate passed a motion to commission the House of Guerra, a ministry in Madruga that would allow the purchase of liao, arising from an opportunity to support refugees.

Madruga.t: Madruga is the site of the new House of Guerra, a ministry through which liao can be purchased, proposed by Madruga's own senator.

Construct House of Healing.d: Proposed by the senator for Therunin and seconded by Reikos, the motion aimed to give Imperial heroes access to much-needed magical items and to make Therunin the "Heart of Healing" in the Empire, with the responsibilities required by Ossegrahn. Construction cost 20 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones in labour, and took three months. Many individuals donated money after the Spring Equinox and Summer Solstice, and Raewynn Farkas provided the weirwood in two deliveries of 10 wains. Once the House of Healing was complete, the position of Hand of the Healers became available for the Imperial Conclave to appoint through a Declaration of Candidacy.

Navarr.t: The motion was proposed by the senator for Navarr-held Therunin, and many of the donors who paid for the work bore Navarr names, giving the nation a new ministry on its land.

Construct House of Healing.o: In Spring 385YE the Senate passed a motion to build the House of Healing, a ministry in Therunin described in the Rain King wind of fortune, creating a title appointed by the Imperial Conclave.

Therunin.t: The House of Healing was built in Therunin, and its backers hoped the ministry would make the territory the Heart of Healing in the Empire, bound by the responsibilities Ossegrahn required.

Construct House of Illumination and Ligh.d: Announced by Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, Master of the Koboldi, the commission followed the Out of the Abyss wind of fortune. It created two sinecures: the Architect of Illumination and the Merchant Boyar of the Light Market. It cost 75 wains of white granite and 225 crowns and took six months to build. Bledri and Siân of the Eternal Family in Navarr were thanked for pledging 10 wains. Many citizens gave crowns, thrones and granite between Winter 385YE and Autumn 387YE. Once complete, both titles became available for election for the first time at the Winter Solstice 387YE.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Bledri and Siân of the Eternal Family in Navarr were thanked for pledging 10 wains towards the construction.

Urizen.t: Urizen gained the Architect of Illumination, a new title in Redoubt to be elected by a tally of the votes of Urizen mana site owners, first at the Winter Solstice 387YE.

Varushka.t: A commission announced by Varushka's Master of the Koboldi and largely funded by Varushkan donors gave the nation the Merchant Boyar of the Light Market, elected by Varushkan forest and mine owners, with a shortened first term of three seasons.

Construct House of Illumination and Ligh.o: In Winter 385YE the Master of the Koboldi announced a commission to build the House of Illumination in Cargo, Redoubt, and the Light Market in Essk, Miekarova, creating two Imperial titles. After nearly two years of donations the work was completed after the Autumn Equinox 387YE.

Miekarova.t: The Light Market was built in Essk, Miekarova, and is the seat of the new Merchant Boyar of the Light Market title.

Redoubt.t: The House of Illumination was built in Cargo, Redoubt, and is the seat of the new Architect of Illumination title.

Construct House of the Proffered Hand.d: Proposed by Semmerholm and seconded by the Conscience, the motion commissioned the House of the Proffered Hand at standard cost: 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns in labour, taking three months to build. The motion named Winterbourne, but the civil service then learned this region was wrong. Because work had not begun, an administrative motion was raised at the Autumn Equinox, and the Senate confirmed construction at Caer Faucon, a small town in southern Astolat near the Highguard border. Lady Eleanor Novarion supplied the granite and crowns after the Spring Equinox 383YE. The work created the title Lady of the Proffered Hand, held with tenure.

Dawn.t: Dawn gains a new Imperial title, Lady of the Proffered Hand, held for life and appointed by the Dawn National Assembly, with the sinecure built in the Dawn territory of Astolat.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Caer Faucon, the corrected site of the House, is described as lying in southern Astolat near the Highguard border.

Construct House of the Proffered Hand.o: In Summer 382YE the Senate passed a motion to build the House of the Proffered Hand, a liao sinecure in Astolat whose holder is appointed for life by the Dawn National Assembly. The site, first given as Winterbourne, was later corrected to Caer Faucon.

Astolat/Winterbourne.t: Winterbourne was named as the site in the original motion, but the civil service found this to be an error, and the Senate later confirmed construction at Caer Faucon.

Astolat.t: Astolat gains the House of the Proffered Hand, a liao sinecure finally confirmed at Caer Faucon, a small town in the south of the territory.

Construct Hufi's Garden.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Hahnmark and seconded by Kallavesa. It followed a unanimous greater majority judgement of the Wintermark National Assembly in Autumn 383YE and took up the opportunity described in the All lift together wind of fortune. The garden cost 16 wains of white granite and 32 crowns and would take three months to build. It produces true vervain, bladeroot, imperial roseweald, marrowort and realmsroot. The Woundbinder of the Mark is to inspire Wintermark's grimnir and healers and see that wounded heroes are well tended. The title is to be appointed unanimously by the Wintermark senators, guided by the healers' wishes. Hengest Dun supplied the granite and 4 thrones after the Spring Equinox.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a herb garden and a new national title, the Woundbinder of the Mark, created at the request of its healers and herbalists. The Wintermark senators are to appoint the holder unanimously, and herbalists have pledged up to 67 additional herbs to help save the lives of wounded heroes.

Construct Hufi's Garden.o: The Senate passed a motion, at 80 Thrones, to commission Hufi's Garden, a herb-garden sinecure outside Masi in Kallavesa Marsh that would carry the new Imperial title of Woundbinder of the Mark.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: Hufi's Garden is to be constructed in Kallavesa Marsh outside Masi, taking three months to complete, and will grow medicinal herbs for the Woundbinder of the Mark.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa's senator seconded the motion, and the garden is to be built in the territory outside Masi.

Construct Hylje Dolmen.d: Logan Dunning, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced a self-funded commission for a white granite marker dolmen on the northern shores of the Rikkivessi. It was meant to let the Hylje bring up from the depths the bones of Imperial Orc heroes who fell during the invasion of Sermersuaq while helping to protect Wintermark citizens. The Imperial Orcs would then collect the remains for proper funerary care. The project cost 10 white granite and 30 crowns and took three months. Raal Dunn provided the money and the granite after the Spring Equinox. On completion it created the Custodian of Bones, a position with tenure that the senators of Wintermark can appoint.

Imperial Orcs.t: The dolmen was built so that the bones of Imperial Orc heroes who fell defending Sermersuaq could be recovered from the depths by the Hylje and collected by the Imperial Orcs for proper funerary care.

Wintermark.t: The completed dolmen honours the orcs who died protecting Wintermark citizens, and Wintermark's senators gained the right to appoint the new Custodian of Bones, a position with tenure.

Construct Hylje Dolmen.o: In Spring 387YE the Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, Logan Dunning, announced the construction of a white granite marker dolmen on the northern shores of the Rikkivessi in Sealtoq, so that the Hylje could return the bones of Imperial Orc heroes who fell defending Sermersuaq. The work was completed and created a new position, the Custodian of Bones.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Sealtoq became the site of the white granite marker dolmen where the Hylje deliver recovered orc bones, and it is the seat of the new Custodian of Bones.

Sermersuaq.t: A new sinecure, a white granite dolmen on the northern shores of the Rikkivessi, was built in Sermersuaq to recover the remains of orc heroes who fell during the territory's invasion.

Construct Hyljehal.d: Proposed by the senator for Hahnmark and seconded by the senator for Kallavesa, the motion commissioned a highly effective mana ministry on Rikkivesi as thanks to the Hylje for their help in the war with the Jotun. The title of Mediator of the Hyljehal is to be appointed by the Wintermark senators, bearing in mind the Hylje's request for a Suaq mediator in good standing. The commission used non-standard costs of 12 wains of weirwood and 24 crowns in labour, taking three months to build. Hengest Dunn provided the weirwood and crowns after the Spring Equinox, and on completion the ministry creates the Mediator title.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the hall is described as thanks to the Hylje for their help in the war against the Jotun.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark senators proposed and seconded the motion and will appoint the Mediator of the Hyljehal, with the Hylje asking for a Suaq mediator in good standing.

Construct Hyljehal.o: In Spring 383YE the Senate passed a motion to build Hyljehal, a floating hall for the Hylje on the lake of Rikkivesi in Skymark, creating the Imperial title of Mediator of the Hyljehal.

Kallavesa/Skymark.t: The Hylje floating hall, a mana ministry, is to be constructed on the lake of Rikkivesi in Skymark, with its materials funded after the Spring Equinox.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa's senator seconded the motion, and the new floating hall is to be built on Rikkivesi, within the territory.

Construct Icarion Qanat.d: The motion followed the opportunity described in the Million miles of water wind of fortune. Construction needed 40 wains of weirwood and 144 crowns, a cost raised by Icarion's under-developed state, and took three months. After the Summer Solstice, Irontide Flax gave 30 wains of weirwood and Pathfinder Gaddak gave 2. Karrak, Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven each gave a crown, and small donations added 10 rings. After the Autumn Equinox, Irontide Flax gave a further 8 wains of weirwood, Stonesworn Crix gave 17 thrones, 3 crowns and 10 rings, and Karrak another crown. With the qanat complete, Icarion is no longer arid.

Grendel.t: As one of the nations holding Mareave that season, Grendel shares a territory where a new qanat has ended Icarion's arid condition.

Imperial Orcs.t: As one of the nations holding Mareave that season, the Imperial Orcs share a territory where a new qanat has ended Icarion's arid condition.

Construct Icarion Qanat.o: In Summer 387YE the Senate passed a self-funded motion, proposed by the senator for Mareave and seconded by Zenith, to build the Icarion Qanat in Mareave. Once completed, it removed the arid quality from Icarion.

Mareave/Icarion.t: The qanat was built in Icarion, where its under-developed state raised the cost. Once finished, it removed the region's arid quality.

Mareave.t: Mareave's own senator proposed the qanat, and it now stands in the territory's Icarion region, paid for with weirwood and coin donated by individual citizens.

Construct Imperial Consulate.d: The motion followed the opportunity described in the All the news from Twin Town Wind of Fortune. It passed at 250 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Tassato. The project carried non-standard costs: 25 wains of weirwood, 15 wains of white granite, 80 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Winter Solstice, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato provided 10 thrones along with the full 25 wains of weirwood and 15 wains of white granite. Once the Consulate is complete, the Imperial Consul will receive regular diplomatic briefings and have access to mercantile support similar to that enjoyed by ambassadors.

The League.t: A major Imperial institution was commissioned in a League city at the initiative of Tassato's senator, and the building materials and some funds were supplied by Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato.

Construct Imperial Consulate.o: In Winter 383YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Tassato and seconded by Hercynia, to fund the construction of an Imperial Consulate building in Tassato.

Tassato.t: Tassato was chosen as the site of the new Imperial Consulate, and 250 thrones were disbursed to its senator to build it, with the weirwood and white granite supplied by Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato.

Construct Imperial Cord Brokerage II.d: Proposed by the senator for Miaren and seconded by Karov, the motion commissioned a ministry drawing on an opportunity presented by the broker of Navarr. It used non-standard costs of 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns, with three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox 383YE, Llewellyn Leafstalker provided 3 thrones, 7 crowns, 19 rings and the 16 wains of weirwood, with a further ring in small donations. On completion the brokerage would create a new Imperial title, the Broker of the Invisible Cord, appointed through the Bourse by Navarr owners of herb gardens.

Navarr.t: The ministry grew from an opportunity presented by the broker of Navarr, and its new title, the Broker of the Invisible Cord, would be chosen by Navarr owners of herb gardens through the Bourse.

Construct Imperial Cord Brokerage II.o: The Senate passed a motion to construct the Invisible Cord Brokerage, a weirwood ministry in Seren, Miaren, offering guaranteed prices as a hedge for independent weirwood traders.

Miaren.t: Miaren's senator proposed the motion, and the Invisible Cord Brokerage was to be built in Seren, Miaren, to guarantee prices for independent weirwood traders.

Construct Invisible Cord Brokerage.d: Proposed by the senator for Miaren and seconded by Temeschwar, the motion sought to commission a ministry in Seren drawing on an opportunity presented by the broker of Navarr. The ministry would have offered citizens the option of selling weirwood at a guaranteed price to a trusted broker, as an alternative to the fluctuating prices of the Public Bourse auction. It would have been a National Bourse position. The motion failed, so the Invisible Cord Brokerage was not constructed.

Navarr.t: Navarr's attempt to turn its broker's opportunity into a Navarr-controlled National Bourse ministry for weirwood failed, leaving the nation without the brokerage.

Construct Invisible Cord Brokerage.o: In Spring 383YE the Senate considered a motion to build a Weirwood ministry in Seren, Miaren, as a National Bourse position, but the motion failed.

Miaren.t: Miaren's senator proposed building the weirwood ministry in Seren, but the motion failed and nothing was constructed there.

Construct Iron Confederacy embassy.d: The motion granted permission to build an Iron Confederacy embassy in Sarvos. Its construction was passed at 187 thrones. The standard cost was 25 wains of weirwood and 25 wains of white granite, plus 12 thrones of labour, with one season's construction time and an upkeep of 5 thrones. Miroslav provided the weirwood, granite and labour money after the Spring Equinox 379YE. Once complete, the embassy would automatically create the Imperial title of Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy.

The League.t: The League's senator for Sarvos proposed the embassy, placing the Empire's diplomatic link to the Iron Confederacy within a League territory.

Construct Iron Confederacy embassy.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Sarvos, to construct an embassy to the Iron Confederacy in Sarvos.

Sarvos.t: The Iron Confederacy embassy was to be built in Sarvos, with materials and labour supplied by Miroslav after the Spring Equinox.

Construct Iron Grove.d: Using the authority of an Imperial Wayleave, Wren Ironclaw announced the commissioning of the Iron Grove, a sinecure that produces eighteen herbs each season. Standard costs applied: 10 weirwood and 30 crowns, with three months to complete. After the Spring Equinox 386YE, Wren Ironclaw provided 3 thrones 6 crowns and 10 wains of weirwood to fund it. The Grove was finished, and its title, Keeper of the Iron Grove, is held with tenure. The Wintermark senators can first appoint it, by unanimous decision, at the Summer Solstice 386YE.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's senators gained the power to appoint the Keeper of the Iron Grove with tenure, by unanimous decision, from the Summer Solstice 386YE.

Construct Iron Grove.o: Wren Ironclaw, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction of the Iron Grove, a herb garden sinecure in Skymark, Kallavesa. It was completed, creating the title Keeper of the Iron Grove.

Kallavesa/Skymark.t: Skymark became the site of the completed Iron Grove, a herb garden built with weirwood and crowns provided by Wren Ironclaw.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa gained a new herb garden sinecure, the Iron Grove, which produces eighteen herbs each season.

Construct Iron Qanat.d: Proposed by Tassato and seconded by Kahraman, the motion sought to take advantage of an opportunity presented by settlers from the Isle of Zemress. It was to be overseen by Almodin Oktístis, Priest of the Builder, at a cost of 50 wains of weirwood, 50 wains of white granite and 200 crowns, taking a year to build with upkeep of 10 thrones a season. Once complete, the Iron Qanat and its Water Tower would have let the Brass Coast support an additional army or navy and upgraded Red Plains Farm and the Golden Terraces. However, after the Senate fired the Asavean Architect, construction could not be completed, and the motion lapsed at the start of the Spring Equinox 383YE.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast stood to gain the capacity to support an additional army or navy from the Iron Qanat, but lost that prospect when the Asavean Architect was fired and the commission lapsed unbuilt.

Construct Iron Qanat.o: In Spring 382YE the Senate passed a motion to employ the Asavean Architect to build the fortified Iron Qanat in Segura, but the commission was never completed and lapsed by Spring 383YE.

Segura.t: Segura was to host the fortified Iron Qanat and its protective Water Tower, which would have upgraded Red Plains Farm and the Golden Terraces, but construction was never completed there.

Construct Iron Qanat II.d: Proposed by Segura's senator and seconded by Sarvos, the motion set non-standard costs of 50 wains of weirwood and 100 crowns, with no upkeep and three months to build. It was self-funded: Alexios i Zemress i Riqueza provided the weirwood and crowns after the Summer Solstice. Although the motion named Yellow Chase, the Iron Qanat was built in the Sobral Grasses, as the Zemress islanders who provided the opportunity had proposed. The basic Iron Qanat allows the Brass Coast to support an additional army or navy, and the Red Plains Farm and the Golden Terraces would immediately be upgraded by a level if in Imperial hands.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gained the capacity to support an additional army or navy and better supply for their existing forces, funded by Alexios i Zemress i Riqueza.

Construct Iron Qanat II.o: In Summer 383YE the Senate passed a motion to commission the Iron Qanat, a great work in Segura that would let the Freeborn support an additional army and secure supply for their existing ones, taking advantage of an opportunity offered by settlers from the Isle of Zemress.

Segura/Sobral Grasses.t: The Iron Qanat was ultimately built in the Sobral Grasses, as proposed by the Zemress islanders who provided the opportunity.

Segura/Yellow Chase.t: The motion named Yellow Chase as the site for the Iron Qanat, but the great work was built in the Sobral Grasses instead.

Segura.t: Segura's senator proposed the great work, which was built in the territory and would upgrade the Red Plains Farm and the Golden Terraces by a level if they were in Imperial hands.

Construct Iron Roads.d: The motion passed at 100 thrones, with non-standard costs of 200 wains of white granite and 400 crowns of labour, one year of construction and one Senate commission. Between Autumn 383YE and Winter 384YE, Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov supplied most of the granite and money, with further contributions from Lieselotte van Holberg, Tomasz, Vesna Borkovna Prochnost and Borz nikoli strazkovitch. Once complete, the roads would act as a great work in Miekarova, Karov and Volodmartz. They would also add 2 wains a season to the Eternal Shafts of Time, the Hunt of Alderei the Fair, the Granites of Veltsgorsk and the Night Quarry while the roads stayed open. Completing them might open further industrial opportunities across the north-east.

The League.t: If the roadbuilding projects were completed, more Varushkan materials could flow to Temeschwar, possibly giving the League an opportunity to expand the Assayer's Guild.

Varushka.t: Varushka gains a major road network linking isolated vales. The roads promise a great work in three of its territories, better output from several Bourse resources, and possible future investment in its industrial might, largely funded by Varushkans such as Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov.

Construct Iron Roads.o: In Autumn 383YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Ossium and seconded by the senator for Miekarova, to build the Iron Roads across Varushka using skilled Varushkan roadbuilders.

Karov.t: Once completed, the Iron Roads would serve as a form of great work in Karov.

Karsk.t: Completing the grand roadbuilding projects could bring easier access to the mines of Karsk as a future opportunity.

Miekarova.t: The senator for Miekarova seconded the motion, and once completed the Iron Roads would serve as a form of great work in the territory.

Temeschwar.t: The completed roads might send more materials flowing to Temeschwar, offering a possible opportunity to expand the Assayer's Guild there.

Volodmartz.t: Once completed, the Iron Roads would serve as a form of great work in Volodmartz.

Construct Iron Roundtower.d: Using an Imperial Wayleave, Dragomir Dragovich announced a commission to build the Iron Roundtower, a mithril ministry in Delev near Temeschwar. The commission takes up an opportunity to create such a ministry in Varushka. Its non-standard costs were 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns, with three months needed to complete it. Dragomir provided both the mithril and the crowns after the Summer Solstice of 383YE. Once finished, the ministry will create the title Bargainer of the Iron Tower, a Varushkan national position. It will also affect the amount of mithril going to the public bourse auction at Anvil.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Roundtower is described as being built in Delev near Temeschwar, a city held by the League.

Varushka.t: Varushka is to gain a mithril ministry and a new national position, the Bargainer of the Iron Tower, funded by the Varushkan Dragomir Dragovich.

Construct Iron Roundtower.o: Dragomir Dragovich, bearing an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction of the Iron Roundtower, a Varushkan ministry dealing in mithril, in Delev near Temeschwar. He supplied the materials and money after the Summer Solstice of 383YE.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar is named as the landmark near which the Iron Roundtower is to be built in Delev.

Construct Jarmish Docks.d: The senator for Kallavesa proposed the motion and the senator for Redoubt seconded it. It called for docks in Cargo, designed by the Asavean Architect, where weirwood could be bought from Jarm. Construction cost 15 wains of weirwood, 15 wains of white granite and 60 crowns in labour, and was to take three months. Olle Markusson supplied all of these after the Winter Solstice. The motion lacked some necessary details, which Senator Kallavesa was allowed to decide. Once completed, the docks created the title Prime Factor of the Pallas Docks.

Urizen.t: Urizen's territory of Redoubt gained a ministry for trading with Jarm for weirwood, and its senator seconded the motion that built it.

Construct Jarmish Docks.o: In Winter 380YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Jarmish Weirwood docks in Cargo, Redoubt: a ministry for buying weirwood from Jarm, to be designed by the Asavean Architect.

Redoubt.t: The Jarmish Weirwood docks were to be built at Cargo in Redoubt, giving the territory a ministry for buying weirwood from Jarm and, once complete, the new title Prime Factor of the Pallas Docks.

Construct Jarmish Embassy.d: Proposed by Sermersuaq's senator and seconded by Upwold's, the motion carried in principle 27–0 and passed at 40 Thrones by 23–4; a 45 Throne cost failed. The non-standard cost of 20 white granite and 20 weirwood was provided by Atte, Senator for Sermersuaq, after the Summer Solstice 378YE. Although the embassy was built in Cargo, the House of Princes refused to name an ambassador until the Senate chose which Jarmish port would host the reciprocal Imperial embassy. The embassy is a ministry letting its Imperial operator buy crystal mana, dragonbone, ambergelt, green iron, iridescent gloaming, cerulean mazzarine and marrowort. Oswi Twice-Burned was appointed Ambassador to Jarm at the Autumn Equinox 378YE.

Urizen.t: The Jarmish embassy was built on Urizen land at Cargo in Redoubt, giving the nation's territory a new diplomatic and trading link with the Principalities of Jarm.

Construct Jarmish Embassy.o: In Winter 377YE the Senate passed a motion at 40 Thrones to construct an embassy for the Principalities of Jarm in Cargo, Redoubt. It was later completed and became a trading ministry.

Redoubt.t: Cargo in Redoubt became the site of the Jarmish embassy, a ministry through which rare materials such as dragonbone, ambergelt and crystal mana can be bought.

Construct Jarmish Jewellers.d: Proposed by Temeschwar and seconded by Kahraman, the motion would have commissioned a fortified premises in Seren for the Kobarid family of Jarm to sell glazamy neba, their magical jewellery, to Imperial customers, following an offer by the Jarmish Magician-Prince Matvei Kobarid. It was to be self-funded at a non-standard cost of 8 wains of white granite, 4 wains of mithril and 24 crowns, taking three months to complete. The resulting Imperial title, a liaison appointed by open auction on the Bourse, would have been able to buy up to three pieces of rare jewellery each season at a bargain price. No progress was made, and the motion was abrogated at the Winter Solstice 382YE.

Navarr.t: The Navarr territory of Miaren was to host a Jarmish jewellery exchange, giving Imperial buyers access to Kobarid magical jewellery, but the project was abrogated before construction began.

Construct Jarmish Jewellers.o: In Autumn 382YE the Senate passed in principle a motion to construct the Jarmish Star Jewellery exchange in Seren, Miaren, but the motion was abrogated at the Winter Solstice 382YE before anything was built.

Miaren.t: Seren in Miaren was chosen as the site for a fortified Jarmish Star Jewellery exchange run by the Kobarid family, but the commission was abrogated at the Winter Solstice 382YE with no progress made.

Construct Jarmish trade hub in Tassato.d: The motion, put forward by the senator for Tassato and seconded by the senator for Holberg, authorised a trade hub for merchants from the Principalities of Jarm who wanted access to the mana exchange in the city of Enterio. It passed in Winter 380YE. The cost is not recorded and was met by the Jarmish traders themselves rather than the Imperial treasury. The work was completed shortly before the Spring Equinox of 381YE, and the Jarmish traders now have a lodge in Enterio, Tassato.

The League.t: A League city gained a permanent foreign trading presence, with Jarmish merchants building and paying for their own lodge to reach Enterio's mana exchange.

Construct Jarmish trade hub in Tassato.o: In Winter 380YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Tassato's senator and seconded by Holberg's, to build a trade hub in Enterio for Jarmish traders wishing to use the city's mana exchange.

Tassato/Enterio.t: The Jarmish lodge was built in the city of Enterio and finished shortly before Spring Equinox 381YE, giving Jarmish traders a base beside the city's mana exchange.

Tassato.t: Tassato's senator proposed the motion, and the territory now hosts a lodge where Jarmish traders base their dealings with the mana exchange in Enterio.

Construct Jonas' Legacy.d: The tower serves as the residence of the Emerald Arcanist, whose role is to advise the Vallornguard on magical matters and monitor the border with Brocéliande. The holder receives nine mana crystals each season, distilled from a network of mithril bowls built into the tower. The title is Imperial and is elected annually in Autumn by majority vote of the Vallornguard. The motion directed that the Castellan of Spiral Castle pay the costs: 10 mithril and 30 crowns, with three months to complete. Tallis Hart provided 10 wains of mithril and 3 thrones 6 crowns after the Summer Solstice. The first Emerald Arcanist could be appointed at the Autumn Equinox 387YE.

Dawn.t: Dawn gained a new magical tower and Imperial title in its territory of Semmerholm, chosen by the Vallornguard, whose magical advice and watch on the Brocéliande border it strengthens.

The League.t: The motion directed the Castellan of Spiral Castle, in the League's territory of Spiral, to pay the tower's costs.

Construct Jonas' Legacy.o: In Summer 387YE Bertrand, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced a Senate commission to build a tower called Jonas' Legacy in Elvette, Semmerholm. It was completed and created the Imperial title of Emerald Arcanist.

Semmerholm/Elvette.t: Jonas' Legacy was built in Elvette, with a network of mithril bowls distilling mana for the Emerald Arcanist who lives there.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: the Emerald Arcanist is charged with monitoring the border with Brocéliande, which the Vallorn held at the time.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm became home to Jonas' Legacy, a tower that produces nine mana crystals each season for the Emerald Arcanist who keeps watch on its border with Brocéliande.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the costs of the tower were to be paid by the Castellan of Spiral Castle.

Construct Journeymage Towers.d: Proposed by Semmerholm's senator and seconded by Karov's, the motion answered the Less welcome tenants wind of fortune. It cost 24 white granite, 72 crowns and three months to complete, and 60 thrones were disbursed to the Senator for Semmerholm. The Wisdom Assembly backed it through a mandate enacted by Kalina Jadwigowna Piosnkowa Prochnost. Many citizens contributed after the Summer Solstice, including Triska Markova, Amicia of the Semmerlak, and Varushkan, League and Dawn citizens. Once the towers were complete, the threat to Semmerlak ships was resolved and the Wavewatchers sodality was firmly established. The Senate then created the title of Watcher of the Semmerlak at the Autumn Equinox 386YE.

Dawn.t: Dawn's senator for Semmerholm proposed the motion and received the funds, and Dawn citizens gave 6 crowns and 2 wains of white granite towards the towers protecting Semmerlak shipping.

Varushka.t: Varushka hosted two of the three towers, in Karov and Ossium. Karov's senator seconded the motion, and Varushkans such as Triska Markova and other citizens supplied much of the granite and coin.

Construct Journeymage Towers.o: In Summer 386YE the Senate passed a motion to build Journeymage Towers, follies in Lacre (Semmerholm), Malimorzi (Karov) and Bittershore (Ossium), to remove the threat Dho'uala posed to shipping on the Semmerlak.
