Karov/Malimorzi.t: Malimorzi became the site of one of the three Journeymage Towers that together removed the danger posed by Dho'uala.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: Bittershore received one of the Journeymage Towers, helping to secure the Semmerlak's waters for shipping.

Karov.t: Karov's senator seconded the motion, and a Journeymage Tower was built in its Malimorzi region to guard ships from Dho'uala.

Ossium.t: A Journeymage Tower was raised in Ossium's Bittershore region as part of the network that ended the threat to Semmerlak shipping.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm's senator proposed the motion and received the 60 thrones, and a tower was built in Lacre, ending the Dho'uala threat to ships on the Semmerlak.

Construct Kallavesa Marshways.d: Proposed by Delara of the House of the Wanderer, Senator for Zenith, and seconded by Rane Shardbearer, Senator for Kallavesa, the motion passed. The work required 80 wains of weirwood and 30 thrones in labour, taking six months to complete; Gisli i Phovas i Guerra provided the full materials and money after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the marshways raise investment in Kallavesa's businesses by one level (an additional 36 rings) and its herb gardens by one level, yielding extra herbs each season, and create a guarding venture in which Wintermark and Dawnish military units protect merchants using the marshways in exchange for herbs.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a great work in one of its territories that enriches its businesses and herb gardens there, and its military units become eligible to guard the marshways' merchants in exchange for herbs, alongside Dawnish units.

Construct Kallavesa Marshways.o: In Autumn 388YE the Senate passed a motion to commission the Kallavesa Marshways, a great work in Kallavesa intended to boost local businesses and herb gardens and create a guarding venture for military units.

Kallavesa.t: The marshways are built in Kallavesa, raising investment in its businesses and herb gardens by one level each once complete, and bringing merchant traffic guarded by Wintermark and Dawnish soldiers.

Construct Kalpaheim Tradehall.d: Proposed by the senator for Hahnmark and seconded by Kallavesa, the motion commissioned a trade hall in Kalpaheim in line with a recent proposal. The commission used non-standard costs of 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns, with three months needed to complete it. Hengest Dunn provided the weirwood and the crowns after the Spring Equinox 383YE. The completed hall is a ministry that creates a new title, the Kalpaheim Tradeholder, and it is described as a very productive tradehall tied into the Northern Trade Network.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's artisans and traders, who requested the hall, gained a productive ministry linked to the Northern Trade Network, along with the new title of Kalpaheim Tradeholder.

Construct Kalpaheim Tradehall.o: In Winter 382YE the Senate passed a motion to commission the Kalpaheim Tradehall, a ministry connected to the Northern Trade Network and requested by the artisans and traders of Wintermark.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark's senator proposed the motion, and the Kalpaheim Tradehall was to be built within the territory as a ministry connected to the Northern Trade Network.

Construct Kauppahall.d: The senator for Hahnmark proposed the motion and Skarsind seconded it. It followed the Apples from a tree Wind of Fortune. Kauppahall cost 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns in labour, took three months to build, and was passed at 84 thrones, which were disbursed to the senator for Hahnmark. Hengest Dun supplied the weirwood and 4 thrones after the Winter Solstice. The motion said Wintermark senators would appoint the title unanimously, but the Constitutional Court ruled this unconstitutional because the role mainly concerns acquiring bourse resources. The Court raised an administrative motion to have the Talon appointed by Tally of the Votes, and it passed. The hall was due to be finished shortly before the Spring Equinox 384YE.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a new trading hall and the title of Talon of Kauppahall, though its senators lost the unanimous right to appoint it once the Court required appointment through the bourse by Tally of the Votes.

Construct Kauppahall.o: In Winter 383YE the Senate passed a motion to build Kauppahall, a trading hall in Hahnmark, along with a new title, the Talon of Kauppahall, which allows the purchase of white granite and a small amount of ilium.

Hahnmark.t: Kauppahall was built in Hahnmark at its own senator's proposal, using weirwood and thrones provided by Hengest Dun, and was due for completion shortly before the Spring Equinox 384YE.

Construct Kennels of Hay.d: Proposed by the senator for Mitwold and seconded by Upwold, the motion created the title of 'Kennelmaster of Hay's Home for Wayward Dogs', a money sinecure in Hay, Mitwold. It cost 10 wains of white granite and 30 crowns in labour and took three months to complete. The Carefoot and Shaw Trading Company undertook to fund it, and after the Autumn Equinox Coal Carefoot provided 3 thrones 6 crowns and the 10 wains of white granite. With the work complete, the Kennelmaster of Hay can be appointed by unanimous decision of the senators of the Marches, for the first time at the Winter Solstice 387YE, and holds the post with tenure.

The Marches.t: The Marches gained a new money sinecure whose holder, the Kennelmaster of Hay, is appointed with tenure by unanimous decision of the Marcher senators. It was proposed by Mitwold's senator, seconded by Upwold's, and funded by Marcher traders Carefoot and Shaw.

Construct Kennels of Hay.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 387YE to construct a money sinecure, the Kennels of Hay, in Golden Downs, Mitwold, self-funded by the Carefoot and Shaw Trading Company.

Mitwold/Golden Downs.t: Golden Downs is where the Kennels of Hay, 'Hay's Home for Wayward Dogs', were built, completed in time for the first Kennelmaster to be appointed at the Winter Solstice 387YE.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold's senator proposed the motion, and the new kennels and their sinecure were built within the territory at Hay.

Construct Kespoena's Nadir.d: Proposed by Aurianna du Meravon, Senator for Semmerholm, and seconded by Ismene of the Scarlet Guard, Senator for Morrow, the motion commissioned a new mithril seat at Kespoena's Nadir in Occursion. It cost 300 thrones in labour with 10 thrones a season upkeep, and took three months rather than six because of the existing exploits under Kespoena's Reach. Funding came from five donors giving just over 50 thrones each, 48 thrones from the Kespoena's Reach exploits, and two smaller one-crown gifts after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, an administrative motion was to be raised to allocate the bourse resource.

Urizen.t: Urizen gains a new mithril seat within its own territory of Zenith, building on the existing workings at Kespoena's Reach.

Construct Kespoena's Nadir.o: The Senate passed a motion to build Kespoena's Nadir, a new mithril seat in Occursion in Zenith, exploiting a fresh mithril vein uncovered by the Argent Sword.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Occursion is where the new mithril vein was uncovered and where Kespoena's Nadir was built, with work speeded by the nearby exploits under Kespoena's Reach.

Zenith.t: Zenith becomes home to a second mithril seat, Kespoena's Nadir, which will add to the Empire's mithril supply once its bourse allocation is decided.

Construct Ketsov Trade Exchange.d: Announced in Spring 383YE under an Imperial Wayleave by Irina Vasileva Dukov, the ministry draws on an opportunity presented by the people of Ketsov and will allow the purchase of magical weapons and armour. It uses non-standard costs: 8 wains of white granite, 8 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns in labour, taking three months to build. Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov provided all the materials and crowns after the Spring Equinox. When complete, it will create the Imperial title Burgher of Ketsov, a Varushkan National Bourse position appointed annually by the votes of Varushkan mine and forest owners.

Varushka.t: Varushkan mine and forest owners will gain a new National Bourse title, the Burgher of Ketsov, chosen annually by their vote, and the full costs were met by Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov.

Construct Ketsov Trade Exchange.o: Irina Vasileva Dukov, bearing an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction of a trading exchange ministry in the town of Ketsov in Galath Fields, Ossium, to sell magical weapons and armour.

Ossium/Galath Fields.t: The Ketsov Trade Exchange ministry is to be constructed in Galath Fields over three months, drawing on an opportunity offered by the people of Ketsov.

Ossium.t: A new trading exchange is to be built in the town of Ketsov in Ossium, offering magical weapons and armour for sale.

Construct Kleist's Winter Gardens.d: The commission followed the In the garden of defiance wind of fortune. Marcher menhirs would turn the lingering Winter curse on Holmauer Park to growing herbs. Kleist von Ennerlund, Vintners and Victuallers of Holberg, offered to fund it themselves, and after the Winter Solstice 384YE Lula Kleist von Ennerlund provided 15 wains of weirwood, 15 wains of white granite and 3 thrones 6 crowns. The work took three months. It was finished once work on Holberg's Melodious Cascade was complete. The new Imperial title, Tender of Kleist's Winter Gardens, is appointed annually by Imperial Bourse auction, which brings coin into the Senate budget. It was to be auctioned for the first time at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

The League.t: A League family, Kleist von Ennerlund, paid for the gardens out of its own resources, framing it as an act of loyalty to the Empire and to their beloved city of Holberg.

Construct Kleist's Winter Gardens.o: Using the authority of an Imperial Wayleave, Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund announced the construction of Kleist's Winter Gardens at the Holberg University Duelling Grounds in Winter 384YE. The commission was a herb-producing sinecure that channels the Winter magic Skathe the Hag Queen left on Holmauer Park.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Skathe's Winter curse on Holmauer Park is put to use, with Marcher menhirs channelling its magic to grow herbs in the new Winter Gardens.

Holberg.t: Holberg gains a new herb-producing sinecure at its University Duelling Grounds, turning the scars of the Hag Queen's attack into a resource under the defiant cry "Holberg Endures!"

Construct Kobarid Jewelers.d: Proposed by Temeschwar and seconded by Madruga, the motion sought to build a ministry in Miaren from which the Kobarid family of Jarm would sell glazamy neba to Imperial customers. The opportunity arose from an offer by the Jarmish Magician-Prince Matvei Kobarid and was raised again after an earlier motion to build the jewellers was abrogated. The project would have cost 8 White Granite, 4 Mithril and 24 Crowns, to be self-funded, and would have created the title of Star Jeweler, appointed by Imperial Bourse auction. The motion failed.

Navarr.t: Navarr would have hosted a Jarmish-run jewellery exchange and the new Star Jeweler title on its land, but the motion failed and nothing was built.

Construct Kobarid Jewelers.o: A Senate motion to commission the Jarmish Jewellery Exchange, a fortified premises for the Kobarid family of Jarm in Miaren, Navarr, failed in Winter 382YE.

Miaren.t: Miaren was the proposed site of the fortified Jarmish Jewellery Exchange, but the failed motion meant no construction took place there.

Construct Kostjyas Respite.d: The commission followed the Thousands or more Wind of Fortune. It cost 30 wains of white granite, 30 wains of weirwood and 144 crowns, raised from 120 because Ossium was under-developed, and took six months to build. Kostjya, Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov and others supplied the money and materials after the Autumn Equinox and Winter Solstice 384YE. The town occupies the cove from which the Druj once launched rafts against Semmerholm. Once complete, it removes the Bittershore's under-developed quality and adds 20 thrones a season in taxes, spread across the Semmerlak territories. It also creates the title of Merchant-boyar of Bittershore and opens opportunities to expand docks around the lake.

Dawn.t: Once the port was complete, an option would be offered to expand the docks at Lacre in Dawn's territory of Semmerholm, and Dawn's Semmerlak lands would share in the increased taxation.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the new town occupies the cove from which the Druj launched rafts to attack Semmerholm during Empress Varkula's reign.

The League.t: The new port might later allow a similar dock in Holberg's Misericorde or Utterlund, spreading Holberg's wealth across the Semmerlak.

Varushka.t: A Varushkan project, self-funded by Cabal Lyktan and Varushkan contributors. It developed Ossium's Bittershore, created a new Merchant-boyar title and opened dock opportunities at Korotny and Ivarsgard.

Construct Kostjyas Respite.o: Kostjya of Cabal Lyktan, bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, commissioned the port-town of Kostjyas Respite on the Bittershore in Ossium, on the shores of the Semmerlak. Cabal Lyktan and the people of Varushka pledged to fund it entirely themselves.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Once Kostjyas Respite was complete, a similar dock might be built in Misericorde, linking it to trade across the Semmerlak.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Once Kostjyas Respite was complete, a similar dock might be built in Utterlund, linking it to trade across the Semmerlak.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: Kostjyas Respite was built here, removing the Bittershore's under-developed quality and creating the Merchant-boyar of Bittershore to oversee the port's prosperity.

Holberg.t: Once the port was complete, there would be a possibility of building a similar dock in Misericorde or Utterlund, letting Holberg's wealth spread across the Semmerlak.

Karov.t: The completed port would open an option to expand the docks at Korotny in Karov, and Karov would share in the extra taxation from the Semmerlak.

Karsk.t: The completed port would open an option to expand the docks at Ivarsgard in Karsk, which would also share in the new Semmerlak taxation.

Ossium.t: Ossium gained the new port-town of Kostjyas Respite on the Bittershore, which cost extra crowns to build because the territory was under-developed.

Semmerholm.t: The town stands in the cove once used by the Druj to raid Semmerholm, and its completion would open an option to expand the docks at Lacre.

The Semmerlak.t: The new port on the lake's shores would raise Imperial taxation by 20 thrones a season, spread among the territories bordering the Semmerlak, and encourage further docks around it.

Construct Kragg's Hollow.d: Kragg's Hollow was a mana sinecure built in Skarsind at a cost of 10 wains of mithril, plus 20 crowns in labour and three months of construction. The announcement said it was funded with the prosperity of Ashborn Kragg, with thanks to the Imperial Spymaster. After the Spring Equinox 385YE, Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad provided the 10 wains of mithril and Kostjya provided 2 thrones 4 crowns. Once construction was completed, the new title of Scholar of Kragg's Hollow became available for appointment by the Imperial Conclave using a Declaration of Candidacy.

Imperial Orcs.t: The new mana sinecure was raised in Skarsind, a territory the Imperial Orcs held at the time, adding a Conclave-appointed magical title within their lands.

Construct Kragg's Hollow.o: In Spring 385YE the Arcane Architect, Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad, announced the construction of Kragg's Hollow, a mana sinecure in Skarsind. With construction complete, it created the Imperial title Scholar of Kragg's Hollow, appointed through the Imperial Conclave.

Skarsind.t: Kragg's Hollow was built in Skarsind as a mana sinecure, and the territory became the seat of the new Imperial title Scholar of Kragg's Hollow.

Construct Kruidenkenner warehouse.d: Proposed by the Necropolis senator and seconded by Casinea's, the motion passed at 40 Thrones. It used non-standard costs of 8 wains of weirwood and 16 crowns of labour, and Thanmir Hrafnar supplied both after the Spring Equinox. When complete, the ministry creates the Imperial title of Kruidenkenner Trademaster, appointed by public auction through the Imperial Bourse. The senator asked that it be called "The Kruidenkenner magazijn" and that the appointment take place in Spring. The Civil Service agreed a Spring appointment was appropriate but noted the motion could not stipulate it. If Spring is set, the first auction will follow completion for a short term.

Highguard.t: Highguard's senator for Necropolis proposed the motion, which brings a new trade ministry and its Imperial title onto Highborn-held land at Crown's Quay.

Construct Kruidenkenner warehouse.o: In Spring 382YE the Senate passed a motion to commission a warehouse ministry at Crown's Quay in Necropolis. It was intended to let the Empire buy Cerulean Mazzarine from the Kruidenkenner herbalists of the Sarcophan Delves.

Necropolis.t: Crown's Quay in Necropolis is the chosen site for the Kruidenkenner warehouse, which will give the Empire access to Cerulean Mazzarine from Sarcophan Delves herbalists.

Construct Kurstrozi's Lumbermill.d: Framed as making use of unused wealth in hard times, the commission was announced by the Master of the Koboldi. The announcement said it would be fully funded by Krasivit Buhkova. It required 40 wains of white granite and 15 thrones, plus standard costs, and would take three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox, Oleinsky Kasprzak provided the 40 wains of white granite and 13 thrones 6 crowns. Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn, Kostjya and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov gave smaller sums of crowns. Once built, the lumbermill will distribute a share of 20 random materials to the Varushkan forest owners of Ossium.

Varushka.t: A Varushkan great work commissioned by the Master of the Koboldi and funded by Varushkan contributors, it will benefit the nation's forest owners in Ossium with a share of 20 random materials.

Construct Kurstrozi's Lumbermill.o: Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, Master of the Koboldi, commissioned Kurstrozi's Lumbermill in Drownbark, Ossium, in Autumn 385YE: a great work meant to increase the prosperity of Ossium's forests.

Ossium.t: Kurstrozi's Lumbermill is to be built at Drownbark to increase the prosperity of Ossium's forests, sharing 20 random materials among the Varushkan forest owners there.

Construct Landskeeper's Study.d: Proposed by the senator for Upwold and seconded by Redoubt, the motion took up the opportunity presented by the Thresher's Summer wind of fortune. The ministry cost 12 wains of white granite and 36 crowns in labour and was self-funded by prosperous Marcher citizens: John Fisher provided 4 thrones 3 crowns and 6 wains of white granite, Watkin 6 wains of white granite, and Farren Silver Streams 1 crown. Construction took three months. The Keeper of the Study is charged with spreading knowledge of the magical arts used to enchant farms, and is appointed annually by unanimous vote of the Marcher senators, first at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

The Marches.t: The Marches gained a new national position, the Keeper of the Study, appointed each year by unanimous vote of its senators to spread knowledge of farm enchantment, with the building paid for by its own prosperous citizens.

Construct Landskeeper's Study.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 386YE to build the Landskeeper's Study, a mana ministry in Oakwood, Ashbrook, Upwold, creating the Marcher title of Keeper of the Study.

Upwold/Ashbrook.t: The Landskeeper's Study was built at Oakwood in Ashbrook, making the region the seat of Marcher efforts to teach the magic of enchanting farms.

Upwold.t: Upwold's senator proposed the motion, and the territory became home to the newly built Landskeeper's Study mana ministry.

Construct Laroc Tournament Grounds.d: The motion passed at 50 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Astolat. The work required 40 wains of weirwood, 10 thrones and three months. Ren Tanner and Guy Grimbold-Antenucci each supplied weirwood after the Winter Solstice 384YE and again after the Spring Equinox 385YE, and Ren Tanner also provided the 10 thrones. Once complete, the grounds would act as a great work giving every business in Astolat a share of 743 rings. In the season of completion, the Castellan of Spiral Castle could raise up to a dozen Dawnish-owned military units to rank 2. For a year afterwards, Dawnish units could be upgraded for one wain of mithril less. The Senator for Astolat would choose the grounds' colours and decorations.

Dawn.t: Dawn stood to gain a grand tourney ground in Astolat, with up to a dozen Dawnish-owned military units upgraded to rank 2 through the Castellan of Spiral Castle, and cheaper mithril upgrades for Dawnish units for a year.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the page names only the Castellan of Spiral Castle and says nothing about Grendel or its people.

Construct Laroc Tournament Grounds.o: In Winter 384YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the Senator for Astolat and seconded by Tassato, to build the tournament grounds of Laroc in Astolat, as set out in the Good old smooth red wine wind of fortune.

Astolat.t: The Laroc tournament grounds were to be built in Astolat, giving every business in the territory a share of 743 rings once complete, with the Senator for Astolat choosing their colours and decorations.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the only link is the title of the Castellan of Spiral Castle, who would choose which Dawnish units were upgraded; nothing happens in the territory of Spiral itself.

Construct Last Battle Wayhouse.d: Proposed by Hercynia and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion followed the opportunity in the wind of fortune The way home. The wayhouse cost 18 wains of weirwood and 54 crowns and took three months to build, with materials and money given by Dax, Corwyn Heartsbane, Aneira Exiles End and others after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the new Keeper of the Last Battle title could be appointed annually by unanimous decision of the generals of Navarr, first at the Winter Solstice 386YE. Nesustak Forest and Turan Flats in Sarangrave gained the under threat quality. Navarri characters can now hold personal resources in the Barrens, and the Barrens' seasonal taxation rises by one throne.

Druj.t: The wayhouse was built expressly as a tool against the Druj, giving the Empire reconnaissance into their territory of Sarangrave and leaving two of its regions under threat.

Navarr.t: The generals of Navarr gain the right to appoint the Keeper of the Last Battle unanimously, and Navarri characters can now hold personal resources in the Barrens, benefiting from great works there.

Construct Last Battle Wayhouse.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 386YE to build the Last Battle Wayhouse in the Bleaks, the Barrens, to provide reconnaissance into Druj-held Sarangrave; it was completed after donations of weirwood and money.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: Nesustak Forest gained the under threat quality once the Last Battle Wayhouse was completed.

Sarangrave/Turan Flats.t: Turan Flats gained the under threat quality once the Last Battle Wayhouse was completed.

Sarangrave.t: Druj-held Sarangrave is now watched from the new wayhouse across the border, and two of its regions have gained the under threat quality.

Construct Legacy of Wisdom.d: Announced under an Imperial Wayleave in Summer 382YE, the great work was to cost 40 wains of mithril and 80 crowns of labour, taking three months, and was funded by 'La Volpe' and the Bloody Butchers of Temeschwar. Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar provided 40 wains of mithril and 10 thrones after the Summer Solstice. The Druj invasion of Morrow then destroyed the construction site of the central stellae and several smaller stellae, so all progress was lost and Lorenzo received a partial refund. If Caeli were recaptured before the Summer Solstice 383YE, work could restart from scratch without a new motion or commission. Completed, it would have distributed 37 crystal mana between Morrow's mana sites.

Druj.t: The Druj invasion of Morrow destroyed the construction site, wiping out all progress on the great work.

The League.t: League citizens, Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar with 'La Volpe' and the Bloody Butchers of Temeschwar, funded the work with mithril and thrones, but saw their investment lost and only partly refunded.

Urizen.t: Urizen stood to gain a great work spreading 37 crystal mana across Morrow's mana sites, but lost it to the Druj invasion unless Caeli is recaptured before Summer 383YE.

Construct Legacy of Wisdom.o: Edmundo, bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced a great work in Morrow, 'Lorenzo's Legacy of Wisdom', to enhance mana production; it was funded but destroyed by the Druj invasion of Morrow before completion.

Morrow.t: The great work's stellae were being raised in Morrow until the Druj invasion destroyed the site; work could restart from scratch if Caeli is retaken before the Summer Solstice 383YE.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the funders were the Bloody Butchers of Temeschwar and Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar.

Construct Lepidean University.d: Proposed by Bastion's senator and seconded by Casinea's, the commission cost 60 wains of white granite, 30 wains of weirwood and 180 crowns in labour, with 20 thrones upkeep, and took six months. The materials were supplied by Rhesa, Asael and Richardo Glostari di Sarvos, with private donors giving over 22 thrones. The Lepidean Librarian, appointed by the Highborn National Assembly, may conduct historical research into paragons, exemplars or true liao visions. The Constitutional Court debated the use of the judgement of rewarding for the true liao at length but allowed it on historical precedent, and amended the guidance so that competing judgements are decided by the greatest margin of votes.

Highguard.t: Highguard gained a university and the Lepidean Librarian, a title appointed and revocable by its National Assembly, with powers to research paragons, exemplars and true liao visions; Highborn citizens Rhesa and Asael supplied much of the granite and weirwood.

Construct Lepidean University.o: In Autumn 383YE the Senate passed a motion to construct the Lepidean University in Bastion, drawing on the plans of Frederick di Sarvos, creating the title of Lepidean Librarian and producing a dose of true liao to be distributed by a Synod judgement of rewarding.

Bastion.t: The Lepidean University was commissioned in Bastion, with its senator proposing the motion that would bring the university and a dose of true liao to the territory.

Construct Leshun Market.d: The Leshun Market was announced by the Boyar of the Iron Roads rather than through a vote. It cost 16 wains of weirwood and 3 thrones and took three months to build. Funding came from several donors after the Winter Solstice 385YE: Druhain Olodniky gave a wain of weirwood, Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn gave 2 thrones, 6 crowns and 17 rings, Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov gave a crown, and others gave small sums. Pavel Novak supplied the remaining 15 wains of weirwood after the Autumn Equinox 386YE. With the work complete, the new Speaker to the Leshun would be appointed for the first time at the Winter Solstice 386YE by Tally of the Votes of Varushkan mine and forest owners.

Varushka.t: Varushkan citizens, led by the Boyar of the Iron Roads, paid for the market, and the Varushkan mine and forest owners gained the right to choose the new Speaker to the Leshun.

Construct Leshun Market.o: Borys Vardovich Straskovich, Boyar of the Iron Roads, announced the construction of the Leshun Market in Karsk in Winter 385YE, creating a ministry as offered by the Pride and Prejudice Wind of Fortune.

Karsk.t: The Leshun Market was built in Karsk, giving the territory a new ministry whose Speaker to the Leshun would first be appointed at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

Construct Liathaven spy network.d: Proposed by the Senator for Miaren and seconded by the Senator for Hercynia, the motion passed 25 votes to 3 and was approved at 10 Thrones. Construction required 10 wains of weirwood and three months. Rhys, Senator for Miaren, supplied the weirwood after the Spring Equinox 378YE. Once complete, any Imperial citizen could assign military units under their control to support the network. With enough units committed, it would reveal a map of Liathaven's settlements, then the location and nature of armies, naval routes and trading partners, and finally the location and size of fortifications. The intelligence would go to those who assigned units.

Jotun.t: Because Liathaven was held by the Jotun at the time, the network was set up to uncover their settlements, armies, naval routes, trading partners and fortifications in the territory.

Construct Liathaven spy network.o: In Autumn 377YE the Senate passed a motion to build a spy network in Liathaven, with an upkeep of 2 Thrones per season from the Senate budget, so that Imperial citizens could gather intelligence on the territory.

Liathaven.t: The Empire commissioned a spy network in Jotun-held Liathaven. Once units were committed to it, it could map the territory's settlements, armies, sea routes, trading partners and fortifications.

Construct Library of Worth.d: Proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by Skarsind, the motion took up the opportunity in The Deer in the Sun wind of fortune. It was backed by the Imperial Orcs Assembly through a mandate enacted by Skywise Gralka. The folly cost 14 white granite and 42 crowns. Imperial Orc citizens supplied much of the white granite across several seasons, and individual donors such as Karrak, Ergot Di Cevia and Richardo Glostari di Sarvos gave crowns and stone. Once complete, the Library lets the Imperial Orcs, through the Weigher of Worth, add one word and its accompanying symbol to the collection each season.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc nation funded the Library with granite from its citizens, and through the Weigher of Worth it can now add one word and symbol to the collection each season to preserve its history.

Construct Library of Worth.o: In Autumn 386YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Library of Worth, a folly in Guildenheim in Skarsind, funded by the Imperial Orc nation, to preserve history through a growing collection of words and symbols.

Skarsind/Gildermark.t: Gildermark is home to the new Library of Worth in Guildenheim, where the Imperial Orcs' collection of words and symbols is kept.

Skarsind.t: The Library of Worth was raised in Guildenheim in Imperial Orc-held Skarsind, whose senator seconded the motion.

Construct Lisabetta Docks.d: The commission cost 75 wains of white granite, 50 wains of weirwood and 375 crowns in labour, with twelve months to complete. The Lijkkever family of the Sarcophan Delves lent their expertise, removing the extra cost of building in a marsh, though they were not granted exclusivity. The Sand Fisher orcs were invited to build a weirwood trade enclave in the new port and donated heavily. Many citizens contributed materials and money through 388YE. Once complete, the docks will raise business and trading-fleet investment in Holberg, boost Semmerlak taxation by 15 thrones a season, found a new coastal town, open a ferry to Ossium, and create a League position, the Prince of the Imperatrix Docks.

The League.t: The League gains a great work in Holberg that, once complete, will raise investment in Holberg businesses and trading fleets, briefly cheapen business upgrades for Holberg citizens, and create a new League position, the Prince of the Imperatrix Docks, with bourse access for Holberg businesses.

Varushka.t: Once the docks are complete, a new ferry across the Nameless River will boost trade between Holberg and Varushkan-held Ossium, and the Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore will see purchase prices rise by a tenth.

Construct Lisabetta Docks.o: In Spring 388YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Holberg and seconded by Sarvos, commissioning the Lisabetta Docks as a great work in Utterlund, Holberg, under the Any port in a storm Wind of Fortune.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Utterlund is the site of the Lisabetta Docks, a marshland great work that will host a new port town, a Sand Fisher weirwood enclave and offices for the new Prince of the Docks.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: The Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore will see purchase prices rise by one tenth once the docks are complete.

Holberg.t: Holberg's senator proposed the commission, and its citizens supplied much of the granite, weirwood and coin to build the docks that will found a new town on its coast and make it a trade hub on the Semmerlak.

Ossium.t: Ossium is to be linked to Holberg by a new ferry across the Nameless River, boosting trade between the two territories, and as a Semmerlak territory it shares in the increased taxation.

Construct Lorenzo's Great Game.d: Proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Reikos, the motion commissioned a great work of white granite in Temeschwar, a gaming house and casino to be known as "Lorenzo's Great Game", funded by the Guild of Good Game. It cost 40 wains of white granite and 10 thrones in labour, with three months to construct. After the Spring Equinox the materials and money were received from Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar. The commission is overseen by Almodin Oktístis, Priest of the Builder, and as a great work it provides additional income to business owners in Temeschwar.

The League.t: A League citizen, Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar, paid for a great work that brings additional income to business owners in one of the League's cities.

Construct Lorenzo's Great Game.o: In Spring 382YE the Senate passed a motion to have the Asavean Architect build Lorenzo's Great Game, a white granite gaming house and casino in Temeschwar intended to benefit business owners.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar gains Lorenzo's Great Game, a white granite gaming house and casino that provides additional income to business owners in the territory.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Ambition.d: Proposed by the senator for Karov and seconded by the senator for Tassato, the motion commissioned a great work using the skills of the Asavean Architect, overseen by Almodin Oktístis, Priest of the Builder. It cost 40 wains of mithril and 10 thrones, to be funded by the Bloody Butchers Bank, and took three months to complete. The materials and money were provided by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar. Lorenzo's Legacy of Ambition was finished in Tassato shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE and provides 37 crystal mana each season, shared among the citizens of Tassato who own a mana site.

The League.t: League mana site owners in Tassato gain a share of 37 extra crystal mana each season, from a great work paid for by the League's Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar and the Bloody Butchers Bank.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Ambition.o: The Senate passed a motion to have the Asavean architect build a great work in Tassato to boost mana production, named "Lorenzo's Legacy of Ambition". It was funded by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar and completed shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE.

Tassato.t: Lorenzo's Legacy of Ambition now stands in Tassato, completed before the Winter Solstice 381YE and providing 37 crystal mana each season to the territory's mana site owners.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Courage.d: Announced in Autumn 381YE by Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar under the construction powers the Senate delegates to holders of an Imperial Wayleave, the great work cost 40 wains of mithril and 10 thrones and took three months to build. The text said it would be funded by the Bloody Butchers Guild, and the materials were provided by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar. Lorenzo's Legacy of Courage was finished in Holberg shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE. It provides 37 crystal mana each season, shared among the citizens of Holberg who own a mana site.

The League.t: A League citizen paid for a great work in a League city, and the League's mana-site owners in Holberg gain a lasting yearly supply of crystal mana from it.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Courage.o: Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar, holding an Imperial Wayleave, commissioned a great work in Holberg called Lorenzo's Legacy of Courage to boost mana production. It was completed shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE.

Holberg.t: Holberg is now home to Lorenzo's Legacy of Courage, which yields 37 crystal mana each season, divided among the territory's mana site owners.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Loyalty.d: Proposed by Tassato and seconded by Zenith, the motion commissioned the Asavean architect, with the work overseen by Almodin Oktístis, Priest of the Builder, to construct a great work for the production of mana in Temeschwar. It cost 40 wains of mithril and 10 thrones, intended to be funded by the Bloody Butchers Bank, and took three months to complete. The materials and money were provided by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar. Lorenzo's Legacy of Loyalty was completed shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE and provides 37 crystal mana each season, shared among the citizens of Temeschwar who own a mana site.

The League.t: A League citizen, Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar, paid for the great work, and League mana-site owners in Temeschwar gain a share of 37 crystal mana each season.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Loyalty.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 381YE to have the Asavean architect build a great work in Temeschwar to boost mana production, to be known as "Lorenzo's Legacy of Loyalty".

Temeschwar.t: Lorenzo's Legacy of Loyalty was built in Temeschwar shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE, and it provides 37 crystal mana each season to the territory's mana-site owners.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Pride.d: Announced by Silas di Sarvos using the Senate's delegated power to commission constructions under an Imperial Wayleave, the great work cost 40 wains of mithril and 10 thrones and took three months to build. The commission named the Bloody Butchers Guild as the funder, and the materials and money were supplied by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar. Lorenzo's Legacy of Pride was finished in Sarvos shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE. It provides 37 crystal mana each season, shared among those citizens of Sarvos who own a mana site.

The League.t: League magicians who own mana sites in Sarvos now share an extra 37 crystal mana each season, paid for by a League benefactor, Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Pride.o: Silas di Sarvos, holding an Imperial Wayleave, commissioned a great work in Sarvos called Lorenzo's Legacy of Pride to boost the city's mana production; it was completed shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos gained the great work Lorenzo's Legacy of Pride, completed before the Winter Solstice 381YE, which adds 37 crystal mana each season for the territory's mana site owners.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Prosperity.d: Proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by the senator for Casinea, the motion commissioned a great work costing 40 wains of mithril and 10 Thrones, taking three months to complete. It was to be funded by Lorenzo 'La Volpe' and the Bloody Butchers Guild of Temeschwar, and was centred near Long Tom's Brewery in Anvil, honouring Long Tom Goodfellow, Exemplar of Prosperity, as inspiration for the Butchers Benevolence and pilgrimage along the Blood Red Roads. Lorenzo 'La Volpe' Macelliao von Temeschwar provided the full cost after the Winter Solstice. The completed work provides 37 crystal mana each season, shared amongst Casinean citizens who own mana sites.

Highguard.t: Highguard gained a great work in its territory of Casinea that adds 37 crystal mana each season for its citizens there who own mana sites, with the motion proposed by Reikos and seconded by Casinea.

The League.t: A League patron, Lorenzo 'La Volpe' Macelliao von Temeschwar, together with the Bloody Butchers Guild of Temeschwar, funded the great work in full and gave it his name.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Prosperity.o: In Winter 381YE the Senate passed a motion to construct a great work in Casinea, known as Lorenzo's Legacy of Prosperity, to enhance the production of mana.

Casinea.t: The great work was built in Casinea near Long Tom's Brewery in Anvil, yielding 37 crystal mana each season shared amongst Casinean mana site owners.

Temeschwar.t: The Bloody Butchers Guild of Temeschwar and Lorenzo 'La Volpe' von Temeschwar were named as the great work's funders, extending Temeschwar's influence through the Butchers Benevolence and the Blood Red Roads.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by Hahnmark, the motion commissioned a great work in New Dunhall at a cost of 40 wains of mithril and 10 thrones, taking three months to complete. It was to be built by the Asavean Architect, with the commission overseen by Almodin Oktístis, Priest of the Builder. After the Winter Solstice 381YE, Lorenzo 'La Volpe' Macelliao von Temeschwar provided the full mithril and thrones. Once complete, the great work provides 37 crystal mana each season, shared among those citizens of Hahnmark who own a mana site.

The League.t: A League citizen, Lorenzo 'La Volpe' Macelliao von Temeschwar, together with the Bloody Butchers Guild, bankrolled the entire great work, which bears his name.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a great work in its territory of Hahnmark that delivers 37 crystal mana each season to Hahnmark's mana site owners, with Wintermark's senators for Sermersuaq and Hahnmark proposing and seconding the motion.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance.o: The Senate passed a motion to construct 'Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance', a great work in New Dunhall in Hahnmark designed to enhance mana production, funded by Lorenzo 'La Volpe' and the Bloody Butchers Guild of Temeschwar.

Hahnmark.t: The great work is built in New Dunhall and provides 37 crystal mana each season, spread among citizens who own mana sites in Hahnmark.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the funders, Lorenzo 'La Volpe' von Temeschwar and the Bloody Butchers Guild, are identified as being of Temeschwar.

Construct Lowther's Lift.d: Proposed by the senator for Mitwold and seconded by Kallavesa, the motion commissioned the self-funded folly. The motion text gave the cost as 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns, but the costs were set by the Wind of Fortune: 15 wains of weirwood, 20 crowns in labour and six months to build. After the Spring Equinox, William Lowther provided 2 thrones, 4 crowns and 10 wains of weirwood, but Jotun raiders took 5 wains of weirwood. Fern provided another 5 wains after the Summer Solstice. Following the actions of Yanya Uranduln, the lifts needed another five wains of weirwood and three more months. Once completed, the lift will give the Custodian of the Singing Caves a ministry to buy mithril at set prices.

Jotun.t: Jotun raiders took 5 wains of weirwood meant for the lift after the Spring Equinox, which delayed and added to the cost of the project.

The Marches.t: The senator for Mitwold proposed the project in Mournwold, and Marcher-held land stands to gain new mithril supplies through the Custodian of the Singing Caves.

Construct Lowther's Lift.o: In Spring 385YE the Senate passed a motion to build Lowther's Lift, a folly in the Singing Caves near Overton in Mournwold that would open rich new veins of mithril, as described in the Wildest Dreams Wind of Fortune.

Mournwold.t: The lift was being built in the Singing Caves near Overton, and once finished it will open new mithril veins there and create a ministry for the Custodian of the Singing Caves.

Construct Lumi's Legacy.d: Announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, Master of Rings, the commission created a herb sinecure called Lumi's Legacy in East Floes, Sermersuaq, intended to focus on bladeroot cultivation. It required 10 wains of weirwood, 30 crowns and three months to complete. Lumi Warmthbringer funded it in full, providing 3 thrones 6 crowns and 10 wains of weirwood after the Spring Equinox. The title of Legal Leaseholder of Lumi's Legacy carries tenure and is chosen by the unanimous decision of the Wintermark senators. With the work complete, the first appointment was due at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the construction was announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, the Master of Rings.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gained a new herb sinecure in its own lands, funded by Lumi Warmthbringer. Its senators hold the power to appoint the tenured Leaseholder by unanimous decision.

Construct Lumi's Legacy.o: In Spring 387YE the Master of Rings announced the construction of Lumi's Legacy, a herb sinecure in the East Floes of Sermersuaq devoted to bladeroot cultivation, paid for entirely by Lumi Warmthbringer.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: East Floes is the site of Lumi's Legacy, a herb sinecure focused on bladeroot cultivation. It was completed and ready for its first Leaseholder at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq became home to Lumi's Legacy, a new bladeroot-growing sinecure built in the territory.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: it appears only in the name of the Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, who announced the construction.

Construct Lyceum Schloss.d: Proposed by the senator for Madruga and seconded by the senator for Karov, the motion authorised the Commonwealth to construct a schloss for its citizens visiting the Lyceum, with the building ceded to the Commonwealth. The construction did not count towards the limit on commissions. Non-standard costs applied: 40 wains of white granite, 10 wains of weirwood and 100 crowns in labour. After the Winter Solstice 383YE, Militärattache Ludkhannah Schöningen provided 12 thrones 4 crowns along with the granite and weirwood. Once complete, the Lyceum gained a permanent improvement in the speed with which it can codify rituals designed to enchant an army.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast's senator for Madruga proposed the motion allowing a foreign power, the Commonwealth, to build and own a schloss within Brass Coast lands near Siroc, strengthening the Lyceum based there.

Construct Lyceum Schloss.o: The Senate passed a motion permitting the Commonwealth to build a schloss on the island east of Siroc in Madruga for its citizens visiting the Lyceum, and ceding the structure to the Commonwealth.

Madruga.t: A Commonwealth-owned schloss was to be built on the island east of Siroc in Madruga, and on completion it improved the Lyceum's ability to codify army enchantment rituals.

Construct Madruga shipyard.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by the senator for Madruga. Construction required 35 wains of white granite and 5 wains of weirwood, with an upkeep of 5 thrones. Mirislav, Senator for Sarvos, paid the costs during the Spring Equinox 377YE downtime. Once built, the shipyard means that every Freeborn fleet operating out of Madruga produces more wealth for its owner. The total benefit is 720 rings per season, divided among all the fleets active in Madruga that season.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn fleet owners sailing from Madruga share an extra 720 rings each season from the new shipyard, strengthening the nation's maritime wealth.

The League.t: The League's senator for Sarvos proposed the shipyard and then paid its construction costs, effectively funding a Freeborn project.

Construct Madruga shipyard.o: In Winter 376YE the Senate passed a motion to build a new Imperial shipyard in Madruga, intended to increase the wealth produced by Freeborn fleets sailing from that territory.

Madruga.t: Madruga gains a new Imperial shipyard, and the fleets operating from it share 720 additional rings of wealth each season.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos's senator, Mirislav, proposed the motion and personally paid the materials for a shipyard built in another territory.

Construct Mana Sinecure in Kallavesa.d: The motion presented the sinecure as support for small halls that had pooled their resources but still could not afford a wayleaf. It carried the standard costs of 10 mithril, 30 crowns and three months to complete. Funding arrived slowly. Amund en Craite, Acwyn, small donors and Hodwyn Aevardson contributed coin between Summer 386YE and Spring 387YE, and Hodwyn Aevardson also supplied the 10 wains of mithril. With the sinecure complete, the title of Remembrancer of Blood and Salt was to be appointed for the first time at the Summer Solstice 387YE, by unanimous decision of Wintermark's senators.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a new mana-producing title, the Remembrancer of Blood and Salt, and its senators must agree unanimously on who holds it, starting at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

Construct Mana Sinecure in Kallavesa.o: In Spring 386YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Hahnmark and seconded by Bregasland, to build a sinecure in Kallavesa that produces mana crystals. It was finished after donations up to the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Kallavesa.t: The mana sinecure stands in Kallavesa, completed after the last of the mithril and coin arrived following the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Construct Meeting Place.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by the Conscience of the Senate, the motion committed the Empire to 55 wains of white granite and 198 crowns of labour, with the Jotun contributing to the joint build. The full edifice cost 110 wains of white granite and 396 crowns, raised because it was built in a marsh, and took nine months. Andos, speaking for the Jarl of Kierheim, supplied 24 thrones, 6 crowns and 55 wains of granite. Fedelmidd Sydanjaa's Heart Floer supplied 24 thrones, 1 crown and 55 wains. Further small sums came from three others. The motion followed the wind of fortune "A stone for a stone".

Jotun.t: The Jotun were partners in the build, with Andos speaking for the Jarl of Kierheim providing half the granite and a large share of the money, giving them a dedicated diplomatic hall with the Empire.

Wintermark.t: A Wintermark territory gained Gull's Isle Hall as a meeting place with the Jotun, after a motion proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq.

Construct Meeting Place.o: The Senate passed a motion in Spring 387YE to build a feasting hall on Gull Island in Kallavesa as a new meeting place for diplomacy between the Empire and the Jotun. The work was completed as Gull's Isle Hall in the West Marsh.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: The hall was built on Gull Island in the West Marsh, and building in the marsh raised the labour costs.

Kallavesa.t: Gull's Isle Hall now stands on Gull Island in Kallavesa as a feasting hall and meeting place for diplomacy between the Empire and the Jotun.

Construct Menagerie.d: Proposed by Morrow and seconded by Conscience, the motion was to be self-funded by the House of Seven Mirrors. The construction was costed at 3 wains of white granite, 2 wains of mithril and 10 crowns in labour, and would take three months; its progress was recorded as unknown. Once complete, it would create the Imperial title of Keeper of the Imperial Menagerie, a lifetime appointment made by the Throne and revocable by the General Assembly and the Assembly of Nine. The Keeper would care for the rakshasa and receive a regular income of Winter vis and 'Tears of the Rakshasa', a substance the creature produces when it is happy.

The League.t: The League was to host a new Imperial sinecure on its soil. The rakshasa it would house had already been given the name 'Flocki' by the children of Holberg.

Construct Menagerie.o: In Winter 380YE the Senate passed a motion to build an Imperial Menagerie in Holmauer, Holberg, to house the tame rakshasa 'Flocki' gifted to Empress Lisabetta by the Eastern Principalities of Jarm.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Holmauer was the planned location of the menagerie, where the enclosure would be built from white granite and mithril over three months.

Holberg.t: Holberg, held by the League, was chosen as the site of the Imperial Menagerie, which would house the Empress's tame rakshasa.

Construct Mercantile Exchange in Temesch.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by the senator for Necropolis, the motion sought to commission a Great Work, the Lukash Biessek von Temeschwar Mercantile Exchange. It would have cost 40 wains of white granite and 10 thrones, taken three months to construct and carried no upkeep. Once complete it would have produced 900 rings, divided between the businesses owned by League citizens in Temeschwar. The motion was defeated, so the exchange was not built and no progress was made.

The League.t: League merchants and business owners in Temeschwar missed out on a share of 900 rings that the proposed exchange would have provided, after the motion put forward by their own senator failed.

Construct Mercantile Exchange in Temesch.o: In Autumn 378YE the Senate defeated a motion to build the Lukash Biessek von Temeschwar Mercantile Exchange, a Great Work intended to boost the profitability of businesses in Temeschwar.

Temeschwar.t: The planned mercantile exchange in Temeschwar was never built after the motion was defeated, leaving the territory's businesses without the extra income it would have generated.

Construct Micah's Stand.d: Proposed by Hercynia and seconded by Miaren in Winter 386YE, the motion authorised a self-funded wayhouse costing 12 wains of weirwood, 12 wains of white granite and 72 crowns, taking three months to build. Sister Micah (who was Earna) of the Navigators of Virtue provided the white granite and most of the money. Sorcha Embracing Fold supplied the weirwood, and Farren Silver Streams, Fintan Nighthaven and Rhys Nighthaven gave a crown each. Once completed, the Stand raised the Benefactor of High Chalcis to eight of each herb and added one Imperial roseweald to the Gardens of High Chalcis' great work production. It also created the title of Keeper of the Stand, first appointable at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Highguard.t: Highguard's territory of Reikos gained the wayhouse, and the Highborn Sister Micah of the Navigators of Virtue provided the granite and most of the money, which gave the Stand its name.

Navarr.t: Navarr senators proposed and seconded the motion, Navarr donors supplied the weirwood and coin, and the new Keeper of the Stand title is appointed by unanimous decision of the Navarr senators, first at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Construct Micah's Stand.o: The Senate passed a motion to build Micah's Stand, a wayhouse in High Chalcis in Reikos, following the Wasp nest Wind of Fortune; it was funded by individual donors and has since been completed.

Reikos.t: Micah's Stand was completed in High Chalcis, raising the Benefactor of High Chalcis to eight of each herb and adding an Imperial roseweald to the Gardens of High Chalcis' great work production.

Construct Mines of Gulhule.d: Proposed by Feroz and seconded by the Senator for Skarsind, the motion answered an opportunity to develop the mines of Gulhule. Three funding options were offered: 6 wains of mithril with 12 crowns plus a 12-crown outlay for green iron and orichalcum; 8 wains and 16 crowns plus 16 for those and tempest jade; or 10 wains and 20 crowns plus 20 for those, weltsilver and potentially more valuable materials. After the Winter Solstice Yargol supplied 10 wains of mithril and 40 crowns, the largest option. The work was completed, creating the Imperial title of Foreman of the Mines of Gulhule.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs gained a ministry through which they can buy ingots, including green iron, orichalcum, tempest jade and weltsilver, funded by Yargol and overseen by the new Foreman of the Mines of Gulhule.

Construct Mines of Gulhule.o: In Winter 379YE the Senate passed a self-funded motion to commission the Mines of Gulhule, a large ministry in Skarsind to recruit and organise the territory's miners and let the Imperial Orcs purchase ingots.

Skarsind.t: The Mines of Gulhule were built in Skarsind to organise its miners, giving the territory a major new ministry and the Imperial title of Foreman of the Mines of Gulhule.

Construct Ministry for Bursar of the Con.d: The commission was announced by Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad as Arcane Architect. It cost 12 wains of mithril and 36 crowns and would take three months to build in Moresvah, Karsk. Novosad supplied 7 wains of mithril and 4 thrones 4 crowns after the Winter Solstice 385YE. Otmar van Holberg provided the remaining 5 wains of mithril after the Autumn Equinox 386YE. With the work finished, the Bursar of the Conclave could purchase mana crystals at the standard costs.

Varushka.t: The Bursar of the Conclave's improved ministry was built on Varushkan soil in Karsk, and a Varushkan-named Arcane Architect, Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad, announced it and provided most of the funding.

Construct Ministry for Bursar of the Con.o: In Winter 385YE the Arcane Architect, Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad, announced the construction of a ministry for the Bursar of the Conclave in Moresvah, Karsk, letting the Bursar buy crystal mana at standard costs. It was later completed.

Karsk/Moresvah.t: The ministry allowing the Bursar of the Conclave to buy mana crystals at standard costs was constructed in Moresvah.

Karsk.t: Karsk was chosen as the site of the ministry, which was completed after mithril was supplied in 385YE and 386YE.

Construct Ministry in Sybella.d: Acting under the power to commission constructions delegated by the Senate, the Civilian Commissioner of Highguard approved a herb garden ministry in Sybella Cross costing fourteen wains of weirwood and 28 crowns in labour, taking three months to build. Rhesa, Exarch of Ravensfell, supplied the materials and money after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the sinecure creates the Highborn national title of High Herbalist of Sybella, expected to provide herbs at a preferential rate to the hospital. The holder is appointed by unanimous agreement of the Highguard senators and may be revoked by the Highguard national assembly, and also by the General Assembly and the Assembly of Nine.

Highguard.t: Highguard gains a new national title, the High Herbalist of Sybella, appointed by unanimous agreement of its senators and funded by Rhesa, Exarch of Ravensfell.

Construct Ministry in Sybella.o: In Autumn 380YE Rhesa of the Scions of Ravensfell, Civilian Commissioner for Highguard, commissioned a herb garden ministry in Sybella Cross, Bastion, to be overseen by a new High Herbalist of Sybella.

Bastion/Sybella Cross.t: Sybella Cross is the site of the new herb garden ministry, whose overseer will hold the title High Herbalist of Sybella.

Bastion.t: Bastion is to gain a herb garden ministry, built over three months from fourteen wains of weirwood, which will supply herbs to the hospital at a preferential rate.

Construct Misericorde Market.d: The self-funded commission required 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns, with construction taking three months. Contributions came from Tom Bull (2 crowns, after Autumn Equinox 383YE), Beatrix Amalia De Rondell zu Holberg (16 wains of weirwood, after Winter Solstice) and Lula Kleist von Ennerlund (3 thrones 6 crowns, after Winter Solstice). Once complete, the market creates a lifetime Imperial title, the Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market, appointed by unanimous decision of the League senators and revocable by the League Assembly and General Assembly. At the Winter Solstice 383YE an opportunity added a ministry allowing mithril and weirwood to be sold to the orcs for large amounts of herbs, and Holberg business owners would gain a way to diversify into herbs.

The League.t: The League gains a new lifetime Imperial title, the Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market, appointed by unanimous consent of its senators and revocable by the League Assembly, along with a route for its merchants to trade mithril and weirwood with the orcs for herbs.

Construct Misericorde Market.o: Tristan Exile's End, bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction of a covered market in Holberg to facilitate trade between Holberg's citizens and the Sand Fishers orcs, and the commission passed in Summer 383YE.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Misericorde is the site of the new covered market, whose Merchant Prince oversees trade with the Sand Fishers, including a later ministry for exchanging mithril and weirwood for herbs.

Holberg.t: A covered market was commissioned in Holberg, then held by the Sand Fishers, to let Holberg citizens trade with the orcs, offering local business owners a chance to diversify into herbs.

Construct Mithril Block.d: The motion commissioned the Block in Cinion as laid out in earlier proposals, and it passed with no throne cost. Construction was set at the non-standard cost of 40 wains of mithril and 80 crowns, with three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice 382YE, Edmundo of Damakhan's Forge provided 22 wains of mithril, and Maximilian provided 18 wains of mithril and 10 thrones. Once complete, the Block would remove the penalties suffered by mana sites, congregations, herb gardens, mines and forests owned by those living in Spiral. Its protection would also let people live in Spiral despite the curse of the Black Plateau, slightly speeding the territory's recovery and its contributions to Imperial coffers.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page, though it held part of Spiral, the territory the Block is meant to protect.

Urizen.t: The Senator for Spiral, a territory Urizen held at least in part, proposed the Block. Once complete, it promised to lift the curse-related penalties on Spiral residents' mana sites, congregations, herb gardens, mines and forests.

Construct Mithril Block.o: In Winter 382YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Spiral and seconded by Bastion, to commission the Block, a mithril ward over the spires of Spiral, to be built in Cinion.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Cinion was chosen as the site of the Block, a mithril ward with three months of construction to follow the commission.

Spiral.t: The Block would shield Spiral's spires from the curse of the Black Plateau. It would make the territory feasibly habitable again, remove production penalties on its residents' resources and slightly increase its rate of recovery.

Construct Mithril Sculptures.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by Redoubt's, the motion took up the opportunity offered by the Wind of Fortune 'The fate of the many'. It was recorded as passed at 11 thrones and 6 crowns. The sculptures needed 10 wains of mithril, 20 crowns in labour and three months to build. Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg supplied the mithril and 2 thrones 4 crowns after the Summer Solstice. Once completed, the folly allowed Vale of Shadows to shield Urizen personal resources in Spiral from foreign-nation penalties, and for the next year let that ritual be made permanent for a third of the usual ilium. The Urizen generals were first to elect an Oblivion Sentinel at the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

The League.t: Holberg's senator proposed the motion and Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg supplied the mithril and labour money that let the folly be completed.

Urizen.t: Urizen gained two mithril statues in its lands and a new national title, the Oblivion Sentinel, elected by its generals to guard against threats from the Black Plateau. Its citizens' personal resources in Spiral could also be shielded by Vale of Shadows.

Construct Mithril Sculptures.o: In Summer 385YE the Senate passed a motion to build a folly of two mithril statues, one in southern Proceris in Zenith and one in the peaks of Optarion in Redoubt. It also created the Urizen national title of Oblivion Sentinel to keep watch over the Black Plateau.

Redoubt/Optarion.t: A mithril statue was commissioned for the peaks of Optarion as one half of the folly.

Zenith/Proceris.t: A mithril statue was commissioned for southern Proceris as one half of the folly.

Redoubt.t: One of the two mithril statues was built in Redoubt, whose senator seconded the motion.

Spiral.t: The completed folly allowed Vale of Shadows to shroud Urizen personal resources in Spiral from foreign-nation penalties, with the option to make that ritual permanent at reduced cost for a year.

Zenith.t: One of the two mithril statues was raised in Zenith, part of the folly tied to watching over the Black Plateau.

Construct Monument in Bastion.d: The monument was to be built in Sybella, in Sybella's Cross, to a design by Lady Josephine, with thanks to the generosity of Livia of the Spire of the Celestial Cascade. It required seven wains of white granite, one of mithril and 24 crowns, and would take three months to complete. Contributions came in from after the Autumn Equinox 386YE to after the Summer Solstice 387YE. Olyvar of Esther's Sanctum gave all seven wains of white granite and much of the money. Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov gave the mithril and several crowns, and smaller sums came from Rhys Nighthaven, Septus Sentinels Tower and Nicodemus of Balthazar's Vineyard. Details of the finished monument were to be added to the Bastion page.

Highguard.t: The monument publicly honours Highborn and others who worked against discrimination toward lineaged people within Highguard, and Highborn including Olyvar of Esther's Sanctum gave much of the stone and money to build it.

Construct Monument in Bastion.o: In Autumn 386YE the Mistress of Monuments, Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov, announced a folly in Sybella, Bastion, celebrating Brother Olyvar of Esther's Sanctum, Lady Josephine of Adina's Charge, Hazelelponi of the Shattered Tower and countless others for their work to end discrimination against lineaged people in Highguard and the wider Empire.

Bastion.t: A folly to Lady Josephine's design was to be raised in Sybella, Sybella's Cross, with its granite and mithril supplied over the following seasons.

Construct Monument to Silent Bell.d: As Mistress of Monuments, Ada Droon proposed the monument and stated that Anatolij Paukov Zorkin would fully fund it. Standard costs applied: 6 wains of white granite, 18 crowns in labour, and three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice 387YE, Zorkin provided 2 thrones 2 crowns and the 6 wains of white granite. The page records no outcome, so it does not confirm whether the pillar was finished.

Highguard.t: The pillar honouring the Silent Bell sodality was to stand in Reikos, a territory Highguard held at the time, adding a monument to the Way within Highguard's lands.

Construct Monument to Silent Bell.o: In Winter 387YE Ada Droon, Mistress of Monuments, announced an edifice in Broken Ride, Reikos: an engraved white granite pillar celebrating the Silent Bell sodality for their tireless work defending the Empire and the Way.

Reikos/Broken Ride.t: Broken Ride was the intended location of the engraved white granite pillar, which was expected to take three months to build once paid for.

Reikos.t: Reikos was chosen as the site of a white granite pillar celebrating the Silent Bell sodality, with materials and funds supplied by Anatolij Paukov Zorkin.

Construct Mountains of the Moon spy netw.d: In Autumn 381YE the Senate considered a motion to construct a spy network in the area called the Valley of the Moon, which the Axou know as the Valley of Silence. The target lay in the Mountains of the Moon, an unknown territory east of Urizen. Casinea proposed the motion and Therunin seconded it. Standard costs would have applied had it passed. The motion failed, so no spy network was built and the Empire gained no new means of observing the region.

Urizen.t: Urizen's eastern neighbour, the Mountains of the Moon, stays unobserved, because the motion to place a spy network across its eastern border failed.

Construct Mountains of the Moon spy netw.o: A Senate motion proposed by Casinea and seconded by Therunin to build a spy network in the Mountains of the Moon, the unknown territory east of Urizen, failed in Autumn 381YE.

Mountains of the Moon.t: No Imperial spy network was built in the Valley of the Moon, so the Tsark-held territory remained beyond the Empire's watch.

Construct Mudlark's Haven.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Therunin and seconded by Hercynia. It took up a limited opportunity, described as fully funded, to build a fortified steading called "Mudlark's Haven" as an expansion of the Feverwater Docks. The cost was 6 wains of white granite, 12 wains of weirwood and 36 crowns in labour, with three months to construct. After the Summer Solstice, Travid Longest Path provided 4 thrones 4 crowns along with all of the weirwood and granite. Once complete, the Dredgemaster of Feverwater gains a larger seasonal income of ingots and access to a ministry. The expanded docks also let Navarr military units take the Adventure in the Sarangrave action.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj-held Sarangrave is named as the target of a new Adventure in the Sarangrave action open to Navarr armies once the docks are expanded.

Navarr.t: Navarr gained an expanded Feverwater Docks in its territory of Therunin, funded by Travid Longest Path. Once complete, Navarr military units can take the Adventure in the Sarangrave action.

Construct Mudlark's Haven.o: In Summer 384YE the Senate passed a motion to build "Mudlark's Haven", a fortified steading in the Feverwater, Therunin. The work expanded the Feverwater Docks.

Sarangrave.t: The expanded docks give Navarr military units a new route into the Druj-held Sarangrave through the Adventure in the Sarangrave action.

Therunin.t: The fortified steading of Mudlark's Haven was commissioned in the Feverwater. Once complete it expands the Feverwater Docks and raises the Dredgemaster's ingot income, as well as giving access to a ministry.

Construct Municipal Docks.d: Proposed by Madruga's senator and seconded by Hahnmark, the motion arose from the Germinating a city wind of fortune. The commission cost 80 wains of white granite, 40 wains of weirwood and 45 thrones in labour, with 5 thrones a season upkeep, all provided by Gisli i Phovas i Guerra after the Winter Solstice. Once complete, the docks boost Madruga's taxation by 12 thrones a season, fortify Calvos Sound, serve as a shipyard for up to two navies, and create the Freeborn title Quaymaster of the Municipal Docks. From Autumn 388YE they also raise investment in Madruga's fleets and businesses, raise Freeborn incomes, cheapen fleet upgrades and open a new kraken-hunting voyage.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gain the new Quaymaster title, a year of increased income and cheaper fleet upgrades, greater investment in Madruga's fleets and businesses, and a new questing voyage to hunt the Free Landing Kraken.

Construct Municipal Docks.o: In Winter 387YE the Senate passed a self-funded motion to raise a commission building the Municipal Docks in Calvos Sound, Madruga, a great work that was subsequently funded and completed.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: The Municipal Docks are built in Calvos Sound, which becomes protected as a level one fortification and home to a shipyard for up to two navies.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Mentioned in passing: the docks open a new Freeborn questing voyage named Hunt the Free Landing Kraken.

Madruga.t: Madruga gains a great work that boosts its taxation by 12 thrones a season, houses a shipyard for up to two navies and draws greater investment to its fleets and businesses.

Construct Naval Academy of Blood and Bra.d: Proposed by Feroz, the motion sought to construct the Naval Academy of Blood and Brass in the city of Siroc to the designs of Frederick di Sarvos, as a school of shipbuilding and international trade. The Great Work was to be funded half by Lorenzo La Volpe von Temeschwar as a Butcher's Benevolence and half by the New Promise Cartel of the Brass Coast, offered as a gift to the Empire celebrating the victory over the Grendel of Dubhtraig. The seconder is unrecorded. The motion failed, so the academy was not commissioned.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the motion framed the academy as a celebration of the Empire's victory over the Grendel of Dubhtraig.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast's New Promise Cartel offered to fund half of a shipbuilding and trade academy in Siroc, but the motion failed and the Brass Coast did not gain the school.

Construct Naval Academy of Blood and Bra.o: A Senate motion to commission the Naval Academy of Blood and Brass, a school of shipbuilding and international trade in Siroc, was put forward in Winter 382YE but failed.

Madruga.t: Siroc in Madruga would have hosted the Naval Academy of Blood and Brass had the motion passed, but it failed and nothing was built there.

Construct Nightingale Chorus.d: The wayhouse was announced under an Imperial Wayleave. It required 25 wains of white granite, 10 wains of weirwood, 105 crowns in labour and three months to build. Many contributors provided materials and money after the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox of 388YE, including Corwyn Heartsbane, Lady Mercy Goldvein and Morgoth SweetBlood. Once complete, it would increase investment in Astolat for military units engaged in the Quest Against the Vallorn, add one throne per season to Astolat's taxation, and let Navarr take a free personal resource in Astolat. It would also create the title of Conductor of the Nightingale Chorus, elected by Cat's Graces. Weirwater and Semmerholm would benefit too if the Dawnish Assembly named the fight against the Vallorn their highest calling.

Dawn.t: Dawnish-held Astolat would gain a throne of tax each season and stronger support for armies fighting the Vallorn. The Dawnish Assembly could extend that support to Weirwater and Semmerholm by naming the fight against the Vallorn their highest calling.

Navarr.t: The wayhouse was announced by Mharen Splitroot, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave. Once complete, Navarr could take a new personal resource in Astolat for free in the season of its completion.

Construct Nightingale Chorus.o: The Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, Mharen Splitroot, announced the construction of the Nightingale Chorus, a wayhouse in Brightway in Grovesyard, Astolat, during Summer 388YE. It was intended to aid the fight against the Vallorn, raise Astolat's taxes and create a new Imperial title.

Astolat/Grovesyard.t: The Nightingale Chorus wayhouse was to be built at Brightway in Grovesyard.

Astolat.t: Astolat would host the wayhouse and gain one throne of taxation per season. Military units engaged in the Quest Against the Vallorn there would receive increased investment.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm would gain increased investment for the Quest Against the Vallorn, but only if the Dawnish Assembly named the fight against the Vallorn their highest calling.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater would gain increased investment for the Quest Against the Vallorn, but only if the Dawnish Assembly named the fight against the Vallorn their highest calling.

Construct Nostos Docks.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Zenith and seconded by the senator for Necropolis. It passed, with the docks to cost 18 white granite and 54 crowns and to take three months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Able the Taller of Sarangrave Reforged provided 5 thrones, 5 crowns and 18 wains of white granite. Triska Markova added 1 throne and Rhys Nighthaven 1 crown. With the docks complete, the Architect of the Conscious River would be chosen by a Tally of the Votes of Urizen mana site owners. The first election was set for the Summer Solstice 386YE, for a short term ending at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

Urizen.t: Urizen senators from Zenith and Necropolis proposed and seconded the motion. Urizen's mana site owners gained the right to elect the new Architect of the Conscious River.

Construct Nostos Docks.o: In Spring 386YE the Senate passed a self-funded motion to build the Nostos Docks in Morrow, following the opportunity in the An angry blade Wind of Fortune. The docks were completed and created the new title of Architect of the Conscious River.

Morrow.t: The Nostos Docks were built in Urizen-held Morrow, and their completion established the Architect of the Conscious River title.

Construct Oath's Roots.d: In Summer 383YE a motion was put before the Senate to commission the Oath's Roots, a Bourse seat that would have produced weirwood in Liathaven. It was proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Therunin. The motion was withdrawn, so the Oath's Roots was not established by this motion.

Jotun.t: The Jotun, who held Liathaven at the time, would have gained a weirwood Bourse seat in their territory had the withdrawn motion gone ahead.

Construct Oath's Roots.o: A Senate motion proposed commissioning the Oath's Roots, a weirwood Bourse seat in Liathaven, but it was withdrawn before taking effect.

Liathaven.t: Liathaven was the proposed site of the Oath's Roots weirwood Bourse seat, but the motion was withdrawn and nothing was built.

Construct Oathwright Press.d: Using an Imperial Wayleave rather than a Senate vote, Prince Ergot di Cevia announced a sinecure to serve the printing needs of Tassatan citizens, students and leafleters and to meet the Oathwright Press's own demands. The announcement described it as producing 216 rings per season, with a tenured League position appointed by the League's senators and revocable by the General, National and Virtue Assemblies. Standard costs were 16 wains of white granite, 48 crowns and three months' work. Otmar van Holberg, Ergot di Cevia and Karrak supplied the materials and money after the Winter Solstice. Once complete, the Printmaster of Cevia became available for the League's senators to appoint for the first time at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

The League.t: The League gained a new national title, the Printmaster of Cevia, which its senators could appoint for the first time at the Spring Equinox 387YE, and which the General, National and Virtue Assemblies could revoke according to the announcement.

Construct Oathwright Press.o: Ergot di Cevia, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction of the Oathwright Printing Press, a sinecure in Cevia, Tassato, in Winter 386YE. The project was completed, creating the title of Printmaster of Cevia.

Tassato/Cascatas.t: The Oathwright Printing Press was built in Cascatas, at Cevia, and was completed using white granite and crowns from Otmar van Holberg, Ergot di Cevia and Karrak.

Tassato.t: Tassato gained a printing-press sinecure in Cevia, intended to serve the printing needs of Tassatan citizens, students and leafleters.

Construct Office of Fire and Stone.d: The construction was announced under an Imperial Wayleave rather than voted on by the Senate, and its costs followed the opportunity described in the wind of fortune The thing with feathers. The edifice required 20 wains of mithril, 10 wains of white granite, 10 rings of ilium and 90 crowns in labour, and took three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice, Edmundo supplied all of the materials and 11 thrones, while Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven each gave a crown. Once it was complete, the Architect of Hammers could be appointed for the first time at the Spring Equinox 388YE, for a shortened term ending at the Autumn Equinox 388YE.

Urizen.t: Urizen gained a new national position, the Architect of Hammers, appointed by a Tally of the Votes of Urizen owners of mana sites, with the first appointment due at the Spring Equinox 388YE.
