Construct Office of Fire and Stone.o: In Winter 387YE, Edmundo of Damakan's Forge, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the self-funded construction of the Office of Fire and Stone, an edifice in Iteri, Zenith. The work was completed and created a new Urizen national position.

Zenith/Iteri.t: The Office of Fire and Stone was built in Iteri and completed there after the Winter Solstice 387YE, largely at Edmundo of Damakan's Forge's own expense.

Zenith.t: Zenith, held by Urizen, gained the Office of Fire and Stone, a completed edifice built of mithril, white granite and ilium.

Construct Office of the Lantern Wolf.d: The commission created a sinecure in Tassato Regario, as described in the Battle cries Wind of Fortune. Besides the standard costs it required 10 wains of weirwood, 10 wains of white granite and 60 crowns, and three months to complete. Ikelos Moretti supplied much of the weirwood and white granite. Gianluca Di Zobbras, Rhys Nighthaven, Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov, Farren Silver Streams, Fintan Nighthaven and others contributed money. Katarina van Palantíri's large donation of money, weirwood and granite after the Autumn Equinox 386YE helped finish it. Once the work was complete, the Lantern Wolf became available for the League's National Assembly to elect as a yearly appointment, for the first time at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

The League.t: The League gained a new national position, the Lantern Wolf, which its National Assembly could elect each year from the Winter Solstice 386YE.

Construct Office of the Lantern Wolf.o: Gustavus Tolski van Temeschwar, Chair of the Wolf, announced in Winter 385YE the commission of the Office of the Lantern Wolf, a new sinecure within the walls of Tassato arising from the Battle cries Wind of Fortune. After donations spanning 386YE the work was completed.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: Tassato Regario became the site of the new Office of the Lantern Wolf, built with weirwood and white granite.

Tassato.t: The Office of the Lantern Wolf was raised within the walls of Tassato, giving the League territory a new sinecure.

Construct Offices of the Iron Roads.d: Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, Master of the Koboldi, announced the commission under the Deep forests and dark hills wind of fortune. The offices were to be built in Ivarsgard (Karsk), Delev (Karov), Lomaa (Ossium), Essk (Miekarova) and Ruin (Volodmartz), at a cost of 30 wains of white granite, 30 wains of mithril and 15 thrones, taking six months. Borys Vardovich Straskovich supplied nearly all the materials and most of the money, with smaller contributions from Triska Markova, Kostjya and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov. The offices were completed, and the Boyar of the Iron Roads was to be appointed for a limited term by Tally of the Votes, first at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Varushka.t: Varushka gained the Offices of the Iron Roads across five of its territories and a new national title, the Boyar of the Iron Roads, chosen by the Tally of the Votes. The work was funded largely by the Varushkan Borys Vardovich Straskovich.

Construct Offices of the Iron Roads.o: At the Summer Solstice 385YE the Master of the Koboldi announced the construction of the Offices of the Iron Roads, a folly spread across five Varushkan territories that creates the title of Boyar of the Iron Roads.

Karov.t: One of the Offices of the Iron Roads was built at Delev in Karov.

Karsk.t: One of the Offices of the Iron Roads was built at Ivarsgard in Karsk.

Miekarova.t: One of the Offices of the Iron Roads was built at Essk in Miekarova.

Ossium.t: One of the Offices of the Iron Roads was built at Lomaa in Ossium.

Volodmartz.t: One of the Offices of the Iron Roads was built at Ruin in Volodmartz.

Construct Open Fan Cicisbeo Academy.d: Proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by the senator for Spiral, the motion commissioned the Open Fan Cicisbeo Academy as a sinecure providing income to its holder. Construction required 10 wains of white granite and 30 crowns in labour (given as 3 thrones 6 crowns) and took three months. Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided the full materials and money after the Autumn Equinox 386YE. With the academy complete, the tenured title of Headmistress of the Open Fan Academy became available to be appointed for the first time at the Winter Solstice 386YE, by unanimous vote of the senators of the League.

The League.t: The League gained a new tenured title, Headmistress of the Open Fan Academy, which its senators appoint by unanimous vote, with the first appointment due at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

Construct Open Fan Cicisbeo Academy.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 386YE to construct the Open Fan Cicisbeo Academy in Cigno, Sarvos, a self-funded money sinecure creating the title of Headmistress of the Open Fan Academy.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: The Open Fan Cicisbeo Academy was built in Cigno, taking three months and 10 wains of white granite to complete.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos became home to the Open Fan Cicisbeo Academy, a new money sinecure proposed by its own senator and completed with materials from Giacomo Corvinoscuro.

Construct Open Hand of the Ancestors.d: The project required 10 wains of white granite, 20 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Summer Solstice the granite was supplied by several donors: Tut, Redhand Gezzar and Frith gave two wains each, and Nirak, Rok, Vrak and Protectorate Thenrik gave one wain each. Tut also provided 2 thrones and 2 crowns, and Rhys Nighthaven and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov gave a crown each. The work was completed. The Imperial Orcs National Assembly would make the first appointment to the new title of Guide to the Lost at the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs gained a new national title, Guide to the Lost, tied to the Open Hand of the Ancestors. Their National Assembly would first appoint it at the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

Construct Open Hand of the Ancestors.o: In Summer 385YE the Legion Engineer, Bleakshield Groza, announced the construction of the Open Hand of the Ancestors, a congregation sinecure in northern Solvihill, Skarsind. Once completed it created the Imperial Orc national title of Guide to the Lost.

Skarsind/Solvihill.t: The Open Hand of the Ancestors congregation was built in the north of Solvihill.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind, held by the Imperial Orcs, became the site of the Open Hand of the Ancestors, a new congregation sinecure built with ten wains of white granite.

Construct Orchard of the Watch.d: The senator for Mournwold proposed the motion and the senator for Necropolis seconded it. It passed with the backing of the Pride Assembly, through a statement of principle raised by Friar John of the Mourn. The cost set by the opportunity was 10 wains of white granite, 20 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns, with three months to complete. Friar John supplied all of it after the Summer Solstice. Once the orchard was finished, Greensward gained the memorial quality: while the trees stand, the angry ghosts remaining there will not trouble the living. If the orchard is ever destroyed, the ghosts will rise again, likely furious, and their wrath will probably fall on whoever destroyed it.

The Marches.t: A Marcher priest, Friar John of the Mourn, paid for the orchard and won the Pride Assembly's support for it. The result calms the angry ghosts haunting Marcher land in Greensward.

Construct Orchard of the Watch.o: In Summer 386YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Orchard of the Watch, a folly in Greensward, Mournwold, following the Let the day die wind of fortune. Friar John of the Mourn paid for it in full.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Greensward gained the memorial quality: its angry ghosts will not trouble the living while the orchard stands, but destroying the trees risks unleashing their fury.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold's senator proposed the motion. The completed orchard now keeps the territory's restless dead in Greensward from troubling the living.

Construct Ossuary Temple.d: Proposed by the senator for Redoubt and seconded by the senator for Skarsind, the motion followed the All too well Wind of Fortune. The temple needed 60 wains of white granite, 15 thrones and six months to complete. After the Winter Solstice the materials were largely supplied by Bloodcrow Rasp, who gave 14 thrones 6 crowns and 31 wains of granite. Many Irontide orcs and others gave smaller amounts of granite, and Fintan Nighthaven and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov each gave a crown. Once the temple is complete, the Illarawm will join the Imperial Orcs. They will share knowledge of their ancestors and help the nation hear its own ancestors' voices better.

Imperial Orcs.t: Once the temple is complete the Illarawm sept will join the Imperial Orcs and help the nation better hear the voices of its ancestors; Bloodcrow, Irontide and Stormsteel orcs supplied most of the granite and coin.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the bones the temple will house were recovered from Ossium, a territory Varushka held at the time.

Construct Ossuary Temple.o: In Winter 384YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Ossuary Temple, a folly in Southpine, Skarsind, to house the bones the Illarawm sept had recovered from Ossium, with the temple to be ceded to the Illarawm.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: Southpine is the site of the new Ossuary Temple, which will take six months to build and will house the Illarawm sept's recovered ancestral bones.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is where the Illarawm sept recovered the bones the temple will house.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind is to gain the Ossuary Temple, a folly ceded to the Illarawm sept, and its senator seconded the motion.

Construct Ossuary of Reikos.d: Proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by the senator for Reikos on the virtue of prosperity, the motion commissioned a great work costing 40 wains of white granite, 40 wains of weirwood and 20 thrones in labour, taking a year to construct. The materials and money were provided by Ianthe after the Spring Equinox 380YE. Once complete, the ossuary was to grant 1300 rings split between the congregations of Reikos. Work on the Grand Ossuary was finished shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE began.

Highguard.t: Highguard's senators for Necropolis and Reikos brought forward the ossuary, which will let thousands of highborn dead be laid to rest and add 1300 rings to the congregations of a Highborn-held territory.

Construct Ossuary of Reikos.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate passed a motion to build a great ossuary in Reikos, intended to lay thousands of highborn dead to rest and allow the territory to be rebuilt.

Reikos.t: Reikos gained the Grand Ossuary, completed shortly before Spring 381YE, which lays its many dead to rest, enables the territory's rebuilding and grants 1300 rings to its congregations.

Construct Otkodov spy network.d: The motion passed at 12 Thrones with no votes against, and the funds went to Morrow. Ioseph, Senator for Morrow, paid the 10 weirwood during the Summer Solstice downtime. The network carries an upkeep of 2 Thrones a season from the Senate budget and takes three months to build. Because a territory map of Otkodov had already been found, the network was to target Verthandi. Once complete, any Imperial citizen may assign military units to it. Five units would reveal a map of Verthandi's settlements, ten its armies, naval routes and trading partners, and fifteen its fortifications. Not all Imperial citizens know the network exists.

Thule.t: The Thule territories of Otkodov and Verthandi became targets of covert Imperial intelligence. The network was meant to expose Verthandi's settlements, armies, trade and fortifications.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Senator for Morrow proposed the motion, received the funds and paid the 10 weirwood to build the network.

Construct Otkodov spy network.o: In Summer 377YE the Imperial Senate secretly passed a motion, proposed by Morrow and seconded by Hahnmark, to build a spy network in Otkodov at a cost of 10 weirwood. It was intended to gather intelligence on the neighbouring Thule territory of Verthandi.

Morrow.t: Morrow's senator Ioseph proposed the motion and paid for it, and the Senate's money was distributed to Morrow.

Otkodov.t: The Empire was to build a secret spy network in Thule-held Otkodov over three months. Otkodov's own territory map had already been discovered.

Verthandi.t: Verthandi, the central Thule territory, was the network's intelligence target. Depending on how many military units are assigned, its settlements, armies, naval routes, trading partners and fortifications could be revealed.

Construct Ozren Orzel Inspirational Tomb.d: The motion commissioned a great work honouring the exemplar of Pride Ozren Orzel in Sandling, as set out in the 'An eagle in song' Wind of Fortune. It cost 30 wains of white granite and 90 crowns in labour, and would take three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice, Starac Sijed Orzel provided 9 thrones 4 crowns and all 30 wains of granite. Smaller sums came from Ser Geoffrey de Lorilam, Farren Silver Streams, Rhys Nighthaven, Ser Gareth Haywain, Lady Nineve Orzel and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov. Once complete, congregations in Weirwater would receive a Philtre of Strength each season. The eighty-one individuals named by Tarik, former High Bard of the Empire, would receive some reward from the Witches of Culwich.

Dawn.t: Two Dawnish senators, those of Weirwater and Astolat, proposed and seconded the motion, and the finished tomb would give congregations in Dawn's territory of Weirwater a Philtre of Strength each season.

Construct Ozren Orzel Inspirational Tomb.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by Weirwater's senator and seconded by Astolat's, to commission a self-funded inspirational tomb to Ozren Orzel, exemplar of Pride, in Sandling, Weirwater.

Weirwater/Sandling.t: Sandling was chosen as the site of Ozren Orzel's inspirational tomb, a three-month great work built of white granite.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater's senator proposed the tomb, and once it is complete, congregations in Weirwater will receive a Philtre of Strength every season.

Construct Palace of Flowers.d: The Senator for Skarsind proposed the motion and the Senator for Morrow seconded it. It passed. The Palace of Flowers is a garden for the Yerende sept, costing 60 wains of weirwood and 120 crowns in labour, and taking six months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Irontide Flax, Bloodcrow Rasp, Abel the Rounder of Sarangrave Reforged, Redhand Gezzar and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov donated money and weirwood towards it. Once it is finished, the Yerende will join the Imperial Orcs and share their herbal lore. The key part of that lore is a set of realmsroot potion recipes useful to orc magicians.

Imperial Orcs.t: Once the folly is finished, the Yerende sept will join the Imperial Orcs. They will bring herbal lore, including realmsroot potion recipes useful to orc magicians.

Construct Palace of Flowers.o: In Spring 385YE the Senate passed a motion to build a folly, the Palace of Flowers, in Solvihill in Skarsind, and to cede it to the Yerende sept, as set out in the All too well Wind of Fortune.

Skarsind/Solvihill.t: Solvihill is the site of the Palace of Flowers, a garden folly due to take six months to build for the Yerende sept.

Skarsind.t: The Senator for Skarsind proposed the motion, which places the new Palace of Flowers in the territory. It will be ceded to the Yerende sept once built.

Construct Parador of Dust.d: Proposed by the senator for Kahraman and seconded by Holberg, the Winter 383YE motion commissioned a ministry at the Parador of Dust. Its holder, the Mistress of the Dust Parador, would have the power to purchase mithril and the responsibility to use it for the benefit of the Freeborn people. The commission was self-funded at non-standard cost: 16 wains of white granite, 32 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Winter Solstice, Bakar i Riqueza provided 4 thrones and the 16 wains of white granite. Once complete, the title is to be appointed through the Bourse by Tally of the Votes.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gained a new ministry whose Mistress may buy mithril for the benefit of the Freeborn people, built on an opportunity offered by their own merchants and paid for by Bakar i Riqueza.

Construct Parador of Dust.o: The Senate passed a motion to refurbish the Parador of Dust in the Jade Range of Kahraman as a mithril ministry, creating the title Mistress of the Dust Parador. The project drew on an opportunity presented by the merchants of the Brass Coast.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: The Parador of Dust in the Jade Range was to be refurbished over three months with 16 wains of white granite, becoming the seat of the Mistress of the Dust Parador.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman's senator proposed refurbishing the Parador of Dust within the territory as a mithril ministry, and the motion passed.

Construct Parador of Salt and Sand.d: The commission cost 15 wains of mithril, 5 wains each of white granite and weirwood, and 50 crowns, and would take three months to build. Small contributions came in after the Winter Solstice, and Bakar i Riqueza supplied the full materials and most of the money after the Spring Equinox 385YE. Once complete, it creates the Brass Coast title of Hakima of Salt and Sand, appointed by Tally of the Votes. The Freeborn are expected to elect only a hakima, and there would be consequences otherwise. The Parador could later be upgraded into a College of Magic. If upgraded, and while the title-holder is a hakima in good standing, the Empire's college upkeep would fall by 20 thrones a season.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gain a new national title, the Hakima of Salt and Sand, chosen by Tally of the Votes. They are firmly expected to elect only a hakima to it and to support a community of hakima who could aid magical research.

Construct Parador of Salt and Sand.o: In Winter 384YE Bakar i Riqueza, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction of the Parador of Salt and Sand, a mana ministry in Quzar, Madruga, taking up the opportunity presented in the wind of fortune The power behind our moves.

Madruga.t: The Parador is built in Quzar, strengthening that city's central importance in Madruga. It could later be expanded there into a full College of Magic.

Construct Parador of the Kindled Flame.d: The folly was announced by Laughlan, Master of the Rings, at a cost of 27 wains of white granite and 54 crowns in labour, with three months needed to construct it. After the Summer Solstice, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar provided 5 thrones, 3 crowns and all 27 wains of white granite, Triska Markova gave 1 throne, Sagua i'Ezmara 2 crowns and Bakar i Riqueza 1 crown. The page records no outcome, so whether the Parador was completed is not stated.

The Brass Coast.t: The planned Parador would give orphaned children of the Brass Coast a home in which hakima and kohan teach them the nation's traditions, and Brass Coast figures such as Sagua i'Ezmara and Bakar i Riqueza contributed coin towards it.

Construct Parador of the Kindled Flame.o: In Summer 385YE Laughlan, Master of the Rings, announced the construction of the Parador of the Kindled Flame, a folly in Siroc, Madruga, intended as an orphanage where Brass Coast children would be cared for and taught their traditions by hakima and kohan.

Madruga.t: The orphanage folly was to be raised in Siroc, Madruga, with all 27 wains of white granite pledged towards its construction, though no completion is recorded.

Construct Path to the Lyceum.d: The edifice was built as set out in the Sound and Vision opportunity. The announcement gave the cost as 15 weirwood, 5 rings of ilium and 45 crowns in labour, self-funded by the Dean of the Lyceum. The recorded costs list 15 wains of weirwood, 5 rings of ilium and 15 crowns in labour, reduced because of the impoverished nature of Fontargenta, with three months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Syl supplied the ilium and weirwood. Lula and Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund each gave 5 crowns 10 rings, and Bakar i Riqueza gave 4 crowns. The completed Path to the Lyceum restored the connection between Oranseri and the Lyceum.

Grendel.t: The Path was raised in Oranseri, part of Feroz, which Grendel held at the time, though the page does not name Grendel or give it any role in the work.

The Brass Coast.t: The new edifice restored Oranseri's link to the Lyceum in Feroz, a territory the Brass Coast held at the time, though the page does not name the nation directly.

Construct Path to the Lyceum.o: In Spring 388YE the Arcane Architect, Amalia Vicente, announced the construction of the Path to the Lyceum in Oranseri, Feroz, under the Sound and Vision Wind of Fortune. Once completed, it restored the connection between Oranseri and the Lyceum.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Mentioned in passing: the labour costs were reduced because of the impoverished nature of Fontargenta.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The Path to the Lyceum was built in Oranseri, and its completion restored the region's connection to the Lyceum.

Feroz.t: Feroz gained a completed edifice, the Path to the Lyceum, which restored the connection between Oranseri and the Lyceum.

Construct Peak Edge trading enclave.d: Proposed under an Imperial Wayleave by Selenius, the commission was counted as a single commission and was self-funded. It carried non-standard costs: 12 wains of weirwood, 12 wains of white granite and 48 crowns in labour. After the Spring Equinox 382YE, Selenius supplied the weirwood, the granite and 24 crowns. The commission was completed, creating a trading post that allows trade with the Khiklotu Khrysoú of Axos for both mana and valuable materials. It also created a new Imperial title, the Eastern Broker, to be appointed by unanimous agreement of the Navarr senators.

Navarr.t: The Navarr senators gained the right to appoint the new Eastern Broker, but only by unanimous agreement, giving the nation control over the Empire's new trading link with the Axou.

Construct Peak Edge trading enclave.o: In Spring 382YE the Senate passed a motion to build Peak Edge, a large self-funded trading enclave in Therunin arranged with the Axou, to allow trade for exotic herbs and resources.

Therunin.t: The Peak Edge trading enclave was built in Therunin, making the Navarr-held territory home to a trading post for mana and valuable materials from the Khiklotu Khrysoú of Axos.

Construct Pegasus Respite.d: The Pegasus Respite was commissioned as a sinecure at a cost of 14 wains of weirwood and 28 crowns in labour, taking three months to build, and was announced as fully self-funded. Its herbs were intended for Highguard's battle physicks in service of the Empire. The House of the Proffered Hand was to run a former slave rehabilitation wing on the premises to support the convalescent hospital's work. Funding came mainly from Tolame, who provided 3 thrones and 12 wains of weirwood after the Autumn Equinox 383YE and a further 2 crowns 19 rings and 2 wains of weirwood after the Spring Equinox 384YE. Septus Sentinels Tower and small donors added smaller sums. Once completed, the commission would be overseen by the Medical Officer of the Pegasus Respite.

Highguard.t: The Highborn national assembly gained the right to appoint the Medical Officer of the Pegasus Respite, and the herbs it produced were destined for Highguard's battle physicks.

Construct Pegasus Respite.o: In Autumn 383YE Nathaniel of Balthazar's Vineyard announced the construction of the Pegasus Respite, a sinecure in Chalcis Mount, Reikos, to be overseen by a Medical Officer appointed by the Highborn national assembly.

Reikos/Chalcis Mount.t: Chalcis Mount was chosen as the location of the Pegasus Respite, a convalescent hospital and herb-producing sinecure built over three months.

Reikos.t: Reikos, held by Highguard, became the site of a new convalescent sinecure, which included a rehabilitation wing for former slaves run by the House of the Proffered Hand.

Construct Pelican Tower.d: Announced under an Imperial Wayleave by Achille di Sarvos, the commission was self-funded at standard sinecure costs. The Pelican Tower will carry a title, the Custodian of the Pelican Tower, held with tenure until death, resignation or reallocation, and appointed by the Senators of the League. After the Spring Equinox 384YE, Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided 10 wains of mithril and 2 thrones 4 crowns towards the work. Once construction is completed, the Custodian of the Pelican Tower may be appointed. The page is a placeholder still being worked on.

The League.t: The League's Senators will appoint the Custodian of the Pelican Tower, a new tenured title, once the tower is complete. The commission was announced by Achille di Sarvos and funded with materials from Giacomo Corvinoscuro.

Construct Pelican Tower.o: Achille di Sarvos, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced a self-funded commission in Spring 384YE to build the Pelican Tower, a sinecure in Foracci in Sarvos.

Sarvos/Foracci.t: Foracci is the site of the Pelican Tower, and its custodian will be appointed once the building work is finished.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos is to gain a new sinecure, the Pelican Tower. Its construction was commissioned and supplied with mithril and money after the Spring Equinox 384YE.

Construct Pilgrim's Trail.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by Karov. It was passed in principle and passed at 60 thrones, which were disbursed to the senator for Kallavesa. The great work was costed at 30 wains of white granite, 10 wains of weirwood and 10 thrones in labour, and would take three months to construct. It was described as an opportunity to draw pilgrims to Kallavesa. After the Spring Equinox 380YE, Olle Markusson provided the granite, weirwood and thrones, and the Pilgrim's Trail was completed.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gained a completed great work in one of its territories, with Olle Markusson supplying the granite, weirwood and thrones needed to finish the Pilgrim's Trail.

Construct Pilgrim's Trail.o: In Winter 379YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Pilgrim's Trail, a great work of roads across Kallavesa meant to ease the movement of pilgrims and improve attendance at its congregations. The work was later completed.

Kallavesa.t: A network of roads was built through Kallavesa to help pilgrims travel, with the aim of raising attendance at the territory's congregations and drawing pilgrims there.

Construct Pit of Revelations.d: Rather than a vote of the Senate, the project was commissioned through an announcement by a bearer of the Imperial Orc Wayleave, made by proxy for Skywise Laika. The Pit of Revelations is a mana sinecure built at standard cost: 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns in labour, taking three months to construct. After the Spring Equinox 383YE, Palerictus Krunk provided the full 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns. The sinecure creates a new Imperial title, the Marshal of the Pit of Revelations, to be held by whoever is appointed to oversee it.

Imperial Orcs.t: An Imperial Orc Wayleave bearer used their authority to commission the sinecure in their own homeland, giving the Empire a new mana-producing title rooted in Imperial Orc lands.

Construct Pit of Revelations.o: In Spring 383YE a bearer of the Imperial Orc Wayleave, Skywise Laika, announced by proxy the construction of the Pit of Revelations, a mana sinecure in south-west Skogei Glens in Skarsind, creating the Imperial title Marshal of the Pit of Revelations.

Skarsind/Skogei Glens.t: The Pit of Revelations is to be built in the south-west of Skogei Glens, with construction taking three months once the mithril and labour were provided.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind gains a new mana sinecure, the Pit of Revelations, and with it the Imperial title of Marshal of the Pit of Revelations.

Construct Potato Fields of Happiston.d: Proposed by the senator for Mournwold and seconded by Ossium, the motion commissioned a mana crystal sinecure at Happiston. It was to be fully funded by the Happiston Volunteers, and its keeper was to be appointed with tenure by unanimous decision of the Marcher senators. The motion gave no size or cost, so the civil service assumed the minimum of 10 wains. Alan Sheppard provided 12 wains of mithril and 2 thrones 6 crowns, and Ergot Di Cevia provided 2 crowns. The missing details about the sinecure's nature and cost were supplied after the Winter Solstice 384YE. The commission was then completed, with the Keeper of the Happiston Fields to be appointed at the Spring Equinox 385YE.

The Marches.t: The Marcher senators gained the right to appoint, by unanimous decision, a tenured keeper to a new mana-producing title in one of their own territories.

Construct Potato Fields of Happiston.o: In Autumn 384YE the Senate passed a motion to build a mana sinecure in Happiston in the Chalkdowns of Mournwold, creating the title Keeper of the Prosperous Potato Fields of Happiston.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: The Prosperous Potato Fields of Happiston were built at Happiston in the Chalkdowns, funded by the Happiston Volunteers, as a sinecure intended to provide mana to its keeper.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold's senator proposed the motion, which gave this Marcher territory a new mana sinecure at Happiston, completed in time for its keeper to be appointed at the Spring Equinox 385YE.

Construct Printers' Guild Bibliopole.d: Proposed by Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar, Senator for Temeschwar, and seconded by Mary Birchsmith, Senator for Mitwold, the motion followed the civil service record "truth but tell it slant" from Winter 387YE. The opportunity was first suggested by Professor Gelberg while the Printers' Guild were patrons of the Beurteilung. The edifice required 8 wains of white granite and 3 thrones in labour, with the motion stating the Printers' Guild would pay, and would take three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox 388YE, Jonah Yakovitch provided the 3 thrones and 8 wains of white granite. Once complete, Printers' Guild publications, including treatises on the Way, will be accessible worldwide.

The League.t: A League senator proposed the motion, and the Printers' Guild's publications held in the League's Tassato will be carried abroad to readers across the world, including treatises on the Way.

Construct Printers' Guild Bibliopole.o: The Senate passed a motion to construct the Printers' Guild Bibliopole in Betovering and Leerdam in the Commonwealth, making Printers' Guild publications held in Tassato accessible to citizens of nations across the world.

Tassato.t: The copies of Printers' Guild publications stored in Tassato are the collection the new bibliopole will make accessible across the world once complete.

Construct Printers' Guild Mausoleum.d: The commission was announced by the Chair of the Wolf rather than passed as a vote of the Senate. It requires 20 wains of mithril and 40 crowns and takes three months to complete, with the mithril provided by the Printers' Guild. Once complete, it creates the tenured title of Custodian of the Printers' Guild Mausoleum, which produces thirteen mana crystals each season. The title is to be appointed by unanimous decision of the League senators.

The League.t: League senators gain the unanimous right to appoint the tenured Custodian of the Printers' Guild Mausoleum, a League guild's monument that will yield thirteen mana crystals each season once complete.

Construct Printers' Guild Mausoleum.o: In Spring 386YE Gustavus Tolski van Temeschwar, Chair of the Wolf, announced the commission of the Printers' Guild Mausoleum in Tassato, a sinecure paid for by the Printers' Guild to create a legacy for its members.

Tassato.t: The Printers' Guild Mausoleum is to be raised in Tassato, taking three months to build at a cost of 20 mithril and 40 crowns.

Construct Printers' Guild Museum of Wond.d: Proposed by Tassato and seconded by Semmerholm in Spring 379YE, the motion created a museum sinecure appointed by the Cardinal of Prosperity, providing 6 liao and 12 Synod votes to its Curator. It required 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns of labour, both supplied by Silvio de Tassato. As first written, the motion was unconstitutional because it could let a citizen vote in a virtue assembly they did not belong to. The Senate agreed amendments at the Autumn Equinox 379YE summit making it a lifetime appointment by the current Cardinal of Prosperity, with votes in the assemblies matching the holder's nationality and virtue. On completion it created the title Curator of the Printers' Guild Museum.

The League.t: The League gained a new cultural institution and Synod title in one of its cities, built with materials and funds supplied by Silvio de Tassato and championed by Tassato's senator.

Construct Printers' Guild Museum of Wond.o: The Senate commissioned the Printers' Guild Museum of Wonders, a sinecure in Tassato to house and display the printers' guild's collection of relics and artefacts for any interested citizen to view and research.

Tassato.t: The Printers' Guild Museum of Wonders was built in the city of Tassato, giving the printers' guild collection of relics and artefacts a permanent public home there.

Construct Printers' Guild Stadium.d: Inspired by renewed interest in foot-the-ball after the pilgrimage of Apulian orcs to the Mournwold, the stadium was commissioned in Regario, across the river from the Printers' Guildhouse in Mestra. It cost 12 wains of white granite, 12 wains of weirwood and 3 thrones in labour, and takes three months to build. Jonah Yakovitch provided all of these after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the stadium will host matches against Marcher teams and possibly the Mestrans. Its sinecure, the Captain of the Regario Byliners, will be appointed by Tally of the Votes of the League's business owners.

The League.t: League business owners gain a new sinecure, the Captain of the Regario Byliners, to be appointed by Tally of the Votes once the stadium is complete. The announcement also playfully casts Regario as having upstaged Mestra.

The Marches.t: Marcher teams are expected to play matches at the new stadium, whose inspiration lay in sporting interest stirred by the Apulian orc pilgrimage to the Mournwold.

Construct Printers' Guild Stadium.o: Taddea Ginori, Chair of the Wolf, announced the construction of the Printers' Guild Stadium, a sinecure in Tassato Regario, home of the Regario Byliners sports team. The materials and labour were provided after the Autumn Equinox 388YE.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: The Printers' Guild Stadium is being built in Regario as the home ground of the teal-clad Regario Byliners, with materials and labour provided after Autumn Equinox 388YE.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the pilgrimage of Apulian orcs to the Mournwold is credited with renewing interest in foot-the-ball and other sports.

Tassato.t: Tassato gains a new stadium in Regario, near the Printers' Guildhouse in Mestra, which will host matches and house the Regario Byliners.

Construct Prosperity of Afal.d: Using an Imperial Wayleave, Vilkas Blake commissioned a mana sinecure in Ashrook, Upwold, at standard cost: 10 wains of mithril, 20 crowns of labour and three months to build. He provided both the mithril and the crowns after the Summer Solstice 382YE. Once complete, it creates the Imperial title Guardian of the Prosperity of Afal, appointed by Marcher senators. The announcement wanted the holder to be a citizen of Upwold, but the constitutional ruling noted an Imperial title cannot be restricted that way. It could be made a Marcher national position, and electors remain free to choose only an Upwold citizen.

The Marches.t: Marcher senators will appoint the Guardian of the Prosperity of Afal, a title that may be made a Marcher national position but cannot legally be limited to Upwold citizens.

Construct Prosperity of Afal.o: Vilkas Blake, bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction of the Prosperity of Afal, a mana sinecure in Ashrook, Upwold, yielding 9 mana per season. He paid the full materials and labour after the Summer Solstice 382YE.

Upwold.t: A mana sinecure, the Prosperity of Afal, is being built in Ashrook, Upwold, to produce 9 mana each season once complete.

Construct Prosperous Counting House in H.d: The commission arose from the Forwards and Rewards Wind of Fortune and cost 5 wains of weirwood, 5 wains of white granite and 30 crowns, with three months needed to build. Funding came slowly through donations from many citizens between Summer 387YE and Spring 388YE. Otmar van Holberg, Morgan Townsend von Holberg, Jonah Yakovitch and several others supplied materials, and Sebastian Adolphus von Temeschwar gave 2 thrones 3 crowns. Once complete, the counting house was to provide an additional 15 crowns each season to the Virtue Fund from donations made there, starting at the Autumn Equinox 388YE.

The League.t: A League city gained a new civic edifice, largely paid for by League citizens such as the van Holbergs and the Adelaars, which channels donations into the Empire's Virtue Fund.

Construct Prosperous Counting House in H.o: In Summer 387YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Reikos and seconded by Segura, to commission a Prosperous Counting House in Holberg, an edifice intended to add 15 crowns a season to the Virtue Fund.

Holberg.t: The Prosperous Counting House was built in Holberg and, once finished, its donations were to swell the Virtue Fund by 15 crowns a season from Autumn 388YE.

Construct Prosperous Counting House in K.d: The commission was announced as self-funded by Wolfs Hearth and Embers of Iversgaard. It cost 5 wains of weirwood, 5 wains of white granite and 30 crowns, with three months of building time. Contributions came in over the following year, including crowns from Triska Markova, Amris Johan Merikovich, Tom Keeper of Copperhill, Ivana Petara Vodjavic, Rhys Nighthaven, Vladimir Vladirovich Reznikov and Askien Alanovich Vesimerov. Katya Vasillova Reznikov supplied all the weirwood and white granite after the Winter Solstice 386YE. Once the work was finished, citizens of Karsk began giving 12 crowns each summit to the Virtue Fund through donations to the Iron Hearth.

Varushka.t: A Varushkan territory gained a Prosperous Counting House, largely paid for by Varushkan contributors such as Triska Markova and the Reznikovs. Karsk's citizens now channel donations through the Iron Hearth into the Virtue Fund.

Construct Prosperous Counting House in K.o: In Spring 386YE Laughlan, Master of Rings, announced the commission of a Prosperous Counting House in Karsk under the Forwards and Rewards wind of fortune. The building was completed, and it now adds 12 crowns to the Virtue Fund each summit.

Karsk.t: The Prosperous Counting House was built in Karsk, and its citizens now give 12 crowns to the Virtue Fund each summit through the Iron Hearth.

Construct Proud Quill Parcel.d: Announced in Autumn 386YE, the motion set out a herb sinecure to be planted in open land behind the Proud Quill Ale Hall in Hahnmark. The title attached to it would carry tenure and be appointed by unanimous agreement of the Wintermark senators. The listed cost was 16 wains of weirwood and 48 crowns, on top of standard costs, with three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice 386YE, Cormack Dun supplied 6 thrones and 16 wains of weirwood. Once construction was finished, the Guard of the Proud Quill Parcel became available for appointment by unanimous decision of Wintermark's senators for the first time at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's senators gain the power to appoint the Guard of the Proud Quill Parcel, a tenured herb-sinecure title, by unanimous decision from the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Construct Proud Quill Parcel.o: A Senate motion announced by the Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, Cormack Dun, commissioned the Proud Quill Parcel, a herb sinecure in Kalpamark, Hahnmark. It was later completed.

Hahnmark/Kalpamark.t: The Proud Quill Parcel is planted in open land behind the Proud Quill Ale Hall in Kalpamark, giving the region a completed herb sinecure.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark gains a new herb sinecure behind the Proud Quill Ale Hall, built with weirwood and coin provided by Cormack Dun.

Construct Publishing Clearing House.d: Taddea Ginori invited the Holberg College of Engineering to build Katarzyna von Carstein's designs. The work was funded by six Tassato guilds: the Camorra Barossa, the Gilded Horn, the Jolly Jackdaws, Oathwright Press, the Silver Rivers Casino and the Printers' Guild. It required 50 wains of white granite, 150 crowns in labour and three months to build. Its custodian, the Printmaster of the Publishers' Exchange, was to be appointed by League Bourse Auction, and this election method drew extended scrutiny. Citizens contributed granite and money after the Summer Solstice and the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, it would raise Tassato business income by 36 rings and lift the Printmaster of Cevia's income to two thrones.

The League.t: A League Chair of the Wolf announced the work, the guilds of Tassato paid for it, and a new League title would be sold by Bourse Auction, intended to make a League city the printing centre of the Empire and its neighbours.

Construct Publishing Clearing House.o: Taddea Ginori, Chair of the Wolf, announced the construction of the Great Publishers' Clearing House in Tassato Mestra. It was funded by six great guilds of Tassato and intended to make the city the printing capital of the world.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Tassato Mestra was the site chosen for the Great Publishers' Clearing House, and contributions of granite and coin towards its construction were recorded through the Autumn Equinox.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Holberg College of Engineering was invited to build the Clearing House to Katarzyna von Carstein's designs.

Tassato.t: Once complete, the Clearing House would increase the income of businesses in Tassato by 36 rings and cement the city as the Empire's centre of printing.

Construct Quartermaster's ministry.d: Proposed by Skarsind and seconded by Karov, the motion amended the title of Quartermaster General to include a ministry in Casinea through which mana could be purchased. The ministry was to use standard costs, though the size of the commission was not specified. The motion passed. After the Summer Solstice 383YE, Rurik provided 12 wains of mithril and 24 crowns towards its construction. Once complete, the ministry is to be assigned to the Quartermaster General.

Highguard.t: Highguard gains a mana ministry on its soil in Casinea, although control of it rests with the Quartermaster General rather than with any Highborn office.

Construct Quartermaster's ministry.o: In Winter 382YE the Senate passed a motion to commission a mana ministry in Casinea, to be placed in the custody of the Quartermaster General of the Imperial Armies.

Casinea.t: Casinea is the site chosen for the new ministry, where the Quartermaster General will be able to purchase mana once construction is complete.

Construct Ratibor's Gate Shrine.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Casinea, the motion commissioned the rededication of Ratibor's Gate as an inspirational memorial to the exemplar Ratibor of Temeschwar. The work cost 20 wains of white granite, 5 thrones (40 crowns in labour) and a dose of true liao, and took three months to construct. Laughlan Vi Temeschwar provided the granite and money after the Summer Solstice, and Laughlan of the Crimson Reaper Cartel supplied the true liao. Once completed it created an inspirational tomb and the Imperial title of Watcher of Ratibor's Torch, appointed by the League National Assembly.

The League.t: The League gained an inspirational memorial to one of its exemplars, funded by League citizens, and its National Assembly gained the right to appoint the new Watcher of Ratibor's Torch.

Construct Ratibor's Gate Shrine.o: The Senate passed a motion in Summer 384YE to consecrate Ratibor's Gate in Temeschwar as an inspirational tomb honouring the exemplar Ratibor of Temeschwar, creating the title Watcher of Ratibor's Torch.

Temeschwar.t: Ratibor's Gate in Temeschwar was rededicated and built up as an inspirational tomb to Ratibor of Temeschwar, a project put forward by the territory's own senator.

Construct Reapers' Repose.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion commissioned the Reapers' Repose for 10 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns, taking three months. Laughlan Vi Temeschwar provided the materials and money after the Autumn Equinox. The civil service believed it related to the proposal by Sovia Lahm von Temeschwar, Merchant-prince of the Emerald Magpie Guild, in the A health to the company Wind of Fortune. On that assumption the Chatelaine, appointed by unanimous decision of the League senators, receives 16 crowns each season, unlimited access to the restful sanctuary and three doses of Tranquil Nostrum. Construction was completed, with the first appointment due at the Winter Solstice 384YE.

The League.t: The League's senators gained a new sinecure to bestow by unanimous decision, with the first Chatelaine of the Reapers' Repose due to be appointed at the Winter Solstice 384YE.

Construct Reapers' Repose.o: In Autumn 384YE the Senate passed a motion to commission the Reapers' Repose, a sinecure in Melfort, Temeschwar, creating the title of Chatelaine of the Reapers' Repose to be appointed by the League's senators.

Temeschwar.t: The Reapers' Repose was built in Melfort, Temeschwar, with Laughlan Vi Temeschwar supplying the white granite, weirwood and money, and it is thought to stem from a proposal by the Temeschwar merchant-prince Sovia Lahm von Temeschwar.

Construct Rebellion's Ridge.d: Rebellion's Ridge was commissioned by Alfred Eawulfson in the name of Jedediah Boon, as a memorial for friars and pilgrims studying Pride and as a boost to the territory's congregations. It cost 50 wains of white granite and 150 crowns of labour, plus standard costs, and took three months to build. Eawulfson and Boon supplied most of the resources, with further granite from Charlie Skinner and smaller sums from Farren Silver Streams, Rhys Nighthaven, Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov and Erasmo di Tassato. Contributions came in between Autumn 387YE and Spring 388YE. Once complete, congregations in Mournwold receive two extra doses of liao each season, with the first arriving at the Autumn Equinox 388YE.

The Marches.t: The Marches gained a great work in its territory of Mournwold, a memorial to the Ore Hills Rebellion's leaders that gives the congregations there two extra doses of liao each season.

Construct Rebellion's Ridge.o: Alfred Eawulfson, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction of Rebellion's Ridge in Autumn 387YE, a great work in Boon County, Ore Hills, honouring the leaders of the Ore Hills Rebellion as exemplars of Pride. Once completed, it gave Mournwold's congregations two additional doses of liao each season.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: Rebellion's Ridge was raised in Boon County in the Ore Hills, the site of the rebellion whose leaders it honours as exemplars of Pride.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold's congregations receive two additional doses of liao each season from the Autumn Equinox 388YE, and the territory gains a memorial to Pride for friars and pilgrims to visit.

Construct Reckoners Reward.d: Proposed by Tassato and seconded by Karov, the motion commissioned a sinecure in Sarvos costing 12 wains of mithril and 3 Thrones of labour. It passed at 10 Thrones, which were disbursed to Senator Tassato. The holder, The Book Keeper, was to be appointed by unanimous decision of the League senators, and completion would automatically create this League national Imperial title. No location within Sarvos was specified, leaving the choice to the senator. No progress was recorded at the Autumn Equinox 379YE, and by the Autumn Equinox 380YE the commission had lapsed without being built.

The League.t: The League stood to gain a new national title, The Book Keeper, appointed unanimously by its senators and drawing mana crystals from the sinecure, but the commission lapsed before completion and the title was never created.

Construct Reckoners Reward.o: In Autumn 379YE the Senate passed a motion to commission Reckoners Reward, a sinecure in Sarvos providing mana crystals and to be held by a new League title, The Book Keeper. The commission was never completed and had lapsed by Autumn Equinox 380YE.

Sarvos.t: Reckoners Reward was to be built somewhere in Sarvos at the senator's discretion, but no work was recorded and the commission lapsed by Autumn 380YE.

Construct Red Wind Wharfs.d: Proposed by Eulàlia i Phovas i Riqueza, Senator for the Madruga, and seconded by Garviel i Abrira i Erigo, Senator for Feroz, the motion followed the opportunity set out in the Mermaids in the basement wind of fortune. The edifice was to cost 5 wains of mithril and 15 crowns in labour and take three months to build. After the Summer Solstice, Gisli i Phovas i Guerra provided 1 throne, 7 crowns and 5 wains of weirwood towards it. Once finished, any army with the Forayer quality can move normally between Free Landing and the mainland, ignoring the island quality, while the upkeep of the Municipal Docks rises by one throne.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast senators for Madruga and Feroz proposed and seconded the motion, and a Brass Coast citizen funded the work. The finished wharfs would give Forayer armies easier movement to and from Free Landing in their home territory.

Construct Red Wind Wharfs.o: In Summer 388YE the Senate passed a motion to add the Red Wind Wharfs to the Municipal Docks at Calvos, in Calvos Sound in Madruga. Once complete, the wharfs let armies with the Forayer quality move freely between Free Landing and the mainland.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: The Red Wind Wharfs were to be built onto the Municipal Docks at Calvos in Calvos Sound, raising the docks' upkeep by one throne.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Once the wharfs are complete, armies with the Forayer quality can move normally between Free Landing and the mainland, ignoring the island quality.

Madruga.t: Madruga, then divided between the Iron Confederacy and the Brass Coast, gained a new edifice at the Calvos docks that would open Free Landing to Forayer armies without the hindrance of its island quality.

Construct Reeds Roost.d: Bregasland's senator proposed the motion and Upwold's seconded it. It commissioned a sinecure called Reed's Roost in Bildewold in the North Fens of Bregasland, producing mana crystals each season. The commission cost 10 mithril and 30 crowns on top of standard costs, and the work took three months. After the Summer Solstice 386YE, Willem Tarne provided 10 wains of mithril and 3 thrones 6 crowns. The sinecure is now complete. The post of Roost's Reeve is filled annually, and appointment requires the unanimous decision of the Marcher senators.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named on the page and are linked only because they held part of Bregasland at the time.

The Marches.t: The Marches gained a mana-producing sinecure in Bregasland and a new national title, Roost's Reeve, which their senators must agree unanimously to appoint each year.

Construct Reeds Roost.o: In Summer 386YE the Senate passed a motion to build Reed's Roost, a self-funded sinecure in Bildewold, Bregasland, that produces mana each season and creates the Marcher national position of Roost's Reeve.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: The North Fens became home to Reed's Roost, a completed sinecure producing mana crystals each season.

Bregasland.t: The sinecure of Reed's Roost was commissioned and completed in Bildewold, Bregasland, at the proposal of the territory's own senator.

Construct Reikos Counting House.d: Proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by Casinea, the motion took up an opportunity from the Forwards and Rewards Wind of Fortune. It cost seven wains of white granite, seven wains of weirwood and 42 crowns, with three months to build, and was to be fully funded by Highguard benefactors. Rhesa provided 5 thrones 1 crown and all the materials, and Septus Sentinels Tower gave the final crown. Once complete, the Benefactor of High Chalcis was first appointable by the Highguard National Assembly at the Spring Equinox 386YE, and from the Summer Solstice 386YE the Virtue Fund receives 10 crowns each summit from Reikos citizens.

Highguard.t: Highguard gained a new national title, the Benefactor of High Chalcis, appointed by its National Assembly from Spring 386YE, and Highguard benefactors such as Rhesa and Septus Sentinels Tower paid for the whole construction.

Construct Reikos Counting House.o: The Senate passed a motion at the Winter Solstice 385YE to build a prosperous counting house in Reikos, creating the Highguard national title of Benefactor of High Chalcis to oversee the Gardens of High Chalcis and use their herbs for the virtuous of the Empire.

Reikos.t: A prosperous counting house was built in Reikos to oversee the Gardens of High Chalcis, and its citizens now donate 10 crowns each summit to the Virtue Fund from Summer 386YE.

Construct Reinos Spy Network.d: The motion, proposed by Madruga and seconded by Therunin, sought Senate approval to build a spy network in the Lasambrian Hills of Reinos, at that time held by the Jotun. The motion failed, so no spy network was commissioned there as a result of this proposal. The page records no vote tallies or further consequences.

Jotun.t: The Jotun held Reinos at the time, and the failed motion meant the Empire did not commission a spy network to watch the lands they occupied.

Construct Reinos Spy Network.o: In Summer 380YE the Senate considered a motion to construct a spy network in the Lasambrian Hills, in the Jotun-held territory of Reinos. The motion failed.

Reinos.t: A proposed spy network in Reinos's Lasambrian Hills, then under Jotun control, was not built after the Senate motion failed.

Construct Rhydian Sepulchre Memorial Hos.d: Announced by Arlen Foreman-Smith, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, the hospital creates the Warden of the Weary, who provides shelter and succour to travellers in Astolat and is paid 18 drams of cerulean mazzarine each season from the hospital gardens. The announcement named 10 wains of weirwood from the Castellan of Spiral Castle. Construction required standard costs, 10 weirwood and 30 crowns over three months. Tallis Hart provided 3 thrones, 4 crowns and the 10 wains of weirwood after the Spring Equinox, and Farren Silver Streams and Rhyn Huckster gave a crown each. Once complete, the Warden was to be appointed by tally of the votes of Dawn's military unit captains, first at the Summer Solstice 387YE for a reduced one-season term.

Dawn.t: Dawn gains a new hospital in its territory of Astolat, and the military unit captains of Dawn choose its Warden of the Weary by tally of their votes.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the announcement named the Castellan of Spiral Castle, in a League territory, as the source of the weirwood for construction.

Construct Rhydian Sepulchre Memorial Hos.o: In Spring 387YE the Rhydian Sepulchre Memorial Hospital was commissioned as a sinecure in Winterbourne, Astolat, creating the title of Warden of the Weary. It was later completed.

Astolat/Winterbourne.t: Winterbourne is the site of the new Rhydian Sepulchre Memorial Hospital, whose gardens yield 18 drams of cerulean mazzarine each season to pay its Warden.

Astolat.t: A memorial hospital is built in Astolat, whose Warden of the Weary will offer shelter and succour to travellers across the territory.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the announcement named the Castellan of Spiral Castle as supplying the 10 wains of weirwood for the hospital.

Construct Ritual School of the White Sha.d: In Autumn 380YE the Civilian Commissioner of the Imperial Orcs used the legal power to commission constructions, delegated to them by the Senate, to approve a mana sinecure in Pakaanan's Pass, Skarsind. Its exact cost is not recorded, though standard costs apply. After the Autumn Equinox Yargol provided 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns towards the work. Once complete, the sinecure will create the title of Storm Shaman, a national title for the Imperial Orcs.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs' own Civilian Commissioner approved the project, and once finished it will give the nation a new national title, the Storm Shaman.

Construct Ritual School of the White Sha.o: The Civilian Commissioner of the Imperial Orcs approved the construction of a mana sinecure, the Ritual School of the White Shaman, in Pakaanan's Pass, Skarsind, using construction powers delegated by the Senate.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: Pakaanan's Pass is the chosen site for the Ritual School of the White Shaman, and Yargol's mithril and crowns went towards its construction there.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind, held by the Imperial Orcs, is to gain a mana sinecure, the Ritual School of the White Shaman, built within its borders.

Construct Roads of the Sky.d: The motion took up the opportunity presented by the Road out of nowhere Wind of Fortune to establish skyways across Urizen and into Spiral. It cost 225 mithril and 675 crowns and took fifteen months to build. Funding came from many individual donors over successive seasons from Spring 386YE to Summer 387YE, with large contributions of mithril from Otmar van Holberg, Rhode, Bartimaeus and others. Once complete, the Arch of the Sky, a white granite bourse resource, was allocated as a national seat at the Autumn Equinox 387YE. The level of investment for businesses and mana sites in Morrow, Zenith, Redoubt and Spiral rose by one.

The League.t: The League's senator for Spiral proposed the motion, and the skyways brought roads and greater investment for businesses and mana sites to League-held Spiral.

Urizen.t: The skyways were built across Urizen, raising the level of investment for businesses and mana sites in Morrow, Zenith and Redoubt.

Construct Roads of the Sky.o: In Spring 386YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Spiral and seconded by Astolat, to build the Arch of the Sky, the Southern Skyways and the Bridge of the Air, creating a white granite seat and roads throughout Spiral and Urizen. The work was completed in 387YE.

Morrow.t: Urizen's Morrow was linked by the new skyways, and the level of investment for its businesses and mana sites rose by one.

Redoubt.t: Urizen's Redoubt was connected by the skyways, and the level of investment for its businesses and mana sites rose by one.

Spiral.t: League-held Spiral, whose senator proposed the motion, received the skyway roads, and the level of investment for its businesses and mana sites rose by one.

Zenith.t: Urizen's Zenith was joined to the skyways, and the level of investment for its businesses and mana sites rose by one.

Construct Root and Stem Apothecarium.d: In Spring 383YE the Senate approved construction of the Root and Stem Apothecarium in Meade, Mitwold, taking up a limited, self-funded opportunity. The project needed 8 wains of weirwood, 16 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Spring Equinox William Lowther supplied 4 wains of weirwood, and Will Talbot supplied a further 4 wains of weirwood and 2 Thrones. Once complete, the ministry will create a new Imperial title, the Master of the Root and Stem, to be appointed nationally by the Bourse.

The Marches.t: Marchers took the lead on the project, with their senators proposing and seconding it and Marcher donors supplying the weirwood. The resulting ministry brings a new Bourse-appointed title, the Master of the Root and Stem, into the nation's Bladeroot trade.

Construct Root and Stem Apothecarium.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by Mitwold's senator and seconded by Mournwold's, to build the Root and Stem Apothecarium, a Kruidenkenner warehouse in the town of Meade trading specifically in Bladeroot.

Mitwold/Meade March.t: The Root and Stem Apothecarium is to be built in the town of Meade, with three months of construction once the weirwood and labour costs are met.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold is to gain a Kruidenkenner warehouse dedicated to the Bladeroot trade, built in its town of Meade at its own senator's proposal.

Construct Rose Towers.d: Announced under a Wayleave, the Rose Towers would create the Imperial title The Queen's Rose, with custodianship of a place of pilgrimage that provides 12 doses of liao and 24 votes in the Imperial Synod. Although the wayleave referred to Semmer's Rose, the work actually uses the minor fortifications at Lacre in Lacuve, replacing the minor benefits they provided. It cost 15 wains of white granite and 30 crowns and takes three months to complete. Sandro Visconti di Sarvos supplied the materials after the Spring Equinox 382YE. Unusually, the title is appointed annually by the Throne as Monarch of Dawn, supported by Dawnish national assembly statements; without a Throne it cannot be appointed.

Dawn.t: Dawn gains a pilgrimage sinecure, The Queen's Rose, in its own lands, and its national assembly's recognition of the Empress as Queen of Dawn secured the Throne's right to appoint the title.

Construct Rose Towers.o: In Winter 381YE Sandro Visconti di Sarvos, bearing an Imperial Wayleave, announced a commission to build the Rose Towers in Semmerholm, a sinecure providing 12 doses of liao and 24 Synod votes; the commission passed.

Semmerholm/Lacuve.t: The minor fortifications at Lacre in Lacuve are converted into the Rose Towers, replacing their previous minor benefits with a place of pilgrimage.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm is the site of the Rose Towers, a new place of pilgrimage yielding liao and Synod votes, built in place of existing minor fortification benefits.

Construct Rose's Respite.d: Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, Master of Rings, used his authority to announce the building of Rose's Respite, a sinecure producing herbs, in The Chase region of Astolat. The project cost 16 wains of weirwood and 6 thrones in labour, and was expected to take three months to construct. The announcement was self-funded, and Laughlan provided the full weirwood and thrones after the Autumn Equinox 388YE. Once complete, the title of Keeper of Rose's Respite would be appointed by the Senators of Dawn.

Dawn.t: Dawn's senators would gain the right to appoint the Keeper of Rose's Respite, a new herb sinecure built on Dawnish land in Astolat.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the announcement was made and paid for by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, whose name ties him to the League city of Temeschwar.

Construct Rose's Respite.o: In Autumn 388YE the Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, announced the construction of Rose's Respite, a self-funded herb sinecure in The Chase in Astolat.

Astolat/The Chase.t: The Chase was chosen as the site of Rose's Respite, a herb sinecure whose Keeper would be appointed by the Senators of Dawn.

Astolat.t: Astolat was to gain a new herb sinecure, Rose's Respite, taking three months to build.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory appears only in the name of the Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar.

Construct Runeforge in Hahnmark.d: The motion authorised construction of a runeforge in Hahnmark at a cost of 45 wains of weirwood, 30 wains of white granite and 30 wains of mithril, with a year needed to build it. Materials arrived in instalments through 385YE. Derowen supplied the largest share: all 30 wains of white granite, 24 wains of mithril and 44 wains of weirwood. Lumi Warmthbringer, Æthwin Aldwynson, Kaapo Kingfishering, Arsenio Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato and Erasmo di Tassato provided smaller contributions. Once finished, the new post of Keeper of the Runegrott was to be filled for the first time by a Tally of the Votes among the military unit captains of Wintermark at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gained a runeforge in its own territory, and the captains of its military units were given the right to choose the first Keeper of the Runegrott by Tally of the Votes.

Construct Runeforge in Hahnmark.o: In Spring 385YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Hahnmark and seconded by Sermersuaq, to build a runeforge in Hahnmark as set out in the Snow might fall wind of fortune. The runeforge was completed, and its first Keeper of the Runegrott was due to be chosen at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

Hahnmark.t: The runeforge was built in Hahnmark under a motion proposed by Hahnmark's own senator, and it was completed using materials supplied by several donors over 385YE.

Construct Runesmith's Caution.d: Announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, Master of Rings, the commission created a money sinecure teaching rune lore. The school also tells the tale of Wayland, Thane of the Proud Quill, who broke his oath by sharing Runesmith's Law with people of other nations. It was to be self-funded by his friend Cormack Dun Farstrider, editor of The Oathwright, and the people of Wintermark. Cormack Dun supplied most of the 10 wains of white granite and the labour costs, and Rhys Nighthaven gave 1 crown. Once complete, it created the Wintermark national title Dean of Runesmith's Caution. The Dean was first to be appointed at the Summer Solstice 388YE by tally of the votes of Wintermark military unit captains.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Wayland Runesmith's Caution, whom the school commemorates, died fighting the Druj in Summer 386YE.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the commission was announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar in his role as Master of Rings.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gained a rune lore school honouring one of its fallen thanes, funded by its own people. It also gained a new national title, Dean of Runesmith's Caution, chosen by its military unit captains.

Construct Runesmith's Caution.o: In Spring 388YE the Imperial Senate commissioned Runesmith's Caution, a white granite school for Wintermark artisans in Kalpamark, Hahnmark. The sinecure honours Wayland Runesmith's Caution, who died fighting the Druj in Summer 386YE.

Hahnmark/Kalpamark.t: The sinecure Runesmith's Caution was built in Kalpamark and was complete by Summer 388YE.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark became home to Runesmith's Caution, a white granite school teaching rune lore to artisans of the Mark.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar appears only in the name of the announcing Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar.

Construct Runic Hearth of Adamant.d: The Runic Hearth of Adamant is a door to be placed at the bottom of Lorenzo's Deep Pockets. It is meant to stop the trogoni amassing an army there to threaten Hahnmark, Temeschwar, Upwold and Miaren. Its non-standard cost was 10 wains of mithril, 25 ingots of green iron and 25 ingots of orichalcum. The announcement named Torbrytan Dunning, Delver of the Depths, and Brianne Stormborn as the providers. The progress record shows Tobrytan Dunning supplying all of the materials after the Winter Solstice 383YE. The commission did not count towards the limit on commissions. Once completed, the seal still has to be installed in the sinkhole.

Navarr.t: Navarr's territory of Miaren is one of the four lands the seal is meant to shield from a trogoni army rising out of Lorenzo's Deep Pockets.

The League.t: The League's territory of Temeschwar is among the lands the ward is intended to protect from trogoni massing below ground.

The Marches.t: The Marches' territory of Upwold is named as one of the lands threatened by the trogoni that the Runic Hearth is built to guard against.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Hahnmark is among the threatened lands. The materials were provided by Torbrytan Dunning, Delver of the Depths, and Brianne Stormborn.

Construct Runic Hearth of Adamant.o: In Winter 383YE Sagua i'Ezmara, Master of the Koboldi, announced that the Koboldi would build the Runic Hearth of Adamant, a door to seal the bottom of Lorenzo's Deep Pockets against the trogoni. It was commissioned as a ward under the Stone and stone wind of fortune.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark is named as a territory at risk from a trogoni army gathering in Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, which the sealed door is meant to prevent.

Miaren.t: Miaren is one of the four territories the Runic Hearth of Adamant is intended to protect from trogoni emerging from below.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar is listed among the territories the trogoni could threaten if they amass an army, which this ward is designed to stop.

Upwold.t: Upwold is one of the territories the seal at the bottom of Lorenzo's Deep Pockets is meant to safeguard against a trogoni host.

Construct Sakari's Legacy.d: Invoking Adamant's Aid, an opportunity linked to the Sound and vision Wind of Fortune, the Master of the Koboldi announced a fortification named Sakari's Legacy in Anduzjasse. The boon makes it a rank two fortification that is unbreakable and quicker to raise. It costs 180 wains of white granite and 540 crowns in labour, with twelve months listed for construction. After the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox of 388YE, contributions of granite and money came from various citizens, led by Isario i Riqueza with 52 wains of granite and 3 thrones, and Cosme i Zuhri i Guerra with 3 wains and 11 thrones. Once complete, the fortification will have its bastion in Anduzjasse.

The Brass Coast.t: Many Freeborn, especially of the Riqueza and Guerra families, gave granite and money towards a permanent, unbreakable rank two fortification to defend their homeland of Segura.

Construct Sakari's Legacy.o: Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, Master of the Koboldi, announced the construction of Sakari's Legacy, a rank two fortification in Anduzjasse, Segura, built with Adamant's Aid to be unbreakable.

Segura/Anduzjasse.t: Anduzjasse was chosen as the site of the bastion of Sakari's Legacy, with construction under way and funded through 388YE.

Segura.t: Segura is to gain Sakari's Legacy, an unbreakable rank two fortification that will strengthen the territory's defences once complete.

Construct Sanctuary for Justicars.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Kahraman and seconded by the senator for Bastion. The sanctuary was to cost 15 wains of white granite and 30 crowns in labour, with the crowns to be provided by the High Exorcist, and would take three months to build. Once complete it would allow the appointment of a new title, the Justicar of Osseini, serving as a ministry for exorcism. After the Spring Equinox, Delara of the House of the Wanderer provided 3 thrones 5 crowns and the full 15 wains of white granite, and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov provided 1 crown. The page does not record the sanctuary as completed.

Grendel.t: The sanctuary was to be built on the Isle of the Osseini in Grendel-held Feroz, which would place a new Imperial ministry for exorcism, the Justicar of Osseini, on Grendel's island.

Construct Sanctuary for Justicars.o: In Spring 384YE the Senate passed a motion, at 70 thrones, to build a sanctuary for justicars on the Isle of the Osseini in Feroz, following the opportunity described in the Bones in the ocean wind of fortune.

Feroz.t: The Isle of the Osseini in Feroz was chosen as the site of the justicars' sanctuary, which would take three months to build and would create the title Justicar of Osseini once finished.

Construct Sarcombe Metal Market.d: Proposed by the Senator for Mournwold and seconded by Bregasland, the motion sought a self-funded ministry at Sarcombe whose holder, the Keeper of Metal, would be appointed annually by agreement of the Marcher Senators and could be revoked by the Marcher assembly. The commission used standard costs. After the Autumn Equinox 382YE, Landon of Longridge provided 20 wains of mithril and 5 Thrones to complete it. The finished ministry created an Imperial title, Master of Sarcombe Metal Market, and is expected to help secure the economic stability of the market town of Sarcombe.

The Marches.t: The Marches gained a metal-trading ministry under its own control. The Marcher Senators agree its holder each year, and the Marcher assembly can revoke the appointment.

Construct Sarcombe Metal Market.o: In Autumn 382YE the Senate passed in principle a motion to commission a ministry in Sarcombe, Mournwold, allowing the purchase of metals. It was later built as the Sarcombe Metal Market.

Mournwold.t: The ministry was built in the market town of Sarcombe, where it is expected to help secure the town's economic stability.

Construct Sarcombe Register.d: Proposed by the senator for Bregasland and seconded by the senator for Feroz, the motion sought to take up the opportunity to build the Sarcombe Register in the newly established market town of Sarcombe. The folly would have allowed orphans to be registered with the aim of finding them new families, and would have created the position of Custodian of the Registry, appointed for life by the Marcher senators and revocable by the Marcher Assembly. The motion failed, so the folly was not commissioned and no Custodian was created.

The Marches.t: The Marches lost a proposed folly that would have helped find families for orphans, along with a new Custodian of the Registry title that Marcher senators would have appointed and the Marcher Assembly could have revoked.

Construct Sarcombe Register.o: In Autumn 382YE the Senate considered a motion to commission a folly called the Sarcombe Register in the new market town of Sarcombe, Mournwold, to register orphans and find them new families; the motion failed.

Mournwold.t: The orphan registry planned for the new market town of Sarcombe in the Mournwold was not built after the motion failed.

Construct Sarcombe Register II.d: Proposed by the senator for Bregasland and seconded by the senator for Skarsind, the motion commissioned the Sarcombe Register as a folly in the newly established market town of Sarcombe. It created the position of Custodian of the Registry, appointed for life by the Marcher senators and revocable by the Marcher Assembly. The commission used non-standard costs of 6 wains of white granite and 12 crowns of labour, with three months to complete. Orrick of House Bolholt provided the granite and crowns after the Spring Equinox 383YE. Once built, the Register helped friars find families willing to take in orphans.

The Marches.t: Marcher senators gained the power to appoint a Custodian of the Registry for life, subject to revocation by the Marcher Assembly, and Orrick of House Bolholt funded the construction.

Construct Sarcombe Register II.o: The Senate passed a motion in Winter 382YE to commission a folly called the Sarcombe Register in the new market town of Sarcombe, Mournwold, to register orphans and find them new families.

Mournwold.t: Sarcombe in the Mournwold became home to the Register, where friars worked to place the territory's orphans with willing families.

Construct Sarcophan Delves Embassy.d: The motion passed at a cost of 200 thrones, which were disbursed to Senator Mitwold. Construction also needed 25 wains of weirwood, 25 wains of white granite and 12 thrones in labour, and took three months. Thanmir Hrafnar supplied all of these materials and labour costs. The motion did not say where the embassy should stand, so the senator for Mitwold chose the City of Cargo in Redoubt. Completing the embassy automatically created a new Imperial title, Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves. Its upkeep is 5 thrones per season, paid from the Senate's budget.

Urizen.t: The Empire's new embassy to the Sarcophan Delves stands in the Urizen-held territory of Redoubt, which gives the nation a hosting role in the Empire's formal relations with the Sarcophan Delves.

Construct Sarcophan Delves Embassy.o: In Summer 380YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Mitwold and seconded by Kahraman, to build an Imperial embassy to the Sarcophan Delves. The embassy was completed in the City of Cargo in Redoubt.

Redoubt.t: The completed embassy was built in the City of Cargo in Redoubt, where the senator for Mitwold chose to site it.

Construct Sarvos Mana Exchange.d: The motion sought to exploit the opportunity created by the Tassato Mana Ministry by building a second ministry in Sarvos to oversee the purchase and sale of crystal mana. It passed, at a cost of 12 mithril and 24 crowns and three months' construction. After the Winter Solstice 381YE Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar provided the 12 wains of mithril and the 24 crowns. On completion the project will create the Sarvos Mana Exchange ministry and a new Imperial title, the Steward of the Sarvos Mana Exchange, to oversee it, with the position appointed by the League.

The League.t: The League gains a second mana ministry and a new national title, the Steward of the Sarvos Mana Exchange, strengthening its hold on the Empire's crystal mana trade.

Construct Sarvos Mana Exchange.o: In Winter 381YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Tassato's senator and seconded by Astolat's, to build a mana ministry in Sarvos for buying and selling crystal mana, assigned as a League national position.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos is to host the new Sarvos Mana Exchange, a ministry overseeing the purchase and sale of crystal mana, due to take three months to build.

Tassato.t: Tassato's senator proposed the motion, which builds on the opportunity created by the existing Tassato Mana Ministry.

Construct Scholars of the Sword Academy.d: The announcement, made in Autumn 384YE under an Imperial Wayleave, commissioned a sinecure whose custodian would be titled the Master of Defence of the Scholars of the Sword Academy. Because the announcement omitted cost details, the Civil Service assumed the minimum size of 10 wains. Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided 2 thrones, 4 crowns and 10 wains of white granite after the Autumn Equinox. The completed sinecure creates an Imperial title with tenure, appointed by unanimous decision of the League's senators, which receives a regular stipend from the college. The first Master of Defence was due to be elected at the Winter Solstice 384YE.

The League.t: The League gains a new Imperial title with tenure, the Master of Defence of the Scholars of the Sword Academy, to be appointed by unanimous decision of its senators, with the first election due at the Winter Solstice 384YE.

Construct Scholars of the Sword Academy.o: Achille di Sarvos, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the self-funded construction of the Scholars of the Sword Academy, a white granite sinecure in the city of Holberg, which was completed after Giacomo Corvinoscuro supplied the materials and money.

Holberg.t: The Scholars of the Sword Academy, a white granite sinecure, was built in the city of Holberg, and its custodian will draw a regular stipend from the college.

Construct Semmerholm Counting House.d: The commission cost 5 wains of weirwood, 5 wains of white granite and 30 crowns, and was due to take three months. Funding arrived slowly through donations from Winter Solstice 385YE to Autumn Equinox 386YE. Amicia of the Semmerlak gave the most, including a throne, crowns, all five wains of weirwood and all five of white granite. Gianluca Di Zobbras, Kostjya, Berith Relieur, Triska Markova, Rhys Nighthaven and Bertrand Gardener also gave money, and there were small anonymous donations. Once the work was complete, citizens of Semmerholm began donating 11 crowns to the Virtue Fund each summit.

Dawn.t: Semmerholm's senator proposed the motion, and Dawnish donors led by Amicia of the Semmerlak supplied most of the money and all of the materials for the counting house.
