Construct Semmerholm Counting House.o: In Winter 385YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Semmerholm and seconded by Temeschwar, to build a Prosperous Counting House in Semmerholm, a folly that increases the Virtue Fund under the Forwards and Rewards wind of fortune.

Semmerholm.t: A Prosperous Counting House was built in Semmerholm, and the territory's citizens now donate 11 crowns to the Virtue Fund each summit.

Construct Seren's Whispering Garden.d: Proposed by the senator for Miaren and seconded by Therunin, the motion sought to exploit the opportunity presented by the Eye of Serenael. Construction would have needed 35 wains of white granite, 35 wains of weirwood and 17 Thrones and 4 Crowns, and taken six months. Once complete, the great work would have safely channelled the magic of the Eye, and possibly several smaller regio, throughout Miaren. Every herb garden would have shared a seasonal bounty of 36 crystal mana and every mana site a bounty of 54 random herbs. The motion passed in principle, but the commission lapsed at the Autumn Equinox 382YE without being completed.

Navarr.t: Navarr's senator for Miaren proposed the great work, which would have enriched the nation's herb gardens and mana sites in Miaren, but the commission lapsed unbuilt.

Construct Seren's Whispering Garden.o: In Winter 381YE the Senate passed in principle a motion to build Seren's Whispering Garden, a great work in Miaren meant to harness the Eye of Serenael to boost mana sites and herb gardens. The commission was never built and lapsed by the Autumn Equinox 382YE.

Miaren/Serenael.t: The Eye of Serenael was the source of magic the garden was meant to harness and spread through Miaren, but because the commission lapsed, that power went untapped.

Miaren.t: Miaren was to host the great work, which would have channelled the Eye of Serenael's magic throughout the territory, but the commission lapsed in Autumn 382YE.

Construct Sergio's Kitchen.d: Announced in Winter 386YE by Lucrezia Corvinascura, Chair of the Wolf, the motion commissioned Sergio's Kitchen at standard cost of 10 wains of weirwood and 3 thrones 6 crowns in labour, taking three months to build. The project was organised by Red Raven Holding, styled the premier building society in the Empire. The sinecure provides coinage and is overseen by the Executive Chef of Sergio's, a tenured position held until death, resignation or revocation. Giacomo Corvinoscuro supplied the full cost after the Winter Solstice. With construction complete, the League's senators could appoint the Chef of Sergio's for the first time at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

The League.t: The League's senators gained the right to appoint the Executive Chef of Sergio's, a tenured, coin-producing position first available at the Spring Equinox 387YE, with the project funded by Giacomo Corvinoscuro.

Construct Sergio's Kitchen.o: The Senate commissioned Sergio's Kitchen, a self-funded sinecure providing coinage, to be built in Cigno, Sarvos, under the supervision of an Executive Chef appointed by the League's senators. The motion was announced by Lucrezia Corvinascura, Chair of the Wolf.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Sergio's Kitchen was built in Cigno, which now hosts the sinecure overseen by the Executive Chef of Sergio's.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos, held by the League, became home to Sergio's Kitchen, a new sinecure completed after construction began in Winter 386YE.

Construct Sermersuaq Spy Network.d: Announced by the Imperial Spymaster under the warning that "the threat of the claw lingers and grows", the commission called for a spy network to be built in Sermersuaq. It cost 10 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns, with standard costs applying, and was due to take three months to complete. After the Summer Solstice, Aengel Dunn provided 3 thrones, 4 crowns and 10 wains of weirwood, and a further 2 crowns came in small donations. Once complete, military units will be able to support the spy network in the territory.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a planned intelligence network in its territory of Sermersuaq, meant to give early warning of the threat the Spymaster called "the claw".

Construct Sermersuaq Spy Network.o: In Summer 387YE the Imperial Spymaster, Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo, commissioned a spy network in Sermersuaq to watch for the growing threat of "the claw", and it was funded after the Summer Solstice.

Sermersuaq.t: A spy network was commissioned in Sermersuaq, due to take three months to build, after which military units there will be able to support it.

Construct Shchaslyvyy Outpost Sappery.d: The Boyar of the Iron Roads announced a ministry in Ossium allowing the purchase of mana crystals, at a cost of 12 mithril and 36 crowns with three months to complete. After the Spring Equinox 386YE Radic Splinterovich Schaslyvyy provided the 12 wains of mithril and 4 thrones 3 crowns 19 rings, with a further ring in small donations. The ministry was completed, and its holder, the Custodian of the Shchaslyvyy Spile, was to be appointed for the first time at the Summer Solstice 386YE by Tally of the Votes of the Varushkan mine and forest owners.

Varushka.t: Varushka gained a new mana ministry whose Custodian is chosen by the nation's mine and forest owners, largely paid for by the Varushkan Radic Splinterovich Schaslyvyy.

Construct Shchaslyvyy Outpost Sappery.o: In Spring 386YE Borys Vardovich Strascovich, Boyar of the Iron Roads, announced the construction of the Shchaslyvyy Outpost Sappery, a mana ministry in Ossium, which was funded and completed.

Ossium.t: The Shchaslyvyy Outpost Sappery was built in Ossium, giving its Custodian a place from which to purchase mana crystals.

Construct Silver Fox Mines.d: Alexnadro von Temeschwar, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the opportunity, linked to the Don't blame me Wind of Fortune. The great work was to be named the Silver Fox Mines and sponsored by the Crimson Reapers. It would cost 50 weirwood, 50 white granite and 25 thrones (300 crowns), and take six months to build. Once complete, Temeschwar's mines would yield 36 rings and its businesses two random ingots. The Custodian of the Assayer's Guild would gain two ministry ranks, and taxation from Temeschwar would rise by five thrones a season. Donations came from the Descent Guild of Ore Extraction (12 thrones 4 crowns) and three individuals (one crown each). The commission lapsed before completion.

The League.t: The League was offered a great work in its own territory that would have enriched Temeschwar's mines and businesses and raised its tax yield, but it lapsed with most of its cost still unpaid.

Construct Silver Fox Mines.o: In Summer 387YE a commission was announced to build the Silver Fox Mines, a great work in Locul, Temeschwar, meant to support the territory's businesses and mines. It received only partial funding and had lapsed by the start of the Summer Solstice 388YE.

Temeschwar/Locul.t: Locul was the planned site of the Silver Fox Mines, but the commission lapsed by Summer 388YE without the great work being completed.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar stood to gain extra rings from its mines, ingots from its businesses and five thrones a season in taxation, but the commission lapsed before it was built.

Construct Skarsind College of Pitfightin.d: The commission required 10 wains of white granite, 20 crowns in labour costs and three months to build, on top of the standard costs. After the Autumn Equinox 383YE, Palerictus Dura provided 2 thrones, 4 crowns and 5 wains of white granite, and Bloodcrow Yargol provided the other 5 wains of white granite. Once it is complete, the College will be overseen by a new Imperial title, the Pitmaster.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs gain a pitfighting college in their homeland of Skarsind, with a new Pitmaster title to oversee it. One of the two contributors of white granite was Bloodcrow Yargol.

Construct Skarsind College of Pitfightin.o: In Autumn 383YE the Senate commissioned the Skarsind College of Pitfighting, a business sinecure in Skogi, Skarsind, which creates the title of Pitmaster. Palerictus Dura, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced it.

Skarsind.t: The College of Pitfighting is being built at Skogi in Skarsind. Once it is finished, the territory will be home to a business sinecure overseen by the Pitmaster.

Construct Smith of Ashes.d: In Summer 383YE Palerictus Krunk used the Imperial Orc Wayleave to commission a mana sinecure in Skogei Glens, Skarsind, at standard cost. After the Summer Solstice he provided 10 mithril and 20 wains towards the work. Once complete, the sinecure will create a new Imperial title, the Smith of Ashes. The size of the sinecure had not yet been set; that detail was left to the Bearer of the Imperial Wayleave to decide.

Imperial Orcs.t: An Imperial Orc, Palerictus Krunk, used the nation's Wayleave to commission the sinecure in Orc-held Skarsind and paid for its materials himself.

Construct Smith of Ashes.o: Palerictus Krunk, holder of the Imperial Orc Wayleave, announced the construction of a mana sinecure in the Skogei Glens of Skarsind, which will create the Imperial title of Smith of Ashes.

Skarsind/Skogei Glens.t: The Smith of Ashes sinecure is being built in the Skogei Glens, with its size still to be set by the Bearer of the Imperial Wayleave.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind is to gain a mana sinecure, creating the Imperial title of Smith of Ashes once it is complete.

Construct Smokehouse of Atalaq.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by Hahnmark, the motion commissioned a vast smokehouse in Atalaq with a network of supporting structures across Sermersuaq, as set out in the Write the lines wind of fortune. It was framed as aiding Sermersuaq's recovery from Jotun invasion and restoring pride to the people of the ice. The project cost 40 wains of weirwood and 10 thrones in labour on top of the motion's cost, and took three months to build. Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason provided the weirwood and labour after the Spring Equinox. Once complete, it would share 60 crowns among Sermersuaq's farms and grant qualities to the fourth Wintermark army.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the motion cites Sermersuaq's recovery from Jotun invasion as one reason for the great work.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a great work that gives its prospective fourth army qualities drawn from Suaq traditions. The Sermersuaq and Hahnmark senators backed it, and a Wintermark citizen, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason, supplied its weirwood and labour costs.

Construct Smokehouse of Atalaq.o: In Spring 385YE the Senate passed a motion, at 215 thrones, to commission the Smokehouse of Atalaq, a great work in Sermersuaq meant to restore prosperity to the territory's farms and hunters and to let the fourth Wintermark army be raised with a focus on Suaq traditions.

Sermersuaq.t: Atalaq becomes the site of a vast smokehouse, with supporting structures across the territory. Once complete, it will share 60 crowns among Sermersuaq's farms as the territory recovers from Jotun invasion.

Construct Smuggler's Cove in Salt Flats.d: Proposed by Miekarova and seconded by Weirwater, the motion commissioned a smuggler's cove in the Salt Flats of Sanath. It was framed as a way to strike at the heart of Druj territory, extend Imperial information gathering, hasten the end of the war and free subjugated peoples. The commission cost 10 white granite and 30 crowns on top of standard costs and took three months to complete. Jaromir Ostrovyn Kostka provided 3 thrones, 5 crowns and 10 wains of white granite, and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov one crown. Once complete, Imperial fleets could support the cove in the same way military units support spy networks.

Druj.t: The Druj faced an Imperial smuggler's cove built in their own heartland, meant to gather intelligence against them and bring the war to an end.

Construct Smuggler's Cove in Salt Flats.o: In Spring 386YE the Senate passed a motion to build a smuggler's cove in the Druj-held Salt Flats of Sanath, following the wind of fortune "An angry blade", to strike at the Druj heartland and improve Imperial intelligence gathering.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Although the territory was held by the Druj, the Empire commissioned a smuggler's cove there, and once finished Imperial fleets could support it much as military units support spy networks.

Construct Smugglers Cove in Ayereed.d: Dugdale's announcement declared the Empire the true masters of the Bay of Catazar and proclaimed the time of the Salt Lord over. The cove required 10 white granite, 30 crowns and three months' work, but only seven crowns were donated, by Llandun Waystone, Rhys Nighthaven, Triska Markova and Protectorate Kardak. Shortly after the Winter Solstice 386YE, mercenaries paid by Maistir Varden overran the area and the work was abandoned. In Spring 387YE Spymaster Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo announced a new cove in Ayereed, together with decommissioning the spy network in Sarangrave. Karrak provided 3 thrones, 6 crowns and 10 wains of white granite. Once complete, fleets would be able to support the cove as military units support spy networks.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the later Spring 387YE announcement decommissioned the Imperial spy network in Sarangrave, a territory the Druj held.

Grendel.t: The Imperial Spymaster targeted Grendel-held Ayereed, vowing to wrest the Bay of Catazar from the Grendel yoke and declaring the time of the Salt Lord over.

Construct Smugglers Cove in Ayereed.o: In Summer 386YE the Imperial Spymaster, Bernard Dugdale, announced the construction of a smugglers cove in the Grendel-held territory of Ayereed. Work was abandoned after mercenaries overran the area that winter, and a fresh attempt was announced in Spring 387YE.

Ayereed.t: The Empire tried to build a smugglers cove in Ayereed, but work was abandoned after the Winter Solstice 386YE when Maistir Varden's mercenaries overran the area. A second attempt was announced in Spring 387YE.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Spymaster's announcement claimed the Empire as the true masters of the Bay of Catazar and vowed to wrest it from Grendel control.

Sarangrave.t: The Spring 387YE announcement called for the Imperial spy network in Sarangrave to be decommissioned alongside the new cove in Ayereed.

Construct Smugglers Cove in Tromsa.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by the senator for Hahnmark. It called for a Smugglers' Cove in Tromsa at standard cost: 10 wains of white granite and 30 crowns, with three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice 386YE, Fedelmidd Sydanjaa's Heart Floer supplied 3 thrones, 6 crowns and 10 wains of white granite. The cove was finished, and Imperial fleets can now support it in the same way that military units support spy networks.

Jotun.t: The Empire built a covert Smugglers' Cove in Tromsa while the territory was held by the Jotun, giving Imperial fleets a foothold that can be supported like a spy network.

Construct Smugglers Cove in Tromsa.o: In Winter 386YE the Senate passed a motion to build a Smugglers' Cove in Tromsa, along with the funds to pay for it. The cove was later completed.

Tromsa.t: A Smugglers' Cove was constructed in Tromsa and completed after Fedelmidd Sydanjaa's Heart Floer supplied the money and white granite. Imperial fleets can now support it as military units support spy networks.

Construct Smugglers Cove in Tromsa Summe.d: The motion arose from the Beneath a Moonless Sky Wind of Fortune. The commission required 14 wains of white granite, 42 crowns in labour costs and three months to complete. After the Summer Solstice, Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo provided 3 thrones 5 crowns and Rhys Nighthaven provided 1 crown. After the Autumn Equinox, Rahmah provided 10 wains of white granite. The page does not record whether the cove was finished. Once complete, fleets from across the Empire would be able to take the Scout Smugglers Cove in Tromsa voyage, and Wintermark fleets would gain the Sail into the Cold voyage.

Jotun.t: The Senate commissioned an Imperial smugglers' cove in Tromsa, a territory the Jotun held at the time, giving Imperial fleets a new way to scout its coast.

Wintermark.t: Once the cove is complete, Wintermark fleets will gain access to the Sail into the Cold voyage, an opportunity open only to them.

Construct Smugglers Cove in Tromsa Summe.o: In Summer 388YE the Senate passed a motion to commission a smugglers' cove in Tromsa, proposed by Mel Bleak, Senator for Mournwold, and seconded by Ramos i Inigo i Raqueza, Senator for Kahraman.

Tromsa.t: A smugglers' cove was commissioned in Jotun-held Tromsa, which would let Imperial fleets take the Scout Smugglers Cove in Tromsa voyage once it was complete.

Construct Sorrowful Tunnels.d: The motion followed opportunities described in the Long Shadows and Sorrowful Tunnels Winds of Fortune of the 387YE Summer Solstice. The mine cost 20 wains of weirwood and 60 crowns in labour, and took three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox, Irontide Flax provided 7 thrones, 2 crowns and the 20 wains of weirwood. Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven gave one crown each. The motion stressed that only the upper levels were to be worked. Once the mine was finished, the Sorrowful Tunnels became a bourse resource that the Imperial Senate could allocate.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs' territory of Skarsind gained a new mithril mine, and their senator for Skarsind seconded the motion.

Construct Sorrowful Tunnels.o: In Autumn 387YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Sorrowful Tunnels, a mithril mine in Gildermark in Skarsind, limited explicitly to the upper levels. The motion was proposed by the senator for Mareave and seconded by the senator for Skarsind.

Skarsind/Gildermark.t: The Sorrowful Tunnels mithril mine was built in Gildermark, with work confined to the upper levels.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind became home to the Sorrowful Tunnels mithril mine, whose output became a bourse resource for the Senate to allocate.

Construct Spark of Ignition.d: The motion was announced by Berrak of The Phoenix Reach, Crystal Architect of the Spires, and was to be funded by Sarangrave Reforged. Standard costs applied: 16 wains of mithril and 76 crowns 16 rings in labour, with three months to build. The labour cost was raised by the presence of outlaw Druj in the territory. After the Autumn Equinox, Able the Taller, Esteban Ezmara, Abel the Rounder, Hector, Terentia and Vossk of Sarangrave Reforged, together with Bartimaeus, contributed mithril and money, together supplying the full 16 wains of mithril. Once complete, the Senators of Urizen will appoint the Lighter of the Forge.

Druj.t: The presence of outlaw Druj in Sarangrave raised the labour cost of building the Spark of Ignition.

Urizen.t: Urizen gains a new mana sinecure in Sarangrave, and its Senators will appoint the Lighter of the Forge once the Spark of Ignition is complete. It was funded largely by Sarangrave Reforged and announced by Berrak of The Phoenix Reach.

Construct Spark of Ignition.o: In Autumn 388YE the Senate authorised construction of the Spark of Ignition, a mana sinecure in Whisperwood, Sarangrave, built as a memorial to those who fell defending the territory. It carries the title Lighter of the Forge.

Sarangrave/Whisperwood.t: Whisperwood is the site chosen for the Spark of Ignition, with three months of building work funded by Sarangrave Reforged and other donors.

Sarangrave.t: Sarangrave is to receive the Spark of Ignition, a memorial to those who fell defending it. Construction cost more because outlaw Druj remain in the territory.

Construct Spider's Dream Bridge.d: Proposed by the Senator for Necropolis and seconded by Segura, the motion originally called for the bridge to be rebuilt with an additional white granite fortification. It passed at 240 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Necropolis, but it was amended later in the season to remove the fortification. Construction needed 30 wains of mithril, 10 wains of white granite, 15 thrones in labour and three months. After the Winter Solstice, Eli of the Cenotaph supplied 15 wains of mithril, 15 thrones and the white granite, and Giacomo Corvinoscuro supplied the remaining 15 wains of mithril. With the bridge complete, rapid army movement was restored and the Spider's Tollkeep again received its seasonal income of two thrones.

The Brass Coast.t: The restored bridge reopened a quick route for Imperial armies into and out of the Brass Coast's territory of Madruga, and the motion was seconded by the Senator for Segura.

The League.t: The League's territories of Sarvos and Tassato regained fast military links to Madruga, and the motion was proposed by the Senator for Necropolis, who received the 240 thrones.

Construct Spider's Dream Bridge.o: In Winter 385YE the Senate passed a motion to repair the Spider's Dream Bridge, damaged as described in the Dreaming in Strands Wind of Fortune. Once the work was complete, Imperial armies could again march quickly between Sarvos and Tassato and Madruga.

Madruga.t: Imperial armies could once again march quickly between Madruga and the League territories of Sarvos and Tassato.

Sarvos.t: Once the repairs were complete, Imperial armies could again move swiftly from Sarvos to Madruga and back.

Tassato.t: The rebuilt bridge restored a quick route for Imperial armies between Tassato and Madruga.

Construct Spooner's Rest.d: Announced in Spring 388YE by Eldrid 'Phoenix Flame' Vestardottir as Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, the commission created a church celebrating the life and passions of the fabled Tobrytan Dunning, decorated with many golden eagles and yellow suns. Its holder, the Conscience of the Dunnings, advises and guides the Dunning family and is appointed annually, and can be revoked, by the Wintermark National Assembly. The work required 10 wains of white granite, 30 crowns in labour and three months. Eldrid provided 3 thrones 5 crowns and the granite, and Rhys Nighthaven gave 1 crown. The sinecure was completed, with the first appointment due at the Autumn Equinox 388YE.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark National Assembly gained a new annual appointment, the Conscience of the Dunnings, which it can also revoke, with the first appointment due at the Autumn Equinox 388YE.

Construct Spooner's Rest.o: Under an Imperial Wayleave, Eldrid 'Phoenix Flame' Vestardottir commissioned Spooner's Rest, a liao sinecure in Dunhearth Hall at Wood Heath in Hahnmark, to be held by the Conscience of the Dunnings. It was completed in 388YE.

Hahnmark/Wood Heath.t: Spooner's Rest was built within Dunhearth Hall at Wood Heath, a church adorned with golden eagles and yellow suns.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark gained a new liao sinecure, Spooner's Rest, a church honouring Tobrytan Dunning that advises the Dunning family.

Construct Spy Network in Forest of Ulnak.d: Bernard Dugdale, Imperial Spymaster, announced a spy network in the Druj-held Forest of Ulnak in the Mallum, framing it as serving Imperial security, stability and victory against the "vile fear cult formerly known as the Druj". The project required 10 wains of weirwood, 20 crowns in labour and three months to build. Contributions arrived after the Summer Solstice from Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad, Triska Markova, Nathair Autumngale and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov, and after the Autumn Equinox Dugdale himself supplied nine wains of weirwood, with further crowns from Laughlan Vi Temeschwar and Ivana Petara Vodjavic. Once complete, military units could support the network to uncover information about the Forest of Ulnak.

Druj.t: The Druj are the explicit target, with the Spymaster declaring the network a means to speed the destruction of their "fear cult" by gathering intelligence on their lands.

Construct Spy Network in Forest of Ulnak.o: In Summer 385YE the Imperial Spymaster, Bernard Dugdale, announced the construction of a spy network in the Forest of Ulnak, intended to hasten the destruction of the Druj.

Forest of Ulnak.t: The spy network was to be built to target the Druj-held Forest of Ulnak, letting Imperial military units uncover information about the territory once it was completed.

Construct Spy Network in Mareave.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Zenith and seconded by the senator for Upwold. It authorised an Imperial spy network in Mareave, then held by the Grendel. The cost was 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns in labour, plus standard costs, with three months to construct. After the Summer Solstice 385YE, Ematius 'Icebreaker' Ankarien provided 2 thrones, 4 crowns and the 10 wains of weirwood. Once complete, Imperial military units will be able to support the network to uncover information about the territory south of Spiral.

Grendel.t: The Empire is building a spy network inside Grendel-held Mareave, which will let Imperial armies gather intelligence on Grendel lands south of Spiral.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the network's purpose is described as gathering information about the territory south of the League's Spiral.

Construct Spy Network in Mareave.o: In Summer 385YE the Senate passed a motion to construct a spy network in Mareave, the Grendel-held territory south of Spiral. Ematius 'Icebreaker' Ankarien, Archmage of Winter, agreed to fund it.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not named on the page, and the motion concerns only Mareave.

Mareave.t: An Imperial spy network is to be built in Grendel-held Mareave, funded by the Archmage of Winter and due for completion after three months of construction.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: League-held Spiral is used as the reference point, with the network watching the territory to its south.

Construct Spy Network in Reinos.d: Bernard Dugdale, the Imperial Spymaster, announced in Winter 385YE that a spy network would be built in Reinos. He framed it as an act of loyalty to the General of the Red Wind Corsairs, honouring a previous agreement, and as a step towards hamstringing the Lasambrians and ending the western front. The work required 10 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns and was to take three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice Dugdale himself provided 3 thrones 6 crowns and the weirwood. Once finished, military units would be able to support the network to uncover information about Reinos.

Jotun.t: The Empire moved to gather intelligence on Jotun-held Reinos, with the stated aim of weakening the Lasambrian Jotun and bringing the war with them to a close.

Construct Spy Network in Reinos.o: Imperial Spymaster Bernard Dugdale announced the construction of a new spy network in Reinos, intended to hasten the end of the war with the Jotun on the western front.

Reinos.t: A new Imperial spy network was commissioned in Jotun-held Reinos. Once complete, military units could support it to uncover information about the territory.

Construct Spy Network in Tsirku.d: Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo, as Imperial Spymaster, announced the commission of a spy network in Tsirku under the words "To unseen shores". The project needed 10 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns in labour, and took three months to finish. After the Winter Solstice Aengel Dunn supplied 3 thrones, 4 crowns and all 10 wains of weirwood, while Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven gave a crown each. The network is now complete, and military units can support it to investigate Tsirku.
Construct Spy Network in Tsirku.o: At the Winter Solstice 387YE the Imperial Spymaster, Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo, commissioned a spy network in Tsirku, and it was completed once private donors met its costs.

Tsirku.t: Tsirku, held by no one at the time, now has an Imperial spy network that military units can support to investigate the territory.

Construct Starlight Drift of Shimmering.d: The motion was proposed by Zenith and seconded by Redoubt. It created the sinecure "Starlight Drift of Shimmering Snow" in Zenith, to produce 9 crystal mana each season. The senator said the motion would be self-funded, and after the Autumn Equinox 378YE Cato, senator for Zenith, supplied the full cost of 10 wains of mithril and 2 thrones. Construction takes three months. When it is complete, the sinecure will automatically create the title of Custodian of the Starlight Drift. This is a lifetime national position, appointed by unanimous decision of Urizen's senators. The Urizen assembly, the General Assembly or the Assembly of Nine can revoke it.

Urizen.t: Urizen gains a new national title, Custodian of the Starlight Drift, which Urizen's senators will fill unanimously and which the Urizen assembly can revoke, along with a steady source of crystal mana.

Construct Starlight Drift of Shimmering.o: In Autumn 378YE the Senate passed a motion to build a sinecure called the Starlight Drift of Shimmering Snow in Zenith, producing 9 crystal mana each season. Cato, senator for Zenith, paid the full cost himself.

Zenith.t: The Starlight Drift of Shimmering Snow is to be built in Zenith at its own senator's expense, and once complete it will produce 9 crystal mana each season there.

Construct Statue Commemorating Conquest.d: The announcement celebrated the liberation of Ossium and the bringing of the Way to the Empire's first new territory in three centuries. The folly cost 3 white granite, 1 weirwood, 1 mithril and 15 crowns, and took three months to build. The motion said it was fully funded by prosperous Ossian citizens. After the Summer Solstice, Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov provided the mithril, weirwood, white granite and 7 crowns. Sławomir Rabovich Bolotstrazh gave 4 crowns, and Ivana Petara Vodjavic, Velko Perunovich Razoradze, Rhys Nighthaven and Kostjya gave one crown each. The completed statue, the Pride of Ossium, now stands in Lomaa.

Varushka.t: Varushkans led the commemoration of their liberation of Ossium, and Bolotnikov and other Varushkan donors paid for most of the statue that now marks the Way's arrival in the territory.

Construct Statue Commemorating Conquest.o: In Summer 386YE the Mistress of Monuments, Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov, announced a statue at Lomaa in the Galath Fields to commemorate the liberation of Ossium, the first new Imperial territory in 300 years. The statue was completed as the Pride of Ossium.

Ossium/Galath Fields.t: The completed Pride of Ossium statue now stands at Lomaa in the Galath Fields.

Ossium.t: Ossium gained the Pride of Ossium, a monument celebrating its liberation as the first new Imperial territory in 300 years.

Construct Statue of Eleonaris.d: Announced by Sagua i'Ezmara, Master of the Koboldi, at the Conclave's urgent request, the statue honours victories in Semmerholm, Ossium and the wider Empire achieved alongside the Knights of Glory, and the long relationship with Eleonaris. It cost 30 wains of white granite, 60 crowns in labour and three months to build. Gancio di Catazar provided 7 thrones, 4 crowns and the 30 wains of white granite after the Summer Solstice. While Sagua installed the Runic Hearth of Adamant, Amica Peddler, proxy senator of Semmerholm, took over the Koboldi's hospitality duties. The Imperial Senate ceded control of the statue in the same session, and the Queen of the Fields of Glory laid claim to it in the town of Semmer's Rose.

Dawn.t: The statue stands in Dawnish Semmerholm and honours Dawn's long relationship with Eleonaris and the Knights of Glory, and Semmerholm's proxy senator Amica Peddler took on the Koboldi's Dawnish hospitality.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the statue celebrates victories in Ossium, a Varushkan-held territory, among others.

Construct Statue of Eleonaris.o: In Summer 384YE the Master of the Koboldi, Sagua i'Ezmara, commissioned a statue of the eldritch Eleonaris at the Semmerholm end of the Golden Causeway in Lacuve, celebrating victories won alongside the Knights of Glory. The Senate ceded the folly, and the Queen of the Fields of Glory claimed it.

Semmerholm/Lacuve.t: The statue is built in Lacuve beside the Golden Causeway, and the Queen of the Fields of Glory has claimed the monument in the town of Semmer's Rose.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: victories in Ossium are among those the statue celebrates.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm gains a statue of Eleonaris at its end of the Golden Causeway, commemorating victories won there, though the Queen of the Fields of Glory has claimed it after the Senate ceded control.

Construct Statue of Murdered Researchers.d: Ada Droon Drifting Bough, as Mistress of Monuments, announced an edifice in Apulus to honour researchers murdered by the Whisper Gallery, with the consent of the Senator for Apulian. Ignacio i Zuhri i Erigo was to fund it fully. The cost was 3 wains of mithril, 1 wain of weirwood, 1 wain of white granite and 15 crowns in labour, with three months to build. After the Summer Solstice Ignacio provided all the materials, and Firesong Arachas, Fiorente Vicente d'Apulian and Rhys Nighthaven contributed money towards the labour. Once complete, a statue will be raised in Apulus.

The League.t: A memorial to researchers murdered by the Whisper Gallery is to stand in the League's territory of Spiral, approved by the Senator for Apulian and largely funded by Ignacio i Zuhri i Erigo.

Construct Statue of Murdered Researchers.o: In Summer 388YE the Mistress of Monuments, Ada Droon Drifting Bough, announced the construction of a statue in Apulus, Spiral, honouring the researchers killed by the Whisper Gallery in their search for the truth.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Apulus is the site of the planned statue to the murdered researchers. The materials were supplied after the Summer Solstice, with money contributed towards the labour, and the statue is to be raised once construction is complete.

Spiral.t: Spiral is to gain a statue honouring the researchers killed by the Whisper Gallery, to be raised in Apulus once its three-month construction is complete.

Construct Statue of Umbar.d: Using her power as Mistress of Monuments, Ada Droon Drifting Bough announced the building of a likeness of Umbar Elba Stado in Madruga. It was to demonstrate his Pride and commemorate virtuous acts verified by individuals across the Brass Coast. The edifice required nine wains of white granite, 27 crowns in labour and three months to build, plus standard costs. After the Spring Equinox, Umbar i Elba Stardo i Guerra himself provided 3 thrones 3 crowns and the nine wains of white granite. The work was finished and a statue now stands in the Lightsea, Madruga.

The Brass Coast.t: A Brass Coast citizen, Umbar Elba Stado, is honoured with a public statue for his Pride and for virtuous acts attested by people across the nation, and he funded its construction himself.

Construct Statue of Umbar.o: The Mistress of Monuments, Ada Droon Drifting Bough, announced a statue of Umbar Elba Stado in the Lightsea, Madruga, in Spring 388YE, honouring his Pride and his virtuous acts. The statue was completed.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: The Lightsea is where the statue of Umbar Elba Stado was raised and now stands complete.

Madruga.t: Madruga, held by the Brass Coast, gains a completed white granite statue of Umbar Elba Stado.

Construct Statue of that Cockscroft Lad.d: Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov, Mistress of Monuments, announced the statue in Spring 387YE to celebrate the Vigilant hue and cry raised by Johnathan Piper of the Cockscroft and to mark the site where the Wayford Wanderers and their supporters were massacred in Mitwold. The announcement stated it was funded by the Cockscroft Household, at a cost of 5 white granite and 15 crowns plus standard costs, taking three months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Bolotnikov provided 1 throne 7 crowns and 5 wains of white granite. The completed statue of Jonathan Piper of Cockscroft now stands in pride of place near the site of the senseless loss of life.

The Marches.t: A Marcher household, the Cockscroft, funded a monument honouring one of its own, Johnathan Piper, for his Vigilant hue and cry, and the statue now commemorates the Wayford Wanderers massacre on Marcher soil.

Construct Statue of that Cockscroft Lad.o: The Mistress of Monuments announced the construction of the "Statue of that Cockscroft Lad" in Maiden Downs, Mitwold, celebrating Johnathan Piper of the Cockscroft and memorialising the massacre of the Wayford Wanderers and their supporters. The statue was completed.

Mitwold/Maiden Downs.t: The statue of Jonathan Piper of Cockscroft was built in Maiden Downs and now stands in pride of place near the site of the massacre.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold gained a completed statue marking the site of the massacre of the Wayford Wanderers and their supporters.

Construct Statue of the White Bear.d: Announced by Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, Master of the Koboldi, the folly was built under the Down the Cavalier Road wind of fortune at a cost of 30 white granite and 90 crowns, taking three months. Funding came in small donations after Autumn 386YE and Winter 387YE, then larger contributions of money and white granite after the Spring Equinox and Summer Solstice 387YE, notably from Dame Aurum De Castellan, Aenar de Forteair, Ser Gaheris Torawyr, Tallis Hart and Bertrand Gardener. On completion the Eastern Sky gained Cathan Canae's favour, allowing its general to issue the Embrace the Storm order once a year, a defensive order that limits movement but strengthens the army's defence of territory.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Eastern Sky army gained Cathan Canae's favour through the statue, letting its general once a year order it to embrace the storm, defending territory far more stubbornly at the cost of heavier casualties on both sides.

Construct Statue of the White Bear.o: In Autumn 386YE the Master of the Koboldi announced a commission for a statue of the White Bear amid the ruins of the Towers of the Dawn in Dawnguard, the Barrens. Once completed, it secured Cathan Canae's favour for the Eastern Sky.

The Barrens.t: A statue of the White Bear was raised in the ruins of the Towers of the Dawn at Dawnguard in the Barrens, marking the site with a folly honouring Cathan Canae.

Construct Stockland Bounders Hall.d: Proposed by the senator for Upwold and seconded by Miaren, the motion commissioned a Bounders Hall in Stockland at a cost of 12 wains of white granite and 36 crowns in labour, taking three months to complete. It arose from the Kith and kin Wind of Fortune. After the Summer Solstice, Henry Birchsmith provided the 12 wains of white granite and Thomas Oak provided 4 thrones and 4 crowns. With the hall complete, the Marcher senators may appoint the Bailiff of the Heath by unanimous decision, first at the Autumn Equinox 387YE for a shortened six-month term. The hall also allows Marcher beaters to send their military units to support the territory.

The Marches.t: The Marcher senators gain a new title, the Bailiff of the Heath, to appoint by unanimous decision, and Marcher beaters may now send their military units to support Upwold. The hall was funded by prosperous Marcher citizens, among them Henry Birchsmith and Thomas Oak.

Construct Stockland Bounders Hall.o: In Summer 387YE the Senate passed a motion to build a Bounders Hall in Stockland, Upwold, creating the title of Bailiff of the Heath, appointed by the Marcher senators. The work was self-funded by prosperous Marcher citizens and has since been completed.

Upwold.t: A Bounders Hall now stands in Stockland, providing a base from which Marcher beaters can send their military units to support the territory.

Construct Stone Smith's Workshop.d: The workshop was meant as a place where smiths could gather, talk, keep a repository of lore and train new smiths. It also created the Stone Smith position, to be appointed by tally of the votes, and the sinecure was to be self-funded. Construction followed the terms of the related opportunity and needed 8 white granite, 8 mithril, 8 ilium and 6 thrones over three months. After the Spring Equinox 387YE Gemma Brightsmith supplied the ilium and white granite and Orrick the thrones. After the Summer Solstice Orrick, Watkin, Annie Webster and Willum of Goatsbridge supplied the mithril. With the workshop complete, the Stone Smith was to be elected for the first time by tally of the votes of Marcher farm owners at the Autumn Equinox 387YE.

The Marches.t: Marcher senators proposed and seconded the motion, and Marchers supplied the materials. The new Stone Smith title is chosen by a tally of votes cast by Marcher farm owners.

Construct Stone Smith's Workshop.o: In Spring 387YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Mitwold and seconded by the senator for Upwold, to build the Stone Smith's Workshop, a sinecure in the Woldstone in Ashbrook, Upwold. Once completed, it created the Stone Smith position.

Upwold/Ashbrook.t: The Stone Smith's Workshop stands in the Woldstone in Ashbrook, where smiths can gather, keep their lore and train apprentices.

Upwold.t: The workshop was built in Upwold, giving the territory a centre for smithing lore and training. Upwold's senator seconded the motion.

Construct Sumaah embassy II.d: The motion followed the defeat of a similar vote in Winter 378YE and passed at 0 Thrones. The embassy required 25 wains each of weirwood and white granite, 12 Thrones of labour and one season to build, with upkeep of 5 Thrones. Lucifer Son of Cyrus supplied 20 wains each of weirwood and white granite after the Summer Solstice 379YE. Cyrus, son of Felix supplied the remaining 5 wains of each and 10 Thrones after the Winter Solstice 379YE. Once complete, the embassy would automatically create the Imperial title of Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.

Highguard.t: The Empire's embassy to the Sumaah Republic was to be raised on Highguard soil in Necropolis, with that territory's senator seconding the motion.

Construct Sumaah embassy II.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Upwold and seconded by Necropolis, granting permission to construct an embassy to the Sumaah Republic in Necropolis.

Necropolis.t: Necropolis was chosen as the site of the Sumaah Republic embassy, and its senator seconded the motion permitting its construction.

Construct Sweetwater Springs.d: Proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by Bastion, the motion commissioned a great work following the plans set out in the wind of fortune "The DOOM that came to Sarvos". It passed at 150 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Sarvos, and creates no Imperial position. Construction required 20 wains of white granite, 20 wains of weirwood and 10 thrones in labour, and was expected to take three months. After the Winter Solstice Gancio di Catazar provided all of these materials and the labour costs. Once completed, the Sweetwater Springs will give a shared bounty to all herb gardens in Sarvos.

The League.t: A League city gains a commissioned defence against fire, its senator received the 150 thrones disbursed, and Gancio di Catazar supplied the granite, weirwood and labour costs needed to build it.

Construct Sweetwater Springs.o: In Winter 383YE the Senate passed a motion to construct the Sweetwater Springs, a great work of wells and fountains in Sarvos intended to protect the city against fire.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos is to gain a network of wells and fountains guarding against fire, and once completed the Springs will grant a shared bounty to every herb garden in the territory.

Construct Swords of Nearweald.d: The motion passed at 150 Thrones and authorised construction of a fortified barracks requiring 30 wains of mithril, 20 wains of weirwood and 120 crowns in labour, raised from 100 because Ossium was under-developed. It took three months to build and carries an upkeep of 5 Thrones each season. Pavuk Vid Strascovich supplied the mithril, Vesna Borkovna Prochnost provided 20 wains of weirwood and 14 thrones 7 crowns, and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov gave a crown. Once complete, it removed the underpopulated quality from Nearweald. While the upkeep is paid, it gives Varushkan armies in Ossium an additional defending order, Hospitality of the Boyars, and allows Varushkan armies to be raised in Ossium in nine months rather than a year.

Varushka.t: Varushkan citizens supplied the mithril, weirwood and funds for the barracks, and while its upkeep is paid Varushkan armies in Ossium gain the Hospitality of the Boyars defending order and can be raised there in nine months rather than a year.

Construct Swords of Nearweald.o: In Autumn 384YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Ossium's senator and seconded by Mournwold's, commissioning the Swords of Nearweald, a fortified barracks in Ossium arising from the Thousands or more Wind of Fortune.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: The barracks stands in Nearweald, and its completion removed the region's underpopulated quality.

Ossium.t: The Swords of Nearweald were built in Ossium at a higher labour cost because of the territory's under-developed state, and the barracks now strengthens the raising and defence of Varushkan armies there.

Construct Sylvihrafn Crystal Henge.d: Proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by Kallavesa, the motion created a mana-producing sinecure costing 10 wains of mithril and 2 thrones, with three months of construction. Jorma Steelhail, senator for Skarsind, supplied the full cost after the Autumn Equinox 378YE. On completion the henge creates the title of Guardian of the Cairn, which yields 9 crystal mana each season. The title is a national position, usually held for life, appointed by unanimous decision of Wintermark's senators. It can be revoked by the Wintermark Assembly, the General Assembly or the Assembly of Nine.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a new national title, the Guardian of the Cairn, appointed unanimously by its senators and drawing nine crystal mana a season from the henge, with funding supplied by its own senator Jorma Steelhail.

Construct Sylvihrafn Crystal Henge.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 378YE to build the Sylvi Hrafn Crystal Henge, a new sinecure in Skarsind that produces nine crystal mana each season.

Skarsind.t: The Sylvi Hrafn Crystal Henge is to be built in Skarsind, proposed and paid for by the territory's senator, Jorma Steelhail.

Construct Tassato Counting House.d: The motion was proposed by the Conscience of the Senate and seconded by the senator for Tassato. It disbursed funds for a Counting House costing 5 wains of weirwood, 5 wains of white granite and 30 crowns, with three months needed to complete it. Gianluca Di Zobbras and Richardo Glostari di Sarvos each provided a crown after the Winter Solstice 385YE. After the Spring Equinox 386YE, Virgil Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato provided 3 thrones 4 crowns along with the full weirwood and white granite. Once the work is complete, citizens of the territory will donate 16 crowns to the Virtue Fund each summit.

The League.t: League citizens funded the folly, most of all Virgil Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato, who supplied the weirwood, white granite and most of the money. Tassato's senator seconded the motion.

Construct Tassato Counting House.o: In Winter 385YE the Senate passed a motion to commission a Counting House in Tassato, a folly that adds to the Virtue Fund under the Forwards and Rewards wind of fortune.

Tassato.t: A Counting House is to be built in Tassato. Once it is complete, the territory's citizens will donate 16 crowns to the Virtue Fund each summit.

Construct Tekupala's Hives.d: Proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by Hahnmark, the motion acted on the 'Thousands or more' Wind of Fortune. It created a sinecure producing unique drugs in Wittal, built with the permission of the Keeper of the Bones Hives of Varushka, whose bees would build the hives of Kallavesa. Construction required 15 wains of weirwood, 30 crowns in labour costs and three months. After the Summer Solstice, Kal provided 3 thrones 6 crowns and the 15 wains of weirwood. With the work complete, the sinecure is held by the Tender of Tekupala's Hives, a Wintermark national title appointed annually each Autumn Equinox by the Wintermark senators.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan Keeper of the Bones Hives gave permission for the sinecure, and their bees were to build the new hives in Kallavesa.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gained a new national title, the Tender of Tekupala's Hives, appointed each Autumn Equinox by its senators to hold the drug-producing sinecure.

Construct Tekupala's Hives.o: In Summer 385YE the Senate passed a motion to commission Tekupala's Hives, a sinecure in Wittal, Kallavesa, which produces unique drugs. It was built with the permission of Varushka's Keeper of the Bones Hives, whose bees would build the hives.

Kallavesa.t: Tekupala's Hives were built in Wittal, Kallavesa, with Kal providing the money and 15 wains of weirwood needed to complete them.

Construct Temeschwar Counting House.d: The motion built an edifice in Temeschwar under the Forwards and Rewards Wind of Fortune. It cost 5 wains of weirwood, 5 wains of white granite and 30 crowns in labour, and took three months to complete. Sebastian Adolphus von Temeschwar supplied most of the money along with all the weirwood and one wain of granite. Askien Alanovich Vesimerov and Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar added further crowns. Laughlan Vi Temeschwar provided the remaining four wains of granite after the Winter Solstice. Once complete, the counting house channels donations to the Bloodied Rose in Temeschwar, giving the Virtue Fund an extra 14 crowns each season from the Summer Solstice 388YE.

The League.t: League citizens, chiefly Temeschwar figures such as Sebastian Adolphus von Temeschwar and Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, largely funded and supplied the counting house that now feeds the Virtue Fund.

Construct Temeschwar Counting House.o: In Autumn 387YE the Senate passed a self-funded motion, proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Kallavesa, to construct a prosperous counting house in Temeschwar that would add 14 crowns to the Virtue Fund each summit.

Temeschwar.t: A new counting house stands in Temeschwar, directing donations to the Bloodied Rose into the Virtue Fund at 14 crowns a season from Summer 388YE.

Construct Temeschwar Mana Exchange.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Miaren, the motion sought to build a mana exchange ministry in Temeschwar, self-funded and described as part of an opportunity offered by the Jarmish. It cost 12 wains of mithril and 24 crowns and would take three months to complete. Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar provided the full cost after the Winter Solstice. The outcome is a mana exchange ministry and a new Imperial title, the Magic Butcher, to oversee it. The Constitutional Court noted that the construction was not tied to any Jarmish offer, but arose from the completion of the great works known as Lorenzo's Legacies of Virtue in the League.

The League.t: The League gains a ministry for trading crystal mana and a new Imperial title, the Magic Butcher, whose holder is appointed by the League's senators, funded by the League citizen Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar.

Construct Temeschwar Mana Exchange.o: In Winter 381YE the Senate passed a motion to build a ministry in Temeschwar to oversee the purchase and sale of crystal mana, with its title holder to be appointed by the Senators of the League.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar is to host the new mana exchange ministry, paid for with 12 wains of mithril and 24 crowns from Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar and taking three months to complete.

Construct Temeschwar Otkodov Mana Exchan.d: The motion created a ministry in Hanuri, Temeschwar, costing 10 wains of white granite, 10 wains of mithril and 5 thrones in labour, and taking three months to build. Laughlan Vi Temeschwar provided all the materials and labour costs after the Spring Equinox. The ministry is overseen by the Keeper of the Tome, appointed by tally of the votes of the League's business owners. The motion intended the post to carry tenure, but a position appointed by tally of votes cannot do so, so the Speaker for the Senate was to raise an administrative motion making it a one-year post. With construction complete, the first appointment was expected at the Summer Solstice 385YE, provided that motion passed.

The League.t: The League gained a new ministry in Temeschwar, funded by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, with its Keeper of the Tome chosen by the votes of League business owners from the Summer Solstice 385YE.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule's territory of Otkodov appears in the ministry's name, but the page says nothing further about Thule's involvement.

Construct Temeschwar Otkodov Mana Exchan.o: In Spring 385YE the Chair of the Wolf, Elsha Bertolf, announced the construction of the Temeschwar Otkodov Mana Exchange, a new ministry in Hanuri, Temeschwar, arising from the Don't blame me Wind of Fortune.

Temeschwar/Hanuri.t: Hanuri is where the Mana Exchange was built, a three-month construction completed using white granite, mithril and labour paid for by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is named in the title of the Temeschwar Otkodov Mana Exchange, but nothing is built or decided there.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar became the site of the Temeschwar Otkodov Mana Exchange, a new ministry overseen by a Keeper of the Tome.

Construct Temeschwar Superlative Citizen.d: Announced in Autumn 387YE by the Master of Rings, the sinecure cost 10 wains of weirwood and 3 thrones 6 crowns in labour. Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar provided the money after the Autumn Equinox, described as paid for by his ever-increasing debts, and Laughlan Vi Temeschwar supplied the weirwood after the Winter Solstice. The resulting title, the Jewel of Anvil, is auctioned annually on the Imperial Bourse and pays 1 throne, 2 crowns and 16 rings a season from the sale of the distillery's goods. Its holder is charged with performing and promoting brazen acts of Pride, enough to make the eternal Barien admit the Way achieves his ends better than any tools of the realms.

The League.t: League citizens Laughlan Vi Temeschwar and Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar funded and supplied a new Imperial title rooted in Temeschwar, with a remit to showcase Pride to the eternal Barien.

Construct Temeschwar Superlative Citizen.o: Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, Master of Rings, announced the construction of the Temeschwar Superlative Citizen Sinecure, a distillery in Hanuri, Temeschwar, creating the title the Jewel of Anvil. The work was completed, with the title first available for auction at the Spring Equinox 388YE.

Temeschwar/Hanuri.t: The Temeschwar Superlative Citizen Sinecure distillery was built in Hanuri, and its title was first auctioned at the Spring Equinox 388YE.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar gained a new distillery sinecure whose goods fund the Jewel of Anvil, a title championing the virtue of Pride.

Construct Temple of the Way in Nemoria.d: Proposed by Feroz and seconded by Madruga, the motion passed at the Winter Solstice 380YE. Construction required 20 wains of white granite and 10 thrones in emancipated labour costs, and would take six months. After the solstice, Oria i Shartha i Riqueza provided both the granite and the money. Once the temple was completed, it created an Imperial title of liaison, charged with making sure the temple receives the liao it needs. In effect this was a ministry allowing liao to be traded for Asavean trade goods. After the Autumn Equinox 381YE it was settled that the Freeborn assembly would appoint the liaison by judgement, with the title available from the Winter Solstice 381YE.

The Brass Coast.t: A Freeborn senator proposed the temple and a Freeborn citizen, Oria i Shartha i Riqueza, paid for it. The resulting liaison title, which trades liao for Asavean goods, is appointed by the Freeborn assembly.

Construct Temple of the Way in Nemoria.o: In Winter 380YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Feroz, to build a Temple of the Way in Nemoria, the capital of Asavea. It followed an opportunity tied to the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull.

Feroz.t: The senator for Feroz proposed the motion that led to the Temple of the Way being built in Nemoria.

Construct Temple of the Winds.d: Proposed by Miekarova and seconded by Morrow, the motion passed in principle in Summer 382YE as part of an opportunity presented by the sword scholars. It cost 10 wains of white granite, 20 crowns and three months. Nikolovich Drakov and Edmundo of Damakan's Forge first supplied the materials, but the Druj invasion of Morrow destroyed the site and they received partial refunds. After Peregro was retaken, Edmundo of Damakan's Forge provided the full cost again after the Spring Equinox 383YE and work restarted from scratch. The temple created the title Envoy to the Disciples of the Tempest Jade Maiden. At the Summer Solstice 383YE the Senate passed an amendment making the Labyrinth Sword part of the Master of the Temple of the Winds' regalia, as the sword scholars demanded.

Druj.t: The Druj invasion of Morrow destroyed the first construction site and wiped out all progress, though they were later driven out of Peregro.

Urizen.t: Urizen gained a temple housing the sword scholars in Morrow and a new title, Envoy to the Disciples of the Tempest Jade Maiden, after the Druj destroyed the first attempt to build it.

Construct Temple of the Winds.o: The Senate commissioned the Temple of the Winds in Morrow, a sinecure giving the sword scholars a central spire and permanent home from which to spread their philosophy. The first construction was destroyed by the Druj invasion, but work began again after Peregro was recaptured.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Peregro was recaptured from the Druj in time for construction to begin again without a new motion or commission, though the work had to start from scratch.

Morrow.t: Morrow is the site of the Temple of the Winds, a permanent home for the sword scholars. Its construction was destroyed during the Druj invasion and restarted once the territory was partly retaken.

Construct The Gloaming Forum.d: Zorya (Zosia) Swietoslawa Przewalski, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction. The Gloaming Merchant may purchase weirwood under the opportunity presented by the Basilisk of the Bourse and the Spire of Golden Wood. The work costs 12 wains of white granite and 36 crowns, plus the costs set by the opportunity, and takes three months. After the Winter Solstice 385YE, Edmundo of Damakan's forge provided 4 thrones 4 crowns and 6 wains of white granite, and Spyridonakes of the Lighthouse-That-Was provided a further 6 wains. Once the work is complete, the Gloaming Merchant will be chosen by Tally of the Votes of Urizen's mana site owners.

Urizen.t: Urizen gains a new national position, the Gloaming Merchant, with access to weirwood. It will be chosen by Tally of the Votes of the nation's mana site owners once the Gloaming Forum is complete.

Construct The Gloaming Forum.o: In Winter 385YE a self-funded ministry, the Gloaming Forum, was announced for Operus in Morrow. It creates a new bourse seat, the Gloaming Merchant, able to buy weirwood, following the Bright yellow blooms wind of fortune.

Morrow/Operus.t: Operus is the site of the new Gloaming Forum ministry, which was funded with white granite and crowns after the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Morrow.t: The Gloaming Forum is being built in Morrow, giving the territory a bourse seat that trades in weirwood.

Construct The Legion's Rookery.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by Hahnmark, the motion sought to exploit an opportunity arising from recent changes in Doctrine. The commission cost 15 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones in labour, with three months to construct. Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason supplied all the materials and money after the Spring Equinox. Work was completed once the civil service received explicit permission from the current owner of the Hall of White Ravens. The Legion's Rookery now provides 25 votes in the Imperial Synod and 12 liao each season, shared among citizens of Skarsind who own congregations, following attendance at the Anvil Summit.

Imperial Orcs.t: The great work was raised in the Imperial Orc territory of Skarsind, so its seasonal Synod votes and liao go to Skarsind's congregation owners, giving them greater religious influence.

Construct The Legion's Rookery.o: The Senate passed a motion in Spring 381YE to transform Cardinal Atla's congregation, the Hall of White Ravens, into a great work called The Legion's Rookery in Skarsind. The work was later completed, giving Skarsind congregations a seasonal share of Synod votes and liao.

Skarsind.t: The Hall of White Ravens in Skarsind was transformed into The Legion's Rookery, which now shares 25 Synod votes and 12 liao each season among the territory's congregation owners.

Construct The Unbound Steel Hall of Lost.d: The great work took advantage of an opportunity arising from a recent period of inspiration. It cost 15 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones in labour, with three months to construct, and Ella provided all of these materials and funds herself. The museum was intended to draw pilgrims to Reikos, increasing the territory's prosperity, and to increase Pride congregations there. Once completed, it is to provide 15 liao and 30 votes in the Imperial Synod each season. These are spread among citizens of Reikos dedicated to Pride who own congregations, following attendance at the Anvil Summit.

Highguard.t: A Highborn citizen funded and announced a great work in a Highguard territory, which is expected to strengthen Pride congregations in Reikos and give their owners liao and Synod votes once complete.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named; the only link is the word "Redoubt" in the name of Ella's Highborn chapter, Reumah's Redoubt.

Construct The Unbound Steel Hall of Lost.o: In Spring 381YE Ella, Daughter of Zemira, of Reumah's Redoubt announced the construction of a Pride museum, the Unbound Steel Hall of Lost Chapters, in Tabernacle in Reikos. She commissioned it using the Senate's construction powers delegated to holders of an Imperial Wayleave.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the word appears only in the name of Ella's chapter, Reumah's Redoubt, and nothing happens in the territory itself.

Reikos.t: The Pride museum is being built in Tabernacle in Reikos. It is meant to attract pilgrims, raise the territory's prosperity and grow its Pride congregations, which are to receive 15 liao and 30 Synod votes each season once it is complete.

Construct The Wellspring of Jade.d: Acting under the power to commission constructions delegated to him by the Senate, the Civilian Commissioner of The League approved the building of a sinecure in Sarvos at standard cost, self-funded by Giacomo Corvinoscuro and Lorenzo La Volpe. After the Winter Solstice 380YE, Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided 16 wains of mithril and 4 thrones towards it. Once complete, the construction will create a new national title within the League related to the Jade Custodian. However, work could not begin until Lorenzo La Volpe set the region and production of the sinecure, which had not yet been done.

The League.t: The League stands to gain a new national title linked to the Jade Custodian once the sinecure is finished, commissioned by its own Civilian Commissioner and paid for by League citizens rather than the Senate treasury.

Construct The Wellspring of Jade.o: In Winter 380YE Lorenzo 'La Volpe', Civilian Commissioner of The League, used his delegated power to commission a sinecure, the Wellspring of Jade, in the countryside of Sarvos, to be funded privately by himself and Giacomo Corvinoscuro.

Sarvos.t: A sinecure, the Wellspring of Jade, was commissioned for the Sarvos countryside, though its exact region and production still had to be chosen before work could start.

Construct Thornsong House.d: Proposed by the senator for Therunin and seconded by Reikos, the motion took up an opportunity from the Make a deal Wind of Fortune. Construction required 120 wains of weirwood and 30 thrones, took nine months, and carries an upkeep of 10 thrones a season. Many individuals, mostly Navarr, contributed weirwood and coin between Winter 384YE and Summer 386YE. Once complete, the Navarr title of Thornsinger was to be appointed for the first time at the Autumn Equinox 386YE, by Tally of the Votes of Navarr herb garden owners. The Thornsinger controls a ministry, may address the Senate to announce a research focus, and oversees the development of new ways for apothecaries to use herbs.

Navarr.t: Navarr gained the new title of Thornsinger, chosen annually by the nation's herb garden owners, to lead potion research and control a ministry. Navarr citizens provided much of the weirwood and coin needed to finish the hospital college.

Construct Thornsong House.o: In Winter 384YE the Senate passed a motion to construct Thornsong House in Therunin, a unique hospital college honouring the territory's healers and apothecaries and allowing the Empire to research new potions. After two years of donations of weirwood and money, the building was completed.

Therunin.t: Therunin's senator proposed the motion, and Thornsong House was built in the territory to honour its heritage of healers and apothecaries. It now stands as the Empire's centre for potion-lore.

Construct Three Hands' Stand.d: The commission, announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar as Master of Rings, followed the opportunity described in The greatest city in the world wind of fortune. It cost 20 wains of mithril and 60 crowns, on top of the cost set by the opportunity, and took three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice the materials were provided in equal shares by Giacomo Corvinoscuro, Claus Friedrich von Holberg, Gancio di Catazar, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar and Lula Kleist von Ennerlund, each giving 4 wains of mithril and 1 throne 4 crowns. With the work complete, the Red-Eyed Reaper was to be auctioned as a League national bourse seat for the first time at the Spring Equinox 386YE, for a reduced term.

The League.t: The League gains a new national bourse seat producing weirwood, the Red-Eyed Reaper of Three Hands' Stand, to be first auctioned among its citizens at the Spring Equinox 386YE for a reduced term.

Construct Three Hands' Stand.o: In Winter 385YE the Senate commissioned a weirwood-producing bourse seat in Holberg at the request of the Sand Fishers, creating the Imperial title of the Red-Eyed Reaper of Three Hands' Stand, to be appointed by League national auction.

Holberg.t: Three Hands' Stand was built in Holberg at the request of the Sand Fishers, giving the territory a new weirwood-producing bourse seat.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, whose name refers to the territory, announced the commission as Master of Rings and contributed materials to it.

Construct Timbermill and Sorting Yard.d: Announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar as Master of Rings, the great work required 40 wains of white granite, 20 wains of mithril and 180 crowns in labour, taking six months to complete. Laughlan Vi Temeschwar provided the mithril, all the white granite and most of the money over two seasons, with a further contribution from the estate of the late Laszlo Gulyas von Temeschwar, who was honoured in the announcement. Once complete, it raised taxation from Temeschwar by ten thrones a season and increased business investment to provide two random measures each season. It created the Vardstein Vandal, who oversees a forest ministry caring for the Vale's natural resources, especially its wolves, elected first at Summer Solstice 387YE by Tally of the Votes of League business owners.

The League.t: League figures drove and paid for the project, and League business owners gained a new office, the Vardstein Vandal, to be elected each Autumn by Tally of the Votes, with the first appointment at Summer Solstice 387YE.

Construct Timbermill and Sorting Yard.o: In Winter 386YE the Master of Rings announced construction of the Temeschwar Drovers' Guild Timbermill and Sorting Yard in Vardstein Vale, a great work arising from the Don't blame me Wind of Fortune. It was fully funded and completed, creating the new Vardstein Vandal position.

Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale.t: The Timbermill and Sorting Yard was built in Vardstein Vale, and the new Vardstein Vandal is charged with the prosperous use and vigilant care of the Vale's natural resources, especially its wolves.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar gained a great work that increased its taxation by ten thrones a season and boosted business investment to provide two random measures each season.

Construct Tolvoli Slaughterhouse.d: Proposed by the senator for Miekarova and seconded by Volodmartz, the motion was described as a limited-time, fully self-funded opportunity. The slaughterhouse required 12 wains of weirwood, 3 thrones in labour and three months to construct. After the Summer Solstice, Misha Klubnika Alexandrovich Petrov provided 2 thrones, 3 crowns and all 12 wains of weirwood, Kostjya gave 4 crowns and Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn gave 1 crown. With the work completed, the Varushkan national title of Tolvoli Butcher is appointed each Autumn Equinox by Tally of the Votes.

Varushka.t: Varushkan citizens funded the slaughterhouse through private donations, and the nation gained a new national title, the Tolvoli Butcher, appointed annually at the Autumn Equinox by Tally of the Votes.

Construct Tolvoli Slaughterhouse.o: In Summer 385YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Tolvoli Slaughterhouse in Miekarova, a ministry intended to sate the dubik of the territory, following the opportunity offered by the Wind of Fortune "The horror and the wild".

Miekarova.t: The Tolvoli Slaughterhouse was built in Miekarova as a ministry to feed and placate the territory's dubik.

Construct Torfast Trading Post.d: Proposed by the senator for Mitwold and seconded by the senator for Upwold in Winter 379YE, the motion sought to take advantage of an opportunity to improve the wealth of Skarsind. The ministry cost 8 wains of white granite and 2 thrones in labour, with three months needed to build it. Yargol supplied the materials and money after the Winter Solstice. Once completed, the ministry created a yearly Imperial Orc position, the Bonesetter of Torfast Trading Post, appointed by the Imperial Orc senators and revocable by the Assembly of Nine, the General Assembly or the Imperial Orc National Assembly.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs gained a new yearly national title, the Bonesetter of Torfast Trading Post, appointed by their senators and revocable by their National Assembly, the Assembly of Nine or the General Assembly.

Construct Torfast Trading Post.o: The Senate passed a motion to commission Torfast Trading Post, a ministry in the town of Torfast in Southpine, Skarsind, to repair the roads and open trade with the rest of the Empire. It was completed, creating the Imperial title Bonesetter of Torfast Trading Post.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: The town of Torfast in Southpine became home to the completed Torfast Trading Post, with its roads repaired to enable trade.

Skarsind.t: The ministry was built to improve Skarsind's wealth by repairing its roads and linking it in trade with the rest of the Empire.

Construct Tower of the Dragon.d: The tower was commissioned as an opportunity arising from the Stone and Stone Wind of Fortune. Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, Master of the Koboldi, announced it as fully funded by herself and the Archmage of Summer, Mirella of the Twisted Rose, at a cost of 15 white granite and 45 crowns, taking three months to complete. After the Spring Equinox Dima provided 3 thrones and 15 wains of white granite, Mirella and Kostjya each gave a throne, and Vesna Borkovna Prochnost added 5 crowns. On completion the Archmage of Summer gained a ministry allowing them to trade tempest jade for Jewels from the Deep Mountain.

Varushka.t: A new ministry for the Archmage of Summer was raised in Varushkan-held Ossium, funded largely by the Master of the Koboldi, with further contributions from Kostjya and Vesna Borkovna Prochnost.

Construct Tower of the Dragon.o: In Spring 387YE the Master of the Koboldi, Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, announced the commission of the Tower of the Dragon in Nearweald, Ossium, an official residence of the Archmage of Summer that functions as a ministry. It was later completed.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: The Tower of the Dragon was built in Nearweald using white granite and crowns, completed as the Archmage of Summer's residence and ministry.

Ossium.t: Ossium became home to the Tower of the Dragon, the Archmage of Summer's official residence and a ministry trading tempest jade for Jewels from the Deep Mountain.

Construct Tower of the Wheel.d: Commissioned in Autumn 382YE as an opportunity based on Richard of Holberg's designs, the Tower of the Wheel used non-standard costs: 10 wains of weirwood plus 20 crowns of labour and additional materials, taking three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox 382YE, Vitore provided 400 rings and the 10 wains of weirwood. When complete, the sinecure will create a new Imperial title, the Watcher of the Wheel, whose holder can each season harvest and process magically infused plants yielding one portion each of warm ashes, vital honey, crystal fire and heart's blood.

The League.t: A League territory is set to gain a new mana-producing sinecure and an Imperial title, the Watcher of the Wheel, built to designs by Richard of Holberg and funded with materials provided by Vitore.

Construct Tower of the Wheel.o: The Arcane Architect announced the construction of the Tower of the Wheel, a sinecure in Tassato built to designs by Richard of Holberg, intended to produce mana from the realms of Spring, Autumn, Winter and Night.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the tower's designer is named as Richard of Holberg.

Tassato.t: Tassato is the site of the Tower of the Wheel, where the Watcher of the Wheel will harvest magically infused plants each season for warm ashes, vital honey, crystal fire and heart's blood once the three-month construction is complete.

Construct Townsend Treasury.d: Using the authority of an Imperial Wayleave, Bertrand announced the commission of a money sinecure named the Townsend Treasury in Sarcombe, Mournwold. Its holder, the Town Clerk of Sarcombe, is a Marcher national title appointed annually by unanimous vote of the Marcher senators at the Winter Solstice. The work cost 10 wains of white granite and 30 crowns plus standard costs, and took three months. Morgan Townsend von Holberg met the costs after the Autumn Equinox 385YE, providing 3 thrones, 6 crowns and the granite. The Treasury was completed, and the Marcher senators first appointed a Town Clerk of Sarcombe at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

The Marches.t: The Marches gained a new national title, the Town Clerk of Sarcombe, which its senators must fill each Winter Solstice by unanimous vote. They made the first appointment at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Construct Townsend Treasury.o: In Autumn 385YE Bertrand, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction of the Townsend Treasury, a money sinecure in Sarcombe in the Mournwold. It created the Marcher national title of Town Clerk of Sarcombe.

Mournwold.t: The Townsend Treasury was raised in Sarcombe in the Mournwold, paid for in full by Morgan Townsend von Holberg, and was completed by Winter 385YE.

Construct Trading Hall at Wreck.d: Proposed by Kallavesa and seconded by Karov, the motion created the Trading Hall at Wreck as set out in the Write the lines wind of fortune. Its holder, the Mediator of Wreck, is appointed by the Tally of the Votes of Wintermark. The motion's stated aim was to help the Thule feed their people and follow a prosperous path after abolishing slavery. Construction required 8 wains of weirwood, 16 crowns in labour and three months. Funding was gathered from several donors after the Winter Solstice 384YE and Spring Equinox 385YE. Once complete, the Mediator can send shipments of food to the Thule in the Silver Peaks in exchange for rings of ilium.

Thule.t: The Thule in the Silver Peaks will be able to receive Imperial food shipments in exchange for rings of ilium, a trade intended to help them feed their people after abolishing slavery.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a new ministry whose holder, the Mediator of Wreck, is appointed by the Tally of the Votes of Wintermark, giving the nation control of food-for-ilium trade with the Thule.

Construct Trading Hall at Wreck.o: The Senate passed a motion in Winter 384YE to commission the Trading Hall at Wreck, a self-funded ministry in the East Floes of Sermersuaq, letting the Empire trade food to the Thule for ilium.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: The Trading Hall at Wreck is built in the East Floes, from where the Mediator of Wreck will dispatch food shipments to the Thule.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The Thule in the Silver Peaks are the intended recipients of food from Wreck, paying for it in rings of ilium.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq becomes the site of a trading hall at Wreck linking the Imperial and Thule-held parts of the territory through trade in food and ilium.

Construct Trading Post of Karov.d: The motion commissioned a trading post in Karov, approved by the Civilian Commissioner of Varushka under the Senate's delegated power to commission constructions. Its stated purpose was to seize an opportunity to improve the wealth of Skarsind. The work cost 8 wains of white granite and 2 thrones in labour, and was to take three months to build. Nadezhda Nadyovna Gremani provided the full materials and funding after the Summer Solstice 380YE. On completion, the project created the title of Overseer of the Westward Road, a national Imperial title.

Imperial Orcs.t: The trading post was commissioned to improve the wealth of Skarsind, an Imperial Orc territory, which made the Orcs among the intended beneficiaries.

Varushka.t: Varushka's Civilian Commissioner approved the trading post on Varushkan land in Karov, and Nadezhda Nadyovna Gremani supplied the granite and thrones needed to build it.

Construct Trading Post of Karov.o: In Summer 380YE the Civilian Commissioner of Varushka approved construction of a trading post in Karov, using powers delegated by the Senate. The motion was raised to take advantage of an opportunity to improve the wealth of Skarsind.

Karov.t: Karov became the site of the new trading post, built with 8 wains of white granite and 2 thrones over three months. On completion it created the title of Overseer of the Westward Road.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind was the territory whose wealth the trading post was meant to improve, according to the motion's stated purpose.

Construct Treasure Ship.d: Proposed by Madruga and seconded by Morrow, the motion was raised on behalf of Solomon, Archmage of Summer, to win the support of Rhianos, Regent of the Eternal Sea. Once completed, the Adventure would leave the Bay of Catazar with any fleets willing to accompany it. It would seek the fiercest tempest, where its crew would lash the wheel, steer it towards the eye of the storm and scuttle it, sending ship and cargo to the deep before boarding the escorting vessels. The motion passed. Anwar i Del Toro i Riquezza provided 3 wains of mithril, 3 wains of weirwood and 12 crowns towards its construction. The outcome of the venture is unknown.
