After the Winter Solstice 383YE, Tog provided 2 thrones 4 crowns and the 5 wains of weirwood towards the project.

Grendel.t: The spy network was to be built in Feroz, a territory then held by the Grendel, giving the Empire a source of intelligence in Grendel-controlled lands.

Construct spy network in Feroz.o: In Winter 383YE Ka'bal, Bearer of an Imperial Orc Wayleave, announced the commissioning of a special spy network in Feroz, as outlined in the Bones in the ocean Wind of Fortune.

Feroz.t: A special spy network was commissioned in Feroz, taking three months to construct, while the territory was held by the Grendel.

Construct spy network in Ossium.d: Proposed by the senator for Karov and seconded by the senator for Ossium, the motion commissioned a spy network in Ossium named the Ossium Watchers. It carried standard costs of 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns in labour, took three months to build, and requires upkeep of 2 thrones per season. Vuk the Wolfeater provided the weirwood and crowns after the Spring Equinox 383YE, and the network was set to be constructed in Ossium.

Varushka.t: Varushka's senators for Karov and Ossium proposed and seconded the motion, giving the nation a new spy network watching over one of its own territories.

Construct spy network in Ossium.o: In Spring 383YE the Senate passed a motion to construct a spy network in the Varushkan territory of Ossium, to be called the Ossium Watchers.

Ossium.t: Ossium was to gain the Ossium Watchers, a spy network built with weirwood and crowns supplied by Vuk the Wolfeater.

Construct spy network in Skallahn.d: Cayleb of Felix's Watch used his authority as Imperial Spymaster to announce the commission of a spy network in the Jotun-held territory of Skallahn. The commission required 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns, plus an upkeep of 2 thrones. After the Autumn Equinox, Cayleb himself provided 2 thrones 4 crowns and the 10 wains of weirwood towards it. The page does not record the network as finished; once complete, Imperial military units would be able to support the spy network.

Jotun.t: The Empire moved to plant a network of spies in the Jotun territory of Skallahn, extending Imperial intelligence-gathering into Jotun lands.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Skallahn is located as lying west of Sermersuaq and Kallavesa, both Wintermark territories at the time.

Construct spy network in Skallahn.o: In Autumn 383YE the Imperial Spymaster, Cayleb of Felix's Watch, announced the commission of an Imperial spy network in Skallahn, the Jotun territory west of Sermersuaq and Kallavesa.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: used as a reference point, with Skallahn described as lying to its west.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: used as a reference point, with Skallahn described as lying to its west.

Skallahn.t: An Imperial spy network was commissioned in this Jotun-held territory, with weirwood and money supplied towards it; once complete, Imperial military units would be able to support it.

Construct spy network in Spiral.d: The commission arose from the opportunity described in the Wind of Fortune The Net of the Realms and was announced by the Imperial Spymaster. It called for a spy network at the Spire of Oblivion's Edge in Spiral, created with the help of the eternal Sung and ceded to that eternal, with no ongoing cost to the budget. The listed cost was 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns in labour, with three months to construct. After the Spring Equinox, Bernard Dugdale provided the 10 wains of mithril and 2 thrones 4 crowns. Once complete it would create a unique spy network in Spiral. The Constitutional Court's concern meant the matter went back to the Senate. The page is an incomplete placeholder.

Grendel.t: The spy network was to be raised in Grendel-held Spiral, though it would be ceded to the eternal Sung rather than placed under Grendel control.

Construct spy network in Spiral.o: In Spring 384YE the Imperial Spymaster commissioned a unique spy network in Spiral, to be built at the Spire of Oblivion's Edge and ceded to the Night eternal Sung. During scrutiny the Constitutional Court spotted a potential problem and raised an administrative motion for the Senate to deliberate at the Summer Solstice.

Spiral.t: Spiral was the site of the commissioned spy network at the Spire of Oblivion's Edge, funded with 10 wains of mithril and due to take three months to build, though the Constitutional Court's concern sent the commission back to the Senate.

Construct spy network in the Mountains o.d: The commission needed 10 wains of weirwood, three months' work and upkeep of 2 thrones a season. Nira of Cantiarch's Hold supplied the weirwood and 20 crowns of labour after the Winter Solstice 381YE. Work could only begin once the Empire controlled a region bordering the territory: Lustri, Occursion, Ossuary or Apstrus. The Grendel and Druj occupation of Zenith and Spiral stalled progress. The conquest of Ossuary in Spiral restored access, and the network was completed shortly before the Summer Solstice 382YE. After Summer 382YE a significant force of scouts supported it and uncovered extensive details of the Mountains of the Moon and some information about the Tsark folk living there.

Druj.t: The Druj occupation of Zenith, along with the occupation of Spiral, cut the Empire off from the Mountains of the Moon and halted work after the Winter Solstice 381YE.

Grendel.t: Grendel's hold on Spiral, along with the occupation of Zenith, blocked work on the network until the Empire conquered Ossuary and regained access.

Urizen.t: The network was aimed at the lands beyond Zenith, but with Zenith occupied, Urizen's border regions could not serve as the route in.

Construct spy network in the Mountains o.o: In Winter 381YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Casinea and seconded by Redoubt, to build an Imperial spy network in the Mountains of the Moon, the independent territory east of Zenith that Axos calls the Valley of Silence.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as one of the regions bordering the Mountains of the Moon whose control would allow work to begin.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: The Empire's conquest of Ossuary restored access to the Mountains of the Moon and allowed the spy network to be finished before the Summer Solstice 382YE.

Zenith/Lustri.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as one of the regions bordering the Mountains of the Moon whose control would allow work to begin.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as one of the regions bordering the Mountains of the Moon whose control would allow work to begin.

Mountains of the Moon.t: An Imperial spy network was completed here before Summer 382YE, and scouts then uncovered extensive details of the territory and some information about its Tsark inhabitants.

Spiral.t: Occupation of Spiral initially blocked the commission, but the conquest of Ossuary there gave the Empire the access it needed to finish the work.

Zenith.t: Zenith borders the Mountains of the Moon, but its occupation by the Druj helped stall the commission after Winter 381YE.

Construct spy network in the Sarangrave.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Karsk, the motion commissioned a spy network in the Sarangrave and passed at the Summer Solstice 383YE at 40 thrones. The listed costs were 10 weirwood and 20 crowns, with upkeep of 2 crowns per season, though the motion's own text named different sums and Cyrus of Felix's Watch as its funder. After the solstice, Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar provided the 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns. Once complete, the network will allow Imperial military units to support it.

Druj.t: The Empire moved to set up a spy network inside Druj-held land, aimed at gathering intelligence on the orcs of the Mallum.

Construct spy network in the Sarangrave.o: In Summer 383YE the Senate passed a motion to commission an Imperial spy network in the Sarangrave, a Druj-held territory in the Mallum.

Sarangrave.t: The Sarangrave was the chosen site for the spy network, and once built it would let Imperial military units support it within the territory despite Druj control.

Construct statue of Janon.d: Using the power to commission constructions delegated by the Senate, the Civilian Commissioner of the League approved a statue of the Eternal Janon in Hanuri in Temeschwar, with no Imperial title attached. It cost one wain of white granite and two crowns in labour, and took three months to build. Drogon Morosini provided the granite and the crowns after the Summer Solstice 380YE. The folly did not last: shortly before the Spring Equinox 383YE the statue was reduced to expensive rubble.

The League.t: The League's Civilian Commissioner approved this folly to Janon on League soil, and a League citizen, Drogon Morosini, paid for its construction.

Construct statue of Janon.o: In Summer 380YE the Civilian Commissioner of the League approved the construction of a folly to the Eternal Janon in Hanuri, Temeschwar, intended to encourage good relations.

Temeschwar/Hanuri.t: Hanuri was the site of the statue of Janon, built from 380YE and destroyed shortly before the Spring Equinox 383YE.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar gained a white granite statue of the Eternal Janon, which was later reduced to rubble shortly before the Spring Equinox 383YE.

Construct summer sinecure.d: Using the power to commission mana structures, the Arcane Architect declared the construction of a highly efficient, self-funded summer sinecure in Reikos. Its cost was unknown, and after the Summer Solstice 382YE Vittore provided 3 white granite, 3 weirwood and 12 crowns towards it. The Architect still needed to supply further details, including the region and how the title would be appointed. Because the Architect's powers strictly covered structures producing crystal mana, and summer vis is not crystal mana, the Constitutional Court asked the Senate for guidance; Senators confirmed they intended vis-producing structures to fall within the Architect's remit. The Architect was assumed to hold a suitable opportunity.

Highguard.t: As holder of Reikos, Highguard would see a new summer vis sinecure and its Imperial title, Keeper of the Cox, established within its lands once the work is completed.

Construct summer sinecure.o: The Arcane Architect announced in Spring 382YE that they would use their power to commission a self-funded summer mana sinecure in Reikos, which would create the Imperial title Keeper of the Cox when completed.

Reikos.t: Reikos was named as the site of the planned summer sinecure, though the specific region within the territory had still to be specified by the Arcane Architect.

Construct the Azure Chorus.d: Raised under an Imperial Wayleave by Lorenzo la Volpe, the motion called for a congregational sinecure for the Brass Coast in Braydon's Jasse, Kahraman. Its holder would be chosen by the Freeborn assembly and serve for life or until resignation. The cost was 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns, which Lorenzo agreed to pay, and the motion stipulated that the title must not include the words Bloody, Red, Cleavers or Butchers. The motion passed, and Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar supplied the materials and money after the Spring Equinox. When completed, it will create an Imperial title, the Azure Sutannir, appointed by the Freeborn national assembly.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn will gain a new congregational sinecure, whose holder, the Azure Sutannir, is to be appointed by the Freeborn national assembly.

Construct the Azure Chorus.o: In Spring 382YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Azure Chorus, a congregational sinecure in Braydon's Jasse in Kahraman, funded by Lorenzo la Volpe.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: Braydon's Jasse is the chosen site for the Azure Chorus, which is to be built there with 10 wains of white granite.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman, held by the Brass Coast, is where the Azure Chorus is to be built. Its materials and labour were paid for after the Spring Equinox.

Construct the Blood Red Roads.d: Proposed by Tassato and seconded by Casinea, the motion set the cost at 360 wains of white granite and 90 thrones, with two years' construction. The roads would first connect the League cities of Temeschwar, Sarvos, Tassato and Holberg with Anvil and the territories of Casinea, Astolat and Semmerholm, then extend to Upwold, Hahnmark, Miaren, Karov and Madruga. Lorenzo La Volpe supplied materials in three instalments after Spring 380YE, Autumn 380YE and Spring 381YE, totalling 360 wains and 90 thrones. Work has begun and specialists are looking at speeding it up. When completed, farms and businesses in territories along the network will see increased income.

Dawn.t: Astolat and Semmerholm are among the first territories to be linked to Anvil and the League cities, so Dawnish farms and businesses there stand to earn more once the roads are complete.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Casinea seconded the motion and lies on the first stage of the network, promising higher income for its farms and businesses on completion.

Navarr.t: Navarr's Miaren is slated for connection in the network's later stage, which would raise income for farms and businesses there once built.

The Brass Coast.t: Madruga is to be reached in the second stage of the roads, giving Brass Coast farms and businesses there a future boost to income.

The League.t: The League drove the project: Tassato proposed it, Lorenzo La Volpe oversees it, Temeschwar's Bloody Butchers Guild funds it, and all four League cities form the network's core.

The Marches.t: Upwold is due to be connected in the later stage, which would raise income for Marcher farms and businesses there on completion.

Varushka.t: Karov is among the territories to be connected in the second stage, promising increased income for its farms and businesses once finished.

Wintermark.t: Hahnmark is to be joined to the network in its later stage, which would boost income for Wintermark farms and businesses there.

Construct the Blood Red Roads.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate passed a motion commissioning the Great Work "The Butchers Benevolence: The Blood Red Roads", a road network to improve trade and transport at the heart of the Empire. It was to be overseen by Lorenzo La Volpe and self-funded by the Bloody Butchers Guild of Temeschwar.

Astolat.t: Astolat is part of the first stage linking the League cities to Anvil, and its farms and businesses will earn more once the roads are complete.

Casinea.t: Casinea's senator seconded the motion, and the territory sits on the first stage of the roads, set to benefit from increased farm and business income.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark is to be connected in the network's subsequent stage, bringing higher income to its farms and businesses on completion.

Holberg.t: The city of Holberg is one of the four League cities at the heart of the first stage of the road network.

Karov.t: Karov is scheduled to join the network in its later stage, with increased farm and business income to follow on completion.

Madruga.t: Madruga is among the territories to be reached in the second stage, set to see higher income for its farms and businesses.

Miaren.t: Miaren is to be linked in the later stage of the roads, raising income for its farms and businesses once built.

Sarvos.t: The city of Sarvos is one of the League cities the roads first connect to Anvil and the neighbouring territories.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm is on the first stage of the network, and its farms and businesses will gain income when the roads are complete.

Tassato.t: Tassato's senator proposed the motion, and the city is one of the four League hubs at the centre of the first stage.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar's Bloody Butchers Guild self-funds the Great Work, and the city is a core hub of the first stage of the roads.

Upwold.t: Upwold is to be connected in the subsequent stage, bringing increased income for its farms and businesses on completion.

Construct the Celesti Lighthouse.d: Using construction powers delegated by the Senate, the Civilian Commissioner of the Brass Coast approved a motion to build the Celesti Lighthouse in Feroz for 16 wains of mithril. Its Keeper would be a Freeborn ministry appointed by the Brass Coast senators, empowered to buy mana directly from ships' captains at rates set by the civil service. The commission was announced after the maximum number of commissions had already been authorised, in case the Synod vetoed one of the earlier ones. The Synod did not use its veto, so the Celesti Lighthouse commission was not authorised and the lighthouse was not built.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn missed out on a ministry that their own senators would have appointed, with the power to buy mana from ships' captains, because the commission fell outside the season's authorised limit.

Construct the Celesti Lighthouse.o: The Civilian Commissioner of the Brass Coast announced a commission to invest 16 wains of mithril in a lighthouse in Feroz, to be called the Celesti Lighthouse, but the commission was never authorised.

Feroz.t: Feroz would have gained the Celesti Lighthouse and its mana-buying ministry, but the commission was not authorised and no lighthouse was built there.

Construct the Celesti Lighthouse II.d: Acting under the construction powers the Senate had delegated to them, the Civilian Commissioner of the Brass Coast commissioned works to renovate the lighthouse lantern in Oran, Feroz. This followed an earlier, unauthorised motion from Autumn 380YE. The project cost 16 wains of mithril and 4 thrones in labour and took three months to build. Ahraz i Guerra provided the mithril and thrones after the Winter Solstice. Once completed, it would create the ministry of the Keeper of the Celesti Lighthouse, a Freeborn national title appointed by the Brass Coast senators and empowered to purchase mana crystals from ship captains at rates set by the Civil Service.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gain a national ministry, the Celesti Lighthouse Keeper, appointed by their senators and able to buy mana from ship captains. The Brass Coast's Civilian Commissioner approved it and the Freeborn Ahraz i Guerra paid its costs.

Construct the Celesti Lighthouse II.o: In Winter 380YE the Civilian Commissioner of the Brass Coast approved the renovation of the lantern of the lighthouse at Oran in Feroz, creating a Freeborn ministry able to buy mana directly from ship captains.

Feroz.t: The lighthouse at Oran in Feroz has its lantern renovated and becomes the base of a ministry where mana crystals can be bought from visiting ship captains.

Construct the Colossus of Sarvos.d: Lorenzo 'La Volpe', Civilian Commissioner of The League, used the Senate's delegated power to commission constructions to approve the Colossus of Sarvos in Autumn 380YE. The great work was to be funded by the Bloody Butchers Guild and other loyal League citizens, and overseen by Lorenzo himself. Standard costs applied. After the Autumn Equinox, Lorenzo 'La Volpe' Macelliao von Temeschwar provided 40 wains of white granite and 10 thrones. Work finished shortly before the Winter Solstice 380YE. The Colossus provides additional income to every citizen who owns a business in Sarvos and attended the previous Anvil summit.

The League.t: The League's own Civilian Commissioner commissioned and personally funded this monument to Sarvos's liberation. League business owners in Sarvos who attend Anvil gain additional income from it.

Construct the Colossus of Sarvos.o: The League's Civilian Commissioner commissioned the Colossus of Sarvos, a great work in the city of Sarvos celebrating its liberation and commemorating citizens who fell defending it. It was completed shortly before the Winter Solstice 380YE.

Sarvos.t: The city of Sarvos gained the Colossus, a completed great work honouring its liberation and the citizens who died defending it, which boosts the income of businesses there.

Construct the Deep Place.d: Proposed by the senator for Volodmartz and seconded by Miekarova, the motion took up a time-limited opportunity from the wind of fortune The horror and the wild. It built a ministry in Volodmartz costing 10 wains of white granite, 5 wains of mithril and 45 crowns, taking three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox 385YE Marzanna Verchernyaya Zorya supplied the granite, Victor Gryllian the mithril and most of the money, with further coin from Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn and Iskra Marzenanova Navratil. With the work completed, the senators of Varushka could appoint the first Bredavoi Emissary at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Varushka.t: Varushka gained a new ministry in its own lands, and its senators received the right to elect the Bredavoi Emissary, first appointable at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Construct the Deep Place.o: The Senate passed a motion to construct the Deep Place, mine workings in the mountains of Brez in Volodmartz, creating the ministry of the Bredavoi Emissary to aid the cabalists of Void and keep watch over their doings.

Volodmartz/Brez.t: The mountains of Brez were the site of the Deep Place, the mine workings built to support and watch over the cabalists of Void.

Volodmartz.t: Volodmartz's senator proposed the motion, and the territory became home to new mine workings meant to aid the cabalists of Void while keeping vigilance over them.

Construct the Dour Fens.d: The Civilian Commissioner of the Marches commissioned the Dour Fens, a mana sinecure in Graven, Bregasland, using the power to commission constructions that the Senate had delegated to them. The exact cost was not recorded, though standard costs applied. After the Winter Solstice of 380YE, Silas Merrick provided 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns towards the work. Once completed, the sinecure will create the Marcher national title of Keeper of the Dour Fens. It is a lifetime appointment made by the Marcher Senators, who must agree unanimously.

The Marches.t: The Marches gain a new national position, the Keeper of the Dour Fens. The Marcher Senators will appoint the holder for life by unanimous decision once the sinecure is complete.

Construct the Dour Fens.o: In Summer 380YE the Civilian Commissioner of the Marches approved the construction of a mana sinecure in Graven, Bregasland, to be known as the Dour Fens.

Bregasland.t: The Dour Fens mana sinecure is to be built in Graven, Bregasland, and Silas Merrick provided mithril and crowns towards its construction after Winter Solstice 380YE.

Construct the Dreaming Spire.d: Announced by Lucrezia Corvinascura, Chair of the Wolf, the commission celebrated two years of friendship and the completion of the League's reckoning with Urizen. It offered a home for the Omphalos, the Library of Solen's Doubt and all Urizen Spiralites. The work needed 26 wains of white granite and labour costs. Several citizens contributed money between Summer and Autumn 387YE, and Raine Tealeaf supplied 25 wains of white granite after the Winter Solstice, which completed the spire. On completion, any Urizen could take a new personal resource in Spiral for free until the close of downtime after the Spring Equinox 388YE. The Urizen Assembly would appoint the new Custodian of the Omphalos for the first time at that Equinox.

The League.t: The League's premier building society, Red Raven Holdings, commissioned the spire as a gift to its Urizen neighbours in League-held Spiral, and the League's Chair of the Wolf announced it.

Urizen.t: Urizen gained a home in Spiral for the Omphalos and the Library of Solen's Doubt. Any Urizen could take a free personal resource in Spiral after completion, and the Urizen Assembly would appoint the new Custodian of the Omphalos to uphold Urizen culture there.

Construct the Dreaming Spire.o: In Summer 387YE the League's Red Raven Holdings commissioned the Dreaming Spire on Mount Cinnius in Ankra, Spiral, as a gift to the Urizen. The edifice houses the Omphalos of Urizen and the Library of Solen's Doubt, and it was completed by the end of 387YE.

Spiral/Ankra.t: The Dreaming Spire was raised on Mount Cinnius in Ankra and now houses the Omphalos of Urizen and the Library of Solen's Doubt.

Spiral.t: Spiral, held by the League, received a new edifice that serves as a cultural heart for its Urizen inhabitants, and it opened to new Urizen personal resources for a limited time.

Construct the Eternal Flame of Miaren.d: The Civilian Commissioner of Navarr approved the construction of the Eternal Flame of Miaren, a sinecure in Seren, Miaren, that produces mana crystals. The commission cost 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns in labour and was to take three months to build. Bronwyn Kane provided both the mithril and the crowns. Certain necessary details had to be settled before work could begin. Once completed, the construction created a new national title within Navarr, the Eternal Flame of Miaren.

Navarr.t: Navarr gained a new national title, the Eternal Flame of Miaren, commissioned by its own Civilian Commissioner and funded by Bronwyn Kane.

Construct the Eternal Flame of Miaren.o: In Winter 380YE the Civilian Commissioner of Navarr commissioned the Eternal Flame of Miaren, a sinecure producing mana crystals in Seren, Miaren, using construction powers delegated by the Senate.

Miaren.t: The Eternal Flame was to be raised in Seren, Miaren, as a sinecure producing mana crystals.

Construct the Five Cities Military Acade.d: Proposed by the senator for Tassato and seconded by Astolat, the motion funded the Five Cities Military Academy in Tassato under the terms of the Schools and sawmills Wind of Fortune. Construction required 30 wains of white granite, 30 wains of mithril and 180 crowns, and took six months. Several individuals paid for it between Autumn 385YE and Autumn 386YE. The largest share, including all the mithril and most of the white granite, came in two instalments from Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato. Rodrigo Barossa de Tassato Regario, Rafael Barossa d'Apulian and others gave smaller sums. With the academy complete, the League can now support three armies.

The League.t: The completed academy raised the number of armies the League can support to three, and League citizens such as Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato supplied most of the materials and money.

Construct the Five Cities Military Acade.o: In Autumn 385YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Five Cities Military Academy, a folly in Tassato Mestra. Once completed, it raised the number of armies the League can support to three.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: The Five Cities Military Academy was built in Tassato Mestra, taking six months to complete.

Tassato.t: Tassato's senator proposed the motion, and the territory gained the Five Cities Military Academy as a new folly.

Construct the Gardens of Pallas.d: Acting as Civilian Commissioner of Urizen, Juliana of Phoenix Reach approved the construction of a herb sinecure, the Garden of Pallas, in Zenith. The commission cost 20 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones in labour, with three months needed to build it. Juliana herself provided the weirwood and thrones after the 380YE Winter Solstice. Once built, the sinecure created the Urizen national title of Head Gardener of Urizen. The title was later amended by the Senate in Autumn 381YE.

Urizen.t: Urizen gained a new national title, Head Gardener of Urizen, commissioned and paid for by its own Civilian Commissioner, Juliana of Phoenix Reach.

Construct the Gardens of Pallas.o: Juliana of Phoenix Reach, Civilian Commissioner of Urizen, commissioned the Gardens of Pallas, a herb sinecure in Zenith, in Autumn 380YE using the commissioning power delegated by the Senate.

Zenith.t: The Garden of Pallas, a herb sinecure, was built in Zenith, giving the territory the seat of the new Head Gardener of Urizen title.

Construct the Gardens of the Grim.d: Proposed by the senator for Karov and seconded by the senator for Volodmartz in Autumn 380YE, the motion sought to construct a herb sinecure in Miekarova named the Gardens of the Grim. Its holder, titled the Grim Gardener, was to be the repository of Chernebog's Chains, and the title was to be elected unanimously by the Varushkan senators. The motion failed, so the sinecure and title were not created.

Varushka.t: Varushkan senators for Karov and Volodmartz sought a Varushkan herb sinecure whose holder would be chosen unanimously by the nation's senators and hold Chernebog's Chains, but the proposal failed.

Construct the Gardens of the Grim.o: A Senate motion proposed creating a herb-producing sinecure in Miekarova called the Gardens of the Grim, held by a title named the Grim Gardener. The motion failed.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova was to be home to the Gardens of the Grim herb sinecure, but because the motion failed, nothing was built there.

Construct the Gates of Holmauer Park.d: Announced by Elsha Bertolf, Chair of the Wolf, the great work followed the Dear green space Wind of Fortune and was inspired by a Summer 384YE judgement of the Cardinal of Wisdom, Hembeneth i Guerra. It cost 20 wains of mithril and 60 crowns and took three months to complete. It was self-funded by League citizens: Lula and Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund gave six wains of mithril each, Lula also providing the coin, while Magdalena Teyhard von Holberg, Otmar van Holberg, Victor van Holberg and Taskel Di Apulian gave two wains each. With the gates complete, the expected influx of paying tourists increases the seasonal production of Holberg's businesses by 36 rings.

The League.t: League citizens privately funded the great work, announced by the Chair of the Wolf, and League business owners in Holberg now benefit from the tourist trade it draws.

Construct the Gates of Holmauer Park.o: The Gates of Holmauer Park, a great work securing the eight gates of the Park in Holmauer with mithril and providing a small garrison of guards, magicians and priests, was commissioned in Autumn 385YE and has since been completed.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Holmauer Park's eight gates are now secured with mithril and its visitors are protected by a small garrison supported by local magicians and priests.

Holberg.t: Holberg gained a completed great work that raises the seasonal production of its businesses by 36 rings through paying visitors to Holmauer Park.

Construct the Glass Point Cove.d: Announced by Dalibor Marek do Saverio Von Temeschwar, a holder of an Imperial Wayleave exercising the power to commission constructions delegated by the Senate, the commission called for a mighty construction to harness the natural mana flows beneath the cliffs of Glass Point. It took the form of a mana sinecure with no upkeep. After the Summer Solstice, Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided the 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns needed. Its completion automatically created the title of Custodian of Glass Point Cove, a national League position appointed by the Senators of the League.

The League.t: The League gained a new national title, the Custodian of Glass Point Cove, appointed by its Senators to control a mana sinecure that carries no upkeep.

Construct the Glass Point Cove.o: The Glass Point Cove, a mana sinecure in Uccelini, Sarvos, was commissioned in Summer 381YE by Dalibor Marek do Saverio Von Temeschwar using the construction powers of an Imperial Wayleave, and was subsequently built.

Sarvos/Uccelini.t: The Glass Point Cove was built in Uccelini to draw on the natural mana flows beneath the region's Glass Point cliffs.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos became home to the Glass Point Cove, a construction harnessing the mana flows beneath the cliffs of Glass Point.

Construct the Glorious Fountain of Dusk.d: Proposed by the senator for Zenith and seconded by the senator for Karsk, the motion would create the sinecure to produce 9 crystal mana each season. It required 10 wains of mithril, 20 crowns in labour and three months to build, with no upkeep. Cato, senator for Zenith, later supplied the mithril and 2 thrones 4 crowns after the Autumn Equinox 379. Once complete, it would create the Imperial title Keeper of the Glorious Fountain. This national lifetime position would be appointed by unanimous decision of the Urizen senators and could be revoked by the Urizen assembly, the General Assembly or the Assembly of Nine.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn appears only in the sinecure's name, the Glorious Fountain of Dusk and Dawn, and plays no part in the motion.

Urizen.t: Urizen would gain a mana-producing sinecure in Morrow, funded by its own senator for Zenith. Its senators would appoint the Keeper of the Glorious Fountain, and the Urizen assembly would be among those able to revoke the title.

Construct the Glorious Fountain of Dusk.o: In Winter 378YE a Senate motion proposed building a self-funded sinecure, the Glorious Fountain of Dusk and Dawn, in Morrow to produce crystal mana. Its keeper would be appointed by the Urizen senators.

Morrow.t: The Glorious Fountain of Dusk and Dawn was to be built in Morrow, where it would produce 9 crystal mana each season.

Construct the Golden Fields.d: Acting under the power to commission constructions delegated to them by the Senate, the Civilian Commissioner of the Marches approved a mana sinecure in Hay, in the Golden Downs region of Mitwold. Its cost is not recorded, but standard costs apply. After the Spring Equinox 381YE Slias Merrick provided 10 mithril and 2 thrones towards the work. Once completed, the sinecure will create the Marcher national position of Keeper of the Golden Fields, a lifetime appointment made by the Marcher Senators.

The Marches.t: The Marches gain a new national position, the Keeper of the Golden Fields, which Marcher Senators will appoint for life once the sinecure is complete.

Construct the Golden Fields.o: In Autumn 380YE the Civilian Commissioner of the Marches approved the construction of a mana sinecure, the Golden Fields, in Hay in Golden Downs, Mitwold, creating the title of Keeper of the Golden Fields.

Mitwold/Golden Downs.t: The Golden Fields sinecure is to be built at Hay in Golden Downs, and its Keeper will be tied to this site.

Mitwold.t: A mana sinecure was commissioned in Hay in Mitwold, and Slias Merrick provided 10 mithril and 2 thrones towards building it.

Construct the Great Chain of Sarvos.d: Sagua i'Ezmara, Master of the Koboldi, announced the project as the Steel Rings of Sarvos, using the Chain against Chains opportunity, with Merchant Prince Shauni di Vergo, Senator of Sarvos, gathering funds. It would also help Sarvos build and protect a navy if the Naval Arsenal were built. The cost was 130 wains of white granite, 260 crowns in labour, 10 thrones upkeep and a year's construction. Contributions of money and granite came from many donors between Spring and Autumn 385YE. At the Summer Solstice the Senate amended the name to the Great Chain of Sarvos. Once complete it has strength 3,000, rising to 6,000 against shore offensives aimed at capturing Cigno.

The League.t: League citizens, led by the Master of the Koboldi, the Senator of Sarvos and the merchant princes of Sarvos, organised and largely funded a defence against naval attack on one of their cities.

Construct the Great Chain of Sarvos.o: In Spring 385YE the Senate commissioned a fortification in Sarvos, later renamed the Great Chain of Sarvos, to protect the territory against naval attack, drawing on the Parents of Security Wind of Fortune.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Once complete, the Great Chain's strength doubles to 6,000 against any shore offensive aimed at capturing Cigno.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos was to gain a fortification of strength 3,000 guarding against naval attack, which could also help it build and protect a navy if the Naval Arsenal were built.

Construct the Great Library of Hacynian.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Zenith, the motion commissioned a folly library on the site of the ancient library of Phaleron in Mourning Hollow, Summersend. Once completed it would create the purely ceremonial Imperial title of Terunael Lorekeeper, to be appointed by the Senators of Navarr. After the Spring Equinox 381YE, Ranulf the Wanderer provided 3 wains of weirwood, 1 wain of white granite, 1 wain of mithril and 10 crowns towards it. In Winter 381YE the Lorekeeper title was effectively abrogated when custodianship of the Great Library was granted to the Advisor on the Vallorn.

Navarr.t: Navarr's senators were to gain the right to appoint the ceremonial Terunael Lorekeeper, honouring the Terunael heritage of the site. That right was effectively lost in Winter 381YE when custodianship passed to the Advisor on the Vallorn.

Construct the Great Library of Hacynian.o: In Spring 381YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Great Library of Hacynian, a self-funded folly in Mourning Hollow, Summersend, on the ruins of the ancient library of Phaleron. It had been approved by the Conclave through a Declaration of Concord.

Hercynia/Summersend.t: Mourning Hollow in Summersend was chosen as the site of the Great Library of Hacynian, built upon the ruins of the ancient library of Phaleron.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia's senator proposed the folly, which was commissioned to raise a great library in the Navarr-held territory on the ruins of ancient Phaleron.

Construct the Greenwatch.d: Proposed by Reikos and seconded by Hercynia, the motion ordered construction of the Greenwatch in Casinea. The ministry strengthens those who fight the vallorn, especially those who must venture into the vallorn miasma, and carries all responsibilities required by Ossegrahn, the Rain Lord. It cost 20 wains of white granite and 60 crowns and took three months to build. Contributions came from several donors after the Autumn Equinox and Winter Solstice 385YE, including Melkior of Balthazar's Vineyard, who supplied 6 thrones and all 20 wains of white granite. With the building complete, the Senators of Highguard could appoint the first Greenwatcher at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

Highguard.t: Highguard gained a new national title, the Greenwatcher, appointed annually by its Senators, with the first appointment available at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

Construct the Greenwatch.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 385YE to construct the Greenwatch in Casinea, a ministry arising from the Rain King wind of fortune that creates the Highborn national title of Greenwatcher.

Casinea.t: The Greenwatch was built in Casinea as a ministry to strengthen those fighting the vallorn and entering its miasma.

Construct the Hanging Fruit Gardens of G.d: Using the power to commission constructions delegated by the Senate, the Civilian Commissioner of Navarr approved a great work, the Hanging Fruit Gardens of Gerondi, in Serenael in Miaren. It was to cost 40 wains of weirwood and 10 thrones in labour, taking three months to build. Once complete, it would have provided an additional 75 herbs each season, shared among the owners of herb gardens in Miaren who had attended the previous Anvil summit. The work was never completed: by the Autumn Equinox 381YE the commission had lapsed.

Navarr.t: Navarr's Civilian Commissioner approved this great work to boost herb production for Navarri herb gardeners in Miaren, but the commission lapsed before it was built.

Construct the Hanging Fruit Gardens of G.o: In Autumn 380YE the Civilian Commissioner of Navarr approved the construction of the Hanging Fruit Gardens of Gerondi, a great work in Serenael, Miaren, to provide herbs; the commission later lapsed by the Autumn Equinox 381YE.

Miaren/Serenael.t: Serenael was chosen as the site of the Hanging Fruit Gardens of Gerondi, though construction never went ahead before the commission lapsed.

Miaren.t: Herb garden owners in Miaren stood to share an extra 75 herbs from the planned gardens, a benefit lost when the commission lapsed in 381YE.

Construct the Hearth of Virtue.d: Raised in Winter 382YE as an Imperial wayleave by Nikolovich Drakov, the commission was for a seminary school called the Hearth of Virtue in Perumaki, Miekarova, at standard sinecure costs. Drakov supplied 20 wains of granite and 8 thrones after the Winter Solstice 382YE, and 3 thrones were returned to him after the Summer Solstice 383YE. The completed sinecure creates a new Imperial title, the Tender of the Hearth. The title has tenure and is appointed by the Varushkan National Assembly. The in-character text had named that assembly as the body able to revoke the appointment.

Varushka.t: Varushka gains a seminary meant to prove its devotion to the Way, and the Varushkan National Assembly appoints its tenured title holder, the Tender of the Hearth.

Construct the Hearth of Virtue.o: Nikolovich Drakov used an Imperial wayleave to commission the Hearth of Virtue, a seminary sinecure in Perumaki, Miekarova, intended to show Varushka's dedication to the Way.

Miekarova/Perumaki.t: The Hearth of Virtue seminary is built in Perumaki, using granite and thrones supplied by Nikolovich Drakov.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova becomes home to a new sinecure, the Hearth of Virtue seminary, which brings with it the Imperial title of Tender of the Hearth.

Construct the Hearth of the Tempest.d: Proposed by the senator for Miekarova and seconded by Volodmartz, the motion called for a folly in Mieriada to be handed into the control of the Spring Eternal Papa Otec, who would operate it as a College of Magic specialising in the Spring realm without ongoing cost to the Senate. After the Autumn Equinox 379YE, Dušan Otecovna Zlata supplied the materials and money: one wain of white granite, one wain of weirwood and four crowns. The official Imperial work was completed. During the Spring Equinox 380YE the folly underwent a dramatic transformation into the Heart of the Tempest.

Varushka.t: Varushkan senators for Miekarova and Volodmartz brought the motion, and the Varushkan Dušan Otecovna Zlata funded it, placing a Spring college under Papa Otec in Varushkan lands.

Construct the Hearth of the Tempest.o: In Autumn 379YE the Senate passed a motion to build a folly called the Hearth of the Tempest in Mieriada, Miekarova, to be given to the Spring Eternal Papa Otec to run as a college of Spring magic at no ongoing cost to the Senate.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Mieriada became the site of the Hearth of the Tempest, a folly in Papa Otec's control that transformed into the Heart of the Tempest at the Spring Equinox 380YE.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova gained the Hearth of the Tempest, a folly given to Papa Otec to serve as a college of Spring magic, which later transformed into the Heart of the Tempest.

Construct the Lakesedge Highway.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by Segura, the motion commissioned a sinecure in Holberg under the Schools and sawmills Wind of Fortune. It required 30 wains of white granite, 54 crowns and three months' work. After the Autumn Equinox the materials and money came from several donors, chiefly Gideon of the suns of Couros with 25 wains of white granite, along with Otmar van Holberg, Lia Adelaar, Jonah Yakovitch, Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund, Claus Friedrich von Holberg, Cees Van Holberg and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov. The highway was completed, and the Rebeshof Roadwarden was to be appointed for the first time at the Winter Solstice 385YE for a limited term.

The League.t: The League gained a new Imperial title, the Rebeshof Roadwarden, which its senators elect each year, with the first appointment due at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Construct the Lakesedge Highway.o: In Autumn 385YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Lakesedge Highway in Holberg, linking the Holmauer Gate to Misericorde through Rebeshof and creating the Imperial title of Rebeshof Roadwarden.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: The new highway begins at the Holmauer Gate, linking Holmauer to Rebeshof and Misericorde.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Misericorde is the far end of the Lakesedge Highway, now joined by road to the Holmauer Gate through Rebeshof.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: The highway runs through Rebeshof, which gives its name to the new Rebeshof Roadwarden title.

Holberg.t: Holberg received a new highway, proposed by its own senator, running from the Holmauer Gate through Rebeshof to Misericorde.

Construct the Ministry of Industry and S.d: Proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Madruga, the motion took advantage of an opportunity to improve the wealth of Skarsind by raising a new ministry in Temeschwar, forming part of the greater Torfast ministries. Construction required 8 wains of white granite and 2 thrones in labour, and three months to build. Gant Archama provided the full cost after the Spring Equinox 380YE. The finished building was named the Northern Traders Guild and stands in Temeschwar city proper, in the region of Hanuri.

Imperial Orcs.t: The ministry was intended to improve the wealth of Skarsind, the Imperial Orc territory whose trade it was built to serve.

The League.t: The League gained a new ministry, the Northern Traders Guild, in its city of Temeschwar, adding to the Torfast ministries there.

Construct the Ministry of Industry and S.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate passed a motion to build the Ministry of Industry and Skarsind Trade in Temeschwar, as part of the greater Torfast ministries, intending to improve the wealth of Skarsind. It was completed as the Northern Traders Guild in Temeschwar city proper.

Temeschwar/Hanuri.t: The Northern Traders Guild was built in Temeschwar city proper, within Hanuri, once Gant Archama had supplied the white granite and labour costs.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind's trade and wealth were the purpose of the ministry, although the building itself was raised in Temeschwar rather than in Skarsind.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar became home to the Ministry of Industry and Skarsind Trade, built as the Northern Traders Guild among the greater Torfast ministries.

Construct the Northern Way.d: Announced by the Master of Rings and so carrying the support of League citizens, the Northern Way cost 50 wains of white granite, 30 wains of mithril and 30 thrones in labour, and took six months to construct. After the Summer Solstice, Bella di Sarvos supplied the largest share of materials and money, with further granite from League citizens, mithril from Leofric d'Apulian and crowns from several others. Once complete it raises investment in Zenith by one, giving each business there 36 rings, removes the Black Plateau's penalty to Spiral's businesses, and lets the Crucible of Fate boost the Legacy's output and upgrade personal resources.

The League.t: The great work was announced by a League Master of Rings, gained the backing of League citizens, and lifts the Black Plateau's burden on businesses in Spiral, a League territory.

Urizen.t: The Northern Way links Apulian with the Urizen territory of Zenith, raising investment there so that every business in Zenith gains 36 rings once it is complete.

Construct the Northern Way.o: In Summer 388YE the Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, announced the commission of the Northern Way, a great work in Apulian to build a safe passage between the city and the territory of Zenith, funded by the Crimson Reapers.

Spiral/Apulus.t: The great work is constructed at the city of Apulian in Apulus, creating a safe route north towards Zenith.

Spiral.t: The Northern Way is built in Spiral, and once complete it removes the penalty that the Black Plateau places on businesses in the territory.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the motion was announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, whose name refers to the territory.

Zenith.t: Zenith is the destination of the safe passage from Apulian, and its investment level rises by one, providing 36 rings for each business there.

Construct the Park of Holberg.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by Feroz, the motion took up the opportunity to clear the ruined Holmauer and create space for parks. It cost 60 wains of weirwood, 40 wains of white granite and 25 Thrones in labour, with nine months of construction. Materials came from several donors: Othello von Holberg after the Autumn Equinox 380YE, Irina Kardaovich after the Winter Solstice 380YE, and Caerwynn von Holberg and Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar after the Autumn Equinox 381YE. Holmauer Park was finished shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE.

The League.t: League citizens proposed and largely paid for the work, with Othello and Caerwynn von Holberg among the donors, and the League city of Holberg gained Holmauer Park.

Construct the Park of Holberg.o: The Senate passed a motion in Spring 380YE commissioning a Great Work to clear the ruins of the Holmauer in Holberg and build a park in their place, funded by the citizens of Holberg. Holmauer Park was completed shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: The ruins of the Holmauer were cleared and restored, and Holmauer Park was completed there shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE.

Holberg.t: Holberg's senator proposed the motion, the work was meant to be self-funded by the city's citizens, and Holberg gained a new park built on cleared ruins.

Construct the Phoenix Flame.d: Proposed by the senator for Weirwater and seconded by Astolat, the motion commissioned the Phoenix Flame in Astolat, Dawn, at a cost of 30 wains of mithril, 30 wains of white granite and 180 crowns. It would take six months to complete. Once built, it was to be ceded to Meraud. Enchantress Areloe Larmallevés provided most of the materials and money after the Winter Solstice 385YE and the Spring Equinox 386YE. Smaller crown donations came from Serenus Starsong, Rhys Nighthaven, Ser Lucan Mortére and Aramis du Froste. Once the work was complete, the Tender of the Phoenix Flame could be appointed by Declaration of Candidacy.

Dawn.t: Dawn gained a new sinecure in one of its territories, with a new Imperial title, the Tender of the Phoenix Flame, to be appointed by Declaration of Candidacy. Dawnish donors such as Enchantress Areloe Larmallevés bore most of the cost.

Construct the Phoenix Flame.o: In Winter 385YE the Senate passed a motion to commission the Phoenix Flame, a sinecure in Astolat, and to create the title of Tender of the Phoenix Flame. The work followed the Back in town Wind of Fortune.

Astolat.t: The Phoenix Flame was built in Astolat over six months and ceded to Meraud once complete. Astolat's senator seconded the motion.

Construct the Pilgrim's Rest.d: Proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion authorised a self-funded sinecure costing ten wains of white granite and twenty crowns, taking three months to build. Once complete, it creates the Imperial title Crow Keeper of the Rest, carrying twelve votes in the Synod and six liao per season. The holder is appointed by the Wintermark National Assembly and may be revoked by that assembly, the General Assembly or the Assembly of Nine. Kitsana provided the granite and crowns after the Winter Solstice 380YE, allowing construction to proceed.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a national title, the Crow Keeper of the Rest, appointed by its National Assembly and carrying twelve Synod votes and six liao each season.

Construct the Pilgrim's Rest.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 380YE to construct the Pilgrim's Rest, a sinecure in Kallavesa Marsh, creating the title of Crow Keeper of the Rest.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: The Pilgrim's Rest is to be raised in Kallavesa Marsh from white granite supplied by Kitsana after the Winter Solstice 380YE.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa's senator proposed the sinecure, which is to be built within the territory once its materials are supplied.

Construct the Red Depths.d: Proposed by the senator for Segura and seconded by Weirwater, the motion created a mithril seat in Kahraman, costing 50 thrones, taking three months to build and carrying 10 thrones in seasonal upkeep. Funding came after the Autumn Equinox, with Bakar i Riqueza providing 49 thrones and 6 crowns and Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov a crown each. Disruption caused by the Lasambrian Orcs delayed completion until the Spring Equinox at the earliest. Once finished, the seat is to be allocated by Tally of the Votes among the fleets of the Brass Coast.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast gains a national mithril Bourse seat paid for by its own citizens, which its fleets will allocate by Tally of the Votes once the delayed construction is finished.

Construct the Red Depths.o: The Senate passed a motion to commission the Red Depths in Kahraman, a mithril-producing Brass Coast National Bourse seat, funded by the citizens of the Brass Coast in line with the Landscape Wind of Fortune.

Kahraman.t: The Red Depths are being built in Kahraman, though Lasambrian Orc disruption has delayed their completion until the Spring Equinox at the earliest.

Construct the Salt Guard.d: The commission used non-standard costs: 100 wains of white granite, 20 wains of weirwood, 30 Thrones in labour, and an upkeep of 10 Thrones each season. It would take a year to complete. Adan i DelToro i Riqueza, Lieselotte van Holberg and Imperatrix Lisabetta supplied materials and coin over the following seasons. Vigilant citizens inspired by the shrine of the Sentinel in Casinea were to provide 20 wains of white granite and 5 Thrones. The Immaculate Architect ritual was also cast on the project after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the Salt Guard would resist conventional invaders anywhere in Madruga with an effective strength of 3,000. Against Shore Offensives aimed at the Siroc Plains, its strength would rise to 6,000.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: citizens inspired by the shrine of the Sentinel in the Highborn territory of Casinea were to contribute granite and Thrones to the build.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast gains a planned major fortification in Madruga to protect Siroc and the Lyceum from invasion, particularly attacks from the sea.

Construct the Salt Guard.o: In Summer 382YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Madruga's senator and seconded by Feroz, to build the Salt Guard, a unique fortification in Siroc designed by the famed architect Menno van Ritsjhof. Its labour costs were set at 80 Thrones.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the shrine of the Sentinel in Casinea inspired vigilant citizens to pledge 20 wains of white granite and 5 Thrones towards the construction.

Madruga.t: The Salt Guard was to be built in Siroc, giving Madruga a defence of strength 3,000 against land invasion anywhere in the territory, and 6,000 against Shore Offensives on the Siroc Plains.

Construct the School of Hard Knocks in T.d: The motion took up the opportunity offered by the Schools and sawmills Wind of Fortune to construct a sinecure in Temeschwar. Besides standard costs, it required 20 wains of white granite and 60 crowns, and took three months to complete. The motion named the new title 'Maestro of Wolves', to be appointed by unanimous decision of League senators. After the Autumn Equinox 385YE, Valentina von Temeshwar provided 7 thrones 4 crowns and the 20 wains of white granite. Once complete, the position, recorded in the outcome as Master of the Sword Academy of Temeschwar, became available for election by the League's senators for the first time at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

The League.t: The League gained a new sinecure title chosen by its own senators, with the first election due at the Winter Solstice 385YE. The project was paid for by Valentina von Temeshwar.

Construct the School of Hard Knocks in T.o: In Autumn 385YE the Senate was presented with a motion, announced by D'ardante as Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, to build the School of Hard Knocks in Temeschwar using 20 wains of white granite. The project was funded and completed, creating a new League title.

Temeschwar.t: The School of Hard Knocks was built in Temeschwar, giving the territory a new academy and an associated title tied to it.

Construct the Signori d’Argento Vineyard.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Holberg, the motion called for a plantation of the most exquisite cultivars of Catazarro wines at the outskirts of the Aversa Estate in Foracci. The vineyards were to be under the jurisdiction of the Vine Tender of the Signori d'Argento Vineyards, a national League position appointed by the League Senators, as a self-funded money sinecure with no upkeep. Although the motion passed, it was abrogated by the Senate at the Summer Solstice 381YE. Brother Dagon of the Shattered Tower, as holder of an Imperial Wayleave, later recommissioned it.

The League.t: The vineyards would create a new League national position, the Vine Tender, appointed by the League Senators and holding a self-funded money sinecure built on Catazarro wine cultivars.

Construct the Signori d’Argento Vineyard.o: In Summer 381YE the Senate passed a motion to create the Signori d'Argento Vineyards in Foracci, Sarvos, a planting of fine Catazarro wine cultivars overseen by a new League national position.

Sarvos/Foracci.t: The vineyards were to be planted at the outskirts of the Aversa Estate in Foracci, bringing fine Catazarro wine cultivars to the region.

Sarvos.t: The League territory of Sarvos was the chosen site for the vineyards. The project was abrogated after passing and was later recommissioned under an Imperial Wayleave.

Construct the Signori d’Argento Vineyard.d: The announcement revived a previous plan to build a vineyard money sinecure in Sarvos, which had been the subject of an earlier Senate motion that was later abrogated. Rather than going back through the Senate, Brother Dagon of the Shattered Tower used the power to commission constructions that the Senate delegates to holders of an Imperial Wayleave. After the Summer Solstice 381YE, Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns towards the work. The vineyards were to be completed by the Autumn Equinox 381YE, creating the title of Signori d'Argento Vine Tender.

The League.t: A new League sinecure, the Signori d'Argento Vine Tender, was set to be created through vineyards in Sarvos, funded with weirwood and crowns from Giacomo Corvinoscuro.

Construct the Signori d’Argento Vineyard.o: Brother Dagon of the Shattered Tower, holding an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction of the Signori d'Argento Vineyards in Sarvos, following an earlier motion to build them that had been abrogated.

Sarvos.t: The Signori d'Argento Vineyards were to be built in Sarvos and completed by the Autumn Equinox 381YE.

Construct the Skarsind School of Warcast.d: The commission called for a mana sinecure in Estermark, Skarsind, at standard but unrecorded cost. Bloodcrow Yargol supplied 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns after the Summer Solstice 380YE. Once complete, the sinecure is to create a national title for the Skarsind College of Warcasting. The motion text names it Headteacher, a lifetime appointment by the Imperial Orcs Senators. The campaign outcome names it Preceptor, appointed by unanimous decision of the Imperial Orcs Senators. The page does not record the project as completed.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs' Civilian Commissioner approved the commission. Once complete, it will give the nation a new national title over the Skarsind College of Warcasting, appointed by the Imperial Orcs Senators.

Construct the Skarsind School of Warcast.o: In Summer 380YE the Civilian Commissioner of the Imperial Orcs approved the construction of a mana sinecure, the Skarsind School of Warcasting, in Estermark, Skarsind, using construction powers delegated by the Senate.

Skarsind/Estermark.t: Estermark is the chosen site for the Skarsind School of Warcasting, a mana sinecure commissioned in Summer 380YE.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind, held by the Imperial Orcs, is to host a new mana sinecure, with mithril and crowns already supplied towards its construction.

Construct the Stones from Blood.d: Proposed by Miaren and seconded by the Conscience of the Senate, the motion created a ministry in Therunin for purchasing mana crystals. Its purpose was to help the Navarr vates organise and to supply mana for national rituals such as Dance of Navarr and Thorn. Construction cost 12 wains of mithril and 36 crowns on top of standard costs, and took three months. The materials were provided after the Autumn Equinox by Bledri Eternal (5 wains and 4 thrones 4 crowns), Eleri Bronwen's Rest (5 wains) and Cara (2 wains). With the work complete, the Factor of Stones from Blood would be elected by the senators of Navarr for the first time at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Navarr.t: The Navarr vates council gained a ministry to support its organisation and to supply mana for national rituals such as Dance of Navarr and Thorn. Navarr senators would elect its Factor from the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Construct the Stones from Blood.o: In Autumn 385YE the Senate passed a motion to build Stones from Blood, a mana ministry in Therunin intended to support the Navarr vates council, with its holder expected to take an oath.

Therunin.t: Stones from Blood was built in Therunin as a ministry for purchasing mana crystals, paid for with 12 wains of mithril and 36 crowns.

Construct the Story Garden.d: Announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, Master of Rings, the Story Garden cost 12 wains of weirwood and 36 crowns in labour and took three months to complete. Lady Nineve Orzel provided 4 thrones 3 crowns and the weirwood, and Daugon Deliquio Orzel added 1 crown. The tenured title of Apothecary of the Story Garden receives bladeroot and was first available for appointment at the Spring Equinox 388YE by unanimous decision of Dawn's senators. The Constitutional Court ruled this appointment method unconstitutional, holding the title should be appointed by the Apothecaries Guild; under its guidance the title can still operate and be re-elected normally, but cannot be amended without addressing the appointment issue.

Dawn.t: Dawn gains a new tenured title whose holder brews potions for virtuous Dawnish citizens in return for tales of their deeds, funded by Lady Nineve Orzel and appointed by unanimous decision of Dawn's senators, though the Constitutional Court ruled that method unconstitutional.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the construction was announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, the Master of Rings.

Construct the Story Garden.o: In Winter 387YE the Master of Rings announced the construction of the Story Garden, a sinecure at Belletain in Weirwater, whose Apothecary provides potions to virtuous Dawnish citizens in exchange for stories of their virtuous acts.

Weirwater/Sandling.t: Sandling became home to the Story Garden at Belletain, completed after three months, where its Apothecary trades potions for stories of virtuous acts.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar appears only in the name of Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, the Master of Rings who announced the motion.

Weirwater.t: The Story Garden sinecure was built at Belletain in Weirwater, using 12 wains of weirwood and 36 crowns of labour.

Construct the Tassato Mana Exchange.d: Proposed by the senator for Tassato and seconded by Kahraman in Winter 379YE, the motion passed in principle and then passed at a cost of 80 thrones. The size of the ministry was left to the senator to decide, with standard costs applying. The 80 thrones were disbursed to Senator Tassato, and Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato supplied 16 wains of mithril after the Spring Equinox 380YE. The mana exchange was duly constructed in Mestra, and the new Imperial title of Steward of the Tassato Mana Exchange became a League national appointment.

The League.t: The League gained a new ministry for buying mana crystals, and the Steward of the Tassato Mana Exchange is appointed by the League nation.

Construct the Tassato Mana Exchange.o: The Senate passed a motion to commission the Tassato Mana Exchange, a ministry in Tassato arranging the purchase of mana crystals. It was later completed in Mestra.

Tassato.t: Tassato's senator proposed the ministry and Tassato's own Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato supplied the mithril, and the Mana Exchange now stands in Mestra.

Construct the Tenebrous Path.d: Proposed by Hercynia's senator and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion framed the sinecure as a way to inspire wisdom in Navarr thorns who aspire to command, as the Empire raised its first army dedicated to fighting the vallorn, Isaella's Dance. The project required ten wains of mithril, 20 crowns in labour and three months to build. Rhisiart Heartsbane supplied six wains of mithril after the Winter Solstice 383YE, then four more wains and 2 thrones 2 crowns after the Summer Solstice 384YE. Nathair Autumngale added 2 crowns. Once complete, the generals of Navarr may appoint the Wisdom of the Tenebrous Path as a Navarr national title.

Navarr.t: Navarr gains a new national title, the Wisdom of the Tenebrous Path, which its generals appoint and which is intended to guide thorns who seek a general's banner in the fight against the vallorn. Navarr citizens Rhisiart Heartsbane and Nathair Autumngale funded the work.

Construct the Tenebrous Path.o: In Winter 383YE the Senate passed a motion to construct the Tenebrous Path, a sinecure in Hercynia's Old Ranging that produces mana crystals and carries the Navarr national title Wisdom of the Tenebrous Path.

Hercynia/Old Ranging.t: The Tenebrous Path sinecure is built in Old Ranging, which became the site of the mana-producing structure tied to the Wisdom of the Tenebrous Path title.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia's senator proposed the motion, and the territory becomes home to the Tenebrous Path sinecure and its supply of mana crystals.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: the motion notes that the anti-vallorn army Isaella's Dance would muster at Miaren the following summer.

Construct the Thorned Rose.d: The motion, tabled under an Imperial Wayleave by Silvio di Tassato, commissioned a sinecure producing crystal mana at standard cost, with its size left to the bearer of the wayleave to determine. The Thorned Rose was to teach would-be vates what swearing the oath means and guide those wishing to learn of magic and the realms. The Dean would be appointed by the Navarr senators, hold tenure, and swear an oath to train the willing and never accept the Vate Oath of the irresponsible, reckless or unworthy. After the Summer Solstice, Bledri Eternal provided 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns towards construction. Once completed, the sinecure creates the title Dean of the Thorned Rose.

Navarr.t: The Navarr senators gain the power to appoint a tenured Dean charged with preparing prospective vates for their oath, giving the nation an Imperial institution devoted to the path of the vate.

Construct the Thorned Rose.o: In Summer 382YE a Senate motion proposed building the Thorned Rose, a place of learning just outside Seren in Miaren, to teach prospective vates and creating the Imperial title of Dean of the Thorned Rose as a mana sinecure.

Miaren.t: The Thorned Rose was to be built just outside Seren in Miaren, establishing a mana-producing seat of learning for vates in the territory.

Construct the Triosk Metal Exchange.d: Proposed by the senator for Ossium and seconded by Karsk, the motion commissioned the Triosk Metal Exchange and created a title, named in the motion as Merchant-Boyar of the Eagle and Stag Exchange, to be appointed by tally of the votes of Varushkan mine and forest owners, with responsibilities as set out in the Wind of Fortune. Construction cost 16 wains of mithril and 6 thrones and took three months. Desilav Sergeyevich Jesen provided the full mithril and money after the Autumn Equinox 385YE. With the work complete, the title, recorded in the outcome as the Eagle of Triosk, was to be appointed for the first time at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Varushka.t: Varushka gained a new ministry whose holder is chosen by the votes of Varushkan mine and forest owners, and a Varushkan, Desilav Sergeyevich Jesen, paid for its construction.

Construct the Triosk Metal Exchange.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 385YE to commission the Triosk Metal Exchange in Triosk, Volodmartz, a ministry seat arising from the Deep forests and dark hills Wind of Fortune.

Volodmartz.t: The Triosk Metal Exchange was built in Triosk, Volodmartz, giving the territory a ministry seat whose title was first due to be appointed at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Construct the Weaver's Market.d: Proposed by Sarvos and seconded by Redoubt, the motion called for a mana ministry in Skarsind, appointed in the usual way for an Imperial Orc National Bourse position. Construction required at least 12 wains of mithril, 3 Thrones in labour costs and three months of work. The mithril and Thrones were provided after the Autumn Equinox 381YE. Once built, the ministry created the Imperial title of Four Seasons' Boneweaver, appointed by Imperial Orcs who own a military unit, giving its holder access to purchases of crystal mana.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs gained a national ministry, the Four Seasons' Boneweaver, which is appointed by Imperial Orcs who command a military unit and gives them a means to buy crystal mana.

Construct the Weaver's Market.o: In Autumn 381YE the Senate passed in principle a motion to construct a mana ministry in Skarsind, "the weavers' market", through which crystal mana could be purchased. The office was to be a self-funded Imperial Orc National Bourse position.

Skarsind.t: The weavers' market mana ministry was to be built in Skarsind, and the 12 wains of mithril and 3 Thrones needed for its construction were supplied after the Autumn Equinox.

Construct the expansion of Spiral Castle.d: The motion commissioned an expansion of Spiral Castle in Weirwater. Before it, the castle's resupply covered only Weirwater. Afterwards, the Castellan of Spiral Castle could use their power of resupply on any army that spent the entire season in Weirwater, Karsk, Karov, Astolat or Semmerholm. The motion was proposed by the senator for Astolat and seconded by the senator for Tassato, and it passed. The expansion raised the castle's upkeep from 7 to 10 Thrones per season.

Dawn.t: Dawn's senator for Astolat proposed the expansion, which extended the castle's resupply to armies spending a full season in the Dawnish territories of Weirwater, Astolat and Semmerholm.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is linked only through Spiral, the territory it held, which shares its name with Spiral Castle in Weirwater; the motion does not otherwise concern Grendel.

Varushka.t: Armies spending a full season in the Varushkan territories of Karov and Karsk came within reach of the Castellan of Spiral Castle's resupply.

Construct the expansion of Spiral Castle.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Astolat's senator and seconded by Tassato's, to expand Spiral Castle in Weirwater so that its Castellan could resupply armies in the territories adjacent to Weirwater.

Astolat.t: Astolat's senator proposed the motion, and armies spending the whole season in Astolat could now be resupplied by the Castellan of Spiral Castle.

Karov.t: Karov was one of the territories adjacent to Weirwater where armies spending the whole season could now be resupplied from Spiral Castle.

Karsk.t: Karsk was one of the territories adjacent to Weirwater where armies spending the whole season could now be resupplied from Spiral Castle.

Semmerholm.t: Armies spending the whole season in Semmerholm came within the expanded resupply reach of Spiral Castle's Castellan.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is linked only through the name of Spiral Castle, which stands in Weirwater; the motion does not concern the territory of Spiral itself.

Weirwater.t: Spiral Castle in Weirwater was expanded, extending its Castellan's resupply from Weirwater to its neighbouring territories and raising its upkeep from 7 to 10 Thrones per season.

Construct the market town of New Dunhall.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by the Conscience, the motion passed at a cost of 30 Thrones. It created a new market town near the ruins of Dunhall in Hahnmark, to be overseen by a new title, the Caretaker of New Dunhall, which will generate coin. The motion framed the work as the beginning of recovery from the catastrophic loss of Dunhearth Hall in the recent collapse. After the Summer Solstice, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason provided the 20 wains of white granite and 40 crowns needed. The town was due to be complete by the Autumn Equinox 381YE. The proposing senator indicated that the Caretaker will be a Wintermark national appointment.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gains a new market town in its own territory, and the Caretaker of New Dunhall is to be appointed by the Wintermark nation, giving the Steinr, Suaq and Kallavesi a new sinecure that generates coin.

Construct the market town of New Dunhall.o: The Senate passed a motion to build New Dunhall, a market town and coin-generating sinecure near the ruins of Dunhall in Hahnmark, as a first step in rebuilding after Dunhearth Hall was lost to a recent collapse.

Hahnmark.t: New Dunhall is to rise near the ruins of Dunhall in Hahnmark, beginning the territory's recovery from the catastrophic loss of Dunhearth Hall in the recent collapse.

Construct theatre in Temeschwar.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion commissioned a great work at a cost of 15 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood, 5 thrones and three months of construction. All materials and money were provided by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar after the Winter Solstice 380YE. The finished Bloody Great Theatre, completed shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE, provides 15 liao and 30 votes in the Synod each season, shared among Temeschwar citizens dedicated to Pride who own congregations, following attendance at the Anvil Summit.

The League.t: League priests of Pride in Temeschwar who own congregations gain a seasonal share of 15 liao and 30 Synod votes from the new theatre, strengthening the League's religious voice.

Construct theatre in Temeschwar.o: In Winter 380YE the Senate passed a motion to build a great theatre in Temeschwar celebrating the city's Pride, taking advantage of an opportunity from a recent period of inspiration; it was completed as the Bloody Great Theatre shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar gained the Bloody Great Theatre, funded by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar and completed shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE as a celebration of the city's Pride.

Construct tomb for Empress Giselle.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Sarvos, the motion addressed the controversy over where Empress Giselle's remains should rest. It called for her body to be moved to Temeschwar and a tomb constructed there, with a Guardian of the Tombs appointed by the League national assembly who would receive liao and votes in the Synod. The motion passed. Ten wains of white granite and 20 crowns were provided towards the work, and the sarcophagus of Empress Giselle has been moved to Temeschwar. Once the tomb is complete, the sinecure will create the League national title of Guardian of Giselle's Tomb.

The League.t: The League gains custody of Empress Giselle's remains and, once the tomb is finished, a national title, Guardian of Giselle's Tomb, appointed by its national assembly and carrying liao and votes in the Synod.

Construct tomb for Empress Giselle.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 380YE to move the body of Empress Giselle to Temeschwar and build her a tomb there, overseen by a new League title.

Temeschwar.t: Empress Giselle's sarcophagus has been moved to Temeschwar, where her tomb is being built with granite and crowns provided towards the work, and it will be home to the new Guardian of Giselle's Tomb.

Construct trade hub in Upwold.d: Proposed by Upwold and seconded by Bregasland, the motion split the cost between the Marches and Lady Sarelta of the Red Moon of the Faraden. The minimum cost was estimated at 20 wains of weirwood, 20 wains of white granite and 80 crowns. The Faraden committed to supplying the white granite and 40 crowns towards labour, and offered to match the Empire's weirwood and half the labour costs if a larger enclave was built. After the Autumn Equinox 381YE, Henry Ward provided 20 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones. Once complete, the hub was expected to act as a great work giving Marcher citizens who own farms and businesses a share of funds. The Senate abrogated it in Spring 384YE.

The Marches.t: The Marches were to pay half the cost of the hub, and Marcher citizens who own farms and businesses stood to receive a share of its funds until the Senate abrogated it in Spring 384YE.

Construct trade hub in Upwold.o: In Summer 381YE the Senate passed a motion to build a trade hub with the Faraden in King's Stoke in Upwold, to strengthen economic and diplomatic ties between the Empire and the Faraden.

Upwold.t: King's Stoke in Upwold was chosen as the site of the Faraden trade hub, which Upwold's own senator proposed.

Construct vale in Karsk.d: The motion called for a new vale to be built at the site of Ivarsgard in the Lestazny region of Karsk, taking the form of a self-funded folly at standard costs. After the Spring Equinox, Maarit Akkova Cendro provided 10 wains of white granite, 10 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones towards the work. The majority of the basic construction of the new vale of Ivarsgard was then completed, and the civil service began investigating what help it could offer to the exiles of Ivarsgard who wish to return to their rejuvenated vale.

Varushka.t: Varushka gains a rebuilt vale at Ivarsgard, largely funded by Maarit Akkova Cendro, and the vale's exiles may now be helped by the civil service to return home.

Construct vale in Karsk.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate passed a motion to build a new vale on the site of Ivarsgard in Lestazny, Karsk, as a self-funded folly proposed by Karsk's senator and seconded by Hahnmark's.

Karsk.t: Most of the basic construction of the new vale of Ivarsgard in Lestazny, Karsk, has been completed, opening the way for its exiles to return.

Construct venom brokerage.d: Proposed by the senator for Miaren and seconded by Therunin, the motion answered an opportunity offered by the brokers of Navarr to build a brokerage dedicated to tools for fighting the vallorn. It passed, with non-standard costs of 30 weirwood and 60 crowns in labour. After the Spring Equinox, Llewelyn Leafstalker supplied 30 wains of weirwood and 7 Thrones 4 Crowns. Once complete, the brokerage, named Honest Twill's Gardening Supplies, will create a new Imperial title, the Blackroot Broker, appointed by unanimous decision of the senators of Navarr.

Navarr.t: Navarr's senators will appoint the Blackroot Broker by unanimous decision, giving the nation control of a new supply of herbs, blade venoms and Scorpion Stings for its war against the vallorn, with the materials provided by Llewelyn Leafstalker.

Construct venom brokerage.o: In Spring 382YE the Senate passed a motion to build a brokerage in Miaren supplying herbs, blade venoms and Scorpion Stings for the fight against the vallorn, with its broker appointed by the Navarri senators.

Miaren.t: Miaren is to host the brokerage Honest Twill's Gardening Supplies, which will become a source of herbs, venoms and Scorpion Stings once construction is complete.

Construct village expansion in Volodmart.d: The motion called for a self-funded village expansion with no upkeep, costing 10 wains of white granite, 20 crowns in labour and three months to construct.
