After the Spring Equinox, Vuk the Wolfeater provided 9 wains of white granite and the 20 crowns, and Sigourney Kavov provided the remaining wain of white granite. Certain necessary details were still required before construction could begin. Once completed, the sinecure will create a new title, Keeper of Berislav's Rest, a Varushkan national position held with tenure.

Varushka.t: The completed sinecure will create the Keeper of Berislav's Rest, a Varushkan national title held with tenure, and Varushkans Vuk the Wolfeater and Sigourney Kavov supplied the granite and crowns needed to build it.

Construct village expansion in Volodmart.o: In Spring 381YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Volodmartz and seconded by Karsk, to build a village expansion housing the growing vigilant population of a virtuous mine in Volodmartz, functioning as a money-producing sinecure.

Volodmartz.t: A village expansion is to be built in Volodmartz to house the vigilant population of a virtuous mine there, producing money as a sinecure once certain outstanding details are settled and construction begins.

Construct walls of Holberg.d: The motion called for raising Holberg's walls from their current level to twice their effectiveness and requested funds to begin building. The listed costs were 200 wains of white granite, 50 thrones and a year of construction, with the upkeep of the walls rising to 28 thrones each season. After the Spring Equinox 382YE, Irina Kardaovich, Caerwyn Von Holberg of The Feasting Crow and Imperatrix Lisabetta von Holberg all donated granite, and the Silent Sentinel opportunity supplied more. Lisabetta completed the supply with 72 wains after the Summer Solstice. The finished walls gave Holberg city an effective defensive military strength of 12,000.

The League.t: The League's senators drove the project, and League citizens largely supplied the granite, including donations from Imperatrix Lisabetta von Holberg and The Feasting Crow. The result greatly strengthened the defences of one of its great cities.

Construct walls of Holberg.o: In Winter 381YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by Tassato, to raise the walls of Holberg city to double their effectiveness. It was carried at a cost of 150 thrones and was believed to be taking advantage of an opportunity.

Holberg.t: Holberg city's walls were greatly improved, reaching an effective defensive strength of 12,000, but their upkeep rose to 28 thrones each season.

Contact the Lasambrian orcs.d: Proposed by the senator for Therunin and seconded by Upwold, the motion called for contact with the Lasambrian orcs to discuss two things: their removing themselves from Segura, and a possible alliance against the Jotun. It passed in principle by 25 votes to none. In response, attempts were made to send Winged Messengers to the Lasambrian orcs. The page records only that these attempts were made, not whether contact was achieved or what the orcs replied.

Jotun.t: The Senate sought to turn the Lasambrian orcs against the Jotun, proposing an alliance aimed squarely at them.

Contact the Lasambrian orcs.o: At the Spring Equinox 378YE the Senate passed, unopposed, a motion to open diplomatic contact with the Lasambrian orcs, seeking their withdrawal from Segura and an alliance against the Jotun.

Segura.t: The Senate hoped to persuade the Lasambrian orcs occupying Segura to withdraw, and Winged Messengers were sent to raise the matter with them.

Conversion of Overton Garrison.d: Proposed by the senator for Upwold and seconded by Bregasland's, the motion passed at no cost. The garrison had become obsolete after Orchard's Watch was completed, and was disbanded. The conversion was due to be finished by the Summer Solstice 380YE. The new sinecure would then automatically create the annual Marcher national title of Sheriff of Overton, chosen by a vote of Marcher farmers at the Anvil Summit and revocable by the Marcher national assembly. The Sheriff's purpose was to stem banditry and raiding against the Mournwold mines and recover ore, though it remained unclear which ores would be recovered.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named on the page; they appear only because they held part of the Mournwold that season.

The Marches.t: The Marches gained a new annual national title, the Sheriff of Overton, elected by Marcher farmers and answerable to the Marcher national assembly. The Sheriff was charged with protecting the Mournwold mines from bandits and raiders.

Conversion of Overton Garrison.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate passed a motion to convert the Overton Garrison in Overton, Mournwold into a sinecure, The Sheriff's House, to curb banditry and raiding on the Mournwold mines and reclaim ore.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Overton in Greensward became home to The Sheriff's House, the seat of the new Marcher Sheriff of Overton, replacing the disbanded garrison there.

Mournwold.t: Overton's obsolete garrison was disbanded and its site turned into The Sheriff's House, which aimed to stem raiding on the territory's mines and reclaim their ore.

Conviction.d: After the Druj were driven from Reikos and their slaves freed, Golan drew fervent crowds among the traumatised survivors. He built on the Assembly of Courage's recent judgement naming the First Empress an exemplar of Courage. The Courage assembly sent Nina of Cantiarch's Hold to preach with at least 25 liao, short of the 50 needed to refute him, and called an Inquisition on Golan for the Spring Equinox 380YE. The General Assembly passed Yael's judgement claiming she was the reborn First Empress. This inflamed matters: followers took it as support for Golan. Courage-led congregations throughout Highguard gained votes and liao, while all others lost attendance, influence and liao.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj occupation, enslavement and terror in Reikos, ended when the Black Thorns drove them out, created the despair in which Golan's preaching took hold.

Highguard.t: Highborn survivors embraced Golan's heresy, and by the end of the season every Highguard congregation led by a Courage priest was gaining votes and liao while those of other Virtues were losing both.

Conviction.o: In Winter 379YE the Highborn preacher Golan the Wanderer began preaching in war-ravaged Reikos that the First Empress was an exemplar of Courage, making Courage the pre-eminent Virtue, and that she would be reborn only when the Empire embraced it. The Synod's responses failed to check him, and Courage congregations across Highguard swelled at the expense of the other Virtues.

Casinea.t: As a Highguard territory, its Courage-led congregations shared in the swelling attendance, votes and liao, while congregations of other Virtues saw reduced influence.

Reikos.t: Freshly liberated from the Druj, Reikos was where Golan preached; Nina's under-supplied counter-campaign failed there and Yael's planned visit to its citizens only fuelled his following.

Cost.d: Eleven armies and thirty thousand champions, aided by Summer and Winter warriors, fought nearly a dozen Mallum armies, the twisted Black Wind and the Rivers Run Red curse. A slave uprising aided by the Winter Sun won the Bitter Strand, though the freed slaves held the Fangs mithril mine and barred the Empire. At the Shadowmere a Druj ambush on the Citadel Guard became a victory, taking the Saltmarsh, and the Vendarri sued for terms. The Hounds of Glory pressed on, rallied the faltering Empire at the Battle of Dusk and broke into the citadel, but the army was destroyed. Over fifteen thousand Druj fell. Five Sentinel Gate conjunctions followed.

Dawn.t: All four Dawnish armies led the campaign, and the Hounds of Glory sacrificed themselves to seize the Spires of Dusk, leaving rows of Dawnish dead and the Black Wind singling out Dawnish soldiers for slaughter.

Druj.t: The Druj lost the Bitter Strand, Saltmarsh, Plains of Teeth and the Spires of Dusk, and more than fifteen thousand Mallum orcs, though they still hold the forests and remain defeated but not beaten.

Highguard.t: The Seventh Wave scouted, foiled Druj traps and brokered the Vendarri surrender, which is now under discussion with the Highborn over the fate of Saltmarsh, while Highborn soldiers were among the thousand who fell at the Shadowmere.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Winter Sun came from Ossium to free Druj slaves, smuggled weapons to the slaves of the Fangs to spark the uprising and helped win over the Vendarri, while the Bronzehoard reavers found a Druj stockpile now offered as a conjunction.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: respectable Navarr bands fought with the Hounds of Glory, and Navarr on the campaign recognised echoes of the Holt of the Oak in the weirwood of the Spires of Dusk.

The League.t: The Wolves of War and Towerjacks fought in the campaign, the Wolves locked in an inconclusive skirmishing duel with the Hunting Scorpion, and League bands swelled the Hounds of Glory.

Urizen.t: The Citadel Guard turned the Druj ambush at the Shadowmere into victory and, protected by Winter magic, lost not a single sentinel or magician throughout the whole campaign.

Varushka.t: The Northern Eagle and Golden Axe fought alongside Summer schlacta through the campaign, with Varushkan dead among the thousand lost at the Shadowmere, and the Bargainer of the Iron Tower is offered a conjunction to secure abandoned mithril.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark bands fought with the Hounds of Glory and Winterfolk advised comrades on crossing the flooded Saltmarsh.

Cost.o: In Spring 385YE eleven Imperial armies drove the Druj from the Bitter Strand, the Saltmarsh and the Plains of Teeth and stormed the Spires of Dusk, but the victory cost the Empire the Dawnish army the Hounds of Glory, which was destroyed winning it.

Reikos/Broken Ride.t: Mentioned in passing: Broken Ride itself is not named; Reikos appears only through references to the citadel of Exile and the Reikos flux.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: A small White Lion force has entered Axmure escorting the Amaranthine Devourer towards the Pits of Brychel, and the Sentinel Gate opens to Melusine's Fields so the Knight-protector of Winter can stop them.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: The Bitter Strand fell to the Empire after a bloody battle and an uprising of the Fangs' slaves, who now hold the mithril mine and refuse the Empire access, and a conjunction to Spinner's Retreat targets Venomclaw and the heralds of Arhallogen.

The Barrens/Farweald.t: Mentioned in passing: Farweald is listed among the forests the Druj twist with magic against Imperial pursuers.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: The flooded, blighted Saltmarsh was taken after the Battle of the Shadowmere and the Vendarri sued for surrender, while a conjunction to the Steadfast Pines offers a chance to loot Raguk Chainforger's stockpile.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: The Druj regrouped in the warded Bleaks to strike at the Battle of Dusk and have fallen back there, and the Sentinel Gate opens to the Blooming Grove for a strike on Zortog Ashtouch.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is named as one of the homes to which the Dawnish dead may be brought back for burial.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the new Spires of Dusk are compared in scale to the Silent Sentinel in Casinea.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks arrived fresh from a triumphal procession through Holberg, and Raguk Chainforger's wealth is likened to that of Holberg's merchant princes.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj het Ortgut Spirebreaker is named for toppling spires in Morrow and Zenith.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun came south having driven the Druj from Ossium, and the broken Tower of the Scorpion there is dwarfed by the Spires of Dusk.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: veterans recalled lessons learned at Exile in Reikos, the Spires were compared to its citadel, and a few cases of the Reikos flux broke out in the Saltmarsh.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: The Druj tepel Zortog Ashtouch is withdrawing to coordinate with the ghulai of the Salt Flats of Sanath, carrying a list of regios, and the Polemarch of Highwatch is asked to intercept it and disrupt their schemes.

Semmerholm.t: A Druj force is escorting the Agramant herald the Amaranthine Devourer through Semmerholm towards the Pits of Brychel, and the Knight-protector of Winter is charged with killing it; Semmerholm is also a home for the Dawnish dead.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bronzehoard reavers went into the Barrens seeking goods to sell to the orcs of Skarsind.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: light infantry from Tassato served with the Wolves of War in their skirmishes against the Hunting Scorpion.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the walls of the Spires of Dusk are said to echo those of Temeschwar.

The Barrens.t: The Empire now holds five regions of the Barrens including the Spires of Dusk, though the Druj still control the territory and its forests, the Fangs are held by independent orc rebels and the Rivers Run Red curse still blights its waters.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr saw echoes of the Holt of the Oak in Therunin in the weirwood construction of the Spires of Dusk.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater is named as one of the homes to which the Dawnish dead may be brought back for burial.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard marched south from a freed if not healed Zenith, and Ortgut Spirebreaker is named for toppling spires there.

Crafted from torment.d: Ossium had almost no native Imperial citizens, so it could go to any of the ten nations. The civil service stressed that contiguity barely mattered thanks to the egregores. Known inhabitants were the morose orc Sand Fishers, the Varushkan-descended Ketsov humans and Druj of the Bone Serpent Clan, though the Empire had no map. Each nation's case was weighed: the League, Varushka, the Marches and the Brass Coast offered the best tax prospects, Dawn the most military support. Relinquishment was possible but risky. The Senate assigned Ossium to Varushka, which elected its first senator, and recognised the Sand Fishers as foreigners. The Ketsov's status remained uncertain.

Dawn.t: Dawn's case rested on the magical Golden Bridge to Lacre, Barrens refugees keen to settle and the Semmerlak's Summer links. Ossium would have given Dawn the most military support but little taxation, and the Senate did not choose it.

Druj.t: Ossium was conquered from the Druj, and the Bone Serpent Clan still had a significant presence there. Those unable to join the new nation might flee east to their kin or remain as a dangerous barbarian population.

Highguard.t: Highguard was argued to offer the fastest conversion of Ossium's people to the Way and secluded land for monastic chapters, though the new pilgrimage meant it could ill afford to lose more citizens.

Imperial Orcs.t: The civil service warned that the cowed Sand Fishers were as unlike the Imperial Orcs as possible. Ossium's warmer lands might still have attracted orc settlers, but the nation would have yielded little tax and still faced its population problems.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun thralls in the Mournwold were cited as a precedent for foreigners living in the Empire, and the Jotun conquest of Sermersuaq was noted as having displaced people.

Navarr.t: The Navarr were presented as the best woodsfolk to face the dark northern forests, which adjoin Sküld's vallorn. They were also seen as best able to help displaced inhabitants resettle peacefully.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn case rested on draining marshes for docks and perhaps a shipyard on the Semmerlak, and on lifting the despairing Sand Fishers' spirits. It offered good long-term taxation but needed costly development.

The League.t: The League's case rested on the towns of Ketsov and Lomaa, the trade-minded Ketsov and the territory's contiguity with Holberg. It promised the largest boost to the treasury but at great development cost.

The Marches.t: The Marches were noted for Ossium's likeness to Bregasland, Mournwold experience of cooperating with orc neighbours and Marcher skill at farming barren land. The territory could have supported an extra army relatively quickly.

Thule.t: The Thule border Ossium and seem to have a particular interest in its dark northern forests. Their prosperity as foreigners in the Silver Peaks was cited as an example, and how each nation would fare as their neighbour was weighed.

Urizen.t: Urizen was seen as best placed to exploit Ossium's powerful magical sites and to engage the literate Ketsov. It would gain the least economically or militarily, and linking the territory to the Heliopticon would be hard.

Varushka.t: Varushka received Ossium, adding a new territory with its own senator. The case for it rested on the Ketsov's Varushkan origins, adjacency to Varushkan lands, a great mithril mine already worked by Moresvah's miners and experience with dark powers and the Thule.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's case rested on Kallavesi experience of wetlands, potential settlers displaced from Sermersuaq and Skarsind, and heroes eager to face the dark forests. The poor relations between the Thule and the Mark were weighed as both a risk and a possible advantage.

Crafted from torment.o: With the conquest of Ossium complete, the first new Imperial territory in decades, the civil service set out the case for assigning it to each Imperial nation. The Senate gave Ossium to Varushka and recognised the Sand Fisher orcs as foreigners.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule prospering in the Silver Peaks was cited as evidence that foreigners can thrive within the Empire.

Bregasland.t: Ossium was judged surprisingly similar to Bregasland, and some of its citizens might have been keen to settle there had the Marches received the territory.

Holberg.t: Holberg was cited as a past contested assignment and lies across the river from Ossium. Its crowded citizens might have moved to Lomaa or Ketsov had the League won the territory.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren was cited as a Navarr territory whose vallorn has long been cleared, now a settled forest haven.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: some Bregaslanders would welcome Ossium's distance from the nosy folk of Upwold and Mitwold.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold's Marchers were noted as the only Imperial humans with good experience of living alongside orcs, and its Jotun thralls served as a precedent. It was suggested the Sand Fishers might even join the Mournwold Thralls.

Ossium.t: Ossium was assigned to Varushka and elected its first Imperial senator, while the Sand Fishers living there were recognised as foreigners under Imperial law. The status of the Ketsov and other former Druj subjects remained unsettled.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium was compared to Reikos before the Highborn civilised it in the Empire's early years.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: people displaced when the Jotun conquered Sermersuaq were suggested as possible Wintermark settlers for Ossium.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind was cited as proof that a territory can change nation, and those who left it might have settled Ossium under Wintermark.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar's joining the League was cited to show that Varushkan heritage need not bar League citizenship.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: some Bregaslanders would welcome Ossium's distance from the nosy folk of Upwold and Mitwold.

Create Chair of the Wolf.d: Proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by Holberg, the motion acted on the A health to the company wind of fortune. It passed, and expansion of the Holberg Guild of Engineers began. The new Chair of the Wolf can announce a commission (a great work, ministry, sinecure or folly) provided it takes place entirely within a League territory, and this does not count against the limited number of commissions the Empire can undertake each season. As part of creating the title, the League commissioned four impressive structures, one in each of its cities. The arrangement differs from the original Winter 383YE proposal but is fully endorsed by the Guild of Engineers.

The League.t: The League gains a new national title, the Chair of the Wolf, chosen by Tally of the Votes and able to commission projects within League territory outside the Empire's usual limit, along with four impressive structures, one in each of its cities.

Create Chair of the Wolf.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 384YE giving the Holberg Guild of Engineers permission to expand their premises and creating the League national title of Chair of the Wolf, appointed by Tally of the Votes.

Holberg.t: Holberg's Guild of Engineers has begun expanding its premises, and the territory's senator seconded the motion creating the Chair of the Wolf.

Create law of delegation protection.d: Proposed by Miaren and seconded by Segura, the motion created a law stating that any delegation from a barbarian nation arriving on the field at Anvil under a flag of peace should be protected under the law as citizens while visiting the Empire. It carried no cost. In practice the law appears to have extended the status of foreigner to any barbarian delegation that reached Anvil, rather than full citizenship. The law was later amended during the Winter Solstice 378YE.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named in the motion; its connection appears to be through the proposer or seconder, Miaren and Segura.

Create law of delegation protection.o: In Autumn 378YE the Senate passed a law granting legal protection to barbarian delegations that arrive at Anvil under a flag of peace, protecting them as citizens for the duration of their visit.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named in the motion; its link appears to be through the senator who proposed or seconded it.

Create law of protection for humans in M.d: Proposed by Mitwold and seconded by Morrow, the motion afforded legal protection to the humans of the Mourn other than the Feni. The court noted a contradiction: some of these humans were fighting for the Jotun, and enemies of the Empire ordinarily have no legal protection. Imperial soldiers facing them in battle would usually be covered by self-defence, but that defence carries a reasonableness test that could place soldiers' conduct under magistrates' scrutiny, and less clear-cut situations might arise during the Mourn campaign. The phrase "Humans of the Mourn" covers people living in the Mourn even when they are outside it, but not barbarian humans whose homes lie elsewhere.

Jotun.t: Humans fighting for the Jotun in the Mourn are now legally protected, which complicates Imperial efforts against Jotun forces by exposing soldiers to possible scrutiny from magistrates.

Create law of protection for humans in M.o: In Summer 381YE the Senate passed a motion granting humans of the Mourn, excluding the Feni, full protection under Imperial law, giving them the same legal standing as foreigners.

Mournwold.t: The Jotun-held Mournwold's non-Feni human inhabitants gained legal protection equivalent to foreigners, wherever they happen to be, which shapes how the Empire can conduct its campaign there.

Create title Custodian of Ivarsgard Dock.d: Proposed by the senator for Karsk and seconded by the Dean of the Academy, the motion took up an offer from the Bedelaar Huisbaas Vak Eck and required no construction or cost. It represents an agreement between a Sarcophan Delves concern and the people of Ivarsgard. The new title is appointed annually at the Spring Equinox by Varushkan citizens who maintain a forest or mine resource. The holder can purchase Cerulean Mazzarine from Sarcophan merchants using the docks on the Semmerlak.
Create title Custodian of Ivarsgard Dock.o: The Senate passed a motion in Summer 382YE creating the Imperial title Custodian of Ivarsgard Docks, designating part of the Ivarsgard docks on the Semmerlak as a herb ministry for cerulean mazzarine.

The Semmerlak.t: An area of the Ivarsgard docks on the Semmerlak became a herb ministry, where the new Custodian can buy Cerulean Mazzarine from Sarcophan merchants trading on the lake.

Create title of Ambassador to the Thule.d: Proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by Morrow, the motion created an ambassadorial title appointed by vote of the Senate and revocable by the well worn path. The campaign outcome records the title as Ambassador to Otkodov. Juha, the Cave Spider of Varushka, became the first holder in Spring 381YE. The motion sought to seize an opportunity offered by the Thule, but one of that opportunity's requirements was that the post be a national Varushkan position, which this Senate-appointed title was not. The Senate was under no obligation to meet the Thule request, but an Imperial ambassador is only as influential as the foreign nation allows them to be.

Thule.t: The Empire gained a formal ambassador to the Thule, though because the post was not the national Varushkan position the Thule had asked for, the Thule alone decide how much influence that ambassador has.

Varushka.t: The Thule opportunity had called for a national Varushkan position, and although the title was made a Senate appointment instead, a Varushkan, Juha the Cave Spider, became the first ambassador.

Create title of Ambassador to the Thule.o: The Imperial Senate passed a motion in Spring 381YE creating the title of Ambassador to the Thule, appointed by Senate vote, to take advantage of a recent diplomatic opportunity. Juha, the Cave Spider of Varushka, was appointed as the first ambassador.

Otkodov.t: The Thule-held territory gave its name to the title as recorded in the outcome, Ambassador to Otkodov, making it the focus of the Empire's new diplomatic post.

Create title of Keeper of the Breadbaske.d: Proposed by the senator for Upwold and seconded by the senator for Mournwold, the motion created a national title chosen by the Marcher senators for a one-year term and revocable by the Marcher Assembly or the Assembly of Nine. The Keeper maintains the Great Work and may decide, once per summit, whether the Breadbasket supports the Mournwold or the Imperial armies, including which army benefits. Decisions are made by announcement. The title also carries a right of address to the Senate once per summit, but the Constitution's review noted that the motion's attempt to require that address be used when changing the allocation was unconstitutional. The motion passed.

The Marches.t: The Marches gained a new national title, appointed by their senators and answerable to the Marcher Assembly or the Assembly of Nine, which gives a Marcher custody of the Imperial Breadbasket and control over where its benefits go.

Create title of Keeper of the Breadbaske.o: In Autumn 381YE the Senate passed a motion creating the Marcher national title of Keeper of the Breadbasket, giving its holder custody of the Imperial Breadbasket great work and the decision over whether its granaries and storehouses support the Mournwold or the Imperial armies.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold's senator seconded the motion, and the new Keeper decides whether the Breadbasket's granaries and storehouses support the Mournwold or are directed to the Imperial armies instead.

Create title of Quartermaster General of.d: Proposed by Astolat and seconded by Morrow, the motion originally sought a Minister for Resupply in Miaren. The Senate was advised that a great work automatically resupplying armies based in Miaren was impossible without a source of mithril or weirwood to meet the costs, so senators created an Imperial title instead. It passed at 25 Thrones, 16 votes to 8, with a stipend of 25 Thrones per season from the Senate budget. Its powers were initially unclear. Procedural motions at the Winter Solstice Summit 377YE established that the Quartermaster General could only resupply an Imperial army. Such resupply would be announced to the Senate without a vote and would remain subject to the Synod's veto.

Navarr.t: The motion was prompted by a wish to secure emergency resupply for Imperial armies fighting in the Navarr territory of Miaren. The result was an Empire-wide title rather than a Navarr-specific measure.

Create title of Quartermaster General of.o: In Autumn 377YE the Senate created the Imperial title of Quartermaster General of the Imperial Armies, holding the Senate's power to authorise the resupply of armies, after being told a great work in Miaren could not provide automatic emergency resupply.

Miaren.t: The Senate had hoped to build a great work in Miaren to resupply armies stationed there automatically. It was told this could not be done without mithril or weirwood, and created a general resupply title instead.

Crimson and green.d: After the Autumn Equinox the vallorn's assault on the west faltered, possibly because of an ettercap poison used in Sweetglades. A Spring ward woven over Eastring by the Voice of the Quiet Forest drew the vallorn there instead. It overwhelmed the Druj defenders, absorbed the ward and claimed the region. The Thimble weirwood grove is now cut off. Agents of the Prince with a Thousand Foes freed some Druj slaves, including nearly a hundred former Imperial citizens. The vallorn, now at 19,000 strength, is waning but will try to expand for one more season. When Thornsong House's ward failed, the Druj burned it. The apothecaries fled carrying lore, and an opportunity arose to rescue them.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Sun withdrew to Astolat after fighting the vallorn in Peakedge Song, and its earlier losses inflicted on the Druj help buy the fleeing apothecaries time.

Druj.t: The Druj lost Eastring and its garrisons to the vallorn, with fugitives slaughtered in Sarangrave. Their remaining forces in Therunin, mostly in East Ashes, are cut off and desperate, though a Druj band burned Thornsong House and is hunting its apothecaries.

Highguard.t: The Wolves of War withdrew to Bastion after Peakedge Song. Highguard's Reikos and the Gardens of High Chalcis are the refuge the Thornsong apothecaries are fleeing towards.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Apothecaries' Guildhouse would have slightly lower upkeep if built in Skarsind.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven appears only in the further reading list of earlier vallorn winds.

Navarr.t: The Navarr see the vallorn take Eastring and the Thimble weirwood grove, which can now only be recovered by linking the vallornhearts. Nearly a hundred captured Navarr and other former citizens were freed, while their apothecary college at Thornsong House was burned and its people hunted.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's earlier advance had threatened the northern regions of Morrow, but that threat eased when it turned east.

Crimson and green.o: In Winter 387YE the roused Tharunind vallorn turned from western Therunin and swept over Druj-held Eastring, claiming the region, while the Druj burned Thornsong House after its Night ward failed, leaving its apothecaries fleeing west towards Reikos with orcs in pursuit.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: Mentioned in passing: Bendol appears only in further reading about an earlier expedition, Into Béantal Dol.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: Druj escaping Eastring fled into the Nesustak Forest, where the rebels and their preternatural allies killed most of them.

Therunin/East Ashes.t: East Ashes holds most of the remaining Druj forces, trapped behind Imperial lines, and is seen as the likeliest target for the vallorn's final season of expansion.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Eastring was overrun by the vallorn, which destroyed the Druj garrisons and absorbed their Spring ward. The region gained the vallorn quality and can only be reclaimed by linking the vallornhearts, and the Thimble is now isolated within it.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: After costing nearly two thousand Imperial lives here, the vallorn's assault on Peakedge Song receded once the armies withdrew.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: An Imperial expedition through the Sentinel Gate to Sweetglades found a poison that burns through ettercap nests. It may explain why the vallorn turned away from the west.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Sun withdrew to Astolat after the Autumn Equinox.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War withdrew to Bastion after the Autumn Equinox.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Brocéliande is cited as the fate awaiting Therunin, lost to the vallorn, if Tharunind is left to expand freely.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven appears only in further reading about earlier victories over its vallorn.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is not named directly and is touched on only through the wider Navarr struggle against the vallorn.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's surge had posed a threat to northern Morrow, which receded when it turned on Eastring.

Reikos.t: The surviving Thornsong apothecaries are fleeing towards the Reikos border and High Chalcis, where a band of Druj lies in wait. If rescued, they would support a new college of potions there.

Sarangrave.t: Druj fleeing the vallorn in Eastring ran into the Nesustak Forest rebels and their allies, and few survived. Freed slaves, both humans and orcs, also reached Sarangrave.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Apothecaries' Guildhouse would cost less upkeep if built in Skarsind.

Therunin.t: The vallorn claimed Eastring and the Thimble, and Thornsong House burned. The weakening vallorn may still take more of the territory before the Spring Equinox, and the cut-off Druj cling to four regions.

Crossroads.d: Across the Empire, runecasters kept drawing Gralm (the Crossroads), Ull (the Coin) and the blank twenty-seventh rune. League troupes found themselves staging the Prince and the Witch. Urizen astronomancers read a conjunction of the Wanderer with the hidden Stork, the sign of making the right choice for the right reasons. While the conjunction lasted, Signs and Portents, Whispering Shadow Courtiers and Dreams in the Witch House rose in magnitude by two. Call Winged Messenger, The Ambassadorial Gatekeeper and The Ethereal Courier fell by two, and green iron could stand in for crystal mana at two measures to one. Sensitive characters dreamt of crossroads, games of chance, ravens and spiders. The effects faded within a month of the Summer Solstice.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Stork's meaning is likened to what Highguard calls the Decision to be Virtuous.

Urizen.t: Urizen astronomancers and Hakima watched the Summer skies and saw a falling star, a crimson tear of the Phoenix, come to earth somewhere in Urizen's mountains. They traced the true sign to a conjunction of the Wanderer with the hidden Stork, the right choice made for the right reasons.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark runecasting carried the omen first, with Gralm, Ull and the blank rune appearing again and again. The page's vignette shows a Wintermark mystic telling a young Grimnir that his choice will shape his life but must be made alone.

Crossroads.o: In Summer 379YE a conjunction of fate and chance settled over the Empire. Runecasters, astronomancers and League players all saw signs of crossroads and fateful choices, and the conjunction made divinatory magic harder while easing rituals that carry decisions already made.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: in the opening vignette, a young Grimnir's fateful choice is whether to go south or stay in Skarsind.

Crow on the cradle.d: Since the Thule invasion of 368YE, a force of Varushkans, Wolves and orc bandits loyal to the Charnel Lord fought from the Broken Hill, eventually backing the Varushkan defenders. As the Thule pulled back to Krevsaty, the Charnel Lord called on old oaths sworn by the Malinov, Sloev and Pravin of Moresvah, who once led the Iron Helm before Empress Mariika disbanded it. His warriors could enlarge an existing army or form the core of a reborn Iron Helm. Years of war had ruined Karsk's roads, so Varushka could not support a third army without repairs. The Senate agreed to rebuild the roads, which was finished shortly before the Spring Equinox 380YE, and to restore the Iron Helm.

Thule.t: The Thule had made at least a short-term peace and withdrawn from Branoc and Crowslook to Krevsaty, though the Charnel Lord predicted that the peace would not last.

Varushka.t: Varushka was offered the Charnel Lord's warriors and the help of the old Moresvah families. The Senate chose to rebuild Karsk's roads so that a third army could be supported and to restore the Iron Helm under the black banner.

Crow on the cradle.o: With the Thule withdrawn from Branoc and Crowslook, the Charnel Lord of the Broken Hill prepared to return to slumber and offered his Varushkan followers to the Empire, either to enlarge an existing Varushkan army or to restore the Iron Helm. The Senate chose to rebuild Karsk's ruined roads and restore the Iron Helm.

Karsk/Branoc.t: The Thule withdrew from Branoc, and the Charnel Lord prepared to sleep in the Broken Hill, leaving Baruk and his blood-kin to guard the barrow. Some vales here supplied the warriors offered to Varushka.

Karsk/Crowslook.t: The Thule withdrew from Crowslook, whose vales included followers of the Charnel Lord available to join a Varushkan army.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: Krevsaty was where the Thule withdrew to after leaving Branoc and Crowslook.

Karsk/Moresvah.t: The Malinov, Sloev and Pravin families of Moresvah were reminded of their oath to raise the Iron Helm's black banner again, and the Moresvah miners were key to restoring that army.

Karsk/Nitrost.t: Mentioned in passing: vales in eastern Nitrost were among those whose people followed the Charnel Lord.

Karsk.t: War had left Karsk's road network ruined. The great work to rebuild it was completed before the Spring Equinox 380YE, allowing a third Varushkan army to be supported and permanently boosting the territory's mines and forests.

Crowned in rose and heather.d: No egregore can sense either missing figure, so the Court ruled both titles vacant, a decision that stands even if they return. Rival memorials were proposed: a park and pavilion in Holberg, or a Custodes Clavium granite tower in the Necropolis. The Senate might make the Chamberlain an Imperial title and decide the future of the Imperial Offices. The Synod could name her greatest achievement, endorse pilgrimage mandates inspired by her final address, or recognise possible ascension or a miracle in the Frieze of Flowers, whose depiction of her now appears to change. The Court also tightened its guidance so that using her Imperial favour in the Senate or Military Council consumes it.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: patriotic volunteers from Dawn and Holberg would provide the labour for the proposed memorial park in Holberg.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Necropolis is the traditional resting place of Thrones, and the Custodes Clavium offered to design a white granite tower there as her memorial. Her final address also fed interest in pilgrimage already strong among the Grey Pilgrims.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperatrix was credited with fortifying the Mourn after the rout of the Jotun.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes the appeal of encouraging pilgrims to walk the trods as the Navarr do.

The League.t: The League lost its Empress, Lisabetta von Holberg, whom its egregore can no longer sense. Many League citizens want her memorialised at home, and League figures such as Severin Teyhard von Holberg, Ortenzia di Sarvos and Benedict Pacelli von Holberg were tied to her offices or proposed mandates.

The Marches.t: Many common Marchers saw the Throne as their last defence against the Military Council, and they now fear for the interdiction of curses such as Rivers Run Red.

Urizen.t: Urizen lost a staunch supporter of its military, and the page asks who will now champion its cause while it is threatened on two fronts.

Varushka.t: Varushka's egregore can no longer sense Imperial Magus Juha, and unconfirmed reports say the Varushkan magician Simargl, the Empty One, guided the pair on a quest into the Dreamscape.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Kellua Itsepainen of Wintermark was one of the Imperatrix's senior chamberlains, and the vanished Empress Mariika is cited as a precedent.

Crowned in rose and heather.o: In Autumn 383YE the Constitutional Court ruled that Imperatrix Lisabetta and Imperial Magus Juha, who vanished on the second night of the Summer Solstice, were legally dead or resigned, leaving both titles vacant. The page set out opportunities for the Senate and Synod to mark her legacy.

Bastion.t: Pilgrims to Bastion customarily visit the Necropolis, which many argue is the right place for the Imperatrix's official memorial.

Bay of Catazar.t: Doubts arose over whether the great plan to fortify the territories around the Bay of Catazar can be completed without an Empress to pay for it.

Holberg.t: Holberg was the Empress's home city, and architect Katarzyna von Carstein proposed a memorial park and white stone pavilion there. It would need a Senate commission, 50 wains of weirwood and 25 of white granite.

Mournwold.t: The Imperatrix was unexpectedly popular in the Mournwold, credited with its development and fortification, and her loss raised the greatest concern here, including over the interdiction of Rivers Run Red.

Necropolis.t: Tradition places Thrones' tombs here, and the Custodes Clavium offered a 189-step tower of 50 wains of white granite. Building it would need a Senate motion and 100 crowns but would not use a civil service commission slot.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Empress Mariika walking into Sydanjaa in 234YE is cited as an earlier Throne who disappeared without trace.

Crusade.d: The new army, proposed by Valentin of House Orzel, Senator for Weirwater, was mustering in Semmerholm amid calls to revive the Gryphon's Pride, lost in the Barrens in 276YE. The Barrens orcs had attacked the Towers of the Dawn, and troubadours urged conquest despite the orcs' legal status as foreigners. The national assembly endorsed glorious battle and crusade there, and Frederik Novarion supplied 50 liao. Dawnish units supporting the Golden Sun or defending the Towers gained a bonus; others suffered the Scorn of the Troubadours. Many nobles helped hold the Towers, but only one army joined the crusade while the Hounds of Glory and Eastern Sky attacked Spiral, and the troubadours abandoned the cause.

Dawn.t: Dawn's national assembly endorsed a crusade in the Barrens, rewarding units that fought there and shaming those that did not. Pride in saving the Towers turned to dismay when only the Golden Sun joined the effort.

Druj.t: The Druj were said to have been driven back from the Barrens, leaving only the Barrens orcs between Dawn and the territory. Tales held that even the Druj feared the heart of the Forest of Peytaht, though they had moved armies through it.

Grendel.t: Rather than join the crusade, the Dawnish Hounds of Glory and Eastern Sky boldly attacked Grendel-held Spiral, which the Dawnish generals evidently saw as the real priority.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named; its link is Reikos, where the Hounds of Glory and Eastern Sky were stationed at the start of the season.

Jotun.t: A well-publicised agreement with the Jotun kept Dawnish armies away from the western border in favour of hero-to-hero battles beyond the Sentinel Gate, freeing Dawn's attention for the Barrens.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the war in Holberg is recalled as a time when the Druj moved armies through the Forest of Peytaht.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: a Dawnish knight warned that once Dawn became bogged down in Urizen, it would not easily get free to strike the Barrens.

Crusade.o: In Winter 379YE, with Dawn's fourth army nearly mustered and Barrens orcs attacking the Towers of the Dawn, Dawnish ambition to conquer the Barrens revived. The Dawnish national assembly backed a crusade, but the enthusiasm faded by season's end.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: The Barrens orcs attacked the Towers of the Dawn and the houses of Dawnguard. Many Dawnish nobles and their retinues helped hold the nearly fallen Towers through the siege.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn-infested depths of Brocéliande were named as one dangerous route from Reikos to Dawnguard.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: in the last months of the war in Holberg, the Druj moved their armies through the Forest of Peytaht.

Reikos.t: The Hounds of Glory and Eastern Sky began the season in Reikos, from where the quickest route to the Barrens lay through the feared Forest of Peytaht.

Semmerholm.t: Dawn's fourth army was nearly mustered in Semmerholm, with nobles pressing for it to take up the banner of the Gryphon's Pride.

Spiral.t: The Hounds of Glory and Eastern Sky attacked in Spiral instead of joining the Barrens crusade, and Spiral Castle was said to have admitted it was part of Dawn again.

The Barrens.t: Dawn proclaimed a crusade to conquer the Barrens, prized for the mithril of the Fangs and the weirwood of Peytaht, but only the Golden Sun joined. Its strategy of ambushes rather than open battle failed to keep the cause alive.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: Valentin of House Orzel, Senator for Weirwater, proposed the fourth Dawnish army and was expected to announce its name and composition.

Culling the threat.d: Naomi offered several routes. Invading the Forest of Ulnak would permanently end the threat to any Ossium region no longer bordering Druj land. Echofell could be secured by commissioning a new Tower of the Manticore before the end of the Autumn Equinox, which Dawn could support by mandate. Alternatively, Varushka or Highguard could arm the orcish Dreamers of the Dark Forest if the Senate approved, or the Empire could permanently cede Echofell to the Thule. The Drownbark Forest could be protected by Dripping Echoes of the Fen, made permanent with 100 rings of ilium. Another option was a sovereign's offer to drown the forest, destroying the Palace of Orieb. The Cabalist of the Hollow Stone was charged with stopping the Druj at Marshstand Skerry.

Dawn.t: Lise de Lionsgate offered reworked plans for the Tower of the Manticore. A proposed Dawnish mandate would send knights-errant, questing knights and war witches to guard its construction and open a Secure the Echofell venture for Dawnish units.

Druj.t: Druj insurgents lurking in Echofell, the Drownbark Forest and the Webwood were the target of every option presented. Meanwhile warriors from across the Arkad, accompanied by heralds of the Burnt Steward, moved to destroy Marshstand Skerry.

Highguard.t: Naomi, herself Highborn, proposed that the Highborn assembly urge citizens to arm the Dreamers of the Dark Forest, echoing Highguard's old gifts of arms to the Imperial Orcs. Doing so would let Highborn units train the Dreamers, but only once the Senate authorised it.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn soldiers once gave weapons and armour to the Imperial Orcs when they joined the Empire, and this was cited as a precedent for arming the Dreamers.

Thule.t: The Thule refused direct aid, saying the Empire had cooled on collaboration. They offered to deal with the Druj in both Echofell and their own Webwood if the Senate permanently ceded Echofell to them.

Varushka.t: Ossium's Senator Vesna Borkovna requested the appraisal, and Varushkan cabalists advised on Dripping Echoes of the Fen and on the Landgrave's offer. The Varushkan assembly could arm the Dreamers or approve the drowning of the Drownbark Forest, and Varushkan units could Seek Glory in the Twisted Woods once the Tower stood.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Webwood had been conceded to the Thule under the Winter treaty that secured their military aid in Sermersuaq.

Culling the threat.o: The Prognosticator Naomi of Virtue's Rest, appointed by the Imperial Auditor at the Senate's request, laid out options for ending the Druj threat to Echofell and the Drownbark Forest in Ossium. Meanwhile a Druj force accompanied by heralds of Surut moved to destroy Marshstand Skerry.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: Mentioned in passing: the Gryphon's Pride was setting up camps and resupplying in Bittershore when the Druj force was spotted.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: The marshy region could be protected by Dripping Echoes of the Fen, or drowned by the servants of the Landgrave of the Still Deeps' sovereign, which would sink the Palace of Orieb. A Druj force was heading through the Broken Clearing to destroy Marshstand Skerry.

Ossium/Echofell.t: Echofell could be secured by building a new Tower of the Manticore before the end of the Autumn Equinox, by arming the Dreamers of the Dark Forest with Senate approval, or by permanently ceding the region to the Thule, which would anger Cathan Canae.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: If the Landgrave's sovereign were allowed to flood the Drownbark Forest, Nearweald would also be affected and gain the marsh quality, making commissions there harder.

Ossium/Webwood.t: The Thule-held Webwood remained under Druj threat, with speculation about the Spider King's temple in its depths. The Thule promised to clear it of Druj if Echofell were ceded to them.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Naomi identified the Druj-held Forest of Ulnak as the root of the threat. Any Ossium region that ceased to border Druj land there would be permanently secured, though an invasion would be blind and would face an immense fortification.

Ossium.t: Echofell, the Drownbark Forest and the Webwood remained under threat from the Druj, and the options to secure them ranged from fortifications and magic to ceding land to the Thule or flooding the eastern marshes. Marshstand Skerry also faced a direct Druj attack.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule's military aid in Sermersuaq was secured by conceding the Webwood to them under the Winter treaty.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dreamers of the Dark Forest were among the orc septs who chose not to relocate to Skarsind.

Cup of choices.d: Following Navarr, Loyalty and Urizen assembly mandates in Winter 387YE, Navarri and Urizeni magicians drew up proposals. Mithril Woven Nets in Ventosi would raise Redoubt's mana sites and create the Woven Architect of Crystal to buy mana and sunfruit. Rebuilding Sunspire in Peregro would create the Arbiter of Sunspire, who would receive prismatic ink, and would add a ritual to Urizen lore. The Citadel Guard could adopt the Technique of the Immanent Claw. A Navarr-built Eastern Citadel in Sarangrave would hold a 3,000-strong garrison. Arhallogen offered the Venom Den one last time, but it remains proscribed by the Synod. All were opportunities, not completed works.

Dawn.t: Dawnish military units, alongside Urizeni and Navarr ones, could take the Patrol Béantal Dol guarding action if the Eastern Citadel were built, earning rewards like those of a quest against the vallorn.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: a Druj force from Therunin is recalled as having looted and burned Sunspire after the Summer Solstice 386YE.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the mithril nets would protect Ventosi from flooding if the Foam and Spittle curse were used against the Grendel.

Navarr.t: The Navarr shared their centuries of vallorn lore with Urizen and helped design the proposals. These included the Eastern Citadel, a wayhouse whose Bulwark of the East would be a Navarr title, with a mixed Navarr and Urizeni garrison.

Urizen.t: Urizen was offered greater mana production in Redoubt and the chance to rebuild Sunspire, with a new ritual for its lore. The Citadel Guard could adopt a venom-focused technique, and a joint citadel could be built to defend Sarangrave.

Cup of choices.o: After the Navarr chose to share their knowledge of fighting the vallorn with Urizen, four months of joint work in the Urizen territories produced several proposed opportunities. They included a mana great work in Redoubt, the rebuilding of Sunspire, a new Citadel Guard technique, a fortified wayhouse in Sarangrave and Arhallogen's final offer of a fane.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Peregro is the site where Sunspire could be rebuilt, creating the Arbiter of Sunspire title and its prismatic ink income.

Redoubt/Ventosi.t: Mithril nets could be strung across the Ventosi cliffs to strengthen mana flows. They would also shield the region from flooding if the territory were cursed with Foam and Spittle.

Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh.t: Bloodwater Marsh is one of three possible sites for the Eastern Citadel, provided no other fortification stands there.

Sarangrave/Turan Flats.t: Turan Flats is one of three possible sites for the Eastern Citadel, provided no other fortification stands there.

Sarangrave/Whisperwood.t: Whisperwood could host the Eastern Citadel. It is also the proposed site of Arhallogen's Venom Den, a fane that is currently proscribed.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: the Scorpion Queen's offer is made despite the recent saga with the Navarr in Brocéliande.

Morrow.t: Sunspire, burned by the Druj in 386YE, could be rebuilt in Morrow as a sinecure. It would again be Urizen's centre for coordinating action against the vallorn.

Redoubt.t: A proposed great work would raise investment in every mana site in Redoubt by one. Its overseer would also be able to buy mana crystals and sunfruit from the territory's spires.

Sarangrave.t: The Eastern Citadel could be built here, giving the territory a 3,000-strong garrison, a patrol of Béantal Dol, higher taxation and continued magical targeting from the Imperial regio. Arhallogen also offered the proscribed Venom Den here.

Therunin.t: If the proscribed Venom Den were built, Arhallogen's heralds would help Imperial armies inflict extra casualties on the vallorn in Therunin as well as in Sarangrave.

Cuttings.d: Briars normally manifest their lineage in adulthood, occasionally in early teens, but almost never as infants. Since the Autumn Equinox eight newborns in Upwold have shown it from birth: seven in Tower March, and one to visitors from Ashill who spent three months in King's Stoke in the Spring. The children are healthy, indeed supernaturally so, age normally, and are being well cared for; one man who called them evil and urged that they be got rid of was sent home with his teeth in a sack. Speculation runs from a misplaced briar burial to the briar agitator or the risen Marcher dead. Talk of soldiers exposed to vernal curses and Rivers of Life elsewhere is largely dismissed as superstition.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj campaign is recalled as one in which potent spring curses were used by both sides in Holberg and Reikos.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard's territory of Reikos is named as a place where the Druj campaign saw potent vernal curses.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: League-held Holberg is named as a territory that saw potent spring curses during the Druj campaign.

The Marches.t: Marcher families in Tower March are raising an unprecedented number of infant briars and caring for them practically. Landskeepers are investigating the cause, and locals suspect a hidden briar burial, the briar agitator or the risen Marcher dead.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan Karsk is cited as a territory where Imperial armies often fought under the influence of Rivers of Life.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is cited as a territory where Imperial armies often fought under Rivers of Life auras.

Cuttings.o: In the winter of 379YE, eight babies born in Upwold over three months showed unmistakable briar lineage from birth, something practically unheard of; all trace back to Tower March, and nobody yet knows why.

Upwold/Tower March.t: Seven of the eight briar infants were born in Tower March, around King's Stoke, and the eighth was born to visitors who had stayed there. Local landskeepers are seeking the cause of what is clearly something amiss in the region.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is cited as a site of potent spring curses during the Druj campaign, though any link to the births is widely derided.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: Karsk is named as a territory where Imperial armies fought under Rivers of Life.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is cited as a site of potent spring curses from both sides during the Druj campaign.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is named as a territory where Imperial armies often fought under Rivers of Life.

Upwold.t: Eight babies born in Upwold in three months showed briar lineage from birth, with every case tracing back to Tower March.

Damming the Doubt.d: The proposed dam would flood the Fallen Valley, where soldiers who died at the Battle of Solen's Doubt lie buried, and send much of the Doubt's water to Icarion. The site is haunted and exposed to the Black Plateau. Nisha Strascovich enacted a Varushkan mandate sending volhovs to ward the dam against ghosts. Illarawm mystagogues began recovering Imperial Orc bones, protected by League priests preaching Loyalty. Carving the names of the fallen into the dam would add 5 thrones to its cost. Halkyon of the Myriad Stream made a statement in the Urizen assembly, and amity was granted to Ylenwe. The Senate, or a suitable title holder, has yet to commission the dam.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: named in the account of the final battle at Solen's Doubt, in which thousands of Imperial soldiers died.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc Assembly asked that bonetenders reclaim the remains of orcs who fell at Solen's Doubt and that their names be carved into the dam's stones. Illarawm mystagogues are now travelling to Apstrus to recover the bones, despite the grave danger the Black Plateau poses to orc priests.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn Assembly had not yet spoken on the matter. Freeborn custom treats life as a matter for the living, and many of their fallen were likely cremated.

The League.t: Rafael Barossa d'Apulian's statement embraced flooding the battle site, in keeping with Leaguish funeral customs. Fabio Costas d'Apulian, Sofonisba Amilcara of the City Below and Merlof Von Temeschwar led their congregations to Apstrus to protect the mystagogues.

Urizen.t: The Urizen Assembly was invited to decide how its dead at Solen's Doubt should be treated and whether the spire's library should be preserved. Halkyon of the Myriad Stream made a well-regarded statement that passed with a greater majority, and its outcome is still to come.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan Assembly backed the reservoir, asked that the deeds of the dead be recognised, and enacted a mandate through Nisha Strascovich. Volhovs will travel to Spiral to ward the dam and its workers against restless spirits.

Damming the Doubt.o: In Spring 387YE, preparations were made to dam the River Doubt in Apstrus to relieve the aridity of Icarion. The Varushkan, Imperial Orc, League and Urizen assemblies all acted on the graves of the fallen at Solen's Doubt, and the Conclave granted amity to the eternal Ylenwe so that zie could aid the project.

Mareave/Icarion.t: A good portion of the River Doubt's waters would be redirected to Icarion to ease its aridity.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: The dam and reservoir would flood the Fallen Valley beside the abandoned spire of Solen's Doubt. Volhovs are coming to ward the site against ghosts, mystagogues are recovering orc bones there, and the River Doubt below would be much reduced.

Spiral/Screed.t: Mentioned in passing: the madness lying in wait at the heart of Screed threatens any army working on the dam.

Mareave.t: The dam is part of ongoing efforts to relieve the aridity of Mareave by redirecting much of the River Doubt into the territory.

Spiral.t: Spiral would gain a dam and a large reservoir, built on haunted ground under threat from the Black Plateau. With amity now granted, the eternal Ylenwe is able to aid the work, and zie has offered plans for a protective fane if friendship lasts a year.

Dark skies.d: Astronomancers in Urizen, Varushka and the Brass Coast reported a new star, invisible to the naked eye, following the Wanderer; the Conclave has not named it, and some mystics link it to the unnamed rune. Scholars of the Observatory of the Blazing Mirror in Iteri, aided by Camillius of Endsmeet, built a device to study it, housed in the new Camillius Steeple, to be unveiled at the Spring Equinox. The Phoenix is waning, making its magic and arcane projections harder, except for Winterfolk. Psychological ailments keep climbing, with tragedies in Bregasland, Temeschwar and Kallavesa. Over Skarsind and Holberg the night sky is empty, and naga who dwell there grow markedly more secretive.

Imperial Orcs.t: The night skies over Skarsind, the Imperial Orcs' new homeland, have become entirely empty save for the moon, an unexplained phenomenon unlike the Penumbral Veil.

The League.t: Holberg's night skies have vanished, and in Temeschwar a troupe master slew his entire cast during a production of "The Swords of Absalom", raving about ghosts of dead actors possessing the living.

The Marches.t: A Bregasland fendweller imprisoned two neighbours in a lightless pit as part of an incomprehensible study of fear, one sign of the mania spreading through the Empire.

Urizen.t: Urizen astronomancers helped sight the new star, and the Observatory of the Blazing Mirror in Iteri built the Camillius Steeple to study it, with an unveiling planned for the Spring Equinox.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: astronomancers from Varushkan observatories were among those who reported sighting the new star.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk magicians alone can create arcane projections without the extra effort the fading Phoenix imposes, for reasons no one understands, while a circle of Kallavesi mystics poisoned themselves in their marshes.

Dark skies.o: In Spring 380YE the heavens grew disturbed: a tiny new star was seen trailing the Wanderer, the constellation of the Phoenix began to fade, and the night skies over Skarsind and Holberg became entirely empty save for the moon, while cases of mania continued to rise across the Empire.

Zenith/Iteri.t: The Observatory of the Blazing Mirror in Iteri constructed the Camillius Steeple to examine the new star, with Arbiter Horace inviting Camillius of Endsmeet to give the keynote at its Spring Equinox unveiling, which archmages and grandmasters were expected to attend.

Bregasland.t: A fendweller imprisoned two of her neighbours in a lightless pit as part of a bizarre study of fear.

Holberg.t: The night skies over the recently liberated city are entirely empty save for the moon, and naga who spend long periods there find their secretiveness greatly strengthened.

Kallavesa.t: A circle of Kallavesi mystics poisoned themselves in the marshes, leaving a hastily scrawled note about their intention to "merge with the cosmos".

Skarsind.t: The night skies over the Imperial Orcs' new homeland are empty but for the moon, and naga who dwell there long grow compulsively secretive.

Temeschwar.t: A production of "The Swords of Absalom" ended in tragedy when the troupe master was found to have slain the entire cast.

Zenith.t: Zenith is home to the Observatory of the Blazing Mirror, whose scholars built a device to study the new star in the newly named Camillius Steeple.

Darkest night.d: Over roughly a year the starless night had spread across ten territories. It now covers all of the Empire, the former Imperial territories of Liathaven and the Mournwold, and Brocéliande. Skies look normal by day, but at night only the moon is visible. The stars' magic can still be felt. A magnitude forty-one Night shroud, detectable even by day, blocks lesser scrying such as Eyes of the Sun and Moon, Eye of the High Places and Dreams in the Witch House, for foreign magicians and eternals alike. Naga across the affected lands struggle to be open or honest. The Augurs of the Opalescent Gloaming of Hahnmark gave the Imperial Seer the Hawk's Demeanour mask and promised two doses of Waters of the Shimmering Shore.

Druj.t: The Barrens, held by the Druj, were among the first lands to lose their stars and remain under the shroud, which blocks attempts to scry them below magnitude forty-one.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Necropolis was already starless, and now Casinea and the rest of its lands are dark at night and shrouded against scrying.

Imperial Orcs.t: Skarsind, held by the Imperial Orcs, was one of the earliest territories swallowed by the Empty Skies and remains under the scrying-blocking shroud.

Jotun.t: The Jotun-held former Imperial territories of Liathaven and the Mournwold are now under the starless sky and shroud, making them very hard for anyone to scry, and naga there feel the urge to secrecy.

The Brass Coast.t: Segura was among the territories already darkened, and the Brass Coast's lands remain shrouded against scrying with no stars visible at night.

The League.t: Holberg was one of the first territories whose stars vanished, and the League's lands remain beneath the magnitude forty-one shroud.

The Marches.t: Bregasland had already lost its stars, and the Marches now sit wholly under the starless night and its scrying-blocking shroud.

Varushka.t: Volodmartz, Karsk and Miekarova were all among the earlier starless territories, leaving Varushka thoroughly shrouded against divination.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's lands are shrouded, and the Winterfolk Augurs of the Opalescent Gloaming answered by gifting the Imperial Seer a magical mask and promising two doses of Waters of the Shimmering Shore.

Darkest night.o: Shortly after the 380YE Autumn Equinox, the Empty Skies phenomenon spread to blot out the stars over every Imperial territory, plus Liathaven, the Mournwold and Brocéliande, leaving only the sky within a mile of Anvil unchanged. A powerful shroud now hampers scrying, naga find their secretive urges greatly strengthened, and a Wintermark circle has stepped forward to aid the Imperial Seer.

Hahnmark/Kronemark.t: The Augurs of the Opalescent Gloaming are based at White Owl Hall on the icy shores of Lake Kronevann, from where they sent their gifts to the Imperial Seer.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland was among the territories already starless before the phenomenon spread, and it remains under the magnitude forty-one shroud.

Brocéliande.t: Though not an Imperial territory, Vallorn-held Brocéliande is now also covered by the starless sky and shroud, and the naga effect applies there.

Casinea.t: Casinea now falls under the starless night sky and the scrying-blocking shroud along with every other Imperial territory.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark is now shrouded and starless, and is home to the Augurs of the Opalescent Gloaming, who have made gifts to the Imperial Seer in response.

Holberg.t: Holberg was one of the earliest territories to lose its stars and remains shrouded against scrying below magnitude forty-one.

Karsk.t: Karsk had already lost its stars before the spread and remains under the shroud.

Liathaven.t: Jotun-held Liathaven, a former Imperial territory, is now included in the starless sky, the shroud and the naga effect.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova was among the territories already swallowed by the Empty Skies and remains shrouded against divination.

Mournwold.t: The Jotun-held Mournwold, a former Imperial territory, is now covered by the starless night and the shroud, and naga there feel driven to secrecy.

Necropolis.t: Necropolis was one of the earlier territories to lose its stars and remains beneath the magnitude forty-one shroud.

Segura.t: Segura had already gone starless before the spread and stays shrouded against scrying.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq was among the first territories to go starless and remains under the shroud.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind was among the territories already starless and continues under the shroud that impedes large-scale scrying.

The Barrens.t: The Druj-held Barrens were already starless, and the naga effect explicitly applies there along with the shroud.

Volodmartz.t: Volodmartz had already lost its stars before the phenomenon spread Empire-wide and remains shrouded.

Daughters of the Empire.d: Highborn priests argued that tradition demands every Throne have a memorial in the Necropolis, and that Britta's shrine fell quiet because its purpose was unclear. They proposed a Highborn mandate naming one virtue tied to one of her deeds, plus a Senate motion costing 20 crowns of labour to alter the shrine and turn the Guardian of Britta's Shrine into the Guardian of Britta's Memorial, appointed by the relevant Virtue assembly. Sister Sarah of the Suns of Couros enacted a mandate for Courage, and the Senate amended the title and approved the alterations. Abigail of Ira's Shield proposed an Echoing Obelisk with an Archivist title. Frederick di Sarvos met several people at the summit about Lisabetta's tomb, with no clear outcome yet.

Highguard.t: The Highborn assembly and congregations drove the debate over Britta's memorial and passed the mandate for Courage. Highborn archivists also championed the proposed Echoing Obelisk to keep forgotten soldiers remembered.

The League.t: The League architect Frederick di Sarvos was invited by Ruth of the Cenotaph to design Empress Lisabetta's tomb. He postponed his trip to the Commonwealth and came to Anvil to hear proposals, refusing to meet Cardinal Viviane de Coeurdefer or Ranae de Rondell.

Wintermark.t: Britta remains an undisputed inspiration to the Winterfolk, and only a few grumbled that she was not interred in the Necropolis. Her memorial was rededicated so that her inspiration would reach the wider Empire.

Daughters of the Empire.o: Elkiah's Autumn 383YE statement calling for Empress Britta's neglected shrine in the Necropolis to be repurposed stirred Highborn priests to propose rededicating it to the virtue she best inspired, alongside a proposed memorial to forgotten soldiers and an invitation to the architect Frederick di Sarvos to design Empress Lisabetta's tomb. After the Winter Solstice, Britta's memorial was rededicated to Courage.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: Empress Britta's body rests in the marshes of Kallavesa, where it was moved from the Necropolis.

Necropolis.t: Britta's quiet shrine in the Necropolis was rededicated as a memorial to her Courage, with Senate-approved alterations, so it could become a place of pilgrimage again. A new Echoing Obelisk beside the Silent Obelisks was also proposed there.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: a young pilgrim in the story comes from Sarvos, and the architect at the centre of the Lisabetta tomb proposal bears the name Frederick di Sarvos.

Daybreak in Spiral.d: After Ylenwe was granted Amity, the Dawn Chorus arrived and settled at Solen's Doubt. Its song silences the Black Plateau's whispers but can confuse attackers. Ylenwe's heralds offered captains supporting the dam-building army a feather that works like a Circlet of Falling Snow. Carving the Imperial Orcs' fallen into the dam would add five thrones, and relocating Solen's Doubt's library to a new Dreaming Spire another five; both must be settled in the dam's commission. The omphalos lies on Mount Lutum in Iteri or Mount Cinnius in Ankra, depending on whether Spiral is counted. The heralds visited the Block, held by the Silver Flame rebels. Their leader Caela asked the Conclave for a Declaration of Concord granting them Imperial Lore.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the rebels are said to be no more Urizeni than the so-called Earl of the Groves is Dawnish.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Urizeni are once again fighting to keep the Druj from their homes in north-east Zenith.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Solen's Doubt was the site of a decisive battle against the Grendel, and the opening story features a Lost orc once of that nation.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc Assembly's demand to carve the names of the fallen into the dam can be met for an extra five thrones. Whoever commissions the dam must state whether this will be done, and the orcs are likely to object if it is not.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the page recalls the bitter days when the League took Spiral and nation seemed set to war against nation.

Urizen.t: Halkyon's statement inspired a call to found a Dreaming Spire at the nation's omphalos, which would preserve Solen's Doubt's library and let Urizeni take new resources there. Meanwhile the Silver Flame rebels, no longer bound by the egregore, seek Imperial Lore their people helped to build.

Daybreak in Spiral.o: In Summer 387YE the Dawn Chorus, a feathered guardian of the Eternal Ylenwe, settled at the ruined spire of Solen's Doubt in Spiral to protect those who would dam the River Doubt. Further opportunities arose to found a Dreaming Spire at Urizen's omphalos, and the Silver Flame rebels asked for access to Imperial Lore.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Damming the River Doubt is intended to relieve Icarion's aridity.

Spiral/Ankra.t: Mount Cinnius in Ankra, on the border with Cinion, is the omphalos if Spiral is counted part of Urizen, and the Silver Flame would support a spire built there.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: The Dawn Chorus settled at the ruined spire of Solen's Doubt, which would sit at the centre of the planned reservoir, and Ylenwe's heralds descended from a spring above Apstrus.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Ylenwe's heralds traced the Block to Cinion and, after tense talks brokered by a herald of That Which Lives In Its Name, were allowed to visit it under the Silver Flame rebels' watch.

Zenith/Iteri.t: Mount Lutum in Iteri, where Spire Calator once stood, is the omphalos if Urizen is counted as Zenith, Redoubt and Morrow, making it a possible site for the Dreaming Spire.

Mareave.t: The planned dam on the Doubt is part of the effort to relieve the aridity of Mareave's Icarion region.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is one of the territories counted when scholars calculate the geographic centre of Urizen.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt counts in the omphalos calculation, and its spires trade and cooperate with the Silver Flame rebels.

Spiral.t: The Dawn Chorus and Ylenwe's heralds now soothe parts of the cursed land, a Dreaming Spire may be founded in Ankra, and the rebels holding the Block in Cinion are seeking Imperial Lore.

Zenith.t: Mount Lutum in Iteri is one candidate site for the Dreaming Spire. Halkyon's words resonate strongly in north-east Zenith, where the Urizeni are fighting the Druj.

Daylight fading.d: Mine and forest owners in Miekarova, Karov and Volodmartz now share 35 ingots and 35 forest measures, and Ossium's forest owners share 70. The Crow Roads in Karsk were reduced to the same level. Five Bourse resources each gain 2 wains a season. Ossium is no longer under-populated, so Varushka could support a fourth army, and the Assembly may offer guidance. Tasya urged the Malinov to release the axe Hunger. Boyar Svetlana refused and offered yearly axes for Varushkan generals instead. The Charnel Lord offered spy networks into Thule and Druj lands, while a rival mandate would reject him. Further mandates could encourage bargaining with sovereigns or peaceful contact with orcs.

Druj.t: The Charnel Lord offered to help Varushkans set up a spy network in the Forest of Ulnak, promising the Druj would not notice it unless someone acted foolishly. This is an offer that depends on a Synod mandate.

Highguard.t: Jared proposed a Partners of Greatness mandate in which Highguard would support Varushkan efforts to deal with the orcs in their lands. It would fail automatically if the Varushkans do not enact their own mandate.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are not named, though the Thule holdings in Crow's Ridge in Skarsind would be covered by the proposed Urdur spy network.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: a previous Varushkan claimant to be Alderei reborn reportedly destroyed the Jotun meeting stone, antagonising the western orcs.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the inspiration of Ratibor of Temeschwar and his attributed saying, 'if you can destroy it, you control it', circulated among Varushkans eyeing the Senate-held Bourse resources.

Thule.t: The Charnel Lord offered to help Varushka spy on Sküld and Urdur, and on Thule holdings in Varushka, Sermersuaq and Skarsind, unseen by Hinodir of the Bright Orb. A rival mandate warned this could break the peace treaty. A further mandate could encourage peaceful dealings with the Thule in Varushka.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen pilgrims visiting the Maze of Zoria recalled Clytemnestra's threat to destroy the Citadel Guard, feeding Varushkan talk about reclaiming Bourse resources.

Varushka.t: The completed Iron Roads enriched Varushka's mines, forests and Bourse resources and made a fourth army possible. The National Assembly now faces choices on the new army, the axe Hunger, the Charnel Lord's spy offer, and whether to bargain with sovereigns or orcs.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the jealousy of Wintermark still rankles with Varushkans, and the hylje of Wintermark were contrasted with the monstrous creatures of Varushka.

Daylight fading.o: Varushka completed the Iron Roads and the port-town of Kostjyas Respite in Spring 385YE, boosting prosperity across its territories and making a fourth Varushkan army possible. Meanwhile an envoy of the Charnel Lord, Tasya of the Black Feathers, walked the new roads with requests and offers, and an Assembly statement about sapient creatures caused confusion in the vales.

Karsk/Branoc.t: The Charnel Lord sleeps beneath the Broken Barrow here. Captains using his spy network must leave a blood gift at the barrow, and woods-wise guides from Branoc's vales, human and independent orc, would lead them.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: The Thule-controlled Krevsaty would be covered by the proposed Sküld spy network, and its orcs are among those Varushkans might be urged to contact peacefully.

Karsk/Moresvah.t: Tasya urged the Malinov of Moresvah to return the bloodthirsty axe Hunger to the Iron Helms. Boyar Svetlana refused, offering yearly axes for Varushka's generals if the Assembly endorses keeping Hunger hidden.

Miekarova/Miechernya.t: The Thule holdings in Miechernya would be covered by the proposed Urdur spy network, and its Thule orcs might be approached for peaceful deals.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: The new port at Bittershore helped clear away the last of Ossium's economic problems.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: The Thule-controlled Bonewood would be covered by the proposed Sküld spy network, and its orcs are among those Varushkans might contact.

Ossium/Echofell.t: Echofell would be covered by the proposed Sküld spy network.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: The sept of the Menrothat in Nearweald is named among the orcs Varushkans could be urged to make peaceful contact with.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Mentioned in passing: the Webwood is listed among the Varushkan lands controlled by the Thule.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: The Empire knows little of Sküld. The Charnel Lord offered a Varushkan-only spy network there, which would also report on Krevsaty, the Bonewood and Echofell.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: The Charnel Lord offered a Varushkan-only spy network in Urdur, which would also report on Thule holdings in the Silver Peaks, Crow's Ridge and Miechernya.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Thule holdings in the Silver Peaks would be reported on by the proposed Urdur spy network.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Thule holdings in Crow's Ridge would be reported on by the proposed Urdur spy network.
