Forest of Ulnak.t: The Empire knows almost nothing of the Forest of Ulnak. The Charnel Lord offered to help Varushkans establish a one-season spy network there, reached through the twisted woods of Branoc.

Karov.t: With the Iron Roads open, Karov's mine owners share 35 ingots and its forest owners share 35 forest measures each season.

Karsk.t: The Crow Roads' extra benefit fell to match the Iron Roads at 35 ingots and 35 measures. Tasya of the Black Feathers visited the Malinov and Karsk's priests, volhov and wise ones on the Charnel Lord's behalf.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova's mine and forest owners each gain a share of 35 ingots and 35 forest measures now that the Iron Roads are complete.

Ossium.t: The Iron Roads brought settlers and trade, so Ossium is no longer under-populated, which lets Varushka support a fourth army. Its forest owners share 70 forest materials, and its former Druj septs are among the orcs Varushkans might treat with.

Otkodov.t: The Charnel Lord offered to guide Varushkan scouts unseen through the mountains into Otkodov to spy on Sküld and Urdur, claiming the Thule dragons would not discover them.

Sermersuaq.t: If created, the proposed Urdur spy network would also report on Thule holdings in the Silver Peaks of Sermersuaq.

Skarsind.t: If created, the proposed Urdur spy network would also report on Thule holdings in Crow's Ridge in Skarsind.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Ratibor of Temeschwar is cited as an inspiration for Varushkan talk of reclaiming Bourse resources.

The Semmerlak.t: Mentioned in passing: work was completed on Kostjyas Respite, the new Varushkan port-town on the northern shores of the Semmerlak.

Verthandi.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire already has a map of Verthandi, unlike the rest of Otkodov.

Volodmartz.t: Volodmartz's mine and forest owners share 35 ingots and 35 forest measures each season thanks to the Iron Roads.

Dear green space.d: Restoring the park would mean destroying all vegetation and sculpture (20 wains of weirwood, 10 of white granite, 160 crowns, nine months) and closing the Wunderkind Woods regio with Wind of Mundane Silence. Sofia Rebeshi's coven offered to cast it in return for the cursed lumber, giving three foci to the Conclave. Tharim offered to lift the curse for two more years of amity, but would take the orchard and Flowers memorial too. Restoration ends the Pavilion's aura, though true liao might reconsecrate it. Alternatively, a ministry could create the Tender of the Blood Orchard title selling Winter vis and staffs, or a mithril great work could gate the park for business income. The two approaches are mutually exclusive.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn business folk are credited with keeping the park's waters safe, and the Highborn are said to be wary of taking a Winter herald at his word.

The League.t: Holberg's burghers must choose between costly restoration and embracing their cursed park; the League Assembly could reconsecrate the Pavilion with true liao, and the proposed Tender of the Blood Orchard would most suitably be a League national title.

The Marches.t: The Marcher Memorial Garden, with its orchard and memorial to General Flowers, survived the curse but would be destroyed if Tharim's offer were accepted unrenegotiated.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: in the fiction a Holberg man recalls his childhood vow to study astronomancy in Urizen.

Dear green space.o: After the Wisdom Assembly sent Hembeneth i Guerra with liao to seek a practical answer to Skathe's curse on Holmauer Park, Wise pilgrims gathered in Holberg and produced rival proposals: cleanse and restore the park, or accept and exploit the curse.

Holberg/Holfried.t: Mentioned in passing: the clocks of Holfried are heard striking midnight in the in-character story.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Holmauer Park is the subject of every proposal: tearing out the cursed woods and closing the regio, letting Tharim strip it, harvesting the Blood Orchard, or gating it for paying visitors, with the Pavilion's aura lost if the curse is lifted.

Holberg.t: Holberg faces a choice between restoring its cursed park as a great work or accepting the curse, with options for a Winter vis ministry, a new Imperial title, or a gated park sharing 743 rings a season with local businesses.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the curse fell as Sarvos's mirrors shattered, and a Sarvosan sage and Sarvosan fright-pamphlets are referenced.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Tharim's herald Obligatus at the Copse of the Bone Birch in Upwold confirmed the Bound King's offer to lift the curse.

Death is not the end.d: Priests from seven nations had shrunk Yael's congregation in Reikos, and their returning pilgrims now spoke out against her. Armies from opposing sides of the schism lost a fifth of their victory points when campaigning together, and military units supporting the other side had their effective ranks halved. Highguard's acceptance of Yael brought a surge in prosperity. Highborn supporters urged a foundationalist mandate declaring their assembly the sole authority on doctrine, which risked a deep rift with the Empire. Condemnation for heresy by the General Assembly or the Council of Nine was set out as the way to bring Yael to trial. Dawn's assembly then passed a mandate repudiating Yael, carried by Odelina de Rondell.

Dawn.t: Having first sung Yael's praises and then rejected a mandate to spread her song, the Dawnish assembly ended the confusion at the Summer Solstice by repudiating her, with Odelina de Rondell taking liao to call Dawnish pilgrims home and placing Dawn among the nations that reject her.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is described as reclaimed from the Druj and reborn, one of the signs Highborn take as heralding a new era.

Highguard.t: Highguard's embrace of Yael brought a surge of national confidence and prosperity, while supporters pressed for a foundationalist mandate making the Highborn Assembly the sole authority on doctrine, risking open conflict with the rest of the Empire. Doubters urged the assembly to reconsider.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs declared themselves no part of this dispute over human destiny, so their armies suffered no penalty and could fight effectively alongside either side of the schism.

Navarr.t: As one of the seven nations that rejected Yael, Navarr had sent a priest to call its people home from Reikos, and its armies now fought less effectively when campaigning beside Highborn or Dawnish forces.

The Marches.t: The Marches, having rejected Yael and sent a priest to bring its pilgrims home, saw returning Marchers turn against her, and its armies were penalised when campaigning alongside the other side of the schism.

Urizen.t: Urizen was among the seven nations that denounced Yael and recalled their pilgrims, and its armies suffered reduced effectiveness when fighting together with Highborn or Dawnish armies.

Varushka.t: Varushka had sent a priest to repudiate Yael and return its people from Reikos, and its armies now faced a penalty when campaigning beside armies from nations that embraced her.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark, one of the nations that rejected Yael, had brought its pilgrims home, and its armies were penalised when fighting alongside forces from the other side of the schism.

Death is not the end.o: In Summer 381YE the schism over Yael of Highguard's claim to be the reborn First Empress deepened: seven nations had denounced her while Highguard and Dawn had embraced her, and armies on opposite sides could no longer fight well together. At the Summer Solstice the Dawnish assembly resolved its uncertainty by repudiating Yael.

Casinea/Mareholm.t: Jerusha of the Black Watch at Mareholm delivered a pointed sermon arguing that no true reincarnation of the First Empress would reject the Synod's judgement, so Yael's defiance proved her false.

Bastion.t: Bastion, long the spiritual heart of the Way, stood to have that role challenged by a foundationalist mandate, and the Illuminators of Shadow scriptorium there announced they would bring a precious gift for the First Empress.

Casinea.t: Devout pilgrims of the First Empress in Casinea could be recruited into the Granite Pillar if the foundationalist mandate were enacted, and at Mareholm Jerusha of the Black Watch preached against Yael's rejection of the Synod.

Reikos.t: Reikos, hailed as restored and reborn, was where Yael's congregation gathered; it shrank as the seven nations' priests drew pilgrims home, though its devoted pilgrims remained a possible source of recruits for the Granite Pillar.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold appears only in the name of Cathy Upwold, one of the seven sent to Reikos to persuade pilgrims to abandon Yael.

Death leaves us homesick.d: A military treaty put the Gates of Ipotavo in the field in Sarangrave, and the Axou plan to take the Tower of the Skink and evict the orcs of Thornfen, expecting the Empire to deal with them. The Grand Council refused to join any plan to wake the vallorn of Visokuma. Kaban arrested the Scions of Cavan, self-proclaimed Navarr cousins accused of plotting to unleash it, and their leader begged for Imperial help. Navarr fleets met a cold reception in Axou ports. Theodosia of Ipotavo's Unified Convocation condemned the Synod over Fintan's execution. In the end the Scions were executed, the Navarr did not back a rescue raid, and the Assembly of the Way invited Axou priests to collect Fintan's remains.

Druj.t: The Axou were fighting the Druj in Sarangrave under the new treaty, with a Druj fortress standing between them and the Imperial armies. They planned to take the Tower of the Skink once the Druj were defeated.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Navarr jailbreak was compared to the Imperial Orcs' earlier freeing of the Tamazi from the citadels.

Navarr.t: Suspicion over the vallorn left Navarr fleets with a cold reception and reduced production in Axou ports. Some thorns urged a rescue raid into Kabanja to save the Scions of Cavan, but the Navarr did not back it and the Scions were executed.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: a League assembly statement on Axou soldiers visiting the Five Cities Military Academy and the Barossa School had gone largely unnoticed in Axos and lacked legal backing.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Axos is described as lying south-east of Urizen, and the Assembly of the Nine is quoted warning that rousing the vallorn would raze Axos.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Ambassador to Axos, Thanmir Hrafnar, is of Wintermark.

Death leaves us homesick.o: In winter 387YE the civil service reported on Imperial relations with Axos. The Axou welcomed the Sarangrave treaty but flatly refused any part in waking the Visokuma vallorn, arrested the Scions of Cavan for plotting to rouse it, turned cold towards the Navarr, and asked to collect Fintan Nighthaven's remains.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: The Axou declared that once they held the Tower of the Skink they would first evict every orc living in Thornfen, including those at Sephals. They assumed the Empire would deal with relocating them.

Sarangrave.t: The Axou Gates of Ipotavo were fighting the Druj here under the treaty, and Axos intended to claim the Tower of the Skink and evict the orcs of Thornfen. A proposed Navarr raid into Kabanja would have been launched from here.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Axou interest in sending soldiers to the Barossa School of Imperial Strategy is noted as an unanswered matter.

Death of a salesman.d: The civil service's acquirers came back empty-handed, and no private auction would be held. Most acquirers were reassigned, and no remedy had been found. Five opportunities arose in its place. Iñes i Daero of the Saffron Sails would auction a long-hallowed fragment of Emperor Barabbas's flagship in the Freeborn camp. The orc bonesetter Whed sought Sunhammer Krag's help to sell a white tablet and letters found in Crow's Ridge. Basileus Flint offered two seasons' hire of the Shrouded spies, with the Grendel's sealed bid as the floor. The Red Maggots would sell the Black Garden, a Realmsroot-bearing estate in West Marsh. Escon called Highborn benefactors to hear funding appeals.

Grendel.t: Basileus Flint had already offered the Shrouded spies to the Grendel, and their sealed bid would set the minimum price at the Anvil auction. The relic for sale also recalled Barabbas's ill-fated fleet, which sailed against the Grendel in 199YE.

Highguard.t: Escon called wealthy Highborn to a benefactors' council in the Highborn camp. There the Heirs of Lepidus and the artisans of Esther's Forge would each seek investment in their work.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc bonesetter Whed bought a strange white tablet at the Torfast Trading Post. He planned to come to Anvil and ask overseer Sunhammer Krag to help him find a buyer.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven, then held by the Jotun, is named as the homeland of the Navarr refugee Hywel, who died fighting there.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Garden estate had belonged to the Navarr thorn Hywel. He pawned it to the Red Maggots before falling in battle in Liathaven.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: an acquirer had been disappointed by the Carta Raisa in Tassato, and the Heirs of Lepidus had worked with Tassato's School of Epistemology.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the letters found with the white tablet were correspondence from 160YE between a Kallavesi mystic and a Thule from Neeyukir about uncovering the past.

Wintermark.t: The Red Maggots would auction the Black Garden, a Kallavesi estate that yields herbs and Realmsroot, in the Wintermark camp. The garden was considered of primary interest to Wintermarkers.

Death of a salesman.o: The Bourse private auction collapsed after years of poor returns, rumours of a price-fixing cartel and the excommunication of the Pledge's owners, so the civil service cancelled it for the coming summit. Instead, several private sellers announced their own sales and appeals at Anvil.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: The Black Garden lies half-sunk in West Marsh, its ruined stone estate overrun with herbs and Realmsroot. Locals rumoured that it was unsafe and close to regiones of Winter or Night.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: The tablet, writing case and letters were found by a hunting orc in Crow's Ridge. Winterfolk there angrily drove him away from the area.

Kallavesa.t: A deserted estate in Kallavesa, the Black Garden, was found overgrown with rare herbs and Realmsroot. Its new owners, the Red Maggots, put it up for sale.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Hywel, the estate's former owner, was a refugee from Liathaven who died after rejoining the army to fight there.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the artisans of Esther's Forge, who asked to address the benefactors' council, have their chapter house near Necropolis.

Skarsind.t: An orc hunting in Skarsind found the white tablet and its letters. He was driven off by angry Winterfolk but kept his find and sold it at the Torfast Trading Post.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the Carta Raisa in Tassato had disappointed a Bourse acquirer, and the city's School of Epistemology had helped the Heirs of Lepidus.

Declare Feni group to be foreigners.d: The motion declared the Feni group calling itself "The Woods That Fell" to be foreigners, and it passed. These are the Feni who fled when the sinkhole opened. At the time there was one large group of them in Hahnmark and another in the Mournwold, and both were still raiding local settlements in those areas. The motion was proposed by the senator for Bregasland and seconded by the senator for Kallavesa.

The Marches.t: The Marcher senator for Bregasland proposed the declaration, which leaves one of the two large groups of raiding Feni, the one in the Marcher-held Mournwold, legally foreign.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's senator for Kallavesa seconded the motion, which applies to one of the two raiding Feni groups, the one sheltering in the Wintermark territory of Hahnmark.

Declare Feni group to be foreigners.o: In Summer 382YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Bregasland and seconded by Kallavesa, declaring the Feni tribe known as "The Woods That Fell" to be foreigners.

Hahnmark.t: One of the two large groups of "The Woods That Fell" Feni was in Hahnmark and was still raiding local settlements there when it was declared foreign.

Mournwold.t: A large group of "The Woods That Fell" Feni was in the Mournwold and was still raiding local settlements there when it was declared foreign.

Declare Mournwold thralls foreigners.d: Proposed by the senator for Upwold and seconded by the senator for Segura, the motion settled the legal status of the former Jotun thralls who remained in the Mournwold. It passed, and the orc thralls there became foreigners in the eyes of the Empire. As a consequence it became legal to trade with them, while it became illegal to force them off their land, kill them, engage them with Imperial armies or steal their holdings.

The Marches.t: Marcher settlers in the Mournwold must now live alongside the former Jotun thralls as lawful foreigners, free to trade with them but barred from driving them off, killing them or taking their holdings, and the motion was proposed by Upwold's senator.

Declare Mournwold thralls foreigners.o: The Senate passed a motion in Winter 381YE designating the orc thralls living in the Imperial territory of Mournwold as foreigners under Imperial law.

Mournwold.t: The orc thralls left in the Mournwold gained legal protection as foreigners, so trading with them became lawful while evicting, killing or robbing them, or sending Imperial armies against them, became illegal.

Declare Ossium orcs as foreigners.d: In Summer 383YE the senator for Ossium proposed, and the senator for Volodmartz seconded, a motion to declare the orc tribes formerly subjugated by the Druj in Ossium to be foreigners in Imperial lands. The motion covered only those orcs of Ossium who are not Druj. It passed, and the orcs of Ossium are now legally foreigners rather than barbarians. The page notes that the decision has implications for the Varushkan settlers in Ossium, though it does not set them out.

Druj.t: The orcs the Druj once held in subjugation in Ossium are now distinguished from them in Imperial law, with the Druj themselves explicitly excluded from foreigner status.

Varushka.t: Varushkan senators for Ossium and Volodmartz proposed and seconded the motion, and its passing has implications for the Varushkan settlers in Ossium.

Declare Ossium orcs as foreigners.o: The Senate passed a motion declaring the orcs of Ossium who are not Druj, the former tribes the Druj had subjugated there, to be foreigners in Imperial lands.

Ossium.t: The non-Druj orcs living in Varushkan-held Ossium are now recognised as foreigners, which bears on how they and the Varushkan settlers there will live alongside one another.

Declare peace with Barrens orcs.d: The motion, proposed by Temeschwar and seconded by Holberg, granted the orcs of the Barrens all the legal protections and responsibilities of foreigners under Imperial law. The stated aim was to open negotiations with the three tribes that had once served the Druj and now occupied the Barrens. Because they were recognised as foreigners, any invasion of their lands by Imperial troops would become a criminal offence while that status stood. By the end of Spring 379YE the orcs of the Barrens had made no official response to the declaration.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the three Barrens tribes are described as having previously been subservient to the Druj, and the motion treats them as separate from their former masters.

Declare peace with Barrens orcs.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate declared the three orc tribes occupying the Barrens, formerly subservient to the Druj, to be foreigners rather than barbarians under Imperial law, in the hope of opening negotiations with them.

The Barrens.t: The orcs occupying the Barrens became foreigners under Imperial law, making any invasion of their lands by Imperial troops a criminal offence. By the end of the season they had made no official response.

Declare peace with Lasambrian orcs.d: Proposed by Segura's senator and seconded by Astolat, the motion passed at 110 Thrones, with the funds disbursed to Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra, Senator for Segura. The magistrate ruled that a declaration of peace is absolute because a Senate motion cannot bind a future Senate, so the conditions were for information only; a future Senate could declare war if they went unmet. After the Autumn Equinox the Lasambrian orcs ceded their Seguran regions to the Empire and withdrew into the Lasambrian hills. Dawn's Eastern Sky army then claimed the vacated regions, facing only token resistance from a few orcs who refused to leave and from bandits who had prospered without Imperial law.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Eastern Sky army claimed the regions the Lasambrian orcs vacated for the Empire, overcoming token resistance from holdout orcs and bandits. Astolat, a Dawnish territory, seconded the motion.

The Brass Coast.t: Segura's senator, Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra, proposed the peace and received the funds, and the Brass Coast recovered the Seguran regions the Lasambrian orcs had occupied.

Declare peace with Lasambrian orcs.o: In Autumn 378YE the Senate passed a declaration of peace with the Lasambrian orcs, making them foreigners under Imperial law, on the stated condition that they return the occupied regions of Segura in exchange for 62 wains of Weirwood, Mithril or White Granite.

Segura.t: The Lasambrian orcs handed back the regions of Segura they still held and withdrew into the Lasambrian hills, after which the Eastern Sky reclaimed them for the Empire against scattered orc and bandit resistance.

Declare peace with Orcs of the Great For.d: The motion extended all the legal protections and responsibilities of foreigners to the orcs of the Great Forest of Peytaht. It followed two earlier motions concerning the orcs of the Barrens: the first declared peace, and the second declared war on the orcs of that territory collectively. As a result of this declaration, the orcs of the Great Forest of Peytaht were recognised as foreigners under Imperial law. This distinguished them in law from the other orcs of the Barrens.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the motion concerns the orcs of the Barrens, and the Druj are not named in it, though the earlier declaration of war against the collective orcs of that territory forms the background.

Declare peace with Orcs of the Great For.o: In Summer 380YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Casinea and seconded by Necropolis, granting the orcs of the Great Forest of Peytaht the legal status of foreigners under Imperial law.

The Barrens.t: The motion carved the orcs of the Great Forest of Peytaht out from the collective declaration of war on the orcs of the Barrens, giving them the protections of foreigners under Imperial law.

Declare war on the Barrens orcs.d: Proposed by Weirwater and seconded by Astolat, the motion called war the only virtuous answer to a surprise attack by a foreign nation that had reportedly slain 3000 Imperial citizens in a season and was besieging an Imperial fortification. The motion passed. The Barrens orcs lost the legal protections given to foreigners, though a delegation from them would still be protected as if they were foreigners. The attack on the Towers of Dawn halved the fortification's effective strength from 6000 to 3000. Only about a fifth of that loss was dead soldiers; the rest was damage to the structure.

Dawn.t: The senators for Weirwater and Astolat brought the motion after the Barrens orcs attacked and besieged the Towers of Dawn, halving the fortification's effective strength from 6000 to 3000.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; the motion targets the orcs of the Barrens, a territory the map records as Druj-held that season.

Declare war on the Barrens orcs.o: In Winter 379YE the Senate passed a motion declaring war on the orcs of the Barrens, who had launched a surprise attack and were besieging an Imperial fort, so they were no longer protected by Imperial law as foreigners.

The Barrens.t: The orcs of the Barrens became enemies of the Empire and lost the legal protection given to foreigners, though a delegation from them would still be treated as foreigners under the law.

Decommission Ossium spy network.d: Cayleb of Felix's Watch, the Imperial Spymaster, made an announcement to deconstruct the spy network then active in the Varushkan territory of Ossium. The page lists standard costs for the work, given as 5 thrones, with decommissioning expected to take three months. No progress or outcome is recorded on the page.

Varushka.t: A spy network operating within the Varushkan territory of Ossium was announced for decommissioning, removing that Imperial intelligence presence from Varushkan lands.

Decommission Ossium spy network.o: In Winter 383YE the Imperial Spymaster, Cayleb of Felix's Watch, announced that the spy network operating in Ossium would be decommissioned.

Ossium.t: The spy network active in Ossium was set to be dismantled over three months at a cost of 5 thrones, following the Imperial Spymaster's announcement.

Decommission Verthandi spy network.d: Proposed by the senator for Kallavesi and seconded by Karsk, the motion text calls for decommissioning the Otkodov spy network, while the summary describes it as the Verthandi spy network in Otkodov. It passed at a cost of 5 Thrones, taken directly from the treasury, and takes three months to complete. The network's 2-Throne upkeep was still paid for that season. As a result, the spy network in Verthandi will be rolled up discreetly, and military units can no longer be assigned to it.

Thule.t: The Empire is dismantling its covert network in lands held by Thule, so the Thule-held territories it covered will no longer be watched by it, and Imperial armies can no longer be assigned to it.

Decommission Verthandi spy network.o: In Winter 381YE the Senate passed a motion to decommission the Verthandi spy network, at a cost of five Thrones from the Imperial treasury.

Otkodov.t: The motion text names the network as the Otkodov spy network, and the summary places the Verthandi network in Otkodov. Its decommissioning ends that Imperial espionage presence there.

Verthandi.t: The Imperial spy network in Verthandi, a territory held by Thule, will be rolled up discreetly over three months, and military units can no longer be assigned to it.

Deep blue sea.d: The Grendel withdrew from southern Redoubt with few engagements, sailing from Elos after looting spires, ruining the Tower of Light and Shadow and abducting about two dozen arcane scholars, their families, shipwrights, glassmongers and a lightstone cutter. Elos's harbours reopened, though its lightstone obelisks blaze nightly. The Tempest, the Simoom and five Asavean warships raced to Calvos Sound but missed the Red Wind, which became an army again in Feroz and then anchored offshore without attacking. Feroz remained quiet, with the Children of Wrecks driven out. Conjunctions offered fights against Grendel in the Crucible, Spiral and Oranseri.

Grendel.t: The Salt Lords abandoned their conquests in Redoubt, taking captives and loot, while their Tempest and Simoom navies, with Asavean allies, failed to catch the Red Wind Corsairs and lingered at anchor off Calvos; Grendel companies also feature in three conjunctions.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel and Asavean armada sailed past the shores of Necropolis and the watchers of Reumah's Redoubt without attacking.

Navarr.t: The Black Thorns, under General Cadwell Waystone, joined the push that drove the Grendel out of Redoubt, framing it as ensuring that Therunin would not fall.

The Brass Coast.t: The Red Wind Corsairs evaded the Grendel armada, landed at Oran to celebration and became an army again in Feroz, while the Freeborn of Madruga watched an enemy fleet anchored off Calvos Sound that did not strike.

The League.t: The Wolves of War, led by Jean d'Apulian, helped reclaim Redoubt, and in Spiral the Oblivion Sentinel was given the chance to destroy a Grendel mercenary company and claim its pay.

Urizen.t: Redoubt was returned wholly to Urizen hands with the Argent Sword's help, but its spires were looted, the Tower of Light and Shadow devastated, and dozens of Elos's scholars and craftsfolk carried off by the Grendel.

Wintermark.t: The sacrifice of the Fist of the Mountains was credited with saving Elos from destruction, and its recapture opened an opportunity to raise that army's banner in the port in their honour.

Deep blue sea.o: In Spring 388YE the Black Thorns, Argent Sword and Wolves of War retook Siluri and Naris as the Grendel abandoned Redoubt, carrying off kidnapped Urizen scholars and craftsfolk. Meanwhile a Grendel and Asavean armada descended on Calvos Sound to catch the Red Wind Corsairs, only to find they had already sailed south and landed at Oran in Feroz.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The Iron Confederacy remained in control and impassive, sending civilian ships, perhaps with spies among them, to trade at Feroz ports.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: The Protectorate of Morajasse remained in the west, its orcs keeping apart from the Red Wind amid tension while honouring their agreement to patrol Feroz's shores.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The Red Wind disembarked at Oran to revelry, and the Corsair of Oran was charged with recovering the Brazen Links from the Grendel Silver Runnel anchored near Escambal.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: The armada's intended trap closed on empty water; the fleet then rested at anchor off Calvos, showing interest in the municipal docks under construction but not attacking.

Madruga/Crucible.t: The Drakespawn sought to bring a breeding pair of dire astacids into the Crucible, threatening the Camp of the Sand Crab unless the Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield killed them.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: The armada briefly pushed into the passage off Free Landing, and a dozen pirate vessels from there that harried the fleet were swiftly destroyed.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: The Red Wind sailed south through Lightsea's coastal waters, and the Grendel pursuit faltered in the narrows off its beaches before turning back.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Elos was retaken and its harbours reopened, but it had been stripped of wealth and kidnapped scholars and craftsfolk, and its lightstone obelisks now blaze strangely each night.

Redoubt/Siluri.t: Three Imperial armies swept through Siluri meeting only brief, one-sided clashes as the Grendel retreated, leaving its spires looted.

Spiral/Apulus.t: The Vorlach Adventurers, hired to threaten holdings in Apulus, were broken up by the Black Plateau and left as prey for the Oblivion Sentinel.

Bay of Catazar.t: A combined Grendel and Asavean armada swept through the bay's waters in pursuit of the Red Wind, which deliberately quit the sea to sow doubt in Grendel dominion of the bay.

Feroz.t: The Red Wind Corsairs landed at Oran and became an army again; the Protectorate of Morajasse kept its watch, the Iron Confederacy stayed impassive, the Children of Wrecks were gone, and the Empire retained overall control.

Madruga.t: The Grendel armada arrived in force but, finding the Red Wind gone, anchored offshore without assailing the largely unprotected shores, while a Grendel company sought to camp in the Crucible.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the armada sailed past the shores of Necropolis without turning shoreward.

Redoubt.t: The territory was reclaimed in full as the Grendel withdrew, though its spires were plundered, people kidnapped and the Tower of Light and Shadow ruined, its regio disrupted.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the armada passed through the southern waters of Sarvos, watched by the Chain against Chains, without attacking.

Spiral.t: A Grendel mercenary company hired against Imperial holdings was splintered by the Black Plateau's malignancy, leaving it open to the Oblivion Sentinel.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns' general declared that Therunin would not fall as they marched on the Grendel.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Pilgrim's Defiance left the Redoubt foothills and headed north into Zenith to fight other battles.

Deep forests and dark hills.d: A herald of Estavus offered the secret of a Forge of Hours at the Eternal Shafts of Time, letting the holder buy extra mithril with enchanted tools, available only while Estavus is not under enmity. A storytellers' Inn of the Granite Stag was proposed to let the Granites of Veltsgorsk yield more white granite. Varushkans proposed a Boyar of the Iron Roads, whose five offices would allow one extra ministry commission each season. The boyar of Triosk proposed the Eagle and Stag Exchange and the title of Eagle of Triosk, available until the end of Autumn Equinox 385YE. Northern trade ministries gained extra purchasing, and the Thule began selling mana for money to buy food.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Bonesetter of Torfast Trading Post in Skarsind gained an additional purchase rank on the eastern trade route, letting orc merchants buy more from Varushka.

Navarr.t: The Treji Wayhouse in Hercynia gained an additional ministry, giving Navarr's northern traders the chance to invest in Varushkan goods.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the boyar of Triosk modelled his proposed Eagle of Triosk title on what he had heard of the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills in Kahraman.

The League.t: Temeschwar's Northbound Trade gained an additional ministry for Varushkan goods, and the city's new mana exchange drew more Thule selling mana to the Keeper of the Tome at the expense of other trading partners.

Thule.t: Thule visiting Imperial markets, after negotiations with the Ambassador to Otkodov, began trading their crystal mana for money to buy large amounts of food to send north, with more selling to Temeschwar's new mana exchange.

Varushka.t: Varushka's people enjoyed a surge of trade, Pride and Prosperity, with opportunities to enhance its two Bourse seats, create a Boyar of the Iron Roads and build the Eagle and Stag Exchange in Triosk.

Wintermark.t: The Kalpaheim Tradeholder in Hahnmark gained an additional ministry allowing Wintermark's traders to invest in Varushkan goods.

Deep forests and dark hills.o: Varushka's completed Iron Roads, Autumn magic and a National Assembly statement encouraging internal trade set off a wave of prosperity, opening several commission opportunities in Varushka and boosting trade across the Northern trade network.

Temeschwar/Metri.t: Mentioned in passing: the woods of Metri being safe to travel again helped more traders bring fine metals to the Assayer's Guild.

Volodmartz/Brez.t: An Inn of the Granite Stag for storytellers could be built at Veltsgorsk in the mountains of Brez, appeasing the quarry's dark influence and letting the Granites' holder buy more white granite.

Volodmartz/Livardz.t: Triosk's boyar proposed turning the town's derelict barracks into the Eagle and Stag Exchange, creating the Eagle of Triosk title able to buy metals and upgrade a mine each year.

Volodmartz/Opascari.t: Mentioned in passing: miners and wagon raiders bring metals and minerals from the mountains of Opascari to market in Triosk.

Hahnmark.t: The Kalpaheim Tradeholder ministry here gained an additional ministry to purchase goods from Varushkan merchants.

Hercynia.t: The Treji Wayhouse here gained an additional ministry to purchase goods from Varushkan merchants.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills in Kahraman inspired the proposed Eagle of Triosk title.

Karov.t: A Forge of Hours could be built at the Eternal Shafts of Time to yield extra mithril, and the Custodian of the Assayer's Guild gained an extra ministry track as more traders brought fine metals through Karov.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: Karsk's reclamation from the Thule left Triosk's old frontier barracks derelict and free to be repurposed.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: travellers from Miekarova pass through Triosk, which stands at a crossroads of the eastern vales.

Otkodov.t: The orcs of Otkodov shifted their trade, selling more mana in Temeschwar and seeking money rather than metals to buy food to send north.

Skarsind.t: The Torfast Trading Post here gained an additional purchase rank on the eastern trade route thanks to Varushka's prosperity.

Temeschwar.t: Northbound Trade gained an additional ministry, and the new Temeschwar Mana Exchange drew more Thule mana sellers to the Keeper of the Tome.

Volodmartz.t: Volodmartz was offered an Inn of the Granite Stag at Veltsgorsk to raise white granite output and the Eagle and Stag Exchange at Triosk to make the town a hub of Varushka's mineral trade.

Deep when the river's high.d: About twenty thousand Imperial troops (the Tusks, Strong Reeds, Bounders and Winter Sun) faced roughly thirty thousand Jotun alongside Mathilda Fisher's Yegarra. A cautious Imperial advance into Grey Fens was overwhelmed and pushed back into Ottermire. Despite Night magic, flooded fields and barricades, the Jotun stormed Ottery's western gates and the Imperials retreated south to Sallow in the Rushes. Nearly fifteen hundred Imperial soldiers and well over a thousand Jotun fell. Bregasland became a Jotun territory and Fisher declared herself Steward of Bregasland, though most Bregas rejected her. Imperial heroes could save the Greywaters from Ulfur executioners, and the Imperial Orcs could try to take Oath-Heart from Dillion Fisher.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Winter Sun force-marched from Segura to bolster the Marchers but shared in the defeat and retreat to Sallow. Sinokenon named the Imperial Orcs as exemplars of Loyalty and offered them, through Archmage of Day Gralka, the chance to recover Oath-Heart from Dillion Fisher.

Jotun.t: Jotun armies led by the Mandowla's Roar overwhelmed the Imperials in Grey Fens and Ottermire, stormed Ottery and conquered Bregasland, though they lost well over a thousand warriors. They are now offering the Bregas the Choice in the name of their puppet Steward, Mathilda Fisher.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun's general said their Brass Coast allies must rest as the orcs left Segura to march north.

The Marches.t: The Marches lost Bregasland to the Jotun after the Tusks, Strong Reeds and Bounders were driven out of Grey Fens and Ottermire, leaving many Bregas as thralls, in hiding or as refugees. Some households have sided with Mathilda Fisher, while House Greywater plans to resist.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is not directly named in this account of the Bregasland fighting.

Deep when the river's high.o: In Summer 384YE the Marcher armies and the Imperial Orcs' Winter Sun tried to drive the Jotun out of Bregasland but were beaten back through Grey Fens and defeated at Ottery, losing Ottermire and with it the territory. Two Sentinel Gate conjunctions were also offered: one to protect House Greywater's resistance and one to recover the shield Oath-Heart.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: Gravenmarch stays in Imperial hands, and many displaced Bregas have moved there and been grudgingly taken in.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: The first clash took place among the dead pools of Grey Fens, where the Imperial advance stalled and was driven out. If House Greywater escapes there to wage a guerrilla campaign, Grey Fens will hold allied insurgents working for the Empire.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: The Jotun assault struck south out of North Fens, and a few smaller households there have thrown in their lot with Mathilda Fisher.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: Ottermire saw the decisive Battle of Ottery, where the Jotun smashed the western gates and took the region, turning its protective mists against the Empire. A conjunction to the Greywater estate there offers a chance to stop the Ulfur sent to execute the household.

Bregasland/The Rushes.t: The beaten Imperial armies retreated past Sabbey's Mound to Sallow in the Rushes, which remains Imperial and has taken in Bregas refugees.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland fell to the Jotun when Ottermire was lost, and Mathilda Fisher proclaimed herself its Steward. The Rushes and Gravenmarch remain in Imperial hands and a sizeable Marcher population stays on under occupation.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun broke Ottery's gates with a rune-carved tree trunk apparently carried all the way from Hordalant.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: retreating east to Odd's End and the safety of Mitwold was considered, but the Imperial forces went south instead.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not directly named in this account.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun made its long, enchanted march north from Segura to join the fighting in Bregasland.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold wood shipped along the Otterway was used to build barricades and spikes around Ottery.

Define Jarmish embassy.d: The motion assigned the Jarmish embassy a remote principality to work with, specifically requesting that Jarm construct its embassy to the Empire in Rigia, a port city in the eastern Principalities. The decision was expected to lead the Principalities of Jarm to recognise the Imperial embassy in Cargo, formalising diplomatic ties in both directions. Oswi Twice-Burned was appointed Imperial Ambassador to Jarm at the Autumn Equinox 378YE.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named in the motion; it is linked only through the Imperial embassy in Cargo, which Jarm was expected to recognise.

Define Jarmish embassy.o: In Winter 378YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the Imperial Civil Service, asking the Principalities of Jarm to build their Imperial embassy in the port city of Rigia in the eastern Principalities.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name Redoubt; it is linked through the Imperial embassy in Cargo, which the decision was expected to see Jarm recognise.

Delirium.d: Nearly seventy units, mostly Dawnish and Varushkan, backed by the Varushkan Assembly, Karsk's magistrates and the Ketsov, stormed Isember. Slain outlaws rose as husks under a plaguewulf's curse, so the Sovereign's Heart and its tunnels were burned. The boyar Alexi Iskandrova Isembrioch and the creature remain unaccounted for, but trade along the Iron Roads now flows freely. In Ossium, twenty thousand Druj, including the Black Wind, overwhelmed the Tower of the Scorpion despite Thule help, took the Echofell and were repulsed from the Drownbark Forest. Conjunctions offered chances to defend the Bone Hives, hunt the boyar, confront the horror in the Whispering Glade and rescue captured Navarri.

Dawn.t: Dawnish knights and yeofolk made up most of the forces that destroyed Isember, some sailing in to Ivarsgard, while Dawnish knights helped defend the Tower of the Scorpion and Dawnish prisoners were shot down by the Black Wind.

Druj.t: A Druj host of twenty thousand, including the burning-beetle army, the scorpion banners and the Black Wind, built siege engines, destroyed the Tower of the Scorpion and conquered the Echofell, but failed to break into the Drownbark Forest.

Navarr.t: A Navarr was the first to notice the sickness among the Isember bandits, and two Sunstalker thorns carrying a relic of ancient Emrys were held captive, prompting a rescue opportunity for the Dean of the First Voice Glade.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: scoundrels from Temeschwar were among the outlaws who joined the Isember bandits.

Thule.t: Thule warriors from Flajokep helped defend the Tower of the Scorpion and lost half their number when it fell, then withdrew to the Bonewood, refusing to return unless Imperial armies defend Ossium.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj tactic of destroying hives had already been used ruthlessly in Zenith and elsewhere in Urizen.

Varushka.t: Varushkan warbands, wardens and the Assembly ended the Isember bandit threat, leaving few outlaws in the nation, but Varushkan vales in Ossium suffered heavily as the Druj took the Echofell and the Tower of the Scorpion.

Delirium.o: In Summer 384YE an Imperial raid destroyed the bandit town of Isember in Karsk, uncovering an Elder plaguewulf, while a huge Druj host invaded Ossium, destroyed the Tower of the Scorpion and conquered the Echofell.

Karsk/Kopevnost.t: A bandit raid on Kosti, repelled by chance and Vigilance, triggered the campaign, and captains gathered at Kosti before the assault; Kosti's wise one Valya Sofyn Kosteva advised on confronting the horror in the Whispering Glade.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: Thule warriors from Flajokep emerged from the Bonewood to fight the Druj and later withdrew back into it, vowing to defend only their own lands unless Imperial armies come.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Protected by the Dripping Echoes of the Fen, the vales of the Drownbark Forest decisively turned back the Druj after only minor skirmishes.

Ossium/Echofell.t: The Echofell fell to the Druj, the Tower of the Scorpion was gutted by fire and its garrison slain, the region keeps its under-threat quality, and only places like the Bone Hives still hold out.

Ossium/Galath Fields.t: With Karsk's roads safe, the Galath Fields permanently lost their under-developed quality, and surviving Thule defenders fell back towards the region.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: Mentioned in passing: a Wooden Fastness raised in the heart of Nearweald offered sanctuary to Ossium's defenders.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj invasion force emerged from the Forest of Ulnak into the Echofell.

Karsk.t: Isember was destroyed and its outlaws killed or tried, making trade and travel along Karsk's Iron Roads much easier, though the robber-boyar and the plaguewulf remain at large near the ruins.

Ossium.t: The Druj returned in force, destroying the Tower of the Scorpion and seizing the Echofell, while panic spread among the new vales; the clearing of Karsk did, however, open supply routes for Ossium's settlement.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: some of the Isember bandits were scoundrels from as far afield as Temeschwar.

The Semmerlak.t: Mentioned in passing: some Dawnish forces crossed the Semmerlak by ship to land at Ivarsgard for the raid.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj had previously destroyed hives in Zenith, the strategy they now aim at the Bone Hives.

Desolation of Yoorn.d: The curse lasts around thirty years, steadily reducing births and harvests while leaving the vallorn slothful unless provoked. Liathaven Navarr may move free to Hercynia, Miaren or Therunin. The Jotun are likely to evacuate their thralls, and hungry Feni may raid neighbouring lands. Tharim and Surut offered to take Liathaven if the Senate ceded it, turning it into a cursed wasteland hostile to armies until about 413YE. Heeding Corey Wayfarer's assembly statement, Brocéliande's people will stay until the end of the Autumn Equinox 384YE, then leave if the curse remains. Lifting it would need a vast Spring working, and a proposed Navarr mandate could reveal ways to do it.

Jotun.t: The Jotun will likely see the curse as an attack on their thralls and evacuate them from Liathaven, though warriors seeking glory may stay. A Court-blighted Liathaven would make it far harder for their armies to reach the Mournwold.

Navarr.t: Navarr families in Liathaven and Brocéliande face a choice between their homes and their descendants' future. Their assembly urged them to stay, and a proposed mandate could rally the nation to find magic to lift the curse from Brocéliande.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the civil service suggest that famished Feni might even raid as far as Kahraman.

The Marches.t: Marcher lands in the southern Mournwold and Bregasland face anticipated Feni raids as the curse starves the forest folk. A blighted Liathaven would also deter Jotun armies from reaching the Mournwold.

Desolation of Yoorn.o: Wither the Seed, a potent Winter curse cast by Navarr magicians on Liathaven and Brocéliande, began sapping the fertility of both territories while lulling the vallorn into quiescence. This forced hard choices on those who lived there and drew an offer from the Thrice-cursed Court to take Liathaven.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Mentioned in passing: Boar's Dell is named as one of the two regions where most of Brocéliande's Navarr live under the curse.

Brocéliande/Dark Ranging.t: The chance to free Dark Ranging from the vallorn is why Brocéliande's people will endure the curse until the end of the Autumn Equinox 384YE.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Mentioned in passing: Elerael is named alongside Boar's Dell as home to most of Brocéliande's Navarr.

Brocéliande/Terunael.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named directly, appearing only as part of cursed Brocéliande and through references to the Heirs of Terunael.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: West Ranging would be among the first regions given to the Thrice-cursed Court if ceded. The Court would allow the Empire to harvest its newly found weirwood grove, but at significantly higher cost.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: Westwood is one of the two regions where the Thrice-cursed Court's malicious influence would initially be confined if the Senate cedes them.

Bregasland.t: The civil service anticipate Feni raids into Bregasland as the curse leaves the Feni short of food.

Brocéliande.t: The territory now lies under Wither the Seed. Its people will stay until the end of the Autumn Equinox 384YE to give Dark Ranging a chance to be freed, but a steady exodus will begin if the curse is not lifted.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia is one of the territories Liathaven Navarr may move to without the usual fee, keeping their resource upgrades if they move before the end of the Winter Solstice 383YE.

Liathaven.t: The already depopulated territory is cursed for some thirty years and would remain a drain on the treasury even if reconquered. The Thrice-cursed Court have offered to take it and turn it into a cursed wasteland if the Senate cedes it.

Miaren.t: Miaren, freed from the vallorn under Emperor Giovanni using this same curse, is now a fee-free destination for Navarr leaving Liathaven.

Mournwold.t: The southern Mournwold may suffer Feni raids, while a Court-blighted Liathaven would make it much harder for Jotun armies to reach the Mournwold.

Therunin.t: Therunin is one of the territories Liathaven Navarr may move to without the usual fee, with help to keep their resource upgrades if they move before the end of the Winter Solstice 383YE.

Desperate affairs, desperate measures.d: Slightly more than thirty Imperial captains guarded the fisherfolk exploiting a boom in marine life. Each protecting fleet earned an extra 3 Crowns, trade rose in several territories, and the Broken Shore Bounty will yield 2 extra rings of ilium a season for a year. Fifty fleets, thirty of them Freeborn, broke the blockade of Zemress and carried its people and livestock to Joharra. The islanders' leader, Dhomiro Tevus i Zemress, burned the village behind them. The Grendel pirates withdrew in disarray. The Islanders, who are Freeborn but distinct, wished to settle together. Feroz, Madruga, Segura and Kahraman were all weighed, and a statement upheld with a greater majority chose Segura.

Grendel.t: Grendel pirates and slavers were beaten off at both the fishing grounds and Zemress, and their independent captains withdrew in disarray. They remain a threat to individual ships, but no longer act in concert.

Highguard.t: Highborn captains joined the fishing-fleet defence and the Zemress evacuation, and trade in Necropolis increased as a result.

Imperial Orcs.t: An Imperial Orc fleet captained by Gish was among the scattering of non-Freeborn ships that helped rescue the Zemress Islanders.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Islanders were suggested as a possible bulwark should the Jotun come down from Liathaven or Lasambria again.

Navarr.t: More than half a dozen Navarr fleets supported the Zemress evacuation, and many Navarr captains took part in the campaign against the pirates.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn led the campaign, providing thirty ships for the Zemress raid, and gained several thousand kin who settled first in Feroz and Madruga. Their Assembly directed the Islanders to Segura.

The League.t: League captains from Sarvos joined the action, and trade in Sarvos and Tassato increased thanks to the protected fishing fleet.

Urizen.t: Urizen fleets, including that of Natalus, took part in the operations, and trade in Redoubt rose as a result.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark captains such as Pendraed the Maker, Drothdir and Kapik joined the Imperial fleets that defied the Grendel and rescued the Islanders.

Desperate affairs, desperate measures.o: In Autumn 381YE, Imperial captains led by the Freeborn defeated a surge of Grendel pirate raids in the Bay of Catazar. They protected the fishing fleet without losing a single boat and evacuated the several thousand people of the Isle of Zemress. The Freeborn Assembly then encouraged the Zemress Islanders to settle in Segura.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: Morajasse was suggested as a place where settling Islanders could aid the herb-growing apothecaries, though Segura was chosen instead.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Oranseri was flagged as somewhere to keep the Islanders away from, given how the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull might react to their worship.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: Braydon's Jasse was proposed as a defensive settlement site in the shadow of Fort Braydon on the Marches border. The option was not taken up.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: The Jade Range was suggested as rich grazing ground where Islander ranchers could ease Kahraman's dependence on imported food. Segura was chosen instead.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: Zemress herself was born in Calvos, and the Kraken's Bane rests on its dock, a touchstone the Islanders will likely want to visit.

Segura/Lucksprings.t: Mentioned in passing: not named on the page, but it lies in Segura, where the Assembly encouraged the Islanders to settle.

Segura/Sobral Grasses.t: The Sobral Grasses were suggested as a place for the Islanders to raise herds and establish farms within their chosen territory of Segura.

Segura/Yellow Chase.t: Yellow Chase was named as a possible site for Islander herds and farms that could raise the prosperity of Segura.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Empire's fleets kept the fishing grounds safe and drove the organised Grendel pirate fleet out of these waters, though lone raiders remain a danger.

Feroz.t: Trade increased here thanks to the protected fishing fleet, and many rescued Islanders arrived here. Feroz was considered as their permanent home but not chosen.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman was considered as a home for the Islanders, with its mines and grazing land, but the Assembly chose Segura instead.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a place from which the Jotun might again descend on Kahraman.

Madruga.t: Madruga saw increased trade and received many of the rescued Islanders. It was weighed as a permanent home but passed over in favour of Segura.

Necropolis.t: Necropolis enjoyed a significant increase in trade as a result of the successful defence of the fishing fleet.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt saw a significant rise in trade thanks to the fishing fleet's safe harvest.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos benefited from a significant increase in trade following the protection of the fishing fleet.

Segura.t: The Freeborn Assembly encouraged the several thousand Zemress Islanders to settle in Segura. Their hard work may help revitalise a territory still recovering from conquest and strengthen its defence.

Tassato.t: Tassato enjoyed a significant increase in trade from the safeguarded fishing fleet.

Despise treachery.d: Acting on Senator Lizzie Stamp's motion, the magistrates searched every household in Bregasland. House Brawness resisted arrest and was executed for treason. The Droverbill Clan were only fined for handling stolen goods. Three dozen Clakes were executed, but Sammy Clake escaped to Sallow with a five-throne bounty on his head. More than a score of other traitors were executed and dozens fined. House Greywater, unrewarded for opposing the Fishers, grew bitter. The North Fens became rebellious, the Grey Fens sullen and the Rushes resentful. The Assembly of Loyalty faced a choice over recognising Bushel Sykes. The Jotun carried the dying Mathilda Fisher to the Wintermark camp, and she asked to be buried at Fisher's Rock.

Jotun.t: Jotun warriors kept their word after losing the battle of champions and bore Mathilda Fisher, whom they honour as a jarl, to Anvil under a flag of truce. They intend to witness how the Empire treats her death and burial, and to report it to the other jarls.

The Marches.t: The Marcher Assembly backed the magistrates' purge of Bregasland and recognised Bushel Sykes' Loyalty. Many Bregas Marchers were executed or fined, and lasting grudges now fester among Marcher households.

Wintermark.t: Iron Osric was asked to supply an honour guard of Wintermark warriors to escort the dying Mathilda Fisher. The Jotun will deliver her into the Wintermark camp at Anvil, where Jarl Igya has asked that she be allowed to die with honour.

Despise treachery.o: Following a Senate motion, the magistrates swept through Bregasland and punished those who had collaborated with Mathilda Fisher and the Jotun. Order was restored, but the purge left deep grudges across several regions, while the mortally wounded Fisher Queen was carried to Anvil to meet her fate.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: Mentioned in passing: Gravenmarch is noted as home to many Marchers who remain loyal to the Empire.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: The Droverbill Clan escaped with heavy fines for profiteering and handling stolen goods. Anger that they got off lightly has left the region sullen, which would raise army upkeep costs if the mood spreads.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: House Brawness was all but destroyed after battling the magistrates, leaving the region rebellious. The unrewarded House Greywater has also made it embittered.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: Bushel Sykes, who died at the Wet Dog tavern in Ottery, came from here. If the Assembly of Loyalty recognises his Virtue, the North Fens' rebellious mood will spread to Ottermire.

Bregasland/The Rushes.t: Three dozen Clakes of Beandown were executed and others fined into poverty, while Sammy Clake went to ground in Sallow. The region is now resentful and hungry for payback.

Bregasland.t: Magistrates searched every farm and settlement, executing and fining collaborators. The territory is stable for now but scarred by sullen, resentful, embittered and rebellious regions. Burying Fisher there would leave the whole territory embittered.

Fjorknae.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun had threatened to spirit Mathilda Fisher away to Fjorknae had the Empire lost the battle of champions.

Tromsa.t: The Empire's invasion of Tromsa led to Fisher's mortal wounding at the Battle of Viheltavathorn and her surrender after a battle of champions at Oksenesfestsal. Returning her body to Tromsa for burial is one option being weighed.

Diadem on my brow.d: Using the Throne's power to address the Empire, Emperor Vesna recalled their promise that the Empire would choose where it fights. They credited the drive for militarisation, which mustered six armies in a year and a half, with making victory possible. The Emperor declared their will to destroy the Druj Empire, conquer its land and liberate its septs. They warned that this would demand hard choices, and pledged that the push east would not leave Imperial homes such as Bregasland or Therunin undefended. The address commended Jaromir Ostrovyn Kostka, the Order of the Golden Pyramid, Vauraus Korppitkotka and several investors in the Imperial budget, and Llewellyn Leafstalker.

Druj.t: The Druj were the explicit target of the address, which called for the destruction of their empire, the conquest of their land and the liberation of their septs.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, but the Emperor cited Bregasland, which they held at the time, as an Imperial home that would not be forgotten.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr are not named, though their territory of Therunin was cited as an Imperial home that would not go undefended.

Diadem on my brow.o: In Autumn 387YE Emperor Vesna addressed every citizen of the Empire, declaring that the time had come to destroy the Druj and conquer their lands. The Emperor called on all citizens to stand with them through the sacrifices ahead.

Bregasland.t: The Emperor named Bregasland, then held by the Jotun, as an Imperial home that would not be forgotten during the push against the Druj.

Therunin.t: The Emperor named Therunin among the Imperial homes in the west and south that would not be left undefended while the Empire turned east.

Digging for fire.d: Dozens of Golden Pyramid magicians explored Mareave, a land few Imperial citizens had seen except as slaves. In Nadir they found a shifting regio among Urizen ruins, holding two bronze bowls that produce three vis each season. Dubbed the Bronze Bowls of the Three Seasons, this sinecure could be set up by the Senate as an Imperial or Imperial Orcs position. Imperial Orcs running mines in Mareave now earn 30 extra rings a season. The Grandmaster could commit the order to stay a year for ingots, mana and cerulean mazzarine each season. The order also proposed a Grand Lodge in Clisearn, which the Senate would need to approve.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Mareave is described as lying on the frontier with the Grendel, one reason it is suggested for a Golden Pyramid grand lodge.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orcs who run mines in Mareave gain 30 extra rings each season. The Bronze Bowls could become a national Imperial Orcs position, and the Golden Pyramid could commit to exploring Mareave alongside them for a year.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: trade through Beoraidh might open access to luxuries from Madruga.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: League magicians were among those who surveyed Mareave's mines, and Beoraidh's trade might reach Sarvos.

Urizen.t: Old Urizen spires in Icarion and Nadir drew Golden Pyramid explorers, and one ruined spire in Nadir held the Bronze Bowls of the Three Seasons, decorated with astronomantic sigils.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction follows two Wintermark prospectors who earned more in Mareave than a month's work in Hahnmark would bring.

Digging for fire.o: After the Conclave asked the Order of the Golden Pyramid to explore Mareave, its magicians found a newly discovered minor wonder in Nadir, rich mines in the northern hills, and the chance to stay on in the territory or build a grand lodge there.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Golden Pyramid magicians held trade talks with the folk of Beoraidh, a neutral city-state whose trade across the bay could bring luxuries from Madruga, Sarvos and beyond if negotiations go well.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: Clisearn's Fundindelve already yields mithril, and the order proposed a Grand Lodge on estates in Clisearn, between Beoraidh and the Fundindelve, costing 20 white granite, 20 mithril and 15 thrones.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Most of Mareave's Urizen ruins stand in Icarion's foothills, and Golden Pyramid magicians explored them with paid local orc guides.

Mareave/Nadir.t: High in Nadir's hills, magicians found a ruined spire holding a shifting regio and the Bronze Bowls of the Three Seasons. The bowls produce three pawns of prismatic ink, vital honey or heart's blood depending on the season, awaiting a Senate decision on who receives them.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the fiction's prospectors compare their Mareave profits with what they would earn in Hahnmark.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Beoraidh's trade across the bay could give access to luxuries from Madruga.

Mareave.t: Mareave proved rich in ores and all four magic metals. Its mines now pay Imperial Orc operators 30 extra rings a season, a vis-producing minor wonder was found there, and the Golden Pyramid may stay on or build a grand lodge in the territory.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Beoraidh's trade across the bay could give access to luxuries from Sarvos.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: unlike Skarsind, Mareave was terra incognita to most Imperial citizens.

Disburse funds for Astolat ministry.d: The senator for Astolat proposed a motion requesting funds for a mana ministry in Astolat, and the senator for Weirwater seconded it. The motion passed, and the disbursement was approved at a cost of 40 Thrones. The page gives no further detail about the ministry itself, its location within Astolat or how it would be run.

Dawn.t: Dawnish senators for Astolat and Weirwater proposed and seconded the motion, securing Imperial funds for a mana ministry in one of Dawn's own territories.

Disburse funds for Astolat ministry.o: In Autumn 381YE the Senate passed a motion requesting funds for a mana ministry in Astolat, with the expenditure approved at 40 Thrones.

Astolat.t: Astolat's senator successfully sought 40 Thrones for a mana ministry to be established in the territory.

Disburse funds for Farstrider's Watch Sp.d: The Senator for Mournwold proposed the motion and Upwold seconded it. It released Senate funds set aside for building the fort named Farstrider's Watch in the Greensward region of the Mournwold. It passed at 80 Thrones, and the money was disbursed to the Senator for Mournwold to buy the materials needed for construction. The page records the release of the funds only. It does not say whether the fortification was finished.

The Marches.t: Marcher senators drove the motion, with Mournwold proposing and Upwold seconding. Its passage put Senate money in Marcher hands to fortify a territory they had reclaimed.

Disburse funds for Farstrider's Watch Sp.o: In Spring 382YE the Senate passed a motion to disburse 80 Thrones of Senate funds to pay for materials to build Farstrider's Watch, a fortification on the Greensward in the Mournwold.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: The Greensward is the planned site of Farstrider's Watch, and the materials paid for by this motion are meant for its construction there.

Mournwold.t: The Senator for Mournwold received the disbursed funds to buy materials for a new fortification within the territory.

Disburse funds for Iron Helms III.d: The motion sought Senate funds to finish raising the Iron Helms army, which the Senate had commissioned in Autumn 379YE. It was the third such funding motion, following two earlier ones. Proposed by the senator for Karsk and seconded by Hahnmark, it passed in principle and was approved at 200 thrones. The 200 thrones were then disbursed to the senator for Karsk to put towards the army's completion.

Varushka.t: Varushka moved closer to fielding a new army, the Iron Helms, as 200 thrones went to its senator for Karsk to help complete it.

Disburse funds for Iron Helms III.o: In Summer 380YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Karsk and seconded by Hahnmark, to disburse 200 thrones towards completing the Iron Helms army in Karsk, Varushka.

Karsk.t: The Iron Helms army was being raised in Karsk, and the territory's senator proposed the motion and received the 200 thrones disbursed to complete it.

Disburse funds for Pilgrim's Trail.d: Proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by the senator for Redoubt, this motion followed an earlier motion that had commissioned the Pilgrim's Trail as a great work. It sought additional funds of 18 Thrones to purchase the resources needed for construction of the pilgrim trails in Kallavesa. The motion was passed in principle and then passed at 18 Thrones, and the money was disbursed to the senator for Kallavesa.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's senator for Kallavesa secured 18 Thrones from the Imperial treasury to help build the Pilgrim's Trail in Wintermark lands.

Disburse funds for Pilgrim's Trail.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate passed a motion disbursing 18 Thrones to purchase resources for constructing the Pilgrim's Trail great work in Kallavesa.

Kallavesa.t: The 18 Thrones were disbursed to Kallavesa's senator to buy the resources needed to construct the pilgrim trails in the territory.

Disburse funds for Summer college.d: Proposed by the senator for Miekarova and seconded by Karsk, the motion asked for 100 Thrones to buy materials for the ongoing construction of a Summer college. The motion itself said it did not matter whether the college was in Urizen or Navarr. The page notes that the Senate had already commissioned two such colleges, one in Morrow and one in Miekarova. The motion passed at a cost of 100 Thrones, and the money was disbursed to the senator for Miekarova.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the motion named Navarr as one of two possible locations for the Summer college, saying the choice did not matter.

Urizen.t: Urizen was named in the motion as a possible home for the Summer college, and its territory of Morrow was the site of one of the two colleges the Senate had commissioned.

Varushka.t: Varushkan senators drove the motion: Miekarova proposed it and Karsk seconded it, and the 100 Thrones went to the Miekarova senator for a college the Senate had commissioned in Miekarova.

Disburse funds for Summer college.o: The Senate passed a motion in Summer 379YE disbursing 100 Thrones towards the continued construction of a College of Magic focused on Summer rituals.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova's senator proposed the motion and received the 100 Thrones, and the territory was the site of one of the two Summer colleges the Senate had commissioned.

Morrow.t: Morrow was the site of one of the two Summer colleges the Senate had commissioned, though the funds from this motion went to the senator for Miekarova.

Disburse funds for The Towerjacks.d: Proposed by Holberg and seconded by Sarvos, the motion requested additional Senate funds towards the commission of The Towerjacks, an army of the League. It passed in principle at a sum of 350 thrones, and that amount was disbursed to Senator Holberg to continue the construction work.

The League.t: The League's planned new army, The Towerjacks, received 350 thrones of Senate funding towards its continued construction.

Disburse funds for The Towerjacks.o: In Autumn 379YE the Senate passed, in principle, a motion to disburse 350 thrones to the Senator for Holberg to continue building the Towerjacks, a League army.

Holberg.t: Holberg's senator proposed the motion and received the 350 thrones to carry on building The Towerjacks.

Disburse funds for mithril research.d: Proposed by the senator for Redoubt and seconded by Astolat, the motion asked for 34 thrones towards research by the Provost of the Halls of Knowledge into raising mithril output in Redoubt, plus a further 10 thrones to make the results part of Imperial Lore. It passed unanimously in principle and at 34 thrones (27 to 0), but failed at 44 thrones (10 to 17). The funds were disbursed to Senator Redoubt. Preliminary research found that ritual magic cannot be used to improve the production of mithril, white granite, weirwood or ilium.

Urizen.t: Urizen's senator for Redoubt proposed and received funding to research boosting the nation's mithril production, but the research concluded that ritual magic cannot improve it.

Disburse funds for mithril research.o: In Winter 377YE the Senate passed a motion to fund research by the Provost of the Halls of Knowledge into increasing mithril production in Redoubt, approving 34 thrones but rejecting the extra 10 thrones to place the findings in Imperial Lore.

Redoubt.t: The research aimed to increase mithril production in Redoubt, but preliminary findings showed that ritual magic cannot raise the territory's mithril output.

Disburse funds for rebuilding of Holmaue.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by the senator for Karov, sought funds for the rebuilding of the Holmauer in Holberg. It followed on from a previous motion to construct a park in Holmauer. The Senate passed it in principle and set the sum at 100 thrones. That money was then disbursed to the senator for Holberg.

The League.t: Holberg's senator, representing a League territory, proposed the motion and received the 100 thrones the Senate granted for rebuilding in Holmauer.

Disburse funds for rebuilding of Holmaue.o: In Autumn 380YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Holberg and seconded by Karov, to disburse funds for rebuilding the Holmauer, following an earlier motion to construct a park there. It passed at 100 thrones.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Holmauer was the subject of the motion, receiving 100 thrones for rebuilding, following an earlier motion to build a park there.

Holberg.t: Holberg's senator proposed the motion and was given 100 thrones for rebuilding works in the territory's Holmauer region.

Disburse funds for rebuilding of Holmaue.d: The motion followed an earlier motion to disburse funds, which had itself come after a motion to construct a great work in Holberg. Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by the senator for Tassato, it called for funds to be released for the rebuilding of Holberg. It passed at 75 thrones, and that sum was disbursed to the senator for Holberg.

The League.t: League senators for Holberg and Tassato proposed and seconded the motion, securing 75 thrones from the Imperial treasury for a League territory.

Disburse funds for rebuilding of Holmaue.o: In Winter 380YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Holberg's senator and seconded by Tassato's, to disburse 75 thrones for the rebuilding of Holmauer in Holberg.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Holmauer was the focus of the rebuilding effort that the 75 thrones were released to fund.

Holberg.t: The senator for Holberg received 75 thrones towards rebuilding in the territory, continuing an earlier great work effort there.

Disburse funds for resupply III.d: The motion sought Senate money for the resupply of the Imperial armies and was put forward by the senator for Bregasland, with Mitwold seconding. It passed in principle and was set at 250 thrones, which were disbursed to Senator Bregasland. The page notes that the motion did not give the senator the power to carry out emergency resupply of the armies themselves, so the funds were handed over without that authority attached.

The Marches.t: Two Marcher senators, from Bregasland and Mitwold, proposed and seconded the motion, and 250 thrones of Senate money went into the hands of the Marches' senator for Bregasland.

Disburse funds for resupply III.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Bregasland and seconded by Mitwold, to disburse 250 thrones of Senate funds intended to resupply the Imperial armies.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland's senator proposed the motion and received the 250 thrones disbursed for resupplying the armies, though without power to perform emergency resupply.

Disburse funds for resupply IV.d: The motion proposed disbursing funds to resupply the Imperial armies. It was proposed by Feroz and seconded by Kahraman, and passed in principle at a cost of 115 thrones 4 crowns, which was disbursed to Senator Feroz. The page notes that the motion did not give Senator Feroz the power to perform emergency resupply on the armies. It only provided the funds.

The Brass Coast.t: Two Brass Coast senators, those for Feroz and Kahraman, proposed and seconded the motion, and its 115 thrones 4 crowns went to the Feroz senator.

Disburse funds for resupply IV.o: In Autumn 380YE the Senate passed in principle a motion, proposed by the senator for Feroz and seconded by the senator for Kahraman, to disburse funds for resupplying the Imperial armies. It was passed at 115 thrones 4 crowns.

Feroz.t: The senator for Feroz proposed the motion and received the 115 thrones 4 crowns disbursed for resupplying the armies, though without any power to carry out emergency resupply.

Disburse funds for strategic rituals.d: In Spring 378YE the Senator for Redoubt raised a motion, seconded by Madruga, to disburse funds for casting strategic rituals on armies. 25 Thrones were disbursed to Probus, Senator for Redoubt. In Autumn 378YE Morrow proposed a similar motion, seconded by Sarvos, to fund the purchase of mana for strategic military purposes. It passed in principle at 95 Thrones, which were disbursed to Ariadne of the Auric Horizon, Proxy Senator for Morrow. Both motions intended the money to buy crystal mana for rituals that would benefit the Empire and the Imperial armies on a strategic level.

Urizen.t: Urizen's senators for Redoubt and Morrow sponsored both motions and received all 120 Thrones, placing responsibility for buying mana for the Empire's strategic rituals in Urizen hands.

Disburse funds for strategic rituals.o: The Senate disbursed Imperial funds to Urizen senators so that crystal mana could be bought for strategic rituals benefiting the Empire and its armies. Redoubt received 25 Thrones in Spring 378YE and Morrow 95 Thrones in Autumn 378YE.

Morrow.t: Morrow proposed the Autumn 378YE motion, and its Proxy Senator, Ariadne of the Auric Horizon, received 95 Thrones to buy mana for strategic military rituals.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt raised the Spring 378YE motion, and its Senator, Probus, received 25 Thrones to fund strategic rituals cast on Imperial armies.

Disburse funds to Bregasland.d: Proposed by Bregasland and seconded by Mitwold, the Summer 378YE motion distributed funds to Bregasland with the intention of resupplying the armies, with the Quartermaster General called as an expert witness. The page records 200 Thrones disbursed to Orrick, Senator for Bregasland, that season. In Autumn 378YE a similar motion, proposed by Bregasland and seconded by Hahnmark, sought funds to resupply the Imperial armies either through future motions or the Imperial Quartermaster, and 400 Thrones were disbursed to Orrick.

The Marches.t: A Marcher senator, Orrick of Bregasland, received Imperial funds entrusted to him for resupplying the Empire's armies.

Disburse funds to Bregasland.o: In Summer 378YE the Senate passed a motion disbursing 200 Thrones to Orrick, Senator for Bregasland, to be used to resupply the Imperial armies; a further 400 Thrones followed in Autumn 378YE.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland's senator Orrick proposed the motion and was given 200 Thrones in Summer and 400 Thrones in Autumn 378YE to put towards resupplying the Imperial armies.

Disburse funds to Grendel raiders.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by the senator for Morrow, the motion responded to demands the Grendel made before the Autumn Equinox. It proposed paying the Grendel in return for their promise not to invade or sack Imperial territories bordering the Bay of Catazar for the season. The motion passed with the sum set at 300 thrones, and the money was disbursed to the senator for Holberg to deliver.

Grendel.t: The Grendel's demands were met with a payment of 300 thrones, given in return for their promise not to invade or sack Imperial territories on the Bay of Catazar this season.

Disburse funds to Grendel raiders.o: In Autumn 382YE the Senate passed a motion to pay the Grendel 300 thrones so that they would not invade or sack any Imperial territories on the Bay of Catazar that season.

Bay of Catazar.t: The payment was meant to secure the Imperial territories around the Bay against Grendel invasion or sacking for the season.
