Disburse funds to Miekarova militia.d: Proposed by the Senator for Miekarova and seconded by the Senator for Volodmartz, the motion sought funds to deal with anarchy cultists causing disruption in Miekarova. It passed at 26 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Miekarova to pay for the militia. The disruption had been hampering military units based in the territory, reducing their effectiveness when raiding or when assisting Imperial armies. The 26 thrones were enough only to partially mitigate this, lessening but not removing the penalty to those units.

Varushka.t: Varushkan senators led the effort to fund action against the anarchy cultists, and Varushkan military units based in Miekarova saw their hampered effectiveness partially restored.

Disburse funds to Miekarova militia.o: In Winter 378YE the Senate passed a motion granting 26 thrones to fund a militia in Miekarova to crush the anarchy cultists troubling the territory.

Miekarova.t: A militia funded with 26 thrones was raised to crush the anarchy cultists in Miekarova, partially easing the disruption to military units based there without ending it.

Disburse funds to Thanmir Hrafn.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by the senator for Redoubt, followed an earlier motion authorising the construction of cargo docks in Cargo, Redoubt. It sought funds for Thanmir Hrafn to purchase the materials needed to build docks for trade with the Sarcophan Delves. The motion passed at 100 thrones, and the money was recorded as disbursed to the senator for Necropolis.

Urizen.t: Urizen's senators for Necropolis and Redoubt secured 100 thrones of Imperial funds to advance the planned cargo docks for trade with the Sarcophan Delves.

Disburse funds to Thanmir Hrafn.o: In Spring 381YE the Senate passed a motion disbursing 100 thrones to Thanmir Hrafn to buy materials for building cargo docks to trade with the Sarcophan Delves.

Redoubt.t: The 100 thrones were meant to buy materials for the cargo docks authorised in Cargo, Redoubt, and Redoubt's senator seconded the motion.

Disburse funds to aid Liathaven citizens.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by the senator for Therunin, asked the Senate to send an aid package to Liathaven. It passed at 10 thrones in Autumn 378YE, and the funds were disbursed to Uskolli, Senator for Kallavesa. Geraint Broad-Backed made a further contribution to the project through the civil service: 4 thrones, 7 crowns, 16 rings and 5 measures of ambergelt. The page does not record how the aid was used or what came of it.

Navarr.t: Senators from two Navarr territories, Kallavesa and Therunin, led the effort, and the Kallavesa senator Uskolli received the money to aid the people of Liathaven.

Disburse funds to aid Liathaven citizens.o: In Autumn 378YE the Senate passed a request for funds to send an aid package to Liathaven, proposed by Kallavesa and seconded by Therunin, with 10 thrones approved.

Liathaven.t: Liathaven was the intended recipient of the aid package, meant to help its citizens, with 10 thrones of Senate money plus Geraint Broad-Backed's private donation behind it.

Disburse funds to citizens of Skarsind.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by the senator for Karov, the motion followed a previous motion to relinquish Skarsind. It was passed in principle, with the amount set at 10 thrones. Those 10 thrones were disbursed to the senator for Sermersuaq, ostensibly to ensure the continued Prosperity of the Wintermark citizens affected when Skarsind was given up.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are not named, though the motion concerns the Wintermarkers affected by the gifting of Skarsind, the territory they held that season.

Disburse funds to citizens of Skarsind.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate passed a motion to allocate funds to the Wintermarkers affected by the gifting of Skarsind, recognising their Loyalty, Pride and Prosperity.

Skarsind.t: The Senate allocated 10 thrones, paid to the senator for Sermersuaq, to support the Wintermark citizens affected by the gifting of Skarsind.

Disburse funds to the Jarmish Cartel.d: Proposed by Segura and seconded by Kahraman, the motion asked the Senate to approve the Jarmish Cartel. The cartel sought to trade exclusively with the new port of Eastern Jarm. In return it would virtuously release its slaves held in contract within one year. The motion requested 50 thrones to cover the agreement with Eastern Jarm, but it passed at 35 thrones, which were disbursed to Senator Segura. The port in question was Rigia, which had recently opened to the Empire after the completion of the Jarmish Embassy in Cargo.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name Urizen directly; its link appears to come through the senators who proposed and seconded the motion.

Disburse funds to the Jarmish Cartel.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate passed a motion approving the Jarmish Cartel and disbursing funds to it. The cartel sought exclusive trade with the newly opened eastern Jarmish port in return for releasing its contracted slaves within a year.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the page does not refer to Redoubt directly; its connection is presumably through the senators involved in the motion.

Disbursement of funds for College of Eng.d: Proposed by the Senator for Tassato and seconded by the Senator for Redoubt, the motion sought a disbursal of funds to finish building the Adamant College in Temeschwar. It followed a previous motion to disburse funds for the College of Engineering and Architecture. The motion passed at 120 thrones, and that sum was disbursed to the Senator for Tassato to complete the work.

The League.t: League senators for Tassato and Redoubt jointly secured 120 thrones from the Imperial treasury to finish the Adamant College on League soil.

Disbursement of funds for College of Eng.o: The Senate passed a motion to disburse funds to complete construction of the Adamant College, the College of Engineering and Architecture, in Temeschwar, following an earlier disbursement motion for the same project.

Temeschwar.t: The 120 thrones were granted to complete construction of the Adamant College in Temeschwar, the territory's College of Engineering and Architecture.

Disloyal, unprosperous, unvigilant, unwi.d: The Private Auction had long caused debate, but opinion had generally favoured the status quo until four citizens were excommunicated for buying an item from it. Friar Alyn of Hay then travelled widely, preaching Prosperity and distributing pamphlets. He argued that the Synod's judgements calling citizens 'disloyal, unprosperous, unvigilant and unwise' were themselves unvirtuous, and that people should keep their artefacts or sell them personally. He claimed to have spoken to people in Astolat, Bastion, Skarsind and Meade, and drew enthusiastic crowds of corsairs in Siroc. Preliminary reports showed far fewer items offered for the Private Auction. Having finished his pilgrimage, Alyn announced he was coming to Anvil to address the Synod, chiefly the National Assembly of the Marches and the Assembly of Prosperity.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the friar claimed to have spoken to the seneschals of Astolat during his tour.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the friar claimed to have spoken to the benefactors of Bastion, and compared the Printer's Guild museum to something that would impress a Highborn archivist.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the friar claimed to have spoken to the bonesetters of Skarsind.

The Marches.t: The campaign came from a Marcher friar of Hay, who also claimed to have spoken to the stewards of Meade. He announced he would come to Anvil to address the National Assembly of the Marches in particular, alongside the Assembly of Prosperity.

Disloyal, unprosperous, unvigilant, unwi.o: In Autumn 380YE Friar Alyn of Hay, Mitwold, toured the Empire urging citizens not to sell their treasures to Imperial Bourse agents for the Private Auction, after the Synod's excommunication of four citizens over a Private Auction purchase. Early reports showed the Private Auction's prospectus significantly reduced.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the friar listed the seneschals of Astolat among those he had spoken to.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the friar listed the benefactors of Bastion among those he had spoken to.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold's town of Hay was home to Friar Alyn, whose preaching against selling treasures to the Bourse cut the Private Auction's prospectus.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the friar listed the bonesetters of Skarsind among those he had spoken to.

Dispatch prospectors to the Pride of Ikk.d: Proposed by the senator for Hahnmark and seconded by Kallavesa, the motion described itself as self-funded, but the costs actually fell to the Senate: 10 Thrones. Hengest Dun donated 10 Thrones to the treasury to cover it. The prospectors returned shortly after the Summer Solstice 382YE and confirmed that the workings could be expanded significantly, though not cheaply. The Senate could commission the expansion for 400 Thrones; the work would take six months, after which the mine's output would rise from 15 to 20 wains of mithril each season.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's senators for Hahnmark and Kallavesa proposed and seconded the motion, which established that a Winterfolk mithril mine could be enlarged if the Senate funded a 400-Throne expansion.

Dispatch prospectors to the Pride of Ikk.o: In Spring 382YE the Senate passed a motion to send prospectors to the Pride of Ikka's Tears, the mithril mine in Sermersuaq, to explore whether it could be expanded.

Sermersuaq.t: Prospectors surveyed the Pride of Ikka's Tears in Sermersuaq and found that its mithril output could be raised from 15 to 20 wains a season through a six-month, 400-Throne expansion.

Disseminate True Liao visions.d: Proposed by Redoubt and seconded by Madruga on the Spider's Vantage Spire's suggestion, the motion led the Civil Service to distribute Echoes of the Labyrinth abroad. Asavean interest centred on a vision about a Coriolani martyr. Followers of the Way in Jarm, the Commonwealth and the Sarcophan Delves embraced the books, blunting Sumaah missionaries for a time. The Faraden found them popular, but the Ogudai and Modnos families were enraged by portrayals of their kin. Axou priests denounced them. The Sumaah recorded every buyer. Suranni priests burned the books, and in Autumn 382YE the motion was amended to exclude the Iron Confederacy.

Dawn.t: A vision by Collwyn de Rondell of Dawn depicted the Faraden Genghis Modnos as a cowardly villain, which enraged the Modnos family, who may seek vengeance on those they see as liars, and unsettled priests who believe souls are reborn only within a family.

Grendel.t: After the peace treaty the books were made available to the Grendel, but apart from a few collectors the orcs of the Broken Shore showed little interest in foreign humans' past-life visions.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the motion was proposed by the senator for Redoubt.

Thule.t: Copies sent to the Thule were accepted without comment, and merchants reported that the books were invariably bought in bulk by a handful of polite warlocks.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the distribution followed a suggestion by the Spider's Vantage Spire of Urizen.

Disseminate True Liao visions.o: In Summer 382YE the Senate passed a motion, at 10 thrones a season, to distribute the Seer of the Gateway's accounts of True Liao visions across the Empire and to every nation the Empire trades with. Foreign reactions to the resulting volumes of Echoes of the Labyrinth ranged from enthusiasm to outrage.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: pilgrims abroad valued the volumes as a connection to Bastion, the heart of the faith, against Sumaah missionaries speaking out against it.

Otkodov.t: Echoes of the Labyrinth was sent to Otkodov, where it was accepted without comment and bought in bulk by a few polite warlocks.

Distant deeps.d: The temple opened shortly before the Spring Equinox. Many Asavean visitors traded in Oran, while some travelled on to Sarvos, Tassato and Crown's Quay. The pleased Plenum recognised Franco i Erigo as its delegate to the temple's priests. At the request of Oria i Shartha i Riqueza, senator for Feroz, it granted land in Nemoria for a temple of the Way, expected shortly before the Summer Solstice. J'zarr i Shartha i Guerra and the Freeborn Assembly warned Feroz against idolatry. The Synod could isolate the temple at a cost to trade, encourage tolerance for a small boost to income, attempt to convert visitors with uncertain and risky results, denounce the Senate's Asavean architect Almodin Oktístis, or do nothing.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Crown's Quay is named as one place some Asavean visitors travel on to after visiting the temple.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gained a busy Asavean trade through the new temple in Oran and a planned temple of the Way in Nemoria, but their Assembly remained deeply uneasy about idolatry. The Synod's choices could either cut the income of Feroz's businesses and its Nemorian trade, or boost them.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos and Tassato are named among the places some Asavean visitors continue on to after the temple.

Urizen.t: The Asavean architect and priest of Baddu, Almodin Oktístis, was designing and overseeing new docks at Cargo in Redoubt. A Synod denunciation would likely drive him from the Empire.

Distant deeps.o: In Spring 381YE the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Oran, Feroz, was completed and opened to Asavean sailors and merchants, and the Plenum allowed work to begin on a temple of the Way in Nemoria. Freeborn unease about the temple's influence persisted, and the Synod was offered several possible mandates in response.

Feroz.t: The Temple of Balo and the Black Bull opened in Oran, drawing Asavean merchants who traded for Freeborn fruit, cloth, wine and stone. The Freeborn Assembly urged the people of Feroz to resist its lure, and Synod mandates could make the territory hostile or welcoming to the visitors, lowering or raising local business income.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Lucifaro Figlio del Mattino, mandated to encourage missionaries to Nemoria, is described as a Madrugan hakima.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Crown's Quay is listed among the destinations of some Asavean visitors to the temple.

Redoubt.t: Almodin Oktístis, paid by the Senate, was at work designing and overseeing the building of docks at Cargo, a public symbol of the Empire's tacit tolerance of the Asavean faith.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: some Asavean visitors to the temple travel on to Sarvos.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: some Asavean visitors to the temple travel on to Tassato.

Distribute food to the thralls of Mournw.d: Proposed by the senator for Morrow and seconded by the senator for Redoubt, the motion arose from opportunities in the Mournwold and called for 75 thrones of food to be given to the thralls living there. The Senate passed it, and the 75 thrones needed were provided by Orrick of House Bolholt. The page gives no further detail of what followed once the food had been distributed.

Jotun.t: The Senate sent Imperial food to the thralls living under Jotun rule in the Mournwold, reaching people within the orcs' conquered lands.

Distribute food to the thralls of Mournw.o: In Summer 381YE the Senate passed a motion to distribute 75 thrones' worth of food to the thralls of the Mournwold, then held by the Jotun.

Mournwold.t: The thralls of the Jotun-held Mournwold were to receive 75 thrones' worth of food, paid for by Orrick of House Bolholt.

Dog days are over.d: Following the Earl of Fools' mandate, noble houses agreed on a tourney season running from the Barrens through Semmerholm and Weirwater to Astolat. Any Imperial military unit could join the Grand Tour for a year. Dawnish yeofolk could upgrade farms, forests, mines and herb gardens for one fewer wain. Established troubadours gained four extra crowns per event. Earl Eoric du Borne proposed a School of Music and Poetry at Culwich with a new Reader title. Hugh de Veran proposed restoring the throne room at Withy. Blasine Carver proposed a church and mithril hero statues at Hope's Rest, an opportunity later superseded by the Poetry and Prose wind.

Dawn.t: Dawn celebrated its conquest of the Barrens with a year-long Grand Tour of tourneys, cheaper resource upgrades for yeofolk, higher earnings for troubadours and several proposed commissions to commemorate the triumph.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are described as soundly beaten, and Dawn's heroes are honoured for their final defeat in the Barrens.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a newly ennobled Dawnish lord talks of fighting the Grendel again in the in-character vignette.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg wine appears in the vignette, and Holberg's merchants are credited with the largest fortification in the Empire.

Dog days are over.o: After the conquest of the Barrens was completed, Dawn's jubilant people launched a year of celebratory tourneys known as the Grand Tour. The wind also offered opportunities to build a school of music in Weirwater, restore the Castle of Thorns' throne room and raise a church at Hope's Rest.

Astolat/Withy.t: Hugh de Veran proposed restoring the dilapidated throne room of the Castle of Thorns at a cost of 15 white granite and 45 crowns. Once complete, it would make Dawnish congregation upgrades cheaper for a year and yield historical research on Dawn's early monarchs.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: Consecrated with true liao, Hope's Rest drew Dawnish pilgrims, and Blasine Carver proposed a Church of Ser Guineve and mithril statues of the conquest's heroes there. The church would give Dawnish units on adventures a permanent boost, though this opportunity was later superseded by the Poetry and Prose wind.

Astolat.t: Astolat was chosen as the culminating stage of the Grand Tour, and its Castle of Thorns throne room was proposed for restoration.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg red wine is served in the vignette, and Holberg's fortification is called the largest in the Empire.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm was to host the second season of the Grand Tour's tourneys, following the Barrens.

The Barrens.t: With its conquest declared complete, the Barrens was to open the Grand Tour's tourney season, and a church honouring the heroes of the conquest was proposed at Hope's Rest.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater was to host the third season of the Grand Tour, and a School of Music and Poetry was proposed at Culwich, supported by its weavers' circles.

Doing it.d: Barien's heralds confirmed that everyone receiving Challenge the Iron Duke would be guaranteed entry to one challenge per summit, choosing a reward from the Dragonforge. Past victors must wait a year to compete again. Six covens had cast the magnitude 30 ritual the previous season. In the Challenge of the Caged Pincer, each challenger and two attendants would fight a dire astacid and its two handlers at the Green Iron Grove in Icarion. In the Challenge of the Black Web, challengers would gather glowing tokens in a chamber resembling the Forest of Arden, reached via Alderly. Venomous spider heralds of Jaheris would stalk them there. The in-character text hints at unease over Jaheris's eagerness to help.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish Coven of Golden Wings is listed among the covens that cast Challenge the Iron Duke last season.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: dire astacids are described as giant lobster war beasts common among the Grendel.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are not named directly; the orcs involved are the now-independent gladiators of Beoraidh on the Broken Shore.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr coven The Eternal Family is listed among the covens that cast Challenge the Iron Duke last season.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: The Glass Mantle and The Tempest Flame, both Brass Coast covens, are listed among those that cast the ritual last season.

The Marches.t: Alderly in the Marcher-held Mournwold was chosen as the point where the Black Web challenge's conjunction would open, because the land there grows close to the Forest of Arden.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wintermark covens Ursolskin and Voices of the Unbound Storm are listed among those that cast the ritual last season.

Doing it.o: In Spring 387YE Barien, the Iron Duke, set two new challenges for those receiving the Challenge the Iron Duke ritual: an arena fight against dire astacids handled by Beoraidh gladiators, and a stealth hunt through a forest of spider heralds lent by Jaheris.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Barien's heralds paid the gladiators of independent Beoraidh to supply two dire astacids and handlers for the arena challenge.

Mareave/Icarion.t: The Caged Pincer bouts were set to take place at the Green Iron Grove in Icarion on the Saturday afternoon.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: The conjunction for the Challenge of the Black Web was set to open to Alderly, where the land grows close to the Forest of Arden.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not named on the page; it is linked only through the wider events of the challenges.

Mareave.t: Mareave was the setting for the Challenge of the Caged Pincer, with a large conjunction open for spectators to watch Imperial challengers fight dire astacids.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold provided the conjunction point at Alderly for the Black Web stealth challenge, a short walk from the forest chamber.

Domain expansion.d: Ursula Smith's Assembly saw the Breadbasket reach Mournwold. Three opportunities followed. A 30-throne Overton Smithy commission would turn the Singing Caves' mithril into a thousand points of resupply for armies in Mournwold. Alternatively, a Senate amendment could merge the Quartermaster General with the Caves' custodian as a Marcher national title. A Synod mandate could stake a Marcher claim to Jotun-held Liathaven, creating an expectation, though not a legal right, of receiving it. Jotun reshaping had made Imperial maps of Liathaven useless for scrying until a new one is made. In Bregasland, the Imperial Orc demand for their dead in Grave Wood inflamed Marchers; an appraisal might find a way to recover them without disturbing Marcher graves.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher Assembly cited the Dawnish 'fancy magic castle' that resupplies armies as something they meant to outdo.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the war to eradicate the Druj in the east is described as drawing Imperial attention away from the Marches, and the Sarangrave is joked about as a worse place to live.

Imperial Orcs.t: Their Assembly's demand for the bones of the Autumn Hammers in Grave Wood angered many Marchers. Orcs caught approaching the wood with axes and shovels were turned back, and only an appraisal seemed likely to find a way to recover their dead without uprooting Marcher graves.

Jotun.t: Their slash-and-burn clearing of Liathaven, which they call Ashvale, had made it fertile and unrecognisable to Imperial maps, and the Marchers eyed it as their next conquest once Bregasland was retaken from them.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven is noted as a former Navarr territory where no Navarr have lived for years.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Freeborn dead are among those taken into Grave Wood, and the transfiguration of Madruga is cited as the last time an Imperial map stopped working.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the prestige of the Spiral Castle is what the Overtonians hoped to rival with their forges.

The Marches.t: Having completed their highest calling, the Marchers were offered forges at the Singing Caves, control of the Quartermaster General and a Synod claim to Liathaven for a possible sixth army. Their Assembly also faced pressure to defend Grave Wood against Imperial Orc demands.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark dead are among the fallen whom Marchers believe were reborn as the trees of Grave Wood.

Domain expansion.o: With their highest calling complete and the Imperial Breadbasket now covering all four Marcher territories, the Marchers were offered new ways to build on it in Autumn 388YE: forges at the Singing Caves, a Marcher-held Quartermaster General and a Synod claim on Liathaven. A broken scrying map of Liathaven and an Imperial Orc demand over the dead of Grave Wood complicated matters.

Liathaven/Liath's Heart.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher Assembly's statement looked to Liath's Heart next door and the coming final battle with the vallorn.

Bregasland.t: Grave Wood, which sprang up overnight over nearly three thousand fallen soldiers, became a flashpoint after the Imperial Orc demand. The Marches were noted as taking Bregasland back from the Jotun, with victory in the Dour Fens promised.

Liathaven.t: Transformed by Jotun clearing and the heralds of the City of Fire and Stone, it could no longer be scried with existing maps, and a proposed Marcher mandate would stake a claim to conquer it. The vallorn and the Feni remain there.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: its transfiguration two years earlier is cited as the last time an Imperial map ceased to work for scrying.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: a tidal wave of Imperial steel is said to have swept through Mitwold, and it is among the four territories now covered by the Breadbasket.

Mournwold.t: The Breadbasket was completed here, and the Singing Caves at Overton could become an industrial district of smithies resupplying armies, or be tied to a Marcher Quartermaster General.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: a Marcher jokes that even Ashvale is better than living in the Sarangrave.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Spiral Castle's prestige is the benchmark the Overtonians wanted to compete with.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named; the only Dawnish reference is the Assembly's comparison with a Dawnish magic castle that resupplies armies.

Don't blame me.d: The tomb was consecrated by Laughlan vi Temeschwar after a Synod judgement. Its torches now barely go out, and pilgrims leave inspired. The League assembly may enact mandates to spread Ambition, to destroy the Vyig, who are regrouping in Varushka and are tied to the bite trade, or to burn out Skathe's servants haunting Metri. Metri has disrupted the Northern Trade Network and raised the Fortress of Salt's upkeep. Proposed projects include modernised mines in Locul, a timbermill in the Vardstein Vale and a mana exchange for trading with the Thule. Any Ambition mandate would tinge League opportunities with ruthlessness for a year. Varushka may also respond to Ratibor's legacy.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orc thief-takers could be hired, and Imperial Orc military units could join the Break the Vyig adventure if the League enacts the mandate to destroy the Vyig.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr's Hercynia is linked to Temeschwar by the Northern Trade Network, which the Metri troubles and a proposed Thule exchange would disrupt.

The League.t: The League gained its only memorial to a specific exemplar. Its assembly can spread Ambition, destroy the Vyig, cleanse Metri or back great works, but any Ambition mandate would make League opportunities ruthless and unsentimental for at least a year.

Thule.t: Thule traders pass through Metri unharmed by propitiating the Mirror of Spite. A proposed Temeschwar market would draw most of their mana crystal trade into the League.

Varushka.t: The Vyig have rebuilt in old Varushkan bolt holes. Varushkan priests may submit alternative mandates on the Vyig, Varushkan units could join their destruction, and a strongly supported statement of principle about Ratibor could spread Ambition through the nation.

Wintermark.t: The Vyig have placed a bounty on the Winterfolk cardinal Veikko Bondforger, mistaking him for Ratibor reborn. Wintermark's Hahnmark is part of the disrupted Northern Trade Network.

Don't blame me.o: After the Autumn Equinox 384YE, Ratibor's Tomb at Ratibor's Gate in Temeschwar was consecrated to Ambition with true liao. The consecration spread a ruthless, unsentimental Ambition through the League and opened several opportunities, including mandates, great works and a campaign against the Vyig.

Temeschwar/Locul.t: The Descent Guild of Ore Extraction proposes the Mines of Temeschwar great work to modernise Locul's mines. It would provide rings to mines and ingots to businesses, and raise Temeschwar's taxation by 5 thrones a season.

Temeschwar/Metri.t: The creatures haunting Metri slaughtered a caravan, disrupting the Northern Trade Network and raising the Fortress of Salt's upkeep. A League mandate or the Order of the Rod and Shield could clear the haunting.

Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale.t: Vardstein Timber proposes building the Vardstein Timbermill and Sorting Yard on the edge of the wild Vale. It would supply forest materials, create the Vardstein Vandal title and clear land for farming.

Temeschwar/Vargat.t: Mentioned in passing: a road built for the proposed Vardstein timbermill would pass through Vargat, making its fertile soil easier to reach.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark is linked to Temeschwar by the Northern Trade Network, whose ministries are disrupted by the Metri haunting. Its traders would lose the top levels of their Thule trade if the proposed Temeschwar exchange is built.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia is a western link in the Northern Trade Network, now disrupted by the dangers in Metri. It would lose Thule trade to a proposed Temeschwar mana exchange.

Holberg.t: Holberg is praised for turning the eternals' enmity to its own ends. If the larger Ambition mandate passes, a chance would open to build an art structure there, and Holberg's mechanisms would inspire the proposed Temeschwar mines.

Karov.t: Karov is the eastern link of the Northern Trade Network, which the Metri troubles disrupt and a Thule exchange in Temeschwar would undercut.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: the robber-boyar Alexi Iskandrova Isembrioch, possibly funded by the Vyig, had his attempt to raise a bandit army in Karsk stymied.

Otkodov.t: The Thule of Otkodov trade mana crystals through the Northern Trade Network. A proposed Temeschwar-Otkodov Mana Exchange would channel most of that trade to Temeschwar.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos's Blood Red Quays Art Gallery would switch from supporting Pride to Ambition if the larger mandate passes. The city was where the earlier purge of the Vyig began.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Northern Trade Network runs east from Temeschwar to Karov via Skarsind.

Tassato.t: Tassato's Blood Red River Museum would switch to supporting Ambition under the larger mandate, which would also offer a chance to secure materials to finish repairing it.

Temeschwar.t: Ratibor's Gate now burns with near-eternal torches and draws pilgrims. Temeschwar faces Vyig violence and Skathe's creatures in Metri, and is offered great works in its mines and forests, a Thule mana exchange, and higher taxes if these succeed.

Volodmartz.t: Mentioned in passing: the wilderness outside Temeschwar's walls is compared to that of Volodmartz.

Double dare.d: Donations from Freeborn citizens gave every military unit supporting the armies in Segura an extra 5 Crowns. Because those armies stayed on defence, the bounty would continue only for units supporting armies that attack in Segura. With Feroz fallen to the Grendel, a proposed mandate needing a greater majority would extend the bounty to armies attacking there, at the cost of a one-rank production penalty to all other Brass Coast personal resources. Conflicting judgements on privateering caused confusion, but corsairs found four targets: the Temple of Tempest Jade, the Vorlach slave markets, Asavean granite ships and the Drake Island shipyard. Full plans for the chosen raid were promised before the Winter Solstice.

Grendel.t: Having taken Feroz, the Grendel faced a possible bounty on armies attacking them there and proposed corsair raids on their temple, their slave markets at Vorlach, their Asavean granite trade or the four warship hulls at their Drake Island shipyard.

Jotun.t: The Jotun did not attack the defended armies in Segura, and the Freeborn would now fund the bounty only for armies that attack Jotun forces there.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn citizens paid for the defence of Segura and could choose to pay again for Feroz, at the cost of lost production. Their corsair families awaited the Assembly's choice of a single raid against the Grendel.

Double dare.o: After the Freeborn Bounty in Segura paid out without any fighting, the Freeborn Assembly was offered the chance to extend it to armies attacking the Grendel in occupied Feroz. Corsairs spurred by a narrowly passed Synod mandate also identified four possible raid targets against the Grendel and asked the Assembly to choose one.

Bay of Catazar.t: Corsair ships scoured the Bay for opportunities. Asavean merchantmen carrying slaves and white granite sail through it unescorted, making them a possible but illegal target unless the Senate declared war on the Asaveans.

Feroz.t: Feroz fell to the Grendel, and a proposed mandate would extend the Freeborn Bounty to military units supporting armies that attack the invaders there.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: any Grendel warships captured in a raid on Drake Island might be sailed back to Madruga.

Segura.t: Units supporting the armies in Segura received an extra 5 Crowns, but no fighting took place. The bounty would continue only for armies that undertake attacking orders against the Jotun there.

Shayeel.t: The mining and slave-market town of Vorlach on Shayeel's northern coast, controlled by Salt Lord Moorvain, was a possible raid target. Such a raid would need Imperial military units as well as fleets, and could free many slaves and carry off mithril.

Double or nothingness.d: The Winter Solstice law made selling or gifting liao into the Confederacy by port or across the border a crime, but it appears to allow trade with Suranni inside the Empire. The Silent Bell reported to Cardinal of Vigilance Irada von Temeschwar a smuggling route, probably run by Imperial citizens from a stockaded camp, that takes liao from Feroz into Arbonne (Kalino) in exchange for silver, green iron and some mithril. Dumon's Hand proposed a concealed ministry in the south-west, trading liao for Winter vis; this would need Senate or other authorisation and risks a diplomatic incident. Susanna of the Seventh Star urged the Synod to invite Dumon's Hand to explain their beliefs, while Mitra the Uncompromising called for their condemnation and an inquisition of Palladius of Urizen.

Highguard.t: The Highborn priest Susanna of the Seventh Star proposed a General Assembly statement inviting Dumon's Hand to explain their beliefs, possibly at the White City or the Seminary of the Swan, and Casinea and Necropolis were floated as possible sites for the liao ministry.

The Brass Coast.t: The smuggling route uncovered by the Silent Bell runs from southern Feroz, and Kahraman and Madruga are among the places Dumon's Hand now favours for a proposed ministry trading liao for Winter vis.

The League.t: Tassato and Sarvos are among the sites Dumon's Hand suggested for a concealed ministry that would exchange liao for Winter vis, should the Empire commission it.

Urizen.t: The Urizeni illuminate Mitra the Uncompromising led priests demanding that Dumon's Hand be condemned as heretics and that Palladius of Urizen be called to inquisition for vindicating them.

Double or nothingness.o: After the Senate banned the sale or gifting of liao to the Iron Confederacy, the Silent Bell uncovered a liao smuggling route from southern Feroz into Kalino, Dumon's Hand sought a lawful way to keep receiving liao, and priests divided over whether the Empire should support the Suranni rebel magicians at all.

Morrow/Ravion.t: Mentioned in passing: Ravion is not named on the page.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the White City is suggested as a neutral place where Dumon's Hand representatives might meet priests of the Way.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: not named, though the new law bans liao reaching the Confederacy via ports.

Casinea.t: Casinea is named as a possible, more distant site for the proposed ministry trading liao to Dumon's Hand for Winter vis.

Feroz.t: The Silent Bell identified a smuggling route carrying large amounts of liao from southern Feroz across the border, and earlier suggestions to build the ministry there have been reconsidered.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman is one of the sites Dumon's Hand now favours for a disguised ministry exchanging liao for Winter vis, if one is commissioned.

Kalino.t: Known to the Suranni as Arbonne, Kalino is the destination of the liao smuggling route, with metals including silver, green iron and mithril flowing back into the Empire.

Madruga.t: Madruga is one of the sites suggested by Dumon's Hand for a concealed ministry trading liao for Winter vis.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: not named; the territory's only link is through Urizeni figures such as Palladius and Mitra.

Necropolis.t: Necropolis is named as a possible, more distant site for the proposed ministry trading liao to Dumon's Hand for Winter vis.

Reikos.t: The Seminary of the Swan in Reikos is suggested as a venue where Dumon's Hand might share their spiritual understanding with Imperial priests.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos is one of the sites Dumon's Hand suggested for a disguised ministry exchanging liao for Winter vis.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: south-east Segura was previously suggested as a ministry site, but this has been reconsidered given the new law and Suranni embargo.

Shavronne.t: Mentioned in passing: not named; it is affected only as part of the Iron Confederacy to which liao trade is now banned.

Tassato.t: Tassato is one of the sites Dumon's Hand suggested for a concealed ministry trading liao for Winter vis.

Down along the cove.d: Fisherfolk from Feroz, Madruga, Necropolis, Sarvos, Redoubt and Tassato could profit by pushing into deeper waters, but Grendel captains sought slaves, boats and dredged-up ilium. The Fellowship of Purple Sails, Freeborn corsair families, Ferozi and Madrugan paradors and League guilds offered a 3-crown bounty to fleets protecting the fishermen. Too little protection would see businesses lose a fifth of production and a permanent drop in taxes; enough would bring extra production, and greater efforts more ilium at auction and a richer Broken Shore Bounty, though this might push Grendel towards foreign traders. Synod mandates could urge captains to defend the fleet or, alternatively, urge caution and cancel the opportunity entirely.

Grendel.t: Independent Grendel captains, not tied up in the Spiral campaign, were drawn to the Bay to seize crews as slaves, boats, cargo and ilium from Imperial fisherfolk; strong Imperial protection would drive them off, perhaps towards ships trading through the southern bay.

Highguard.t: Highborn fishermen off the Necropolis coast, like Captain Amos of Candle Cove, saw the moonfish boom first-hand, and Necropolis businesses stood to gain or lose depending on how well the fleet was protected.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn corsair families and the paradors of Feroz and Madruga helped fund the bounty for protecting fishermen, and Freeborn captains taking the action would count it towards the Broken Shore Bounty, which could rise if protection was strong.

The League.t: League guilds involved with fishing helped fund the protection bounty, while Sarvos and Tassato's businesses stood to profit or suffer depending on whether the Grendel raids were stopped.

Urizen.t: Redoubt, which draws some of its prosperity from the sea, was among the territories whose businesses would gain extra production or lose a fifth of it, along with some permanent tax revenue, depending on the outcome.

Down along the cove.o: In Summer 381YE, years of Spring and Night magic in the Bay of Catazar caused a boom in sea life, giving Imperial fisherfolk the chance of bumper catches while drawing independent Grendel captains eager to raid them. Imperial fleets were offered the chance to protect the fishing fleet for one season.

Bay of Catazar.t: The magic worked on the Bay produced a boom in fish and sea creatures, and its open waters became the hunting ground of both bold Imperial fisherfolk and Grendel raiders.

Feroz.t: Feroz's businesses risked losing a fifth of their production and suffering one of the most severe permanent tax drops if the Grendel raids succeeded, but would gain extra production if the fleet was protected; Ferozi paradors helped fund the bounty.

Madruga.t: Madrugan paradors helped back the bounty, as the territory's businesses faced either bumper profits or one of the heaviest losses in production and permanent tax revenue should the Grendel prevail.

Necropolis.t: Fishing boats off the Necropolis coast were hauling up unusually large moonfish, and the territory's businesses and tax revenue depended on whether Imperial fleets kept the Grendel away.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt's partly sea-based businesses could gain extra production or lose a fifth of it, along with some permanent tax revenue, depending on how well the fishing fleet was protected.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos's fishing concerns stood to profit from the boom, but a successful Grendel raid would cost its businesses a fifth of their production and cause one of the worst permanent drops in taxes.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel navies were noted as being engaged in the Spiral campaign, leaving independent captains free to prey on fishermen.

Tassato.t: Tassato's businesses would gain extra production if the fishermen were protected or lose a fifth of it if raided, though the loss of boats would not reduce its tax revenue.

Down that road.d: Freeborn Autumn magic, Summer citadels and the Empire's partial success at Rojota stopped the Corazón and Stephen of Sarcombe's Yegarra from seizing any mithril or white granite. The Hierro, Corazón and the zealous Escuta under Lefsnir Red-armed still took Nestor's Bounty and Jade Range with few deaths, offering Freeborn loyalty or exile and sending a flood of refugees into Madruga. Only one of Braydon's Jasse, Serra Briante or Serra Damata now stands between them and conquest. Heroes could destroy three runeboxes of tools to stop the orcs isolating the hill regions, kill Stephen to withdraw his Yegarra and bring Sarcombe's aid, or capture Meketh of the Flames to curse the Corazón.

Jotun.t: The Lasambrian Jotun and their allies, including the Jotun orcs of Narkyst, now hold two fifths of Kahraman with few losses, and plan to wreck the hill roads and bridges of Serra Briante as the next step in their conquest.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn are losing Kahraman region by region: Fort Braydon is near breaking point, refugees flood into Madruga, and only Freeborn Autumn magic and the Empire's victory kept the Bourse mithril and white granite flowing this season.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is named as one source of emergency supplies for the defenders of Fort Braydon.

The Marches.t: Stephen of Sarcombe's Mournwold Yegarra have sworn to stay in Kahraman to avenge Wallis; if Stephen is killed and his head delivered to the Marcher egregore, the people of Sarcombe would send support to Fort Braydon.

Down that road.o: In summer 384YE the Lasambrian Jotun consolidated their hold on Gambit and captured Jade Range in Kahraman, leaving the exhausted defenders of Fort Braydon clinging to the northern hills. A major conjunction offered the Empire a chance to stop the orcs crippling the hill roads and to strike at Stephen of Sarcombe.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: Fort Braydon's garrison, cut off from the plains that fed it, is near breaking point; destroying even one runebox would prevent the orcs isolating Braydon's Jasse.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: The Lasambrian Jotun consolidated their hold on Gambit after taking Rojota, and launched their push into Jade Range from there.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: Jade Range fell after the decisive battle for Nestor's Bounty, its western settlements overwhelmed and its Freeborn offered loyalty or exile.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: The Great Mine's mithril was protected this season, but the orcs are gathering tools in the southern hills of Serra Briante to wreck its bridges and roads, making it the site of the coming battle.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: Summer citadels guarded Serra Damata and the Damatian Cliffs' white granite reached the Empire, though Corazón raids may claim half its production next season and the region risks being isolated.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Lefsnir Red-armed names the azure shores of the Bay of Catazar among the lands the Lasambrians mean to claim.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Stephen of Sarcombe's Yegarra chose to stay in Kahraman rather than return to Bregasland to support Mathilda Fisher.

Kahraman.t: Gambit and Jade Range fell to the Lasambrian Jotun, leaving only the northern hill regions in Imperial hands, with a battle opportunity to stop the orcs isolating them from one another.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: orcs who once lived in the passes overlooking Liathaven, now allied to the Lasambrians, lend their knowledge of Kahraman's high places.

Madruga.t: The stream of Kahraman refugees into Madruga became a flood, Madruga is a source of emergency supplies for Fort Braydon, and armies travelling to or from Segura must now pass through it.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold is a source of emergency supplies, and Sarcombe's residents would send aid to Fort Braydon if the traitor Stephen of Sarcombe's death is proved.

Segura.t: With Gambit and Jade Range lost, Imperial armies moving to or from Segura must go via Madruga, and the Corazón's new raiding prowess may stem from whatever the Lasambrians achieved there.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is listed as a source of emergency supplies for Fort Braydon.

Down the cavalier road.d: Eleonaris accepted her ceded statue, which became a mist-shrouded island in the Semmerlak. She still forbade Knights of Glory but promised Brother Luke a replacement ritual at the Winter Solstice. Jaheris sent two heralds to the Icy Crag, speeding curse research. Cathan Canae remained angered by the Empire's surrender of land. Hayaak, blaming Edric du Gauvain (dead since 381YE) for his fall, demanded the knight's head. He reinforced the Jotun, loosed gryphons in Coombe and worked to turn Eleonaris against the Empire. Dawn has until Summer 385YE to win eternals' favour, through statues or negotiation, and so make the Eastern Sky Favoured.

Dawn.t: Dawn's enchanters were offered the chance to make the Eastern Sky a Favoured army under up to five Summer eternals, with Eleonaris already willing. Meanwhile Hayaak's monsters menace Astolat and he demands the head of the long-dead Dawnish knight Edric du Gauvain.

Druj.t: The Druj hold Dawnguard, where Cathan Canae insists her statue be raised in the ruined Towers of the Dawn, meaning Dawn would have to take the region from them to win her favour.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae cited the ceding of two territories to the Grendel as an example of the Empire's failure to defend its land.

Jotun.t: The Jotun gained significant reinforcements and a powerful ally, as Hayaak's feathered heralds joined their forces and he vowed to support them on every battlefield against the Empire until he receives Edric du Gauvain's head.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Adamant's heralds continue to work with Imperial citizens at the College of Engineering in the League's territory of Temeschwar.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae decried regions of Varushka given up to buy Thule support, and Meraud is said to show some slight interest in the Thule but offer them little patronage.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the surrender of entire regions of Varushka to the Thule is one of the losses that angered Cathan Canae.

Down the cavalier road.o: In Autumn 384YE the Summer eternals' attitudes to the Empire shifted: Eleonaris was mollified by her statue, Jaheris rewarded his tourney champions, and Hayaak turned furiously against the Empire to back the Jotun. Lady Nimue de Moraine also opened an opportunity for Dawn to win up to five Summer eternals as patrons of the Eastern Sky.

Astolat/Coombe.t: Gryphons and other monsters sent by Hayaak now prowl Coombe's forests, attacking travellers bound for Caer Faucon and forcing armed patrols into the woods.

Semmerholm/Elvette.t: The page names Semmerholm, without singling out this region, as the proposed site of statues to Barien at the Semmerstones and Rhianos at Racqueen, should Dawn seek their favour.

Semmerholm/Ulvenholm.t: The page names Semmerholm, without singling out this region, as the proposed site of statues to Barien at the Semmerstones and Rhianos at Racqueen, should Dawn seek their favour.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Cathan Canae demands her statue stand in the ruined Towers of the Dawn in Dawnguard, so the Empire would have to reconquer the region from the Druj to gain her favour.

Astolat.t: Hayaak's gryphons and other beasts now stalk the forests of Coombe. Adamant and Meraud have proposed statues at the Castle of Thorns and in Weaving as the price of their favour for the Eastern Sky.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Rhianos wants his statue ceded to him so that he can watch brave Dawnish knights try their hands in the forests of Brocéliande.

Semmerholm.t: Barien has asked for a statue at the Semmerstones and Rhianos for one at Racqueen as the price of their favour for the Eastern Sky.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: the recent Imperial raid on Skallahn is among the bold adventures that delighted Rhianos.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: a House deCassilon representative brought the news that sparked Nimue's negotiations back to Spiral Castle from Anvil.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Adamant's heralds continue to work with Imperial citizens at the College of Engineering in Temeschwar.

The Barrens.t: Cathan Canae will only accept a statue in the ruins of the Towers of the Dawn in the Barrens, which she regards as Dawn's rightful dominion lost to the Druj.

The Semmerlak.t: The waters of the Semmerlak rose around Eleonaris's statue, turning its promontory into a fog-shrouded island guarded by sharp hidden rocks.

Weirwater.t: Jaheris's heralds suggested a statue of the Unicorn Prince beside the Weirwater Vales, though he would accept another suitably storied site.

Drain the flooded streets of Caricomare.d: Proposed by Sarvos and seconded by Zenith, the motion sought no Senate funding. The cost of 50 wains of white granite and 50 Thrones was presented by Mirislav, Senator for Sarvos, after the Autumn Equinox, and construction took six months with no upkeep. Completion created the Mayor of Caricomare, appointed by the sitting senator for Sarvos, paid 15 Crowns a season and holding 25 votes in territorial elections. The Constitutional Court let the unusual appointment method pass scrutiny. It later judged the sinecure unconstitutional because it gives senatorial votes to people not present at Anvil. The motion was not struck down, but no future sinecure of this kind will be approved.

The League.t: A League senator restored a historic flooded district of Sarvos and gained a new League title, the Mayor of Caricomare. The precedent of appointing a voter in a senatorial election will not be repeated for future League sinecures.

Drain the flooded streets of Caricomare.o: In Autumn 378YE the Senate passed in principle a motion from the senator for Sarvos to rebuild the docks of Caricomare, sunk thirty years earlier by a terrible storm. The work was paid for and completed, making the flooded district habitable again and creating the title of Mayor of Caricomare.

Sarvos.t: The sunken docks and flooded streets of Caricomare in Sarvos were rebuilt, making the district habitable again. Sarvos gained a Mayor of Caricomare, appointed by its senator and holding 25 votes in its territorial elections.

Draw strength from vulnerability.d: The Autumn 382YE mandate, upheld 164–0, named Ser Isidore Ossienne and Lord Colwyn de Rondell. Its preaching spread the view that love, like glory, takes many paths and that sex is not fundamental to it, changing Dawnish attitudes to love and marriage. Weavers of Spiral Castle made a Troubadour's Ring for the Champion of Love, and weavers of Laroc a Circlet of Command for the Champion of Glory. The egregore suggested bestowing them at the Grand Tourney. Troubadours proposed assembly statements of Love or Glory, to be spread by the Civil Service. Lady Zaha Arien designed the Arbor of the Twin Roses in Auvanne, which awaits a Senate commission or wayleave.

Dawn.t: Dawn's people embraced a broader, more varied understanding of True Love, reshaping national attitudes to love and marriage. Its troubadours gained new laurels for their Champions of Love and Glory, a way to honour inspiring figures through assembly statements, and plans for a pilgrimage monument with a new national title.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but the weavers of Spiral Castle, in Grendel-held Spiral, created the Troubadour's Ring for Dawn's Champion of Love.

Draw strength from vulnerability.o: After the Dawn National Assembly sent the Earl of Fools to preach that true Love and true Glory arise from the seven Virtues, Dawn saw a resurgence of interest in True Love. The wind also brought new laurels for the Champions of Love and Glory, a proposed statement of Love and Glory, and plans for a monument called the Arbor of the Twin Roses.

Semmerholm/Ferrond.t: The weavers of Laroc crafted the Circlet of Command, to be hallowed by Dawn's troubadours and bestowed on the Champion of Glory.

Semmerholm/Lacuve.t: Mentioned in passing: the architect Lord Caradoc, Lady Zaha Arien's father, recently completed the Rose Towers in Lacuve to celebrate Dawn's victories.

Astolat.t: The Arbor of the Twin Roses is proposed for Auvanne, within sight of Endric's Hill, to honour the troubadour Elayne Silverlark. It would need a Senate commission or a wayleave to be built.

Semmerholm.t: The weavers of Laroc crafted the Circlet of Command for Dawn's Champion of Glory. The page also notes the Rose Towers built in Lacuve to celebrate Dawn's victories in Semmerholm and Weirwater.

Spiral.t: The weavers of Spiral Castle created the Troubadour's Ring, a garland for Dawn's Champion of Love that now rests with the egregore.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn's victories in Weirwater are among those celebrated by the Rose Towers in Lacuve.

Dream on.d: Enis's 383YE judgement sought recognition of Seren as a city equal to any other nation's, and work on the Temple began in Summer 386YE. Every congregation in Miaren now receives a dose of Goosewhisper Infusion and an extra liao. The Navarr Assembly can appoint a Dreamspeaker of Seren, and the dreamspeaker archetype is open to Navarr. The Temple could become a major pilgrimage site if it were consecrated with true liao, but this would need a Synod writ from a virtue assembly and general assembly support. Deryn of Vision's End asked the brands to vote on whether the Navarr should explore ways to show their importance to the Empire, such as ceasing to carry messages. Eirwen of Mountains Slumber asked the wayhouses to choose one territory and a shared dream to pursue there.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Eirwen recalls Navarr messengers helping the First Empress build her alliance with Dawn, and notes that defeating the vallorn is the shared highest calling of the Navarr and the Dawnish.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: dreamspeakers list the destruction of the Druj as a worthy dream and cite the effort to free the Great Forest Orcs from them, while Deryn blames Therunin's fall to the Druj on Imperial choices.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: victory over the Grendel and the freeing of slaves in Axos are cited as dreams as important as purging the vallorn.

Highguard.t: Reikos hosts the Navarr wayhouse Micah's Stand, so it could be chosen as the territory to benefit from a shared dream. Eirwen also disputes the Highborn claim that the Empire is uniquely their destiny.

Imperial Orcs.t: Skarsind hosts the Ashen Tears wayhouse, so the Imperial Orcs could be the hosts of any shared dream the Navarr wayhouses choose to pursue.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: defeating the Jotun is named as a dream, and Deryn asks why there is no drive to recover Liathaven when the Empire rallies whenever the Jotun threaten Marcher lands.

Navarr.t: The nation gains a Dreamspeaker of Seren to appoint, a new archetype, liao and Goosewhisper Infusion for Miaren's congregations, and the chance to seek a true liao consecration. Its brands and wayhouses must each decide on Deryn's call for leverage and Eirwen's call to build civilisation.

The League.t: Holberg hosts the Splintered House wayhouse in Utterlund, making it a possible focus for the Navarr wayhouses' shared dream.

The Marches.t: Deryn holds up Marcher generals' oaths to defend their home territories, and the Marchers' sheathed threat to withhold grain, as the model of leverage the Navarr should emulate.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Deryn cites the Urizeni readiness to tear apart the Citadel Guard if Zenith were abandoned as an example of a nation fighting for its interests.

Varushka.t: Ossium hosts the Awstin's Rest wayhouse and could benefit from the Navarr wayhouses' dream. Deryn also praises the Varushkans who refused to let the Senate take the Iron Roads.

Dream on.o: The Navarr completed the Temple of the Waking Dream in Seren, Miaren, and Seren became known as the City of Dreams. New dreamspeakers emerged with two rival visions for the nation's future, each calling for a decision at the Autumn Equinox.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Home to the Splintered House, one of the five Navarr wayhouses eligible to be chosen for the shared dream.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: Home to Awstin's Rest, one of the five Navarr wayhouses eligible to be chosen for the shared dream.

Reikos/Chalcis Mount.t: Home to Micah's Stand, one of the five Navarr wayhouses eligible to be chosen for the shared dream.

Skarsind/Skogei Glens.t: Home to the Ashen Tears, one of the five Navarr wayhouses eligible to be chosen for the shared dream.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: The Last Battle wayhouse stands here on lands the Karass claim as their own, and is one of the wayhouses that could be chosen for the shared dream.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Deryn laments that all the work clearing the vallorn from Eastring has been undone in a way that cannot be resolved without uniting the vallornhearts.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the Temple is compared with the grand stone basilicas of Bastion.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Deryn notes that the Empire threw itself into the fray whenever the Jotun threatened Bregasland.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: freeing Brocéliande from the taint of Spring magic is cited as one dream among many.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Eirwen of Mountains Slumber, who urges the Navarr to build civilisation, is based in Hercynia.

Holberg.t: The Splintered House wayhouse makes Holberg one of the territories the Navarr wayhouses could choose as the focus of a shared dream.

Liathaven.t: Deryn lived in Liathaven until Vision's End steading was lost. He asks why there is no drive to recover the territory and what might have been had Navarr generals sworn to die defending it.

Miaren.t: The completed Temple of the Waking Dream has made Seren the City of Dreams, drawing visionaries to it and giving every congregation in Miaren Goosewhisper Infusion and an extra liao.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is cited as one of the Marcher lands the Empire always rallies to defend against the Jotun.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold is cited as one of the Marcher lands the Empire always rallies to defend against the Jotun.

Ossium.t: The Awstin's Rest wayhouse makes Ossium a possible focus for the Navarr wayhouses' shared dream.

Reikos.t: The Micah's Stand wayhouse makes Reikos a possible focus for the Navarr wayhouses' shared dream.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is not named on the page; the League's only stake here is the wayhouse in Holberg.

Skarsind.t: The Ashen Tears wayhouse makes Skarsind a possible focus for the Navarr wayhouses' shared dream.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens hold the Last Battle wayhouse and the newly built Caedwynn's Hold. Caedwynn's Hold's Keeper, due to be appointed by the Navarr senators, could join the wayhouse meeting if appointed in time.

Therunin.t: Deryn cites Therunin's fall to the Druj and the vallorn as proof of Navarr sacrifice. Thousands of Navarr died, Thornsong House and Peakedge Stead were destroyed, and the Thimble was lost.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Urizeni readiness to fight if the Empire abandoned Zenith is cited as an example of leverage.

Dream to me.d: Several responses were coloured by Ourania Neofoti's Synod mandate urging caution in dealings with inhuman powers. Siakha withdrew her favour from the Grendel and offered to unleash her heralds if the Empire removed its enmity. Eleonaris asked House de Gauvain to meet her herald and for the cursed dagger used against Prince Hayaak to be returned. Wise Rangara agreed to a quiet parley with Emperor Vesna and offered Heart's Blood bargains in Ossium and Urizen. Sinokenon arranged a meeting with the people of Tsark. Estavus declined to close the Zenith–Sarangrave border but offered trades. Lashonar offered a ritual to realign the Ring of Dust and Glass to Night.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Estavus noted that the Senate's fortification in Lustri could slow a Druj invasion from Sarangrave, and Wise Rangara's offer would grow Bladeroot to counter lingering Druj influence in Urizen.

Grendel.t: Siakha confirmed she had withdrawn her favour from the Grendel, not at the Archmage's demand but because High Priestess Shivaarn and her people had earned its loss.

The Brass Coast.t: Siakha mocked the Freeborn for choosing protection over vengeance after the fighting in Madruga, while Lashonar's Night ritual in Burnish promised to draw the Fire Beacon remnants back to the regio, where kohan and corsairs could pick them off.

Urizen.t: Wise Rangara offered the Custodian of the Bleak Tower and the Keeper of the Tower of the Fall richer Heart's Blood harvests in return for Declarations of Concord, and Sinokenon's meeting with Tsark asked for philosophically trained Urizeni to attend.

Varushka.t: Wise Rangara welcomed a quiet chat with the Varushkan Emperor Vesna and proposed rededicating the Hollow Stone in Ossium to her. The Synod's mandate had been largely ignored in Varushka.

Dream to me.o: Six eternals answered the Imperial archmages' Winter Solstice plenipotentiaries ahead of the Spring Equinox 386YE. Eleonaris, Wise Rangara, Sinokenon and Lashonar offered meetings or encounters, while Siakha and Estavus declined to parley and made offers directly to Imperial magicians.

Segura/Burnish.t: The Ring of Dust and Glass in Burnish, where Cold Sun-tainted Day guardians stood watch, was the target of Lashonar's proposed realignment ritual, which needed performers to restore those guardians.

Zenith/Lustri.t: The Senate's fortification in the forest of Lustri had made little progress, but Estavus said that once finished it would help slow any invasion from Sarangrave.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Siakha framed her boons to Imperial magicians as a celebration of the mayhem the Empire helped spread in the Bay of Catazar.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Siakha praised the testing of twelve thousand warriors in Madruga and Mareave, though she scorned the Freeborn for choosing the course of protection.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: Siakha cited the twelve thousand warriors tested and found wanting in Madruga and Mareave as earning the Empire some of her favour.

Morrow.t: Wise Rangara offered to install a raven statuette at the Bleak Tower, raising its Heart's Blood yield and changing its herbs to Bladeroot, if the Custodian committed to protecting the herb gardens of Morrow.

Ossium.t: Wise Rangara offered that if the Conclave displaced Arhallogen and dedicated the whole Hollow Stone at Marshstand Skerry to her, it would yield five measures of Heart's Blood each season, likely at the cost of a dreadful fight and the Spring eternal's anger.

Sarangrave.t: Estavus said there was no pass between Sarangrave and Zenith that could be closed, only a long woody marsh running to the Feverwater, so any barrier against invasion from Sarangrave would have to come from the Senate's fortification in Lustri.

Segura.t: Lashonar offered to permanently realign the Ring of Dust and Glass to Night so the remnants of the Fire Beacon could not use it to reform, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction would take up to fifty people there.

Zenith.t: Estavus refused to raise a barrier on the border between Zenith and Sarangrave, saying none existed to close and creating one would badly damage the territory.

Dreaming in strands.d: The bridge, badly damaged in a raid before the Summer Solstice 385YE, blocks armies moving between Madruga and Sarvos or Tassato, cuts off refugees fleeing the Grendel and halts southern trade and the Tollkeep's tolls. With plans obtained from the Sarvosi engineer Margueritte, repair would cost 30 mithril, 10 white granite and 120 crowns. Optional additions were Tall Hal's barbican fortifications, a Trivento merchants' quarter creating the Ostiary of Trivento ministry, a great work wharf at Vassa's Eye boosting Madruga fleets, and Emperor Giovanni's plan to pay the Tollkeep five thrones per army crossing. All depend on the bridge being restored, and the Grendel threat to Madruga makes construction risky without an army to protect it.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: a Highborn magistrate eyes Eilian as though he might be a Druj assassin in disguise.

Grendel.t: The Grendel invasion of Madruga threatens any rebuilding. If they captured Torres or Bocche, work would become impossible and all materials would be lost. The page also recalls their failed attempt to destroy the bridge in Spring 380YE.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard journals were among Margueritte's sources, and a historical senator for Necropolis led the opposition to Giovanni's toll plan.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Emperor Ahraz's preoccupation with the Orc Rebellion is given as the reason Concetta di Trivento's proposals failed.

Jotun.t: The page credits a Jotun raid with badly damaging the bridge. Liathaven, then in Jotun hands, would only gain a Trivento-linked title if conquered.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn have lost a major trade route and refugees cannot reach the League. A proposed Vassa's Eye wharf would boost Madruga fleets and could create a Freeborn Harbourmaster position, alongside a possible Caravan Master of the Sunset Road in Calvos.

The League.t: The Sarvosi Tollkeep has lost toll income and could gain five thrones per army crossing under Giovanni's plan. Trivento could become a trade hub with a new League title, the Ostiary of Trivento.

The Marches.t: Marchers could gain a Bailiff of Sarcombe Market if a later great work boosted Mournwold farms after the Gateway to the South was built. The fortification plans were drawn up by Tall Hal, a yeofolk architect from Odd's End.

Dreaming in strands.o: Commissioned by the Senate at the Autumn Equinox, Eilian Sweetwater of the Department of Historical Research recovered Carmen i Dehasa i Erigo's original blueprints for the damaged Spider's Dream bridge. He set out a costed repair alongside several long-rejected historical proposals that the Senate could add to it.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: Mentioned in passing: the page refers to Kahraman's mines and a proposed title at Nestor's Bounty but does not name the Jade Range.

Madruga/Torres.t: Torres's capture by enemies would make the repair impossible and forfeit all materials contributed. If the bridge were fortified, holding Torres would preserve military control of the bridge and allow a beachhead across the river.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: Bocche anchors the bridge's northern side. Losing it would halt repairs, while holding it would keep control of a fortified bridge and allow invasion of Torres beyond the usual beachhead limit.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: Mentioned in passing: the trading post at Torfast is held up as the model for a southern trade network.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the bridge plays an important but limited role in supporting Bay of Catazar trade routes.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman is linked to Trivento by river under the proposed trade network, and a future great work boosting its mines could create a Mistress of the Bounteous Parador at Nestor's Bounty. Recent events there are cited as a warning about building under barbarian threat.

Liathaven.t: The rivers would link Liathaven to Trivento. A boost to its forests could create a similar trade title, though only if the Jotun-held territory were conquered.

Madruga.t: Madruga is cut off from Imperial armies by the broken bridge and is not in Imperial hands amid the Grendel invasion. It stands to gain restored access, a fleet-boosting wharf at Vassa's Eye and a possible Caravan Master in Calvos.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the architect of the old fortification plans, Tall Hal, was a yeofolk from Odd's End.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold is linked to Trivento by river. A future great work boosting its farms could create the Bailiff of Sarcombe Market, a rival to Meade's Grand Market.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: a historical senator for Necropolis led the opposition that defeated Emperor Giovanni's toll plan.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos holds the northern end of the bridge and its Tollkeep, who would regain toll income from the repair. Neighbouring Trivento could be expanded into a trade hub to rival Sarvos.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Torfast trading post is cited as the anchor of the Northern trade network that a southern equivalent might imitate.

Tassato.t: The damaged bridge impedes armies moving between Tassato and Madruga. Tassato would be reached by river trade from an expanded Trivento.

Dredge the Westmere.d: Proposed by Mitwold's senator and seconded by Kallavesa's, the commission cost 50 wains of weirwood, 30 wains of white granite and 30 thrones, and took six months. Henry Birchsmith supplied most of the materials and money across two seasons, with smaller donations from Watkin, Kostjya, Fintan Nighthaven and others. Once complete, it created the Alder of Meade, a Marcher Bourse position and liaison to the Tseriyn family of Faraden, elected annually by the owners of Marcher farms. It also created the Mediator of Fisk, elected by the commanders of Wintermark's military units. Meade March gained the coastal quality, and seasonal taxation from Bregasland, Kallavesa and Mitwold rose by nine thrones overall.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun is not named on the page, but it held Bregasland, one of the territories listed as contributing to the increase in taxation.

The Marches.t: Mitwold's senator proposed the motion, Marcher donors largely funded it, and the farm owners of the Marches gained the right to elect the Alder of Meade, a new mithril ministry and Bourse position.

Wintermark.t: Kallavesa's senator seconded the motion, and the commanders of Wintermark's military units gained the right to elect the Mediator of Fisk, a new ilium ministry.

Dredge the Westmere.o: In Autumn 385YE the Senate passed a motion to dredge the Westmere at Meade March in Mitwold, creating a mithril ministry in Meade and an ilium ministry in Fisk, Kallavesa, as offered by the Butterfly in Reverse wind of fortune.

Mitwold/Meade March.t: Dredging the Westmere gave Meade March the coastal quality, and the region became home to the new mithril ministry held by the Alder of Meade.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland is named among the territories sharing in the overall nine-throne seasonal rise in taxation.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa gained an ilium ministry in Fisk, held by the Mediator of Fisk, and shared in the rise in taxation.

Mitwold.t: The Westmere was dredged at Meade March in Mitwold, creating the mithril ministry of the Alder of Meade and raising the territory's taxation.

Dressed in smoke and fire.d: With the League National Assembly's endorsement, Sarvos became the City of Masks, gaining renown for elegance and couture, and the Hag Queen's doom was lifted. Fires ravaged the rebuilt Caricomare docks; the Mayor of Caricomare lost their income and Senate votes but can now buy valuable goods, and the Constitutional Court made it a national Senate appointment open to non-residents. Perhaps a hundred masks gained strange auras and became sought-after. The Mirrored Maschieri planned a 'Feast of Fools' masquerade for the Summer Solstice. Genia Bourné offered her schema-broker network if the League commissions a Brokers Office folly (30 wains each of white granite, weirwood and mithril, 180 crowns, 5 thrones upkeep), appointed annually by the Bourse; the offer lasts a year.

The League.t: The League triumphed over the Hag Queen's attempt to doom Sarvos and is invited to celebrate with a nationwide masquerade at the Summer Solstice. It also has a year to commission a Brokers Office that would let a Bourse-appointed titleholder buy schemas for mage robes, magical jewellery and ritual foci.

Dressed in smoke and fire.o: Following the Hag Queen's curse that shattered its mirrors, Sarvos completed its transformation into the City of Masks, lifting the doom over the city. Fires at Caricomare reshaped the Mayor of Caricomare title, magic settled on many Sarvosan masks, a Summer Solstice masquerade was proposed, and Genia Bourné offered a Brokers Office for buying magical schemas.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos shed the doom of its shattered mirrors to become the City of Masks, famed for fashion, while fires gutted Caricomare's docks and magical auras settled on around a hundred of its masks. The proposed Brokers Office would have to be built in the city, perhaps on the rebuilt Caricomare dockfront.

Drinking song for the socially anxious.d: Axou narcotics sellers Evander Slak and Hippolata of Kaban planned to trade outside the Forge, including more doses of Bone Dust. A Jarmish dhow, nominally commissioned by a Sarcophan merchant, docked at Spirewood Wharf in Elos offering rare spices to Urizen's finest magicians, reachable through a Sentinel Gate conjunction. A herald of Ephisis brought an Autumn trading game to the Hall of Worlds. Thule's Five Fang Consortium headed south from Otkodov seeking investment. The would-be sodality The Rising Tide sought to meet Heilyn Bronwen's Rest. The herald Venator sought to speak with Cecilia de Gauvain, and Apulian orcs, led by Merchant Prince Mahiri Kaliact, prepared to seek League citizenship.

Dawn.t: The herald Venator, who once hunted the yeofolk of House Perigord, now sought to speak peacefully with Cecilia de Gauvain in the Hall of Worlds, needing an Imperial citizen to invite him in.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Merchant Prince Mahiri Kaliact di Apulian is described as formerly the Salt Lord of Spiral.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the nation is not named, but the roads of its territory Casinea were busy with merchants heading for Anvil.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the nation is not named, though Venator was last seen in the Jade Range of its territory Kahraman, terrorising Dawnish yeofolk.

The League.t: A contingent of Apulian orcs was to camp with the League, with Mahiri Kaliact intending to swear an oath to the League's egregore and become the first of her people to take citizenship, while others sought to discuss bishops, fashion and the Test of Citizenship.

Thule.t: The Five Fang Consortium, Thule business folk, artisans and Autumn magicians with limited prospects under warlock rule, headed to Anvil seeking Imperial investment for ventures in their homeland after the end of slavery in Otkodov.

Urizen.t: A Jarmish ship moored at Spirewood Wharf in Elos sought well-placed Urizeni magicians to buy rare spices, with the Quaymaster of the Elosian Docks responsible for overseeing an expedition through the Sentinel Gate; the trade was framed to sidestep the Jarmish embargo since the seller was a Sarcophan merchant.

Drinking song for the socially anxious.o: With the Empire steeped in Autumn's power after the Spring Equinox, a host of traders, heralds and foreign visitors made their way towards Anvil for the Summer Solstice, each seeking trade, patronage or conversation with Imperial citizens.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jade Range is where Venator was last seen hunting the yeofolk of House Perigord.

Casinea.t: Casinea's roads were busy with merchants, traders and peddlers from across the Empire and beyond, all bound for the summit at Anvil.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Venator was last seen in Kahraman's Jade Range terrorising Dawnish yeofolk.

Otkodov.t: The end of slavery in Otkodov was slowly bringing change, giving rise to the Five Fang Consortium, some reportedly former slaves, who sought outside capital for projects there.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Mahiri Kaliact di Apulian, who sought League citizenship, was formerly the Salt Lord of Spiral.

Drive back.d: Defending Brocéliande required up to 30,000 strength. Military units could Slow the Vallorn for herb payment, and armies could commit up to 15,000 strength each in Boar's Dell and Elerael. Aid came from Dawnish knights, Highborn congregations, the Great Forest Orcs and the eternal Tharim. Zakalwe offered a boon, and Arhallogen and Tharim offered further help at a price. Yaw'nagrah proposed turning the vallorn against the Mallum if Brocéliande were abandoned. Full success could open a chance to clear Dark Ranging. A weirwood forest in the Westwood could be developed for 75 Thrones, with road improvements. A Senate motion to commission the Bourse seat was raised and later withdrawn.

Dawn.t: Ranae de Rondell rallied Dawnish knights-errant and questing knights to fight in Brocéliande, and Dawnish military units were offered bonus rewards for taking part.

Druj.t: The Druj presence made the route from Drycastle impractical. Yaw'nagrah offered to drive the vallorn of Béantal Dol in their lands if the Empire abandoned Brocéliande, and clearing Dark Ranging could also ease any Druj invasion of the territory.

Highguard.t: Answering the call of the Hazelelponi of the Shattered Tower, Highborn congregations sent at least 500 strength to Brocéliande. Tharim offered further aid if allowed to feed on Highguard's herb gardens and forests.

Imperial Orcs.t: A warband of Imperial Orcs discovered the weirwood forest in the Westwood during the campaign to free the region from the vallorn.

Jotun.t: The Jotun still held most of Liathaven, leaving the new weirwood forest precarious. Some urged building a fortification there to guard against their return.

Navarr.t: The Navarr faced the vallorn's strongest surge yet in Brocéliande and paid helpers in herbs. Their herb gardens suffered Tharim's black frost, and many felt Liathaven and its new weirwood should be theirs.
