Every time it rains.d: No rain fell between the Spring Equinox and the Summer Solstice, so farms everywhere faced heavy losses; only Segura, protected by the Iron Qanat, and Skarsind, protected by Spring magic, were spared. The Imperial Breadbasket could stave off famine. During the Solstice, tempest jade could substitute for mana in several Spring rituals. Thunderous Deluge, Rivers of Life, Rivers Run Red or Regrow the Land's Heart cast on Casinea would affect the whole Empire, bringing floods, renewal, sickness or vallorn activity depending on the ritual. Other opportunities involved Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea on the Semmerlak, a cheaper permanent Call Down Lightning's Wrath, and Olic the Wanderer's offer of a ritual tome.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Culwich in Weirwater would suffer serious flooding under an Empire-wide Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart. Semmerholm and Weirwater could also be targeted with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea to spread storms and farm-boosting rain around the Semmerlak.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Zenith and the Barrens, held by the Druj, are named among the non-Imperial territories that Imperial-regio rituals would not touch, leaving them simply to endure the drought.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Casinea, home of the Imperial regio, was the target through which certain rituals could be spread across the entire Empire during the conjunction.

Imperial Orcs.t: The farms of Skarsind were spared the drought thanks to the Spring enchantment placed on them at the Spring Equinox.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun-held Liathaven is named as a territory beyond the reach of the Imperial rituals, left to endure the drought.

Navarr.t: Empire-wide Rivers of Life or Rivers Run Red would energise the vallorn in Hercynia and especially Therunin, bringing more vallornspawn attacks or spreading miasma. Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart would also leave Eastring permanently marshy.

The Brass Coast.t: The farms of Segura were protected from the drought by the Iron Qanat, which kept the dry grasslands irrigated despite the crushing heat.

The League.t: Tassato faced the worst flooding if the Vassa burst its banks under Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart, and Sarvos some lesser flooding. Holberg risked flooding and Utterlund permanently becoming marsh.

The Marches.t: Marcher farms suffered the drought, though the Imperial Breadbasket's surplus and income could stave off famine and cushion Mitwold and Upwold. Meade risked serious flooding, while Bregasland, not counted as Imperial, would gain nothing from the rituals.

Thule.t: Any Empire-wide ritual would also affect the Thule orcs in their regions of Sermersuaq, Skarsind, Miekarova and Ossium, and the civil service advised the Ambassador to Otkodov to warn them, though flooding was unlikely to harm them.

Urizen.t: Olic the Wanderer offered to send the Concordance of Earthbound Stars to the Celestial Library if an Empire-wide curse ran its course, alongside an earlier offer to add it to Urizen lore for performing Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths.

Varushka.t: Karov, Karsk and Ossium were among the Semmerlak territories where Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea could be cast to batter shipping but bring farm-boosting rain to every territory around the lake.

Wintermark.t: Sermersuaq counted as an Imperial territory, so any Empire-wide curse or enchantment would reach it, including the regions held by Thule orcs there.

Every time it rains.o: In the summer of 384YE a three-month drought struck the Empire and blighted farm harvests, while a rare conjunction of the Wanderer, the Fountain, the Stallion and the Lock empowered rain, water and storm rituals during the Summer Solstice. Certain curses and enchantments cast on Casinea would spread across every Imperial territory.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Utterlund would be so saturated by an Empire-wide Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart that the Morass would spread, permanently adding the marsh quality to the forest. Hallow of the Green World cast under the conjunction would certainly have the same result.

Therunin/Eastring.t: If the Feverwater rose under an Empire-wide Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart, Eastring would permanently gain the marsh quality.

Bregasland.t: Because Bregasland could not elect a Senator that season, rituals cast through the Imperial regio would neither help nor harm it, and it had simply to endure the drought.

Brocéliande.t: As a non-Imperial territory, Brocéliande lay beyond the reach of the Imperial-regio rituals and would simply endure the drought.

Casinea.t: Casinea, where the Imperial regio lies, was the target through which Thunderous Deluge, Rivers of Life, Rivers Run Red or Regrow the Land's Heart could be spread across the whole Empire. Detect magic cast on the regio would reveal whether any had been used.

Hercynia.t: An Empire-wide Rivers of Life or Rivers Run Red would energise the vallorn in Hercynia, bringing increased vallornspawn attacks or a spread of miasma.

Holberg.t: Parts of Holberg would flood under an Empire-wide Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart. As a Semmerlak territory, it could also be targeted with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea.

Karov.t: Karov was one of the Semmerlak territories that could be targeted with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea to spread storms and farm-boosting rain around the whole lake.

Karsk.t: Karsk was one of the Semmerlak territories that could be targeted with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea to spread storms and farm-boosting rain around the whole lake.

Liathaven.t: Held by the Jotun, Liathaven was outside the reach of the Imperial-regio rituals and would simply endure the drought.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova is listed among the territories where Thule orcs hold regions that any Empire-wide ritual would also affect.

Mitwold.t: Meade risked serious flooding under Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart, though the Imperial Breadbasket's income would help Mitwold absorb a lean autumn and winter.

Ossium.t: Ossium could be targeted with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea to spread storms around the Semmerlak, and Thule orcs holding regions there would feel any Empire-wide ritual.

Otkodov.t: The civil service advised the Ambassador to Otkodov to inform the orcs there of any Empire-wide magical effects that might reach Thule-held regions within the Empire.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos faced some flooding under an Empire-wide Thunderous Deluge but was well prepared and expected to suffer minimal lasting damage.

Segura.t: Segura's farms were shielded from the drought by the Iron Qanat, which kept its grasslands irrigated through the heat.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm was one of the Semmerlak territories that could be targeted with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea to spread storms and farm-boosting rain around the whole lake.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq counted as Imperial, so any Empire-wide curse or enchantment would reach it, including the regions held by Thule orcs.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind's farms escaped the drought, receiving gentle healing rain from the Spring enchantment cast on them at the Spring Equinox.

Tassato.t: Tassato was expected to be hit worst if the Vassa burst its banks under an Empire-wide Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart, causing extensive damage to the city.

The Barrens.t: Held by the Druj, the Barrens were beyond the reach of the Imperial-regio rituals and would simply endure the drought.

Therunin.t: Therunin's vallorn would be especially energised by an Empire-wide Rivers of Life or Rivers Run Red, bringing vallornspawn attacks or spreading miasma. Flooding from the Feverwater threatened Eastring.

Upwold.t: The Imperial Breadbasket's income was expected to help Upwold absorb the shock of a lean autumn and winter after the drought.

Weirwater.t: The town of Culwich faced serious floods under Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart. As a Semmerlak territory, Weirwater could also be targeted with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea.

Zenith.t: Held by the Druj, Zenith was outside the reach of the Imperial-regio rituals and would simply endure the drought.

Everything has a price.d: Grendel ships began arriving in Imperial ports on the Bay of Catazar via Oran and Apulus, and the Treasury expected tax revenues to rise. Governor Rahab opened Oran to Imperial fleets, although sanctions in both directions cut their profits. Having lost its Druj trade, Wind Speaker Gwindhon offered mithril for weirwood through a proposed Broken Shore Mithril Market, and urged a costly embassy in Cargo for Fleet Master Esteban. Achan of the Fort Fuil Merchants of Bonds offered to trace named slaves for payment. Maistir Bradach planned to visit Anvil. An Imperial Wayleave commissioned the Mithril Market, but after Feroz was evacuated Rahab's fury withdrew every other unused opportunity.

Druj.t: Under the treaty the Grendel may no longer trade with the Druj, ending a lucrative route that had exchanged Grendel mithril for Druj weirwood. That mithril was now offered to the Empire instead.

Grendel.t: The Salt Lords, Wind Speaker Gwindhon, Achan and the Gainmeachdubh Merchant Adventurers all sought profit from the new peace, through Oran, a mithril market, an embassy, slave searches and a visit to Anvil. They faced the threat of an Imperial embargo, and Governor Rahab later withdrew the unused offers in fury.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Crown's Quay was listed as one of the southern ports where the Broken Shore Mithril Market could be built.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel acknowledged the Empire's punishing wars against the Jotun as a reason funds might be short.

The Brass Coast.t: Fleet Master Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra, as ambassador to the Broken Shore, was offered a grand embassy in Cargo and a role naming captives for Achan to trace. Freeborn enslaved in Feroz began to be returned, while corsairs objected that Oran sold Freeborn goods seized in Feroz's fall.

The League.t: Sarvos was one of the two trade hubs Gwindhon favoured for the mithril market, and Trivento received freed slaves taken during the Grendel occupation of Sarvos in 380YE.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named on the page and is linked only through the wider question of Imperial trade with the Grendel.

Everything has a price.o: In Winter 383YE, after the Senate ratified a peace treaty recognising the Grendel as foreigners, the Grendel offered the Empire a series of trade opportunities: an open port at Oran, a mithril-for-weirwood market, a grand embassy and paid searches for enslaved citizens. Some citizens called for an embargo instead.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though the herbs sold at Oran were said to be native to Feroz.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The port of Oran was opened to Imperial fleets on Governor Rahab's orders, offering herbs, liao and luxuries subject to stern tariffs. Some corsairs urged captains to shun it, or called for an embargo.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Mentioned in passing: Crown's Quay was listed among the southern ports that could host the Broken Shore Mithril Market.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though Sarvos was one of the hubs suggested for the mithril market and Trivento received returned slaves.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Apulus served as the eastern route for Grendel vessels, which disposed of any slaves there before sailing on into Imperial waters.

Bay of Catazar.t: Grendel vessels began arriving at Imperial ports on the bay, coming via Oran and Apulus, and trade across its waters slowly grew.

Feroz.t: Governor Rahab opened the port at Oran to Imperial fleets, selling Feroz herbs and seized liao, and Freeborn enslaved during the invasion began to be returned. After the evacuation of Feroz, Rahab's fury ended the unused opportunities.

Madruga.t: The first freed Freeborn slaves were escorted over the border into Siroc by Stone Born, and Siroc was named as a possible site for the mithril market.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Crown's Quay was suggested as one possible port for the Broken Shore Mithril Market.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named on the page and is attached only through the wider Grendel trade situation.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos was proposed as a site for the mithril market, and groups of former slaves taken during the 380YE occupation were delivered to Trivento each month under the treaty.

Spiral.t: Grendel ships reached Imperial waters by way of Apulus, unloading slaves there first. An embargo would have serious implications for relations with Salt Lord Kaliact.

Everything has rhythm.d: In Spiral, Iron Helms soldiers driven mad by the Black Plateau roamed Ossuary, and the Grendel arranged to hand over Dogri Thulebane's body at Blue Haven. Jotun Raðljóst who had found the Pride of Ikka's Tears mithril mine had to be stopped in Suaq Wastes. Grendel moridun fortified Free Landing. Feni raiders spread from Upwold into the Mournwold. Husks and merrow mages crossed the East Floes. Surut asked the Navarr to bring Winter's Flame to two vallorn regio in West Ranging. A warlock-led warband, possibly Thule, raided Volodmartz mines. A rescue of at least two hundred Highborn prisoners was possible at Ceramic Meander in Zenith. Each was an opportunity, not a settled outcome.

Druj.t: Chikad warriors guarded the Ceramic Meander camp holding Highborn prisoners, where a Tepel apothecary poisoned one captive each day, while Druj warbands took selected prisoners towards the Barrens.

Grendel.t: Speaker Morna arranged to return Dogri Thulebane's remains at Blue Haven. In Madruga, elite moridun organised leftover raiders and pirates behind new defences, and Imperial conjunctions were set to strike them.

Highguard.t: Highborn soldiers captured during the retreat from Zenith faced brutal treatment, and a rescue could return at least two hundred to the Granite Pillar, Valiant Pegasus and Seventh Wave. The Citadel Guard's camp in Spiral was also threatened by frenzied soldiers.

Jotun.t: Raðljóst pathfinders who had discovered the Imperial mithril mine were heading back to their Jarls in two bands. Prognosticators warned the find might redirect the Jotun invasion north towards Suaq Wastes and Suaq Fount.

Navarr.t: Surut's heralds asked the Navarr to keep leading his fires against the vallorn, wanting Brennos Brackensong, general of the Quiet Step, to be the focus of Winter's Flame at both West Ranging regio.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn corsairs had helped liberate Lightsea and Free Landing in Madruga. Conjunctions offered a chance to break the Grendel redoubts so Imperial forces could swiftly retake the Free Landing islands.

The Marches.t: Marcher lands faced spreading Feni raids through Upwold and into the Mournwold, and the Towerjacks' camp in Spiral was threatened by frenzied soldiers. Marchers had also fought in Madruga and were asked to join the Navarr against the vallorn.

Thule.t: An orc and husk warband led by a warlock raiding Volodmartz mines strongly appeared to be Thule, though it was unconfirmed and was unusually not taking slaves.

Urizen.t: The Winter Sun's camp in Ossuary was among those threatened by the frenzied Iron Helms. Urizen egregores identified the conjunction to Blue Haven for Dogri Thulebane's handover.

Varushka.t: About a hundred Iron Helms soldiers succumbed to the Black Plateau's Night Magic and became murderous bands, and Varushkans might wish to deal with them. Volodmartz also suffered raids on its mines.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark was offered the return of Dogri Thulebane's body and the chance to protect the mithril mine held by seat holder Algar of Ashenhall. It also faced husks rising on the East Floes, while the Feni threat in Hahnmark seemed to have eased.

Everything has rhythm.o: Before the Spring Equinox 382YE, the civil service listed nine sets of Sentinel Gate conjunctions offering Anvil's heroes chances to act across the Empire. They ranged from frenzied soldiers in Spiral and Jotun scouts near a mithril mine to Feni raiders, risen husks, vallorn regio and a Druj slave camp.

Hahnmark/Southridge.t: Feni attacks crossed into the hills of Southridge about a month after the Winter Solstice but have since abated significantly.

Hahnmark/Wood Heath.t: The Winter Solstice attempt to strike the Feni warband here failed, and its raids continued before spreading into Southridge.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: Conjunctions to Silent Stand and Far Steading offered battle against vallorn husks and creatures amid a venomous miasma. Success at both would give the Empire control of the whole region.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: Mentioned in passing: success in West Ranging would let Imperial forces push into Westwood without fear for their supply lines.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Grendel moridun built redoubts and stockades on the islands, and conjunctions to Summer's Stone at Halcorim, Estavia's Key and the Isle of Seven Goats offered a chance to drive them back.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: Mentioned in passing: its liberation from the Grendel was described as swift and decisive.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: A conjunction to Connor's Rock offered a chance to stop the Feni as their raids pushed westwards into the Chalkdowns.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: Several thrall farms in Freemoor were thoroughly sacked by Feni raiders.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: Husks rose from the lakes, accompanied by living merrow mages, and two large conjunctions to Iqaluit Rise and Pangnirtung Station offered battle against them.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Prognosticators suggested the mithril find might draw the Jotun invasion away from populous Sealtoq.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun armies had crossed into Stark, and one band of pathfinders was returning to them there.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: Prognosticators suggested the Jotun might divert their invasion north to claim Suaq Fount because of the mithril.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: Jotun pathfinders could be intercepted at West Bay and Bitter Tundra, and none were to be left alive so the Jarls would not learn of the mithril mine. The Jotun might yet turn north to claim the region.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun armies were in Tanikipari, and one band of pathfinders was returning towards them.

Spiral/Apulus.t: The Grendel funeral escort waited at Blue Haven, a cove in south-eastern Apulus, to hand over Dogri Thulebane's remains to a small Imperial party.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: Frenzied Iron Helms soldiers roamed Ossuary threatening Imperial camps, and conjunctions to the Nephan Traps offered a chance to intercept them by calming, subduing or killing them.

Spiral/Screed.t: The Black Plateau had awoken, and Night Magic pouring out of Screed drove soldiers to madness.

Upwold/Ashbrook.t: Homesteads, monasteries and market towns in Ashbrook were targeted by the growing Feni warband.

Upwold/Birchland.t: The Feni warband here survived a failed Solstice strike and swelled to the equivalent of two or three military units.

Upwold/Tower March.t: Homesteads, monasteries and market towns in Tower March were targeted by the spreading Feni raids.

Volodmartz/Brez.t: The raiding warband was last seen heading towards the White Granite mine at Veltsgorsk in Brez.

Volodmartz/Opascari.t: A conjunction for fifteen people opened to the road near the Granites of Veltsgorsk, listed under Opascari, to confront the warlock's warband.

Zenith/Iteri.t: Conjunctions to the Ceramic Meander Slave Camp and Ceramic Meadows offered a chance to distract and hold off the Chikad while Highborn prisoners escaped.

Hahnmark.t: The Feni raids that troubled Wood Heath spread into Southridge but have since largely abated, for reasons still unclear.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: named as the territory next to Sealtoq, which a Jotun shift north might spare.

Liathaven.t: Two conjunctions to the remaining Spring regio in West Ranging offered the chance to burn them with Surut's flame, weaken the vallorn and secure a beachhead in the territory.

Madruga.t: After Lightsea and Free Landing were liberated, Grendel moridun dug in remaining raiders behind defences, and three conjunctions offered a chance to clear them.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: Blue Haven, the handover point for Dogri Thulebane's body, lies near the border with Mareave.

Mournwold.t: Feni raids crossed into the Mournwold, sacking thrall farms. If they were not stopped at Connor's Rock, every farm and business there would lose 36 rings and every herb garden two herbs.

Sermersuaq.t: Jotun pathfinders who found the mithril mine could be intercepted in Suaq Wastes, while husks accompanied by living merrow mages marched inland across the East Floes.

Spiral.t: The Black Plateau awoke in Screed, driving Imperial soldiers mad and turning some Iron Helms into killers in Ossuary. Apulus hosted the handover of Dogri Thulebane's remains.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Druj slave parties were thought to be taking a circuitous route around Therunin to the Barrens.

Upwold.t: The Feni warband in Birchland swelled to two or three units and raided homesteads, monasteries and market towns across Ashbrook and Tower March.

Volodmartz.t: A warlock-led warband of orcs and husks, possibly Thule, raided mine caravans for gold, gems and orichalcum, and a conjunction offered a chance to confront it near Veltsgorsk.

Zenith.t: Highborn prisoners were held at a Druj camp in Iteri, and two conjunctions offered a chance to rescue them across the Utique.

Everything is broken.d: Dawnish scouts contacted Houses Robar and Garland, who asked for weapons, armour and mithril. Prognosticators advised patience, but the Hounds' sacrifice sparked a rising, and contact with the rebels was lost as the Druj counter-attacked. On the Sunday of the summit the Empire could strike Dharrik Bonebite's force at Merigionne. Killing enough of it would let the rebels take Dawnguard and give the Empire the Barrens. Other objectives were to kill Bonebite, save the captive Rousers of Glory from sacrifice to Agramant, and cast The Basalt Citadel with Sorin's boon. Senators could move early to assign the territory, a choice with risks either way.

Dawn.t: Dawn mourned and celebrated the Hounds of Glory, and its Assembly was urged to propose a fitting memorial rather than re-raise the army. Its kin in the Barrens rose in revolt, and the Dawnish there would be furious if the territory went to any other nation.

Druj.t: Reeling from the loss of the Spires of Dusk, the Druj under Serra Grubfeast sent Dharrik Bonebite to crush the Dawnish rebels and sacrifice captive troubadours for Agramant's aid. Plaguetouch sent another force to slaughter the Rahvin at the Fangs, while holdouts raised slain Imperial soldiers to spread terror.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; its only link is the Castellan of Spiral Castle, who was tasked with recovering Gyre's Edge.

Everything is broken.o: After the Hounds of Glory died capturing the Spires of Dusk, the Dawnish in the Barrens rose in open revolt against the Druj, ending the Empire's careful plans to arm them first. The Military Council was offered a Sentinel Gate battle at the Merigionne Estate that could win the Barrens, along with several smaller conjunctions.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: Mentioned in passing: Bitter Strand is listed among the regions the Empire had taken from the Druj.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: The Druj gathered their forces and counter-attacked the Dawnish rebels in Murderdale as well as Dawnguard, cutting off all contact with them.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: Now taken from the Druj, Saltmarsh was the destination of a conjunction to Hadrienne's Lament, where the Champion of Ambition was to recover the Goblet of Adelmar from the undead remains of Hadrienne de Deveou's retinue.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the yeofolk of Ville Deleroi in Semmerholm asked the Dean of Laroc Cathedral to lay their extinct house's knights to rest at Bloodrun Dell.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Castellan of Spiral Castle, Maryc, was made responsible for recovering House de Casillon's ancestral blade, Gyre's Edge.

The Barrens.t: Dawnish houses and yeofolk across the Barrens rose against the Druj. A victory at Merigionne would let the rebels seize Dawnguard and bring the territory under Imperial control, ready for the Senate to assign.

Everything is on show.d: The Senate approved the army at the Winter Solstice 386YE on Cesare's motion, seconded by Aspar, with most of the funding from Empress Vesna Borkovna Prochnost. Eighteen months later, its recruits from all five League cities were finishing at the Five Cities Military Academy. Cesare could choose Conquering, Fast or Resourceful at no extra cost, and the army gained the Resourceful quality, letting it resupply anywhere, even under attack. Its creation swelled Pride in Tassato, whose new army would rival Holberg's Towerjacks and the Wolves of War. Lingering effects of the Hammers of Fury enchantment also made the Chain shine over Tassato, giving local artisans and cambions brief benefits at the summit.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Gryphon's Pride, raised as conquerors for Dawnish ambitions in the Barrens, was cited as the model for the Conquering option, which was not chosen.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks are remembered for spending three decades on Holberg's walls keeping the Druj out.

The League.t: The League gained its third army, the Sparrows Reckoning, drawn from all five cities and made Resourceful. Its ambitious, hot-headed soldiers are eager to prove themselves the equals of the Wolves of War and the Towerjacks.

Everything is on show.o: In Summer 388YE the League's third army, raised in Tassato and named Sparrows Reckoning by Senator Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato, neared the end of its training, and Cesare was asked to choose its quality. It became a Resourceful army.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's fame for the Towerjacks' thirty-three-year siege is the reputation Tassato's proud citizens now hope their new army will rival.

Tassato.t: Tassato gained its first army of its own, swelling the city's Pride. Lingering Hammers of Fury magic made the Chain shine brightly overhead, letting local artisans refresh a bonded item and cambions gain a temporary hero point at the summit.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish ambitions in the Barrens are referred to as the reason the Gryphon's Pride were raised as conquerors.

Everything is trying to kill us.d: Imperial and Druj armies were still fighting over the Sarangrave. A Vigilant fervour, inspired by Urizen's victory over the recidivist sword scholars, let the Urizen Assembly pick one problem and one archetype each summit. The investigators would not solve the problem themselves but would bring forward opportunities the following season; appraisals could speed this up. The problems were a hostile populace with rebels holding Nesustak Forest, a venomous lowland marsh where ushabti cannot work, miasma pillars in all but one region, and little Urizeni appetite to settle. Irra Harah was also stirring the rebels, a huge vallornheart was walled up by Druj wards, and Kroll's Spring guardian had been defeated but not slain.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish Assembly's judgement inviting the rebel septs to break bread with them appears to have gone unnoticed, and the bloody legacy of the Barrens feeds the Sarangrave's hostility towards the Empire.

Druj.t: The Druj were still campaigning to retake the Sarangrave. Their hidden miasma pillars, lifelong propaganda, walled-up vallornheart and the fed monster of Kroll were all burdens left for the Empire.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel-held Mareave is referred to in the opening dialogue as an arid land.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: their sept-by-sept approach to settling Mareave is held up as the model Urizen should follow.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the text notes that even a Bregas might balk at moving to the Sarangrave.

Navarr.t: Urizen had committed to working with the Navarr towards destroying the vallorn. The Navarr were named as the best source of aid against the Sarangrave's vallornheart, especially if their national assembly offered support.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's loss of Spiral is described as the reason the Sarangrave felt like a consolation prize.

Urizen.t: Urizen took on the Sarangrave and faced years of costly work to make it prosper. Its Assembly could set one archetype each season to investigate the territory's many problems.

Everything is trying to kill us.o: After the Senate assigned the Sarangrave to Urizen, the nation faced a host of obstacles to making the Druj-scarred swamp a prosperous territory. The Urizen Assembly was given the opportunity to direct one named archetype each season, by a statement of principle upheld with a greater majority, to investigate one of these problems.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: Kroll's giant octopus-like guardian, believed to be a Druj-fed creature of the Spring realm, was defeated but not slain and was expected to return to hunt when hungry.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: Rebel septs aided by Irra Harah controlled Nesustak Forest. They were fighting the Druj but were no friends of the Empire.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Bregas are invoked as people who might still balk at the Sarangrave's marshes.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: Mareave serves as the precedent for incorporating a newly won orc-populated territory, and is described as arid.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is not named; it is covered only by the general point that Urizen's mountain spires are a world away from the Sarangrave.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen curses unleashed here without regard for the inhabitants are cited as fuel for Druj propaganda.

Sarangrave.t: The newly Urizen territory was still contested and faced many problems: hostile inhabitants, deadly marshland, miasma pillars, few willing settlers, Irra Harah's meddling, a caged vallornheart and the monster of Kroll.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen displaced from Spiral are cited as weary of moving again, and its loss frames the Sarangrave as a consolation prize.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the bloodshed of the Barrens is cited as a warning, and its tragedies shape how Sarangrave's people see the Empire.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen forced from Zenith are among those tired of resettling.

Excavate Gildenheim Runeforge.d: Proposed by the Bastion senator and seconded by the Kallavesa senator, the motion followed the Conduit to Destiny wind of fortune. It authorised the careful transport, preservation and removal of the Gildenheim runeforge ruins to Runegrott, Hahnmark. The work required 12 thrones in labour costs and three months. After the Winter Solstice Baal provided 11 thrones and Richardo Glostari di Sarvos provided 1 throne, meeting the cost. Once the excavation is complete, building a runeforge in Runegrott will need 30 fewer wains of white granite and 60 fewer crowns.

Wintermark.t: The Senate formally recognised Wintermark's runesmiths as the rightful heirs of the old runeforge, bringing its remains under their care for a future runeforge in Runegrott.

Excavate Gildenheim Runeforge.o: In Winter 383YE the Senate passed a motion confirming the runesmiths of Wintermark as rightful heirs of the Gildenheim runeforge, allowing its ruins to be excavated and moved to Runegrott in Hahnmark.

Hahnmark.t: The salvaged ruins are to be brought to Runegrott in Hahnmark, where they will cut the cost of building a runeforge there by 30 wains of white granite and 60 crowns.

Excavate Holberg Embankment.d: The motion sought the Senate's permission to dig a deep embankment before the Walls of Holberg. It stated that the work needed no commission and would not raise the upkeep of the walls. It cost 500 thrones and was to take twelve months to build. The motion passed. Funding came from many individual citizens between Winter 385YE and Summer 387YE. The largest donors were Lula and Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund, with Morgan Townsend von Holberg giving 100 thrones in Summer 387YE. Once finished, the Walls of Holberg will become a rank 6 fortification.

The League.t: The League's great city gained Senate approval to strengthen its defences, and many League citizens, especially of Holberg, paid for the work out of their own purses.

Excavate Holberg Embankment.o: In Winter 385YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the Citizens' Voice, to excavate a deep embankment in front of the Walls of Holberg, as described in the opportunity from "The greatest city in the world" Wind of Fortune.

Holberg.t: A deep embankment is to be excavated before the Walls of Holberg, raising them to a rank 6 fortification once complete, with no increase in their upkeep.

Expand Academy of Arms.d: Proposed by the senator for Redoubt and seconded by Madruga, the commission followed the Build up my body Wind of Fortune. It cost 25 wains of white granite, 50 crowns in labour and three months to build. The new title, Prelate of Adelmar's Shrine, grants 10 liao, 20 Synod votes and one free upgrade of a basic military unit each season. Materials and money came from several citizens, many of them of the Lighthouse-That-Was and the Astral Observatory, including Laelius Webworker, Spyridonakes, Limonos and others. With construction complete, the Assembly of Ambition would make the first appointment at the Summer Solstice 385YE.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Redoubt gained an expanded Academy of Arms, largely funded with white granite and coin from Urizeni citizens of the Lighthouse-That-Was and the Astral Observatory, and a new Synod title tied to military training.

Expand Academy of Arms.o: In Spring 385YE the Senate passed a motion commissioning the expansion of the Academy of Arms in Siluri, Redoubt, creating the title Prelate of Adelmar's Shrine. The work was completed, and the Assembly of Ambition was to appoint the first holder at the Summer Solstice.

Redoubt/Siluri.t: The Academy of Arms in Siluri was expanded, creating Adelmar's Shrine, whose prelate can upgrade a basic military unit for free each season.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt's senator proposed the expansion of the Academy of Arms within the territory, and it was built there to house the new Prelate of Adelmar's Shrine.

Expand Breadbasket into Mournwold.d: Proposed by the senator for Mournwold and seconded by Weirwater, the motion called for 39 wains of weirwood, 19 wains of white granite and 174 crowns in labour costs, with six months to complete. Materials and money came from many contributors after the Spring Equinox and Summer Solstice, notably Orson BogMyrtle, Mel Bleak, the Alders of Hay and Wayford, and Stockwater Monastery. Once complete, every farm in the Mournwold gains an additional 36 rings each season from the Winter Solstice 388YE, and the Marcher ability to support armies rises by one once Bregasland returns to Marcher hands. The Keeper's Cottage gives the Keeper of the Breadbasket 12 crowns a season.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, but the extra Marcher army support depends on Bregasland, which they held at the time, returning to Marcher hands.

The Marches.t: Marcher senators drove the motion and Marcher citizens largely paid for it, gaining richer Mournwold farms, an income for the Keeper of the Breadbasket and, once Bregasland is recovered, the capacity to support one more army.

Expand Breadbasket into Mournwold.o: The Senate passed a motion in Spring 388YE commissioning the Mournwold expansion of the Breadbasket great work, along with the Keeper's Cottage sinecure in Maiden Downs, Mitwold, following the Search high and low Wind of Fortune.

Mitwold/Maiden Downs.t: Maiden Downs is the site of the newly built Keeper's Cottage, the sinecure that funds the Keeper of the Breadbasket.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the Breadbasket's boost to Marcher army support only takes effect once Bregasland is back in Marcher hands.

Mitwold.t: The Keeper's Cottage sinecure is built in Mitwold, giving the Keeper of the Breadbasket 12 crowns a season from the Winter Solstice 388YE.

Mournwold.t: The Breadbasket great work is expanded into the Mournwold, granting every farm there an additional 36 rings each season from the Winter Solstice 388YE.

Expand College of Warcasting.d: Passed in Spring 384YE, the motion commissioned work on the College of Warcasting in Skarsind at a cost of 12 wains of weirwood, 24 crowns in labour and three months of construction. After the Spring Equinox, Bloodcrow Yargol supplied 3 thrones and 4 wains of weirwood, and Ashborn Vana, Ghillihg, Zerk and Ringforge Kerath each supplied 2 wains. Once complete, the Preceptor gains custody of a ministry provided by the Tamazi orcs. Although the motion's text named the Bourse voting style, the recorded outcome is that the Preceptor is now chosen by Tally of the Votes, cast by Imperial Orc military unit owners who supported an Imperial army in the previous year.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Preceptor of the Warcaster College now answers to Imperial Orc military unit owners who have supported an Imperial army, giving the nation's fighting bands a direct say in the title, while Imperial Orc citizens supplied the weirwood and money for the work.

Expand College of Warcasting.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by Skarsind's senator and seconded by Weirwater's, to expand the Warcaster College of Skarsind, giving its Preceptor custody of a ministry and changing how the title is appointed. The opportunity arose from the Tired of sleeping Wind of Fortune.

Skarsind.t: The College of Warcasting in Skarsind is being expanded with a ministry provided by the Tamazi orcs, placed in the custody of its Preceptor once the three months of construction are complete.

Expand Mana Ministries.d: The motion took up the opportunity described in the Honey and Vinegar Wind of Fortune to upgrade the League's mana ministries, which serve the grandmasters of the Conclave orders. It passed at 200 thrones. The listed costs were 60 wains of mithril and 120 crowns in labour, with six months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Oscuro Kira di Tassato gave 2 thrones, and Richardo Glostari di Sarvos and Catellus di Tassato-Regario gave 1 throne each. After the Summer Solstice, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato gave 60 wains of mithril and 11 thrones. Once complete, each grandmaster will have more mana available.

The League.t: The League's three mana ministries were chosen for upgrade. League citizens from Tassato and Sarvos provided the thrones and mithril recorded towards the work.

Expand Mana Ministries.o: In Spring 384YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Tassato and seconded by Astolat, to fund upgrades to the mana ministries in Tassato, Sarvos and Temeschwar. The upgrades would expand how much crystal mana the Conclave grandmasters can buy.

Sarvos.t: The mana ministry in Sarvos was one of the three to be upgraded, and Richardo Glostari di Sarvos contributed a throne towards the work.

Tassato.t: Tassato's senator proposed the motion and its mana ministry was among those to be upgraded. Citizens styled di Tassato supplied most of the recorded funding and all 60 wains of mithril.

Temeschwar.t: The mana ministry in Temeschwar was one of the three to be upgraded, increasing the mana available to the grandmasters it serves.

Expand Pride of Ikka's Tears Autumn 387Y.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by Mournwold, the motion took up an opportunity from the Metal and stone Wind of Fortune. The expansion cost 250 thrones and takes six months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox the money was provided almost entirely by Lumi Warmthbringer and Vauraus Korppitkotka, who each gave 124 thrones 7 crowns, with Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven adding a crown apiece. Once finished, the Pride of Ikka's Tears will produce an additional five wains of mithril each season, while its upkeep rises by two thrones per season.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's senator for Sermersuaq proposed the motion, and the expanded mine in Wintermark's land will yield five more wains of mithril per season once complete, at two thrones more upkeep.

Expand Pride of Ikka's Tears Autumn 387Y.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 387YE to expand the Pride of Ikka's Tears mithril mine in Suaq Fount by sinking a deep shaft and galleries, funded directly rather than through a commission.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: Suaq Fount is home to the Pride of Ikka's Tears, where a deep shaft and new galleries are being dug to raise the mine's mithril output by five wains per season.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq's senator championed the expansion of the territory's great mithril mine, which will deepen its workings with a new shaft and galleries over six months.

Expand the Kruidenkenner Magazjin.d: Proposed by Segura and seconded by Madruga, the motion took up the Kruidenkenner guild of herbalists' opportunity, available for the last season. It created no new titles but enhanced the ministries of the High Herbalist of Sybella, the Master of the Clearing House, the Vizier of the Incarnadine Satchel and the Kruidenkenner Trademaster. The civilian commission cost 24 wains of weirwood and 48 crowns in labour and took three months. Dino i Riqueza provided 6 thrones and the 24 wains of weirwood after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the High Herbalist, the Master of the Clearing House and the Trademaster gained a ministry for buying Sarcophan herbs. The Vizier also gained one, but the Senate must first establish new offices as described in the To curb those raging appetites Wind of Fortune.

Highguard.t: Highguard's High Herbalist of Sybella saw their ministry significantly enhanced, gaining access to herbs bought from the Sarcophans through the expanded Magazjin in Highguard's own territory of Necropolis.

Expand the Kruidenkenner Magazjin.o: In Autumn 383YE the Senate passed a motion to expand the Kruidenkenner Magazjin at Crown's Quay in Necropolis. The expansion was completed shortly before the Winter Solstice 383YE and gave several Imperial ministries access to herbs bought from the Sarcophans.

Necropolis.t: The Kruidenkenner Magazjin at Crown's Quay in Necropolis was expanded and completed shortly before the Winter Solstice 383YE, becoming the base for an Imperial herb trade with the Sarcophans.

Exploit Tassatan Hills.d: Proposed by the senator for Tassato and seconded by Mitwold, the motion took advantage of the opportunity in the Light upon the Water wind of fortune, presented by Gemma Stewart of Tassato on behalf of the city's mining guilds. With the guilds' help the ilium seat cost only 75 Thrones and three months to complete. A single motion both created the seat and made it a League national position. Small donations came from Fintan Nighthaven, Otmar van Holberg, Laurencio Lemmini di Sarvos and Nikolai Dravi, while Arsenio Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato provided the bulk, 74 thrones 4 crowns, after Spring Equinox 385YE. The Tassatan Hills were then complete.

The League.t: The League gained a new national bourse position producing ilium, its holder appointed by a Tally of the Votes of League business owners.

Exploit Tassatan Hills.o: In Winter 384YE the Senate approved funding to exploit the hills above Tassato, creating a new ilium-producing bourse seat assigned as a League national position chosen by a Tally of the Votes of business owners. The project was completed after the Spring Equinox 385YE.

Tassato.t: The hills above Tassato were opened up for ilium extraction with the help of the city's mining guilds, with Tassato's senator proposing the motion and Arsenio Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato funding most of the cost.

Extend Iron Roads.d: Proposed by the senator for Ossium and seconded by Volodmartz, the motion took up the opportunity set out in the Thousands or more wind of fortune. Because Ossium is under-developed, labour costs rose by two-fifths, giving a requirement of 70 wains of white granite and 140 crowns in labour, plus six months of construction beyond the main Iron Roads project. From Autumn 383YE to Winter 384YE, contributions of granite and thrones came from several donors, most of all Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov. Once complete, the roads will function as a great work and remove a negative quality from one of Ossium's regions, depending on the situation at the time.

Varushka.t: Varushkan senators for Ossium and Volodmartz proposed and seconded the extension. Varushkans such as Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov supplied much of the white granite to bring the Iron Roads into their lands.

Extend Iron Roads.o: In Spring 384YE the Senate passed a motion, at a cost of 128 thrones, to extend the Iron Roads project into Ossium and to request the funds needed to do so.

Ossium.t: Ossium is to receive its own stretch of the Iron Roads, though its under-developed state made the labour dearer. When finished, the roads should lift a negative quality from one of its regions.

Fade out again.d: Irada von Temeschwar and Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti carried mandates to root out the Vyig. Once fear of reprisal broke, accusations flushed them out across the League, and Varushka barred its doors against them. The purge cost Sorensdromen, Travy Mudrosti and Drusilla's Obelus, all destroyed, and the Vereski Stzena were slaughtered in retaliation. Confiscated businesses in Temeschwar, Holberg and Karsk await new owners. Fleeing Vyig joined Druj forces, opening conjunctions at Elsbeth's Well and Drusilla's Farm. In Metri the Rod and Shield ended the haunting. The Grand Enchantrix and her Spites remain, however, with a conjunction to Agnieszka's Grove offering the chance to finish them.

Druj.t: Raids revealed that the Vyig had long smuggled bite into the Empire from Druj lands. Druj forces now protect fleeing Vyig in Utterlund and the Barrens, and Druj valuables are said to have been seized.

The League.t: The League drove the Vyig from its cities through dawn raids and street battles, though Valentin von Temeschwar's call for mercy was ignored. Confiscated Vyig businesses in Temeschwar and Holberg are now available to new owners.

Thule.t: Thule trade through Metri was never disrupted, because the northern orcs propitiate the Mirror of Spite whenever her servants appear. They had assumed the creatures were part of a Temeschwari deal with the Thrice-cursed Court.

Varushka.t: Following Velko Perunovich Razoradze's mandate, Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti ensured every Varushkan door was barred to the Vyig, leaving them nowhere to flee. Travy Mudrosti was razed, and confiscated Vyig holdings in Karsk passed to Vaclav.

Fade out again.o: Spurred by mandates in the League and Varushkan assemblies, magistrates and their allies purged the Vyig from the League and Varushka in Spring 385YE, uncovering their bite-smuggling links with the Druj. Meanwhile the Rod and Shield cleared the Hag Queen's beasts from the woods of Metri.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Vyig thieves stole Misericorde's Blade, a Sand Fisher symbol of resistance against the Druj. The Sand Fishers asked Merchant Prince Jonah Yakovitch to recover it and promised to pay well.

Holberg/The Morass.t: Drusilla's Obelus, used by the Vyig to smuggle bite since its creation, was burned to the ground. A conjunction to Drusilla's Farm was assigned to Irada von Temeschwar to deal with the Vyig and their Druj escort.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: The Sand Fisher scout Grey Tooth tracked the Vyig thieves to Elsbeth's Well, where they met orcs of the Mallum. A conjunction opens there to recover the stolen blade.

Temeschwar/Metri.t: The Rod and Shield slaughtered the Hag Queen's beasts, ending the haunting and the disruption to trade. The Grand Enchantrix and her Spites remain, and Grandmaster Sakari Nightscale is responsible for a conjunction to Agnieszka's Grove to deal with them.

Holberg.t: A bar brawl in Holberg became a week-long street battle between bravo gangs, and the Sorensdromen forest, used as a bite dead-drop, burned down. A Holberg herb garden was razed, a rank three business was confiscated, and citizens may request new businesses here without the usual two-crown fee.

Karsk.t: A herb garden in Karsk was razed by the Vyig to hide its contents. A rank three forest and a rank three herb garden, both formerly Vyig-owned, were confiscated and their deeds given to Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti.

Temeschwar.t: Two running battles against the Vyig were fought through Temeschwar's streets. Rank four and rank two businesses were confiscated and given to Irada von Temeschwar, and new businesses may be requested here without the two-crown fee.

The Barrens.t: The Vyig had been smuggling bite out of the Barrens. Druj who crossed the border there now escort fleeing Vyig through the territory towards the port of Leen.

Faded from the winter.d: Dreams sent to briars, traced to the magicians of Urizen's Greenfountain Spire, failed thanks to Synod judgements against briar prejudice and for vigilance. Skirmish opportunities arose against a Spire band at Beaten Branch Wayhouse in Therunin, and against the Varushkan Cabal of the Green Mother, blamed for the Rivers Run Red curse, at Gildenroad in Hercynia. Two further strikes targeted Heirs: the Fellorich Striding at Needlestead, holding a stolen heirloom, and the Greenstride Steading at Tower's Edge Holt, holding captive Winter vates. Scouts at the Liathaven spy network could probe the Heirs' leadership. The Senate ordered magistrates to investigate Yaw'nagrah's cults, causing widespread disruption.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Grey Pilgrims supported the forces fighting the Heirs, tipped off scouts to the Twisting Hive in Summersend, and brought word of the captive Frozen Steps coven at Tower's Edge Holt.

Jotun.t: The Jotun held at least two northern regions of Liathaven, battered by both the war with the Empire and the vallorn; a large scouting force there might learn how they were responding to the Heirs.

Navarr.t: The Heirs were disaffected Navarr, many of them briars, and Navarr lands bore the brunt; vates, stridings and steadings were offered chances to free captive vates and recover the Promise of Home, which could lead to the lost Vate's Shelter.

Urizen.t: The Greenfountain Spire, a Urizeni spire drawing disaffected briars, was identified as the source of the Yaw'nagrah dreams, and its magi and sentinels marched openly with vallornspawn under Agrippina of Green Fountain.

Varushka.t: The Cabal of the Green Mother, Varushkan schlacta and cabalists from Miechernya calling themselves the Twisting Hive under Roman Andrevich, was blamed for laying the illegal Rivers Run Red curse.

Faded from the winter.o: In winter 383YE the Heirs of Terunael and their Yaw'nagrah-aligned allies, beaten back in Hercynia and Therunin, were left exposed, and the Silent Bell's findings opened opportunities to strike at them. The Senate chose to have magistrates root out the cults of Yaw'nagrah within the Empire.

Hercynia/Northpines.t: Fenella Fellorich's striding, linked to many attacks in the territory, was located at a hideaway in Needlestead, offering a chance to kill her and recover the stolen Promise of Home.

Hercynia/Summersend.t: The Twisting Hive and a herald of Yaw'nagrah were found in Summersend and could be confronted at Gildenroad; the Marshstalker Steading's wayhouse there had been raided by the Fellorich.

Morrow/Peregro.t: The Greenfountain Spire is said to lie hidden in Peregro's mountain pine forests, and its magicians were blamed for the dreams sent to briars across the Empire.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: A Sentinel Gate conjunction near Beaten Branch Wayhouse offered the chance to confront the Greenfountain Spire band and kill its powerful magicians.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: The Greenfountain band vanished into the vallorn miasma of Sweetglades, then emerged openly serving Yaw'nagrah alongside spawn, ettercaps and husks.

Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley.t: At Tower's Edge Holt the Greenstride Steading held the Frozen Steps coven captive, forcing them to find ways to shield vallornspawn from Winter magic, and the Empire had a chance to free them and kill Clevorn Greenstride.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: the Heirs of Terunael are said to have previously tried to stir the vallorn here.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia, freed from Rivers Run Red by the Brackensongs' Rivers of Life, saw opportunities to confront the Cabal of the Green Mother at Gildenroad and the Fellorich Striding at Needlestead.

Liathaven.t: Liathaven was named as the source and refuge of the Heirs, where defeated members fled; stationing scouts at its spy network before the Spring Equinox could reveal their leadership.

Morrow.t: The Greenfountain Spire, hidden in Morrow's Peregro, was revealed as the source of the briar dreams, and a band of its magi and sentinels left Morrow for Therunin.

Therunin.t: Therunin, saved from Rivers Run Red by the Great Forest Orcs, faced a Greenfountain Spire band with vallornspawn and the Greenstride Steading holding captive vates, and both became targets for Imperial strikes.

Volodmartz.t: The Cabal of the Green Mother, which cursed Hercynia in Yaw'nagrah's name, was said to come from northern Volodmartz, with its cabalists from Miechernya.

Fading like a Flower.d: Madruga had already fallen to Grendel and Asavean invaders. Blightheart gained the blighted quality: no army can conquer it, and nothing lives there. The Spring rains holding the blight back are fading, and they cannot easily be renewed with Madruga cut off from the Imperial regio. Of four Dry Patricians seen entering the blight in Summer, three emerged in bone-white robes bearing the runes Yoorn, Hunger and Wisdom, leading cadres poised to advance when the rains stop. Options included Conclave orders investigating or seeking foreign aid, a Senate appraisal, a Silent Bell investigation, defensive armies, a rescue of captured Thule observers, and even giving the Grendel a Spring ritual.

Grendel.t: Grendel raiders captured Thule observers and are taking them towards the ruins of Siroc. The page floated a risky, possibly treasonous plan to give a Grendel coven such as Saltbinder Grekodh's the ritual Regrow the Land's Heart, since they control Madruga's Spring regio.

Highguard.t: The Freeborn di Tutamen family behind the blight has an unresolved historical link to the Highborn of Casinea and to Syrene's Wisdom. Wintergard magisters sought a midnight meeting with Highguard magisters in the Highguard chapel to share secrets.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian Jotun's invasion of Kahraman is listed among the threats besetting the Brass Coast.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn lost the Great Grasses to the blight. Harbingers now threaten Segura and Kahraman, and hakima led by Ishala i Erigo called a council at Anvil with the Hakima of Salt and Sand to address the blight and the Coast's wider hardships.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel magicians' earlier offer to cooperate against the horror in Spiral is cited as a precedent.

Thule.t: Thule warlocks investigating the blight were attacked by Grendel raiders, and at least two survivors are being taken towards Siroc. A rescue through the Sentinel Gate, needing The Cuckoo's Egg ritual, was proposed under the Ambassador to Otkodov.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Lutomysla Niegoslava, a cabalist from Karov, is one of the civil servants the Senate could choose for an appraisal of the blight.

Fading like a Flower.o: As Winter 385YE approached, the blight completed its consumption of Madruga's Great Grasses, now called Blightheart, and the region slipped from Imperial control, while three rune-marked Harbingers led gatherings of Dry Patricians and Parched to the borders of Segura and Kahraman. The page set out options for the Conclave, Senate, Synod and Military Council to respond.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: A cadre of Dry Patricians and Parched gathered south of Nestor's Bounty, led by a bone-robed Harbinger marked with the Rune of Wisdom.

Segura/Lucksprings.t: A Harbinger bearing the Rune of Hunger leads a crowd of the blightbound massed across the bridge west of Cerevado, waiting for the rains to end.

Segura/Sobral Grasses.t: The first Harbinger, bearing the glittering rune Yoorn, was seen at sunset along the edge of the Sobral Grasses with several dozen Dry Patricians and Parched.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the bay's surf is recalled as the place the nomads of the Great Grasses once brought their herds down towards.

Casinea.t: A cursed survivor of the blight has wandered Casinea begging for water, food and mana crystals amid rumours, though he appears human and is not spreading the blight. The Highborn of Casinea are historically linked to the di Tutamen.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Rahab still occupies Feroz, and Saltbinder Grekodh's Grendel coven on the Isle of Osseini is suggested as a possible recipient of a Spring ritual.

Kahraman.t: A third Harbinger, bearing the Rune of Wisdom, leads Dry Patricians and Parched gathered south of Nestor's Bounty, while the Lasambrian Jotun also invade the territory.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: the cabalist Lutomysla Niegoslava, a possible appraiser for the Senate, hails from Karov.

Madruga.t: With the territory overrun by the Grendel and Siroc burned, the Great Grasses became Blightheart, a blighted region no army can conquer. The Spring rains protecting the rest of Madruga are fading.

Otkodov.t: Warlocks from Otkodov had gone to study the blight with a Dragon's interest; survivors have been captured by Grendel. Otkodov is also suggested as a place where the Celestial Arch might seek help.

Segura.t: Two Harbinger-led gatherings of Dry Patricians and Parched have massed on Segura's borders, held back only by the last Spring rains, while the Cold Sun's forces also contend in the territory.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel magicians once sought to cooperate with Imperial peers to contain the horror in Spiral, a precedent for the proposed approach.

Fair play is turnabout.d: After the Empire killed Jarl Haakon Gydasson honourably rather than in a way that pleased Basileia, Mistress Alabaster of the Guild of Accountants accepted some of Haakon's belongings as down payment and was given the name of Salt Lord Seonag, de facto chair of the Council of Salt Lords. She demanded forty measures each of Ambergelt, Beggar's lye, Dragonbone and Iridescent gloaming up front, warned it could take years, and promised only an opportunity for Imperial heroes to strike. She warned that reciprocity would expose Anvil's dignitaries to Grendel contracts. Separately, bribery contracts were distributed via Enchanter Edmund Torawyr, one foreign bribe offer was extended to Autumn 387YE, and Overseer Hook and the Union of Lock-Keepers offered further services via Plenipotentiary.

Grendel.t: The Grendel face a potential City of Locks-brokered assassination of Salt Lord Seonag, which could throw their politics into turmoil for months; as regular clients of the City, Salt Lords might also commission killings of Imperial figures in return.

Jotun.t: Jarl Haakon's personal effects were sent to Mistress Alabaster, giving Basileia possible leverage over the Jotun, who refuse to deal with the City of Locks and reportedly drown anyone caught doing so.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Haakon's death in the Marcher territory of the Mournwold is cited as an easy target amid Imperial armies, illustrating the Guild's pricing.

Fair play is turnabout.o: In Spring 387YE the City of Locks, under Basileia, offered the Empire a costly, long-term opportunity to arrange the assassination of Salt Lord Seonag of the Grendel, set up a standard contract system for Imperial title-holders to name their bribery price, and sent letters offering espionage and help to destabilise the Asavean Plenum.

Bay of Catazar.t: A successful killing of Salt Lord Seonag would be the biggest political assassination the Bay of Catazar has seen in decades and could open the way for an all-out attack on Grendel fronts.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Haakon was killed in the Mournwold, surrounded by Imperial land and armies, which made him a cheap and easy target compared with Seonag.

Fair share of labour.d: The Guild's manifesto covers artisans and the study, innovation and creation of magic items, without conflicting with the Apothecaries' Guild or the Conclave. If ratified, it would take the power to enjoin magic items and disseminate schemas from the Senate, resolving what the magistrate called the Conclave's overreach in interdicting items. Four titles would automatically be appointed by the Guild, and seven more could be. Estavus offered schemas, the Carmine Band promised donations to the Golden Pyramid for its support, Treji's artisans proposed a great work in Hercynia, and Jasna Kazimerczyk urged the Pride Assembly to back the Guild. The magistrate also warned that the name was confusingly similar to the Apothecaries' Guild and risked suggesting League ties.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Pyramid's grandmaster, expected to rally Conclave support, is named as Terentia of Sarangrave Reforged.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Prosperity Assembly is noted as having a highest calling to discharge in Feroz, after which it may have views on sodalities.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Jasna recalls years of travelling to Anvil in Casinea to campaign for artisans' recognition.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting is listed among titles that the Senate could make appointable by the Guild.

Navarr.t: The artisans and brokers of Treji hope to win over Navarr senators to back the Guild, and offered a great work to boost Hercynia's mines and forests if it passes.

The League.t: The magistrate warned that the term 'Guild', common in League business, risked giving the sodality an apparent League affiliation and narrowing its appeal to other nations.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are recalled as having enslaved Treji's artisans to make weapons and magic items after conquering Hercynia.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Jasna reflects that had Urizen been a nation of artisans rather than magicians, the Conclave would have been a hall of craftspeople.

Varushka.t: Jasna Kazimerczyk, a Varushkan artisan and former Assembly preacher, wrote to her old allies across the north and urged the Pride Assembly to make supporting new sodalities its highest calling.

Fair share of labour.o: At Emperor Vesna's request, Magistrate Abraham of the Constitutional Court appraised the implications of making the Imperial Guild of Artisans an Imperial sodality, setting out the powers and titles it would gain and the groups offering support if the Senate ratified it.

Hercynia/The Glen of Shadows.t: Treji in the Glen of Shadows would host the proposed Starsrest or Goodfellow Brokerage, costing 12 weirwood and 36 crowns, which can only be built if the Senate approves the Guild.

Miekarova/Perumaki.t: Mentioned in passing: the vales of Perumaki are Jasna's home, where she arms young schlacta against wolves.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Jasna remembers travelling to Casinea each season to lobby in Anvil before giving up in frustration.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the Prosperity Assembly's highest calling is noted as being discharged in Feroz.

Hercynia.t: If the Guild became a sodality, the Empire could commission a great work at Treji to raise investment in Hercynia's forests and mines, overseen by the Broker of Treji Wayhouse.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: Jasna gives a Biting Blade each year to young schlacta defending the vales of Perumaki in Miekarova from wolves.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarangrave appears only in the name of the Golden Pyramid's grandmaster, Terentia of Sarangrave Reforged.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting could be made a Guild appointment by Senate motion.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Seer of the Spiral Sword is one of four titles that would automatically become Guild appointments if the sodality is created.

Fake empire.d: Drawing heavily on the former salt lord Kaliact, Naomi described a Council of six salt lords, four storm lords and one wind lord. Each salt lord must control a bourse resource. She warned that the salt lords close ranks against the Empire and distrust it, and that bribing one without Senate authorisation could be treason. She identified possible openings: a Suranni-permitted spy network watching Tathar, bullying Sarcophan into cutting Grendel trade, and Asavean withdrawal if Shivaarn's head came with a grovelling apology. Possible informants included Ehsan, the Black Sand Circle, the North Mareave Trading Consortium, Gallum Fiersach and the Children of Wrecks. She also proposed a Regario Dossier office in Vorlach.

Druj.t: The Grendel make only occasional one-off deals with the Druj, whom they distrust. They likely feed the Druj intelligence on Imperial movements, and the Druj cannot know whether the Empire is at war with the Jotun unless the Grendel tell them.

Grendel.t: The appraisal laid bare the Salt Lords Council, its reliance on mithril, white granite and weirwood, and its subtle infighting. It also showed the nation's dependence on Sarcophan, Jarmish and Asavean support, which the Empire might seek to undermine.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the five septs joining the Sunstorm are cited as evidence of the many orcs willing to support an expansion of the Regario Dossier.

Jotun.t: The Jotun trade a little with the Grendel and find them smug and dishonourable. They have confirmed that the Grendel pass them intelligence on Imperial military movements, apparently tailored to draw them into fighting the Empire.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn generals were named as well suited to approach the Grendel commander Gallum Fiersach. The Children of Wrecks, who claimed land in Madruga and colluded with the Asaveans against a Brass Coast lighthouse, were also discussed as possible negotiating partners.

The League.t: Kaliact sold her Spiral assets largely to League citizens and settled in Sarvos, where the Apulians and the Suranni embassy were Naomi's chief sources.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the pacifist orcs of the Mournwold joining the Marches are cited among the orcs willing to help the Empire.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel appear to have no diplomatic links with the Thule.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: much of the mithril the Council took from Spiral was traded with Urizen for weirwood, which was used to build the new Grendel navy.

Fake empire.o: Naomi of Virtue's Rest of the Prognosticators Office delivered the appraisal the Senate commissioned at the Autumn Equinox. It described how the Grendel Salt Lords Council works and set out possible ways to disrupt the salt lords and their foreign allies.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Mentioned in passing: the Cazar Straits are named as the narrow waters separating Grendel-held Tathar from Shavronne and Veroigne.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: Mentioned in passing: Morajasse is not named, though the page discusses Gallum Fiersach, walled up and well supplied in Mora's Rock in Feroz.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Beoraidh, ruled by the disowned salt lord Ehsan, hosts the Black Sand Circle and the North Mareave Trading Consortium, all named as potential paid informants on the Grendel.

Mareave/Sinfoyard.t: The North Mareave Trading Consortium has bought land from Ehsan in Sinfoyard, from which it is building trade links that could make it a source on salt lords' assets.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Kaliact has bought a resplendent waterfront property in Cigno, where she now lives in luxury after defecting.

Bay of Catazar.t: Grendel ambitions to dominate the Bay put them at odds with the Suranni. The Iron Confederacy nonetheless values the Grendel as a check on Imperial expansion across these waters.

Feroz.t: The Council installed Rahab as governor of Feroz hoping to distract the Empire from Spiral. Gallum Fiersach now holds out in Mora's Rock, and the Children of Wrecks have claimed land in the territory.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is listed among the lands where the Children of Wrecks have claimed territory.

Mareave.t: Lord Ehsan's Beoraidh, the Black Sand Circle and the North Mareave Trading Consortium, all based in Mareave, were identified as possible paid sources on the salt lords, wind lords and Grendel assets.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the pacifist orcs of the Mournwold joining the Marches are cited as orcs willing to support the Empire.

Raineach.t: Mentioned in passing: Raineach is listed among the lands where the Children of Wrecks have claimed territory.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named, though the page notes that Grendel mithril from Spiral was traded with Urizen for weirwood.

Sarvos.t: Kaliact settled in Sarvos, and Naomi held her discreet talks with the Suranni at the embassy there.

Shavronne.t: If the Suranni could be persuaded, Imperial agents might travel through Shavronne to establish a spy network or smugglers cove watching Tathar across the Cazar Straits. This was only a proposal.

Spiral.t: Kaliact explained that the Council always saw Spiral as a poisoned chalice: rich in mithril but made unbearable by the Black Plateau, and never realistically defensible. She has since liquidated her assets there, largely to League settlers.

Tathar.t: Tathar was identified as the target for a possible Imperial spy network or smugglers cove operated from Suranni lands across the straits, should the Iron Confederacy permit it.

Veroigne.t: Veroigne lies across the Cazar Straits from Tathar, near enough to see across. It forms part of Naomi's proposal for Suranni-permitted Imperial espionage against the Grendel.

Falcon in winter.d: Angry Winterfolk accused Wintermark of betraying Skarsind's traditions. Under the war hero Dogri, they entrenched themselves at Crow's Ridge, collapsed passes and destroyed a bridge, and warned the Senate and Military Council to stay out. No violence occurred, but an army sent against fellow citizens would be committing murder. The Wintermark assembly was offered two courses: urge withdrawal from Skarsind, or back those who stayed. Its judgement discouraged joining Dogri, encouraged settling in Wintermark lands and sought an amicable agreement. Withdrawal only works if Skarsind's spoils of war pass to the orcs, and the Four Seasons Market stayed in Wintermark hands. The judgement therefore had no effect.

Imperial Orcs.t: Their new homeland was challenged: Crow's Ridge was not counted under their control, and any orc entering would be supplied and sent back. They could still return a senator, but removing Dogri by force risked bloodshed and murder charges.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Dogri bitterly asks why Holberg was not given up instead, blaming its wealth and influence.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Crow's Ridge sits on the Otkodov border, and its defenders are veterans of the Thule war who refuse to submit to orcs of any kind.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Dogri asks why Karsk was not given up instead, blaming its wealth and influence.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark faced a rebellion of its own people claiming its name in Skarsind. Its assembly discouraged support for Dogri and urged resettlement, but this failed because the Four Seasons Market was never handed over.

Falcon in winter.o: In Winter 379YE, Thane Dogri Thulebane and his self-proclaimed Skarsind Loyalty Congregation rejected the handing of Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs. They fortified Crow's Ridge and declared it still part of Wintermark.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Mentioned in passing: Crow's Ridge lies in the south-eastern foothills of the Silver Peaks.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Dogri's followers fortified Crow's Ridge, collapsed passes and destroyed a bridge, and declared it Wintermark still. The region was not counted as Imperial Orc territory, and its defenders vowed to fight any intervention.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: Mentioned in passing: any Imperial Orc entering Crow's Ridge would be supplied and sent back to Pakaanan's Pass or Skogei Glen.

Skarsind/Solvihill.t: Mentioned in passing: the Solvihill Beggarwood Barrens is listed among the Skarsind spoils of war that would need to pass to the orcs.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: Mentioned in passing: Southpine Southbound is listed among the Skarsind spoils of war that would need to pass to the orcs.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark was named as one of the Wintermark territories where Skarsind's Winterfolk might find new homes if they withdrew. Its senator is also among those that Skarsind resource holders could still help to appoint.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Dogri resentfully asks why Holberg was not relinquished instead of Skarsind.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa was named as one of the territories where Winterfolk leaving Skarsind might resettle. Skarsind resource holders could still take part in appointing its senator.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: Dogri resentfully asks why Karsk was not relinquished instead of Skarsind.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Crow's Ridge lies isolated on Skarsind's border with Otkodov.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq was named as a possible new home for Winterfolk leaving Skarsind. Skarsind resource holders could still help appoint its senator.

Skarsind.t: The Winterfolk rebels split Skarsind, holding Crow's Ridge against orc settlement while disgruntled residents left their farms and mines to join them. Wintermark resources there suffered reduced production under orc rule.

Fall of Brocéliande.d: The vallorn's expansion was stymied and Winter magic hinders its recovery. Clearing Dark Ranging would require Imperial armies to claim the entire region, with casualties doubled by the miasma and supporting military units suffering lasting losses. Dawnish rewards and Highborn pilgrim aid continued until the Winter Solstice, with Highguard able to recall or extend its pilgrims by mandate. Tharim offered continued and potentially greater aid at the cost of more herb gardens and forests. The Great Forest Orcs went home, disgusted by Druj aid to the Navarr. Proposals were made to reinforce the Broch, fortify Greenstead and build Houses of Healing in Elerael, the last conditional on a Navarr statement condemning the Druj alliance. It was later withdrawn.

Dawn.t: Dawnish military units supporting armies in Brocéliande continued to earn four random ingots from the nobles of Rucastle and Semmerholm until the Winter Solstice. Rucastle also proposed fortifying Greenstead as a castle for questing knights.

Druj.t: Druj aid to the Navarr in northern Brocéliande drove the Great Forest Orcs home and angered Highborn pilgrims, and the Broch scouting was meant to check for Druj surprises left in Boar's Dell.

Highguard.t: Highborn congregations kept losing Synod votes and liao while their pilgrims aided Brocéliande, worth about 1,400 strength to any attack. The national assembly could recall them early or extend their service by mandate, and a Highborn physick co-proposed the Houses of Healing.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun-held Liathaven's earlier weakened vallorn was cited as a comparison, and its curse was covered elsewhere.

Navarr.t: The Navarr of Brocéliande survived the vallorn surge and were offered a chance to reclaim Dark Ranging, along with proposals to reinforce the Broch, fortify Greenstead and build Houses of Healing. The healing houses depended on the national assembly condemning the Druj alliance.

Wintermark.t: Tharim offered to triple his aid in Brocéliande if the Conclave let him feed on the herb gardens and forests of Wintermark and other nations, each losing two herbs or resources until Winter 384YE.

Fall of Brocéliande.o: After a year-long vallorn surge into Boar's Dell and Elerael was weathered, the Brocéliande vallorn was left weakened, opening a window until the Autumn Equinox 384YE to clear Dark Ranging with Imperial armies. Several allied proposals to strengthen the Navarr in Brocéliande were also put forward.

Brocéliande/Black Boughs.t: Mentioned in passing: if the vallorn were driven from Black Boughs, the Broch would be an ideal site for a fortification.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Boar's Dell withstood the vallorn surge, and Rucastle proposed fortifying its steading of Greenstead as a Dawnish-style castle and base for questing into the vallorn.

Brocéliande/Dark Ranging.t: Imperial armies could clear the vallorn from Dark Ranging, but only by claiming the whole region before Autumn 384YE, fighting in miasma that doubles casualties.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Elerael held against the vallorn with Highborn and Great Forest Orc help, and Houses of Healing were proposed at Eleri's Stead, conditional on the Navarr condemning the Druj alliance.

Brocéliande/Terunael.t: Mentioned in passing: the region itself is not discussed, though the Heirs of Terunael are named as a threat the Broch could watch for.

Brocéliande.t: The weakened vallorn could be driven from Dark Ranging before it recovered by Autumn 384YE. Proposals to reinforce the Broch, fortify Greenstead and build Houses of Healing in Elerael were put forward to strengthen the territory.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: a fortification at the Broch, if Black Boughs were cleared, would help guard the eastern approach to Casinea.

Hercynia.t: Herb gardens and forests in Hercynia continued to lose two herbs or two measures each to Tharim's feeding until the Winter Solstice.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: its previously weakened vallorn was used as a comparison, and the Winter curse over it was covered in another Wind of Fortune.

Miaren.t: Herb gardens and forests in Miaren continued to lose two herbs or two measures each to Tharim's feeding until the Winter Solstice.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: clearing Dark Ranging would let armies move from Reikos to Semmerholm or the Barrens, and the fall of Reikos was recalled.

Semmerholm.t: The nobles of Rucastle and Semmerholm continued rewarding Dawnish units in Brocéliande, and clearing Dark Ranging would open an army route between Semmerholm and Reikos.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: clearing Dark Ranging would let armies pass from Reikos into the Barrens, and Greenstead serves knights exploring there.

Therunin.t: The Great Forest Orc warriors returned to Therunin in disgust at Druj aid, and its herb gardens and forests kept suffering Tharim's feeding until the Winter Solstice.

False kings.d: The Jotun, aided by fey knights from the Fields of Glory, dug in defensively in North Fens and Grey Fens, and no battle was fought, so control did not change. The Strong Reeds lay low, rearmed from equipment recovered at Miresend, while Night magic in Ottermire set lantern-bearing marsh creatures against the invaders. Steven of Sarcombe's Mournwold Exiles had left, but several hundred newcomers from Hordalant and around 250 former Marcher citizens swelled Mathilda's warband. Her messengers urged secession and offered a Jotun pause on claims to Marcher lands if Bregasland's independence were recognised. A conjunction offered the Empire a chance to defeat a Jotun warband in Grey Fens and discredit her.
