Jotun.t: Jotun armies stayed on the defensive in Bregasland, backing Mathilda Fisher under a treaty recognising an independent Bregasland, and offering to set aside their claim to the Mourn, Mitwold and Upwold for five years if Bregasland's independence were recognised.

The Marches.t: The Marches faced a growing secessionist movement in Bregasland, with about 250 former citizens openly joining Mathilda Fisher, and Marcher military units given the treasonous option of fighting alongside the Jotun-backed rebels.

False kings.o: In Spring 384YE Bregasland was quiet: the Jotun held their ground in the western fens while the Strong Reeds lay low, but Mathilda Fisher's campaign for an independent Bregasland began drawing disaffected Bregas to her Yegarra.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: The Jotun still held Grey Fens, though shakily, and a cautious Jotun picket for the Fist of Ulven roamed there; the village of Dank Mere offered to rebut Mathilda's propaganda if the Empire defeated it through the Sentinel Gate.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: The Jotun remained firmly in control of North Fens, building palisades, while their fey allies held tourneys and banquets among the northern marshes; Mathilda claims it as Fisher land.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: Night magic woven into Ottermire made the marshes resist the Jotun, with lantern-bearing creatures luring orc camps into the quagmires, though Mathilda counts Ottermire as Fisher land.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland saw no battles, but it was divided: southern and eastern households loudly professed loyalty while the north and west weighed the future, and Mathilda's recruitment threatened to grow each season.

Hordalant.t: Several hundred people dressed in a mix of Bregas and Jotun fashion crossed out of Hordalant to join Mathilda's warband, and she claims her household has dwelled in Hordalant's marshes for some four hundred years.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold was named among the Marcher lands the Jotun would leave alone for five years if Bregasland's independence were recognised, and Mathilda told the Bregas to leave the Empire to Mitwold's squabbling households.

Mournwold.t: Steven of Sarcombe's Mournwold Exiles, driven by grief over the curses that struck the Mourn, had left Bregasland, and the Mourn was included in the Jotun offer to suspend their claims.

Upwold.t: The Tusks were billeted in comfort in Upwold, and Upwold was among the lands the Jotun offered not to pursue for five years in return for Bregas independence.

Famine and feast.d: The Lictors agreed to a very formal parley and offered to sustain Scrivener's Bloodmark contracts in exchange for ilium. Ossegrahn agreed to parley, offering thanks and questioning Navarr ties to Arhallogen. Rhianos declined parley, empowered Golden Voyage and began a year-long race to the four corners of the world. Kimus declined parley but offered a boon of finding for Gilda Ashwine's grave or Emperor Frederick's Pauper's Key. Sung sent heralds to trade boons for vision interpretations and eased Clear Counsel of the Everflowing River. Blood-on-the-Snow demanded an oath before parleying and offered boons through Crimson Letters. The Archmage of Winter swore no oath, so that parley failed.

Dawn.t: Ossegrahn wished to thank those who protected the Tarnfather's charges on the expedition to Dawn, to meet Ser Elienne of Dawn over an act of profound healing, and he condemned the recent bloodshed in the Barrens.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Blood-on-the-Snow's herald cited wishing for the Druj to all die in a fire as an example of a boon not worth requesting.

Grendel.t: Rhianos took an interest in the Grendel as a sworn enemy of Siakha, and offered boons to anyone taking part in the four conjunctions of the Sentinel Gate at the coming Solstice.

Highguard.t: Kimus revealed that Gilda Ashwine's remains, once interred in a basilica in Bastion, were secretly reburied after she lost her exemplar status. The eternal offered to find the grave if the Conclave asked, and Ossegrahn refused to raise forests over the meadows and orchards of Necropolis.

Imperial Orcs.t: Kimus advised that the orc researcher Snowstorm Henk, commissioned to explore the Sorrowful Tunnels in Skarsind, would be better served by an investigator sent by Walker on the Littoral, because the servants of secrets might take offence at the delving.

Navarr.t: Ossegrahn summoned the Hand of the Healers and the Granger of the Golden Orchard to explain why the Navarr seemed to be allying with the children of the Spider King. He warned that he was reconsidering his patronage of the Houses of Healing.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossegrahn's message was carried by a Freeborn hakima, and Rhianos pointed to the extended docks at the Great Harbour of Elos as a means to raise a navy.

The League.t: Ossegrahn refused to displace the natural life of Sarvos's grasslands and orchards to raise forests for ward-making. Kimus noted that the lost Pauper's Key was the work of the artisan Catherine de Sarvos.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Willowbraid was curious about the Archmage of Spring's suggestion that they travel together to the lands of the Thule to feed their people.

Urizen.t: Ossegrahn declined to help with Urizen's cursed mana sites, saying crystal mana is not essential to life. Blood-on-the-Snow invited magicians able to cast Crimson Letters, a ritual of Urizen lore, to use it to request his boons.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening scene features a civil servant, Jorgen, who knows Wintermark well, and Kimus noted that the Gildenheim runeforge was moved to Runegrott in Hahnmark.

Famine and feast.o: Six eternals replied to the Imperial archmages' plenipotentiary messages. The Lictors, Ossegrahn, Sung and Blood-on-the-Snow arranged meetings at Anvil, while Rhianos and Kimus declined parley but offered boons; in the end the Conclave asked Ossegrahn for a college proposal, and the Blood-on-the-Snow parley never took place.

Bastion.t: Kimus recounted that Gilda Ashwine's remains were once interred in a basilica in Bastion before the civil service disinterred and secretly reburied them.

Bay of Catazar.t: Rhianos had lost interest in raids across the Bay and dismissed a race around it as too small. The eternal said an Imperial navy raised on the Bay would be the moment to seek their boons.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Gildenheim runeforge was noted as having been dismantled and moved to Runegrott in Hahnmark.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Rhianos suggested the Empire could use the extended docks at the Great Harbour of Elos to raise a navy.

Necropolis.t: Ossegrahn refused to kill and displace the meadows and orchards of Necropolis to raise forests for Imperial ward-making.

Sarvos.t: Ossegrahn named the grasslands, meadows and orchards of Sarvos as rich with life and refused to replace them with forests for magicians' convenience.

Skarsind.t: Kimus discussed the Sorrowful Tunnels, which Snowstorm Henk had been commissioned to explore. The eternal advised seeking an investigator from Walker on the Littoral to protect the delving.

The Barrens.t: Ossegrahn condemned the recent violence in the Barrens and vowed to work so that such actions never happen again. He thanked those who saved creatures driven into the Empire by the Merciless One.

Farewell wanderlust.d: The enchantment touched only territories that were Imperial at the end of the Spring Equinox, including the newly conquered Barrens, but not Liathaven, Brocéliande, Feroz or Spiral. Lucky windfalls left every citizen at Anvil wealthier. Cambion felt Autumn's pull strongly. Businesses could diversify once without cost and gained new production options. The Bailiffs of the Guttered Flame offered vouchers for mithril, white granite and weirwood wains, though these were seized from the vaults of Pharam Vex and were surely proceeds of the slave trade. Deepstones appeared in the deepest mines. Farms yielded Ashen Residue instead of some produce, and forests yielded metallic fruit. Some Marcher farms with menhirs began turning into mana sites.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: a dusty bottle of century-old wine from the vineyards of Astolat is given as an example of a lucky find.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens, conquered from the Druj by Imperial heroes at the Battle of Merigionne, fell within the enchantment's reach.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Feroz, held by the Grendel, was outside the Empire's grasp and untouched by the enchantment.

Jotun.t: Liathaven, held by the Jotun, was untouched by the enchantment. The dissonant effects on farms and forests were nonetheless felt in Bregasland.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Siroc and Cargo are named among the places where the Bailiffs' otherworldly caravans emerged from Autumn regio.

The League.t: Bailiffs' caravans emerged around Tassato, Sarvos, Holberg and Temeschwar to bank materials for Bourse notes. Spiral lay outside the enchantment's reach, and a League theatre profited from a crowd-pleasing new play about Basileus Flint and Spiral.

The Marches.t: Marcher farms with more than two sets of menhirs began transforming into mana sites. The Circle of the Rosy Rook of Wayford offered to dismantle the menhirs for farmers who wished to keep their farms, paying a throne per set.

Urizen.t: An Urizen magician who oversees ushabti labourers studied the ruined farm produce and published findings showing that it was rich in useful Autumn magic.

Wintermark.t: The Net and Vine of Wintermark performed the Bounty of the Brilliant Broker, the first Imperial enchantment tied to the realm of Autumn, which caused all these effects.

Farewell wanderlust.o: In Summer 385YE the Wintermark Net and Vine's Autumn enchantment, the Bounty of the Brilliant Broker, swept across the Imperial territories. It brought windfalls, new trade opportunities and rare deepstones, but its clash with the lingering Spring magic of the Hallow of the Green World twisted farm and forest produce.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: wine from the vineyards of Astolat is cited as an example of a serendipitous find.

Bregasland.t: Although untouched by the Spring Hallow, Bregasland still felt the dissonant effects on farm and forest produce.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Brocéliande was not Imperial at the end of the Spring Equinox, so the enchantment did not affect it.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Feroz was excluded from the enchantment, so businesses there could not gain its benefits.

Hahnmark.t: Otherworldly caravans of the Bailiffs of the Guttered Flame emerged from Autumn regio around Kalpaheim to bank magical materials.

Holberg.t: Bailiffs' caravans drawn by six-legged lead-scaled lizards emerged from Autumn regio around Holberg, unloading materials in exchange for Bourse notes.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven was outside the enchantment's reach.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Siroc and Cargo are listed among the places where the Bailiffs' caravans appeared.

Mitwold.t: Bailiffs' caravans emerged around Meade, while Marcher farms with menhirs began turning into mana sites.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is used as an example of an affected territory where a cambion might have spent the season.

Sarvos.t: Bailiffs' caravans emerged from Autumn regio around Sarvos. A lost Throne coin feeding a Sarvosan orphan is cited as a lucky windfall.

Spiral.t: Spiral lay outside the enchantment's reach, though a new League play about Spiral and the Keeper of the Black Vaults was drawing full houses.

Tassato.t: Bailiffs of the Guttered Flame caravans emerged from Autumn regio around Tassato to bank mithril, white granite and weirwood.

Temeschwar.t: Bailiffs' caravans emerged from Autumn regio around Temeschwar, depositing materials in Imperial warehouses for Bourse notes.

The Barrens.t: Newly conquered at the Battle of Merigionne, the Barrens fell within the enchantment's reach, and its farms and forests felt the dissonant effects.

Farm, fur, and fish.d: Graciana found that Sermersuaq already paid its way and was recovering from the Jotun invasion. She suggested a further appraisal to reopen Pakaanan's Pass to Skarsind, and proposed revisiting the Thule offer to hunt in Suaq Fount and East Floes, perhaps by moving the Thule embassy to Sermersuaq. Her commission proposals included gardens and a lodge at the Hot Springs of Taniki, and a fishery and a tradehall at Atalaq. A Mediator of Atalaq could redirect the benefits of these works. To ease the treasury, she suggested decommissioning the Jotun-built castles in favour of beacons, or relinquishing the Pride of Ikka's Tears. Two Jotun warbands were hunting the returning Icebarn Twins.

Imperial Orcs.t: Reopening Pakaanan's Pass could let Skarsind trade its wood and metal for Sermersuaq's meat, fish, herbs, furs and ivory, to the benefit of both nations. Their herbalists might also gain from proposed cerulean mazzarine gardens at Taniki.

Jotun.t: Jotun forces sealed Pakaanan's Pass in 383YE and built the costly Sermersuaq castles. Two Jotun warbands were moving to intercept the Icebarn Twins and claim the items embedded in them.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Mine of Briante in Kahraman is cited as the model for relinquishing the Pride of Ikka's Tears.

The League.t: Graciana visited the Imperial mint in Tassato and drew inspiration from Temeschwar's Reaper's Repose. A proposed Atalaq Tradehall would let the Custodian of the Bloody Great Sausage bring Sermersuaq's exotic meats to League cities for 7 crowns a season.

Thule.t: Graciana suggested a Wintermark ambassador could revisit the Thule request to hunt in Suaq Fount and East Floes, perhaps by moving the Thule embassy to Sermersuaq. A trade ministry could then exchange furs and meat for Thule vis or raw materials, though current tensions must first be resolved.

Varushka.t: The Thule embassy could be moved out of Mieriada to Sermersuaq. Varushkan herbalists also share the difficulty of growing cerulean mazzarine in cold climes that the Taniki gardens would address.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark proposed the appraisal, and it offered many ways to enrich Sermersuaq, including Atalaq great works, a Mediator of Atalaq, Taniki sinecures and fleet trade bonuses. Ways to raise its contribution to the treasury included beacons or giving up the Pride of Ikka's Tears.

Farm, fur, and fish.o: At Wintermark's request, the Imperial Senate commissioned Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra to appraise how Sermersuaq's untapped natural wealth could raise its prosperity and its contribution to the Empire. She returned with proposals covering trade, new great works and sinecures, and cost-cutting. The page also gave notice that the Icebarn Twins would emerge during the Summer Solstice.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: The Thule embassy at Wendell's Hope in Mieriada could be relocated to Sermersuaq, which is easier for the orcs of Otkodov to reach.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: The Thule had asked to hunt in East Floes, and Graciana suggested the request be revisited and the Thule embassy perhaps moved nearby.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Atalaq in Sealtoq would host the proposed Atalaq Fishery, Atalaq Tradehall and a Mediator of Atalaq. The proposed Beacons of Sermersuaq would also be sited here, operating as long as Atalaq remains Imperial.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Mentioned in passing: the Silver Peaks are noted as rich in weltsilver and tempest jade that the Thule might trade.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: The Thule had asked to hunt in Suaq Fount, which is easy for them to reach and a possible new home for the Thule embassy.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: The Icebarn Twins were due to emerge from Sydanjaa in the Suaq Wastes during the Summer Solstice, pursued by two Jotun warbands. Liv Tidgaring and Derowen were responsible for stopping the warbands.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: The Hot Springs of Taniki could host the Gardens of Taniki, growing cerulean mazzarine, and a Hot Springs Hall lodge. The Hall would spur new businesses and add two thrones to Sermersuaq's taxation.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: The pass, sealed by a Jotun force in 383YE, is impassable to armies and caravans. Graciana recommended a separate appraisal to reopen it for military and merchant use.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: its beacons are cited as a model for Sermersuaq, and the old Gulnar's Deephall mithril proposal there might be revisited.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: its Great Mine of Briante, which brings in over 400 Thrones a year, is cited as a comparison for relinquishing the Pride of Ikka's Tears.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: its beacons, used without fortifications, are cited as the model for Sermersuaq's proposed beacons.

Miekarova.t: The Thule embassy currently stands in Miekarova, and Graciana suggested a single Senate motion and commission could move it to Sermersuaq.

Otkodov.t: The orcs of Otkodov might be offered hunting rights in Sermersuaq in exchange for vis, mana or raw materials, though relations are currently on a knife edge.

Sermersuaq.t: The territory was the subject of the appraisal, which proposed fisheries, a tradehall, gardens, a lodge, beacons, trade with neighbours and treasury savings. The Icebarn Twins were also due to emerge there during the Summer Solstice.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind's trade with Sermersuaq remains blocked by the collapsed Pakaanan's Pass. Reopening it would require a further appraisal, but could benefit both territories.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Graciana spent a few days visiting the Imperial mint there before heading north.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: its Reaper's Repose lodge inspired Graciana's proposal for the Hot Springs Hall.

Fate and function.d: The Crucible, built under the Master of the Koboldi and hastened by Autumn magic, was endorsed by a greater-majority Urizen Assembly mandate carried by Able of Zenith Ascendant. Zenith lost its bereft of hope and stifled by miasma qualities. Settlers returned to build compact, defensible spires, helped by new ushabti and Adamant's koboldi, who were allowed to live beneath the Crucible. Prospero's incentives saw the heliopticon towers repaired. Ushabti cut the cost of boosting Urizeni mines, forests and herb gardens. An Architect of the Crucible title was to go to the Senate, with powers to commission ushabti, buy staves and buy ilium found by Estavus's bronze birds. Rival Synod mandates proposed a Prosperity shrine or a tomb to Achilles.

Druj.t: The miasma and despair the Druj left behind in Zenith were finally dispelled, though scattered remnants of their malice still lurk in the territory's dark corners and their marks will take a generation to heal.

Navarr.t: A proposed tomb to the exemplar Achilles at the Crucible risks unexpected consequences for Navarr, since he was murdered by a Navarr citizen, apparently of the Quiet Step, barely three years earlier, a killing still unsolved despite Idanach Listing Beacon's condemnation.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Achilles's home of Damakhan's Forge is noted as soon to be in a League territory, one reason given for memorialising him at the Crucible instead.

Urizen.t: Urizen gained a new arete founded on commerce and craftsmanship. Citizens could move resources to Zenith on favourable terms, pay less to increase mine, forest and herb garden production, and potentially gain an Architect of the Crucible with valuable powers.

Fate and function.o: In Summer 385YE the completed Crucible of Fate in Iteri dispelled the Druj miasma and the despair hanging over Zenith. Guided by an Urizen Assembly mandate favouring practical and effective work, it began transforming the territory and Urizen's economy.

Zenith/Iteri.t: The Crucible of Fate stands in Iteri, producing ushabti and magic items, housing Adamant's koboldi in tunnels beneath it, and offered as the site of a possible Prosperity shrine or a tomb to Achilles.

Zenith/Lustri.t: Mentioned in passing: work on the defences being built in Lustri helps ease fears that the Druj will soon return.

Morrow.t: Many refugees from Zenith had settled in Morrow, and the repaired heliopticon restored swift communication with it. Resources there may be upgraded through the Architect's bespoke ushabti, and the faithful were urged to gather there for a consecration before travelling to Iteri.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt had taken in Zenith's refugees, some of whom are content to stay. The heliopticon now links it again with Zenith, and its resources are eligible for upgrades through the Crucible's bespoke ushabti.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos's reinvention as the City of Masks is cited as a comparable, though less ambitious, example of a new story reshaping a territory.

Zenith.t: Zenith shed its bereft of hope and stifled by miasma qualities. Settlers began raising new, defensible spires, the heliopticon towers were repaired, and Urizen characters gained a temporary chance to relocate resources there until the Autumn Equinox.

Fear quickens the breath.d: Anka Karass withdrew her treachery allegations against members of her own sept and accepted a transactional relationship with the Empire, backed by the threat of force. She was attacked at the meeting, and the matter is under criminal investigation. Karass scouts confirmed Thule armies attacking the Druj in the Forest of Ulnak. The Imperial Spymaster could authorise a joint venture to survey Thule attempts to claim a Black Lotus. The Karass also proposed that the Senate cede the Last Battle to them, which the Navarr Assembly could veto, in exchange for scouting on the borders. Separately, they offered potions for beggar's lye through the Carmine Fields Trading Post. Illegal potions were surrendered to a magistrate.

Dawn.t: The Karass want the Dawnish investment in the Barrens to turn a healthy profit, and they offered the Envoy potions in place of herbs through the Carmine Fields Trading Post.

Druj.t: The Karass admit they fear Druj vengeance, and their scouts confirmed that Thule forces are attacking Druj lands in the Forest of Ulnak, possibly to seize the Buruk Tepel's Black Lotus plants.

Navarr.t: Ceding the Last Battle would devastate the Navarr of the Barrens, whose steadings and stridings rely on the wayhouse, so the Navarr National Assembly could veto the motion.

Thule.t: The Karass regard the Thule as enemies and offered to help the Empire spy on Thule attempts to claim a Black Lotus. They are unaware that the Thule already know of the Imperial spy network in Ulnak.

Fear quickens the breath.o: After the Envoy to the Karass met Anka Karass, relations between the Empire and the Barrens sept advanced markedly, and the Karass came forward with three offers: a joint scouting venture against the Thule in the Forest of Ulnak, a request that the Last Battle Wayhouse be ceded to them in return for scouting services, and a potion trade.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: If the Last Battle were ceded, the Spymaster could have the Karass watch the Nesustak Forest rebels and report any changes. The region would remain protected by the Gryphon's Pride watchtowers.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: The Last Battle Wayhouse stands in the Bleaks, and the Karass are deeply agitated by its presence and want it ceded to them.

Therunin/Eastring.t: If the Last Battle were ceded, Eastring would cease to be under threat, because the Karass refuse to enter vallorn-claimed land. No Imperial army can currently claim the region in any case.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: Under the cession proposal the valley would stay under threat, and the Karass offered to study its Druj poison so that it could be cured. That antidote opportunity has since been superseded by another wind of war.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Karass scouts confirmed Thule armies attacking the Druj here, and the Imperial spy network could support a joint survey of Thule efforts to seize a Black Lotus. The network is likely to last only a season or two before the Thule destroy it.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov is named as one of the few ways the Thule might learn of the Karass scouting.

Sarangrave.t: If the Last Battle were ceded, the Karass would take over watching the Sarangrave border in place of the wayhouse's projection of Imperial force.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the in-character text recalls a past Druj push into Semmerholm in which Lenna's parents died.

The Barrens.t: The Karass of the Barrens are now cooperating with their Imperial overlords and offering trade. They have also asked for the Last Battle Wayhouse to be ceded to them.

Therunin.t: Rumours of worrying events in Therunin have alarmed the Karass, who offered to watch for Druj movements there if the Last Battle were ceded.

Fearful symmetry.d: The Winter Solstice heralded a year of storms. Grendel navies off Spiral and Redoubt were battered, and wreckage washed up as far north as the Necropolis. A magical storm then covered Redoubt, possibly cast at Anvil or through the powerful Spring regio at Evenstar in Naris, which the Grendel had held since Winter. Urizeni morale and arête suffered. Ageing spires crumbled, the Heliopticon failed, and floods and landslides destroyed paths and bridges. A huge rockfall buried the Cargo Road pass near Iteri, leaving only a rough goat track. Armies moving through Redoubt counted it as two territories until repairs were made. The Northern Eagle completed the repairs in two seasons.

Grendel.t: Grendel navies off Spiral and Redoubt were battered by the storms, which also threatened the rations their armies relied on from Dubhtraig. Suspicion fell on Grendel-held Evenstar as the regio through which the curse on Redoubt might have been cast.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: wreckage from the storms washed up as far north as the Necropolis.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: a visiting Holberger silk-merchant was caught in a roof collapse in a Redoubt spire.

Urizen.t: The Urizeni of Redoubt endured six weeks of storm that sapped their arête and poise, damaged their spires, cut the Heliopticon and ruined key roads. Their engineers cut a temporary path around the Cargo Road rockfall and estimated that full repairs would take a year without help.

Fearful symmetry.o: In Spring 381YE fierce storms lashed the coasts of Spiral and Redoubt, and a magical storm mirroring them settled over Redoubt itself, wrecking roads and bridges and blocking the main pass on the Cargo Road. Armies crossing Redoubt were slowed until the Northern Eagle repaired the routes over two seasons.

Redoubt/Naris.t: The Spring regio at the Grendel-held spire of Evenstar in Naris was suspected as the means by which the storm curse was laid on Redoubt.

Redoubt/Siluri.t: Part of the cliffside where Mount Siluri meets the sea was washed away, and the main road into Redoubt from the northern side of the Siluri range was blocked by a rockfall.

Redoubt/Tomari.t: Observers in the Tomari Heights Spire were the first to notice that the storm over Redoubt was a magical effect.

Redoubt/Ventosi.t: Flooding in Ventosi knocked a central Heliopticon relay tower out of alignment and brought the network down for a time, and a landslide blocked the path to a long-abandoned spire.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the storms were described as raging along the Bay.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: a Holberger silk-merchant visiting Redoubt was woken by a collapsing roof.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: wreckage from the storms was found as far north as the Necropolis.

Redoubt.t: A magical storm battered Redoubt with floods, avalanches and rockfalls that blocked the main Cargo Road pass and made any army crossing it lose a territory of movement. The Northern Eagle cleared the damage over two seasons.

Spiral.t: Spiral's coast was battered by violent spiralling winds and waves that tormented the Grendel navies stationed there.

Fight.d: The Marcher and Imperial Orc assemblies each sent a priest with 50 doses of liao. Working together, the two recruited dozens of preachers. They found the thralls peaceful, unarmed, and very like their Marcher neighbours, and already well informed about the virtues. The news that the Senate had recognised them as foreigners, so they would not be driven from their land, was met with relief. Yet as the priests explained the doctrines of the Way, crowds became upset or hostile and drove them off. The thralls' influential figures, the timber merchant Sigdór and Hamma the Lame of Eversweet Orchard, asked to meet the priests at Anvil. Persuading them would bring many thralls to the faith.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc Assembly sent Bloodcrow Losak to preach to the thralls. Hamma had also been invited to meet Bloodcrow Yargol, the Advisor for Orc Affairs, and Bloodcrow Morghur, the orc General of the Winter Sun.

Jotun.t: The Jotun thralls of the Mournwold were relieved to keep their land, but their response to the Way turned from interest to angry rejection. They say their leaders are the Jotun jarls, though in daily matters figures like Sigdór and Hamma hold real sway.

The Marches.t: The Marcher Assembly sent Sister Meredith with liao to convert the thralls. Many Marchers of the Mourn already treated the thralls as neighbours or friends, trading with them and playing foot the ball together.

Fight.o: In Spring 382YE, Sister Meredith of the Marchers and Bloodcrow Losak of the Imperial Orcs led a mission to preach the Way of Virtue to the Jotun thralls living in the Mournwold. The thralls showed genuine interest at first, but then grew agitated and angrily rejected the sermons for reasons no one could discover.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: The Chalkdowns was one of the key regions occupied by Jotun thralls, where preachers met interest that soured into hostility.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Green March was one of the key regions held by the Jotun thralls targeted by the preaching mission.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Mentioned in passing: the thrall leader Sigdór, a timber merchant, lived on the edge of the Greensward.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Southmoor was one of the key regions occupied by Jotun thralls, where the priests' sermons were received first with interest and then with anger.

Mournwold.t: The Marcher-held Mournwold was home to a large population of Jotun thralls on prized farmland. Efforts to bring them to the Way stalled there, pending talks with their leaders at Anvil.

Fight or flight.d: After conquering Zenith, five Druj armies attacked Morrow. The appraisal found that refugees could only leave safely under escort, either by an Imperial army making a heroic stand or by military units coordinated by the civil service. A combined fighting strength of 5000 could save at most 80% of the people. Redoubt was the preferred destination, then Bastion or Necropolis, while Therunin was risky. Evacuation would cut Morrow's taxes, move costs and some revenue to the receiving territory, and delay recovery if Morrow were retaken. Separately, Portia the Elder backed a plan to restore the Heliopticon (12 wains of mithril and 24 crowns) and create the Doyen of the Spires, chosen by Urizen magicians, to lead research across the spires.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the civil service apprentice Anton reminds himself he is no longer in Dawn and stops himself bowing.

Druj.t: Having taken Zenith and destroyed the Halls of Knowledge, five Druj armies were pressing their attack on Morrow, threatening to slaughter or enslave any Urizeni who fled without protection.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Spiral, which it held, contains one of the central Heliopticon towers the Senate commissioned to be repaired.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Bastion was named as the fallback refuge for Morrow's evacuees via the Couros bridge, with possible later dispersal to Necropolis. Reikos was ruled out as a destination.

Navarr.t: Navarr-held Therunin was judged a possible but dangerous refuge, as vallorn-infested regions could leave fleeing Urizeni trapped if the Druj pursued them.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the immortals of Otkodov are listed among the few magicians who could rival Urizen's mastery of magic.

Urizen.t: Urizen faced the possible evacuation and long-term depopulation of Morrow. It also gained the prospect of restoring its pride by linking its spires through a repaired Heliopticon under a Doyen of the Spires, elected by its magicians.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the civil servant Mila is Varushkan, and the Wise Ones of Varushka are imagined arguing that their nation should host any new college of magic.

Fight or flight.o: In Winter 382YE the civil service reported to the Senate on how Morrow might be evacuated in the face of a Druj invasion. Alongside this, Urizeni magicians proposed repairing the Heliopticon so that their spires could act together as a college of magic, and the Senate commissioned the repair of the towers in Morrow and Spiral.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: The vallorn in Greenheart was one reason refugees sent to neighbouring Peakedge Song risked being trapped.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Peakedge Song was the region of Therunin to which Morrow's people could in theory be evacuated, though they risked being cornered there by pursuing Druj.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: The vallorn in Sweetglades hemmed in Peakedge Song, making it a dangerous refuge for fleeing Urizeni.

Bastion.t: Bastion was the second-choice refuge for Morrow's people, reached over the bridge across the Couros. It would gain half of any tax revenue lost from Morrow, along with the matching support costs.

Morrow.t: Under Druj attack, Morrow could see up to 80% of its population evacuated, with matching losses of taxation. Its central Heliopticon tower was commissioned for repair, though heavy evacuation would stop it contributing to Urizen's magical research.

Necropolis.t: Refugees could not reach Necropolis directly across the Couros, but could disperse there from Bastion in a later season.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the sinister immortals of Otkodov are cited as rivals to Urizen's magical mastery.

Redoubt.t: The civil service recommended Redoubt as the best destination for Morrow's evacuees, along a good road towards Cargo. Redoubt would take on half of any lost revenue and the costs of supporting the refugees.

Reikos.t: Reikos was ruled out as a refuge because its roads and trods could not carry so many people to safety.

Spiral.t: Spiral's central Heliopticon tower was commissioned for repair as part of the plan to link Urizen's spires into a single research network.

Therunin.t: Therunin was considered a possible but hazardous destination for Morrow's refugees, since the vallorn could trap them if the Druj followed.

Zenith.t: Already conquered by the Druj, Zenith was where those who stayed suffered a terrible fate. Reclaiming it and restoring its Heliopticon would raise Urizen's research speed to 20 magnitude per season.

Fight with monsters.d: At the Spring Equinox 382YE the Wintermark Assembly upheld (236–0) a mandate sending Gunnbrand Ironwill with liao to remind the Mark of the hero's path. Any Wintermark army may now fight with honour when attacking, forcing allied Imperial forces alongside it to abandon plunder and butchery and protecting civilians on both sides. Wintermark armies fighting the Jotun now permanently gain more victory but inflict fewer casualties, fighting them as equals in honour. The Rune-bound mystics emerged from Kallavesa to offer the Fist of the Mountains the Farsighted quality, and the Green Shields could become Heroic, each for 25 wains of mithril. Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason and Osric provided the mithril for each respectively.

Jotun.t: Wintermark armies now permanently fight the Jotun as honourable equals, winning ground more readily but slaying significantly fewer Jotun, and recent Jotun actions suggest the change has been noticed.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule gathering in Wintermark's north are cited as one of the threats the Green Shields must stand against.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark has irrevocably committed its armies to heroic traditions, gaining the fight with honour order, permanent honourable tactics against the Jotun, and the Farsighted Fist of the Mountains and Heroic Green Shields, though at the cost of strained cooperation with allied armies using crueller methods.

Fight with monsters.o: After the Wintermark Assembly upheld Gunnbrand Ironwill's final mandate committing the Mark to the path of the hero, Wintermark's armies permanently adopted honourable tactics against the Jotun and gained new heroic orders. Both the Fist of the Mountains and the Green Shields were offered, and took up, new army qualities.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the reawakening of heroism is described as spreading through the mountains of Hahnmark.

Kallavesa.t: The Rune-bound, a hall of mystics from all three Wintermark traditions who had tended Emperor Guntherm's resting place, emerged from the Kallavesa swamps to rejoin the Fist of the Mountains, and the reawakening of heroism is said to have begun there.

Sermersuaq.t: With Jotun warriors pushing forward across Sermersuaq, the Green Shields' heroic resolve to stand between Wintermark and her enemies is framed as more important than ever there.

Fighting fish.d: Brother Luke of the Navigators of Virtue's statement, upheld 205-32, called Sykes Loyal to a free Bregasland but told the Empire it must inspire Loyalty and heal its rifts. Stories now recast Sykes as a freedom fighter. Rebellious sentiment spread from the North Fens to Ottermire, so any future rising would be worse, though not more likely, and the mood is calmer than feared. Old Harry renamed his Ottery tavern Sykes' End. After the Spring Equinox, congregations preaching Loyalty gain extra liao and votes. Loyalty statements carried by a greater majority will be read by all assemblies, and any assembly member may now raise mandates for the eyes of Loyalty.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Sykes is newly cast as having the spirit that led the Marchers' ancestors to march out of Dawn.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun invasion of Bregasland is recalled as the opportunity Sykes tried to turn into a rebellion against the Empire.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League is not named; the page refers only to Urizen rebels being Loyal to Spiral, which the League held.

The Marches.t: Marchers are recasting Bushel Sykes as a hero who stood up for Bregasland, and some boast they will take up arms if the Empire fails to earn their Loyalty, though most are simply getting on with the planting.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Urizen rebels, whom the Loyalty assembly backed last Summer, are compared with Sykes as people Loyal to their homeland, and their situation is among the topics congregations want to hear about.

Fighting fish.o: In Spring 386YE the Loyalty assembly upheld Brother Luke's judgement acknowledging the Loyalty of the late Bregas poacher Bushel Sykes while challenging the Empire to earn its citizens' Loyalty, turning Sykes into a romanticised folk hero and drawing wider attention to the assembly.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: The rebellious sentiment of the North Fens' unhappy households has spread beyond the region into Ottermire.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: Rebellious feeling has spread to Ottermire, where folk boast of following Sykes's example, and Old Harry's Ottery tavern, renamed Sykes' End, has become a place where drinkers toast the old poacher.

Bregasland.t: Sykes's memory is being turned into a symbol of Bregas self-reliance; if the territory ever rose in open rebellion the results would now be worse, though a rising is no more likely than before.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is named as the homeland to which the Urizen rebels are Loyal.

Figure of eight.d: Imperial law on the five religious crimes (abuse of powers, blasphemy, desecration, heresy and idolatry) stays unchanged and remains under the Senate's control. From the end of the Winter Solstice, however, priests stop condemning individuals. Instead they pass proscriptions, which the Constitutional Court scrutinises for constitutionality and clarity. The Tribune was to raise five administrative proscriptions at the summit: excommunication without a writ, dedication to false virtues, the desecration of paragon and exemplar relics, the Excessionist Heresy, and statues of eternals. The Court set out what passing or rejecting each would mean. It also flagged unresolved issues, including the Marcher orcs' heretical belief in reincarnation, fanes, and the Feast of the Broken Wheel.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: raids to free slaves from the Druj are cited as having produced spontaneous auras that appeared Anarchist in nature.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: raids to free slaves from the Grendel are cited as having produced spontaneous auras that appeared Anarchist in nature.

Imperial Orcs.t: Hap the Soft warned the Imperial Orcs assembly that Marcher orcs would face death rather than abandon their beliefs, which conflict with the Doctrine of the Howling Abyss. The magistrates also confirmed that the proposed idolatry proscription would not forbid statues honouring orcs.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher orcs' heretical belief in reincarnation is traced to their Jotun roots.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the true consecration in Holberg is cited as an example of something not protected by the current desecration law.

The Marches.t: The Marcher orcs' belief in reincarnation contradicts the Doctrine of the Howling Abyss, making it heretical. The magistrates deliberately raised no proscription on the matter but warned that the Synod must eventually either outlaw it or implicitly approve it.

Figure of eight.o: After nearly a year of review following the collapse of the trial of the 'peaceful Four', the Constitutional Court replaced the Synod's judgement of condemnation with a new judgement of proscription. Under it, the General Assembly defines which specific acts count as religious crimes, and the magistrates then enforce those definitions directly.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: under the current law it would not be illegal to try to destroy the true consecration in Holberg.

Mournwold.t: Hundreds of Marcher orcs living in the Mournwold openly reject a Doctrine of Faith. The Empire has so far looked the other way, but the issue threatens the Synod's moral authority and will have to be settled.

Figures from the past stand tall.d: Though Reikos had known peace since the last Druj holdout in Tamarbode fell in 380YE, the approach of the Winter Solstice brought far more ghosts than usual, with panicked letters flooding in from Chalcis Mount. The shades included Highborn, Druj orcs, League bravos, Urizen scholars and Navarr guides, victims of fighting in Reikos, Holberg, Therunin and Zenith, all bitter over their deaths or failures in life. The overwhelmed stewards sought help. A conjunction to the High Arboretum at 23:30 on the summit's second day, just after the Day of the Dead procession, would admit a hundred people. The civil service asked High Exorcist Alessi of the Basilisks of the Labyrinth to have the Highborn stewards lead a party from all nations to mediate with or exorcise the spirits.

Druj.t: Shades of dead orcs, mostly Druj warriors, rose among the restless dead in Reikos. The ghosts of those slain by Druj poison, flux and blood magic also bore witness to Druj cruelty.

Highguard.t: Highborn stewards of the dead in Reikos were overwhelmed by the ghosts, and the civil service asked the High Exorcist, Alessi of the Basilisks of the Labyrinth, to have the Highborn lead a party from every nation through the conjunction.

Navarr.t: Ghosts of Navarr guides appeared in Reikos crying out for aid in finding their way back to the Great Dance, alongside victims recently murdered by the Druj in Therunin.

The League.t: Ghosts of free company bravos, still in their finery, and victims of the bloody siege of Holberg were among the restless dead, and the stewards suggested League citizens might help calm them.

Urizen.t: Shades of Urizen scholars wailed over their deaths by poison or flux and their life's work cut short, and some ghosts came from those slaughtered by Druj magic in Zenith.

Figures from the past stand tall.o: In the winter of 386YE Reikos was beset by a surge of restless ghosts from the Empire's wars against the Druj, and a conjunction opened to the Gardens of High Chalcis so that a hundred Imperial citizens, led by the Highborn stewards of the dead, could lay them to rest.

Reikos/Chalcis Mount.t: Panicked citizens of Chalcis Mount sent floods of letters to priests and exorcists, and a conjunction to the High Arboretum, where most of the ghosts had gathered, opened for a hundred citizens to deal with them.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Mentioned in passing: Tamarbode is recalled as where the eternal Llofir was expelled and where the last Druj holdout fell in 380YE.

Holberg.t: Ghosts of those killed in the bloody siege of Holberg were drawn to Reikos for reasons no one could explain.

Reikos.t: Despite years of peace and healing, Reikos suffered a plague of restless ghosts from many Druj wars, too many for its local stewards of the dead to handle without help from across the Empire.

Therunin.t: Victims recently murdered by the Druj in Therunin appeared among the ghosts in Reikos, and some suspected the recent bloodshed there had called the dead forth.

Zenith.t: Ghosts of those slaughtered in Zenith by the bloody magics of the Druj were found among the restless dead in Reikos.

Finding is the final act.d: The Highborn and League Assemblies could enact a mandate creating the lecture Preach Vigilance - Investigate Sarvos; if at least 40 congregations took part, Sentinel Gate opportunities to expose and potentially shut down the ring would follow at the Spring Equinox 388YE, at a cost of four thrones of Sarvos tax for the season. The Sarvosan Chamber of Commerce could vote to send orcs of the College of the Liberated to help, cutting the congregations needed by ten but losing the College's extra money. The Vigilance Assembly could send the Silent Bell to investigate every Bay of Catazar territory for six months. The Whisper Gallery offered an illegal venture to exploit the ring, and Sofia di Sarvos offered weirwood for Bay of Catazar spy networks in exchange for roseweald.

Grendel.t: Grendel spy networks in Sarvos were targeted for exposure and possible dismantling, and the Silent Bell might confirm which Bay of Catazar territories host Grendel agents.

Highguard.t: Joran of Reikos's judgement of peerless kinship meant Highborn congregations could be mandated to travel to Sarvos and help uncover the espionage ring alongside the League.

The League.t: League congregations, the Sarvosan Chamber of Commerce and merchant Sofia di Sarvos were all offered ways to fight the Grendel spies in Sarvos, though the investigation would cost the city four thrones of tax for a season.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: a judgement by Asteria of Ocean Kites Root in the Urizen Assembly helped inspire the Silent Bell's proposed survey of the Bay of Catazar.

Finding is the final act.o: Following religious judgements in the Vigilance, Highborn and League Assemblies, opportunities arose in Winter 387YE to root out the Grendel espionage ring in Sarvos, survey the Bay of Catazar for spy rings, and build new Imperial spy networks, while the Whisper Gallery offered a treasonous way to exploit the ring instead.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Silent Bell could spend six months confirming which Bay of Catazar territories host Grendel agents, and Sofia di Sarvos offered weirwood towards a spy network in an Imperial territory on the Bay.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Joran of Reikos raised the Highborn Assembly judgement calling for peerless kinship with Sarvos.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos was the focus of the effort: congregations could investigate its espionage ring, its Chamber of Commerce would vote on enlisting College of the Liberated orcs, and the disruption would reduce its tax revenue by four thrones for the season.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the espionage ring in Spiral was noted to remain, though damaged by order of the Senate.

Fire and the flood.d: The Boyar's Hasta, Golden Axe, Granite Pillar, Lions of Adelmar and Summer Storm fought under the Druj miasma and the Rivers of Life against the Marshlizard sept and six Druj armies that had slipped from Zenith to the Tower. Five more Druj armies struck Kroll and Turan Flats, forcing the Empire to divide its effort. Nesustak rebels helped, and the Empire won at Turan. At Jarangir's Levy the dam was breached and Imperial lines were scattered. Half the Druj then withdrew south to meet the Shield of Ipotavo, whose bound ghosts aid them. About 2,500 died on each side. A battle opportunity, a Golden Axe transformation and a conjunction followed.

Dawn.t: The Lions of Adelmar shielded their allies from spears and arrows and saved dozens of lives when the levy flooded. Alongside the Summer Storm they drew the Marshlizards' particular hatred.

Druj.t: The Druj lost around 2,500 troops. Their northern counter-attack was driven back into the Salt Flats, and a major force stayed trapped in Thornfen with the Tower weakened but standing. Their septs remained riven by rivalry.

Highguard.t: The Granite Pillar advanced carefully to spare Highborn lives, then turned north with disciplined resolve to meet the Druj armies out of the Salt Flats.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Summer Storm hunted the Druj with ruthless aggression and took the brunt of casualties at Jarangir's Levy. Soldiers who fought beside them and the Summer champion Murmastis could gain a heroic boon.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn at Sarangrave's heart is said to threaten worse than the situation in Navarr's Therunin, from which the Druj armies had earlier moved south.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman's Redgate Pass is cited as an earlier pass brought down by the Flasks of Fire and Fury.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tower of the Skink is compared to the Walls of Holberg and its siege, and Spiral is cited as a place where a mountain pass was blocked.

Urizen.t: Sarangrave was granted to Urizen, but it remained a warzone with only a handful of new spires. The Strategos Lanius was charged with killing Grettek Skinflawed, and five unidentified Urizeni captives awaited rescue.

Varushka.t: The Boyar's Hasta distinguished themselves at Jarangir's Levy. The Golden Axe, fighting beside Ser Gaspare's Summer schlacta, stayed barred from cautious orders but gained a chance to become a Victorious army.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is listed among places where mountain passes have been blocked by sabotage or destructive magic.

Fire and the flood.o: In Winter 387YE five Imperial armies pressed the Druj in Thornfen and the Tower of the Skink while also turning back a fresh Druj attack out of the Salt Flats, ending three-tenths of the way to capturing Thornfen. The Axou Shield of Ipotavo joined the assault from the south.

Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh.t: Mentioned in passing: bands of Druj lie hidden here, and the Druj armies fleeing Zenith slipped past Imperial forces in the area.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: The Druj host out of the Salt Flats pushed into Kroll, where rebels helped Imperial watchposts escape before the Empire drove the invaders back.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: The rebel former slaves and free septs holding the forest, backed by the Prince with a Thousand Foes, harried the northern Druj and warned Imperial soldiers, though they remained no friends of the Empire.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: The Empire advanced toward Sephals and the Tower of the Skink and reached three-tenths of the way to conquest. The battle at Jarangir's Levy ended in floods, and the Shield of Ipotavo attacked the Tower from the south.

Sarangrave/Turan Flats.t: The Red Lizard tried to retake Turan at Het Traaka's urging. Days of fighting burned part of the town before the Empire pushed the Druj back.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; it is linked only through the Dawnish Lions of Adelmar fighting in Sarangrave.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: the Cicatrix Vekor Amberlure is a warden of Cassad Ûln, the mountain fortress in the Forest of Ulnak.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: only the Walls of Holberg are said to surpass the Tower of the Skink, and Holberg's old siege is used as a comparison.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Redgate Pass in Kahraman was brought down by the same Flasks of Fire and Fury that the Druj sought to use.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Five Druj armies led by the Black Wind struck out of the Salt Flats into northern Sarangrave. They were forced back here by season's end, and the trapped Druj hoped to escape here too.

Sarangrave.t: The territory remained a warzone. The Empire made inroads in Thornfen and held the north, while Druj, rebels and a contained vallorn kept its grip fragile and Urizen settlement minimal.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as one of the places where a mountain pass has been blocked by sabotage or magic.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as one of the places where a mountain pass has been blocked by sabotage or magic.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj armies that conquered Therunin had moved south, and the Sarangrave vallorn is said to threaten worse than the situation there.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Druj armies had cast down the Stork's Gaze in northern Zenith before an Imperial counter-attack, then escaped under Night magic to the Tower of the Skink.

Fire on fire.d: After the Empire took Lustri, seven Druj armies were trapped in Proceris and Occursion. Imperial heroes disrupted their Night enchantment, but four armies were still shrouded. As the Druj fled toward Sarangrave, the Eastern Sky and Golden Axe held Lustri, and perhaps four thousand orcs died. The Hounds of Glory and Citadel Guard then stormed Proceris and Occursion for around three hundred Imperial casualties. Under a Highborn Assembly mandate, the Seventh Wave and Granite Pillar freed most tormented souls and destroyed many Druj warbands, so Zenith was neither terrorised nor under threat. Miasma pillars remain, Proceris is a poisoned swamp, and the territory lies devastated.

Dawn.t: Dawnish armies were central to the victory: the Eastern Sky held Lustri against the fleeing orcs, and the Hounds of Glory led the heedless charge that broke the Druj defences in Proceris and Occursion.

Druj.t: The Druj lost Zenith entirely, and perhaps four thousand orcs died fleeing through Lustri. The unshrouded Arrow Viper, Hidden Snake and Poison Blade suffered worst, and the Druj failed to leave the territory terrorised.

Highguard.t: Driven by the Highborn Assembly's mandate, the Seventh Wave and Granite Pillar freed most of the tormented souls, many forged from captured Highborn soldiers, and hunted down Druj guerrilla camps. Some displaced Urizen have begun new lives in Highguard.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is cited as an earlier example of Druj spite in destroying what they cannot hold.

Urizen.t: Zenith was freed, with the Citadel Guard helping to trap and assault the Druj. However, the Urizen return to shattered spires and ruined farms, and many exiles have settled elsewhere and may be reluctant to come home.

Varushka.t: The Golden Axe held fast in Lustri alongside the Eastern Sky and inflicted a heavy toll on the fleeing Druj armies.

Fire on fire.o: In Winter 384YE the Empire liberated Zenith after trapping seven Druj armies there; the fleeing orcs were cut down in Lustri, and Imperial forces then retook Proceris and Occursion and cleared much of the Druj legacy.

Zenith/Lustri.t: The hostile, magically roused forests of Lustri became a killing ground for the fleeing Druj, whose bodies now rot among the ancient trees. Granite Pillar scouts later rooted out guerrilla camps in its far reaches.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Imperial heroes disrupted the Druj Night ritual at the Glade of Night Enshrouding in Occursion. Its mountains were then retaken, and Druj hiding in its caves were hunted down.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Proceris fell after an assault on the Druj night fortress that caused most Imperial casualties. It remains a poisoned swamp full of venomous bog octopuses, its great farms are gone, and its lingering Night magic enhances Dripping Echoes of the Fen regardless of who casts it.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as a place where the Empire has previously seen the Druj destroy what they could not control.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: some displaced Zenith Urizen have begun establishing new lives in Morrow.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as a recent example of Druj guerrillas left behind to trouble defenders after the armies were driven out.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: some displaced Zenith Urizen have begun establishing new lives in Redoubt.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: cited, alongside Holberg, as a place that suffered Druj spite when they lost control.

Sarangrave.t: The surviving Druj armies fled north into Sarangrave, where Citadel Guard magic stopped them venturing further. Ghulai allies from Sarangrave were scattered at the Glade of Night Enshrouding.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky's general, Dame Aurum De Castellan, styles herself the star of Semmerholm.

Zenith.t: Zenith was freed and secured, with most tormented souls laid to rest and remaining Druj bands scattered. It is left devastated, with miasma pillars still to be removed and rebuilding under discussion by the Senate and Synod.

Fit and proper.d: At the Spring Equinox 382YE the Conclave refused to reconcile Rivers Run Red, then passed declarations reaffirming virtuous magicians' right to use curses and instructing the Voice of the Quiet Forest to cast the curse on Therunin. Many magicians across the Empire felt this undermined the Conclave's moral authority and implied interdiction could be ignored. Camila i Erigo proposed that the Senate create a Declaration of Endorsement so the Conclave could lawfully approve particular uses, expecting more interdictions as a result. The Constitutional Court saw no objection in principle but needs a clearly worded Senate motion addressing targets, timing, who is endorsed and eternals under enmity, and would not allow open-ended endorsement of individuals. The proposal awaits a senator to take it up.

Navarr.t: Navarr magicians, the Voice of the Quiet Forest, were told by the Conclave to cast the interdicted Rivers Run Red on Therunin, the very defiance of interdiction that sparked the controversy over the Conclave's authority.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn magician Camila i Erigo leads the push for a Declaration of Endorsement, and one of the two contested declarations was raised by Alejandra i Erigo.

Fit and proper.o: After the Conclave kept Rivers Run Red interdicted yet instructed the Voice of the Quiet Forest to cast it on Therunin, the Freeborn magician Camila i Erigo of Kahraman proposed a new Declaration of Endorsement allowing the Conclave to approve specific uses of interdicted rituals or items.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Camila i Erigo, the proposal's author, is described as coming from the hills of Kahraman.

Therunin.t: Therunin was the target of the interdicted Rivers Run Red curse that the Conclave instructed the Voice of the Quiet Forest to cast there, prompting the debate on interdiction.

Five flames.d: The Court of the Five Winds welcomed work beginning on Yakholme Grange and the prospect of trade with Dawn. Faraden expected to renew its peace treaty with the Jotun at the Summer Solstice. A true consecration of the Temple of the High Flames, made possible by liao from the Imperial Gatekeepers, weakened Asavean religious influence but cooled Faraden interest in the Way. Ambassador Mistress Singua Karadragha sought assurance that the Synod's new proscriptions on Vengeance, which the Empire holds to be the same as Faraden's flame of Justice, would not apply to Faraden travellers. The Cinders' leaders were tried and executed, including Zuchlagch, who was burned at the stake. The Lictors offered a chamber for Asavean Tommaso Triusti's trial and requested testimony from Imperial Spymaster Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo.

Dawn.t: The Court of the Five Winds was pleased that Faraden trade with Dawn might be moving forward, and saw that overland trade with the Empire avoided the perils of the sea routes the Asaveans depend on.

Jotun.t: Faraden could not afford war with the Jotun and seemed certain to renew its peace treaty with them at the Summer Solstice, though Mistress Karadragha expected Suranni adventurism to help her nation extract some concessions.

Five flames.o: Faraden remained caught between the Empire and the Asavean Archipelago in Spring 388YE, pressing for closer trade with the Empire while the Synod's proscriptions on Vengeance troubled its faithful. Its authorities also crushed the Cinders extremists and arrested an Asavean merchant accused of funding them.

Reinos.t: Faraden lies beyond the Lasambrian Hills of Jotun-held Reinos. Mistress Karadragha's hope that the Empire would join an attack on Reinos came to nothing, as the Military Council's focus lay elsewhere.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the dangers of the Sea of Snow were cited as one reason Faraden merchants prefer overland trade with the Empire to Asavean shipping routes.

Fixing What is Broken.d: The Marcher Assembly had passed two statements with primacy, by Nicolas Reaper and Sister Meredith, urging threshers to bring sorcerers to Imperial justice and calling cursing treason. Threshers feared risking their lives only for the law to do nothing, since no one was punished for the earlier curses or for Navarr flouting the interdiction. A proposed Marcher Assembly mandate would reassure them, reinvigorating threshers to hunt sorcerers Empire-wide, but would risk apoplectic anger if future curses go unpunished. Alisoun Bathwater instead asked the Vigilance Assembly to endorse threshers dealing with sorcerers by any means necessary, reviving the old tradition of direct action. The two mandates are not in competition and would inspire different groups of threshers.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Alisoun Bathwater jibes that Imperial law works best when instructed by a Dawnishman, and notes the Cardinal of Vigilance she appeals to is Dawnish.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr are cited as having flouted the interdiction on Rivers Run Red without anyone being punished.

The Marches.t: Marcher threshers, unsettled by fears that the curse interdiction might be lifted, could be steered either towards lawful pursuit of sorcerers through a Marcher Assembly mandate or towards direct action through a Vigilance Assembly mandate, both still only proposals.

Fixing What is Broken.o: Three years after Imperial curses devastated the Mournwold, Marcher threshers grew uneasy that the Conclave might lift its interdiction on Rivers Run Red, and two competing Synod mandates were proposed. One would urge lawful action against sorcerers; the other would back threshers acting by any means necessary.

Mournwold.t: The memory of the Mournwold's devastation by Imperial curses three years earlier is the root of the threshers' anger and the debate over how to deal with sorcerers.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Alisoun Bathwater suggests the Empire's response would have been very different had Rivers Run Red and Mountain Murders the Children been used on Semmerholm.

Flames and the dark.d: Thanks to Umarth "Winter's Flame" Kannask and the Fist of the Mountains, Elos escaped the worst, and no major Senate repairs were needed. The Grendel instead looted spire libraries and citadel armouries for anything magical, and used Sky magic to strip the Night aspect from the Tilphussian Reach. Sadogua, the Whisper Gallery, the Azoth and Phaleron each offered to rebuild it, all needing a Conclave declaration of acceptance. Phaleron's offer was accepted, and the arcane projection to entreat the guardian Phoebus Al-Pulpi was delivered in Summer 388YE. Umarth's prophecy about retaking Elos also gave the Synod an opportunity to consecrate the docks with true liao, binding Wintermark and Urizen.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: their incursions are cited as usually requiring major Senate repairs, and their past attack on Canterspire is recalled as when Phaleron first intervened.

Grendel.t: Grendel invaders were driven from Redoubt, but they carried off arcane texts and magical equipment and used Sky magic to wreck the Tilphussian Reach's Night aspect, for purposes that remained unknown.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the in-character scene features Myfanwy and Gavyn of the Black Thorns arguing on the ruined Elos docks.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs are noted as an exception to Grendel naval dominance, and the Azoth's cauldron would grow marsh flowers last seen in Madruga.

Urizen.t: Urizen's spires recovered Redoubt but lost arcane texts and the Tower of Light and Shadow. Its magicians weighed four eternal offers to restore the regio, and the Conclave chose Phaleron's guardian, which would fall under the Emissary to the Celestial Library rather than the Penumbral Watcher.

Wintermark.t: Umarth "Winter's Flame" Kannask and the Fist of the Mountains were credited with saving Elos, and Umarth's prophecy about the banner raised at the docks opened a chance for the Synod to consecrate the site and tie Wintermark and Urizen together.

Flames and the dark.o: After six months of occupation, the Grendel were driven from Redoubt, leaving surprisingly little general damage but having looted arcane equipment and texts and devastated the Tower of Light and Shadow on the Tilphussian Reach. Four eternals offered ways to restore the regio, and the Conclave accepted Phaleron's proposal.

Redoubt/Naris.t: The Tilphussian Reach in Naris lost its tower and nearly all its Night aspect. With Phaleron's offer accepted, the regio would be aligned to the Celestial Library and guarded by Phoebus Al-Pulpi, making Naris harder to conquer.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel sought to reaffirm their naval stranglehold on the bay, and Phaleron's guardian would remain until the last Spine-Cracker navy is sunk in the Catazar.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the Azoth's proposed cauldron would grow marsh flowers last seen in Madruga.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is not named directly; the page concerns events in neighbouring Redoubt.

Redoubt.t: Freed from the Grendel, Redoubt found its spire libraries and citadel armouries stripped of magic but little other damage, leaving Elos ready for possible dock expansion and the consecration of the site where Umarth's banner was raised.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Gavyn of the Black Thorns hails from Therunin and jokes that nothing that swims there is fit to eat.

Flight of birds.d: Guided by the Raven Seer, the mystics found that a new Kallavesi army, which the Senate could authorise at any time, might be relentless, glorious or resourceful. Leofric, following swans into the Sovevann, discovered the ruined Hall of the Soturi. Restoring it would allow one fearless army. Alternatively, a Hall of Names recording Wintermark's named heroes would allow one named army. The two commissions are mutually exclusive. The mystics also asked Wilda, the Wintermark egregore, to call a Witan at the summit so the nation could choose a single Wintermark-relevant problem for them to appraise. They would present at least one opportunity by the following summit.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fist of the Mountains is said to have died defending Urizen against the depredations of the Grendel.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's lost army gave its lives defending the people of Urizen in Redoubt.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark could raise a new Kallavesi army, gaining the fearless or named quality by commissioning one of two rival halls. The mystics of Ishal also called on the nation to assemble a Witan and choose the problem they should next appraise.

Flight of birds.o: The mystics of Ishal, having divined how Wintermark might raise a new Kallavesi army to replace the destroyed Fist of the Mountains, asked for a Witan to direct their next appraisal. They also revealed two rival opportunities to rebuild a ruined hall in the Sovevann.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: The ruined Hall of the Soturi lies deep in the Sovevann here. Either the restored hall or the Hall of Names could be commissioned as an edifice on its site, the former before the end of Autumn Equinox 388YE.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa is the source of any new army, drawing on its fearless warriors, foragers and named heroes. A Hall of Names would especially stir the Pride and Loyalty of the often-overlooked Kallavesi.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is where the Fist of the Mountains was destroyed in battle.

Tsirku.t: Mentioned in passing: the mystics confirmed they could investigate Tsirku, as they consider Sydanjaa part of Wintermark's cultural traditions.

Fly high.d: Holmauer, ruined during the Druj occupation, was transformed into a grand park with orchards, a bathhouse, an open-air venue and the Imperial Menagerie. Merchant-princes proposed turning Holfried into a garden city (60 wains of weirwood, 40 of white granite, 25 Thrones), with a University alternative producing healing herbs. The menagerie could be expanded for 20 weirwood and 5 Thrones. Monoliths boosted League-owned mana sites, allowing either expansion of the Tassato Mana Exchange or new exchanges in the other cities. Meanwhile Bite, a blue powder heightening confidence and aggression, spread from Holberg, fuelling bravo brawls. The Senate declined the garden city but commissioned the Temeschwar and Sarvos Mana Exchanges; the menagerie opportunity remains open.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish are said to have severely bloodied the Druj's noses in Semmerholm.

Druj.t: The Druj have left Holberg and show no sign of returning, their attention now turned to Dawn and Urizen, where they have reportedly suffered heavily in Semmerholm.

The League.t: The League's cities flourished with three completed great works and new mana exchanges in Temeschwar and Sarvos, though the Senate passed on the Holberg garden city and the narcotic Bite spread among its bravos.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is named alongside Dawn as where Druj attention now seems focused.

Fly high.o: In Winter 381YE the League celebrated the completion of the Blood Red Roads, the Grand Park of Holmauer and Lorenzo's Legacy of Virtue monoliths, opening opportunities for a garden city in Holberg, an expanded Imperial Menagerie and new mana exchanges, while a new narcotic called Bite spread among the bravos of the League cities.

Holberg/Holfried.t: Merchant-princes proposed turning war-scarred Holfried into a garden city or a source of healing herbs, but the Senate declined and the opportunity expired.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Holmauer's ruined suburbs were transformed into the Grand Park with the Imperial Menagerie, whose expansion with exotic beasts remains open for the Senate to commission.

Holberg.t: Holberg completed its Grand Park and was offered a garden city transformation, which the Senate declined, while Bite originated here and bravo brawls increased.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos gained a Mana Exchange commissioned by the Senate, while Bite began to appear and brawls rose to a lesser degree.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish are reported to have badly bloodied the Druj in Semmerholm.

Tassato.t: The Tassato Mana Exchange could have been dramatically expanded, though the Senate instead built exchanges elsewhere, and Bite-fuelled brawls between bravos increased here.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar gained a Mana Exchange commissioned by the Senate, benefiting from Lorenzo's monolith, while Bite began to appear on its streets.

Focused and methodical.d: Frederick refused Viviane de Coeurdefer's request to design ten national colleges and to tour the Empire teaching. Instead he toured existing centres of learning and proposed four projects. One was expanding Holberg University with a Faculty of Architecture that would add an extra commission. Another was rebuilding Diora University in Sarvos with a College of Autumn Magic. A third was restoring the Lepidean Library in Highguard with a liao-producing Garden of Atun. The last was founding a School of Shipbuilding in Siroc. At the Winter Solstice no project was commissioned. Frederick paused all work pending an Inquisition called by Ranae de Rondell. The Lepidean Library was later commissioned in Winter 383YE. After Frederick left for the Commonwealth in 385YE, the opportunity closed.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Cardinal of Ambition, Viviane de Coeurdefer, prompted the opportunity with her Statement of Endeavour. Frederick rejected her specific requests for ten national colleges and a teaching tour, though her challenge inspired his alternative proposals.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj destruction of the Halls of Knowledge is cited as a reason to found a centralised college of magic at Diora.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel invasion of Sarvos is blamed for Diora University's troubles, and the Siroc school's site under the Salt Guard would make it harder for the Grendel to burn down.

Highguard.t: Highguard was offered the restoration of the Lepidean Library, which Nicovar had burned. The Heirs of Lepidus pledged to cover its labour and first upkeep if its Librarian became a Highborn national appointment. The library was eventually commissioned in Winter 383YE.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Frederick dismissed the idea of a university in a tiny Hercynian steading as a pointless folly.

The League.t: Three of the four proposals centred on League figures and cities: Frederick himself, the expansion of Holberg University and the renovation of Diora University in Sarvos. The Diora Chair of Dramaturgy was also floated as a possible League national title.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Frederick visited far Kalpaheim during his tour of the Empire's centres of learning.

Focused and methodical.o: Master architect Frederick di Sarvos answered the Cardinal of Ambition's Statement of Endeavour by offering four ambitious, white-granite-heavy proposals for Imperial centres of learning. The Senate could commission only one, and none was raised that Winter.

Bastion/Woodbury.t: Under the Lepidean Library proposal, the Heirs of Lepidus would move their books to the new library and eventually abandon their modest chapter house in Woodbury.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Under the Holberg proposal, the new arts campus would be built within Holmauer Park, and Katarzyna Von Carstein would be asked to lead that section of the work.

Bastion.t: The White City in Bastion was proposed as the site of a restored Lepidean University and Library, enclosing the park that stands on the ruins Nicovar left. The library would include the Garden of Atun, producing an extra dose of true liao each season.

Bay of Catazar.t: Under the proposal, a Siroc School of Shipbuilding would let navies built there, and later any Imperial navy built on the Bay, gain a unique quality. It would also spark a wave of naval enthusiasm across the Bay.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Frederick used a tiny Hercynian steading as his example of where a university would be nothing but a giant folly.

Holberg.t: Holberg University, home of Frederick's own faculty, was offered four new faculties and a five-storey Faculty of Architecture tower. The expansion would also permanently upgrade the Wunderkind and Leger Domain.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim was among the places Frederick visited on his tour of centres of learning.

Sarvos.t: Diora University in Sarvos was proposed for a sweeping rebuild with mithril-mirrored towers and an international College of Autumn Magic and Dramaturgy. The Siroc school could also revive the Sarvos Arsenal and Dockyard opportunity.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato's decorative woodwork is one of the influences in Frederick's sketches for the Faculty of Architecture tower.

Fog on the brine.d: On the last night of the half-moon before the Equinox, a pearlescent, phosphorescent mist rose six or seven feet above the sea along the coasts of Feroz, Madruga, Sarvos, Necropolis, Redoubt and Spiral. It covers the northern half of the Bay, beginning a little over a dozen miles south of Feroz, follows only salt water, chokes the mouths of the four great rivers and resists sun and wind. It troubles fisherfolk and small boats and hides reefs and rocks, causing upsets for foreign ships, though Imperial traders who know the waters pass through. Detect magic reveals only a 30th magnitude Night effect that conceals information, including about itself. Magicians suggest The Eye of the High Places could examine it.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn merchant grumbles that the fog might be some magician's work to protect against the Grendel, and their coast at Spiral is among those affected.

Highguard.t: Highguard's coastline at Necropolis was shrouded by the fog, adding to the hazards for its fisherfolk and small craft.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn coasts of Feroz and Madruga were engulfed; some greeted the fog with impromptu night-time parties and boat trips, though their fisherfolk soon found it gloomy and dangerous.

The League.t: Sarvos's shores were blanketed, prompting revelry among some boat owners at first, before the persistent fog began to hamper fishing and cause accidents.

Urizen.t: The Urizeni coast at Redoubt was among those where the fog appeared, bringing the same hazards to small boats and fishing.

Fog on the brine.o: In Autumn 379YE a strange, faintly glowing magical fog rose without warning from the Bay of Catazar, blanketing the northern half of the Bay and lingering with no sign of dissipating.

Bay of Catazar.t: The whole northern half of the Bay lies beneath an impenetrable magical fog that conceals reefs and rocks, troubles small boats and foreign ships, yet leaves night skies unusually clear for star navigation.

Feroz.t: The fog rose along Feroz's coast and was found to begin a little over a dozen miles south of its tip; revellers took boats out to explore it on the first night.

Madruga.t: Madruga's coast was cloaked in the fog, which locals initially suspected was more magicians' meddling with the sky like that already seen in the territory.

Necropolis.t: The fog settled along Necropolis's coastline, lapping occasionally onto the shore but never spreading inland.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt's shores were covered by the fog, making the waters hazardous for fishing boats and smaller vessels.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos saw impromptu parties and boat trips into the glowing fog on the first night, followed by growing concern as it lingered, hindered fisherfolk and caused accidents.

Spiral.t: The fog appeared along Spiral's coast at the same moment as elsewhere around the Bay, shrouding its waters.

Foggy mountain top.d: House Vexille's shroud lifted, but a strengthened magnitude-fifty Night shroud persisted over Semmerholm and the Barrens, making naga there unusually secretive. Distil the Serpent's Stone kept producing shadow eggs. Aleksandra's Watch in Karsk was finished early with Autumn magic, and a serpent-garrisoned castle briefly rose in the Morass.
