Richard of Holberg offered designs for menhirs in Mournwold, a loom on Starstep in Morrow (later lost in 385YE) and a garden in Tassato. Eleonaris became patron of the Icy Crag, Jaheris sought his champions, Sadogua sought a lost medallion, Donum hunted orc-enslavement relics, hare-marked briars aided Zenith and Mournwold, and the Senate's treasure ship was sunk for Rhianos.

Dawn.t: House Vexille's star-shroud lifted across most of the Empire but persisted, strengthened, over Dawnish Semmerholm, where the koboldi hope to rebuild the Gate and Eleonaris's attention is fixed on Dawn.

Druj.t: The shroud hiding the stars remained over the Druj-held Barrens, while the castle that rose in the Morass resembled a mirror-image of the old Druj fortress at Rebeshof.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Richard of Holberg is described as having been rescued from the Grendel by Imperial heroes the previous Summer.

Imperial Orcs.t: The sinister herald Donum was seen in Skarsind questioning antiquity collectors, miners and historians, seeking relics of orc enslavement in exchange for old coins, heart's blood and minor boons.

Jotun.t: The stars, hidden for a year over Jotun-held Liathaven, returned to its night skies along with the rest of the Empire.

The League.t: A Night-born castle garrisoned by serpent heralds friendly only to League citizens briefly rose in Holberg, Richard of Holberg offered a garden design for Tassato, Donum prowled Temeschwar, and a Madrugan senator paid for the ship sacrificed to Rhianos.

The Marches.t: Richard of Holberg designed a network of menhirs for Mournwold offering crystal mana and protection from curses, and hare-marked briars came to aid struggling Mournwold farmers and refugees.

Thule.t: Thule orcs in Krevsaty reportedly took considerable interest in the Autumn magic used to complete Aleksandra's Watch early.

Urizen.t: Urizen lost the Halls of Knowledge from Zenith only for the college to reappear, empty, in Peregro in Morrow, and was offered a design for a starlight loom on Starstep in Operus.

Varushka.t: Aleksandra's Watch in Karsk was completed early, Eleonaris became patron of the Icy Crag in Miekarova, Donum roamed Varushka seeking orc-enslavement relics, and Sadogua's heralds hinted his lost medallion went to the Gremani family.

Foggy mountain top.o: A season of strange magic swept the Empire: the stars returned everywhere except the Barrens and Semmerholm, the Halls of Knowledge vanished from Zenith and reappeared in Peregro, and Richard of Holberg published designs for three magical structures. Several eternals also stirred, from new emissaries and boons to the mysterious withdrawal of Murit and Soghter.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: Mentioned in passing: witnesses realised the Morass castle looked like a mirror-image of the Druj castle that once stood at Rebeshof.

Holberg/The Morass.t: An enchanted fortress of mud and mist, guarded by serpent heralds hostile to all but League citizens, rose here and sank back before the Solstice.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: Thule orcs in Krevsaty showed considerable interest in the magic used to finish Aleksandra's Watch.

Karsk/Lestasny.t: Mentioned in passing: reports from Lestasny describe the interest shown in the magic used to build Aleksandra's Watch.

Morrow/Operus.t: Richard of Holberg proposed a grand loom atop the Day-aligned regio on Starstep, a design later lost after the 385YE Cold Sun attacks.

Morrow/Peregro.t: The Halls of Knowledge materialised intact but lifeless beside one of Peregro's largest hot springs.

Tassato/Madeiras.t: A ruined, ivy-covered tower with a weirwood tree in northern Madeiras was proposed as the site of Richard of Holberg's Watcher of the Wheel garden.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Senate's treasure ship Adventure was sailed into the bay and scuttled, and Rhianos consumed it in a storm.

Holberg.t: A dripping castle of mud, black stone and solid mist, garrisoned by spear-wielding serpent heralds, rose in the Morass after the Autumn Equinox and sank again before the Winter Solstice.

Karsk.t: The Senate-commissioned fortification Aleksandra's Watch was completed several months ahead of schedule through powerful Autumn magic.

Liathaven.t: The stars, absent for a year over Liathaven, were fully restored to its skies by the week before the summit.

Miekarova.t: Eleonaris, the Lion of Summer, became patron of the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, and is likely to send someone to meet its Master of Ice and Darkness.

Morrow.t: The Halls of Knowledge reappeared in Peregro, and Richard of Holberg designed a loom on Starstep in Operus to spin starlight into prismatic ink for a Weaver of Stars.

Mournwold.t: Richard of Holberg proposed menhirs across the territory providing crystal mana and protection from curses, while hare-marked briars offered food, labour and healing to the needy.

Semmerholm.t: A strengthened Night shroud of magnitude fifty kept the stars hidden and blocked lesser scrying, naga spending time there grew intensely secretive, and the koboldi hoped to rebuild its Gate.

Skarsind.t: The herald Donum was seen talking to collectors, quarry workers and historians in Skarsind, seeking relics of orc enslavement.

Tassato.t: Richard of Holberg designed a night-flowering garden at a ruined weirwood tower in Madeiras, creating a Watcher of the Wheel who would harvest magical materials each season if built.

Temeschwar.t: The herald Donum was seen in Temeschwar seeking relics related to orc enslavement from antiquarians and workers.

The Barrens.t: The shroud hiding the stars persisted over the Barrens, impeding scrying, and naga who spent time there became markedly secretive.

Zenith.t: The Halls of Knowledge vanished into shimmering mist, leaving a shallow mountain lake and some scholars unaccounted for, while hare-marked briars aided Zenith's needy.

Folklore.d: The General Assembly could pass one of three competing mandates. Work and Worship would boost production in the nations that had welcomed them. Study and Spirituality would bring 36 rings to every congregation. Inspiration and Understanding would swell sinecures and sacred sites. Passing any of them would end the Pride bonus from Rafael Barossa di Tassato's denunciation of the Asavean Architect's idols. Highguard's assembly could fund the training of about a hundred Free Folk priests at the cost of business production. The Free Folk planned to return to Anvil for the Day of the Dead and demanded the return of their miraculous effigy, threatening legal action. Recognising a Divine Family member as paragon or exemplar, or a permissive mandate, would clear their path to citizenship.

Dawn.t: Dawn, where the Free Folk are based and had been welcomed by the Earl of Fools's statement, would see a one-rank bonus to every farm in Astolat, Semmerholm and Weirwater if the Work and Worship mandate passed.

Highguard.t: The Highborn could enact a mandate costing every Highguard business a rank of production for the year to train around a hundred Free Folk priests in Highborn doctrine. The Inspiration mandate would also enrich congregations in Bastion and Necropolis.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the nations where the Free Folk had so far spent little time.

The League.t: Congregations in Tassato and Temeschwar would lose the liao and votes they gained from Rafael Barossa di Tassato's anti-idolatry mandate if any pilgrimage mandate passed. The Free Folk had so far spent little time in the League.

The Marches.t: Already visited by the Free Folk and explicitly welcomed through Tom Keeper's statement, the Marches would see a one-rank bonus to every farm in Mitwold, Mournwold and Upwold under the Work and Worship mandate.

Urizen.t: The Study and Spirituality and Divine Family mandates would only reach Urizen with a greater majority, and failing that the Free Folk might face future problems there. Redoubt's congregations would lose their anti-idolatry bonus if any pilgrimage mandate passed.

Varushka.t: Varushka had welcomed the Free Folk through Radomír Oleksandrovych Dvorak's statement and could gain extra metal and materials with a greater majority. Karsk would lose its anti-idolatry bonus regardless of majority, and without a greater majority on the Divine Family mandate the Free Folk might face future problems there.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark, which welcomed the Free Folk through Rikke's statement, would see bonuses to herb gardens in Kallavesa, mines in Hahnmark and farms in Sermersuaq under the Work and Worship mandate. Hahnmark's congregations would lose their anti-idolatry bonus if any pilgrimage mandate passed.

Folklore.o: Following the Autumn statements of principle urging the Empire to embrace them, the Free Folk planned a pilgrimage across the Imperial nations. The Synod was offered several ways to shape it and was told they would not become citizens until one of their Divine Family was recognised.

Astolat.t: Every farm in Astolat would gain a one-rank production bonus from the Winter Solstice until the Spring Equinox if the Work and Worship mandate passed.

Bastion.t: Every congregation in Bastion would gain an extra dose of liao and two Synod votes as the Free Folk visited its basilicas, if the Inspiration and Understanding mandate passed.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark's mines would gain a one-rank bonus under Work and Worship, but its congregations would lose the liao and votes from Rafael's anti-idolatry mandate if any pilgrimage mandate passed.

Kallavesa.t: Every herb garden in Kallavesa would gain a one-rank production bonus if the Work and Worship mandate passed.

Karov.t: With a greater majority on the Work and Worship mandate, every mine in Karov would produce an extra ingot and every forest an extra measure of material.

Karsk.t: Karsk's congregations would lose the liao and votes from Rafael's anti-idolatry mandate if any pilgrimage mandate passed, even without a greater majority.

Miekarova.t: With a greater majority on the Work and Worship mandate, every mine in Miekarova would produce an extra ingot and every forest an extra measure of material.

Mitwold.t: Every farm in Mitwold would gain a one-rank production bonus as the Free Folk helped clear fields, if the Work and Worship mandate passed.

Mournwold.t: Every farm in Mournwold would gain a one-rank production bonus as the Free Folk helped clear fields, if the Work and Worship mandate passed.

Necropolis.t: Every congregation in Necropolis would gain an extra dose of liao and two Synod votes as the Free Folk visited the tombs of the dead thrones, if the Inspiration and Understanding mandate passed.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt's congregations would lose the liao and votes from Rafael's anti-idolatry mandate if any pilgrimage mandate passed, even without a greater majority.

Semmerholm.t: Every farm in Semmerholm would gain a one-rank production bonus if the Work and Worship mandate passed.

Sermersuaq.t: Every farm in Sermersuaq would gain a one-rank production bonus if the Work and Worship mandate passed.

Tassato.t: Tassato's congregations would lose the liao and votes they had enjoyed since Rafael Barossa di Tassato's mandate if any pilgrimage mandate passed.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar's congregations would lose the liao and votes from Rafael's anti-idolatry mandate if any pilgrimage mandate passed.

Upwold.t: Every farm in Upwold would gain a one-rank production bonus as the Free Folk helped plant crops, if the Work and Worship mandate passed.

Volodmartz.t: With a greater majority on the Work and Worship mandate, every mine in Volodmartz would produce an extra ingot and every forest an extra measure of material.

Weirwater.t: Every farm in Weirwater would gain a one-rank production bonus if the Work and Worship mandate passed.

Follow me my friend.d: After Quickening Cold Meat raised Tassato's entombed dead to join the Fist of the Mountains, five armies gathered at Burnish: the Fist, the Bloodcloaks, the Autumn Hammers, the Summer Storm and the Bounders. They made a careful, Day-enhanced steady advance into Reinos. Ribeira fell, and the Autumn Hammers plundered it with Callidus's heralds. Bastasor was four-fifths taken, but Grismont Township and the Arena of Virtue held, and casualties were light. Some Fist soldiers grew unusually bloodthirsty. Opportunities followed: killing Carmo Stoneblade, rescuing Faraden traders, joining the Balankas Rush, and a battle at Grismont against Jarl Vafri, with the chance to capture Pastor Ximena.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel-held Feroz appears in a list of lands the Lasambrians say were stolen from them.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Corazón and Jotun from northern Reikos are said to have reinforced the Arena of Virtue's defence.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Autumn Hammers and the Summer Storm helped conquer Ribeira. The Hammers plundered rich goods with the aid of Callidus's heralds, and the Summer Storm secured access to the Crown of Bastasor. Irontide Skorr was charged with killing Carmo Stoneblade.

Jotun.t: The Jotun lost Ribeira and most of Bastasor, holding only Grismont Township and the Arena of Virtue. Jarl Vafri now commands Grismont's defence, while Carmo Stoneblade gathers a fyrd to retake Ribeira.

The Brass Coast.t: The campaign was waged to take a blade from the Freeborn's throat, with armies passing through Kahraman and Segura into Reinos. Some of the plunder recovered had clearly been stolen from Segura or Kahraman.

The League.t: Tassato's wealthy and murdered dead were torn from their tombs and the Vassa to march with the Fist of the Mountains. Many Tassatans were left furious and horrified by the desecration.

The Marches.t: The Bounders set out from Mournwold, scouted the route into Reinos and fought in the steady conquest of Ribeira and Bastasor. Their scouts also found a captive Faraden merchant who could be rescued.

Wintermark.t: The Fist of the Mountains fought beside Tassatan ghouls, which drew the enemy's contempt, and some of its soldiers grew strangely bloodthirsty amid tales of a black dog in its camp. The Bloodcloaks' healers kept losses low but found no thralls to free.

Follow me my friend.o: In Spring 387YE five Imperial armies marched from Segura into Jotun-held Reinos. They conquered Ribeira and took most of Bastasor, while the Fist of the Mountains brought along ghouls raised from the tombs of Tassato.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: Mentioned in passing: the armies marched through Braydon's Jasse, past the memorial that was once Fort Braydon.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Mentioned in passing: the armies from Mournwold passed through Southmoor on their way south.

Reinos/Bastasor.t: The Empire took four-fifths of Bastasor, including access to the Crown of Bastasor, but Grismont Township and the Arena of Virtue held out. A battle opportunity offers the chance to defeat Jarl Vafri and complete the conquest.

Reinos/Chaveiro.t: Mentioned in passing: Chaveiro is likely to fall next if nothing changes after the Spring Equinox.

Reinos/Cimeira.t: Mentioned in passing: refugees fled south to Cimeira, and Pastor Ximena had preached the Virtues as far as Cimeira.

Reinos/Pedreira.t: Mentioned in passing: commanders chose not to press west into Pedreira and its fortification, turning south instead.

Reinos/Ribeira.t: Ribeira was conquered and plundered of its oils, wines, jewellery and icons. Carmo Stoneblade is now gathering a fyrd of Jotun and Lasambrians to retake it.

Segura/Burnish.t: The plains of Burnish hosted a grand camp for five armies and six thousand independent captains before the invasion crossed into Reinos.

Tassato/Cascatas.t: Around Cascatas, the bodies of Jotun orcs and yegarra who died attacking the Sapphire Stair were raised as ghouls to join the Fist of the Mountains.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: named by the Lasambrians as one of the lands they say the Empire stole from them.

Kahraman.t: The Imperial armies marched through Kahraman on their way south to Segura, and some loot seized in Reinos had clearly been taken from Kahraman.

Kalino.t: Mentioned in passing: the Hierro claim western Kalino as ancestral land, and a captured Faraden merchant was bound for the Iron Confederacy.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: named by the Lasambrians as one of the lands they say the Empire stole from them.

Mournwold.t: The Autumn Hammers, the Summer Storm and the Bounders set out from Mournwold to join the campaign against Reinos.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Corazón and Jotun from northern Reikos reinforced the defenders of the Arena of Virtue.

Reinos.t: Reinos remains in Jotun hands, but the Empire conquered Ribeira and controls most of Bastasor. Further gains are likely after the Spring Equinox before the armies must face the fortified passes to the west.

Segura.t: Segura served as the staging ground for the invasion, with five armies and thousands of independent captains camping at Burnish before crossing west into Reinos.

Tassato.t: Quickening Cold Meat raised the territory's entombed and murdered dead as ghouls, leaving shattered tombs on both sides of the Vassa and an angry populace. No living citizens were harmed.

For the Common Good.d: Militärattache Ludkhannah Schöningen reported that the war with Jarm had left the Commonwealth on the back foot against Jarmish magic. They asked for Imperial mercenaries, which would need a Senate motion. They warned that any further military rituals given to Jarm would breach the Liberty Pact, which they believed was doomed by Axos's vote. They offered a fortified embassy to replace the one the Grendel destroyed in Madruga, and an ilium-selling ministry, the Sternenmetal Tower. They also voiced suspicion of Imperial interest in Rachensgrab and thanked the Empire for a storm warning and the Gatekeepers for their restraint. The Senate built the diplomatenschloss in Necropolis. The Sternenmetal Tower remained available until the end of Spring Equinox 387YE.

Grendel.t: The Grendel destroyed the Commonwealth embassy in Madruga when Siroc burned, and their violent presence in the Bay of Catazar made trade there difficult. The new embassy was offered as a fortification partly so it would be harder for them to destroy.

Highguard.t: The Senate chose Highguard's territory of Necropolis for the new Commonwealth diplomatenschloss, an embassy that doubles as a fortification garrisoned by Commonwealth soldiers.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn lost the Commonwealth embassy in Madruga when the Grendel burned Siroc, where Commonwealth soldiers had died alongside them. Freeborn corsairs had helped keep Bay of Catazar trade going until the storm warning drove Commonwealth merchants elsewhere.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule were cited as a nation the Empire deals with on its own terms, and as a possible future Liberty Pact member the Commonwealth feared would dilute its voice.

Urizen.t: The Commonwealth insisted that its new embassy must not be built in Urizen's Redoubt, fearing the danger of placing it close to the Jarmish embassy.

For the Common Good.o: In Summer 386YE the Commonwealth, locked in war with Jarm over Lantir, sought Imperial mercenaries, mana and a new embassy while voicing deep pessimism about the Liberty Pact. The Senate commissioned a fortified Commonwealth embassy, a diplomatenschloss, in Necropolis.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Commonwealth wanted its new embassy somewhere on the Bay because it was easiest to reach, despite the area being a Grendel-infested warzone. Commonwealth shipping there fell sharply after the Imperial warning of magical storms.

Madruga.t: The old Commonwealth embassy in Madruga had been destroyed by the Grendel when Siroc burned, prompting the plan to build a replacement.

Necropolis.t: The Senate commissioned the Commonwealth diplomatenschloss in Necropolis. It was to be both an embassy and a rank one fortification garrisoned by Commonwealth soldiers.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt was explicitly ruled out as a site for the new Commonwealth embassy because of the risk of placing it near the Jarmish embassy.

For those in peril on the sea.d: Cyrus, senator for Reikos, seconded by Pathfinder Gaddak of Mareave, asked for the appraisal to guard against new eternal threats and restore national Pride. Experts from the Brass Coast, League, Highguard, Urizen and the Unshackled met in Sarvos, joined by Fotismos, herald of Kimus. Plans for lighthouse edifices and fleet-boosting great lighthouses were made available. The Shining Pillar cannot be rebuilt because a maelstrom has devoured its island. The Celesti Lighthouse could instead be restored, or rebuilt as a fortified great lighthouse that lifts Oranseri's abandoned quality, and Kimus offers an infused light enabling a Bay patrol voyage and the Broken Shore Bounty. Eilian asks the Senate to approve a year-long sabbatical to study further sites.

Grendel.t: Sannite delegates said the Grendel prize lighthouses, with Salt Lords paying their keepers, and that Rahab's endorsement of the looting of the Celesti Lighthouse troubled traditional Grendel lords. An infused Celesti light would remind Grendel navies of Freeborn defiance.

Highguard.t: Highborn architects joined the symposium, recalling the lost Pharos of Necropolis as a symbol of Vigilance. Their tower-building skill and Highguard warning bells feature in the fortified Celesti proposal.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Unshackled of Mareave attended, newly appreciative of lighthouses now that they hold a coastline. They pointed to the ruined lighthouse at Icarion and a smaller one above the docks at Beoraidh.

The Brass Coast.t: Lighthouses carry near-spiritual meaning for the Freeborn, and the loss of the Shining Pillar and the Celesti Lighthouse hurt corsair families deeply. The proposals would restore the Celesti Lighthouse, its Keeper title and possibly the Broken Shore Bounty.

The League.t: League delegates valued lighthouses as practical symbols of Prosperity and their mirror-masters claim unrivalled skill. The unbuilt Caricomare lighthouse of Sarvos is one of the six sites proposed for further study.

Urizen.t: An Urizen speaker championed lighthouses as symbols of illumination and sanctuary, and Urizen lightstone craft is essential to great beacons. The lost Lighthouse of Nikephoros and the lighthouses of Naris are both candidates for Eilian's further study.

For those in peril on the sea.o: Prognosticator Eilian Sweetwater delivered a Senate-commissioned appraisal on restoring the great lighthouses of the Bay of Catazar, after a symposium in Sarvos attended by a herald of the eternal Kimus. He set out plans for standard and great lighthouses, proposals to restore or fortify the Celesti Lighthouse in Feroz, and an offer to spend a year studying six more sites.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Mentioned in passing: the Children of Wrecks' continued control of the Cazar Straits is why Eilian proposes a fortified lighthouse, and the old Celesti beacon once guided ships through Cazar's isles and sandbanks.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Both Celesti Lighthouse commissions would be built here. The fortified version would defend the region, let fleets guard it from the sea and remove its abandoned quality, encouraging Freeborn to resettle Oran.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: The Shining Pillar once stood here but is now destroyed. Its island has been devoured by a maelstrom said to open into Siakha's realm, so it cannot be rebuilt.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: a smaller lighthouse stands above the docks, and Beoraidh's bazaars gossip about Rahab's looting of the Celesti Lighthouse.

Mareave/Icarion.t: The ruined Light of Virtue, built in an old Urizen style on the clifftops, is a site Eilian is keen to revisit and a candidate for further study.

Necropolis/Coursmouth.t: The great Pharos stood on these cliffs until it was burned in the civil war. Eilian believes a rebuilt lighthouse here could draw strength from its link to Atuman.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Naris holds the destroyed Lighthouse of Nikephoros and the lighthouses linked to the port of Elos, both proposed for study, with the herald Fotismos especially interested.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: The Caricomare lighthouse planned here was never built because of economic realities, and it is a candidate for Eilian's further study.

Bay of Catazar.t: The appraisal surveyed the Bay's lost great lighthouses amid fears that an unknown eternal threat lurks in its depths. A Kimus-infused Celesti light would create a Patrol the Bay of Catazar voyage that also reports unusual events at sea.

Feroz.t: The Celesti Lighthouse at Oran could be restored, or rebuilt as a fortified great lighthouse that boosts Feroz-based fleets and lets fleets guard its coastal waters. An infused version would strengthen divinations against shrouds over the territory.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Celesti monastery near the Gilded Peak holds the archived plans for the lighthouse's golden lamp.

Madruga.t: The famed Shining Pillar cannot be restored, because its island is held by the Children of Wrecks and has been swallowed by a perpetual maelstrom.

Mareave.t: The ruined Light of Virtue at Icarion is one of the six sites proposed for further study, and a smaller lighthouse still stands at Beoraidh. Pathfinder Gaddak of Mareave seconded the original request.

Necropolis.t: The territory was once called Pharos after its great lighthouse, burned in the civil war and never rebuilt. That site is a candidate for future study, and Reumah's Rest inspired the fortified Celesti design.

Redoubt.t: The destroyed Lighthouse of Nikephoros, said to stand on a Winter regio, and the lighthouses of Naris near the restored port of Elos are both proposed for further study.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Cyrus, senator for Reikos, proposed the appraisal.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos hosted the week-long lighthouse symposium, and its never-built Caricomare lighthouse, meant partly to protect the city from storms, is a candidate for further study.

Spiral.t: The pre-Imperial Lighthouse of Apulian, the Eye of Kimus, destroyed by Hadrian of Apulian, is one of the six sites proposed for further study.

Forests of the night.d: This was the third masterful Night enchantment on the Empire in as many months. Shimmering lights led forest workers to extra ambergelt, dragonbone, beggar's lye and especially iridescent gloaming, and the effect spilled into Mournwold and Liathaven. Weak Night regio were empowered, tales of Night creatures spread, and several Night eternals were expected to seek audiences at Anvil. Everyone had vivid, refreshing dreams, and naga gained extra mana or discerning senses. During the Spring Equinox, any Verdant Bounty of the Twilight Bayou would permanently alter its target forest to yield crystal fire. The Senate was also offered the chance to commission an Iridescent Butterfly reserve.

Dawn.t: A faceless ebony knight in armour of woven darkness was said to offer a night of hospitality to knights of Semmerholm, and Dawn's forests shared in the Empire-wide bounty.

Jotun.t: The Jotun are not named, but the enchantment washed over into Mournwold and Liathaven, which they held, so the forests there were affected even though those lands lay outside the Empire.

Navarr.t: In Miaren, a rippling shadow was said to wander the trods, stealing romantic memories from anyone who could not answer its riddles, while Navarr's forests shared in the extra bounty.

Urizen.t: Urizen magicians of the Coven of Umbral Reflection and the Spire of the Auric Horizon wove the enchantment, and three enigmatic crows were said to offer auguries in northern Morrow.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sherard Hunters of Wintermark are noted for a similarly powerful Spring working laid on the Empire almost a year earlier.

Forests of the night.o: At the Winter Solstice, Urizen's Coven of Umbral Reflection and Spire of the Auric Horizon laid the Wondrous Forests of the Night across the Empire. The enchantment boosted every forest's production, stirred Night regio and eternals, and brought vivid dreams to the Empire.

Liathaven.t: Although not technically part of the Empire at the time, Liathaven's forests were affected as the enchantment washed over its borders.

Miaren.t: Stories spread of a rippling shadow on Miaren's trods that stole romantic memories from those who failed its riddles.

Morrow.t: Three black crows were said to haunt trees in northern Morrow, offering peculiar auguries to those who brought white stones and perfumed smoke.

Mournwold.t: Although not technically part of the Empire at the time, Mournwold's forests were affected as the enchantment washed over its borders.

Semmerholm.t: A faceless ebony knight in armour of woven darkness was said to offer a night of hospitality to Semmerholm's knights.

Forever is composed of nows.d: Retired prognosticator Mladen Escovitch offered to work with the Imperial Master of Works to update three existing fortification opportunities, but only if the vacant post is filled and he is engaged during the Winter Solstice. Gerard La Salle proposed hiring a temporary prognosticator, with the Senate choosing by administrative motion between Lisane de Terresford, Rosemary Stockland and Vainakoma Dawnstongue. Alternatively, the Senate could hire all three permanently for 6 extra thrones a season, which would also open a power to review a lapsed opportunity. For a year the Throne may ask Magistrate Abraham and Leontes to appraise a proposed sodality's manifesto. Professor Gelberg's Beurteilung remains available, and Eilian Sweetwater is still missing in Redoubt.

Dawn.t: Lisane de Terresford, a Dawnish earl of House Terresford known for her Wisdom and past work with the Synod, is one of three candidates offered to the Senate as a prognosticator who would seek virtuous solutions.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Mladen Escovitch's freelance work included a recent appraisal of the vulnerabilities of the Druj military.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Eilian Sweetwater vanished during the Grendel attack on Redoubt and may be a prisoner of the Grendel.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the missing prognosticator Eilian Sweetwater is described as a Navarr historian, whose absence prompted the search for a stand-in.

The Marches.t: Rosemary Stockland, an alder of Stockland in Upwold and a former Bailiff of the Grand Market, is offered as a candidate prognosticator who would favour mercantile solutions in which all parties gain.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Eilian Sweetwater and his team disappeared at the fallen Lighthouse at Nikephoros in the Urizen-held territory of Redoubt.

Wintermark.t: Vainakoma Dawnstongue, a Suaq veteran of the Green Shield from Hahnmark, is offered as a candidate prognosticator whose solutions to military problems would make novel use of Imperial armies.

Forever is composed of nows.o: In Winter 387YE, with the Prognosticator's Office stretched thin, several opportunities were set out to support it. They included Mladen Escovitch's offer to revisit old fortification plans, a choice of three candidates to stand in for the missing Eilian Sweetwater, and a new power for the Throne to have proposed sodalities appraised.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the candidate prognosticator Vainakoma Dawnstongue was born and raised in Hahnmark.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the "Third Pie" opportunity in Mournwold is cited as an example of an earlier opportunity that could be refreshed.

Redoubt.t: Eilian Sweetwater and his team went missing in Redoubt during the Grendel attack, just as they reached the fallen Lighthouse at Nikephoros, and they remain unaccounted for amid rumours involving the eternal Khobel Tavah.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: candidate Lisane de Terresford leads House Terresford, a minor noble house that keeps the ford on the River Terres in Semmerholm.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: candidate Rosemary Stockland is an alder of Stockland, an Upwold region known for its fair and its sheep and cattle markets.

Forge of sorrows.d: The Thule had dug tunnels beneath Gildenheim during their occupation and collapsed them when Imperial armies drove them out, apparently to hide the runeforge and perhaps return for it later. Some speculated the whole invasion of Skarsind aimed at acquiring it. The remains of Ryv Ironbones, a Navarri rune worker thought enslaved after the fall of Treji, were found there. Repair could be commissioned by the Senate for 60 wains of weirwood, 50 of mithril, 40 of white granite and at least 50 Thrones, taking six months and creating a new title. The Senate did not commission it; the opportunity remains, but as Skarsind now belongs to the Imperial Orcs, any national runeforge there would go to the Orcs.

Imperial Orcs.t: With Skarsind now theirs, any rebuilt runeforge there established as a national resource would belong to the Imperial Orcs rather than Wintermark.

Navarr.t: The skeleton of Ryv Ironbones, a Navarri rune worker believed enslaved by the Thule after the fall of Treji, was found in the ruins, suggesting he had been forced to work on the forge.

Thule.t: The Thule had secretly tunnelled to the runeforge, used slave labour to try to repair it and collapsed the passages on retreat, possibly intending to return; some speculated their invasion of Skarsind sought this prize.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk explorers and architects found and assessed the runeforge, but the pending relinquishment of Skarsind meant Wintermark would not gain it as a national resource.

Forge of sorrows.o: A Winterfolk band sent by the civil service to explore collapsed Thule tunnels beneath the runecarved cave of ice at Gildenheim, in Skarsind, discovered an ancient, damaged runeforge that the Thule had been trying to repair.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the fall of Treji in Hercynia is cited as when Ryv Ironbones was believed taken into Thule slavery.

Skarsind.t: Deep beneath the cave of ice at Gildenheim lies an ancient runeforge that could be repaired in six months if commissioned, now within Imperial Orc territory.

Forging links.d: The House of the People gave twenty wains of white granite and forty doses of liao, plus sevensalve for Ambassador Accalon, unloaded at Oran. Sumaah volunteers in Feroz offered to halve the labour cost of one single-season commission there, if a Senate motion asks for their help. A Winter Liberty Pact meeting chaired by Axos dissolved into confusion over tie-breaks, and only three of seven points stood. Judging the Pact's anti-slavery aims largely won, Oxtitocszin proposed ending regular meetings and leaving Pact business to ambassadors. Sumaah also agreed to one Senate-arranged appraisal of magical cooperation, available until the end of the Spring Equinox 388YE.

Dawn.t: Five Dawnish captains, including Ser Raine de Sarroi and Sir Edmund de Verlaine, helped escort the Stone Fleet, and Jarrigk Silktongue of Dawn, as Voice of Liberty, faces Sumaah's proposal to end Liberty Pact meetings.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page; its only link is holding part of Feroz, where the Sumaah aid was delivered.

Highguard.t: Ambassador Accalon of Highguard was to collect the aid package at Anvil for distribution to the Freeborn and had brokered the magical cooperation offer, while Highborn captains including Raoul, Samuel and Tyden sailed in the escort.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Protectorate Kardak is listed among the captains who escorted the Stone Fleet.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Alim Longstride, Llandun Waystone and Derwyn are listed among the captains who escorted the Stone Fleet.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn supplied most of the escort captains and are the intended recipients of the granite, the liao meant to fortify their Pride, and the Sumaah volunteers' help rebuilding Feroz.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: around ten League captains, including Giovanni von Temeschwar and Albrecht von Holberg, are listed among the Stone Fleet's escort.

Urizen.t: Xanthippe, Grandmaster of the Celestial Arch, originated the magical cooperation proposal, though Sumaah refused any work on astronomancy as heretical; Xanthippe and Cerewyn, Magnus of Starfall, also sailed in the escort.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Triska Markova, Sokol Bradach Uzbek and Rudolfs Kafka are listed among the captains who escorted the Stone Fleet.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Beornwulf Redwaldsson is listed among the captains who escorted the Stone Fleet.

Forging links.o: Escorted by nearly a hundred Imperial captains who drove off an Asavean armada, the Sumaah Stone Fleet delivered white granite and liao to Feroz to help rebuild the Brass Coast. Sumaah also questioned the value of further Liberty Pact meetings and offered a single joint magical appraisal with the Empire.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: The Stone Fleet sailed along the Fontargenta coast to Oran, where it unloaded the white granite donated for rebuilding.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Asavean agents threatened to intercept the Sumaah convoy bound for the Bay of Catazar, prompting the Imperial escort.

Feroz.t: Feroz received twenty wains of white granite and Sumaah volunteers who are repairing homes and offering medicines, and they would halve the labour cost of one single-season Senate commission raised there this season.

Fortify Ateri in Spiral.d: Acting under the Senate's legal power to raise fortifications, the Imperial Master of Works approved finishing the partial fortification at Ateri in Spiral, known as Fort Mezudan. The work required 25 wains of white granite and a season to build, with upkeep of 10 Thrones. Marcus of Endsmeet Autumn Coven supplied the full 25 wains of white granite after the Winter Solstice 377YE, and the fortification was completed. Two years later, at the Autumn Equinox 379YE, a powerful magical storm struck the fortress and destroyed it completely.

Grendel.t: Fort Mezudan was finished in Spiral, a territory Grendel shared control of that season. The page does not mention Grendel directly.

Urizen.t: The Empire completed Fort Mezudan in Spiral, a Urizen territory that Urizen shared with Grendel that season. Its later destruction in 379YE removed this Imperial stronghold from the territory.

Fortify Ateri in Spiral.o: In Winter 377YE the Imperial Master of Works approved completing Fort Mezudan, a partially built fortification at Ateri in Spiral. The fort was finished but was later destroyed by a magical storm in Autumn 379YE.

Spiral/Ateri.t: Ateri was the site of Fort Mezudan, completed from a partial fortification after Winter 377YE and wholly destroyed by a powerful magical storm in Autumn 379YE.

Spiral.t: Spiral gained a completed fortification, Fort Mezudan, which stood until a magical storm destroyed it at the Autumn Equinox 379YE.

Fortify Coursmouth.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Casinea and seconded by the senator for Necropolis. It used standard costs: 80 wains of white granite, 160 crowns in labour, a year to build and 10 Thrones in upkeep. Lieselotte van Holberg supplied 24 wains of granite and 48 crowns after the Autumn Equinox 382YE, and the project was targeted by The Immaculate Architect. Imperatrix Lisabetta added 30 wains and 10 Thrones after the Winter Solstice. The Silent Sentinel opportunity effectively contributed a further 16 wains and 32 crowns. Ehud of Reumah's Redoubt gave the final 10 wains after the Spring Equinox 383YE. The finished fortification was named Reumah's Rest.

Highguard.t: Highguard senators for Casinea and Necropolis proposed and seconded the work. Highborn donors helped see it through, and it left the nation with a new fortification guarding the Necropolis coast.

Fortify Coursmouth.o: In Autumn 382YE the Senate passed in principle a motion to build a coastal fortification at Coursmouth in Necropolis. Once the commission was completed, it produced the fortification Reumah's Rest.

Necropolis/Coursmouth.t: Coursmouth became the site of Reumah's Rest, a white granite fortification built along its coastline.

Necropolis.t: Necropolis gained Reumah's Rest, a new fortification on its coast, after its own senator seconded the motion.

Fortify Delev.d: The motion built on fortification work begun at the Spring Equinox 377YE, aiming to finish the fortified walls surrounding Delev. It required standard costs of 70 white granite and 210 crowns, with nine months to complete. Funding came from many individual donors after the Spring Equinox and Summer Solstice 386YE. Myshki Marishka Letuchaya provided a large sum and white granite, Triska Markova gave money and further granite, and numerous others contributed crowns, thrones and small donations. The fortification is now complete, and Delev is protected by The Little Boyar's Welcome.

Varushka.t: A Varushkan town gained completed fortified walls, finishing work started nine years earlier, with Varushkan donors among those who funded the construction.

Fortify Delev.o: In Spring 386YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Karov's senator and seconded by Volodmartz, to build a fortification completing the walls around the town of Delev in Duzekani, Karov. Once funded and completed, the walls became known as The Little Boyar's Welcome.

Karov/Duzekani.t: Delev in Duzekani is now surrounded by completed fortified walls, The Little Boyar's Welcome, protecting the town.

Karov.t: Karov's own senator proposed the motion, and the territory now has a completed fortification at Delev, The Little Boyar's Welcome.

Fortify Foracci.d: The motion commissioned a fortification in the Foracci region of Sarvos. It cost 80 wains of white granite and 20 thrones in labour, would take a year to build, and needs 10 thrones a season in upkeep. Magdelena Alanga Di Sarvos supplied 20 wains of white granite after the Autumn Equinox 380YE, and a further 20 wains with the 20 thrones after the Winter Solstice 380YE. After the Autumn Equinox 381YE, Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar and Magdelena each gave another 20 wains, making up the full 80. When finished it will be a rank one fortification called "Our Lady of Pride".

The League.t: League senators for Sarvos and Tassato drove the motion, and League citizens, chiefly Magdelena Alanga Di Sarvos, provided most of the granite and money to strengthen the defences of a League city.

Fortify Foracci.o: In Autumn 380YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by Tassato, to build a fortification in Foracci, Sarvos. Once complete it would be a rank one fortification named "Our Lady of Pride".

Sarvos/Foracci.t: Foracci is the site of the new rank one fortification, "Our Lady of Pride", built from 80 wains of white granite over a year.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos gains a rank one fortification, "Our Lady of Pride", in Foracci. It was paid for largely by Sarvosan donations and costs 10 thrones a season to maintain.

Fortify Freemoor.d: Proposed by Miekarova and seconded by Temeschwar, the motion called for a new fortification in Freemoor, at the standard cost of 80 wains of white granite and 20 thrones, taking a year to build with an upkeep of 10 thrones. Nikolovich Drakov supplied 29 wains of white granite after the Winter Solstice 381YE and 16 thrones after the Spring Equinox 382YE. The Silent Sentinel opportunity effectively provided another 16 wains and 4 thrones. Landon of Longridge gave 15 wains and Orrick of House Bolholt gave 20 more over 383YE, which met the full cost. The fortification of Landskeepers Bulwark was then completed.

The Marches.t: The Marches, which held the Mournwold at the time, gained Landskeepers Bulwark as a new fortification on their land in Freemoor.

Fortify Freemoor.o: In Autumn 381YE the Senate passed in principle a motion to build a fortification in Freemoor in the Mournwold. Once fully funded with materials, the fort was completed as Landskeepers Bulwark.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: Freemoor is where Landskeepers Bulwark was built, and it now stands complete in the region.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold, then held by the Marches, gained a new fortification, Landskeepers Bulwark, built after several years of contributions of granite and thrones.

Fortify Gildenheim.d: Announced in Summer 386YE by Groza, Legion Engineer, the commission took up the opportunity from the Standing in the sun wind of fortune. It benefited from a mandate enacted by Viviane Barossa de Coeurdefer. The cost was 48 white granite, 16 mithril and 240 crowns, with the crowns paid in full by the Tamazi, and the work takes a year to complete. Irontide Flax supplied the 16 wains of mithril and 48 wains of white granite after the Autumn Equinox 386YE. Once complete, Gildenheim will be protected by a rank one fortification of 3000 strength that takes only half the normal damage from magical attacks such as Thunderous Tread of the Trees.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs' territory of Skarsind gains a warded fortification at Gildenheim, strengthening their hold against military and magical assault once the year-long construction finishes.

Fortify Gildenheim.o: Groza, the Legion Engineer, announced a commission to fortify Gildenheim in Gildermark, Skarsind, with a rank one fortification bearing runic wards offered by the Tamazi, as set out in the Standing in the sun wind of fortune.

Skarsind/Gildermark.t: Gildenheim in Gildermark is the site of the new fortification, with materials supplied by Irontide Flax after the Autumn Equinox and completion due a year after the commission.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind is to receive a rank one fortification of 3000 strength at Gildenheim, with Tamazi runic wards halving damage from magical attacks such as Thunderous Tread of the Trees.

Fortify Golden Downs in Mitwold.d: The motion to create a fortification in Mitwold was approved by the Imperial Master of Works rather than by a Senate vote. The standard cost was 100 wains of white granite and a year of construction, with an upkeep of 10 Thrones. Richard Tunstall, Imperial Master of Works, supplied all of the granite himself in four instalments of 25 wains, after the Winter Solstice 377YE and the Spring Equinox, Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox of 378YE. Construction of the fortification, named Forte Fidelis, was completed.

The Marches.t: The Marches gained a new fortification, Forte Fidelis, strengthening the defence of their territory of Mitwold.

Fortify Golden Downs in Mitwold.o: In Winter 377YE the Imperial Master of Works approved the construction of a new fortification, Forte Fidelis, at Golden Downs in Mitwold, using the power to raise fortifications granted by the Senate.

Mitwold/Golden Downs.t: Golden Downs became the site of Forte Fidelis, a new fortification whose construction was completed after the Autumn Equinox 378YE.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold gained a completed fortification, Forte Fidelis, built over a year from 100 wains of white granite and requiring 10 Thrones in upkeep.

Fortify Greensward.d: The motion was proposed by the Conscience of the Senate and seconded by Holberg. It called for a rank one fortification costing 80 wains of white granite and 20 Thrones, taking a year to build, with upkeep of 10 Thrones. Orrick provided 40 wains of white granite after the Winter Solstice 381YE. The Silent Sentinel opportunity effectively contributed 16 wains of white granite and 32 crowns. Orrick then supplied the remaining 24 wains and 16 Thrones after the Spring Equinox 382YE. Farstrider's Watch was due for completion shortly before the Winter Solstice 382YE.

The Marches.t: The Marches gained a new rank one fortification, Farstrider's Watch, to strengthen the defence of their Mournwold lands.

Fortify Greensward.o: In Autumn 381YE the Senate passed in principle a motion to build a new fortification named Farstrider's Watch in the Greensward region of Mournwold, to be funded by the Imperatrix.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: The Greensward was the chosen site for Farstrider's Watch, a new rank one fortification built with white granite supplied largely by Orrick.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold, held by the Marches, was to receive its new fortification of Farstrider's Watch, due for completion shortly before the Winter Solstice 382YE.

Fortify Lestasny in Karsk.d: The fortification required 80 wains of white granite, 20 thrones in labour and twelve months to build. Maarit supplied the first instalment after the Spring Equinox, and Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov supplied the remaining materials and labour after the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox 381YE. An amendment brought the Asavean architect Almodin Oktístis onto the work. During the Autumn Equinox 381YE powerful magic greatly accelerated construction, so the fortification was completed in nine months rather than a year.

Varushka.t: Varushkan citizens drove and funded the project: the senator for Karsk proposed it, Miekarova seconded it, and Maarit and Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov supplied the granite and thrones that saw a new fortification raised in Varushkan land.

Fortify Lestasny in Karsk.o: In Spring 381YE the Senate passed a self-funded motion, proposed by the senator for Karsk and seconded by Miekarova, to commission a fortification in Lestasny, Karsk.

Karsk/Lestasny.t: Lestasny is the site of the new fortification, built from white granite with the involvement of the Asavean architect Almodin Oktístis and completed in nine months.

Karsk.t: Karsk gained a new fortification in Lestasny, finished ahead of schedule thanks to magical acceleration during Autumn 381YE.

Fortify Lower Tarn Valley.d: Proposed by Redoubt and seconded by Segura, the motion arose from an opportunity offered by the Great Forest orcs. It would have cost 80 wains of weirwood and 20 thrones, taken a year, and not counted against the Senate's limited commissions. The orcs would garrison and control the rank one fortification, so the Empire would pay no upkeep. Constitutionally this amounted to ceding the fortification, though not the region, to the orcs. If the treaty broke and the orcs took the region, the Holt could support them against the Empire. Only 10 wains of weirwood, from Cybi Farkas, arrived after the Winter Solstice 381YE, so no work began before the commission lapsed.

Navarr.t: The motion would have placed an orc-controlled fortification inside Navarr's territory of Therunin, ceding the stronghold, though not the land, to the Great Forest orcs. The commission lapsed before any work was done.

Fortify Lower Tarn Valley.o: In Autumn 381YE the Senate passed in principle a motion accepting the Great Forest Orcs' offer to build a weirwood fortification, the Holt of the Oak, in the Lower Tarn Valley of Therunin. Too little weirwood was supplied, and the commission lapsed at the end of the Autumn Equinox 382YE without being built.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Lower Tarn Valley was the planned site of the Holt of the Oak, but only 10 wains of weirwood were delivered and the commission lapsed after the Autumn Equinox 382YE.

Therunin.t: Therunin would have gained a rank one weirwood fortification garrisoned by the Great Forest orcs, which could have turned against Imperial forces if the treaty were broken. It was never built because too little weirwood arrived.

Fortify Lower Tarn Valley II.d: Proposed by the senator for Therunin and seconded by Miekarova, the motion took up an offer from the Great Forest orcs. It called for 80 wains of weirwood, 20 thrones and a year's work, did not count against the Empire's limited commissions, and carried no upkeep while the orcs held the garrison. Work restarted at Winter 383YE. Contributions came from Cybi Farkas, Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar, Vauraus Korppitkotka and the orcs themselves. Constitutionally, the motion amounted to ceding the fortification, though not the region, to the orcs. If the treaty broke and the orcs took the region, the fort could support them against Imperial forces.

Navarr.t: Navarr's senator for Therunin proposed the motion, accepting orc-built and orc-held defences in a Navarri territory in return for a fortification the Empire need not maintain.

Fortify Lower Tarn Valley II.o: In Winter 382YE the Senate passed a motion to recommission the Holt of the Oak, a weirwood fortification in the Lower Tarn Valley of Therunin, after the original motion lapsed. The fort was to be built, garrisoned and controlled by the orcs of the Great Forest.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Lower Tarn Valley was the site of the Holt of the Oak, to be built of weirwood and occupied by the Great Forest orcs. Construction restarted at Winter 383YE.

Therunin.t: Therunin was to gain a rank one weirwood fortification garrisoned by the Great Forest orcs. This would strengthen the territory while the treaty held, but the fort could aid the orcs against the Empire if it failed.

Fortify Lustri.d: Proposed by the senator for Semmerholm and seconded by Weirwater, the motion called for 80 wains of white granite, 20 thrones and a year's work, with upkeep of 10 thrones a season. Progress depended on contributions from individual citizens between Winter 384YE and Summer 386YE. Cadeus gave substantial sums and 23 wains of granite. Able the Taller of Sarangrave Reforged supplied the final 57 wains of granite and 12 thrones. Once complete, Lustri was protected by The Stork's Gaze. The people of the Mountains of the Moon offered to help, but the Senate did not ask them to take part.

Urizen.t: The Urizen territory of Zenith gained a major defensive work in Lustri, though its construction depended on donations from citizens across the Empire.

Fortify Lustri.o: In Winter 384YE the Senate passed a motion to build a fortification in Lustri, Zenith. After donations from many citizens it was completed as The Stork's Gaze, a fortification of 3000 strength.

Zenith/Lustri.t: Lustri is now guarded by The Stork's Gaze, a fortification of 3000 strength built from 80 wains of white granite.

Mountains of the Moon.t: Mentioned in passing: the people of the Mountains of the Moon offered to help build the fortification, but the Senate did not ask them to participate.

Zenith.t: Zenith now has The Stork's Gaze, a 3000-strength fortification in Lustri, costing 10 thrones a season in upkeep.

Fortify Miekarova.d: Proposed by the senator for Volodmartz and seconded by the senator for Zenith, the motion would have authorised a rank one fortification in Miekarova. Its standard costs would have been 80 white granite and 20 Thrones, with a year to construct and an upkeep of 10 Thrones per season. The Senate defeated the motion, so no fortification was commissioned and no construction took place.

Varushka.t: Varushkan senators from Volodmartz sought stronger defences for one of their own territories against the northern barbarians, but the defeat of the motion left Miekarova without the new fortress.

Fortify Miekarova.o: In Winter 378YE a Senate motion sought permission to raise a new, unnamed fortress in Miekarova to guard against possible threats from the Northern Barbarians, but the motion was defeated.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova would have received a new rank one fortification against threats from the Northern Barbarians, but the motion failed and no fortress was raised there.

Fortify Miekarova II.d: The motion called for a new fortification, Grimhold, to be built in the Vale of Strascovia, home of the Vor'Azi people, using the crumbling ruins of their ancestral castle as its foundation. The standard cost was 80 wains of white granite and 20 thrones, with a year to construct and upkeep of 10 thrones per season. Dušan Otecovna Zlata supplied 40 wains of white granite and 20 thrones after the Spring Equinox 379YE, and a further 40 wains after the Autumn Equinox 379YE, meeting the full material cost. Once complete, it will give Miekarova a rank one fortification. A previous motion to fortify the territory had been defeated in Winter 378YE.

Varushka.t: Varushkans renewed their effort to fortify one of their own territories after an earlier defeat, with Dušan Otecovna Zlata personally providing all the granite and thrones the work required.

Fortify Miekarova II.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate considered a self-funded motion, proposed by the senator for Miekarova and seconded by Karsk, to raise a fortress named Grimhold in the Perumaki region of Miekarova. It followed a failed attempt to fortify the territory in Winter 378YE.

Miekarova/Perumaki.t: Grimhold is being raised in Perumaki's Vale of Strascovia, built on the crumbling ruins of the Vor'Azi people's ancestral castle.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova is to gain its first fortification, Grimhold, a rank one fortress, once the year-long construction is complete, at an ongoing upkeep of 10 thrones per season.

Fortify Morajasse.d: The commission passed at 90 thrones and used standard costs: 80 wains of white granite, 20 thrones in labour, a year to build and 10 thrones upkeep. Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza supplied 24 wains and 6 thrones after the Autumn Equinox 382YE. The Silent Sentinel opportunity effectively provided another 16 wains and 4 thrones, and the work was also targeted by The Immaculate Architect. Imperatrix Lisabetta gave 20 wains and 5 thrones after the Winter Solstice and a further 5 thrones after the Spring Equinox 383YE. Landon of Longridge provided the last 20 wains. A new fortification now stands at Morajasse.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast's senator for Feroz proposed the motion, and Brass Coast lands gained a new fortification at Morajasse, which Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza helped to fund.

Fortify Morajasse.o: In Autumn 382YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Feroz and seconded by Mournwold, to commission a new fortification at Morajasse in Feroz; it was later completed.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: A new fortification was built at Morajasse, completed with white granite and money gathered from several donors.

Feroz.t: Feroz gained a new fortification at Morajasse, which strengthens the territory's defences and carries an upkeep of 10 thrones.

Fortify Overton.d: Proposed by the senator for Mitwold and seconded by Bregasland, the commission called for 100 wains of white granite, a year's construction time and upkeep of 10 Thrones. Bridget Eastville of the Marches provided 25 wains after each of the Winter Solstice 378YE, Spring Equinox, Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox 379YE, and Orchard's Watch was completed. The Civil Service made accounting and processing errors, delaying the recording of the Summer shipment and wrongly claiming that construction could not finish in time. A Senate commission in fact has a year to begin construction, not to complete it. The page's overview places Overton in the Mournwold, but the motion itself names Mitwold.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, and the page refers only to the Mournwold, which they held at the time, in its summary of where Overton lies.

The Marches.t: Marcher senators for Mitwold and Bregasland proposed and seconded the fortification. The Marcher Bridget Eastville single-handedly supplied all 100 wains of white granite to complete Orchard's Watch.

Fortify Overton.o: In Autumn 378YE the Senate passed in principle a motion to build a new fortification, Orchard's Watch, at Overton in Mitwold. It was completed after Bridget Eastville of the Marches supplied all the white granite needed.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold gained a new fortification, Orchard's Watch, at Overton, built on the motion of its own senator.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the page's overview describes Overton as being in the Mournwold, though the motion itself places it in Mitwold.

Fortify Reikos.d: The motion to fortify Reikos was proposed by the senator for Bastion and seconded by Upwold, and it passed in Winter 380YE. The fortification was to be built in Broken Ride and cost 160 wains of white granite and 45 thrones in labour, take 12 months to construct, and carry 12 thrones a year in upkeep. Brother Ibrahim the South Paw supplied 20 wains of white granite and 5 thrones after the Winter Solstice 380YE. Sammual of the Cohort of the Winter Bear then provided 40 wains and 7 thrones after the Spring Equinox 381YE, and 100 wains and 33 thrones after the Summer Solstice 381YE, which together met the full materials and labour costs.

Highguard.t: Bastion's senator proposed a fortification for Highguard's territory of Reikos. Highguard citizens and allies then supplied the granite and thrones needed to strengthen the defences of Broken Ride.

Fortify Reikos.o: In Winter 380YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Bastion and seconded by Upwold, to build a fortification at Broken Ride in Reikos, taking advantage of an opportunity there.

Reikos/Broken Ride.t: Broken Ride was chosen as the site of the new fortification, which was fully funded by Summer 381YE.

Reikos.t: Reikos was to gain a new fortification in Broken Ride, adding to the defences of the Highguard-held territory.

Fortify Ruicraic's Redoubt.d: Proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by the senator for Mareave, the motion was to be fully funded by the Imperial Orc nation with help from Reumah's Redoubt. It cost 50 white granite, 30 weirwood and 36 thrones, the price raised by the under-developed nature of Icarion, with 8 thrones upkeep and six months to build. Ehud and Karrak supplied most of the materials and money after the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox, with crowns from Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven. Ruicraic's Redoubt now stands in Eoradal and could also serve as an embassy to Skoura if that foreign nation agrees.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named in the motion, which concerns Mareave, a territory Grendel shared control of that season.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc nation pledged to fund the fortification in full, and orc contributors such as Ehud and Karrak supplied the granite, weirwood and thrones that saw Ruicraic's Redoubt completed.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the motion names Reumah's Redoubt as helping the Imperial Orcs fund the work, and Urizen is otherwise not mentioned.

Fortify Ruicraic's Redoubt.o: The Senate passed a motion in Summer 387YE to build a fortification at Ruicraic's Redoubt in Eoradal, Mareave, acting on an opportunity identified by the Tamazi sept in Autumn 386YE. Once fully funded, it was completed as a rank one fortification.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: Ruicraic's Redoubt was raised in Eoradal and now stands there as a rank one fortification.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Mentioned in passing: the under-developed nature of Icarion is cited as raising the cost of the project to 36 thrones.

Mareave.t: Mareave gained a new rank one fortification, Ruicraic's Redoubt in Eoradal, which could also serve as an embassy to Skoura if that nation agrees.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the only link is the name Reumah's Redoubt, cited as helping to fund the work, and nothing is built or decided in the Redoubt.

Fortify Skogei.d: Proposed by Hahnmark and seconded by Therunin, the Summer 377YE motion funded reinforcement of the foothold in Skarsind on the military council's recommendation. It passed at 15 Thrones, with the money going to Hahnmark. In Autumn 377YE a Hahnmark motion seconded by Kallavesa, to maintain and upgrade the fortifications in Skarsind, passed unanimously. The work cost 88 wains of white granite, took four seasons and carries an upkeep of 10 Thrones. Hengest Dun, Senator for Hahnmark, presented all the granite in four instalments between Summer 377YE and Summer 378YE. The finished fortification at Skogei is the Will of the Wintermark, called Hengesthal.

Thule.t: The fortification was built in Skarsind, a Thule-held territory, strengthening the Empire's foothold against Thule control there.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Senator for Hahnmark, Hengest Dun, drove the project and supplied all 88 wains of granite. The completed fortress bears the nation's name as the Will of the Wintermark, or Hengesthal.

Fortify Skogei.o: In Summer 377YE the Senate commissioned a fortification at Skogei in Skarsind to reinforce the Imperial foothold there, and the motion was amended in Autumn 377YE to upgrade it. Built with white granite supplied by the Senator for Hahnmark, it was completed as the Will of the Wintermark, known as Hengesthal.

Skarsind/Skogei Glens.t: Skogei became the site of Hengesthal, the Will of the Wintermark, a granite fortification raised over four seasons to secure the Imperial foothold.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark's senator proposed both motions and received the Senate funds. Hengest Dun then personally presented every wain of white granite needed for construction.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind gained a new fortification at Skogei to hold the Imperial foothold established there. It was completed as the Will of the Wintermark.

Fortify Southmoor.d: In Autumn 381YE a motion was put before the Senate to construct a new fortification in the region of Southmoor in the Mournwold. It was proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by the senator for Miekarova. The motion failed, so no fort was commissioned in Southmoor as a result of it. The page records no further details of the vote or any debate surrounding it.

Jotun.t: Jotun, which held the Mournwold at the time, faced no new Imperial fortification in Southmoor because the motion failed.

The Marches.t: The Marches, whose people sought to reclaim the Mournwold, did not gain a new Imperial fort in Southmoor to support that effort, as the motion failed.

Fortify Southmoor.o: A Senate motion to build a fortification in Southmoor in the Mournwold was proposed in Autumn 381YE but failed.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Southmoor was the intended site of the proposed fort, but the motion's failure meant no fortification was commissioned there.

Mournwold.t: The proposal to raise a new fortification in the Mournwold's Southmoor region came to nothing when the Senate rejected it.

Fortify Spider's Dream Bridge.d: The motion was proposed by Necropolis and seconded by Segura, and asked for only a modest disbursement of funds. The work cost 20 wains of white granite and 60 crowns and took three months. After the Spring Equinox, Eli of the Cenotaph provided 7 thrones 4 crowns and 20 wains of white granite. Once complete, warbands could no longer sabotage the bridge. An enemy army could still destroy it only by controlling the regions on both sides of the river and spending a season on the task. If either Torres or Bocche were lost, the Empire would keep military control of the Spider's Dream and could use the bridge to get past the beachhead limit when invading one region from the other.

The Brass Coast.t: The fortified bridge secures the Brass Coast's link from Torres across to the League. It means Imperial armies could cross from Bocche to retake Torres without being held back by the beachhead limit if the region were ever lost.

The League.t: The fortified bridge protects the League's crossing at Bocche against sabotage. Imperial forces could use it to strike back into Bocche from Torres if the region fell.

Fortify Spider's Dream Bridge.o: In Spring 386YE the Senate passed a motion to fortify the Spider's Dream Bridge, the crossing that links Torres in Madruga with Bocche in Sarvos, taking up the opportunity offered by the Dreaming in Strands Wind of Fortune.

Madruga/Torres.t: Torres is one of the two banks the fortified bridge connects. An enemy would now need to hold both Torres and Bocche, and spend a season, to destroy it.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: Bocche is one of the two banks the fortified bridge connects. If Bocche were lost, the Empire could still hold the Spider's Dream and invade from Torres without the beachhead limit.

Madruga.t: Madruga's end of the Spider's Dream Bridge, in Torres, can no longer be sabotaged by warbands, and the bridge gives the Empire a secure route back into Torres from Bocche.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos's end of the Spider's Dream Bridge, in Bocche, is now protected from warband sabotage, and the bridge gives the Empire a secure route back into Bocche from Torres.

Fortify Tassato.d: The fortification's standard cost was 80 wains of white granite and 20 Thrones, or 100 wains of white granite. It would take a year to build and need 10 Thrones of upkeep. Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato paid for all of it in instalments across four seasons. He gave 20 wains after the Autumn Equinox 378YE, 20 wains and 10 Thrones after the Winter Solstice, 20 wains and 10 Thrones after the Spring Equinox 379YE, and a final 20 wains after the Summer Solstice 379YE. The Rezia Redoubt was then reported complete.

The League.t: The League gained a new fortification in its city-territory of Tassato, paid for entirely by the League citizen Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the page describes no Urizen involvement in the fortification's commission or construction.

Fortify Tassato.o: In Autumn 378YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Tassato and seconded by Feroz, to build a new fortification called the Rezia Redoubt in Tassato Mestra. It was passed at a cost of 250 Thrones.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Tassato Mestra is the site of the Rezia Redoubt, built from white granite over the year after Autumn 378YE and reported complete.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory plays no part in the motion, and the shared name comes only from the new fortification's title, the Rezia Redoubt.

Tassato.t: Tassato's senator proposed the motion, and the territory gained the completed Rezia Redoubt fortification, which carries an upkeep of 10 Thrones.

Fortify Town defences.d: Proposed by the Senator for Mitwold and seconded by the Senator for Temeschwar, the motion passed at 60 Thrones with 13 votes against, and the money went to Senator Mitwold. Full fortification needed 300 wains of White Granite, but 40 wains were enough to suppress banditry. Bridget Eastville née Talbot, Senator for Mitwold, presented 40 wains in the Winter Solstice 2013 downtime. Meade, Sybela and Mellfort were partially fortified, which ended the banditry problems but gave no military advantage. Completing all three would take another 260 wains. The motion broke constitutional protocol by covering more than one item, but magistrates did not strike it down and construction went ahead.

Highguard.t: Highguard was one of the three nations whose towns the motion sought to fortify, and banditry there was suppressed once the partial fortifications were built.

The League.t: League towns benefited from the partial fortifications, which suppressed banditry in the League, and the motion was seconded by the Senator for Temeschwar.

The Marches.t: The Marches led the motion through Mitwold's senator, Bridget Eastville née Talbot, who received the funds and presented the 40 wains of White Granite that suppressed banditry in the nation.

Fortify Town defences.o: In Winter 376YE the Senate passed a motion to fortify towns in the League, the Marches and Highguard, and the White Granite later supplied partially fortified Meade, Sybela and Mellfort, which suppressed banditry in those nations.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Bastion is not named; the page refers only generally to towns in Highguard being fortified against banditry.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold's senator proposed the motion, received the Thrones and delivered the 40 wains of White Granite that paid for the work.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar's senator seconded the motion to fortify League, Marcher and Highborn towns.

Fortify Vigilant Swan.d: Proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by Hercynia, the motion called for improving the Vigilant Swan into a 3000-strong fortification defending Riverwatch, with no upkeep and no commission required. It cost 20 mithril, 20 ilium and 120 crowns, and took six months to complete. After the Summer Solstice, Shiloh provided the 20 rings of ilium, 20 wains of mithril and 14 thrones 7 crowns, with Farren Silver Streams adding a further crown. The work is now complete, and Riverwatch is defended by the Swans of Alabaster and Onyx fortification.

Highguard.t: Highguard gains a new fortification, the Swans of Alabaster and Onyx, strengthening its defence of Reikos, with the construction materials and most of the money supplied by Shiloh.

Fortify Vigilant Swan.o: The Senate passed a motion in Summer 386YE to fortify the Vigilant Swan, a White Granite bourse seat in Riverwatch, Reikos, with the aid of the Manse of the Lionsmith, under the Metal and Stone Wind of Fortune.

Reikos/Riverwatch.t: Riverwatch is now defended by the Swans of Alabaster and Onyx, a 3000-strong fortification raised at the Vigilant Swan that needs no upkeep.

Reikos.t: Reikos's own senator proposed the motion, and the territory now has a 3000-strong fortification built around the Vigilant Swan bourse seat.

Fortify multiple towns.d: Proposed by Upwold and seconded by Sermersuaq, the motion passed at a cost of 60 Thrones with 9 votes against, and the money went to Upwold. White granite was put towards fortifying regions in Miaren, Karov and Semmerholm. The motion broke constitutional protocol because Senate motions should contain a single item, but magistrates did not strike it down and construction began. The civil service suggested an Imperial position with authority and a treasury stipend to order fortifications would have achieved the same end. Seren, Delev and Lacre were only partially fortified. This curbs banditry but gives no military advantage, and 261 more wains of white granite are needed to complete all three.

Dawn.t: A Dawnish territory, Semmerholm, was one of the three chosen for fortification, though the work there remained only partial.

Navarr.t: The Navarr territory of Miaren was chosen as one of the three sites, but its fortification was left incomplete.

The Marches.t: The Marcher senator for Upwold proposed the motion, received the funds and chose which towns would be fortified.

Varushka.t: Karov, a Varushkan territory, was selected for fortification and received partial defences that ease banditry but give no military edge.

Fortify multiple towns.o: In Spring 377YE the Senate passed a motion from Upwold's senator to fortify three towns or regions of the Empire over Spring and Summer, with the senator for Upwold choosing the sites. Work in Miaren, Karov and Semmerholm left Seren, Delev and Lacre only partially fortified.

Karov.t: White granite was spent fortifying a region in Karov, but the fortification stayed partial: enough to deal with banditry, not enough to count as a full fortification.

Miaren.t: A region in Miaren was partially fortified under the motion, which helps against banditry but needs more white granite to become a proper fortification.

Semmerholm.t: Fortification work began in a region of Semmerholm but was left incomplete, giving relief from banditry but no military advantage.

Upwold.t: Upwold's senator proposed the motion, received the Senate's funds and selected the three sites, none of which lay in Upwold itself.

Fortify the Ore Hills.d: The motion passed in principle and at 150 Thrones, which were disbursed to Senator Upwold. Construction costs were reduced because the Empire had captured the partially built Jotun fort, so the work needed only 40 wains of white granite, 10 Thrones in labour and six months. Silas Merrick provided the white granite and the 10 Thrones after the Winter Solstice 379YE. Work began and was due to finish shortly before the Summer Solstice 380YE, provided the Empire still controlled the site.

Jotun.t: The Jotun had begun this fort in the Ore Hills and abandoned it half-built. The Empire captured it and set about finishing it as an Imperial fortification.

The Marches.t: Upwold's senator proposed the motion and received the funds. The fortification was intended to strengthen the Empire's hold on the Mournwold, a Marcher territory.

Fortify the Ore Hills.o: In Winter 379YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Upwold's senator and seconded by Hahnmark's, to complete a half-built fortification abandoned by the Jotun in the Ore Hills of Mournwold. The fortification was named The First Step.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: The captured, half-built Jotun fort in the Ore Hills was to be completed as The First Step over six months, using 40 wains of white granite.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold, then divided between the Jotun and the Marches, was to gain an Imperial fortification. It was due to be completed before the Summer Solstice 380YE if the site stayed in Imperial hands.

Forward into depthless dark.d: The Gryphon's Pride, Lions of Adelmar, Quiet Step, Black Thorns and Citadel Guard fought the White Lions, Hidden Widow, Jagged Claws, Red Lizard and Black Wind. The Northern Eagle's sabotage kept the garrisons of the Witness, Spires of Rarckan and Beacon of Iskrid out of the fighting. Lower Saarnath fell, costing a thousand Imperial lives, while the Druj suffered far worse. The Vileshrike sept, with Night heralds, hid Dripping Tor behind a magnitude 120 shroud and raised three Night Shackles. These threatened to make Lower Saarnath, Upper Saarnath and Beladrarsh terror-stricken. An Autumn Equinox battle offered a chance to break the shackles and finish off the Beacon.

Dawn.t: The Gryphon's Pride spearheaded the conquest, while the Lions of Adelmar, fighting beside Elodian's Knights of Glory, shielded their Navarri and Urizeni allies. The Lions' general was charged with recovering the Chain of the Hammerwright.

Druj.t: The Druj lost Lower Saarnath, suffered heavy losses and saw the Beacon of Iskrid in Leen almost destroyed. Meanwhile the Vileshrike ghulai prepared to curse their own subjects with the Delirium King's terror.

Navarr.t: The Black Thorns advanced cautiously to preserve lives, while the Quiet Step used ambushes and poison and set a watch on the shrouded Dripping Tor. The Thorns' general must kill the het Huk'nar Skintwister.

Urizen.t: The Citadel Guard spent the season working the Technique of the Transcendent Claw, which left the Beacon of Iskrid barely standing. An Urizeni Spring coven could finish it by casting Thunderous Deluge on a broken shackle.

Varushka.t: The Northern Eagle collapsed passes and bridges and destroyed caches, so that the Druj fortification garrisons could not intervene. They also scouted for the other armies before vanishing to plan their next strike.

Forward into depthless dark.o: In Summer 388YE five Imperial armies, aided by the Northern Eagle's groundwork, conquered Lower Saarnath in the Salt Flats of Sanath. The Citadel Guard's Technique of the Transcendent Claw then left the Beacon of Iskrid in Leen devastated but still standing.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Beladrarsh.t: Druj armies passed through its marshes with little help from the ruling Skinweavers. Its seven subject septs face the Shackle of Anguish curse unless the Empire breaks it, which could win a diplomatic victory.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Leen Rarckan.t: In the city of Leen the Beacon of Iskrid, seat of Prince Tristain the Golden, was battered by Urizeni storm magic and left barely standing. Scouts confirmed that armies cannot move between Leen Rarckan and Upper Saarnath without an opportunity.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Lower Saarnath.t: The region was conquered entirely by the Empire after a season of forest fighting. Its people now face terror from the Shackle of Sorrow unless the curse is stopped.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Sydathian Fens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Northern Eagle's general named the Sydathian Fens as the army's destination in his address.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Upper Saarnath.t: Imperial forces fought Vileshrike-backed Druj on the slopes rising toward this plateau, the gateway to Ûrinth. It is threatened by the Shackle of Misery curse and cannot be used to reach Leen Rarckan directly.
