Salt Flats of Sanath/Ûrinth.t: Mentioned in passing: described as the centre of the Salt Flats and a remaining Druj stronghold, reached through Upper Saarnath.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Axou of Thornfen were mobilising to advance to the Fens of Varreth, hopefully keeping the supply route open.

Sarangrave/Turan Flats.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial armies marched through the Turan Flats on their way into Sanath.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, which lets captured or vallorn-stricken citizens choose a painless death, extends into Brocéliande.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj armies were still battered from fighting there, and similar Night heralds had been met there months earlier.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: some of the armies joining the invasion marched from Ossium.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: The Empire seized Lower Saarnath, and the Beacon of Iskrid was left in ruins. Dripping Tor now lies hidden under Night magic while the Vileshrikes threaten neighbouring regions with a terror curse.

Sarangrave.t: The invading armies marched out of northern Sarangrave. The Axou of Thornfen mobilised in the hope of keeping the supply route into the Salt Flats open.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: some of the armies joining the invasion came from Semmerholm.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step's general left its defence to Varushkan cousins and hoped the campaign would draw its citizens away from Agramant; Kaela's Gift also extends there.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: some of the armies came from Zenith, and the season's nightmares were said to be worse than those reported during its liberation.

Forwards and Rewards.d: Dialogos proposed Prosperous Counting Houses, each costing 5 weirwood, 5 white granite and 30 crowns, to gather donations for the Virtue fund. They would yield 10 to 16 crowns a season in thirteen listed territories. Haravgi established that fines had been kept by magistrates only by tradition. Gerard La Salle accepted that they belong in the treasury, and the Constitutional Court ruled that the Senate could send them to the Virtue fund. Haravgi offered a Virtue Assembly mandate withdrawing labour from the Senate until it does so. Velko Perunovich Razoradze offered a rival General Assembly mandate demanding the fines return to the magistrates. Other proposals were the Beneficiary of the Golden Cascade, the Benefactor of High Chalcis, a Mitwold statue and a Mistress of Monuments title.

Dawn.t: A counting house in Semmerholm could add 11 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

Highguard.t: Jemimah of Chalcis Ford proposed the Benefactor of High Chalcis, chosen by the Highborn Assembly and given herbs to heal the virtuous. The title could also redirect the Gardens' bounty by Senate announcement if created by Senate motion. A counting house in Reikos could add 10 crowns a season.

Imperial Orcs.t: A counting house in Skarsind could add 13 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

Navarr.t: A counting house in Miaren could add 11 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

The Brass Coast.t: A counting house in Segura could add 13 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

The League.t: The League's wealthy territories topped Dialogos' list, with counting houses in Tassato, Holberg, Sarvos and Temeschwar yielding 14 to 16 crowns each a season.

The Marches.t: The Marcher Assembly exalted Jonathan Piper of Cockscroft for warning of Siakha's heralds. Mitwolders then proposed a statue of him at Wayford that would also remember the Wayford Wanderers and some thirty people killed by the heralds.

Urizen.t: Urizeni priests Dialogos and Haravgi drove the Virtue fund proposals. Dialogos also proposed the Beneficiary of the Golden Cascade, a Urizen Assembly appointment that would use herbs and potions from Zenith to win friends for Urizen across the Empire.

Varushka.t: The boyars were formally thanked by the Urizen Assembly for providing the wayleave for the Gardens of Pallas. Velko Perunovich Razoradze proposed a rival mandate to return fines to the magistrates. Without a greater majority, that mandate would still allow commissions in Varushkan territories and leave the Boyar of the Iron Roads unaffected. A counting house in Karsk could add 12 crowns a season.

Wintermark.t: A counting house in Hahnmark could add 11 crowns a season, while Sermersuaq was cited as a place where donations would be far smaller.

Forwards and Rewards.o: Following a Urizen Assembly judgement thanking the Varushkan boyars for a wayleave that helped build the Gardens of Pallas, Urizeni priests proposed ways to permanently boost the Imperial Virtue fund. Alongside these came proposals for herb-funded Imperial titles in Zenith and Reikos and a monument in Mitwold, while the Civil Service confirmed that magistrates' fines now go to the Imperial treasury.

Mitwold/Maiden Downs.t: The proposed Statue of the Cockscroft Lad would stand at the old Wayford Wanderers practice ground in Wayford, costing 5 white granite and 15 crowns.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Mentioned in passing: the City of Sarvos in Cigno was cited as an especially wealthy place where a counting house would gather far more donations.

Hahnmark.t: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 11 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

Holberg.t: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 15 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

Karsk.t: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 12 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

Miaren.t: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 11 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

Mitwold.t: A Statue of the Cockscroft Lad was proposed at Wayford, commemorating the warning against Siakha's heralds and those they killed. A counting house here could also add 12 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

Reikos.t: Reikos citizens would fund the proposed Benefactor of High Chalcis with 7 each of five herbs a season, from offices beside the Gardens of High Chalcis. A counting house here could add 10 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

Sarvos.t: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 14 crowns a season, its wealthy merchants making it one of the most lucrative sites.

Segura.t: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 13 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

Semmerholm.t: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 11 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as an example of where a counting house would draw far fewer donations than one in Sarvos.

Skarsind.t: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 13 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

Tassato.t: Tassato was the most lucrative site on the list, where a counting house could add 16 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

Temeschwar.t: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 14 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Jonathan Piper of Cockscroft, honoured by the proposed Mitwold statue, is noted to be an Upwolder.

Zenith.t: The Golden Cascade has boosted Zenith's farms and herb gardens, and its citizens would fund the proposed Beneficiary of the Golden Cascade from an enlarged counting house. That house would provide 10 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

Four and four.d: Barien's heralds were to hold court with House Geris in Wintermark and asked Wintermark's artisans to choose a schema. Janon's heralds fought beside the Burning Falcon in Kahraman, offered to join any general's army, and proposed ways to give the army True Conviction; more would visit the Imperial Orcs. Kimus challenged the Synod to explain what happens after death. Lashonar asked Eliza of Sarvos to rescue its herald Decius from Druj in Nesustak Forest. With its enmity lifted, Siakha's heralds stirred trouble across the Empire, marched from Semmerholm and challenged Mitwold travellers to fights. Tharim sought cursed Sarcophan curios, Ylenwe offered restitution, and Zakalwe rewarded Dawn's strategists and approached Wintermark and the Orcs.

Dawn.t: Zakalwe's herald Agon was to reward the Dawnish team from the Great Game, Janon's heralds sought Kahendrin Wordsmith, and Siakha's heralds goaded people into settling old scores in Dawn.

Druj.t: A Druj force of Arkad warriors and heralds of the Ashen Knight was hunting Lashonar's herald Decius in the Sarangrave, and a Druj ghulai held and befouled the Swan's Chalice.

Highguard.t: Ylenwe offered to help with the beacon of the Way in the White City if the enmity were removed and the General Assembly or Highborn National Assembly invited zie by statement of principle.

Imperial Orcs.t: Janon's heralds planned to visit the Orc camp to speak with the shatterers of chains, especially Ashborn Pakt, and Zakalwe's herald Asp was to discuss devising a new strategy game for the nation.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun were the foe the Burning Falcon fought in Kahraman with Janon's heralds alongside.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Spider King's support for some Navarr armies was cited as a model for Janon's proposed watch over the Burning Falcon.

The Brass Coast.t: Janon's heralds fought with the Burning Falcon, and the eternal offered ways, via a Freeborn assembly statement or a ritual using his token and 25 rings of ilium, for the army to gain True Conviction.

The League.t: Eliza of Sarvos was asked by Lashonar to save its herald from the Druj, and Siakha's heralds encouraged violence and theft in the League.

The Marches.t: Siakha's heralds were challenging Mitwold travellers to fights to the death, and Sally Thresher of House Talbot was asked to deal with them; similar incidents occurred elsewhere in the Marches.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka was one of the nations where Siakha's heralds egged people on to settle old scores.

Wintermark.t: House Geris was to host Barien's heralds, Wintermark's artisans had to choose the schema Barien owed them, and Zakalwe sought Wintermark strategists for the next stage of the Great Game.

Four and four.o: In Summer 385YE several eternals reached out to the Empire: Barien, Janon, Kimus, Lashonar, Siakha, Tharim, Ylenwe and Zakalwe sent heralds, offers, challenges and problems, including Sentinel Gate conjunctions to Sarangrave and Mitwold.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though the page refers to battles to retake Kahraman generally.

Mitwold/Golden Downs.t: The Sentinel Gate was to open to the Long Road in Golden Downs so threshers could confront the Siakha heralds challenging locals to fights.

Mitwold/Oddmire.t: Mentioned in passing: the troubled track begins at Odd's End before running towards Hay.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: Decius Frostspire took refuge in the Thicket of Thorns in Nesustak Forest, where the Sentinel Gate was to open for a rescue against the pursuing Druj.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: For several seasons bodies had been found gouged in Axmure's waters and dire beasts rumoured in its woods, before Siakha's heralds left for Anvil.

Bastion.t: Ylenwe expressed interest in contributing belltowers to the planned beacon of the Way in the White City, subject to the enmity being lifted and an invitation from the Synod.

Kahraman.t: Janon's midnight-blue heralds fought alongside the Burning Falcon in the battles to retake Kahraman from the Jotun, with little effect on the outcome.

Mitwold.t: More than half a dozen Siakha heralds were challenging travellers on the little-used track from Odd's End to Hay to fights to the death, and someone was suspected of having made a deal with them.

Sarangrave.t: Lashonar's herald Decius was trapped and pursued by Druj and Surut's heralds, the Druj miasma threatened any rescuers, and a ghulai there held the Swan's Chalice.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Eliza, the magician Lashonar asked to rescue its herald, hails from Sarvos.

Semmerholm.t: A posse of armed shark-like Siakha heralds and glowing changeling-like creatures emerged from Semmerholm and set off on foot for Anvil, following their prey.

Four strong winds.d: The opportunities were a mithril exchange, the Parador of Dust, in Kahraman; the Zeinodin Caravanserai, to be built in Segura once Anduz is freed; a renewed Iron Qanat for the Sobral Grasses; Zemress Islander payments to Imperial units fighting in Segura; a salvage Haven of Peredio; and relocating the Broken Shore Bounty offices out of Grendel-held Cazar. The Prosperity Assembly's condemnation of Lasambrian plunder angered corsairs, and two competing mandates followed. The Senate commissioned the Iron Qanat and sanctioned the House of Guerra. The Assembly sent Mazo i Zabala i Erigo to rally Segura's defence and Efenia i Maristela i Riqueza to champion privateering over trade. The Bounty stayed in Cazar, and the caravanserai remained available in Summer 384YE.

Grendel.t: The Grendel invasion of Feroz left the Broken Shore Bounty offices in Cazar in their hands, where they remained. Their weirwood-carrying ships were named as prey for corsairs, and the Assembly's mandate pushed Freeborn captains towards privateering against them.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Cinderpath Exchange in Casinea, whose construction began with rumblings among the Highborn, served as the model for the Parador of Dust, and the i Orieni had ties with fishing families in southern Highguard.

Jotun.t: The Lasambrian Jotun held Anduzjasse and parts of Anozeseri, and the Prosperity Assembly condemned them for taking rather than earning. The Zemress Islanders offered to pay Imperial units to fight them, and the Assembly sent a priest to rally Segura's defence.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gained a slate of opportunities, from a mithril exchange to a fortified caravanserai, and saw the Iron Qanat and House of Guerra sanctioned. Their corsairs were angered by the Prosperity statement until the Assembly's mandate endorsed privateering over trade.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the i Orieni family who ran the Broken Shore Bounty had ties with fishing and mercantile families in the southern territories of Urizen.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Roundtower in Varushka was cited as a similar commission that reduces the mithril offered at the public auction.

Four strong winds.o: In Summer 383YE, statements passed at the Spring Equinox, mostly by the Freeborn National Assembly, opened a series of opportunities across the Brass Coast while Jotun and Grendel invaders threatened its territories. The Senate went on to commission the Iron Qanat and the House of Guerra, and the Assembly backed privateering and the defence of Segura.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The Broken Shore Bounty offices remained in Grendel-held Cazar. Moving them would have signalled that the Senate doubted the Cazar Straits corsairs could protect them, a blow to the i Orieni family.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: The i Liscano parador in the western Jade Range, beside a major road towards Segura and Madruga, was proposed as the site of the Parador of Dust mithril exchange.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: The mithril-bearing hills of Serra Briante, home to the Great Mine of Briante, are one of the sources the Parador of Dust was meant to draw on.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: The Damatian Cliffs and the mines of Serra Damata, whose occasional mithril finds reach the town of Damata, would supply the proposed Parador of Dust.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Mentioned in passing: the corsair Isidore i Boyaga i Erigo put into harbour at Free Landing just long enough to propose the Haven of Peredio.

Segura/Anduzjasse.t: Conquered by the Jotun, Anduzjasse was where the Zeinodin Caravanserai would be built at the heart of the region once Anduz is freed. The caravanserai would cost 75 wains of white granite, 150 crowns and a Senate motion, and would pay the units that defend it.

Segura/Anozeseri.t: Parts of Anozeseri were held by the Jotun, so the Zemress Islanders' farms elsewhere in Segura were not under occupation, despite the wording of the Assembly's judgement.

Segura/Burnish.t: Mentioned in passing: fortifying Burnish was listed among Angelina i Duarte i Riqueza's plans for Segura.

Segura/Sobral Grasses.t: The Zemress Islanders revived the Iron Qanat to irrigate the sandy soils of the Grasses, allowing the Freeborn to support one more army or navy. The Senate commissioned it this season.

Segura/Yellow Chase.t: Mentioned in passing: Yellow Chase is one of the regions where the Zemress Islanders were given lands, which were not occupied by the Jotun.

Bay of Catazar.t: An Assembly statement urged the Freeborn to search the bay for salvageable weirwood, and the corsair Isidore proposed a haven on Peredio to gather salvage and captured Grendel weirwood. The bay's fishing nets are also the source of the Broken Shore Bounty's ilium.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the successful Cinderpath Exchange in Casinea inspired the proposed Parador of Dust in Kahraman.

Feroz.t: Grendel-occupied Cazar still housed the Broken Shore Bounty offices, which remained there in the Grendel's notional hands. The page warned that moving them would have damaged the morale of the corsair families and people of Feroz.

Kahraman.t: The i Liscano family proposed the Parador of Dust as a mithril exchange for the territory's mines, costing 16 white granite, 32 crowns and a Senate motion or wayleave. Kahraman hakima Chiara i Erigo led the case for celebrating privateering.

Madruga.t: The only Brass Coast territory not threatened by barbarians, Madruga was encouraged to build a hostelry, and there was talk there of urgently re-establishing the Broken Shore Bounty. The proposed Haven of Peredio would lie on an island where Madruga merges into the open sea.

Segura.t: The architect Angelina i Duarte i Riqueza proposed the Zeinodin Caravanserai, and the Senate commissioned the Iron Qanat. The Assembly also sent a priest to encourage soldiers to fight for the territory, backed by Islander payments to units supporting armies there.

Free to live.d: Backed unanimously by the Freeborn Assembly, the Islanders settled the Sobral Grasses and Yellow Chase with almost all their possessions, even livestock. They proposed the Iron Qanat irrigation works, or a fortified Water Tower variant, for the Grasses, and the Black Locks canals on the Scorrero. They also asked the Conclave and Spring Archmage to seek a Spring eternal to transform the arid Yellow Chase. Their tribal heritage is unknown and some may not descend from a Founder, so the egregore is reluctant to swear more of them. Horror at the Iron Confederacy slaughtering rebels in Feroz has halted oath-taking entirely, and some Islanders question whether another nation might suit them better.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: as the would-be conquerors and enslavers of the Isle of Zemress, whose navy the Empire evaded and whom the Islanders still fear.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Islanders are described as almost as devout as any Highborn citizen, and the transformation of Highborn-held Reikos inspired their Yellow Chase plan.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gained a hard-working new population with offers of great works that could feed an extra army or navy and enrich local fleets and congregations. However, unresolved questions of tribe and doctrine have stopped Islanders swearing to the egregore, and some now doubt they chose the right nation.

Free to live.o: In Spring 382YE the Zemress Islanders, rescued from the Grendel by a Freeborn-led armada, were raising hundreds of farms in Segura's Sobral Grasses and Yellow Chase. They proposed great works to improve their new home, while disputes over tribal heritage and doctrine stalled their integration into the Brass Coast.

Segura/Sobral Grasses.t: Hundreds of Islander farms have turned the once barren Grasses into busy grain land, though water and soil are poor. The proposed Iron Qanat or Water Tower would irrigate every farm and upgrade the Red Plains Farm and Golden Terraces.

Segura/Yellow Chase.t: The Chase proved too arid and rocky for crops, supporting little more than sheep and goats. The Islanders asked the Conclave and the Spring Archmage to consider persuading a Spring eternal to transform it.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Scorrero is described as the fastest and most turbulent of the great rivers that pour into the Bay.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: news that the Iron Confederacy was invited to slaughter the rebels sheltering in Feroz horrified the abolitionist Islanders and halted their integration.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the eternal Llofir's transformation of Reikos inspired the Islanders' hope that a Spring eternal might revive the Yellow Chase, though they noted it came at some cost.

Segura.t: Segura, still recovering from the Lasambrian orc conquest, was being revitalised by the Islanders' new farms. The proposed Black Locks would open the Scorrero to trade and pay rings to every fleet and congregation in the territory, and a Water Tower would fortify the whole territory.

Friend of mine.d: Asavean forces prepared a major assault on the northern Sumaah coast, with at least four likely targets including Zemeh. If Imperial fleets with at least 10,000 effective strength undertook Thwart the Blockade after the Winter Solstice, the assault would be repelled; otherwise a Sumaah city would burn. Some cynical voices argued that letting this happen would weaken a future rival. Through Ambassador Accalon, the Sumaah declined to help anchor the Way in Asavea but would not impede it. They sought rituals for scouting, raiding and defence, and urged the Synod to destroy the works tied to Vardas. Sumaah pilgrims would visit Holberg only if an assembly explicitly welcomed them.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: some argue that a Sumaah city's destruction would keep Asavean military might focused westward rather than on supporting the Grendel.

Highguard.t: Ambassador Accalon of Highguard led the Empire's dealings with the Sumaah and was thanked with liao and a personal gift of Sevensalve. Accalon was also asked what rituals could be offered and what the proposed magicians' secondment would involve.

The League.t: Sumaah pilgrims would come to Holberg only if the League National Assembly, the Assembly of the Way or the General Assembly passed a greater-majority statement welcoming them. The Civil Service warned that League congregations preaching support for Solokha could provoke a diplomatic incident.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen and Varushka were the only nations whose ships had not answered the mandate urging captains to aid the Sumaah in the Sea of Salt.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan ships, like Urizen's, had not answered the mandate to aid the Sumaah in the Sea of Salt.

Wintermark.t: Ambassador Oxtitocszin hoped Rafe would receive a gift at the Winter Solstice for supporting the Republic. She also hoped Wintermark could spare warriors and ships to help defend the Sumaah coast.

Friend of mine.o: In Winter 386YE the Sumaah Republic braced for an all-out Asavean naval strike intended to raze one of its cities, as Siroc had been razed. Imperial fleets had the chance to prevent it, while the Sumaah also responded to Imperial diplomacy on the Way, magic, gifts and a proposed pilgrimage to Holberg.

Bay of Catazar.t: Freeborn efforts in the Bay helped keep Sumaah trade flowing despite the Asavean bounty. Some warned that the more obviously the Empire foiled Asavean vengeance, the more force Asavea might commit to the Bay.

Holberg.t: After Bernard Kleist bon Holberg's invitation to the city's 250-year celebration, which Oxtitocszin declined, Sumaah pilgrims of Pride, Ambition and Wisdom showed interest in visiting Holberg's walls and shrines. They would come after the Winter Solstice only if an assembly explicitly welcomed them, and could take offence at preaching in support of Solokha.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: a Sumaah courier was to deliver 33 doses of liao to the embassy in Necropolis.

Friendly rivalry.d: Orc military units deployed away from their parent armies increasingly fought alongside one another. This built stronger links between them but also sparked competition in sparring, athletics and claims over which army had done more for The Plan. The civil service saw no harm in it. Imperial prognosticators judged that a statement of principle from the Imperial Orc National Assembly praising only one army's contribution to the Imperial Orc ambition would give that army's units a temporary but significant boost in morale and effectiveness. Praising both armies would have no appreciable effect. Atla raised a statement praising the Winter Sun alone, and its units duly received the boost.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, though the orc soldiers boast of the barbarian orcs they have killed, and one asks who broke the siege of Holberg.

Imperial Orcs.t: The rivalry between the Summer Storm and Winter Sun drew the two armies closer while sharpening their pride. Atla's statement of principle in the Imperial Orc assembly gave the Winter Sun's units a temporary surge of morale and battlefield effectiveness.

Friendly rivalry.o: In Winter 378YE, a friendly rivalry grew between the Imperial Orc armies of the Summer Storm and the Winter Sun as their military units fought side by side. Preacher Atla answered it with a statement of principle in the Imperial Orc assembly praising the Winter Sun, boosting the morale of its units.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: a Summer Storm soldier cites the breaking of the siege of Holberg as evidence of his army's achievements.

Froggy went a'courting.d: The Thule treaty of Summer 379YE expires at the Summer Solstice 382YE. It had brought an embassy in Miekarova, the Gift of the Dwindling Star, returned slaves and the Blood Cloak, and crystal mana trade through Crow's Ridge. The Thule built a slave-made castle in Krevsaty and showed armies there and on the Silver Peaks, without hostility. Their ambassador met Yevgeni Katzev, but no new treaty was reached. A Grendel delegation landed at Sarvos under truce, and its treaty offer was deemed unacceptable. The Great Forest orcs in Therunin sought clarity on ritual texts and payment. Cybi Farkas's ten wains of weirwood let work begin on the Holt of the Oak, though much remains outstanding.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as the reason the Great Forest orcs were forced to flee their homes.

Grendel.t: Speaker Morna's Grendel delegation sailed into Sarvos under a flag of truce to speak with the Imperial Consul at Anvil, but the peace treaty they offered was deemed unacceptable.

Imperial Orcs.t: Slaves taken from Skarsind had been returned under the Thule peace, and Imperial merchants travelled north from Skarsind to trade directly with the Thule while Thule traders passed through Crow's Ridge.

Navarr.t: Therunin's people were urged to share herbs with the Great Forest orcs, the Thimble's Navarr custodian lost 4 wains of weirwood a season, and Therunin's senator Cybi Farkas supplied the weirwood that let work on the Holt of the Oak begin. There were also rumours of Navarr dealings with the Thule over the vallorn.

The League.t: The League city of Sarvos received the Grendel ship bound for Anvil and gave it a frosty welcome, while its magistrates reminded everyone that the Grendel were protected by Imperial law.

Thule.t: With their three-year treaty ending in Summer 382YE, the Thule sent an ambassador to Anvil and showed restrained strength with armies in Krevsaty and the Silver Peaks. No new treaty was agreed.

Varushka.t: Varushka had gained an embassy in Miekarova and the Gift of the Dwindling Star under the Thule peace, but now faced a new Thule castle and army in Krevsaty, which was reported by the people of Branoc and Crowslook.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark had recovered slaves and the Blood Cloak from the Thule, with a dozen more slaves returned to Raknar, but it remained bitter over the ceding of the Silver Peaks, where Suaq hunters now saw large numbers of orcs.

Froggy went a'courting.o: Ahead of the Winter Solstice 381YE, delegations from the Thule, the Grendel and the Great Forest orcs were expected at Anvil, as the three-year Thule peace treaty neared its end and the Thule massed armies in Krevsaty and the Silver Peaks. No new Thule treaty was agreed, and the Grendel's peace offer was rejected.

Karsk/Branoc.t: Residents of Branoc reported the new Thule castle and army in neighbouring Krevsaty.

Karsk/Crowslook.t: Residents of Crowslook reported the new Thule castle and army in neighbouring Krevsaty.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: The Thule built a castle in Krevsaty using slave labour and stationed a substantial force there, which appeared to be drilling and hunting rather than preparing to attack.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: Suaq hunters in East Floes reported large numbers of orcs moving on the flanks of the Silver Peaks.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The Thule-held Silver Peaks, home to a castle conjured from the Summer realm, saw large numbers of orcs on its flanks, while Wintermark remained bitter over its ceding.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: Suaq hunters in Suaq Fount reported large numbers of orcs moving on the flanks of the Silver Peaks.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Thule merchants travelled through Crow's Ridge as part of the Senate-approved Northern trade network, bringing crystal mana to Imperial traders.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: rumours spoke of contact between the Thule and the Navarr of Hercynia, including talk of agreements on the secrets of the vallorn.

Karsk.t: The Thule built a slave-made castle in the Krevsaty region of Karsk and stationed what was almost certainly an army there, though it showed no signs of hostility.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: rumours spoke of contact between the Thule and the Navarr of Miaren, including talk of agreements on the secrets of the vallorn.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: an Imperial embassy to the Thule had been built in Miekarova under the peace treaty.

Otkodov.t: The dragons of Otkodov sent a delegation to Anvil to discuss the expiring treaty, while a few Imperial merchants traded directly with the Thule in southern Otkodov.

Sarvos.t: An Asavean-style Grendel ship docked at Sarvos under a flag of truce on its way to Anvil, and received a frosty reception given the Grendel's last visit.

Sermersuaq.t: Suaq hunters saw large numbers of orcs moving on the flanks of the Thule-held Silver Peaks, where bitterness over the ceding of that region persisted.

Skarsind.t: Slaves taken from Skarsind had been returned by the Thule, Thule merchants passed through Crow's Ridge, and a few Imperial merchants travelled north from Skarsind to trade in Otkodov.

Therunin.t: The Great Forest orcs living in Therunin received herbs, a share of the Thimble's weirwood and ritual texts, and work on their weirwood fortification, the Holt of the Oak, began after Cybi Farkas supplied ten wains.

From the sieve of your hands.d: Despite the Black Plateau's oppressive aura, Grendel forces took all of Spiral. The Salt Lord ruled from Apulian and promised the spires their rights and assets in return for hospitality and first refusal on surplus mana. While cooperation lasted, personal resources avoided the conquered territory penalty and Spiral's scholars helped the Doyen of the Spires codify rituals, though the Grendel would learn what was being worked on. She offered to let Spiral's Urizen support the failing Citadel Guard for six months in return for the secret of the Block's protective mithril ward. She threatened to destroy the Block or seize the spires if refused. Alcuin enacted the cooperation mandate, backed by Veikko Bondforger as Cardinal of Loyalty.

Druj.t: The Druj in Zenith became the Grendel's new neighbours. The Salt Lord sought to contrast her rule with theirs and began fortifying Ossuary against them.

Grendel.t: Grendel armies claimed all of Spiral under Salt Lord Mahiri Kaliact, at a cost from the territory's madness and despair. Urizen cooperation promised her trade, wealth and easier fortification work, and she sought the secret of the Block for her own settlements.

Urizen.t: Urizen citizens left in Spiral faced Grendel rule, and the Assembly chose to urge them to cooperate and trade. Meanwhile the Citadel Guard kept crumbling for lack of territory, with the Salt Lord's offer the only temporary reprieve on the table.

From the sieve of your hands.o: After the Senate ceded Ankra, Ateri and Cinion in Spiral under the Grendel peace treaty, Grendel armies claimed the whole territory. Salt Lord Mahiri Kaliact offered the remaining Urizen spires a light-handed rule if they cooperated, and the Urizen Assembly later enacted a mandate urging them to do so.

Spiral/Ankra.t: Ankra had been ceded to the Grendel under the treaty, and their armies moved in to claim it. Its citizens had two seasons' grace to leave.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: The Grendel consolidated their hold on Apstrus, and slave caravans hauling white granite were reported heading north through it towards Ossuary.

Spiral/Apulus.t: The Salt Lord established her court at Apulian on the southern coast and sent emissaries across Spiral from there, as the Grendel consolidated their hold on the region.

Spiral/Ateri.t: Ateri was one of the regions ceded to the Grendel by the Senate, and orc armies moved in to claim it.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Cinion was ceded to the Grendel, and the Salt Lord's proclamation was delivered to half its spires. It was home to the Block, the mithril ward the Grendel coveted and threatened to destroy.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: Grendel forces moved to take Ossuary. The Salt Lord set about fortifying it against the Druj, securing the Legacy and the Twilight Gate.

Spiral/Screed.t: Screed, the source of the oppressive aura of the Black Plateau, was among the regions the Grendel moved to take control of.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: listed in further reading on the wider Grendel situation in the Bay and opportunities there for the Empire.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: referenced in further reading as a Grendel-held territory in a situation both similar to and very different from Spiral's.

Morrow.t: Many Urizen displaced from Spiral had already made new lives in Morrow, and soldiers leaving the Citadel Guard joined fellow exiles there. Abandoning Spiral would have strengthened the territory further.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt sheltered many exiles from Spiral, and the Salt Lord's emissary appeared on its border to propose her bargain over the Block. An exodus from Spiral would have reinforced it.

Spiral.t: The whole territory came under Grendel control. The remaining Urizen spires were offered a cooperative détente, which the Assembly endorsed, while the fate of the protective Block hung on the Empire's answer to the Salt Lord.

Zenith.t: Druj-held Zenith now bordered Grendel Spiral. Urizen would need to reconquer several regions there, already damaged by the destruction of the Golden Cascade, to save the Citadel Guard.

Full circles.d: While helping resist Cold Sun in Jarm, Sevenfold Path magicians grew close to the Convocation of Virtue, a structureless fellowship of Jarmish pilgrims. A Conclave declaration brought by Damiàn i Martàn i Erigo, rather than Grandmaster Elagabala, sent them a gift of liao, and magistrates are investigating it as possible subversion. The Convocation honours Vasilia the Pilgrim as its spiritual founder and offered to share her story if invited for historical research. It proposed a House of the Pilgrim on the Bay of Catazar coast to host Jarmish pilgrims, offering four Jarmish star jewels in return. The Wayward House was commissioned in Spiral, and the Grandmaster successfully guided the order towards closer ties.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the accompanying story follows Nevyn, a Navarr vate, dining with a Jarmish magician after campaigning together against Cold Sun.

The League.t: The Wayward House, a shrine offering hospitality to Jarmish pilgrims of the Way, was commissioned in the League's territory of Spiral. The page also compares the Convocation's sect leaders to League bishops.

Full circles.o: The Sevenfold Path continued fighting Cold Sun in Jarm and made a major gift of liao to the Convocation of Virtue, a loose Jarmish fellowship of Way followers. The Convocation proposed a pilgrims' house in the Empire, which was later commissioned in Spiral as the Wayward House.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Convocation asked that the House of the Pilgrim be built in a coastal region on the Bay of Catazar.

Spiral.t: Spiral became home to the Wayward House, commissioned to welcome Jarmish pilgrims visiting the Empire's sites of virtue and meeting Imperial followers of the Way.

Full of sacred sound.d: Highborn armies had fought beside the Urizeni since 381YE, and the liberation of Zenith, together with the ending of slavery among the Axou, Sarcophans, Faraden and Thule and the destruction of Rachensgrab's slavers, rekindled the nation's fire. Highborn generals could no longer issue crusading storm. Instead, any Highborn army on campaign would create a mandate opportunity for the Assembly each season. Three mandates were proposed. Eli of Walter's Tomb urged Highguard to support its sibling nations. Mordecai of the Basalt Throne Chapter urged the nation to strengthen congregations and build places of worship at home. Dinah of the Passine Chapter, backing Lady Josephine's mandate, urged Highguard to put aside prejudice against orcs and the lineaged.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: temples are being raised in Dawn, and the Highborn Assembly has taken a keen interest in Dawnish Assembly affairs.

Druj.t: The Druj had been driven out of Zenith and Ossium, were falling back in the Barrens and were vulnerable in the Sarangrave. Many Highborn now called for their total annihilation.

Highguard.t: Highborn armies could no longer submit crusading storm but would automatically create mandate opportunities while on campaign. The Assembly was offered three compatible mandates: aiding other nations, strengthening the faith at home, and embracing orcs and the lineaged.

Imperial Orcs.t: Dinah argued that Highguard's focus on the human soul may have delayed the orcs' manumission. Lady Josephine's mandate, if enacted, would lead the Highborn to embrace orcs within the Empire.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn soldiers were sometimes redeployed to shore up the Western front as the Jotun pressed.

Navarr.t: Highguard had helped the Navarr turn back the vallorn in Brocéliande, so Navarr could not be named for further aid under Eli's proposed Peerless Kinship. The Highborn Assembly had also been considering Navarr Assembly judgements.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are listed among those the Empire convinced to abandon slavery.

Urizen.t: With Highborn help the Urizeni had their home of Zenith back, though it had been devastated. Because of that help, Urizen could not be named for further aid under Eli's proposed Peerless Kinship.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: temples are being raised in Varushka, and the Druj had been driven out of Ossium.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Dinah cited the hylje of Wintermark as creatures the Highborn have misjudged.

Full of sacred sound.o: Victories over the Druj in Zenith and the Empire's blow against slavery stirred a wave of Pride across Highguard in Winter 384YE. The Wind of Fortune changed how Highborn armies fight and offered the Highborn National Assembly three mandates that could all be enacted together.

Bastion.t: Mordecai of Bastion's Basalt Throne Chapter complained that few places of worship were being built there. Her mandate would boost congregations and support new temples and cathedrals in Highguard.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard had helped the Navarr turn back the vallorn there.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn blood was spilled against the Druj there during the long campaign.

Necropolis.t: Mordecai noted that very few temples or basilicas were being raised there. Her mandate would support building places of worship in Highguard's lands.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj had been defeated and driven out of Ossium.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj once took and devastated Reikos, the same evil Highborn armies kept returning to fight.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were described as vulnerable in the Sarangrave.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn blood was spilled there and the Druj were falling back after victories aided by Highborn generals.

Zenith.t: The comprehensive defeat of the Druj in Zenith, returning the land to the Urizeni though devastated, was the victory that sparked Highguard's surge of Pride.

Fund the Academy.d: Proposed by the senator for Bastion and seconded by the senator for Casinea, the motion asked the Senate to fund the Academy so that it could provide resources for training the next generation. It passed at a cost of 5 Thrones, with 12 votes recorded against. The motion is complete, and the funds were disbursed to Simiel of the Shattered Tower, the Senator for Bastion.

Highguard.t: A Highborn senator, Simiel of the Shattered Tower, proposed the funding and received the 5 Thrones on Bastion's behalf to resource the Academy.

Fund the Academy.o: In Spring 377YE the Senate passed a motion granting 5 Thrones to the Academy to train the Empire's next generation, with the money paid out to Bastion's senator.

Bastion.t: Bastion's senator proposed the motion, and the 5 Thrones granted for the Academy were paid out to Bastion through Simiel of the Shattered Tower.

Germinating a city.d: Relations with the Commonwealth improved thanks to progress on the Diplomatenschloss, busier trade at Leerdam and Volkavaar, and the Empire's respect for Commonwealth authority over Viyerda. The Jarmish embassy at Cargo remained a concern. The Senate had not approved the professors' appraisal auction, so they would leave after Spring Equinox unless it did. Their appraisal for Gisli found Siroc sunk beyond rebuilding and Madruga hampered by uncontrolled regions and the Children of Wrecks. They proposed the Municipal Docks great work at Calvos Sound, an optional Sternenmetal Tower giving the Commonwealth five years of exclusive access, and alternatives such as Sarcophan builders, Quzar or Autumn eternals. The docks were commissioned in Winter 387YE and completed before Autumn Equinox 388YE.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn learned that Siroc could not be rebuilt as their Assembly had urged, but were offered the Municipal Docks at Calvos as its successor. The docks would boost Freeborn fleets, businesses and incomes and create a Quaymaster post chosen by Tally of the Votes.

The League.t: The League Assembly's judgement welcoming Commonwealth guests was gratefully received, but it avoided endorsing the Common Good or calling the war against Jarm virtuous. As a result it drew only modest visitors and opened no new opportunity.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the scholars drew on intelligence from the recent scouting by the Unfettered Mind and the Rod and Shield.

Wintermark.t: Gisli 'the Provider' Baerson of Wintermark received the first Beurteilung, reportedly to fulfil an oath. Gisli used it to commission the study of building a new city in Madruga.

Germinating a city.o: Commonwealth scholars led by Professor Gelberg, acting for Gisli Baerson of Wintermark, reported that Siroc could never be rebuilt and proposed the Municipal Docks at Calvos to help the town grow into a great city. The wind also covered Commonwealth relations, the unused Beurteilung auction and the League's welcome to Commonwealth visitors.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: Calvos Sound was the proposed site of the Municipal Docks, which would fortify the region, act as a shipyard for two navies and could house the Sternenmetal Tower. The docks were eventually commissioned and completed in 388YE.

Madruga/Crucible.t: Mentioned in passing: the Crucible was listed as uncontrolled, an obstacle the scholars thought the Military Council could fix with relative ease.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: The Children of Wrecks' hold on Free Landing was named as the gravest threat to any building work in Madruga. The docks would also let Freeborn fleets hunt the young kraken growing in its waters.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: Mentioned in passing: Lightsea is not named directly and falls only under the general assessment of Madruga.

Madruga/Quiet Grasses.t: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Grasses were listed as uncontrolled, hindering development of the territory.

Madruga/Siroc Bayou.t: The ruins of Siroc sank beneath the water when the Scorrero rose, so the city can never be rebuilt there; the region was also uncontrolled. Only Sarcophan experts, at a premium, might manage building in the drowned ruins.

Holberg.t: Holberg's invitation to the Commonwealth during its 250th anniversary brought some interest but only a modest number of visitors, as the Lantir War made the voyage dangerous.

Madruga.t: The scholars judged Madruga hard to develop while three regions were uncontrolled and Free Landing was held by the Children of Wrecks. They proposed growing Calvos into a city through the Municipal Docks, which would raise taxation from the territory by 12 thrones a season.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named on the page; the only Urizen link is the scouting intelligence from the Unfettered Mind and the Rod and Shield.

Gifts of a green mother.d: Magistrate Nihm Farkas met the Watcher of Fragrant Leaves after Archmage Ibiss Briarheart's missive. The Green Mother offered several boons. One was aid in uniting the vallornhearts, if a coven cast Hallow of the Green World and let her children roam the Empire. Another was a Black Oak bough to lift the Wither the Seed curse from Brocéliande through Thunderous Tread of the Trees. She also offered milksap brewed with Churning Cauldron of Bravash, chaotic donahorti from farms, forests and mana sites, and empowered enchantments for briars and orcs. Magistrates warned they would prosecute anyone who accepted. The Silent Bell, the Senate and Netweaver's Eye were all offered as ways to detect lawbreakers.

Dawn.t: Astolat, Semmerholm and the Barrens were among the territories where the Black Oak bough could be used. Whichever was chosen would be ravaged by awakened trees so that the curse on Brocéliande could be lifted.

Druj.t: Yaw'nagrah is said to offer patronage to the Druj, but she is losing patience with their refusal to free the vallorn of Béantal Dol. She promised to help the Navarr do so instead if the Brocéliande curse were removed with her aid.

Highguard.t: Reikos and Casinea were offered as possible targets for the empowered Thunderous Tread of the Trees, and would suffer rampaging trees if chosen.

Navarr.t: The offer opened a perilous route to freeing Brocéliande from Wither the Seed, but at the risk of rousing its vallorn. It also held out the eternal's help in freeing the vallorn of Béantal Dol, alongside the Navarr's own expedition there. The herald blamed Navarr 'jealousy' for the gulf between Imperial magicians and the Green Mother.

Urizen.t: Yaw'nagrah offered to warp the Urizen rituals Fountain's Bounty and Woven Strands of Life on mana sites, producing milksap and donahorti instead of the usual yield. This relied on the complicity of Urizeni magicians and would be a crime while she remains under enmity.

Gifts of a green mother.o: In Winter 386YE a herald of the enemy eternal Yaw'nagrah answered the Spring Archmage's plenipotentiary with a range of boons for Imperial magicians. Because she is under the Conclave's enmity, accepting any of them was a serious crime unless that enmity was lifted.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Boar's Dell risked being lost to the vallorn if the curse were removed with the Black Oak bough, and Imperial heroes would be needed to defend its steadings.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Elerael risked falling to a roused vallorn if the Green Mother's boon were used to lift the curse, depending on which way the vallorn went.

Astolat.t: Astolat was one of five territories on which the bough-empowered Thunderous Tread of the Trees could be laid. It would face ravaging trees if chosen.

Brocéliande.t: Brocéliande was offered a way to remove the Wither the Seed curse with the help of Yaw'nagrah's servants. Doing so would inevitably rouse its vallorn, which the Broch could only partly blunt.

Casinea.t: Casinea was listed as a possible target for the empowered Thunderous Tread of the Trees, which would bring rampaging trees there.

Reikos.t: Reikos was listed as a possible target for the empowered Thunderous Tread of the Trees, which would bring rampaging trees there.

Sarangrave.t: If the Brocéliande curse were lifted with her bough, Yaw'nagrah would send servants to Sarangrave to help the Navarr free the vallorn of Béantal Dol.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm was one of the territories on which the bough-empowered Thunderous Tread of the Trees could be cast, which would leave it ravaged by awakened trees.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens was offered as a possible target for the empowered Thunderous Tread of the Trees, which would bring rampaging trees there.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Yaw'nagrah was first placed under enmity after her agents tried to rouse the vallorn of Therunin.

Given and denied.d: The Summer Storm, Marcher Drakes, Bloodcloaks and Green Shield gathered at Atalaq with nearly fourteen thousand warriors from independent warbands. The Thule laid the Rivers of Life enchantment over Sermersuaq and fell on the Jotun from the north. East Floes was liberated, and the Empire came four-fifths of the way to conquering Suaq Fount before the Jotun made a stand at Ikka's Tears. Each side lost roughly two thousand soldiers. The Jotun collapsed the western end of Pakaanan's Pass, destroying the Clattering Gulley and the Krampushal. The Thule offered to destroy a Jotun fortress if Imperial forces escorted their warlocks to the Pyhatunturi regio. A separate raid on Ikka's Trail could also seize four wains of mithril.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish heroes were among those fighting with the Autumn-enchanted Wintermark army, their bright tabards seen under fur coats.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Summer Storm fought at the heart of the Imperial push, and the Shield of the Mountain treated the orcs of Skarsind as respected rivals, with some soldiers hearing Sjöfn of the Bittenblade urging glorious conquest or death. The sealing of Pakaanan's Pass cut Skarsind off from Sermersuaq.

Jotun.t: The Jotun lost East Floes and were driven back across Suaq Fount to a stand at the Pride of Ikka's Tears, losing around two thousand warriors. They fulfilled their threat to seal Pakaanan's Pass and swore not to forgive the Thule for siding with the Empire.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr fought within the Wintermark army, and a Navarr messenger brought the Summer Storm word that Pakaanan's Pass had been sealed.

Thule.t: Three Thule armies joined the campaign as allies of the Empire, and their Rivers of Life enchantment greatly reduced the loss of life. Their warlocks offered to annihilate a Jotun fortification with the power of the Five-Who-Are-One, while making plain what such magic could do to others.

Wintermark.t: The Bloodcloaks and the Green Shield led the campaign to begin reclaiming Sermersuaq, liberating East Floes and pressing into Suaq Fount. Winterfolk heroes were singled out for challenge by Eisa Winterborn's Yegarra, and Rakner Ravenstorm was asked to lead a raid for mithril.

Given and denied.o: In Spring 384YE the Empire's armies, fighting alongside three Thule armies under the new alliance, drove the Jotun out of East Floes and pushed deep into Suaq Fount. The Jotun held on at the Pride of Ikka's Tears and sealed Pakaanan's Pass.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: After fierce fighting, including the fall of a Jotun camp at Wreck and the Battle of the Three Armies, East Floes was liberated by the Empire.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: The Imperial armies mustered at Atalaq in Sealtoq, where a Thule warlock camped outside the walls and sent messenger lizard-owls north-east before the advance.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Mentioned in passing: the retreating Jotun armies kept well clear of the foothills of the Silver Peaks as the Thule struck from the north.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: The Fastness of Kalant in Stark was cut off by months of blizzard and failed to support the Jotun. It is now one of the two fortresses the Thule have offered to destroy.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: The Empire is four-fifths of the way to conquering Suaq Fount, but the Jotun hold the Pride of Ikka's Tears. Suaq thralls there have hidden stolen ore that a raid on Ikka's Trail could carry off.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: The Jotun are moving mithril into the Suaq Wastes. The Pyhatunturi regio there, held by Eisa Winterborn's Yegarra and used by the Ice Dragon, is the site of the Thule ritual battle opportunity.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: Olgafsdottirshal in Tanikipari was kept out of the campaign by blizzard and is one of the two fortresses the Thule have offered to destroy.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: The Jotun sealed the western end of the pass, closing the route to Sermersuaq and destroying the Clattering Gulley and the Krampushal.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is not named; the page only involves the Thule armies and warlocks who joined the campaign from the north.

Sermersuaq.t: Imperial and Thule armies liberated East Floes and came close to taking Suaq Fount, but the Jotun still hold the mine at Ikka's Tears and their fortresses in Stark and Tanikipari. The territory is no longer linked to Skarsind by Pakaanan's Pass.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Yegarra under Eisa Winterborn may be descendants of Suaq thralls raised among the Jotun in Tromsa and Skallahn.

Skarsind.t: The Jotun collapsed the western end of Pakaanan's Pass, so armies can no longer pass between Skarsind and Sermersuaq.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Yegarra under Eisa Winterborn may be descendants of Suaq thralls raised among the Jotun in Tromsa and Skallahn.

Glass and flame.d: After the Summer Solstice the Empire withdrew from Madruga. The Burning Falcon, Fire of the South, Red Wind Corsairs, Fist of the Mountains, Narwhal's Spear, Eastern Sky, Valiant Pegasus and Wolves of War invaded Feroz under cursed rains, probably raised by the Children of Wrecks. The Wolves' engines broke Oran within a day and Rahab's palace was razed. Bramar and Afar fell and slaves were freed. Gallum Fiersach still holds Mora's Rock. The pirates have seized the Cazar Straits. The Senate may now assign Feroz, which is ruined and under a ruinous rains curse. Surrendered Asavean priests await the Freeborn generals' judgement, and Grendel raiders are looting Sarvos's Isle of the Fox.

Dawn.t: The Eastern Sky, fighting beside the Summer war-witch Dindrayne and Eleonaris' trumpeters, kept pace with the Burning Falcon at the head of the invasion and pursued the fleeing Grendel through Fontargenta and Afarjasse.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj miasma is cited as an example of a fear effect that inspired Imperial soldiers might answer with anger.

Grendel.t: The Grendel lost Oran, Bramar, Afar and three regions of Feroz. Many of their fleeing ships were butchered by pirates, and their remaining forces hold Mora's Rock under Gallum Fiersach while their main army stays in Siroc Plains.

Highguard.t: The Valiant Pegasus under Zadok joined the overwhelming assault and wiped out Grendel fleeing towards the Suranni border before they could reach it.

The Brass Coast.t: All three Freeborn armies helped reclaim Feroz, and assigning the territory to the nation would restore its army supply. The Freeborn generals must also decide the fate of the surrendered Asavean priests in Oran.

The League.t: The Wolves of War and their Tassatan siege engineers broke Oran and fought the dock fire through the night. Meanwhile Grendel raiders are looting the Isle of the Fox, which supplies the Sarvos Mana Exchange.

Wintermark.t: The Fist of the Mountains, alongside the Summer herald Elodian, and the Narwhal's Spear took Afar. They freed hundreds of slaves and executed the orcs who held them.

Glass and flame.o: Eight Imperial armies, backed by Summer realm champions, marched from Lucksprings into Feroz in Autumn 386YE and liberated Oranseri, Fontargenta and Afarjasse from the Grendel, conquering the territory. The Grendel fortress of Mora's Rock held out in Morajasse.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: The Fist of the Mountains and the Narwhal's Spear stormed Afar, Rahab's regional capital, and freed the slaves worked on his farms, bringing the region under Imperial control.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The Children of Wrecks have seized the islands, which are now infested with beasts and pirates. The region has gained the island quality and cannot be attacked without naval support.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: The Grendel made a stand at Bramar while pirates raided its docks, then fled before the Empire, and the region fell to Imperial forces.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: The Imperial advance faltered before Mora's Rock, which Gallum Fiersach holds with a large garrison and possibly the Wind Lord Saoirse. The region remains under Grendel control.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Oran fell within a day to the Wolves of War's siege engines and Rahab's palace was reduced to rubble. The town was left heavily damaged by fighting and a dock fire.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Mentioned in passing: timber for the Wolves of War's siege engines was carted from the forests of Misericorde.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Mentioned in passing: Free Landing, stolen by the Children of Wrecks, is cited as the model for the pirates' seizure of the Cazar Straits.

Segura/Lucksprings.t: All eight Imperial armies and their Summer allies mustered at Cerevado in Lucksprings under Spring-infused rain before marching into Feroz.

Bay of Catazar.t: Pirate vessels from the Cazar Straits fell on Grendel ships fleeing Oran across the bay, and only about one in three escaped.

Feroz.t: The Empire conquered Feroz and it awaits assignment by the Senate. The territory lies ruined after Rahab's rule and the fighting, and suffers a Spring curse of ruinous rains, while Mora's Rock remains in Grendel hands.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves' engineers hauled timber from Holberg's Misericorde forests, and a few Sand Fishers accompanied them.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Zadok recalls the Valiant Pegasus's hard-won victory in Kahraman, and the territory had given sanctuary to refugees from Feroz.

Kalino.t: An Iron Confederacy army camped just across the border watched as the Valiant Pegasus destroyed fleeing Grendel, amid rumours of a Suranni pact with the Grendel.

Madruga.t: The Imperial armies withdrew, leaving the Grendel and their Asaveans fortified in Siroc Plains. Foul weather persists, and the Spring-roused Scorrero has broken its banks into the Blightheart.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the strengthened Mora's Rock is compared to Reumah's Rest.

Sarvos.t: A company of Grendel is looting the Isle of the Fox's mana stockpiles, and Steward Wolfgang Wilheim Von Vanderghast must stop them or the Mana Exchange's supply will fall.

Segura.t: The Fire of the South moved through Segura under cover of darkness to strike Oranseri, and many displaced Ferozi had earlier found refuge in the territory.

Goatfoot.d: For three months a horned, shaggy figure was sighted around Pakaanan's Pass, and occasionally in northern Northspires and eastern East Floes. At least a dozen mammoth carcasses were found near the Clattering Gulley, killed by apparent misfortune, then stripped of bones and tusks and their organs eaten. A week before the equinox the creature was identified as the Krampus, which curses those who confess crimes to it, the curse lasting until the next winter. It accosted caravans of the Crossroads of the North entering Skarsind, while expeditions sent to hunt it fell into disaster. It sought a compact with the Skarsind orcs, lamented that Burnlin Drum-Heart had not sent Runesmiths to carve the stones, wanted a hall of bones and a home before winter, and invited them to its camp. A Sentinel Gate conjunction would let eight people visit it.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Krampus addressed its message to the orcs as the new masters of Skarsind, offering to hear their sins and form a compact with the Skarsind tribe, and inviting them to its camp. One orc band that tried to hunt it suffered disaster.

Wintermark.t: The Krampus, previously associated with the Wintermark egregore, now seemed to seek a new home among the orcs, and lamented that Burnlin Drum-Heart had sent no Runesmiths to carve the stones. A Suaq hunting party that set out to challenge it met with ruin.

Goatfoot.o: In autumn 380YE the Krampus, a curse-dispensing spirit linked to the Wintermark egregore, was revealed as the shaggy beast haunting Pakaanan's Pass in Skarsind after months of mutilated mammoth corpses. It began shouting a message to the Imperial Orcs, inviting them to its camp above the Clattering Gulley.

Hahnmark/Northspires.t: Northern Northspires saw occasional sightings of the Krampus during the three months before the equinox.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: The Krampus was occasionally spotted along the eastern shores of the East Floes.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: The Krampus lurked at Pakaanan's Pass, accosting travellers and merchants entering Skarsind while ignoring those leaving, and its camp above the Clattering Gulley became the target of a Sentinel Gate conjunction.

Hahnmark.t: The Krampus was occasionally seen in northern Northspires, though its activity centred on neighbouring Skarsind.

Sermersuaq.t: The Krampus was sometimes sighted along the eastern shores of the East Floes, and a Suaq hunting party that tried to challenge it ended in chaos and lasting injuries.

Skarsind.t: The Krampus made its camp above the Clattering Gulley, slaughtered mammoths in the area, accosted Crossroads of the North caravans entering the territory, and sought a compact with its new orc masters.

Golden Sails.d: A Grendel navy roughly equivalent in strength to an Imperial army anchored south of Shantarim and the Isle of Osseni, too large for individual fleets to challenge. It escorted a single weirwood trading vessel carrying a Grendel diplomat and a small honour guard. The Grendel were furious that the Empire had kept raiding their ships in the Bay of Catazar despite agreeing a cessation of hostilities, having hoped the Jotun threat on their border would bring the Empire to a profitable accord. The diplomat travelled via Sarvos under Freeborn escort and was protected by the law of delegation protection. Ambassador Cartok was received at Anvil, where a peace treaty was discussed; he returned to Feroz without incident and the fleet sailed south.

Grendel.t: The Grendel sent a massive war fleet as a pointed show of force to escort their ambassador Cartok, demanding an end to Imperial raiding of their ships, and discussed a peace treaty at Anvil before sailing home.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the growing Jotun threat on the Grendel border is cited as a reason the Grendel hoped the Empire would agree to an accord.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn of Feroz were alarmed by a Grendel war fleet anchored off their coast that could threaten the whole territory, while Freeborn vessels escorted the Grendel diplomat onward towards Anvil.

The League.t: The Grendel diplomat's ship passed safely through League waters via Sarvos on its way to Anvil.

Golden Sails.o: In Summer 379YE a Grendel war fleet, the Golden Winds, arrived off southern Feroz escorting a diplomat sent by Salt Lord Suriad to negotiate with the Empire at Anvil over continued Imperial raiding of Grendel ships in the Bay of Catazar.

Bay of Catazar.t: Continued Imperial raiding of Grendel shipping in the bay, despite an agreed cessation of hostilities, provoked the Grendel show of force, and the Grendel warned that the bay was not safe.

Feroz.t: A Grendel navy roughly equivalent to an Imperial army anchored south of Shantarim and the Isle of Osseni, posing a serious potential threat until it sailed south after the diplomat's return.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn girl in Feroz mistook the Grendel fleet for the new navy being built in Madruga, still at least six months from completion.

Sarvos.t: The Grendel diplomat's route to Anvil took him through Sarvos under Freeborn escort.

Golden Trumpets.d: The trumpets sounded over the Semmerstones, in a Sarvosian theatre, at the Gate of Summer, in a quiet hall in Hahnmark, at a crossroads in Karov and in the great hall of the Lyceum. The message declared that whoever performed the greatest arcane projection, drawing on any realm, between the Winter and Summer Solstices would be named Champion of Meraud and carry his favoured staff for a year and a day. What the staff does is unknown, though it is expected to be potent and may relate to the realm of the winning ritual. Meraud cares only who performs a projection, not who devised it. The contest also offers a chance to impress, and perhaps gain the patronage of, the Summer eternal.

Dawn.t: A chorus of trumpets sounded over the Semmerstones in Dawnish lands, bringing Meraud's challenge directly to Dawn's magicians.

Navarr.t: Meraud's proclamation thundered through the great hall of the Lyceum in Navarri-held Hercynia, inviting the covens there to compete for his staff.

The Brass Coast.t: The announcement rang out at the Gate of Summer in Brass Coast territory, giving Freeborn wizards the chance to compete for the title of Champion of Meraud.

The League.t: A deafening roar of trumpets burst out in a Sarvosian theatre, carrying Meraud's challenge to the League's magicians.

Varushka.t: A terrifying explosion of sound at a crossroads in Karov delivered Meraud's challenge to Varushkan wizards.

Wintermark.t: A deafening blast of brass broke the quiet of a hall in Hahnmark, announcing Meraud's contest to Wintermark's magicians.

Golden Trumpets.o: In Winter 379YE, golden trumpets rang out from the air at places connected to Summer magic across the Empire, and a voice proclaimed that the eternal Meraud challenged Imperial wizards to create and perform arcane projections. The coven performing the highest-magnitude ritual before the start of the Summer Solstice would win a boon.

Hahnmark.t: Golden trumpets blasted through an otherwise quiet hall in Hahnmark, one of the Summer-linked sites where Meraud's challenge was proclaimed.

Hercynia.t: The trumpets and Meraud's proclamation resounded triumphantly in the great hall at the Lyceum in Hercynia.

Karov.t: A terrifying explosion of trumpet sound erupted at a crossroads in Karov, where the voice announced Meraud's contest.

Madruga.t: Meraud's challenge was announced at the Gate of Summer, one of the places tied to Summer magic where the trumpets sounded.

Sarvos.t: A deafening roar of golden trumpets filled a Sarvosian theatre as Meraud's challenge was proclaimed there.

Semmerholm.t: A chorus of trumpets rang out over the Semmerstones, carrying the Summer eternal's call for wizards to perform great arcane projections.

Golden light.d: Capodomus, an ancient centre of study for the Way looted during the Grendel sack of Sarvos, had been restored after a three-year League effort. If the General Assembly sent a named priest with true liao to consecrate the Atrium of Golden Light to Ambition, the cathedral would become the pre-eminent place to study the Way. The Archbishop would gain ten extra crowns each season and could deliver an inaugural sermon heard across the Empire. Further options would include a 50-crown Lucati Gallery of paragons and exemplars, and a 30-crown tomb for Empress Giselle. Citizens could freely switch to their nation's voting resource, priests could encourage pilgrimage, and each national assembly could reward one ambitious citizen.

Dawn.t: If the consecration went ahead, Dawnish citizens could switch their personal resource to a military unit in the same territory without paying the usual fee, and their national assembly could reward an ambitious citizen each season for a year.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: as the raiders who sacked Sarvos, looted the cathedral's art and gold filigree, and carried off Empress Giselle's remains.

Highguard.t: Highborn citizens could freely gain a congregation, the resource that counts in their Tally of the Votes, and the cathedral was described as larger even than Highguard's Basilica of Seven Doors.

Imperial Orcs.t: Orcs could freely switch to a military unit, though only units supporting Imperial armies accrue votes, and Thrace, founder of the Imperial Orc nation, was proposed for the Lucati Gallery.

Navarr.t: The famous painting of the Navarr Thorn Isaella hangs in the cathedral and the guardian Thorn was proposed for the Lucati Gallery, while Navarr citizens could freely acquire herb gardens if the consecration went ahead.

The League.t: The League would gain the Empire's most prestigious seminary of the Way, a richer and more influential Archbishop of Capodomus, and the chance to bring Empress Giselle home to Sarvos, while its citizens could freely acquire businesses.

Urizen.t: Urizen citizens could freely switch their personal resource to a mana site in the same territory if the mandate passed, and their national assembly could reward an ambitious citizen.

Varushka.t: Varushkans could freely switch to a mine or forest in the same territory if the consecration went ahead, and Ratibor of Temeschwar was proposed for depiction in the Lucati Gallery.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark citizens could freely switch to a military unit in the same territory if the mandate passed, and their national assembly could reward an ambitious citizen each season.

Golden light.o: After the Assembly of Ambition backed Prince-Bishop Estella Lucati's call to truly consecrate Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos, the civil service set out what a Synod mandate from the General Assembly consecrating the cathedral's Atrium of Golden Light to Ambition would achieve. The consecration was a proposal awaiting that mandate.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Empress Giselle refused her place in the Necropolis on her deathbed, asking to be buried in Caricomare instead.

Sarvos.t: Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos would host the true consecration, drawing pilgrims and scholars from across the known world, and could receive the Lucati Gallery and Empress Giselle's tomb.

Temeschwar.t: Empress Giselle's recovered remains rest in a modest tomb in Temeschwar that recent events made untenable, and the Archbishop could have them moved to Sarvos with little effect on Virtue's Respite.

Golden magicians fayre.d: Dawnish characters, and Navarr whose personal resource lay in the Barrens, could each choose one Summer boon for the Spring Equinox, which came with a sense of fierce pride. Meraud, recovering from his malady, appeared changed and now contests Hayaak's old realm with Jaheris. Heralds of Eleonaris and Cathan Canae clashed while offering boons to the armies in Astolat and to frozen citadels, including a permanent citadel in Hope's Rest. Jaheris offered to retune the Harps of Astolat, Adamant and Meraud proposed a college at the Semmerstones, Rhianos boosted questing, and Barien gave Dawnish artisans a schema. The vigilant warned of rising borderline idolatry, and the conjunction means such national weavings may not happen again.

Dawn.t: Every Dawnish citizen could take a Summer boon with a roleplaying effect of fierce pride, and the nation received several offers to accept or decline: the Harps proposal, the Semmerstones college, the Rimebound citadel, questing rewards and Barien's focus schema.

Druj.t: The heralds of Cathan Canae loathe Druj corruption and are eager to fight the servants of the Buruk Tepel. The Thane's proposed citadel would garrison Hope's Rest against the Druj of the Mallum, and some servants of Rhianos accompanied thorns scouting into the Mallum.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Granite Pillar, encamped in Astolat, was among the seven armies eligible for Eleonaris' boon if enchanted with Knights of Glory. Units supporting it would then gain a boon that includes a Golden Apple.

Navarr.t: Navarr who had moved their personal resource to the Barrens could choose a Summer boon and shared its roleplaying effect, and heralds visited the new Navarr wayhouses, steadings and stridings there.

The League.t: The League's Wolves of War, encamped in Astolat, could benefit from Eleonaris' boon if enchanted with Knights of Glory. Some heralds of Rhianos also accompanied questors as far as Lorenzo's Deep Pockets.

Varushka.t: The Northern Eagle in Astolat was eligible for Eleonaris' boon and was tested by the warriors of Cathan Canae. If the Semmerstones college is built, the Summer eternals would be less fixated on competing for patronage of the Icy Crag.

Golden magicians fayre.o: In Spring 387YE a Dawnish weaving of Summer magic, lasting six months rather than one season, drew heralds of almost every Summer eternal except Hayaak into Dawn's four territories. They brought personal boons, rival offers and proposals, and a pervasive urge towards splendour and pride.

Astolat/Coombe.t: If Jaheris' offer is accepted, creatures of the Forest of Arden would congregate in Coombe and it would gain the wild woods quality, raising the labour cost of most commissions there by half. Locals already fear vallornspawn from neighbouring Brocéliande.

Astolat/The Chase.t: The folk of The Chase, who already suffer occasional miasma and vallornspawn, fear being defenceless if abominations pour out of Brocéliande. They are making what preparations they can without support from the Synod, Senate or Military Council.

Brocéliande/Black Boughs.t: Mentioned in passing: Black Boughs is named as a place from which Astolat's people fear vallorn monsters will come pouring.

Brocéliande/Greenweald.t: Mentioned in passing: Greenweald is named alongside Black Boughs as a feared source of vallorn abominations.

Semmerholm/Causse.t: The proposed Circle of the Semmerstones would stand at the Semmerstones in Causse as an unbreakable college of Summer magic. It must be commissioned before the end of the Summer Solstice 387YE.

Semmerholm/Estmure.t: Heralds of Cathan Canae roamed the hills of Estmure, already guarded by the castle of the Adamant Gate, while weighing how best to protect Dawn.

Semmerholm/Lacuve.t: The heralds of Eleonaris established a camp at Lacuve, around the Dawnish end of the Golden Causeway.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: A frozen citadel raised here every season for a year would give Hope's Rest the Rimebound quality, and 100 rings of ilium could summon the Thane's own citadel as a permanent, upkeep-free fortification against the Druj. That offer stands until the Spring Equinox 388YE.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: Heralds of Rhianos made a particular point of seeking out the Last Battle Wayhouse in the Bleaks, to the chagrin of the already unhappy Karass.

Astolat.t: Seven Imperial armies camped here amid visiting heralds. The Bards of the Crescent offered to retune the Harps of Astolat so they yield silver pears and moonberries instead of extra mana, if the Knight-protector of Winter invites them. The vigilant found no sign of Agramant's cults but warned of growing borderline idolatry.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: people in eastern Astolat fear that vallorn abominations will pour out of Brocéliande once plans to fight the vallorn come to fruition.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: some heralds of Rhianos accompanied Dawnish questors as far afield as the Forest of Ulnak.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris' heralds camped at Lacuve within sight of the memorial to the invasion of Ossium.

Semmerholm.t: Rival heralds of Eleonaris and Cathan Canae clashed here, causing damage and disruption but no deaths. Adamant and Meraud's servants proposed building the Circle of the Semmerstones college at the stones in Causse.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: a number of Meraud's heralds visited the de Casillon nobles at Spiral Castle, given their shared history.

The Barrens.t: Heralds visited Dawnish settlements, orc septs and Navarr settlers alike, and Cathan Canae's heralds camped at the White Bear construction site. The Thane of the Rimebound Shore offered empowered and permanent frozen citadels for Hope's Rest.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thane of the Rimebound Shore prowled the banks of the great lake between the Barrens and Therunin.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater was under the Summer weaving, and its people met visiting heralds and saw open fighting between the courtiers of Eleonaris and the warriors of Cathan Canae.

Good apples.d: Following a Marcher Assembly judgement citing a true aura on Bastard Tom of Stoke as Good Walder's inspiration, rumours of the paragon spread across the Marches, and villages decorated old apple trees they claimed were his grave. In the Golden Downs, just south of Hay near the Mourn border, the oldest tree in a copse said to mark Walder's grave, and all its neighbours, became heavy with fruit. The friars proposed a folly (5 wains of white granite, 10 crowns) creating the title Keeper of Good Walder's Grave, or a larger sinecure shrine yielding liao and Synod votes. Alternatively, the site could become an inspirational tomb using true liao. None was commissioned during the Summer Solstice, but the opportunities remain open.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Good Walder's lessons are said to be preached in Highguard today.

The Marches.t: Marcher villages across several territories are claiming a part in Walder's story, and the friars of Hay asked that the Marcher Assembly, or at a stretch the Prosperity Assembly, appoint any Keeper of Good Walder's Grave.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Walder's warnings about good hospitality are said to be appreciated as far afield as Varushka.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Walder's stories were told in Wintermark long before there was an Empire.

Good apples.o: After rumours spread that Good Walder's ghost had appeared at Anvil, an old apple copse near Hay in the Golden Downs of Mitwold, long said to mark his grave, burst into miraculous fruit. The friars of Hay proposed honouring the site with a folly, a larger shrine sinecure or an inspirational memorial.

Mitwold/Golden Downs.t: Just south of Hay, an old apple copse said to be Walder's grave is groaning with fruit, and it could host a folly, a sinecure shrine or an inspirational tomb if the resources are provided.

Bregasland.t: A few places in Bregasland have joined in the rumours, reminding passers-by of their village's part in Walder's story.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold is home to the miraculous apple copse near Hay, where the friars proposed a folly, shrine or memorial to Good Walder, none of which has yet been built.

Mournwold.t: Even a couple of pubs in the Mourn are claiming a part in Walder's story, and the miraculous copse lies near the Mourn border.

Upwold.t: Several places in Upwold are claiming a part in Walder's story and tying ribbons to ancient apple trees said to mark his grave.

Good as gold.d: Shortly before the Summer Solstice, Grendel wave riders seized Gelberg near the mouth of the Couros; someone had clearly betrayed his whereabouts. An attempted rescue through the Sentinel Gate ran into a trap, and he remains a living prisoner. His team published their report: the Visitors Docks of Hedra in Hedrossan, Necropolis, costing 100 white granite, 20 mithril and 360 crowns, taking 12 months.
