It would give congregations in Necropolis, Bastion, Morrow and Redoubt 36 rings each per season, but only once the Grand Inspiration of the Way is complete. It is available until the end of Summer 390YE. A student revealed Gelberg had an unfinished idea for creating coastal access where geography forbids it.

Grendel.t: Grendel wave riders penetrated Imperial defences to abduct Professor Gelberg, foiled the rescue attempt with a trap, and show no sign of releasing him.

Highguard.t: Gelberg judged Highborn Necropolis and Bastion the lands most in need of investment, blaming the Grand Inspiration of the Way for absorbing Highguard's wealth, yet the proposed docks depend on that monument's completion to draw pilgrims.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr-held Therunin marked one end of the stretch of the Couros the appraisal was asked to consider.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Morrow and Redoubt already benefit from significant great works, but would still gain 36 rings each season for their congregations if the Hedra docks are built.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark merchants are listed among the traders who use the port of Hedra.

Good as gold.o: Professor Immanuel Gelberg's Commonwealth scholars, commissioned through the Beurteilung by Nekoda of the Shattered Tower, published their appraisal of the River Couros after Gelberg himself was abducted by Grendel raiders. They proposed a great work, the Visitors Docks of Hedra, to channel pilgrim donations to congregations along the river.

Necropolis/Hedrossan.t: The port-town of Hedra in Hedrossan, already a trading hub boosted by the diplomatenschloss, is where the Visitors Docks great work would be built to receive passenger vessels bound for the White City.

Bastion.t: Bastion, home of the Grand Inspiration a short journey from Hedra, would see its congregations receive 36 rings each season from pilgrims once the docks and the monument are complete.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar marked the far end of the river stretch the appraisal was asked to examine.

Morrow.t: Morrow's congregations would gain 36 rings each season from pilgrim donations if the proposed Hedra docks are built and the Grand Inspiration finished.

Necropolis.t: Necropolis, judged the place where the most good could be done, is the proposed site of the Visitors Docks, which would give its congregations 36 rings each season after the Grand Inspiration is complete.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt's congregations would receive 36 rings each season from the pilgrim trade if the Hedra docks great work is completed.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Therunin was named as the starting point of the Couros stretch the scholars were tasked to appraise.

Good faith.d: After negotiations collapsed and the Grendel assaulted The Fist, copies of a letter from High Lady Suriad, Salt Lord of Dubhtraig and Head of the Council of Attar, reached Navarr couriers and were passed on to senators and notable citizens. She accused the Empire of piracy on the Bay of Catazar and of twice negotiating in bad faith, and declared that the hostages would work the salt. Those who know the Grendel say this means a short, brutal life of slavery in their salt mines, and that once the captives reach Attar any hope of recovering them is lost. In response, the Senate voted to invite a Grendel delegation to Anvil at the Winter Solstice to discuss terms for ending the war.

Grendel.t: The Grendel, led by High Lady Suriad, abandoned any pretence of seeking peace and refused to free the Imperial hostages, an act that shows how furious, and perhaps surprised, they were at how their negotiations with the Empire had gone.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr couriers received copies of the Grendel letter and delivered them to senators and other notable citizens.

Good faith.o: In Autumn 379YE the Grendel sent a letter from High Lady Suriad declaring that the Imperial children they had taken hostage would not be released but would instead be put to work in the salt, ending hopes that they would honour their earlier promise.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Grendel blamed Imperial 'merchants' for decades of piracy on the Bay of Catazar, claiming they wanted no war there while declaring that the Empire's demands for war would now be met.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is not named, though the letter refers to an earlier Grendel offer to restore land to the Empire in exchange for an end to piracy.

Good old smooth red wine.d: Building on the wealth brought by the Blood Red Roads, four projects were proposed. The first was a Boar's Hollow market-fayre in Winterbourne, creating a yeofolk Reeve of Boar's Hollow to buy Bourse materials. The second was a Three Fayres ministry at Brightway, Oldheart and Weaving, creating a Reeve of the Three Fayres who would keep merchants safe and buy goods. The third was the Field of Silver Fishes at Laroc, which must be ceded to the eternal Rhianos and would allow Summer Quests. The fourth was a refurbishment of the Laroc tourney grounds as a great work. None had been built. Each would remain available until the end of the Summer Solstice 385YE.

Dawn.t: Dawn's yeofolk and noble houses were offered new reeve titles, fayres, a Rhianos-linked folly for adventuring military units and fleets, and a refurbished tourney ground that would make upgrading Dawnish military units cheaper for a year.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the page refers to Spiral Castle, a Dawnish house seat in Weirwater, rather than to the Grendel-held territory of Spiral.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is named as one of the prosperous lands reachable by the Blood Red Roads, and as a source of travelling merchants for the proposed fayres.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr is listed among the nations whose merchants could reach the proposed Astolat fayres via the Blood Red Roads.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: League merchants are expected to visit the proposed fayres, and Temeschwar and Holberg are linked to Astolat by the Blood Red Roads.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is named as a trading partner reachable by the Blood Red Roads, and Varushkans appear among the guests in the opening story.

Good old smooth red wine.o: After the Cardinal of Prosperity, Darian Numbers, directed the Prosperity assembly's attention to Astolat at the Summer Solstice, the seneschals and visiting pilgrims put forward four commission opportunities to further enrich the territory and Dawn as a whole.

Astolat/Grovesyard.t: A monthly fayre was proposed at Brightway in Grovesyard, selling herbs and potions, as one of the Three Fayres.

Astolat/The Chase.t: Laroc in The Chase would host both the proposed Field of Silver Fishes, ceded to Rhianos, and the refurbished tourney grounds great work.

Astolat/Winterbourne.t: Winterbourne would gain the proposed Boar's Hollow market-fayre for Bourse materials and the Weaving fayre, which would sell raw materials at the crossroads of the Blood Red Roads.

Astolat/Withy.t: A fayre was proposed at Oldheart in Withy, selling enchanted rods and mage armour, as one of the Three Fayres.

Semmerholm/Lacuve.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named. The page only notes that the Blood Red Roads pass through Semmerholm.

Astolat.t: Astolat, described as perhaps Dawn's richest and most peaceful territory, was the focus of all four proposed commissions: two fayre ministries, a folly at Laroc and a great work that would add a share of 743 rings each season to every business in the territory.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: in the opening story, knights return from Brocéliande with Wisdom pilgrims.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: one branch of the Blood Red Roads runs through the Castle of Thorns to connect Astolat with Casinea.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the northern branch of the Blood Red Roads runs through Weaving and Semmerholm to Holberg city.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the Blood Red Roads pass through Semmerholm, and its yeofolk had earlier proposed market-fayres at Applefell or Lacre, which failed to win support.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only as Spiral Castle, a de Cassilon seat in Weirwater, not as this territory.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Blood Red Roads link Astolat to Temeschwar, whose prosperity the Boar's Hollow market-fayre hopes to draw upon.

Weirwater.t: The de Cassilons of Spiral Castle in Weirwater pledged to patron a grand tourney if the Laroc grounds were refurbished, letting their Castellan upgrade up to a dozen Dawnish military units to rank 2.

Goodwill.d: Dawn opened Greenwood Manor so that units across the Empire could quest against the vallorn, subject to a Senate motion. Gwinthav offered vials of Whitesmoke if Whitesmoke Brook is diverted at the Flame of the Phoenix. Hayaak offered the Eastern Sky the Slay the Monsters order if its general swears to oppose tyranny. The Earl's Council was asked to endorse the highest calling. Navarr visiting Highguard prompted proposals for a Vallornguard office in Tabernacle, an appraisal for a grand chancery, and having the Vallornguard elect the general of the Pilgrim's Defiance. The Necropolis Stewards recovered Rhonwen's cursed wand. The Great Forest Orcs urged the Conclave to interdict magical deforestation or place Surut under enmity.

Dawn.t: Dawn gained several vallorn-focused opportunities: an Effervescent Brook ministry, Hayaak's offer to the Eastern Sky, and an invitation for the Earl's Council to back the Assembly's highest calling to unlock further preparations.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the current war with the Druj is cited as a conflict that would become a lesser priority if Dawn's earls endorse the vallorn as its highest calling.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: battles against the Grendel in the south are named among conflicts Dawn would deprioritise by focusing on the vallorn.

Highguard.t: Highguard welcomed visiting Navarr and offered to host the Vallornguard, with proposals for an office in Tabernacle, a grand chancery appraisal, and letting the Vallornguard elect the general of the Pilgrim's Defiance.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: battles against the Jotun in the west are named among conflicts Dawn would deprioritise by focusing on the vallorn.

Navarr.t: Navarr shared their accumulated wisdom with Highguard to support the Vallornguard, aided the Necropolis Stewards in recovering Rhonwen's wand, and relayed the Great Forest Orcs' appeal against Surut and magical deforestation.

Goodwill.o: Following Summer 388YE judgements making the war against the vallorn Dawn's highest calling and pledging Navarr support for the Vallornguard, a series of opportunities emerged in Dawn, Highguard and the Conclave to prepare for the coming final war against the vallorn.

Astolat/Grovesyard.t: The Effervescent Brook ministry would be built in Grovesyard, giving the Tender of the Phoenix Flame access to vials of Whitesmoke for one year.

Reikos/Riverwatch.t: A Vallornguard Office sinecure could be commissioned in Riverwatch, rebuilding the ruined Unbound Steel Hall as the sodality's headquarters and providing an income to its Speaker.

Astolat.t: Diverting Whitesmoke Brook through the regio of the Flame of the Phoenix in Astolat could create a ministry yielding vials of Whitesmoke for vallorn-fighting rituals.

Casinea.t: Casinea was named as one of two possible sites the Senate could appraise for a grand Vallornguard chancery.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Miaren is listed as a possible recipient of Rhonwen's cursed wand.

Necropolis.t: The Stewards of the Necropolis, aided by Navarri historians, recovered Rhonwen's cursed wand and asked the Highborn Assembly who should receive it to speak with her shade.

Reikos.t: Reikos could host a Vallornguard headquarters in the rebuilt Unbound Steel Hall in Tabernacle, and was proposed as a possible site for a grand Vallornguard chancery.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr character laments that folk are dying in Therunin while the fight against the vallorn stalls.

Gorgeous.d: Sarcophan Alders-Baart merchants returned to sell cursed curios, and Axou apothecaries of Evander and Associates came to trade outside the Forge. Two exiled Faraden nobles planned a curse duel in the Dawnish Glory Square, and four Grendel questioners invited by Clarice Novarion came to debate with the Synod. The late Urizen seer Flavia of Crystal Hall left an undisclosed prize for whoever solves her puzzles. Three Suranni siblings from Shavronne came to sell metal, and Krampus's attendance was uncertain after its Wintermark hall was destroyed. The six weirwood seats, the wayleaves, the rogue declaration and a dose of true liao were auctioned, and several national titles were put to the vote.

Dawn.t: The Faraden curse duel was to be held in the Glory Square of the Dawnish camp, and Dawnish citizens commanding military units were to choose the first Reeve of Boar's Market; the Suranni traders might also seek out Dawnish yeofolk, with whom they had traded well before.

Grendel.t: A small group of bickering Grendel questioners from the Broken Shore visited the Empire as guests of the Synod while peace held, touring Imperial monuments and seeking philosophical debate with Imperial priests in the Senate.

Highguard.t: The visiting Grendel priests toured the Necropolis and the City of Bastion, taking in its tombs and basilicas, including the cenotaph of Emperor Barabbas and the Basilica of Seven Doors.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orcs who command military units were to choose the new Four Seasons' Boneweaver and the Preceptor of the expanded College of Warcasting, with votes weighted by how often their units had supported an army in the past year.

Jotun.t: Krampus's known connection to the Jotun, and its lack of interest in a new Wintermark hall, raised fears it had relocated to Jotun lands, perhaps Skallahn; the defeat of the Lasambrian Jotun was also noted as having settled matters in Segura.

Navarr.t: Navarr herb garden owners were to choose who controls the Thimble and the Broker of the Invisible Cord, Navarr were paid to carry Flavia's puzzles across the Empire, and questions about the Navarr were thought likely to affect interest in some weirwood seats.

The Brass Coast.t: Bramar in Feroz no longer gave Suranni traders access under Grendel occupation, while Iron Confederacy caravans tested trade links in settling Segura; Flavia had lived and died at the Lyceum in Madruga.

The League.t: League business owners were to appoint the first Chair of the Wolf and a short-term Northbound Trademaster, and a mix-up wrongly cast the Axou traders as an entourage for the now-legal League magician Evander Slak.

Urizen.t: The late seer Flavia of Crystal Hall left most of her collection to her surviving spire to help those returning to Zenith, and one undisclosed item to whoever solves her puzzles, overseen by her executor Advocatus.

Wintermark.t: With the Krampushal destroyed in the collapse of Pakaanan's Pass and the spirit silent for a year, it was unclear whether Krampus would visit the Wintermark camp, and what its absence might mean for the Winterfolk.

Gorgeous.o: Ahead of the Winter Solstice of 384YE, a crowd of foreign visitors, traders and curiosities made their way to Anvil, alongside the season's Imperial auction of titles and the Bourse's tally of the votes.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Mentioned in passing: Bramar, once a route for Suranni land trade, was under Grendel occupation and no longer gave access to the Empire.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Mentioned in passing: lies on the Necropolis route the Grendel questioners took on their way to Anvil.

Segura/Anduzjasse.t: Iron Confederacy caravans explored possible trade links in Anduzjasse as Segura settled after the Lasambrian Jotun's defeat.

Segura/Anozeseri.t: Iron Confederacy caravans explored possible trade links in Anozeseri, though sanctions limited Suranni enthusiasm.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: The western end of the pass, collapsed by Eisa Winterborn and her allies a year earlier, remained sealed, its avalanches having swept away the Clattering Gulley and Krampus's hall.

Bastion.t: The Grendel questioners visited the City of Bastion, viewing its tombs, monuments and basilicas, including the cenotaph of Emperor Barabbas and the Basilica of Seven Doors.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: referenced only in a brief aside about the obstacles discouraging Suranni trade with the Empire.

Casinea.t: Anvil in Casinea hosted the summit's visitors, with the Grendel questioners arriving in Casinea and renting the top floor of the Sun and Sand Inn in Outer Anvil.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel occupation of Bramar meant the Freeborn town no longer offered Suranni land traders access to the Empire.

Madruga.t: Flavia of Crystal Hall had spent a decade in her apartments at the Lyceum in Madruga and was found peacefully dead in its Quiet Annexe after the Autumn Equinox.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel questioners travelled via the Necropolis on their route to Anvil.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest at Reikos was one of the six weirwood seats put up for auction.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: most Suranni merchants trade through the embassy in Sarvos, and the three siblings set out north from there to Anvil.

Segura.t: With Segura settling after the defeat of the Lasambrian Jotun, a couple of Iron Confederacy caravans explored possible trade links there, though sanctions made such trade unappealing to most Suranni.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the collapse of Pakaanan's Pass sealed the passage between Skarsind and Sermersuaq.

Shavronne.t: The Larbin siblings, rival merchants of Shavronne, joined forces to bring metals mined from its hills to sell directly at Anvil.

Skallahn.t: There was growing worry that Krampus had relocated to Jotun lands, with Skallahn suggested as a possible new home.

Skarsind.t: The collapse of Pakaanan's Pass in Skarsind a year earlier had destroyed both the Clattering Gulley and the Krampushal, leaving Krampus without its hall.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: the Weirwater Vales weirwood seat was among those auctioned.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Flavia's collection was to be sold to help members of her spire returning to Zenith.

Gossamer threads.d: The Wings of Kobol navy defeated the Wreckers in the Cazar Straits, and the Dukes refused to cede the islands. They planned to take Free Landing after the Spring Equinox and invited Freeborn fleets to join, offering loot and, with 4000 military strength, access to Atalaya's relics. A hakima, Indira 'Stormdancer' i Guerra, proposed an ilium-enhanced curse on Madruga to wreck the assault at heavy local cost. Suranni troops attacked Reinos, and Duke Guiscard of Arbonne sought supply passage through Segura for mithril. Four conjunctions involved the Hand of Dumon and a fleeing Lasambrian warband.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are recalled as earlier conquerors of the Cazar Straits, as holders of some lost corsair wealth, and as having once saved the Naguerro sept from destruction.

Jotun.t: The Lasambrian Jotun homeland of Reinos came under Suranni attack, raising fears it might meet Kalino's fate while the rest of the Jotun look elsewhere. A fleeing Lasambrian warband carried intelligence on the invaders.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn fleets were invited to join the Suranni assault on Free Landing for loot and a chance to reclaim Atalaya's relics. A Freeborn hakima instead proposed a costly curse on Madruga to make the attack fail.

The League.t: A sect of the Hand of Dumon plotted to curse the Suranni embassy in Sarvos, and the Dukes suggested land around that embassy might be ceded to them as trade premises.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark historical researcher Marko Siwarsbairn was seized by the Hand of Dumon while returning through Arbonne, to be sacrificed unless rescued along with his research.

Gossamer threads.o: In Spring 388YE the Iron Confederacy, at peace with the Empire but no ally, held the Cazar Straits after crushing the Children of Wrecks, announced an attack on Free Landing and invaded Reinos. Ambassador Baroness Katerine Lavasse floated treaty, trade and supply-route proposals.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Seized from the Children of Wrecks by two Suranni armies, the islands are claimed by the Confederacy. Trapped Freeborn are free to leave on Suranni ships.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Oranseri's Bay of Oran keeps Feroz connected to the wider sea, and the Dukes might help bridge the Scorrero there. A Suranni invasion would isolate Feroz's ships.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: If the proposed curse were cast, work on the municipal docks funded by Gisli 'Provider' Baerson would halt, delaying completion to Spring 389YE.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: The Wings of Kobol planned to attack the Wreckers here after the Spring Equinox, with Freeborn fleets invited. A rival plan proposed devastating storms to turn the Suranni back.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: If the proposed curse were cast, work on the Well of Life would be delayed by three months.

Madruga/Siroc Bayou.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Oran is described as stretching between Oranseri and Siroc Bayou.

Reinos/Chaveiro.t: Chaveiro's plains are speculated to be the first target of the Suranni invasion, though this rests only on the lie of the land.

Bay of Catazar.t: Many Wrecker vessels fled the Bay of Catazar after their defeat, and the civil service found that Feroz cannot be cut off from the bay while the Bay of Oran stays in Imperial hands.

Feroz.t: The Suranni held the Cazar Straits and would not give them up. The Hand of Dumon moved to sacrifice the herd of Afar, and a Suranni invasion of Oranseri would isolate Feroz's ships.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: curse-warding designs by Richard of Holberg are cited as a precedent for a Suranni anti-curse temple.

Kalino.t: Called Arbonne by the Suranni, it remained plagued by Hand of Dumon curses and was the launch point for attacks on Feroz and Reinos. Its Duke sought ilium for a protective temple.

Madruga.t: The Suranni planned to take Free Landing, and a proposed ilium-enhanced curse to stop them would cost Madruga's fleets, farms, herb gardens and coastal settlements heavily.

Reinos.t: A significant Suranni force invaded from Arbonne after the Winter Solstice. Its progress is unknown because the Imperial spy network there had been decommissioned.

Sarvos.t: Hand of Dumon diabolists prepared to call down a curse on the Suranni embassy, and the Dukes suggested land around the embassy as possible trade premises.

Segura.t: The Dukes proposed a treaty letting Suranni supply lines pass through Segura in exchange for mithril for Kabalai Palace. A fleeing Lasambrian warband was also targeted there.

Shavronne.t: Mentioned in passing: Baron du Bestel of Shavronne wrote to the Champion of Ambition asking for the Lasambrian warband to be destroyed.

Veroigne.t: Mentioned in passing: the ambassador's seat of Chaubrette is said to lie west of Veroigne.

Grace that comes with healing.d: With Ylenwe's Dawn Chorus aiding the work, the River Doubt was dammed, flooding much of Apstrus, and part of its flow was diverted to Icarion. Kirriemuir in Icarion gained a fizzing Day-regio spring, offering a Senate opportunity for a beauty spot that would encourage Yerende settlement. Ylenwe proposed the Harmonious Chimes edifice in Screed which, with music by Hieronymus Dowland, Lirielen Starsong and Kespoena Archsky, would quiet the Black Plateau for a year, though Pawdrig duSesna warned this could invite Grendel invasion. Ylenwe also offered to name a Cultivator of Solace, now illegal to accept, and sought to discuss a holistic manifesto with the Silver Chalice.

Dawn.t: Hieronymus Dowland of Dawn was asked to perform his perfect piece in the Hall of Worlds and was Ylenwe's first choice to be offered the role of Cultivator of Solace, though accepting it would now be illegal under the Synod's proscription.

Grendel.t: The Salt Lords Council, having lost entire armies when the Black Plateau exploded, are wary of invading Spiral while it rages, so quieting it could remove a deterrent against a Grendel invasion.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orcs ensured none of their kin's bones lie beneath the Apstrus reservoir and inscribed the names of their fallen at Solen's Doubt into the dam, and their senators would appoint the proposed Keeper of the Kirriemuir Campgrounds.

The League.t: Red Raven Holdings built the Dreaming Spire as a League gift to Urizen Spiralites, while Pawdrig of the duSesna Guild of Reckoners argued that the Black Plateau may be helping to keep Grendel armies away from Apulian.

Urizen.t: The texts of the drowned Solen's Doubt library were moved to the Dreaming Spire, the new Omphalos and heart of the Urizen nation, and Urizen's Lirielen Starsong and Kespoena Archsky were asked to perform the music needed to soothe the Black Plateau.

Grace that comes with healing.o: The Day eternal Ylenwe, after a year of amity, reached out to the Empire with a plan to quiet the Black Plateau using perfect mortal-composed music, while the damming of the River Doubt in Apstrus and the new Dreaming Spire reshaped Spiral and helped turn Icarion into an oasis.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Icarion is thriving on the Lesser Doubt's waters, and the Senate may develop the Kirriemuir campgrounds into a beauty spot producing prismatic ink and giving the region the Yerende quality.

Spiral/Ankra.t: The Dreaming Spire now stands on Mount Cinnius in Ankra, housing the Omphalos of Urizen and the rescued Library of Solen's Doubt.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: Much of Apstrus, including the Solen's Doubt battle site, now lies beneath a calm reservoir behind the Holbergian-designed dam, and the region gained the ruins and marsh qualities.

Spiral/Screed.t: Ylenwe proposed the Harmonious Chimes, thirteen mithril and ilium monoliths spiralling out across Screed from the Black Plateau, to lull it to quiescence for a year and open the way to a permanent solution.

Mareave.t: Water diverted from the dammed Doubt is reducing Mareave's aridity, with Icarion fast becoming an oasis and a Day-regio spring rising at Kirriemuir.

Spiral.t: Spiral saw the Doubt dammed and the Dreaming Spire completed, and was offered a chance to quiet the Black Plateau for a year, at the possible risk of losing its deterrent effect on Grendel.

Graveyard rats.d: After the Summer Solstice the Chamber of Commerce paid the Rat Kings a nine-month retainer, which may need renegotiating at the Spring Equinox 387YE. Their traps and dogs curbed the swarms, but Virtue's Respite, Empress Giselle's tomb, was attacked twice, halving its liao and money. Four people were eaten in grisly deaths, including the d'Hanuri brothers, and some citizens wondered whether the Silent Bell might investigate. The mountebank Brinton von Temeschwar, who claimed a token for parleying with the King of Rats, has vanished. Bishops preaching Vigilance or Loyalty gained congregants. Doctors proposed a Temeschwar Apothecary Supplies ministry for bladeroot and prismatic ink, and rumours spread of a great beast stalking the streets.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the d'Hanuri brothers' smashed bottle of wine had been brought all the way from Astolat.

The League.t: League citizens in Temeschwar gained respite from the swarms through the Rat Kings, whose contract may need renegotiating. Temeschwar congregations preaching Vigilance or Loyalty will gain two votes but lose a dose of liao, following Emil Radana von Temeschwar's statement in the League assembly.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the doctors blamed nearness to Varushka for some of the city's strange maladies and noted that bladeroot is easy to get from there, and one rumour blamed a Varushkan merchant's potion for a bravo's monstrous transformation.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: a crude charm against the rats carried by one of the d'Hanuri brothers bore Wintermark runes.

Graveyard rats.o: Temeschwar's rat plague was brought under control in autumn 386YE after the city's Chamber of Commerce hired the Rat Kings guild, though Giselle's Tomb kept suffering attacks, several people were gnawed to death and the King of Rats remained at large. The city's doctors also proposed a new ministry to stockpile cures for the rat sickness.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: wine brought from Astolat appears in the story of the d'Hanuri brothers.

Temeschwar.t: The Rat Kings contained the plague in the city, but Giselle's Tomb produced half its usual income, four people were gnawed to death and rats still watched the streets. A proposed apothecary ministry in Hanari remained open until at least the end of the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Great prosperity and strength.d: With the Cinderpath Exchange built, white granite withheld by virtuous citizens went to auction (about a dozen extra wains) and to the Cinderpath Custodian. Ilium meant for the lost Broken Shore Bounty went partly to auction and partly, as a private gift, to Imperial Fleet Master Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra. The Iron Roundtower was built, while the Invisible Cord Brokerage was commissioned but not yet built. The Marches were offered the Blackfield Market. Dawn, the Imperial Orcs, Wintermark, Urizen and the League received outline proposals, each needing a statement of principle with a greater majority. Bishop Imago Monta also suggested an Ombudsman of the Bourse. Wintermark backed Valashal, Dawn failed to back Applefell, and interest faded by Winter.

Dawn.t: Dawnish yeofolk proposed a weirwood market-faire at Applefell and an ilium Star Metal Market at Lacre, both overseen by yeofolk appointed by military unit captains. The Dawnish assembly failed to win a greater majority for Applefell.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Legacy mine remains in Druj hands, and the loss of Zenith is cited as a blow to Urizen.

Grendel.t: The Grendel invasion of Feroz cost the Empire the Scorrero Nets and the Broken Shore Bounty, leaving Bay of Catazar ilium undeliverable to its Freeborn seat.

Highguard.t: The Cinderpath Exchange was finally built in Highguard. Highborn who had withheld white granite at the Synod's urging now offered it to the Cinderpath Custodian, and other withheld granite went to auction.

Imperial Orcs.t: The orcs were offered a possible Miner's Market at Krysse in Skarsind, where a bonesetter appointed by military unit owners could buy mithril at reasonable prices, if their assembly showed interest with a greater majority.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Pride of Ikka's Tears now serves the Jotun once repaired, and a new weirwood grove has been found in Jotun-held Liathaven.

Navarr.t: The Invisible Cord Brokerage was commissioned in Navarr but not yet built. If completed, it is expected to reduce the weirwood available at the public auction.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn lost the Broken Shore Bounty and Scorrero Nets. Grateful mariners began gifting ilium to Fleet Master Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra, and the Freeborn are discussing the mithril-dealing Parador of Dust.

The League.t: League merchant-princes proposed a single market in Holberg, Tassato, Temeschwar or Sarvos buying all four Bourse resources. It would need an assembly statement choosing the city, and how it would be appointed remained hotly debated.

The Marches.t: Following its assembly's call for an exchange, the Marches were offered the Blackfield Market in Mitwold. It would buy white granite under a Blackfield Bailiff elected annually by Marcher farm owners.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule invasion and conquest of Skarsind is recalled as the cause of Gulhule's and Krysse's past losses.

Urizen.t: Urizeni architects proposed a market in northern Siluri in Redoubt for mithril, ilium or both, which would need an assembly statement naming the resources. This came after Urizen's prosperity suffered from losing Zenith, the invasion of Morrow and fighting over Spiral.

Varushka.t: The Varushkans completed the Iron Roundtower, reducing mithril at the public auction. Its title became available for appointment at the Autumn Equinox.

Wintermark.t: Hahnmark traders proposed Gulnar's Deephall for mithril and a Valashal hall for white granite, with each also able to buy some ilium. The Wintermark assembly indicated that Valashal would benefit the nation.

Great prosperity and strength.o: In Autumn 383YE the Bourse was reshaped by Synod-driven calls for 'fair prices'. The Cinderpath Exchange and Iron Roundtower were completed, the Grendel seizure of Feroz diverted ilium, and several nations were offered proposals for their own national Bourse ministries.

Hahnmark/Valasmark.t: A white granite trading hall was proposed at Valashal in south-east Hahnmark, and the Wintermark assembly indicated it would benefit the nation.

Redoubt/Siluri.t: A mithril and/or ilium market was proposed in the foothills of northern Siluri, needing new roads and a bridge.

Skarsind/Estermark.t: Estermark's Gulhule is booming once more, while Krysse proposed a Miner's Market buying mithril, which would need road works.

Bay of Catazar.t: Fisherfolk and mariners unable to deliver ilium to the Broken Shore Bounty sent 10 rings to auction (then about four a season). Wealthier captains sent six rings to the Fleet Master, then four a season, with help from the Fellowship of the Purple Sails.

Casinea.t: An estimated additional dozen wains of white granite, released by citizens who had withheld it, were brought to Casinea to be auctioned.

Feroz.t: The Grendel invasion of Feroz cost the Empire the offices of the Broken Shore Bounty and the Scorrero Nets.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark's merchants and miners proposed two possible trading halls: Gulnar's Deephall for mithril and a hall at Valashal for white granite, each also buying some ilium.

Holberg.t: Holberg was one of four League cities that could host the proposed market buying all four Bourse resources.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: the page refers only to ilium netted along Varushkan shores of the Semmerlak and Skarsind mithril heading east to Delev and the Iron Roundtower.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: a new weirwood grove has been discovered in Liathaven.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: a Summer proposal would move the Broken Shore Bounty's offices to Siroc, where the Salt Guard could protect them.

Mitwold.t: The Blackfield Market could be built at Blackfield on the road between Meade and Wayford, buying white granite. It would need a Senate motion or wayleave, 12 wains of weirwood, 24 crowns in labour and three months' work.

Morrow.t: Morrow's peaks are a noted source of fallen ilium, though invasion has hurt its prosperity. Its miners could sell mithril and ilium at the proposed Siluri market.

Redoubt.t: Stable Redoubt was chosen by Urizeni architects as the site of a possible national Bourse market for mithril and/or ilium.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos was one of four League cities that could host the proposed all-resource market.

Semmerholm.t: Yeofolk of Lacre proposed a quarterly Star Metal Market buying ilium netted from the Semmerlak, overseen by a Starmetal Seneschal.

Skarsind.t: Gulhule is booming again, while struggling Krysse proposed a Miner's Market where an orc bonesetter could buy mithril, rather than see Skarsind's mithril drift east to Varushka.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the constant back-and-forth over Spiral is cited as damaging Urizen's prosperity.

Tassato.t: Tassato was one of four League cities that could host the proposed all-resource market. It is also home to Bishop Imago Monta di Tassato Regario, who suggested an Ombudsman of the Bourse.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar was a candidate host for the League market, and its merchants might also trade at the proposed Krysse and Valashal halls.

The Semmerlak.t: Small amounts of ilium drawn from the lake in fishing nets would supply the proposed Star Metal Market at Lacre.

Weirwater.t: A weirwood market-faire was proposed at Applefell, with support pledged by a Seneschal of Spiral Castle, but the Dawnish assembly could not secure a greater majority for it.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the loss of Zenith is cited as a blow to Urizen's prosperity.

Green and pleasant lands.d: The envoys claimed to represent the two great clans of the independent orcs east of the Empire, which reportedly threw off Druj rule over Winter 377YE. They were led by a shaman of the Great Forest clan and a warrior of the Black Wind clan, with evident tensions between them, and accompanied by a human of strong briar lineage. They were encouraged chiefly by the Senate's Spring decision to recognise them as foreigners rather than barbarians, so they came under the protection of the law, not delegation protection. A herald of Lashonar led them into Greenstead; members of the Splitroot Striding escorted them by the trods to Anvil. There they negotiated a treaty that was discussed in the Senate, then returned safely to the Barrens.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of the Barrens are reported to have thrown off the oppressive chains of the Druj over Winter 377YE.

Navarr.t: Navarr guardians met the orc delegation in Brocéliande, and after much discussion members of the Splitroot Striding agreed to escort the envoys along the trods to Anvil, leaving the Navarr likely to be the first to hear of their approach.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the orcs carried an invitation from the Wintermark senator Jorma Steelhail, one of the factors behind their journey.

Green and pleasant lands.o: In Summer 379YE a delegation of independent orcs from the Barrens emerged under a flag of truce in Boar's Dell in Brocéliande, seeking passage to Anvil to negotiate with the Imperial Senate. It was believed to be the first peaceful contact between the Empire and the orcs of the Barrens.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Boar's Dell was where the band of orcs from the Barrens first appeared without warning, flying a flag of truce.

Brocéliande.t: The orc envoys emerged unannounced into Brocéliande under a flag of truce and were led into Greenstead by a herald of Lashonar before being handed over to Navarr guides.

The Barrens.t: The independent orc clans of the Barrens, said to have freed themselves from the Druj, sent their first peaceful envoys to the Empire, and the delegation returned there safely after negotiating a treaty at Anvil.

Grind.d: Five Jotun armies led by King Gudmunder Arasonn's Fist of Ulven attacked from Liaven's Glen, accompanied by Summer knights and seemingly every major Jotun champion's warband, among them Stephen of Sarcombe's Mournwold traitors and the mountain-banner of Geht Ahan. The Red Wind Corsairs, Black Thorns and Quiet Step chose to strike and withdraw, giving ground. Fort Braydon's exhausted garrison could not hold; Gudmunder reportedly shattered its weirwood gate, and defenders who did not surrender were killed. The Jotun took Nestor's Bounty, offered captives servitude or death, and dug in short of full control of Jade Range. A Sentinel Gate conjunction to Kahraman, apparently linked to the Jotun champions, was identified for the Spring Equinox.

Jotun.t: Five armies of Narkyst under King Gudmunder Arasonn, with the Hierro and a host of champions, captured Fort Braydon and Braydon's Jasse and now hold eight-tenths of Jade Range, digging in with armed camps rather than chasing Navarr ambushes.

Navarr.t: The Black Thorns and Quiet Step harried and ambushed the Jotun while giving ground, but the orcs showed them no mercy, dumping Navarr dead in unmarked mass graves or burning them on pyres.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn lost Fort Braydon, with much of its garrison trapped and killed or forced to surrender, while the Red Wind Corsairs rescued what residents they could as the Jade Range families fled, fought, or faced servitude.

The Marches.t: Stephen of Sarcombe and the treacherous scions of the Mournwold fought at the forefront for the Jotun in Braydon's Jasse, though his earlier destruction ironically kept the Jotun from easily assaulting Serra Briante.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ice Fishers of Ldansk were last seen conquering Sermersuaq, and Jotun champions came south swollen by victories in the north, offering the same Choice given there.

Grind.o: In the winter before Spring 385YE, forty thousand Jotun of Narkyst, backed by Summer knights and their greatest champions, struck south from Liathaven into Kahraman. They stormed Fort Braydon, took all of Braydon's Jasse and seized eight-tenths of Jade Range, including Nestor's Bounty.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: The whole Jasse fell to the Jotun after Fort Braydon was stormed and its weirwood gate shattered, leaving the fortress in orc hands and garrisoned by the Fist of Ulven.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: War returned only six months after the last fighting, Nestor's Bounty fell, and eight-tenths of the region came under Jotun control as its proud families fled or fought rather than take the Choice.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: Jotun-allied mountain folk raided its mines, and while Stephen's destruction blocked an assault this season, the Jotun are now free to strike at its mithril.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: Geht Ahan's mountain warband harried caravans out of Damata, though the Jotun cannot attack it in the same season as Serra Briante with the same force.

Liathaven/Liaven's Glen.t: The five Jotun armies struck south out of Liaven's Glen to begin the assault on Braydon's Jasse.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman's northern lands were overrun as Fort Braydon fell, Braydon's Jasse was conquered and most of Jade Range taken, with Serra Briante and Serra Damata now exposed to further attack.

Liathaven.t: The Jotun-held forest served as the springboard for the invasion, with forty thousand orcs marching south out of it into Kahraman.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Stephen of Sarcombe's Mournwold traitors fought for the Jotun and kept close to the borders of the Mourn.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ice Fishers were last seen in its conquest, and the Choice offered on Jade Range is the same harsh one given there.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Skjaldirborn's general invoked the memory of Skallahn as he rallied his warriors.

Grown from the revolution seed.d: Rachensgrab lies in the Tears of the Moon archipelago, more than three weeks' sail north of Volkavaar across the Sea of Steel. Magistrate Abraham found that Empress Deanne's 316YE declaration of war on the slavers had never been revoked, so the attack would be lawful. Sumaah could spare no ships, and the Commonwealth offered only a few ships and a haven for freed slaves. The General Assembly could appoint an admiral to lead the raid. The outcome depended on the strength committed, ranging from scattering ships to razing the city and looting the treasury. No one would pay for the raid unless the guerdon was applied, and the opportunity would pass if it was not taken that season.

Druj.t: The Druj were named as possible trading partners of the Slave Lords. If the Sacrificial Tower were destroyed, the slavers' ships would not dare sail as far as the Bay of Catazar for a generation, cutting the Druj off from new slaves.

Grendel.t: The Slave Lords were said to visit Dubhtraig frequently. A successful assault on the Sacrificial Tower would deny the Grendel access to new slaves for a generation.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marchers' and Winterfolk's earlier raid on Jotun-held Skallahn was cited as the precedent for appointing a leader for a raid.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: one of the codebreakers began on the stages of Sarvos, and the silk-clad slavers were said to dress in a way a League bravo would envy.

Grown from the revolution seed.o: Documents seized in the Liberty Pact's raid on Chalonsio revealed that the Noble Lady of the Sea is a ship, the flagship of the Slave Lords of Rachensgrab, and gave the location of their island stronghold. The Empire was offered a one-season opportunity to assault it with Imperial fleets and military units.

Bay of Catazar.t: If the Sacrificial Tower were destroyed, the Slave Lords' ships would stop sailing as far as the Bay of Catazar for a generation, ending the supply of slaves to the Grendel and Druj there.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the codebreaker Senzio was said to have started out on the cheap stages of Sarvos.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marchers' and Winterfolk's raid on Skallahn was cited as the model for appointing someone to lead the assault.

Guide the spirit.d: Relations were stable but strained. The Sumaah wanted Axos expelled from the Liberty Pact, distrusted the new Doctrine of Enlightenment, and curbed bulk liao sales. They welcomed the ban on Ocean's Caress and Imperial help against the Asavean blockade of Zemeh. They sought Senate or Throne permission to give Ambassador Accalon an apology gift, offered sympathy over Siroc, and sent delegates to discuss recognising Amika and Alberto Acciai. Wreckers serving Siakha ran the Swift Eagle aground in Longbeach and seized the präst Kauitalic, whom Accalon was charged to rescue. The Conclave disseminated Hammers of the Brilliant Shore and Stalwart Stand on Solid Ground. The assembly mandates meant every nation except Varushka and Urizen could aid Sumaah.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sumaah cited Axos's alliance with Grendel slavers to attack Tsark as proof of Axou insincerity about ending slavery.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Accalon, the Imperial Ambassador to Sumaah, was charged with rescuing the kidnapped präst Kauitalic and was the intended recipient of a Sumaah apology gift. Highborn fleets, already fighting Asaveans in the Sea of Salt, were praised by the Sumaah and needed no mandate to continue.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Sumaah trading vessels had become noticeably absent from the docks of Sarvos.

Urizen.t: Urizen was one of only two nations whose fleet captains could not join the effort to help the Sumaah against Asavean pirates and privateers after the assembly mandates passed.

Varushka.t: Varushka was one of only two nations whose fleet captains could not join the effort to help the Sumaah against Asavean pirates and privateers after the assembly mandates passed.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark Assembly passed a mandate by greater majority (309-0), sending Rafe with 50 doses of liao to urge Wintermark's sailors and fleet captains to help the Sumaah resist Asavean pirates.

Guide the spirit.o: In Summer 386YE the Civil Service reported on relations with the Sumaah Republic, covering the Liberty Pact, their war with Asavea, liao trade, ritual sharing and calls for Imperial fleets to aid them at sea. The Conclave disseminated two fortification rituals to Sumaah, and the General and Wintermark Assemblies passed mandates urging Imperial captains to help the Sumaah.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: In Longbeach, the Children of Wrecks ran the Swift Eagle aground, threw most of its crew overboard and dragged the bound präst Kauitalic ashore. A rescue mission led by the Ambassador to Sumaah was called for, with Rhianos offering boons to those who fought there.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the split in the Way was framed as reducing animosity between pilgrims who look to Bastion and those who look to Timoj.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: ongoing problems in the Bay of Catazar were noted alongside the decline in Sumaah trading ships reaching Imperial ports.

Necropolis.t: The Sumaah ship Swift Eagle was boarded and run aground on the Necropolis coast. Wreckers following High Priestess Shivaarn carried off the präst Kauitalic to sacrifice to Siakha, prompting a rescue mission through the Sentinel Gate.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the brightly coloured sails of Sumaah traders had been noticeably absent from the docks of Sarvos.

Half-time score.d: Fransesca di Matos's competition counted commissions and personal resource upgrades alike. After two seasons the scores stood at Temeschwar 120, Holberg 90, Sarvos 47 and Tassato 33. Temeschwar was offered two great works, new mining roads or the Vardstein Timber mill, and both would raise Imperial taxes. Holberg could help the Sand Fishers start their sawmills through a 50-throne loan endorsed by a League Assembly mandate. Sarvos faced a possible Grendel threat as the peace treaty neared its end, and its merchant princes offered to match white granite given to the Chain Against Chains coastal fortification. Genia Bourné extended her brokers office offer. Tassato was offered a great statue of Barell, a founder of the League.

Grendel.t: With their peace treaty due to expire and three armadas off the Imperial coast, the Grendel were seen as a serious threat to Sarvos, which they had sacked once before. They were expected to be angered by Spiral joining the League.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the League's founders sought a nation of equal power and importance to Highguard and the other nations.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun destroyed the Sapphire Stair in Tassato, and rebuilding it would need 30 wains.

The League.t: The League's cities were competing to out-build one another. Its National Assembly was asked to mandate a citizen to lend the Sand Fishers 50 thrones, and its people were offered opportunities ranging from fortifications to a statue of the founder Barell.

Half-time score.o: Halfway through the year-long contest to see which League city could spend the most Bourse resources improving itself, the civil service reported that Temeschwar led, Holberg ran second, and Sarvos and Tassato trailed far behind. It also set out new building opportunities for each city.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Misericorde was one site of the Sand Fishers' planned sawmills, the Just Rewards sinecure, and its market's merchant princes had kept the orcs supplied with the resources they had saved.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Utterlund was the other site of the Sand Fishers' planned sawmills, which a League loan could allow them to begin at once.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Cigno was the location of the Chain Against Chains, a coastal fortification needing 130 wains of white granite, which Sarvos merchants offered to support with matching contributions for two seasons.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: The proposed statue of Barell would stand in the Vassa with arms outstretched between Mestra and Regario as a symbol of their unity.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: Regario would be joined symbolically to Mestra by the proposed statue of Barell standing in the river between them.

Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale.t: Marina Pretensa proposed the Vardstein Timber mill and Sorting Yard on the edge of the Vale, with a road to the city, to supply forest materials to Temeschwar's businesses and create a new Imperial title.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: historical accounts describe Barell as proud leader of the greatest city on the Bay of Catazar.

Holberg.t: Holberg ran second with 90 wains, helped by Kleist's Winter Gardens and by citizens upgrading their personal resources. A loan to the Sand Fishers could let them start their sawmills and add 30 wains to the city's total.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos trailed with 47 wains and stayed in the race only through individual citizens. It faced a looming Grendel threat, and the Chain Against Chains fortification, the Glass Palace, the Greatest Taste and Genia Bourné's brokers office were all offered as opportunities.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral had just joined the League, which was expected to anger the Grendel.

Tassato.t: Tassato looked set to finish last with 33 wains, mostly from repairs to the Blood Red River museum, and had suffered the loss of the Sapphire Stair to the Jotun. A 75-wain statue of Barell was proposed to restore the city's Pride.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar led with 120 wains, largely thanks to the new Department of Architecture, but personal investment there had been low. Two great works were proposed, mining roads and a timber mill, which would add 5 and 10 thrones a season to Imperial taxes respectively.

The Semmerlak.t: Mentioned in passing: completed Sand Fisher sawmills would leave them well placed to help the League build a port on the Semmerlak.

Hammers and boxes.d: Invited by the Archmage of Autumn through Ashborn Trosk, the Architects of Iron and Stone assessed Pakaanan's Pass. The House of Fire and Flame offered to clear it for 250 measures of beggar's lye and mineral rights, if the Conclave passed a declaration before Summer 387YE. Baas Sterner of the Coalition of Stone and Struggle offered 100 crowns of labour on Curstag's Way if League business owners admitted their Strugglers, granite and mithril for ambergelt or orichalcum, and greater prosperity if the Senate relinquished the Brilliant Shore to the Imperial Orcs. The City of Gold and Lead reordered box handling, offered auctioned Broker's Box sigils and an oversized box, and sought to buy Bound by Common Cause.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the late Archmage Maurice de Gauvain died fighting unliving horrors invading Dawn, and one offered item, the Marching Banner, was made by the Dawnish weaver Yvelle Silver-Eyes.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Mareave, then held by Grendel, is named only briefly before being corrected to Spiral.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs were offered help clearing Pakaanan's Pass and completing Curstag's Way. If the Senate relinquished the Brilliant Shore to them, the Coalition proposed raising its output and lifting every Imperial Orc's income by 2 rings a season for at least a year.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun, aided by the heralds of Adamant, were responsible for the damage that blocked Pakaanan's Pass.

The League.t: League business owners were to vote at a public meeting on whether to let Coalition Strugglers talk to their workers in exchange for 100 crowns of labour on Curstag's Way, despite civil service warnings about rising construction costs. The Crimson Reapers' camp was to host a negotiation over Bound by Common Cause.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are said to have kept the Imperial copy of the Immaculate Architect ritual, one of the items offered for Bound by Common Cause.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Herminius of Urizen was asked to run the Broker's Box auction in return for an oversized box, and Urizeni magicians appear in the story working on Spiral's roads.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the clearing of Pakaanan's Pass is described as potentially of interest to Wintermark, and heralds examined the pass from Sermersuaq.

Hammers and boxes.o: Heralds from the Autumn realm visited the Empire in Winter 386YE: agents of the City of Fire and Stone offered paid help clearing Pakaanan's Pass and building Curstag's Way, while agents of the City of Gold and Lead changed how Ephisis' Scale boxes are handled and sought to buy the permanent Bound by Common Cause enchantment on the Wolves of War.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: The Architects of Iron and Stone found the pass extensively blocked by mountains closed around it. The House of Fire and Flame offered to clear a route wide enough for an army for 250 measures of beggar's lye and mineral rights, an offer open until Summer 387YE.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: Mareave is named once alongside Skarsind as a place the heralds came to help, before the page corrects this to Spiral.

Sermersuaq.t: Heralds of the Architects of Iron and Stone appeared in Sermersuaq as well as Skarsind while examining the damage to Pakaanan's Pass.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind was the focus of two proposals: clearing Pakaanan's Pass, and handing the Brilliant Shore white granite quarry to the Imperial Orcs. The second would raise output from 26 to 30 wains a season and the territory's taxation by 5 thrones a season.

Spiral.t: With 38 wains of white granite, 14 wains of mithril and 205 crowns of labour still needed on Curstag's Way in southern Spiral, the Coalition offered labour and materials. Workers there were described as lacking protection from the plateau's oppressive atmosphere.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Denize, one of the roadbuilders in the story, is from Temeschwar.

Handful of magic.d: Spring magic filled the waters of Redoubt, Spiral and Segura, healing any non-fatal wound almost overnight. Magical storms battered Spiral and Feroz, penalising local fleets by up to a quarter and damaging any navy that started, ended or passed through them. Five more high-lineage briar children were born around Tower March in Upwold, and the first appeared in Mieriada in Miekarova. The thirtieth-magnitude Night fog still clung to the northern Bay of Catazar. Penumbral Veils continued over Madruga, Zenith and Tassato, warping the night skies. In Redoubt the Court of the White Fountain began to crumble under a Winter curse of around magnitude one hundred, its fire plume shrinking by a quarter.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: a curse on the Barrens is noted as Spring-tinged magic and said to have been detailed in the Winds of War.

Grendel.t: Grendel-held Spiral was battered by magical storms that hampered its fleets and damaged passing navies, even as its waters gained Spring healing power; Summer observers also speculated the Catazar fog might be an attack on the Grendel.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named; Highguard-held Casinea is associated with the lingering Night fog on the northern Bay of Catazar.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: a Summer eminence's servant, Lytemna, is said to be delayed visiting the deCasillon and their Navarr guests.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn saw healing waters in Segura, damaging storms off Feroz, and a powerful Penumbral Veil over Madruga, where the Freeborn Storm fortunately remained docked at the Atalaya shipyards.

The League.t: The night skies over Tassato were warped by a Penumbral Veil, the least potent of the three, which also produced seven strange rainbows during one rainstorm.

The Marches.t: Five more briar children were born in Upwold, mostly around Tower March, making up over half the area's births that season.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Redoubt gained healing Spring waters but its great Court of the White Fountain began to crumble under a Winter curse, while a potent Penumbral Veil continued to shroud Zenith.

Varushka.t: The first eerie briar child was born in Mieriada in Miekarova, and Summer observers noted a Spring aura over the forests of central Varushka.

Handful of magic.o: In Spring 380YE a series of potent magical effects spread across the Empire: healing Spring waters, damaging storms, a surge of briar-born children, lingering Night shrouds and fog, and a powerful Winter curse eating away at the Court of the White Fountain in Redoubt.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Mieriada saw its first briar child born after the Winter Solstice, the phenomenon spreading from distant Tower March.

Redoubt/Optarion.t: The Court of the White Fountain in the foothills of Optarion began crumbling under a Winter curse, its plume of liquid fire losing perhaps a quarter of its height.

Upwold/Tower March.t: Most of the new briar children were born around Tower March, over half of the area's births in the season.

Bay of Catazar.t: The glowing thirtieth-magnitude Night fog still mired the northern bay, concealing even its own nature from Imperial magicians.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named, but is associated with the lingering Night fog on the northern Bay of Catazar.

Feroz.t: Magical storms lashed the Feroz coast, cutting the effectiveness of local fleets by up to a quarter and damaging any navy that began, ended or passed through the territory.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: a Summer eminence notes two of 'That Damn Woman's' fortresses in Kahraman, effects detailed in the Winds of War.

Madruga.t: A Penumbral Veil with a magnitude in the high forties made Madruga's night skies entirely unnatural, including a seemingly destroyed moon, and blocks divination of the territory; the Freeborn Storm stayed safely docked at Atalaya.

Miekarova.t: Shortly after the Winter Solstice the first briar child appeared in Miekarova, in Mieriada.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt's waters healed almost any wound overnight, but the Court of the White Fountain fell under a Winter curse of around magnitude one hundred, crumbling its walls and weakening its fire plume.

Segura.t: Powerful Spring magic filled Segura's waters, healing any non-fatal wound practically overnight.

Spiral.t: Spiral's waters gained healing Spring power while magical storms battered its coast, penalising local fleets and damaging navies passing through.

Tassato.t: A Penumbral Veil, the weakest of three but still impressive, altered Tassato's night skies, produced seven strange rainbows and hinders scrying of the territory.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: a curse on the Barrens is noted as Spring-flavoured magic, detailed in the Winds of War.

Upwold.t: Five more high-lineage briar children were born in Upwold, supernaturally healthy with emerald eyes and patches of bark.

Zenith.t: A Penumbral Veil of low-thirties magnitude continued to distort Zenith's night skies and block divination.

Handle with care.d: Hakima Razzia i Guerra offered a lead on the Ring of Atun sought by the Freeborn assembly, and the Highborn Heirs of Lepidus urged archivists to investigate. Khanum Hanima, a Faraden merchant, braved Jotun-dominated Reinos with mithril, coin and precious metals to buy gloaming. Navarr broker Gwyn Redpine planned to recruit young apprentices at the Academy. Hudeca Goodeye, a self-proclaimed maggot, brought modest loot from the Dubhtraig raid to sell. Ogpog, servant of the Azoth, announced a Night Market in the Hall of the Worlds, warning its goods might profoundly transfigure buyers. A cursed-seeming carved wooden map fragment from Varushka was added to the auction.

Grendel.t: Carpets, jewellery, weapons and furniture plundered from Dubhtraig during the successful Imperial raid, which freed slaves and burned Salt Lord Suriad's shipyard and palace, were being sold at Anvil.

Highguard.t: The Heirs of Lepidus hoped the ring might be Atun's original, lost after Permion's death, or another historic Highborn ring, and urged Highborn archivists to investigate; Terah of Highguard, the Gloaming Sentinel, was sought by the Faraden buyer.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Faraden merchant had to cross Jotun-dominated Reinos, and Lasambrian-Jotun forces now held the eastern end of the gloaming trade route after conquering Anduzjasse.

Navarr.t: Therunin broker Gwyn Redpine came to recruit Academy apprentices aged 14 to 17, and Navarr merchants were invited to sell their gloaming stocks to Khanum Hanima.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn assembly's call for the Ring of Atun drew a lead from hakima Razzia i Guerra, due to meet Sagua i Ezmara at the Forge, while the Freeborn Gloaming Road was shown to fall short of Faraden demand.

Urizen.t: Urizen merchants were invited to sell gloaming to the Faraden buyer, and the sought ring might be one of those Highborn artificers crafted as gifts to the Urizen.

Varushka.t: Varushkan merchants were sought as gloaming sellers, and a strange carved wooden map fragment brought out of Varushka by a terrified trader went to the public auction.

Wintermark.t: Hudeca Goodeye, a Wintermark raider more interested in loot than freeing slaves, planned to sell Dubhtraig treasures to newcomers at the Wintermark camp.

Handle with care.o: Ahead of the 382YE Winter Solstice, several traders and visitors announced their arrival at Anvil: a lead on a Ring of Atun, a Faraden buyer of iridescent gloaming, a Therunin broker seeking apprentices, a Wintermark raider selling Grendel plunder, and a Night Market offered by the eternal Azoth.

Segura/Anduzjasse.t: Anduzjasse's conquest by invading Lasambrian-Jotun forces put the eastern end of the gloaming trade route under their control.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is not named; it is linked only through the raid on Dubhtraig whose plunder came to Anvil.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren's brokers are described as wealthier than those of Therunin.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Faraden merchant's three mithril wagons crossed Jotun-dominated Reinos intact to reach the Empire.

Segura.t: Lasambrian-Jotun conquest of part of Segura left invaders controlling the eastern end of the gloaming trade route.

Therunin.t: Therunin's wealth in lumber, herbs, iridescent butterflies and more esoteric sources was described, and its broker Gwyn Redpine set out to recruit apprentices at Anvil.

Hard times.d: The rebels, the same faction that sought the Synod's aid a year earlier, camped near Feroz's southern border. From there they raided Kalino, robbing Suranni caravans, sabotaging mines and farms and freeing slaves, while buying supplies from Freeborn traders. Duke Guiscard's envoy said he would not cross the border without explicit Imperial permission. He offered future sales of white granite from Arav's Delve if the problem was resolved. The options set out were to declare the rebels barbarians, eject them with an Imperial army, invite the Duke in, ignore them, or aid them. Freeborn visitors reported an unknown consecration aura and Imperial liao in the camp. A hallowed item was sent to the Imperial Inquisitor for examination.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Zadkiel de Coeurdefer of Dawn, the Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy, was briefed by the civil service, and it was the Ambassador whom the Senate authorised to invite the Duke's forces in.

The Brass Coast.t: The rebels set up camp in Freeborn Feroz and traded with Freeborn merchants. The hakima Marcela i Erigo obtained a hallowed item from the camp and sent it to Anvil, raising concerns about the priests preaching there.

Hard times.o: In Winter 381YE some two hundred escaped slaves rebelling against Duke Guiscard of Kalino fled into Feroz and began raiding back across the border, and the Duke asked the Empire for help dealing with them. At the Winter Solstice the Senate authorised the Imperial Ambassador to invite the Duke's troops over the border to suppress the rebels.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the page gives no specific role to the Bay of Catazar.

Feroz.t: About two hundred rebels made makeshift camps near Feroz's southern border and raided Kalino from there. The Senate's decision opened the way for Suranni troops to enter Feroz to suppress them.

Kalino.t: Duke Guiscard's Kalino suffered cross-border raids on caravans, mines and farms, with dozens of Suranni killed and slaves freed. The Duke offered future white granite sales from Arav's Delve in return for help.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the in-character story describes Marcela's chicken as the plumpest to be found in Segura.

Hard times come again no more.d: After the Senate declared Ossium's orcs foreigners and the Synod sought to bring Pride to Ossium, refugees reached Skarsind, claiming abandoned Wintermark farms and clearing new land. A statement by Skywise Fal urged the Imperial Orcs to welcome them, and the spirit of Grud the Unshackled persuaded many to join the nation along the way. Three septs held back. The Ethengraw in Gildermark want their own smithy-armouries. The Illarawm in Southpine want a Synod mandate respecting their ancestor beliefs and an ossuary. The Yerende in Solvihill want a palace of flowers and plants. If two septs join, Skarsind could support a third orc army. Stormcrow Skred later enacted the Illarawm mandate.

Druj.t: The refugees fled centuries of Druj cruelty in Ossium, and each sept had secretly kept its warrior, ancestral or herbal traditions alive in defiance of its former Druj overlords.

Imperial Orcs.t: The nation gained many new members and a more prosperous Skarsind that its people now call home. It also faces three septs whose demands for edifices and a mandate could, if met, bring fighting arts, ancestor lore, apothecary skills and a possible third army.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Grud is glad Arl's teaching lacks the reincarnation beliefs he had heard from Jotun thralls.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule is not named, though orcs from Ossium, a territory it partly held, left for Skarsind.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the three-mile train of soldiers and orc refugees travelled along Varushka's roads on its way to Skarsind.

Wintermark.t: Ossean newcomers claimed farms and forests abandoned by Wintermarkers who had returned to their nation, and ever fewer Wintermarkers remain in Skarsind.

Hard times come again no more.o: In Winter 383YE a great many orcs who had lived under the Druj in Ossium completed the trek through Varushka to Skarsind, where the Imperial Orcs welcomed them and many joined the nation. Three large septs settled as foreigners in their own enclaves, each with conditions to meet before they would join.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ethengraw were forced to farm northern Bittershore under the Druj.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Mentioned in passing: the Yerende sept once lived in the Drownbark Forest.

Ossium/Echofell.t: Mentioned in passing: the Illarawm sept lived in the Echofell before the Druj rose.

Ossium/Galath Fields.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ethengraw were made to work as subsistence farmers on the Galath Fields.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: Mentioned in passing: the Yerende sept once lived in the Nearweald.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Mentioned in passing: the Illarawm once lived in parts of the Webwood.

Skarsind/Gildermark.t: The warrior Ethengraw sept settled here and would join the Imperial Orcs if an armoury-smithy costing 60 wains of mithril and 120 crowns were built and ceded to them.

Skarsind/Solvihill.t: The herbalist Yerende sept settled here and seek a palace of flowers and plants, costing 60 wains of weirwood and 120 crowns, before they will join the nation and share their realmsroot potion lore.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: The Illarawm sept settled here with their ancestors' bones and want a mandate respecting their beliefs, later enacted by Stormcrow Skred, and an ossuary costing 60 wains of white granite and 120 crowns.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ethengraw recalled that when Imperial warriors crossed from Karsk into western Ossium, the Druj sent them to face the Empire first.

Ossium.t: A great many of Ossium's orcs left between the Autumn Equinox and Winter Solstice for new lives in Skarsind, taking their tools, seeds and, in the Illarawm's case, the bones of their ancestors.

Skarsind.t: New orc villages sprang up across the territory, making it prosperous and bustling, and three foreign septs settled in enclaves in Gildermark, Southpine and Solvihill. Its people would now fight any attempt to give it up.

Hard to find.d: More than three thousand questing knights, guided by the Karass, explored the Untrod Groves. They gathered dragonbone and gloaming, but a Forge the Wooden Fastness enchantment favoured the Earl, implying an older claim to the land. They reached the Earl's Dawnish-style manse before being driven back. Some yeofolk stung by the manticore became its vassals. These vassals courted minor Dawnish houses and moved towards bandits threatening the Golden Sun's baggage train. A Witch of the Silver Woods offered the Knight-Protectors an alliance against the Earl on Silverbrow's behalf. The Last Battle wayhouse opened supply routes into Sarangrave and Therunin, sheltered survivors of the Therunin rout, and awaited a Keeper.

Dawn.t: Dawnish questing knights suffered heavy losses and some yeofolk became the Earl's vassals, while several minor Barrens houses allied with the Earl. The Knight-Protectors were invited to an audience offering alliance against it.

Druj.t: The Karass, used to Druj rule, warned that the Last Battle wayhouse would hasten the Druj's return. Its supply routes now threaten Druj-held regions in Sarangrave and Therunin.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr travelling through Karass lands said they got a friendlier reception from the Jotun.

Navarr.t: The Last Battle wayhouse gave Navarr a base in the Bleaks, a free new personal resource there this season and Therunin voting rights for those resources. Its Keeper, appointed by Navarr generals, faces Karass resentment.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the page compares the Earl to a hylje, which cannot truly be a member of Wintermark.

Hard to find.o: In winter 386YE a Dawnish questing expedition into the Untrod Groves of the Barrens was turned back by a magical thorn barrier and a manticore-like being calling itself the Earl of the Groves. Meanwhile the Navarr completed the Last Battle wayhouse in the Bleaks, angering the Karass.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: The Last Battle's supply routes reached into the Nesustak Forest, leaving it under threat.

Sarangrave/Turan Flats.t: The Turan Flats came under threat as the Last Battle established supply routes into them.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: Unarmed vassals of the Earl visited small Dawnish settlements here, and a few houses agreed to ally with the Earl.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: The Earl's vassals watched events in the Fangs from Hope's Rest and courted local minor Dawnish houses, winning some as allies.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: The Navarr completed the Last Battle wayhouse here, angering the resident Karass, and it now shelters Therunin survivors. Well-equipped bandits threatened the Golden Sun's baggage train while the Earl's vassals moved to intercept them.

The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth.t: Mentioned in passing: the Karass had asked for the Plains of Teeth to be ceded to them, and the Dawnish refused.

The Barrens/The Untrod Groves.t: A huge questing expedition was driven back by a Wooden Fastness enchantment and the manticore-like Earl of the Groves, who claims the Groves and turned stung yeofolk into vassals.

Therunin/Eastring.t: The Last Battle established supply routes into Eastring, which is now under threat.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the Earl's manse with banners and a tournament square was likened to a field in Astolat.

Sarangrave.t: The Last Battle established supply routes from the Bleaks into the Turan Flats and Nesustak Forest, putting those Druj-held regions under threat.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens saw the failed Untrod Groves expedition, the emergence of the Earl's vassals among Dawnish houses and the Golden Sun's camp, and the completion of the Navarr wayhouse amid Karass anger.

Therunin.t: Survivors of the bloody rout in Therunin sheltered at the Last Battle, whose supply routes now threaten Eastring. Navarr resources in the Barrens count as being in Therunin for elections.

Harvest of infamy.d: Three Asavean battleships, Leaping Bull, Wind Tamer and Venger's Blade, sailed through the Kongegőr and the Gullet into the newly dredged Westmere with about a dozen Asavean privateers and a dozen Grendel ships, aiming to burn Meade as Madruga had been ruined. After Imperial heroes slew Iacq Indurain in Madruga and seized his orders, the Drakes marched north. Nearly four thousand warband fighters and half the Forte Fidelis garrison joined them. The raiders were routed. Leaping Bull was trapped by merrow and scuttled, Venger's Blade fled badly damaged and Wind Tamer withdrew. Nearly a hundred Marcher soldiers died. Meanwhile High Voice Chiara led Asaveans and Grendel mercenaries towards the Phytwin Clearing in Kallavesa.

Grendel.t: Grendel ships sailed with the Asavean flotilla to plunder Meade and were beaten alongside their allies, while a Grendel mercenary company accompanied High Voice Chiara's attempt to desecrate the Phytwin Clearing.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Meade's walls were built against Jotun raiders, and Forte Fidelis kept watch on the border with Jotun-invaded Mournwold.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Leaping Bull and Wind Tamer were known for their attacks along the Brass Coast, and the raiders meant to do to Meade what had been done to Madruga and Siroc.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes marched through Tassato on their way north to Meade.

The Marches.t: The Drakes, warbands, the Forte Fidelis garrison and the people of Meade saved the Pride of the Marches from destruction, though nearly a hundred Marcher soldiers fell and the docks were damaged.

Wintermark.t: An Asavean priest and Grendel mercenaries threatened the Phytwin Clearing, a pilgrimage site tied to Gilda Ashwine, and the Speaker of the Crows, Ingrid, was charged with stopping them.

Harvest of infamy.o: In Autumn 386YE an Asavean and Grendel raiding fleet sailed down the Westmere to sack the Marcher market-town of Meade, but the Drakes, forewarned by orders seized in Madruga, were waiting and drove the raiders off. A separate Asavean-led band also threatened to desecrate the Phytwin Clearing on Kallavesa's Pilgrim's Trail.

Mitwold/Meade March.t: Some townsfolk fled Meade into Meade March along the river-road to Wayford, while the Drakes and local defenders broke the raid on the town's harbour. The Marchers are already repairing the damaged docks.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the slain Iacq Indurain is described as a liaison to Rahab, the late former Governor of Feroz.

Kallavesa.t: High Voice Chiara's force threatened to desecrate the Phytwin Clearing on the Pilgrim's Trail; if it was not stopped, the Trail would yield half the usual liao to Kallavesa's congregations for two seasons.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Iacq Indurain was slain and his orders seized in Madruga, and the Drakes marched north from there. The raiders hoped to repeat their earlier ruin of the territory.

Mitwold.t: The Asavean raid on Meade was defeated on its docks. Leaping Bull was sunk and Venger's Blade driven off, but nearly a hundred defenders were killed.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Forte Fidelis garrison could spare only half its strength because of the threat from Jotun-invaded Mournwold.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Asavean ships were ordered to rendezvous at Caitun on the Sea of Snows before passing the Kongegőr, and some vessels trading with Caitun were destroyed as the fleet passed.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named, though the flotilla's route ran through the Gullet towards the Westmere.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes marched through Tassato racing to reach Meade.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes marched through Upwold racing to reach Meade.

Has reared himself a throne.d: Estavus proposed an Office of Fire and Stone at the Crucible of Fate in Iteri, Zenith, and invited Archmage Edmundo to a meeting to settle its purpose. Llofir declined parley, offering whisperspore so a Hallow of the Green World could bypass enmity as a test of trust. Both acts would be crimes. Lashonar offered the Conclave one Caucus Forum meeting, with the Asavean Plenum, the Mallum's inhabitants or a Prince of Jarm. Jaheris could arrange a meeting with the Lady of the Semmerlak, but would not approach Dho'uala until her allegiance was settled. Zakalwe asked whether the Military Council truly sought liberation in the Mallum. A Winter eternal set a midnight parley in the Hall of Worlds.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe cited the Barrens, now part of Dawn with small enclaves for surviving septs, as a warning of supposed liberation becoming conquest.
