Druj.t: Zakalwe offered, if the Military Council committed to liberation, an enchantment helping Imperial armies arm the non-Druj peoples of the Mallum and hand them any land taken from the Druj. He also judged that the vast fortress of Cassad Ûln shows how much the Druj fear defeat.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Llofir's herald recalled the eternal tending the ruined and broken in Reikos, a Highborn-held territory.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Office of Fire and Stone resembles a fane, a commission the Empire copied from Jotun techniques for dealing with eternals.

Urizen.t: Estavus proposed an Urizen-sited office whose overseer, the Architect of Hammers, could be either an Urizen title chosen by Tally of the Votes or an Imperial one. The offer answered a message from Vossk of Zenith Ascendant on the Archmage of Autumn's behalf.

Has reared himself a throne.o: Six eternals answered the Imperial archmages' plenipotentiary messages ahead of the 387YE Autumn Equinox. Estavus proposed an office in Zenith and an unknown Winter eternal agreed to parley, while Llofir, Lashonar, Jaheris and Zakalwe declined parley but set out conditions, offers or questions.

Zenith/Iteri.t: The proposed Office of Fire and Stone would stand at the Crucible of Fate in Iteri, where the Lady of Hammers already has a significant presence. It would cost white granite, mithril and ilium and take three months to build.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Zakalwe said the immense Druj fortress of Cassad Ûln in the north of the forest was built to protect their borders and reveals their fear of defeat.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Llofir's tending of the ruined and broken in Reikos was cited as the model for what it would do if invited in through the Hallow of the Green World.

Sarangrave.t: Lashonar's heralds were nonplussed at the Archmage of Night's suggestion of a grand plan in Sarangrave, saying they had only encouraged communication and delivered a message Imperial magicians had requested over Decius Frostspire's rescue.

The Semmerlak.t: Jaheris could not arrange talks with Dho'uala in the Semmerlak's depths, but offered a meeting with the Lady of the Semmerlak, a Summer witch-knight who loathes the creature. Settling her disputed allegiance is his price for any later parley with Dho'uala.

Zenith.t: The City of Fire and Stone proposed building a permanent Office of Fire and Stone in Zenith, letting heralds of Estavus enter regardless of the eternal's standing with the Conclave, overseen by a new Architect of Hammers.

Have you seen me lately.d: Sung agreed to a Friday-night parley with the Archmage of Night, asking for the Shaman of Wintermark and up to four others to discuss three mysteries, with no petitions. Ylenrith, still an enemy of the Empire, sought to regain trust and warned of a 'Cold Sun'. Rhianos would discuss Atun's Ring, the sword Fortinbras and the Eastern Sky, but refused looting requests. Ephisis auctioned slots for City of Gold and Lead heralds and waived parley protections. Kaela offered tribute to her Grim Legion and a route for the Suns of Couros to end her enmity. Ossegrahn blessed farmers and fishers and proposed a Conclave envoy to the Tchemetzi of Caitun.

Dawn.t: Rhianos was considering what Dawn might do to win their favour over the Eastern Sky and offered possible help tracking down Fortinbras, a Summer gift once earned by a hero of Dawn; Dawnish enchanters were invited to the parley.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on the page; its only possible link is Rhianos's refusal to help find the regalia of the first Empress, which the eternal said does not exist.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the civil servant Jorgen recalls having faced Jotun charges in his youth.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Jorgen recalls facing a Thule warlock, and Rhianos dismissed a request about the 'staves of power' of the Thule elite as not really a thing.

Wintermark.t: Sung specifically asked the Archmage of Night to bring the Shaman of Wintermark to the Friday-night parley on the mysteries of the Labyrinth, Freedom and the Shears.

Have you seen me lately.o: In Spring 385YE six eternals answered the archmages' plenipotentiary messages: Sung, Ylenrith, Rhianos and Kaela agreed to formal parleys, Ephisis asked for a meeting that would not be a parley, and Ossegrahn declined but offered help in other ways. The second Arcane Colloquium was also scheduled for Saturday afternoon of the Spring Equinox.

Brocéliande.t: Rhianos had liked the idea of a statue watching over knights adventuring in Brocéliande, but their enthusiasm waned after the grand adventure there.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page, and no event there is described.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: Rhianos's heralds hoped to hear what the three champions who represented their master in the tourney for patronage of the Icy Crag had done since.

Hear your footsteps.d: Preceptor Malachai complained that finding lost objects is not the sodality's calling. Its agents confirmed the bell was probably an artefact, lost when Agramant-inspired sorcerers killed Friar Jillian Bevan at an old tower near King's Stoke. They linked the theft to the Circle of the Stones, a Marcher coven destroyed in Ashill in 346YE. The bell may lie in those ruins or with the raiders who destroyed the coven. They found no obvious Agramant cults in the Marches. They described three kinds of cult (pawns, fools and malefactors), warned about other Winter eternals, and suggested pursuing Kaarina White-Eye or Wemba the Bloody. Three mandates were proposed: two for the Wintermark assembly and one for the General Assembly.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: an investigator grumbles about trouble in Madruga that is not the Grendel's doing, and about Grendel spy rings.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the investigator Ziri is Highborn, and the Silent Bell note that the Highborn have always regarded the Winter eternals as monsters.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Bell speculate that whoever destroyed the Meeting Place in Sermersuaq was a 'fool' serving Agramant to make peace with the Jotun impossible.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: some of the Brass Coast are unhappy that their Prosperity was gifted to the eternal Tharim, a concern echoed by the Wisdom judgement.

The League.t: The investigation uncovered League history: the Circle of the Stones had cursed League cities, and its accuser Paulus Magen di Sarvos and his coven, the Childer of the Black Drop, were later declared sorcerers themselves.

The Marches.t: The bell was a Marcher relic held by the Threshers of Upwold, and the Silent Bell traced its theft to the Marcher coven Circle of the Stones, while finding no obvious signs of Agramant cults in the Marches today.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule is not named, though it holds part of Sermersuaq, where the remaining Agramant cult leaders are at large.

Urizen.t: The Wisdom judgement came from the Urizeni Ourania Neofoti, which lent it weight because many see Urizen as quick to accept eternal bargains. The proposed General Assembly mandate would have little effect on Urizen unless it passed with a greater majority.

Varushka.t: The page recalls that the Varushkan assembly had urged its people to make deals with dark powers, and notes that the proposed caution mandate would not affect Varushka without a greater majority.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark assembly could pass mandates urging its people to support one another through a harsh winter or to fight the monsters threatening the whole nation. Either mandate would reward units that hunt in the Suaq Wastes or fight these threats and penalise those that do not.

Hear your footsteps.o: At the Assembly of Nine's request, the Silent Bell sodality searched for the Silent Bell of Brian Heathford, a relic lost at King's Stoke in Upwold in 290YE. They failed to find it but tied its theft to an Agramant-tainted Marcher coven, and the page offered mandates against Agramant and against suspiciously easy boons.

Casinea/Casfall.t: Mentioned in passing: Preceptor Malachai of the Silent Bell is from Casca's Doom.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Mentioned in passing: the cult leader Maarik the Golden Tongued is out of the Silent Bell's reach in the Silver Peaks.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: Under either proposed Wintermark mandate, units that hunt in the Suaq Wastes would gain strength rather than suffer a penalty.

Upwold/Ashbrook.t: Mentioned in passing: Ashill, where the Circle of the Stones made its last stand and where the bell may still lie, is named but not placed in any region.

Upwold/The Heath.t: Mentioned in passing: the relic's legend begins with Brian of Heathford, who drove a ghost back into the Labyrinth with three days of rough music.

Upwold/Tower March.t: Mentioned in passing: neither King's Stoke, the ruined tower nor the Sign of the Tower inn where the investigators searched is placed in any region.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Bell's preceptor, Malachai, is from Casca's Doom.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the scions of Cold Sun remaining here are cited as one reason for the nationwide Wintermark mandate.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the scions of Cold Sun are still here, one of the threats cited in the nationwide Wintermark mandate.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: an investigator refers to unexplained trouble in Madruga beyond the Grendel.

Sermersuaq.t: Facing a harsh winter, with three Agramant cult leaders still at large, Sermersuaq could be rallied by a Wintermark mandate. It would ensure no settlement goes hungry, strengthen farms, and make it nearly impossible for Blood-on-the-Snow to win support here throughout 386YE.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: a Silent Bell agent posed as a League merchant from Tassato while visiting King's Stoke.

Upwold.t: The Silent Bell searched King's Stoke for the bell lost there in 290YE. Without finding it, they reconstructed the story of the haunting, the sorcerers' attack and the deaths of Friar Bevan and Creg Watcher.

Heart of gold.d: Naomi found that the thralls' pacifism meant inducting them would not give the Marches a fifth army, though clearing Alderly's forest via a Senate-commissioned sawmill could. Inducting them would bring a small rise in taxation and reduce a defensive risk. Their children who choose to become warriors might instead be encouraged to join the Imperial Orcs. However, the thralls believe orcs reincarnate, which is heresy, and Naomi advised against bonding them until this was resolved. The Whittle folk, led by Bill Tavistock, would turn violently on the orcs, and she suggested dealing with them before or after. At Summer Solstice the Marcher Assembly condemned Whittle's Hate and endorsed closer contact, while the Imperial Orcs sent Bloodcrow Udoo to welcome thrall children.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc Assembly was offered a mandate to draw warrior-minded thrall children into their nation, and they sent Bloodcrow Udoo to reassure the thralls that their children were welcome in the north, though such children would hear the Jotun ancestors.

Jotun.t: The Mournwold orcs remain loyal to the Jotun jarls and some of their children slip west to join Jotun warbands, which Naomi judged a defensive risk that bonding them to the Marches would curtail.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr were suggested as particularly helpful in guiding Mournwold orc youths towards the Imperial Orcs, given their experience of the Great Dance.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman is cited as a neighbouring land with which Mournwold Marchers have less in common than with the thralls.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is cited as a neighbouring land with which Mournwold Marchers have less in common than with the thralls.

The Marches.t: The Marcher Assembly gained an open, irreversible mandate to have Jack bond the Mournwold orcs to the nation, and at Summer Solstice it demanded the Whittle folk abandon Hate and endorsed greater contact with the thralls.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the mora of Varushka are cited in an out-of-character note as an example of a non-playable people.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: an out-of-character note cites the hylje of Wintermark and states the thralls could never join Wintermark, being so unlike it culturally.

Heart of gold.o: Following the Senate's request, an appraisal by the civil servant Naomi of Virtue's Rest set out what would happen if the Mournwold orcs, former Jotun thralls, were bonded to the Marcher nation, after the Marcher egregore Jack confirmed this was possible. The Marcher Assembly was offered an open mandate to proceed, but serious problems of faith and of Whittle's hatred stood in the way.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: With the Feni driven off, Alderly's fertile forest could be cleared over a year to let the Marches raise a fifth army, requiring a Senate-built sawmill at Alderly Edge costing 20 wains of weirwood, 5 of mithril and 50 crowns, which would create the Woodcutter of Alderly Edge title.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Orrick, Senator of Bregasland, co-wrote missives urging the Mournwold orc leaders to cooperate and attend Anvil.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a land across the border with which Mournwold folk share less than with the thralls.

Mournwold.t: The territory's thralls might become Marchers, raising taxes and easing the risk of welcoming a Jotun return, but their heretical belief in reincarnation and Whittle's violent hatred, voiced by Bill Tavistock, threaten bloodshed and possible executions; the thralls declined to attend Summer Solstice but might come at Autumn.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a land across the border with which Mournwold folk share less than with the thralls.

Hearth Tithe.d: The invasion of Lasambria ended the ceasefire with the Jotun before the Spring Equinox 380YE, when the western Empire was poorly prepared. Tassato's fortifications were only just complete, Overton was still being built, most Marcher armies were in the east, and Wintermark was weakened by curses. Community spirit rose in response, and talk turned to the Hearth Tithe. Dating from Emperor James's time, it saw farmers grow medicinal herbs for physicks, apothecaries and grimnir. A national assembly could revive it with a judgement, virtuous auras, a named priest and liao. At the Autumn Equinox, Wintermark named Ealstan of Stormspire and the Marches named James Appleseeder of Upwold. The Hearth Tithe would run in both nations for a year.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: one story claims the Hearth Tithe came from pre-Marcher Dawn, perhaps growing out of noble houses forcing yeomen to grow herbs instead of food.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, a Marcher farmer takes comfort that the Druj have fled back east, and the Abbott notes the fighting in Reikos.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Abbott in the story refers to the war with the Grendel in the south.

Jotun.t: The early end of the ceasefire after the invasion of Lasambria left the western Empire facing imminent Jotun invasion. That threat prompted the revival of the Hearth Tithe.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the fortifications at Tassato are noted as only just complete, and a Marcher recruit has gone to fight in Holberg.

The Marches.t: The Marcher assembly revived the Hearth Tithe and named James Appleseeder of Upwold to lead it. For a year, Marcher farms would give up some produce to grow cerulean mazzarine, marrowort and true vervain for the war effort.

Wintermark.t: Weakened by curses but rallying, Wintermark revived the Hearth Tithe through its assembly, with Ealstan of Stormspire named to encourage it. Its farms would grow healing herbs for a year, traditionally given to the grimnir who march with Winterfolk armies.

Hearth Tithe.o: In Autumn 379YE, with the Jotun ceasefire ended early, the Marcher and Wintermark national assemblies both revived the Hearth Tithe. This old custom sees farmers give over part of their fields to growing healing herbs for their communities and soldiers.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: one story holds that Marcher grain merchants first saw the Hearth Tithe in Hahnmark during old border hostilities between Wintermark and the Marches.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, a Marcher farmer's granddaughter has gone to Holberg to fight with Old Tom's brigade under Dick Talbot.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold is not named on the page, though the expected Jotun invasion of the western Empire forms the backdrop.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Abbott notes that the Bounders and Strong Reeds are in Reikos helping the Highborn reclaim their homes, and that sickness has taken many there.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the fortifications at Tassato are described as only just complete when the ceasefire ended.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: James Appleseeder of Upwold was the priest the Marcher assembly named to coordinate the Hearth Tithe.

Here comes the night.d: The army was raised by a Winter Solstice 386YE motion proposed for Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad and seconded by Myshki Marishka Letuchaya. Cabal Lyktan's Hammers of Fury enchantments sped its mustering. Most Varushkans did not want the lost Iron Helms recreated. The options were the conquering quality inspired by Ratibor of Temeschwar, the foraging quality of the wagon raiders, and the sell sword quality, which required a Hound's Hall. Sovereign offers included the Dubik (bloodthirsty, needing a shrine in Suvretz), the Charnel Lord (Branoc born), the Howling Queen (accursed), and a rumoured bargain with the Night Below. Aleksandr chose the name Boyar's Hasta and backed the wagon raiders and sell swords. The Hound's Hall was built and the Sell Sword quality took effect.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Morrigan Mortere of Dawn was asked to host, at the Mortere camp, a meeting between Varushkans and a servant of the Charnel Lord.

Druj.t: The new Varushkan army was raised to take the fight to the Druj, and those inspired by Ratibor hoped it would end their threat for good by claiming their lands.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: a young Varushkan recruit hoped that Reinos, then held by the Jotun, would be assigned to Varushka once claimed.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the schlacta recalled Varushka's oath to stand with the Navarr against the vallorn, and the Iron Helms' final orders spoke of finishing the work in Therunin.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League was cited as the only nation with a stronger mercenary tradition than Varushka.

Varushka.t: Varushka gained its third army, Boyar's Hasta, which drew on the nation's wagon raiders and sell swords through a newly built Hound's Hall. The bargains offered by the Dubik, the Charnel Lord, the Howling Queen and the Night Below were all passed over.

Here comes the night.o: Six months after the Senate voted to raise a third Varushkan army in Karov, the nearly mustered force needed a name and a defining quality, with several sovereigns offering their patronage. The former Senator for Karsk, Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad, named it Boyar's Hasta and gave it the Sell Sword quality.

Karsk/Branoc.t: Mentioned in passing: the Charnel Lord's patronage would have made the army Branoc born, but this was not chosen.

Volodmartz/Suvretz.t: A Shrine of the Dubik was proposed at an abandoned outpost in eastern Suvretz, all that remained of the old vale of Krastavya. The opportunity was lost when the army took the Sell Sword quality.

Karov.t: The new army was raised in Karov, where Cabal Lyktan's Hammers of Fury hastened its mustering. Delev was one of the proposed sites for the Hound's Hall.

Karsk.t: The army's raising senator, Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad, was the former Senator for Karsk and chose its name and quality. Ivarsgard was one of the proposed sites for the Hound's Hall.

Ossium.t: The success of Ossium's Stinking Market was cited as evidence of Varushkan appetite for raiding, and Karantzy was one of the proposed sites for the Hound's Hall.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: a recruit hoped Reinos would be assigned to Varushka when it was claimed.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Ratibor, boyar of Temeschwar, inspired the proposed conquering quality, which was not chosen.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Helms' final orders spoke of finishing the work in Therunin by eradicating the Druj there.

Volodmartz.t: The Dubik was said to slumber beneath Volodmartz's soil, and its offer of patronage would have required a shrine there. The offer lapsed when the army took a different quality.

Here to stay.d: Imperial Orcs, Golden Pyramid magicians and an Autumn enchantment aided Eilian, but the enchantment also helped resisters band together, raising the spectre of rebellion. He identified three groups: resentful former Grendel elites in Clisearn, cynical Eoradal orcs awaiting the Salt Lords' return, and the Brine Turtles sept of Fleisardh. He proposed a Clisearn Grand Market great work with an Imperial Orc Steward of Works, and an adamant-infused fortified settlement at the Skouran ruins in Eoradal backed by the Tamazi. With the Illarawm mystagogue Bonesung Reller, he proposed protecting turtles to open talks with the Brine Turtles. He warned that using force would sour relations with all Broken Shore orcs. The Imperial Orcs sent Skywise Tylva to urge the Illarawm to negotiate.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Eilian studied past events in the Dawnish Barrens, and the Adamant Gate of Semmerholm served as the model for the proposed fortress.

Grendel.t: Former Grendel elites in Clisearn and orcs loyal to the Salt Lords in Eoradal resist the Empire in expectation of a Grendel return. Eilian warned that crushing them by force would strengthen Grendel resolve and help them raise and resupply armies.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs were offered a Steward of Works position and a Tamazi-built fortified settlement in Mareave to cement their hold on the territory. Their assembly sent Skywise Tylva to urge the Illarawm to open peaceful negotiations with the Brine Turtles.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the prognosticator Eilian Sweetwater, who carried out the appraisal, is Navarr.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League assembly urged its nation to offer expertise to help the Imperial Orcs in Mareave, as recounted elsewhere.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Eilian consulted the document Mareave and Urizen during his historical research.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Eilian considered past events in the Varushkan territory of Ossium as precedent.

Here to stay.o: In Autumn 386YE the Navarr prognosticator Eilian Sweetwater appraised how to win over the uncooperative orcs of southern Mareave. The Senate then recognised all orcs in Mareave not actively fighting the Empire as foreigners and banned turtle hunting in the Bay of Catazar.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: Eilian consulted scholars in the independent city, whose people already hold foreigner status, a privilege the Clisearn orcs resent.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: Resentful former Grendel families led by Devan Adahr, Savurn Marr and Regan Tholdie resist the Empire. A proposed Clisearn Grand Market at Ohwinn Dell, with an Imperial Orc Steward of Works, could remove the region's uncooperative quality now that its orcs are foreigners.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: The Uthni and other cynical orcs expect the Grendel to return. Eilian and Ketus Stonewalk proposed an adamant-infused fortified settlement at the Skouran ruins to prove the Imperial Orcs are here to stay.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: The proud, frightened Brine Turtles sept, centred on Fioroult, resists the Empire while its warriors fight under Grendel banners. The turtle-hunting ban and Illarawm diplomacy are meant to open negotiations with its elders.

Mareave/Sinfoyard.t: Mentioned in passing: the people of Sinfoyard had already been granted foreigner status under the treaty with former Salt Lord Ehsan.

Ayereed.t: Mentioned in passing: the Brine Turtles' warriors are fighting the Empire in Ayereed, and recent developments there highlighted the difficulty of moving water through Mareave.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Senate made it illegal for Imperial citizens to hunt turtles in the Bay, a gesture of respect for the Brine Turtles' sacred sea-turtles, at an estimated cost of no more than 4 thrones in taxes.

Mareave.t: Three southern regions remain uncooperative, which prevents the territory supporting an Imperial army. The Senate's recognition of the orcs there as foreigners opened the way to proposed great works and negotiations.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Eilian examined how matters went in Ossium when considering how to make peace with conquered peoples.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the adamant-infused Adamant Gate in Semmerholm was cited as the model for the proposed Eoradal fortress.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Eilian recovered from the effects of Spiral, and the Eoradal orcs compare the Empire's hold on Mareave to the Grendel's temporary conquests of Spiral.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: Eilian looked at events in the Barrens for lessons in reconciling with conquered people.

Here you come again.d: Sinokenon could not help find black lotus, which the Druj conceal, but offered aid with one of three projects if the Conclave accepted. Eleonaris asked the Freeborn to host a soiree for her heralds before a parley with Archmage Mirella. The Lictors judged that the anti-sacrifice proscription was not a jurisdictional overstep, offered three bounty bonds to Beaters, Thief-Takers and Wardens, and arranged trade through the City of Gold and Lead. A wounded Lashonar agreed to an informal parley. Surut agreed to parley but vowed to keep supporting the Druj. Llofir questioned the trod-network interdiction and offered a magnitude 100 Hallow of the Green World on the Mallum to hasten the Druj collapse.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris praises her friends in Dawn and the balls of Astolat and Semmerholm, and Llofir asks what the trod interdiction means for Dawnish magicians.

Druj.t: Surut vowed never to withdraw support from the Druj, while Llofir offered a Hallow of the Green World over the Mallum to bring sickness and ruin and speed their collapse. Sinokenon noted that their wards make black lotus almost impossible to locate.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Mareave, which the Grendel held, was named as a place Sinokenon would send ministers to help the Imperial Orcs if the Conclave chose that option.

Imperial Orcs.t: Sinokenon told the orc Archmage of Day, Skywise Gralka, that it could not find black lotus, but it offered to send ministers to help the Unshackled build their nation. Unshackled Thief-Takers were among the few permitted to bid for the Lictors' bonds, and the orc Bloodcrow Arora won a parley with Surut.

Jotun.t: Llofir warned that the coral husks are evolving new strains and that the Jotun, like the Winterfolk and Marchers, must adapt their tactics or be subsumed.

Navarr.t: The Navarr Archmage of Spring, Arwydd Clearbramble, was invited to parley with Llofir over the interdiction on completing the trod network. Lashonar said it had recently sung with the Navarr and sent servants to aid them in Therunin.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Archmage of Day could approach the Dragons of Otkodov, then held by Thule, about black lotus, though Sinokenon doubted it would help.

Varushka.t: Varushkan Wardens were among the only citizens allowed to bid green iron for the Lictors' three bounty bonds, and Llofir questioned what the trod interdiction meant for Varushkan magicians.

Wintermark.t: Llofir confirmed that the coral husks haunting the Gullet between the Marches and Wintermark come from Spring, and warned that the Winterfolk must adapt as the husks grow more complex.

Here you come again.o: Six eternals answered the Imperial archmages' plenipotentiary messages from the Summer Solstice, and five of them agreed to parleys or meetings at the Autumn Equinox. Sinokenon declined to meet but offered help with one of three projects.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris's courtiers are said to love the grand balls held in the castles of Astolat.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Lashonar recalled aiding the Navarr in Brocéliande shortly before the Conclave declared enmity against it.

Forest of Ulnak.t: If the Empire cast Llofir's proposed Hallow of the Green World on the Mallum, its effects would also be felt in the Forest of Ulnak.

Mareave.t: Under one of Sinokenon's proposals, the eternal would send ministers to Mareave to help the Imperial Orcs build their nation, if the Conclave accepted.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dragons of Otkodov were suggested as a possible source of help with black lotus, though Sinokenon was not confident of success.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: The Citadel Guard stationed in the Salt Flats could serve as the focus for Llofir's proposed Hallow of the Green World, and the ruinous effects would be concentrated there.

Sarangrave.t: Eleonaris demanded an explanation for the delayed frieze celebrating the joint victory in the Sarangrave as the first item of her parley.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris's courtiers are said to love the grand balls held in the castles of Semmerholm.

Skarsind.t: Under one of Sinokenon's proposals, the eternal would send ministers to Skarsind to help the Unshackled build their nation, if the Conclave accepted.

Therunin.t: Lashonar said it had already sent servants to Therunin so that those fighting the darkness there could speak to one another.

Heroes.d: After the Autumn Equinox 381YE, Suranni rebels set up camps in Feroz and raided Kalino. The Senate backed Ambassador Zadkiel de Coeurdefer in inviting the Duke of Kalino to intervene. The Freeborn assembly denounced the rebels as heretics, and the Assembly of the Nine urged that refugees who could be brought to the Way be offered succour. A fortnight after the Winter Solstice, five thousand Suranni soldiers destroyed the camps. Fighters were killed and hung from trees, survivors were chained and returned to slavery, and the ringleader Ahraz Reborn was torn apart by templars. A few escaped, some perhaps given sanctuary. The army remains camped in Fontargenta, and the Duke is sending a delegation to Anvil to thank the Ambassador.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn assembly denounced the rebels as heretics and blasphemers, and Freeborn citizens refused them succour, handing some over to the Suranni. Yet the tale of a drover secretly adopting two rebel children shows not everyone turned them away.

Heroes.o: After Suranni rebels claiming to be escaped slaves crossed from Kalino into Feroz and raided the Iron Confederacy, the Duke of Kalino's army entered Feroz with Imperial approval and crushed them. The slave revolution ended in executions and re-enslavement.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: The Duke of Kalino's army is camped in Fontargenta awaiting new orders, and is expected to return to Kalino once the last revolutionaries are captured.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the bay is not named, but the opening tale takes place on a clifftop coast road where a drover throws a rebel boy's amulet over the cliff into the sea.

Feroz.t: Five thousand of the Duke of Kalino's soldiers crossed into Feroz, destroyed the rebel camps, hung fighters from trees along the border and hunted down fleeing rebels across the territory.

Kalino.t: The rebellion against the Duke of Kalino was crushed, and captured rebels were marched back in chains to slavery in his mines and fields. The delighted Duke is sending a delegation to Anvil to thank the Imperial Ambassador.

Hey now how you doing?.d: Kimus found Emperor Frederick's Pauper's Key and sent a report to Ignacio i Zuhri i Erigo. Sadogua offered to keep the Lyceum's warding mists up until Winter 387YE if asked through a Declaration of Alignment, and offered to make magic items for Navarr magicians. Ephisis's herald Keel publicly sought Flavio i Flav i Riqueza to escort him to his vault. Lashonar abandoned Summoning the Loquacious Birds and priority Caucus Forum access. Sung extended her riddle about a herald's name. Irra Harah offered to enchant small tokens of personal struggle. Zakalwe ended the Pearls of Manush after one was used against the Grendel. A thousand of Tharim's knights stayed near Quzar. Skirmishes were called against the Feasters of Marrow in Holberg and the Speakers of Famine in Astolat.

Dawn.t: Dawnish citizens, especially those who had backed killing the Montanians or oppressing orcs, received Lashonar's unsettling vision. Dawn's Astolat became the last refuge of the Speakers of Famine.

Druj.t: The Pearls of Manush, given only for the war against the Druj, were withdrawn after misuse. Lashonar chose not to send the commissioned vision to orcs suffering in Druj lands.

Grendel.t: A Pearl of Manush used on armies fighting the Grendel in Mareave broke the deal with Zakalwe. The threat of Grendel raids on the Lyceum drove Sadogua's offer to extend its wards.

Navarr.t: Sadogua offered to turn materials sent by Navarr magicians and covens into magic items by the Winter Solstice, as a smaller boon ahead of their war with the vallorn.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn figures were at the centre of several offers: Ignacio i Zuhri i Erigo was to receive Kimus's report and Flavio i Flav i Riqueza was sought by Ephisis's herald. Madruga's Lyceum and the town of Quzar faced magical concerns.

The League.t: A League Assembly mandate in Holberg left only the Feasters of Marrow to confront. The Speakers of Famine hunted by Vigilance had come from Temeschwar, and Spiral was cited in the Conclave's removal of Lashonar's amity.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Ematius of Urizen, as Archmage of Winter, had declined Tharim's new offer, and Sadogua's earlier item-making for the Urizen is cited as precedent.

Varushka.t: Varushkans, notably those who had called for suppressing the Rahvin or terrorising the Black Wind, received Lashonar's vision of a rebuilt Ossium. Irra Harah's heralds were to return enchanted items at the Varushkan Hearth Fire.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Irra Harah's agents were to return enchanted items at the Tree of Names in Wintermark.

Hey now how you doing?.o: In Autumn 386YE several eternals reached out to the Empire: Kimus located the Pauper's Key, Sadogua offered to extend the Lyceum's wards and to make items for the Navarr, Lashonar withdrew favours after losing amity, Zakalwe stopped the Pearls of Manush, and Tharim's knights stayed camped in Madruga. Two skirmishes were also called against cults of Agramant.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Mentioned in passing: these islands next to the Lyceum isle, held by the Children of Wrecks, are cited as a threat behind Sadogua's offer to keep the wards up.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: A thousand of Tharim's Ashen Knights stayed camped in Lightsea near Quzar after the Fire of the South left, worrying the townsfolk, who want them moved or the threat explained.

Astolat.t: The Speakers of Famine, a dozen boon-bearing followers of Agramant, were cornered at their last refuge here. Jared of the Silent Tower was responsible for killing them before they could flee deeper into the Empire.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South left Madruga to fight the Grendel here, and the Children of Wrecks' hold on its Cazar Straits fed Sadogua's concern for the Lyceum.

Holberg.t: The Feasters of Marrow, the last cannibal cult left in Holberg, planned a profane ritual in the Wunderkind Woods. Kanute Adelaar van Holberg was responsible for killing them.

Madruga.t: Sadogua offered to keep the hidden Lyceum's wards up for another year against the Grendel and the Children of Wrecks. A thousand of Tharim's Ashen Knights remained camped near Quzar.

Mareave.t: During the Winter Solstice, two armies enchanted with a Pearl of Manush fought the Grendel here, which ended Zakalwe's supply of Pearls to Highwatch.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Lashonar's vision showed Ossium rebuilt from ruin into one of the Empire's most prosperous territories.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Mentioned in passing: recent events here are among those that angered Lashonar.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Conclave's declaration removing Lashonar's amity claimed the eternal had endangered the citizens of Spiral.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Speakers of Famine originated here before fleeing to Astolat.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: Lashonar was known to favour peace in the Barrens and was angered by recent events there.

Hidden inventory.d: Brittashal was offered as an edifice in Valasmark, Hahnmark, costing 14 white granite and 42 crowns and available until Autumn Solstice 389YE. If built, it would add the Defiant Jackdaw banner schema to Runesmith's Law and create the Warcaller, a martial title chosen by the Wintermark Assembly. The runesmiths asked the Cat's Graces to find a weaver for a new war banner, paying five thrones, and asked the Benefactor of Regalia to make it the Warcaller's regalia. They would then enchant it as a Defiant Jackdaw. The Empire could also research the lost banner Foe-Slayer. Koskinen invited Winterfolk to a conjunction to Tanikipari, which Raal Dunn will allocate.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Empress Britta is recalled as having died in Skarsind, now held by the Imperial Orcs.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, though the hylje speak of the mysterious orcs of Fjorknae and of an Imperial smugglers' cove in Tromsa, both lands held by the Jotun.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Empress Britta is remembered as having died at the hands of the Thule.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's artisans proposed a banner hall, a new Warcaller title and an artefact banner to inspire a new generation of banner-bearers in Britta's mould. The hylje also invited the Winterfolk to share stories of their heroes at the Festival of Autumn's Easing.

Hidden inventory.o: The artisans of Runegrott proposed Brittashal, a hall in Valasmark to display Wintermark's banners, along with a new Warcaller title and an artefact banner to carry Empress Britta's legacy. Separately, the hylje invited Winterfolk to their Festival of Autumn's Easing.

Hahnmark/Valasmark.t: Valasmark is the proposed site of Brittashal, an expansion of Valashal to display banners and paintings of the Empire's great banners and inspire new heroes.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: A 60-minute conjunction for 50 people to the shore of Atkonaroq in Tanikipari opens at 20:15 on the Saturday of the Autumn Equinox, with the Mediator of the Hyljehal choosing who goes.

Fjorknae.t: The hylje reaffirmed their wish to help the Empire learn about the mysterious orcs of Fjorknae and their monstrous akhlut allies, through the Sail into the Cold voyage once the Tromsa cove is complete.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark would host Brittashal, an expansion of Valashal in Valasmark to display banners and record Wintermark's martial history, if the commission is built.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: Kallavesa is not directly named on the page.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sea of Snow is not directly named on the page.

Sermersuaq.t: A conjunction to the shore of Atkonaroq in Sermersuaq was identified for the Festival of Autumn's Easing, when Koskinen is to be married and crowned as one of the Palliko.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as the place where Empress Britta met her untimely death.

Tromsa.t: The Palliko welcomed the Empire's commission of another smugglers' cove in Tromsa, which once complete will open the Sail into the Cold voyage towards Fjorknae.

Tsirku.t: The hylje cannot aid exploration of Tsirku against its baleful Northern lights without three measures of stardust, though Koskinen said two rings of ilium would suffice instead.

Hierarchs of sea and sky.d: Kimus's viziers watched events in every territory. Kimus offered weltsilver-powered Day rituals, crystal repel implements, a boon of finding, a Day-aligned orrery for the Penumbral Watcher's tower and a one-off spy network over the Salt Flats of Sanath. Phaleron offered fact-filled parchments, historical research, a one-time ritual to fortify the libraries at Canterspire or Hacynian, and vallorn tomes for Miaren. Zakalwe offered to assess defences and hone armies, but would not assess Varushka's, and sought an interdiction on savagery enchantments. Sinokenon offered a single appraisal. A reconciled Ylenwe proposed the Canticle Circle in Altis. Leviathan asked for a hall in a historical city.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Meade is named among the 'historical cities' where Leviathan would accept a hall for his heralds.

Druj.t: Kimus dislikes the Druj for their shrouds and secrecy, and offered to help the Shuttered Lantern map the Salt Flats of Sanath, their one territory without an Imperial spy network.

Highguard.t: Ylenwe offered support for the sacred city at Bastion if asked. Leviathan's heralds visited the White City Museum and resented the destruction of the Unbound Steel Hall of Lost Chapters in Reikos.

Imperial Orcs.t: Sinokenon's growing interest in the Empire was apparently sparked by the Loyalty of the Imperial Orcs, whom it helped recover the shield Oath-Heart from the Fishers.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Phaleron's historical research, delivered at the Winter Solstice, was published under the title Steinr, Vard, and Jotun.

Navarr.t: Phaleron offered the Advisor on the Vallorn copies of every major vallorn tome, cutting the research into its destruction by three months. Zakalwe criticised the Night magic that gave Navarr armies murderous fervour in Kahraman.

The Brass Coast.t: Zakalwe cited the Fire of the South's recent enchantment as the kind of savagery magic he wants interdicted. Diora University was named among the storehouses of knowledge the Empire must protect.

The League.t: Viziers of Kimus lingered in a League tavern. Leviathan's heralds visited Tassato's museums, and Tassato and Sarvos were offered as sites for a Leviathan Hall.

Urizen.t: Phaleron reaffirmed its support for Urizen lore and offered a one-time ritual to protect the Grand Library of Canterspire. Ylenwe proposed a conservatory of music and mathematics at the Spire of the Canticle.

Varushka.t: Zakalwe refused, without explanation, to assess or hone any Varushkan army.

Hierarchs of sea and sky.o: The Imperial enchantment Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths drew the Day eternals who are not enemies of the Empire to send heralds across Imperial lands in Autumn 385YE. Most offered boons or proposals, chiefly for the Autumn Equinox, while Roshanwe stayed notably aloof.

Morrow/Altis.t: Ylenwe proposed the Canticle Circle near the Spire of the Canticle, costing 30 wains of white granite, 15 wains of mithril and 135 crowns. The edifice would draw musicians, scholars and instrument-makers and house heralds of Ylenwe.

Bastion.t: Ylenwe offered help building the sacred city, whose designs include great bells. Leviathan's heralds visited the White City Museum, and Bastion was named as a possible site for a Leviathan Hall.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: Kimus noted that the Empire already has a spy network in the Forest of Ulnak.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg University was listed among the great storehouses of knowledge whose loss would void Phaleron's library-defence ritual.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe cited the Night magic that made Navarr armies murderously fervent in the recent Kahraman campaign as an example of savagery enchantments.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Diora University was listed among the great storehouses of knowledge whose loss would void Phaleron's library-defence ritual.

Miaren.t: Phaleron offered to deliver its vallorn tomes to the library in Miaren and could protect the Great Library at Hacynian. Miaren was also named as a possible site for a Leviathan Hall.

Morrow.t: Ylenwe offered to help build the Canticle Circle, an auditorium and school of music and mathematics at the Spire of the Canticle, available until the end of the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Redoubt.t: Phaleron provided an arcane projection that could transform the Grand Library at Canterspire into a fortification, though it will never offer the magic again.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: a herald of Leviathan visited the Unbound Steel Hall of Lost Chapters before its destruction, which left the eternal quite miffed.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Kimus offered heralds to support a one-off Shuttered Lantern spy network mapping the territory. Units would work two ranks more effectively if the Citadel Guard, already there, used the Technique of the Celestial Key.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Kimus noted that the Empire already has a spy network in the Sarangrave.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos was named among the historical cities where Leviathan would accept a hall for his heralds.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: a vizier of Kimus sat on a stile in Segura for a month watching sheep and gathering shepherds' songs and stories.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Meade was named among the historical cities where Leviathan would accept a hall for his heralds.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Leviathan's heralds visited the Weigher of Worth museum in Skarsind.

Tassato.t: Leviathan's heralds visited the Blood Red River Museum and the Printers' Guild Museum in Tassato, and the city was named as a possible site for a Leviathan Hall.

High hopes.d: Marcher farm owners drove cattle to market after the Winter Solstice, receiving 484 Stockland and 334 Wayford bonds. Imperial Orcs needed at least 240 bonds to found a Southern Herd in Nadir to end its aridity; 272 were provided, and Marcher and Orc forces can now escort the drovers via Bastion and Necropolis. The Dhomiro of Afar could expand the Herds of Afar, and the Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy could trade with the Baron de Hauteville. Frost Eyes received twelve bonds for sixteen drams of realmsroot, a hundred bonds were secured to lure Typhawn, and Thule merchants, the heralds of Callidus and the Hakhandra family also bought bonds. Wayford sold 49 cows at 54 rings; Stockland sold 168 at 48 rings.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page, though it held parts of Feroz and Mareave, where the Herds of Afar and the planned Southern Herd lie.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the drovers' route for the Southern Herd runs from the Marches through the Highborn territories of Bastion and Necropolis.

Imperial Orcs.t: Orcs at Anvil gathered 272 cattle bonds, enough to establish the Southern Herd in Nadir and fund the Shepherd of the Southern Herd, and Orc armies must now help escort the drovers to Mareave.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are blamed for drawing the Summer beast Typhawn into the mortal realm.

The Brass Coast.t: The Dhomiro of Afar had the chance to use a hundred cattle bonds to expand the Herds of Afar, recently re-established with coin from Feroz senator Garviel i Abrira i Erigo, and raise the sinecure's income to 410 rings a season.

The Marches.t: Marcher farmers supplied the 818 bonds traded at Anvil, sold 168 cows at Stockland and 49 at Wayford, and Marcher armies are now needed to escort the drovers south to Mareave.

Thule.t: Thule merchants offered mana crystals for cattle bonds and an economic consortium of Thule bought an unknown number, while the Suaq Wastes plagued by Hayaak's beasts since her attack on the Thule saw a plan to trap Typhawn.

Wintermark.t: The Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq acquired a hundred cattle bonds to lure Typhawn, a wily guardian of Hayaak, into a trap in Sermersuaq, continuing Winterfolk efforts to protect the Suaq.

High hopes.o: Following the Senate's creation of cattle markets in Stockland and Wayford, Marcher farmers brought 818 cattle bonds to Anvil in Spring 387YE, with buyers across and beyond the Empire competing for them. Enough were gathered to found the Southern Herd in Mareave and to lure the beast Typhawn in Sermersuaq.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: The Herds of Afar could be expanded by half again if the Dhomiro of Afar acquired a hundred cattle bonds.

Mareave/Nadir.t: At least two hundred cattle are to be driven to Nadir to form a new great herd that should let local flora and fauna adapt and end the region's aridity.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: A herd of a hundred cattle is to be used to bait Typhawn, which has been savaging the mammoth herds, into a trap in the Suaq Wastes.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Bastion lies on the route the drovers and their military escort must take from the Marches to Mareave.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is not named; the only related item is the Sand Fisher Frost Eyes trading realmsroot for twelve cattle bonds through Misericorde Market.

Feroz.t: The Herds of Afar in Feroz could grow by another hundred head if the Dhomiro of Afar gathered a hundred cattle bonds, raising the sinecure's seasonal income.

Mareave.t: With 272 cattle bonds provided, a Southern Herd can be founded in Mareave once the drovers complete their escorted journey across the Empire.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold is home to one of the two cattle markets, where Marcher farmers could sell bonds at prices that rose the fewer cattle were sold.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis lies on the route the drovers and their escort must take before the last leg to Mareave.

Sermersuaq.t: A hundred cattle bonds were secured to lure the Summer beast Typhawn into a trap, offering a chance to slay one of the worst of Hayaak's creatures haunting the territory.

Upwold.t: Upwold is home to one of the two cattle markets, whose sales and fees were to fund improvements to the markets and summer fetes.

Hoist up the thing.d: In Bregasland, three conjunctions offered relief against the Jotun at Jeer's Hay, Trent Tun and Skop's Landing. In Sermersuaq, a raid at Briar's End could strike a Jotun supply line, and three small forays into the Suaq Font could probe a mystery shown in Kallavesi runecasting. At Ocaso Pines in Segura, Jotun reinforcements bound for the Escuta could be stopped. In Hercynia and Therunin, the Empire could strike the Fellorich and Greenstride Heirs, the Twisting Hive cabal and the Greenfountain Spire. Druj warbands with Tortured Souls threatened Semmerholm and Ossium. A captured Illuminate was held in Zenith, and a phantom orc village appeared near Sun's Rest in Ulnak.

Dawn.t: A Druj scouting warband with Tortured Souls was moving through Averlune Chase in Semmerholm, probing Dawnish defences. A vanishing silent orc village appeared near the Golden Sun's encampment at Sun's Rest.

Druj.t: Druj warbands with Tortured Souls were reaving in Semmerholm and Ossium. Having repulsed the Imperial campaign into Zenith, they held captured Citadel Guard soldiers and an Illuminate at Daenorius Rise.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Grey Pilgrims supplied the intelligence behind the strikes at Tower's Edge Holt and Gildenroad. Highguard priests and exorcists were called on to dispatch the Druj Tortured Souls.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Summer Storm had suffered losses in last stands in Bregasland, and saving Trent Tun could restore up to one hundred soldiers to its strength. Orcs were also among those called to strike at Ocaso Pines.

Jotun.t: Jotun warbands besieged Jeer's Hay, Trent Tun and Skop's Landing in Bregasland, and their Sermersuaq supply line was exposed at Briar's End. Reinforcements meant to rescue the retreating Escuta in Segura faced ambush at Ocaso Pines.

Navarr.t: The Navarr were offered strikes against the Fellorich Striding, which could recover the Promise of Home and gain word of the lost Vate's Shelter. They could also rescue the Frozen Steps vates from the Greenstride steading and confront the cultists troubling Hercynia and Therunin.

The Brass Coast.t: The Red Wind Corsairs and Black Thorns were driving the Jotun out of Segura. Freeborn were called to destroy Jotun reinforcements at Ocaso Pines before they reached the Escuta.

The League.t: The League was among the nations called to confront the Druj scouts in Semmerholm, who were probing the roads towards Holberg.

The Marches.t: Marchers in Bregasland stubbornly resisted the Jotun, with the people of Jeer's Hay vowing to fight to their last breath. Rosie Little brought word of the siege there.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Greenfountain Spire was exposed as cultists of Yaw'nagrah sending dreams to briars. After the failed Zenith campaign, Citadel Guard soldiers and an Illuminate were held prisoner by the Druj.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan Cabal of the Green Mother, calling itself the Twisting Hive under Roman Andrevich, could be confronted at Gildenroad. Druj raiders threatened the pioneers of Ossium, and Varushkan scouts had reported eerie phantom villages in Oerwealt.

Wintermark.t: Kallavesi fought alongside the Summer Storm in Bregasland while thralls scouted West Marsh. In Sermersuaq, the Mark could raid Briar's End and send small forays into the Suaq Font, where the runes Naeve, Ull and Kyrop had been drawn.

Hoist up the thing.o: Before the 383YE Winter Solstice, the Imperial prognosticators published the conjunctions they had found from war scout reports. These offered chances to strike at the Jotun, the Druj, vallorn-allied Navarr and the cultists of Yaw'nagrah across the Empire.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: Trent Tun faced being overrun with a trapped Summer Storm unit, and a conjunction offered the chance to save both.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Jotun warriors besieged Jeer's Hay and blockaded the road to the quays at Skop's Landing, and conjunctions were found to both.

Forest of Ulnak/Oerwealt.t: Amid barely buried remains, a phantom orc village appeared near the Golden Sun's camp at Sun's Rest.

Hercynia/Northpines.t: Fenella Fellorich was believed to be coordinating Heir attacks from Needlestead, where a strike could kill her and recover the Promise of Home.

Hercynia/Summersend.t: The Fellorich had raided the wayhouse of a Summersend steading and stolen its heirloom. The Twisting Hive and a herald of Yaw'nagrah could be confronted at Gildenroad.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: Small groups of human thralls were exploring the wildlands outside Westerhal, and militia were alerted.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Mentioned in passing: the Greenfountain Spire's band left Peregro after the Autumn Equinox.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Druj raiders with Tortured Souls preyed on settled vales near Marshstand Rise, where a conjunction offered a chance to stop them.

Segura/Yellow Chase.t: Jotun reinforcements camping at Ocaso Pines could be ambushed at sunset, and Yellow Chase was expected to be freed soon.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: A Druj scouting force with Tortured Souls moved through the woods to Averlune Chase.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: The Jotun prepared for war near Atalaq. A raid at Briar's End, by the trod south-west of Atkonaroq, could hamper their supplies.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun provisions and reinforcements were arriving in Sealtoq from Stark.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: The Greenfountain Spire's cultists and spawn had attacked settlements here, and a conjunction near Beaten Branch Wayhouse offered a chance to destroy them.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: The Greenfountain band vanished into the miasma of Sweetglades and emerged openly allied to Yaw'nagrah with a host of vallorn creatures.

Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley.t: The Greenstride steading held the Frozen Steps vates at Tower's Edge Holt, where the Empire could rescue them and perhaps kill Clevorn Greenstride.

Zenith/Clypion.t: Close to fifteen hundred Imperial casualties fell in Clypion, and a Druj warband held a captured Illuminate at Daenorius Rise.

Bregasland.t: Three conjunctions offered the chance to relieve Jeer's Hay, save Trent Tun and its trapped Summer Storm unit, and break the Jotun blockade of Skop's Landing amid the confusing fens.

Forest of Ulnak.t: A silent orc village that vanished after dark appeared near Sun's Rest in Oerwealt. A conjunction allowed it to be explored under the Druj miasma.

Hercynia.t: Conjunctions to Needlestead and Gildenroad offered strikes against the Fellorich Striding and the Twisting Hive cabal, who had inflicted a Yaw'nagrah curse on the territory.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj scouts in Semmerholm were thought to be probing the roads to Holberg.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun control of the water at Skop's Landing could enable incursions by Hordalant folk.

Kallavesa.t: Human thralls, apparently using stolen Bregas boats, were exploring West Marsh outside Westerhal. Local militia were alerted to deal with them.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: the desolation of Liathaven was named as part of the Jotun threat along the western border.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: the beaten Imperial armies retreated from Zenith into Morrow, and the Greenfountain Spire band had set out from Peregro.

Ossium.t: Druj raiders, including Tortured Souls, emerged near Marshstand Rise to prey on newly settled vales and threaten army supply trains. A conjunction offered a chance to stop them.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj Tortured Souls were first encountered on the battlefields of Reikos, and its citizens know to fear them.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun in Segura were expected to be driven back over the hills into Reinos within a season or two.

Segura.t: With the Jotun retreating, a conjunction to Ocaso Pines offered a chance to destroy reinforcements before they could resupply the Escuta army.

Semmerholm.t: A Druj scouting warband with Tortured Souls moved through Averlune Chase, possibly a prelude to renewed attack from the Barrens.

Sermersuaq.t: The Jotun massed near Atalaq, and a raid at Briar's End could disrupt their supply trod. Three small conjunctions reached deep into the harsh Suaq Font behind Jotun lines.

Therunin.t: Conjunctions to Tower's Edge Holt and Beaten Branch Wayhouse offered chances to rescue the Frozen Steps vates from the Greenstride steading and to destroy the Greenfountain Spire's cultists.

Zenith.t: After the Imperial campaign was repulsed with close to fifteen hundred casualties, the Druj held Citadel Guard prisoners. A conjunction to Daenorius Rise offered a chance to free a captured Illuminate under the Druj miasma.

Home fires.d: Friar John's statement, upheld 102-0 at the Winter Solstice 382YE, urged farm owners to feed and rest soldiers. Marchers judged a nightly meal impractical and instead proposed billeting whole armies across a territory's farms, with able soldiers working for their board. This would cut the cost of supporting the army by ten thrones per territory, in Bregasland, Upwold or Mitwold. Competing mandates would allow only Marcher armies or any Imperial army. After the Spring Equinox, Friar John enacted the version open to all Imperial armies. Other opportunities were also raised: extending the Breadbasket to the Mournwold, helping soldiers trade military units or fleets for farms, and building a fortification in Gravenmarch after Friar William's vigilance statement.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Friar William's statement named the Jotun as a threat Marchers should watch for, and the page notes they have never shown interest in Bregasland.

The Marches.t: Marcher farms can now billet Imperial armies, with able soldiers working the land in exchange for food and board. Not every Marcher welcomes the cost or the presence of outsiders on their land. Further proposals were offered to help soldiers settle as farmers and to fortify Bregasland.

Home fires.o: After the Marcher Assembly upheld Friar John of the Mourn's call to support soldiers resting in Marcher lands, Marchers debated how to make it real. Friar John later enacted a Synod mandate allowing any Imperial army to be billeted on Marcher farms.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: Gravenmarch is the only part of marshy Bregasland suited to a standard fortification, and one could be built there to protect the territory. This was offered as an opportunity, not completed.

Bregasland.t: An army can now be billeted across Bregasland's farms, reducing its support cost by ten thrones. As the only Marcher territory without a fortification, it was also offered the chance to build one in Gravenmarch.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold is one of the Marcher territories where a general may now billet an army on the farms, cutting the cost of supporting it by ten thrones.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold's less fertile farms lack access to the Imperial Breadbasket, so armies cannot be billeted there. That would change if the Breadbasket were extended to cover it, which remained an opportunity.

Upwold.t: Upwold is one of the Marcher territories where an army can now be dispersed across the farms, with soldiers working in exchange for bed and board.

Home from the wars.d: Tens of thousands of humans and orcs died in the Greensward, souring the earth. Most survivors left, and only friars and ghosts remained in any numbers. Working from Honour's Rest, friars had begun using liao to lay ghosts to rest, but the Marcher Assembly acknowledged it needed help. Three mandates were proposed, each sending 50 doses of liao. The first would comfort the spirits, reducing the danger while the haunting slowly faded. The second would simply exorcise them, ending the haunting but leaving vicious remnants. Brother Oswin's third would aid Imperial dead and exorcise Jotun and thrall spirits, harming relations with the Mournwold thralls. Any of the mandates could be escalated to the General Assembly.

Jotun.t: The ghosts of Jotun warriors and thralls who died in the Greensward haunted the region alongside Imperial dead, and one proposed mandate would exorcise them rather than guide them across the Howling Abyss.

The Marches.t: Marcher friars at Honour's Rest struggled to lay the region's ghosts to rest, and the Marcher Assembly had to choose how priests would deal with them so that Marchers could return to farm the land.

Home from the wars.o: Following the fall of Overton and the razing of Orchard's Watch, the Greensward was beset by angry Imperial and Jotun ghosts, and the Marcher Assembly was offered three possible mandates for sending priests with liao to deal with them.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: The Greensward was haunted by countless angry dead who re-enacted their battles around the ruins on moonless nights, and depending on the mandate chosen the haunting could be eased gradually or removed outright, though dangerous remnants would remain.

Mournwold.t: The Marcher-held Mournwold faced a haunted region in the south that discouraged resettlement, and one option risked souring relations with the territory's thralls.

Honey and vinegar.d: Tassato merchants proposed expanding the mana exchanges of Tassato, Sarvos and Temeschwar (one commission, 60 wains of mithril, 120 crowns) to improve every grandmaster's ministry. Holberg's burghers offered a new exchange for the warmage or bursar, or a great exchange for both. Marcher landskeepers let farm owners diversify to produce mana while Rivers Run Red stays interdicted. Mournwold miners pledged a bequest to the Silver Chalice for a declaration against cursing citizens, and Landskeeper Shem brought a proposal to the Throne. Displaced hylje sought a floating Hyljehal with a Suaq mediator. The Senate later approved the grandmasters' expansion in Spring 384YE. The Holberg opportunity lapsed.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: their invasion of Sermersuaq has driven the hylje south, and the sealfolk hope to see the orcs driven back.

The League.t: League merchants offered to expand the exchanges of Tassato, Sarvos and Temeschwar to supply the grandmasters, a project the Senate approved in Spring 384YE. Holberg's burghers proposed their own exchange for the warmage or bursar, an opportunity that later lapsed.

The Marches.t: Grateful that Rivers Run Red stayed interdicted, the landskeepers let Marcher farm owners raise menhirs to produce mana, and sent Landskeeper Shem to Anvil with a proposal for the Imperatrix. Mournwold miners offered the Silver Chalice a bequest in return for a declaration against cursing Imperial citizens.

Wintermark.t: The hylje, crediting Wintermark for their recognition as a people, offered trade and mana through a floating Hyljehal on the Rikkivesi. It would have a Suaq merchant as Mediator, possibly as a Wintermark national title.

Honey and vinegar.o: In Spring 383YE, after the old bequests to the font ran dry, League merchants offered new ways to fund the Conclave's mana, the hylje of the Rikkivesi proposed a floating trading hall with Wintermark, and Marcher landskeepers made offers in gratitude for Rivers Run Red remaining interdicted.

Hahnmark/Bruckland.t: Mentioned in passing: hylje displaced by the Jotun have been seen in greater numbers on Bruckland's northern lakes.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: hylje fleeing the Jotun have been seen in greater numbers on the northern lakes of Bruckland.

Holberg.t: Holberg, the only League city without a mana exchange, was offered one for the warmage or bursar, or a great exchange for both. The opportunity later lapsed.

Kallavesa.t: The hylje proposed mooring a floating Hall of the Hylje on the Rikkivesi. There they would trade fish, crabs, eels and lake-bed mana crystals with the Suaq.

Mournwold.t: Half a dozen Mournwold mine owners pledged green iron, weltsilver and tempest jade each season to the Silver Chalice if the Conclave declared that curses must never be used to slay Imperial citizens. Marcher farms here could also be diversified to produce mana.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos's mana exchange was one of three proposed for expansion to supply the grandmasters, a project the Senate approved in Spring 384YE.

Sermersuaq.t: Hylje driven from Sermersuaq by the Jotun invasion intend to return home once the fighting ends. Meanwhile they offered to support the Mark through trade.

Tassato.t: Tassato's merchants devised the plan to expand the three League exchanges, including their own, to sell surplus mana to the civil service. The Senate approved it in Spring 384YE.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar's mana exchange was one of three proposed for expansion to supply the grandmasters, a project the Senate approved in Spring 384YE.

Honey off a thorn.d: Since Wintermark gave Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs, many orcs arriving there want to farm and prosper rather than fight. Groups already accepted by the egregore, such as the Liberated and former Hierro, have struggled for acceptance. The options put forward were: 'War is in our Soul', limiting membership to committed soldiers; 'Building a Nation', welcoming any loyal orc; Irontide Lok's variant, which places the legions at the nation's heart; and Anka Fleshbinder's 'Life is Precious', which would open the nation to soldiers of any species. If no mandate passed, the status quo would continue. The civil service could not predict the full consequences of any of them.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Assembly was asked to define the nation's identity: a purely martial people, open heirs building a homeland, a legion-centred nation, or even one open to humans. The choice could drive away the Liberated and some Hierro, and could change how the nation elects its senators.

Jotun.t: Jotun thralls who met Imperial Orcs saw no affinity with them, but a 'Building a Nation' mandate might lead some to settle in Skarsind. The Jotun's acceptance of humans and orcs alike, as seen in the Mournwold, was cited in support of Anka's mandate.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the Liberated, who now struggle for acceptance among the orcs, were freed in Sarvos, and the Unbroken once hired a ship from Sarvos.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the fighting against the Jotun in the Mournwold is cited as evidence that not all enemies separate orcs and humans.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's senators began giving up Skarsind in 379YE in gratitude for the return of the Crown of Three Tears, and most orc slaves held in Wintermark chose exile after the rebellion.

Honey off a thorn.o: On the sixtieth anniversary of Thrace's slave uprising, the Imperial Orc egregores asked the Imperial Orc Assembly to settle who may join the nation, now that orcs settling Skarsind include many who have never served in the legions. Several competing mandates were offered for the Assembly to consider.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's experience fighting the Jotun here is cited to show that some enemies accept humans and orcs alike.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Liberated, former Jarmish slaves, were emancipated here, and the Unbroken sailed east from here on a hired vessel and were never seen again.

Skarsind.t: Orcs settling Skarsind, many with no interest in war, are at the heart of the dispute. The Foreman of the Mines of Gulhule refuses to let orc citizens work its mines, and the chosen mandate will shape who may make a home here.

Hope and fear.d: With no prognosticator assigned, Gerard La Salle coaxed Mladen Escovitch out of retirement for one last job. Mladen found that each Druj army is supplied by its sept's lands, so completely conquering every region of a territory puts its armies out of supply, though emergency resupply with weirwood or mithril and sept relocation remain possible. He rejected costly alternatives and noted that slaughtering Druj subjects would work but was politically unpalatable. He offered to appraise such cruel strategies if the Senate asks explicitly. He would return to full service, at ten thrones a season, only if the Assembly of Nine passed a judgement with a greater majority and the Senate requested an appraisal that same season.

Druj.t: The appraisal maps which sept supplies each of thirteen Druj armies. It identifies the Salt Flats of Sanath as their political heartland, whose fall alongside one other territory would end the rule of the Buruk Tepel.

Grendel.t: Mladen suggests the Grendel might raid and loot collapsing Druj holdings in Sanath, possibly eyeing eastern islands for weirwood, though he has little experience of them and notes they do not supply armies the Druj way.

Highguard.t: Mladen cites the Stone Toad sept, whose army went out of supply after the Empire reclaimed Reikos and was converted into a garrison in High Chalcis, as evidence for his supply analysis.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are said to support more armies than any nation outside the Imperial Orcs might normally manage.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Mladen has little experience fighting the Jotun and is certain they do not supply their armies as the Druj do.

Thule.t: Mladen speculates the Thule might try to extend their dominion into the Forest of Ulnak if the Druj collapsed, though he cautions they do not supply their armies as the Druj do.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen armies are cited as a recent example of an entire nation's armies going out of supply.

Varushka.t: The appraisal was written by Mladen Escovitch, a Varushkan schlacta and former general of the Golden Axe who spent years fighting the Druj. He hopes to retire to his family in Miekarova.

Hope and fear.o: Retired Varushkan general Mladen Escovitch delivered the Senate's commissioned appraisal of the Forest of Ulnak. He concluded that Druj armies depend on their septs' home lands, and that fully conquering the Salt Flats of Sanath plus either the Sarangrave or the Forest of Ulnak would collapse the Druj.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Five Druj armies, from the Iron Asp, Sawscaled Viper and relocated Amber Scorpion septs, draw supply here, and completely conquering every region would leave them in insufficient supply.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: Mladen Escovitch intends to return to his family in Miekarova once his work is done.

Ossium.t: The surviving Amber Scorpion sept fled Ossium to the Forest of Ulnak, while the Bone Serpent were wiped out by other Druj when they tried to flee, and the septs of Ossium helped Mladen identify Druj armies.

Reikos.t: After the Empire reclaimed Reikos, the Stone Toad army lost its supplying fiefs there and was converted into a garrison in High Chalcis rather than collapse.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Five armies are supplied from the Salt Flats, and complete conquest would also sever the link between the Sarangrave and the Forest of Ulnak, with the loss of this heartland plus one other territory bringing down the Druj.

Sarangrave.t: Three Druj armies from the Banded Snake, Marshlizard and Thornwasp septs are supplied here, and the Axou would likely leap at the chance to overrun the territory if the Druj collapsed.

Hopeless as a feather.d: Sadogua will parley in the Hall of Worlds. He will restore three expired boons and reclaim the rest, wants to hear from unhappy Navarri magicians, and will hold a contest to choose the Scholar in the Well. Callidus will open a spirit market run under T'ganyan Auction Rules, with access by ticket. Irra Harah will meet Elienne of Dawn through a Sentinel Gate conjunction to Halver's Dip to discuss Sarangrave and the Barrens, and wants the Hewn Hare returned. Meraud asks for 250 crystal mana to help Suranni magicians flee and to fund a Hand of Dumon breakout from Axiom Prison. Wise Rangara warned that contacting the Silent Witness is extremely unwise. Sinokenon's myrmidons helped the Tsark against Grendel and Axou invaders.

Dawn.t: Elienne of Dawn has been invited to parley with Irra Harah at Halver's Dip, and the Dawnish Archmage of Spring, Ser Fabienne De Miel, may come along without counting against Elienne's two companions.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, but helping the people of Sarangrave, which they hold, is the main topic Irra Harah wants to discuss.

Grendel.t: Grendel invaders of the Mountains of the Moon faced Sinokenon's myrmidons, sent to help the Tsark defend their homes. Grendel collectors are also invited to bid separately at Callidus' spirit market.

Highguard.t: Exarch Luke of Highguard, Archmage of Summer, will host Meraud's parley. Ahzrukhal of Highguard holds a seat in Sadogua's contest for Scholar in the Well.

Imperial Orcs.t: Irra Harah complains that the Imperial Orcs were sent the Hewn Hare at the Winter Solstice but did not use it as intended, and wants it returned.

Navarr.t: Sadogua wishes to hear the grievances of Navarri magicians who are unhappy with him, and asks Brat Umbral Path to encourage Morwenna Winterbuilt to attend his parley.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Meraud proposes that some of the requested mana help independent Suranni covens flee across the border into Segura.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sentinel Gate conjunction for Irra Harah's parley leads to Halver's Dip, a Marcher village in Stock March.

Urizen.t: Urizeni archmages Elyssiathain (Night) and Ematius (Winter) are tied to Sadogua's parley and the Silent Witness meeting respectively, and Spyridonakes of Urizen holds a seat in the Scholar in the Well contest.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: a civil servant recalls dreading Varushka's dark forests, and Sadogua's herald suggests asking the Circle of Zulgan-Tash about the Scholar in the Well.

Wintermark.t: Bærywyn of the Sussivari holds a seat in Sadogua's Scholar in the Well contest, and the Sussivari are named as a source of advice about the role.

Hopeless as a feather.o: Following the Summer Solstice, eternals answered the plenipotentiaries sent by the Imperial archmages. Sadogua, Callidus, Meraud and Irra Harah agreed to parleys, Wise Rangara arranged a perilous non-parley audience with the Silent Witness, and Sinokenon sent its thanks without offering a parley.

Upwold/Stock March.t: Halver's Dip, a village in Stock March, is the destination of the Sentinel Gate conjunction where Elienne's party must find Irra Harah's friends to hold the parley.

Bay of Catazar.t: Meraud says he cannot grant the Summer Archmage's request to split the Bay of Catazar and make a walkway for fleeing Suranni wizards.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: the civil servant Jorgen recalls visiting Miekarova and vowing never to go near its forests.

Mountains of the Moon.t: After a warning from the Archmage of Day, Sinokenon sent myrmidons to help the Tsark defend their homes against Grendel and Axou invaders. The Tsark elders have been told the warning came from the Empire.

Sarangrave.t: Helping the people of Sarangrave is to be the main subject of Irra Harah's parley with Elienne of Dawn.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Meraud's proposal would use some of the mana to help Suranni covens escape across the border into Segura.

Upwold.t: The Civil Service identified a Sentinel Gate conjunction to Halver's Dip in Upwold, open for half an hour from 18:30 on Saturday, for Irra Harah's parley.

Volodmartz.t: Mentioned in passing: Jorgen recalls Volodmartz's forests as places he vowed never to approach.

House of earth.d: After the Jotun retreat, large numbers of unarmed, unwarlike thralls remained, mainly in Green March, Southmoor and Chalkdowns. Fed by 75 thrones a season of Imperial aid since Summer, they had returned to their farms and could now feed themselves. The page set out the options: declare peace and treat them as foreigners, convert them to the Way with 50 doses of liao, or evict them by military force. Eviction would have freed land for an extra Marcher army and let the Military Council claim the Golden Hoof, Black Hill and Eversweet Orchard as spoils, but would have angered many Mournwolders. In the end the Marcher Assembly sent Sister Meredith to preach, and the Senate recognised the thralls as foreigners, making eviction illegal.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc Assembly had resolved to send missionaries led by Bloodcrow Losak, and could pass a similar mandate to preach to the thralls. It remained unclear whether converted thralls could ever become Imperial Orcs, given orc scepticism and that they live in the Mournwold rather than Skarsind.

Jotun.t: Thralls left behind by the retreating Jotun armies now live under Imperial rule and were recognised as foreigners protected by Imperial law. Across the border, Ysra and Gudmundur were said to have fallen out over the thrall deaths, with Gudmundur reportedly swearing a blood oath of vengeance.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: any thralls driven west through Liathaven might have faced attack from the Navarr or the vallorn on the way.

The Marches.t: Mournwold Marchers had been quietly trading with the thralls, who hold the best farmland and so prevented the Marches raising an extra army from the Mourn. The Marcher Assembly sent Sister Meredith to convert them, and the Marcher egregore insisted the thralls could never become Marchers.

House of earth.o: In Winter 381YE the Empire faced the question of what to do with the many Jotun thralls who stayed in the reconquered Mournwold, farming much of its best land. The Marcher Assembly sent Sister Meredith to bring them to the Way, and the Senate recognised them as foreigners.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Mentioned in passing: the Feni-infested woods at Alderly are described as largely a no-man's land, held by neither Marchers nor thralls.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: Chalkdowns is one of the regions with especially large numbers of Jotun thralls, who now farm there under Imperial protection as recognised foreigners.
