Mournwold/Green March.t: Green March holds a particularly large thrall population working its farms, and they can no longer legally be evicted following the Senate's recognition.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Southmoor is home to many of the remaining thralls, who have returned to their farms and are now protected from eviction as foreigners.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: thralls evicted from the Mournwold, or stripped of their property, would most likely have gone back over the border to Hordalant.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: any thralls driven out of the Mournwold would have faced a dangerous trek west through Liathaven.

Mournwold.t: Thralls hold about three fifths of the territory, including the Golden Hoof, Black Hill and Eversweet Orchard. With the Senate recognising them as foreigners, they cannot legally be driven from their farms or homes, and they will pay taxes but will not support Imperial armies.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: raised as a complication if converted Mournwold thralls were ever to become Imperial Orcs while living in the Mournwold rather than Skarsind.

Houses of Silence.d: Under the Vandersaar family the Alivetti estates have become a rich enclave outside Imperial law, where the illegal Ocean's Caress is sold and eternals declared enemies of the Empire may be approached. Magistrates have arrested citizens bringing the drug home, foiled a smuggling attempt into Riposi, and heard rumours of Sarcophan interest in interdicted Druj potions. The Bladgoud Tuiniers offered discounted narcotics to the Sarvosan Chamber of Commerce in return for endorsing their handelsschool, at the cost of income from the College of the Liberated; the Chamber declined. Separately, the Community of Silence sought 40 wains of white granite at 4 thrones each, and Imperial artists, for a Silent Manse temple. The Vigilance assembly warned of heresy, and the Synod could delay the work through judgements.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the interdicted potions Warming Armour and Weakening Sun, which Sarcophan merchants are rumoured to want, originated with the Druj.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the curse storms Imperial magicians raised in the conflict with the Grendel had aggrieved the Vandersaar, prompting an apology from the Ambassador.

The League.t: The League's Sarvosan business owners were offered Sarcophan narcotics in exchange for endorsing a rival merchant school, and chose to decline. A League national assembly mandate was identified as a way to delay the heretical temple by three months.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Delves had once proposed establishing a trading enclave in Varushka, before the Senate chose the Alivetti estates instead.

Houses of Silence.o: Three years after the Senate ceded the Alivetti estates in Sarvos to the Sarcophan Delves, the thriving enclave raised concerns about lawlessness, offered Sarvosan businesses a narcotics trade deal that the Chamber of Commerce declined, and saw a Sarcophan sect begin building a heretical temple there.

Sarvos/Riposi.t: A band of smugglers tried to bring a significant quantity of Ocean's Caress into Riposi hidden in barrels of salt fish, but were stopped thanks to an anonymous tip-off.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the threat of the Children of Wrecks had raised the cost of shipping white granite for the temple to the Bay of Catazar.

Sarvos.t: The Sarcophan enclave on the old Alivetti estates in Sarvos sold drugs illegal in the Empire, leading to arrests at the border. The city's Chamber of Commerce rejected the handelsschool deal, keeping its full College of the Liberated income, while a Sarcophan temple began rising in the enclave.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: Kraken's Ink was renamed Stoneheart Syrup to avoid confusion with the real kraken's ink brought back by hunters on the Sea of Snow.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: in a play described in the fiction, the drug-supplying cicisbeo is first said to be from Temeschwar before being revealed as Sarcophan.

How sweet is the sea.d: Captains from every Imperial nation took part in mapping the Bay, with civil service coordination and Senate funds. Just over half were Freeborn, and Dawn sent a sizable contingent. Each fleet received half its usual privateering income, paid partly by patrons and partly by raids on Grendel vessels, along with a copy of the map and a gazetteer. The map is not detailed enough for magicians, but it fills gaps in Imperial geography. It was made public after the Spring Equinox. Grendel pirates, some devoted to the eternal Siakha and aided by sharks, heralds and unnatural weather, continued raiding. Trading fleets from Tassato, Sarvos, the Brass Coast, Highguard and Urizen suffered reduced production.

Dawn.t: A sizable contingent of Dawnish captains joined the mapping project, and each received a copy of the map and gazetteer.

Grendel.t: The Grendel still dominate the Bay of Catazar, and their pirates raid Imperial shipping, some in the name of Siakha. Imperial mariners have now charted the shores of five Grendel territories and raided Grendel vessels and settlements along the Broken Shore.

Highguard.t: Highborn trading fleets suffered reduced production because of Grendel piracy in the Bay, and a few Highborn captains contributed to the map.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: two Imperial Orc captains are listed among the contributors to the mapping project.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: several Navarr captains are listed among the contributors to the mapping project.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn captains made up just over half the mapping expedition, and a Freeborn civil servant helped collate the results. Freeborn trading fleets also suffered reduced production from Grendel raids.

The League.t: League captains, including several from Sarvos, helped map the Bay. Trading fleets from Tassato and Sarvos suffered reduced production because of Grendel pirates.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: two Marcher captains are listed among the contributors to the mapping project.

Urizen.t: Urizeni captains helped map the Bay, but Urizeni trading fleets suffered reduced production because of Grendel piracy.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: a single Varushkan captain is listed among the contributors to the mapping project.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: several Wintermark captains are listed among the contributors to the mapping project.

How sweet is the sea.o: Following the Senate's Winter Solstice decision, more than eighty Imperial captains mapped the shores of the Bay of Catazar, charting three Iron Confederacy and five Grendel territories. Meanwhile, Grendel pirates continued to prey on Imperial trade in the Bay.

Ayereed.t: The coast of this Grendel territory was mapped by Imperial captains, who found a rugged shore full of inlets and hiding places infested with pirates.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Bay's surrounding shores were charted for the Empire for the first time in detail. Grendel pirates continued to dominate its waters, and only its northern arc stayed relatively safe for Imperial ships.

Kalino.t: Imperial captains mapped the shores of this Iron Confederacy territory, where Suranni ports met them with suspicion, hold searches and sometimes refused them a berth.

Mareave.t: Imperial captains mapped the coast of this Grendel territory amid the dangers of Broken Shore pirates, using its inlets and coves to stay hidden.

Raineach.t: Imperial captains charted the shores of this Grendel territory, a rugged stretch of the Broken Shore where they could anchor briefly and explore on foot.

Sarvos.t: Trading fleets based in Sarvos suffered reduced production because of Grendel raids, and several Sarvosan captains helped map the Bay.

Shavronne.t: Imperial captains mapped the coast of this Iron Confederacy territory, where Suranni nobility treated visiting ships with suspicion and would meet defiance with force.

Shayeel.t: The shores of this Grendel territory were mapped by Imperial captains braving pirates who would enslave or sacrifice their crews.

Tassato.t: Trading fleets based in Tassato suffered reduced production because of Grendel piracy in the Bay.

Tathar.t: Imperial captains charted the coast of this Grendel territory on the Broken Shore, exploiting its islands and flooded caves to avoid orc pirates.

Veroigne.t: Imperial captains mapped this Iron Confederacy territory's shores. Robec was the exception to the generally unwelcoming Suranni ports.

How the sausage is made.d: Following Spring Equinox statements by Paulus Adelaar van Holberg and Prince Bishop Jonah Yakovitch, the new Custodian of the Bloody Great Sausage, Kanute Adelaar van Holberg, became a sought-after arbiter of good food, and the title now attracts 5 crowns a season while free of scandal. Vigilance led magistrates to pie-makers on Flotilla Street and the Holmauer Park Howler, cultists empowered by Agramant's boons; they were executed, but no malefactor was found and a ledger of pseudonymous buyers hints at a deeper conspiracy. Jonah also revealed that Divina Inquilina di Tassato Regario of the Childer of the Black Drop survives. The League and Vigilance assemblies may enact mandates to hunt the cannibals in Holberg or across the Empire.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highrod lemon zest, called the best in the Empire, appears among the delicacies the enchanted gourmands of Holberg sought out.

The League.t: League citizens embraced the Custodian of the Bloody Great Sausage as a guide to safe victuals, while reeling from news of Agramant cannibals in Holberg and the survival of the Black Drop magician Divina; the League National Assembly may mandate a hunt for the conspiracy's ringleaders, who will otherwise escape.

How the sausage is made.o: In Summer 386YE a subtle Night enchantment settled over Holberg, inspiring its people to seek out the finest food and drink, just as cannibal followers of the eternal Agramant were exposed grinding up victims into food in the city. The murdered merchant Anthony de Woort von Temeschwar's cooked head was served at a guild banquet, and the Synod was offered mandates to hunt the conspiracy.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: In Holmauer Park a courting couple found a gold ring in a sausage, and the sausage seller, the Holmauer Park Howler, froze would-be captors with a terrible howl before bravos tackled him; his source of meat remains unknown.

Necropolis/Highrod.t: Mentioned in passing: Highrod is named as home of the best lemons in the Empire, whose zest featured in Holberg's enchanted feasting.

Holberg.t: A Night enchantment drew Holberg's people towards exotic food just as Agramant's cannibal cultists were uncovered there, likely leading some unwitting diners to the butchers; several cultists were caught and executed but the conspiracy's centre remains hidden.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: lemons from Highrod in Necropolis are cited as an imported luxury sought by Holberg's enchanted gourmands.

How to be dead.d: Hundreds of Rod and Shield battlemages, supplied from Hahnmark, Miaren and Upwold, descended into the sinkhole. Every member fell sick, and the fallen rose again as husks, as at Isember. The expedition rescued lost miners in a vast cavern, but hidden worshippers struck and over a hundred died. Survivors revealed that cultists had fled into Goldglades and the Crimson Band were camped in Wood Heath. The Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield is to kill the followers, and the Imperial Huntsmarshall the Crimson Band. The Delver of the Depths is to use Alexi Isembrioch's skull, sent by the Fellowship of the Black Goose, to lure out and kill the Braying Lord in Vardstein Vale.

Dawn.t: Knights of Dawn fought alongside the Rod and Shield's battlemages in the push downward, and nine Dawnish heroes are named among those who explored the depths.

Navarr.t: The Braying Lord's worshippers fled south into Navarr's Goldglades, threatening to reach the Blood Red Roads of Miaren and spread the plaguewulf's taint; four Navarr heroes explored the depths.

The League.t: The plaguewulf's lair threatens Temeschwar, and the Delver of the Depths is asked to lure out and kill the Braying Lord in Vardstein Vale; two League heroes are named among the explorers.

The Marches.t: Upwold supplied the expedition as a territory bordering the sinkhole, and five Marcher heroes are named among those who explored the depths.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan Assembly unanimously urged Varushkans to aid the Rod and Shield, inspiring the Fellowship of the Black Goose to send the skull of the former Boyar of Isember to help destroy the Braying Lord.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark heroes fought in the depths, and the Crimson Band camped in Wood Heath threaten to find sanctuary in Hahnmark and spread the plaguewulf's taint into Wintermark, possibly giving rise to a horror like the Deadwood Knight.

How to be dead.o: After a Rod and Shield expedition into Lorenzo's Deep Pockets exposed the Braying Lord, an elder plaguewulf serving the Howling Queen, three Sentinel Gate opportunities arose to destroy its followers, its mercenary allies and the beast itself.

Hahnmark/Wood Heath.t: The Crimson Band mercenaries, who struck a bargain with the Braying Lord, have made camp in Wood Heath and can be attacked there through the Sentinel Gate by the Imperial Huntsmarshall.

Miaren/Goldglades.t: The Braying Lord's worshippers fled south into Goldglades, where the Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield is asked to kill them before they reach the roads.

Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale.t: Vardstein Vale is where the Braying Lord first entered the sinkhole, and where the Delver of the Depths is asked to use the skull to lure it out and destroy it.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark supplied the expedition, and the Crimson Band are now camped in its Wood Heath, threatening to vanish into its wilds unless the Imperial Huntsmarshall destroys them.

Karsk.t: The Fellowship of the Black Goose, guardians of the ruins of Isember in Karsk, provided the skull of Alexi Iskandrova Isembrioch from their ossuary to help lure out the Braying Lord.

Miaren.t: Miaren supplied the expedition, and the plaguewulf's followers are encamped in Miaren, seeking to reach its roads and spread the sickness across the Empire.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: a Varushkan warden in the opening fiction remarks that the threatened lands are far from Miekarova and the Razors.

Temeschwar.t: The Braying Lord has nested in the sinkhole threatening Temeschwar, and the Delver of the Depths is asked to lure it out and kill it in Temeschwar's Vardstein Vale.

Upwold.t: Upwold, bordering the sinkhole, supplied the Rod and Shield expedition and is named among the territories threatened by the plaguewulf.

Hunter of stars.d: Two horned, skull-masked heralds told the Civil Service that Capradan had not been given leave to answer. Their master, apparently not Siakha, Yaw'nagrah, Arhallogen, Irra Harah or Llofir, wanted no further messages. Adamant agreed to parley with the Summer Archmage on the Throne of Stone, the Walls of Holberg, the fortification Remember Exile and the mines of Skarsind. Ylenrith offered the Day Archmage a meeting in a chamber. Estavus offered ashes for ambergelt and talk of the lost art of the blacksmith. Sorin's heralds, through Ania of Necropolis, summoned a long list of named attendees. The Boar King agreed to meet the Night Archmage and Little Owl. Each parley was confined to agreed topics.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Sorin's message was carried by Ania of Necropolis, and Ylenrith's herald was dressed in the manner of a Highborn.

Imperial Orcs.t: The mines of Skarsind, a territory held by the Imperial Orcs, were among the four topics Adamant's representative agreed to discuss with the Summer Archmage.

The League.t: The Walls of Holberg were among the four topics Adamant agreed to discuss in formal parley, giving the League a stake in the Summer Archmage's meeting.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Ursa of Wintermark and at least two others suffering a curse from the same source were named among those Sorin's heralds expected at the parley.

Hunter of stars.o: Ahead of the Spring Equinox 382YE, several eternals answered the archmages' plenipotentiary messages. Adamant, Ylenrith, Estavus, Sorin and the Boar King agreed to formal parleys, while menacing heralds of an unnamed master refused the Spring Archmage's message to Capradan.

Holberg.t: The Walls of Holberg were a named topic for the formal parley with Adamant's representative, and the herald was to indicate what acts would secure the boons requested.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Draughir messenger who carried Sorin's reply was Ania of Necropolis.

Skarsind.t: The mines of Skarsind were one of four agreed topics for the parley with Adamant, whose herald would set out the acts required to secure the boons asked for.

Hunters and wolves.d: A draughir messenger reached the Castle of Thorns with a letter from Exquy, herald of Sorin the Hungry Wolf. It invited nominations, placed in a locked box in the Hall of Worlds, for a trial of hard choices and suffering. Sorin's agent Ania of Necropolis would choose a few to face the first trial at the Winter Solstice. In Birchland three chained heralds of Tharim emerged from the Copse of the Bone Birch, claiming the Conclave's sanction. Two vanished into the woods and one, Obligatus, sat motionless on a stump for two months. Meanwhile magistrates traced mutilated corpses in Skarsind and Wintermark to a deranged devotee of Agramant, the Hahnmark strangler, who was caught, tried and executed. The Varushkan and Wintermark assemblies affirmed their alliance.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is not named on the page, whose events take place in Upwold, Hahnmark, Skarsind and at Anvil.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Sorin's draughir messenger was at first assumed to carry messages from Highguard senators, and his agent is Ania of Necropolis.

Imperial Orcs.t: Lurid reports of mutilated corpses in the orcs' territory of Skarsind were traced to Agramant's fanatic, who has since been executed.

The Marches.t: Three heralds of Tharim appeared among the Marcher coven in Birchland and claimed the Conclave's sanction. One stayed seated in the regio under Landskeeper Benjamin Bickwoll's watchful eye.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan National Assembly declared the mutilations the work of a common enemy and stood with Wintermark, and the attempt to divide the two nations failed conclusively.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's people were the target of the Hahnmark strangler's killings and defilements, meant to set them against Varushka. The Wintermark Assembly unanimously reaffirmed its alliance with Varushka.

Hunters and wolves.o: In autumn 381YE three encounters with Winter eternals came to Imperial attention: Sorin's herald sought nominees for the Trials of the Pallid Charm, heralds of the Bound-King Tharim emerged from a Winter regio in Birchland, and an Agramant-worshipping killer who sought to divide Wintermark and Varushka was caught and executed.

Upwold/Birchland.t: Near Bickwoll, the heralds interrupted the ceremonial watering of the birch trees at the Copse of the Bone Birch. Obligatus sat motionless on a stump there for two months, and Landskeeper Benjamin Bickwoll may answer messages about it.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is not named on the page.

Hahnmark.t: A militia patrol in Hahnmark caught the strangler carrying severed heads beside a ditch full of bodies, ending the series of killings meant to sow distrust.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Sorin's human agent, who would interview nominees for the trials, is named as Ania of Necropolis.

Skarsind.t: Reports of mutilated corpses in Skarsind were investigated by Imperial magistrates and attributed to the Agramant devotee, now executed.

Upwold.t: Heralds of Tharim emerged from a Winter regio in Upwold. Two disappeared into the woods heading north and east, while the third, Obligatus, remained.

Hurricane party.d: Siakha offered to empower Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea and Thunderous Deluge into near-cataclysmic storms in exchange for an invocation, shed blood and a ring of ilium. She also offered to empower Merciless Wrath of the Reaver and Blood and Salt, leaving a detectable mark of storms and opening a Slaughter the Weak adventure against neighbouring orcs. A third boon would strengthen Call Down Lightning's Wrath for battle mages. She promised further boons for storms laid on chosen nations' lands, designed to stoke conflict. Only removing enmity or a Senate motion could make these boons legal. The civil service warned that removing enmity would let her heralds enter the Empire.

Dawn.t: Siakha promised the enchanters of Dawn a destructive boon if the Barrens were struck by one of her empowered storm curses.

Druj.t: The Druj were named among the barbarian orcs that those taking Siakha's raiding boons could slaughter and plunder in the Slaughter the Weak adventure.

Grendel.t: Much Imperial knowledge of Siakha came from Grendel magicians, and she promised boons like those given to her Grendel followers. The Grendel were also named among the orcs to be raided under Slaughter the Weak.

Jotun.t: Siakha offered the Marches boons to fight the Jotun, and the Jotun were among the orcs targeted by Slaughter the Weak. In the accompanying story, blessed Outsmaw fisherfolk were sent across the Gullet to raid Jotun halls.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the story's victim, Roberto Fenwater, was a merrow jeweller from Tassato.

The Marches.t: Siakha would reward Marchers with boons against the Jotun for every Urizen territory struck by her empowered storms, while every Marcher territory struck would earn Urizen a boon. The story depicted a Bregasland village secretly worshipping her.

Thule.t: For each territory where the Thule abide struck by her empowered curses, Siakha promised Thule a boon to embrace savagery, kill their enemies and destroy their castles and cities.

Urizen.t: Every Marcher territory struck by an empowered storm would earn Urizen a boon for destructive magic, while every Urizen territory struck would earn the Marches a boon against the Jotun.

Hurricane party.o: After Archmage of Spring Ibiss Briarheart reached out by plenipotentiary at the Winter Solstice, the Spring eternal Siakha, who is under Conclave enmity, offered Imperial citizens a set of destructive boons for the Spring Equinox. Accepting any of them is treason punishable by death.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: The story was set in Outsmaw, a merrow fishing village in the North Fens, where locals drugged and ritually sacrificed Roberto Fenwater to 'the Lady' to empower fisherfolk raiders against the Jotun.

Bregasland.t: In the accompanying story, merrow villagers of Bregasland, already troubled by magistrates, sacrificed a visiting kinsman to Siakha to bless raiders against the Jotun. As a Marcher territory, an empowered storm here would earn Urizen a boon.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Roberto Fenwater, the story's victim, had grown up in Tassato after his parents left Bregasland.

Hyenas and herbs.d: The Asavean bounty on ships trading with the Empire has cut Sarcophan visits, so Imperial fleets trading with the Delves earn better profits. The Delves want to know the Empire's plan against the Children of Wrecks. The Vandersaar offered eight more wains of white granite a season at the Concordium Docks. The Debruin family offered weirwood if the Pallas Docks in Cargo were reopened. The House of the Hyena would invest in the Brass Coast once the pirates are dealt with. The Kruidenkenner refused to cut herb prices but proposed specific herbs for Sybella and a larger Meade magazijn. Jasmijn Dijkgraaf offered to carry a letter to the Elakar for eleven thrones. Hahnmark's farmers accepted, giving up Brenna's Gift income for viezesmaak.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Delves' treaties with the Grendel do not protect their ships from the Children of Wrecks, and the Grendel are named as Asavean allies in burning Siroc.

Highguard.t: The Kruidenkenner proposed that the High Herbalist of Sybella receive set amounts of true vervain and marrowort instead of random herbs, to be arranged through the Ambassador. Their Crown's Quay magazijn remains their largest Imperial investment.

The Brass Coast.t: The House of the Hyena, prompted by Damian i Martan i Erigo, wants to sell mithril and artisan metals to Freeborn markets and settle at Calvos or Quzar. Allied families would pay well to salvage drowned Siroc, but none of this will happen until the Children of Wrecks are dealt with.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the Kruidenkenner sell herbs to the Clearing House in Tassato, and the Sarcophan enclave in Sarvos is covered in a separate wind.

The Marches.t: The Kruidenkenner offered to expand their magazijn in Meade so the Master of the Root and Stem could buy two more specific herbs. The offer went untaken at the Equinox but stays open until the end of Winter 386YE.

Urizen.t: The Debruin family offered up to 15 wains of weirwood a season if the Pallas Docks in Cargo were refitted as the Debruin Docks. The same motion could make the Prime Factor title an Urizen national position. No one took up the offer at the Equinox.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Kruidenkenner merchants use the Sarcophan mooring in Ivarsgard to trade with Varushkan herbalists, though demand there has fallen sharply.

Wintermark.t: Hahnmark's farm owners voted to grow vlinderbloem for the Kraft brothers, giving up Brenna's Gift income in exchange for viezesmaak. Wintermark's Thanmir Hrafnar is the only person from whom Jasmijn Dijkgraaf will accept an Elakar letter.

Hyenas and herbs.o: In Autumn 386YE the Sarcophan Delves set out their dealings with the Empire. They complained about the Asavean bounty and the Children of Wrecks, and offered trade proposals on weirwood, white granite, metals, herbs and a letter to the Elakar. Hahnmark's farmers voted to accept the Kraft brothers' vlinderbloem scheme.

Kallavesa/Wittal Grove.t: Mentioned in passing: the page names the port of Fisk as the Krafts' export route to Faraden, without saying where it lies.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: Hyena interest in Madruga's coast, including salvage of Siroc and a possible presence at Calvos or Quzar, waits on the Empire dealing with the Children of Wrecks. The page does not say which of these sites lie in Lightsea.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Mentioned in passing: the page names the Kruidenkenner Magazijn at Crown's Quay as their main Imperial investment, without saying where it lies.

Bastion.t: The High Herbalist of Sybella may switch the Kruidenkenner herb supply for the Anvil hospital to set amounts of true vervain and marrowort, at the same price as before.

Bay of Catazar.t: Attacks by the Children of Wrecks across the Bay are forcing Sarcophan captains to hire more marines and ships. The Delves expect the Empire to deal with the pirates.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark's farmers voted to give land over to vlinderbloem. Each farmer now receives two doses of viezesmaak a season, and Brenna's Gift income is lost while the scheme lasts.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Kraft brothers plan to export viezesmaak through the revitalised port of Fisk along the new route to Faraden.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: the Kruidenkenner trade with Varushkan herbalists at the Sarcophan mooring in Ivarsgard, though demand there has declined sharply.

Madruga.t: Sarcophan families would pay the treasury or Madruga's senator well for exclusive rights to salvage drowned Siroc, but only once the Children of Wrecks are dealt with.

Mitwold.t: An offered expansion of the Kruidenkenner magazijn in Meade, costing 8 weirwood and 24 crowns, would add two herb tracks for the Master of the Root and Stem. It remains open until the end of Winter 386YE.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Kruidenkenner Magazijn at Crown's Quay is named as the association's largest and best-known Imperial investment.

Redoubt.t: A 90-crown refit could reopen the Pallas Docks in Cargo as the Debruin Docks, with a bear statue, and bring up to 15 wains of weirwood a season. The offer was not taken up at the Equinox.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sarcophan enclave at the Alivetti Estates is covered in another wind, and a sailor recalls buying an enchanted carving there.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Kruidenkenner merchants regularly sell herbs to the Clearing House in Tassato.

The Semmerlak.t: Mentioned in passing: the threat of Dho'uala has made the Semmerlak less appealing to the Kruidenkenner.

I already know you.d: Highguard delayed its peerless kinship with the Marches, asking the Marcher Assembly for a clear invitation during the Spring Equinox. The dredged Westmere opened trade via Meade and Fisk, but a cursed forgestone was recovered, and a Westmere Council passed the decision to Senator Sally of Mitwold: sink it deep, send it to Anvil, or something else. Marcher and Imperial Orc mandates affirmed the former Jotun thralls as Marchers. Questions arose over orc monks, and canal-maintaining Mourn orcs, now called beaters, sent a delegation to Anvil. The Synod passed three mandates, spread by Larkin Otterways, Sister Meredith and Friar John of the Mourn, so that each army gains local yeofolk support at home but breaks its oath if it fails to return when its territory is attacked.

Highguard.t: The Highborn held back their peerless kinship with the Marches for fear of inflaming Bregasland, asking the Marcher Assembly for a clear invitation during the Spring Equinox before setting to work.

Imperial Orcs.t: Bloodcrow Knott's mandate told Imperial Orcs that the Mourn orcs are Marchers, and their preachers' winter discussions softened tensions, with Marcher orc spiritual leaders helping put names to Jotun ancestral voices some Imperial Orcs hear.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher orcs are former Jotun thralls, and their spiritual leaders know something of the Jotun ancestors and the Kirkja.

The Marches.t: The Marches embraced their orcs as Marchers, faced questions over orc monks and beaters, received a cursed stone from the Westmere, and saw its Synod bind the Drakes, Bounders and Tusks by oath to their home territories.

Wintermark.t: The completed Westmere dredging, backed by the Senator for Kallavesa, brought new trade and prosperity to Fisk, while the cursed stone raised from the mere bears Wintermark runes.

I already know you.o: In spring 386YE the Westmere dredging was completed, bringing prosperity around the Gullet but also raising a deeply cursed rune-carved stone, while the Marches wrestled with how to fold the Marcher orcs into their traditions. The Marcher Synod then passed mandates binding the Drakes, Bounders and Tusks to Mitwold, Upwold and the Mournwold.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Mentioned in passing: North Fens landskeeper Larkin Pewter again proposed having the generals' oaths witnessed by the Lictors, was rebuffed, and went home to sulk.

Mitwold/Meade March.t: The cursed forgestone sat dripping on the Meade shore, injuring dredging workers and threatening Meade itself, while the opened Westmere brought a boom in trade to the city.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland shared in the prosperity from the dredged Westmere, while its delicate situation made Highguard cautious about intervening, and the Strong Reeds' existing oath to defend it inspired the new army mandates.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Westmere Council suggested sending the cursed stone to Anvil so any disaster would strike Casinea rather than the Marches.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa benefited from the completed dredging, with a Mediator of Fisk to be appointed during the Spring Equinox to handle new trade with the Tseriyn and Salagiin.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold gained prosperity and an Alder of Meade from the dredging but must deal with the cursed stone via Senator Sally, and the Drakes are now oath-bound to defend it.

Mournwold.t: Mourn orcs maintaining the Black Canal were dubbed beaters and sent a delegation to Anvil, and the Tusks were sworn to always fight to keep the Mournwold safe.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the dredged Westmere improves trade with the coastal towns and cities of Faraden on the Sea of Snow.

Skarsind.t: Orc preachers from Skarsind debated the Marcher orcs over the winter, and Bloodcrow Knott's mandate softened the prickly feelings between them.

Upwold.t: The Synod mandate declared that the Bounders will always call Upwold home and never abandon it, binding them to defend the territory when attacked.

I am easy to find.d: In Winter 386YE Emperor Vesna delivered a personal message, carried across the Empire and beyond by the civil service, concerning the orders issued to the Gryphon's Pride in the Barrens. Vesna declared that the Rahvin were foreigners protected by Imperial law, seeking to work with the Empire through legal means, and that both the Empire and Vesna had sworn no harm would come to them. Archavion was accused of hiding his scheme, waiting until Vesna could not intervene, undermining negotiations by the Earl's council, and betraying the Empire, his soldiers and his nation. Vesna branded him a criminal with no place at Dawn's hearth and vowed the crime would be answered to the fullest extent of the law.

Dawn.t: Dawn's own Emperor publicly disowned a Dawnish general, declaring that Archavion did not act in the nation's name, had brought it death and shame, and had undermined the Earl's council's efforts to secure Dawn's resources lawfully.

I am easy to find.o: Emperor Vesna used the Throne's power to address the Empire to publicly denounce General Archavion of the Gryphon's Pride as a criminal for his actions against the Rahvin in the Barrens, which the Empire had sworn to protect.

The Barrens.t: The address concerned the Gryphon's Pride's actions in the Barrens against the Rahvin, whom Vesna said had been under Imperial protection, leaving what Vesna called a desert that Dawn must now learn to live in.

I heard a source.d: Ephisis offered to sell Autumn vis through a refurbished tower in Kalpaheim, needing 16 wains of mithril, 32 Crowns and a Senate commission or Wayleave. Pained by the Liberty Pact, the City wanted new Senate wayleaves as a sign of commitment to trade. Each one would allow a similar ministry for another realm at sites in Temeschwar, Meade, Seren, Siroc and Bastion. It refused an unlimited Ephisis' Scale. If the Senate relinquished every major Bourse seat and made them all Imperial, it promised Autumn vis trade everywhere and a strengthened Imperial regio. Prospero's herald urged the opposite, making every seat national, for matching benefits.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral Castle is named as a lesser Bourse resource whose status would not matter under Ephisis' all-Imperial Bourse proposal.

Highguard.t: Ephisis' heralds identified Bastion as a site where a ministry could supply prismatic ink to the Empire, provided the Senate created an additional wayleave and commissioned the facility.

Navarr.t: Seren was named as a possible site for a ministry trading vital honey from the City of Gold and Lead, available only if the Senate created more wayleaves.

The Brass Coast.t: Siroc was put forward by Ephisis' heralds as a location for a ministry supplying crystal fire, should the Senate create an extra wayleave and commission it.

The League.t: Temeschwar was proposed as the site of a possible ministry trading heart's blood, depending on the Senate creating additional wayleaves.

The Marches.t: Meade was identified as a possible site for a ministry supplying golden apples, contingent on new wayleaves and a separate commission.

Wintermark.t: The Hidden Prince claimed the deeds to Ogila's unfinished, sealed runesmith tower on the street of runes in Kalpaheim. He proposed completing it as a mithril-doored trading post where heralds of Ephisis would sell Autumn vis.

I heard a source.o: In Spring 383YE the City of Gold and Lead politely declined the Autumn Archmage's invitation to parley with Ephisis and instead sent heralds with three offers to the Empire. The Eternal Prospero then countered with an offer of his own; all the opportunities lasted until the end of the Winter Solstice 383YE.

Bastion.t: Bastion was named as a suitable location for a ministry providing prismatic ink, requiring a new wayleave, 16 wains of mithril and 32 Crowns.

Hahnmark.t: An abandoned tower in Kalpaheim, sealed since the runesmith Ogila's death, could be completed with mithril and fitted with doors for heralds of the City of Gold and Lead. Merchants would then sell Autumn vis there.

Madruga.t: Siroc was identified as a site where a ministry could supply crystal fire, if the Senate created a further wayleave and commissioned the facility.

Miaren.t: Seren was proposed as the location for a possible ministry providing vital honey through trade with Ephisis.

Mitwold.t: Meade was put forward as a site for a ministry supplying golden apples, available only alongside a new Senate wayleave.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral Castle is cited as a lesser Bourse resource excluded from Ephisis' requirement that all major Bourse seats be Imperial.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar was named as a suitable site for a ministry supplying heart's blood, should the Senate create an additional wayleave and commission it.

I knew you were trouble.d: Prospero's lieutenant Maestro Fisetojin would meet the Archmage of Autumn with two invited Varushkans. Sorin's court would parley with the Archmage of Winter, questioned the boons requested, and offered to open the Gauntlet of Fangs to Throne candidates if the Conclave declared concord. Kimus would meet only the Archmage of Day and offered three gifts. Eleonaris would bring her Seat of Judgement for the Summer Archmage and declared friendship restored. The Whisper Gallery refused a parley, sought new agents, and cut ties with Luciano Vivaci Rezia di Tassato. Llofir, its Tamarbode garden ravaged, would forgive the Empire only after being granted amity and visiting famine on every Imperial farm.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Prospero's herald arrived at the Castle of Thorns in Astolat, and Sorin's heralds were at first mistaken for Dawnish knights.

Highguard.t: Brother Luke of Highguard, Archmage of Summer, was invited to ascend Eleonaris's Seat of Judgement and have his empery tested, while Llofir's grievance stems from the destruction of its garden in Highguard-held Reikos.

The Marches.t: Should the Conclave grant Llofir amity, Marcher farms would suffer with the rest of the Empire, though the Keeper of the Breadbasket might mitigate some of the effects in Upwold and Mitwold.

Urizen.t: The civil service warned that if Llofir took its retribution, Urizen would face especially severe starvation because it relies heavily on food imported from other nations.

Varushka.t: Prospero specifically invited Loom-Master Borys and Boyar Vasiliy Strascovich of Varushka, or their representatives, to accompany the Archmage of Autumn to a discreet parley on a sensitive matter.

I knew you were trouble.o: Ahead of the Winter Solstice 384YE, six eternals answered the plenipotentiary messages of the Imperial archmages: Prospero, Sorin, Kimus and Eleonaris agreed to formal parleys, the Whisper Gallery agreed only to an informal meeting, and Llofir refused, demanding amity so that it could take revenge on the Empire.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Tamarbode held the garden Llofir asked only to be left alone; after the Conclave declared it an enemy, Imperial armies destroyed everything living there, which Llofir now means to avenge.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Prospero's genial herald appeared at the Castle of Thorns in Astolat to deliver his response to the Archmage of Autumn.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris's herald spoke of the enduring good relationship between the Fields of Glory and the Catazarri Empire.

Mitwold.t: If Llofir's threatened blight came to pass, the Keeper of the Breadbasket might be able to soften some of its effects in Mitwold, though that would do little for the wider Empire.

Reikos.t: Llofir's garden lay in Tamarbode in Reikos; Imperial armies ravaged it a year earlier, and that attack is the root of the eternal's refusal to parley and its demand for retribution.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm is not named on the page; the nearest link is Eleonaris's reference to the statue guarding the Golden Causeway as a symbol of friendship with the Empire.

Upwold.t: If Llofir's threatened blight came to pass, the Keeper of the Breadbasket might be able to mitigate some of the famine's effects in Upwold.

I remember you.d: Evander Slak announced what is probably his last Axou drug-selling visit, accompanied by the cambion Ilarch Kyther Deianeira. The theologian Theodosia of Ipotavo, believed to hold the Shield of Vigilance Bawn-watch, returned to Anvil. Endric of Lepidus found three lyric-only songs possibly by Elayne Silverlark and invited songsmiths to set them. Iosif Kosta brought Caoimhe Tend-Fallen a report on a Commonwealth aura. Annukka Juhaling came to warn of astronomancy's dangers. Cassius, a shattered stargazer, preached doom on the road. The sick herald Archipelago the Rising Leviathan sought healers. Thule merchants of the Five Fang Consortium sought investment. The Charnel Lord welcomed a Varushkan Empress and promised an unspecified gift.

Dawn.t: One of the three lost Silverlark songs appears to adapt a Dawnish original, and Dawnish troubadours are among those invited to compose a tune for its lyrics.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the stargazer Cassius was left shattered after escaping when the Druj took his spire, the Arch of the Sky.

Highguard.t: The Highborn poet Endric of Lepidus found the lost Silverlark songs, one adapted from a Highborn original, and hopes to publish the best arrangements for pilgrims of Loyalty.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the visiting Thule merchants planned to head first to the Imperial Orcs camp on arrival.

Thule.t: Merchants of the Five Fang Consortium, turned back twice before by heat and weather, came seeking Imperial investment in a scheme in Otkodov, though why they were not seeking it from fellow Thule was unclear.

Urizen.t: Cassius, a grief-stricken stargazer from the fallen Arch of the Sky, left his refuge in Morrow and walked to Anvil preaching visions of doom, apparently bound for the Brass Coast camp.

Varushka.t: The Charnel Lord of Branoc welcomed Varushka's return to the throne and promised Empress Vesna Borkovna Prochnost a gift, while the Varushkan merchant Iosif Kosta brought the Synod a report from the Commonwealth.

Wintermark.t: One of the three lost Silverlark songs appears to adapt a Wintermark original, and scops and other Wintermark songsmiths are invited to set its lyrics to music.

I remember you.o: As the Winter Solstice of 385YE approached, a varied assortment of foreign and unusual visitors made their way to Anvil. They included Axou traders and scholars, a Suaq astronomancer, a doom-preaching Urizen stargazer, an ailing Summer herald and Thule merchants, while the Charnel Lord of Branoc promised a gift for the new Empress.

Karsk/Branoc.t: The Charnel Lord, sleeping in its well-guarded barrow in the hills of Branoc, declared its welcome for a Varushkan Empress and promised her a gift of unknown nature and timing.

Necropolis/Fishguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Axou theologian Theodosia of Ipotavo rented a small house on the outskirts of Myfanwy's Rest and welcomed missives from Imperial scholars there.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening scene describes travellers on pilgrimage to Bastion passing through a crossroads inn.

Karsk.t: The Charnel Lord's minions, mortal and otherwise, are sometimes encountered in the hills of Karsk, and the sovereign sleeping in its barrow there promised a gift to the new Empress.

Morrow.t: The stargazer Cassius had been given refuge in a spire in Morrow before abruptly leaving it after the Autumn Equinox to walk to Anvil.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening scene notes travellers journeying down the coast to the Necropolis.

Otkodov.t: The Thule merchants of the Five Fang Consortium sought Imperial investment for an unspecified scheme in Otkodov.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, but linked through Cassius, a refugee from the Arch of the Sky, a spire that fell to the Druj.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, but linked through Cassius, a refugee from the Arch of the Sky, a spire that fell to the Druj.

I wish you would.d: The Senate passed the Thule treaty, but the General Assembly faced a judgement of veto; if the treaty failed, war with Otkodov would resume after the Summer Solstice. The Thule enchanted and strengthened their fortifications in the Silver Peaks, Crow's Ridge, Miechernya, Krevsaty and the Bonewood, and warded the Webwood. A Thule consortium's cattle were stranded at Crow's Ridge. The Suranni reported a Dumon curse on Arbonne (Kalino) and warned of black pearls in the Bay. Morajasse's Grendel demanded recognition as foreigners. Beoraidh offered land for a temple or basilica and sought investment in a new arena. Skoura raised no objection to weirwood trade with Tsark and sent traders to Anvil.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to the Grendel, Finna of Dawn, handles Grendel negotiations and is invited to meet Wind Lord Morath at the Black Sand Tower.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: a Sage of Tsark travelling to Anvil was forced to retreat after running afoul of the Druj in Zenith, and the Webwood is described as largely untouched since Druj rule.

Grendel.t: The Grendel stayed at war but quiet, claimed to have dealt with the Children of Wrecks at the Tempest Jade Temple, and offered a meeting with Wind Lord Morath. Commander Gallum's soldiers at Mora's Rock demanded recognition of Morajasse as a foreign protectorate.

Imperial Orcs.t: A Skouran delegation from the Geltcourse Trade Security Council planned to visit the Imperial Orc camp to buy forest resources and discuss long-term trade with the Senator for Mareave.

The Brass Coast.t: The Grendel of Mora's Rock demanded that Bakar and the Seaglass Beacon cease cursing Morajasse, offering protection of the Feroz coast against the Children of Wrecks in return. The Suranni also urged checks that a Dumon-style curse does not strike Segura or Feroz.

The Marches.t: Thule cattle wranglers collected cows bought at Upwold markets, and Suranni historians were so impressed by the Marchers that Baroness Katerine proposed a visit to observe their harvest festival, perhaps as guests of the Garamond household.

Thule.t: The Thule considered their treaty settled but threatened renewed war if it was vetoed. They enchanted and expanded their five fortifications inside the Empire, and their Company of the Icebound Wind was left with cattle exposed at Crow's Ridge.

Urizen.t: Vossk of Zenith Ascendent was specifically invited to meet Wind Lord Morath, while a Tsark sage was driven back by the Druj in Zenith. The Grendel are noted as having been rebuffed from Redoubt.

Varushka.t: Thule fortifications in Miechernya, Krevsaty and the Bonewood were enchanted and strengthened, and the Webwood was warded. Rak invited Senator Sławomir Rabovich Bolotstrazh to write again so Thule and Varushkans might pool knowledge of a threat in the Webwood.

Wintermark.t: The Citadel of Bone and Silver in the Silver Peaks was enchanted and reinforced, and Rak commended Isolde Tempest Shield over the madness in the north-west. Marko Siwarsbairn was a guest of Baroness Katerine, researching Suranni military history until at least Autumn.

I wish you would.o: In Summer 387YE the Empire's dealings with five foreign powers developed: Otkodov, the Iron Confederacy, the Grendel, the city state of Beoraidh and Skoura. The Thule treaty awaited a possible Synod veto while Otkodov fortified its holdings inside the Empire.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: Commander Gallum Fiersach and Wind Lord Saoirse asked the Senate to recognise Morajasse as a protectorate under their command, with its people declared foreigners, and to end Bakar's curses there.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Mentioned in passing: before the Spring Equinox, Gallum's troops fought the Children of Wrecks in Oranseri.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: Krevsatyzmei was enchanted; pale wolves larger than oxen were said to stalk the wooded hills watching the southern border.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Lord Ehsan spent mithril strengthening the city's walls and harbour and offered quayside land for a temple or basilica of the Way, while the Diamant Drakes sought Imperial bonds to rebuild the colosseum.

Mareave/Sinfoyard.t: Attempts to establish farms in barren Sinfoyard were going badly, and a proposed shrine in Beoraidh would also preach to its orcs.

Miekarova/Miechernya.t: Eldfell was iced over and garrisoned with bear-like figures, and Rak warned the Dragons might act themselves if the Falconer's madness kept troubling Miechernya.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: Fljajokep was seriously reinforced and bound with glowing brass sigils, with bronze four-armed creatures supplementing the garrison and extra defences at the Silent Pines grove.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Reports told of magic seething in the forest's depths, spawning shadowy shapes, probably a Thule night ward. Rak offered to pass Varushkan concerns about a malign threat there to his warlocks.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The Citadel of Bone and Silver was improved and enchanted with glowing runes and drake-like guardians, and the region was among those troubled by the Falconer's madness.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Crow's Keep was expanded and enchanted, and the Company of the Icebound Wind's cattle were camped here, open to seizure by a victorious Imperial general if war came.

Skarsind/Skogei Glens.t: Mentioned in passing: the expanded Crow's Keep is visible from parts of the Skogei Glens.

Bay of Catazar.t: Strange bells were heard across much of the Bay, and the Suranni warned that black pearls pulled from its waters were blasphemous tools of Dumon. Beoraidh feared attacks by the Children of Wrecks.

Feroz.t: The Grendel of Mora's Rock offered to protect the Feroz coast from the Children of Wrecks if Morajasse was recognised as theirs and the curses stopped, and threatened rituals of their own in Feroz.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the hilly terrain of Hahnmark slowed the Thule cattle drive north.

Kalino.t: Known to the Suranni as the Duchy of Arbonne, it was struck by a curse blamed on the Hand of Dumon: weeds, orchard blight, vermin, and sickness that left bark-like scabs.

Karsk.t: The Thule fortification of Krevsatyzmei, watching over Oloy, was enchanted; massive pale wolves were reported watching the southern border.

Mareave.t: Beoraidh fortified itself and offered land for a temple or basilica of the Way. Skouran traders crossed the territory, once their land of Mahal, seeking to meet its Senator.

Miekarova.t: Eldfell, securing Ustyma's Gate, was enchanted with ice and unseasonable snow and reinforced by bear-like servants likely of Cathan Canae.

Mountains of the Moon.t: Skoura raised no objection to Imperial weirwood trade with Tsark but warned that Tsark's motives are philosophical rather than economic; a Tsark sage hoped to attend the Autumn Equinox.

Ossium.t: The Thule reinforced Fljajokep and the Silent Pines in the Bonewood and laid a probable night ward in the Webwood, where a malign threat may be investigated jointly with Varushka.

Otkodov.t: The Thule homeland awaited the treaty's fate. Rak planned to retire if it passed, and the Empire's maps of Otkodov remained poor, with even Verthandi's nearly six years out of date.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel have been notably quiet since being rebuffed from Redoubt.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Baroness Katerine suggested the Empire investigate to ensure a curse like Arbonne's does not happen in Segura.

Sermersuaq.t: The Citadel of Bone and Silver was enchanted and its Stonefield Ice Caves defences improved, and a large Thule force passed through to collect cattle from the Marches.

Shavronne.t: Mentioned in passing: a citizen's past life vision of being a cousin to the Duke of Shavronne prompted Baroness Katerine to advise keeping the matter quiet.

Skarsind.t: Crow's Keep was expanded to a rank two fortification and enchanted, and the Thule cattle herd camped at Crow's Ridge could be seized back if war broke out.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule bought their cattle from the markets of Upwold.

Veroigne.t: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni ambassador's seat in Chaubrette is said to lie west of Veroigne.

Verthandi.t: Mentioned in passing: it is the only Otkodov territory the Empire has mapped, and that map is almost six years old.

Zenith.t: A Sage of Tsark bound for Anvil was forced to retreat from the Druj in Zenith, hoping to come in Autumn if the Druj threat was not imminent.

Idle hands are the devil's playthings.d: Almodin's Senate commissions were all decorated with effigies of Asavean gods. The Synod could fund a year-long blockade (100 liao) that would shut the Great Game, Pallas Docks, Runeforge and Lorenzo's Legacies. It could instead send a mob to tear down the idols (25 liao), wrecking the buildings and giving a year's boost to local congregations. A third option (50 liao) would follow Ivarsgard's example and repurpose the idols, giving a permanent boost. Chainbreaker Snark proposed a variant that would also storm the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz. Action against the Temple would hurt trade and anger Asavea. The Senate could also alter the commissions or revoke the Temple's permission.

Grendel.t: The Grendel currently hold a cordon around the Temple of the Black Bull in Feroz. Snark's proposed mandate would need a large mob to break through it, probably at the cost of Grendel and Imperial lives, and how the Grendel would respond is uncertain.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn would face lost taxes, lost orichalcum profits from trade with Nemoria and local unrest if the Temple in Feroz were blockaded or destroyed. Freeborn sutannir Franco i Erigo would lose his delegate's benefits, or the post entirely.

The League.t: The League holds several of Almodin's works: Lorenzo's Legacies in Temeschwar and Tassato and the Great Game. A League senator, Rafael Barossa di Tassato, raised the Pride Assembly's condemnation, and Holberg's Wunderkind guild designed the stelae that protesters could turn out of phase.

Urizen.t: The Runeforge in Redoubt is one of Almodin's buildings. Pilgrims in Redoubt could ring it in protest, and its idols could be torn down or repurposed, damaging it until it is repaired.

Varushka.t: Varushka had already led the way: the boyar of Ivarsgard had the idols at Lestasny ground into gravel, and Karsk's buildings were already defaced. Karsk congregations would gain double benefits for a year if a destruction mandate passed.

Wintermark.t: Veikko Bondforger's condemnation of the architect was echoed by the Pride Assembly. Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance in Hahnmark is among the works that could be shut down, defaced or repurposed.

Idle hands are the devil's playthings.o: After the Synod convicted the Asavean architect Almodin Oktístis of idolatry and the Assembly of Pride condemned his works, Imperial citizens were ready to act against his idol-decorated buildings across the Empire. Three competing Synod mandates and Senate options were offered for dealing with his legacy.

Karsk/Lestasny.t: Almodin fortified Lestasny, but the boyar of Ivarsgard had its Asavean statues used to gravel the courtyard so Imperial boots tread on the false gods. This lasting act of defiance is held up as the model for the third mandate.

Feroz.t: The Temple of Balo and the Black Bull at Oran would be cordoned under the first mandate and destroyed under the others, costing trade and taxes and causing local unrest. Snark's variant would see a mob storm it and force its Asavean priests to recant or die.

Hahnmark.t: Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance stands here. Locals could turn its stelae out of phase to shut it down, or a mandate to remove its idols would damage it but swell local congregations.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's Wunderkind guild designed the adjustable red stone stelae used in Lorenzo's Legacies.

Karsk.t: Almodin's buildings in Karsk had already been defaced. Under either destruction mandate its congregations would gain four extra votes and two extra doses of liao for a year, for having led the Empire's response.

Redoubt.t: The Runeforge here could be ringed by protesting pilgrims and shut down. Alternatively it could be damaged by the removal of its idols, with Pride boosting local congregations.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Qanat commissioned in Segura was never begun and its motion has lapsed, so it needs no action.

Tassato.t: Lorenzo's Legacy of Ambition here could be shut down by locals turning its stelae out of phase, or damaged and stripped of its idols under the other mandates.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar hosts Lorenzo's Legacy of Loyalty and the Great Game. Local pilgrims could blockade them, or have their idols torn down or repurposed, closing them until they are repaired.

If one be gone we carry on.d: After Jarl Haakon Gydasson was defeated at the Winter Solstice, the Tusks and Drakes drove the Jotun from the Ore Hills with help from miners, grateful locals and servants of the Prince with a Thousand Foes. They are a little short of two-fifths of the way to taking the Chalkdowns, but the Greensward and Farstrider's Watch remain in Jotun hands. In Bregasland some forty to fifty thousand Jotun, backed by the Burhfæst garrison and Summer knights, took the Rushes, Grey Fens and North Fens and came eight-tenths of the way to taking Ottermire. The territory is no longer Imperial and Willem Tarne lost his Senate seat. The Lasambrian Corazón looted the Bregasland Breadbasket. A battle opportunity at Sal-Ott Meet offers a chance to halt the final Jotun push.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Military Council sent Imperial heroes to challenge the Druj and eliminate Governor Rahab instead of stopping the Burhfæst's return.

Jotun.t: The Jotun lost the Ore Hills and are losing ground in the Chalkdowns, but they still hold the Greensward and Farstrider's Watch. In Bregasland they conquered almost the whole territory, offering the Choice and gaining the support of the Clakes of Beandown.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: a number of Navarr traders were killed when the Jotun captured Graven the previous Summer.

The Marches.t: Marcher armies won hard victories in Mournwold, where locals cheered them as liberators, while Bregasland fell almost entirely to the Jotun and lost its senator. The Strong Reeds held together a divided resistance at Ottery.

Wintermark.t: A yegarra raiding band crossed the Westmere into Kallavesa Marsh to plunder Hufi's Garden near Masi, and the Woundbinder of the Mark, Conrald Mystrim, was called on to stop them.

If one be gone we carry on.o: In Spring 387YE the Tusks and the Drakes liberated the Ore Hills of Mournwold and pushed into the Chalkdowns. Meanwhile a vast Jotun host poured out of Ashvale and conquered nearly all of Bregasland, leaving only Ottery and its causeway held by the Strong Reeds and a fractious Bregas resistance.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: The Burhfæst rose around Graven Rock under the Ice Fishers of Ldansk, and its garrison joined the Jotun invasion that poured through Gravenmarch.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: The Jotun conquered Grey Fens, which remains sullen. Presenting five captured Corazón pennants could ease that mood.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: North Fens fell to the Jotun, and warbands are now picking their way east from it towards Ottery.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: The Jotun are eight-tenths of the way to taking Ottermire, where the Bregas resistance and Strong Reeds have fortified Ottery as the last holdout.

Bregasland/The Rushes.t: Sallow and most of the Rushes fell almost at once, and the resentful Clakes of Beandown welcomed the invaders. An elite kirkja force is now marching north from Sallow towards Ottery.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: A yegarra warband landed here and must pass through Aethelric's Fence on its way to Hufi's Garden. Stopping it there would force it back across the Westmere.

Liathaven/Liath's Ring.t: Mentioned in passing: the castellan of the Burhfæst secured a supply route back to Liath's Ring.

Mitwold/Meade March.t: Strong Reeds recently billeted in Meade March recruited defenders here, who marched along the causeway to help hold Ottery.

Mitwold/Oddmire.t: Refugees fled along Odd's Way to Oddmire, which the Jotun would march on next if Ottery falls. Strong Reeds formerly billeted there recruited defenders for Bregasland.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: A Spring ward and the hares of the Prince with a Thousand Foes aided locals in Alderly, while Einar the Cunning gathers a yegarra warband at the Boar's Hall for the Tusks' general to confront.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: The Marcher armies pushed into the Chalkdowns and are a little shy of two-fifths of the way to liberating it, though the Jotun still control it.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Mentioned in passing: Green March is named as a region Jotun armies could strike into from Ashvale at any moment.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Jarl Haakon's allies remain in full control of the Greensward, guarded by veteran champions at Farstrider's Watch.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: The Ore Hills were liberated, with miners both human and orc lending their supplies and tunnels to the Marchers. Some Marcher orcs sought to enlist, inspired by the voices of their ancestors.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: A Frozen Citadel was raised in Southmoor to defend Sarcombe, though the region remains exposed to a Jotun strike from Ashvale.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland was almost entirely conquered, with only Ottery, the Otterway and the Sallow Way as far as Sal-Ott Meet still resisting. It is no longer Imperial and its Breadbasket granaries were looted, though the Strong Reeds helped the Bregas hide much of their wealth.

Kallavesa.t: Yegarra from Bregasland landed in Kallavesa Marsh aiming for Hufi's Garden. If they reach it, the garden will be devastated and produce half as many herbs until repaired.

Liathaven.t: Ashvale was the staging ground from which tens of thousands of Jotun invaded Bregasland, and Jotun armies there could strike at Mournwold at any moment.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold suffered Jotun raids and a Kalsea yegarra foray repelled by Meade's bounders, sent defenders along the causeway to Ottery, and faces Jotun advance if Bregasland falls.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold is Imperial but far from secure. The Ore Hills were liberated and the Chalkdowns contested, but Jotun champions still hold the Greensward and Farstrider's Watch.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: news of the invasion of Reinos reached the Lasambrians of the Corazón only sporadically.

If the wheel is fixed.d: The Sumaah House of Courage narrowly passed a statement pausing missionary work in the Empire, so penalties on congregations along the Bay of Catazar ended for now. The House of the Way narrowly pledged no new paragons, exemplars or doctrine changes for a year. Laloc, pilgrim of Courage, set out five Sumaah concerns: unilateral doctrine changes, compromise with false faiths, the role of paragons and exemplars, differing views of the virtues, and the place of orcs in the Way. If the General Assembly passes a matching statement by the Summer Solstice, delegates will meet at Anvil. Otherwise the Sumaah will assume reconciliation is impossible. Meanwhile the Sumaah remain divided over orc virtue and still exterminate orcs.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: in the in-character exchange, Laloc remarks that the Empire's treatment of the Druj has not changed since they accepted the doctrine of the ancestors.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Bastion is set against Timoj as a rival heart of the Way, and the Sumaah Embassy in Necropolis serves as a point of diplomatic contact.

Imperial Orcs.t: The place of orcs in the Way is a central Sumaah grievance: they question the recognition of two orc exemplars and an orc cardinal and suggest the Empire may have been guilty of idolatry. The Sumaah still exterminate the orcs they encounter while their Houses remain divided over whether orcs can be virtuous.

If the wheel is fixed.o: After Jorma Steelhail's mandate urging the Empire and the Sumaah Republic to treat Timoj and Bastion as equals, the Sumaah Houses of Virtue paused missionary preaching against the Synod. They offered talks at Anvil if the Imperial Synod's General Assembly pledged to make no recognitions or changes of doctrine for a year.

Bastion.t: Bastion's standing as the heart of the Way is at stake: the mandate urged that it be seen as Timoj's equal, and the Sumaah want any reconciliation between Timoj and Bastion settled through talks.

Bay of Catazar.t: The penalties suffered by congregations along the Bay of Catazar from Sumaah missionary preaching have ended, at least for now.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sumaah Embassy in Necropolis handles relations between the House of the People and the Senate, separate from Laloc's role for the Sumaah Synod.

If we never meet again.d: Jarm publicised the Empire's confirmation that a Volkevaar coven under Professor Eva Giersan conjured Cold Sun, and the Commonwealth had to accept a ceasefire fixing their borders. The two powers are not cooperating, and Jarm is extending protection to neutral border states. Both nations offered paid mercenary ventures to Imperial military units. Fuchsbach put all Commonwealth opportunities on hold and dismissed the Rod and Shield and Golden Pyramid. Imperial fleets were barred from Murolosch and faced worse trade at Volkavaar and Leerdam. In Jarm, the Celestial Arch helped secure the ceasefire. The Sevenfold Path deepened ties with the Convocation of Virtue, but Lord-Magister Trescher grew suspicious. Professor Gelberg remains a Grendel prisoner.

Dawn.t: The House of Princes particularly sought Dawnish warrior-wizards for its Jarm Against Oblivion venture, and Dawnish military units taking it gain a bonus to their effective rank.

Grendel.t: Grendel captors still hold Professor Gelberg after a failed Imperial rescue. The attempt convinced them he is worth more alive, and a ransom remains possible but likely expensive.

Highguard.t: Highborn ambassadors Thaumiel and Cyrus delivered the revelations that reshaped eastern diplomacy. The Commonwealth still sends Soldatentrunk to the General of the Granite Pillar and seeks Highborn soldiers as mercenaries, while the Hexenjäger Academy opportunity is on hold. A strongly supported Assembly statement denouncing the disclosure might salvage relations.

The League.t: Both Jarm and the Commonwealth particularly sought League professionals for their campaigns against Cold Sun, offering League military units a rank bonus. Meanwhile, Jarmish pilgrims began using the new pilgrim's house in the League city of Apulian.

Urizen.t: Jarm especially sought Urizeni warrior-wizards for its campaign against Cold Sun. Prince Mila singled out Ibiss Briarheart and the Urizeni for their wisdom in seeing the value of trade with the Principalities.

If we never meet again.o: After Imperial disclosures that Commonwealth citizens unleashed Cold Sun on Lantir, the Principalities of Jarm forced the Commonwealth into a ceasefire, and Imperial-Commonwealth friendship began to collapse. Militärattache Ludkhannah Schöningen resigned as Commonwealth ambassador and was replaced by Otto Fuchsbach.

Spiral.t: The Wayward House, a pilgrim's house in Apulian, was completed and welcomed the first Jarmish pilgrims in some time. They brought star jewels for the Sevenfold Path's vault, a gift that will continue each season while the house stands.

Immortal hand.d: Yaw'nagrah, under enmity, agreed to send her Voice to a formal parley with the Spring Archmage, Rosamund Holt, who appears to have called her to answer charges. Cathan Canae will send the Warden of the Adamant Tower to the Summer Archmage, Solomon of the Shattered Tower, to discuss the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, and asked William Talbot of the Marches or their champion to attend. Estavus will send Supervisor Quench to the Autumn Archmage, Maurice de Gauvin, to discuss the lost Art of the Marches. Tharim will hold private audiences with the Winter Archmage and a 'Keeper of Tharim's Throne'. The Whisper Gallery declared it would speak to Ancel Steward, a declared sorcerer, and the magistrates will investigate whether the law has been broken.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on the page and is attached to it only through the map.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: a herald of Cathan Canae appeared in the Varushkan vale of Volchitrava with a message for the Gremani, pointedly not for the Master of Ice and Darkness at the college above.

Immortal hand.o: In the wake of the Winter Solstice, five Imperial archmages used their power of plenipotentiary to contact eternals, and all five responded publicly. Their responses ranged from a formal parley to private audiences and, in one case, a legally fraught message to a declared sorcerer.

Miekarova/Srodkoja.t: Mentioned in passing: the herald's visit to the Volchitrava vale, with its message for the Gremani that seemingly snubbed the Master of Ice and Darkness, is the only local reference.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page and is attached to it only through the map.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: the vale of Volchitrava was visited by a herald of Cathan Canae, who brought word to the Gremani but not to the college above.

Impossible landscapes.d: Lord Rain agreed to parley with the Spring Archmage and up to four of the Silver Chalice, hoping to resume work on the ritual From the Mountain to the Sea. Ephisis flatly refused to curb the Sanguine Market or name its clients, though the City arranged a meeting with agents of Prospero and Basileus Flint. Roshanwe would not sponsor the Day Archmage's festival of innovation but asked to meet five seekers from five nations. Sung invited particular magicians and the Seer of the Gateway. Adamant's koboldi scouted building projects across the Empire. Kaela would grant her gift to vallorn fighters only if the General Assembly passed a statement of principle by greater majority. Each parley went ahead without obvious harm.

Dawn.t: Ser Fabienne De Miel of Dawn, the Spring Archmage, secured a parley with Lord Rain on behalf of the Silver Chalice. This followed Ser Elienne De La Chasse's successful Declaration of Neutrality, which ended the old enmity with the eternal.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's emissary noted she already grants her gift to Imperial citizens facing lingering torment at the hands of the Druj.

Imperial Orcs.t: Skywise Gralka, the Archmage of Day, was told Roshanwe would not sponsor his festival of innovation. The eternal asked him instead to arrange a meeting between her favoured and five seekers, each from a different nation.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun-held territory of Liathaven is one of the places where Kaela said she could readily offer her gift to those fighting the vallorn.

Navarr.t: Kaela offered her gift to those battling the vallorn in Navarr's Hercynia and Therunin. She would act only if the General Assembly passed a statement of principle urging acceptance of her gift by greater majority.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Adamant expressed pleasure that the College of Engineering in Temeschwar had at last been completed.

Urizen.t: Autumn Archmage Edmundo of Damakan's Forge was rebuffed by Ephisis over the Sanguine Market bounties, which threaten Livia of the Spire of Celestial Cascade among others. Night Archmage Elyssiathain received Sung's offer of parley, and Livia was invited to attend both meetings.

Wintermark.t: Sung specifically asked that at least one Wintermark Mystic join the Night Archmage's delegation, which would shape the topics the eternal discussed.

Impossible landscapes.o: In Winter 383YE five eternals answered the plenipotentiary messages of the Imperial archmages. Lord Rain, Ephisis, Roshanwe and Sung arranged meetings at Anvil, Adamant sent koboldi in place of a formal parley, and Kaela declined to meet but offered her gift against the vallorn.

Brocéliande.t: Kaela said she could extend her gift to those facing the vallorn in Brocéliande without difficulty, but only if the General Assembly endorsed it.

Hercynia.t: Since Kaela already holds the Conclave's amity, nothing would stop her blessing vallorn fighters in Hercynia once the General Assembly passed the statement she required.

Liathaven.t: Kaela said she could reach those fighting the vallorn in Liathaven without difficulty, provided Imperial priests gave their explicit approval through the General Assembly.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Adamant's koboldi celebrated the completion of the College of Engineering in Temeschwar.

Therunin.t: Kaela offered to let those fighting the vallorn in Therunin call on her gift, reducing their bodies to dust the vallorn could not use, if the General Assembly requested it by greater majority.

Improve Court of the White Fountain.d: The improvement was a special opportunity arising from the Stone and Stone wind of fortune, costing 10 rings of ilium and taking three months to complete. Edmundo of Damakhan's Forge agreed to supply the ilium and provided the 10 rings after the Spring Equinox 384YE. Cato Auricspire of the Scarlet Guard was to organise a ritual to be cast on completion. The plans also included an office and suite of rooms for a new Captain of the Fountain's Guard, a tenured national position chosen by the general or generals of Urizen and responsible for the fortress and for the morale and training of its guards. The outcome was not recorded.

Urizen.t: Urizen stood to gain a strengthened fortress and a new tenured national title, the Captain of the Fountain's Guard, appointed by its generals, with Urizen citizens supplying the ilium and organising the completion ritual.

Improve Court of the White Fountain.o: In Spring 384YE Sagua i'Ezmara, Master of the Koboldi, announced plans to improve the Court of the White Fountain fortification in Redoubt with the help of the eternal Adamant, aiming to make it unbreakable.

Redoubt.t: The Court of the White Fountain in Redoubt was to be rebuilt over three months to be unbreakable, with an office and rooms added for the captain of its guard.

Improve House of Barbs.d: Proposed by the senator for Semmerholm and seconded by the senator for Madruga, the motion would have upgraded the House of Barbs, a sinecure in Hercynia, so that its holder, the Voice of Barbs, gained an extra 2 liao and 4 votes in the Imperial Synod. That would have brought the sinecure to 7 liao and 14 votes each season. The work was to cost 2 wains of white granite and 4 crowns and was to be self-funded. The Senate passed the motion, but there were not enough opportunities available to commission the work, so the improvement did not go ahead.

Navarr.t: A Navarr sinecure would have grown in liao and Synod influence, but the improvement failed for lack of commission opportunities despite the Senate's approval.

Improve House of Barbs.o: In Spring 382YE the Senate passed a motion to upgrade the House of Barbs sinecure in Hercynia, raising its yield to 7 liao and 14 Synod votes a season. The work was never commissioned because the Senate had no commission opportunities left.

Hercynia.t: The House of Barbs in Hercynia was to be enlarged with white granite to yield 7 liao and 14 votes, but the work never began because the commission failed.

Improve Our Lady of Pride.d: The commission, raised by the Imperial Master of Works, used standard costs of 100 wains of White Granite and 200 crowns of labour, taking a year to complete. It would benefit from vigilant citizens if materials were provided before the Winter Solstice. Contributions came from Gancio (30 wains and 7 thrones 4 crowns), the Silent Sentinel opportunity (effectively 20 wains and 40 crowns), Landon of Longridge (25 wains), Imperatrix Lisabetta (6 thrones 2 crowns, plus 50 crowns given on her behalf by Severin Teyhard von Holberg) and Lieselotte van Holberg (25 wains), across seasons up to Summer 383YE. On completion the fortification's effective strength would rise to 6,000.

The League.t: League citizens, including Imperatrix Lisabetta, Lieselotte van Holberg and Severin Teyhard von Holberg, supplied much of the granite and money to strengthen a key fortification in their own territory.

Improve Our Lady of Pride.o: In Autumn 382YE the Imperial Master of Works announced a commission to enlarge Our Lady of Pride, the fortification in Sarvos, raising its effective strength to 6,000 once complete.

Sarvos.t: Our Lady of Pride in Sarvos was to be enlarged to an effective strength of 6,000, bolstering the territory's defences once the year-long work was finished.

Improve Reumah's Rest.d: In Autumn 383YE the Senate considered a motion to improve the fortification Reumah's Rest, which stands in the Coursmouth region of Necropolis, a Highguard territory. The motion noted that funds would be required for the work. It was proposed by Semmerholm and seconded by Kahraman, but it did not pass, so no upgrade to the fort was commissioned that season.

Highguard.t: The failed motion left Highguard's fortification at Reumah's Rest in its Necropolis territory un-upgraded, although outside senators had pushed for the improvement.

Improve Reumah's Rest.o: A Senate motion to upgrade the fort Reumah's Rest in Coursmouth, Necropolis, was proposed by the senator for Semmerholm and seconded by the senator for Kahraman, but it failed.

Necropolis/Coursmouth.t: Reumah's Rest in Coursmouth was the fort the motion sought to upgrade, but the motion failed and the fortification stayed as it was.

Necropolis.t: The defences of Necropolis did not change, because the proposed upgrade to Reumah's Rest was not approved.

Improve Reumah's Rest II.d: The commission used standard costs: 100 wains of white granite and 200 crowns of labour, taking one year to complete. Marley of Treen made the first contribution after the Autumn Equinox 383YE, giving 6 thrones 2 crowns and 25 wains of white granite. Richardo Glostari di Sarvos, Lieselotte van Holberg and small donors added money. Further contributions came after the Winter Solstice 383YE from Ehud and Richardo, after the Winter Solstice 384YE from Nemuel and Asael, and after the Spring Equinox 385YE from Arlais, Daughter of Mari, who gave 24 wains of white granite.

Highguard.t: Highguard stands to gain a stronger defence in Necropolis, with the fortification of Reumah's Rest due to rise to a strength of 6,000 once the upgrade is finished.

Improve Reumah's Rest II.o: In Autumn 383YE the Imperial Master of Works, Marley of Treen, announced a commission to upgrade Reumah's Rest, the fortification in Necropolis. When complete, it will raise the fort's strength to 6,000.

Necropolis.t: Reumah's Rest, the fortification in Necropolis, is the subject of the upgrade, funded by donations of white granite and money from Autumn 383YE through Spring 385YE.

Improve Syrene's Wisdom.d: Proposed by the senator for Casinea and seconded by the senator for Kallavesa, the motion commissioned new pumps for Syrene's Wisdom to improve ilium returns and make conditions safer for miners.
