The work cost 10 wains of mithril, 10 wains of weirwood and 40 crowns in labour, and takes three months to build. Until it is completed, the mine produces only 4 rings of ilium each season. After the Autumn Equinox, Solomon provided the mithril, the weirwood and 5 thrones. Once complete, the mine's ilium output rises by 2 rings each season, access to silver and other precious metals brings new prosperity to the nearby town, and the new system copes better with flooding, greatly reducing the risk of deaths in the mines.

Highguard.t: Casinea's Highborn senator proposed the motion, and once the work is complete it will make one of the nation's ilium mines more productive and much safer for the miners who work it.

Improve Syrene's Wisdom.o: In Autumn 384YE the Senate passed a motion to fund the modernisation of the pumps at Syrene's Wisdom, the ilium mine in Casinea, taking up an opportunity described in the Wake up crying Wind of Fortune.

Casinea.t: Syrene's Wisdom in Casinea is to receive modernised pumps; it yields only 4 rings of ilium a season until the work is done, after which output rises by 2 rings, the nearby town gains new prosperity from silver and other precious metals, and the danger of deadly flooding is greatly reduced.

Improve Towerjacks.d: Proposed by the Senator for Astolat and seconded by the Conscience of the Senate, the motion passed with the full amount disbursed to the Senator for Astolat. The improvement required 50 wains of mithril and 100 crowns. Magdalena Teyhard von Holberg contributed a small sum after the Spring Equinox, and Natalia 'The Falcon' Barossa supplied the remaining mithril and most of the coin across the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox. To complete the work, the Towerjacks' general must order the army back to Holberg for a season before the Spring Equinox 385YE, entering in triumph through the Holmauer Gate and processing through the city, which can be done while the army rests and recuperates.

The League.t: The Towerjacks, bound to Holberg, the city they fought for years to save, were to become engineers rather than siege troops, with Magdalena Teyhard von Holberg among those funding the work.

Improve Towerjacks.o: In Spring 384YE the Senate passed a motion to fund improvements to the Towerjacks army, replacing its Siege quality with the Engineer quality, following an opportunity raised in the Watches from the Wall wind of fortune.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: The Towerjacks were to enter Holberg in triumph through the Holmauer Gate and parade through the streets as part of completing their improvement.

Holberg.t: Holberg was to host the Towerjacks for a season, as the army must return to the city before Spring 385YE to complete its transformation.

Improve Walls of Holberg.d: The commission required 100 wains of white granite, 200 crowns in labour costs and six months to build. Funding came from many individual citizens between the Autumn Equinox of 384YE and the Autumn Equinox of 385YE. Jonah Yakovitch and Landon Hawcombe were the largest early donors, and others included Lula Kleist von Ennerlund, Magdalena Teyhard von Holberg and Doctor Luther Manfredi von Holberg. By Autumn 385YE the recorded granite donations totalled 100 wains. Once complete, the strength of the Walls of Holberg fortification would rise to 15,000.

The League.t: A League senator proposed the expansion of one of the League's major city fortifications, and many League citizens, a number bearing the von Holberg or van Holberg name, paid for it with their own money and granite.

Improve Walls of Holberg.o: In Summer 384YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by Volodmartz, commissioning the expansion of the Walls of Holberg, to be funded by the citizens of Holberg.

Holberg/Holfried.t: Holfried is the region attached to the Walls of Holberg, and the commissioned expansion would raise the fortification's strength to 15,000 once complete.

Holberg.t: Holberg's walls were to be expanded so that, once finished, the fortification's strength would rise to 15,000, with the cost met largely by Holberg's own citizens.

Improve the Great Chain of Sarvos.d: The upgrade carried a special costing of 100 white granite, 300 crowns in labour and one year to complete. Giacomo Corvinoscuro supplied the bulk of the resources, delivering 25 wains of white granite and money after each season from Winter Solstice 386YE to Autumn Equinox 387YE, which covered the full 100 wains of granite. Smaller donations of money came from Richardo Glostari di Sarvos, Rebecca Fabbro di Sarvos, Rhys Nighthaven, Alvaro Nocciola Di Tassato, Magdalena Teyhard von Holberg, Karrak and Farren Silver Streams. Once complete, the Great Chain was upgraded to a rank two fortification.

The League.t: The League's defences in its city of Sarvos were strengthened, with Sarvos citizens among those who helped pay for the upgrade.

Improve the Great Chain of Sarvos.o: In Winter 386YE the Master of the Koboldi, Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, announced a commission to improve the Great Chain, the fortification in Sarvos. It was funded over the following year and completed, raising the Great Chain to a rank two fortification.

Sarvos.t: The Great Chain in Sarvos was upgraded to a rank two fortification once the year-long work was complete.

Improve the vale of Orieb.d: Proposed by Karsk and seconded by Miekarova, the motion expanded Orieb as set out in the Thousands or more wind of fortune, using a single commission slot. It cost 10 wains of mithril, 10 wains of white granite and 6 thrones in labour (raised from 5 because the site lies in a marsh), and takes three months to build. After the Summer Solstice the materials and money were supplied, chiefly by Krasivit Buhkova, with further crowns and granite from Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov, Velko Perunovich Razoradze, Fintan Nighthaven, Sławomir Rabovich Bolotstrazh and Triska Markova. Once complete, the Merchant-Boyar of the Stinking Market gains 5 crowns a season and two new ministry tracks offering magic weapons and armour, and herbs from Ossium's eastern forests.

Varushka.t: Varushkan senators proposed the motion and Varushkan citizens largely paid for it, gaining a first true vale in the Drownbark and a richer Merchant-Boyar of the Stinking Market.

Improve the vale of Orieb.o: In Summer 385YE the Senate passed a motion to fully improve the town of Orieb and its Stinking Market in Ossium, establishing the first true vale of the Drownbark Forest, funded entirely by Varushkans.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: The Drownbark Forest is to receive its first true vale at Orieb, a three-month build in marshland that drove the labour cost up to 6 thrones.

Ossium.t: Ossium gains an expanded Orieb, whose Stinking Market will offer magic arms and armour and herbs from the territory's eastern forests once construction is complete.

In Virtue and Reason.d: Delivered by the civil service to citizens across the Empire and beyond, the address argued in Virtue that eradicating another culture could never be a true Legacy or Inspiration, and that Jotun children are not monsters to be scourged. In Reason, it held that slaughtering civilians escalates war into a struggle for survival, whereas wars are won when foes know they are beaten. Lisabetta praised the response to her coronation call, noting that the Valiant Pegasus had become an army of physicks, and commended Raewynn Farkas's proposed Conclave order, the Silver Chalice, devoted to magical healing. She also named the Generals of seven armies who had ordered their troops to spare civilians.

Jotun.t: The Throne acknowledged that the Mournwold campaign had dealt a terrible blow to Jotun armies but had also killed many Jotun non-combatants, and declared that the children of the Jotun are not monsters to be scourged, calling them future citizens and allies.

Navarr.t: The Navarr Raewynn Farkas was singled out for praise for her plan to found the Silver Chalice, a new Conclave order dedicated to using magic to heal body and mind in partnership with Imperial healers.

In Virtue and Reason.o: Imperatrix Lisabetta used her power to address the Empire to condemn the heavy civilian toll of the previous season's war in the Mournwold and to urge that ruthless tactics be reserved for enemy armies, not ordinary people.

Mournwold.t: Fighting in the Jotun-held Mournwold the previous season killed far more civilians who till the soil and raise families than soldiers, prompting the Throne's call to stop targeting non-combatants there.

In brightest day.d: The enchantment drove artists to new heights and moved everyone to celebrate their nation's art, with a flourishing unseen since Empress Richilde. Until it faded, Hallowings of Richilde were two points stronger. The Senate could commission galleries, museums and performance spaces as great works costing 15 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood and 5 Thrones in labour. Each would give 30 Synod votes and 15 liao to Pride congregations in its territory if finished before the Summer Solstice; otherwise it would be a folly. Civilian Commissioners could not build them. House Bourné revealed six raiment schemata, one for each realm, which any Imperial artisan could learn in Sarvos.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Abraham of Bastion appears in the opening fiction, tackling his distracted comrade out of the path of a javelin.

Imperial Orcs.t: Kalpaheim was among the cities where art flourished, and Blackspear Tak features in the opening fiction, shielding his companions in battle.

The Brass Coast.t: Siroc saw a marked flowering of the arts, and the fiction recalls how Empress Richilde won over the Freeborn senators of the Erigo, Riqueza and Guerra with honest words.

The League.t: All four League cities saw an unprecedented artistic flourishing, and the Sarvosan House Bourné revealed six ritual-robe schemata through the League broadsheet The Looking Glass.

The Marches.t: Meade was named among the cities that saw a flowering of artistic expression and interest in the arts.

Wintermark.t: Even Gildenheim shared in the Empire-wide surge of artistic expression and pride in national art.

In brightest day.o: After the Autumn Equinox a powerful Night enchantment settled over the whole Empire, inspiring artists and stirring national Pride, with the effect strongest in the Empire's cities. It gave the Senate a rare chance to commission Pride-focused great works, and led Sarvos's House Bourné to reveal six new ritual-robe schemata.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: only through the name of Abraham of Bastion, a soldier in the opening fiction.

Hahnmark.t: Gildenheim was noted, perhaps surprisingly, as one of the cities where interest in the arts flourished.

Madruga.t: Siroc saw a marked flourishing of artistic expression under the enchantment's influence.

Mitwold.t: Meade was among the cities where the enchantment's effect on art and artists was particularly marked.

Sarvos.t: The city flourished artistically, and the wealthy guild House Bourné opened its estate to any Imperial artisan wishing to learn its six new raiment schemata.

Skarsind.t: Kalpaheim was named among the cities that saw an unprecedented flourishing of artistic expression.

Tassato.t: As one of the League's four cities it shared in the artistic flourishing, and the fiction recalls a play about Empress Richilde staged in a Tassato theatre.

In each line lies another line.d: In Greenwall, Eisa Winterborn and the Autumn herald Blade Quencher were advancing to destroy the Imperial spy network. Holding a rotten palisade at Jarlsward for an hour would save it, and killing the herald would stop a planned fane at the Well of Whispers. At Broker's Wynd, Igya Olgafsdottir was raising a fortress with keystones from Cathan Canae; destroying them would delay it and let the Moonsilver Prince loose forest creatures. A Spring regio there could also be used for rituals, or given to Surut. In Ottermire, the Empire could stop a Jotun causeway towards Mitwold by rousing the marshwalker Old Marjoram, and could seize the traitor Bushel Sykes.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: local folklore recalls that the first Marchers came to the Bregas marshes from Dawn, and the Knight-Protector of Spring, Jasper Hunter scion De Beaumont, is named as responsible for the Kay's Lament conjunction.

Jotun.t: Jotun forces under Eisa Winterborn, Igya Olgafsdottir and their Fisher allies were pressing their gains in Skallahn, Liathaven and Bregasland, and each was open to an Imperial strike that could cost them their fane, their fortress or their causeway.

Navarr.t: Liathaven, now wholly under Jotun control, was the scene of a planned Jotun fortress. Surut's heralds offered the Navarr egregore to burn Liaven's Glen in return for the Spring regio, and an artefact found by fallen Navarri vates could make Thunderous Tread of the Trees easier to cast.

The Brass Coast.t: A Jotun fortress in Liaven's Glen would threaten Kahraman, either as a springboard for invasion or as a base for raiders striking at the important mines and quarries of northern Kahraman.

The Marches.t: Mathilda Fisher and her Jotun allies were building a military causeway through Bregasland towards Oddmire in Mitwold, aided by the traitor Bushel Sykes. A Liathaven fortress might also threaten the Mournwold, but the Empire could rouse Old Marjoram or bring Sykes to justice to stop the rot.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the page does not refer to Varushka or its people directly; it is linked only through its holding of Ossium.

Wintermark.t: A Jotun fane at the Well of Whispers would sit right on the border of Sermersuaq. The destruction of the Greenwall spy network would also strip the advantages held by armies crossing from Sermersuaq or Kallavesa.

In each line lies another line.o: At the Winter Solstice 384YE, prognosticators identified three major conjunctions on the Sunday morning that offered Imperial heroes the chance to fight the Jotun in Skallahn, Liathaven or Bregasland. The Military Council was to choose between them at the Friday muster.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: Sot's 'Ole in Ottermire was the conjunction target. Rough music there could rouse Old Marjoram to wreck the causeway, and the traitor Bushel Sykes could be taken at the Oathstone.

Liathaven/Liaven's Glen.t: Broker's Wynd held Igya's three keystone stockades and the strong Spring regio of the Circle of Unending Growth. Surut offered to burn the whole region to ash if granted dominion over the regio.

Mitwold/Oddmire.t: Once the Otterway causeway was complete, Oddmire would be under threat from the Jotun, who could pour into the region and lay claim to Odd's End.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: Mentioned in passing: the fortress in Tanikipari that still bears Igya Olgafsdottir's name is noted as lost to the Jotun.

Skallahn/Greenwall.t: Greenwall was the scene of the battle at Jarlsward, where heroes could hold an old palisade to save the spy network near the Well of Whispers and stop Blade Quencher from taking up residence there.

Bregasland.t: Jotun and Fisher forces were widening the Otterway into a military causeway towards Mitwold. Imperial heroes could reach Sot's 'Ole to rouse Old Marjoram against it and capture the turncoat Bushel Sykes at the Oathstone.

Brocéliande.t: A conjunction to Kay's Lament in the vallorn offered the chance to recover the Tairiscint na Foraoise, a potent boon for Thunderous Tread of the Trees found by Gwendolyn Sixthstep, though it was guarded by vallornspawn and at least one massive monstrosity.

Kahraman.t: A completed Jotun fortress in neighbouring Liathaven could serve as a springboard for invading Kahraman, or let raiders threaten the mines and quarries of its north.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: armies crossing into Skallahn from Kallavesa would lose their advantages if the spy network fell, and a Kallavesi ritual from Empress Teleri's reign is said to have quietened the Bregas marshwalkers.

Liathaven.t: Igya Olgafsdottir was laying keystone-anchored foundations for a fortress at Broker's Wynd. The Empire could destroy the keystones, use or surrender the Spring regio there, curse the territory with Thunderous Tread, or kill Igya herself.

Mitwold.t: The Jotun causeway from Bregasland would let their armies pour into Oddmire and invade Mitwold more swiftly unless the Empire destroyed it.

Mournwold.t: A Jotun fortress in Liaven's Glen, on Liathaven's eastern glades bordering the Mourn, could act as a springboard for a potential attack into the Mournwold.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not named on the page and has no stated role in these events.

Sermersuaq.t: A powerful Autumn fane at the Well of Whispers would sit right on Sermersuaq's border. Losing the Greenwall spy network would also remove the advantages of armies crossing from Sermersuaq into Skallahn.

Skallahn.t: Eisa Winterborn and Blade Quencher were advancing on Greenwall to destroy the Imperial spy network. Holding them for an hour would preserve the network and its benefits, and killing the herald would prevent a fane at the Well of Whispers.

Tromsa.t: If the Greenwall network fell, the Jarl of Kierheim would use the intelligence to destroy the Empire's planned spy network in Tromsa before it was completed. Igya Olgafsdottir is named as daughter of the Jarl of Tromsa.

In good company.d: Nearly fifty thousand alliance troops assaulted about thirty-five thousand Jotun at the mithril mine, which fell after a week. The Thule Shard of Winter then seized several hundred thralls and their mithril, angering many Winterfolk. The Suaq Wastes fell next, and more than four thousand died across the campaign. Sermersuaq became Imperial again, but the Senate must still assign it to a nation and allocate the mine. Igya Olgafsdottir was upgrading Olgafsdottirshal and the Fortress of Kalant. Heroes could destroy the Stonetoothed Obelisks to delay the work, kill Jotun champions Eisa Winterborn or Yanya Uranduln, rescue a Thule warlock or a hylje hostage, or intercept a spear meant for Hayaak.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Summer Storm, whose general voiced disgust at fighting alongside slavers, helped break the Jotun line at the mine. The Weigher of Worth was asked by Jaheris's heralds to arrange the interception of the Spear of Bounty.

Jotun.t: The Jotun lost the Pride of Ikka's Tears and the Suaq Wastes, along with many thralls and much mithril taken by the Thule. They fell back to strongly fortified halls in Tanikipari and Stark that Igya Olgafsdottir was racing to expand.

The Marches.t: The Marcher army the Drakes fought in the assault on Suaq Fount, its general framing the campaign as a way to draw Jotun forces away from Bregasland.

Thule.t: Three enchanted Thule armies and the garrison of the Citadel of Silver and Bone were the deciding factor in the victory. They also enslaved Jotun thralls and kept seized mithril, and they needed the Empire to recover the captured warlock Hustavok if they were to enchant their armies this season.

Wintermark.t: The Bloodcloaks helped retake the Suaq homeland, and Wintermark heroes cleared the last defenders from the mine. Sermersuaq and the mithril mine still awaited Senate assignment and allocation, while the hylje's continued aid to Wintermark depended on rescuing Koskinen.

In good company.o: In Summer 384YE the Imperial and Thule alliance drove the Jotun from Suaq Fount and Suaq Wastes, recapturing the Pride of Ikka's Tears and returning Sermersuaq to Imperial hands, though the Jotun still held fortified positions in Tanikipari and Stark. The page also set out a Sentinel Gate battle in Tanikipari and three conjunction opportunities.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The Thule Citadel of Silver and Bone supplied Summer-touched warriors to the alliance, and the captured thralls and mithril were sent back there. Because the Thule hold these peaks, the Empire's grip on Sermersuaq remained precarious.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: The retreating Jotun fell back here, where work on the Fortress of Kalant was too far advanced to stop. Conjunctions led to the Flat Hills to recover Hustavok and to White Plume Rocks, where Koskinen was held.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: After a week-long assault the alliance captured the Pride of Ikka's Tears, freeing several dozen Suaq miners. The mine was left empty of mithril, and the Senate must now decide whether it will be Imperial or national.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: Ominous northern lights blazed over the Wastes as the alliance overran newly built Jotun villages and drove the orcs out, with the Thule taking any thralls left behind as slaves.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: The alliance took outlying areas but stalled before Igya Olgafsdottir's fortified halls, including Olgafsdottirshal. A battle was offered to destroy the Stonetoothed Obelisks, delay its expansion, and possibly capture and complete the castle for the Empire.

Skallahn/Greenwall.t: Mentioned in passing: the hylje scout Koskinen was captured while leading Wintermark heroes out of Greenwall.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes' general said fighting the Jotun in Sermersuaq would help save Marcher land unless the Jotun drew forces from Bregasland.

Hahnmark.t: The artisans of Runegrott rallied the people of Hahnmark to create up to six ritual staffs, a gift from Wintermark for the battle in Tanikipari.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the alliance was described as being between the Empire and Otkodov, and Thule strategy and concerns were to go through the Ambassador to Otkodov.

Sermersuaq.t: Spring magic kept the land flourishing as the alliance retook Suaq Fount and Suaq Wastes, making the territory Imperial once more. The Jotun still held Tanikipari and Stark, and losing a single region would cost the Empire the territory again.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: the hylje had helped Imperial units escape after the earlier raid on Skallahn, and Koskinen was captured while doing so.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun siege engineer Igya Olgafsdottir is the eldest child of the Jarl of Tromsa.

Tsirku.t: A Jotun party under the ghodi Allok Surefoot had recovered the Spear of Bounty from the Grave of the Giants, an ice-cavern on the shore of Nutjuitoq, intending to give it to Hayaak.

In harmony and unison.d: Grandmaster Elagabala chose the site of Atun's landing for the order's grand lodge. The design centres on an enormous weirwood vessel, proposed name Elagabala's Vision, beside a basilica to the Way and a pier into the Catazar. The commission costs 20 white granite, 15 mithril, 65 weirwood and 300 crowns, with upkeep of 5 thrones. Once built it would add 15 mana crystals to the Conclave font each season, cheapen the Grandmaster's mana, raise congregation investment in Necropolis, let Highguard support one extra navy, and supply true liao each solstice. The Paragon's Voice Chapter and the Black Tablet offered further benefits, conditional on an interdiction and a declaration of concord respectively. The basilica might later be consecrated or expanded into a cathedral.

Grendel.t: The coastal site was acknowledged as an obvious Grendel target, and Elagabala's Vision would be vulnerable to Grendel navies whenever it was at sea, though the Grendel are often loath to destroy valuable things.

Highguard.t: The lodge would celebrate the Highborn role in bringing the Way to the world and their seafaring past, permanently allowing Highguard to raise and support one additional navy once it was built. The vessel could accompany any Highborn navy to give spiritual succour.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: they are not named, though the threat to the Golden Pyramid lodge in Mareave came from the orcs of the Broken Shore.

In harmony and unison.o: The Conclave requested, and Imperial magicians prepared, plans for a Grand Lodge of the Sevenfold Path at Sanctuary in Sanctuary Sands, Necropolis, honouring the paragon Atun's voyage to the continent. The great work still had to be commissioned by the Senate and built.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Pyramid's grand lodge in Clisearn had been protected by the Military Council, which locals cited as reason not to fear for the new site.

Necropolis/Coursmouth.t: Mentioned in passing: the fortress of Reumah's Rest overlooking the cliffs in Coursmouth was cited as reassurance against threats to the coastal site.

Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand.t: Sanctuary, at or just inland from Atun's landing site, was chosen for the planned grand lodge, to the delight of its people. The plans include a basilica to the Way, a pier and a great moored vessel that could evacuate magicians and locals if the region were seriously threatened.

Bay of Catazar.t: Once complete, Elagabala's Vision could sail along the coast to any Imperial territory on the Bay in a season, but it would be clumsy and vulnerable to attack on these waters. A pier from the lodge would also extend into the Catazar.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: a steward's lesson recalls that the First Empress went on to found the Empire at Anvil in Casinea.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the recently completed Golden Pyramid grand lodge here was briefly threatened by the orcs of the Broken Shore before the Military Council secured it.

Necropolis.t: The territory would host the proposed grand lodge, which would raise the level of investment of every congregation in Necropolis until the vessel sailed elsewhere. The Black Tablet offered to seek a relic from the Necropolis for Whispers through the Black Gate.

In the Court of Far Horizons.d: Magistrate Abraham's analysis found the manifesto covered maritime trade only. Overland trade, and fleet espionage or warfare, fell outside it. If passed, the sodality would gain the power to set tariffs, though the Court advised softening the 'never hindered' wording. Five titles would automatically become sodality appointments, and others, including Bourse seats and most ambassadors, could be transferred by Senate motion. The Fellowship of the Purple Sails would join en masse and share docking rights at Hayden if tariffs were granted. The Bedelaar Huisbaas offered up to 12 thrones a season for control of trade titles. The City of Salt and Sail offered a yearly message to anyone if the sodality appointed all ambassadors.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the leader of a named Druj sept is given as an example recipient of the City of Salt and Sail's yearly message.

Grendel.t: The Grendel are named as a mercantile power for whom trade matters in foreign relations. The Ambassador to the Grendel is among the posts the Senate could transfer to the new sodality, despite the ongoing war mentioned at Caricomare's docks.

The League.t: Caricomare's rebuilt docks frame the story, as Fleet Master Giovanni von Temeschwar receives word from the Purple Sails. The Mayor of Caricomare could become a sodality appointment, and the Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market would come under a broader trade sodality.

Thule.t: The Empire's extensive trade with the Thule of Otkodov is entirely overland, so it falls outside the proposed remit. The Ambassador to Otkodov is the one envoy the sodality could not be given.

In the Court of Far Horizons.o: In Summer 388YE, at Emperor Vesna's request, the Constitutional Court appraised the proposed Imperial sodality, the Court of Far Horizons, finding it would govern maritime trade and receive the power to set tariffs. Three groups offered support if the Senate backed it with real powers.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Mentioned in passing: the Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market is listed among the overland trade titles that would need re-evaluation if the sodality's remit were widened to all foreign trade.

Holberg.t: Overland trade with the Sand Fishers of Holberg lies outside the maritime manifesto. It would come under the sodality only if the manifesto were broadened to cover all foreign trade.

Otkodov.t: Imperial trade with Otkodov involves no fleets, which is why its ambassador is excluded from any transfer to the Court of Far Horizons.

In the charnel pit.d: Heilyn Bronwen's Rest's calling let the Prosperity Assembly name a territory each summit for a year, leading to costly chances to help it rebuild. Ada of House Meliora's Courage calling sought to free those scarred by Druj auras of fear. The Silent Bell report on fear, held by Earl Adel de Òrdraig and Gaelen Embercast, would be published by the Autumn Equinox, and a lecture, 'Courage in Convalescence', would gather accounts from formerly oppressed peoples. Supporters of the Proffered Hand proposed First Light Refuge at Hope's Rest. Esther urged a General Assembly mandate to let Druj fear-craft die with them; without a greater majority, Wintermark, Varushka and Urizen could still pursue it.

Dawn.t: The proposed First Light Refuge would be built at Hope's Rest in the Dawnish-held Barrens, serving as the first stop for people escaping or rescued from the Druj.

Druj.t: The Druj's methods of creating auras of fear are the subject of a Silent Bell report and of a debate over whether the Empire should seek the secret lore of the Buruk Tepel or let it die with them.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named directly; Grendel-held Feroz is cited as still in poverty after Governor Rahab's rule, and roughly a thousand people were rescued from Leen.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule-held Otkodov is listed among lands where the Empire might one day build further refuges if it sought to liberate their people.

Urizen.t: If Esther's mandate passes without a greater majority, Urizen would still gain chances to acquire the skills of the Buruk Tepel.

Varushka.t: Varushka would be unaffected by Esther's proposed mandate unless it passes with a greater majority, keeping open its chances to learn the Buruk Tepel's skills.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark would retain the chance to acquire Buruk Tepel lore unless Esther's mandate to forgo it is enacted with a greater majority.

In the charnel pit.o: Following the Spring Equinox, the Prosperity and Courage assemblies' highest callings opened pastoral opportunities to aid damaged territories and those who had suffered under Druj fear. A proposed refuge for escaped Druj slaves was also put forward, and Esther of the Watchers of Belial urged the Synod to forgo the Druj's secret lore.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: Hope's Rest was proposed as the site of First Light Refuge, a hub of the Proffered Hand Network close to the Mallum, overseen by a new Lantern Keeper appointed by the Courage Assembly.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Freeborn and other nations on the Bay of Catazar are helping roughly a thousand people rescued from Leen come to terms with their ordeal.

Feroz.t: Feroz is named as still languishing in poverty after Governor Rahab's corrupt rule, making it a possible focus for the Prosperity Assembly's aid.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is listed among lands on whose borders new refuges might be built if the Empire ever sought to liberate their people.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named; the page refers only generally to eastern lands left in ruins by the Druj and to peoples learning to live free of miasma.

Sarangrave.t: Ada of House Meliora's calling explicitly aims to liberate the sept of the Sarangrave from their cruel Druj captors by learning to combat auras of fear.

The Barrens.t: A charitable edifice, First Light Refuge, was proposed for Hope's Rest in the Barrens to receive and outfit ex-Druj people, costing 12 white granite and 36 crowns with an upkeep of six thrones a season.

In the end everything collides.d: Yevgeni Katzev's treaty guaranteed Thule holdings in the Silver Peaks and Lestazny and ceded Crow's Ridge, which a Thule army occupied without bloodshed. The Thule agreed to ransom Imperial slaves, with talks due at the Winter Solstice, and Grand Warlock Fljajokull was to visit Anvil to discuss military aid in Ossium. The Thule rejected the Senate's claim to Sungold Pass, though both sides agreed not to build until it is settled. The Thule demanded reparations after the hungry dead in Sermersuaq killed twenty orcs. Up to a hundred Great Forest orcs, along with a few briars, joined Navarr stridings. A Grendel envoy sought to ransom Commander Innevia.

Druj.t: The Thule agreed in principle to an alliance against the Druj, promising strategic information, and sent a grand warlock to discuss direct military aid against them in Ossium.

Grendel.t: Grendel privateers continued raiding in the Bay of Catazar, while an emissary of Salt Lord Moorvain of Vorlach headed to Anvil to negotiate the ransom of Commander Innevia and her surrendered troops.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the many Highborn becoming pilgrims after Highguard's grand sacrifice are contrasted with the Great Forest orcs walking the trods.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs lost Crow's Ridge in Skarsind to the Thule under the treaty, and their few settlers there moved south. Some resented it, but most felt they would not complain when Wintermark and Varushka had also given up land.

Jotun.t: The former Jotun thralls in the Mournwold went on farming and paying taxes, though a murder case and Hap the Soft's dismissal of the magistrates caused some unease.

Navarr.t: At the invitation of the Navarr National Assembly, perhaps a hundred Great Forest orcs and a few briars joined Navarr stridings on the trods. Meanwhile, Navarr artisans captured by the Thule remained a sticking point in the slave negotiations.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: following Eska Crowspeaker's mandate, well-meaning folk from the Brass Coast travelled to the Mourn to help thralls, who insisted they were farmers, not slaves.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel armada off Sarvos is noted, and well-meaning citizens of Tassato went to offer succour to the Mournwold thralls.

The Marches.t: Anna Pernn's statement led thralls to be advised to take disputes to the Mournwold senator, who has no power to resolve criminal cases. Some Mournwolders still decried the Empire's "appeasement" of the orcs.

Thule.t: The Thule gained Crow's Ridge and agreed to ransom Imperial slaves and share intelligence on the Druj. They also disputed the Empire's claim to Sungold Pass and demanded reparations for orcs killed by the hungry dead in Sermersuaq.

Varushka.t: Varushkan soldiers watched over Sungold Pass after the Senate claimed it for Opascari and faced a Thule force across the pass. Varushka is also among the nations that ceded land to the Thule.

Wintermark.t: The treaty confirmed Thule control of the Silver Peaks, and the last Wintermark halls in Crow's Ridge had already been abandoned. The hungry dead in Sermersuaq provoked Thule outrage and a demand for reparations.

In the end everything collides.o: In the autumn of 382YE the new Thule treaty took effect: Crow's Ridge passed bloodlessly to the Thule, and talks began on slaves, Druj intelligence and a disputed claim to Sungold Pass. Meanwhile Great Forest orcs began walking the trods with the Navarr, the Mournwold thralls kept the status quo, and a Grendel emissary sought to ransom captured troops.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: The Thule claimed that the Traveller lies partly in Kógur in Sküld and that Sungold Pass sits on their side of the mountain.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: The Thule army that took Crow's Ridge marched south from Urdur, and new garrisons now overlook the passes into Urdur.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The treaty guaranteed Thule control of the Silver Peaks, but the hungry dead attacked two patrols and a mining settlement there, killing twenty orcs.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Crow's Ridge was ceded to the Thule and occupied without bloodshed. They are now restoring Crow's Keep and garrisoning the passes north and west.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: A band of Great Forest orcs, apparently after receiving Vitality of Rushing Water, cautiously explored the vallorn in Sweetglades, unsettling the local steadings.

Volodmartz/Opascari.t: The Senate asserted that Sungold Pass belongs to Opascari. Varushkan soldiers and a Thule force are now camped across the pass from each other while the dispute awaits negotiation.

Bay of Catazar.t: Independent Grendel privateers continued to harry merchant shipping in the bay, though Imperial magic proved more than a match for them.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is not named; it is touched only by the general news of Great Forest orcs joining Navarr stridings on the trods.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Vuk the Wolfeater, the senator for Karov, raised the Senate motion claiming Sungold Pass for the Empire.

Karsk.t: The treaty guaranteed Thule control of the land they hold in Lestazny. Runesmiths and artisans captured during the Thule occupation of Treji remained a contested part of the slave negotiations.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Commander Innevia and her Grendel troops surrendered to Will Talbot during clean-up operations in Madruga, and a ransom emissary is now coming.

Mournwold.t: The thralls in the Mournwold kept working their land despite tensions over a murder case and an influx of outsiders trying to help "escaped slaves". The status quo held, but their issues, especially with the Way, remained unresolved.

Ossium.t: A Thule grand warlock was due at Anvil to discuss with the Military Council possible direct Thule military aid against the Druj in Ossium.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov's orcs sent an army south to occupy Crow's Ridge and agreed to begin slave ransom talks at the Winter Solstice. Their embassy formally rejected the Imperial claim to Sungold Pass.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel armada off the coast of Sarvos is noted as already documented elsewhere.

Sermersuaq.t: The treaty guaranteed Thule control of their lands in the Silver Peaks, but the hungry dead rising in Sermersuaq killed Thule orcs, prompting a demand for reparations.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind lost Crow's Ridge to the Thule under the treaty, and the few Imperial Orc settlers there withdrew south.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: some well-meaning citizens of Tassato travelled to the Mourn to offer succour to the thralls.

Therunin.t: The news of the Navarr invitation reached the Great Forest orcs in Therunin, and the first of them joined stridings there. One band also began exploring the vallorn-infested Sweetglades.

Volodmartz.t: The Senate declared Sungold Pass and the Traveller part of Opascari, but the Thule disputed this, and the two forces now face each other across the pass.

In the flat field.d: Lily Guildenstern made the breadbasket available for Marcher festivals. A Marcher Assembly mandate with 25 liao would see households share it with the thralls and invite them to Upwold, Mitwold and Bregasland for the harvest, reducing the liao needed for the egregore to bond them. Whittle, which resisted the Jotun for thirty years through Hatred, answered the Assembly's offer through Sally Thatcher with defiance. Priests think about a score of ringleaders hold Whittle together. Options presented: a Senate-ordered magistrates' investigation, a Silent Bell inquiry with grey pilgrims backed by an Assembly of Nine mandate, provoking an uprising for armies to crush, or sanctuary in Tassato. Separately, young thralls who wish to fight may join the Imperial Orcs.

Imperial Orcs.t: Bloodcrow Udoo's mandate made clear that any young former thrall who wishes to fight may join the Imperial Orcs, though few are expected to do so; their descendants would come to hear both Imperial Orc and Jotun ancestors.

Jotun.t: The Jotun former thralls of the Mournwold, who honour their ancestors with household harvest shrines, may be invited to feast with Marchers, while the Jotun conquest of Bregasland continues to loom over the Marches.

The League.t: The League's bishops are considering Merchant-Prince Mariana's proposal to offer the Whittle folk sanctuary in Tassato, where some of their kin already live.

The Marches.t: The Marcher Assembly could pass a mandate urging households to share the breadbasket with the thralls, while its offer to let Whittle recant Hatred was flatly refused, forcing a choice over how to deal with the village.

In the flat field.o: The Marchers' efforts to bring the Mournwold's Jotun former thralls into their nation continued, with a proposed Synod mandate to share the breadbasket's bounty with the thralls at the Autumn Wassail. The Hate-following village of Whittle rejected the Marcher Assembly's final offer to recant, leaving the Empire to choose how to deal with its ringleaders.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Mestra is home to Little Mournwold, a Marcher enclave of Whittle folk who never returned home, and the proposed destination for those offered sanctuary in Tassato.

Bregasland.t: Despite the Jotun conquest, Marchers in beleaguered Bregasland celebrate the Wassail in defiance, and the thralls may be invited there as harvest guests; the spirit of wassail could help bring orc and human together if the Military Council chooses to fight at Bill Sabbey.

Mitwold.t: If the breadbasket mandate is passed, Mournwold thralls would be invited to Mitwold as guests for the harvest festival.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold is where the thralls may be welcomed to Wassail feasts, and where the Hate-following village of Whittle stands defiant, facing possible investigation, a Silent Bell hunt, armed suppression or relocation.

Tassato.t: Tassato has been proposed as a sanctuary for the Whittle folk, an option now being discussed by the League's bishops.

Upwold.t: If the breadbasket mandate is passed, Mournwold thralls would be invited to Upwold as guests for the harvest festival.

In the flesh.d: The Earl claimed Penni DuBlanche, later Penni the White, defeated it and tested it into his house with the task of making him Monarch of Dawn. It offered to let its favour be magically examined. Invoking hospitality, it named Enchantress de Carsenere guest of honour at a tourney: a grand melee, then a single-elimination contest of eight knights from Anvil against eight of its allied Barrens knights. It added 50 to the Golden Sun's resupply and was winning over some soldiers, though the General could forbid fraternisation. Hayaak challenged the Knight-Protector of Summer to a hunt for one of the Earl's favours, and Tuki of the Little Bones sought to meet Alistair de Vere.

Dawn.t: Dawn's earls rejected the manticore as Dawnish, but the debate continued among the people. The Earl drew support from some Golden Sun soldiers and minor Barrens houses, the Dawnish Assembly had a chance to speak out, and the Knight-Protector of Summer faced Hayaak's challenge.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are not named, though a conjunction opened to the Cave of Bones in Skarsind, which they held.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the herald of Jaheris may be the same one recently seen in Sermersuaq, though she denies it.

In the flesh.o: In spring 387YE the manticore known as the Earl of the Groves published an open letter to the people of Dawn, claiming its nobility through Penni the White and inviting Dawnish knights to a tourney at its manse in the Untrod Groves. It was also bolstering the Golden Sun with vassals and recruits, while eternals and heralds moved against it.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: Tuki of the Little Bones, a herald of Wise Rangara nesting among ancient bones in the Cave of Bones here, invited Alistair de Vere through a conjunction to talk about the Earl.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: The Earl had courted minor Dawnish houses here with talk of glory and ambition, and some had begun to accept it as a peer.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: Minor Dawnish houses here had been approached by the Earl, and some had begun to treat the manticore as a fellow noble.

The Barrens/The Untrod Groves.t: The Earl of the Groves called its tourney at Tournament Square by its manse in the heart of the Groves, reachable by a conjunction, with all spectators welcome under guest-law.

Astolat.t: A lone herald of Hayaak came to the Castle of Astolat to deliver the Bandit-King's challenge to the Knight-Protector of Summer.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the herald of Jaheris involved may be the one lately seen in Sermersuaq, though she denies it.

Skarsind.t: A conjunction opened to the Cave of Bones in Skarsind, where Tuki of the Little Bones waited to discuss the Earl of the Groves with Alistair de Vere.

The Barrens.t: The Earl of the Groves held its tourney in the Untrod Groves and drew minor Barrens houses into alliance, supplying eight of their knights to face Anvil's champions.

In the garden of defiance.d: Most of Holmauer Park withered, though the Imperial Menagerie, the Marcher apple grove and General Flowers' Memorial Garden were spared. Rotting vegetation fouled the waters, and League or Highborn Synod mandates were proposed to fund a clean-up. Rats driven into Holfried raised the Custodian of the Kennels' income by 72 rings a season. The Wunderkind Woods now ooze a sap usable as Winter vis, and the Senate could create titles for this orchard, a souvenir stall at the twisted Sculpture Garden, and an inspiring pavilion on the Looking Glass Lake. A menhir-ringed herb garden was proposed for the Duelling Fields. Rival mandates were also proposed to honour General Flowers or remake her garden for Empress Lisabetta.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are cited as the enemy Holberg held off for thirty years, and their reputation for disease makes the fouled waters more dangerous.

Highguard.t: Ethan of the Gilded Sceptre urged the Highborn Assembly to make amends for the mess their people helped create by funding the clean-up of Holmauer's waters, at the cost of a one-rank production penalty to every Highborn business if enacted.

The League.t: Holberg's foremost park lay blighted, and League merchant-princes, assemblies and senators were offered a mandate to clean its waters, several possible new titles and sinecures, and a mandate to remake the Memorial Garden as a flower garden for Empress Lisabetta.

The Marches.t: The Marcher apple grove and General Flowers' Memorial Garden escaped the curse, and the Marcher Assembly could send pilgrims to honour her there, while a Marcher landskeeper proposed protective menhirs and a herb garden on the Duelling Fields.

In the garden of defiance.o: After agents of the Hag Queen cursed Holmauer Park in Holberg at the Summer Solstice 383YE, the blight left fouled waters, a Winter regio, corrupted woods and statues, and a string of opportunities for the Senate and Synod to turn the disaster to advantage.

Holberg/Holfried.t: Rats driven out of the cursed park flooded Holfried in numbers unseen since 379YE, boosting demand for Georgie's House ratting dogs, while the Marcher graveyard by its southern wall was untouched.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: The park at the heart of Holmauer was cursed, its rivers fouled and the Wunderkind Woods turned into a Winter regio, leaving the sites at the centre of every proposed mandate and title.

Upwold/Ashbrook.t: Mentioned in passing: Abigail Ashill, the landskeeper who proposed the menhir ring, is described as being of Ashill, Ashbrook.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: not named, but as a Highborn territory its businesses would share the one-rank production penalty if the Highborn clean-up mandate were enacted.

Holberg.t: The city suffered the blighting of Holmauer Park and faced fouled waters and a plague of rats, but was offered mandates and Senate titles to clean up and profit from the ruin before the end of the Winter Solstice.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed menhirs drew on plans the late Richard of Holberg drew up to protect the Mourn.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the landskeeper Abigail Ashill, who proposed the menhirs on the Duelling Fields, hails from Ashill in Upwold.

In the ground.d: Adamant's herald Meon of the Chisel answered Stone Smith Gemma Brightsmith. All his aid depends on the Senate recommissioning Eastern Guard in Upwold or conceding it to him. If that is settled, he offers to raise Farstrider's Watch to an unbreakable rank-three fortification, to build an unsinkable Hall of the Kingfisher at Fisher's Rock with optional marsh-draining dykes, and to raise a sealed dolmen weakening curses on the Mournwold. All must be commissioned by the Autumn Equinox 388YE, and a Ring of the Dragon schema is offered for ilium. Tharim's knights compensated farmers for damage with Heart's Blood, and his herald Poena offered landskeepers blades, Bitter Salt and a savage army enchantment. Sadogua offered mushroom elixirs and masks to mummers.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Adamant Gate in eastern Semmerholm is cited as the standard of unbreakability for the proposed Hall of the Kingfisher.

Jotun.t: The Jotun hold Bregasland, where Adamant offers to build a fortress regardless, and they are advancing across Mitwold. Several of Tharim's boons are expected to be turned against them, and some smiths worry because Adamant has aided the Jotun in the past.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: plans for curse wards drawn up by Richard of Holberg are dismissed by Adamant's herald as relying on less reliable magics.

The Marches.t: Marcher smiths, landskeepers and mummers were each courted by a different eternal, gaining offers of great fortifications, curse wards, military enchantments and magical gifts. Much of this depends first on resolving the fate of Eastern Guard.

In the ground.o: In Winter 387YE three eternals courted the Marches. Adamant answered the Stone Smith's missive with fortification and curse-ward offers conditional on Eastern Guard, Tharim offered landskeepers boons and compensation, and Sadogua's heralds joined Wassail and offered gifts to mummers.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Adamant proposes dykes and bulwarks connected to the Hall of the Kingfisher to drain parts of the fens. This would remove the marsh quality while leaving fens in place, and the keep would remain safe even if the sea drowned the region.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Farstrider's Watch here could be improved to a rank-three fortification infused with adamant, partly paid for in weltsilver and orichalcum. It could also be consecrated to Pride with a shrine to the Ore Hills Rebels.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: A ring of sealed dolmen could be built in the western Ore Hills with Adamant's aid to weaken curses affecting the Mournwold, at the cost of altered mana production across the territory.

Bregasland.t: Although the territory is held by the Jotun, Adamant offers to help carve an unbreakable, unsinkable Hall of the Kingfisher from Fisher's Rock. Dykes could be added that would raise farm investment, and the keep could become a shrine to Loyalty honouring Bolstering Bill.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Richard of Holberg's curse ward plans are rejected by Adamant's herald.

Mitwold.t: Tharim's knights damaged Mitwold farms while hunting Agramant's servants, and the Bound King paid compensation in Heart's Blood. The Jotun are advancing across the territory, and Tharim suggests his Bitter Salt boon could help garrison Forte Fidelis.

Mournwold.t: Adamant offers to make Farstrider's Watch a majestic, unbreakable castle and to raise a sealed dolmen that would weaken curses on the territory, though its mana sites would yield bronze dragonseyes in place of some crystal mana. Sadogua's heralds flocked especially to the Mournwold's Wassail.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the Adamant Gate in eastern Semmerholm is used as a comparison for the unbreakable keep Adamant proposes.

Upwold.t: Adamant's herald met the smiths at the Woldstone and made all aid conditional on the decommissioned Eastern Guard being recommissioned or ceded to him. Tharim's knights remain camped here, and his herald Poena visited the Silent Giant seeking the landskeepers.

In the hills, the cities.d: The Axou still blamed the Empire for their losses in the failed 384YE raid on the Mountains of the Moon. They accepted reparations but refused any military cooperation. The Empire's blocking of Commonwealth and Sumaah efforts to expel Axos from the Liberty Pact was welcomed even by hostile citadels. In Kaban, Ilarch Kyther Deianeira, allied with the scholar Theodosia and advocating Nikitis Axou unification, offered to have a priest hallow one item to Understanding (Peace) for each Assembly of the Nine member who swore to bear it for a year. In return the Ilarch sought 100 doses of liao, safe conduct and a thank-you letter from the Throne. Separately, Ilarch Maxatios offered 18 crowns a wain for up to fifty wains of white granite this season and next.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj siege of the Gates of Ipotavo, lifted by the Empire, is recalled, and the Axou are said to want the Druj destroyed and might move against them if they were fatally weakened, but not in coordination with the Empire.

Grendel.t: The Grendel Paymaster Muireall's 384YE proposal of a joint raid on the Mountains of the Moon lay at the root of the Tsark Debacle, in which the Grendel suffered heavy losses after Tsark was apparently forewarned.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Ambassador to Axos is listed as Fintan Nighthaven of Navarr.

In the hills, the cities.o: In Summer 386YE, relations between the Empire and Axos remained badly damaged by the Tsark Debacle, though they were eased somewhat by the Empire's defence of Axos's place in the Liberty Pact. Two new opportunities arose: an offer of Understanding-hallowed items for the Assembly of the Nine, and an Axou bid to buy white granite.

Mountains of the Moon.t: The white granite-rich Tsark passes were the target of the failed 384YE Grendel and Axou raid, whose collapse with heavy losses still poisoned Axou relations with the Empire.

In the lonely hour.d: Dawnish, Varushkan, League and Highguard armies reinforced the Causeway, aided by the Whelpmaster's white wolves and the Bound King's black knights. The Druj fought alongside servants of Arhallogen and a new army bearing crimson brambles. They fought cautiously, relying on their Spring curse. The Empire still holds Carmine Fields and Hope's Rest and is about a fifth of the way to taking Bitter Strand, where the Druj fell back towards the damaged mithril mine at the Fangs. Following the Synod's call, and with the agreement of Dawn's troubadours, emissaries urged the subject orcs to resist the Druj. This slowed conquest and imposed penalties on most armies.

Dawn.t: The Gryphon's Pride led the assault on Bitter Strand under Garravaine De Rondell, who issued his final orders, and the Golden Sun joined them. Dawn's troubadours backed the Synod's call to free the Barrens' subject peoples, which cost Dawnish armies a three-tenths penalty to conquest.

Druj.t: The Druj failed to close the Steel Causeway and were forced to cede parts of the Bitter Strand shoreline. They fielded the Black Wind, a mysterious new crimson-bramble army and servants of Arhallogen, but fought cautiously and kept their own losses low.

Highguard.t: The Valiant Pegasus crusaded in the Barrens under Achseh, hoping to repeat the successes of Zenith and to liberate the tribes held in subjugation by the Druj.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: scattered Great Forest Orcs were left in the Barrens when most of their sept fled south into Therunin.

The League.t: The Wolves of War advanced carefully under Jean Di Sarvos, supported by free companies from Holberg, and League scouts judged the Druj at least as numerous as the Imperial soldiers.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj had been trapped in Zenith, turning the tables on the would-be tyrants of Urizen, and Urizen's armies are exempt from the conquest penalty in the Barrens.

Varushka.t: The Northern Eagle and Iron Helms pressed the Druj cautiously beside the Dawnish, pushing back the Causeway's borders and burning mounds of orc dead. Varushkan armies are exempt from the conquest penalty.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Sun marched from Sermersuaq to the Barrens.

In the lonely hour.o: In Winter 384YE Druj forces led by the Black Wind tried to break the Steel Causeway in the Barrens, but six Imperial armies beat them back and gained a small foothold in Bitter Strand. The cost was six thousand Imperial dead, and the campaign was slowed by a deliberate effort to reach the Druj's subject orcs.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: Bitter Strand was the focus of the Imperial advance. Its defences had been ruined by the storm, and the Druj ceded parts of the shoreline and fell back towards the damaged mithril mine at the Fangs.

The Barrens/Farweald.t: The ghulai's corrupting wards over the forests of Farweald struck at any Imperial forces that tried to push into the region.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: The Druj tried to recapture Hope's Rest, but the Imperial armies held it.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: Saltmarsh lies drowned beneath the Bitter Sea after the summer's magical tempest, and is now coastal rather than marsh until at least the Summer Solstice.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: free companies recruited in Holberg supported the Wolves of War, whose general vowed to push the foe further from Holberg's walls.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Sun crossed from Sermersuaq to the Barrens with the help of Autumn magic.

The Barrens.t: The Steel Causeway held against a Druj counter-attack, and the Empire gained about a fifth of Bitter Strand at a cost of six thousand dead. The territory still festers under the Rivers Run Red curse and remains largely in Druj hands.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: most of the Great Forest Orc sept fled south from the Barrens into Therunin.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were trapped and broken in Zenith, where the Granite Pillar stayed behind to cleanse the remnants.

In the tents of prosperity.d: Druj traders registered eighteen wains of mithril with the civil service and travelled to Anvil to exchange the certificates for the white granite promised by treaty. Their party also included magicians seeking Conclave business and a herb trader. Magistrates reminded citizens that the Druj are foreigners under law, so attacking, robbing or killing them is illegal. Agents of House Cudo of Redoubt offered Urizen mages three droplets of night, which lessen a Night ritual, each sold only for a set form of payment. Naomi of the Wandering Star sought a buyer for a pre-Imperial relic found near Reikos. Walter Applecart of Meade weighed offers for a magical seal skin, and Emris Oakhaven brought an ancient knife from Liathaven.

Druj.t: Druj traders came out of the Barrens with eighteen wains of mithril to trade for white granite under their treaty with the Empire, accompanied by magicians and a herb trader, and the magistrates warned that they were protected as foreigners.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a Druj trader taunted a civil servant that the Grendel claim to trust the Druj more than the Empire.

Highguard.t: Naomi of the Necropolis chapter house the Wandering Star found a pre-Imperial relic in a Highborn village near Reikos's border and sought to sell it in Anvil, ideally to a fellow Highborn, to pay her expedition debts.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: many of Emris Oakhaven's striding had been slain by the Jotun over the previous year.

Navarr.t: Emris Oakhaven, who lost his thorn sister in the Westwood, sought to sell an ancient relic from Liathaven, preferably to a Navarri who would honour its history, so that he could begin a new life as a broker.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: House Cudo began as a Holberg guild of Autumn magicians, and its arbiter keeps agents in League towns and cities reporting on markets.

Urizen.t: House Cudo of Redoubt sent agents to sell three droplets of night to Urizen mages, one each for coin, for mana and for common artisan resources, before the Conclave met.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the magical seal skin Walter Applecart was offering for sale was said to come from his last trip to Sermersuaq.

In the tents of prosperity.o: In Spring 381YE several traders headed to Anvil with valuable goods. Druj merchants came to exchange mithril for white granite, Urizen's House Cudo offered three droplets of night, and a Highborn explorer, a Marcher trader and a Navarri survivor of Liathaven each sought buyers for rare relics.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: In the vallorn-filled Westwood, where his sister Catrin died guarding the army's rear, Emris Oakhaven found the old knife he hoped to sell in Anvil.

Brocéliande.t: Tombs near the border between Reikos and Brocéliande had been disturbed by Llofir's magic, and in that area the Wandering Star recovered a pre-Imperial relic.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: House Cudo is said to have begun as a Holberg guild of Autumn magicians who emigrated to Urizen in the Second Interregnum.

Liathaven.t: Navarri who had long called Liathaven home struggled to settle elsewhere, and Emris Oakhaven brought an ancient knife from Lan Thuven to sell in Anvil.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Emris Oakhaven planned to travel to Miaren to start a new life.

Necropolis.t: The Wandering Star, a Necropolis chapter house of genealogical archivists, finally made a significant find through Naomi's expeditions.

Redoubt.t: House Cudo of Redoubt, led by its shrewd arbiter Prascylla, sent agents to Anvil to sell three droplets of night to Urizen mages.

Reikos.t: A pre-Imperial relic was recovered from a small Highborn village near Reikos's border with Brocéliande, among tombs disturbed by Llofir's magic, and a local magister confirmed it as genuine.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Walter Applecart was rumoured to have brought a magical seal skin back from his last trip to Sermersuaq.

Inextricable, indefatigable, and inevita.d: Using the Throne's power to speak to the whole Empire, carried across the land by the civil service, Emperor Vesna praised the Military Council for adding three territories in a few years: Ossium, the Barrens and most recently Mareave. The Emperor called land one of the Empire's most valuable assets, won with Imperial lives, and urged citizens to settle and live virtuously in it. Vesna denounced anyone who curses an Imperial territory to harm its citizens as no friend of the Empire, deserving the sack and sword, and applauded those in Anvil seeking a better path. Citing the Legacy of the First Empress and the Synod's expansion of doctrine, the Emperor set the ambitious goal that no corner of the Empire be anything less than a shining example of Prosperity.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is not named, but the Barrens, which it holds, is praised as one of three territories recently brought into the Empire.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Mareave, which it holds, is hailed as the most recent territory added to the Empire.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is not named, but Ossium, which it holds, is listed among the territories recently added to the Empire.

Inextricable, indefatigable, and inevita.o: In Summer 386YE Emperor Vesna addressed every Imperial citizen, celebrating the recent addition of Ossium, the Barrens and Mareave to the Empire and condemning those who curse Imperial territories. The Emperor also challenged the Empire to make every corner of its lands an example of Prosperity.

Mareave.t: The Emperor named Mareave as the most recent territory won by the Military Council, a land where lost souls might now find the Way and where citizens are urged to settle and prosper.

Ossium.t: The Emperor named Ossium as one of three territories added to the Empire in recent years, a place now offered to citizens as a new home in which to find Prosperity.

The Barrens.t: The Emperor named the Barrens among the territories recently brought into the Empire, holding it up as land won with Imperial lives that citizens should put to virtuous use.

Inkpot gods.d: Ephisis changed how Ephisis' Scale worked for the solstice and offered a Golden Market of Aggido, a vis market to be built in Anozel, Ashill or Gildenheim by wayleave. Callidus sought liao and true liao, and offered Jarmish white seed to one nation chosen by the Synod. His associate Sanvar Isk offered access to Prospero's Loom of Spells. Estavus held a fire sale of magical items, offered schema to Wintermark and proposed a fane in Proceris. Prospero offered diplomatic favours, including keeping Jarm out of the Grendel war. Flint offered a surprise attack opportunity if Axos was cut from the Liberty Pact. Mazen's boons ceased working, and Autumn boggarts spread mischief.

Grendel.t: Prospero offered to use his influence so that Jarm would stop aiding the Grendel in their coming war with the Empire. Flint revealed he had urged a surprise attack on the Grendel in Feroz, which the Military Council had declined.

Imperial Orcs.t: Golden Consortium agents had been active in Skarsind, and Needa's Hall near Gildenheim was offered as one possible site for the Golden Market of Aggido.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Estavus is described as a firm ally of the Jotun, supplying them with weapons and warriors against the Empire.

The Brass Coast.t: Golden Consortium agents had been active in Segura, and an abandoned parador in the struggling town of Anozel was offered as a possible site for the Golden Market of Aggido.

The League.t: Sanvar Isk found an anchor in Tassato Mestra for linking the Loom of Spells to the Empire. Meanwhile silver-skinned Autumn creatures harassed homesteaders in Madeiras.

The Marches.t: Golden Consortium agents had been active in Upwold, and Quick Alice offered the Grosvenor family home in Ashill as a possible site for the Golden Market of Aggido.

Urizen.t: Scores of Estavus's heralds emerged around Zenith. The Forgemistress proposed a Fane of Shadows in Proceris, with Urizen to appoint an Architect who could buy her heralds' magical items.

Wintermark.t: Estavus offered Wintermark's artisans five schema for sale during the solstice, on the strict condition that any purchased were added to Runesmith's Law at Runegrott.

Inkpot gods.o: In Summer 385YE the Bounty of the Brilliant Broker drew heralds of Ephisis, Estavus, Callidus, Prospero and Basileus Flint into the Empire, bringing a wide range of trades, commissions and bargains. The heralds also brought news that Mazen had been destroyed and that the Lictors had fallen silent.

Tassato/Madeiras.t: Mobs of silver-skinned realm-creatures in the forests demanded pay for unrequested work and carted off homesteaders' crates, nails and tools.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Sanvar Isk located a site here to anchor the Loom of Spells. Connecting it required one hundred ingots or measures during the Summer Solstice.

Upwold/Ashbrook.t: Ashbrook was a permitted location for the Golden Market of Aggido, via the Grosvenor family home in Ashill, which was in need of repairs that would accommodate mithril tie beams.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Estavus was intrigued by the nightwoven marshes and proposed a Fane of Shadows here, costing 10 wains of mithril, 10 rings of ilium and 20 crowns, if her heralds were allowed to study them.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Flint's heralds had proposed a surprise attack on the Grendel in Feroz last season, which the Military Council declined.

Hahnmark.t: Estavus offered schema on condition that any purchased were added to the body of lore kept at Runegrott under Runesmith's Law.

Segura.t: Golden Consortium agents had been active in Segura and identified an abandoned parador in Anozel as a candidate site for their vis market.

Skarsind.t: Golden Consortium agents had been active in Skarsind. Needa's Hall, a ruined meadery near Gildenheim, was offered as a candidate site for the Golden Market.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Flint's heralds cited Kaliact's betrayal of the Grendel in Spiral as an example of profitable treachery.

Tassato.t: An Autumn regio in Tassato Mestra could anchor the Loom of Spells, while realm-creatures in Madeiras demanded pay for unasked-for work.

Upwold.t: Golden Consortium agents had been active in Upwold. The Grosvenor home in the charcoal-burning village of Ashill was offered as a candidate market site.

Zenith.t: Estavus's heralds emerged in large numbers around Zenith in response to the Autumn Archmage's plea for help rebuilding, and a fane was proposed in Proceris.

Into the spin.d: The Civil Service had the Speaker raise a motion of allocation, open to any of the ten nations, and the Senate could also allocate the Fundindelve mithril mine. Four challenges were identified: certain Grendel attempts at reclamation; an orc population with no interest in joining any nation; arid land unable to support an army; and remoteness, reachable by land only through Spiral. Former Salt Lord Ehsan offered neutrality and to withdraw to Beoraidh and Sinfoyard if recognised as foreign, and freed the remaining slaves there. The Senate assigned Mareave to the Imperial Orcs, their second territory, and recognised Ehsan's people as foreigners holding Beoraidh and Sinfoyard.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish presence in Dawnguard, in the Barrens, is cited as a comparison for integrating a territory that was never Imperial.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: a Sannite gladiator contrasts the Grendel with the Druj, noting the people of Rathmonna were not enslaved or living in fear.

Grendel.t: The Grendel lost much of Mareave and the Fundindelve mithril mine, and further hostility and attempts to retake the territory were expected. Former Salt Lord Ehsan broke with his peers and secured recognition of his people in Beoraidh and Sinfoyard as foreigners.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: some free humans in Mareave may once have come from Highguard, and its rocky coast is likened to Sanctuary Sands in Necropolis.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs were assigned Mareave, their second territory, and inherit the challenges of Grendel opposition, unaligned orc inhabitants, arid land and isolation. Some liberated orcs have already joined their Sannite sept.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr are cited as a nation that maintains territories scattered across the Empire.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Brass Coast armies fighting west of the Bay of Catazar are noted as legally irrelevant to assignment, and Mareave's climate is compared to Freeborn lands.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League is cited as a nation with widely scattered territories, and Holberg is listed among recent straightforward reconquests.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Marcher help in feeding Urizen is cited as proof that dry lands can support citizens, and the Mournwold is listed among recent reconquests.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's success in supporting citizens on poor land with Marcher help is cited, and some Mareave humans may once have been Urizen.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Varushkan settlement of Ossium, which took a year or more of work by politicians and priests, is cited as a comparable challenge.

Into the spin.o: After Imperial victories in Mareave, including the conquest of Clisearn, the Senate was asked to assign the former Grendel territory, which has no Imperial citizens. The Senate allocated Mareave to the Imperial Orcs and ratified a treaty recognising the orcs of Beoraidh as foreigners.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Beoraidh, Ehsan's port-city and Mareave's only easy harbour, stayed in Grendel hands. Ehsan freed its slaves, and the Senate ratified a treaty recognising its orcs as foreigners.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: The Imperial conquest of Clisearn turned the tide in Mareave; it is one of the territory's more fertile regions and once held wealthy Grendel estates.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: Eoradal is home to small, loosely organised Broken Shore septs, many former slaves, on arid land, and could be recognised as foreign as a first step towards peaceful contact.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: Fleisardh is held by the hostile Brine Turtles on relatively fertile land, and Ehsan offered intelligence that might help neutralise them.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Icarion's small, independent orc communities, many liberated from slavery, live around jealously guarded wells and could be recognised as foreign to open peaceful contact.

Mareave/Nadir.t: Nadir is home to loose communities of Broken Shore orcs on desolate land, who could be recognised as foreign to establish peaceful contact.

Mareave/Sinfoyard.t: Ehsan offered to withdraw his forces to Sinfoyard and freed its slaves. The Senate's treaty recognised his people's claim to the region as foreigners.

Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand.t: Mentioned in passing: Mareave's high, rocky coast is compared to Sanctuary Sands.

Redoubt/Optarion.t: Mentioned in passing: Mareave's coast is likened to the high bluffs of Optarion.

Redoubt/Tomari.t: Mentioned in passing: Mareave's coast is likened to the high bluffs of Tomari.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Apulus carries the Apulian Way, the only easy land route into Mareave, so keeping it in Imperial hands is vital to reaching the new territory.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnguard's citizens are noted as never having been the majority in the Barrens.

Ayereed.t: Mentioned in passing: some Grendel fleeing Mareave sought sanctuary in neighbouring Ayereed.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Brass Coast armies are noted as busy fighting on its western side.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the fertile farms of Clisearn, Fleisardh and Beoraidh are likened to those of Feroz.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among recent, relatively straightforward reconquests of formerly Imperial territory.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: southern Mareave's dry grasslands are compared to Kahraman.

Mareave.t: Mareave was assigned to the Imperial Orcs, with its mithril mine open to allocation, while Beoraidh and Sinfoyard were recognised as belonging to foreign orcs under Ehsan. Its orc population, arid climate, isolation and Grendel threat all remain to be addressed.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among recent, relatively straightforward reconquests of formerly Imperial territory.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Mareave's high, rocky coast is compared to Sanctuary Sands in Necropolis.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as a precedent of a territory with no Imperial citizens that took a year or more to settle.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Mareave's coast is likened to the high bluffs of Tomari and Optarion.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among recent reconquests, and its climate and farms are compared to southern Mareave.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among recent reconquests, and a few Mareave orcs may seek a fresh start there.

Spiral.t: Spiral holds the only easy land route to Mareave, the Apulian Way, where travellers face the Black Plateau and armies suffer. Mareave is expected to become a Grendel frontier as Spiral once was.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as a comparison, a territory where Dawnish citizens were never the majority.

Into the valley.d: Three Dawnish armies and the Varushkan Golden Axe advanced from the Morass, while the Iron Helms, Northern Eagle and Wolves of War came up the Tarn Valley. More than thirty-five thousand Imperial troops faced only the garrison of the rebuilt Towers of Dusk and Druj enchantments. Despite the Rivers Run Red curse, casualties were negligible, and the armies met in northern Hope's Rest. The Iron Helms waged a merciless assault and the Wolves of War plundered. Conjunctions offered a Great Forest Orc reconciliation at Dourfell Keep, recovery of the Staff of Conviction, use of a Night regio, a Spring horror in the Bleaks, a cursed treasure trap, a threatened bridge and a chance to flood the Fangs.

Dawn.t: The Golden Sun, Gryphon's Pride and Hounds of Glory spearheaded the conquest of the Carmine Fields, and Dawnish generals may order a triumphant charge here under Tobias Field's mandate. The Great Forest Orcs offer a reconciliation ceremony with the Dawnish, while a released Spring beast threatens around three hundred Dawnish casualties.

Druj.t: The Druj lost the Carmine Fields and Hope's Rest, defended only by the Towers of Dusk garrison and their enchantments. They laid traps including a cursed treasure, a released Spring horror and a plan to destroy the Singing River bridge.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the oppressive aura of Grendel-held Spiral is compared to the aura around Dourfell Keep.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: if the reconciliation succeeds, Imperial troops could move secretly between the Eaves of Peytaht and Highguard-held Reikos.

Navarr.t: The southern armies advanced out of Navarr's Therunin, and the Navarr vate Drustan Brocs Guard proposed using Align the Celestial Net to turn the Night regio to Spring or Summer magic. The Great Forest Orcs had first offered to help the Navarr fight in the Barrens.

The League.t: The Wolves of War, swelled by mercenaries and Temeschwari bravos, plundered Druj garrisons in Hope's Rest. A cursed treasure now threatens the loss of two hundred and fifty strength and no plunder orders before 386YE Winter.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: several generals said their aim was to open a route south and help liberate Zenith for Urizen.

Varushka.t: The Golden Axe, Iron Helms and Northern Eagle fought from both north and south, meeting in northern Hope's Rest, and Varushkan physicks helped keep casualties low. The Golden Axe vanguard now risks around three hundred deaths if Druj ritualists destroy the Singing River bridge.

Into the valley.o: In Summer 384YE Imperial armies returned to the Barrens for the first time in three years, striking from Holberg and Therunin to conquer the Carmine Fields and Hope's Rest and drive a 'steel causeway' through the centre of the territory.

Holberg/The Morass.t: Mentioned in passing: the northern Imperial armies marched into the Barrens out of the Morass.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: Gryphon's Pride scouts probed Bitter Strand without attacking, finding the Saltmaw Spring regio from which a ritual could flood the Fangs' mithril mines for at least two seasons.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Mentioned in passing: with the central regions taken, the Druj are expected to struggle to hold Dawnguard.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are expected to find the Heart of Peytaht difficult to hold once the centre fell.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: Hope's Rest fell to the Empire as northern and southern armies met in its foothills. At Dourfell Keep the Empire may reconcile with the Great Forest Orcs, recover the Staff of Conviction for lasting insurgent support, and exploit a Night regio.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Mentioned in passing: Murderdale is named among regions the Druj will struggle to hold after the causeway.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: Saltmarsh's marshes teem with Druj enchantments. The proposed 'Dark Clouds Gather' ritual would drown much of it, turning it coastal and preventing a Druj fortification there for a year.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: Druj raiders struck from the Bleaks, and Druj ghulai have released a Spring horror in its Lupine Arbour that the Knight Protector of Spring is expected to stop.

The Barrens/The Carmine Fields.t: The Dawnish armies and Golden Axe conquered the Carmine Fields across open ground. A conjunction to the Red Plains offers a chance to seize cursed Druj treasure afflicting the Wolves of War.

The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth.t: The Towers of Dusk loom over the Plains of Teeth, rebuilt and heavily reinforced, and their garrison provided the only Druj troops opposing the Empire.
