The Barrens/The Untrod Groves.t: Mentioned in passing: Druj raiders melted back into the Untrod Groves, now within the eastern half left to the orcs.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The recovered Staff of Conviction can be sent to the Lower Tarn Valley via Anvil, and Great Forest Orc hunters there will leave to establish a free spy network in the Barrens.

Holberg.t: The Golden Sun, Gryphon's Pride, Hounds of Glory and Golden Axe launched their invasion from Holberg, and the causeway lets armies withdraw north into it.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj-created insurgent advantage in Ossium is cited as the model for the allied insurgents Hope's Rest could gain.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Great Forest Orc guides could let Imperial troops travel unexpectedly between the Eaves of Peytaht and Reikos.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Emerald Harvester clan guarding Dourfell Keep originally came from Sarangrave.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral's unique oppression is compared to the Dourfell aura, and the magicians of Spiral Castle supplied the 'Dark Clouds Gather' arcane projection.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwari bravos joined the Wolves of War seeking profit from the war against the Druj.

The Barrens.t: The Empire conquered the Carmine Fields and Hope's Rest, cutting the territory in half and confining the Druj largely to the east. Several conjunctions offered chances to secure that presence or blunt Druj traps.

Therunin.t: The Iron Helms, Northern Eagle and Wolves of War marched into the Barrens through the Tarn Valley, and armies can now return south into Therunin. The Great Forest Orcs sheltering there offer reconciliation and support.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater is not named directly; the page concerns Dawnish armies campaigning in the Barrens.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish and Varushkan generals described the push as opening a route south to help free Zenith.

Into the woods.d: Since the coldest night of the winter, spirits and wandering dead have been seen across Metri. Bandits, muggers and anyone intending violence are torn apart by gaunt figures who claim to serve the Prince of the Icy Heart and offer safe passage. Robbers have abandoned the region, and trade routes north to Skarsind and east to Karov have never been easier to travel. Yet people feel watched, and some are fleeing. At the Fortress of Salt mithril mine, a miner's heart was torn out during a brawl. Production continues, but the mood is strained. Metri has gained the haunted quality. Diviners doubt it is an enchantment but cannot be certain, and strange individuals have been asking after Tobias Shanks.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the trade route from Metri north to the Imperial Orc territory of Skarsind is named among those that have become unusually safe to travel.

The League.t: A League region in Temeschwar has become haunted, its roads now free of bandits but its people uneasy and some fleeing, while the Fortress of Salt's mithril output continues under a tense atmosphere.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the trade route east from Metri to Karov has become safer, and the page closes with a traditional Varushkan tale about the woods.

Into the woods.o: In Winter 380YE the Metri region of Temeschwar fell under a strange darkness, with ghostly figures serving 'the Prince of the Icy Heart' brutally killing anyone who threatened violence on its roads, leaving Metri haunted but free of banditry.

Temeschwar/Metri.t: Metri gained the haunted quality, with spirits of the Prince of the Icy Heart slaying would-be robbers and brawlers, its roads made safe, and the Fortress of Salt mine still producing despite deep unease among its workers.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: the road east from Metri to Karov is among the trade routes now unusually free of bandits.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the trade route north from Metri to Skarsind has never been easier to travel.

Temeschwar.t: One of Temeschwar's regions has fallen under a haunting presence that kills anyone threatening violence, and some residents are fleeing Metri for the presumed safety of the rest of the territory.

Into tired shadow.d: After three seasons of Highborn crusading storm, backed by liao sent from congregations across the Empire, Imperial armies outmanoeuvred and encircled the Druj in Zenith. Two mandates offered to focus Highborn zeal on the attack. One would impose a two-rank penalty for a season on Highborn military units not supporting the Zenith armies. The other would raise casualties inflicted by Highborn armies fighting the Druj by a fifth for a year, while penalising Highborn armies fighting elsewhere. A competing mandate would have armies hunt down tortured souls, black wraiths and Winter spirits instead. That would cost ten percent fewer casualties and require a Highborn army to stay in Zenith, but would stop Zenith gaining the terrorised quality.

Druj.t: Their six armies in Zenith, thrown into disarray by Karvor Eyepeel's death, were encircled and attempting to flee. Highguard was weighing mandates meant to destroy them, or even carry the war to their heartland.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly faced a choice between mandates. It could pour its zeal into annihilating the Druj, at a heavy cost in Highborn lives and penalties for units or armies that stood aside, or it could purge the Druj's legacy from Zenith instead.

Urizen.t: The Urizeni people of Zenith, labouring under Druj tyranny, faced the prospect that tortured souls, restless dead and miasma could leave their territory permanently terrorised unless Highguard acted.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is not named directly; the page refers only to the Druj's earlier rule of Ossium, which Varushka held at the time.

Into tired shadow.o: In Autumn 384YE, with six Druj armies encircled in Zenith and preparing to flee after Karvor Eyepeel's death, the Highborn Assembly was offered competing Synod mandates. It could either press the attack on the Druj or turn aside to purge the lingering evil of their occupation before Zenith became permanently terrorised.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj armies in Zenith are said to be reinforced by the terrors they unleashed in Proceris.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj's terror tactics in Zenith are compared to how they ruled Ossium.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a place where Highborn armies could fight the Druj and still benefit from the second Death to the Druj mandate.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a place where Highborn armies could fight the Druj and still benefit from the second Death to the Druj mandate.

Zenith.t: Six Druj armies were trapped and preparing to flee. Without the Shadows of War mandate, the territory would become terrorised, impeding armies and raising commission labour costs by two-fifths.

Invest in Beoraidh Docks.d: Bloodcrow Rasp, Senator for Skarsind, proposed the motion and Rane Shardbearer, Senator for Kallavesa, seconded it. It passed at 75 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Skarsind. The edifice required 30 wains of weirwood, 90 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Summer Solstice, Pathfinder Gaddak, Zaccaria di Sarvos and Farren Silver Streams contributed money. After the Autumn Equinox, Bloodcrow Rasp and Karrak supplied the 30 wains of weirwood. Once complete, the docks would open Beoraidh to Imperial fleet captains, raise taxation in Mareave by three thrones and raise tariffs by seven thrones. Further background appears in the Each ages a lens wind of fortune.

Grendel.t: The docks were to be built at Beoraidh, a port the Grendel held at the time, and would open it to Imperial fleet captains for trade.

Invest in Beoraidh Docks.o: In Summer 388YE the Senate passed a motion to commission new docks at Beoraidh in Mareave, disbursing 75 thrones so that Imperial fleet owners could trade with the port and the Empire could raise revenue from tariffs and tax.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Beoraidh was the site of the commissioned docks, which would open its port to Imperial fleet captains for prosperous trade.

Mareave.t: Once complete, the new docks would raise taxation in Mareave by three thrones and bring a further seven thrones in tariffs.

Invited with asperity.d: Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-Undivided, who plans to retire, was to attend the Senate with potential successors to celebrate the five-year peace treaty and discuss the Druj, the vallorn and the Jotun. The skuldyr invited Imperial storytellers to Leopard-Tooth Pass. The Dragons refused to allow a sea route to Otkodov. Thule forces moved into Ossium's woods, and Tathenon the Gyre invited Imperial warbands and armies to join an assault on the Forest of Ulnak. Caridis offered Varushkans a joint raid on the trudnik face-peelers, which would cast suspicion on the draughir. Thule warlocks at the Icy Crag sought ritual texts, Fraynir sought Dreadful Ending, and Orobus offered ilium for living weirwood trees.

Druj.t: The Thule were preparing to invade the Druj-held Forest of Ulnak after their hunters scouted it, and they invited Imperial warbands and armies to join the assault.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of Skarsind are said to keep the Thule at arm's length where possible.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the ever-present Jotun in the west were listed among the topics for Rak's state visit.

Navarr.t: Navarr was sending food north to Otkodov, and Navarri bards were invited to the storytelling exchange. The Thule also asked for advance warning before the trods network is completed, and Orobus offered ilium for living weirwood trees from Hercynia or Miaren.

Thule.t: The Dragons sent Rak and his possible successors to Anvil, refused an Imperial sea route, moved armies into Ossium and towards Ulnak, and placed warlocks at the Icy Crag. They also sought Imperial rituals and weirwood trees to prepare Sküld against its vallorn.

Varushka.t: Varushka, the nation most critical of the peace, was offered a joint raid with the Claws of the Dragon against the trudnik in Karsk and Ossium, with the Boyar's Hasta able to support it. Any attack on the trudnik would unsettle the nation's draughir.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark scops were invited to exchange tales with the skuldyr at Leopard-Tooth Pass. The page also notes quiet Wintermark grumbling about the Empire surrendering land to the northern orcs.

Invited with asperity.o: In Winter 387YE the Thule sent word that their ambassador Rak would make a state visit to Anvil with his potential successors, and set out a series of offers and refusals. These included an invitation to join a Thule invasion of the Forest of Ulnak, a joint raid on face-peelers in Varushka, and several requests for Imperial rituals and weirwood trees.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: Thule forces entered the Bonewood, which had been woven with Spring magic so that its trees attack intruders. Orobus also hoped to transplant weirwood that 'remembers' the vallorn to share with the trees of the Bonewood.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Thule forces entered the Spring-warded Webwood, a known haunt of the face-peelers. Under Caridis's terms, any trudnik spoils from Slomavetka, a lair just across the border here, would go to the Thule.

Otkodov/Nithoggir.t: The Dragons refused to cooperate in finding a sea passage to the coast of Nithoggir and would not permit an Imperial trading post there.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: The Thule were building rings of warded white granite stones around the vallorn at Emrys and asked for a season's warning before the vallorn's transformation. Imperial storytellers were invited to Leopard-Tooth Pass in Kógur.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Thule hunters scouted the forest through the Imperial spy network ahead of a planned Thule invasion. Imperial warbands joining it were promised crystal mana, and armies were welcome if their generals accepted Tathenon the Gyre's strategy, with a risk of clashes if they did not.

Hercynia.t: Orobus offered 12 rings of ilium for living trees from the Heartwood of the Great Vale, which would permanently cut its weirwood production by 1 wain a season. The decision fell to whoever won the seat at auction.

Karsk.t: Tasya of the Black Feathers, envoy of the Charnel Lord, visited the Thule fortification of Krevsatyzmei here. Karsk was also a target of the proposed face-peeler raid, which would bring a production penalty to its draughir.

Miaren.t: Orobus offered 12 rings of ilium for living trees from the Golden Trees of Seren, which would permanently reduce their weirwood production by 1 wain a season, if the seat's holder agreed.

Miekarova.t: Thule warlocks led by Thania of the Blackstaff took up residence at the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, cutting its upkeep by five thrones a season. Thania offered mithril or golden apples for certain ritual texts.

Ossium.t: Thule forces moved into the Bonewood and Webwood, and Ossium was the main target of the proposed raid on the trudnik, with the Boyar's Hasta able to support it from here. The raid would cost Ossium's draughir a production penalty.

Otkodov.t: The Thule homeland was due to receive Imperial storytellers at Leopard-Tooth Pass, while the Dragons refused any Imperial sea route or trading post on its coast. Food from the Marches and Navarr continued to flow north to feed its people and armies.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial fighting along its border was said to help the Thule goals in Ulnak.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's campaign to conquer Sarangrave was said to aid the Thule even without direct support in Ulnak.

Sea of Snow.t: An Imperial proposal to map its northern waters and find a passage to Otkodov's coast was rejected. The Thule cited terrible beasts in the ice-strewn seas, and plainly did not want Imperial fleets near their shores.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule recalled fighting alongside the Empire to liberate Sermersuaq.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs of Skarsind are said to keep the Thule at arm's length.

Tsirku.t: Mentioned in passing: Rak cited a recent overland trade route attempt through the wastes of Tsirku as an unmitigated disaster that cost many lives.

Iron and wine.d: Senator Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato oversaw 500 Thrones raised at Anvil, and private donors added more. The League's cities held a week of revelry in which Tassato turned the Vassa purple-and-gold with wine and gilding. Other nations held their own festivities, including a legendary Grand Tourney in Dawn. Foreign merchants and Summer and Night eternals joined in, though Sumaah stayed aloof. Inspired by the Empress' message, physicks and healing magicians now accompany every Imperial army, making the Steady Conquest order permanently available. The Senate was also offered a chance, open until the end of the 380YE Winter Solstice, to give one existing army the physick quality.

Dawn.t: Dawn held a Grand Tourney at the Castle of Thorns, said to be unmatched since Empress Richilde's day. Barien welcomed Dawn's nobles and yeomen to a Summer fair near the Semmerstones, and Dawn's weavers and war-witches were named among the battle-hardened healers.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard's herb masters are listed among the battlefield healers keen to help, and the Sumaah ambassador preached a sermon in Necropolis.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, the Jotun are described as a barbarian threat just over the horizon from the League.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr's herb masters are named among the battle-hardened healers eager to help the armies.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, two League potion-sellers rely on trade contacts in Feroz and Madruga.

The League.t: The League led the celebrations with a week of non-stop revelry in four cities and welcomed citizens of neighbouring nations. Its people produced art, a statue and a popular coronation song, and Senator Cesare took the lead in spending the celebration funds.

Urizen.t: Urizen marked the coronation with drifts of enchanted lightstones lighting the night sky, and its warmage healers are named among those eager to aid the armies.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's grimnir are named among the battle-hardened healers interested in helping the Empire.

Iron and wine.o: Lavish celebrations of Empress Lisabetta's coronation, led by the League and funded by the Senate, Synod and private donors, spread across the Empire. Her message to stem the flow of Imperial blood inspired healers to support the armies.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Mestra competed with Regario to outdo the celebrations, decked in golden-horn bunting, and helped turn the Vassa purple-and-gold.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: Regario vied with Mestra in the revelry under red-fox bunting, contributing to the wine and gilding thrown into the Vassa.

Astolat.t: Despite the lingering curse on Astolat, Dawn's Grand Tourney was held on the fields around the Castle of Thorns, and troubadours claim it has never been matched.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the wine-and-gilt colouring of the Vassa reportedly reached as far south as the Sapphire Stair.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, two potion-sellers cite their contacts in Feroz as a source of supply for a planned military potion venture.

Holberg.t: Citizens of Holberg worked feverishly on a great frieze honouring the Empress, whom many see as a patron of their city, and the coronation song praises Holberg's walls.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, two potion-sellers cite their contacts in Madruga as a source of supply for a planned military potion venture.

Necropolis.t: Sumaah's ambassador stayed out of the festivities but preached a sermon in Necropolis, conceding that the Empire understands the role of celebration in the path of Prosperity.

Sarvos.t: In Caricomare the cursed statue of Mirislav mysteriously changed to show the ex-Senator smiling triumphantly with a coin and a lantern, and locals hailed it as another miracle.

Tassato.t: Under Prince Cesare's guidance, Tassato held extravagant celebrations, dyeing the Vassa purple-and-gold with red wine and Imperial Mint gilding, without undue violence between its two halves.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar unveiled a statue of Janon commissioned by Lorenzo La Volpe, prompting debate about public art in a city seen as dour. Vivier Iskander van Temeschwar's coronation song spread his name across the Empire.

Irreconcilable differences.d: The law would have banned preaching the Way anywhere in the Archipelago and criminalised helping others to do so. That put it in open conflict with Synod mandates. Aspar's mandate created the Anchor the Way commission, the Freeborn enabled smuggling missionaries to Asavea, and Lutobor Branislavovich Glinka urged citizens to double down on Asavea. Amika Acciai was also recognised as an exemplar. The Plenum sees the Way as an existential threat and has increased aid to the Grendel. A successful veto would stoke Asavean fury, while a failed one would doom the sects. The Sevenfold Path also sought virtuous magicians, including the Cerularios. Shardbearer later said the Senate would respect the veto.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Hamelo angrily warns Othet not to lecture her about the Druj during their argument.

Grendel.t: The Grendel are the Plenum's proxies in its war on the Empire, already bolstered with Asavean warships, and they could expect still more Asavean support if the missionaries continued.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Dagon of Highguard, former Champion of Loyalty, carried the Loyalty Assembly's mandate, and earlier Synod mandates had urged Highborn wayfarers to preach the Way abroad.

The Brass Coast.t: Pacheco i Shartha i Guerra's mandate set Freeborn captains to smuggling missionaries and aid into Asavea, and Freeborn corsairs carried the Sevenfold Path magicians there. All of this would have been lost had the ban come into force.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Plenum's surprise attack on Meade is cited as evidence of Asavea's escalating hostility.

Urizen.t: Glinka's mandate did not reach a greater majority, so it had no particular impact in Urizen, unlike most other nations, whose national assemblies drew extra attention on the issue.

Varushka.t: Lutobor Branislavovich Glinka, a Varushkan, enacted the General Assembly mandate to double down on Asavea. Paradoxically, it had no particular impact in Varushka itself.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Rane Shardbearer, Senator for Kallavesa, raised the contentious ban. After the Synod's veto, Shardbearer declared that the Senate would respect the decision.

Irreconcilable differences.o: Rane Shardbearer, Senator for Kallavesa, passed a Senate motion by a single vote making it illegal to preach the Way in Asavea, and Sabella of the Silent Tide sought a Synod veto. At the Autumn Equinox the General Assembly upheld the veto and struck the law down.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: loose-lipped Beoraidh mercenaries are the reason the Empire learned of Catella Cerularios's interest in the relic Glistering.

Ayereed.t: Mentioned in passing: Hamelo describes the Grendel as battered in Ayereed.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Plenum's attack on Meade is described as striking the far side of the Empire from the Bay of Catazar.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Hamelo says the Grendel were rousted from Feroz.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa's senator, Rane Shardbearer, raised the motion banning preaching in Asavea and later acknowledged the Synod's veto in the Senate.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Hamelo says the Grendel were beaten back in Madruga.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: Hamelo says the Grendel were rousted from Mareave, and the loose lips of Beoraidh mercenaries revealed Catella Cerularios's interest in Glistering.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Plenum's surprise attack on Meade is cited as part of Asavea's escalating campaign against the Empire.

Is there anybody out there?.d: Adamant's koboldi offered to help codify Pillars of Adamant, fortify the heliopticon towers and provide beacon plans for Ossium. Barien's heralds will check on the Dawn–Wintermark challenge, and Jaheris extended his fane offer to Wintermark and announced a magicians' tourney for patronage of the Icy Crag. Estavus's heralds cleared Pakaanan's Pass between Skarsind and Sermersuaq. Tharim's knights left Lightsea, spreading nightmares through Calvos and Trivento, camped in Tassato and are bound for Upwold to avenge the herald Obligatus. Sorin's houndmaster offered the Northern Eagle the Elusive quality. Ephisis, Callidus, Zakalwe, Sinokenon, Ylenwe and Sung sought dealings, and greenteeth boggarts plagued Grey Fens and Misericorde.

Dawn.t: Barien's heralds will visit Dawn late on Sunday morning to judge its deeds in his challenge, while Jaheris has offered the fane boon Dawn never built in Dawnguard to Wintermark instead.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: named among the threats the proposed beacon at Kostjya's Respite would warn against.

Imperial Orcs.t: Ashborn Trosk raised the declaration and supplied the beggar's lye that saw Pakaanan's Pass cleared, reopening the route from Skarsind to Sermersuaq for Imperial armies.

Jotun.t: The pass the Jotun blocked with Adamant's aid in 383YE is open to Imperial armies again, and greenteeth now plague the Jotun-held Grey Fens.

Navarr.t: Tharim's knights are expected to pass through Miaren after the Spring Equinox on their way to Upwold.

The Brass Coast.t: Tharim's knights broke camp in Lightsea and filled Calvos with nightmares, the Burning Falcon and Red Wind Corsairs met them in Tassato, and Mina i Yashum i Riqueza was asked to gather storytellers for Sung's constellations in Burnish.

The League.t: Tharim's knights brought nightmares to Trivento and camped in Tassato, Astrid Rezia di Tassato was asked to organise constellation makers, Spiral's heliopticon could be fortified, and Claus Friedrich von Holberg must hunt greenteeth in Misericorde.

The Marches.t: Tharim's knights seek vengeance for Obligatus, slain at the Copse of the Bone Birch alongside Marchers including Gerraint Black, and may run riot in Upwold, while Zakalwe's heralds seek views on the Mournwold battle.

Urizen.t: The koboldi offered to help Ioseph codify Pillars of Adamant once Able the Taller finishes his current work, and to fortify the heliopticon towers if Urizen commissions the edifice.

Varushka.t: Dima Vasilyevna Novosad received koboldi plans for a dragon beacon in Bittershore, and the Northern Eagle was offered the new Elusive quality by Sorin's houndmaster Esgyrn.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark faces Barien's midpoint check, Jaheris's herald seeks a meeting with its icewalkers and offers a guarded fane in the Suaq Wastes, and Pakaanan's Pass now links Sermersuaq to Skarsind.

Is there anybody out there?.o: In Spring 387YE a roundup of eternal activity reached the Empire. Tharim's thousand Ashen Knights marched north from Madruga seeking vengeance, the House of Fire and Flame reopened Pakaanan's Pass, and numerous eternals made offers, challenges and visits.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: Greenteeth burst from stagnant pools to kill fenlanders, and only one person survived the attack on the Breadbasket station at Drowner's Dell.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Greenteeth are killing the vulnerable across the region, and a conjunction to Sacrifice Point lets heroes hunt the clutch that slew Sand Fishers at the Flaxen Pillars.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: Tharim's knights marched through Calvos after sunset, filling the town's sleep with nightmares of being buried and bound.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: The Ashen Knights who had camped in Lightsea for a year broke camp after the Winter Solstice and marched north.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: The proposed dragon beacon would stand on Bittershore's shore and, in its grander form, tower over Kostjya's Respite, warning of attacks and guiding Varushkan sailors home.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: The knights were allowed over the Spider's Dream toll bridge into Bocche and left Trivento suffering a night of dreams of helplessness.

Segura/Burnish.t: Lights settle like flowers in the Meadow of Dust and Glass, where volunteers will name constellations and craft their lore for Sung's heralds.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: Jaheris offers to send creatures to defend the Suaq Wastes if Wintermark builds him a fane there.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: Pakaanan's Pass has been blasted clear enough for armies to pass, though there is no road and the foothills remain treacherous.

Tassato/Enterio.t: Tharim's knights marched north along the road into Enterio and made camp on Tassato's southern borders.

Astolat.t: The Northern Eagle rested and resupplied in Astolat while Esgyrn studied the army and devised its proposed Elusive quality.

Bregasland.t: Greenteeth have overrun the deeper Grey Fens, and Orson BogMyrtle is charged with destroying them so households will stay despite the Jotun invasion.

Holberg.t: Ravenous greenteeth are killing people across Misericorde, including Sand Fisher orcs at the Flaxen Pillars.

Madruga.t: Tharim's thousand knights left their camp in Lightsea and marched north through Calvos Sound, leaving terrible dreams behind them.

Miaren.t: Tharim's knights are expected to pass through Miaren after the Spring Equinox on their way to Upwold.

Morrow.t: Morrow's heliopticon tower would become almost impossible to destroy if Urizen commissions the koboldi's reinforcement edifice.

Mournwold.t: Zakalwe's heralds want to hear views on last season's Mournwold battle and fighting alongside heralds of Day, and the miners of the Mourn are among those interested in Jarl Haakon's armour.

Ossium.t: The koboldi have drawn up plans for a dragon-topped beacon in Bittershore that could warn Kostjya's Respite of attack and raise fleet investment in Ossium.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt drew the koboldi to study the Pillars of Adamant enchantment cast there, and its heliopticon tower could be fortified against destruction.

Sarvos.t: Tharim's knights crossed the Spider's Dream into Bocche and brought nightmares to Trivento, and a Sarvos consortium is interested in Jarl Haakon's armour.

Segura.t: Sung has set a field of temporary stars around a night regio in Burnish for Imperial volunteers to shape into constellations for the Night realm.

Sermersuaq.t: Jaheris's herald returned to Rest to court the icewalkers and offer a guarded fane in the Suaq Wastes, while the reopened Pakaanan's Pass links Sermersuaq to Skarsind.

Skarsind.t: Explosions shook western Skarsind as Estavus's heralds cleared Pakaanan's Pass, reopening an army route into Sermersuaq.

Spiral.t: Spiral's heliopticon tower could be made nearly indestructible and kept operating even if the Urizen–League détente collapsed.

Tassato.t: Tharim's knights have camped on Tassato's southern borders, where they met the Burning Falcon and the Red Wind Corsairs and refused to be turned aside.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: a koboldi herald delivered the Ossium beacon blueprints to the College of Engineering in Temeschwar.

The Semmerlak.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Ossium beacon would face out across the Semmerlak, and greenteeth drag victims into its stagnant pools in Misericorde.

Upwold.t: Obligatus was slain at the Copse of the Bone Birch, and Tharim's vengeful knights are expected to enter Upwold after the Spring Equinox.

Zenith.t: Zenith's heliopticon tower would be protected from destruction if Urizen commissions the koboldi's reinforcement edifice.

Islands in the dream.d: Lost in woods confounded by Ossium's dream enchantment, the party was guided by a herald of the Night Singer to Dimmorden, now a walled village twice its former size after several hundred kin left Thule-held Webwood. Three dimwalkers lead the sept. They believe ancestors dwell in a dream-world called the Dark Forest, that bad ancestors rise from the Nightmare, and that six precepts mark a good ancestor. They do not count the Thule as people. They refused to let the Illarawm build bridges to their ancestors. Their missing families remain scattered across Ghul'Thak, and conquering the region this season would bring 2,000 strength from the Dreamers and 2,000 from Irra Harah. It would also let the Winter Sun issue a Break the Chains order there.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: an attack on Ghul'Thak could be launched from the Dawnish-held Barrens, and the Karass of the Barrens are named as an earlier Unshackled contact.

Druj.t: The Dreamers despise the Druj, raid them constantly, and fear the Druj will slaughter the half of their sept still held in Ghul'Thak rather than lose it, as they nearly did with the Great Forest Orcs.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun, who could otherwise break the chains in Ghul'Thak, is currently in Grendel-held Mareave.

Highguard.t: Highborn who had armed and trained the Dreamers accompanied the expedition as advisors, were keenly interested in the sept's six precepts, and are among those the Dreamers ask to rescue their kin.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Unshackled assembly led the expedition under its highest calling. The Dreamers rejected sharing their ancestors with the Illarawm and grew guarded on learning Bloodcrow Knott had been executed, but they asked the Imperial Orcs to help reunite their sept.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarri magicians have granted Irra Harah access to the Forest of Ulnak, and the Druj use of the vallorn in Therunin is cited.

Thule.t: The Dreamers regard the Thule as barely better than the Druj and not truly people. They resent Otkodov for having held their Webwood kin, and Thule agreement to use Oerwealt would offer a bridgehead into Ghul'Thak.

Varushka.t: Varushkans who had worked with the Dreamers advised the expedition. The sept trades regularly with its Varushkan neighbours, has built a Varushkan-style walled village, and credits Varushkan spirit magic with clarifying its ancestors' voices.

Islands in the dream.o: In Autumn 388YE an Unshackled expedition, guided by Bloodcrow Meep with Varushkan and Highborn advisors, visited the Dreamers of the Dark Forest in Echofell to learn about their ancestors. The Dreamers declined to share their ancestors, but begged the Empire to free the other half of their sept from the Druj-held Ghul'Thak Forest.

Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest.t: The three missing families of the Dreamers are spread across Ghul'Thak. An Imperial attack this season would gain 2,000 strength from the Dreamers and 2,000 from Irra Harah, and would allow a Break the Chains order there.

Forest of Ulnak/Oerwealt.t: Thule-held Oerwealt could serve as a bridgehead for an attack on Ghul'Thak, if the Thule agree.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Mentioned in passing: twice a year the Dreamers trek to Stinking Market in Drownbark to sell raid spoils and buy metal goods.

Ossium/Echofell.t: The Dreamers' village of Dimmorden near the Bonehives has been rebuilt in hardwood and stone, has doubled in size, and hosted the Unshackled expedition.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Mentioned in passing: several hundred Dreamer kin formerly held by the Thule in Webwood left to join the sept in Echofell.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Half the Dreamers' sept is scattered across Ulnak's Ghul'Thak Forest. Freeing them requires conquering that region against Druj armies and the garrisons of Cassad Ûln and the Thistle of Barbs.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun is stationed in Mareave and so cannot reach Ulnak to break the chains this season.

Ossium.t: A Spirit enchantment over Ossium confounded travel through its woods and gave the Dreamers unusually vivid dreams of their ancestors, while the Unshackled met the sept at Dimmorden in Echofell.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule of Otkodov begrudgingly let several hundred Dreamer kin leave Webwood, which has not endeared them to the sept.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj use of the vallorn in Sarangrave reinforces the Dreamers' fear that the Druj will destroy entire septs.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dreamers earlier ignored the opportunity to leave Ossium and travel to Skarsind.

The Barrens.t: Without Thule agreement to use Oerwealt, an Imperial attack to free the Dreamers' kin in Ghul'Thak would need to come from the Barrens.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj use of the vallorn in Therunin is cited as evidence of their willingness to destroy rather than lose control.

It can't get much worse.d: On Friday, heroes could rescue Wintermark refugees fleeing the Jotun at Floes Descent in Skarsind. They could also strike Druj bands in Morrow while saving scholars who escaped the Halls of Knowledge, and raid fugitive House Martel nobles at Rookwood Estate in the Barrens. Saturday's opportunities included saving poisoned Highborn physicks in Operus, which would preserve the Valiant Pegasus's ability to Tend the Fallen. Others were slaying an oduli at Cascade Pass and ambushing Writhing Shadow ritualists, raiding green iron carriers and hunting another oduli in Ossium. Heroes could also attempt to break a fear miasma pillar in Bittershore and drive off Grendel marines landing at Orieni Villa and Glass Point Cove.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish could raid disgraced House Martel at Rookwood Estate and avenge the Gryphon's Pride knights ambushed by an oduli in Galath Fields. They also had House Chambrun's anointed scout Heloise Fletcher's discovery of a miasma pillar in Bittershore to act on.

Druj.t: Druj bands were rampaging across Morrow with poisons, Tortured Souls and an oduli, while in Ossium their ritualists, green iron convoys and fear miasma pillars were all exposed to Imperial strikes.

Grendel.t: Grendel moridun marines made sudden landings at Orieni Villa in Feroz and Glass Point Cove in Sarvos, seeking to loot a mana sinecure and disrupt the ilium trade unless driven off.

Highguard.t: Highborn defenders were being driven back in Morrow. Physicks of the Valiant Pegasus were pinned down and poisoned near Silver Light Tower, and their rescue would decide whether the army had enough healers to Tend the Fallen.

Imperial Orcs.t: Jotun warriors were pursuing refugees into Pakaanan's Pass in the orcs' new home of Skarsind, and defeating them would stop the Jotun scouting routes into Imperial Orc lands.

Jotun.t: A Jotun warband of Skjaldir and Ulvenwar pursued fleeing Wintermark refugees into Skarsind, offering them The Choice, and risked defeat if heroes intercepted it at Floes Descent.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr skirmishers were expected to want to help in Morrow, and the in-character tale shows Thorns from Peakedge guiding fleeing Urizeni students.

The Brass Coast.t: Grendel marines surrounded the Orieni Villa near Cazar, seat of the Broken Shore Bounty, threatening to deprive the Empire of the coming season's ilium.

The League.t: Grendel marines landed at Glass Point Cove in Sarvos to loot the mana sinecure, and League-held Holberg served as the base for spies who located the House Martel fugitives.

Urizen.t: Morrow was being ravaged by the Druj, with the Halls of Knowledge destroyed. Scattered scholars who might be rescued could form the foundation of a new centre of magical learning.

Varushka.t: Varushkan wardens tracked Druj convoys carrying green iron through the Bonewood, giving Varushka a chance to raid them at Wither Oak and Warden's Reach.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark heroes and refugees fleeing the Jotun invasion of Sermersuaq were being hunted in Floes Descent, and a rescue could save citizens who would otherwise not reach Anvil.

It can't get much worse.o: Ahead of the 382YE Autumn Equinox, the civil service published the conjunctions found by war scouts and prognosticators. They offered Imperial heroes chances to rescue refugees and scholars, hunt Druj monsters and ritualists, raid fugitives and green iron, and repel Grendel landings.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Grendel marines besieged the Orieni Villa near Cazar. If they were not repulsed, no ilium would be acquired that season, though a larger haul might follow.

Morrow/Caeli.t: Druj bands hunted villagers and fleeing scholars across Caeli, and conjunctions to Iron Citadel Field, Meadow of Clouds and Cascade Pass offered chances to strike back and slay an oduli being escorted through its ruins.

Morrow/Operus.t: Chikad and hupul attackers pinned down poisoned Valiant Pegasus physicks near Silver Light Tower, where Druj orc mages had also been harrying the Granite Pillar.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Druj fighters criss-crossed Peregro hunting refugees and scholars, with conjunctions to Peakedge Road and Sulphur Vent, and some feared the oduli might be led to its hot springs.

Morrow/Ravion.t: Mentioned in passing: some speculated that the Druj might use the oduli in Ravion to repeat the rite that turned Proceris into swamp.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: An anointed Chambrun scout found a miasma pillar inland from Scarred Bay, which heroes could try to break through consecration or ritual.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: Writhing Shadow ritualists could be ambushed at Blood Spike Glade, and Druj convoys carrying green iron could be raided at Wither Oak and Warden's Reach.

Ossium/Galath Fields.t: An oduli and chikad ambushers that killed most of a band of Dawnish questing knights were last seen at Fangmoor Dwell, north of Lomaa.

Sarvos/Uccelini.t: Grendel marines and slaves landed at Glass Point Cove to loot the mana sinecure's coming season's production.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: Refugees fled through the woods of Floes Descent with Jotun warriors close behind, and defeating them would deny the Jotun the chance to scout the pass.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Magistrate Karkovitch's militia could raid the Rookwood Estate to seize House Martel nobles wanted for murder, at the risk of alerting nearby Druj.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Mentioned in passing: refugees from Proceris told of Druj monsters, and the valley had been turned into a foetid swamp by a Druj rite.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Grendel armada had lingered in the Bay for over a month, and fast ships hidden far out in its waters launched landings on the Feroz and Sarvos coasts.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wintermark heroes would already have been travelling to Casinea had their lands not been invaded.

Feroz.t: Grendel marines stormed and surrounded the Orieni Villa near Cazar, threatening the ilium supply of the Broken Shore Bounty.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: magistrates' spies slip across the border from Holberg into the Carmine Fields, which helped locate the House Martel fugitives.

Morrow.t: The Druj were rampaging through eastern Morrow, using poisons, Tortured Souls and an oduli. Five conjunctions offered chances to strike back and to save the physicks and scholars fleeing there.

Ossium.t: As the Golden Axe advanced into Ossium, conjunctions offered strikes against Writhing Shadow ritualists, green iron convoys, an oduli and a fear miasma pillar, all within the Druj miasma.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn who suffered in Reikos recognise the Tortured Souls now seen in Morrow.

Sarvos.t: Grendel marines landed at Glass Point Cove and held the cliff tops, threatening to loot the mana sinecure's coming production and leave the Custodian with repair costs.

Sermersuaq.t: Jotun armies swept across Sermersuaq, burning halls and forcing refugees and Wintermark heroes to flee east into Skarsind.

Skarsind.t: Refugees from Sermersuaq fled into Skarsind with Jotun warriors in pursuit, and defeating the warband would stop a Jotun raiding force scouting the territory.

The Barrens.t: The militia could raid fugitive House Martel nobles at Rookwood Estate, and dead yeofolk bearing Barrens house heraldry had been seen among the Druj as Tortured Souls.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: fleeing scholars and students were heading north to Therunin's forests, and poisoned soldiers collapsed near its border with Morrow.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: dead Zenith mages appeared among the Druj as Tortured Souls, and refugees from Proceris told of Druj monsters.

It never happened.d: Shuttered Lantern cabals investigated the politics of five citadels, reporting at the Winter Solstice. Ilarch Maxatios distanced Kantor from Theodosia's Peace auras. Grand Ilarch Adonai of Ipotavo collapsed after their heir Phoeb died in Imperial care, and the pro-Empire General Dancia Terricos is expected to succeed them; she invited League generals to send plans regarding the Mallum. Sarcophan investment is reopening Issyk's docks. If the General Assembly passes a mandate and 40 congregations support Solokha, the worst hauntings will be cleansed and relations improved, though supporting priests may be offered dedication to Anarchy, Vengeance or Peace. Vigilance mandates could instead study the Axou sects or watch participating priests.

Druj.t: General Dancia Terricos, a veteran of Ipotavo's defence against the Druj and the campaign that freed Kaban from the Mallum, offered to consider what part Ipotavo might play in League generals' plans regarding the Mallum.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grand Ilarch Andronicus of Issyk is said to consider the attempted Axou alliance with the Grendel a mistake.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Ambassador to Axos, Fintan Nighthaven, is of Navarr.

The League.t: General Dancia Terricos felt kinship with Holberg and asked League generals, especially the general of the Towerjacks, to send her their plans regarding the Mallum by Winged Messenger before the Spring Equinox.

Urizen.t: Axou tradition blames the Empire, and in-character the Urizen, for Solokha's fall, and Urizeni congregations cannot join any of the Solokha mandates unless they pass with a greater majority.

Varushka.t: Varushkan congregations cannot take part in the Solokha project unless the relevant mandate passes with a greater majority; a Varushkan icewalker of the Shuttered Lantern features as a spy in Axos.

It never happened.o: In Winter 386YE the Civil Service reported on rocky relations with the Citadels of Axos amid internal upheaval driven by Grand Ilarch Kyther of Kaban and Theodosia of Ipotavo. Shuttered Lantern magicians spied in Axos, and the Synod was offered mandates to join, study or watch the effort to cleanse the haunted ruins of Solokha.

Holberg.t: General Dancia Terricos, herself a survivor of a Druj siege, admired Holberg's resistance and had hoped to attend the 250th anniversary of the city joining the League, but her plans fell through.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Axos once tried to invade Spiral in retaliation for the fall of Solokha.

It's all wrong, but it's all right.d: Although the Synod repealed the proscription treating false-virtue dedications as blasphemy, Faraden Pride was injured. Imperial fleets trading with Caitun suffered a two-rank penalty, the Azure Sutannir's Faraden benefits were halved, and the families trading with the Alder of Meade and Mediator of Fisk came under pressure to end those arrangements. Faraden had begun curbing Asavean influence and signed peace with the Jotun. The Iron Confederacy sent envoys to discuss its Brass Coast holdings, the Lasambrian conquest, the Hand of Dumon and trade. It offered Imperial warbands pay and plunder for fighting the Jotun in Reinos. Another curse struck Kalino, and a Synod proscription technically branded all Suranni heretics.

Dawn.t: General Hendrick of the Black Eagle Banner wished to fight alongside Dawnish knights, offering any Dawnish military unit that joined the Reinos campaign two extra ingots of green iron regardless of experience.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page; it is linked only through its shared hold on Feroz, where the Iron Confederacy controlled the Cazar Straits.

Jotun.t: The Jotun signed a peace treaty with Faraden but faced an Iron Confederacy war of conquest against the Lasambrian Jotun in Reinos, where Imperial warbands were invited to join the Suranni and share the plunder.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn ambassadors handled both nations; the Azure Sutannir's benefits from Faraden pilgrims to Kahraman were halved, and Suranni holdings on two former Freeborn island chains were to be discussed with the Suranni delegation.

The Marches.t: The Tseriyn family, who trade mithril to the Alder of Meade for Marcher produce, were pressed to reconsider the arrangement, and Marcher captains already troubled by Jotun ships in the Gullet faced the Caitun trading penalty.

Wintermark.t: The Salagiin traders supplying ilium to the Mediator of Fisk were pushed to reconsider their dealings with Wintermark, and Winterfolk captains faced both Jotun ships in the Gullet and the Caitun trading penalty.

It's all wrong, but it's all right.o: In Autumn 388YE the Empire's relations with Faraden were strained by Faraden anger at Synod hostility to their Five Flames faith, while the Iron Confederacy, now holding Cazar Straits and Free Landing, sent a delegation to Anvil to negotiate a treaty.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The Iron Confederacy controlled the Cazar Straits after taking the former Children of Wrecks stronghold there.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Free Landing was held by the Iron Confederacy, whose navies took it with support from Freeborn corsairs, a success that prompted the Suranni offer to Imperial mercenaries.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the bay is not named, though the Iron Confederacy's capture of the former Children of Wrecks strongholds in its island chains is discussed.

Feroz.t: The Iron Confederacy controlled the Cazar Straits in Feroz after capturing the former Children of Wrecks stronghold, and Suranni holdings in the Brass Coast were on the agenda for treaty talks.

Kahraman.t: Faraden pilgrims grew reluctant to visit the Azure Chorus's Parador of Wind and Flame, halving the Azure Sutannir's Faraden benefits, though the Sutannir might help ease Faraden concerns through a Synod judgement.

Kalino.t: Known to the Suranni as Arbonne, Kalino was struck by another Winter curse resembling Naeve's Twisting Blight; the warding temple prevented total failure but the Autumn harvest would still be poor.

Kallavesa.t: Beggar's lye from the marshes of Kallavesa forms part of the Salagiin trade with the Mediator of Fisk, which Faraden pressure now threatened.

Madruga.t: The Iron Confederacy controlled Free Landing in Madruga, taken with help from Freeborn corsairs, and its Brass Coast holdings were expected to feature in the treaty negotiations.

Mitwold.t: The mithril trade between the Tseriyn family and the Alder of Meade, restored after the Jotun occupation of Meade, was at risk unless reassurance was found for Faraden.

Reinos.t: The Iron Confederacy waged a war of conquest in the hills of Reinos, having reportedly taken several regions, and Imperial warbands were offered pay and plunder to fight alongside the Black Eagle Banner there.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial efforts had created a new maritime trade route to Faraden through the Sea of Snow.

It's my time.d: Responding to Yrkja Riansson Sigeing's Wintermark Assembly judgement on drawing inspiration from Wintermark's legacy, Jared's judgement (378=0) sent Highborn archivists and benefactors north. Welcomed in Wintermark's halls, they found three possible causes: recovering Foe-slayer and building a hall for Wintermark's banners, compiling the history of the Witan to restore its prominence, or aiding the exploration of Tsirku. The Highborn Assembly could enact one of three competing mandates, each costing 25 liao, or none if Jared is named and goes north personally. The chosen effort would exceed expectations if it supported Wintermark, or achieve something alone. Meanwhile, Highguard could not use archivists or benefactors for peerless kinship elsewhere that season.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly was offered a choice of three competing mandates directing its archivists and benefactors in Wintermark, and those groups were tied up there, unavailable for other peerless kinship that season.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark stood to gain Highborn help with whichever cause the Highborn Assembly chose: the banner-bearers' hall, the restoration of the Witan, or the exploration of Tsirku.

It's my time.o: Highborn archivists and benefactors, sent north by Jared of the Suns of Couros's peerless kinship judgement, arrived in Wintermark but could not agree which of three causes to support. They turned to the Highborn Assembly to choose between mandates backing the banner hall, the Witan, or the exploration of Tsirku.

Tsirku.t: One of the three mandates would turn Highborn benefactors and archivists to helping Wintermark face the dangers of exploring Tsirku, even if Wintermark paused the exploration over winter.

It's only me.d: Annukka Juhaling returned for an Astronomantic Symposium in the Senate. Highborn stewards of Gideon's Vigil sought volunteers to be possessed by ghosts from the wrecked pilgrim ship the Virtuous. Anthony de Woort von Temeschwar came to discuss troubles in Holberg's sausage trade, and Doctor Aodann de Spiral brought an unidentifiable League patient with a magical malady. Two separate, unsettling Ketsov delegations travelled from Ossium. The Burning Vine offered a conjunction to the Old Green Fort in Goldglades. The eternal Sadogua agreed to attend Morwenna Withered Rose's inquisition. A delegate of the Spiral rebels was due to address the Urizen. Theodosia of Ipotavo left early, reportedly unsettled by Vesna's inaugural address.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium was wrested from the Druj, and the Ketsov family are resented for the accommodations they once made with their orc masters.

Highguard.t: Stewards of the dead from the Highborn chapter Gideon's Vigil came to the chapel in the Highborn camp seeking volunteers to host the restless ghosts of the Virtuous's drowned passengers and crew so the spirits could move on.

Navarr.t: Ambition guides of the Burning Vine, debating what the Navarr's ambition should be once the vallorn can be defeated, invited a small delegation of guides gathered by Aniera Exiles End to meet them by conjunction; Brat Umbral Path was also asked to advocate for Sadogua at his inquisition.

The League.t: League visitors sought help at Anvil: Anthony de Woort von Temeschwar on the faltering Holberg sausage trade and the Custodian of the Bloody Great Sausage, and Doctor Aodann de Spiral with a League patient whom not even the egregore could identify.

Urizen.t: A delegate from Caela of the Silver Flame, leader of the Spiral rebels, was due to arrive late on Saturday to be received by the Urizen egregores and discuss the rebellion with their fellow Urizeni, who legally regarded the rebels as foreigners.

Varushka.t: Two separate groups of Ketsov emissaries, apparently unaware of each other and leaving many who met them uneasy, travelled to the Varushkan camp to meet Jaromira Orlov; Sadogua also objected to the Circle of Zulgan-Tash being declared sorcerers.

It's only me.o: Ahead of the Spring Equinox 386YE, the first summit of Emperor Vesna's reign, a range of visitors announced their intention to come to Anvil seeking aid, counsel or business, while one foreign scholar abruptly left the Empire.

Miaren/Goldglades.t: The Old Green Fort in Goldglades was the destination of the Burning Vine's conjunction for guides travelling from Anvil.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Mentioned in passing: tied to the Necropolis coast, off which the Virtuous was lost and from where Theodosia of Ipotavo took ship.

Spiral/Ankra.t: Ankra was held by Caela of the Silver Flame's rebels, whose delegate came to Anvil to speak with the Urizen.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Cinion was held by the Urizeni rebels, whose last-minute delegate sought to discuss their rebellion with the nation at Anvil.

Bay of Catazar.t: Magical storms raged across the bay, and the pilgrim ship the Virtuous was lost there after its captain ignored warnings; the anchors of its ghosts presumably lie on the seabed.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: stargazers along the road to Casinea were heading to the Symposium, while the Burning Vine judged the trip to Casinea too risky because of Cold Sun.

Holberg.t: Holberg butchers struggled to sell their sausages amid cancelled orders and accusations of poor or even cursed goods, prompting Anthony de Woort von Temeschwar to bring his findings to Anvil.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ketsov family has prospered both in Ossium and in neighbouring Karsk since joining Varushka.

Miaren.t: The Burning Vine, a Miaren-based sect of Ambition priests, opened a conjunction for up to eight guides from Anvil to visit them in the territory.

Necropolis.t: The Virtuous sank off the Necropolis coast, and Theodosia of Ipotavo left from Crown's Quay on an Axou ship a day before the storms struck.

Ossium.t: Emissaries of the Ketsov family, residents of Ossium whose Burgher is Jereni Hinda Bogdanov, set out for Anvil in two separate and strangely unsettling groups.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the doomed Virtuous set sail from Sarvos for Sanctuary Sands despite the warnings of League bishops.

Spiral.t: The Urizeni rebels holding Ankra and Cinion sent a delegate to Anvil at the last minute to discuss the situation in the territory.

It's what we do.d: The civil service provided a magnitude 20 Autumn arcane projection so that all willing citizens could join through a single ritual, and reserved the Senate chamber for the Guild's first meeting and the election of its leader. The Constitutional Court prepared an administrative motion to transfer the power to add potions to Imperial lore to the Guild, and noted that a constitutional motion could also give it the power to interdict potions. League and Freeborn apothecaries offered herbs in return for a statement backing apothecaries' pay. Yerende orcs offered to support a new herbal school if the Druj destroyed Thornsong House. Navarr and Varushkan apothecaries sought interdiction powers covering potions, poisons and drugs.

Druj.t: The Druj encircle Thornsong House, and the page warns that they would destroy it if the Empire's efforts to conceal it failed, as they once destroyed the Halls of Knowledge.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Yerende sept wanted the Guild to focus on service rather than its members' interests, and offered to back a new Apothecaries' Guildhouse under Guild control if Thornsong House were lost. This offer was later superseded by another Wind of Fortune.

Navarr.t: Navarr apothecaries proposed rewriting the manifesto so the Guild would determine the use of potions, poisons and drugs. Control of their Thornsong House could pass to the Guild only through a constitutional motion that the Navarr Assembly could veto.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Yerende devotion to apothecary arts is compared to Urizeni magic, and the Halls of Knowledge, whose Provost was once appointed by Urizeni magicians, is cited as a precedent.

Varushka.t: Varushkan herbalists, worried by the rising trade in foreign narcotics, backed giving the Guild interdiction powers. They offered to investigate substances for the Guild, at ten thrones per season, if the Senate granted those powers.

It's what we do.o: Following the Senate's creation of the Imperial Apothecaries Guild at the Winter Solstice, the civil service publicised the new sodality, arranged a means for members to join, and set out the legal powers it might be granted. Three groups of citizens offered support in return for changes to its manifesto or powers.

Karov.t: Herbalists from Karov were among the Varushkans supporting interdiction powers for the Guild and offering to research suspect substances on its behalf.

Karsk.t: Herbalists from Karsk joined those from Karov in backing the Navarr proposal for the Guild to control potions, poisons and drugs.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is not named, but the page cites the Halls of Knowledge, destroyed by the Druj, as a precedent for Thornsong House.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Apothecaries' Guildhouse would cost 10 thrones in upkeep, rather than 12, if built there.

Therunin.t: Thornsong House, the Empire's only potion-research commission, stands in Therunin but is encircled by the Druj and unlikely to operate soon. The Yerende argued that its Thornsinger should be chosen by the Guild.

Journeys end in lovers meeting.d: Freeborn from a Crucible parador planned to bring transformative rainbow water to the Brass Coast camp. Tasya of the Black Feathers invited named Varushkans to meet Irontooth, who intends to do something for Karsk. Marracossans from Trajadoz sought to renegotiate their treaty. Mendicant Garev, called to inquisition, was trapped in Kaela's regio near Syrene and needed rescuing. Armed Summer boggarts, heralds of the Azoth, a mysterious King Rat from Temeschwar and would-be cicisbeo were all heading for the League. Hahnmark stormcrows sought hosts for restless ghosts, and Kaisa the Sewn Tongue's sister sought answers about the Falconer cult. The Circle of Black Sand came to conclude a deal, and the rejected Tribunal of the Silver Flame sought out its Urizeni supporters.

Dawn.t: Mendicant Garev became lost in the regio near Syrene controlled by Kaela, a place Dawn's locals avoid because it saps the strength of all who enter.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named as the foe the Red Wind Corsairs escaped and the enemy the Marracossans fought alongside the Empire.

Highguard.t: Highborn Mendicant Garev, called to inquisition by the Inquisitor of Prosperity, was stranded in a draining regio and needed rescue. He asked the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly to find him an advocate.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn from the Crucible parador came to the Brass Coast camp to celebrate with lineage-changing water. Marracossans also arrived there to meet their Sendito and the senator for Madruga about deepening their treaty.

The League.t: The League camp expected heralds of the Azoth offering transformative trials to League artisans, the sinister King Rat from Temeschwar and two aspiring cicisbeo from Spiral. Armed boggarts were also being herded from Spiral Castle towards Anvil.

Urizen.t: The Tribunal of the Silver Flame, whom the Urizen National Assembly had declared to be Urizen, planned to visit the Urizen camp. They wished to meet Callista of the Dark Shard and other supporters after the Conclave condemned their offer.

Varushka.t: Irontooth, pleased with Varushkan tribute, invited named Varushkans and representatives of two Karsk vales to a conjunction to discuss what Karsk needs. He also sent pointed messages to others who had courted him.

Wintermark.t: Stormcrows led by Grey Aleks brought Hahnmark's restless ghosts to the Tree of Names seeking willing hosts. Kiara Last-Lantern came to Sigehold Hall to learn about the Falconer cult that claimed her sister.

Journeys end in lovers meeting.o: Ahead of the Spring Equinox of 388YE, a range of visitors sent word that they were coming to Anvil. They included Freeborn with transformative waters, envoys of the Charnel Lord Irontooth, Marracossan treaty partners, armed boggarts, Hahnmark ghosts and the rebuffed Tribunal of the Silver Flame.

Casinea/Casfall.t: Mentioned in passing: Garev's fall into one of the fissures around Casfall last season, and his rescue, are recalled.

Madruga/Crucible.t: The Freeborn who keep the old parador fountain in Crucible, whose rainbow waters can grant naga, briar or draughir lineage, travelled to Anvil to celebrate the Red Wind Corsairs' victory.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is noted as the site of Anvil, and Garev's earlier fall into a fissure near Casfall is recalled.

Hahnmark.t: The casting of Regrow the Land's Heart in Hahnmark uncovered the bones of the restless dead in war-scarred land, raising ghosts that could not be exorcised.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter's Guest of Karov was warned by Irontooth not to intrude on the Charnel Lord's affairs.

Karsk.t: Irontooth intends to do something for the people of Karsk and invited two representatives each from the Vales of Utovshy and Yarizov to discuss what the territory needs.

Madruga.t: Freeborn from Madruga's Crucible brought their transformative fountain water to Anvil. Marracossans from Trajadoz sought the senator for Madruga to renegotiate their treaty with the Empire.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Irontooth questioned why a self-styled True Son of Karsk now bases his military unit in Ossium.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaisa the Sewn Tongue, the executed leader of the Falconer cult, is noted as coming from Sermersuaq.

Spiral.t: An irritable yeofolk from Spiral Castle herded armed boggarts to Anvil, and two new League citizens from Spiral sought advice on becoming cicisbeo. The Silver Flame also called Spiral the heart of Urizen.

Temeschwar.t: A creature calling itself King Rat, a name tied to Temeschwar's rat plague and to strange deaths in the city, travelled south from Temeschwar towards Anvil.

Weirwater.t: Mendicant Garev was given poor directions near Syrene and is lying exhausted in Kaela's regio there, reachable by a Sentinel Gate conjunction on Saturday.

Judged by their company.d: The Temple of the Seven Virtues in Nemoria, funded by the Senate and staffed by Imperial volunteers, drew local pilgrims, sightseers and some opposition. Ressia i Afanera i Guerra, the sutannir from Feroz who runs it, refused would-be priests he judged insincere, including sworn warriors of the Asavean God of War and slaves sent by their owners, several of whom offered money. The Synod could refuse all training, train a carefully chosen few, or open training widely, which was estimated to add 10 Thrones a season to the Virtue fund. The Synod upheld an inquisition of Almodin Oktístis. Zemress Islanders in Segura feared he would put idolatrous symbols into the Iron Qanat, which he would certainly do.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel ship merchants are listed among the foreign traders who come to Nemoria for luxuries and rare materials.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn missionaries and wayfarers are among the Imperial volunteers serving as priests at the Nemoria temple.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn priests are central to the Nemoria temple: its overseer Ressia i Afanera i Guerra and the liaison Franco i Erigo are both Freeborn. At home, the Zemress Islanders in Segura objected to Almodin Oktístis decorating the Iron Qanat with Asavean idols, whatever the Coast's wider tolerance of the Asavean temple on its shores.

The League.t: League priests serve at the Nemoria temple, and one Asavean noble claimed a powerful League citizen would vouch for his slave. A Tassato printing house produced the popular pamphlet on the Asavean gods, and Oktístis had built a casino in Temeschwar.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the newly completed runeforge near Cargo is listed among the commissions Almodin Oktístis oversaw for the Senate.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Almodin Oktístis built a fortification in Varushka, and the page notes the recent controversy over its 'defilement'.

Judged by their company.o: Requests from Asaveans wishing to be ordained at the new Temple of the Seven Virtues in Nemoria prompted its overseer to seek the Imperial Synod's guidance, with three possible mandates offered on who, if anyone, should be trained. The page also covered the Synod's inquisition of the architect Almodin Oktístis, Zemress concerns over his commission for the Iron Qanat, and a pamphlet on the Asavean gods.

Segura/Sobral Grasses.t: The Iron Qanat, a fortified irrigation great work planned for the Sobral Grasses, could turn the sandy soil into rich farmland. The architect's insistence on working his gods' symbols into its foundations alarmed the Zemress settlers.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: The Honourable Press of Tassato Regario was the source of the widely copied Asavean religion pamphlet. It defended the work as helping the faithful resist Asavean priests and kept its patron secret.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Ressia i Afanera i Guerra, the sutannir who runs the Nemoria temple, comes from Feroz.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the runeforge near Cargo, built under Almodin Oktístis, is listed among his Senate commissions.

Segura.t: Segura welcomed the Senate's commission of the Iron Qanat, but its Zemress refugee community demanded assurance that Almodin Oktístis would not build Asavean idols into it, saying they would rather go without the great work than accept idolatry.

Tassato.t: The Honourable Press in Tassato printed 'A Primer on the Asavean Gods', which spread along the Blood Red Roads, and refused to reveal who paid for it.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: a casino in Temeschwar is listed among the commissions Almodin Oktístis oversaw for the Senate.

Keep talking.d: Baroness Katerine Lavasse announced that Josse Argent and fellow priests would meet Silk Farkas, Minister of Historical Research, at the Anvil Library at 12:30 on the Sunday of the Spring Equinox. They would bring artefacts of Suranni victories and wanted a tour of Anvil and introductions to Imperial generals, but no talk of theology. Jotun ghodi under a red banner camped on Gull Isle in West Marsh, Kallavesa. Agnar Tawny Owl asked why the Iron Jarl and Consul Silktongue had proposed it for a Meeting Place, and the ghodi sought tales rather than negotiations until summer. The Imperial Consul would choose who answered. Speaker Morna insisted the Grendel had not worked with the Children of Wrecks in the attack on Redoubt.

Grendel.t: Speaker Morna firmly denied any military alliance with the Children of Wrecks, calling them traitors and suckers, while freely admitting the Grendel had meant to seize Redoubt for its wealth.

Jotun.t: Jotun ghodi led by Agnar Tawny Owl camped on Gull Isle until summer, inviting knowledgeable Imperials to share tales about the proposed Meeting Place while refusing to discuss diplomatic terms. Meanwhile the war continued, with the Jotun conquering Bregasland as the Empire invaded Reinos.

Urizen.t: The Grendel insisted that their failed attack on Urizen's Redoubt had not been coordinated with the Children of Wrecks, though they openly admired the wealth of Cargo.

Wintermark.t: Jotun ghodi camped on Gull Isle, just off Wintermark's coast, and left a note of parley on the Kallavesa shore, alarming local hunters at first but showing no interest in raiding.

Keep talking.o: In Spring 387YE the Civil Service reported on foreign relations. A Suranni priestly delegation planned to visit Anvil to discuss military history, Jotun ghodi camped on Gull Isle asking how it was chosen for a new Meeting Place, and the Grendel denied any alliance with the Children of Wrecks.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: Gull Isle, a small tidal island in West Marsh with traces of old walls, became the camp of Jotun ghodi seeking tales about its proposed use as a Meeting Place, with a Sentinel Gate conjunction opening there at 10:35 on Saturday.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name the Bay of Catazar directly; its only apparent link is the Grendel discussion of the Children of Wrecks.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun were noted as having conquered Bregasland this season.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Feroz was noted as having been reclaimed by the Empire during the war with the Grendel.

Kallavesa.t: Jotun ghodi camped on Gull Isle off the Kallavesa coast, and their messenger left a note of parley above the tideline after crossing the Kallavesa causeway. A Sentinel Gate conjunction would open to the island on Saturday morning.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: Mareave was noted as having been claimed by the Empire from the orcs of the Broken Shore.

Redoubt.t: The Grendel denied that last season's failed attack on Redoubt was a joint effort with the Children of Wrecks, saying they had been as surprised as the Empire to see the wreckers arrive.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire was noted as having invaded Reinos this season.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Gull Isle was described as lying near where Kallavesa, Sermersuaq and Skallahn meet.

Skallahn.t: The Jotun ghodi under their tattered red banner crossed the Skallahn causeway at low tide to make camp on Gull Isle.

Veroigne.t: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni ambassador's seat in Chaubrette was said to lie to the west of Veroigne.

Key of dreams.d: Cathan Canae agreed to a parley through her Thane of the Rimebound Shore but refused ever to renew the Fist of Black Ice. She demanded the ruined ritual text back and planned to reward the Phoenix Rising coven for raising her citadel in Hope's Rest. Azoth opened a Shadow Souk night market. Phaleron offered a pocket of its archives and lectors to channel writings of four lost cultures. Wise Rangara invited six Varushkan storytellers to hear her tales. Ptolemy of the City of Salt and Sail sought a preliminary parley with the Archmage of Autumn. Arhallogen declined to parley and offered boons for lifting interdictions or declaring enmities, two of which the Conclave took up.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae's citadel stands in Hope's Rest in the Barrens, a territory held by Dawn, and she means to reward the coven that raised it.

Druj.t: Arhallogen cited the Empire's treatment of the Druj in Nesustak Forest as the reason she would make no offer about the Druj armies and septs being conquered. She also called the Rivers Run Red ritual she offered well known to the Druj.

Grendel.t: Arhallogen promised that if Ossegrahn were placed under enmity she would help the Empire against the Orcs of the Broken Shore, which would mean killing many Grendel. She warned that the Grendel themselves were also seeking a boon from Ossegrahn. The Conclave did place Ossegrahn under enmity.

Key of dreams.o: Six eternals answered the plenipotentiary messages of the Imperial archmages, arranging parleys, a night market, a library archive and conditional boons for the Spring Equinox summit. Arhallogen declined to parley but offered boons if the Conclave changed course; the interdiction on savage army enchantment was removed and Ossegrahn was placed under enmity.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: The Queen of Ice and Darkness meant to reward the Phoenix Rising coven for raising her citadel in Hope's Rest. Her herald would imbue an unworked set of mage armour, brought by the coven, with a shard of her power.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Arhallogen's herald appeared at Spiral Castle, and the Senator for Spiral, Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian, might be brought to the Cathan Canae parley.

The Barrens.t: Cathan Canae acknowledged that her citadel had been called forth in Hope's Rest in the Barrens. She planned to give the Phoenix Rising coven a personal gift for that work.

Keys of Enlightenment.d: Sumaah sought Imperial mithril and weirwood for its war with the Asaveans. The City of Salt and Sail offered to carry at least a hundred wains until the end of Winter 388YE, if Ambassador Accalon named a price. Oxtitocszin sent an essay on the paragon Sjördeyr and offered scholars for historical research. The Republic doubted the Liberty Pact could survive without the Commonwealth and feared an Imperial–Axou voting bloc. The true liao gift will continue. The ship Tumlare, struck by an unknown malady, needs aid from the Hand of Guerra. Agent Vassa's network vanished, and several possible investigations were offered, most needing Albrecht von Holberg's cooperation.

Highguard.t: Ambassador Accalon of Highguard was asked to name a price and volume for mithril and weirwood wains, and the Sjördeyr enquiry he received came from the Senator of Bastion.

The League.t: The League's Regario Dossier, held by Albrecht von Holberg, lost its Zemeh spy network, and League ship-captains could join a special scouting voyage to Zemeh if the Spymaster arranged one.

Keys of Enlightenment.o: In Summer 388YE, Sumaah ambassador Oxtitocszin offered a deal to transport Imperial mithril and weirwood and shared an essay on the paragon Sjördeyr. The Republic also voiced doubts about the Liberty Pact, a Sumaah ship lay stricken by sickness in Free Landing, and the Regario Dossier's spy network in Zemeh went dark.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: The Regario Dossier's offices here received a single genuine-seeming ciphered message reporting dead and vanished agents in Zemeh, and their contact attempts since have gone unanswered.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the Regario Dossier's offices in Tassato Regario received the sole ciphered warning that the Zemeh network had been rolled up.

Kingdom by the sea.d: Farsighted offered a Map the Eastern Sea scouting voyage past Druj lands. The greater the strength committed, the more it would reveal, from territory names to Gloomsea's secrets, the Axou coast, Thronaskoni, Skoura, the Cliffs of Vore and rumoured eastern isles. Tempest offered a Raid Asavean Shipping voyage now that the Pax Sarcophan had ended the bounty. A flotilla of 15,000 strength could draw out and sink one great warship such as the Wind Tamer. Raptor offered a Hunt Free Landing Kraken voyage that yields valuable Ambrellic, with Freeborn and corsair fleets favoured. Johann Van Basten offered two crowns a portion for the Ambrellic. All three were opportunities only.

Druj.t: The proposed eastern armada would slip past Druj lands while their attention is on Sarangrave, avoiding battle. It could map their coasts and reveal how the Hathjuk sept supports them.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: sinking an Asavean warship would reduce the naval strength the Asaveans could deploy to help the Grendel.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are listed among those the bravest Asavean merchants sail across the Sea of Storms to trade with.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn fleets would count one rank higher, and corsair fleets two ranks higher, when hunting the juvenile kraken off Free Landing, because they know those treacherous waters best.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sarcophan trader Johann Van Basten, who offered to buy Ambrellic, was visiting the Alivetti Estates on business.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule, like the Druj, are said to be tight-lipped about what lies beyond the mountains near the Cliffs of Vore.

Kingdom by the sea.o: After the victors of the Great Race met Rhianos, the eternal's heralds offered Imperial fleet captains three possible voyages for the season after the Autumn Equinox 387YE: mapping the eastern coastline, raiding Asavean shipping, and hunting the juvenile kraken off Free Landing.

Forest of Ulnak/Gloomsea.t: Gloomsea's misty isles, kept unmapped by the Hathjuk sept, could have most of their secrets uncovered if enough ships joined the voyage. At minimum this would reveal how the Hathjuk support the Druj.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Fleets could spend the season hunting one of the immature kraken released off Free Landing for its prized Ambrellic. The creatures could not be eradicated, however.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Bay has already been mapped by the Empire. The young, hungry kraken unleashed in its waters were the quarry of the proposed hunt.

Forest of Ulnak.t: An eastern armada of 5,000 to 10,000 strength could delve into the mist-wreathed, largely unmapped isles of Gloomsea on this territory's coast.

Madruga.t: Shining beacons over Madruga's coast had forced some of the kraken released by the Children of Wrecks into the open, letting fleets hunt them. Others hidden in deep caverns would remain a threat whatever happened.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: With 10,000 to 15,000 strength, the armada could push south past the Salt Flats and chart the coast of the Axou territories beyond.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj focus on Sarangrave is what gave the armada its chance to sail past Druj lands.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: a wealthy Sarcophan trader was visiting the Alivetti Estates on business and offered to buy any Ambrellic gathered.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sea of Snow is noted as already mapped by the Empire and home to massive, mature kraken.

Kith and kin.d: Nigel Hornbeam's unanimous judgement asked the Highborn to help the beaters patrol Marcher borders. Two mandates became possible: Marcher beaters could hunt the traitor Dalton Royse, and the Highborn unconquered could spoil Jotun supply caches in Southmoor. Plans for the Bailiff of the Downs to organise paid beaters stalled when Bounders Hall in Sarcombe fell to the Jotun. The Empire could build Bounders Halls in other Marcher territories, fortify Southmoor with the Third Pie, or build an unbreakable fort at Fishers Rock in Bregasland. Highguard's peerless kinship was extended by two seasons. Jotun ghosts appeared at Halebale Farm in Oddmire. James Forrester used a Wayleave to commission a Bounders Hall in Bregasland.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly could mandate its unconquered to spoil Jotun caches in Southmoor. Its peerless kinship was also extended by two more seasons, and it could now name the aid it would offer without waiting for the other nation's assembly.

Jotun.t: Jotun forces had invaded the Mournwold, exploiting Jarl Haakon's supply caches and Dalton Royse's intelligence. They captured Bounders Hall in Sarcombe and threatened Bregasland.

The Marches.t: The Marchers gained the chance to hunt the traitor Dalton Royse, to have their beaters paid to Beat the Bounds, and to build new fortifications. The first new Bounders Hall was commissioned in Bregasland.
