Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard's peerless kinship is said to have arisen from the flush of victory in Zenith.

Kith and kin.o: Following the Marcher Assembly's judgement accepting Highguard's peerless kinship, Highborn priests worked with the Marchers to defend the Mournwold against the Jotun, which opened up mandates, a new way for beaters to defend the bounds and proposed fortifications. A Bounders Hall was then commissioned in Bregasland at the Summer Solstice 386YE.

Mitwold/Oddmire.t: Spectral Jotun raiders gathered at Halebale Farm after farmers dug up an ancient relic, and locals insisted the Champion of Prosperity lead fighters and exorcists to clear them out.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: Mentioned in passing: Freemoor's existing keep is one of the established fortresses the Third Pie would complete the Mourn's line of defences with.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Mentioned in passing: Greensward's existing keep is one of the established fortresses the Third Pie would complete the Mourn's line of defences with.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Much of Southmoor was held by Jotun armies, with hidden supply caches, the traitor Dalton Royse at large and Bounders Hall in Sarcombe fallen. The Third Pie fortification could be built at Sarcombe once the Jotun are driven out.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland had no Imperial fortification, so an unbreakable, haunted fort at Fishers Rock with a Friar of the Dead Marshes was proposed. A Bounders Hall was commissioned there via a Wayleave to extend the beaters' protection.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold was named as a possible site for a Bounders Hall and a Bailiff to extend the beaters' protection. Jotun ghosts also appeared at a farm in Oddmire.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold was under Jotun invasion and lost Bounders Hall, halting plans for paid beaters to Beat the Bounds until it is retaken. The Third Pie fortification was proposed to make it impossible to put the territory under threat.

Upwold.t: Upwold was named as a possible site for a Bounders Hall and a new Bailiff, so that the beaters could defend it against invasion.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the victory in Zenith is cited as the origin of Highguard's peerless kinship.

Knocking on every door.d: Irada von Temeschwar's statement passed 250-0 at the Autumn Equinox 385YE. Any such site would swell Vigilance congregations for a year. It would let the Vigilance assembly send the vigilant into a named territory to root out threats, at the cost of disruption there. It would also make people less inclined to rely on magistrates, and would strengthen aspirationalism. Three General Assembly mandates were prepared. The first is his fire-damaged basilica in Bastion, which needs restoring and focuses on Empire-wide threats. The second is his tomb in the Necropolis, focused on local threats and the young. The third is the Ringblack Shrine in Tassato Regario, focused on direct action and ringblack stories. The choice could rekindle old disputes between the Virtue assemblies.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the threat of Grendel invasion is credited with silencing old arguments over Berechiah, and a League mountebank removing someone paid by a Grendel to spy is given as an example of the vigilant acting without magistrates.

Highguard.t: Berechiah, who left the League to become Highborn, has two of the three candidate sites in Highguard: his damaged basilica in Bastion and his tomb in the Necropolis. Highborn Vigilants and the Custodes Clavium stand to play a central role in the consecration.

The League.t: Berechiah was a Tassatan orphan and bravo, and one candidate site is a Vigilance shrine in Tassato Regario. That choice is expected to have a profound influence on the League's bravos, though vigilant investigations in League cities could disrupt Businesses.

Knocking on every door.o: After the Assembly of Vigilance endorsed consecrating an inspirational location to the contentious exemplar Berechiah with true liao, the Civil Service treated the statement as the first Writ of Consecration. They identified three candidate sites, each of which would shape his inspiration differently.

Tassato/Enterio.t: Mentioned in passing: Merchant-Prince Maria Moor, who published Berechiah's works, closed her press and retired to an orange orchard in Enterio, where she still lives.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: The former Moor's Mill printworks, which published Berechiah's books, is now a shrine where bravos and mountebanks watch the neighbourhood and print "Stories of the Vigilance". Its congregation is willing to see it consecrated as an inspirational location focused on direct action.

Bastion.t: Berechiah's basilica in Bastion, burned in 303YE and never repaired, is one proposed site. Restoring it would need a commission of at least 10 wains of white granite and 5 of weirwood, and could lead to a new title, the Clavem Iudicii.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: recent events in Holberg involving sword scholars, Emperor Frederick and the mandate of Erasmo di Tassato are expected to combine with ringblack novels to influence League bravos if the Tassato Regario shrine is chosen.

Necropolis.t: Berechiah's little-known tomb, built under the name Bertolli di Tassato, lies in the Necropolis and is one proposed site. Consecrating it would emphasise teaching the young and guarding against local threats, and would likely shake up the sodality of the Silent Bell.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is not named on the page; it only notes generally that vigilant investigations in a League city could disrupt Businesses for a season.

Tassato.t: Tassato is Berechiah's birthplace, where he rose from orphan to wealthy citizen. It hosts one of the three candidate sites, the Ringblack Shrine in Tassato Regario.

Know your enemy.d: The mandate passed by over a thousand votes but without a greater majority, so it was ineffective in Urizen, Varushka and Wintermark, where heresy is now more likely to take deep root. Three Peace-hallowed relics remain with Synod figures, and Cardinal of Wisdom Silas of the Cenotaph has not stepped down. Doubts about this threaten the credibility of the Assembly of Nine and of the other assemblies. The Silent Bell now answers to the Vigilance Assembly and could investigate one false virtue each season. The options are spying on Faraden for Vengeance, Axos for Peace, the Iron Confederacy for Freedom, Urizeni sword scholars for Hatred or the Druj for Fear. Every option carries serious risk of capture. Wintermark's own mandate has left it outside other assemblies' influence unless they reach a greater majority.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is not named; its only link is the Barrens, where the Freedom Heresy rebels once tried to found a nation of the free.

Druj.t: The Silent Bell could be sent into the Mallum to learn how the Druj create and understand Fear, but most of the spies would certainly be caught and brutally executed.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; it holds Feroz, where the Suranni were once invited to reclaim escaped slaves.

Highguard.t: Historically, many Highborn embraced Purity (Hatred) and some refused to give it up. Constant vigilance is still needed against it in Highguard, with notable failures reaching the top of Highborn society, and Caleb of the Cenotaph's commissioned research on Hatred is available across the Empire.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are named as the foe that the people of Whittle used Hatred to fight, and as the object of a hypothetical Marcher priest's hatred.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: it notes that even the Navarr members of the Silent Bell would struggle to infiltrate the hidden Montanian survivors.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marches are cited as a place where Hatred has history, from Whittle's reliance on it to old household grudges that the Marcher Assembly denounces.

Urizen.t: Because of its scepticism towards the Synod, the mandate had no effect in Urizen, and heresy there is now more likely to put down deep roots. Severus of the Blinding Sun is already preaching Hatred across its citadels, and the Silent Bell could be sent to spy on such sword scholars in the mountains at grave personal risk.

Varushka.t: The mandate had no effect in Varushka, leaving its people more open to false virtues and heresy that would be hard to uproot. The page also recalls that Varushkans destroyed the Montanian sept.

Wintermark.t: After the Wintermark Assembly urged its people to heed only the stormcrows, Wintermark ignores other assemblies' mandates unless they reach a greater majority. It is therefore more vulnerable to false virtues unless the Wintermark Assembly enacts its own mandate, with its own liao, urging people to bring malign auras to the stormcrows.

Know your enemy.o: The Imperial Synod chose to reject the false virtues, and Viviane Barossa's General Assembly mandate urged the Empire to stay vigilant against them, though it had no effect in Urizen, Varushka or Wintermark. The mandate left open questions about the Peace auras still borne at the heart of the Synod, and it offered the Vigilance Assembly a chance to send the Silent Bell to spy on followers of false virtues.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Feroz is recalled as the place where the Empire invited the Suranni to reclaim escaped slaves inspired by a Freedom-embracing leader.

Kalino.t: The escaped slaves who followed a leader devoted to Freedom are believed to be held, most likely in Kalino, after being dragged back there in chains. The Silent Bell could seek them out, though captured spies would be executed and relations with the Iron Confederacy reversed.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Morrow appears only in the opening story, where Lucia is said to be good enough to cross swords with its best scholars.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold is recalled through the people of Whittle, who relied on Hatred to fight the Jotun and are now gone after failed reintegration.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens are recalled as where the Freedom Heresy rebels settled and where their descendants, the Montanians, later lived until their destruction.

Laid low.d: Before the assault the traitor Old Bushel Sykes helped the Jotun turn the Otterway into a major causeway, now finished, and spread anti-Imperial sentiment with stolen liao. The Jotun held back from invading Mitwold. The Strong Reeds and House Greywater then rose across Bregasland, aided by captains, beaters, Tom of Otterly and summoned Knights of Glory. Allied armies crossed from West Marsh and took Fisher's Rock. North Fens fell quickly and Grey Fens after harder fighting. The Empire also took the Rushes and parts of Ottermire, while the Jotun regrouped near Graven Rock. About four thousand fighters died, mostly Imperial. A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered a chance to defend House Greywater's estate from a Jotun band.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm's general notes that their sister legion is fighting the Druj in the Battens.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fist of the Mountains' general quotes Highborn siblings saying now is the time of miracles.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Tusks advanced from Graven March with a balanced strategy and supernatural clarity, and their scouts helped time the strike on Fisher's Rock. General Jakkan of the Fell Hammers made a point of seeking out the Imperial Orcs in battle.

Jotun.t: The Jotun completed the Otterway but chose not to invade Mitwold. They were then driven from both Fens, the Rushes and parts of Ottermire, and regrouped near Graven Rock. They fought to preserve their strength, and the Fell Hammers showed open disdain for the alliance with the Fishers.

Navarr.t: Isaella's Dance fought with envenomed weapons that killed swiftly, adding to the slaughter of Fishers and Jotun in the fens.

The Brass Coast.t: The Fire of the South marched to oust Mathilda Fisher and hunt Stephen of Sarcombe. The newly raised Burning Falcon blazed across the fens, and the Jotun eagerly sought them out after a century-old grudge.

The Marches.t: The Strong Reeds' uprising and the Drakes' assault helped return Bregasland to the Empire, and many wavering households welcomed the Marcher armies. Traitors such as Old Bushel Sykes, however, keep some Free Bregas support alive.

Wintermark.t: The Fist of the Mountains fought in the vanguard against the yegarra, and the Summer Storm attacked from Kallavesa via Fisher's Rock. The Winterfolk fought honourably, suffered fewer deaths and claimed more ground.

Laid low.o: In spring 385YE eight Imperial armies, alongside the Strong Reeds' uprising inside the territory, drove the Jotun and Mathilda Fisher's 'Free Bregas' forces out of most of Bregasland. The territory became Imperial again, though Fisher refused to surrender and called her supporters to retreat.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: Grey Fens was liberated after a more drawn-out fight, with the Fishers scattered and the Jotun driven back.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: North Fens fell almost at once, including Fisher's Rock. A Jotun band now threatens House Greywater's estate here, and the Strong Reeds' general has been asked to stop it through the Sentinel Gate.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: The Jotun had focused their work on the Otterway around Ottery and Sallow and fought more comfortably on Ottermire's firmer ground. The Empire occupied only parts of the region.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: Imperial armies crossed the river from West Marsh to besiege Mathilda Fisher's forces at Fisher's Rock.

Mitwold/Oddmire.t: With the Otterway completed before the Imperial assault, Oddmire is still under threat of Jotun invasion.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland was liberated and became an Imperial territory again, with the Senate to decide which nation receives it. Mathilda Fisher still lingers, rallying her remaining supporters to retreat.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fisher storytellers praise those Fishers who fled to Hordalant as valiant heroes.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South's general vows to hunt Stephen of Sarcombe for fleeing Kahraman.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa served as the launch point for the attack: the Summer Storm moved out from here, and allied armies crossed the river from West Marsh into Bregasland.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: with Liathaven under Jotun control, the Otterway may be meant to bring white granite into the fens for fortifications.

Mitwold.t: The Jotun did not invade Mitwold this season, but the Otterway is complete and the territory remains under threat.

Land fit for heroes.d: Wintermark gave up Skarsind, liberated from the Thule in late 377YE, as a homeland for the Imperial Orcs in recognition of their friendship and heroic deeds. The Synod could still veto the assignment, though not the relinquishment, until the first Senate session of the Winter Solstice. If vetoed, the Senate could assign Skarsind to any nation. Otherwise the orcs moved their holdings to Skarsind with civil service help and bonesetters' savings. Orc soldiers living in the territory will elect a senator by placing weapons before candidates. That senator will appoint generals and the Advisor on Orc Affairs. The Brilliant Shore becomes an Imperial Orc national seat, and the Steel Fist's offices move to Torfast.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the offices of the Steel Fist bourse seat were relocated away from Crown's Quay to Torfast.

Imperial Orcs.t: The orcs gained Skarsind as a homeland and the right to elect a senator by a vote of their soldiers. That senator will now appoint the Summer Storm and Winter Sun generals and the Advisor on Orc Affairs, ending the old pit-fighting stop-gap. All of this still depended on the Synod not vetoing the assignment.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is noted as having been liberated from the Thule orcs in late 377YE.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gave up its fourth territory to the Imperial Orcs, a decision not popular with everyone in the nation. The Senate was to decide whether the steinr Joakim keeps the Brilliant Shore seat until Summer 380YE or whether it passes to the orcs at once.

Land fit for heroes.o: Following Wintermark's relinquishment of Skarsind and its ratification through Empress Britta's Imperial Favour, the Senate assigned the territory to the Imperial Orcs at the Autumn Equinox 379YE, giving them a homeland for the first time. Over the winter Imperial Orcs moved there in large numbers, and new arrangements were set out for their senator, generals and national titles.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: The offices of the Steel Fist were relocated to Torfast in Southpine. Sarcophan Delves merchants are now obliged to trek there to deliver the seat's ilium, which they resent.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Steel Fist's offices were moved from Crown's Quay to Torfast in Skarsind.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind became the Imperial Orc homeland, with large numbers of orcs settling there over the winter. Its Brilliant Shore became an Imperial Orc national bourse seat. The assignment remained open to a Synod veto, which would halt further efforts to help the orcs claim it.

Landscape.d: Heralds of the Bronze Artisan helped the Civil Service survey the area. The Red Depths mithril seam could be an Imperial Bourse seat for 170 thrones producing 16 wains a season, or a national seat for 50 thrones producing 19 wains, because Kahraman's mining families would offer their labour only for a national seat. A Mountainhome ministry, costing 15 white granite and 45 crowns, was proposed so that a mine captain could oversee the weltsilver and orichalcum workings. The House of Fire and Flame sought mining rights through a Declaration of Concord. The Senate approved the Red Depths as a national seat. The work was disrupted by the Lasambrian Jotun but completed, with the title to be first elected at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

Jotun.t: The new mineral wealth makes Serra Damata an even more tempting target for the Jotun. The collapsed passes stop them striking the region directly, but they could still attack through Gambit, and the Lasambrian Jotun disrupted the Red Depths work before the Winter Solstice.

The Brass Coast.t: Kahraman's mining families secured the Red Depths as a national Bourse seat of the Brass Coast, the territory's first mineral wealth kept for its own people. A Mountainhome mine captain was also proposed to keep the feuding families' workings safe.

Landscape.o: After Imperial heroes used the House of Fire and Flame's rondures to tear open Redgate Pass in Serra Damata, the shattered mountain was found to hold mithril, weltsilver, orichalcum and bloodstones. Several opportunities were offered to exploit the wealth, and the Senate chose to build the Red Depths as a Brass Coast national Bourse seat.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: Gambit, still under Imperial control, became the likely route for any Jotun assault on Serra Damata. A significant fortification there was recommended to protect the whole territory.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: The ruined mountain here holds the Red Depths mithril seam, now a national Bourse seat, along with proposed Mountainhome mines for weltsilver, orichalcum and bloodstones. The House of Fire and Flame also asked for the right to mine here, while the region remains a prime Jotun target.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman gained a national mithril Bourse seat on top of its two Imperial seats. However, with Fort Braydon destroyed, the territory remains largely unprotected, and a rank two or greater fort in Gambit or Serra Damata was urged to deter Jotun attacks.

Liathaven.t: The collapse of the mountain passes means Jotun armies can no longer move between Liathaven and northern Kahraman.

Reinos.t: The blocked passes mean Jotun armies in Reinos can no longer reach northern Kahraman directly.

Lantern's light.d: The star's impact lit the night over Varushka and northern Dawn, was heard as far as Highguard, and was accompanied by scattered starfalls, some bearing small amounts of ilium. A Thule delegation came through Brez to the cabalists of Void and offered 4 rings of ilium each season, but only to a Varushkan and only while Varushka stays at peace with Otkodov. The warlock Rak invited the Empire to build an embassy, preferably Varushkan. Gar the Trader sought to join the Northern trade network, but Dogri Thulebane's control of the northern Skarsind passes blocked this. The Thule would not remove him without an invitation from the Senate.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the night sky over parts of northern Dawn briefly blazed crimson-bright as the star fell.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the sound of the star's impact was heard as far south as Highguard.

Imperial Orcs.t: Starfalls struck parts of Skarsind, and Thule trade through the Imperial Orc territory to Torfast was blocked by Dogri Thulebane's hold on its northern passes. Gar regretted losing the chance to learn more about the Imperial Orcs.

Thule.t: The Thule honoured their agreement by sharing the star metal from Sküld with Varushka, sought a Varushkan-run embassy, and hoped to join the Northern trade network. They would not move against Dogri in Skarsind without an invitation from the Senate.

Varushka.t: Varushka alone was offered the ilium share for keeping faith with the Thule, and gained it as the national Bourse seat Gift of the Dwindling Star, held so long as it stays at peace with Otkodov. The Thule also favoured a Varushkan embassy.

Wintermark.t: Burning rock fell on parts of northern Wintermark, and the stubborn Winterfolk following Dogri Thulebane held the Skarsind passes against the Thule.

Lantern's light.o: The red star fell into the Thule region of Sküld in Otkodov, and the Thule offered Varushka a share of the resulting ilium as they had agreed. The Senate accepted, creating the Gift of the Dwindling Star as a Varushkan national Bourse seat with offices at Void in Brez.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Mentioned in passing: Wendell's Hope in Miekarova was among the Thule's suggested sites for the ilium offices; the page does not name Mieriada itself.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: The red star slammed into Sküld, creating the star metal deposit the Thule chose to share with Varushka.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Mentioned in passing: Dogri Thulebane's control of the routes from Silver Peaks was cited as a reason the Thule would not risk caravans south.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: Mentioned in passing: the page refers only to the northern Skarsind passes held by Dogri Thulebane and does not name Southpine.

Volodmartz/Brez.t: The Thule delegation came down through the mountains of Brez to the cabalists of Void, where Rak was hosted and where the Gift of the Dwindling Star's offices were established.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: Ivarsgard in Karsk was one of the Thule's suggested sites for the ilium trade offices.

Miekarova.t: The pillar of ash from the impact was visible for hours across Miekarova, and Wendell's Hope was suggested as a possible site for the ilium offices.

Otkodov.t: The red star struck eastern Otkodov and left a significant deposit of star metal. The ilium trade depends on Varushka remaining at peace with the territory.

Sermersuaq.t: Dogri Thulebane's control of the routes from Silver Peaks helped deter the Thule from sending caravans south.

Skarsind.t: Starfalls struck parts of Skarsind, and Dogri Thulebane's 'Skarsind congregation of Loyalty' held the northern passes, violently turning back Thule orcs surveying a road.

Volodmartz.t: The ash pillar was visible across Volodmartz, and the Thule delegation came to Void in Brez, where the new ilium offices were established.

Large but far away.d: Asavea's Plenum began moving towards an accord with Jarm, and trade with Nemoria suffered a penalty while its temple stood damaged. Imperial captains evacuated defeated rebels, and Marracossans settled in Trajadoz, Torres, where they sought Senate permission for a temple. Commonwealth magicians crowded the Siroc embassy, raising Madruga's taxes. The Commonwealth proposed a schloss by the Lyceum, while Frederick di Sarvos offered his Diora University as an alternative. Jarm cut mana crystal exports, and war with the Commonwealth began after a failed coup in Lantir. Sumaah planned a Synod summit. Sarcophan enclave and Kruidenkenner opportunities would expire at the season's end, and the Gjullit docks offer had already lapsed.

Grendel.t: Under the orders of the Salt Lords, the Grendel still let Asavean merchants dock at the Feroz temple, so the goodwill it once gave Imperial fleet owners now flows to the Grendel.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Accalon of Felix's Watch of Highguard is named as Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Chainbreaker Pakt of the Imperial Orcs is named as Ambassador to Asavea.

Navarr.t: The Sumaah präst Nikolaj Rondtyig has walked the trods with several stridings. He planned to go straight to the Navarr camp at Anvil to consult the Advisor on the Vallorn and hoped to join a foray through the Sentinel Gate.

The Brass Coast.t: Marracossan refugees have settled in Trajadoz in Madruga, and Commonwealth trade through Siroc has raised the territory's prosperity. The Brass Coast also faces a choice over a Commonwealth schloss near the Lyceum.

The League.t: Frederick di Sarvos offered to build his Diora University, which would draw Commonwealth trade to Sarvos. The Tassato Mana Exchange faces reduced Jarmish crystal supplies, and Lucia Sanguineo di Tassato serves as Ambassador to the Commonwealth.

Varushka.t: The chance to authorise a Sarcophan enclave at Isember in Karsk, with reciprocal Imperial enclaves in the Delves, would expire at the end of the Autumn Equinox.

Large but far away.o: This Wind of Fortune set out the state of the Empire's relations with the great foreign powers at the Autumn Equinox 383YE. Key developments were Marracossan refugees settling in Trajadoz, Commonwealth magicians arriving to study Imperial lore, and Jarm and the Commonwealth sliding into war over Lantir.

Madruga/Torres.t: Around a thousand Marracossan refugees have made camp in the largely abandoned town of Trajadoz and wish to stay. They asked for a Senate motion permitting a temple to their three gods, and a separate group set out on pilgrimage to Anvil.

Feroz.t: The Asavean temple in Feroz still stands and Asavean merchants still dock there, though its goodwill now benefits the Grendel. The Marracossans cited it when hoping for a temple of their own.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Trajadoz was founded to foster trade between the mines of newly conquered Kahraman and Sarvos.

Karsk.t: A Sarcophan proposal for an enclave at Isember awaited a Senate decision, with a deadline at the end of the Autumn Equinox.

Madruga.t: Marracossan refugees have settled in Trajadoz, and Commonwealth trade through Siroc raised Madruga's taxation by ten Thrones, rising to fifteen if the proposed Lyceum schloss were built. The Gjullit offer to build docks in Siroc has expired.

Sarvos.t: The Sarcophan enclave proposal at the Alivetti estates was extended to the end of the Autumn Equinox. If Frederick di Sarvos's Diora University were built first, Commonwealth trade benefits would flow to Sarvos instead of Madruga.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Trajadoz last swelled with people during the invasion of Segura in 363YE and emptied after its reclamation in 378YE.

Tassato.t: As Jarm stockpiles for war, the Tassato Mana Exchange will see a slight reduction in the mana crystals available from its highest tier.

Last rays of the sun.d: In Miaren the Quiet Step stormed Rhonwen's Fall and killed the Empty Hands' Grand Archon. More than a hundred Navarr died, and both steadings and much ancient artwork were ruined. In Kronemark the Silence Arc used the Tower of the Eagle regio to build a mithril, crystal and ilium gate to bring more scions from Day. The Imperial assault killed the Grand Archon before the gate was anchored, and its collapse annihilated the scions. Over two hundred Imperial soldiers fell. A burning Sungate remains, held shut only while the Conclave keeps enmity with Cold Sun. Remnant scions now threaten Wood Heath, the Tower of Light and Shadow and the Icy Crag.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: some Navarr from Rhonwen's Fall fled into Astolat, and the pillar of fire was seen as far east as Laroc.

Highguard.t: Asenath led the Granite Pillar into Hahnmark and spearheaded the assault on the Tower of the Eagle, while Highborn warbands also fought in Miaren; Highborn soldiers were among those killed or marked by the collapsing gate.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Summer Storm and the newly mustered Autumn Hammers protected the Highborn advance at the Tower of the Eagle, chanting the names of those lost in Skarsind; heralds of Janon and observers from the City of Bar and Bond accompanied them, and many orcs died or were scarred by the gate's backlash.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step's general urged the thorns on with the words "Liathaven awaits".

Navarr.t: The Quiet Step avenged the burning of First Voice Glade by destroying the Empty Hands, but more than a hundred Navarr were slain and the sanctuary and scholarship of Rhonwen's Fall were left in ruins.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the earlier beacon built in Segura with Lashonar's help is recalled as one of the victories against the scions.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the column of blue-green flame from the Tower of the Eagle was visible as far south as Tassato.

Urizen.t: Urizen warbands swelled the ranks fighting in Miaren, and a remnant scion force is advancing on the Tower of Light and Shadow in Redoubt, which the Penumbral Watcher Izora Highwind must stop.

Varushka.t: The Quiet Step marched out of Karov to fight in Miaren, and a scion remnant threatens to break the high hill above Volchitrava and damage the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun in Miekarova.

Wintermark.t: After six months of defending Hahnmark alone by the light of the beacons, Wintermark saw the Silence Arc destroyed, but it is left with a deadly Sungate in Kronemark and a scion threat to Wood Heath.

Last rays of the sun.o: In Summer 386YE the last two scion armies of Cold Sun in the Empire were destroyed. The Quiet Step and Navarr allies wiped out the Empty Hands at Rhonwen's Fall in Miaren, while the Granite Pillar, Summer Storm and Autumn Hammers broke the Silence Arc at the Tower of the Eagle in Hahnmark, ending the incursion but leaving a deadly gateway behind.

Hahnmark/Kronemark.t: The Silence Arc were destroyed at the Tower of the Eagle, and Kronemark now holds the Sungate, a lethal gateway to the Day realm kept closed only by Conclave enmity towards Cold Sun.

Hahnmark/Wood Heath.t: Scions are trying to unleash a disaster from a north-eastern peak that would devastate New Dunhall and nearby commissions, and Tobrytan Dunning, thane of Dunhearth Hall, must stop them.

Karov/Duzekani.t: Mentioned in passing: the events at the White Tower in Duzekani are recalled as a warning when planning the attack on the Tower of the Eagle.

Miaren/Greenfalls.t: The Empty Hands, based in Greenfalls, were annihilated at Rhonwen's Fall, but the Fallshome and Longshadow steadings were utterly ruined and the ancient carvings partly defaced.

Miaren/Serenael.t: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step entered Miaren at Serenael before moving south against the Empty Hands.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: Mentioned in passing: the scions' earlier channelling of Storm Pass above Pakaanan's Pass, which damaged Whitelake, is recalled as the model for the threat to Wood Heath.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: some of the Navarr who lived at Rhonwen's Fall escaped into Astolat ahead of the scions.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the previous season's blunting of the Winnowers' dying curse in Bastion, aided by Lord Rain, is recalled.

Hahnmark.t: Three Imperial armies, independent warriors and the host of the red bear destroyed the Silence Arc at the Tower of the Eagle, but its ruins now hold a burning gate that kills anyone who comes within about a quarter mile.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step marched from Karov, and the earlier defence of the Haamrikoht Stone and events at Duzekani are recalled.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: named in the Quiet Step general's rallying cry, "Liathaven awaits".

Miaren.t: The Empty Hands were destroyed and their tree-killing aura ceased, but more than a hundred Navarr died, Rhonwen's Fall was ruined and a few scion warbands remain at large.

Miekarova.t: A remnant of the Blade of Skies threatens to break the hill above Volchitrava and damage the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun; Ceinwen Eternal, the Master of Ice and Darkness, must stop them and has received aid from Silverbrow.

Redoubt.t: Scions who looted the Brilliant Star are advancing on the Tower of Light and Shadow to transform it, and the Penumbral Watcher Izora Highwind is responsible for stopping them.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the beacon that artists and musicians built there with Lashonar to lure scion warbands is recalled.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the costly fight against the Still Walkers there, whose remnants unleashed storms across the territory, is recalled as the source of the orcs' grief.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the pillar of blue-green fire from Hahnmark could be seen from Tassato.

Lay the foundations.d: The judgement passed 750-0 with a greater majority. Just over two years in, slightly more than two-thirds of the thousand wains has been contributed, and a little over 281 wains of white granite are still needed. Popular support added four ranks to the Cinderpath Exchange for at least a year. The Senate could approve seven mithril bells in place of 49 wains of white granite. The City of Gold and Lead will offer to buy one Highborn commission each season. Congregations can preach the Second Age of Virtue to cut labour costs. The Custodes Clavium offer to empower the Highborn Speaker if the work is finished by Spring 389YE. The Assembly must also choose which Virtue titles receive offices first.

Highguard.t: Highguard has made the Grand Inspiration its highest calling, leaving fewer chances to attend to other matters. Its citizens are pooling resources to buy white granite, and its Assembly is invited to direct how the holy site's interiors and offices will be used.

Lay the foundations.o: After the Highborn National Assembly upheld Eli of the Cenotaph's judgement declaring completion of the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion to be the nation's highest calling, Highguard's enthusiasm surged. A range of new opportunities to speed and shape the project arose.

Bastion.t: The vast, unfinished Grand Inspiration with its seven towers is rising in Bastion and already awes visitors. Volunteers inspired by the Second Age preaching may come to help build it, and Bastion's senator gets the City of Gold and Lead's commission offer in Autumn 388YE.

Casinea.t: Casinea's senator will receive the City of Gold and Lead's chit in Winter 388YE, allowing a single Casinean structure to be offered for sale to the City.

Necropolis.t: Necropolis's senator goes first: this summit they can use Ephisis' Scale to put one Necropolis commission up for sale to the City of Gold and Lead. Any deal still needs Senate approval at the next summit.

Reikos.t: Reikos's senator will receive the City of Gold and Lead's chit in Summer 388YE, allowing one structure in Reikos to be put up for sale to fund the Grand Inspiration.

Lean and athirst.d: Championed by Sławomir Rabovich Bolotstrazh, with Ambassador Kindra Surefoot raising the matter with Otkodov, more than seventy Varushkan units joined Thule warlocks and hunters to execute trudniki wherever found. Draughir in Karsk and Ossium were questioned, often via insight ceremonies, though without violence. The unpopular Ketsov funded a bonus to units protecting the vales and hope for national recognition. Hunters recovered forest materials and a strength-giving concoction, elder's gift, which wise ones asked the Apothecaries Guild to assess and report on in the Senate; the Constitutional Court confirmed the Guild could share such findings. The waning warding power of Varushka's roads was mysteriously restored, and Sentinel Gate conjunctions revealed troubled wagon raiders in Drownbark Forest and Karsk.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish questing-knights are credited, alongside the schlacta, with helping keep monsters at bay while Varushka's road wards weakened.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ketsov of Ossium are resented for having suffered less under the Druj yoke than their neighbours.

Thule.t: On the instruction of the Dragons of Otkodov, the Claws of the Dragon and Thule hunters worked with Varushka, leading the hunt in Krevsaty, the Bonewood and the Webwood and supporting Imperial efforts elsewhere. The Thule reportedly have no use for elder's gift and might sell it to the Speaker to the Leshun.

Varushka.t: Varushkan schlacta, wagon raiders and wardens wiped out the trudniki and gained loot, but draughir and reclusive citizens in Karsk and Ossium suffered suspicion and lost production. The roads' protective power was restored and the Ketsov's funding boosted units protecting the vales.

Lean and athirst.o: Over the winter of 387YE a large force of Varushkan captains, aided by the Thule Claws of the Dragon, systematically rooted out the face-peeling trudniki across Karsk and Ossium. The hunt was an overwhelming success but left draughir and other 'suspicious' Varushkans facing distrust.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: The Thule Claws of the Dragon took the lead in hunting trudniki in Krevsaty, including among the human vales left under orc rule.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: The Claws of the Dragon led the search for face-peeler nests and hidden trudniki in the Bonewood.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Wagon raiders from Orieb who punted into the flooding Drownbark marshes seeking trudniki plunder have fallen prey to some spiritual force, and the Merchant-Boyar of the Stinking Market must investigate their stranded camp.

Ossium/Webwood.t: The Webwood held the largest known trudniki den, making Thule cooperation vital; the Claws of the Dragon led operations there.

Karsk.t: Karsk was swept for trudniki dens and disguised face-peelers, leaving its draughir under suspicion. A sickened band of wagon raiders, the Gregadze, shunned by a local outpost, await treatment from the Apothecaries Guild.

Ossium.t: Ossium was a main focus of the hunt, with its draughir investigated and its Ketsov family funding the defence of the vales. Wagon raiders who pressed into Drownbark Forest have since been bewitched.

Otkodov.t: The Dragons of Otkodov ordered the Claws of the Dragon to help Varushka, and human vales in regions ceded to Otkodov were searched for trudniki hiding among them.

Leaves and fruit.d: Johanna of Ravensfell designed the White Roads, linking Casfall to Bastion and Bastion to Necropolis and Reikos. They would cost 120 wains of white granite and 240 crowns, and would enrich those territories and the Virtue's Rest hostels. The Custodes Clavium, approached by Lev of the Unbound, offered to refurbish the Basilica for 15 wains of white granite and 5 of weirwood, paying the labour themselves, and to revive the Speaker title, with 10 liao and 20 Synod votes. Benefactors also proposed the Cinderpath Exchange, where white granite would be bought at a fair price. It would come with a Cinderpath Benefactor title and optional Assembly mandates, but would reduce Bourse supply. The Basilica work and the Speaker title were completed before Summer 383YE.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: some virtuous Dawnish folk would heed a General Assembly mandate condemning market forces and bring white granite to the Cinderpath Exchange.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a planned church carving shows the exemplar Zemress with her boot on the chest of a Grendel pirate.

Highguard.t: The Highborn were offered White Roads, a refurbished Basilica of the Seven Doors with a restored Speaker of the Highborn Assembly, and a fair-price white granite exchange. The Basilica and the Speaker title were completed before Summer 383YE.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: some virtuous orcs would heed a General Assembly mandate against market greed and bring white granite to the Cinderpath Exchange.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: some virtuous Navarr would heed a General Assembly mandate promoting fair prices for white granite.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the idea that market forces are unvirtuous was thought unlikely to gain traction there, though scholars mused about a Freeborn Assembly Speaker at Atalaya.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League's Blood Red Roads were the benchmark for the White Roads, scholars imagined a League Assembly Speaker at Capodomus Cathedral, and the anti-market idea was expected to find little favour there.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka was noted as producing better white granite than Highguard, and as unlikely to embrace the fair-price ideal.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's pilgrim roads in Kallavesa had left Highguard looking behind, and some virtuous Winterfolk might heed a General Assembly mandate on white granite.

Leaves and fruit.o: In Summer 382YE a revival of Highborn interest in building with white granite raised three opportunities: a network of White Roads for pilgrims, refurbishing the Basilica of the Seven Doors in Bastion with a restored Speaker of the Highborn Assembly, and a white granite ministry called the Cinderpath Exchange. Of these, only the Basilica refurbishment and the Speaker's restoration are recorded as completed, shortly before the Summer Solstice 383YE.

Bastion/Stoneside.t: The proposed White Road from Casfall to the White City would run through Stoneside's light woods.

Casinea/Casfall.t: Casfall was to be the starting point of the proposed White Road, connecting the Blood Red Roads to Sybela and Bastion.

Casinea/Mareholm.t: Mareholm's mineral-rich hills, crossed by the trade routes to Anvil, were proposed as the home of the Cinderpath Exchange, a ministry buying white granite at a fair price.

Bastion.t: The White City was to be the hub of the proposed White Roads, and its Basilica of the Seven Doors was refurbished as the seat of the restored Speaker of the Highborn Assembly before Summer 383YE.

Casinea.t: Casinea's quarries produce white granite, the proposed White Roads would start from Casfall, and the Cinderpath Exchange was proposed for a village near its eastern borders.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Senate's pilgrim roads and bridges commissioned in its marshes in Winter 379YE were cited as a contrast with roadless Highguard.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: Karsk's existing road network was cited to show how far Highguard lagged behind.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: scholars speculated about a Speaker for the Freeborn Assembly with offices at Atalaya.

Necropolis.t: A proposed White Road along the River Couros would link Bastion to Necropolis, helping pilgrims and enriching its businesses and farms.

Reikos.t: Reikos would gain a White Road to Tabernacle, possibly extended to High Chalcis and Casca's Doom, to aid its rebuilding and wealth. Its Vigilant Swan produces white granite but never enough to meet demand.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: scholars imagined a Speaker for the League Assembly based in Capodomus Cathedral.

Less welcome tenants.d: Lutomysla learned that the Sand Fishers of Misericorde propitiate Dho'uala with seasonal offerings. She proposed three non-competing commissions: the Semmerlak Tollbooth, paying tribute of 30 Thrones a season; the Blades of the Semmerlak, a Dawnish knightly estate and Varushkan wardenhouse with a Knight-Warden title; and the Journeymage Towers for volhov, guisers and mountebanks, with a Watcher of the Semmerlak title. The Silent Bell suggested mandates for the Prosperity, Pride and Wisdom assemblies. Further options included later plenipotentiary diplomacy with Dho'uala over ilium and fishing, seeking the Lady of the Semmerlak's patronage, and a radical, costly idea of draining the lake. The Silent Bell also planned to publish its reports. All these opportunities have since expired.

Dawn.t: Many Dawnish, echoing Earl Ailsa Temerlaine, rejected propitiation and human sacrifice, and Dawnish knights, enchanters and guisers were central to two proposals: a knightly estate for the Blades of the Semmerlak and a role alongside the volhov in the Journeymage Towers.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj had tolerated the Sand Fishers' lake ceremonies so they could use them to bargain with Undertow, and their cruelty is contrasted with that of the Iron Helms.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: priests in Highguard were among those significantly concerned about proposals to sacrifice people to Dho'uala.

The League.t: Holberg's Waterroad Ring of merchant guilds, hurt by Dho'uala's attacks, backed the tribute idea if the Prosperity assembly declared it virtuous, while Holberg's mountebanks joined the volhov and League merchant-princes offered Goldentide Mail to a Knight-Warden.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen members of the Silent Bell objected that its secret letters smacked of conspiracy, pushing the sodality to share its reports publicly.

Varushka.t: Varushkan expertise underpinned the proposals: warden fellowships from Karov, Karsk and Ossium would staff a wardenhouse, the Wavewatcher volhov would lead the Journeymage Towers, and Varushkan merchant-boyars would supply magic items and could contribute to construction.

Less welcome tenants.o: Following a Senate appraisal requested by the senators for Holberg and Semmerholm, the cabalist Lutomysla Niegoslava set out several proposals to end Dho'uala's attacks around the Semmerlak, while the Silent Bell sought Synod guidance on countering the sovereign virtuously.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Lutomysla visited the Sand Fishers' port here and learned of Reedpiper's offerings to Dho'uala; the orcs agreed the Empire could build the Tollbooth here, though they could withdraw access at will.

Karov/Malimorzi.t: The port of Korotny in Malimorzi was proposed as the site of both the Varushkan wardenhouse for the Blades of the Semmerlak and one of the Journeymage Towers.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: The Kostjyas Respite in Bittershore was proposed as an alternative wardenhouse site and as one of the three Journeymage Tower locations.

Semmerholm/Lacuve.t: Lacuve, near the port of Lacre, was proposed as a site for the Dawnish knightly estate, and Lacre itself for a Journeymage Tower, given that guisers are drawn to its tourneys and fairs.

Weirwater/Sandling.t: Sandling, near Culwich, was put forward as one of two possible sites for the Dawnish knightly estate of the Blades of the Semmerlak.

Holberg.t: Holberg's senator co-sponsored the appraisal, and its Sand Fisher region of Misericorde, the only part touching the lake, was offered as a Tollbooth site, while its merchants and mountebanks were key to the tribute and Journeymage proposals.

Karov.t: Warden fellowships from Karov helped shape the proposals, and the port of Korotny in Malimorzi was suggested for both a wardenhouse and a Journeymage Tower.

Karsk.t: Warden fellowships from Karsk took part in the talks, and as a lakeside territory Karsk could host the Tollbooth and would send representatives to any future talks with Dho'uala.

Ossium.t: Ossium's wardens contributed to the proposals, and the Kostjyas Respite in Bittershore was suggested as a site for a wardenhouse or a Journeymage Tower.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm's senator Amicia of the Semmerlak co-sponsored the appraisal, its enchanters advised Lutomysla, and Lacuve near the port of Lacre was proposed for a knightly estate or a Journeymage Tower.

The Semmerlak.t: The lake is Dho'uala's domain, and every proposal aimed to stop her creatures preying on its shipping and shores, while a radical last-minute idea suggested draining it entirely to kill the sovereign.

Weirwater.t: Enchanters from Weirwater advised Lutomysla, and Sandling near Culwich was proposed as a possible site for the Dawnish knights' estate under the Blades of the Semmerlak.

Let that be your last battlefield.d: The Free Folk spent their wages on offerings and on hand-written pamphlets of ancestor stories. Their greatest concentration was around Caer Faucon in Astolat, where a scarecrow-like effigy at the House of the Proffered Hand became a site of worship said to bear an unusual aura. None had taken citizenship. Adopting the phrase 'The Empire will have All of Us or None of Us', they were saving to make their case to each nation. Priests across the Empire disagreed. The page set out three paths for the General Assembly: accept their beliefs, forbid their public practice, or expel them. It warned that inaction would see the situation deteriorate.

Dawn.t: Dawn gave the Free Folk their first welcome as distant kin. They gathered most heavily around Caer Faucon, helping Dawnish yeofolk with the harvest and visiting their effigy at the House of the Proffered Hand, though they have not settled there as citizens.

Highguard.t: Highborn wayfarers of Shimi's Orchard Chapter examined the Free Folk's paragons and exemplars and found oddities but nothing overtly dangerous. Esau of Shimi's Orchard argued they should be treated no differently from Sumaah figures.

Navarr.t: Some Navarr guides argued that the Free Folk have a place in the Great Dance without changing themselves. They held that it is the Empire's responsibility to help them reach that home, even if it lies outside the Empire.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Free Folk know most about Dawn and the Brass Coast, and have earlier worked gutting the catch in Siroc.

The League.t: Bishop Jago Heshel di Temeschwar condemned the Free Folk's 'Divine Family' as incompatible with the Doctrines of the Way and likened it to the Yaelian Schism. He demanded that the General Assembly act.

The Marches.t: The Free Folk worked Marcher harvests and gave pamphlets to travellers passing through the Marches, and they adopted a Marcher saying as 'All of Us or None of Us'. Marcher friars urged priests to remember the Doctrine of the Labyrinth and the example of Kethry.

Urizen.t: Urizeni questors called for reason from the Synod, arguing that an unfinished Way must leave room to examine the limits of doctrine. One Urizen priest noted the precedent for inspirational figures not recognised by the Synod.

Let that be your last battlefield.o: By Autumn 384YE the Free Folk were working the harvest across the Empire and spreading pamphlets about their ancestors and their 'Divine Family', while refusing to seek citizenship. Imperial priests divided over whether their beliefs were acceptable, and pressure mounted on the Synod's General Assembly to give a clear ruling.

Astolat/Coombe.t: Mentioned in passing: the Free Folk effigy is described as a scarecrow that would do little to dissuade the jackdaws of Coombe.

Necropolis/Highrod.t: Mentioned in passing: the Free Folk had earlier worked taming the undergrowth in Highrod's forests.

Astolat.t: Astolat held the largest concentration of Free Folk, who helped bring in its harvest. A scarecrow-like effigy at the House of the Proffered Hand in Caer Faucon became their weekly place of worship, and access to it has been restricted.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the Free Folk had earlier worked gutting the catch from Siroc.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Free Folk had earlier fixed walls and dug ditches in the Mournwold.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Free Folk had earlier tamed the undergrowth in the forests of Highrod.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the Free Folk helped reap the autumn harvest across Semmerholm.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: it is home to Bishop Jago Heshel's Church of the Golden Orator, whose bishop called for the Synod to act against Free Folk beliefs.

Let the day die.d: The Greensward had stayed haunted since the bloody battles of 381YE, despite earlier efforts by the friars of Honour's Rest and Albert Fugglestone-Copperhill's priests. The Saker coven's Autumn Equinox enchantment calmed ghosts and helped the living understand them. Stories spread across the Mourn: some spirits found justice or rest, while a hateful spectre had to be destroyed. Friar John's call for aid was upheld but missed a greater majority, though some priests still came to Overton. Most remaining ghosts, human and orc, want to be remembered. The proposed Orchard of the Watch folly would cost 20 weirwood, 10 white granite and 60 crowns, take three months, and replace the haunted quality with memorial. If it were ever destroyed, the ghosts would rise furious.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Saker coven cast the Winter enchantment over the whole Mournwold that roused the ghosts and drew them closer to the living.

Jotun.t: Jotun ghosts from the Greensward battles fear the oblivion of the Howling Abyss and wish to be honoured. Mournwold thralls who understand some Jotun beliefs advised the priests on how to approach the orc dead.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr phantom led a friar to a shallow grave, and the remains are being carried north to Miaren.

The Marches.t: Marcher friars led the work to lay the Mourn's ghosts to rest, and the Marches may now build the Orchard of the Watch to quiet the Greensward dead for good.

Let the day die.o: In Winter 384YE a Winter enchantment woven by Highguard's Saker coven stirred the Mournwold's ghosts to communicate with the living. Priests answering Friar John of Honour's Rest learned that the Greensward dead chiefly wished to be remembered, which opened the opportunity to build a memorial orchard at Orchard's Watch.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: The hateful spectre of a former owner drove everyone from the Hill-bridge Inn until the abbot and monks of Fordwater Monastery destroyed it and reclaimed the inn.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: Mentioned in passing: in Freemoor a murderer was exposed by the weeping ghost of her dead lover, thanks to a brave governess.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Mentioned in passing: the ghosts of a long-dead company of soldiers paraded nightly through a Green March market town until the townsfolk came out to thank them.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Priests at Overton and Orchard's Watch found that the remaining ghosts want to be remembered. The proposed Orchard of the Watch would turn the region's haunted quality into a memorial one for as long as the trees stand.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: the remains of a Navarr whose ghost was found in the Mourn are being taken to a final resting place in Miaren's glades.

Mournwold.t: The whole territory lay under the Saker enchantment, and ghostly encounters, both sorrowful and dangerous, spread across it before the magic began to fade.

Lethal and elusive.d: The Liathaven vallorn was sliding into slumber under the thirty-year winter of Wither the Seed. Westwood could be cleared if Imperial armies, attacking from the West Ranging beachhead, claimed the entire region before the Summer Solstice 383YE, though miasma would double casualties. Surut offered further boons for a Navarr assault if granted amity again, in exchange for devouring the forest of Birchland, Tower March or Alderly. Liathaven's trods had been severed by unknown magic. The southern Feni and the Alderly survivors entered Liaven's Glen, where a Senate treaty allows them to live. The northern band raided Hercynia, targeting mana sites. The Senate declined to act, so the raids will hit Hercynia's production.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tusks are named as one of the armies that fought the vallorn's expansion in Liathaven in Spring 382YE.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire had secured West Ranging from the Jotun, and Liaven's Glen, where the Feni have gone, is still technically in Jotun hands.

Navarr.t: The northern Feni became a Navarr problem, raiding Hercynia's steadings, trade routes and mana sites, while Surut offered fresh boons to aid a Navarr assault on Liathaven if he was granted amity and paid in advance.

The Marches.t: The southern Feni finally left the Mournwold after months of disruption, but Surut sought to devour one of three Marcher forests, Birchland, Tower March or Alderly, as the price of further aid.

Wintermark.t: The northern Feni band, swelled by local Feni, left Hahnmark for Hercynia after raids on Wintermark's halls and a failed peace attempt by the Suaq grimnir Kaukana Broken Wing.

Lethal and elusive.o: In Winter 382YE the Liathaven vallorn, weakened by its failed expansion and smothered by the Wither the Seed curse, offered a closing chance to clear Westwood, while the Feni of the Woods-that-Fell moved on: the southern band into Liathaven and the northern band into Hercynia, where they raided Navarr steadings.

Hahnmark/Southridge.t: The northern Feni lingered in southern Southridge and gathered more Feni before moving on into Hercynia.

Hercynia/Old Ranging.t: The Feni crossed into Old Ranging and spread out, raiding unprepared steadings and the merchants on its important trade route.

Hercynia/Summersend.t: Minor Feni raids reached as far east as Summersend, though the bands showed no sign of moving into it in force.

Liathaven/Liath's Heart.t: Liath's Heart is the vallorn's core and would be its only holding if Westwood were cleared, and a powerful Spring regio there or in Westwood is needed to restore the trods.

Liathaven/Liaven's Glen.t: The southern Feni and the survivors from Alderly passed into Liaven's Glen, beyond the ken of the Navarr.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: West Ranging served as the Empire's vital beachhead for any campaign against the vallorn, and is cited as already bearing the Burnt quality from Surut's fire.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: Westwood could be wholly cleared of the vallorn if Imperial armies claimed the entire region before the Summer Solstice 383YE, at the cost of doubled casualties from the miasma.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Survivors of the Imperial attack on the Feni camp in Alderly followed the southern band into Liathaven, and Alderly's forest was one of three Surut offered to devour.

Upwold/Birchland.t: Birchland's forest was one Surut proposed to consume with magical fire, leaving it Burnt, as payment for further aid to the Navarr.

Upwold/Tower March.t: Tower March's forest was one Surut proposed to consume with magical fire, leaving it Burnt, as payment for further aid to the Navarr.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Brocéliande is described as stirring, in contrast with Liathaven, and its delaying techniques are cited as a comparison.

Hahnmark.t: The northern Feni of the Woods-that-Fell left Hahnmark for Hercynia, taking with them Feni who had dwelt in Hahnmark's gulleys and woodlands.

Hercynia.t: Feni raiders roamed southern Hercynia, and with the Senate declining to act, every farm and business faces a 36 ring production penalty and every mana site will yield one less crystal mana.

Liathaven.t: The vallorn was weakened and slumbering under a thirty-year winter, offering a brief chance to clear Westwood, while the territory's trods were severed and Feni bands settled in its east under a Senate treaty.

Mournwold.t: The southern branch of the Woods-that-Fell left the Mournwold for Liathaven, ending their disruption there.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim is named as one end of the Old Ranging trade route menaced by Feni bandits.

Upwold.t: Two Upwold forests, Birchland and Tower March, were among those Surut proposed to burn as payment for aiding the Navarr if amity was granted.

Light upon the water.d: The storms ended the drought but halved the production of every farm and business and cost every mine a rank. Loss of life was small. Regrow the Land's Heart left extra herbs and eased old grudges. Utterlund and Eastring became marshes, and marsh commissions cost a fifth more labour for at least a year. The Vassa flooded Tassato and damaged the Imperial Mint, revealing hidden flooded chambers, and the rains uncovered ilium in the hills. The Semmerlak washed up curious treasures. The Meade flooded the Marches, angering threshers and reviving the Great Western Canal proposal. True liao was stolen in Madruga, and Syrene's Wisdom gained ilium.

Dawn.t: Dawnish lakeshore lands flooded, Culwich worst of all, where the drowned bells rang in Summer. Troubadours warned of cursed Sedaret, and a proposed mandate would send 50 doses of liao to keep Dawnish folk from the Semmerlak's trinkets.

Druj.t: The Barrens and Druj-held Zenith escaped the rituals' direct effects but still face the higher labour costs on marsh commissions. Sarangrave's Nesustak Forest became swampier near the lake.

Highguard.t: The storm clouds seemed to spread from Casinea, where Regrow the Land's Heart was targeted. The Silver Chalice shielded Syrene, which gave the order two vials of Pool of Syrene water, and Syrene's Wisdom stays flooded but gains a ring of ilium each season.

Jotun.t: Jotun-held Bregasland and Liathaven were spared the magical storms but still face the fifth-higher labour cost on marsh commissions, as floodwater ignored borders.

Navarr.t: The Feverwater rose and turned Eastring in Therunin into a marsh, while the Navarr and Great Forest Orcs struggled to limit the damage elsewhere in the territory.

The Brass Coast.t: A flooded Civil Service vault in Madruga was emptied in haste and a dose of true liao was stolen. The Great Grasses dried out oddly fast, and there are worries about the Scorrero River.

The League.t: The Vassa flooded Tassato despite the Assembly's warning, damaging the Imperial Mint and leaving businesses penalised until repairs are paid for. New ilium was found in the hills, Holberg's Utterlund became a marsh, and Sarvos's precautions largely protected it.

The Marches.t: The Meade burst its banks across Mitwold, Upwold and the Mournwold, and threshers grew angry at the Empire cursing its own people. They want the Assembly to name the casters, and the Great Western Canal has been proposed.

Urizen.t: Zenith, shared with the Druj, was outside the rituals' direct reach but faces higher marsh labour costs, and the Lustri forests became swampier near the lake.

Varushka.t: Floods struck Varushkan settlements on the Semmerlak, including the vales of Bittershore. Wise ones warned that the lake's treasures may be Dho'uala's lures, and a proposed mandate would send 25 doses of liao to discourage Varushkans from taking them.

Light upon the water.o: In Summer 384YE Imperial magicians cast Thunderous Deluge and Regrow the Land's Heart under a conjunction that spread both across every Imperial territory, turning the Great Drought into the Great Storm. Three months of destructive but renewing rain flooded the Empire, with Tassato worst hit.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: The Great Pits of Ennerlund saw some of their worst flooding since reverting to the Morass, though the Bourse seat weathered it without permanent damage.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Utterlund permanently gained the marsh quality alongside its forest, so commissions there cost a fifth more labour for at least a year.

Karov/Malimorzi.t: As part of Karov's Semmerlak shore, Malimorzi shared in the lakeside flooding, which affected settlements such as Korotny and forced people onto higher ground.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: Flooding in the vales along Bittershore was less severe than at Culwich but still drove people to upper storeys and higher ground.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: The Nesustak Forest endured the storm better than most places but grew significantly more swampy where it meets the lake.

Semmerholm/Lacuve.t: Lacuve's stretch of the Semmerlak shore shared in the lakeside flooding, which affected settlements such as Lacre and left many people seeking higher ground.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Mestra was flooded, and ilium washed out of old mines in the hills above it could become a Bourse seat yielding 6 rings a season: 75 Thrones with the guilds' help if made a League position, or 250 Thrones otherwise.

Therunin/Eastring.t: The rising Feverwater gave Eastring the marsh quality, making commissions there costlier to build.

Zenith/Lustri.t: The forests of Lustri endured the storm relatively well but became significantly swampier where they border the lake.

Bregasland.t: Not Imperial at the time, Bregasland escaped the direct storms, but the higher labour cost on marsh commissions still applies there.

Brocéliande.t: Brocéliande only had to endure the drought, but floodwater ignored borders and marsh commissions there now cost a fifth more labour.

Casinea.t: The storm clouds seemed to spread out from Casinea's regio. In Syrene the Silver Chalice protected the people, though homes were lost and Syrene's Wisdom remains flooded, with higher upkeep but an extra ring of ilium each season.

Holberg.t: Utterlund became a marsh and the Great Pits of Ennerlund flooded badly. Sand Fisher orcs helped shore up defences to protect the city, but Holberg gains no Semmerlak bounty as the city does not border the lake.

Karov.t: Karov's shores of the Semmerlak flooded, and its businesses stand to gain 2 crowns and two random ingots of rare metal at the Winter Solstice unless a Varushkan mandate turns people away from the lake's treasures.

Karsk.t: As a territory bordering the Semmerlak, Karsk suffered flooding, and its businesses may share in the lake's Winter Solstice bounty unless a Varushkan mandate is upheld.

Liathaven.t: Liathaven was spared the magical storms but is among the territories where marsh commissions now carry a fifth more labour cost.

Madruga.t: A Madruga vault holding Civil Service cargo for Anvil flooded, and a dose of true liao was stolen in the confusion. The Great Grasses dried out unnaturally quickly afterwards.

Mitwold.t: The Meade flooded parts of Mitwold, ruining crops. The proposed Great Western Canal would boost its businesses and farms and help prevent future floods.

Mournwold.t: The Meade flooded parts of the Mourn. The Great Western Canal would link Meade to Sarcombe and enrich its businesses and mines, and the Mournwold thralls offer half the labour cost if it is commissioned before the end of the Spring Equinox 385YE.

Ossium.t: The vales along Bittershore flooded. Ossium's businesses may gain the Semmerlak bounty, but its under-developed areas now also face the higher marsh labour costs.

Sarangrave.t: The Nesustak Forest weathered the storm better than most but became significantly swampier where it borders the lake.

Sarvos.t: Precautions Sarvos had taken since Skathe's curse helped the city endure the storms with minimal lasting damage.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm's lakeshore suffered flooding, and its businesses may gain 2 crowns and two random rare-metal ingots from the Semmerlak's flotsam unless a Dawnish mandate is upheld.

Tassato.t: The Vassa broke its banks and flooded Tassato, damaging the Imperial Mint and leaving businesses at a rank penalty until the Senate pays 50 Thrones or a year passes. Hidden chambers were found beneath the Mint and ilium in the northern hills.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Gemma Stewart says missing mining infrastructure for the new Tassatan ilium seat could be sourced from Holberg or Temeschwar.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens were outside the rituals' direct effects, but the higher labour cost for marsh commissions applies there too.

The Semmerlak.t: The lake rose dramatically, and as it receded it left junk and strange treasures that drew scavengers. Some fear these are Dho'uala's lures or relics of drowned Sedaret.

Therunin.t: The rising Feverwater turned Eastring into a marsh, while the Navarr and Great Forest Orcs worked hard to contain the damage across the rest of Therunin.

Upwold.t: The Meade flooded parts of Upwold. An alder suggested the canal might make up for wealth lost when Moonwater Hall was abrogated.

Weirwater.t: Culwich suffered the worst of the Semmerlak flooding, and its drowned bells were heard in Summer as an ill omen. Weirwater's businesses may share the lake's bounty, which some link to the territory's strange dreams.

Zenith.t: Zenith escaped the direct effects of the rituals, but marsh commissions there now cost a fifth more labour and the Lustri forests became swampier near the lake.

Like a wheel within a wheel.d: The raid drove Grendel forces back from the Legacy. The Senate returned Spiral to Urizen control and elected Tanwyn Ankarien as its senator, with Edmundo of Endsmeet replacing her as Senator for Zenith. The Grendel still held Apulus, Ateri and, nominally, Screed, with a significant army. Personal resources reclaimed from the Grendel became spoils of war for the Military Council to allocate, among them the Ankarien Chess Set of thirty ushabti soldiers. The Legacy, mined again by ushabti and Urizen volunteers, became a national Bourse seat chosen by Urizen mana site owners. Recovering Spiral would not let Urizen support more armies. The Stonemasons offered to help build one cheap castle in Apulus or Apstrus, but only once all of Spiral was in Imperial hands. A report on further opportunities was expected by the Winter Solstice.

Grendel.t: The Grendel were pushed back from the Legacy and lost control of Spiral, though they still held three regions centred on Apulus and Ateri and kept a significant armed force there. Their continued presence was the condition holding back the Stonemasons' offer to build a castle.

Urizen.t: Spiral was returned to Urizen control under Senator Tanwyn Ankarien, and Urizen mana site owners would vote at the Autumn Equinox on who held the restored Legacy Bourse seat. The territory's sparse population meant its recovery would not let Urizen support any more armies.

Like a wheel within a wheel.o: After an Imperial raid through the Sentinel Gate at the Summer Solstice captured Ossuary and gave the Empire control of Spiral, the Civil Service assessed the reclaimed territory. It reported on spoils of war, the restored Legacy mithril mine, Urizen's army capacity and a conditional offer by the Stonemasons of Mezudan to help build a castle.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: Apstrus was one of the two sites the Stonemasons of Mezudan proposed for a castle, near the old heliopticon tower on the northern slopes, where it could deter attacks from the south and watch the unknown lands towards Axos.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Apulus remained a centre of Grendel control. It was also the Stonemasons' other proposed castle site, on the coast, where a fortress could resist Grendel naval assaults and control passes into the Broken Shore.

Spiral/Ateri.t: Ateri remained one of the two centres of Grendel control in Spiral.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: The Empire captured Ossuary after the Solstice raid, which gave it enough regions to take control of Spiral.

Spiral/Screed.t: Screed, where the Black Plateau squats, remained under nominal Grendel control.

Spiral.t: Spiral passed back into Imperial hands, yielding spoils of war such as the Ankarien Chess Set and a working Legacy mithril mine. Its remaining Grendel presence still left the territory volatile.

Lines of care and sorrow.d: The Brine Turtles, Iron Gulls, Naguerro and Storm Sharks advanced cautiously through Ayereed, enchanted by Sky magic. Heralds from a Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae in Icarion and wolves from a Tomb King citadel in Eoradal, joined by a few mostly Sannite Imperial Orcs, could only delay them. Fleisardh fell within a month, its Brine Turtle sept welcoming the invaders. The Grendel are three-fifths of the way to taking Clisearn and the Fundindelve mithril mine, though the Golden Pyramid grand lodge was completed before the Autumn Equinox. Former Salt Lord Ehsan kept Beoraidh neutral. Losing one more region would leave Mareave under no control.

Grendel.t: Four Grendel armies, enchanted by Sky magic, took Fleisardh and are close to seizing Clisearn, the Fundindelve mithril mine and the newly finished Golden Pyramid grand lodge.

Imperial Orcs.t: A few handfuls of Imperial Orcs, mostly Sannites, fought beside the summoned defenders of their arid territory, knowing they could only delay the Grendel advance.

Lines of care and sorrow.o: In Autumn 387YE four Grendel armies invaded Mareave from Ayereed, seizing Fleisardh with the help of the Brine Turtle sept and pushing deep into Clisearn. Summoned Winter and Summer defenders slowed them, and the city of Beoraidh stayed neutral.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Ehsan's city stayed strictly neutral, offering sanctuary to anyone but sending no soldiers. Its control of the only navigable coastal waters may be what kept navies out of the fighting.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: Fighting rages here and the Grendel are three-fifths of the way to taking the region. The completed grand lodge and the Fundindelve mine are at risk, and wary former Grendel households are increasingly inclined towards the Empire.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: A basalt citadel of the Tomb King rose in the shadow of the aqueduct, sending pale wolves to fight the Grendel in Fleisardh.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: The Grendel seized the region with the full cooperation of the Brine Turtle sept, which welcomed the returning armies with open arms.

Mareave/Icarion.t: A Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae here sent its orc-like heralds charging south to meet the invaders and slow their advance.

Ayereed.t: The Grendel armies launched their land offensive against Mareave by marching up through the petrified forest of Ayereed.

Mareave.t: Mareave stays in Imperial hands for now, but with Fleisardh lost and Clisearn under threat, losing one more region would leave it under no control. Because of Beoraidh, the Grendel must hold four regions to claim it outright.

Listen to your heart.d: Angered by Freeborn corsairs smuggling citizens out from under Governor Rahab and stealing the Scorrero Nets, the Grendel struck hard at the Brass Coast. Their raiders now menace all Imperial fleets on the Bay of Catazar. Building on Martha i Guerra's Autumn Equinox statement calling for raids on enemy shipping, a mandate could send Freeborn corsairs to hunt the Grendel. This would lift the penalty on Freeborn fleets and unlock a lucrative 'Hunt the Grendel' action, but would break the terms of the eternal Ephisis's offer. Alternatively, Beatriu i Dalila i Guerra proposed an 'Escort Imperial Shipping' mandate. This would lift the penalty for all fleets on the Bay and win allies from other nations. Only one mandate could be pursued.

Grendel.t: Grendel raiders were boarding Imperial fleets across the Bay of Catazar in revenge for Freeborn humiliations. Freeborn corsairs might be sent to slaughter their crews and plunder their ships, or to steer Imperial merchants away from them.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun raids are listed among the attacks the Freeborn had been fending off before the Grendel struck.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn Assembly could choose between taking the fight to the Grendel for plunder, at the cost of breaching the Ephisis offer, or protecting all Imperial shipping to win allies for reclaiming Madruga.

Listen to your heart.o: With Madruga burning, Grendel fleets began targeting and boarding Imperial ships across the Bay of Catazar. The Freeborn Assembly was offered two competing Synod mandates: strike back at Grendel shipping, or escort Imperial merchants safely past them.

Bay of Catazar.t: Grendel fleets were seeking to dominate the Bay, penalising Imperial shipping there. Either proposed mandate would lift that penalty, for Freeborn fleets alone or for all fleets on the Bay.

Madruga.t: Madruga was described as burning under Grendel attack. Supporters of the escort mandate argued the Brass Coast could not reclaim it without allies from other nations.

Lit up.d: The Golden Pyramid dropped its modest lodge plan and proposed rebuilding the green keep in Clisearn as a grand lodge. The Imperial Orcs' inspiration of Thrace could cut its cost to 50 white granite, 50 mithril and 60 crowns, and it would create a Bonesetter of the Delving Market. Using the new turtle-protection law as their pretext, the Illarawm found the Brine Turtles hostile but identified their true leader, Opaugh 'the Hook', with whom the Empire might negotiate. The Twelfth Mercenaries of Jadefall offered to garrison a Mareave citadel. Urizen historians learned of the artefact rod Stormcaller and the Courath of Icarion, leading to a conjunction against a Grendel paymaster. The Senator for Mareave was asked to save Lord Ehsan's ship, the Salt Shaker.

Grendel.t: A Grendel paymaster, accompanied by Asaveans, is expected in Icarion to pay local mercenaries to attack Imperial Orc holdings, and the Minister of Historical Research is tasked with killing him. Meanwhile the Brine Turtles still await the Salt Lords' promised but undefined return.

Imperial Orcs.t: The nation could co-fund the Golden Pyramid's grand lodge through the inspiration of Thrace and gain a new Bonesetter of the Delving Market. Its Illarawm envoys have opened a cautious path to negotiate with the Brine Turtles, and Skouran mercenaries have offered it a citadel garrison.

Urizen.t: Invited by the Imperial Orc Assembly, Urizeni historians uncovered the lost rod Stormcaller of the Army of the Citadels and its link to the Courath of Icarion. This gives Urizen a stake in the conjunction against the Grendel paymaster.

Lit up.o: In Winter 386YE, Mareave offered several opportunities. The Golden Pyramid proposed a far grander lodge in Clisearn, and Illarawm envoys mapped the leadership of the Brine Turtles in Fioroult. Skouran mercenaries offered to garrison a citadel, and two conjunctions arose: a Grendel paymaster in Icarion and a storm-stranded Beoraidh ship.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Lord Ehsan's independent Beoraidh continues to seek closer trade ties and has adopted Imperial currency. Its representative warned of the Grendel paymaster, and Ehsan asked the Senator for Mareave to rescue his ship, the Salt Shaker, promising a small gift in return.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: The Golden Pyramid proposed rebuilding Clisearn's green keep, with Ehsan's old villa, into a grand lodge that would boost the Fundindelve and local investment. It would also remove the region's Uncooperative quality by ending the open opposition of the local families.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: The Skourans have offered aid in rebuilding Eoradal's aqueduct. Locals there gave Urizeni historians only one-word answers about the Courath.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: The Illarawm spent the season in Fioroult and found the Brine Turtles guarded and loyal to the Grendel. They identified the fisherman Opaugh 'the Hook' as the town's true leader, whom the Empire could approach by winged messenger.

Mareave/Icarion.t: A Grendel paymaster is due to meet local mercenaries led by the Courath of Icarion, the last reputed holder of Stormcaller. This creates a highly likely combat conjunction there.

Mareave/Nadir.t: Mentioned in passing: Nadir is not named on the page and is covered only as part of Mareave's general situation.

Ayereed.t: Mentioned in passing: the armies of the Salt Lords could cross the border into Mareave from Ayereed at any moment.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Senate's law protecting turtles in the bay gave the Illarawm their pretext to visit the Brine Turtles and opened a small window for trust; the Salt Lords are said to have abandoned Mareave to seek riches across the bay.

Mareave.t: The territory was offered a transformative grand lodge, a possible treaty with the Brine Turtles and a Skouran citadel garrison. Two conjunctions also arose on its soil and coast.
