Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel's unsuccessful invasion of Redoubt is cited as a sign of Mareave's exposure.

Little boats.d: A year after a Druj delegation from Reikos fared badly before the Senate, three crude boats with bile-yellow sails crossed the Semmerlak. A swimmer bearing a flag marked with the rune of Lann declared they came in peace to discuss an end to hostilities. Two boats came ashore with a small band of diplomats; the third stayed at anchor beyond bowshot, silent but not hostile, watched by Lacre's yeofolk. The Druj invoked the law of delegation protection, which the Constitutional Court held protects them at Anvil as if they were citizens, and asked the Dawnish to keep them safe. At Anvil they negotiated extensively, the Senate discussed a proposed peace treaty, and the Druj went home unharmed.

Dawn.t: The Druj landed on Dawnish shores, praised the honour of the people of the rising sun, and asked Dawn to escort them to Anvil and protect them as guests under Imperial law.

Druj.t: The Druj sent a second delegation under a flag of truce to discuss terms for peace with the Senate; it negotiated at Anvil and returned safely to the Mallum.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on the page; it is attached only through the map.

Little boats.o: In Summer 379YE three Druj boats crossed the Semmerlak and landed a delegation near Lacre under a flag of truce, asking to speak to the Senate about peace. The diplomats travelled to Anvil, negotiated at length and later returned safely to the Mallum.

Semmerholm/Lacuve.t: Yeofolk working the shore east of Lacre spotted the Druj boats and received the delegation, then kept day-and-night watch on the boat left at anchor.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page; it is attached only through the map.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the previous year's Druj delegation is said to have come from Reikos.

Semmerholm.t: The Druj boats approached the shore east of Lacre, where the yeofolk raised the town and the delegation landed before setting out for Anvil.

The Semmerlak.t: The Druj crossed the lake from the Mallum in three small boats, and one stayed at anchor offshore, refusing all communication but showing no hostility.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: the page recalls the Druj attack on Weirwater across the Semmerlak during the reign of Empress Varkula, the last attack in force across the lake.

Little faith.d: The Great Library of Hacynian, where the Empire found the way to defeat the vallorn, was becoming a pilgrimage site for Navarr, grey pilgrims and historians. Three mandates were proposed: one directing scholars to research chosen topics (vates, Empress Giselle's death, the volodny), one having visiting magicians codify a ritual, and one embracing Night Singer and Phaleron, the eternals linked to the Library's regio. The General Assembly upheld Judgement 34, the third option, so Nathair Autumngale consecrated the Library, and an administrative motion was raised to create the title Singer of the Silence, appointable from Spring 387YE. Separately, the Navarr could commission a Vinery whose Keeper would receive herbs and a Bloodcloak; that opportunity has since expired.

Navarr.t: The Navarr were the people most affected, as the prospect of defeating the vallorn within their own lifetimes spread a fierce urgency through the nation and drew more healers to the oaths of the vine. The nation was offered a chance, now expired, to build a Vinery whose Keeper, appointed by the National Assembly, would receive herbs each season and a Bloodcloak each year.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League are noted as applying their ingenuity to the problems arising from the Library's revelations about the vallorn.

Little faith.o: Following the Wisdom Assembly's call to make the Great Library of Hacynian a true sacred site, the General Assembly chose between three competing consecration mandates and upheld Judgement 34, under which Nathair Autumngale consecrated the Library with true liao to seek the right question between Night and Day. The Library's success also inspired the Navarr vines movement, opening a time-limited opportunity to commission a Vinery.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is the location of the Great Library of Hacynian, but the page does not name the territory or describe any effect specific to it.

Little mercy.d: With the Iron Helms gone, two Dawnish armies watched the Black Wind without bloodshed. Roughly a third of the Black Wind planned to rejoin the Rahvin; the rest prepared to flee east, and their exposed army could be ambushed at a heavy disadvantage. Druj envoy Akhan Wormspeak sought an audience with the Imperial Consul at Anvil, and the Rahvin's Jannik returned to speak with the Imperial Orcs. The Great Forest Orcs, shaken by the Montanian massacre, would withdraw from the Empire unless the Navarr swore a protective oath by mandate. The Karass proposed a Carmine Fields trading post, and an Autumn enchantment set the Barrens talking.

Dawn.t: Dawnish settlers pushed east into Dawnguard and the Carmine Fields, the Eastern Sky and Golden Sun watched the Black Wind without fighting, and Dawn could build a trading post to trade beggar's lye for Karass herbs through a new Envoy to the Karass.

Druj.t: The Black Wind army returned to evacuate most of its sept to the Mallum, while Akhan Wormspeak led a Druj delegation with a Black Wind representative to negotiate with the Imperial Consul at Anvil.

Imperial Orcs.t: Statements by Stiv and Bleakshield Zorra in the Imperial Orc Assembly gave the Rahvin hope, and their representative Jannik returned to Anvil to seek the Imperial Orcs' help in drawing all the Black Wind into the Rahvin.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: cited by the Great Forest Orcs as a powerful nation that could decry the Empire to the world if it broke a treaty, unlike themselves.

Navarr.t: The Navarr were seen as the Great Forest Orcs' last true ally, and the National Assembly could enact one of two competing mandates to swear a binding, tattoo-marked oath to protect the sept, one also covering the Montanian remnants.

Little mercy.o: In Spring 386YE an uneasy calm settled on the Barrens. The Black Wind army returned unopposed to evacuate its sept, a third of whom chose to join the Rahvin, while the Great Forest Orcs looked to the Navarr for protection and the Karass offered Dawn a herb trade.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: The Black Wind army spread into the Bitter Strand, where the sept's first settlements lay, holding long debates over whether to flee east or join the Rahvin.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Inspired by Emperor Vesna's address, growing numbers of Dawnish settlers focused on Dawnguard and pushed east to claim land abandoned in the war.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: The Great Forest Orcs withdrew into their forest, sheltering Montanian survivors there, and would draw most of their people back to the Heart of Peytaht and fortify if the Navarr did not swear to protect them.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: The main body of the Black Wind army crossed into Saltmarsh a few days after its vanguard, avoiding the Dawnish armies, and no fighting followed.

Hercynia.t: Great Forest Orcs who had built steadings in Hercynia would be reassured and stay if the Navarr swore the oath; otherwise most would leave for the Heart of Peytaht.

Miaren.t: Great Forest Orc steadings in Miaren depended on the Navarr oath; without it, only a few would remain in their new homes.

The Barrens.t: After the bloodletting the Barrens fell quiet and then filled with talk between the septs, as the Black Wind evacuated, Dawnish settlers spread east and a potent Autumn enchantment encouraged conversation across the land.

Therunin.t: Most Great Forest Orcs in Therunin were set to return to the Heart of Peytaht, though some would remain behind if the Navarr swore their oath.

Living with war.d: Imperial fleets had battered Grendel pirates in the Bay of Catazar, leaving wrecked crews ashore at the Golden Keys in Free Landing and at Letivius Station in Apulus. In the East Floes of Sermersuaq, four Jotun stockades showed signs of unrest, possibly linked to thrall resistance. In Brocéliande, Urizen sentinels carrying Vital Honey were trapped at Exile Trod, and a monstrous dire canthon menaced Deep Weaver Wood. Ser Ancél Watcher's questing knights located Druj miasma pillars at Lomaa Spoils and Tanglethorn Glade in Ossium. Druj tortured souls, likely former Dawnish citizens, attacked Varushkan settlers at Korlack Marsh. Druj raiders had followed the victorious armies into Misericorde and camped at Semmerpine Shore.

Dawn.t: Dawnish knights led by Ser Ancél Watcher found two Druj miasma pillars in Ossium, Dawn's warriors were invited to slay a dire canthon in Boar's Dell, and its priests were called to exorcise tortured souls who were likely Dawnish captives from Dawnguard.

Druj.t: Druj miasma pillars still blanket Ossium, Druj bands with tortured souls raided Varushkan settlers at Korlack Marsh, and a Druj scouting party has camped secretly at Semmerpine Shore in Holberg.

Grendel.t: Grendel pirates were badly mauled across the Bay of Catazar, and two stranded crews, one raiding Free Landing and one holding Letivius Station in Spiral, were left vulnerable to Imperial strikes.

Highguard.t: Highguard was among the nations called on to join the Saturday strikes against the vallorn at Exile Trod and Deep Weaver Wood in Brocéliande.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the peaks of Skarsind are named as one end of the long Jotun border that the barbarians cannot fully secure.

Jotun.t: Although they hold most of Sermersuaq, the Jotun cannot secure its long border, and their four stockades in the East Floes are troubled by supply disruptions, quarrels and possible thrall resistance.

Navarr.t: Navarr efforts to stop the vallorn spreading into Elerael and Boar's Dell held for a third season, with chances to thin the husk hordes and rescue trapped sentinels.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn corsairs helped sink Grendel ships, and a desperate band of shipwrecked marines raided settlements near the Golden Keys before being driven off, offering a chance to destroy them.

The League.t: A Druj raiding band has slipped into Holberg's Misericorde forests and may learn about the Sand Fishers' new home or the city's strengthened defences unless it is dealt with.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule is not named; the page concerns Ossium only through Dawnish and Varushkan efforts against the Druj.

Urizen.t: Urizen was called to attack the Grendel pirates holding Letivius Station in Spiral, while its Citadel Guard gathered mana in Brocéliande and some of its sentinels were trapped with Vital Honey at Exile Trod.

Varushka.t: Varushkan settlers in Ossium face Druj skirmishers and the tortured souls that destroyed hamlets around Korlack Marsh, prompting initial false rumours of Dawnish treachery.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk near the border secretly supply Suaq thralls under Jotun rule, and Icewalkers reported four troubled Jotun stockades where Suaq cunning could aid strikes and uncover thrall resistance.

Living with war.o: Before the Summer Solstice of 383YE the civil service published the military conjunctions it had found: chances to strike at stranded Grendel pirates in Madruga and Spiral, Jotun stockades in Sermersuaq, vallorn threats in Brocéliande, Druj miasma pillars and tortured souls in Ossium, and a Druj scouting camp in Holberg.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: A dire canthon, a giant Spring-infused beetle able to shatter lances, was reported in Deep Weaver Wood, and Dawn's warriors were offered a chance to slay it.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Sentinels who had found a large store of Vital Honey were trapped by husks at Exile Trod, and destroying the horde there would help hold back the vallorn next season.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Druj raiders crept through Misericorde's dark forests and made a fireless, picketed camp at Semmerpine Shore on the Semmerlak.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Grendel marines wrecked near the Golden Keys raided local settlements for money and supplies, but they were repelled and now seek a way to escape.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: Scattered parts of the Bittershore are free of miasma because its pillar at Scarred Bay was destroyed last year, and the victorious armies crossed the Barrens River from there.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: Mentioned in passing: its miasma pillar has yet to be discovered.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Druj Chikad warriors and tortured souls destroyed several hamlets and farms around Korlack Marsh, and priests skilled in exorcism were sought to banish them.

Ossium/Echofell.t: Mentioned in passing: its miasma pillar remains undiscovered.

Ossium/Galath Fields.t: Ser Ancél's knights located a Druj miasma pillar at Lomaa Spoils near the mithril mine, which could be broken by Chimes of Annulment or priestly consecration.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Mentioned in passing: its miasma pillar is already known to stand at Fang Tree.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: Rumours of thrall rebellion are spreading, and four Jotun stockades here, Thenga's Camp, the Hall of Crows, Arroweye's Fast and Bearer's Rest, were identified as targets for Imperial strikes and investigation.

Spiral/Apulus.t: A stranded Grendel crew seized Letivius Station, guarding the approaches to ruined Apulian, and are disorganised and vulnerable while still under the Black Plateau miasma.

Bay of Catazar.t: Imperial fleet owners and privateers sank, scuttled and captured many Grendel ships, leaving wreckage and bodies of Grendel sailors washing ashore across the Bay.

Brocéliande.t: Imperial forces held back the vallorn for a third season, and two conjunctions offered chances to rescue trapped sentinels and kill a monstrous dire canthon while thinning the husk hordes.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: its hills form part of the Sermersuaq border that the Jotun cannot fully secure.

Holberg.t: A Druj band that followed the armies out of Ossium is camped at Semmerpine Shore and could scout the Sand Fishers' new lands and Holberg's defences if not defeated.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: its marshes mark one end of the porous Jotun-held border of Sermersuaq.

Madruga.t: Shipwrecked Grendel marines landed near the Golden Keys and twice raided local settlements before retreating, leaving a chance to destroy them before they escape by sea.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the stranded pirates in Spiral may try to cross the border into Mareave.

Ossium.t: Druj miasma pillars still shroud most of the territory, two were located by Dawnish knights, and Druj raiders with tortured souls continue to threaten Varushkan settlers.

Sermersuaq.t: Under Jotun rule, Suaq thralls endure hard but bearable lives, and four Jotun stockades in the East Floes show signs of unrest that Imperial forces were invited to exploit.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: its peaks are named as part of the long border with Jotun-held Sermersuaq.

Spiral.t: A wrecked Grendel crew seized Letivius Station near Apulian, and any strike against them must contend with the Black Plateau miasma.

Lonely, dark and deep.d: After Drefa, Voice of the Quiet Forest, led the Dance of Navarr and Thorn for a third time, the vallorn stirred and vallornspawn attacked settlements on the forest's edge. The remaining Druj in Elerael pulled back to Reikos, leaving the region open either to vallorn expansion or to an Imperial army that could take it with little resistance. After the Summer Solstice, miasma and bands of ettercaps spread into Casinea, Astolat and Semmerholm. The ettercaps were swiftly dealt with and the miasma soon dissipated, but over the following month a quarter of farm and forest produce in those territories emerged twisted. Most was burned, but magisters found some of the fruit could serve like crystal mana in Spring rituals.

Dawn.t: Astolat and Semmerholm suffered miasma and ettercap attacks, and a quarter of their farm and forest produce was twisted, though Dawnish knights and yeomen helped drive off the creatures.

Druj.t: The Druj abandoned Elerael and fell back to Reikos, apparently with more knowledge of the vallorn than other orcs, though it is unknown whether they provoked it.

Highguard.t: Casinea's borders with Brocéliande were struck by miasma and ettercaps, and a quarter of its farm and forest produce emerged twisted and strange.

Navarr.t: Navarr's repeated expansion of the trods, led by Drefa of the Quiet Forest, appears to be weakening the vallorn, which lashed out in response; Thorns fought vallornspawn emerging from the Black Boughs.

Lonely, dark and deep.o: In Summer 379YE the vallorn in Brocéliande grew restless, apparently weakened and provoked by the repaired trod network, while the Druj withdrew from Elerael. Miasma and ettercaps spilled into Casinea, Astolat and Semmerholm, twisting a quarter of their farm and forest produce, though some of the strange fruit proved usable like crystal mana in Spring rituals.

Brocéliande/Black Boughs.t: Vallornspawn stumbled out of the Black Boughs to attack nearby steadings, where Thorns rallied to repel them.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: The Druj left Elerael unoccupied, giving the restless vallorn an easy chance to expand there, or an Imperial army the opportunity to claim it with minimal resistance.

Astolat.t: Miasma and ettercaps spread into Astolat from the forest, and a quarter of its farm and forest produce was transformed, some usable in Spring magic.

Brocéliande.t: The vallorn within Brocéliande shifted restlessly and loosed vallornspawn and miasma on its surroundings, seemingly in reaction to the repaired trods draining its power.

Casinea.t: Casinea's border farms and forests endured miasma and ettercap attacks, with a quarter of their produce twisted into unnatural forms.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj remaining in Elerael were withdrawing to Reikos.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm was touched by the spreading miasma and ettercaps, and a quarter of its farm and forest produce, including orchards and butterflies, emerged strange and misshapen.

Long grass and stormclouds.d: Children of Wrecks pirates increasingly preyed on Bay of Catazar shipping, while Freeborn corsairs, stretched by missionary runs to Asavea, struggled to protect it. Grendel privateer attacks declined and Grendel armies were largely unseen. In Feroz the Grendel garrison at Mora's Rock held its borders amid rumours of diplomacy. Wintermark's Fist of the Mountains and the Freeborn Burning Falcon reclaimed the eerily silent Quiet Grasses, making Madruga Imperial again for the Senate to assign. The Gathered Storm, traitor corsairs under Isidore i Boyaga and Ioan Bloodstride's false Navarr attacked Trivento but were repelled by the Great Chain and Our Lady of Pride before abruptly withdrawing south.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the School of Imperial Strategy warns that the Children of Wrecks, if unchecked, could rival the Druj for the damage they inflict on the Empire.

Grendel.t: Their privateers attacked Imperial ships less often, their armies stayed silent after clearing the Imperial inroad into Ayereed, and their Feroz garrison held Morajasse. Meanwhile Grendel companies backed Asavean scouts in Necropolis, funded the Courath of Icarion and guarded a cache for the Brine Turtles in Mareave.

Highguard.t: Necropolis faced Grendel-escorted Asavean scouts probing its defences while the Shamal lay anchored offshore, and the General of the Citadel Guard was charged with defeating the Courath of Icarion in Mareave.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Skywise Gralka is named as one of those whose statements of principle drew researchers to Mareave, where Grendel agents were active.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the traitor Ioan Bloodstride is described as a refugee from a lost striding in Liathaven, now held by the Jotun.

Navarr.t: A false-steading called Liath's Blade, half Navarr traitors and half Imperial dregs posing as Navarr, attacked Trivento's defenders from behind under Ioan Bloodstride before being forced back.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn corsairs were stretched protecting the Bay, the Burning Falcon helped reclaim the Quiet Grasses, and Madruga was expected, though not guaranteed, to be reassigned to the Brass Coast. Traitor corsairs under Isidore i Boyaga joined the raid on Trivento.

The League.t: League defenders, backed by the Great Chain and Our Lady of Pride, repelled the Children of Wrecks at Trivento, though the town suffered burned ships and looted businesses and strategists warned a full assault might succeed.

Wintermark.t: The Fist of the Mountains, with Janon's subdued mystics and Winter-raised dead of Tassato, helped reclaim the Quiet Grasses, where soldiers whispered that the undead were growing more aware and menacing.

Long grass and stormclouds.o: In Summer 387YE the Fist of the Mountains and the Burning Falcon reclaimed the Quiet Grasses, restoring Madruga as an Imperial territory, while the Children of Wrecks launched a massive but ultimately failed raid on Trivento in Sarvos. Grendel forces in Feroz stayed quiet, and three conjunctions offered chances to strike at Grendel agents in Necropolis and Mareave.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a Children of Wrecks holding that nothing appeared to threaten when their fleet broke off.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: The Grendel still controlled Morajasse, with Imperial and Grendel forces watching its borders but no fighting.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a Children of Wrecks holding that nothing appeared to threaten when their fleet broke off.

Madruga/Quiet Grasses.t: The restored, Winter-touched grassland of towering, resilient grass and strange silence was reclaimed for the Empire by the Fist of the Mountains and the Burning Falcon, and an old road was found for caravans.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: its drinking houses are cited as places buzzing with speculation about the Children of Wrecks.

Mareave/Icarion.t: The Courath of Icarion, bearing the Grendel-supplied artefact Stormcaller, threatened to become an entrenched rebel presence unless defeated by the General of the Citadel Guard.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Longbeach would come under Grendel threat if the Asavean scouts escorted by Grendel reported back successfully to the Salt Lords.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: The Children of Wrecks assaulted Trivento's harbour and gates, but mithril chains, watchtowers and the garrison drove them off, leaving burned ships and raided businesses.

Sarvos/Uccelini.t: Mentioned in passing: its coast was among those fortified with watchtowers as part of the Great Chain defences.

Ayereed.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel removed the minor Imperial inroad into Ayereed and then went silent.

Bay of Catazar.t: Children of Wrecks attacks on shipping rose steadily while Grendel privateer raids declined, leaving overstretched Freeborn corsairs in a tense balance with the pirates.

Feroz.t: Wind Lord Saoirse and Commander Fiersach kept their forces at Mora's Rock without clashing with the Freeborn, amid rumours of correspondence with Imperial citizens.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Ioan Bloodstride, leader of the false Navarr who attacked Trivento, came from a lost striding in Liathaven.

Madruga.t: With the Quiet Grasses retaken, Madruga became an Imperial territory again despite the magical marsh and the Children of Wrecks' hold on the island, and the Senate was to decide its assignment.

Mareave.t: Two conjunctions arose here: the Courath of Icarion meeting Grendel paymasters while wielding Stormcaller, and a Grendel company guarding a resource cache intended for the Brine Turtles.

Necropolis.t: The Shamal stayed anchored off the coast, and Grendel escorting servants of the Red God scouted for weaknesses, a threat the Champion of Pride was charged to counter.

Sarvos.t: Trivento withstood a huge raid by the Children of Wrecks and their traitor allies, suffering damage but preventing a loss of the territory's taxation.

Segura.t: The Grendel garrison did not raid Segura, and Freeborn warbands found an old road that, with some work, could serve as a caravan pass from the Quiet Grasses into Segura.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's undead were raised from the dead of Tassato, and the Barossa School of Imperial Strategy there studied the Trivento battle.

Long roads to ruin.d: A dozen Druj, including a coven of ghulai, crossed the Semmerlak under a flag of truce to address the Senate. They kept apart from their escort and performed daily blessings as a precaution against Imperial treachery. A small Thule party came south through Karsk without a flag of truce, citing the peace with Otkodov, and brought a bound orc prisoner over a legal matter tied to events in Hercynia. A Grendel vessel docked at Crown's Quay under truce, claiming an invitation to discuss ending the war, and seemed notably more sombre. Orcs from the Barrens emerged into northern Reikos with the heads of two dozen fleeing Stone Toad Druj and sought out the Navarr over the unhonoured peace treaty.

Dawn.t: Dawnish escorts brought word of the Druj delegation, while the Barrens orcs were unhappy to find two Dawnish armies in Reikos and quietly distrusted the Dawnish not to attack them.

Druj.t: A grim, aloof Druj delegation with ghulai travelled under truce to address the Senate on a serious matter, while two dozen Stone Toad stragglers fleeing the weirwood slave camps were killed by the Barrens orcs.

Grendel.t: A sombre Grendel representative and his "servant" arrived by ship under a flag of truce, claiming to have been invited to discuss terms to end the conflict with the Empire.

Highguard.t: The Grendel landed at Crown's Quay and were escorted to Anvil by armed guards, with the Highborn responsible for bringing word of their procession.

Navarr.t: The Barrens orcs asked to speak to their friends among the Navarr, chiefly about why the peace treaty had not been honoured, and the Navarr were to be told of their coming.

Thule.t: A confident Thule party travelled to Anvil without a flag of truce, relying on the peace between the Empire and Otkodov and bringing a bound prisoner over a legal matter to be dealt with under the treaty.

Varushka.t: Varushkan patrols in Krevsaty challenged the Thule and provided them with an escort despite their refusal of one, and were to bring word of the emissaries to Anvil.

Long roads to ruin.o: In Winter 379YE four separate orc contingents (Druj, Thule, Grendel and orcs from the Barrens) travelled overland or by sea towards Anvil for the Winter Solstice, each with its own purpose.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: A patrol on the southern borders of Krevsaty challenged the Thule delegation, whose leader sarcastically invoked the peace, and then escorted them south.

Necropolis/Hedrossan.t: The Grendel ship arrived at Crown's Quay, where the harbour-master checked their intentions and armed guards escorted their representative towards Anvil.

Astolat.t: The Thule party passed through Astolat, where it became clear that one of their number was a bound prisoner.

Casinea.t: All four orc contingents were expected to come down through Casinea on their way to Anvil, and the Thule were led towards it by their Varushkan escort.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule said their prisoner's presence related to a legal matter arising from recent events in Hercynia.

Karsk.t: The Thule delegation came south through Karsk and was challenged by a Varushkan patrol before being escorted onwards.

Necropolis.t: A Grendel vessel docked at Crown's Quay under a flag of truce, briefly causing panic and rumours of invasion before their peaceful intent was confirmed.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule cited the state of peace between the Empire and the orcs of Otkodov as their right to travel.

Reikos.t: Orcs from the Barrens emerged into northern Reikos and presented the heads of two dozen Druj to the captains of the Black Thorns, finding two Dawnish armies present.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: some speculated that the Grendel's defeat in Spiral had taught them humility.

The Barrens.t: Orcs from the Barrens made the tiring journey out to seek the Navarr, having killed Stone Toad Druj who fled north from the pyres of the weirwood slave camps.

The Semmerlak.t: The Druj delegation crossed the Semmerlak out of the Mallum under a flag of truce to begin their overland trek to Anvil.

Weirwater.t: The Thule party travelled through Weirwater with their bound prisoner on the way to Anvil.

Long shadows.d: Prospectors searched undeveloped northern Skarsind, avoiding Thule-claimed Crow's Ridge. They found iron and silver, and Golden Pyramid magicians each earned 2 crowns. Plentiful green iron and weltsilver let Skarsind businesses diversify for free. Three opportunities emerged. The Cracking Void, a collapsed tempest jade mine in Eastermark, could be reopened as a sinecure. The Sorrowful Tunnels in Gildermark hold troll ruins and rich mithril, which could become a Bourse seat, though mining would destroy the ruins unless a year of historical research came first. Two abandoned mines were also found. The Wells of Janon are hidden by the Night eternal's shroud. Crimson Peak Mining, overrun by trogoni, was cleared by eight heroes' units, giving the Steward of the Mines of Gulhule new orichalcum options.

Imperial Orcs.t: Irontide Flax funded the venture, and orc heroes including Brog, Gaddak and three Irontide leaders cleared Crimson Peak Mining. The Sunstorm sept's dislike of working mines is offset by incoming labourers, while orcs gain cheap metals and a proposed share of Cracking Void profits.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Rashid i Hayim i Riqueza is listed among the heroes whose military units cleared Crimson Peak Mining.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: prospectors avoided Crow's Ridge because the Thule would claim any wealth found there, and the past Thule occupation of Skarsind is recalled as the time miners sheltered in the Wells of Janon.

Varushka.t: Varushkan miners from Volodmartz braved the dolorous aura of the Sorrowful Tunnels and discovered the troll ruins and mithril seams. Torvel Jasnaov Sorrowfall helped clear Crimson Peak Mining.

Wintermark.t: Two of the lost mines were once Wintermark holdings: Crimson Peak Mining belonged to the long-dead Wulfric Kelvinsson and the Wells of Janon to the late Ashborn Larch. Winterfolk miners there have since turned to Janon's traditions.

Long shadows.o: A Senate-approved drive, fully funded by Irontide Flax and aided by Golden Pyramid magicians, sent prospectors into the mountains of Skarsind. They found iron, silver, magical metals and several valuable sites, and Imperial heroes later cleared the trogoni from Crimson Peak Mining.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Mentioned in passing: prospectors deliberately avoided Crow's Ridge, expecting the Thule to claim any wealth found there.

Skarsind/Estermark.t: Estermark bustled with prospectors. Alonsios de Temeschwar found the collapsed Cracking Void mine there, whose tempest jade could be worked again through a proposed sinecure.

Skarsind/Gildermark.t: The Sorrowful Tunnels in Gildermark hold centuries-old troll ruins and rich mithril seams. They could become a Bourse seat producing 18 wains a season, unless historical research is commissioned first.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: Pakaanan's Pass was one of the regions soon bustling with prospectors searching for metal deposits.

Skarsind/Skogei Glens.t: Skogei Glens was one of the regions soon bustling with prospectors searching for metal deposits.

Skarsind.t: The territory's wild mountains yielded iron, silver and magical metals, letting local businesses diversify for free. They also offered potential sites at the Cracking Void, the Sorrowful Tunnels and the reclaimed Crimson Peak Mining.

Volodmartz.t: Mentioned in passing: the Varushkan miners who led the expedition into the Sorrowful Tunnels came from Volodmartz.

Long walk home.d: Nearly forty captains, aided by the Winter Sun, the Great Forest orcs and briars, and heralds of the Golden Hare, brought all the recovered Dubhtraig slaves to Skarsind, boosting Imperial Orc production for two seasons. The Holt of the Oak neared completion, and the briars sought Senate permission to refine liao from material salvaged at the lost Liao Garden. The Thule released about a hundred slaves, freed Snowstorm Henk and alleged that Imperials murdered a Krevsaty mine owner. They also built fortifications at supernatural speed. Jarl Geir's warband collected the 200-throne weregild. In the end the Senate ratified a Thule treaty ceding Sungold Pass and made the Fleet Master responsible for Grendel diplomacy.

Dawn.t: Eadric Fjellrevening, knight-errant of House de Rondell, led the expedition that uncovered the lost Liao Garden. About a hundred and fifty freed orcs headed to Astolat, where the Winter Sun were billeted, seeking land in return for military service.

Grendel.t: Salt Lord Moorvain of Vorlach demanded that the Empire recognise a worthy ambassador, namely the Imperial Fleet Master, before any talk of Feroz's surrender. The Grendel refused to deal with the Imperial Consul, and the Senate later granted the Fleet Master responsibility for Grendel diplomacy.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orc captains and the Winter Sun led the effort to bring the freed Dubhtraig orcs home to Skarsind, and their assembly's mandate rewarded the captains. Every Imperial Orc owning a business, farm, forest or herb garden gains a rank of production until the Winter Solstice.

Jotun.t: A Jotun delegation had agreed a weregild of 200 thrones for those killed at the Meeting Place. Jarl Geir the Iron Bull then led a kirkja warband to Anvil to compete for a Wintermark shield, and the warband returned home with the two hundred Throne pieces.

Navarr.t: The Navarr were the only nation not to aid the rescue of the freed orcs, being occupied with the vallorn and joined by Great Forest warriors in Brocéliande. The briars' liao proposal would involve Navarr traders and possibly a Navarr-appointed overseer of a new sinecure.

The Brass Coast.t: The Grendel's invasion of Feroz continued and they spoke of discussing its surrender. They demanded the Fleet Master, Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra, as their ambassador, and the Senate granted that title responsibility for Grendel diplomacy.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel message arrived in Sarvos, lost orcs were found in the forests of Temeschwar, and the Sand Fishers' settlement in Holberg is referenced.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: lost orcs were found in Bregasland, and developments with the Mournwold thralls are referenced elsewhere.

Thule.t: The Thule released around a hundred Imperial slaves and Snowstorm Henk, but they still chafe under sanctions and allege that Imperials murdered a Krevsaty mine owner. They are rapidly fortifying Ossium, Karsk and Skarsind, and the Senate later ratified a treaty ceding Sungold Pass to them.

Varushka.t: Yevgeni Katzev of Varushka, Ambassador to Otkodov, was invited to the Caucus Forum and to investigate the Krevsaty murder. Freed slaves arrived at Wendell's Hope, and the Thule continued to build fortifications in Ossium and Karsk.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's mediators had agreed the Jotun weregild, and Jarl Geir's warband came to compete in the Winterfolk shield contest. Freed Thule slaves travelled west seeking Erska Crowspeaker and were met by the Wintermark egregore.

Long walk home.o: The Summer 383YE Wind of Fortune reported on the Empire's foreign affairs and their consequences. Freed Dubhtraig orcs were settled in Skarsind, the Great Forest orcs and briars made requests, and tensions with the Thule over raids and slaves continued. A Jotun warband came to Anvil for a contest and the weregild, Tsark dismantled the Imperial spy network, and the Grendel demanded the Imperial Fleet Master as their ambassador.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: Thuli's mine was allegedly raided by Imperials who killed the owner and stole slaves, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction offered four investigators a chance to examine the evidence. Meanwhile, the Thule fort in the hills neared completion.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Released Imperial slaves were deposited at Wendell's Hope with a note saying they had been purchased by Erska Crowspeaker.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: The Thule began a fortification here that scouts reported half complete after only three months.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: Mentioned in passing: watchtowers of the new Thule castle at Crow's Keep overlook the passes into Urdur.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though the wider Thule frontier dispute, including Sungold Pass, forms the backdrop.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Thule watchtowers and garrisons around Crow's Keep now overlook the passes into the Silver Peaks from the east.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: Work on the Holt of the Oak continued and was due shortly before the Winter Solstice. The briars there proposed a liao workshop and named Ursol Gwin as their point of contact.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: Eadric Fjellrevening's expedition uncovered the lost Liao Garden near Sweetglades, cleared vallornspawn, and enabled the recovery of preserved vinum sap and refining equipment.

Astolat.t: Around a hundred and fifty freed orcs set out for Astolat, where the Winter Sun were billeted, drawn by the offer of land in return for military service.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire had mounted a convincing challenge to Grendel supremacy in the bay.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: heralds of the Golden Hare found lost orcs here.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: most Great Forest orc warriors had gone to aid the Navarr here.

Feroz.t: The Grendel invasion continued, and the Grendel demanded a worthy ambassador with whom to discuss the territory's surrender.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is linked to Wintermark's affairs this season, including the Jotun contest and freed slaves heading west to the 'Mark.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: heralds of the Golden Hare found lost orcs here.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers are noted as settling into new homes here.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: heralds of the Golden Hare found lost orcs here.

Karsk.t: The Thule alleged that Imperial raiders killed mine owner Thuli in Krevsaty and stole slaves. Their fortification there is expected to be completed by the Autumn Equinox.

Miekarova.t: About a hundred released Imperial slaves were left at Wendell's Hope, where the civil service helped them, though many chose to head on to Wintermark.

Mountains of the Moon.t: The people of Tsark located and dismantled the entire Imperial spy network, leaving the Empire with no knowledge of events there.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: developments with the Mournwold thralls are referenced in further reading.

Ossium.t: A major Thule force remained as the only significant army in the territory, and their Bonewood fortification was already half built.

Otkodov.t: The orcs of Otkodov chafed under trade sanctions while still claiming Sungold Pass, which the Senate later ceded to them by treaty.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel message from Salt Lord Moorvain was received here.

Sermersuaq.t: The new Thule castle at Crow's Keep has watchtowers overlooking the passes into the Silver Peaks, and the dispute over Sungold Pass ended with the pass being ceded to Otkodov.

Shayeel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel holding it issued their diplomatic demand, though the territory itself is not named.

Skarsind.t: The freed Dubhtraig orcs were brought to Gildenheim and found new lives across the territory. The Thule completed their castle at Crow's Keep, with garrisons overlooking Urdur and the Silver Peaks.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: lost orcs were found in its forests by heralds of the Golden Hare.

Therunin.t: The Great Forest orcs continued making the territory their home as the Holt of the Oak neared completion. The briars sought permission to refine liao there, and about twenty freed orcs chose to settle among them.

Lost in translation.d: Skywise Tulva's Winter mandate invited the freed slaves to settle in Skarsind, but without provisions they set out at winter's end with little idea of the way. Progress was slow, and many survived only by the charity of Imperial citizens. The civil service judged that a motion would no longer help and that independent captains must track the refugees down. The more military strength committed, the more would reach Skarsind: 10,000 would bring all of them, while under 5,000 would bring fewer than a quarter and leave bandits on the frontiers. Help might also come from the Winter Sun, the Freedom-Heresy humans travelling with the Great Forest Orcs, or Irra Harah. Rewards could come from the guerdon or an Imperial Orc Synod mandate.

Dawn.t: Handfuls of refugees strayed as far as Astolat and Semmerholm, and those on outskirts such as Dawn were unlikely ever to be found unless a large search was mounted. Papa Otec also restated its intent to kill Semmerholm's senator Zadkiel de Coeurdefer.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj, with the Dawnish, crushed the Barrens, from which the Great Forest Orcs and their human companions fled.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the freed slaves were rescued from the Grendel in the raids on the Broken Shore.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn well-wishers were among those who donated food and resources to the refugees.

Imperial Orcs.t: The refugees were heading for an Imperial Orc homeland, and their arrival could give Imperial Orc businesses and farms extra production if enough were escorted there. The national assembly could also pass a mandate trading a season of reduced production for rewards to the captains who helped.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs were walking the trods in support of their Navarr allies, and could leave them to join the search.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast well-wishers donated supplies to the refugees, and a handful of them ended up as far astray as Kahraman. Papa Otec restated its intent to kill Feroz's senator Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza.

The League.t: League well-wishers donated to the refugees, and some orcs reached as far north as Temeschwar by following the Blood Red Roads.

Wintermark.t: A few refugees reached Kalpaheim, and the accompanying story follows a young Wintermark refugee from Solvi stealing food to feed starving orcs in the spirit of 'all that is worthwhile'.

Lost in translation.o: In Spring 383YE most of the orc slaves freed in the raid on Dubhtraig were scattered across the Empire, begging or turning to banditry, because no Senate motion was raised to supply their journey to Skarsind. Imperial military units were offered the chance to find them and escort them north.

Astolat.t: A handful of refugees ended up in Astolat, an out-of-the-way territory where they were unlikely to be found without a substantial search.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: many refugees were reduced to begging outside the villages and towns north of the Bay.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Papa Otec remained committed to the death of the senator for Feroz, Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the story's young narrator mourns his home city of Solvi, lost to the orcs.

Kahraman.t: A handful of refugees strayed as far as Kahraman, having underestimated the size of the Empire.

Semmerholm.t: A handful of refugees wandered into remote Semmerholm, and Papa Otec restated its intent to kill the territory's senator, Zadkiel de Coeurdefer.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind was the refugees' intended new home, but only a handful had arrived by the Equinox. Whether the rest arrive, bringing a possible boost to Imperial Orc production, depended on how much military strength was committed to escorting them.

Temeschwar.t: A few refugees reached Temeschwar by following the Blood Red Roads northward.

Loud and proud.d: After Kish of the Flame Beneath the Earth's statement, aspiring Highborn cantors offered the Cat's Graces 6 thrones to stage a Winter Solstice concert, which Malachi of the Custodes Clavium would attend. Eli of the Cenotaph's call for inquisitorial rooms opened a 30-crown commission amendment. If it passes, the Blade of Wisdom would give the Imperial Inquisitor a yearly focus, and Magistrate Abraham would draft legal options for restoring the Inquisitorial Court. Sister Elysium's Ambition Assembly publicly committed to finishing the Grand Inspiration by the start of 389YE, and Bastion's trade boomed. Präst Stelltus listed six signs for Zemress, and the Sumaah offered to host historical research costing 5 thrones. They expect the Synod to rule.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly's focus on the Grand Inspiration brought offers to Highborn cantors and inquisitors, and a 30-crown amendment for inquisitorial chambers. Bastion's businesses also prospered as pilgrims prepared for the planned opening.

Loud and proud.o: In Autumn 388YE the Highborn and Ambition Assemblies pressed on with the unfinished Grand Inspiration of the Way, prompting offers around a cantor concert and inquisitorial chambers, and a public pledge to complete it by Spring 389YE. Meanwhile the Sumaah answered the Way Assembly's challenge with their case that Zemress is a Paragon of Prosperity.

Bastion.t: Pilgrims booked inns and hostels across Bastion ahead of the promised opening ceremony. As a result, every business in the territory operates one rank higher following the Autumn Equinox.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Präst Stelltus's letter setting out the Sumaah case for Zemress was delivered to the Sumaah Embassy in Necropolis.

Louder than words.d: Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-Undivided arranged a Saturday meeting with Ambassador Kindra Surefoot. The Dragons offered three years of peace against the Empire's hoped-for six, and would return half the output of any ceded bourse resource. Ephisis proposed four deals. One would trade food from up to three of Navarr, Highguard, the Marches, Dawn and Varushka for Thule mana, adding a year to the treaty per nation. Orobus offered warlocks to staff Imperial colleges. Caridis offered 50 thrones if the Synod renounces preaching in Otkodov. Thule merchants also sought Marcher cattle bonds. Rejecting the treaty might help bring the Jotun to peace. The Dragons sought an account of the lost Thule of Volham and thanked the Empire for Frekki's death.

Dawn.t: Dawn is one of five nations that could spare food for the proposed Thule trade, gaining 3 thrones per territory in taxes while losing one army's supply. The Reeve of Boar's Market would oversee the trade.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named among the nations already at war with the Empire, and as unlikely ever to offer peace terms.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named among the Empire's current enemies, and as unlikely ever to offer peace terms.

Highguard.t: Highguard could commit food to the Thule trade, trading one army's supply for higher taxes and mana. The Cinderpath Custodian would gain ten crystals a season to run it.

Jotun.t: Naomi had judged the Jotun more likely to make peace if the Empire were being weakened by war with the Thule. Rejecting the treaty could therefore be a route to bringing the Jotun to the negotiating table.

Navarr.t: Navarr could supply food to the Thule in exchange for mana and higher taxes, at the cost of one army's supply. The Broker of Treji Wayhouse would manage the trade.

Thule.t: The Dragons demanded Imperial land and offered only three years of peace. They sought food after a devastating famine, offered warlock aid to Imperial colleges and payment for a Synod ban on preaching, and hunted the renegade Nolith Silver-Hand.

Urizen.t: The magicians of Urizen were to vote in the Hall of Worlds on whether Orobus' warlocks should help staff the Doyen of the Spires, in return for reduced upkeep and the Thule receiving copies of codified rituals.

Varushka.t: Two Varushkan regions, Opascari and Mieriada, were named as the land the Dragons want, and many Varushkans resent ceding more territory. Varushka could also supply food to the Thule through the Custodian of the Shchaslyvyy Spile.

Wintermark.t: Kindra Surefoot of Wintermark leads the negotiations as Ambassador to Otkodov, while some in Wintermark feel too much land has already been surrendered. Wintermark figures were also thanked for their information about the Agramant's servants.

Louder than words.o: In Spring 387YE the Thule pressed the Empire for land, wanting at least one of Opascari or Mieriada, as the price of renewing the peace treaty that expires at the Summer Solstice. Ephisis brokered several side offers intended to ease the negotiations.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Mieriada was demanded by the Dragons. If ceded, the Night Quarry would pass to the Thule with half its output possibly returned, and the Imperial embassy in its frigid north would then sit in Thule-held land.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: In the opening story, the Whisperer's minions are spreading through Urdur in the wake of the famine, and a Claw of the Dragon sets out from there to hunt the renegade Silverhand.

Verthandi/Askja.t: Mentioned in passing: the region itself is not named; the page refers only to the Warlock Askja, who disavowed the Thule raiders of Volham.

Volodmartz/Opascari.t: Opascari was one of the two regions the Dragons named. If ceded, the Hunt of Alderei the Fair would be worked by the Thule, with half its production possibly remitted to the Empire.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova's region of Mieriada was one of two the Dragons sought, and it houses the Imperial embassy to Otkodov. The Thule offered to keep the Maze of Zoria under Imperial control if it were ceded.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov is recovering from a famine that killed thousands and left it unable to raise armies without Imperial food. The Dragons wanted any treaty to outlaw preaching the Way there unless the Synod renounced it.

Sermersuaq.t: The Dragons welcomed news that Maarik the Golden Tongue, one of the Agramant's servants threatening Sermersuaq, had been dispatched. They hoped the other followers of the Voice of the Pines would soon follow him.

Verthandi.t: Mentioned in passing: Verthandi is not named, though it is among the lands the Dragons have claimed that some Imperial citizens would like to retake.

Volodmartz.t: Volodmartz's region of Opascari was named by the Dragons as land they want ceded, which would put the Hunt of Alderei the Fair under Thule control.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Pen of Vossk of Zenith Ascendant is named as having helped task Ephisis with finding trade opportunities with the Thule.

Love and War.d: After nearly two years the army was almost mustered. Its name was expected to stand apart from the lost Hounds of Glory, and Dawn's weavers would make banners and surcoats once it was chosen. The egregores suggested announcing the decision in the Glory Square before the election of the Senator for the Barrens, to lift spirits. The civil service offered three cost-free qualities: Glorious, with Eleonaris giving its general a triumphant blade each year; Guardian; and Vanguard. House deCassilon of Spiral Castle proposed a fourth, the Magic quality. This required building a Circle of the War-witch in Weirwater, delaying the quality by a season and ending Dawn's ability to support a college of magic.

Dawn.t: Dawn's new army awaited a name and a quality from the Senator for Astolat, a choice between glory, love, conquest or witchery that would shape how Dawnish nobles and yeofolk make war for years.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj appear as the enemy who killed Sir Elegar during the retreat in Therunin, and as the foe Dawn once drove from Ossium.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr is not named, though Therunin, a Navarr-held territory, is where Sir Elegar fell fighting with the Golden Sun.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League is not named; the only link is Spiral Castle, which lies in Dawnish Weirwater.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan allies are credited with helping Dawn capture Ossium from the Druj.

Love and War.o: In Spring 387YE Dawn's new army, mustered in Astolat and funded largely by Emperor Vesna Borkovna Prochnost through the Hand of the Chancellor, neared completion. The new Senator for Astolat, Éamon Ashenmourn de Cordraco, was left to choose its name and its defining quality.

Weirwater/Weirmoor.t: The proposed Circle of the War-witch is listed as sited near Spiral Castle in Weirmoor, with the castle providing hospitality and upkeep if it is built.

Weirwater/Wickmoor.t: The deCassilon proposal describes building the Circle of the War-witch, a stone duelling ground ringed by a dozen monoliths, in Wickmoor in the vale below Spiral Castle.

Astolat.t: The new Dawnish army was mustering in Astolat, and Astolat's Senator was charged with naming it and choosing its quality. Astolat's artisans of rods, staves and mage armour had ties with Spiral Castle.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is recalled as the land Dawnish and Varushkan armies took from the Druj, and as the setting of Sir Jory's tale of hunting Druj infiltrators.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the page refers to Spiral Castle in Weirwater rather than the territory of Spiral itself.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens is cited as the Hounds of Glory's legacy, now part of Dawn, and the election of its Senator was suggested as the moment to announce the army's name.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Sir Elegar is said to have fallen in Therunin, fighting with the Golden Sun during the retreat from the Druj.

Weirwater.t: House deCassilon of Spiral Castle in Weirwater proposed building a Circle of the War-witch there, a 25 white granite and 75 crown edifice that would give the new army the Magic quality.

Love and monsters.d: With the Barrens won and the Druj crumbling, Dawn turned to the vallorn. Several opportunities were offered. One was a grand monument in Murderdale that would halve the cost of enlarging Dawnish armies until the vallorn is defeated. Another was a pair of competing Synod mandates: one supporting the Vallornguard's leadership of the Knight of the Greenwood, the other pressing a Dawnish claim on Brocéliande. A third was the Gardens of the Sphinx in Weaving, which would trade a college of magic for an army of war witches. Eleonaris also summoned General Katelyn. Lord Reynard Griffinsong's Vallornguard mandate was upheld, so an administrative motion was due at the Autumn Equinox 388YE. Katelyn met Eleonaris, but the details remain unclear.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Assembly embraced the vallorn as its Highest Calling and backed the Vallornguard to lead questing from Greenwood Manor. Opportunities remained for a monument to cheapen enlarging Dawnish armies and for gardens that would let Dawn raise a war-witch army.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are described as beaten and crumbling, with Dawnish folk debating whether to finish them or turn on the vallorn.

Navarr.t: Navarr had already embraced the Vallornguard, and Dawn chose to follow suit rather than enact the rival mandate that would have pressed a Dawnish claim on Brocéliande, a vallornheart territory Navarr would regard as its concern.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard is cited as the only rival to Dawnish war witches in battlefield magic.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish characters recall the conquest of Ossium as one of the Empire's victories over the Druj.

Love and monsters.o: After the Dawnish National Assembly upheld the Earl of Fools' Highest Calling to fight the vallorn, Dawn was offered several ways to prepare for war against it. The Assembly backed a mandate opening Greenwood Manor to the Vallornguard and citizens of all nations, and Dame Katelyn Quinnell De Cordraco met the eiaran Eleonaris.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Dawnish yeofolk would have settled in Boar's Dell under the competing Brocéliande mandate, which was not the one the Assembly upheld.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Murderdale was offered as the site of The Vallorn's Demise, a statue costing 75 white granite, 225 crowns and a dose of true liao that would halve the cost of enlarging Dawnish armies until the vallorn is defeated.

Astolat.t: The Gardens of the Sphinx could be built in Weaving, giving up a Dawnish college of magic so that Dawn could raise another army built around war witches.

Brocéliande.t: A competing mandate would have sent Dawnish nobles and yeofolk into Brocéliande and raised Dawn's banner there, but the Assembly upheld the rival Vallornguard mandate instead.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is not named, though the page notes that three vallornhearts lie adjacent to the Barrens.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: in the opening dialogue, Ossium is recalled as conquered from the Druj.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarangrave's conquery is cited as a joint victory with Eleonaris to be celebrated with a triumph, and as an example that a vallornheart territory need not be Navarr land.

The Barrens.t: Now held by Dawn and bordered by three vallornhearts, the Barrens could host a vast monument in Murderdale to rally Dawnish soldiers against the vallorn.

Love and rockets.d: Mael Donjeon of House Remys urged Dawn's troubadours to teach the Highborn about glory and love. Both assemblies ignored the civil service's warning that this could worsen conflicts of faith, and Kerem of the Chantry's welcome passed 269-0. Most troubadours moved their hosts and linked love and glory to the virtues, though some dismissed the virtues entirely. Claims that love and glory should be pre-eminent among the virtues still troubled many Highborn. The Highborn Assembly may pass one of three competing mandates, each needing a Greater majority. Calling love and glory virtuous would bind the nations closer. Calling them a harmless distraction would simply lift the Dawnish congregations' penalty. Calling them a vice would expel the Grey Pilgrims from Dawn and hamper joint military campaigns.

Dawn.t: Dawn's troubadours carried the nation's ideals of love and glory into Highguard and were mostly well received. If the Highborn endorse those ideals as virtuous, Dawnish congregations would gain liao and votes, but if they condemn them, Grey Pilgrims would be barred from Dawn and its armies would struggle to fight alongside Highborn ones.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: in the opening tale, a Dawnish yeofolk's husband and family were killed by the Druj after the Barrens fell.

Highguard.t: Highborn chapters opened their doors to the Dawnish troubadours, and many were moved by their songs. The Highborn Assembly must now decide whether love and glory are virtuous, merely other qualities, or a vice, with consequences for its kinship with Dawn and for joint military campaigns.

Love and rockets.o: In Autumn 383YE, responding to a Dawnish Assembly mandate, Dawnish troubadours travelled across Highguard to sing of love and glory, and the Highborn welcomed them warmly. Their visit left the Highborn Assembly with a choice of mandates on whether these Dawnish ideals are virtuous, a distraction or a vice.

Astolat.t: If the Highborn Assembly declares love and glory a vice, the Grey Pilgrims would no longer be welcome to walk the trods of Astolat.

Bastion.t: Troubadours sang across Bastion's chapter halls, and many visited Elayne Silverlark's basilica there; a few were allowed to play her mandolin, reviving interest in the proposed Arbour of the Twin Roses.

Casinea.t: Dawnish troubadours spread through Casinea's chapter halls, singing of love and glory and debating the virtues with their Highborn hosts.

Necropolis.t: Dawnish troubadours performed in Necropolis's chapter halls as part of their mission to bring Dawn's understanding of the Way to Highguard.

Reikos.t: Reikos was among the four Highborn territories where Dawnish troubadours sang their songs of love and glory to welcoming chapters.

Semmerholm.t: If the Highborn Assembly declares love and glory a vice, the Grey Pilgrims would no longer be welcome to walk the trods of Semmerholm.

Weirwater.t: If the Highborn Assembly declares love and glory a vice, the Grey Pilgrims would no longer be welcome to walk the trods of Weirwater.

Made anew.d: Captains taking Explore the Southern Reaches mapped Siroc Bayou, the Crucible and the Quiet Grasses, which remain uncontrolled. The Unfettered Mind traced the marsh's strange flora, fauna and temporary regio to Spring, Night and Winter magic, Azoth, Ossegrahn and diffuse ilium. The Rod and Shield found Grendel camps and confirmed that the Children of Wrecks' navy, the Gathered Storm, lies at Free Landing. They also found that armies cannot cross to Feroz or Segura now the bridges are gone. Grendel and Asavean mage-killers in the Crucible were left for Sakari Nightscale to face. Opportunities included marsh flowers, the Rainbow Conservatory, Sand Crab Camp, the Chimes of Silence and the Enigmatic Tower college.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: many Dawnish captains are listed among those who explored the southern reaches.

Grendel.t: Grendel encampments were found and neutralised in the marshes, and an abandoned Grendel supply camp became Sand Crab Camp. A large band of Grendel and Asavean mage-killers still lurks in the Crucible, readying a last raid on the Rod and Shield.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: one Highborn captain, Thomas, is listed among the explorers.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; the only link is that the new southern marshes are contrasted with those of Bregasland.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: several Navarr captains are listed among those who explored the southern reaches.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn captains led the exploration of their transformed territory, and many of the opportunities discovered would benefit the Brass Coast, including a possible Mistress Sand Crab title and a Freeborn-only venture. Bakar i Riqueza funded the Parador of Salt and Sand expansion, while the Gathered Storm's stolen Storm Child figurehead taunts the Freeborn.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: League ingenuity helped Rod and Shield magicians reach the Enigmatic Tower, and a League writer is evoked in the opening tale.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: a Marcher, Billiam, features in the opening tale, John a Woode is listed among the explorers, and Marcher landskeepers might be drawn to the proposed Enigmatic Tower college.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen explorers are listed, a conversation with an Urizen magician helped inspire the Chimes of Silence, and the proposed tower college might attract Urizen stargazers.

Varushka.t: The Rod and Shield proposed that Lutomysla Niegoslava bring Varushkan road builders south to appraise how a durable road could cross the Night-and-Spring infused marshes. Several Varushkan captains also took part in the exploration.

Wintermark.t: Sakari Nightscale, Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield and a Kallavesi mystic, is responsible for dealing with the mage-killers in the Crucible and would receive the order's oddities if they are killed. Many Wintermark captains joined the exploration, and Wintermark mystics might be drawn to the proposed tower college.

Made anew.o: After the Autumn Equinox 386YE, explorers and the Unfettered Mind and Rod and Shield Conclave orders charted the new marsh created when the Scorrero flooded southern Madruga, mapping three transformed regions and uncovering several opportunities. Bakar i Riqueza took one of them, funding an expansion of the Parador of Salt and Sand.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The Children of Wrecks' control of the Cazar Straits is one of the holdings that lets them sustain their new navy.

Madruga/Crucible.t: The Crucible is now an uncontrolled, wild and enigmatic marsh where Grendel and Asavean mage-killers lurk and a powerful sense of boundless possibility grips visitors. It holds Sand Crab Camp and the Enigmatic Tower, and is a possible site for the Rainbow Conservatory.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: The Children of Wrecks have completed their navy, the Gathered Storm, and anchored it at Free Landing, its flagship bearing the stolen Storm Child figurehead.

Madruga/Quiet Grasses.t: The former Great Grasses are now the uncontrolled Quiet Grasses, home to strange tall trees and a profound silence. Cabella i Riqueza has proposed the Chimes of Silence great work there, and hakima explorations of the region inspired the Parador expansion.

Madruga/Siroc Bayou.t: The former Siroc Plains are now the Siroc Bayou, a wild, uncontrolled and hallucinatory marsh of mangroves and altered beasts. It is a possible site for the Rainbow Conservatory.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Its existing mix of ilium-infused marshwater and Night magic makes it the likeliest place outside Madruga where an appraisal might allow marsh flowers to be cultivated.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Children of Wrecks' new navy, the Gathered Storm, can now threaten any settlement along the Bay of Catazar, alarming the people of Quzar and Calvos.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: its marshes are contrasted with the warm new marshes of Madruga, and a Bregas mage features in the opening tale.

Feroz.t: The Midpoint bridge is destroyed, so Imperial armies still cannot move between Madruga and Feroz. The Rod and Shield suggested a Varushkan appraisal to find a way to build a lasting connection.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: its marshes are contrasted with the warm new marshes of southern Madruga.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the ilium particles infusing the Scorrero and the new marshes were swept down from Kahraman's mountains.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: its marshes are contrasted with the warm new marshes of southern Madruga.

Madruga.t: The territory's southern reaches have been remapped as three uncontrolled, transformed regions full of altered creatures, shifting land and temporary regio. Opportunities there include marsh-flower herb gardens, the Rainbow Conservatory, Sand Crab Camp, the Chimes of Silence great work and the Enigmatic Tower college, and the Parador of Salt and Sand has been expanded to trade in Adversity vis.

Ossium.t: The Drownbark Forest shares the ilium-infused waters and Night magic of the new marshes, and an appraisal might find a way to grow marsh flowers there.

Raineach.t: Mentioned in passing: rumour holds that the Temple of Tempest Jade there is one of the bastions helping to sustain the Children of Wrecks' navy.

Segura.t: The Cerevado bridge is gone, so armies cannot move between Segura and Madruga until a new crossing is built. Altered creatures from the marshes have been sighted as far upstream as Cerevado.

Make a deal.d: Three opportunities arose. Thornsong House, a Senate-commissioned weirwood college at Peakedge Song, would create the Thornsinger title and allow research into new potions. Expanding the Feverwater docks into a fortified steading would let the Dredgemaster push into Sarangrave and Zenith waters, raid the shores, and offer Navarr an Adventure in the Sarangrave. The Great Forest Orcs offered cheaper herb garden upgrades in Therunin. If the Senate promised to cede them the Heart of Peytaht during this Solstice, they would extend that aid to other Navarr territories and permanently enrich the Thimble. A Sentinel Gate conjunction also opened onto a Feverwater wreck, while outlaws troubled East Ashes.

Druj.t: Druj raiders harry the Feverwater shores and hold a settlement in Bloodwater Marsh. The proposed docks expansion would let armed boats push into Druj-dominated waters and raid their shores, while outlaws in East Ashes already raid the Druj in Zenith.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Peakedge Stead owes much of its size to lingering Highborn exiles, it is popular with Highborn healers, and it trades with the herb gardens of Reikos.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: some of the East Ashes outlaws are said to be Navarr displaced from Liathaven, which the Jotun hold.

Navarr.t: The Navarr were offered a prestigious herb-lore college with a Thornsinger chosen by their herb garden owners, an expanded Feverwater operation, and an Adventure in the Sarangrave open only to Navarr units. Great Forest Orc help would also make upgrading herb gardens cheaper, nation-wide if the Senate made its promise.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: reasonable roads link Peakedge Stead to Highwatch in Morrow, bringing Imperial merchants to trade.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: recent events in Varushka have left some Therunin steadings nervous about the outlaw gang in East Ashes.

Make a deal.o: Prompted by Cardinal Darian Numbers of the Prosperity assembly, Navarr brokers and their Great Forest Orc neighbours put forward several proposals to improve the prosperity of Therunin. These included a great herb-lore college at Peakedge, a fortified expansion of the Feverwater docks, and a request that the Senate promise the Heart of Peytaht to the orcs.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: The river feeding the Sarangrave runs through the vallorn heart of Bendol, part of the route the proposed Navarr adventurers would take from the Feverwater docks.

Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh.t: The Bloodwater Spears orc sept lives along the eastern banks here. Raiding boats would need to give the Druj settlement in the marsh a wide berth, though paid thorns could push into its Druj-dominated waters.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: The river from the Feverwater runs up through Nesustak Forest, opening it to Navarr adventurers if the docks were expanded.

Sarangrave/Turan Flats.t: Turan Flats lies along the river route that Navarr adventurers could follow from an expanded Feverwater docks.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: The Great Forest Orcs, who long tended the weirwood grove of the Eaves of Peytaht here, asked the Senate to promise them the region once the Barrens is conquered.

Therunin/East Ashes.t: East Ashes holds the ancient Feverwater docks, proposed for expansion into a fortified steading, and the submerged wreck reached by a Sentinel Gate conjunction. An outlaw gang is harassing travellers on its southern trods.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Great Forest Orcs' herb gardens and potion-brewing skill in the Lower Tarn Valley underpin the Thornsong House plan and their offer of cheaper herb garden upgrades. The region's briars are still awaiting a decision on the Lost Liao Garden salvage.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Peakedge Song would host Thornsong House, a Senate-commissioned weirwood college meant to make it the Empire's foremost centre of herb lore, overseen by a new Thornsinger.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: The vallorn of Sweetglades shapes where East Ashes steadings are built. The Lost Liao Garden, whose salvage remains undecided, was found just outside the region.

Brocéliande.t: If the Senate promised the Heart of Peytaht to the Great Forest Orcs, their woodshapers would visit even Brocéliande to help expand herb gardens. Some of the East Ashes outlaws are said to be Navarr displaced from there.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia's herb gardens would gain the Great Forest Orcs' help, cutting upgrade costs by one wain of weirwood per rank, but only if the Senate made its promise over the Heart of Peytaht.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: some of the outlaws troubling East Ashes are former Navarr displaced from Liathaven.

Miaren.t: The excitement over Seren in Miaren highlighted how undeveloped Therunin remains. Miaren's herb gardens would also benefit from the orcs' woodshaping if the Senate made its promise over the Heart of Peytaht.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: a reasonable road links Highwatch in Morrow to Peakedge Stead in Therunin.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Peakedge Stead lies on the border with Reikos, is linked to High Chalcis by road, and trades with Reikos's herb gardens.

Sarangrave.t: Expanded Feverwater docks would let Imperial boats dredge and raid the Sarangrave half of the lake, and would serve as a staging point for Navarr adventurers heading up its river. The Senate might later appraise using the docks to help invade the territory.

The Barrens.t: The Great Forest Orcs asked the Senate to commit, at this Solstice only, to ceding the Heart of Peytaht to them once the Barrens becomes Imperial.

Therunin.t: Therunin was the focus of all the proposals: Thornsong House at Peakedge, a fortified steading at the Feverwater docks, cheaper herb garden upgrades and a richer Thimble. The territory also faces unresolved questions over the Lost Liao Garden salvage and a growing outlaw problem.

Zenith.t: Feverwater boats could push into occupied Zenith if the docks were expanded. Outlaws based in East Ashes already raid the Druj there, and would need new targets if the Druj were driven out.

Make good use.d: A Feni warband of roughly a thousand fighters, which the Spring Equinox efforts had failed to stop, was raiding across the Mournwold, chiefly from the Chalkdowns. Its concealing magic had apparently failed, letting scouts observe its camps. No conjunctions were found, but any Imperial army taking an offensive order in the Mournwold could destroy it by inflicting at least 400 casualties. Otherwise farms and businesses would lose 36 rings each season and herb gardens two herbs. The Alderly enclave could not be found without someone giving the Herald of the Council the means to locate it. In Hahnmark, raids centred on Southridge carried the same penalties, and two conjunctions were identified.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Alderly Feni enclave is said to have resisted the Jotun occupation of the Mournwold as well as the later Imperial liberation.

The Marches.t: Marcher farms, businesses and herb gardens in the Mournwold faced heavy losses unless an army dealt with the raiders. Suspicion also grew among other Marchers that the insular Alderly folk, rumoured to have Feni blood, had drifted from Marcher custom or were colluding with the Feni.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Hahnmark suffered renewed Feni ambushes on farms, businesses and herb gardens. Two conjunctions were identified that offered a chance to strike back at the raiders.

Make good use.o: In Summer 382YE Feni raiding surged across the Mournwold and Hahnmark, threatening production on every farm, business and herb garden there, while the long-standing Feni enclave in Alderly remained hidden and untouched by the raids.

Hahnmark/Kalpamark.t: Feni raiding bands extended their reach from Southridge into prosperous Kalpamark.

Hahnmark/Southridge.t: Southridge, long suspected of hiding a Feni community in its hills and gullies, was the centre of the renewed Hahnmark raids.

Hahnmark/Valasmark.t: Feni bands were sighted raiding in militant Valasmark, west of their Southridge base.

Hahnmark/Wood Heath.t: Wood Heath was strangely given a wide berth by the Feni raiders, despite the limited defence its folk could muster.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Alderly reported no Feni attacks at all, even though it shelters a hidden Feni enclave that no Imperial force has been able to find. This drew suspicion of collusion onto its insular charcoal burners and woodcutters.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: The Chalkdowns were the main focus of the Feni warband, whose disguised camps scouts were able to approach and assess now that the Feni's concealing magic had failed.

Hahnmark.t: Several Feni warbands, centred on Southridge, raided across Hahnmark. Unless they were stopped, every farm and business would lose 36 rings of production and each herb garden two herbs.

Mournwold.t: A Feni warband of around a thousand fighters raided across the territory, threatening a 36-ring loss to every farm and business and two herbs to each herb garden each season. Any Imperial army taking an offensive order there could destroy it.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the large Feni warband was sighted travelling across Upwold before raiding in northern Mournwold.

Make it happen.d: Graciana identified three septs able to fight: the Bloodwater Spears under Halyx Fireeyes, the Water Walkers under the blind Agoska, and the human Grynbor under Queen Olwenna. Arming each would take a Senate motion, six months, 100 wains of mithril and 50 thrones, yielding a green army of 3,000 strength. Their morale, rated craven, would have to rise to resolved before they would revolt. Options to raise it included the Winter Sun's Break the Chains order, arming all three septs, treaties of military support or independence, and visible defeats of the Druj. Naomi and Lutomysla proposed diplomatic and magical alternatives. A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered a chance to rescue a captured Bloodwater Spear from Druj torture.

Druj.t: The Druj clans ruling Sarangrave, the Thornwasp, Banded Snake and Marshlizard, face an Imperial appraisal of how their hated slave septs might be armed and emboldened to rise against them. Defeats in Zenith or the Barrens were named as ways to break the septs' fear of them.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr-held Therunin is named as the only Imperial territory bordering Sarangrave from which the Winter Sun could work to incite the septs.

The League.t: The Senator for Temeschwar proposed the motion behind the appraisal and was urged to gather heroes for the conjunction to save the captured Bloodwater Spear orc.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the recent capture of Ossium from the Druj is cited as a defeat too distant to inspire the Sarangrave septs, and Ossium's Sand Fishers as a people more broken than they are.

Make it happen.o: Acting on a Senate motion proposed by Temeschwar, the prognosticator Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra appraised how the Empire might use its spy network in Sarangrave to incite the Druj's subject septs to rise up. She concluded that the septs loathe the Druj but are too frightened to rebel without arms and real encouragement.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: The human Grynbor sept makes regular forays into Bendol from neighbouring Nesustak Forest.

Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh.t: Bloodwater Marsh is home to the Bloodwater Spears, the largest of the three septs, whose spear-fishers could become a formidable force if armed and armoured.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: The Water Walkers, boatmen who ferry goods and people for the Druj, keep a number of small settlements in Kroll.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: Nesustak Forest is home to the Grynbor, a human sept under Queen Olwenna that sends expeditions into the vallorn-infested forest near the ruins of Béantal Dol.

Sarangrave/Turan Flats.t: The Water Walkers maintain small settlements on the Turan Flats, making the region one base of a sept the Empire might arm.

Sarangrave/Whisperwood.t: The Bloodwater Spears, led by the short-tempered matriarch Halyx Fireeyes, live in the Whisperwood as well as Bloodwater Marsh.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the taking of Ossium is cited as a crushing Imperial defeat of the Druj, though too far from Sarangrave to stir the septs, and its Sand Fishers are recalled as having been completely broken.

Sarangrave.t: The appraisal assessed whether Sarangrave's three septs could be secretly armed through the spy network and encouraged to revolt against Druj rule, which has gone unchallenged in living memory. A conjunction to Dead Stone Woods near the Feverwater offered a chance to rescue a tortured Bloodwater Spear.
