Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar's senator proposed the motion commissioning the appraisal, and the civil service suggested that same senator organise the heroes for the Dead Stone Woods conjunction.

Therunin.t: As the only Imperial territory bordering Sarangrave, Therunin is where the Winter Sun could stand while issuing Break the Chains to embolden a sept. Lutomysla also suggested a fane to Papa Otec on its border with Sarangrave.

Zenith.t: Driving the Druj from neighbouring Zenith was identified as a visible defeat that would raise the morale of the Sarangrave septs.

Map the Bay of Catazar.d: Kahraman proposed, and Madruga seconded, a Senate motion to map the Bay of Catazar, supplying Imperial fleets with the resources needed to explore the waters and create an Imperial map. The motion passed in Winter 381YE with an upkeep of 50 Thrones. It created an opportunity for fleet captains to contribute to a special project. That project was completed after the Winter Solstice, when the new map of the Bay of Catazar was finished, with details of the map and the territories surveyed recorded separately.
Map the Bay of Catazar.o: In Winter 381YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Madruga, to give Imperial fleets the resources to explore the Bay of Catazar and produce an Imperial map of it.

Bay of Catazar.t: The then-uncontrolled Bay was the subject of the Imperial survey, with fleet captains contributing to an expedition that produced a completed map of its waters after the Winter Solstice.

March on their belly.d: After the Autumn Equinox, hail, giant rats, root blight, a cyst-breeding sickness in livestock and a nasty influenza struck the Marches. Nobody starved, but farm incomes halved, food prices climbed across the Empire, army costs rose by a tenth to a fifth and natural resupply of armies, navies and fortifications fell by a fifth. The Marcher assembly chose to encourage farmers to cut the price of food sold to the Civil Service, naming Martin Orchard to coordinate with fifty liao. As a result, Marcher-owned farms, including those in Mournwold, produced half their usual coin the following season, but the status quo was expected to return by the end of the Spring Equinox.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; the page only reaches Mournwold, which they held, through the Marcher-owned farms there that shared the income loss.

The Marches.t: Marcher farmers saw their incomes halved by the cursed harvest, and after their assembly chose self-sacrifice under Martin Orchard they accepted another season of half income to restore Imperial resupply by Spring.

March on their belly.o: In late 379YE a Winter curse, identified as Naeve's Twisting Blight, devastated the Marcher harvest across Mitwold, Upwold and Bregasland. Food prices rose and Imperial military resupply suffered, until the Marcher assembly urged farmers to sell cheaply to the Civil Service for the good of the Empire.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland was one of the three territories struck by Naeve's Twisting Blight, suffering ruined crops, sick herds, vermin and influenza among its farmers.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold was among the territories hit by the curse, its fields, stores and herds damaged and its labour-force thinned by sickness.

Mournwold.t: Marcher-owned farms in Mournwold were bound by the assembly's judgement and produced only half their usual coin in the following season.

Upwold.t: Upwold suffered the curse's hail, blight, vermin and livestock sickness, and its people fell ill with influenza, leaving fewer hands to gather what harvest remained.

Mark of the Ravadi.d: The Vigilance Assembly recognised Ravadi Founders' Dance as an exemplar in 386YE, authorised a memorial in 387YE and chose Madruga for it in Spring 388YE. Ravadi died fighting the Dry Patricians in the old Great Grasses, but that spot now lies in the Quiet Grasses, where lingering Winter magic prevents an inspirational site. Instead the Custodes Clavicum offered the labour for Ravadi's Bow at Lightsea, a home and training keep for future Champions of Vigilance. The Senate could commission it without using one of its limited commissions, for 10 white granite and 5 mithril. If it is consecrated with true liao, it gives the Champion of Vigilance a permanent income of 24 ingots. Once in the following year, the Vigilance Assembly could also mandate the Champion to lead a new venture against a named threat.

Dawn.t: Ravadi was born Ravadi Watcher to House Berinore of Dawn, served House Castellan as a retainer and fought as a marksman in the Golden Sun before leaving to stride with the Navarr.

Navarr.t: Ravadi swore a Binding of Thorns and joined the Founders' Dance striding, walking the original path of Navarr and Thorn against the vallorn. Their partners in the Great Dance were Nathair Autumngale and the later blasphemer Fintan Nighthaven.

The Brass Coast.t: The memorial keep was proposed for Lightsea in Madruga, giving the Brass Coast territory a potential site of pilgrimage and a permanent home for the Champions of Vigilance.

Mark of the Ravadi.o: In Summer 388YE the Custodes Clavicum offered to build Ravadi's Bow, a keep at Lightsea in Madruga, as the inspirational memorial to the Exemplar of Vigilance Ravadi Founders' Dance. The Senate had until the end of the Summer Solstice to commission it.

Madruga/Crucible.t: Mentioned in passing: the wild, uncontrolled Crucible, formed when the Great Grasses were split, is described as a nexus of the realms of Adversity and their most dangerous magic.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: Lightsea was the proposed site of Ravadi's Bow, a small keep housing and training future Champions of Vigilance, to be built if the Senate commissioned it by the end of the Summer Solstice.

Madruga/Quiet Grasses.t: The exact spot where Ravadi fell lies in the Quiet Grasses, but the lingering touch of Winter magic means no inspirational location can currently be created there.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Ravadi's remains are presumed to have been washed into the Catazar by the flood, and the Wreckers once used a Siakha-powered maelstrom in Madruga to launch assaults across the Bay.

Madruga.t: The Vigilance Assembly chose Madruga, where Ravadi fell fighting the Dry Patricians, for the memorial. The potent and dangerous magic lingering there shaped where the keep could be built.

Mean what you say.d: Autumn magic shielding Bay of Catazar traders from Grendel pirates was fading. Fleets from Tassato, Sarvos, the Brass Coast, Highguard and Urizen faced poorer trade returns. Wintermark, Dawnish and Navarr magicians raised defences in fens and Urizen mountains. Spiral's trods were restored, and the Colossus of Sarvos reshaped itself into Empress Giselle. The Reapers enchanted the Mournwold's farms. Stars stayed hidden over Semmerholm, the Barrens and Zenith, and veils covered several territories. In the Conclave, Adamant offered a stone academy and a Master of the Koboldi, Eleonaris offered a research boon, and Sadogua offered gifts. Agramant thanked four magicians, offered heart's blood and proposed a parley.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish witches of Summer Dawning Relentless, aided by House de Gauvain, raised a Frozen Citadel in Limus, while Dawn's own Semmerholm still lay under a starless Night shroud of magnitude fifty.

Druj.t: The stars remained hidden over Druj-held Barrens and Zenith, and new magical fortifications in the fens and Urizen's mountains stood ready to resist any Druj advance.

Grendel.t: Grendel pirates in the Bay of Catazar had been confounded by Autumn magic, but the protection was fading and they might soon raid freely again. Agramant also boasted of catastrophic Grendel losses at the Black Plateau in Spiral.

Highguard.t: Highborn fleets faced poorer trade returns this season, and a scrying-blocking veil with heavy dark fog lay over Necropolis.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a possible invader that the new fenland defences would have resisted, and Jotun-held Liathaven was among the places where the stars had been missing in 381YE.

Navarr.t: The Eternal Family raised a Frozen Citadel in Caeli, and the Voice of the Quiet Forest restored Spiral's trods. A Navarr Assembly mandate puzzled priests, and Arhallogen demanded a meeting with up to four Navarr vates.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast fleets faced poorer trade returns this season, and a veil fell over Madruga once the nightly phantasmagoric displays ended.

The League.t: The Colossus of Sarvos now depicts Empress Giselle, and Dripping Echoes defences guarded the Morass. Tassato and Sarvos fleets faced poorer trade returns, Sarvos lay under a veil, and Sadogua was tending the ailing Richard of Holberg.

The Marches.t: The Reapers' Summer enchantment promised excellent Mournwold harvests, and the North Fens gained magical defences. A Marcher Assembly mandate confused priests, and Sadogua invited a Master Pearl to request a boon.

Thule.t: A Penumbral Veil was reported over Urdur in Otkodov, and it was unclear whether Nithoggir, Sküld or Verthandi were similarly shrouded.

Urizen.t: Frozen Citadels were raised in Limus and Caeli to guard against the Druj. Urizeni fleets faced poorer trade returns, and a veil with dark fog covered Redoubt.

Wintermark.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised the Dripping Echoes of the Fen over Kallavesa's West Marsh, the Morass and the North Fens, shielding these wetlands against Jotun or Druj invasion.

Mean what you say.o: A summer round-up of magical occurrences across the Empire: enchanted fortifications, restored trods in Spiral, a transformed Colossus of Sarvos, bountiful Mournwold farms and lingering starless skies and veils. It also set out Conclave business, including offers from Adamant, Eleonaris, Sadogua, Azoth and Arhallogen, and an unsettling message from Agramant.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised the Dripping Echoes of the Fen here, ready to resist any invader.

Holberg/The Morass.t: The Morass was protected by the Dripping Echoes of the Fen raised by Wintermark magicians.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: West Marsh's wetlands were guarded by the Dripping Echoes of the Fen from the Sussivari Frost Coven.

Morrow/Caeli.t: The Navarr Eternal Family raised a Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae in Caeli's mountains.

Otkodov/Nithoggir.t: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether Nithoggir also lay under the Penumbral Veil.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether Sküld also lay under the Penumbral Veil.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: Merchants and pedlars reported that the ritual Drawing the Penumbral Veil had been worked over Urdur.

Redoubt/Limus.t: Summer Dawning Relentless, aided by House de Gauvain, raised a Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae in Limus.

Bay of Catazar.t: Autumn magic had slowed time around Imperial ships to help them escape Grendel pirates, but captains feared it would dissipate entirely by the end of the Solstice.

Bregasland.t: Its North Fens were protected by the Dripping Echoes of the Fen raised by the Sussivari Frost Coven, though the defences were not tested.

Holberg.t: The Morass was fortified with the Dripping Echoes of the Fen by Wintermark magicians, ready to resist any hostile force.

Kallavesa.t: West Marsh gained the Dripping Echoes of the Fen from the Sussivari Frost Coven, which would have met any invasion with stiff resistance.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: noted as one of the places where the stars were absent for most of 381YE.

Madruga.t: A scrying-blocking veil with heavy dark fog lay over Madruga after the nightly phantasmagoric displays, and its fleets faced poorer trade returns.

Morrow.t: A Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae was raised in Caeli by the Navarr Eternal Family, ready to repel any Druj attack.

Mournwold.t: The Reapers' Strong Oxen, Golden Sunshine enchantment strengthened beasts and workers and bolstered crops, promising excellent harvests for Marcher and thrall alike. Agramant also offered a boon to whoever laid curses on the territory.

Necropolis.t: A ritual shroud warped the stars over Necropolis, blocking scrying and bringing heavy, dark fog.

Otkodov.t: Merchants reported a Penumbral Veil over Urdur, but whether its other regions were shrouded remained unclear without scrying.

Redoubt.t: A Frozen Citadel was raised in Limus, and a veil with inky clouds and dark fog hindered scrying over the territory.

Sarvos.t: The Colossus reshaped itself from the First Butcher into Empress Giselle, to many citizens' approval. A veil also hung over the territory, and its fleets faced poorer trade returns.

Semmerholm.t: The stars stayed missing beneath a Night shroud of magnitude fifty that blocked lesser scrying, and naga who spent time there felt a strong urge to secrecy.

Spiral.t: The Voice of the Quiet Forest restored its trods along new paths that skirt but never cross the Black Plateau, binding Spiral back into the trod network.

Tassato.t: Fleets from Tassato faced poorer returns from trade during the coming season.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Empress Giselle's tomb there was described by many as gaudy and not really a monument to her.

The Barrens.t: The stars remained absent above the Barrens, impeding scrying and heightening naga secretiveness, with the shroud expected to last until shortly before Winter 382YE.

Verthandi.t: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the Penumbral Veil over Urdur also covered Verthandi.

Zenith.t: The stars vanished from Zenith's sky shortly before the Spring Equinox, impeding scrying and affecting naga who spent time there.

Mercy is weakness.d: The Tempest Jade Maiden sect, reconciled with Urizen in 382YE, lost two thirds of its scholars when the Druj attacked the construction site in Morrow. With the temple now complete and backed by the Wisdom Assembly, the scholars challenge Synod priests across the Empire. Any mandate without a greater majority is now ineffective. Recognising Sulemaine as a paragon or exemplar would double the liao a mandate needs. A Urizen Assembly mandate passed with a greater majority could allow new sword scholar temples across Morrow. Opponents led by the sentinel Leoditus urge condemnation, which could open mandates to cast the scholars out.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the nation plays no part, and its only apparent link is the name of the Citadel of the Silver Dawn, where Leoditus teaches.

Druj.t: The Druj had slaughtered two thirds of the sword scholars when they attacked the temple site. Any new sword scholar temples in Morrow would turn their pitiless warriors against them.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Summer mandate encouraging corsairs to raid the Grendel is cited as one that would have failed. The Grendel are also named as a foe any new temples would fight.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Summer mandate supporting the Great Dance of the Navarr is cited as one that would have failed under the scholars' opposition.

Urizen.t: Urizen's sword scholars, backed by the Wisdom Assembly, now check the whole Synod. The Urizen National Assembly could urge the nation to embrace the Paragon of Blades, though sentinels such as Leoditus argue against them.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the mandate upholding the Wintermark tradition of interring the dead in the Kallavesa marshes is cited as one that would have failed.

Mercy is weakness.o: With the Temple of the Winds in Morrow finally rebuilt, the sword scholars of Sulemaine resumed their role as foils to the Imperial Synod, so every Synod mandate now needs a greater majority to be effective. The Wind also set out ways the Synod and Urizen could strengthen or condemn the scholars.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Summer mandate upholding the interment of the dead in the Kallavesa marshes is given as an example of one that would have failed.

Morrow.t: The Temple of the Winds in Morrow is complete and is the scholars' base. A Urizen Assembly mandate with a greater majority could allow more sword scholar temples across Morrow, each defending the territory like a fortification.

Redoubt.t: Sword scholar temples could not be effectively built in Redoubt, where the rival sentinels hold stronger influence and would resist any such effort.

Mermaids in the basement.d: Lutomysla found the bridges would cost over three thousand wains of white granite, would need engineering the Empire lacks, and would not remove the island quality. She offered several alternatives. Dedicated berths could let the Red Wind Corsairs cross freely. A fane to Janon could do the same for the Burning Falcon. Lashonar's songbirds could summon the corsair families to defend the islands, and Azoth's Archipelago Parador could end the Cazar Straits' poverty. Khobel Tavah might sink the islands entirely. New shipyards at Elos, Atalaya or Oran could support a navy. Of these, only the Red Wind Wharfs were later built, being commissioned in Summer 388YE.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Causeway that carried Dawn's armies across the Semmerlak was cited as a magical precedent unlikely to be repeated.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were named as the enemy the Golden Causeway was created to fight, and as a far greater threat than the Wreckers.

Grendel.t: The Grendel were named as a key obstacle, as they hold the Elos docks, smash bridges, have destroyed the shipyards at Atalaya and control the seas with their armada. Lutomysla judged that they fear an Imperial navy more than anything.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard was listed among the nations already supporting as many forces as they can.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn were offered several ways to reach their islands: berths for the Red Wind Corsairs, a fane to Janon for the Burning Falcon, corsair defence through Lashonar's songbirds, the Archipelago Parador, and a new navy rallied around the prow of the Storm's Child. Only the Red Wind Wharfs were later built.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: League engineers of Temeschwar and Holberg rejected the idea of undersea tunnels, and the League was noted as soon to be at its force limit.

Urizen.t: Urizen was noted to have an existing opportunity to support a navy alongside its two armies. This would require reclaiming Elos intact and building the Cargo Cranes.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the prognosticator Lutomysla Niegoslava who led the appraisal is Varushkan.

Mermaids in the basement.o: Following a Senate motion to appraise bridging the Brass Coast islands to the mainland, the prognosticator Lutomysla Niegoslava concluded in Winter 387YE that such bridges were effectively impossible. She instead set out alternative ways to reach, defend, enrich or even remove the islands of Free Landing and the Cazar Straits.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The Straits, controlled by the Iron Confederacy and impoverished by Rahab's rule, could have that poverty lifted by the Archipelago Parador. The region would also be covered by the berths and corsair defence proposals.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: New berths at Oran would let the Red Wind Corsairs cross to the Cazar Straits freely, and these were commissioned in Summer 388YE. A costlier expansion of the wharfs into a full shipyard was also offered.

Madruga/Crucible.t: Mentioned in passing: 'Crucible' appears only as a title of the eternal Azoth, not in reference to the region.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Free Landing, still held by the Children of Wrecks, was proposed as the site for Janon's Alcazar of Flame and a rebuilt Atalaya shipyard, though neither was built.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: Quzar in Lightsea was named as the location for the Song of Salt and Sand. Through it, Lashonar's songbirds could call the corsairs to defend the islands, but Lashonar was not approached.

Redoubt/Naris.t: The Elos docks in Naris could be cheaply expanded into a shipyard, but only once they were reclaimed from the Grendel.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: expanding Oran's wharfs was said to secure Oran as a crucial port on the Bay, and every nation adjoining it was said to be at its force limit.

Feroz.t: Feroz's Cazar Straits, held by the Iron Confederacy, was assessed for bridges, berths and corsair defence, and was offered the Archipelago Parador to end its poverty. The Red Wind berths at Oran were later built.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the walls and pumps of Holberg were invoked as comparisons for the scale of the problem.

Madruga.t: Madruga's Free Landing remained in Wrecker hands. It was proposed as the site for a fane to Janon and a rebuilt Atalaya shipyard, and Lightsea was proposed as the home of the songbird defence.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium was named as the land Dawn invaded via the Golden Causeway.

Redoubt.t: Expanding the Elos docks into a shipyard was offered, but Elos was in Grendel hands, so nothing could be done until it was reclaimed.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos's island bridges and the Spider's Tollkeep were cited as far smaller precedents.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm was not named directly, but the Golden Causeway that Dawn's armies used was cited as an example of eternal aid.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar's mining professors dismissed undersea tunnels as impossible, and a Temeschwar academic appears in the in-character fiction.

The Semmerlak.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Causeway across the Semmerlak was cited as a precedent for eternal-built crossings.

Metal and stone.d: The Archmage of Autumn sent the Architects to three seats. For the Brilliant Star, Izenbra offered two ideas: bespoke tempest-jade ushabti from the Crucible of Fate, adding 3 wains of mithril a season, and the Tower of Shield and Spear to guard the mine. For the Vigilant Swan, Assessor Hedymarr offered swan-shaped construct guardians from the Manse of the Lionsmith, or a House of Fire and Flame expansion adding 4 wains of white granite that would destroy the Seminary of the Swan. For the Pride of Ikka's Tears, Architect Noether proposed the Bastion of the North fortification, which Estavus's heralds could build faster, and a deep shaft adding 5 wains of mithril. These are offers only, and the guild offers lapse after the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: they are blamed for turning the once-beautiful Vigilant Swan into a vast open-cast quarry worked by enslaved Highborn during their occupation of Reikos.

Grendel.t: Izenbra judged the Grendel of the Broken Shore the greatest threat to the Brilliant Star. A landing at Naris could let raiders strike the mine, its mithril caravans or the new skyways.

Highguard.t: Highborn face a hard choice at the Vigilant Swan. They could gain seven swan guardians, one for each virtue, or expand the quarry at the cost of the Seminary of the Swan, which local Highborn already mourn as a reminder of the Druj occupation.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: invasion from Jotun is cited as one of the dangers that make fortifying the Pride of Ikka's Tears worthwhile.

Thule.t: Threats from Thule and a continuing breakdown in relations with the orcs of Otkodov help justify the proposed Bastion of the North. Negotiation with the Thule of the Silver Peaks is suggested as one possible route for mithril caravans.

Urizen.t: Urizen is offered ways to strengthen the Brilliant Star. The Architect of the Crucible could turn the Crucible's ushabti to mining, and the Tower of Shield and Spear, garrisoned by Redoubt's sentinels, could secure the mine's mithril.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Pride of Ikka's Tears could gain a great fortification to rival Kalant and Olgafsdottirshal, with a garrison drawn from Sermersuaq's warriors. A deep shaft could also make it one of the Empire's most lucrative mithril mines.

Metal and stone.o: After the Conclave accepted an offer from the Sovereign Lord of the City of Fire and Stone, heralds of the Architects of Iron and Stone spent a season assessing three Bourse seats. They returned with proposals to improve the Brilliant Star in Redoubt, the Vigilant Swan in Reikos and the Pride of Ikka's Tears in Sermersuaq.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Mentioned in passing: Naris is named as the likely landing point for a Grendel force that might raid the Brilliant Star or its caravans.

Redoubt/Tomari.t: Tomari, home of the Brilliant Star, is the proposed site of the Tower of Shield and Spear. The mine would hold out with the tower's sentinels unless the whole region fell.

Reikos/Riverwatch.t: Riverwatch could be guarded by seven swan constructs that fight only within the region. Its lakes and the Seminary of the Swan would be lost if the quarry were widened.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Mentioned in passing: negotiation with the Thule of the Silver Peaks is suggested as one alternative route for getting mithril out of Sermersuaq.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: Suaq Fount is the proposed site of both the Bastion of the North, a rank two fortification, and the deep shaft that would add 5 wains of mithril a season.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory itself is not discussed, and the link appears to come only from the name of the proposed Bastion of the North fortification in Sermersuaq.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: holding Sermersuaq regions that link to Hahnmark is named as the easiest way to keep mithril flowing from the Pride of Ikka's Tears.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: a continuing breakdown in relations with the orcs of Otkodov is cited as one reason for urgency in fortifying the Sermersuaq mine.

Redoubt.t: The Brilliant Star beneath Tomari could gain mithril-mining ushabti and a sentinel-held tower to protect its output. Izenbra privately admitted that its help there would be limited.

Reikos.t: The Vigilant Swan could gain construct guardians or a major expansion of white granite. The expansion would drain the lakes and destroy the Seminary of the Swan.

Sermersuaq.t: The Pride of Ikka's Tears could be ringed by the Bastion of the North and deepened with a new shaft. Both would boost mithril output and shield the mine from barbarians and monsters.

Tsirku.t: Mentioned in passing: attacks by creatures out of Tsirku are listed among the threats to the Pride of Ikka's Tears.

Zenith.t: The Crucible of Fate in Zenith could switch its bespoke ushabti from supporting Zenith's restoration to working the Brilliant Star, and its koboldi are eager to help design them.

Metamorphosis.d: Orcs evicted from Thornfen by the Axou were starving in Urizeni-held lands. The Empire could spend the Imperial Breadbasket to prevent famine, forgoing its benefits for two seasons and inevitably feeding scattered Druj warriors, or let famine run its course, crippling the Druj but inflaming anti-Imperial feeling. Rebel leaders Halyx Fire-Eyes and Agoska were coming to Anvil to meet the Imperial Consul, wanting self-rule and the Bloodwater Marsh. Agoska's Waterwalkers destroyed the last miasma pillar using a Conclave ritual. Sentinels of Urizen were offered a venture to destroy Kroll's lair, or alternatively to learn its names and ward the lair so Urizen could control it.

Druj.t: Thousands of Druj warriors scattered across the Sarangrave would profit from any Breadbasket food sent there but would be too busy surviving to cause trouble if famine ran its course, and the loss of their last miasma pillar ended their grip on the septs.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: diverting the Imperial Breadbasket to feed the Sarangrave would deny its benefits to the Marchers for two seasons.

Urizen.t: Urizen's new territory faced famine among displaced orcs gathered around its settlements, negotiations that would shape relations with the septs, and a choice for its Sentinels to destroy Kroll's lair or attempt to bind the beast to Urizeni control.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium, which Varushka held, was cited as a place where the Empire's liberation of Druj-ruled septs seemed to work.

Metamorphosis.o: In Autumn 388YE the Sarangrave faced looming famine among orcs expelled from Thornfen, delicate negotiations with the Nesustak rebels, and a threat from the regenerating beast Kroll, even as the last Druj miasma pillar was finally destroyed.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: Bendol remained lost to the vallorn; retaking it would let the Empire grant the Bloodwater Marsh to the rebels while keeping the territory, so a future promise of the Marsh was possible though the timescale was difficult.

Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh.t: Halyx Fire-Eyes of the Bloodwater Spears was expected to demand the Marsh for its former occupants, but ceding it would cost the Empire control of the territory and its senator unless Thornfen or Bendol were also held.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: Kroll was regenerating in its lair and could rampage if the region were attacked or reached by husks, and the Sentinels of Urizen could either destroy its three Spring-fed sacs with 7,500 force strength or divine its names and ward the lair with seven rings of ilium to control it.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: The rebels holding the forest took in exiles who could fight but turned most away for lack of food, and they seemed ready to defend the region to the death, though an Imperial army could take it with minimal losses.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: The Axou's eviction of Thornfen's orcs under their treaty with the Empire caused the famine crisis, and Axos held the region with one army and a huge fortification that would grow harder to take as its garrison resupplied.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the page concerns spending the Imperial Breadbasket, which would stop its benefits to the Marchers for two seasons.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium was cited as a place where liberating septs from the Druj appeared to have worked, in contrast to the Barrens and the Sarangrave.

Sarangrave.t: The territory faced winter famine among the Thornfen exiles, Druj remnants and advancing husks, rebel demands for land and self-rule, and the threat of Kroll, but the destruction of the last miasma pillar began to lift the spirits of all its inhabitants.

Midnight rain.d: After the summer raid on Skallahn opened the Gullet to large numbers of ships, the Senate funded a project to chart the Sea of Snow. Captains from every nation except the Imperial Orcs took part, with roughly two-thirds being from Wintermark. The resulting map was not detailed enough for magicians, but it located the Narkyst territory of Ankashun, the Faraden territories of Menendram and Tujahan, and the Kalsea territories of Bryadvik, Tromsa and Fjorknae. Each fleet earned only modest returns from raiding and petty trade, plus a copy of the map and a gazetteer. Crews reported many kraken and other sea monsters. The findings were published after the Winter Solstice.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: three Dawnish captains, including Lord Romande Remys, are listed among the contributors.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: a single Highborn captain, Matthew, is listed among the contributors.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs were the only Imperial nation with no vessels involved in the project.

Jotun.t: The coasts of Kalsea and Narkyst were charted by Imperial ships, which also raided Jotun settlements, while the Jarls and their warriors drove off any crews who lingered or came ashore.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: two Navarr captains, Antur Longstep and Sylvan Blackleaf, are listed among the contributors.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: three Freeborn captains, including Aldo Russo, are listed among the contributors.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: a single League captain, Erasmo di Tassato, is listed among the contributors.

The Marches.t: Around a dozen Marcher captains sailed with the expedition, the largest contingent after Wintermark, and each received a copy of the map and gazetteer.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: a sailor's tall tale in the in-character story jokes about a Thule dragon riding a Summer dragon.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: two Urizen captains from Netherwatch are listed among the contributors.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk captains made up just over two-thirds of the fleets that mapped the Sea of Snow, braving kraken and hostile Jarls to chart the coast north of their homeland.

Midnight rain.o: Following the Senate's Autumn Equinox vote, a fleet of over seventy Imperial captains, mostly Winterfolk, sailed the Sea of Snow and mapped its coastline, filling gaps in the Empire's knowledge of the Jotun and Faraden lands along its shores.

Bryadvik.t: The name and rough coastline of this Kalsea territory were charted for the first time by the Imperial expedition.

Fjorknae.t: Imperial captains recorded the name and rough coastline of this northern Kalsea territory.

Sea of Snow.t: Seventy or more Imperial fleets sailed these monster-haunted waters to map their shores, and many reported clashes with kraken and other beasts from the depths.

Skallahn.t: The earlier Imperial raids on this southernmost Kalsea territory, especially the damaging summer raid on the Kongegőr, opened the Gullet and made the mapping expedition possible.

Tromsa.t: The name and rough coastline of this Kalsea territory were mapped by the Imperial fleets.

Million miles of water.d: For Eoradal, Skourans from Jadefall offered to supply water through a restored Great Aqueduct for 12 thrones a season, or in exchange for exclusive mining rights in Eoradal, Clisearn and Nadir. They also offered a Healer's Pool. A former Grendel mage, Ila Bared, instead proposed secretly tapping a Skouran lake via the Yellow Fish Adit. For Nadir, the Senate could buy Marcher cattle for a Southern Herd, or an archmage could seek help from Kimus or Ossegrahn. For Icarion, the Freeborn could build a qanat, or the River Doubt in Apstrus could be dammed. Doing both would make Icarion an oasis. Several options lapse after Summer Solstice 387YE.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Ila Bared, who proposes the Adit scheme, is a former Grendel magician-merchant, and the page recalls three Grendel armies broken at Solen's Doubt.

Imperial Orcs.t: The orcs faced choices over how to make Mareave's arid regions liveable, from a Southern Herd with a Shepherd sinecure to a Healer's Pool with an elected Bonesetter. Their Assembly could also send a sept to help the Freeborn in Feroz or Madruga in return for the Freeborn's aid.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun are not named, but farmers from Bregasland, which they held, are listed among those who could drive cattle to Wayford.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn experts, some of whom designed Segura's Iron Qanat, offered to build an Icarion Qanat for little more than token payment. In return, the Imperial Orcs could send a sept to help rebuild Feroz or Madruga.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League's Assembly is named among those that might object to flooding the Fallen Valley, where many who died freeing Spiral are buried.

The Marches.t: Marcher experts from Mitwold and Upwold judged Mareave's land poor. Marcher farmers could be offered cattle-bonds to sell their herds to the Imperial Orcs at the Spring Equinox, and Marcher military units could help escort the drovers south.

Urizen.t: A Urizeni visitor, Severina, proposed damming the River Doubt at the abandoned spire of Solen's Doubt to water Icarion. The Urizeni Assembly is named among those that might object to flooding the Fallen Valley.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka's Assembly is listed among those that might object to flooding the Fallen Valley, where many fallen heroes lie.

Million miles of water.o: Freeborn and Marcher experts, Skouran water-guardians and others offered competing ways to bring water to the arid regions of Mareave, the Imperial Orcs' newly assigned territory. Each scheme came with its own costs, risks and deadlines.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: the lights of Beoraidh are glimpsed in the distance in the opening story.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: Clisearn's eastern hills could be handed to Skouran miners as exclusive mining rights in exchange for water.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: Eoradal could have the Great Aqueduct restored with Skouran water or water tapped secretly through the Yellow Fish Adit, ending its aridity and, once Curstag's Way is complete, supporting a large town. A Healer's Pool could add further taxation.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Icarion could lose its arid quality through a Freeborn qanat or a dam on the Doubt. With both, it would become an oasis adding 6 thrones a season.

Mareave/Nadir.t: Nadir's aridity could be ended by driving a Marcher-bought Southern Herd there or by eternal aid in reaching deep reservoirs, though drakes would threaten the cattle. Its hills could also be given to Skouran miners.

Mareave/Sinfoyard.t: Mentioned in passing: Icarion's mining camps send their ores to the town of Aghnayadh in Sinfoyard.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: The River Doubt near Solen's Doubt in Apstrus is the proposed site for a dam and reservoir to feed Icarion. This would flood the Fallen Valley, resting place of thousands from eight Imperial armies.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Mentioned in passing: Apulus's hills run into Icarion, but the region is too low to supply water economically.

Spiral/Screed.t: Mentioned in passing: the dam work would take place in a troubled site outside Screed itself.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the arid eastern shore of the Bay and the bitter winds blowing in from it are described.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland farmers are named among those who could drive cattle to the Wayford market.

Feroz.t: The Imperial Orc Assembly could mandate a sept to travel to Feroz to help the Freeborn rebuild, instead of exploring Mareave.

Madruga.t: An Imperial Orc sept could be mandated to go to Madruga to help the Freeborn rebuild, repaying the aid given in Mareave.

Mareave.t: Mareave was offered several ways to end the aridity of Eoradal, Nadir and Icarion, including an aqueduct, a cattle herd, a qanat and a dam. Each brought costs, possible tax gains and new political complications with Skoura.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold sent Marcher experts to Mareave, and its Wayford cattle market could gain holding pens for cattle bought under the bond scheme.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold's mining is referenced in the opening story, and its farmers could drive cattle to Stockland.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Segura's Iron Qanat is cited as the model for the proposed Icarion Qanat.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's Great Herd is the model for the proposed Southern Herd, and orcs there might be drawn to settle Mareave.

Spiral.t: The River Doubt in Spiral could be dammed to divert water to Icarion. This would require Towerjacks or a Bound by Common Cause army to work under the Black Plateau's deadly influence, and would flood a mass grave.

Upwold.t: Upwold sent Marcher experts to Mareave, and its Stockland cattle market could take in cattle for sale to the Imperial Orcs under the bond scheme.

Mime each lonely word.d: For a year, pilgrims who walk the Maze alone may emerge with new insight or purpose, though each person only once. Through the Law of Dominion the Guardian gained innate powers, including insight without liao, unique potions, unremovable personal auras and one oracular dream this year. The Thule ambassador Rak confirmed that the Dragon Hinodir of the Bright Orb holds Zoria's Staff of Pure Vision. He offered to sell it for exactly 120 thrones, 4 crowns and 11 rings, for one season only. The Maze's beasts speak in lucid dreams, letting the Guardian catalogue Varushka's sovereigns. Meanwhile the Wolves of Varushka grow more active, creating paid monster-hunting work for Varushkan and Dawnish forces.

Thule.t: Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-Undivided confirmed that the Dragon Hinodir holds Zoria's Staff of Pure Vision and offered it for one season at an exact price. Any payment would be spent within the Empire on food sent north to the Thule.

Varushka.t: Varushka's Guardian gained unusual powers, its pilgrims could be transformed by the Maze, and dreams began to map its great sovereigns. Rising activity among the Wolves of Varushka also brought paid work for schlacta and wardens fighting monsters across the nation.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: some Suaq stories claim Zoria was a daughter of Sermersuaq who practised the lore of the icewalkers.

Mime each lonely word.o: Illya Nikovitch Volkov, Guardian of the Maze of Zoria, consecrated the ancient Maze in Miekarova with True Liao at the Varushkan national assembly's urging, infusing it with the Dagger of the Mind. Pilgrims emerged transformed, the Guardian gained strange powers, and dreams began revealing the sovereigns of Varushka.

Miekarova/Miechernya.t: Mentioned in passing: some of the Maze dreams were idle talk of snowfalls in the mountains of Miechernya.

Volodmartz/Brez.t: Mentioned in passing: some of the Maze dreams were gossip about a wedding in a vale in Brez.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: characters who went to Brocéliande could not also have visited the Maze before the Winter Solstice.

Karov.t: More rusalka were reported in the rivers of Karov as the Wolves of Varushka grew more active.

Karsk.t: More dubik were reported active in the forests of Karsk, adding to the work for monster-hunting forces.

Miekarova.t: The consecrated Maze of Zoria in Miekarova drew growing numbers of pilgrims seeking a personal, transformative experience of Wisdom, an opportunity lasting until the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Ossium.t: More dubik were reported active in the forests of Ossium among the stirring Wolves of Varushka.

Otkodov.t: Legends hold that one of Zoria's relics fell into the hands of the Thule orcs of Otkodov in pre-Imperial times, and the Thule now confirm they hold her staff.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: characters who went to map the Sea of Snow could not also have visited the Maze before the Winter Solstice.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: some Suaq stories say Zoria was a daughter of Sermersuaq.

Volodmartz.t: More rusalka were reported in the rivers of Volodmartz, part of the growing monster threat facing Varushka.

Mirror and the flame.d: The Tribunal appointed Alexius as Ambassador to the Empire, asked the Empire to reciprocate and suggested neither side build an embassy. It announced a fane to Sinokenon that would take at least a year; an Imperial ambassador could try to coerce them to drop it, at diplomatic cost. Through its herald, Sinokenon offered a magnitude 120 ritual stronger than Clarity of the Master Strategist in return for Silver Flame access to Imperial lore, and a ritual adding five ranks to a military unit for a 60-throne Senate offer. It also offered a Circlet of Supreme Authority to Emperor Vesna. Oblivion Sentinel Floria Sunshaper was made responsible for defeating the Grendel and their Asavean companions.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named among those who have invaded Spiral in the past.

Grendel.t: A Grendel company escorting Asaveans carrying shards of Black Plateau glass was trying to reach a ship in Apulus, and Floria Sunshaper was charged with defeating them; the Silver Flame also said they would not trade with the Grendel out of respect for the Empire.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral's assignment to the League is recalled as the cause of the Urizeni rebellion, and the League city of Apulian is noted for its explosive growth since the rebellion was settled.

Urizen.t: The rebels who formed the Tribunal still embody Urizeni culture but have mostly severed their bond with Menos, and their offer of access to Urizeni lore proved impossible because Urizen magically means only the nation within the Empire; Urizen's senators had earlier chosen to receive Silver Flame foci under the peace settlement.

Mirror and the flame.o: In Winter 387YE the Spiral rebels announced they had formed the Tribunal of the Silver Flame under Grand Arbiter Caela, planned a fane to Sinokenon in Cinion, and brought the eternal's offers of war rituals and a gift for the Throne. Separately, a Grendel company escorting Asaveans carrying Black Plateau glass was found trying to leave Spiral through Apulus.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Grendel escorting Asaveans with shards of volcanic glass were heading for a ship in a sheltered cove in Apulus, posing a threat to the Black Plateau that Floria Sunshaper was charged with ending.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Cinion, ruled by the rebels, became the seat of the Tribunal of the Silver Flame, which planned a fane to Sinokenon there that could bring as many heralds into the region as there are Urizeni.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that the Grendel's main focus remains on Redoubt and Mareave.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that the Grendel's main focus remains on Redoubt and Mareave.

Spiral.t: Spiral now contains a self-declared independent Tribunal in Cinion that plans a fane to Sinokenon inside an Imperial territory, while a Grendel and Asavean party threatened to carry Black Plateau glass out of the territory.

Missionary work.d: A Senate motion by Senator Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra of Segura asked the Synod to make missionaries available to anyone in the Iron Confederacy willing to receive them. The Dukes and Suranni citizens gave no formal response. However, a representative of several hundred rebels, mostly escaped human slaves camped in the hills of Kalino, sought out the civil service. They wanted teaching on the Way and auras of Courage and Loyalty to help their struggle. The General Assembly could send a priest with liao to support the rebellion, or one to persuade the rebels to seek sanctuary in the Empire. During the Winter Solstice the Empress intervened, both mandates failed to reach the Greater Majority, and Kalino was left to unfold without Imperial involvement.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: a civil servant tells the rebel envoys that the Empire's nobles will be camping with the Dawnish.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: a group of Imperial Orcs walking by at Anvil frightens one of the rebel envoys.

The Brass Coast.t: A Brass Coast senator from Segura raised the motion that opened this opportunity, and the rebels' camp lies just south of the Brass Coast's border at Feroz, but the Synod's failure to act meant no Imperial help reached them.

Missionary work.o: Escaped human slaves rebelling against the Suranni in Kalino asked the Empire for missionaries to teach them the Way, following a Senate motion offering General Assembly missionaries to the Iron Confederacy. The Synod considered aiding the rebels or offering them sanctuary, but Empress Lisabetta intervened and neither mandate was upheld.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Kalino, where the rebels are camped, is described as lying south of Feroz.

Kalino.t: Several hundred escaped slaves camped in the hills of Kalino sought Imperial missionaries to aid their rebellion against the Suranni, but with both Synod mandates failing, events there continue without Imperial intervention.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the motion offering missionaries to the Iron Confederacy was raised by Senator Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra of Segura.

Mistaken for strangers.d: The Kulsdottir trading house sought invitations to games of chance, and heralds of the Commander in Crimson and Gold came to the Wintermark camp. They offered Blaze Dunning's circle a dialogue, three draughts of a changeling-making liquor to unlineaged contestants judged by High Bard Tarik, and boons for captains who fought beside the Knights of Glory. The Stzena of Tears, leading freed husks north after the Deadwood Knight's fall, sought Dawn and Varushka. Others included the Falconer's diplomats, the Azoth's herald hiring musicians, two Ketsov facing inquisition, Seventh Wave unconquered, merchants from the League and Spiral, and Marracossan exiles. After five Synod judgements, a small Sand Fisher group planned to arrive on the final day.

Dawn.t: The Stzena of Tears, seen leading leftover husks out of Wickmoor, sought Dawnish representatives, and the Falconer's envoys asked to meet a senator in Dawn's glory square. A community supporting Laroc was divided over yeofolk who had left to seek glory.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns fought the Druj in Therunin, and the Sand Fishers are described as former Druj slaves.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard fought the Grendel in Redoubt, the Marracossans recalled defending Trajadoz against the Grendel invasion, and a League merchant sought investors for a trade mission with the North Mareave Trade Consortium.

Highguard.t: A Highborn priest of Prosperity from Reikos came to sell Isazaiya's incense to fund research into Tamarbode's mushrooms. Highborn unconquered of the Seventh Wave invited Anvil's unconquered through a conjunction to their Mournwold camp.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Falconer's two envoys asked to meet a senator in the Imperial Orc fighting pit at 21:00. Generals of the Granite Pillar and Tusks could each nominate a captain to receive a boon from the Lion of Summer's herald Rikkan.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes, Granite Pillar and Tusks fought the Jotun in the Mournwold, and the Seventh Wave's scouts were on the front lines against them.

Navarr.t: The Urizen questor Varinius extended his dreaming opportunity to Navarr dedicants of Wisdom he had met before, and the Black Thorns' general could nominate a captain for Rikkan's boon. The High Roller came to Anvil at the invitation of the Navarr vate The Red Bramble.

The League.t: The League camp expected merchant Dieter D'Apulian seeking investors and, on the final day, the Sand Fishers answering the League Assembly's invitation. Rahuun Amahuz of Spiral returned, and the Marracossan exiles of Trajadoz came to thank the Artisan's Guild.

The Marches.t: The Drakes, who fought the Jotun in the Mournwold beside the Knights of Glory, could nominate a captain for a boon. The Seventh Wave's unconquered opened a conjunction from their camp at West Millston after helping secure Imperial victory in the Marches.

Urizen.t: Varinius, a questor from Eudokia's Spire, offered twelve places for dreaming to Urizen and Navarr Wisdom dedicants he knew, gathering at the Hub because the Urizen tea rooms might be closed. The Citadel Guard's general could nominate a captain for Rikkan's boon.

Varushka.t: The Howling Queen's Stzena of Tears, leading husks north into Varushka, came to discuss the Deadwood Knight's fall and her relationship with Varushka. Two Ketsov from Ossium came to have their kin's Virtue held to account in an inquisition.

Wintermark.t: The Kalpaheim trading house the Kulsdottir sent a representative to settle obligations from the Chocolate Game and seek invitations. Heralds of Eleonaris held their contests in the Wintermark camp, with Scarrow Dawnbreak nominated to greet and escort them.

Mistaken for strangers.o: In Winter 386YE a stream of visitors made for Anvil during the solstice, from heralds of the Lion of Summer and the Howling Queen's envoy to merchants, petitioners and a delegation of Sand Fishers answering the Synod's invitations.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: The Synod praised the Sand Fishers for making a home in Misericorde, discovering and guarding the Flaxen Pillars and repaying a loan for its sawmills, while the Prince of the Misericorde Market invited them to Anvil.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: Mentioned in passing: the Rebeshof Roadwarden was among those inviting the Sand Fishers to Anvil, and had written to Swift Fisher.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: The sale of Isazaiya's incense at Anvil was meant to fund her ongoing research into the mushrooms of Tamarbode.

Astolat.t: A small community supporting Laroc lost several prominent yeofolk to the pursuit of glory, with Helene Fletcher urging their return and Jean Cooper defending their choice.

Holberg.t: The Sand Fishers, living richly in Holberg's marshes and keen not to jeopardise their new lives, nervously agreed to send a small group to Anvil to learn what the Empire wanted of them.

Mareave.t: League merchant Dieter D'Apulian sought investors for a potential trade mission with the North Mareave Trade Consortium, presented as an opportunity rather than an agreed deal.

Mournwold.t: Imperial armies fought the Jotun here alongside the Knights of Glory, and with fighting still ongoing, the Seventh Wave's unconquered opened a conjunction for six visitors to West Millston in the Chalk Downs.

Ossium.t: Two Ketsov, from the Ossian settlement of that name, travelled to Anvil seeking an inquisition into their kin's Virtue, in an encounter involving themes of cannibalism, slavery and violence.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard fought the Grendel and the Children of Wrecks in Redoubt beside the Knights of Glory, making its general eligible to nominate a captain.

Reikos.t: A Highborn priest of Prosperity from Reikos brought three doses of Isazaiya's incense and one experimental dose to sell, raising funds for her research.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marracossan travellers passed through Sarvos, and Dolce and Novella di Sarvos authored two of the Sand Fisher judgements.

Spiral.t: Rahuun Amahuz returned to Anvil to build on the Circle of Black Sand's ambition to become an up-and-coming power in Spiral, seeking progress and further introductions.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns fought the Druj in Therunin alongside the Knights of Glory, making their general eligible to nominate a captain.

Mithril and rope.d: The Summer Storm, Towerjacks, Argent Sword and Wolves of War defended Clisearn alongside Rucraic's Redoubt and Summer-realm heralds from three magical fortresses, while the Rivers of Life healed wounds overnight on both sides. The Storm Sharks led the Grendel assault, and the Black Eels, Bone Nautilus and Hamsin stole the season's 24 wains of Fundindelve mithril. The Argent Sword and Wolves of War intercepted the raiders and recovered much of it. The violet-sailed Katabat, a fifth Grendel navy bearing Urizeni lightstones, and an Asavean flotilla turned the tide. The Grendel now stand three-quarters of the way to taking Clisearn; the Empire lost over a thousand soldiers. Several battle opportunities followed.

Grendel.t: Grendel armies led by the Storm Sharks advanced three-quarters of the way to seizing Clisearn and raided the Fundindelve, and they raised the new Katabat navy with Asavean help, though they may have suffered up to twice the Empire's casualties.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Summer Storm and the garrison of Rucraic's Redoubt fought hard to hold Clisearn but were pushed back. Orcs with resources in Mareave may have gained a boon from Cathan Canae, and the Uthni offered a bounty against the Grendel healer Leagsaidh.

The League.t: The Towerjacks helped contain the Grendel advance while the Wolves of War plundered the enemy and recovered stolen mithril. League citizens were also offered the chance to hire the Ilium Jackals and to release the Spiteri Bequest.

Urizen.t: The Argent Sword marched to Mareave to plunder the Grendel and helped intercept the Fundindelve raiders. Urizeni scouts noted with concern that the Katabat bears Urizeni lightstones and may draw on lore stolen from Redoubt.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushkans acting for the general of the Boyar's Hasta were named as able to hire the Ilium Jackals mercenaries.

Mithril and rope.o: In Summer 388YE the Grendel pressed their invasion of Clisearn in Mareave and, aided by a new navy and Asavean warships, drove the Imperial defenders back until only Iskander's Donjon stopped the region from falling. Grendel raiders also plundered the Fundindelve mithril mine, though much of the loot was recovered.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: The city state of Beoraidh stayed neutral, and its fortification, the Palace of Chains, aided neither side.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: Clisearn was the main battlefield: the Grendel came within a quarter of taking it, held back only by Iskander's Donjon. The Fundindelve was stripped of mithril, though it and the Grand Lodge stayed in Imperial hands, and a battle loomed at the Ruins of Sinat.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: The Summer Storm passed through Eoradal, where they were joined by the orc soldiers of the enchanted bastion Rucraic's Redoubt, whose ranks were swelled by northern Mareave volunteers.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: Grendel navies, including the new Katabat, gathered off the coast of Grendel-held Fleisardh, and the Fundindelve raiders raced to reach its safety.

Mareave/Icarion.t: A Frozen Citadel of white marble and blue ice, garrisoned by pale-eyed elfin warriors of the Summer realm, rose in Icarion.

Mareave/Nadir.t: A Frozen Citadel of ice with six iron minarets, manned by Summer-realm archers, rose over Nadir.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Grendel completed a fifth navy, the violet-sailed Katabat, on the Bay, and the Asavean Plenum sent more warships there to fight the Empire.

Mareave.t: Mareave saw ferocious fighting under the Rivers of Life, and the Grendel drove the defenders back across Clisearn while Beoraidh stayed neutral. The Empire lost over a thousand soldiers, and the Grendel perhaps twice as many.

Redoubt.t: There was concern that the Katabat drew inspiration and power from magical resources stolen from Redoubt during the recent Grendel invasion.

Sarvos.t: A necklace looted when the Grendel sacked Sarvos was located with a Grendel maistir in Mareave, and its return would release the Spiteri Bequest and a trading schooner.

Spiral.t: Imperial armies marched south through Spiral, and a Grendel maistir was recruiting mercenaries to raid the Legacy, which the Custodian of the Legacy was charged to stop.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun withdrew to Zenith along with the Seventh Wave.

Momento mori.d: The creature's attacks escalated from bandits to travellers and then whole villages. The village of Woodbury in Wickmoor was destroyed, and its force was believed to number a hundred or more, possibly reaching several thousand by the Summer Solstice. Its servants sometimes overcame the wards on Varushkan roads. It offered to leave Varushka for Dawn if given 'the crown', and it fought by the rules at House Seerkan's tourney before slaughtering knights in the grand melee. It cannot yet be permanently killed. Ekaterina de Casillon proposed rewarding Dawnish volunteers with golden apples if the Dawnish assembly backed the call to arms. Three warbands threatened Karov and Weirwater, with named Imperial title-holders responsible for defeating each.

Dawn.t: Dawnish villages, knights and weirwood trade in Weirwater suffered, and the National Assembly was asked to amplify the call to arms, with de Casillon golden apples offered to volunteers if a greater majority was reached.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League is not named; the only link is to Spiral Castle, a Dawnish house in Weirwater.

Varushka.t: Varushkan vales and traders were attacked, road wards proved unreliable against the creature's servants, and the Schlacta of Rot demanded 'the crown' in exchange for leaving Varushka to other powers.

Momento mori.o: An undying horror known as the Schlacta of Rot in Karov and the Deadwood Knight in Weirwater failed to return to slumber after its Summer challenge and began a growing rampage along the Dawn–Varushka border, raising those it slew into an unliving warband.

Karov/Duzekani.t: The Iron Helms, Northern Eagle and Quiet Step stationed there partly contained the threat while fighting the Blade of Skies, though Duzekani was named as a vulnerable target.

Karov/Skoremujac.t: Skoremujac was one of the two regions where the Deadwood Knight was concentrating its attacks.

Weirwater/Garthmoor.t: Mentioned in passing: Garthmoor was named as a vulnerable target if the warband kept growing.

Weirwater/Hawksmoor.t: Mentioned in passing: Hawksmoor was named as a vulnerable target if the warband kept growing.

Weirwater/Weirmoor.t: The Broken Errant's warband struck isolated holdings in Weirmoor and gravely wounded Liege Roland de Casillon, and Spiral Castle might raise its mists again; the Castellan of Spiral Castle was responsible for defeating it.

Weirwater/Wickmoor.t: Woodbury was destroyed with nearly a hundred and fifty yeofolk slain or displaced, and the Deadwood Knight's black knights killed several competitors at House Seerkan's tourney before being driven off.

Karov.t: Southern and western Karov faced the Festering Warden on the Westward Road and the Iron Boyar on the road to Korotny, with Kolvy and Korotny both at risk of attack if these warbands were not stopped.

Karsk.t: If the Iron Boyar was not defeated, the benefits the Iron Roads provide to Karsk would be halved for the coming season.

Ossium.t: If the Iron Boyar was not defeated, the benefits the Iron Roads provide to Ossium would be halved for the coming season.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: most knights on the Grand Tour attended events in Semmerholm over the Winter rather than House Seerkan's tourney.

The Semmerlak.t: Wise ones crossed the lake despite the threat of Dho'uala to bring their lore to Anvil, while fear of the lake pushed more travellers onto the threatened land routes, and an unchecked Iron Boyar would raise the Harbourmaster's weirwood costs.

Weirwater.t: Northern Weirwater bore the brunt of the rampage: villages were destroyed, guarding weirwood caravans from the Weirwater Vales grew costlier, and the Vales themselves might eventually be attacked.

Monarchs and outcasts.d: The Prince with a Thousand Foes was outraged that his gifted Protector's Stone was destroyed with Words of Ending. Llofir raised his offer for herbs to fund a Navarr army against the vallorn. The Summer regents granted boons to Dawn's Knight-Protectors. Ephisis offered to buy the Quicksilver's Flame, auctioned a final vault and proposed Counting Houses in Kallavesa, the Barrens or Hercynia. Khobel Tavah held Eilian Sweetwater safe with dangerous 'jetsam'. Sorin, Agramant, Sinokenon, Kimus, Janon, Sadogua and Lashonar also made overtures or complaints. Outcome: the Navarr gave 750 marrowort for 15 mithril towards their fourth army, the Quicksilver's Flame was not sold, and the Counting House proposals were requested.

Dawn.t: Dawn's victory in the Drottningbjotha earned each Knight-Protector a boon from a Summer regent, with Meraud and Adamant's favours granted this season and the others awaiting new elections, while the Barrens was named a Counting House candidate.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel invasion of Redoubt in 387YE is the reason Eilian Sweetwater fled into the Cave of the Drowned, and Sinokenon once warned Tsark of a Grendel raid.

Highguard.t: Elodian of Eleonaris sought out Lucifer, the new General of the Valiant Pegasus and Sychar of Ebon's Hall to learn why Highborn soldiers treated her warband strangely in Mitwold, while Highguard's chapter houses showed little interest in Janon's cursed 'blessings'.

Imperial Orcs.t: Sorin praised the Unshackled, Karrak, Stormsteel Skorr and new Archmage of Winter Bloodcrow Arora, still seeking a declaration giving him the tomb in Eoradal, and summoned Umarth Kannask, Odd Twiceborn and Towlen Nighthaven to have their weaknesses enumerated.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Stephen of Sarcombe was born in Mournwold while it was under Jotun rule, clouding whether he ever swore oaths to the Marches.

Navarr.t: Llofir offered 20 mithril for 1,000 same-type herbs to equip an army sworn to destroy the vallorn; the Navarr gave 750 marrowort via Avery Farkas and received 15 mithril towards their fourth army, and Hercynia was named a Counting House candidate.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Ephisis passed over the thriving League cities as Counting House sites, and Lashonar urged magistrates to begin their theft inquiry with the League's Guild of Ash and Embers.

The Marches.t: The Prince with a Thousand Foes dared anyone to cast Forge the Wooden Fastness in Alderly again, and the Lictors found no evidence that Stephen of Sarcombe was ever oathbound to the Marches, though a Reckoner would meet the Sun Chamber.

Urizen.t: Ephisis offered to buy the Quicksilver's Flame in Morrow (the sale did not happen), Kimus summoned Volidus over a Delving coven studying Cold Sun, and Leviathan withdrew its interest in Clytemnestra's Sword of Damakhan.

Varushka.t: Agramant offered any Varushkan who sent a bloodied handprint with Tribute to the Thrice Cursed Court a twig talisman to contact him, and Sadogua blamed a Varushkan named Vaclav for the Synod judgement calling him Dumon the Liar.

Wintermark.t: Callidus sent secretaries to empower Wintermark's maggots, the enmity-bound Whisper Gallery illegally offered crystal fire for Steinr poetry, and Kallavesa was named the top Counting House candidate.

Monarchs and outcasts.o: In Spring 388YE a host of eternals reached out to the Empire with offers, boons, complaints and warnings, from Llofir's mycelium-for-herbs deal with the Navarr to Ephisis' bids to buy the Quicksilver's Flame and build Counting Houses.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: Sorin hoped the new Archmage of Winter would ease a declaration offering him the contents of the tomb of Alicia-who-knew-the-path in Eoradal in exchange for a great boon.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: The Prince with a Thousand Foes dared the Empire to cast Forge the Wooden Fastness in Alderly again, implying the ritual there may be unreliable until he is placated.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Meraud proposed loosing three giants into Astolat's forests to test the yeofolk, an idea abandoned when the Summer regents settled on individual boons.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia was the third of three territories Ephisis judged would benefit from a Counting House boosting trade and taxation, and the Conclave accepted the offer to draw up proposals.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg was listed among the thriving League cities Ephisis passed over for a Counting House.

Kallavesa.t: Ephisis judged Kallavesa the territory that would benefit most from a Counting House, which would need at least thirty wains and be ceded to the City; the Conclave accepted the offer to draw up proposals.

Mareave.t: Sorin still sought a declaration granting him the contents of the tomb of Alicia-who-knew-the-path in Mareave, a bargain he felt events there this season made more useful.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Elodian's hammersmiths fought alongside the Green Shields and the Valiant Pegasus in Mitwold, where she felt the Highborn treated her strangely.

Morrow.t: Ephisis offered 80 wains of white granite and 240 crowns to dismantle and remove the Quicksilver's Flame in Morrow, but the fortification was not sold.

Mournwold.t: Stephen of Sarcombe was born in Mournwold under Jotun rule, complicating the Lictors' search for oaths to the Marches, and Shacklebreaker's anger threatened Forge the Wooden Fastness in Alderly.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not named; its only connection is Agramant's boon to Varushkan citizens generally.

Redoubt.t: Eilian Sweetwater vanished at Nikephoros during the Grendel invasion of Redoubt and is held by Khobel Tavah in the Cave of the Drowned, while a Delving coven worked with Kimus to study Cold Sun at Terminus Sol.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos was listed among the thriving League cities Ephisis passed over for a Counting House.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is not named on the page; at most it is covered by the general note that Ephisis excluded war-torn territories from its Counting House plans.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato was listed among the thriving League cities Ephisis passed over for a Counting House.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar was listed among the thriving League cities Ephisis passed over for a Counting House.

The Barrens.t: Ephisis named the Barrens the second of three territories that would benefit from a Counting House where trade is scarce, and the Conclave accepted the offer to draw up proposals.

More love, less paperwork.d: La Volpe, Master of the Butchers Bank of Temeschwar, funded the Blood Red Roads, the Colossus of Sarvos and three blood-red places of pilgrimage in Temeschwar, Sarvos and Tassato. The General Assembly passed a mandate sending Jonah Yakovitch with 25 liao, so the faithful helped finish the roads' first leg just before the Winter Solstice 381YE rather than at Spring 382YE. A planned second phase would link Meade, Kalpaheim, Seren, Delev and Siroc. Irada von Temechwar's League Assembly mandate to recognise the monuments as inspiring all virtues, which would also have opened a similar great work in Holberg, was not upheld. The Druj destruction of The Gate in Semmerholm left one leg of the roads exposed. Astrid von Tassato consecrated the Colossus after Spring 383YE.

Dawn.t: The Druj invasion of Semmerholm and the destruction of The Gate put the Blood Red Roads through Dawnish land at risk. Losing Estmure could reduce the economic benefits the roads bring to Semmerholm.

Druj.t: The Druj invasion of Semmerholm and their destruction of The Gate were the one obstacle the roadbuilders could not overcome. Conquering Estmure would cut Holberg off from the rest of the Empire.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Seren in Miaren is named as one of the cities La Volpe plans to connect in the roads' second phase.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Siroc in Madruga is named as one of the cities La Volpe plans to connect in the roads' second phase.

The League.t: La Volpe's roads, Colossus and blood-red monuments shaped all four League cities, and the General Assembly hastened the roads' completion. The League Assembly failed to uphold the mandate recognising the monuments as inspiring every virtue, though the Colossus was later consecrated by Astrid von Tassato.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Meade in Mitwold is named as one of the cities La Volpe plans to connect in the roads' second phase.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Delev in Karov is named as one of the cities La Volpe plans to connect in the roads' second phase.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim in Hahnmark is named as one of the cities La Volpe plans to connect in the roads' second phase.

More love, less paperwork.o: The great building works of Merchant-prince Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar across the League created Synod opportunities to hasten the Blood Red Roads, to recognise his monuments as broadly inspirational, and to consecrate the Colossus of Sarvos. The General Assembly sped up the roads, the League Assembly mandate failed, and the Colossus was consecrated after the Spring Equinox 383YE.

Semmerholm/Estmure.t: Estmure became the key to the roads' Holberg leg: a Druj conquest here would cut Holberg off from the Empire and from the roads' benefits.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: its city of Kalpaheim is a proposed destination for the second phase of the Blood Red Roads.

Holberg.t: The roads reached Holberg through The Gate, now destroyed by the Druj, so a Druj conquest of Estmure would cut Holberg off from their benefits. A blood-red great work offered there depended on the League Assembly mandate, which failed.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: its city of Delev is a proposed destination for the second phase of the Blood Red Roads.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: its city of Siroc is a proposed destination for the second phase of the Blood Red Roads.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: its city of Seren is a proposed destination for the second phase of the Blood Red Roads.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: its city of Meade is a proposed destination for the second phase of the Blood Red Roads.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos is home to the Colossus and the Blood Red Quays art gallery, and Astrid von Tassato consecrated the Colossus after Spring 383YE. Consecration was said to raise the coin the Colossus gives Sarvos businesses from 900 to 1350 rings a season.

Semmerholm.t: The Druj invaded Semmerholm and destroyed The Gate on the road to Holberg, leaving that leg of the Blood Red Roads precarious. It also threatened the economic benefits the roads bring to the territory.

Tassato.t: Tassato's Blood Red River museum was among the monuments the failed League mandate would have made inspirational regardless of virtue. Astrid von Tassato later consecrated the Colossus.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar is home to La Volpe, the Butchers Bank and the Bloody Great Theatre, the origin of the building works that are reshaping the League.

More work.d: Statements of principle passed by the Assembly of the Nine with a greater majority now carry as much weight as national assembly statements, but with wider reach. Several further changes were proposed but not enacted. Vibia of Fossegrimm Spire suggested escalating virtue assembly statements to the Nine. The Senate could restore cardinals as voting senators, which would abolish the Conscience of the Senate. Abigail of Forestgard proposed eight cardinal palaces in Bastion. Bishop Jago and Teodora Bezavina suggested ending protection from repeated revocation, or barring revoked citizens from the same title for a year. Bonewall Col's statement on virtuous ancestors produced no clear effect.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Abigail of Forestgard proposed eight cathedral-palaces for the cardinals ringing Bastion, which would cement the White City as the global heart of the Way if the Senate commissioned them.

Imperial Orcs.t: Bonewall Col's statement on recognising virtuous ancestors met a mixed and uneasy response among orc congregations. Many feared it would create an orc-only category of inspiration, but Severin's sermon stopped it from causing wider conflict or a clear effect.

The League.t: League figures led the debate. Severin von Holberg's encyclical started it, Bishop Orlando di Holberg argued that the national assemblies had grown at the Synod's expense, and Bishop Jago di Temeschwar proposed strengthening revocation, which a League prince privately criticised.

Urizen.t: Vibia of Fossegrimm Spire proposed that the Senate escalate virtue assembly statements to the Assembly of the Nine. Architects from the School of Epistemology helped draw up plans for the proposed cardinal palaces.

Varushka.t: The constitutional scholar Teodora Bezavina of Delev worked with Bishop Jago on the revocation proposals. She persuaded him to soften a permanent ban on reappointment to a one-year ban.

More work.o: Following Severin von Holberg's encyclical stressing that the Seven Virtues unite the Empire, scholars and priests put forward several proposals to strengthen the cardinals and the Synod's power of revocation. Severin's sermon also stifled religious conflict, leaving some statements of principle without effect.

Casinea/Woodwych.t: Forestgard, an old chapter in Woodwych, is home to Abigail, who proposed building palaces for the cardinals in Bastion.

Bastion.t: Bastion was proposed as the site of eight cardinal palaces ringed around the White City with parks and monuments. The commission would cost 120 white granite, 40 weirwood and 320 crowns and take six months to build.

Casinea.t: The palace proposal came from Abigail of Forestgard, a dedicate of Pride from an old chapter in Casinea who had studied the Houses of Virtue in Timoj.

Holberg.t: Holberg is home to Severin von Holberg, whose encyclical prompted the debate, and to Bishop Orlando di Holberg of the University of Holberg. Holberg engineers also helped plan the proposed palaces.

Karov.t: Karov is home to Teodora Bezavina of Delev, the constitutional scholar who co-authored the proposals to strengthen the Synod's power of revocation.

Morrow.t: Vibia of Fossegrimm Spire in Morrow proposed the compromise of escalating greater-majority virtue assembly statements to the Assembly of the Nine, which the Constitutional Court judged constitutional in principle.

Skarsind.t: Bonewall Col's statement on virtuous ancestors was distributed among Skarsind's congregations. It drew a mixed and largely disapproving response and created no clear effect.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is not named on the page; its only apparent link is the opening vignette of a League prince walking a riverbank and criticising Bishop Jago.

Temeschwar.t: Bishop Jago Heshel di Temeschwar of the Church of the Golden Orator proposed ending the protection from repeated revocation, or barring revoked citizens from their title for a year.

Mosaic.d: More than eighty Imperial warbands and twice that many fleets joined the Sumaah and Commonwealth at Xeier before striking Chalonsio, a rich slaving and shipbuilding city in the satrapy of Chanteolleth. The harbour and defences fell quickly. Raiders broke the slave markets of the Chain District and freed captives, assaulted the Grand Temple during a convocation of the God of Chains' priesthood and slew its leaders, then besieged the Sapphire Keep. They executed Patrio Sebastian Ceruleo, looted the vaults and fired the palace, docks and shipyards. The Asavean slave trade is crippled for years. Participants gained crowns, materials, herbs and mithril. Recovered intelligence on the slaving fleet of the Noble Lady of the Sea creates an opportunity to strike its stronghold.

Dawn.t: Dawnish nobles and their forces, including Destan Weaver of house DeRondell and Solene d'Alba, sailed with the armada and shared in the spoils of Chalonsio.

Highguard.t: A sizeable Highborn contingent, among them Caleb of the Cenotaph and Lazarus of the Necropolis, fought in the raid. Their units and fleets claimed a share of the plunder and the chance of a righteous epiphany.

Imperial Orcs.t: Dozens of orc citizens' units took part, including many of the Irontide and Bloodcrow. Rather than an epiphany, orcs who fought may have heard an ancestor urging them to kill the slavers and the priests of the God of Chains, and may go on hearing that voice clearly.

Navarr.t: A large number of Navarr citizens sent their warbands and fleets with the Liberty Pact armada and gained a share of the treasure, herbs and mithril taken from the city.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn sent by far the largest contingent of named participants to the raid. Their fleets and units shared in the wealth seized from the Chain District, the temple and the Ceruleo vaults.

The League.t: League citizens from Holberg, Tassato, Catazar, Sarvos and Temeschwar joined the raid, and their forces shared in the plunder of Chalonsio.

The Marches.t: Only two Marcher citizens, Tomothy Crowle and William Delerougemont, are listed as supporting the raid. Their forces shared in the rewards.

Urizen.t: Urizeni citizens, including Laurentius Julianus Netherwatch and Romulus of the Scarlet Guard, committed their forces to the raid and shared its spoils.

Varushka.t: Varushkan citizens such as Vuk the Wolfeater and Yulia Kasimirova Voronov sent forces to Chalonsio and received a share of the plunder.

Wintermark.t: A small Wintermark contingent, including Leif Arnbjorn and Sven Cuttler, took part in the raid and shared in its rewards.

Mosaic.o: In Autumn 384YE the Liberty Pact armada of Sumaah, Imperial and Commonwealth ships sailed from Xeier and sacked the Asavean city of Chalonsio. The raiders freed slaves, destroyed the priesthood of the God of Chains and burned the Ceruleo family's Sapphire Keep.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: one Highborn participant in the raid is named Lazarus of the Necropolis.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: several League participants in the raid bear the Temeschwar name, such as Danica Lidija van Temeschwar.
