Moving mountains is no easy task.d: Highborn benefactors proposed the Cinderpath Exchange so that Highborn white granite could be sold at a virtuous price rather than auctioned at Anvil. The Senate rejected it twice, partly on misleading Civil Service information, but the Prosperity Assembly and Bartimaeus declared it virtuous. Similar grievances about Bourse resources surfaced in other nations, though League, Freeborn and some other traders defended the auction. At the Winter Solstice three mandates were upheld, one with a Greater Majority. The General Assembly sent Bartimaeus to urge citizens to strengthen their nations. Raziel of the Shattered Tower urged the Highborn, and Edna of the Chantry urged the prosperous, to shun the Public Auction until the Exchange is built.

Highguard.t: Highborn holding white granite were urged by Raziel of the Shattered Tower to refuse the Bourse auction at Anvil until the Cinderpath Exchange is built, reflecting their national scepticism of the 'invisible hand' of the market.

Navarr.t: Some Navarr brokers resent that only one of the three great weirwood forests in their lands is in Navarr hands, though other Navarr traders are content with their auction profits.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the nations, 'from Wintermark to Urizen', where traders question sending Bourse resources to Anvil.

Varushka.t: Varushkan merchant families nurse a centuries-old jealousy that some Bourse seats in Varushka are not in Varushkan hands, while some Varushkan mine owners are happy with their auction profits; Varushka's white granite is noted as the Empire's finest.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the nations, 'from Wintermark to Urizen', where traders question sending Bourse resources to Anvil.

Moving mountains is no easy task.o: Senate's refusal to build the Cinderpath Exchange, a proposed white granite market in Mareholm, prompted the Synod to back it, and at the Winter Solstice 382YE three mandates were upheld urging citizens to withhold Bourse resources from the Public Auction at Anvil.

Casinea/Mareholm.t: The hills of Mareholm were the proposed site of the Cinderpath Exchange, which the Senate has twice declined to build despite the Synod's support.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed palaces of the cardinals in Bastion are listed among the building projects driving demand for white granite.

Casinea.t: Casinea's quarries and mines are one of Highguard's steady sources of white granite, and the territory was the intended home of the Cinderpath Exchange.

Reikos.t: Reikos's quarries and mines produce a steady stream of the white granite that Highborn are now urged to withhold from the Anvil auction.

Mud, blood, and manacles.d: Strong Reeds sympathisers struck Jotun positions as the Empire attacked. The Jotun were caught preparing a cautious foray into Gravenmarch and lost Sallow and the Rushes. Would-be Jarl Kiergmunt was found dead in the eel ponds. The Burning Falcon broke the Jotun at Sallow Walk at heavy cost. A flanking raid by the Bounders, Strong Reeds and Sparrow's Reckoning took Ottery after Jorgen Hylasson was wounded. Ottermire fell, and the Empire got seven-tenths of the way to claiming North Fens. Thousands died, mostly Imperials. The Lictors' curse limits Jotun armies to moving one territory. Battle opportunities offered a chance to kill Friar Bloughton of House Brawness, approach the Raven Jarl about Stephen of Sarcombe, and consult Ghodi Torvi about the coral husks.

Dawn.t: The Golden Sun joined the advance into Bregasland, and at Ottery enchanted Jotun warbands sought out the knights of Dawn, breaking many Dawnish shields.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes only that the Knights of Glory influence first showed itself during recent fighting in the Sarangrave.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Autumn Hammers fought alongside contracted Lictors of the City of Bar and Bond and cursed every Jotun army in Bregasland, so none can move more than one territory after the Equinox.

Jotun.t: The Jotun lost Sallow, the Rushes and Ottermire, and with them Bregasland, suffering heavy defeats at Sallow Walk and Ottery. Their remaining armies are bound by the Lictors' curse and fall back on Fisher's Rock.

The League.t: The untested Sparrow's Reckoning used its bravos' skill at street fighting to help storm Ottery from the east, and a League crossbowman helped seize an archer tower.

The Marches.t: The Strong Reeds, Tusks and Bounders led the liberation of Bregasland, which is Imperial again and due to be assigned by Senate motion. Marchers who fought or hold resources there may gain hearth magic benefits, while House Brawness's treachery remains to be dealt with.

Wintermark.t: The Bloodcloaks, Green Shield and Narwhal's Spear fought in the campaign, with the Bloodcloaks running field hospitals in Ottery. Under the Knights of Glory's influence, the Green Shield cannot take cautious orders for a year.

Mud, blood, and manacles.o: In Autumn 388YE twelve Imperial armies, led by the Strong Reeds, retook the Rushes and Ottermire from the Jotun, making Bregasland an Imperial territory once more. Meanwhile the Autumn Hammers and the Lictors cursed every Jotun army in the territory.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: The Jotun had planned a cautious foray to retake Gravenmarch, but the Imperial assault overwhelmed them. Graven Rock's Spring magic still ripples outward from here.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: The Grey Walkers drive out humans and orcs alike and are one-tenth of the way to claiming the region. No Jotun army would retreat into it.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: The Empire is seven-tenths of the way to claiming North Fens, where the Jotun hold Fisher's Rock. Friar Bloughton of House Brawness can be stopped at the Whelksquay before he leads rebels west.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: The Empire won the Battle of Ottery after its townsfolk rose to help, and the Bloodcloaks set up field hospitals. Ottermire is Imperial again.

Bregasland/The Rushes.t: The Strong Reeds rose here, Sallow and the Rushes fell quickly to the Empire, and would-be Jarl Kiergmunt and his household were found cut down in the eel ponds.

Bregasland.t: The Empire took the Rushes and Ottermire and, holding Gravenmarch, regained the territory, though North Fens and Grey Fens remain contested. Spring magic from Graven Rock continues to heal those who use its waters.

Hordalant.t: Hordalant is one of only two places the cursed Jotun armies can retreat to, and it is where House Brawness plans to flee with Jotun help.

Liathaven.t: The Tower of the North brought lumber from Liathaven to fortify Ottery, and Liathaven is the other limit of the cursed Jotun armies' retreat.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun withdrew from Mitwold the previous season, and the Odd's Way runs east from Ottermire into it.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Sallow's Walk leads toward the Mournwold, the Valiant Pegasus's crusade began there, and Stephen of Sarcombe hails from it.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian armies had headed south toward their home in Reinos, beset by the Iron Confederacy.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: recent fighting in the Sarangrave was where the Knights of Glory influence first manifested.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: an earlier Imperial attack on Skallahn drew Jotun attention away, and coral husks have come ashore there.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sparrow's Reckoning's general addressed the bravos of Tassato in his orders.

Murder of Crows.d: Cynerik's judgement called for Yulia to be interred in Kallavesa's Sovevann marshes. She had backed the Thule alliance that freed Sermersuaq, and Varushka revoked her for it. No one not of the Mark had ever been interred there, and the marsh-keepers urged caution. The alternatives were to write her in the Chronicle of Heroism, adopt her into Wintermark, or seek recognition of her as an exemplar. Dogri, already chronicled, could be made an exemplar, given a tomb, or honoured with a Crows Ridge memorial that would spark an uprising against the Thule. Ingrid Seiging's judgement raised the option of a mandate to drop "fight with honour" and wage ruthless war on the Jotun.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Dogri Thulebane is said to have died fighting the Grendel in service to the Empire.

Imperial Orcs.t: Dogri's legend grew from his refusal to leave Crows Ridge when the Empire gave Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs in 379YE. Making him an exemplar would ensure that no Wintermark land could again be given away without a fight.

Jotun.t: Wintermark could abandon its honourable way of fighting the Jotun and refuse to let them recover their wounded, killing as many as possible. Doing so would throw away any rapport that restraint had built.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr are cited as having seized every opportunity to slaughter the Jotun, which may have hindered any rapprochement.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jarl of Kierheim has said the war cannot end while Jotun who bear the shame of their failure in Mournwold still live.

Thule.t: The Thule alliance that freed Sermersuaq lies at the heart of Yulia's story. A Wintermark memorial to Dogri in Crows Ridge would provoke uprisings against Thule-held land, shattering relations and risking war or demands for reparations.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Yulia was mortally wounded on the battlefields of Zenith before dying on the Throne in Anvil.

Varushka.t: Yulia, a Varushkan senator, was revoked and shunned by her own Assembly for supporting Wintermark. Mystics warned that honouring her in the Chronicle of Heroism would bring good fortune unlikely to please the Varushkans.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark Assembly faced compatible choices on honouring Yulia and Dogri, including an unprecedented interment in the Sovevann and a provocative memorial at Crows Ridge. It also had to decide whether to end its honourable conduct of war against the Jotun.

Murder of Crows.o: After three Wintermark Assembly judgements at the Spring Equinox 385YE, the Assembly was offered choices on how to honour the Varushkan senator Yulia Kasimirova Voronov and the rebel thane Dogri Thulebane. It could also decide whether Wintermark should abandon its policy of fighting the Jotun with honour.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: If Wintermark consecrated a memorial to Dogri in Crows Ridge, inspired young Wintermarkers would attack the fortified Silver Peaks. The attack would fail without strong support and would sour relations with the Thule.

Kallavesa.t: The Sovevann marshes could receive Yulia's body, a step never before taken for anyone not of the Mark, with uncertain effects on the spirits there. A virtue assembly could also raise an inspirational tomb to Dogri there, drawing pilgrims from across the Empire.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: Yulia had been senator for Miekarova, and the judgement says she sacrificed her homeland to help Wintermark reclaim Sermersuaq.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun failure in Mournwold is cited as a reason the Jarl of Kierheim says the war cannot end.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov, Yevgeni Katzev, spoke in support of the Thule alliance and later faced Varushkan censure.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq was freed from Jotun rule by the Thule alliance Yulia championed. A Dogri memorial would send Wintermark insurgents against the Thule-held Silver Peaks.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: it is not named directly, and is touched only through the wider Wintermark–Jotun war the page discusses.

Skarsind.t: Dogri defied the Senate's gift of Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs by holding Crows Ridge, now in Thule hands. A Wintermark memorial there would spark an uprising against its fortifications that would fail without Imperial armies or many military units.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Yulia was mortally wounded on the battlefields of Zenith.

Mushroom, mushroom, mushroom.d: Llofir accepted neutrality as a compromise but refused any favours to the nations it blames for destroying its Tamarbode garden. Its heralds sought a Navarr-only meeting through Advisor on the Vallorn Seren Embercast. They offered scouring support for a new army in Miaren and up to 15 wains of mithril-equivalent equipment in exchange for 1,000 herbs. They also proposed Llofir's Paludarium in Greenfalls. Llofir urged casting Hallow of the Green World on the Druj through conjoined conjunctions to Eastring, where Druj ghulai sought to rile the vallorn, although an interdiction made this illegal. The Paludarium was not built and Hallow was not cast. Regrow the Land's Heart enhanced with Llofir's power was cast on Hahnmark and Ossium.

Druj.t: Llofir judged the Druj to be in decline and proposed Hallow of the Green World in Therunin to bring sickness and ruin upon them, while Druj ghulai at Eastring tried to rile the vallorn further. The ritual was never cast on them.

Highguard.t: Llofir still blames Highguard for destroying its Tamarbode garden and offered it no favours or assistance. Casting Regrow the Land's Heart with Llofir's power on a Highborn territory would invite vengeance, but might also ease the eternal's anger.

Navarr.t: The Navarr were singled out for Llofir's aid. It offered scouring support and mycelial arms for a new army in Miaren and proposed a garden in Greenfalls. In Summer 388YE the Senate commissioned that army with Llofir's help.

The League.t: Llofir counts the League among those responsible for its garden's destruction, denies it any aid, and openly welcomes anyone willing to bring it to account.

Urizen.t: Llofir continues to hold Urizen to account for the Tamarbode garden and refuses it favours. It warned that Regrow the Land's Heart cast with its power on an Urizen territory would provoke vengeance, though this might also repair relations.

Varushka.t: Ossium received Regrow the Land's Heart infused with Llofir's power, so its farms and herb gardens yielded magical mushrooms for the following season.

Wintermark.t: Hahnmark received Regrow the Land's Heart infused with Llofir's power, so its farms and herb gardens yielded magical mushrooms for the following season.

Mushroom, mushroom, mushroom.o: After the Conclave declared neutrality with Llofir in Winter 387YE, the Spring eternal offered the Navarr help against the vallorn, proposed a new garden in Greenfalls and a plan to hasten the Druj's collapse, and extended new whisperspore boons. It continued to nurse a grudge against Highguard, the League and Urizen.

Miaren/Greenfalls.t: Llofir chose Greenfalls for a new garden, Llofir's Paludarium, which would have consumed the region and its Navarr ruins. It was never commissioned.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Llofir's former garden at Tamarbode was destroyed, and that loss is the root of the eternal's lingering grudge.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Conjoined conjunctions opened to Greensward Lea in Eastring, where Druj ghulai sought to rile the vallorn. Securing the site would have allowed a ritual team to cast Hallow of the Green World.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: Had Hallow of the Green World been cast, this region would have lost its poisoned quality and gained the Mycelial quality. The ritual was not performed.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Had Hallow of the Green World been cast, Peakedge Song would have become forested as Llofir swept away its ruins. The ritual was not performed.

Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley.t: Had Hallow of the Green World been cast, the Upper Tarn Valley would have become forested as Llofir swept away its ruins. The ritual was not performed.

Brocéliande.t: Heralds of Llofir appeared here after the Autumn Equinox to talk with Navarr magicians and vates about the war against the vallorn.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Had Hallow of the Green World been cast on the Druj, its effects would have concentrated here and freed Spring eternals to act. The ritual was not performed.

Hahnmark.t: Regrow the Land's Heart was cast here with Llofir's power, so its farms and herb gardens produced magical mushrooms for the following season.

Hercynia.t: Heralds of Llofir visited Hercynia to speak with Navarr magicians and vates about aiding the fight against the vallorn.

Miaren.t: Llofir offered to support the new Navarr army raised in Miaren if it was dedicated to destroying the vallorn. It also proposed a garden at Greenfalls, which was never commissioned.

Ossium.t: Regrow the Land's Heart was cast here with Llofir's power, so its farms and herb gardens produced magical mushrooms for the following season.

Reikos.t: Llofir's original garden here was destroyed, the source of its grudge against Highguard, the League and Urizen. The eternal's earlier scouring of Reikos had erased Druj scars along with much Highborn history.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: This was one of the Druj territories where Hallow of the Green World would have concentrated and freed Spring eternals to act, but the ritual was not cast.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: its vallorn heart is one of only two not yet linked to the trod network in the Navarr plan to render the vallorn mortal.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: it lies dangerously close to the proposed garden site at Greenfalls, though Llofir believed it could repel any attack.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: it lies dangerously close to the proposed garden site at Greenfalls, though Llofir believed it could repel any attack.

Therunin.t: Druj ghulai sought to rile the vallorn here, threatening further expansion, and the territory was the proposed casting site for Hallow of the Green World. That ritual would have weakened the vallorn and transformed the land, but it was not cast.

Music of a distant drum.d: Angered that Liberty Pact tariffs were imposed without consultation, the Thule of Otkodov imposed their own and stopped Imperial harvesting of ambergelt and mana crystals in Krevsaty. Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-Undivided and Grand Warlock Fljajokull planned a delegation to the Senate to discuss tariffs and the ransom of nearly three thousand Imperial slaves, likely payable in weirwood, mithril and white granite. Snowstorm Henk's research expedition was detained in Otkodov near disputed Sungold Pass. The Great Forest Orcs proposed a weirwood embassy at Peakedge Stead. The Tsark spy network was discovered and is being dismantled. A Jotun delegation sought Wintermark's mediators, relations with the Mournwold thralls stagnated, and the Grendel took nearly half of Feroz.

Druj.t: Thule warbands in Ossium were rumoured to be taking captured Druj soldiers north into the Bonewood, and the Druj sent a grim new message shortly before the Equinox after Urizen rebuffed their peace overture.

Grendel.t: The Grendel armada conquered nearly half of Feroz while their pirates kept harassing Imperial merchant shipping, even as Imperial captains raided Beoraidh.

Highguard.t: The Great Forest Orcs, who value friends made in Reikos, said they would much prefer a Highborn or Navarr Ambassador to the Great Forest if the embassy were built.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orc scholar Snowstorm Henk was detained by the Thule in Sküld, Bloodcrow Losak's statement urging outreach to the Mournwold thralls failed badly, and a Jotun delegation asked to observe the Imperial Orcs' Night of Worth.

Jotun.t: A delegation from Jarl Haska Whitemane, led by Arne Emblasbarn and Val Longarm, was coming to Anvil to discuss the destruction of the Meeting Place with Wintermark, while a third Jotun force moved into Liathaven.

Navarr.t: The Great Forest Orcs proposed a weirwood embassy at Peakedge Stead, preferring a Navarr or Highborn ambassador. Work began on the Holt of the Oak, and a Navarr magistrate was allowed to visit the detained Imperial scholars.

The Brass Coast.t: The Grendel armada conquered nearly half of Feroz, and the Empire continued to fight the Jotun in Segura.

The Marches.t: Mournwold Marchers stayed on relatively cordial terms with the former Jotun thralls, but tensions grew as the orcs spread further afield, stoked by agitator Bill Tavistock of Whittle.

Thule.t: Otkodov answered Imperial sanctions with tariffs of its own, closed Krevsaty's resources to Imperial harvesters, detained an Imperial expedition, kept its claim to Sungold Pass and sent a formal delegation to negotiate slave ransoms and tariffs.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen had soundly rebuffed the Druj's earlier peace overture.

Varushka.t: Varushkan Yevgeni Katzev served as ambassador to Otkodov, Sungold Pass in eastern Varushka stayed contested, and the Varushkans were due to choose the Gift of the Dwindling Star seat, whose ilium the Thule could withdraw.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's mediators were sought by a Jotun delegation that wanted to discuss the destruction of the Meeting Place with Wintermark rather than with the Empire.

Music of a distant drum.o: Relations with the Thule of Otkodov soured after the Empire imposed Liberty Pact sanctions without warning, and a Thule delegation was announced for the Spring Equinox. The page also gave diplomatic updates on the Great Forest Orcs, the Mournwold thralls, the Jotun, Tsark, the Grendel and the Druj.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: Imperial harvesting of ambergelt from the Krevsaty Yelta and mana crystals from the Proritsatel Oloy was halted by the Thule, who had also begun a fortification in the hills.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Imperial ship captains completed a daring raid on Beoraidh.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: Matriarch Hamma the Lame, a respected thrall elder considered exceptionally wise, owns the Eversweet Orchard here and could be contacted by Winged Messenger.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: Bill Tavistock of Whittle, an outspoken opponent of the former thralls, could be contacted here.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Hap the Soft, who takes in orc and human orphans and trains them as shepherds, lives at Golden Hoof Farm here.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Timber merchant Sigdór, thought to be an expert on the thrall religion, lives at Sigdór's Stead here.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Ritual magician Casta the Black, one of the thralls' respected figures, lives at the Circle of the Steel King here.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: The Thule used the Bonewood as their base for aiding the Empire and were rumoured to be dragging captured Druj soldiers into its depths.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Snowstorm Henk and four companions were held in the Thule camp at Sküld, unharmed but not released.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: Mentioned in passing: Crow's Keep's watchtowers and garrisons overlook the passes into Urdur.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Mentioned in passing: Crow's Keep's watchtowers overlook the passes into the Silver Peaks.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: Mentioned in passing: noted as the primary home of the Great Forest Orcs.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: The Great Forest Orcs proposed an embassy at Peakedge Stead, built entirely of weirwood with their help, which would require a Senate motion.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Empire and the Grendel remained locked in a struggle for the bay, with pirates still harrying Imperial vessels and a proposal raised to take the fight to them.

Feroz.t: The Grendel armada conquered nearly half of Feroz.

Karsk.t: The Thule tightened border controls in Krevsaty, ended Imperial access to its ambergelt and mana crystals, and began building a fortification in its hills.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: a third force of western orcs was noted as having moved into Liathaven.

Mareave.t: Imperial ship captains completed a daring raid on Beoraidh, and the success raised Imperial morale.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: named with Skarsind as a place where ransomed Imperial slaves would be delivered.

Mountains of the Moon.t: The people of Tsark discovered the Imperial spy network and were systematically breaking up its caches and camps, with the network due to be fully dismantled by the Summer Solstice.

Mournwold.t: The former Jotun thralls lived relatively peacefully but grew more confident, and relations neither improved nor worsened amid calls both to embrace and to eject them.

Ossium.t: Thule forces aided the Empire in Ossium from the Bonewood, were rumoured to be taking Druj captives north, and sought Imperial approval before approaching the local orcs.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov held nearly three thousand Imperial slaves in its farms, mines and quarries, imposed retaliatory tariffs, and detained Imperial scholars accused of trespass, theft and espionage.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs meet friends from Reikos at Peakedge Stead.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire continued to engage the Jotun in Segura.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire continued to engage the Jotun there, and Crow's Keep's watchtowers overlooked passes into its Silver Peaks.

Skarsind.t: Expansion of Crow's Keep, with watchtowers over passes into Urdur and the Silver Peaks, was expected to finish shortly before the Summer Solstice, and Skarsind was named as a delivery point for ransomed slaves.

Therunin.t: Work began on the Holt of the Oak with Navarr weirwood and donated funds, and the Great Forest Orcs offered to help build an embassy at Peakedge Stead.

My friends are my estate.d: Senator Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian's appraisal sent Naomi to Spiral. She proposed five options. The Obsidian Shipwrights great work would protect fleets from the Plateau, aid scouting and Sarcophan trade, harm Sumaah and Commonwealth trade, and add taxes; it could include a giant Sailor or Witch statue to rival the Colossus of Sarvos. The Palace of Mists would raise Apulian to a rank-two fortification and hamper seaborne attacks. Swords Against Darkness would be a questing venture, needing League and Urizen statements of principle. The Northern Way would link Apulian to Zenith and could expand the Crucible of Fate. A revised Oblivion's Edge would enclose the Black Plateau. All remain proposals.

Dawn.t: Dawnish military units could join the proposed Swords Against Darkness quest in Spiral alongside League and Urizen units, as their glory hunters are thought impossible to keep away.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: remnants of Druj insurgents lurk in Spiral's wilds, and Oblivion's Edge is meant partly to deter Druj raids on the Black Plateau.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel remnants hide in Spiral, the Grendel attack on Elos is cited as a maritime threat, and their old highways towards the Legacy would form the base of the Northern Way.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn vessels are among the ships now seen entering Apulian's harbour.

The League.t: League engineers, guilds and merchants are central to every proposal. Success could make Apulian a rival to Sarvos, and League artisans might be invited to learn ushabti-making at the Crucible of Fate.

Urizen.t: Urizen seers, architects and spires would share in the proposals. The Urizen Assembly's statements could unlock the venture and cheapen the Northern Way, and Urizen fleets, businesses and spires in Spiral would benefit.

My friends are my estate.o: After the Senate dispatched Naomi of Virtue's Rest to appraise Spiral's prosperity, she put forward several League–Urizen proposals to blunt the Black Plateau's effects and enrich the territory. They include a Night-infused shipyard and a fortified Palace of Mists in Apulian, a questing venture, a Northern Way road to Zenith, and a revised Oblivion's Edge fortification.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: Beoraidh is noted as a new Sarcophan protectorate south of Spiral, and one of its merchants backed the shipping talks.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Chain of Sarvos, which guards Cigno against shore offensives, inspired the proposed Apulian defences.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: The proposed Northern Way would run through Apstrus, carrying trade between Apulian and Zenith with protected stopping places.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Apulus would host the proposed Obsidian Shipwrights and Palace of Mists. Seaborne attackers there would face a 20% penalty, and the region could gain a giant statue rivalling the Colossus.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: The Northern Way would pass through Ossuary on its route from Apulian towards the Twilight Gate and Zenith.

Spiral/Screed.t: Oblivion's Edge, a proposed level-one fortification, would enclose the Black Plateau in Screed. It would stop a single season of fighting from rousing the Plateau and require 20 victory points to capture the region.

Zenith/Proceris.t: The Northern Way would climb through the Twilight Gate into Proceris to join the Bridge of the Sky between the Golden Cascade farms and the Crucible of Fate.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: crossing the bay by sail was once preferred to overland travel, and a night crossing in a converted bumboat proved the shipwrights' protective enchantments.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the four older League cities whose centuries of history Apulian is measured against.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: Curstag's Way already links Mareave to the Empire, and the Northern Way might benefit the orcs there too.

Morrow.t: If the Northern Way is built and League artisans join the Crucible, Urizen or League characters with resources in Morrow could have them upgraded with bespoke ushabti.

Redoubt.t: The Brilliant Star's output could fall by three wains if Crucible ushabti were diverted to the Legacy, or keep its support if League artisans doubled the Crucible's capacity. Resources here could also become eligible for upgrades.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Apulian's ambitions are framed as rivalry with Sarvos and its Colossus, and the Great Chain of Sarvos inspired the Palace of Mists.

Spiral.t: The territory would gain from any of these proposals: fewer Black Plateau penalties on fleets, businesses and military units, higher taxation, stronger defences, and a fortification enclosing the Plateau.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is named among the older League cities, and the shipwrights' method was co-developed by Danilo di Tassato.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Apulian is compared with Temeschwar as a League city blending another nation's wisdom with League ambition.

Zenith.t: The proposed Northern Way would raise investment in Zenith's businesses by one level and connect its spires and the Crucible of Fate to Apulian's trade.

My passions from a common spring.d: The Commonwealth paid in goods for Imperial crystal mana and offered another 200-mana deal. It declined the covenstone and runesmith proposals and was irritated that Axos had called a Liberty Pact meeting. It offered Imperial admirals study at the Academy of the Cresting Wave for 50 thrones. Doktor Kunz of the University of Volkavaar sought a sungold tablet from the Advisor on the Vallorn, offering future help in exchange. Jarm flatly refused to prove anything to the Liberty Pact. Prince Mila had the Jarmish client nation Zemelslo open its port of Radosmo to Imperial traders, prompting an administrative Senate motion on whether trading there was lawful.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Therunin is referred to as a territory still to be liberated from the Druj.

Highguard.t: The Highborn's wish for dialogue with the Commonwealth on military doctrine, trade and philosophy was welcomed cautiously. The Militärattache suggested they use die Beurteilung to appraise how closer ties might be built.

Navarr.t: Nathair Autumngale, the Advisor on the Vallorn, hosted Commonwealth scholars at the Great Library of Hacynian and set a price for its cracked sungold tablet. The University of Volkavaar accepted that price, offering expertise to help restore Therunin and first access to any discoveries from the tablet.

The League.t: Professor Gelberg's team completed an examination relating to sieges in Holberg. The Commonwealth turned down the Ambassador's offer of places at the Zemress Naval Academy.

Wintermark.t: Finn Pridetalker of Wintermark, Ambassador to the Commonwealth, was thanked for the mana deal and secured another offer. However, Commonwealth crafters refused to share their runesmithing knowledge, and the Militärattache offered apologies to Stormcrow Cynerik of Grayholm Hall for having only limited knowledge of funerary rites.

My passions from a common spring.o: The Civil Service's Autumn 387YE diplomatic report described the Lantir War between the Commonwealth and the Principalities of Jarm. Neither side was clearly winning, though the Commonwealth seemed to be slowly pushed back. It also set out the state of Imperial relations with both great powers.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Professor Gelberg and his scholars had recently completed an examination relating to sieges in Holberg.

Therunin.t: If the sungold tablet is handed over, the University of Volkavaar promises to send experts to help appraise how Therunin might be restored once it is liberated from the Druj, whenever the Ambassador asks.

Myth makers.d: Morajasse's Grendel, recognised as foreigners under Commander Gallum Fiersach, asked to deal through Imperial Consul Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason. The Spice Gardens of Feroz reopened under Sadiq i Isa i Erigo, and orc soldiers helped restore farms. A delegation met the requested citizens at Anvil, and the Freeborn Assembly upheld with a greater majority a statement encouraging trade with the Protectorate. The Thule still invited Imperial help against the Druj, but no armies joined. Their Ambassador met Runa at the Aureate Jetty. Beoraidh, under Sarcophan protection, held talks with Skoura, traded salt for Unshackled beef, and gained Senate-commissioned docks. The Gull Isle shrine was consecrated to Loyalty. Speaker Morna derided Starlight Starchaser but promised a private reply.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn sends food shipments north to feed Otkodov's people and armies under the treaty with the Thule.

Druj.t: The Thule continued their invasion of the Forest of Ulnak against the Druj, offering crystal mana to Imperial warbands who aided the Earthquake Drummers, though no Imperial armies joined the campaign.

Grendel.t: Speaker Morna sarcastically dismissed Starlight Starchaser as an ambassador without a palace but promised a private reply, while the orcs of Morajasse and Beoraidh both stood apart from the Grendel.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Beoraidh is the Highborn Melkior of Balthazar's Vineyard, who warned Ehsan about the Rivers of Life, assured him of dock funding and cautioned him about the Sarcophan Delves.

Imperial Orcs.t: Frith of the Unshackled serves as Advisor on Orc Affairs, and a new trading post exchanging Beoraidh salt for Unshackled beef brought prosperity to Skarsind's herds.

Jotun.t: The Jotun remained at war with the Empire, yet three ghodi came to Gull Isle to witness the consecration of the Virtuous shrine to Loyalty and discuss what the aura means to the Empire.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr helps ship food to Otkodov, and the Great Forest Orcs are said to regard the Navarr as close allies.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn regained the Spice Gardens and reopened farms in Morajasse, Feroz figures met the Protectorate's delegation at Anvil, and the Freeborn Assembly upheld with a greater majority a call to trade with the Protectorate.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: free Jotun thralls of the Marches are noted as an orc community within the Empire, and the Jotun invasion of Mitwold is said to have only just ended.

Thule.t: Otkodov stayed at peace with the Empire while waging war on the Druj in Ulnak, met the Imperial Ambassador at the Aureate Jetty, and had warlocks watch Imperial pilgrims heading to the Maze of Zoria.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to the Grendel, mocked by Speaker Morna, is Starlight Starchaser of Urizen.

Varushka.t: Varushkan wise ones travelled through Thule lands to the Maze of Zoria to learn about the face-peelers' creature and were watched by silent Thule warlocks.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk led much of the diplomacy: Consul Atte and Ambassador Kindra Surefoot dealt with the orc nations, and Erlend led the consecration of the shrine at the Gull Isle Meeting Place.

Myth makers.o: In Summer 388YE the Empire's dealings with five orc nations moved forward: the Protectorate of Morajasse sent emissaries to Anvil, the Thule pressed their war in Ulnak and met the Ambassador, Beoraidh expanded trade, a shrine was consecrated at the Jotun Meeting Place, and the Grendel mocked the Imperial ambassador.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: Gallum Fiersach's Protectorate held Mora's Rock, reopened farms around the restored Spice Gardens under food quotas, and lost its impoverished quality as orc soldiers helped clear land and dig irrigation.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Ehsan, Lord of Sand, accepted Sarcophan protection as the price of survival, gained a salt-for-beef trade, and saw the Senate commission Imperial docks for his free port.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: Eoradal provided neutral ground for guarded but cautiously optimistic talks between Beoraidh and Skoura, attended by a Sarcophan advisor.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: Ehsan arranged a meeting between Imperial representatives and the Brine Turtles sept of Fleisardh, to include an elder, a warleader and a Grendel advisor.

Mareave/Sinfoyard.t: Goods flowed across barren Sinfoyard's borders through the new trading post, and the Rivers of Life spurred short-lived growth on its farms, with Ehsan hinting at strange crops north of Beoraidh.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as one of the Imperial lands under Jotun control.

Feroz.t: The Spice Gardens returned to the Brass Coast, farms reopened in Morajasse, and the Protectorate guarding Feroz's borders pursued a treaty, though many locals still kept the orcs at arm's length.

Forest of Ulnak.t: The Thule invasion of Ulnak against the Druj continued under Tathenon the Gyre, with Imperial warbands welcome to join, though no Imperial armies did after the Summer Solstice.

Kallavesa.t: The Virtuous shrine at the Meeting Place on Gull Isle, an ancient place of exchange between the ancestors of the Jotun and the Kallavesi, was consecrated to Loyalty with true liao.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: named as under Jotun control, with the Jotun calling it Ashvale.

Mareave.t: Beoraidh, in Mareave, opened a salt-for-beef trading post, saw the Senate commission docks, held talks with Skoura in Eoradal, and arranged a meeting with the Brine Turtles of Fleisardh.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the related Varushkan pilgrimage crossed Thule lands to reach the Maze of Zoria under the treaty.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the recent Jotun invasion of Mitwold is said to have only just ended.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov stayed at peace with the Empire, hosted Imperial pilgrims to the Maze of Zoria under Thule watch, and sent Runa to meet the Ambassador on an agenda including the Vallorn and the war in the Mallum.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; Urizen appears only as the nation of Ambassador Starlight Starchaser.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: some politically engaged priests of Segura were aware of the Freeborn statement on trading with the Protectorate.

Skarsind.t: The new salt-for-beef trade with Beoraidh brought prosperity to the Shepherd of the Southern Herd and the Shepherd of the Great Herd.

Never be found at home.d: Imperial fleets destroyed the bridges, watchtowers and garrisons of the Kongegőr, which links Skallahn and Hordalant and normally blocks large naval forces leaving the Gullet. The Jotun were already working on repairs, so the chance lasted only one season. A Senate motion costing 50 thrones would have the civil service supply cartographers to captains willing to commit fleets. The more fleets that joined, the more the Empire would learn: names of territories, a route south to Faraden, details of Narkyst and Kalsea and their monarchs, and the icy waters of Tsirku. A legendary passage to Ultima Thule might also be found. Any new ports reached could raise tax revenues in the territories bordering the Gullet.

Jotun.t: The Imperial raid tore down a thousand years of Jotun infrastructure on the Kongegőr, and the Jotun were hurrying to rebuild it. An expedition could chart the coasts of Narkyst and Kalsea and perhaps learn about King Gudmundur Arason and Queen Yrsa Jansdóttir.

The Marches.t: Only Marcher and Wintermark fleets could join the expedition at full strength. Marcher merchants are among the few who have ever slipped past the Jotun into the Sea of Snow, and new ports could boost Mitwold's tax revenues.

Thule.t: In the accompanying story the Thule are named as a people wary of the sea. A large enough armada might find the fabled passage to Ultima Thule and open a port with the northern orcs.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark captains could commit fleets at full strength, and some Wintermark merchants have already braved the Sea of Snow. New ports could raise tax revenues in Kallavesa.

Never be found at home.o: After the Empire's raid on Skallahn wrecked the Kongegőr land bridge, a brief chance opened for Imperial fleets to sail into the Sea of Snow. The Senate could fund a 50-throne expedition to map its coasts before the Jotun finished repairs.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland borders the Gullet and could gain tax revenue from new ports, but only once it is back under Imperial control rather than Jotun rule.

Hordalant.t: Hordalant is joined to Skallahn by the damaged Kongegőr, and expedition fleets would turn south past its already well-mapped coast to chart what lies beyond.

Kallavesa.t: If the expedition opened new ports in Faraden or Nithoggir, merchants would find new business opportunities and Kallavesa's tax revenues would rise.

Mitwold.t: As a territory bordering the Gullet, Mitwold would see increased tax revenues if new ports were opened through the expedition.

Sea of Snow.t: With the Kongegőr broken, large Imperial fleets could for once enter the Sea of Snow to map its little-known coastline and the territories around it.

Skallahn.t: Last season's Imperial raid on Skallahn destroyed the Kongegőr defences, and expedition fleets could sail quickly past its well-mapped shore on their way north.

Tsirku.t: A big enough armada could reach the ice-choked waters of Tsirku, a region almost unknown and said to hide frozen-buried jungles and man-eating sea monsters.

New port, old wine.d: Many Bregas welcomed the Jotun's expulsion, but the occupation left lingering grievances. Challenged by Knife-eared Francis, General Amberlain swore a binding oath that the Strong Reeds will protect Bregasland. This cemented the loyal Bregas' support for the army, but the oath breaks if Bregasland is attacked and the army is not present by the start of the next season. House Greywater, whose guidance had let the Reeds hide during the occupation, received twenty thrones from the Synod. Steward Margary Greywater then sought a charter for Eel's Landing, a smugglers' haunt on her family's land, together with a commissioned dock expansion. The Senate approved both, cutting Imperial taxes by two thrones a season.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun appear as the former occupiers of Bregasland whose banishment from the territory forms the background to these events.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League is not discussed directly, but a related Wind of Fortune on the Empress's address in Spiral is listed under further reading.

The Marches.t: Marcher Bregasland gained a binding protective oath from the Strong Reeds' general, and the Greywaters' grievances were eased by Synod coin and a new chartered market town at Eel's Landing. The charter came at the cost of two thrones a season in Imperial taxes.

New port, old wine.o: After the Jotun were driven from Bregasland, General Amberlain swore a binding oath that the Strong Reeds would protect the territory, and House Greywater sought a lasting reward for aiding the resistance. The Imperial Senate later agreed to expand the docks at Eel's Landing and granted it a charter as a market town, ending the embittered mood in the North Fens.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: Mentioned in passing: Knife-eared Francis, the friar of Graven who challenged General Amberlain to swear her oath before the Marcher Assembly, appears to hail from here.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: The fishing village of Eel's Landing on the Gullet, a notorious haunt of smugglers and poachers, has had its docks rebuilt and been chartered as a market town under Greywater control. As a result, the North Fens are no longer embittered.

Bregasland.t: The loyal Bregas are bound more closely to the Strong Reeds by Amberlain's oath, though those who sided with the Jotun remain resentful. The territory also gains a disreputable new market town at Eel's Landing.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Empress Lisabetta's charter for Sarcombe, which the senator for Mournwold raised as a Senate motion, is cited as the precedent for chartering Eel's Landing.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral appears only in a further-reading reference to the impact of Empress Vesna's address there.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: Tromsa is not mentioned directly; the page concerns only the aftermath of the Jotun occupation of Bregasland.

News from the north.d: With the crown recovered and Erkenbrand crowned champion, the threat of Wintermark tearing apart passed, though the Thule sorcerer behind the curse escaped. In Sermersuaq the ritual Winter's Ghosts cut all production by a quarter, amid sightings of sinister spirits; the curse later ran its course. Kallavesi mana sites remained halved. Auras of Prosperity raised mine output and congregation influence in Hahnmark and Skarsind while hurting businesses. In Skarsind, news that Wintermark would give the territory to the Imperial Orcs caused anger, and miners began stripping their mines with no maintenance. Freeborn intelligence warned of major Jotun attacks on western Kallavesa.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: a Steinr pilgrim travels to Emperor Guntherm's tomb in Necropolis, and rumour vaguely blames the Highborn, through the Young Empress, for the draining of Kallavesi mana.

Imperial Orcs.t: Wintermark's decision to give Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs as a homeland was celebrated at Anvil, but some Skarsind miners began stripping their mines so that the incoming orcs would not profit from their work.

Jotun.t: Jotun raiders struck along Wintermark's western borders into Stark, the Suaq Wastes, Westmark and Skymarsh, and Freeborn intelligence pointed to major Jotun attacks on western Kallavesa in the months ahead.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the tale is set in a Navarr wayhouse, where a Suaq hunter travelling with a striding hears the northern news over Navarr beer.

Thule.t: The Thule kept fighting for the Silver Peaks and laid the curse Winter's Ghosts on Sermersuaq, while the Thule sorcerer behind the Bane of Tradition escaped.

Wintermark.t: The Bane of Tradition faded with the crown's recovery and Erkenbrand's crowning, but Wintermark's homelands suffered curses, Jotun raids, and anger in Skarsind at its senators' decision to give the territory away.

News from the north.o: In Summer 379YE the Bane of Tradition faded from Wintermark after the Crown of Three Tears was recovered, but Thule curses ravaged Sermersuaq, Kallavesa's mana stayed drained, auras of Prosperity shook Hahnmark and Skarsind, and Jotun raids grew bolder.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: Mystics reported eerie dancing lights over the Kallavesa Marsh and muttered grimly about what they might portend.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The Thule continued to fight Imperial forces for control of the Silver Peaks.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: Jotun reavers raided into Stark but were driven off by the armies in Sermersuaq.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: Jotun raiders reached as far as the Suaq Wastes before the armies in Sermersuaq drove them off.

Hahnmark.t: Auras of Prosperity sharply increased mine profits and congregation influence while hurting other businesses, and there was talk of building a great shrine or cathedral to Prosperity to keep the mines blessed.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesi mana sites stayed at half production under a lingering curse, and the Freeborn warned of major Jotun attacks on western Kallavesa after raids into Westmark and Skymarsh.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: a Steinr woman is travelling to Necropolis on pilgrimage to the tomb of Emperor Guntherm.

Sermersuaq.t: Winter's Ghosts cut all production in the territory by a quarter, bringing crop failure, sickness, fires, floods and an angry mammoth herd, before the curse ran its course; icewalkers feared these spirits might combine dangerously with husk-raising magic.

Skarsind.t: Many felt betrayed by the decision to give Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs, and as the Prosperity auras lingered, miners neglected maintenance to strip their mines, threatening to leave them unsafe.

Nightcall.d: The mystics of Ishal have left their aviary to travel Wintermark seeking omens. Asked by the Raven Seer to find alternatives to Dripping Echoes of the Fen, Wyr proposed three fanes, each costing 10 mithril, 10 ilium and 30 crowns: the Dreaming Barrow for Feather on the Breeze, the Toadstone for the Toad King, and a converted Aviary at Ishal for the Speaker in Dreams. The omens say that all three together would anchor the Night realm around Kallavesa and make it much harder to invade. Brennir Calversbairn also called in a favour to arrange a meeting for up to nine Wintermark magicians, chosen by the Shaman, with Sadogua at the Equinox. The mystics offered further proposals for the coming year.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are cited as foes that Sadogua has little reason to like and that Lashonar would not welcome, and Ephisis's protection of an apparent fane in Jotun lands is given as a precedent.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the patronage that Spiral Dancer gives the magicians of the Deathless Cave in Spiral is cited as an example of a fane drawing an eternal into defending a region.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the mystics point to Urizen studies of magical resonance to explain why three fanes together might have a potent and unexpected effect.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's mystics offered the nation three fane commissions to defend Kallavesa, each with a Wintermark steward, and a chance for up to nine of its magicians to bargain with Sadogua over his withdrawn favour. They also offered to bring further proposals for the coming year in answer to problems the Ravenseer sends them by ritual.

Nightcall.o: The mystics of Ishal, guided by the Raven Seer, proposed new ways to protect Kallavesa now that the Toad King has weakened Dripping Echoes of the Fen. They suggested building three fanes to three night eternals in the territory, and arranged a private meeting with Sadogua at the Autumn Equinox.

Kallavesa/Rundhal Marsh.t: Feather on the Breeze has suggested a fane at the Dreaming Barrow in Rundhal Marsh, an ancient mound where sleepers have prophetic dreams. She would likely take a personal interest in protecting the site.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: Wyr proposed a fane housing the Toadstone, an onyx carving near Westerhal in West Marsh, to be ceded to the Toad King. The local wizards would become a fraternity supporting it.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa is the territory the proposals aim to protect. The mystics believe that three night fanes placed around its borders would shroud the marshes and help defend them against invasion from any quarter.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is cited as a precedent, where Spiral Dancer's patronage of the Deathless Cave's magicians appears to give the eternal a stake in the region's safety.

Nightfall in Apulian.d: Five dramaturgical personae (all but the Mountebank) now appeared openly in Apulian. Its streets shifted unpredictably, favouring pleasure and subterfuge, though the Black Plateau seemed unaffected. Proposals for an Academy or University of Dramaturgy had popular support. Teodore duSesna of the DuSesna Guild accused Rafael Barossa, Genoveva Barossa, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato and Sofonisba Amilcara of complicity in a pact with Sung through the Chamber of Euphony. Few believed him, but Synod scrutiny was suggested. Victo von Temeschwar revealed a single Grendel ring across the Bay of Catazar. The Senate could guarantee destruction of the Spiral jewel, or the Military Council could gamble on luring or deterring Grendel attacks.

Grendel.t: The Salt Council's bribery-and-blackmail espionage ring was exposed, and its Spiral jewel could be destroyed or used to feed them false intelligence. This could lure their armies into attacking Spiral or scare them away for two seasons.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Barachel of Adina's Charge was recalled as having uncovered Grendel spies in Necropolis, and the Senate's refusal to restore Berechiah's Basilica in Bastion was noted.

The League.t: League citizens of Apulian could draw on the manifest personae and gain strength in Night magic, while prominent League figures of the Camorra Barossa were publicly accused over Sung's fane.

Urizen.t: Urizeni magicians, backed by an Urizen Assembly statement, were eager to study Apulian's dramaturgical confluence, and Urizen characters from Spiral could share in the city's magical effects.

Nightfall in Apulian.o: In Summer 387YE the city of Apulian in Spiral sank deeper into the influence of the Night realm and an intensifying dramaturgical confluence, while suspicion fell on Sung's fane and its backers. The infiltration of a Grendel espionage ring gave the Empire a choice: destroy its outpost or attempt counter-espionage.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Apulian's shifting Night-touched streets and walking dramaturgical personae made it a place of intrigue, and it held the Grendel espionage jewel awaiting an Imperial decision.

Spiral/Screed.t: The Black Plateau seemed untouched by the rising Night magic, and false reports of a commission to trigger it could be used to deter Grendel attacks on Spiral.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: a proper restoration of Berechiah's Basilica there, with a Clavem Iudicii title, would have clarified authority over the matter, but the Senate had declined it.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel espionage ring was revealed to span the territories adjoining the Bay, feeding the Salt Council.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: it was where the Empire first found proof of Grendel espionage, a ring since wound up.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sign of Tamar there was cited as an example of a place resonant with particular constellations.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War and the Shuttered Lantern had earlier closed a Grendel spy ring there.

Spiral.t: Spiral hosted a Grendel jewel that could be destroyed by Senate motion, or used by the Military Council to lure or deter Grendel attacks on the territory over the next two seasons.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the accusing DuSesna Guild was of Tassatan extraction, and Tassato's senator was condemned for seconding the fane motion.

No Matter What.d: Acting on an Imperial Orc Assembly mandate, the Sunstorm spent a year studying Feroz. They proposed an Afarjasse Training Camp, costing 16 white granite and 48 crowns. It would create a Drill Sergeant title, train the Winter Sun and Summer Storm for humid regions and end Afarjasse's abandonment. It would also open the way for a Senate appraisal, with Vainakoma Dawnstongue as appraiser, of supplying the Fire of the South from Feroz. Their second plan was a Wranglers Market at Bramar, costing 14 weirwood and 42 crowns. Freeborn cattle trading with the Iron Confederacy would let Sunstorm units spy on Arbonne. This market was commissioned, and its Brass Coast Chief Wrangler is first appointed at the Autumn Equinox 388YE.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: a small orc settlement from the old legion-camp days is noted as still existing in Estcastle.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page and is linked only through its holdings in Feroz and Mareave at the time.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Sunstorm sept repaid Freeborn aid with two proposals. Their Wranglers Market now gives Imperial Orc military units a covert means of spying on the Suranni in Arbonne. A proposed Afarjasse camp would train the Winter Sun and Summer Storm for humid regions under a Sunstorm Drill Sergeant.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gained a new national title, the Chief Wrangler, appointed by Tally of the Votes, with a ministry trading cattle for orichalcum and weltsilver. They also have the chance to appraise supplying the Fire of the South from Feroz if the training camp is built.

No Matter What.o: After Freeborn expertise helped the Imperial Orcs turn desert into oasis in Mareave, the Sunstorm sept came to Feroz with two proposals: a military training camp in Afarjasse, and a joint spy network against the Suranni in Arbonne disguised as a cattle market. The Wrangler's Market spy network was commissioned and funded.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: The Wranglers Market was funded for Bramar, working with the Dhomiro of Afar and drawing on Afar's restored herds. A proposed Sunstorm training camp could also end the region's abandoned status.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Mentioned in passing: the Cazar Straits are noted as now under Suranni control, a daily reminder of the uneasy peace with the Iron Confederacy.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: Mentioned in passing: the martially minded Protectorate of Morajasse might enjoy joint exercises with the Sunstorm, a matter for the Imperial Consul to pursue.

Mareave/Icarion.t: The oasis created in Icarion with expert Freeborn advice was the aid the Sunstorm set out to repay in Feroz.

Semmerholm/Estmure.t: Mentioned in passing: a small orc settlement from the legion-camp days is said still to exist at Estcastle.

Feroz.t: The Sunstorm studied impoverished Feroz for a year and proposed a training camp and a cattle-market spy network there. The market was funded, while the camp and a later appraisal of Feroz's underpopulation remain open opportunities.

Kalino.t: Now called Arbonne under Suranni rule and unmapped by the Empire, this territory is the target of the newly funded Wranglers Market spy network. Imperial Orc units will travel south with Freeborn herds to watch the Suranni there.

Mareave.t: Freeborn advice helped the Imperial Orcs tackle Mareave's aridity, and this aid prompted the Sunstorm's return favour in Feroz. Many Sunstorm are also looking to settle in Mareave.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South traditionally drew supply from the plains of Segura and Feroz, though lately mostly from the Iron Qanat.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Estcastle is cited as home to a small orc settlement surviving from the legion-camp era.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: many Sunstorm settled in Skarsind when the Senate granted it, and Sunstorm founded the Great Herds there.

No Peace.d: The Navarr Black Thorns, Isaella's Dance and Quiet Step, aided by servitors of Arhallogen, swept west through Gambit alongside the Brass Coast's Fire of the South and Red Wind Corsairs. The Lasambrians and Skjalderborn had already withdrawn in good order to Reinos, leaving only a few warbands and depots. Kahraman was liberated, but wrecked roads and bridges still crippled northern travel. In Bregasland the Strong Reeds and House Greywater kept up a guerrilla resistance while the Fishers courted the Bregas. In Liathaven, Jotun forces took every region except Liath's Heart, captured Hotter's Mire and slaughtered any Navarr they found. Four conjunctions offered chances to oppose Lasambrian raiders and Jotun patrols.

Jotun.t: The Lasambrian Jotun gave up Kahraman and retreated to Reinos. Other Jotun upheld Mathilda Fisher's rule in Bregasland and conquered nearly all of Liathaven, planning a white granite citadel at Hotter's Mire.

Navarr.t: The Black Thorns, Isaella's Dance and Quiet Step led the merciless sweep through Gambit. In Liathaven, however, the Jotun crushed the Navarr presence and executed any Navarr they caught, while the Blackroot Broker was asked to rescue Mott's apprentice.

The Brass Coast.t: The Fire of the South and Red Wind Corsairs helped free Kahraman, with the Burning Falcons due to join next season. The nation now faces the costly task of repairing the shattered northern roads and protecting its mithril caravans from raiders.

The Marches.t: Bregasland remains under Fisher and Jotun rule, contested by the Strong Reeds and House Greywater, who need 10 thrones and 40 drams of herbs to continue. The fall of Liathaven left the Mournwold's people facing the Jotun at the threshold of the Mourn once more.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule cunning is credited, alongside Imperial strength, with driving the Jotun out of Sermersuaq.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is not directly named; the page touches it only through the map's attachment of Ossium.

Wintermark.t: Sermersuaq is noted as free of the Jotun. In Kallavesa, Lasambrian raiders threatened a hylje settlement, and the Mediator of Hyljehal, Raal Dunn, was called on to drive them out.

No Peace.o: In Winter 384YE five Imperial armies drove the Lasambrian Jotun out of Kahraman, which they abandoned with little resistance and retreated to Reinos. Meanwhile Mathilda Fisher held Bregasland under Jotun protection, and a Jotun host conquered almost all of Liathaven, bringing them back to the threshold of the Mournwold.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: The Greywaters' harassment gave Grey Fens the allied insurgents quality. A Jotun force struck from here into West Ranging, and the Greywaters asked for supplies to be left at a copse in the south of the region.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: Its garrison supported the Brass Coast armies, but destroyed roads and bridges badly hampered patrols and travel to the neighbouring mountain regions.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: The five Imperial armies swept west across Gambit's dry plains, overcoming only straggling warbands and garrisoned depots. Diverted granite and mithril caravans now pass through it, exposed to bandits.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: Caravans of white granite and mithril must now detour south through Jade Range before heading east, increasing the risk from raiders and bandits.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: Heralds of Cathan Canae descended from a conjured citadel here to aid the Fire of the South. Travel remains crippled, and a Lasambrian warband lay in ambush for the Great Mine of Briante's mithril caravans.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: Passage through Serra Damata was brought to a standstill by the earlier destruction of roads and bridges, cutting it off from Serra Briante.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: Mentioned in passing: West Marsh is not named; the Lasambrian raid in Kallavesa is placed near Rest and Lake Rikkivesi.

Liathaven/Liath's Heart.t: The vallorn heart was the only part of Liathaven not in Jotun hands, though the few Imperial garrisons watching it were left isolated.

Liathaven/Liath's Ring.t: The combined Jotun forces pushed east and captured Liath's Ring from the Feni, ending the recent uneasy détente there.

Liathaven/Liaven's Glen.t: This Feni region, part of the earlier détente, fell under Jotun control along with the rest of Liathaven. Duarte's Lasambrian warband set out from here to raid Kahraman.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: Jotun from Grey Fens smashed through West Ranging, crushing the Imperial garrisons and Navarr presence before using it as a base to push east.

Liathaven/Western Scout.t: The Lasambrian Jotun came down from the Lasambrian Hills into Western Scout and quickly subdued it, along with the vallornspawn there.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: The Jotun overwhelmed the small Imperial presence and garrisons in Westwood, conquering the region.

Mournwold/Green March.t: A messenger expected at Green March never arrived, one of the first signs that Liathaven had fallen.

Bregasland.t: Mathilda Fisher ruled from Fisher's Rock with Jotun backing and worked to win over the Bregas. The Strong Reeds lay low and House Greywater kept harrying the occupiers, though some households chose the quiet life.

Kahraman.t: The territory was wholly Imperial again after the Lasambrians withdrew. Sabotaged roads and bridges in the northern mountains, however, still crippled travel, and a Lasambrian warband planned to ambush mithril caravans from the Great Mine of Briante.

Kallavesa.t: A Lasambrian warband led by Sofio, calling themselves Hessar's Voice, marched near Rest to slaughter a hylje settlement on Lake Rikkivesi, threatening the Mediator of Hyljehal's mana crystal supply.

Liathaven.t: Jotun forces conquered every region except Liath's Heart, scattered the Feni and took Hotter's Mire as their base. They killed any Navarr they found, crushed Imperial steadings and stridings, and began dealing with the vallornspawn.

Mournwold.t: Navarr survivors fled into the Mournwold, whose farmers and miners now look west with dread, fearing a repeat of the earlier Jotun invasion of the Mourn.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not referred to anywhere on the page.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian armies retreated from Kahraman into the hills of Reinos.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are said to be gone from Sermersuaq, driven out by Imperial strength and Thule cunning.

No evil shall escape our sight.d: Founded under Emperor Nicovar as an investigative arm of the Vigilance Assembly, the Silent Bell kept operating after being disbanded and has a mixed reputation for both uncovering threats and discrediting political movements. Its preceptor, Malachai, proposed that the Council of Nine direct its investigations by statement of principle, or alternatively by greater majority let it report privately to the Cardinal of Vigilance. The sodality insisted on staying apolitical and would not investigate threats whose primary source lies at Anvil. The Synod could endorse or reject it. It endorsed the sodality, and Esau the Highborn executed a supporting mandate, bringing improved attendance at Vigilance congregations across the Empire.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel Salt Lord is used as an example of a foreign figure the Silent Bell would struggle to gather intelligence about directly.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn Esau executed the mandate supporting the Silent Bell, which boosted Vigilance congregations across the Empire.

No evil shall escape our sight.o: The Silent Bell, a Vigilance sodality officially disbanded in 210YE but still quietly active, offered its investigative services formally to the Imperial Synod. At the Winter solstice the Synod declared its support, the Council of the Nine gave its first instruction, and a mandate endorsing the sodality was executed.

Casinea/Casfall.t: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Bell's preceptor, Malachai, is named as Malachai of the Silent Bell, in Casca's Doom.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Bell's current preceptor, Malachai, is styled as being in Casca's Doom.

Not a drop to drink.d: The blight is driven by Dry Patricians, intelligent creatures akin to ushabti, and by the Parched who are slowly becoming them. Regrow the Land's Heart has kept the blight from spreading but cannot weaken it. If the ritual is cast every season, the Great Grasses would be lost to desert by Winter 385YE but the blight held at its borders. Making it permanent would need 120 rings of ilium. Missing a single season risked desertification across Madruga, including Siroc. Three conjunctions were offered: the Champion of Loyalty, Dagon, could recover a living Tutamen survivor; Grandmaster Eliza could escort Unfettered Mind scholars to a minor Winter regio; and Senator Chiara Zayden Riqueza could stop Dry Patricians gathering at a powerful regio.

Highguard.t: Unconquered from Syrene suspect the blight's Aldea di Tutamen family descends from the Tutamen, a pre-revelation Highborn patrician family. They asked the Champion of Loyalty to recover a living survivor dressed as a Highborn magister.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun-held Bregasland is home to the Landskeeper tradition of the Marcher scholar Barti Dourfen.

Navarr.t: The Navarri vate Merry Songbird's Passing wished to study the blight as a possible Winter-fuelled vallorn and sought fellow Navarr to escort her. She hoped Navarr understanding of the Dance of Navarr and Thorn might be turned against it.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn faced losing the Great Grasses, and potentially all of Madruga including Siroc, unless Regrow the Land's Heart was cast every season. Some Freeborn muttered that this was the Empire's own vallorn, and the Senator for Madruga was charged with confronting the Dry Patricians.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: an ancestor of the orc shaman Frostbiter Grik had been enslaved by a Thule warlock who experimented with Winter magic to blight the land.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dry Patricians were likened to the ushabti of Urizen, creatures closer to enchanted objects than truly living beings.

Not a drop to drink.o: A Winter-fuelled blight continued to threaten the Great Grasses of Madruga, held back only by repeated castings of Regrow the Land's Heart. The Sentinel Gate offered three conjunctions into the blight at the Summer Solstice to further the search for a permanent cure.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the scholar Barti Dourfen comes from a proud tradition of Bregas Landskeepers and proposed using standing stones to contain or redirect the blight.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: a group of unconquered from Syrene had been asking about the Aldea di Tutamen family and its possible Highborn ancestry.

Madruga.t: The Great Grasses faced being lost to a deadly desert, held at its borders only if Regrow the Land's Heart was cast every season. A missed season risked spreading desertification to Siroc, Cazar, Qatar and Trajadoz, and possibly beyond Madruga.

Not dark yet.d: The Freeborn, Marcher and Wintermark assemblies had condemned the Iron Helms' cruelty, while the Varushkan and Navarr assemblies backed it. The Iron Helms had arrested Dogri Thulebane at Crow's Keep and then waged a merciless onslaught against the Jotun in the Mourn. Gunnbrand Ironwill took 50 liao for Wintermark to shun the Iron Helms and show true heroism. Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra took 25 liao for the Freeborn to reject them. Amris Johan Merikovich took 100 liao for Varushka to show real cruelty, giving the Iron Helms the dark-magic order Terror in the Night. Corey Wayfarer took 75 liao for Navarr, so the Quiet Step may become a Cunning army. The Marcher option was not taken up.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is named as a nation attacked by the Druj, and its lands were among those where an unenacted Varushkan mandate would have strengthened Varushkan defenders.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj resurgence in the east is cited as the threat to Karsk, Dawn and Urizen that some Varushkans argued their armies should face instead of the Jotun.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the nation is not named, but the Iron Helms' action against the rebel Dogri Thulebane took place in Skarsind, which the Imperial Orcs held.

Jotun.t: Jotun forces in the Mourn suffered the Iron Helms' merciless onslaught, and the Varushkan mandate now lets the Iron Helms send night terrors into Jotun dreams to break their armies. The Marcher option to fight them with restraint was not enacted.

Navarr.t: The Navarr assembly had declared the Iron Helms' cruel tactics virtuous, then sent Corey Wayfarer with 75 liao. The general of the Quiet Step may now permanently make the army Cunning by supplying 50 wains of weirwood.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League's Holberg was named among territories where Varushkan armies would have gained a defensive bonus under a mandate that was not enacted.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is named as attacked by the Druj, and its lands were among those where an unenacted Varushkan mandate would have aided Varushkan defenders.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan assembly defended the Iron Helms and sent Amris Johan Merikovich with 100 liao. Until the Spring Equinox 382YE, dark spirits, cabals and wolves accompany the army, letting its general order Terror in the Night for 25 mana crystals.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark sent Gunnbrand Ironwill with 50 liao, so for a year its soldiers shun the Iron Helms, reducing that army's victory points when they campaign together. Wintermark generals fighting alongside the Iron Helms may also order a triumphant charge or final stand.

Not dark yet.o: After the Iron Helms' cruelty against the Jotun, several national assemblies were offered Synod mandates to shun or support the Varushkan army at the Summer Solstice 381YE. Wintermark, the Freeborn, Navarr and Varushka each enacted one.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg was listed where Varushkan armies would have gained a 10% defensive bonus under a mandate that was not enacted.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: Karsk is described as once again directly threatened by Druj barbarians, a reason given for turning Varushkan armies east.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven was listed among places where Varushkan orders would have been restricted under a mandate that was not enacted.

Mournwold.t: The Iron Helms' cruelty against the Jotun in the Mourn was seen by Winterfolk, Freeborn and Marchers, prompting these mandates. The Quiet Step's tactics there also stirred debate among the Navarr.

Skarsind.t: In Skarsind the Iron Helms crushed Dogri Thulebane's rebellion, destroyed Crow's Keep and carried him in chains to Anvil, angering many Winterfolk.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Therunin was listed where Varushkan armies would have gained a defensive bonus under a mandate that was not enacted.

Not from the benevolence.d: The Senator for Reikos agreed in principle to cede Remember Exile to Ephisis for 100 wains of white granite, on condition it is not sold to the Druj or Grendel. The deal needs Senate approval, and only the General Assembly may veto. Bastion's senator, Merari Navigators of Virtue, may offer a sale next. Seven contracts were offered for auction in the Hall of Worlds. Dorys Delgorokov, Damiàn i Martàn i Erigo and Terentia of Sarangrave were invited to submit contracts of their own. Following Terentia's declaration, plans for fanes at Treji, Fisk and Drycastle now await Senate motions. Each must be ceded to Ephisis and creates a national title, but building more than one reduces each fane's tax boost.

Dawn.t: Dawn stands to gain the Drycastle Emporium in the Barrens, which would create the Dawnish title Seneschal of the Drycastle Emporium. The holder must be a yeofolk in good standing to submit contracts, and could buy warm ashes and Pauper's Keys.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the sale of Remember Exile is conditional on Ephisis not selling the fortification on to the Druj or the Grendel.

Grendel.t: The Remember Exile deal forbids Ephisis from selling the fortification on to the Grendel. A detailed Map of Tathar offered in one contract is hinted to come from a single obvious source, implying the Grendel are the counter-party.

Highguard.t: To help pay for the Grand Inspiration of the Way, the Senator for Reikos arranged, through Eli of the Cenotaph, to cede Remember Exile for 100 wains of white granite, pending Senate approval. Necropolis passed on its turn, and Bastion's senator now has the chance to offer something for sale.

Navarr.t: The proposed Treji Plaza in Hercynia would create the Navarr title Broker of the Treji Plaza. The holder must be a broker in good standing to submit contracts, and could buy warm ashes and Rings of the Golden Market.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: one of Ephisis's contracts offers the deed to Rootha's Exports, a level seven business in Sarvos, in exchange for 70 thrones.

Wintermark.t: The proposed Fisk Wareroom in Kallavesa, which grew from a scheme involving the Wintermark merchant Erlend Gunnulfsson, would create the title Mediator of the Fisk Wareroom. The holder must be a mediator or maggot in good standing to submit contracts, and could buy warm ashes and tradesoil.

Not from the benevolence.o: In Autumn 388YE the heralds of Ephisis, the City of Gold and Lead, returned with new trade offers: a proposed sale of the Reikos fortification of Remember Exile, seven bulk contracts for auction, invitations for chosen citizens to submit contracts, and completed plans for three Autumn market fanes in Hercynia, Kallavesa and the Barrens.

Hercynia/The Glen of Shadows.t: The Treji Plaza would be built at Treji in the Glen of Shadows, giving Ephisis's heralds free passage there and a market for the region's herb gardens to trade unwanted herbs for herbalists' tools.

Kallavesa/Wittal Grove.t: The Fisk Wareroom would be built at Fisk in Wittal Grove, letting Ephisis's heralds come and go freely and giving local questing and guarding military units a market for their goods.

Bastion.t: A herald reminded the Empire that it is Bastion's turn this summit. Senator Merari Navigators of Virtue may choose whether to offer something from the White City or elsewhere in the territory for sale to Ephisis.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not named directly in the page's text.

Hercynia.t: The Treji Plaza fane is proposed here, costing 20 white granite, 40 weirwood, 10 ilium and 180 crowns. It would add 4 thrones of taxation a season, boost herb gardens and raise Hercynian characters' income by 9 rings for a year, but must be ceded to Ephisis.

Kallavesa.t: The Fisk Wareroom fane is proposed here, costing 30 white granite, 30 weirwood, 10 ilium and 180 crowns. It would add 7 thrones of taxation a season, aid military units questing or guarding, and raise Kallavesa characters' income by 12 rings for a year, but must be ceded to Ephisis.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Necropolis chose to pass on their turn to sell a feature of the territory to Ephisis.

Reikos.t: The fortification of Remember Exile would be ceded to Ephisis for 100 wains of white granite if the Senate passes the motion. Heralds of the Iron Labyrinth have already gathered at the castle with measuring and excavation tools.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Terentia of Sarangrave is named as one of the citizens invited to submit a contract to Ephisis, and as the Grandmaster whose declaration accepted all three fanes.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the deed to Rootha's Exports, a level seven business in Sarvos, is offered as payment in one of Ephisis's contracts.

Tathar.t: Mentioned in passing: a detailed, verified Map of Tathar suitable for scrying is offered as payment for 1000 thrones in one contract.

The Barrens.t: The Drycastle Emporium fane is proposed in Dawnguard, costing 35 white granite, 25 weirwood, 10 ilium and 180 crowns. It would add 5 thrones of taxation a season, aid military units, and raise Barrens characters' income by 10 rings for a year, but must be ceded to Ephisis.

Not to conquer.d: Ser Dindrane's policy persuaded new Dawnish settlers to hold back while negotiations began, aided by Highborn priests using peerless kinship. Almost every faction understood 'liberation' as having land ceded to it. The Rahvin held the Fangs and wanted three regions. The Karass, already foreigners, wanted the Bleaks and a peace with the Druj. The flooded Vendarri sought a new home, possibly in Holberg. The Great Forest Orcs wanted the Heart of Peytaht retaken.
