The Montanian heretics claimed Hope's Rest. The Black Wind refused all talks. The Druj still held Murderdale and the Heart of Peytaht. Dawn would not accept the Barrens ceasing to be Dawnish, and Cathan Canae's stance on ceding land complicated any concessions.

Dawn.t: Dawn held the Barrens and embraced Ser Dindrane's call to work with the orcs rather than flood the territory with settlers. Its people wanted the Towers of the Dawn rebuilt, the Fangs and Eaves of Peytaht made Dawnish bourse seats, and Dawnguard, Murderdale, the Carmine Fields and the Plains of Teeth kept, and would be outraged by any outcome that left the Barrens no longer Dawnish.

Druj.t: The Druj still held Murderdale and the Heart of Peytaht and were using them to launch attacks into the Barrens. Their expected return and reprisals against collaborators shaped the fears of every sept.

Highguard.t: Highborn priests used peerless kinship to mediate for Dawn, drawing on the Vendarri's surrender to them and their past work with the Great Forest Orcs. A proposed mandate would have Highguard help the Great Forest Orcs retake Peytaht instead of supporting an Imperial nation that season.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Winter Sun had helped the Rahvin free themselves at the Fangs and some Imperial Orcs still supplied them. A relief mandate could make the Imperial Orcs the Empire's chosen negotiators with that sept.

Navarr.t: The Great Forest Orcs and Montanians had lived as guests of the Navarr in Therunin. Navarr mandates were offered to help the orcs retake the Heart of Peytaht; if the Highborn did so instead, most of the orcs would leave Therunin and the closeness with the Navarr would fade.

The League.t: The Vendarri asked for the Morass or Rebeshof in Holberg as a new home. The Sand Fishers objected strongly, warning that such a settlement would sour their relations with the League.

Urizen.t: Two alternative Urizeni mandates were offered: one urging the Citadel Guard to attack the Heart of Peytaht, the other calling on Urizeni to aid the Great Forest Orcs, as the Druj had been driven from Zenith.

Varushka.t: From Varushkan-held Ossium, the Menrothat offered a dose of black lotus in return for Farweald, and the Vendarri refused the Drownbark Forest because the Menrothat lived there.

Not to conquer.o: Following the Barrens' assignment to Dawn, Dawnish and Highborn priests opened talks with the territory's septs, each of which set out what 'liberation' should mean for them. The Wind set out Senate, Synod, Military Council and Conclave options for answering their demands, along with the risks of each.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn and Great Forest Orcs had cooperated in Elerael over a shared interest in healing and herbs.

Brocéliande/Terunael.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs had been called to fight the Heirs of Terunael in Brocéliande.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj almost destroyed the Great Pits of Ennerlund, cited as proof of their spite.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: The Sand Fishers of Misericorde sent a delegation to Misericorde Market to protest against the Vendarri settling in Holberg.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: Rebeshof was the Vendarri's second choice of a new home if the Morass was unavailable.

Holberg/The Morass.t: The Morass was the Vendarri's preferred new home. The Senate could cede it, with an escort paid for by the treasury or provided by an Imperial army.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Highborn priests proposed the Drownbark marshes for the Vendarri, who rejected them because the Menrothat lived there and the Druj of Ulnak were nearby.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: Around 750 Rahvin held the Fangs mithril mine here, and Bitter Strand was their first demand. The options set out ranged from recognising their control of the mine to besieging or attacking them.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Returning Dawnish were reclaiming estates here and wanted the Towers of the Dawn rebuilt, while small Black Wind settlements remained in the region.

The Barrens/Farweald.t: The Menrothat of Ossium asked for Farweald in exchange for a dose of black lotus, a return opposed by every faction except the Karass.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: The Druj still held the region and its weirwood grove, where Great Forest Orc slaves were at risk of massacre. Mandates and army orders were offered to retake it for the orcs.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: Montanians were gathering at the ruins of Dourfell Keep and wanted Hope's Rest ceded to them. A single army could instead annihilate them there.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Murderdale remained under Druj control. The Rahvin wanted it ceded, the Dawnish regarded it as theirs, and the Great Forest Orcs would help claim it.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: The Vendarri's home was wrecked by Imperial-raised floods. Conclave endowments, an Order mission, or an army protecting them could help, or the region could be ceded to them.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: The Karass withdrew into the Bleaks and wanted it ceded to them first; an Imperial army could attack them there at the Autumn Equinox.

The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth.t: The Karass abandoned most of their settlements here but asked for the region and the Towers of Dusk, which the Dawnish refused to give up.

The Barrens/The Untrod Groves.t: The Karass were digging in within the Untrod Groves, and a second army would be needed here to break them.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat was expected to celebrate the Barrens being assigned to Dawn.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Great Forest Orcs had worked with the Highborn in Brocéliande, and Druj holdings in the Barrens could theoretically reach it.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: Rahvin slaves might be held there, the Dawnish wanted to campaign against it, and its Druj made Ossium unsafe for the Vendarri.

Holberg.t: The Vendarri asked for the Morass or Rebeshof, with an escort into Holberg, but the Sand Fishers warned against sharing the territory with them.

Ossium.t: The Menrothat of Ossium offered black lotus for Farweald, and Highborn priests suggested the Drownbark Forest to the Vendarri, who declined because of the Menrothat and the nearby Druj.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as an example of the horrors the Druj inflicted when driven out.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Mentioned in passing: more Rahvin slaves were believed held there, the Empire was striking against it, and the Dawnish wanted it invaded to secure the border.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: it bordered the Karass regions, and the Dawnish wanted it invaded to push the Druj border beyond the Barrens.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: expected to celebrate Dawn's gain of the Barrens, and theoretically within reach of Druj attacks from the Barrens.

The Barrens.t: Newly assigned to Dawn, the territory's septs each demanded regions of their own while the Druj still held two regions and no armies were present. The Wind set out options ranging from treaties and cessions to military action against the septs.

Therunin.t: The Great Forest Orcs and Montanians had lived in Therunin, though many Montanians were returning to Hope's Rest. A Highborn-led retaking of Peytaht would see most of the orcs leave Therunin.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater was expected to celebrate the Barrens being assigned to Dawn.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: a Urizeni mandate cited the Druj being driven from Zenith as inspiration to aid the Great Forest Orcs.

Nothing great without cost.d: Writing from Holfried, Lisabetta announced that four foreign powers would join a Liberty Pact meeting at Anvil next summit, pursuing the liberation of slaves across Creation. Invoking 'no new fronts', she set out the Empire's priorities: fighting the Jotun without extreme measures to keep diplomacy possible, exterminating the Druj alongside a new Thule military alliance, keeping faith with Highborn pilgrims and Navarr against the vallorn, and confronting the Grendel. She revealed a maritime expedition of private fleets and forces heading for the Grendel homeland, and fortifications on the south coast needing at least five more seasons. She also pledged to speak more with citizens at Anvil.

Druj.t: The Imperatrix declared the Druj a scourge to be eliminated by exterminating the evil of their society, using whatever measures the Empire can muster, including the new Thule alliance.

Grendel.t: With diplomacy having failed, the Imperatrix revealed a great maritime expedition of private fleets and military forces sailing south to prove the Grendel homeland is not safe across the ocean, alongside south-coast fortifications against their raids.

Highguard.t: The Imperatrix pledged to keep faith with the Highborn pilgrims newly walking the trods and with those who agreed to share prosperity so the cost of the vallorn fight is not borne by Highguard alone.

Jotun.t: The Imperatrix expected the Jotun war to rage for long years, but urged it be fought without extreme measures so that Jotun notions of honour are respected and future diplomacy remains possible.

Navarr.t: The Imperatrix praised the Navarr who have stayed their weapons against the vallorn so that the Empire can strike more surely together when the opportunity returns.

The League.t: The League Imperatrix wrote from her guildhouse in Holfried, framing her message around the League saying 'nothing great, without cost' and the legacy of Emperor Frederick.

Thule.t: The Imperatrix announced a new military alliance with the Thule against the Druj, sealed with the Empire's commitment not to abandon its allies to fight alone for as long as it takes.

Nothing great without cost.o: Imperatrix Lisabetta used the Throne's power to address the Empire, sending a personal letter from her guildhouse in Holfried weighing the cost of the Empire's many wars against its ambitions, chiefly the Liberty Pact and an end to the Grendel threat.

Holberg/Holfried.t: The address was written from the highest window of Lisabetta's guildhouse in the heart of Holfried, looking towards the horizon Emperor Frederick once beheld.

Holberg.t: The Imperatrix described Holberg flourishing again, protected by white granite and invested coin, regaining the prosperity forfeited under Empress Giselle.

Nowhere and everywhere.d: Irra Harah tersely offered the Spring Archmage alone a parley at 10pm on Friday. Basileus Flint offered the Autumn Archmage, Marcus of Endsmeet, Adelina of Felix's Watch and one other a formal parley with his Vizier. Topics were the Druj relationship with the eternals, Druj armies, maps of Druj territory and help finding and setting spies. Flint also asked for a dose of lethal poison, and any agreement would bind the Empire. Phaleron granted Gralka a parley on the archive and the Anvil library. Wise Rangara offered a meeting, not a parley, on poison. Lashonar set its own agenda for the Archmage of Night, and Rhianos praised the Dubhtraig raid.

Druj.t: The Druj were the subject of Basileus Flint's parley, which offered the Empire information on their dealings with the eternals and on their armies. It also opened discussion of maps of Druj territory.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Archmage of Night invited to Lashonar's parley is Elyssiathain of Urizen.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wise Rangara's offer of a meeting was addressed to the Winter Archmage, Syn Truth-Walker Returned, who was asked to bring six Academy students.

Nowhere and everywhere.o: After the Autumn Equinox, six eternals answered the archmages' plenipotentiary messages. Five arranged parleys or meetings with the Empire for the Winter Solstice, and Rhianos declined a parley but offered aid instead.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is not named on the page, and none of the arranged parleys or meetings is said to take place there.

O rose thou art sick.d: Despite rumours that many de Lusignan nobles had taken their own lives, curses continued. In Astolat, Dawn's witches identified a curse, almost certainly Night magic, that inflamed noble rivalries and stirred yeofolk resentment, especially around Laroc. Astolat soldiers questioned orders and some deserted. Their warbands lost a quarter of their fighting strength unless doing paid work. Tassato suffered stinking heat from Icy Maw Devours the Spark of Essence, which halved its crystalline mana. Naeve's Twisting Blight halved Casinea's farm production. These curses ran their course by the Summer Solstice. The Winter curse on the Court of the White Fountain persisted, slowed but not reversed by the Spire of the Auric Horizon's magic.

Dawn.t: Astolat's nobles saw tempers flare into Tests of Resolve, yeofolk grew insolent and questioned old traditions, and Astolat soldiers wherever they served became slow to obey, with some desertions.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: an Astolat seneschal fumes that the abandoned keep could have been attacked by Druj.

Highguard.t: Highborn farms in Casinea were devastated by three rainless months, with crop failures, food poisoning and a few deaths before the blight passed.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: fear of the Jotun after their conquest of the Mournwold left Tassato's discontented citizens subdued.

The League.t: Tassato's people endured a stinking, oppressive heat, and its magicians suffered malaise while the city's mana sources yielded only half their usual crystal mana.

Urizen.t: The Court of the White Fountain in Redoubt continued to crumble under a Winter curse, and the Spire of the Auric Horizon's magic delayed but did not reverse the decline.

O rose thou art sick.o: In Summer 380YE a suspected Night curse inflamed resentment in Astolat, particularly among yeofolk and Dawnish soldiers, while other curses brought a sapping heat to Tassato, drought to Casinea and continued decay to the Court of the White Fountain in Redoubt.

Redoubt/Optarion.t: The Court of the White Fountain's plume of fire guttered and its white stone cracked again, and the decline was slowed but not reversed.

Astolat.t: A curse spread from the eastern woodlands, setting yeofolk against nobles, prompting talk near Laroc of whether their ancestors should have marched west, and undermining discipline among local soldiers.

Casinea.t: No rain fell from the Spring Equinox to the Summer Solstice, halving all farm production. Spoiled food and hidden thirst caused some deaths before the curse abated.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun conquest of the Mournwold weighed on the minds of Tassato's people.

Redoubt.t: The fortification at Optarion was still being eroded by a Winter curse, held back only by the Auric Horizon's adamant and Summer magic.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: wags noted that people had also called Sarvos too damp to burn.

Tassato.t: An unseasonable heatwave festered the spring floodwaters into a great stink, weak regio collapsed and mana sources produced only half their normal output until the Solstice.

Obsidian shards.d: Just as Spiral seemed to be stabilising, a caravan bringing arms from Holberg to the Ballaghadruh garrison was massacred, and the Prismatic Garden was overrun and looted. A dead attacker's obsidian shard symbol was identified by Caela of the Silver Flame as belonging to the Spire of Black Glass, former Citadel Guard sentinels turned conspiratorial under the Black Plateau's influence. Caela and other former rebel leaders disavowed them. Leaguish and Urizen folk worked together and learned the sentinels meant to damage the Block and kill researchers in Screed. Magistrates deputised over a hundred citizens. The Senator for Spiral, Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian, was charged with defending the Block, and the Oblivion Sentinel, Floria Sunshaper, with protecting the researchers, both in fights to the death under the Plateau's malign influence.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: lingering questions about contact with the Grendel are noted, and the Spire of Black Glass's origins are traced to the battle of Solen's Doubt against them in 382YE.

The League.t: Leaguish interests were among those targeted, beginning with the massacre of the Holberg arms caravan, and Leaguish citizens worked alongside Urizen to uncover the sentinels' plans.

Urizen.t: A Urizen spire was wiped out by renegade sentinels from among the former rebels, whom Caela of the Silver Flame disavowed, and the Oblivion Sentinel Floria Sunshaper was charged with bringing them to justice.

Obsidian shards.o: In Winter 386YE a renegade faction of former rebels, the sentinels of the Spire of Black Glass, slaughtered a merchant caravan and the Urizen spire of the Prismatic Garden in Spiral, then moved against the Block and a group of Black Plateau researchers. Two conjunctions gave Imperial heroes the chance to stop them.

Spiral/Ankra.t: The Holberg caravan was found slaughtered in a pass on the edge of Ankra and Ossuary, and the Spire of Black Glass's abandoned citadel lies on Ankra's border.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Former rebels' status as foreigners relies on the Senate recognising their control of Cinion, and a free company scouting a pass there spotted the armed sentinels on the move.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: The massacred caravan was discovered in a pass on the edge of Ossuary and Ankra, near the abandoned Spire of Black Glass on Ossuary's border.

Spiral/Screed.t: Researchers studying the Black Plateau in Screed were caught out of position and faced massacre unless the Oblivion Sentinel's forces stopped the sentinels hunting them.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the slaughtered caravan was carrying weapons and armour from the forges of Holberg.

Spiral.t: Spiral's fragile peace was shattered by murders and looting from the Spire of Black Glass, whose sentinels threatened the Block that restrains the Black Plateau and researchers sheltering there.

Of earth and sky.d: After the Summer Solstice the Lasambrians and their yegarra allies tore up roads and bridges, cutting Braydon's Jasse off from Serra Briante and Serra Damata, then massed on Jade Range to take Fort Braydon. The Black Thorns, Quiet Step, Isaella's Dance, Fire of the South and Red Wind Corsairs, aided by the fort's garrison, struck instead. The Navarr pursued slaughter under a ravens-haunted mist that fed bloodlust, while the Freeborn raided supplies. Skjalderborn reinforcements failed to stop the rout at Nestor's Bounty. The ritual Shroud of Fog and Ravens has been rendered unworkable by the Lock's conjunction. The Empire could fight at Rojota over the fate of the wounded orcs, and could use a conjunction to Talaeiros to rescue the abducted quarry-woman Catalina.

Jotun.t: The Lasambrian Escuta, Hierro and Corazón were routed from Jade Range into Gambit with heavy losses despite Summer elves and Skjalderborn reinforcements. Up to a thousand of their wounded trapped in Rojota, and a thousand more across Gambit, could be rescued, ransomed, released or killed depending on the battle.

Navarr.t: All three Navarr armies, including the newly mustered Isaella's Dance, led a merciless campaign of slaughter in Kahraman. Two were under a fog-and-ravens enchantment that magnified bloodlust and has now failed. Arhallogen has offered vague aid to the Navarr generals.

The Brass Coast.t: The Fire of the South and Red Wind Corsairs helped liberate Jade Range and raided Lasambrian supplies and plunder, alongside Fort Braydon's garrison. The Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills has been asked to rescue Catalina i Burna i Riqueza of the Damatian Cliffs.

The Marches.t: The Mournwolder renegade Steven of Sarcombe and his yegarra bill block fought for the Jotun and are leading the push to rescue the wounded at Rojota. Killing him would break his force.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's habit of avoiding needless bloodshed against the Jotun is cited as the model for letting the wounded Lasambrians withdraw.

Of earth and sky.o: In Autumn 384YE five Imperial armies, both Freeborn armies and all three Navarr armies, overwhelmed the Lasambrian Jotun in Kahraman. They reclaimed Jade Range and drove the orcs back into Gambit, even after the Lasambrians had wrecked the mountain roads to isolate Fort Braydon.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: Fort Braydon was the Lasambrian target. Its garrison, reinforced by brass constructs from Shikal, sallied out to join the counter-attack, but the broken roads mean the fort now defends only its own region.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: The Lasambrians were driven back into Gambit and are camped at the edge of the Sand Woods, with wounded trapped in Rojota and scattered across the region. A conjunction to Talaeiros offers a chance to ambush Catalina's captors.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: The Lasambrians massed on the drought-wilted Jade Range, then were broken at Nestor's Bounty and swept from the region, which the Empire has reclaimed.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: Collapsed roads and bridges cut Serra Briante off from Braydon's Jasse and Serra Damata, threatening access to the Great Mine of Briante and limiting the reach of local fortifications.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: Serra Damata was isolated by the sabotage, and Corazón raiders abducted Catalina i Burna i Riqueza, the legendary head quarry-woman of the Damatian Cliffs, a bitter blow to the quarry.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: news of Mathilda's sweeping victory in Bregasland has raised the spirits of Steven of Sarcombe's yegarra.

Kahraman.t: Imperial armies reclaimed Jade Range and are a third of the way to expelling the Lasambrians. The wrecked roads still isolate Braydon's Jasse, Serra Briante and Serra Damata from one another until they can be repaired.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the yegarra fighting for the Lasambrians are humans raised under Jotun rule in the Mourn, and the Jotun's hostility is traced back to the Mournwold's devastation.

Reinos.t: Corazón raiders are fleeing towards Reinos with plunder and the captive Catalina. They apparently plan to force her to open a white granite quarry on small deposits there.

Of tribute.d: The boons went to many claimants. The Royal Houses of Dawn won the Keeper of Tharim's Throne for Gui de Lusignan. The Hierro of Segura won food for their territory and Agramant's Cruel Blessing against Baroness Jaqueline duMoi in Kalino, which creates a difficult legal situation. A grim legion strode to Liaven's Glen to slay the Jotun. Axos claimed the Destruction of the Walls against the Court of the Fountain and a dream-plaguing hunt against Gabriel Barossa and the Wolves of War. Zamashka, Prince of Votika, a powerful Jarmish magician-prince, won several gifts, including ten more years of life. Tharim, the Bound King, judged the Solstice a success. Some boons have already taken effect and others will follow.

Dawn.t: The Royal Houses of Dawn won the boon of the Keeper of Tharim's Throne, and Gui de Lusignan is named as the chosen of Tharim.

Grendel.t: Grendel faces two hostile boons. Skathe's Vengeance will be directed at High Lady Suriad, Salt Lord of Dubhtraig, and the Raging Fire of Surut will fall on the enemies of the Masters of the High Peaks in Grendel-held Spiral.

Jotun.t: A grim legion fighting in the name of the tribes of Kallavesi and Suaq has strode forth to Liaven's Glen to slay the Jotun.

The Brass Coast.t: The sons and daughters of Naguerro and Hierro won food for an entire territory, to be delivered to Segura, and Agramant's Cruel Blessing. Their claim on a boon from Agramant creates a difficult legal situation.

Urizen.t: The descendants of the Sorcerer-Kings won the Destruction of the Walls, to fall on the Court of the Fountain in Redoubt at their command. This is a grave concern given that Axos was thought to be somewhat friendly to the Empire.

Of tribute.o: At the end of Winter 380YE, heralds of the eternals of Winter revealed which peoples had won the boons offered at the Winter Solstice in return for tribute of dragonbone. Thirteen hundred measures were given, most of it by the Empire, but Axos, Jarm and others also claimed powerful gifts.

Kalino.t: The Cruel Blessing of Agramant, claimed by the sons and daughters of Naguerro and Hierro, is to fall on Baroness Jaqueline duMoi, general of the Wolves of Kobol, in Kalino.

Redoubt.t: The Court of the Fountain in Redoubt is threatened by the Destruction of the Walls, a boon won by the descendants of the Sorcerer-Kings.

Segura.t: The people of Hierro in Segura are to receive enough food to fill the bellies of an entire territory, with the blessings of Agramant.

Spiral.t: The Raging Fire of Surut, won by the Masters of the High Peaks, is to fall on their enemies in Spiral.

Oh so intricate.d: Autumn magic protecting Bay of Catazar traders faded, leaving fleets from Tassato, Sarvos, the Brass Coast, Highguard and Urizen exposed to Grendel pirates. Citadels rose in several territories. Stars stayed missing over Semmerholm, the Barrens and Zenith, while penumbral veils covered Otkodov and several Imperial territories. The Icy Maw curse halved Segura's mana before fading. Meraud challenged magicians to feats of battle magic, Kimus sought volunteers for an experiment, and Leviathan arranged a meeting with the Lake Dwellers. Irra Harah renewed his bounty on two hearts. Sadogua, furious at the Druj, offered boons to Urizen and Highborn magicians and to Nicassia of the Citadel Guard.

Dawn.t: Semmerholm remained starless under a magnitude-fifty Night shroud, the Sherard Hunters raised Spring citadels in Axmure's forests, and Zadkiel de Coeurdefer still carries Irra Harah's bounty on his heart.

Druj.t: The Druj almost certainly maintain the star-shrouds over the Barrens, Zenith and Semmerholm, and their burning of the Halls of Knowledge enraged Sadogua, who broke his deal with the Ghulai and offered Imperial magicians power to devastate them.

Grendel.t: Grendel pirates had been thwarted by Autumn magic on the Bay of Catazar, but with that magic fading Imperial trading ships may again be at their mercy; a citadel was also raised in the hills and mountains of Spiral.

Highguard.t: Highborn fleets faced reduced trade as the protection on the Bay of Catazar faded, Necropolis lay under a penumbral veil, and Highborn magicians were offered Sadogua's boon of increased personal mana to use against the Druj.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven was among the lands starless in 381YE, and the Jotun presence in Sermersuaq may have caused the Lake Dwellers to rethink their attacks.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn fleets faced reduced trade, Madruga and Feroz lay under penumbral veils, a citadel rose in Kahraman, Segura suffered the Icy Maw curse, and Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza remains under Irra Harah's bounty.

The League.t: Fleets from Tassato and Sarvos faced reduced trade, Sarvos and Temeschwar lay under penumbral veils, and the Sussivari Frost Coven wove a misty citadel over Holberg.

The Marches.t: Henry Ward of Upwold was said to have paid the price demanded by Irra Harah, and Sadogua wished to speak privately with the three cleverest magicians of the Marches.

Thule.t: A penumbral veil was reportedly drawn over Urdur in Thule-held Otkodov, though it is unclear whether Nithoggir, Sküld or Verthandi are similarly veiled.

Urizen.t: Urizen fleets faced reduced trade, Redoubt and Morrow were veiled and fortified, and Morrow's veil resisted an attempt to steal its stars; Sadogua offered Urizen magicians mana and forged boons, and offered Nicassia the chance to have him devour parts of the Citadel Guard's cyclic magic.

Wintermark.t: Citadels rose over Kallavesa and Hahnmark, and Leviathan arranged for Tarqeq Icetongue and up to two Icewalkers to meet the mysterious Lake Dwellers linked to Sermersuaq.

Oh so intricate.o: In Autumn 382YE the magic that had shielded Imperial traders from Grendel pirates faded, citadels were conjured across the Empire, and Druj star-shrouds and Imperial veils persisted. A curse struck Segura, and eternals including Meraud, Kimus, Leviathan, Irra Harah and Sadogua made offers and challenges, Sadogua raging at the Druj burning of the Halls of Knowledge.

Otkodov/Nithoggir.t: Mentioned in passing: it is not yet clear whether the penumbral veil also covers Nithoggir.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Mentioned in passing: it is not yet clear whether the penumbral veil also covers Sküld.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: Merchants report the ritual Drawing the Penumbral Veil has been worked over Urdur, hindering scrying there.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: The Sherard Hunters infused Axmure's forests with Spring magic, raising a protective citadel until the Autumn Equinox.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Autumn magic that slowed Grendel pirates and sped Imperial ships faded as the Equinox approached, leaving traders exposed unless it is renewed.

Feroz.t: A penumbral veil drawn during the Summer Solstice warps the stars into a scrying-blocking shroud, bringing heavy dark fog.

Hahnmark.t: A frozen citadel of stone and ice was raised in Hahnmark's hills and mountains, protecting the land until the Autumn Equinox.

Holberg.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven wove mists over Holberg's marshes, raising a protective citadel until the Equinox.

Kahraman.t: A citadel of stone and ice was conjured in Kahraman's hills and mountains, offering safe haven while it stood.

Kallavesa.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a misty marsh citadel over Kallavesa that faded with the Autumn Equinox.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: the stars were absent over Liathaven for much of 381YE.

Madruga.t: A ritual penumbral veil hides Madruga's stars from scrying and shrouds the territory in dark fog.

Morrow.t: Morrow is veiled and was fortified with a citadel; an attempt to steal its stars after the Summer Solstice failed against the Urizen veil, though naga there still feel the urge to secrecy.

Necropolis.t: A penumbral veil drawn over Necropolis interferes with scrying and brings heavy, dark fog.

Otkodov.t: A penumbral veil has reportedly been worked over Urdur, but whether the rest of Otkodov is veiled remains unclear without scrying.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt lies under a penumbral veil and also gained a citadel of stone and ice in its hills.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos fleets faced reduced trade as the Bay of Catazar protection faded, and a penumbral veil now shrouds the territory.

Segura.t: The Icy Maw curse brought a damp, maddening summer, halved mana production and ruined some minor regio, but also smoothed the post-earthquake magical disruption before fading by the Equinox.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm's stars remain stolen under a magnitude-fifty Night shroud expected to last until near Winter 382YE, while citadels rose in its forests and hills.

Sermersuaq.t: Leviathan arranged for Tarqeq Icetongue to meet the Lake Dwellers, possibly connected to the drowned dead that once attacked the territory and its recent rising dead.

Spiral.t: A citadel of stone and ice was raised in the hills and mountains of Spiral.

Tassato.t: Tassato's fleets faced reduced trade production as the magic protecting them from Grendel pirates faded.

Temeschwar.t: A penumbral veil drawn during the Summer Solstice obscures Temeschwar's stars and blankets it in dark fog.

The Barrens.t: The stars remain missing over the Barrens, impeding scrying, with the shroud expected to last until shortly before Winter 382YE.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Henry Ward of Upwold is said to have paid the price for Irra Harah's bounty.

Verthandi.t: Mentioned in passing: it is unclear whether the penumbral veil over Urdur also lies over Verthandi.

Zenith.t: The stars vanished over Zenith before the Spring Equinox, and the shroud is expected to last until the Spring Equinox 383YE unless removed or reinforced.

Old blue banners dancing.d: Most Jotun armies left Bregasland for Hordalant, leaving the Howling Night, Iron Host, Shield of the Mountain, Southern Bear and the Bear Who Swims to hold it. The Strong Reeds and Bounders were joined by the Narwhal's Spear, Autumn Hammers, Fire of the South and Burning Falcon. Nearly three thousand Imperial soldiers and at least two thousand Jotun died. Unexplained magic raised a woodland on the Gravenmarch–Rushes border, and landskeepers fear its link to Graven Rock. A battle opportunity followed in the Grey Fens: stop ghodi Sunne Astar taking the Ullsmere Rock to Hordalant, banish the Grey Walker shades, and possibly rescue Friar Bloughton of House Brawness.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the only link is a note that the Fire of the South fought alongside the Knights of Glory in Sarangrave the previous Summer.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: uneasy landskeepers looked south-east towards Casinea and Anvil as they muttered about the strange forest.

Jotun.t: The Jotun pulled most of their forces back to Hordalant and lost Gravenmarch, with at least two thousand dead, but five armies still held the rest of Bregasland. Ghodi Sunne Astar sought the Ullsmere Rock to strengthen the Howling Night.

The Marches.t: Led by the Strong Reeds and Bounders, the Marchers reclaimed Gravenmarch as a beachhead in Bregasland, while the Drakes went to defend Mitwold. They were also offered a chance to reopen talks with the once-rebellious House Brawness.

Wintermark.t: The Narwhal's Spear marched south from Skallahn and fought at the right hand of the final Imperial advance. Its general was given a chance to seize Jotun supplies bound for the Southern Bear, while the Bloodcloaks fell back to Hahnmark.

Old blue banners dancing.o: In Spring 388YE six Imperial armies drove the Jotun out of Gravenmarch in Bregasland after a costly campaign, pushing into the edge of the Rushes. Graven Rock roared during the final battle, and overnight a forest grew from the bodies of the fallen.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: Gravenmarch was liberated after brutal fighting beneath Graven Rock, which roared during the final battle. A forest now stands in its west, grown from the fallen.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: Jotun warriors dragged away the Ullsmere Rock at Drayham Mere, releasing the Grey Walker shades. The region will become haunted unless the stone is restored.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: House Brawness, still resentful and rebellious, keeps to its farm here. Rescuing its friar could open talks to resolve the region's rebellious spirit.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bounders' general named the Ottermire as a target, and Helma Skutasdóttir's warband was rooting out Bregas rebels in Ottery.

Bregasland/The Rushes.t: The Empire pushed the Jotun back into the Rushes and made some headway there, and a supernatural woodland rose overnight along its border with Gravenmarch.

Hordalant/Vallorberg.t: Ghodi Sunne Astar intended to place the Ullsmere Rock in Vallorberg's kirkja sacred to Ulven, believing it would raise the fighting spirit of the Howling Night.

Bregasland.t: Six Imperial armies fought five Jotun armies here and liberated Gravenmarch at a cost of thousands of lives. The rest of the territory, including the Rushes and the Grey Fens, remained contested.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: landskeepers cast baleful glances towards Casinea and Anvil after the forest appeared.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bloodcloaks fell back to Hahnmark from Bregasland.

Hordalant.t: Most of the Jotun armies withdrawn from Bregasland raced west to Hordalant, and ghodi Sunne Astar planned to drag the Ullsmere Rock there.

Mitwold.t: Four Jotun armies returned from Mitwold to Bregasland while Lasambrian forces held the territory. The Drakes answered the call to defend it against the unexpected invasion.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the warband of Yantan Tethrason of Reinos, a former Lasambrian goatherd, fought for the Jotun in the south of Bregasland.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South last fought alongside the Knights of Glory in Sarangrave during the Summer.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial armies that had been attacking in Skallahn moved south to Bregasland, the Burning Falcon having been denied a true battle there.

Old ways.d: With the Basilica of Seven Doors refurbished and the Highborn Speaker restored, several opportunities were proposed. The bishops of Sarvos suggested refurbishing Capodomus Cathedral to create a title guiding the League assembly, with its name still disputed between Archbishop, Speaker or Bishop. Wintermark priests proposed rebuilding the Hall of Rund in Kallavesa, possibly as the seat of the Speaker of the Crows. Abbot Matilda of Becktunn urged a seminary honouring the Exemplar Margaret of Meade to help Marchers win Imperial titles. Varushkan wise ones suggested expanding the Tender of the Hearth's duties by Senate motion. Other assemblies, such as Dawn and Navarr, might pursue similar titles through statements of principle. The opportunities remain open until at least the Autumn Equinox.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the troubadours of Dawn were given as an example of an assembly that might seek a First Troubadour seated at Laroc Cathedral.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel were recalled as having stolen Capodomus Cathedral's artworks and damaged it during the sack of Sarvos.

Highguard.t: The restored Speaker of the Highborn Assembly, custodian of the Basilica of Seven Doors, became the model that other national assemblies now considered copying.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr assembly was suggested as one that might announce the intent to create a Priests' Brand.

The League.t: League bishops proposed refurbishing Capodomus Cathedral to create a title guiding the League assembly. That title would carry 20 Synod votes, 10 liao and 7 crowns each season, though priests continued to squabble over what it should be called.

The Marches.t: Abbot Matilda proposed building the Seminary of Margaret's Oak, whose prior would encourage and help Marchers win Imperial titles and revive the forgotten legacy of the Exemplar Margaret of Meade.

Varushka.t: Varushkan wise ones suggested a Senate motion to make the Tender of the Hearth an annual national assembly appointment. The expanded role would guide the assembly and would gain an extra dose of liao and two extra votes.

Wintermark.t: Amid renewed interest in priests acting in the Synod, Wintermark could rebuild the Hall of Rund to create a title guiding its assembly with 18 liao. That title might become an official Speaker of the Crows advising the Thane's Council.

Old ways.o: Following the restoration of the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly in Summer 383YE, other national assemblies began considering similar leadership titles. Specific opportunities emerged for the League, Wintermark, the Marches and Varushka.

Bastion.t: The refurbished Basilica of Seven Doors in Bastion, completed shortly before the Summer Solstice, restored the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly to prominence.

Kallavesa.t: The ancient Hall of Rund in Rundhal, birthplace of the stormcrow tradition, could be rebuilt upwards with weirwood and white granite to house all Wintermark's priests once more.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: wise ones from Karov were among those suggesting the Tender of the Hearth's responsibilities be expanded.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: wise ones from Karsk were among those suggesting the Tender of the Hearth's responsibilities be expanded.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Margaret of Meade was recalled as having served as Senator for Mitwold on and off for two decades.

Sarvos.t: Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos, damaged and looted in the Grendel sack, could be refurbished as the seat of the League assembly's new leader and filled with new artwork from across the League.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Margaret of Meade argued that cities such as Tassato were luring skilled yeomen away from the Marches.

Volodmartz.t: Mentioned in passing: wise ones from Volodmartz were among those suggesting the Tender of the Hearth's responsibilities be expanded.

On southern sands.d: Urizen magicians laid storms, healing waters, Summer citadels and Autumn enchantments across Redoubt. The Citadel Guard, Towerjacks and Northern Eagle then prepared its defence. A Grendel armada raided the coast and made a full assault on Elos, which was driven back. A second, chaotic attack by the Children of Wrecks followed, including former Freeborn, League and Marcher fighters, and it too was repulsed. The defenders of the Lighthouse at Nikephoros collapsed it into the sea rather than let it fall. Redoubt stayed under Imperial control, and the Towerjacks left temporary fortifications in Naris. Further wreckers raided the interior, which set up a solstice battle opportunity to protect the Ribbon of Salt and Visten.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Axe is named among the armies that invaded Ayereed in an earlier season, in the background to the Ayereed conjunction.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: their poisoning of the Lower Tarn Valley cost the Northern Eagle nearly two hundred soldiers, and the Children of Wrecks' savagery is compared to theirs.

Grendel.t: Their Broken Shore armada raided Redoubt and threw its full strength at Elos, but was forced to retreat without a foothold and lost ships to the storms and to Children of Wrecks pursuers. Separately, a Grendel maistir was sent to fund mercenaries to retake the Imperial foothold in Ayereed.

Highguard.t: Necropolis would have been threatened had Elos fallen. The Highborn traitor Ezhabbenar of Hedrossan is among the turncoats to be slain at Visten Head, and if he escapes the wreckers could plunder Highguard lands.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven, which they hold, is named only as the home of the lost striding that the traitor Ioan Bloodstride came from.

Navarr.t: The armies sent to Redoubt marched out of war-torn Therunin. The Navarr traitor Ioan Bloodstride, who joined Siakha's forces at Meade, is a target at Visten Head; if he escapes, the wreckers could raid Navarr lands.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel force included ships that assaulted Madruga and burned Siroc, and ex-Freeborn fought among the Children of Wrecks and the wreckers who raided the Spire of the Wealdawn.

The League.t: The Towerjacks fortified the Redoubt coast and Elos Harbour, held the docks against both assaults and left temporary fortifications across Naris. League traitors fought among the raiders, and the Uccelini Maurizia Spada di Sarvos is a target at Visten Head.

The Marches.t: Perhaps half a dozen Marcher warbands, their livery removed, fought with the Children of Wrecks at Elos. This soured hopes that the recent conflict with the Marches had been laid to rest.

Urizen.t: Redoubt was defended by the Citadel Guard and Urizen magic, and the Assembly's warning helped prepare its people. Elos was damaged, the Lighthouse at Nikephoros was destroyed and the Littilian Fast was sacked, but the territory remains fully under Imperial control.

On southern sands.o: In Winter 386YE the Grendel and then the Children of Wrecks attacked the southern coast of Redoubt. Three Imperial armies, backed by heavy Imperial magic, repulsed both assaults on the harbour of Elos, but at a steep cost.

Ayereed/Gainmeachdubh.t: Its Grendel lord sent Maistir Varden, with a guard of Grendel and Asaveans, to pay mercenaries to retake the Imperial foothold in Ayereed.

Ayereed/Petrified Forest.t: The Empire's foothold and newly begun smugglers' cove here are the target of the mercenaries Maistir Varden has been sent to hire.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the page refers only to the earlier Grendel assault on Madruga.

Necropolis/Hedrossan.t: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn traitor Ezhabbenar of Hedrossan is one of five turncoats to be killed at Visten Head.

Redoubt/Limus.t: A cohort of Autumn constructs led by minotaurs strengthened the garrison of Cargo, whose walls burned with sigils binding them to Shikal. The Spring storms reached even here.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Naris bore the Grendel landings and both battles of Elos, and the Lighthouse at Nikephoros was destroyed. The Towerjacks left a temporary fortification here that fades by the end of Summer 387YE.

Redoubt/Optarion.t: Autumn constructs reinforced the Court of the White Fountain, to the unease of its koboldi. Later, wreckers who had sacked the Littilian Fast headed into Optarion.

Redoubt/Siluri.t: A Summer citadel of pale stone and dark ice, garrisoned by bear-like heralds, rose on Mount Siluri, and the Citadel Guard marched south through the region to the coast.

Redoubt/Tomari.t: The Northern Eagle defeated Black Eels raiding the Brilliant Star. Wreckers later landed in southern Tomari and sacked the Littilian Fast.

Redoubt/Willstone.t: Mentioned in passing: the Spring storms were felt as far north as Willstone.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Northern Eagle lost nearly two hundred soldiers marching through this Druj-poisoned vale, the only route that would get them to Redoubt in time.

Ayereed.t: The Lord of Gainmeachdubh sent Maistir Varden with funds to pay mercenaries to retake the Empire's foothold and destroy the new smugglers' cove. The Imperial Spymaster, Bernard Dugdale, is charged with killing him and may free an unknown captive in his company.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Grendel armada came at Redoubt from the open sea, raising fears that it had crossed the heart of the Bay. Both the Grendel and the Children of Wrecks retreated into its deep waters, fighting each other as they went.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks' fortification work is credited to Holbergian ingenuity.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: the traitor Ioan Bloodstride is described as a refugee from a lost striding in Liathaven.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel force that attacked Redoubt included ships and soldiers that had earlier assaulted Madruga.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: Ayereed is described as the territory to the south of Mareave.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: not named; the only Marcher link is the disguised Marcher warbands at Elos, who were thought to intend returning to the Marches.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard marched south out of Morrow, and the Towerjacks and Northern Eagle passed through it by Highwatch on their way to Redoubt.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel beachhead at Elos would have threatened Necropolis as well as Redoubt.

Redoubt.t: Wrapped in Imperial curses, healing waters and magical fortifications, Redoubt saw off the Grendel and the Children of Wrecks and remains fully under Imperial control. It suffered casualties, storm damage, reduced fleet and ministry income and odd effects on farms, herb gardens and forests.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: lingering ill-feeling over Spiral is noted, as is Redoubt's readiness for attack from that direction.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks and Northern Eagle left war-torn Therunin to reinforce Redoubt.

On the outside looking inside.d: The new Consulate raised the Imperial Consul's prestige, and the Senate could now strip the Fleet Master of representing the Empire to the Grendel. The Sumaah Symposium shrank to one injured cardinal, Cosatti, after food poisoning. Asavean hostility grew, and Axou anger over the Tamazi cut trade at the Black Sails Quay, though the Elosian Docks, Kantor enclave and House of Spirits were completed. The Commonwealth built the Lyceum Schloss and offered four rituals to the Conclave. Jarm gave the Senate until Summer to disavow war or lose all ties. A Bregasland delegation sought the Marchers, and a conjunction offered a chance to rescue magistrate Kaisa Kaisasbarn from captors near Kabalai Campo.

Dawn.t: The devout Free Folk exiles have settled at Caer Faucon under the Lady of the Proffered Hand, and some came to Anvil to question Imperial priests about why their Way is considered wrong.

Grendel.t: With the Consulate complete, the Senate could remove the Imperial Fleet Master's role as representative to the Grendel, forcing them to deal with the Imperial Consul; mutual sanctions still hamper trade with Oran.

Highguard.t: Highborn congregation leaders were to appoint the first Bursar of the Axou House of Spirits in Mareholm, while Necropolis saw falling Axou trade at the Black Sails Quay and received the Sumaah list of inspirations at its embassy.

Imperial Orcs.t: Fal of the Imperial Orcs, as Imperial Consul, gained a new Consulate, greater standing and authority over the Bregasland delegation, while Ashborn Pakt faced worsening relations as Ambassador to Asavea.

Jotun.t: The Lasambrian Jotun pulled back from Kahraman into Reinos, and the Bregasland delegation sent by their human ally Mathilda Fisher could technically be seen as representing the Jotun.

Navarr.t: Gelert Ashborn, the Navarr Ambassador to Jarm, faced a Jarmish ultimatum blamed on a lack of Imperial correspondence, and a Navarr striding escorted Cardinal Cosatti to Anvil.

The Brass Coast.t: Magistrates pursued Freeborn and Faraden smugglers in Segura while the National Assembly stayed silent. The Commonwealth built the Lyceum Schloss in Madruga, and the Marracossan exiles in Trajadoz sought formal recognition.

The League.t: Tassato gained the Imperial Consulate but its Jarmish lodge and mana exchange were threatened by the ultimatum, while in Sarvos the Sarcophan enclave prospered and the Cavabianca Docks' Asavean backers came under pressure.

The Marches.t: A delegation from Mathilda Fisher in Bregasland arrived wishing to speak first with Marchers and the Bregas, and Faraden merchants at Moonwater Hall in Upwold obstructed the smuggling inquiry.

Thule.t: The Thule fought alongside Imperial armies in Sermersuaq and claimed Miechernya and Webwood under treaty, raising a query about army numbers and offering a meeting via the Hall of Worlds.

Urizen.t: The Elosian Docks were completed on the Redoubt coast, Urizen's places of learning expected Axou students, and Urizeni Ambassador Tarquinius Ankarien faced public Axou anger.

Varushka.t: Varushka saw Miechernya in Miekarova and Webwood in Ossium pass to Thule control under the treaty, and Varushkan Ambassador Yevgeni Katzev handled continued peace with Otkodov.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark magistrate Kaisa Kaisasbarn was captured while investigating smugglers, prompting a rescue conjunction, and Thanmir Hrafnar serves as Ambassador to the friendly Sarcophan Delves.

On the outside looking inside.o: In Spring 384YE the Empire's foreign relations were in flux: the Imperial Consulate was completed in Tassato, the Liberty Pact delegates gathered at Anvil, the Principalities of Jarm issued an ultimatum, and the Thule took regions ceded to them by treaty.

Casinea/Casfall.t: The Sumaah Symposium delegation was struck down with food poisoning while resting at Casca's Fall, leaving only Cardinal Cosatti to continue.

Casinea/Mareholm.t: The Axou House of Spirits was completed near the Silent Sentinel, with its first students expected the following month.

Miekarova/Miechernya.t: Thule armies took control of Miechernya, ceded to them by treaty in return for aid in Sermersuaq.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Thule armies took control of Webwood, ceded to them under the treaty.

Astolat.t: The Asavean Free Folk have moved to Caer Faucon and are settling in easily beside their Dawnish neighbours.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is not named on the page and is linked only through the maritime trade it describes.

Bregasland.t: After the Yegarra and Jotun were beaten at Miresend, Mathilda Fisher remained at Fisher's Rock and sent a delegation to Anvil to speak with the Bregas.

Casinea.t: The Axou House of Spirits, a campus of the Halls of Maykop, was completed in Mareholm, and the Sumaah delegation fell ill at Casca's Fall.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel control of Feroz is cited as one reason few Suranni merchants trade north.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the University of Holberg is among the institutions expecting Axou students.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the presence of the Lasambrian Jotun in Kahraman slowed the magistrates' smuggling investigation.

Madruga.t: Commonwealth workers built the fortified Lyceum Schloss on the Isle of the Lyceum, improving its ability to codify army enchantments, with scholars due after the Equinox.

Miekarova.t: Thule armies moved in to claim Miechernya, ceded to them under the treaty that secured their aid.

Necropolis.t: Angry Axou traders shunned the Black Sails Quay, worsening its liao deals, while the Sumaah list of inspirations was lodged at the Imperial Embassy there.

Ossium.t: Thule armies moved in to claim Webwood under the terms of the treaty.

Otkodov.t: The Empire remained at peace with the Thule of Otkodov, who proposed talks on the Sermersuaq war in Lashonar's caucus forum.

Redoubt.t: The Axou Elosian Docks were completed on the Redoubt coast, with an associated Imperial title due for appointment.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian Jotun were seen retreating back into Reinos.

Sarvos.t: The new Sarcophan enclave was thriving, while the Asavean families backing the Cavabianca Docks were pressured to stop trading with the Empire.

Segura.t: Magistrates were investigating a smuggling ring here, Suranni traders reported the Arav purge, and magistrate Kaisa Kaisasbarn vanished nearby.

Sermersuaq.t: Three Thule armies fought alongside Imperial armies, and the Thule queried whether the treaty required them always to be outnumbered there.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: listed only in further reading on the Grendel in Spiral.

Tassato.t: The Imperial Consulate was completed here, but the Jarmish lodge and the extra mana at the Tassato Mana Exchange would be lost if Jarm severed ties.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Faraden merchants using the Moonwater Hall enclave were described as uncooperative with the magistrates.

On the road ahead.d: Anduz, built from the ruins of a pre-Imperial city and sacked by the Lasambrians in 363YE, faced four options. The Brazen Propylaeum would make it the City of Adventure and inspire Trailblazers. The Market of a Thousand Sails would make it the City of Deals with Hawkers. The Burning Agora, a torchlit space for debate proposed partly as a counterweight to fears of Highborn orthodoxy, would make it the City of Passions with Firebrands. Dust, Glass and Flame would combine all three with an ilium-enchanted fountain, making it the City of Wonders, but it needed a foundational artwork and a far larger cost. If nothing was built, Anduzjasse would gain the ruins quality as the City of Stones.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: their attempt to catch the Red Wind Corsairs is said to have been countered by Freeborn cunning.

Highguard.t: Some Freeborn, especially the Riquezans, feared the Highborn might use the Grand Inspiration of the Way to push a rigidly orthodox doctrine, and the Burning Agora was proposed as a counterweight to that.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun forces are noted as still pressing into the Marches.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn National Assembly passed the mandates for the Cities of Deals, Passions and Wonders, which could create the Hawker and Firebrand archetypes once their edifices are built. Work then began on the costly Dust, Glass and Flame project to remake Anduz.

On the road ahead.o: Freed for once from immediate threat, the people of Anduz in Segura sought a new future for their ruined city, and the Brass Coast was offered four edifice commissions, each paired with a Freeborn National Assembly mandate, that could recast Anduz's fate. The Assembly passed the mandates for the Cities of Deals, Passions and Wonders, and construction of the grand City of Wonders project began in Summer 388YE.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni are said to have laid claim to the Cazar Straits.

Segura/Anduzjasse.t: Anduzjasse was offered edifices that would fix its city's fate, and building began on Dust, Glass and Flame, combining the Propylaeum, the Market of a Thousand Sails, the Burning Agora and an enchanted Fountain of Wonders. If work stalls for a year, the region instead gains the ruins quality.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Segura is described as almost as far from Bastion as one can get and still be in the Empire, making it a fitting haven for free debate.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni are noted to have claimed the Cazar Straits in Feroz, while showing no sign of attacking the mainland.

Segura.t: Segura, already enjoying prosperity from the Zemress Islanders and the restored Towers of Anduz, saw its chief city set on course to become the City of Wonders, with construction beginning in Summer 388YE.

On wings aspire.d: Summer heralds spread conflicting stories that Hayaak's Forest of Arden has become far more dangerous, whether through conquest, illness or exile. Jaheris alone is said to know the truth and may discuss it with an Imperial representative at the Spring Equinox. Roshanwe offered ten vials of prismatic ink for each Whisper Gallery pawn cursed with All the World in a Grain of Sand, and sought to send a herald to Kyra Halcyon Spire. The Sussivari Frost Coven raised Night citadels in Kallavesa and Bregasland. Two Cathan Canae citadels left garrisoned soldiers uneasy. The starless shroud persisted except in Urizen and Skarsind, where the Wanderer aligned with the Chalice, a sign of healing, reflection and prophecy.

Dawn.t: Gossip about the transformed Forest of Arden was most common in Dawn, especially among visitors to Spiral Castle, and Jaheris let it be known there that he might share secrets at the Equinox.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: devastating magical storms harried Grendel navies off the coasts of Redoubt and Spiral.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Casinea remained under the starless shroud, so naga visiting Anvil would still feel their urge towards subtlety and secrecy strengthened.

Imperial Orcs.t: Stars returned over the Imperial Orc territory of Skarsind, freeing its naga from the shroud's influence and revealing the Wanderer's conjunction with the Chalice.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: a host of unliving husks was unleashed on the Jotun in Liathaven, and the Frost Coven's citadels were raised as protection against Jotun attack.

The Brass Coast.t: An ice-and-stone citadel of Cathan Canae rose over newly liberated Serra Damata, Roshanwe's heralds visited the Lyceum in Madruga, and the Brass Coast knows the Chalice as the Mirror Cup, linked to prophecy and foretelling dooms or triumphs.

The Marches.t: In Bregasland's North Fens a glowing dome of mist filled with huge iridescent butterflies sheltered Bounder patrols, though it was found completely empty when they returned seeking gloaming cocoons.

Urizen.t: Stars were restored across all of Urizen, showing the Wanderer aligned with the Chalice, while Roshanwe's heralds visited the Halls of Knowledge in Zenith and a Cathan Canae citadel rose in Tomari.

Varushka.t: Rumours about the Forest of Arden spread widely in Varushka among the heralds of the Summer Mage who visit the college there.

Wintermark.t: Husks were raised to fight alongside a Wintermark army, and the Sussivari Frost Coven used Night magic to protect the marshes of Kallavesa and Bregasland from the Jotun.

On wings aspire.o: In Spring 381YE the Winds of Fortune brought rumours of upheaval in the Summer realm's Forest of Arden, a bounty from the eternal Roshanwe on pawns of the Whisper Gallery, a strange butterfly-filled citadel in Bregasland's marshes, and a conjunction of the Wanderer with the Chalice wherever stars still shone.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: The glowing butterfly dome was woven in North Fens, leaving sheltering Bounders coated in alabaster dust, but it was empty of creatures and cocoons by the Spring Equinox.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: A Cathan Canae citadel of ice and stone rose overlooking newly liberated Serra Damata, unsettling the soldiers who took refuge in its empty chambers.

Redoubt/Tomari.t: A second ungarrisoned Cathan Canae citadel rose in Tomari, where soldiers alone in its cold halls reported a strong sense of unease.

Bregasland.t: The Frost Coven's citadel in Bregasland, a phosphorescent dome of silver mist full of giant butterflies, offered shelter to patrolling Bounders, though no enemy attacked.

Casinea.t: Casinea remained without stars, so naga coming to Anvil would still find their urge towards secretiveness greatly strengthened.

Kahraman.t: A citadel of ice and stone from Cathan Canae appeared, ungarrisoned, overlooking newly liberated Serra Damata, and soldiers sheltering there felt uneasy in its empty halls.

Kallavesa.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven warped Kallavesa's marshes with Night magic to provide protection from the Jotun, though no enemy force attacked.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: a host of unliving husks was unleashed to fall upon the Jotun in Liathaven.

Madruga.t: Heralds of Roshanwe visited the Lyceum in Madruga to deliver her offer of reward for cursing pawns of the Whisper Gallery.

Redoubt.t: A Cathan Canae citadel rose in Tomari, and magical storms harried Grendel navies off Redoubt's coast.

Skarsind.t: The stars were restored over Skarsind, lifting the shroud's influence on its naga and revealing the Wanderer's alignment with the Chalice.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: devastating magical storms harried Grendel navies off the coast of Spiral.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name Weirwater, but notes that visitors to Dawn's Spiral Castle heard much gossip about the Forest of Arden.

Zenith.t: Roshanwe's heralds visited the Halls of Knowledge in Zenith, urging action against the Whisper Gallery's agents, and Zenith shared in Urizen's restored stars.

One last song.d: Heroes from every nation except the Imperial Orcs, aided by Great Forest Orcs and Highborn grey pilgrims, cleared the Druj from Elerael and Boar's Dell and set sentries along the borders. In Dark Ranging they slew a herald of Yaw'nagrah bound with the living heads of Heirs magicians. Others braved gardens of abomination for Spring-charged fruit. A weirwood Sanctuary Grove yielded the last singing stone, claimed by the Navarr. In Terunael explorers found a Wintermark-style runeforge, and some reached the vallornheart. The recovered lore will cut six months from the Great Library of Hacynian's vallorn research, if the library is built. The spent cauldron remains at the Broch.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: husks of Dawnish questing knights were found in the vallorn, and the Great Forest Orcs fought beside any Imperial force except perhaps the Dawnish.

Druj.t: Druj bands that had slipped into Brocéliande from the Barrens were scoured from Elerael and Boar's Dell by many small Imperial units, with scores killed and the rest fleeing east.

Highguard.t: Grey pilgrims and lay followers of the Way, urged on by a Highborn Assembly motion backed with liao, brought supplies and fighters to the assault on the Heirs' stronghold. Supporting congregations will receive herbs brought back by returning pilgrims.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: they were the only Imperial nation with no champions on the expedition.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, but the last remnants of the Heirs of Terunael were said to be hiding in Liathaven, which they hold.

Navarr.t: Navarr champions led the exploration, kept Rhianos' cauldron at the Broch as a monument, and claimed the last singing stone of Terunael from the Sanctuary Grove. Some of their number became perhaps the first brands, thorns or vates ever to look upon a vallornheart.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn hero travelled all the way from Madruga to join the exploration.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: League heroes who reached Terunael saw in the ruined city an echo of Sarvos and Temeschwar.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark heroes found a ruined building in western Terunael marked with Wintermark runes, holding what may be the remains of a runeforge like those of Skarsind and Gildenheim. Its presence there remains an unsolved mystery.

One last song.o: In Winter 384YE more than three hundred Imperial champions, sustained by Rhianos' golden cauldron at the Broch, explored the vallorn of Brocéliande. They drove out the Druj, destroyed the last Heirs of Terunael stronghold, reached the ruins of Terunael and looked upon its vallornheart before the cauldron's power faded.

Brocéliande/Black Boughs.t: The Broch in Black Boughs was the expedition's base, where the heralds of Rhianos served the cauldron's soup. The spent cauldron remains there in Navarr keeping as a monument.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: The Druj were driven out of Boar's Dell with help from Great Forest Orcs who once lived there. Sentries now watch its borders, and a path through the vallorn links it to Elerael.

Brocéliande/Dark Ranging.t: The hidden Heirs of Terunael stronghold in Dark Ranging was stormed and its castellan, a herald of Yaw'nagrah bound with living Heirs magicians, was destroyed. The woven fortress then unravelled.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Elerael was cleared of Druj and guarded with sentry posts, and paths were carved so small groups could pass safely to Boar's Dell or the Broch.

Brocéliande/Terunael.t: Explorers breached the ruined city of Terunael, finding the Wintermark-style runeforge and a mysterious step-pyramid. Some pressed on to look upon the vallornheart itself.

Brocéliande/Vale's Lament.t: A battlefield in eastern Vale's Lament, where Highborn and Heirs had destroyed each other, yielded clues that led to the Heirs' hidden stronghold.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn-free weirwood grove recalled a similar discovery made when the Westwood was cleansed.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: Mentioned in passing: it appears only in further reading, through a later report of an expedition to Bendol.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat farmers had reported Spring-steeped plants growing where the vallorn has touched, which raised the possibility of cultivating the vallorn fruit.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn explorers saw in Terunael's ruin an echo of what could befall Bastion.

Brocéliande.t: Heroes swept the Druj from the territory, opened temporary paths through the vallorn and destroyed the last Heirs stronghold. They also explored the gardens of abomination, the Sanctuary Grove and the ruins of Terunael, carrying out great treasure and lore before withdrawing as Winter came.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea farmers had reported eerie Spring-steeped plants in vallorn-touched places, suggesting the fruit might be grown there.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the Heirs of Terunael were earlier driven from Hercynia, and Great Forest Orcs had faced abominations there.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: the last scattered Heirs of Terunael hide in Liathaven, and the weirwood sanctuary recalled one found when the Westwood was cleansed.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn hero came from Madruga to join the expedition.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: no Navarr had looked upon a vallornheart since the destruction of Miaren's.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold farmers had spoken of Spring-steeped plants in vallorn-touched places, where the vallorn fruit might be cultivated.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: it appears only in further reading, through a later expedition to Bendol.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: League heroes saw in ruined Terunael an echo of Sarvos.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the runeforge-like ruin in Terunael struck explorers as eerily reminiscent of the runeforge beneath Skarsind.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Terunael's walls, when whole, would have equalled those of modern Temeschwar.

The Barrens.t: Druj had been slipping into Brocéliande from the Barrens, and the survivors fled back east towards it. New sentry posts now watch the border.

Therunin.t: The Senator for Therunin rallied the Great Forest Orcs who now live in Therunin, and their hunters, scouts and healers fought alongside the Imperial heroes.

One more day's light.d: A mutilated yeofolk, Ramsey, was released to carry a Druj ultimatum to Semmerholm. For every army attacking a Druj territory, one in ten Dawnish prisoners in Dawnguard would be killed, and the children held at Drycastle would lose their protection. Healed by a Dawnish witch, Ramsey reported that the children were kept in relative comfort while the adults were worked mercilessly. After the Conclave reconciled with Irra Harah and granted it amity, its agents, the Children of Papa Otec, prepared hidden routes for a mission of mercy. Military units, and possibly the Winter Sun or Seventh Wave, could support it, with rescues growing with strength. A Sentinel Gate strike on Dourfell Chase could bolster the effort.

Dawn.t: Dawn's captive people in Dawnguard faced Druj threats of torture and death for every Imperial attack. The foray offered a chance to free the children at Drycastle and up to two-fifths of those taken when Drycastle fell.

Druj.t: The Druj used hostages as leverage to deter invasion and grew crueller to their slaves. The proposed foray threatened their hold on prisoners, their watch on the Eaves of Peytaht and production at the Fangs mithril mine.

Highguard.t: The Seventh Wave could commit half its strength to the foray while defending an Imperial territory, gaining a detailed military report on the Barrens. Reikos would receive those rescued through the Forest of Peytaht.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Winter Sun could support the foray instead of escorting the orcs. If a rebel band formed in the Barrens, the rebels would see the Imperial Orcs, and the Winter Sun's general especially, as allies.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: most orc slaves freed in a full-strength raid would be expected to join their Great Forest cousins in Navarr-held Therunin.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: hare-marked agents of Irra Harah were recalled as having aided refugees of the Mournwold a few years earlier.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the earlier Druj peace overture to the Urizen had been soundly rebuffed, and the Urizen are noted as knowing Druj oppression.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj message came after their armies retreated from Varushkan-held Ossium, which they said they would leave to the Empire for now.

One more day's light.o: In Spring 383YE the Druj threatened to torture and kill Dawnish prisoners in Dawnguard if any Imperial army entered the Mallum. At the same time, the Spring eternal Irra Harah, newly granted amity, offered secret routes for a raid into the Barrens to rescue the children of Dawn and other slaves.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: With at least 15,000 strength, the foray could free slaves held in Bitter Strand.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: The Dawnish children held at Drycastle and the enslaved adults across Dawnguard were the foray's main objective, and the prisoners the Druj threatened to kill.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: With at least 10,000 strength, prisoners in the Heart of Peytaht could be freed, and the raid would disrupt the Eaves of Peytaht to secure 10 wains of weirwood.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: The Druj shun the ruins of Dourfell Keep. A Sentinel Gate strike on their watch-post at Dourfell Chase could boost the foray and, if Irra Harah claimed it, become a lasting sanctuary.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: With at least 10,000 strength, the foray could free prisoners held in Murderdale.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: Mentioned in passing: the hidden routes might let particularly daring heroes reach people in need as far afield as Saltmarsh.

The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth.t: With at least 15,000 strength, slaves could be freed here and production at the Fangs mithril mine roughly halved for a year.

The Barrens/The Untrod Groves.t: Freed orcs who wished to stay and fight the Druj could find sanctuary in the Untrod Groves with Irra Harah's aid.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: refugees of the Mournwold were among those once aided by Irra Harah's hare-marked friends.

Ossium.t: The last orc armies had withdrawn from Ossium, and the Druj declared they would allow the Empire and its allies to hold it for now.

Reikos.t: Reikos was a destination for rescued children, Dawnish slaves and freed orcs, who would be escorted there through the haunted Forest of Peytaht.

Semmerholm.t: Ramsey arrived in Semmerholm bearing the Druj ultimatum. A secret route from Semmerholm into Dawnguard would carry heroes in and bring rescued captives back to safety.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens was the target of the proposed covert mission of mercy, which at higher strengths would free thousands of slaves, disrupt Druj operations and possibly create a rebel sanctuary.

Therunin.t: At the highest level of support, most of the extra orc slaves freed would be expected to join their cousins in Therunin.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: refugees of Zenith were among those once aided by Irra Harah's hare-marked friends.

One of us.d: Missionaries, helped by Freeborn smugglers, kept heading east after the Synod vetoed a Senate ban on preaching in Asavea. The project to establish the Way there needs 750 wains of white granite and 280 thrones, but only 37 thrones, 2 crowns, 1 ring and 1 wain had been given. The Sevenfold Path contacted three groups: the Cerularios, who want the shield Glistering; the death-obsessed Mikanos covenant, who want ten doses of true liao; and the rebellious magicians of Becephelas, who want Imperial lore. Winning each over would lower the cost. The Loyalty assembly could back violent rebellion against the Plenum or slow reform from within. The Whisper Gallery taunted that one group is a Plenum double-agent.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: only indirectly, as the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion is used to measure the vast amount of white granite needed for Asavea.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: as a warning, the Lasambrians are recalled as having marched off to fight alongside the Jotun after the Empire brought them to Virtue.

One of us.o: In Winter 386YE the Empire's effort to spread the Way to Asavea reached a crossroads. The Sevenfold Path found three groups of Asavean magicians who might be won over, the Assembly of Loyalty was offered two competing strategies, and the Whisper Gallery warned that one of the three groups planned to betray the Empire.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the white granite needed to establish the Way in Asavea is likened to the amount used to build the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion.

One side stone, one side fire.d: The koboldi warned that trogoni breeding in the sinkhole would eventually erupt against mines and mana sites in southern Hahnmark, Temeschwar, northern Upwold and Miaren. The Master of the Koboldi could announce the door's installation, opening an Expedition to the Depths for Imperial military units. The more strength committed, the deeper the seal: from the natural caverns, costing the Delver of the Depths income, down to the Terunael Mineworkings, ancient tunnels or trogoni burrows, each bringing greater treasure. If the door was not in place by the Winter Solstice 384YE, a trogoni horde might emerge. Several National Assemblies could urge support, League armies could assist, and the koboldi shared the secret of Red Iron wards.

Dawn.t: The Dawn National Assembly could urge knights to seek glory in the abyss, granting Dawnish units a rank bonus, full access to later exploration and more mithril and ilium for all delvers if the burrows were reached.

Navarr.t: The Navarr National Assembly could urge Navarr to help reach the Terunael Mineworkings, giving their units a rank bonus and, at 5,000 strength, a report for the Advisor on the Vallorn on what their ancestors did there.

The League.t: The Towerjacks or Wolves of War could be sent to a bordering territory to storm the depths, adding half their base strength and boosting League units, at the cost of halved defence and no resupply.

The Marches.t: The Marches National Assembly could urge Marchers to remove the threat to Upwold, earning participating Marcher units 24 rings each from grateful households.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark National Assembly could call on Winterfolk heroes to face the trogoni, granting their units a rank bonus and, if the ancient tunnels were reached, rune secrets for the Runegrott Runeforge.

One side stone, one side fire.o: The koboldi of Adamant completed the Red Iron Door, a great rune-marked mithril gate meant to seal the trogoni-infested sinkhole known as Lorenzo's Deep Pockets. The Empire was offered the chance to fight its way into the depths so the door could be installed, with deeper progress bringing richer rewards.

Miaren/Goldglades.t: Goldglades was named as directly threatened by the trogoni, one reason given for Navarr to support sealing the sinkhole.

Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale.t: Part of the Vardstein Vale had fallen into the sinkhole, and the wilderness now faced mana-hungry trogoni drawn to nearby mana sites.

Upwold/Birchland.t: The sinkhole opened in Birchland, swallowing households, and its people would be foremost among those paying Marcher units who helped seal it.

Hahnmark.t: Southern Hahnmark's mines and mana sites, bolstered by Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance, were thought the likeliest first target should the trogoni horde erupt.

Miaren.t: Northern Miaren, possibly including Seren and the Eternal Flame, lay under threat of a trogoni eruption, and League armies could be sent there to aid the expedition.

Temeschwar.t: Southern Temeschwar's mana sites, including those boosted by Lorenzo's Legacy of Loyalty, were at risk from the trogoni, and it was one of the territories where League armies could join the expedition.

Upwold.t: Northern Upwold borders the sinkhole and faced a trogoni threat, and its households would pay Marcher units that helped seal the hole if the mandate passed.

Only forward.d: The Fist of Ulven, led by Gjeirfund Haggarsdottir rather than King Gudmunder, advanced cautiously, fearing Night wards, while Bjorgthorn Hammerhand's Southern Bear pressed boldly. They met only levies and a few absent Strong Reeds. Graven Rock fell at once, again denying the Keeper of the Dour Fens its mana, and the Jotun began fortifying it. The Jotun's caution gave the rest of Bregasland time to prepare. A battle opportunity followed: stop Adamant's Mountain Bulwark from restoring the Burhfæst fortification, capture the ghodi Svynna to ransom four Navarr thralls, and show Pride at the Graven Door to lift Bregasland's sullen mood. A Jotun warband under Urse Longarm also raided Mitwold.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun call the Navarr "Imperial Druj" as they execute them at Graven.

Jotun.t: Jotun armies seized Gravenmarch and began fortifying Graven Rock, and Adamant has offered them the Burhfæst fortification for a year. The Ice Fishers of Ldansk and the Howling Bears joined the campaign, and Urse Longarm's warband raided Mitwold.

Navarr.t: Two Navarr stridings caught in Graven fought beside the Marchers, and the Jotun executed every Navarr survivor in revenge for past dishonour. The exception was the Graven Stand family of four, taken as thralls by Svynna of Ldansk, who might be ransomed if the ghodi is captured.

The Marches.t: The Marchers lost Gravenmarch, and those captured were offered the Choice. The Bregas yeomen are arming and waiting for the Strong Reeds to return, and a show of Pride at the Graven Door offers a chance to restore the region's morale.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark is not named; the only northern link is the Ice Fishers of Ldansk, drawn from minor clans across Kalsea who fight for Kierheim and Tromsa.
