Only forward.o: In Summer 386YE the Jotun armies the Fist of Ulven and the Southern Bear marched north from Liathaven and conquered Gravenmarch in Bregasland, taking Graven Rock and the town of Graven and executing the Navarr they found there.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: Gravenmarch fell to the Jotun, who took Graven Rock and the town of Graven and are fortifying the plateau. The battle opportunity centres here, at Graven Rock and the Graven Door near Rock Foot Wood.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: Mentioned in passing: the sullen mood affecting the Grey Fens could be dispelled by a show of Pride at the Graven Door if the Strong Reeds return.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland lost Gravenmarch to the Jotun, and the Keeper of the Dour Fens lost its mana bounty for the second time in a year. The rest of the territory is preparing to resist while a lingering sullen mood persists.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: the captured Navarr family may be destined for thralldom further west in Hordalant.

Liathaven.t: The Jotun, who now call it Ashvale, launched the invasion of Gravenmarch from Liathaven. Svynna's captive Navarr were taken there, and Urse Longarm had earlier won a victory there against a Feni enclave.

Mitwold.t: Urse Longarm's warband raided Mitwold's farmland and roads, evading the scattered Strong Reeds. The Bailiff of the Grand Market, Sebastian Shaw, is charged with killing them before their fame draws more Jotun raiders.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is not named on the page; the only northern reference is to the Ice Fishers of Ldansk and the lands of Kalsea.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ice Fishers of Ldansk are said to fight for the honour of Kierheim, Tromsa and more distant lands.

Other monstrous geographies.d: Under the Rivers of Life curse, the Eastern Sky, Lions of Adelmar, Summer Storm, Citadel Guard and Quiet Step took Sephals and broke the Tower of the Skink's gate with a stone-and-mithril ram, capturing Thornfen. The Hidden Snake and Poison Crane fled to the Salt Flats, losing 500 more each, and the scattered garrison left Outlaw Druj across four regions. The Gryphon's Pride crushed Banded Snake and Thornwasp attacks on Nesustak. The Boyar's Hasta only partly thwarted the Tainted Basilisk, who loosed Béantal Dol on Nesustak and Bloodwater Marsh. A Senate motion will confirm the Axou claim to Thornfen, and the Drowned Man is now called the Drowned Shepherd.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Eastern Sky and Lions of Adelmar led the breach of the Tower of the Skink, while the Gryphon's Pride saved the Nesustak rebels and won their wary trust; the Strategos of Dawn must now rescue sept members from Druj ghosts at Dahis.

Druj.t: The Druj lost Sephals, the Tower of the Skink and their last hold on the Sarangrave, their Hidden Snake and Poison Crane fleeing to the Salt Flats, though the Tainted Basilisk spitefully unleashed the vallorn of Béantal Dol.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; Bregasland, which they held, appears only in a comparison between its Otterway and the Tail of the Skink.

Navarr.t: The Navarr of the Quiet Step hunted Druj across the marshes, struck the Druj flanking force at the Tower, and with freed Great Forest Orcs built the weirwood frame for the ram that broke its gate.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is listed among the places where the Druj have tried to make examples of those who escaped them.

Urizen.t: The Citadel Guard helped take the Tower, which gives Urizen control of Thornfen; the Urizen assembly may veto the coming motion ceding it to the Axou, and Urizeni seers captured in Bloodwater Marsh await rescue.

Varushka.t: Varushka's Boyar's Hasta scouted for every Imperial army and ambushed the Tainted Basilisk's ghulai, limiting the vallorn's release to two regions; its general must now clear ghosts that took Hasta scouts near Béantal Dol.

Other monstrous geographies.o: In Spring 388YE five Imperial armies, aided by the Axou of Ipotavo, took Sephals and stormed the Tower of the Skink, ending Druj dominion over the Sarangrave, while the Gryphon's Pride saved the Nesustak rebels. In retaliation the Tainted Basilisk broke the wards of Béantal Dol and unleashed its vallorn.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: The Tainted Basilisk breached the Terunael warding stones around Béantal Dol, freeing the vallorn; the remaining stones will be destroyed by the Summer Solstice, leaving it a potent but ordinary vallorn.

Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh.t: The vallorn advances into Bloodwater Marsh at strength 30,000, and an equinox opportunity at Mantifent's Bier offers a chance to ward its stones, break the Bilious Breath and rescue captured Urizeni seers.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: The fleeing Druj armies crossed north through Kroll to the Salt Flats, and the region now suffers from Outlaw Druj.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: The rebels repelled Banded Snake and Thornwasp attackers with the Gryphon's Pride's help, but now face the vallorn at strength 30,000, with an equinox opportunity at the Feverbank Trees to ward the stones.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: Sephals and the Tower of the Skink fell and Thornfen is now Imperial, though flooded and plagued by Outlaw Druj, with a Senate motion due to confirm the Axou claim to it.

Sarangrave/Turan Flats.t: The Gryphon's Pride camped in the western Turan Flats to guard Nesustak; the region now has Outlaw Druj, and Druj ghosts menace the Bloodwater Spears near the village of Dahis.

Sarangrave/Whisperwood.t: Four Great Forest Orcs freed from Whisperwood's weirwood grove helped build the ram's frame, but the region now suffers from Outlaw Druj.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial armies passed swiftly through the Bleaks, watched silently by the Karass.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step marched from Astolat into the Sarangrave.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the raised Tail of the Skink causeway is likened to Otterway in Bregasland.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Béantal Dol is described as a vallorn with the full power of Brocéliande packed into a single region.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one place where the Druj have sought to punish those who threw off their yoke.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as a place where the Druj have attacked escaped slaves, and toasted by the Hasta's general for Varushkans slaying peelers there.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: The battered Hidden Snake and Poison Crane fled to the Salt Flats, a temporary refuge where desertion is expected, after supplies smuggled from there had armed the attack on Nesustak.

Sarangrave.t: The Empire now holds all of the Sarangrave save Nesustak Forest and Bendol, but the unleashed vallorn, floods, a surge of vermin and Outlaw Druj in four regions blight its conquest.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky, Gryphon's Pride and Citadel Guard marched out of Semmerholm to join the campaign.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the relieving armies passed through the Barrens, which are also recalled as a place where the Druj punished their former slaves.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: recalled as the place where the Tainted Basilisk have previously shown themselves willing to unleash a vallorn.

Our choice.d: Bogdan Bogdanovich's mandate made clear that what affects one Varushkan army affects all. Soldiers blaming the Iron Helms for the awakening of Screed in Spiral led Wintermark and Brass Coast armies to shun every Varushkan army, cutting victory points by a tenth, or a fifth if both are present. At the Spring Equinox 382YE only, the Northern Eagle could become Plighted for 25 wains of weirwood, and the Golden Axe could become Driven for 50 wains of mithril. A consortium led by the miners of Morsvah also offered cheap enlargement of either army. Belakov Zakharovich Prochnost provided 50 mithril to make the Golden Axe Driven, and the Senate commissioned its enlargement.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish knights are recalled grumbling about the lack of glory in the historic conquest of Karsk.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel are not named; the page refers only to the Varushkan victory in Spiral, a territory they partly held.

Thule.t: In the opening fiction, a Varushkan boyar resents Thule ilium deals as chains and schemes over the star-metal brought down in Keyursal in Sküld. The page also recalls the Golden Axe crushing the Thule during the conquest of Karsk.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen are not named; the page refers only to the Varushkan victory in Spiral, a territory they partly held.

Varushka.t: Every Varushkan army now suffers penalties when campaigning with Wintermark or Brass Coast armies. The Golden Axe was set to become Driven and to be enlarged, drawing on Vard heritage and the backing of a mine- and forest-owners' consortium interested in the power of relinquishment.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark soldiers now shun Varushkan armies, believing the Iron Helms caused the awakening of Screed. Any campaign shared with a Varushkan army loses a tenth of its victory points, or a fifth if Brass Coast armies are also present.

Our choice.o: Following the Varushkan National Assembly's mandates, all Varushkan armies came to share the penalties for fighting alongside Wintermark and Brass Coast armies, while the Northern Eagle and Golden Axe were offered a one-season chance to embrace their Ushkan and Vard heritage. The Golden Axe took the Driven quality and the Senate commissioned its enlargement.

Spiral/Screed.t: Some soldiers blame the Iron Helms' cruel tactics for the awakening of Screed and the resulting wave of madness and deaths, and that belief led to the rift with Wintermark and the Brass Coast.

Volodmartz/Brez.t: Mentioned in passing: Brez is not named; the page mentions Volodmartz only as a territory where the assembly's message spread and the Northern Eagle recruited.

Karov.t: Bogdan Bogdanovich spread the assembly's message here. Karov is the heartland of the Golden Axe, whose Driven transformation draws on the Vard who conquered Karov and on its wagon raiders and volhov.

Karsk.t: The miners of Morsvah in southern Karsk led the consortium offering to equip up to two and a half thousand new troops for one army. The territory's conquest under the Sun Queen is recalled as the first campaign of both the Eagle and the Axe.

Miekarova.t: Bogdan Bogdanovich carried the assembly's words here. Miekarova's Ushkan vales were a traditional recruiting ground of the Northern Eagle, which was offered the chance to become Plighted.

Spiral.t: The Varushkan victory in Spiral made many Varushkans proud. Others blamed the Iron Helms for the awakening of Screed and the madness and deaths that swept the territory, and that belief turned Wintermark and Brass Coast soldiers against Varushkan armies.

Volodmartz.t: Bogdan Bogdanovich spread the assembly's message here. Volodmartz's Ushkan vales were a traditional source of the Northern Eagle's troops.

Our elaborate plans.d: The magic in Apulian grew in 'vorticity': engaging things felt closer, rainbow cats warred with songbirds, and the thrones and personae began reshaping businesses and performances. Sung became less agitated but more reclusive. The League National Assembly was due to appoint the Map to the City Below, who could claim 37 crystal fire to recruit captains. A scouting venture, Map the City Below, was open to League, Urizen and Dawnish units, succeeding with 3000 strength despite unknown resistance. The duSesna Guild, whose prince Teodore had vanished after accusing Sung, offered a rival venture, Rescue the Missing Prince. Units assigned to it subtracted from the mapping effort, and the guild urged the Assembly to condemn Sung.

Dawn.t: Dawnish military units were not formally invited but could join the Map the City Below venture if they found the quixotic adventure glorious enough, earning crystal fire and a rainbow feather.

The League.t: League citizens bore the brunt of Apulian's strange magic and its benefits. Their National Assembly faced appointing the Map to the City Below and answering the duSesna Guild's demand to condemn Sung, while League units were invited to map the city.

Urizen.t: Urizeni architects helped build the Chamber of Euphony and Urizeni scholars studied the city's magic. Urizen military units were invited to help map the sewers their forebears originally built.

Our elaborate plans.o: In Spring 388YE the strange night magic and dramaturgical effects gripping Apulian grew more turbulent after the Chamber of Euphony, Sung's new fane, was completed. Sung's heralds sought military units to map the City Below, while the duSesna Guild sought help to find their missing merchant prince.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: Mentioned in passing: the Greater Doubt, flowing more strongly from Apstrus since the dam's construction, feeds into Apulian's sewers.

Spiral.t: Apulian, Spiral's City Below, saw intensifying night magic. Resident night magicians gained ritual strength, and two rival scouting ventures in the city's tangled sewers were set against each other.

Our eyes in Spiral.d: The Vigilant sorted the Black Plateau's dangers into naifs, the Lost and the enemy. They urged close watch over the Oblivion Sentinel, more resources for that office, and enmity with Lashonar, the Muse of Fire, Azoth and the Whisper Gallery. They proposed Oblivion's Edge, a fortification around the Plateau in Screed, as an opportunity open until Spring Equinox 388YE. In Apulus, their pilgrim Victo von Temeschwar vanished while infiltrating a suspected Grendel ring and was later found paranoid and maddened. A Sentinel Gate conjunction gives the Voice of Vigilance a chance to save Victo. Caela's rebels are abiding by the treaty and have rebuffed the Grendel. Further Vigilant are still investigating Redoubt.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Vigilant's search of Astolat found no active cultists of Agramant.

Druj.t: The Vigilant warn that if southern Zenith ever fell to the Druj, they might raid Spiral to target the Black Plateau, as the Iron Helms once did. The proposed Oblivion's Edge fortification is meant partly to deter such a strike.

Grendel.t: The Grendel are suspected of running an espionage ring in Apulian, and their approaches to Caela's rebels have been firmly rebuffed. The Vigilant expect any Grendel bid to retake Spiral to come as a swift surprise attack.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Vigilant's mandate drew on the true liao consecration of the damaged basilica in Bastion in Berechiah's name.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel armies would have to pass through Imperial Orc-controlled Mareave to contest Spiral.

The League.t: League citizens in Spiral live in Apulian, a booming city the Vigilant see as fertile ground for Grendel spies. One League pilgrim, Victo von Temeschwar, lost their senses while trying to infiltrate the ring. The Vigilant also warn that any League settlement nearer Screed could be disastrous.

Urizen.t: Most Urizeni rebels in Spiral have been mollified, and Urizeni magicians now share knowledge of the Block with League neighbours. Caela's Silver Flame holds Cinion under the treaty but poses no active threat. The Vigilant are still investigating Redoubt.

Our eyes in Spiral.o: The Vigilant followers of Berechiah, sent to Spiral by the Vigilance Assembly in Spring 386YE, reported back after a year of thorough and largely undisruptive investigation. They found no active threats at the Black Plateau or among the rebels, but uncovered signs of a Grendel espionage ring in Apulus.

Spiral/Ankra.t: Mentioned in passing: Ankra is named as a home of Urizeni rebels and as bordering the spire of the Lost Spire of the Black Plateau.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: Mentioned in passing: a companion Wind of Fortune about damming the River Doubt in Apstrus is listed, and Zie of the Perfect Morning's offer of protection is tied to that plan.

Spiral/Apulus.t: The Vigilant found evidence of a Grendel espionage ring in the city of Apulian, where their undercover pilgrim Victo was found maddened. A conjunction to The Cellar Below safehouse offers a chance to restore Victo and learn what they uncovered.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Ceded by treaty to Caela of the Silver Flame, Cinion's rebels have disavowed the violent Spire of Black Glass and rejected Grendel approaches. The Vigilant report no active threat there for now.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossuary is one of the regions bordering the abandoned spire taken over by the Lost Spire of the Black Plateau.

Spiral/Screed.t: The Black Plateau at the heart of Screed shows no active threats and may calm within ten to twenty years, but remains incredibly dangerous. The Vigilant propose building Oblivion's Edge here to secure the passes, keep naifs out and defend against direct attack.

Temeschwar/Vargat.t: Mentioned in passing: Victo's parents ran Vargataia Delicacies, a business selling the foods of the Vargat region.

Astolat.t: The Vigilant's search for cultists of Agramant here found none currently active, which the page treats as a success.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the Vigilant mandate took advantage of the true liao consecration of the damaged basilica in Bastion.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that Grendel armies would have to come through Mareave, described as Imperial Orc-controlled, to contest Spiral.

Redoubt.t: Followers of Berechiah, sent by a Summer 386YE Assembly mandate, are still seeking threats here. Their report is expected by Summer or by Autumn at the latest.

Spiral.t: After a year of watching, the Vigilant found no active threats at the Black Plateau or among the rebels, though the Plateau remains deeply dangerous. They did uncover a likely Grendel espionage ring in Apulus and proposed the Oblivion's Edge fortification to contain the Plateau.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Vigilant pilgrim Victo von Temeschwar is from here, orphaned when the Vyig burned their parents' business.

Zenith.t: Zenith is now fully back in Urizeni hands, but the Vigilant warn that losing its southern part to the Druj could open a path for a raid on Spiral's Black Plateau.

Our thumping hearts.d: Barien's herald Revel would moderate the tag-team grand melee alongside the Archmage of Summer and the Master of Ice and Darkness. Teams were three magicians, armed only with implements, with no potions, vis or crystal mana once fighting began, and no killing. Champions were announced for Meraud, Cathan Canae, Jaheris, Adamant, Prospero, Sadogua and others. Eleonaris, Hayaak, Zakalwe and Wise Rangara kept their teams obscure or still recruiting. A Highborn team sought to keep the college free of any patron, and Agramant, though under enmity, offered rewards to anyone who fought for him. The result would stand until 387YE at the earliest.

Dawn.t: The tourney was to be held in the Dawnish Glory Square. Tristan Wolfborn fought for Meraud, while Jaheris's team was entirely Dawnish: Senators Zadkiel de Coeurdefer and Bohemond de Rondell, with Drake de Coeurdefer.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: in the opening tale, a Freeborn hakima coven had fled the Bay of Catazar because of the Grendel.

Highguard.t: Highborn magicians fielded two teams. Ahzrukhal chose Aemon and Ingrid, daughter of Jan, to champion Sadogua, and Baalam, Isolde and Gideon fought to keep the Icy Crag free of any eternal patron.

Navarr.t: Cedric Gallows of Navarr was one of Meraud's three champions, and Zakalwe's undisclosed team was said to include a Navarr magician.

The Brass Coast.t: Rhianos sought to recruit Freeborn battle magicians with the most exciting adventures to fight on its behalf, and Esteban i DelRio Blanco i Guerra was among Cathan Canae's champions.

Urizen.t: Sejanus of Urizen was the only one of Adamant's original champions still available and was charged with recruiting two more, while Zakalwe's team reportedly included an Urizen magician.

Wintermark.t: Tiberius the Rainmage fought for Meraud, and the Kallavesi Runar Hval of Raven's Hold was one of Cathan Canae's chosen champions.

Our thumping hearts.o: The tourney to decide which eternal would become patron of the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, the Empire's Summer college, was set to take place in the Glory Square, with around a dozen eternals from Summer and other realms fielding teams of Imperial magicians.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Bohemond de Rondell, Senator for Astolat and throne aspirant, was named as one of Jaheris's champions.

Bay of Catazar.t: In the opening tale, a lone hakima who had stayed behind when her coven fled the Grendel honoured an old compact with the Guardian of the Cloudsea. In return he promised that none of her family would drown in the Bay in the coming year.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the rest of Caita i Guerra's hakima coven had fled north to Madruga.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Zadkiel de Coeurdefer, Senator for Semmerholm, was named as one of Jaheris's champions.

Ourselves and immortality.d: Prospero granted Vossk of Zenith Ascendant a parley and called in the favour owed by the Celestial Arch. Siakha agreed to discuss destruction with Ibiss Briarheart and gave three new rituals to Urizen lore. The Thrice-cursed Court accepted a midnight parley, invited the Keeper of Tharim's Throne, and Surut demanded tribute from warriors. Ylenwe said the Kronemark Sungate cannot be closed, proposed a hall of music in Skarsind and urged aid for the Commonwealth and Jarm against Cold Sun. The Whisper Gallery set a masked-only parley in the Hall of Worlds. Adamant offered the Throne of the Mountains ritual in return for wider building powers for four Imperial titles.

Dawn.t: The Keeper of Tharim's Throne, Claudia Varkulova Remislav, was invited as the King-in-Chains' guest at the Thrice-cursed parley. The Court also said that Armand Remislav Who Was Remys remains beloved of them but will not be given Unleash Wild Fire.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Siakha's tempest declared there would be no talk of Grendel or wreckers at her parley.

Imperial Orcs.t: Ylenwe proposed an edifice in the White Wood of Skarsind, the Harmonious Hall, which would have to be ceded to the eternal. Her herald will discuss it with the Archmage of Day, Skywise Gralka, and the High Bard.

The League.t: The Whisper Gallery's parley singled out several invitees, including Archmage of Night Bella Vicente d'Apulian, Senator for Spiral Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian and Custodian of Legacy Rafael Barossa d'Apulian.

Urizen.t: Siakha placed three new rituals in Urizen lore as a gift requested by Ibiss Briarheart. Vossk of Zenith Ascendant was summoned to parley with Prospero, who wants the Celestial Arch to repay its favour.

Varushka.t: Adamant welcomed more white granite fortresses in northern Varushka but refused to make them cheaper, saying the Vorazi do not see the bigger picture.

Wintermark.t: Ylenwe declared the Sungate in Kronemark an open wound sustained by the Oblivion Flame, beyond her power to close. For now it can only be avoided.

Ourselves and immortality.o: Ahead of the Winter Solstice 387YE, six eternals answered the plenipotentiary messages of the Imperial archmages. Five arranged parleys or meetings at Anvil, while Adamant declined a formal parley and instead made proposals about ritual magic.

Hahnmark/Kronemark.t: The Sungate in Kronemark is fed directly by the fury of the Oblivion Flame. Ylenwe cannot close it or let mortals near it, so it must simply be avoided.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the page names no event there, though the Thrice-cursed parley will touch on the Keeper of Tharim's Throne, knights, regio and the vallorn.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the robe of Siakha's tempest herald is described as evoking the wind-tossed breakers of the Bay of Catazar.

Hahnmark.t: Ylenwe confirmed that the Sungate in Hahnmark's Kronemark cannot be closed and that mortals cannot approach it, unless fate changes in future.

Skarsind.t: Ylenwe proposed building the Harmonious Hall in the White Wood. It would cost 15 weirwood, 10 mithril, 10 ilium and 75 crowns, must be ceded to her, and its effects are still unclear.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian, Senator for Spiral, is among those the Whisper Gallery invited to its parley.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the page describes no events in Temeschwar itself.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Archmage of Autumn summoned by Prospero is Vossk of Zenith Ascendant.

Out of the abyss.d: Priests answering Marzanna's statement anointed some miners but were barred from the Deep Chamber by the cabalists of Void. The work is now complete. Missing miners and failing lights have driven demand for Urizeni lightstone, which Cold Sun is disrupting. Businesses in both nations could diversify to secure light supplies. A one-season great work offered a House of Illumination at Cargo and a Light Market in Miekarova, raising mine and business investment, creating two titles and reducing the danger to miners. The sovereign offered to trap the Cold Sun scions in the Star Caverns, asking for those caverns and Berislav's Rest mine. Varushkans were invited to negotiate through a Sentinel Gate conjunction.

Urizen.t: Urizeni businesses could diversify for free to supply lightstone northwards. The proposed House of Illumination and Architect of Illumination title would boost trade in Morrow and Redoubt and could forge closer ties with Varushka, building on Cassia Silkweaver's statement of thanks.

Varushka.t: Varushkan miners face a resurgent Night Below and dwindling supplies of good lightstone. Varushka was offered a Light Market and a Merchant-Boyar title, while its cabalists and senators were invited to bargain with the sovereign to destroy the Shepherds of Ash.

Out of the abyss.o: After the Varushkan Assembly urged priests to aid the miners building the Deep Chamber, the ancient sovereign called the Night Below grew more active beneath Varushka's northern mountains. A lightstone trade with Urizen and a joint great work were proposed, and the sovereign offered to destroy the Shepherds of Ash in return for a price.

Miekarova/Dupadealuri.t: The proposed Light Market would be established at the walled town in Dupadealuri, receiving Urizeni lightstone carried north along the Blood Red Roads.

Volodmartz/Brez.t: The Deep Chamber was completed in the darkness beneath the Mountains of Brez, where the Night Below has its places of power. Under the sovereign's plan, Brez must be left unwarded so the Shepherds of Ash are drawn towards its people.

Volodmartz/Livardz.t: The Shepherds of Ash are currently penned in at Livardz by the Varushkan covens, and the sovereign's plan would draw them out towards Murupa.

Volodmartz/Murupa.t: The sovereign wants to trap the scions in the Star Caverns in northern Murupa and then claim the caverns. Murupa must be left unwarded as bait, and the conjunction opens on the nearby Varyu Mets woodland.

Volodmartz/Opascari.t: The sovereign's plan calls for ice citadels to be raised in Opascari to wall off the Shepherds of Ash and funnel them towards Murupa.

Volodmartz/Suvretz.t: The sovereign's plan calls for wards of living wood to be woven in Suvretz, helping channel the Shepherds of Ash towards the Star Caverns.

Karov.t: The Cold Sun scions' brief proximity to the Tallowman's Post in Karov drew the Night Below's attention, and disruption in Karov has endangered the supply of good lighting; Karov's cabalists are listed among those invited to the conjunction.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: two cabalists of Karsk are listed among the cabalists of Varushka who may attend the conjunction.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova's miners are among those most threatened by the Night Below, and the proposed great work would establish a Light Market there and raise mine investment in the territory to 2.

Morrow.t: As a centre of Urizeni lightstone production, Morrow's businesses would gain 1 level of investment if the House of Illumination great work were completed.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: six cabalists of Ossium are listed among the cabalists of Varushka who may attend the conjunction.

Redoubt.t: The proposed House of Illumination would be built at Cargo in Redoubt, raising business investment there by 1 and becoming the charge of the Architect of Illumination.

Volodmartz.t: Cold Sun's presence is disrupting lightstone imports to Volodmartz. Its senator must consent if the sovereign is to take the Star Caverns, and the sovereign also demands the mine at Berislav's Rest in return for destroying the Shepherds of Ash.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Urizen Assembly's statement thanks the Varushkan boyars for donating an Imperial Wayleave so the Gardens of Pallas could be built in Zenith.

Out of the realm.d: Seven magical fortifications were raised: Spring forests in Nearweald, ice castles in Kahraman against the Lasambrian Jotun, and mist castles in Bregasland, Ossium and Kallavesa. Penumbral Veils shrouded Ossium, Madruga, Kahraman, the Barrens and Zenith. Regrow the Land's Heart spared Skarsind from the Great Drought. The expanded College of Warcasting drew many Tamazi into the Imperial Orcs. Prospero's golden spiders began aiding Urizen's heliopticons and the Doyen of the Spires. Cathan Canae threatened to withdraw support if more land is ceded. Kaela will triple her grim legions for the Druj whenever the Suns of Couros steal them. Four of the Childer of the Black Drop were found dead in Vardstein Vale.

Dawn.t: Barien, Lord of the Crossroads, will hold a rewarding ceremony for challengers via the Semmerstones in Causse, a Dawnish region.

Druj.t: Penumbral Veils hide the Barrens and Zenith from divination. Kaela's grievance means nine cadres of grim legionnaires will fight alongside the Druj this season, while new Imperial fortifications in Ossium stand against them.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: golden spiders descended on heliopticon towers in Grendel-held Spiral, and former Mareave gladiators are joining Skarsind's septs and its College of Warcasting.

Highguard.t: Kaela declared a bounty on the Highborn coven of the Suns of Couros. She will send three of her grim legionnaires against Highborn armies for every one they summon, unless one of the coven secures Imperial lore status for Abandon the Mortal Shackles.

Imperial Orcs.t: Skarsind's farms were spared the Great Drought by Regrow the Land's Heart. The expanded College of Warcasting drew a wave of Tamazi to join the nation, though their bonecarvers remain cautious and plan to visit Anvil in Autumn.

Jotun.t: Two castles of ice and granite were raised in Kahraman to bolster Fort Braydon against the Lasambrian Jotun.

The Brass Coast.t: Kahraman was fortified with two castles of ice and granite, and Penumbral Veils now shroud both Kahraman and Madruga against divination.

The League.t: The bodies of four members of the Childer of the Black Drop, a League sorcerous cabal declared sorcerers in 354YE, were found in Vardstein Vale. Jodeya Watiker and the cabal's library remain missing.

The Marches.t: Castles of mist were raised over the fens of the Rushes and Ottermire in Bregasland.

Urizen.t: Prospero's golden spiders now aid Urizen's heliopticon towers and let the Doyen of the Spires speed codification for orichalcum, provided the resulting rituals stay out of Imperial lore. Agon also extended the chance to expand the Citadel of Highwatch to the end of the Summer Solstice.

Varushka.t: Ossium gained a Spring forest fortification in Nearweald and a mist castle in Drownbark Forest, and is shrouded by a Penumbral Veil. Wise Rangara will become patron of Marshstand Skerry if the Conclave asks her.

Wintermark.t: Restless Suaq spirits trouble Turelva in Hahnmark, and Kallavesa's West Marsh gained a mist castle. The Icewalkers are invited to perform before Barien to claim their reward, and his heralds will visit Lumi's.

Out of the realm.o: The Summer 384YE Wind of Fortune reported the magical consequences of the Spring Equinox across the Empire. These included new fortifications and veils, an enchanted Skarsind, Tamazi joining the Imperial Orcs, eternal patronages, ultimatums and grievances, a ghostly conjunction in Hahnmark, and the discovery of long-missing sorcerers dead in Temeschwar.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: A castle of mist was raised over the fens of Ottermire.

Hahnmark/Bruckland.t: Restless spirits wail near Turelva, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction at 23:00 on Saturday lets up to fifty performers reach the woodland to calm them.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: A castle of ice and granite was raised here to help fortify Kahraman against the Lasambrian Jotun.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: A castle of ice and granite was raised here to fortify Kahraman.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: A castle of mist now fortifies the marsh of West Marsh.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: A castle of mist was raised over the bogs of Drownbark Forest.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: A Spring realm fortification strengthened the forests of Nearweald against Druj depredations.

Semmerholm/Causse.t: A conjunction at 2pm on Saturday will lead challengers through the Semmerstones to Barien's ceremony of rewarding.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Mentioned in passing: Padik Tarvin and the still-missing Jodeya Watiker of the Childer of the Black Drop hailed from Tassato Mestra.

Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale.t: Scouts near Lorenzo's Deep Pockets found four sorcerers dead in a cottage, with a fifth place set at the table and an empty rune-inlaid trunk.

Bregasland.t: Castles of mist now fortify the fens of the Rushes and Ottermire.

Hahnmark.t: Anguished ghosts of Frayed Suaq haunt the lands near Turelva, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction offers scops a chance to lay them to rest.

Kahraman.t: Two castles of ice and granite drawn from the Breath of Winter fortify the territory against the Lasambrian Jotun, and a Penumbral Veil hides it from scrying.

Kallavesa.t: A castle of mist was raised over the marsh of West Marsh.

Madruga.t: A Penumbral Veil now hangs over the territory, so rituals must overcome it to scry there.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: former Mareave gladiators living in Skarsind benefit from its enchantment and are joining the College of Warcasting.

Morrow.t: Golden spiders from the Autumn realm descended on Morrow's heliopticon towers, making message-sending faster and more reliable.

Ossium.t: The territory gained a Spring forest fortification and a mist castle, and lies under a Penumbral Veil. Wise Rangara awaits the Conclave's invitation to become patron of Marshstand Skerry.

Redoubt.t: Golden spiders settled at Redoubt's working heliopticon towers to assist their Urizen operators.

Semmerholm.t: Barien summons challengers to the Semmerstones in Causse, from where they may pass to the Grove of Thousands for his rewarding ceremony.

Skarsind.t: Regrow the Land's Heart brought gentle rain that spared its farms from the Great Drought. The expanded College of Warcasting was flooded with Tamazi, young orcs and former gladiators.

Spiral.t: Golden spiders descended even on the functioning heliopticon towers in Spiral.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: two members of the Childer of the Black Drop were of Tassato Mestra.

Temeschwar.t: Scouts found four long-missing sorcerers of the Childer of the Black Drop dead in a cottage in Vardstein Vale, a mystery that has baffled the magistrates.

The Barrens.t: A Penumbral Veil shrouds the Druj-held Barrens against divination.

Zenith.t: A Penumbral Veil shrouds Druj-held Zenith against divination.

Out of these convertites.d: Most of the visitors were human priests, with some orcs who were once Grendel. They worked the Mournwold fields by day and listened to the Marcher orcs by night. The Marcher orcs renounce violence but hear their warrior ancestors through sport, and League orcs playing foot-the-ball heard Rucraic, Sheanduir and even Curstag van Apulian. The page confirms that League orcs hear their ancestors as well as any other orc. Two opportunities arose. Bishops of Mestra and Regario proposed rival foot-the-ball stadia in Tassato. Greumach von Apulian proposed a Duellists Colosseum in Apulian, and Cigno's orcs argued for Sarvos instead. Monks from Boarsford Monastery plan to visit Anvil and ask that reincarnation not be discussed.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: many League orcs are former Grendel, and the Grendel view of ancestors and their gladiatorial arenas inspire the colosseum proposal.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher orcs are former Jotun thralls who still hear Jotun warrior ancestors such as Ulven, Skaldi and Raðljóst.

The League.t: League priests and orcs made the pilgrimage, and League orcs learned to hear their ancestors through foot-the-ball. The nation may now build stadia in Tassato and a Duellists Colosseum, which would create titles including Mistress of Duels.

The Marches.t: Marcher farms gained willing if inexperienced hands for the harvest, and Leaguish coin flowed into Marcher taverns. The Marcher orcs shared their beliefs and their love of foot-the-ball with the visitors.

Out of these convertites.o: After the League and Marcher assemblies endorsed a pilgrimage at the Summer Solstice, Leaguish priests and orcs spent the autumn of 388YE in the Mournwold. They helped bring in the harvest and learned how the Marcher orcs hear their ancestors, chiefly through foot-the-ball.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: A party of orc monks from Boarsford Monastery in Chalkdowns set out to meet League pilgrims at Anvil and talk of ancestors, but not reincarnation.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Cigno's League orcs proposed it as a central, wealthy home for the Duellists Colosseum as an alternative to Apulian.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Bishop Leonore Fidalgo di Mestra proposed a stadium and foot-the-ball team for Mestra, available as a commission until the end of the Summer Solstice 389YE.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: Bishop Luis Calazan di Regario drew up plans for a rival stadium and team in Regario, on the other side of the river.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: pilgrims from Holberg were among those who travelled to the Mournwold.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold hosted the League pilgrims, whose fields were worked by mixed crews of orcs and humans. Its orcs taught the visitors how they hear their ancestors through foot-the-ball.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos pilgrims were among the first to arrive in the Mournwold. Cigno's orc community argues that Sarvos should host the proposed Duellists Colosseum.

Spiral.t: Greumach von Apulian proposed building the Duellists Colosseum in Apulian. It would host duelling contests and cheapen military unit upgrades in the territory for a year.

Tassato.t: Tassato's pilgrims arrived first, and rival bishops of Mestra and Regario proposed foot-the-ball stadia so the twin cities could field teams against the Marches and each other.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: pilgrims from Temeschwar followed the first arrivals to the Mournwold.

Out of void, out of chaos.d: Across the Empire, people dreamt of profound personal change and impossible things. For the Equinox, Distil the Serpent's Stone produced shadow eggs instead of serpent's stones. These eggs grant a temporary boost of six effective ranks of realm lore for a single ritual, but cannot cure poisons, lift curses or transform materials. Transmogrification of the Soul's Echo was enhanced, allowing targets to shed or gain naga lineage, change skills, or forget whole categories of rituals or recipes. Heralds of Murit and Soghter concluded their arrangements and vanished, apart from Centimani and Alkahest at Anvil. Their regio were sealed, and the eternals could not be contacted.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: enchanters in Dawn are among the magicians who reported that the heralds of Murit and Soghter were disappearing.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the 'incident in the Mournwold', a Marcher territory, is cited as the point since which the heralds of the two eternals have been conspicuously absent.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni Stargazers are among the magicians who reported the vanishing of Murit's and Soghter's heralds.

Out of void, out of chaos.o: During Autumn 381YE the Wanderer hung in the constellation of the Great Wyrm, bringing dreams of transformation and altering powerful night rituals for the coming Autumn Equinox. Meanwhile, the heralds of the night eternals Murit and Soghter were withdrawing from the Empire and their regio became sealed.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: an incident in the Mournwold is named as the moment after which heralds of Murit and Soghter all but disappeared.

Outreach across the marshes.d: The visit followed the League Assembly's call to bring others into the Empire. The Sand Fishers are deeply grateful to the Empire and devoted to the Virtues, but they have four main objections. They cherish self-rule of Misericorde. They would be financially worse off, since they currently receive defence and education without paying taxes. Their reincarnation beliefs could see them executed under Imperial law. They also fear sharing culpability for massacres like those in the Barrens. Practical worries include losing League control of the Flaxen Pillars and the draining of Rebeshof and Utterlund. Three Hands will meet the League at Lia Adelaar's camp at 4pm on Saturday. Arios von Temeschwar also discovered that the sept is secretly drilling a small mithril-armed force.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers' horror at the conquest of the Barrens and the massacres of the septs there is cited, but Dawn itself is not named.

Druj.t: The Sand Fishers' decades of brutal Druj rule shape every objection they raise. They now suspect their belief in reincarnation was a lie the Druj spread to crush their spirits, and they refuse to belong to an Empire that imitates the Druj.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Sand Fishers have studied war magic with the Imperial Orcs in Skarsind, and the recent execution of the Imperial Orc Bloodcrow Knott for failing to observe the Doctrines feeds the sept's fears.

The League.t: League merchant princes pinned down why the Sand Fishers hesitate and concluded the problem cannot be solved with money. The League's leaders now have a rare chance at Anvil to address the sept's concerns and bring them into the nation.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers' communal decision-making is likened to the approach used by most Urizen spires.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers do not imagine they could have stopped the Varushkans wiping out the Montanians in the Barrens.

Outreach across the marshes.o: In Autumn 388YE the merchant princes of the League, led by Lia Adelaar von Holberg, visited Misericorde to persuade the Sand Fishers sept to join the Empire. They identified the sept's sticking points, and the sept's leaders agreed to discuss them at Anvil.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: The merchant princes visited Misericorde, which the Sand Fishers treasure as their self-ruled paradise and are reluctant to give up. Arios von Temeschwar found a hidden camp there where the sept is drilling perhaps five hundred soldiers in mithril arms and armour.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: The Adelaarskade dykes are slowly draining Rebeshof's wetlands, which will lose their marsh quality by Spring 389YE. The Sand Fishers worry no one, themselves included, will farm the new land.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Utterlund's marshes are being drained into farmland and will lose their marsh quality by Spring 389YE. The sept fears neither they nor League citizens will want to settle and farm there.

Holberg.t: Holberg's diplomats sought to bring its Sand Fisher neighbours in Misericorde into the Empire. Questions now hang over the Flaxen Pillars, the drained wetlands of Rebeshof and Utterlund, and a small orc army training within the territory.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is recalled as where the Sand Fishers suffered brutal Druj rule before the Empire freed them.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is not named, and the page touches the wider League only through references such as the Apulian Orcs having already joined the League.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: members of the sept have been sent to Skarsind to study war magic with the Imperial Orcs.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is not named. The nearest references are the Apulian Orcs' joining the League and the Sarcophan enclave on the Alivetti estates, which enjoys similar benefits without taxation.

The Barrens.t: The treatment of the Rahvin, Black Wind, Vendarri and Montanians during the conquest of the Barrens horrified the Sand Fishers. It is a key reason they fear sharing culpability for Imperial actions.

Outside the wall.d: Naomi found few displaced Varushkans beyond those unhomed by Cold Sun and the Schlacta of Rot, and many were already in Delev. She proposed warding the Little Boyar's Welcome (20 mithril, 60 crowns), which would raise Karov's taxation by 6 thrones. She also proposed a Great Market at Delev (50 white granite, 150 crowns) and a Golden Bee Assayer's Office sinecure (14 mithril, 42 crowns). A Synod mandate could turn miners away from Temeschwar. Oksana Lyava Pinavora offered 900 thrones towards buying the Hunt of Alderei the Fair for Varushka. The bees of Duzekani remain missing, possibly for supernatural reasons, and magicians suggested a further appraisal or dealings with eternals. None of these proposals is time sensitive.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: folk from Dawn were among those Naomi consulted.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the concedence of Miechernya is recalled as the price of securing Otkodov's aid against the Jotun.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step is among the armies honoured on the Little Boyar's Welcome mural for defending Delev from Cold Sun.

The League.t: Temeschwar is cast as Delev's great rival, and its Assayer's Guild is resented for drawing Varushkan metal trade into the League. A proposed mandate would cut Temeschwar's taxation by 2 thrones, and Holberg is held up as the exemplar of a true city.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Meade is cited as a small city Delev might come to match.

Thule.t: Thule merchants trade crystal mana in Delev but were reluctant to commit with the Otkodov treaty due for renegotiation. Varushkans fear further regions, perhaps Opascari or Mieriada, might be traded to the orcs for peace.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen merchants trade in Delev, and Urizen pilgrims to the Maze of Zoria recalled Clytemnestra's threat to destroy the Citadel Guard.

Varushka.t: The proposals offer Varushka a chance to make Delev a fortified, prosperous rival to Temeschwar and to keep its metal trade at home. Oksana Lyava Pinavora urged Varushkans to pool funds to buy the Hunt of Alderei the Fair, while worries persist over the vanished bees and further territorial concessions to the Thule.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark merchants travel to Delev, and Kalpaheim is named as a city Delev might rival.

Outside the wall.o: Commissioned by the Senate at the Winter Solstice, the Highborn prognosticator Naomi of Virtue's Rest appraised how displaced Varushkans might be drawn to Delev in Karov, and how the town's prosperity and safety could be built up. She proposed warding its walls, building a great market and founding an assayer's office to rival Temeschwar, and she reported on the unsolved disappearance of Duzekani's bees.

Karov/Duzekani.t: Delev lies in Duzekani, and every proposal would be built there, adding to its taxation and protecting sites such as the Iron Roundtower. Its bees have vanished since Cold Sun's attack and have still not returned.

Karov/Kamienczka.t: People fled the dead of the Schlacta of Rot here and no longer feel safe in isolated settlements, and there are anxious reports of fewer bees as spring approaches.

Karov/Skoremujac.t: Folk displaced by the Schlacta of Rot, or fearful in remote vales, would welcome new defended homes, and locals report seeing fewer bees.

Karov/Wieliczka.t: Anxious reports from Wieliczka suggest there are fewer bees as spring approaches, raising fears that Duzekani's problem is spreading.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: Its ceding to the Thule seven years ago forced Varushkans to migrate south or remain as subjects of the Dragons. Most who left are now settled elsewhere.

Miekarova/Miechernya.t: Its concedence displaced Varushkans such as the woodcutter Vasily's family, who later fled the scions south and fell on hard times.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Mieriada holds a bourse seat rumoured to be at risk of being traded to Otkodov. Oksana hopes Varushkan ownership of the Hunt and Quarry would protect it.

Volodmartz/Opascari.t: Opascari holds a bourse seat rumoured to be a possible bargaining chip for peace with Otkodov, which Oksana's offer seeks to guard against.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: its city of Kalpaheim is cited as a benchmark for Delev's possible growth.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg was consulted as the exemplar of a true city, and its splendid defences were held up as a model for Delev's walls.

Karov.t: Karov is the focus of the appraisal. Warding Delev's walls, building the Great Market and founding the Golden Bee Assayer's Office would together raise its taxation by up to 12 thrones and boost its businesses, while the missing bees threaten its farms and trade.

Karsk.t: The region of Krevsaty was ceded to the Thule seven years ago. Karsk's proxy senator is praised for having provided all the mithril and funds for a new army up front.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not described directly, and appears only through the wider references to other nations' armies and merchants.

Miekarova.t: Miechernya was conceded to Otkodov, displacing Varushkans, and Mieriada is rumoured to be at risk of being traded away in a new peace.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: its town of Meade is cited as a small city Delev might come to equal.

Ossium.t: Two regions of Ossium are claimed by the Thule, which chafes with Varushkans. The Vale of the Sunless Depths beneath a town there is cited in the argument over Imperial bourse seats.

Otkodov.t: The five-year peace treaty with Otkodov, lucrative but costly in ceded land, expires this year. Varushkans fear its renegotiation may cost more regions.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar's dominance of Varushkan metal trade and the old dispute over the Eternal Shafts of Time fuel Delev's rivalry. A proposed Synod mandate would strip it of the Delev Market stream and 2 thrones of taxation.

The Semmerlak.t: Delev guards the road from the Semmerlak, and the Great Market would add a rank to the Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak's ministry.

Volodmartz.t: Cold Sun's scions destroyed vales in Volodmartz, unhoming many, and its region of Opascari is rumoured to be at risk of being traded to the Thule.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only in the Battle of the Weirwater Gate, fought at Delev, whose ruined gate was built into the new walls.

Over western hills.d: Ten Jotun armies besieged Landskeeper's Bulwark in Freemoor, where the Tusks and the Granite Pillar held on, and King Gudmundr offered terms of surrender. Marcher and Imperial Orc armies then struck through Alderly into Southmoor, while Highborn, Wintermark and League armies advanced from the south. In the Battle of the Oakleaves, rebel Mournfolk opened Sarcombe's gates to the Tusks and the Bounders. Threatened with losing their supply lines, the Jotun withdrew into Liathaven. Six thousand Imperial soldiers fell. Chalkdowns, Ore Hills and Greensward remain Jotun-held, and the Senate may now assign the territory. Knights of Eleonaris fought on both sides. A battle opportunity was offered to kill Haakon.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: a Highborn Assembly statement cites the Druj being forced back and the septs they enslave as further targets of the crusade of Loyalty.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn armies left the fronts at Feroz and distant Ayereed to fight in the Mournwold.

Highguard.t: The Granite Pillar helped hold Landskeeper's Bulwark, and the Valiant Pegasus and the Seventh Wave (sped by Autumn magic) joined the southern push on Sarcombe. The Highborn Assembly's crusade of Loyalty gives anointed Highborn an extra hit point in the Mourn, and two competing mandates are proposed: one to hold conquered Jotun regions, one to strike into Hordalant.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Summer Storm and the Autumn Hammers marched with the Marcher armies through Alderly into Southmoor, part of the northern strike that helped break the Jotun hold.

Jotun.t: Despite their overwhelming numbers, the Jotun lost Southmoor and Sarcombe and withdrew into Liathaven to protect their supply lines, paying a heavier price than the Empire. Jarl Haakon defied King Gudmundr and Queen Yrsa to hold Farstrider's Watch with many champions, and still keeps Chalkdowns, Ore Hills and Greensward.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr armies were part of the alliance pushed out of the Mournwold before the Autumn Equinox, and Miaren is named as a likely line of retreat from Freemoor.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the southern Imperial force came up into Southmoor from the Brass Coast, where the Jotun had expected an attack from Kahraman.

The League.t: The Wolves of War joined the southern advance on Sarcombe, backed by independent captains and battle dancers of the Shadowed Flame. A Sarvosian consortium has offered to buy Haakon's effects for a museum if he is slain.

The Marches.t: The Tusks held Landskeeper's Bulwark and, with the Bounders, took Sarcombe when Marcher rebels opened its gates. Mournwold is Imperial again and likely, though not certainly, to be assigned to the Marches. The Strong Reeds guarded Bregasland, and Marchers who supported the Tusks or the Reeds may gain extra endurance through anointing.

Wintermark.t: The Narwhal's Spear raided the Jotun, linked the separate Imperial forces and helped rebels in Ore Hills and Chalkdowns. A yegarra champion, Halbera Strongarm, has since challenged their general, Determination of Ice Kaisa.

Over western hills.o: In Winter 386YE the Jotun pressed to take all of the Mournwold, but Imperial armies holding Freemoor and two forces striking into Southmoor liberated Sarcombe, drove the Jotun armies back into Liathaven and returned the Mournwold to Imperial control. Jarl Haakon refused to withdraw and now holds Farstrider's Watch in the Greensward.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: The Jotun and their Summer allies still hold the fortified Graven Rock, but the Strong Reeds' vigil kept them pinned there and unable to turn on the Imperial forces.

Hordalant/Vallorberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the yegarra Einar the Cunning came from the forests of Vallorberg to raid Alderly.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: The northern Imperial force advanced through Alderly into Southmoor, and a later Jotun strike to cut supply lines there was foiled by the Narwhal's Spear and the Drakes. Bryce the Hare must now stop Einar's yegarra hunting a New Longstwick herbalist.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: Chalkdowns remains under Jotun control, but rebellion grew there as Jotun armies tried to stamp out the guerrillas.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: The Jotun swept into Freemoor and besieged Landskeeper's Bulwark, but the Tusks and the Granite Pillar held it, refused Gudmundr's surrender terms and repelled a later assault by the Fell Hammers and the Mandowla's Roar.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Mentioned in passing: a third of the Jotun forces turned towards Alderly and Green March, and the northern Imperial force passed through woods on its border.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Jarl Haakon now holds the region from Farstrider's Watch with veteran warbands and champions. A battle opportunity to kill him was offered, with Friar Heggy Rosemund of the Greensward joining the fight.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: Still Jotun-held, Ore Hills was a centre of rebellion: Imperial heroes aided its miners, defeated three Summerborn champions, and the miners armed resisters elsewhere.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Southmoor was conquered by the Empire after victory at Miller's Crossing and the Battle of the Oakleaves, when rebels opened Sarcombe's gates. The town was scarred by the fighting and Jotun control there was ended.

Ayereed.t: Mentioned in passing: the Seventh Wave came from the distant Ayereed front, sped to the Mournwold by Autumn magic.

Bregasland.t: The Strong Reeds stayed to defend Bregasland, turning back Jotun champions who tried to push into the marshes from Graven Rock and earning the grudging respect of the locals.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar marched from Casinea to reinforce Landskeeper's Bulwark.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the Valiant Pegasus marched north from Feroz to join the attack on Southmoor.

Hordalant.t: A proposed alternative Highborn mandate would strengthen Highborn armies attacking into Hordalant. It competes with a mandate to hold conquered Jotun regions.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun had expected an Imperial attack to come from Kahraman.

Liathaven.t: The Jotun armies retreated west into Liathaven after the Empire threatened the supply lines that run out of it into Southmoor.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is named as a place the Freemoor defenders might be forced back into.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher and Imperial Orc armies set out through Mitwold, where the Drakes had earlier repelled ships on the river Meade.

Mournwold.t: The Empire won Southmoor and with it control of the territory, which the Senate may now assign. Jarl Haakon still holds three regions from Farstrider's Watch, and the Jotun have not given up their ambition to retake it.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn are said to look west towards the wealth along the coast of the Sea of Snow.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is named as a possible line of retreat for the Freemoor defenders and as a direction the Jotun expected an attack from.

Parched earth.d: Each rune-marked Dry Patrician is driving the Blight towards a region beside the Great Grasses. It can only be destroyed by Words of Ending at magnitude 18, while Ashwalkers fall to Turns the Circle. Destroying one halts the spread into that region for a year, and conjunctions were found to the Sobral Grasses, Jade Range and Lucksprings. Evidence points to the Aldea di Tutamen family as the source, and the Silent Bell may know more. Dyan of Eagle's Striding offered a magnitude 140 projection to flood the Great Grasses with the Scorrero, but it should not be cast before the curse is broken. A Senate-commissioned Silver Chalice Grand Lodge was also proposed.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is described as scarred by the Druj occupation, which tried to break the spirit of its people.

Highguard.t: The Assembly of Nine has asked the Silent Bell to investigate the Blightheart and the Tutamen family's place in Highborn history, with a report due at the Spring Equinox. High Chalcis in Reikos was offered as a possible site for the Silver Chalice Grand Lodge.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn lands face the spread of the Blight into Segura and Kahraman. Nemi i Riqueza and the hakima Bakar i Riqueza were made responsible for two of the conjunctions, and the Tutamen family is suspected as the source of the curse.

Wintermark.t: New Dunhall in Hahnmark was proposed as a Grand Lodge site, drawing on the grimnir tradition and Wintermark's fine artisans to supply healing magic items.

Parched earth.o: Lutomysla Niegoslava's Senate-commissioned appraisal of the Blight in Madruga, worked with the Unfettered Mind, set out how to halt, end and heal the curse. It identified three rune-marked Dry Patricians threatening neighbouring regions and proposed a Grand Lodge for the Silver Chalice.

Hahnmark/Wood Heath.t: New Dunhall was offered as a Grand Lodge site, letting the Grandmaster buy items such as Escharotic Cauldrons and Phials of the Sun each season.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: If the Irremais-marked Patrician is not destroyed, the Dust Parador can buy no more than 12 wains of mithril, falling by 3 wains each season once the blight takes hold. A wounded Lasambrian champion, Hitar of the Jaboon, is also present.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: Quzar was proposed as a Grand Lodge site, focusing the Silver Chalice on magical catastrophes and giving its magicians the protection of the kohan.

Reikos/Chalcis Mount.t: High Chalcis was proposed as a Grand Lodge site, allowing the Grandmaster to buy herbs from its gardens each season.

Segura/Lucksprings.t: The Naeve-marked Patrician threatens the region and, if unchecked, the Cerevado Nets' ilium. The Azoth asked for dust from its remains and offered Bakar i Riqueza's ritual against Ashwalkers.

Segura/Sobral Grasses.t: Gideon of the Farthest Shore is trapped north of Gita's Veils after trying to destroy the Yoorn-marked Patrician alone. Grandmaster Eliza was charged with rescuing him and stopping the blight reaching the region.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark was offered as a site for the Silver Chalice Grand Lodge, which would focus the order on natural disasters such as the Dunsfall Sinkhole.

Kahraman.t: The Irremais-marked Dry Patrician was crossing into Kahraman, threatening the Jade Range and the Dust Parador's mithril trade.

Madruga.t: The Great Grasses lie blighted and uninhabitable, and the appraisal offers ways to contain the curse, find its source and possibly flood the region clean. Quzar was proposed as a Grand Lodge site.

Reikos.t: Reikos was proposed as a Grand Lodge site, where the Silver Chalice would focus on healing the scars of war left by the Druj occupation.

Segura.t: Two Dry Patricians threaten Segura, one bound for the Sobral Grasses and one for the Lucksprings. Each region would begin to blight if its Patrician is not destroyed.

Part of this together.d: Lady Clarice Novarion's change of doctrine passed the General Assembly 3013-159, and the Assembly of Nine endorsed it. Priests spent personal liao promoting it, and three effects followed. Pride in the Empire surged, making virtue-focused statements of principle likelier to produce mandates for a year. Interest in the Assembly of the Way revived: priests preaching the Way gain two extra Synod votes until Autumn 386YE, and that Assembly's greater-majority statements carry General Assembly weight this summit. Acceptance of orcs also increased. Abroad, the Sumaah will urge retention of the old doctrine, while the Commonwealth and the Sarcophan approve. Mandates to spread the new doctrine to the Delves and Asavea are possible.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Lady Clarice Novarion proposed the change and was widely praised for the poetic, inspiring prose of the new Doctrine.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were thought very unlikely to care one way or the other about the change.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel somehow learned of the change and responded smugly, as they do to everything.

Highguard.t: The new Doctrine satisfied Highborn guardians seeking words to fortify the soul. The Highborn Assembly is one of the bodies that could mandate missionaries to carry it to Asavea's hidden pilgrims.

Imperial Orcs.t: The doctrine affirms that orcs share in virtue as equals. Credit for the change was given to the Imperial Orcs' example and their armies' service in every nation, and their priests Bonewall Rek and Bonewall Cole were credited with the earlier groundwork.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun were thought very unlikely to care one way or the other about the change.

Navarr.t: The change nurtures the growing relationships between the Navarr and the Great Forest Orc steadings settling in Therunin, Hercynia and Miaren.

The Marches.t: The change makes it impossible not to recognise the Mournwold Orcs as fellow Marchers. Its words also gave Marcher friars a rousing sermon for the muddy fields.

Urizen.t: Urizen questors found the new Doctrine able to withstand the intellectual rigour they demand.

Part of this together.o: In Winter 385YE the Synod's replacement of the Doctrine of Human Destiny with the Doctrine of Enlightenment, which recognises orcs and humans as equals in the Way, was embraced across the Empire with little opposition. It spread swiftly through all ten nations and sharply reduced prejudice against orcs.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: a proposed mandate urges pilgrims in Sarcophan to follow Bastion's lead in embracing the change.

Hercynia.t: Relations with the Great Forest Orc steadings in Hercynia are strengthened by the new acceptance of orcs.

Miaren.t: The change nurtures growing relationships with the Great Forest Orc steadings in Miaren.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold Orcs there gain wider acceptance, now unmistakably recognised as fellow Marchers.

Therunin.t: The change eases relations with the Great Forest Orc steadings in Therunin.

Parts of speech.d: Tabris, Son of Armisael, Bishop of the Navigators, preached in the Delves, gaining an extra ministry and bringing Sarcophan visitors to Imperial congregations. The Sumaah urged their faithful to keep the Doctrine of Human Destiny and discouraged liao sales to foreigners. In Asavea, missionaries found hidden sects and tales of Alberto Acciai, a Wayist rebel leader whom the Synod might recognise. The wayfarer Enoch is returning to speak with Athiel Westernborn. The Plenum is openly discussing more aid to the Grendel. The Free Folk became Dawnish yeofolk near Caer Faucon, boosting the Proffered Hand, and at Tabris's request will send 2 liao each season to the Abbey of Reconciliation.

Dawn.t: The Free Folk asked the egregores to be welcomed as yeofolk, joined Dawnish armies or set out as knights-errant, and their priests add 3 liao each season to the Lady of the Proffered Hand.

Grendel.t: Angered by Imperial missionaries, the Asavean Plenum is openly discussing sending more aid to its Grendel allies, though a diplomatic spat currently gives it pause.

Highguard.t: Highborn wayfarers led the missionary effort and paid the heaviest price, with eight killed in Asavea. Athiel Westernborn is sought by the returning wayfarer Enoch, and the Abbey of Reconciliation now receives 2 liao each season from the grateful Free Folk.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: an in-character story features a hidden Asavean congregation retelling a tale of Inga Tarn and a little Navarr girl.

The League.t: Prosperity and Ambition congregations in Tassato and Sarvos gain extra income from curious Sarcophan visitors, and Arsenio Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato's liao vision of Saul of the Cora is linked to an Asavean strand of the Way.

Urizen.t: Urizen priests were slow to join the missionary effort, sensing the Synod was not truly united, though Prosperity and Ambition congregations in Redoubt gain extra income from Sarcophan visitors.

Varushka.t: Varushkan priests were reluctant missionaries, doubting the Synod's unity, but Prosperity and Ambition congregations in Karsk benefit from Sarcophan visitors arriving via the Sarcophan Mooring.

Parts of speech.o: After the Winter Solstice mandates, Imperial missionaries spread the Doctrine of Enlightenment abroad, winning interest in the Sarcophan Delves but angering the Sumaah and provoking Asavea to execute nearly thirty Imperial priests. Meanwhile the Free Folk settled in Dawn as Imperial citizens.

Astolat/Coombe.t: The Free Folk founded a village near Caer Faucon in Coombe, whose influx of yeofolk brought a small but appreciable improvement to the House of the Proffered Hand.

Astolat.t: The Free Folk settled near Caer Faucon in Astolat, building a bustling village and strengthening the House of the Proffered Hand.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Tabris's mandate urged Sarcophan adherents of the Way to follow Bastion's lead in embracing the new doctrine.

Karsk.t: Thanks to the Sarcophan Mooring, every congregation preaching Prosperity or Ambition in Karsk gains an extra 18 rings next season from Sarcophan visitors.

Necropolis.t: Congregations preaching Prosperity or Ambition in Necropolis gain an extra 18 rings next season from visitors from the Sarcophan Delves.

Redoubt.t: Congregations preaching Prosperity or Ambition in Redoubt gain an extra 18 rings next season as Sarcophan visitors come to see what the excitement is about.

Sarvos.t: Congregations preaching Prosperity or Ambition in Sarvos gain an extra 18 rings next season from curious Sarcophan visitors.

Tassato.t: Congregations preaching Prosperity or Ambition in Tassato gain an extra 18 rings next season from Sarcophan visitors drawn by the new doctrine.

Patterns of fairytales.d: The Silver Chalice aided flood victims in Segura and Kahraman, saving hundreds of lives, and wealthy Freeborn offered to plan a Chalice grand lodge on the Coast if endowed with 25 crystal mana. The Penumbral Veil altered most Imperial night skies. A Wyrm–Mountain conjunction left older war-enchanting arcane projections unusable but exchangeable for mana. The Church of The Little Mother took over the Loom of Spells and will auction it. The Mystics of Ishal named three possible Meeting Place sites, and the Sentinel Gate will open to their Aviary. Sadogua's heralds joined Marcher Wassails, and Azoth, Lashonar, Barien, Basileia's heralds and an unknown herald announced visits to Anvil. A thousand Bleak Knights remain camped in Madruga.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the herald from the Silver Woods says her sister has business with Dawn this summit, and expects Wintermark to keep nosy Dawnish away from her own meeting.

Grendel.t: Gentle rains in Grendel-held Feroz help wash away scars of Governor Rahab's occupation, Feroz is named as a suitable site for a Silver Chalice lodge, and developments in Mareave had halted earlier lodge plans.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the night skies above Highguard's Casinea are, for some unexplained reason, untouched by the Penumbral Veil.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: orcs in Skarsind are among those in the north-west who may have suffered unsettling animal attacks.

Jotun.t: The Silver Woods herald walked out of Jotun lands, Jotun-held Tromsa, Skallahn, Hordalant and Bregasland border all three candidate Meeting Place sites, and the City of Locks has accepted a contract on the life of Jarl Haakon in the Mournwold.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the skies above Therunin are untouched by the Penumbral Veil, and Hercynia is among the north-western territories seeing more animal attacks.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn suffered over two hundred flood deaths and widespread homelessness, eased by Silver Chalice relief; Segura's bridges and the Cerevado Nets are broken, the Sunset Roads stay closed, and Bleak Knights loom over Quzar in Madruga.

The League.t: Tassato's gossips mourn the loss of Sanvar Isk as the Church of The Little Mother takes over the Loom of Spells and its mountebank work crews, and plans to auction access to it.

The Marches.t: Sadogua's heralds joined Marcher Wassails, Blessing of New Spring farms not using Yaw'nagrah's boon will yield Shinemoon elixirs, a Well of Shadows door appeared in Tower March, and Upwold enjoyed gentle rains.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Ematius of Urizen, as Archmage of Winter, declined Tharim's new deal, and the Urizen ritual Quick Study is noted as working with the Loom of Spells.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua's servant the Almighty Panjandrum will continue to answer Missives for Sadogua sent by Varushkan magicians.

Wintermark.t: The Mark gains Sadogua's full backing for Dripping Echoes of the Fen on Rundahl Marsh, a Sentinel Gate conjunction to the Aviary of Ishal, praise for the mystic Wiglaf, Sorin's cold prosperity in Hahnmark, and visits from Barien's herald Timbrel and the Silver Woods herald.

Patterns of fairytales.o: A Winter 386YE grab-bag of magical happenings across the Empire, chiefly the Silver Chalice's relief of the Scorrero flood victims, a Grand Conjunction that permanently disabled warlike arcane projections, and a series of eternal and herald visits and offers.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Coracle Rock on the North Fens border is a candidate site for the new Meeting Place.

Hordalant/Blutgahn.t: Coracle Rock, on Blutgahn's border with the North Fens, is one of the Mystics of Ishal's three candidate sites.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: With the bridges down, Gambit is now the only secure way to enter the Sobral and Segura from the north.

Kallavesa/Skymark.t: A Sentinel Gate conjunction will open to the Aviary of Ishal in Skymark at 22:05 on Friday for a Goosewhisper ceremony.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: A thousand Ashen Knights loyal to Tharim remain camped in Lightsea near Quzar, showing no sign of leaving.

Segura/Sobral Grasses.t: The Sobral Bridge is the only crossing left standing, leaving the Sobral reachable securely only via Gambit.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: The garrison of Rest in Stark was visited by the Witch or Wit of the Silver Woods, an unidentified herald seeking ambitious icewalker diplomats.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: The shores of Lake Nutjuitoq where the Suaq Wastes meet Tromsa are a candidate site for a new Meeting Place.

Upwold/Tower March.t: A round green door to Sadogua's Well of Shadows appeared in an ancient oak a day's hike east of King's Stoke, reached by a newly remembered path.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: not named, but as an Imperial territory its night skies fall under the Empire-wide Penumbral Veil.

Bregasland.t: Coracle Rock, an ancient dolmen on the border of North Fens and Hordalant's Blutgahn, is one of three possible sites for a new Wintermark Meeting Place.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea's night skies are inexplicably untouched by the Penumbral Veil.

Feroz.t: Gentle rains help wash away the scars of Governor Rahab's occupation, and Feroz is named as a suitable location for a Silver Chalice grand lodge.

Hahnmark.t: Wintermark magicians brought cold prosperity to herb gardens as Sorin's servants culled weak plants, and the territory is among those seeing more animal attacks.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is listed among north-western territories where people may have had unsettling encounters with animals.

Hordalant.t: Coracle Rock, on the border between Blutgahn and Bregasland's North Fens, is a candidate site for the new Meeting Place.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman suffered some flood damage and receives Silver Chalice relief until Summer 387YE; Gambit is now the only secure route into the Sobral, though Kahraman is thought a poor choice for a lodge.

Kallavesa.t: Dripping Echoes of the Fen cast on Rundahl Marsh will now protect the whole territory, the Sentinel Gate will open to the Aviary of Ishal, and Gull's Isle on its border is a candidate Meeting Place site.

Madruga.t: Madruga's blight prompted the flooding, Segura cannot now be reached from it, its skies escape the Penumbral Veil, and a thousand Bleak Knights camp in Lightsea while some wander to watch people.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: developments in Mareave halted the Chalice's lodge plans, and the Golden Pyramid's proposed structure there is the yardstick for any Coast lodge.

Mournwold.t: Its skies are spared the Penumbral Veil, Night heralds joined Wassail even here, and the City of Locks' Guild of Accountants is working on a contract to kill Jarl Haakon here.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: not named, but as an Imperial territory it lies under the Empire-wide Penumbral Veil.

Segura.t: Segura bore the brunt of the flood: two of three bridges are destroyed, Cerevado's waterfront flattened, the Cerevado Nets damaged and the Sunset Roads closed, though Silver Chalice aid saved many lives and it is a candidate lodge site.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq sees a rise in attacks by mundane animals and restless guardians, borders Gull's Isle, and received a mysterious herald at the garrison of Rest in Stark.

Skallahn.t: Gull's Isle, a tidal island in the Gullet on the border of Skallahn, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq, is a candidate site for the new Meeting Place.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is listed among north-western territories where unsettling animal encounters may be roleplayed.

Tassato.t: Tassato's salons lament Sanvar Isk's fall while the Church of The Little Mother's child overseers now drive the Loom's mountebank crews, though they pay actual money.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the night skies above Therunin remain untouched by the Penumbral Veil.

Tromsa.t: The shores of Lake Nutjuitoq, where Tromsa meets the Suaq Wastes, are one of three potential sites for a new Meeting Place.

Upwold.t: Gentle rains fall on Upwold, a Well of Shadows door appears in Tower March, and the Tharim herald Obligatus remains at the Copse of the Bone Birch while two companions are unaccounted for.

Pay in blood.d: The loss affected every regio, including those in conquered territories, but only Imperial citizens; foreign magicians could still use them. The regio and their portals remain, but no Imperial citizen can use a regio to strengthen a Spring ritual, target one at a territory through the Imperial regio, or affect a whole territory from a local regio. Rituals such as Rivers of Life, Thunderous Deluge and Hallow of the Green World have become impossible to perform. Workarounds such as the Citadel Guard's targeting or Align the Celestial Net also fail. No divination could detect the cause. How long it will last, and whether anything can be done, is unknown; the earlier loss lasted four seasons.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, but Liathaven, which they hold, is cited as a conquered territory whose regio are closed to Imperial magicians.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the ritual The Dance of Navarr and Thorn is listed among the Spring rituals that can no longer be performed.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: a Thule coven is given as an example of foreign magicians who can still use a Spring regio inside the Empire's borders.

Urizen.t: Urizen magicians were quick to identify that their Spring regios had lost their power entirely, and like all Imperial citizens they can no longer use them for Spring rituals.

Pay in blood.o: Shortly after the Spring Equinox, Imperial magicians found they could no longer draw on the power of any Spring regio for ritual magic. Historians found a precedent from Empress Deanne's reign, when the Empire lost access to Winter regio for a year after Highborn magisters disrupted a formal parley with the eternal Agramant.

Liathaven.t: Liathaven is named as a conquered territory whose regio are also closed to Imperial magicians for Spring magic, though others can still use them.

Peace song.d: Lashonar's bird-like heralds sang in every tavern and inn across Dawn, lamenting the dead and urging peace with the Druj, who had sued for peace. All four Dawnish armies became a fifth less effective when attacking, though they defended normally. The civil service set out options: enmity, a Synod judgement to exterminate the heralds, a joint exclusionist response, or a Synod-backed peace in the Barrens. The Conclave removed Lashonar's amity without declaring enmity. The Dawnish National Assembly condemned the message and named Lady Tamain Sepulchre, backed by a hundred liao, to oppose it. She composed and popularised 'The Heralds of Lashonar'. The penalty applied through the autumn campaign but was gone by the Winter Solstice.
