Dawn.t: The heralds' relentless songs sapped the morale of all four Dawnish armies, cutting their offensive effectiveness by a fifth for the autumn campaign. The National Assembly answered by sending Lady Tamain Sepulchre, whose counter-song ended the effect by the Winter Solstice.

Druj.t: Lashonar's heralds took up the cause of peace with the Druj, singing that those the Dawnish killed had come to sue for peace and offering to split the Barrens. The Synod was given the option of demanding an immediate peace with them, but the Empire chose to resist the eternal instead.

Peace song.o: In Autumn 380YE heralds of the eternal Lashonar flooded Dawn with mournful songs against the war in the Barrens, sapping the morale of all four Dawnish armies. The Conclave stripped Lashonar of amity and the Dawnish National Assembly countered the songs, ending the effect by the Winter Solstice.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: an Earl consulted the weavers of Weirwater, who judged that the heralds' influence was not a spell as the Empire understands it but was magical in nature because Lashonar is a being of magic.

Peaks and planes.d: Following Clytemnestra's and Jedediah Boon's statements, the Urizen Assembly could send mages, sentinels and sword scholars to help bring in the Marcher harvest, raising every Marcher farm's income but halving the Doyen of the Spires' research. Elagabala's alternative would also push Urizen armies to support the Tusks and Strong Reeds against Jotun. The Marcher Assembly could send friars to Urizen, boosting Urizen congregations at a cost to Marcher ones, or back Rhubarb Ironwood's more confrontational version. The Assembly's and Emperor Vesna's denunciations of those praising the condemned covens instead drove more Marchers to support them. Jack Tiller, Frankie Moulder and Old Tam Witch-hazel were coming to Anvil to talk it out.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Elagabala's proposed alternate mandate speaks of Urizen helping defend the Marches from Jotun incursion.

The Marches.t: The Marches might gain Urizeni harvest helpers and could send friars to Urizen at a cost to its own congregations, while its people grew openly at odds with their Assembly over its condemnation of the cursing covens and its failure to see sorcerers punished.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Assembly could send its mages, sentinels and sword scholars to labour on Marcher farms at the cost of halving the Doyen of the Spires' research, and its congregations would gain from any visiting Marcher friars.

Peaks and planes.o: In Summer 386YE the Marcher and Urizen National Assemblies were offered competing Synod mandates for a pilgrimage exchange to mend relations after the Cold Sun affair. Meanwhile a growing rift opened between the Marcher Assembly and ordinary Marchers over the condemned landskeeper covens who cursed Urizen.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: Mentioned in passing: Jedediah Boon is named as being of the Ore Hills, his pride in his land having inspired Clytemnestra's pilgrimage.

Bregasland.t: Under Elagabala's proposed alternate mandate, Urizen military units would be encouraged to support the Strong Reeds defending Bregasland, with any that did not losing strength as warriors went to the Marches instead.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Old Tam Witch-hazel, a Mitwold landskeeper, was persuaded to travel to Anvil to speak with the shunned covens.

Mournwold.t: The past cursing of the Mournwold, which killed thousands of Marchers, fuels the present distrust of magic, and Elagabala's proposed mandate would encourage Urizen forces to support the Tusks in the Mournwold.

Pebbles drawn from a heap.d: The Urizen National Assembly upheld a mandate by Alcuin, backed by Cardinal Veikko Bondforger. Tarquinius's statement offered a middle way, and Palaphon Ankarien's Conclave declaration warned that sharing magical secrets could be sorcery. Spiral's citizens therefore warded the Salt Lord's palace free, with further wards for payment. The Grendel accepted, and the Citadel Guard stopped deteriorating until after Summer. The Salt Lord proposed a Senate-created Spiral Envoy, and the Northern Mareave Trading Consortium offered to buy weirwood and white granite. The Circle of Black Sand sought to trade ritual lore. Speaker Morna would visit Anvil over the robbery of Maistir Bradach. The opportunities lasted until the end of Autumn 384YE.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; the page only refers to the malign forces of the Black Plateau, which the mithril wards guard against.

Grendel.t: Salt Lord Kaliact accepted free wards for her palace and paid for any others, and her merchants, the Northern Mareave Trading Consortium and the Circle of Black Sand sought trade, while Speaker Morna was coming to Anvil to demand answers, and perhaps reparations, for the robbery of Maistir Bradach.

Urizen.t: Urizen kept the Block's secrets while warding the Salt Lord's palace, faced only a modest tribute and regained support for the Citadel Guard. It was also offered a national Spiral Envoy title and a white granite for mithril exchange.

Pebbles drawn from a heap.o: After the peace treaty ceded all of Spiral to the Grendel, Salt Lord Kaliact and the Urizen reached a compromise: Spiral's citizens would ward only her palace in Apulian with the Block's mithril wards, and the Citadel Guard could again be supported. The page also set out several time-limited Grendel trade, envoy and magical opportunities, and announced a diplomatic visit over an assault in Anvil.

Spiral/Apulus.t: The Salt Lord's palace in Apulian received the Block's mithril wards free, and the city became the hub for Grendel trade with the Consortium's representative and the Circle of Black Sand based there.

Spiral/Screed.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel merchant in the opening fiction complained of nightmares and a feeling of insignificance caused by 'the place in Screed'.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the Salt Lord's hands-off rule in Spiral is contrasted with the Grendel approach in Feroz, and an earlier Feroz Wind is listed for further reading.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Northern Mareave Trading Consortium, which offered to buy weirwood and white granite, takes its name from the region, though its representative was based in Apulian.

Redoubt.t: Grendel merchants began crossing the Onyx Path and Crow Road into Redoubt to trade for Urizen mana and metals, paying border tariffs. The Salt Lord planned to send armed mithril caravans through the Crow Road pass.

Spiral.t: Spiral was now wholly under Grendel rule, but its Urizen resources counted as being in a foreign rather than a conquered territory while the détente lasted. Its people paid a moderate tribute, warded the Salt Lord's palace and could again support the Citadel Guard.

Permit Great Forest Orcs to work the Thi.d: Proposed by the senator for Therunin and seconded by Karov, the motion answered an offer from the orcs of the Great Forest to tend the Thimble's weirwood groves. In return the orcs receive four wains of weirwood each season. The agreement lasts until the treaty with the Great Forest Orcs ends or the motion is revoked. The motion passed, and as a result the Great Forest Orcs work the Thimble, removing the cost to the Empire of maintaining that Bourse resource.

Navarr.t: Navarr's senator for Therunin proposed the motion, handing the work of the weirwood groves in a Navarr territory to the Great Forest Orcs in return for a share of the timber.

Permit Great Forest Orcs to work the Thi.o: In Autumn 381YE the Senate passed a motion accepting the Great Forest Orcs' offer to work the Thimble, the weirwood groves of Therunin, in return for four wains of weirwood each season.

Therunin.t: The Thimble, Therunin's weirwood groves, is now worked by the Great Forest Orcs, who take four wains of weirwood each season while the Empire no longer bears the cost of its upkeep.

Permit dredging of Feverwater.d: Proposed by the senator for Therunin and seconded by Miaren, the motion authorised an attempt to dredge the Feverwater. The cost was hard to estimate but put at more than ten wains of weirwood; Merel of the Pathfinders of Therunin later paid thirteen wains after the Spring Equinox. The civil service warned that the lake is home to swamp monsters likely to kill many who try, and noted that no magical netting techniques are known, the Brass Coast using ordinary nets on the Scorrero. Once complete, the dredging yielded a modest four measures of crafting materials each season. The position was treated as a Navarr national appointment, voted on by Navarr senators.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the civil service mused that the apparent madness of the venture might lead Druj forces active in the area to underestimate the Empire in some unpredictable way.

Navarr.t: A Navarr pathfinder, Merel, was granted the right to dredge the Feverwater and paid thirteen wains of weirwood for it, and the resulting position became a Navarr national appointment chosen by Navarr senators.

Permit dredging of Feverwater.o: In Summer 377YE the Senate passed, by 26 votes to 1, a motion permitting Meryl of Navarr to scout and then dredge the Feverwater, a lake partly within Therunin, for materials using riverboats.

Therunin.t: Therunin's senator proposed the dredging of the Feverwater, a monster-haunted lake partly within the territory, which went on to produce four measures of crafting materials each season.

Petals in the snow.d: The Kraft Brothers grow vlinderbloem in Hahnmark to brew the narcotic viezesmaak, while the rival Zuredruiven vintners have learned to cultivate draaikolkbloem at scale. Hahnmark's farm owners were to vote at the Tree of Names at the Spring Equinox on whether to keep growing vlinderbloem or end the Kraft deal. The Senate could commission the Zuredruiven Benefice in Kalpamark, raising herb garden investment and creating a Zuredruiven Cultivator title to trade draaikolkbloem for Woven Fortune, but this would drive the Kraft Brothers out. Alternatively, both partnerships could be ended amicably. Herb garden owners were also secretly offered draaikolkbloem in place of some herbs, but if more than 20 accepted, the Kraft Brothers would withdraw.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: rumour holds that Astolat's wines are finer than the Zuredruiven vintages.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Seguran vintages are said to compare favourably with the Zuredruiven wines.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: a dubious bottle passed off as a genuine 312YE Sarvosi vintage features in the story, and Sarvos's wines are said to outclass the Zuredruiven ones.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's people had to decide between two rival Sarcophan partnerships, through a farmers' vote, a possible new Wintermark national title of Zuredruiven Cultivator, and a quiet offer to herb garden owners.

Petals in the snow.o: Rival Sarcophan merchants, the Kraft Brothers and the Zuredruiven vintners, had both invested in Hahnmark's farms. After being kept from discovering each other at the Winter Solstice, Hahnmark's farmers were offered a choice over which partnership, if either, to keep.

Hahnmark/Kalpamark.t: Kalpamark was the proposed site of the Zuredruiven Benefice, a great work that would raise herb garden investment, produce draaikolkbloem, or Imperial roseweald if the deal failed, at the cost of the Kraft Brothers' departure.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat's wines are cited as finer than those of the Zuredruiven vineyards.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark's farmers and herb gardeners faced a choice between keeping vlinderbloem production for the Kraft Brothers, switching to the Zuredruiven vintners' draaikolkbloem, or ending both deals, with the risk that a mixed decision would drive both away.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: a supposed Sarvosi vintage of 312YE appears in the story, and Sarvos wines are said to surpass the Zuredruiven vintages.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Seguran vintages are rumoured to be finer than the Zuredruiven wines.

Phantasms and foam.d: The Red Wind Corsairs, with allied soldiers from Dawn, the Marches and Urizen, raided and pushed into Siroc Bayou. Day magic helped them cope with its warped time and distance, and they ended about three-fifths of the way to claiming it. Phantasmal soldiers and beasts then began attacking after the Maw of Siakha closed. The Fire of the South returned from Bregasland to guard Quzar. The Wings of Kobol and other Suranni forces took Free Landing, closed the Maw of Siakha and broke the Children of Wrecks. Freeborn corsairs rescued relics from Atalaya, and surviving wreckers fled or planned final attacks on Madruga, the Necropolis and Tassato.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish soldiers, used to wild and dangerous places, marched with the Red Wind Corsairs into the bayou.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj-held marshes of Sarangrave are contrasted with the Bayou, which does not actively try to kill intruders.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Corsairs slipped past the Grendel to reach Feroz, phantoms of Grendel haunt the bayou, and Grendel vessels hunt the fleeing wreckers.

Highguard.t: Wreckers carrying a cursed bucket of Siakha's water sailed up the Couros to extinguish the flame of Britta's shrine in the Necropolis, and its Guardian, Neala Blackhawk, was charged with stopping them.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South marched home from Bregasland, which the Jotun held at the time.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn armies advanced into Siroc Bayou and guarded Quzar, and Freeborn corsairs recovered lost relics of the Founding from Atalaya as the Iron Confederacy took Free Landing, the nation's first home.

The League.t: A wrecker crew led by the Duke of Lies attacked the Sapphire Stairs in Tassato, threatening the Keeper's income and Sarvos' farms, while the guardians of Sarvos killed fleeing pirates.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni soldiers, attuned to the bayou's magical resonances, accompanied the Red Wind Corsairs.

Phantasms and foam.o: In Summer 388YE the Red Wind Corsairs pushed deep into the strange, Night-touched Siroc Bayou, where phantasms slowed their advance. The Iron Confederacy, aided by Freeborn corsairs, conquered Free Landing and destroyed the Children of Wrecks.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wings of Kobol are noted as the navy that led the earlier assault on Cazar Straits.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: A near-catastrophic tempest and massive waves from the battle in Free Landing pounded Calvos Sound, but its Freeborn, used to the sea invading their homes, coped.

Madruga/Crucible.t: The Corsairs hope to retake the Crucible from the Bayou; wreckers carrying 'The Snapping Face' passed through, and part of the Crucible lies under the Echo of Transformation.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: The Iron Confederacy conquered Free Landing with Freeborn help, closing the Maw of Siakha and breaking the Children of Wrecks, while relics of Atalaya were carried to Quzar.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: The Fire of the South took up defensive positions around Quzar to watch for the Iron Confederacy, and the region was battered by the Free Landing tempest.

Madruga/Siroc Bayou.t: The Red Wind Corsairs raided for treasure and got about three-fifths of the way to claiming the wild Bayou, before phantasms of Night magic slowed their advance to a crawl.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: Mentioned in passing: a merchant-prince with vineyards in Bocche promised four wains of weirwood to the Keeper of the Sapphire Stair if the wreckers were repelled.

Bay of Catazar.t: The only Children of Wrecks to escape fled into the Bay, where Imperial, Grendel and Sarcophan vessels will hunt them, and the remnants vowed to go out bringing ruin to the Empire.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South left Bregasland, having fulfilled their loyalty to the Marchers, and marched home.

Feroz.t: The Corsairs put to port here, and the Suranni fleets sailed from Feroz to assault Free Landing; the Iron Confederacy also crushed the wreckers on the islands of Feroz.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs marched through Kahraman, where villagers cheered them and offered cheap food and drink.

Madruga.t: Imperial forces made headway in Siroc Bayou while the Suranni took Free Landing. A magnitude 80 Autumn enchantment lies over the territory, and wreckers threaten to curse it with Thunderous Tread of the Trees.

Necropolis.t: A wrecker sloop carrying a boon of Siakha sailed up the Couros to quench the eternal flame at Britta's shrine; if it was repelled, pilgrims' donations would rise by four crowns a season.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: its deadly marshes are compared unfavourably with the less hostile Siroc Bayou.

Sarvos.t: The guardians of Sarvos gave fleeing pirates a fatal welcome, but Sarvos' farms and vineyards stood to lose 36 rings a season if the attack on the Sapphire Stairs succeeded.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs marched through Segura, cheered by its villages.

Tassato.t: Wreckers flying a crude image of Dumon sailed up the Vassa to clog the Sapphire Stairs with corpses and kelp, and the Keeper Raphael Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato was charged with killing Siakha's heralds.

Pieces missing everywhere.d: Silas of the Cenotaph's mandate swelled congregations and stirred interest in a hugely ambitious construction at Bastion. Lady Josephine's mandate began changing Highborn attitudes towards lineaged, orcs and other sapient peoples. Jared's mandate let the Assembly support a chosen nation and respond to other assemblies' mandates. Urizen's Assembly had rejected such influence, and mandates were proposed in several nations to refuse or reciprocate Highborn aid. General Barachel arranged a meeting with the Vendarri on Greenstone Isle for nine Highborn, though the conjunction allowed fifteen, raising the possibility of betrayal. Asenath's Granite Pillar laid Aureli Major to rest, leaving only Clypion's miasma pillar for a possible Highborn mandate.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn Assembly's new outreach mandate cannot be used to contact the Dawnish in the Barrens.

Druj.t: Having been driven from Zenith, the Druj face Highborn efforts to destroy their remaining miasma pillar and holdouts in Clypion, and to win over their subjugated septs, beginning with the Vendarri.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: General Asenath hoped the Grendel would witness Imperial triumph; they are likely aware of it, but whether they were moved is impossible to tell.

Highguard.t: Highguard's people swelled their congregations, began to set aside prejudice against lineaged and orcs, and gained new Assembly powers. Its generals also created chances to contact Barrens septs and to destroy Zenith's last miasma pillar.

Imperial Orcs.t: Highborn attitudes towards the Imperial Orcs began to change as Lady Josephine's mandate urged citizens to renounce long-standing prejudice and judge by Virtue alone.

Navarr.t: Two mandates were proposed in the Navarr Assembly: Aneira Exiles End's would refuse further Highborn aid beyond the vallorn and City of Dreams, while Fintan Nighthaven's would seek to repay Highguard's sacrifice.

The League.t: The League Assembly faced rival mandates: Sofonisba Amilcara di Sarvos proposed refusing all Highborn aid, while Astrid Rezia Fjellrevening di Tassato proposed offering friendship and aid in return.

Urizen.t: Urizen, having rejected Highborn influence, could pass a mandate refusing all Highborn aid, or Tarquinius Ankarien's alternative to reciprocate; refusal would also block the Highborn mandate to destroy Clypion's pillar.

Varushka.t: Anastasiya Volkov proposed a mandate for the Varushkan Assembly to accept Highborn aid and offer aid in return, granting it the ability to respond to Highborn mandates.

Pieces missing everywhere.o: Buoyed by Pride in recent victories, the Highborn Assembly passed three mandates with greater majorities, softening prejudice against lineaged and orcs, spurring religious construction, and granting the Assembly new powers to aid or answer other nations. Other assemblies faced proposals either to refuse Highborn aid or to reciprocate it, while Highborn generals opened contact with the Vendarri and the chance to clear the last Druj miasma from Zenith.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: Greenstone Isle, in the mouth of the Greenstone estuary, was agreed as the site where nine Highborn could meet the Vendarri Pyroclast Garl Huonor and his ritualists.

Zenith/Clypion.t: Clypion holds Zenith's last miasma pillar. A Highborn mandate could send priests, alongside Urizeni sentinels and sword scholars, to destroy it with a powerful consecration.

Zenith/Iteri.t: Mentioned in passing: the Senate paid to tear down the miasma pillar in Iteri.

Zenith/Lustri.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial heroes had already destroyed Lustri's miasma pillar, and General Asenath's orders proclaimed her stand there.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar destroyed the miasma pillar in Proceris.

Bastion.t: An appraisal by Eilian Sweetwater set out a hugely ambitious construction to make Bastion the indisputable centre of the Way. Highborn citizens could be persuaded to focus all their contributions on it.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard's support for the Navarr attacking the vallorn in Brocéliande is cited as an example of Highborn loyalty.

The Barrens.t: General Barachel arranged a meeting with the treacherous Vendarri, and a Highborn mandate could open friendly contact with the Black Wind, the Karass or the Montanians.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the subjugated Barrens tribes lie on the far side of Therunin, too distant to witness the Granite Pillar's deeds in Zenith.

Zenith.t: The Granite Pillar laid Aureli Major and the tortured souls around two Druj spires to rest. Only the miasma pillar in Clypion now remains to be destroyed.

Pilgrimage.d: The message met confusion, curiosity and accusations of heresy, but a few in every land embraced it, and together they became a flood of pilgrims to Reikos, home of the Congregation of the First Empress, and Casinea, where Yael is rumoured to live. No living person had drawn such a following since Nicovar. By the Autumn Equinox Yael's congregation earned 160 votes and matching liao. The page set out opportunities: a Senate-authorised Sanctuary of the First Empress of white granite in Reikos or Casinea, with 10 wains donated by pilgrims; national assemblies spending liao to boost pilgrimage, possibly moving the movement's centre; or a General Assembly refutation backed by 500 liao.

Highguard.t: The pilgrimage centred on Highborn lands at Reikos and Casinea, with believers found in every Highborn chapter. Any sanctuary built there could have its priest appointed by the Highborn national assembly.

The League.t: A believer from each League street joined the pilgrimage, and merchants of every trade from the League swelled Yael's congregation.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: wagon raiders from Karsk are listed among the pilgrims flocking to hear Yael.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the hero-tombs in the marshes of Kallavesa are cited as an example of a traditional pilgrimage site.

Pilgrimage.o: In Autumn 380YE, after the Synod's backing, Jared of the Suns of Couros and others spread word across the Empire of the First Empress reborn in Yael and of the Land Without Tears. A growing tide of pilgrims set out for Reikos and Casinea to hear her preach.

Casinea.t: Pilgrims poured into Casinea, where Yael's personal congregation is said to live, and it was proposed as one possible site for the Sanctuary of the First Empress.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: in the accompanying story, a merchant had heard a street preacher in Holberg telling of the First Empress reborn.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: its marshes, where great heroes are interred, are named as an established place of pilgrimage.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: wagon raiders from Karsk are among the pilgrims travelling to see Yael.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the tombs of the Empresses and Emperors in Necropolis are cited as a traditional pilgrimage destination.

Reikos.t: Reikos, base of the Congregation of the First Empress and the centre of the new revelation, received a growing flood of pilgrims needing lodging and was proposed as the site of a sanctuary for them.

Pitiless as the sun.d: Starless skies persisted over the Barrens, Zenith, Holberg and Spiral, and a strange urge to secrecy affected naga who spent time there. Penumbral veils lay over Urdur in Otkodov, Feroz, Temeschwar and Morrow, while the shrouds over Madruga and Sarvos faded. The Sussavari Frost Coven again raised a night citadel over Kallavesa, and a mysterious mist briefly wreathed Grimhold. Llofir asked to parley with the Archmage of Spring and closed Tamarbode, cutting off Tamar's Toes. Sadogua mourned Richard of Holberg. Eleonaris's herald asked for a statue marking the alliance. Meraud delayed his challenge after his hidden role in Lions of Phoenix Reach came to light. The koboldi completed the indestructible Adamant Gate in Semmerholm.

Dawn.t: Weirwater was cursed so that the name Edric de Gauvain intruded into every conversation, while Semmerholm gained the Adamant Gate, a Summer-imbued fortress that can be captured but not destroyed by normal means.

Druj.t: The Druj were said to have stolen the stars over the Barrens and Zenith and, with their forces in the heart of Screed, over Spiral too. Kaela's Gift still let their Imperial prisoners choose a painless death that left no corpse to defile.

Grendel.t: The stars over Spiral, which Grendel shared with Urizen, were devoured a week before the Equinox while the Druj occupied the heart of Screed.

Highguard.t: Highguard's region of Tamarbode in Reikos, claimed by Llofir, was closed to all Imperial citizens. The mana site of Tamar's Toes was overgrown and lost to Imperial magicians.

The Brass Coast.t: A penumbral veil, thick with dark fog, hid Feroz from scrying until shortly before the Summer Solstice, while the shroud over Madruga faded away.

The League.t: Holberg's stars stayed obscured amid fears of a hidden Druj coven, Temeschwar lay under a penumbral veil, and Sarvos's shroud faded. The League also lost its magical architect Richard of Holberg, who died of his long illness.

Thule.t: Penumbral veils hung over Urdur in Otkodov. It remained unclear whether Nithoggir, Sküld or Verthandi were veiled as well.

Urizen.t: Morrow was hidden beneath a penumbral veil, and the stars over Spiral, shared with Grendel, were devoured while the Druj held the heart of Screed.

Varushka.t: A strange mist with odd lights coiled around Grimhold Fortress in Miekarova through a lunar cycle. The Vor'Azi who live there revealed nothing of its origin.

Wintermark.t: The Sussavari Frost Coven again raised a castle of fog and shadow over Kallavesa, and Kallavesi mystics were invited to share Goosewhisper Infusion on Friday evening to seek ancestral spirits.

Pitiless as the sun.o: In spring 382YE a range of magical phenomena were reported across the Empire and beyond. Stars stayed missing over Druj-held and threatened lands, penumbral veils lay over several territories, Weirwater was cursed with the name Edric de Gauvain, and Llofir sealed Tamarbode in response to the Conclave's enmity.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Some feared a hidden Druj coven lurked in Misericorde's forests beneath Holberg's starless sky, though no attacks had followed.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: The forests of Utterlund were suspected of hiding a Druj coven behind the obscured stars, but no attacks had taken place.

Otkodov/Nithoggir.t: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the penumbral veil also covered Nithoggir.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the penumbral veil also covered Sküld.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: Penumbral veils hung over several places in Urdur, hindering scrying there.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Tamarbode was sealed against all mortals by Llofir's armoured heralds. Tamar's Toes was overgrown by giant fungi and lost as a source of crystal mana.

Spiral/Screed.t: With the Druj occupying the heart of Screed, the stars above were devoured a week before the Spring Equinox.

Feroz.t: A penumbral veil hampered scrying over Feroz and brought heavy dark fog and inky clouds. It was due to fade shortly before the Summer Solstice.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the completion of the Wintermark beacons in Hahnmark and Kallavesa raised the question of whether Kallavesa's citadel was still needed.

Holberg.t: The stars over Holberg had been obscured since the Autumn Equinox, which raised fears of a hidden Druj coven, although no attacks had followed. Naga who spent time there felt a strong pull towards secrecy.

Kallavesa.t: A night-woven citadel raised by the Sussavari Frost Coven protected Kallavesa's lowlands until the Spring Equinox. Its future was uncertain now that the Wintermark beacons were complete.

Madruga.t: The shroud that had hung over Madruga faded away.

Miekarova.t: A serpentine mist with moving lights gathered around Grimhold Fortress through one lunar cycle, then vanished by the next new moon.

Morrow.t: A penumbral veil warped Morrow's stars to block scrying, bringing heavy fog until shortly before the Summer Solstice.

Otkodov.t: Penumbral veils hung over Urdur. Whether they also covered Otkodov's other regions could not be determined without scrying.

Reikos.t: Llofir's region of Tamarbode was sealed by armoured heralds against all mortals, ending the gathering of crystal mana at Tamar's Toes.

Sarvos.t: The shroud that had hung over Sarvos faded away.

Semmerholm.t: The koboldi of Adamant completed the Adamant Gate, a white granite fortress whose strength cannot be reduced below 1,000 and which can be captured but not destroyed by normal means.

Spiral.t: With the Druj occupying the heart of Screed, the stars over Spiral were devoured a week before the Equinox, leaving nights darker and fuller of terrors.

Temeschwar.t: A penumbral veil interfered with scrying over Temeschwar and brought dark fog until shortly before the Summer Solstice.

The Barrens.t: The stars over the Barrens remained missing, said to be stolen by the Druj. Kaela's Gift still reached Imperial captives held there.

Verthandi.t: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the penumbral veil over Urdur also lay over Verthandi.

Weirwater.t: A curse made the name Edric de Gauvain intrude into conversation, wind and thought across Weirwater, though few knew who he was.

Zenith.t: Hopes that Zenith's stars would return before the Spring Equinox came to nothing. Kaela's Gift still extended to Imperial prisoners there.

Pitter patter.d: After the Chamber of Commerce chose to ride out the plague, bites spread a hallucinatory sickness that was treatable with bladeroot and, in bad cases, prismatic ink. The Unfettered Mind, protected by League captains, found about one rat in twelve enchanted, the source beneath the city, and wolf-sized rats in the tunnels. Rituals identified the domain of the King of Rats. Brinton von Temeschwar offered to sell a token for safe contact, and the Rat Kings guild sought talks with the Chamber, which again faced a vote. At Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, tainted air left nearly a third of workers ill, reducing the Delver of the Depths' bounty.

The League.t: League captains guarded the investigating magicians, and League magicians confirmed Shadowsmith's fate. Temeschwar's business owners again had to choose between the Wardog Kennels, the Guild of the Green Flower, possibly the Rat Kings, or riding out the plague.

Varushka.t: Varushkans built the city in pre-Imperial times. A coven of Varushkan cabalists proved a Winter ward against the swarms possible but ruinously costly, and sensed a powerful, malign force ruling parts of the undercity.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: a Steinr runesmith helped treat the stricken Cartagia, a Wintermark magician was mauled by a giant rat, and the Steinr grimnir Kylara is a voting member of the Chamber of Commerce.

Pitter patter.o: Through the summer of 386YE a magically influenced rat plague continued to beset Temeschwar, and the Unfettered Mind traced it to a previously unknown power called the King of Rats, which had apparently devoured the volodny Shadowsmith. Meanwhile, a separate and intelligent menace sickened workers at Lorenzo's Deep Pockets.

Temeschwar/Hanuri.t: A Sentinel Gate conjunction opened to the Old Priory inn in Temeschwar, Hanuri, where Brinton von Temeschwar offered to sell a token allowing safe contact with the King of Rats.

Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale.t: Mentioned in passing: a 'fell wind' blowing in off the Vardstein Vale preceded the sickness among workers at Lorenzo's Deep Pockets.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: a Holberg scholar's pet rats stayed placid in Temeschwar, suggesting only the city's own rats are affected, and Albrecht Von Holberg was among the rat hunters.

Temeschwar.t: Rat swarms, a spreading sickness and a sovereign-like King of Rats beneath the city disrupted daily life. Those who could fled, physicks were kept busy, and the mine at Lorenzo's Deep Pockets lost workers to tainted air and disappearances.

Poetry and prose.d: Three proposals were made for the Towers of Dawn site at Dawnguard: Etienne de Maravel's Tombs of Glory, Christian's Gates of Adventure with a Knight of the Gate, and Josephine du Lune's Towers of Enchantment college, two of whose four eternal patrons are under enmity. A mandate could consecrate the remodelled Spires of Dusk to Ambition, raising Dawn's army capacity. A folly at Hope's Rest could spread Dawnish settlement. The Rahvin mourned the vetoed treaty and armed themselves with some Black Wind at the Fangs. Most Navarr swore the Loyalty-backed oath to protect the Great Forest Orcs, who are now fleeing the Druj in Therunin. Legal advice held the treaty may not have been broken.

Dawn.t: Dawn could choose between three ambitious rebuilds of the Towers of Dawn, a consecration of the Spires of Dusk that would let it support an extra army, and a chapel at Hope's Rest to spur new Dawnish settlement, though its people were warned to keep away from the Great Forest Orcs.

Druj.t: The Druj saw the last traces of their power stripped from the Spires of Dusk, faced the prospect of a Dawnish surge aimed at their surrounding territories, and invaded Therunin, overwhelming the Great Forest Orcs there.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Etienne de Maravel studied sculpture in Necropolis under the Highborn artist Dinah of Sanctuary's End, and the Highborn tombs for dead Thrones inspired her Tombs of Glory.

Navarr.t: Driven by Brynn Tendfallen's mandate and the Loyalty Assembly's use of the Eyes of Loyalty, most Navarr swore a binding oath to protect the Great Forest Orcs as family, and Chief Vallack's party planned to meet them at Anvil.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Josephine du Lune cited the Brass Coast's Lyceum, still hidden in its misty wards, as an example of a national college of magic Dawn lacks.

The League.t: A League citizen, Serrusto Caeli Rezia di Tassato, raised the call to consecrate the Spires of Dusk, whose remodelling had been paid for by the Castellan of Spiral Castle.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Doyen of the Spires was cited as an example of a national college of magic Dawn lacks.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Icy Crag was cited as an example of a college of magic, and Varushkans were warned to keep their distance from the visiting Great Forest Orcs.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Tombs of Glory were likened to the Wintermark Chronicle of Heroes.

Poetry and prose.o: In Summer 386YE the Barrens settled into an uneasy calm under Dawnish rule, and several Dawnish opportunities arose: three rival proposals to rebuild the ruined Towers of Dawn, a Synod mandate to consecrate the Spires of Dusk to Ambition, and a chapel to strengthen the true aura at the Shrine of Hope. Meanwhile the Navarr swore oaths to protect the Great Forest Orcs as the Druj invaded Therunin.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: The ruins of the Towers of Dawn here could become the Tombs of Glory, the Gates of Adventure or the Towers of Enchantment college of magic, depending on which proposal the Empire chose.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: The Shrine of Hope, now holding a true aura of Ambition and haunted by Ser Guineve, could gain a chapel folly to turn a trickle of visitors into a flood and spread Dawnish settlement.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Murderdale was named as unclaimed land that new Dawnish houses would settle if a chapel were built at the Shrine of Hope.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: Parts of the Bleaks not claimed by the Karass were named as land the Dawnish would settle if a chapel were built at the Shrine of Hope.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the Druj territories the Dawnish would set their sights on if the Spires of Dusk were consecrated to Ambition.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Etienne de Maravel is said to have studied architecture in Holberg.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lyceum, the Brass Coast's college of magic still hidden by misty wards, was cited by Josephine du Lune.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: the Icy Crag was cited as Varushka's college of magic.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Etienne de Maravel studied sculpture here, and she found that Rodric the Lame has no tomb of his own in the Necropolis.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: recalled as a land from which the Dawnish drove the Druj.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the Druj territories the Dawnish would set their sights on if the Spires of Dusk were consecrated to Ambition.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the Druj territories the Dawnish would set their sights on if the Spires of Dusk were consecrated to Ambition.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Castellan of Spiral Castle paid for the remodelling of the Spires of Dusk.

The Barrens.t: Now firmly Dawnish, the Barrens faced proposals to rebuild the Towers of Dawn, consecrate the Spires of Dusk and expand Dawnish settlement, while most Black Wind departed and the Rahvin armed themselves at the Fangs.

Therunin.t: The Druj invaded Therunin, overwhelming the Great Forest Orc warriors who had tried to delay them and who were now falling back from steadings near the Holt of the Oak and the Thimble.

Poets light but lamps.d: Cinder zealots attacked the docks at Fisk and Meade and the Azure Chorus. The Fisk attack was contained, but both others turned bloody. Faraden condemned the attacks, shared intelligence, and conjunctions opened to stop further attacks in Sarvos, Madruga and Upwold. Faraden proposed that the Empire attack Ribeira and Pedreira while the Suranni struck southern Reinos, and the Sansar offered a Moonsong Market in the Barrens. The Iron Confederacy took the Cazar Straits from the Children of Wrecks and threatened Free Landing. Sumaah white granite awaits an escort, and the Frieøyer helped complete the Zemress Academy's work. Tsark offered two gardens, and Skoura offered troops for dragonbone.

Dawn.t: Faraden merchants of the Sansar family offered a Moonsong Market in the Barrens, trading Dawnish wine and cloth for Faraden mooncheese and cloth, overseen by a Moonsong Reeve whose benefits are halved if the post is not held by yeofolk.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Faraden declined the Imperial suggestion that its troops might fight the Druj, citing distance and danger.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: named as the foe that Skouran war-engineers could help resist at Rucraic's Redoubt, as former conquerors of the Cazar Straits, and as a naval benchmark.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Accalon of Highguard is the Sumaah ambassador, and the Basilica of Seven Doors is used as a comparison for the Faraden Temple of the High Flames.

Imperial Orcs.t: Skoura wishes to deal mainly with the Unshackled, and its Geltcourse Trade Security Council seeks wider trade only if the Artisans Guild becomes an Imperial sodality. It also offered 500 war-engineers for Rucraic's Redoubt in return for 50 dragonbone.

Jotun.t: Faraden proposed an Imperial attack on Ribeira and Pedreira alongside a Suranni assault on southern Reinos. At Meade, the Jotun fought the Cinders beside the Marchers, drowned the three captured attackers and restored the docks, adding an idol of Skjaldir.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: northern Hercynia is named as a possible alpine site for future zaboravi gardens.

The Brass Coast.t: Cinders massacred pilgrims at the Azure Chorus before Freeborn and Faraden stormed the Parador together, and Cinders now threaten the House of Guerra. The Suranni hold the Cazar Straits but let Freeborn leave freely, Sumaah granite awaits an escort, and the Zemress Academy has completed its work.

The League.t: Cinders are marching on the Anvil Library Scriptorium in Sarvos, which the Armarius Ricardo Glostari di Sarvos must defend, and the Suranni commended Senator Laurencio Lemmini di Sarvos.

The Marches.t: The Cinders struck the docks at Meade, where Marchers and Jotun fought them together, and more Cinders aim at Benson's Orchard in Upwold. Ebenezer of the Marches, as ambassador, secured Faraden intelligence on the sect.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are listed among the nations with an Imperial ambassador, and the orcs of Otkodov are covered elsewhere.

Urizen.t: Tsark proposed the Garden of the Perfect World in Occursion, a ministry overseen by a Seeker of the Perfect World chosen by the Urizen National Assembly to trade white granite for weirwood and liao. Tsark is also curious about ushabti and the Golden Cascade.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: northern Varushka is named as a possible alpine site for future zaboravi gardens.

Wintermark.t: Tsark offered to help Wintermark cultivate zaboravi through the Garden of Peaceful Quietude sinecure. Warnings about the Cinders were also carried there, and the scholar Marko Siwarsbairn remains in the Iron Confederacy.

Poets light but lamps.o: A diplomatic roundup reported on the Empire's neighbours. Faraden helped the Empire against the Cinders after their attacks on Imperial sites, and offered trade and a joint campaign against the Jotun. The Iron Confederacy seized the Cazar Straits, the Sumaah and Frieøyer completed the work of the Zemress Naval Academy, and Tsark and Skoura made cautious offers of their own.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Two Suranni armies carried by the Wings of Kobol smashed the Children of Wrecks here. The Iron Confederacy now claims the islands by right of conquest while inviting trapped Freeborn to leave.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the page refers only to Feroz generally, the town of Bramar and severed trade routes.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: Cinders heading for the House of Guerra can be intercepted along the Corsair's Road, under the responsibility of the Hand of Guerra, Sufyan i Zuhri i Guerra.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Most of the Wreckers fleeing the Cazar Straits went to Free Landing. The Suranni Dukes intend to attack it after the Spring Equinox, and to keep it, unless the Empire acts first.

Reinos/Pedreira.t: Faraden proposed an Imperial attack here after the Winter Solstice, noting it would give the Empire the white granite quarry at Cantera Balanka and shield Segura.

Reinos/Ribeira.t: Faraden urged the Military Council to send a powerful force to take this region after the Winter Solstice in concert with the Suranni attack in the south.

Sarvos/Foracci.t: The main group of Cinders is approaching along Vintner's Way, where the Armarius of the Anvil Library must cut them off.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Dawnguard is one of the two sites the Sansar requested for the proposed Moonsong Market, being close to well-defended centres.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Murderdale is one of the two sites the Sansar requested for the proposed Moonsong Market.

Upwold/Tower March.t: The Cinders must pass through Benson's Bawn to reach Benson's Orchard, and Martin Orchard is responsible for stopping them there.

Zenith/Occursion.t: The foothills of Occursion are the proposed site of Tsark's Garden of the Perfect World, a meditative garden and meeting hall serving as a trading ministry.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; Zenith appears only through the Occursion garden and the Golden Cascade.

Bay of Catazar.t: Some of the Wreckers driven from the Cazar Straits quit the Bay altogether. Suranni control of the Straits could in principle cut Feroz off from the Bay, and Sumaah granite awaits an escort across these waters.

Feroz.t: The Iron Confederacy drove the Children of Wrecks from the Cazar Straits and claims them by conquest. It lets Freeborn leave and Ferozi ships pass, and its merchants eye Bramar once trade routes severed by disaster are restored.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: northern Hercynia is noted as potentially suitable for a zaboravi garden after an appraisal.

Kahraman.t: The Freeborn Assembly warned of a planned attack here, and Cinder pilgrims massacred people in the Parador of Wind and Flame at the Azure Chorus before Freeborn and Faraden stormed it together.

Kalino.t: Known to the Suranni as Arbonne, Kalino suffered a second, far worse curse of ruined crops, sickness and demonic revenants. Its Duke's position is shaky, and Veiled Shrine priests blame Imperial involvement.

Madruga.t: Cinders seek to destroy the House of Guerra in Calvos, and the Iron Confederacy plans to attack the Wreckers in Free Landing after the Spring Equinox if the Empire has not dealt with them. A Frieøyer ship also arrived at Calvos.

Mareave.t: Skoura's Delvemistress wrote to Mareave seeking to deal mainly with its Unshackled neighbours, weighing an embassy and trade. She also offered war-engineers to help defend Rucraic's Redoubt against the Grendel.

Mountains of the Moon.t: Tsark, still refusing an embassy, proposed limited trade through a garden ministry in Zenith and offered to help cultivate zaboravi in the Empire.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: relations with the orcs of Otkodov are noted as covered in another wind of fortune.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only in Rucraic's Redoubt, the Unshackled fortification Skoura offered to reinforce.

Reinos.t: Faraden proposed that the Empire attack Ribeira and Pedreira after the Winter Solstice while the Iron Confederacy attacks the south, catching the Jotun between hammer and anvil.

Sarvos.t: Cinders are approaching the Anvil Library Scriptorium to burn its books, and a conjunction lets heroes intercept them. War also rages in the seas off Sarvos.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: its dangers make overland trade with the Empire more attractive to Faraden merchants than seaborne trade with Asavea.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Faraden argued that taking Pedreira would protect Segura's western border from future Jotun invasion.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial ambassador told the Suranni that the Empire intends to attack Skallahn.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a possible alpine location for a future zaboravi garden.

The Barrens.t: The Sansar proposed building the Moonsong Market here, a great work that would raise farm investment and draw more Faraden trade and visitors to Dawn.

Upwold.t: Cinders plan to desecrate Benson's Orchard, the Vigilance memorial whose pilgrims stand ready to defend it, and a conjunction lets heroes stop them first.

Veroigne.t: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni ambassador's seat at Chaubrette is said to lie west of Veroigne.

Zenith.t: Tsark proposed the Garden of the Perfect World in Occursion as a trading ministry, and expressed interest in the Golden Cascade that feeds Zenith.

Point of the spear.d: In Sermersuaq, heroes could fight Jarl Heimgar to free about 50 captured Imperial soldiers, free Suaq thralls held at Thoki's Camp, or visit a broken Jotun warband in Suaq Font. Two Brocéliande skirmishes could each add 500 military strength against the vallorn. In Feroz, conjunctions targeted Kraken's Jaw beast masters and their sand crabs, and aimed to free islanders, Highguard pilgrims and stranded Imperial orc reavers. In Segura, heroes could protect Faraden trade. Other conjunctions offered to cleanse a Druj monolith in Ossium, intercept a Vikari warband in Spiral, find a League ship off Redoubt, stop Feni in the Marches, clear ghouls from a Karsk dragonbone forest and pursue the thieves of the Magistrate's Grasp in Casinea.

Dawn.t: Dawn's lands were where the trail began: travellers vanished in Coombe and bandits stole the Magistrate's Grasp. Astolat's militia then traced the hirers, The Harvesters, to Casinea.

Druj.t: A lingering Druj monolith spread fear over Sullen Vale in Ossium. A Druj warband of Vikari mages, Chikad warriors and slave artisans led by a young Ghulai was marching out of Screed and could be intercepted.

Grendel.t: Grendel forces in Feroz were targets of several conjunctions: Kraken's Jaw beast masters with sand crabs, a garrison on Ponta Delgordo, skirmishers on the Lucksprings Road and mercenaries at Green Coast. A Grendel slave ship had also chased a League vessel to Redoubt.

Highguard.t: Highguard grey pilgrims who had protested the Temple of the Bull in Oran were fleeing along the Lucksprings Road with Grendel skirmishers close behind. The Harvesters were also believed to be operating in Highguard-held Casinea.

Jotun.t: Jotun forces faced challenges in Sermersuaq at Pinehall Meadow, at Thoki Hawkspear's thrall camp and at Vanda Frostaxe's broken warband. In Segura, Jotun raiders from the Corazon threatened Faraden trade at the Seguridade Plain and the Kabalai Campo.

Navarr.t: Navarr vates identified a ruined way house in Vale's Lament that could become a warded stronghold. Navarr reports tracked a herald of Yaw'nagrah swelling the vallornspawn in Boar's Dell; each victory would add 500 military strength to Brocéliande's defence.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn in Feroz were hiding, fleeing to Madruga or fighting back against the Grendel. Conjunctions offered the chance to free the villagers of Ponta Delgordo and protect evacuations along the coast.

The League.t: A League fleet captain had taken a trained Mandowla from Beoraidh and vanished near Granite Isle while fleeing a Grendel slave ship. The League egregore might know more about the captain's intentions.

The Marches.t: Feni were heading for the Singing Caves mithril mine in the Mournwold and for Oakwood Monastery in Upwold. Only one of the two could be intercepted through the conjunction.

Urizen.t: A conjunction opened to Granite Isle off Optarion in Urizen's Redoubt, where a League ship had last been seen braving the rocks in a storm.

Varushka.t: Varushkan settlers needed the Druj monolith at Sullen Vale in Ossium cleansed before they could found a new vale. In Karsk, dragonbone workers offered to follow the Senator's nominee if ghouls were cleared from Mir Mozga.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's war for Sermersuaq offered chances to free captured Imperial soldiers and rescue Suaq thralls from Atalaq. The freed Suaq were expected to swear to the Wintermark egregores or become Frayed.

Point of the spear.o: Before the Spring Equinox summit of 383YE the prognosticators listed the conjunctions they had found through the Sentinel Gate. They offered strikes against the Jotun, Grendel, Druj, vallorn, Feni and other threats across the Empire.

Astolat/Coombe.t: The trouble started in Coombe, where travellers vanished and a militia patrol lost the Magistrate's Grasp to hired bandits.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: In North Weaver Wood, a herald of Yaw'nagrah had empowered ettercaps and swelled the vallornspawn. Breaking its strength would add 500 military strength.

Brocéliande/Vale's Lament.t: A ruined way house at Darkening Boughs could be cleared and warded into a stronghold worth 500 military strength.

Casinea/Mareholm.t: The Broken Thicket, once used for Winter magic, was the suspected base of The Harvesters.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: A Grendel garrison held Ponta Delgordo's islanders captive. A swift strike could let Freeborn resistance evacuate them to Madruga.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Kraken's Jaw beast masters with sand crabs had landed at Valdez Cove and the Brazen Sands Forest. Stranded Imperial orc reavers needed rescue at Green Coast.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Highguard grey pilgrims fleeing from Oran along the Lucksprings Road were being hunted by Grendel skirmishers.

Karsk/Lestasny.t: Ghouls infested the Glade of Mir Mozga. Clearing them would win over Ottokar Lestasnovic's dragonbone workers.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: the successful raid on Beoraidh's port led to the stranded orc ship and the theft of a Mandowla from its fighting arena.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: The Silent Copse conjunction would let heroes stop Feni before they reached the Singing Caves mithril mine.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Settlers at Sullen Vale were blocked by a Druj monolith's fear miasma that a ritual team or priests needed to remove.

Redoubt/Optarion.t: The missing League ship had last been seen manoeuvring around the jagged rocks of Granite Isle off Optarion.

Segura/Anduzjasse.t: On the Jotun-held Kabalai Campo, a Faraden merchant and a war scout needed a distraction to reach safety. Success would slightly improve relations with the Faraden courts.

Segura/Anozeseri.t: Jotun raiders were closing on the Seguridade Plain garrison. Failure to stop them would reduce trade income from Faraden.

Segura/Lucksprings.t: Mentioned in passing: the fleeing pilgrims took the Lucksprings Road towards Segura.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: At Pinehall Meadow, heroes could challenge Jarl Heimgar to free captured Imperial soldiers. At Thoki's Camp they could free Suaq thralls from Atalaq.

Spiral/Screed.t: A Vikari-led Druj warband was leaving Screed via Tractus Animo after days on the Black Plateau.

Upwold/Ashbrook.t: The Cursed Glade conjunction would let heroes stop Feni before they slaughtered the monks of Oakwood Monastery.

Astolat.t: A family of travellers went missing in Astolat, and bandits hired by The Harvesters stole the Magistrate's Grasp from a magistrate and militia.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: an Imperial orc raiding ship was blown across the entire Bay of Catazar to Feroz.

Brocéliande.t: Two conjunctions offered fights against the vallorn here. Each success would add 500 military strength to Brocéliande's defence for the season.

Casinea.t: The Harvesters, who hired the thieves of the Magistrate's Grasp, were believed to be working from the Broken Thicket in Casinea.

Feroz.t: Five conjunctions opened to Grendel-assailed Feroz. They offered chances to destroy sand crabs and their handlers, liberate islanders and save fleeing pilgrims and stranded orc sailors.

Karsk.t: Ghouls had taken over the dragonbone forest of Mir Mozga. Its workers would follow the Senator's nominee, waiving the usual 2 crown fee, if the forest was cleared.

Madruga.t: Madruga was the refuge for Freeborn fleeing Feroz across the Sorecco estuary, and the intended destination for evacuated villagers.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the great Imperial raid on Mareave and Beoraidh was the background to the stranded orc ship and the stolen Mandowla.

Mournwold.t: Feni were moving towards the Singing Caves mithril mine, where they would slaughter miners and steal mithril unless intercepted.

Ossium.t: A Druj monolith at Sullen Vale needed cleansing so settlers could found a new vale. This would be a step towards lifting the fear miasma over all of Ossium.

Redoubt.t: A conjunction opened to Granite Isle, where a League ship carrying a Mandowla had last been seen evading a Grendel pursuer in a storm.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos was the missing League ship's intended destination.

Segura.t: Jotun raiders threatened Faraden trade in Segura as a protective Autumn enchantment faded. Conjunctions offered to safeguard the garrison and a merchant's caravan.

Sermersuaq.t: Three conjunctions offered to free about 50 captured Imperial soldiers, rescue Suaq thralls and visit a broken Jotun warband in Suaq Font.

Spiral.t: A Druj warband with Vikari mages and slave artisans was leaving Screed. Intercepting it might reveal what the Vikari had been making.

Upwold.t: Feni were moving through the Silver Chase towards Oakwood Monastery, where they would slaughter the monks unless intercepted.

Poor boy.d: Rico i Matra i Riqueza, a clam diver near Calvos Sound, found an ugly green pearl holding the equivalent of thirty mana crystals, usable only all at once as the sole power for a Spring ritual; he would seek the Grandmaster of the Golden Pyramid. The vate Meri Sixstep searched for remaining Pages of Constellations for 'the Bound King'. A merrow captain of 'the House of the Sixth Wind' salvaged a wrecked ship of the Freeborn Storm that had fled Atalaya, renamed it the Storm Reborn and sought the Freeborn egregores' help to auction it as a non-military vessel equal to a level four fleet. Envoys of Magician-Prince Matvei Kobarid sought Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato's help to auction star jewels.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel attack that destroyed the Atalaya Shipyards and the Freeborn Storm is the backdrop to the salvaged ship, which had slipped their blockade before being wrecked.

The League.t: Jarmish merchants in Tassato brokered the Kobarid envoys' visit, and the envoys hoped Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato would find them a venue and provide security for their star-jewel auction, offering League magicians access to rare enchanted talismans.

Poor boy.o: Four opportunities arose ahead of the Winter Solstice at Anvil: a poor clam diver sought to sell a powerful Spring-aligned pearl, a Navarri vate hunted pages of The Book of the Stars, a merrow captain brought a salvaged Freeborn warship to auction, and Jarmish envoys from Kobarid offered enchanted star jewels.

Tassato.t: Jarmish merchants based in Tassato arranged for the nephews and nieces of Magician-Prince Matvei Kobarid to visit the Empire on official business to sell enchanted jewellery.

Possibility days.d: The Conclave accepted the Brother of Wizards' offer. The Celestial Arch endowed crystal mana, and the League's Celestial Eclipse coven raised Penumbral Veils over Madruga and Segura, which the Eater of Secrets wove into a concealing fog. Imperial magicians met most arrivals, but many refugees fear priests, armoured knights, magistrates and militia, and some are surely Hand of Dumon cultists. Sephora of Sylaire gathered twenty potions as a bequest to the Conclave, and a group planned to visit Anvil. The Navarr Assembly could pass a mandate offering sanctuary in steadings and stridings, aiding integration but also helping malign wizards spread. Highguard had an alternative mandate. Otherwise the Suranni will form isolated enclaves.

Dawn.t: Many refugees are frightened of heavily armoured, heraldic figures such as knights of Dawn, and if left to themselves none will settle in Dawn for fear of priests and nobles who resemble Suranni knights.

Highguard.t: Exarch Luke proposed an alternative mandate urging Wayfarers and Magisters to welcome the Suranni, though its effect was uncertain and it would not see them settle in Highguard; the refugees fear cataphracts and Highborn priests.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: if the Navarr mandate passes, the refugees will settle in every corner of the Empire except among the Imperial Orcs.

Navarr.t: The Navarr Assembly had the opportunity to mandate that guides, vates and brands offer the Suranni sanctuary in their steadings and stridings, making most of them Navarr guests and aiding integration, at the risk of helping Hand of Dumon members and criminals spread across the Empire.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn magicians met refugees crossing into Madruga and Segura, but the Suranni distrust them because of the return of Arbonne's rebel slaves, and none will choose to settle in the Brass Coast.

The League.t: The League's Celestial Eclipse coven raised the veils that hid the refugees' flight, and affluent Suranni are eager to learn about the League, with some likely to form enclaves in Temeschwar and Holberg.

Urizen.t: Urizen's assembly invited the Suranni on condition they embrace the Way, an overture they mostly ignored, though many may still end up in Urizen and its northern reaches, and wealthier refugees show interest in the nation.

Varushka.t: Varushka's assembly welcomed the refugees but stressed virtue and the Way, which most rebuffed; nonetheless many Suranni are expected to settle in Varushka, either via the Navarr or in their own isolated villages.

Wintermark.t: Some refugees expressed interest in settling in Wintermark, and if left alone some will seek wild places there to found their own enclaves.

Possibility days.o: Several hundred Suranni magicians and their families fled persecution in the Iron Confederacy and reached the Empire, hidden by a magical fog along the south-western border, with no sign so far of any diplomatic incident. Their arrival raised questions about where they would settle and what dangers might come with them.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: few refugees wish to remain in territories bordering the Bay of Catazar.

Holberg.t: If the Suranni are left to their own devices, some will try to form enclaves in Holberg, hoping to blend into its crowded population.

Madruga.t: A Penumbral Veil raised over Madruga helped form the concealing fog, and many exhausted refugees, along with some more open-minded wizards, arrived here.

Sarvos.t: Some refugees reached the Empire by boat into Sarvos, including several of the more well-travelled, open-minded wizards.

Segura.t: A Penumbral Veil over Segura fed the protective fog, and many refugees crossed here, Sephora of Sylaire among the first to arrive and help liaise with Imperial magicians.

Shavronne.t: Mentioned in passing: the League magician Robert von Temeschwar was originally from Shavronne, rescued as a child from soldiers there.

Temeschwar.t: Robert von Temeschwar offered a band of refugees a home with his troupe in Temeschwar, and if left alone some Suranni will form enclaves in the city.

Power, corruption, and lies.d: Urizen astronomancers spotted a conjunction that empowered destructive enchantments and kept part of the Icy Maw curse on Bastion and Casinea alive, disrupting chamber rituals at Anvil. The Conclave's new running order was adopted for the Equinox. Seven magical castles were raised in Hahnmark, Kahraman, Bregasland and Kallavesa, and Cathan Canae sent two bands of frost giants to guard Wintermark's Beacons. Nightly lights over Reikos celebrated the liberation of Tamarbode, Imperial Orcs shared ancestral dreams, and the curse on Zephaniah's Lament lifted. Several territories stayed starless or veiled. Summer eternals, including Sadogua, prepared champions for a new tourney for the Icy Crag. Prospero, Callidus, Sorin, Lashonar and Sung offered various opportunities.

Dawn.t: Dawnish troubadours sought out the story of Zephaniah's Lament and wrote songs about the League heroes of Tamarbode, while Adamant was expected to look for tourney champions among the Dawnish and Semmerholm's skies stayed starless.

Druj.t: The Druj-held Zenith and the Barrens remained under inky starless skies, which impeded divination on them and strengthened the secretiveness of any naga who had spent time there.

Grendel.t: Grendel-held Spiral stayed starless and shrouded against divination, and former gladiators of Mareave were helped by the orc dreams to settle into Imperial Orc society.

Highguard.t: The Highborn suffered the after-effects of the Icy Maw curse on Bastion and Casinea and watched three months of celebratory lights over Reikos, while the curse and long malaise over the chapter of Zephaniah's Lament finally lifted.

Imperial Orcs.t: For three months every Imperial Orc dreamed of their nation's history and achievements and woke refreshed and proud, which especially helped the newly joined gladiators of Mareave and slaves of Dubhtraig to integrate.

Jotun.t: Magical castles in Hahnmark, Kahraman and Bregasland stood against Jotun advances, notably impeding them in the Marches, and Cathan Canae's frost giants now guard Wintermark's Beacons against them.

The Brass Coast.t: A castle of white stone and black ice was raised over Serra Briante, certain Freeborn were summoned to honour an old bargain with Callidus, and Sung set Maya of the Brass Coast a riddle challenge.

The League.t: League armies and independent captains were celebrated nightly over Reikos for liberating Tamarbode, the stars returned over Holberg, and the Highborn chapter that cursed Sarvos and Holberg saw two members declared sorcerers.

The Marches.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven's castle of fog and water over North Fens significantly slowed the Jotun advance into Bregasland.

Thule.t: Penumbral Veils were reported over Thule-held Otkodov's regions of Urdur, Nithoggir and Sküld, and over Verthandi, impeding divination there.

Urizen.t: Urizen astronomancers were first to notice the conjunction, which held particular meaning for them, Adamant was expected to seek tourney champions from Urizen, and the Grandmaster of the Celestial Arch received an invitation to Prospero's game.

Varushka.t: Ossium's skies stayed starless and some Varushkans, citing the recent Synod mandate, wondered aloud about the nature of Zephaniah's Lament's deal with Skathe.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gained castles in Hahnmark and Kallavesa and two bands of Summer frost giants to guard its Beacons in honour of three of its heroes, the Kallavesi were invited to share the Raven's Dream at Ishal, and Shaman's curse coins passed to his supporters.

Power, corruption, and lies.o: In Autumn 383YE a conjunction of the Great Wyrm, the Drowned Shepherd and the Claw strengthened destructive enchantments, while magical castles, a lingering curse, shrouded skies, Summer frost giants sent to Wintermark and a crop of eternal opportunities shaped the season across the Empire.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a castle of fog and water over North Fens, which significantly slowed the Jotun advance.

Hahnmark/Kalpamark.t: The Voices of the Unbound Storm raised a castle of ice and granite in Kalpamark against any Jotun push south.

Hahnmark/Northspires.t: A castle of ice and granite was raised in Northspires by the Voices of the Unbound Storm.

Hahnmark/Valasmark.t: Valasmark gained a castle of ice and granite called from the Breath of Winter by the Voices of the Unbound Storm.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Mentioned in passing: the withering of Holmauer Park is recalled as part of the earlier curse by Zephaniah's Lament.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: Summer Dawning Relentless raised a castle of white stone and black ice over Serra Briante, which would have hampered the Jotun had they not withdrawn.

Kallavesa/Skymark.t: A Sentinel Gate conjunction was to open in the marshes near Ishal in Skymark on Friday night, so the Kallavesi mystics could share the Raven's Dream and meet the mystics of Ishal.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a castle of fog and water over West Marsh.

Otkodov/Nithoggir.t: Nithoggir was reported to lie under a Penumbral Veil that impeded divination.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Sküld was reported to be shrouded by a Penumbral Veil that blocked divination.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: Imperial merchants reported that the Penumbral Veil still hung over Urdur.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: The League's destruction of the Garden of Llofir and liberation of Tamarbode was celebrated by three months of nightly lights over Reikos.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is not named on the page; the only Dawnish connections are travelling troubadours and Adamant's interest in Dawnish champions.

Bastion.t: Bastion endured a season of the Icy Maw curse, with halved mana yields, foul weather and uneasy magicians, and its lingering power reached Anvil thanks to the conjunction.

Bregasland.t: A castle of fog and water raised over North Fens by the Sussivari Frost Coven significantly impeded the Jotun advance into the territory.

Casinea.t: Casinea suffered the Icy Maw curse alongside Bastion, with weakened magic, halved mana sites, harsh weather and troubled magicians.

Hahnmark.t: Three castles of ice and granite were raised in Hahnmark's hills, and five score frost giants arrived to defend its Beacons until Summer 384YE.

Holberg.t: The darkness that hid Holberg's stars faded, which some credited to Juha the Cave Spider, after last season's curse by Zephaniah's Lament had withered Holmauer Park.

Kahraman.t: A castle of white stone and black ice was raised over Serra Briante, and it would have troubled the Jotun had they not retreated from the hills above Damata.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa received five score frost giants to guard its Beacons and a castle of fog and water over West Marsh, and Ishal's mystics invited the Kallavesi to share the Raven's Dream there.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the gladiators of Mareave are noted as among the newest Imperial Orcs whom the ancestral dreams helped to integrate.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Sorin's agent who delivered the notice of the new trials is known as Ania of Necropolis.

Ossium.t: Ossium's night skies stayed starless, which impeded divination and gave naga who had spent time there a strong urge towards secrecy.

Otkodov.t: Penumbral Veils hung over Urdur, Nithoggir and Sküld in Otkodov, impeding divination on the territory.

Reikos.t: Glowing lights celebrating the League's liberation of Tamarbode filled Reikos's skies every night for three months, delighting children and visiting troubadours but wearying many Highborn.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the transformation of Sarvos after its destruction is cited as a possible reflection of the conjunction, and the city is named as a target of the Zephaniah's Lament curse.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm's skies remained starless, impeding divination and intensifying the secretiveness of naga who had spent time there.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Hahnmark castles were meant to make that territory harder for the Jotun to conquer than Sermersuaq had been.

Spiral.t: Spiral stayed under inky starless skies, impeding divination there and strengthening naga secretiveness.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens remained starless, with divination impeded and naga who had stayed there gripped by an urge for secrecy.

Verthandi.t: Verthandi was reported to lie under a Penumbral Veil that impeded divination.

Zenith.t: Zenith's skies remained inky black, impeding divination and affecting naga who had spent time there.

Praise and blame.d: Any of the Varushkan, Navarri, Highborn, Urizen or Dawnish assemblies could send a priest with 50 doses of liao to unlock the ruthless onslaught order, which raises casualties on both sides by a fifth. With 100 liao and 30 wains of mithril, three armies could also be permanently changed. The Eastern Sky could become bloodthirsty to avenge Druj ravages in Semmerholm. The Seventh Wave could become vengeful, remembering the Druj sack of Reikos. The Citadel Guard could trade cyclic magic for arcane mastery and its devastating Storm of Curses. Brat Umbral Path and Belakov Prochnost raised the ruthlessness mandates but neither was upheld. Sophus Cascade's Citadel Guard mandate was upheld, but after Lucretius died, Zeno, Stallion's Sibling, declined it. The opportunities have now lapsed.

Dawn.t: Dawn's assembly had already endorsed cruel armies, which opened the ruthless onslaught mandate. It also had a chance to make the Eastern Sky permanently bloodthirsty in revenge for the Druj invasion of Semmerholm, but the resolution records no Dawnish mandate taking effect.

Druj.t: The Druj invasion is the provocation behind every opportunity: their conquest of Axmure, their threat to Zenith and their past sack of Reikos. Each proposed mandate would have turned Imperial ruthlessness specifically against them.

Highguard.t: Highguard's assembly had upheld support for the Iron Helms as virtuous tools of cruelty. It could have made the Seventh Wave permanently vengeful in memory of the Druj sack of Reikos, but the resolution records no Highborn mandate taking effect.

Navarr.t: Navarr was one of the nations able to authorise a mandate for ruthless onslaught. Brat Umbral Path raised it, but the Navarri assembly did not uphold it.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are cited as claiming to rival Urizen in the arcane arts, yet falling short of the Citadel Guard's magical mastery.

Urizen.t: Urizen's assembly upheld Sophus Cascade's mandate to turn the Citadel Guard from cyclic magic to arcane mastery and its Storm of Curses. After the named priest Lucretius died, Zeno, Stallion's Sibling, declined to carry it out, so the change will not happen.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan Iron Helms inspired the whole debate, and Varushka could authorise ruthless onslaught for its armies. Belakov Prochnost raised the mandate, but the assembly did not uphold it.

Praise and blame.o: After the Urizen, Highborn and Dawnish assemblies joined Navarr and Varushka in endorsing cruelty in war, inspired by the Iron Helms, several time-limited opportunities arose for national assemblies to make their armies more ruthless. None took effect: the Navarri and Varushkan mandates failed, and the upheld Urizen mandate was declined by its priest.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: Axmure has been conquered by the Druj after the fall of the Towers of the Dawn and the Gate. This loss is cited as driving Dawnish soldiers' thirst for revenge.

Reikos.t: The memory of the Druj sack and brutal occupation of Reikos, with its enslavement and experimentation, was the stated motive for offering the Seventh Wave the chance to become vengeful.

Semmerholm.t: Druj armies have conquered Axmure and threaten all of Semmerholm, with Dawnish manor houses burning. This fuelled the opportunity for the Eastern Sky to become bloodthirsty.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: The Barrens is not named; the page refers only to the Druj armies whose invasion prompted these opportunities.

Zenith.t: The Druj threat to Zenith's Halls of Knowledge, following the fall of Endsmeet, prompted the offer to give the Citadel Guard arcane mastery. The mandate was upheld but its priest declined to carry it out.

Price of experience.d: The Great Forest orcs came to the Lower Tarn Valley after the Senate ended the war with them in Summer 380YE, invited by then-Senator Caerwyn Summercrow. Their army is depleted from fighting the Dawnish and the Druj, and is sustained by 50 thrones a season from the Empire. They reject absorption by the Navarr or Imperial Orcs, refuse the Way, and travel with about 150 briars believed to be Dourfell Keep heretics. Talks with the Navarr have stalled, and minor clashes with local steadings are growing. A Thule delegation may have invited them to join the hegemony. A small delegation will visit Anvil to speak with their hosts and Skywise Fal.

Druj.t: The Druj are the orcs' hated foe. Their near-total domination of the Barrens drove the Great Forest orcs out, and their army has been worn down fighting them.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest orcs claim their ancestors roamed forests in what is now Highguard long ago.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Navarr reportedly want the Great Forest orcs absorbed into the Imperial Orcs, which neither group wants. The orcs' delegation to Anvil intends to speak with Skywise Fal.

Navarr.t: Negotiations between the Navarr and the orcs have stalled. In-character reports say the Navarr demanded the orcs leave Therunin within a year and pay their way, souring a relationship that began as sanctuary.

Thule.t: A Thule delegation came to Therunin to speak with the Great Forest orcs and may have invited them to join the Thule hegemony.

Price of experience.o: In Spring 381YE the Great Forest orcs camped in Therunin's Lower Tarn Valley neared the end of their patience and began preparing to break camp. They announced a final delegation to Anvil to seek an accord with the Empire.

Brocéliande/Terunael.t: Mentioned in passing: the page refers to Brocéliande's forests but does not single out Terunael.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest orcs emerged from Hope's Rest in 380YE before settling in Therunin.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The orcs' camp here has reached the limit of what the land can sustain. Minor bloodless clashes with Tarn Valley steadings are fuelling frustration, and the orcs are preparing to break camp.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: some Great Forest orcs once lived free in Brocéliande's forests, and the orcs claim it as ancestral land.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule orcs of Otkodov sent the delegation, and the orcs claim their Great Forest once stretched to Otkodov's borders.

The Barrens.t: The orcs claim the Barrens as ancestral forest but fled it as Druj domination became all but complete. The briars with them are believed to be survivors of the Dourfell Keep heretics there.

Therunin.t: Therunin faces a growing crisis: a large orc host is preparing to move, and no forces there can stop them or mount a coherent defence. Even a peaceful departure would badly disrupt the territory.

Price of prosperity.d: Representative Puala of the House of the People exiled the Regario agents from Zemeh. She cited Imperial contempt and the recognition of an inhuman exemplar. Sumaah now treats Imperial ships in its waters as pirates, though the Empire has not declared war in return. Work on the Sumaah embassy in Necropolis has stalled. The Commonwealth still imposes tariffs and refuses to sell artisan's oil to Imperial captains. Rigia thanked the Empire but has arranged for Jarmish slaves to arrive at the Spring Equinox. Jarm awaits formal apologies. Angered by the ban on trading Bourse resources with Asaveans, the Tarquinius family withdrew its white granite offer.

Highguard.t: Work has stalled on the Sumaah embassy under construction in Highguard's territory of Necropolis, now that Sumaah has broken off relations with the Empire.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Senator Atte of Sermersuaq is named as the person Imperial captains should approach about Commonwealth tariffs and bureaucracy.

Price of prosperity.o: In Winter 379YE the Sumaah Republic expelled every Imperial citizen from Zemeh, declared war on the Empire and denounced the entire Synod as heretical. The same Trade Winds reported cooling relations with the Commonwealth and Asavea and tentative progress with Jarm.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Tarquinius family says it has found another buyer on the Bay of Catazar for its white granite, one willing to deal pragmatically with Asaveans, and Sarcophan merchant-captains remain regular visitors to the Bay's ports.

Necropolis.t: Construction of the Sumaah embassy in Necropolis has stalled following Sumaah's declaration of war, and the ambassador the Senate agreed to appoint has not yet been named.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Senator Atte of Sermersuaq is the suggested contact for Imperial captains troubled by Commonwealth tariffs.

Pride and paragons.d: Gaelen Embercast's judgement, passed by a greater majority, confirmed that Vardas was a fiction written by Ivar Olyankavic Nathavolava. This prevented a schism, and people did not start doubting the other paragons.
