Instead they questioned where the signs of the paragons come from, what exemplars are for, and why a paragon may embody only one Virtue. Grieving archivists agreed to stay at the Lepidean Library only if it avoids researching paragons and exemplars for a year. They offered to research one of the three questions for the Librarian instead. Their delayed work on Tom Drake prompted an informal appeal to the Marcher Assembly. Donations to the Grand Inspiration have slowed sharply, which threatens a decade's delay.

Dawn.t: Dawn's national assembly had encouraged donations to the Grand Inspiration, but those contributions have now stopped. Highguard has invited Dawnish priests to preach in Bastion, yet some Highborn worry the troubadours may preach glory and love rather than the Virtues.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: a Highborn preacher's sermon claims Imperial generals have dragged the Druj to the verge of destruction.

Highguard.t: Highborn faith has been shaken by Vardas and the Assembly of Nine's troubles: donations to the Grand Inspiration have fallen to about ten wains a season. Many traditional Highborn archivists at the Lepidean Library are grieving and threatening to retire.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs declined to support the Grand Inspiration and chose to build a Library of Worth instead.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr was among the nations that donated to the Grand Inspiration, and the Highborn Assembly invited it to send priests to Bastion; its donations have since ended.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen rejected the call to support the Grand Inspiration in favour of its own projects, though its Assembly stopped short of calling it folly.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka declined to support the Grand Inspiration and created its own Hall of Fabric Arts instead.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark was among the nations that donated to the Grand Inspiration and were invited to send priests to Bastion; its donations have since stopped.

Pride and paragons.o: After the Synod renounced Vardas as a paragon of Vigilance in Autumn 386YE, the faithful began asking deeper questions about the nature of paragons and exemplars. The Lepidean Library's archivists threatened to quit, and confidence in the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion faltered.

Bastion.t: Construction of the Grand Inspiration in Bastion has 583 of 1000 wains of white granite and 167 of 250 thrones. With donations waning it could take a decade to finish, and Highborn doubt is growing over what will be preached there.

Pride and prejudice.d: Velko Perunovich Razoradze and Jared of the Suns of Couros spread the mandates. Short of food, the Thule offered more ilium if a High Path were cut from Brez into Otkodov. The warlock Orathator offered magical masks in return for access to the Well of Shadows or the ritual Delve Deep, Beneath the Mountain. The Mirnatocz warlocks offered red moss for a warehouse at Ivarsgard, and rival mandates proposed stealing or protecting its secret. The Leshun of Branoc agreed to a market and a Speaker. The Menrothat sought Farweald and offered help with shrines at Orieb. Highguard proposed aid to Thule former slaves. Anti-orc prejudice continued to erode.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is not named, but it shares the Barrens, where the Menrothat want their ancestral heartland of Farweald returned.

Druj.t: The Druj once ruled Ossium and used the Palace of Orieb. Menrothat still under their yoke in the Forest of Ulnak, or serving as their scouts, risk reprisals if the sept cooperates too closely with the Empire.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly backed the Varushkan outreach and proved useful in talks with the Leshun. They were offered mandates to have the unconquered steal the red moss secret and to send secret aid to Thule former slaves, though a Varushkan counter-mandate threatened to turn Highborn soldiers back by force.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orcs helped make first contact with the Menrothat, and they have agreed to receive the sept's single dose of black lotus and knowledge of its use if Farweald is given to the Menrothat.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: negotiations took place at a Navarr wayhouse in Srodkoja, and Navarr helped make first contact with the Menrothat, likening them to the feni.

Thule.t: The Thule, struggling to feed their freed slaves, offered more ilium for Varushkan food via the High Path, and their warlocks offered masks and red moss in trade. They faced possible theft of the red moss secret and covert Highborn aid to their underclass, both of which would anger the Dragons.

Varushka.t: Varushka led the outreach to orcs and gained opportunities to trade with the Thule, the Leshun and the Menrothat, along with competing mandates over the red moss. The episode further eroded traditional Varushkan prejudice against orcs.

Pride and prejudice.o: After Varushkan and Highborn mandates urged peaceful contact with the orcs who share Varushka, cautious overtures to the Thule and independent orc septs produced several trade opportunities and competing mandates. The Senate later built the High Path, and the Leshun Market was commissioned.

Karsk/Branoc.t: The Sept of the Leshun near Broken Hill agreed to formal trade, and a market creating the title of Speaker to the Leshun was commissioned here.

Karsk/Crowslook.t: Mentioned in passing: Mirnatocz in Krevsaty stood near the border with Crowslook.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: In this Thule-held region, the warlocks of the Mirnatocz tower offered red moss in trade, and rival mandates proposed either stealing its secret or preventing any such raid.

Karsk/Nitrost.t: Mentioned in passing: orc settlements here were conquered by the Thule in 368YE, and their people fled to Branoc.

Miekarova/Miechernya.t: This Thule-held region is Orathator's base and a target for closer trade. The Highborn could reach it through Skarsind even if Varushka blocked their route.

Miekarova/Srodkoja.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan and Highborn pilgrims negotiated with Orathator at a Navarr wayhouse here.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bonewood is Thule-controlled, and the Thule freed Druj slaves from it during the liberation of Ossium.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Mentioned in passing: some Menrothat live in the eastern Drownbark Forest.

Ossium/Echofell.t: Mentioned in passing: some Menrothat live in south-eastern Echofell.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: The Menrothat sept is based in Nearweald and provides guides, workers and tithes to nearby vales.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Mentioned in passing: the Webwood is listed among the regions controlled by the Thule.

Otkodov/Nithoggir.t: Mentioned in passing: Orathator suspects the catacomb-library of Nithoggir holds a ritual like Delve Deep, Beneath the Mountain, but he cannot access it.

The Barrens/Farweald.t: The Menrothat seek the return of Farweald, their ancestral heartland, offering strong trade with Varushka and black lotus to the Imperial Orcs in exchange.

Volodmartz/Brez.t: The Gift of the Dwindling Star in Brez was the starting point of the High Path, completed before the Autumn Equinox 385YE so that its holder could buy up to four extra rings of Thule ilium.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Menrothat still under Druj rule here risk reprisals if their sept cooperates with the Empire, and the Dreamers of the Dark Forest have been asked for help against the threat of Druj invasion from here.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Delev Market in Karov is noted as the main existing route for quiet trade with the Thule.

Karsk.t: Karsk held several of the opportunities: masks for the Warden of the Trees and Hills at Ivarsgard, red moss from the Thule warlocks of Mirnatocz in exchange for a warehouse at the Sarcophan Mooring, and the Leshun Market in Branoc. A Varushkan counter-mandate could bring fighting with the Highborn here.

Miekarova.t: Orathator is based in Thule-held Miechernya and regularly visits the Butterfly Holt, where he offered masks to the Gloaming Sentinel. He seeks the Well of Shadows, which he believes lies somewhere in the territory.

Ossium.t: The Menrothat live in Ossium as guests of the Varushkans, offering guides, workers and help restoring vis-giving shrines at the Palace of Orieb. A Varushkan counter-mandate could bring fighting with the Highborn here.

Otkodov.t: The Thule homeland faces food shortages after the slaves were freed. The High Path through the mountains was opened so that Varushkan food could be traded for ilium from the fallen star in Sküld.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Well of Shadows once stood in Skarsind as Pakaanan's Tower, and the Highborn could reach Miechernya through the territory.

The Barrens.t: The Menrothat regard Farweald in the northern Barrens as their ancestral heartland and want it restored to them. The Highborn drew on recent experience in the Barrens when dealing with the Leshun.

The Semmerlak.t: Mentioned in passing: Ivarsgard, one of Orathator's regular stops, lies on the edge of the Semmerlak.

Volodmartz.t: The High Path to Otkodov was built from Brez. The Leshun also have ties with orc settlements in Volodmartz.

Pride in the Marches.d: The Lasambrian Jotun fled Mitwold, probably to defend Reinos against the Iron Confederacy. Meade, looted but jubilant, could repair its walls and raise a statue of Tom Drake to bolster the Drakes. The stolen Beater's cup went as tribute to the Fjorknae, whose fearless orc ships now harass Marcher and Wintermark fleets. Appraisals on the Fjorknae, the Gullet and a foot-the-ball league were proposed. In Bregasland, Grey Walkers released at Ullsmere Rock erode Jotun control of Grey Fens. Marchers want to know William Guildenstern's heroic deeds. Consecrating Rebellion's Ridge could reopen the Mournwold senator debate. Marchers would resist any persecution of Marcher orcs, risking civil war. Two Red Walder scions threaten Mitwold landmarks.

Jotun.t: The Lasambrian Jotun withdrew from Mitwold, apparently to defend Reinos, but still hold Bregasland, where Grey Walkers are loosening their grip on Grey Fens. Their Fjorknae kin received Meade's loot and now raid the Gullet by ship.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: a Marcher compares any foot-the-ball league unfavourably with the League's great game.

The Marches.t: Mitwold is freed and Meade can honour Tom Drake, but Marchers face Jotun in Bregasland, Fjorknae raiders at sea, debates over folk heroes and Mournwold's senator, and a near-unanimous resolve to defend Marcher orcs against the Synod.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark fleets escorting the fisherfolk of Westerhal, raiding Kalsea or trading with Caitun suffer from Fjorknae warships in the Gullet, and akhlut trailing those ships trouble the Winterfolk.

Pride in the Marches.o: In the summer of 388YE the Jotun abandoned Mitwold, leaving a looted Meade to welcome the Drakes, while blood-sailed Fjorknae warships appeared in the Gullet and ghosts haunted the Grey Fens. The Marches also weighed folk heroes, Rebellion's Ridge, defending Marcher orcs against heresy charges, and rowdy scions of Red Walder.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: Recovered by the Empire last season, Gravenmarch was unexpectedly left alone by the Jotun, while the Strong Reeds wait in the fens.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: Grey Walkers released at Ullsmere Rock haunt the region, harassing Jotun and Marcher households alike and steadily pushing to take the region for themselves.

Hordalant/Alsterbo.t: Holding Alsterbo alone no longer guarantees severing the Kongegőr; the Empire would need both ends of the bridge.

Mitwold/Golden Downs.t: Dusty Cobb leads rebels to burn the Golden Fields of Hay, and the Keeper of the Golden Fields, Nicolas Reaper, must stop him or the Silent Giant will suffer.

Mitwold/Maiden Downs.t: Jyll Longleys and her band march to wreck the Maiden Stone, and Champion of Prosperity Tom Appleseed must stop her or Mitwold's farms lose their profits for months.

Mitwold/Meade March.t: Meade was looted but freed and welcomed the Drakes, and may now repair its walls and raise a statue of Tom Drake.

Mitwold/Oddmire.t: Seized by the Jotun last year, Oddmire and Odd's End were abandoned as the Lasambrians fled before Imperial armies.

Mitwold/The Meadows.t: Reclaimed after the Battle of Wayford, the region lost treasures from Wayford, including the Beater's cup, to the Jotun.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: Rebellion's Ridge, honouring the executed leaders of the Ore Hills Rebellion, is complete, and consecrating it would stir the miners' old demands for a voice.

Skallahn/Bjarkey.t: The Empire nearly claimed Bjarkey, but holding the Kongegőr's northern end alone no longer guarantees cutting the bridge.

Bregasland.t: The Jotun consolidate their hold while the Strong Reeds lie low, a stone of the Ullsmere Rock dolmen has been carried off, and Grey Walkers now haunt Grey Fens.

Bryadvik.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial fleets mapping the Sea of Snow did not cross the Blood Straits between Bryadvik and Fjorknae.

Fjorknae.t: Its orcs received Meade's stolen treasure as tribute and now sail blood-red warships into the Gullet, yet the Empire knows almost nothing about the island and has no spies within reach.

Hordalant.t: A leg of the Ullsmere Rock dolmen has apparently been dragged here to inspire the Howling Night, and Alsterbo at the Kongegőr's southern end matters to any plan to sever the bridge.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: the retreating Lasambrian Jotun withdrew south into Liathaven, where Imperial scouts lost track of them.

Mitwold.t: The Jotun abandoned the territory after looting Meade and the Beater's cup; Meade may rebuild its walls with a Tom Drake statue, while Red Walder's scions threaten the Maiden Stone and the Golden Fields of Hay.

Mournwold.t: Rebellion's Ridge stands complete, and its consecration would revive bitter arguments over who appoints the senator, while Mournwold priests propose fining the Marcher orcs rather than persecuting them.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: news of the Iron Confederacy invasion of Reinos is the likely reason the Lasambrian Jotun fled Mitwold.

Sea of Snow.t: Fjorknae warships now prowl the Gullet and northern Sea of Snow, attacking Marcher and Wintermark vessels and possibly stirring the coral husks.

Skallahn.t: The earlier Imperial attack here came close to taking Bjarkey, and the Jotun are now alert to the threat of their jarldoms being cut apart at the Kongegőr.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: the hylje's proposal would need the smugglers cove at Tromsa re-established before it could be fully realised.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the loss of the Beater's cup has dampened foot-the-ball enthusiasm in Upwold as well as Mitwold.

Pride of the Marches.d: Using a Boon of Finding, Kimus' heralds traced the vorpal sword with which Tom Drake slew the tyrant-boyar Alderei the Fair. It is not an artefact, but it is the lawful heirloom of William Drake, a retired yeoman of Redstone. It was last wielded against the Jotun in the Mournwold in 349YE. William distrusts the Conclave. He will release the blade as regalia of the General of the Drakes only if two conditions are met. First, Tom Drake must be researched and published or recognised by the Synod as an exemplar of Pride. Second, the Senate must reinstate Drake's Due, adding 5 Thrones to the Drakes' upkeep each season. That would restore the Drummers and give the army the Pride of the Marches quality.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the sword was last wielded in battle against the Jotun in the Mournwold in 349YE, before that territory was lost.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Drummers' recruitment in other nations is contrasted with how the Navarr help those already seeking a new place in the Empire.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening story shows a carta of mountebanks trying to pass off a battered shield as Tom Drake's relic to hopeful Marchers.

The Marches.t: The Marches have a chance to recover their founding general's sword for the Drakes. They could also see Tom Drake honoured as an exemplar of Pride and the Drummers revived, if the Senate restores Drake's Due and the historical research or Synod recognition goes ahead.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the sword is the blade that killed the Varushkan tyrant-boyar Alderei the Fair in the battle that also cost Tom Drake his life.

Pride of the Marches.o: The heralds of the eternal Kimus, sent by the Imperial Conclave, found Tom Drake's vorpal sword hanging over the fireplace of his descendant William Drake in Upwold. William will give it only to the General of the Drakes, and only if the Empire meets certain conditions.

Upwold/The Heath.t: The region is tied to the discovery of Tom Drake's vorpal sword in Upwold, where his descendant William Drake keeps it above the hearth and refuses to let visitors trespass to see it.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the fake relic in the opening story was a real Marcher shield recovered from a battlefield outside Holberg.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is named as one of the territories where the Drakes' billet order is already available.

Mournwold.t: The sword was last used in the final fight against the Jotun here in 349YE. If Drake's Due is reinstated, the billet order would also become available in the Mournwold.

Upwold.t: Tom Drake's vorpal sword was found in Upwold, at William Drake's home on the family farmland in Redstone, where Tom Drake lies buried in Tom's Orchard.

Professional killers.d: A fortnight after the Summer Solstice, Edgar of Woldstone was attacked while researching the vallorn's origins in Rundhal. Marcher yeomen Warren of Aldstock and Jennifer Greenwood drove off the masked assassin, who died fleeing. Kallavesi mystics helped confirm it was a faceless herald, whose remains dissolved; its mask and gloves later vanished in transit to the Castle of Thorns. A second attacker escaped into a canal, and a third was captured in Helena Raminci di Sarvos's library. Found guilty of murder by Magistrate Avedon de Remourics, the herald destroyed itself. The Conclave later placed the Whisper Gallery under enmity. The Senate kept funding protection, but only two historical research projects could still be commissioned each season.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the herald's mask and gloves vanished from a sealed box while being sent to the Castle of Thorns in Astolat.

Wintermark.t: Several Kallavesi mystics helped Edgar of Woldstone examine the dead assassin, confirming it was a faceless herald rather than a mortal.

Professional killers.o: In Autumn 379YE, Senate-funded bodyguards foiled three further assassination attempts against civil servants of the department of historical research, and one assassin, revealed to be a herald, was captured. It was later confirmed as an agent of the Eternal council known as the Whisper Gallery.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the herald's mask and gloves were being taken to the Castle of Thorns in Astolat when they disappeared in transit.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the mystics who helped identify the slain herald are described as Kallavesi, though the examination took place in Rundhal.

Promises to keep.d: A small Thule party, led by a spellbinder and accompanied by armoured warriors and an apparent slave, approached the vale of Wendell's Hope near Coldmere. The schlacta at first refused them, but the spellbinder swore an oath of peace in the name of Orobus the Chained before witnesses, and the gates were opened. The Thule sought to address the Varushkans at Anvil and the Senate, and perhaps the Conclave, to discuss borders between Otkodov and the Empire and a possible end to hostilities. They were escorted south through Karov, then by Delev wardens. Protected under the law of delegations, they negotiated at Anvil, a peace treaty went before the Senate, and they returned safely to Otkodov.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on the page and plays no stated part in the Thule delegation.

Thule.t: The Thule of Otkodov sent a spellbinder-led embassy under oath to Orobus the Chained to negotiate borders and a cessation of hostilities, leading to a peace treaty being presented to the Senate before the delegation returned home safely.

Varushka.t: Varushkans guarded, received and escorted the Thule envoys from vale to vale, and were expected to be the first at Anvil to learn of their arrival and to hear their offer of peace and borders.

Promises to keep.o: In Summer 379YE a small Thule delegation came down from Otkodov to Wendell's Hope in Miekarova under a flag of truce, seeking to parley with the Empire at Anvil in the name of Orobus the Chained. It was later received at Anvil, where a peace treaty was presented to the Senate.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: The Thule party descended through the woods of Mieriada to Coldmere and the vale of Wendell's Hope, where the parley at the gates and the spellbinder's oath took place.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page and has no stated role in the events.

Karov.t: The Thule delegation was passed south through Karov by Varushkan escorts on its way to Anvil.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule spellbinder invoked what the people of Karsk would say if the schlacta turned the envoys away.

Miekarova.t: The Thule envoys arrived at Wendell's Hope in Miekarova, where the schlacta first refused them before opening the gates once the spellbinder swore an oath of peace beneath Miekarova's trees.

Otkodov.t: The Thule-held territory was the source of the delegation, which sought agreed borders between Otkodov and the Empire and returned there safely after the talks.

Promising light.d: Vesna, only the second Varushkan Throne after Varkula, called for Loyalty and unity, urged citizens to reach out to the disaffected, and declared the Barrens Imperial and Dawnish. Coal Carefoot led the festivities, funded by 250 thrones from the Senate, and celebrations ran from Varushkan bonfires to League masked balls and Dawnish fairs. Vesna chose to be styled Emperor and Empress interchangeably, with she/they pronouns. Her message created opportunities in Bregasland, Spiral and the Barrens. For as long as she reigns, any nation not currently supporting the Holy City may enact a Synod mandate committing each of its territories to donate four wains of white granite and eight crowns each season for a year.

Dawn.t: Dawn received the address especially warmly, giving most of the Grand Tour's tourneys over to the new Throne and holding new fairs, while Vesna declared the Barrens to be Imperial and Dawnish; Dawn had promised a single year's support for the Holy City.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Brass Coast's celebrations carried the hope that the new Throne would drive the Grendel from their lands once and for all.

Highguard.t: Highborn celebrations were restrained but well attended, and the address spoke to the Highborn ideal of a grand destiny while renewing attention on their commitment to build the Holy City at Bastion until it is complete.

Imperial Orcs.t: Great feasts marked the coronation in Skarsind, and as a nation that had declined to support the Holy City, the Imperial Orcs could enact the new mandate to back the project.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, though Bregasland, which they held, is one of the troubled places where the call for unity created new opportunities.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: there was feasting and storytelling in the steadings of Navarr, and Navarr is listed among the nations that pledged a single year's support to the Holy City.

The League.t: Masked balls were held in every League city and one Merchant Prince commissioned a touring play about the new Throne advised by ghosts of past Thrones, while the address opened new opportunities to address strife in Spiral.

Urizen.t: Urizen held restrained but well-attended celebrations, and having declined to support the Holy City, it could enact the new mandate to contribute granite and funds.

Varushka.t: Varushka led the celebrations with bonfires and feasts in almost every vale, proud to see the first Varushkan Throne since Varkula, and as a nation that had declined to support the Holy City it could enact the new mandate.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: there was feasting and storytelling in Wintermark's halls, and Wintermark is listed among the nations that pledged a single year's support to the Holy City.

Promising light.o: Following her coronation at the Autumn Equinox, the civil service distributed Emperor Vesna Borkovna Prochnost's inaugural address across the Empire, sparking breath-taking celebrations and a renewed sense of optimism. Her call for unity and for the Empire to unite the world under the Way opened new opportunities in troubled lands and revived support for the Holy City at Bastion.

Astolat/Coombe.t: A new fair was arranged in Coombe to celebrate the coronation.

Semmerholm/Ferrond.t: Mentioned in passing: Ferrond is not named, though it lies within Dawn, where the address was especially well received.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: A new fair was arranged in Dawnguard, in the Barrens that the Throne declared Imperial and Dawnish.

Astolat.t: A new fair was arranged in Coombe as part of Dawn's celebrations of the new Throne.

Bastion.t: The Throne's call to unite the world under the Way renewed focus on transforming the White City of Bastion into a new Holy City, a project needing a thousand wains of white granite.

Bregasland.t: The call to put aside division and reach out to the disaffected created new opportunities to address the strife in Bregasland.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm is not named, though it shared in Dawn's wider celebrations of the new Throne.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: great feasts were held in Skarsind to mark the coronation.

Spiral.t: The impassioned plea for unity resonated strongly in strife-torn Spiral, where it created new opportunities to address the turmoil.

The Barrens.t: Vesna declared the Barrens Imperial and Dawnish, pledging to claim it for citizens while honouring treaties, offering friendship to those who would live alongside them and meeting violence with force, which brought new opportunities there.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater is not named, though it shared in Dawn's wider celebrations of the new Throne.

Propensity to truck, barter, and exchang.d: After fast-moving prices and a change of trading staff angered Imperial merchants at the Spring Equinox, the herald Crown consulted the Urizeni architect Abel the Rounder. The City then made eight contracts available for auction to the highest bidder in the Hall of Worlds. Each had to be fulfilled in full at the same summit, with payment three days later, to keep bulk sales from flooding the market. The City also published guidance on the goods it values, favouring ingots, measures, unique goods, herbs and liao, and said large bulk sales outside contracts would draw lower offers. Heralds were open to becoming patron of the Golden Pyramid or its grand lodge, provided the Archmage of Autumn secured a dedicated plenipotentiary before the end of Spring 389YE.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; their only link is that they held Sarangrave, the territory the heralds' banter calls Abel the Rounder's home.

Propensity to truck, barter, and exchang.o: Ephisis, Sovereign Lady of the City of Gold and Lead, announced changes to trading through Ephisis' Scale after price problems at the Spring Equinox. Eight large contracts would be auctioned in the Hall of Worlds, alongside published price guidance and an offer to discuss patronage of the Golden Pyramid.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: in the in-character exchange, the herald Patina describes Abel the Rounder as one of Sarangrave's foremost architects and calls it a territory with major investment needs.

Propose treaty of limited warfare to the.d: Proposed by the senator for Bregasland and seconded by the senator for Mitwold, the motion sought to open communications with the Jotun to limit the war to Mournwold and Liathaven. It would have suggested an amendment to the Jotun ceasefire then in place. The motion was defeated at the in-principle stage, with 7 votes for and 20 against, so no such proposal was made to the Jotun.

Jotun.t: The Jotun would have been approached with a proposal to confine fighting with the Empire to Mournwold and Liathaven, but the Senate voted the idea down, so no offer was sent.

Propose treaty of limited warfare to the.o: In Spring 378YE the Senate rejected a motion to open communications with the Jotun proposing that fighting be restricted to Mournwold and Liathaven, an amendment to the existing Jotun ceasefire.

Liathaven.t: Liathaven, held by the Jotun, was named as one of the two territories where fighting would have been confined, had the failed motion passed.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold, held by the Jotun, would have been one of only two territories where war with the Jotun continued under the proposed amendment, which the Senate rejected.

Prospecting in Skarsind.d: Proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by Spiral, the motion took up the opportunity from the Standing in the Sun Wind of Fortune. With support from the Order of the Golden Pyramid, encouraged by the Imperial Conclave, the cost fell to 100 thrones, which Irontide Flax provided after the Winter Solstice; the work takes three months. Once complete, upgrading Imperial Orc military units costs one wain less mithril (minimum one wain), and Imperial Orc armies in Skarsind gain the Forge Hammers order: camping around the Black Forge above Gildenheim, suffering a fifth more casualties but defending three tenths better, with extra strength from mithril used for emergency resupply.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orc armies gain cheaper upgrades, needing one wain less mithril, and access to the Forge Hammers order to defend Skarsind from the Black Forge.

Prospecting in Skarsind.o: The Senate passed a motion in Winter 385YE inviting human prospectors and mining experts to explore the northern hills of Skarsind and work the Imperial Orc mines, at a cost of 100 thrones funded by Irontide Flax.

Skarsind.t: Human miners come to work the Imperial Orc mines in Skarsind's northern hills, and the Black Forge above Gildenheim becomes a fortified camp from which orc armies can defend the territory.

Protect or punish.d: Navarr warbands had slowed the vallorn, but three husk swarms, lured by heralds of Yaw'nagrah and guarded by ettercaps, still roamed Brocéliande, and a Navarr party was trapped at Highborn Rest Wayfort. Orc bandits in Willstone had enslaved pilgrims bound for the Conservatory of Music. Druj ambushers and a miasma pillar lurked in the Webwood, where captured scouts were held. Chikad slavers were marching Urizen captives from Caeli towards Zenith. Conjunctions to Stark and East Floes offered a small advantage against the Jotun if taken that season. The Silent Bell found that the Eater-of-Hope's last anchor might lie in Estmure.

Dawn.t: Dawn's region of Estmure was beset by twisted knights, war-witches and yeofolk, possibly through the Eater-of-Hope's final anchor. Its soldiers had also been vanishing in the woods of Ossium.

Druj.t: Druj ambushers, saboteurs and a miasma pillar in the Webwood, and Chikad slavers driving captives out of Caeli, were all targets for Imperial strikes through the Sentinel Gate.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel warlord had been the Eater-of-Hope's anchor, defeated and exorcised in the Summer battle in Spiral.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the trapped Navarr party was heading for Casinea, and Highguard heroes were among those urged to help free captives in Morrow.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun scouts were patrolling the border with Skarsind.

Jotun.t: Jotun skirmishers at Bleak Rise in Stark and on the Sundered Plain in East Floes faced Imperial strikes meant to weaken their hold on those regions.

Navarr.t: Navarr warbands had slowed the vallorn in Brocéliande. Some of their fighters were now trapped in Vale's Lament, and three herald-led husk swarms remained to be struck.

The Marches.t: Marcher beaters fed reports to the prognosticators. Victory at Bleak Rise would help forward units of the Bounders against the Jotun, whose scouts patrolled the Bregasland border.

Urizen.t: Urizen faced pilgrims enslaved by bandits in Willstone and citizens dragged off by Druj slavers in Caeli. Menos urged all ten nations to help free the captives.

Varushka.t: Varushkan soldiers had vanished in the Webwood, where the Golden Axe had recently passed by Fang Tree. Varushkan heroes were also urged to help rescue captives in Morrow.

Wintermark.t: Suaq hunters scouted Jotun movements as the Empire pushed into Sealtoq, and strikes in Stark and East Floes offered help towards retaking more of Sermersuaq.

Protect or punish.o: Ahead of the Winter Solstice 382YE, the civil service published the Sentinel Gate conjunctions it had found. They offered chances to fight vallorn swarms in Brocéliande, free captives in Redoubt and Morrow, harry the Druj in Ossium and strike Jotun raiders in Sermersuaq. It also reported a dark stirring in Estmure tied to the Eater-of-Hope.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Navarr efforts had stopped the vallorn gathering strength here. A conjunction to West Weaver Wood, near the Semmerholm border, allowed an attack on one herald-led swarm.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: A conjunction to the Exile Trod allowed an assault on the third herald of Yaw'nagrah moving through the region with its husks and ettercaps.

Brocéliande/Vale's Lament.t: In this miasma-drowned region a Navarr party was trapped at Highborn Rest Wayfort, and a second conjunction targeted a herald in the Depths of Lament.

Casinea/Mareholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn Rest Wayfort lay close to the border with Mareholm.

Morrow/Caeli.t: Chikad skirmishers were leading Urizen captives out of the region. Conjunctions to the Meadow of Sighs and Derontian Field offered a race to rescue them.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Druj ambushers and a hidden temple of the Spider King troubled the region. Conjunctions offered a chance to destroy a miasma pillar at Fang Tree and rescue captured scouts at Dark Bark Glade.

Redoubt/Willstone.t: Bandits had enslaved pilgrims bound for the Conservatory at Willstone Spire. Four conjunctions offered light-resistance fights to free them so they could finish their journey.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Mentioned in passing: the Exile Trod in Elerael lay close to the Llofir-claimed woods of Tamarbode.

Semmerholm/Estmure.t: A dreadful shadow fell over Estmure as knights, war-witches and yeofolk were twisted to cruelty, likely by the Eater-of-Hope's last anchor. A conjunction opened to a tortured glade.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: A conjunction to the Sundered Plain offered a chance to overcome Jotun raiders near the Red Wind Corsairs, giving a small advantage towards seizing the region.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Imperial forces had pushed the Jotun back and begun forcing a beachhead here to support the wider campaign in Sermersuaq.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: A conjunction to Bleak Rise offered a chance to overcome Jotun skirmishers near the Bounders' forward units, giving a small advantage towards seizing the region.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun scouts were patrolling its border with Sermersuaq.

Brocéliande.t: The vallorn had been slowed but not defeated. Four conjunctions opened to rescue trapped Navarr and attack three husk swarms led by heralds of Yaw'nagrah.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the trapped Navarr party had been heading to Casinea, and Vale's Lament lies near its region of Mareholm.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is not named; the page only notes that without a beachhead it would be hard to cross from West March into Stark.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun scouts were patrolling its border with Sermersuaq.

Morrow.t: As Imperial forces advanced, Druj slavers were driving Urizen captives towards Zenith. Two conjunctions into Caeli offered chances to rescue them.

Ossium.t: Despite the Imperial conquest of the Webwood, Druj ambushers and servants of Arhallogen remained there, and two conjunctions offered strikes against them.

Redoubt.t: Orc bandits had grown bold amid the Druj war and enslaved a pilgrimage to the Conservatory of Music. Four conjunctions offered a chance to free the pilgrims.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Exile Trod conjunction lay close to the Llofir-claimed woods of Tamarbode.

Semmerholm.t: Estmure suffered acts of cruelty and murder that the Silent Bell traced to the Eater-of-Hope's possible last anchor, and a conjunction opened to a tortured glade there.

Sermersuaq.t: With a beachhead forced in Sealtoq, conjunctions to Stark and East Floes offered chances to counter Jotun warbands and prepare future advances.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun scouts were patrolling its border with Sermersuaq.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Solstice battle against the Eater-of-Hope's Grendel anchor had been fought there.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Druj slavers were leading Urizen captives along tracks from Caeli towards Zenith, which the Druj had invaded.

Proud to serve.d: Heilyn named the Empire's greatest challenges as internal: threats to the unity of the faith, to trust between nations and to the economy. With the strategic mana fund severely reduced, individual mages and covens had paid for the border fortresses and several army enchantments; Heilyn thanked them, naming covens including the Saker, Skywise and Carta Notturno, and urged citizens to donate crystals. Acknowledging terrible magic used by the Empire, he swore to consult carefully and, if he supported action costing Imperial civilian lives, to submit himself to the affected nation's Senators and National Assembly. He stood by the military council's Mournwold decision and welcomed the new Conclave Order of the Silver Chalice under Raewynn Farkas.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the three external foes the Empire faces, which Heilyn set aside to speak of internal challenges.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the three external foes the Empire faces, which Heilyn set aside to speak of internal challenges.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the three external foes the Empire faces, which Heilyn set aside to speak of internal challenges.

The Marches.t: The Warmage addressed the Mournwold, a Marcher territory, directly, saying he had seen first-hand what the military council's decision there cost and stood by it, while pledging to submit to the Senators and National Assembly of any nation bearing grave civilian losses from future strategic magic.

Proud to serve.o: Imperatrix Lisabetta lent her power to address the Empire to the Imperial Warmage, Heilyn Bronwen's Rest, who spoke to all citizens about the strain of funding strategic magic, the grave costs of recent ritual decisions such as those in the Mournwold, and the founding of the Order of the Silver Chalice.

Mournwold.t: Heilyn acknowledged the heavy cost of the military council's strategy in the Mournwold, which he witnessed himself, and declared he stood by the decision though he would have preferred a better option.

Provide aid to the Hierro Clan.d: Proposed by Feroz and seconded by the senator for Segura, the motion directed the civil service to supply the Hierro Clan, refugees then camped in Segura, with vital provisions. It was passed with an ongoing cost of 75 thrones each season. As a result, the Hierro Clan began receiving supplies and had not, at the time, been forced to turn to banditry to survive.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast's senators drove the motion that saw the Empire take on the cost of feeding the Hierro Clan refugees sheltering in their nation, keeping them from turning to banditry.

Provide aid to the Hierro Clan.o: In Autumn 379YE the Senate passed a motion authorising the civil service to provide aid to the Hierro clan refugees camped in Segura, at an upkeep of 75 thrones per season.

Segura.t: The Hierro Clan refugees camped in Segura began receiving Imperial supplies, which had so far kept them from resorting to banditry in the territory.

Pruning shears.d: Benson was recognised as an exemplar of Vigilance in 379YE but remains little known outside the Marches. In Spring 385YE the Marcher Assembly passed Rowan Harper's judgement by greater majority, but Martin Orchard's General Assembly judgement fell short of one. A conjunction of unstable size, currently twenty, lets Martin Orchard lead Marchers to consecrate the orchard with true liao. Proposed mandates included: sending Upwold pilgrims to seek out dangers in the territory; competing Marcher mandates freeing threshers against the Whisper Gallery, either in the Marches or in Tassato, each costing mana production; and a Highborn mandate urging inquisitors and magisters to hunt Gallery cultists in Highguard.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Benson is believed to have taken part in the March from Dawn, and his recognition credits him with saving Dawnish as well as Marcher souls.

Highguard.t: Aemon of the Suns of Couros proposed a Highborn mandate urging inquisitors and magisters to hunt Whisper Gallery cultists in Highguard. It would cost every Highborn mana site one crystal until Winter 385YE in exchange for a chance to ensnare a major Gallery agent.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the war in Bregasland is cited as the matter keeping Upwold's folk too busy to pry into their neighbours' business.

The League.t: Martin Orchard proposed a Marcher mandate sending threshers into Tassato after Whisper Gallery allies. This would bring street fighting and lost mana to the League territory.

The Marches.t: Marchers could consecrate Benson's grave-orchard to Vigilance and might pass mandates for Upwold pilgrims to root out hidden dangers. They might also let threshers hunt the Whisper Gallery beyond the bounds of law, at a cost to every Marcher mana site and monolith farm.

Pruning shears.o: Following Synod judgements honouring the little-known Marcher exemplar "Major" Joshua Benson, a Sentinel Gate conjunction opened to his grave-orchard at Pickham Monastery so it could be consecrated to Vigilance. The Wind of Fortune also set out proposed mandates for unleashing threshers and others against the Whisper Gallery.

Upwold/Tower March.t: The Sentinel Gate opened to Benson's Orchard in Tower March, letting around twenty Marchers led by Martin Orchard consecrate the exemplar's resting place to Vigilance with true liao.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the war in Bregasland is described as the focus of most folk's attention in neighbouring Upwold.

Tassato.t: A proposed Marcher mandate would send threshers into Tassato, the first home of Berechiah, to hunt the Whisper Gallery. It would cause armed clashes in the streets and cost every mana site two crystals after the Summer Solstice.

Upwold.t: Pickham Monastery's grave-orchard in Upwold could be consecrated to Vigilance. A proposed mandate would send Upwold's Vigilant pilgrims hunting heretics, traitors and other threats, with a report of active dangers due at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Push for victory.d: Vesna praised Navarr for privately funding its third army and commended several heroes. A Freeborn corsair, Aracely, proposed a raid on Leen through the Salt Flats smugglers' cove, which would expose the cove to destruction. The raid was an overwhelming success, freeing thousands of slaves. The Barossa School offered to make one army fast for ten wains of mithril. A Sand Fisher offer to approach a sept under Druj rule went unused. Dawn, the Imperial Orcs and Wintermark could enact mandates to raise military units. Highguard's benefactors offered to fund any commission. Further offers covered weirwood for the Breadbasket, Urizen mana sites (not enacted), a weirwood-built Navarr army, Delev mithril for the Throne, and a Rahvin attack on the Karass.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish Assembly could enact a mandate letting Dawnish citizens convert farms, mines, forests and similar holdings into military units of the same level in the same territory for a season.

Druj.t: Vesna declared the Druj a dying regime. Freeborn raiders struck Leen and freed thousands of their slaves, and the Rahvin sought leave to destroy the Karass, whom they call Druj servants.

Highguard.t: Inspired by the Throne, the Highborn Council of Benefactors agreed to direct its twelve wains a season to any commission, rather than only civilian works such as the Grand Inspiration of the Way.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc Assembly could enact a mandate encouraging the Unshackled to turn their holdings into military units of the same level, supporting the war on the Druj.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Vesna warned that the Jotun will see the Empire fight for what is its own from Bregasland to Sermersuaq to Tassato.

Navarr.t: Vesna praised Navarr for funding its third army without public money or bourse seats; that army finishes mustering at the Autumn Equinox 388YE. A further army could be raised with Great Forest Orc help, using weirwood in place of mithril, and Navarr supply will fall if no new army begins by Autumn 389YE.

The League.t: The League's third army in Tassato was funded two seasons early as Vesna's 'hand in the West'. The Barossa School offered to make an army fast, and the League Assembly could direct the Sand Fishers to approach a Druj-ruled sept, though that judgement was withdrawn.

The Marches.t: Alders of Wayford secured ten wains of weirwood for expanding the Marcher Breadbasket into the Mournwold, paid for by Keeper Orson BogMyrtle. Alders of Hay offered ten more for 30 thrones, and Vesna named the Marches among the nations that could raise more armies.

Urizen.t: The Urizen Assembly faced two competing mandates to cut the cost of upgrading mana sites, one adding a contest between territories, but neither was enacted.

Varushka.t: A Delev consortium offered to sell the Throne up to forty wains of mithril a season, starting at three thrones a wain, to raise armies. Varushkans celebrated Vesna, even comparing him flatteringly with Empress Varkula.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark Assembly could enact a mandate letting citizens convert holdings into military units of the same level. Vesna also commended Ematius Ankarien for his years as Archmage of Winter.

Push for victory.o: In his Spring 388YE Throne address, Emperor Vesna announced the early completion of the third League army and urged a final push against the Druj. Citizens across the Empire rallied in response, producing a series of opportunities for the war and beyond.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: The Throne's words reached the Misericorde Market, where the Sand Fishers resolved to try to persuade a Druj-ruled sept to trust the Empire, despite Three Hands' fears.

Redoubt/Siluri.t: Adelmar the Lion's Academy of Arms in the mountains of Siluri, now a place of pilgrimage, inspired Urizen's second, unenacted mandate.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Leen Rarckan.t: Freeborn corsairs raided Leen Rarckan with overwhelming success, freeing thousands of slaves, many of whom had never been Imperial citizens.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: The Rahvin army was still being raised in Bitter Strand, and some of its eager recruits offered to attack the Karass under General Utmar.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: The Karass of the Bleaks faced possible annihilation by the Rahvin if, during this one season, the Empire declared war on them or the Senate ceded the Bleaks to them.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Imperial heroes prevented the riling of the vallorn in Eastring, and Vesna commended the Vallornguard and Ser Rhydian de Rondell for leading and funding the skirmish.

Bastion.t: The Grand Inspiration of the Way under construction in Bastion could lose its twelve wains a season of Highborn funding if the Council of Benefactors redirected it to another commission.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Vesna named Bregasland among the western lands the Empire will fight to reclaim from the Jotun.

Hercynia.t: Navarr's third army was nearly mustered in Hercynia, with its general due at the Autumn Equinox 388YE. Hercynia was also a possible site for a new Navarr army built with weirwood.

Holberg.t: Three Hands wrote to Holberg's senator offering to have the Sand Fishers approach a sept under Druj rule. He warned that failure could harm the Empire's relations with Holberg's orcs, and no such approach was made.

Karov.t: Delev merchants, having completed the wards on the Little Boyar's Welcome, offered mithril from their vales and outposts to the Throne for raising armies, rather than selling it to the Commonwealth.

Miaren.t: Miaren was one of two possible sites for a new Navarr army built with weirwood, though such an army could not be combined with the Miaren opportunity to raise an army of vates.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold is not named directly; its relevance lies in the Marcher Breadbasket, whose expansion into the Mournwold was being supplied with weirwood through the alders of Wayford and Hay.

Mournwold.t: Ten wains of weirwood were set aside for expanding the Marcher Breadbasket into the Mournwold, and ten more were offered for 30 thrones if bought by the Summer Solstice.

Redoubt.t: Adelmar the Lion's Academy of Arms in Redoubt inspired a Urizen mandate for a contest between territories over mana investment, but it was not enacted.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: The hidden Imperial smugglers' cove here was used to launch the Freeborn raid on Leen. The price of the raid was its exposure and destruction by the Druj after the corsairs evacuated it.

Sarangrave.t: Vesna declared the Empire on the verge of completing its conquest of the Sarangrave, with thoughts already turning to settling and building up the lands won there.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Vesna named Sermersuaq among the western lands the Empire will fight for against the Jotun.

Tassato.t: The third League army was mustering in Tassato, and the Barossa School of Imperial Strategy there offered to make any one army except the Argent Sword fast, for ten wains of mithril.

The Barrens.t: The Rahvin sought a chance to wipe out the Karass, whom they call Druj traitors in the Barrens, if the Empire declared war on that sept or ceded the Bleaks to it. The Barrens slave rebellion was also cited as the reason Druj-ruled septs distrust the Empire.

Therunin.t: Vesna commended the heroes who stopped the riling of the vallorn in Eastring. The Great Forest Orcs, who once offered to support an army in Therunin, renewed their pledge to help raise a Navarr army.

Put on your war paint.d: The Footfall of the Beginning returned the Burning Falcon's banner, so the Freeborn assembly could pass competing mandates to rally kohan to a revived army. Either would cut its cost by 20 wains and 40 crowns, and the bolder one would grant the True Conviction quality. A third mandate would help the Fire of the South and Red Wind Corsairs seize mithril. None takes effect until the Senate approves the army. Serra Briante and Kahraman citizens offered 20 wains of mithril to the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills at 22 crowns each. Marcher and Dawnish mandates could let generals refine army qualities, though Dawn's would bar giving ground. Wintermark's would extend fight with honour to poison-using allies.

Dawn.t: A Dawn assembly mandate, in a general or witch-focused version, would bar Dawnish generals from the Give Ground and Cautious Advance orders for a year and offer them chances to refine army qualities at the Winter Solstice. The ban would become permanent if any general took up such a chance.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj invasion of Semmerholm was defeated and Dawn has invaded Ossium, and Wintermark likens poisoning and ambush tactics to Druj ways.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel have been forced out of Kahraman and their last soldiers rounded up in Madruga by Marcher armies.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are cited as having already reshaped their armies to suit their traditions over the past year.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the original Burning Falcon was lost to a Jotun invasion of Kallavesa, and the Jotun have since been driven from Kahraman.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr have reshaped their armies to fit their traditions, and Navarr armies helped drive the Grendel and Jotun from Kahraman.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn assembly could rally kohan to revive the Burning Falcon, cheapening the army and possibly giving it True Conviction, and could urge its armies to plunder mithril. All of this depends on Senate approval of the new army.

The Marches.t: Marcher generals are celebrated for never giving ground. An assembly mandate would let them refine their armies' qualities at the Winter Solstice, with an emphasis on defending the land without drowning it in blood.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is cited as having already reshaped its armies to suit its traditions.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's generals have already made the Fist of the Mountain farsighted and the Green Shield truly heroic. A new mandate would extend fight with honour to allied armies using whatever it takes or fire in the blood.

Put on your war paint.o: Several national assemblies were offered Synod mandates to reshape their armies after statements of principle at the Summer Solstice 382YE. The Freeborn could support reviving the historical Burning Falcon army, the Marches and Dawn could refine their armies' qualities, and Wintermark could widen its condemnation of dishonourable tactics.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: The people of Serra Briante, led by Loida i Drazia i Erigo's suggestion, offered 20 wains of mithril to the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills at 22 crowns a wain. The mithril can be bought once the Senate approves a new Freeborn army.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Marcher armies are praised for driving back the vallorn to protect Bregasland.

Kahraman.t: Mine owners and traders of Kahraman joined Serra Briante in offering 20 wains of mithril toward a new Freeborn army, an offer open until the end of the Spring Equinox 383YE. Purchasing the mithril and then failing to raise the army would destroy the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills' standing there.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Burning Falcon was lost over 130 years ago defending Kallavesa against a Jotun invasion.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Marcher armies rounded up the last Grendel soldiers in Madruga.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Marcher generals are credited with liberating the Mournwold.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish invasion of Ossium is said to have cemented the nation's pride in its armies and generals.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish armies defeated the Druj invasion of Semmerholm before striking north.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Marcher armies fought the Jotun in defence of Sermersuaq.

Queens and kings.d: Solomon, the Archmage of Summer, had proposed a tourney to end Cathan Canae's blizzards over the Icy Crag. Barien organised a grand melee in the Dawnish Glory square, with each interested eternal sponsoring three champions. Eleonaris publicly rebuked Dawn for snubbing her herald and siding with Jaheris, and invited willing champions to her Marshal. Her champions won, and she became patron of the college; rival eternals accepted the result for now. Koboldi offered mine owners help expanding their mines in exchange for white granite and any non-magical finds. Arsenio Rezia di Tassato raised the required Declaration of Concord, so mines enchanted with Delve Deep, Beneath the Mountain could be upgraded using white granite that season.

Dawn.t: Eleonaris singled out Dawn for ignoring her herald and siding with the traitor Jaheris, while still calling on her Knights of Glory. She said she would judge the nation's heart by whether Dawnish champions stood forth for her, and her rebuke shocked many in Dawn's lands.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris is noted to have been openly supportive of the Jotun orcs.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening scene shows Varushkan miners suspiciously hearing a koboldi foreman's offer on behalf of King Adamant, whom one of them briefly mistakes for Agramant.

Queens and kings.o: Several Summer eternals approached the Empire. A Tourney of Sun and Ice was held to settle patronage of the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, and King Adamant sent his koboldi to offer help expanding Imperial mines. Eleonaris's champions won the tourney, and the Grandmaster of the Golden Pyramid accepted Adamant's offer.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova is not named. The page's only Varushkan link is a scene of Varushkan miners meeting koboldi, whose offer applied to mine owners across the Empire.

Questions of virtue.d: The Jotun withdrew from Kahraman into Liaven's Glen, leaving champions who had survived Orchard's Watch to fight to the death under empty red banners at Fort Braydon. A Highborn priest urged the Freeborn to decide the fate of the bodies: competing mandates offered a Jotun burial mound, return of the corpses to the Jotun borders, a Freeborn pyre, or looting them and leaving them for carrion, which would make the Jotun treat the Freeborn like the Navarr. Highguard could mandate support for Freeborn armies in the Brass Coast and Feroz. Tharim offered 1,000 knights for a year in exchange for feasting on Freeborn mana sites and herb gardens. After Asavea destroyed the Isle of the Osseini and Shantarim, corsairs could be urged to vengeance, to break the Sumaah blockade, or to guard the Bay.

Dawn.t: Tharim's agreement to help Dawn retake the Barrens had just expired, and he proposed sending the knights stationed there to the Fire of the South instead.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun insult the Navarr as 'Imperial Druj', and the Freeborn were judged unlikely to honour Druj customs under one mandate.

Grendel.t: Grendel-held Feroz was named as a target the Highborn could help the Freeborn reclaim, and Tharim's knights would fight the Grendel as well as the Jotun; the destruction of Osseini and Shantarim was carried out by their Asavean allies.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly, acting on its peerless kinship, could mandate that Highborn armies and units fighting in the Brass Coast or Feroz gain bonuses until Summer 386YE, and could also send its fleets to help thwart the Asavean blockade of Sumaah.

Jotun.t: The Jotun left Kahraman, their champions from Orchard's Watch dying at Fort Braydon to expunge their shame, and how the Freeborn treat the bodies would shape Jotun views of the Brass Coast, possibly leading them to treat it like the Navarr.

Navarr.t: The Jotun reserve particular hatred for the Navarr, Navarr soldiers fought at Fort Braydon and argued against honouring the dead, and a contemptuous treatment of the bodies would see the Freeborn regarded much as the Navarr are.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn Assembly faced competing mandates on the Jotun dead, on corsair vengeance or the Sumaah blockade, and on a proposed naming convention for newcomers, while Highguard and Tharim offered aid amid the looming threat from the Broken Shore.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun champions had fought in the Mournwold and survived Orchard's Watch, shamed by their failure to protect the thralls of the Mournwold.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn's earlier help in reclaiming Zenith was cited as a model for aiding the Freeborn.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: adding a fourth Freeborn tribe was likened to Wintermark developing a new tradition.

Questions of virtue.o: After the Jotun quit Kahraman, leaving only champions to die defending Fort Braydon, the Brass Coast faced a choice over how to treat their bodies. Highguard was offered a way to aid the Freeborn, Tharim offered his knights to the Fire of the South, and the Freeborn weighed naming customs and corsair vengeance on Asavea.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: The last Jotun encampment around Fort Braydon fought to the death here, and the Freeborn must decide whether their bodies are mounded, burned, returned or left for carrion.

Liathaven/Liaven's Glen.t: The Jotun retreated from Kahraman back into Liaven's Glen before the Imperial armies arrived.

Bay of Catazar.t: One proposed mandate would have Freeborn corsairs forgo vengeance and instead guard the Bay against barbarians.

Feroz.t: The Isle of the Osseini and Shantarim in Feroz were destroyed by Asavean warships, ending the Justicars, and a Highborn mandate could aid Freeborn armies seeking to retake the Grendel-held territory.

Kahraman.t: The Jotun abandoned Kahraman after raiding across the Cinnabar Hills, leaving its people to decide how to deal with the champions slain at Fort Braydon.

Liathaven.t: The Jotun withdrew into Liathaven, and one mandate would see cartloads of Jotun dead carried to its borders.

Madruga.t: With the peace treaty ending, an invasion of Madruga by the orcs of the Broken Shore was considered almost inevitable, and Highborn aid against the Dry Patricians there was suggested.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the fallen Jotun champions were veterans of the Mournwold fighting at Orchard's Watch.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: one mandate would return the Jotun bodies to the borders of Reinos and Liathaven.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Segura was noted as sharing a long border with Jotun lands, open to renewed invasion.

The Barrens.t: Tharim's knights in the Barrens, whose deal with Dawn had expired, would leave to join the Fire of the South if the Freeborn accepted his offer.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn help in reclaiming Zenith was cited as precedent.

Quietude.d: Anka Karass identified two sept members who revealed the Last Battle's location to the Druj and expected the Empire to execute them. Imperial law does not make it a crime for foreigners to aid the Empire's enemies, so the Envoy to the Karass had to tell her at the Execution Field in the Bleaks that she must free them. Knights-errant of House Courcillon were goading the Karass, and Dawnish troubadours' poetry outreach was angrily rebuffed. Anka again asked for the wayhouse to be moved. The Hearth Hearted's enchantment aided Dawn, Navarr, the Great Forest Orcs and the Rahvin, but not the Karass. The Great Forest Orcs completed the Fastness of Thorns, proposed a Navarr Broker of Thorns receiving 11 wains of weirwood, and gifted Lady Renata a wain of weirwood.

Dawn.t: Dawnish settlers gained prosperity from the Hearth Hearted enchantment and the Great Forest Orcs answered Renata's Gift with a wain of weirwood, but House Courcillon's knights-errant and the troubadours' poetry outreach inflamed the Karass.

Druj.t: Druj influence over the Barrens is ebbing. Their recent attack on the Last Battle relied on information from two Karass, whom Anka Karass has now handed over.

Navarr.t: The Navarr benefited from the Autumn enchantment and faced Karass demands to move the Last Battle. The Great Forest Orcs offered them a proposed Broker of Thorns seat receiving 11 wains of weirwood a season, in return for aid if the Eaves of Peytaht are threatened.

Quietude.o: In Winter 387YE the Barrens grew quieter as Druj influence faded. The Karass handed over two members accused of betraying the Last Battle wayhouse to the Druj, while a Dawnish Autumn enchantment brought prosperity to most of the territory's other inhabitants.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: Aided by the Autumn enchantment, the Rahvin made significant progress mustering and arming an army with Fangs mithril. They pointedly ignored the Dawnish apart from a complaint that stolen mithril has not been returned.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: The Great Forest Orcs completed the weirwood Fastness of Thorns, sheltered thriving communities of refugees and offered weirwood to the Navarr and Rahvin. They also sent a gift of weirwood to Lady Renata.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: Mentioned in passing: survivors of the destruction of Hope's Rest now live in the Heart of Peytaht, where the Great Forest Orcs keep them apart from the Therunin refugees.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: The Last Battle wayhouse, attacked by the Druj, remains a grievance for the Karass, who also face harassment there by Courcillon knights-errant. Anka Karass waits with the accused pair at the Execution Field.

The Barrens/The Untrod Groves.t: The Karass live scattered here, and the Earl of the Groves is rumoured to be making mysterious preparations in his manse at the heart of the Groves.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the remnants of the Black Wind are said to have fled alongside the Druj after a failed invasion of the Sarangrave.

The Barrens.t: The territory grew quieter and more Dawnish as an Autumn enchantment spread prosperity among those with dominion there. Tensions with the Karass festered while the Great Forest Orcs and Rahvin grew stronger.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: refugees from Therunin have gathered at the Last Battle wayhouse and among the Great Forest Orcs in the Barrens.

Rabbits and snares.d: Irra Harah answered Volfe of Ashenhall, Archmage of Spring, through a young Marcher-garbed briar. He agreed to parley around two on Saturday about the Mournwold, the Barrens and the tyrants of Asavea. He asked to hear from non-citizens, to meet Raewynn Farkas of the Navarr and Highborn Hazelelponi, and only then to speak briefly with the archmage. He would withdraw if the Imperial Warmage attended. The Lictors sent an engraved square of green iron accepting a formal parley at eleven on Friday night, and the civil service advised caution. Zakalwe declined a formal parley but would send representatives at five on Saturday. He asked that Vaan of the Auric Horizon attend so he could fulfil an obligation.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the state of the Barrens, then held by the Druj, is one of the subjects Irra Harah wishes to raise at his parley.

Navarr.t: Irra Harah specifically asked to meet Raewynn Farkas of the Navarr during his parley with the Empire.

The Marches.t: Irra Harah's messenger came dressed in Marcher garb, and the eternal wants to discuss the Mournwold. In the heralds' account, Dourfell keep has fallen and some of its people survive among the orcs.

Urizen.t: Zakalwe asked that Vaan of the Auric Horizon, a citizen of Urizen, be invited to the discussion so that the eternal can fulfil an unspecified obligation owed to him.

Rabbits and snares.o: After the Summer Solstice, three eternals publicly answered the archmages' plenipotentiary messages. Irra Harah and the Lictors agreed to formal parleys at the Autumn Equinox, and Zakalwe offered an informal discussion.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold heads Irra Harah's parley agenda. His heralds speak of poison and curses there, and the Warmage would not promise that they would not be used again.

The Barrens.t: Irra Harah intends to discuss the state of the Barrens, then held by the Druj, at his Saturday parley with the Empire.

Rain king.d: Magical rains spread from Casinea, and every farm in a territory touched by the Hallow produced two extra drams of marrowort. Heralds offered to slowly upgrade standard farms for anyone who kept Blessing of New Spring cast through the year. They helped fight the blight in Madruga and gave arcane projections to the Sails of the First Flame, the Silver Chalice and the Marcher landskeepers. Ossegrahn proposed three commissions, each open until the end of the Autumn Equinox 385YE: the Houses of Healing, Winewater Hall and the Greenwatch. In return he hoped for amity, the shunning of Arhallogen, interdiction of venom magic, a Spring college and less killing in war.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: a herald's quote says even the Druj can hope, and a Highborn magister notes that the anti-vallorn tools would also work against them.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: an orc's quote recalls the Beoraidh arena and Mareave's Blood River, and warns against invading the Broken Shore.

Highguard.t: Ossegrahn offered the Greenwatch in Casinea, creating a Greenwatcher to be chosen unanimously by Highguard's senators from among Highborn citizens. Reikos's High Chalcis was also named as a possible site for the Houses of Healing.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Archmage cited Tamazi support for the College of Warcasting in Skarsind as a model, which horrified the heralds, and an Imperial Orc oathwright is quoted on the Blood River.

Navarr.t: Heralds spoke with Navarr and Grey Pilgrims in Hercynia, Therunin and Miaren, and offered Winewater Hall, creating a Forestmender to be chosen unanimously by Navarr's senators to fight the vallorn.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn Sails of the First Flame cast the Hallow, heralds helped against the blight in Madruga's Great Grasses, and Dhomiro Cassandra i Periera i Erigo received arcane projections from Lord Rain.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossegrahn permitted his arcane projections to be codified into Urizen lore as well as Imperial lore.

Rain king.o: After the Sails of the First Flame cast Hallow of the Green World at the Winter Solstice, the eternal Ossegrahn, guided by a plenipotentiary from Archmage of Spring Ibiss Briarheart, sent heralds across the Empire offering healing, help to farmers and several building opportunities.

Casinea/Mareholm.t: A nameless Spring regio among ancient hardwoods on the Brocéliande border was proposed as the site of the Greenwatch, which would cost 20 wains of white granite and 40 crowns.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: an Imperial Orc's quote recalls being sent to the arena at Beoraidh.

Miaren/Greenfalls.t: The Winewater Spring here, a regio whose waters cleanse venom and poison, would be the foundation of the proposed Winewater Hall.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: The Spring regio near Peakedge Stead was proposed as a site for the Houses of Healing, which would create the Imperial title of Hand of the Healers.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Greenwatch site in Mareholm lies on the border with Brocéliande, where it would watch over the vallorn.

Casinea.t: The gentle, magic-infused rains first fell over Casinea, and a Spring regio in Mareholm was proposed as the site of the Greenwatch.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: heralds of Ossegrahn visited the Navarr in Hercynia while discussing support against the vallorn.

Madruga.t: At the Archmage's request, heralds came to Madruga to help deal with the blight turning the Great Grasses to ash and sand, and they studied the Sails of the First Flame's healing magic there.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: an orc's quote explains that Mareave's Blood River is mine effluent, not blood.

Miaren.t: Chosen as the symbol of victory over the vallorn, Miaren is the proposed site of Winewater Hall, a gathering place for those fighting the vallorn without destructive magic.

Mountains of the Moon.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossegrahn praised its practice of building defences instead of armies, and a herald urged the Empire to leave the people of Tsark alone.

Reikos.t: The Gardens of High Chalcis in Reikos, near a Spring regio, were one of two proposed sites for the Houses of Healing.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Tamazi support for the College of Warcasting in Skarsind was cited as a model, which the heralds found faintly horrifying.

Therunin.t: Heralds visited the Navarr here, and the Spring regio near Peakedge Stead was one of two proposed sites for the Houses of Healing.

Raise Autumn Hammers.d: Proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by The Barrens, the motion raised a legion from the Ethengraw sept, named the Autumn Hammers in deference to their heritage. It cost 200 wains of mithril and 75 thrones and would normally take a year. Bloodcrow Rasp and Irontide Flax supplied most of the mithril and thrones across Autumn 385YE and Winter 385YE, with Kostjya adding a single crown. Once fully funded, and thanks to Hammers of Fury, the army finished raising early, in time for its first general to be elected at the Spring Equinox 386YE. Because it was raised early it initially had no army quality and could take only standard army orders.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs gained their third army, the Autumn Hammers, funded largely by Bloodcrow Rasp and Irontide Flax, with its first general to be elected at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

Raise Autumn Hammers.o: In Autumn 385YE the Senate passed a motion to raise a third Imperial Orc army, the Autumn Hammers, from the Ethengraw sept in Skarsind.

Skarsind.t: The Autumn Hammers were raised in Skarsind from the Ethengraw sept, on a motion proposed by Skarsind's own senator.

Raise Dawnish army.d: The motion proposed raising a fourth Dawnish army, to be based in Astolat. It was proposed by Semmerholm and seconded by Weirwater. The standard costs would have been 250 mithril in materials, one year to construct, and upkeep of 50 Thrones per season once complete. The Senate defeated the motion, so construction of the new army never began and Dawn's military strength remained unchanged.

Dawn.t: Dawn was denied a fourth army when the Senate defeated the motion, despite the backing of Semmerholm and Weirwater.

Raise Dawnish army.o: A Senate motion to raise a fourth Dawnish army in Astolat, proposed by the senator for Semmerholm and seconded by Weirwater, was defeated.

Astolat.t: Astolat would have been the place where the new Dawnish army was raised, but no army was begun there after the motion failed.

Raise Dawnish army II.d: The motion passed at a cost of 500 Thrones, disbursed to Senator Weirwater, and required 250 wains of mithril and a year of construction, with upkeep of 50 Thrones per season once complete. Valentin Ivarovich Severyan supplied the mithril over the following year: 60 wains after the Spring Equinox, 60 after the Summer Solstice, 65 after the Autumn Equinox, and 76 wains plus 19 Thrones after the Winter Solstice 379YE. With the materials delivered, the recorded outcome was that a new Dawnish army would muster in Semmerholm.

Dawn.t: Dawn gained Senate approval for a new army, to be added to its military strength once construction finished, at an ongoing upkeep of 50 Thrones per season.

Raise Dawnish army II.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Weirwater and seconded by Morrow, permitting the Dawnish to raise a new army mustering in Semmerholm.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm was chosen as the mustering ground for the new Dawnish army raised under this motion.

Raise Dawnish army Summer 385YE.d: The motion to disburse funds for a Dawnish army was proposed by Astolat and seconded by Kallavesa. It passed at 250 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Astolat. The Speaker for the Senate also raised an administrative motion amending it, and that amendment passed. Construction required 200 wains of mithril and 50 thrones over a year. These were supplied in instalments from Autumn 385YE to Winter 386YE. The largest donors were Vesna Borkovna Prochnost and Bohemond De Rondell, with further crowns and rings from Aliss Thorn, Agoval of house Meliora, Farren Silver Streams and others. Once complete, the Lions of Adelmar took their place as the fourth Dawnish army.

Dawn.t: Dawn gained a fourth army, the Lions of Adelmar, adding to the nation's military strength once the required mithril and money had been gathered.

Raise Dawnish army Summer 385YE.o: In Summer 385YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the Senator for Astolat, to raise a fourth Dawnish army. After a year of donated materials it was completed as the Lions of Adelmar.

Astolat.t: The army was raised in Astolat, whose Senator proposed the motion and received the 250 thrones disbursed to fund it.

Raise Fifth Marcher Army.d: The motion carried the standard cost of 200 wains of mithril and 75 thrones in labour, with twelve months needed to complete the work. After the Summer Solstice 388YE, Henry Birchsmith provided the 200 wains of mithril and 74 thrones 7 crowns, and Tom Keeper of Copperhill gave the final crown. The new army also benefited from Hammers of Fury performed by the Cabal Lyktan during that solstice. Once it is complete, the fifth general of the Marches is to be chosen by unanimous decision of the Marcher senators.

The Marches.t: The Marches gained the commission for a fifth army, paid for largely by its own Senator for Upwold. Its general is to be elected by unanimous decision of the Marcher senators once the army is raised.

Raise Fifth Marcher Army.o: In Summer 388YE the Senate passed a motion to raise a fifth Marcher army in Upwold, proposed by Henry Birchsmith, Senator for Upwold, and seconded by Mary Birchsmith, Senator for Mitwold.

Upwold.t: The fifth Marcher army is being raised in Upwold, at the proposal of the territory's own senator, Henry Birchsmith, with twelve months needed to complete it.

Raise Fourth Highborn Army.d: The motion drew on an opportunity described in the Wind of Fortune 'The war of thorns and flowers'. Its cost was cut from 200 to 80 mithril and from 600 to 240 crowns because each of Highguard's generals had received a hallowed banner as regalia. The new army's general would carry the hallowed banner Ever Forward. Work took six months. Asael gave most of the mithril and money over two seasons, with smaller donations from Naomi of Felix Watch and several other citizens. Once complete, the general of the Pilgrim's Defiance was to be chosen for the first time at the Autumn Equinox 387YE, by unanimous decision of the Highborn senators, for a shortened term of one season.

Highguard.t: Highguard gained a fourth army, the Pilgrim's Defiance, at a much lower cost because of the hallowed banners given to its generals. Its senators were to choose the new general unanimously at the Autumn Equinox 387YE.

Raise Fourth Highborn Army.o: In Spring 387YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Casinea and seconded by Bastion, to raise a fourth Highborn army in Casinea. Once completed, the new army was named the Pilgrim's Defiance.

Casinea.t: The new Highborn army was raised in Casinea, whose senator proposed the motion.

Raise Fourth Navarr Army.d: Proposed by Rowyn of the Waystone Path, Senator for Hercynia, and seconded by Thalia of Netherwatch, Senator for Redoubt, the motion passed. It carries standard costs of 200 wains of mithril and 75 thrones in labour, and takes twelve months to complete. Llofir, the Rot Lord, provided support equivalent to fifteen wains of mithril after Gwdihŵ gave the eternal seven hundred and fifty drams of marrowort. Many Navarr individuals contributed mithril and money after the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox, Rowyn among them. Once complete, the army's general will be chosen by unanimous decision of the Navarr senators. Further detail appears in The first shot wind of fortune.

Navarr.t: Navarr will gain a fourth army built to fight the vallorn, funded in part by many Navarr donors and by the eternal Llofir, with its general to be elected unanimously by the Navarr senators.

Raise Fourth Navarr Army.o: In Summer 388YE the Senate passed a motion to raise a fourth Navarr army, mustering in Oakways in Miaren, intended to fight the vallorn with the support of an eternal such as Llofir or Kaela.

Miaren/Oakways.t: Oakways is named as the mustering point for the fourth Navarr army.

Miaren.t: The new fourth Navarr army is to muster in Miaren once its construction is complete.
