Raise Fourth Varushkan Army.d: Proposed by Bronimir, Senator for Ossium, and seconded by Tristan duLac, Senator for Weirwater, the motion passed. Raising the army requires 200 wains of mithril, 75 thrones in labour costs and twelve months to complete, in addition to standard costs. After the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox of 388YE, individuals including Vesna Borkovna Prochnost, Alexandrina Ivanova Cherenkov, Dorys Delgorokov and Mayra Zoronova Prochnost contributed mithril and money, though the page records only partial progress towards the total. Once complete, the fourth general of Varushka becomes available for election by unanimous decision of the Varushkan senators.

Varushka.t: Varushka stands to gain a fourth army and a new general, chosen by unanimous decision of its senators, and many Varushkans contributed mithril and coin towards raising it.

Raise Fourth Varushkan Army.o: In Summer 388YE the Senate passed a motion to raise a fourth Varushkan army in Karsk, with Varushka seeking Senate funding for the work.

Karsk.t: Karsk is where the fourth Varushkan army is to be raised once the twelve months of work and the required mithril and labour are complete.

Raise Freeborn navy.d: The Senator for Madruga proposed the motion and Kahraman seconded it. It passed at a cost of 500 thrones, which were paid to Senator Madruga. Construction takes a year and the navy has an upkeep of 50 thrones per season. Thanks to recent victories in Segura and a judgement of the Assembly of Pride, it needed only 200 wains of weirwood instead of the standard costs. Anwar i Del Toro i Riquezza supplied that weirwood in four shipments of 50 wains, after each summit from Winter Solstice 378YE to Autumn Equinox 379YE. The finished navy creates the Imperial title of admiral.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gained a new Imperial navy, built in their own shipyards and largely supplied with weirwood by the Freeborn Anwar i Del Toro i Riquezza.

Raise Freeborn navy.o: In Winter 378YE the Senate passed a motion to build a new Imperial navy for the Brass Coast at the Atalaya shipyards in Madruga.

Madruga.t: The navy was built at the Atalaya shipyards in Madruga, and Madruga's senator proposed the motion and received the 500 thrones to fund it.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: recent victories in Segura are cited as one reason the navy needed only 200 wains of weirwood.

Raise Highborn army.d: The motion, proposed by Reikos and seconded by Necropolis, called for a fourth Highborn army to be recruited in the territory of Reikos. It passed in the Senate during Spring 382YE at a cost of 0 Thrones, with standard costs applying to the army's construction. No progress had been recorded on the page, but the stated outcome was that a fourth Highborn army would be raised, adding to Highguard's military strength.

Highguard.t: Highguard was set to gain a fourth army, expanding the nation's military forces beyond its existing three Highborn armies.

Raise Highborn army.o: In Spring 382YE the Senate passed a motion to recruit a fourth Highborn army in Reikos, proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by the senator for Necropolis.

Reikos.t: Reikos was chosen as the place where the new Highborn army would be recruited, and its senator proposed the motion.

Raise Highguard army.d: Raised by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Necropolis, the motion passed at 120 thrones with 9 votes against. The army required 150 wains of mithril and a year to construct, though the page notes it should have cost 250 wains. Adamah, Senator for Necropolis, supplied the full 150 wains of mithril over the course of 376YE. The result was to be a new Highborn army, whose general would be appointed by the Highborn senators through the standard procedure once it was complete.

Highguard.t: Highguard gained a new army of its own, with its general to be chosen by the Highborn senators once construction was complete.

Raise Highguard army.o: In Winter 376YE the Senate passed a motion to raise a new Highborn army to muster in Anvil under a Highguard general, with the funds distributed to Necropolis.

Necropolis.t: Necropolis seconded the motion and received the money for the work, and its senator Adamah supplied all 150 wains of mithril needed to build the army.

Raise Second Urizen Army.d: Proposed by Zenith and seconded by Segura, the motion raised the Argent Sword as Urizen's second army in Redoubt, following the opportunity in the A box for a sword Wind of Fortune. It cost 300 mithril and 900 crowns and took six months. After the Spring Equinox the costs were met by contributors including Able the Taller of Sarangrave Reforged, Bartimaeus, Herminius of the House of the Wanderer, Aulus Warcaster and Spyridonakes of the Lighthouse-That-Was, with single crowns from two others. Once complete, the army's general was to be chosen for the first time at the Summer Solstice 387YE by unanimous decision of the Urizen senators, serving a shortened term to the Winter Solstice 387YE.

Urizen.t: Urizen gained a second army, the Argent Sword, whose first general was to be appointed by unanimous decision of the Urizen senators at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

Raise Second Urizen Army.o: In Spring 387YE the Senate passed a motion to raise a second Urizen army, the Argent Sword, in Redoubt. The 300 mithril and 900 crowns it needed were paid by individual contributors.

Redoubt.t: The Argent Sword was raised in Redoubt, which became the home of Urizen's new second army.

Raise Third League Army.d: Passed in Winter 386YE, the motion carried the standard costs of 200 mithril and 75 thrones, with twelve months to complete. Donations arrived over the following year from many individuals, including several Holberg and Tassato names. By far the largest contributor was Vesna Borkovna Prochnost, who supplied most of the mithril and thrones in several instalments, including 105 wains of mithril and 55 thrones after the Winter Solstice 387YE. Once complete, the new army, the Sparrows Reckoning, finished mustering shortly before the Summer Solstice 388YE. It was engaged in Bregasland over the following season.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; the page notes only that the new army was engaged in Bregasland, which the Jotun held when the motion passed.

The League.t: The League gained a third army, the Sparrows Reckoning, raised in Tassato and paid for by donations from many citizens, several of them from Tassato and Holberg.

Raise Third League Army.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Tassato and seconded by the Conscience of the Senate, to raise a third League army in Tassato. Fully funded through public donations, it mustered as the Sparrows Reckoning shortly before the Summer Solstice 388YE.

Bregasland.t: The newly mustered Sparrows Reckoning was engaged in Bregasland in the season after it finished mustering before the Summer Solstice 388YE.

Tassato.t: Tassato's senator proposed the motion, and the Sparrows Reckoning was raised in the territory, with a number of Tassato citizens donating mithril and money towards it.

Raise Third Navarr Army.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Weirwater. It followed the opportunity described in The first shot wind of fortune. The army takes twelve months to raise. Rare materials could replace mithril, and the support of the Ethengraw cut the amount needed for each wain to 36 ingots or measures. Contributions came in from Spring to Winter Solstice 387YE from many individual Navarr, from the City of Gold and Lead and from the Artisans of Treji. Mandates at the Summer Solstice brought support from citizens of Dawn, the Marches, Varushka and the Imperial Orcs. Once the army is complete, its general will be elected by unanimous decision of the Navarr senators.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: citizens of Dawn supported the motion through a mandate enacted by The Fool of Glory, and provided 10 wains of mithril.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: citizens of the Imperial Orcs supported the motion through a mandate enacted by Skywise Gralka at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

Navarr.t: Navarr gains a third Imperial army, raised largely through donations from its own people, and its senators will elect that army's general by unanimous decision once it is complete.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: citizens of Varushka supported the motion through a mandate enacted by Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov, and provided 10 wains of mithril.

Raise Third Navarr Army.o: In Spring 387YE the Senate passed a motion to commission a third Imperial Navarr army, to muster in Treji in the Glen of Shadows, Hercynia, paid for by self-funding at a cost of 200 wains of mithril and 75 thrones.

Hercynia.t: The new Navarr army is to muster in Treji in the Glen of Shadows, Hercynia, and the Artisans of Treji contributed mithril towards raising it.

Raise Third Varushkan Army.d: The motion called for the third army of Varushka to be 'reborn from losses on the Eastern front'. It was proposed by Karsk, seconded by Karov, and passed. The commission carried standard costs of 200 mithril and 75 thrones and took twelve months to complete. After the Winter Solstice 386YE, Blazh Zbignev provided the 200 wains of mithril and almost all of the coin, 74 thrones 4 crowns 2 rings. Radic Splinterovich Schaslyvyy, Kostjya and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov gave the remaining small sums. With the work complete, the new army, the Boyar's Hasta, was raised in Karov.

Varushka.t: Varushka regained a third army, the Boyar's Hasta, replacing forces lost on the Eastern front. Its own senators proposed the motion and Varushkan citizens such as Blazh Zbignev paid almost all of the cost.

Raise Third Varushkan Army.o: In Winter 386YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Karsk and seconded by Karov, to raise a third Varushkan army in Karov to replace losses on the Eastern front. Once fully funded and completed, it was raised as the Boyar's Hasta.

Karov.t: Karov's senator seconded the motion, and the Boyar's Hasta was raised in the territory once the twelve-month commission was complete.

Raise Thornbound Army of Navarr.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Bastion, the motion called for a self-funded commission at non-standard cost: 200 wains of mithril, 50 wains of weirwood and 500 crowns, taking a year to complete. Contributions began after the Summer Solstice 383YE and continued through the Winter Solstice. Major donors included Corey Wayfarer, Gwendolyn Splinterspear and Rhisiart Heartsbane, with a smaller gift from Lleu Winter's Reach. The recorded donations add up to the full 200 wains of mithril and 50 wains of weirwood, alongside money. When the commission is complete, a third Navarr army with the Thornbound quality will be raised.

Navarr.t: Navarr stands to gain a third army with the Thornbound quality, largely paid for by mithril, weirwood and coin given by Navarri donors, through an opportunity presented by the nation's vates.

Raise Thornbound Army of Navarr.o: In Summer 383YE the Senate passed in principle a motion to commission a third Navarr army, mustered in Miaren with the Thornbound quality, taking up an opportunity presented by the Navarr vates.

Miaren.t: Miaren is named as the place where the new Thornbound army is to be mustered once the year-long commission is complete.

Raise Towerjacks army.d: The motion permitted the League to restore the Towerjacks, an army incorporating many siege experts, under special circumstances that differed from the standard costs of raising an Imperial army. It passed in principle and at 200 Thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Holberg. Construction required 125 mithril and six months, with upkeep of 50 Thrones per season. Ros Jordan supplied 65 wains of mithril after the Summer Solstice and 60 wains after the Autumn Equinox 379YE, providing the full 125. The army will muster in Holberg, and once it is raised it will automatically create the Imperial title of General.

The League.t: The League regains the Towerjacks, a siege-expert army of its own, along with a new Imperial General's title, at a cost of 125 mithril and ongoing upkeep of 50 Thrones a season.

Raise Towerjacks army.o: In Summer 379YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Sarvos and seconded by Holberg, to restore the Towerjacks to full fighting strength as an Imperial League army, approving 200 Thrones for the work.

Holberg.t: Holberg's senator seconded the motion and received the 200 Thrones, and the restored Towerjacks will muster in Holberg.

Raise Varushkan army.d: The motion let the Varushkans begin raising a new army in Karsk. It cost 160 wains of mithril and 40 thrones, needed a year to raise and carried an upkeep of 50 thrones per season. No progress could be made until work began to rebuild the roads of Karsk, and that work had to be finished before the army could be completed. The motion arose from an opportunity concerning Varushkan forces already in Karsk, especially the people of Branoc and Moresvah. The materials were supplied over the following year: Maximov Goraniv Strascovich provided 80 wains of mithril, and Maarit Akkova Cendro provided 80 wains and the 40 thrones by Autumn 380YE.

Varushka.t: Varushka gained the right to raise a new Imperial army, the Iron Helms, and Varushkan citizens went on to supply all of the mithril and thrones it needed.

Raise Varushkan army.o: In Autumn 379YE the Senate passed in principle a motion, proposed by Karov and seconded by Necropolis, to commission a new Imperial Varushkan army, the Iron Helms, to muster in Karsk, the Broken Barrow.

Karsk/Branoc.t: The people of Branoc were named in the opportunity behind the motion, which concerned Varushkan forces already present in Karsk.

Karsk/Moresvah.t: The inhabitants of Moresvah were named alongside Branoc in the opportunity that led to raising a Varushkan army in Karsk.

Karsk.t: Karsk, then uncontrolled, was chosen as the mustering ground for the Iron Helms, but the army depended on first rebuilding the territory's roads.

Raise Wintermark army.d: In Spring 379YE the Senate was asked to permit the Winterfolk to begin raising a new army, reformed as the Bloodcloaks, a Grimnir-laden army focused on physick. The motion would have carried all the standard costs of raising a new army. The original Bloodcloaks were a Wintermark army famed for their crimson cloaks and made up of many grimnir and mystics. They were lost to the Thule during the reign of Empress Brannan, when all but a few were slaughtered in a disastrous retreat from Otkodov. The motion was withdrawn after the Senate passed a motion to let the Dawnish raise an army instead, so no new Wintermark army was raised.

Thule.t: The Thule are named as the destroyers of the original Bloodcloaks, who were wiped out during a retreat from Otkodov in Empress Brannan's reign.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's senators for Hahnmark and Bregasland sought to restore the lost Bloodcloaks as a grimnir-heavy army. The motion was withdrawn once a Dawnish army motion passed, leaving Wintermark without its new force.

Raise Wintermark army.o: A Senate motion proposed by the senator for Hahnmark and seconded by Bregasland sought to raise a new Wintermark army, reforming the Bloodcloaks as a force rich in grimnir. It was withdrawn after a motion allowing the Dawnish to raise an army passed.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov was the scene of the disastrous retreat in which nearly all of the original Bloodcloaks were slaughtered by the Thule.

Raise Wintermark army II.d: The motion permitted the Winterfolk to begin raising a new army at a cost of 200 wains of mithril and 50 thrones, taking a year to raise and requiring upkeep of 50 thrones a season from the Senate's budget. Scrutiny required the proposing senator to name the Wintermark region where the army would be raised. Hengest Dun supplied the materials in instalments between the Winter Solstice 381YE and the Winter Solstice 382YE, completing the 200 wains of mithril and 50 thrones. The new army was to muster in Kallavesa, and on completion a new national title of general would be created.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark gained the prospect of an additional army and a new national general's title, with the mithril and thrones to build it provided over several seasons by Hengest Dun.

Raise Wintermark army II.o: In Summer 380YE the Senate passed in principle a motion, proposed by Hahnmark and seconded by Skarsind, to levy a new Wintermark army, following an earlier version of the motion that had been withdrawn.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa was named as the territory where the new Wintermark army would muster.

Raise a glass.d: Citizens across the Empire, especially in Holberg, Tassato and Temeschwar, prepared bunting, commemorative plates and food for week-long street parties. Private donations covered only minor festivities. A Senate motion could appoint someone to organise the celebrations, release Imperial funds and receive donations and Virtue fund allocations. There were three tiers: grand celebrations at 80 thrones, breath-taking at 250 and wondrous at 500. Larger celebrations would bring a greater surge in morale and Virtue, shaped by the Throne's message. Past Thrones such as Britta, James, Nicovar and Teleri had used their messages to secure lasting benefits. The Senate disbursed 40 thrones and appointed Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato to oversee the preparations.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: a grand tourney for Dawnish citizens was described as part of the possible 500-throne wondrous celebrations.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj-held Barrens appear only in a historical example, the repair of the Tower of the Dawn funded by donations after Emperor James's coronation.

The League.t: The new Empress was one of the League's own, and its cities led the preparations. Proud League citizens were urged to dig deep to celebrate her elevation, and its cities would become wonderlands if the most lavish celebrations were funded.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: magical light displays imported from Urizen, and glass bridges linking its spires, were described as features of the larger possible celebrations.

Raise a glass.o: In the summer of 380YE the Empire prepared to celebrate the coronation of a new Empress from the League, and the Senate was offered the chance to fund grand celebrations. Alongside the festivities, the Throne could issue a celebratory message to rally the citizens behind her vision. The Senate voted 40 thrones and appointed Tassato's senator to oversee the preparations.

Holberg.t: Holberg was one of the League territories abuzz with preparations for the festivities that would follow the coronation.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos, still wounded from its occupation, had weathered the storm and was eagerly looking forward to the coronation.

Tassato.t: Tassato was busy preparing for the coronation festivities. Its senator, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato, was appointed by the Senate to oversee the celebrations.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar was among the League territories most caught up in preparations for the festivities, and some citizens believed the new Empress was Temeschwari.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens were cited as the site of the Tower of the Dawn, whose repair was largely funded by donations after Emperor James's coronation.

Raise fourth Wintermark army.d: The motion was framed as fulfilling Wintermark's ambition to field a fourth army, with the proposer reminding other nations of the support he had given their own military levies. The commission required 200 wains of mithril and 50 thrones and would take a year to complete. Hengest Dun supplied most of the materials across several seasons from Winter Solstice 384YE to Winter Solstice 385YE, with smaller contributions from Lumi Warmthbringer, Farren Silver Streams, Corwyn Heartsbane and Arlen Frostmire. Once complete, a fourth Wintermark army would be raised. If the smokehouse of Atalaq had been built at least six months before mustering finished, the army would be offered qualities in line with the Suaq tradition without further opportunities.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark secured Senate approval to field a fourth army, achieving a stated national ambition, with Hengest Dun and other Wintermark citizens largely funding the mithril and money required.

Raise fourth Wintermark army.o: In Winter 384YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Hahnmark and seconded by the senator for Sermersuaq, to raise a fourth Wintermark army in Sermersuaq, citing the consecration of the Kallavesa marshes in support.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the motion cited the consecration of the Kallavesa marshes as support for raising the new army.

Sermersuaq.t: The new fourth Wintermark army was to be raised in Sermersuaq, whose senator seconded the motion, and it could gain Suaq-tradition qualities if the smokehouse of Atalaq was completed in time.

Ratify Axos Treaty Autumn 387YE.d: Proposed by the senator for Weirwater and seconded by the senator for Madruga, the motion ratified a seven-point treaty. Axos would commit its army, the Shield of Ipotavo, to aid the military conquest of the Sarangrave in line with the Military Council's strategy. The Empire accepted Axos's claim over Thornfen and ceded any claim to it, while Axos agreed not to impede Imperial forces passing through the Sarangrave, including Thornfen. Axos also committed to the safety of the Bloodwater Spears, Waterwalkers and Free People of Sarangrave, including those in Sephals, with the Empire as mediator in disputes. The Empire may hire further Axou military aid, and Axos is to be approached when the Empire moves on the Salt Flats of Sanath.

Druj.t: The Druj, who held the Sarangrave and the Salt Flats of Sanath, faced the prospect of an Axou army, the Shield of Ipotavo, joining the Imperial campaign against them.

Ratify Axos Treaty Autumn 387YE.o: The Imperial Senate passed a motion in Autumn 387YE ratifying a treaty with Axos, under which Axos committed the Shield of Ipotavo to the conquest of the Sarangrave in exchange for Imperial recognition of its claim to Thornfen.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: The Empire accepted the Axou claim to Thornfen and ceded its own, while Axos agreed to let Imperial forces pass through it and to protect the people living in Sephals.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: The treaty provides that Axos is to be approached about further cooperation when the Empire looks to make an incursion into the Druj-held Salt Flats of Sanath.

Sarangrave.t: The Druj-held Sarangrave became the target of a joint campaign, with Axos committing the Shield of Ipotavo to its conquest and promising free passage to Imperial forces and safety for the Bloodwater Spears, Waterwalkers and Free People there.

Ratify Coiled Krait Treaty.d: Under the proposed treaty the Empire would have declared the Coiled Krait foreigners with all the protections of Imperial law, and ceded a town where they could make homes and live freely, safe from their kinfolk. In return the Coiled Krait would have given the Empire militarily significant information to aid its campaign in the Sarangrave. They would not take up arms against the Druj, but would offer other help that season before leaving for their new home. They also agreed to be bound by Imperial law and to end slavery among their people once they crossed into Imperial lands. The Senate did not ratify the treaty.

Druj.t: The Coiled Krait, a sept that had broken from the Banded Snake clan, sought refuge from its own kin and offered intelligence against the Druj. The failed vote left them without Imperial protection or a promised town.

Ratify Coiled Krait Treaty.o: In Summer 387YE the Senate considered a motion, proposed by Karov and seconded by Karsk, to ratify a treaty with the Coiled Krait, a Druj sept formerly of the Banded Snake clan. The motion failed.

Sarangrave.t: The treaty would have given the Empire militarily significant information for its campaign in the Druj-held Sarangrave, but the motion failed and the treaty was never ratified.

Ratify Sungold Treaty.d: Proposed by Karsk and seconded by Temeschwar, the motion ratified a treaty under which the Empire ceded the Sungold Pass to the Thule orcs and the Senate paid 300 Thrones. In return, the Thule would return 2900 Imperial slaves and all Navarri citizens, and defend Ossium for the next season. The Thule queried two points of wording: they understood the treaty to recognise that Sungold Pass lay in Otkodov, not that it was Imperial land ceded to them, and they understood the Navarr artisans were to be released in return for that recognition rather than for payment.

Navarr.t: All Navarri citizens held by the Thule were to be freed under the treaty, though the Thule understood the Navarr artisans' release to be in exchange for recognising Sungold Pass as part of Otkodov.

Thule.t: The Thule orcs gained the Sungold Pass and 300 Thrones, agreeing in return to free 2900 Imperial slaves and all Navarri citizens and to defend Ossium for a season, while disputing how the treaty described the Pass.

Varushka.t: Varushkan-held Ossium was to be defended by the Thule for the next season, and the Varushkan senator for Karsk proposed the motion.

Ratify Sungold Treaty.o: In Summer 383YE the Senate passed a motion ratifying a treaty with the Thule, drawn up by Ambassador to Otkodov Yevgeni Katzev, ceding the Sungold Pass and paying 300 Thrones in return for the release of Imperial captives and Thule defence of Ossium.

Ossium.t: The Thule committed to defend Ossium, then held by Varushka, for the season following the treaty.

Otkodov.t: The Sungold Pass passed to the Thule, who held Otkodov and understood the treaty as recognising the Pass as part of that territory rather than as Imperial land ceded to them.

Ratify Thule Treaty Spring 387YE.d: Proposed by the senator for Miekarova and seconded by Karsk, the treaty was to take effect at the end of the Summer Solstice 387YE, when the previous peace treaty expired. The Empire would cede Mieriada to Otkodov, send food sufficient for two armies (initially from Navarr and the Marches, changeable by the Senate) and outlaw preaching the Way of Virtue to Otkodov's citizens there. In return Otkodov would provide half the Night Quarry's production as an Imperial bourse seat, pay for the food in taxes and mana crystals, and allow continued Imperial custody of the Maze of Zoria. Both sides agreed a five-year peace. Nikolai "The Butcher" Petravich sought a Synod veto, which failed.

Navarr.t: Navarr was named as one of the first two nations obliged to send food to Otkodov, in return for 3 extra thrones of taxation a season in its territories and 10 mana crystals.

Thule.t: The Thule of Otkodov were to gain Mieriada, Imperial food shipments and a ban on Virtue preaching to their citizens, while sharing the Night Quarry's output and paying for the food.

Varushka.t: Varushka was set to lose the Mieriada region of Miekarova to Otkodov, under a treaty proposed by Miekarova's own senator and seconded by Karsk.

Ratify Thule Treaty Spring 387YE.o: The Senate ratified a treaty with the Thule of Otkodov in Spring 387YE, presented by the Ambassador to Otkodov. It ceded the Mieriada region of Miekarova and committed Imperial food supplies in exchange for resources and a five-year peace.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Mieriada was to be ceded to Otkodov at the end of the Summer Solstice 387YE, with Otkodov agreeing to maintain its current treatment of Imperial citizens who chose to stay in ceded lands.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova was to lose its region of Mieriada to Otkodov when the treaty took effect at the end of the Summer Solstice 387YE.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov was to receive Mieriada and Imperial food, with Virtue preaching to its citizens outlawed, while sharing the Night Quarry's production and allowing Imperial custody of the Maze of Zoria.

Ratify Thule peace treaty.d: The ratified treaty grants five years of peace in exchange for the Empire ceding Crow's Ridge in Skarsind to the Thule. The Thule agree to free enslaved Imperial citizens and their descendants for a mutually agreed ransom. They will cast Rivers of Life on Sermersuaq if the Empire supplies the mana, will make no alliance with the Druj, and will share strategic information about them. Neither side will raid or send soldiers into the other's territory without agreement, though the Thule clarified they may still move troops in Silver Peaks, Krevsaty and Crow's Ridge. The clause on attacks is not a mutual defence pact. The Thule are treated as foreigners, and the Constitutional Court still required a copy of the text.

Druj.t: The Thule pledged to make no alliance with the Druj, said they wished to see them destroyed, and agreed to pass strategic information about them to the Empire.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs lose Crow's Ridge in Skarsind to the Thule under the treaty, though the Thule declared them welcome to visit the region.

Thule.t: The Thule of Otkodov gain Crow's Ridge and five years of peace with the Empire, in return for freeing Imperial slaves for ransom, forgoing raids and any Druj alliance, and being treated as foreigners.

Varushka.t: Varushka gains peace with the Thule, although the Thule reserve the right to keep moving soldiers through Krevsaty in Karsk.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Sermersuaq may receive the Thule's Rivers of Life ritual if the Empire provides the mana, while the Thule keep the right to send soldiers into the Silver Peaks.

Ratify Thule peace treaty.o: In Summer 382YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Holberg and seconded by Hahnmark, ratifying a five-year peace treaty with the Thule of Otkodov presented by the Ambassador to Otkodov.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: The Thule explicitly retained the freedom to send their soldiers into Krevsaty despite the treaty's ban on troops entering the other side's territory.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The Thule clarified that they may continue to send soldiers into the Silver Peaks under the treaty.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Crow's Ridge was formally ceded by the Empire to the Thule, who said Imperial Orcs would be welcome to visit it.

Karsk.t: Karsk is covered by the peace, but the Thule clarified they remain free to send soldiers into Krevsaty, the region of Karsk they hold.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov is the Thule homeland with which the treaty was made, through the Imperial Ambassador to Otkodov.

Sermersuaq.t: The Thule agreed to cast Rivers of Life on Sermersuaq in the coming season, provided the Empire offered the required mana.

Skarsind.t: The Empire ceded the Skarsind region of Crow's Ridge to the Thule as the price of the five-year peace.

Ratify treaty with Salt Lord Kaliact.d: Proposed by Reikos and seconded by Volodmartz, the treaty would have set three years of peace with Grendel residing in or operating from Spiral, with renegotiation after two years and a 50-mithril break clause. Spiral would have stayed uncontested, and no Grendel forces would have moved through it into Imperial land. Kaliact's people would have refused trade with and aid to the Druj, the north Mareave trading consortium would have offered better rates, and Kaliact would have provided a fort-construction ritual text and 10 wains of mithril. The Senate rejected it. The Constitutional Court warned that its activation clause could only work by letting the Ambassador announce treaties without a Senate vote.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the treaty would have barred Kaliact and those in Spiral from trading with the Druj or giving them material help against the Empire without Imperial leave.

Grendel.t: Salt Lord Kaliact's proposed separate peace with the Empire, which offered mithril, a ritual text and trade concessions, was rejected by the Senate.

Ratify treaty with Salt Lord Kaliact.o: In Winter 384YE the Ambassador to the Grendel presented the Senate with a treaty with Salt Lord Kaliact, covering peace with the Grendel of Spiral, and the Senate rejected it.

Mareave.t: The treaty would have had the north Mareave trading consortium offer the Empire improved rates on several resources, but this did not happen because the treaty was rejected.

Spiral.t: The rejected treaty would have kept Spiral uncontested, barred Grendel forces from attacking the Empire through it, and protected the treatment of law-abiding Imperial citizens living there.

Ratify treaty with Salt Lord Kaliact Spr.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by Redoubt, the motion was presented as a treaty by the Ambassador to the Grendel and passed. According to Civil Service records, Salt Lord Kaliact agreed to cede Spiral and every holding within it to the Empire. In return, the Empire undertook to assign Spiral to the League and to allow those currently living there, orc and human alike, to become citizens. The ratification marked a negotiated, rather than military, return of Spiral to Imperial hands.

Grendel.t: Salt Lord Kaliact, dealing through the Imperial Ambassador to the Grendel, gave up Grendel control of Spiral and all its holdings in exchange for Imperial promises, including citizenship for the orcs living there.

Ratify treaty with Salt Lord Kaliact Spr.o: The Senate ratified a treaty agreed at the Spring Equinox 385YE under which Salt Lord Kaliact ceded the territory of Spiral and all its holdings to the Empire.

Spiral.t: Spiral and all its holdings passed from Salt Lord Kaliact to the Empire, to be assigned to the League, and its current inhabitants, orc and human alike, were to be allowed to become citizens.

Ratify treaty with Thule Winter 383YE.d: Proposed by Upwold and seconded by Madruga, the motion ratified the treaty presented by the Ambassador to Otkodov. It passed. Under its terms the Otkodov Thule would provide three armies for a full year against the Jotun in Sermersuaq, cede back any territory they captured there, return captured Imperial citizens, offer non-citizen Jotun thralldom or death, and spare Imperial settlements. The Empire agreed to let the Thule use protective rituals such as Rivers of Life and not to use powerful rituals of slaughter in Sermersuaq. The Thule noted a missing agreed clause, that Imperial armies would always outnumber theirs in Sermersuaq. Rak said they would still abide by the treaty, but any imbalance would be for the ambassadors to negotiate.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard held Casinea, whose name appears in a garbled form in the treaty's title ('the Casinea Empire').

Jotun.t: The Jotun became the target of a new Imperial–Thule military alliance in Sermersuaq, and any non-citizen Jotun captured by the Thule would face the choice of thralldom or death.

Thule.t: The Otkodov Thule gained Webwood and Miechernya in exchange for committing three armies against the Jotun for a year, and they won the right to send representatives to Anvil to coordinate military matters.

Varushka.t: Varushka lost two regions to the Thule, Miechernya in Miekarova and Webwood in Ossium. The treaty required their people to be peacefully moved to other Imperial regions.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's war against the Jotun in Sermersuaq gained three Thule allied armies. The treaty promised the return of captured Imperial citizens and that Imperial settlements would not be targeted, but the Empire gave up powerful slaughter rituals there.

Ratify treaty with Thule Winter 383YE.o: The Senate ratified a treaty with the Thule of Otkodov, ceding the regions of Webwood in Ossium and Miechernya in Miekarova in exchange for three Thule armies to fight alongside the Empire against the Jotun in Sermersuaq for a year.

Miekarova/Miechernya.t: Miechernya was ceded to the Thule, and its people were to be helped to move to another Imperial region.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Webwood was ceded to the Thule, and its people were to be helped to move to another Imperial region.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the name Casinea appears only in the treaty's heading, 'Treaty between Otkodov and the Casinea Empire'.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova lost its region of Miechernya, which was ceded to the Thule under the treaty.

Ossium.t: Ossium lost its region of Webwood, which was ceded to the Thule under the treaty.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov's Thule agreed the treaty with the Empire, committing three armies and gaining two neighbouring Varushkan regions.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq became the theatre of the new alliance. Thule armies would fight the Jotun there and cede any captured territory to the Empire, and the Empire agreed to allow Thule protective rituals but to use no powerful rituals of slaughter there.

Ratify treaty with the Axos Autumn 383YE.d: The treaty, presented as such after discussion with the Constitutional Court, contained five points. The Empire would provide maps of the Mountains of the Moon and let Axos use the Sarangrave spy network. Axou military captains would be invited to defend the Eastern Brokerage in Therunin. Students from the College in Maykop could apply to Imperial centres of learning, and the Axou ambassador could buy land at the Quayside in Issyk. The Military Council approved the military aspects. The treaty could not extend Therunin's offer of payment to the Axou, because those rewards come from private citizens and the Senate cannot direct how citizens spend their wealth. The claim that points could be combined to save Senate time was also ruled invalid.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the treaty grants Axos use of the Sarangrave spy network, which operates in Druj-held land.

Navarr.t: Navarr's Therunin proposed the treaty, which invited Axou captains to help defend the Eastern Brokerage. Whether to pay those Axou soldiers is left to the Navarr citizens of Therunin.

Ratify treaty with the Axos Autumn 383YE.o: In Autumn 383YE the Senate passed a treaty with Axos, proposed by the senator for Therunin, committing the Empire to share maps, intelligence, defence arrangements, academic exchange and land rights with the Axou.

Mountains of the Moon.t: The Empire agreed to give Axos maps of the Mountains of the Moon, which were held by the Tsark at the time.

Sarangrave.t: Axos was permitted to use the Imperial spy network in the Sarangrave, which was held by the Druj that season.

Therunin.t: Axou military captains were invited to defend the Eastern Brokerage in Therunin. The treaty could not extend the territory's privately funded rewards to them, so that choice rests with its Navarr citizens.

Ratify treaty with the Grendel Autumn 38.d: Proposed by Madruga and seconded by the Conscience of the Senate, the treaty passed. It established peace for two years, to be renegotiated at the Spring Equinox 385YE. The Grendel agreed not to trade with or materially assist the Druj, and to release one Imperial slave for each day the treaty holds. The Empire ceded Afarjasse and Morajasse in Feroz and Ankra, Cinion and Ateri in Spiral, and agreed to build no shipyards or navies in the Bay of Catazar. Citizens in the ceded regions had two seasons to relocate with their possessions. Both sides renounced raiding, and disputes go first to ambassadors. The Grendel became foreigners, and raiding Grendel vessels or attacking the Broken Shore became illegal.

Druj.t: The Grendel agreed not to trade with the Druj or give them any material assistance in their war against the Empire, cutting off a potential source of support.

Grendel.t: The Grendel gained five Imperial regions and two years of peace, in return for releasing Imperial slaves, refusing aid to the Druj and giving up raids. Under Imperial law they are now foreigners rather than enemies.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast lost Afarjasse and Morajasse in Feroz to the Grendel, and its citizens there had two seasons to relocate. Its captains may no longer raid Grendel ships or attack the Broken Shore.

Urizen.t: Urizen lost Ankra, Cinion and Ateri in Spiral to the Grendel, and its citizens there were given two seasons' grace to move into Imperial territory with their possessions.

Ratify treaty with the Grendel Autumn 38.o: In Autumn 383YE the Senate ratified a peace treaty with the Grendel, presented by the Imperial Fleet Master, ceding five regions in Feroz and Spiral in exchange for two years of peace, the release of Imperial slaves and a Grendel pledge not to aid the Druj.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: Afarjasse was ceded to the Grendel. Imperial citizens living there had two seasons to leave with their possessions.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: Morajasse was ceded to the Grendel, and its Imperial residents were given two seasons to relocate to Imperial territory.

Spiral/Ankra.t: Ankra was handed to the Grendel under the treaty, with two seasons' grace for Imperial citizens to depart.

Spiral/Ateri.t: Ateri was ceded to the Grendel. Its Imperial citizens were allowed two seasons to relocate with their belongings.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Cinion was ceded to the Grendel, and Imperial citizens there had two seasons to move into Imperial lands.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Empire agreed to build no shipyards or navies in the Bay of Catazar while the treaty lasts, and raiding between the Empire and the Grendel is forbidden.

Feroz.t: Two of Feroz's regions, Afarjasse and Morajasse, were ceded to the Grendel, leaving the territory partly in orc hands.

Spiral.t: Ankra, Cinion and Ateri in Spiral were ceded to the Grendel, formalising their control of much of the territory.

Ratify treaty with the Iron Confederacy.d: Proposed by Semmerholm and seconded by Segura, the motion passed in Winter 382YE. The treaty committed the Empire to provide copies of maps of the Bay of Catazar showing all Iron Confederacy and Grendel lands, at a cost of 10 Thrones from the Imperial treasury. The Imperatrix donated 10 Thrones to cover this. The treaty also changed Imperial law: all sale or gifting of liao to the Iron Confederacy, whether through ports or across the Suranni-Imperial border, was banned, making such trades by Imperial citizens illegal.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the maps handed to the Iron Confederacy show all Grendel lands in the Bay of Catazar.

Ratify treaty with the Iron Confederacy.o: The Senate ratified a treaty with the Iron Confederacy, prepared by Ambassador Lord Colwynn de Rondell, under which the Empire provided maps of the Bay of Catazar and banned the sale or gifting of liao to the Confederacy.

Bay of Catazar.t: Under the treaty, the Empire gave the Iron Confederacy copies of its maps of the Bay of Catazar, showing all Iron Confederacy and Grendel lands there.

Ratify treaty with the Sarcophan Delves.d: The treaty, proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by the senator for Segura, ceded the Alivetti estate in Sarvos to the Sarcophan Delves, to be granted to the Bedelaar Huisbaas Vandersaar for their use. In return, the Huisbaas agreed to preserve the tomb ruins of Empress Giselle as a historic landmark and to pay 4 rings of ilium each season to the Imperial holder of the Steel Fist bourse seat for as long as the land remained conceded. The Huisbaas also undertook to provide land within the Buitenlandsewijk, in keeping with the Constitution, for Imperial construction. The Empire agreed to build a Temple of the Way there at a time of its choosing.

The League.t: A League territory lost the Alivetti estate to a foreign enclave. The tomb of Empress Giselle there was protected as a historic landmark, and the Empire gained land within the Buitenlandsewijk for a Temple of the Way.

Ratify treaty with the Sarcophan Delves.o: The Senate passed a treaty with the Sarcophan Delves, presented by the Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves, conceding the Alivetti estate in Sarvos to the Delves as an enclave for the Bedelaar Huisbaas Vandersaar.

Sarvos.t: The Alivetti estate in Sarvos was conceded to the Sarcophan Delves for the Bedelaar Huisbaas Vandersaar, who undertook to preserve Empress Giselle's tomb ruins as a historic landmark and to pay the Empire 4 rings of ilium each season.

Reap what you sow.d: Troubled by their Prosperity and by word from Anvil that Wintermark had sold them out, the people of Skarsind did not resent the Imperial Orcs. They still believed they deserved the fruits of their labour before handing over the land. Miners over-exploited the mines, leaving unsafe tunnels that would need a serious clean-up, possibly a Senate commission with weirwood-and-mithril supports. Foresters, herb gardeners and mana producers considered following suit. The Wintermark assembly passed two judgements and the Assembly of Loyalty one, all calling the practice unvirtuous. Over-production declined, but the remaining hard-liners' morale fell further. Meanwhile the curse on the Kallavesa marshes persisted unchanged.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on the page and is linked only through its holding of Casinea.

Imperial Orcs.t: Skarsind was expected to become the Imperial Orcs' homeland. The Winterfolk there held no grudge and credited the orcs with helping liberate it, but they rushed to strip its wealth before handing it over.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winterfolk of Skarsind are described as having struggled under Thule tyranny before liberation.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: recent events in Urizen are cited as one reason crystal mana was in demand.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's people in Skarsind felt betrayed by the rest of the nation. Its National Assembly passed two judgements condemning the strip-mining as unvirtuous, which reduced it but further lowered the hard-liners' morale.

Reap what you sow.o: In Autumn 379YE the miners of Skarsind, believing their lands were soon to be handed to the Imperial Orcs, began strip-mining to take what they felt they were owed before leaving. Wintermark's National Assembly and the Assembly of Loyalty condemned the practice as unvirtuous, curbing it at a cost to local morale.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: Mystics reported eerie dancing lights over the Kallavesa Marsh and muttered grimly about what they might portend, as the curse on its mana continued.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page and is only associated with it on the map.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the auras spread to commemorate the Miracle at Hahnmark are noted as having faded.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa's marshes remained under a potent curse, with the draining of mana flows neither worsening nor improving.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind's miners over-exploited the mines, leaving unsafe tunnels, and other producers there considered over-harvesting too. Condemnation by the assemblies slowed the practice but deepened the gloom of those who persisted.

Rebellion's Ridge.d: The six Ore Hills rebels, recognised as exemplars of Pride in Winter 386YE, are honoured by Rebellion's Ridge. It was built by Alfred Aewulfson-Boon under an Imperial Wayleave, and Jedediah Boon's writ of consecration was upheld 296-10. If the General Assembly enacts the consecration mandate, every personal resource in the Mournwold suffers a two-rank penalty for a season, and from the Spring Equinox the Mournwold senator would be chosen by mine owners rather than farmers. If it is not enacted, Marcher priests in the Mournwold could preach rebellion to stoke the miners' anger. The egregores confirmed there is no compromise and that no other Marcher territory would be affected.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the writ describes the Mournwold as a territory stricken by the Jotun bootheel time and time again.

The Marches.t: Marcher priests and the General Assembly faced a generational choice over whether Mournwold miners or farmers choose their senator. The egregores warned of possible strife between cousins, and either outcome risked shunning, rough music or worse within the nation.

Rebellion's Ridge.o: With Rebellion's Ridge completed in honour of the leaders of the Ore Hills Rebellion, the Pride Assembly upheld a writ of consecration, leaving the General Assembly to decide at the Autumn Equinox 388YE whether to consecrate it with true liao. Either choice would inflame the centuries-old feud between the miners and farmers of the Mournwold.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: The region gives its name to the Ore Hills Rebellion, whose six leaders Rebellion's Ridge commemorates. Their legacy was now at the heart of the struggle between the Mournwold's miners and farmers.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland is cited as a place where land, as in the Marches generally, means farmland.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is cited as farmland country. The page says the Mournwold decision would not change how it is governed.

Mournwold.t: If the consecration were enacted, personal resources here would suffer a two-rank penalty for a season and mine owners would elect the senator from the Spring Equinox. If it were refused, priests could preach rebellion to the miners.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is cited as farmland country. The page says the Mournwold decision would not change how it is governed.

Rebels and loyalists.d: The Pride Assembly upheld recognition of Esme Hooper, Mary Digger, Ezekial Boon, Henry Killinghall, Maggie John and Tom John, together, as ringleaders of the Ore Hills Rebellion; the General Assembly must now decide. Passing it may look like the Synod siding with the miners, and rejecting it like siding with the farmers, though either is manageable. A true liao memorial, sought by Jedediah Boon and his allies, would reopen the question of who appoints Marcher senators. Separately, the Marcher Assembly revoked Hal Talbot 108-16. The Loyalty Assembly must act at the Winter Solstice: denouncing the revocation risks conflict between assemblies, while failing to do so loses the Eyes of Loyalty.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: any rebel memorial is presumed to be built in Ore Hills once the Jotun there are dealt with.

The Marches.t: Marchers face renewed tension between miners and yeofolk over the rebels' recognition, and a possible split as some Loyal dedicates question their own national assembly's revocation of Hal Talbot.

Rebels and loyalists.o: After the Autumn Equinox 386YE, two Synod developments unsettled the Marches: the Pride Assembly's recognition of the six leaders of the Ore Hills Rebellion as exemplars, and the Marcher Assembly's revocation of Hal Talbot as Senator for Mitwold for apparent disloyalty to the nation.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: The region that gave the rebellion its name is the presumed site of a proposed true liao memorial to its leaders, should recognition and a writ of consecration both pass once the Jotun are dealt with.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold's senator Hal Talbot was revoked by the Marcher Assembly for showing loyalty to his house over his nation, a judgement the Loyalty Assembly may denounce at the Winter Solstice.

Mournwold.t: The old rift between the miners of the central and southern Mourn and the northern yeofolk is stirred again, and a consecrated memorial to the rebels would strengthen independent spirit and revive disputes over who appoints the Mournwold senator.

Rebirth in Reikos.d: After more than a decade of deliberate Druj ruin, Reikos was transformed after the Spring Equinox: fungi and moulds sprang up everywhere, poisoned waters ran clean, and ruins were overgrown. Yael and Jared, backed by Synod judgements and a large bounty of liao, countered the heretic Golan's message of Courage as the prime virtue. Many of Golan's followers returned to their congregations, while others joined the new Congregation of the First Empress. Some called the change a miracle of a living paragon; others blamed fell Realm creatures, noting memorials drowned beneath the growth. The Synod could boost, spread or counter the movement. In the event, it supported Jared, Cardinal of Loyalty, in spreading Yael's teachings across the entire Empire.

Druj.t: The lingering legacy of the Druj occupation, including the poisoned wells and fouled streams they left behind, was being washed away by the new growth sweeping Reikos.

Highguard.t: The Highborn people of Reikos, broken by Druj oppression, turned from Golan's heresy to Yael's message, with many rejoining their old congregations and others swelling the fervent Congregation of the First Empress, a movement the Synod then chose to spread across the Empire.

Rebirth in Reikos.o: In Summer 380YE, as a wave of fungal new life swept Reikos, the Synod-authorised priests Yael and Jared of the Suns of Couros preached that Yael was the First Empress reborn, drawing Golan's followers away and forming the Congregation of the First Empress.

Reikos.t: Reikos was physically and spiritually reborn as fungi and greenery overran the ruins and cleansed poisoned waters, while Yael and Jared's preaching birthed the Congregation of the First Empress there, though some memorials and graves were drowned beneath the growth.

Rebuild Aleksandra's Watch.d: Proposed by the senator for Karsk and seconded by the senator for Reikos, the motion called for construction work at Aleksandra's Watch, a fortress in Karsk. It passed the Senate at the Winter Solstice 381YE with a cost of 20 Thrones. After the summit, Magnus Anatolyvich Prochnost provided the full 20 Thrones, and the reconstruction work was set to be undertaken.

Varushka.t: Varushka saw a fortress in one of its territories restored, with the motion brought by its Karsk senator and funded by Magnus Anatolyvich Prochnost.

Rebuild Aleksandra's Watch.o: In Winter 381YE the Senate passed a motion to undertake reconstruction work on Aleksandra's Watch, a fortress in Karsk, at a cost of 20 Thrones.

Karsk.t: Aleksandra's Watch, a fortress in Karsk, was to undergo reconstruction work once the 20 Thrones had been provided.

Rebuild Binding Oak Spire.d: Velasco i Guerra, Senator for Kahraman, proposed the motion and Bartimaeus, Senator for Sarangrave, seconded it. It followed the Architect of Hammers' announcement the previous season, and Architect Noether drew up the spire's design. The cost was set by the opportunity, with 70 thrones in labour and three months to complete. Able the Taller of Sarangrave Reforged paid the 70 thrones after the Autumn Equinox, so the project was self-funded. Once complete, the Arch of the Sky produces an additional two wains of white granite, and its custodian can purchase further wains. In return, the investment that businesses in Zenith received from the Bridge of the Air was removed and redirected to support the quarry workers.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, and the only link is that the Senator for Sarangrave, a territory they held, seconded the motion.

Urizen.t: Urizen gains a rebuilt spire in Zenith that boosts white granite production at the Arch of the Sky. The cost is that Zenith's businesses lose their investment from the Bridge of the Air.

Rebuild Binding Oak Spire.o: In Autumn 388YE the Senate passed a commission to rebuild the Binding Oak Spire, an edifice in Proceris, Zenith. The spire increases the output of the Arch of the Sky quarry and lets its custodian buy more white granite.

Zenith/Proceris.t: The Binding Oak Spire is rebuilt in Proceris to Architect Noether's design, taking three months to complete.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Bartimaeus, Senator for Sarangrave, seconded the motion, and Able the Taller of Sarangrave Reforged funded the labour costs.

Zenith.t: Zenith's Arch of the Sky quarry produces two extra wains of white granite and can buy more, but businesses in the territory lose their Bridge of the Air investment, which is redirected to the quarry workers.

Rebuild Drycastle.d: Proposed by the Senator for the Barrens and seconded by Kallavesa, the motion commissioned repairs to Drycastle following the 'A glorious victory' Wind of Fortune. It cost 20 wains of white granite, 20 wains of weirwood and 120 crowns, and 50 thrones were disbursed to the Senator for the Barrens. Many citizens donated materials and money between Summer 386YE and Spring 387YE, and the work was completed. The Knight of Dawnguard, chosen by unanimous decision of the Dawnish senators, guards the region and its settlements. The Reeve of Drycastle, held by a yeofolk and chosen by Tally of the Votes of Dawnish military captains, oversees the town's prosperity. Both titles became available from Summer Solstice 387YE.

Dawn.t: Dawn gained a rebuilt Drycastle and two new Dawnish titles: the Knight of Dawnguard, chosen unanimously by Dawn's senators, and the Reeve of Drycastle, a yeofolk chosen by Tally of the Votes from Summer 387YE.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the motion describes liberated citizens living in the ashes and rubble left by the Druj.

Rebuild Drycastle.o: In Summer 386YE the Senate passed a motion to rebuild the town of Drycastle in Dawnguard, the Barrens, after its liberation from the Druj. The motion also created the titles of Knight of Dawnguard and Reeve of Drycastle.

The Barrens.t: The town of Drycastle in Dawnguard was rebuilt from the ruins left by the Druj, and the Barrens now has a Knight charged with securing Dawnguard and a Reeve overseeing Drycastle's prosperity.

Rebuild First Voice Glade.d: Announced in Autumn 387YE, the commission would rebuild the corpse glade and school of the great bard Gerallt Brackensong. The site had already been consecrated with true liao after a Synod writ of consecration and mandate. The work cost 30 wains of weirwood and 90 crowns in labour, took three months, and was self-funded by a union of bards from across the Empire. It was meant to inspire pilgrims to learn Navarr song and storytelling and to develop their own nations' musical and literary cultures. After the Autumn Equinox, members of the Splitroot and others supplied the full 30 wains of weirwood, plus money including 11 thrones from Nemae Splitroot. No outcome is recorded.

Navarr.t: The project honours the Navarr bard Gerallt Brackensong and promotes Navarr traditions of song and storytelling, and it was announced and largely supplied by Navarr of the Splitroot.

Rebuild First Voice Glade.o: Nemae Splitroot, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced a great work to rebuild the ruined First Voice Glade and School in Oakways, Miaren, as an inspirational site honouring Gerallt Brackensong, exemplar of Pride.

Miaren/Oakways.t: The ruined First Voice Glade and School in Oakways, already consecrated with true liao, was the site chosen for rebuilding as a place of pilgrimage.

Miaren.t: Miaren was to gain a rebuilt glade and school dedicated to Gerallt Brackensong, intended to draw pilgrims seeking inspiration in the performing arts.

Rebuild Great Library of Ankarien.d: Proposed by the senator for Redoubt and seconded by Miaren's senator, the motion commissioned an edifice costing thirty wains of white granite and 90 crowns in labour, taking three months to complete. Funding came from several citizens after the Winter Solstice 387YE, led by Fausta Ankarien with 9 thrones 4 crowns, alongside smaller donations from Eleri Bronwen's Rest, Bakar i Riqueza and others. The thirty wains of white granite were finally supplied by Spyridonakes of the Lighthouse-That-Was after the Autumn Equinox 388YE. Once complete, the ruins of Ankarien are to be restored to their former glory.

The League.t: The League sees a long-held promise kept, as the Great Library of Ankarien is rebuilt in its Spiral homeland, with Fausta Ankarien foremost among its funders.

Rebuild Great Library of Ankarien.o: The Senate passed a motion in Winter 387YE to rebuild the Great Library of Ankarien on its original site in Ankra, Spiral, fulfilling an ambition two centuries old.

Spiral/Ankra.t: Ankra is the site of the rebuilt Great Library, which on completion will restore the ruins of Ankarien to their former glory.

Spiral.t: Spiral, held by the League, is to gain the restored Great Library of Ankarien, rebuilt on its original site.

Rebuild Roads of Kahraman.d: Proposed by the senator for Kahraman and seconded by Volodmartz, the commission passed at 200 thrones. It aimed to improve troop movement and defence, and promised reimbursement to Faraden families for their materials if trade ties were ever cut. The work needed 130 wains of white granite, 50 of weirwood and 45 thrones in labour over nine months, and could not progress while the Lasambrian Jotun had free access to Kahraman. Delara of the House of the Wanderer supplied most of the materials, with further contributions from the Bataguin Family and Vesna Borkovna Prochnost. Jotun disruption after the Autumn Equinox delayed completion, and raiders seized 10 wains of white granite, which had to be replaced.

Jotun.t: Lasambrian Jotun raiders delayed the project after the Autumn Equinox and seized 10 wains of white granite, and their free access to Kahraman was a condition that could halt the work entirely.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gained repaired roads and a network of Kamkrag across one of their territories, improving defence and giving their citizens better access to abundant mines. The Bataguin Family helped pay for the work.

Rebuild Roads of Kahraman.o: In Spring 385YE the Senate passed a motion to rebuild the roads of Kahraman and build a series of Kamkrag across the territory, following the Time and time again wind of fortune. Despite delays and theft by Lasambrian Jotun raiders, the project was eventually completed.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman's roads were rebuilt and Kamkrag were raised throughout the territory, despite Jotun raids that delayed the work and stole building materials.

Rebuild the Colossus of Sarvos.d: The motion called for the repair of damage inflicted on the Colossus of Sarvos. The work was costed at 8 wains of white granite and 16 crowns, with three months needed to complete it. Shauni di Vergo, bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the project and provided the full 8 wains of white granite and 16 crowns after the Winter Solstice 381YE. With the materials and money supplied, reconstruction work on the Colossus was to be undertaken.

The League.t: A Leaguer landmark in one of the nation's cities was set to be restored, with Shauni di Vergo supplying the granite and crowns for the work.

Rebuild the Colossus of Sarvos.o: In Winter 381YE a Senate motion to repair the damaged Colossus of Sarvos passed, announced by Shauni di Vergo as bearer of an Imperial Wayleave.

Sarvos.t: Reconstruction of the damaged Colossus was to begin in Sarvos, with the work expected to take three months once funded.

Rebuild the Storm Vault.d: Tiberius Echostorm, Crystal Architect of the Spires, announced the rebuilding of the Storm Vault, a mana sinecure in Proceris that had been sacked by the Druj. The work cost 8 wains of mithril and 10 thrones and took three months; the materials and money were provided by Xanthius Storm's End after the Summer Solstice 386YE. Once complete, the Custodian of the Storm Vault again received 10 mana crystals each season and could fund the gathering of precious tempest jade through a ministry.

Druj.t: The Druj had sacked the Storm Vault and left it infested, and this rebuilding undid that damage.

Urizen.t: Urizeni leaders announced and paid for the rebuilding, which restored a valuable mana sinecure and a tempest jade ministry to the nation.

Rebuild the Storm Vault.o: In Summer 386YE the Storm Vault in Proceris, Zenith, a mana sinecure the Druj had sacked and turned into an infested vault, was rebuilt following the Write your own ending wind of fortune.

Zenith/Proceris.t: The Storm Vault in Proceris was repaired over three months, and its custodian again received 10 mana crystals each season and could fund the gathering of tempest jade.

Zenith.t: The Storm Vault in Zenith was rebuilt from its sacked, infested state and once again produced mana crystals for its custodian.

Rebuild the Towers of Anduz.d: Proposed by the senator for Segura and seconded by Miaren in Winter 378YE, the motion sought permission to rebuild the Towers of Anduz to boost trade with the Faraden and the prosperity of the Empire. It passed in principle without requesting funds. The work required 50 wains of white granite and three months to construct, with no upkeep. The granite was provided by Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra after the Spring Equinox 379YE. Once completed, the towers protect merchant caravans travelling through the Lasambrian Hills, and businesses in Segura operated by Freeborn citizens gain a share of additional money from improved trade with the Faraden and the Iron Confederacy.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn-run businesses in Segura stand to gain extra money from the improved trade with the Faraden and the Iron Confederacy, and a Freeborn citizen, Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra, supplied the white granite for the work.

Rebuild the Towers of Anduz.o: The Senate gave permission in principle to restore the Towers of Anduz in Segura, a great work intended to promote trade and good relations with the Faraden; no funding was requested from the Imperial treasury.

Segura.t: The Towers of Anduz were restored in Segura as a great work, guarding merchant caravans crossing the Lasambrian Hills after Segura's own senator proposed the motion.

Rebuild the roads of Karsk.d: Proposed by the senator for Karsk and seconded by Holberg, the self-funded motion commissioned the Rebuilding of the Roads of Karsk at a cost of 80 wains of white granite and 20 thrones in labour, taking six months to construct. Radomir of Varushka supplied 40 wains of white granite and the 20 thrones after the Autumn Equinox 379YE, and the remaining 40 wains after the Winter Solstice 379YE. Once completed, the work will increase production for all mines and forests in Karsk, and restoring the roads to their former state will allow Varushka to support a third army.

Varushka.t: Varushka gains the prospect of supporting a third army once Karsk's roads are restored, with Radomir of Varushka supplying all the granite and thrones needed to build them.

Rebuild the roads of Karsk.o: In Autumn 379YE the Senate passed a motion to commission a great work rebuilding the devastated road network of Karsk, intended to boost the territory's mines and forests and allow Varushka to support a third army.

Karsk.t: Karsk's devastated road network is to be rebuilt, and once completed the work will increase production for all mines and forests in the territory.

Received with a strange delight.d: Alexander of Axos sought private meetings, while the Bastion herbalist Nain of Gamul's Gate urged the Synod, healers and Conclave to scrutinise untested foreign drugs such as the Unwound Coil. Around fifteen Axou claiming Terunael descent travelled the trods and planned to show a relic lekythos to the Navarr vates. Two Free Mark fighters, with the Stormcrow Aedwin the Weaver, sought guidance on their skeins. The Urizeni refugees Eucleus and Valerius pursued the Hand of Guerra, and Valerius planned to sell an heirloom. Maistir Comyn and Lir rushed to Anvil over a danger linked to the evacuation of Feroz. Ezra Von Sarvos of the Silver Frame Carta intended to call on the High Bard.

Grendel.t: The Grendel trader Maistir Comyn and his bodyguard Lir hurried to Anvil on an emergency apparently connected with the evacuation of Feroz, claiming someone was in terrible danger and that a Cardinal would hear of any delay.

Highguard.t: The Highborn coast and roads saw the Grendel ship's hurried arrival at Crown's Quay and its crew's dash through Necropolis toward Casinea, while the Bastion herbalist Nain of Gamul's Gate led calls to scrutinise foreign narcotics and medicines.

Jotun.t: As the Empire reclaimed dominion over Sermersuaq from Jotun occupation, the Free Mark fighters who had waged a brutal sabotage campaign against the Jotun began returning home.

Navarr.t: Axou travellers claiming Terunael descent visited wayhouses across the southern trods seeking out the Navarr, some adopting Navarr dress, and planned to bring their relic to the Navarr woods entrance at Anvil to show the vates and the citizens who had helped them.

The Brass Coast.t: The House of Guerra in Calvos took in a party of Urizeni refugees, two of whom set off after the Hand of Guerra and could be found in the Brass Coast encampment, while the Grendel visitors headed for the Freeborn camp.

The League.t: Ezra Von Sarvos, the ageing Merchant Prince of the Silver Frame Carta, a Sarvosan guild of art dealers, made a rare journey out of Sarvos to call on the new High Bard.

Urizen.t: A spire-in-exile of Urizeni refugees reached the House of Guerra, with the philosopher Eucleus chasing the Hand of Guerra and Valerius seeking to sell a family heirloom to fund a new life far from Urizen, while the High Bard was to receive Ezra Von Sarvos in the Urizen camp.

Wintermark.t: Former Free Mark resistance fighters, dogged by rumours of dark pacts and Frayed skeins, returned to their homes, and two of them came to Anvil with the Stormcrow Aedwin the Weaver to seek guidance on their skeins.

Received with a strange delight.o: At the Summer Solstice 384YE, several groups of visitors made their way to Anvil, including an Axou narcotics trader, Axou travellers claiming Terunael descent, former Free Mark fighters from Sermersuaq, Urizeni refugees, a pair of Grendel traders on an urgent errand and a Sarvosan art guild's merchant prince.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: The House of Guerra's hostel in Calvos sheltered a group of tired Urizeni refugees, whose philosopher Eucleus left almost at once in pursuit of the absent Hand of Guerra.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the herbalist Nain of Gamul's Gate claimed to make the best Feverfail Elixir in Bastion.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: the Axou travellers of Terunael descent unsurprisingly avoided visiting Brocéliande.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Maistir Comyn and Lir hurried through Necropolis toward Casinea on their way to Anvil.

Feroz.t: The Grendel traders' urgent errand was said to concern the evacuation of Feroz, prompting speculation about the fate of the few human citizens left there.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the Axou travellers seeking the Navarr had so far avoided visiting Hercynia.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: the Axou travellers unsurprisingly avoided visiting Liathaven.

Madruga.t: A bedraggled party of Urizeni refugees arrived at the House of Guerra in Calvos seeking sanctuary.

Necropolis.t: A Grendel ship docked in a rush at Crown's Quay without tariff paperwork, its captain's attempts to pay off questioners annoying the civil servants until a young crew member filled out the forms and faced the local magistrate.

Sarvos.t: The Silver Frame Carta, an old Sarvosan art-dealing guild with a shady reputation but generous patronage, saw its rarely travelling Merchant Prince leave the city for Anvil.

Sermersuaq.t: With the Empire reclaiming Sermersuaq, former thralls were freed and surviving Free Mark fighters began rebuilding homes scarred by occupation amid suspicion and gossip from their neighbours.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Axou travellers seeking the Navarr had so far avoided visiting Therunin.

Reclaimers.d: Three decades of Druj occupation, the war to expel them and a year of rampaging trees left Holberg in ruins, cutting its taxation. For Holmauer, Piet Van Holberg proposed a clearance and triumphal arch drawing pilgrims, while Katarzyna Von Carstein proposed a park and civic rebuilding that would enrich local businesses. Doing nothing would leave the ruins permanent. Brechtje Van Holberg proposed fearsome new walls for Holmauer, and Menno Van Ritsjhof proposed vastly enlarging Holfried's fortifications to make them the Empire's biggest. A now-unavailable option offered either restoring the dykes of Rebeshof and Ennerlund or letting the Morass reclaim them for herbs. Unnatural briars in Misericorde and Utterlund could impede large armies.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: in the fiction, an investigator notes that the Towerjacks are now in Dawn.

Druj.t: The Druj had been driven from Holberg, but their occupation and destruction of its walls, dykes and suburbs drove these proposals, and Holbergers expected them to return one day.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed triumphal arch in Holmauer was said to rival some of the most impressive architecture in Highguard.

The League.t: League citizens in Holberg were offered competing great works to clear ruins, restore taxation, rebuild the city's famed fortifications and shape the territory's herb production, with the city's pride and prosperity at stake.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: in the fiction, Jonas Quayle still carries an Upwold accent after years in Holberg.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: letting the Morass spread was said to create marshes that could rival Kallavesa's for healing herbs.

Reclaimers.o: With the Druj driven from Holberg and the animate trees subsided, Holberg faced widespread devastation in Spring 380YE, and its citizens put forward rival proposals to clear the ruins of Holmauer, rebuild and expand the territory's walls, and manage the spreading Morass. Unnatural briars also continued to grip the northern forests.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: The Morass was spreading back into Ennerlund after the Druj destroyed its dykes; a now-unavailable option offered either restoring them or letting it become marsh, raising the upkeep of the Great Pits of Ennerlund.

Holberg/Holfried.t: Holfried's walls still stood, and Menno Van Ritsjhof proposed raising them to a strength of 12,000 within a year to make them the biggest fortification in the Empire.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: The worst-hit region, Holmauer's suburbs lay in vermin-ridden ruins with shattered walls; rival plans proposed an arch, a park-filled rebuilding or inaction, and Brechtje Van Holberg proposed deadly new defences inflicting extra casualties on attackers.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Unnatural vines and briars grew stronger in Misericorde's northern forests, where scattered orc bands avoided Imperial troops, threatening to impede any large-scale army movement.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: Rebeshof lost its fortifications and its farmland was devastated, while the Morass crept in to drown estates; the now-unavailable herbs option would have either restored its dykes or turned it to marsh.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Utterlund's northern forests remained under a sinister atmosphere, with unnatural briars that could significantly impede campaign armies.

Holberg.t: Holberg lay damaged throughout with reduced taxation, and its citizens proposed clearing Holmauer's ruins, building formidable new walls at Holmauer and Holfried, and dealing with the returning Morass, while unnatural briars choked its northern forests.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: its marshes were the benchmark a re-expanded Holberg Morass might rival for valuable healing herbs.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Jonas Quayle's accent is noted as being from Upwold.

Recognise Sand Fishers as foreigners.d: The Sand Fishers are a tribe of orcs living in Ossium who had until recently been subjects of the Druj. The motion, proposed by Miekarova and seconded by Therunin, declared those Sand Fishers who wished to remain part of their tribe to be foreigners. It passed. As a result the Sand Fishers became foreigners in Imperial eyes, receiving the protection of Imperial law for as long as they abide by it. The page notes that the further implications of this recognition were uncertain.

Druj.t: The Sand Fishers, an orc tribe of Ossium who had until recently been Druj subjects, were recognised by the Senate as foreigners, distinguishing them from the Druj enemy.

Recognise Sand Fishers as foreigners.o: In Winter 382YE the Senate passed a motion declaring that those Sand Fishers of Ossium who wished to remain part of their tribe were foreigners rather than enemies of the Empire.

Ossium.t: The Sand Fishers living in Ossium who wish to remain part of their tribe were declared foreigners, protected by Imperial law so long as they abide by it.

Recognise ducal quality.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Astolat and seconded by the senator for Mitwold, declared that the Empire wished to recognise the Ducal Quality of Kalino, a land of the Iron Confederacy, and to open a continuing dialogue for mutual benefit. It passed. As a statement of the Senate it carried no legal force within the Empire, but it was noted that it might have diplomatic consequences for relations with the Iron Confederacy.
Recognise ducal quality.o: In Summer 381YE the Senate passed a motion recognising the ducal quality of Kalino of the Iron Confederacy and calling for an ongoing dialogue to the benefit of both nations.

Kalino.t: The Senate formally acknowledged Kalino's ducal standing within the Iron Confederacy, a diplomatic gesture that could shape future dealings between the Empire and its rulers.

Recognise the House of Guiscard.d: Proposed by Segura and seconded by Skarsind, the motion formally announced Imperial support for the House of Guiscard, a house of the Iron Confederacy, in its bid to become rulers of Kalino. It followed a similar motion passed at the Summer Solstice 381YE. The motion passed. As a statement of the Senate's position it carried no legal force within the Empire, but it was noted that it might have diplomatic consequences in dealings with the Iron Confederacy.
Recognise the House of Guiscard.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 381YE recognising the Iron Confederacy's House of Guiscard as the rulers of Kalino, reaffirming a similar motion from the Summer Solstice.

Kalino.t: The Senate formally backed the House of Guiscard's claim to rule Kalino, then held by the Iron Confederacy, though the recognition carried no legal weight and only possible diplomatic consequences.

Reconstruct Gardens of Pallas.d: Nikolai, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the reconstruction, taking advantage of the previous season's appraisal and following a withdrawn Senate motion. It required 30 wains of weirwood, 12 wains of mithril, 116 crowns in labour and three months to build. Funding came slowly from many donors, including Anastasia, Bartimaeus, Fintan and Rhys Nighthaven, Richardo Glostari di Sarvos, Juno of Lapis Heights and Serenus Starsong. Esteban Ezmara of Sarangrave Reforged supplied the bulk of the mithril, weirwood and money after the Winter Solstice 385YE and Summer Solstice 386YE. With the Gardens complete, the senators of Urizen could appoint the Gardener of Pallas for the first time at the Autumn Equinox 386YE.

Urizen.t: Urizen's senators gain a new sinecure, the Gardener of Pallas, which they could appoint for the first time at the Autumn Equinox 386YE.

Reconstruct Gardens of Pallas.o: In Summer 385YE an Imperial Wayleave was used to commission the reconstruction of the Gardens of Pallas in Proceris, Zenith, creating a sinecure under the Restoration and renewal wind of fortune. The work was completed after a year of donations.

Zenith/Proceris.t: The Gardens of Pallas were reconstructed in Proceris, a project completed after the Summer Solstice 386YE with 30 wains of weirwood and 12 wains of mithril.

Zenith.t: Zenith gained a restored landmark when the Gardens of Pallas were rebuilt within its borders, creating a new sinecure tied to the territory.

Reconstruct Golden Cascade.d: The motion passed at 200 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Mournwold. The reconstruction required 60 wains of weirwood, 15 thrones and six months' work. Cadeus supplied the 15 thrones and 44 wains of weirwood after the Winter Solstice 384YE and the remaining 16 wains after the Spring Equinox 385YE. With the work complete, the Golden Cascade provides a share of 100 random herbs to farms and 30 crowns to herb gardens in Zenith.
