It also gives a significant boost to food supply across Urizen, allowing the nation to keep fully supplying the Citadel Guard indefinitely, provided Urizen retains all three of its current territories.

Urizen.t: The rebuilt Golden Cascade boosts food supply across Urizen, letting the nation fully supply the Citadel Guard indefinitely so long as it holds all three of its current territories.

Reconstruct Golden Cascade.o: In Winter 384YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Mournwold and seconded by Zenith, to reconstruct the Golden Cascade in Proceris, Zenith, following the Write your own ending wind of fortune.

Zenith/Proceris.t: The Golden Cascade was rebuilt in Proceris over six months using 60 wains of weirwood and 15 thrones, both supplied by Cadeus.

Zenith.t: Zenith regains the Golden Cascade, whose output shares 100 random herbs among the territory's farms and 30 crowns among its herb gardens.

Reconstruct Starlight Drift of Shimmerin.d: The commission cost 6 wains of mithril and 7 thrones, with three months needed to complete it. It was funded piecemeal across several seasons. Felix of the Wise Citadel, Nathair Autumngale and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov each gave a crown after the Winter Solstice 384YE. Peregrinus, Serenus Starsong and Nathair Autumngale gave further crowns after the Spring Equinox 385YE. Crassus then provided the 6 wains of mithril and 6 thrones 1 crown after the Summer Solstice 385YE, finishing the work. With the sinecure complete, the Urizen title of Custodian of the Starlight Drift became available to appoint from the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

Urizen.t: Urizen gained a new national title, the Custodian of the Starlight Drift, which became available to appoint from the Autumn Equinox 385YE once the mana sinecure was finished.

Reconstruct Starlight Drift of Shimmerin.o: The Legion Engineer, Bleakshield Groza, announced the commission of a mana sinecure, the Starlight Drift of Shimmering Snow, at Endsmeet in Zenith, following the Write your own ending Wind of Fortune. It was completed after the Summer Solstice 385YE.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Occursion became home to the Starlight Drift of Shimmering Snow, a mana sinecure at Endsmeet commissioned in the wake of the Write your own ending Wind of Fortune.

Zenith.t: A mana sinecure was built at Endsmeet in Zenith, which was held by Urizen. It was paid for over several seasons and completed after the Summer Solstice 385YE.

Reconstruct the Tower of the Fall.d: Proposed by the senator for Zenith and seconded by Kahraman, the motion took up an existing opportunity arising from the Write your own ending wind of fortune. The rebuilt Tower of the Fall forms part of the Proffered Hand network and yields ten mana and six measures of heart's blood each season to the Keeper of the Tower of the Fall, an existing tenured Urizen title appointed by the Urizen senators. Herminius supplied the six wains of mithril and 9 thrones 6 crowns after the Autumn Equinox. The work, which took three months, is complete, and the Keeper's position becomes available for appointment again at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Urizen.t: Urizen regained a working mana sinecure whose Keeper, a tenured Urizen title chosen by the nation's senators, receives ten mana and six heart's blood each season, with appointment possible again from Winter Solstice 385YE.

Reconstruct the Tower of the Fall.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 385YE to reconstruct the Tower of the Fall in Occursion, Zenith, as a mana sinecure joined to the Proffered Hand network, self-funded by Herminius of the Temple of the Wanderer.

Zenith/Occursion.t: The Tower of the Fall in Occursion was rebuilt with mithril and money from Herminius of the Temple of the Wanderer and now produces mana and heart's blood each season.

Zenith.t: Zenith gained a restored magical site linked to the Proffered Hand network, rebuilt at the urging of its own senator, who proposed the motion.

Red phoenix down.d: After the Spring Equinox, a thin, unnaturally penetrating drizzle soaked Redoubt, Zenith and Morrow at once. Urizen's many magicians grew lethargic, restless or short-tempered, struggling to keep their poise, with headaches and sleepless nights widespread. Mana sites in all three territories yielded half their normal crystal mana. The magicians quickly recognised the curse, though not who had cast it. Several weak regio collapsed and magical creatures grew more aggressive, with the trogoni driven into a ravenous frenzy that threatened mines, especially tempest jade mines. Coming after a similar situation in the League, mana shortages led the Imperial Bourse to offer no crystal mana at the coming Equinox auctions. The curse later abated and conditions returned to normal.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; the only link is a comparison with the torrential rain of Reikos, and the page does not say who cast the curse.

Urizen.t: Urizen's magicians, a large share of its people, struggled to keep their poise under the curse, and the nation lost half its crystal mana, saw weak regio collapse and faced frenzied trogoni threatening its mines.

Red phoenix down.o: An unknown party placed the Urizeni territories of Morrow, Redoubt and Zenith under the Winter curse Icy Maw Devours the Spark of Essence. Cold rain fell, Urizen's magicians suffered a debilitating malaise, and every mana site produced only half its usual crystal mana.

Morrow.t: Morrow was one of the three cursed territories, enduring the cold, seeping rain and halved production at its mana sites until the curse lifted.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt suffered the curse's drizzle and malaise, and its mana sites produced only half their usual crystal mana.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the curse's thin drizzle is contrasted with the torrential rain of Reikos.

Zenith.t: Zenith fell under the curse alongside Morrow and Redoubt, with sodden libraries and stores, troubled magicians and mana sites yielding only half their output.

Red skies.d: The Gathered Storm set a trap for the Red Wind Corsairs off Trivento but was flanked by Imperial captains, many bolstered by Summer magic, and routed. General Joaquim i Erigo's Corsairs pursued them into Madruga and destroyed them in a bloody battle in Calvos Sound, losing under four hundred sailors and capturing the Storm's Child with the stolen Freeborn Storm figurehead, later given to the Freeborn egregores. The Children of Wrecks still hold Free Landing behind Siakha's maelstrom. The Iron Confederacy's Wings of Kobol conquered the Cazar Straits, executing Wreckers, with unclear intentions. A coded Grendel gull message reporting the Corsairs in Madruga was intercepted in Sarvos. Three Wrecker skirmishes were all defeated.

Dawn.t: A great many of the Imperial ships that joined the Corsairs sailed under the flags of Dawn, sharing in the destruction of the Gathered Storm.

Grendel.t: Gallum Firesach's orcs at Mora's Rock defended the Feroz coast from Wreckers and vowed to resist any Confederacy advance, while a Grendel-ciphered message about the Corsairs' presence in Madruga was intercepted before reaching its destination.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: they were the only nation without ships among the Imperial fleets, not being known for maritime prowess.

Navarr.t: Ioan Bloodstride recruited Navarr of Therunin who feel abandoned by the Empire to join a Wrecker raid on Peregro, which was defeated.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn corsairs avenged years of losses by destroying the Gathered Storm and capturing the stolen figurehead, which went to the egregores with hope of reviving the Freeborn Storm, but Suranni forces now hold the Freeborn islands of the Cazar Straits.

The League.t: The Sarvos coast was made safe as the Gathered Storm was destroyed, a Great Chain soldier intercepted a Grendel messenger gull, and Champion of Wisdom Rhydian de Rondell's forces defeated Wreckers at Antonio's Glebe.

Urizen.t: A scattering of Urizeni ships joined the Imperial fleets, and Arbiter of the Four Winds Athenus defeated Wreckers seeking to curse the geysers of Peregro.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark sailors are invoked for the saying that one can never be sure whom an omen favours.

Red skies.o: In Winter 387YE the Red Wind Corsairs, joined by over a hundred and fifty Imperial ships, destroyed the Gathered Storm, the navy of the Children of Wrecks, off Sarvos and in Calvos Sound, capturing its flagship. Meanwhile a Suranni navy and two armies from the Iron Confederacy crushed the Wreckers in the Cazar Straits and claimed the islands.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The Wings of Kobol and two Iron Confederacy armies scoured the Wreckers from the ruins of Shantarim and Cazar, executing captives, and conquered the islands.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni forces made no attempt to approach its coast.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni did not approach its coast, and Oran is described as still seeking its future.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: The Red Wind Corsairs caught and annihilated the Gathered Storm there, seizing the Storm's Child, and now shelter at Calvos.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: The Wreckers failed to reach it before being destroyed but still hold the region, protected by the Maw of Siakha's magical wards.

Madruga/Siroc Bayou.t: Patroco i Boyaga's Wreckers landed in western Siroc Bayou and fled into the Crucible, where Imperial Fleet Master Giovanni von Temeschwar's forces defeated them at Draws Sward.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Wreckers carrying a bottled Spring boon threatened the geysers and the Monastery of the Four Winds' gardens but were defeated at Xavier's Path.

Bay of Catazar.t: With the Gathered Storm destroyed, the Children of Wrecks can no longer directly threaten the Bay's coasts, though some pirate fleets and the corsair Isidore i Boyaga escaped onto its waters.

Feroz.t: The Iron Confederacy crushed the Wreckers in Feroz and conquered the Cazar Straits, while Gallum Firesach's garrison stood ready to defend the coast should the Suranni advance.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the sun is described setting behind its distant mountains.

Madruga.t: The Red Wind Corsairs destroyed the Gathered Storm in Calvos Sound and are now based there, leaving the Wreckers' hold on Madruga tenuous though they still keep Free Landing.

Morrow.t: Wreckers and Navarr recruits attempting to curse Peregro's geysers were defeated by the Arbiter of the Four Winds.

Sarvos.t: The decisive fight began off Trivento, damaged ships sheltered at Caricomare and Trivento, a Grendel gull was shot down, and Wreckers threatening a settlement near Glass Point were defeated at Antonio's Glebe.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Ioan Bloodstride recruited Navarr there who feel the territory has been abandoned by the Empire.

Veroigne.t: Mentioned in passing: one Suranni army was the force Marko Siwarsbairn encountered there earlier in the year.

Red star.d: Scholars grew unsure how many stars make up the Phoenix. Its magic now needs extra effort, and those attached to it suffer listlessness. Astronomancers in Urizen, Varushka and the Brass Coast reported a tiny star, possibly red, trailing the Wanderer. It is unnamed, and the Conclave might name it by Declaration of Concord. The Observatory of the Blazing Mirror in Iteri offered to build a device to study it if given 75 weltsilver and 10 crowns. It promised a grand unveiling at the Spring Equinox. Meanwhile mania spread, with afflicted magicians reported in Varushka, Dawn and the Navarr trods, and in foreign lands too.

Dawn.t: In Dawn's rose gardens, a cabal of weavers found one of their number cackling to the plants and whispering stories to the leaves. This was one of the reported cases of the spreading mania.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the story remarks that it had been a long time since the Druj threatened Zenith.

Urizen.t: Urizeni observatories were among those that spotted the new star. The Observatory of the Blazing Mirror offered to build a device to study it. Meanwhile the Spire of Twisting Shadows was overwhelmed by Urizeni mages harmed by astronomantic accidents and by a tulpa of the Phoenix.

Varushka.t: Varushkan observatories reported sighting the new star. From the dark woods came word of a volhov howling at the sky after a chance encounter on the road at night.

Red star.o: In Winter 379YE the constellation of the Phoenix began to seem to waver and wane, a tiny new star was seen following the Wanderer, and houses of healing across the Empire and beyond reported a rise in madness.

Zenith/Iteri.t: Arbiter Horace's Observatory of the Blazing Mirror in Iteri offered to build a device to view the new star if given 75 weltsilver and 10 crowns. It planned a grand unveiling at the Spring Equinox for the archmages, grandmasters and its benefactor.

Zenith/Lustri.t: In Lustri's snowbound forests, Papiria's Spire of Twisting Shadows was swamped with new patients from Ankra, Caeli and Peregro. Three of them had been damaged by a tulpa of the Phoenix and would not eat, and she feared the spire would have to stop taking admissions.

Zenith.t: Zenith was home to both responses to the strange skies: an Iteri observatory sought materials to examine the new star, while a healing spire in the forests struggled with a flood of maddened magicians.

Redesign Pallas Docks.d: Proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Segura, the motion acted on the Autumn proposal of the Debruin Family of the House of the Bear, set out in the Hyenas and herbs wind of fortune. The renamed Debruin Docks would stay an Imperial Bourse position, overseen by the Prime Factor of the Pallas Docks, to bolster the Senate's funding. The Ambassador to the Delves supported it. The project was to be self-funded, costing 90 crowns and taking three months. After the Winter Solstice, Marta Kotova Novikova gave 11 thrones and 1 crown and Kostjya gave 1 crown. Once complete, the Custodian of the Pallas Docks becomes the Custodian of the Debruin Docks.

Urizen.t: The redesigned ministry sits in Urizen-held Redoubt, where an unused set of docks is to be revived as a trading post for weirwood from the Sarcophan Delves.

Redesign Pallas Docks.o: In Winter 386YE the Senate passed a motion to redesign the unused Pallas Docks ministry in Limus, Redoubt, so that weirwood could be bought from the Sarcophan Delves, renaming it the Debruin Docks.

Redoubt/Limus.t: Limus is home to the Pallas Docks, which the motion renames the Debruin Docks and redesigns for the weirwood trade once three months of work are complete.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt's long-unused Pallas Docks are to be rebuilt and reopened as the Debruin Docks, an Imperial Bourse position for buying weirwood from the Sarcophan Delves.

Reed of fortune.d: Although Ephisis lacked amity, Reed, a powerful genie, was seen across the Empire over three months. He spoke with League silversmiths and printers, a Feroz paradour mistress, Atalyan shipwrights, the Imperial Mint, Bourse auctioneers, Wintermark smiths, Marcher merchants and others about their work and their politics. This raised suspicion that an Imperial citizen had summoned him by ritual. At Anvil he offered to purchase amity for no more than one hour so that the City of Gold and Lead could make a single address. He suggested a Declaration of Neutrality be raised alongside it, scrupulously following protocol. The Conclave declared amity, heard his address, and then restored neutrality.

The Brass Coast.t: Reed took syrah with the mistress of a Feroz paradour and counted planks on the docks of the Atalyan shipyard as part of his audit of Freeborn commerce.

The League.t: League craftsmen drew Reed's attention: he talked business with silversmiths in Temeschwar and printers in Tassato, and was reportedly seen outside a theatre in Sarvos.

The Marches.t: Reed evaluated the price of grain, beets and beer with Marcher merchants and was reported in Bregasland. The tale's opening tells of a genie who counted a Marcher farm's grain and helped dig a ditch by borrowing a farmhand's time.

Wintermark.t: Reed watched a Wintermark forge from sunrise to sunset while barely speaking to the hard-working smiths.

Reed of fortune.o: In Autumn 379YE Reed, the Reckoner of Hours and herald of the eternal Ephisis, moved through the Empire conducting an apparent audit of its wealth-producers. He then asked the Conclave for one hour of amity so that he could address it. The Conclave granted the amity, heard him, and then returned him to neutrality.

Bregasland.t: Somewhat unreliable reports placed Reed in Bregasland, deep in conversation with a Winter Sun orc.

Feroz.t: In Feroz the herald took syrah with the mistress of a paradour, questioning her about her trade.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name Madruga; its only Brass Coast references are a Feroz paradour and the Atalyan shipyard.

Sarvos.t: Scattered, unreliable reports placed Reed outside a theatre in Sarvos one night.

Tassato.t: Reed was spotted discussing business with printers in Tassato.

Temeschwar.t: Reed was spotted discussing business with silversmiths in Temeschwar.

Reestablish Herds of Afar.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Feroz and seconded by the senator for Kahraman. It commissioned work, as outlined by the civil service, to reestablish the herds of Afar and to create a new sinecure, the Dhomiro of Afar. The commission cost 300 crowns, took three months to complete, and was to be entirely self-funded. After the Winter Solstice 386YE, Garviel i Abrira i Erigo contributed 37 thrones and 2 crowns, and Karrak and Farren Silver Streams each gave 1 crown. With the work complete, the Dhomiro of Afar was to be appointed for the first time at the Spring Equinox 387YE by Tally of the Votes of Freeborn fleet owners.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page; it is linked only because it held part of Feroz that season.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gained a new title, the Dhomiro of Afar, to be chosen by their fleet owners, and saw the herds of Afar restored in Feroz.

Reestablish Herds of Afar.o: In Winter 386YE the Senate passed a motion to restore the herds of Afar in Afarjasse, Feroz, at a cost of 300 crowns, and to create the Dhomiro of Afar to oversee them. The motion followed the 'Send for me' Wind of Fortune.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: Afarjasse became home to the restored herds of Afar and the seat of the new Dhomiro of Afar sinecure.

Feroz.t: The senator for Feroz proposed the commission, which restored the herds of Afar and created a sinecure to oversee them in the territory.

Refusal of the ceding of territories to.d: The Hierro Clan laid claim to two Freeborn territories, Segura and Feroz. In response, the Senate passed a motion proposed by the senator for Madruga and seconded by the senator for Semmerholm, stating plainly that the Empire would not surrender either territory to the Hierro. The page records the motion as having passed, making the Senate's stance on the claim clear. It does not record what the Hierro did in response.

The Brass Coast.t: The Senate refused to give up two of the Freeborn's own territories to the Hierro Clan, affirming that Segura and Feroz would remain part of the Brass Coast and the Empire.

Refusal of the ceding of territories to.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate passed a motion refusing to cede the Freeborn territories of Segura and Feroz to the Hierro Clan, who had laid claim to them.

Feroz.t: Feroz was one of the two territories claimed by the Hierro Clan, and the Senate formally refused to surrender it.

Segura.t: Segura was claimed by the Hierro Clan alongside Feroz, and the Senate passed a motion refusing to cede it.

Reikos flux.d: Two weeks before the Summer solstice the Valiant Pegasus was struck by a terrible disease of exhaustion, diarrhoea and vomiting that killed many, and the Granite Pillar and Quiet Step soon followed. Affected armies were expected to lose one in ten soldiers each season, and resources in Reikos were to produce only three quarters of normal output; any army leaving would spread it. After the solstice the Granite Pillar and Quiet Step withdrew, the flux burnt from them by rituals of Day, while the Valiant Pegasus remained exposed. During the Autumn Equinox a herbal cure was found, and Spring magic focused through the Urizen Citadel Guard brought cleansing rain that cured the armies and citizens of Reikos.

Druj.t: The Druj appeared to be falling back before the Highborn advance in Reikos, and the Empire suspected the plague might be a malignant Druj scheme to drive the Imperial armies out.

Urizen.t: The Urizen army, the Citadel Guard, served as the focus for the Spring magic that filled Reikos at the Autumn Equinox and washed away the flux.

Reikos flux.o: In Summer 379YE a virulent flux broke out in Druj-held Reikos, striking the Imperial armies campaigning there and the local population, amid suspicion that the retreating Druj had turned to foul magics and pestilence.

Reikos.t: Reikos was ravaged by the flux, its inhabitants and property suffering alongside the Imperial armies there, with resources cut to three quarters of normal output until cleansing Spring rain cured the territory at the Autumn Equinox.

Relinquish Brilliant Shore.d: Proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by Sermersuaq, the motion used the Senate's power of relinquishment over the Brilliant Shore, a Bourse position in Skarsind. It passed with a constitutional majority and was ratified by the Throne, so no veto was possible. As a result, the Brilliant Shore ceased to be a National position and became available for allocation. The motion cost nothing.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs lost the Brilliant Shore as a National Bourse position in their territory of Skarsind, and control of it was opened up for allocation instead.

Relinquish Brilliant Shore.o: The Senate passed a motion, with a constitutional majority and ratified by the Throne, to relinquish the Brilliant Shore, the National Bourse position in Skarsind, making it available for allocation.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind's senator proposed the motion, and the Brilliant Shore on its coast stopped being a National position and became available for allocation.

Relinquish Skarsind.d: The Winterfolk senators presented the relinquishment as an act of loyalty to the Empire and to the Imperial Orcs. The Constitutional Court judged it to represent the true will of Wintermark, given its senators' unanimous support and the Wintermark Assembly's right of veto. It could be abrogated by the Senate before ratification, or vetoed by the Assembly of the Nine, the General Assembly or the Wintermark National Assembly before the first Senate session of the Summer Solstice. The Brilliant Shore Bourse seat would stay with Wintermark until reassignment. At the Autumn Equinox 379YE the Imperial Favour of Empress Britta allowed ratification without a Throne, and the Senate assigned Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs. The motion led directly to the Senate's power of relinquishment.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's senators voluntarily gave up their nation's claim to Skarsind out of loyalty to the Empire and the Imperial Orcs, keeping the Brilliant Shore Bourse seat only until the territory was reassigned, and the Wintermark National Assembly was given its own power to veto the motion.

Relinquish Skarsind.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate unanimously passed a motion, proposed by the senators of Sermersuaq and Skarsind, renouncing Wintermark's claim to Skarsind so that it could become the first home of the Imperial Orc nation. It required ratification by the Throne and could be vetoed by the Synod, including the Wintermark National Assembly.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind was to cease being part of Wintermark, and after the motion was ratified at the Autumn Equinox 379YE through Empress Britta's Imperial Favour, the Senate assigned it to the Imperial Orcs as their first home.

Remodel Virtue's Rest.d: Proposed by Reikos and seconded by Spiral, the motion commissioned the remodelling of the great work Virtue's Rest as detailed in the War of Thorns and Flowers wind of fortune. The work cost 120 crowns plus the usual costs of the opportunity, and took three months. Cyrus of Ebon's Hall, Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven contributed towards it. The remodelling completely removed the investment and returns Virtue's Rest had previously offered. Instead, eligible armies of Navarr, Highguard, Varushka and the League could take the Resupply in Virtue's Rest order in Bastion to improve their resupply. The new Exarch of Virtue's Rest would first be appointed at Summer Solstice 387YE by the votes of Highborn congregation owners.

Highguard.t: Highborn citizens gave up the hostels they had offered to pilgrims so they could shelter recovering soldiers, and Highguard's armies can now resupply at Virtue's Rest. The new Exarch of Virtue's Rest is chosen annually by Highborn congregation owners.

Navarr.t: Navarr armies are among those eligible to take the Resupply in Virtue's Rest order in Bastion, which improves their resupply during the War of Thorns and Flowers.

Varushka.t: Varushkan armies are among those eligible to resupply at the remodelled Virtue's Rest in Bastion, which strengthens their recovery during the war.

Remodel Virtue's Rest.o: The Senate passed a motion in Winter 386YE to remodel Virtue's Rest in Bastion, turning its pilgrim hostels into a place where soldiers of the War of Thorns and Flowers could recover, overseen by a new annually elected Exarch of Virtue's Rest.

Bastion.t: Virtue's Rest in Bastion was rebuilt from pilgrim hostels into a recovery place for soldiers. It lost its former investment returns but now offers the Resupply in Virtue's Rest order to eligible armies.

Repair Berechiah's Basilica.d: The motion drew on a civil service report from before Winter Solstice 385YE and the Knocking on every door wind of fortune. It created a sinecure costing 10 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood, 45 crowns in labour and three months of work. The Custodes Clavium undertook to cover construction costs and gave 5 thrones 5 crowns after Autumn Equinox 387YE. Cyrus of Athaliah's Handiwork supplied the white granite in two loads of 5 wains, and Merari Navigators of Virtue supplied the 5 wains of weirwood across Spring and Summer 388YE. Once complete, the work creates a title to be appointed by the Vigilance Assembly.

Highguard.t: Highguard benefactors carried the restoration: the Custodes Clavium covered the costs, Cyrus of Athaliah's Handiwork gave the white granite and Merari Navigators of Virtue gave the weirwood, all for a basilica in a Highborn territory.

Repair Berechiah's Basilica.o: In Autumn 387YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Bastion and seconded by Karsk, to commission repairs to Berechiah's Basilica in Bastion as a rallying point for the vigilant against foreign threats.

Bastion.t: Berechiah's Basilica in Bastion was to be repaired as a rallying point for the vigilant against foreign threats, and the motion was proposed by Bastion's own senator.

Repair Blood Red River Museum.d: Proposed by the senator for Tassato and seconded by Temeschwar, the self-funded motion commissioned repairs costing 15 wains of white granite, 15 wains of weirwood and 150 crowns in labour and art, taking three months. Several citizens donated over the following seasons. Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato provided most of it after Spring Equinox 385YE: 17 thrones, 1 crown, 18 rings and all the materials. The museum remains a great work of Pride. The motion intended the Curator to be a League citizen chosen unanimously by the League senators. Because the title carries votes in the Synod, that method was ruled impossible, and the Senate passed a Constitutional Court motion clarifying this. The Curator was to be appointed at Summer Solstice 385YE.

The League.t: League citizens, led by Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato, funded the restoration of one of their nation's great works of Pride. However, the League senators lost the power to choose the new Curator by unanimous vote, because the title carries Synod votes.

Repair Blood Red River Museum.o: In Summer 384YE the Imperial Senate passed a motion to repair and rebuild the Blood Red River Museum in Tassato and to create the tenured title of Curator of the Blood Red River. The work was completed after the Spring Equinox 385YE.

Tassato.t: The Blood Red River Museum in Tassato was repaired and rebuilt, remaining a great work of Pride. A new Imperial title, Curator of the Blood Red River, was created for it, with the appointment due at Summer Solstice 385YE.

Repair Capodomus Cathedral.d: Announced by Estella Lucati di Sarvos as proxy to the Master of Rings, the commission followed the Old Ways Wind of Fortune. It cost 20 white granite, 10 mithril and 90 crowns and took three months. Jules von Holberg, Estella Lucati, Laurencio Lemmini di Sarvos, Sebastiano and Luciana Valesi each gave mithril, white granite and money, and Gino de Sarvos, Luca Lucati and Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg added further coin. The motion hoped to restore the oldest and greatest cathedral to the Way of Virtue and ready it for consecration with True Liao as a symbol of rebirth. The work is complete, and the National Assembly may now appoint the Archbishop each Summer Solstice.

The League.t: The League National Assembly gained the annual appointment of the Archbishop of Capodomus, who coordinates and supports the Assembly and acts as a point of contact. League citizens largely funded the repairs.

Repair Capodomus Cathedral.o: In Summer 386YE the Senate commissioned the long-overdue repair of the Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos, damaged during the Grendel sack of the city. The work also created the Archbishop of Capodomus, a sinecure appointed by the League National Assembly.

Sarvos.t: The Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos was finally restored after the Grendel sack and made ready for consecration with True Liao, intended as a symbol of the city's rebirth and renewal.

Repair Celesti Lighthouse.d: Proposed by the senator for Feroz and seconded by Segura, the motion restored the lighthouse according to Eilian Sweetwater's Summer 387YE appraisal, returning it to the care of the Celesti Lighthouse Keeper. It cost 16 wains of mithril, 10 rings of ilium, 60 ingots of weltsilver, 40 ingots of tempest jade and 48 crowns in labour, taking three months. Manolo i Erigo, Bakar i Riqueza, Estevanico i Hayim i Riqueza and Iago i Guerra supplied the materials and money. Once complete, Brass Coast senators could again appoint the Keeper, the Escort Imperial Shipping voyage was replaced with Patrol the Bay of Catazar, and the Senate could restore the Broken Shore Bounty.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page and is linked only because it held part of Feroz that season.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast citizens funded the restoration themselves, and the nation's senators regained the right to appoint the Celesti Lighthouse Keeper.

Repair Celesti Lighthouse.o: The Senate passed a motion in Autumn 387YE to restore the Celesti Lighthouse in Oranseri, Feroz, including a magically infused lamp, a watchstone, empowered by Kimus. It was self-funded by prosperous Brass Coast citizens and has been completed.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The restored Celesti Lighthouse stands in Oranseri, where it was rebuilt to its former glory with a magically infused watchstone lamp.

Bay of Catazar.t: The completed lighthouse replaced the Escort Imperial Shipping voyage with a new Patrol the Bay of Catazar voyage on these waters.

Feroz.t: The Celesti Lighthouse in Feroz was rebuilt with a watchstone lamp. The territory's senator proposed the motion.

Repair Great Pits of Ennerlund.d: After Imperial forces liberated the Great Pits of Ennerlund, the Senate voted at Spring 379YE to repair the mines. The Druj had collapsed them in Winter 378YE and destroyed the pumping mechanisms, causing great loss of life and leaving the workings inoperable. The repair required 250 thrones of materials and nine months. Bridget Eastville of the Marches provided the 250 thrones after the Spring Equinox. Mithril was first expected after the Spring Equinox 380YE, but an extensive haunting of the mines delayed production by a season, with the first mithril due at the Autumn Equinox 380YE. The Great Pits were fully repaired, returning to their pre-destruction output of 27 wains of mithril a season.

Druj.t: The Druj sabotage of Winter 378YE, which collapsed the pits and wrecked the pumps at great cost in lives, was undone by the Imperial repair.

The League.t: The League's Holberg regained a major mithril mine, restored to its full output of 27 wains a season after the Druj destruction.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Bridget Eastville of the Marches provided the 250 thrones that paid for the repairs.

Repair Great Pits of Ennerlund.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by Sermersuaq and seconded by Mitwold, to repair the Great Pits of Ennerlund in Holberg, which the Druj had collapsed in Winter 378YE. The repairs were funded and the pits were eventually restored to full production.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: The collapsed mineworkings at Ennerlund were repaired despite an extensive haunting, and the pits returned to producing 27 wains of mithril a season.

Holberg.t: Holberg's Great Pits, liberated from the Druj, were rebuilt over nine months. A haunting delayed the first mithril until the Autumn Equinox 380YE.

Repair Holberg defences.d: Proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by Karov, the motion followed plans that the engineer Rhiner Van Hesselman had presented to the League. It passed with 45 Thrones in favour and 13 votes against, and the funds were disbursed to Adamah of the Silent Tide, Senator for Necropolis. The cost was 100 crowns, 25 wains of white granite, 10 wains of weirwood, 25 measures of Bladeroot and 25 measures of Imperial Roseweald. Oksana Kazaku, senator for Temeschwar, paid it during the Spring Equinox downtime. Van Hesselman's plans were carried out and Holberg's defences were repaired to their pre-siege levels.

Druj.t: The walls and gates of Holberg, a territory then outside Imperial control and held by the Druj, were rebuilt to their pre-siege strength by Imperial effort.

Highguard.t: Highguard's senator for Necropolis, Adamah of the Silent Tide, proposed the repairs and received the funds to carry them out.

The League.t: Plans by the League engineer Rhiner Van Hesselman were used to restore the defences of Holberg, and the Temeschwar senator paid for the work.

Repair Holberg defences.o: In Spring 377YE the Senate passed a motion for the emergency repair of the gates and walls of Holberg, and the walls were restored to full strength even though the territory was not then under Imperial control.

Holberg.t: Holberg's gates and walls were repaired to full, pre-siege strength, although the territory was not under Imperial control at the time.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the senator for Necropolis proposed the motion and received the funds for the repairs.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Oksana Kazaku, senator for Temeschwar, paid for the repairs during the Spring Equinox downtime.

Repair the Sapphire Stair.d: The Sapphire Stair was damaged by Eisa Winterborn during the raid described in the Shallows and Miseries Wind of War. The Senate authorised its repair at the cost set out in the opportunity: 10 wains each of white granite, weirwood and mithril, plus 90 crowns, with three months to complete. After the Summer Solstice 386YE, Raphael Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato supplied 10 wains each of mithril, weirwood and white granite, along with 11 thrones and 2 crowns. With the work finished, the Keeper of the Sapphire Stair once again receives their previous income.

The League.t: A League landmark damaged in a hostile raid was restored, largely funded and supplied by the League citizen Raphael Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato, and its Keeper's income was restored.

Repair the Sapphire Stair.o: In Summer 386YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Tassato and seconded by Karsk, authorising the repair of the Sapphire Stair in Tassato after it was damaged in Eisa Winterborn's raid.

Tassato.t: The Sapphire Stair in Tassato, damaged in Eisa Winterborn's raid, was rebuilt on the motion of Tassato's own senator, and its Keeper now receives their former income again.

Repair the Spider's Dream.d: Proposed by the senator for Madruga and seconded by Feroz, the motion sought funds to repair the Spider's Dream bridge, which had fallen into a sorry state. It passed at a cost of 15 Thrones, with 3 votes against, and the money went to Madruga. The project required 20 wains of weirwood, all provided by Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra, Senator for Madruga, and the repairs were completed. Restoring the bridge reinstated the Spider's Tollkeep sinecure, which had lapsed under Emperor Walter. It pays its holder 2 Thrones each season from tolls. The holder is chosen unanimously by the senators of the Brass Coast and the League, and the post was left vacant.

The Brass Coast.t: A Brass Coast senator proposed the motion and personally supplied the weirwood. Brass Coast senators now share, with the League's, the unanimous choice of who holds the restored Spider's Tollkeep sinecure.

The League.t: League senators gain a joint say, with the Brass Coast, in appointing the holder of the reinstated Spider's Tollkeep sinecure, which is funded by tolls on the bridge into Sarvos.

Repair the Spider's Dream.o: In Spring 377YE the Senate passed a motion to repair the Spider's Dream, the decaying bridge linking Sarvos and Madruga, and the work was completed using 20 wains of weirwood.

Madruga.t: Madruga's senator proposed the repair and provided the 20 wains of weirwood, and the Senate's funds were distributed to Madruga to restore its end of the bridge.

Sarvos.t: The Spider's Dream, Sarvos's bridge link to Madruga, was repaired and restored to working order, allowing tolls to be collected for the Spider's Tollkeep once more.

Repair the cargo dock at Caricomare.d: Proposed by Temeschwar and seconded by Holberg, the motion called for a self-funded restoration of the Sarvos docks, which had been damaged by the Grendel when they invaded in Winter 380YE. The cost was unknown and the commission was presented as an opportunity. After the Spring Equinox 381YE, Gant Archama provided 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns. The docks were completed, creating the Overseer of the Cavabianca Dock, a national League title appointed through the Bourse, with the first white granite shipment expected after the Summer Solstice. The Constitutional Court noted the motion had not specified whether the title was Imperial or national, and that as a Bourse title it cannot later be amended by the Senate.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named as having damaged the Caricomare docks during their invasion of Sarvos in Winter 380YE.

The League.t: The League recovered a working trade dock in Sarvos and gained a new national Bourse title, Overseer of the Cavabianca Dock, controlling access to white granite traded from Asavea.

Repair the cargo dock at Caricomare.o: The Senate passed a motion to repair the cargo dock at Caricomare in Sarvos, damaged during the Grendel invasion of Winter 380YE, so that trade in white granite with Asavea could resume. The work was completed, creating the title Overseer of the Cavabianca Dock.

Sarvos.t: The Grendel-damaged cargo dock at Caricomare in Sarvos was rebuilt, restoring white granite trade with Asavea, with the first shipment expected after the Summer Solstice.

Repair the docks at Caricomare.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by the senator for Sarvos, the motion sought to repair the Caricomare Quays, a ruined great work at the docks of Sarvos. The repairs were costed at 35 white granite and 5 weirwood. Had they been carried out, every League fleet operating out of Sarvos would have produced more wealth, with a total benefit of 480 rings per season shared among all fleets active there. The Senate rejected the motion in principle, 10 votes for and 14 against, so the quays remained in ruins.

The League.t: League senators for Temeschwar and Sarvos championed the repair, but its defeat denied League fleet captains working out of Sarvos an extra 480 rings per season to share between them.

Repair the docks at Caricomare.o: In Winter 377YE the Senate considered a motion to restore the ruined Caricomare Quays in Sarvos to basic functionality, but it was defeated in principle by 14 votes to 10.

Sarvos.t: The Caricomare Quays at Sarvos stayed ruined after the Senate voted down their restoration, leaving the territory's fleets without the added wealth the repaired docks would have brought.

Research Aneira Dancewalker and her brot.d: Announced in Summer 381YE, the research request was made under the power to announce historical research that the Senate has delegated to the Dredgemaster of Feverwater. It concerns two figures from Liathaven's past. Aneira Dancewalker is thought to have been General of the Quiet Step at the time Liathaven fell. Her brother Eurion Dancewalker forged Aneira's Talon, an improved version of the Scorpion's Sting. The pair are believed to have lived in a steading in West Ranging. At the time of the record the research was still in progress, and no findings had been reported.

Jotun.t: The Jotun held Liathaven that season, and the research looked into figures from the history of the land they now controlled.

Research Aneira Dancewalker and her brot.o: Eleri Bronwen's Rest, Dredgemaster of Feverwater, commissioned historical research through the civil service into Aneira Dancewalker, believed to have been General of the Quiet Step during the fall of Liathaven, and her brother Eurion, who forged Aneira's Talon.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: West Ranging is believed to have been home to the Dancewalker siblings' steading, making it the likely focus of the research.

Liathaven.t: The research focuses on Liathaven's past: a general of the Quiet Step at the time of its fall, and the smith who forged Aneira's Talon there.

Research Apaayuqiu King.d: Ioseph, the Minister for Historical Research, used the power to approve historical research delegated by the Senate to commission an inquiry into Apaayuqiu King and the pre-Wintermark history of the Sermersuaq area. He was particularly interested in a chain of bronze that marked her status as chief of chiefs. The request apparently followed a past-life vision experienced by Asenath of Felix Watch. The research cost 5 Thrones, which Ioseph of Phoenix Reach provided after the Winter Solstice 380YE. The civil service will compile research reports and present them to the Minister for Historical Research.

Wintermark.t: The research looks into history from before Wintermark, in lands Wintermark now holds. It may shed light on Apaayuqiu King and the bronze chain that marked her as chief of chiefs.

Research Apaayuqiu King.o: In Winter 380YE the Minister for Historical Research, Ioseph, authorised civil service research into Apaayuqiu King, a figure of pre-Wintermark history in the Sermersuaq area. The inquiry focused on a bronze chain said to mark her position as chief of chiefs.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq is the focus of the inquiry, which examines the area's pre-Wintermark past and the chieftain Apaayuqiu King who once held authority there.

Research Fire from the Heavens.d: Using the legal power to announce historical research that the Senate has delegated to the office, Ioseph, Minister of Historical Research, commissioned the civil service to research "Fire from the Heavens". This is an enchantment originating from an old coven in Willstone, in the Urizen territory of Redoubt. The page records only the commission, not any findings. A historical research report was due to be delivered to the Minister at the Spring Equinox and published publicly afterwards.

Urizen.t: The research concerns magical lore from Urizen's own past, an enchantment worked by an old coven in one of its territories, and the report may shed light on the nation's magical history.

Research Fire from the Heavens.o: In Winter 381YE Ioseph, Minister of Historical Research, announced a commission to research "Fire from the Heavens", an enchantment associated with an old coven in Willstone, Redoubt.

Redoubt/Willstone.t: Willstone is named as the home of the old coven whose enchantment, "Fire from the Heavens", is the subject of the research.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt, held by Urizen, is the territory where the old coven associated with "Fire from the Heavens" was based, making it the focus of the commissioned research.

Research Mfanwy.d: Using the power to announce historical research delegated by the Senate, the Dredgemaster of Feverwater (also styled the Fevermaster of Dredgewater on the page) announced research into Myfanwy of Hercynia, covering her travels and her relationships with the First Empress. The commission cost 5 thrones, all of which were provided by Eleri Bronwen's Rest. The page states that research begins once the funds are provided; it does not record any findings.

Navarr.t: The research looks into a figure from Navarr's own Hercynian past, Myfanwy, and her links to the First Empress. Its 5-throne cost was met by Eleri Bronwen's Rest.

Research Mfanwy.o: In Autumn 381YE the Dredgemaster of Feverwater commissioned historical research through the civil service into Myfanwy of Hercynia, her travels and her relationships with the First Empress.

Hercynia.t: The territory gives Myfanwy of Hercynia her name, and she is the subject of the commissioned research into her travels and her relationships with the First Empress.

Research Purifying Flame.d: The motion, proposed by Casinea and seconded by the Conscience of the Senate, sought research into the activities, goals and members of the Society of the Purifying Flame. The research was to begin with the lives of Benedict Di Tassato, Mario De Regiario and their known associates around 270–300YE and trace the society up to the present day. It was classed as historical research costing 5 thrones. Its progress was recorded as unknown, and the stated outcome was that a report on the Purifying Flame would be compiled and delivered to the Senator for Casinea.

The League.t: The research was put forward by the Senator for Casinea, a League senator, who was to receive the finished report on the Society of the Purifying Flame.

Research Purifying Flame.o: In Winter 378YE the Senate motion proposed by Casinea's senator commissioned historical research into the secretive Society of the Purifying Flame, at a cost of 5 thrones.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory appears only in the name of Benedict Di Tassato, one of the historical figures whose life was the starting point for the research.

Research Sungold Pass.d: Announced by the Minister of Historical Research, this action commissioned historical research into the history of the Sungold Pass mine. The page notes that the Thule were laying claim to the mine, which lies on the boundary of Otkodov in the eastern foothills of Opascari. The page records only that the research was commissioned; it gives no findings or outcome of the investigation.

Thule.t: The research examined the history of a mine the Thule were claiming, which could bear on the strength of their claim to Sungold Pass.

Research Sungold Pass.o: In Winter 382YE the Minister of Historical Research announced a commission of historical research into the Sungold Pass mine, which the Thule were laying claim to on the boundary of Otkodov in the eastern foothills of Opascari.

Otkodov.t: The Sungold Pass mine under research lies on the boundary of Otkodov in the eastern foothills of Opascari, held by Thule at the time.

Research the Terunael site of Ghita's Ve.d: The commission was issued by Harwyn Hollowwatcher, acting as Proxy of Siân Eternal, and announced by the Advisor on the Vallorn. It directed the Civil Service to carry out historical research into Ghita's Veil, a Terunael site in Segura, and comparable places such as Sobral's Stand. A report was compiled and provided to the Advisor, and the bulk of that report was afterwards made publicly available.

The Brass Coast.t: A Terunael site within Brass Coast lands became the subject of formal Civil Service historical research, and most of the resulting report was made public.

Research the Terunael site of Ghita's Ve.o: In Spring 383YE Harwyn Hollowwatcher, Proxy of Siân Eternal, commissioned the Civil Service to research the Terunael site known as Ghita's Veil in Segura, along with similar locations such as Sobral's Stand.

Segura.t: Ghita's Veil, a Terunael site in Segura, was the focus of the commissioned research, and the resulting report was largely made publicly available.

Research the vallorn for the Academy.d: Proposed by the senator for Astolat and seconded by the senator for Miaren, the motion authorised a research project into the origins of the vallorn, with the Civil Service compiling the findings for the Academy. The senator for Astolat indicated the motion would be self-funded, and the 5 Thrones required have been provided. Information about the vallorn is being compiled, and the resulting report is to be delivered to Bohemond De Rondell, Senator for Astolat.

Dawn.t: A Dawnish senator, Bohemond De Rondell of Astolat, proposed and personally funded the research and is to receive the finished report on the vallorn.

Research the vallorn for the Academy.o: In Autumn 378YE the Senate passed a motion commissioning the Civil Service to research the origin of the vallorn on behalf of the Academy, at a cost of 5 Thrones.

Astolat.t: Astolat's senator proposed the motion, met its 5 Throne cost, and will be the recipient of the Civil Service's report on the origin of the vallorn.

Resonance and mitigation.d: Æsa Sigeling called for investigation into mitigating the detrimental effects of Imperial enchantments, while Ariadne of Auric Horizon committed the Conclave to completing the omnihedron. Urizen stargazers hold that the benefits outweigh the costs, but other nations doubt this, and many fear the next ritual will align the Empire with Winter. Cold Sun's heralds have killed hundreds, and the magistrates intend to investigate possible treason. The Conclave could still pass an Endorsement to protect those involved. The Marchers are enraged and are quietly considering withholding taxes. Attention now falls on the Witness of Conclave, the Imperial Censor, the Warmage, the Warcaster, the Imperial Magus and the Archmage of Day.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's armies are noted as being deeply engaged against the Druj while heralds roam Imperial territories.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the peace treaty with the Grendel is noted as being about to end, adding to the military pressure.

Highguard.t: Highborn magicians question rituals that draw inhuman forces' attention and keep opening regio, making a Vigilant watch almost impossible. Cold Sun's heralds now occupy Bastion.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's armies are noted as being deeply engaged against the Jotun.

Navarr.t: Navarr vates watching for Terunael-like hubris have voiced serious concerns about the Conclave's motives and cautioned against such tumultuous seasonal rituals. Heralds now threaten Hercynia and Miaren.

The Brass Coast.t: The Imperial Censor, Cassandra i Periera i Erigo of the Brass Coast, is singled out as able to interdict the practice of Imperial enchantments. Heralds are also present in Segura.

Urizen.t: Urizen's stargazers champion the omnihedron and believe its benefits outweigh its costs, while the enchantment is widely believed to have been raised by an Urizen coven. Bryn Netherwatch of Urizen, the Witness of Conclave, is under close scrutiny.

Varushka.t: Many Varushkan magicians broadly agree with the stargazers, having suffered only minimal ill effects from Imperial enchantments, though heralds of Cold Sun now roam Volodmartz and Karov.

Wintermark.t: Armies of Cold Sun's heralds are now present in the Wintermark territories of Kallavesa and Hahnmark.

Resonance and mitigation.o: After the Imperial Conclave upheld declarations at the Summer Solstice 385YE to investigate mitigating the harms of Empire-wide enchantments and to complete the omnihedron sequence, magicians across the Empire questioned the Conclave's judgement. The questions were sharpened by the deadly incursion of Cold Sun's heralds, which was linked to Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths.

Bastion.t: Bastion is one of eight territories where armies of murderous heralds of Cold Sun are now present.

Hahnmark.t: Armies of Cold Sun's warlike heralds are now at large in Hahnmark, killing anyone they encounter.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia is among the eight territories where Cold Sun's herald armies are now present.

Kallavesa.t: Cold Sun's herald armies are now present in Kallavesa, posing a magical military threat there.

Karov.t: Karov is one of the territories now hosting armies of Cold Sun's heralds.

Miaren.t: Armies of Cold Sun's heralds are now present in Miaren, destroying what offends them.

Segura.t: Segura is among the eight territories where Cold Sun's herald armies are now at large.

Volodmartz.t: Cold Sun's herald armies are now present in Volodmartz.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Zenith is not named directly; the page refers only to Urizen's stargazers and an Urizen coven in general.

Restoration and renewal.d: The Senate asked for an appraisal of the Gardens of Pallas, a Urizen herb-garden sinecure in Iteri smashed and burned by the Druj. Rebuilding would cost 20 wains of weirwood, 40 crowns and three months, creating a Gardener of Pallas title. Lutomysla proposed optional improvements. These were specialised ushabti from the Crucible of Fate costing 4 Thrones, and a Nightwoven site in Proceris to grow realmsroot. Others were the return of Bleak Tower herbalists through a Urizen National Assembly mandate, and support from Fountainhome Spire magicians, which depends on Ossegrahn not being declared an enemy. A Sadogua herald held by Lumi of Wintermark could also be moved with Lumi's permission. All the options lapsed if not commissioned that Solstice.

Druj.t: The Druj had thoroughly destroyed the gardens and their ushabti, and the proposal sought to turn the lingering Night magic they left in Proceris to Imperial advantage.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel aggression is named as one reason refugees, including the Fountainhome Spire magicians, fled Spiral.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League appears only through Spiral, the territory from which the Fountainhome Spire refugees had fled.

Urizen.t: Urizen could regain its lost herb-garden sinecure, enhanced by ushabti from the Crucible of Fate. Its National Assembly was offered a mandate to persuade Bleak Tower herbalists to return to Zenith.

Wintermark.t: Lumi of Wintermark could allow the Silent Gardener, Sadogua's herald working at Lumi's Teahouse, to move to the new gardens and grow realmsroot there. Doing so would mean losing that benefit for Lumi's own garden.

Restoration and renewal.o: In Summer 385YE the Varushkan prognosticator Lutomysla Niegoslava appraised restoring the Gardens of Pallas in Zenith, which the Druj had utterly destroyed. She found nothing left to rebuild but set out several improvements that could be added if the gardens were recommissioned during the Summer Solstice.

Morrow/Ravion.t: Lutomysla visited Ravion to speak with the Bleak Tower's magicians and botanists. She found that most were unwilling to return to Zenith, though a few might be persuaded by a Synod mandate.

Zenith/Iteri.t: Iteri was the site of the original Gardens of Pallas, now wholly destroyed, and the default location if they are simply rebuilt.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Proceris was proposed as a new home for the gardens, linked to the Golden Cascade's irrigation. There nine mithril monoliths would harness the lingering Druj Night magic to grow realmsroot.

Morrow.t: The Bleak Tower in Morrow, founded partly by refugees from the ruined gardens, could lose some of its herbalists and Fountainhome magicians to the new gardens. Its own herb output would be reduced if the herbalists returned.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is named as the territory the Fountainhome Spire magicians fled because of Grendel aggression and echoes of madness.

Zenith.t: Zenith could see the Gardens of Pallas rebuilt, with options to give herbs to every herb garden and mana site in the territory. The Fountainhome option would also improve the general standard of life there.

Restore the Throne Room.d: Proposed by the senator for Astolat and seconded by Mitwold, the motion followed the opportunity described in the Dog days are over Wind of Fortune. The motion credits the Castellan of Spiral Castle and houses of Dawn with securing the resources. After the Summer Solstice, several citizens, including Tallis Hart, Berith Relieur, Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn and Morien de Carsenere, donated white granite, crowns and thrones. Once complete, the restoration reduced the cost of upgrading Dawnish congregations by one white granite for a year, to a minimum of one wain. Hugh de Veran would complete and publish historical research into the pre-Imperial monarchs of Dawn.

Dawn.t: Dawn's ancient throne room was restored. This lowered the cost of upgrading Dawnish congregations for a year and led to published research on the nation's pre-Imperial monarchs.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the Castellan of Spiral Castle is thanked for helping to secure the resources for the restoration.

Restore the Throne Room.o: In Summer 387YE the Senate passed a motion to restore the throne room of the Castle of Thorns in Withy, Astolat, at a cost of 15 white granite and 45 crowns. The work was completed.

Astolat/Withy.t: The throne room of the Castle of Thorns in Withy was restored over three months using 15 white granite and 45 crowns.

Astolat.t: The Castle of Thorns, a fortification in Astolat, had its throne room restored after a motion proposed by Astolat's own senator.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Castellan of Spiral Castle is credited with helping to secure the restoration's costs.

Restraint.d: Graciana proposed that the Senate hire mercenary patrols at ten thrones per territory each season, which would stop sweeping raids on personal resources but not attacks on commissions, named resources or armies. Alternatively, the Conclave could seek out whoever has been casting an unknown Autumn enchantment that protects Brass Coast territories, and have it added to Imperial Lore. Wintermark's Raven's Plight offered Gulnar's Eye as a reward for this. Freeborn families complained that the Conclave's deal letting Tharim feast on their mana sites and herb gardens amounted to raiding. They threatened to withhold taxes if such deals continued. Possible Synod mandates for the Brass Coast or Highguard assemblies would encourage tax refusal.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Graciana spoke with citizens who had endured years of Druj depredations.

Highguard.t: Jared of the Suns of Couros offered the Highborn Assembly a Partner of Greatness mandate supporting the Freeborn against the Tharim deal. If enacted, it would cut taxes from four Highborn territories through tax refusal.

Jotun.t: Recent Jotun raids into the western Empire informed the appraisal, which found that their organised warbands and armies could not be stopped by mercenary patrols alone. Tharim's knights are being provided to fight them.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Freeborn contrasted themselves with Navarr, saying they do not expect to sacrifice Prosperity to support an army.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn families resented Tharim draining their vervain and mana crystals under the Conclave's deal and warned they would withhold taxes over any future such agreements. Their territories had also been shielded by a mysterious protective enchantment.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Graciana spoke with Wintermark folk who had suffered Thule raids before the peace treaty.

Wintermark.t: The Steinr coven Raven's Plight offered Gulnar's Eye, a rare talisman boosting Autumn lore, to whoever shares the protective ritual so it can enter Imperial Lore. Graciana also drew on Wintermark's experience of Thule raids.

Restraint.o: Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra answered the Senate's request for an appraisal on defending the Empire against raids. She concluded that stopping all raids was impossible but offered partial measures, and Freeborn families warned against further deals with Tharim that drain their Prosperity.

Bastion.t: If the proposed Highborn mandate were enacted, taxation from Bastion would fall by about a tenth, rising further if the dispute went unresolved.

Casinea.t: If the proposed Highborn mandate were enacted, taxation from Casinea would fall by about a tenth, rising further if the dispute went unresolved.

Hahnmark.t: The Raven's Plight, a Steinr coven based in Hahnmark, offered Gulnar's Eye, an artifact found in the Deeps, as a reward for bringing the anti-raiding enchantment into Imperial Lore.

Kahraman.t: If the proposed Brass Coast mandate were enacted, taxation from Kahraman would drop by about a tenth, rising to two fifths if unresolved by the Spring Equinox 386YE.

Madruga.t: If the proposed Brass Coast mandate were enacted, taxation from Madruga would drop by about a tenth, rising to two fifths if unresolved by the Spring Equinox 386YE.

Necropolis.t: If the proposed Highborn mandate were enacted, taxation from Necropolis would fall by about a tenth, rising further if the dispute went unresolved.

Reikos.t: If the proposed Highborn mandate were enacted, taxation from Reikos would fall by about a tenth, rising further if the dispute went unresolved.

Segura.t: If the proposed Brass Coast mandate were enacted, taxation from Segura would drop by about a tenth, rising to two fifths if unresolved by the Spring Equinox 386YE.

Resupply the Quiet Step.d: Proposed by Sarvos and seconded by Upwold, the motion sought emergency resupply for the Quiet Step using 25 wains of weirwood costed at 7½ crowns per wain, on a pass-at-this-sum-or-withdraw basis. It passed unanimously and the monies were disbursed to Sarvos. After the Winter Solstice 377YE, Mirislav, senator for Sarvos, provided the 25 wains of weirwood. The Senate authorised the weirwood to be spent resupplying the Quiet Step until the end of Summer 378YE.

Navarr.t: The Navarr army the Quiet Step was granted emergency resupply, with 25 wains of weirwood authorised for its use until the end of Summer 378YE.

The League.t: The League's senator for Sarvos proposed the motion and received the funds, and Senator Mirislav later supplied the 25 wains of weirwood to resupply the Navarr army.

Resupply the Quiet Step.o: In Autumn 377YE the Senate unanimously passed a motion to resupply the Navarr army the Quiet Step with 25 wains of weirwood, funded at 23 thrones, 3 crowns and 10 rings.

Sarvos.t: The motion was proposed by the senator for Sarvos, the monies were disbursed there, and Mirislav, senator for Sarvos, provided the weirwood after the Winter Solstice.

Right now.d: The Child of Thunder, crewed only by its captain Artur di Sarvos, rammed the plinth of the Colossus of Sarvos and caused significant damage. Artur asked for clemency from one of three named bishops and was sent to Casinea, to Magistrate Karkovich. Conjunctions were identified to: fight the drowned dead in East Floes; rescue Black Thorns warriors and intercept Grendel looters in Lightsea; counter Druj raiders in Axmure, Lacuve and the Dawnish camps; stop Grendel flanking attacks in Screed and Apulus; and strike Feni warbands in Wood Heath and Birchland. Failures would carry stated penalties to resources or armies. A planned Jotun-related element in Sermersuaq and Segura was dropped.

Dawn.t: Druj skirmishers were harassing Dawnish yeofolk in Semmerholm and poisoning supplies near the Hounds of Glory and Golden Sun camps. Unless stopped, they would cut those armies' casualty-dealing by one tenth.

Druj.t: Druj forces raided Semmerholm, including a relief force from an unknown Tepel heading for the Black Wind army, raiders preying on Lacuve's yeofolk, and Chikad saboteurs near the Dawnish camps.

Grendel.t: Grendel troops were hunting Black Thorns warriors and looting Lightsea. Their elite skirmishers struck the Imperial flanks in Screed, tried to bribe the Wolves of War's mercenaries, and stalked Green Shields patrols in Apulus.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the accused captain Artur di Sarvos was sent to Casinea, where Anvil lies, to face Magistrate Karkovich.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun presence in the west of Sermersuaq was noted, and a planned Wind of Fortune element involving them was withdrawn.

Navarr.t: The Navarr egregores reported that Grendel heavy troops were hunting Black Thorns warriors in Lightsea. A conjunction offered the chance to let them escape and rejoin their army.

The Brass Coast.t: Grendel warbands had ransacked paradors, smiths' warehouses and avocado farms in Lightsea. Heroes could intercept them and recover the loot, with the Brass Coast egregores advising on its return.

The League.t: The League's great Colossus of Sarvos was rammed by one of its own merchant vessels. Grendel agents also tried to buy off the Wolves of War's mercenaries, which threatened to cost that army its mercenaries for a year.

The Marches.t: Feni warbands were ambushing Marcher households in Birchland and stealing food and valuables. The Marches egregores were the contact for a conjunction to strike back.

Wintermark.t: Drowned dead were rising in East Floes and killing those who faced them, and Feni raided halls in Wood Heath. The Wintermark egregores also reported Grendel stalking Green Shields patrols in Apulus.

Right now.o: Ahead of the Winter Summit 381YE, the Colossus of Sarvos was rammed by a League merchant ship, and the civil service identified Sentinel Gate conjunctions against threats across the Empire. Those threats were drowned dead in Sermersuaq, Grendel raiders in Madruga and Spiral, Druj skirmishers in Semmerholm and Feni bands in Hahnmark and Upwold.

Hahnmark/Southridge.t: Mentioned in passing: the snowy hills of Southridge were glimpsed in the in-character story of a Feni attack on Wymarc's Hall.

Hahnmark/Wood Heath.t: Feni warbands were robbing halls in Wood Heath, and a conjunction opened to Bjarwood so fifteen heroes could strike back.

Holberg/Holfried.t: Mentioned in passing: the climber Rihanna recalled once running the roofs and towers of Holfried.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: Conjunctions opened to White Cedars to shield fleeing Black Thorns warriors, and twice to the Plains of Lightsea to intercept Stone Born looters and recover the stolen goods.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: Druj relief troops were heading for Castle Rock and the Old Wood, and saboteurs were preying on the Ax Glades camps, with four conjunctions offered against them.

Semmerholm/Lacuve.t: Three Druj raiding groups in Lacuve Weald were hitting businesses, supplies and resource shipments, and three conjunctions offered a chance to stop them.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: Drowned dead were attacking the settlements of Kuujjuaq, Puvirnituq and Akulivik, each the target of a Friday-evening conjunction, and even the hylje were threatened.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Grendel skirmishers were stalking Green Shields soldiers, and a conjunction to The Bluehaven offered a chance to strike them and learn the fate of lost patrols.

Spiral/Screed.t: Grendel elites were harassing the Iron Helms and suborning Wolves of War mercenaries, with conjunctions to Calvar Field and the Gethern Expanse offered to stop them.

Upwold/Birchland.t: Feni warbands were ambushing Birchland households for loot, and a conjunction to Markwood offered fifteen heroes a chance to strike them.

Casinea.t: Artur di Sarvos was sent under escort to Casinea to surrender to Magistrate Karkovich and seek a bishop's clemency, and an engineer's report on the Colossus was due there too.

Hahnmark.t: Feni warbands were ambushing halls in Wood Heath at dawn and dusk to steal resources, and a conjunction offered a counter-strike.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the vandals posing at the Colossus claimed to be outraged students from Holberg.

Madruga.t: Grendel raiders were sacking Lightsea and pursuing Navarr warriors there, and three conjunctions offered a chance to intervene.

Sarvos.t: The Colossus of Sarvos was rammed and significantly damaged by the merchant ship Child of Thunder, and magistrates were still hunting its escaped crew.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: a planned Wind of Fortune element about the Jotun presence here was withdrawn, with details left to the generals' brief.

Semmerholm.t: Seven conjunctions targeted Druj raiders across Semmerholm. Failure risked reducing local resources by one rank and weakening the Dawnish armies camped there.

Sermersuaq.t: Over three months, unexplained drownings culminated in bloated husks rising from East Floes to attack fishing villages.

Spiral.t: Grendel elites were harrying the Imperial advance in Screed and stalking Green Shields patrols in Apulus, and three conjunctions were identified to stop them.

Upwold.t: Feni bands were raiding Marcher households in Birchland, and a conjunction to Markwood offered a chance to hit them.

Rimbaud eyes.d: Many League citizens moved to Spiral seeking opportunity, but election law barred nearly half of the newcomers from voting for the territory's first senator. Odhrin van Apulian, an ally of Kaliact, stood for the seat, while most orcs in Apulus stayed on the sidelines ahead of expected war with the Grendel. Kaliact suffered under a ruinous Urizen curse that threatened her fortune. Because the Urizen would not share the secret of the Block, commissions in Spiral needed extra mithril and cost 75 rings per wain. The Apulians chose to call audacity Pride and fidelity Loyalty, kept cunning private, and replaced retribution with dead reckoning. Not one newcomer founded a congregation.

Grendel.t: The Apulians were Grendel only three months earlier, war with the Grendel was expected, and orcs who opposed Kaliact stayed loyal to the Council of Salt Lords while many others in Apulus hedged their bets.

The League.t: The League took in the Apulians as new citizens, saw a rush of its people into Spiral chasing wealth and power, and faced a contested election for Spiral's senator. Its bishops and priests set up businesses there rather than congregations, while Apulian ideas of audacity and fidelity began spreading through the nation as Pride and Loyalty.

Urizen.t: A Urizen curse was ruining Kaliact's fortune, and the Apulians asked whether this cleared any reckoning the League owed Urizen. The Urizen still refused to share the secret of the Block, which pushed up building costs in Spiral, and they kept many congregations there.

Rimbaud eyes.o: Following Spiral's adoption into the League, the former Grendel followers of Kaliact, now calling themselves Apulians, settled into League life as citizens flooded into Apulus. A contested senatorial election loomed, building costs soared, and the Apulians adapted their faith to the Synod's mixed judgements.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Apulus was flooded with League settlers short of protected housing, and its orc majority mostly held back from choosing sides between the League and the Salt Lords. No League congregation was established there, so League citizens in Apulus received no liao.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: several citizens with Holberg names appear on the Spiral voter list, and Holberg-named priests put forward Synod judgements about the Apulians.

Spiral.t: Spiral faced its first senatorial election with a restricted electorate. A housing shortage and the need for mithril protection against the Black Plateau raised commission costs to 75 rings per wain, with extra mithril worth a fifth of the wain cost.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: citizens moving to Spiral from Tassato were exempt from the rule barring recent voters from the Spiral election.

Rings and crowns.d: Urizen, Varushka and the League gained the ability to answer Highborn mandates in their own assemblies, but the League refused all Highborn aid. The Seventh Wave found a Grendel espionage ring in Necropolis that relies on bribed locals. A proposed Highborn mandate would let the army root it out, and similar rings are likely elsewhere on the Bay. Isaac of the Silent Tide destroyed the remaining pillars in Clypion. The Hall of the Newborn Sun gave an original Atun's Ring for the Conclave to endow. Bastion's sacred city still lacks a design, and the League opposes it. The Court ruled the Virtue Fund withdrawals unconstitutional, and stipend motions will follow.

Dawn.t: Pontius Figures of a Dawnish organisation raised the judgement of rewarding seeking Virtue Fund money for Bastion's white granite, which prompted the Court's review. Dawn remains one of five nations Highguard may still aid.

Druj.t: The last major Druj miasma pillars in Zenith were destroyed by Highborn priests, ending the lingering aura they left in the territory.

Grendel.t: Grendel spymasters were found to have built a well-established espionage ring in Necropolis, using merchants and money to buy information from locals. Similar rings are suspected across the Bay of Catazar before the peace treaty ends.

Highguard.t: Highguard extended its peerless kinship across the Empire and uncovered Grendel spies in Necropolis. It may empower the Seventh Wave by mandate, and it was offered a counter-mandate against League involvement in the Bastion project.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the five nations Highguard can still offer its peerless kinship to.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar helped the Marches secure the borders of Bregasland, a territory the Jotun held.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the nations that have already received Highborn aid.

The Brass Coast.t: The Highborn offered the Freeborn their insight in Kahraman and their strength in retaking Feroz. Madruga is thought likely to host a Grendel espionage ring.

The League.t: The League Assembly refused all Highborn aid and denounced the Bastion project, with a mandate proposed to keep its citizens from helping. Ophelia's mission lets League priests answer Highborn mandates, and Sarvos and possibly Tassato and Spiral may harbour Grendel spies.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn working with Varushka are said to have found their own answer to the question of Thule virtue.

Urizen.t: Urizeni priests can now answer Highborn mandates in their own assembly, and Zenith is free of miasma. The Hall of the Newborn Sun gave an original Atun's Ring in gratitude, and Redoubt likely hosts Grendel spies.

Varushka.t: Highborn unconquered, magisters and wayfarers aided Varushka in seeking out the orcs of its forests and securing its eastern borders. Anastasiya Volkov's mission lets Varushkan priests answer Highborn mandates.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the five nations Highguard can still offer its peerless kinship to.

Rings and crowns.o: Highguard's priests continued reaching out to the other nations. The Seventh Wave uncovered a Grendel espionage ring in Necropolis, the last Druj miasma pillars in Zenith were destroyed, and the Constitutional Court stripped three titles of their power to draw on the Virtue Fund.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, but it lies within Necropolis, where the Grendel espionage ring is spread across the territory.

Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand.t: Mentioned in passing: Sanctuary is named as a place where visiting Grendel sailors could have been reporting to a spymaster.

Zenith/Clypion.t: Isaac of the Silent Tide led priests, exorcists, guardians and cataphracts to Clypion and destroyed the last major Druj miasma pillars there.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Mentioned in passing: the Hall of the Newborn Sun's original temple stood in Occursion before the Druj came.

Bastion.t: The grand project to rebuild Bastion as a beacon of the Way still awaits a chosen design and cannot yet be commissioned. The League Assembly urged its citizens not to aid it.

Bay of Catazar.t: Grendel merchants and navies have visited every Imperial port along the Bay since the treaty, and espionage networks are thought likely throughout its shores.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar accompanied the Marches in securing Bregasland's borders.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn offered their strength to help the Freeborn retake Feroz.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn offered their insight to the Freeborn in Kahraman.

Madruga.t: Grendel navies have been sighted off Madruga, and it is considered almost certain to harbour a Grendel espionage ring.

Morrow.t: The Hall of the Newborn Sun, refugees from Occursion now settled in south-eastern Morrow, offered a gift of thanks for freeing Zenith from miasma. Most of its members chose to stay in Morrow for now.

Necropolis.t: The Seventh Wave, resupplying here, uncovered a long-established Grendel espionage ring that uses bribed locals and merchants. It will be far harder to root out than an ordinary spy network.

Redoubt.t: Grendel navies have visited Redoubt, and an espionage ring there is thought almost certain.

Sarvos.t: Grendel ships have visited Sarvos and spies are likely there. Sarvosan priests led the League's rejection of Highborn aid and its criticism of Bastion.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: there may be Grendel spies in Spiral that Salt Lord Kaliact is unaware of.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato might possibly host Grendel spies, depending on whether the Salt Lords count it as part of the Bay.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Seventh Wave fought in the Barrens' liberation from the Druj, and Highborn are said to be talking with orcs there.

Zenith.t: The last of the Druj miasma faded from Zenith after the remaining pillars were destroyed, completing work begun by the Senate and General Asenath.

Ripple of echoes.d: Llofir-empowered Regrow the Land's Heart erased Freya's Garden and the Tower of the Scorpion and filled Ossium and Hahnmark with marrowort. This offered sinecures and a time-limited great work. The Wise Flower Chapter offered to fund a Spring herb-garden ritual. A darkness linked to the Night Below unsettled Volodmartz and Miekarova, where mine owners were offered Blackdamp's aid or the chance to oppose it. Magistrates found Starwood Roots Steading's cannibals gone, with hints of Agramant behind them. Igraine's Regio cursed the Castle of Thorns. Suaq traders reported unexplained curse coins. The song 'Painted' kept spreading, prompting a proposed Nightingale Chorus Wayhouse in Astolat to rally Dawn against the vallorn.

Dawn.t: The Castle of Thorns suffered a hostile, frozen regio curse, and a proposed Astolat wayhouse would rally Dawnish nobles and yeofolk against the vallorn, with greater benefits if the Dawnish Assembly named that fight their Highest Calling.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: marrowort grew over the charnel pits and mass graves left in Ossium by the fight against the Druj.

Navarr.t: Navarr cannibals of Starwood Roots Steading escaped Hercynia's magistrates. The Navarr song 'Painted' kept spreading, offering Navarr a proposed Thorn Singer title and a spring surge of pride in their oaths.
