Navarr.t: The vates of the Pool of Silver Clouds foresaw their own murders and the destruction of the Pool. They sent word that the attackers had to be stopped at the Verdant Grove, and the Dean of the Thorned Rose, Bledri Eternal, was charged with protecting them.

The League.t: The third band of attackers emerged in the foothills of central Locul in Temeschwar before heading for Miaren. A League character's marriage ring was also given as an example of a personal omen.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Prognosticator Ingvarn Thunderbrow wondered whether the mysterious attackers might have something to do with the Thule.

Wintermark.t: Attackers butchered the garrison of a Skymark beacon and marched on the Aviary of Ishal, where contact with seers including Maiko Greywolf was lost. The Raven Seer, Odelia Nelda, was made responsible for its defence.

Ruin.o: In Summer 385YE astronomancers reported two conjunctions: the Lock and the Key, entangled with the Web and the Spider, coming to a head, and a greater conjunction of the Wanderer, Claw and Three Sisters bringing violence, sorrow and family strife. Mysterious blue-sashed warriors were also reported moving to attack three magical sites in Kallavesa, Astolat and Miaren.

Astolat/Winterbourne.t: The Sentinel Gate was to open to the Gardens of House Cadence at 18:00 on the Saturday so heroes could protect the prime harp.

Kallavesa/Skymark.t: Attackers came south from northern Skymark after butchering a beacon garrison, and the Sentinel Gate was to open to Maiko's Copse at 17:30 on the Saturday to intercept them.

Miaren/Goldglades.t: The Pool of Silver Clouds and its vates were the target, and the Sentinel Gate was to open to the Verdant Grove in northern Goldglades at 18:30 on the Saturday.

Temeschwar/Locul.t: The third group of blue-sashed attackers emerged in the foothills of central Locul before threatening Miaren.

Astolat.t: A band of attackers crossed Astolat in a straight line towards the town of Weaving and the prime Harp of Astolat. The harp's destruction could derange the whole web of harps and disrupt mana production in the territory.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Miaren vates divined that they had to send a messenger to Casinea to tell the Dean of the Thorned Rose of their visions.

Kallavesa.t: Attackers emerged in northern Skymark, wiped out a beacon garrison and headed for Ishal and its Aviary of raven seers.

Miaren.t: The vates and the Pool of Silver Clouds faced destruction, which could only be averted by intercepting the attackers at the Verdant Grove.

Temeschwar.t: The third band of mysterious attackers was reported to have emerged in the foothills of central Locul.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: a Dawnish minor house was celebrating the victory in the Barrens when the attackers struck it.

Rumblings in the Gullet.d: A week before the Winter Solstice, a brief quake struck along the Gullet, causing minimal casualties and only partial collapses of a few older buildings in neighbouring territories. Strange stonework, coral and body parts then washed ashore, investigators vanished, and long-dead husks were seen capsizing fishing boats and pulling people under. Westerhal fisherwoman Ingrid Longsight disappeared. The husks were judged no military threat but a matter for heroes. Around a dozen threatened Reed's Roost in the North Fens, under Haylock Blackthorn's responsibility; another dozen harassed Westerhal, with Kjellen Saltmire asked to act; and injured survivors stranded on a sand bar in Stark were entrusted to Nekoda, who might learn the threat's source from them.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun-held territories of Hordalant and Skallahn felt a small impact from the quake, and the husks are likened to a Jotun warband in scale.

The Marches.t: Reed's Roost in Marcher Bregasland faced a band of around a dozen husks, with its Reeve, Haylock Blackthorn, charged with stopping them before they damaged the building and reduced its mana crystal output.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark bore much of the threat: Westerhal's fisherfolk in Kallavesa faced husk attacks and the loss of Ingrid Longsight, while injured survivors stranded off Sermersuaq were placed in the care of Nekoda, Claviger of the Basilica of Cora Holdfast.

Rumblings in the Gullet.o: In Winter 386YE a small earthquake shook the shores of the Gullet, after which coral-studded husks began emerging from the sea, attacking lone travellers and dragging victims into the depths. Three opportunities arose for heroes to confront the threat in Bregasland, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Reed's Roost in the North Fens was threatened by around a dozen husks; its folk prepared to leave, and failure to defeat the husks risked damage to the Roost and lower mana crystal production.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: The fishing settlement of Westerhal in the West Marsh was harassed by a dozen husks, risking damage to the fleet and reduced voyage production if they were not stopped.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: Wilda, a host of Sulkavaris, reported survivors stranded on a sand bar in Stark, whose treatment might reveal the source of the husks and how to counter them.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland felt the quake, and beaters from Greywater tracked a dozen husks heading for Reed's Roost, due to arrive a few days after the Winter Solstice.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: Hordalant is listed among the neighbouring territories that felt a small impact from the quake.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa felt the quake and saw fishing boats capsized and crews dragged under, with Westerhal's fisherfolk threatening to withdraw inland unless Kjellen Saltmire defeated the husks.

Sermersuaq.t: A missing fishing boat's survivors were reported stranded and in great pain on a sand bar off Sermersuaq's coast, and Nekoda was made responsible for tending them.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: Skallahn is listed among the neighbouring territories that felt a small impact from the quake.

Saint of Bees.d: Bees fled or fell torpid when Cold Sun attacked, sensitive to shifts in mana, and the loss was slowly weakening plants, especially herb gardens. The priests of Zoloto in Skoremujac said the bees must be reassured the danger had passed. Two remedies were offered: a Highborn mandate sending a priest with 50 liao to spread Prosperity ceremonies, and a great work to build weirwood 'regal hives' in Malimorzi, available until the end of Winter 388YE. Unchecked, the decline would penalise Karov's herb gardens and farms, then its forests and businesses. At the Spring Equinox 388YE the mandate enacted by Ada of Balthazar's Vineyard was upheld, and Lepidean Librarian Hazelelponi called on Lepidean archivists to research Kvetmir.

Highguard.t: Highborn wayfarers and grey pilgrims went north to aid their Varushkan kin, and the Highborn Assembly upheld Ada of Balthazar's Vineyard's mandate to spread Kvetmir's inspiration and support Zoloto's work.

Varushka.t: Varushka's bees, cherished symbols of Prosperity in its folk tales, were disappearing from Karov and neighbouring territories, threatening its herb gardens, farms and wider prosperity. The upheld mandate was expected to halt the decline and slowly coax bees back over at least a year.

Saint of Bees.o: After Cold Sun's invasion, bees began vanishing from Karov and then across southern Varushka, threatening the nation's prosperity. Highborn answering a call to aid Varushka joined the beekeepers of Zoloto, devotees of the exemplar Kvetmir Kvetmirovic, to find remedies, and the Highborn Assembly upheld a mandate to spread his inspiration.

Karov/Duzekani.t: Duzekani, where the scions did the greatest damage, reported fewer bees, and its sunburned state was named as the root cause of the problem.

Karov/Kamienczka.t: Kamienczka was among the Karov regions where fewer bees were being encountered after Cold Sun's invasion.

Karov/Malimorzi.t: Malimorzi's folk reported fewer and fewer bees, and the region was chosen as the central site for the proposed regal hives, a great work offered until the end of Winter 388YE.

Karov/Skoremujac.t: Skoremujac reported fewer bees, and in its northern vale of Zoloto the devotees of Kvetmir Kvetmirovic, whose own bees were leaving, shared their beekeeping knowledge and hive designs with the Highborn.

Karov/Wieliczka.t: Wieliczka was among the Karov regions where fewer bees were being encountered after Cold Sun's invasion.

Karsk/Kopevnost.t: Kopevnost reported deserted hives and few bees visiting the spring flowers as the decline spread beyond Karov.

Miekarova/Dupadealuri.t: Dupadealuri reported deserted hives and a marked lack of bees as the decline spread beyond Karov.

Volodmartz/Livardz.t: Highborn arriving in Livardz to support its restoration found deserted hives and a shortage of bees there, prompting them to take up the bee problem.

Karov.t: Karov was where the bee loss began after Cold Sun's attack. Unchecked, it would penalise its herb gardens and farms, and later its forests and businesses, while regal hives built there would restore its bees and boost its herb gardens.

Karsk.t: Deserted hives were reported in Kopevnost as the bee loss spread into Karsk, and regal hives could also be built in the territory to support its herb gardens.

Miekarova.t: Deserted hives and a dearth of bees were reported in Dupadealuri as the problem spread from Karov into Miekarova.

Reikos.t: Reikos's Highborn are no strangers to beekeeping, and if the regal hives in Karov were completed, Zoloto's bee tenders would come to help the Gardens of High Chalcis, giving Reikos herb gardens extra herbs for a year.

Volodmartz.t: As the bees vanished, plant health across Volodmartz began a subtle but worsening decline, with each generation of herbs in its gardens a little less potent than the last.

Salt lions.d: Five armies joined the Wolves of War in Mareave, all enchanted with Day magic's Clarity and aided by Summer citadels, bronze giants and Polemarchs of the Master Strategist. The Wolves, Eastern Sky and Fire of the South attacked, while the Granite Pillar, Seventh Wave and Winter Sun defended Clisearn's Imperial quarter. Four Day-enchanted Grendel armies, backed by forces camped in Fleisardh and by navies bringing supplies, repelled every probe. The Spring curse kept losses down: the Empire lost just over a thousand soldiers and the Grendel more. The Golden Winds had withdrawn after the poisoning of their wells. A battle opportunity followed at the Syagrian Haven to collapse the Icarion tunnels and to coerce the Asavean prefectoi Zarides into standing down the Quintian Spears.

Dawn.t: The Eastern Sky, with a great host of warbands under captains from every nation but Navarr, attacked the Grendel lines in southern Mareave, and Dawnish lives were among those put at risk by the bitter fighting.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: invoked in the Eastern Sky's orders recalling battles in the Barrens, and by a Grendel admiral who called the poisoning of wells a Druj tactic.

Grendel.t: The Grendel held their conquered three-quarters of Clisearn with four Day-enchanted armies and naval supply, and suffered heavier losses than the Empire. The Golden Winds fled after their wells were poisoned, and their navies began building a temporary beachhead beneath Icarion's cliffs.

Highguard.t: The Granite Pillar held a quiet defensive line in Clisearn, while the Seventh Wave's scouts uncovered the Grendel scheme at Icarion. The Seventh Wave's general may also pursue a Polemarch-offered opportunity to learn about Grendel military capabilities.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Winter Sun defended Clisearn alongside the Highborn, and the orc garrison of Rucraic's Redoubt took losses supporting the southern armies. Imperial Orcs with resources in Mareave could gain a stubbornness-enhancing boon from the servants of Cathan Canae.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: warband captains came from every Imperial nation except Navarr.

The Brass Coast.t: The Fire of the South left its garrison in Madruga, marched along the Bay of Catazar and threw itself straight into the fighting in southern Mareave, where Freeborn lives were at hazard.

The League.t: The Wolves of War remained in Mareave and led the offensive against the dug-in Grendel, bearing much of the perilous fighting.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar's general recalled liberating the Mournwold alongside the Seventh Wave.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky's orders recall Zenith, and the Icarion tunnels are thought to be remnants of an old Urizeni port near a former Urizen lighthouse.

Salt lions.o: In Autumn 388YE the Empire rotated fresh armies into Mareave and pressed the Grendel there, but the dug-in Salt Lords held their ground and no land changed hands. Highborn scouts also uncovered a Grendel scheme to build makeshift quays beneath the cliffs of Icarion and open it to attack from the sea.

Ayereed/Petrified Forest.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel avoided the desiccating overland trek through the Petrified Forest by bringing supplies by sea.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: The city-state stayed neutral, its Palace of Chains aiding neither side, though Seventh Wave scouts extended some attention there. Its stubborn neutrality remains a barrier to Grendel naval support.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: The main battleground: Imperial armies, backed by a Summer citadel on the border, probed Grendel lines without gaining ground, and the Grendel made no attacks into the Imperial quarter.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: Most of the Grendel host camped here to reinforce its front-line armies, and the cliffs along its coast had earlier been collapsed by the Hawser of the Drowned.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Grendel fleets were found building quays beneath the cliffs at the Syagrian Haven to reach inland tunnels. Unless the four active tunnels are collapsed, the Grendel could treat Icarion as coastal for a year and threaten the Apulian Way.

Mareave/Nadir.t: A Summer citadel loomed over Nadir, and warriors of the Queen of Ice and Darkness marched from it to join the Empire's armies and guard the orcs who live there.

Ayereed.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel navies shipped in supplies to avoid the desiccating trek through Ayereed's Petrified Forest.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: only through the name of the Bastion of Rucraic's Redoubt, a fortification in Mareave, not this territory.

Bay of Catazar.t: Grendel ships worked its waters below Icarion, dumping rubble to build temporary quays that the Bay's tides would wear away within a year. The Fire of the South also marched along its northern coast.

Madruga.t: The Fire of the South, previously garrisoned in Madruga to defend the Brass Coast homeland, left to join the assault in Mareave.

Mareave.t: No land changed hands: the Empire kept its quarter of Clisearn, the Grendel held the rest, and Beoraidh stayed neutral, while a Grendel plan threatened to make Icarion coastal for a year and cut the Apulian Way.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: recalled in the Granite Pillar's speech as land liberated with the Seventh Wave.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: only through the name of Rucraic's Redoubt, a bastion in Mareave, not this territory.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar's general honoured the Imperial Orcs who bled to reclaim Reikos.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Icarion tunnels may once have let vessels from Spiral dock beneath the cliffs.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky's general recalled shining the way through Zenith.

Say her name.d: The Wintermark Assembly honoured Yulia, the former Miekarova senator whom Varushka revoked for backing the Thule alliance that helped retake Sermersuaq. Seeing Varushkan resentment and Wintermark's acceptance of the deal, the Dragons of Otkodov said they would welcome a Wintermarker as Ambassador to Otkodov. If one is appointed, Wintermark warbands may enter the Silver Peaks to hunt Maarik the Golden Tongue. Eska, co-creator of the Liberty Pact, was also honoured, and for two seasons any fleet or military unit may attempt to Provide Prosperity to Rachensgrab. Sermersuaq's resources gain 22 rings for three seasons. The Sentinel Gate did not open to Kallavesa this season.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Eska Crowspeaker's citation praises her advocacy for the Skarsind Loyalty Congregation and Winterfolk traditions in Skarsind, now an Imperial Orc territory.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are recalled as the foe from whom Sermersuaq was retaken, and Varushka's condemnation of Yulia cites the enslavement of Jotun thralls by the Thule.

Thule.t: The Dragons of Otkodov, angered by the Senate's dominion motion and Varushkan hostility, are re-evaluating their friendships. They signal that they would welcome a Wintermark ambassador and would let Wintermark warbands hunt Maarik in their lands if one is appointed.

Varushka.t: Varushka's long-assumed claim to the Thule ambassadorship is in jeopardy, as the Thule now see Varushkans as resentful of their alliance. Varushka's disowned senator Yulia is meanwhile celebrated by Wintermark.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark immortalised two heroes, including its first outsider, Yulia. It is courted by the Thule over the Otkodov ambassadorship and a possible hunt for Maarik, and its people in Sermersuaq rallied together through a harsh winter.

Say her name.o: In Spring 386YE Wintermark's addition of Yulia Kasimirova Voronov and Eska Crowspeaker to the Chronicle of Heroes drew outside interest, prompting the Thule to court Wintermark and inspiring a possible relief effort to the former slaves of Rachensgrab. Inspired Loyalty also brought Sermersuaq a three-season bounty.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Mentioned in passing: the page refers only to Yulia sacrificing part of her Varushkan homeland to the Thule, without naming Mieriada.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The Thule-held Silver Peaks, whose loss Wintermark accepted, could be opened to Wintermark warbands hunting the Agramant cultist Maarik the Golden Tongue, but only if the Senate appoints a Wintermarker as Ambassador to Otkodov.

Kallavesa.t: The Sentinel Gate did not open to the Kallavesa Marshes this season, so the Mystics of Ishal held no goosewhisper ceremony there.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: Yulia Kasimirova Voronov was senator for Miekarova when she backed the Thule alliance that gave up part of Varushka's lands.

Otkodov.t: The Dragons of Otkodov are reconsidering their allies. They would warmly welcome a Wintermarker appointed as Imperial Ambassador to Otkodov when the post is re-elected.

Sermersuaq.t: Inspired by Loyalty mandates and tales of heroism, Wintermarkers in Sermersuaq stood together through a harsh, monster-plagued winter. As a result, every resource in the territory gains 22 extra rings for the next three seasons.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Eska Crowspeaker's citation praises her advocacy for the Skarsind Loyalty Congregation and the preservation of Winterfolk traditions in Skarsind.

Scarlet sands.d: Four Broken Shore armies had pushed north from Ayereed. The Naguerro besieged the newly finished Grand Lodge and demanded seasonal 'rent', while the Iron Gulls, Storm Sharks and Brine Turtles assailed the Fundindelve. General Ansleah's demands alienated Clisearn's former Grendel families. The Imperial armies, aided by magical allies, drove the Grendel back to Fioroult, losing nearly two thousand soldiers against comparable enemy losses. The Empire is three-tenths of the way to securing Fleisardh. The Lodge and Ruicraic's Redoubt removed the Uncooperative quality from Clisearn and Eoradal, and Beoraidh stayed neutral. The opportunity offers stopping a cliff-collapsing Winter boon, breaking a seal to poison the Brine Turtles' lake, extracting a reaver, and killing questioner Kester.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun had just been fighting the Druj in the Sarangrave before marching south to Mareave.

Grendel.t: The Broken Shore armies were driven out of Clisearn and back to Fioroult in Fleisardh at heavy cost. General Ansleah's heavy-handed demands also pushed Clisearn's former Grendel families further from Attar.

Highguard.t: The Seventh Wave marched along Carstag's Way to join the campaign, helped retake Clisearn and drove the Brine Turtles from the Tholdie estates.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Winter Sun led the counter-attack to defend Mareave's settlers. Imperial success, with a warband of Uthni youths joining them, began to win over the territory's independent orcs.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Naguerro's cousins in Hierro and Corazón are said to have rebuilt their pride with the aid of the Jotun.

The League.t: The Towerjacks marched through Spiral to fight in Clisearn and secure the Golden Pyramid Lodge, and some were invited to inspect the near-complete Ruicraic's Redoubt.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun marched through Zenith and the armies passed through sodden Proceris on their way south.

Scarlet sands.o: In Winter 387YE three Imperial armies, the Winter Sun, the Towerjacks and the Seventh Wave, entered Mareave and drove the Grendel invaders out of Clisearn, relieving the Fundindelve mithril mine and the besieged Golden Pyramid Grand Lodge, and pushed on into Fleisardh. A battle opportunity at Capstone Veld followed.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Beoraidh stayed neutral under the patronage of the Sarcophan Delves, welcoming both Imperial and Grendel merchants, which kept the Grendel from threatening the northern regions.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: The Naguerro besieged the Golden Pyramid Grand Lodge and the other armies assailed the Fundindelve until Imperial armies drove them out. The Lodge's completion removed the region's Uncooperative quality.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: The Imperial armies mustered at the Basalt Citadel conjured by the Lord Sorin. Uthni youths joined the Winter Sun, and the completed Ruicraic's Redoubt removed the Uncooperative quality.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: The Grendel fell back to Fioroult and the Empire is three-tenths of the way to securing the region, which remains Uncooperative and Under Threat. The Capstone Veld battle opportunity is set here, including a Winter boon threatening the cliffs and a seal protecting the Brine Turtles' lake.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial armies marched through Icarion's arid hills from the Apulian Way to Eoradal.

Mareave/Nadir.t: Six basalt towers from the Queen of Ice and Darkness's demesne appeared in Nadir's foothills, and a legion of white-bear warriors joined the armies passing through.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: Mentioned in passing: the armies moved as swiftly as possible through Apstrus towards the Apulian Way.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Mentioned in passing: the armies carried mud from their passage through sodden Proceris, which soon turned to dust in Mareave.

Ayereed.t: The Grendel land forces launched their invasion north from Ayereed, and the Empire hopes to drive them back there.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Naguerro once sailed the western Bay, and Fleisardh's cliffs, threatened by a Grendel boon, face the Bay.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks' general recalled the Imperial Orcs rallying to lift the siege of Holberg.

Mareave.t: The Empire drove the Grendel out of Clisearn and advanced into Fleisardh. Imperial successes and the completion of the Grand Lodge and Ruicraic's Redoubt eased the hostility of the independent orcs.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: only the name connects it, through Ruicraic's Redoubt, a fortification being completed in Eoradal in Mareave.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun came south from fighting slavery and the Druj in the Sarangrave.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Naguerro were once fierce sailors and a thorn in the side of the people of Sarvos.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the chill of the Winter fortress in Nadir relieved Imperial Orcs used to Skarsind's alpine climate.

Spiral.t: The Winter Sun and Towerjacks crossed Spiral as quickly as they could, pausing at Ballaghadruh. The oppressive power of the Black Plateau took a toll in night terrors and dark moods.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun marched south into Zenith to join the Towerjacks before heading for Mareave.

Schools and sawmills.d: The civil service tallied Sarvos 157, Holberg 153, Temeschwar 142, Tassato 35 and Apulian 2; the contest ends at the start of the Winter Solstice 385YE. Inspired by Holberg's popular sword academy, similar schools could be built in Sarvos, Tassato, Temeschwar or Apulus. Diora University proposed a College of the Arts in Cigno, which must be commissioned by the Winter Solstice. Veterans Lynada and Batheka proposed a Five Cities Military Academy in Tassato, allowing a third League army. The Sand Fishers finished their sawmills early and want a port at Misericorde, needing the Lakesedge Highway first. The Company of the Torch is terrorising Polseg in Vardstein Vale.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: a quoted statement of principle observed that Dawn and Varushka were currently winning the Semmerlak trade.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel invasion of Sarvos and the battle at Solen's Doubt are recalled, and about a dozen former Grendel have settled in Tassato.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: donations from Highborn citizens helped resolve Diora University's past financial troubles.

The League.t: The League's cities raced to finish Fransesca's contest and were offered sword academies, a College of the Arts, a military academy that could support a third army appointed perhaps by public auction, and a highway towards a Sand Fisher port.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is named alongside Dawn as winning the Semmerlak trade, and the Varushkans' role at the Black Plateau is recalled in a veterans' argument.

Schools and sawmills.o: With one season left in Fransesca di Matos' contest to see which League city invests most in itself, Sarvos narrowly led Holberg and Temeschwar. A renewed push for education opened opportunities for sword academies, a Diora University College of the Arts, a military academy in Tassato and a highway to a planned Sand Fisher port, while a changed mercenary company threatened a Temeschwar mining settlement.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers noted that no suitable port site exists along the Nameless River in Ennerlund.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Lakesedge Highway would begin at the Holmauer Gate of Holberg.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: A large orc-run sawmill was completed here, and the Sand Fishers proposed a port at Misericorde with discounted docking for League ships, reached via their settlement of Lakesedge.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: The Lakesedge Highway, a 30-wain white granite road raised above the marshes, could be commissioned here, with a Rebeshof Roadwarden to keep it safe and collect tolls.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: A Sand Fisher sawmill was completed in Utterlund's forests, though the region was judged unsuitable for a port.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Cigno is the proposed site of the Diora University College of the Arts, which would create the Dioran Muse and must be commissioned by the end of the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Apulus was offered the chance to build its own sword academy combining swordplay and philosophy.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: Batheka d'Apulian and other former Grendel have settled here, and Tassato Regario is one of two possible sites for the proposed Five Cities Military Academy.

Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale.t: The brutal, changed Company of the Torch has been terrorising the mining settlement of Polseg, demanding the riches taken from Lorenzo's Deep Pockets.

Holberg.t: Holberg's bravos flocked to the sword academy to study philosophy, the Sand Fishers completed their sawmills, and a highway was proposed to open the way for a joint port on the Semmerlak; Holberg stood second in the contest with 153.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos led the contest with 157 and was offered a grand Diora University College of the Arts, plus the chance to build its own sword academy.

Spiral.t: The city of Apulian scored only 2 in the contest, having joined the League after it began, but could gain a sword academy, and its wealth was credited with making a third League army possible.

Tassato.t: Tassato lagged badly at 35, but veterans debating at the Barossa School proposed a Five Cities Military Academy there, and a sword academy could also be built.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar scored 142 and could build a sword academy, while the Company of the Torch menaced a mining settlement and the Custodian of the Assayer's Guild was charged with dealing with them.

Scuppernong.d: The vines grew from Gawain's effort after Timinion Splitroot's death in 381YE to organise Navarr healers. Enis Splinterspear's statement, passed by greater majority, asked the egregores to walk the trods with the message. Steadings and stridings were intrigued but raised three questions. Who bears the costs of herbs and mana? Who should be healed, including foreigners and barbarians? What do vines heal: the maladies of the world, or making people stronger? An egregore will attend the vines' meeting at the next summit to seek agreed answers. Anything affecting how other Navarr treat vines would need a further Assembly statement. Separately, Avery Farkas will gather vines and thorns to rescue missing Marchers in Brocéliande.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Maire of the Leaping Salmon Steading asks whether a Druj slave is truly her enemy when arguing that vines might heal anyone.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel paymaster appears in Imma Heartshrew's triage dilemma, and Maire asks whether a Grendel merchant is an enemy.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Maire's suggestion that vines might treat wounded Jotun, to address the cycle of killing between Jotun and Navarr, provoked considerable anger.

Navarr.t: The egregores carried news of the vines to every steading and striding, and the nation now awaits answers from Anvil on funding, whom to heal and the vines' guiding philosophy before the vines can become a true Navarr archetype like guides, brands and vates.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: securing a lasting peace between the Thule and the Empire is offered as an example of the kind of malady a vine might seek to heal.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the out-of-character notes cite recent Urizen archetype pages, such as architect and sword scholar, as models for what a vines archetype would need.

Scuppernong.o: The Navarr egregores spread word of the vines, a proposed new Navarr archetype of healers, after the Navarr Assembly's Autumn Equinox 384YE statement of principle. They returned with three key questions for the vines to answer at Anvil. A conjunction also called Navarr volunteers into Brocéliande to aid trapped Marchers.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: A band of Marcher champions went missing along the northern borders of Elerael, apparently caught by a malignant threat other than the vallorn, and Navarr volunteers are called to reach them through the Sentinel Gate.

Brocéliande.t: A conjunction leads into the depths of Brocéliande, where Avery Farkas will gather vines and thorns to rescue a band of Marchers trapped by a danger other than the vallorn, after many champions pushed into the forest last season.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: a physick treating the sick in a surgery in Miaren is cited as someone for whom battlefield-focused vine practices matter little.

Sea-wood fed with copper.d: Winter Solstice successes broke the Grendel in Eoradal, where the Seventh Wave stormed the Gate of Storms using captured intelligence. Despite reinforcements from the Bone Nautilus, the newly raised Hamsin, Stone Born and Shamal ships, the Golden Axe led a direct assault on the Fundindelve, whose mithril had already been stolen by the mercenary Gaineamh Tine. Ehsan offered to withdraw his forces and cease hostilities if his people were recognised as foreigners, freed his remaining slaves, and offered a way to neutralise the Brine Turtles by stealing their eggs. Further opportunities included the Golden Portan standard, the mercenary Catella Cerularios, and Kimus's offer of scrying for the Citadel Guard.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: a Towerjack likens the Brine Turtles' relationship to the Grendel to that of the yeofolk and nobility of Dawn.

Grendel.t: The Grendel lost Mareave's northern regions, the Fundindelve and their hold on the territory, and their raising of the Hamsin exposed strain after Salt Lord Kaliact's betrayal. Salt Lord Ehsan has now turned against his peers, offering neutrality and to betray the Brine Turtles.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Winter Sun welcomed many freed Sannite slaves into the free Sannite sept and helped secure Clisearn, though some freed orcs hint at something afoot in Beoraidh's markets.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast's Towerjacks fought through Clisearn and then held it against attack from the west, while the presence of Catella Cerularios offers a chance at vengeance for the burning of Siroc.

The League.t: The League's Seventh Wave stormed the Gate of Storms using captured intelligence and carried the general's invitation to parley that drew Ehsan's offer of neutrality.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Citadel Guard joined the campaign, and the Unblinking Eye offers it a unique order to scry the lands south and east of Mareave if the Empire enchants five travertine pillars.

Varushka.t: Varushka's Golden Axe, reinforced by elfin knights of the Queen of the Pennants, led the direct assault that took the Fundindelve and then pursued the Grendel into Fleisardh.

Sea-wood fed with copper.o: In Spring 386YE the Golden Axe, Winter Sun, Seventh Wave, Towerjacks and Citadel Guard took Clisearn and the Fundindelve mithril mine, making Mareave an Imperial territory, and pushed two-fifths of the way into Fleisardh. Salt Lord Ehsan then sued for recognition of Beoraidh and Sinfoyard as neutral foreigners.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Ehsan's forces withdrew to defend Beoraidh, from where he offered neutrality, freed his remaining slaves and promised to send negotiators to Anvil.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: Clisearn, with its villas and mines, fell to the Empire after the Golden Axe stormed the Fundindelve, though the season's mithril had already been stolen by the Gaineamh Tine.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: The Seventh Wave took the Gate of Storms and completed Eoradal's conquest, and Vitore van Temeschwar must stop Grendel mercenaries fleeing the region with buried treasure.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: The Empire is two-fifths of the way to conquering the Brine Turtles' homeland, and stealing their turtle eggs could force the sept to disband its army.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Shamal ships raided Imperial supply lines in Icarion, forcing the Empire to pull soldiers back to guard its baggage trains.

Mareave/Sinfoyard.t: Ehsan's soldiers fell back to defend Sinfoyard, which he asks the Senate to recognise as neutral foreign land, and fleeing mercenaries aim to pass through it to Beoraidh.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orc town of Torfast is used as a comparison for the size of Fioroult.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Mentioned in passing: Ehsan contrasts his refusal to betray his ancestors with the conduct of the former Salt Lord of Apulus.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: violent storms from the Bay sweep Mareave, its brine turtles spawn in Fleisardh, and the crimson river flows into it.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: the Varushkan town of Ivarsgard is used as a yardstick for the size of Fioroult in Fleisardh.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Catella Cerularios's company aided the Grendel assault on Madruga and was present at the sack of Siroc, offering a chance at vengeance.

Mareave.t: With Clisearn taken Mareave became Imperial territory that the Senate may assign to a nation, and its Fundindelve mithril Bourse seat can be allocated, though three regions remain outside Imperial control.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orc town of Torfast is compared with Fioroult in Fleisardh.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial baggage trains pass along the Apulian Way, and Ehsan refuses to betray his ancestors as the former Salt Lord of Apulus did.

Seals and stars.d: Empty night skies persisted over much of the Empire, including Casinea where Anvil lies, so naga there and at the summit felt a strengthened urge towards secrecy. Skies were clear over Morrow, Spiral, Redoubt, Miekarova, Skarsind and Zenith, though a Penumbral Veil settled over Zenith again. Imperial citizens still could not draw on Spring regio, which made rituals such as Forge the Wooden Fastness impossible. Highguard's Blazing Sun coven raised two citadels, Wintermark's Sussivari Frost Coven raised four, and Urizen's Concordium of Pallas used a new ritual, The Immaculate Architect, to finish the Broken Ride fortification early. The hylje ended their raids and blessed Sermersuaq's farms and fleets.

Druj.t: The Druj were blamed, as Urizen saw it, for the renewed Penumbral Veil over Zenith, where Highborn armies were holding them back, and the stars stayed hidden over their Barrens.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the skies over Grendel-held Spiral were clear, and the Grendel were recalled as having enslaved Richard of Holberg when Evenstar fell.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Blazing Sun coven raised icy citadels in Clypion, aiding Highborn armies defending Zenith, and on Chalcis Mount in Reikos. Naga at Anvil in Highborn Casinea still felt the shroud's pull towards secrecy.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the night skies over Imperial Orc-held Skarsind were clear.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun-held Liathaven was among the territories still lacking stars.

Navarr.t: A Wintermark citadel of night magic protected the marshes of the Upper Tarn Valley in Navarr's Therunin. The loss of Spring regio still made rituals such as The Dance of Navarr and Thorn impossible.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: one of Richard of Holberg's past designs was a mithril dome in Segura that produced prismatic ink.

The League.t: A Sussivari citadel was raised in the Morass near Holberg, and Holberg-trained architect Richard agreed to design a mana structure for Tassato.

The Marches.t: Sussivari citadels guarded Ottermire and Grey Fens in Bregasland. Mournwold stayed starless but was chosen as one of the three sites for Richard of Holberg's mana structure designs.

Urizen.t: The Concordium of Pallas unveiled The Immaculate Architect to complete the Broken Ride fortification early. Zenith lost its empty sky but gained a new Penumbral Veil, and Morrow was chosen for one of Richard's mana structure designs.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the night skies over Varushkan Miekarova were clear.

Wintermark.t: The hylje ended their raids and blessed Sermersuaq, bringing bonus production to Wintermark farms and fleets there, while the Sussivari Frost Coven raised four citadels across the Empire. Sesi of the Suaq received a mysterious seal-folk gift he wished to discuss with his tradition.

Seals and stars.o: In Autumn 381YE the stars remained absent over most of the Empire and Spring regio stayed beyond Imperial reach, while Imperial covens raised magical citadels and the hylje seal-folk left Atkonaroq to bless Sermersuaq. Richard of Holberg offered to design three mana structures for the Conclave, which chose Morrow, Mournwold and Tassato.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a citadel of coiling mist, shadow and night magic in Grey Fens.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: A Wintermark citadel of night magic was raised in Ottermire to protect against the Empire's enemies.

Holberg/The Morass.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven conjured a citadel of mist and shadow in the Morass near Holberg.

Reikos/Broken Ride.t: The Concordium of Pallas used The Immaculate Architect to fit six months of work into twelve weeks, completing the grand fortification early.

Reikos/Chalcis Mount.t: The Blazing Sun coven raised an icy citadel on Chalcis Mount to guard the slow rebuilding against surprise invasion.

Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley.t: A Sussivari citadel of night magic was raised amid the marshes of the Upper Tarn Valley.

Zenith/Clypion.t: The Blazing Sun coven raised an icy citadel in Clypion to help Highborn armies protect Zenith against the Druj.

Bregasland.t: Wintermark's Sussivari Frost Coven raised citadels of mist and night in both Ottermire and Grey Fens to guard Bregasland.

Casinea.t: Casinea remained under the starless shroud, so naga at Anvil felt their urge towards subtlety and secrecy strengthen, though the sky directly over Anvil appeared normal.

Holberg.t: A Sussivari citadel was raised in the Morass, and Holberg's university was named as where Richard of Holberg trained as a magician-architect.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven was listed among the adjacent territories whose skies remained empty of stars.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: the night skies over Miekarova were clear.

Morrow.t: Morrow's skies were clear, and the Conclave chose it as one of three territories for which Richard of Holberg would design a mana structure.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold's skies stayed empty of stars, but it was chosen as a site for one of Richard of Holberg's mana structure designs.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt's skies were clear, and the fall of its spire of Evenstar to the Grendel was recalled as the place of Richard's capture.

Reikos.t: A Highborn icy citadel was raised on Chalcis Mount, and the Immaculate Architect ritual let the Broken Ride fortification be finished well ahead of schedule.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Richard of Holberg once designed a mithril dome over a granite structure in Segura that yielded prismatic ink.

Sermersuaq.t: The hylje left Atkonaroq and blessed Sermersuaq with full nets, plentiful game and safe passages, a blessing expected to continue through Winter.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the night skies over Skarsind were clear.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the night skies over Spiral were clear.

Tassato.t: The Conclave chose Tassato as one of three territories for which Richard of Holberg would design a mana structure.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens were listed among the adjacent territories whose skies remained starless.

Therunin.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven invoked the power of night to raise a protective citadel amid the marshes of the Upper Tarn Valley.

Zenith.t: The empty sky lifted over Zenith but a Penumbral Veil settled again, which Urizen blamed on the Druj, while a Highborn citadel in Clypion aided the armies defending it.

Search high and low.d: The Mournwold Breadbasket would need Senate approval and cost 15 white granite, 35 weirwood and 150 crowns over two seasons. It would give every Mournwold farm 36 extra rings a season and let the Marches support one more army once Bregasland is regained. Stockwater Monastery offered up to ten wains of white granite at 18 mana per wain. Anne Craig's Wayford alders offered ten weirwood for 28 thrones. Harry the Axe offered five weirwood if the Assembly declared with a greater majority that Alderly belongs to the Feni. A Keeper's Cottage could be built in the Mournwold, Upwold or Mitwold. Building both would open further opportunities.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun hold Bregasland, and Marchers are confident they will be driven out, as they were from the Mournwold.

The Marches.t: Marchers were urged to answer the Assembly's highest calling by completing the Breadbasket, which would enrich Mournwold farms and let the nation support an extra army once Bregasland is retaken. Several Marchers offered materials, though Harry's price of recognising the Feni claim to Alderly stirred contempt.

Search high and low.o: Following the Marcher Assembly's call to empower the Breadbasket, the Marches were offered the chance to complete the Breadbasket with a great work in the Mournwold, along with offers of materials from three wealthy Marchers and a proposed sinecure, the Keeper's Cottage.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Woodcutter Harry the Axe offered five wains of Alderly weirwood if the Marcher Assembly declared with a greater majority that Alderly Woods belongs to the Feni, some of whom reportedly still live deeper in the woods.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: Mentioned in passing: metals from the Ore Hills mines would supply the ingot income of a Keeper's Cottage built in the Mournwold.

Bregasland.t: Under Jotun occupation, Bregasland was ruled out as a site for the Keeper's Cottage, and the Breadbasket's extra army support depends on the Marches retaking it.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: many of the Alderly Feni who fled the Marcher attack are said to have ended up in Liathaven.

Mitwold.t: The Wayford alders wanted the Keeper's Cottage built in Mitwold, where it would give the Keeper 12 crowns a season, and offered ten weirwood for 28 thrones.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold was the proposed site of the final Breadbasket great work, which would add 36 rings a season to every farm there. A Keeper's Cottage there would yield 12 random ingots a season.

Upwold.t: Stockwater Monastery in Upwold offered its stored white granite, saved to rebuild its crumbling transept, in exchange for mana. It also offered land for the Keeper's Cottage, which would yield 12 liao a season there.

Second star.d: Captains who chose riches came home weathered but wealthy, each bearing one star-bright gem; any vessel enchanted with Golden Voyage may now join that option. Those sailing deosil to mystery were led on whimsical fetch quests and must continue one more season to reach unknown seas and gain a map. Those sailing straight on for glory were driven by unceasing winds but suffered grievous attacks from Asaveans, Grendel pirates and unknown foes, and must persist two more seasons; personal Summer enchantments are encouraged. Six buyers, including a Thule Dragon, Azoth, a Varushkan boyar and the Prince of the Argent Tontine, are offering to purchase the gems through Ephisis Boxes, but only this season.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel pirates are named among the enemies that attacked ships sailing straight on for glory.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Tathenon the Gyre, one of the Thule Dragons, has offered to buy all the Empire's Fire Rubies for an unknown purpose.

Second star.o: In Winter 386YE the great race of Rhianos, Regent of the Eternal Sea, reached its half-way point: captains who turned widdershins by riches returned to Anvil with treasure and a single brilliant gem, while those sailing deosil to mystery or straight on for glory were urged to stay their course.

Sea of Snow.t: Captains turning widdershins by riches were harassed by krakens in the Sea of Snow on their perilous voyage home.

Secret meeting.d: Meraud's herald Ethod warned that the Golden Magician was trapped and failing, and asked for the return of items he had made, including Urizen's Churnspire regalia and two rings. Sorin agreed to a strictly conditioned parley and offered an appraisal of one fortification or army for 160 drams of true vervain. Yaw'nagrah declined to parley but offered illegal boons. Estavus's heralds proposed clearing Pakaanan's Pass and finishing Curstag's Way. Zakalwe identified a chance to confront Jarl Haakon at the Sentinel Gate and offered gifts to Marcher generals and mana sites. The Whisper Gallery invited artworks containing secrets. The Prefects offered a Declaration of Concord on publishing plenipotentiaries.

Dawn.t: The heralds arrived at Dawn's Castle of Thorns, and Meraud's messenger could only come thanks to the Golden Magician's Fayre laid across Dawn by Phoenix Rising. The Summer Archmage, Mirella of the Twisted Rose, was to meet his apprentice.

Druj.t: Yaw'nagrah's herald said the Druj she escorted to Brocéliande were fleeing slaughter in the Barrens, and that she prefers some Druj to many Imperials because they reject the shackles of civilisation.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: a young magister at the Castle of Thorns was described as fresh from the seminary at Necropolis.

Imperial Orcs.t: Archmage of Day Gralka received Zakalwe's response, and Architects of Iron and Stone assayed the Jotun damage to Pakaanan's Pass in Skarsind, bringing an offer from the House of Fire and Flame to clear it.

Jotun.t: Zakalwe's emissaries studied Jotun strategy in the Mournwold and identified a chance for Imperial heroes to confront Jarl Haakon outside Farstrider's Watch, using the Sentinel Gate. Their earlier damage to Pakaanan's Pass was assessed for repair.

Navarr.t: Yaw'nagrah refused to escort the Navarr into Brocéliande, saying the children of Terunael can do that themselves, though she was interested in the claim that the Empire would connect the vallornhearts.

The League.t: A herald of the Coalition of Stone and Struggle studied Curstag's Way in southern Spiral, then presented proposals at the Palace in Apulian for finishing the road, along with requests that might have wider implications for the League.

The Marches.t: Zakalwe praised Marcher generals, especially Amberlain and Stanley, for putting their people's defence first, and offered personal gifts to all four generals. He also offered Marcher mana sites transformed by Carve the Crystal Guardian two pawns of prismatic ink.

Urizen.t: Urizen held three archmagecies. Meraud asked for the return of the Staff of the Storms and Mask of the Geyser, part of the Churnspire Adjutor's regalia, to help free himself from the snare that binds him.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Sorin's parley would ask the former Dawnish coven of Whelps whether they wish to bring the Empty One's power to Varushka.

Wintermark.t: Archmage of Night Eliina Lailasdottir was granted a meeting by the Whisper Gallery, and assayers of the Architects of Iron and Stone explored the mountains of Sermersuaq around Pakaanan's Pass.

Secret meeting.o: In Winter 386YE six eternals answered the Imperial archmages' plenipotentiary messages: Meraud, Sorin and the Whisper Gallery agreed to meetings, while Yaw'nagrah, Estavus and Zakalwe sent offers, opportunities or gifts instead. The Prefects of the Conclave also proposed a voluntary way for archmages to publish their plenipotentiaries.

Brocéliande/Terunael.t: Mentioned in passing: Terunael appears only in references to the Navarr as 'children of Terunael' and to the 'great work of the Terunael' of connecting the vallornhearts.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: Assayers evaluated the damage the Jotun did to the pass and how it might be reopened, and the House of Fire and Flame offered to take on the contract of clearing it.

Astolat.t: The heralds of the eternals came to the Castle of Thorns to deliver their responses, including Ethod with a Skyborn guard and Sorin's bone-masked herald Ossium.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe said the magical fortification at Graven Rock offered no opportunity like the one found against Jarl Haakon.

Brocéliande.t: Yaw'nagrah explained that the Druj she brought here were refugees and refused to escort the Navarr in. She offered illegal boons tied to the Empire's plan to connect the vallornhearts and wake the forest's trees.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova is not named on the page; at most it is touched by the parley question of bringing the Empty One's power to Varushka.

Mournwold.t: Zakalwe's emissaries assessed the Jotun here and identified a chance to confront Jarl Haakon via the Sentinel Gate, with a report going to the military council. They noted that the people of the Mourn are heartened when generals keep their promises.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the novice magister at the Castle of Thorns had recently come from the seminary at Necropolis.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only as that of Sorin's herald, Ossium, who delivered the Empty Throne's response.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is not named on the page and has no direct connection to the events described.

Sermersuaq.t: Assayers of the Architects of Iron and Stone explored the mountains between Sermersuaq and Skarsind, assessing how Pakaanan's Pass might be repaired and reopened.

Skarsind.t: Autumn assayers examined the Jotun damage to Pakaanan's Pass, and the House of Fire and Flame offered to clear it with explosive tools, as set out in Hammers and boxes.

Spiral.t: A herald of Shikal's Coalition of Stone and Struggle studied the coast and the work on Curstag's Way in southern Spiral, talking only with the labourers, before offering proposals to complete the road.

Secure Wunderkind Woods.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by Sarvos, the motion took up the opportunity set out in the Dear green space Wind of Fortune. It let the Rebeshi Players of Holberg cultivate the Blood Orchard in Holmauer Park, formerly Wunderkind Woods, and harvest both vis and wood from its twisted trees. It was to be funded by the Looking Glass, cost 32 crowns and take three months; Flávio Capra Gláucio van Holberg provided 4 thrones after the Autumn Equinox. The new title, Tender of the Blood Orchard, is appointed annually by unanimous decision of the League's senators. It liaises with the Players and may buy the valuable Winter vis, with access to a ministry producing Winter vis and ritual staves.

The League.t: The League gained a new Imperial title, the Tender of the Blood Orchard, appointed by its senators, giving a League citizen access to Winter vis and ritual staves from Holberg's Rebeshi Players.

Secure Wunderkind Woods.o: In Autumn 384YE the Senate passed a motion to secure Wunderkind Woods in Holberg, recognising the Rebeshi Players as Guardians of the Wood and creating the Imperial title of Tender of the Blood Orchard.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Holmauer Park, formerly Wunderkind Woods, became the site of the Blood Orchard, whose twisted trees the Rebeshi Players may now harvest for vis and wood.

Holberg.t: Holberg's Rebeshi Players were recognised as Guardians of the Wood and allowed to cultivate the Blood Orchard within the city.

Seeds of discord.d: Axos took Thornfen, expelled all former Druj subjects into Whisperwood and Kroll, and began salvaging Sephals to rebuild the Tower of the Skink. It asked for a Senate motion letting its slowly forming garrison defend Imperial Sarangrave, hinted at a need for mithril or weirwood, and offered lemuré research for 50 liao. A Grendel crew threatened a grounded Axou ship. Faraden executed Tommasso Triusti, the Asavean embassy left, and Faraden queried the Justice proscription. The Iron Confederacy proposed treaty talks for the Autumn Equinox but would not readily give up Free Landing or Cazar Straits. Tsark invited discussion of Prosperity, and the Marracossans feared prosecution under the Theist Heresy judgement.

Druj.t: Former Druj subjects were thrown out of Thornfen by the Axou, Druj guerillas from the old Tower garrison still harass Axou soldiers there, and the Halls of Maykop are studying how to counter Druj armies supported by the walking dead.

Grendel.t: A Grendel crew landed near a grounded Axou trading ship, and the Quaymaster of the Elosian Docks had to ensure fewer than a dozen of them survived to reach it, with lethal force judged fully justified.

Jotun.t: Faraden was to sign a new peace treaty with the Jotun at the Summer Solstice. The Iron Confederacy, whose invasion of Reinos was apparently faltering, offered mutual recognition of any Jotun land each nation took there.

The Brass Coast.t: The Iron Confederacy held the corsair islands of Free Landing and Cazar Straits and showed no willingness to return them, while Freeborn diplomats, including the new ambassador to Faraden, Mina i Yashum i Riqueza, carried much of the season's diplomacy. The Freeborn Assembly was also asked to reassure the Marracossans.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos was suggested as one possible site for dedicated Iron Confederacy markets.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Liege of the Five Winds sent thanks to former ambassador Ebenezer of the Marches for his work with Faraden.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are listed among the nations to which the Empire has an ambassador.

Urizen.t: Urizen was left to deal with the stateless exiles the Axou drove out of Thornfen into Sarangrave. Urizeni priests were invited to discuss Prosperity with the Tsarkoi adepts in Occursion.

Wintermark.t: Thanmir Hrafnar of Wintermark, ambassador to Axos, handled the Thornfen garrison and lemuré negotiations. The Wintermark scholar Marko Siwarsbairn returned from the Iron Confederacy, angry about Suranni censorship of their research.

Seeds of discord.o: A diplomatic roundup of the Empire's lesser neighbours in Summer 388YE. Axos completed its claim on Thornfen, Faraden executed an Asavean financier of the Cinders, the Iron Confederacy proposed treaty talks while keeping its Brass Coast island conquests, Tsark sent an adept to Occursion, and the Marracossans sought help over the Theist Heresy proscription.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The Iron Confederacy kept the Cazar Straits, seized from the Children of Wrecks, and said relinquishing them was unlikely to be on the table.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: The Suranni proposed a trading enclave in the town of Bramar, with a market and a temple to Evra the Smith. This was a proposal only.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Free Landing remained under Suranni occupation. A withdrawal might in theory be negotiated, but only at a very great price in money or materials.

Madruga/Torres.t: The Freeborn of Torres who have befriended and traded with the Marracossans may fear prosecution under the Theist Heresy proscription, and the Marracossans asked them to speak on their behalf.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: Mentioned in passing: Bendol was excluded from the area the proposed Axou garrison motion would cover.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: Mentioned in passing: a few stragglers among the people expelled from Thornfen ended up in Kroll.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: Mentioned in passing: Nesustak Forest was excluded from the area the proposed Axou garrison motion would cover.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: Thornfen passed fully into Axou hands. Its inhabitants were expelled, Druj guerillas continue to harass the occupiers, Sephals is being stripped for white granite, and a garrison is slowly forming at the Tower of the Skink.

Sarangrave/Whisperwood.t: Most of the orcs and humans the Axou expelled from Thornfen were driven into the Whisperwood, without supplies, shelter or clear legal status.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Tsarkoi Adept Camilla settled at the Garden of the Perfect World to meet Urizeni priests and congregations wishing to discuss Prosperity.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is not named directly and is touched on only through the coastal shipping and island affairs described.

Feroz.t: The Iron Confederacy held the Cazar Straits and refused to discuss returning them. The town of Bramar was floated as a possible Suranni trading enclave.

Kalino.t: The Iron Confederacy accepted that the Empire had no role in the Hand of Dumon curses on Arbonne (Kalino), where Imperial ilium was helping to build a warding temple. Marko Siwarsbairn revealed that a mithril mine there supplies Suranni armies.

Madruga.t: Free Landing remained in Suranni hands with only a costly withdrawal conceivable. The Marracossans of Trajadoz feared the Theist Heresy proscription would cut them off from their Freeborn neighbours.

Reinos.t: The Iron Confederacy's invasion of Jotun-held Reinos appeared to be going poorly. The Dukes offered to recognise any land the Empire took there in exchange for the same recognition.

Sarangrave.t: Axos claimed Thornfen and scattered its expelled inhabitants across the territory. It asked for a Senate motion so its slowly forming garrison could defend Imperial Sarangrave outside Nesustak Forest and Bendol.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos was suggested as a site for a dedicated market for Iron Confederacy ships.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: last season's Suranni request to resupply their Reinos armies through western Segura was recalled as having been refused.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is not named on the page; any connection is only indirect.

Veroigne.t: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni ambassador's seat in Chaubrette is said to lie west of Veroigne.

Zenith.t: Adept Camilla of Tsark arrived at the Garden of the Perfect World in Occursion to discuss Prosperity with Imperial citizens, with more Tsarkoi adepts and sages expected to follow.

Seize the fire.d: Proposed by Bonewall Rek and Bonewall Cole, the doctrines state that orcs live one life and either fall into the Howling Abyss or cross it to become Ancestors, with the Seven Virtues offering a path across. The Synod also kept orcs within the Way and appointed Atla as Cardinal of the Way. Preachers proposed converting Atla's Hall of White Ravens into a seminary, which the Senate could commission with Atla's permission. A Synod mandate could send missionaries abroad to explain the changes, especially to Jarm. The Sumaah House of the Way is sending Tipoa the Insightful to Necropolis to inquisition the two Bonewall orcs. This is likely a sincere inquiry that could help mend relations.

Highguard.t: Tipoa the Insightful asked respected Highguard citizens to help arrange the Sumaah inquisition, which will be held on Highborn soil at Necropolis.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Synod accepted the orcs' beliefs about the Howling Abyss and their Ancestors as true doctrine. Their preachers have proposed a seminary, and Bonewall Rek and Bonewall Cole face a request to submit to a Sumaah inquisition held for orcs alone.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the marshes of Kallavesa are cited as an example of the kind of spiritual centre the proposed orc seminary would resemble.

Seize the fire.o: After the Winter Solstice Synod adopted the Doctrine of the Howling Abyss and the Doctrine of the Ancestors, recognising the orcish soul within the Way, the Imperial Orcs were deeply affected. The changes opened opportunities for a seminary and foreign missionaries, and prompted the Sumaah to send an inquisitor.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: followers of the Way abroad are said to look to Bastion and the Empire for guidance on doctrine.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: its marshes are named as a comparable spiritual centre to the proposed orc seminary.

Necropolis.t: Tipoa the Insightful and a small staff are expected to arrive at Necropolis, site of the largely closed Sumaah Embassy, shortly before the Summer Solstice to conduct the inquisition. Necropolis is also named as a model for the proposed orc seminary.

Skarsind.t: If the Senate commissioned the seminary at the Hall of White Ravens, every Imperial Orcs congregation in Skarsind would receive 12 liao and a share of 25 Synod votes.

Seize the moments.d: With Ossium conquered and the Druj on the back foot in the Forest of Ulnak, the Imperial Orcs could seize the moment. Their Assembly could choose between a war of annihilation under the Summer Storm and a liberation under the Winter Sun. Ambition and Vigilance could add their blessings. The Great Forest Orcs and the Montanians might also be persuaded to help. Dawn could either shun the orc advance or issue an open challenge. At the Winter Solstice, Lochias's Vigilance mandate was upheld but lacked liao, so it was not enacted. Tobias Field's Dawnish challenge was upheld, granting bonuses to armies campaigning in the Barrens for the next year.

Dawn.t: Tobias Field of House Orzel's mandate was upheld. It challenges every nation to prove its claim to the Barrens by taking the most regions, and gives Dawnish armies extra natural resupply in Dawnish territories after campaigning there for at least a year.

Druj.t: The Druj, who hold the Barrens firmly, became the target of a proposed Imperial Orc campaign, with options ranging from their annihilation to inciting their orc slaves to revolt.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard's Reikos is noted as bordering the Heart of the Peytaht and as the target of a Druj surprise attack in 367YE.

Imperial Orcs.t: Bloodcrow Udoo's call to claim the Barrens opened two competing strategies for the nation's armies, conquest or liberation, each requiring the Summer Storm and Winter Sun to commit fully. The resolution does not record either mandate passing.

Navarr.t: The displaced Great Forest Orcs live in Navarr lands and have promised to fight alongside the Navarr, and their warchief Vallack was expected at the Winter Solstice as a Navarr guest. The Navarr guide Wyl of the Golden Pines urged the Ambition assembly to back the campaign.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun was stationed in Segura and would need to move to reach the Barrens.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm was stationed in Bregasland and would need to move to reach the Barrens.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: killing Druj in the Barrens is described as meaning fewer to brutalise the Urizen in Zenith.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the conquest of Ossium is cited as weakening the Druj and as showing the cruelty they inflict on enslaved orcs.

Seize the moments.o: After the Imperial Orc Assembly declared its ambition to claim the Barrens, this Wind of Fortune offered several assemblies mandates to shape a campaign against the Druj there. Dawn's challenge, that the nation taking the most Barrens regions holds the rightful claim, was enacted, while a Vigilance mandate was upheld but never funded.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The surviving Great Forest Orcs, who know how to bypass the malignant Heart of the Peytaht, are living in the Lower Tarn Valley and might be persuaded to aid an Imperial Orc incursion.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm was located in Bregasland at the time.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: the Heart of the Peytaht forest is described as touching Brocéliande.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were on the back foot here, and slaying Druj in the Barrens would mean fewer to ambush the Dawnish in the Forest of Ulnak.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: its recent conquest is cited as weakening the Druj and revealing their cruelty to enslaved orcs.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Reikos borders the Heart of the Peytaht and suffered a Druj surprise attack through that forest in 367YE.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun was located in Segura at the time.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens became the focus of rival plans to conquer or liberate it from the Druj. Under the enacted Dawnish challenge, the nation whose armies take the most regions there is to hold the rightful claim, with bonuses for armies campaigning there for at least a year.

Therunin.t: The displaced Great Forest Orcs and their Montanian allies have taken refuge in Therunin. The page notes it as a southern route into the Barrens if Dawnish territories were closed to the orc armies.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are said to brutalise the Urizen in Zenith.

Send for me.d: Graciana proposed restocking the Breadbasket with seed so the Keeper could send aid to a hungry territory or unsupplied army. This would need a vote of Marcher farm owners in Bregasland, Mitwold and Upwold and a change to electing the Keeper by Tally of the Votes, and it would cost farm income. She suggested the Senate create titles to oversee other great works. Every region of Feroz was declared impoverished and abandoned; Morajasse and the Cazar Straits were lawless and underpopulated, as was Afarjasse. She offered four opportunities: replanting Bramar's fields, restoring the herds of Afar, building the Inkworks of Joharra and building the Oran Wharfage. A conjunction tasked the Strategos of the Brass Coast with defending the Celesti Lighthouse from Isidore i Boyaga's raiders.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Harps of Astolat are cited as a great work that might have helped the Empire had it had an overseeing title.

Grendel.t: Grendel rule of Feroz is blamed for its ruin. Rahab looted the territory, Quartermaster Maeve wrecked Bramar's fields and Maistir Fionnula sold off the herds of Afar, and former Grendel were among the wreckers raiding the lighthouse.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the herds of Afar are compared to the more celebrated great herd of Skarsind.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; their only link is that Bregasland's Marcher farm owners were asked to vote on adapting the Breadbasket.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: most herb gardens are said to use companion-planting techniques the Navarr pioneered before the Empire.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn Feroz was found economically devastated and largely abandoned, with Graciana proposing commissions and new Brass Coast national titles to restore it. The Strategos of the Brass Coast, Gael i Guerra, was charged with saving the Celesti Lighthouse and could claim Isidore's ship, the Finder of Ways.

The Marches.t: Marcher farm owners were asked to vote on turning the Breadbasket into a tool for aiding devastated territories, at a cost to their own farm income. Their cattle-bonds could also help fund the restoration of the herds of Afar.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Urizen architect Majorian of the Verdant Tower is recalled for his unfinished almanacs on companion planting.

Send for me.o: Answering a Senate appraisal on seed banks and companion planting, the Freeborn prognosticator Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra proposed adapting the Marcher Breadbasket to aid devastated territories. She also set out the ruined state of Feroz and a series of opportunities to begin restoring it, while wreckers moved to destroy the Celesti Lighthouse.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: Afarjasse was found impoverished, abandoned and underpopulated after Maistir Fionnula sold off its herds. A 300-crown sinecure could restore them, create the Dhomiro of Afar to trade cattle with the Suranni of Arbonne and lift its impoverishment.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Under the Children of Wrecks the straits became lawless and underpopulated, and the Oran Wharfage was proposed as a way to end their lawlessness. Wreckers prowling these waters were raiding the Celesti Lighthouse.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: The once-golden fields of Bramar were ruined under Quartermaster Maeve. If the Breadbasket were adapted, two seasons of its support could replant them and end the region's abandoned and impoverished state.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: Morajasse was declared lawless and underpopulated, overrun by bandit groups. Only the area around Mora's Rock remains under the tight control of Gallum Fiersach.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The Inkworks of Joharra, a great work, could revive the region's ruined dye trade and end its impoverishment, and the Oran Wharfage could be built at Oran. Wreckers were attacking the Celesti Lighthouse above Oran's cliffs.

Segura/Lucksprings.t: Mentioned in passing: Lucksprings is not named on the page; Segura's only link is the Cerevado hakima supporting the inkworks.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the Harps of Astolat are given as an example of a great work that might have aided the Empire with an overseer.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: wealth plundered from Feroz was shipped across the bay to the Broken Shore, and a wharfage would let Oran offer cheaper dock fees than elsewhere on the bay.

Bregasland.t: Its Marcher farm owners were among those asked to vote on adapting the Breadbasket to support struggling territories.

Feroz.t: Every region was declared impoverished and abandoned, so no Synod mandate affects the territory and its taxation cannot grow while any region is lawless. Civilian commissions there now cost one crown per wain, and several restoration opportunities were proposed.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Graciana is a native of Madruga who hopes to revive the friendly rivalry between Oran and Siroc.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: plans already proposed for Mareave's herds served as the model for restoring the herds of Afar, and the Shepherd of the Southern Herd is detailed in a companion wind.

Mitwold.t: Its Marcher farm owners were asked to vote on the Breadbasket change, and their cattle-bonds could help fund the herds of Afar.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the Oath at Sunset, hakima from Cerevado, offered a Therasia's Chain each year to the Scrivener of the Inkworks.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's great herd is cited as more celebrated than the herds of Afar.

Upwold.t: The appraisal built on the Upwold Seed Exchange, and Upwold's farm owners were asked to vote on adapting the Breadbasket. Their cattle-bonds could also help fund the herds of Afar.

Sense and sensibility.d: At midnight each night a glowing, idealised miner struck the Ore Hills with a flaming pickaxe and left a rune of Feresh hanging in the sky. The vision faded by the Summer Solstice. Some saw it as a reminder of the 326YE miners' uprising and the push for miners to vote. Mine-captain Jedediah Boon was urged to have the uprising's leaders researched and recognised for virtue. Some Mournwold Orcs feared it meant they were unwelcome, so a delegation including Hap the Soft planned to attend Anvil. A Synod mandate was offered that would encourage young orcs to join itinerant harvest labour across the Marches. A few romantics read the vision as a love story.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Synod's view that the Imperial Orcs' understanding of their souls holds for all orcs is cited as the obstacle to the Mournwold Orcs joining the Marches, and northern Marchers are said to know only the Sunstorm sept.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold Orcs are former Jotun thralls who cannot go back, since their resistance to Eisa Winterborn's raid means many Jotun would treat them as oathbreakers.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the welcome the Navarr gave Great Forest Orcs settling in Hercynia and Miaren is contrasted with the Mournwold Orcs' slow acceptance.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: neighbouring Kahraman is noted as sharing the Mournwold's rich veins of green iron.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: news of the League's treatment of the Apulian Orcs unsettles the Mournwold Orcs, and Tassato's presses print lurid ringblack tales about the golden miner.

The Marches.t: The vision revived divisions over whether miners should vote, the status of the Mournwold Orcs and their religious obstacles. The Marcher assembly was offered a mandate to welcome young orcs as itinerant labourers across the nation.

Sense and sensibility.o: After the Spring Equinox 385YE, a nightly magical vision of a giant golden-haired miner bearing the words "Mine" and "Free" appeared over the Ore Hills of the Mournwold. It stirred old grievances over miners' enfranchisement, unsettled the Mournwold Orcs, and inspired romantic speculation.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: The wealthy farmers of Chalkdowns, raided in the 326YE uprising, still resent the Ore Hills' songs mourning the executed ringleaders, and old tensions are growing louder.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: Freemoor's farmers, on the opposite side of the old conflict from the mine owners, find the miner vision reviving grievances from the 326YE uprising.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: The vision erupted nightly from the heart of the Ore Hills, disturbing sleep and livestock. Its miners, including Jedediah Boon of the Boon County Miners, saw it as a possible rallying cry for enfranchisement.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Home to mine owners at the heart of the old enfranchisement struggle, sometimes called the Southmoor Uprising, Southmoor finds those rumblings stirred again by the vision.

Bregasland.t: Young Mournwolders, possibly including orcs, planned to seek seasonal farm work here, where restoring the land after the Jotun invasion promises plenty of labour.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the places where Great Forest Orcs were welcomed by the Navarr.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as a neighbour sharing the Mournwold's green iron deposits.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the places where Great Forest Orcs were welcomed by the Navarr.

Mitwold.t: Folk from Mitwold travelled to gawk at the vision, and young Mournwolders planned to seek harvest work on its farms. Orc labourers on the Black Canal linking it to the Mournwold had already begun to accustom locals to working alongside orcs.

Mournwold.t: The nightly vision drew sightseers and complaints about lost sleep. It rekindled bad blood between miners and farmers, and between the territory's human and orc neighbours.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: its printing presses churned out lurid ringblack tales about the golden miner, and it is rumoured among Mournwold orcs to take anyone in.

Upwold.t: Visitors from Upwold came to see the vision, and young Mournwolders planned to travel there as itinerant farm labourers.

Series of dreams.d: Stars stayed hidden across most of the Empire, strengthening naga secretiveness. Skies were clear over Morrow, Spiral, Redoubt and Skarsind, while a Penumbral Veil settled on Zenith. The Archmage of Summer apparently persuaded Cathan Canae to lift the storm over the Icy Crag, and a contest will decide its patron. Koboldi sent by Barien built the Empress of All Goats Theatre in Veresk for Hubert Annanovich Gremani. Magical citadels raised in Kahraman and Bregasland faded unused when no Jotun attack came. Urizeni realigned the Ribbon of Salt to Night just before it exploded, inflaming the Freeborn Storm navy's passions. Heralds of Murit and Soghter rendered orc corpses for the Azoth. Two rituals entered Imperial Lore.

Druj.t: The Barrens remained beneath the starless sky, and the Urizen blamed Druj invaders for conjuring the Penumbral Veil that settled over Zenith.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral, held by the Grendel, is listed among the territories where the night skies were clear.

Highguard.t: Casinea, home of Anvil, stayed under the starless sky, and in Reikos Llofir kept its living fungal castle in Tamarbode, which Highborn magisters judged to be playing a long game.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is listed among the territories with clear night skies, so naga living there were free of the shroud's influence.

Jotun.t: Their Mournwold and Liathaven stayed starless, the Imperial citadels raised against them in Kahraman and Bregasland faded when no Jotun attack came, and Night heralds harvested dead orcs from the Mournwold battlefields.

Navarr.t: The Eternal Family of Navarr raised a Frozen Citadel above Serra Damata, Navarr vates watched Llofir's Tamarbode warily, and a Navarr wayhouse sheltered Hubert while his home was demolished.

The Brass Coast.t: A keep of black ice guarded Serra Damata, and the Freeborn Storm navy, sailing off Redoubt, felt the Ribbon of Embers inflame their passions, fuelling sudden friendships and bitter feuds.

The Marches.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven's fog-wrapped citadels protected Bregasland unopposed, and in the shared Mournwold Night heralds harvested dead orcs and the occasional Feni.

Urizen.t: Morrow and Redoubt had clear skies but Zenith fell under a Penumbral Veil, and heroic Urizeni realigned the Ribbon of Salt to Night just before it exploded, leaving locals with strange dreams.
