Varushka.t: Koboldi sent by Barien demolished playwright Hubert Annanovich Gremani's home in Veresk and built the Temeschwari-style Empress of All Goats Theatre in its place, his reward for completing a challenge.

Series of dreams.o: In Summer 381YE a collection of magical happenings swept the Empire: the starless skies persisted over most lands, the storm over the Icy Crag ended, koboldi built a theatre in Karsk, and Llofir kept its fungal castle in Tamarbode. The Ribbon of Salt in Redoubt was transformed into a fountain of Night embers, and Night heralds harvested dead orcs in the Mournwold.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: A Dripping Echo of the Fen covered Grey Fens in fog and whispers to resist a possible Jotun invasion, fading when none came.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: A Dripping Echo of the Fen shrouded Ottermire against a possible Jotun attack before dissipating unused.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: The Eternal Family of Navarr raised a keep of black ice above Serra Damata, which faded when no Jotun attack materialised.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Scaled and feathered Night heralds emerged from Alderly's shadowy woodlands to harvest unburied orc corpses in bubbling cauldrons.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: Night heralds came out of Freemoor's chalk barrows to render dead orcs for the Azoth, leaving circles where no grass will grow.

Redoubt/Optarion.t: The Ribbon of Salt off Visten, realigned to Night by Urizeni heroes, exploded in shadows and embers, then subsided to occasional vents, with locals reporting peculiar dreams.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Llofir still held Tamarbode, whose living fungal castle enclosed the Sign of Tamar regio, and mana gatherers at Tamar's Toes told of watching creatures and strange moulds.

Bregasland.t: Dripping Echoes of the Fen settled as fog and whispers over Grey Fens and Ottermire, then faded when no Jotun invasion arrived.

Casinea.t: Casinea stayed under the starless sky, so naga attending the summit at Anvil felt their urge towards secrecy strengthen, though the skies directly over Anvil appeared normal.

Kahraman.t: A Frozen Citadel of black ice was raised above Serra Damata against a possible Jotun attack and faded once none came.

Karsk.t: In the vale of Veresk, twenty koboldi built the Empress of All Goats Theatre over Hubert Annanovich Gremani's former home, a tiny folly that drew growing interest.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven is named among the neighbouring territories whose night skies stayed empty of stars.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is listed among the territories with clear night skies, freeing its naga from the shroud's influence.

Mournwold.t: The skies stayed starless, and Night heralds of Murit and Soghter came out of Alderly and Freemoor to boil unburied orc corpses in black cauldrons, leaving barren circles behind.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt's skies were clear, but the Ribbon of Salt off Visten erupted as a torrent of Night magic and subsided into vents of ash and embers, leaving odd dreams and phenomena.

Reikos.t: Tamarbode remained claimed by Llofir, its ever-changing fungal castle looming over a forest closed to Imperial citizens except the mana site at Tamar's Toes.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is listed among the territories where the night skies were clear.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is listed among the territories where the night skies were clear.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens are named among the neighbouring territories still beneath the starless sky.

Zenith.t: The empty sky lifted from Zenith, but a Penumbral Veil settled over the territory, which the Urizen blamed on Druj invaders.

Serpent's tooth.d: After two earlier overtures failed, the Druj sent a third, unusually ordinary-seeming delegation, arranged to arrive at 11pm on the summit's first night. Their proposed terms: Murderdale and the Carmine Fields relinquished to them as traditional Barrens orc homelands, Dawn keeping Dawnguard and Drycastle; Fangs mithril traded for white granite (27 wains initially, up to 18 a season), though such trade is illegal while at war and would need a Senate motion and Bourse position; staged mutual army withdrawals; and the Great Forest orcs driven from Therunin. They sought at least five years of peace and stressed flexibility. Only the Senate could authorise a treaty, with the Imperial Consul expected to negotiate.

Dawn.t: Dawn was offered recognition of its hold on Dawnguard and Drycastle, but would have to surrender Murderdale and the Carmine Fields and reduce its presence to a single army at the Towers of the Dawn.

Druj.t: The Druj sent a high-ranking Tepel to bargain for Barrens lands they call orc homelands, offering mithril trade, staged withdrawal of their armies and a peace of five years or more.

Navarr.t: The Druj proposed that the Great Forest orcs be expelled from Navarri Therunin, either by the Empire or by two Druj armies that would then return to the Barrens.

Serpent's tooth.o: In Winter 380YE a Druj delegation led by a figure styled a "Tepel" came to Anvil under a flag of truce to negotiate a peace treaty, seeking Murderdale and the Carmine Fields in exchange for recognising Dawnish control of Dawnguard and offering a mithril trade.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: The Druj offered to accept Dawnish control of Dawnguard and Drycastle, a return to the long-standing status quo.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: The Druj demanded Murderdale be relinquished to them, with an army cautiously advancing to occupy it if terms were agreed.

The Barrens.t: The proposed treaty would partition the Barrens, ceding Murderdale and the Carmine Fields to the Druj while Dawn kept Dawnguard, with armies on both sides withdrawn over time and Fangs mithril potentially traded.

Therunin.t: Under the Druj terms the Great Forest orcs would be driven out of Therunin and resettled in the Barrens, possibly by two Druj armies entering the territory.

Set a twisted thing straight.d: The Granite Pillar, Seventh Wave and Valiant Pegasus launched a virtuous crusade beside the Eastern Sky, Wolves of War, Iron Helms and Citadel Guard. Scores died, but every Highborn felt inspired, and anointed Highborn gain extra heroism while fighting in Zenith. Proposed mandates could swell the Citadel Guard with Urizeni survivors if it stays until Zenith is freed, spur Highborn and Dawnish armies to race for the Barrens, or penalise armies leaving Zenith. Highguard's acceptance of Dawn's challenge opened Dawnish territories to both nations' armies with improved resupply. Unbound Winter spirits animated corpses around Winter regio in Clypion. Two conjunctions, at Lutum Descent and Kyrinian Spring, offered chances to destroy or ward these regio.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish Assembly's challenge was taken up by Highguard, so Dawnish and Highborn armies may pass freely through Dawnish territories to the Barrens with better resupply. A proposed mandate would let Dawnish armies make triumphant charges there next season.

Druj.t: The Druj were forced reluctantly to give ground in Zenith before a seven-army assault. Warding the Kyrinian Spring regio could drive Winter spirits towards their armies, inflicting perhaps 250 casualties.

Highguard.t: All three Highborn armies launched their first virtuous crusade into Zenith, inspiring every Highborn citizen and granting anointed Highborn extra heroism there. Their Assembly also accepted Dawn's Barrens challenge, with a further mandate proposed to commit Highborn forces to the race.

Imperial Orcs.t: Bloodcrow Udoo had declared the Imperial Orcs' ambition to take the Barrens, but the nation did not answer Dawn's challenge and no Imperial Orc armies attacked there.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr is noted as one of the nations bordering the Barrens.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: League forces are listed among the armies in Zenith threatened by the risen dead, and the League is noted as bordering the Barrens.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Citadel Guard fought alongside the Highborn crusade, and a proposed mandate could rally experienced Urizeni survivors and refugees to its banner, at the risk of mass desertion if it leaves Zenith before liberation. Unchecked Winter spirits could turn on Zenith's remaining Urizeni if no Imperial armies stay.

Varushka.t: The Iron Helms fought in Zenith as the Winter spirits once bound to them broke free, and a Varushkan cabal with that army proposed warding the Kyrinian Spring regio with Hold Back Frozen Hunger.

Set a twisted thing straight.o: In Spring 384YE seven Imperial armies, spearheaded by all three Highborn armies on their first virtuous crusade, pressed the Druj in Zenith despite stiff resistance, while the Highborn Assembly accepted Dawn's challenge to a race for the Barrens. Freed Winter spirits began raising the dead across Clypion.

Zenith/Clypion.t: Spontaneous Winter regio erupted across Clypion, sustaining spirits that animated the dead, and missions to the Lutum Descent and Kyrinian Spring were proposed to close or ward them. Failure could cost Imperial armies 250 extra casualties.

Zenith/Iteri.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lutum Descent valley is described as leading down to Iteri as well as into Clypion.

Morrow.t: The three Highborn statues guarding the passes between Morrow and Zenith inspired the crusade, and Urizeni refugees in Morrow might join the Citadel Guard if the Urizen mandate passes.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni refugees who fled to Redoubt are among those who might join the Citadel Guard.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens became the prize in a proposed race between Highguard and Dawn, with the nation taking the most regions holding the rightful claim, though no Imperial army had yet moved against them.

Zenith.t: Seven Imperial armies drove into Zenith against stubborn Druj defenders, while freed Winter spirits raised the dead and threatened both armies and the surviving Urizeni population.

Set in stone.d: Morale in the Mourn had been rising with the fortification of Freemoor and Greensward, Sarcombe's charter and the Singing Caves becoming a Marcher national resource. Then the Conclave backed the casting of Rivers Run Red, and the anger soon turned to weary resignation. The Mourners resolved to protect themselves. Richard of Holberg offered four options. Menhirs in the Mourn would give mana and halve curse casualties there. Protection for the Marches would halve curse effects nationwide. Menhirs in the Marches would quarter them and add mana. A Wonder of the Known World would add mana, farm wealth, a fifth-strength curse effect and an improved Imperial Breadbasket. The last three depended on Richard being alive, and he has since died.

Jotun.t: The Mourners accepted that the curse had shortened the Jotun war there, and expected the Jotun to return one day. That fear is why they want defences against the Military Council ever cursing their land again.

Navarr.t: The Navarr cast Rivers Run Red on Therunin with the Conclave's leave. Navarr travellers who tried to justify the need for it in the Mourn only fuelled the anger there.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the menhir designs come from the League architect Richard of Holberg.

The Marches.t: The Marchers were offered menhir networks paid from the Singing Caves' stockpile of over 100 wains of mithril. These ranged from protecting the Mourn alone to a nationwide wonder giving mana, farm wealth and strong protection against curses on any Marcher territory.

Set in stone.o: After the Conclave allowed Rivers Run Red to be cast despite its interdiction, the landskeepers of the Mournwold worked with the ageing architect Richard of Holberg to offer the Marchers four menhir proposals that would shield the Mourn, or the whole Marches, from curses. They hoped to pay for them with the stockpiled mithril of the newly allocated Singing Caves.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: Mentioned in passing: work to fortify Freemoor was among the news that lifted spirits in the Mourn.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Mentioned in passing: work to fortify Greensward was among the news that lifted spirits in the Mourn.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg appears only in the name of the architect Richard of Holberg.

Mournwold.t: The Mourn's people felt betrayed by the Conclave's backing of Rivers Run Red. Their landskeepers proposed menhirs that would give each farm mana and halve curse casualties there, which would lay to rest their last doubt about their place in the Empire.

Therunin.t: Rivers Run Red was cast on Therunin, and that casting reopened old wounds in the Mournwold.

Set my lands in order.d: Orcs of Skarsind, led by the Sannite sept, began moving to Mareave along trods extended by Navarr. The first Senator for Mareave was to be elected at the Summer Solstice for a nine-month term, by voters not eligible in Skarsind's last election. Salt-Lord Ehsan's Beoraidh will send the senator 10 crowns a season in gifts. Icarion is under-developed; Icarion, Nadir and Eoradal are arid; Clisearn, Eoradal and Fleisardh are uncooperative; Fleisardh is under threat; and the only land route runs through Spiral. The Assembly may each season send a different sept to Mareave. Ehsan offers mazzarine for dragonbone and poor land for a shrine. The Senate may allocate the Fundindelve mine, and Regrow the Land's Heart had little effect.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens is cited as a comparable territory whose integration takes a year or more.

Grendel.t: The Grendel are expected to try to reclaim Mareave, which they regard as part of the Broken Shore, and the Brine Turtles of Fleisardh still support an army in their service.

Imperial Orcs.t: The nation now holds two territories and will elect its first Senator for Mareave. It faces aridity, under-development, hostile southern orcs and a Grendel threat, and its Assembly can send a different sept each season to help settle the land.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Voice of the Quiet Forest extended the trods into Mareave, easing the orcs' journey south.

The Brass Coast.t: With its experience of dry plains, the Brass Coast is suggested as a nation whose Assembly could offer expertise to help reclaim Mareave's arid regions.

The League.t: The League, especially its Apulian orcs, is suggested as a source of help with moving materials into under-developed Mareave. Ehsan's opening haggle over shrine land is a move the League would recognise.

The Marches.t: As the Empire's acknowledged masters of agriculture, the Marchers are suggested as able to help grow crops in Mareave's near-desertified regions if their Assembly asks.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is cited as a comparable territory whose challenges take a long time to resolve.

Set my lands in order.o: After the Senate assigned Mareave to the Imperial Orcs at the Spring Equinox 386YE, the civil service set out the territory's challenges: an inaugural senatorial election, six regional and structural problems, a looming Grendel threat, and opportunities in sept mandates, trade with Beoraidh and the Fundindelve mithril mine.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Retained by Ehsan's city-state under treaty, Beoraidh holds the territory's only real port. Its factions will send gifts to the new senator, and Ehsan offered a meagre plot in its worst quarter for a shrine of the Way.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: Clisearn is uncooperative, its remaining wealthy Grendel and skilled miners resentful. It is open to assault from the south, and its mountains hold Fundindelve, a mithril mine producing 22 wains a season that awaits allocation by the Senate.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: Eoradal is both arid and uncooperative, with hostile Brine Turtles and former Grendel servants. The ruins of an immense Skouran aqueduct there could perhaps be rebuilt as a wonder.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: Home of the Brine Turtles, who still back a Grendel army, Fleisardh is uncooperative and under threat as a gateway for any Grendel return.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Icarion is under-developed and arid, raising commission labour costs and harming farms across Mareave, though its scattered orcs are cautiously interested in the Imperial Orcs.

Mareave/Nadir.t: Nadir is arid and sparsely settled, mostly by mining communities, but its orcs, many linked to the Sannite sept, are cautiously open to Imperial Orc rule.

Mareave/Sinfoyard.t: Kept by Beoraidh under the treaty, Sinfoyard's herb gardens supply the cerulean mazzarine Ehsan offers in trade for dragonbone. Its inhabitants are among those courting the new senator with gifts.

Ayereed.t: Mentioned in passing: some orcs of southern Mareave fled south into Ayereed after the conquest.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the treaty with Beoraidh guarantees Imperial access to the bay, albeit with tariffs, though this does not help move armies.

Mareave.t: Newly assigned to the Imperial Orcs, Mareave gains its first senatorial election and settlers, but suffers arid, under-developed, uncooperative and threatened regions, cannot support an Imperial army, and remains a likely target for Grendel reconquest.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is cited as a precedent for regional qualities that represent the challenges of settling a territory.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: a rebuilt Eoradal aqueduct is likened to the Colossus of Sarvos as a possible wonder.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: even Segura is said to have more water than Mareave.

Skarsind.t: Many orcs of Skarsind, especially Sannites, debated or began leaving for Mareave, while others stayed. Those eligible to vote for Skarsind's senator last winter cannot vote for Mareave's.

Spiral.t: The Apulian Way through Spiral is the only land route to Mareave, risking passage near the Black Plateau, and Spiral's inhabitants have first-hand experience of Ehsan's city-state.

Seven locks.d: A herald apparently of the Whisper Gallery invited the Archmage of Night and cadets investigating the Tomb of Achism to meet the Veiled Caballero. Kaela invited named groups to offer songs of death and proposed recruiting dying heroes into her Grim Legion. Basileia Brazen of the City of Locks offered knowledge for tempest jade. Adamant declined parley but offered to help build an unbreakable fortification in Segura. The Centipede General declined parley and pressed the Navarr to build it a fane. Roshanwe invited covens to discuss Combing the Beach. Azoth prepared a brew to realign the Terunael Singing Stone. Afterwards the Conclave paid tempest jade for intelligence on the Grendel's Salt Lords.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Adamant compared his promised Segura fortification to the unbreakable Gate in Semmerholm.

Druj.t: The Centipede General said it had already withdrawn some support from the Druj and would not favour either side in Therunin, though it would not stop them using rituals drawing on its aid. Arhallogen keeps offering his protective magics to the orcs while refusing them to the Empire.

Grendel.t: Basileia Brazen offered knowledge to help the Empire in its war with the Grendel. After a Conclave declaration of Concord, tempest jade was paid for insight into Grendel society and the Salt Lords who rule it.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's herald came as a Highborn cataphract bearing the banner of a long-dead chapter, and she disclaimed any interest in enforcing a claim to Rhonwen's Fall.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Veiled Caballero wanted cadets who had investigated the Tomb of Achism, particularly its connection to the Jotun and a missing archivist.

Navarr.t: Kaela is sending her herald Marcescence to help against the Folly of Terunael. The Centipede General will renew its boons once the Navarr build it a fane. Azoth, delighted by their acceptance of the Great Forest Orcs as kin, prepared a brew to realign the Terunael Singing Stone to the Navarr, though they must guard it from theft.

The Brass Coast.t: Adamant offered the Master of the Koboldi an unbreakable rank-two fortification in Segura, built in a year, if commissioned by Summer 388YE. Azoth took a keen interest in what the river's rise had wrought in Madruga.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Archmages of Winter and Spring are both of Urizen, and Adamant declined to discuss the Eye of Morrow.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Adamant's koboldi left Anvil for Karov to help put the final touches to the Great Hall of Fabric Arts.

Wintermark.t: Eliina Lailasdottir of Wintermark, Archmage of Night, received two answers: the Whisper Gallery meeting and Azoth's gift. Azoth told her it could not help close the destructive regio in Hahnmark.

Seven locks.o: Following the Summer Solstice 386YE, seven eternals sent emissaries to Anvil, apparently answering plenipotentiary messages from the Imperial archmages. Four arranged meetings for the Autumn Equinox and the other three sent messages, opportunities or gifts.

Hahnmark.t: Azoth said nothing could survive the light of the destructive regio in Hahnmark long enough to close it. It suggested gathering residues from other Cold Sun-tainted places and sending another plenipotentiary.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Adamant's koboldi headed to Karov to help finish the Great Hall of Fabric Arts.

Madruga.t: Azoth was excited by what the mix of magic, water and star-metal had created in Madruga after the river's rise. It noted that the conflux of Winter, Spring and Night there mirrors the Ring of Adversity.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is not named, but the Navarr campaign against the Folly of Terunael drew offers of help from Kaela's herald Marcescence and the Centipede General.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Adamant declined to speak of the Eye of Morrow.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela said she makes no claim she means to enforce on Rhonwen's Fall and advised letting it collapse into ruin.

Segura.t: Adamant offered that a fortification commissioned in Segura by the Master of the Koboldi could be built as a rank-two, unbreakable stronghold within a year, with its foundations infused with adamant. The offer is open until Summer 388YE, given the rising river, and can be invoked only once.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the unbreakable Gate in Semmerholm was cited as the model for Adamant's promised fortification.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Roshanwe's herald came dressed in the garb of a Suaq hunter.

Therunin.t: The Centipede General acknowledged the Druj had made a good showing in Therunin but said it was not inclined to favour either side in the fighting there.

Seven lords of virtue.d: Lady Madrianna of the Blue Stones made the request on the Plenum's behalf, with the priests Hueva Joãon, Caesli Onorato and Olybrius Pancratius. It was Asavea's third attempt and first formal one. The Asaveans would build a minor or major temple in a coastal Bay of Catazar region with their own white granite, local paid labour and free staff. The Empire could then build a temple of similar size in Nemoria, needing 10 or 20 wains of white granite plus Thrones, which the Joãon family offered to waive. Either the Senate or a civilian commissioner could act. Building the temples would improve diplomacy, trade in gloaming and orichalcum, and create liaison roles.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but the Asaveans would only build in the Sarvos regions if that territory, then held by Grendel, returned to Imperial hands.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Asaveans said they would prefer to avoid building their temple in Highguard's Necropolis.

The Brass Coast.t: Most of the proposed sites for the Asavean temple lie in the Brass Coast's Feroz and Madruga, with Siroc Plains the Asaveans' particular preference. That makes the nation central to where the temple and its trade benefits might be based.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League's Sarvos regions of Bocche, Uccelini and especially Cigno would be acceptable sites, but only if Sarvos were back in Imperial hands.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Naris, in Redoubt, was named as one of the coastal regions where the Asaveans would be willing to build their temple.

Seven lords of virtue.o: In Spring 380YE the Asavean Plenum petitioned the Senate for permission to build a temple to Balo of the Foam and the Black Bull on the Bay of Catazar. In return it offered to let the Empire build a temple of the Way in Nemoria.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Cazar Straits was listed as a suitable coastal site for the proposed Asavean temple.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Fontargenta was listed as a suitable coastal site for the proposed Asavean temple.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Oranseri was listed as a suitable coastal site for the proposed Asavean temple.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: Calvos Sound was listed as a suitable coastal site for the proposed Asavean temple.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Free Landing was listed as a suitable coastal site for the proposed Asavean temple.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: Lightsea was listed as a suitable coastal site for the proposed Asavean temple.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Naris was the one Urizeni region the Asaveans named as a suitable site for their temple.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: Bocche would be an acceptable temple site, but only if Sarvos were back in Imperial hands.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Cigno was the Asaveans' ideal site in Sarvos, should the territory return to Imperial hands.

Sarvos/Uccelini.t: Uccelini would be an acceptable temple site, but only if Sarvos were back in Imperial hands.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Asaveans asked to build their temple in a coastal region on the Bay of Catazar, which would bring better trade with Nemoria for Imperial ships.

Feroz.t: Three of Feroz's regions, Cazar Straits, Fontargenta and Oranseri, were listed as suitable sites for the proposed Asavean temple.

Madruga.t: Madruga offered several suitable sites, and its Siroc Plains was the Asaveans' especially favoured location for their temple.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Asaveans said they would prefer to avoid building their temple in Necropolis.

Redoubt.t: Naris in Redoubt was named as one of the regions where the Asaveans would accept building their temple.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos was then held by Grendel and the League. The Asaveans would build in Bocche, Uccelini or ideally Cigno only if the territory returned to Imperial hands.

Shadow in the grass.d: Imperial heroes destroyed all four Falconer pillars and slew three of its four Voices. Only the Voice of the Fount survived, fleeing powerless into the wastes, while scattered cultists remain. Big Icebarn was supported by over 24,000 strength, but fewer than 7,000 came from Wintermark, and it was forced back into Sydanjaa. It still drew out the Ceaseless Hunter and the Feasting Lord. Conjunctions to slay them fall to Ceolmund Dreth and Maryc of House Orzel. The Hunt the Suaq Wastes venture now yields rings, Wasteland vis and, for strong units, interdicted Keen Lifeblood. Eawyn Icerunner's crossing of Nutjuitoq opened options to scout or appraise Tsirku.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes there are no Jotun armies in Sermersuaq and that the Suaq Wastes' monsters have plagued the land since it was lost to the Jotun in 382YE.

Thule.t: Thule forces killed the Voice of the Peaks and dealt with the Falconer pillar in the north-east mountains, playing their part in the cult's defeat.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's heroes and their allies emphatically defeated the Cult of the Falconer. However, the nation's small share of support for Big Icebarn saw the artok driven back north, and its Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq, Ceolmund Dreth, must now lead heroes to slay the Ceaseless Hunter.

Shadow in the grass.o: In Winter 387YE Sermersuaq emerged from its recent crises: the Cult of the Falconer was broken, Big Icebarn was driven back into Sydanjaa, and two of Agramant's heralds were exposed in the Suaq Wastes. The civil service also confirmed that the Empire could build a spy network in, or appraise, the unknown territory of Tsirku.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: Two conjunctions offer the chance to kill Agramant's last great guardians in the Wastes, the Ceaseless Hunter and the Feasting Lord. The Hunt the Suaq Wastes venture now rewards units with rings, Wasteland vis and, for the strongest, Keen Lifeblood.

Sermersuaq.t: The territory has been largely freed from the Falconer cult and the Winter monsters, though cultist remnants and more aggressive beasts still trouble remote halls, held in check by the garrisons of Olgafsdottirshal and the Fortress of Kalant.

Tsirku.t: Tsirku, a storm-wracked wasteland beyond the inland sea of Nutjuitoq, could now host an Imperial spy network or be appraised for exploitation. Neither option would reveal anything about Sydanjaa.

Shadow in the west.d: Jotun raids, rumoured to be intensifying at the Spring Equinox, hit Bregasland, Mitwold and Upwold, the lands around Meade and Tassato, and halls in western Sermersuaq and Kallavesa. Imperial armies in Sermersuaq destroyed two warbands. The units at Fort Braydon in Kahraman, reinforced by crystal warriors under Anwar i Del Toro i Riqueza, caught a Jotun scout who revealed that probing attacks on Mitwold and Kahraman would continue while major raids targeted Kallavesa, Bregasland, Upwold and Tassato. These threatened heavy losses of production there. The Red Wind Corsairs, Winter Sun, Fist of the Mountains and Hounds of Glory were sent to these four territories and blunted the raids through several skirmishes. Historians warned such raids often precede war.

Jotun.t: Jotun warbands raided across the Imperial border from the Mournwold, lost two warbands in Sermersuaq and a captured scout. Their planned major raids were then blunted by the Imperial armies sent against them.

The Brass Coast.t: Fort Braydon's garrison in Kahraman, aided by crystal warriors under Anwar i Del Toro i Riqueza, intercepted the Jotun scout whose interrogation revealed the enemy's plans.

The League.t: The lands around Tassato were plagued by raids, and the city's territory was named as a target for major Jotun raids that threatened all its production before the Hounds of Glory were sent to defend it.

The Marches.t: Marcher farmsteads in Bregasland, Mitwold and Upwold were raided, and Bregasland and Upwold faced major raids threatening their production until Imperial armies were sent there.

Wintermark.t: Jotun attacked halls in western Sermersuaq and Kallavesa. Imperial armies wiped out two warbands in Sermersuaq, while Kallavesa faced major raids until the Red Wind Corsairs defended it.

Shadow in the west.o: In Summer 379YE Jotun raiders struck farmsteads and halls along the Empire's western border, from the Marches to Tassato and western Wintermark. The interrogation of a captured Jotun scout revealed plans for major raids on Kallavesa, Bregasland, Upwold and Tassato, and Imperial armies were sent to blunt them.

Mitwold/Golden Downs.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named on the page, which only reports Jotun raids on Mitwold farmsteads and the protection of Forte Fidelis across the territory.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland farmsteads were raided and the territory was targeted for major raids threatening all production, but the Winter Sun's presence blunted the attacks.

Kahraman.t: Fort Braydon's units intercepted a Jotun scout here. Probing attacks were expected to continue, but the fortification was enough to protect Kahraman provided the raids did not worsen.

Kallavesa.t: Jotun attacked halls in Kallavesa, and it was named as a target for major raids threatening every business, farm, forest, mine and herb garden until the Red Wind Corsairs blunted them.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold farmsteads were raided and probing attacks were expected to continue, but Forte Fidelis was sufficient to protect the territory provided the raids did not grow worse.

Mournwold.t: The Jotun raiders struck from the Mournwold and retreated back over the border into it after attacking Marcher farmsteads.

Sermersuaq.t: Halls in western Sermersuaq were attacked, but the Imperial armies stationed there cornered and wiped out two Jotun warbands and protected the territory.

Tassato.t: The city of Tassato stayed safe but its surrounding lands were plagued by raids. Major raids threatening its production were blunted by the Hounds of Glory.

Upwold.t: Upwold farmsteads were raided and the Eastern Guard was too far from the border to help, but the Fist of the Mountains was sent to blunt the major raids planned there.

Shadowed boughs of twilight.d: Everyone in Ossium dreamed of fantastical forests. Some woke injured, and around two dozen magicians vanished. Off-road travellers got lost and many never returned. Sung's heralds sang a threnody at the Field of Glory and posed questions on grief and forgetting to the Varushkan and Navarr assemblies. A boggart-like infestation drained the Towers of Zulgan Tash garrison to zero, which cannot recover until the curse is lifted. Azoth offered to take the Palace of Orieb for a year. Dubik attacks will cut forest output. Wisdom dreamers learned that the Dubik and the Stranger walk Ossium, and the Thule protested the enchantment's effect on their forests.

Dawn.t: Dawnish military units joining the Protect the Vales of Varushka venture after the Autumn Equinox will receive extra consumable rewards from the frightened vales, alongside their usual production.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is recalled as once held in the Druj's iron fist, the Palace of Orieb's shrines were built for Druj ghulai, and Kaela's Gift lets Imperial captives escape Druj defilement.

Navarr.t: The Navarr of Awstin's Rest and Navarr-held forests in Ossium share the dreams, the dangers and the dubik losses. The Navarr National Assembly is invited to answer Sung's questions on grief and being forgotten in return for possible boons.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: some dreamers in Ossium saw waterlogged willows and mangroves reminiscent of the Siroc Bayou.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the Rat King of Temeschwar is listed among the known sovereigns of Varushka.

Thule.t: The Thule-held Bonewood and Webwood were shrouded by the enchantment. Through their ambassador Runa they expressed significant dissatisfaction and expect the Empire to deal with those responsible, while the Stranger reportedly seeks to poison relations between Thule and Varushkans.

Varushka.t: Varushka's people in Ossium faced dreams, disappearances, lost travellers, dubik raids and a forgotten garrison at the Towers of Zulgan Tash. Its assembly was offered Sung's questions and a chapel boon at the Field of Glory, and its Wise learned that the Dubik and the Stranger are loose in Ossium.

Shadowed boughs of twilight.o: In Autumn 388YE an enchantment of Wondrous Forest magic spread across Ossium after the Summer Solstice, bringing strange dreams, treacherous woodlands, the attention of Night eternals, and stirring Varushkan sovereigns such as the Dubik and the Stranger.

Karsk/Moresvah.t: A servant of Undertow emerged from the Semmerlak on a wet night to warn a cabalist in Moresvah of the approaching Mirk Lizards.

Madruga/Siroc Bayou.t: Mentioned in passing: dreamers in Ossium saw waterlogged willows and mangroves reminiscent of the Siroc Bayou.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: Bittershore's open lands were spared the woodland disorientation. Bandits who robbed a trader bound for Kostjyas Respite are to be brought to justice by the Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore, Kostjya, with a twelve-crown pledge offered, and Agramant's messenger shouted his approval at Kostjyas Respite's walls.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: This Thule-held forest was shrouded by the enchantment, and dubik are rumoured to be gathering there. The Academy's cadets are tasked with aiding an injured patrol in Bonewood that nobody remembers setting out.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: The Towers of Zulgan Tash here lost their entire garrison to a memory-eating curse that needs Piercing Light of Revelation at magnitude 60 to lift, and Azoth offered to take the Palace of Orieb for a year. Dho'uala's servants and dubik also troubled the forest, and grateful boyars gave mithril to the Watcher.

Ossium/Echofell.t: Echofell's great woodlands became hard to navigate, with travellers easily lost, and multiple dubik encounters were reported there.

Ossium/Galath Fields.t: Thirteen heralds of Sung sang a day-long threnody at the Field of Glory. Sung offered seasonal feather tokens to the Grieftender if a chapel is built there by Autumn 389YE, while the open fields escaped the woodland dangers.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: Sung's heralds visited the Navarr at Awstin's Rest, and travellers in Nearweald reported multiple encounters with the vampiric dubik.

Ossium/Webwood.t: This Thule-held forest was shrouded by the enchantment, to the Thule's displeasure, and unsubstantiated reports suggest dubik may be gathering there.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, allowing Imperial citizens to choose painless dissolution, is noted as extending into Brocéliande.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: an out-of-character note allows that something awful might yet lurk in the Forest of Ulnak.

Karsk.t: A conjunction revealed a band of Mirk Lizards from the Mallum attempting to camp on an island in the Semmerlak, with the Watcher of the Semmerlak, Romand Reinetova Remislav, tasked with killing them.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: dream forests in Ossium sometimes resembled the willows and mangroves of the Siroc Bayou.

Ossium.t: The whole territory was enchanted with Night magic, causing vivid dreams, dangerous woodlands and dubik attacks on forests. It also left a curse on the Towers of Zulgan Tash, an offer from Azoth for the Palace of Orieb, and both the Dubik and the Stranger at large.

Otkodov.t: The orcs of Otkodov, already negotiating with the Ambassador to Otkodov, are considering whether to invoke the treaty to resolve the enchantment's effects on their Ossium forests through diplomatic channels.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Rat King of Temeschwar is named among Varushka's documented sovereigns.

The Semmerlak.t: The enchantment touched the domain of Dho'uala, whose servants were repelled by the Watcher and the Journeymage Towers, earning the Watcher two wains of mithril. A Mirk Lizard band is also trying to establish a camp on an island in the lake.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift is noted as extending into Therunin.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: some dreamers described the stalking beast as a brindled lion larger than any in the wild forests of Weirwater.

Shake it off.d: The Conclave rejected Meraud's offer but backed Sadogua's plan and dropped the requirement that refugees convert to the Way. Sadogua sought 100 to 200 crystal mana. That sum would fall if Drawing the Penumbral Veil were cast on Segura and Madruga, or if a Declaration of Concord urged magicians to settle refugees far from the border. The outcomes depended on how much was raised. Barien asked the Weigher of Worth to challenge Jarl Roneth. Callidus, Wise Rangara and Zakalwe issued invitations, and Ylenrith asked for a parley. Five more Black Drop rituals entered Urizen lore, and the last of the Black Drop's Childer was found murdered in Kahraman.

Dawn.t: Zakalwe's lieutenant Agon was to visit the Dawnish camp to pick five strategists for a Spring Equinox game based on Empress Brannan's failed Barrens campaign. Wise Rangara also wanted Safir du Cercle of Dawn at her meeting and hinted at foolishness to come in Dawn.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe is said to have aided Imperial heroes against the Druj, and his strategy game draws on Brannan's failed conquest of the Barrens.

Grendel.t: Sadogua's proposed cunning mist would let him guide fleeing Suranni magicians through Grendel-held Feroz, though his heralds would not explain how.

Jotun.t: Jarl Roneth of Overgaard was carrying an ancestral sword recovered from Lake Lansipari back towards Skallahn. Barien asked the Weigher of Worth to give the Jarl's Ulfur and their Cathan Canae heralds a harder fight on the way.

Navarr.t: Sadogua named the peripatetic Navarr as one of the preferred refuges for Suranni magicians. A Navarr was also among the three strangers who met the murdered Black Drop member in Kahraman.

The Brass Coast.t: Segura and Madruga were the proposed sites for a Night-magic shroud to hide Suranni refugees crossing the border. Separately, Jodeya Watiker, the last of the Black Drop's Childer, was found murdered in a Kahraman parador.

Urizen.t: Five more illegal Black Drop rituals calling on Agramant entered Urizen lore, to the discomfort of Phaleron's attendants. Barien's heralds were also to hold court at the Scarlet Guard's tent.

Varushka.t: Sadogua suggested Varushka as one of the places where Suranni refugee magicians might find safe homes far from the Iron Confederacy's reach.

Wintermark.t: Sadogua suggested Wintermark as one of the places where Suranni refugee magicians might settle safely, far from Suranni lawkeepers.

Shake it off.o: In Winter 384YE several eternals sought to involve themselves in Imperial affairs. Chief among them was Sadogua, who asked for crystal mana and magical help to bring persecuted Suranni magicians from the Iron Confederacy to sanctuary in the Empire.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: The body of the last Black Drop member was found in The Gecko's Nest, a parador in the Jade Range. She died after meeting a Marcher, a Navarr and an Urizeni.

Skallahn/Iron Stand.t: Mentioned in passing: Iron Stand is not named; any link is Jarl Roneth's journey to return the sword to Overgaard in Skallahn.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not named; the page refers only to refugees taking a ship north to reach the Empire.

Feroz.t: If the cunning mist were woven, Sadogua said it would let him guide fleeing Suranni magicians through Feroz by means his heralds would not explain.

Kahraman.t: Jodeya Watiker di Tassato Mestra, the last known member of the Black Drop's Childer, was found dead in Kahraman. Her killers appear to have come and gone through the Sentinel Gate from Anvil.

Madruga.t: Sadogua proposed that Drawing the Penumbral Veil be cast on Madruga at magnitude 24 or more, so he could weave a mist hiding Suranni refugees from Confederacy pursuers.

Segura.t: Segura was one of the two border territories where Sadogua wanted Drawing the Penumbral Veil cast at magnitude 24 or more to shroud fleeing Suranni magicians.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is not named on the page; any link is likely Jarl Roneth's journey from Lake Lansipari towards Skallahn.

Skallahn.t: Jarl Roneth was making for the border of Skallahn to return the recovered sword to Overgaard, while the Weigher of Worth was asked to challenge the Jarl's force before it got there.

The Barrens.t: Zakalwe's planned strategy game draws on Empress Brannan's failed attempt to conquer the Barrens in 257YE, and Agon wished to hear about Dawn's current war of conquest there.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Irontide Wessek is said to have died on the battlefield in Zenith, and Bartimaeus of Zenith Ascendant was summoned to a meeting arranged by Callidus.

Shallow days.d: The Salt Lords sent a formal delegation to meet Ambassador Abel at the Senate on Friday evening, proposing their customary exchange of written opening offers; any treaty would need ratifying by both sides. The Golden Winds stayed off Necropolis, and a second navy, the Tempest, sheltered between Mudport and Siroc. Highguard and Freeborn Synod mandates were offered that could earn local businesses extra income, or, in Highguard's case, condemn such trade. The Cerevado Nets were established, and an enraged Rahab was barred from retaliating. Grendel Questioners of Cunning sought to debate priests of Wisdom. An unnamed Spiral figure asked to meet seven named citizens in Outer Anvil.

Grendel.t: The Council of Salt Lords sent diplomats to open treaty talks and kept two navies in Imperial waters to trade. Rahab was forbidden to retaliate over the lost nets, while Questioners and a Spiral dignitary pursued their own meetings at Anvil.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly faced two competing mandates: one fully endorsing trade with the Grendel navy off Necropolis, and one from Eli of the Cenotaph condemning it. The earlier, heavily caveated judgement had persuaded only a few traders.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn gained the new Cerevado Nets, whose custodian the fleet captains would choose. The Tempest's arrival near Madruga gave the Freeborn Assembly the chance to mandate profitable trade with the Grendel.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to the Grendel, Abel, is identified as being of Urizen.

Shallow days.o: In Spring 385YE, with the two-year peace treaty due to end, Grendel diplomats were expected at Anvil to discuss extending it. Grendel navies lingered off Necropolis and Madruga, and the Grendel half-fortified Oran in Feroz. Questioners and a mysterious Spiral dignitary also sought meetings with Imperial citizens.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The Grendel began reinforcing the walls of the town of Oran shortly after the Winter Solstice. The work was already half-complete, probably with Autumn magic, and it was unclear who was paying for it.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Mentioned in passing: Apulus is not named directly, and is touched on only through the rumours about powerful Spiral factions seeking contact with the Empire.

Feroz.t: Governor Rahab was furious at the theft of the Scorrero Nets but barred by the treaty and the Salt Lords from striking back. Meanwhile, work to fortify the walls of Oran was already half-finished.

Madruga.t: The Grendel navy Tempest anchored between Mudport and Siroc to resupply and trade. A Freeborn mandate could give every business in Madruga 2 extra crowns while the navy remained.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the North Mareave Trading Consortium is rumoured as one possible power behind the Spiral dignitary seeking a meeting at Anvil.

Necropolis.t: The Golden Winds remained moored off the coast without hostile action. A Highborn mandate could give each business 2 extra crowns, while a rival mandate would condemn all trade with the Grendel there.

Segura.t: The Cerevado Nets were established, with a new Bourse seat upriver at Cerevado and ilium already being gathered. The Tempest sheltered in waters between Mudport and Siroc.

Spiral.t: A Grendel merchant from Spiral, perhaps a leader of a powerful faction or someone from Salt Lord Kaliact's court, sent Graime the Questioner to arrange an exclusive meeting in Outer Anvil. Whether Kaliact's representatives would join the treaty delegation remained unclear.

Tathar.t: Mentioned in passing: Tathar is not named directly, and is touched on only through the wider Grendel treaty talks.

Shallows and miseries.d: The Black Thorns, Isaella's Dance, Fire of the South, Burning Falcon, Fist of the Mountains and Drakes reclaimed the Jade Range and Braydon's Jasse. Most Jotun had already withdrawn, but a handpicked garrison of Orchard's Watch veterans died almost to the last orc at Fort Braydon. The fort is technically destroyed, held up only by fading Summer magic, and can be saved at the Summer Solstice. Eisa Winterborn sacked Cevia and destroyed the Sapphire Stair. Yanya Uranduln raided the Mournwold and stole mithril and weirwood. Stephen of Sarcombe broke the Spider's Dream. Geht Aran seized Bourse mithril and white granite. Around a thousand Jotun and no more than two hundred Imperial soldiers died.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are cited as the kind of enemy who might simply have collapsed or flooded the Singing Caves, unlike the Jotun.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are recalled as having tried and failed to destroy the Spider's Dream five years earlier.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the only link is the note that Eisa Winterborn helped bring down the western end of Pakaanan's Pass the year before.

Jotun.t: The Jotun abandoned their conquests in Kahraman, losing perhaps a thousand warriors, mostly in a chosen last stand at Fort Braydon. Their raiding warbands carried off thralls, Bourse materials and weirwood, and remaining bands under Geht Aran, Tora Helmhand, Magnus Ironarm and Jarl Haakon offer battle at the Solstice.

Navarr.t: Isaella's Dance and the Black Thorns fought to reclaim Kahraman, with Isaella's Dance killing ruthlessly using Spring magic and poisons. Both armies were hunted by the heralds of Hayaak, who still managed to bring down some of their warriors.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn armies helped reclaim Kahraman. The Fire of the South fought under a merciless Winter enchantment, and the Burning Falcon fought alongside heralds of Eleonaris and Janon. However, Fort Braydon now teeters on collapse, Bourse caravans were robbed and the Spider's Dream was cut, isolating the nation from the League.

The League.t: League lands suffered heavily. Cevia was sacked, about a hundred and fifty people were taken as thralls, the Sapphire Stair was destroyed and the Red Rock mural defaced. Raiders also attacked Trivento and seized League citizens there.

The Marches.t: The Drakes marched south to aid the Freeborn. Meanwhile Yanya Uranduln's raiders struck the Mournwold, stealing mithril and the weirwood for Lowther's Lift and carrying off a few score Marchers. The traitor Stephen of Sarcombe led the attack on the Spider's Dream.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the general of the Fist of the Mountains credits Urizen with entrusting the army with its magical prowess.

Wintermark.t: The Fist of the Mountains fought for glory rather than slaughter in reclaiming the Jade Range and took part in the storming of Fort Braydon. Wintermarkers recalled the Jarl of Kierheim's words explaining the garrison's death-seeking stand.

Shallows and miseries.o: Six Imperial armies drove the Jotun out of Kahraman and stormed Fort Braydon, while Jotun warbands raided Tassato, the Mournwold, Madruga and western Kahraman, wrecking the Sapphire Stair and part of the Spider's Dream.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: Imperial armies stormed Fort Braydon and wiped out its Jotun garrison. The fort survives only through fading Summer magic, and casting Hammer of the Brilliant Shore at Destrillo Kahras offers a chance to save it.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: The Burning Falcon, Fist of the Mountains and allied armies reclaimed the Jade Range plains as the Jotun retreated towards the Jasse hills.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: Geht Aran's orcs seized caravans carrying mithril from the Great Mine of Briante, though the mine itself was undamaged.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: Caravans of white granite from the Damatian Cliffs were seized by Geht Aran's raiders. The House of Fire and Flame proposes collapsing Red Pinnacle to seal the passes into Serra Damata.

Liathaven/Beacon Point.t: Collapsing Red Pinnacle at Redgate Pass would block the route into Beacon Point and prevent armies moving between it and Kahraman.

Liathaven/Liaven's Glen.t: Mentioned in passing: the great Jotun armies that swept out of Liaven's Glen retreated back the way they came.

Madruga/Torres.t: Stephen of Sarcombe's warband crossed the Torres plains to reach the Spider's Dream. A Jotun force still roams Torres towards Trajadoz, which the Marracossa Sendito must stop.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Haakon is recalled as having led his warband into Alderly forest three times in search of the Feni.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Yanya Uranduln's raiders spilled across the Greensward, raiding farms and villages, while a small group visited the burial mound and apple trees near Overton.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Jotun raiders attacked farms, villages and caravans across Southmoor. Jarl Haakon is now secretly building supply caches there for a future invasion, which the Bailiff of the Downs must stop.

Reinos/Bastasor.t: Jotun at Beatriz's Field hold the Overflowing Platter looted from a slain priest, and the General of the Red Wind Corsairs is charged with recovering it.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: Raiders crossing the Spider's Dream struck at Trivento across the Vassa, seizing caravans and League thralls before the bridge's middle-west span fell.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: Mentioned in passing: Eisa Winterborn is noted as having helped bring down the western end of the pass last year.

Tassato/Cascatas.t: Eisa Winterborn's raiders overwhelmed Cevia, took around a hundred and fifty thralls, destroyed the centuries-old Sapphire Stair locks and defaced the Red Rock with a walrus and the Rune of Victory.

Tassato/Enterio.t: The Sentinel Gate opens to Duarte's Repose so the Custodian of the Arratan Gamble can stop Magnus Ironarm's band before it raids the Gamble for white granite and thralls.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: five of the armies came to Kahraman fresh from its liberation, and some Drakes wished they were still there finishing the conquest.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman was entirely liberated and is Imperial again, but Fort Braydon is technically destroyed. Mithril and white granite caravans were robbed, and battles at Fort Braydon and Redgate Pass may decide the fort's survival and the security of its western border.

Liathaven.t: The Jotun invasion came out of Liathaven, and the raiders and retreating armies withdrew back into it. Geht Aran's band passed through Redgate Pass towards the Glade of Dead Night to perform his Twelve Breaths ritual.

Madruga.t: Stephen of Sarcombe's warband crossed Madruga to wreck the Spider's Dream, which now forces armies crossing to or from Tassato or Sarvos to halt. A remaining Jotun force threatens Trajadoz.

Mournwold.t: Yanya Uranduln's thousand-strong raid hit the Singing Caves, stealing mithril and the weirwood for Lowther's Lift and plundering farms. Miners, yeomanry, garrisons and some Mournwold orcs resisted until the raiders withdrew with a few score thralls.

Reinos.t: The House of Fire and Flame proposes collapsing Red Pinnacle, which stands where Reinos, Liathaven and Kahraman meet, to seal the passes. A looted relic, the Overflowing Platter, has ended up among the Jotun of Beatriz's Field.

Sarvos.t: Raiders crossed the Spider's Dream to attack Trivento, damaging businesses and taking a score or more League citizens as thralls. The ruined bridge now cuts Sarvos off from Madruga for traders and armies.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Eisa Winterborn's successes in Sermersuaq are said to have made her warband mighty.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: Eisa's omen urges her to show the southern Empire what the people of Skallahn can bring, and the Towers of Calx and Coom are noted as aiding the Jotun there.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Eisa Winterborn is noted as one of those who brought down the western end of Pakaanan's Pass last year.

Tassato.t: Eisa Winterborn's raiders sacked Cevia, took about a hundred and fifty thralls, destroyed the Sapphire Stair and defaced the Red Rock. Tassatan fleet owners suffer until the locks are rebuilt, and a splinter band under Magnus Ironarm threatens the Arratan Gamble.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs and the Quiet Step withdrew from Kahraman, heading north toward Upwold.

Shelter from the storm.d: The Isle of Zemress, settled by the crew of the mariner Zemress a century and a half ago, had been recognised by the Freeborn assembly in 380YE, and Freeborn missionaries had persuaded its Prosperity-focused people to value all seven Virtues. Grendel privateers then found the island and gathered to loot it and carry the islanders off as slaves. Dhomiro Tevus i Zemress appealed to Sol i Riqueza for aid. Independent Imperial captains could attempt an evacuation during the Summer downtime only. Success would depend on the fleet strength committed, ranging from total enslavement to a full rescue with all possessions. Grateful islanders offered payment to participating captains. The Synod could mandate captains to help, and the Quartermaster General could extend the Guerdon to the effort.

Grendel.t: Grendel pirate and slaving vessels, rather than a full navy, gathered to descend on the island to loot it and take its people to places such as the salt mines of Dubhtraig. Their privateers would be beaten back, blockaded or routed depending on how strongly Imperial captains responded.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn faced the loss of cousins they had recently recognised as entitled to Brass Coast citizenship and had converted to the full Way. The Freeborn assembly could pass a mandate pressing Freeborn captains to join the rescue, and a successful one would bring refugees and new wealth to their lands.

Shelter from the storm.o: Grendel pirates and slavers discovered the Isle of Zemress, a Freeborn-descended community in the Bay of Catazar, and massed to plunder it and enslave its people. The islanders sent a desperate plea for help, opening a single-season opportunity for Imperial fleets to evacuate them.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Isle of Zemress lies within the Bay of Catazar, well outside Imperial waters, where Grendel privateers were massing to attack it. Any rescue would require Imperial ships to run or break their blockade through treacherous waters.

Feroz.t: Feroz was one of two destinations for rescued islanders if the evacuation achieved sufficient strength. A complete rescue would see new resources established there by the exiles, eventually raising its tax revenue.

Madruga.t: Madruga was the other destination for evacuated Zemress islanders, who might arrive destitute or with enough wealth to prosper, depending on the rescue's success. A complete rescue would add new resources run by the exiles, increasing its tax revenue over time.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel navies engaged in Spiral were cited as an obstacle that the Freeborn Storm would need to get past to reach the island.

Shimmerglisten.d: The Empire's surprise was spoiled by a letter signed by Watt of Lambrooke, Senator Travid Longest Path and General Lleu Tarw. The Feni chose to talk instead. Urhalin, who loathes Terunael, agreed to lure the Heirs in if no Feni were harmed. The ninety Heirs were massacred, but Druss escaped to the vallorn's heart. Urhalin then asked the Empire to withdraw. She declared the Feni would seize Liaven's Glen, named Watt their contact, and offered to send envoys to Anvil about the curse. Navarr were offered competing Synod mandates on whether to abandon Terunael's legacy. The vallorn remains a lurking threat of up to 15,000.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: a smattering of Dawnish allies joined the Navarr-led force that surrounded Hotters Mire.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn allies were among the smaller contingents in the force sent into Liathaven.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named on the page; the events took place in Liathaven, which they held at the time.

Navarr.t: Navarr thorns led the stealthy encirclement and the slaughter of the Heirs, and their own General Lleu Tarw co-signed the warning to the Feni. The Navarr Assembly now faced rival mandates on whether to forsake the legacy of Terunael, which would win Feni goodwill at the cost of historical research.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark allies were among the smaller contingents accompanying the Navarr into Liathaven.

Shimmerglisten.o: An Imperial force of roughly ten thousand, mostly Navarr, surrounded the Feni settlement of Hotters Mire in Liathaven. After a letter from three Imperial citizens warned the Feni, their leader Urhalin let the Empire ambush and all but destroy the Heirs of Terunael when they arrived to break the Wither the Seed curse.

Liathaven/Liaven's Glen.t: Urhalin warned the Empire that the Feni of Hotters Mire intended to seize Liaven's Glen by force and make the whole region their home.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is noted as home to at least one large group of Feni who might respond to a Navarr shift away from Terunael.

Liathaven.t: Imperial forces destroyed the Heirs of Terunael at Hotters Mire, ending their attempt to break the curse there. The Feni now plan to claim more land, while the vallorn's heart remains a regenerating threat of up to 15,000.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Travid Longest Path, Senator for Therunin, was one of the three signatories of the letter that warned the Feni.

Shining like fire.d: Every Imperial mine produced two extra ingots and suffered no accidents. People recovered lost items, confessed secrets and saw flaws in themselves and their surroundings, and stalled investigations were solved. Merrow felt calm and sensed magic, while mana sites became easier to establish and upgrade. Mana sites near Lorenzo's Legacies of Virtue yielded Vitrified Oculi, and fifteen sinecures could be enhanced with weltsilver using the Windgleam Geometries. As side effects, shrouds below magnitude 100 collapsed, art and passion-based great works lost half their votes and liao, and labour costs for new Imperial commissions rose by half. The magnitude of Imperial enchantments rose to 210. Three skirmishes were also offered.

Dawn.t: The Rose Towers drew significantly fewer pilgrims as Day dissonance dulled appreciation of art, halving its Synod votes and liao for the Autumn Equinox.

Druj.t: A Druj patrol from across the Arkad, with a herald of the Queen of the Forest, was carrying the Vate's Shelter, taken from the Grynbor, back towards Turan. The Advisor on the Vallorn was tasked with reclaiming it.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel-held Feroz lay outside the enchantment, so its resources gained none of the benefits.

Highguard.t: Mana sites in Casinea each produced a Vitrified Oculus thanks to a Legacy of Virtue there. The Day magic also aided efforts to root out the espionage ring in Necropolis.

Jotun.t: A Jotun warband of Raoljost, Ulvenwar and Skjaldir held the Grimnir's Glass, a Phial of the Sun taken over a century ago, and faced Imperial efforts to reclaim it in Tromsa. Jotun-held Liathaven gained none of the enchantment's benefits.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Windgleam Geometries used to enhance sinecures with weltsilver draw on a long-neglected theory by the Navarr magician Donnaya Windgleam.

The Brass Coast.t: The Azure Chorus at Braydon's Jasse and the Crimson Drummers of Madruga saw far fewer attendees as Day dissonance smothered passion, halving their Synod votes and liao for the Equinox.

The League.t: League mana sites near Lorenzo's Legacies of Virtue each produced a Vitrified Oculus. However, the Blood Red Quays Art Gallery, the Bloody Great Theatre and Lorenzo's Great Game lost visitors, and Tassato's merchant princes were targeted by bandits in Upwold.

The Marches.t: The Drake's Dozen bandits preyed on travellers on Upwold's long roads, and a skirmish was opened against them. The giant miner phantasm seen in Mournwold was cited as the kind of illusion that could not be raised during the Equinox.

Urizen.t: Multiple Urizen covens working together performed Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths, the enchantment behind both its boons and its dissonances.

Wintermark.t: Hahnmark's mana sites each produced a Vitrified Oculus, but its mediators were targeted by the Drake's Dozen. The Grimnir of Wittal Grove was asked to reclaim the lost Grimnir's Glass from the Jotun in return for a seasonal gift of herbs.

Shining like fire.o: Urizen covens laid the Imperial enchantment Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths over the Empire at the Summer Solstice 385YE, enriching mines and revealing lost things and hidden flaws. It also brought damaging side effects, most notably drawing the attention of Cold Sun.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: The Azure Chorus at Braydon's Jasse saw significantly fewer people at its feasts and performances as Day dissonance dampened passion.

Kallavesa/Wittal Grove.t: The Grimnir of Wittal Grove, Branwynn Helsbur, was charged with reclaiming the Grimnir's Glass, lost around 238YE, in return for seasonal herbs from Redleaf's Hall.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: Mentioned in passing: the Vate's Shelter was claimed from the Heirs of Terunael in connection with a visit to the vallorn-infested region of Bendol.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: The Sentinel Gate was to open to the Queen's Claim in Nesustak Forest, where a Druj patrol carrying the Vate's Shelter could be intercepted under the miasma.

Tassato/Enterio.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening story is set at a country house in Enterio, where two siblings unearth their grandmother's hidden second will.

Tromsa/Icewood.t: The Grove of Einar in Icewood was the site of a skirmish to reclaim the Grimnir's Glass from a Jotun warband.

Upwold/The Heath.t: Tom's Dale in The Heath was the site of a skirmish against the Drake's Dozen bandits troubling the long roads of Upwold.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Brocéliande was not Imperial at the end of the Summer Solstice, so mines and resources there gained nothing from the enchantment.

Casinea.t: As home to one of Lorenzo's Legacies of Virtue, Casinea's mana sites each produced a Vitrified Oculus of Day magic.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Feroz lay outside the enchantment, and is used as an example of where a merrow's home would not prevent personal effects felt elsewhere.

Hahnmark.t: Mana sites near Hahnmark's Legacy of Virtue each produced a Vitrified Oculus, while mediators from Hahnmark were among the travellers targeted by the Drake's Dozen.

Holberg.t: Holberg's mana sites each produced a Vitrified Oculus from its Legacy of Virtue, a great work designed with help from Holberg's Wunderkind guild.

Kahraman.t: The Azure Chorus at Braydon's Jasse saw far fewer attendees at its feasts and performances, halving its Synod votes and liao for the Equinox.

Kallavesa.t: Elina of Redleaf's Hall, a descendant of the founders of Wittal Grove's Healing House, traced the lost Grimnir's Glass. Redleaf's Hall offered seasonal herbs if it is returned to the hosts of Sulkavaris.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun-held Liathaven was outside the enchantment, so its resources received none of the effects.

Madruga.t: The Crimson Drummers of Madruga drew significantly smaller crowds under the Day dissonance, halving their Synod votes and liao for the Equinox.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: a reformed League gossip writer announced plans to move to Morrow and become a torchbearer.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the giant miner phantasm recently seen in Mournwold is cited as the kind of large illusion that would fail during the Equinox.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Day magic aided efforts to root out the espionage ring in Necropolis.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: used as an example of a territory where a merrow might have spent the season and felt the enchantment's effects.

Sarangrave.t: Over five thousand Imperials explored the Sarangrave during the season. A skirmish under Druj miasma was opened to intercept the Druj carrying the Vate's Shelter.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos's mana sites each produced a Vitrified Oculus, but the Blood Red Quays Art Gallery lost audiences, halving its Synod votes and liao for the Equinox.

Spiral.t: Shrouds over Spiral made with Sung's help survived the collapse of other shrouds. Merrow could also face the influence of the Black Plateau with calm focus.

Tassato.t: Tassato's mana sites each produced a Vitrified Oculus, while its merchant princes were favoured targets of the Drake's Dozen bandits in Upwold.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar's mana sites each produced a Vitrified Oculus, but the Bloody Great Theatre saw a significant drop in audiences, halving its Synod votes and liao for the Equinox.

The Barrens.t: Imperial scholars theorised that adding the Barrens, the largest territory the Empire has ever encountered, raised the magnitude of Imperial enchantments to 210.

Tromsa.t: Some Wittal Grove grimnir joined the Empire's push into Tromsa. A skirmish was opened at the Grove of Einar to recover the Grimnir's Glass from a Jotun warband.

Upwold.t: The Drake's Dozen preyed on traders between Redston and Ashill, evading magistrates and Eastern Guard troops. The Bailiff of the Grand Market was tasked with dealing with them.

Ship to wreck.d: The Council of Salt Lords showed no interest in extending the treaty. Backed by the Asavean Plenum, they massed navies and armies even though Salt Lord Kaliact's defection and the loss of Spiral had disrupted their plans. Jarmish support for the Grendel ended thanks to Prospero. After the Equinox, every Imperial fleet in the Brass Coast, Highguard, Urizen, Feroz, Sarvos, Spiral and Tassato would lose a rank of production to Grendel raiding. Corsairs and Highborn captains kept trade with Sumaah open despite the Asavean blockade, though the Commonwealth and Sumaah grumbled about the Pact amendments. The Thule bought food with anonymous Imperial funds. The Faraden raised mithril prices after concessions to the Jotun. A Skouran delegation was expected at Anvil.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Cedric Gallows of Dawn is named as Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy, and Jarrigk Orzel of Dawn as the Imperial Consul whom the Skourans wished to meet.

Grendel.t: With the treaty ending, the Salt Lords were set to return to war with Asavean backing. Independent Grendel pirates, privateers and followers of Siakha were expected to raid Imperial shipping with impunity for at least a season, though Kaliact's defection had forced them to rethink their strategy in the Bay.

Highguard.t: Highborn fleets were among those facing a one-rank production penalty from Grendel raiding. Highborn ship captains helped the corsairs break the Asavean blockade so that Sumaah trade could continue, and Accalon of Highguard served as Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.

Jotun.t: The Jotun forced the Faraden to pay heavily for passage through the Lasambrian Hills. They also won concessions, including mithril and white granite sold to the orcs significantly cheaper than to Imperial traders.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Fintan Founder's Dance of Navarr is listed as Ambassador to Axos.

The League.t: League fleets in Sarvos, Spiral and Tassato faced a one-rank production penalty from Grendel raiding. League citizens held the posts of Ambassador to the Commonwealth and Ambassador to Faraden.

Thule.t: The Thule's food shortages eased markedly after an anonymous sum of Imperial money reached Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragon's-Undivided. His agents used it to buy food in Imperial markets and ship it north.

Urizen.t: Urizeni fleets were among those facing a one-rank production penalty from Grendel raiding. Abel of Urizen was named Ambassador to the Grendel and Ariadne of the Auric Horizon Ambassador to Jarm.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Eska Crowspeaker of Wintermark is named as Voice of Liberty, and the quoted Liberty Pact amendment was raised by the senator for Sermersuaq.

Ship to wreck.o: In Autumn 385YE the Grendel peace treaty was due to expire after the Equinox, with Grendel raiders poised to strike at Imperial shipping across the south. The wind also reported on the strained Liberty Pact, food purchases by the Thule, Faraden concessions to the Jotun, turmoil in Asavea, and an arranged visit by a delegation from Skoura.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Grendel still sought to rule uncontested over the Bay, and their raiders were set to prey on Imperial ships there. Jarmish vessels were reportedly leaving the Bay, while Axou traders grew reluctant to risk its sea-lanes.

Feroz.t: Governor Rahab still controlled Feroz, where corsairs had lost homes and boatyards. Fleets in Feroz faced a one-rank production penalty from Grendel raiding.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: intelligence captured in Necropolis revealed that recent losses had disrupted the Salt Lords' plans.

Otkodov.t: Reports from Otkodov described a marked improvement in its food crisis, as Imperial funds were used to buy food and ship it north to feed starving people.

Sarvos.t: Imperial fleets in Sarvos faced a one-rank production penalty following the Autumn Equinox as Grendel raiders attacked their ships.

Spiral.t: The Grendel's loss of Spiral had disrupted the Salt Lords' plans. Imperial fleets there now faced a one-rank production penalty from Grendel raiding.

Tassato.t: Imperial fleets in Tassato faced a one-rank production penalty following the Autumn Equinox as Grendel raiders attacked their ships.

Shovels and spades.d: Under new general Jack Ashton, the Tusks steadily reclaimed the Chalkdowns. They were aided by the Thorn of the Ancestors' servants in Alderly and twenty heralds of Janon, who stirred grumbling over the Guerdon. The Jotun remain penned at Farstrider's Watch in Greensward. In Bregasland the Jotun swept into Ottermire within an hour. Queen Yrsa hunts the Strong Reeds, with a bounty on their general, and keeps Stephen of Sarcombe on a short leash. Bregas resentment towards the Empire eased. Conjunctions offer chances to seize Jotun mithril and rescue Marcher orcs. A battle opportunity offers a chance to stop a Mountain Bulwark renewing the Burhfæst at Graven Rock and to rescue the Clake family.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Strong Reeds are said to be harder to root out than a spy network or a ring of Grendel agents.

Jotun.t: The Jotun lost the Chalkdowns but hold Greensward and Farstrider's Watch, and completed their conquest of Bregasland. Queen Yrsa Jansdóttir hunts the Strong Reeds and a new Mountain Bulwark marches to renew the Burhfæst.

The Marches.t: The Tusks reclaimed the Chalkdowns while the Strong Reeds hold out in conquered Bregasland. Marcher orcs are taking up arms, heralds of Janon stoke grievances over the Guerdon, and Marcher Pride and Loyalty grow stronger.

Shovels and spades.o: In Summer 387YE the Tusks drove the Jotun out of the Chalkdowns, leaving only Greensward in Jotun hands in the Mournwold. In Bregasland the Jotun took Ottermire and completed their conquest, while the Strong Reeds stayed hidden and organised resistance.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: The Jotun swept into Ottermire and took the town in less than an hour, offering the Choice and completing their conquest of Bregasland.

Bregasland/The Rushes.t: Strong Reeds sympathisers hide in The Rushes, and a Mountain Bulwark can be intercepted on the Cinder Drove before it reaches Graven Rock. Rescuing the captive Clakes from Jarl Aertha would end the region's resentful mood.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Servants of the Thorn of the Ancestors harried the Jotun here. A Jotun warband that retreated into Alderly was found strangled in a bramble hedge, its weapons gone.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: The Tusks pushed the Jotun out of the Chalkdowns step by step, and by the Summer Solstice the region was Imperial once more.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Greensward remains in Jotun hands, including Farstrider's Watch, the Singing Caves and Honour's Rest. Conjunctions offer chances to ambush a mithril caravan and rescue Marcher orcs hunted by the Ulvenwar.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Mentioned in passing: since the Empire conquered Southmoor, Jotun mithril caravans have had to take careful routes through Marcher lands.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland fell entirely to the Jotun with Ottermire's capture, though the Strong Reeds organise hidden resistance. Bregas bitterness towards the Empire has subsided, and copies of the Life of Tom Drake circulate in secret.

Mitwold.t: With the Chalkdowns reclaimed, the Black Canal will give its full benefit to businesses and farms in Mitwold. The Burhfæst at Graven Rock has given the Jotun a vantage point over the territory.

Mournwold.t: The Tusks liberated the Chalkdowns, leaving only Greensward under Jotun control. Conjunctions offer chances to seize Jotun mithril and rescue Marcher orcs hunted by the Ulvenwar.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: Igya Olgafsdottir, Jarl of Tromsa, was reportedly seen visiting the Ice Fishers at the Burhfæst in Bregasland.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold's rich farmlands are evoked as what people usually imagine of the Marches.

Signal fire.d: Rane, who raised the Senate motion criminalising preaching in Asavea, spoke on the Emperor's behalf, saying Vesna would accept the Empire's choice and that missionaries could not be faulted in Virtue. She warned that Asavea would respond, that wars were at a knife-edge, and that losing sixty thrones a season in trade would cost more than feeding an army. She asked whether priests would sacrifice the Brass Coast, the Marches, Therunin or the Holy City, and demanded they either support the Empire's defences or stay their hand. The Synod upheld the veto; Rane then made a Senate statement, endorsed by the Senate, respecting the Synod's decision.

Navarr.t: Rane cited Navarr's declaration that it was time to fulfil its oldest oath and take the fight to the vallorn, asking whether missionaries would risk sacrificing that campaign.

Wintermark.t: A Wintermark senator, Rane spoke for the Throne, recalling how she had brought Pride to Kallavesa to bolster Wintermark in its hour of need.

Signal fire.o: Emperor Vesna used the Throne's power to address the Empire to let Rane Shard-Bearer, Senator for Kallavesa, deliver a message urging citizens to weigh the true costs of sending missionaries to preach the Way in Asavea. At the Autumn Equinox the Synod upheld its veto, striking down the law criminalising such preaching.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa's senator delivered the address, citing her efforts in its swamps as proof of her willingness to pay a price, and later made the Senate statement accepting the Synod's veto.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: named among the lands, alongside the Brass Coast, the Marches and the Holy City, that could pay the price if Asavea retaliated against Imperial missionaries.

Signs and sigils.d: The roots of Llofir's lingering forest were consuming the Sign's trenches, which would be destroyed within six months without action. Every mana site in Tamarbode had vanished when the Garden of Llofir was destroyed. Three preservation routes were offered: a Senate motion costing 20 thrones plus 1 throne a season, an army of at least four-fifths strength spending a season clearing the forest, or a Highborn Assembly mandate backed by liao. Graciana also proposed three Winter commissions: beacons yielding Winter vis, a trapped woodland and hostel producing Barren Watchtower potions, or a drowning moat creating a powerful Winter regio and the Conclave title Consort of the Drowning Man. Sela of the Suns of Couros enacted the preservation mandate.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj once used the Sign's Spring regio for their magic, and the dead Druj Ghulai Greenmask was rumoured to have bound himself to it.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Highborn Assembly answered Brother Vashti's earlier call by enacting Sela of the Suns of Couros's mandate for Highborn chapters to preserve the Sign of Tamar, and Highborn Winter magicians helped draw up Graciana's proposals.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr magicians were named, alongside Highborn, as likely visitors if the trapped woodland made the Sign a minor Winter regio.

Signs and sigils.o: Senate-commissioned appraiser Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra found the Sign of Tamar in Reikos threatened by the forest Llofir left behind, with its Spring regio gone, but discovered strong Winter potential and proposed three grim commissions. At the Winter Solstice the Highborn Assembly enacted a mandate urging Highborn chapters to preserve the Sign.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Tamarbode had lost its Spring regio, Tamar's Toes and every other mana site, but the Sign of Tamar there was found to hold enormous Winter potential and was to be cleared and tended by Highborn chapters under the new mandate.
