Reikos.t: Reikos's great Sign of Tamar was being eaten away by the forest Llofir left behind, and a Highborn mandate was enacted to preserve it, while proposals were laid out to turn it into a source of Winter magic.

Silver clouds with grey linings.d: Sumaah declared peace but now looks to Timoj as the heart of the Way. Its orthodox missionaries, led by Lalok in Sanctuary, are denouncing the Synod, and preaching abroad led Limitu in Jarm to close the House of the Way. Nemoria is losing its war against rebel satrapies and still hires Imperial mercenaries. The Synod allowed a few carefully chosen Asaveans to train as priests. Faraden trade boosts Segura. The Iron Confederacy demands copies of the Empire's maps of its coast and warns about liao smuggling. The Commonwealth and the Sarcophan agreed to attend the slavery summit. Cargo was fortified, and over twenty-five captains crossed into the Mountains of the Moon.

Dawn.t: Faraden merchants want a trade enclave in central Astolat to reach Dawnish luxuries, and the Sarcophan Kruidenkenner guild is reportedly interested in warehouses in Dawn, though neither has yet happened.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: their attack on Morrow is cited as proof that they could have devastated Cargo had they moved south instead of north.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: their territory of Spiral is used to locate the Mountains of the Moon, which lie to its east.

Highguard.t: The Sumaah no longer recognise the White City of Bastion as the heart of the Way, and their missionary leader Lalok has based himself in Sanctuary in Necropolis, where Sarcophan warehouses have also been completed.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Faraden merchants enter the Empire from the Jotun territory of Reinos.

The Brass Coast.t: Feroz's temple keeps Asavean trade favourable but is blamed by the Suranni for liao smuggling. Segura prospers from Faraden trade, and the Asavean architect Almodin waits in Yellow Chase with no progress on the Iron Qanat.

The League.t: Asavean merchants frequent Sarvos and Asavean travellers visit the Great Game in Temeschwar. Faraden traders route through Tassato, and the Kruidenkenner are reportedly interested in League warehouses.

The Marches.t: The Sarcophan Kruidenkenner guild is reportedly interested in establishing warehouses in the Marches, and Moonwater Hall serves as the Faraden model for new trade enclaves.

Urizen.t: Cargo in Redoubt has been fortified, protecting its embassies, docks and runeforge, though this is scant comfort to Morrow after the Druj attack. Asavean travellers are visiting the Spiral Sword.

Varushka.t: Faraden merchants hope for an enclave in Volodmartz, probably at Triosk, to reach Varushkan timber and ore. A Kruidenkenner representative will attend Varushkan Winter Markets, and Varushkan armies are stationed in Redoubt.

Wintermark.t: The Sarcophan Kruidenkenner have opened a second enclave in Ivarsgard and are reportedly interested in further warehouses in Wintermark.

Silver clouds with grey linings.o: In Autumn 382YE the Sumaah Republic ended its war with the Empire but rejected Bastion and the Synod, sending missionaries to preach against them. The same report updated relations with Asavea, Jarm, Faraden, Axos, the Iron Confederacy, the Commonwealth and the Sarcophan Delves, and announced that Cargo had been fortified and the Mountains of the Moon scouted.

Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand.t: Lalok, Pilgrim of Courage, leader of the Sumaah missionaries, is staying at the Bright Destiny Inn in Sanctuary and welcomes visitors and messengers wishing to discuss the mission.

Segura/Yellow Chase.t: The Asavean architect Almodin Oktístis has returned to his lodgings in Yellow Chase to oversee the Iron Qanat, but is concerned that no progress appears to be being made on it.

Astolat.t: Faraden merchants would like a trade enclave in central Astolat, ideally at Laroc and Oldheart, though there has been no movement on it yet.

Bastion.t: The Sumaah Republic has formally declared that it no longer recognises the White City of Bastion as the heart of the Way.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Empire's recent mapping of the Bay has angered the Iron Confederacy, which demands copies of the maps. Sharing them would need a Senate motion costing 10 Thrones.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: it is not named directly; the page refers only to Sumaah missionaries arriving at ports along the Empire's southern coast.

Feroz.t: The Temple of Balo and the Black Bull helps secure preferential Asavean trade, but the Suranni accuse Feroz of being a route for liao smuggling and threaten to act themselves.

Kalino.t: Its coast was mapped during the Imperial survey of the Bay, which the Suranni call espionage and for which they demand the maps and recompense.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: it is not named directly; the page refers only to Faraden interest in Varushkan timber and ore.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: news of the Druj attack on Morrow, and how badly its defenders fared, is cited to show what Cargo has been spared.

Mountains of the Moon.t: The delayed spy network was finally completed, and over twenty-five Imperial captains crossed into the mountains with the Penumbral Watcher. Their findings are not yet public, and Axou scouts apparently did not take part.

Necropolis.t: The Sarcophan warehouses here have been completed, and the Sumaah missionary leader Lalok is resident in the port town of Sanctuary.

Redoubt.t: Cargo, home to three embassies, has been fortified with Axou planning, Jarmish magic and Sarcophan materials, making it safer from orc invasion. Asavean travellers are also visiting the Spiral Sword.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: Faraden merchants pass through Reinos as they enter the Empire on their way to Segura.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Asavean merchants are common visitors to Sarvos.

Segura.t: The completed south-west road network has brought Faraden merchants and increased prosperity to Segura, their first port of call in the Empire.

Shavronne.t: Its coast was mapped during the Imperial survey of the Bay, prompting Suranni demands for the maps and recompense.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mountains of the Moon are described as lying to the east of Zenith and Spiral.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Faraden traders reach Tassato along the Sunset roads before spreading out along the Blood Red Roads.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Asavean travellers have begun visiting the Great Game in Temeschwar.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: it is not named directly; the page cites Moonwater Hall as the model the Faraden want for new trade enclaves.

Veroigne.t: Its coast was mapped during the Imperial survey of the Bay, which the Suranni call spying and for which they demand the maps and recompense.

Volodmartz.t: Faraden merchant families hope to build a trade enclave in Volodmartz, most likely at Triosk, though nothing has happened yet.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mountains of the Moon are described as lying to the east of Zenith and Spiral.

Sinews of the heart.d: The i Tsagaan sisters, who confessed at the Winter Solstice to serving the spiritual power Faraden call Justice and the Empire calls Vengeance, were sanctioned by the Synod and all three died. Khotol Tsagaan, backed by many priests and sympathetic military families such as the Ogudai, sent a communique to the Faraden embassy in Segura demanding an explanation. A priestly investigator will arrive at the Spring Equinox, with threats of bloody retribution if dissatisfied. Ambassador Tal'Shar i Zabala i Erigo was briefed. Jarmish ports offered extra goods, Axou paid 18 rings a dose for liao, and Nemoria gave fleets extra iridescent gloaming after the Feroz temple was completed.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as the Empire's eastern orc neighbours, with relations described as another delicate balancing act.

The Brass Coast.t: The dead sisters were Freeborn, the Faraden embassy in Segura received the Tsagaan demand, and the Freeborn ambassador Tal'Shar i Zabala i Erigo must handle the Faraden investigator. Meanwhile the completed Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz brought Asavean captains to the nation's shores.

The League.t: The Regario Dossier, a Bourse seat giving insight into the Great Game, was appointed in the League this season, and the Jarmish enclave in Tassato and the planned weirwood quayside at Cargo tie League interests to good relations with Jarm.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule in Otkodov are noted as having been at peace with the Empire for a handful of years.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named directly; the page only notes that nearby powers such as Faraden may share borders with Imperial territory.

Sinews of the heart.o: In Spring 381YE the Faraden priesthood, led by Lady Khotol of the Tsagaan family, denounced the Empire over the deaths of three Freeborn sisters adopted into her house and announced an investigator would come to the Empire. The wind also reported warming ties with Jarm, continued high Axou demand for liao, Asavean goodwill over a temple in Feroz, and cool Sumaah and Commonwealth relations.

Feroz.t: The Temple of Balo and the Black Bull was finally completed here, drawing Asavean captains and mariners to Feroz and improving Imperial traders' standing in the Asavean Archipelago.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is named as the land of the Thule, who have been at peace with the Empire for a handful of years.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named on the page, which only refers generally to neighbouring nations sharing borders with Imperial territory.

Segura.t: The Faraden embassy in Segura received the House of the Five Winds' formal communique demanding answers for the i Tsagaan sisters' deaths, and its civil servants have been exchanging letters with the Hall of Five Winds.

Tassato.t: The Senate's permission for a Jarmish enclave in the Tassatan countryside is part of strengthening Jarmish ties, though it could become an expensive folly if relations with the Principalities sour.

Sing a sad song.d: While the Golden Sun hunted the Druj through Holberg's forests, brightly coloured heralds of Lashonar came up the road from a Night regio in Axmure and infested its camps with a song of Glory, lost love and death. The song provoked sorrowful, contemplative moods rather than determination, which was dangerous against the Druj. Soldiers sought out congregations and comforts, and attendance rose in Holberg. Any army in the affected territory would lose 5% combat effectiveness, while congregations gained two extra votes and extra liao and every business gained 18 extra rings. The Golden Sun then moved to Spiral Castle in Weirwater, and the heralds followed, carrying both the harm and the benefits to that territory.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Golden Sun army was followed by Lashonar's heralds, and its soldiers' resolve was dulled by the song. The positive and negative effects were then felt across Dawnish Weirwater, where the army was being hosted at Spiral Castle.

Druj.t: The Druj were the foe the Golden Sun was hunting in Holberg, and the song's sorrowful effect on Imperial morale threatened to weaken the armies facing them.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are not involved; the only link is the name Spiral Castle, a Dawnish noble seat in Weirwater where the Golden Sun was staying.

The League.t: Lashonar's song first spread among the Golden Sun's camps in League-held Holberg, where attendance at the territory's congregations crept upwards as soldiers sought comfort for their souls.

Sing a sad song.o: In Summer 379YE a stream of bird-heralds of the Night eternal Lashonar emerged from a regio in Axmure and followed the Dawnish Golden Sun army, singing a mournful commissioned song that sapped soldiers' fighting spirit while driving them towards priests and alehouses.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: A Night regio somewhere in the depths of Axmure was the source of the stream of bird-heralds of Lashonar that went on to join the Golden Sun.

Holberg.t: The Golden Sun was hunting the Druj through Holberg's forests when the heralds arrived, and congregation attendance in the territory rose as soldiers contemplated their likely deaths, until the army moved on to Weirwater.

Semmerholm.t: The heralds of Lashonar issued forth from a Night regio somewhere in Semmerholm's region of Axmure before travelling up the road to Holberg.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory itself is not involved; the page refers only to Spiral Castle in Weirwater, where the Golden Sun was enjoying noble hospitality.

Weirwater.t: With the Golden Sun lodged at Spiral Castle, the heralds' song spread across Weirwater. Armies there would lose 5% combat effectiveness, while congregations would gain two extra votes and extra liao and every business 18 extra rings.

Sing a song.d: The Great Library stands in Mourning Hollow in Summersend, built around Terunael ruins and a regio that once cycled between Day and Night. Until 388YE, priests may encourage Wise pilgrimages there, giving up three liao a season for four extra Synod votes and joining the Wisdom Assembly. The Singer of the Silence now gains Prismatic Ink and Crystal Fire each season, an obscured aura, and can use materials in place of crystal mana for mastered Day or Night rituals. Through Declarations of Alignment, the Conclave could align the regio to Phaleron by day and Sung by night. This would unlock Librarian's Incense and Pearlescent Wine and grant single uses of each eternal's protection in Hercynia. Such gifts would be hard to revoke.

Navarr.t: The Great Library that helped the Navarr solve the vallorn now has true Wisdom consecration in their Hercynian lands, and the proposed alignments could bring eternal protection or concealment to Navarr-held Hercynia.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: a fane is noted as being built for Sung at Apulian in the League's territory of Spiral.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are named, alongside the Empire, as the only nearby power able to perform the magnitude 200 Day ritual needed to pierce Sung's shroud.

Sing a song.o: Following the true consecration of the Great Library of Hacynian to Wisdom, priests gained the option to encourage pilgrimages there, the Singer of the Silence gained unique abilities, and the eternals Phaleron and Sung offered bargains requiring the Conclave to align the library's regio to them.

Hercynia/Summersend.t: The Great Library at Mourning Hollow in Summersend now carries a true Wisdom aura, and its Day-Night regio could be aligned to Phaleron by day and Sung by night if the Conclave so declares.

Hercynia.t: Pilgrims may travel to the newly consecrated Great Library in Hercynia. If the Conclave agrees, Phaleron could protect the library once from attack, and Sung could once hide a single Imperial commission in the territory from all spying eyes.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: a fane to Sung is being built at Apulian in Spiral.

Sing your name.d: The Heirs of Lepidus, stewards of the dead who recover lore on paragons and exemplars, showed that the Silent Sentinel's ancient foundations match the Sentinel's known towers and are the largest of them. Highborn researching the Sentinel were repeatedly attacked by an unidentified 'red shadow'; nobody was killed. The General Assembly mandated Rhesa, Exarch of the Scions of Ravensfell, to consecrate the site in the name of Vigilance. For roughly a year, until shortly before Winter Solstice 382YE, new or improved white granite fortifications need a fifth less granite. The Senate voted to build the tower of the Sentinel, a sinecure and pilgrimage site expected to be finished shortly before Spring Equinox 382YE.

Highguard.t: The discovery centres on a Highborn fortress and Highborn scholars, who alone have faced the red shadow's attacks, and Highborn patrons funded the Heirs; the Highborn national assembly was suggested as a possible appointer of the new sinecure.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the School of Epistemology in Tassato is noted as having worked with the Heirs of Lepidus on the earlier recovery of lore about Berechiah.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: benefactors of Reumah's Redoubt are named among the patrons who funded the Heirs of Lepidus.

Sing your name.o: The Heirs of Lepidus established that the Silent Sentinel in Casinea was most likely the abode of the paragon the Sentinel, despite attacks on their scholars by a mysterious red shadow. The General Assembly mandated its true consecration and the Senate voted to build the tower of the Sentinel there.

Casinea.t: The Silent Sentinel in Casinea was truly consecrated as the likely home of the Sentinel and became a site of Vigilance pilgrimage, with the Senate commissioning a grand beacon tower there due shortly before Spring Equinox 382YE.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the benefactors of Reumah's Redoubt are cited as providing significant backing to the Heirs of Lepidus.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato's School of Epistemology is credited with helping the Heirs recover and publish information on the exemplar Berechiah in late 380YE.

Sitskrieg.d: After seasons of raiding, the Jotun were met by Imperial fortifications and armies, including those of the Freeborn, the Mark, Dawn and the Imperial Orcs, as well as personal retinues sent by several nations, and were driven back across the border. Only scattered reports came in: a large warband moving south past Rest in Kallavesa, a heavy raid on five properties at Fisher's Rock in the North Fens, and three Jotun scouts at the Gilded Peak in Kahraman. The Winter Sun reported no raiders in the Grey Fens, and knights of the Hounds of Glory slaughtered raiders attacking stoneworks in Tassato. Some hailed the quiet as a triumph, but the raiders had been recalled by their Kings ahead of an imminent Jotun invasion.

Dawn.t: Dawn's army was among the Imperial forces positioned to defend the Western Empire against the Jotun raiders, whose withdrawal heralded a coming invasion.

Imperial Orcs.t: An Imperial Orc army was among the forces deployed against the Jotun raids, which have now given way to the threat of a full invasion.

Jotun.t: The Jotun Kings recalled their clan warriors from raiding the Empire, ending the raids as they prepared to invade.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven appears on the scribe's map as one of the territories she studied for signs of Jotun activity.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn armies helped hold the line against the raiders, and the only sign of the Jotun in Brass Coast lands was three scouts sighted at the Gilded Peak in Kahraman.

The League.t: Raiders who tried to attack the stoneworks under way in Tassato were slaughtered by knights of the Hounds of Glory, one of the last clashes before the raids fell silent.

The Marches.t: Armies of the Mark helped repel the raiders, but a heavy raid struck five properties at Fisher's Rock in Bregasland's North Fens, and the Marches lay in the path of the expected invasion.

Wintermark.t: A large warband was reported moving south past Rest in Kallavesa, one of the few signs of Jotun movement as Wintermark faced the prospect of invasion.

Sitskrieg.o: In Autumn 379YE the Jotun raids across the Western Empire suddenly stopped, and scouting reports dried up from Wintermark to the Brass Coast. Military historians recognised the silence as a warning: the clan warriors had been recalled by their Kings, and the Jotun were about to invade the Empire.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: The Winter Sun reported that no raiders had been seen in the Grey Fens for a week, a silence that foreshadowed the Jotun invasion.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Five properties at Fisher's Rock in the North Fens were struck by a heavy Jotun raid.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland suffered a heavy raid on five properties at Fisher's Rock in the North Fens, while the Winter Sun reported the Grey Fens free of raiders for a week.

Kahraman.t: Three Jotun scouts were sighted at the Gilded Peak in Kahraman, a lone sign of Jotun interest in the territory.

Kallavesa.t: Two reports placed a large Jotun warband moving south past Rest in Kallavesa.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven is one of the territories the scribe scanned on her map while trying to predict Jotun movements.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is one of the territories the scribe scanned on her map while trying to predict Jotun movements.

Tassato.t: Raiders attacking the stoneworks under construction in Tassato were cut down by knights of the Hounds of Glory.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is one of the territories the scribe scanned on her map while trying to predict Jotun movements.

Six sheets to the wind.d: Challengers had to receive the magnitude 30 ritual Challenge the Iron Duke, preferably from a coven that had mastered it, and could enter only one challenge. Past victors had to wait a year, and winners chose a reward from the Dragonforge. In the Challenge of the Domination Sands, challengers and visiting Summer heralds would fight individually for five minutes to hold three fixed markers, scoring a point every ten seconds. The top half of scorers with at least one point would win. In the Challenge of the Swift Seas, overseen by the herald Windward, racers would steer token boats through six checkpoints on a gridded map. The first half to finish would be victorious.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: six Dawnish covens, including Drake's Fire, Phoenix Rising and the Golden Grove, are listed among those that cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr coven The Eternal Family is listed among those that cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Brass Coast covens The Glass Mantle and The Tempest Flame are listed among those that cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wintermark coven Voices of the Unbound Storm is listed among those that cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season.

Six sheets to the wind.o: For the Summer 388YE summit, the heralds of the Iron Duke offered two new challenges to citizens who had received the Challenge the Iron Duke ritual: a grand melee called Domination in the Anvil Arena and a simulated boat race in a Summer chamber.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the in-character vignette shows the herald Curator gleefully shouting nonsense orders aboard a ship sailing along the Bay of Catazar.

Skeleton key.d: Casting Cast Off the Chain of Memory with iridescent gloaming still swapped lost memories for new ones, and new magic items carried strange auras. Roshanwe offered the ritual Netweaver's Eye in exchange for release from Combing the Beach, and the Conclave later accepted. Tharim offered his Ashen Knights to any Imperial army if he could feed on several great works, but the Archmage of Winter declined. Sadogua cut Dripping Echoes of the Fen to protecting a single region. Janon offered the title of Shadowed Torchbrand, and Zakalwe invited strategists to talk. Sanvar Isk feuded with Tassatan bishops and auctioned the Loom of Spells. Barien's challenge ritual still failed. Ossegrahn asked for help returning boggarts hunted by Arhallogen's warriors, and three conjunctions opened to reach them.

Dawn.t: Dawn's territory of Weirwater saw harmless Spring boggarts hunted by insect-soldiers of Arhallogen near Wickmoor. The heralds of the Iron Duke also chose Glory Square in Dawn as their Friday meeting place.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: an out-of-character note confirms that the Druj's ritual resembling Dripping Echoes of the Fen is unaffected by Sadogua's mood.

Highguard.t: Tharim asked to consume all the mana from Lorenzo's Legacy of Prosperity in Highguard's Casinea in return for his knights, but the offer was declined.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe wished to discuss with the Imperial Seer an engagement against the Jotun that the Seer had overseen.

Navarr.t: Navarr was named among those Tharim's knights once aided, and his rejected price included the mana of the Blade of Thorn in Hercynia. Boggarts and Arhallogen's warriors also appeared in Navarr's Summersend.

The League.t: In Tassato, Sanvar Isk printed broadsheets claiming a League National Assembly judgement proved him Prosperous. Bishops of the Little Mother drove him off with rotten produce and condemned his 'apprenticeship' scheme.

The Marches.t: Boggarts and their insect hunters emerged near Birchland in Upwold, and the Marcher-associated Keeper of the Golden Fields was asked to supervise a conjunction there.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named directly on the page; its link to these events is not made explicit.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: one of Agon's wargames recreated the north-western front in Wintermark, and the Iron Duke's heralds were seeking Winterfolk among others.

Skeleton key.o: In Spring 386YE a round-up of magical incidents and eternal offers reached the Empire, from lingering memory-altering effects and oddly aura-touched magic items to bargains offered by Roshanwe, Tharim, Janon and others. Boggarts fleeing a war in Arhallogen also spilled into Weirwater, Upwold and Hercynia.

Hercynia/Summersend.t: A Saturday conjunction at 21.15 would allow fifteen people, supervised by the Granger of the Golden Orchard, to reach the boggarts and Arhallogen's warriors in Summersend.

Upwold/Birchland.t: A Saturday conjunction at 20.45 would allow twenty people, supervised by the Keeper of the Golden Fields, to reach the creatures in Birchland and help return them.

Weirwater/Wickmoor.t: A Saturday conjunction at 20.15 would allow twenty people, under the Knight Protector of Spring, to reach the boggarts sighted near an old spring in Wickmoor.

Casinea.t: Tharim sought to devour all the mana from Lorenzo's Legacy of Prosperity in Casinea for a year, a price the Conclave declined to pay.

Hercynia.t: Fleeing boggarts and hunting insect-creatures appeared in Summersend. Separately, Tharim's declined bargain would have consumed the mana of Hercynia's Blade of Thorn.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: the Birchland sightings in Upwold were described as being not far from the border with Miaren.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is not named on the page, and no specific event there is described.

Tassato.t: Sanvar Isk plastered Tassato with broadsheets proclaiming himself Prosperous. Tassatan bishops of the Little Mother pelted and denounced him, and the feud spawned hastily written topical plays in the twin cities.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: Tharim's knights had once supported Dawn in the Barrens, and one of Agon's wargames replayed the Empire's failed invasion of the Barrens under Empress Brannan.

Upwold.t: Strange Spring creatures, pursued by Arhallogen's insect-warriors, appeared in Birchland, and a conjunction was identified to reach them.

Weirwater.t: Odd boggarts appeared near an old spring in Wickmoor, hunted by monstrous insect-creatures initially feared to be a vallorn manifestation.

Skull beneath the skin.d: The collapse of the Hidden Snake and Poison Crane loosed Winter spirits that now animate husks, among them fallen Imperial champions, while souls broken by Het Trakaa roam the Turan Flats. Trakaa and Sul Maggotgnaw still lead guerrillas. Given leave by the Ambassador to Axos, the Shield of Ipotavo, estimating some two thousand spirits, protected the Flats' spires and slave villages and delayed the spread into Kroll by about six weeks, but took significant casualties. Refugees, especially in Whisperwood, face mass starvation, and disguised Druj hide among them. Two conjunctions were offered: destroying a husk-drawing column at Tercia's Bluff, and unmasking a Druj Tepel among captured refugees bound for the Nesustak Forest.

Druj.t: Their armies in the Sarangrave are broken, but Trakaa and Sul Maggotgnaw still raise banners and gather guerrillas, Tower survivors hide in the territory's corners and among the refugees, and some have even settled within the vallorn of Béantal Dol.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Druj in Bendol are said to use lessons learned in Therunin and Brocéliande, and Kaela's Gift extends into those lands.

Urizen.t: Their newly claimed territory is beset by husks, tormented souls, Druj insurgents and a looming refugee catastrophe; the few spires depend on Axou protection, and Senator Bartimaeus is charged with destroying the husk-drawing column at Tercia's Bluff.

Skull beneath the skin.o: In Autumn 388YE the Sarangrave remained in turmoil after the Druj collapse: Winter spirits wearing the corpses of the fallen and tormented souls stalked the north, Druj remnants regrouped in hiding, and thousands of freed slaves and exiles faced a deadly winter. The Axou army the Shield of Ipotavo held back the husks in the Turan Flats before falling back towards the Tower of the Skink.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: Some Druj have taken up residence within the vallorn of Béantal Dol, building a kind of steading of their own, a move even other Druj consider mad.

Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh.t: Freed folk here are in a parlous position, working farms haphazardly after the Druj destroyed what supplies they could not carry.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: The Shield of Ipotavo delayed the spread of Winter spirits into Kroll by around six weeks, but they will keep rampaging while the region remains tormented, and its lakeland folk also face hardship.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: The rebel septs still permit Imperial passage for now, and a conjunction tasked the Imperial Spymaster with unmasking a Druj Tepel hidden among captured refugees trying to reach the septs here.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: The Axou garrison of the Tower of the Skink, estimated at around 500, stayed behind its walls and offered sanctuary to Urizen settlers, while orcs exiled from the region swelled the refugee crisis elsewhere.

Sarangrave/Turan Flats.t: Some two thousand Winter husks and Het Trakaa's tormented souls prey on the Flats; the Shield of Ipotavo prevented significant damage, but if the column at Tercia's Bluff is not destroyed husks will ravage the spires and leave the region underpopulated.

Sarangrave/Whisperwood.t: Whisperwood holds the worst of the refugee crisis, with exiles from Thornfen and former Thornwasp thralls in Uklead facing hunger and the winter rains, with hundreds or even thousands of deaths feared.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Druj in Bendol apply lessons learned in Brocéliande, and Kaela's Gift extends there.

Sarangrave.t: Though the Druj stranglehold is broken, the territory is plagued by Winter husks, tormented spirits, Druj guerrillas and starving freed slaves, with Thornfen under Axou control, the Nesustak Forest held by rebels and Bendol a vallornheart.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Druj in Bendol apply lessons learned in Therunin, and Kaela's Gift extends there.

Small but nearby.d: Axos remains the only Liberty Pact signatory. An Ilarch, Penthesil Lerophon, claimed descent from Kaban and sought Imperial aid, chiefly white granite, money and recognition, to rebuild the Tunnels of Kaban. Trade at Kantor stayed disrupted after the end of slavery. Freed orcs in Axos remain heavily restricted, and Snowbound Dukka urged a Synod statement calling on Imperial Orc captains to help them flee. The Modnos family reportedly offered 10 thrones for each heart of Livia, Astrid and Lord Colwynn. Smuggling rumours persisted, and survivors of an attacked Faraden caravan were escorted to Damata. The Iron Confederacy kept its embargo, but Ser Pippin Lavasse planned a Winter visit and two Hand of Dumon priests were travelling to Anvil.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were driven from the Tunnels of Kaban in 380YE, and Axos fears that freed orcs might join them.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Axos fears that freed orcs might join the Grendel, and poor maps of the Grendel territory of Mareave block any overland escape route.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Hand of Dumon delegation joined a merchant caravan bound for Casinea on its way to Anvil.

Imperial Orcs.t: Snowbound Dukka, a preacher from the Legion's Rookery, called on Imperial Orc priests to raise a Statement of Principle. It would urge Imperial Orc ship captains to help any orc who wishes to escape Axos.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn lands bore the brunt of events: rumoured Faraden smuggling through Segura and Kahraman, invasions in Feroz and Segura, and a land border to the Confederacy that stays closed. It was also suggested that the Freeborn National Assembly raise a statement about the smuggling.

The League.t: Erasmo di Tassato of the League is Ambassador to Faraden, and the Sarvos embassy serves as the landing point for Iron Confederacy visitors. The Sarvos thief-taker Maria Giacora also weighed in on the smuggling.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is named as one of the smaller nations near the Empire, but no developments there are described.

Urizen.t: Tarquinius Ankarien of Urizen is Ambassador to Axos. The Hand of Dumon delegation, invited by Pallidius of Highwatch's statement, will go first to the Highwatch camp in Urizen to discuss the Way.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Vladimir Sasha Volkov of Varushka is the Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy whom Ser Pippin Lavasse intends to meet.

Small but nearby.o: A Wind of Fortune set out the state of the Empire's relations with its smaller neighbours (Axos, Faraden, the Iron Confederacy and Otkodov) at the start of the Autumn Equinox 383YE. It covered the rebuilding of Kaban, the plight of Axou orcs, a Faraden bounty on three Imperial citizens, and a Suranni delegation coming to discuss the Way.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: Survivors of a Faraden caravan attacked in a disused mine said they were bound for the town of Damata. A Green Shield patrol escorted them there with their dead and a strange symbol daubed on their wagons.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: it is not named, though the page refers to Imperial ships trading at Kantor and the closure of Robec to Imperial vessels.

Casinea.t: The Hand of Dumon delegates were travelling with a merchant caravan into Casinea, bound for Anvil.

Feroz.t: Feroz is under invasion, which forced Ser Pippin Lavasse to travel by sea. The Suranni priests Florent Chappuis and Abélia Gaubert crossed the border here.

Kahraman.t: Southern Kahraman is rumoured to be a Faraden smuggling route. A Green Shield patrol found a battered Faraden caravan in a disused mine in the south west and escorted the survivors to Damata.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the Hand of Dumon delegates travelled through Madruga before taking ship to Sarvos.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is listed among the smaller nearby nations under Imperial trade sanctions, but no specific developments are described.

Sarvos.t: The Iron Confederacy embassy in Sarvos is the arrival point for Ser Pippin Lavasse and was a stop for the Hand of Dumon delegates. Rumours there suggest Ser Pippin's early notice is meant to ensure his meeting goes ahead.

Segura.t: Segura is under invasion. Northern Segura is also rumoured to be a route for Faraden smugglers, though this remains unconfirmed.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Snowbound Dukka, who is calling for help for Axou orcs, teaches at the Legion's Rookery in Skarsind.

Small things and large.d: The Spring planting in Bregasland, Upwold and Mitwold was ruined by torrential rain and Naeve's Twisting Blight, which had faded by the Summer solstice. Catastrophic news from the Mourn followed. Rather than turning on each other, Marchers helped their neighbours, though they treated that aid as a loan. Meade's alders, knowing the towns starve when the farmers do, proposed granaries and seed stores, and alders across the Marches contributed funds. The work needed 100 wains of weirwood, 40 wains of white granite and 35 Thrones, and would take two seasons. It promised to boost farm income in each territory and to halve army decay for one struggling nation. The Senate commissioned it, with completion expected by Spring Equinox 381YE. Decisions on it later passed to the Keeper of the Breadbasket in autumn 381YE.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun-held Mournwold is referred to only through the catastrophic news from the Mourn and the Marchers' sacrifices to free it.

The Marches.t: Marcher farms suffered a second ruined crop, but the market towns and alders pulled together to fund a granary network. It was meant to support every Marcher farm and to help mend the rift between town and country.

Small things and large.o: In Summer 380YE, after a failed harvest and a blighted Spring planting under Naeve's Twisting Blight, the market towns led by Meade proposed a great network of granaries and seed stores across the Marches, and the Imperial Senate voted to commission it.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland's Spring planting was blighted, and it was one of the three territories to receive the new granaries and seed stores, with the extra income they were expected to bring its farms.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold's farms lost their Spring planting to rain and blight. Meade, which relies on Mitwold's produce, launched the granary plan that would extend into the territory.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the page refers to catastrophic news from the Mourn, and to Marcher farmers selling their food so the armies could try to free the Mournwold.

Upwold.t: Upwold's crops were again ruined by the curse, and the territory was included in the granary and seed-store network the Senate commissioned.

Smash it up.d: Inspired by a Winter 382YE judgement of the Assembly of Nine condemning eternal idolatry, the brotherhood led by the changeling firebrand Sobena Strogobor smashed the white granite statue of Janon, commissioned in Summer 380YE, to rubble with great hammers. They fled before the militia arrived and remain in hiding, though their identity is no secret. Local artist Richard Von Temeschwar dismissed fears of Janon's anger. Sobena's letter to Lady Clarice Novarion, Cardinal of Courage, offers to attack any construction the Assembly identifies as idolatrous. The civil service warns that directing such attacks could make supporting cardinals culpable, and advises consulting chief magistrate Stanislav Karkovich.

The League.t: A League-held monument, a statue of Janon arranged by the League's former civilian commissioner and paid for by Drogon Morosini, was destroyed in a criminal act by outsiders.

Varushka.t: A Varushkan warden brotherhood from Kosti has openly broken Imperial law and fled the militia, and now offers to strike at further eternal-linked constructions with the Synod's encouragement.

Smash it up.o: In Spring 383YE the Wardens of the Souls Road, a warden brotherhood from Kosti in Karsk, illegally destroyed the statue of the eternal Janon in Hanuri, Temeschwar. They then wrote to the Assembly of Nine offering to destroy further idolatrous constructions if the Cardinal of Courage raises judgements naming them.

Karsk/Kopevnost.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named on the page, though it is linked as the home of the wardens' town of Kosti.

Temeschwar/Hanuri.t: Hanuri's plaza statue of Janon, commissioned in 380YE and dedicated to his Vigilance, was smashed to rubble by the Wardens of the Souls Road.

Karsk.t: Karsk is home to the Wardens of the Souls Road, based in Kosti, whose leader Sobena Strogobor is thought to live somewhere in the town.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar lost its statue of Janon, pulverised by the wardens before the militia could intervene, leaving some local unease about the eternal's reaction.

Smile like you mean it.d: The Free Folk are former Marracossan slaves who settled around Caer Faucon in Astolat with the help of the House of the Proffered Hand. They erected effigies to Lady Eleanor and debated three paths. The first was supporting the Lions of Adelmar. The second was aiding Dawnish efforts to spread the Way in Asavea as spies, saboteurs and missionaries. The third was strengthening the Proffered Hand network within and beyond the Empire. Each path drew objections from Dawnish and Highborn voices. Holding that they must move as one, the Free Folk will follow Synod judgements, especially from the Dawnish Assembly or the General Assembly. Prognostication proved impossible. A delegation set out for Anvil to celebrate and seek advice.

Dawn.t: The Free Folk are Dawnish yeofolk and knights-errant, and their choice could see them support the Lions of Adelmar, serve Dawn's efforts in Asavea or expand the Proffered Hand. The Dawnish Assembly holds the strongest sway over that choice.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Florence d'Astolat cites the Druj as foes against whom compassion is of little use, arguing the Lions of Adelmar should be an avenging force.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard helped educate the Free Folk in the Way, and Antius, a Grey pilgrim who tutored them in priestly skills there, objects to sending them as missionaries to Asavea.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the former plenum of Marracossa settled in the ruins of Trajadoz after fleeing Asavea, while the Free Folk parted from them.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Venka Kuraĝo names the Thule despots among the Empire's neighbours where the Free Folk might work to bring change through the Proffered Hand network.

Smile like you mean it.o: After Lady Eleanor Novarion was recognised as an exemplar of Pride, the Free Folk of Dawn gathered in Astolat to honour the 'Lady of Compassion'. They divided over three ways to celebrate her example and asked the Synod for guidance.

Astolat.t: The Free Folk have returned from across the Empire to Caer Faucon to raise effigies to the Lady of Compassion, and their debate has spread to the local yeofolk and nobility. A delegation set out from here for Anvil.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Lady Eleanor's final pilgrimage was to Bastion, where she spoke the words on Pride, shame and Compassion cited in her recognition.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the former plenum of Marracossa settled in the ruins of Trajadoz with those household servants who chose to stay with them.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Merita Saĝo, who urges the Free Folk to aid efforts in Asavea, is a guiser from Semmer's Rose.

Smoke and oakum.d: Statements by Brother Hugh and Friar John of the Mourn, urging yeomen to take up arms and neighbours to tend their fields, won sympathy but few backers, since Marchers' identity is bound to their land. Many felt that clearing Alderly to raise a fifth army would be a better course. Sister Elspeth's privateering boast proved impractical, but it prompted the idea of a land raid on Hordalant, Skallahn or the unnamed 'King's Pantry'. Henry Fletcher enacted a mandate to prepare a raid on Skallahn after the Spring Equinox. Maarit Suvidotti and Corey Wayfarer enacted supporting mandates for Wintermark and Navarr. Abbot Matilda separately proposed a history monastery in Ashbrook for a Convener, costing 20 wains of white granite and 40 crowns. A no-favouritism proviso would halve that cost.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as one of the foes against whom the Freeborn honed the corsair traditions the Marchers lack.

Jotun.t: Their occupation of Bregasland spurred Marcher plans to raid their homelands and draw their attention, and possibly some of their grand champions, away from the offensive. Skallahn was chosen as the target.

Navarr.t: Soldiers of the Quiet Step, billeted in Upwold, offered their knowledge of routes through Liathaven. Corey Wayfarer's mandate urged the Navarr to aid the Marcher raid with scouts and pathfinders.

The Marches.t: Marchers refused to abandon their farms to fight the Jotun but rallied to the idea of a raid, which Henry Fletcher set against Skallahn. The assembly was also offered a revived Convener of the Assembly to guide its priests.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk fighting in Bregasland pointed out the route from Kallavesa to Skallahn. Maarit Suvidotti's mandate urged Wintermark, especially the folk of Westerhal, to aid the raid across the Gullet.

Smoke and oakum.o: In Winter 383YE the Marches responded coolly to Synod calls for yeomen to leave their farms and fight the Jotun, but Sister Elspeth's call to strike back opened the way for a Marcher raid into Jotun lands, and Henry Fletcher's mandate set that raid against Skallahn. A separate proposal offered to revive the title of Convener of the Assembly, housed in a new monastery in Ashbrook.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the regions the Jotun temporarily held.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the regions the Jotun temporarily held.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: It was the proposed crossing point for raiders heading into Skallahn with the help of Marcher fisherfolk and Westerhal ships.

Liathaven/Liath's Ring.t: The Navarr suggested raiders could pass through Liath's Ring by marsh boat on the way to West Ranging and Hordalant.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: It formed the onward leg of the proposed Navarr-guided route from Liath's Ring into Hordalant.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: With the vallorn uprooted from the Westwood, it became possible to travel from the Marches into the unknown King's Pantry.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Many Marchers argued that the assembly should see the forest of Alderly cleared so a fifth army could be raised.

Skallahn/Greenwall.t: Mentioned in passing: recalled from Emperor Guntherm's campaigns as low-lying farmland and fisheries, part of the scant knowledge of Skallahn.

Skallahn/Iron Stand.t: Mentioned in passing: remembered from Emperor Guntherm's stories as 'the great plains of the Iron Stand'.

Upwold/Ashbrook.t: Abbot Matilda proposed building a monastery dedicated to Marcher history between Ashill and the Woldstone, to house a Convener of the Assembly.

Upwold/Birchland.t: Mentioned in passing: named in the myth of the first Marchers emerging from its forests to see Upwold's grasslands.

Bregasland.t: The Jotun presence in the Bregas swamps was the root of the Synod's calls to arms, and the raid aimed to pull Jotun attention away from the territory.

Hordalant.t: It was one of three possible raid targets. The Empire's map would have allowed precise targeting, and Mathilda Fisher claimed to have lived in its marshes, but it was not chosen.

Kallavesa.t: Its West Marsh offered a crossing over the narrow straits to Skallahn, the route the Jotun had once used to invade, now proposed for Marcher and Westerhal raiders.

Liathaven.t: The Quiet Step held that small groups could still slip through Liathaven to Hordalant, and the uprooting of the vallorn from the Westwood opened a path to the King's Pantry.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: past Conveners from Mitwold or Upwold faced accusations of bias from rival Marcher households.

Mournwold.t: Marchers recalled wanting the Jotun gone from the Mournwold, and many argued that clearing Alderly forest to raise a fifth army was the better defence.

Skallahn.t: It was chosen as the target of the Marcher raid after the Spring Equinox. The territory is rich but poorly known, home to the town of Kierheim, and raiders would rely on scouts and Westerhal memories unless a map was secured.

Upwold.t: The Quiet Step was billeted across Upwold, working its farms. Ashbrook was proposed as the site of a monastery for a revived Convener of the Assembly.

Snap rope and pass foil.d: Spymaster Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo's network was built mostly in northern Sermersuaq. It will scout Tsirku one region per season, beginning north of Suaq Fount, and needs far more strength than a normal spy network. Units from nations other than Wintermark and Varushka suffer a three-rank penalty. Army upkeep there is doubled, and in Autumn and Winter armies take casualties and scouting costs double. The Whisper Gallery will oppose the effort, Blood-on-the-Snow claims the land, and nobody returns from Sydanjaa. The opportunities include an Adventure in Tsirku venture, the Citadel of the Warm Hearth, new duties for the Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq, two Synod mandates, magical aid and a possible Senate statement recognising Wintermark's connection to Tsirku.

Dawn.t: Dawnish military units may take the Adventure in Tsirku venture, but they suffer the same three-rank penalty that applies to scouting.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarangrave, which the Druj hold, is named as a past challenge that Tsirku will dwarf.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Mareave, held by the Grendel, is named as a past challenge that Tsirku will dwarf.

Jotun.t: The Jotun border Tsirku through Tromsa and are expected to have opinions on Imperial interest there. Scouts at higher strength will report on any Jotun presence, though the Jotun have never conquered the wastes themselves.

Thule.t: The Thule border Tsirku to the east and are expected to react to Imperial interest. Scouts may uncover Thule presence and links to Otkodov, though the Thule have never mastered the wastes either.

Varushka.t: Alongside Wintermark, Varushkan units are best suited to the cold and suffer no rank penalty when supporting the Tsirku scouting network.

Wintermark.t: The Witan and the mystics of Ishal lead the effort. Wintermark gains the Adventure in Tsirku venture, the chance to build the Citadel of the Warm Hearth, two Synod mandates for its National Assembly, and a possible Senate recognition of its historic tie to Tsirku.

Snap rope and pass foil.o: With a scouting network commissioned by the Imperial Spymaster now in place on the border, the mystics of Ishal reported to the Witan on the many obstacles to exploring the frozen wastes of Tsirku. They set out a range of opportunities to help Wintermark explore and eventually claim it.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: Mentioned in passing: Urdur is described as lying to the east of Tsirku.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: Scouting will begin in the region of Tsirku north of Suaq Fount, using the caching tradition of the hunters who range there.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: Mentioned in passing: the supply-cache tradition of its hunters inspires the scouting method, and the Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq prepares hunters for its dangers.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: the Regent of the Eternal Sea is recalled as having aided a dangerous Imperial foray into Brocéliande.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark's senator, Bron Dunwolf, had earlier proposed an appraisal of Tsirku exploration, which was withdrawn.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Kallavesa are named among those whose custom of entering Sydanjaa predates the Empire.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a territory whose conquest challenges will pale beside those of Tsirku.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a territory whose conquest challenges will pale beside those of Tsirku.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: higher-strength scouting may reveal connections between Tsirku and Otkodov.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a territory whose conquest challenges will pale beside those of Tsirku.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: believed to border Tsirku, and its beasts are cited as a hint of what treasures Tsirku may hold.

Sermersuaq.t: The scouting lodges and supply stocks were built in northern Sermersuaq, and its roads would carry materials for the Citadel. A Synod mandate could divert the Smokehouse of Atalaq's output to supply the scouts instead of its farms.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: higher-strength scouting may reveal connections between Tsirku and Skallahn.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: Tsirku is said to be larger than the Barrens, which is also named as a lesser conquest challenge.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: Tromsa lies west of Tsirku, and scouts may report on links between the wastes and Tromsa.

Tsirku.t: The wastes became the target of a long, region-by-region scouting effort hampered by cold, doubled army upkeep, winter casualties, the Whisper Gallery, Blood-on-the-Snow and the deadly storm Sydanjaa.

Snow and rain.d: Blizzards cut off northern communities, some kept alive only by Navarr stridings, while food shortages from the failed Marcher harvest made matters worse. Skarsind fared worst. Divination revealed Naeve's Twisting Blight, which halved farm production, but Winterfolk and Imperial Orcs set aside their quarrel to endure it together. The thaw swelled the Vassa and Scorrero, threatening floods and killing several net riggers. Some scholars blamed widespread Spring magic and talked of urging the Conclave to restrict weather enchantments. More ilium washed down the Scorrero, giving the Bourse seat holder an opportunity to invest more in the Scorrero Nets. Heavy rain from magic could still burst the Vassa and flood Tassato.

Highguard.t: Highguard's lands felt the cold, with heavy snow in Bastion and light flurries in Casinea and Necropolis.

Imperial Orcs.t: The orcs' first winter in their new home of Skarsind was atrocious, worsened by a Winter curse that halved its farms' production, though they worked alongside the Winterfolk to survive.

Jotun.t: Jotun-held Mournwold saw heavy snow and holds the swollen headwaters of the Vassa, where storms or river rituals could cause flooding or farm effects downstream.

Navarr.t: Navarr stridings ferried food and necessities to cut-off communities, and Hercynia was battered by blizzards.

The Brass Coast.t: The Brass Coast felt only poor weather and tightened belts, but the swollen Scorrero threatened Segura's net riggers, several of whom died, and storms there could hurt businesses in Segura and Madruga.

The League.t: League lands along the Vassa braced for floods with sandbags, cellars in Tassato were flooded, and its dramaturgists responded with black-humoured plays about Vassa.

The Marches.t: The Marches were still feeling the failed harvest, and the Synod urged Marcher farmers to sell their surplus cheaply through Martin Orchard, who is likely to find a cool welcome on Marcher farms.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr character recalls the fimbulwinter the Thule sent before their attack on Skarsind.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the mountains of Urizen saw poor weather, tightened belts and unseasonably cold winds.

Varushka.t: Angry blizzards raged across Varushka's Volodmartz and Miekarova, adding to a harsh winter in the north.

Wintermark.t: Sermersuaq was struck by blizzards, and in Skarsind the native Winterfolk joined the Imperial Orcs in enduring the frigid months.

Snow and rain.o: In the Winter before Spring 380YE the Empire suffered one of its worst winters in thirty years, with blizzards across the north and snowmelt swelling the Vassa and Scorrero rivers in the south. Skarsind was found to be under a Winter curse, Naeve's Twisting Blight.

Hercynia/Northpines.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Navarr fear the snow piled on the Northpines will come down in Spring, and some Pridestalkers talk of triggering an avalanche deliberately.

Segura/Lucksprings.t: The region is not named on the page. It is tied to Segura's swollen Scorrero, which brought flood risk and deaths among net riggers but also extra ilium for the Scorrero Nets.

Tassato/Cascatas.t: The region is not named on the page. It is tied to Tassato's swollen Vassa, where flood defences were raised and cellars flooded, with the threat of the river bursting its banks.

Bastion.t: Bastion saw heavy snowfalls during the harsh winter.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea saw light flurries of snow.

Hercynia.t: Angry blizzards raged across Hercynia, and its Navarr worried about the snow coming down the mountains in the Spring.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman saw light snow and holds the deep Scorrero. Heavy rain there could damage the Scorrero Nets, while river rituals there would affect farms downstream in Segura and Madruga.

Madruga.t: Madruga's business owners could suffer if storms struck the Scorrero. The Spider's Dream crossing from Madruga to Sarvos could be damaged by a severe Vassa flood.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova was battered by angry blizzards.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold had heavy snow and holds the swollen Vassa headwaters. Magical storms there would likely make the Vassa burst its banks and flood Tassato.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis saw light flurries of snow.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos's farms and herb gardens along the Vassa would gain or suffer from river rituals upstream, and its Spider's Dream crossing could be damaged by severe flooding.

Segura.t: The swollen Scorrero threatened Segura, killing several net riggers but loosening extra ilium for the Scorrero Nets, and storms could damage the nets and local businesses.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq was struck by angry blizzards that left isolated communities cut off.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind endured an atrocious, curse-blighted winter that halved farm production, forcing farmers to open their stockpiles while Winterfolk and orcs worked together to survive.

Tassato.t: The Vassa ran dangerously high through Tassato, flooding cellars. Heavy rain could flood the city, harm personal resources and damage the Sapphire Stair locks.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Martin Orchard, chosen to tackle the food shortages, is a monk of Pickham Monastery in Upwold.

Volodmartz.t: Volodmartz was battered by angry blizzards.

Snow might fall.d: The Rime Hammer was recovered, the Gildenheim runeforge ruins moved to Runegrott and Barien's challenge completed. This cut the runeforge's cost to 30 wains each of white granite and mithril and 60 of weirwood, with no labour costs and a year to build. When the Thule Dragons outlawed slavery, the artisans taken from Skarsind in 373YE were freed, and most settled at Runegrott. If the Wintermark National Assembly sends a priest with true liao to consecrate the caves as an inspirational tomb for Isenbrad, locals would give fifteen wains of weirwood. The freed smiths would also establish the Runesmith's Law, seven unique magic items that only Wintermark artisans could make. The opportunity remained open, and it did not depend on the runeforge being built.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; the only link is the word 'spiral', used for the ice pillars at Runegrott and for the Spiral Sword in Redoubt.

Imperial Orcs.t: Gildenheim now lies in Imperial orc lands, which is why most of the returning artisans settled at Runegrott instead. A further runeforge opportunity involving the Ethengraw sept of orcs is described in a separate wind.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule raid on the forges at Treji in Hercynia is recalled as the place where several masters of runic lore were captured.

Thule.t: The Thule Dragons' outlawing of slavery secured the release of the Wintermark runesmiths their armies had captured and forced to labour in Otkodov.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the building of the Spiral Sword in Redoubt may have inspired Wintermark, and the Runesmith's Law is likened to the unique knowledge held by the Urizeni.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark stood close to reclaiming its place as home of the greatest artisans. It had a cheaper runeforge within reach and a National Assembly mandate available to consecrate Isenbrad's tomb, which would unlock the nation-only Runesmith's Law.

Snow might fall.o: Four of the five tasks towards building a runeforge at Runegrott beneath Northspires in Hahnmark were complete, and the runesmiths enslaved by the Thule had returned home. Wintermark's National Assembly was offered a mandate to consecrate Isenbrad's tomb with true liao, which would establish the Runesmith's Law.

Hahnmark/Northspires.t: The rune-carved ice caves of Runegrott beneath Northspires are where the runeforge would be built and where Isenbrad's tomb could be consecrated with true liao.

Otkodov/Nithoggir.t: The workshops of Nithoggir were where the enslaved Wintermark runesmiths were forced to toil before their release.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark is the proposed site of the Runegrott runeforge, which would also create a Wintermark national position. Most of the freed artisans have settled there.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule raid on the forges at Treji in Hercynia, during the fall of Skarsind, is where several runic masters were taken.

Otkodov.t: The captured Wintermark runesmiths were held as slaves in Otkodov until the Thule ended slavery, and they have now left for home.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the building of the Spiral Sword in Redoubt is suggested as an inspiration for Wintermark's runeforge ambitions.

Skarsind.t: The Thule conquest of Skarsind and Gildenheim in 373YE is what robbed Wintermark of its runesmiths. Gildenheim's ruined runeforge has now been moved to Runegrott.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named; 'spiral' appears only to describe the Runegrott ice pillars and the Spiral Sword in Redoubt.

So far so fast.d: After talks at Anvil in Autumn 386YE, the Lasambrians, with their three armies and Yantan Tethrasson's warband, offered to help reconquer Kahraman, Segura, Madruga and Feroz. In return the Empire would cede all of Segura, Gambit and Morajasse, with a six-month grace period for Freeborn residents. Other terms included a three-year mutual defence pact, free trade, Mercantile tariffs for the Faraden, perpetual Lasambrian neutrality between Empire and Jotun, and a three-year lease of the Damatian Cliffs. The civil service warned of losing the Iron Qanat and Freeborn army supply, the Iron Confederacy threat, and Cathan Canae's likely displeasure. The Lasambrians called it their final offer. The Senate rejected it.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish seneschal Chauntecleer Words asked the civil service how the Lady of the Frost might react to the treaty.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the civil service noted the Druj would react very badly to such negotiations, unlike the honour-bound Jotun.

Grendel.t: The Grendel held parts of Feroz and Madruga that the joint Imperial–Lasambrian campaign would have had to retake from them and the Children of Wrecks.

Jotun.t: The Jotun had agreed in principle to let the Lasambrians and their three armies leave the nation. Once the Senate rejected the treaty, the Lasambrians fought alongside the Jotun in the conquest of Bregasland.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn stood to see their whole coast reconquered but would lose Segura, Gambit and Morajasse. That would include the Iron Qanat, which was needed to supply their armies, as well as the Spice Gardens and the seat of the Incarnadine Satchel.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's joining of the Empire was cited as the kind of union the Lasambrians would never accept.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule armies were cited as earlier foreign orc allies of the Empire, and the Thule were said likely to react badly to such negotiations.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's joining of the Empire was cited as a path the Lasambrians would never follow.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the conquest of Ossium alongside Thule armies was cited as a precedent for cooperating with foreign orcs.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the conquest of Sermersuaq alongside Thule armies was cited as a precedent for cooperating with foreign orcs.

So far so fast.o: The Lasambrian orcs, with Jotun agreement in principle, offered the Empire a final Treaty of Lasambria recognising them as an independent nation in exchange for helping retake the Brass Coast and receiving Segura, Gambit and Morajasse. The Senate voted against ratifying it, after which the Empire invaded Reinos and the Lasambrians joined the Jotun in conquering Bregasland.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Retaking the Cazar Straits was required by the treaty, but the Empire could not invade it without a navy.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: Morajasse was to be reconquered and then ceded. That would have cost the Empire Mora's Rock, the Spice Gardens of Feroz and the offices of the Incarnadine Satchel.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: Gambit was to be ceded to the Lasambrians. Its Freeborn residents would have had six months to leave or to face the higher taxes paid by foreigners.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Free Landing had to be retaken under the treaty, but the Empire could not invade it without a navy, which risked Lasambrian accusations of bad faith.

Bregasland.t: After the Senate rejected the treaty, the Lasambrians joined the Jotun in their conquest of Bregasland.

Feroz.t: Retaking Morajasse and the Cazar Straits was required under the treaty, but Morajasse would then have been ceded. The civil service noted that Feroz's underpopulation after Rahab's devastation worsened the Freeborn supply problem.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's joining of the Empire was cited as a union the Lasambrians would never emulate.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman was wholly in Imperial hands, but its region of Gambit would have been ceded to Lasambria and the territory covered by the proposed defence pact.

Kalino.t: Kalino was held by the Iron Confederacy, who call it Arbonne. The Lasambrians still covet it, and the civil service warned they might one day seek Imperial backing to retake it.

Madruga.t: The joint campaign would have had to retake the Great Grasses, Free Landing and the Mysterious Swamp, and Lasambrian armies there would suffer attrition without supply lines back to Reinos.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium's conquest with Thule help was cited as a precedent for alliance with foreign orcs.

Reinos.t: Reinos was the Lasambrian homeland, where the treaty was debated in the Arena of Virtue, and it was to fall under the mutual defence pact. Once the treaty failed, the Empire invaded Reinos.

Segura.t: The whole territory would have been ceded, losing the Empire the Iron Qanat, the Cerevado Nets seat, the Towers of Anduz, the Faraden Embassy and substantial tax revenue.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq's conquest with Thule help was cited as a precedent for alliance with foreign orcs.

So little I wanted, so little I got.d: From the Autumn Equinox the observers' cost of about 50 thrones a season falls on the treasury, unless the Senate removes them. The Purple Sails offered to fund the embassies if the Court were recognised and allowed to appoint ambassadors. The civil service will give private briefings to ambassadors with embassy staff and publish them after each summit. The Beoraidh and Grendel ambassadors have no staff unless the Senate pays five thrones a season each. War with Asavea continues, and the Loyalty assembly arranged a meeting with Ibarian rebels. The Sumaah answered Imperial tariffs with their own. A mandate was proposed to protect the theist Marracossan exiles. Morajasse asked for materials to expand Mora's Rock.

Grendel.t: The Grendel remain at war with the Empire, backed by Asavean warships and mercenaries. Their envoys sent missives after the Summer Solstice, believed to concern future embassies and ending hostilities, but Ambassador Starlight Starchaser now lacks embassy staff for briefings.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Michael of Crown's Quay, one of the Purple Sails' three spokespeople, reluctantly dropped his objection to withdrawing the fleet funding. Accalon of Highguard remains Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the observers are credited with stopping traitorous merchants from enriching the Jotun and the Grendel through illegal trade.

The Brass Coast.t: Olivero i Farad i Riqueza helped decide the Purple Sails' withdrawal. The Freeborn faced a proposed mandate to protect the theist Marracossan exiles in Madruga, and the Freeborn of Feroz have begun trading with Morajasse. The Brass Coast also continues to smuggle missionaries and resources westward against Asavea.

The League.t: Therese di Sarvos led the Purple Sails' decision and plans how to spend the money saved. League merchants' old contacts helped reach the Ibarian rebels, and the League assembly was suggested as one route to help the Marracossan exiles.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marches are not named on the page. Its nearest reference is the rumoured Asavean backing of the Cult of the Falconer's attempted magical disaster in the northern Empire.

Urizen.t: Two Urizen hold key ambassadorships: Herminius of the House of the Wanderer, newly appointed to Asavea, has reopened correspondence with Lady Madrianna, while Starlight Starchaser handles the Grendel without embassy staff.

So little I wanted, so little I got.o: The Fellowship of Purple Sails announced it would no longer pay for civil service observers on Imperial fleets, apparently in protest at the Senate's lukewarm attitude to the Court of Far Horizons. The wind also surveyed Imperial diplomacy with Asavea, the Sumaah, the Marracossan exiles, the Grendel and the Protectorate of Morajasse.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: Mentioned in passing: Commander Gallum noted that an expanded Mora's Rock would only hinder invaders if Afarjasse had already fallen.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: The Protectorate asked for thirty wains each of mithril and white granite to raise Mora's Rock higher. Construction could be sped up if the Conclave provides 60 or 120 mana crystals. Its garrison will keep defending Feroz if attacked.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: The Ambassador to Beoraidh has no embassy staff and will lose civil service briefings unless the Senate pays five thrones a season, or abrogates the title so the Imperial Consul handles relations.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: The Brine Turtles sept, at home in Fleisardh and at the forefront of reclaiming it from the Unshackled, are sending a representative to Anvil to discuss the future of Fioroult.

Bay of Catazar.t: Intelligence suggests four Asavean warships remain in the Bay supporting the Grendel navies. Grendel missives arrived from across the Bay for the first time in a long while.

Feroz.t: The Protectorate of Morajasse continues to flourish here and Ferozi merchants have begun trading with it. Wind Lord Saoirse warned that any curse on Feroz other than Rivers of Life would prompt the Protectorate to seek its source and recompense.

Madruga.t: The theist Marracossan exiles of Trajadoz face trouble under the new proscription. A proposed mandate would make Madruga resist any move against them for ten years. Madruga's quays also grumbled at tariffs on Sumaah merchants.

Mareave.t: The fighting with the Grendel is concentrated in southern Mareave, where Asavean mercenaries fight alongside the orcs. The Senator for Mareave is invited to meet a Brine Turtles delegation.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is not named on the page and nothing described takes place there.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the quays of Necropolis voiced some dissatisfaction at tariffs being imposed on Sumaah merchants without warning.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: eyewitnesses in Redoubt reported Asavean warships, and the former Grendel embassy in Cargo was shut down at the end of 387YE.

Sarvos.t: The Asavean Embassy in Sarvos received new missives from Lady Madrianna. Sarvos's quays grumbled at the abrupt tariffs on Sumaah merchants, and Therese di Sarvos of the Purple Sails plans her next moves there.

So our path is laid.d: After Imperial heroes dismissed the Burhfæst at Graven Rock, the Ice Fishers lost their magical citadel but may build a mundane fort. Under Idun Yrsasdóttir, the Lion of the North hunted the Strong Reeds while the Tower of the North and Fist of Ulven secured the fens. Captured Ottery smugglers betrayed the resistance network, exposing supply drops and safe houses. Jotun raids into Mitwold were held off by four armies. The Strong Reeds now face 1,000 casualties if they leave, or 500 per season if they keep lying low. At Leakey Moss the Empire could seize Jotun orders, hold the standing stones, or kill Eisa Winterborn.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: legend holds that the standing stones at Leakey Moss have stood since the first yeofolk marched to Bregasland from Dawn.

Jotun.t: Jotun armies held Bregasland and, led by Queen Yrsa's daughter Idun with hunters from Tromsa and Raðljóst from Skallahn, began dismantling the Strong Reeds' support network. Meanwhile King Gudmundr and the Queen were both unusually absent from their armies.

The League.t: A significant number of League soldiers, several from Holberg, joined the roughly twenty Imperial warbands helping keep the Strong Reeds hidden and supplied.

The Marches.t: Bregasland remained under Jotun thralldom and the Strong Reeds were left in a perilous position, facing heavy losses whether they leave, lie low or rise. The Marcher Assembly unanimously urged the Bregas to shelter and aid their army.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Eisa Winterborn is noted as having fought the Empire during the earlier campaign in Sermersuaq.

So our path is laid.o: In Autumn 387YE the Jotun tightened their grip on conquered Bregasland, with Queen Yrsa's Lion of the North using veteran hunters and Raðljóst to expose and unravel the hidden Strong Reeds, leaving the Marcher army increasingly vulnerable. A battle opportunity at Leakey Moss in the Grey Fens offered the Empire a chance to blunt the Jotun campaign.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: The Burhfæst anchored to Graven Rock was not renewed and returned to the Summer realm, though there are signs the Ice Fishers of Ldansk may be preparing to build a mundane fortification there.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: A Jotun muster of jarls and Ulfur hunters at Leakey Moss, site of three legendary standing stones, became the target of an Imperial battle opportunity during the Autumn Equinox.

Mitwold/Meade March.t: Jotun warbands raided into southern Meade March but never approached the city of Meade, and the defending armies prevented significant damage.

Mitwold/Oddmire.t: Jotun raids struck Oddmire, and without the armies present the warbands might have seriously threatened the people of Odd's End.

Bregasland.t: The Jotun kept control of the territory, with its people as thralls, while the Strong Reeds' hidden network was exposed through raids, arrests and a smuggler's confession.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: several League soldiers supporting the Strong Reeds came from Holberg and were used to fighting in marshes.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lion of the North was noted to have previously torn apart the old Imperial spy network in Hordalant.

Mitwold.t: Jotun warbands under Eisa Winterborn and Yanya Uranduln raided across the border, but the four armies present prevented any significant damage or loss of wealth. The raids also helped the Jotun identify the Strong Reeds' smuggling routes.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: Seeker Alma, one of the Jotun leaders carrying orders at Leakey Moss, is a tracker from the plains of Reinos.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Eisa Winterborn is noted as having fought during the campaign in Sermersuaq.

Skallahn.t: Veteran Raðljóst from Skallahn were summoned to Bregasland and their scouting proved key to exposing the Strong Reeds. Eisa Winterborn, a prominent yegarra leader from Skallahn, led arrests across the east of Bregasland.

Tromsa.t: Seasoned hunters from Tromsa answered the Queen's call, and their expertise repeatedly forced the Strong Reeds to abandon their positions.

Some heavenly music.d: After the Grand Library of Canterspire was ceded to Phaleron, Urizeni custodians came forward with grimoires. The architects of Delving wanted a Senate appraisal of new fortification sites. The Hall of the Newborn Sun wanted a Synod statement on auras. The Bleak Tower wanted the Silver Chalice to drop one of its four goals. The sword scholar Helos wanted fifty doses of liao. The sentinels under Lutia of Willstone offered The Guardian Gate freely, asking only for a General Assembly call to retake Zenith. Olic the Wanderer would share the Concordance of Earthbound Stars if Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths were cast by the end of Autumn 384YE. The Book of the Restless Spirit was not added because its statement was never raised. The Conclave then added Gift of Knowledge to Imperial lore.

Druj.t: The Druj are blamed for overrunning the Hall of the Risen Sun and burning the Gardens of Pallas and Morrow, and Urizen's sentinels called for every nation to unite to drive them from Zenith.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel hold Ankra, Cinion and Ateri under the peace treaty, which has sent Urizeni refugees west and put the Court of the White Fountain back on the front line.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn armies helped some inhabitants of the Hall of the Risen Sun flee when the Druj came, and the stargazer Olic planned a sabbatical in Casinea.

Urizen.t: Urizen magicians gained four new grimoires in Urizen Lore, covering fortification, defence, healing, herb lore and curses against priests. The nation's sentinels warned that the Citadel Guard is in serious decline since the loss of Zenith and Spiral.

Some heavenly music.o: Several Urizen spires and groups offered their private grimoires for inclusion in the new Urizen Lore, most of them on conditions. At the Winter Solstice 383YE four of the five books presented were added: A Year of Perfect Stillness, The Well of Nine Stars, A Single Strike and The Guardian Gate.

Morrow/Caeli.t: The Gardens of Morrow on Caeli's slopes were burned by the Druj. The Wellspring of the High Peak ritual loses its power if the Spring of the Grey Falls in Caeli is ever harmed.

Morrow/Ravion.t: The Bleak Tower spire, built around the Senate-commissioned arboretum in north-west Ravion, offered The Well of Nine Stars, and it was entered into Urizen Lore.

Redoubt/Tomari.t: Mentioned in passing: Tomari is not named on the page, which concerns Redoubt's spires and its western frontier with Spiral more generally.

Redoubt/Willstone.t: Lutia of Willstone, descendant of the battle mage Atallanna of Willstone who wrote The Guardian Gate, was chosen to present the book freely to Urizen Lore.

Spiral/Ankra.t: Mentioned in passing: Ankra is one of the regions ceded to the Grendel by the peace treaty, prompting refugees to flee west into Redoubt.

Spiral/Ateri.t: Mentioned in passing: Ateri is one of the regions ceded to the Grendel by the peace treaty, prompting refugees to flee west into Redoubt.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Mentioned in passing: Cinion is one of the regions ceded to the Grendel by the peace treaty, prompting refugees to flee west into Redoubt.

Zenith/Occursion.t: The Hall of the Risen Sun in Occursion was overrun by the Druj. Its priests, rescued in Spring 383YE, saved the Book of the Restless Spirit, which was not added to Urizen Lore because their statement was never raised.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Olic the Wanderer intended to spend a year or so in Casinea while waiting to see whether Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths is cast.

Morrow.t: Morrow was named among the places the Delving architects wanted surveyed for new fortifications. Displaced priests also planned to found the Hall of the Newborn Sun in the south-eastern mountains near the Three Watchers.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt's Delving architects and Willstone sentinels supplied two of the new grimoires. The Stone's Unyielding Defiance ritual will fail permanently if the Court of the White Fountain, now a frontier citadel facing Spiral, is ever destroyed.

Spiral.t: Refugees from Spiral, including Cassirra Greenwell of the lost Fountainhome Spire, brought The Well of Nine Stars west. The architects asked that new fortification sites be sought in Spiral where possible.
