Zenith.t: Priests rescued from Druj-held Zenith saved the Book of the Restless Spirit, and Zenith refugees helped found the Bleak Tower. The sentinels sought a General Assembly call for all nations to retake the territory.

Some kind of fight.d: Nearly thirty Navarr military units, with prognosticator Rhian Swiftlark, scouted Liathaven from its spy network; their leaders carried a report offering a chance to attack the Heirs of Terunael. Several hundred vallornspawn left Vale's Lament for Mareholm, trapping the villagers of Holmwood, while Holberg free companies of the Towerjacks moved to oppose them. Twinned conjunctions offered a choice: save Holmwood and let Shadowspore escape, or strike at Shadowspore at Vale's Fast and leave the villagers to be slaughtered. The General of the Towerjacks was suggested to decide. Separate conjunctions offered chances to hold a spring regio at Broch's Approach and to save Black Hearth Steading in Black Boughs for reoccupation by the Autumn Equinox.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Holberg soldiers are described as hardened by fighting the Druj on their besieged city walls.

Highguard.t: A vallornspawn horde invaded Mareholm in the Highborn territory of Casinea, trapping the farming settlement of Holmwood, whose people could be saved only if the Empire chose that conjunction.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are noted as known enemies controlling the northern regions of Liathaven, where the Navarr scouts operated.

Navarr.t: The Navarr sent nearly thirty units and a team of prognosticators under Rhian Swiftlark into Liathaven to find the Heirs of Terunael, while their thorns tracked the spawn into Mareholm and their former steading of Black Hearth faced destruction by heralds of Yaw'nagrah.

The League.t: Holberg free companies of the Towerjacks moved to fight the spawn in Mareholm, and the General of the Towerjacks was suggested to choose which of the twinned conjunctions the Empire would take.

Some kind of fight.o: In Spring 384YE, as the hunt for Yaw'nagrah's cultists continued, Navarr scouts entered Liathaven seeking the Heirs of Terunael. Meanwhile a vallornspawn horde led by a cultist dubbed Shadowspore invaded Mareholm, presenting the Empire with linked conjunctions of which only one could be used.

Brocéliande/Black Boughs.t: Heralds of Yaw'nagrah tearing down signs of civilisation threatened ruined Black Hearth Steading; keeping them from its palisade for ten minutes would allow it to be reoccupied by the Autumn Equinox, while failure would see it destroyed.

Brocéliande/Vale's Lament.t: A host of vallornspawn shambled out of Vale's Lament across the border into Mareholm, though the vallorn's miasma did not spread with it.

Casinea/Mareholm.t: The spawn horde corralled the villagers of Holmwood in its farm buildings and chapel; choosing the Holmwood conjunction would save everyone but leave the settlement badly damaged, while choosing Vale's Fast would see them slaughtered.

Brocéliande.t: The spawn horde emerged from Vale's Lament, and conjunctions opened to Broch's Approach, where vallorn were drawn to a spring regio, and to Black Hearth Steading in Black Boughs, both steeped in vallorn miasma.

Casinea.t: Several hundred vallornspawn directed by Shadowspore crossed into Mareholm and surrounded Holmwood, with the Towerjacks resupplying in the region moving to stand against them.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the free companies attached to the Towerjacks come from Holberg, whose city walls are described as besieged by the Druj.

Liathaven.t: Navarr scouts worked from a concealed spy network to trace the Heirs of Terunael to the unconquered vallorn heart, returning with a report and an opportunity to attack them; the Empire held only a handful of steadings here amid Jotun and Feni.

Some kind of trouble.d: Four major conjunctions were listed. Two on Saturday would channel Thule ritual magic to destroy a fortification at Pyhatunturi in Sermersuaq, perhaps reducing Cathan Canae's aid to the Jotun, and intercept a Lasambrian Jotun and Yegarra force seeking to take Rojota and a beachhead in Gambit. Two on Sunday targeted the Druj in Zenith: destroying miasma pillars with Zakalwe's aid and intercepting ghulai supplying the Tainted Basilisk ritualists. Fifteen large conjunctions covered exorcisms, raids, the Skallahn spy network, the vallorn in Brocéliande and Casinea, and winter regio work. Three small conjunctions involved rescues and selecting heroes for the Summer Tourney.

Dawn.t: In Dawn's Semmerholm, Hayaak chose five people to organise teams at the Forest of Affray to select heroes for the Summer Tourney.

Druj.t: The Druj were the enemy at both Sunday major conjunctions in Zenith, where Imperial forces aimed to destroy their miasma pillars and intercept ghulai supplying the Tainted Basilisk ritualists. A further opportunity in the Druj-held Forest of Ulnak sought to enable the return of Imperial soldiers.

Grendel.t: The Hand of Guerra had an opportunity to rescue several Zemress Islanders in the Afar Hills of Grendel-held Feroz.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Casinea faced the vallorn, with the General of the Towerjacks deciding how to combat it in Mareholm. A fallen Highguard Exarch was also to be exorcised in Zenith.

Jotun.t: The Jotun were the main foe: Yegarra-aided forces in Sermersuaq faced Thule ritual magic against a fortification, Lasambrian raiders threatened Kahraman, and a Jotun warband was to be defeated in Bregasland. Imperial preparations for a raid on Jotun-held Skallahn were also under way.

The Brass Coast.t: Kahraman was threatened by a Lasambrian Jotun and Yegarra push on Rojota and Gambit, which the Empire sought to intercept. In Segura, missions were planned to rescue a lost magistrate and magicians taken by the Iron Confederacy.

The Marches.t: The Senator for Bregasland was to lead an attack on a Jotun warband in the Grey Fens to counter Mathilda Fisher's propaganda. In Mitwold, the Shuttered Lantern was to hide preparations for the Skallahn raid.

Thule.t: Thule ritual magic was to be channelled by Imperial forces to destroy a Jotun fortification at Pyhatunturi in Sermersuaq.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Sermersuaq saw a major battle against the Jotun and Yegarra, a raid on a mithril mine and an effort to enlist the Hylje. Kallavesa's West Marsh hosted work to keep the Skallahn spy network secret.

Some kind of trouble.o: For the Spring Equinox 384YE summit, the civil service's prognosticators published the Sentinel Gate conjunctions they had identified, ranging from major battles against the Jotun, Yegarra and Druj to smaller missions against the vallorn, spy operations and rescues.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: At Dank Mere, a Jotun warband was to be defeated to counter Mathilda Fisher's propaganda.

Brocéliande/Black Boughs.t: A steading at the Black Hearth Wayhouse was to be defended from attack.

Brocéliande/Vale's Lament.t: Vallornspawn near a regio at Broch's Approach were to be dispersed under the Advisor on the Vallorn.

Casinea/Mareholm.t: The General of the Towerjacks was to decide how to combat the vallorn at Holmwood or Vale's Fast.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: Several Zemress Islanders were to be rescued in the Afar Hills by the Hand of Guerra.

Forest of Ulnak/Oerwealt.t: A conjunction at the Beetle Tree aimed to enable the return of Imperial soldiers.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: The Yegarra and Lasambrian Jotun sought a beachhead here, and Lasambrian raiders were to be made an example of at Redhill Pastures.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: At Starkmarsh, the Imperial Spymaster was to maintain the secrecy of the Skallahn spy network.

Mitwold/Oddmire.t: At Steward's Landing, the Shuttered Lantern was to hide preparations for the Skallahn raid.

Segura/Anduzjasse.t: Two rescues were planned: a magistrate lost investigating smugglers at Kabalai Campo and magicians held by the Iron Confederacy at Kalino Watch.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: The Forest of Affray was the site where heroes for the Summer Tourney were to be selected.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: A major battle at Pyhatunturi aimed to destroy a Jotun fortification with Thule magic, and a raid on a mithril mine was to be supported at Ikka's Trail.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: The Mediator of Hyljehal was to enlist the help of the Hylje at Lansipari Pines.

Zenith/Clypion.t: Clypion saw the effort to destroy Druj miasma pillars with Zakalwe's aid at the Bulwark of Lutum, alongside the exorcism of a lost Urizeni seer, manipulation of a winter regio and warding against winter spirits.

Zenith/Iteri.t: The Master of the School of Exorcism was to exorcise a fallen Highguard Exarch at the Ceramic Meander.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Imperial forces were to intercept ghulai bringing vital resources to the Tainted Basilisk ritualists at the Fields of Resplendent Twilight.

Bregasland.t: A Jotun warband at Dank Mere was to be defeated, under the Senator for Bregasland, to combat Mathilda Fisher's propaganda.

Brocéliande.t: Imperial forces aimed to disperse vallornspawn near a regio at Broch's Approach and to defend a steading at the Black Hearth Wayhouse.

Casinea.t: The General of the Towerjacks was to decide how to combat the vallorn at Holmwood or Vale's Fast in Mareholm.

Feroz.t: The Hand of Guerra had a small conjunction to rescue several Zemress Islanders in the Afar Hills.

Forest of Ulnak.t: The Imperial Spymaster had a conjunction at the Beetle Tree in Oerwealt to enable the return of Imperial soldiers.

Kahraman.t: A Lasambrian Jotun and Yegarra force threatened to take Rojota and secure a beachhead in Gambit, and Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills was to make an example of Lasambrian raiders at Redhill Pastures.

Kalino.t: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Confederacy, which held Kalino, had taken magicians whom the Celestial Arch sought to rescue from Kalino Watch in Segura.

Kallavesa.t: The Imperial Spymaster was to maintain the secrecy of the Skallahn spy network at Starkmarsh in the West Marsh.

Mitwold.t: The Grandmaster of the Shuttered Lantern was to hide preparations for the Skallahn raid at Steward's Landing in Oddmire.

Segura.t: A magistrate lost investigating smugglers was to be rescued at Kabalai Campo, and magicians were to be rescued from the Iron Confederacy at Kalino Watch.

Semmerholm.t: Heroes for the Summer Tourney were to be selected at the Forest of Affray in Axmure, with Hayaak choosing five people to organise teams.

Sermersuaq.t: Thule ritual magic was to destroy a Jotun fortification at Pyhatunturi, possibly reducing Cathan Canae's aid to the Jotun, while other missions supported a mithril mine raid and sought the Hylje's help.

Skallahn.t: A Skallahn spy network and preparations for a raid on the territory were being protected by conjunctions in Kallavesa and Mitwold.

Zenith.t: Zenith hosted both Sunday major battles against the Druj and several large conjunctions to exorcise lost Highguard and Urizeni souls, manipulate a winter regio and ward against winter spirits.

Some to misery are born.d: With the Tassato Chamber of Commerce's approval, the Whittle folk fairly bought two streets in Tassato Mestra, opened a bakery and a pub, and kept their streets clean, safe and well maintained. They held a vigil for kin who died at Overton, celebrating twenty thousand dead Jotun. Angered by Friar Robin's execution for blasphemy, they drove off visiting Marcher priests, including an Upwold monk. The League assembly could denounce them as blasphemers, ending the Chamber's green iron arrangement and likely forcing them out by year's end, possibly violently. The Marcher assembly could instead have Upwold, Mitwold and Bregasland shun them, denying them trade and sanctuary.

Jotun.t: The Jotun are the object of the Whittle folk's Hatred, which they credit with thirty years of resistance, and their vigil celebrated the twenty thousand Jotun dead at Overton.

The League.t: The League hosts the Whittle enclave in Tassato, and its national assembly has the option of a mandate denouncing the newcomers as blasphemers, which would end the Chamber of Commerce's profitable arrangement with them and risk violence.

The Marches.t: The Marcher assembly, which executed Friar Robin and condemns Hatred, could pass a mandate to have the Whittle folk shunned as not being good Marchers. Its visiting priests have been driven out of the enclave by the angry Whittle folk.

Some to misery are born.o: Marcher refugees from Whittle settled in a two-street enclave in Tassato Mestra, where their open reverence for Hatred as a virtue drew growing concern from the League and Marcher assemblies of the Synod. Two possible Synod mandates were set out for denouncing or shunning them.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: The Whittle folk bought two streets in Tassato Mestra and opened a bakery and a pub there. Those streets are now perhaps the cleanest and best-lit in the city, but they are at the centre of the Synod's dispute over Hatred.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland is one of the three Marcher territories where a proposed Marcher assembly mandate would urge people to shun the Whittle folk, refusing them trade and sanctuary.

Mitwold.t: Under the proposed Marcher assembly mandate, the people of Mitwold would shun the Whittle folk and refuse them trade or sanctuary if they were driven from Tassato.

Mournwold.t: The Whittle folk left the Mournwold after resisting a thirty-year Jotun occupation there. Many of their young people died defending Overton and Orchard's Watch when it fell, and the Drakes were praised for refusing to cede an inch of the territory.

Tassato.t: Tassato's Chamber of Commerce welcomed the Whittle enclave and shares in its green iron. However, a possible League assembly mandate would turn the enclave into a shunned ghetto and probably drive its people out by year's end.

Upwold.t: An Upwold monk was forcibly driven from the enclave for preaching against Hatred, and Upwold is named among the territories where a proposed mandate would have the Whittle folk shunned.

Something must break.d: Sadogua's consumption of the Night technique left a crack in the Citadel Guard's cyclic magic. If Transmogrification of the Soul's Echo is performed on Saturday night of the coming summit, with 7 rings of ilium and the general's consent, Cyclic Magic would become Highest Discipline: five techniques, one per season, each usable once a year. Canterspire, ceded to Phaleron, became the Grand Library, which underpins Urizen Lore, though it contains no rituals yet. The Doyen of the Spires' codification of Regrow the Land's Heart has slowed to 15 a season since Spiral was lost, and alternative versions are suggested. Adamant sends Galene Netherwatch a gift, and mandates promoting virtuous cooperation with eternals are proposed.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn's enchanters are cited as having long and profitable experience of dealing with eternals.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as the foe the Highborn armies held back from Morrow after the fall of Zenith.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes Spiral has been lost to Urizen again, slowing the Doyen of the Spires, but does not name Grendel.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Three Watchers memorialise three Highborn armies that helped Urizeni flee Zenith, and Highguard is described as cautious about dealing with eternals.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: some astronomancers link the conjunction to events in Sarvos, where destruction is becoming a chance for something new.

Urizen.t: Urizen may transform the Citadel Guard's magic into Highest Discipline, now has its own national lore anchored by the Grand Library of Canterspire, and its assembly could pass a mandate opening Winter opportunities to work with eternals.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan cabalists are cited as having long and profitable experience of treating with creatures of the realms.

Something must break.o: In Autumn 383YE a conjunction of the Wanderer, the Great Wyrm, the Drowned Shepherd and the Claw, read as favouring transformation over endings, gave Urizen a chance to recast the Citadel Guard's cyclic magic. It also marked the founding of the Grand Library of Canterspire and Urizen Lore, and opened Synod opportunities to endorse cooperation with eternals.

Redoubt/Tomari.t: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name Tomari, and refers to Redoubt only as the place where the unmade trove was found beneath the Unmade spire.

Morrow.t: The Three Watchers, giant statues raised by Adamant's koboldi, guard the approach to Morrow from Zenith and honour the Highborn armies who defended it. Adamant has now sent a token of esteem in recognition of that work.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the unmade trove that empowered the Citadel Guard was originally found beneath the Unmade spire in Redoubt.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: astronomancers point to Sarvos as a place where an ending wrought by destruction is being turned into an opportunity for something new.

Spiral.t: The loss of Spiral cut the Doyen's codification rate to 15 a season. Regrow the Land's Heart, a planned year-long Spring enchantment to heal Spiral's war scars, might be reworked to target any territory.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: refugees from Zenith have swelled Canterspire, and the Three Watchers look out over the approach from Zenith to Morrow.

Song of the lakefolk.d: Hundreds of figures in dark animal skins, some emerging from the lake itself, gathered around a naked singer whose song spoke of theft, a lost lover and righting wrongs. They raided halls and houses, searching but neither stealing nor pressing attacks, fighting only when Winterfolk defended their homes, and refused all attempts at talk. Too small to be an army, they were nonetheless a nuisance, threatening to cost local farms and businesses 36 rings next season. Divination revealed nothing, though a conjunction near Atkonaroq was expected in Winter. Three Synod responses were offered; the Assembly of Wisdom, with some Wintermark National Assembly support, urged the people to learn about the Lakefolk, so the disruptive raids continued.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk in the far north faced raids on their halls by the mysterious Lakefolk, and the Wintermark National Assembly lent some support to the Assembly of Wisdom's call to investigate, with Savik Summerstorm sent to coordinate.

Song of the lakefolk.o: A growing band of strange, skin-clad spear-hunters calling themselves companions of the Ætheling of Atkonaroq camped on the northern shore of Lake Atkonaroq in Sermersuaq and began raiding nearby halls, searching for something but taking nothing. The Assembly of Wisdom chose to have the locals gather information, sending Savik Summerstorm to lead the effort.

Sermersuaq.t: The raiders camped on the northern shores of Lake Atkonaroq and kept searching local settlements, and because the chosen response focused on gathering knowledge rather than resisting them, farms and businesses in the territory continued to suffer disruption.

Songs like trees.d: The vallorn, roused by Druj magic, was drawn away from the Upper Tarn Valley towards the Imperial armies and was stopped in Peakedge Song. The untested Winter ritual Why Sulemaine Walked Away From The Baker protected the soldiers from Green Lung and greatly reduced their losses. The Druj had also cast a curse akin to Thunderous Tread of the Trees. Ossegrahn's herald explained that the Conclave had failed him, so he had withdrawn and would offer no more boons. He left an enchanted grove where Peakedge Stead stood. The Houses of Healing and Stones from Blood were destroyed. Therunin remains nominally Druj, with the Empire about a fifth of the way to reclaiming Peakedge Song. Wards on the Thorn Guardians and poisoning ettercap nests were offered as opportunities.

Dawn.t: The Golden Sun returned from Astolat to fight the vallorn in Peakedge Song, Dawnish captains marched alongside it, and Dawnish enchanters identified heralds of Woodwyf among the vallornspawn, prompting a Dawnish and League cadre of monster hunters to hunt them.

Druj.t: The Druj burned Peakedge Stead once Lord Rain's protection lapsed and cast a tree-animating curse over Therunin, which they still nominally hold. Their remaining forces appear concentrated in the east, leaving only guerrillas and traps in Peakedge Song.

Highguard.t: Highborn captains joined the campaign, and the priests of Reikos blessed and anointed the soldiers on Chalcis Mount, with some choosing to march with the armies against the vallorn.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War had been recovering from campaigning against the Jotun in the west before this deployment.

Navarr.t: Navarr thorns and brands made up most of the captains fighting in Therunin, but their ancient Peakedge Stead was burned and the Houses of Healing and Stones from Blood were lost. Ossegrahn has withdrawn his support from Greenwatch, and Thornsong House is hidden by Night magic only until the Winter Solstice.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War marched out of Urizen's Morrow, where they had earlier helped the Urizen root out vallorn harbingers probing Peregro.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark captains were among the warbands well represented alongside the two armies.

Songs like trees.o: In Autumn 387YE the Golden Sun and the Wolves of War, joined by well over a hundred independent captains, marched from Reikos into Therunin and held back a vallorn surge in Peakedge Song. They arrived to find that the Druj had burned Peakedge Stead after Lord Rain withdrew his protection and turned away from the Empire.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War had helped the people of Urizen root out vallorn harbingers probing Peregro's defences.

Reikos/Chalcis Mount.t: The armies gathered at High Chalcis, where priests offered dedication and anointing on the eve of the march. Some Highborn reflected uneasily on how short the distance is between the Gardens of High Chalcis and Therunin.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj-roused vallorn had spilled out beyond Sweetglades and the Greenheart.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named directly, though the Druj fled east towards the Tarn Valley and their remaining forces in Therunin seem concentrated in the east.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: The vallorn was halted here after relentless fighting, and the Empire is about a fifth of the way to reclaiming the region. Peakedge Stead was burned, and the Thorn Guardians and an ettercap hive at Thorngroves offer chances to weaken the vallorn.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: The vallorn surged out of Sweetglades, and ettercaps migrated from hives at its heart. Two nests found there, in the Squamous Woods and the Twitching Grove, could be poisoned to reduce the vallorn's strength.

Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley.t: The vallorn had seemed set on devouring the Upper Tarn Valley, but it was drawn away towards the Imperial armies instead. The Druj who burned Peakedge Stead left on a trail heading north-east towards the valley.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Sun had been recovering in Astolat since its retreat from Therunin and marched out from there.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War set out from Morrow after six months of furlough there.

Reikos.t: Reikos served as the mustering ground where the Golden Sun, the Wolves of War and the independent captains joined forces before crossing into Therunin. The burning across the border brought home how close the vallorn threat now lies.

Therunin.t: The vallorn was prevented from claiming any further land in Therunin, but the territory remains nominally Druj and is plagued by animated plant life. Peakedge Stead has been destroyed, and an enchanted grove now stands in its place.

Sorrow and death.d: During the Spring Equinox a riot engulfed the Spire, which treated those broken by dangerous magic, and several dangerous patients escaped. Its last Arbiter, Papiria, murdered a healer and vanished. Nazares, a former warmage obsessed with destroying the Druj, raised the dead as husks, attacked spires in eastern Lustri and marched north towards Embersfall Spire. A subtle Winter pall of sadness, blamed on three women who became vessels of the Three Sisters, spread through Proceris and Occursion. The Conclave was offered the chance to name a group to succeed the Spire, with a Custodian of the Lost. At the Solstice the husks collapsed, and Urizen priests freed the pall's source.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the unliving horde marching through Dawn-held Weirwater is cited as a far larger threat than Nazares' husks.

Druj.t: Nazares sought to raise an army for an insane war to "extinguish the foul Druj" and may have been heading for the Mallum border, while the pall of sorrow was seen as a weakness the Druj would be quick to exploit.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Zenith's shared border with the Grendel is noted as one of the real dangers its people blamed for their grim mood.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the strengthening pall was likened to the miasma that until recently smothered Highguard-held Reikos.

Urizen.t: Urizen lost the Spire of Twisting Shadows, saw outlying spires attacked by husks and its people weighed down by a curse of sorrow, but the husks collapsed and Urizen priests lifted the pall at the Cave of the Weeping Sisters.

Sorrow and death.o: After a riot at the Spire of Twisting Shadows in Lustri, Zenith, two magical threats spread across the territory: the escaped patient Nazares Praesidio raised a growing legion of husks, and a Winter curse of sorrow spread from Lustri. Both were ended by the Summer Solstice.

Zenith/Lustri.t: The Spire of Twisting Shadows in Lustri's forest foothills was lost to riot, Nazares' husks attacked spires in eastern Lustri and moved north towards Embersfall Spire, and the pall of sorrow began here.

Zenith/Occursion.t: The pall spread into Occursion, and it was at the Cave of the Weeping Sisters here that Urizen priests persuaded a magician trapped between life and death to move on, breaking the Three Sisters' hold.

Zenith/Proceris.t: The pall of sorrow spread through Proceris over the three months before the Summer Solstice, bringing sadness, regret and visions of two figures weeping over a third.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the miasma that until recently smothered Reikos is used as a comparison for how the pall of sorrow might worsen.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: the unliving threat marching through Weirwater is described as far larger than Nazares' corpse-herd.

Zenith.t: Zenith faced two magical threats at once, a growing husk-legion picking off isolated spires and a creeping Winter pall that threatened to sap its people's will and output, until both ended by the Summer Solstice.

Sound and vision.d: Heralds of Jaheris paid performers to recite 'Grinning General Gabriel'. Wintermark researchers found that twenty mana crystals could bind Little Icebarn to the Pride of Ikka's Tears for another year, with the cost doubling for each further year. Mount Polus in Occursion rose to become the Empire's tallest mountain, offering a spire edifice or the Eye of the Heavens observatory. Two gate plans could restore contact with the Lyceum, and Amalia Vicente later completed gates in Oranseri. Lights Aliss secured an interdiction on shedding blood through the Claw. Koboldi idled in Murderdale, strange constellations appeared over four territories, and the Falconer cult and coral husks prompted skirmishes in Miekarova, Skarsind, Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Bregasland.

Dawn.t: Koboldi sent by the King under the Mountain arrived in Murderdale expecting the Phoenix Rising coven to tell them what statue to build, and they wait on Dawnish direction before the Autumn Equinox.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the poem boasts of Barossa baiting the Druj to free Holberg and Reikos, and the Druj must be pushed out of Zenith before the Mount Polus crevasse can be explored.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the poem mocks the Grendel for losing a three-minute dance-off to Barossa's League troops.

Highguard.t: Casinea folk dreamed strangely, the Woven Banner constellation hung over Necropolis, and the Pilgrim Flame tulpa from Casinea was expected to visit the Highborn camp at Anvil.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Trident constellation brought a surge of creativity and strange dreams to Skarsind. Falconer cultists were threatening the Great Herd in Estermark.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the poem claims Barossa beat a Jotun warlord without a sword, and the Jotun invasion of Bregasland is recalled.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the old Paths of Lan Thúven that let Navarr armies cross West Ranging inspired one Lyceum gate plan, and a Navarr figure appeared in the Feroz sky vision.

The Brass Coast.t: Oranseri was proposed as the site of gates to the Lyceum and Amalia Vicente later saw them built there. The Eye of the Heavens would spread crystal mana through Brass Coast businesses, and the Pilgrim Flame was expected at the Freeborn camp.

The League.t: League general Gabriel Barossa became the subject of a widely performed poem crediting him with freeing Holberg and Reikos, while the Golden Ferret constellation inflamed Tassato's rivalries.

The Marches.t: The Serpent Sheds its Skin constellation over the Mournwold stirred people's urge to change their lives and became a popular subject of song and art.

Urizen.t: Mount Polus rose in Occursion, offering Urizen the chance to found a new spire or build the Eye of the Heavens observatory, and the Spire of Shadowed Glass catalogued strange constellations.

Varushka.t: Falconer cultists and wild beasts menaced the woods of Mieriada around the Painted Clearing, and Senator Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti was charged with defeating them.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk mystics found how to bind Little Icebarn at the Pride of Ikka's Tears. The Falconer cult spread in Sermersuaq, and Wintermark leaders were called to fight cultists in Hahnmark and coral husks in Kallavesa.

Sound and vision.o: In Summer 387YE a wide range of magical events swept the Empire. Jaheris paid performers to spread a comic poem about General Gabriel Barossa, Winterfolk mystics found a way to bind the artok Little Icebarn, and Mount Polus rose in Zenith. Plans emerged to reach the Lyceum again, the Conclave interdicted the Claw's blood magic, and Falconer cultists and coral husks threatened several territories.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Proposed as the mainland site for gates to the Lyceum, most likely at the docks of Oran, where the gates were completed after the Spring Equinox 388YE.

Hahnmark/Valasmark.t: Falconer cultists left victims to bleed in Dunhall Copse, leading to a skirmish where innocents may be present.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: Mentioned in passing: the Paths of Lan Thúven once let Navarr armies pass through vallorn-held West Ranging.

Madruga/Siroc Bayou.t: Proposed as a possible site for gates to the Lyceum, despite lying outside the Empire and being costlier to build in.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Falconer cultists and enraged beasts haunted the woods around the Painted Clearing near the Night Quarry.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: A small band of Winterfolk researchers gathered at an isolated hall here to uncover the method of binding Little Icebarn.

Skarsind/Estermark.t: Falconer cultists left a trail of mutilated corpses towards the Great Herd's cattle in eastern Estermark.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Koboldi gathered here to build a statue and offered a 'Palace of the Moon' for 500 wains of white granite.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Mount Polus rose and a crevasse opened at its base, which an army could explore once the Druj are driven out, with spire and observatory edifices proposed for its summit.

Bregasland.t: Robin Hopper of the Strong Reeds asked the Academy's cadets to rescue magicians trapped by coral husks while studying the creatures.

Casinea.t: Residents dreamed of shadowed spires and silent gatherings, said to be a gift of Night eternals, and an unfamiliar Wanderer tulpa called the Pilgrim Flame appeared here.

Feroz.t: A powerful Summer enchantment lit the night skies with a recurring vision until shortly before the solstice, to some local grumbling about wasted mana. Oranseri was proposed as a site for gates to the Lyceum.

Hahnmark.t: Falconer cultists strung up a victim in Dunhall Copse to draw in beasts, and Senator Runa Whiteoak was made responsible for freeing them.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the poem credits Gabriel Barossa with freeing Holberg from the Druj.

Kallavesa.t: Coral husks attacked pilgrims along the Pilgrim's Trail towards the Sovenann, and Crow Keeper Cynerik was called on to destroy them.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: the historic Paths of Lan Thúven in western Liathaven inspired one plan to reach the Lyceum.

Madruga.t: Siroc Bayou was proposed as one possible site for gates to the Lyceum, though it lies outside the Empire and is costly to build in.

Miekarova.t: Falconer cultists struck at travellers and outposts while evading Grimhold's garrison, and were rumoured to be planning a sacrifice and an attack on Olodny.

Mournwold.t: The Serpent Sheds its Skin constellation drew people to thoughts of transformation and became a popular subject of tales and songs.

Necropolis.t: Chapters and archivists eyed the Woven Banner constellation with suspicion, while those beneath it felt an urge to work together.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the poem credits Gabriel Barossa with freeing Reikos from the Druj.

Sermersuaq.t: Researchers at a hall in Suaq Fount found a way to bind Little Icebarn to the Pride of Ikka's Tears for a year for twenty mana crystals. The Falconer cult also spread, with rumours of pillars raised in the wilds.

Skarsind.t: The Trident constellation inspired creativity and dreams of voyages, while Falconer cultists butchered travellers and threatened the Great Herd.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral's proposed Omphalos and school of dramaturgy are cited as comparisons for the Zenith spire plans.

Tassato.t: The Golden Ferret constellation only deepened the rivalry between Mestra and Regario among those who gazed at it.

The Barrens.t: Koboldi made a nuisance of themselves in Murderdale, touting absurd building schemes while awaiting instructions for a statue.

Zenith.t: Mount Polus rose to become the Empire's tallest mountain after the Ashen Flame's ritual, opening a crevasse to explore and opportunities for a new spire or the Eye of the Heavens observatory.

Sound the bells.d: Morrow, Redoubt and Zenith produced half their usual mana, raising costs for the grandmasters, the Quartermaster General and the mana exchange stewards. The two national Assemblies made gestures towards de-escalation. The sword scholar Marcus of the Pale Sun proposed ways Urizen might reconcile: enchanting Marcher farms, removing hated curses from Imperial lore, or developing a better farming ritual. Meanwhile Fanny Moulder called Marcher landowners to vote on leaving their fields idle, which would cut every other nation's supply. Storms hit Necropolis, Redoubt, Sarvos and Spiral, damaging fleets and prompting Axos, the Sarcophan Delves, Sumaah and the Iron Confederacy to warn their ships away. Flood-defence and mithril-net projects were offered, and three skirmishes were set against stranded Grendel.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: recalled as the invaders Urizen struggled to repel, when only the Highborn aided Urizen and Marcher food supplied the Citadel Guard.

Grendel.t: Grendel fleets were caught unprepared by the storms and many were forced to break off attacks to rescue their own. Three ships, the Merry Mariner, Swift Reprise and Flying Civet, were driven ashore, stranding their crews in Necropolis.

Highguard.t: Highborn-held Necropolis weathered the storms better than its neighbours but was left facing stranded Grendel raiders. They stole a chapter heirloom, sought an old spy cache and stirred up ghosts.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: orc inhabitants of Apulian wryly noted past magical storms, and the Sarcophan captain delivering ilium for the Imperial Orcs complained about storms around Crown's Quay.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: recalled as the enemy in the war for the Mournwold, when Imperial curses killed thousands on both sides.

The League.t: Forewarned by Chessia Gordost von Temeschwar in their Assembly, League citizens limited casualties, but Sarvos flooded and Spiral was storm-struck. The mana exchange stewards in Sarvos and Tassato faced higher costs.

The Marches.t: The Marches were offered an olive branch through Marcus of the Pale Sun's proposals for reconciliation. At the same time, Fanny Moulder called landowners to vote on leaving half the nation's fields idle, at a cost of 98 rings per farm, in protest against Urizen and the Empire.

Urizen.t: All three Urizeni territories suffered Icy Maw, halving their mana and leaving magicians short-tempered, while Marcus urged Urizen to show Wisdom with a generous gesture of reconciliation to the Marches. Redoubt was also offered a mithril-net great work.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Marcus cited Wintermark magic as having ravaged Marcher farms and suggested Wintermark, like Urizen, owed the Marches a reckoning.

Sound the bells.o: In Spring 386YE, curses born of the feud between Urizen and the Marches battered the Empire: Icy Maw halved mana production across Urizen and drove up mana prices, while Foam and Spittle storms lashed the northern Bay of Catazar against the Grendel. The storms flooded Sarvos, strained foreign trade and stranded Grendel crews in Necropolis.

Necropolis/Coursmouth.t: Mentioned in passing: not named on the page, and covered only by the general storms along the Necropolis coast.

Necropolis/Highrod.t: The Bronze Rill, stranded when the Flying Civet ran aground, were stirring up ghosts. High Exorcist Alessi of the Basilisks of the Labyrinth was charged to defeat them at the Coppice of Athaliah.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Grendel castaways, including a Salt Lord agent, moved towards an old crypt of the broken spy ring in Ada's Woods. Imperial Spymaster Bernard Dugdale was tasked with stopping them recovering intelligence.

Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand.t: Grendel stole a founder's dagger and coin from the chapter of Elijah's Bastion at the Orchard of the Third Step, and Champion of Prosperity Hugh Farrier was charged with reclaiming them. Storms also kept funeral vessels from reaching Sanctuary.

Redoubt/Ventosi.t: The sparsely inhabited plains of Ventosi saw few casualties. Claudius Nightstricken proposed mithril nets across its cliffs, costing 50 mithril and 150 crowns, to blunt future storms and boost Redoubt's mana sites.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Cigno suffered badly from the flooding that overwhelmed Sarvos's meagre sea defences.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory itself is not described; the only echo is the Necropolis chapter named Elijah's Bastion.

Bay of Catazar.t: Curses raised violent storms across the northern Bay, sinking fishing boats, damaging every fleet based on its coasts and driving foreign traders to avoid Imperial ports.

Morrow.t: Morrow remained under Icy Maw, with snowdrifts blocking its passes and its mana sites producing half their usual crystals.

Mournwold.t: Marcus of the Pale Sun settled near Overton and debated with the friars there. He recalled how Rivers Run Red and a Winter curse killed thousands in the Mournwold during the Jotun war.

Necropolis.t: Crown's Quay was flooded and funeral vessels could not reach Sanctuary. Three wrecked Grendel crews were stranded along the coast, giving Imperial heroes the chance to ensure they never return home.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt suffered both Icy Maw and the Bay storms, with lightning striking its towers and its mana output halved. The high-built spires spared it heavy casualties.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos flooded for three days, with Caricomare and Cigno hit hard. The Vandersaar family offered flood defences for 12 white granite and 72 crowns, pending a Senate motion, and the Sarcophan complained of damage to the Alivetti estates.

Spiral.t: Spiral was among the coastal territories battered by the storms, and Marcus noted that Urizen had demanded a reckoning from the League over its loss.

Tassato.t: The mana exchange stewards in Tassato faced rising costs as Urizen's mana shortage spread to the Empire's markets.

Zenith.t: Zenith joined Morrow and Redoubt under Icy Maw, its spires pelted with great hailstones and its mana sites producing half as much.

Sowing on the mountains.d: In Mieriada, floods at Wendell's Hope exposed an ossuary of pre-Imperial Varushkan heroes who fell fighting the Thule. Its wise ones proposed a great work of monument and shrine, costing 30 wains of white granite, 10 of weirwood and 10 Thrones, that would add 50 Synod votes and 25 liao. In Brez, a tempest jade cave at Bredavoi could become a mine yielding 20 ingots a season, but its deep tunnels hide dark spirits. In Opascari, a Terunael orichalcum mine on the Traveller could be restored. In Suvretz, the plans and foundations of the unfinished Irontooth Keep were found, and koboldi offered to help build it. All four lapsed at the Spring Equinox 384YE.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Sentinel in Casinea and Remember Exile in Reikos are named as the fortifications Irontooth Keep might rival.

Navarr.t: The Navarr are said to be very interested in why a Terunael outpost stands on the Traveller in Opascari, and reopening the pass might reveal more for them to study.

Thule.t: The Thule embassy was reportedly damaged by a rockslide, the Wendell's Hope monument would be built partly as a warning to them, and they may claim the reopened Sungold Pass mine if the Empire does not.

Varushka.t: Varushka gained the chance to honour its ancient dead with a pilgrimage site and to commission new mines and a great fortress, with the titles that would follow, in its storm-wracked northern territories.

Sowing on the mountains.o: In Winter 381YE a week-long storm battered the mountains between Volodmartz and Otkodov, and its floods and landslides uncovered four building opportunities: an ancient ossuary in Miekarova and three finds in Volodmartz.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: At Wendell's Hope on the Coldmere, wise ones proposed turning the newly exposed ossuary into a monument and shrine to Courage, visible from the nearby Thule embassy.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Thule armies have three times marched out of Sküld into Suvretz, and the Sungold Pass ruins can be reached as easily from Sküld as from Volodmartz.

Volodmartz/Brez.t: Wagon raiders found a rich tempest jade seam in a cave below Bredavoi peak, which could be commissioned as a mine with a Foreman title, though dark spirits lurk in the deep tunnels.

Volodmartz/Opascari.t: An avalanche on the Traveller uncovered a Terunael orichalcum mine with heat-holding mithril designs, which could be restored with a Warden of the Sungold Pass title before the Thule claim it.

Volodmartz/Suvretz.t: Floods revealed the foundations and original plans of Irontooth Keep, a great fortress to guard against the Thule and Otkodov's creatures, which koboldi were eager to help build.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Sentinel in Casinea is cited as a fortification Irontooth Keep might rival.

Miekarova.t: Floods at Wendell's Hope uncovered an ossuary of ancient Varushkan heroes, and a proposed great work there would draw more pilgrims and grant Synod votes and liao to Varushkan-led congregations in Miekarova.

Otkodov.t: The storm raged through the mountains bordering Otkodov, whose tunnels may connect to Brez and whose warped forest creatures sometimes raid Suvretz.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Remember Exile in Reikos is cited as a fortification Irontooth Keep might rival.

Volodmartz.t: The storm revealed three opportunities in Volodmartz: a tempest jade mine in Brez, a Terunael orichalcum mine in Opascari, and the unfinished Irontooth Keep in Suvretz.

Speak to me.d: Skathe offered formal parley to the Winter Archmage, the Grandmaster of the Celestial Arch and the Custodian of the Bleak Tower. Her gifts for the Sarangrave depend on a sincere show of hatred for the Druj. The Invisible Hand sent assessors into the Empire and Otkodov. Cathan Canae will send Volstann to discuss the frozen citadels and Eoradal. Sadogua's heralds will hold an informal celebration, and he will privately consult the Unfettered Mind about the Lyceum's wards. Ylenwe declined parley but offered a ritual to harmonise Skarsind's white wood and help with Solen's Doubt. Ossegrahn will discuss watering Mareave, and offers lasting protection for Peakedge Stead if the Conclave removes two rituals from Imperial lore through a power of Remorse.

Druj.t: Skathe offers gifts for the Sarangrave if the Empire convinces her of its hatred for the Druj. Ossegrahn warns that the Druj will destroy Peakedge Stead unless his demands are met.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel are not named. Their only link is through Mareave, where eternals discuss Imperial Orc plans to bring fresh water to the territory.

Imperial Orcs.t: Cathan Canae asks the Legion Engineer to explain how the Orcs will hold Eoradal. Ossegrahn wants Orcs at his parley to discuss watering Mareave and peace with the Brine Turtles, and Ylenwe offers a ritual to harmonise Skarsind's white wood.

Navarr.t: Ossegrahn offers lasting protection for Peakedge Stead in Therunin at the price of a power of Remorse. Sadogua invites Navarr magicians to discuss threatened magical places in Therunin, and Skathe speaks of the scions of Terunael's bitterness towards the Druj.

The League.t: Skathe welcomes the Archmage's admission that events in Holberg and Sarvos were the work of Zephaniah's Lament, not her. Both Ylenwe and Ossegrahn take an interest in plans to dam Solen's Doubt in Spiral.

The Marches.t: Sadogua invites Marcher magicians to speak with his apprentices about their studies. He warns that this is their last season of easy access to the Well of Shadows before he seeks a new scholar at the Summer Solstice.

Thule.t: The City of Gold and Lead has sent agents into Otkodov, drawing on its good relations with the Thule to pursue the Autumn Archmage's request.

Urizen.t: The masters of the Celestial Arch and Bleak Tower are invited to Skathe's parley. Cathan Canae questions why three defenders of Redoubt were singled out, and Ossegrahn is sceptical about a fane in Redoubt and the Urizen request about mana-site food.

Varushka.t: Varushkan members of the Unfettered Mind are warned to be very cautious at Sadogua's Lyceum meeting. The eternal is still angry over the Towers of Zulgan Tash.

Wintermark.t: A Wintermark civil servant received Skathe's message. Sadogua's heralds hope to meet the Wintermark magicians responsible for a recent splendid enchantment.

Speak to me.o: Six eternals answered the Imperial archmages' plenipotentiary messages after the Winter Solstice. Skathe, Cathan Canae, Sadogua and Ossegrahn arranged meetings for the Spring Equinox, while the Invisible Hand and Ylenwe chose to act directly instead.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: Cathan Canae wants to hear, through Volstann, how the Imperial Orcs intend to hold Eoradal and the building there, and why they seek her aid rather than the Dragon Beneath the Mountain's.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Ossegrahn wishes to discuss plans to channel the released waters of Solen's Doubt into Icarion.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: Mentioned in passing: Apstrus is not named. Spiral's part in the page concerns damming Solen's Doubt, detailed in the Damming the Doubt wind.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Skathe refers to past events in 'enlightened Holberg', which she says were caused by Zephaniah's Lament, and offers to clear up any doubts about them.

Mareave.t: Ylenwe cautions about the costs of bringing water to the arid territory but judges the plans gentle. Ossegrahn offers to help with founts in north-eastern Mareave.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not named. The page's Varushkan content concerns a warning to Varushkan Unfettered Mind magicians and Sadogua's anger over the Towers of Zulgan Tash.

Otkodov.t: Assessors, brokers and planners from the City of Gold and Lead have been dispatched into Otkodov to speak with the Thule on the Autumn Archmage's behalf.

Redoubt.t: Cathan Canae asks why three particular defenders of Redoubt merit special note. Ossegrahn is prepared, if sceptical, to discuss the Urizen notion of a fane there.

Sarangrave.t: Skathe has prepared gifts to bring weal to the Sarangrave's inhabitants, conditional on a sincere show of Imperial hatred for the Druj. Ossegrahn suggests Peakedge Stead could become a sanctuary for those fighting the vallorn there.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Skathe refers to past events in 'beautiful Sarvos', attributing them to Zephaniah's Lament.

Skarsind.t: Ylenwe offers a way to harmonise the warped white wood. A tree from its edge is to be brought to the Imperial regio and sung through all seven modes using magical chimes, rendering the dangerous Day magic inert.

Spiral.t: Ylenwe has sent heralds to Solen's Doubt to help with damming it. Ossegrahn asks that a representative of Spiral attend his parley to discuss releasing and channelling its waters.

Therunin.t: Ossegrahn's protection of Peakedge Stead and his Houses of Healing will fail within a day of the Equinox unless the Conclave removes Rivers Run Red and Mountain Remembers Its Youth from lore. Sadogua invites talk of the territory's threatened magical places.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is not named. The only Marches content is Sadogua's invitation to Marcher magicians and his note about the Well of Shadows.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the herald of the City of Gold and Lead thanks Vossk of Zenith Ascendant for her concise missive.

Spear of the stars.d: With Crow's Ridge held by the Imperial Orcs, the passes from western Otkodov were open. Rak Who Speaks for the Dragons United now lodged above the Red Lantern in Void. The Thule offered three things. They would join the Northern trade network if the Senate built a road from Torfast to Crow's Ridge, and would open a trading post in southern Urdur. They asked for an Ambassador to the Thule, preferably a Varushkan national title. They offered 30 wains of white granite for the Gildenheim runeforge relics. The Wintermark Assembly's judgements demanded the return of enslaved citizens and reparations. The Senate appointed Juha the Spider as Ambassador to Otkodov, refused to make it a Varushkan title, and built an embassy by Autumn.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orcs held Crow's Ridge after Crow's Keep fell, received cautious Thule overtures, and could trade with the Thule in Skarsind and act as observers at any Thule excavation of Gildenheim.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: rumours spoke of private negotiations between agents of the Dragons and Navarr emissaries.

Thule.t: The Thule, content with Dogri Thulebane's removal, sought trade, an ambassador and Gildenheim's relics, and Rak revealed the names of the five Dragons. They faced Wintermark demands over slaves and reparations, and the Senate ultimately appointed an Imperial Ambassador to Otkodov.

Varushka.t: Varushka gained the ilium Bourse seat, hosted Rak in Void, and was the Thule's preferred source of an ambassador, though the Senate declined to make the post a Varushkan national title.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's National Assembly led opposition to the détente, demanding the return of Imperial citizens enslaved by the Thule and reparations for Winterfolk murdered in Crow's Ridge's green iron mines.

Spear of the stars.o: With Dogri Thulebane captured and Crow's Keep ruined, the Thule extended cautious friendship to the northern Empire through their envoy Rak. They offered a trade link, an ambassadorship and a deal over Gildenheim's relics, while Wintermark pressed demands over slaves and murdered Winterfolk.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: As part of a trade agreement, the Thule proposed a trading post in southern Urdur, open to Imperial merchants and with safe passage guaranteed for them.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Crow's Keep lay in ruins and the region was under Imperial Orc control, with its passes now open. Any Senate road from Torfast would have to reach one of them, and the Wintermark reparations demand concerns Winterfolk murdered in its green iron mines.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, its link being the Skarsind matters of Thule trade and the Gildenheim runeforge.

Volodmartz/Brez.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, its link being Varushka's dealings with the Thule envoy and the new ilium Bourse seat.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named, its link being Varushka's growing dealings with the Thule and the proposed Northern trade network.

Otkodov.t: The Thule homeland's western passes into Skarsind were opened, the Thule offered to build a road on their side of the mountains, and the Senate created the post of Ambassador to Otkodov, completing an embassy by Autumn.

Skarsind.t: With Crow's Keep ruined and Crow's Ridge in Imperial Orc hands, Skarsind became the gateway for any Thule trade road, and the Thule sought permission to take the relics of its Gildenheim runeforge.

Volodmartz.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named, its link being the Varushkan threads of the story, such as the ilium Bourse seat and Rak's lodgings in Void.

Splitting the pot.d: After the Synod condemned Whittle's Hatred sect, General Ciaphas 'Black Jack' Dekar ordered the Bounders to encircle Whittle, admitting only Marcher magistrates and militia. Short-handed, Magistrate Cooper negotiated for a week without success. He then deputised two hundred and fifty Bounders and advanced. In the Battle of Whittle Hill more than two-thirds of the Whittlers died, along with thirty-three Bounders and sixteen militia. The three surviving condemned were tried, and investigators found many villagers had been anointed with auras of Hatred using stockpiled liao. Whittle is now a ghost town, and the Mournwold remained calm. The legality of Dekar's actions remains an open question.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Whittlers resented that they had been condemned through the actions of the Dawnish Cardinal of Vigilance.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Whittlers credited their Hatred of the Jotun with sustaining their resistance during the occupation, and accused the Marchers of doing the Jotun's work.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: passing Navarr are named as people a magistrate might normally have recruited to help, had outsiders not been barred.

The League.t: Tassato militia rounded up the Whittler enclave of Little Mournwold and its alder Margaret Steward was executed. The Marchers there are leaving, League citizens are moving in, and the flow of Mournwold green iron to Tassato's businesses has ended.

The Marches.t: Marcher soldiers and militia fought and killed fellow Marchers at Whittle, wiping out the condemned sect at heavy cost. Most Marchers blamed the Whittlers for their fate, but General Dekar's conduct remains contested.

Splitting the pot.o: In Spring 384YE the Bounders sealed off the Mournwold village of Whittle so that only Marchers could try its Hatred sect. When the villagers refused to surrender, a brutal battle left most of them dead, and the sect's enclave in Tassato was broken up.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Whittle was encircled by the Bounders and largely destroyed in the Battle of Whittle Hill. Its leaders, priests and many young defenders were killed and the village left deserted.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: A few hundred Tassato militia seized the Whittler enclave here and executed alder Margaret Steward. The remaining Marchers are leaving and the city is reclaiming their homes.

Mournwold.t: The village of Whittle was besieged and stormed, leaving it an empty ghost town with orphans rehomed and an orchard planted over the graves. The wider territory stayed calm despite shock at the violence.

Tassato.t: The Little Mournwold enclave was broken up with little resistance and is being abandoned to League citizens, ending its trade in Mournwold green iron.

Spreading the Way.d: Rane Shardbearer, Senator for Kallavesa, sought the appraisal at the Summer Solstice. Lisane de Terresford was engaged in Sumaah, so Gerard la Salle assigned Naomi. She gave three caveats: faith is hard to prognosticate, no one-size-fits-all solution exists, and conversion does not guarantee good relations, as the Lasambrians showed when they joined the Jotun. She outlined aura-led, doctrine-led and culture-led approaches, drawing on the Sand Fishers, Barrens septs, Apulian Orcs, Suranni and Asavea. She urged the Synod, Senate and other bodies to take small, careful steps, and to commission future appraisals on specific groups and simple goals.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: their miasma pillars, which the Sand Fishers lived under, and the rebellion of three Druj armies in the Barrens are cited as examples, as is the risk of Imperial Lore falling into Druj hands.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: former Grendel who joined the Empire are said to wear their new religious beliefs like a loose cloak, but still to hold them.

Jotun.t: Naomi judged that converting the Jotun would be incredibly difficult and dangerous, but that a doctrine-led approach would suit them best, given their established ancestor worship and respected ghodi. The Lasambrians, who were converted to the Way and then joined the Jotun, were cited as a warning.

The League.t: The League's willingness to give up land to the Sand Fishers was called pivotal in drawing that sept towards the Empire and the Way. Naomi also saw no reason why future League Orcs should not become bishops.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn missionaries' debates in Urizen centuries ago are cited as an example of a doctrine-led approach, and Urizen also serves as an example of a fortification that can be divined precisely.

Wintermark.t: The appraisal was commissioned by Rane Shardbearer, Senator for Kallavesa. A monument to a fallen Wintermark hero is used to illustrate what Night rituals can divine.

Spreading the Way.o: Naomi of Virtue's Rest delivered a civil service appraisal on bringing non-Wayist cultures within the Empire into the Way of Virtue. She concluded that no general answer or commission was possible, and instead offered three broad approaches and urged the Empire to appraise specific groups with simple goals.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Naomi credits the gift of Misericorde to the Sand Fishers, offered alongside the auras and the Virtues, with making them enormously well inclined towards the Empire and open to the Way.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: a fortification built in Hahnmark is given as an example of a solution that works the same anywhere, unlike efforts to spread faith.

Holberg.t: The Sand Fishers' settlement in Holberg, on land given up by the League, is presented as the key example of conversion succeeding through auras combined with a secure homeland.

Kallavesa.t: The motion behind the appraisal came from Kallavesa's senator, and the consecration of Kallavesa's marshes is cited as a true aura that moves Imperial citizens.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: a fortification in Redoubt is used as an example of a solution that works the same anywhere.

Spreading the word.d: Since the death of Empress Britta, Livia Cascade's Torchbearers had been recording citizens' accounts of Past-Life Visions. The Spider's Vantage Spire in Redoubt then published them Empire-wide. Citizens across the Empire devoured them eagerly. Navarri shuddered at a remembered fall of Terunael, Highborn debated an ancient exarch honouring a herald, Winterfolk scops retold their last King's negotiations with the First Empress' ambassador, and some Imperial Orc preachers bristled at mentions of their enslaved ancestors. Storytellers from less austere traditions embellished the tales freely. The accounts are retellings of other people's stories, not guaranteed to be true, and their widespread publication is expected to have unpredictable effects in years to come.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Torchbearers, led by Livia Cascade, the Seer of the Gateway, compiled the accounts, and a Redoubt publishing-house spread them across the Empire, making Urizen the source of the first published Past-Life Visions in living memory.

Spreading the word.o: Accounts of Past-Life Visions, gathered by a team of Torchbearers under Livia Cascade, the Seer of the Gateway, were published across the Empire by the Spider's Vantage Spire, a publishing-house in Redoubt. It was the first such publication in living memory, and possibly the first since Nicovar's purge.

Redoubt.t: The Spider's Vantage Spire, a publishing-house in Redoubt, printed the accounts and distributed them throughout the Empire.

Stand amid the roar.d: Under Determination of Ice Kaisa, the Narwhal's Spear broke the Cult's strongholds with few casualties and ended its plans to raise an army. The Sun Chamber located all four obelisks, in Tanikipari, Suaq Fount, Suaq Wastes and the Thule-held Silver Peaks, and recovered a coded message. Highborn inquisitors learned that the Cult meant to make Sermersuaq as savage as the Claw. Destroying one obelisk limits the curse to regions that still hold one. Destroying all four ends it. Corrin Arrowsbane, the Sun Chamber's Counsel Zoria and Speaker Nicodemus were each charged with destroying a pillar and slaying its Voice. The Thule said the Dragons would attend to the fourth.

Highguard.t: Highborn pilgrims answering Destin of the Woodwych Harts went north, and their inquisitors exposed the Cult's plan. A Highborn band failed to reach Suaq Fount, so the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly, Nicodemus of Balthazar's Vineyard, is now charged with destroying that pillar.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the page recalls that the Jotun not long ago stormed through Sermersuaq.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Megaris of the Empty Sword, a keen-eyed young sentinel from Spiral, spotted the first obelisk for the Sun Chamber.

Thule.t: Thule warlocks investigating feral beasts and curse wars examined the fourth obelisk in the Silver Peaks alongside Sun Chamber scouts. They said the Dragons would attend to it, without clearly promising to destroy it.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Narwhal's Spear returned home and shattered the Cult while trying to spare its misguided kin. The Winterfolk of Sermersuaq hunted out cultists, and Corrin Arrowsbane is tasked with destroying the Tanikipari pillar.

Stand amid the roar.o: In Autumn 387YE the Narwhal's Spear, the Sun Chamber and pilgrims answering the Wintermark and Highborn assemblies moved against the Cult of the Falconer in Sermersuaq, shattering its forces and uncovering a plan to mark the territory with the power of the Claw using four buried white granite obelisks.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The fourth obelisk stands here in Thule-held land near the Stonefield Ice Caves. The Thule warlocks investigating it have promised only that the Dragons will attend to it.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: An obelisk guarded by the Voice of the Fount stands here, where cultists sought to disrupt the Pride of Ikka's Tears and seize its mithril. Its destruction now falls to the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: Cultists rallied around the Voice of the Wastes guard an obelisk here, and the Counsel of the Sun Chamber, Zoria, is responsible for destroying it and slaying the Voice.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: The first obelisk was found buried near Ittanpari. After Merewalh the Fox's band was driven back, Corrin Arrowsbane is asked to destroy it and kill the Voice of Tanikipari.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the coded message was found on the body of one of the Chosen, a merchant originally from Kallavesa.

Sermersuaq.t: The Cult's army was broken across the territory, but four buried obelisks threaten to curse Sermersuaq with the savagery of the Claw at the Equinox unless they are destroyed.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Megaris of the Empty Sword, who found the first obelisk, is a sentinel from Spiral.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Suaq Wastes obelisk lies close to the border with Tromsa.

Stand proud, you're strong.d: The Assembly's statement, upheld with a greater majority of 216-0 in Summer 388YE, gave it a year to direct Freeborn efforts. Each season it may choose one option by statement of principle. The options cover four areas: fortifying Kahraman, Feroz, Segura or Madruga; approaching eternals such as Adamant, Cathan Canae, Janon (who is under enmity), Sorin or Ephisis; seeking closer ties with the Suranni, Faraden, Morajasse or Marracossans; or building spy networks against the Lasambrians, Jotun or Suranni. For a year, Freeborn armies may also Burn Brightly when defending Freeborn territory. This greatly boosts their defence and the casualties they inflict, but doubles their own losses.

Grendel.t: The Grendel are named as the threat the Coast must fortify Feroz and Madruga against, while the Grendel Protectorate of Morajasse is offered as a possible mortal ally for further mutual military deals.

Imperial Orcs.t: The proposed Suranni espionage option depends on Imperial Orc military units operating the new Arbonne spy network, using the cover of guarding Freeborn merchants.

Jotun.t: The Jotun are treated as a likely source of attack through Liathaven, and spying on them there is one of the options open to the Assembly. The page also notes the Faraden recently re-signed their peace treaty with them.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn Assembly can direct its people towards up to four defensive projects over the year. Meanwhile, Freeborn armies gain the Burn Brightly order to defend their homelands at great cost to themselves.

Stand proud, you're strong.o: After the Freeborn National Assembly raised its highest calling to defend the nation's borders, the hakima identified over a dozen ways to strengthen the Brass Coast's defences, of which the Assembly could pursue up to four over the following year. Freeborn armies were also inspired to take a ferocious new defensive order in Freeborn-held territories.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: Mentioned in passing: in the opening fiction, the commander at Mora's Rock dreads the prospect of the Suranni taking Afarjasse.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mora's Rock commander doubts the Suranni will stop at the Cazar Straits.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: The fiction shows the Mora's Rock garrison under orders to hold the fortification, fearing both Imperial and Suranni attack. The Protectorate that controls it is offered as a possible partner for mutual military deals.

Madruga/Crucible.t: Mentioned in passing: several hakima have raised concerns about threats that might emerge from Crucible as a reason to fortify Madruga further.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction notes that news of the conquest of Free Landing has reached Mora's Rock.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named directly, and the opening fiction only notes that the Suranni now hold the islands along the Coast.

Feroz.t: Fortifying Feroz is one option, to guard against an eventual Grendel return and possibly the southern border, alongside existing efforts to restore its people's livelihoods. Freeborn armies there may Burn Brightly in its defence.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman has been largely undefended since the fall of Fort Braydon despite holding three bourse seats. Fortifying it against renewed Lasambrian raids is one of the options offered.

Liathaven.t: A new spy network in Jotun-held Liathaven is proposed, since its earlier network was destroyed, Imperial maps are increasingly outdated and any Jotun attack on the Coast would likely come from there.

Madruga.t: The completed Well of Life in Madruga reduces Imperial casualties across the Coast. Further fortification is proposed against the Grendel armada and possible threats from Crucible, and the Marracossans are named as a potential ally with an interest in its safety.

Reinos.t: With the Imperial spy network in Reinos decommissioned almost two years ago, a new one is proposed to watch the Suranni campaign against the Lasambrian homeland.

Segura.t: Segura has only recently found quiet after nearly two decades of war, and Adamant has already offered protection now that the City of Wonders is complete. Further fortification of this remote territory is one of the options.

Standards.d: Queen Yrsa Jansdóttir's Lion of the North, reinforced by Tromsan siege engineers, joined Derun Stonetower's Tower of the North. Jarl Haakon's warband and Stephen of Sarcombe's yegarra fought alongside them. Captured Marchers, orcs included, were offered the Choice, and those who refused became thralls. Rumour says Haakon condemned the yegarra's dishonourable conduct and Yrsa made Stephen swear to uphold Jotun honour or be cast out. Nearly ten thousand orcs overwhelmed about six thousand defenders at Sarcombe, which had no fortress. The Imperial positions and ministries tied to Sarcombe were lost. The people expect the Tusks to return by the Autumn Equinox. Jotun ghosts were also sighted near the Liathaven border.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named only to suggest the Jotun are unlikely to harm the Sarcombe Register, since they are not the Druj.

Jotun.t: Two Jotun armies led by Queen Yrsa and Derun Stonetower, aided by Jarl Haakon and Stephen of Sarcombe's yegarra, retook much of Southmoor and raised their standards over Sarcombe. Rumours also told of friction between Haakon and Stephen over the yegarra's conduct.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr are suggested as possible helpers in investigating the Jotun ghosts, since the orcs currently hold Liathaven.

The Marches.t: The Marches lost three-fifths of Southmoor and the market town of Sarcombe, along with the ministries, offices and incomes tied to it. Marcher orcs who refused the Choice were made thralls again, and the folk of the Mourn now expect the Tusks to return by the Autumn Equinox.

Standards.o: In Summer 386YE the Jotun armies the Lion of the North and the Tower of the North marched out of Liathaven and conquered three-fifths of Southmoor in the Mournwold, storming the market town of Sarcombe and driving out its Marcher and Highborn defenders.

Liathaven/Liaven's Glen.t: The Jotun force moved east out of Liaven's Glen to begin the invasion, and the Jotun ghosts appeared to be heading towards the Glen of Red Shadow there.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Mentioned in passing: the defeated Imperial garrisons and some Southmoor folk made a fighting retreat towards the Greensward.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: Mentioned in passing: the retreating Imperial soldiers and some Southmoor folk fell back towards the Ore Hills.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Three-fifths of Southmoor, including Sarcombe, fell after the town's gates were broken by siege engines. A beacon now burns where Hillstop once stood, Jotun standards fly over the Old Oak Inn, and those who stayed face the Choice. Jotun ghosts were also reported in the north of the region.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun armies were marching into Bregasland at the same time, and some of the Fisher household, their ambitions there shattered, now fought under Stephen of Sarcombe.

Liathaven.t: The Jotun-held forests served as the launching point for the invasion of Southmoor. A haunt of Jotun ghosts was sighted on its border with the Mournwold.

Mournwold.t: The Jotun returned to the Mourn, seizing most of Southmoor and Sarcombe and once again forcing the Choice on its people.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Olgafsdottir of Tromsa sent siege engineers south to bolster Queen Yrsa's army.

Standing in the sun.d: After Ashborn Atla accepted Highborn aid, priests and experts visited Skarsind. The Senate paid 100 thrones, with Golden Pyramid support, to bring miners to Skarsind. Orc units now upgrade for one fewer wain of mithril, and an army can defend the Black Forge with improved resupply. General, Highborn and Varushkan Assembly mandates opened a Bone Pilgrimage for orc and Highborn units everywhere except Urizen. The Senate declined to outlaw exorcising orc ghosts. The Feldspar Distillery and Wise Arborist were created, but realmsroot secrets were not shared with Highguard. An amended Legion Engineer let the Tamazi wall Gildenheim, completed shortly before Autumn 387YE. The Sannite fighting pit was not built, and the Ambition Assembly pursued a memorial to Thrace.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: as the former masters who denied the Ethengraw their own weapons, from whom the Illarawm hid their ancestors' bones, and whose auras the Yerende knew in Ossium.

Highguard.t: Highborn priests, gardeners and engineers offered peerless kinship to the orc septs and consecrated Loyalty and Prosperity auras in the Palace of Flowers. Highborn military units may now join the Bone Pilgrimage, though the orcs chose not to share herbsheart with High Chalcis.

Imperial Orcs.t: The septs gained cheaper unit upgrades from the Black Forge, a Wise Arborist teaching realmsroot cultivation, walls around Gildenheim and the Bone Pilgrimage to bring their ancestors home. Their plea to outlaw exorcism of orc ghosts and the Sannite fighting pit both went unanswered.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Tamazi who had seen the walls of Temeschwar and Holberg were spurred to want Gildenheim fortified.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: as the breakers of Gildenheim's old walls, holders of a fortification at Crow's Ridge and builders of old mine-workings in Skarsind.

Urizen.t: Because the General Assembly mandate lacked a greater majority, Urizen remains the one Imperial nation where orcs seeking their ancestors' bones are not welcome.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan Assembly sent Yevanshka to urge Varushkans to support the Bone Pilgrimage, so orcs seeking Sunstorm ancestors in the vales are welcomed. Varushkan units may face any dark forces this stirs through the Adventure in Varushka.

Standing in the sun.o: Highguard extended its peerless kinship to the Imperial Orcs, helping the six septs in Skarsind work together in virtue and setting out proposals for each sept. In response the Senate funded miners for the Black Forge, assemblies backed a Bone Pilgrimage, the Feldspar Distillery was built and Gildenheim was walled.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Mentioned in passing: as the site of the Thule fortification built from the ruins of the old Crow's Keep.

Skarsind/Estermark.t: Mentioned in passing: as the forested hills where many Sannite live and where a Sannite folly might one day be built.

Skarsind/Gildermark.t: Gildenheim was fortified with Tamazi labour by Autumn 387YE, and the Black Forge in the hills above the city now offers improved resupply to a defending army. A proposed fighting pit near the Legion's Rookery was not built.

Skarsind/Skogei Glens.t: Mentioned in passing: as home to the Will, the Winterfolk-built castle facing Otkodov.

Skarsind/Solvihill.t: The Yerende Palace of Flowers received Highborn consecrations of Loyalty and Prosperity, and the Feldspar Distillery was built there to train orc herbalists to grow realmsroot under the Wise Arborist.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn likened a possible memorial to Thrace to Atuman's tomb on the cliffs overlooking the bay.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, but linked through the Highborn comparison with Atuman's tomb.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Tamazi who had visited Holberg were inspired to want walls for Gildenheim, and its walls inspired Ketus Stonewalk's impractical first plan.

Necropolis.t: The Highborn Assembly's support for the Bone Pilgrimage widened the stewards of the dead's calling, offering occasional chances to recover Imperial heroes and bring them back to the Necropolis.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: as the old home from which the Illarawm carried their ancestors' bones and the Yerende came to Skarsind.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: as the land whose potential aggression the Will in Skogei Glens was built to guard against.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: not named, but as Urizen land it lies outside the Bone Pilgrimage's welcome.

Reikos.t: A mandate could have had the Yerende supply herbsheart to the Gardens of High Chalcis, adding realmsroot to Reikos herb gardens, but the Imperial Orcs did not pass it.

Skarsind.t: The territory gained new miners and prospectors, Black Forge resupply for defending armies, the Ossuary Temple as the Bone Pilgrimage's destination, the Feldspar Distillery in Solvihill and new walls around Gildenheim.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: its walls galvanised the Tamazi and set the standard the Walls of Gildenheim were meant to rival.

Starfall.d: The Stalker, a red star visible only in parts of the north, grew until it eclipsed other stars. Shooting stars carrying small amounts of ilium drew prospectors north, and three larger fragments fell in Kallavesa, Bregasland near Rushring, and West Ranging in Liathaven. The Senate and Conclave favoured diverting the star to Sküld under a peace agreement with the Thule, but Magistrate Abraham warned that someone must actually work the magic. Divinations showed it would otherwise hit Miekarova, devastating one region and costing every resource there improved beyond level one a level. Only spontaneous Autumn magic, worked in Miekarova or at the Anvil regio within a narrow window, could shift it. More ilium came to auction, and the star's strange influence on lineaged people and certain ailments ended.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Stalker was visible over Wickmoor and Sandling in Dawn's territory of Weirwater.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on the page and is linked only to the wider starfall.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Stalker could be seen in the northern sky over Skarsind.

Jotun.t: A large star fragment fell in the forests of West Ranging in Jotun-held Liathaven, and Imperial prospectors went searching for its ilium even in Jotun lands.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the star was visible over Hercynia, whose senator seconded the Senate statement on diverting the Stalker to Sküld.

The Marches.t: One of the three large star fragments struck Bregasland near Rushring, and the smoke and debris made the likely ilium bounty hard to locate.

Thule.t: Under the peace treaty, the Senate and Conclave backed using a Thule ritual to divert the Stalker onto Sküld, apparently by agreement with the northern orcs. The page notes that no one had yet actually worked the magic.

Varushka.t: The Stalker was visible across all of Varushka and was set to strike Miekarova, destroying one region and costing its improved resources a level, unless magic moved it. Volodmartz's senator proposed the diversion to Sküld.

Wintermark.t: A large star fragment fell in the marshes of Kallavesa, and the Stalker was visible over Sermersuaq and over Northspires and Bruckland in Hahnmark.

Starfall.o: In Autumn 380YE the red star known as the Stalker began its final descent, set to strike Miekarova during the Autumn Equinox unless ritual magic diverted it. Showers of shooting stars scattered ilium-bearing fragments across the north.

Hahnmark/Bruckland.t: Mentioned in passing: Bruckland was one of the places where the Stalker could be seen.

Hahnmark/Northspires.t: Mentioned in passing: Northspires was one of the places where the Stalker could be seen.
