Liathaven/West Ranging.t: A large star fragment burned down into the deep forests here, leaving smoke and debris and drawing prospectors after its ilium.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Sküld was the Senate's and Conclave's chosen target for the diverted Stalker as part of the Thule peace treaty, though actually moving the star still required someone to work the magic.

Weirwater/Sandling.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible in the sky over Sandling.

Weirwater/Wickmoor.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible in the sky over Wickmoor.

Bregasland.t: A large star fragment struck near Rushring, throwing up smoke and debris, and prospectors searched for what may be a significant bounty of ilium.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page and is linked only to the wider starfall.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Stalker was visible in the skies over Northspires and Bruckland.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible over Hercynia, and its senator seconded the Senate statement on diverting the star.

Kallavesa.t: One of the three larger star fragments struck the marshes of Kallavesa, where its exact resting place was obscured but prospectors hunted for ilium.

Liathaven.t: A large star fragment fell in the deep forests of West Ranging, drawing Imperial prospectors into Jotun-held Liathaven in search of ilium.

Miekarova.t: Divinations showed the Stalker would land here during the Autumn Equinox, devastating one region and costing every resource improved beyond level one a level. Any ritual to divert it had to be worked here or at the Anvil regio.

Otkodov.t: The Senate and Conclave declared their wish to divert the Stalker onto Sküld under the peace treaty with the Thule, though the target region within the territory was not public.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Stalker was visible in the northern sky over Sermersuaq.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Stalker was visible in the northern sky over Skarsind.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: the red star could be seen over Wickmoor and Sandling.

Stars and sigils.d: Beast attacks and unexplained brawling spread from Sermersuaq into Skarsind, Hahnmark and Hercynia, and more faintly further south. The Mystics of Ishal offered the Ravenseer three mutually exclusive paths. A Night enchantment filled Kallavesa with feasting. All seventy villagers of Zurrah in Ossium were found devoured, with their skulls and clothes missing. The Grand Conjunction made older army and fleet projections defunct, though they could be exchanged for mana, and it empowered several personal enchantments. The Claw stirred violent urges. The Penumbral Veil persisted over most of the Empire, and Sir Gaeris's Twisted Torc enriched the Barrens. Other omens included a doom-bell in the Bay of Catazar, vision-dreams in Casinea and a mysterious tavern in Mournwold.

Dawn.t: Dawn saw unexplained animal attacks in the wild places of Astolat and Weirwater. All four of its territories lay under the shroud, and Sir Gaeris's use of the Twisted Torc brought prosperity to the Barrens.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Feroz, which Grendel held, is listed among the shrouded territories, where it is described as the Brass Coast's reclaimed land.

Highguard.t: Liao dreams in Casinea took the form of fragmentary past-life visions linked to a dramaturgical confluence, and Bastion, Casinea and Reikos remained shrouded.

Imperial Orcs.t: Skarsind was caught up in the wave of beast attacks and violence, and the largest wolf pack seen since the orcs gained their homeland attacked the Great Herd in Estermark.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the Jotun were feeling the spreading violence, and their territory of Bregasland was listed among those under the shroud.

Navarr.t: Hercynia suffered pronounced beast attacks, and a dire bear struck travellers in Miaren's Goldglades. Navarr-owned resources in the Barrens also shared in the cheaper upgrades there.

The Brass Coast.t: Kahraman, Segura and the reclaimed Feroz lay under the Penumbral Veil, leaving their night skies strange and unfamiliar.

The League.t: All five League cities remained shrouded, with Sarvos veiled over three times more strongly than elsewhere. Temeschwar saw unexplained animal attacks, though not from rats.

The Marches.t: A mysterious Wintermark-style tavern, the Crow's Rest, appeared in the Ore Hills of Mournwold, and Mitwold and Upwold remained shrouded.

Thule.t: The Thule would not say whether the violence had reached Otkodov, and rumour in Ossium blamed Thule cannibals for the slaughter at Zurrah.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the attempted raid on Redoubt is cited in the tale of the doom-bell, and Urizen lore and the Doyen of the Spires are referenced elsewhere.

Varushka.t: The whole village of Zurrah in Ossium was found slaughtered and devoured, western Karov saw animal attacks, and Karsk, Miekarova and Ossium remained shrouded.

Wintermark.t: Sermersuaq was the heart of the spreading beast attacks, the Ravenseer was offered a choice of three tasks for the Mystics of Ishal, and Kallavesa enjoyed a season of enchanted feasting.

Stars and sigils.o: In Spring 387YE a series of magical and uncanny events swept the Empire. Maddened beasts and sudden violence spread from Sermersuaq, a Varushkan village was slaughtered in Ossium, and a Grand Conjunction of the Great Wyrm and the Mountain unravelled warlike magic while empowering other enchantments.

Miaren/Goldglades.t: A dire bear attacked travellers in Goldglades, leaving two dead and half a dozen badly injured; Roadwardens prevented worse.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: The Crow's Rest, a mysterious tavern with a Wintermark feel, appeared high on a rocky hill in the Ore Hills.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: The slaughtered village of Zurrah lay on the edges of the Bonewood, and nearby communities were urged to take extra care.

Ossium/Galath Fields.t: Consternation spread in the Galath Fields when Zurrah's usual Spring trade caravan never arrived, prompting the investigation.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Zurrah, whose villagers were found devoured, stood on the edges of the Webwood.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: Mystics of Ishal found an isolated hall here holding vellum records of the runesmith Storm's Folly and their study of the artoks.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: Heroes hunting the Suaq Wastes each season helped keep losses to a minimum as maddened beasts took hunters from the Hall of the Hunters.

Skarsind/Estermark.t: The largest wolf pack seen since the orcs gained their homeland attacked the Great Herd. It was driven off under the Shepherd of the Great Herd, but sporadic attacks continued.

Astolat.t: The wild places of Astolat saw unexplained animal attacks as the Spring Equinox approached, and the territory remained under the shroud.

Bastion.t: Bastion remained under the Penumbral Veil, its night skies showing displaced stars and odd lights.

Bay of Catazar.t: A bell was heard tolling above or beneath the bay's dark waters, filling sailors with dread and seeming to herald, or avert, shipwrecks.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland remained under the Penumbral Veil that persisted across most of the Empire.

Casinea.t: Liao dedication dreams in Casinea became snippets of past-life visions, some unknown to the Echoes, and the territory remained shrouded.

Feroz.t: Feroz remained under the Penumbral Veil, where it was described as the Brass Coast's reclaimed territory.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark suffered pronounced attacks by beasts and mundane animals, along with outbreaks of deadly brawling.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia was among the four territories worst hit by maddened beasts and sudden violence, and it remained shrouded.

Holberg.t: Holberg remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.

Kahraman.t: Kahraman remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.

Kallavesa.t: A Night enchantment filled Kallavesa with dreams of feasting and good company and left lasting benefits for its residents. It may also explain why the north of the territory was spared the beast attacks.

Karov.t: The wild places of western Karov saw unexplained animal attacks as the Spring Equinox approached.

Karsk.t: Karsk remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.

Miaren.t: Northern Miaren was not spared the attacks: a dire bear struck travellers in Goldglades. The territory remained shrouded.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.

Mournwold.t: A mysterious tavern called the Crow's Rest appeared out of the fog on a rocky hill, welcoming those who accepted its hospitality.

Ossium.t: All seventy villagers of Zurrah were found slain and gnawed, with their skulls and clothes missing, and folk across Ossium were urged to secure their gates against strangers.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: it was unknown whether the spreading violence had reached Otkodov, and the Thule were not saying.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the attempted raid on Redoubt is noted as the time the Lighthouse at Nikephoros fell and the bell-tolling grew stronger.

Reikos.t: Reikos remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos lay under the strongest shroud in the Empire, more than three times as powerful as those over other territories.

Segura.t: Segura remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq was the source of the escalating beast attacks and violence. A captured husk from the Gullet awaited vivisection by an Unfettered Mind magician, and the territory remained shrouded.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind suffered pronounced beast attacks and violence, including a massive wolf pack's assault on the Great Herd.

Spiral.t: Spiral remained under the Penumbral Veil, and the page points to a separate wind on odd dramaturgical events in the city.

Tassato.t: Tassato remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar saw unexplained animal attacks in its wild places, though rats there were unaffected, and the territory remained shrouded.

The Barrens.t: Sir Gaeris's use of the Twisted Torc spread prosperity across the Barrens, making most personal resources there cheaper to upgrade until the Autumn Equinox. The territory remained shrouded.

Upwold.t: Upwold remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater saw unexplained animal attacks in its wild places, and the territory remained shrouded.

Start a fire.d: The Quiet Step and its allies used Surut's fire to throw back the vallorn's push into West Ranging, but did not take the whole region. A force unlike anything seen before seems to be at work in Liathaven. Retaking the ancient Westwood is a far riskier prospect, and it must happen by the Winter Solstice. Several options were offered. The Synod could pass mandates urging soldiers to fight in Liathaven. Surut offered more boons in return for Conclave amity. Brokers proposed a ministry in Miaren supplying anti-vallorn tools. The Dance of Navarr and Thorn had already restored trods in Mournwold and around Liathaven, leaving only Spiral's trods broken.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj withdrawal left the empty space the vallorn spread into, and Zenith is said to have fallen to them.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a soldier refers to rumours of a massacre in Spiral.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: a Marcher soldier has heard there are Jotun in Wintermark.

Navarr.t: The Quiet Step won a costly victory, and the Navarr assembly could bind its thorns to the Liathaven fight by mandate. Navarr brokers and vates were weighing a Miaren ministry and help from Surut or Arhallogen.

The Marches.t: Marcher troops fought beside the Navarr to burn out the vallorn in Liathaven. The trods in the Marcher-held Mournwold were repaired during the Winter Solstice.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: a soldier predicts war with the Thule again soon.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the Empire's ongoing wars.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Marchers talk of marching north to Sermersuaq against the Jotun.

Start a fire.o: After the Navarr and their Marcher allies drove the vallorn back from West Ranging in Liathaven, the vates declared the vallorn weakened, opening a rare chance to attack and reclaim the Westwood before the Winter Solstice.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns thwarted a similar vallorn expansion here a few years earlier.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: The vallorn's push here was driven back by Surut's fire, but the Empire does not control the whole region. Securing it would spare an attack on Westwood the penalties of a beachhead.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: This ancient heart of the vallorn, untouched for over a thousand years, could be reclaimed by a well-supported attack before the Winter Solstice. Divination is needed first to gauge its strength.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: its earlier vallorn expansion is compared with Liathaven's, and the restored trods now encircle its vallorn.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the trods now wrap around its vallorn.

Liathaven.t: The vallorn here was beaten back and weakened, and a mysterious new power seems to be stirring. The Westwood could be reclaimed if enough force arrives before the Winter Solstice.

Miaren.t: Navarr brokers gathered here and proposed building a brokerage to supply roseweald, bladeroot, Oil of Blackroot and Scorpion's Sting daggers. It could only be built at the Spring Equinox.

Mournwold.t: The Dance of Navarr and Thorn reinforced and repaired trods here that had suffered thirty years or more of neglect.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Marchers speculate about marching north to Sermersuaq.

Spiral.t: It is the only territory where the trods remain broken and fading. Most vates believe they could be rewoven from the Anvil regio despite the plateau's dark influence.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the trods now wrap around its vallorn.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: a soldier says Zenith has gone to the Druj.

Start a war.d: The Fangs, a thirteen-rock mithril mine in the Bitter Strand, fell into Imperial hands in poor repair: 16 wains a season for 20 thrones upkeep, with a possible 300-throne rebuild. Nineteen wains' worth of worked mithril arms became spoils for the Military Council. The Rahvin, about 500 strong, fled to the Carmine Fields with Irra Harah's help and vowed to retake the Fangs, facing destruction by Houndsgate unless ceded the land. The civil service raised a motion requiring fortifications to resist any attack, whatever its source. Archavion and his supporters were sentenced to death, and the Senate ceded the Bitter Strand to the Rahvin. A Dawnish Assembly veto was not upheld.

Dawn.t: Dawn was bitterly divided: Gryphons hailed Archavion for securing the Barrens and its mithril, while Unicorns, inspired by the Assembly's liberation crusade, wanted the Fangs ceded to the Rahvin. Archavion and his supporters were ultimately sentenced to death.

Druj.t: The Druj left a cruel legacy of slave cells at the Fangs. They were said to be spreading word of Imperial massacres to their subjects, undermining hopes that their slaves would rise against them.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn armies were noted as part of the Barrens liberation crusade, and several Highborn heroes are listed among those who helped the Rahvin flee.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: numerous Imperial Orc heroes are listed among those who supported the Rahvin's escape.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the weirwood groves of the Heart of Peytaht went to Navarr's allies the Great Forest Orcs, and Navarr heroes are listed among the Rahvin's supporters.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: two Freeborn heroes are listed among those who helped the Rahvin escape.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: some Dawnish resent Holberg going to the League, and League heroes are listed among the Rahvin's supporters.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: three members of the Hartell Household are listed among those who supported the Rahvin.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: four Urizen heroes are listed among those who helped the Rahvin flee.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fangs' state is compared to Ossium's Sunless Depths, and Varushkan heroes are listed among the Rahvin's supporters.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: several Wintermark heroes are listed among those who helped the Rahvin escape.

Start a war.o: In the aftermath of the Gryphon's Pride's night assault on the Rahvin at the Fangs, Dawn split between Gryphons backing General Archavion Wolfborne and Unicorns condemning the attack. The Senate had to decide the fate of the captured mithril mine.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: The Fangs mine lies here, its abandoned Rahvin tools and worked mithril now Imperial spoils. The Senate ultimately voted to cede the Bitter Strand to the Rahvin.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: Mentioned in passing: its weirwood groves were given to the Great Forest Orcs, a sore point for Dawnish who felt denied the spoils of war.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Rahvin sheltered in caves in the Carmine Fields near the Holberg border, and some Dawnish grumble that Holberg should have been theirs.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fangs' cruel, ill-built workings recall the state of Ossium's Sunless Depths when they were claimed.

The Barrens.t: Support for the attack on the Rahvin was strongest here. The territory's newest mithril mine passed into Imperial hands, and the expelled Rahvin vowed to retake it at once.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: a Dawnish noble cites the Druj having just destroyed two armies in Therunin as a reason to press the war.

Weirwater.t: Opposition to the attack on the Rahvin, and support for the Unicorns' call for peace, was strongest in Weirwater.

Starting at the end.d: Inspired by the Blood Red Roads, civil service engineers proposed several projects. The Iron Roads (200 wains of white granite, 400 crowns, one year) would expand roads across Karov, Miekarova and Volodmartz, boosting mines, forests and four Bourse resources. Wintermark's beacons (40 granite, 40 weirwood, 160 crowns) would make barbarian invasions of Hahnmark and Kallavesa contested and allow units to garrison them. The Marches were offered the Grand Western Highway, the Otterway and the Great Westward Canal. The Brass Coast was offered the Garden Roads in Feroz, a possible road into Kalino and the Cinnabar Roads, later withdrawn after Jotun damage. The beacons were completed before Spring 383YE, and the Iron Roads were later extended into Ossium.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat and Semmerholm are listed among the territories the Blood Red Roads pass through.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Senate approved an expansion of the Iron Roads into Ossium in Spring 384YE.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the planned White Roads are cited as an ambitious project that would bring more pilgrims to Bastion and Necropolis.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial Orc traders are among those who regularly use the central road through Miekarova.

Jotun.t: Jotun invasions loom over the proposals: the beacons might have warned of their seizure of Sermersuaq, the Sermersuaq beacons await its liberation, and Jotun damage to Kahraman ended the Cinnabar Roads opportunity.

Navarr.t: Navarr traders stood to gain from roads into Kahraman and Miekarova, and surveyors sketched a protected route into Liathaven, though no work is possible while it lies outside the Empire.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn were offered the Garden Roads in Feroz, a possible trade road into Kalino, and the Cinnabar Roads in Kahraman, which were withdrawn after Jotun damage.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League's cities are linked by the Blood Red Roads, and the Iron Roads might bring more materials to Temeschwar's Assayer's Guild.

The Marches.t: The Marches were offered the Grand Western Highway, the Otterway and the Great Westward Canal to spread prosperity beyond Upwold to Mitwold, Mournwold and Bregasland.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: a proposed Miekarova road would end at the Embassy to Otkodov.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's heliopticon is cited as a far grander counterpart to Wintermark's beacons.

Varushka.t: The Senate approved the Iron Roads in Autumn 383YE, bringing safer warded roads, ingots and materials to mine and forest owners, and greater output from four Varushkan Bourse resources.

Wintermark.t: Uninterested in new roads, the Winterfolk had their beacons and watchtowers in Hahnmark and Kallavesa approved in Autumn 382YE and completed before Spring 383YE.

Starting at the end.o: The Civil Service presented the Senate with a set of surveyed infrastructure opportunities across the Empire: the Iron Roads of Varushka, beacons and watchtowers in Wintermark, a highway, causeway and canal in the Marches, and new roads in the Brass Coast. The Senate later approved the Wintermark beacons in Autumn 382YE and the Iron Roads in Autumn 383YE.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: A highway spur to Graven Rock would open access to Gravenmarch's mineral riches, adding 25 ingots of production each season across Bregasland's mines.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: The proposed Otterway repairs would widen and pave the raised causeway to Ottery.

Bregasland/The Rushes.t: The Otterway would continue south to Sallow, though the Bregas rejected any extension further into the Fens.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: The hakima of Afar politely but firmly refused any road linking their isolated settlement to Bramar and vowed to oppose one.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: The region would share in the Garden Roads' proposed maintenance and expansion of the Feroz road network.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: The withdrawn Cinnabar Roads would have run from Briante to Fort Braydon and better protected the Great Mine of Briante.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: The Cinnabar Roads would have extended Fort Braydon's protection to the Damatian Cliffs, and past trade with Beacon Point here was choked by bandit orcs.

Kallavesa/Rundhal Marsh.t: The Kallavesa beacons would stop working if an enemy force took control of the Rundhal Marsh.

Karov/Kamienczka.t: The region would benefit from the Iron Roads' expansion of Karov's network between Delev, Olvanshka and Kolvy and its isolated vales.

Karov/Malimorzi.t: The region would benefit from the Iron Roads' expansion of Karov's network, including the new road from Kolvy to Korotny.

Karov/Skoremujac.t: The region would benefit from the Iron Roads' improved access to Karov's lesser-known vales.

Liathaven/Beacon Point.t: Bandit orcs once strangled trade between Beacon Point and Serra Damata, and surveyors could only sketch a protected route while Liathaven remains outside the Empire.

Miekarova/Dupadealuri.t: The region would benefit from the Iron Roads' reinforcement of Miekarova's central road and access to isolated vales, forests and mines.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: The region would benefit from the Iron Roads in Miekarova, including better access to the Eternal Shafts of Time and the Night Quarry.

Miekarova/Srodkoja.t: The region would benefit from the Iron Roads' reinforced road linking Essk, Olodny and Mormyk.

Mitwold/Oddmire.t: The Western Road to Meade and Odd's End, now fallen into disrepair, would be restored under the Grand Western Highway and could continue as the Otterway.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: The Grand Western Highway would be extended through the Chalkdowns to Sarcombe, which is being rebuilt.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: The highway would run east from Sarcombe across the Greensward to Tassato.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: The region would share in the Mournwold benefits of the proposed highway or canal, and the withdrawn Cinnabar Roads would have run north from Kahraman into the Mournwold.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Any future Sermersuaq beacon network would only work while Sealtoq was not in enemy hands.

Volodmartz/Brez.t: The region would benefit from the Iron Roads' ambitious new road through Volodmartz towards Void and Veltsgorsk.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as a territory the Blood Red Roads pass through.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed White Roads would bring more pilgrims to the holy city of Bastion.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the White Roads would help traders on the south-eastern shores of the Bay reach the wider Empire.

Bregasland.t: Proposals included a highway spur to Graven Rock that would boost Bregasland's mines, and repairs to the Otterway causeway to enrich its farms; the Bregas angrily rejected any extension further into the Fens.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as a territory the Blood Red Roads pass through.

Feroz.t: The proposed Garden Roads would bring rings to Feroz businesses, herbs to its gardens and extra herbs to the Keeper of the Spice Gardens; a further road from Bramar towards Kalino was also suggested.

Hahnmark.t: Expanded beacons and watchtowers were approved and completed, making barbarian invasions of Hahnmark contested unless an enemy takes Kalpaheim.

Kahraman.t: The Cinnabar Roads would have enriched Kahraman's mines and businesses and raised Fort Braydon to a rank two fortification, but Jotun damage made the opportunity unavailable.

Kalino.t: A possible Sunlit Road from Bramar to Ruenda in Kalino would need negotiation by the Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy and Confederate work on their side of the border.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa's pilgrim trails were judged good enough, but its beacons and watchtowers were approved and completed, making barbarian invasions there contested while the Rundhal Marsh holds.

Karov.t: Under the Iron Roads, roads between Delev, Olvanshka and Kolvy would be maintained and expanded, and a new road would link Kolvy to Korotny along the Weirwater border.

Karsk.t: The Crow Roads of Karsk served as the template for the Iron Roads, which might in turn open easier access to Karsk's mines.

Liathaven.t: Surveyors could only make vague sketches of a protected route into Liathaven while it remains outside the Empire, though the Cinnabar Roads would have eased resettlement.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as a territory the Blood Red Roads pass through.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as a territory the Blood Red Roads pass through.

Miekarova.t: The Iron Roads would reinforce the Essk–Olodny–Mormyk road and add a new route to the Night Quarry, Wendell's Hope and the Embassy to Otkodov.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold would gain from a repaired Western Road through to Meade and Odd's End, or from a canal along the River Meade, with rings for its businesses and farms.

Mournwold.t: The highway or canal would reconnect the Mournwold to the north, bringing rings to farms and businesses and extra ingots to mines, with uncertain effects on contact with its ex-Jotun orcs.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed White Roads would bring more pilgrims to the tombs of Necropolis.

Ossium.t: The Senate approved an expansion of the Iron Roads into Ossium in Spring 384YE.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: a new Miekarova road would end at the Embassy to Otkodov.

Segura.t: The Sunset Road already brings Segura prosperity through trade with the Faraden, and the Garden Roads would extend the Feroz highway into Segura to Anduz.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: listed as a territory the Blood Red Roads pass through.

Sermersuaq.t: Once Sermersuaq is liberated from the Jotun, a smaller beacon network could cover it for 25 wains each of white granite and weirwood and 100 crowns.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the Blood Red Roads run north from Tassato, and the proposed highway would end there.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: more materials reaching Temeschwar might allow the Assayer's Guild to expand.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold's trade boom from the Blood Red Roads has made other Marchers grumble, and the canal might one day extend there.

Volodmartz.t: The Iron Roads would add a major new road from the foothills north of Triosk past the Hunt of Alderei the Fair to Void and Veltsgorsk.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: a new Karov road would run along the border with Weirwater.

Statement of Intent regarding the Stalke.d: The Stalker, a red star then believed to be set to fall in Miekarova, prompted this motion. Proposed by the senator for Volodmartz and seconded by the senator for Hercynia, it framed the diversion as part of the Empire's ongoing peace treaty with the Thule and as acceptance of a Thule gesture of goodwill. The Senate agreed in principle that the Thule ritual should be used to redirect the comet away from Imperial land and onto Sküld, a Thule territory. The motion was a statement of intent that passed in principle; the page does not record whether the ritual was carried out.

Thule.t: The Thule offered the ritual as a gesture of goodwill under the peace treaty, and the Senate agreed in principle to have the Stalker diverted onto their own territory of Sküld.

Varushka.t: The motion sought to spare Varushka's territory of Miekarova from the red star, and it was proposed by the senator for Volodmartz, a Varushkan territory.

Statement of Intent regarding the Stalke.o: In Summer 380YE the Senate passed in principle a statement of intent, as part of the ongoing peace treaty with the Thule, to accept their gesture of goodwill and use a Thule ritual to divert the Stalker comet to the Thule territory of Sküld.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova was where the Stalker was believed to be set to fall, and the motion aimed to divert the comet away from it.

Steel and salt.d: Joined by around a thousand soldiers under independent captains, the three armies entered the Cravanclosh, a forest turned to stone where choking ash, wound-petrifying infection and scarce water hampered them. They collided with the Hamsin and Brine Turtles, who had been marching north to attack Mareave. Commander Marradhol, granddaughter of Salt Lord Azshur, arrived with nearly ten thousand reinforcements and took command, causing friction with the Hamsin. The cautious Grendel lost more troops than the Empire and were pushed slowly south. Highborn scouts found petrified ambergelt and identified two fortifications, Stormlords Rise and Beynagahoyne. Uncooperative Mareave septs raised army upkeep by three tenths. Lord Alessia Heraclien was found carrying money to fund mercenaries at Stormlords Rise.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: The Barrens is named as one of the lands the Golden Axe helped bring into the Empire.

Grendel.t: The Hamsin's planned attack on Mareave was thwarted, and Commander Marradhol's forces took over the defence of Ayereed. The Grendel suffered heavier casualties as they were driven slowly south through the Petrified Forest.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Winter Sun marched into Ayereed to claim new land, using supernatural strategic insight to counter the Grendel and exploit friction between Marradhol and the Hamsin. However, Brine Turtle septs in their newly secured Mareave remained resentful and uncooperative.

Varushka.t: The Golden Axe led the advance and drove the Grendel back most aggressively, coping best with the hostile forest. Their soldiers discovered that the giant scorpions were edible and excelled at preserving and seizing water.

Steel and salt.o: In Autumn 386YE the Golden Axe, Winter Sun and Seventh Wave marched south from Mareave into Ayereed and met the Grendel in the Petrified Forest, pushing them back until the Empire was almost halfway to conquering the region.

Ayereed/Cornaghan.t: Lord Alessia Heraclien and Grendel guards were tracked through Cornaghan carrying a chest of at least twenty thrones to hire mercenaries for Stormlords Rise. The General of the Seventh Wave was given the task of stopping them.

Ayereed/Gainmeachdubh.t: The Grendel city of Gainmeachdubh is the seat of Salt Lord Azshur, whose household troops under Commander Marradhol formed the bulk of the reinforcements that took charge of Ayereed's defence.

Ayereed/Petrified Forest.t: The Cravanclosh became the battleground, where ash, petrifying infection, scarce water and giant scorpions troubled the armies. The Empire pushed the Grendel south and was almost halfway to conquering the region, and scouts found petrified ambergelt in abandoned logging camps.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: Clisearn was one of three Mareave regions disinclined to support Imperial troops, which added to the upkeep burden on the armies in Ayereed.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: Eoradal was one of three Mareave regions disinclined to support Imperial troops, which made supplying the invasion of Ayereed harder and costlier.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: The Brine Turtle sept watched the armies with fearful, resentful suspicion and offered no welcome in Fioroult. Their warriors fighting for the Grendel tried in vain to slip scouts through Imperial lines to reach their septmates there.

Ayereed.t: Imperial armies invaded this largely unknown Grendel territory, came almost halfway to conquering the Petrified Forest and learned of two fortifications, Stormlords Rise and Beynagahoyne. Ayereed is also too arid for the Rivers of Life and Rivers Run Red rituals to work as expected.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: a Senate-backed survey five years earlier mapped the Bay's coastline but revealed little of Ayereed's interior.

Mareave.t: Mareave served as the staging ground for the invasion of Ayereed, but its septs' control of scarce fresh water made supplying the armies hard and increased their upkeep. The Hamsin had been marching to attack it before being intercepted.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is cited as a land the Golden Axe helped bring under the Imperial banner.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens is cited as a land the Golden Axe helped bring into the Empire.

Stings like the truth.d: The Whisper Gallery now works through mortal agents. Leontes the Scribe was stabbed in his garden, and Peter of Hintown's husband Dorcas was poisoned with Virus Lunarae, apparently by Antonia di Sarvos, who remains at large. The Senate could empower the Conclave or magistrates, and the Synod could direct the Silent Bell against such agents. Hannah's Silence, a secretive Highborn chapter led by Exarch Zipporah, proposed replacing Livia, having the Highborn assembly elect the Seer, or restricting publication of past-life visions. Livia's publishers, Spider's Vantage Spire, instead offered wider distribution. The Senate funded distribution of Echoes of the Labyrinth to foreign trading nations. Sung's herald Curious Breeze said it would probably attend Anvil.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; its only link is through the Spiral territory, which the page does not discuss directly.

Highguard.t: Hannah's Silence, a Highborn chapter, sent a delegation to Anvil to lobby Highborn senators to curb the Seer of the Gateway, including a controversial proposal that the Highborn National Assembly elect the Seer. Highborn benefactors were also noted as supporters of the Heirs of Lepidus.

The League.t: A League mountebank, Antonia di Sarvos, was believed by the militia to be the poisoner who targeted Peter of Hintown on the Whisper Gallery's instructions, and remains at large.

Urizen.t: Livia Cascade of Urizen faced calls for her replacement as Seer of the Gateway, while her Urizen publishers, the Spider's Vantage Spire, offered to spread her work further. The Senate then funded distribution of Echoes of the Labyrinth to foreign trading nations.

Stings like the truth.o: In Summer 382YE the Whisper Gallery's agents kept targeting Imperial scholars, a Highborn chapter campaigned to curb the Seer of the Gateway, Livia Cascade, and the eternal Sung grew displeased with the Empire over some spoiled mystery.

Necropolis.t: Hannah's Silence is based in the Necropolis, where Exarch Zipporah preached publicly against the Seer of the Gateway's publications before sending a delegation to Anvil.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the fall of Reikos left many Highborn chapterless, some of whom are said to have joined Hannah's Silence.

Sarvos.t: Militia investigating the attempted poisoning searched Sarvos and found that the suspect, Antonia di Sarvos, had vanished from their usual haunts.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not directly referenced; the word appears only in the title of the eternal Sung, the Spiral Dancer.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Peter of Hintown's bodyguard Alva, a Temeschwari woman, recognised the poison symptoms in time to help save Dorcas.

Stone and stone.d: The opportunities had no time limit unless Adamant was declared an enemy, the Master's powers changed or the College of Engineering in Temeschwar was lost. They were: the Tower of the Dragon for the Summer Archmage; a Deepforge in Gildenheim for Imperial Orc magic items; a Deepwyrm Aerie guarding Srodkoja; three mine-enriching statues in Mournwold, Weirwater and Hahnmark; making the Court of the White Fountain unbreakable; and a Red Iron Door against massing trogoni. The Aerie, Deepforge, Black Boar and Three Magpies later expired. Sagua i'Ezmara, the first Master, commissioned the Door, the Court's reinforcement (completed Summer 384YE) and the Owlbeast (completed 385YE). Dima Vasilyevna Novosad announced the Tower in Spring 387YE.

Dawn.t: Weirwater was offered the Alabaster Owlbeast, a lit statue enriching every mine there with a share of 900 rings, which was eventually built and completed before the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel Wind magicians were recalled as the destroyers of Fort Mezudan, and Adamant feared for the Court of the White Fountain should hostilities with them resume.

Imperial Orcs.t: The koboldi offered to turn the accursed runeforge ruins beneath Gildenheim into a Deepforge making magic items for orc champions, but the opportunity later expired.

Navarr.t: Northern Miaren was among the lands whose mines and mana sites the koboldi warned could face a trogoni assault from the sinkhole within a year or so.

The League.t: The League's Temeschwar housed the College of Engineering on which these opportunities depended, and southern Temeschwar was warned of the trogoni threat massing beneath the sinkhole.

The Marches.t: The Black Boar statue offered Marcher-owned mines in the Mournwold 50 green iron each season but expired unbuilt, while northern Upwold was warned of the trogoni threat.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule orcs were noted as still interested in acquiring the Gildenheim runeforge ruins, a rival to the Deepforge plan.

Urizen.t: Redoubt's Court of the White Fountain was offered adamant reinforcement, and Urizeni magicians would see it completed when the Ashen Flame coven performed Hammers of the Brilliant Shore in Summer 384YE.

Varushka.t: Miekarova's Srodkoja was offered the protection of deepwyrms in an Aerie above Volchitrava, with potions for the Master of Ice and Darkness, but the opportunity later expired.

Wintermark.t: Hahnmark was offered the Three Magpies relief to enrich its mines, which later expired, and southern Hahnmark was warned of a growing trogoni threat from the sinkhole.

Stone and stone.o: In Winter 383YE Adamant's koboldi presented a series of proposals for unique structures that only the newly created Master of the Koboldi could commission, from a residence for the Archmage of Summer to great statues, an adamant-reinforced fortress and a door to seal the trogoni-infested sinkhole.

Hahnmark/Northspires.t: The Three Magpies relief on Rodthorn would have been visible across the Northspires, but the opportunity later expired.

Miekarova/Srodkoja.t: The Deepwyrm Aerie would have defended Srodkoja like a 1,000-strength fortification if directly attacked, but the opportunity later expired.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: Mentioned in passing: a landskeeper noted the Old Pig in Freemoor lay on a line with the proposed Black Boar passing through the Singing Caves.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Mentioned in passing: the broken-crowned stag statue High Courage in Green March was cited in a landskeeper's observation about alignments with the proposed Black Boar.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Mentioned in passing: Southmoor is not named, though the Black Boar was proposed for the hills south of Sarcombe in the Mournwold before the opportunity expired.

Redoubt/Optarion.t: The Court of the White Fountain in the foothills of Optarion, guarding the Onyx Pass, was made unbreakable with adamant by Summer 384YE.

Spiral/Ateri.t: Mentioned in passing: the ruins of Fort Mezudan on the slopes of Ateri, destroyed by Grendel Wind magic, were recalled as a warning for the Court of the White Fountain.

Weirwater/Wickmoor.t: The Alabaster Owlbeast was to stand on a hill in Wickmoor northwest of the Weirwater Vales, lit by two great lightstones, and was completed in 385YE.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the koboldi were noted as having supported efforts to strengthen the Castle of Thorns.

Hahnmark.t: The koboldi proposed the Three Magpies relief on Rodthorn, offering every mine 25 orichalcum and 25 tempest jade, and warned that trogoni massing beneath the sinkhole could threaten southern Hahnmark; the statue opportunity later expired.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the koboldi were noted as enthusiastic supporters of efforts to improve the Walls of Holberg.

Miaren.t: The koboldi warned that a trogoni legion from the sinkhole could attack mines and mana sites throughout northern Miaren within a year or so unless the shaft was sealed.

Miekarova.t: A Deepwyrm Aerie was proposed above Volchitrava and Olodny to guard the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, but this opportunity later expired.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is not named on the page, which concerns Urizen chiefly through the Court of the White Fountain in Redoubt.

Mournwold.t: The Black Boar statue south of Sarcombe would have given Marcher-owned mines 50 green iron each season, but the opportunity expired unbuilt.

Redoubt.t: The Court of the White Fountain was offered adamant reinforcement to make it unbreakable; the work was announced in Spring 384YE and completed in Summer 384YE.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the Adamant Gate, rebuilt with koboldi help, was cited as an example of adamant's unbreakable fortifications.

Skarsind.t: The koboldi proposed repurposing the accursed runeforge ruins beneath Gildenheim into a Deepforge for Imperial Orc smiths, but the opportunity later expired.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Onyx Pass linking Redoubt and Spiral and the ruins of Fort Mezudan were described as context for fortifying the Court of the White Fountain.

Temeschwar.t: The completed College of Engineering here underpinned all the opportunities, and southern Temeschwar was warned that massing trogoni might one day attack its mines and mana sites.

Upwold.t: The koboldi warned that a trogoni legion from the sinkhole could pour out against mines and mana sites in northern Upwold within a year or so.

Weirwater.t: The Alabaster Owlbeast was proposed to give every mine a share of 900 rings and guide travellers through the woods; it was completed before the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

Strange allies.d: Scouts in the Brass Coast saw smoke and carrion crows across the border, and Faraden merchants reported Jotun legions from Narkyst burning south. The Iron Confederacy, under the Duke called the Grey Wolf, attacked Kalino, and Suranni merchants at the Sarvos embassy justified it as protecting trade. Juevar of the Hierro and a Lasambrian general came to Anvil seeking aid. Gudmundur Arason, King of Narkyst, warned that helping the Lasambrians would break the treaty. The civil service would not support the Lasambrians without Senate instruction. The Senate abrogated the Jotun ceasefire and agreed military support against the Jotun in northern Lasambria. Nothing more was heard from the south.

Jotun.t: Jotun hosts from Narkyst invaded northern Lasambria, and their King warned that Imperial aid to the Lasambrians would end the treaty; the Senate then abrogated that ceasefire.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun King cited Navarr working 'cursed magics' in Jotun lands as one of two earlier breaches of the treaty.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast scouts reported the fighting across the border, the Lasambrian delegation entered the Empire through Segura, and the Freeborn were divided between old grief over Lasambrian raids and the wish to befriend those who come in peace.

The League.t: Suranni merchants visiting the newly completed embassy in Sarvos argued the Iron Confederacy's case and were surprised the Empire cared about Lasambria's fate.

Strange allies.o: In Summer 379YE Lasambria was invaded twice, by the Jotun from the north and the Iron Confederacy from the south, and Lasambrian, Suranni and Jotun envoys all sought to sway the Senate. The Jotun warned that any Imperial aid to the Lasambrians would end their ceasefire with the Empire.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: Mentioned in passing: a cloud of carrion crows over the fighting was seen from its western woods.

Liathaven/Beacon Point.t: Mentioned in passing: a great cloud of carrion crows was seen from Beacon Point.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: Mentioned in passing: a Jotun Jarl noted that her clan had been fighting in the West Ranging for over a year.

Segura/Burnish.t: Mentioned in passing: pillars of black smoke from the Lasambrian war were visible from Burnish.

Segura/Yellow Chase.t: Mentioned in passing: pillars of black smoke from the fighting were visible from Yellow Chase.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: carrion crows over the fighting were seen from the western woods of Serra Damata.

Kalino.t: Iron Confederacy soldiers under the Grey Wolf attacked the southern Lasambrian hills here; no chance arose to help the defenders, and no further news came.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: crows were seen from Beacon Point, and a Jotun Jarl spoke of her clan fighting in the West Ranging for over a year.

Reinos.t: Faraden merchants crossing the Reinos hills reported Jotun legions burning and killing their way south, and the Senate agreed to send military support against the Jotun in northern Lasambria.

Sarvos.t: Suranni merchants came to the new embassy in Sarvos to defend the Iron Confederacy's attack on the Lasambrians.

Segura.t: The Lasambrian delegation crossed Segura's western plains under a flag of truce, and Segurans were divided between memories of the Lasambrian invasion and the recent concord.

Strange fruit.d: The Synod had supported Duke Ferrero preaching tolerance of the refugee Hierro and Elka Nadyanova Gremani guiding them using the example of the Paragon of Kethry. Influential Lasambrians such as Kenza began extolling the Virtues to their own people, even confronting bandit warlords. Priests reported that the conversion of thousands was widespread and heartfelt, the greatest since the Empire's founding or the integration of the Imperial Orcs. The Hierro did not adopt the Way exactly, rejecting reincarnation and the Labyrinth, but reached a compromise around the Virtues. Quarrels with Segura's Freeborn almost stopped, yet all agreed the Lasambrians could not stay there forever. The Civil Service offered no suggestions on their future.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the integration of the Imperial Orcs is cited as the last conversion comparable to that of the Lasambrians.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are named as the enemy who defeated the Hierro in battle and to whom the other Lasambrian orcs had sold out.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn, long robbed by Lasambrian bandits, admitted that something extraordinary had been achieved, and their quarrels with the refugees all but ceased. They still agreed the Lasambrians could not remain among them forever.

Strange fruit.o: Following two Synod judgements of the 379YE Winter Solstice, the efforts of Elka Nadyanova Gremani and Duke Ferrero bore fruit: the Hierro clan of Lasambrian refugees genuinely and widely embraced the Virtues. This left open the question of what the Empire would now do with them.

Segura.t: The Hierro refugees sheltering in Segura embraced the Virtues, and calls to drive them off or kill them died away. Even so, Segura's people agreed the Lasambrians could not stay there permanently, leaving their future for the Empire to decide.

Strange harvest.d: Ettercaps attacking settlements near the forest's edge were destroyed within three weeks by soldiers of the Northern Eagle and the Silent Sentinel in Casinea, the Castle of Thorns garrison in Astolat, and knights, yeofolk militia, troops from the Gate and Navarri thorns in Semmerholm. A transformation then struck farms and forests, cutting their output by a quarter. Vates confirmed the energy flowed from the Brocéliande vallorn along the trods, though the trods were undamaged. The seed pods risked breaching the Conclave's interdiction on vallorn seeds, and the Senate was invited to clarify the law. Cultivating the plant was possible with Spring magic. The vallorn later returned to quiescence, and nobody publicly admitted cultivating the fruit.

Dawn.t: Farms and forests in Astolat and Semmerholm lost a quarter of their produce, while Dawnish knights, yeofolk militia and the Castle of Thorns garrison fought off the ettercaps.

Highguard.t: Highborn farms and forests in Casinea lost a quarter of their output to the Spring transformation, and workers in Mareholm unearthed corrupted dragonbone.

Navarr.t: The Brocéliande vallorn was confirmed as the source of the transformation, carried along the trods; Navarri vates helped trace it and thorns from Boar's Dell fought in Semmerholm.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: troops from the Gate, the fortification guarding the passes into Holberg, helped defend Semmerholm.

Strange harvest.o: In Autumn 379YE, vallorn miasma and ettercap raids spilled from Brocéliande into Casinea, Astolat and Semmerholm, followed by a wave of Spring magic that twisted a quarter of farm and forest produce. Among the aberrations grew thorny bushes whose fruit yields seed pods usable as Spring mana.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Mentioned in passing: bands of Navarri thorns from Boar's Dell helped fight the ettercaps in Semmerholm.

Casinea/Mareholm.t: Highborn workers in Mareholm unearthed half-formed, corrupted deposits of dragonbone twisted into unsettling organic shapes.

Astolat.t: The Castle of Thorns garrison destroyed attacking ettercaps, but farms and forests lost a quarter of their produce, and beggarwood near Rucastle put forth foul blossoms that drew biting flies.

Brocéliande.t: The vallorn here unleashed miasma, ettercaps and a surge of Spring energy that flowed out along the trods before receding back into quiescence.

Casinea.t: Soldiers of the Northern Eagle and the Silent Sentinel kept the ettercaps within half a mile of the forest, but a quarter of the territory's farm and forest produce was twisted.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Gate guarding the now-secure passes into Holberg supplied seasoned troops to fight in Semmerholm.

Semmerholm.t: Questing knights, yeofolk militia, troops from the Gate and Navarri thorns put down the ettercap raids, but farms and forests lost a quarter of their produce to the transformation.

Struggle with the sea.d: Finna i Fijadoz i Guerra's Winter mandate urged the Freeborn to abandon Feroz, and many from Afarjasse and Morajasse fled into Madruga and Segura, where kin, Zemress islanders and priests of the Little Mother took them in. Those in the Cazar Straits, Fontargenta and Oranseri had no such right, and Grendel at Mora's Rock now arrest anyone near the border. Imperial military units and fleets could stealthily evacuate them, raising taxes in Segura and Madruga and hurting Rahab's profits. Further options included a Synod mandate allowing open fighting at the cost of a diplomatic incident, aid from the Commonwealth and Asavean priests in Oran, a Sarcophan ritual, and a rescue of two stranded Zemress islanders. Rocio's 'Feroz is waiting' statement had no effect.

Grendel.t: The Grendel now fully control Feroz and Spiral and have sealed the Feroz border, but Governor Rahab stands to lose much of his profit if the evacuation succeeds, and a bolder Imperial approach would provoke a diplomatic incident and Grendel demands for reparations.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn heeded their Assembly's mandate to abandon Feroz, taking in refugees through ties of kin and tribe, and Freeborn fleets were offered the chance to smuggle the remaining countryfolk out by sea, while the Assembly could choose to sanction open fighting.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Brother of Wizards asked that the Sarcophan covert-fleet ritual be made part of Imperial or Urizen lore before the end of the year.

Struggle with the sea.o: With the first phase of the Grendel peace treaty concluded, Governor Rahab sealed the borders of Feroz after a Brass Coast mandate drove a torrent of Freeborn to flee west, and the Empire was offered the chance to mount a covert land and sea evacuation of those left behind.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: Many Freeborn fled Afarjasse into Madruga and Segura, but some remain, and the Zemress islanders Mira and Ira were trapped in its western woods, hunted by Grendel patrols, with a Sentinel Gate rescue offered from the Afar Hills.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The corsair families of the Cazar Straits were among those barred from leaving by land, but their coastline made them the likeliest to be evacuated wholesale by Imperial fleets.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Freeborn in Fontargenta were trapped under Grendel rule, needing both overland escorts and sea evacuation, and rescued vintners and agricultural specialists could found new vineyards in Madruga.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: Many Freeborn left Morajasse for Segura, but Grendel soldiers garrisoning Mora's Rock have now sealed the border and arrest those near it, leaving the stragglers needing Imperial military escort.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: As a Grendel stronghold, Oranseri's port towns held many trapped Freeborn who would be the hardest to evacuate, though a full sea evacuation could bring them to swell Madruga's coastal towns.

Feroz.t: Fully under Grendel rule, Feroz saw much of its western population flee and its borders sealed, with a covert operation offered to rescue the many still trapped and so permanently reduce the territory's taxation revenue for its holder.

Madruga.t: Madruga received refugees fleeing by land and would host most of those evacuated by sea, bringing short-term disruption but potentially raising its taxation by up to 30 Thrones a season and offering new vineyards and coastal towns.

Segura.t: Segura took in Freeborn crossing from western Feroz, with Zemress islanders offering work on their fields; a successful overland evacuation could raise its taxation by up to 20 Thrones a season and bring herb garden expertise.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral was noted as now wholly Grendel-held, with Salt Lord Kaliact apparently more interested in undisturbed access to the Legacy than in profit.

Summer in Winter.d: Snow fell early across the north, and isolated vales risked being cut off before Spring. More Wolves, rusalka, snow goblins and dubik were reported, along with wax-caked unliving warriors on the roads of Kamienczka. Yet a Summer enchantment urged Varushkans to seek out and challenge dark powers. Such tales often ended well, and every Varushkan with a personal resource in Varushka, including military units and fleets, gained a little extra production. Many Sovereigns mistook the season for a second Summer and stayed quiescent, leaving sacrifices unclaimed. A few grew more active instead, and new horrors may have stirred. The wise warned of overconfidence, expecting it all to end with the new year.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: there are stories that the cold crept south, bringing hail and sleet to Dawn.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on the page, which concerns Varushka's winter.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a land where snow is no stranger during the harsh winter.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is named among the places where the winter was harsh and snowy.

Varushka.t: Varushkans endured a brutal winter but were stirred by a Summer enchantment to face dark forces, gaining extra production from their personal resources. Many of their Sovereigns stayed quiescent, though a few grew more active and new horrors may have arisen.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that snow is no stranger to Wintermark during the harsh winter.

Summer in Winter.o: In Winter 379YE a harsh winter gripped Varushka, but a potent Summer enchantment settled across Miekarova, Karov, Volodmartz and Karsk, stirring Varushkans to confront the dark forces around them, usually with happy outcomes.

Karov/Kamienczka.t: Stories spread of unliving warriors caked in dripping hot wax attacking travellers along the roads of Kamienczka.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named. The page refers only to creatures on the northern shores of the Semmerlak and to cold spreading further south.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is named as a place where snow fell during the harsh winter.

Karov.t: Karov lay under the Summer enchantment, which drove its people to confront the dark. Stories told of unliving warriors caked in hot wax attacking travellers on its roads.

Karsk.t: Karsk was one of the four territories touched by the Summer enchantment. Wardens there might struggle to lay vengeful wraiths to rest in ruined vales and uncover treasures in the process.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova fell under the Summer enchantment, and sightings of wood-skinned dubik haunting its forests increased.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a land where snow is no stranger during the harsh winter.

The Semmerlak.t: Tales of sinister rusalka, snow goblins and less nameable creatures haunting the Semmerlak's northern shores increased dramatically.

Volodmartz.t: Volodmartz suffered the harshest of the winter, so travellers to Anvil feared being unable to return before Spring. It lay under the Summer enchantment, and dubik were sighted haunting its forests.

Summer tree.d: Over thirty thousand orcs and their human allies overran The Rushes and Gravenmarch. Mathilda Fisher planted her leaping-fish standard at Graven and set up her court at Fisher's Rock, where a wooden town of stilt-houses is rising. Many Bregas stayed as thralls, giving the bare minimum of cooperation. The Strong Reeds, supported by House Greywater, lay low and raided Jotun supplies. Fisher's cousin Bron claimed the Keeper of the Dour Fens's mana, and the Imperial Breadbasket now feeds Jotun armies. Fisher planned to send a delegation to Anvil to seek Bregasland's neutrality. A Sentinel Gate conjunction to Jayne's Top Copse offered heroes a chance to destroy a Jotun stockade.

Jotun.t: Jotun armies, including the Mandowla's Roar, now hold all of Bregasland and claim the Imperial Breadbasket's bounty, but their supply lines and food stores suffer constant raids. They have built no fortifications, apparently because moving white granite through the rebel-held marshes is so hard.

The Marches.t: Marchers lost the whole of Bregasland. Many Bregas fled, while those who stayed live as surly, minimally cooperative thralls. The Marcher army the Strong Reeds remains hidden in the marshes, harrying the occupiers alongside House Greywater.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the new buildings at Fisher's Rock are likened to Kallavesi stilt-houses rather than traditional Marcher dwellings.

Summer tree.o: In Autumn 384YE the Jotun and Mathilda Fisher's forces completed the conquest of Bregasland, taking The Rushes and Gravenmarch. The Strong Reeds stayed in the marshes, working with the renegade House Greywater to harry the invaders.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: Gravenmarch fell to the Jotun, and Mathilda Fisher planted her battle standard in Graven's town square. Her cousin Bron now styles himself Keeper and claims the crystal mana from beneath Graven Rock.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: House Greywater's harassment gives the Grey Fens allied insurgents, so it counts as a beach head for the Empire. A conjunction to Jayne's Top Copse there offered heroes the chance to destroy a Mandowla's Roar stockade.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Mathilda Fisher has firmly established her court at Fisher's Rock in the North Fens, where a wooden town of stilt-houses is being built around the rock. It is the only significant construction in the marshes.

Bregasland/The Rushes.t: The Rushes fell quickly to the Jotun force of more than thirty thousand orcs and their human allies.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland fell entirely under Jotun and Fisher control, with Mathilda Fisher as its new steward. Resistance by the Strong Reeds and House Greywater continues, and Fisher hopes to have the territory recognised as a neutral free state between the Jotun and the Marches.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is one of the places Bregas fled to as their marshes fell.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not referred to on this page; the only Varushkan link is a comparison of Fisher's Rock's buildings to Kallavesi stilt-houses.

Sun green.d: Stars vanished over the Barrens, Spiral, Zenith, Holberg, Ossium and Semmerholm, impeding divination and making naga there more secretive. The Penumbral Veil covered Thule's lands, while the shrouds over Feroz, Temeschwar and Morrow faded. Summer Dawning Relentless raised ice castles in Ankra, Ateri and Estmure, and the Sussavari Frost Coven raised one in the North Fens and performed Wondrous Forests of the Night. Ashen Flame created the Three Watchers. Cathan Canae, Callidus, Agramant, Sung and the Black Tablet made offers to the Conclave. In the resolution, the Conclave passed declarations on necromancy and on Wintermark's strength, so ice-giant warbands now guard the beacons. Dawn's apology to Adamant lacked a greater majority.

Dawn.t: Summer Dawning Relentless raised three ice castles and had earlier sent Knights of Glory against the Barrens. Alexander of House Tallstag was offered a Summer draught, and Dawn's failure to thank Adamant for the Gates of Adamant left his koboldi hinting at disappointment, with Mordred's apology falling short of a greater majority.

Druj.t: Every territory under the starless skies is occupied by or of obvious interest to the Druj, raising fears of what else they can do, and the new ice castles appear intended to defend against them.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Spiral, which it shares with Urizen, lies under the starless sky and now hosts two of Dawn's ice castles.

Highguard.t: The Three Watchers now memorialise Highborn sacrifice and are expected to draw Highborn pilgrims. A Necropolis chapter pressed for oversight of necromancy, and the chapter of Zephaniah's Lament was struck by a withering curse.

Jotun.t: Cathan Canae's ice giants were sent to help guard the beacons of Kallavesa and Hahnmark specifically to keep the Jotun out of Wintermark.

The Brass Coast.t: The shroud that had hung over Feroz faded away. Callidus sought out the Autumn Archmage, Edmundo of Damakan's Forge, about his Tassato request.

The League.t: Holberg remained starless and Temeschwar's shroud lifted. Callidus asked for the Freedom of the City in Cascatas, Tassato, a request that would raise the territory's taxes if granted.

The Marches.t: A Wintermark coven raised a protective citadel in Bregasland's North Fens. Cathan Canae entrusted Will Talbot with a ritual that grants dangerous strength to Marcher halberdiers for a year.

Thule.t: The Thule kept the Penumbral Veil over Urdur, Nithoggir, Sküld and Verthandi, impeding Imperial divination of their lands.

Urizen.t: The Urizen coven Ashen Flame created the Three Watchers in Morrow at Furia Severia's direction, and the shroud over Morrow faded.

Varushka.t: The stars went out over Varushka's Ossium. Cathan Canae praised the Varushkans and Dawnish who took Ossium from the Druj.

Wintermark.t: The Sussavari Frost Coven performed Wondrous Forests of the Night and raised a citadel in the North Fens. After the Conclave recognised Wintermark's strength, Cathan Canae sent ice-giant warbands to guard the beacons of Kallavesa and Hahnmark.

Sun green.o: The Summer 383YE Wind of Fortune reported on the Empire's magic. Stars vanished over Druj-linked territories, Thule veiled its lands, and magical castles were raised in Spiral, Semmerholm and Bregasland. The Three Watchers were carved in Morrow, and several eternals made offers to the Conclave.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: The Sussavari Frost Coven raised a citadel of mist and fog here, sheltering defenders and travellers until the Summer Solstice.

Otkodov/Nithoggir.t: Nithoggir lay under the Penumbral Veil, impeding divination.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Sküld lay under the Penumbral Veil, impeding divination.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: The Penumbral Veil still hung over Urdur, according to Imperial merchants.

Semmerholm/Estmure.t: An enchanted citadel of stone and ice was called up in the hills of Estmure by Summer Dawning Relentless.

Spiral/Ankra.t: An ice castle from the Lady of the Frost's domain was raised in the hills of Ankra.

Spiral/Ateri.t: An ice castle from the Lady of the Frost's domain was raised in the hills of Ateri.

Tassato/Cascatas.t: Callidus asked the Conclave for the Freedom of the City here, which would let his heralds come and go and raise Tassato's taxes by one throne each season, cumulatively; it remained only an offer.

Bregasland.t: A magical citadel of mist and fog was raised in the North Fens, protecting the Dour Fens until the Summer Solstice.

Feroz.t: The shroud that previously hung over Feroz faded away.

Hahnmark.t: A warband of Cathan Canae's ice giants was sent to help guard Hahnmark's beacons against the Jotun.

Holberg.t: The night skies over Holberg stayed starless, divination there was impeded, and naga who spent time there felt a strong urge to secrecy.

Kallavesa.t: A warband of Cathan Canae's ice giants was sent to help guard Kallavesa's beacons against the Jotun.

Morrow.t: Three statues nearly two hundred feet tall now guard the pass from Morrow to Zenith, with a liao-consecrated shrine of Loyalty, and Morrow's shroud has lifted.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Tablet, which proposed support for the Imperial Necromancer, is a Necropolis chapter.

Ossium.t: After the Spring Equinox the stars over Ossium flickered out, impeding divination and affecting naga who stay there.

Otkodov.t: The Penumbral Veil hung over Urdur, Nithoggir and Sküld, shrouding Otkodov from scrying.

Semmerholm.t: The stars went out over Semmerholm and an ice castle was raised in Estmure. The Gates of Adamant there became a point of friction with the eternal who built them.

Spiral.t: Spiral's skies stayed starless, and ice castles were raised in Ankra and Ateri, though the Druj did not attack there.

Tassato.t: Callidus sought the Freedom of the City in Cascatas, and his herald turned up at the Edmundo's Forge tavern looking for the Autumn Archmage.

Temeschwar.t: The shroud that previously hung over Temeschwar faded away.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens remained starless and shrouded, and Dawn's Knights of Glory had been called to aid the attack there in Spring.

Verthandi.t: The Penumbral Veil was reported over Verthandi, impeding divination of the territory.

Zenith.t: Zenith's skies stayed starless, and the Three Watchers now loom over the pass leading into it from Morrow.

Sunrise over Livardz.d: Rebuilding needed two Senate commissions plus 20 thrones a season for a year, and a Triosk forestry whose wardens would clear wolves at the cost of a year of Iron Roads trade. The silent menace could be removed by walling up the Star Caverns under a Murupan Goose-herd and destroying the Sumisev Peegel with Wind of Mundane Silence. The ashen wind required a Wyrding Tower and laying the Shadow Fellowship's ghosts to rest. Solving two would lift the ruins; all three would bring the Security of Volodmartz. Most Highborn volunteers turned to the missing bees instead. The ghosts were dealt with at the Spring Equinox, the Sumisev Peegel was destroyed at Summer, and the Wyrding Tower was completed before Autumn.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is cited as proof that people can live almost anywhere.

Varushka.t: Varushkans faced the work of reclaiming Livardz. Their Assembly named Auntie Armand Mariyavich Remislav, who destroyed the Sumisev Peegel, and Borys Vardovich Straskovich, as Boyar of the Iron Roads, announced the Wyrding Tower.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tower of the Eagle regio in Hahnmark is contrasted with the Sumisev Peegel.

Sunrise over Livardz.o: Following a Senate motion by Ostrik Vulpe, prognosticator Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra identified three challenges to restoring the prosperity of Livardz in Volodmartz, left ruined by Cold Sun's Shepherds of Ash: rebuilding the vales, removing the silent menace, and breaking the curse of the ashen wind.

Volodmartz/Livardz.t: Livardz was the focus of every proposal. The Shadow Fellowship's ghosts in the Sunless Vale were dealt with, the Sumisev Peegel was destroyed, and the Wyrding Tower was raised at the ash-choked Wyrding Pond.

Volodmartz/Murupa.t: Murupa holds the Star Caverns where the Shepherds of Ash vanished. A sinecure was proposed to wall them up behind wards and establish geese under a Murupan Goose-herd to watch over them.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: its Tower of the Eagle is noted as a regio that, unlike the Sumisev Peegel, seemed at risk of opening.

Karov.t: Karov, attacked by the Blade of Skies in 385YE, would have had its mines and forests each lose one level of investment if the Triosk forestry were commissioned.

Karsk.t: Karsk's mines and forests would each lose one level of investment for a year if the wardens were diverted from the Iron Roads to clear Livardz.

Miekarova.t: Its senator Vasilmir Radovanovna Esskivic seconded the motion, and its mines and forests would each lose one level of investment under the proposed forestry.

Ossium.t: Ossium's forests stood to lose two levels of investment for a year if the Triosk forestry drew the wardens away from the Iron Roads.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as evidence that people can live almost anywhere.

Volodmartz.t: Clearing two of the three challenges would lift Livardz's ruins and raise treasury revenue by six thrones a season, and all three would grant a year of extra income across the territory. The ghosts, the Sumisev Peegel and the Wyrding Pond were all addressed.

Support Expansion of Caitun.d: Proposed by the Senator for Kallavesa and seconded by the Senator for Mitwold, the motion backed the expansion described in the Butterfly in Reverse Wind of Fortune. It passed at a cost of 70 thrones. The Empire was to supply 15 wains of weirwood plus 45 crowns in transport costs, with the work taking six months. After the Spring Equinox, Rane Shardbearer provided the weirwood and Fancy Jack contributed 5 thrones 5 crowns. The expansion was completed. From the Autumn Equinox 385YE Imperial fleets could trade at Caitun, and Wintermark, Marcher and Freeborn fleets could hunt monsters in the Sea of Snow.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark Senator for Kallavesa proposed the motion, and once the expansion was complete Wintermark fleets gained the ability to hunt monsters in the Sea of Snow from the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

Support Expansion of Caitun.o: In Spring 385YE the Senate passed a motion to support the Faraden expansion of their port of Caitun, providing 15 wains of weirwood and 45 crowns in transport costs, so that Imperial fleets could trade there and hunt monsters in the Sea of Snow.

Sea of Snow.t: The completed expansion of Caitun opened the Sea of Snow to monster hunting by Wintermark, Marcher and Freeborn fleets from the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

Support medical school and Anvil hospita.d: The motion called for funds to be disbursed for the benefit of a medical school and an Anvil hospital, and for both to be formally recognised as Imperial institutions. The Senate solicited testimony from an expert witness, Elizabeth Eastville née Talbot. The motion passed at 20 Thrones with 11 votes against, and no further cost is recorded. The funds were disbursed to Richard of Bourholt, Senator for Bregasland, who proposed the motion. It was seconded by Sarvos.

The Marches.t: A Marcher senator, Richard of Bourholt of Bregasland, led the motion and was entrusted with the funds for the new medical school and Anvil hospital.

Support medical school and Anvil hospita.o: In Spring 377YE the Senate passed a motion to fund, found and recognise an Imperial school of medicine and a hospital in Anvil. It was proposed by the Senator for Bregasland and seconded by the Senator for Sarvos.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland's Senator, Richard of Bourholt, proposed the motion and received the disbursed funds to put towards the medical school and the hospital in Anvil.

Survival.d: Key questions, such as whether a fully roused vallorn can spread beyond its territory, cannot yet be answered. Civilian commissions can now be built inside weirwood groves at double labour cost; the vallorn would deactivate them but not destroy them. The Conclave could interdict new arcane projections to save mana, and the Summer Archmage could seek adamant from Deep Dragon for the Master of the Koboldi. Neighbours know far less than the Empire. Tathenon may trade a ritual protecting against miasma. A controversial idea is to copy the Axou strategy of abandoning and walling off vallorn territories. A weirwood fortification of the Heartwood in Summersend is also proposed.

Druj.t: The Druj inherited the heart of Bendol already contained by Terun wards and maintained them until recently. Their knowledge of the vallorn was stolen from Urizeni spires, and they are seen as unlikely partners in any treaty.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the report doubts the Grendel have ever even encountered the vallorn.

Jotun.t: The Jotun hold Liathaven as Ashvale and use their military strength to manage bursts of vallornspawn. They reportedly secured a boon from Surut of the Thrice-cursed Court, though its purpose is unclear.

Navarr.t: The Navarr's long work against the vallorn underpins existing options, including plans with Holberg in Brocéliande and with Urizen in the Sarangrave. The Great Forest Orcs would cut the cost of fortifying the Heartwood if the Navarr national assembly swore not to use, and to oppose Imperial use of, the Ancestor Slayer's fire.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: engineers of Holberg worked with the Navarr on a plan to improve the defensibility of Brocéliande.

Thule.t: The Thule keep the vallornheart of Emrys in Sküld quiescent with their own version of Wither the Seed. Their dragon Tathenon reportedly holds a Day ritual protecting against vallorn miasma that the Empire might negotiate for, and aid from the Tower of the Skink garrison against Bendol would be valuable.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj stole their vallorn knowledge from Urizeni spires, and recent Navarr work with Urizen produced opportunities to defend the Sarangrave.

Survival.o: The Sun Chamber's appraisal, aided by Vainakoma Dawnstongue, examined how to protect Imperial infrastructure from vallorn expansion. It concluded that armies and fortifications remain the main answer, but identified several new opportunities.

Hercynia/Deer's Folly.t: If the vallornheart of Deer's Folly rouses, a weirwood-grown fortification at the Heartwood might prove more resistant to it, though this is uncertain.

Hercynia/Summersend.t: The proposed Fortify the Heartwood commission would be built here for 80 weirwood and 240 crowns over four seasons, available until Summer Solstice 389YE. The Great Forest Orcs offer to reduce the cost in return for a Navarr oath.

Liathaven/Liath's Heart.t: Occasional bursts of vallornspawn emanate from Liath's Heart, which the Jotun reportedly manage with little difficulty.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: The Thule, long holders of Sküld, keep the vallornheart of Emrys quiescent with their own version of Wither the Seed.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: The heart of Bendol was contained by ancient Terun wards made with Sadogua's help, which the Druj maintained until recently. Aid from the Thule garrison of the Tower of the Skink against it would be of great value.

Brocéliande.t: Navarr and Holberg engineers drew up a plan to make Brocéliande more defensible by luring the vallorn to a chosen battleground. The territory is also among those the controversial Axou-style strategy would abandon.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia is noted as largely undefended beyond the Grim Pyramid. A weirwood fortification of the Heartwood in Summersend is proposed, though Hercynia is also listed among territories the Axou-style strategy would abandon.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's engineers joined the Navarr in planning Brocéliande's defences.

Liathaven.t: The Jotun-held part, called Ashvale, is managed through Jotun military strength against occasional vallornspawn. Liathaven is among the territories the Axou-style containment idea would abandon.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is noted as fine and excluded from the territories the Axou-style strategy would abandon.

Otkodov.t: The Thule keep the vallornheart of Emrys in Sküld quiescent using their own version of Wither the Seed.

Sarangrave.t: The vallorn reared in the Sarangrave this season. Navarr and Urizeni work has produced opportunities to defend key sites, and relations with Axos are judged pivotal to the damage in the east.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Therunin is listed among the territories the controversial Axou-style strategy would abandon to the vallorn.

Swans will sing.d: After a stalemate over the Silver Peaks, a treaty costing the Stonefield Ice Caves, and the relinquishment of Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs, Wintermark's injured pride festered over winter. The national assembly could have passed a statement of principle naming a priest to spend liao on auras of Ambition, Courage and Pride, inspiring raids into the Silver Peaks and Otkodov. Depending on the liao spent (25, 50 or 100), this would boost Wintermark businesses and military units, risk diplomatic incidents with the Thule, and possibly seize wains and ilium. The raids would be crimes under Imperial law. No judgement was passed; with Jotun concerns in Kallavesa growing, the moment passed.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: their acquisition of Skarsind is cited as one of the losses fuelling Wintermark's frustration.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the new war with the Jotun and Wintermark's fear of an invasion of Kallavesa helped the moment for raiding to pass.

Thule.t: The Thule faced possible Wintermark raids on the Silver Peaks and Otkodov in breach of the treaty, but none were sanctioned as the assembly passed no judgement.
