Wintermark.t: Wintermark's national assembly was offered a way to channel its wounded pride into illegal raids on the Thule for profit, but declined to pass any judgement, and the opportunity lapsed.

Swans will sing.o: In Winter 379YE, resentment in Wintermark over the peace treaty that ceded the Stonefield Ice Caves to the Thule created an opportunity for the Wintermark national assembly to urge illegal raids across the border into Thule lands. The assembly passed no judgement, and the opportunity lapsed.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The Silver Peaks, contested in a stalemated battle and lost with the Stonefield Ice Caves, would have been the first target of any raids, but the assembly passed no judgement.

Hahnmark.t: Citizens with personal resources in Hahnmark would have gained a bonus from the raids, but the opportunity was not taken up.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa residents would have shared in the raiding profits, but growing concern about the Jotun threatening Kallavesa helped the moment pass.

Otkodov.t: Thule-held Otkodov, especially its south and south-west, was the proposed target of Wintermark raids, which never took place as no judgement was passed.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq, divided between Wintermark and the Thule, was the centre of the proposed raids and home to Wintermark citizens who would have profited, but nothing came of it.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's relinquishment to the Imperial Orcs is named as one of Wintermark's grievances.

Swords and sorcery.d: Pelleas Thorne's mandate filled the Dawnish armies with zeal, so no Dawnish general could order Give Ground or Cautious Advance until Winter 383YE. If any general took up an opportunity, that ban became permanent for every Dawnish army. The Hounds of Glory could spend 25 wains of mithril to gain indomitable glory, allowing a No Matter the Cost order to seize a named region at heavy cost in casualties. Enthusiastic yeofolk made enlarging the Golden Sun cheaper, at 100 wains and 200 crowns. Eastern Sky enchanters negotiated a proposed Tower of the East at the Semmerstones, costing 75 wains, to make that army favoured by Summer eternals. The Senate approved the Golden Sun's enlargement, and the Hounds' general paid for indomitable glory.

Dawn.t: Dawn's armies were given a chance to grow stronger through glory: the Hounds of Glory gained indomitable glory and the Golden Sun's enlargement was approved. Because these opportunities were taken, the page's terms mean no Dawnish army may ever again give ground or advance cautiously.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as the foe Dawn drove from Semmerholm and from whom Dawn took Ossium, the victories that sparked this fervour.

Swords and sorcery.o: After driving the Druj from Semmerholm and conquering Ossium, Dawn's war fervour, stoked by Pelleas Thorne's mandate, opened three limited opportunities at the Winter Solstice 382YE. The Hounds of Glory became an army of indomitable glory, and the Senate approved enlarging the Golden Sun.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn's surprise crossing of the Semmerlak with Summer eternals' aid to invade and swiftly conquer Ossium is cited as one of the triumphs behind the opportunity.

Semmerholm.t: Dawn drove the Druj out of Semmerholm, and the Semmerstones regio was put forward as the site of the proposed Tower of the East, where Dawnish enchanters and Summer eternals could meet.

Symposium of Revelation.d: Watcher secured a General Assembly judgement that invited speakers would not count as preaching under the laws on blasphemy, idolatry and heresy. This was widely read as a signal that religious crimes at the Symposium would not be prosecuted. The Symposium had no formal powers. Sessions ran from 2pm to 8:30pm and covered Exemplars, Yael's Revelation, the realms and Eternals, the Eternal Schism, true and false virtues, and orcs and the Howling Abyss. Assemblies invited foreign guests. Grendel, Axou, Faradene, Sarcophan, Jarmish and Commonwealth representatives were confirmed or expected. Asavean priests, the Lasambrian orcs, the Eternal Roshanwe and the Sumaah Republic remained uncertain.

Grendel.t: Although at war with the Empire, the Grendel accepted the League assembly's invitation and confirmed they would send a spiritual representative, apparently eager to educate the Synod about the true virtues.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named directly on the page, and its people may only have taken part in the Symposium's debates on the Way like any other Imperial priests.

Imperial Orcs.t: The newly formed Imperial Orc national assembly played an active part. Bonewall Rek invited a Commonwealth delegation, Cardinal Atla invited the Sumaah Republic, and Imperial Orc preachers convened a panel on orcs, the Howling Abyss and their place in the doctrine of the Way.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian orcs were said to have left the Empire to join or ally with the Jotun, and the invitation to them was noted as not meant for the Jotun who hold western Lasambria.

The Brass Coast.t: Danita i Riqueza and the Brass Coast national assembly invited the priests of Faraden, and at least one Faradene priest was expected, possibly to seek the return of the Copper Scrolls. Immeldar of the Freeborn assembly also invited the Lasambrian orcs, without reply.

Urizen.t: Belisarius and the Urizen national assembly invited their Axou "cousins", and despite Axos's usual reticence on religion, a priest was confirmed as travelling to present at the Symposium.

Symposium of Revelation.o: At the Winter Solstice of 380YE the Synod held the Symposium of Revelation in Anvil, a public programme of sermons, panels and debates organised by the Marcher Symposiarch Edward Watcher of King's Stoke to address recent upheavals in the Imperial Faith. Foreign priests and delegations, including some from nations at war with the Empire, were invited to attend.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: several Asavean priests invited to the Symposium were already in the Empire working on the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis is not named on the page, and the Symposium took place in Anvil rather than in the territory.

Take it further.d: Half the Imperial nations shunned the Spring raid, but around forty captains and warleaders from Highguard, the League, the Marches, Wintermark and the Imperial Orcs plundered Skallahn as far as Iron Stand, Bjarkey and Ulfrsmoor before withdrawing safely. They secured no Bourse resources and did no strategic damage. A Summer raid by fleets and military units, aimed at military targets and sparing graves and shrines, could achieve tiered results depending on its total strength. These ranged from overrunning Greenwall to looting Eyrarfell's Shining Caverns, while strong enough fleets could burn the Kongegőr causeway or reach the Sea of Snow. Spring veterans gained a bonus. Wintermark and the Marches could jointly name a Marshal, and House Oddsboy and the hylje offered further aid.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Killian Mortére's mandate urged the Dawnish not to take part in the Spring raid.

Highguard.t: Highborn ship captains helped carry Imperial forces safely to Greenwall in Spring, and the seven Highguard participants would gain a bonus if they joined the Summer raid.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orcs led by Ergot pressed deep into Skallahn during the Spring raid, which would give them a veterans' advantage in any return.

Jotun.t: The Jotun Jarls drove off the Spring raiders but grew overconfident. A strong Summer raid could scatter several Jarls, plunder their mines and stores, damage the Kongegőr causeway and disrupt the resupply and raising of their armies.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr assembly, at first supportive, endorsed Meredith Nighthaven in renouncing the Spring raid as unwise.

The League.t: A handful of League companies joined the Spring raid, and their six citizens would gain the veterans' bonus if they returned to Skallahn.

The Marches.t: The Marcher Assembly's guidance to strike only military targets shaped the Summer raid, and Marcher fleets could operate in the Gullet at full strength. Jointly naming a Marshal with Wintermark and honouring House Oddsboy's captains could bring more ships to the raid and possibly a permanent Gullet raiding option for Marcher fleets.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Lochias's mandate urged the Urizen not to take part in the Spring raid.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk supplied the largest share of the Spring raiders, and Wintermark fleets could sail the Gullet without penalty. The assembly could name a Marshal jointly with the Marches, the hylje offered further aid, and the Westerhal fisherfolk stood to gain new fishing grounds.

Take it further.o: After a disappointing Spring raid on Skallahn that lacked the strength to achieve lasting harm, the Empire was offered the chance to launch a second, better-planned raid in Summer 384YE. The Jotun were overconfident and had not yet shored up their defences.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: The fisherfolk of Westerhal in the West Marsh helped ferry warriors and could, with enough fleet escort, win a permanent opportunity to fish the rich western and northern Gullet.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: If Greenwall were overrun and the Jotun lost Tanikipari, they could not resupply the Fortress of Kalant in Stark until the Spring Equinox 385YE without giving the Empire a battle opportunity.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: The Floes of Tokusok, only technically part of the Suaq Wastes, were the Sentinel Gate destination where the Mediator of Hyljehal might secure 1,000 strength from the hylje's estranged cousins.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: A Jotun loss of Tanikipari, combined with an overrun Greenwall, would cut off resupply to the Fortress of Kalant in Stark.

Skallahn/Bjarkey.t: Mentioned in passing: some Spring raiders got as far as Bjarkey before being forced to retreat.

Skallahn/Eyrarfell.t: With 15,000 strength the raid could breach Eyrarfell against Jarl Gilla Sverrisdóttir's ulvenwar and plunder her mines. At 20,000 it could loot the Shining Caverns mithril mine and threaten the Steelweaver's Crucible, denying Jotun armies natural resupply for two seasons.

Skallahn/Greenwall.t: Spring raiders landed safely in Greenwall. With 5,000 to 10,000 strength, a Summer raid could overrun its forges and mines, scatter Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard and burn his hall, and make Greenwall easier to capture until the end of the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

Skallahn/Iron Stand.t: Spring raiders reached Iron Stand. With 10,000 strength, a Summer raid could defeat Jarl Ebbe of Overgaard and Jarl Alvilda Ottesen and plunder the Broken Chasm for white granite, crippling Jotun emergency resupply for two seasons.

Skallahn/Ulfrsmoor.t: Raiders would spare the temple of Ulfrskelf and the market town of Overgaard. With 12,500 strength they could storm Jarl Ottesen's fortified hall and empty his storehouses, cheapening Imperial spy networks across Kalsea.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the earlier mapping of the Bay was cited as the model for any future scouting of the Sea of Snow.

Hordalant.t: If 10,000 strength of fleets burned the Kongegőr causeway linking Skallahn and Hordalant, Jotun armies crossing between the two would have to halt on arrival for at least six months.

Kallavesa.t: If at least 5,000 strength of fleets supported the raid, Westerhal's fisherfolk could fish the rich Jotun-held waters of the Gullet under Winterfolk escort and bring prosperity to western Kallavesa.

Mitwold.t: Jarvey "Strongoar" Oddsboy of Steward's Landing near Odd's End pledged 1,000 strength to the raid. With 5,000 strength of fleets, the village could become a permanent staging post for Marcher raids on the Kalsea coast.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Lazarus of the Necropolis is listed among the Highguard participants in the Spring raid.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Uberto Alessandri di Caricomare vacino a Sarvos is listed among the League participants in the Spring raid.

Sea of Snow.t: If fleets reached 12,500 strength, they could push into the Sea of Snow, letting the Senate commission voyages at the Autumn Equinox to map the coasts west of the Empire.

Sermersuaq.t: Overrunning Greenwall would stop the Jotun resupplying the Fortress of Kalant in Stark if they lost Tanikipari. A Sentinel Gate conjunction to the Floes of Tokusok, technically in the Suaq Wastes, offered the chance to recruit the hylje's bloodthirsty cousins.

Skallahn.t: Skallahn was raided in Spring without lasting effect, and faced a second raid whose results ranged from overrunning Greenwall to looting the Shining Caverns of Eyrarfell. After this season the Jotun would be ready, ruling out another grand raid for a year or so.

Taken at the flood.d: Six armies (the Golden Sun, Golden Axe, Citadel Guard, Valiant Pegasus, Winter Sun and Iron Helms) advanced from the Towers of Dusk. The Druj armies had fled to the Mallum, leaving only warbands and holdouts. Their parting curses brought a devastating deluge, Spring-bound killer trees and malign Winter spirits. A Dawnish enchantment spread black roses, and a desiccating wind withered the Bleaks and Farweald. Druj resistance remains only in Murderdale and the Heart of Peytaht. The Karass refuse to co-operate, the Vendarri seek control of the Saltmarsh, and the Rahvin hold the Fangs. Three conjunctions offer chances to rescue Montanians, stop Varag Soulflayer and protect the Great Forest elders.

Dawn.t: With the Barrens newly allocated to Dawn, the Golden Sun ground forward alongside the Knights of Glory and the servants of the Bound King, whose clashes forced the Dawnish to keep them apart, while three Dawnish covens spread black roses in the armies' wake.

Druj.t: The Druj armies fled to the Mallum and left only holdouts in Murderdale and the Heart of Peytaht, but their ghulai unleashed a final barrage of curses and their warbands still threaten Montanian captives and the Great Forest elders.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Winter Sun led the effort to free the Druj slaves and met a mixed reception, and the Menrothat reminded the Varushkans of the offer they had made the Imperial Orcs regarding Farweald.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thunderous Tread of the Trees raging across Jotun-held Liathaven is compared with the Druj tree-spirits.

Navarr.t: The Senator for Therunin, Travid Longest Path, is charged with stopping a Druj force in the Heart of Peytaht, and success would see the Great Forest elders teach Navarr armies how to cross the Great Forest.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj binding of Spring spirits into trees is described as the first since Holberg.

Urizen.t: The Citadel Guard advanced steadily through the Bleaks and Farweald, ignored the Synod's call to act as liberators, and its scholars noted a surge of new Winter regio across the Barrens.

Varushka.t: The Golden Axe and the Iron Helms fought at the forefront of the advance but disregarded the Synod, and the Menrothat of Ossium sent emissaries to remind their Varushkan neighbours of the offer regarding Farweald.

Taken at the flood.o: In Summer 385YE the Imperial armies drove the scattered Druj from most of the Barrens, conquering the Bleaks, the Untrod Groves and Farweald, while a storm of Druj curses brought floods, murderous trees and Winter spirits across the territory.

The Barrens/Farweald.t: Farweald was conquered but scarred by a desiccating wind, and the Menrothat are pressing their earlier offer concerning the region.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: Druj holdouts, reinforced by orcs fleeing Dawnguard, remain here, and a Druj band with heralds of Surut is moving to slaughter the elders of the Great Forest Orcs.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: A Druj force has captured Montanians, including Circe the Strider, to turn them into tortured souls, and the General of the Valiant Pegasus is asked to rout them.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Murderdale remains outside Imperial control, held by Druj holdouts reinforced by orcs fleeing Dawnguard, though they could do little to delay a renewed advance.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: A further magical tempest worsened the drowned marshes and caused deaths at the Fangs, still held by the Rahvin, while the Vendarri seek concessions ceding the Saltmarsh largely to their control.

The Barrens/The Untrod Groves.t: The Groves were conquered after Druj Spring wards claimed Imperial lives, but Varag Soulflayer is moving to a Winter regio there to release a Dream of Famine.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is cited as the last time the Druj bound killer spirits into trees.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Thunderous Tread of the Trees is noted as currently raging across Liathaven.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Menrothat of Ossium sent emissaries to the Varushkans about their offer concerning Farweald.

The Barrens.t: All of the Barrens except Murderdale and the Heart of Peytaht came under Imperial control, but the territory was ravaged by floods, killer trees, Winter spirits and spreading Winter regio, with heavy losses among both Dawnish and orc civilians.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Therunin is made responsible for stopping the Druj in the Heart of Peytaht.

Tale of the Golden Hare.d: At Spring Equinox the Fellowship of the Tangled Thorns was inquisited by Ula Ulanya Ulanaya of the Vigilance Assembly over blasphemy, idolatry and heresy; the assembly declined to castigate them. At Autumn Equinox Hubert Gremani passed a statement that the executed coven members were good and virtuous Varushkans. In defiant sympathy, Varushkans painted golden hares on signs, wore hare buckles and considered the less fortunate, though nobody agreed what the hare symbolised and some ideas bordered on heresy. The assembly could ignore it, name it a virtuous animal or denounce it as an idol. Hubert Gremani led a mandate naming the hare a symbol of Ambition; Esrys added a statement that revering or worshipping the golden hare remains idolatrous.

Varushka.t: Varushkans embraced the golden hare in memory of the Tangled Thorns, and their national assembly settled the matter by declaring the hare a symbol of Ambition while warning that worshipping it is idolatry.

Tale of the Golden Hare.o: After the Varushkan assembly declared the executed members of the Tangled Thorns coven good and virtuous Varushkans, people across Varushka, especially in Miekarova, began adopting the golden hare as a symbol. The Varushkan national assembly then mandated that the hare is a symbol of Ambition.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova, where the Tangled Thorns were largely based and Dušan Otecovna Zlata had served as senator, was a centre of the discussion that led vales to take up the golden hare.

Tales of imagination.d: Barien let Imperial heroes reach the Four Corners Fair from the Imperial regio, and each nation's egregore received invitations for five people. Meraud asked Catrina Words of Dawn to help run a game there. Sanvar Isk feuded with the orphans of the Little Mother and would again auction the Loom of Spells. Cathan Canae's heralds defended the Kallavesa and Hahnmark beacons, and she pledged the Drums of the Iron Harpoon if beacons are built in Sermersuaq and a white bear statue is raised. Azoth judged that the Navarr had transformed their nation. Janon's Shadowed Torchbrand title became available to appoint. Sadogua made offers to the Lyceum and the Marcher landskeepers. Jaheris and Eleonaris arranged a debate in Foracci. Barien announced a Pinnacle Tourney, and Lashonar sought letters of longing.

Dawn.t: Meraud sent a special invitation to Catrina Words The Unbelievably Magical, asking her to help run a game at the Four Corners Fair. Dawn's enchanters are said to know the Fair well, and the Knight of Roses received the nation's five invitations.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel threat is cited as the reason the Lyceum's scholars remain hidden behind walls of mist.

Navarr.t: Azoth declared itself satisfied that the Navarr had made a profound, lasting change to their nation. It offered to help reattune the last singing stone for Navarr covens once the Archmage of Night arranges a parley. Liaven also received the nation's invitations to the Four Corners Fair.

The League.t: Tassato's playwrights and comedians gleefully satirised Sanvar Isk's feud with the orphans of the Little Mother. Jaheris and Eleonaris's debate contest was set for the Solare Estate in Sarvos, overseen by the Guerra arbiters, and Escon received the League's Fair invitations.

Urizen.t: Meraud's magical lion-owl delivered an invitation to Menos of Urizen allowing five Urizen to visit the Four Corners Fair.

Varushka.t: Jaheris's silver-tongued emissary brought Mother Varushka an invitation for five Varushkans to visit the Four Corners Fair. A herald of Lashonar would also hand out tokens near the Varushkan Fire.

Wintermark.t: Cathan Canae's warrior-heralds defended the beacons of Kallavesa and Hahnmark. She pledged a third ritual, the Drums of the Iron Harpoon, if Sermersuaq's beacons are built and a white granite bear statue honours her aid, and she means to give it to the general of the Narwhal's Spear. Sulkavaris received the nation's Fair invitations.

Tales of imagination.o: In Summer 386YE a series of eternal-driven opportunities reached the Empire, including access for heroes to the Four Corners Fair, Cathan Canae's offer of a third ritual to Wintermark and Azoth's readiness to help the Navarr reattune the last singing stone. Further items covered Sanvar Isk's Loom auction, Janon's Shadowed Torchbrand, Sadogua's offers, a debate contest, Barien's planned tourney and Lashonar's call for letters of longing.

Sarvos/Foracci.t: The Solare Estate in Foracci would host the debate between Jaheris's and Eleonaris's champions at 11pm on the Saturday of the Summer Solstice. The Sentinel Gate allows up to 100 people to attend.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: One of Cathan Canae's ogre-like heralds came to Atalaq bearing her pledge of a third boon if beacons are built in Sermersuaq.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: the last singing stone that Azoth offers to help reattune was recovered from the depths of Brocéliande.

Hahnmark.t: Crimson-robed bear-people of Cathan Canae emerged from Kalpaheim and fought alongside the Imperial armies there to defeat Cold Sun, defending the beacons.

Kallavesa.t: Wolf-like archers and scouts of Cathan Canae came forth from Rundahl Hall to protect the marshes and their beacons alongside Wintermark's heroes.

Miaren.t: A brightly painted herald of Azoth arrived in Seren with the eternal's message that it was ready to help the Navarr reattune the singing stone.

Sarvos.t: The Solare Estate in Sarvos was chosen to host the debate contest between the champions of Jaheris and Eleonaris. Eliza di Sarvos is also named as a past participant in a Lashonar opportunity.

Sermersuaq.t: Cathan Canae pledged that if beacons are built in Sermersuaq she will grant the Drums of the Iron Harpoon to call forth tusked-folk to protect them. In return she asks for a white granite bear statue on the shores of Lake Atkonaroq.

Tassato.t: Sanvar Isk's broadsheets and his commissioned play 'The Rats Of The Little Mother' became a comic sensation in Tassato. His attempt to sue the theatre company turned the play into a runaway commercial success.

Tales of mystery.d: The Deadwood Knight answered the Earl of Fools' challenge by sending over a hundred unliving warriors against the Earl's estate. Dawnish and Varushkan defenders repelled them. Brass Coast hakima who attended the Spring Equinox were cursed by the Three Sisters, and the Urizeni stargazer Cassius was returning to Anvil. Memory-swapping through Cast Off the Chain of Memory ceased, but tales spread of Night magicians losing their identities. An unseen beast began stalking Kalpaheim after Ogila's Tower cracked. Navarr reclaimed Miaren's calcified trees as art. Combing the Beach lost its power in exchange for Netweaver's Eye. A cambion whale harried ships in the Sea of Snow. Conjunctions were offered to Gorek's Reach and the Starstrand steading.

Dawn.t: The Earl of Fools' estate was attacked by the Deadwood Knight's unliving cohort, which left behind the heads of the troubadours Gerard and Margueritte of Valewatch. Separately, a Dawnish guiser gained a long-dead wizard's ritual knowledge through stolen memories and has since disappeared.

Navarr.t: Inspired by an enchantment and Nathair Autumngale's statement of principle, the Navarr turned Miaren's bone trees into living art, a practice stridings carried across the Empire. The Starstrand steading meanwhile sought Imperial help with a strange affliction.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: The Marches are not named on this page, and no event described takes place in Marcher lands.

Urizen.t: An Urizeni illuminate was among three Night magicians brought to the Quiet Hall with a fractured identity. The Urizeni stargazer Cassius was returning to Anvil with new portents concerning the Three Sisters.

Varushka.t: The Varushka assembly urged its soldiery to band together against the Schlacta of Rot, and Varushkan warriors helped repel the attack on the Earl of Fools' estate. Tales also spoke of two Varushkan cabalists who traded away their childhood memories, and of former cultists discovered in Moresvah.

Wintermark.t: A mysterious unseen beast began stalking Kalpaheim after Ogila's Tower cracked. A Wintermark mystic was also among the Night magicians left with a shattered identity by memory-swapping.

Tales of mystery.o: A Summer 386YE Wind of Fortune gathered several magical mysteries across the Empire. They included the Deadwood Knight's attack on the Earl of Fools' estate, a Three Sisters curse on Freeborn hakima, an unseen beast stalking Kalpaheim, an inspiring enchantment over Miaren and a strange affliction at a Navarr steading.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: The Starstrand steading in Boar's Dell was the site of a conjunction for 50 participants. It was organised by the Spear of the Seven, Corwyn Heartsbane, to investigate an aura driving people to seek connection.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: Mentioned in passing: West Marsh is not named on this page, and none of its events take place there.

Karsk/Moresvah.t: The shunned vale of Gorek's Reach in Moresvah was found to be home to former cultists of an unknown power. A possible combat encounter there fell to the Custodian of the Lost, Anthemius Netherwatch.

Brocéliande.t: The Starstrand steading in Boar's Dell, near the Semmerholm border, was afflicted by a feeling of incompleteness after a merrow offered to "call down the stars". Heroes were invited to investigate.

Hahnmark.t: In Kalpaheim, a roar from Ogila's Tower left a crack through its regio, and the sounds and breath of an unseen great beast began spreading across the city at night. Some rumours accused the tower's owner, Kaapo Kingfishering, of a dark pact.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: Kallavesa is not named on this page, and none of its events take place there.

Karov.t: The Deadwood Knight continued to build its forces in Karov, threatening the people there, and it cannot yet be permanently destroyed.

Karsk.t: In the vale of Gorek's Reach in Karsk, the volhov Rakhel Vitkusovna discovered many adults were former cultists seeking to atone. The Custodian of the Lost was charged with finding out more.

Miaren.t: A Night enchantment charged Miaren with inspiration, and its people painted, carved and decorated the trees calcified by Cold Sun's Empty Hand, transforming them into works of art before the magic faded.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is not named on this page, and none of its events take place there.

Sea of Snow.t: A scarred cambion whale rammed ships and swallowed objects held overboard, favouring laden trading vessels. The Lictors believe a Callidus herald inside it is corrupting the creature, and its attacks may come to affect trade with Faraden.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the afflicted Starstrand steading sits almost on the border between Brocéliande and Semmerholm, so Dawn was asked to be represented among the volunteers.

Weirwater.t: The Deadwood Knight continued to build its unliving forces in Weirwater and remained a looming threat to its people.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Zenith is not named on this page; its only Urizeni links are the stargazer Cassius and an afflicted illuminate.

Talk softly.d: The Great Forest Orcs stored Rivers of Life after realising its danger near the vallorn. Recovered with Navarr and Highborn aid, they no longer need herb support, though the Holt of the Oak has stalled. Around a hundred asked to join stridings for a year, but only with a Senate motion or a strongly passed Navarr Assembly statement; this risked them mapping the Empire and their briar allies coming too. The Thule sent Rak to Anvil for a last attempt at a treaty, warned over magic in the Silver Peaks, massed armies in Sermersuaq and Karsk, and freed Wintermark slaves paid for by Eska Crowspeaker. Jotun thralls awaited a Synod resolution. The Grendel rejected peace but ceded Spiral.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: there was no news of the Druj, though the Great Forest Orcs hoped to return to the Barrens once the Druj were defeated.

Grendel.t: The Salt Lords flatly refused the offered peace treaty, embassy and mithril trade, called Solen's Doubt a setback rather than a defeat, and formally ceded Spiral to the Empire while the Black Plateau endured.

Highguard.t: The Highborn were thanked for helping the Great Forest Orcs recover, and visiting orcs were greatly impressed by the gardens of High Chalcis in Reikos.

Imperial Orcs.t: The stream of Thule orc merchants coming through Crow's Ridge into Skarsind slowed to a trickle. The Thule also offered to negotiate a mithril route through the Silver Peaks into Skarsind.

Jotun.t: The Jotun were expected to possibly conquer southern Sermersuaq, prompting Thule offers over the Pride of Ikka's Tears mine. Separately, the former Jotun thralls awaited a Synod resolution of their concerns with the Way.

Navarr.t: The Navarr were asked, by Senate motion or Assembly statement, to let around a hundred Great Forest Orcs travel with their stridings for a year, and the orcs thanked them for their aid. Merel was advised to ready a coven for the Dance of Navarr and Thorn at the Thule parley.

The League.t: A Grendel envoy came under a flag of truce to the docks of Sarvos to reject Consul Aureliana di Sarvos's peace offer before a jeering crowd.

The Marches.t: Continued improvement in the Mournwold depended on a satisfactory outcome for the Jotun thralls, whose representative Sigdór had left the matter with the Synod.

Thule.t: The Thule sent Rak to Anvil for a final attempt at a treaty before the 379YE peace expired, warned against harmful magic in the Silver Peaks, and moved additional armies into Sermersuaq and Karsk.

Urizen.t: The Grendel ceded Spiral to the Empire and mockingly wished the Urizen luck reclaiming the poisoned wasteland while the Black Plateau persisted.

Varushka.t: Thule merchant traffic through the mountains into Varushka dwindled. The Thule massed armies in Krevsaty in Karsk and again raised an icy magical fortress there.

Wintermark.t: About two dozen former Wintermark slaves, freed by Eska Crowspeaker's payment, reached Fjellreven Hall and resolved to join her congregation to repay their debt.

Talk softly.o: In Summer 382YE the Great Forest Orcs, recovered and settled in Therunin, asked for formal Imperial or Navarr permission to travel the trods with Navarr stridings. Meanwhile the Thule prepared a final round of peace talks amid troop build-ups, and the Grendel rejected peace while ceding Spiral to the Empire.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: Imperial scouts reported additional Thule armies and a newly raised magical fortress of ice and iron spikes in the hills here.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: A caravan of freed Wintermark slaves was escorted by Thule warriors to within sight of Fjellreven Hall in the East Floes.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The Thule moved more armies onto the slopes, warned against harmful magic, and offered either a mithril route or to seize the Pride of Ikka's Tears mine.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: The once steady flow of Thule orc merchants through Crow's Ridge slowed to a trickle as the treaty's end approached.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: The Grendel said the insane remnants of their armies remained camped around Apstrus, leaving the Empire to deal with them.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Great Forest Orcs continued building their new lives here, with weirwood-fed herb gardens and some farms tending goats and cows, though the Holt of the Oak stalled.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Great Forest Orc apothecaries took temporary residence at Peakedge Stead as healers, and orc hunters encountered the trods in the Song.

Verthandi/Hengill.t: Mentioned in passing: the freed slaves had farmed near Samkǒma in Hengill under the Thule.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel noted that they hold other territories on the Bay of Catazar, and further information on their threat to fleets there was referenced.

Karsk.t: The Thule moved additional armies into Krevsaty and raised a glittering magical fortress of ice and iron spikes, possibly in preparation for war.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: Rak issued his statement on Sermersuaq from the Thule embassy in Miekarova.

Mournwold.t: The territory's improving situation rested on finding a satisfactory resolution to the Jotun thralls' problems with the Way.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: any Thule claim on the bounty of the Silver Peaks mithril mine would be a matter for the Ambassador to Otkodov, Yevgeni Katzev.

Reikos.t: Great Forest Orcs visited High Chalcis, whose gardens would begin benefiting Reikos herb gardens after the Summer solstice. Reikos's assistance had helped the orcs recover.

Sarvos.t: A lone Grendel envoy landed at the Sarvos docks under a flag of truce to reject the Empire's peace offer and cede Spiral, departing amid heckling.

Sermersuaq.t: The Thule warned against magic harming their people in the Silver Peaks, massed troops there and offered deals over the mithril mine. Freed Wintermark slaves arrived in the East Floes.

Skarsind.t: Thule merchant traffic into Skarsind slowed to a trickle, and the Thule offered to negotiate a mithril route from the Silver Peaks into the territory.

Spiral.t: The Grendel formally ceded all control of Spiral to the Empire while the Black Plateau persists, leaving maddened remnants of their armies around Apstrus.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs kept the Rivers of Life text for their hoped-for return to the Barrens after the Druj are defeated.

Therunin.t: The Great Forest Orcs became a common sight trading with the Navarr, herb and business penalties ended after the Summer solstice, and around a hundred orcs sought to join stridings from Therunin.

Verthandi.t: Mentioned in passing: the freed Wintermark slaves had worked a farm near Samkǒma in Hengill supplying the settlement with a hardy root.

Talking sailor.d: In the weeks before the Winter Solstice 381YE, attacks on traders crossing the Bay rose, with pirates aided by shark-like creatures likely to be heralds of the Mother-of-Wrecks. Unless the situation changed, trading fleets from Tassato, Sarvos, the Brass Coast, Highguard and Urizen faced a one-rank production penalty. Asavean, Sarcophan and Jarmish ships were left alone. The Senate could have let Imperial ships fly those nations' colours, at a diplomatic cost. It could also fund a 50-Throne project for captains and civil service cartographers to chart the Bay's coasts and territories. The Senate voted to map the Bay, and many captains took part. The Grendel continued to raid Imperial shipping.

Grendel.t: Grendel pirates of the Broken Shore, spurred by Siakha's growing influence and left loosely organised by the defence of the fishing fleet, stepped up their raids on Imperial traders and continued raiding after the Solstice.

Highguard.t: Highguard's trading fleets faced a one-rank production penalty from increased Grendel piracy if they traded through the Bay in the coming season.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast trading fleets risked the piracy penalty, while their corsairs, sworn to protect Imperial shipping, were stretched by the Grendel invasion of Madruga. Their long family knowledge of the Bay made them obvious partners in mapping it.

The League.t: League fleets based in Tassato and Sarvos faced reduced production from Grendel piracy if they engaged in trade through the Bay.

Urizen.t: Urizeni trading fleets were among those facing a one-rank production penalty from the surge in Grendel piracy.

Talking sailor.o: Grendel pirates, emboldened by their control of the Bay of Catazar and backed by heralds of the eternal Siakha, began preying more heavily on Imperial trading ships. The Senate was offered two responses, flying foreign colours or funding a map of the Bay, and it voted to map the Bay.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Bay was dominated militarily by the Grendel armada and plagued by Siakha-backed pirates. The Senate voted to fund a concerted effort to chart its coastline, territories and features.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel invasion of Madruga is cited as a problem distracting the Brass Coast corsairs from protecting shipping.

Sarvos.t: Fleets based in Sarvos faced a one-rank production penalty if they traded through the pirate-infested Bay in the coming season.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the ongoing campaign in Spiral is noted as a reason the Military Council was unprepared for any strike against the Broken Shore.

Tassato.t: Fleets based in Tassato faced a one-rank production penalty if they engaged in trade while Grendel piracy surged.

Talking to friends.d: Mauriac of Eyrie's respectful letter persuaded Lady Madrianna to tell the Empire that the Plenum considered the burning of Siroc to have answered the attack on Chalonsio. As a goodwill gesture, the Plenum lifted its bounties on ships trading with the Empire. Peace talks would require an end to all missionary work. In return, Asavea might withdraw its support for the Grendel and reopen its ports. If the Empire refused, Asavea would increase its military aid to the Grendel. The Regario Dossier's agents obtained contact details for three Asavean factions. The Sumaash sent a dose of true liao and promised one each season until the Plenum falls. They rejected joint efforts to anchor the Way and answered questions about Abrasian oil and excommunication.

Grendel.t: The Asaveans would consider withdrawing their military support for the Grendel if peace were agreed, but warned they would increase it if the Empire kept sending missionaries.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Accalon of Highguard is listed as the Imperial ambassador to the Sumaah Republic, whose sharply worded letter left the Sumaash uncertain how to respond.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Asavean Plenum cites the Grendel capture and Asavean burning of Siroc as having avenged the attack on Chalonsio.

Talking to friends.o: In Summer 387YE the Asavean Plenum, humbled by the Pax Sarcophan and its naval defeat at Zemeh, signalled that it was open to ending its war with the Empire if Imperial missionaries stopped preaching the Way in the Archipelago. Meanwhile the Sumaah Republic, grateful for Imperial help against the Asavean armada, began sending true liao each season but refused to work jointly on anchoring the Way in Asavea.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the destruction of Siroc is recalled as the Asavean revenge for Chalonsio, which the Plenum now regards as settled.

Tears in the rain.d: Stone Toad orcs still held out in Tamarbode and Grey Charge but were disorganised. A Druj fear miasma, anchored by hard-to-damage monoliths, blocked resettlement and would drain the treasury until it was cleared. Spring magic had eradicated the Reikos flux. The Vigilant Swan and the Great Forest weirwood groves were back in Imperial hands, giving the Senate two Bourse seats to allocate. Spoils of war awaited the Military Council. Many restless dead haunted the land, and Magister Gideon proposed a plan to deal with them. Two great works were offered: restoring the Gardens of High Chalcis and building the fortress of Exile in Broken Ride. The Senate later assigned Reikos to Highguard, and both works were commissioned.

Druj.t: The Druj lost Reikos and their citadel of Urith Barath, and their last orcs were left disorganised in Tamarbode and Grey Charge, many sheltering around the fear-exuding monoliths. Their gardens under Buruk Tepel had prospered and could teach the Empire lessons.

Highguard.t: Highborn refugees expected Reikos to be assigned to them, and the Senate did assign it to Highguard, making the Vigilant Swan a national seat. Highguard went on to commission both the Gardens of High Chalcis and the fortress of Exile, though it faced the miasma and the unquiet dead of its slaughtered people.

Navarr.t: The Navarr helped liberate Reikos: the Black Thorns under General Foxden struck north into Broken Ride fast enough to stop a massacre and free the slaves in the camps. Navarri of Peakedge Stead also wished to help restore the gardens in gratitude to the Highborn who had defended Therunin.

Tears in the rain.o: After Dawnish and Navarr forces liberated Reikos from the Druj in Winter 379YE, this Wind of Fortune set out the state of the ravaged territory and the opportunities for rebuilding it. Everything depended on the Senate deciding which nation the territory would be assigned to.

Reikos/Broken Ride.t: Navarr forces took the camps below the Great Forest, where many slaves fought their way free and the weirwood groves returned to Imperial hands. Broken Ride was also the chosen site for the fortress of Exile, commissioned in Winter 380YE.

Reikos/Chalcis Mount.t: The Druj citadel of Urith Barath at High Chalcis was destroyed and the town lay in ruins, though its Druj-tended gardens survived. Those gardens were reclaimed as a great work in Summer 380YE.

Reikos/Grey Charge.t: Grey Charge remained one of the last two regions held by disorganised, defensive Druj, and Imperial forces were expected to retake it easily.

Reikos/Haros Water.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn soldiers found the same suffering and atrocity across Haros Water as elsewhere in Reikos.

Reikos/Longshire.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn soldiers reported widespread suffering and atrocity across Longshire after its liberation.

Reikos/Riverwatch.t: The Vigilant Swan in Riverwatch, haunted and defiled by Druj atrocities, was back in Imperial hands. Its white granite Bourse seat was later allocated as a national resource.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Tamarbode was one of the two western regions still held by disorganised Druj remnants, expected to fall easily to Imperial forces.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Mentioned in passing: the people of Peakedge Stead, Highborn exiles and Navarri alike, were said to be keen to help restore the Gardens of High Chalcis.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: refugees from Bastion were among those assuming Reikos would go to Highguard, and siege engineers from the White City helped draw up the plans for Exile.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed fortress of Exile would keep watch on the threat from Brocéliande to the north-east.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: refugees from Casinea expected Reikos to be assigned to Highguard, and engineers from the Silent Sentinel helped present the plans for Exile.

Reikos.t: Reikos was liberated but left poisoned, haunted and blanketed in Druj miasma, which prevented resettlement and taxation. It was later assigned to Highguard, and the Gardens of High Chalcis and the fortress of Exile were commissioned to help restore it.

Therunin.t: Highborn refugees from Therunin awaited Reikos's assignment, and the people of Peakedge Stead, both Highborn and Navarri, were keen to help restore the Gardens of High Chalcis.

Temple of the bull.d: The Asaveans shipped about fifty wains of white granite to Oran under warship escort, brought no slaves and paid Imperial labourers handsomely. Once complete, the temple was expected to warm relations with the Archipelago, improve business income across Feroz and create an Asavean-appointed liaison chosen with guidance from Feroz's senator. Asavea also invited the Way to build a temple in Nemoria. The Assembly of Nine judged that assisting construction was idolatry, and Abaddon de Rondell's work in Feroz slowed the project and raised its labour costs, likely creating a diplomatic incident. Jorma Steelhail's call to destroy the temple failed 327 to 421; a motion funding the Nemoria temple was withdrawn after a theft.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn faced a foreign temple to Asavean idols rising in Oran, with even their relaxed priests resenting it, while Freeborn labourers were offered lucrative work that the Synod now declared idolatrous. Senator Pedro i Taziel i Riquezz was invited to put forward candidates for liaison with the Asavean priests.

Temple of the bull.o: With Senate permission, Asavean priests began building a grand temple to Balo of the Foam and the Black Bull at the port of Oran in Feroz. The Assembly of Nine denounced it as idolatry, and Abaddon de Rondell's preaching delayed its completion until shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The temple was being built at the port of Oran, where Asavean warships had escorted the granite cargo and where the Synod's named priest worked to discourage local labourers from joining the project.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the completed temple was expected to draw traders away from other ports around the Bay of Catazar.

Feroz.t: Feroz hosted the Asavean temple and stood to gain a modest boost to business income from traders it attracted, but Abaddon de Rondell's preaching against it pushed completion back to shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE.

Ten travellers tales.d: The Kabani traders returned to sell narcotics outside the Forge, though no Blue Lotus. Brewton merchants planned to sell their Bittersweet Brew at the same time. The Ethengraw, Illarawm and Yerende septs, whose armoury, ossuary and gardens the Imperial Orcs had built, came to pledge to the nation. The Axou scholar Theodosia landed at Crown's Quay holding the shield Bawn-watch. The Venturesome Harrier explorers returned from Screed's Black Plateau. Two Thule warlocks asked to meet Navarr scholars of the vallorn. The Jotun ghodi Osgar Hildsson sought talks on ancestors at the Tree of Names. Tassatan orcs came to watch their senator's election. Doktor Meier wished to debate the Greater Good. Pilgrims who had renounced Asavea landed near Sanctuary bearing news for Eli of the Cenotaph.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the three septs left Ossium after the Druj were defeated, having lived under them for years, and the Yerende's herbal arts are said to nearly rival those of the Druj.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Crown's Quay harbourmaster had uneasy dreams of Grendel invaders reaching the docks.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Necropolis shores received the Axou scholar Theodosia with the shield Bawn-watch at Crown's Quay. A Highborn Inquisitor confirmed the anointings of the Asavean pilgrims, and Highborn wayfarers then escorted them towards Anvil.

Imperial Orcs.t: Now that the Ethengraw Armoury, Illarawm Ossuary and Yerende Gardens are built, the three septs came to Anvil to formally pledge themselves to the nation and stand as equals beside the Sunstorm and Sannite septs.

Jotun.t: The Jotun ghodi Osgar Hildsson travelled alone under a flag of truce. He swore he sought no fight and wished only to discuss ancestors, mysticism and shared ancient culture.

Navarr.t: Two Thule warlocks acting for some of the Dragons asked the Ambassador to Otkodov to introduce them to Navarr scholars versed in the vallorn. A Navarri was also named as the new opposite number of the Crown's Quay harbourmaster.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Axou scholar Theodosia has leased a small house on the outskirts of Myfanwy's Rest for her year-long stay in the Empire.

The League.t: Leaguers could expect the Harrier explorers' tale of Screed and their bid for investment, a Tassatan playwright seeking a dramaturgical company, and Tassatan orc business owners weighing up the senatorial candidates. The Harlequin had also invited the Kabani traders to a play premiere at the League Theatre.

Thule.t: Two prestigious Thule warlocks travelled from Otkodov on the personal business of two Dragons rather than the Five-Who-Are-One. They were escorted by blue-cloaked orc warriors.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: unlike earlier Thule delegations, the two warlocks expressed no interest in speaking to the people of Varushka.

Wintermark.t: Osgar Hildsson invited Wintermark mystics, and anyone interested, to meet him at the Tree of Names in the Wintermark camp to talk about ancestors and shared culture.

Ten travellers tales.o: Ahead of the 385YE Autumn Equinox, word spread of several groups of visitors bound for Anvil. They included Axou traders and scholars, three orc septs ready to pledge themselves to the Imperial Orcs, Thule warlocks, a Jotun ghodi, new orc citizens of Tassato, a Commonwealth philosopher and self-declared former Asaveans.

Necropolis/Fishguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the harbourmaster sent Theodosia on her way to Fishguard after she landed.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Mentioned in passing: Longbeach is not named directly; the page describes arrivals on the Necropolis coast at Crown's Quay and near Sanctuary.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossuary is not named directly; Spiral appears as the place many new orc citizens left and many human Leaguers moved to.

Spiral/Screed.t: The Company of the Venturesome Harrier claim to have climbed the south face of the Black Plateau in Screed with paying customers, and now seek investment for further expeditions.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the orcs leaving Spiral mostly settled in Sarvos and Tassato, preferring not to stray too far from the Bay of Catazar.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Brewton traders were making their way east to Casinea and Anvil.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: a few adventurous orc citizens from Spiral moved to Holberg.

Madruga.t: The visiting Axou scholar Theodosia has taken a lease on a small house on the outskirts of Myfanwy's Rest and is open to missives from Imperial scholars.

Necropolis.t: Theodosia landed at Crown's Quay with reams of paperwork and the shield Bawn-watch, declared as diplomatic luggage. Pilgrims who had renounced Asavea came ashore near the funerary jetties of Sanctuary and were questioned before being allowed onward.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ethengraw, Illarawm and Yerende septs left Ossium after the Druj were defeated.

Otkodov.t: Two Thule warlocks set out from Otkodov for Anvil in a covered ox wagon and asked the Ambassador to Otkodov for an introduction to Navarr vallorn scholars.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the harbourmaster thought of Reikos on recognising the Shield of Vigilance and wished it could stay.

Sarvos.t: Many of the new orc citizens leaving Spiral settled in Sarvos, and some of them established businesses there.

Skallahn.t: The Jotun ghodi Osgar Hildsson emerged from Skallahn under a flag of truce, bound for Anvil.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind has been home to the three septs since they arrived two years ago, and the Imperial Orcs have now built them an armoury, an ossuary and gardens.

Spiral.t: Some new orc citizens left Spiral for other League cities while human Leaguers moved in to become citizens of Apulian. Explorers also returned from an expedition to Screed.

Tassato.t: Tassatan orc business owners planned to watch their city's senatorial election and might back a candidate with their wealth. The explorer Alexandre and the playwright Mirabil also hail from Tassato.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: a few adventurous orc citizens from Spiral moved to Temeschwar.

Tend to the Flame.d: Only Marcher agents of the Silent Bell could get close to the suspicious Whittlefolk. Their list of ringleaders went to Cardinal Ser Ancél Watcher, and they also warned of Hatred dedicates among Marchers at Anvil. Condemning three-quarters of the named leaders would destroy the sect. Any condemnation would end Whittle's green iron shipments to Tassato, and a leader from Little Mournwold would cause that enclave to collapse. The Synod condemned twelve, including Margaret Whittle of Little Mournwold. The wind proposed a Beater's Hall at Sarcombe to protect the pacifist thralls from bandits. It noted that their reincarnation beliefs still block their admission as Marchers. Marchers also debated a "Declaration of Remorse" and thresher reprisals against curses.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: a Silent Bell agent used Dawnish wine as a pretext in Whittle, and the sect's anointing stirred hatred of the Dawnish in him.

Imperial Orcs.t: Bloodcrow Udoo's mandate offered a place to thralls willing to fight, but Irontide Lok's statement rejected the thralls' belief in reincarnation. The thralls reacted calmly and respected the nation more for it, though the statement deepened the doctrinal obstacle to their becoming Marchers.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: as the thralls' former masters who were driven from the Mourn, and as a continuing threat of raiders across the Mournwold border.

The League.t: The League assembly had refused sanctuary to the Whittlefolk. Under the terms set out, any condemnation ended Whittle's green iron shipments to Tassato, and a sect leader proving to be from Little Mournwold would see that enclave shunned and scattered.

The Marches.t: Marcher Silent Bell agents exposed the Whittle sect, and Marchers at Anvil were suspected of harbouring Hatred dedicates. The Marcher assembly still holds the open mandate to invite the thralls into the nation. Its people feared renewed curses, and the thresher Alisoun Bathwater urged a statement encouraging reprisals against anyone who curses Marcher lands.

Tend to the Flame.o: In Winter 383YE the Silent Bell's covert investigation of Whittle gave the Cardinal of Vigilance the names of the leaders of a sect of Hatred, and the Synod went on to condemn twelve Whittlefolk for blasphemy and heresy. The wind also covered the Mournwold thralls' future, bandits preying on them, and Marcher fears over the Rivers Run Red interdiction.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Green March is one of the regions where the former Jotun thralls farm, and it is now marked as home to many foreign orcs. These farms have become easy prey for bandits and thieves because the thralls will not take up arms.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Southmoor is one of the regions where the Mournwold thralls are content on their farms, and it is now marked as home to many foreign orcs. These pacifist farmers are increasingly targeted by outlaws and thieves.

Bregasland.t: Marcher magicians feared that if the Conclave lifted the Rivers Run Red interdiction, the Bregas marshes could be cursed next. Bregasland threshers were among those pressing for reprisals against cursers, though its landskeepers were sanguine about Mountain Remembers Its Youth.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: its vallornspawn were described as currently agitated and prone to boiling across into Mournwold.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: its landskeepers were more sanguine than Mournwold's about destroying Mountain Remembers Its Youth.

Mournwold.t: The Whittle sect of Hatred was exposed, and twelve Whittlefolk were condemned for blasphemy and heresy. Bandits preyed on the pacifist thralls, prompting proposals for a Beater's Hall at Sarcombe, and the territory still bore the scars of Rivers Run Red.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: none of the Mournwold thralls planned to move to Skarsind despite the Imperial Orc offer.

Tassato.t: Tassato is home to the Little Mournwold enclave and received seasonal green iron from Whittle. That arrangement would end with any condemnation, and the enclave faced collapse if a sect leader was found among its citizens; Margaret Whittle of Little Mournwold was among those condemned.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: its landskeepers were more sanguine than Mournwold's about destroying Mountain Remembers Its Youth.

Tested again and again.d: After Synod statements urged priests to use their Right of Witness at the Military Council, Tarrat of the Legion's Rookery proposed ten national chaplains with judgement powers over their nation's generals. Carabella di Sarvos revived a plan to strengthen the Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path, including a veto on Declarations of Concord that would need a constitutional motion. Vitruvia of Tabulos suggested a Virtuous Wayleave appointed by the Synod. Jereboam of Sanctuary proposed Synod appointment of ambassadors and stronger powers for the Chaplain Consular, and others suggested similar changes for the Auditor and Imperial Inquisitor. The Constitutional Court found none of these unconstitutional in principle. The Freeborn objection to Almodin Oktístis building the Iron Qanat had little effect, and the Zemress festival was declined.

Dawn.t: Viviane de Coeurdefer's Assembly of the Nine mandate called priests to witness the Military Council, and the Dawn National Assembly sent Odelina de Rondell to act as confessor to the Dawnish generals until the end of Autumn 383YE.

Highguard.t: Jereboam of Sanctuary proposed that the Synod appoint the Empire's ambassadors and that the Chaplain Consular gain powers of revocation and excommunication. He praised Accalon of Felix's Watch's handling of Sumaah, and Zephaniah of Felix's Watch, Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path, was named as seeking Synod guidance.

Imperial Orcs.t: Tarrat, a veteran orc preacher at the Legion's Rookery, proposed national chaplains who would support and hold to account each nation's generals. Plans to assign an Imperial Wayleave to the orcs inspired Vitruvia's Virtuous Wayleave idea.

Navarr.t: The Navarr National Assembly backed the call for guides to attend the Military Council and nominated Neala as liaison between Navarr guides and their generals.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn Assembly's objection to Almodin Oktístis building the Iron Qanat drew little support among the Freeborn, apart from the Zemress refugees. The Senate could commission the Qanat again without him, and a Freeborn mandate already bars Synod interference with the Temple in Oran.

Tested again and again.o: Debate sparked by Severin von Holberg's sermon turned in Autumn 382YE to the Synod's relationship with the Military Council, Conclave, Bourse and Senate. Several priests and scholars put forward proposals that would need Senate motions to enact, while the lingering effect of the sermon blunted some potential religious conflicts.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The Temple in Oran, which welcomes dozens of Asavean visitors each season, remains protected from Synod interference by the earlier Freeborn mandate of tolerance.

Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand.t: Mentioned in passing: linked to Jereboam of Sanctuary, the young wayfarer behind the ambassadorial and Chaplain Consular proposals.

Redoubt/Tomari.t: Mentioned in passing: linked to Vitruvia of Tabulos, the architect who proposed a Synod-appointed Virtuous Wayleave.

Feroz.t: The Freeborn statement against idolatry appeared to attack the Asavean Temple in Oran. An earlier mandate of tolerance means the Synod cannot interfere with the temple without major changes in relations with Asavea.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: home of Jereboam of Sanctuary, who proposed Synod oversight of Imperial diplomacy.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: associated with the Urizen architect Vitruvia of Tabulos, who proposed a Virtuous Wayleave for the Synod.

Segura.t: The Iron Qanat to be built in Segura by the Asavean Almodin Oktístis was denounced by the Freeborn Assembly. Unless the Senate commissions it afresh without him, he remains free to adorn it with whatever imagery he wishes, provided it meets the specifications.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Legion's Rookery in Skarsind is where Tarrat, author of the chaplain proposal, teaches.

That's where my heart is.d: Vesna marched with Ossium's Iron Sparrows alongside the Quiet Step, keeping a promise to fight the Druj in person. Speaking as Custodian of Virtue, Vesna described the Synod debate between a vigilant faction and a pragmatic faction over false virtue. Vesna backed the Synod's decision to rebuild religious law on uplifting true virtue and protecting communities, and called direct engagement with false virtue auras unacceptable. Vesna then commended Kindra Surefoot, Ambassador to Otkodov, for securing a peace treaty with the Thule. Lord Rhydian de Rondell was praised for victory in Hayaak's hunt. Highguard, Urizen and Varushka were praised for each self-funding an army in a single season, with named contributors.

Druj.t: The Druj were the foe Vesna marched against in person, alongside the Iron Sparrows and the Quiet Step, vowing that the Druj would bleed more than the Empire.

Highguard.t: Highguard was commended for self-funding an army in a single season, with the Highguard Benefactors Council and the Chapter of Reumah's Redoubt singled out for their ambition and perseverance.

Thule.t: Vesna praised the recent peace treaty with the Thule, crediting Ambassador Kindra Surefoot's diplomacy in securing it.

Urizen.t: Urizen was commended for self-funding an army in a single season, with contributors including Zenith Ascendent members, the House of the Wanderer and the Stillwater Citadel named.

Varushka.t: Varushka was commended for self-funding an army in a single season, with many Varushkan contributors named. Kindra Surefoot was also praised for consideration for the people of Varushka during the Thule peace treaty.

That's where my heart is.o: Emperor Vesna delivered an Imperial address in Summer 387YE, written on the road to war against the Druj. In it Vesna endorsed the Synod's stance against false virtue, urged all citizens to reject false virtues, and began a practice of commending exceptional citizens.

Otkodov.t: Kindra Surefoot, Ambassador to Otkodov, was commended for securing the recent peace treaty with the Thule, who held Otkodov.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the Chapter of Reumah's Redoubt was named among those who helped self-fund a Highguard army.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: members of Zenith Ascendent were named among those who helped self-fund an Urizen army.

The Ambition of Thrace.d: At the Winter Solstice the Assembly of Ambition passed, 352-0, a writ of consecration raised by League bishop Serrusto Caeli Rezia di Tassato on behalf of Bloodcrow Rasp's band, seeking a memorial to Thrace in Skarsind or Varushka. The civil service weighed sites in Varushka and Casinea but concluded a site marking a nation's founding must lie within that nation, settling on the Legion's Rookery. Highborn offered the stone for icons. Because orcs cannot use liao, an orc raising the mandate could choose a human to perform the consecration. If enacted, the Imperial Orcs would gain a year of inspired construction. The mandate must pass this summit or the process restarts.

Highguard.t: Highborn who saw parallels between Thrace and their founder Atuman have offered to supply all the stone needed for icons at the Rookery, as their ancestors once did for the League's basilica of Aldones di Sarvos.

Imperial Orcs.t: If the Rookery is consecrated, for a year labour costs for civilian commissions and fortifications in Imperial Orc territories would be met by willing labourers, Legion Engineer commissions there would need a fifth fewer wains, and their National Assembly could inspire a unique construction opportunity. As orcs cannot use liao, an orc raising the mandate could choose a human ally to carry the true liao.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Rookery is noted as having survived an occupation by the Thule.

Varushka.t: Varushka, where Thrace's journey began, was named in the writ as a possible site, but the civil service rejected the Varushkan locations they considered because the memorial must stand within the Imperial Orcs' own nation.

The Ambition of Thrace.o: Following a Synod writ of consecration honouring Thrace, Exemplar of Ambition, the civil service identified the Legion's Rookery in Gildenheim, Skarsind, as the ideal site for an inspirational location to his memory. Consecrating it requires a General Assembly mandate and a dose of true liao at the Spring Equinox.

Casinea.t: The civil service considered the place in Casinea where the former slaves camped before entering the Senate with Emperor Ahraz, but judged it unsuitable as it lies outside the Imperial Orcs' borders.

Skarsind.t: The Legion's Rookery in Gildenheim has been chosen as the site to consecrate to Thrace's Ambition, needing little new construction; if the mandate passes at the Spring Equinox, orcs would also be inspired over coming years to finish making Skarsind their homeland.

The Courageous Priest.d: Golan preached across Reikos that the First Empress was an exemplar of Courage and that the Empire must embrace Courage alone. Nina's Synod-backed campaign was wise but lacked resources, and the Synod had not refuted the claim about the Empress's Courage. Yael's presence drew as many pilgrims to Courage as Golan did. Every Courage congregation in Highguard gained liao and votes, and all others lost them. Golan has been called to inquisition at the Spring Equinox. A General Assembly judgement refuting the Empress's Courage, backed by liao, could halt or reverse the movement. Supporting judgements could spread it to further territories in several nations.

Dawn.t: Astolat could be affected if the Synod backs Golan's claims, and Semmerholm and Weirwater could follow in a wider second spread of the Courage of the First Empress.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: in the accompanying fiction, the Druj are described as scattered and defeated as the liberation of Reikos nears completion.

Highguard.t: The Courage of the First Empress has spread to every corner of Highguard. Courage congregations there are swelling with liao and votes while congregations of every other virtue are losing both, and families are being divided over the movement.

Navarr.t: Miaren and Therunin are among the first territories the movement could spread to if the Synod endorses Golan's teaching or recognises the First Empress as an exemplar of Courage.

The Brass Coast.t: Madruga and Feroz could be affected in a second, wider spread of the Courage of the First Empress if the Synod chooses to promote it further.

The League.t: Sarvos and Tassato are first in line to be affected if the movement spreads beyond Highguard, and Temeschwar could follow later. A Leaguer, Vitória Barossa di Tassato Regario, raised the judgement putting Golan's inquisition in the hands of the Courage Assembly.

The Marches.t: Upwold could be reached by the Courage of the First Empress in a second spread, if the Synod recognises the First Empress as an exemplar of Courage and then commits further liao.

Urizen.t: Morrow and Redoubt are among the first territories the movement could spread to if the Synod gives its backing to Golan's claims.

Varushka.t: Karov could be affected in a second, wider spread of the Courage of the First Empress if the Synod chooses to extend it.

The Courageous Priest.o: In spring 380YE the Courage of the First Empress, a movement inspired by the preaching of Golan the Wanderer and of Yael of Felix's Watch, who claims to be the First Empress reborn, took root across Highguard. Citizens abandoned other virtues for congregations of Courage, and the Synod's own preacher, Nina of Cantiarch's Hold, could not stem the tide.

Astolat.t: Astolat is named as one of the first territories the movement could reach, if the Synod supports Golan's claims with 75 liao or recognises the First Empress as an exemplar of Courage.

Feroz.t: Feroz could see the movement's effects in a second spread, after a recognition of the First Empress's Courage and a further 75 liao from the Courage Assembly.

Karov.t: Karov is listed among the territories the movement could reach in a second spread, if the Synod chooses to extend it further.

Madruga.t: Madruga could be affected in the second wave of the movement's possible spread, should the Synod recognise the Empress's Courage and commit more liao.

Miaren.t: Miaren is among the first territories that would feel Golan's teaching if the Synod endorses his claims or recognises the First Empress as an exemplar of Courage.

Morrow.t: Morrow could see congregations of Courage swell at others' expense if the Synod's backing spreads Golan's teaching into the first wave of territories.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt is named among the first territories to which the Courage of the First Empress could spread with Synod support.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Reikos, the territory where Golan, Nina and Yael preached, is not among the territories listed for this entry.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos is among the first territories the movement could reach if the Synod gives its support to Golan's claims or recognises the Empress's Courage.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm could be reached in a second spread of the movement, after a recognition of the First Empress's Courage and a further 75 liao.

Tassato.t: Tassato is named among the first territories the Courage of the First Empress could spread to if the Synod backs it.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar is listed among the territories the movement could reach in a second, wider spread.

Therunin.t: Therunin could see Golan's teaching take hold in the first wave of spread, should the Synod back his claims.

Upwold.t: Upwold could be affected in the second wave of the movement's possible spread if the Synod chooses to extend it.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater is among the territories the Courage of the First Empress could reach in a second spread with further Synod support.

The DOOM that came to Sarvos.d: The curse left no lingering magic, but a deep malaise and fear of doom took hold. Three follies were proposed, each able to underpin a League Assembly mandate giving Sarvos a new epithet: Bethany Gustava von Sarvos's renovation of the Glass Palace (City of Songs), Genia Bourné's Night Masks fashion school (City of Masks), and Martina di Sarvos's Greatest Taste banqueting hall (City of Spices). If none is completed before Autumn 384YE, Sarvos may become the Doomed or Sinking City. Fire-safety commissions were also proposed. Husks from the Iron Helms were going missing and a winter regio appeared in the Caricomare sewers. Eduardo von Tassato sought a meeting of reckoners.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: wild rumours in the League cities speak of curses being levied against Highguard's territories in retaliation, and the city's founding is dated to before the wars between the patricians and the chapters of Highguard.

The League.t: The League faces a choice over Sarvos's identity, with the Senate able to commission one or more follies and the League Assembly then able to mandate a new epithet for the city. Its reckoners are also being summoned by Eduardo von Tassato, likely to discuss a reckoning for the curses on Sarvos and Holberg.

The DOOM that came to Sarvos.o: After the Hag Queen's agents shattered every mirror in Sarvos at the Summer Solstice 383YE, the Jewelled City lost its famous identity. The League was offered a chance to choose a new future for the city through Senate commissions, or else risk Sarvos becoming 'doomed'.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the attack on Holberg is referenced alongside Sarvos as one of the two curses fuelling calls for a reckoning, and architect Bethany Gustava von Sarvos studied there.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos lost every mirror, including its famed rooftop mirrors, and must complete a commission defining its new character before Autumn 384YE or risk lasting doom. Meanwhile corpses and a winter regio haunt the Caricomare sewers, with the Iron Helms and Wolves of War stationed nearby.

The Deer in the Sun.d: The Pride Assembly urged nations to answer Cold Sun's hatred of creativity with lasting cultural monuments. Gralka's Imperial Orc judgement proposed a Library of Worth of words and symbols in Skarsind, possibly expanded into a Great Library. Anatolij Paukov Zorkin's unanimous Varushkan judgement proposed a Hall of Fabric Arts in Karov, perhaps at Vorota, with a grander option that could spark a renaissance in weaving and needlework. Mandates pledged Imperial Orc support of 4 white granite and 8 crowns and Varushkan support of 20 white granite and 40 crowns each season, but only once the Senate commissions the buildings. The Navarr mandate against the Empty Hands in Miaren gave supporting military units two random herbs.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed hall site at Vorota sits on a road leading south-east to Weirwater, bringing merchants with fine cloth.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named directly; it figures only within the general account of Cold Sun's attacks on cultural sites across the Empire.

Imperial Orcs.t: Gralka's judgement passed 185-23 and Emperor Vesna's mandate committed the nation to 4 white granite and 8 crowns a season for a year towards a Library of Worth. This support only begins once the Senate commissions it, and it bars any other such mandate on the nation in the meantime.

Navarr.t: The Navarr Assembly declared the fight against Cold Sun one with the fight against the vallorn, and its mandate gave two random herbs to every military unit supporting an army against the Empty Hands. Navarr armies faced a morale penalty if no Imperial army attacked Cold Sun in Miaren.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: a road from the proposed hall site at Vorota leads south-west to Temeschwar, carrying merchants selling wool, linen and silk.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named directly; it figures only within the general account of Cold Sun's attacks on cultural sites across the Empire.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan Assembly unanimously called for a Hall of Fabric Arts celebrating weaving and needlework, and its mandate readied 20 white granite and 40 crowns a season once the Senate commissions the hall. A greater hall could double as a school and revive these arts as a celebrated part of Varushkan culture.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tamazi suggested housing the Library inside The Will of Wintermark, perhaps renaming it, though some worried this might offend the Wintermark.

The Deer in the Sun.o: Following Cold Sun's destruction of cultural sites, the Imperial Orc and Varushkan Assemblies called for new monuments to national Pride (a Library of Worth in Skarsind and a Hall of Fabric Arts in Karov), while the Navarr Assembly urged its people to fight the scions. Mandates supporting all three passed, but neither building had yet been commissioned by the Senate.

Karov/Wieliczka.t: Mentioned in passing: Wieliczka is not named; the page refers only to Karov generally and the settlement of Vorota as the hall's suggested site.

Miaren/Goldglades.t: Mentioned in passing: Goldglades is not named; the page refers to the Empty Hands in Miaren generally.

Karov.t: Karov was the proposed site of the Hall of Fabric Arts, with the civil service suggesting the fortified settlement of Vorota. The hall had not yet been commissioned by the Senate.

Miaren.t: The Cold Sun army Empty Hands remained in Miaren. Units supporting armies fighting it gained two random herbs from the Navarr mandate, and Navarr armies faced a penalty if no Imperial army attacked Cold Sun there.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named; it is linked only through the general account of Cold Sun's attacks on cultural sites.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is not named; it is linked only through the general account of Cold Sun's attacks on cultural sites.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind was the proposed home of the Library of Worth, possibly expanded into a Great Library to give the Sunstorm a monument to their Pride. The location within the territory had not been settled and the Senate had not yet commissioned it.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar lies at the end of a road from Vorota that brings cloth merchants to the proposed hall site.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater lies at the end of a road from Vorota that brings cloth merchants to the proposed hall site.

The Glorious Advance.d: With Segura fully back under Imperial control, celebrations ran strongest in the Brass Coast and Dawn, whose soldiers died to restore it. Prognosticators advised that a Statement of Principle from the Assembly of Pride validating a single nation would channel this mood. Celebrating Dawn, alongside a Senate motion at the Winter Solstice 378YE to found a Dawnish army, would save 50 mithril. Celebrating the Brass Coast, alongside a motion for a Freeborn navy, would save 50 weirwood. Celebrating both nations would dilute the effect and lose the benefit. The General Assembly could supersede the Assembly of Pride's judgement only after Pride had ruled. Pride celebrated the Brass Coast, aiding the mustering of the Freeborn Storm.

Dawn.t: The Eastern Sky and Hounds of Glory, two Dawnish armies, fought in the liberation, and a Pride statement celebrating Dawn could have saved 50 mithril on a new Dawnish army. The Assembly of Pride chose the Brass Coast instead, so Dawn did not receive the benefit.

The Brass Coast.t: The Red Wind Corsairs helped drive the Lasambrians off the Iron Plains, and the Assembly of Pride celebrated Freeborn efforts in reclaiming Segura. The resulting zeal helped muster the Freeborn Storm navy.

The Glorious Advance.o: After the Red Wind Corsairs, Eastern Sky and Hounds of Glory drove the Lasambrians out of Segura, patriotic fervour in Dawn and the Brass Coast created a short-lived chance to raise a new army or navy more cheaply. The Assembly of Pride chose to celebrate the Brass Coast, and the resulting enthusiasm helped muster the Freeborn Storm navy.

Segura/Iron Plains.t: The Red Wind Corsairs were credited with driving the Lasambrians off the Iron Plains while the Dawnish armies engaged Summer realm soldiers.

Segura.t: Segura was returned fully to Imperial control after the Lasambrians were pushed to the negotiating table and then off Imperial land.

The Net of the Realms.d: Megaris of Glowspire offered Meraud's friendship, gifts and yearly regalia to a Churnspire Adjutor if a spire taller than Pakaanan's Tower were built in Peregro and ceded to him. Valeria proposed expanding Highwatch Citadel for Zakalwe's heralds, who would supply resources for use only against the Druj. This was commissioned in Summer 384YE, creating the Polemarch of Highwatch. Balbus relayed Prospero's offer of a Market of Iron and Ash in Willstone selling Autumn vis. Sung offered an upkeep-free, hidden spy network at Oblivion's Edge in exchange for the Night Arbour. Sadogua offered to craft magical items for covens. The Tomb King refused aid, and the Whisperer offered famine. Declarations concerning Agramant were withdrawn.

Druj.t: Zakalwe's heralds offered Urizen Pearls of Manush and primessence, to be used solely in the war on the Druj. The page also notes that the Druj invasion of Morrow drove the Glowspire into introspection.
