Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the page recalls that Spiral fell to the Grendel in 331YE, leaving the spire of Oblivion's Edge ruined.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: they are not named, but Meraud's spire had to be declared taller than Pakaanan's Tower, which vanished from Pakaanan's Pass.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe's heralds would abandon Highwatch if a Pearl of Manush were used to enchant an army facing the Jotun.

Urizen.t: Urizen's mandate drew offers from several eternals of titles, vis, regalia, a market, a hidden spy network and coven items, alongside a warning from the Tomb King that the nation had lost half its territory. Highwatch Citadel was later expanded for Zakalwe.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tomb King contrasted Varushka, almost twice the size it was a decade ago, with Urizen's losses.

The Net of the Realms.o: After the Urizen National Assembly upheld Maximillian's mandate urging cooperation with eternals, several Urizeni came forward with offers from Meraud, Zakalwe, Prospero, Sung, Sadogua and the Whisperer to aid the nation. The Whisperer's offer to bring the Dream of Famine on an enemy territory was put before the Conclave but withdrawn without a vote.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Megaris of Glowspire proposed a white granite and mithril spire overlooking the Churn in Peregro for Meraud, with luxurious apartments for the Churnspire Adjutor.

Redoubt/Willstone.t: Balbus of the Spire of Willstone judged that Willstone could host Prospero's Market of Iron and Ash, with a chamber for trade with the Cities of Iron and Ash.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: Mentioned in passing: Pakaanan's Tower vanished from Pakaanan's Pass, and nobody can remember its exact height.

Spiral/Screed.t: Oblivion's Edge in Screed would house Sung's heliopticon spy network, and the Night Arbour below it would be consumed to shroud the spire from enemies if the Conclave agreed.

Morrow.t: A folly overlooking the Churn geyser was proposed for Morrow and would be ceded to Meraud, who would support a Churnspire Adjutor. The local Glowspire is recovering from the Druj invasion.

Redoubt.t: Prospero proposed a Market of Iron and Ash in Redoubt, allowing direct trade in Autumn vis overseen by an Agent of Ash and Iron.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Pakaanan's Tower, which disappeared from Skarsind's Pakaanan's Pass, was the benchmark Meraud's spire had to exceed in height.

Spiral.t: Sung offered a concealed, upkeep-free spy network based at Oblivion's Edge to watch the Black Plateau and all of Spiral, provided it was ceded to her and given the Night Arbour.

The Oran operation.d: The engineers judged that bridging the ilium-laden Scorrero, with a magical marsh on its northern bank, was infeasible. They proposed a caisson road bridge from near Oran to the coast east of ruined Siroc, costing 50 white granite, 15 mithril, 15 weirwood and 96 crowns over six months. It would let armies cross, lift Oranseri's impoverishment and restore the Sunset Roads to Segura. With Senate permission, salvaging the drowned Salt Guard or the abandoned Temple of Balo and the Black Bull would reduce the materials needed. An optional Oran Tollkeeper title and adamant reinforcement via the Stone Dragon were also offered. Both the Assembly of the Way and the Freeborn Assembly upheld exorcism mandates to protect the Salt Guard salvage.

Grendel.t: Former Grendel soldiers now serving the Protectorate offered Grendel caisson techniques for the bridge. Their engineer spoke bitterly of Salt Lords who starve professional soldiers in favour of the navies, which has made these troops adept at salvage.

The Brass Coast.t: The bridge would make the Freeborn nation whole again by reconnecting Feroz with Madruga and restoring Segura's trade. The Freeborn and Way assemblies both upheld mandates sending exorcists to honour the dead of the Salt Guard, while the Kanza family objected to tearing down the temple that once sheltered them.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Protectorate engineer Grayune recalled being pinned down by Urizen sentinels, in which soldiers could not simply sail away.

The Oran operation.o: In Summer 388YE, Protectorate of Morajasse engineers, guided by Lutomysla Niegoslava, assessed how to reconnect Feroz and Madruga across the flood-ravaged Scorrero. They proposed an Oran Bridge across the Bay of Oran as a commission opportunity, along with optional salvage and toll arrangements.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Mentioned in passing: Fontargenta is not named on the page and is linked only as part of Feroz, the territory at the centre of the bridge plan.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: The Protectorate of Morajasse supplied the engineers behind the proposal. The optional Oran Tollkeeper's income would rise by 6 crowns a season if Morajasse's impoverished quality were removed.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The bridge would make landfall near Oran, removing Oranseri's impoverished quality and reviving its paradors. The abandoned Asavean temple in Oran could be torn down for materials, and the Inkworks of Joharra could additionally remove the region's abandoned quality.

Madruga/Crucible.t: Crucible is trackless, marshy and outside Imperial control, so the engineers ruled out bridging there. The Red Wind Corsairs aim to retake it after their raid on the Bayou.

Madruga/Quiet Grasses.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the haunted-grass and marsh regions created when the Spring-infused Scorrero transfigured Madruga.

Madruga/Siroc Bayou.t: The bridge's northern end would sit on the coast east of ruined Siroc as the Red Wind Corsairs raided to bring the Bayou under Imperial control. The drowned Salt Guard here could be salvaged for granite, with exorcist mandates upheld to keep the dead at rest.

Feroz.t: Oranseri would anchor the proposed bridge, and Feroz's cheap labour keeps the cost low, though some questioned the fairness of this and an option to pay full wages was offered. The bridge was framed as a symbol of Feroz's recovery from Governor Rahab's ruin.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: ilium washing down from the Kahraman peaks has made the Scorrero's magical wildness linger.

Madruga.t: The bridge would restore army movement and overland trade between Madruga and Feroz. However, Madruga's transfigured northern bank of marsh and haunted grass makes building there very difficult.

Segura.t: By linking to the old white granite road into Segura, the Oran Bridge would restore the Sunset Roads benefits that Segura lost when the Scorrero flooded.

The Pride of Gerallt Brackensong.d: At the Winter Solstice 385YE Halwyn Splitroot's writ of consecration passed the Pride assembly 571-24, prompted partly by the Empty Hands of Cold Sun razing First Voice Glade, Gerallt's memorial in Miaren. The civil service identified three sites: First Voice Glade in Miaren, Foxden Steading in Hercynia and Return in Therunin. Each would host a school of music and performing arts with a garden grown from surviving cuttings. Building it would cost 30 wains of weirwood and 90 crowns over three months, and it would need true liao to consecrate. Once consecrated, it would give every herb garden in that territory three extra herbs each season. The mandate had to be enacted at the Spring Equinox or the process would begin again.

Navarr.t: The proposed school would honour one of their own exemplars and would especially inspire Navarr pilgrims. Depending on the site, it would celebrate Navarr songs and stories, encourage guides and missionaries of the Way, or remind them of the sacrifice needed to defeat the vallorn.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr striding in the in-character story is travelling towards Sermersuaq.

The Pride of Gerallt Brackensong.o: Following a Pride assembly writ of consecration for the Navarr exemplar Gerallt Brackensong, the civil service presented three possible sites for a consecrated memorial school and garden, leaving the General Assembly to choose one by mandate at the Spring Equinox.

Hercynia/Summersend.t: Foxden Steading in Summersend, where Gerallt studied the Way and became a guide, was proposed as a centre where guides and stridings could gather for spiritual counsel.

Miaren/Oakways.t: First Voice Glade in Oakways, the performing-arts school and garden destroyed by the Empty Hands after the Autumn Equinox 385YE, could be rebuilt as the consecrated memorial.

Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley.t: Return in the Upper Tarn Valley, the abandoned site of Gerallt's sacrifice, could be reclaimed as a school preserving Navarr songs and stories about fighting the vallorn and about sacrifice.

Hercynia.t: Foxden Steading was one of three proposed sites. A school there would teach Navarr understanding of the Way and the Great Dance, and its herb gardens would gain extra herbs each season.

Miaren.t: The razed First Voice Glade could be rebuilt on a larger scale as a consecrated school and garden, offering a defiant answer to Cold Sun's destruction and extra herbs for Miaren's herb gardens.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: it is the destination of the striding in the in-character story.

Therunin.t: The abandoned steading of Return, where Gerallt died thwarting Yaw'nagrah, could be reclaimed as a memorial school, and Therunin's herb gardens would gain extra herbs each season.

The Prosperity of Good Walder.d: At the Winter Solstice 385YE the Prosperity assembly unanimously urged that Good Walder's Orchard be consecrated with true liao. The civil service also offered two alternatives: Corwin's Thump, which stresses punishing the wicked, and the Abbey of Harry's Pot, which stresses rewarding the virtuous. Either alternative would need a pilgrims' lodge built as a folly, costing 20 white granite and 60 crowns over three months. The Orchard already has a suitable structure. Any consecration would raise the Prosperity assembly's influence. Benefactors it named would gain to their personal resources, and those it castigated or condemned would suffer penalties. The mandate had to be enacted at the summit where it was presented.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: a tree-filled site in Dawn was among the many claimed resting places of Good Walder, and Marcher tales of him trace back to soon after the Marchers left Dawn.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: a Highguard chantry claiming to hold Good Walder's thighbone was among the many sites the civil service considered and set aside.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: a well in Miaren was listed among the many places with a claimed tie to Good Walder.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: dry stone walls in Tassato, said to have been built by Good Walder himself, were among the claimed sites not chosen.

The Marches.t: All three proposed sites for Good Walder's inspirational location lie in the Marches, the nation most closely tied to the paragon. Marcher orders such as the Order of the Sack and the Fellows of the Stout Stick would spread the assembly's rewards and sanctions.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Karov was named among the places where a site could claim to be Good Walder's resting place.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark was named among the places where a site could claim to be Good Walder's resting place.

The Prosperity of Good Walder.o: In response to a Prosperity assembly writ of consecration, the civil service proposed three sites in the Marches for an inspirational location dedicated to the paragon Good Walder. These were Good Walder's Orchard and the Abbey of Harry's Pot in Mitwold, and Corwin's Thump in Upwold. The General Assembly was invited to choose one at the Spring Equinox.

Mitwold/Golden Downs.t: The Abbey of Harry's Pot in the Golden Downs, home of a miraculous soup pot, was proposed as the site of a pilgrims' lodge. Any additional effects there would centre on rewarding the virtuous and sharing fairly.

Upwold/Ashbrook.t: Corwin's Thump, a low hill in Ashbrook between Ashill and Stockland with a small shrine kept by the Fellows of the Stout Stick, was proposed as the site of a pilgrims' lodge focused on exposing misers and wastrels.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: a site in Astolat was cited as one that could claim to be Good Walder's resting place.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: a site in Hahnmark was cited as one that could claim to be Good Walder's resting place.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: a site in Karov was cited as one that could claim to be Good Walder's resting place.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: a well in Miaren was among the claimed Good Walder sites.

Mitwold.t: Two of the three proposed sites lie in Mitwold. One is Good Walder's Orchard south of Hay, which is disputed as his resting place but needs no new building. The other is the Abbey of Harry's Pot, which would need a pilgrims' lodge built.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: a site in Necropolis, including a chantry claiming Good Walder's thighbone, was among the claimed resting places.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: dry stone walls in Tassato said to have been built by Good Walder were among the claimed sites.

Upwold.t: Corwin's Thump in Upwold was proposed as a site for a consecrated pilgrims' lodge. Its legend has Good Walder cudgelling a miserly steward into a flock of crows, and the site would focus his inspiration on punishing the unvirtuous.

The Queen's door.d: Eleonaris cannot refuse a Knights of Glory summons, but she had threatened to aid the Empire's enemies if it was cast again, so the Empire stopped using it. Words of thanks would no longer suffice; a Senate commission was needed. The safe option was a folly ceded to her, ideally at Semmer's Rose, costing 30 wains of white granite and 60 crowns. Alternatively, a fane (10 wains of mithril, 10 rings of ilium, 20 crowns), based on a design by the executed sorcerer Arvandor the White, could be built at the Giltmere or Oremont, winning her approval. A fane at the Semmerstones would make her withdraw support from the Jotun but enrage Meraud, Cathan Canae and Jaheris.

Dawn.t: Three of the four proposed sites lay in Dawnish lands: a folly at Semmer's Rose or a fane at the Semmerstones in Semmerholm, or a fane at the Giltmere near Weaving in Astolat. The fane design itself came from the Dawnish enchanter Arvandor the White.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Llofir's garden in Highguard's Reikos was cited as an example of an eternal building on a site ceded to it.

Jotun.t: The Jotun were revealed to have ceded fanes to most Summer eternals, which is how they secured Eleonaris' aid against the Empire; ceding her the Semmerstones would persuade her to withdraw that support.

Wintermark.t: Oremont, a mountain in Wintermark's Northspires, was identified as a possible site for a fane ceded to Eleonaris, an alternative to giving up Dawnish land.

The Queen's door.o: Eleonaris, the Lion of Summer, remained enraged at the Empire's repeated use of Knights of Glory without public thanks, and the civil service identified four commissions that could placate her: a folly at Semmer's Rose, or a fane at the Giltmere, Oremont or the Semmerstones.

Hahnmark/Northspires.t: Oremont, an orichalcum-rich peak in Northspires with ancient ruins and rumoured gryphons, was proposed as a fane site whose warding would let Eleonaris' heralds come and go throughout the region.

Astolat.t: The Giltmere, a regio near Weaving claimed by Eleonaris and home to a legendary burning ram, was proposed as a site for a fane, which would mean ceding it and the surrounding hills to her.

Hahnmark.t: Oremont in Hahnmark was proposed as a site for a fane to Eleonaris, ceding the mountain regio to her and allowing her heralds to move freely through the region.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Llofir's garden in Reikos was given as a precedent for an eternal building on a ceded site.

Semmerholm.t: Semmer's Rose was the civil service's preferred site for the safe folly option, while ceding a fane at the Semmerstones would hand Eleonaris one of the Empire's greatest Summer regios and enrage Meraud, Cathan Canae and Jaheris.

The Synod speaks.d: Gaelen Embercast's Assembly of Nine statement (7-1) declared the vallorn the greatest spiritual threat and urged every nation to join the war. Statements from Kaspar Yakovitch von Holberg (League, 288-48) and Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti (Varushka, 222-10) recalled debts owed to the Navarr. Each nation could enact one of three competing mandates that would shape later opportunities to aid the Navarr, but would also stop other national calls to action having effect for a year. Dawn, Highguard and Urizen passed conflicting statements, none by greater majority. Other nations had only this season to respond. The Varushkan Wisdom mandate and the League Ambition mandate were enacted, and Highguard sent Hazelelponi to call the grey pilgrims home.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Assembly passed both supportive and cautionary statements, none with a greater majority. The nation could still take a clear stand this season.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; the page touches them only through links to vallorn-related places such as Sarangrave.

Highguard.t: Highguard was praised for standing with the Navarr but passed mixed statements. It later enacted a mandate sending Hazelelponi to call the grey pilgrims home to prepare for war with the vallorn.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; only earlier Liathaven vallorn events appear in the further reading.

Navarr.t: The Navarr gained the backing of the Assembly of Nine, the League and Varushka for their war against the vallorn, with two-thirds of stridings already leaving the trods to prepare.

The League.t: The League Assembly could commit its citizens to aiding the Navarr through its wealth, senators and engineering skills. It enacted the Ambition mandate, sending Ortenzia di Sarvos to urge new ways to fight the vallorn, which barred other national calls to action for a year.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Assembly passed conflicting statements both supporting the Navarr and urging delay, none with a greater majority. The nation could still take a clear stand this season.

Varushka.t: Varushka, with three armies, mithril and artisan resources, could commit to aiding its Navarr cousins. It enacted the Wisdom mandate, empowering Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti, and its people will not answer other national calls to action for a year.

The Synod speaks.o: After the Navarr Assembly chose to begin the final war against the vallorn, the Assembly of Nine and the League and Varushkan Assemblies backed them with greater majorities. The League and Varushka were each offered competing mandates to commit their people to the fight.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: Mentioned in passing: Bendol appears only in a link to the earlier report of the expedition Into Béantal Dol.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Brocéliande appears only in further reading links to earlier vallorn adventures and rituals.

Hercynia.t: The page raised the possibility that Varushkan artisan resources could help the Navarr raise their new army in Hercynia.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: the Varushkan statement recalled that the Navarr stood with Varushka when Karsk was attacked.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven appears only in further reading links to earlier fighting against its vallorn.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is not named on the page and is connected only as Navarr land.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarangrave appears only in a further reading link to an expedition to Bendol.

The Visitation.d: A shipment for the Golden Fleet Salvagemaster caused a commotion when unloaded at Crown's Quay in Necropolis. Irate stewards of the dead from Oreb's Vault harassed and delayed it, so a courier arranged to meet the Salvagemaster on Saturday morning to resolve the dispute. The Magistrates confirmed the goods were his. A letter to an unknown "Marisol i Erigo" from the Sovereign Lords of the City of Bar and Bond was found at the regio and published. Landskeeper Shem announced a rock, paper, scissors tournament in the Hall of Worlds, with proceeds split between the winner, the Academy and Upwold. Wayblade Skana planned to visit the Imperial Orc camp to learn about the executed heretic Bloodcrow Knott, who was later added to the Annals of the Ancestors.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; its only link is that Wayblade Skana comes from Mareave, which Grendel held at the time.

Highguard.t: Stewards of the dead from the chapter house at Oreb's Vault in Necropolis were angered by the Salvagemaster's shipment and harassed and delayed it. The Salvagemaster was asked to placate them, although the Magistrates confirmed the goods were his.

The Marches.t: Landskeeper Shem toured Upwold gathering ribbon for his Anvil tournament. A quarter of the takings would go back with him to help with the problems of being a landskeeper in trying times.

The Visitation.o: In Summer 388YE several visitors and matters publicly bound for Anvil were announced. They included a disputed salvage delivery delayed by stewards from Oreb's Vault, a mysterious letter from the City of Bar and Bond, a rock, paper, scissors tournament run by Landskeeper Shem of Upwold, and a visit by Wayblade Skana of Mareave.

Mareave.t: Wayblade Skana, a preacher from Mareave, was set to travel to the Imperial Orc camp at Anvil to learn about the life and death of Bloodcrow Knott.

Necropolis.t: The Salvagemaster's shipment caused a commotion when it was unloaded at Crown's Quay, and stewards from Oreb's Vault hounded the cart carrying it all the way to Anvil.

Upwold.t: Landskeeper Shem spent the month travelling across Upwold preparing his tournament. A quarter of its proceeds was earmarked to help with the troubles landskeepers faced there.

The Witches of Applefell.d: Two large bandit groups, many of them witches using spells to scatter guards and empower warriors, attacked a weirwood shipment heading south from the Weirwater Vales. They took five wains of weirwood, wagons and oxen, and left guards seriously injured. Evidence points to Applefell, but its yeofolk will not cooperate, and the witches' purpose for the weirwood is unknown. The new holder of the Weirwater Vales, auctioned at the Winter Solstice, will receive only 18 wains and may lose future production. An anonymous informant offered to sell information to the new holder at the auction. A general in Weirwater could issue the Leave no stone unturned order to end the bandit threat for at least a year, at the risk of fighting poorly if attacked.

Dawn.t: The theft of weirwood from a Dawnish territory, and the uncooperative and possibly subverted yeofolk of Applefell, left Dawn facing a witch-backed brigand problem that a Dawnish general could tackle with the Leave no stone unturned order.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: troubadours suggest Applefell's yeofolk have Varushkan blood, and Weirwater's wilds are compared with the more dangerous Varushkan wilderness.

The Witches of Applefell.o: Witch-supported bandits, apparently operating from around the Dawnish hill town of Applefell in Weirwater, stole five wains of weirwood from a caravan of the Weirwater Vales Bourse seat. The magistrates have met a wall of silence from the townsfolk.

Weirwater/Hawksmoor.t: Mentioned in passing: Hawksmoor is not named on the page and is attached only as part of Weirwater, where the bandits and witches operate.

Weirwater/Sandling.t: Bandits have been reported attacking along the edges of Sandling as their raids grow bolder.

Weirwater/Weirmoor.t: Mentioned in passing: Applefell's yeofolk are more worried about the army of unliving horrors in Weirmoor than about the bandits, and the unliving forces in western Weirwater are a risk to any army hunting brigands.

Weirwater/Wickmoor.t: Bandits have been reported attacking along the edges of Wickmoor as their raids grow bolder.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: merchants passing through Applefell travel to and from Karov.

Semmerholm.t: The emboldened bandits have been reported making occasional attacks across the border into Semmerholm, a destination for merchants passing through Applefell.

Weirwater.t: Witch-supported bandits based around Applefell robbed the Weirwater Vales of five wains of weirwood. An army in the territory could be ordered to sweep its hills and forests to end the threat for at least a year, at the cost of fighting badly if attacked.

The arch of the door.d: Chancellor Lady Jaycinda Griffonsbane regretted the move, though relocating nearer the heart of the Empire had been discussed before the invasion. With the barbarians only weeks from the spire, the safety of the students forced the decision. The Academy no longer seeks liao donations, so the Dean of Pilgrims, created by Zephram of Cantiarch's Hold, saw donations dwindle. The civil service proposed two Senate options at no cost and without a commission. One was a Canterspire College of the Way as an Urizen national title with 8 liao and 16 Synod votes. The other was the Canterspire Trust, a ministry aiding sanctuary seekers, with Delilah of Felix's Watch suggested. Doing nothing left the title at 6 liao. Neither option was taken before the Winter Solstice.

Dawn.t: Dawn became the Academy's new home, with buildings near the Castle of Thorns secured and most of the staff already moving there.

Druj.t: The Druj invasion of Morrow, with the barbarians within a few weeks' march of Canterspire, forced the Academy to abandon the spire.

Urizen.t: Urizen lost the Academy from Canterspire and was offered a College of the Way there, which would have become a national title chosen by the Urizen national assembly. The opportunity lapsed unused.

The arch of the door.o: With the Druj advancing through Morrow, the Academy abandoned its offices at Canterspire and began moving to new buildings near the Castle of Thorns in Dawn. The move left the Dean of Pilgrims title without purpose, and the civil service offered the Senate two ways to redefine it; the opportunity later lapsed and the title is no longer active.

Astolat.t: The Academy's new buildings near the Castle of Thorns became the destination for its relocated staff and charges.

Morrow.t: Canterspire in Morrow was vacated by the Academy as the Druj closed in, leaving its shrine and buildings open for possible reuse while their survival hung on the spire not falling.

The art of restraining power.d: Sumaah recognised the virtue of Bonewall Rek and Cole and invited them to Timoj; Rek sailed for Zemeh, and the Senate later accepted a Sumaah ceasefire. Asavea completed the Temple of the Way in Nemoria and sent white granite to Sarvos, leaving the liaison's appointment method to Maher i Zaydan i Riqueza. The Black Sails Quay ended high liao prices. Axou priests of the Order of the Ivory Cup lectured widely, provoking hostility. Jarm favoured Vezak while Kavor and Rigia cooled. Faraden welcomed the King's Stoke hub. Sarcophan herb surpluses ended, Commonwealth relations stayed cool, and Otkodov recognised Ambassador Juha the Cavespider as Skogr freed fifty slaves.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: rumour says Faraden advisor Lady Saretta favours a trade enclave in Dawn similar to the one planned for Upwold.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial fleets have no opportunity to trade with the Druj this season.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan merchants make no secret of an orc embassy in the Delves, and rumours claim they sell Imperial goods in Dubhtraig.

Highguard.t: Highborn of Felix's Watch helped the Sumaah inquisition pass smoothly at Anvil. Necropolis's Black Sails Quay normalised liao prices and its Chantry of the Silver Skull hosted Axou lecturers.

Imperial Orcs.t: Sumaah formally recognised the virtue of Bonewall Rek and Bonewall Cole, and Rek set sail for Zemeh on his way to address the assemblies in Timoj. Separately, Axou visitors declined an invitation to the Legion's Rookery in Skarsind.

Navarr.t: Axou priests lectured at Bronwen's Rest Wayhouse in Therunin, where one visiting priest was afterwards struck by a curse of swarming insects.

The Brass Coast.t: Maher i Zaydan i Riqueza must decide how the Nemoria temple liaison is appointed. Antonio i Carno i Guerra's Gloaming Road is in demand as blight ravages Faraden gloaming.

The League.t: Sarvos received the first Asavean white granite. Axou priests lectured in Tassato, where students pelted them, and Faraden merchants praised the Blood Red Roads and mooted mercenary markets in Tassato and Temeschwar.

The Marches.t: The Senate-approved Faraden trade hub at King's Stoke in Upwold was widely welcomed, with the Court of the Five Winds eager for Marcher grain, fruit and alcohol, though work has yet to begin.

Thule.t: Thule recognised Ambassador Juha the Cavespider, and their emissary moved to Coldmere. Skogr the Red freed fifty Imperial slaves under a ransom agreement with Wintermark and plans to send traders to the Varushkan Winter Market.

Varushka.t: The Embassy to Otkodov in Miekarova was completed and the Thule emissary relocated to Coldmere. Axou priests lectured at the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, and Skogr the Red plans to trade at the Winter Market.

Wintermark.t: A ransom agreement with the people of Wintermark secured the release of fifty Imperial slaves held by Skogr the Red. Sarcophan traders also ventured towards Hahnmark to sell healing supplies to the grimnir.

The art of restraining power.o: The Autumn 381YE foreign-relations Wind of Fortune covered the Empire's neighbours. Sumaah recognised the orc priests Bonewall Rek and Cole, Axou priests lectured across the Empire, Faraden hailed a planned trade hub in Upwold, and the Thule warlock Skogr the Red freed fifty Imperial slaves under a ransom agreement.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: The fifty slaves freed by Skogr the Red were given furs, boots and enough food and water to reach Atalaq.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Thule orcs released fifty Imperial slaves in the foothills of the Silver Peaks, some of them captured during earlier Thule aggression in the region.

Upwold/Tower March.t: King's Stoke was chosen by the Senate as the site of a Faraden trade hub, though construction has yet to begin.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan traders are a common sight around the Bay of Catazar.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: a band of Sarcophan traders reportedly made a speculative journey to Hahnmark to sell herbs and healing supplies to the grimnir.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the University of Holberg issued an informal invitation to the visiting Axou scholars.

Miekarova.t: The Embassy to Otkodov was completed here and the Thule emissary Rak relocated, grudgingly, to Coldmere. Axou priests also lectured at the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun.

Necropolis.t: The completed Black Sails Quay gave Axou merchants reliable access to liao, ending inflated prices. The Sumaah embassy buzzed with gossip about the orc doctrines, and Axou priests lectured at the Chantry of the Silver Skull.

Otkodov.t: The orcs of Otkodov grudgingly recognised Ambassador Juha the Cavespider. The Dragons remain keen to join the northern trade network and to acquire the remnants of the Runeforge beneath Gildenheim.

Sarvos.t: The first shipments of Asavean white granite arrived at the Sarvos docks after the Cavabianca Dock affair was resolved, and the Diora University invited Axou scholars to speak.

Segura.t: Faraden merchant families want the Blood Red Roads extended to Anduz, in Segura, and have reportedly been negotiating an offer of cheap white granite for such a project.

Sermersuaq.t: Red-cloaked Thule orcs escorted fifty freed Imperial slaves, provisioned to reach Atalaq, to the foothills of the Silver Peaks under a ransom agreement with Wintermark.

Skarsind.t: Some of the freed slaves had been taken during the recent invasion of Skarsind. The Axou declined an invitation to the Legion's Rookery, while Sarcophan traders journeyed here to sell to orc bonesetters.

Tassato.t: Axou priests lectured at the Printers' Guild Museum of Wonders, and School of Epistemology students pelted two of them with rotten vegetables and eggs. Faraden merchants talk of a future mercenary market here.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: there is talk of a Faraden mercenary market in Temeschwar once the enclaves are complete.

Therunin.t: Axou priests lectured at Bronwen's Rest Wayhouse, and afterwards one of them was subjected to a curse of swarming insects; the priests cooperated with magistrates and pressed charges where appropriate.

Upwold.t: The Senate approved a Faraden trade hub at King's Stoke, welcomed as a sign of expanding Faraden presence. Work has not yet begun, though granite is already stockpiled in Anduz.

The best soil.d: Mel Bleak's mandate sent Sister Meredith and the egregore Jack to welcome the orcs, with 'paperwork later'. Almost all orcs seeking to bond with the egregores succeed, though integration will take time. The orcs reject the Doctrines of the Howling Abyss and question the Ancestors, so they remain heretics. A strong Synod denunciation could bring bloodshed on them from their neighbours. The Marcher and Imperial Orc assemblies were offered mandates pledging to defend them, and Highguard an alternative sending grey pilgrims to challenge them. Shared work on the Black Canal won Marcher hearts. That Great Work still needs 20 weirwood, 22 white granite and 3 crowns. The Marches could now raise a fifth army.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Doctrine of Enlightenment is said to have smoothed the transition of the Apulian orcs from being Grendel to joining the League.

Highguard.t: Aemon offered the Highborn National Assembly an alternative mandate sending grey pilgrims to persuade the Marcher Orcs that orcs do not reincarnate. The page warns the pilgrims would be forced to accept that the orcs will not give up the belief.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc assembly had already declared the Mourn Orcs to be Marchers and orc souls a matter for orcs. It could now pass a mandate sending preachers to debate the afterlife with the Marcher Orcs and pledging to defend them against any charge of heresy.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher Orcs are their former thralls, who fear what would happen if the Jotun returned. Future orc warriors might join Marcher armies to fight them.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the new doctrine removed another barrier between the Navarr and the Great Forest Orcs who established steadings in Miaren and Hercynia.

The Marches.t: The Marches began taking in the Mournwold Orcs as citizens, accepting heretics into the nation for their virtue, though some resistance remains. The nation now has the chance to raise a fifth army supported by its new orc citizens.

The best soil.o: Following the Marcher Assembly's Autumn Equinox 385YE mandate welcoming the former Jotun thralls, the Mournwold Orcs began joining the Marches as citizens, despite their heretical belief in reincarnation. The Doctrine of Enlightenment eased the way, and the change opened the possibility of a fifth Marcher army.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Mentioned in passing: before the orcs became Marchers, fully exploiting the Mournwold's wealth would have required clearing the old woodlands at Alderly.

Bregasland.t: A few Marcher Orcs are very cautiously seeking homes here. The unsettled situation in Bregasland is also the main risk to supporting a fifth Marcher army should it slide into open rebellion.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Great Forest Orcs established steadings here, and the new doctrine eased relations with their Navarr neighbours.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Great Forest Orcs established steadings here, and the new doctrine eased relations with their Navarr neighbours.

Mitwold.t: Mournwold Orcs are studying the great farms of Mitwold and some hope to settle there. The nearly finished Black Canal would raise investment in Mitwold's farms and businesses once completed.

Mournwold.t: Most Marcher Orcs still live in the Mournwold, holding much of its best farmland and mines, and are joining the Marches there. The Black Canal would boost the territory's businesses and mines on completion.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: some Marcher Orcs are already seeking new homes and opportunities in Upwold.

The bird and the child.d: Yaw'nagrah agreed to parley at the Cwllwch Stone in Liathaven, reached via the Sentinel Gate. Phaleron refused a parley in anger that the Gift of Knowledge had been placed in Imperial lore, offering contact only through the Emissary to the Celestial Library. Sinokenon sought talks on the Imperial Orcs. Prospero accepted, proposing permanent patronage of the Urizeni heliopticon college and seeking tourney champions. Wise Rangara accepted, bringing an emissary of Blood-on-the-Snow. Cathan Canae accepted, sending a champion to challenge Wintermark. Lashonar arranged a Caucus Forum meeting with the Sentinels of the Lambent Claw and a contest of words in the Imperial Regio. The Civil Service warned that dealings with eternals under enmity risk treason.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Archmage of Spring who will lead the parley with Yaw'nagrah is Ser Fabienne De Miel of Dawn.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Wise Rangara notes the Empire is beset by the Druj, and the Sentinels of the Lambent Claw are described as fighting the Druj.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Archmage of Summer, who receives Cathan Canae's emissary, is Exarch Luke of Highguard.

Imperial Orcs.t: Sinokenon invited the Archmage of Day to bring up to half a dozen orcs, ideally including magicians such as the Weigher of Worth and a representative of their national assembly, to a parley focused on the challenges facing their nation.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae's emissary wishes to hear from battle mages who have bested Jotun warriors, in battle or otherwise.

Urizen.t: Phaleron rebuked the Empire over the Gift of Knowledge leaving Urizen's control, while Prospero offered permanent patronage of the new Urizeni college and Lashonar invited three Urizen to meet the Sentinels of the Lambent Claw, possibly involving Herminius of House of the Wanderer.

Wintermark.t: Cathan Canae's champion Barag Glacier-Splitter was to undertake a Threefold Challenge with the people of Wintermark, and Blood-on-the-Snow's emissary asked that up to three Wintermark citizens, preferably icewalkers, attend Wise Rangara's parley.

The bird and the child.o: Ahead of the Spring Equinox 384YE, eternals of all six realms answered the Imperial archmages' plenipotentiary invitations, and Sinokenon unusually requested a parley with the Archmage of Day without having been invited.

Liathaven/Liath's Heart.t: A Sentinel Gate conjunction to the Cwllwch Stone in Liath's Heart opens for half an hour on the Friday evening, allowing no more than 26 people to travel to the parley with Yaw'nagrah's agents.

Liathaven.t: Yaw'nagrah agreed to parley at the Cwllwch Stone within the vallorn of Liathaven, sending the Old One of Liathaven, some Heirs of Terunael and children of her own.

Sermersuaq.t: The emissary of Blood-on-the-Snow attending Wise Rangara's parley wishes to discuss recent events in Sermersuaq with Winterfolk.

Zenith.t: Lashonar arranged for representatives of the Sentinels of the Lambent Claw, Zenith folk who have embraced a dangerous word-forging power to fight the Druj, to meet the Archmage of Night seeking a compromise.

The blessing way.d: League and Imperial Orc mandates gave the Sand Fishers shelter, a school and a hospital, and Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg found them receptive to the Virtues. The Druj then invaded Holberg and offered to release one Imperial captive for each Sand Fisher handed back. Some Sand Fishers hid at Grafflers Old Camp, now apparently a tulpa's lair. The Jotun accepted weregild but refused passage through Sermersuaq, saying any hall should stand empty in Skarsind. Thule took the Sungold Pass, built forts in Bonewood and Krevsaty, and arranged deliveries of freed slaves and Navarr artisans. Grendel Speaker Morna sailed to Sarvos to meet the Imperial Fleet Master.

Druj.t: The Druj invaded Holberg, apparently to punish the Sand Fishers for fleeing. Through a terrified Utterlund youth they offered to free one tormented Imperial citizen for every Sand Fisher returned to them.

Grendel.t: Speaker Morna and a Stone Born guard arrived at Sarvos under a flag of truce and travelled to Anvil to meet Imperial Fleet Master Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra, protected by Imperial law throughout.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel delegation travelled through the Highborn territory of Casinea on its way to Anvil.

Imperial Orcs.t: Skywise Rykana carried Imperial Orc support to the Sand Fishers and preached hope beyond the Howling Abyss. Consul Skywise Fal's embassy request was redirected by the Jotun to a hall in Skarsind.

Jotun.t: The Jotun settled the blood-price for the Meeting Place but refused safe passage or an embassy, saying the war would continue. Meanwhile escaped thralls and unknown hunters were striking at their holdings in Sermersuaq, and their mana-gathering drew Imperial attention.

Navarr.t: Under the Thule treaty, the Navarr artisans taken at the fall of Treji were to be delivered to Skogei before winter. Winterfolk ex-thralls also intended to trade their looted goods with the Navarr.

The League.t: Leonora van Holberg rallied Holberg's citizens to support the Sand Fishers, and Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg taught them the Virtues. League lands now faced a Druj invasion, while Sarvos received the Grendel envoy.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: developments with the Mournwold orcs are noted as covered elsewhere, and the former thralls there are compared to the Sand Fishers in their belief in reincarnation.

Thule.t: The Thule took the Sungold Pass, set out how slaves would be released for payment, kept their promise to defend Ossium and built new fortresses. They planned to reduce their Ossium presence temporarily to deal with a matter in Sküld.

Varushka.t: Varushkan Yevgeni Katzev served as Ambassador to Otkodov and must sign the payments for freed slaves. Varushkan observers and Karsk wardens reported on Thule activity, and freed slaves could be delivered to Varushkan lands.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark-mediated weregild closed the matter of the Meeting Place. The Jotun delivered their refusal at Atalaq, while thralls sought out Hendel Hearth and the Wintermark egregore found Sentinel Gate conjunctions into Sermersuaq.

The blessing way.o: In Autumn 383YE the Empire's dealings with several orc nations shifted: the Sand Fishers flourished in Misericorde under Imperial support until a Druj invasion of Holberg terrified them, while the Jotun rebuffed an embassy, the Thule began honouring their treaty and a Grendel envoy came to Anvil.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Some three thousand Sand Fishers settled in Misericorde with shelters, a school and a hospital, but now hid from the Druj. Their missing musicians were heard at Grafflers Old Camp, apparently a tulpa's lair reachable by a Sentinel Gate conjunction.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Druj shadows woke young Micha di Holberg in a forest cabin in Utterlund to carry their offer to the Senate. Micha refused to return home and enlisted with the Holberg garrison.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: Warden fellowships reported that the Thule had completed a fortification in the hills of Krevsaty, apparently using the Immaculate Architect.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Mentioned in passing: Mieriada is not named, though Wendell's Hope in Miekarova is listed as a delivery point for freed slaves.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: A brand new Thule fortress was completed in the Bonewood in six months, and Grand Warlock Fljajokull came down from there to confer with Imperial captains at Lormaa.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule said something had come up in Sküld requiring their attention, prompting a temporary drawdown from Ossium.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Mentioned in passing: Sealtoq is not named; the page speaks only of Sermersuaq generally, including a raid on the Pride of Ikka's Tears in the north.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: A Sentinel Gate conjunction at Asiaat's Hollow in Stark offered heroes access near a former Wintermark hall where thralls were gathering mana for the Jotun.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: A Sentinel Gate conjunction at Stag Fount in Suaq Fount offered heroes a chance to disrupt Jotun mana-gathering near a former Wintermark hall.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: The Jotun said any Imperial meeting hall should be built in Pakaanan's Pass, but warned it would stand empty until they chose to talk as equals.

Skarsind/Skogei Glens.t: Skogei was named as the place where the Thule would deliver the Navarr artisans before winter and where freed Imperial slaves could be handed over.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Speaker Morna's Grendel delegation travelled through Casinea along the Blood Red Roads.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is not named; its only link is that Navarr artisans taken at Treji are to be returned under the Thule treaty.

Holberg.t: Holberg's citizens poured support into the newly settled Sand Fishers, but a major Druj force invaded the territory to punish them, and the Druj demanded the orcs' return.

Karsk.t: Karsk wardens reported a completed Thule fortification in the hills of Krevsaty, and Ivarsgard was named as a delivery point for freed Imperial slaves.

Miekarova.t: Wendell's Hope in Miekarova was named as one of the places where the Thule would deliver freed Imperial slaves as payments arrived.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: developments with the Mournwold orcs are covered elsewhere, and their former Jotun thralls are compared to the Sand Fishers.

Ossium.t: The Thule kept their bargain to defend Ossium, patrolling its eastern borders alongside three Imperial armies and completing a fortress in the Bonewood. They planned a temporary reduction of their forces after the Equinox.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov ratified a treaty trading Imperial land slaves and Navarr artisans for the Sungold Pass, though it raised questions over one section. It agreed staged payments through the City of Gold and Lead.

Sarvos.t: A Grendel ship in Asavean style docked at Sarvos under a flag of truce, carrying Speaker Morna on his way to Anvil.

Sermersuaq.t: The Jotun refused Imperial passage through Sermersuaq. Escaped thralls offered Imperial heroes a strike against high-status Jotun, Naeve-marked attacks plagued occupied halls, and thralls were forced to gather mana under guard.

Skarsind.t: The Jotun proposed that any Imperial meeting hall be built in Pakaanan's Pass, and Skogei was chosen to receive the returned Navarr artisans and freed slaves.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are noted to have invaded Spiral just long enough to do something with the Black Plateau.

The Barrens.t: The Druj had beaten back an invasion of the Barrens, and the civil service advised that handing over the Sand Fishers would mean forcing the tribe into the Barrens.

The bones of what you believe.d: The Great Library at Mourning Hollow could be commissioned as a folly, available until the end of the Winter Solstice 384YE: 50 wains of white granite, 40 of weirwood, 30 of mithril and 240 crowns, taking a year. Two further years of study would follow. Mandates open to the League, Highguard and the General Assembly, and the Imperial Archivist's offer of historical research, could shorten that study or divert Bourse materials to the build. A Miaren brand proposed the Hall of the Seven, which would create the Spear of the Seven title and a ruin-exploring action. Minions of Cintra Blackstaff seized two vates, and a conjunction to Whisperwood offered a rescue attempt.

Dawn.t: Dawnish knights questing into the heart of Brocéliande inspired Navarr thorns and the Hall of the Seven proposal, and Navarr formally thanked Bertrand of House Sepulchre for building Greenwood Manor as a staging point for those knights.

Druj.t: Having fled to Sarangrave after reverses in Zenith, the ghulai Cintra Blackstaff had minions capture and interrogate two Navarr vates, apparently desperate to learn more about the vallorn.

Highguard.t: The Highborn assembly could mandate archivists and grey pilgrims to copy their vallorn lore, cutting the research by three months. A separate mandate could share statements of principle with the Navarr assembly for a year, though a General Assembly mandate would cut the Cinderpath Exchange's output.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, though the opening poem speaks of orcs squabbling on the outskirts of Liathaven, whose ruins Navarr explorers might one day reach.

Navarr.t: The Navarr could gather their scattered lore, guarded since Nicovar burned the libraries, into an expanded Great Library that promises a way to destroy the vallorn. They were also offered the Hall of the Seven, the Spear of the Seven title and the Temple of the Waking Dream, while two of their vates were held by the Druj.

The League.t: Building on Alessi di Trivento's statement, the League assembly could urge its scholars to search their libraries for vallorn and Navarr lore, cutting the research by three months. League donations and the Towerjacks might also help with construction.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening poem describes the vallorn heart Emrys in Sküld as a prisoner of the Thule, smothered by winter.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: if a General Assembly mandate passed with a greater majority, the Iron Roundtower and the Docks at Korotny would lose part of their output to the library effort.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Kauppahall would lose its top two ranks of production if the General Assembly mandate supporting the library were enacted.

The bones of what you believe.o: Following Navarr Synod mandates, the Empire was offered the chance to expand the Great Library of Hacynian into a true repository of Navarr lore whose study, once built, would reveal a way to destroy the vallorn. The wind also proposed a Hall of the Seven in Miaren and reported two vates captured by Druj on the Feverwater.

Brocéliande/Dark Ranging.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening poem laments that the chance to take Dark Ranging was slipping through Navarr fingers.

Brocéliande/Terunael.t: Mentioned in passing: the poem names the forests of Terunael as the heart of hearts and the battlefield where the Navarr were then fighting.

Miaren/Serenael.t: The proposed Hall of the Seven would be built in the City of Seren in Serenael, which the Navarr had also voted to make the City of Dreams.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Mentioned in passing: the poem says the vallorn heart Emrys on Sküld's cold plains has been bound with oaths and will fall in time.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: Mentioned in passing: the poem refers to the fallen city of Béantal Dol as lying beyond the trods, too far to reach for now.

Sarangrave/Whisperwood.t: A conjunction to Karliss in Whisperwood led to the Druj camp holding the captured vates, and the Dredgemaster of the Feverwater was asked to arrange a rescue.

Brocéliande.t: Dawnish knights were exploring the heart of Brocéliande, the battlefield where the Navarr were fighting. Its ruins were among the harder-to-reach sites that the proposed Explore the ruins of Terunael action would cover.

Hercynia.t: The Great Library of Hacynian at Mourning Hollow could be rebuilt as an Empire-wide centre of Navarr history and vallorn study. Hercynia's accessible ruins would also be open to Navarr explorers if the Hall of the Seven were built.

Holberg.t: The recent consecration in Holberg inspired its academics to seek novel solutions to the Empire's problems, and the League assembly urged Holberg's citizens to visit the Great Library to help tackle the vallorn.

Liathaven.t: Liathaven's vallorn was described as wounded but cut off from the trods. The Navarr pointedly rejected closer ties with its Feni, and its ruins were counted among the harder-to-reach sites for explorers.

Miaren.t: Miaren was proposed as the site of the Hall of the Seven. Enthusiasm also grew for turning Seren into the City of Dreams, awaiting a Senate commission for the Temple of the Waking Dream.

Otkodov.t: The Terunael ruins in Otkodov, outside Imperial borders, would be among those Navarr military units could explore if the Hall of the Seven were built.

Sarangrave.t: Cintra Blackstaff fled to Sarangrave with a stolen vallorn ritual text, and her minions held two captured vates there. Its ruins would also be open to Navarr explorers via the Hall of the Seven.

Therunin.t: Therunin's ruins were among the relatively accessible sites for the proposed exploration action. Prognosticators had expected Cintra Blackstaff to flee here, though she went to Sarangrave instead.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: a sudden reversal of Druj fortunes in Zenith drove Cintra Blackstaff east, and Highguard's armies were said to be focused on the fight there.

The brightest flame.d: Nim of Ebon's Hall's mandate sent Highborn wayfarers and pilgrims to Anduz. Lita i Nadir i Riqueza's call for unity kept the passionate debates from turning into arguments. The firebrands proved to be driven chiefly by politics rather than Virtue or doctrine. Some likely bear auras of Freedom, but they do not seek to spread them. Their causes vary widely, and they blame the Senate and Military Council for sacrificing the Coast. Building the Burning Agora will restore them to prominence. Felix of the Far Tower's engineers offered to build the Anduz Pools bathhouse, creating a Freeborn sinecure, if it is commissioned in time.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: some firebrand hakima want the Military Council to concentrate its resources on wiping out the Druj.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: firebrands cite Grendel's years-long hold on Feroz as proof the Coast has been sacrificed by Imperial strategy.

Highguard.t: Highborn pilgrims and wayfarers, under Nim of Ebon's Hall's mandate, debated the firebrands at length but could not influence them. A Highborn chapterhouse, Felix of the Far Tower, has offered to build a bathhouse in Anduz.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: some firebrand hakima argue the western nations should be left to their own Vigilance against the Jotun.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn welcomed the Highborn, and the debates exposed the firebrands as passionate political idealists. Building the Burning Agora will restore them to prominence in Freeborn society, for better or worse.

The brightest flame.o: In Summer 388YE the Highborn Assembly extended peerless kinship to the Brass Coast, sending pilgrims to Anduz to debate the resurgent firebrands. The visit revealed much about the movement but did nothing to change it, and it produced a proposal for a Highborn bathhouse in Anduz.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: firebrands point to Feroz languishing under Grendel control as a failure of Imperial strategy, and one Freeborn voice insists a firebrand would sooner have burned it than lost it.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: firebrands cite Madruga, drowned in salt and exposed to Wreckers and Asaveans, as evidence the Coast has been sacrificed.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is home to the newly established Felix of the Far Tower chapterhouse, whose engineers propose the Anduz bathhouse and will return there if it is not commissioned in time.

Segura.t: The Highborn debates with the firebrands took place in Anduz, in Segura, where the Burning Agora is to be built. Highborn engineers offered to build the Anduz Pools there, a sinecure whose Keeper would receive 7 liao and 7 crowns each season.

The circle game.d: Graciana concluded that most citizens and foreigners prefer coin to barter. Following Emperor Giovanni's design, money spent at Anvil circulates back to the treasury, and it is lost only through armies, fortifications and ministries. She offered several options: abrogating the Grandmaster mana ministries, which would put an extra 127 crystal mana a season into the font; ending embassy ministries; and converting the Northern trade network into great works. She advised against touching the six Prosperity ministries. She found barter deals with Axos, the Sarcophan Kruidenkenner and the Ossium Ketsov. She also reviewed outstanding great works in Feroz, Sermersuaq, Kallavesa, Madruga, Karov and Zenith. Finally, she suggested Synod mandates urging League and Marcher citizens to take up businesses and farms.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Boar's Market is one of the Prosperity ministries Graciana advised against abrogating. If the Kallavesa Marshways were built, Dawnish military units would gain a guarding venture protecting merchants there.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page and is linked only through its share of Feroz, where the Inkworks of Joharra opportunity remains open.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Cinder Path Exchange, the first of the Prosperity ministries, should be left alone according to Graciana. Separately, the House of Spirits in Casinea could trade liao to the Axou for ilium if the Senate accepted their offer.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Torfast Trading Post in Skarsind anchors the Northern trade network. Graciana proposed upgrading it to a great work that would trade the Bonesetter's routes for higher business investment across the territory.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland, now held by the Jotun, is noted as no longer under Imperial control, which rules out building the Marshways there.

Navarr.t: Navarr's Invisible Cord Brokerage is a Prosperity ministry Graciana advised keeping. The Treji Wayhouse in Hercynia could be converted into a great work boosting herb gardens. Therunin's lost status means no Marshways can be built there.

The Brass Coast.t: The Parador of Dust is a protected Prosperity ministry, and two Freeborn opportunities remain open. The Inkworks of Joharra in Feroz would create a Scrivener of the Inkworks title. The Municipal Docks in Madruga would raise taxation, fleets and businesses and add a Quaymaster title.

The League.t: Graciana proposed a Synod mandate urging League citizens to invest in businesses, letting them convert other resources for free and upgrade businesses for one wain less for a year. Temeschwar's Northbound Trademaster could also become a great work once the rest of the network is upgraded.

Thule.t: The Thule take part in the Northern trade network, exchanging crystal mana for Imperial ingots and measures. Their Urdur trade is the only option each ministry would keep if converted into a great work.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Graciana notes a new appraisal by Naomi of Virtue's Rest proposing roads in Zenith to raise business investment there.

Varushka.t: The Iron Tower is a protected Prosperity ministry. The Ketsov of Ossium would accept ingots instead of coin for herbs, and Delev in Karov could receive either a modest market conversion or the larger Great Market, but not both.

Wintermark.t: The motion came from Sermersuaq's senator, and Wintermark scholar Vauraus Korppitkotka's analysis was confirmed by the appraisal. Several Wintermark opportunities are listed: the Kauppahall is protected, the Kalpaheim Tradehall, Atalaq Fishery and Tradehall, and Kallavesa Marshways remain open, and the Marshways would add a guarding venture for Wintermark units.

The circle game.o: In Winter 387YE the prognosticator Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra delivered the Senate's appraisal of trades that ministries could make without coin. She found few options and instead examined the Imperial treasury's declining revenues, setting out ways to abrogate or convert ministries and listing great works that would draw more money into the Anvil economy.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The Inkworks of Joharra would be built in Oranseri, and its completion would remove the region's impoverished quality.

Hahnmark/Kalpamark.t: Kalpamark is the site of the proposed Kalpaheim Tradehall great work, costing 30 wains of white granite, 90 crowns and three months.

Hercynia/The Glen of Shadows.t: The Treji Wayhouse in the Glen of Shadows could be upgraded into a great work for 30 wains of white granite and 90 crowns to boost Hercynian herb gardens.

Karov/Duzekani.t: Delev in Duzekani is the site of two mutually exclusive proposals: the Delev Market great work or the larger Great Market at Delev.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: The Municipal Docks would be built at Calvos. They would protect Calvos Sound as a level one fortification and serve as a shipyard for up to two navies.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Mentioned in passing: completing the Municipal Docks would create a new Freeborn questing voyage, Hunt the Free Landing Kraken.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Sealtoq would host both the Atalaq Fishery and the Atalaq Tradehall, centred on the town of Atalaq.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: The Torfast Trading Post in Southpine could be upgraded to a great work for 30 wains of white granite, 90 crowns and three months.

Temeschwar/Hanuri.t: Hanuri is the site of the proposed Northbound Trade great work, costing 60 wains of white granite and 180 crowns. It depends on the rest of the northern network being upgraded first.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland was part of the original Marshways plan but is no longer controlled by the Empire, so building there is out of the question.

Casinea.t: The Bursar of the House of Spirits in Casinea could acquire ilium from the Axou in exchange for large amounts of liao, if the Senate accepted the offer.

Feroz.t: The Inkworks of Joharra remains available for 60 white granite and 60 crowns. It would raise business investment in Feroz, boost scriveners' income for a year and create the Scrivener of the Inkworks.

Hahnmark.t: The Kalpaheim Tradeholder's ministry could be converted into the Kalpaheim Tradehall great work. This would raise business investment across Hahnmark by one while leaving the title only the Urdur trade.

Hercynia.t: The Treji Wayhouse could become a great work that raises herb garden investment in Hercynia by one, removing the Broker's other trade options apart from the Urdur trade.

Kallavesa.t: Updated Marshways plans for Kallavesa alone would cost 80 wains of weirwood and 240 crowns. They would raise investment in businesses and herb gardens and create a guarding venture for Wintermark and Dawnish units.

Karov.t: Delev could see either the Delev Market great work, which requires the other northern upgrades first, or Naomi's larger Great Market at Delev. The Great Market would add four thrones of taxation but would increase spending by several ministries.

Madruga.t: The Municipal Docks proposal for Calvos remains open. It would raise investment in fleets and businesses, add 12 thrones of taxation for 5 thrones of upkeep, and give Freeborn characters extra income for a year.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction recalls Giovanni's Miaren campaign as a moment of heroism that he apparently regarded as a disaster.

Ossium.t: The Ketsov would accept ingots instead of coin for the herbs bought by the Merchant-Boyar of the Stinking Market and the Apothecary of Orieb. Graciana warned this would make both ministries depend on the often touchy Ketsov.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sarvos mana exchange was among those expanded in 384YE to enhance the Grandmasters' ministries, and economist Laurencio Lemmini di Sarvos is cited.

Sermersuaq.t: The appraisal was raised by Sermersuaq's senator. Two opportunities remain open there: the Atalaq Fishery, which would raise farm investment, and the Atalaq Tradehall, which would raise business investment and add 4 thrones of taxation.

Skarsind.t: The Torfast Trading Post, anchor of the Northern trade network, could become a great work raising business investment across Skarsind. The Bonesetter would be left with only the northern Urdur route.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is noted as the seat of the Imperial Mint established by Giovanni and as one of the expanded mana exchanges.

Temeschwar.t: The Northbound Trademaster's ministry could be converted into the Northbound Trade great work, raising business investment, but only once every other branch of the northern network is upgraded. It would work well alongside the Silver Fox Mines.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Therunin was in the original Marshways plan but is suffering invasion and is no longer Imperial, so it was dropped.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Naomi of Virtue's Rest has proposed roads in Zenith that would raise business investment in the territory.

The cities and the city.d: The Seventh Wave and Isaac of the Silent Tide broke the Grendel spy ring in Necropolis, ending Grendel trade with Highborn merchants. Seized papers showed the Salt Lords undecided on a target and keen to despoil the tombs by holding Coursmouth. The Shuttered Lantern, helped by the Wolves of War, mapped a separate ring in Sarvos that either could now destroy, and confirmed rings in Madruga, Redoubt, Tassato and Spiral. The Winter Sun's Day enchantment drew items of worth from the Highborn. Stewards found nothing amiss at Varkula's tomb. Building began in Bastion while some three thousand Cold Sun heralds gathered at Woodbury.

Druj.t: Their heartland of the Salt Flats of Sanath is under Imperial attack, and Imperial assemblies may urge their soldiers to reach out to orc septs oppressed by the Druj.

Grendel.t: Their Necropolis spy ring was rolled up and its agents expelled, their Sarvos network was mapped, and recovered papers exposed turmoil among the Salt Lords, their Asavean pact and their designs on the tombs of Necropolis.

Highguard.t: The Seventh Wave broke the Necropolis spy ring at the cost of Grendel trade, Highborn gave up items of worth to the Imperial Orcs, Highguard funds the Grand Inspiration in Bastion, and the Valiant Pegasus fights in Sanath while Cold Sun threatens the White City.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Winter Sun recovered items of worth from the Highborn in Necropolis and sent many to Skarsind's Halls of Worth, and Skywise Gralka's art was chosen as an inspiration for the sacred city in Bastion.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn are committing white granite and money to the Grand Inspiration until Summer 386YE, corsairs acting for a Madrugan magistrate exposed a Grendel smuggling ring, and a Grendel spy ring was confirmed in Madruga.

The League.t: A Grendel spy ring of mostly League citizens and disguised Salt Lord agents was mapped in Sarvos, which the Grendel may still attack. The Wolves of War could destroy the ring, and further rings were confirmed in Tassato and Spiral.

Urizen.t: Naris in Redoubt was named as one of two regions the Grendel must hold to strike Necropolis, a spy ring was confirmed in Redoubt, and the Urizen assembly may urge the Citadel Guard to seek out oppressed septs in Sanath.

Varushka.t: Wise ones sent under Father Drakov's statement were refused entry to Empress Varkula's tomb, which showed no sign of a rising sovereign, and the Varushkan assembly may direct the Iron Helms to seek out oppressed septs in Sanath.

The cities and the city.o: In Autumn 385YE the Grendel spy ring in Necropolis was broken, a second ring was found in Sarvos, work began on the Grand Inspiration in Bastion under the threat of Cold Sun, and the Winter Sun sought items of worth in Necropolis. Varushkan wise ones were refused entry to Empress Varkula's tomb, and Synod mandates were offered to armies advancing into the Salt Flats of Sanath.

Bastion/Stoneside.t: Cold Sun would need to pass through Stoneside to threaten the White City directly.

Bastion/Woodbury.t: Some three thousand Cold Sun heralds have gathered here, leaving its lightly fortified farming chapters terrified of losing their harvests and treasures if forced to flee.

Necropolis/Coursmouth.t: Grendel papers show they would need to occupy Coursmouth to break into the tombs of the Thrones and heroes, though a counterattack might trap such an army there.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Mentioned in passing: Longbeach is not named on the page and relates only to the wider espionage and Grendel threat to Necropolis.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Naris is one of two regions the Grendel must take and hold to reach and raid the Necropolis.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: The Shuttered Lantern mapped Grendel agents here as part of a ring best struck in all three Sarvos regions at once.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Grendel agents here form part of the Sarvos spy web, which needs simultaneous action in all three regions to dismantle.

Sarvos/Uccelini.t: Agents in Uccelini were mapped as part of the Sarvos ring, and if left in place they could covertly support a Grendel attack.

Bastion.t: Construction of the Grand Inspiration of the Way began on the designs of Millward Cowley and Skywise Gralka, but a large Cold Sun force in the territory leaves workers, granite caravans and the unfortified White City vulnerable.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not named on the page and relates only to the wider Grendel threat to the Empire's southern coast.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel espionage ring was confirmed here, and corsairs acting for a Madrugan magistrate helped expose the Necropolis smuggling ring.

Necropolis.t: The Grendel spy ring and a smuggling ring were broken, ending extra Grendel trade, and the Winter Sun sought items of worth here. Seized papers showed the Grendel intend to despoil the tombs, while Varkula's tomb stayed sealed.

Redoubt.t: A Grendel spy ring was confirmed in Redoubt, and Naris was identified as one of two regions the Grendel must take to raid the Necropolis.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Cold Sun had already destroyed the Unbound Steel Hall of Lost Chapters here.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: The Valiant Pegasus and other Imperial armies are advancing into this Druj heartland. Assemblies may pass mandates trading slower conquest for contact with local septs, but these fail if any army makes a merciless assault.

Sarvos.t: A separate Grendel espionage ring was mapped in the city, which remains a possible Grendel target. The Shuttered Lantern, the Wolves of War or both could destroy the ring, and if left alone it could covertly aid an attack.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: many items of worth recovered in Necropolis are sent to Skarsind's Halls of Worth for the oathwrights to assign to new champions.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War's general boasted of taking Spiral in a single season, and a Grendel spy ring was confirmed here.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the territories where a Grendel espionage ring was confirmed.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Empress Giselle's body was moved from Necropolis and interred in a new tomb here.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun marched south from the Barrens, and the Dawnish approach used in its conquest is the model for the Sanath mandates.

The city asleep.d: Drawn by Imperial daring, Rhianos proposed placing the ancient, nearly exhausted cauldron at the Broch in Black Boughs. Its onion soup grants protection from venom, sickness and the miasma. Brocéliande's vallorn remains weakened by Wither the Seed. Military units, not armies, could join an expedition into the forest in place of normal production, earning forest resources, herbs, weirwood, ilium and relics. Greater strength reaches deeper: securing northern Brocéliande, looting the abandoned Heirs of Terunael base, the vallorn gardens, a hidden weirwood grove, the walls of Terunael and finally the vallorn heart itself. Navarr, Highborn and Dawnish mandates and choices, and Great Forest Orc aid, could swell the effort.

Dawn.t: Rhianos' heralds came to Dawn, and Dawnish knights who joined the expedition were offered a one-rank bonus to strength and rewards. Alternatively they could quest independently from the newly completed Greenwood Market and Manor.

Druj.t: If the expedition gathered enough strength, the remaining Druj would be cleared out of northern Brocéliande, with treasures seized from them.

Highguard.t: Heralds visited Highguard, and the Highborn Assembly could revive the Blade of the Pilgrims for a final season. Congregations would sacrifice liao and Synod votes to add 1,000 or 2,000 strength, with reduced cost if Hazelelponi of the Shattered Tower enacted it.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's raid on Skallahn is cited, and the vallorn of Liathaven serves as a point of comparison.

Navarr.t: The Navarr hosted the heralds at the Broch and prepared for many visitors. Their National Assembly could urge every thorn to join, with Navarr units taking any other action penalised until Winter.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: farmers in Mournwold are among those reporting eerie Spring-touched plants where the vallorn has reached.

The city asleep.o: In Autumn 384YE heralds of Rhianos, Regent of the Eternal Sea, offered the Empire a dying Cauldron of Gold whose food protects against the vallorn miasma. They invited heroic bands to a grand adventure from the Broch in Brocéliande into the heart of ruined Terunael.

Brocéliande/Black Boughs.t: The cauldron was to be placed at the heart of the reinforced Broch in Black Boughs, the starting point for every band joining the adventure.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Boar's Dell is free of vallorn, and success could secure its borders against Mallum orcs and link it by safe routes to the Broch. It was once home to the Great Forest Orcs.

Brocéliande/Dark Ranging.t: Mentioned in passing: the earlier opportunity to attack Dark Ranging is noted as no longer available.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Elerael is free of vallorn, and a successful adventure could secure its borders with watches against Mallum orcs and safe routes to the Broch.

Brocéliande/Terunael.t: The ruined city of Terunael and its vallorn heart were the ultimate goal. Deep success could breach its walls or even look upon the heart for the first time in centuries.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: Mentioned in passing: a later report from an expedition to Bendol appears in further reading.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs are said to have returned to the Eaves of Peytaht after the Barrens were liberated.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: Chief Vallack of the Great Forest Orcs is in the Lower Tarn Valley. A Winged Messenger to him from Therunin's senator or the Consul would send the Spears of the Pines.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat farmers have spoken of eerie plants steeped in Spring magic growing where the vallorn has touched.

Brocéliande.t: The whole adventure takes place in Brocéliande, the largest vallorn near the Empire. Success could secure the north of the forest, uncover the Heirs' base and penetrate ruined Terunael.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea farmers have reported strange Spring-steeped plants growing where the vallorn has touched.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: its vallorn is dwarfed by Brocéliande's, and the weirwood grove found there is compared to the hoped-for sanctuary near Terunael.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: the destruction of Miaren some 350 years ago was the last time anyone looked upon a vallorn heart.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold farmers have spoken of eerie vallorn-touched plants.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: listed only in further reading, via a later expedition to Bendol.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial raid on Skallahn was one of the daring deeds that caught Rhianos' attention.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the liberation of the Barrens by independent orcs led the Great Forest Orcs to leave Boar's Dell for the Eaves of Peytaht.

Therunin.t: The Great Forest Orcs of Therunin offered to send the Spears of the Pines, adding 1,000 strength, if invited by Therunin's senator or the Imperial Consul. They would give more help, including extra weirwood, if granted Imperial lore by the Conclave.

The city below.d: Urizeni magicians, many aligned with the Deathless Cave, offered to help shape Apulian's character. The League Assembly enacted Lia Adelaar van Holberg's mandate urging Apulians to embrace them, backed by the Loyalty Assembly. Actius proposed the Chamber of Euphony, which could be ceded to Sung as a fane creating the title Map to the City Below; it remains open for commission until the 387YE Summer Solstice. Apulian orcs doubted the warned Grendel plot to weaponise the Black Plateau, and no public action was taken. Urizen's mandate released the Block's secrets, removing commission penalties in Spiral. The League condemned the Company of the Venturesome Harrier's Plateau tours as a scam. Blue Spring-touched flowers blossomed across Spiral.

Grendel.t: Imperial assemblies warned of a Grendel plot to weaponise the Black Plateau, but Apulian's orcs judged the nation to have neither the skill nor the will for it. Sharing the Block's secrets openly now leaves them within easy reach of Grendel spies.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the mausoleums of the Necropolis are cited as resonating with the Winter realm, by way of comparison with cities.

The League.t: The League Assembly enacted a mandate urging Apulians to learn from their Urizeni neighbours and condemned the Harrier company's Plateau tours as a scam. The League may also commission the Chamber of Euphony and a national Map to the City Below.

Urizen.t: Urizeni magicians of the Deathless Cave became a common sight in Apulian and offered to share their culture and Sung's patronage. The Urizen Assembly, by a greater majority but with notable dissent, chose to share the secrets of the Block with the League.

The city below.o: With the Urizeni rebellion in Ankra and Cinion largely stabilised, attention turned to the fast-growing city of Apulian in Spiral. The League chose to embrace Urizeni culture there, and Urizen agreed to share the secrets of the mithril Block that protects minds from the Black Plateau.

Spiral/Ankra.t: Ankra has returned to the Empire, and the Night mages of its Deathless Cave, now hidden behind Sung's mithril statues, have grown comfortable mixing with their League neighbours.

Spiral/Cinion.t: The rebellion in Cinion's mountains has been stabilised after the Senate recognised the Silver Flame there as foreigners, though reconciliation with Caeli's rebels remains distant.

Spiral/Screed.t: Two Harrier hiking parties ran into trouble in the woods of Screed near the Black Plateau, with Estella Lucati and the Mistress of Medicine asked to rescue them.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's grandeur and the City of Locks' regio in one of its clock towers are cited as comparisons for Apulian.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: its mausoleums are cited as an example of places resonating with the Winter realm.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Apulian is said to fall far short of Sarvos's size, and several Sarvosan figures appear in the related votes and tasks.

Spiral.t: Apulian's character began to absorb Urizeni philosophy and magic, and the Block's secrets removed the Black Plateau's penalty on commissions in the territory. Blue Spring-touched flowers bloomed across it, refreshing some people and making others violent.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar's Varushkan heritage is cited as a model for Apulian, and a Temeschwar priest raised the statement condemning the Harrier tours.

The concisest tenant.d: Rumours of an ancient rat spirit beneath Temeschwar persist, and plays of the Steadfast Soldier and the King of Rats are thriving. Temeschwari citizens wearing a Doctor's mask could draw on cold resolve, and League magicians could channel the Doctor in Day or Winter rituals.
