The Rat Kings planned to attend the Masquerade of the Reaper at Anvil. With Giselle reinterred in Sarvos, Bishop Jarek proposed recasting Virtue's Respite as a monument to Temeschwari Pride, with a Pride of the City lecture. Lorainne Brouat proposed a Rat Garden acknowledging the rat spirit, which the Unfettered Mind wished to study. Either option needs a Senate motion and would allow the Guardian's title to be renamed.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: their sacking of Sarvos and theft of Giselle's body are recalled as the origin of the memorial, and the rebuilding of Sarvos after their attack appears on its friezes.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the escort of Giselle's body from Highguard to Temeschwar is depicted on one of Virtue's Respite's friezes.

The League.t: League citizens in Temeschwar could draw on the Doctor's influence, and League magicians could channel it in ritual. The League Assembly could also spread a Pride of the City lecture to every League city, though this risked stoking fierce rivalry over which city is greatest.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar was once Varushkan land, the King of Rats tale has Varushkan origins, and the rat spirit is likened to what Varushkans call a sovereign.

The concisest tenant.o: In Winter 387YE Temeschwar's rat plague had been largely tamed by the Rat Kings guild, while the dramaturgical figure of the Doctor, especially in rat-masked form, began lending magical strength to the city. Two rival proposals also emerged to remodel Virtue's Respite, the former tomb of Empress Giselle.

Temeschwar/Hanuri.t: Virtue's Respite stands in Hanuri, and both proposed commissions to remodel it as a Pride memorial or a Rat Garden would be carried out there, raising the Guardian's income.

Temeschwar/Metri.t: Mentioned in passing: the victory over the night terrors of Metri is suggested as a subject for new Temeschwari friezes at Virtue's Respite.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the liberation of Holberg appears on the friezes of Virtue's Respite, and Holberg is said to have recently claimed the crown of greatest League city.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the bravo Lorainne Brouat fought alongside Varushkan armies in the conquest of Ossium.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Empress Giselle's remains now rest in a courtyard at Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos, leaving her Temeschwar tomb empty.

Temeschwar.t: The city's rats now mostly come out at night thanks to the Rat Kings, while the rat-masked Doctor lent its citizens and magicians cold strength. The city faced a choice over remodelling Virtue's Respite as either a shrine to Temeschwari Pride or a Rat Garden acknowledging the spirit beneath its streets.

The cry of gulls.d: The Grendel pressed into Calvos Sound backed by three navies, Asavean warships and the plundering Black Eels, but were broken at Calvos. The Empire then drove them through Lightsea and took Quzar after fierce fighting. Sky Mage Faireoir escaped with treasures of the hakima. About 2,500 Marchers and 1,500 Freeborn died. The Empire holds Torres, Calvos Sound and Lightsea; the Grendel hold Siroc Plains. Siakha's heralds attacked both sides, and Shivaarn's emissary declared the Bay hers. A battle opportunity at Siakha's Maw offered chances to stop kraken eggs and rituals, rescue a captive and protect a spy who could betray Rahab. A skirmish in Feroz targeted a Faraden agent.

Grendel.t: Grendel armies were driven from Calvos Sound and Lightsea with severe losses and now hold only Siroc Plains, while Shivaarn's cultists turned on them at Free Landing and the Salt Lords renounced Siakha.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Freeborn captains were urged to protect trading vessels crossing the Bay to Highguard.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman is described as Jotun-threatened as the Marcher armies passed through it.

The Brass Coast.t: The Fire of the South and Burning Falcon helped retake Calvos Sound and Lightsea at a cost of about 1,500 Freeborn dead. The nation's armies remain in decline until another prosperous coastal region is recovered.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the damaged Spider's Dream bridge hampers armies crossing from the League, and Freeborn ships were asked to protect trade bound for the League.

The Marches.t: Three Marcher armies came from Bregasland to help liberate Madruga out of loyalty to the Freeborn, losing around 2,500 soldiers in the campaign.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Freeborn captains were urged to protect trading vessels bound for Urizen.

The cry of gulls.o: In Spring 386YE five Imperial armies, the Freeborn Fire of the South and Burning Falcon with the Marcher Bounders, Drakes and Strong Reeds, counter-attacked the Grendel in Madruga. They held Calvos and liberated Lightsea at heavy cost, while the Siakha cult of High Priestess Shivaarn seized Free Landing and claimed the whole Bay of Catazar.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: Mentioned in passing: the Burning Falcon dodged orc armies in Jade Range on its way to Calvos Sound.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: The Grendel assault on Calvos was broken in a bloody battle that left the town standing and free, though Siakha's heralds emerged from the sea that night.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Free Landing has fallen to Shivaarn's Siakha cult at Siakha's Maw. An opportunity was offered to stop their kraken eggs and Spring rituals, free Mohrain Luain and protect the Sea-Wraith's informant.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: Lightsea was liberated after fighting across its grasslands and a fierce battle for Quzar, which freed the Parador of Salt and Sand. Siakha's cultists later sent Shivaarn's emissary to Quzar's docks.

Madruga/Torres.t: Torres was the Imperial mustering point and remains in Imperial hands. Marracossans from Trajadoz joined the Freeborn armies there to defend their new home.

Segura/Yellow Chase.t: A suspicious Faraden-garbed agent entered Yellow Chase and fled from citizens as they headed towards Feroz.

Bay of Catazar.t: A monster-spawning maelstrom now churns where the Shining Pillar stood, and High Priestess Shivaarn has claimed the entire Bay for Siakha, declaring all who live on its shores her prey.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bounders, Drakes and Strong Reeds marched from Bregasland, which the Marchers had recently liberated.

Feroz.t: The Grendel retreated toward the Feroz border, and a skirmish opportunity tasked the Champion of Wisdom with intercepting a suspicious Faraden agent before they reached Grendel lines there.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher armies swept through Jotun-threatened Kahraman on their way to Madruga.

Madruga.t: The Empire won back Torres, Calvos Sound and Lightsea at a terrible cost. Siroc Plains stays in Grendel hands and Free Landing has fallen to Siakha's cultists.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher armies marched through Mournwold en route to Madruga.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: armies moving between Sarvos and Madruga must cross the ruined Spider's Dream bridge.

Segura.t: The Burning Falcon marched from Segura to Calvos Sound, and Freeborn militia in Segura tracked a suspicious Faraden agent heading for Feroz.

Shayeel.t: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel Storm Lord compared the Freeborn's fury to the winds of Shayeel.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: armies moving between Tassato and Madruga must cross the damaged Spider's Dream bridge.

The current when it serves.d: More than fifteen thousand Imperial soldiers gathered at the Fortress of Kalant. They then followed Emperor Guntherm's old route into Skallahn. Jotun beacons gave early warning, but the defenders were overwhelmed. The Winterfolk fought honourably and quarter was given on both sides, while terrified thralls mostly fled west. Greenwall fell within a month and Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard retreated to Bjarkey. Iron Stand was half taken by the Solstice, and aid was rumoured from Tromsa and Hordalant. Blade Quencher's Hall began growing and attacking Imperial troops. A battle was offered to sever or destroy its regio and kill Blade Quencher. Conjunctions offered the chance to recover Blerung's shield and to stop Greenwall's fyrd forming.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Summer Storm advanced steadily into Skallahn to free thralls, guided by the voice of Sjöfn of the Bittenblade. Its General was charged with stopping Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard from raising Greenwall's fyrd at Paegga's Rest.

Jotun.t: The Jotun were caught outmatched on their home ground, losing Greenwall and half of Iron Stand. However, reinforcements were reportedly coming from Tromsa and Hordalant, and Blade Quencher's Autumn warriors rallied routed warbands at his Hall.

Wintermark.t: The Bloodcloaks and Green Shield led the offensive and fought as heroes, offering quarter and insisting that their allies fight honourably. Blerunning Hall asked the Watcher of Britta's Pool to recover Blerung the Bright Lantern's lost shield.

The current when it serves.o: In Summer 385YE the Bloodcloaks, the Green Shield and the Summer Storm invaded Jotun-held Skallahn from Stark, conquering Greenwall and fighting halfway through Iron Stand. Meanwhile Blade Quencher's Hall, an Autumn fane allied to the Jotun, began expanding and disgorging Estavus' warriors.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: The three armies gathered and planned the offensive at the Fortress of Kalant in Stark. Blade Quencher's fane stands right on Stark's border.

Skallahn/Bjarkey.t: Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard retreated to Bjarkey after losing Greenwall. He was awaiting the Greenwall fyrd at Paegga's Rest, where the Summer Storm's General could intercept him.

Skallahn/Greenwall.t: Greenwall fell to the Empire within a month and most of its thralls fled. Blade Quencher's Hall threatens the Imperial beachhead there unless it is severed from Autumn or its regio destroyed.

Skallahn/Iron Stand.t: The armies pushed into Jarl Ebbe of Overgaard's lands around the ruined Iron Banner and held half the region by the Solstice. Blerung's lost shield is held by a ghodi at Kevan's Holt there.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: General Styx recalled the Summer Storm's earlier fighting in Bregasland to push back the Jotun.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: scouts reported orc forces crossing from Hordalant, probably to defend Skallahn.

Kallavesa.t: Blerung the Bright Lantern's effects rest in Kallavesa's marshes. If her lost shield is recovered and given to a host of Sulkavaris, it can be laid there beside her.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sea of Snow is not named on the page, which concerns the land campaign in neighbouring Skallahn.

Sermersuaq.t: The invasion was launched from Sermersuaq, and the armies in Iron Stand rely on its border for reinforcement and retreat. Blade Quencher's Hall threatens the supply routes back into the territory.

Skallahn.t: Skallahn was invaded by the Empire for the first time in a generation; Greenwall was claimed as a beachhead and Iron Stand was half conquered. Blade Quencher's expanding Hall threatened to undo these gains and strengthen the Jotun.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: scouts reported scattered aid being sent south by the Jarls of Tromsa to Skallahn.

The darkest road.d: After Kavor Eyepeel's death, Druj forces in Zenith lost cohesion. The Towerjacks took Iteri and the Citadel Guard raised a citadel in Clypion. Thousands of doses of liao, sent under Aurum of the Nightingale Temple's mandate, anointed Imperial soldiers against the miasma. A Highborn and Dawnish host came through Morrow into Lustri, and the Hounds of Glory lost hundreds to complete the encirclement. Zenith became Imperial again, but the hold is fragile: losing any region loses the territory. The Druj armies remain hale and plan to have the Tainted Basilisk enchant them with Night magic before fleeing. The Glass Labyrinth limits their escape, and conjunctions offer chances to destroy miasma pillars and monsters.

Dawn.t: The Hounds of Glory, bound with Autumn magic and reinforced by eleven thousand soldiers, refused to accept anything short of victory and drove the last orcs from Lustri at the cost of hundreds of knights and yeomen. The Endless Stalker has since been preying on their camps in Lustri.

Druj.t: The Druj lost Zenith. Seven of their armies are trapped in Proceris and Occursion and can only escape at devastating cost, and their generals are gathering at the Glade of Night Enshrouding to be enchanted by the Tainted Basilisk.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the trapped Druj armies cannot easily leave Zenith unless they attack Grendel-held Spiral.

Highguard.t: The Highborn armies inspired the virtuous crusade in both the west and north of Zenith. Nearly a thousand of Kaela's unkillable warriors were sent among the Druj specifically to face Highguard's soldiers.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the trapped Druj armies are compared to the Black Thorns once trapped in Liathaven.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Seventh Wave marched through Therunin, and a Druj escape into Therunin is described as near suicide.

The League.t: Thomas di Holberg, a reformed bravo turned priest, located a lone miasma pillar in Iteri. He has offered the Captain of the Sea Wolves 5 crowns to deal with it and hopes other loyal Holbergers will add to the sum.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Seventh Wave's route ran through Mournwold, and even dour Marchers among the warbands were stirred by Dawn's fire.

Urizen.t: Zenith is an Imperial territory again, and the Citadel Guard raised a citadel and renewed the Glass Labyrinth. Urizeni dreamed of a song, 'The Darkest Road', which strengthened their resolve and sharply reduced the number accepting Kaela's Gift.

The darkest road.o: In Autumn 384YE Imperial armies retook Zenith, holding Clypion and Iteri while the Hounds of Glory seized Lustri at heavy cost, trapping seven Druj armies in Proceris and Occursion. The page also sets out a major battle at the Glade of Night Enshrouding and six linked conjunctions across the territory.

Zenith/Clypion.t: The Empire held Clypion after the summer victory over Kavor Eyepeel, and the Citadel Guard raised a citadel of ice and black stone there as a refuge.

Zenith/Iteri.t: The Druj quickly conceded Iteri to the Towerjacks. A lone miasma pillar has been found at the Pallasian Steps, guarded by Druj and at least three tortured souls.

Zenith/Lustri.t: The northern host smashed through Lustri's Night-magic defences, and the Hounds of Glory claimed the region at great cost, sealing the Druj escape route. Linked miasma pillars at the Spire of Twisting Shadow and the Endless Stalker at the Rift in the Veil remain threats.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Occursion is one of the two regions where the Druj armies are trapped. Their generals are gathering at the Glade of Night Enshrouding for a Night enchantment, the target of the Sunday battle. Further conjunctions target the Field of Celestial Mist pillar and a poison camp near the Tower of the Fall.

Zenith/Proceris.t: The Druj refused to yield Proceris, defending it from a Spring-magic fortress amid corrupted waters teeming with carnivorous octopus creatures. Three linked miasma pillars and a marshling at the Plantation of Tall Ferns are conjunction targets.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the Valiant Pegasus had briefly resupplied in Bastion before returning to Zenith.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Thomas di Holberg's past and the Druj attacks on the city are recounted, and he argues Holberg owes the Empire its help.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj predicament is likened to the Black Thorns once trapped in Liathaven.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky and Seventh Wave circled through Morrow's mountains to join the attack on Lustri.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Seventh Wave's general planned to move through Mournwold on the way round to Lustri.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: tortured souls were first encountered during the Druj invasion of Reikos.

Sarangrave.t: With Lustri taken, the Empire controls the passage to Sarangrave. Druj armies trying to push through to it from Zenith would suffer heavy losses.

Spiral.t: Attacking Spiral is the only way the trapped Druj armies can easily leave Zenith.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Seventh Wave's planned route ran through Therunin, and a Druj break-out there would be tantamount to suicide.

Zenith.t: Zenith returned to Imperial control and can be assigned to a nation, though it has no Bourse resources and will be lost if any region falls. Druj armies, miasma pillars and tortured souls remain within it.

The day writes the words.d: Dawnish armies led the Empire's invasion, but tallies credited Varushka with 45.3% of land taken, Dawn 41.8% and the League 12.9%. The General Assembly upheld a mandate rejecting the contest. It could send a priest whose preaching would cut conquest gains in the Barrens by 20%. Assessors found that past Imperial massacres and the deaths of rebel leaders mean no effective uprising is possible for ten years. That could be shortened by the Winter Sun breaking chains, reconciling with the Great Forest Orcs, a Senate motion promising them the Heart of Peytaht, tolerating Freedom in doctrine, or the eternal Irra Harah. Dawnish, Varushkan and Highborn mandates could strengthen military units supporting the conquest.

Dawn.t: Dawn's armies led the invasion and cut the Barrens in two, but were credited with only 41.8% of the land taken. The Great Forest Orcs blame Dawn for the failed rebellion, while a Dawn mandate could give Dawnish units an extra rank when supporting Dawnish armies there.

Druj.t: The orcs of the Barrens regard Druj rule as a known horror preferable to death at Imperial hands, so no effective rebellion against the Druj is expected for ten years unless the Empire acts to rebuild trust.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly backed the contest for the Barrens, and a proposed mandate would give Highborn military units an extra rank when supporting Dawnish or Highborn armies there.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs' bid for the Barrens sparked the contest, and their Assembly vowed loyalty to allies over the challenge. Their Winter Sun army could cut a year from the wait for rebellion for each season it spends breaking chains in the Barrens.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: a Dawn Assembly mandate urged Dawnish captains to stop raiding Jotun-held Skallahn and turn east to the Barrens.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs and Montanians who fled the Barrens were granted rights to live in Therunin and remain close allies of the Navarr.

The League.t: League forces were credited with 12.9% of Barrens land taken. The League's earlier award of Holberg, after Dawn had fought to liberate it, was cited as a warning that the Senate decides who receives conquered land.

Varushka.t: Driven chiefly by the Golden Axe, Varushkan forces were credited with 45.3% of land taken, and the Varushkan Assembly urged its people to fight alongside Dawn. A mandate could give Varushkan units an extra rank, and Varushkan armies would escape the General Assembly's penalty unless it passed with a greater majority.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's long ties to Sermersuaq were cited as an example of a moral claim to a territory that carries no legal right.

The day writes the words.o: The contest between Dawn and the Imperial Orcs for the Barrens divided the Synod. Civil servants also found that the Barrens orcs are too hostile to the Empire to rise against the Druj for ten years, and several ways were offered to shape the campaign and shorten that wait.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: A Senate motion promising the Heart of Peytaht and its valuable weirwood grove to the Great Forest Orcs once the Barrens is taken was proposed. Such a motion would ease their fears and cut a year from the wait for an effective rebellion.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs long to return to their homes in the Forest of Peytaht, which spans the Barrens and Casinea.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg was cited as the city Dawn bled to liberate, only for the Senate to give it to the League.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan priests urged repaying Dawn for standing with Varushka in Ossium.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq was used as an example of Wintermark's moral rather than legal claim to a territory.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish military captains were urged to give up raiding Skallahn in favour of conquering the Barrens.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Prince-Bishop's mandate told the Empire to 'remember Skarsind' as a lesson against treating territories as prizes.

The Barrens.t: Imperial armies hold two central regions of the Barrens, but its orc inhabitants are bitterly hostile to the Empire and leaderless. Civil servants judge that no effective uprising against the Druj is possible for ten years unless the Empire acts to speed reconciliation.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Therunin is home to the Great Forest Orcs and Montanians who fled the Barrens after the failed rebellion.

The dead tree gives no shelter.d: Early rumours spoke of a Jotun invasion of fifteen thousand. Freeborn reports soon showed that the force was the remnant of the Hierro army: warriors and raiders escorting children and elderly orcs, with more arriving daily from Reinos and Kalino. They met no Imperial armies, but local Segurans took up arms, remembering the invasion of 363YE. The orcs had supplies only until about a week after the Equinox, after which they would have to scavenge or turn to banditry. The Senate or Synod could fund supplies, citizens could resupply them, and the Synod could send missionaries. The General Assembly appointed the Navarr priest Taryn of Exile's End to bring the Way to the orcs, funded with 100 liao.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Hierro showed no interest in joining the Imperial Orcs. Segurans who spoke with them found them ambivalent, and sometimes openly hostile, towards the orcs already in the Empire.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: early garbled reports wrongly claimed the orcs were the vanguard of a Jotun invasion, and they had crossed from Jotun-held Reinos.

Navarr.t: The Navarr priest Taryn of Exile's End was appointed by the Synod's General Assembly to lead efforts to bring the Way to the Lasambrian orcs.

The Brass Coast.t: Thousands of armed Lasambrian orcs camped in Freeborn Segura and would soon run out of food. Local Freeborn took up arms, recalling the 363YE invasion and generations of Hierro raids on their caravans.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: news of the orc incursion reached Sarvos and Tassato soon after the Brass Coast.

The dead tree gives no shelter.o: In Autumn 379YE several thousand Lasambrian orcs of the Hierro army, the Empire's recent allies, crossed from Reinos into Segura with their non-combatant families. They camped near Anduz and sent a delegation to Anvil to ask for Imperial support.

Segura/Anduzjasse.t: The Hierro crossed into Anduzjasse and set up a fortified makeshift camp twenty miles south-east of the partially rebuilt town of Anduz. They faced food shortages on its dry southern plains.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the nearest Imperial armies to the Hierro were in Feroz.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the nearest Imperial fortification to the orc camp was in Kahraman.

Kalino.t: Mentioned in passing: more Hierro orcs arrived in Segura every day from Kalino as well as Reinos.

Reinos.t: The Hierro army and its baggage train crossed the border from Reinos into Segura, and more orcs continued to arrive from there daily.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: news of the orc crossing reached Sarvos early, soon after the Brass Coast.

Segura.t: Several thousand Lasambrian orcs camped in Segura with dwindling supplies. Armed Freeborn locals left a volatile situation that risked turning into banditry or open conflict.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: news of the orc crossing reached Tassato early, soon after the Brass Coast.

The deepest cut.d: Although Sulemaine was never recognised by the Synod, her uniquely Urizen status means only the Urizen Assembly can mandate her tomb. A consecration to Wisdom, Ambition, Courage, Pride or Vigilance would permanently free Urizen from General, Nine and virtue assembly statements and mandates. A Wisdom aura would also bring a flowering of philosophy and let the Arbiter of the Four Winds oppose one Synod mandate each season. Clytemnestra's alternative Wisdom mandate would instead end the rift with the Synod. Severus of the Blinding Sun offered a consecration to Hate, allowing a second Urizen army but cutting Doyen of the Spires ranks. The Synod's only counters were declaring her a false paragon or removing the aura.

Highguard.t: Sulemaine hunted and executed Highborn missionaries and is widely seen as a murderous villain there. Hazelelponi offered a Highguard Assembly mandate to lead pilgrims to the tomb, which would likely turn Highborn opinion strongly against Urizen.

Urizen.t: The Urizen Assembly alone decides the tomb's fate. Most consecrations would permanently put the nation beyond the reach of most Synod assemblies, Clytemnestra's mandate would reconcile it with the Synod, and a Hate aura would raise a sword-scholar army at the cost of the Doyen of the Spires.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as a nation where Sulemaine is not well known.

The deepest cut.o: After the Urizen Assembly backed Herminius of the House of the Wanderer's plan to consecrate the newly found tomb of Sulemaine i Taziel in Peregro with true liao, this Wind of Fortune set out how such an inspirational tomb could be created and what each choice of virtue would mean. Sulemaine has never been recognised as an exemplar or paragon by the Synod.

Morrow/Peregro.t: The caverns Herminius excavated in Peregro are confirmed as Sulemaine's resting place and haunted by at least two ghosts of her followers. Severus of the Blinding Sun wanders the region.

Zenith/Iteri.t: Mentioned in passing: the newly built Crucible of Fate in Iteri was named as the site for a separate consecration to Prosperity by Bartimaeus of Zenith Ascendant.

Morrow.t: Sulemaine's burial site lies in Morrow, where the tomb would be consecrated. Any Synod attempt to strip its aura would face sword scholars there and need an Imperial army escort.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Urizen statements also urged the faithful to go on to Zenith to witness the Crucible of Fate being consecrated to Prosperity.

The divide between.d: The magistrates ruled that the rebels were still Asaveans, so fighting either side was illegal but trading with the rebels was lawful. A Vigilance mandate began listing Imperial units shipping to Nemoria. Lady Madrianna of the Blue Stones, through the embassy in Sarvos, insisted the revolt was not a slave uprising and urged Imperial support for the Plenum. Terentia, directing the rebels from Maragladia, asked for 50 to 100 wains of mithril or weirwood, to be carried by Sumaah ships. The Purple Sails highlighted lucrative trade at Maragladia and Timor. Franco i Erigo chose not to enact his Synod mandate. The Senate then legalised mercenary service on either side.

The Brass Coast.t: Prominent Freeborn were among those who received Terentia Comasigne's petitions for aid, and the Freeborn priest Franco i Erigo chose not to enact his upheld mandate urging Asavean slaves to join the rebellion.

The League.t: Prominent League citizens received Terentia Comasigne's appeals for help, while the Asavean Embassy in Sarvos lobbied the Senate and leading citizens to back the Plenum instead.

The divide between.o: In Winter 382YE the Empire faced competing appeals over the revolt of the Asavean satrapies of Marracoss and Emphedor: the Asavean Plenum sought continued support, while the rebel leader Terentia Comasigne petitioned for aid. The Senate resolved the question by making it legal for Imperial mercenaries to fight for either side.

Feroz.t: Had the Senate declared war on Asavea, the white granite trade through the Cavabianca Docks and the temples of Feroz and Nemoria would have ended; the Senate instead chose to allow mercenary service on either side.

Sarvos.t: The Asavean Embassy in Sarvos reached out to the Senate and prominent citizens on Lady Madrianna's behalf, arguing that the uprising was a political betrayal rather than a revolt against slavery.

The dose makes the poison.d: Guided by the Last Battle steading, nearly seven thousand Varushkans fought fragmented Druj rallied by Egrech, a self-styled het, at Razorhill, the ruined Holt of the Oak. Warriors of Dochas Weeping Glade, who bear Agramant's gifts, broke a Druj ambush. Egrech fired the camp, sacrificed his followers and fled west to the Upper Tarn Valley with his herbalists. The Golden Axe took five wains of Thimble weirwood. The Lower Tarn remains poisoned. The Apothecaries' Guild may cleanse it over two seasons at a cost of 30 thrones a season and heavy personal sacrifice. Highguard's herbs or healing armies could ease the cost or speed the work.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish knights are recalled as having helped save Peakedge Stead earlier in the war.

Druj.t: The Druj lost the Lower Tarn Valley and Egrech's Blackrazor rabble was burned or scattered at Razorhill. They still hold Peakedge Song, the Upper Tarn Valley and East Ashes.

Highguard.t: Highguard could supply herbs from High Chalcis to remove the treasury's cost of cleansing the poison, at the expense of Reikos's bounty and the High Herbalist of Sybella. The Valiant Pegasus could speed the cleansing.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj frenzy drug Warspice is noted as the preparation Imperial Orcs call Warming Armour.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun-held Liathaven is cited as a territory once troubled by a vallorn dividing it, as Therunin now is.

Navarr.t: Holdout Navarr steadings welcomed the Golden Axe as cousins and as proof they had not been forgotten. Dochas Weeping Glade's Agramant-tainted warriors turned the battle at Razorhill, and the Willowjoy thorns were cut down for consorting with Wasteland beasts.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Axe began its march from the Turan Flats of Sarangrave, where the route east is sealed against the Druj.

Varushka.t: The Golden Axe under Vojsuli Cherenkov won the Lower Tarn Valley and deepened bonds with the Navarr. It lost up to three hundred soldiers, mostly to poison, and its general received five wains of weirwood.

Wintermark.t: The Bloodcloaks of Wintermark are named as one army that could use its physicks to halve the time needed to cleanse the poison, protected by the Winter ritual Why Sulemaine Walked Away From The Baker.

The dose makes the poison.o: In Autumn 388YE the Golden Axe of Varushka marched from the Bleaks into the poisoned Lower Tarn Valley of Therunin, broke the Druj warlord Egrech's stronghold at Razorhill and claimed the region for the Empire. They lost perhaps three hundred soldiers, mostly to the lingering poison of the Sephals Cauldron.

Sarangrave/Turan Flats.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Axe marched up out of the Turan Flats, fording the Unnamed River at Turan on their way north.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: Imperial forces could pull back to Hope's Rest and attack the Upper Tarn Valley from there, avoiding the poison but needing a new beachhead.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: The Golden Axe stopped at the Last Battle Wayhouse, whose steading guided them south, and cut tree trunks on the edge of the Bleaks to bridge Razorhill's poisoned moat. Resentful Karass orcs watched but neither helped nor hindered.

Therunin/East Ashes.t: The Druj still hold East Ashes around the Feverwater Docks, cut off from the north by the vallorn, so any fight there is a separate engagement.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Eastring remains wholly dominated by the vallorn. A Druj shipment of five wains of Thimble weirwood was seized on the raised road that once led there.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: Greenheart is completely dominated by the vallorn. Some Navarr steadings that withdrew into its depths survived and still strike at the Druj to the north.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Golden Axe claimed the region after destroying Razorhill, but it remains poisoned and will inflict 250 casualties on any Imperial army passing through or fighting there. The Apothecaries' Guild may choose to cleanse it.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: The Druj still control Peakedge Song, whose warlords traded herbs for Egrech's hoarded weirwood and heard the drums warning of the Empire's approach.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: Mentioned in passing: Sweetglades is listed among the regions completely dominated by the vallorn.

Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley.t: Egrech fled here with his herbalists and core supporters, and the Druj still hold the region. Any Imperial attack from the Lower Tarn beachhead would suffer the poison's effects.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: its vallorn is cited as creating a strategic challenge similar to the vallorn band now splitting Therunin.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: it is noted as a territory where a dividing vallorn once caused similar strategic problems.

Reikos.t: The bounty of Reikos can no longer simply be redirected to cure the poison. If the Benefactor of High Chalcis commits Highguard's herbs instead, the Gardens of High Chalcis would yield nothing until the cleansing ends.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Axe set out from the Turan Flats, and the Druj route east into Sarangrave is noted as sealed by the vallorn and the Empire.

The Barrens.t: The Last Battle Wayhouse in the Barrens provided the scouts and intelligence key to the victory. Hope's Rest offers an alternative, poison-free route to attack the Upper Tarn Valley.

Therunin.t: The Empire now holds the Lower Tarn Valley, the Druj hold three regions and the vallorn three, so no single force controls the territory. Agramant's influence lingers among the remaining Navarr but has not worsened this season.

The falling sky.d: Axos refused to send delegates until its dispute with the Empire was resolved. The Commonwealth and Sumaah asked to postpone the Pact meeting to the Summer Solstice. The Commonwealth claimed the Tears of the Moon in Rachensgrab and welcomed gifts of mithril, weirwood or white granite. A Grendel force torched Issyk's docks, and the Eastern Broker lost or downgraded Axou trade ministries. After Asavea's declaration of war, unconfirmed rumours told of warships striking Sarvos, Siroc or Trivento. The Sarcophan opened Betovering Docks to Imperial fleets and urged the Gjullit to keep their Pallas Docks offer open. Merchant-prince Vito Danierri de Sarvos offered to carry ambassadors' letters unread.

Grendel.t: A large Grendel force sacked Issyk's docks, looting warehouses and burning the piers, apparently in anger at Axou sanctions and Axos siding with the Empire. The raid damaged Imperial trade with the Axou.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Accalon of Felix's Watch of Highguard is named as Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Pakt of the Imperial Orcs is named as Ambassador to Asavea, the nation now at war with the Empire.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Fintan Nighthaven of Navarr is named as Ambassador to Axos, whose people are boycotting the Liberty Pact meeting and refusing to send delegates.

The League.t: League lands were at the centre of rumours of an Asavean naval attack on Sarvos or Trivento. Sarcophan families showed interest in the idle Cavabianca Docks, and Vito Danierri de Sarvos of the Golden Sugar cartel offered to carry ambassadors' letters. Lucia Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato is named as Ambassador to the Commonwealth.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is listed among the neighbouring nations whose closeness gives them outsized influence over the Empire.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Thalia of Netherwatch, Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves, persuaded the Sarcophan to have the Gjullit keep their Pallas Docks offer open another season. Ariadne of Urizen is named as Ambassador to Jarm, which has severed ties with the Empire.

The falling sky.o: A spring 385YE round-up of the Empire's foreign relations: the Liberty Pact summit collapsed after Axos boycotted it, Grendel raiders burned the docks at Issyk, and rumours spread of an Asavean surprise attack on the Imperial coast. Elsewhere the Sarcophan Delves warmed further to the Empire.

Bay of Catazar.t: In the islands of Rachensgrab, the Commonwealth has claimed the Tears of the Moon and is working with freed former slaves to restore order. It has asked wealthy Imperials for gifts of mithril, weirwood or white granite to help rebuild.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is named among the smaller neighbouring nations that hold unexpected influence over the Empire.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos was among the places rumoured to have been struck by Asavean warships, though no reports were confirmed. The merchant-prince Vito Danierri de Sarvos offered to carry ambassadors' letters abroad.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the page refers readers to opportunities concerning Faraden that arose from the Sea of Snow mapping expedition.

The fate of the many.d: Unless the Assembly intervened, most Urizeni would leave Spiral for Zenith, Morrow and Redoubt, abandoning its spires. The Assembly could back one of several competing mandates. Caela of the Tower of the Silver Flame urged people to stay until the League lost Spiral to the Grendel, which would weaken the Citadel Guard there. Agathea urged magicians to join the League and shape Apulian. Hector of Tropaion's alternative proposed staying apart in enclaves. Separate mandates would either share the secret of the Block with the League or withhold all aid; if neither passed, new commissions there would cost 25% more in labour. Sadogua offered to move one thing out of Spiral. Sung offered to create an Oblivion Sentinel title and mithril sculptures.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: bitter Urizeni compared the loss of Spiral to the "theft" of Holberg from Dawn.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua is noted for past boons helping Urizen against the Druj.

Grendel.t: With the peace treaty about to end, Caela predicted a Grendel invasion of Spiral to punish Kaliact's followers. The Urizen had never shared the secret of the Block with them, though sharing it with the League would likely spread it to the Grendel too.

The League.t: The League was taking on a territory its Urizeni residents largely resented. Its fate there could turn on whether Urizen magicians joined it in Apulian, shared the secret of the Block, or withheld aid, raising building costs and cutting taxation.

Urizen.t: Urizen faced losing a land it had claimed since before the Empire. Its Assembly had to choose between mandates to stay, join the League, or secede in enclaves, while Sung offered a new national title of Oblivion Sentinel to keep watch over the Black Plateau.

The fate of the many.o: After the Senate assigned Spiral to the League, the territory's Urizeni inhabitants reacted with anger, relief and grief, and looked to the Urizen National Assembly for a plan. The Wind also brought offers from two eternals of Night, Sadogua and Sung.

Redoubt/Optarion.t: A mithril sculpture would stand in the peaks of Optarion above the Brilliant Star if the Senate created the Oblivion Sentinel title.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Attention was shifting to the burgeoning City of Apulian. Agathea, an architect still dwelling in Apulus, urged Urizen magicians to join the League and shape the city with philosophy and learning.

Spiral/Screed.t: The baleful influence of the Black Plateau in Screed drove much of the exodus. Sung offered to make the hidden spire of Oblivion's Edge the base of a new Oblivion Sentinel watching over it.

Zenith/Proceris.t: A mithril sculpture would be placed at the northern end of the Twilight Gate in southern Proceris, aligned with Oblivion's Edge, if the Senate created the Oblivion Sentinel title.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: its transfer from Dawn to the League was invoked in bitter comparisons with the loss of Spiral.

Morrow.t: Morrow was one of the destinations for Urizeni leaving Spiral, and its legacy would be bolstered by the newcomers' ideas.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt would receive many Urizeni emigrants from Spiral. If the Senate created Sung's title, a mithril sculpture would be placed in its peaks above the Brilliant Star, and Caela predicted that a Grendel-held Spiral would threaten it.

Spiral.t: Spiral's Urizeni faced mass emigration that would leave its spires silent unless the Assembly gave them a plan. Its future also hung on competing mandates over staying, joining the League, secession and the secret of the Block.

Zenith.t: Zenith, now the Crucible of Fate, was expected to gain brilliant minds from Spiral. It could host one of Sung's mithril sculptures and perhaps the remains of Damakhan's Forge if Sadogua moved them.

The fayre fight.d: Lady Griffonsbane invited the sixteen people who had fought in every stage of the Grand Tour to a series of one-on-one bouts at Anvil. The prize was a magical weapon made by the Moon Weavers of the Semmerstones. The Reeve, Trystan Tanner, organised a fayre around the contest, open to all. The Culwich Weavers gave a Watchers' Flute to Emmeline Weaver for 'Race for the Barrens'. The Hidden Prince offered the Twisted Torc, which brings one season of prosperity to a territory, to the new Knight-protector of Autumn. Bedegrayne of the Silver Nightingales asked the Senate to clarify the Challenger in Waiting. The Senate removed its tourney and made it an Assembly appointment.

Dawn.t: Dawn's nobles and yeofolk celebrated the Barrens conquest with tourneys and a fayre, and Rhydian de Rondell took the Grand Tour's final glory. The nation's Challenger in Waiting was recast as a Dawnish Assembly appointment without a tourney.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: only through Spiral Castle, home of House de Casillon, whose Reeve promised to contribute to the fayre.

Urizen.t: A Urizen sentinel was one of the few to complete every stage of the Grand Tour, and was invited to compete in the final contest at Anvil.

The fayre fight.o: In Autumn 386YE Dawn marked the end of the Grand Tour at Anvil with a final tourney among its most dedicated competitors, a yeofolk fayre in the Glory Square, the Knight-protector of Autumn tourney and a debate over the Challenger in Waiting. Rhydian de Rondell won the final contest, and the Senate made the Challenger in Waiting an appointment of the Dawnish Assembly.

Astolat.t: Torag Meliora, earl of House Meliora of Astolat, was the sitting Knight-protector of Autumn going into the tourney, and was considered a favourite if they re-entered.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Urizen sentinel who completed the Grand Tour came from Morrow.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only in Knightly Redoubt, one of the items the Silver Nightingales offered under a rejected proposal for the Challenger in Waiting.

Semmerholm.t: The Moon Weavers who dwell near the Semmerstones made the magical weapon for the Grand Tour champion. The election of Semmerholm's senator was held between the Autumn tourney and the final contests.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Reeve of House de Casillon, who hail from Spiral Castle, agreed to provide something for the fayre.

The final countdown.d: Statements by Aniera of Exiles End, Siân Eternal and Doctor Lysimachus stirred hopes of finally ending the vallorn, though some urged caution. The Navarr Assembly could mandate either total commitment or a decade of preparation. Failing to choose by the end of the Autumn Equinox would have caused a catastrophic loss of confidence. The Highborn Assembly could recall the grey pilgrims, and other nations could issue statements of principle. The war would begin once trods were cast in Béantal Dol in Sarangrave and in Kabanja and Visokuma in Axos. The Navarr committed in Summer, with most stridings leaving the trods and their armies rising from three to six. Highguard followed in Autumn, raising its armies from three to four.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Siân Eternal cites Dawn's questing knights, alongside the grey pilgrims, as having joined the Navarr cause to eradicate the vallorn.

Druj.t: The Druj had just invaded Therunin. It was argued that triggering the vallorn heart in the Sarangrave would spell disaster for them, forcing them to pull back armies to contain it. The Navarr must also time their trod castings so the Druj cannot take them down.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are noted as not yet defeated in the South, and Doctor Lysimachus warns Highguard to prepare for them on its shores.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly chose in Autumn 386YE to commit to the war against the vallorn. The grey pilgrims stopped walking the trods and returned home, and the armies Highguard can support rose from three to four.

Jotun.t: The Jotun, already attacking in the West and holding Liathaven, were cited as likely to be forced to divert armies if the Liathaven vallorn burst forth from its heart.

Navarr.t: The Navarr Assembly committed the entire nation to the war against the vallorn in Summer 386YE. Most stridings stopped walking the trods and returned home, and the armies the Navarr can maintain rose from three to six.

The final countdown.o: Following calls from the Navarr and Highborn Assemblies to act on newly discovered knowledge of how to destroy the vallorn, the Navarr and Highguard were asked to decide whether to begin the final war against it. Both nations chose to commit: the Navarr in Summer 386YE and the Highborn in Autumn 386YE.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: Navarr scouts were to seek opportunities to place trods in Béantal Dol. Casting The Dance of Navarr and Thorn here is one of three castings needed to begin the final war, and they must be timed so the Druj cannot simply take them down.

Bastion.t: A Highborn commitment to the vallorn war raised the question of whether to keep building the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion while the Empire's survival might be at stake.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: it is recalled as the place where a rare chance to weaken a vulnerable vallorn was lost because 'it was not the time'.

Liathaven.t: Recalled as Navarr land lost to the Jotun, with its steadings destroyed. Triggering its vallorn heart was argued to be a way to force the Jotun to divert armies against westward vallorn expansion.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is not named on the page; it is linked only as a Navarr-held territory affected by the nation's decision.

Sarangrave.t: Trods must be placed in Béantal Dol in the Sarangrave before the final war can begin. Triggering its vallorn heart was argued to spell disaster for the occupying Druj.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the recent Druj invasion of Therunin is listed among the military difficulties facing the Empire.

The first shot.d: Corey Wayfarer's mandate committed the Navarr to war. The war itself begins only once the trod network links all six remaining vallorn hearts, and the Sarangrave and Visokuma in Axos are still unconnected. More than two thirds of stridings plan to settle, doubling the Navarr army cap to six. That capacity will shrink if no new army is begun by the Spring Equinox 387YE. Each army costs 200 mithril and 75 thrones, with regional substitutions offered: artisan materials in Hercynia, weirwood in Therunin, and an eternal's aid in Miaren. Druj, Thule, Jotun and Axou lands are all threatened. By the end of the Autumn Equinox no armies had been mustered, and the Imperial Orc and Wintermark support mandates had lapsed.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is not named; it is covered only by the general warning that the vallorn will attack virtually every Imperial nation once the trods are joined.

Druj.t: The Druj hold the Sarangrave, whose vallorn heart must be linked to the trods. They are unlikely to cooperate and may tear the trods down, though they might be able to contain the heart.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Axos's lingering grudge over its failed alliance with the Grendel slavers is cited as a reason relations with the Axou remain poor.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc Assembly was offered a mandate asking the Ethengraw to set the Black Forge to equipping a Hercynian army, at the cost of their own forge hammers order. It was not raised and the opportunity has passed.

Jotun.t: The Liathaven vallorn heart is already connected to the trod network, and its eruption when the final war begins will be a huge problem for the Jotun.

Navarr.t: The nation has committed itself irrevocably to war on the vallorn. Most stridings are returning to settle, the army cap has doubled to six, and the nation now faces the costly task of raising new armies and completing the trod network with allies' help.

Thule.t: The vallorn heart in Sküld in Thule lands is already linked to the trods, so the coming war will threaten the Thule as much as the Empire.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the northern vallorn lies on the border between Otkodov and Varushka, and Varushkan opportunities to support the Navarr are covered in a separate wind of fortune.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark Assembly was offered a mandate asking the artisans of Runegrott to arm a new Hercynian army, at the cost of the Keeper's own forging. It was not raised and the opportunity has passed.

The first shot.o: After the Navarr Assembly voted by greater majority (464-18) at the Summer Solstice 386YE to begin the final war against the vallorn, many Navarr stridings left the trods and returned home. The nation gained the capacity to raise three new armies in Hercynia, Therunin and Miaren.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: The vallorn heart in Sküld is already joined to the trod network, so it will awaken when the final war begins.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: The Sarangrave heart lies in the warded ruined city of Béantal Dol, and a Spring regio must be found nearby to connect it to the trods.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: members of stridings that become steadings may take a new resource in Brocéliande without the normal charge.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is named as a neighbour of Hercynia and home to some of the Empire's most skilled smiths.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia can now support a new Navarr army rich in artisans from the restored forges at Treji. If it is raised by the end of Summer Solstice 388YE, artisan materials may be substituted for mithril at 40 per wain.

Liathaven.t: The Liathaven vallorn heart is already connected to the trod network and will become a grave danger once the final war begins.

Miaren.t: Returning Navarr are gathering in Miaren, which can now support a new army full of vates. Through a plenipotentiary, that army could seek the aid of one of five interested eternals.

Otkodov.t: The vallorn on Otkodov's border with Varushka threatens the Thule. Otkodov is also where Navarr smiths from Treji were once taken in slavery.

Sarangrave.t: The Sarangrave heart must be linked to the trods, which requires finding a Spring regio there. Only the Seventh Wave, the Narwhal's Spear or the Wolves of War could locate one, and the Druj may destroy any trods made.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a neighbour of Hercynia and home to some of the Empire's most skilled smiths.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens is not named; it is attached only through the general warning that the vallorn will threaten nearly every Imperial nation.

Therunin.t: Therunin, where Druj invaders are being pushed back, can now support a new army of herbalists. With Great Forest Orc help it could substitute weirwood for mithril one-for-one if raised by the end of Summer Solstice 388YE.

The flood and the storm.d: After six months in which no Spring regio could be drawn upon, the realm's magic returned with unusual force, blamed by some on a Fountain–Stallion conjunction and by suspicious goetic magicians on a primal Spring power. Magicians working Spring rituals through a regio could embrace the surge for added strength at the risk of traumatic wounds. Three opportunities arose: a mithril-inlaid Moonwell in Hahnmark, a garden sinecure at ruined Evenstar in Redoubt, and a granite-and-weirwood great work over the Eye of Serenael in Miaren. The Senate commissioned Seren's Whispering Garden. Meanwhile the Heart of the Tempest in Miekarova began to spread before falling quiet after the Solstice, as the flood subsided and the remaining opportunities lapsed.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel raiders are recalled as having sacked Evenstar in Winter 380YE, enslaving its healers and using its regio to unleash sea magic against Redoubt.

Navarr.t: Navarr magicians, masters of herding Spring magic, gained a great work when the Senate voted to build Seren's Whispering Garden over the Eye of Serenael to channel its power along Miaren's trods to the nation's steadings.

Urizen.t: The Urizen identified the ruined spire of Evenstar as seething with Spring power and were offered the chance to raise a sinecure providing crystal mana and healing herbs, appointable by their senators, though only the Miaren project is recorded as taken up before the flood subsided.

Varushka.t: Varushkans faced the slow expansion of the Heart of the Tempest, whose plant-like creatures were reported spiriting away lone travellers, until the woods became quiescent after the Winter Solstice.

Wintermark.t: Steinr runesmiths Hurik and Manun offered to inlay the ancient Spring well near Valashal with mithril, creating a Moonwell Runewarden title yielding vital honey, possibly appointed by the Wintermark senators; it is not recorded as built before the opportunity lapsed.

The flood and the storm.o: In Winter 381YE the six-month silence of Spring-aligned regio ended abruptly in a surging flood of Spring magic, empowering Imperial magicians at a cost and creating short-lived opportunities to build structures in Hahnmark, Redoubt and Miaren. The Senate chose to build Seren's Whispering Garden in Miaren.

Hahnmark/Valasmark.t: South-west of Valashal, the rune-carved Spring well turned thick and sweet, and runesmiths proposed a mithril-inlaid Moonwell producing a seasonal bucket of vital honey.

Kallavesa/Rundhal Marsh.t: Mentioned in passing: the marsh's edges serve only as a landmark for the location of the Hahnmark well.

Miaren/Serenael.t: The Eye of Serenael on the outskirts of Seren became a troubling fountainhead of Spring energy, prompting the Senate to commission Seren's Whispering Garden over it.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: The Heart of the Tempest in Mieriada spread slowly and its plant-like creatures were reported abducting travellers, until the forest became quiescent in the weeks after the Solstice.

Redoubt/Naris.t: At Evenstar on Naris's southern coast, overgrown herb gardens and mana-bearing fruit offered a brief chance to harness the regio with a web of mithril and weirwood.

Hahnmark.t: The traditional Steinr fertility well near Valashal filled with sweet, treacle-thick water, offering a brief chance to build a mithril Moonwell yielding vital honey each season.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Hahnmark well stands not far from the edges of Kallavesa's Rundhal Marsh.

Miaren.t: Surging power from the Eye of Serenael caused bursts of wild growth and weather near Seren, and the Senate voted to build Seren's Whispering Garden to channel it, promising crystal mana to herb gardens and herbs to mana sites across the territory.

Miekarova.t: The Heart of the Tempest began expanding a few paces a week, its strange denizens venturing beyond it amid fears of an unknown sovereign, before growing quiet after the Solstice.

Redoubt.t: The ruined hospital-spire of Evenstar burst into a flowering memorial garden bearing crystalline mana fruit, offering a fleeting chance to build a sinecure for an Evenstar Defender.

The gathering storm.d: Four Wrecks captains (Murchadh Lughaidh, the Black Corsair, the Reaver of Attar and Friar Arwenack) planned an Autumn ceremony drawing on the Lictors to form a navy based at Atalaya. Each captain killed would reduce its starting strength by 1250, and three or more deaths would prevent it entirely. The Turn of the Gyre coven sought to cast an empowered Thunderous Deluge over Madruga, and stopping them would end the Wrecks' large Spring rituals for a year. Scouts also found the Storm's Child figurehead and a Grendel Sand Mage holding the Chest of Sand boon. Wrecker raids threatened the House of Guerra, a Kruidenkenner caravan in Necropolis, and Spiral.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named in an out-of-character note as a threat that cannot reproduce the Empire's options.

Grendel.t: The Grendel spymaster Sea-Wraith supplied the intelligence, though scouts found he had withheld details, and a Grendel Sand Mage, Arhrun Fhearghes, held the stolen Chest of Sand. A Wrecks navy would threaten Grendel coasts as well as the Empire's.

Highguard.t: Wreckers landed in Highguard's territory of Necropolis to hunt a Kruidenkenner caravan, putting the Kruidenkenner Trademaster's herb supply at risk.

The Brass Coast.t: The Wrecks gathered on the Freeborn Plain where the Freeborn nation was born, and the Storm's Child figurehead offered a chance to upgrade a Freeborn fleet or rally families to revive the Freeborn Storm navy. Wreckers also threatened pilgrims at the House of Guerra.

The League.t: The Wailing Gyre coven, funded by Azzura di Cazarri, planned to curse Spiral with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea, and its senator, Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian, was charged with stopping them.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: one of the four Wrecks captains, Friar Arwenack, sails with a cursed crew of Mitwold sailors.

The gathering storm.o: In Autumn 386YE the Military Council learned, via the Grendel spymaster Sea-Wraith, that the Children of Wrecks were massing on the Freeborn Plain outside Atalaya in Free Landing, where four captains planned to bind their fleets into a navy. Imperial forces were offered objectives to stop the navy and a favoured coven, and to recover two valuable items.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: The Children of Wrecks massed on the Freeborn Plain outside Atalaya, where four captains planned to found a navy using the captured marina as home port, and where the Storm's Child figurehead and Chest of Sand could be recovered.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: A wrecker fleet landed in Longbeach and spent a week tracking the Kruidenkenner caravan towards the magazijn.

Bay of Catazar.t: A Wrecks navy operating from Free Landing would be able to strike coastal territories right around the Bay, and Kruidenkenner herb trade across the Bay was threatened by wreckers.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies were noted as having pushed past the Grendel in Madruga to enter Feroz.

Madruga.t: Madruga was the battleground, where the Wrecks sought to found a navy and the Turn of the Gyre planned to unleash an empowered Thunderous Deluge, while wreckers raided the House of Guerra, whose Hand, Ahshen i Fiel i Guerra, had to defend the pilgrims or see the sinecure's output halved for a year.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Friar Arwenack's cursed crew aboard the Barrel of Best are described as Mitwold sailors.

Necropolis.t: Wreckers hunted a Kruidenkenner caravan nearing the magazijn, and if Trademaster Bernardo Von Temeschwar failed, the exchange would be limited to 24 cerulean mazzarine and 33 random herbs for two seasons.

Spiral.t: The Wailing Gyre planned to curse Spiral with a non-empowered Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea that would still cause widespread coastal destruction, even threatening Apulian.

The greatest city in the world.d: Holberg won the competition Harlequin spread across the League with 306 wains, ahead of Sarvos (212), Temeschwar (165), Tassato (76) and Spiral (21). Three opportunities followed: excavate before Holfried's walls (500 thrones, no slot); make Holmauer an uplifting Garden City (50 thrones, four commission slots); and develop the Flaxen Pillars, a weirwood grove the Sand Fishers found in Misericorde. The Senate commissioned the Garden City, now begun, and, after a League Synod statement by Isaia Davonne di Sarvos, the Flaxen Pillars as an auctioned national League seat. Hildebrand von Holberg's judgement led to plans for the Temple of Tall Flowers, a temple-orphanage. Frederick di Sarvos's Memorial of Flowers to Lisabetta began in the Necropolis, open to donations.

Druj.t: The Sand Fishers fear the Druj will covet the Flaxen Pillars' weirwood, so the new Burgher is charged with defending the grove and Misericorde against them; their earlier siege had left Holmauer in ruins.

Highguard.t: Work began in the Necropolis, with the Cenotaph and the House of Seven Mirrors, on the Memorial of Flowers honouring Empress Lisabetta, due for completion by the Summer Solstice.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: flower cuttings for Lisabetta's memorial were brought from as far away as Segura.

The League.t: Holberg was crowned the League's greatest city, the Senate began the Holmauer Garden City and commissioned the Flaxen Pillars as an auctioned League national Bourse seat after a League Synod statement, and a temple-orphanage was planned on a Holberg priest's judgement.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: flower cuttings for Lisabetta's memorial were brought from as far away as Kallavesa.

The greatest city in the world.o: Holberg won the League's year-long contest to see which city spent most on commissions and improvements, and the resulting surge of civic Pride brought opportunities to deepen Holfried's defences, turn Holmauer into a garden city, and exploit a newly discovered weirwood grove in Misericorde. Work also began on Empress Lisabetta's memorial in the Necropolis.

Holberg/Holfried.t: Holfried was offered a year-long, 500-throne plan to excavate bedrock before its walls, raising its fortification without increased upkeep or a commission slot; the opportunity can be taken at any time.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: The Senate commissioned the transformation of Holmauer into an uplifting Garden City, which has begun but needs more money and commissions to finish, and the Temple of Tall Flowers orphanage is planned at its centre.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: The Sand Fishers found the Flaxen Pillars weirwood grove here, and the Senate commissioned its development as an auctioned League Bourse seat producing 22 weirwood a season and charged with defending the region from the Druj.

Holberg/The Morass.t: Mentioned in passing: seeping groundwater from the Morass adds to Misericorde's damp, favouring kiln-drying of the weirwood.

Holberg.t: Holberg won the contest comfortably, hung a banner proclaiming its greatness, and gained plans to deepen Holfried's defences, a Garden City under way in Holmauer, the Temple of Tall Flowers, and the Flaxen Pillars weirwood seat in Misericorde.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: cuttings from Kallavesa were among the flowers arranged for Lisabetta's memorial.

Necropolis.t: Construction of the Memorial of Flowers, a gold-veined green marble wall around a lily-studded reflecting pool, began quietly in the Black City, with donations accepted until the Summer Solstice.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos came a respectable second with 212 wains, and Sarvosans were prominent elsewhere: Isaia Davonne di Sarvos's Synod statement shaped the Flaxen Pillars seat and Frederick di Sarvos designed Lisabetta's memorial.

Spiral.t: Spiral came last in the contest, investing just 21 wains in total.

Tassato.t: Tassato finished fourth in the contest with 76 wains invested.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar finished a close third with 165 wains invested, including 30 wains of weirwood.

The Semmerlak.t: Mentioned in passing: cold wet winds off the Semmerlak keep Misericorde damp, which is why the Sand Fishers want to kiln-dry the weirwood.

The greatest plurality.d: Estella Lucati's sermon urged the Empire to make destroying the vallorn its foremost Ambition. Rival judgements favouring Asavea, the Grand Inspiration, the vallorn, or all four goals at once failed. A call to defeat the Druj first won a majority but not a greater majority. Sofia i Tiera i Riqueza of Feroz argued this plurality is a strength and proposed a mandate turning citizens towards their national and virtue assemblies. Rhubarb Ironwood offered a competing mandate reaffirming the General Assembly. Saul, exarch of the Stone Cliffs, secured seasonal donations of mithril, white granite and weirwood to the Virtue fund. A dead Freeborn dhomiro also bequeathed 82 thrones to the fund.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Sofia cites Dawn, alongside Urizen and Highguard, as a nation that might see defeating the Druj as more important than any other goal.

Druj.t: The Synod's call to defeat the Druj first drew majority support but fell short of a greater majority. The faithful therefore did not unite behind war on the Druj as the Empire's single greatest Ambition.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Sofia, a Loyal Freeborn, says she would rather her congregants devoted their energies to defeating the Grendel.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is named as a nation that might favour defeating the Druj, and Renovating Bastion appeared in a failed all-four judgement.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr statement laments that Liathaven, then held by the Jotun, is long lost.

Navarr.t: Harwyn Eternal described Navarr as at its weakest ebb in a decade and called for Imperial aid to rebuild it. The Navarr desire to destroy the vallorn was not adopted as the Empire's single Ambition.

Urizen.t: Urizen has rejected the General Assembly's authority, so Sofia's mandate would not affect its citizens unless it passed with a greater majority.

Varushka.t: Varushka has rejected the General Assembly's authority, so Sofia's mandate would leave it unmoved unless it passed with a greater majority.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark has rejected the General Assembly's authority, so its citizens would not turn to their national or virtue assemblies under Sofia's mandate without a greater majority.

The greatest plurality.o: After the Archbishop of Capodomus's sermon, the Synod's General Assembly failed to unite behind a single great Ambition for the Empire, splitting its votes between the Druj, the vallorn, Asavea and other goals. This prompted two competing proposed mandates on assembly authority and new donations of wains and money to the Virtue fund.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Yosephus Morningson's failed judgement listed Renovate Bastion among four goals for the Empire to pursue at once.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Sofia i Tiera i Riqueza is a sutannir from Feroz who would rather see her home reclaimed than the vallorn destroyed.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Harwyn Eternal's statement describes Liathaven as long lost.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Harwyn Eternal's statement describes Therunin as under the heel of the Druj.

The hammer and the anvil song.d: Faraden and Axou apothecaries planned a market for narcotic concoctions outside the Forge. Wintermark runesmith Leofraed the Deft proposed a season-long exchange of crafts, and the herald Brazen sought an Anvil auction house to sell three wild-card invitations to Basileus Flint's Game of Cunning and Curses. Varushkan warden Vesela Lechovic brought a sword from the Forest of Ulnak, believed to date from the Freedom Heresy, seeking magical confirmation before auction. The displaced house de Coyne offered talismans and Raise the Standard of War for beggar's lye. Six Imperial weirwood seats and other titles were auctioned, while national titles went to the Tally of the Votes. Visitors met with varying success.

Dawn.t: Ser Sevelan de Coyne and seneschal Robin Counter, from a house driven out of Dawnguard and now camping in Ulvenholm, came to Anvil to trade Summer talismans and rituals for beggar's lye, and hoped to visit the Dawnish camp.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as having displaced house de Coyne from Dawnguard, and the sword was taken while fighting in their territory of Ulnak.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn apothecaries appear only in the in-character story, and the Great Forest at Reikos was one of the weirwood seats auctioned.

Imperial Orcs.t: Orc military captains could elect the Four Seasons' Boneweaver and appoint the vacant Bearer of the Imperial Orc Wayleave through the Tally of the Votes.

Navarr.t: Navarr herb garden owners were to choose who controls the Thimble, the nation's own weirwood Bourse seat, for the coming year.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark runesmith Leofraed the Deft proposed an exchange of hand-made crafts between citizens, to be completed at the Spring Equinox, as a show of the Empire's Pride in its artisans.

The hammer and the anvil song.o: Over the Winter Solstice 383YE, several visitors brought trade opportunities to Anvil, including a narcotics market, a crafts exchange, an auction of invitations to Basileus Flint's game, the sale of a sword from the Freedom Heresy and an offer of Summer talismans for beggar's lye. The Bourse's weirwood seats and several national titles were also up for appointment.

Semmerholm/Ulvenholm.t: What remained of house de Coyne was camped in Ulvenholm, halfway between Arnet and the Pits of Brychel, from where Ser Sevelan set out for Anvil.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnguard is named as the former home from which the Druj drove house de Coyne.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Varushkan warden Vesela Lechovic came by a sword with a spiritual aura while fighting here with the Golden Axe, and believed it to be a weapon from the Freedom Heresy.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest at Reikos was among the six Imperial weirwood seats offered at the public auction.

Semmerholm.t: The remnants of house de Coyne were sheltering in Semmerholm, camped in pavilions and tents, after losing their lands in Dawnguard.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: house de Coyne is described as having been displaced from Dawnguard in the Barrens by the Druj.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: the Weirwater Vales weirwood seat was among the six Imperial seats offered at the public auction.

The hard way.d: Lucati's sermon, delivered in the Atrium of Golden Light, spread across the Empire through pilgrims and Sarvos pamphlets. Drawing on work at the Great Library of Hacynian, it argued that destroying the vallorn was achievable within a decade if the Empire united. The General Assembly could enact a mandate, sending a named priest with 250 liao, urging the faithful to focus on the vallorn above all else. Only with a greater majority would it create new opportunities against the vallorn. The price was steep: no new opportunities against the Druj or for converting the Asaveans, and muted appraisals on those subjects. Only Lucati could submit or amend the mandate.

Druj.t: If the mandate passed, the Empire would stop seeking ways to bring down the Druj or invade the Mallum, leaving their evil to fester until the vallorn was destroyed, even though the Druj were already pushing the Empire back on the Eastern front.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the foes the Empire was then fighting, alongside the Druj and the Jotun.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the foes the Empire was then fighting, alongside the Druj and the Grendel.

Navarr.t: The sermon praised the Navarr's centuries of walking the trods against the vallorn and offered the prospect of the final victory that had eluded them for nearly a thousand years, if the Empire united behind the mandate.

The League.t: The sermon came from the Archbishop of Capodomus in the League's own cathedral, invoked the League's mantra "nothing great without cost", and was spread by Sarvos printers alongside the League assembly's recent words of support for the fight against the vallorn.

Urizen.t: Urizen's priests declared they would not support a mandate that did not reflect the clear will of the General Assembly, which is why a greater majority was required.

Varushka.t: Varushkan priests declared they would not support a mandate that did not reflect the clear will of the General Assembly, which is why a greater majority was required.

The hard way.o: After the true consecration of Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos, Archbishop Estella Lucati preached a sermon on Ambition urging the Empire to commit itself to destroying the vallorn. It offered the General Assembly a mandate to make the vallorn the Empire's overriding goal, at the price of neglecting the Druj and the Asaveans.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia was named as a territory in the grip of the vallorn that great armies would need to free if the Empire committed to the mandate's ambition.

Liathaven.t: Liathaven, held by the Jotun, was named as a territory in the grip of the vallorn that great armies would need to free if the Empire took up the vallorn as its goal.

Sarvos.t: The truly consecrated Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos drew pilgrims from across the Empire and beyond, hosted the sermon, and saw its printers spread the speech as pamphlets, while also housing Empress Giselle's completed resting place.

The honey offering.d: A coalition led by Oksana Lyava Pinavora offered 1,000 Thrones for the Senate to relinquish the Hunt of Alderei the Fair as a Varushkan national seat. It warned that any later reversal would be a betrayal, and it would favour the Night Quarry if more money were found. A proposed Iron Roundtower near Delev would act as a mithril-buying ministry. Belakov the Wolf of Karsk vetted about 150 refugees freed from the Druj. Some 140 settled in Karsk, three proved to be monsters and about six remain unaccounted for. A commission could reopen Karsk's mines and forests for these settlers. The Iron Roads proposal was presented again. The assembly endorsed a liao mandate promoting mines and forests.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the refugees were former Druj slaves from Ossium's northern forests, and one was corrupted by cannibalism in a Druj camp.

The League.t: Temeschwar's choice to join the League, taking the Fortress of Salt, is remembered as the root of Varushkan grievance. Some Temeschwari mine owners might sell mithril at the proposed Iron Roundtower.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule freed the Druj slaves and brought them to Ivarsgard, and Karsk is recalled as having been liberated from the Thule.

Varushka.t: Varushkans were offered ways to reclaim lost Bourse seats, build a national mithril exchange, settle vetted refugees and expand the Iron Roads. Their assembly endorsed a mandate to boost the mines and forests.

The honey offering.o: In Spring 383YE a wave of Varushkan ambition, spurred by Bartimaeus's mandate and Winter Synod judgements, produced several proposals to restore the nation's wealth: buying back the Hunt of Alderei the Fair, rebuilding the Iron Roundtower, resettling freed refugees in Karsk and reviving the Iron Roads. The Varushkan national assembly endorsed a mandate urging its people to prosper through mines and forests.

Karsk/Moresvah.t: Mentioned in passing: Moresvah is one possible site for the offices of the proposed Karsk mediating title.

Temeschwar/Metri.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fortress in Metri once sent mithril and salt past the Iron Roundtower to the eastern vales.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Karov is not named directly. As a Varushkan territory it would share in the nation-wide mine and forest mandate and the proposed Iron Roads.

Karsk.t: Some 140 freed refugees settled in sparsely populated Karsk, many at Ivarsgard. A commission was proposed to reopen its abandoned mines and forests and create a title to mediate disputes there.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: many Varushkans in Miekarova are especially keen to see the Night Quarry returned to Varushkan hands.

Ossium.t: The freed refugees had been Druj slaves in Ossium's northern forests. Under the mandate, citizens could take mines or forests in Ossium, and mapping it with a spy network was proposed as a step towards extending the Iron Roads there.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar's secession to the League with the Fortress of Salt is the old wound behind these proposals. Its mine owners might trade at the Iron Roundtower, and the Iron Roads could send more materials there and expand the Assayer's Guild.

The horror and the wild.d: Tales spread of miraculous recoveries and sudden riches, but also of a vanished vale and a Navarr wayhouse swallowed by the Semmerlak. Dho'uala's drowned emissaries demanded that criminals be cast into the lake and that theft from its depths cease. The Senate could pass laws on either point, and Dawnish, Varushkan and Holberg fleets remained penalised. Three opportunities arose: Irina's Grove in Skoremujac, where trapped mora trade herbs; a slaughterhouse at Tolvoli to feed blood-hungry dubik in exchange for potions; and the Deep Place at Void, where cabalists offer tempest jade. In northern Weirwater, the village of Surlac had been abandoned, and the Schlacta of Rot demanded both a Dawnish and a Varushkan champion.

Dawn.t: Dawnish fleets on the Semmerlak still suffered from Dho'uala's disruption, and Varushkan merchants taught a sceptical Dawn how to deal with the sovereign. Dawnish heroes were also needed at Surlac and to supply a champion against the Deadwood Knight.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: two members of the doomed wagon-raider band were said to have died in Ossium fighting the Druj.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: a lakeside Navarr wayhouse in Karov was swallowed by the Semmerlak overnight, leaving forty people unaccounted for.

The League.t: Holberg fleets continued to suffer a production penalty from Dho'uala's disruption of the Semmerlak. Holberg was also among the territories where a proposed law would have criminals drowned in the lake.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: a fabled tunnel was said to run beneath the mountains of Brez into Thule-held Otkodov.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: one of the wagon raiders was said to have died in Urizen-held Zenith fighting the Wolves of War.

Varushka.t: The Assembly's call to bargain with dark powers brought Varushkans both windfalls and disasters. It also opened opportunities at Irina's Grove, Tolvoli and Void, and left Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti responsible for meeting the Schlacta of Rot's challenge.

The horror and the wild.o: After the Varushkan National Assembly urged its people to seek out and bargain with the dark powers of their lands, Varushkans struck private deals that brought strange windfalls and terrible prices. The results included three commission opportunities, continued trouble from the sovereign Dho'uala on the Semmerlak, and two dangerous conjunctions in northern Weirwater.

Karov/Skoremujac.t: Hunters found mora trapped in a delusion of village life at Irina's Grove, trading herbs for trinkets. Restoring the grove's paths would create a Tender of Irina's Grove, an opportunity open until the end of the Summer Solstice.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Wagon raiders from Tolvoli proposed a slaughterhouse to feed the nearby dubik in exchange for Bloodwine Liquor, Blackblood Thorns and Darkwine. Unless it was completed by the Winter Solstice, the dubik might turn to human blood.

Miekarova/Perumaki.t: Mentioned in passing: the former guardians of Irina's Grove died fighting a plaguewulf in Perumaki.
