Volodmartz/Brez.t: The cabalists of Void apparently struck a bargain with something malignant beneath the peaks of Brez. They offered tempest jade to a Bredavoi Emissary if the Deep Place was commissioned by the end of the Autumn Equinox.

Weirwater/Sandling.t: The people of Surlac fled to the hills after something began picking them off. A Sentinel Gate conjunction let five people investigate under Areloe Larmallevés.

Weirwater/Wickmoor.t: The Schlacta of Rot emerged in the woods on the Karov border, demanding a Dawnish and a Varushkan champion. Twenty heroes could reach it through a conjunction, and if the challenge went unmet it would begin a murderous rampage.

Holberg.t: Holberg's Semmerlak fleets remained penalised, and the Senate could direct magistrates there to execute criminals by drowning in the lake.

Karov.t: A Navarr wayhouse on Karov's shore vanished beneath the Semmerlak, and Irina's Grove offered a commission opportunity. The Deadwood Knight stirred in the southern woods, and a law against taking from the lake would hit Karov's fishing.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: Karsk was listed among the Semmerlak territories where a proposed law would have criminals drowned in the lake.

Miekarova.t: Dubik nesting among the ruins of the Heart of the Tempest had begun trading potions for animal blood. Wagon raiders proposed a slaughterhouse at Tolvoli to keep the dubik supplied.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium was named as a battleground where two raiders died against the Druj, and was listed for the proposed drowning law.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov was the rumoured end of a mythical tunnel beneath the mountains of Brez.

Semmerholm.t: Varushkan merchants explained Dho'uala to the people of Semmerholm. The territory was named in the proposed drowning law and would lose fishing revenue if taking from the lake were outlawed.

The Semmerlak.t: Dho'uala's drowned emissaries appeared on ships' decks demanding that the condemned be drowned and theft from the depths stop. Port expansion around the lake was impossible while the disruption lasted.

Volodmartz.t: The cabalists of Void in Volodmartz sought help to build the Deep Place in exchange for tempest jade. Separately, a wagon raider was said to have died in a wayhouse brawl in Volodmartz.

Weirwater.t: Varushkan advice on Dho'uala found a receptive audience in Weirwater. Two conjunctions threatened its north: the abandoned village of Surlac and the Deadwood Knight's challenge.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: a wagon raider named Olag Gannovic was said to have died in Zenith fighting the Wolves of War.

The illusion of majesty.d: Estavus offered twice the usual warm ashes for ambergelt traded through Before the Throne of Estavus during the next summit. If she received more than 100 measures, she would lend bronze constructs for defence only at the Summer Solstice. The Revelry, former bandits who fought outlaws in Misericorde, sought a new patron through Erika von Holberg. Rodrigo von Mestra offered to teach the Autumn card game Threadweaver and staked his invitation to Prospero's game. The Sweetroot Bakery was put up for public auction. Laurel of Delving sought ritualists to study a bracelet found in Willstone that was possibly linked to the Lion of Arnet. The Dream-Singer offered Lashonar's Tears to the High Bard in return for new music.

The League.t: Two League-related opportunities arose. The Revelry, a Holberg company of former bandits, sought a new patron among the city's guilds and free companies, and Rodrigo von Mestra planned to teach Threadweaver at the League camp.

The Marches.t: The rundown Sweetroot Bakery in Sweetroot Town was put up for public auction because its owner, Thomas Marrowdene, needed a new investor.

Urizen.t: Laurel of Delving, a young torchbearer, found an old magical bracelet with rumoured links to the Lion of Arnet. They meant to seek out Urizen's egregore, along with autumn and day ritualists and sentinels, to study it.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: grimnir from Hahnmark were said to have kept the Sweetroot Bakery afloat by buying its sweetwater.

The illusion of majesty.o: In Spring 383YE several opportunities came to the Empire ahead of the summit: the eternal Estavus offered doubled rewards for ambergelt, while a Holberg bandit-hunting company, an Autumn card game, a struggling Marcher bakery, a mysterious Urizen bracelet and a herald of Lashonar each sought Imperial attention.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: The Revelry had fought the bandit groups still infesting Misericorde's forests and recruited others back into the Empire.

Redoubt/Willstone.t: The bracelet was found in Willstone, and early rumours tied it to the Lion of Arnet.

Upwold/Ashbrook.t: Sweetroot Town's poorly regarded bakery, criticised for skimping on licorice and under-fermented sweetwater, was put up for auction in search of new investment.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: grimnir from across the border in Hahnmark had been the bakery's main customers for sweetwater.

Holberg.t: The Revelry, a company of former bandits operating out of Holberg, sought a new patron among Holberg-based guilds and free companies.

Redoubt.t: A torchbearer uncovered an old bracelet of possible historical significance near their spire in Redoubt.

Upwold.t: The Sweetroot Bakery, a struggling business in Sweetroot Town, was offered for sale on the Bourse public auction.

The keys of blood.d: A Grendel Iontach raiding Wittal Grove sought to defect through the City of Locks. Janon, newly under enmity, sent heralds to curse Ossium and Sarangrave unless stopped. Sinokenon's mortal supporters came to Anvil fearing enmity. Arhallogen offered the Silver Chalice a way to poison a Grendel camp in Mareave for five hundred casualties. Surut offered generals aid, and Tharim's Ashen Knights camped in Karov. Agramant offered Navarri units an illegal venture to retake Therunin. Khobel Tavah set deadlines for Eilian Sweetwater's recovery and repeated its Everlasting Flame offer. Rhianos asked for Laroc to be ceded and charged the General of the Eastern Sky to stop a Druj sacrifice in Sarangrave. An Enterio quarry commission was also offered.

Dawn.t: Rhianos asked the Senate to cede Laroc's Tourney Grounds in return for 36 extra rings for Dawnish units questing or raiding from Astolat. Dame Aurum De Castellan, General of the Eastern Sky, was charged with recovering treasure from the Druj in Sarangrave.

Druj.t: Het Tavix Boneshaver's Druj were nearing the end of a vigil to sacrifice treasure to Agramant in Sarangrave. Surut was exacting ever greater tribute from the Druj and offering to help Imperial arson in Sanath, while Agramant-backed Navarri sought to retake Therunin from them.

Grendel.t: A Grendel mercenary company marched on Wittal Grove under Iontach Meddool Miniog, who secretly wished to defect. Arhallogen offered to poison a Golden Winds marine encampment in Mareave, causing five hundred casualties.

Highguard.t: Highguard's national assembly had urged its citizens, chapters and military units to aid refugees fleeing Therunin, so that Agramant would not be seen as their rescuer. Many of those refugees had fled to Reikos.

Imperial Orcs.t: Sinokenon was said to have favoured the Imperial Orcs since their nation's founding, approving of ordered legion life. Its heralds were particularly prevalent in the Unshackled's northernmost territory.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel ship slipped past the Fjorknae fleets, and Azoth's orcish heralds were at first mistaken for Jotun emissaries.

Navarr.t: Agramant offered Navarri military units an illegal Reconquer Therunin venture alongside Dochas Weeping Glade, carrying a likely death sentence from the magistrates. The Navarr national assembly had urged its people to support the refugees instead.

The League.t: A herald of the City of Locks brokered the Grendel Iontach's defection, and Guise could accept him into the League if he is rescued. A commission was also offered to expand the Arratan Gamble in Tassato.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Surut was indifferent to whether the Druj survive being crushed between the Empire and the Thule.

Urizen.t: Sinokenon's heralds were most numerous in Urizen, and Zenith's illuminates travelled to Anvil to lobby for it. Janon's heralds challenged Elagabala, Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path, in Sarangrave, and Naris was named as the possible site of Khobel Tavah's Everlasting Flame.

Varushka.t: Janon's heralds challenged Vellenka Vanyanova to stop a curse on Ossium, and Tharim's Ashen Knights camped near Vorota in Karov. Surut praised General Aksel Reznov Razoradze, and Wieliczka's vales lobbied for Sinokenon.

Wintermark.t: Grendel mercenaries landed in Kallavesa to raid the Healing House of Wittal Grove. Theowold Vakarsson, Grimnir of Wittal Grove, was offered a contract to defeat them and escort the defecting Iontach to Anvil.

The keys of blood.o: In Summer 388YE several eternals approached the Empire with threats, offers and opportunities. These included Janon's heralds threatening to curse Ossium and Sarangrave, a Grendel defector in Kallavesa, Agramant's illegal aid to Navarri in Therunin, and Rhianos's request for the Tourney Grounds of Laroc.

Kallavesa/Wittal Grove.t: Grendel mercenaries aimed to raid the Healing House of Wittal Grove. If the Iontach is not secured, the great work will provide no herbs until after the Autumn Equinox 388YE.

Karov/Wieliczka.t: Wieliczka's vales sometimes consult Sinokenon on rulership, and their representatives headed to Anvil to defend the relationship.

Ossium/Echofell.t: Janon's heralds kept returning to the Burned Glade in Echofell, where Vellenka Vanyanova was expected to confront them.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Rebekah's Leap in Naris may house the Everlasting Flame, and Khobel Tavah suggested pairing it with plans for the Lighthouse at Nikephoros.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: Janon's heralds took the field around Slow Worm's Hill, calling out the Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path to fight them.

Sarangrave/Turan Flats.t: The Druj held a vigil over treasure at the Stone of Thonkilch, and the General of the Eastern Sky was charged with recovering it. If they fail, Brokenhull's creatures would enter the region.

Tassato/Enterio.t: An outpost on the far side of the Arratan Gamble's largest vein was offered, adding five wains of white granite a season for three thrones more upkeep.

Zenith/Occursion.t: The illuminates of Occursion were described as long enjoying Sinokenon's favour.

Astolat.t: Ceding the Tourney Grounds of Laroc to Rhianos would remove business investment in Astolat in favour of military units. Units questing or raiding from Astolat would gain an extra 36 rings.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the wreckers' presence there makes naval superiority uncertain for Grendel mercenary companies.

Fjorknae.t: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel ship managed to evade the ships of the Fjorknae on its way to Kallavesa.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: Janon's heralds marched into Ossium across the border from the Forest of Ulnak.

Kallavesa.t: A Grendel mercenary ship sailed up the Gullet and landed near Wittal Grove, and its crew was marching on Wittal itself.

Karov.t: A legion of Tharim's Ashen Knights established a camp outside Vorota and intended to remain indefinitely, for reasons no one could learn.

Mareave.t: A Golden Winds marine encampment downstream of a Spring regio could be poisoned through Arhallogen's offer, costing the Grendel five hundred casualties.

Ossium.t: Janon's heralds threatened to curse Ossium with violent, unchecked passions unless the Shadowed Torchbearer stopped them. Soldiers of the Gryphon's Pride had failed to catch them.

Redoubt.t: The Empire may have chosen Rebekah's Leap in Redoubt for Khobel Tavah's Everlasting Flame, which would give the region a haunted quality and grim omens of coming doom.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: many Navarri fleeing Therunin had taken refuge in Reikos.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Surut offered to help the Northern Eagle find further opportunities for arson the next time it infiltrates Sanath, if its general invokes his name.

Sarangrave.t: Janon's heralds threatened to curse Sarangrave unless Elagabala stopped them. Separately, the Druj were sacrificing treasure to Agramant here, and if they succeed Brokenhull's creatures would trouble its settlers.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel ship avoided the monsters of the Sea of Snow on its way to Kallavesa.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: as the Unshackled's northernmost territory, it was one of the places where Sinokenon's heralds were particularly prevalent.

Tassato.t: The Architects of Iron and Stone proposed the Arratan Surety, a commission to boost the Arratan Gamble's white granite output.

Therunin.t: Agramant claimed to aid Navarri left in Therunin, backing Dochas Weeping Glade's survivor settlement. It offered an illegal venture to retake regions from the Druj.

Zenith.t: Illuminates of Zenith, long favoured by Sinokenon, travelled to Anvil to lobby against the Conclave declaring enmity on the eternal.

The lake and the deep, dark woods.d: Dawnish, Varushkan and Holberg fleets kept suffering losses on the Semmerlak. The Senate's law against taking things from the water appeared to stop the lake spreading, but hoped-for port expansions would now need a Senate appraisal. Dho'uala was angered that the Imperial emissary at Surlac had refused to hand over a bargain-breaker. Suggested responses included an appraisal, historical research, questing knights, approaches to Summer heralds, or simply leaving her be. After the Summer challenge, Weirwater received its boon but Karov escaped its curse, and the Deadwood Knight stayed awake. It raised its slain foes into a warband of several dozen and, just before the Solstice, began killing Imperial citizens. Historical research might reveal a weakness.

Dawn.t: Dawnish fleets kept losing production on the lake, and Dawnish emissary Areloe Larmallevés's refusal at Surlac angered Dho'uala. Northern Weirwater now faces the Deadwood Knight's rampage, while some houses urge questing knights to defend lakeside villages.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story the bandits first mistake their attackers for Druj ambushers, and destroying the Druj is cited as one of the Empire's more pressing concerns.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the 'affront of the Grendel' is listed among the concerns some argue deserve more attention than Dho'uala.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story the bandits briefly think their silent attackers might be Navarr.

The League.t: Holberg's fleets continued to suffer the lake penalty, and a Holberg professor proposed that the Sand Fishers might know something useful about Dho'uala.

Varushka.t: Varushkan fleets kept losing production on the Semmerlak, and some lakeshore Varushkans opposed probing the sovereign's secrets. Meanwhile the Schlacta of Rot began preying on south-eastern Karov.

The lake and the deep, dark woods.o: In Winter 385YE Dho'uala, the dark sovereign of the Semmerlak, lost patience with the Empire after being denied her due and continued to take her tithe from the lake. Meanwhile the undying Deadwood Knight, or Schlacta of Rot, failed to return to slumber and began a growing rampage in the woods between Weirwater and Karov.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: A Holberg professor proposed that the Sand Fisher orcs of Misericorde might know something useful about Dho'uala, though any approach to them would need careful handling.

Karov/Duzekani.t: The Deadwood Knight has avoided Duzekani, apparently unwilling to face the scions of Cold Sun there.

Weirwater/Hawksmoor.t: Shortly before the Winter Solstice the Deadwood Knight slaughtered a band of refugees fleeing south from Cold Sun, north of Hawksmoor.

Weirwater/Wickmoor.t: Wickmoor was the site of the Summer Solstice meeting where the Knight's ban may have been broken, and shortly before Winter the warband slaughtered a merchant caravan there.

Holberg.t: Holberg's fleets on the Semmerlak continued to lose crew and cargo to Dho'uala, and one of its professors proposed approaching the Sand Fishers for knowledge of the sovereign.

Karov.t: Karov escaped the curse that normally follows the Deadwood Knight's challenge, but the creature is now killing in south-eastern Karov. Karov's Senator also withdrew, without discussion, a motion on the fate of criminals due for execution around the lake.

Karsk.t: People along Karsk's lakeshore are among the Varushkans who fear an appraisal would anger Dho'uala, and who will only cooperate with Lutomysla Niegoslava.

Ossium.t: Ossium's new port of Kostjyas Respite remained unmolested by Dho'uala, and its lakeshore folk share Varushkan wariness about probing the sovereign's secrets.

Semmerholm.t: Dawnish voices urged Semmerholm's senator, alongside Weirwater's, to call for champions to protect lakeside villages and vessels from Dho'uala's servants.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Nameless River is described as flowing east from the Semmerlak along the Barrens.

The Semmerlak.t: Disappearances of crew, cargo and boats continued, and Dho'uala vowed to keep taking her tithe. The waters stopped spreading, but port expansion stalled and would now need a Senate appraisal.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater received a boon after the Summer challenge, but the Deadwood Knight has since rampaged through its northern woods, killing bandits and then Imperial citizens. Surlac was where Dho'uala's emissary met the Empire.

The last assignment.d: The Celesti Lighthouse in Oranseri, Feroz, remains buildable largely unchanged. It would provide a rank one fortification, raise trading fleet investment, let Freeborn fleets guard Oranseri, remove its abandoned quality and restore a reworked Celesti Lighthouse Keeper. The Four Points fortification in Operus, Morrow, could be a rank two fortification, built in one year with a Urizen Assembly mandate. The original upgrade to Reumah's Rest in Necropolis was defunct. Mladen offered a cheap White Sails version, a rank three garrison with boats that can support Imperial navies, and an ambitious version with a warship flotilla able to intercept a barbarian navy. Only one can be commissioned. All are available until Spring 390YE.

Grendel.t: Grendel armadas, which often sail past Necropolis, could be forced into battle by the White Sails flotilla if the ambitious upgrade to Reumah's Rest were built. The southern coast forts were originally raised against Grendel invasion.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Necropolis could see Reumah's Rest raised to a rank three fortification, either as a cheap fort with boats or as an ambitious flotilla able to engage enemy navies off its coast.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn could gain the Celesti Lighthouse in Feroz. It would let their fleets guard Oranseri and restore a Lighthouse Keeper chosen by Tally of the Votes, funded by willing donations from Freeborn captains.

Urizen.t: Urizen could see the Four Points fortification built in Morrow. A greater-majority mandate from the Urizen Assembly urging Loyal sentinels to join the garrison could halve its construction time.

The last assignment.o: In Spring 388YE the ageing prognosticator Mladen Escovitch reviewed, at the Imperial Master of Works' instruction, three expired opportunities to fortify Feroz, Morrow and Necropolis. He found two still viable and drew up two new alternative plans for the third.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Oranseri would gain the Celesti Lighthouse bastion and garrison, lose its abandoned quality, and be defended from sea attack by Freeborn fleets on guarding voyages.

Morrow/Operus.t: Operus is the site of the proposed Four Points rank two fortification, costing 140 white granite and 280 crowns, with a bastion and a patrolling garrison.

Necropolis/Coursmouth.t: Coursmouth, home of Reumah's Rest, would gain the coastal quality through work on its cliffs and bay. Its White Sails garrison could then move along the coast and the River Couros, or become a full warship flotilla.

Feroz.t: The opportunity to fortify the Celesti Lighthouse in Feroz remains open until Spring 390YE. It would raise trading fleet investment in the territory by one and give it a garrison to patrol it.

Morrow.t: Morrow could gain a rank two fortification and garrison under the revived Four Points plan, which builds on the inspiration provided by the Three Watchers.

Necropolis.t: Necropolis faces a choice between two upgrades to Reumah's Rest. Either would make it a rank three fortification, and the ambitious version would add a flotilla able to intercept barbarian navies in its waters.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening in-character exchange refers to "Reumah's Redoubt" on the southern coast, but no opportunity concerns the Redoubt territory.

The last leg.d: Fleets that kept to the race gained a permanent Summer boon to their vessels, suited to scouting (Deosil to Mystery), questing (Straight on for Glory) or raiding (Widdershins by Riches). The Glory captains sailed a final day on the Sea of Stars, had their fleets upgraded, and were invited to a celebration with Rhianos's heralds in a Summer regio in the Shallow Woods near Woodwych. The Archmage of Summer was asked to find musicians for it. Other fleets were each guided to a cold black pearl, a rare Winter vis. Riches captains were offered two crowns per pearl, up to thirteen, to return them at the regio. The Purple Sails' Lorana i Maqez i Erigo offered four thrones for the best map of the newly charted lands. Mystery captains can now return to the lands they discovered.

Dawn.t: Many Dawnish captains, including Captain Gawain de Licorne and Sir Dragon, finished the race, most of them Straight on for Glory, and their enchanted vessels earn them a place at the eternal's celebration near Woodwych.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but one pearl was guarded by an immature kraken released into the waters off Feroz, which Grendel then held.

Highguard.t: Highborn captains Creed (Straight on for Glory), Miriam Daughter of Esther and Raoul (both Widdershins by Riches) gained Summer boons for their vessels. The Glory captains' celebration was set in the Highborn-held territory of Casinea.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Bloodcrow Reek is the only orc captain listed, gaining the Widdershins by Riches enchantment for their fleet.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the in-character story describes a ship that had sailed past Jotun waters on its way home to Meade.

Navarr.t: A large number of Navarr captains completed the race across all three courses. Those who sailed Deosil to Mystery, such as Juniper and Llyr, can now return to the strange lands they found.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast captains made up the largest share of the race's finishers and gained enchanted vessels on every course. The Freeborn Purple Sails, through Lorana i Maqez i Erigo, sought to buy and publish a map of the newly charted lands.

The League.t: League captains such as Danica Lidija van Temeschwar and Valentino Crass finished mostly Straight on for Glory. The Purple Sails planned to have a printing house in Tassato copy any map they bought.

The Marches.t: Marcher captains including Alix Flowers, Fancy Jack and Jeb of the Sails gained Summer boons. The in-character story follows Anne Sailor homeward to Meade, her crew fearing for friends and family in the marshes.

Urizen.t: Many Urizen captains, among them Cerewyn, Magnus of Starfall and Xenia, completed the race, most of them Deosil to Mystery, and gained vessels better suited to scouting.

Varushka.t: Varushkan captains such as Kostjya, Triska Markova and Witold Stefanovic Petrov finished the race on all three courses and had Summer magic woven into their fleets.

Wintermark.t: Numerous Wintermark captains, including Hakon Dunning and Hilda Sirens Scream Ursan, completed the race and gained permanently enchanted vessels.

The last leg.o: The Great Race sponsored by the Summer eternal Rhianos ended in Summer 387YE, with the captains who stayed Straight on for Glory claiming the winner's laurels and every fleet that completed the race receiving a permanent touch of Summer magic. Fleets that took no part each found a cold black pearl that the eternal is eager to buy back and destroy.

Casinea/Woodwych.t: The Shallow Woods near Woodwych hold a minor Summer regio where the sea can be heard on certain nights. Its borders were to open on Saturday evening so the Glory captains could meet Spume Sailor and the heralds there.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Race began as a request for Rhianos to sponsor a race around the Bay of Catazar.

Casinea.t: Rhianos's heralds invited the Straight on for Glory captains to a minor Summer regio in the Shallow Woods, on the far side of Casinea from Anvil, to celebrate and discuss future adventures.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: one pearl was guarded by one of the immature kraken released into the waters off Feroz, and a captain only narrowly averted disaster there.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: some Imperial fleets spent the season hunting monsters in the Sea of Snow, and each such fleet still found a cold black pearl.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the Purple Sails intended to give any map they bought to a printing house in Tassato to be copied and sold across the Empire.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Esteban Ezmara of Zenith Ascendant is listed among the captains who gained the Widdershins by Riches enchantment.

The lights of Temeschwar.d: Angered by the curses on Sarvos and Holberg, Merchant-Prince Alexi di Temeschwar of the Guild of Lanterneers offered 300 thrones, hoping others would add to it, if the Senate relinquished the Fortress of Salt as a League national seat. The Constitutional Court confirmed it could be appointed by vote or by auction, but relinquishment awaits a new Throne. Bishop Beagan Locular proposed a true-liao memorial to Ratibor in one of three possible sites, while bishops disputed whether his virtue was Ambition or Vigilance. Yermolay Lopakin urged historical research first. A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered a way into an unexplored cavern beneath Mellfort.

Highguard.t: The Highborn were widely blamed for the curses on Sarvos and Holberg, and the Highborn chapter of the Heirs of Lepidus could be encouraged to complete their study of Ratibor through a statement of principle.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: some scholars believe Mellfort was destroyed in conflict between the Ushka and the ancestors of the Navarr.

The League.t: League citizens could contribute to a purse to buy the Fortress of Salt as a national seat, the National Assembly was asked to state whether Bourse seats should be auctioned or voted on, and League bishops could settle Ratibor's virtue by competing mandates.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar's Varushkan roots are recalled, and Alexi's bid drew on a proposal by Oksana Lyava Pinavora and her patriotic boyars and merchants.

The lights of Temeschwar.o: In Autumn 383YE Temeschwar stirred with three opportunities: a guild-backed bid for the League to acquire the Fortress of Salt as a national Bourse seat, a push to raise an inspirational memorial to Boyar Ratibor, and growing interest in the strange ruins of Mellfort.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: If auctioning League Bourse seats proved profitable, the method could have implications for how the Great Pits of Ennerlund are appointed.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Mentioned in passing: the destruction of Holmauer Park is cited as a sign that League cities cannot afford complacency.

Temeschwar/Hanuri.t: Mentioned in passing: Hanuri is not named directly and is covered only as part of the wider Temeschwar territory.

Temeschwar/Locul.t: A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered ten people a way into an unexplored cavern beneath Mellfort, whose grief-easing aura has drawn pilgrims and would-be exploiters alike.

Temeschwar/Metri.t: Its forests remained haunted by spirits that tore apart bandits but had not harmed honest travellers.

Temeschwar/Vargat.t: Mentioned in passing: the scholar-priest Yermolay Lopakin, who urged research into Ratibor, hails from the village of Tornvale in Vargat.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the rise of the White City in Bastion is said to have drawn pilgrims away from Mellfort in the past.

Holberg.t: The attacks on Holberg, including the destruction of Holmauer Park, were seen in Temeschwar as an affront to the League, and the Fortress of Salt proposal was discussed in its salons.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: travellers on the road from Temeschwar to Vorota in Karov reported being watched by half-seen figures in the woods of Metri.

Sarvos.t: The curse-driven attacks on Sarvos spurred the Temeschwari to act, and the Fortress of Salt proposal was debated in Sarvos's salons.

Temeschwar.t: Its guilds sought the Fortress of Salt, its bishops weighed building a memorial to Ratibor at Ratibor's Gate, the Red Tower or a city gate, and Mellfort offered a mysterious cavern to explore.

The little things.d: Thule scribes proposed that the civil service consult foreign landholders before territory-wide magic. A Senate administrative motion would put this forward, applying to the Thule alone, to all foreigners, or to none. As an example, Tathenon the Gyre announced that *Three Blasts Upon the Horn of Victory* would be cast on Ossium unless the Ambassador, the Throne or Ossium's senator objected before 6pm Saturday. The Dragons welcomed Regrow the Land's Heart on Sermersuaq. They disowned the Night darkness over Ossium. Runa supplied a primer on oath-based Thule law. Stürmherra of the White Mountain Fire took Bonewall and the Great Pit, then declined further Imperial support. Two Thule warlocks sought Imperial heroes against the Mirk Lizards.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is named as one of the nations shipping food north to feed Otkodov under the peace terms.

Druj.t: The Druj lost Bonewall and the Great Pit to the Thule, and their routed armies were left seriously damaged by a Spring curse. They also sent their Mirk Lizards to take vengeance on a Grimfen Mire clan allied with the Thule.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Regrow the Land's Heart is said to be washing away the scars left in Sermersuaq by the coalition against the Jotun.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr sends food to Otkodov, and the surge of Navarri into Ulnak is said to have flushed out the Mirk Lizards.

Thule.t: The Thule sought closer magical coordination with the Empire and planned a Summer enchantment on Ossium to improve the Jaws of Winter Lightning. They also won Bonewall from the Druj, after which Stürmherra ended military cooperation with the Empire in Ulnak.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is noted as sharing a long mountainous border with Otkodov.

Wintermark.t: Kindra Surefoot of Wintermark serves as Ambassador to Otkodov and can halt the Thule enchantment on Ossium. The Dragons also expressed contentment with the Regrow the Land's Heart enchantment on Sermersuaq.

The little things.o: In Autumn 388YE the Thule of Otkodov remained at peace with the Empire. Through their ambassador Runa they proposed coordinating magic on shared territories, gave notice of a planned Summer enchantment on Ossium, ended military cooperation in Ulnak after taking Bonewall from the Druj, and offered payment for Imperial help against the Mirk Lizards.

Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest.t: Mirk Lizards, practitioners of the rite of excommunication, were trying to go to ground in Ghul'thak Forest. Warlock Krafvötn offered mana crystals to the Master of the School of Exorcism to root them out.

Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire.t: A band of Mirk Lizards was travelling to butcher a Grimfen Mire clan that had allied with the Thule. Warlock Tungjökull asked Rhydian de Rondell to slay them in return for mana crystals.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: The Unbounded Tower of Feresh coven planned to cast the Thule Summer enchantment at 7pm on Saturday, at a regio near the Silent Pines in Bonewood, unless the Empire declined in time.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, which lets captured or dying Imperial citizens choose a painless death, is said to extend into Brocéliande.

Forest of Ulnak.t: The Thule took Bonewall and the Great Pit from the Druj in Ulnak, and the White Mountain Fire under Stürmherra replaced the Earthquake Drummers there. Stürmherra then declared Imperial military support would no longer be needed after the Autumn Equinox.

Ossium.t: Tathenon the Gyre intended to enchant Ossium with Summer magic unless the Empire objected in time. Separately, an unknown Night enchantment had wrapped the territory in darkness and caused travellers to become lost, which the Thule denied causing and called ill-advised.

Otkodov.t: Runa explained that Otkodov has no single legal code; its society is ordered by solemn oaths. Visitors must obey any warlock's instruction unless it is overridden by someone of higher status.

Sermersuaq.t: The Dragons were grateful for warning of Regrow the Land's Heart on Sermersuaq and comfortable with its effect. It is gently healing the remaining scars of war.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mirk Lizards were first encountered during the invasion of Therunin, and Kaela's Gift extends there.

Verthandi.t: Mentioned in passing: Verthandi appears only in the further reading list as a territory in Otkodov.

The lives you love to lead.d: Bite, believed to be of Druj origin and smuggled in through Holberg, was linked to bravo violence in Temeschwar, Sarvos, Holberg and especially Tassato, but could be stamped out by next year. With a greater-majority statement of principle, the League assembly could have Empress Giselle moved from Temeschwar back to Sarvos: to her repaired tomb in Caricomare, or to Capodomus Cathedral for 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns, creating a Bishop of Capodomus. Her return would stiffen resistance to the Grendel for a year. Holberg's upper-city walls became the Empire's largest fortification. The Ilotari offered two leomarids in return for a Senate invitation to the summit against slavery.

Druj.t: Bite is widely believed to have originated among the Druj, and Holberg's newly completed walls stand as a bulwark against them on the eastern border.

Grendel.t: The Grendel sacked Sarvos in 380YE, attempting to loot Giselle's tomb and carrying off Teodore von Mestra's remains. If Giselle were restored to Sarvos, any Grendel invasion within a year would face stiff civilian resistance.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the question of interring Giselle in the Necropolis alongside other Thrones was noted as settled years ago.

The League.t: Bite fuelled bloody bravo clashes across all four League cities while the militia slowly gained ground. The League assembly was offered the chance to bring Giselle home to Sarvos and possibly have her recognised as an exemplar to inspire all four cities.

The lives you love to lead.o: In Autumn 382YE the militia and magistrates were slowly winning the war on the outlawed drug bite, which was fuelling bravo violence across the League. A movement arose to return Empress Giselle's remains to Sarvos, Holberg completed its great new walls, and the Ilotari of Asavea offered leomarids to the Imperial Menagerie.

Holberg/Holfried.t: Mentioned in passing: Holfried is not named, though the page's news of bite smuggling, the city walls and the Imperial Menagerie concerns Holberg generally.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Holmauer Park lay outside the new upper-city walls, but with such a fortification nearby it was considered hardly defenceless, despite some lower-city grumbling.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Giselle's repaired family tomb at Caricomare on Cigno could take her sarcophagus again at no extra cost, provided the Grendel did not conquer the island again.

Holberg.t: Holberg was the route by which bite entered the Empire. The city also finished its immense new upper-city walls and expanded the Imperial Menagerie, which now drew greater tourist revenue.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Giselle is noted as one of the few Thrones not interred in the Necropolis, a matter settled years before.

Sarvos.t: Bite was linked to bravo violence here, and Sarvos was offered the return of Giselle to her old tomb or Capodomus Cathedral, which would inspire its people to resist Grendel invasion for a year.

Tassato.t: Outside Holberg, most smuggled bite was ending up in Tassato, where several clashes between bravo bands had turned bloody.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar held Giselle's widely criticised tomb. Moving her would reduce the Guardian of Giselle's Tomb to 6 votes and 3 liao, and the city also suffered bite-linked bravo violence.

The long bench.d: Alders-Baart Sarcophans arrived from Crown's Quay with a sack of cursed items to sell. Lord Barien's heralds held court at House Del'Toro with challenge scrolls and invitations to rewardings. Jezda the Harbinger sought Alderei the Fair. Priests questioned the looting during the Chalonsio and Skallahn raids. Marracossans of Trajadoz, Asavean visitors, the Tamazi, Terun-Axou ex-slaves, Kaban traders, a Grendel game-master and Parnau's Hanus Kovac, seeking to settle the idle Pallas Docks, all planned visits. The Wintergard chapter sought help with strange events after the Syrene flood. Conjunctions reached the Ketsov Winter Market, soured by accusations of inhospitality, and Calvos, where visiting Sumaah were behaving strangely.

Dawn.t: Barien's heralds asked Solene d'Alba or another representative of House de Gauvain to confirm a completed challenge, and they hoped for hosts outside Dawn, Wintermark and the Brass Coast.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ketsov of Karsk are described as a former subject clan of the Druj from Ossium.

Grendel.t: Kayley, a Grendel Master of Ceremonies, brought the Broken Shore game Beggars' Lot to Anvil, running four games on Friday evening with buy-ins of 1 and 10 thrones.

Highguard.t: Members of the Wintergard chapter planned to visit the Highguard camp seeking help, and possibly inquisitors, to investigate reports of people in Syrene's Wisdom linked to the recent flood.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Tamazi, freed orcs of Axos increasingly embracing citizenship as Imperial Orcs, came to Anvil to meet artisans, academics and bankers and learn about Imperial magic.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: priests asked whether the attack on Skallahn was a virtuous response to the Jotun threat or an excuse for plunder.

Navarr.t: Terun-Axou former slaves who had asked the Navarr about their shared history planned to meet past helpers and anyone supporting their fight against the vallorn in Axos at the Navarr noticeboard.

The Brass Coast.t: Barien's heralds held court at House Del'Toro, Asavean 'priests' landed at Siroc, Marracossans of Trajadoz traded with Torres, and sutannir were invited to lift spirits in Calvos.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni spires were among those gathering, and Kayley's game met at the gate between the Urizen and Varushka camps.

Varushka.t: Jezda the Harbinger of the Seers of the Black Gate planned to visit the Varushkan camp to meet Alderei the Fair, and tensions arose around the Ketsov settlers in Karsk.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Barien's heralds preferred offers to host them from nations other than Wintermark, Dawn or the Brass Coast.

The long bench.o: At the Autumn Equinox of 384YE a host of visitors announced plans to come to Anvil, among them Sarcophan curse-sellers, Barien's heralds, a Varushkan seer, concerned priests, Marracossan exiles, Asavean 'priests', Tamazi orcs and Jarmish envoys. Sentinel Gate conjunctions to troubled Ketsov in Karsk and Calvos in Madruga were also identified.

Casinea/Syrwatch.t: The town of Syrene, flooded with Winter-tainted water during the Great Drought, saw unexplained reports of people inside Syrene's Wisdom mine that the Wintergard chapter wanted investigated.

Karsk/Lestasny.t: The Ketsov's results-first attitude divided opinion in Lestasny, and their interrogations and ejections of visitors, often draughir, worsened local attitudes ahead of their Winter Market.

Madruga/Torres.t: A bountiful season saw the Marracossan exiles of Trajadoz surge their trade with neighbouring Torres before seeking wider Imperial ties.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: Barien's heralds were to hold Gemma Brightsmith's rewarding ceremony at the Grove of the Thousand near the Semerstones.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: not named on the page; the link is through the discussion of the raid on the Asavean city of Chalonsio and Asavean visitors arriving by sea.

Casinea.t: After a Winter-tainted flood struck Syrene in Syrwatch, the Wintergard chapter sought help investigating strange reports from Syrene's Wisdom mine.

Karsk.t: The Ketsov clan's Winter Market in their new vale was marred by accusations of poor hospitality, and a conjunction let a small group visit.

Madruga.t: Sumaah Präster visiting Calvos for the Festival of Zemress acted strangely, and Marracossans from Trajadoz traded with Torres and travelled towards Anvil.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sarcophan Alders-Baart visitors were met on the road to Anvil from Crown's Quay.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ketsov clan, now settled in Karsk, originally came from Ossium.

Redoubt.t: With the Jarm embargo, weirwood stopped flowing through the Pallas Docks in Cargo, and Parnau's Hanus Kovac came to discuss their ownership with the Prime Factor and the Ambassador to Jarm.

Semmerholm.t: Gemma Brightsmith's rewarding ceremony with Barien's heralds was set for the Grove of the Thousand near the Semerstones in Axmure.

Skallahn.t: Priests questioned whether the recent attack on Skallahn was virtuous or mere banditry, and sought those who had sent forces there.

The long march.d: Shadrach's mandate set the pilgrims preaching against false virtues and eternal veneration, making it harder for such beliefs to take hold, though more hidden cults were expected to come to light. Dinah's mandate, carried by Able of the Shattered Tower, sent them to convert foreign visitors, at the risk of tension with their nations. Lilith of the Chantry's mandate caused attendance to fall at every congregation outside the Imperial Orcs, possibly for years. The Navarr trod extension into Sküld raised the open question of preaching to the Thule, which awaited a further Highborn mandate. The Assembly of the Nine later endorsed the pilgrims.

Highguard.t: The Highborn National Assembly defined the pilgrimage's purpose through three upheld mandates, and was left to decide whether the grey pilgrims should preach to the Thule or leave the orcs to find their own way.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orc congregations were spared the decline in attendance felt by every human nation, and few Highborn were keen to denounce them given their recent efforts for the Empire.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrians, who fled the Empire to join the Jotun after embracing the Way, were cited as an example of the faith's transforming power.

Navarr.t: The pilgrims' walking of the trods aids the Navarr quest against the vallorn, and the Navarr-negotiated trod into Sküld offered the only route beyond the Empire's borders.

The League.t: League congregations shared the loss of attendance as the pilgrims questioned human faith, and those clinging to Hatred in Tassato were named as targets of their preaching.

Thule.t: The trod extension into Sküld meant pilgrims might cross into Thule lands to convert them, which the civil service warned could harm relations; no decision had yet been made.

Varushka.t: Varushkan congregations suffered the same decline in attendance as other human nations, and the accompanying story follows a Navarr striding through Volodmartz towards Opascari.

The long march.o: In Spring 383YE the Highborn grey pilgrimage took to the trods in growing numbers, shaped by three Winter Solstice mandates of the Highborn National Assembly. The pilgrims set out to preach against idolatry and false virtues, convert visiting foreigners and question the faith of every human nation.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Sküld is reached by the new trods negotiated in the Thule peace, making it the possible gateway for pilgrims seeking to bring the Way to the Thule.

Volodmartz/Opascari.t: Mentioned in passing: the story's Navarr striding is bound for Opascari, waiting for the thaw before pressing north into Sküld.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Asavean and Jarmish merchants in every port on the Bay became targets for the pilgrims' efforts to convert foreigners to the Way.

Otkodov.t: The Navarr trod extension into Sküld in Otkodov offered the pilgrims a way into Thule lands, should the Highborn mandate preaching there.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr strider contrasts the trods of Reikos with the harsher trods of Varushka.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr strider contrasts the trods of Sarvos with the harsher trods of Varushka.

Tassato.t: Folk clinging to the false virtue of Hatred in Tassato were named among those the grey pilgrims would preach against.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr strider notes even Temeschwar is gentler going than the trods of Varushka.

Volodmartz.t: Mentioned in passing: the story's striding, slowed by inexperienced companions, crosses Volodmartz towards the border.

The long road.d: For four summits no one could challenge Barien. Once the conjunction passed, the ritual returned in a changed form: the Iron Duke now sets the contests, and willing challengers need a coven to cast Challenge the Iron Duke on them. The Challenge of the Endless Sea, offered through Rhianos' herald Latitude, has crews of four hunting the metal-skinned Adamantilus in the Gosgala chamber. The Challenge of the Frayed Pennant pits ten Imperial combatants against ten Jotun, led by Kjellaug Spearbiter and Oddmund Gunnesbarn, in a pennant-capture battle at the Emerald Glade in Southridge, Hahnmark. Those who yield must be spared. The winners may each choose an item from the Dragonforge, and extra prizes are offered.

Jotun.t: Two Jotun champions, Kjellaug Spearbiter of Kierheim and Oddmund Gunnesbarn of Fjorknae, have challenged the Empire to the Frayed Pennant battle and are raising a team of ten. Their priest Brynta welcomes the return of Barien's challenges as a way for restless newcomers to prove themselves.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named; the only possible link is the Steelskin prize, a Knightly Redoubt armour.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Frayed Pennant contest is staged at the Emerald Glade in Southridge, Hahnmark, a Wintermark territory.

The long road.o: After a year in which a celestial conjunction blocked the ritual Challenge the Iron Duke, the heralds of Barien announced that the eternal would now set his own challenges, offering two for the Winter Solstice 386YE: a naval contest against a Summer sea beast and a mock battle against Jotun champions.

Hahnmark/Southridge.t: The Emerald Glade in Southridge hosts the Frayed Pennant battle. Two teams of ten will defend menhirs in a patch of woodland and try to seize each other's pennants, and anyone who yields must be spared.

Fjorknae.t: Mentioned in passing: Oddmund Gunnesbarn, one of the two Jotun champions in the Frayed Pennant challenge, is described as hailing from far-flung Fjorknae.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark is the venue for the Challenge of the Frayed Pennant. Imperial and Jotun teams, with up to 80 spectators, are to fight a mock battle there under Barien's heralds.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not referred to; the word appears only in the name of the Knightly Redoubt armour offered as the Steelskin prize.

The mathematics of tears.d: The bedelaar huisbaas made slave trading a crime punishable by forfeiture and being made ongelukkig. Some slaving families fled to Asavea and Jarm, and their former slaves flooded the labour market. The Kruidenkenner herbalists offered more warehouses until the end of Spring, and an expansion of their Magazjin at Crown's Quay that would benefit four herb-buying titles. The Gjullit proposed docks at Siroc selling weirwood and white granite. Johann Van Basten offered 100 wains of white granite for 500 Thrones. The Vandersaar sought the ruined Alivetti estates in Sarvos and the Diepenbeek sought the ruins of Isember in Karsk, both by concedence. The Empire bought the granite after the Summer Solstice, and the Senate approved the Magazjin expansion at the Autumn Equinox.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel broke open Empress Giselle's tomb in the Alivetti estates during their sack of Sarvos.

Highguard.t: The Kruidenkenner already trade herbs in Highguard from their Magazjin at Crown's Quay. The High Herbalist of Sybella was among the titles to gain an extra herb purchase track once the Senate approved the expansion.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs in Skarsind are named as a northern trading partner for a proposed Sarcophan enclave at Isember.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr in Hercynia are listed among those a Sarcophan enclave at Isember would trade with.

The Brass Coast.t: The Gjullit family proposed building docks at Siroc to sell weirwood and white granite. The Vizier of the Incarnadine Satchel gained an extra herb purchase track when the Kruidenkenner Magazjin was expanded.

The League.t: The Vandersaar asked the Senate to concede the ruined Alivetti guild estates in Sarvos for a Sarcophan enclave. The Master of the Clearing House in Tassato benefited from the approved Kruidenkenner expansion.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Isember was destroyed in the war with the Thule, and the Diepenbeek expected an enclave there to trade with the Thule at Krevsaty and Urdur.

Urizen.t: Under the Vandersaar proposal, the Steel Fist's ilium bounty would rise by four rings to twelve a season if the Senate conceded the Alivetti estates.

Varushka.t: The Diepenbeek proposed leasing and rebuilding the ruins of Isember as a Sarcophan enclave, building on the existing Sarcophan Mooring at Ivarsgard. Varushkan mine and forest owners might appoint a landlord for a restored Sovereign's Heart inn.

Wintermark.t: The Diepenbeek expected to trade with the Winterfolk at Kalpaheim, and the Kalpaheim Tradeholder would gain a Sarcophan purchase track once its tradehall was complete.

The mathematics of tears.o: After the Winter Solstice the Sarcophan Delves outlawed the slave trade, and several Sarcophan families and guilds put trade proposals to the Empire, including warehouses, docks, a bulk white granite sale and enclaves at Sarvos and Isember.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: The Vizier of the Incarnadine Satchel's offices in Morajasse benefited from the completed Kruidenkenner Magazjin expansion with an extra herb purchase track.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule at Krevsaty are named as a potential trading partner for a Sarcophan enclave at Isember.

Karsk/Lestasny.t: The Diepenbeek planned to seek the help of the people of Lestasny so that their Isember enclave would not transgress the unwritten laws of the Varushkan wilds.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: The Kruidenkenner Magazjin at Crown's Quay was expanded after the Senate's Autumn vote, giving it and three other titles an additional herb purchase track.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule at Urdur are listed among those a Sarcophan enclave at Isember would trade with.

Feroz.t: The Vizier of the Incarnadine Satchel in Feroz was offered a loose partnership with the Kruidenkenner, and gained an additional herb purchase track when the expansion was completed.

Hahnmark.t: The Kalpaheim Tradeholder would gain access to Sarcophan bargains through the northern trade network if the Isember enclave were built and the tradehall finished.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is listed as a place where Navarr would trade with a Sarcophan enclave at Isember.

Karsk.t: The Diepenbeek proposed that the Senate concede the wolf-haunted ruins of Isember so they could clear them and build a Sarcophan trading enclave. Imperial captains would be paid to secure the area and guard caravans; the offer ran until the end of the Autumn Equinox.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is not named directly; its only Brass Coast link is the Gjullit proposal for docks at Siroc.

Necropolis.t: The Kruidenkenner Magazjin at Crown's Quay was the subject of an expansion requiring 24 wains of weirwood and 48 crowns. The Senate approved it in Autumn and it was completed before the Winter Solstice.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule-held Urdur is named as a place a Sarcophan enclave at Isember would trade with.

Redoubt.t: The Steel Fist would receive four more rings of ilium each season, twelve in all, if the Vandersaar enclave at Sarvos were conceded.

Sarvos.t: The Vandersaar asked for the swampy, storm-ruined Alivetti estates near Caricomare to be conceded so they could build a Sarcophan dock and enclave. They offered to spare Empress Giselle's broken tomb if asked.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a place where the Imperial Orcs would trade with a Sarcophan enclave at Isember.

Tassato.t: The Master of the Clearing House in Tassato gained an additional Kruidenkenner herb purchase track after the Magazjin expansion was approved and built.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Empress Giselle's body now rests in Temeschwar, and the League there is listed as a trading partner for a Sarcophan enclave at Isember.

The matter will be done.d: The manticore of the Untrod Groves led a procession through Dawn, gathering some fifty nobles, including Earl Valerie de Courcillon. Its backers were called the romantics, the brutal and the sinister; its opponents the romantics, the realists and the ambitious. Realists warned that any monarch other than the Throne would force Dawn out of the Empire. Alyss Retainer secured the Anvil arena for a noble-only grand melee, with the Challenger in Waiting expected to ensure a glorious contest. Emperor Vesna planted her banner and challenged. Her forces won an overwhelming victory. The page notes such a victory ends the matter but gives no surge of national Pride.

Dawn.t: Dawn's nobility split over the manticore's challenge, but the threat of a constitutional crisis passed when Emperor Vesna won overwhelmingly, was crowned Monarch of Dawn and the beast was slain.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: realists warned that Dawn's four armies could not face the Druj's nine or more alone, and the brutal faction promised death to every Druj orc.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: realists questioned whether Holberg's citizens would keep paying taxes to maintain the Castle of Thorns if Dawn left the Empire, and Empress Lisabetta's work for Holberg was cited.

The matter will be done.o: In Spring 388YE the manticore styling itself Earl of the Groves challenged for the crown of Dawn, and Emperor Vesna answered by challenging for the Rose Throne herself. The matter was settled by grand tourney at Anvil, where Vesna's forces won overwhelmingly, Vesna was crowned Monarch of Dawn and the manticore was killed.

Semmerholm/Estmure.t: Earl Sebastian De Marigny, leading voice of the manticore's romantic supporters, keeps estates in Estmure.

Semmerholm/Ulvenholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the tale of the challenge spread as far as the sacred walls of Arnet in Ulvenholm.

The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth.t: Mentioned in passing: the story of the challenge reached the Plains of Teeth at the Mallum's door.

The Barrens/The Untrod Groves.t: The manticore's procession set out from the Untrod Groves, its seat as self-proclaimed Earl, before it was slain at Anvil.

Astolat.t: The Seat of the Sun, the Rose Throne of Astolat, was the prize contested; it went to Emperor Vesna rather than the manticore.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: realists asked whether Holberg's wealthy citizens would still pay to maintain the Castle of Thorns if Dawn left the Empire.

Semmerholm.t: The manticore's procession passed through Semmerholm on its way towards the Crown of Thorns, and one of its leading supporters held estates there.

The Barrens.t: The manticore's challenge and procession began from its seat in the Barrens, where Earl Valerie de Courcillon's knights had been harassing the Karass in the south.

Weirwater.t: The manticore's procession marched through Weirwater, and the story of its challenge spread across Weirwater's moors.

The money goes round.d: Building on the new Chair of the Wolf and Aureliana di Sarvos's Spring Equinox Assembly call for a city to be first to 100 Thrones in tax, Fransesca reworked the idea. The winner will be the city where the most wains are spent on commissions and personal resources between the Winter Solstice 384YE and the 385YE solstice; Imperial armies do not count. The civil service will publish a seasonal 'League table'. For the year, upgrading business resources in the League costs one wain of white granite less. Nine opportunities, many previously lapsed, can be commissioned until the end of the Autumn Equinox 385YE. They include sea defences, a cathedral and a university renovation in Sarvos, a Colossus of Tassato and a University of Temeschwar.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the revived Holmauer fortifications were originally proposed in 380YE as defences designed to kill the Druj.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the uncertain Grendel peace treaty is cited as a reason for Sarvos sea defences, and the Grendel are noted as having looted Capodomus Cathedral.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: a restored Capodomus Cathedral is said to rival the Basilica of Seven Doors in Bastion.

The League.t: The League's four cities are pitted against each other for a year to prove which is greatest through investment. League businesses gain cheaper upgrades, and several commission opportunities are now open in League territories.

The money goes round.o: Merchant Prince Fransesca di Matos, with the Harlequin's backing, launched a year-long competition from Winter 384YE to find which of the League's four great cities invests the most wains in commissions and resources. The enthusiasm made business upgrades cheaper and revived several lapsed commission opportunities.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Brechtje Van Holberg's 380YE plan to add deadly defences against the Druj at Holmauer is available again. So is a proposal to turn the old Duelling Society field in Holmauer Park into a magical herb garden.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Mentioned in passing: Fransesca describes herself as running some of the least prestigious gambling houses in Tassato Mestra.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: its Basilica of Seven Doors is the benchmark that a restored Capodomus Cathedral would rival.

Holberg.t: Holberg competes as one of the four cities and can pursue revived opportunities for lethal new fortifications at Holmauer and the Duelling Field Gardens.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos has the most revived opportunities. These are sea defences, the Diora University renovation with a College of Autumn Magic, the restoration of Capodomus Cathedral, the Glass Palace and Greatest Taste follies, and a firehouse.

Tassato.t: Tassato competes as one of the four cities and could commission the Colossus of Tassato, a giant statue on the Red Rock meant to outdo the Colossus of Sarvos.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar competes as one of the four cities, and the proposed University of Temeschwar remains available until Summer 385YE.

The moth for the star.d: Day-magic divinations had spread the names of individual stars across the Empire, though Tacita of Zenith's Twisted Chambers disputed them. Since the Summer Solstice astronomantic rituals had felt heavy and draining, and alignment with tulpas was stronger. The Claw's power to empower violent rituals with blood, interdicted by Lights Aliss, now also extended to the empower spell. The Great Wyrm–Mountain conjunction had ended, but a new one with the Drowned Shepherd meant personal-curse arcane projections would be permanently defunct after the Equinox. Pseudo-constellations appeared over Karov, Hahnmark, Holberg, Spiral and Semmerholm. The Eye of the Heavens observatory was proposed for Mount Polus, and the Pilgrim Flame was expected to return to Anvil.

Dawn.t: The Bondring rose over Semmerholm, stirring thoughts of love and an urge to help others strengthen their bonds, though it had only a limited impact on the people there.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Woven Banner pseudo-constellation recorded last season over Necropolis is noted, its influence now faded.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Trident pseudo-constellation recorded last season over Skarsind is noted, its influence now faded.

The League.t: League presses spread sensationalist copies of the star-name pamphlets, and new night stars appeared over Holberg (the Looking Glass, inspiring reinvention) and Spiral (the Mask, inspiring false personas), while Tassato's Golden Ferret faded.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Serpent Sheds its Skin pseudo-constellation recorded last season over Mournwold is noted, its influence now faded.

Urizen.t: Urizeni scholars were at the heart of the debate: Spider's Vantage spread the first star-name pamphlets, the Twisted Chambers disputed them, the Spire of Shadowed Glass catalogued the night stars, and the Eye of the Heavens observatory was proposed for Mount Polus in Zenith.

Varushka.t: The Paired Dancers appeared over Karov, inspiring a rash of ill-considered romances, several weddings and one memorable fight.

Wintermark.t: The Crab appeared over Hahnmark, prompting inventive thinking and the questioning of established beliefs, coinciding with increased criticism of the Imperial Synod.

The moth for the star.o: Around the Autumn Equinox 387YE the stars grew turbulent: astronomancy became harder to practise and more prone to tulpa influence, the Claw's blood-empowered magic spread to the empower spell despite a Conclave interdiction, and a new grand conjunction of the Great Wyrm and the Drowned Shepherd began unravelling personal-curse arcane projections. Fresh 'night stars' were also seen under the Penumbral Veil.

Zenith/Occursion.t: The Eye of the Heavens observatory was offered as an opportunity in Occursion, costing 30 mithril, 20 white granite, 10 weirwood and 225 thrones over two seasons; it would found a new spire and a centre for astronomancy, with the offer ending after the Spring Equinox 388YE.

Hahnmark.t: The Crab pseudo-constellation was seen in Hahnmark's veiled skies, encouraging people to dwell on past choices and propose seemingly unworkable solutions.

Holberg.t: The Looking Glass rose over Holberg, driving some to abandon their lives for new paths, including a merchant-prince who gave away their wealth to become an artist in the Sumaah Republic.

Karov.t: The Paired Dancers over Karov made it easy to see the best in others, sparking hasty romances, weddings and a brawl.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Serpent Sheds its Skin was recorded here last season, but its influence over sleepers has faded.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Woven Banner was recorded here last season, but its influence over sleepers has faded.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Spider's Vantage Spire in Redoubt helped circulate the first scholarly pamphlets on the names of the stars.

Semmerholm.t: The Bondring appeared over Semmerholm, inclining people to reflect on love and help others' connections, though visiting Urizen found little obviously changed.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Trident was recorded here last season, but its influence over sleepers has faded.

Spiral.t: The Mask appeared over Spiral, encouraging deception and false personas, though it was largely overshadowed by everything else happening in the territory.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Ferret was recorded here last season, but its influence over sleepers has faded.

Zenith.t: Tacita of the Twisted Chambers, an old Zenith spire, argued the star names were artefacts of the ritual used, while the Eye of the Heavens observatory was proposed for Mount Polus in the territory.

The mother of morality.d: Wintermark's condemnation by Ylmiska Ferbow and Gunnbrand Ironwill meant the Iron Helms would be shunned by Wintermark armies. The Helms then left the west for Sarvos, presumably to face the Grendel or the Druj. Three opportunities followed. Wintermark could urge its warriors to face the Jotun with respect, winning more victories but inflicting fewer casualties. The Freeborn could make the Red Wind Corsairs a Daring army that captures and ransoms enemies. The League could shun the Helms, or also let the Wolves of War take the physick quality. Gunnbrand Ironwill carried Wintermark's mandate and Gonzalo i Riqueza the Freeborn one. The resolution records no League mandate.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the departing Iron Helms were thought to be heading through Sarvos to face either the Grendel or the Druj.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Helms were thought to be heading east to face the Grendel or the Druj, and a recent Red Wind and Wolves of War raid on Grendel wealth in Spiral was cited as an example.

Jotun.t: Driven from the Mourne in part by the Iron Helms' butchery, the Jotun will for a year face Wintermark armies fighting for heroic victory rather than slaughter. These armies inflict fewer casualties but gain more victory points, which some mystics hoped might restore the old mutual respect between the two peoples.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr apothecaries were among those the Wolves of War might have recruited had the League taken the physick mandate.

The League.t: The League assembly's narrowly passed condemnation of the Iron Helms opened mandates to shun them or to give the Wolves of War the physick quality. The resolution records no League mandate being taken, so these opportunities were lost.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Helms' butchery took place in the Marcher territory of the Mournwold, from which the Jotun fled.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: in Emperor Guntherm's reign, Wintermark and Jotun warriors briefly joined forces to fight the Thule.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's priests shunned the Iron Helms, and Gunnbrand Ironwill was sent to urge the Mark's warriors to face the Jotun as heroes. Until Autumn 382YE, Wintermark armies fighting the Jotun gain more victory points but inflict fewer casualties.

The mother of morality.o: After the Wintermark and Freeborn assemblies, and narrowly the League's, condemned the cruelty of the Varushkan Iron Helms, the Synod was offered mandates to reshape how Imperial armies fight. Wintermark chose to fight the Jotun as heroes rather than butchers, and the Freeborn permanently turned the Red Wind Corsairs towards ransoming their foes.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperatrix Lisabetta is noted as a daughter of Holberg, and Holberg physicks were among those the Wolves of War might have recruited.

Mournwold.t: The Iron Helms' cruelty here helped drive the Jotun from the Mourne, a victory some Wintermark mystics called hollow and whose consequences cannot be undone.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the shunned Iron Helms left the west and headed to Sarvos, presumably on their way to face the Grendel or the Druj.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs' and Wolves of War's recent raid on enemy wealth in Spiral was cited as proof of the profit in war without butchery.

The mystic, the willful.d: The stars stayed hidden over the Barrens, Zenith and Holberg, strengthening naga secretiveness, while Penumbral Veils covered Urdur and several Imperial territories. Citadels were raised in Hahnmark, Kahraman, Kallavesa and Morrow, and pale wolves from a Winter regio in Altis stirred draughir pack instincts. The Concordium of Pallas sped work on the Coursmouth castle and the Salt Guard and wiped away the damage of the Grendel raid on Quzar. Kaela's gift let Imperial citizens held by the Druj die painlessly. Eleonaris's herald Nezha asked for a mithril monument, but the Senate did not engage. The Conclave declined Sadogua's rings and did not instruct him to share a blight cure with Faraden.

Dawn.t: The stars returned over Semmerholm at the Winter Solstice, and the shores of the Semmerlak were suggested as a possible site for Eleonaris's monument.

Druj.t: The Druj were presumed to be behind the shrouds over the Barrens and Zenith, and the Knights of Glory fought them in Morrow and Ossium. Kaela's gift now denies them the corpses of Imperial captives.

Grendel.t: Urizeni Autumn magic wiped away every trace of the Grendel raid on the port of Quzar, and the Knights of Glory refused to fight in Spiral, which Grendel partly held.

Highguard.t: Urizeni magic doubled the pace of work on the new castle at Coursmouth in Necropolis, and the shroud over Necropolis faded away.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Ancestor's Heralds coven raised one of Cathan Canae's castles of stone and ice in the Northspires of Hahnmark, and Krampus stirred in western Skarsind, due to visit Anvil on the Friday night.

Jotun.t: A Navarr citadel was raised over Serra Damata as a sentinel against a possible Jotun return, and the Knights of Glory fought the Jotun in Sermersuaq.

Navarr.t: The Eternal Family raised a citadel to guard Serra Damata in Kahraman, and Revel, the herald of the Lord of the Crossroads, planned to seek their hospitality or that of the Bitterbark Teahouse.

The Brass Coast.t: Madruga and Feroz stayed under Penumbral Veils, a Navarr citadel guarded Kahraman, and Quzar was fully restored after the Grendel raid.

The League.t: The stars vanished over Holberg after the Autumn Equinox, Sarvos and Temeschwar remained veiled, and the League bravos known as the Cuore di Pietra were favoured with Callidus's Tontine tokens.

Thule.t: A Penumbral Veil hung over Urdur in Otkodov, and it was unclear whether Nithoggir, Sküld or Verthandi were also shrouded.

Urizen.t: The Spire of the Auric Horizon turned the Canterspire into a crystal fortress, and the Concordium of Pallas sped castle-building and restored Quzar. Morrow remained veiled and was roamed by winter wolves.

Wintermark.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a castle of fog and shadow in Kallavesa, and Kallavesi mystics planned to take Goosewhisper Infusion on the Friday evening. The Knights of Glory fought the Jotun in Sermersuaq.

The mystic, the willful.o: In Winter 382YE a round of magical effects touched the Empire and its neighbours: star-shrouds and Penumbral Veils persisted, magical citadels were raised, giant winter wolves appeared in Morrow, and Urizen magic sped castle-building and repairs. Several eternals also sent messages and offers, among them Kaela, Eleonaris, Sadogua, Callidus, Barien, Kimus and Jaheris.

Hahnmark/Northspires.t: The Ancestor's Heralds called forth one of Cathan Canae's frozen castles of stone and ice here to protect the land until the Winter Solstice.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: A Navarr citadel was raised to stand guard over Serra Damata against a possible Jotun return.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: Urizeni Autumn magic helped repair the port of Quzar until every sign of the Grendel raid was gone.

Morrow/Altis.t: Giant, intelligent white wolves emerged from the Regio of the Hound, guarding it and ranging across Morrow by night.

Necropolis/Coursmouth.t: Autumn magic from the Concordium of Pallas let labourers at the new Coursmouth castle achieve six months' work in three.

Otkodov/Nithoggir.t: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the Penumbral Veil also lay over Nithoggir.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the Penumbral Veil also lay over Sküld.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: A Penumbral Veil hung over Urdur, interfering with magical scrying.

Spiral/Screed.t: The horror lurking at the heart of Screed is why the Knights of Glory will not fight in Spiral.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat was not singled out by any of the season's enchantments or eternal messages.

Feroz.t: Feroz remained under a Penumbral Veil, with dark fog and warped stars, expected to fade shortly before the Summer Solstice.

Hahnmark.t: A frozen castle of Cathan Canae stood in the Northspires until the Winter Solstice, and northern Hahnmark was suggested as a site for Eleonaris's monument.

Holberg.t: The stars over Holberg winked out after the Autumn Equinox under a potent shroud, which impeded scrying and heightened naga secretiveness.

Kahraman.t: The Eternal Family of Navarr raised a citadel over Serra Damata to guard against a possible Jotun return.

Kallavesa.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a castle of fog and shadow in its marshes, and Kallavesi mystics planned a Friday-night visionary gathering.

Madruga.t: Madruga's Penumbral Veil was expected to fade before the Spring Equinox, and Quzar in Lightsea was fully restored after the Grendel raid.

Morrow.t: The Canterspire became a crystal fortress through Phaleron's power, the territory remained veiled, giant wolves ranged from Altis, and the Knights of Glory fought the Druj there.

Necropolis.t: The shroud over Necropolis faded, and Autumn magic sped construction of the new castle at Coursmouth.

Ossium.t: The Knights of Glory fought the Druj in Ossium this season.

Otkodov.t: A Penumbral Veil hung over Urdur, and it was unclear without scrying whether the rest of Otkodov was also shrouded.

Redoubt.t: The shroud that had hung over Redoubt faded away.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos remained under a Penumbral Veil expected to fade shortly before the Spring Equinox.

Semmerholm.t: After a year of empty night skies, the stars over Semmerholm gradually returned as the Winter Solstice approached.

Sermersuaq.t: The Knights of Glory fought the Jotun in Sermersuaq this season.

Skarsind.t: Krampus stirred from its cold house of bones in western Skarsind, set to visit Anvil on Friday night.

Spiral.t: The Knights of Glory refused to fight anywhere in Spiral after being exposed to the horror at the heart of Screed.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar remained under a Penumbral Veil expected to fade shortly before the Summer Solstice.

The Barrens.t: The stars remained hidden over the Barrens, probably under a recast shroud. Naga there grew more secretive, and Kaela's gift extended into the territory.

The Semmerlak.t: Mentioned in passing: Nezha suggested the shores of the Semmerlak as a possible site for a monument to Eleonaris.

Verthandi.t: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the Penumbral Veil also lay over Verthandi.

Zenith.t: The stars over Zenith stayed hidden, and that shroud was expected to fade at the Spring Equinox 383YE but likely to be recast. Kaela's gift reached into the territory.

The only reason that I sing.d: At the Summer Solstice 382YE the troubadours of Dawn named champions for all seven virtues for the first time in many years. They also named Odelina de Rondell champion of the Way, Ser Isidore Ossienne champion of Love and Colwyn de Rondell champion of Glory. A proposed Synod mandate, available only at the Autumn Equinox, would make the Love and Glory champions permanent. The weavers of Spiral Castle and Laroc would then craft a Troubadour's Ring and a Circlet of Command for them each year, though some fear heresy. Separately, the Senate created the Champion of Courage to bear Torchbrand, one of seven shields lost at Reikos in 367YE. Measure is held by a Jarmish magician-prince, and the Senate could create titles for the other six.

Dawn.t: Dawn's troubadours named a full slate of Summer champions, and the new champions of Love and Glory captured the imagination of nobles and yeofolk alike. The national assembly may now enact a mandate making these uniquely Dawnish champions permanent, despite concerns it may be heretical.

Druj.t: The Pilgrim's Shields were lost when their bearers fell before the Druj at Reikos in 367YE. The orcs may hold one or more of the missing shields, and their habit of using religious items to bait traps might be turned against them.

Grendel.t: Grendel is not named on the page, but it held Spiral, whose Spiral Castle weavers would craft a Troubadour's Ring each year for Dawn's Champion of Love if the mandate passes.

Highguard.t: The seven Pilgrim's Shields, including the Senate-recognised Torchbrand, were forged by Ezkiah the Benefactor, greatest smith of the Highborn in the Empire's early years. Their recovery would inspire the Empire's faithful.

The only reason that I sing.o: After the Dawnish troubadours named Summer champions for all seven virtues, plus champions of the Way, Love and Glory, Dawn had an opportunity to make Love and Glory permanent champion titles. Meanwhile the Senate's new Champion of Courage, keeper of the shield Torchbrand, stirred interest in recovering the six other lost Pilgrim's Shields.

Astolat.t: As Dawnish land, Astolat's nobles and yeofolk share in the enthusiasm for the new champions of Love and Glory. Dawnish weavers would craft regalia for these champions if the mandate is enacted.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the seven Pilgrim's Shields were lost when their bearers fell before the Druj at the battle of Reikos in 367YE.

Spiral.t: If the Dawnish mandate passes, the weavers of Spiral Castle would be inspired to create a Troubadour's Ring each year, delivered to the troubadours of Dawn for the Champion of Love.

Weirwater.t: As Dawnish land, Weirwater's people share in the national enthusiasm for the champions of Love and Glory. Dawnish weavers would craft regalia for these champions should the mandate be enacted.

The other empress.d: During the occupation of Sarvos, Highborn Unconquered seized Giselle's coffin before the Grendel could defile it. With help from League heroes they escaped through the Sentinel Gate to Anvil. Magistrates impounded the coffin near Sybella because Giselle's reported wish to be buried in the League had never been written down or witnessed. Highborn Stewards of the Dead argued for the traditional burial in the Necropolis, while League bishops called moving her an attack on League Pride. The Senate was asked to choose a site and commission a tomb with an Imperial title, but passed no motion. Her husband Teodore's body had been stolen by the Grendel. Virtue's Respite in Temeschwar was completed shortly before Spring 381YE.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the in-character vignette shows two Dawnish folk, a retired Weirwater advocate and a Hawsmoor pig farmer, discussing a wager on where Giselle will be buried.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the in-character text recalls that Giselle died in agony from Druj poison, which casts doubt on her deathbed wishes.

Grendel.t: Grendel raiders broke open Giselle's tomb in Sarvos and took its grave goods, though the Unconquered had already removed her coffin. They also tore apart her husband Teodore's sarcophagus and carried off his body, for reasons no one knows.

Highguard.t: Highborn Unconquered saved the Empress's remains, and Highborn Stewards of the Dead argued that only the Necropolis could protect her and uphold tradition. In the end she was re-interred in the League, not Highguard.

The League.t: League heroes helped the Unconquered escape with the coffin, and League bishops condemned any move to bury Giselle outside the League as an attack on its Pride. Her eventual re-interment in Temeschwar respected her reported wish to rest in the League.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wintermark Empresses Mariika and Britta are cited as precedents for Thrones who were not entombed in the Necropolis.
