The other empress.o: After the Grendel raided Sarvos, Highborn Unconquered rescued the remains of Empress Giselle from her tomb, setting off a dispute between Highguard and the League over where she should be re-interred. The Senate issued no ruling at the Summer Solstice, but by Spring 381YE she had been laid to rest in a new tomb, Virtue's Respite, in Temeschwar.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Marcher abbots wrote urging the Senators of Highguard and the League to fortify the Bay of Catazar coast against further Grendel raids.

Casinea.t: Magistrates intercepted the Unconquered just outside Sybella, impounded Giselle's coffin and held it in a cellar there while the Senate considered the matter.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Giselle reportedly refused burial in the Necropolis during the retreat from Holberg.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: Empress Britta, whose burial was similarly disputed, was given to the marshes of Kallavesa as a precedent.

Necropolis.t: The Necropolis, traditional resting place of almost every Throne, was proposed for Giselle's new tomb on the grounds that it could be properly protected. It was not chosen.

Sarvos.t: Giselle's marble tomb on the Alivetti estates in Sarvos was effectively destroyed by the Grendel. Highborn critics argued that Sarvos could not protect a new tomb against further raids.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is touched on only through the Wintermark precedents for Thrones not laid in the Necropolis.

Temeschwar.t: Bishop Jago Heshel di Temeschwar led the League bishops who opposed moving Giselle out of the League. Shortly before Spring 381YE she was re-interred in Temeschwar, in the new tomb of Virtue's Respite.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: Isolde, who appears in the in-character vignette, was once the best advocate in Weirwater.

The parents of security.d: Plans by Francesca di Sarvos for a Sarvos Arsenal and Dockyard were found at Diora University. The Arsenal would be a great port and shipyard, and would let the League maintain a navy while it held Cigno; it could be commissioned until the end of the Winter Solstice. Menno Van Ritsjhof designed a fortification of walls and granite-anchored chains that remains available. A mandate condemning the Iron Helms, who were already unpopular after a brawl, would have boosted League armies' resupply and cut Varushkan resupply, but it lapsed. About two-thirds of the College orcs, facing prejudice, moved to Skarsind and bonded to the Imperial Orc egregore as the liberated.

Grendel.t: Their sack of Sarvos lies behind both building proposals: the Arsenal could support a navy to repay their sneak attack, and the fortification was meant to stop any future seaborne invasion. Fear of Grendel infiltrators also fed suspicion of the College orcs.

Imperial Orcs.t: About two-thirds of the orcs educated at the College of the Liberated moved to Skarsind and bonded to the Imperial Orc egregore, where they are known as the liberated.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Freeborn are named as the Empire's foremost seafarers, and the Arsenal was pitched as a way for the League to become their naval equal.

The League.t: The League was offered a Naval Arsenal and its own navy, a great fortification for Sarvos, and a chance to strengthen citizen support for its armies. The Senate and the League Assembly took none of them, and the army-support opportunity was lost.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: stories of atrocities committed by the Iron Helms in the Mournwold circulated in Sarvos.

Varushka.t: The Iron Helms, wintering in Sarvos, gained a probably unjust reputation for savagery and anti-orc bigotry. A mandate that would have reduced Varushkan armies' resupply in League territories was never raised.

The parents of security.o: After the Grendel sack of Sarvos, the League was offered three opportunities: commissioning a Naval Arsenal, building a great chain fortification, and turning citizens against the Varushkan Iron Helms through a Synod mandate. Meanwhile most orcs freed from Jarm left the College of the Liberated for Skarsind. Neither the Senate nor the League Assembly acted on any of the opportunities that Autumn.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: The proposed fortification would resist any Shore Offensive in Bocche with an effective strength of 3,000.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: A League navy raised through the Arsenal could be supported only while Cigno stayed under League control. The proposed fortification would defend Cigno against shore offensives with an effective strength of 6,000.

Sarvos/Uccelini.t: The proposed fortification would resist any Shore Offensive in Uccelini with an effective strength of 3,000.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: Mentioned in passing: Southpine is not named; it is linked through the liberated orcs settling across Skarsind in its mines and businesses.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the fortification's designer, Menno Van Ritsjhof, is described as perhaps the most skilled siege architect in Holberg.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is named, alongside Siroc, as the place people think of when they think of Imperial shipping.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: tales of Iron Helms atrocities in the Mournwold fuelled hostility towards them in Sarvos.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos could gain a Naval Arsenal and Dockyard, open to commission until the end of the Winter Solstice, and a fortification of walls and chains that can still be commissioned. Neither was commissioned that season, while tensions over the College orcs and the Iron Helms grew in the city.

Skarsind.t: Most of the College-educated Jarmish orcs settled here, taking mine work and business roles such as those tied to Torfast Trading Post, and bonded to the Imperial Orc egregore.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: grumbling citizens of Sarvos suggested the Iron Helms might be happier in Temeschwar.

The path that winds.d: A curse of Naeve's Twisting Blight rotted harvests and spread sickness across Morrow, Redoubt and Spiral. The Druj anchored a miasma of despair over Zenith, and sentinels and Highborn soldiers proposed a stealthy rescue raid for the coming season. The Illuminated Circle of Bloodsilver Twilight proposed a 40-wain mithril Block in Cinion to protect Spiral's spires from the Black Plateau, which the Senate commissioned. Fausta of the Arbiter's Seat prepared an arcane projection to seal Morrow's passes, and Tulley of Elos prepared two Day rituals offering hope, but neither was used. Sadogua and Janon offered boons to magicians fighting the Druj.

Dawn.t: Tulley of Elos prepared a ritual to send a message of hope to every Dawnish citizen, fearing those enslaved in the Barrens would take Kaela's gift, but it was never performed; Dawnish magicians were also offered Sadogua's mana boon.

Druj.t: The Druj anchored a miasma of despair over Zenith to break their Urizen prisoners, and faced a proposed rescue raid on their captives and an unused ritual that could have trapped their forces in Morrow.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel armada anchored off Sarvos threatens Redoubt, and the earlier Grendel invasion is blamed for Spiral's lost peace.

Highguard.t: Highborn aid helped keep Morrow's refugees from starving, and a successful raid into Zenith could have freed captured soldiers of the Valiant Pegasus, Granite Pillar and Seventh Wave.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Fausta's unused projection would have sealed the passes between Morrow and Navarr's Therunin.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Brass Coast is named as perhaps the only nation more vulnerable than Urizen.

The League.t: League magicians were among those offered Sadogua's boon of extra personal mana at the Winter Solstice for fighting the Druj.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: peace with the Thule is noted as having been secured.

Urizen.t: Urizen suffered a starving curse across its territories while being offered a rescue raid into Zenith, the Spiral Block, a pass-collapsing ritual, messages of hope and eternal boons; only the Block was commissioned.

Varushka.t: Varushkan magicians were among those offered Sadogua's boon of extra personal mana for the Winter Solstice.

The path that winds.o: In Winter 382YE a curse of blight struck Urizen, and several opportunities to aid the beleaguered nation were raised: a rescue raid into Druj-held Zenith, a mithril Block to shield Spiral's spires, a ritual to collapse Morrow's passes, and messages of hope for Urizen and Dawn. The Senate commissioned the Block, but none of the other rituals were cast.

Casinea/Casfall.t: Mentioned in passing: Casfall is not named on the page.

Morrow/Caeli.t: Mentioned in passing: Caeli is not named individually, sharing only in Morrow's general plight.

Morrow/Operus.t: Had Morrow's passes been collapsed, the river crossing at Operus would have been the only route for campaign armies between Morrow and Redoubt.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Fausta's projection would have drawn on Peregro's volcanic hot springs, shaking the region into hills, but it was never cast.

Redoubt/Limus.t: Limus's southern riverbank, guarded by the fortified town of Cargo, would have held the sole remaining crossing from Morrow had the passes been sealed.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Mentioned in passing: orcs still technically control Apulus, though it is unclear who they now are.

Spiral/Cinion.t: The Block commissioned by the Senate will be built in Cinion, harnessing the Winter regio of a blasted grove to protect Spiral's spires.

Zenith/Iteri.t: Mentioned in passing: a summary names the bridge between Operus and Iteri as the remaining route had Morrow's passes been sealed, though the main text places it towards Limus.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Mentioned in passing: Proceris is not named, sharing only in Zenith's general fate under the Druj.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page; its only link is the Highborn support for Urizen described.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is not named; the page only notes the Brass Coast's vulnerability.

Morrow.t: Morrow's refugees suffered the blight curse and survived on Highborn and Marcher food, and Fausta's projection to seal its passes against invaders went uncast, leaving them open.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the despairing oppression met during the conquest of Ossium is compared to Zenith's miasma.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt, the only Urizen territory fully in Imperial hands, was struck by the blight curse and threatened by the Grendel armada, and would gain tax and refugees from any successful Zenith rescue.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the oppression encountered during Reikos's liberation is compared to Zenith's miasma.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel armada lies anchored off Sarvos, threatening Redoubt.

Spiral.t: Spiral, still blighted by the Black Plateau and the curse, saw the Senate commission a mithril Block to shield its spires and lift production penalties on mana sites, congregations, herb gardens, mines and forests.

Therunin.t: Fausta's projection would have sealed the passes between Therunin and Morrow to campaign armies, but it was not cast and they remain open.

Zenith.t: A Druj miasma of despair settled over Zenith, and sentinels and Highborn soldiers proposed a stealthy raid from Spiral to free Urizen captives during the following season.

The place you called home.d: Refused a homeland, the orcs ceremonially cast aside their war spears, though about half kept their arms as the Spears of the Pines. Navarr generals fighting in Therunin or the Barrens may call on them as a 1,000-strong force. Chief Vallack became their liaison to the Military Council and promised a map of the Mallum. The Senate approved their weirwood fortification, the Holt of the Oak, and let them run the Thimble for four wains of weirwood a season. It also redirected the Gardens of High Chalcis' herbs to them, while the Navarr Assembly urged Therunin to share herbs. Volfe of Ashenhall had a Rivers of Life ritual text given to their magicians.

Druj.t: The Druj drove the Great Forest Orcs from the Barrens and still hold their weirwood groves. The orcs promised the Empire maps of the Mallum and what they know of Druj armies, though Vallack warned the information is years out of date.

Highguard.t: Highborn were offered ways to aid the orcs through Reikos, whose people share their experience of Druj oppression. The Senate chose to redirect the bounty of the Gardens of High Chalcis to the orcs for a year.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs are said to be cordial to Imperial Orcs and treat them as equals.

Navarr.t: The Navarr gained orc neighbours in Therunin, and Navarr generals can call on the Spears of the Pines in Therunin or the Barrens. The Navarr Assembly charged Tynan Lonestriker to urge Therunin's people to share herbs, and the Navarr custodian of the Thimble will receive four fewer wains of weirwood each season.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the civil service remarked that the orcs were hardly likely to become the equal of the Urizen in magic within a few years.

The place you called home.o: After the Empire refused to cede them a region of their own, the Great Forest Orcs who fled the Druj settled as guests in Therunin, centred on the Lower Tarn Valley, and disbanded their army. Several opportunities to aid them followed, and the Senate, Synod and Conclave took up most of them.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: The orcs once tended valuable weirwood groves here and speak fondly of them, but the groves now lie in Druj hands.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: Mentioned in passing: being occupied by the vallorn, it is one of the two regions the orcs will not spread into.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: This is the centre of the orcs' settlement and home of the Great Forest Encampment where Chief Vallack can be reached. The Senate approved the orc-garrisoned weirwood fortification, the Holt of the Oak, to be built here.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: Mentioned in passing: being occupied by the vallorn, it is one of the two regions the orcs will not spread into.

Reikos.t: The Senate redirected the herbs of the Gardens of High Chalcis to the Great Forest Orcs, so the great work will give Reikos' herb garden owners no benefit for the next year.

The Barrens.t: This was the orcs' lost homeland, now in Druj hands, which they hope one day to retake. Any Navarr army fighting to conquer it may call the Spears of the Pines to its side.

Therunin.t: The Great Forest Orcs now live throughout Therunin's non-vallorn regions as guests, and their warriors guard against the forest's beasts. If Tynan provides the liao for the Navarr mandate, its herb gardens and businesses will give up part of their output to aid the orcs.

The play that came to Apulian.d: Residents of Apulian found themselves lost in unfamiliar streets, always ending up at some thrilling performance, as the city reverberated with Night magic. Plays drawing on the six personae drew rave reviews, personae appeared where they should not, and citizens felt inspired by them. Heated debate between astronomancers and dramaturgists turned to fruitful cooperation, producing two rival proposals: Salina of the White Harbour's Academy of Dramaturgical Arts, or Sean de Apulian's larger University, a college of magic with a Virtuoso of Apulus title, both available until Summer Solstice 387YE. Separately, Actius of the Deathless Cave pressed again for the Chamber of Euphony, now slightly costlier, as the Dancer grew discordant and insistent.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dancer fell silent after Spiral was lost to the Grendel five decades ago, and the orc Sean de Apulian is described as a former Grendel.

The League.t: League dramaturgy enjoyed a striking renaissance in its city of Apulian, and the League was offered a University of Dramaturgical Arts that would use its capacity for a college of magic, along with a Virtuoso of Apulus title, while the League Assembly's long-backed fane for Sung remained unbuilt.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Apulian's modest size is compared to the Marcher town of Meade.

Urizen.t: Urizen magicians living in Apulian joined League colleagues to study the phenomena and could gain from the proposed University, which could speed the Doyen of the Spires' codification work, while Actius of the Deathless Cave pressed the Empire to build Sung's fane.

The play that came to Apulian.o: In Spring 387YE strange Night-tinged dramaturgical phenomena swept the city of Apulian, prompting League and Urizen magicians to propose an Academy or University of Dramaturgical Arts there. Meanwhile Sung's herald, the Spiral Dancer, grew increasingly agitated and renewed its urgent request for a fane in the city.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Mentioned in passing: wits claim one can cross Apulian in the time it takes to stroll round Holmauer Park.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: Mentioned in passing: a companion wind of fortune on damming the River Doubt in Apstrus is listed as further reading.

Spiral/Apulus.t: In Apulus people got lost in new streets full of performances, personae seemed to walk among them, and the city was proposed as the home of a dramaturgical academy or university and of Sung's Chamber of Euphony.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: a doctor from Holberg is described fighting off two bravos with a parasol after imagining themselves as the Captain.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Apulian is said to be not much bigger than Meade.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: a critic's barb about the play The DOOM that came to Sarvos is quoted, and the Academy might teach theatre beyond the classical Sarvosi style.

Spiral.t: Spiral's capital became the focus of Night-touched dramaturgical wonders and a magical debate, with opportunities for an Academy or University of Dramaturgy, and League and Urizen citizens with resources there could draw on the personae for strength this summit.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is invoked through a narrator's quip, the play Three Princes of Tassato and the playwright Antonio di Tassato.

The poisoned air.d: After the Druj were driven from the Sarangrave and the Senate granted it to Urizen, seers mapped the pivotal pillar in each region. Destroying one would clear that region's miasma. They found none in Bendol, one already removed in the Whisperwood, one in Turan Flats and two each in Thornfen, Bloodwater Marsh and Kroll. Several seers died or were captured. Many survivors swore never to return. The miasma is already poisoning the ritual magic of Urizeni settlers and will worsen unless the pillars fall. Named Imperial officials were tasked with expeditions against overgrown foliage, a poison cauldron, a screaming ghost and two bands of Druj Kallad.

Druj.t: The Druj have lost all hold on the Sarangrave, but their ancient pillars remain to break the will of its people. Two elite Kallad banners, the Kull and the Kri, stayed behind to guard pillars in Turan and Kroll and are blamed for the deaths of many seers.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, which lets captured or vallorn-stricken Imperial citizens choose a painless death, extends into Brocéliande and Therunin.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni who once lived in Spiral compared the Sarangrave to their former home at the worst of the Black Plateau.

Urizen.t: Urizen's seers bore the cost of the survey: some were lost, and many survivors vowed never to return. The nation's settlers already feel the miasma corrupting their ritual magic, and it attacks the very ambition, reason and magic that define them.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: much of the Empire's knowledge of miasma pillars came from Ossium, where the pillars had been hastily and cheaply built.

The poisoned air.o: In Spring 388YE, at the Urizen National Assembly's request, Urizeni seers used divination to locate the keystone miasma pillars of the newly conquered Sarangrave, at the cost of seers lost to the Druj. Their findings opened several conjunctions through which Imperial heroes could destroy the pillars.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: Mentioned in passing: the seers found, unsurprisingly, no keystone pillar in Bendol.

Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh.t: Two keystone pillars lie here. One is shrouded in deadly fumes from an abandoned Druj cauldron, which the Guild Leader of the Apothecaries is tasked with neutralising. The seers who know where the other lies have been captured but might still be rescued.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: The Kri banner of Kallad, aided by Spring practitioners, guards two linked pillars here, and the Scribes of Atonaius were among the seers lost investigating them. The Knight-protector of Spring is charged with destroying both pillars.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: Two keystone pillars stand in Thornfen. One is choked by semi-sentient strangling foliage that killed two seers and is assigned to the Gardener of Pallas. The other is guarded by a screaming ghost that the High Exorcist must deal with.

Sarangrave/Turan Flats.t: The Kull banner of Kallad guards the region's pillar while a Winter coven of ghulai tries to use the Culling Stone regio to curse the territory. The Keeper of the Tower of the Fall is tasked with stopping them both.

Sarangrave/Whisperwood.t: Mentioned in passing: the Whisperwood's keystone pillar had already been removed.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift reaches into Brocéliande, letting those fallen in vallorn miasma choose dissolution.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the pillars destroyed in Ossium are described as hastily erected affairs, unlike the ancient ones of the Sarangrave.

Sarangrave.t: The territory remains blighted by ancient, deeply rooted miasma pillars that have shaped its land and people for generations. Seers identified the keystone pillars whose destruction would lift the miasma region by region, and Druj Kallad still guard some of them.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: former residents of Spiral likened the Sarangrave to Spiral when the Black Plateau was at its worst.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift extends into Therunin.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire first learned about miasma pillars in Zenith, and the Kull are said to have corrupted its Tower of the Fall to unleash the Endless Stalker as the Druj retreated.

The power behind our moves.d: Freeborn corsairs led the seaborne evacuation along the coast, while Imperial Orc and Dawn units, with Commonwealth soldiers, reached families in the hinterland. Grendel patrols were bought off with bribes until it was too late. A furious Rahab closed Oran to Imperial ships and the border with the Brass Coast, and ordered Imperial fleets and units in Feroz harassed. He now faces ruinous costs buying slaves. The High Council did not treat the treaty as broken. It declared its slave-release obligation discharged and demanded the six wains of weirwood by the end of the Summer Solstice. Taxes from Madruga and Segura rose. Several great works were proposed, and a conjunction was offered to stop a Grendel raid into Segura.

Dawn.t: Dawnish military units, together with the Imperial Orcs, provided the bulk of the forces that slipped past Grendel patrols to rescue families from the hinterland of Morajasse and Afarjasse.

Grendel.t: The Grendel lost tens of thousands of workers from Feroz, and Governor Rahab must now buy slaves from Dubhtraig at ruinous cost. The High Council rebuffed his call for war but demanded the weirwood owed by the Empire, warning that failure to pay by the end of the Summer Solstice would breach the treaty.

Imperial Orcs.t: A quarter of all the military units in the hinterland operation were Imperial Orc, so many that one Freeborn observer wondered whether the entire nation had come to help people escape.

Navarr.t: Navarr contributed fleets to the evacuation, and the in-character tale celebrates a lone Navarr who guided Freeborn to safety across the border as a symbol of friendship between the nations.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn fleets made up more than half of the armada, to great national pride, and the evacuees settled mostly in Madruga and Segura, bringing wealth and expertise. Freeborn units and fleets still based in Feroz now face active Grendel harassment.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark sent ships to the evacuation, with Navarr, Wintermark and the League together providing nearly sixty fleets.

The power behind our moves.o: Nearly 200 fleets and almost 100 military units evacuated the Freeborn from Grendel-held Feroz in a complete success, leaving only a handful of families behind. Governor Rahab retaliated, and the evacuees' resettlement in Madruga and Segura opened new opportunities there.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: Few but hard-to-reach families in the Afarjasse hinterland were rescued by military units, and a quest into the Afar Hills freed two Zemress islanders from the orc garrison at Mora's Rock.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The Freeborn of the conquered Cazar Straits, who had been forbidden to leave, were smuggled out in the evacuation.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Freeborn in conquered Fontargenta were evacuated, including a consortium of vintners who fled to establish new vineyards in Madruga.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: Military units slipped past Grendel patrols to evacuate families from the Morajasse hinterland, including workers from the Spice Gardens and the offices of the Vizier of the Incarnadine Satchel.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The conquered Freeborn of Oranseri were evacuated, among them the Cereva family, who escaped Captain Dubha's household with much of his treasure and provoked a Grendel raid in pursuit.

Segura/Iron Plains.t: Former Spice Gardens head gardener Tariq i Cotarez i Guerra has proposed building the Viridian Glasshouse in the Iron Plains, which would supply herbs across Segura and re-establish the Vizier of the Incarnadine Satchel.

Segura/Lucksprings.t: The Cereva have taken sanctuary at a parador near Cerevado, and Captain Dubha's Wave Riders are closing in. A conjunction offers Imperial heroes the chance to intercept them before a bloodbath.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: corsairs remarked that with this many fleets behind the Freeborn Storm the Empire might still be contesting the Bay, and the treaty bars new shipyards or navies on it.

Feroz.t: Almost all of the Freeborn population was evacuated from Feroz. Rahab closed the port of Oran and the border, and Imperial fleets and military units based there now suffer the conquered territory penalty.

Madruga.t: Most evacuees settled in Madruga, raising its taxes by 30 thrones a season. Vintners from Fontargenta are founding vineyards, and opportunities arose to rebuild the Atalaya shipyards, found a School of Naval Warfare at Calvos and build the Parador of Sand and Salt at Quzar.

Segura.t: Evacuees swelled Segura's towns and raised its taxes by 20 thrones a season. Spice Garden workers will upgrade its herb gardens, and a column of Grendel Wave Riders has crossed its border to raid a Freeborn parador.

The prettiest star.d: Volstann agreed that the Crown of Black Ice would not limit access to its citadels if the Empire ceded a region, provided a new territory was conquered within a year; Bregasland, Liathaven, Madruga and Therunin would not count. Meraud aided Urizeni battlemage rituals, and a herald's Pentad challenge was won by the Eternal Family of Navarr. Eleonaris heralds and Jotun converged on Typhawn in the Suaq Wastes. Callidus, Keel, Arhallogen, the Thrice-Cursed Court, Sadogua and Sung made offers or challenges. Skathe promised aid to named citizens seeking the Druj's destruction. Bulgakov became safe to rebuild, and Southpine's white wood was revived, its trees yielding prismatic ink.

Druj.t: Skathe pledged to aid named Imperial citizens who used the Conclave, Synod, Senate or army orders to pursue the erasure of the Druj as a civilisation.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orcs with forest resources could permanently diversify them to yield a dose of prismatic ink, thanks to the revived white wood in Skarsind.

Jotun.t: A dozen or so Jotun were seen accompanying Eleonaris heralds across the Suaq Wastes, and the Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq was charged with defeating them. Jotun-held Bregasland and Liathaven were excluded from counting as new conquests under Volstann's terms.

Navarr.t: The Eternal Family of Navarr won Morgayne the Pentadurge's challenge and claimed the Orb. Therunin was named as not counting as a new territory under Volstann's terms.

The Brass Coast.t: The recently recovered Madruga was excluded from counting as a new territory under Volstann's terms, and two heralds of Callidus arranged to meet the Artisans Guild in the Brass Coast.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: a separate wind of fortune, Daybreak in Spiral, is referenced as covering further eternal-related events.

Urizen.t: Meraud, drawn partly by the raising of Mount Polus, lent power to Urizeni ritualists casting battlemage enchantments, letting them use the Philtre of Heavenly Lore and golden apples to greater effect.

Varushka.t: The vale of Bulgakov became safe to rebuild, and its boyar Valja Nikodemin Kopec proposed a memorial to the lost, which Ylenwe would safeguard if it were ceded to zir.

Wintermark.t: Suaq scouts raised the alarm over Eleonaris heralds advancing on Typhawn in Sermersuaq, and Sadogua asked Eerikki Korpi and the icewalkers to deliver a parcel to an offering-stone in the Dark Woods of Fereskov.

The prettiest star.o: A roundup of eternal activity at the Summer Solstice 387YE, covering bargains, challenges, offers and threats from eternals of all six realms. It included Volstann's terms on ceding regions, Meraud's support for Urizen, a herald battle in the Suaq Wastes and Ylenwe's restoration of scorched lands.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: A legion of Eleonaris heralds and a dozen or so Jotun advanced across the Suaq Wastes towards Typhawn, prompting a skirmish for the Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: The white wood in Southpine fell silent and came alive again, rejoining the wider forest while its glowing trees bled prismatic ink.

Bregasland.t: Under Volstann's terms, retaking Bregasland would not count as conquering a new territory to offset any ceded region.

Karov.t: The once-scorched vale of Bulgakov became safe to rebuild, though two glass-filled pools remained uncleansed; a memorial of at least five wains was proposed, which Ylenwe offered to protect if ceded to zir.

Liathaven.t: Under Volstann's terms, retaking Liathaven would not count as conquering a new territory to offset any ceded region.

Madruga.t: Although recently recovered, Madruga was named as not counting as a new territory under Volstann's terms for ceding regions.

Sermersuaq.t: Typhawn, lured by cattle, was in the territory as a legion of Eleonaris heralds and some Jotun marched towards it, and the Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq was charged with defeating them all.

Skallahn.t: Sadogua arranged a conjunction in the Dark Woods of Fereskov, where icewalkers were to deliver his parcel to an offering-stone, with the Wyrm-King also taking an interest.

Skarsind.t: The white wood was brought back to life by Ylenwe's harmonising power, and its trees now yield prismatic ink that local forest owners could exploit by diversifying.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the separate wind of fortune Daybreak in Spiral is cited as covering eternal-related events there.

Therunin.t: Under Volstann's terms, retaking Therunin would not count as conquering a new territory to offset any ceded region.

The price is great.d: The Diplomatenschloss in Necropolis was finished and garrisoned by veteran Commonwealth soldiers under Commander Inka Kraul, who echoed concerns about Jarmish vessels on the Couros. Three possible commissions for a river patrol were outlined: a Highborn Coursguard at Haros Water, an Urizen River Sentinel at Couros Seat, or a joint River Watcher. Militärattache Schöningen dismissed fears about Commonwealth diplomats aiding Asavea. She warned that the Surveyors' Cartel alleged Imperial trade with Jarm through Zemelslo. The Sternemetal Tower and mana-for-goods trade were withdrawn. Leerdam philosophers might visit Dawn if its National Assembly passed a suitable statement. The University of Volkavaar took the sungold tablet and offered help restoring Therunin.

Dawn.t: Lord Sable's interest in discussing love led Leerdam's Hochschule der Seele to offer a visit. If the National Assembly backed a statement welcoming Commonwealth guests with a greater majority, Dawnish congregations could host lectures on The Universality of Love, receive gifts and join the Assembly of the Way.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the University of Volkavaar offered help restoring Therunin once it is liberated from the Druj.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel's past attacks on the mouth of the Couros and its bridges were cited as a reason to secure the river.

Highguard.t: Highguard gained a garrisoned Commonwealth embassy in Necropolis and might create a Coursguard title at Haros Water to keep peace on the Couros. Its Prognosticator's Office could also be sent to the Commonwealth to carry out an appraisal.

Navarr.t: A Navarr broker proposed the compromise of joint patrol quays in Reikos and Morrow. The Couros also forms part of the border with the vallorn of Therunin.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: an earlier invitation for Commonwealth citizens to visit Holberg was cited, as were the unfulfilled assurances of the previous ambassador Lucia Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Commander Kraul privately likened the Empire's view of Jarm to its view of Jarm's Thule neighbours.

Urizen.t: The architects of Cargo argued that the river patrol should be Urizen, which opened the option of a River Sentinel at Couros Seat in Morrow or a joint title with Highguard. Concern also centred on the Jarmish embassy in Cargo.

Wintermark.t: The Imperial ambassador, Finn Pridetalker of Wintermark, had his concerns about Asavea dismissed and his crystal mana offer declined. He was given warning of Commonwealth accusations of Imperial trade with Jarm so that he could prepare a response.

The price is great.o: The Civil Service's Winter 387YE diplomatic report on the Commonwealth announced that the Commonwealth embassy, the Diplomatenschloss in Necropolis, had been completed and garrisoned. It also set out options for a patrol on the Couros river, Commonwealth accusations of Imperial trade with Jarm, and a proposed exchange on love with Dawn.

Morrow/Ravion.t: Couros Seat in eastern Ravion was put forward as a site for an Urizen River Sentinel or as part of the joint Couros Patrol Quays.

Reikos/Haros Water.t: Haros Water was proposed for the Haros Riverpatrol or the joint Couros Patrol Quays, which would guard against pirates, raiders and clashes between Jarm and the Commonwealth.

Reikos/Riverwatch.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though the proposed river patrol is referred to as a riverwatch.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the Couros was described as a border between the Highborn heartlands and other lands.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: last year's invitation for Commonwealth citizens to visit Holberg was cited as a precedent for the Dawnish visit.

Morrow.t: The spire of Couros Seat in Morrow was proposed as an alternative site for a river patrol commission, or as one half of a joint Highborn-Urizen one.

Necropolis.t: The Commonwealth Diplomatenschloss was completed in Necropolis. A veteran Commonwealth garrison under Inka Kraul took up residence to protect the embassy and the territory, and Kraul toured the territory, admiring Reumah's Rest.

Redoubt.t: The Jarmish embassy in Cargo worried Commonwealth officers, and Cargo's architects argued that the river watch should be based on the Urizen side rather than at Haros Water.

Reikos.t: Haros Water in Reikos was proposed as the site of the Haros Riverpatrol, a sinecure creating the Highborn Coursguard to keep peace on the Couros and Haros rivers.

Therunin.t: The University of Volkavaar offered to help appraise how Therunin might be restored once it is liberated from the Druj, and took the sungold tablet recovered from its northern sinkhole.

The price of liberty.d: Most sanctioned nations retaliated. Jarm (49 thrones 4 crowns), Asavea (46 thrones) and the Thule of Otkodov (21 thrones 2 crowns) imposed tariffs, and the Iron Confederacy closed Robec (5 thrones 3 crowns). Faraden delayed responding, but already costs 21 thrones 2 crowns, which would double if it retaliated. Incoming trade is expected to halve by Autumn 383YE. Proposals include ceding Asavean temples on the Bay of Catazar, sharing Imperial lore with Jarm and the Commonwealth, conquering Reinos, a mountain road into Otkodov, Sarcophan enclaves and a Synod statement on Justice. Naomi warns that boosting trade with slavers may undermine the Pact's purpose. Some citizens resent losing their livelihoods for foreigners' liberty.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Druj-held Sarangrave in the Mallum might lie north of Axos and so offer a possible land route, though this needs further investigation.

Grendel.t: Grendel interference hampers Axou trade across the Bay of Catazar, and Grendel control of Mareave blocks a possible Axou route via Skoura. Meanwhile Jarmish suppliers court the Grendel as eager buyers of weirwood, and a Jarmish prince sends an envoy to their Council.

Highguard.t: A ceded Asavean temple is proposed for Necropolis. Resolving the schism between Bastion and Timoj, perhaps with the palaces of the cardinals, could draw Sumaah and other pilgrims to Bastion and boost trade.

Jotun.t: The Jotun levy heavy tariffs on Faraden caravans crossing Reinos, and the Empire is invited to consider conquering enough of Reinos to bypass them. The page also notes the recent Lasambrian Jotun invasion of Segura.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast commissions are hit hard: the Towers of Anduz, already reduced by the Jotun invasion of Segura, Moonwater Hall, the Gloaming Road and the Feroz temple all suffer. A new Asavean temple is proposed for Madruga.

The League.t: Jarmish merchants in Tassato are shunning the Tassato Mana Exchange, reducing its mana. Sarvos is proposed as a site for both an Asavean temple and a Sarcophan enclave.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marches are not named directly, though some of the affected trade commissions may touch their lands.

Thule.t: The Dragons of Otkodov, angered at being excluded from the summit, imposed retaliatory tariffs but have not yet reconsidered peace. A proposed mountain road into Erskjuvaten would restore trade but would also open an invasion route both ways.

Urizen.t: Redoubt is named among the Bay of Catazar territories where a temple could be built and ceded to Asavean priests to recover lost trade.

Varushka.t: A road north from Olodny in Miekarova into Erskjuvaten is proposed to restore Thule trade, though it would let a Thule army bypass the Grimhold's protection unless Mieriada were fortified. Karsk is suggested as a site for a Sarcophan enclave.

The price of liberty.o: After the Liberty Pact was signed at the Winter Solstice, its trade sanctions on slaving nations cost the Imperial treasury a net 143 thrones and 4 crowns each season. A civil service appraisal led by Naomi of Virtue's Rest set out the losses and proposed ways to mitigate them.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: With the proposed road built, an Imperial army could attack Otkodov from Mieriada without the usual penalty, and only a fortification in Mieriada would stop Thule armies gaining the same advantage.

Verthandi/Erskjuvaten.t: Erskjuvaten would be the northern end of the proposed trade road from Olodny, and the Dragons might fortify it against an Imperial attack along that road.

Bastion.t: A strong resolution of the schism between Bastion and Timoj, perhaps with the palaces of the cardinals, could make Bastion a beacon of the Way and draw trade-bearing pilgrims.

Bay of Catazar.t: Asavean granite suppliers threaten to sell to other nations on the Bay. Temples are proposed for the Imperial territories along it, and Axou trade across the Bay suffers Grendel interference.

Feroz.t: The existing Asavean temple in Feroz, held up as the model for new temples, receives fewer offerings, and the Imperial Delegate to the Temple has fewer options.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman is cited as lying east of Jotun-held Reinos, which blocks the Faraden route.

Karsk.t: Karsk is proposed as the site of a Sarcophan enclave that would draw traders from the Delves and support businesses hurt by the sanctions.

Madruga.t: Madruga is proposed for an Asavean temple costing at least 30 white granite and 60 crowns, which would have to be ceded to Asavean priests.

Mareave.t: Grendel control of Mareave prevents a possible Axou trade route via Skoura.

Miekarova.t: A road from Olodny through the mountains is proposed to restore Otkodov trade. It would let a Thule army bypass the protection of the Grimhold in Perumaki.

Necropolis.t: Necropolis is proposed for a ceded Asavean temple to win back lost trade.

Otkodov.t: The Thule Dragons imposed punitive tariffs, cutting trade, raising mana crystal prices across the Northern trade network and driving up the Ambassador to Otkodov's costs.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt is proposed for a ceded Asavean temple to recover trade.

Reinos.t: Conquering enough of Reinos to let Faraden caravans avoid Jotun tariffs would negate the Faraden loss and cost the Jotun equivalent taxation.

Sarangrave.t: Sarangrave might lie north of Axos and offer a land trade route, but this is uncertain without further investigation.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos is proposed for both an Asavean temple and a Sarcophan enclave to offset lost trade.

Segura.t: After the Lasambrian Jotun invasion took seven Towers of Anduz, the new Faraden tariffs further cut the remaining towers' profits.

Tassato.t: The Jarmish enclave in Tassato is shunning the Tassato Mana Exchange in protest, reducing the mana for sale there.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is not named on the page.

Verthandi.t: A proposed mountain road would run into well-populated Erskjuvaten, needing the Dragons' permission and possibly prompting a Thule fortification there.

The price of peace.d: The Thule treaty expires in Summer 387YE, and the Dragons will not talk until the Senate passes, word for word, a motion declaring Silver Peaks, Miechernya, Krevsaty, Crow's Ridge, Bonewood and Webwood part of Otkodov forever. Wintermark's hunt for Maarik the Golden Tongue drove her to Aino's Rest, and Ambassador Kindra Surefoot was made responsible for killing her. The Grendel, still at war, sent Speaker Morna to Anvil to discuss the Children of Wrecks. The Iron Confederacy warned it may aid the Grendel unless the Empire offers inducements. Skoura proposed a Treaty of Stone over Mareave and Tsark, and Lasambrian Jotun envoys arrived seeking Avisena, the Golden Jarl.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial Consul Jarrigk Orzel of Dawn handles relations with Skoura and the Lasambrian Jotun, and negotiated the proposed Skouran treaty.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial and Thule forces once fought side by side against the Druj in Ossium, a campaign in which the Thule took the Bonewood.

Grendel.t: The Grendel remain at war with the Empire but keep their embassy in Cargo open, and Speaker Morna was coming to Anvil to discuss cooperating against Shivaarn's Children of Wrecks, who have broken from them. The Iron Confederacy openly trades with them and was weighing material aid for them.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian Jotun delegation reached Highguard-held Casinea on its way to Anvil.

Imperial Orcs.t: Skoura's proposed Treaty of Stone welcomed the Imperial Orcs to Mareave as 'scions of freedom' and fitting stewards of the lowlands once called Mahal. Crow's Ridge in their territory of Skarsind is among the regions the Thule demanded the Empire renounce.

Jotun.t: A delegation of Lasambrian Jotun, orcs sworn to the Jotun, crossed into the Empire under a flag of truce after their latest repulsed assault on Kahraman. They were due at Anvil to meet Avisena, the Golden Jarl, apparently on behalf of their own septs alone.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast citizens hold the embassies to the Grendel (Finna) and the Iron Confederacy (Tethros i Zuhri i Erigo), and former Segura senator Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra was named by the Lasambrian envoys as the person they wished to meet. Madruga remains contested by the Children of Wrecks.

Thule.t: The Dragons of Otkodov refused any talks on extending the peace until the Senate passes their exact motion recognising six ceded regions as Otkodov forever, after the earlier Senate wording enraged them. They signalled they expect a heavy price for further peace.

Varushka.t: The Thule used Wintermark's honouring of Yulia Kasimiova Voronov to publicly slight the Varushkans and called for a Wintermark ambassador instead. Varushkan-held regions Krevsaty, Miechernya, Bonewood and Webwood are among those the Thule demanded the Empire renounce.

Wintermark.t: Kindra Surefoot of Wintermark became Ambassador to Otkodov, and nearly three thousand Wintermark heroes searched the Silver Peaks, forcing Maarik the Golden Tongue to retreat to Aino's Rest. Kindra is now responsible for killing her.

The price of peace.o: In Summer 386YE the civil service set out the state of the Empire's foreign relations: the Thule refused to negotiate a renewed peace unless the Senate passed their exact wording renouncing six ceded regions, while the Grendel, the Iron Confederacy, Skoura and a Lasambrian Jotun delegation each made overtures of their own.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: The hills of Krevsaty, ceded in the 379YE treaty, must be declared part of Otkodov 'now and forever' in the Senate motion the Thule demand.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: The passage to Free Landing has become impassable to armies, frustrating any short-term Imperial move against the Children of Wrecks.

Miekarova/Miechernya.t: Miechernya, the Thule's price for aid against the Jotun, is named in the motion the Dragons insist the Senate pass before any talks.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: The Bonewood, conquered by the Thule while fighting the Druj, was left out of the Senate's earlier motion but is named in the exact wording the Dragons now demand.

Ossium/Webwood.t: The Webwood, ceded for Thule aid against the Jotun, is among the regions the Empire is asked to renounce forever.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: With Thule permission, Wintermark forces searched the Silver Peaks for Maarik the Golden Tongue, who has withdrawn to Aino's Rest. The region is also named in the Thule's demand for permanent recognition as Otkodov.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Crow's Ridge, taken by the Thule when the peace was extended in 382YE, is named in the motion the Dragons insist the Senate pass unchanged.

Bay of Catazar.t: Grendel threats make crossing the Bay treacherous, and the Children of Wrecks have claimed the entire Bay for their eternal. Skoura's proposed treaty would renounce all Skouran claims to territories on the Bay.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian Jotun delegation arrived in Casinea ahead of the Summer Solstice, heading to Anvil.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: a proposed Suranni-Imperial alliance to drive the Grendel from Feroz had collapsed because the Suranni expected to keep any regions they freed.

Kahraman.t: The Lasambrian Jotun had recently been driven back from their latest bloody assault on Kahraman before sending envoys to Anvil under a flag of truce.

Karsk.t: The Thule demanded that the Senate declare Krevsaty in Karsk, ceded in 379YE, part of Otkodov forever and renounce any claim to it.

Madruga.t: Madruga was assaulted by Grendel forces in Winter 385YE, and the passage to Free Landing is now impassable to armies, leaving it unclear how the Empire can defeat the Wreckers there.

Mareave.t: Skoura's proposed Treaty of Stone would acknowledge the Empire's conquest of Mareave, renounce Skoura's claim to it, welcome the Imperial Orcs, and ask the Empire to return Skouran artefacts uncovered there.

Miekarova.t: Miechernya in Miekarova, given to the Thule as payment for aid against the Jotun, is among the regions the Thule demanded the Empire recognise as Otkodov forever.

Mountains of the Moon.t: Skoura's proposed treaty would commit the Empire to consult Skoura on substantive matters concerning the Tsark of the Mountains of the Moon, with whom the Empire has no formal relations.

Ossium.t: Both the Bonewood, taken by the Thule while fighting the Druj, and the Webwood, ceded for aid against the Jotun, are named in the Thule's demand that the Empire renounce them forever.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov's Dragons set an exact Senate motion as their condition for opening talks to extend the peace that expires in Summer 387YE, and rejected an address by the Throne as a substitute.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Segura's grasslands have seen a decade of Lasambrian invasion and retreat, and the envoys sought Avisena, once Segura's senator.

Sermersuaq.t: Wintermark armies hunted Maarik the Golden Tongue in Sermersuaq's Silver Peaks, driving her to her hideaway of Aino's Rest, where a skirmish to kill her is very likely to involve combat.

Skarsind.t: Crow's Ridge in Skarsind, taken by the Thule when the peace was extended in 382YE, is among the regions the Thule demanded the Empire renounce.

Veroigne.t: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni ambassador operates from Chaubrette, a territory said to lie west of Veroigne.

The price of wisdom.d: Synod mandates now needed a greater majority, because the Wisdom Assembly had urged the virtuous Empire-wide to question them and Urizen's sword scholars did the same at home. Options included condemning Sulemaine i Taziel, overruling or recanting the Wisdom Assembly, and Urizeni or Freeborn mandates. At the Winter Solstice the spiritual pilgrimage meant simple majorities sufficed. Rafael Barossa di Tassato enacted the General Assembly mandate overruling the Wisdom Assembly. Galene Netherwatch raised a Wisdom mandate urging continued opposition, and Eurybia Melampus de Tassato enacted a Loyalty mandate joining it, leaving the outcome unclear. Clarice Novarion enacted a Courage mandate, and Clytemnestra enacted the Urizen mandate ending debate over Sulemaine.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the foes the sword scholars of any fortified Morrow temples would be eager to fight.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the foes the sword scholars of any fortified Morrow temples would be eager to fight.

Urizen.t: Urizen's embrace of Sulemaine as the Paragon of Blades meant the sword scholars' opposition to Synod mandates would persist there whatever the General Assembly did. Clytemnestra enacted the Urizen Assembly mandate stating that Sulemaine's enemies are not Urizen's and halting further mandates about her for at least a year.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as an example of the doubt that would follow if the General Assembly reversed its earlier rulings, with people asking whether Wintermark might be condemned for drawing inspiration from its forebears.

The price of wisdom.o: After Wisdom Assembly and sword-scholar challenges stopped several Autumn mandates taking hold, Synod mandates came to need a greater majority to be enacted. This Wind of Fortune set out competing responses for the General, Wisdom, Urizen, Brass Coast and other assemblies, and a Senate opportunity to fund fortified sword scholar temples in Morrow.

Morrow/Peregro.t: The Temple of the Four Winds in Peregro would be the focus of the proposed commission, becoming a strength 3000 fortification garrisoned by sword scholars and inflicting half again as many casualties on attackers. Once ceded, it would lie beyond the Senate's control.

Morrow.t: The Senate was offered the chance to fund fortified sword scholar temples across Morrow, ceded to the sword scholars, for 60 wains of white granite, 50 wains of mithril and 220 crowns, taking six months to build. The opportunity lasted until the end of the Spring Equinox 384YE.

Redoubt.t: Sword scholar temples could not be built in Redoubt because resistance from the sentinels there was still too strong.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: sword scholar temples could be funded there if the Empire reconquered Spiral, provided the situation in Urizen had not changed.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: sword scholar temples could be funded there if the Empire reconquered Zenith, provided the situation in Urizen had not changed.

The prime colour of the world.d: The Hallow was the first such Empire-wide enchantment since before Emperor Hugh's reign. Every herb garden produced extra Cerulean Mazzarine, and animals, plants and people grew more fertile. Briars felt their lineage strengthened, and weak Spring regio and heralds stirred. Floodwaters spread a Rivers of Life curse along the Scorrero, boosting farms and gardens in Kahraman, Segura and Madruga. Realmsroot bloomed in Upwold, Hahnmark and Miaren. Dawn's new Gardens of Tiberius' Bequest were offered a mithril upgrade, which was never taken. In Holberg, Rebeshof became marsh, cutting farm production. Ennerlund was threatened next, with options to save it or embrace the marsh, but no immediate effort was made.

Dawn.t: The newly built Gardens of Tiberius' Bequest in Laroc were found to sit on a Spring regio, offering a chance to boost production with mithril mirrors, but the opportunity was not taken and lapsed.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are noted as having destroyed paths and bridges in Holberg that any new dike-building would try to replace.

Navarr.t: Navarr's trods pulsed with Spring magic but needed far more clearing, and Realmsroot bloomed in unprecedented quantities in Miaren.

The Brass Coast.t: The Hallow amplified the Rivers of Life curse carried down the Scorrero by floodwaters, further enhancing every farm and herb garden in Kahraman, Segura and Madruga.

The League.t: The enchantment worsened the Morass in Holberg, turning Rebeshof to marsh and cutting the territory's farm production, with Ennerlund threatened next and costly options offered to save it or turn it into a herb-rich marsh.

The Marches.t: Realmsroot, a rare herb with a powerful narcotic effect on the lineaged, bloomed in unprecedented quantities across Upwold.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Sherard Hunters wove the Hallow of the Green World, and Realmsroot bloomed in unprecedented quantities in Hahnmark.

The prime colour of the world.o: At the Spring Equinox the Sherard Hunters of Wintermark wove the Hallow of the Green World across the Empire under the conjunction of the Fountain, unleashing a season of extraordinary fertility, extra Cerulean Mazzarine, rare Realmsroot blooms and strengthened Spring magic, but also hastening the spread of the Morass in Holberg.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: Ennerlund was set to become a marsh by the Winter Solstice, sooner if further strong Spring magic struck, which would raise the upkeep of the Great Pits of Ennerlund; the Senate could pay to save it or to turn it into a tended herb marsh.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: Without dike repairs, large parts of Rebeshof reverted to sodden marsh and the region was officially declared a marsh, too late to prevent.

Holberg/The Morass.t: The Hallow exacerbated the already worrying spread of the Morass, which swallowed Rebeshof and continued to advance without immediate efforts to contain it.

Astolat.t: The Gardens of Tiberius' Bequest in Laroc could have been made more fertile by harnessing a Spring regio at their centre, but the opportunity was not taken.

Hahnmark.t: Rare Realmsroot bloomed in unprecedented quantities across Hahnmark, and herb gardens there yielded prepared doses of it.

Holberg.t: The Hallow accelerated the Morass, making Rebeshof a marsh and permanently reducing farm production, while Ennerlund faced the same fate by Winter unless 60 wains of weirwood and 15 Thrones were spent.

Kahraman.t: The Rivers of Life evoked in Kahraman was made especially potent, further boosting every farm and herb garden in the territory.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: its marshes are the benchmark for healing herbs that a deliberately tended Holberg marsh might nearly rival.

Madruga.t: Floodwaters along the Scorrero carried the empowered Rivers of Life downstream, enhancing every farm and herb garden in Madruga.

Miaren.t: Rare Realmsroot bloomed in unprecedented quantities across Miaren, and herb gardens there yielded prepared doses of it.

Segura.t: The empowered Rivers of Life, spread by floodwaters down the Scorrero, further enhanced every farm and herb garden in Segura.

Upwold.t: Rare Realmsroot bloomed in unprecedented quantities across Upwold, and herb gardens there yielded prepared doses of it.

The risk-all point.d: The Pact recognised hylje and daeva as persons and sanctioned Asavea, Jarm, Faraden, the Iron Confederacy and the Thule. Axos outlawed slavery with Imperial and allied aid, avoided civil war, but passed harsh laws making orcs second-class citizens. The Iron Confederacy closed Robec and its southern border and demanded that Mordecai of Zephaniah's Lament and his accomplices be handed over for killing ten templars. Faraden was angered by the sanctions, and smuggling was rumoured. Asavea and Jarm imposed counter-sanctions, while the Commonwealth and Sarcophan Delves offered trade benefits. Grendel pirates of Attar continued raiding Bay of Catazar shipping, and an opportunity to stop them was offered.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn's Lord Colwynn de Rondell and Jarrigk Orzel are named as the Imperial Ambassadors to the Iron Confederacy and Asavea respectively.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Axou fears about freed orcs are rooted in Druj invasions, and orcs leaving Axos to the north or west are arrested as presumed recruits for the Druj.

Grendel.t: Grendel pirates of Attar continued raiding Imperial shipping in the Bay of Catazar, and Grendel interference in Axos was blamed for unrest, with Issyk's new Grand Ilarch said to be critical of ties to the Grendel.

Highguard.t: Highborn fleets that traded during the season suffered production losses from Grendel piracy; the Highborn Accalon of Felix's Watch remained Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Faraden traders pay a tithe to the Jotun to cross the Lasambrian Hills, and the Lasambrian Jotun hold parts of Segura including the main route through Anduz.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast fleets were hit by Grendel piracy, the Iron Confederacy closed its land border with the southern Brass Coast, and Brass Coast businesses trading with Faraden saw merchant numbers fall as smuggling was rumoured along the western border.

The League.t: Fleets from Tassato and Sarvos suffered production losses from Grendel piracy, and Lucia Sanguineo di Tassato served as Ambassador to the Commonwealth.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are listed among the slaving nations sanctioned under the Liberty Pact.

Urizen.t: Urizeni fleets suffered production losses from Grendel piracy, and Tarquinius Ankarien of Urizen served as Ambassador to Axos as it abolished slavery.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Thanmir Hrafnar and Izsák Blár Skipstjóri of Wintermark are named as Ambassadors to the Sarcophan Delves and Jarm.

The risk-all point.o: In Spring 383YE the Empire's foreign relations were reshaped by the Liberty Pact, signed by the Empire, the Sumaah Republic, the Commonwealth and Axos, and by trade sanctions on the slaving nations, which responded with tariffs and embargoes of their own.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Mentioned in passing: a priest linked to the Black Sails Quay in Longbeach remarked that "we all understand each other perfectly well" and refused to carry the Nine's invitation to her sect's leaders.

Bay of Catazar.t: The pirates of Attar continued harassing merchant vessels from territories along the Bay of Catazar, and an opportunity to end the raids was offered.

Feroz.t: The Temple of the Black Bull in Feroz continued to soften the effect of sanctions on trade with Nemoria, standing as a symbol of cooperation with Asavea.

Kahraman.t: Faraden traders were reportedly seeking routes into the Empire through Kahraman, raising concern that they were smuggling goods to avoid the new tariffs, though there was no evidence yet.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: a priest associated with the Black Sails Quay in Longbeach declined to pass on the Assembly of the Nine's invitation to Axou priests.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is named among the smaller nations close enough to affect Imperial politics.

Sarvos.t: Fleets from Sarvos that traded during the season suffered production losses from Grendel pirate raids.

Segura.t: Faraden traders who once used the Sunset Roads declined in number and were rumoured to be slipping into northern Segura to evade tariffs, while the Lasambrian Jotun held the main route through Anduz.

Tassato.t: Fleets from Tassato that traded during the season suffered production losses from Grendel pirate raids.

The sack of Sarvos.d: Grendel ships landed thousands of Broken Shore soldiers, crushing armed resistance. Civilians who cooperate are largely left alone, but harming an invader means enslavement in the southern salt mines, and laying hands on a Grendel means execution. The orcs looted Diora University, Capodomus Cathedral and even the tomb of Empress Giselle, shipping treasures to the Broken Shore. Resource production would be halved if occupation continued, and Imperial taxation suffered, partly permanently. The Synod or League assembly could call the people to rise up, backed by the Mayor of Caricomare; Vitória Barossa provided 25 liao. The Grendel are seizing builders and engineers and clearing ground near the quayside, apparently for a major construction project.

Grendel.t: Grendel forces from the Broken Shore seized Cigno, looted its treasures for shipment home, enforced brutal martial law and began rounding up architects and engineers, apparently for a major building project on the island.

The League.t: The League suffered a grievous blow to its pride and wealth as one of its greatest cities was occupied and pillaged, including the tomb of Empress Giselle; its national assembly was given the opportunity to call the citizens of Sarvos to armed uprising.

The sack of Sarvos.o: In Spring 380YE the Grendel invaded the League city of Sarvos, conquering the island of Cigno and imposing draconian martial law while they systematically pillaged one of the richest cities in the Empire.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: Cigno, home of the city proper, was conquered; its university, cathedral and imperial tomb were looted, the partly built Caricomare cargo dock was stripped bare, and civilian labour gangs were forced to flatten ground near the quayside.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos faced halved resource production if Grendel occupation persisted, a significant and partly permanent loss of taxation to the Imperial Treasury, and the prospect of a bloody popular uprising that could inflict heavy casualties on the occupiers but provoke retaliation.

The same bed.d: From the Spring Equinox, nightly light shows over Madruga depicted Imperial victories, lifting Freeborn morale before fading near the Solstice. An earthquake centred on Ghita's Veils in the Sobral Grasses broke its ancient pillars and trenches, revealing they had contained mana; the site gained two ranks, though magicians suffered a shared nightmare. Cheaper upgrades for Ghita's Veils and the Garden of Sighs, and a proposed standing-stone great work across Segura, were offered for the Summer Solstice only. Prompted by the League Assembly, Menno van Ritsjhof proposed twin harbour towers guarding Siroc and the Lyceum, requiring a Senate commission. A Freeborn statement that military donations are not unprosperous drew little interest.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel burning of Atalaya still stings the Freeborn, and the Drakes are said to be still fighting the remaining Grendel on the islands.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are back in Kahraman, though the Freeborn are confident they can be beaten again.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: some see similarities between the design of Ghita's Veils and patterns favoured by the Navarr.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn morale was lifted by the skyborne displays, Segura gained stronger mana flows and time-limited upgrade opportunities, Siroc was offered an ambitious sea defence, and the Freeborn largely shrugged off their assembly's statement on charity, insisting giving is a private matter.

The League.t: A League Assembly statement urged Menno van Ritsjhof, architect of Holberg's walls, to design fortifications for Madruga, and visitors from Sarvos and Tassato travelled to enjoy the lights.

The same bed.o: In Summer 382YE the Brass Coast, despite invasions by the Grendel and Jotun, buzzed with talk of nightly fiery displays of Imperial victories over Madruga, an earthquake at Ghita's Veils in Segura, a League architect's proposal to fortify Siroc, and a Freeborn Assembly statement on charity.

Segura/Anduzjasse.t: Freer mana flows offered the owner of the Garden of Sighs a chance to upgrade it to rank three for a single wain of mithril, available only after the Summer Solstice.

Segura/Sobral Grasses.t: The quake shook the whole region, collapsed an old house in Anozel and wrecked Ghita's Veils, which gained two ranks as released mana surged and could be raised to rank six for four wains of mithril, while local magicians shared an ominous nightmare.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: people from Feroz travelled to Madruga to see the lights in the sky.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Menno van Ritsjhof is famed for his work on the walls of Holberg.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory's renewed Jotun invasion worries the Freeborn, and people from Kahraman came to see the lights over Madruga.

Madruga.t: Nightly light shows of Imperial victories drew crowds to Madruga until shortly before the Solstice, and a proposed twin-tower fortification costing 100 wains of white granite, 20 of weirwood and 30 Thrones would guard Siroc and the Lyceum if the Senate commissions it.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: visitors from Sarvos came to see the lights, and Menno's unbuilt 'chain against chains' design for the city is recalled.

Segura.t: An earthquake strengthened mana flows across Segura, and a hakima proposed a standing-stone great work, needing a Senate motion or Wayleave, to yield 37 crystal mana across its mana sites, though another warned of astronomantic side effects.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: visitors from Tassato travelled to Madruga to enjoy the lights in the sky.

The scars from tomorrow.d: A proposed Navarr mandate would set guides to challenge heresy among foreign trod-walkers. It would cost every Navarr congregation a rank and drive away Faraden merchants. Several trods briefly and strangely strengthened. In Liathaven, Wither the Seed began blighting all life for thirty years and slowing the vallorn, which extends the chance to cleanse Westwood until Summer 383YE, but wild Spring magic shredded its newly restored trods. Spring ritual magic linked to Yaw'nagrah pushed Brocéliande's vallorn into Boar's Dell and Elerael. Military units could defend Greenstead and Brackensong: 1,000 force saves Boar's Dell and 2,000 saves both. Llofir sought a parley about the vallorn.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's spread into Dawn's Astolat three years earlier is recalled as unlike the current Brocéliande advance.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: their earlier withdrawal from Elerael and their rampage across Urizen are cited, as is the loss of Zenith's trods.

Highguard.t: Highborn pilgrims crowd the trods and are unlikely to accept Navarr guides lecturing them about the virtues. Llofir asked for a representative of the pilgrims at its parley on the vallorn.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: their hold on Liathaven blocks easy restoration of its trods, and their capture of Sermersuaq strains the Empire's armies.

Navarr.t: The nation faced a costly choice over policing the trods. It saw its Liathaven trod work undone, and its steadings in Boar's Dell and Elerael are threatened by a deliberately roused vallorn they must defend or abandon.

The League.t: The east-west trod through Foracci in Sarvos was one of the few routes where travellers noticed the trods briefly running faster and farther than normal.

The Marches.t: The trod through the market town of Sarcombe briefly strengthened, and Marcher Rucastle's support built Greenstead's stone walls, a rallying point for the defence of Boar's Dell.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj rampaging across Urizen is cited as a reason Imperial armies may not be spared for Brocéliande.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the fall of Sermersuaq to the Jotun is cited as straining the Empire and cutting into the trod network.

The scars from tomorrow.o: In Autumn 382YE the Navarr weighed a Synod mandate to send guides to escort foreigners on the trods, the Wither the Seed curse began sending Liathaven's vallorn into a thirty-year slumber, and the vallorn of Brocéliande was deliberately roused to creep into Boar's Dell and Elerael.

Brocéliande/Black Boughs.t: A few Navarr live at the Broch deep in the Black Boughs, and the trod joining the Broch to Anvil briefly strengthened.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: The vallorn's miasma, husks and ettercaps creep in and may claim a tenth of the region this season. Greenstead's stone walls offer a rallying point, and 1,000 effective force would hold the advance here.

Brocéliande/Dark Ranging.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns dashed through Dark Ranging to secure Elerael after the Druj withdrew.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: The vallorn's slow advance threatens its fragile new steadings and could take a tenth of the region this season. Brackensong Steading could anchor a defence, but holding Elerael as well as Boar's Dell requires 2,000 effective force. Llofir's herald also emerged here.

Brocéliande/Terunael.t: Mentioned in passing: very old vallornspawn husks come from Brocéliande, where Terunael itself once stood.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: The curse has slowed the vallorn's recovery, so the chance to clear West Ranging lasts beyond the Winter Solstice, and its weakened vallornspawn may offer less resistance.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: The vallorn is slowly regaining strength here and will be fully restored by the Summer Solstice 383YE unless rooted out first. Scrying might reveal how much the curse has weakened its spawn.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: The trod through Sarcombe was one of the routes where travellers noticed a brief, unexplained strengthening.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: A green herald of the eternal Llofir crossed from Tamarbode into Elerael, carrying the request for a parley about the vallorn.

Sarvos/Foracci.t: The east-west trod through Foracci, but not the one running north, briefly let travellers walk faster and farther before the effect disappeared.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's expansion into Astolat three years ago is contrasted with the present advance, which shows no sign of spilling into neighbouring territories.

Brocéliande.t: Ritual Spring magic drawing on Yaw'nagrah has roused the vallorn here to creep into Boar's Dell and Elerael. The Empire must commit military force or abandon the Navarr footholds, possibly losing them entirely within about two years.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's expansion into Casinea three years ago is recalled as a different kind of event from the current spread.

Liathaven.t: The Wither the Seed curse began a thirty-year blight on all life here while lulling the vallorn back to sleep, but an intentional burst of Spring magic tore apart the newly restored trods to the vallorn's heart.

Mournwold.t: The trod through the market town of Sarcombe was one of those observed to strengthen briefly before the effect vanished.

Reikos.t: A green herald of Llofir crossed from Tamarbode into Elerael, bearing the eternal's request to parley about the vallorn.

Sarvos.t: The east-west trod through Foracci, though not the northern one, briefly carried travellers faster and farther than usual.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: no events are described here, though the territory is linked to the strengthened trod joining the Broch to Anvil.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: its loss to the Jotun is cited among the setbacks to the trod network and to Imperial strength.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: in the opening story, the thief-taker picked up his quarry's trail after meeting an acquaintance in Tassato.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns dashed through the Barrens to reach Elerael after the Druj withdrew.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the loss of Zenith is noted as reducing, though not ending, the trods' draining of the vallorn.

The shadows fall behind you.d: The Ambition Assembly upheld a greater-majority call to consecrate Elos harbour, comparing General Umarth's sacrifice to Tian's. A General Assembly mandate to consecrate the site with true liao was proposed. If enacted, it would allow a Fist's Memorial sinecure with a Custodian drawn from Urizen or Wintermark. With a greater majority, it would also aid natural resupply for Urizen and Wintermark forces at Elos. Urizen would gift the Dissipating Silks schema to Runesmith's Law, and Kallavesi mystics would add Hero's Journey to Urizen Lore. Incommodus, then Mael of the Shattered Tower, offered a rival mandate that also celebrated Grendel Ambition, with unknown diplomatic effects. Eli of the Cenotaph's alternative would forgo the memorial and the exchanges.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's offer to share swamp-craft with Urizeni stargazers is meant to further Urizen's aims in the Druj-held Sarangrave.

Grendel.t: The Grendel were driven from Elos and their Maelstrom plot foiled. Rival mandates propose celebrating their audacious Ambition, though any effect on Grendel diplomacy or their view of Elos is unknown.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as a barbarian nation that honours fallen enemies and reveres memorials to Imperial heroes.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Apulian orcs were approached for comment on Grendel attitudes but declined to speculate, saying they now follow the Way.

Urizen.t: Urizen honours the Fist's sacrifice for Elos. If the consecration goes ahead, Urizen gains a possible memorial and custodian title, better resupply for its forces at Elos, and Hero's Journey in Urizen Lore, while Arethas's magicians would gift the Dissipating Silks schema to Wintermark.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark lost its oldest army, the Fist of the Mountains, whose sacrifice is to be honoured at Elos. A consecration could bring Wintermarkers the custodian title, better resupply for their forces there and Dissipating Silks in Runesmith's Law.

The shadows fall behind you.o: After the Fist of the Mountains sacrificed itself to stop the Grendel destroying Elos with a weapon called Maelstrom, the Ambition Assembly sought true consecration of the restored Elos docks in Redoubt, where the army's last banner flies. Competing Synod mandates were drawn up, some also honouring the Grendel's own Ambition.

Redoubt/Naris.t: The proposed Fist's Memorial sinecure, producing liao for its Custodian, would be built in Naris, but only if Elos Harbour is consecrated with true liao.

Redoubt/Siluri.t: Mentioned in passing: Siluri's Academy of Arms is cited as a comparable place of pilgrimage.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Mael's mandate wording would make Elos a beacon of Ambition shining across the waters of Catazar to Attar.

Kallavesa.t: The Wintermark Assembly invited Urizeni stargazers to meet Kallavesi mystics, and the Crescent's Eye coven plans to add Hero's Journey to Urizen Lore if Elos is consecrated.

Redoubt.t: Elos's docks, retaken from the Grendel and back in service, are the proposed site of a true consecration of Ambition. This could draw pilgrims, a memorial and extra resupply for Urizen and Wintermark forces resting there.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark offered to share its swamp knowledge to help Urizen's aims in the Sarangrave.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Apulian orcs, asked about Grendel attitudes, declined to comment as followers of the Way.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Zenith's great foundries helped Arethas's magicians copy the Dissipating Silks schema meant as a gift to Wintermark.

The shape of things to come.d: Following the Golden Pyramid's grand lodge in Mareave, the Conclave endowed 25 mana to the Silver Tears, wealthy Freeborn from Kahraman, Madruga and Segura, to plan a Silver Chalice lodge of equal scale in Madruga. They rejected Crucible and Siroc Bayou as unstable, Torres and the Quiet Grasses as too remote, Free Landing because of the Children of Wrecks, and Calvos Sound as already crowded. They chose Quzar, meeting place of the hakima, where the once-cursed caravanserai well flows again. The commission would cost 40 white granite, 40 weirwood, 20 mithril and 60 Crowns over two seasons. It would provide mana, a great hospital, vital honey and herbs, and fewer army casualties in four territories, and would create the Hakima of the Rippling Marshes. Further lodges must wait.

Grendel.t: Grendel held Feroz and Mareave that season; if built, the lodge would cut casualties for Imperial armies fighting in Feroz by a tenth. Mareave is named as the site of the Golden Pyramid's grand lodge.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn patrons proposed to host the Silver Chalice's grand lodge at Quzar, drawing on the hakima and their kohan. If built, it would reduce Imperial army casualties across the Coast and create the elected Freeborn post of Hakima of the Rippling Marshes to support exploration of Crucible and the Bayou.

The shape of things to come.o: In Spring 387YE the Parador of the Silver Tears, funded by the Conclave, drew up plans for the Well of Life, a grand lodge for the Silver Chalice at the restored Jayyani Caravanserai near Quzar in Lightsea, Madruga. The page also set out how further grand lodges for other Conclave orders could be planned.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: Calvos Sound was considered as a site but rejected because a great deal of other work, including the Professors' new city, is already proposed there.

Madruga/Crucible.t: Crucible was discounted as a building site for fear the Night-touched marsh might transform or swallow it, but the lodge would let the grandmaster buy its vital honey. The new Hakima would be expected to support Freeborn exploring it.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Free Landing was ruled out as a site because it is currently controlled by the Children of Wrecks.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: The Well of Life would be built at the abandoned Jayyani Caravanserai outside Quzar, whose cursed well now flows again. The opportunity ends if Lightsea leaves Imperial control.

Madruga/Quiet Grasses.t: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Grasses were judged less appealing than the coast and passed over as a site.

Madruga/Siroc Bayou.t: Siroc Bayou was discounted as a site because of the unstable Night-wrought changes, though its vital honey would be sold through the lodge. Its exploration would be supported by the new Hakima of the Rippling Marshes.

Madruga/Torres.t: Mentioned in passing: Torres was judged less appealing than the busy coast and passed over as a site.
