Feroz.t: If the Well of Life were completed, Imperial armies fighting in Feroz would suffer a tenth fewer casualties each season, as healers travelled the roads from Quzar.

Kahraman.t: Some of the Silver Tears' founders came from Kahraman, and Imperial armies fighting there would lose a tenth fewer casualties once the lodge was complete.

Madruga.t: Madruga was chosen for the Silver Chalice's grand lodge, which would boost its herb gardens and bring vital honey and ilium from its transformed regions and bay. It would also field a great hospital and cut casualties for Imperial armies fighting there.

Mareave.t: Mareave hosts the Golden Pyramid's grand lodge under construction, the model whose scale the Silver Chalice's plans were to match. Its completion is one trigger allowing the Conclave to seek a further lodge.

Segura.t: Some of the Silver Tears' founders came from Segura, and Imperial armies fighting there would suffer a tenth fewer casualties once the lodge was built.

The silent page.d: After seizing the Carmine Fields and Hope's Rest and repelling a Druj counter-attack, the Empire chose to send messages of hope rather than take the Fangs. The Highborn Assembly, and thanks to the Gryphon's Pride's orders also the Dawn Assembly, could each mandate an approach to one faction: the Great Forest Orcs, Black Wind, Vendarri, Montanians, Karass or Barrens Dawnish. A successful approach would let generals meet that faction's representatives. Three competing mandates were offered: the Way and Lenarius Ankarien's versions would boost casualties against the Druj by a fifth, while Fintan Nighthaven's would penalise generals urging "Death to the Druj". The tepel Varag Soulflayer, torturing Montanian captives in the Untrod Groves, fell to the Champion of Vigilance to kill.

Dawn.t: The Gryphon's Pride under the late Garravaine De Rondell pushed into the Barrens, opening a chance for the Dawn Assembly to mandate an approach to a faction. The Dawnish yeofolk still living under Druj rule were eager to help but wary of Imperial politics over the territory's future.

Druj.t: The Druj were driven back from Hope's Rest and the Carmine Fields and faced Imperial efforts to turn their subject peoples against them. They also faced possible mandates calling for their outright extermination, while their tepel Varag Soulflayer threatened to unleash tortured souls on Imperial armies.

Highguard.t: The Valiant Pegasus committed itself wholly to a crusade to liberate the Barrens, giving the Highborn Assembly the opportunity to mandate an approach to one of six Barrens factions. Highborn wayfarers and grey pilgrims would find the Great Forest Orcs the easiest to reach.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr's relationship with the Great Forest Orcs settled in Therunin was noted to have slowly improved.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar was to remain in Zenith to clear the Druj remnants, and the Druj destruction of Zenith's libraries was invoked as a reason for vengeance.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Karass of the Barrens were believed to be distant kin of the Menrothat sept in Ossium.

The silent page.o: Imperial armies invading the Barrens, led by the Valiant Pegasus and Gryphon's Pride, held back from full conquest to reach out to the territory's embittered inhabitants. This created Synod mandate opportunities to approach one of six local factions, and competing mandates either embracing or condemning the cry "Death to the Druj".

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: Imperial forces advanced towards the Fangs, the vital mithril resource here, but chose not to take them. The Black Wind orcs, once based around the Fangs, now fight for the Druj out of hatred for the Empire.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: The remaining Great Forest Orcs in the Barrens dwell mostly here, a weak faction but the easiest for Imperial envoys to approach.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: Hope's Rest was captured by the Imperial attack, and surviving Montanians scattered into the surrounding mountains offered to show the Empire "how to make swords".

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish yeofolk still living here were among those the Empire could approach.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: The secretive and pragmatic Vendarri orcs dwell here, their home flooded by storms on the Bitter Sea; they might be persuaded to switch sides while victory over the Druj seems likely.

The Barrens/The Untrod Groves.t: The tepel Varag Soulflayer had set up camp here with arkad troops to turn captured Montanians into tortured souls, and the Champion of Vigilance was responsible for killing him.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Menrothat sept here was said to be related to the Karass and to have had a similar relationship with the Druj.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj torture of the people of Reikos was cited as a reason for the cry "Death to the Druj".

The Barrens.t: Imperial armies held the line here rather than conquer outright, seeking to win over its six rival factions against the Druj. A tepel's camp in the territory threatened 500 additional casualties among Imperial armies unless the Champion of Vigilance acted.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs who fled the Barrens were settled here by treaty on condition they help defend it, and most of their leadership dwells here.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar would stay to cleanse Druj remnants, and the despoiling of its libraries was invoked against the Druj.

The stars aren't right.d: Bregasland and Kallavesa were protected for three months by what magicians identified as the Dripping Echoes of the Fen, curtailing Jotun raiders; an entire band of orc raiders was found drowned in southern Bregasland. A thirtieth-magnitude Night effect still concealed the northern Bay of Catazar. Drawing the Penumbral Veil shrouded Madruga (high forties), Zenith (low thirties) and Tassato (weaker), distorting their night skies, and Madruga saw a rain of harmless Sumaah frogs. Two weeks before the Winter Solstice, Thule magicians used ilium to make the Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae a permanent physical fortress in the Silver Peaks, almost certainly with the Eternal's consent, achieving about a year's construction overnight. Shroud rituals were also reclassified as shrouds rather than enchantments or curses.

Jotun.t: The marsh enchantments in Bregasland and Kallavesa were raised specifically to defend against the Jotun, curtailing their raiders, and a band of orc raiders was found drowned in southern Bregasland.

The Brass Coast.t: Madruga bore the most powerful Penumbral Veil, its night skies wildly unnatural, and a rain of harmless Sumaah frogs there gave Freeborn children new pets.

The League.t: Tassato remained under a Penumbral Veil, the weakest of the three but still impressive, frustrating any attempt to scry the territory.

The Marches.t: Bregasland's fens were guarded for three months by phantasmal protectors, quicksand and mists that spared Marchers while thwarting thieves, rustlers and orc raiders.

Thule.t: Thule magicians permanently bound the Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae into the Silver Peaks with ilium, almost certainly in collusion with the Eternal, and are already expanding it with white granite.

Urizen.t: Zenith remained shrouded by a potent Penumbral Veil in the low thirties, distorting its night skies and blocking divination.

Wintermark.t: Kallavesa's marshes were protected against the Jotun by the Dripping Echoes of the Fen, while in Sermersuaq the Thule raised a permanent fortress in the Silver Peaks.

The stars aren't right.o: In Winter 379YE a round-up of magical phenomena across the Empire reported protective night enchantments on the western marshes, continuing shrouds over the northern Bay of Catazar, Madruga, Zenith and Tassato, and the Thule permanently binding the Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae into the Silver Peaks with ilium.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: An overnight ritual made the Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae a permanent physical fortress on one of the highest peaks, roughly a year's construction, now being further fortified with white granite.

Bay of Catazar.t: An eerie glowing fog of thirtieth magnitude still clung to the northern shores, concealing even its own nature; a powerful Eye of the High Places might examine it.

Bregasland.t: For three months the fens were protected by night magic, lost thieves were caught and an entire band of orc raiders was found drowned in southern Bregasland.

Kallavesa.t: The western Wintermark marshes shared the Dripping Echoes of the Fen protection, with phantasmal guardians aiding travellers and deterring Jotun raiders.

Madruga.t: Madruga carried the strongest Penumbral Veil, in the high forties, with extra moons, red stars and vanished skies at night, plus a rain of Sumaah frogs in autumn.

Sermersuaq.t: The Thule permanently raised the Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae, a castle of unmelting ice and adamant stone with an inhuman garrison, in Sermersuaq's Silver Peaks.

Tassato.t: Tassato's night skies were altered by the least potent of the three Penumbral Veils, which still blocks scrying of the territory.

Zenith.t: Zenith's skies showed misplaced stars and wrong moon phases under a Penumbral Veil in the low thirties.

The sweetest of songs.d: The Senate's free trade pact with Sumaah, the Commonwealth and Axos boosted fleets trading there but cost the treasury. Its embargo on Jarm led the House of Princes to outlaw trade with Imperials, closing the Pallas Docks and emptying the Jarmish Lodge. The Thule Dragons freed all slaves, sought recompense for storm damage and completed Eldfell in Miechernya. Faraden's new Liege ended foreign slavery and offered the Gloaming Road as an Imperial title. Sarcophan offered port access in return for free trade. Mathilda Fisher was coming to seek a treaty for a 'Free Bregas'. Kaliact finished two Spiral forts with Jarmish help, and Asavea fell silent.

Dawn.t: Lord Colwynn de Rondell, Dawn's Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy, was due to meet the Suranni envoy Ser Pippin at Anvil, and the Modnos price on his heart was rescinded.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; the page only alludes to the malign force at the centre of Spiral, against which the Grendel trade protective building knowledge.

Grendel.t: Governor Rahab of Feroz remained furious and was shipping in slaves from Tathar at his own expense. Salt Lord Kaliact kept Spiral's freedoms and finished Suilven and the walled Palace of Apulian, apparently with Jarmish magicians' enchantments.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orc prisoners in Faraden would be freed or allowed to seek ransom like other foreigners rather than handed to the Jotun, and Ashborn Pakt of the Imperial Orcs remained Ambassador to Asavea.

Jotun.t: Mathilda Fisher came with the backing of the Jotun of Narkyst to seek Bregasland's neutrality, failing which a Jotun invasion of Mitwold and Mournwold was likely. The Jotun also paid off the debts of orcs enslaved in Faraden and took them into their hands.

The League.t: Erasmo di Tassato, the League's Ambassador to Faraden, was praised by the Faraden and arranged restitution over Moonwater Hall. League cities felt Jarm's trade ban and the Sarcophan enclave in Sarvos.

The Marches.t: The Marcher assembly rejected Mathilda Fisher's claim to Bregasland, where the Strong Reeds and House Greywater still resisted. Yet households in Mitwold and the western Mourn feared the Jotun invasion that refusing a treaty might bring.

Thule.t: The Dragons freed all Thule slaves and expected the Senate to lift sanctions, though their caste society was otherwise unchanged. They sought recompense for storm-damaged mines, completed Eldfell and offered to trade at the Winter Markets.

Urizen.t: Urizen citizens paid to weave mithril nets into Kaliact's Spiral fortifications reported Jarmish magicians enchanting them. Some in Urizen suggested the Marchers should also give up land for peace.

Varushka.t: Varushkans remaining in Miechernya were forced to pay heavy taxes to their new Thule overlords, though some lowlanders were curious about the orcs' trade. Yevgeni Katzev of Varushka remained Ambassador to Otkodov.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark artisans still enslaved by the Thule were freed and were being sent back over the border, and the fort of Eldfell now secured the eastern end of what Wintermark called Wulfric's Fall.

The sweetest of songs.o: After the Summer Solstice 384YE, the Empire joined its Liberty Pact allies in free trade and an embargo on Jarm, and Jarm cut all ties in return. The Thule and the Faraden both abolished slavery and asked for sanctions to be lifted, while Sarcophan, Bregasland, Iron Confederacy, Grendel and Asavean affairs also moved on.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: Mentioned in passing: Gravenmarch is named as lying within striking distance of Meade should the Jotun advance.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: The Thule-held Krevsaty was among the regions ravaged by the Solstice storms, harming its farms and mines.

Miekarova/Miechernya.t: The Thule finished building Eldfell here, overlooking the passes to Otkodov. Their settlers taxed the remaining Varushkans harshly while offering ore, mana and furs for food at the Winter Markets.

Mournwold/Green March.t: The orcs of Green March feared that a Jotun invasion would return them to thralldom under their former masters.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: The storms ravaged Thule-held Bonewood, damaging orc farms and mines.

Ossium/Webwood.t: The storms ravaged Thule-held Webwood, damaging orc farms and mines.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The storms hit the Thule-held Silver Peaks hard, though the Thule seers expected a crop of magical healing herbs to follow.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Crow's Ridge suffered storm damage to its Thule settlements, part of the grievance over which the Thule sought Senate recompense.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: Salt Lord Kaliact completed the fortification of Suilven in Ossuary, guarding the southern end of the Twilight Gate, probably with Jarmish magic.

Tassato/Enterio.t: Mentioned in passing: Enterio is not named; the page touches Tassato only through its flooded streets and the Jarmish Lodge and Mana Exchange losses.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: ships in the Bay reported vessels carrying many slaves from Fort Fuil into Feroz.

Bregasland.t: The Jotun-backed 'Steward' Mathilda Fisher sought Senate recognition of Bregasland as a neutral 'Free Nation of Bregas', while the Strong Reeds and House Greywater fought on against the invaders.

Feroz.t: With most Freeborn evacuated, Governor Rahab was importing slaves from Tathar at great personal expense to replace their labour.

Karsk.t: The Solstice storms ravaged the Thule-held region of Krevsaty, damaging orc farms and mines.

Miekarova.t: The Thule completed the fortification of Eldfell in Miechernya, and their settlers taxed the remaining Varushkans while offering to trade at the Winter Markets.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold faced the prospect of Jotun invasion if no treaty over Bregasland was secured.

Mournwold.t: The western Mourn feared Jotun attack: Meade lay within striking distance of Gravenmarch, and the orcs of Green March dreaded a return to thralldom.

Ossium.t: The magical storms struck the Thule-held regions of Bonewood and Webwood, harming orc farms and mines.

Otkodov.t: The Thule of Otkodov promised to welcome Imperial merchants if the Senate lifted its sanctions, and the new fort of Eldfell overlooked the passes into their land.

Sarvos.t: The Sarcophan enclave at the old Alivetti Estates prospered but gained a reputation for licentiousness, with drugs and services sold that troubled some priests and magistrates.

Sermersuaq.t: The storms ravaged the Thule-held Silver Peaks, damaging orc settlements, farms and mines.

Skarsind.t: The storms ravaged Thule-held Crow's Ridge, adding to the orcs' complaints about damage to their mines.

Spiral.t: Salt Lord Kaliact kept the people of Spiral's freedoms and completed the fortified Palace of Apulian and Suilven in six months, apparently with Jarmish enchantments.

Tassato.t: Tassato's streets were flooded, and Jarm's trade ban emptied the Jarmish Lodge there and reduced the mana reaching the Tassato Mana Exchange.

Tathar.t: Mentioned in passing: Fort Fuil in Tathar was the source of the slaves being shipped into Feroz.

The tale that speaks to your heart.d: Following Maarit Suvidottir's mandate, Imperial fleets fighting Asavea in the Sea of Salt now receive rings, liao, metals and the Frieøyer healing brew 'Oilybrag'. Imperial traders visiting Zemeh also do better business. The Sevenfold Path and Rod and Shield each gain ten liao a season for two fortification rituals. Censor Oxtitocszin declined two Spring curses, showed interest in rituals that help or hinder spies, and denied any dealings with Yaw'nagrah. Gifts were promised for Rafe of Wintermark and for the rescuers of Präst Kauitalic. The Sumaah asked to see the evidence that Vardas was not real. They also welcomed Emperor Vesna's letter and said an emissary would deliver a gift to Ambassador Accalon.

Highguard.t: Ambassador Accalon of Highguard was central to the exchanges, and an emissary from the High House of Pride is due at Anvil to present a gift to Accalon at the Highborn camp.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is one of only two nations whose ships did not sail west to aid Sumaah, because the mandate lacked a greater majority there.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is one of only two nations whose ships did not sail west to aid Sumaah, because the mandate lacked a greater majority there.

Wintermark.t: Rafe of Wintermark's mandate to support Sumaah was superseded by Maarit Suvidottir's, but the House of Pride is sending him twenty liao and four bottles of Frygtede øglebryg in thanks.

The tale that speaks to your heart.o: The Sumaah Republic sent its seasonal diplomatic news to the Empire. It thanked Imperial fleets for their help against the Asavean Archipelago, rewarded rituals and rescuers, and reported that its Houses of Virtue had begun recognising Alberto Acciai, rather than Amika, as an exemplar of Courage.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sumaah would rather Asaveans look to Timoj than to Bastion for their understanding of the Way, though they judge spreading the faith more important.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sumaah embassy is in Necropolis, and the civil service could send copies of the Saul and Vardas research there.

The thing with feathers.d: Agramant's heralds began aiding starving Navarr in Therunin and offered boons for Unleash the Beasts Within and Treacher's Quill. Sorin sent the Sepulchral Pontifex to the Imperial Orcs to honour a year of Basalt Citadels at Eoradal. Irra Harah offered the Gryphon's Pride the chance to finish watchtowers in Nesustak Forest, and Llofir asked the Vallornguard to ease the dying in Eastring. Janon sent a ring for the next Shadowed Torchbearer, and the Whisper Gallery turned its attacks on the Magpies, with a skirmish foreseen in Hahnmark. Knights of Glory continued to bind armies, prompting a possible Highborn mandate. Cathan Canae's test at Hope's Rest needed one final casting, and Estavus finalised an office at Iteri.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Phoenix Rising coven needed one more Frozen Citadel at Hope's Rest to complete Cathan Canae's test. Separately, Irra Harah invited the Gryphon's Pride under Ser Guy of the Twisted Rose to help the Sarangrave rebels build watchtowers.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj appear as the foe behind the Knights of Glory reliance and the Hope's Rest citadel offer, and Agramant would hand out potions taken from Druj remnants in Therunin.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Callidus's herald Multitudo asked the Imperial Ambassador to the Grendel, Starlight Starchaser, to join a private discussion of "sashes and shields".

Highguard.t: Following Frater Pontius's upheld judgement, the Highborn Assembly could enact a mandate for its soldiers to shun heralds. This would restore cautious advance and give ground orders to its armies, but at a cost of 1000 strength when supported by heralds.

Imperial Orcs.t: Sorin's Sepulchral Pontifex came to the Imperial Orc camp to honour the Heralds of the Reaper's year of Basalt Citadels at Eoradal and to weigh an undisclosed offer. Heralds of Ylenwe sought Archmage Skywise Gralka as a guide to dance, and heralds of Janon came to watch the orc fighting pit.

Navarr.t: Navarr cut off in Therunin were increasingly accepting Agramant's aid, and the Howler offered extra strength and Druj potions to Navarr units enchanted with Unleash the Beasts Within. Llofir also asked the Vallornguard to grant peaceful deaths to those suffering in Eastring.

Urizen.t: Estavus finalised plans for an Office of Fire and Stone in Zenith with a new Architect of Hammers title. Agramant offered Urizen magicians foci or a relic for performing Treacher's Quill on Therunin, and Bartimaeus was named a "Prince" of Callidus's auction.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka's territory Ossium was named among the conquests discussed when the now-broken Fist of the Black Glacier ritual was first awarded.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Vanja Oddsbreaker, the first Shadowed Torchbearer, had vacated her post, prompting Janon to send a ring for her successor. A Whisper Gallery attack on the Magpies near Gulnar's Depths in Hahnmark was foreseen as a skirmish for the following summit.

The thing with feathers.o: In Winter 387YE a host of eternals reached out to the Empire with offers, challenges and warnings. Among them were Agramant tempting the beleaguered Navarr of Therunin, Cathan Canae's test at Hope's Rest nearing completion, Irra Harah's watchtowers for Nesustak Forest and Estavus's finalised Office of Fire and Stone in Zenith.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: The ruins of Eoradal had hosted Sorin's Basalt Citadel every season for a year, earning the Silent Kingdom's notice.

Reikos/Chalcis Mount.t: Mentioned in passing: a haggard group of Navarr crossed out of Therunin into Chalcis Mount to warn of Agramant's activities.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: If the Gryphon's Pride gave a supporting defensive order, rebel watchtowers would be finished by Spring 388YE, removing the region's under-threat status.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: One more Frozen Citadel would make Hope's Rest Rimebound, empowering Summer enchantments there. It would also offer Dawn a permanent Citadel of the Rimebound Shore for 100 rings of ilium.

The Barrens/The Bleaks.t: Mentioned in passing: the Last Battle Wayhouse in the Bleaks was the source of the threat hanging over Nesustak Forest.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Llofir asked the Speaker of the Vallornguard to travel with the vines to Eastring and give painless deaths to those who could not be saved, near a strangely behaving vallornspawn briar.

Zenith/Iteri.t: The proposed Office of Fire and Stone would stand at the Crucible of Fate in Iteri. It would let heralds of Estavus enter there regardless of alignment.

Hahnmark.t: Servants of the Whisper Gallery attacked Magpies near Gulnar's Depths, where Vanya Heartsworn may have found a clue to the lost hammer Avalanche. A skirmish there was foreseen for the Spring Equinox.

Mareave.t: The Heralds of the Reaper's year-long defence of Mareave with the Basalt Citadel won the grudging respect of Sorin's Monarch of the Silent Kingdom.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium was one of the conquests whose strategy generals once discussed with a castellan of Cathan Canae.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mourningstone Navarr escaped from Therunin across the border into Chalcis Mount in Reikos to bring their warning.

Sarangrave.t: The Sarangrave rebels sought the Gryphon's Pride's help to build watchtowers in Nesustak Forest. The lasting effects of Knights of Glory on armies were observed most clearly here.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq was named among the conquests discussed when the Fist of the Black Glacier ritual was awarded.

The Barrens.t: A final Frozen Citadel at Hope's Rest would complete Cathan Canae's test, bringing a permanent wintry quality and a strong citadel offer to the southern Barrens.

Therunin.t: Agramant's heralds were active in Therunin, buying the loyalty of desperate Navarr with aid. Llofir also sought peaceful deaths for those suffering after fighting vallornspawn in Eastring.

Zenith.t: The Architects of Iron and Stone finalised an Office of Fire and Stone at the Crucible of Fate in Zenith, available to commission until the end of Autumn 388YE.

The three pillars.d: The Zenith senator's motion to have Urizeni generals appoint the Warmage failed scrutiny. The Court instead had the Speaker raise two alternatives. Either would make the Warmage an Urizeni national title, appointed by Urizeni magicians in the Hall of Worlds or by the Senate. Each needs a two-thirds constitutional vote and the Throne's ratification. If either passes, Tiborion of the Endless Horizen's followers will stand down and move to Zenith, Morrow or Redoubt. Actius is already satisfied, so the Empire would regain Ankra. Caela of the Silver Flame still holds Cinion, waiting for a Grendel conquest. Two conjunctions target Grendel near the Black Plateau and a raid on the Legacy.

Grendel.t: Grendel mercenaries were found sheltering near the Black Plateau, and Maistir Orla's surviving company was moving to raid the Legacy's mithril. Caela's rebels hope Grendel will invade and conquer Spiral.

The League.t: The League's newly allocated territory of Spiral faced open Urizeni secession, though it was growing prosperous on Lorenzo's mana. Taskel Di Apulian, as Custodian of the Legacy, was charged with stopping a Grendel raid on it.

Urizen.t: Urizen was offered a chance to make the Warmage a national position, elected by Urizeni magicians or appointed by the Senate, to win back Tiborion's rebels. Caela's faction still demanded Spiral's return, and the Shuttered Lantern was sent to investigate.

The three pillars.o: In Spring 386YE, rebel Urizeni spires held parts of Spiral after the territory was allocated to the League. The Constitutional Court offered two constitutional motions to make the Warmage an Urizeni national position, which would end Tiborion's rebellion in Ankra. Grendel mercenaries also threatened Spiral.

Spiral/Ankra.t: Ankra remained in rebel hands, but the Empire would regain control if the Senate passes either Warmage motion, since more than half the rebels would stand down.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Cinion stayed under Caela of the Silver Flame's control whatever happens and was not considered under Imperial control.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: Maistir Orla's mercenaries had been assumed to have fled across the mountains to Mareave.

Morrow.t: Morrow is one of the territories where Tiborion's magicians would resettle and petition to rejoin the Empire if a Warmage motion passes.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt is one of the territories where Tiborion's magicians would resettle and petition to rejoin the Empire if a Warmage motion passes.

Spiral.t: Spiral's spires in Ankra and Cinion remained in open revolt against League rule. Grendel mercenaries lurked near the Black Plateau and threatened the Legacy.

Zenith.t: Zenith's senator raised the failed Warmage motion, and the territory is one of the possible new homes for Tiborion's returning rebels.

The troubled words.d: Achille di Sarvos commissioned the Holberg Scholars of the Sword Academy, with the Master of Defence as custodian. The Urizen Assembly announced that Cato Hypation and Clytemnestra would teach there, and other sword scholars followed. The League Assembly could enact a mandate urging bravos to remember Alexander von Holberg and embrace the philosophy, or Erasmo di Tassato's variant invoking Emperor Frederick and calling for more teachers. Either would raise the Master's stipend by a third and spark political interest among bravos. Opposing mandates would curtail the Academy's cultural influence and cut its income by a third. If nothing is done, sword scholar ideas will slowly spread. The Lepidean Librarian might commission research into Alexander.

The League.t: The League Assembly faces a choice over whether Holberg's bravos should embrace sword scholar philosophy and the legacy of Alexander von Holberg, risking a radical, Synod-sceptical movement, or reject it to preserve tradition.

Urizen.t: Urizeni sword scholars, led by Cato Hypation and Clytemnestra, have taken up teaching in Holberg, offering a chance to spread their philosophy of independence from the Synod beyond Urizen.

The troubled words.o: After a new sword academy was commissioned in Holberg and Urizeni sword scholars agreed to teach there, the League Assembly was given the opportunity to decide whether Holberg's bravos should embrace or reject the sword scholars' philosophy, which echoes the executed local preacher Alexander von Holberg.

Holberg.t: Holberg hosts the new sword academy, and its bravos may embrace or reject the sword scholars' teachings, either igniting a philosophical and political renaissance or confining the Academy to mere swordsmanship.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: renewed interest in the inspiration of Ratibor of Temeschwar is cited as a reason opposition to the Synod may arise sooner.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Clytemnestra's defence of threatening to dissolve the Citadel Guard is cited as having forced the Empire to free Zenith.

The truth but tell it slant.d: Impressed by Tassato's use of movable type, Gelberg proposed three options. The first was a Printers' Guild Grand Guildhouse in Tassato Mestra, raising the Guild's Museum and Mausoleum incomes, allowing a publication to be spread each season, and granting one address to the Empire. The second was a Bibliopole offering translated publications in Betovering and Leerdam. The third was a Publishing Clearing House great work, adding 36 rings to every Tassato business and boosting the Printmaster of Cevia. Carina Schiver added an edifice to renovate Moor's Mill in Tassato Regario, promoting ringblack novels. If the Chair of the Wolf commissioned any of these, extra benefits would follow. All remain proposals.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is named as a place where interest in ringblack novels would grow if Moor's Mill were supported.

The League.t: The League's printers, guilds and Chair of the Wolf were offered several commissions that could make Tassato the printing centre of the Empire, or even the world. One option would also foster a new literary movement of ringblack novels celebrating League vigilance.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: travellers from Thule's Otkodov might take an interest in the proposed Publishing Clearing House.

The truth but tell it slant.o: Professor Immanuel Gelberg's Commonwealth appraisers, working under the Beurteilung at the Printers' Guild's request, proposed three commissions to expand printing in Tassato, plus a student's subsidiary plan to revive the struggling Moor's Mill guild.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Tassato Mestra, home to the Printers' Guild enclave, was the proposed site of both the Grand Guildhouse and the riverside Publishing Clearing House.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: Tassato Regario's Moor's Mill printworks, revived by youths printing "Stories of the Vigilant", could be renovated as an edifice. If consecrated by the Vigilance assembly, it might inspire League vigilance.

Bastion.t: If the Chair of the Wolf completed the Moor's Mill investment, Esmeralda di Rodez offered to donate a relic of Berechiah to the title running Berechiah's Basilica in Bastion. This would follow once both relevant commissions were complete.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Chair of the Wolf, the title able to gain extra benefits from these commissions, was established in Holberg with the support of its College of Engineering.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: travellers from Otkodov are named as potential visitors drawn by the Publishing Clearing House.

Tassato.t: Tassato stood to gain a grand guildhouse, a Publishing Clearing House adding 36 rings to every business in the territory, and a renovated Moor's Mill press. Together these would cement the city as the Empire's centre of printing.

The tune without the words.d: Agents of the Moonsilver King prompted the addition of Bells of Silver and Brass and Might of Vstaive to Urizen lore. A gift for Ibiss Briarheart added three illegal Siakha rituals. The Children of Wrecks' Thunderous Deluge battered Madruga, Feroz and Sarvos, where flood defences saved the city but Riposi's cliffs collapsed. Night magic in Madruga stirred rebellious sentiment, empowered a transformative pool and offered marsh flowers. Strange dreams touched the Gullet territories, and coral husks took the dead into the sea. Conjunctions were raised in Hercynia and Therunin. The Crimson Reapers announced an auction of the Loom of Spells, the last faux constellations vanished from memory, and the Silent Market reopened.

Dawn.t: The Roses of Racqueen, a Weaver cabal from Semmerholm, contributed Might of Vstaive to Urizen lore. Strangers sought tales of fear in Astolat and Weirwater, and Dawnish folk in the Barrens heard the Navarri song in their dreams.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as destroyers of the Halls of Knowledge and as overrunning Therunin, driving out the Glimmerwater steading.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel are not named; their link is through Feroz, which the cursed storms struck heavily.

Highguard.t: Strangers asking for stories of fear were reported on the roads to Casinea, and unfamiliar faux constellations had earlier appeared over Necropolis.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is listed among the territories where faux constellations appeared after the Spring Equinox.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are noted as claiming Bregasland and pressing the Fenlanders, and the Green Shield's attack into Skallahn is referred to.

Navarr.t: Nathair Autumngale's arcane projection spread dreams of the song Painted to every Navarr, offering pride in their oaths. Navarri also face a disturbing conjunction in Hercynia, and the Glimmerwater steading has fled Therunin with its merrow lantern.

The Brass Coast.t: Cursed storms battered Madruga and Feroz, while Night magic in Madruga stirred a rebellious love of liberty against Azir i Shartha i Riqueza's statement on Anarchy. It also strengthened naga and briar trappings at a Crucible pool and opened a chance to grow marsh flowers.

The League.t: Sarvos weathered the Thunderous Deluge thanks to Senator Rosalina Gulia Viola di Sarvos's flood defences, though Riposi was ravaged. Spiral remains steeped in dramaturgical magic, and the Crimson Reapers will auction use of the Loom of Spells.

The Marches.t: Mitwold folk shared strange dreams tied to the Gullet. Bill of Middleton, Keeper of the Dour Fens, must lead a group against coral husks in North Fens.

Urizen.t: Five new rituals entered Urizen lore: two that restore and strengthen garrisons, and three illegal Siakha rituals. Urizeni in Spiral continue to experience its theatrical strangeness.

Varushka.t: Strangers asking for tales of fear were encountered across all five Varushkan territories. Faux constellations had earlier hung over Karov.

Wintermark.t: Kallavesa saw strange Gullet dreams, and coral husks massed in West Marsh and Stark, to be dealt with by the Watcher of Britta's Pool and the Academy. The Silent Market made an offer to Wintermark casters for provably Hahnmark viezesmaak.

The tune without the words.o: A Winter 387YE roundup of strange magical events across the Empire. Five new rituals entered Urizen lore, cursed storms struck Madruga, Feroz and Sarvos, coral husks massed around the Gullet, and a Navarri arcane projection spread a song through the trods.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Coral husks are massing here. Bill of Middleton, Keeper of the Dour Fens, must lead a group to cut them down, with lethal force fully justified.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: The Thunderous Deluge reached as far west as Morajasse, drenching the region.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The flooded Scorrero added to the hardship of reclaiming Oranseri and will make bridging the river harder.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: Coral husks that killed warriors on the coast are hunting the marsh for more dead. The Watcher of Britta's Pool, Rafe, is to stop them.

Madruga/Crucible.t: Night heralds were most often met around Crucible. Its rainbow fountain flooded into a pool that intensifies naga and briar trappings.

Madruga/Torres.t: The cursed rains fell as far north as Torres.

Redoubt/Willstone.t: The Shield of Thought coven of Willstone Citadel submitted Bells of Silver and Brass to the Canterspire Library.

Sarvos/Riposi.t: Riposi's southern cliffs collapsed into the sea during the storms, stripping topsoil from its farms. The region has permanently become coastal.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: Coral husks were sighted near Stark by Jimothy o' Hay. Chancellor Hildebrand Von Holberg is to send Academy cadets to investigate.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Those in Apulus were likely to get lost in unfamiliar parts of the city and stumble into dramatic productions.

Therunin/Eastring.t: The Glimmerwater steading abandoned its flooded Day regio in Eastring after attacks by chikad and vallornspawn husks.

Astolat.t: Travellers reported strangers on the roads asking for stories of fear and paying a token ingot or two in thanks.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Bastion is not named; it falls only within the general account of the vanished penumbral veils and faux constellations.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not named; the page touches on related sea-storm magic of Siakha and her Children of Wrecks.

Bregasland.t: Sensitive folk had vivid dreams linked to the Gullet, and coral husks massed in North Fens to drag away the dead.

Brocéliande.t: Nathair Autumngale led hundreds of Navarr through the Sentinel Gate to a Night regio here to cast An Ode To Blood And Sacrifice. The song dreams spread outward from here along the trods.

Casinea.t: Strangers asking for tales of fear were met on the roads to Casinea. The territory was one of the few untouched by the penumbral veils.

Feroz.t: The Thunderous Deluge hit rebuilding Feroz hard, flooding the Scorrero and soaking makeshift homes. Wisps of Madruga's Night enchantment spilled over, letting herb gardens be diversified to grow marsh flowers.

Hahnmark.t: The Silent Market offered Wintermark casters narcotics or Imperial Roseweald or Cerulean Mazzarine in exchange for viezesmaak sworn to come from Hahnmark's farms. Faux constellations had earlier hung overhead.

Hercynia.t: An injured Navarri reported troubling events at the remote Starwood Roots Steading. The Archmage of Winter is charged with investigating a conjunction there involving gore and hints of cannibalism.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is listed among the territories where faux constellations appeared around the Summer Solstice.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa was one of the centres of the strange Gullet dreams, and coral husks are hunting for corpses in West Marsh.

Karov.t: Strangers seeking stories of fear walked Karov's roads as in the rest of Varushka, and faux constellations had earlier appeared above it.

Madruga.t: Madruga was soaked by cursed storms and wrapped in Night magic that brought transformative dreams, active heralds of Azoth and Janon, and a fierce urge for liberty. It also opened chances to grow marsh flowers and seek hallows of Anarchy.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold was one of the main territories where folk dreamed of floods, drowned seas and a terrible living thing in warm waters.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is not named; it falls only within the general account of the vanished penumbral veils and faux constellations.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold is listed as untouched by the penumbral veils, yet also among the places where faux constellations appeared after the Spring Equinox.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis is listed among the territories where faux constellations appeared after the Spring Equinox.

Redoubt.t: The Shield of Thought coven of Willstone Citadel contributed Bells of Silver and Brass to Urizen lore. Redoubt's lightstone is mentioned in the opening tale.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarangrave is excluded from the lingering urge to recall the vanished faux constellations.

Sarvos.t: Wreckers used the Circle of Savagery to curse Sarvos with months of storms. Flood defences built with the Vandersaar family protected the City of Masks, though Rodez, Trivento and Riposi suffered.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sea of Snow is not named; the page's sea-related events concern the Gullet and other waters.

Semmerholm.t: The Roses of Racqueen, a Weaver cabal from Semmerholm, gave Might of Vstaive to Urizen lore in return for undisclosed boons. Faux constellations had earlier hung over the territory.

Sermersuaq.t: Jimothy o' Hay spotted coral husks in Stark, and the Academy's students are to investigate.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Green Shield's attack into Skallahn is referred to in passing.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is listed among the territories where faux constellations appeared after the Spring Equinox.

Spiral.t: Spiral's theatrical magical convocation has grown stronger, filling the city with drama. Resident League and Urizen citizens can draw on the dramaturgical personae and Night magicians gain lore.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is listed among the territories where faux constellations appeared after the Spring Equinox.

The Barrens.t: The Navarri song dreams spread first to the Last Battle Wayhouse in the Barrens, where people of Dawn and some orcs also heard them.

Therunin.t: Overrun by Druj and the vallorn, Therunin has lost the Glimmerwater steading, which fled west with its merrow lantern. Therunin was also untouched by the penumbral veils.

Weirwater.t: Strangers asking for tales of dread were reported on Weirwater's roads, paying ingots for the stories.

The twentieth empress.d: Lisabetta, founder of the House of Seven Mirrors and Prince of the Hearthfire Guild of Arms and Artisans, rose swiftly after her first Anvil summit in Winter 378YE, serving as Conscience of the Senate and then as proxy to the Warmage. After nearly a year of campaigning she won the Senate's support. Her coronation was to begin with a procession through the ten nations, ending with her chosen Cardinal crowning her. Asavea, Jarm, the Commonwealth, Faraden, Axos and Sarcophan, along with the Grendel, Jotun and Thule orcs, signalled they would send gifts. Historians wondered whether she would challenge Dawn for the title of monarch.

Dawn.t: Empress Lisabetta might challenge for the title of Monarch of Dawn, though as a League citizen she could not fight in the resulting tourney and would need Dawnish nobles to fight on her behalf; no Throne has sought it since Empress Brannan.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: an in-character civil servant had compared citizens who fail to address the Throne properly to the Druj, a remark that was edited out.

Grendel.t: The Grendel informed the civil service that they intended to send gifts to the new Empress in recognition of her coronation.

Jotun.t: The Jotun informed the civil service that they intended to send gifts to the new Empress in recognition of her coronation.

The League.t: A League citizen, Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, became the twentieth Throne of the Empire, with roots in Tassato, Temeschwar and Holberg.

Thule.t: The Thule informed the civil service that they intended to send gifts to the new Empress in recognition of her coronation.

The twentieth empress.o: The Senate appointed Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg of the League as the twentieth Empress, elected during the Spring Equinox 380YE, with her formal coronation set for the Summer Solstice.

Holberg.t: The new Empress takes her name from Holberg, where six years earlier she established a new branch of her family's Hearthfire Guild after becoming its Prince.

Tassato.t: The Empress's mother, Elise Giacomi, is of Tassato, and Lisabetta studied music and philosophy at the prestigious University of Tassato.

Temeschwar.t: The Empress's father, Gyorgy Yakovitch, is of Temeschwar, home of her family's long-established Hearthfire Guild of Arms and Artisans.

The two of us.d: Dawn's enchanters have until the Summer Solstice to choose and agree terms with Summer eternals. Eleonaris stands ready and would resent being passed over; Hayaak refuses outright, demanding the head of the long-dead Ser Edric du Gauvain; most others want a giant statue, while Adamant has offered an alternative through the Master of the Koboldi. Jaheris will not share patronage with Eleonaris, but would accept her existing statue being magically altered to depict him for a year, at the cost of her wrath falling on someone. Alternatively, Dawn could turn wholly to Winter eternals, which Eleonaris would ignore. The egregores proposed a meeting at 2pm on Saturday to decide.

Dawn.t: Dawn's enchanters and enchantresses must decide whether to court the Summer eternals, try the Jaheris statue gambit or switch entirely to Winter to secure patrons for the Eastern Sky, with their egregores calling a meeting to settle the matter.

Jotun.t: Rumour holds that the Jotun jarls declined the Gryphon-King's free offer as a likely trap, only grudgingly allowing a handful of his heralds to take the field with their kirkja after the Queen of Glory took offence.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is cited as a place where Night magic has reportedly changed a statue's appearance at least twice before.

The two of us.o: Lady Nimue de Moraine's scheme for the enchantresses of Dawn to win five Summer eternals as patrons of the Eastern Sky moved forward, with the eternals setting out their terms and two alternative approaches, a Night-magic trick on Eleonaris' statue and a turn to the Winter realm, put forward.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is noted as where Night magic has apparently altered statues at least twice, as precedent for disguising Eleonaris' statue as Jaheris.

The virtue of sharing.d: Simon of Haros and Ulla Redstaff would back Houses of Healing in Elerael only after a public inquisition, by a Highborn or Urizeni inquisitor, of those behind accepting Druj aid. Imperial Inquisitor Galene Netherwatch inquisitioned Harwyn Eternal and judged him and the Spring archmage totally vindicated, upheld by the General Assembly. Both then offered support, but the Houses were never commissioned and the chance passed. Hazelelponi's Highborn mandate sent congregations to aid Dark Ranging, about 1,400 strength, yet no Imperial army came. New mandates were proposed: Dawnish and Highborn rewards for units fighting there, a Dawnish congregational sacrifice, and Highborn or Navarr commitments to fight only in Brocéliande. Only the Dawnish reward mandate was enacted.

Dawn.t: Ranae de Rondell enacted the mandate urging Dawnish houses to reward any knight who fights to reclaim Dark Ranging, granting Dawnish units extra crowns and herbs for a year. A congregational sacrifice of votes and liao was also proposed but not enacted.

Druj.t: The alliance by which Druj orcs aided the eternal Arhallogen in Brocéliande prompted demands for public inquisition and condemnation of those responsible, though the Conclave did not condemn the alliance.

Highguard.t: Highborn congregations bore a year-long sacrifice under Hazelelponi's mandate, sending pilgrims and supplies worth about 1,400 strength to Dark Ranging only to find no army there. Mandates were proposed to reward guardians who fight there and to commit Highborn soldiers solely to Brocéliande.

Navarr.t: The Navarr Assembly condemned accepting Druj aid, and Harwyn Eternal faced inquisition and was vindicated. Corey Wayfarer proposed a mandate binding Navarr armies to fight the vallorn until Brocéliande is free, while Highborn pilgrims helped Navarr steadings rebuild.

Urizen.t: An Urizeni inquisitor was named acceptable to conduct the inquisition, and the Urizeni Imperial Inquisitor Galene Netherwatch carried it out, returning a judgement of total vindication.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: a Dawnish troubadour jokes that Dark Ranging is no more Navarr land than Ossium was Varushkan.

The virtue of sharing.o: Dawnish and Highborn assemblies sought to learn from each other in supporting the reconquest of Dark Ranging from the vallorn, while a demand for a public inquisition into the Druj alliance in Brocéliande ended with Galene Netherwatch vindicating Harwyn Eternal. Ranae de Rondell later enacted a mandate rewarding Dawnish knights who fight in Dark Ranging.

Brocéliande/Dark Ranging.t: Dark Ranging is the target of the proposed reconquest, with Highborn pilgrims already there and an enacted mandate rewarding Dawnish units that support armies fighting in the region for a year.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Houses of Healing were proposed for Elerael, with backing conditional on the inquisition; support was eventually offered, but they were never commissioned and the opportunity passed.

Brocéliande.t: The Highborn, Dawnish and Navarr assemblies focused on reclaiming Dark Ranging from the vallorn, but the Imperial armies expected there never arrived, leaving congregational aid to support recovery and the fight against the Heirs of Terunael.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: cited in a troubadour's jest that Ossium was once no more Varushkan than Dark Ranging is Navarr.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the places two Dawnish adventurers had travelled through before coming to Brocéliande.

The war makers.d: The Senate approved the army at the Spring Equinox 387YE on a motion by Rowyn of the Waystone Path, Senator for Hercynia, seconded by Tristan du Lac, Senator for Weirwater. The artisans of Dawn, the Marches, Varushka and the Imperial Orcs backed it, and Navarr gave more than eight hundred measures and ingots. Fifteen months later, after Cabal Lyktan's Hammers of Fury on Hercynia, the army was nearly ready. Rowyn weighed Siege, Resilient or Resourceful. Most Navarr wanted the lost Isaella's Dance left as a legacy, not reused as a name. The Star Forged was chosen. The ritual's lingering effects also briefly empowered Hercynian artisans and cambions.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn's artisans backed the motion to raise the army, and Weirwater's senator, Tristan du Lac, seconded it.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs supported the motion through the backing of their artisans.

Navarr.t: Navarr gained its third army, the Star Forged, funded from across the nation and raised by the steadings' artisans. The nation now expects another army to follow, and its supply will fall by one if no further Navarr army is approved by the Summer Solstice 389YE.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka supported the motion through the backing of its artisans.

The war makers.o: The third Navarr army, raised in Hercynia around the artisans and runesmiths of Treji, finished mustering, and its raising senator was asked to choose its name and quality. It was named the Star Forged and given the Resourceful quality.

Hercynia.t: The new army was mustered in Hercynia around the forges of Treji. As the Hammers of Fury faded, the Chain shone brightly over the territory for a night, and Hercynian artisans and cambions gained brief potent benefits at the coming summit.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: Tristan du Lac, as Senator for Weirwater, seconded the motion to raise the army.

The war of thorns and flowers.d: With the grey pilgrims home, Highguard could support a fourth army, but the pilgrims refused to serve under the Thundering Tide's name. Banners hallowed with true liao could cut its mithril cost. Virtue's Rest in Bastion could become an army resupply hostel. Else Van Temeschwar proposed tolls on the Empire's major roads, and Varushka was offered sovereign patrons, Irontooth Keep and a Winter-aligned Icy Crag. In the outcome, four banners were hallowed, saving 120 wains, the Pilgrim's Defiance was commissioned, Virtue's Rest was remodelled, and tolls on the Blood Red and White Roads raised 100 thrones a season. Irontooth Keep and the Icy Crag were not taken up.

Dawn.t: Larkin Shrike's call for a War of Thorns and Flowers passed 282-64 without a greater majority, so the nation was not yet committed. Separately, the Knight of the Greenwood was asked to recover Druj herb caches in Brocéliande.

Druj.t: Kaela's Gift let captured Imperial citizens die painlessly beyond their reach. Druj herb caches abandoned in Brocéliande might be reclaimed if Imperial knights failed to recover them.

Highguard.t: The returning grey pilgrims allowed a fourth Highborn army, which they refused to raise under the Thundering Tide's name. Highguard hallowed four banners with true liao, commissioned the Pilgrim's Defiance and remodelled Virtue's Rest.

Navarr.t: Navarr's war on the vallorn was the cause other nations rallied to or refused, with Wintermark declining to support it. Navarr armies were eligible to resupply at Virtue's Rest, and Deer's Folly sought the Spear of the Seven's help against a vallornspawn horde.

The Brass Coast.t: The Sunset Roads were included in the toll proposal and the Freeborn Assembly could have vetoed it, but in the end only the Blood Red and White Roads were tolled. Varushkan armies no longer suffered a penalty for fighting alongside Freeborn armies unless the Freeborn Assembly renewed its concerns.

The League.t: The League Assembly committed its citizens' ambition and ingenuity to the vallorn war, so its other statements of principle would have no effect for a year. Else Van Temeschwar's road-toll scheme led to tolls on the Blood Red and White Roads.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule were named as a possible future threat to Suvretz, one reason to build Irontooth Keep, and the vallornheart in Sküld lies across the border.

Urizen.t: Eurydice Starchaser's statement backing the Navarr's magical army in Miaren passed 150-0 but without a greater majority, so Urizen remained uncommitted despite the threat from Therunin's vallorn.

Varushka.t: Varushka committed to the vallorn war, locking its Assembly's other causes for a year. It could support two more armies and was offered sovereign patronage, Irontooth Keep and a Winter-aligned Icy Crag, though the last two were not taken up. The penalty for fighting beside Freeborn or Wintermark armies was lifted.

Wintermark.t: Ingrid Talon-of-the-Mark's statement that Wintermark cannot support the Navarr above every other threat passed with a greater majority but gave no clear call to action. The Runegrott in Northspires was threatened by a vallornspawn horde.

The war of thorns and flowers.o: In Winter 386YE several Imperial nations prepared for the war against the vallorn. Highguard recalled its grey pilgrims to raise a fourth army, the League proposed road tolls to fund the war, and Varushka looked to dark powers. Dawn, Urizen and Wintermark held back.

Brocéliande/Dark Ranging.t: The Order of the Emerald Dogs came out of Dark Ranging with reports of scattered Druj and abandoned herb stockpiles overrun by vallornspawn.

Hahnmark/Northspires.t: The Runegrott, the region's most substantial construction, was at risk if the vallornspawn horde crossed the border, drawing the interest of its Keeper, Derowen.

Hercynia/Deer's Folly.t: The western steadings faced abandonment unless the Spear of the Seven stopped the advancing vallornspawn horde.

Miekarova/Srodkoja.t: The Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun here could have become a college of Winter magic, but this was not done.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Its vallornheart threatened to spill through the forests into Suvretz if the hearts were linked.

Volodmartz/Suvretz.t: Suvretz was offered Irontooth Keep, a quickly built fortress on old ruins, against vallorn from Sküld and future Thule attack, but it was not commissioned.

Bastion.t: Virtue's Rest was remodelled into hostels where eligible armies can resupply, at the cost of its investment and liao returns, and the title Exarch of Virtue's Rest was created.

Brocéliande.t: Knights-errant found abandoned Druj herb caches amid the vallornspawn, and the Knight of the Greenwood was asked to recover them. Kaela's Gift extends into the territory.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: its Silent Sentinel was cited as the kind of major fortification Irontooth Keep might rival.

Hahnmark.t: A vallornspawn horde from Hercynia threatened to cross into Northspires and attack the Runegrott and its artisans.

Hercynia.t: A horde of vallornspawn husks led by a huge chitinous monster moved through Deer's Folly towards the Northspires border, and the Spear of the Seven was asked to stop it.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Kamkrags of Kahraman were excluded from the road-toll proposal on constitutional grounds.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: Karsk is not named directly and is touched only through wider Varushkan matters such as the debate over tolling the nation's roads.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is not named directly and is touched only through the wider proposal to toll Freeborn roads, which was not adopted.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's statement called for support for the magical army the Navarr planned to raise in Miaren.

Miekarova.t: The Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun could have been realigned from Summer to Winter magic with Cabalist funding, but the opportunity was not taken.

Otkodov.t: The vallornheart in Sküld is the one nearest Varushka, and its forests run unbroken into Suvretz.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: its fortification Remember Exile was cited as a benchmark for Irontooth Keep.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening vignette is set in Temeschwar, where accountant Else Van Temeschwar is confronted over her road-toll recommendations.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the loss of Isaella's Dance and the Iron Helms there was recalled, its vallorn was noted as a threat to Urizen, and Kaela's Gift extends there.

Volodmartz.t: A rank 2 fortification, Irontooth Keep, was proposed for Suvretz to guard against the vallorn and the Thule, but it was not built.

The warmth of an invisible light.d: The rescuers crept over the border and freed soldiers and civilians held by the Druj. Rescued Highborn soldiers returned to their armies, but the civilians, whose spires had been destroyed or despoiled, needed a home. Three mandates were offered. A Urizeni one would commit everything to retaking Zenith, inspiring the Citadel Guard there but penalising them elsewhere. A competing Urizeni one would resettle refugees in Morrow and Redoubt. A Highborn one would shelter orphans, the sick and the wounded in Reikos. The Urizen assembly endorsed resettlement. The refugees can therefore support the Doyen of the Spires as if Zenith were recaptured, raising its cost from 15 to 20 thrones a season and speeding research.

Dawn.t: Dawn supplied a large share of the heroes who crossed into Druj-held Zenith and freed its enslaved people.

Druj.t: The Druj lost more than half of the Zenith captives they had enslaved to a series of daring Imperial raids, though they still held Zenith and were pressing into Spiral.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Spiral, which it held, is described as a place no-one would now choose to settle given the Druj attack there.

Highguard.t: Highborn heroes helped lead the rescue, and the Highborn soldiers freed returned to their armies. A proposed Highborn mandate would have sheltered Urizeni orphans and the wounded in Reikos, though no outcome for it is recorded.

Urizen.t: Many Urizeni held captive in Zenith were freed. The National Assembly chose to resettle them in Morrow and Redoubt rather than stake everything on retaking Zenith, which lets the Doyen of the Spires draw on their scholarship at once.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: bands from Varushka were among the three distant groups that joined the rescue raids into Zenith.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: bands from Wintermark were among the three distant groups that joined the rescue raids into Zenith, and the opening story follows a soldier carrying the winged lion device.

The warmth of an invisible light.o: Several hundred Imperial heroes from Urizen, Dawn, Highguard, the League, Wintermark and Varushka raided Druj-occupied Zenith and freed more than half of its remaining enslaved inhabitants. The Urizen National Assembly then endorsed a mandate urging the rescued refugees to resettle in Morrow and Redoubt.

Morrow.t: Zenith refugees were urged to settle among the spires of Morrow. The territory will strain under the numbers, but sharing the burden with Redoubt should find everyone a home.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt was named as one of the two territories where the Zenith refugees would build new lives, sharing the burden with Morrow and supporting the Doyen of the Spires.

Reikos.t: A Highborn mandate proposed evacuating Urizeni orphans, the sick and the wounded to Reikos for safety, far from the fighting. The page does not record it being enacted.

Spiral.t: Spiral faced a recent Druj attack and advance, and the page notes no-one would now choose to move there.

Zenith.t: Imperial raiders crept into Druj-occupied Zenith and freed more than half its remaining enslaved inhabitants. The chosen resettlement plan means its people will rebuild elsewhere until it is reclaimed.

The way home.d: Eilian Sweetwater's proposal let the Navarr commission a wayhouse sinecure in any non-Navarr Imperial territory with a trod network, outside City regions, with a Navarr keeper. The first wayhouse in a territory would raise Imperial taxation there by eight crowns, and Navarr living nearby would avoid the foreign-nation penalty and share in local great works, though they could not vote for that territory's senator. Three projects were offered: restoring Myfanwy's Rest in Fishguard, Necropolis; the Last Battle Striding's wayhouse beside an enemy territory holding a vallorn heart, which would put that territory's regions under threat; and the Scale and the Source's Primal Forest for sharing magical traditions. The Myfanwy's Rest and Primal Forest opportunities later expired.

Dawn.t: The Plains of Teeth in the Dawnish-held Barrens was named as a possible site for the Last Battle wayhouse, from which Navarr thorns would scout into the Sarangrave.

Druj.t: A Last Battle wayhouse built next to the Druj-held Sarangrave would let Navarr thorns patrol across the border and put the Sarangrave's regions under threat.

Highguard.t: Restoring Myfanwy's Rest in Necropolis promised a steady stream of Highborn visitors, with Navarr historians meeting Highborn archivists, benefactors, grey pilgrims and wayfarers to study the founding of the Empire.

Jotun.t: Liathaven, held by the Jotun and containing a vallorn heart, was named as a territory whose regions would come under threat if the Last Battle wayhouse were built in the neighbouring Grey Fens.

Navarr.t: Navarr gained the means to build wayhouse sinecures with Navarr keepers in other nations' territories, at the price of their residents losing a vote for a senator, and three striding and wayhouse projects sought the nation's support.

The Marches.t: The Grey Fens in Bregasland was named as a possible site for the Last Battle wayhouse, and any wayhouse built in a Marcher territory would raise its Imperial taxation and bring Navarr settlers.

Thule.t: The Scale and the Source suggested the Primal Forest could forge links with the warlocks of Thule-held Otkodov and discuss the vallorn in Sküld.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen was called the obvious choice of nation for the Primal Forest's exchange of magical learning.

Varushka.t: The Primal Forest was pitched as a way to bond Varushkan cabalists with Navarr vates, noting that Varushka borders Sküld.

The way home.o: Following Winifred Blackhawk's Winter Solstice judgement on the importance of the trods and wayhouses, the civil servant Eilian Sweetwater proposed that the Navarr build large wayhouses outside their own territories, presented alongside three specific wayhouse opportunities.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: The Grey Fens was proposed as a home for the Last Battle wayhouse, where Navarr thorns would scout across the border into Liathaven.

Necropolis/Fishguard.t: Fishguard held Myfanwy's Rest, legendary home of the First Empress's companion Myfanwy, and was the site of the proposed restoration with a Navarr Keeper drawing liao and crowns.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Sküld was cited as a place on Varushka's borders where the vallorn could be discussed with the warlocks of Otkodov through the Primal Forest.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland's Grey Fens was offered as an example site for the Last Battle wayhouse, as it borders vallorn-infested Liathaven.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr living in Brocéliande were noted as unable to vote for a senator but still hopeful that one day they might.

Liathaven.t: As an enemy-held territory with a vallorn heart, Liathaven's uncontrolled regions would come under threat if Navarr thorns built a Last Battle wayhouse in the Grey Fens.

Necropolis.t: Necropolis was home to Myfanwy's Rest, the Empire's most famous wayhouse, which Eirian asked the Navarr to restore with a library and a collection of founding-era relics.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov's warlocks and the vallorn in Sküld were cited as reasons a Varushkan-linked Primal Forest wayhouse could prove valuable.

Sarangrave.t: The Sarangrave was named as an enemy territory with a vallorn heart whose regions a Last Battle wayhouse on the Plains of Teeth would put under threat.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens' Plains of Teeth was suggested as a site for the Last Battle wayhouse, giving Navarr thorns a base for patrols into the Sarangrave.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr in Therunin were noted alongside those in Liathaven and Brocéliande as being unable to vote for a senator.

The way that the sunshine gleams.d: Several books sent to the library had carried hidden charms meant to leech knowledge, which instead destroyed it. Phaleron excised the corruption and reconsidered its purpose, choosing to protect and share knowledge rather than hoard it. Books sent by The Celestial Library will now be sealed and destroyed. A replacement ritual, Gift of Knowledge, was to be given to Archmage of Day Gancius della Notte di Sarvos. Phaleron asked the Conclave to seek a Senate-created Emissary of Phaleron title, offered a Declaration of Concord shielding the Anvil Library from hostile heralds, and said its herald Lioc would bring an arcane projection offering sanctuary to the people and books of Morrow and Zenith against the Druj.

Druj.t: The Druj conquest of Zenith and of many spires in Morrow, and their killing or enslavement of Urizeni scholars, has moved Phaleron close to wrath and prompted it to offer sanctuary against them.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the in-character story shows Myfanwy of Teeth Striding and representatives from Therunin's stridings and steadings helping Urizeni plan the evacuation of Canterspire.

Urizen.t: Phaleron's herald Lioc will meet Urizeni magicians at the Autumn Equinox with an arcane projection intended to offer sanctuary to the people of Morrow and Zenith and a refuge for their books and libraries.

The way that the sunshine gleams.o: After a year closed to the Empire following an attack on its archives, the eternal Phaleron announced that it would reopen its doors, offering a new ritual, a proposed Imperial title, protection for the Anvil Library and sanctuary for the Urizeni of Morrow and Zenith.

Morrow.t: With many of Morrow's spires fallen to the Druj, Phaleron offers a potent arcane projection meant to give its people and libraries sanctuary from the invaders.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Myfanwy travels from Therunin, and representatives from almost every striding and steading of Therunin help with the Canterspire evacuation.

Zenith.t: Zenith's spires fell to the Druj before Morrow's, and Phaleron's offered projection is meant to provide sanctuary for its people and books against the Druj.

The whole world.d: Liao rose to 18 rings a dose. Magician-Prince Barbara Radz of Rigia was killed in a coup, the port closed and the Imperial embassy damaged. Sumaah sent a delegation to Anvil under a ceasefire. Nemoria stopped selling herbs and now pays money instead. The architect Almodin Oktístis offered a third seasonal commission in return for a temple to Baddu, but threatened to quit if another of his works was defiled. Faraden declined a theological exchange. Axos offered staged abolition of slavery if trade was sustained. Robec opened to Imperial captains. With Zenith taken by the Druj, the Sarcophan offered cheap white granite, the Axou a deadly fortification design and the Jarmish faster construction to protect Cargo.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is named as one of the preferred sites for a proposed Asavean temple of Baddu the Builder.

Druj.t: Having conquered Zenith, the Druj now threaten Limus and Cargo, and the embassies there are urgently seeking ways to defend the town against them.

Grendel.t: Grendel traders are offering cheap slaves to patrons in Issyk to undermine the Imperial push for abolition in Axos, and their pact with the Sarcophan keeps Sarcophan ships unmolested.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is a preferred site for the proposed temple of Baddu, and the Chantry of the Silver Skull is listed among the places of religious learning.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Seminary of the Hall of the White Ravens and the Legion's Rookery in Skarsind are listed as places for religious debate with Faraden priests.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Faraden merchants transported mithril through Jotun lands, at some expense, for auction through the Bourse.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is named as a preferred site for the proposed Asavean temple of Baddu.

The Brass Coast.t: Work has begun on extending the Blood Red Roads from Anduz in Segura to Madruga, the Iron Confederacy has opened Robec after developments in Feroz, and the Commonwealth ambassador in Siroc has made statements of interest to the Freeborn.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the School of Epistemology is listed as a place of religious learning, and Temeschwar is a preferred site for the proposed temple of Baddu.

The Marches.t: The completed Faraden trading enclave, Moonwater Hall in Upwold, is bringing prosperity to the Marches and drawing more Faraden merchants into the Empire.

Urizen.t: Urizen has lost Zenith to the Druj, and Cargo in Redoubt, with its embassies, docks and nearby runeforge, is now at risk unless the Senate fortifies it with foreign help.

Varushka.t: The architect Almodin Oktístis was enraged that his fortification in Karsk, Aleksandra's Watch, had been defiled, and he warned that any repeat would make him leave the Empire.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Meagenstede Hall is listed among the places of learning for religious debate with Faraden priests.

The whole world.o: In Spring 382YE this diplomatic Wind of Fortune updated the Empire's foreign relations. It reported a violent coup in Rigia, a Sumaah peace delegation coming to Anvil and an Axou proposal to end slavery, and set out Sarcophan, Axou and Jarmish offers to help fortify Cargo against a possible Druj advance.

Redoubt/Limus.t: Limus is the likely starting point of any Druj assault on Redoubt, putting Cargo's embassies, the Concordium and Pallas Docks and the nearby runeforge at risk, and prompting foreign offers to help fortify Cargo.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is one of the preferred central locations for the proposed temple of Baddu the Builder.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan ships regularly visit ports along the Bay, where their pact with the Grendel causes some discontent.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is one of the preferred central locations for the proposed temple of Baddu the Builder.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: developments in Feroz are cited alongside improving relations with the Iron Confederacy.

Karsk.t: Aleksandra's Watch in Karsk was "defiled by philistines" with Senate approval, which nearly drove its architect Almodin Oktístis to quit the Empire.

Madruga.t: Work has begun on extending the Blood Red Roads to Madruga, which will give Faraden merchants easy access across the Empire.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is one of the preferred central locations for the proposed temple of Baddu the Builder.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: the new runeforge lies a short walk from Cargo along the road towards Necropolis.

Redoubt.t: Cargo in Redoubt is threatened by the Druj, and the Sarcophan, Axou and Jarmish embassies there have each offered help if the Senate commissions a fortification for the town.

Segura.t: Work has begun on extending the Blood Red Roads from Anduz in Segura to Madruga, and the Towers of Anduz are listed as a place of religious learning.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: two places of learning in Skarsind are listed for religious debate with Faraden priests.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar is one of the preferred central locations for the proposed temple of Baddu the Builder.

Upwold.t: The completion of the Faraden enclave Moonwater Hall has brought prosperity to Upwold.

Zenith.t: Zenith has been conquered by the Druj, who have destroyed the settlements they captured there.

The widening gyre.d: After nearly a year of impasse at Crows Keep, Dogri's warriors turned back Thule traders at Crows Ridge; a fight left one Wintermarker and all the Thule dead. Dogri refused to hand anyone over to an Imperial Orc magistrate, saying he would yield only to a Wintermark army. A raid would not break the Thule peace treaty but would bring reparations proportional to its size. Captains could covertly support the raid with military units; any Imperial army could occupy Crows Ridge and arrest him, with casualties, though a Wintermark army could do so bloodlessly. Alternatively, leaking his target to the Thule would see him destroyed and improve relations, or the Senate could cede Crows Ridge to the Thule.

Imperial Orcs.t: Crows Ridge in their territory of Skarsind was effectively outside their control, and their magistrate was turned away; betraying Dogri to the Thule or arresting him would let them resume full control of Skarsind.

Thule.t: Thule traders were killed at Crows Ridge and their lands faced a planned raid, for which they could demand weregild; if warned of the target they could ambush Dogri, and they could even be offered Crows Ridge by the Senate.

Wintermark.t: A Wintermark war hero from Britta's day was in open defiance, seeking support from like-minded Wintermarkers, and he would submit only to a Wintermark general, offering a Wintermark army the chance to arrest him without bloodshed.

The widening gyre.o: Dogri Thulebane, the rebellious Wintermark thane holding Crows Ridge in Skarsind against the Senate's will, killed Thule traders and turned away an Imperial Orc magistrate, and was rumoured to be gathering warriors for a raid into Thule lands. The Wind laid out options to support the raid, prevent it, or betray him to the Thule.

Otkodov.t: If Dogri were betrayed to the Thule, the resulting thaw in relations would open new opportunities for trade with Otkodov in rare materials and rituals.

Skarsind.t: Dogri held Crows Keep and Crows Ridge in Skarsind as a rebel stronghold where the killings occurred; an Imperial army could occupy the area to end his defiance, or the Senate could cede Crows Ridge to the Thule.

The wild wind rises.d: Some twenty-two thousand Imperial fighters and six thousand Summer heralds faced eleven Jotun armies. The Frozen Citadel in Southmoor fell first. Farstrider's Watch held for four days before its gates fell, and the Singing Caves were lost, though the miners escaped with a final mithril shipment. King Gudmunder Arasonn rebuked Stephen of Sarcombe and placed Honour's Rest under his protection, and he again recognised Jarl Haakon as Jarl of the Mourn. Freemoor, Alderly and Green March remain free, and miners wage a guerrilla war in the Ore Hills. The Mournwold loses its Senator. General Stanley of Chalkdown must stand or break his oath, with a chance to rescue the miners' leaders at Jade Wood.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly's mandate saw the vigilant unconquered clear most of Jarl Haakon's caches in Southmoor. Olyvar of Esther's Sanctum is charged with raiding the last and best-defended cache.

Jotun.t: Eleven Jotun armies under King Gudmunder Arasonn and Queen Yrsa Jansdóttir conquered half the Mournwold, and Jarl Haakon was again recognised as Jarl of the Mourn. The king's protection of Honour's Rest opened a rift with Stephen of Sarcombe and his yegarra.

Navarr.t: The Quiet Step left a safe Miaren to fight in the Mournwold, but captured Navarr were denied the Choice and honourable burial, and were beheaded and left for carrion.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun king praised the Brass Coast's honour in letting the mound at Fort Braydon be raised, and two Jotun armies arrived fresh from a failed strike into northern Kahraman.

The League.t: Jarl Helgarn's warband raided Tassato Mestra for ilium from the Tassatan Hills, and Custodian Serafina di Sarvos is responsible for stopping it. Workers at the Orchard of the Watch are to be escorted back to Tassato.

The Marches.t: The Tusks and the Mournwold's yeomen, beaters, miners and Marcher orcs fought hard but lost four regions and their Senator. General Stanley of Chalkdown now faces breaking his oath, a fate that once sent Nedry of the Cullachs into the Wicker Man.

Wintermark.t: The Green Shield fought at the forefront alongside the Shadowed Flame and faerie knights. The Bloodcloaks recovered and tended the fallen, but both armies were forced back with the rest of the Imperial host.

The wild wind rises.o: In Autumn 386YE the Tusks, Green Shield, Bloodcloaks and Quiet Step marched to drive the Jotun from the Mournwold. More than sixty thousand Jotun and Summer allies overwhelmed them, taking Southmoor, Greensward, Ore Hills and Chalkdowns, and the Mournwold ceased to be Imperial territory.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: A Jotun warband is pursuing the Moon-That-Sings Feni here, and the Imperial Advisor for the Feni, Syn Truth-Walker Returned, is responsible for stopping it.

Hordalant/Vallorberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Helgarn, leader of the warband raiding the Tassatan Hills, is of Vallorberg.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tusks marched north through Braydon's Jasse into the Greensward.

Liathaven/Liath's Ring.t: If the Empire saves the Moon-That-Sings Feni, they offer to help the next Imperial army attack Liath's Ring from Bregasland, which would put the region under threat.

Liathaven/Liaven's Glen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun spared Liaven's Glen, and the Bear who Swims and Roaring Thunder moved through it into the Mourn.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Alderly remained free of the Jotun at the season's end, at least for the moment.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: The last battle, at Lindenford farm, ended in Jotun conquest of the Chalkdowns. The Happiston titles lost their production, and the Black Canal's benefits were cut until the region is reclaimed.
