Mournwold/Freemoor.t: Freemoor remains in Imperial hands, and the Tusks fell back there to the sanctuary of Landskeeper's Bulwark.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Green March remains free, but it is under threat from the traitor Dalton Royse's network. Nigel Hornbeam must kill him at Charlie's Coppice to lift that threat.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Farstrider's Watch fell after four days and Jarl Haakon is reportedly setting up his hall there. King Arasonn placed Honour's Rest and the Orchard of the Watch under his protection.

Mournwold/Ore Hills.t: The Jotun overran the Ore Hills and the Singing Caves, but miners fight on as guerrillas. Their encircled leaders at Jade Wood could be rescued and won over to the Tusks.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: The Frozen Citadel was overwhelmed and Southmoor fell to the Jotun. The Highborn's cache-clearing has lifted the threat there, leaving one last cache to raid.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Jarl Helgarn's warband struck into the northern hills to steal ilium for the Jarl of Mists. Custodian Serafina di Sarvos must stop him or lose the Hills' ilium at the Winter Solstice.

Bregasland.t: The Southern Bear left the Burhfæst in Bregasland to join the Mournwold assault. A Jotun warband is hunting Moon-That-Sings Feni in the Grey Fens.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the page refers only to the Tusks' recent fighting against the Lasambrian orcs and to the Lasambrian Jotun resting after their defeat in the Cinnabar Hills.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Helgarn, who led the ilium raid into Tassato, is of Vallorberg.

Kahraman.t: The Tusks marched north through Braydon's Jasse to reach the Mournwold. The Bear who Swims and Roaring Thunder came to the Mourn straight from their failed strike into northern Kahraman.

Liathaven.t: Liathaven was the staging ground from which eleven Jotun armies poured into the Mournwold. If the Feni are saved, Liath's Ring could come under threat from the Empire.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: with Cold Sun destroyed, Miaren was safe for the moment, freeing the Quiet Step to march to the Mournwold.

Mitwold.t: The Bloodcloaks and Green Shield marched south after their furlough in Mitwold. The Black Canal now gives Mitwold only reduced benefits while Chalkdowns and Southmoor are in Jotun hands.

Mournwold.t: The Jotun took four of its regions, so the Mournwold is no longer Imperial, has no Senator and cannot be targeted from the Anvil regio. Its people now face the Choice and punishing tithes.

Tassato.t: Jarl Helgarn's warband struck into Tassato Mestra to steal ilium. Imperial labourers from the Orchard of the Watch are to be escorted back to Tassato under Jotun guarantee.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: fast-moving light infantry from Tromsa strengthened Queen Yrsa's vanguard.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Green Shield and Bloodcloaks set out after their furlough there, the Green Shield 'from fine Upwold feasting'.

The winds of fashion.d: Fears of the Doom of Sarvos largely came to nothing. A spate of fires was traced to the Carta du Incendio, whose bravos and leaders were caught and tried. Two weeks before the Winter Solstice, however, an accidental blaze destroyed half the Caricomare waterfront, although the docks kept working. The completed School of Couture made the Mirrored Maschieri title available, but the Senator for Sarvos, Nessetta Constanta, had to decide how it would be appointed. Genia Bourné left a letter for whoever took the title. A League Assembly mandate could make Sarvos the City of Masks, and masquerades were proposed. The Lion's Academy announced a bridge-duelling tournament.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the word appears only in the opening fiction, where a Sarvosan boy likes to rise at dawn.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel piracy is cited as one of the hardships Sarvos suffered in recent years.

The League.t: The League Assembly was invited to embrace Sarvos as the City of Masks, and both egregores urged League citizens to plan a masquerade to celebrate triumph over the Hag Queen. Aureliana di Sarvos went on to enact that mandate.

The winds of fashion.o: In the wake of Skathe's mirror-shattering curse, Sarvos weathered arson and a major waterfront fire as the House Bourné School of Couture was completed, opening the way for the League to remake Sarvos as the City of Masks. After the Winter Solstice 383YE, Aureliana di Sarvos enacted the mandate that formally renewed it as such.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: Mentioned in passing: Bocche is not named directly. The page concerns the city of Sarvos as a whole, its Caricomare docks and the new School of Couture.

Holberg.t: The Lion's Academy of Holberg, founded by Brann von Holberg in Adelmar's legacy, announced a bridge-duelling tournament at the summit in honour of the School of Couture. Eight League Free Companies were invited to enter.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos suffered arson by the Carta du Incendio and a fire that destroyed half the Caricomare waterfront, but gained the School of Couture. The mandate that followed renewed it as the City of Masks, averting its threatened doom.

Tassato.t: Merchant princes of Tassato, like those of Sarvos, were making plans for rival masquerades to capitalise on the expected flowering of Pride.

The wolves tempt you.d: Using the Throne's power to address the Empire, Emperor Vesna mourned Alderei the Fair, slain fighting in the Sarangrave, as the last pillar of the Iron Helms' memory, whose schlacta fell fighting for a nation not their own. The Emperor described the Empire as a promise of unbreakable loyalty and called on citizens tempted by the Wolves to remember who had stood with them. Commendations went to the Imperial Auxiliaries, Edward of Gwent, the Vallornguard, the Marches and Vesna's betrothed Sally B Baker. The address avoided naming any group, but seemed aimed at the Navarr struggling in Therunin while sidestepping a trap set by Agramant, whose response remained to be seen.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Vesna signs the address as Warden Queen of Dawn among the Emperor's titles.

Druj.t: The address recalls Druj cruelty, which held no terror over the Iron Helms, and appears crafted to blunt the temptation offered by Agramant, the Druj warlord, whose response is awaited.

Navarr.t: The address appears designed to reach the Navarr fighting desperately for survival in Therunin, urging them not to be lured from the path by the Wolves and to remember who has fought for them.

The Marches.t: The Emperor commended the Marches for self-funding their fifth army in a single season, and praised Edward of Gwent for his years of service to Mitwold.

Varushka.t: Vesna honoured Alderei the Fair and the Iron Helms, whose schlacta died fighting for another nation and whose legacy to Varushka and the Military Council endures; the Wolves imagery also echoes Varushkan tradition.

The wolves tempt you.o: In Autumn 388YE Emperor Vesna addressed the whole Empire, honouring the fallen Iron Helms and urging every citizen not to be tempted from the path by the Wolves but to remember who has fought and died for them.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Edward of Gwent is commended for his years of service to the people of Mitwold.

Sarangrave.t: The Sarangrave is where Alderei the Fair was slain the previous season, and where the Vallornguard arranged military units to fight the Vallorn in Spring, for which they were commended.

Therunin.t: The address appears aimed at the Navarr fighting desperately for their survival in Therunin, encouraging them to resist the temptation set before them by Agramant.

The worth of a life.d: With Skarsind, the Imperial Orcs held land of their own for the first time, and orcs such as those from the training camp at Estcastle moved there. Because orcs shun mining, a ministry in Gulhule (or Gildenheim) could recruit human miners from across the Empire and create an Imperial title, buying green iron, orichalcum and more at larger scales. The Fellowship of the Red Blade proposed a great work, inspired by Navarr's Memorial Gardens at Treji, to honour orcs who never saw Skarsind and share herb lore, yielding true vervain for orc herb gardens. A Torfast ministry could link trade with Temeschwar, Varushka and Hercynia, improved by matching League, Navarr and Varushkan ministries. The Senate pursued all three.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: orcs in the tale remark that Skarsind is colder than Dawn and recall their experience dealing with the Dawnish.

Imperial Orcs.t: Settling Skarsind, the orcs turned their military experience to building a homeland, gaining a ministry recruiting human miners in Gulhule, a trading post at Torfast, and a completed memorial great work tended by the Fellowship of the Red Blade.

Navarr.t: Navarr's Memorial Gardens at Treji inspired the orc memorial, and the Navarr were invited to build a matching trade ministry in the Glen of Shadows, where a trading post was begun.

The League.t: The League was offered the chance to build a ministry in Temeschwar to strengthen the Skarsind trade network, though the resolution records no such ministry being started.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: worries about the Thule are among the concerns the orcs in the tale set aside.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: an orc in the tale mentions liking their Knight's Redoubt as a reason to keep the mines productive.

Varushka.t: Varushkans, with their mining expertise, were seen as likely recruits, and Varushka was invited to build a matching trade ministry in Delev, though none is recorded as begun.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk miners already in Skarsind could be hired by the orcs, and Wintermark's past focus on trade routes into Hahnmark left Torfast's southern and western trade underdeveloped.

The worth of a life.o: In Winter 379YE many experienced Imperial Orc bonesetters settled in newly held Skarsind, presenting three Senate-backed opportunities: a ministry recruiting human miners, a memorial great work of herb gardens, and a network of northern trade ministries. The Senate commissioned the miners' ministry in Gulhule, began trading posts in Torfast and the Glen of Shadows, and the Fellowship of the Red Blade's great work was completed.

Hercynia/The Glen of Shadows.t: The Senate began work on a trading post in the Glen of Shadows, a Navarr ministry meant to widen the goods available through the Torfast crossroads.

Semmerholm/Estmure.t: Mentioned in passing: orcs from the training camp at Estcastle departed to establish a new base in Skarsind.

Skarsind/Estermark.t: Estermark's key mines were the focus of the smallest version of the miners' ministry, which would bring human labour to work them for the orcs.

Skarsind/Solvihill.t: Solvihill, bordering Karov, formed part of the proposed crossroads of the north linking Skarsind's trade eastward into Varushka.

Skarsind/Southpine.t: Southpine, bordering Temeschwar and Hercynia, was singled out by the orcs as key to the trade routes the new Torfast ministry would protect.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's trade focus from Skarsind had been on the passes into Hahnmark rather than routes south and west.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia was one of the destinations for Torfast's improved trade, and work began on a trading post in its Glen of Shadows.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Karov is cited as richer than Skarsind and as bordering Solvihill.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: only the orcs' Knight's Redoubt is referred to, not the territory itself.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: orcs who had lived at the main Imperial Orc training camp in Estcastle left for Skarsind.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind gained a Senate-commissioned ministry in Gulhule recruiting human miners, a trading post at Torfast, and a completed memorial great work of herb gardens for its orc settlers.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar lay on the proposed trade route south from Torfast, and a League ministry there could have enriched the network, though none is recorded as begun.

Theory of the crows.d: Asavea's Plenum rebuffed Sarcophan protests over its bounty on ships trading with the Empire. In response the Delves proposed the Free Seas Pact: signatories would bar pirates, place no bounties on other signatories' ships except in war, and embargo any nation that refused to sign. Negotiator Johann Van Basten was sent to Anvil to agree terms with Ambassador Dino i Riqueza. Sarcophan escorts were keeping trade routes open for now, but not indefinitely. Other matters included revised Kruidenkenner herb deliveries, the Alivetti Estates, a raised offer for white granite, vlinderbloem farming in Wintermark, meetings with Elian Vlas and the Lijkkever, puzzlement over the Barrens, and a warning about the Elakar.

Dawn.t: Elian Vlas proposed meeting Imperial officials at the Wise Guise in Dawn, and the Community of Silence had engaged a renowned Dawnish artist from Astolat to decorate their temple.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj being in retreat is cited as one reason the Delves now take an interest in trade with Holberg.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sarcophan presence at Crown's Quay in Necropolis is noted as a possible cheaper site for the Bladgoud Tuiniers' business.

The League.t: League cities drew Sarcophan interest: the Lijkkever sent Schuyler Koopman to meet Holberg's Chamber of Commerce, and the Bladgoud Tuiniers sought buyers for their legal drugs in Sarvos or would leave. Elian Vlas also hoped to visit League theatres.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name Urizen directly.

Varushka.t: Varushka's Ivarsgard in Karsk is described as the closest Sarcophan trade hub to the Barrens and a place with an established Sarcophan presence.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark farmers had harvested their first vlinderbloem crop for the Kraft brothers in exchange for viezesmaak. The brothers invited Wintermark merchants to propose further trade.

Theory of the crows.o: In Winter 386YE the Sarcophan Delves, angered that Asavean bounties were harming their shipping, proposed a Free Seas Pact with the Empire to outlaw piracy. Their ambassador, Bedelaar Huisbaas Annike, also set out a range of trade offers, meetings and diplomatic replies.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: a renowned Dawnish artist from Astolat had been offered to the Community of Silence to decorate their temple.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: in the opening fiction the Asavean envoy refers to Imperials as the 'assassins of Catazar'.

Hahnmark.t: The first Imperially grown vlinderbloem was ready to harvest, and the resulting viezesmaak was shared with Hahnmark's farmers, with most of it exported.

Holberg.t: With the Barrens no longer hostile, the Lijkkever's Schuyler Koopman planned to come to Anvil to explore trade with Holberg's Chamber of Commerce. Annike declined the invitation to its 250th anniversary celebration.

Karsk.t: Ivarsgard in Karsk was named as the nearest Sarcophan trade hub to the Barrens and a possible site for the Bladgoud Tuiniers to set up shop.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Crown's Quay in Necropolis is noted as having a Sarcophan presence that could lower setup costs for the Bladgoud Tuiniers.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named on the page.

Sarvos.t: After the Sarvosan Chamber of Commerce declined their offer, the Bladgoud Tuiniers' handelsschool was failing. Aaven Beekhof sought buyers for their legal drugs, warning they would probably leave Sarvos by the Spring Equinox without a convincing offer.

The Barrens.t: Annike was baffled by the Ambassador's reassurance about General Archavion's actions in the Barrens, since the Delves had no interests there. She allowed that a port on the Barren Sea would interest them if the territory proved rich in resources.

There is hope.d: After Imperial magicians chose to forge ahead through the chaos, the constellations returned to normal, and an awareness rippled out from the Imperial regio that an unassuming star had become the Beacon. Its law, 'there is hope', caused consternation given hope's malign reputation, and like the Wanderer it moves unpredictably. Foreign magicians soon learned of it. Embodied tulpas vanished and can no longer be created, and stars cannot be deliberately bound to mortals, though constellations can still shape enchantments. The regio still did not enhance realm lore, but same-nation covens could cooperate and ritualists gained a sense of spiritual strength. Territory-scale magic remained unpredictable for one last season, with things expected to settle by Winter.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named, but the revelation of the Beacon rippled out from the Imperial regio at Anvil in Casinea, a territory Highguard held at the time.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial regio can still be used alongside the Citadel Guard to focus magic and channel rituals through the Urizen army.

There is hope.o: The magical chaos that had gripped the Empire's astronomancy since the Winter Solstice abated, leaving behind a nineteenth constellation, the Beacon, whose law is 'there is hope'. Embodied tulpas vanished, and the Imperial regio at Anvil remained partly altered for one final season.

Casinea.t: The awareness of the new Beacon constellation spread outward from the Imperial regio at Anvil in Casinea, where the regio still could not enhance realm lore but let same-nation covens work together and gave ritualists a peculiar source of spiritual strength during the Autumn Equinox.

There is thunder.d: Chalonsio, ruled from the Sapphire Keep by Patricio Sebastian Ceruleo, handles most foreign slaves entering Asavea. Its Chain District holds the Grand Temple of the God of Chains, where the priesthood was gathering. The Sumaah aimed to free slaves, sink slavers and destroy the markets and temple. The Commonwealth pledged only limited ships. Without Senate action, Imperial participation would be illegal. The raid's outcome would depend on how much Imperial strength joined, with rewards and plunder on offer but a likely collapse in Asavean relations. A mountebank proposed that the Ambassador to Asavea secretly warn Lady Madriannia of the Blue Stones instead, at great risk to the Liberty Pact.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the current Ambassador to Asavea, the only person Lady Madriannia would believe if warned of the raid, is Ashborn Pakt of the Imperial Orcs, though the title was up for election.

The Brass Coast.t: Sumaah enthusiasm for the raid was strengthened by the example of Zemress, the Blade of the Isles, and the former pirates leading the attack hoped to fight beside Imperial citizens who follow her path.

There is thunder.o: The Sumaah House of the People planned a surprise raid on Chalonsio, the heart of the Asavean slave trade, and invited the Empire to join it alongside the Commonwealth. Imperial captains could only take part if the Senate legalised the action or declared war on Asavea.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Asavean shipping along the Bay of Catazar had fallen to an all-time low amid worsening relations and mutual sanctions.

Madruga.t: Sumaah visitors to the Zemress Seminary in Madruga were credited with strengthening support for the plan to strike at Chalonsio.

They bit the cats.d: Rats attacked tourists at Virtue's Respite and gamblers at Lorenzo's Great Game, and partially devoured the apothecary Ernesto di Temeschwar. Someone wrote "SHADOWSMITH IS DEAD YOU FOOL" in his blood. Theories ranged from a buried Varushkan Sovereign to a Skathe-like curse. The Temeschwari Chamber of Commerce was asked to vote on three options: hiring the Wardog Kennels for 10 Thrones, poisoning the rats with the Guild of the Green Flower, or riding it out. The Synod and Conclave orders were invited to investigate. League military units could take paid but risky rat-hunting work. At Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, a fell wind left workers who had handled sinkhole wealth sick, and the Fox and Fowl Company sought Conclave help.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: a party of Imperial Orcs visiting Empress Giselle's tomb was swarmed by rats, and several were bitten.

The League.t: The League's city of Temeschwar faced a rat menace, and its Chamber of Commerce had to choose a response. League military units were offered well-paid but dangerous rat hunts in the sewers.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar's old Vard heritage, including the volodny Shadowsmith and a possible Sovereign beneath the city, was suggested as a possible root of the trouble.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Winterfolk tourists were bitten at Virtue's Respite, and the Steinr grimnir Kylara was eligible to vote in the Temeschwari Chamber of Commerce.

They bit the cats.o: In spring 386YE Temeschwar suffered a plague of unnaturally bold and vicious rats, culminating in the gruesome killing of an apothecary beside a bloody message about the volodny Shadowsmith. Meanwhile a mysterious sickness struck workers at Lorenzo's Deep Pockets.

Holberg/Holfried.t: Mentioned in passing: ratters from the Kennels of Holfried were suggested as useful protection against the rats.

Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale.t: Mentioned in passing: the fell wind that preceded the sickness at Lorenzo's Deep Pockets was said to have come from the Vardstein Vale.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the murdered apothecary Ernesto came from Holberg, and the Hag Queen's earlier curse there, which brought a tide of rats, was offered as a possible parallel.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is named as the home of Empress Giselle, whose tomb in Temeschwar was the site of a rat attack.

Temeschwar.t: The city was overrun by fearless, aggressive rats that killed an apothecary and closed Lorenzo's Great Game. Its business owners had to choose between wardogs, poison or riding it out, while sickness struck workers at Lorenzo's Deep Pockets.

Things go awry.d: The regio still worked in every other respect. Covens of the same nation could still cooperate freely, while arcane projections creating personal curses failed for good after the Equinox. The shrouds over the Empire and its neighbours collapsed, and the Key and the Spider now prevented any territory-scale shroud. Vivid star-dreams granted inspiration to dreamers. Rivers of Life had strange effects: a fertility boon in Feroz, blood weeping from Mitwold's Pale Chain, and a sudden woodland in Bregasland. In Redoubt it agitated the Ribbon of Salt, which threatened to devastate the Bay of Catazar. A Night shroud hid Miekarova's Painted Caves, and a Day enchantment brought clarity to Sermersuaq.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: their Mallum lands lost their mysterious shrouds, the Salt Flats of Sanath cannot now be shrouded, and the miasma over Druj-claimed land colours visions felt through the Citadel Guard in Sarangrave.

Grendel.t: Grendel-held shores of the Bay of Catazar would be struck by ruinous storms if the Ribbon of Salt erupted, and some at Anvil might think that damage worth inflicting simply to hurt the Grendel.

Highguard.t: The shroud over Casinea and the Imperial regio, broken at the Winter Solstice, proved to be the lynchpin of the wider shrouds, and Necropolis lies on the coast threatened by the Ribbon of Salt.

Jotun.t: The shrouds that had settled over Skallahn, Tromsa, Hordalant, Liathaven and Bregasland disintegrated, and no territory-scale shroud could be raised over these lands during the Spring Equinox.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Therunin was among the neighbouring territories whose unexplained shroud collapsed after the Winter Solstice.

The Brass Coast.t: Feroz's farms and the Dhomiro of Afar's Herds were offered a Stallion-touched fertility boon, but the Brass Coast's recovering coastal towns would suffer badly if the Ribbon of Salt erupted.

The League.t: Sarvos and Spiral lie on the Bay of Catazar, and Sarvos would be pounded by Spring storms if the Ribbon of Salt exploded.

The Marches.t: Blood seeped from the soil around the Pale Chain in Mitwold, where Red Walder's heirs were seen taking something from the ground, while a new woodland sprang up in Bregasland and Graven Rock echoed strangely.

Thule.t: The Thule faced a magical mist barring the Painted Caves of Mieriada that they did not create and resent, and which Imperial magicians could extend for a year or make permanent, angering them.

Urizen.t: Magicians channelling ritual magic through the Citadel Guard felt a physical connection to its Urizeni soldiers. Meanwhile Redoubt's agitated Ribbon of Salt threatened disaster, and its senator Thalia of Netherwatch was sent seawater for a mitigating ritual.

Varushka.t: The Painted Caves, special to Varushkans who feel their Ushkan heritage, were hidden by mists under the Lock. Some saw this as passive resistance to Thule occupation that could be extended or made permanent.

Wintermark.t: A Day enchantment over Sermersuaq tore apart the last echoes of the Falconer's influence and brought calm, clarity and encounters with Day heralds to the territory's people.

Things go awry.o: In Spring 388YE magical chaos tied to an unprecedented astronomantic conjunction kept the Imperial regio unable to enhance ritual lore and caused territory-scale magic across the Empire to have unpredictable side effects. It also opened several opportunities and dangers, from Feroz to Redoubt, Mitwold, Miekarova and Sermersuaq.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: A brand new woodland erupted overnight on Gravenmarch's border with the Rushes, amid speculation that it is linked to Rivers of Life and to strange resonances in Graven Rock.

Bregasland/The Rushes.t: The sudden new woodland rose on the Rushes' border with Gravenmarch, prompting landskeepers to suggest divination and mummers to plan dramatisations of a moving forest.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Beoraidh was named among the places that devastating Spring storms would pound if the Ribbon of Salt exploded.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: The Painted Caves of Mieriada, some holding Night regio, were sealed off by mists that led travellers astray and could be extended for a year or made permanent by invoking the Lock.

Redoubt/Optarion.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named directly and is attached through Redoubt, where the agitated Ribbon of Salt threatened the territory's coast.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Ribbon of Salt beneath the bay was erupting roughly every eighteen hours. Any Spring enchantment or curse on Redoubt during the Equinox would unleash storms that cripple fleets and inflict heavy navy casualties across the bay.

Bregasland.t: A brand new woodland rose in a single night between Gravenmarch and the Rushes and Graven Rock echoed with unsettling resonances, possibly linked to Rivers of Life. The territory's earlier shroud also collapsed.

Casinea.t: The potent shroud over Casinea was broken at the Winter Solstice, and now the Key and the Spider, rather than the Lock, glitter in its skies.

Feroz.t: Rivers of Life under the Stallion brought a surge of births and fertility, so farms blessed at the Winter Solstice would yield extra rings. The Dhomiro of Afar was offered a star-metal ritual to permanently increase the Herds' income, though the territory would also face the Ribbon's storms.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among Jotun lands whose shroud collapsed and which could not be shrouded again during the Equinox.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: named among neighbouring territories whose unexplained shroud disintegrated after the Winter Solstice.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the Bay of Catazar territories that would be struck by storms if the Ribbon of Salt erupted.

Mareave.t: Mareave would be battered by Spring storms if the Ribbon of Salt exploded, with Beoraidh among the places named as being pounded.

Miekarova.t: The Painted Caves in ceded Mieriada were hidden by a magnitude 30 Night shroud that the Thule did not cast. Imperial magicians invoking the Lock could extend it for a year or make it permanent.

Mitwold.t: Blood-like liquid seeped from old battlefields, and the Pale Chain wept blood under the Key, where Jyll Longleys, Bill of Beatsdown and Cobb were seen pulling something from the ground: an ill omen for the warzone.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the Bay of Catazar territories threatened by storms should the Ribbon of Salt erupt.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: almost all of Otkodov had been shrouded before the shrouds collapsed, and its orcs are referred to in the context of resistance in Miekarova.

Redoubt.t: Rivers of Life promised fine harvests but agitated the Ribbon of Salt under the Mountain, Stork and Wanderer. Any Spring enchantment or curse on Redoubt would cause disaster unless a precise Regrow the Land's Heart invoking the Fountain bled off its power.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as one of the territories over which no shroud could be created during the Spring Equinox.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard were stationed there, colouring rituals channelled through them with phantoms of marsh and battle, and Rivers of Life caused chaos at the Tower of the Skink.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos was named among the places that Spring storms would pound if the Ribbon of Salt exploded across the Bay of Catazar.

Sermersuaq.t: A Day enchantment unravelled the Falconer's lingering corruption, dimmed the Claw, and filled the territory with clarity, wellbeing and gentle encounters with Day heralds. Its people felt Day magic more keenly as a result.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among Jotun lands whose shroud collapsed and which could not be shrouded during the Equinox.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the Bay of Catazar territories at risk of storms if the Ribbon of Salt erupted.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: named among the neighbouring territories whose unexplained shroud disintegrated after the Winter Solstice.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among Jotun lands whose shroud collapsed and which could not be shrouded during the Equinox.

Things that burn.d: Wintermark warbands and heralds of Cathan Canae won at Valashal and saved the Sovevann, but both Day armies remain in Hahnmark and Kallavesa. In Varushka the Shepherds of Ash ruined Livardz, while the Blade of Skies burned vales across Karov and now threatens Delev. A pulse of Day magic destroyed the trods of Volodmartz, Karov and Miaren. The Black Thorns drove the Still Walkers out of Hercynia, but the Empty Hands are petrifying Oakways. The Burning Falcon and Fist of the Mountains halved the Fire Beacon in Segura. Marcher armies destroyed the Ending Tide and the Still Rock. The Granite Pillar contained the Winnowers at the White Tower in Bastion. Six Sentinel Gate opportunities were announced.

Dawn.t: Dawnish knights-errant died defending Bulgakov in Karov, Dawnish captains fought in Segura and in large numbers beside the Granite Pillar in Bastion, and a band of the Empty Hands has crossed into Astolat towards the Castle of Thorns.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the White Tower in Bastion, now seized by Cold Sun, was destroyed by the Druj some fifteen years earlier.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Feroz, which Grendel holds, appears only as the home territory of two Freeborn captains serving with the Burning Falcon.

Highguard.t: The Winnowers seized the White Tower and Oath-heart, the Shield of Loyalty, and spread a famine-wind through Sybella Cross, but the Granite Pillar and independent captains contained them at a cost of three hundred soldiers.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Halls of Worth in Skarsind were saved at the Autumn Equinox, and scions were seen to flee the Weeping Stone near the Skarsind border.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bounders' general referred to traitors left behind by Fisher and the Jotun, and Jotun-held Liathaven is listed as home to some Navarr captains.

Navarr.t: The Black Thorns drove the Still Walkers from Hercynia at a cost of nearly three hundred thorns, but the trods of Hercynia, Volodmartz, Karov and Miaren were destroyed, vates were burned, and the Empty Hands devastated Miaren and destroyed First Voice Glade.

The Brass Coast.t: The Fire Beacon burned its way across Segura towards Sunsong Ranch until the Burning Falcon and Fist of the Mountains destroyed about half of it, though it remains in Burnish.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar merchants trade at Delev, now threatened by the Blade of Skies, and a Tassato captain fought in Bastion.

The Marches.t: The Bounders, Drakes and Strong Reeds, with Isaella's Dance and Marcher captains, encircled and destroyed the Ending Tide in Gravenmarch before it could grow, and the Still Rock imploded.

Thule.t: A Thule army waited at the Sungold Pass for a signal that never came and withdrew, while Thule war-wizards with bear-wolves fought beside the Fist of the Mountains against the Fire Beacon in Segura.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: scions bound for the hot springs of Peregro were intercepted at the Equinox, and Urizen captains from Morrow and Redoubt fought in Segura and Bastion.

Varushka.t: The Shepherds of Ash left Livardz in ruins and the Blade of Skies razed vales across southern Karov, killing hundreds, cutting northern trade ministries and now threatening Delev, while every trod in Volodmartz and Karov was destroyed.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk warbands won the Battle of Valashal with the heralds of Cathan Canae and saved the Sovevann from the Exigent Span, yet both Day armies remain in Wintermark and hundreds of Winterfolk have died.

Things that burn.o: In Winter 385YE, armies of scions of the eternal Cold Sun, tens of thousands strong after emerging from regio across the Empire, ravaged Wintermark, Varushka, Navarr, the Brass Coast, the Marches and Highguard, while Imperial armies, warbands and enchantments fought back.

Bastion/Stoneside.t: The Winnowers launched attacks into Stoneside, but the Granite Pillar's stand kept their famine-wind confined to Sybella Cross.

Bastion/Sybella Cross.t: The Winnowers seized the White Tower, raised a fortress there and blighted herb gardens, and the Granite Pillar fought them to a standstill; the Champion of Loyalty may seek Oath-heart via Tamar's Stand.

Bastion/Woodbury.t: The Winnowers erupted from a ring of magister statues in eastern Woodbury and later launched attacks back into the region.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: The Ending Tide gathered at the Still Rock and was destroyed when the Marcher armies closed on it; the Rock imploded and the menhirs now weep a rainbow-coloured liquid.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen ward was raised over the Grey Fens, its mists slowing the scions across Bregasland but also confusing Marchers and magistrates.

Bregasland/The Rushes.t: Mentioned in passing: in a world where the Ending Tide grew unchecked, it would have spilled west into the Rushes and taken Sallow.

Hahnmark/Kronemark.t: Halls on the southern downs of Kronemark burned, and the defeated Silence Arc has now been driven into Kronemark, forcing people to flee north.

Hahnmark/Valasmark.t: The Silence Arc emerged at the Lantern Gate and burned halls until defeated at Valashal by Winterfolk and a Frozen Citadel, at the cost of two hundred defenders.

Hahnmark/Wood Heath.t: A splinter of the Silence Arc is moving east through Wood Heath to threaten New Dunhall and the keystone of the Legacy of Vigilance.

Hercynia/Deer's Folly.t: The vallorn in Deer's Folly remains cut off from the trods, which can only be restored from a Spring regio inside the vallorn itself.

Hercynia/Northpines.t: The Still Walkers emerged from the eternal flame's cavern and burned the pines until the Wooden Fastness drove them to vanish from the region.

Hercynia/Old Ranging.t: Mentioned in passing: the Still Walkers retreated west towards Old Ranging before being trapped.

Hercynia/Summersend.t: The Still Walkers reappeared here threatening the Heartwood and the Great Library of Hacynian, but the Black Thorns killed nearly a third of them before they fled.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: A Night ward shrouded the marsh against the scions, and an Exigent Span force threatens the healers of Hufi's Glen, reachable via the Road to Masi.

Kallavesa/Rundhal Marsh.t: The Exigent Span destroyed the Swanmere and tried to purge the Sovevann, but its grand archon was slain and the army driven out after months of fighting.

Kallavesa/Skymark.t: The Exigent Span retreated into Skymark, where it is regrouping with Wintermark's heroes in pursuit.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: A Night ward shrouded West Marsh, and the fishing fleet of Westerhal carried warriors to relieve Rundahl.

Karov/Duzekani.t: The Blade of Skies razed Bulgakov and other vales, left the region Sun Burned with cursed glass, drove off its bees, and now threatens Delev and the northern trade ministries.

Karov/Kamienczka.t: The Blade of Skies destroyed vales including Olvanshka, home of three warden fellowships, though scions fled the Weeping Stone.

Karov/Malimorzi.t: Scouting parties of the Shepherds of Ash struck into northern Malimorzi, killing travellers and burning farms.

Karov/Skoremujac.t: A Wooden Fastness was forged in Skoremujac, which the Blade of Skies avoided.

Karov/Wieliczka.t: Imperial magic raised a keep of blue ice and stone in Wieliczka, which the Blade of Skies avoided.

Karsk/Nitrost.t: Scouting parties of the Shepherds of Ash struck into western Nitrost, killing merchants and pilgrims and burning farms.

Miaren/Goldglades.t: A Spring ward over Goldglades sheltered refugees, though its regio were scorched by the trod-pulse; the Spear of the Seven may confront scions here at Golden Meadow.

Miaren/Greenfalls.t: The Empty Hands launched assaults into Greenfalls, attacking steadings, stridings and wayhouses.

Miaren/Holtford.t: The Empty Hands launched assaults into Holtford, attacking steadings, stridings and wayhouses.

Miaren/Oakways.t: The Empty Hands emerged at Tomma's Well, overran steadings and are nearly a third of the way to conquering Oakways, which has become Petrified.

Miaren/Serenael.t: The Empty Hands raided Serenael without attacking Seren itself, whose walls sheltered many fleeing the scions.

Miekarova/Dupadealuri.t: Scouting parties of the Shepherds of Ash struck into eastern Dupadealuri, slaughtering travellers and burning farms.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Mentioned in passing: scions moving to unleash the hot springs of Peregro were intercepted at the Autumn Equinox.

Segura/Burnish.t: The Fire Beacon emerged from a regio in Burnish's hills and, though halved in battle, is regrouping there.

Upwold/The Heath.t: Empty Hands raiders threaten the Sutton Stone Quarries, and the Sentinel Gate will open to Sammy's Paling to stop them.

Volodmartz/Livardz.t: The Shepherds of Ash emerged at the Sumisev Peegel and razed nearly a dozen vales, killing hundreds; Livardz has gained the ruins quality.

Volodmartz/Opascari.t: A black granite fortress raised on Opascari's hilltops helped shield the rest of Volodmartz from the Shepherds of Ash.

Volodmartz/Suvretz.t: Spring wards over the forests of Suvretz turned the land and its beasts against the scions, keeping the Shepherds of Ash away.

Astolat.t: A band of the Empty Hands has crossed into Astolat heading for the rose garden of the Castle of Thorns, an opportunity for the Knight-protector of Autumn to stop them through the Sentinel Gate.

Bastion.t: The Winnowers built a fortress at the White Tower and spread a withering famine-wind, but the Granite Pillar contained them there; their presence stops herb imports from the Sarcophan Delves.

Bregasland.t: The Ending Tide gathered at the Still Rock in Gravenmarch and was destroyed by Marcher armies and Isaella's Dance, though the Keeper of the Dour Fens lost this season's mana and the sinecure's yield has changed.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: three Navarr captains from Brocéliande marched with the Black Thorns in Hercynia.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar marched into Bastion from Casinea, and several Casinea captains fought beside it.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: two Freeborn captains from Feroz fought with the Burning Falcon in Segura.

Hahnmark.t: The Silence Arc burned halls across Valasmark and southern Kronemark before being defeated at Valashal, but it remains in Kronemark and a splinter force threatens New Dunhall.

Hercynia.t: The Still Walkers burned Northpines and Summersend until the Wooden Fastness and the Black Thorns forced them to flee the territory, but its trods remain severed.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fire Beacon was driven back towards the Kahraman borders, and Kahraman captains fought in the Burning Falcon.

Kallavesa.t: The Exigent Span tried to burn the Sovevann and the resting dead, but Night wards and warbands killed its grand archon and broke its beacon, driving it north into Skymark.

Karov.t: The Blade of Skies razed Bulgakov, Olvanshka and many other vales in Duzekani and Kamienczka, killing hundreds, reducing the territory's prosperity and now threatening Delev, while all trods here were destroyed.

Karsk.t: The vale of Veresk was defended at the Equinox, but scouting parties of the Shepherds of Ash raided western Nitrost.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr captains from Liathaven fought with the Black Thorns and the Burning Falcon.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns marched north from Madruga, and Madruga captains fought with the Burning Falcon and in Bastion.

Miaren.t: The Empty Hands are almost a third of the way to conquering Oakways, petrifying the land, burning steadings across Miaren and destroying First Voice Glade and every trod in the territory.

Miekarova.t: Scouting parties of the Shepherds of Ash struck into eastern Dupadealuri, slaughtering merchants and pilgrims and burning farms.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: southern Mitwold would have been assaulted had the Ending Tide reached full strength, and Mitwold captains fought in Bregasland.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: scions moving on the hot springs of Peregro were intercepted at the Equinox, and a Morrow captain fought with the Burning Falcon.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: northern Mournwold might have been attacked had the Ending Tide grown, and Mournwold captains fought in Segura and Bregasland.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: many Necropolis captains fought alongside the Granite Pillar in Bastion.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: a Thule army waited at the Sungold Pass on the Otkodov border before withdrawing, and a captain from Otkodov fought with the Fist of the Mountains.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: a Redoubt captain fought alongside the Granite Pillar in Bastion.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the White Tower once watched the trods into Reikos, and many Reikos captains fought in Bastion.

Segura.t: The Fire Beacon burned settlements on the plains until the Burning Falcon and Fist of the Mountains saved Sunsong Ranch and destroyed about half of it, though it remains in Burnish.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm captains fought with the Burning Falcon and in Bastion.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: captains from Sermersuaq joined the defence of Valashal and of the Sovevann.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Halls of Worth were preserved at the Equinox, and scions fled from the Weeping Stone near the Skarsind border.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: a Tassato captain fought alongside the Granite Pillar in Bastion.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar merchants trade at Delev, a vale some think could one day rival Temeschwar.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: captains from the Barrens fought alongside the Granite Pillar in Bastion.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: an earlier attack on Therunin was driven off, and Therunin captains fought in Hercynia and Bastion.

Upwold.t: A breakaway force of the Empty Hands is raiding towards the Sutton Stone Quarries on the Heath, an opportunity for the quarries' holder to stop them through the Sentinel Gate.

Volodmartz.t: The Shepherds of Ash razed nearly a dozen vales in Livardz, killing hundreds and reducing the territory's taxes, while wards held them away from the rest of Volodmartz and all its trods were destroyed.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: Bulgakov lay on the road into Weirwater, and Weirwater captains fought in Segura and Bastion.

Think of the children.d: Cesare's statement passed 215–0, but the Mourn showed little enthusiasm, since Marcher friars traditionally find homes for orphans with relatives or charitable souls. Friar Margaret of Green March proposed converting the Jarl's Head, an abandoned inn in Sarcombe, into a register of births and deaths. The civil service offered three options: the register alone (6 wains of white granite, 12 crowns); the register plus shrines to the Little Mother across human settlements (40 wains, 80 crowns, yielding 900 rings a season to Mournwold Prosperity congregations); or the same including Jotun thrall settlements (50 wains, 100 crowns). Frederick di Sarvos offered to devote himself to any feat named by Viviane de Coeurdefer, provided the Assembly of the Nine upholds her judgement.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Viviane de Coeurdefer, Cardinal of Ambition, was challenged to submit a Statement of Endeavour to the Assembly of the Nine, with Frederick di Sarvos pledging to pursue any feat she names if it passes.

Jotun.t: Many new orphans of the war are Jotun, and one costlier option would extend the shrines and register to thrall settlements, signalling Imperial intent to incorporate the thralls into Marcher society; otherwise Jotun orphans would have to fend for themselves.

The League.t: The League's Cesare Enzo di Trivento drew on his nation's tradition of Little Mother orphanages to call for the great orphanage, while Holberg's Frederick di Sarvos was inspired to challenge the Cardinal of Ambition.

The Marches.t: Marchers largely rejected a grand orphanage as alien to their custom of placing orphans with kin, favouring instead the Sarcombe Register and possibly a network of Little Mother shrines across the Mourn.

Think of the children.o: After the Assembly of Prosperity upheld Cesare Enzo di Trivento's call for a great orphanage for the Mournwold's orphans, Marcher friars instead proposed the Sarcombe Register, a central record of households to help place orphans with relatives and foster families. Separately, the Holberg architect Frederick di Sarvos challenged the Cardinal of Ambition to pass a 'Statement of Endeavour'.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Friar Margaret of Green March originated the register proposal, and the region is home to Hap the Soft, a Jotun thrall known for taking in dozens of orphans.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Mentioned in passing: Southmoor is not named directly, but lies within the Mournwold where the register and shrine network are proposed.

Holberg.t: Frederick di Sarvos, a renowned architect holding a chair at the University of Holberg, offered to devote himself and rally fellow devotees of Ambition to whatever feat the Cardinal of Ambition names.

Mournwold.t: The Senate could build the Sarcombe Register in the town of Sarcombe, optionally with shrines to the Little Mother across the territory, providing 900 rings a season to its Prosperity congregations and possibly including Jotun thrall settlements.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: in the opening story, an orphan's late father's estate was sold to a family moving back from Upwold.

This is the end.d: The war between the cats and the birds in Apulian ended with the cats routed. Birdsong now drowns out the Black Plateau's malevolence for a season. Just under forty-five military units supported Sofonisba Amilcara and uncovered the Shadow Den of the Adumbral Volution beneath the Vicente School and Orphanage, a fane-like lair created by cultists. The lair was destroyed, but the empty orphanage vanished, apparently stolen by the Whisper Gallery. The duSesna Guild fled, and permanent night marks remain on the city. Sung rewarded the Map, who is now bound to the city. Sadogua and the Azoth proposed the Delectable Refectory and the Grand Laboratory, with unknown effects. The dramaturgical confluence largely ended, though its cause remains a mystery.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: thirteen Dawnish citizens, including members of House de Vere and the Amber Lance, are listed among those who supported the Map to the City Below.

The League.t: League businesses in Apulian are spared the Black Plateau's penalty for a season, and the League-appointed Sofonisba Amilcara is now bound to the city as Sung's Map to the City Below. The orphanage at the heart of the Whisper Gallery's lair has been lost, and the duSesna Guild has fled.

Urizen.t: Many Urizeni captains, including the Spiral Council's banner, aided the venture beneath Apulian. Every Urizeni magician who wishes it now keeps at least one of the clever, night-touched cats, which work hard and keep spires free of vermin.

This is the end.o: In Summer 388YE the songbirds of Sung drove the Whisper Gallery's cats out of Apulian, and Sofonisba Amilcara became the Map to the City Below after military units uncovered and destroyed a hidden Whisper Gallery lair. Sadogua and the Azoth also proposed edifices of their own in the city.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Songbirds now fill Apulian and shield it from the Black Plateau, and the Whisper Gallery's lair beneath the city has been destroyed, though its marks remain. Two proposed edifices for eternals could be built in Apulus until Summer 389YE.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Mentioned in passing: the Silver Flame's Fellowship of the Cinion Dawn appears among the banners supporting the Map to the City Below.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: a Holberg professor of civil engineering dryly criticises the Azoth's unplanned approach to building the Grand Laboratory.

Spiral.t: A Night enchantment brought shared dreams of the war and renewed optimism across Spiral. The routed cats fled to the citadels and spires in the hills, and the heralds of Sadogua and the Azoth now call across the territory.

This land is your land.d: The Conclave interdicted Rivers Run Red and Mountain Remembers Its Youth, though the Senate did not remove them from Imperial lore. Nedry Galest, General of the Tusks, went to the wicker man to atone for the curses. The Senate commissioned fortifications in Greensward and Freemoor but rejected one for Southmoor. The Mournwold stays stable if those are built and the interdictions hold for five years. Lifting either would be disastrous. Many Whittle folk returned home, still shunned and still devoted to Hatred. Three further opportunities were offered: Richard of Holberg's mithril menhirs, a third fortification, and granting the Singing Caves to the Marches. The Senate later voted itself a power of relinquishment, and construction began on the two fortifications.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Mournwolders blame Dawn's senators, without much evidence, for the Senate's failure to remove the two curses from Imperial lore.

Imperial Orcs.t: A rumour that the Imperial Orcs might give up their own Bourse resource so that the Singing Caves could go to the Marches was seen as an exceptional gesture. The Constitutional Court set out a lawful route for doing so, and the Senate later created the power of relinquishment. Imperial Orc preachers were also invited to preach the Way to the freed thralls of the Mourn.

Jotun.t: The Jotun had fled the Mournwold. The new fortifications are meant to stop them ever retaking it, and their former orc thralls were invited to send leaders to Anvil.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: a revived market town at Sarcombe could renew trade with the Navarr once they retake Liathaven.

The League.t: Mournwolders contemptuously see handing the Singing Caves to the Bourse as giving them to the League. The Marcher enclave in Tassato prospers even as many Whittle folk leave it. Leaguers Ricardo de Tassato and Cesare Enzo Di Trivento were praised by the Marcher Assembly.

The Marches.t: Nedry Galest's sacrifice and the Empire's concessions renewed Marcher loyalty and pride in the Mournwold. The Marcher Assembly still struggles to persuade a grudge-holding people of the difference between the false virtue of Hate and everyday hatred. The Marches could gain its first national Bourse seat if the Singing Caves were granted to it.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's decision to fund a new monastery in Overton, and the Winterfolk's Senate motion for a memorial there, were well received, though folk want a Mournwolder put in charge of the monastery.

This land is your land.o: After the Jotun were driven from the Mournwold, the Empire's response to the demands carried to Anvil by Mel Greenhill, Long Tom and Edda Counter calmed talk of rebellion there. Further opportunities remained to win the territory's lasting loyalty.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: The Senate commissioned a fortification in Freemoor, and construction has since begun.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: The Senate commissioned a fortification in Greensward, and construction has since begun.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: The Senate rejected a fortification for Southmoor, but locals hope it will reconsider and favour the ruined mining town of Sarcombe, on the foundations of the Jotun fort Hillstop. That could revive the town as a chartered market and trade hub.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the returning Whittle folk are described as 'as cold as a Bregasland eel'.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: only through the name of the architect Richard (Dicky) of Holberg, who designed the proposed menhir network for the Mourn.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: trade through Sarcombe could resume with the Navarr once they have retaken Liathaven from the Jotun.

Mournwold.t: The territory's mood shifted from open rebellion to cautious patience. Stability depends on the commissioned fortifications being built and the two curses staying interdicted for five years. Menhirs, a third fortification and the Singing Caves remain open opportunities.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Constitutional Court said relinquishment would not be allowed by extraordinary motion, as had happened with Skarsind.

Tassato.t: More than half the remaining Whittle folk left Tassato to return home. The younger Marchers who stayed form a prospering enclave, 'Little Mournwold', that increasingly takes on Tassatan ways.

This little light of mine.d: The Citadel Guard, Eastern Sky, Granite Pillar, Seventh Wave, Towerjacks and Fist of the Mountain, bolstered by Autumn and Day magic, clashed with Druj armies that were bent on slaughter and empowered by Spring magic. The Empire narrowly prevailed, but more than 2,500 Imperial soldiers died and Clypion's eastern spires stayed in Druj hands. Survivors and refugees joined the Citadel Guard. Zenith's trods collapsed, and Proceris gained the Nightwoven quality. The Solstice battle offered a chance to kill Karvor Eyepeel and seize Clypion, and to kill his tepel to weaken Iteri. Conjunctions targeted a stolen magical text, the Druj champion Khelver and the Amulet of Truth, and two groups of mysteriously afflicted former prisoners.

Dawn.t: The Eastern Sky, under its new General Dame Aurum De Castellan, led the assault in Clypion, and Aurum's virtuous auras inspired Zenith's survivors. Yeomen of Dawn were among the emptied former prisoners at the Grove of the Halls.

Druj.t: The Druj matched the Empire's numbers but favoured slaughter over holding ground, and they were narrowly driven east. Their leader in Zenith, Karvor Eyepeel, was left trapped in a salient at Mount Ossa and exposed to an Imperial strike.

Highguard.t: The Granite Pillar and Seventh Wave fought on their Virtuous Crusade in Zenith. A conjunction offered the chance to slay Khelver and recover the Amulet of Truth stolen from Tabernacle, which would make both armies unbreakable while they stayed in Zenith.

Navarr.t: The trods of Zenith collapsed, possibly through Druj action, so the Dance of Navarr and Thorn would need to be performed again. Some vates doubted whether restoring them from Anvil was wise.

Urizen.t: The Citadel Guard, swelled by 1,000 Urizeni recruits who would desert if the campaign faltered, helped push the Druj back in Clypion. The surviving Urizen of the territory began to come out of hiding to fight for their home.

Wintermark.t: The Fist of the Mountain marched across the Empire to join the fight and helped turn the tide in Clypion. Wintermark war scout Kefry Lanesson sought aid for emptied former prisoners, some of them Wintermarkers.

This little light of mine.o: In Summer 384YE nearly forty thousand Imperial soldiers from five nations fought an equal Druj host in Zenith and narrowly pushed the orcs back in Clypion, leaving the Empire nine-tenths of the way to a beachhead. The page also set out a Summer Solstice battle to kill Karvor Eyepeel and several conjunctions.

Hahnmark/Kronemark.t: Prosperous grimnir of Kronehal pledged a true vervain and another herb for each of their afflicted folk saved from the Grove of the Halls.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: The text looted from the Spire of Sleet was being carried to the Palace of the Sleepers in Kroll, unless Imperial heroes intercepted it.

Zenith/Clypion.t: Imperial armies came nine-tenths of the way to capturing Clypion, though its eastern spires stayed with the Druj. Killing Karvor Eyepeel at the Solstice would collapse the Mount Ossa salient and take the region.

Zenith/Iteri.t: Taking Clypion would isolate Iteri. Each of Karvor's tepel killed and looted would cut the victory points needed to take Iteri, provided the Empire attacks it next season.

Zenith/Lustri.t: The Druj kept a familiar Spring-magic fortification over Lustri's woods. A conjunction to Sleetstorm Pass in south-western Lustri offered a chance to recover the stolen text.

Zenith/Proceris.t: A Druj labyrinth of rotting wood and mist rose around the ruined Golden Cascade, and Proceris permanently gained the Nightwoven quality. Conjunctions there concerned Khelver and the looted Spire of Sleet.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj champion Khelver is described as a veteran of the war in Casinea.

Hahnmark.t: The grimnir of Kronehal in Hahnmark promised herbs, including true vervain, for every afflicted former prisoner saved, since some of them hail from their Hall.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fist of the Mountain marched from Kallavesa to Zenith, guided by Autumn magic.

Morrow.t: The Druj sought to rout the Imperial armies back into Morrow. An Imperial victory at the Solstice might inspire Morrow's spires to help drive the Druj from Iteri.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: a clear victory might inspire the spires of Redoubt to help retake Zenith.

Reikos.t: The Amulet of Truth sought in Zenith was stolen by Khelver from the Tabernacle museum in Reikos, where he slew its last curator. The ruined museum has since been swallowed by Llofir's magic.

Sarangrave.t: Druj reinforcements marched out of the Sarangrave's forests into Zenith. Vikari serving the ghulai Cintra Blackstaff were bearing a stolen text back there.

Zenith.t: The Empire narrowly pushed the Druj back but still lacked a beachhead. The territory remained Terrorised and under miasma, its trods collapsed, and a Solstice battle offered the chance to cut it in two.

This might be your battle.d: Mazo i Zabala i Erigo's statement urging attacks around the Isle of Balsagoth caught on among the Freeborn, League, Highguard and some Urizen captains. The Grendel, overconfident after destroying the Freeborn Storm and the Atalaya shipyard, had an armada off Sarvos and privateers chasing Imperial merchants. Fleets could join "Attack the Slavers" and military units "Raid the Salt Mines". Total fleet strength would set the target, from Grendel shipping through the Temple of Tempest Jade, Vorlach, Balsagoth, up to Dubhtraig itself. Soldier strength would decide how many slaves were freed and how much was looted. Fleet Master Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra was expected to coordinate the raid. Freed slaves would gain sanctuary under Eska Crowspeaker's mandate.

Grendel.t: The Grendel faced a possible large Imperial raid on their shipping, the Temple of Tempest Jade, Vorlach, Balsagoth or Dubhtraig. Their slaves, mithril, weirwood and Salt Lords' prestige were all at risk, as was their ability to raise new navies and armies.

Highguard.t: The call to strike the slavers spread to Highguard. Its captains could join the raid, and freed slaves would likely be settled around the Bay of Catazar nations, Highguard among them.

The League.t: League captains embraced the call to raid the Broken Shore. The League was among the Bay of Catazar nations likely to receive liberated slaves.

Urizen.t: Some Urizen captains took up the call to attack the Grendel. Southern Urizen was named as a likely destination for slaves freed in the raid.

This might be your battle.o: Spurred by a Freeborn statement of principle calling for privateers to strike Grendel slavers, an opportunity arose in Autumn 382YE for Imperial fleets and military units to raid the Broken Shore, free slaves and disrupt the Grendel. It was available only for the Autumn Equinox and the season that followed.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Grendel believed they owned the bay, but Imperial fleets were invited to sail across it to strike the Broken Shore. The freed slaves would likely be brought to the nations around its shores.

Sarvos.t: A Grendel armada lay at anchor outside Sarvos, one the Empire could not match. The Grendel invasion of the city a year earlier was cited as reason to strike back at Dubhtraig.

Shayeel.t: The Grendel slave port and mining town of Vorlach on Shayeel's northern coast was a potential raid target if Imperial fleet strength reached 10,000. A strong enough attack could free up to 1,500 slaves, halt Salt Lord Moorvain's salt and mithril mines and leave lasting damage.

This old house.d: Feroz was left financially ruined by Governor Rahab, and recovery had already begun, aided by an appraisal proposed by Lizzie Stamp of Bildewold. Last season the Prosperity Assembly sent Katya Vasillova Reznikov to aid the territory. Ivan Veralova Esskvich proposed a Prosperity Assembly mandate that would remove the abandoned quality from Oranseri and Afarjasse. It would also raise labour costs in Feroz to four crowns a wain until no region there is impoverished. Inspired by Mabel's statement, Marcelo i Porfirio i Guerra proposed a General Assembly mandate that would permanently raise labour costs for all commissions to four crowns a wain and lift the Senate's available commissions to fourteen. That mandate would not apply in Feroz. If both were enacted, the Feroz increase would also become permanent.

Grendel.t: Grendel held part of Feroz that season, so any increase in labour costs for commissions in the territory under the Prosperity Assembly mandate would bear on works there.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Mabel's statement of principle cites Casinea, a Highborn-held territory, as a place where the same work should earn the same pay as in Feroz.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Lizzie Stamp of Bildewold's appraisal of Feroz is credited from her time as Senator for Bregasland, a territory then held by the Jotun.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn are central to the story: their territory of Feroz is being rebuilt, and it is a Freeborn architect, Marcelo i Porfirio i Guerra, who urged higher wages across the Empire.

Urizen.t: If the General Assembly mandate passed without a greater majority, it would not affect commissions wholly in Urizen. The Urizen national assembly would then likely have the chance to enact a similar mandate.

Varushka.t: If the General Assembly mandate passed without a greater majority, it would not affect commissions wholly in Varushka. The Varushkan national assembly would then likely have the chance to enact a similar mandate.

Wintermark.t: If the General Assembly mandate passed without a greater majority, it would not affect commissions wholly in Wintermark. The Wintermark national assembly would then likely have the chance to enact a similar mandate.

This old house.o: In Autumn 388YE the Prosperity Assembly's work to rebuild Feroz prompted two proposed Synod mandates. One would lift the abandoned quality from Oranseri and Afarjasse, and the other, put forward by a Freeborn architect, would raise wages for labourers and architects across the Empire.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: The proposed Prosperity Assembly mandate would immediately remove Afarjasse's abandoned quality.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: The Cazar Straits would remain impoverished even if the Prosperity Assembly mandate were enacted, so the higher Feroz labour costs would continue while it stays so.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The proposed mandate would immediately lift Oranseri's abandoned quality, though the region would remain impoverished, keeping the higher Feroz labour costs in place.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Lizzie Stamp of Bildewold proposed her appraisal of Feroz while serving as Senator for Bregasland.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Mabel's statement holds that the people of Feroz should not accept less pay than for the same work in Casinea.

Feroz.t: Still recovering from Rahab's ruinous rule, Feroz could see its abandoned regions restored under the Prosperity Assembly mandate, with labour costs for new commissions there raised to four crowns a wain. Only that mandate can change things in Feroz, and the General Assembly proposal would not apply there.

Thorn and bone.d: With its warding stones gone, the vallorn surged from Bendol into Nesustak Forest. Irra Harah's Wooden Fastness ward aided the defenders but also invigorated the vallornspawn, sharply raising casualties. When retreat was debated, the Black Thorns refused, and the Imperial forces pushed the spawn back; by the Summer Solstice the vallorn was quiescent. Meanwhile the Hidden Snake and Poison Crane, accompanied by Agramant-bound Winter husks and tortured souls, attacked from Lower Saarnath. They were routed, losing nearly twice the Empire's roughly five hundred dead, but they escaped pursuit, only to be cut down by Druj archers at the Sanath border. Both armies will disband after the Solstice. Axos completed its claim on Thornfen.

Druj.t: The Hidden Snake and Poison Crane were broken in Turan Flats and denied refuge by the Druj of the Salt Flats of Sanath. Both armies will disband, bringing an end to the Banded Snake and Marshlizard septs, and their Winter spirits and tortured souls threaten to be unleashed when they fall.

Highguard.t: The Granite Pillar defended the septs of the Mallum in Nesustak Forest and stood by the Black Thorns when retreat was considered. Rebels unable to fight fled west under Highguard's protection.

Navarr.t: The Black Thorns led the first line of defence against the vallorn and refused point blank to retreat, determined that Nesustak Forest should not share the fate of Eastring. Their resolve turned the tide.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the trapping of the fleeing Druj is compared to the old Druj retreat from Holberg.

Urizen.t: The Citadel Guard held firm in the marsh to defeat the Druj invasion of Turan Flats, and studied the Winter magic binding the enemy armies. The Urizeni now face raids from Druj remnants, which will be far more dangerous if the two generals survive.

Varushka.t: The Boyar's Hasta fought between the Black Thorns and Granite Pillar against the vallorn, aided by Irra Harah's servants. The Golden Axe flanked and broke the Druj invaders in Turan Flats.

Thorn and bone.o: In Summer 388YE the Black Thorns, Boyar's Hasta and Granite Pillar, fighting alongside the Nesustak rebels, drove the vallorn of Bendol back out of Nesustak Forest. In Turan Flats the Citadel Guard and Golden Axe defeated an invasion by the Druj Hidden Snake and Poison Crane, who were then trapped in Sarangrave when their own kin in the Salt Flats of Sanath refused to let them return.

Hercynia/Northpines.t: Mentioned in passing: used as a comparison for the lingering vallorn danger now facing Nesustak Forest.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Lower Saarnath.t: Mentioned in passing: the Hidden Snake and Poison Crane launched their invasion across the border from Lower Saarnath into Turan Flats.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: With its warding stones spent, the vallorn of Béantal Dol erupted outward before being driven back. It has now slipped into an uneasy quiescence, still uncontained and still very powerful.

Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh.t: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn had already been held back here by heroes using the Sentinel Gate, and the Bloodwater Spears joined the defence of Nesustak.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: Thornfen's displaced population was exiled to Kroll. If the Winter spirits bound to the Druj armies are not contained, Agramant's ravenous husks will torment the region.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: The vallorn surged across the river and nearly overwhelmed the forest before the Imperial armies and rebels drove it back and uprooted its seeds. The forest was spared lasting infestation, but heavy blood was shed where the Wooden Fastness empowered the spawn.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: Axos finished claiming Thornfen with the Senate's approval and exiled its population, save those with ties to the citadels. The region faces torment from Agramant's husks if the Druj Winter spirits are not trapped.

Sarangrave/Turan Flats.t: Imperial forces defeated the Druj invaders here, and the trapped remnants now face a final battle at the Fens of Varreth. If Het Trakaa's tortured souls are not exorcised, the region will be tormented.

Sarangrave/Whisperwood.t: The vallorn's eruption was weakened here, and Thornfen's exiles were sent here. Druj guerrillas with heralds of Surut also threaten to burn a weirwood tree at the Fingers of the Devourer.

Therunin/East Ashes.t: Mentioned in passing: the Pilgrim's Defiance's fight against Tharunind there is cited as a warning of what vallorn infestation brings.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Mentioned in passing: its loss to the Tainted Basilisk's malice spurred the Navarr's refusal to abandon Nesustak Forest.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, which allows a painless death to Imperial citizens captured by the Druj or dying in vallorn miasma, extends into Brocéliande.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Nesustak Forest is said to be left in no more danger from the vallorn than Northpines.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the page recalls the Druj retreat from Holberg years ago as a precedent for the fleeing armies' fate.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Warriors of the Witness, the Spires of Rarckan and the Beacon of Iskrid lined the border and shot down the retreating Hidden Snake and Poison Crane, refusing to let the defeated armies return.

Sarangrave.t: The vallorn was driven back from Nesustak Forest and the Druj invasion of Turan Flats was defeated, though the trapped Druj armies remain in the territory. Axos completed its claim on Thornfen, and an Autumn enchantment helped reduce casualties across the territory.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tainted Basilisk's raising of Tharunind and the losses of East Ashes and Eastring are recalled, and Kaela's Gift extends into Therunin.

Those memories of you.d: The Sarcophan Delves stayed friendly but resented the Senate's new tariffs, which may complicate customs at the Alivetti estates in Sarvos. Hahnmark had ended its viezesmaak arrangement with the Kraft brothers, and Brenna's Gift reverted to 36 rings per farm. The Zuredruiven vintners offered draaikolkbloem cultivation and new Wintermark potion recipes, and invited an Apothecaries Guild assessment. The House of the Jackal sought 70 thrones to keep Jakhalsmarkt open, and a Sarcophan scholar offered to buy vallorn goods. Axos held Thornfen, removed its Druj inhabitants and was rebuilding the Tower of the Skink. It resented being left to defend Sarangrave, and Navarr captains still faced suspicion in Axou ports.

Druj.t: The Axou removed the former Druj subjects living in Thornfen, and still fight the Winter spirits the Druj drew into Sarangrave.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but the Sarcophan Delves extended their protection to the independent city-state of Beoraidh in Mareave.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn stevedores appear in the opening fiction at Crown's Quay, where a Sarcophan captain refuses to pay the new duty.

Navarr.t: Navarr ship captains visiting Axou ports still face suspicion and a trade penalty after the Autumn Equinox. This is expected to ease by the Winter Solstice unless something goes wrong.

The League.t: The tariffs that angered Sarcophan merchants were proposed by Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar, Senator for Temeschwar. The Sarcophan enclave at the Alivetti estates in Sarvos may now become a route for goods to slip past customs.

Urizen.t: Most Urizen still shun settling Sarangrave, while Axou settlers flow in and may eventually outnumber them there. The deBruin family also supplies weirwood to Urizen.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sarcophan have made inroads into Varushka, and the Varushkan example of the Apothecaries Guild assessing Elder's Gift inspired calls to examine draaikolkbloem.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk ended the Kraft brothers' viezesmaak trade, and Wintermark apothecaries gained two new draaikolkbloem potion recipes, subject to continued good relations with the Zuredruiven vintners. Wintermark's Thanmir Hrafnar serves as ambassador to Axos.

Those memories of you.o: An Autumn 388YE Wind of Fortune updated Imperial relations with the Sarcophan Delves and the Citadels of Axos. It covered Sarcophan unhappiness at new mercantilist tariffs, a herb opportunity in Hahnmark and a price for keeping the Jakhalsmarkt open, alongside Axou settlement of Thornfen and their frustrations over Sarangrave.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: The independent city-state of Beoraidh came under Sarcophan protection, ostensibly to help guarantee its neutrality.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: The Axou cleared Thornfen of its former Druj subjects and are rebuilding the Tower of the Skink with white granite and salvage from Sephals. Its garrison still struggles to grow while Axou settlers move in.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction takes place at Crown's Quay, where Sarcophan ships are turned away over the newly imposed duties.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: an earlier Wind of Fortune on growing Sarcophan influence in the Bay of Catazar is listed in further reading.

Hahnmark.t: Brenna's Gift returned to providing 36 rings per farm once the Kraft brothers left. Herb garden owners received a gift of draaikolkbloem and may now choose to cultivate it, at the cost of some other herbs.

Mareave.t: The Sarcophan Delves extended their protection to the city-state of Beoraidh, ostensibly to guarantee its neutrality.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: The Axou showed no interest in supporting the Imperial venture into the Salt Flats, at least not with their armies.

Sarangrave.t: Axou forces defended northern Sarangrave against Winter spirits, but the Grand Council resents the Empire leaving the defence to them. Axou settlers steadily arrived in the territory.

Sarvos.t: The Alivetti estates remain the centre of Sarcophan influence. The new tariffs mean goods are only inspected at the land border into Sarvos proper, making smuggling easier.

Those that break a thing.d: The Gathered Storm, swollen with pirates, the fallen corsairs of Isidore i Boyaga, the Navarr traitors of Liath's Blade and a dozen escaped Iron Confederacy ships led by Suranni servants of Dumon, struck Trivento by sea and land. Fighting reached the streets, and the College of the Liberated came under attack. The Red Wind Corsairs, caught part-way through taking to the sea, harried the pirates and were joined by Sarcophan ships from the Alivetti Estates. The attackers fled west, probably towards Madruga or Feroz, having done only minor damage. Afterwards, wrecker gangs accompanied by heralds of Siakha landed to threaten regiones in Sarvos and Necropolis, and Mawrig's Point in Madruga.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: former Grendel vessels sailed with the Gathered Storm, and the newly seaborne Red Wind Corsairs are said to be ready to face the Grendel.

Highguard.t: A wrecker gang landed east of Crown's Quay, butchered a merchant bound for Sanctuary and made for the Stone of Suffering, apparently to curse Necropolis. The Champion of Loyalty, Talos, was asked to stop them.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the traitors of Liath's Blade blamed the Empire for failing to recover Liathaven from the Jotun.

Navarr.t: The traitorous false-steading Liath's Blade, under Captain Ioan Bloodstride, led the bloody fighting in Trivento's streets. They claimed they were angered by the Empire's failure to recover Liathaven, but they seemed just as eager to plunder.

The Brass Coast.t: The Red Wind Corsairs, built around three flagships and rallying corsair family vessels, were decisive in saving Trivento and routed the renegade corsairs of Isidore i Boyaga. They lost several ships and crews, but are now a navy.

The League.t: League soldiers fought in Trivento's streets to protect Sarvos's second city, while the Great Chain and Our Lady of Pride held. The raid did only minor damage and had no real effect on taxation.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs marched to Sarvos from Mitwold after the Summer Solstice.

Those that break a thing.o: In Autumn 387YE the Children of Wrecks attacked Trivento in Sarvos for a second time with a larger armada. They were driven off by the Great Chain, the garrison of Our Lady of Pride and the Red Wind Corsairs, who took heavy losses but completed their transformation into an Imperial navy.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Mentioned in passing: the curses of Siakha have cut the Cazar Straits off from the Coast with churning seas and monsters.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: The village of Meceares raised the alarm and warned villages deeper in Calvos Sound when wrecker sails appeared. The wreckers landed out of sight and were later found camped around Mawrig's Point.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Mentioned in passing: the islands of Free Landing are isolated from the Coast by Siakha's curses.

Sarvos/Bocche.t: Trivento was assailed from the sea and from the east, its harbour chain was attacked by carcharadon, and fighting spread through its streets as raiders tried to loot Bocche's wealth. The defenders drove them off with only minor damage.

Sarvos/Uccelini.t: Some wrecker ships slipped through the eastern isles of Uccelini and landed near Glass Point. They were bound for the Circle of Savagery, apparently to curse Sarvos.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Children of Wrecks gathered pirates and raiders from across the Bay into their armada. The Red Wind Corsairs, now a navy, can reach any port on the Bay to pursue them or face the Grendel.

Feroz.t: Many Red Wind corsair families come from Feroz, now held by the Children of Wrecks, and the defeated Gathered Storm is thought to be retreating west towards bases in Madruga or Feroz.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Liath's Blade invoked the Empire's failure to retake Liathaven from the Jotun in their battle-cries.

Madruga.t: The servants of Siakha occupy Atalaya, and the Gathered Storm may be retreating there. A wrecker gang also landed near Meceares and camped at Mawrig's Point, and the Champion of Vigilance, Jared, was asked to stop them.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs set out from Mitwold to march to Sarvos.
