Necropolis.t: Wreckers landed east of Crown's Quay, left a trail of destruction and headed for the Stone of Suffering, a Winter regio, probably to curse the territory. Talos, the Champion of Loyalty, was asked to stop them.

Sarvos.t: Trivento was attacked from sea and land, with fighting in its streets and at the College of the Liberated, but the defenders drove the raiders off with little damage. Wreckers then landed near Glass Point seeking the Circle of Savagery, and the Champion of Prosperity, Tom Appleseed, was asked to stop them.

Those who worship.d: The temple had been delayed by opposition from Abaddon de Rondell and the Assembly of the Nine and ran over time and budget, but only finishing work remained. Once complete it would improve relations with Asavea, and the Asaveans would appoint an Imperial liaison guided by the Senator for Feroz. A temple of the Way in Nemoria could then begin, needing 20 wains of white granite and either 10 Thrones or the Joãon family's slave labour. The Synod endorsed the Nemorian temple, mandating Lucifaro to use liao to encourage missionaries there. The Asavean priest Almodin Oktístis offered to oversee two large Senate commissions a season for 8 Thrones, and the Senate agreed to pay his stipend.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn Oran hosts the new Asavean temple, a Freeborn senator's earlier motion underpins the planned temple in Nemoria, and Almodin Oktístis, who had grown fond of the Brass Coast and worked closely with Freeborn architects and builders, was retained by the Senate.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Urizen priest Solas had attempted a veto that very nearly ended the temple project before it began.

Those who worship.o: In Winter 380YE the Asavean temple of Balo and the Black Bull in the port of Oran neared completion and was expected to open to Asavean sailors by the Spring Equinox 381YE. Its completion would allow a reciprocal temple of the Way to be built in Nemoria, the Asavean capital.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: In the port of Oran the Asavean temple's structure is finished, and three months of decoration and furnishing should see it offering services to Asavean sailors by the Spring Equinox.

Feroz.t: The temple of Balo and the Black Bull nears completion in Oran, and the Senator for Feroz will guide the Asavean choice of the Imperial liaison to its priests, a role offering access to Asavean goods.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Maher i Zaydan i Riqueza, who raised the original temple motion as Senator for Kahraman, is expected by the Asaveans to oversee the Nemorian temple and decide how its title is appointed.

Thoughts are free (Trade Winds).d: The Sumaah Republic remained at war and Zemeh stayed closed, though dispatches still reached its embassy in Necropolis. Its Synod was considering the late Highborn Asher of Felix's Watch as a Paragon or Exemplar, while it claimed to hold the Imperial Crown and refused the Winter Solstice symposium unless it was wholly orthodox. Asavea resented delays to the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz, putting off any Temple of the Virtues in Nemoria until after Spring 381YE. The Commonwealth rescinded its extra tariffs but awaited concrete action. Jarm let its restrictions lapse and sent a negotiator. The Sarcophan Delves exchanged embassies with the Grendel. Axos invited Imperial traders after the Senate commissioned an embassy in Cargo.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Axou ships risking the Barren Sea approach could prove a boon to ports on the shores of the Semmerlak.

Grendel.t: The Grendel Salt Lords exchanged embassies with the Sarcophan Bedelaar Huisbaas, with Sarcophan diplomats opening one somewhere on the Broken Shore. Grendel pirates in the Bay of Catazar were seen as a threat to Axou merchants sailing to the Empire.

Highguard.t: The Sumaah kept sending dispatches to their embassy in Necropolis, and their Synod was considering naming the late Highborn Asher of Felix's Watch among their Paragons and Exemplars.

The Brass Coast.t: The delayed Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz soured Asavean feeling and pushed any trade benefits back to Spring 381YE at the earliest. Sarcophan merchants also made curious but seemingly unthreatening enquiries about the Krakenfire Armada, believed to be a Freeborn corsair family.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos and Tassato are named as ports from which Imperial captains set sail each season.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Meade is named as one of the Empire's ports sending trade ships abroad.

Urizen.t: The Senate had commissioned an Axou embassy in Cargo, near the Jarmish embassy, and Axos reciprocated by inviting Imperial civil servants to the Towers of Kantor.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Korotny is named as one of the Empire's ports sending trade ships abroad.

Thoughts are free (Trade Winds).o: In Autumn 380YE, trade captains brought news of how foreign powers reacted to the Senate's statement denouncing slavery and to other Imperial affairs. The Commonwealth eased its trade restrictions, Asavea grew displeased, Jarm shrugged, the Sumaah stayed hostile, and Axos opened its ports to Imperial trade.

Bay of Catazar.t: The constant threat of Grendel pirates in the bay was expected to test whether Axou black-sailed merchant ships would brave the route to Imperial ports.

Feroz.t: Delays in completing the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull, and the Synod's opposition to it, angered the Asaveans and held up the proposed Temple of the Virtues in Nemoria.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Korotny is listed among the Imperial ports whose captains trade overseas.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Brass Coast ports such as Siroc and Lacre are listed among the Empire's trading harbours.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Meade is listed among the Imperial ports whose captains trade overseas.

Necropolis.t: The Sumaah embassy in Necropolis continued to receive diplomatic dispatches despite the ongoing war.

Redoubt.t: An Axou embassy had been commissioned in Cargo, not far from the Jarmish embassy, opening the way for trade with the citadels of Axos.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the ports from which brave captains set sail each season.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: as a territory on the Semmerlak, it could benefit if Axou merchants chose the Barren Sea approach.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the ports from which brave captains set sail each season.

The Semmerlak.t: Ports on the shores of the Semmerlak could gain substantially if Axou ships took the Barren Sea approach to avoid Grendel pirates.

Thousands or more.d: The survey found Ossium's forests unusually rich, so forest resources there yield 2 extra measures. Its metals are poor, so mining commissions cost double. The five spoils of war were the Palace of Orieb, the Stinking Market, Marshstand Skerry, the Bonehives and the Field of Glory. Each came with a recommended title and possible upgrades. Marshstand Skerry is a dual Spring–Winter regio tied to Agramant that needs animal sacrifice. The civil service also proposed a port at Bittershore, a barracks at Karantzy in Nearweald and an extension of the Iron Roads across Ossium. It warned that the territory's under-developed state greatly raises labour costs, including those for upgrading the Crawling Depths and for Ketsov's opportunities.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish forces are named alongside Varushkans in the slaughter at the Field of Glory, and a Bittershore port would open an option to expand the docks at Lacre.

Druj.t: The Druj's former holdings in Ossium, including Bleakbane's palace, a Bone Serpent ghulai's skerry and the Amber Scorpion insect farms, were catalogued as Imperial spoils of war.

Imperial Orcs.t: Bonewall Tresshak and Bonewall Koshhok helped win over the freed servants at the Bonehives, and most of the freed orcs left to join the Imperial Orcs.

Navarr.t: The Lower Tarn Valley in Navarr's Therunin was named as one of the few places where a new bonehive could be established, with the Keeper's approval.

The League.t: Holberg's Utterlund or Misericorde, where the Sand Fisher orcs now thrive, could host a new bonehive or a future Semmerlak dock.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule may have slain Bleakbane or her apprentices during the events at Orieb in Spring 383YE.

Varushka.t: Varushkan forest owners in Ossium gain extra production, Varushkan settlers drive the new vales, and the Senate placed all five new titles under the unanimous appointment of the Varushkan senators.

Wintermark.t: Wittal Grove in Wintermark's Kallavesa was identified as a possible site for a new bonehive, with the Keeper's approval.

Thousands or more.o: After Ossium's conquest, the civil service surveyed the territory's wealth and catalogued five captured Druj structures that could become Imperial titles, along with further development opportunities. The Senate then decided that all five titles would be appointed by unanimous decision of the Varushkan senators.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Misericorde, now home to the thriving Sand Fishers, could host a new bonehive and was named as a likely first site for a new Semmerlak dock.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Utterlund was named as an alternative site for a new bonehive or a future Semmerlak dock.

Kallavesa/Wittal Grove.t: Wittal Grove's mix of forest and marsh makes it a possible site for a new bonehive producing three doses of each substance.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: Bittershore, vacated by the Sand Fishers, was proposed for a costly new port that would end its under-developed status and create a Merchant-boyar of Bittershore.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: The Drownbark Forest holds three of the spoils: the Palace of Orieb, the rowdy Stinking Market and the dual-natured Marshstand Skerry.

Ossium/Echofell.t: The Echofell's south-east holds the Bonehives, an Amber Scorpion insect farm producing unique narcotic and medicinal substances.

Ossium/Galath Fields.t: The haunted Field of Glory in Galath Fields yields marrowort for a Grieftender of the Forgotten, and nearby Ketsov's reassessed fortification options now look costly.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: Boyar Irina Karantzy's new vale in Nearweald could gain a barracks and armoury, which would remove the region's underpopulated quality and aid Varushkan armies.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Mentioned in passing: Marshstand Skerry is said to have been abandoned since before the Webwood fell.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Lower Tarn Valley's forest and marsh make it a possible site for a new bonehive, with the Keeper's approval.

Volodmartz/Livardz.t: Mentioned in passing: settlers from Livardz founded the Karantzy vale in Nearweald.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: wagon raiders from Orieb sell goods taken in daring raids across the border into the Forest of Ulnak.

Holberg.t: Holberg's Utterlund or Misericorde could host a new bonehive, and a Bittershore port could lead to a new Semmerlak dock there.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa's Wittal Grove was named as a possible site for a duplicate bonehive, built by separate commission with the Keeper's approval.

Karov.t: Karov already has Iron Roads, and a Bittershore port would open an option to expand the docks at Korotny.

Karsk.t: Wagon raiders from Karsk run the Stinking Market, an Iron Road from Karsk could cross Ossium, and the docks at Ivarsgard could be expanded if a Bittershore port were built.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova is cited as already having a road network, unlike Ossium.

Ossium.t: Ossium's resources, five captured structures and development options were catalogued, and the Senate set all five new titles to be appointed by the Varushkan senators.

Semmerholm.t: The Bittershore cove once used for Druj raft attacks on Semmerholm is the proposed port site, which would open an option to expand the docks at Lacre.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: freed orcs at the Bonehives were drawn by tales of Skarsind and left to join the Imperial Orcs.

The Semmerlak.t: A proposed port at Bittershore would raise taxation from the territories bordering the Semmerlak and could lead to expanded docks around its shores.

Therunin.t: Therunin's Lower Tarn Valley could host a duplicate bonehive, built by separate commission with the Keeper's approval.

Volodmartz.t: Wagon raiders from southern Volodmartz trade at the Stinking Market, and settlers from Livardz founded the Karantzy vale in Nearweald.

Threats that are to come.d: Commissioned by Lula, Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund and Cees van Holberg, Gelberg found Holberg well supplied by imports from Dawn, so the benefits are mostly for the future. The Seven Stores, in Holfried, would drill three deep wells and build seven food stores. They would protect the city against a siege for two seasons, feed any number of refugees and keep one sheltering army in supply. An option would subsidise food for the poor. The Seven Dykes would revive old civil service plans to drain Rebeshof and Utterlund and end the farm penalty in Holberg. A further amendment, the Seven Farms, would persuade the Sand Fishers to raise Marcher pigs there as foreign owners. That would raise taxes by up to six thrones and modestly increase League army supply. All three remain proposals.

Dawn.t: Holberg currently relies on Dawnish yeofolk and Semmerholm merchants for much of its food. Dawn's Estmure, guarded by the Adamant Gate, keeps open the mountain pass that makes any siege of Holberg fail.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: their thirty-year campaign failed to close the Estmure pass, and their destruction of Holberg's dykes let the marshes return.

The League.t: The League could fund siege stores, wells and drainage for Holberg, and court the Sand Fishers as pig farmers. Doing so would boost taxes and League army supply, though not by enough to raise a fourth army.

Threats that are to come.o: Professor Immanuel Gelberg's Commonwealth appraisers, Die Beurteilung, assessed ways to secure Holberg's food and water against future sieges or a flood of refugees. They proposed three opportunities: deep wells with seven grain stores, draining marshland with the Seven Dykes, and persuading the Sand Fishers to farm the drained land.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the marshlands whose draining would most obviously improve Holberg's food supply, though the Seven Dykes proposal drains only Rebeshof and Utterlund.

Holberg/Holfried.t: The proposed Seven Stores edifice, with three deep wells and seven Virtue-named food stores, would be built in hilly Holfried, where the city abuts Estmure's mountains.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: An enemy holding Holmauer and Rebeshof could cut the city's supply lines. The proposed stores would let refugees in Holmauer be fed without starvation.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: The Sand Fishers practise subsistence fishing and gathering in Misericorde. The appraisal suggests they might expand from there into large pig farms on drained neighbouring land.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: The Seven Dykes would drain Rebeshof, removing its marsh quality a year after completion. The Seven Farms idea would then see Sand Fisher pig farms established there. Its loss to an enemy would help cut the city's supply.

Holberg/The Morass.t: Mentioned in passing: named among the drowned marshes whose draining would improve food supply, but it is not part of the Seven Dykes proposal.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: The League Assembly urged making Utterlund more productive. The Seven Dykes would drain it within a year of completion, opening it to Sand Fisher pig farms as foreign-owned land.

Holberg.t: Holberg was offered wells and seven grain stores to withstand a two-season siege and feed any number of refugees. It was also offered the Seven Dykes to end its farming penalty and drain marshland for new farms.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm's merchants help feed Holberg. Its Estmure pass and the Adamant Gate form the main barrier any besieger would need to break before starving Holberg.

Three and three.d: Estavus declined to parley and instead sent servants to help rebuild Zenith and Urizen. She also said the Empire should make the offer if it wants her to staff a fane. Azoth agreed to a parley about the Last Singing Stone, the Tower of Light and Shadow and Skywise Gralka's ideas, and asked the Conclave to interdict Mark the Flesh Incorruptible. Eleonaris replied for Hayaak, who refuses all parley until Edric deGauvin is executed, and offered Blaze Dunning a trial of service. Wise Rangara agreed to parley but would not discuss herb lore. Siakha refused a formal parley but will meet the Spring Archmage at Azcara's Field. An unknown eternal agreed to parley with the Archmage of Day.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Wise Rangara mocked the Empire's belief that the Druj know more herb lore than it does, suggesting it simply keep fighting them and take that lore.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Siakha's chosen meeting place, Azcara's Field near the ruins of Shantarim, lies in Grendel-held Feroz.

Jotun.t: Hayaak, the Knight of Hawks, has sworn to support the Jotun on every battlefield where they fight the Empire until Edric deGauvin is executed. Blaze Dunning could only be his champion by renouncing the Empire and fighting alongside the Jotun.

Navarr.t: Azoth wants to discuss the Last Singing Stone with the Advisor on the Vallorn, suggesting its power might be unlocked for the Navarr nation's use and testing how adaptable the Navarr truly are.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: there were unreliable reports of Siakha's representatives observing League-held Sarvos.

Urizen.t: Estavus sent dozens of Autumn heralds across Urizen, and especially to Zenith and the Crucible of Fate, to aid the nation's rebuilding. Urizeni archmages Elyssiathain and Ematius secured parleys with Azoth and Wise Rangara.

Wintermark.t: Eleonaris offered the Winter-mark hero Blaze Dunning a chance to enter the Lion of Summer's service. She is to face three tests in the Hall of Worlds and must first find a way to get there.

Three and three.o: In the run-up to the Summer Solstice of 385YE, six eternals answered plenipotentiary messages sent by the Empire's archmages at the Spring Equinox. Three agreed to formal parleys, while the others declined or made other arrangements.

Feroz.t: Siakha's emissaries will meet the Archmage of Spring and her party at Azcara's Field, near the ruins of the corsair town of Shantarim, reached through a Sentinel Gate conjunction. Those staying inside the circle of safety will be unharmed.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: there were unreliable reports that heralds of Siakha had been seen in Sarvos, apparently observing the Empire.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: there were unreliable reports that representatives of Siakha had been seen in Sermersuaq, though their purpose was unclear.

Zenith.t: Dozens of Estavus's heralds descended on Zenith to suggest improvements and help rebuild it and the Crucible of Fate. Heralds of Siakha were also reportedly seen there.

Three celebrations and a funeral.d: An apparently accidental fire wrecked the Bastion basilica, the largest Little Mother orphanage outside Sarvos. Bishop Marianne di Sarvos died in it and was interred in Sarvos, leaving the prelacy vacant with reduced liao and votes. Cesare Enzo Di Trivento used an Imperial Wayleave to commission the repairs. The seminary of Zemress at Calvos drew pilgrims from at home and abroad. Rhaego i Zemress enacted a Freeborn mandate opening the way to replace the Broken Wheel festival. The Calvos pilgrimage mandate was never raised, but a translated Sumaah tale of Zemress was published. The General Assembly upheld Killian Mortére's mandate to consecrate the Academy of Arms. The Maze of Zoria remained available for consecration.

Dawn.t: Adelmar the Lion's birthplace at Weaving and the hall at Arnet were both put forward as shrines to the Dawnish-born exemplar. The General Assembly instead backed the Academy of Arms in Urizen.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a few Grendel orc merchants visiting Madruga reportedly paid their respects to Zemress, whom they call the Demon of the Bay.

Highguard.t: Highguard's city of Bastion lost its great white-granite Basilica of the Little Mother and orphanage to fire. Its repair has since been commissioned.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: they are the only nation whose priests have never held the title of Prelate of the Little Mother.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn saw pilgrims and trade flood to the Zemress seminary, and the Sumaah pressed them over the Broken Wheel. A mandate was enacted giving the nation the chance to seek a replacement festival, and a translated Sumaah tale of Zemress was published.

The League.t: The League mourned Bishop Marianne di Sarvos, a former Cardinal of Prosperity, who was buried in Sarvos. Merchant-prince Francesco Falenjame drew wide criticism for his callous remarks about the fire.

Urizen.t: The General Assembly upheld a mandate to consecrate Adelmar's original Academy of Arms in Redoubt as his shrine, though it was not yet known whether the true liao would be supplied.

Varushka.t: The Maze of Zoria, guarded by Illya Nikovitch Volkov, could be consecrated to Wisdom with true liao, but the page records no such consecration happening.

Three celebrations and a funeral.o: Fire gutted the Basilica of the Little Mother in Bastion, killing Prelate Marianne di Sarvos as she rescued children. At the same time the Synod was offered chances to honour Zemress, Adelmar the Lion and Zoria. The basilica's repair was later commissioned, and the General Assembly backed consecrating the Academy of Arms in Redoubt.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: Calvos Sound's seminary and the Kraken's Bane drew pilgrims from the Empire, Sumaah and beyond. Demand for local wine soared, and the seminary published a translated Sumaah tale of Zemress.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: The Maze of Zoria near Griejezdo in Mieriada could be consecrated to Wisdom. The Heirs of Lepidus stand ready to gather and publish pilgrims' stories of Zoria if it is.

Redoubt/Siluri.t: The original Academy of Arms on the slopes of Mount Siluri is to be consecrated as Adelmar's shrine under the upheld mandate, which carries a resonance of building a legacy.

Semmerholm/Ulvenholm.t: The shrine in the shadow of Arnet, associated with decisive action, was one of the competing consecration proposals but was not upheld.

Astolat.t: Adelmar's birthplace shrine in the town of Weaving was one of three proposed sites for consecration. It was not the option the General Assembly upheld.

Bastion.t: Fire gutted the Basilica of the Little Mother and killed its prelate. The scaffolded shell must be repaired or torn down, and repair was commissioned by Imperial Wayleave.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: an anecdote in the opening fiction recalls a magistrate threatening an arrest in Holberg.

Madruga.t: The seminary of Zemress at Calvos became a bustling pilgrimage site. It boosted the local wine trade and revived talk of shipyards.

Miekarova.t: The Maze of Zoria in Miekarova awaits a possible consecration to Wisdom. The Wisdom assembly's call to pilgrimage there met a mixed reception.

Redoubt.t: The General Assembly upheld a mandate to consecrate the first Academy of Arms in Redoubt as Adelmar's shrine, pending true liao.

Sarvos.t: Bishop Marianne di Sarvos was interred at the chapel of the Little Mother in Sarvos, beside the earlier prelates.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Zemress Islanders visiting Calvos return to their new homes in Segura.

Semmerholm.t: The pilgrim hall at Arnet, marking Adelmar's role in liberating Semmerholm, was proposed as a shrine but not chosen.

Three keys.d: Heralds who fought alongside the Bloodcloaks in Skallahn and the Golden Sun in the Barrens proposed changing their qualities to Woundbinder and Golden Juggernaut. With the Rod and Shield, they proposed walls and a sea-gate for Meade, a third Mournwold fortress at Sarcombe, an expanded Reumah's Rest guarding the Necropolis coast, a deadlier Spires of Dusk, and a Water Tower in Segura. Dawnish yeofolk offered the 'Last Hound' memorial as an alternative, and Sorin's herald offered the Black Hounds statues. After the Conclave interdicted the practice, Zakalwe made Prismatic Ink stronger for certain rituals at the Winter Solstice, except for Varushkan covens. The Senate later chose to remodel the Spires, and Lofyn Blood-cloak honed the Bloodcloaks.

Dawn.t: The Golden Sun was offered an upgrade to Golden Juggernaut with a new order honouring the Hounds of Glory. The Spires of Dusk were remodelled into a monument to the Hounds and to Dawnish rule in the Barrens.

Druj.t: The Golden Sun's campaign against the Druj in the Barrens was observed by Zakalwe's heralds. The Druj traps and the last traces of their power at the captured Spires of Dusk were torn out when the Senate chose the remodelling.

Grendel.t: The Grendel threat to the Necropolis coast prompted the proposal to raise Reumah's Rest to rank three and protect Longbeach and Sanctuary Sand from attack by sea. Their growing threat also figured in the Segura Water Tower plan.

Highguard.t: Highguard was offered a costly upgrade of Reumah's Rest in Necropolis, with sea walls, watchtowers and seabells along the whole coast to guard the tombs against the Grendel.

Jotun.t: The Jotun were the foes the Bloodcloaks fought in Skallahn. The proposed Sarcombe Pie scheme would stop them making Mournwold 'under threat' or using beachhead-easing orders there while all three fortresses stood.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Night magic that gave Navarr armies murderous fervour in Kahraman was cited as an example of the practice the Conclave interdicted.

The Brass Coast.t: Segura was offered the Water Tower fortress, with kamkrag outposts, protection from raiding and more marrowort. The Fire of the South's recent savagery enchantment was cited as the kind of magic now interdicted.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the walls of the League's cities are said to stir long-held jealousy among Meade's alders.

The Marches.t: The Marches were offered Bridget's Walk at Meade, with a new Merchant of Meade title, and the Sarcombe Pie scheme to guard Mournwold. Marcher orcs and alders offered to fund a third of the latter.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule is referenced only through the Bloodcloaks' disastrous retreat from Otkodov a century ago.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the page makes no specific reference to Urizen; it is linked only through the Empire-wide boons.

Varushka.t: Varushkan covens were singled out as the only ones Zakalwe would not let benefit from his Winter Solstice Prismatic Ink boon, and his heralds would not say why.

Wintermark.t: The Bloodcloaks could become a Woundbinder army by reviving the old scildran tradition of shield-bearers protecting grimnir. General Lofyn Blood-cloak provided the mithril and weirwood to make the change.

Three keys.o: After the Empire accepted three boons from Zakalwe, General of Day, at the Autumn Equinox 385YE, his heralds proposed ways to hone two Imperial armies and strengthen fortifications across the Empire. Zakalwe also rewarded the Conclave's interdiction of savagery-inducing magic with an extra ritual boon.

Mitwold/Meade March.t: Bridget's Walk, a rank one fortification with walls across the river mouth and a sea-gate, was proposed for Meade here.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Mentioned in passing: Alderly was named as a region where the Jotun might plant hidden caches as they did in Southmoor.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Mentioned in passing: Green March was named as vulnerable to Jotun caches and would be covered by the proposed protection.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Jarl Haakon's hidden caches had left Southmoor under threat, and the Sarcombe Pie fortress was proposed there to end that threat.

Necropolis/Coursmouth.t: Reumah's Rest stands in Coursmouth, and the proposed upgrade would make it a rank three fortress overseeing coastal defences.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Longbeach and Crown's Quay, currently poorly protected, would be shielded by the upgraded Reumah's Rest against attacks from the sea.

Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand.t: The beaches where the first Highborn landed would be protected by the upgraded Reumah's Rest against seaborne assault.

Segura/Iron Plains.t: The Iron Plains were proposed as the central site for the Water Tower, a rank two fortification guarding the whole of Segura.

Segura/Sobral Grasses.t: Home to the Zemress Islanders and the Iron Qanat, whose farms the proposed Water Tower would shield from plundering raiders.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish yeofolk cautiously returning here were among those who argued for the Last Hound memorial.

The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth.t: The Spires of Dusk stand here. The Senate chose to strip out the Druj defences and remodel the fortress as a memorial to the Hounds of Glory.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: Bastion is not specifically addressed; Highguard's interest here lies in Necropolis.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: its occupation was noted among recent invasions of the Marches, and the heralds asked to explore its fens.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the kamkrag proposal there inspired the Segura plan, and a Navarr campaign there was cited as an example of savagery magic.

Mitwold.t: Meade could be walled with a sea-gate as Bridget's Walk, creating a Merchant of Meade title to buy Caitun metals and swords for the market towns of Mitwold.

Mournwold.t: A new fortress at Sarcombe, backed by towers, sanctuaries and armouries, was proposed to guard the whole territory against Jotun incursions.

Necropolis.t: Reumah's Rest could be raised to a rank three fortification whose protection extended along the whole coast against seaborne Grendel attacks.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bloodcloaks were destroyed in a retreat from Otkodov almost a century ago.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not specifically addressed on the page.

Segura.t: The Water Tower and kamkrag were proposed to protect all of Segura from raiders such as the Corazón and to extend irrigation to its herb gardens. The Zemress families offered half the cost if it were commissioned by the Spring Equinox 386YE.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe's heralds observed the Bloodcloaks campaigning against the Jotun there.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar is not specifically addressed on the page.

The Barrens.t: The heralds observed the Golden Sun fighting the Druj here. Of the rival plans for the Spires of Dusk, the Senate chose to remodel it as a monument to the Hounds of Glory.

Three soldiers.d: The Urizen coven Ashen Flame performed The Three Watchers at the Spring Equinox, calling in a boon from Adamant. Aurum of the Nightingale Temple consecrated the shrine with an aura of Loyalty. Highborn or Urizen armies attacking Zenith from Morrow, or defending Morrow against attack from Zenith, gain 20% and take 10% fewer casualties. Druj patrols flee at the sight of the statues. Until the Autumn Equinox 384YE, Highborn military units cost one less mithril to upgrade and Highborn armies receive extra natural resupply. The Highborn assembly may pass one of two competing mandates, each needing a greater majority, granting either the Crusading Storm or the Put them to the Sword order.

Druj.t: Druj patrols turn and flee at the sight of the Three Watchers, unable to bear the statues and their Loyalty aura. A proposed Highborn mandate would give Highborn armies a merciless Put them to the Sword order aimed specifically at the Druj.

Highguard.t: Highborn pilgrims are flocking to the statues. Until the Autumn Equinox 384YE, Highborn armies recover twice as fast and military units cost one less mithril to upgrade. The assembly has one season to choose between the Crusading Storm and Put them to the Sword orders, and either mandate needs a greater majority.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn soldiers camped in Feroz hear of the statues and are heartened.

Urizen.t: Urizen commissioned the statues as thanks for Highborn sacrifice. Urizeni armies attacking Zenith from Morrow, or defending Morrow from Zenith, gain a morale bonus to territory and suffer fewer casualties.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers of Ossium are cited as an example of how ruling by fear weakens a people's virtue over time.

Three soldiers.o: Koboldi lent by the eternal Adamant completed the Three Watchers, three colossal statues of Highborn soldiers carved into the mountains to guard the High Pass between Morrow and Zenith, with a shrine consecrated with an aura of Loyalty at their base. The monument now strengthens Highborn and Urizen armies fighting over the pass, draws Highborn pilgrims, and lets the Highborn assembly choose a new permanent strategy for its armies.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn soldiers camped in Brocéliande have their spirits lifted by news of the statues.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn soldiers camped in Feroz have their spirits lifted by news of the statues.

Morrow.t: The Three Watchers guard the High Pass from Morrow. Highborn and Urizen armies attacking Zenith from here, or defending Morrow against attack from Zenith, gain 20% and take 10% fewer casualties.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers of Ossium are given as an example of how fear erodes a people's virtue.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is recalled as the first place where Highborn soldiers lost family and friends to the Druj.

Zenith.t: The statues watch over the High Pass into Druj-held Zenith. Highborn and Urizen armies attacking from Morrow gain a bonus, and Druj patrols flee rather than approach the pass.

Thresher's summer.d: Inspired by Clytemnestra of the House of the Wanderer, Urizeni visitors spread across Upwold and Mitwold. Some reached Bregasland, and those who went to Mournwold retreated before the Jotun invasion. Their willingness to endure gruelling work such as threshing won grudging respect, and every farm became a little more profitable. Jedediah Boon's Marcher friars found their beliefs about reincarnation as trees dismissed, but shriving and their pastoral guidance fascinated Urizeni priests. Urizen congregations swelled while Marcher spiritual matters were neglected. The architect Tacitus proposed a Landskeeper's Study at Oakwood where Urizen mana could be sold, and the empty Temple of the Four Winds in Peregro could become a monastery for debate. The Senate approved both, and they will benefit from each other while both endure.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are recalled as having sacked the Temple of the Four Winds before it was completed, until they were driven out of Morrow.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun invasion of the Mournwold forced Urizeni visitors there to retreat.

The Marches.t: Marcher farms received hundreds of Urizeni helpers for the harvest, making each a little more profitable and building respect between the nations. Marcher friars sent east earned admiration in Urizen, although spiritual matters at home were neglected in their absence.

Urizen.t: Urizeni mages, sentinels and scholars learned first-hand how hard farm work is and won Marcher respect. Visiting friars swelled Urizen congregations, raising their liao and votes, and sparked intense interest in shriving.

Thresher's summer.o: Following mandates from the Urizen and Marcher national assemblies, hundreds of Urizeni mages, sentinels and scholars helped bring in the Marcher harvest while scores of Marcher friars and monks shared their Virtue in Urizen, easing the rift between the two nations. The exchange inspired two commissions, a Landskeeper's Study and a Monastery of the Four Winds, both of which the Senate chose to build.

Morrow/Peregro.t: The Temple of the Four Winds in Peregro hosted Marcher monks and Urizeni priests, and the Senate chose to repurpose it as the Monastery of the Four Winds with a new Urizeni arbiter, liao and garden income.

Upwold/Ashbrook.t: Tacitus stayed with the short-handed monks of Oakwood in Ashbrook, where the Senate chose to build the Landskeeper's Study for visiting Urizen architects to discuss farm magic and sell mana.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: a few Urizeni visitors travelled as far as Bregasland to help with the harvest.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold was one of the two main territories where Urizeni visitors spread out to help farmers bring in the harvest.

Morrow.t: Marcher monks were housed at the empty Temple of the Four Winds in Morrow, which became a thriving centre of debate. The Senate chose to convert it into a permanent monastery.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: some Urizeni visitors went to the Mournwold but were forced to retreat in the face of the Jotun invasion.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the architect Tacitus, who proposed the Landskeeper's Study, came from the Spire of the White Sun in Redoubt.

Upwold.t: Upwold was a main destination for the Urizeni harvest helpers, and the Senate chose to build the Landskeeper's Study there to share farm magic and sell Urizen mana.

Thrones and principalities.d: Relations with Jarm remained hostile after the Liberty Pact, the sharing of Imperial lore with the Commonwealth and the Senate's embargo, and Jarm was at open war with the Commonwealth. Jarm had founded the Freedom Accord with Asavea and the Sarcophan Delves. Ambassador Anton Trescher offered the shield Measure in exchange for the Conclave disseminating Brotherhood of Tian. Jarm would add 10 rings of ilium for the disseminating order and 100 thrones to the Senate as clear inducements. Bojana Etura of the Circle of Six offered to buy ritual items in bulk through Guildmaster Xanthius, with collection planned at the Autumn Equinox. Trescher curtly dismissed warnings about the Hand of Dumon.

Grendel.t: Jarm had earlier supplied the Grendel with magical aid, including fortification rituals and rumoured mana, vis and foci, until Prospero's intervention ended it. The two still trade openly, and the Grendel are rumoured to have been approached to join the Freedom Accord, possibly already as signatories.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the new Imperial ambassador to Jarm, Nikita Teanga Volkov, is of Varushka and had worked to reopen communication with the Jarmish.

Thrones and principalities.o: The civil service's Summer 386YE report on the Principalities of Jarm found relations still bitter under a mutual trade embargo. It also set out a Jarmish offer to trade the relic shield Measure for the ritual Brotherhood of Tian and a request from the merchant Circle of Six to buy goods through the Artisans Guild.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Ambassador Trescher cited the situation in the Bay of Catazar as a reason the Empire might struggle to convey the shield from Jarm.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: Karov is named among the ports the House of Princes refuses to let Imperial fleets visit, apparently a variant spelling of the Jarmish port Kavor.

Through my sails.d: The Iron Confederacy executed ten Imperial citizens in Robec for alleged espionage. It kept its embargo, replaced its embassy staff in Sarvos and named the secular Baroness Lavasse as its voice, while still angered by the fine imposed on the Highborn behind the border killings. A Freeborn raid in Afarjasse broke a liao smuggling route. In Asavea a mob wrecked the Temple of the Seven Virtues in Nemoria after the Synod defaced Oktístis's works, and the northern rebellion collapsed. The Sarcophan offered land for an Imperial enclave in the Delves. The Faraden gained a blight cure and offered mithril to the Conclave. The Sumaah proposed a symposium on the Way.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish noble Ser Flora Du Soleil was among the ten Imperial citizens executed by the Iron Confederacy, and Dawn remained a possible site for a Kruidenkenner herb warehouse.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: a Synod statement blamed dealings with the Grendel and Druj for Axos's false expectations of orcs.

Grendel.t: The Grendel were letting Asavean merchants dock at the temple in Feroz, and the goodwill Imperial captains drew from it was likely to shift to the Grendel if Oran stayed in their hands for another season.

Highguard.t: The Iron Confederacy denounced the fine levied on Mordecai of Zephaniah's Lament and the other Highborn who killed its templars as an insult, and the matter ended talks on a criminal extradition treaty. The Highborn Accalon of Felix's Watch served as ambassador to the Sumaah.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Synod specifically called on Imperial Orc traders to show Axos their prosperity, offering an alternative to the example the Axou had seen in the Grendel and Druj.

Jotun.t: The Jotun charged Faraden traders a tithe to cross the Lasambrian Hills, and the page suggested that disaffected Faraden merchants might increasingly trade with the Jotun, who were at peace with them.

Navarr.t: The Navarr Hearc Stormsailor was executed in the Iron Confederacy, and the Kruidenkenner added Seren in Miaren as a possible site for a herb warehouse.

The Brass Coast.t: Four Freeborn were executed by the Suranni and the land border to the Confederacy stayed closed. Freeborn magistrates and militia destroyed a liao smuggling route through Feroz, and rumours persisted of Faraden smugglers slipping through Segura and Kahraman.

The League.t: Three League citizens were executed in Robec and the Suranni embassy in Sarvos saw its staff abruptly replaced. The Sarcophan asked that their own enclave be built in Sarvos or Karsk, and League citizens served as ambassadors to Faraden and the Commonwealth.

The Marches.t: The Senate had approved a Kruidenkenner warehouse at Meade in Mitwold to import Bladeroot from the Sarcophan Delves.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the page said developments involving the orc nations were covered elsewhere, and named Otkodov only as one of the Empire's smaller neighbours.

Urizen.t: Tarquinius Ankarien of Urizen, Ambassador to Axos, was sent by the Synod's enacted mandate to urge Imperial citizens to trade with the Axou.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark ship captain Jayce Audricsson was executed by the Suranni. Wintermark citizens held the ambassadorships to the Sarcophan Delves and to Jarm, and Wintermark remained a possible site for a Kruidenkenner warehouse.

Through my sails.o: The Summer 383YE Wind of Fortune set out the state of the Empire's relations with its human neighbours: Suranni executions of Imperial citizens and a new Iron Confederacy envoy, mob damage to the Imperial temple in Nemoria, fresh Sarcophan enclave offers, and Sumaah plans for talks on the Way. The Synod then enacted a mandate sending Tarquinius Ankarien to urge trade with Axos.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: Following a raid on a criminal stronghold during the Equinox, Freeborn magistrates and militia stormed a parador in Afarjasse and arrested members of the liao smuggling ring.

Mitwold/Meade March.t: Meade was the site of the Senate-approved Kruidenkenner warehouse importing Bladeroot from the Sarcophan Delves.

Necropolis/Longbeach.t: Mentioned in passing: Longbeach was not named on the page.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Axos trade mandate could inspire the territories along the Bay of Catazar if 50 doses of liao were committed.

Feroz.t: A liao smuggling route into the Iron Confederacy via Feroz was destroyed. The Imperial-Asavean temple there still stood, but with Oran in Grendel hands its benefits risked being lost, and the ongoing fighting deterred Suranni merchants.

Kahraman.t: Rumours persisted, still unconfirmed, that Faraden smugglers were entering the Empire through southern Kahraman to avoid tariffs.

Kalino.t: Baroness Lavasse advised the Suranni Dukes to secure the northern border of Arbonne, which the Empire calls Kalino, and chastised Duke Harold Guiscard for failing to do so.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Madruga was not named; the page referred only to the closed land border from the southern Brass Coast.

Miaren.t: The Kruidenkenner herbalists added the city of Seren in Miaren as a possible warehouse site because of its central location, an opportunity open until the end of the Summer Solstice.

Mitwold.t: The Senate had approved a Kruidenkenner warehouse at Meade, focused on importing Bladeroot.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis was not named; Highguard's only link on the page is the fine levied on the Highborn involved in the border incident.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov was listed as one of four smaller neighbours close enough to affect Imperial politics, with orc developments covered elsewhere.

Sarvos.t: The Suranni embassy in Sarvos was emptied and restaffed with new ambassadors, who announced that the High Priest would burn messages from Imperial citizens. The Sarcophan also asked for their own enclave to be built in Sarvos or Karsk.

Segura.t: Unconfirmed reports of Faraden smugglers in northern Segura persisted, and the ongoing conflict there was discouraging Suranni merchants from coming north.

Throw back the echoes.d: The General Assembly's upheld mandate imposed a one-fifth penalty on territory captured by Imperial armies in the Barrens using any order other than break the chains, until the Summer Solstice 385YE. Urizen and Varushkan armies were exempt because it lacked a greater majority. The Dawnish Assembly could pass one of three mandates: defy the rebuke while penalising Dawnish units not supporting the Barrens campaign, or embrace it and raise the penalty to a quarter or three tenths. Jaheris offered monsters to guard Dawnguard in return for a fane. Janon offered triumphant charge to Dawnish armies in return for rededicating Laroc Cathedral. Tharim offered steel-bound knights in return for feasting on Dawn's farms, mana sites and commissions. Sorin offered wolves to House Aurelius through a ritual.

Dawn.t: Dawn's centuries-old ambition to conquer the Barrens faced the Synod's penalty, and its Assembly and enchanters were offered mandates and eternal bargains to press the claim, each at a cost.

Druj.t: The Druj, whose armies were described as trapped in Zenith facing annihilation, held the Barrens and guarded the regio that House Aurelius could use to summon Sorin's wolves against them.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard was noted as having answered Dawn's challenge to take the most regions in the Barrens.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Tharim had previously sent his servants to fight the vallorn alongside the Navarr in return for feasting on their herb gardens and forests.

Urizen.t: Urizen's armies, including the Citadel Guard, were exempt from the Synod's penalty on conquering the Barrens because the mandate lacked a greater majority.

Varushka.t: Varushka explicitly joined Dawn's challenge to help reclaim the Barrens, and its armies were exempt from the Synod's penalty as they reject mandates not passed with a greater majority.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the symbols on Tharim's steel-bound knights were said to be nothing like Wintermark runes.

Throw back the echoes.o: After the General Assembly rebuked any campaign of conquest in the Barrens, Dawn was presented with Synod mandates to answer the rebuke and with offers of aid from the eternals Jaheris, Janon and Tharim to press its ancient claim. A conjunction also gave House Aurelius a chance to summon Sorin's wolves against the Druj.

Astolat/The Chase.t: Janon offered to grant Dawnish armies triumphant charge in the Barrens if Laroc Cathedral were rededicated to passion, replacing the Dean of Laroc Cathedral with a Keeper of the Silver Flame title, ideally held by Kahendrin Wordsmith.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Dawnguard, the Dawnish stronghold destroyed by the Druj, could be guarded by Jaheris's creatures with an effective military strength of 2500 if the Empire retook it and built him a fane there.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: The Barren Glen regio on the edge of the Heart of Peytaht, guarded by the Druj, was the site where House Aurelius could cast Sorin's ritual to gain wolves worth 1500 strength for a season, with some remaining for eleven winters.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Mentioned in passing: Murderdale was noted as having had Dawnish settlements during centuries of contest with the Druj.

Astolat.t: Janon asked that Laroc Cathedral be rededicated to passion, and Tharim sought consent to destroy commissions in Dawn including the Harps of Astolat, in return for aid in the Barrens.

The Barrens.t: Imperial armies conquering the Barrens faced a one-fifth penalty unless breaking the chains of Druj slaves, while Dawn weighed mandates and eternal offers to strengthen its campaign there.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: the Synod's messenger Osran recalled seeing memorial stones when his striding passed through Weirwater in his youth.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj armies were described as trapped in Zenith facing annihilation, prompting Dawn to see the moment to strike.

Time and time again.d: Ruined roads have crippled army movement between Braydon's Jasse, Serra Briante and Serra Damata, and fortifications now defend only their own region. Raiders cut Damatian Cliffs output by 7 wains and the Great Mine of Briante by 6. The Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills and the Mistress of the Dust Parador lost their top two ministry ranks. The options set out were: Senate-funded mercenaries at 10 thrones a season; a repair folly costing 70 white granite, 50 weirwood and 240 crowns over nine months; Faraden Kamkrag towers part-funded by the Bataguin; and help from Commonwealth engineers working with an Imperial army. Two Sentinel Gate conjunctions targeted Jotun bands led by Jarl Thraggan and Venator.

Jotun.t: Some forty thousand Jotun arrived after the Winter Solstice, hold Braydon's Jasse and are pushing into the Jade Range, where bands under Jarl Thraggan and the herald Venator threaten mining families and Dawnish yeofolk.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn of Kahraman face lost mine and quarry output, weakened ministries and feuding families, though the proposed Kamkrag would add two ingots a season to every Freeborn mine in the territory.

The League.t: League mercenaries could be hired by the Senate to guard Kahraman's caravans, and League military units would gain a lucrative Kahraman Caravan Guards adventure if the Senate paid for it.

Time and time again.o: Naomi of Virtue's Rest delivered the Senate's requested appraisal of how to restore Kahraman's roads and bridges, which the Jotun had sabotaged in 384YE. She set out the economic damage, short-term and long-term remedies, and foreign offers of help, while two Jotun bands threatened traders in the Jade Range.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: The Jotun invaded and now control Braydon's Jasse, so road repairs can be started but not finished until they are driven out, and Fort Braydon's protection no longer reaches neighbouring regions.

Kahraman/Jade Range.t: The Dust Parador stands here and the Jotun are advancing on it, while two Sentinel Gate conjunctions sent heroes against Jarl Thraggan's band near the Liscano family and against Venator on the Sylvan Track.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: The Great Mine of Briante loses 6 wains of mithril a season to raiders, and armies can no longer move freely between Serra Briante and its neighbouring regions.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: The Damatian Cliffs lose 7 wains of white granite a season to raids, and the ruined roads cut Serra Damata off from Serra Briante for armies and fortification support.

Kahraman.t: The territory's sabotaged roads, raided caravans and reduced Bourse output are the subject of the appraisal, which offers costed plans to repair the roads and build Faraden-style Kamkrag watchtowers across the territory.

Madruga.t: Kahraman's caravans are now forced to detour south-east through Madruga, where orc raiders prey on them, and the Commonwealth Embassy there has offered the Baumeister engineers to help rebuild the roads.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the Towers of Anduz that protect merchants visiting Segura are noted as having been inspired by Faraden Kamkrag.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: mithril and white granite caravans can no longer take their old direct routes to Tassato.

Tired of sleeping.d: Following Skywise Gralka's mandate, captains from every nation reached Kantor, Issyk and Maykop and found the former orc slaves already waiting, guided by dreams of ancestral voices. Several thousand Tamazi, a single extended family who honour ancestor bones and dragonbone, were settling in Skarsind, many joining the Imperial Orcs. Some practise secret ancestral magic, and their bonecarvers hold rituals but have not yet joined the nation. Hundreds wanted to attend the College of Warcasting, which would need a Senate-commissioned expansion. Their beliefs about the Howling Abyss may concern the Synod. Imperial fleets trading with Kantor or Issyk faced a 3 rank penalty. Talk also turned to a 60th anniversary festival and Varushkan amends.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: one Dawnish captain joined the rescue, a Dawnish sailor's joke spread through the fleet, and a few human former slaves may settle in Dawn.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Axou feared freed orcs might spy for the Druj, whom they mostly fight, and the Druj are named among those who once enslaved defeated enemies.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Axou feared freed orcs might serve the Grendel, and orcs once subject to the Grendel are contrasted with the Tamazi.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: six Highborn captains are listed among those who sailed to Axos.

Imperial Orcs.t: Their mandate brought several thousand Tamazi to Skarsind, many of whom joined the nation. It also raised questions about expanding the College of Warcasting, how the Assembly should approach Tamazi beliefs, and how to mark the nation's 60th anniversary at the Autumn Equinox.

Navarr.t: Navarri captains made a particularly strong showing in the voyage to Axos, with around eighteen listed among those who carried refugees away.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn captains made up the largest contingent of the rescue fleets, and many of the human former slaves are expected to make new lives on the Brass Coast.

The League.t: League captains joined the voyage, most of the human former slaves are expected to settle in the League, and Sarvos ox-cart vendors profited from the orcs' overland journey.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: three Marcher captains took part, and Marcher farms are named among those once worked by orc slaves.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are named among the antecedents of the Imperial Orcs who enslaved defeated enemies in wars with Varushka.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: five Urizen captains took part, Urizen is noted to have kept slaves, and the Ambassador to Axos is Tarquinius of Urizen.

Varushka.t: A Varushkan statement calling for orc remains to be returned to Skarsind prompted debate over the dangers of disturbing graves. It also raised the suggestion that resource-rich Varushka might instead make amends by funding the Illarawm ossuary or another sept project.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: ten Wintermark captains took part, a few human former slaves may settle there, and its farms are named among those once worked by orc slaves.

Tired of sleeping.o: Answering the Imperial Orc call, nearly 120 Imperial fleet captains sailed to Axos and brought away every orc who wished to leave, along with a few human former slaves. The freed orcs, who call themselves the Tamazi, began settling in Skarsind, while the angered Axou imposed a chilly reception on Imperial trade.

Skarsind/Estermark.t: Several hundred Tamazi petitioned to attend the College of Warcasting in Estermark, which would need a likely Senate-backed expansion costing 12 wains of weirwood and 24 crowns over three months. In return, Tamazi artisans would supply warcaster items to the Preceptor.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the human former slaves were keen to reach the Bay of Catazar on the voyage from Axos.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Commonwealth captains who came to visit the Empire were left well placed to help evacuate Feroz should the call come.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the former soldiers and gladiators of Mareave are contrasted with the Tamazi.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the septs of Ossium are contrasted with the Tamazi, who are far less resistant to joining the Imperial Orcs.

Sarvos.t: Ox-cart vendors in Sarvos did a roaring trade in the month after the first Tamazi arrived, carrying them on their overland trek.

Skarsind.t: Several thousand Tamazi were settling across Skarsind, many in Gildenheim, offered sanctuary there by Imperial Orc reavers and preachers. The territory was also suggested as the resting place for repatriated orc remains, possibly in the Illarawm's proposed ossuary.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: caravans heading towards Temeschwar were swollen with orcs on their way to Skarsind.

To curb those raging appetites.d: Lord Rahab imposed draconian Grendel law on Feroz: higher taxes, bans on bearing arms and practising magic, class-based punishment, and enslavement in the salt mines, sometimes of whole families. The treaty lets Freeborn in Afarjasse and Morajasse leave with their possessions until Spring 384YE, but those in Fontargenta, Oranseri and parts of the Cazar Straits face enslavement if they try. The assembly could urge resistance, flight or cooperation. The flight mandate was enacted, opening a chance next season for fleets to smuggle trapped citizens out by sea. Several Imperial titles tied to Feroz were lost, and Freeborn with holdings there could relocate them.

Grendel.t: Lord Rahab and his stone born enforcers are imposing Grendel rule on Feroz with an eye to profit, but the enacted flight mandate will drain the population he hoped to tax and weaken him politically and economically.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn assembly chose to urge their people to flee Feroz rather than resist or cooperate, a bitter blow to Freeborn Pride, while the nation lost several titles tied to the territory and can now support only three armies.

To curb those raging appetites.o: After the Senate ceded Feroz to the Grendel by treaty, the Freeborn faced harsh orc rule under Governor Lord Rahab, and the Brass Coast assembly weighed three competing mandates on how the Freeborn of Feroz should respond. Finna i Fijadoz i Guerra enacted the mandate urging them to abandon the territory.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: The Grendel have moved soldiers into Afarjasse, whose Freeborn may leave for Madruga or Segura with their possessions until Spring 384YE, though businesses and farms must be left behind.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Freeborn in parts of the Cazar Straits are not covered by the treaty's free movement and risk enslavement if they leave, but the open coastline offers a chance for fleets to smuggle them out.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: The Freeborn of Fontargenta are barred by Rahab's soldiers from leaving and must look to a sea rescue by Freeborn fleets to escape.

Feroz/Morajasse.t: Grendel soldiers have moved into Morajasse, whose Freeborn may still leave under the treaty, and the Spice Gardens there are now in Grendel hands, ending benefits for their Imperial keeper.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Freeborn in Oranseri are trapped under threat of enslavement, and the Scorrero Nets Bourse seat and the Celesti Lighthouse title will only return if the Empire retakes the region.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the lost Broken Shore Bounty Bourse seat honoured the corsairs who kept the Bay of Catazar safe.

Feroz.t: Now under Grendel rule, Feroz faces harsh laws and enslavement, and its Freeborn were urged to abandon it; Imperial titles tied to its spice gardens, lighthouse, ilium and temple have lapsed or lost their ministries.

Madruga.t: Madruga is a destination for Freeborn fleeing Feroz, where refugees with kin will be welcomed; the civil service expects disruption followed by increased taxation from new businesses, farms and fleets.

Segura.t: Segura is set to receive Freeborn refugees from Feroz, and the civil service expects that once the disruption settles new businesses, farms and fleets will raise its taxation.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is noted as the other territory under Grendel occupation, discussed in a separate Wind.

To fight aloud.d: Over half an army's worth of Urizeni military captains swept the mountains with the help of local spires and citadels. Most Disciples made a final stand and were overwhelmed, and several hallowed items were recovered. Severus was captured and brought to Anvil for trial, having agreed to face an inquisition only from the raising priest. Some fugitives were turned away by the Silver Flame or handed over by Tsark, while a few escaped. The Assembly's recognition of the reforged Damakhan's Wisdom drew interest from Leviathan and the Thrice-Cursed Court. Three Sentinel Gate conjunctions were also identified, each offering a chance to intercept fleeing Disciples.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is named as perhaps the only nation where Heralds of the Eternals are seen more often than in Urizen.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are recalled as having once tried to destroy the sword scholars at the Fall of the Four Winds, and the fleeing Ten Echoes coven may be heading for Druj-held Sarangrave.

Grendel.t: The Temple of the Stinging Blade fled south to seek Grendel protection, hoping to trade a powerful blade-oil schema for safe passage. Another group tried to slip into Grendel-held Mareave.

The League.t: Refugees from the Temple of the Inviolate Spirit were turned away by the Silver Flame in League-claimed Spiral and captured. A dozen Wayfarer's Answer Disciples are believed to be hiding somewhere in Spiral.

Urizen.t: Urizen's captains, sentinels and citadels destroyed the Disciples of Sulemaine as an organised group and captured Severus for trial at Anvil. The reforged Damakhan's Wisdom now raises the question of how the nation will preserve Damakhan's legacy.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Kindra Surefoot of Wintermark is among those thanked for helping reforge Damakhan's Wisdom.

To fight aloud.o: In Winter 387YE, after Senate, Conclave and Synod alike condemned them, Urizeni captains crushed the Disciples of Sulemaine across Redoubt, Morrow and Zenith, capturing their leader Severus of the Blinding Sun and scattering the survivors.

Redoubt/Limus.t: Limus was home to the Temple of the Stinging Blade, famed for its blade oils, whose members fled towards the Grendel with a schema to barter for safe passage.

Spiral/Cinion.t: Refugees from the Temple of the Inviolate Spirit sought shelter with the Silver Flame in Cinion, but were turned away and promptly captured.

Zenith/Lustri.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ten Echoes, a small coven from Lustri, escaped northwards, possibly towards the Sarangrave.

Mareave.t: A group of Disciples was trying to cross from Spiral into the rocky hills of Mareave, and an opportunity arose for the Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path to intercept them there via the Sentinel Gate.

Morrow.t: Captains swept Morrow for Disciple temples. A band carrying a rare dose of true liao was reported heading for Highwatch, possibly intending to create a permanent aura of Purity, and the Polemarch of Highwatch was asked to stop them.

Redoubt.t: The purge began in Redoubt. The Temple of the Stinging Blade fled south from there towards the Grendel, offering the Champion of Loyalty a chance to intercept them.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ten Echoes coven from Lustri fled north, apparently heading for the Sarangrave or beyond.

Spiral.t: The Silver Flame in Spiral turned away fleeing Disciples, who were then captured. A dozen Wayfarer's Answer members may be hiding in Spiral, and another group tried to cross from Spiral into Mareave.

Zenith.t: Zenith was the last territory swept by the Urizeni captains, who visited known temples and followed leads from local spires to destroy the Disciples there.

To hold death's hand in mine.d: With no Imperial army left in Therunin, the Navarr assembly told those who could not fight to flee to Reikos, the Barrens and northern Urizen. Druj hosts poured from Eastring and East Ashes and took the Lower and Upper Tarn Valley and Peakedge Song. The Senate's new Apothecaries' Guild could not use its antidote on the poisoned Lower Tarn and spent its ten thrones aiding refugees and defenders instead. Thornsong House vanished behind a warding fog. Ossegrahn's bramble wall saved Peakedge Stead and the Houses of Healing for now, but it will fail without action by the Conclave and Senate. Using goetic magic and treasures taken from Return, the Tainted Basilisk woke the vallorn of Tharunind, which now spreads miasma towards neighbouring lands.

Dawn.t: Dawn was among the nations that opened their doors to Therunin's refugees. Its Barrens face Druj tortured souls advancing on Hope's Rest, and Navarr fear the waking vallorn may eventually threaten Dawnish people.

Druj.t: The Druj conquered all of Therunin except Sweetglades and Greenheart, slaughtering or enslaving those in their path. They were halted only at Peakedge Stead, where a force waits outside Ossegrahn's failing hedge, and the Tainted Basilisk roused the vallorn of Tharunind.

Highguard.t: The Highborn assembly asked the chapters of Reikos to shelter Navarr and Great Forest Orc refugees, and many from Peakedge Stead took sanctuary in High Chalcis. Highborn support had helped find the antidote to the Lower Tarn poison.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun's continued hold on Liathaven, which they have renamed Ashvale, is cited as the reason Therunin's people doubt they will ever return.

Navarr.t: The Navarr lost Therunin, and with it their capacity to support armies fell from six to five. Their assemblies urged evacuation, and almost all stridings and many steadings fled while those who stayed died buying time. Peakedge Stead, the Houses of Healing and Thornsong House now stand alone in enemy hands.

Urizen.t: Northern Urizen took in Navarr refugees, but vallorn miasma has appeared in the foothills of Peregro and Altis, and a vallornspawn horde threatens the Spire of the Canticle. A Spring pulse also swept along the trods of Redoubt and Zenith.

Varushka.t: The undying remnants of Varushka's Iron Helms ravaged the Druj in Eastring, but their bound winter spirits overwhelmed what remained of the soldiers. The Navarr assembly honoured Alderai the Fair and the Iron Helms for their sacrifice.

To hold death's hand in mine.o: After the Imperial armies withdrew west, the Druj overran Therunin in the winter of 386YE, conquering all but the vallorn regions while the Navarr assemblies urged the people to flee. Only Peakedge Stead held, behind a temporary hedge raised by Ossegrahn, and the Tainted Basilisk roused the vallorn of Tharunind.

Morrow/Altis.t: Pools of vallorn miasma have appeared in Altis's northern foothills, and a vallornspawn horde is moving through the valleys towards the Spire of the Canticle. The Archmage of Winter is charged with stopping it.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Pools of vallorn miasma, bringing vallornspawn and ettercaps, have been reported in Peregro's northern foothills.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: Refugees from the Lower Tarn Valley fled north to the welcoming Eaves of Peytaht and the weirwood groves of the Great Forest Orcs.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: A Druj band escorting tortured souls, corrupted fallen Navarr, is advancing on the Shrine of Hope. The High Exorcist is charged with exorcising them.

Therunin/East Ashes.t: Druj forces massed here before spilling west in uncountable thousands to overrun the Tarn Valley.

Therunin/Eastring.t: The undead Iron Helms tore into the Druj here before their hunger turned indiscriminate. Imperial forces are called to destroy a Druj miasma pillar being raised in the region.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: Greenheart escaped Druj conquest, but abominations stir as the vallorn wakes and its steadings are under siege. Prognosticators expect most of them to be overrun by the Summer Solstice.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The poisoned valley was evacuated and then fell swiftly to the Druj. This ended the Apothecaries' Guild's plan to cleanse it with the new antidote until the Druj are driven out.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Peakedge Song fell despite the Towerjacks' fortifications. Peakedge Stead and the Houses of Healing survive only behind Ossegrahn's temporary bramble wall, and Thornsong House is hidden in warding fog, while the vallorn's expansion is now focused here.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: Sweetglades escaped Druj conquest, but its steadings are besieged as the vallorn wakes. The Lord of Thorns gathers vallornspawn there, and the Champion of Vigilance is charged with slaying it.

Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley.t: Defenders armed with Bloodharrow Philtre and aided by healers bought only hours before the Druj rolled over them. The region now lies in the path of the expanding vallorn.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: named by the Navarr assembly as one of the places to which the young, old and weak might be guided to safety.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as a place where the Druj miasma is deeply rooted in the soil.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: named by the Navarr assembly as one of the places to which the young, old and weak might be guided to safety.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: held up as a warning, since years after similar assurances it remains under Jotun control and has been renamed Ashvale.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: named by the Navarr assembly as one of the places to which the young, old and weak might be guided to safety.

Morrow.t: Vallorn miasma has been spotted in Morrow's northern foothills, and a horde led by heralds of Yaw'nagrah marches on the Spire of the Canticle. Its chaos-fruit forests will yield two extra fruit.

Redoubt.t: The pulse of Spring magic from the rousing vallorn struck along Redoubt's trods, and Redoubt's senator had raised the motion creating the Apothecaries' Guild. Therunin's defences had already weakened when the League engineers left for Redoubt.

Reikos.t: Reikos became a key refuge, with chapters opening their doors and many from Peakedge Stead fleeing to High Chalcis. The Druj impaled stragglers along the road there, and its chaos-fruit forests gain two extra fruit from the Spring pulse.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as a place where the Druj miasma is deeply rooted in the soil.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as a place where the Druj miasma is deeply rooted in the soil.

The Barrens.t: The Imperial armies and the Great Forest Orcs retreated here, and Therunin refugees found welcome among the Great Forest Orcs. Druj with tortured souls now push into Hope's Rest, while its chaos-fruit forests gain two extra fruit.

Therunin.t: Therunin fell entirely to the Druj except the vallorn regions, and most of its people fled or died. Only Peakedge Stead, the Houses of Healing and the fog-warded Thornsong House remain, while the awakened vallorn of Tharunind begins to spread.

Zenith.t: The surge of Spring magic from Therunin swept along Zenith's trods, and its chaos-fruit forests will produce two additional fruit.

To loose the fateful lightning.d: Fleets based on the Bay (Tassato, Sarvos, the Brass Coast, Highguard and Urizen) again suffered a penalty when trading abroad. The Salt Lords were said to be offering bounties for Imperial ships after the raids on Dubhtraig and Mareave, and would negotiate only with Fleet Master Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra. The proposed attack would scale with the strength committed. It could end the trade penalty for a year or more, bring raids on Shayeel and Ayereed, cripple Grendel resupply, and ultimately strike Gainmeachdubh and the Tower of Tempest Jade in Raineach. Every participating fleet would be damaged for six months and earn only about half its usual production.

Grendel.t: Grendel pirates and privateers kept raiding Imperial shipping and the Salt Lords reportedly offered bounties on Imperial vessels. They faced a possible bay-wide counterattack that could sink their ships, disrupt their trade and resupply, and raid their holdings and their Spring rites to Siakha.

Highguard.t: Highborn fleets on the Bay faced a production penalty when trading abroad and could join the attack on the pirates. A Highborn captain also appears in the opening fiction.

The Brass Coast.t: With the Grendel armada focused on invading Feroz, the Freeborn corsairs were cast as the coordinators of the proposed counterattack. Their trading fleets still suffered the penalty while the pirate threat lasted.

The League.t: Fleets from Tassato and Sarvos suffered the trade penalty from Grendel raiding, and League captains could join the attack to lift it.

Urizen.t: Urizen's fleets were among those penalised when trading across the Bay and could take part in the Dominate the Bay attack.

To loose the fateful lightning.o: In Spring 383YE Grendel pirates kept raiding Imperial shipping on the Bay of Catazar. Imperial fleet captains, coordinated by the Freeborn corsairs and the Imperial Fleet Master, were offered a one-season chance to mount a bay-wide attack, Dominate the Bay, against the overconfident pirates.

Ayereed/Gainmeachdubh.t: If 40,000 strength was committed, Imperial privateers would raid into and near the larger Salt Lord settlements of Gainmeachdubh.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: the earlier lightning raid on Beoraidh is contrasted with this open, bay-wide campaign.

Ayereed.t: If at least 20,000 strength was committed, Imperial fleets would raid Grendel-dominated coastal settlements here and in Shayeel, seizing mithril and ilium for the Fleet Master.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Bay was the scene of the Grendel pirate raids and of the proposed fighting, which would range across its whole length. Success could lift the trade penalty on Imperial shipping or break the Grendel's claim to mastery of it.

Feroz.t: The Grendel armada was focused on its invasion of Feroz, and the news from there was bleak, with many Freeborn fearing for kin on the eastern coast.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the recent Imperial raids on Mareave were said to have enraged the Salt Lords.

Raineach.t: At the highest level of success the campaign would end in a raid on the Grendel's grand Spring festival at the Tower of Tempest Jade, damaging but not destroying the temple.

Sarvos.t: Fleets based in Sarvos suffered the trade penalty, and pirates were said to strike at will at merchant ships between Sarvos and Veroigne.

Shayeel.t: If at least 20,000 strength was committed, Imperial fleets would raid Grendel-dominated coastal settlements here, adding to the mithril and ilium bounty.

Tassato.t: Fleets based in Tassato faced a production penalty if they traded abroad while the pirates went unchecked.

Veroigne.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction notes pirates attacking merchant ships between Sarvos and Veroigne.

To ride the earth.d: Six Imperial armies were pressing into Zenith. Urizeni volunteers answering the Assembly's call added a thousand to the Citadel Guard's strength. Because Cardinal of Loyalty Veikko Bondforger rallied the faithful, Urizen's spires and temples committed supplies, so the Guard faces no supply problems until the end of Summer 385YE, provided no region of Redoubt or Morrow is lost. The General Assembly could tithe liao from every congregation to negate the Druj miasma in Zenith for a season and make Imperial armies there unbreakable. Following Clytemnestra's unanimously upheld statement, the Urizen Assembly may enact a mandate disbanding the Citadel Guard while any part of Zenith remains in Druj hands.

Dawn.t: Dawnish armies were fighting alongside Urizen and Highguard in Zenith and would benefit from the proposed General Assembly mandate. Urizeni also feared armies might be called north to conquer new territories for Dawn.

Druj.t: The Druj face six Imperial armies in Zenith. If the General Assembly mandate passes, their miasma would have no effect there for a season, and Imperial armies fighting them would become unbreakable.

Grendel.t: Salt Lord Kaliact's détente had kept the Citadel Guard supplied, but Urizen no longer needs that deal for the coming year. This may weaken the Salt Lord's leverage in further negotiations with the Empire.

Highguard.t: The Highborn crusade continued in Zenith: the Valiant Pegasus withdrew to Bastion to resupply, while the Granite Pillar and Seventh Wave kept attacking and inspired those who witnessed them.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni feared Imperial armies might be called west to face the Jotun before Zenith was freed.

Urizen.t: Loyalty-driven volunteers and supplies strengthened the Citadel Guard and secured its supply for a year. Meanwhile, Clytemnestra's unanimous statement gave the Urizen Assembly the option of disbanding the Guard if the Empire abandons Zenith.

Varushka.t: The proposed General Assembly mandate would only take its liao tithe from Varushka, and only make Varushkan armies unbreakable, if it passed with a greater majority. Urizeni also feared armies being diverted to conquests for Varushka.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark armies had come to Zenith to aid Urizen and Highguard and would gain the proposed mandate's protection against the miasma.

To ride the earth.o: In Summer 384YE the Imperial campaign to free Zenith from the Druj gained momentum, and Urizen's Loyalty-driven support for the Citadel Guard secured its supply for a year. Two Synod opportunities followed: a General Assembly mandate to aid armies in Zenith, and a Urizen Assembly mandate that could disband the Citadel Guard.

Zenith/Lustri.t: Mentioned in passing: Clytemnestra's statement asks whether the Senate might leave the spires of Lustri in Druj hands.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Mentioned in passing: named among the Zenith regions Urizeni fear the Senate might leave under Druj control.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Mentioned in passing: its spires are cited in Clytemnestra's warning against abandoning Zenith to the Druj.

Bastion.t: The Highborn army the Valiant Pegasus pulled back to Bastion to resupply before continuing the crusade.

Morrow.t: The Citadel Guard's year of secure supply depends on no region of Morrow being lost.

Redoubt.t: The Citadel Guard's guaranteed supply until the end of Summer 385YE depends on no region of Redoubt being lost.

Spiral.t: Grendel-held Spiral's détente with the Empire had kept the Citadel Guard supplied, but that deal ends at the Summer Solstice and Urizen no longer needs it for the coming year.

Zenith.t: Six Imperial armies were pushing the Druj back in Zenith. A proposed mandate could negate the miasma there for a season and make Imperial armies unbreakable while fighting in the territory.

To ruin.d: The Grendel landed three armies at Elos with Asavean support, took the port, then spread across Naris and came seven-tenths of the way to taking Siluri. They plundered crystal mana and valuables and seized the Great Harbour and the Tower of Light and Shadow. The Fist of the Mountains arrived unexpectedly and slowed the invaders, letting most Urizen and their libraries escape. It then fought back into Elos, where a Wintermark warrior shattered the catastrophe sphere, but the army was disbanded. A thousand freed Winter husks now roam Naris, and Eilian Sweetwater is missing.
