The harbour, docks and tower face ruin by Winter unless the Empire answers. An equinox battle opportunity was offered.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fist's general had planned to unleash the husks in the Sarangrave, and Redoubt's people wonder whether armies can be spared from the eastern front against the Druj.

Grendel.t: The Grendel took Elos, Naris, the Great Harbour and the Tower of Light and Shadow, looting great wealth, but lost hundreds of mercenaries and their stolen sphere. Their Moridun forces are now quarrelling over the blame.

Highguard.t: The Grendel meant to stop Highguard or Urizen raising navies at Elos, and their sphere might have threatened the Necropolis just across the Couros before it was shattered.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the mountains of Skarsind are named among the places where the Fist of the Mountains learned to fight.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fist's Winter dead are recalled as having fought in Reinos.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fist had liberated Madruga and fought in the Quiet Grasses before marching to Redoubt.

The League.t: Tassatan dead walk among the freed husks, and their families seek the return of their burial jewellery. A Grendel maistir hopes League companies will help her defect and settle in Sarvos.

Urizen.t: Urizen lost Elos, Naris and the Tower of Light and Shadow and is close to losing Siluri, and suffered a costly raid. Most of its people and spire libraries were saved by Wintermark's sacrifice.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's eldest army, the Fist of the Mountains, was destroyed saving Elos from devastation. Its founding relic, Pinnacle, was looted by the Grendel and can be recovered on the battlefield.

To ruin.o: In Autumn 387YE a Grendel armada of four navies and five Asavean battleships seized Elos and all of Naris in Redoubt. The Fist of the Mountains was destroyed stopping them from using a stolen tempest jade sphere to devastate the harbour.

Madruga/Quiet Grasses.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fist's Winter dead are recalled as having fought in the Quiet Grasses.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Naris fell entirely to the Grendel, with Elos, its harbour and the Tower of Light and Shadow. A thousand Winter husks now roam the region, and Grendel Sky ritualists seek the hidden tower.

Redoubt/Optarion.t: Mentioned in passing: Optarion is not named on the page; it is touched only by the wider Grendel assault on Redoubt.

Redoubt/Siluri.t: The Grendel are seven-tenths of the way to conquering Siluri and threaten its Academy of Arms, though the shrine to Adelmar the Lion is still in Imperial hands.

Redoubt/Tomari.t: Mentioned in passing: the armada swept around Tomari's headlands on its way to Elos.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Grendel intended the destruction of Elos to show that they alone own the Bay, and the missing Eilian Sweetwater may be stranded on a rock somewhere in its waters.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the would-be defector Muirgheal Cuindlis once had links to Feroz under Governor Rahab's occupation.

Hahnmark.t: The lost Fist trained in Hahnmark's mountains, and its relic Pinnacle came from there by tradition. Survivors hope to return it to the summit of the Fingers.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: songs of the fallen Fist of the Mountains will be sung in Kallavesa.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fist had liberated Madruga before its long march, and the Grendel's earlier attack on Elos came on their way from Madruga.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: news of a Grendel advance in Mareave adds to the fear in Redoubt.

Necropolis.t: The Fist marched through under disapproving eyes, and the Grendel sphere might have reached the Necropolis had it been set off.

Raineach.t: Mentioned in passing: the tempest jade sphere was taken from the Temple of Tempest Jade in Raineach.

Redoubt.t: Grendel and Asavean forces took Naris, including Elos, the Great Harbour and the Tower of Light and Shadow, and press on Siluri. These sites face ruin by Winter unless the Empire answers.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fist and its Winter dead are recalled as having fought in Reinos.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fist's general had planned to unleash the Winter husks in the Sarangrave.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fist marched through Sarvos, a raid there is reported, and the defector Cuindlis hopes to settle in the city.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Fist learned mountain fighting in Sermersuaq, where its fall will be sung.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's mountains are named among the Fist's old battlegrounds.

Tassato.t: Tassato's dead, raised by the Fist's ritual, still carry their burial finery. A merchant prince will reward those who recover it from the husks.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: unliving horrors still linger in parts of Zenith from an earlier use of the ritual, and former Zenith refugees fear a repeat.

To see what you sell.d: A Prosperity mandate prompted a proposal to restore the Elos docks in Redoubt: 35 wains of weirwood, 35 of white granite and 140 crowns over six months, to be commissioned by the end of 384YE. The docks could later be cheaply expanded into a shipyard, possibly hidden from the Grendel. The Sand Fishers studied in Holberg, trained with House Remys, at Skarsind's School of Warcasting, as scriveners and on the Navarr trods. They resolved to log Misericorde and Utterlund once they had bought the materials themselves. The Freeborn were urged to create a Prosperity festival by Spring 385YE. A tomb apparently belonging to the forgotten exemplar Badir i Durr i Riqueza was found near Rojota.

Dawn.t: House Remys offered to teach magic to the Sand Fishers, and the young winter-adept White Breath travelled alone to Dawn to study necromancy under Enchantress Claudia Remys.

Druj.t: The Sand Fishers studied and armed themselves to resist the Druj, but declined to spy on them because they refused to endure the miasma again; Urizeni refugees from the Druj invasion of Zenith were swelling Redoubt.

Grendel.t: The Elos docks would be commercial and could not legitimately be called a breach of the peace treaty, but the Grendel would recognise the threat. Any later shipyard there could be veiled from Grendel spies by the Penumbral Watcher.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs' offer to teach battle magic was taken up, cautiously, by more than thirty Sand Fishers. They came to Skarsind's School of Warcasting despite their wariness of other orc tribes.

Jotun.t: Three Lasambrian Jotun armies were advancing on Rojota and threatening all of Gambit, though they were thought unlikely to desecrate the newly found tomb.

Navarr.t: In response to the Navarr Assembly's invitation, more than a dozen Sand Fishers began walking the trods. They stayed at Navarr wayhouses and insisted on working for their board.

The Brass Coast.t: A mandate stirred the Freeborn to found a new festival honouring Zemress and Prosperity, ideally at the Spring Equinox of 385YE. A proposal was also made to mark Broken Wheel participants with white headscarves. A handful of Sand Fishers apprenticed as scriveners, and a tomb of the lost exemplar Badir i Durr i Riqueza was discovered.

The League.t: The League National Assembly's list of ways to repay the Empire drew the warmest response from the Sand Fishers. It led to their plan to improve Holberg's lands and boost Senate revenue.

Urizen.t: Restoring Elos could double Redoubt's shipping capacity, reward Urizeni fleets based there and raise taxes. It might even let Urizen support a navy alongside the Citadel Guard.

To see what you sell.o: In Spring 384YE several Prosperity-driven opportunities emerged. Redoubt was offered a chance to restore the old port of Elos, the Sand Fisher orcs took up Imperial offers of learning and planned to repay the Empire, and the Freeborn began debating a new festival of Prosperity as a mysterious tomb of a forgotten exemplar was found in Gambit.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: The Sand Fishers planned to build sawmills and log Misericorde's forests to create profitable woodland preserves. They would buy the 15 wains each of mithril and weirwood at the Misericorde Market, which would take at least two years.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Utterlund's forests were included in the Sand Fishers' logging plan, which aimed to tame the woods into well-managed, profitable woodland.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: The tomb was found a day or so south-west of Rojota, in grasslands that the advancing Lasambrian Jotun might control by the end of the Spring Equinox, which made any expedition difficult.

Redoubt/Naris.t: Mentioned in passing: Naris is not named on the page, which concerns Redoubt's ports at Elos, Cargo and Visten in general.

Redoubt/Optarion.t: Mentioned in passing: Optarion is not named on the page, which concerns Redoubt's ports at Elos, Cargo and Visten in general.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Mentioned in passing: the destruction of the Apulus docks diverted shipping to Redoubt's ports.

Bay of Catazar.t: Trade in the Bay had grown greatly since the peace treaty with the Grendel, but the treaty forbade the Empire to build a shipyard on it. That made any veiled shipyard at Elos a sensitive prospect.

Holberg.t: Sand Fishers were increasingly seen attending the city's university and schools at the Senate's expense. They also planned to sell timber in Holberg to raise the territory's wealth and taxation.

Kahraman.t: Soldiers skirmishing with Lasambrian raiders discovered a buried tomb with a potent Prosperity-like aura, apparently belonging to the forgotten exemplar Badir i Durr i Riqueza.

Redoubt.t: Redoubt was offered the restoration of the old naval port of Elos, which would relieve its congested ports, increase taxation by 10 thrones a season and benefit refugees. The offer lapsed if the work was not commissioned by the end of 384YE.

Segura.t: The Zemress Islanders settled in Segura pressed for a more uplifting celebration than the Feast of the Broken Wheel, sparking the Freeborn debate over a new Prosperity festival.

Skarsind.t: More than thirty Sand Fishers arrived at the Skarsind School of Warcasting to learn battle magic so they could fight the Druj.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel conquest of Spiral sent Urizeni refugees to Redoubt and left Redoubt as Urizen's only coastline.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni refugees fleeing the Druj invasion of Zenith had settled in Redoubt.

To sleep in Kallavesa.d: During the Autumn Equinox 379YE a contingent travelled through the Sentinel Gate to the Shrine of Britta in Necropolis and removed her armour, weapons and accoutrements. In a stormcrow ceremony these were sunk in a weirwood boat in the lake where Britta was interred in 376YE. Pilgrims now travel to Wintermark instead, so from Spring 380YE the Guardian of Britta's Shrine becomes a purely ceremonial title. The dour curse on Kallavesa's marshes abated, which mystics tentatively credit to the reunion. Britta joins the few Thrones not interred in Necropolis. The Senate chose to build a major shrine in Kallavesa Marsh and a pilgrims' trail. Work on the shrine has begun, but the trail has made no progress.

Highguard.t: Highborn helped remove Britta's relics from the Necropolis shrine. With pilgrims now going to Wintermark, the Guardian of Britta's Shrine there becomes a purely ceremonial title from Spring 380YE.

Wintermark.t: The Winterfolk laid their Empress's relics to rest beside her in the lake, and the curse on Kallavesa's marshes lifted. A major shrine is now being built in Kallavesa Marsh, its sinecure expected to be appointed by the Wintermark national assembly.

To sleep in Kallavesa.o: Highborn and Winterfolk removed Empress Britta's relics from her shrine in Necropolis and sank them in the lake at Sovvengard in Kallavesa, reuniting them with her body according to Wintermark custom. The Senate then commissioned a major shrine to her and a pilgrims' trail across the marshes.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: The Senate chose to build a major shrine to Empress Britta here, and work has begun. It is intended to house pilgrims and create a congregational sinecure with liao and Synod votes.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: named as the place where Emperor Barabbas's body was lost, making him another Throne not interred in Necropolis.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Empress Giselle is noted as interred in her family tomb in Caricomare rather than in Necropolis.

Kallavesa.t: Britta's relics were sunk in the lake at Sovvengard and the curse on the marshes abated. The Senate commissioned a major shrine, now under construction, and a pilgrims' trail on which no progress has yet been made.

Necropolis.t: Britta's relics were removed from her white granite shrine, pilgrim numbers fell sharply, and its guardianship becomes purely ceremonial from Spring 380YE.

To the last syllable.d: Raids began during the Summer Solstice and grew more organised afterwards. Warnings from the Navarr, Dawnish and Vigilance assemblies saved many lives, but around two thousand citizens were slain. Freya's Garden, the Grand Conservatory of Music and the Hall of Lost Chapters were destroyed, and Therunin's trods were damaged. Every Imperial fortification lost 500 casualties and receives no resupply, except those in Dawn and Spiral and the Broch. Dawn, protected by Summer magic, lost no one. Cold Sun armies now stand in Rundhal Marsh, Valasmark, Northpines, Oakways, Livardz, Duzekani, Burnish and Woodbury. Enmity would cut off reinforcements but would not remove them. Sentinel Gate skirmishes are offered against further attacks.

Dawn.t: Under Meraud's Summer magic, Dawn's defenders were reinforced by heralds of Summer eternals and not a single Dawnish citizen was slain. Its fortifications were spared casualties, and the General of the Eastern Sky is summoned to defend Karov's Eternal Shafts of Time.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are recalled as having once besieged the Great Library and as the horror the people of Zenith have already endured.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Brass Coast's loss of Feroz to the Grendel is cited as one reason for Freeborn fury.

Highguard.t: The Highborn assembly's warning failed to reach a greater majority, but congregations heeding Vigilance turned back an attack at Sybella. The Hall of Lost Chapters at Tabernacle was still destroyed, a Cold Sun army now holds ground in Woodbury, and Bastion's senator must defend the White Tower.

Imperial Orcs.t: The orc garrison of the Will fought several days of pitched battle to drive heralds from a Day regio in Estermark. The Halls of Worth now face a threat that falls to the Weigher of Worth, Ghillihg.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: recent Jotun invasions of Bregasland and of the Brass Coast's western territories are recalled.

Navarr.t: Navarr thorns heeded their assembly and fought Cold Sun across the Empire via the trods. However, the heralds have learned to burn out trods, damaging Therunin's network and threatening Hercynia's, and Cold Sun armies stand in Northpines and Oakways.

The Brass Coast.t: Families, hakima and kohan met every incursion with overwhelming fury born of past losses. A Cold Sun army is spreading across Burnish, and the Cerevado Nets are threatened.

The League.t: League cities quickly dealt with the heralds, the largest attack falling on Holberg. Spiral alone of all Imperial territories saw no heralds at all.

The Marches.t: The well-organised Marches drove off the heralds. Orcs and humans died defending Honour's Rest in the Mournwold, and the Keeper of the Dour Fens must stop heralds claiming the Still Rock in Bregasland.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Miechernya is noted as a now Thule-controlled region beyond the Wulfric's Fall pass.

Urizen.t: All three Urizeni territories were attacked. Morrow and Zenith repelled the heralds with Day-realm and magical aid, but Redoubt's Grand Conservatory of Music was destroyed, and the Churn and the Brilliant Star are now threatened.

Varushka.t: Varushkan vales defeated the heralds with ruthless pragmatism, aided by patrols on the Iron Roads and Jaheris's servants at the Icy Crag. Cold Sun armies now stand in Livardz and Duzekani, and Veresk is in danger.

Wintermark.t: Hahnmark's beacons were lit too late to save Freya's Garden, though Kallavesa's beacons foiled the largest attack. Cold Sun armies now hold ground in Rundhal Marsh and Valasmark.

To the last syllable.o: After Urizen magicians cast Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths, Day regio across the Empire flourished, and the eternal Cold Sun sent its blue-clad heralds through them to attack Imperial landmarks and people. By the Autumn Equinox these raids had grown into eight armies of roughly three thousand each, set on destroying the Empire.

Bastion/Sybella Cross.t: An attack on Sybela was intercepted, and heralds are now moving to fortify the ruined White Tower, which would add a thousand strength to Cold Sun's push to claim the region.

Bastion/Woodbury.t: A Cold Sun army of around three thousand has coalesced in Woodbury.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: Heralds are marching on the Still Rock, a potent unaligned Day regio. Holding it would let Cold Sun bring in another army even under enmity.

Hahnmark/Bruckland.t: If the White Owl Hall falls, citizens would begin withdrawing from Bruckland towards Kalpaheim.

Hahnmark/Kronemark.t: Heralds are advancing on the White Owl Hall of the Augurs of the Opalescent Gloaming, and the Imperial Seer is charged with stopping them.

Hahnmark/Valasmark.t: A major Cold Sun army is now present in Valasmark.

Hercynia/Deer's Folly.t: A conjunction to Deer's Folly would be needed to repair Hercynia's trods if the heralds burn them out.

Hercynia/Northpines.t: A Cold Sun army is present, and heralds who killed most of the Long Day striding are heading for a crossing of the trods.

Kallavesa/Rundhal Marsh.t: A major Cold Sun army is now present in Rundhal Marsh.

Karov/Duzekani.t: A major Cold Sun army is now present in Duzekani.

Karov/Wieliczka.t: Heralds are advancing on the Eternal Shafts of Time to slaughter the miners and seize their mithril.

Karsk/Nitrost.t: The vale of Veresk faces three bands of heralds, and a Sentinel Gate opens to Gulgisaz to intercept one of them.

Miaren/Oakways.t: A major Cold Sun army is now present in Oakways.

Miekarova/Miechernya.t: Mentioned in passing: named as the Thule-controlled region reached through the Wulfric's Fall pass.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Heralds are advancing on the Churn, a volatile geyser whose eruption would damage the Churnspire and the surrounding land.

Redoubt/Tomari.t: Heralds drawn by its Day affinity threaten the Brilliant Star mine, its workers and its mithril.

Reikos/Riverwatch.t: Mentioned in passing: not named on the page, and linked only through the attacks on Reikos.

Segura/Burnish.t: A Cold Sun army is slowly spreading across Burnish.

Segura/Lucksprings.t: Heralds are marching on the Cerevado Nets to slaughter the workers and claim the gathered ilium.

Skarsind/Estermark.t: Heralds fortified a hidden Day regio near Wulfric's Fall until the Will's garrison drove them back after days of battle; a watch now guards the regio.

Skarsind/Gildermark.t: Heralds are climbing towards the Halls of Worth above Gildenheim, threatening every orc trapped there.

Volodmartz/Livardz.t: A major Cold Sun army is now present in Livardz.

Zenith/Lustri.t: The defeated heralds were driven into the forests of Lustri and did not return.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Nightbound Proceris anchors the Dripping Echoes of the Fen ward that protected Zenith's defenders.

Astolat.t: The Prime Harp was targeted at the Solstice, but afterwards Meraud's golden lions fought beside Astolat's defenders while the Golden Sun celebrated there on furlough.

Bastion.t: An attack on Sybela and its Physician's Hall was intercepted with only token damage. A Cold Sun army has since appeared in Woodbury and is pushing towards the White Tower.

Bregasland.t: Still recovering from the Jotun invasion, Bregasland's beaters and its magical wards held off the heralds. A force is now moving to claim the Still Rock regio in Gravenmarch.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: its Broch is exempt from the fortification losses because it lies outside Imperial territory.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: its loss to the Grendel is cited as fuelling Freeborn anger.

Hahnmark.t: Heralds destroyed Freya's Garden before the halls could rally. A Cold Sun army now stands in Valasmark, and the White Owl Hall in Kronemark is threatened.

Hercynia.t: A Cold Sun army is present in Northpines and is moving to burn out Hercynia's trods. If it succeeds, repairs will require a conjunction to Deer's Folly.

Holberg.t: The Pavilion on Looking Glass Lake was attacked at the Solstice, and Holberg suffered the largest League attack, which was dealt with by its fortification and watch.

Kahraman.t: A Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae helped the Freeborn defend the labour camps building roads and kamkrag, so no serious damage was done.

Kallavesa.t: After the Raven Seers of Ishal were attacked, a Suaq hero helped light the beacons in time to foil a second attack against Ishal. A Cold Sun army now holds ground in Rundhal Marsh.

Karov.t: A Cold Sun army stands in Duzekani, and heralds are marching on the Eternal Shafts of Time in Wieliczka.

Karsk.t: The weary defenders of Veresk face three bands of heralds and will fall unless the Empire intercepts one of them.

Madruga.t: Freeborn families crushed the heralds so swiftly that the armies stationed in Madruga barely had time to respond.

Miaren.t: The Pool of Silver Clouds was attacked at the Solstice, and a Cold Sun army now stands in Oakways.

Miekarova.t: The assault on the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun became a siege, broken by the college's battle-magicians, the Gremani family and Jaheris's elfin warlocks before Grimhold's defenders arrived.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold's only serious trouble came from other heralds, a matter left for another time.

Morrow.t: A crystal ward and the prismatic lizard-sentinels of the Celestial Library destroyed the heralds at Canterspire. Heralds now threaten the Churn geyser in Peregro.

Mournwold.t: Orcs and Marchers, with the beaters and the garrison of Farstrider's Watch, stopped a major attack on Honour's Rest, though many defenders died.

Redoubt.t: The Grand Conservatory of Music was destroyed, and the Tower of Light and Shadow was attacked at the Solstice. The Brilliant Star mine in Tomari is now threatened.

Reikos.t: The Grey Watch Grasses were attacked at the Solstice, and the Hall of Lost Chapters at Tabernacle was destroyed, with the town badly damaged.

Sarvos.t: The Wellspring of Jade was attacked at the Solstice. Like other League cities, Sarvos dealt quickly with the heralds.

Segura.t: A Cold Sun army is slowly spreading across Burnish, and heralds are advancing on the Cerevado Nets in Lucksprings.

Semmerholm.t: Not named individually, but as Dawnish land it shared in the Summer-aided defence in which no Dawnish citizen died.

Skarsind.t: Orc defenders fought for days to dislodge heralds fortifying a Day regio in Estermark. Heralds are now climbing towards the Halls of Worth in Gildermark.

Spiral.t: Alone of all Imperial territories, Spiral reported no heralds, and its two fortifications were spared casualties.

Tassato.t: The Blood Red River Museum was attacked during the Solstice, though League cities dealt quickly with the heralds.

The Barrens.t: Jaheris sent giant spiders, warlocks and goblin slingers from the ruins of the Towers of the Dawn to help households protect the new settlers.

The Semmerlak.t: Rhianos sent trident-wielding tritons to fight Cold Sun's heralds on the shores of the Semmerlak.

Therunin.t: Navarr and the Holt of the Oak saved Peakedge Stead, but its trods were damaged. They will slowly deteriorate unless repaired at a vallorn-quality regio.

Volodmartz.t: A Cold Sun army of around three thousand has appeared in Livardz.

Weirwater.t: The resting Eastern Sky went mana hunting here, and trumpets at Spiral Castle summoned its general to Karov.

Zenith.t: Defended by the Dripping Echoes ward, koboldi and heralds of Estavus, Zenith's furious sentinels drove the heralds into the marshes and forests of Lustri, and they did not return.

Tomb of the Courageous.d: Ahraz's well-kept tomb in the Necropolis already draws hundreds of pilgrims, especially Freeborn and Imperial Orcs. One mandate would stress his part in freeing the orcs and let the Imperial Orcs support a fourth army or navy. The other would stress following one's own heart and let the Brass Coast support a fourth. If consecrated, a steward of the dead would come to Anvil at the Autumn Equinox to collect items of worth from Freeborn and orcs for the tomb, as the Highborn Assembly had requested. Firebrands and scriveners each want any statue in Kahraman to honour their side of Ahraz. Some still call him a heretic, and proof of this after consecration would cause a spiritual crisis.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: named as the foe the orcs are fighting in Mareave, whose spirits the orc-focused mandate would lift.

Highguard.t: Ahraz's tomb lies in the Highborn Necropolis, where experienced caretakers could handle more pilgrims, and the Highborn Assembly had backed unsealing it for items of worth. If consecrated, one of its stewards of the dead would come to Anvil to collect them.

Imperial Orcs.t: If the mandate honouring Ahraz's role in freeing the orcs passed, the Imperial Orcs could support a fourth army or navy. Their people were also invited to give items of worth to lie beside his orc honour guard.

The Brass Coast.t: If the mandate honouring Ahraz's devotion to his own convictions passed, Freeborn spirits would rise after years of hardship and the nation could support a fourth army or navy. Firebrands and scriveners were also vying over what a proposed statue to him should celebrate.

Tomb of the Courageous.o: After the Courage Assembly resolved in Spring 388YE to consecrate the tomb of Emperor Ahraz, the General Assembly of the Synod was offered two competing mandates to frame the consecration. Each could strengthen either the Imperial Orcs or the Brass Coast, and the Senate was offered a chance to raise a statue to Ahraz in Kahraman.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Governor Rahab's predations in Feroz are listed among the recent hardships of the Brass Coast.

Kahraman.t: The Senate or the Mistress of Monuments could commission a statue of Ahraz in Kahraman, where he spent his last years, honouring him as either a firebrand or a scrivener.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the depredations of the Dry Patricians in Madruga are cited among the Freeborn's recent sufferings.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the orc-focused mandate would bolster orcs fighting to keep their grip on Mareave against the Grendel.

Necropolis.t: Ahraz's tomb in the Necropolis would be the site of the consecration and draw even more pilgrims, which its caretakers could manage. A steward of the dead would gather items of worth to place there.

Too much of nothing.d: With the Tower of Dawn fallen and the Barrens lost, Earl Hugo the Scarred of House Renard led his many destitute yeofolk towards Semmerholm. He came to Anvil to sell a single box of Barrenberry seeds, the only stock outside Druj-held Drycastle, to feed them through winter. Sir Morold Lionsgate's seneschal sought a buyer for incomplete writings by a long-dead Dawnish senator, to fund a memorial to Morold's grandmother. A young Steinr, cast out after the mysterious drowning of the Suaq icewalker Ilma Erkking, offered an ancient skinning knife from a cave. Felipa i Manola i Guerra brought an uninvestigated curio said to come from a freeborn exemplar of Prosperity's tomb.

Dawn.t: Dawn's loss of Drycastle left House Renard's yeofolk homeless and hungry, forcing Earl Hugo to sell the last Barrenberry seeds. Sir Morold Lionsgate's seneschal also offered a dead Dawnish senator's writings, looking for buyers first in the Dawnish camp.

Druj.t: The Druj had taken Drycastle and expelled the Imperial presence from the Barrens. This left the renowned Renard vineyards and their Barrenberry grapes in orcish hands.

Too much of nothing.o: After the fall of Drycastle to the Druj, several minor characters were expected at Anvil in Summer 381YE to sell rare goods. These included Earl Hugo of House Renard with the last Barrenberry seeds, and a Dawnish seneschal with a lost senator's writings.

Semmerholm.t: Ancient families and House Renard's many farm workers, driven out of the Barrens, made their way to the relative safety of Semmerholm's wooded glades. They arrived with no harvest to see them through the coming winter.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: the seneschal wondered whether someone from Weirwater might be interested in a past senator's writings.

Tooth by tooth.d: Ubarius's statement passed the Pride Assembly at Winter 384YE by 285 to 26. It warned that growing numbers of foreigners were settling in the Empire without adopting the Way. Each summit until the end of Winter 385YE, the Cardinal of Pride could submit a mandate, using 75 doses of liao, to send priests to learn the beliefs of a named group. This would yield understanding rather than conversions. The civil service suggested the Faraden, Feni, Great Forest Orcs, hylje, Marracossans, Montanians, Sand Fishers and the septs of Skarsind, and warned that targeting the Axos would fail. Under Cardinal Harwyn Eternal, missions went to the Faraden in Spring, the hylje in Summer and the Great Forest Orcs in Autumn. The last was cut short by events in the Barrens.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, but unspecified events in the Barrens cut short the Autumn mission to the Great Forest Orcs.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel's claim to have been brought to the Way by Urizeni missionaries over a century ago is cited as a past success.

Imperial Orcs.t: The four septs living in Skarsind were a possible missionary target, but the civil service warned that a careless approach could upset delicate negotiations with them.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun thralls in the Marches are listed among non-believers, and the conversion of the Lasambrians is said to have benefited the Jotun more than the Empire.

Navarr.t: The Montanians of Therunin, some of whom roam the trods with the Great Forest Orcs, were offered as a possible target, though their embrace of Freedom makes them hard to reconcile with the Way.

The Brass Coast.t: The Marracossans of Trajadoz in Madruga were a possible target, though the cession of that town would limit the Empire's legal recourse if they responded badly; the story is set among Freeborn in a parador in Sobral.

The League.t: The Sand Fishers settled near Holberg, the Empire's greatest recent success in spreading the Virtues, were named as an easier group to approach.

The Marches.t: The Jotun thralls of the Mournwold are named among non-believers in the Empire and as a possible target whose scattered beliefs could be collated and published.

Wintermark.t: At the Summer Solstice the Assembly sent Eska Crowspeaker to urge a mission to Wintermark's hylje allies, producing startling insights into their spiritual beliefs.

Tooth by tooth.o: Following a Pride Assembly judgement by Ubarius of Tropaion Citadel, urging priests to convert foreigners living in the Empire without the Way, the Cardinal of Pride gained the chance to direct missionary work each summit until Winter 385YE. Priests were ultimately sent to the Faraden, the hylje and the Great Forest Orcs.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the various foreign enclaves and embassies in the Bay's territories are cited as examples of non-believers in the Empire.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the Asavean temple to the Black Bull built in Feroz is cited as a cautionary example.

Holberg.t: The Sand Fishers living in the marshy forests on Holberg's edge, favourably inclined to the Empire and the Virtues, were proposed as a likely easy target for missionaries.

Madruga.t: The Marracossans of Trajadoz, newly ceded as an independent enclave, were expected to build a temple to their gods and were listed as a risky missionary target.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold thralls were suggested as a group whose already known beliefs missionaries could gather and publish.

Skarsind.t: The Ethengraw, Illarawm, Yerende and Tamazi septs of Skarsind could be approached, but only at the risk of disturbing precarious negotiations.

The Barrens.t: The Great Forest Orcs of Peytaht were the Autumn target, but events in the Barrens cut the mission short after it learned only something of their beliefs about the Great Forest.

Therunin.t: The Montanians living in Therunin, remnants of the Freedom Heresy, were named as a possible target whose devotion to Freedom complicates any reconciliation with the Way.

Top and Bottom, Up and Down.d: Sinokenon argued that the Omnihedron should use only Day magic, and that the Empire should freeze all Senate, Synod and Conclave decisions and army movements for a year. Stargazers dismissed both ideas. More practically, it proposed that the Senate create a Conclave title, such as an 'Overseer of the Omnihedron', able to raise one declaration of endorsement each summit. If this is done, Carve the Crystal Guardian would gain a seven-rank bonus for a season. It also offered a cheaper Day college at Sunspire in Morrow, with an everturning wheel for its Dean. The Almighty Panjandrum (Night), Fleeting Beat for Sorin, and Grimcrow for Wise Rangara offered dissenting views.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Turning Mirror notes that the Lyceum is currently in Grendel hands, which narrows the Empire's opportunities for magical research.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Sunspire is described as guarding the forests of Therunin against incursions from the Spring realm.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: Ragged Anne, an Ashill Landskeeper, mocks the Day eternal for answering a question about magic with more Day magic.

Urizen.t: Sinokenon calls the Urizeni theory of the Omnihedron flawed and is troubled that Anthemius Netherwatch was declared for organising the Urizen covens. It also proposes a cheaper Day college at Sunspire and warns that the Heliopticon may be pushed towards Autumn magic.

Varushka.t: Grimcrow, a herald of Wise Rangara, emerges from a regio in Varushkan Miekarova. It wanders the roads asking what the wisest course would be, and suggests pauses between rituals or abandoning the Omnihedron altogether.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: a Wintermark runesmith likens the Omnihedron to making steel, arguing that the right imperfections matter more than purity.

Top and Bottom, Up and Down.o: After the Conclave asked the Turning Mirror how the harm from Empire-wide Omnihedron rituals might be fixed, Sinokenon's heralds roamed the Empire offering mostly self-serving advice, along with two practical opportunities. Heralds of the Night, Winter and Spring realms also joined the debate with opposing views.

Upwold/Ashbrook.t: Mentioned in passing: Ragged Anne of the Ashill Landskeepers is quoted mocking the Day eternal's insistence on more Day magic.

Miekarova.t: Grimcrow, a bundle of sticks, feathers and bones with a corvid skull, emerges from a regio here to spread Wise Rangara's counsel along the Empire's roads.

Morrow.t: Sunspire in Morrow is identified as the ideal site for a cheaper College of Day Magic for the next year, costing 45 mithril, 45 white granite, 60 weirwood and 450 crowns. The opportunity has not yet been taken up.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Therunin's forests are watched over by Sunspire in neighbouring Morrow, which guards them against Spring incursions.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: an Ashill Landskeeper named Ragged Anne is quoted ridiculing the Turning Mirror's advice.

Touch the night.d: The magnitude 160 ritual, only the third such Empire-wide enchantment since before Emperor Hugh, boosted every forest's produce. Naga could strengthen their lineage trappings, gained an extra hero point and felt drawn to avarice and indifference to others, and more naga children are expected. Valeria of the Cloistered Eye catalogued altered rituals, including doubled alchemical transmutations and a cheaper Still Waters, Running Deep, while Wondrous Forests itself rose to magnitude 200. Azoth offered alchemical talismans. Lashonar offered nine Jarmish quills for ambassadors. Janon's herald Spark sought to talk faith. The Whisper Gallery offered to lift one enmity in exchange for a stolen ritual text. Sung offered three motes. The Conclave accepted the boons of Lashonar and Sung.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is not named directly, though heralds of Azoth are said to have visited the Castle of Thorns to offer their alchemical aid.

Highguard.t: Caleb of the Cenotaph, Minister of Historical Research, remained on the Whisper Gallery's list of Arch-Offenders whose deaths they sought, with a reward offered for his heart at the Summer Solstice.

Navarr.t: Two Navarr title-holders, Hywel Summercrow as Cardinal of the Way and Siân of the Eternal Family as Advisor on the Vallorn, stood on the Whisper Gallery's list of Arch-Offenders marked for death, though the Court offered to lift one enmity if its stolen ritual were returned.

The League.t: The League's Jaffo di Tassato suffered a botched transmutation in the opening tale, and Janon's herald Spark specifically sought a conversation with Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato about a statue destroyed in Temeschwar.

Urizen.t: The Urizen stargazer Valeria of the Cloistered Eye and her spire catalogued the ritual's ripples for the Conclave, Spark planned to visit the Archmage of Night Elyssiathain in the Urizen camp, and Livia of the Spire of the Celestial Cascade was named on the Whisper Gallery's list of Arch-Offenders.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: a Kallavesi naga in Hahnmark was reported to have woken to find their hair replaced by red and gold feathers.

Touch the night.o: After a night coven cast Wondrous Forests of the Night at the Spring Equinox, every forest in the Empire yielded extra bounty, naga felt a powerful pull of their blood, and lingering ripples altered several rituals for the Summer Solstice. Several Night eternals also offered gifts to the Empire.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is not named; the page only notes heralds of Azoth visiting the Castle of Thorns.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: a Kallavesi naga in Hahnmark reportedly went to sleep with a full head of hair and woke with a covering of brilliant red and gold feathers.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Janon's herald Spark wished to discuss the destruction of a statue in Temeschwar with Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato.

Tourney of the Damned.d: After two champions, one Dawnish and one Varushkan, defeated the knight a year earlier, his bargain went awry and his rampage began. Heroes limited his strength to a standard army, but it raises those it kills, and would gain about 1000 effective strength each season it went unchallenged. The two original champions could force him to a grand melee if they found him, likely in Wickmoor or Skoremujac, via an as-yet-unfound Sentinel Gate conjunction. Research commissioned by Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti might help. Executing him would leave his unliving troops rampaging, needing an army in each territory to contain them at up to 500 casualties; permanently destroying him would make them fall lifeless.

Dawn.t: Dawn faced an army of the dead that sought to conquer it as a kingdom of the dead, and one of the two original champions plus Dawnish warriors were needed for the challenging warband.

Varushka.t: A creature of the Varushkan Howling Queen threatened Karov, and the Varushkan champion and Varushkan warriors were required to challenge it, while Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti's commissioned research might reveal the knight's location.

Tourney of the Damned.o: The Deadwood Knight, an unliving lieutenant of the Howling Queen also called the Schlacta of Rot, finished gathering an army of the dead equivalent to a campaign army, poised to attack Weirwater or Karov after the Autumn Equinox. A last chance arose to challenge him to a grand melee and end his rampage.

Karov/Skoremujac.t: Skoremujac was one of the two likely places where the knight was gathering his forces and where the challenge might be issued, if the precise location could be found.

Weirwater/Wickmoor.t: Wickmoor was one of the two likely places where the knight was gathering his forces and where the champions might confront him in a grand melee.

Karov.t: Karov was the other possible target of the army of the dead, and would need a defending army to contain rampaging unliving soldiers even if the knight were killed.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater was one of the two possible targets of the knight's army after the Autumn Equinox, facing massive loss of life and possible permanent scarring if no army defended it.

Tourney of two cities.d: Months of fierce but so far good-natured rivalry over recruits, including scores of duels, led the Barossa School and the Five Cities Military Academy to sponsor a tourney for young citizens who had recently passed their Test of Arms but were still young enough for the Sun Chamber. The first eight teams of three to register by 16:00 on Saturday would compete from 18:30. Each member took a different role (beater, bravo, cataphract, questing-knight or warcaster), which set their permitted weapons, under Iron Duke rules without consumables or barbarism. The sponsors lodged nine thrones with the Artisans Guild so each winner could buy a magic item worth up to three thrones. Runners-up each received a Skop's Mead or a Philtre of Heavenly Lore.

The League.t: Two League academies were using the tourney to find young citizens they could train as future officers for Imperial armies. They sponsored it with nine thrones.

Tourney of two cities.o: The rival military academies of Tassato, the Barossa School of Imperial Strategy and the Five Cities Military Academy, asked the Anvil Academy to arrange a sponsored fighting tourney at the Anvil arena. The first Twin Cities Tourney was announced as a way to find young recruits.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Home of the Five Cities Military Academy, one of the two sponsors competing to draw young recruits through the tourney.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: Home of the Barossa School of Imperial Strategy, the Five Cities Academy's rival and co-sponsor of the tourney.

Tassato.t: The city's two great military academies were locked in a rivalry over recruits. They channelled it into a jointly sponsored tourney at Anvil rather than more duels at home.

Towards a common good.d: Paulk Thornweaver won the patronage of the Beurteilung at the Winter Solstice for twenty-six thrones. Gelberg's team proposed that Highborn generals on defensive orders could send officers and experts to aid Commonwealth counterparts in return for gifts, or send key figures from a newly raised army to Commonwealth war colleges for six months. Henrik Hexenjäger asked Highguard to build a Hexenjäger Academy, creating the national title of Bursar of the Hexenjäger. The Synod could also explicitly rule that preaching the Common Good was not heresy, though Naomi of Virtue's Rest warned this risked weakening the faith. Gelberg announced he would complete one final assignment and return home shortly before the Summer Solstice 388YE.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; the only link is Naomi of Virtue's Rest saying she had been engaged with matters in the Sarangrave, which they held.

Highguard.t: Highborn generals were offered the chance to aid the Commonwealth or train a new army there, and the nation could commission the Hexenjäger Academy in any Highborn region to create the Bursar of the Hexenjäger, appointed by Tally of the Votes or the National Assembly. Naomi of Virtue's Rest cautioned the Synod against permitting the Common Good to spread.

Towards a common good.o: Die Beurteilung, led by Professor Immanuel Gelberg, appraised how Highguard and the Commonwealth could forge stronger ties, on behalf of Solomon of the Shattered Tower. It identified three avenues: military doctrine, a witch-hunters' academy and legalising the preaching of the Common Good.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Naomi of Virtue's Rest explained she had not fully appraised the matter because she had been engaged with matters in the Sarangrave.

Towers and crows.d: Relations with the Delves stayed positive but were tinged with disappointment after several failed trade deals, and the Delves remained determined to stay neutral in the wars. They proposed opening negotiations at two thrones a wain for mithril, weirwood or white granite, or three thrones for weirwood if they could sell it straight on to the Grendel. The civil service noted that the legality of this was murky. The Sarcophan were troubled by Conclave-endorsed storm magic and resented the unwarned storms on their Sarvos enclave. Fearing for their neutrality, they offered 18 thrones for the Regario Dossier rather than an exchange of intelligence. They also declined to share anything about the Elakar or the Book of Silence.

Grendel.t: The Grendel were the unnamed 'local buyer' already buying all the weirwood the Delves could supply to build navies. Any Imperial weirwood sold through the Sarcophan would speed their shipbuilding.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sarcophan were not trading much in Madruga anyway because of the turmoil in that Brass Coast territory.

The League.t: The Sarcophan enclave in the old Alivetti estates in Sarvos was hit by storms before the Spring Equinox. The Vandersaar family were aggrieved that they had not been warned and that no apology followed.

Wintermark.t: Thanmir Hrafnar of Wintermark, the Imperial ambassador to the Delves, gave no apology for the Sarvos storms, which irked the Vandersaar. The Sarcophan did thank him for his candid advice on their narcotic herb proposals and intended to follow it.

Towers and crows.o: In Summer 386YE the Sarcophan Delves, through ambassador Bedelaar Huisbaas Annike, offered to open negotiations to buy Imperial bourse materials, including a higher price for weirwood they would sell on to the Grendel. They also complained about storms in the Bay of Catazar and Sarvos, withdrew from intelligence sharing, and refused to help with the Elakar or the Book of Silence.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Bay had become a war zone and its piracy risk depressed the price the Sarcophan would pay for bourse materials. They proposed carrying weirwood safely across it to the Grendel, and they were wary of the recent storm magic cast on its waters.

Madruga.t: Madruga was the only place where the warned-of storms actually materialised. The Sarcophan were not trading much there anyway because of the turmoil in the territory.

Sarvos.t: Storms before the Spring Equinox struck the Vandersaar family's Alivetti estates, ceded to the Delves in 383YE. Local Sarcophan were angry that they had received no warning.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: named as an alternative shipping route for bourse materials that was no safer than the Bay of Catazar.

The Semmerlak.t: Mentioned in passing: reaching the Semmerlak through the Mallum was named as an alternative shipping route that was no safer than the Bay.

Towers behind the moon.d: Starless shrouds persisted over Ossium and Semmerholm, the Penumbral Veil hung over Madruga and Kahraman, and the shrouds over the Barrens, Spiral and Zenith faded. Strange constellations appeared over Astolat. Winter's Ghosts cursed Casinea, cutting its production by a quarter. Twelve magical fortifications were raised across six territories. The Concordium of Pallas aided the Doyen of the Spires. Eternal news followed: Callidus's High Tontine continued, Sorin set his next trial in Bittershore, and Revel arranged to meet challengers. Tharim recognised a new Keeper, Ylenrith withdrew from contact and Lashonar postponed her game. On the Het's orders, Druj released a hundred slaves at Parel, crediting Danica Lidija van Temeschwar as representative of Mazen.

Dawn.t: Strange magical birds appeared in Astolat's night sky, Semmerholm remained starless, and two heralds of Tharim visited the Castle of Thorns; a brace of tortured Dawnish knights were among the slaves freed at Parel.

Druj.t: The shrouds over the Barrens and Zenith faded, and a small Druj force released a hundred human slaves near Parel on the Het's orders before melting back into the forest.

Grendel.t: The shroud that had hung over Grendel-held Spiral faded away this season.

Highguard.t: A Winter's Ghosts curse ravaged Casinea and cut its production by a quarter, and two score Highborn from an ill-starred crusade into the Barrens were among the freed slaves.

Navarr.t: The Voice of the Quiet Forest wove Spring fortifications of thickets, thorns and branches across Hercynia and Therunin, and generals of Navarr are among those Zakalwe's heralds wish to meet about the Tourney.

The Brass Coast.t: The Penumbral Veil hung over Madruga and Kahraman, and Revel intended to hire space from a Brass Coast family at Anvil to meet challengers.

The League.t: Most of the freed slaves at Parel were League citizens taken from the farms of Holberg over a decade ago, and generals of the League are among those Zakalwe's heralds wish to meet.

The Marches.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised castles of mist over the fens of the Rushes and Ottermire in Bregasland.

Urizen.t: An Autumn enchantment from the Concordium of Pallas aided Urizen magicians codifying the Doyen of the Spires' ritual, despite the loss of Spiral and Zenith hampering their work; a castle of ice was raised in Caeli and a dozen former Zenith citizens were freed.

Varushka.t: Ossium's skies remained starless, strengthening naga secrecy, and Sorin's next Trial of the Pallid Charm was set for the Regio of the Unquiet Hounds in Bittershore.

Wintermark.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised five castles of mist across Imperial marshes, and a Winter castle of ice and granite rose in Northspires in Hahnmark.

Towers behind the moon.o: A Wind of Fortune for Winter 383YE reported the lingering effects of magic cast at the Autumn Equinox, from shrouds, a curse and twelve magical fortifications, and relayed news from the eternals. Tharim announced a new Keeper of Tharim's Throne, and the Druj freed a hundred slaves at Parel.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a castle of mist over the fens of Ottermire.

Hahnmark/Northspires.t: A great castle of ice and granite, called from the Breath of Winter, was raised in Northspires' hills.

Hercynia/Northpines.t: A castle of ice and granite drawn from the Breath of Winter was raised in Northpines.

Hercynia/Old Ranging.t: The Voice of the Quiet Forest turned the region's thickets and thorns into Spring fortifications.

Hercynia/Summersend.t: Swathes of thickets and thorns in Summersend were woven into Spring fortifications.

Hercynia/The Glen of Shadows.t: Thickets and thorns in the Glen of Shadows were turned into Spring fortifications.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not discussed; the name appears only in that of Zakalwe's herald, the Opening Gambit.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: A castle of mist was raised over Kallavesa Marsh by the Sussivari Frost Coven.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: A castle of mist was raised over West Marsh by the Sussivari Frost Coven.

Morrow/Caeli.t: A castle of ice and granite from the Breath of Winter was raised in Caeli's hills.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: The next Trial of the Pallid Charm is due at the Regio of the Unquiet Hounds in Bittershore on the summit's second evening.

Semmerholm/Estmure.t: Druj released a hundred slaves at Parel in Estmure; most are recovering at the House of the Proffered Hand.

Therunin/East Ashes.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a castle of mist over the murky waters of East Ashes.

Therunin/Eastring.t: The bayous of Eastring became moats for Spring walls of woven branches.

Astolat.t: Unfamiliar constellations appeared over Astolat, showing a silver firebird with a rose and a horned eagle, before fading; the Castle of Thorns also received two heralds of Tharim.

Bregasland.t: Castles of mist were raised over the fens of the Rushes and Ottermire.

Casinea.t: Winter's Ghosts tormented Casinea for three months, and all its farms, forests, businesses, mines, mana sites and herb gardens produced only three quarters of their usual yield.

Hahnmark.t: A great castle of ice and granite was raised in the hills of Northspires.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia gained a Winter castle in Northpines and Spring fortifications of thickets and thorns in the Glen of Shadows, Old Ranging and Summersend.

Holberg.t: Many of the slaves freed at Parel were League citizens taken from Holberg's farms over a decade ago.

Kahraman.t: The Penumbral Veil, a more traditional shroud, hung over Kahraman.

Kallavesa.t: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised castles of mist over West Marsh and Kallavesa Marsh.

Madruga.t: The Penumbral Veil, a more traditional shroud, hung over Madruga.

Morrow.t: A castle of ice and granite was raised in the hills of Caeli.

Ossium.t: Ossium's night skies remained starless, strengthening naga secrecy, and Sorin's next trial was set for Bittershore.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm's skies stayed starless, affecting naga there, and a hundred freed slaves were released at Parel in Estmure.

Spiral.t: The shroud over Spiral faded away, and its loss is said to impede the work of Urizen's Doyen of the Spires.

The Barrens.t: The shroud over the Barrens faded away; some freed Highborn slaves had been captured on an ill-starred crusade into the Barrens.

Therunin.t: Eastring's bayous served as moats for walls of woven branches, and a castle of mist rose over East Ashes.

Zenith.t: The shroud over Zenith faded, its loss hampers the Doyen of the Spires, and a dozen Urizen formerly of Zenith were among the freed slaves.

Towers of the moon.d: Sadogua offered a commission for the Toadstool Palace around the Toadstone in West Marsh. If built and ceded to him, it would create the chosen title Toadstool Wizard, grant the Froghaven quality and strengthen Dripping Echoes of the Fen in Kallavesa, though it would give him lasting magical leverage there. He also offered the Well of Shadows to Archmage of Night Brat Umbral Path, with future access as a prize for the largest Tithe of Bats. He proposed a Twilight Pier on the Lyceum isle for the Arcane Architect, a pre-wassail mushroom boon for Marcher farms and a Senate appraisal for arcane great works. He thanked the Conclave for its enmity against Apeiron, kept feuding with the Circle of Zulgan Tash and made peace with other Varushkans.

The Brass Coast.t: Sadogua's heralds visited Madruga, and he offered the Arcane Architect the chance to build a Twilight Pier on the Isle of the Lyceum. This would bring a Night-realm trading vessel offering Night foci, robes and crystal fire.

The Marches.t: Sadogua offered access to his Well of Shadows in Upwold and promised heralds for the Anvil wassail. Marcher farms enchanted with Fallow Fields and Dried Meat plus crystal fire could grow black mushrooms that yield Shinemoon elixirs.

Varushka.t: Sadogua continued his feud with the Circle of Zulgan Tash, accusing them of stealing a fortress protecting his western woods. He promised other Varushkan wizards a return to his usual friendly advice through missives, but refused to send heralds to Miekarova or Ossium for now.

Wintermark.t: Sadogua promised arcane projections to Tarqeq Icetongue and Sigebryht and offered the Toadstool Palace commission in Kallavesa. If built and ceded to him, it would create a Toadstool Wizard title, always held by a Wintermark magician without an Imperial title, who would use Night magic to protect the nation and harvest Shinemoon.

Towers of the moon.o: In Autumn 388YE the eternal Sadogua, Brother of Wizards, roused himself to catch up on obligations to his Imperial friends, offering a string of boons and opportunities across Wintermark, the Marches, the Brass Coast and Varushka.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: The onyx Toadstone near Westerhal could become the Toadstool Palace, a garden ceded to Sadogua. This would grant West Marsh the Froghaven quality, making its frogs prosper and grow big and wise.

Upwold/Tower March.t: The Well of Shadows near King's Stoke would open to Brat Umbral Path after the Autumn Equinox. Its door could be placed under watch by a Vigilance mandate.

Kallavesa.t: If the Toadstool Palace is built and ceded, Sadogua will back every casting of Dripping Echoes of the Fen in Kallavesa, raising the victory points needed to take a region and inflicting casualties on invaders. However, he would also gain the power to shape Night enchantments and curses on the territory.

Madruga.t: Sadogua claimed dominion over the Isle of the Lyceum off Madruga and offered a Twilight Pier there, available only to the Arcane Architect until the end of Summer 389YE. Once built, it would host regular visits from the Twilight Barque.

Miekarova.t: Sadogua refused to send heralds to Miekarova, and he would be angered if the Senate named it in the appraisal for arcane great works.

Ossium.t: Sadogua's heralds have reportedly been fighting spider monsters in Ossium. He nonetheless excluded the territory from his proposed arcane great works appraisal and would be angered if it were chosen.

Upwold.t: The Well of Shadows, Sadogua's college of magic inside an oak tree near King's Stoke, was offered to Brat Umbral Path. The Vigilance assembly could post a priest with liao to watch who uses it, at the risk of irritating Sadogua and the Marcher assembly.

Towers of the sun.d: Meraud offered plans for wizard towers, available until the end of the Summer Solstice 389YE, each harnessing a Summer regio and granting a title four golden apples a season. The civil service judged them to be fanes that only work if the Senate concedes them to the eternal. Meraud proposed judging the most impressive tower before the Winter Solstice 389YE and rewarding it with a boon. He asked the Senate to let him choose the Churnspire Adjutor, offering a yearly missive and Rings of Majesty in return. He also asked the Conclave to accept Orchard Tender's Tribute in place of From the Mouth of Babes, and sent a herald to deliver golden missives at the Arcane Colloquium.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: several magicians invited to collect Meraud's golden missives bear Dawnish-style titles, among them Enchanter Vesper Lucentia, witch-warden of Weirwater.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire once used armies to retake Llofir's garden in Reikos, a warning about trying to reclaim a fane from an eternal.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are cited as building palaces for the Regents of Summer, from which heralds march out to fight alongside their armies, as an example of how useful fanes can be.

Urizen.t: Meraud asked the Senate to let him, rather than Urizen's senators, choose the Churnspire Adjutor, making the post his representative to Urizen. In return the Adjutor would gain a yearly missive to him and Rings of Majesty. Artemis Grey would remain in the role for now.

Towers of the sun.o: In Autumn 388YE heralds of Meraud, the Summer Enchanter, brought the Empire plans for Summer wizard towers with a contest for the grandest, a proposal that he appoint the Churnspire Adjutor, and a request to replace From the Mouth of Babes with a new ritual. He also promised replies to last season's missives.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is recalled as the place where the Empire used armies to take back Llofir's garden many years ago.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: Enchanter Vesper Lucentia, witch-warden of Weirwater, was among the magicians invited to receive a golden missive from Meraud's herald.

Trade all my tomorrows.d: A new road north of Mellfort, bypassing Hercynia's trods, eased the flow of metals west to Kalpaheim, while Steinr weapons, armour and jewellery spread outward. Building a Kalpaheim Trade Hall, which needed a Senate motion or wayleave, 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns, would connect Wintermark to the network, including cheap mana crystals from Thule. It might also send Wintermark weapons to Thule merchants serving their dragon masters. Mott of Fisher's Rock sent an apprentice with venomous weapons against vallornspawn. Llinos Fabledwing brought the Summer Acorn, said to come from Arden's Great Oak. Dhomiro Ximen i Suerta i Guerra sought backing for a stone casino in Cerevado, and Eli of the Seventh Step brought an ancient sun symbol.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the northern neighbours sharing the trade network's wealth, and as holders of a dedicated wayleave that Ximen i Suerta hoped to use.

Navarr.t: Navarr were part of the northern trade network. The Fabledwing Striding brought the Summer Acorn to Anvil, and Twyll Eternal, the Blackroot Broker, was asked to find buyers for Mott's venomous blades.

The Brass Coast.t: Dhomiro Ximen i Suerta i Guerra sought a wayleave, commission or Senate motion to build a great stone casino in Cerevado. He claimed it would bring prosperity to a town strained by poor refugees, after failing to win sponsorship from the Brass Coast's senators.

The League.t: Eastern metals had traditionally gone to Temeschwar first, but the new road diverted some trade west. Meanwhile Temeschwar developed a fashion for Steinr depictions of Varushkan Virtue-animals.

The Marches.t: Mott of Fisher's Rock, a reclusive Bregasland herbalist, sent an apprentice to Anvil with venomous weapons, surprising many by seeking a Navarr broker rather than a fellow Marcher.

Thule.t: Thule traders sold mana crystals cheaply into the northern trade network. There were fears that a Kalpaheim Trade Hall would let Wintermark weapons reach Thule merchants buying for their dragon masters.

Varushka.t: Varushkan miners and merchants such as Miloš of Delev drove the new trade, selling metals to Hahnmark's crafters and buying their weapons, armour and mail in return.

Wintermark.t: Steinr artisans profited from easier access to eastern metals. Wintermark could commission a Kalpaheim Trade Hall to join the northern trade network, at the risk of its weapons flowing to the Thule.

Trade all my tomorrows.o: In Autumn 382YE a new road from Delev to Kalpaheim was quietly linking Varushkan miners with the Steinr artisans of Hahnmark, and Wintermark was offered the chance to join the northern trade network by building a Trade Hall in Kalpaheim. Several traders also announced visits to Anvil with unusual goods and proposals.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Mott's name was a byword in the North Fens, and Greywater's eel-fishers reported her apprentice asking the quickest way to Anvil.

Hercynia/Deer's Folly.t: Bont Goch, the village behind the Fabledwing Striding's founding, re-enchanted the Summer Acorn as a Coven Stone. The striding had also freed nearby Tyr Uchaf from vallorn-infested mandowlas.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: Urdur was the point where Thule trade fed into the northern network, exchanging tempest jade for crystal mana that the network's members could buy cheaply.

Bregasland.t: Mott of Fisher's Rock, a surly merrow herbalist living among marshspiders, dispatched an apprentice from Bregasland to sell venomous weapons at Anvil.

Hahnmark.t: Kalpaheim became the western end of a busier road from Delev, and a proposed Trade Hall there would require 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns and could be finished in a single season.

Hercynia.t: The new road to Kalpaheim bypassed Hercynia's rough trods, and the Fabledwing Striding had freed Hercynian villages from vallorn-infested mandowlas.

Otkodov.t: The Thule of Otkodov were part of the northern trade network, selling mana crystals cheaply, and might become buyers of Wintermark weapons if the Trade Hall were built.

Temeschwar.t: Temeschwar, traditionally the first destination for eastern metals, saw a growing fashion for Steinr portrayals of Virtue-animals. The Fabledwing had freed its village of Seraya Derevnya from plaguewulves.

Trade winds.d: After the Senate placed the Imperial embassy to Jarm in Rigia, the eastern princes gained trade with the Empire, though the port was still unprepared for the influx. The northern and southern factions blamed Imperial interference and resented rumours of secret orc slave dealing, so captains met cold receptions in Kavor and bureaucratic obstruction in Vezak. The Commonwealth introduced tariffs on Imperial goods, citing the Empire's friendship with Jarm and its lack of interest in diplomacy with them, and might in theory close its ports. In Zemeh the Sumaah were openly hostile over Imperial ties to Asavea. Meanwhile Grendel Salt Lords gathered warships to harass and destroy Imperial vessels, making raiding less profitable.

Grendel.t: The Salt Lords massed their warships to patrol the southern bay and actively hunt Imperial ships, carrying heavily armed marines that made raids on Grendel shipping costly and less profitable.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the story's captain sails the Meade Minstrel carrying flour from the mills of Upwold, which was held up by Jarmish inspectors in Vezak.

Trade winds.o: Imperial ship captains found their dealings with foreign powers soured in Summer 379YE: Jarm's northern and southern ports turned cold after the Empire's embassy went to eastern Rigia, the Commonwealth imposed tariffs, Sumaah met traders with fury, and Grendel warships began hunting Imperial raiders in the Bay of Catazar.

Bay of Catazar.t: Grendel warships gathered in force in the southern waters of the bay, harassing and seeking to destroy Imperial ships, making engagements with Grendel vessels more dangerous than usual.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: flour from Upwold's mills formed part of a cargo that Jarmish officials in Vezak demanded be inspected for pests.

Tread of dust and darkness.d: Gideon of the Farthest Shore concluded that the Blight's power was gathering at the abandoned di Tutamen villa, probably in the missing body of Aldea di Tutamen, which sits in a Winter regio. A five-person conjunction to the villa was identified and assigned to the Hakima of Salt and Sand. Aligning the regio with Spring might let the Rainmaker Ossegrahn claim it and cut the Blight off. That would make it safer to cast Dyan of Eagle's Striding's projection, held by Grandmaster Eliza, which would flood the Scorrero and wash the region clean. Separately, Azoth studied Dry Patrician ashes for Bakar i Riqueza. Detachments of the Drakes and the Burning Falcon had also corralled two groups of displaced Parched.

The Brass Coast.t: Brass Coast figures stood at the centre of the struggle. The Hakima of Salt and Sand was charged with the conjunction to the Blight's heart, Bakar i Riqueza awaited Azoth's alchemical research, and General Aracelis i Erigo had to defeat Parched cornered by the Burning Falcon's kohan to return 50 strength to the army.

Tread of dust and darkness.o: In Summer 386YE, following the Empire's decisive Spring victory over the Dry Patricians, the Blight in Madruga's former Great Grasses lay quiescent but undefeated. Several opportunities arose to end it for good, including a Sentinel Gate conjunction to its very heart.

Segura/Lucksprings.t: The hard-fought Spring Equinox incursion against the Parched in Lucksprings is where Bakar i Riqueza apparently claimed the Dry Patrician dust and ashes that Azoth is now studying.

Madruga.t: The Blight still holds the ashen desert of Blightheart, though its power has drawn inward to the di Tutamen villa. Proposed remedies include claiming its regio through Ossegrahn and flooding the land via the Scorrero, while Imperial armies hold off stray Parched displaced by the storms.

Segura.t: Ashes from the Dry Patrician that attacked Segura were delivered to Azoth. The Crucible's study of them may yield a new ritual alchemy for Bakar i Riqueza once the Blight is resolved.

Troop of echoes.d: After the revocation and condemnation of Ambassador Fintan Nighthaven, The Flame of Riqueza became Ambassador to Axos. Axos's new envoy, Ilarch Kario Skopos, arranged a ceremonial delegation to the Senate. He also hoped to discuss joint action against the Druj Tower of the Skink and the Liberty Pact. Axos will host a Pact meeting through the Midnight Owl's Caucus Forum to repeal the 384YE Jarm embargo amendment. The Unified Convocation named Fintan an "Enemy of the Creator", and the General Assembly could still vindicate him before his trial. Kantor now offers tomb dust and Masks of the Citadel. Maykop sought reassurance that no theft occurred during the Shuttered Lantern codification. A Great Library request remains unanswered.

Druj.t: Axou representatives of Grand Ilarch Dancia Terricos of Ipotavo remain committed to action against the Druj Tower of the Skink, and they hope to discuss a joint strategy for the Sarangrave war with the Military Council.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Apulian orc Batheka de Tassato Regario was an experienced Grendel commander before joining the League.

Highguard.t: More black-sailed Axou ships are arriving at Crown's Quay in Necropolis now that the Asavean bounty has ended, and trade is returning towards normal levels.

The Brass Coast.t: The Flame of Riqueza of the Brass Coast has succeeded Fintan Nighthaven as Ambassador to Axos. The new ambassador is expected to receive the Axou delegation in the Senate and to handle the coming Liberty Pact business.

The League.t: Axos proposed paying 5 thrones a season for its officers to study at the Five Cities Military Academy in Tassato, which would need a Senate motion to accept. The League's Batheka de Tassato Regario suggested casually inviting Axou siege commanders or toxatai captains so the Empire might learn from them.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the codified Oath of the Bleak Garden is believed to draw on work by the Urizen Spyridonakes of the Lighthouse-That-Was, and Axou battle-mages are compared to Urizen sentinels.

Troop of echoes.o: In Autumn 387YE the Citadels of Axos, under their new ambassador Ilarch Skopos of Solokha, announced a formal delegation to Anvil and called a Liberty Pact meeting for the Winter Solstice. They also raised concerns about espionage in Maykop and proposed that Axou officers study at the Five Cities Military Academy.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Mistress Isephenia of Maykop helps run the House of Spirits in Casinea alongside Bursar Rinnah.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: Axou engineers are described as almost as skilled as those from Holberg.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is not named directly, and the only apparent link is the new Ambassador, The Flame of Riqueza of the Brass Coast.

Necropolis.t: Trade through Crown's Quay is recovering, with more black-sailed Axou ships arriving now that the Asavean bounty has ended and Imperial escorts continue.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the Oath of the Bleak Garden codified in Maykop is believed to be based on work by Spyridonakes of the Lighthouse-That-Was.

Sarangrave.t: Axos hopes to agree a joint strategy against the Druj Tower of the Skink in the Sarangrave. Representatives of Grand Ilarch Dancia Terricos remain committed to taking action there.

Tassato.t: Axou officers from Ipotavo, Kaban and Issyk wish to study at the Five Cities Military Academy and the Barossa School in Tassato. Their attendance would bring in 5 thrones a season but carries a risk of espionage, and it depends on the Senate approving it.

Trove remade.d: Probus of the Shattered Spire, Senator for Redoubt, provided a significant amount of ilium to imbue the recovered mage weapons and armour. They now resonate with the six realms in a fixed seasonal cycle following the pattern of Align the Celestial Net: day, winter, spring, night, summer, autumn, then day again. The Citadel Guard's magic quality became Cyclic Resonance. Each season the general may choose whether to use a unique order drawn from the current realm, but cannot choose which realm it is. The ilium means the cycle cannot be interrupted, reversed, delayed, skipped or shifted by magic. General Nicassia Avicia of Phoenix Reach was to decide where the cycle began. The quality was replaced by highest discipline in Autumn 383YE.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening vignette only alludes to orcs as the enemy the Citadel Guard faces in Spiral, and Grendel are not named.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening vignette shows a Navarr cambion archer, Comac, fighting alongside the Citadel Guard in Spiral and grumbling about his own poor supplies.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Citadel Guard gained the Cyclic Resonance quality, using magic drawn from the six realms in a fixed seasonal cycle. Their general, Nicassia Avicia of Phoenix Reach, was to choose where that cycle began.

Trove remade.o: The trove of mage weapons and armour found beneath the ruins of the Unmade Spire in Redoubt was imbued with ilium and used to equip the Citadel Guard. This gave the army a new Cyclic Resonance quality tied to the six realms of magic.

Spiral/Ateri.t: Mentioned in passing: in the opening vignette, the Navarr archer recalls meeting the sentinel Punam earlier in Ateri.

Redoubt.t: The trove came from the vaulted chamber beneath the Unmade Spire in Redoubt, and Redoubt's senator, Probus of the Shattered Spire, supplied the ilium that empowered it.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening vignette is set among Citadel Guard sentinels and Navarr fighting in Spiral.

True faith.d: Hazelelponi of the Shattered Tower released the Library's findings, backed by statements in the Vigilance, Wisdom and Varushkan Assemblies, and confidence in the Synod faltered. Three paths were offered: a mandate declaring that it does not matter whether paragons are real, a greater-majority judgement of recognition removing Vardas, or a mandate denouncing the findings as lies, which would destroy the Library. Masha Sigeling called Hazelelponi to inquisition. While the crisis lasted, new inspirational memorials had no effect, the Capodomus Cathedral consecration guidance was delayed, and no new mandates could support the Grand Inspiration. The General Assembly revoked Vardas' recognition and defeated The Fool of Glory's stories-over-facts mandate.

Dawn.t: Dawn's existing mandate urging its people to support the Grand Inspiration of the Way still resolved normally, with its contribution due to be completed shortly before the Winter Solstice.

Highguard.t: Highguard's call to support the sacred city of the Grand Inspiration continued, but the crisis blocked any new mandates in its support. The faithful also questioned the pilgrimage to Bastion as a sign of the paragon.

Navarr.t: Navarr was unable to restate its support for the Grand Inspiration of the Way while the crisis of faith lasted.

The League.t: The evidence held that a League mountebank penned the stories of Vardas. The League's Grand Inspiration contribution still resolved normally, but guidance on consecrating Capodomus Cathedral was delayed.

Urizen.t: Urizen, troubled by its own recent experience with an inspirational figure, would have been left in disastrous crisis had a reassurance mandate passed without a greater majority.

Varushka.t: Vardas was a much-loved figure in Varushka, and the Varushkan Assembly urged the faithful to look instead to the real deeds of Varushkan wardens once attributed to the fictional paragon.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark was unable to restate its support for the Grand Inspiration of the Way while the crisis of faith lasted.

True faith.o: After the Lepidean Librarian published research showing that Vardas, a paragon of Vigilance, never existed and was the invention of a League fraudster, a crisis of faith spread across the Empire. The General Assembly ultimately revoked its recognition of Vardas, heading off the crisis but inviting hard questions about the other paragons.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: Mentioned in passing: the Kallavesa marshes were named as an example of a sacred site that could still be consecrated.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the pilgrimage to Bastion, one of the signs of a paragon, was questioned because many older paragons appear to predate Bastion itself.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Kallavesa marshes were cited as a sacred site the Synod could still consecrate whatever the outcome.

Sarvos.t: The writ to consecrate Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos was upheld, but its guidance and supporting mandate were delayed until the crisis of faith was resolved. Aldones di Sarvos's past life vision was also cited as an earlier case that led to a paragon being de-recognised.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Houndsgate in the Barrens was cited as a sacred site the Synod could still consecrate.

Turbulence.d: Two days after the Summer Solstice a fierce thunderstorm struck the Semmerlak at sunset and battered fishing boats, costing catches and damaging some vessels. It ceased at dawn, leaving a windless day, then returned each night. Reports followed of hostile creatures active in the water after dark, named Semmerfolk or kalpie by the Dawnish and rusalka by the Varushkans. Fleets based in Semmerholm, Weirwater, Karov and Karsk faced a significant loss of production unless the problem was dealt with, and fisherfolk who rely on the lake were already suffering. The weather was clearly supernatural and seemed more than a simple curse. Magical investigation could target any of the four shore territories.

Dawn.t: Dawnish fleets in Semmerholm and Weirwater faced serious losses, yeomen and noble houses fishing the lake were already hurt, and the Dawnish named the attacking creatures Semmerfolk or kalpie.

Druj.t: Sailors reported that the storms battered the eastern shores of the Semmerlak just as hard as elsewhere, so the Druj in the Mallum were presumably suffering as well.

Varushka.t: Varushkan fleets in Karov and Karsk faced significant losses, and Varushkans named the predatory creatures in the water rusalka.

Turbulence.o: In Autumn 380YE an unnatural cycle of dead calm by day and violent storms by night gripped the Semmerlak, while monstrous creatures called Semmerfolk, kalpie or rusalka began attacking people on and near the lake.

Karov.t: Fleets based in Karov faced a significant penalty to production unless the turbulence was dealt with, and Karov was one of the shore territories through which magical investigation could be made.

Karsk.t: Fleets based in Karsk were hampered by the nightly storms and windless days, and Karsk could serve as a target for magical investigation into the phenomenon.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm's fleets and fisherfolk were troubled by the storms and lake creatures, and the territory could be targeted to investigate the supernatural weather.

The Semmerlak.t: The lake itself suffered calm days and violent stormy nights, with monstrous creatures hunting its waters after dark. Because it is not a territory, it could only be investigated through the territories along its shores.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater's fleets faced a significant loss of production and its fisherfolk were hurt by the turbulence, and the territory was a possible focus for magical investigation.

Twelfth of never.d: Citadel Guard scouts in the Salt Flats of Sanath took the Druj messengers into custody before the summit.
