The message to Emperor Vesna proposed that if the Empire withdrew all forces from the Salt Flats of Sanath and the Forest of Ulnak for a season and a year, no Druj would attack Imperial citizens or holdings. One complete Black Lotus plant had been placed with the Lictors of Bar and Bond, the Green Iron Gaolers, to be released to the Throne if the truce held for five seasons, or sooner if the Druj attacked. The Druj threatened to destroy every plant rather than let them be taken. Historians believe this may be the first formal Druj offer of terms. The messengers were sent away unharmed.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: one of the Druj signatories styles himself 'Livid-Eye, who is Dayne of the False Dawn'.

Druj.t: The Congress of Buruk Tepel made what may be the first formal Druj offer of surrender terms, staking a Black Lotus plant with the Lictors to guarantee a truce, while threatening to destroy all their Black Lotus rather than lose it in battle.

Twelfth of never.o: In Autumn 388YE a small Druj delegation under a flag of truce brought the Empire an offer of conditional surrender from the Congress of Buruk Tepel: an Imperial withdrawal from the Salt Flats of Sanath and the Forest of Ulnak in exchange for a truce and, eventually, a Black Lotus plant.

Forest of Ulnak.t: The Druj demanded that the Empire withdraw all its forces from the Forest of Ulnak for a season and a year as a condition of the proposed truce.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Druj messengers approached Citadel Guard pickets here under a white flag, and the offer required the Empire to pull all its forces out of the Salt Flats for a season and a year.

Two for joy.d: The Magpies will exist only if the Throne ratifies them. If they do, an Autumn arcane projection will help citizens join, and members will elect a Speaker. The Constitutional Court found that the manifesto passes authority over historical research to the sodality. An administrative motion would decide whether to abridge it or devolve research, including appointment of the Minister of Historical Research. The Senate could also make the Golden Fleet Salvagemaster a Magpie appointment. Urizeni torchbearers of Spider's Vantage offered 21 mana a season, Highguard and League historians sought a preservation clause, and Leviathan offered a wetstone. Kimus offered to find one of three items the Archmage of Day had sought, with the Magpies choosing which.

Highguard.t: Highborn historians want the Magpies to take on the preservation of lore, libraries and museums. The Highborn Golden Fleet Salvagemaster, whose salvage rights Caleb of the Cenotaph bought, might become a Magpie appointment.

The League.t: League historians join the call to broaden the manifesto towards preservation. The Holberg Historical Press offers to publish one manuscript a season for the Magpies if that change is made.

Urizen.t: Sacharissan torchbearers of Spider's Vantage offer the Magpies an ongoing bequest of 21 mana each season. They require the sodality to win authority over historical research and leave the Minister's title vacant or abrogated.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: a Wintermark scribe records the message from Kimus's herald in the opening in-character text.

Two for joy.o: After the Senate approved the creation of the Magpies, a new Imperial sodality devoted to recovering lost artefacts, the civil service found it had failed to obtain Throne ratification, leaving the sodality in suspension. Constitutional questions over historical research and salvage rights were raised, and several groups offered patronage in exchange for changes to its manifesto.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Fleet Salvagemaster recovers historical items from the wreck of the Barabbine Fleet off the coast of Arbonne. The Senate could make that title a Magpie appointment.

Holberg.t: The Holberg Historical Press, with spare capacity and high scholarly standards, hopes to gain prominence by publishing for the Magpies. This depends on the sodality's manifesto being rewritten to include preserving and promulgating knowledge.

Redoubt.t: The spire of Spider's Vantage in Redoubt still holds an impressive library despite a Faraden attempt to destroy it three years ago. It offers to gather 21 mana each season from Urizeni torchbearers for the Magpies if its conditions are met.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the Printers Guild of Tassato is named as one of the Empire's foremost publishing houses and the more successful rival of the Holberg Historical Press.

Two minutes.d: Celestial Arch emissaries spent three months with the Tchemetzi family in Pelabuhan. The family offered two vital honey a season for the ritual text of Regrow the Land's Heart, and said they would endorse the Conclave to Ossegrahn if it were given. The Arshlan family provided nine wains of mithril for endowment. The Quiet Hall in Oakways became a hospital for magical ailments, and could be expanded by commission. The Shuttered Lantern destroyed the vis-bleeding rock of ice in Tanikipari, rejecting Blood-on-the-Snow's boons. Sadogua thanked the Conclave. With Navarr guides and the Loyalty Assembly, the Suranni wizards began to find homes across most of the Empire.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Assembly sent Exarch Luke to urge wayfarers and magisters to welcome the Suranni. Most refugees rejected these overtures, but Highborn patience has begun to ease their fear, though none will settle in Highguard.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are listed among the three nations where the Suranni wizards will not settle.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tchemetzi see Regrow the Land's Heart as useful for Faraden lands ravaged by war with the Jotun.

Navarr.t: Navarr guides sent under Teleri Thornweaver's mandate took in most of the Suranni wizards and found them homes. The Assembly's statement urging conversion to the Way led some stridings and steadings to turn families away until the Loyalty Assembly's backing won them round.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grandmaster of the Golden Pyramid set the order to support the Crucible of Fate in Zenith.

Wintermark.t: Shuttered Lantern magicians, miners and runesmiths broke apart and boiled away the vis-bleeding rock of ice in Tanikipari. The Celestial Arch's gifts to the Tchemetzi included a wand inscribed by the runesmiths of Kalpaheim.

Two minutes.o: In the wake of the Spring Equinox 385YE, several Conclave declarations took effect. A Celestial Arch delegation won goodwill with Faraden magician families, the Quiet Hall was endowed on the Custodian of the Lost, the bleeding ice rock in Tanikipari was destroyed, and the Suranni wizards began settling in the Empire.

Miaren/Oakways.t: The Quiet Hall in Oakways now serves as a hospital for magical maladies. It could be expanded with apothecary gardens for 10 weirwood, 20 crowns and three months' work, yielding Magpie and Ravenwing Infusions each season.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: In a secluded Tanikipari valley, miners hired by the Shuttered Lantern broke the bleeding ice boulder into rubble and boiled it to steam, with no sign of any trap or wrath from Agramant.

Zenith/Lustri.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes Golden Pyramid support for the Crucible of Fate in Zenith but does not name Lustri directly.

Miaren.t: The former wayhouse of Harad of the High Path in Miaren became the Quiet Hall, a hospital for those harmed by magic, under the Custodian of the Lost.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Celestial Arch delegation endured a freezing, storm-beset crossing of the Sea of Snow to reach Pelabuhan.

Sermersuaq.t: The rock of bleeding ice in Sermersuaq was destroyed, ending a source of Heart's Blood tied to Blood-on-the-Snow.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Shuttered Lantern's recent investigations in Skarsind are what led them to the bleeding ice rock.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Pyramid has been set to support the Crucible of Fate in Zenith.

Two silhouettes.d: The first battle option targeted Sarra Grubfeast, the brutal Druj governor of Dawnguard, at the de Challon Estate. Its objectives were to kill her, capture the declared sorcerer Renee du Loire, and deal with the Venom Weavers coven and tortured fallen knights. The second, via the Sentinel Gate to Bitterhead near The Fangs, aimed to rescue surviving Rahvin orcs, ideally without Dawnish diplomats, and to threaten a summer regio. Three conjunctions were also offered. One would stop the Bone Serpent clan bringing a herald to destroy the Palace of Orieb. Another would halt the Burnt Fist coven heading for the weirwood of the Eaves of Peytaht. A third would stop Garsnag Mudchurner slaughtering Dawnish partisans.

Dawn.t: Dawnish yeofolk in Dawnguard suffered under Sarra Grubfeast, and killing her would lift Dawnish morale and remove the risk of the region being sacked. The Rahvin hated the Dawnish, so Dawn could fight at Bitterhead but should not join any talks with them.

Druj.t: The Druj were offered as targets on several fronts: Grubfeast and her council, the Bitterhead mithril workings and their Rahvin slaves, and the Bone Serpent, Screaming Wasp and Garsnag Mudchurner forces.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj burning of spires and slaughter of their occupants in Zenith was cited as an example of Druj despoiling.

Varushka.t: Scouts of the Northern Eagle spotted the Bone Serpent clan escorting the Sleepless Nightmare towards the Palace of Orieb. Responsibility for the conjunction fell to the Apothecary of Orieb, Nikolai Desovich Patazca, unless the Varushkan Senators appointed a successor first.

Two silhouettes.o: At the Winter Solstice 384YE, prognosticators identified two Saturday-morning opportunities for Imperial heroes to strike into the Barrens, with the Military Council to choose between them, alongside three smaller conjunctions against Druj forces.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: If the Bone Serpent group crossed the border into Drownbark Forest, it would be lost to Imperial eyes and the Palace of Orieb would fall.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: Imperial armies were pressing into Bitter Strand, where heroes could strike at Bitterhead by The Fangs to free the Rahvin from a woodland stockade near the Druj mithril mine and threaten a summer regio.

The Barrens/Farweald.t: The Bone Serpent clan's elite warriors and Vikari were escorting the Sleepless Nightmare through Farweald towards the Ossium border.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: The Burnt Fist coven was heading for the Eaves of Peytaht to enchant weirwood workers. Stopping it would hamper Druj harvesting for at least a season and let scouts recover wains of weirwood.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: Recently conquered as part of the Iron Causeway, Hope's Rest was where a coven holding the Bitterhead regio could summon one of Cathan Canaes's Frozen Citadels.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Murderdale had no significant Druj military presence, but Garsnag Mudchurner's clan was retreating towards the lands of House de Percy to slaughter its partisans.

Astolat.t: Elation in Astolat over the Steel Causeway risked turning to frustration as news of Dawnguard's suffering spread, and killing Grubfeast would quiet the most impatient voices.

Ossium.t: The Bone Serpent clan, driven from Ossium almost two years earlier, was moving towards its border with a herald able to destroy the Palace of Orieb.

Semmerholm.t: Public mood in Semmerholm risked souring over the plight of Dawnguard's people, and a strike on Grubfeast would help consolidate support for the Imperial strategy.

The Barrens.t: The territory was split by the Iron Causeway, and every option on the page lay here: the Dawnguard governor, the Bitterhead mine and Rahvin, the Peytaht weirwood and the Murderdale partisans.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater's joy at the Steel Causeway victory risked becoming frustration at the brutal conditions in Dawnguard, which killing the governor would help ease.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as where the Druj burned spires and slaughtered their occupants simply to damage the Empire.

Two steps on the water.d: The Free Folk, guests of the House of the Proffered Hand, work across the Empire, especially in the Marches, and venerate statues of a 'Divine Family' including unknown figures such as Truthful Alexio and Tajlora the Wise. Conservative priests call this idolatry and heresy; the Synod was asked for statements of principle, particularly in the Assembly of the Nine, General Assembly or Dawnish assembly. Hostile judgements would likely lead them to seek homes elsewhere rather than to violence. Meanwhile the Marracossans, led in negotiations by Leonorada Rousseau, proposed that the Senate cede Trajadoz in return for a Bourse-appointed Marracossa Sendito with a ministry selling unique talismans. Legate Glaucia Herminia planned to visit Anvil to speak with the Ambassador to Asavea.

Dawn.t: Dawn hosts the Free Folk in Astolat; yeofolk largely see them as 'a little weird', but the Dawnish national assembly was named as a suitable place for a statement of principle on whether their faith should be tolerated.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Pakt of the Imperial Orcs was noted as the incumbent Ambassador to Asavea whom the Marracossan Legate hoped to meet.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: visiting Free Folk mistook the statues at the House of Barbs in Hercynia for unknown exemplars.

The Brass Coast.t: The Marracossans live as foreigners in Madruga, employing Freeborn labourers and clashing with Freeborn honesty through their habits of discreet bribery; they asked that the Marracossa Sendito be appointed via the Bourse, possibly as a Freeborn national position.

The Marches.t: Many Free Folk worked as fair-waged labourers in the Marches, and planned to visit the Marches camp at Anvil to share delicacies with 'the distant cousins of our distant cousins'.

Two steps on the water.o: Two groups of Asavean refugees sought to settle in the Empire in Summer 384YE: the Free Folk, former slaves living in Astolat whose unorthodox veneration of 'Divines' drew accusations of idolatry, and the Marracossans, exiled rebels at Trajadoz in Madruga who asked the Senate to cede the town to them.

Madruga/Torres.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named directly, though the Marracossans' settlement at Trajadoz lies in northern Madruga.

Astolat.t: The Free Folk have begun building homes in Astolat, where local troubadours and faithful sought clarity on how to treat them amid fears of 'another Whittle'.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Free Folk visiting the House of Barbs in Hercynia were confused, taking its statues for images of unknown exemplars.

Madruga.t: The Marracossans resettled the abandoned town of Trajadoz in northern Madruga, restoring farms and workshops, and requested that the Senate cede it to them.

Mitwold.t: Many Free Folk travelled to Mitwold seeking farm and outdoor labour, sharing stories and their faith after work.

Upwold.t: Free Folk visited Upwold in numbers to work fields, orchards and building projects for a fair wage.

Two suns in the sunset.d: Sufyan i Zuhri i Guerra's Loyalty mandate turned the war with the Plenum into one of survival. Three potential allies were found: the poor, martial satrapy of Ibaria, which could raise up to three armies if supplied with mithril; the reactionary Children of Asav, who would need at least 75 thrones a season; and the Lost Weepers, a dark cult wanting curse ritual texts and mana. After a League Assembly judgement, the incoming Regario Dossier could redirect spies to Asavea, but only at this summit. Donations to anchor the Way have reached 47 thrones and 14 wains of white granite but have stalled because people are confused by competing appeals. At Zemeh the Asaveans were driven off, the blockade was broken, and Sumaah pledged a dose of true liao each season.

Dawn.t: Dawnish captains such as Ursiel, Edmund Reaver and Seraphine De Sarroi took their fleets to Sumaah and fought in the victory that saved Zemeh.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the final defeat of the Druj is listed as one of several competing Imperial goals dividing public support.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Asavean forces are said to dwarf the Grendel's, and the Plenum's warships are expected to keep bolstering the Grendel.

Highguard.t: Highguard captains including Shibboleth of Tziporah's Chase and Accalon fought at Zemeh. Highguard's benefactors letting their council direct their resources is cited as an example of how future support might be organised.

Imperial Orcs.t: The orc captains Urq and Tamazi Kardak were among the fleets that fought alongside the Frieøyer to defend Zemeh.

Navarr.t: Navarr captains such as Owain Farkas and Garr helped break the Asavean assault. Navarr's call to destroy the vallorn is one of the rival appeals competing for the Empire's support.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn sent the largest contingent of captains to defend Zemeh and are helping smuggle missionaries and resources into Asavea.

The League.t: Rafael Barossa's League Assembly judgement led to the chance for the new Regario Dossier to redirect spies to Asavea. Ibarian rebel refugees are believed to have settled in the League, and League captains fought at Zemeh.

The Marches.t: Marcher captains such as Misha Kemi and Thaddeus Grimm sailed to Zemeh, where cries of "A marcher!" rang out during the battle.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark sent one of the largest contingents of fleet captains, including Bron Mordssen and Káre Markusdottir, to the successful defence of Zemeh.

Two suns in the sunset.o: In Spring 387YE the Loyalty Assembly's call to overthrow the Asavean Plenum identified three possible rebel groups, while efforts to anchor the Way in Asavea stalled amid public weariness. Nearly a hundred Imperial fleets joined the Frieøyer to defend the Sumaah city of Zemeh and forced five Asavean navies to retreat.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: some captains feared the Asavean fleet might instead strike the Necropolis while they waited at Sumaah.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is named as a feared alternative Asavean target, and several captains bearing the name di Sarvos fought at Zemeh.

Unable to see.d: At the Summer Solstice 381YE the General Assembly condemned Yael for preaching the rejected doctrine of The Beyond, and the magistrates executed her when she refused clemency. The Highborn Assembly had earlier endorsed her as the First Empress Reborn, so Highborn grief was marked more by sorrow than by rage. The schism worsened, and penalties on Highborn armies fighting alongside other forces rose to 60% for military units and 25% for armies. Two paths were offered: a Highborn mandate to disavow Yael, or a General Assembly change of doctrine accepting the Land Without Tears, backed by a mandate to embrace it. The Highborn Assembly supported Melchior of Adina's Charge's conciliatory mandate, and with 250 liao he set out to return Highguard to orthodoxy.

Highguard.t: Highguard grieved its executed daughter and saw its armies suffer growing penalties when fighting beside other nations, until its Assembly chose Melchior's mandate to turn the nation back from Yael's teachings towards orthodoxy.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr Assembly is cited as having utterly rejected Yael's claim to be the First Empress reborn.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Marches are not named directly, and the only nearby reference is to the troubled situation in the Mournwold, used as a comparison.

Unable to see.o: After the Imperial Synod condemned Yael of Highguard, who claimed to be the First Empress reborn, for heresy and she was executed, Highguard mourned her. The nation stood doctrinally at odds with the rest of the Empire until the Highborn Assembly backed a mandate to return its people to orthodoxy.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the out-of-character notes compare the Yael schism to the similarly complex and strife-filled situation in the Mournwold.

Under eastern skies.d: The Black Thorns, Iron Helms, Golden Sun and Isaella's Dance advanced into Eastring and found themselves outnumbered and caught in a Druj ward. The vengeful Black Wind led a merciless onslaught. Isaella's Dance gave their lives to break the ward, then the Iron Helms, aided by Winter spirits and their own risen dead, cut a path north into the Bleaks. Some twelve and a half thousand Imperial soldiers were lost and both armies disbanded. The Druj hold Eastring and East Ashes, and Therunin stays uncontrolled. Opportunities followed: binding the undead Helms, recovering lost regalia, and making a corpse glade at Isaella's Fall.

Dawn.t: The Golden Sun lost about a thousand soldiers, and Eleonaris' knights died fighting beside them. The Druj offered to enslave surrendering Dawnish, and Lady Laudine du Lac was asked to lead questing knights against Druj traders in the Salt Flats.

Druj.t: The Druj sprang their trap, destroyed two Imperial armies and recaptured Eastring, though they surely lost thousands to the furious Varushkans. The Tainted Basilisk has left Therunin, which denies them large-scale rituals there.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a quoted Prosperity Assembly judgement names the Grendel among raiders stealing the Empire's prosperity.

Navarr.t: Isaella's Dance was wiped out and around two thousand Black Thorns died. The nation is offered the chance to recover the Knife of Thorns standard and to braid its dead with the Great Forest Orcs in a corpse glade at Isaella's Fall.

The League.t: The Towerjacks had fortified Peakedge Song before leaving to help defend Redoubt. Their weakened defences remain until the Spring Equinox.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks and Northern Eagle marched south into Urizen to aid the defence of Redoubt.

Varushka.t: The Iron Helms were destroyed and the Northern Eagle lost some two hundred in the Lower Tarn Valley. Varushka may bind the risen Helms with a hearth rite at the Stained Rock, or recover the Barrow Axe to bargain with a sovereign.

Under eastern skies.o: In Winter 386YE an Imperial push to drive the Druj from Therunin walked into a Spring-warded trap in Eastring. Isaella's Dance and the Iron Helms were destroyed covering the escape of the surviving armies into the Barrens, and the Druj retook Eastring.

Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire.t: The Varnalis, a Druj family of Grimfen Mire, were expecting a weirwood shipment that wagon raiders planned to seize after killing its guards.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj homestead targeted by raiders lies just across the border from Drownbark Forest.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Beladrarsh.t: The Skinweavers of Beladrarsh host the Dripping Market, the destination of the Druj traders the Dawnish knights were hunting.

Sarangrave/Kroll.t: Mentioned in passing: the Krollthorned coven likely serves a ghulai allied to the Palace of the Sleepers in northern Kroll.

Therunin/East Ashes.t: The Druj still hold East Ashes, giving them both shores of the Feverwater, and protect it with a malign Spring ward. A captured Great Forest Orc treetender was being forced to work rafts on the Feverwater's edge.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Eastring was the killing ground where a Druj ward trapped the Imperial armies, and the Druj recaptured it. The risen dead of the Iron Helms now roam its marshes, and Isaella's Fall lies here.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: Mentioned in passing: Greenheart remains under the control of the vallorn.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: Still held by the Navarr, the valley lies poisoned by the Sephals Cauldron, worsened by the Druj curse. Some two hundred Northern Eagle soldiers died crossing it, and the trapped armies dared not retreat through it.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Still held by the Navarr, Peakedge Song kept the Towerjacks' fortifications around its hospital. Displaced Navarr and Great Forest Orcs gathered at Peakedge Stead.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: Mentioned in passing: Sweetglades remains under the control of the vallorn.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Isaella's Dance had recuperated in Astolat the previous season before marching to Therunin.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, a painless death for Imperial citizens held by the Druj, extends into Brocéliande.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Wagon raiders asked Champion of Prosperity Hugh Farrier to kill Druj guards so they could loot a weirwood shipment. Success would reward him with four wains of weirwood and encourage further raids.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: the Malinov family of Karsk holds the artefact axe Hunger and refused to return it to the Iron Helms.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Varnalis homestead targeted by wagon raiders lies just across the border from Ossium's Drownbark Forest.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks and Northern Eagle left Therunin to aid Redoubt's defence.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Dawnish questing knights tracked Druj carrying goods to the Dripping Market and asked Lady Laudine du Lac to kill them and claim their wares.

Sarangrave.t: A coven of human Winter ritualists from eastern Sarangrave, the Krollthorned, was aiding the Druj. If Varushka binds the dead Iron Helms, they could be sent to ravage Sarangrave and prevent Druj resupply there.

Therunin.t: Imperial forces lost some twelve and a half thousand soldiers here, and Isaella's Dance and the Iron Helms were destroyed. The Druj retook Eastring and the territory remains uncontrolled, with a Spring curse fouling the land and the undead Helms roaming its marshes.

Under heaven.d: Hundreds of Imperial champions landed in Greenwall, overwhelmed Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard and burnt his hall, then raided Iron Stand, Ulfrsmoor and Eyrarfell. They sacked the Broken Chasm quarry and Ulfrshal, and looted mines, the Shining Caverns' supply lines and Steelweaver's Crucible. Thralls and ancestral sites were deliberately spared. At sea, fleets harried Jotun boats, struck Kierheim's docks and tore down defences along the Kongegőr, with the hylje's hostile 'cousins', the people of the salt, appearing in the fighting. The Jotun cannot resupply or raise armies until Spring 385YE. Greenwall is easier to capture, and the Kongegőr's damage hampers Jotun army movement. Furious northern Jarls promise an answer.

Dawn.t: Dawnish knights and yeofolk led the daring assault on the Broken Chasm quarry, which was at first repulsed before the raiders overran its defenders and looted its white granite.

Grendel.t: Half a dozen Grendel trading ships at Kierheim declared their neutrality, refused to fight alongside the Jotun and watched the battle on the docks, ready to flee.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: seven Highborn citizens are listed among the raid's participants.

Imperial Orcs.t: A warband of Imperial Orcs struck down Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard of Greenwall, and the orc Ergot was thanked for blazing the trail in the earlier raid.

Jotun.t: The Jotun lost great wealth from Skallahn's mines, forges and quarries, saw Kierheim's docks raided and the Kongegőr badly damaged, and cannot resupply or raise new armies until Spring 385YE. Their northern Jarls are furious and vow an answer.

Navarr.t: Navarr raiders took part in the raid, and Navarr scouts who approached the Shining Caverns reported that its garrison had been swollen by troops from Tromsa.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: three Freeborn citizens are listed as participants, and a Freeborn corsair remarked that overladen ships were a good problem to have.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: fourteen League citizens are listed among the raid's participants.

The Marches.t: Marchers gathered at Odd's End and supplied the raid leader, Orrick of House Bolholt, and Marcher captains led attacks on the Kongegőr. The raid's success lets Steward's Landing become a permanent staging post for Marcher captains raiding the Kalsea coast.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: a navigable passage through the Sea of Snow might allow a few ships to reach the coast of Otkodov, held by Thule.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: two Urizen citizens are listed among the raid's participants.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: three Varushkan citizens are listed among the raid's participants.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk gathered at Westerhal alongside hylje guides, made up a large share of the raiders and led attacks on the Kongegőr. Westerhal's fisherfolk may now fish the Gullet under Wintermark fleet escort.

Under heaven.o: In Summer 384YE a large Imperial raid led by Orrick of House Bolholt struck Skallahn from Odd's End and Westerhal, looting mines, forges and quarries while Imperial fleets dominated the Gullet, raided Kierheim's docks and wrecked the Kongegőr land bridge.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: Westerhal in the West Marsh launched Winterfolk vessels for the raid and offered a retreat route across the shallow straits, and may now become a thriving escorted fishing port.

Skallahn/Bjarkey.t: Bjarkey was among the coastal targets the raiding ships planned to strike as Imperial fleets harried Jotun boats and shore settlements along the Skallahn coast.

Skallahn/Eyrarfell.t: Raiders hit almost all of Eyrarfell's mines despite fierce resistance from Jarl Gilla Sverrisdóttir's ulvenwar, and looted mithril from the caravans and storehouses supplying the Shining Caverns.

Skallahn/Greenwall.t: The raiders landed in Greenwall, overwhelmed Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard's warriors, burnt his hall and attacked its smithies, forges and mines. Imperial armies need one fewer victory point to capture it until Autumn 385YE.

Skallahn/Iron Stand.t: Winterfolk warbands visited the ruins of Guntherm's Iron Banner but left the town of Overgaard untouched, while Jarl Ebbe sent warriors south to aid the defence of the Broken Chasm.

Skallahn/Ulfrsmoor.t: Raiders fought across Ulfrsmoor, sparing the temple of Ulfrskelf but storming the Broken Chasm quarry and besieging and looting Jarl Alvilda Ottesen's castle at Ulfrshal.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: captains who berth on the Bay of Catazar crossed the Sea of Snow to the rendezvous, and the Empire's earlier scouting there is cited as a precedent.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the raid leader hoped the raid would help speed Bregasland's return to Imperial hands.

Hordalant.t: Imperial captains braved Hordalant's northern coast, and the Jarls of Hordalant joined the defence of the damaged Kongegőr. Armies crossing between Hordalant and Skallahn must now halt on arrival.

Kallavesa.t: Westerhal in Kallavesa served as a gathering and retreat point for the raid, and its fisherfolk may now bring prosperity to western Kallavesa by fishing the Gullet.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is named as one of the rendezvous points through which Imperial ships passed on the way to the raid.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: cartographers believe a passage through the Sea of Snow's ice might let a few ships reach the coast of Otkodov.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: several of the League raiders listed bear names of Sarvos.

Sea of Snow.t: Some Imperial captains pushed past the Kongegőr into the icy Sea of Snow, where the people of the salt seemed at home and cautious, unfamiliar orc warships scouted the Imperial fleets before fleeing.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the raid leader hoped to speed Sermersuaq's return to Imperial hands, and the hylje who joined the raid were dressed in the Suaq style.

Skallahn.t: Skallahn was ravaged across Greenwall, Iron Stand, Ulfrsmoor and Eyrarfell and its coast harried, leaving the Jotun unable to resupply or raise armies there until Spring 385YE. Greenwall is easier to capture, and the Jarl of Kierheim cannot move against the Imperial spy network before Winter 384YE.

Tromsa.t: The Jarl of Tromsa and his allies sent several hundred troops south to reinforce the Shining Caverns and Steelweaver's Crucible against the raiders.

Under the firelight.d: At Wyndyn Path in Liath's Ring, the Bronze Harvesters of Shikal were clearing forest. If their Bronze Titan were not destroyed, the region would lose its forested quality and up to four Jotun armies would gain resupply. The Mourn traitor Dalton Royse had fled there, leaving Green March under threat while he lived. Five Feni trapped behind Jotun lines might be rescued in return for aid against Liath's Ring. At Hvalgrunn, Idunn Ironjaw carried the Bear Who Swims' banner while Jotun searched for three storied swords, Skofnung, Angrvurdr and Hofnd, amid Night heralds of Janon and a restless ghost. In Sermersuaq, Freydis led a raid on the mithril mine.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orcs who had fought alongside Janon's heralds could draw an extra hero point at Hvalgrunn. They might also earn a boon from the Shadowed Flame's heralds by recounting their exploits.

Jotun.t: The Jotun worked on several fronts: settling cleared Liathaven forest with Estavus' aid, raiding Hvalgrunn to show off the Bear Who Swims' banner and recover three blades to empower their generals, and sending Freydis against the Pride of Ikka's Tears.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn who had fought alongside Janon's heralds could use an extra hero point at Hvalgrunn and might win a boon from the heralds. Separately, Royse was linked to the earlier attacks on Kahraman's roads.

The Marches.t: A Mourn beater, Dalton Royse, was exposed as Stephen of Sarcombe's informant and fled to Liathaven. While he lived, Green March was left vulnerable to Jotun invasion.

Wintermark.t: Jotun raiders entered the sacred Kallavesi marshes of Hvalgrunn to hunt for lost Suaq-forged swords near a restless ghost. A Jotun warband also targeted the Pride of Ikka's Tears in Sermersuaq.

Under the firelight.o: In Spring 386YE the Military Council was presented with three Jotun-related opportunities: a battle at Wyndyn Path in Liathaven, where Autumn heralds of Estavus were clearing forest for Jotun settlement; a Jotun raid on the sacred marshes of Hvalgrunn in Kallavesa; and a warband raid on the Pride of Ikka's Tears in Sermersuaq.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: Jotun raiders spread across West Marsh into Hvalgrunn, an ancient battleground where Wintermark heroes and Jotun champions alike lie buried.

Liathaven/Liath's Ring.t: Estavus' Bronze Titan and harvesters threatened to strip Liath's Ring of its forested quality. Rescuing the trapped Feni could leave the region under threat from the Empire until Winter 387YE.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: Mentioned in passing: West Ranging was noted as the ashen waste that is the one part of Liathaven not covered by forest.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Green March gained the Under Threat quality while Dalton Royse lived, because he knew its roads, villages and militia defences.

Tromsa/Majastind.t: Mentioned in passing: Mount Majastind was cited as a sacred Jotun site that the orcs assumed was as well protected as Hvalgrunn.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Dalton Royse was said to have played a small part in preparing the attacks on Kahraman's roads.

Kallavesa.t: An elite Jotun raiding force crossed Hvalgrunn, several days south of Rest, carrying the Bear Who Swims' standard and searching for three lost swords. Night heralds of Janon filled the area with a zealous aura.

Liathaven.t: Heralds of Estavus were clearing forest at Wyndyn Path so the Jotun could settle and farm it, while Wither the Seed continued to blight the territory's natural cycle.

Mournwold.t: The exposure of Dalton Royse as a spy for Stephen of Sarcombe left Green March under threat until he was captured or killed.

Sermersuaq.t: Feather'd Rain's raven warned the Olgafsdottirshal garrison that Freydis' warband was coming to raid the Pride of Ikka's Tears. Its incumbent, Tuija Dunning, was made responsible for defeating them.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: Freydis' warband set out from Tromsa and would return there hailed as heroes if its raid succeeded.

Under the red sky.d: Syrus Skybreaker's second missive to Tharim brought the herald Shakle, who confirmed a formal parley with The Three at midnight on the Friday. Tharim wished to discuss forging chains to take on part of his curse. Skathe wished to discuss fashion, and Surut asked for a formal representative of Imperatrix Lisabetta. Llofir declined parley but promised messenger heralds. Roshanwe announced that 'The Mariner' would come to discuss the Symposium. Lashonar accepted a challenge of music and song for the Winter Solstice and returned an unopened note to Murit. Barien said the Summer nobles had accepted a tournament for patronage of the Icy Crag, to be held no earlier than Autumn, and that the icy winds over Volchitrava had stopped.

Varushka.t: The icy winds that had been damaging the Varushkan vale of Volchitrava stopped, with no current sign of Cathan Canae's anger, though Cathan Canae is among the Summer eternals sending heralds to find champions.

Under the red sky.o: In Summer 381YE, five eternals answered the Spring Equinox plenipotentiary missives from the Imperial archmages with open, formal responses, arranging parleys, meetings and herald visits for the Summer Solstice. The most prominent was the Thrice-cursed Court, which agreed to a full formal parley.

Miekarova/Srodkoja.t: The vale of Volchitrava gained relief as the icy winds tied to Cathan Canae's anger stopped blowing.

Miekarova.t: The damaging icy winds over the vale of Volchitrava ceased this season, and Cathan Canae's anger showed no sign of returning for the moment.

Underwater sunshine.d: Kostjyas Respite, built under an Imperial Wayleave, raised taxation by 5 thrones a season in every Imperial territory bordering the Semmerlak except Holberg, where the Sand Fishers hold Misericorde. Civil servants are drawing up proposals for further ports. Dho'uala's tithe brought disappearances, including all aboard the Dawnish ship Lady Celementine, and gave Dawnish, Varushkan and Holberg fleets a production penalty. Cerulean Mazzarine and ilium prices rose. Monstrous beavers tried to dam rivers in Ossium and Semmerholm but were defeated. Dreams at the Maze of Zoriah warned that something tied to the Semmerlak would happen at Anvil during the Hour of Smoke.

Dawn.t: Dawnish lake shores share in the port's economic boom, but Dawnish fleets suffer Dho'uala's tithe, cursed flotsam has harmed beachcombers, and the Lady Celementine was found emptied of every soul aboard.

The League.t: Holberg gains nothing from the new port's trade because the Sand Fishers control Misericorde, yet its fleets still suffer the production penalty and its sailors are among the vanished.

Varushka.t: Varushka completed both the Iron Roads and Kostjyas Respite, but its fleets and lakeside ministries now suffer from Dho'uala's wrath, and its heroes fought off beaver horrors in Ossium.

Underwater sunshine.o: In Spring 385YE the new Varushkan port of Kostjyas Respite opened on the Semmerlak, boosting taxation in the surrounding Imperial territories except Holberg. At the same time the lake sovereign Dho'uala stirred, and people and cargo began vanishing from the lake.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Sand Fisher control of Misericorde keeps Holberg from the new trade; a Sand Fisher raft vanished, leaving only a splintered spearhead on its beach, and a dock here is a possibility.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Mentioned in passing: Utterlund is named as a possible site for a new dock to spread Holberg's wealth across the Semmerlak.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Since the Maze of Zoriah in Mieriada was consecrated with true liao, its pilgrims have had lucid dreams of speaking animals warning of Dho'uala and the Hour of Smoke.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: Bittershore is no longer under-developed now that Kostjyas Respite's docks are open, and its first Merchant Boyar is due to be appointed at the Spring Equinox.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: Mentioned in passing: the Drownbark Forest's marshes were at risk of damage had the beaver horrors' dam on the Lanit River not been stopped.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: Varushkan heroes stopped beaver horrors damming the Lanit River in Nearweald, and the vanished Lady Celementine was carrying spear-tips for the fortified barracks there.

Weirwater/Sandling.t: Mentioned in passing: Sandling is not named, but it is tied to Weirwater's Semmerlak shoreline, where cursed objects washed ashore and the tax boom applies.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the lost Lady Celementine was carrying Dawnish silk, wine and bread from Astolat.

Holberg.t: Holberg is the one lakeside territory without a tax increase, though a dock in Misericorde or Utterlund might be possible, and its traders and treasure hunters have fallen victim to the lake's disappearances.

Karov.t: Karov's taxation rises by 5 thrones a season and civil servants are preparing proposals to improve it, but the Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak faces less available ilium at a higher price.

Karsk.t: Karsk gains the 5-throne tax increase and is included in the civil service's prosperity proposals, while the Ketsov Mir Mozga shrug off the lake's troubles and their deals are unaffected.

Miekarova.t: Pilgrims at the Maze of Zoriah in Miekarova have dreamt of weasels and otters warning that Dho'uala is roused and something will happen at Anvil.

Ossium.t: Ossium is now home to Kostjyas Respite, which ends its extra building costs, and its flooding has subsided after Varushkan heroes destroyed beaver horrors damming the Lanit River.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm's taxation rises and proposals to improve it are under way, but cursed objects have washed up on its beaches and beaver horrors flooded the land near Semmer's Rose until House Tamerlaine's knights destroyed them.

The Semmerlak.t: The sovereign Dho'uala has stirred in the depths, bringing strange lights, torn nets, stolen cargo and vanished sailors to the lake's waters.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater gains the 5-throne tax increase and is included in the port proposals, though cursed objects have washed up on its beaches and weirwood traders may prefer the road past Sentinel's Folly to the lake.

United in law.d: Delivered through the Throne's power to address the Empire, Lisabetta reminded citizens that their oath binds them to support the law, and that Clemency requires other legal avenues to be pursued first. She mourned Senator Gant Archama of Temeschwar, who died defending Zenith against the Druj, and condemned the murder of Senator Lady Jocelyn Cordraco and the lawless killing and execution that followed. She pledged greater support for the citizen Militia, praising Nadia Borodina di Sarvos. Following League tradition, she announced she would seek a spouse, negotiated by Benedict Pacelli von Holberg. Finally, with the Mournwold reclaimed, she granted Sarcombe an Imperial Charter to encourage rebuilding and trade.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the address names the "reviled Druj" as the enemy against whom Senator Gant Archama died defending Zenith.

The League.t: The Imperatrix invoked League tradition of marrying at the height of one's power, entrusting her marriage negotiations to the Master of Hearts of the House of Seven Mirrors, and mourned Senator Gant Archama of Temeschwar.

The Marches.t: With the Mournwold reclaimed, the Throne granted an Imperial Charter to Sarcombe, seeking to restore trade between the people of the Mourn and the rest of the Empire.

United in law.o: Imperatrix Lisabetta von Holberg addressed the whole Empire, urging citizens to honour their oath to support Imperial law, announcing her intention to seek a spouse through the House of Seven Mirrors, and granting an Imperial Charter to the market town of Sarcombe in Southmoor.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: Sarcombe in Southmoor, already legally restored as a market town by the Senate, received an Imperial Charter to encourage further rebuilding and prosperous trade.

Mournwold.t: The address celebrated the reclamation of the Mournwold and the chance to restore its commerce with the wider Empire through Sarcombe's charter.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Senator Gant Archama of Temeschwar was honoured for giving his life defending Zenith at the Winter 381YE summit.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperatrix grieved the failed defence of Zenith against the Druj, in which Senator Gant Archama and many others died.

Unleashing the storm.d: Two maimed former gladiators freed at Dubhtraig, and an Axou captain forced into Siroc by dolphins, revealed that Beoraidh's coliseum holds hundreds of slaves, trains Grendel armies and is guarded by a white granite fortification one season from completion. The eternal Rhianos, invited by the Archmage of Summer, admitted arranging both encounters and eased Golden Voyage for captains sworn to attack Beoraidh. The civil service warned there was little loot to take, but that equal numbers of fleets and soldiers could free up to 2,000 or more slaves, wreck the fortification and destroy the arena. Enough freed fighters could let the Imperial Orcs raise a third army. The outcome was left to the Spring Equinox.

Grendel.t: The Grendel faced a possible raid on Beoraidh that could free thousands of their slaves, destroy their unfinished fortification and coliseum, and hamper the army recruitment they badly need after the Black Plateau. The page also reports rumours that Salt Lady Suriad fell in the Dubhtraig raid.

Imperial Orcs.t: If enough freed gladiators and recruits joined the nation, the Imperial Orcs could raise a third army, provided they secured a second suitable territory. Even fewer recruits would help them replace losses, and the Winter Sun's general could encourage soldiers to go reaving in support of the raid.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn corsairs uncovered the Axou captain's story, and Freeborn paradors buzzed with brawls over whether the Dubhtraig raid surpassed Erigo's attack on Trivento. Freeborn captains also stood to benefit from Rhianos's help with Golden Voyage.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orc army the Winter Sun was stationed far away in Wintermark's Sermersuaq.

Unleashing the storm.o: After the sack of Dubhtraig, Queen Rhianos, Regent of the Eternal Sea, steered the Empire towards a raid on Beoraidh in Grendel-held Mareave, where a great coliseum serves as a slave market and army training ground. During the Winter Solstice the Quartermaster General declared that fleets and military units joining the raid would share in the Imperial Guerdon.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Beoraidh, a poor port sliding into the sea, held a coliseum, slave camps and a half-built white granite fortress. A raid here could free up to 2,000 or more slaves and destroy both structures, though it promised little wealth.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: freed slaves are expected to want a life as far from the Bay of Catazar as they can get.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the Axou captain who confirmed the gladiators' story put in at Siroc after dolphins damaged his ship.

Mareave.t: Mareave became the proposed raid target. A successful attack would damage its economy, including the mithril pits at Fundindelf, for at least a year, and destroying the coliseum would stop the Grendel raising an army in the territory.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun was stationed here, and its general could encourage soldiers to support the raid if the army stayed on the defensive.

Spiral.t: Mareave lies south of Spiral, and the civil service warned that a completed Beoraidh fortification would free Grendel armies to attack the Empire in Spiral sooner.

Unlock thy hidden gate.d: The Golden Axe, supported by the Crimson Schlacta, led the invasion. The Towerjacks and Winter Sun advanced cautiously and tried to reach the subject septs. The Citadel Guard were protected by Winter's Mantle, with their injuries passed to their allies. A Night magic ward, the Druj miasma, the Tower of the Skink garrison and three recuperating Druj armies slowed progress. Tabun nevertheless fell. Around a thousand Imperial soldiers and nearly twice as many Druj died. Lahkev could fall by Summer if nothing changes. Terrified slaves and septs shunned the Empire. Scouts found the Mirelith. Heroes could link it to the trods with Dance of Navarr and Thorn, or destroy its stones to unleash the vallorn on Bloodwater.

Druj.t: The Druj lost Tabun and much of the Bloodwater Marsh, with nearly two thousand dead, though their armies and the Tower of the Skink garrison were still fighting a war of attrition. They now face the possibility that the Empire might unleash the Bendol vallorn on their lands.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: veterans who once fought in Reikos recognised the familiar Druj miasma.

Imperial Orcs.t: Imperial Orc soldiers took part in the combined campaign, and the cautious Winter Sun helped spot and break the Hidden Snake ambush at Tabun. Attempts to win over the septs and the Bloodwater Spears proved fruitless.

Navarr.t: The Mirelith offered a chance to use Dance of Navarr and Thorn to bind the Terunael stones into the trod network. This would make the trods effectively unbreakable and leave only Cavan and the severed Therunin trod still to reconnect.

Urizen.t: The Citadel Guard marched through Lustri under Winter's Mantle and escaped bodily harm at their allies' expense. Memories of their curses on the Salt Flats of Sanath made the slaves of the Sarangrave fear the Empire.

Varushka.t: The Golden Axe, alongside the Crimson Schlacta, spearheaded the invasion, lived off the land and stormed Tabun. Without its order to take the land, the Empire would likely have made little headway.

Unlock thy hidden gate.o: In Spring 387YE four Imperial armies marched from Lustri into the Sarangrave, defeated the Druj at the Battle of Tabun and came a little over halfway to securing a beachhead in the Bloodwater Marsh. The advance also revealed the Mirelith, a Terunael ward holding back the Bendol vallorn, which created a battle opportunity.

Salt Flats of Sanath/Sydathian Fens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard's curses during their earlier invasion of the Sydathian Fens fuelled the slaves' fear of the Empire.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: The vallorn heart here is held in check by the Mirelith on its border, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction would take heroes to Mirereach on the Spring Equinox. It currently makes the region impassable to armies.

Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh.t: Imperial forces broke through the Night ward and the miasma and captured Tabun, and are pushing toward Lahkev with full control projected by Summer if nothing changes. Destroying the Mirelith stones could see the region swallowed by the vallorn.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: If all three Mirelith stones were destroyed, the Druj would have to pull armies back to save Nesustak Forest, and the Grynbor there would risk being wiped out.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: The Tower of the Skink, a massive fortification in Thornfen, sent its garrison to resist the invasion and fought at Tabun, delaying the Imperial conquest.

Sarangrave/Whisperwood.t: Whisperwood is the only onward route east once Bloodwater is taken, but a vallorn breach could block the path from Lustri and force the Druj to defend it.

Zenith/Lustri.t: The four armies marched north through Lustri's shadowed forests, where soldiers reported strange dreams and shy spirits, and the ground had grown boggy. A vallorn breach could cut Lustri off from the Sarangrave.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Mentioned in passing: the smell of the Sarangrave was likened to the Proceris marshes.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: veterans of Ossium recognised the Druj miasma, and the rich marsh is contrasted with Ossium's harsher land.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the miasma was familiar to those who once fought the Druj in Reikos.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sarangrave's slaves had heard of the terrible curses the Citadel Guard unleashed here, and veterans recognised the miasma.

Sarangrave.t: Imperial armies won a tenuous toehold in the territory, just over halfway to a beachhead, and the Citadel Guard's presence allows Imperial rituals to be cast on it. The Mirelith offers either an unbreakable trod link or a vallorn catastrophe.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: its trod was noted as recently severed, and it would be an alternative route if the vallorn blocked Bloodwater.

Zenith.t: Four Imperial armies marched through Zenith's forests to invade the Sarangrave by the Druj's old invasion route. Unleashing the vallorn could block passage between Zenith and the Sarangrave entirely.

Unmade trove.d: Drusa found between 800 and 900 boxes of finely made mage implements, apparently preserved by a winter ritual. The find raised fresh questions about whether the Unmade Spire had planned to raise an army. The civil service calculated that 150 further mithril could make the Citadel Guard a large army in two seasons rather than a year. Alternatively, the cache could be gifted or sold to another nation, or worked with ilium to enhance the Army of the Citadel. The trove belonged to Urizen and was assigned like a national appointment. In the end Probus provided 25 rings of ilium to use the trove for enchantments after the Autumn Equinox 379YE.

Urizen.t: The trove legally belonged to Urizen, to be assigned by Senate motion or a unanimous decision of its senators. It offered the Citadel Guard faster growth or new enchantments, and was ultimately committed to enchantments with Probus's ilium.

Unmade trove.o: Torchbearer Drusa of Mute Spire found a trove of non-magical battle mage's staffs and armour in a vaulted chamber beneath the ruins of the Unmade Spire in Redoubt. Urizen was offered a choice over how to use it.

Redoubt/Tomari.t: The map places here the discovery of the vaulted chamber beneath the Unmade Spire ruins, where hundreds of boxes of battle mage regalia had been preserved by a winter ritual.

Redoubt.t: The long mystery of the Unmade Spire's ruins in Redoubt deepened when a hidden chamber of preserved mage weapons and armour was uncovered there, prompting new theories about the spire's intentions.

Unspoken words.d: With winter approaching and their numbers more than tripled, the Rahvin agreed to send their negotiator Jannik to Anvil after invitations from the Imperial Orcs and the Dawnish Assembly. Jannik was willing to meet Claude Deeds on neutral ground. The Dawnish Assembly rejected settling the Barrens but called for Dawn to defend its foreigners, and it was suggested that Dawnish generals might bind their armies by oath to protect the Rahvin and Great Forest Orcs. Meanwhile the Lone Path Striding and the Karass scout Canta came to Anvil to warn of new trods and Druj magic in the Untrod Groves. Following talks with the Karass, the senator permitted knights to explore the Groves.

Dawn.t: Dawn's Assembly rejected settling the Barrens but called for its foreigners to be defended, its generals were challenged to swear a binding oath protecting the Rahvin and Great Forest Orcs, and its knights won the chance to explore the Untrod Groves for riches.

Druj.t: A Karass scout detected Druj magic enchanting a new path through the Untrod Groves, while many of the Black Wind had fled into Druj lands and the Rahvin continued to seek escape from the Druj yoke.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest of Peytaht is described as stretching from Broken Ride in Highguard-held Reikos.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc Assembly invited the Rahvin back to Anvil to find a way for them to survive winter, and Jannik declared himself eager to talk with his friends among the Imperial Orcs.

Navarr.t: The Lone Path Striding, travelling through the Untrod Groves on new trods, lost Emyri Lonepath for a day and came to Anvil with the Karass scout Canta to speak with the Barrens senator and interested Navarr; the Navarr oath to defend the Great Forest Orcs was held up as an example.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Varushkans are noted as having slaughtered the last of the Montanians in Hope's Rest, and Ossium is named among the remote places the Lone Path Striding walk.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the far north of Sermersuaq is named among the remote places the Lone Path Striding walk.

Unspoken words.o: Tensions persisted in the Barrens in Autumn 386YE as the Imperial Orcs and Dawnish Assembly reached out to the Rahvin ahead of winter, Dawn's generals were challenged to swear an oath protecting the Barrens orcs, and strange new trods were found through the mysterious Untrod Groves. After negotiations between Senator Aramis du Froste and the Karass, Dawnish knights were able to explore the Groves for their wealth.

Reikos/Broken Ride.t: Mentioned in passing: identified as the starting point of the Great Forest of Peytaht that stretches across the southern Barrens.

The Barrens/Bitter Strand.t: Mentioned in passing: the remaining Black Wind who did not flee are noted as confined to the Bitter Strand, where the vetoed Rahvin treaty would have granted land.

The Barrens/Farweald.t: Mentioned in passing: the Menrothat are said to be desperate to claim Farweald, which is listed among regions Dawn could settle without displacing anyone.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: Mentioned in passing: noted as home of the Great Forest Orcs whom the Navarr have sworn to treat as family.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: Mentioned in passing: noted as emptied after Varushka slaughtered the last Montanians, leaving only the ruins of Dourfell Keep, and as the hills where the Untrod Groves begin.

The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth.t: Mentioned in passing: the Untrod Groves are said to stretch to the very edge of the Plain of Teeth.

The Barrens/The Untrod Groves.t: New trods tainted with Druj magic were found running through the Groves, a Navarr strider went missing there, and after the senator's negotiations with the Karass, Dawnish knights were able to explore the region for iridescent gloaming, beggarwood and dragonbone.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: named in Viviane Knotes' judgement as a Dawnish territory whose loss would be no more acceptable than that of the Barrens.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lone Path Striding intended to return to Miaren, where their journey began, anticipating the end of the fight against the vallorn.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: its far corners are named among the remote places the Lone Path Striding walk.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest of Peytaht is said to stretch from Broken Ride in Reikos across the southern Barrens.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: named in Viviane Knotes' judgement as a Dawnish territory whose loss would be no more acceptable than that of the Barrens.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: its far north is named among the remote places the Lone Path Striding walk.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens remained unsettled and uneasy as the Rahvin faced winter at the Fangs, Dawn debated defending its foreign peoples, and new trods and Druj magic were discovered in the Untrod Groves, which Dawnish knights went on to explore.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: referenced only in further reading about an earlier invasion of Therunin.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: named in Viviane Knotes' judgement as a Dawnish territory whose loss would be no more acceptable than that of the Barrens.

Unwelcome guest.d: Acting on stories of a vallorn encroachment, General Cuth sent the Unconquered scouts attached to the Seventh Wave to investigate. With good information from the Suns of Couros and others, they found the infestation in a burgeoning Spring regio and spent several days mapping its extent. Judging it well within their ability, the general had the army surround the area and attack, with heavily armoured cataphracts cutting through the foliage and the husks within. Imperial magicians then confirmed that no trace of the vallorn remained. Left alone for a decade or two, it might have taken root. Two strange pods were presented to the Conclave. Later vallorn-related troubles in Casinea appeared unconnected to this incident.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: a soldier remarks that the Pillar and the Pegasus are fighting the Druj in Reikos at the time.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Seventh Wave cleared a vallorn infestation from Highguard land at a cost of over ninety casualties, helped by information from the Suns of Couros.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: a cataphract grumbles that the vallorn ought to be the Navarr's problem to deal with, and his comrades mock him for it.

Unwelcome guest.o: In Summer 379YE the Seventh Wave, under General Cuth, located and destroyed a vallorn infestation growing in a Spring regio in Casinea. The army suffered over ninety casualties, and two strange pods found at the site were sent to Anvil for the Conclave.

Casinea.t: A vallorn encroachment in a Spring regio in Casinea was found and wholly destroyed before it could take root. Later vallorn-related problems in the territory appeared to have no link to it.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Pillar and the Pegasus are said to be in Reikos, deep in fighting against the Druj.

Up on Whittle Hill.d: With the Imperial advance in the Mournwold stalled by the Jotun defence, scouts from the army of the Tusks reached Whittle, at the foot of Whittle Hill in Freemoor. After a brief Jotun occupation, the villagers had retaken their land and waited three decades for help. They grudgingly quartered Imperial troops and showed marked hostility to lineaged soldiers, but declared themselves loyal to the Empire and had kept Marcher traditions such as their yearly fayres. With no liao for thirty years, they were eager to reconnect with their faith. They resolved to send representatives to Anvil, hinted at a hidden treasure, possibly a rich vein of ore, that they might sell, and might offer further unspecified support to the liberation.

Jotun.t: Jotun patrols that usually watched the Whittle valley had been called away, and the village proved to be an enclave that had resisted them for thirty years. The villagers wanted to discuss how to drive the Jotun out of Freemoor.

Up on Whittle Hill.o: Imperial patrols probing into Freemoor in the Jotun-held Mournwold made contact with Whittle, a Marcher village that had held out against the Jotun for thirty years, cut off from the rest of the Empire.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: Imperial scouts reached Freemoor and found Whittle still held by its Marcher folk. The villagers offered a possible ore discovery beneath Whittle Hill and planned to send envoys to Anvil to discuss ousting the Jotun from the region.

Mournwold.t: Although the Imperial campaign to liberate the Mournwold had stalled against the Jotun defence, contact with Whittle opened a possible new source of support and a sign of Marcher resilience within the Jotun-held territory.

Upgrade Grimhold.d: The upgrade cost 70 wains of white granite and 210 crowns, with standard costs applying and twelve months needed to complete the work. Contributions were made over the following year. Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad, Keir Amourd (two gifts of 25 wains) and Blazh Zbignev together supplied the granite, and Blazh Zbignev also gave 24 thrones and 2 crowns. Smaller sums came from Triska Markova, Rhys Nighthaven and Pjesmina Zbirka, with the last donations recorded after the Spring Equinox 388YE. Once complete, the Grimhold will be a rank 2 fortification.

Varushka.t: Varushkan citizens, led by a Master of the Koboldi from the Novosad family, organised and largely funded this strengthening of a fortification in their own lands.

Upgrade Grimhold.o: In Summer 387YE the Master of the Koboldi, Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, announced a commission to upgrade the Grimhold, a fortification in Perumaki, Miekarova.

Miekarova/Perumaki.t: Perumaki is home to the Grimhold, the fortification being upgraded to rank 2 with white granite and crowns gathered between Summer 387YE and Spring 388YE.

Miekarova.t: Miekarova's defences are being strengthened, as the Grimhold is set to become a rank 2 fortification once the twelve months of work are complete.

Upgrade Palace of Apulian.d: Arising from the My friends are my estate Wind of Fortune, the project cost 80 wains of white granite and 30 thrones (240 crowns) in labour, and was due to take twelve months to build. Once complete, the upgrade would raise the fortification at Apulian to rank two and rename it the Palace of Mists. It would also make attacks on the region from the sea significantly harder, with seaborne assaults such as a shore offensive suffering a 20% penalty. Taxation from the territory would rise by five thrones a season. After the Summer Solstice, Casha di Apulian, Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven each contributed a single crown towards the work.

The League.t: The League's defences in Spiral were set to be strengthened. Once the work was complete, the upgraded Palace of Mists would make its Apulian holdings harder to assault from the sea and bring in five more thrones a season in taxes.

Upgrade Palace of Apulian.o: In Summer 388YE the Imperial Master of Works, Ehud, announced the start of work to upgrade the Palace of Apulian fortification in Apulus, Spiral, which would be renamed the Palace of Mists once complete.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Apulus was the site of the Palace of Apulian, due to become the rank-two Palace of Mists after twelve months of building. Once finished, seaborne attacks on the region would suffer a 20% penalty.

Spiral.t: Work began on upgrading Spiral's Palace of Apulian. On completion it would make the territory harder to attack from the sea and raise its taxation by five thrones a season.

Upgrade the Red Wind Corsairs.d: The motion cost 80 weirwood and 30 thrones (240 crowns), with six months to complete. Chiara Zayden Riqueza supplied 29 thrones 7 crowns and the 80 wains of weirwood after the Autumn Equinox 386YE, and Rhys Nighthaven gave the final crown. The Red Wind Corsairs gained the Forayers quality. When defending a coastal region of the Bay of Catazar they can use the Take to the Sea or Take to the Land order, spending a vulnerable season becoming a navy or reverting to an army. When attacking they can use the Daring Raid order, reflecting their instinct to take defeated enemies' money rather than their lives.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that some Wintermark armies dislike fighting alongside a foraying army, though many Wintermark heroes prefer ransoming defeated enemies to butchering them and have no reason to dislike a daring army.

Upgrade the Red Wind Corsairs.o: The Senate passed a motion proposed by Chiara Zayden Riqueza, Citizens' Voice, to upgrade the Red Wind Corsairs with the Forayers quality, letting the army convert between an army and a navy. The upgrade followed the An angry blade Wind of Fortune and was completed.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Bay of Catazar is currently the only place the Red Wind Corsairs can use their new ability. While defending a coastal region there, they can take to the sea as a navy or return to land.

Upon a midnight dreary.d: Callidus offered to find Brass Coast founders' relics for a heavy price, and Basileia sent cryptic next steps in the plot against Salt Lord Seonag. Irra Harah threatened war if the Empire attacked the Nesustak rebels, while Arhallogen offered to slaughter them. Cathan Canae warned that a new territory must be conquered by Summer 388YE after Mieriada's cession. Knights of Glory armies in Sarangrave can no longer take cautious orders. Barien summoned Dawnish and Wintermark victors to judge glory against heroism. Skathe offered Catena help codifying a curse. Surut's Brand will stay in Necropolis if granted amity. Tharim's knights destroyed Agramant's covens in Upwold but badly damaged its farms and businesses.

Dawn.t: Dawnish challenge victors were summoned to Axmure to argue before Barien that glory surpasses heroism. Miners in Dawnish lands have suffered drowning nightmares that Jaheris's heralds claim they can turn to profit.

Druj.t: The Druj lost the Nesustak Forest to rebel slave septs backed by Irra Harah, though they kept Whisperwood. Skathe offered Catena help in codifying a curse to spread misery across Druj lands.

Grendel.t: Overseer Hook reported that Salt Lord Seonag had hosted Broken Shore orcs calling for abolition, while Basileia's plot to assassinate her moved forward. Cathan Canae raised no objection to recognising the Protectorate of Mareave.

Highguard.t: Surut's Brand, around 1,000 burned knights, guarded Necropolis's coast for a season. They will stay until Spring 388YE only if the Conclave grants Surut amity.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae will not count retaking the Jotun-held lands of Bregasland and Liathaven as conquering a new territory.

Navarr.t: Ossegrahn withdrew his support from Greenwatch, so the Greenwatcher lost the Implements of Willowbraid. Arhallogen hinted it might deal with the Conclave, not only its Navarr allies, if its offer were taken up.

The Brass Coast.t: Callidus offered, at a steep price, to track down Erigo's gold-and-ruby circlet and Guerra's crimson sash. The Freeborn armies Fire of the South and Burning Falcon now share the Knights of Glory effect that bars cautious orders.

The League.t: Miners in League lands have reported drowning nightmares. Jaheris's heralds invited affected mine owners to the Plot and Plunder bar in the League camp to hear their scheme.

The Marches.t: Tharim's knights wiped out Agramant's covens in Upwold, but their brutal methods damaged farms and businesses across the territory. Alf Alwen and Jim Bribben were not found.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae cited the Empire's cession of Mieriada to the Thule as the kind of thing that angers her.

Urizen.t: Catena's Urizeni Assembly pledge to eradicate the Druj so pleased Skathe that the eternal offered to help her codify a curse of any realm and magnitude.

Varushka.t: Varushkan miners have suffered nightmares of drowning. Jaheris's heralds, who crossed Varushka from Miekarova, claim to know their source and a scheme to profit from it.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's victors were summoned to argue before Barien that heroism surpasses glory. Eleonaris praised the Voices of the Unbound Storm for their Knights of Glory enchantments.

Upon a midnight dreary.o: In Autumn 387YE eternals of every realm approached the Empire with offers, warnings and consequences. Irra Harah backed slave rebels in Sarangrave's Nesustak Forest, Ossegrahn turned away after Peakedge Stead fell, Surut's knights guarded Necropolis, and Tharim's knights scoured Upwold.

Brocéliande/Vale's Lament.t: The Sentinel Gate opens to the Singing Circle, a strong Night regio here, where Lashonar hopes to see An Ode To Blood And Sacrifice cast.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Cathan Canae has no objection to the Empire recognising the city state of Beoraidh.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Its cession to the Thule prompted Volstann's warning that the Empire must conquer a new territory by the end of Summer 388YE.

Necropolis/Coursmouth.t: Surut's burned knights took up positions in Coursmouth to watch the coast.

Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand.t: Surut's Brand stationed itself in Sanctuary Sand to guard against attack from the sea.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: The Bloodwater Spears, the Water Walkers and another sept overthrew the Druj here with Irra Harah's backing. Attacking them would be illegal and would bring Irra Harah's war, though Arhallogen offered to do it for the Empire.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: Mentioned in passing: if the Druj are forced out of Thornfen, the rebels might claim more of Sarangrave.

Sarangrave/Whisperwood.t: The rebels tried and failed to take Whisperwood from the Druj. The Empire could still seize it by driving the Druj out.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: Barien's victors and their skops and troubadours gather at the Grove of the Thousand here to present their deeds.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the page does not discuss the Bay directly; its only link is indirect, through the knights watching Necropolis's coast against attack from the sea.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae will not count Bregasland as a new territory, as it was once Imperial.

Brocéliande.t: A Sentinel Gate conjunction opens to a strong Night regio here, which Lashonar's heralds urge be used to cast Nathair Autumngale's arcane projection. Ritualists would face only a minor risk of vallorn miasma.

Holberg.t: Holberg's mine owners were invited to hear Jaheris's heralds explain the drowning nightmares and their scheme to profit from them.

Karov.t: Karov's mine owners were invited to the Jaheris heralds' meeting about the subterranean nightmares and a plan to profit from them.

Karsk.t: Karsk's mine owners were among those invited to hear the Jaheris heralds' scheme about the miners' nightmares.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae will not count Liathaven as a new territory if it is retaken.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the recently recovered Madruga does not count as a new territory under Cathan Canae's terms.

Mareave.t: Cathan Canae confirmed that recognising the Protectorate of Mareave would not anger the Lady of the Frost.

Miekarova.t: Volstann cited the cession of Mieriada to the Thule as the kind of loss that angers Cathan Canae. Jaheris's heralds began their journey across Varushka from Miekarova.

Necropolis.t: Surut's Brand took up positions to defend Necropolis from attack by sea, worth around 1,000 troops. They will remain until Spring 388YE only if Surut is granted amity.

Ossium.t: Ossium's mine owners were invited to the Jaheris heralds' meeting about the miners' drowning nightmares.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only in a reference to Reumah's Redoubt as Necropolis's main coastal defence, not to this territory.

Sarangrave.t: Rebel septs backed by Irra Harah seized the Nesustak Forest, and Arhallogen offered to slaughter them. Imperial armies there enchanted with Knights of Glory can no longer take cautious orders.

Semmerholm.t: Barien's challenge finale will be held at the Grove of the Thousand in Axmure. Semmerholm's mine owners were also invited to the Jaheris heralds' meeting.

The Barrens.t: Mine owners in the Barrens were invited to the Jaheris heralds' meeting. The contested Nesustak Forest lies on the Barrens' border.

Therunin.t: Peakedge Stead was destroyed by the Druj and Ossegrahn turned away from the Empire, leaving an enchanted glade said to be untouched by the vallorn. Therunin also does not count as a new territory for Cathan Canae.

Upwold.t: Tharim's knights destroyed two Agramant covens and the Circle of Stone remnants. Their damage will cost every farm and business 36 rings at Winter, with Heart's Blood compensation possible if the Conclave approves.

Volodmartz.t: Volodmartz's mine owners were invited to the Jaheris heralds' meeting about the subterranean nightmares.

Weirwater.t: Weirwater's mine owners were invited to hear Jaheris's heralds explain the miners' nightmares and their money-making scheme.

Urizeni Experiment.d: The Stargazers salvaged warding stones from Bendol. Theodora and the Spear of the Seven were made responsible for casting Wardens of the Black Waste at two sites in Bloodwater Marsh, past ettercaps and vallornspawn. If both wards are made, Sorin will let the Empire summon a Basalt Citadel there. A third conjunction let the Warmage clear the way to the Turbulent Wellspring so the Archmage of Spring could perform Dance of Navarr and Thorn, at the risk of a pulse of chaotic energy. Agoska and Halyx delayed their visit to Anvil until Autumn, asking to bring a servant of Irra Harah and to be given Dreadful Ending. Servadi of the Severed Hornets offered the Sun Chamber a chance to explore the Hungry Earth.

Druj.t: The Druj legacy shapes the Sarangrave: the buruk tepel of the Thornwasp sept worked Severed Hornet labourers to death in the Hungry Earth mithril mines, and the Nesustak rebels hope to fell a Druj miasma pillar. Kaela's Gift lets captured Imperial citizens deny the Druj their corpses.

Navarr.t: The Archmage of Spring, Arwydd Clearbramble, was charged with performing Dance of Navarr and Thorn at the Turbulent Wellspring to join the Bendol vallorn heart to the trods. Doing so risks a chaotic pulse that could stir the hearts already connected.

Urizen.t: The Urizen National Assembly set the Stargazers to work on the vallorn. Theodora and the Spear of the Seven now carried the warding of Bloodwater Marsh, and Urizeni settlers stood to gain if the Druj miasma pillars were destroyed.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Boyar's Hasta is credited with helping save the Nesustak rebels, and the Hungry Earth mines are compared to the Crawling Depths in Ossium.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sun Chamber last used the Door of Hidden Possibilities to scout in Sermersuaq, a year before this offer.

Urizeni Experiment.o: After the Urizen National Assembly called on the Stargazers to study the Sarangrave's vallorn, they identified conjunctions to place permanent wards in Bloodwater Marsh and to connect the Bendol vallorn heart to the trods. Alongside this, the Nesustak Forest rebels postponed their delegation to Anvil, and a Severed Hornet orc revealed the mithril-rich caves of the Hungry Earth in the Whisperwood.

Sarangrave/Bendol.t: The Stargazers salvaged surviving warding stones from Bendol. A conjunction to the Turbulent Wellspring offered the chance to connect its vallorn heart to the trods, which would also allow the proposed Eastern Citadel to be built.

Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh.t: Dilapidated warding stones at opposite ends of the marsh could be made permanent with Wardens of the Black Waste and a ring of ilium, if ettercaps and vallornspawn are driven off. If both wards are completed, a Basalt Citadel could be summoned here.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: The Waterwalker and Bloodwater Spear rebels survived the vallorn but postponed their delegation until Autumn. They asked to bring a servant of Irra Harah to Anvil and to be given Dreadful Ending so they can destroy the forest's miasma pillar.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: Mentioned in passing: any Axou who have moved to Thornfen are presumed to suffer the same miasma-pillar effect as the Urizeni settlers.

Sarangrave/Whisperwood.t: Servadi of the Severed Hornets in Uklead revealed the Hungry Earth, a deadly narrow cave network in the southern cliffs once mined for mithril by the Thornwasp. A five-person conjunction offered the Sun Chamber a first look inside.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, which lets captured or miasma-stricken citizens choose a painless death, extends into Brocéliande.

Mountains of the Moon.t: Mentioned in passing: the entrance to the Hungry Earth caves lies on a plateau where the Sarangrave meets the Mountains of the Moon.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thornwasp mithril operation is likened to the Crawling Depths in Ossium, and Ossium seconded a Senate statement on Nesustak Forest.

Sarangrave.t: The Sarangrave became the focus of efforts to contain the vallorn through new wards, a possible Basalt Citadel and a link to the trods. Its tangled rebel politics and the hidden mithril caves of the Hungry Earth were also coming to light.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sun Chamber's Door of Hidden Possibilities was last directed to scout in Sermersuaq.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift extends into Therunin.

Value beneath the mountain.d: After the Ashen Flame raised Mount Polus (renamed Kespoena's Reach) with the Hand that Shakes the Heavens, a crevasse opened at its base. The Argent Sword's heralds explored it, delivering three wains of mithril to their general and finding a mithril vein.
