The vein could become the Kespoena's Nadir bourse seat (300 thrones, six months, 12 wains of mithril a season) by Senate motion or announcement by the Master of the Koboldi, whose heralds wish to build it. Six perilous conjunctions into the caverns, facing Disciples of Sulemaine, bandits and strange humanoid creatures, could each cut the cost by eight thrones, and all six would halve the build time. Once built, a suitable army could explore deeper still.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Argent Sword found the mithril vein, and several Urizeni title-holders, including Clytemnestra, Herminius, Felix of the Wise Citadel, Arephanes and Donato, were charged with clearing the caverns in return for rewards. Their nation stood to gain a new mithril seat in Zenith.

Value beneath the mountain.o: Heralds of the Argent Sword, sent by General Clytemnestra to explore the crevasse beneath the newly raised Kespoena's Reach in Occursion, discovered a deep vein of mithril, along with caverns haunted by hostile creatures. A new mithril bourse seat, Kespoena's Nadir, could now be commissioned.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Beneath Kespoena's Reach in Occursion lay the mithril vein, an underground lake, lightstone deposits and a gemstone cache, all of them threatened by hostile dwellers in the dark. These caverns were where Kespoena's Nadir could be built.

Zenith.t: Zenith gained a newly discovered mithril vein beneath its highest mountain and a possible new bourse seat. Its caverns, however, harboured hostile creatures, a band of Disciples of Sulemaine and fleeing bandits.

Various storms and saints.d: The Unfettered Mind found that Sadogua powers Dripping Echoes of the Fen and Irra Harah powers Forge the Wooden Fastness. Sadogua moved Damakhan's Forge from Spiral to Zenith in return for amity. Ephisis' Scales was suspended for the Equinox, Estavus barred Varushkan magicians from Before the Throne of Estavus for a year, and Basileus Flint was reportedly deposed. The Great Grasses blight kept slowly spreading. Kaela offered a compromise on extending her Gift to vallorn fighters. Janon's heralds inspired the Green Shield and Summer Storm and offered to transform the Burning Falcon. Sentinel Gate openings led to Southmoor and Sarvos, and a Varushkan expedition lost eight people at Zoria's Cave.

Dawn.t: The heralds of Barien chose to be hosted by House Griffinsong in Dawn, a reward for the Dawnish gift of power to the Summer eternals against the realm of Day.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift is described as letting Imperial citizens captured by the Druj escape torment through painless death.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Damakhan's Forge is described as battered by successive Grendel invasions, and Grendel-held Feroz is named in the Freeborn mandate.

Imperial Orcs.t: Janon's heralds will fight alongside the Summer Storm until Spring 386YE, inspiring Imperial Orc units that support it, though the army cannot use Give Ground or Cautious Advance.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's move into Tromsa and its conquest of Jotun lands is the campaign in which Janon's heralds aided two Imperial armies.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Barien's heralds dropped their plan to enjoy Navarr hospitality, and the Spider King's watch over Navarr armies is used as a comparison.

The Brass Coast.t: Janon offered to give the Burning Falcon True Conviction if priests gather 50 wains of mithril and the National Assembly enacts a mandate before the Spring Equinox, while the hakima kept watch on the slowly spreading Great Grasses blight.

The League.t: Sanvar Isk opened the Loom of Spells in Tassato and will auction its use, while Lictors arrived in Sarvos to collect dramaturgical debts that could threaten League dramaturgy.

The Marches.t: Sadogua left an offer for Marcher landskeepers with the Marcher egregore, and threshers acting on Brother Martin Orchard's mandate tracked the Whisper Gallery cultist Quiet Charlie to Southmoor.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: a Thule raiding party is said to have looted Zoria's Cave over a century ago, probably taking the Staff of Zoria.

Urizen.t: The ruins of Damakhan's Forge now stand beside the Crucible of Fate in Zenith, and observers noted a new bitterness among Urizen magicians.

Varushka.t: Estavus barred Varushkan magicians from Before the Throne of Estavus until Autumn 386YE over an alleged theft, and a Varushkan expedition to Zoria's Cave lost eight people to a devouring darkness.

Wintermark.t: Zakalwe invited Winterfolk competitors to his strategy game, and Wintermark units supporting the Green Shield will be inspired by Janon's heralds for the coming year.

Various storms and saints.o: A seasonal roundup of magical happenings across the Empire in Autumn 385YE: the Unfettered Mind identified the eternals behind two citadel rituals, Sadogua moved the ruins of Damakhan's Forge to Zenith, Sanvar Isk opened the Loom of Spells in Tassato, and several eternals made offers. A Varushkan expedition also found Zoria's Cave claimed by a hungry darkness.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: Mentioned in passing: no events take place in Gambit; the word appears only in the name of Zakalwe's herald, the Opening Gambit.

Mournwold/Southmoor.t: The Sentinel Gate was set to open to Crowned Trees in Southmoor, where Brother Martin Orchard was to confront Quiet Charlie and gathered cultists and heralds.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: The Sentinel Gate was set to open to Bertram's Square in Cigno, allowing up to 50 people to settle the Lictors' dramaturgical debts.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: An Autumn regio in Tassato Mestra released heralds who built the Bridges and Chains doorway to the Loom of Spells.

Volodmartz/Opascari.t: Zoria's Cave in the Opascari mountains was found filled with a hungry darkness that ate light and swallowed several of the expedition.

Zenith/Lustri.t: Mentioned in passing: scholars of the Unfettered Mind ventured into the depths of Lustri to consult an ancient tree spirit during their research.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Feroz is named in the proposed Freeborn mandate as one of the territories from which everburning flames would be brought.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman is named in the proposed Freeborn mandate as one of the territories from which everburning flames would be brought.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is named in the proposed Freeborn mandate as one of the territories from which everburning flames would be brought.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: the Maze of Zoria in Miekarova is noted as the site the Synod chose over Zoria's Cave for consecration.

Mournwold.t: The cultist Quiet Charlie was found meeting heralds near a Night chamber in Southmoor, and a Mournwold landskeeper reported a tulpa tempting him while working a green iron mine.

Ossium.t: The Unfettered Mind's findings should allow the Conclave to begin negotiating with the relevant eternals for a permanent fortification in Ossium, if it wishes.

Sarvos.t: Lictors beating sinister drums appeared at Bertram's Square to demand payment of debts owed by mountebanks who guised as dramaturgical personae.

Spiral.t: Sadogua removed the ruins of Damakhan's Forge from Spiral, leaving a crater already filling with water.

Tassato.t: An entrance to the Loom of Spells opened in Tassato, where many volunteers worked for Sanvar Isk in exchange for training in ritual theory.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens is named as a place where Kaela's Gift is used by captured citizens, and the Bound King has shown interest in a regio there.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's advance into Tromsa is where the Green Shield and Summer Storm first called on Janon's heralds.

Volodmartz.t: A Varushkan expedition to Zoria's Cave in Volodmartz's mountains found it consumed by a light-eating darkness, and eight members vanished.

Zenith.t: The ruins of Damakhan's Forge were set down less than half a mile from the Crucible of Fate, and the Urizen named the old site's crater Damakhan's Lake.

Vermin.d: With Holberg free, the League could field the Towerjacks again, and the League senators were expected to appoint its general. Without Old Tom's Finest, Druj-animated trees attacked Holberg's walls unopposed, though the walls stood at about two-thirds strength and the trees were expected to stop shortly before the Spring Equinox. Restoration of the Great Pits of Ennerlund continued despite flooding, with first Imperial mithril expected after Summer 380YE. Holmauer's ruins were infested by vyig and giant vermin. The Druj had dismantled the dykes holding back the Morass, which was flooding Rebeshof, raising the option of cultivating rather than containing it. Venomous briars spread through the forests of Misericorde and Utterlund where a Druj 'poison beast' had shed its venom.

Druj.t: The Druj legacy dominated Holberg: their animated trees, the dykes they dismantled, and the venomous briars sprouting where their 'poison beast' bled all plagued the territory, while scattered orc bands lingered in the northern forests as brigands avoiding Imperial troops.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Highguard-held territory of Reikos is said to be in a far worse state than Holberg.

The League.t: The League could field the Towerjacks for the first time in decades, and its senators were expected to unanimously appoint a general or risk the Senate doing so. Its people also faced the clean-up of a scarred Holberg.

Vermin.o: In Winter 379YE the newly liberated League territory of Holberg faced the Druj occupation's aftermath: animated trees battering its walls, vermin overrunning the ruins of Holmauer, the Morass spreading north and poisonous briars in the northern forests. Meanwhile the Towerjacks army was re-formed and needed a general.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: Restoration of the Great Pits continued despite unexpected flooding in the lower tunnels, with first Imperial mithril expected after the Summer solstice 380YE. However, the spreading Morass and the creeping briars both threatened parts of the region.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: The ruined suburbs were becoming a lair for vyig agents, cat-sized rats and dog-sized feral cats. Any plans for the ruins had to wait until the killer trees subsided.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Venomous, unnatural briars spread through Misericorde's northern forests, where orc remnants also lurked as bandits. The briars threatened to hamper any large troop deployment.

Holberg/Rebeshof.t: Southern Rebeshof suffered regular flooding from the spreading Morass, with the waters subsiding less each time and risking engulfing the region. The northern briars might also reach this far south.

Holberg/The Morass.t: With the Druj having dismantled its dykes, the Morass was spreading north and sending out murderous trees. Its surprising fertility raised the option of cultivating it for herbs at the cost of farmland.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Utterlund's northern forests were overrun by poisonous briars grown where the Druj 'poison beast' shed its venom, and scattered orc bands still haunted the woods as brigands.

Holberg.t: Holberg's walls held at around two-thirds strength against one last season of animated trees, while its mines, ruins, marshes and northern forests all bore the marks of Druj occupation, with repairs and decisions awaiting once the trees settle.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is cited as suffering a situation far more terrible than Holberg's.

Victory and unity.d: Ilarch Maxatios said Axos could not lead opposition to the Freedom Accord. He also declined to explain a white granite purchase and refused Imperial scholars access to study the sorcerer-kings. Rumours spoke of outside funding for Issyk's docks and of Jarmish-backed construction at Maykop, which might anger the Commonwealth. Kyther, aided by Theodosia of Ipotavo's liao-fuelled preaching, urged the citadels to unite. The Regario Dossier, a Conclave order or the Synod might act on several opportunities, including joining the exorcism of Solokha. Sophia Anacharsis did visit Anvil, and several cardinals received items hallowed with auras of understanding, which proved controversial. The Shuttered Lantern was sent to investigate Kyther and Theodosia.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: an Axou preacher warned the Druj might strike again across the Path of the Eye, though Kyther's talk of threatening military powers was not aimed solely at them.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel once partly destroyed Issyk's expanded docks in retaliation when Axos joined the Liberty Pact and ended their short-lived alliance.

Navarr.t: Fintan Nighthaven of Navarr, the Ambassador to Axos, led Imperial diplomacy with Ilarch Maxatios. Fintan pressed the Axou on the Freedom Accord, granite, the sorcerer-kings and memory magic, and was expected to escort Sophia Anacharsis to the Assembly of Nine.

Urizen.t: The Axou blame Urizeni emissaries for the fall of Solokha, and Imperial historical testimony partly corroborates this. Any Urizen role in Synod statements on the Solokha exorcism would therefore be particularly sensitive.

Victory and unity.o: In Autumn 386YE, Imperial relations with the Citadels of Axos stayed rocky as the demagogue Ilarch Kyther Deianeira rallied Axou to a populist call for unity. His rise was backed by Imperial liao and a letter from Emperor Vesna, while signs of foreign investment and a plan to reclaim haunted Solokha drew Imperial attention.

Mountains of the Moon.t: Mentioned in passing: the Tsark debacle in the Mountains of the Moon is cited as the source of Axou bitterness towards the Empire, and some Axou mourners lost kin there.

Viridian nemesis.d: Following Urizen last season, Navarr urged by Teleri Thornweaver (Greater Majority) and Leliel, Daughter of Armisael, turned to the League, which upheld its welcome 328-10. The cities offered five opportunities. Holberg engineers proposed the Boar's Hide, a costly level two fortification in Boar's Dell that would draw the vallorn's assault and boost Brocéliande's mana sites. Sarvos merchants proposed a Market of Everything ministry with a Merchant-Prince of the Vallornguard. Tassato proposed a Vallornguard Military Academy granting the Stem the Green Tide order. Temeschwari bishops suggested a mandate sending League military units against the vallorn. Spiral actors proposed plays about defeating the vallorn, with Apulian merchants offering five thrones through the Cat's Graces.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: fine wines from Dawn are cited among the goods traded in Sarvos's markets.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Spiral's actors want the vallorn seen as an enemy that can be defeated once and for all, just like the Druj.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: a Sarvosi merchant prince scoffs that the Grendel think themselves masters of the Bay of Catazar though Dubhtraig's markets are barely twice Trivento's size.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: dramatising the recent triumph in Liathaven was suggested as a play subject but met little enthusiasm.

Navarr.t: The Navarr fulfilled their highest calling by sending their people, led by Teleri Thornweaver and Leliel, to arm and train the League, though steadings of Boar's Dell would bear the brunt of the vallorn's assault if Holberg's fortress were built.

The League.t: The League welcomed Navarr aid and each of its cities produced a proposal, from a fortress and a market ministry to a military academy, a Synod mandate for its bravos and inspiring plays, to prepare its people to join the Vallornguard.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Sküld, in Thule-held Otkodov, is noted as a vallorn-infested territory lying north of Holberg.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr worked with Urizen the previous season, and the League cities are said to be no less enthusiastic.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: rare metals from Varushka are listed among goods sold in Sarvos.

Viridian nemesis.o: In Summer 388YE, after the Navarr and Loyalty Assemblies sent their people to share their vallorn-fighting knowledge with the League and the League Assembly welcomed the aid, each League city drew up its own plan to prepare the Vallornguard for war against the Doom of Terunael.

Brocéliande/Black Boughs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Broch here is already fortified but deliberately built not to rouse the vallorn, as Black Boughs lies within the miasma.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: The proposed Boar's Hide would be raised on the foundations of Greenstead here, creating a level two fortification that would become the focus of the vallorn's assault on local steadings.

Brocéliande/Terunael.t: The vallorn of Terunael is the foe all these preparations target, and the Boar's Hide's mana benefit would last only until its vallornheart is destroyed.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Mentioned in passing: Sküld is described as infested with the vallorn and lying north of Holberg.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: The Market of Everything ministry was proposed at Cigno, whose docks on the Bay of Catazar draw ships and trade from across the world.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Despite turmoil in its streets, Apulian merchants offered five thrones, to be awarded by the Cat's Graces at the Autumn Equinox, for the best play inspiring victory over the vallorn.

Tassato/Madeiras.t: The Vallornguard Military Academy was proposed for Madeiras, letting League armies with Vallornguard-appointed generals take the Stem the Green Tide order.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos's trade reaches the Bay of Catazar at the docks of Cigno, and the Grendel are said to fancy themselves its masters.

Brocéliande.t: Holberg engineers proposed building the Boar's Hide fortress in Boar's Dell, which would draw the vallorn's attacks and raise investment in Brocéliande's mana sites while a vallornheart remains there.

Holberg.t: Holberg's engineers, after abandoning a scheme to channel the vallorn to their walls, proposed taking their skills to Brocéliande to build a grand fortification against it.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: the recent triumph in Liathaven was floated as a subject for an anti-vallorn play without much enthusiasm.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: its vallorn-infested region of Sküld is noted as lying north of Holberg.

Sarvos.t: Sarvosi merchants proposed a Market of Everything ministry to supply the Vallornguard with materials, herbs and mana crystals through a new Merchant-Prince of the Vallornguard.

Spiral.t: Spiral's actors and troupe magicians proposed using plays and dramaturgy to convince citizens the vallorn can be defeated, with a prize contest through the Cat's Graces.

Tassato.t: Amid the mustering of the League's third army, Tassatan bravos proposed an academy to train League soldiers in Vallornguard defensive tactics.

Temeschwar.t: Bishop Marko von Vardstein and the bravo Livinnia urged a Synod mandate so League military units could start fighting the vallorn immediately through relevant ventures.

Voice irresistable.d: Runa proposed a private Summer meeting with Ambassador Kindra. Thania of the Blackstaff's offer of Icy Crag ritual texts still stands. Orobus's offer of 12 rings of ilium for weirwood saplings lapses at the end of the Equinox. Fraynir offered a Senate appraisal of the Thule Winter wards in Sküld, available until the Summer Solstice, if the Conclave sanctions sharing Dreadful Ending. Runa objected to Imperial rituals in Ossium, Sermersuaq and Miekarova, threatening to charge the Empire mana if another shroud covers Miechernya's Painted Caves. Hinodir warned against meddling with the constellations. The Thule claimed victory in Ulnak and asked the High Exorcist for help against ghosts. A joint Varushkan–Thule hunt for face-peelers succeeded.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is named as one of the nations sending food shipments north to Otkodov under the peace.

Druj.t: The Thule marched east out of Ossium and claim victory in their initial conquest of the Druj-held Forest of Ulnak, aided by Imperial mercenary captains, and they invite Imperial armies to join under Tathenon's strategy.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are not named. Their territory of Skarsind appears only through Crow's Ridge, listed among the regions that are politically Thule but still subject to Imperial magic cast on the territory.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr is named as one of the nations shipping food north to Otkodov under the peace treaties.

Thule.t: Otkodov installed Runa as its new ambassador to the Empire. It pressed the Empire on vallorn wards, ritual texts and weirwood, and warned against rituals touching its people. It also claimed victory in its push into the Forest of Ulnak.

Varushka.t: Many Varushkan captains joined the Thule Claws of the Dragon in successfully rooting out face-peelers in Karsk and Ossium. Runa protested the Rot-empowered enchantment on Ossium and the shroud over Miechernya's Painted Caves.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Kindra Surefoot serves as the Empire's ambassador to the Thule. The Sky and Ice enchantment on Sermersuaq drew little Thule concern, and Runa noted that the Thule committed three armies to Sermersuaq's liberation.

Voice irresistable.o: In Spring 388YE the new Thule ambassador, Runa Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-Undivided, succeeded the late Rak. He proposed a private Summer Solstice meeting, renewed offers on ritual texts, weirwood and ward appraisals, and protested Imperial magic laid over Thule-held lands, while the Thule claimed victory in their first assault on the Forest of Ulnak.

Karsk/Krevsaty.t: Mentioned in passing: Krevsaty is listed among the regions that are politically part of Otkodov but still subject to Imperial magic laid on Karsk.

Miekarova/Miechernya.t: An Imperial shroud made the Painted Caves of Miechernya unreachable, which Runa called unacceptable under the treaty. If it recurs, Hinodir will remove it and the Empire must pay the mana.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: The Thule ambassadorial offices in Mieriada were hurriedly prepared for the new ambassador, Runa.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: Rot-empowered heralds and magic caused ruin in the Bonewood. Orobus wants weirwood saplings that remember the vallorn to share their experiences with its trees.

Ossium/Webwood.t: The Rot lord-empowered enchantment on Ossium caused consternation and some ruin in the Webwood, though warlocks dealt with the heralds.

Otkodov/Sküld.t: Fraynir is building warded camps around the vallorn of Stathas surrounding Emrys in Sküld and offers the Empire an appraisal of them. Sküld was also shrouded by the Empire's star-related disorder.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The Sky and Ice alignment let Day heralds enter the Silver Peaks unbidden; Thule warlocks dealt with them at some cost in time.

Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge.t: Mentioned in passing: Crow's Ridge is listed among Thule-held regions that remain within Skarsind under the Law of Dominion.

Forest of Ulnak.t: The Thule began a systematic conquest of the Forest of Ulnak and claimed victory, but ghosts in the forest have cost them valuable materials, which they have asked the Empire's High Exorcist to help recover.

Karsk.t: Varushkan captains and the Claws of the Dragon hunted the trudniki face-peelers across Karsk, briefly disrupting draughir communities, and the effort appears to have succeeded.

Miekarova.t: The ambassadorial offices in Miekarova were readied for Runa, and Thania of the Blackstaff keeps her ritual text offer open while she remains there. An Imperial shroud over the Painted Caves drew a firm Thule protest.

Ossium.t: The Rot lord-empowered Spring enchantment brought heralds and ruin to the Thule regions of Ossium, prompting Runa to call for a ritual protocol. Orobus seeks weirwood saplings to plant there, and face-peelers were hunted there too.

Otkodov.t: The Thule are building permanent Winter-warded camps against the vallorn in Sküld, and the Empire may appraise them. Imperial astronomantic disorder spread magical shrouds over Verthandi, Urdr and Sküld.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the ghosts troubling the Thule in Ulnak are described as the same kind as those afflicting the Sarangrave orcs.

Sermersuaq.t: An Imperial ritual aligned Sermersuaq with the realm of Sky and Ice, helping clear corruption from the Dragon's Talon but letting Day heralds into the Silver Peaks. The Dragons were largely unconcerned.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind appears only through Crow's Ridge, listed among Thule-held regions that remain part of their Imperial territory for magical purposes.

Verthandi.t: Warlocks found Verthandi blanketed by a magical shroud, which Hinodir identified as a spill-over of the Empire's constellation disorder rather than cover for an attack.

Volumes of forgotten lore.d: A fifty-mana Night vision of Vesna crushing the Empire appeared over Casinea, and strange dreams returned there. Blackdamp proposed Nightfingers, a great work yielding deepstones for Varushkan mines. Thorns found the Three Stones regio in Therunin's Greenheart. The Woundbinder of the Mark was called to aid merchants attacked in Stark. The City of Gold and Lead refused potions and drugs, offered vis trades and advertised Callidus's auction. The Loom of Spells auction continued. The Conclave could request a new grand lodge proposal. Grateful Marchers gave a harvest bounty and gifts to titles. The Unfettered Mind gained the Well of Shadows, generals gained the Passionate Furlough order, and Spiral's dramatic strangeness persisted.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater is named as a place to which Blackdamp might later extend the Nightfingers bargain.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are blamed for destroying Therunin's trods when the Tainted Basilisk used blood magic to unleash the vallorn of Tharunind.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel invasion of southern Mareave is noted, as the Golden Pyramid grand lodge there was completed despite it.

Highguard.t: Highguard's Casinea saw the controversial vision of Empress Vesna and renewed unsettling dreams. Some Highborn and Casinean priests questioned whether such images amounted to idolatry and urged the Imperial Censor to act.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a territory to which Blackdamp might later extend its Nightfingers offer.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland, held by the Jotun that season, is the destination of aid caravans now avoiding Stark. Marcher magicians also fear what Rivers Run Red might do there.

Navarr.t: Thorns of the Sevencut striding found the Three Stones, a potent Spring regio in Therunin where Dance of Navarr and Thorn might be performed. Navarr messengers carried a flood of letters in the debate over Imperial enchantments.

The League.t: League citizens with resources in Spiral continued to experience dramatic magical strangeness and could draw on a dramaturgical persona, with Night magicians gaining extra ritual strength. The League was also noted as untouched by the Cold Sun incident.

The Marches.t: Marchers, angered by the attempt to license Rivers Run Red, gathered a 10-Throne harvest bounty for the Conclave to endow to anyone but the Rod and Shield. They sent gifts to several Marcher title holders and suggested the Senate amend those titles to make the gifts partly permanent.

Urizen.t: Urizen citizens with resources in Spiral shared in its dramatic phenomena and persona benefits. Urizen's Quick Study ritual was confirmed to work with the Loom of Spells.

Varushka.t: Blackdamp offered Varushka the Nightfingers, standing-stone great works costing 60 white granite and 15 mithril. Each would give every mine in its territory two deepstones a season. They could be built in Volodmartz, Karov, Miekarova or Karsk but not Ossium, and there were undisclosed further terms.

Wintermark.t: In Sermersuaq, aid caravans bound for Bregasland were shunning Stark's roads after attacks. A lost Atalaq expedition left wounded merchants whom Woundbinder of the Mark Conrald Mystrim was responsible for treating.

Volumes of forgotten lore.o: An Autumn 387YE wind of fortune gathered a range of strange magical events across the Empire. These included a costly sky-vision of Empress Vesna over Casinea, an offer from the shadowy Blackdamp to Varushka, and Marcher gratitude after the Conclave kept Rivers Run Red interdicted.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Mentioned in passing: linked to the account of the lost aid expedition from Atalaq, whose wounded travellers the Woundbinder of the Mark was called to treat.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: Aid caravans for Bregasland avoided Stark's roads amid rumours of derailed wagons and wind-borne attackers. A missing expedition's survivors reported bandits hurling coins, led by a horned woman veined with ore.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Visitors to Apulus often found themselves lost in unfamiliar parts of the city, stumbling into dramatic productions and wild revelry.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: The Three Stones, a potent Spring regio sheltered by a weirwood grove against vallorn miasma and vallornspawn, was found in Greenheart as the best available site for Dance of Navarr and Thorn.

Upwold/Tower March.t: A herald of the eternal Sadogua settled in the woods near King's Stoke to escort a member of the Unfettered Mind to the Well of Shadows each season.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland is the destination of aid caravans avoiding Stark, and Marcher magicians fear for it should Rivers Run Red ever cease to be interdicted.

Casinea.t: A towering vision of Empress Vesna shattering a crystal Empire lit Casinea's sky, sparking debate over its meaning and its fifty-mana cost. Strange dreams of intrigue and battle returned to those sleeping there.

Karov.t: Karov, home of the Weeping Stone, is one of four territories where Blackdamp's proposed Nightfingers could be built to supply its mines with deepstones.

Karsk.t: Karsk is one of four territories where the proposed Nightfingers great work could be raised, giving each mine there two deepstones a season.

Mareave.t: The Grand Lodge of the Golden Pyramid was completed in Mareave despite the Grendel invasion in the south of the territory, opening the way for a new grand lodge proposal.

Miekarova.t: Blackdamp's messenger claimed to bring word from Miekarova, which is one of the four territories eligible for the Nightfingers.

Mitwold.t: Grateful Mitwold folk joined a harvest whip-round of food and drink, sold to fund a 10-Throne bounty for the Conclave to endow.

Mournwold.t: Lingering anger over Rivers Run Red's use in the scouring of the Mournwold fuelled Marcher hostility to the declaration. Its people joined the harvest whip-round in thanks that the interdiction stayed.

Ossium.t: Ossium was declared unsuitable for the Nightfingers, for reasons Blackdamp's messenger would not explain.

Sermersuaq.t: Rumours of wind-riding monsters made aid caravans avoid Stark's roads. A missing expedition carrying food for Sanna's Hall left wounded merchants in need of the Woundbinder of the Mark.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a possible future extension of the Nightfingers bargain.

Spiral.t: Spiral's magical tumult of drama, masks and strange phenomena intensified. League and Urizen residents could draw on dramaturgical personae, and Night magicians gained an extra effective rank.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar is named as a place Blackdamp might extend the Nightfingers to once one was built.

Therunin.t: Therunin's trods had been shattered by the Druj unleashing the vallorn. Thorns found the Three Stones regio, where the Archmage of Spring was responsible for supporting a casting of Dance of Navarr and Thorn.

Upwold.t: A herald of Sadogua took up semi-permanent residence in the woods near King's Stoke, ready to guide a member of the Unfettered Mind to the Well of Shadows each season.

Volodmartz.t: Volodmartz is one of four territories where the Nightfingers could be built to grant its mines deepstones each season.

Weirwater.t: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater is suggested as a possible future beneficiary of the Nightfingers bargain.

Wages of sin.d: The Synod had condemned aiding Asavea, and the Imperatrix declared that crushing a slave rebellion debases the Empire. The Plenum still offered bounties well above the Imperial guerdon, and the law could not stop captains accepting. The Temple of the Way in Nemoria would act on one of two proposed mandates. One would call slaves to rise and join the rebels, risking a major international incident and the priests' safety. The other would urge Asaveans towards a peaceful, wise settlement, improving relations with Asavea. Bishop Henrietta von Holberg proposed a Vigilance mandate to list captains serving Asavea for the Imperatrix and the Cardinal. The Senate's only clear recourse was to abrogate the Temple's commission.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that the agreement which created the Temple in Nemoria also allowed the Asaveans to build their own temple in the Brass Coast.

Wages of sin.o: In autumn 382YE, as Asavea sought Imperial mercenaries to crush the revolt in Marracoss and Emphedor, the Imperial Temple in Nemoria and a young League bishop sought Synod guidance on how the Empire should respond. Three possible mandates were proposed, and the Senate was left weighing whether to close the Temple.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Feroz is not named; the only link is the reference to the Asavean temple permitted in the Brass Coast under the agreement that founded the Temple in Nemoria.

Waiting for the worms.d: Ambassador Dino i Riqueza judged that the Free Seas Pact would clash with the Liberty Pact's free trade clause, and Annike considered the required changes fatal. Several Sarcophan-linked ministries faced price rises, and the Kruidenkenner withdrew their offers, though the deBruin family kept prices steady. The Alivetti Estates prospered despite magistrates' concerns about drugs and a planned Sarcophan temple. The Lijkkever envoy Schuyler Koopman proposed a Senate appraisal for a port in Utterlund, Holberg, and offered to share its costs. House Lijkkever's entanglement in Axou politics at Issyk was being unwound. The Delves also offered to buy wains at two thrones each should market prices fall that low.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lijkkever envoy voiced fears of the violent orcs of the 'nation of Sanath' and remained keen on a Holberg route even after learning the real nature of the Druj.

Highguard.t: A Sarcophan art dealer offering trade in stone goods with a Sarcophan sect, and a Prosperity priest warning against the deal, were due to meet Highguard benefactors at the Chapel. A Highborn egregore would hold a majority vote on accepting the offer.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the new Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves, Dino i Riqueza, is of the Brass Coast, and the Madruga Municipal Docks proposal was cited as a model.

The League.t: The League saw the Alivetti Estates enclave in Sarvos prosper amid concern over drugs and a foreign temple. The Lijkkever proposed a joint port in Holberg, and the Jolly Jackdaw Cartel was named as the go-between for Wintermark investment pitches.

Urizen.t: The Pallas Docks in Urizen were completed on schedule as the deBruin Docks, protected from storms by the Ashen Flame's Summer enchantment over the south-western mountains. Their Prime Factor, Marta Kotova Novikova, would not face the price rises hitting other Sarcophan trade.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark farmers continued growing vlinderbloem for the Kraft brothers in exchange for viezesmaak. The brothers asked Winterfolk with investment schemes to pitch them through the Jolly Jackdaw Cartel.

Waiting for the worms.o: In Spring 387YE the Sarcophan Delves reported that their proposed Free Seas Pact against piracy had foundered over conflicts with the Liberty Pact, and warned that Asavean privateering would push the prices of their goods up by as much as a fifth. The Wind also covered developments in Sarvos, Holberg, Wintermark and Highguard, and an offer to buy surplus wains if Imperial prices collapsed.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Schuyler Koopman visited the Sand Fishers in Misericorde to discuss buying lumber and weirwood from their sawmills, or hiring them to clear woodland for the proposed port.

Holberg/Utterlund.t: Utterlund's marshy riverbanks were explored by a Lijkkever-funded party as the proposed site of a new port, which would also need warehouses, a road to the city and defences against the Mallum.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Bay was described as hardly safe waters because of Asavean-backed piracy, which pushed the Lijkkever to seek a northern route instead. The deBruin family's interest in the Bay was noted as a possible opening for securing marines.

Holberg.t: The Lijkkever envoy explored Holberg and proposed that the Senate commission Naomi of Virtue's Rest to appraise a municipal port there, with costs shared in return for priority berths. Some Holbergers warned it could draw trade away from the Semmerlak.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposal for the Municipal Docks in Madruga was cited by the Lijkkever as the kind of outcome they hoped for in Holberg.

Redoubt.t: The redesigned Pallas Docks were completed as the deBruin Docks under the protection of the Ashen Flame's enchantment. Marta Kotova Novikova became Prime Factor, able to buy Sarcophan weirwood from the Spring Equinox.

Sarvos.t: The Sarcophan freehold at the Alivetti Estates kept prospering despite magistrates' alarm at drugs such as bite and ocean's caress, and Aaven Beekhof lingered there to sell legal narcotics. A slow-building Community of Silence temple worried the city's Vigilant.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato was listed among the League cities the Lijkkever chose not to pursue trade with, given the danger in the Bay of Catazar.

The Semmerlak.t: A northern Holberg port would let foreign traders avoid crossing the haunted lake. Sceptical Holbergers warned this could harm trading posts on its shores, such as Ivarsgard Docks.

Wake up crying.d: At least thirty miners are believed dead and forty seriously injured. The tainted water leaves people listless or ill-tempered and corrodes metal, wood and structures. Fennir of Brackenbeak Hall still receives this season's 7 rings of ilium, but the mine may produce nothing afterwards. The Senate could invest in a rune-forged refit proposed by Holberg engineers, which would raise output by 2 rings. It could instead pay 10 Thrones to reopen the mine at a higher upkeep, or do nothing and accept upkeep of 15 Thrones. The Silver Chalice could heal Syrene with 50 crystal mana, and miners sought Synod guidance. Regrow the Land's Heart could not help that season.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: because the Scorrero Nets are in Grendel hands, experienced workers used to dangerous waters are available to work Syrene's Wisdom if the Senate does nothing.

Highguard.t: Highborn miners and the townsfolk of Syrene suffered deaths, injuries and lost homes. Grieving families turned to the Synod for a statement on whether such dangerous work can ever be fairly recompensed.

The League.t: A cadre of Holberg engineers diverted to Syrene and proposed an expensive rune-forged refit of the Lady Isabella pump. Their plan would make the mine safer and more productive.

Wake up crying.o: Shortly before the Summer Solstice 384YE, a catastrophic flood tainted with Winter magic tore through the silver and ilium mine of Syrene's Wisdom in Casinea and down into the town of Syrene. It killed miners, ruined homes and fields, and left the mine's future production in doubt.

Holberg/Ennerlund.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed refit would draw on techniques developed when the Great Pits of Ennerlund were improved against flooding from the Morass.

Casinea.t: Casinea's town of Syrene was devastated by tainted floodwater and a mudslide that washed out the roads to Anvil. Its chapters allied in relief, aided by draughir and briar-born volunteers who were unaffected by the taint, while the mine itself remained a flooded death trap.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the engineers who offered the refit plan for Syrene's Wisdom came from Holberg, on their way to visit the Silent Sentinel.

Walk on.d: Each human nation had a contested practice: the Freeborn Feast of the Broken Wheel, Dawnish love and glory, League dead reckoning, Marcher rebirth as non-humans and shriving, the Navarr Great Dance, Urizeni veneration of Sulemaine, Varushkan bargains with sovereigns and Wintermark reverence for ancestors in Kallavesa. Endorsing a nation's mandate would end the fall in its congregations. Highguard was offered a Highborn Assembly mandate committing its people to rooting out blasphemy, idolatry and heresy. The Marcher Assembly could shun the pilgrims or drive off all Highborn with rough music. Dawn could send troubadours to Highguard. All General Assembly mandates except Dawn's passed, and Mael Donjeon of House Remys went to Highguard.

Dawn.t: The General Assembly mandate affirming that love and glory benefit humanity was the only one not enacted, so Dawnish congregations stayed troubled. The Dawn Assembly instead sent Mael Donjeon of House Remys to spread understanding of love and glory in Highguard, despite warnings that this could inflame opinion.

Highguard.t: Highborn pilgrims were the source of the questioning, and Highguard was offered a mandate committing its citizens to eradicating blasphemy, idolatry and heresy, at the cost of narrowing its assembly's focus for a year. It also became the destination of Dawnish troubadours under Mael Donjeon.

Navarr.t: The General Assembly confirmed that nothing in the Great Dance is incompatible with the Way, ending the decline in Navarr congregations. The Navarr Assembly's earlier statement against criticism of hearth magic was noted as irrelevant to the pilgrims' concerns.

The Brass Coast.t: The General Assembly ruled that the Feast of the Broken Wheel, questioned by the pilgrims and by Zemress Islanders, does not diminish doctrine because it is a parody, ending the penalty on Freeborn congregations.

The League.t: The General Assembly declared dead reckoning an embodiment of prosperity rather than a dedication to Vengeance, ending the drop in League congregations.

The Marches.t: The General Assembly ruled that shriving and belief in rebirth as trees or animals do not contradict doctrine, ending the penalty on Marcher congregations. The Marcher Assembly was also offered mandates to shun the pilgrims or drive off all Highborn with rough music, but the page does not record either being enacted.

Urizen.t: The General Assembly held that Sulemaine, though not a recognised paragon, taught Wisdom and is not a false paragon, so Urizeni may call for virtuous humans to be recognised as paragons. This ended the penalty on their congregations.

Varushka.t: The General Assembly confirmed that doctrine no longer forbids bargaining with sovereigns, just as it does not forbid bargaining with eternals, settling whether wise ones and volhov commit idolatry and ending the decline in Varushkan congregations.

Wintermark.t: The General Assembly ruled that 'to sleep in Kallavesa' is a metaphor and that interring heroes in the swamp is like Highborn tombs, ending the penalty on Wintermark congregations.

Walk on.o: Grey pilgrims from Highguard, walking the trods to weaken the vallorn, questioned people across the Empire about their faith, leaving many citizens doubting nation-specific beliefs and congregations thinner. The Synod was offered mandates to settle these questions, and the General Assembly enacted every one except Dawn's.

Kallavesa.t: The practice of interring heroes in Kallavesa's swamps, and the belief that their spirits sleep there, was at the heart of Wintermark's question. The General Assembly declared it a metaphor compatible with the Doctrine of the Labyrinth.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Whittle folk living in Mournwold were cited by Highborn critics as an example of false-virtue followers the Synod tolerates.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the Whittle folk living in Tassato were cited by Highborn critics as an example of false-virtue followers the Synod tolerates.

Walk with me.d: Vesna looked back on a year of losses and recoveries: two armies lost and two rebuilt, one in Dawn by the Throne's own hand and one through Varushka's prosperity, with a third on the way in the League. The Throne condemned the assassination of Earl Aramis Du Froste, first senator for The Barrens, as cowardice and called him a martyr. Vesna repeated his final call to shelter refugees from Therunin, a call echoed in the Synod by Gwenllain Heart's End, Keziah of the Suns of Couros, Damascius and Travid Longest Path, Therunin's senator in exile. Navarr, Dawn, Urizen and Highguard had already answered, and Vesna asked every citizen to do the same, promising to retake Therunin together.

Dawn.t: Vesna rebuilt an army in Dawn by the Throne's own hand and mourned the Dawnish Earl Aramis Du Froste, Senator for The Barrens, as a martyr for his nation. Dawn was named as one of the nations that had already opened its doors to Therunin's refugees.

Druj.t: The Druj are the enemy whose grasp the people of Therunin are urged to outlast, and the Throne promised that the Empire will one day walk Therunin's trods again.

Highguard.t: Keziah of the Suns of Couros of Highguard echoed the call to shelter Therunin's refugees in the Synod, and Highguard was named among the nations that had answered it.

Navarr.t: The address focuses on the displaced Navarr of Therunin and states that the Empire has not forgotten Navarr. It notes that Gwenllain Heart's End and the exiled senator Travid Longest Path supported the call in the Synod, and that Navarr has already taken in refugees.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Vesna noted that a third army was on the way in the League.

Urizen.t: Damascius of Urizen echoed the call to shelter Therunin's refugees in the Synod, and Urizen was named among the nations that had answered it.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Vesna credited Varushka's prosperity with rebuilding one of the Empire's lost armies.

Walk with me.o: Emperor Vesna marked a year on the throne with an address to all Imperial citizens. The Throne urged every citizen to open their homes to the displaced people of Therunin and honoured the murdered senator Earl Aramis Du Froste.

Therunin.t: Therunin's people are described as displaced, with their senator in exile and the territory in the Druj's grasp. The Throne called on all citizens to shelter them and vowed that the Empire would walk its trods together once more.

War games.d: Ambassador Thaumiel told Jarm that the perpetrators of the Lantir incursion were dead and that no Jarmish prince was responsible. Ambassador Cyrus told the Commonwealth that the Shuttered Lantern had traced it to deceased Commonwealth citizens and that Jarm and the world would be told. Jarm now demands everything the Empire knows, threatening war if the Empire is implicated. The Commonwealth demands secrecy, has put observers on the Conclave orders aiding it and has declared the Liberty Pact at an end. Cold Sun made only minor gains. The City of Locks offered a hidden smugglers' port on the Sea of Steel, and the Senate could make embassy letters public.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; the only link is that the Autumn Archmage who arranged the summit is Vossk of Sarangrave Reforged.

Highguard.t: Both Highborn ambassadors, Thaumiel of Steeplechase Toll and Cyrus of Ebon's Hall, are at the heart of the crisis. Officers of the Pilgrim's Defiance, Seventh Wave and Valiant Pegasus visited the Commonwealth, which earned every Highborn general a heldenstein, gesetzstein and kriegsamulett, but further training opportunities are stalled until the crisis is resolved.

War games.o: In Summer 388YE a summit brokered by Prospero to arrange a ceasefire between the Commonwealth and Jarm against Cold Sun collapsed into recriminations, after Imperial ambassadors had told both powers that the Empire knew who caused the Lantir incursion.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory appears only in the name of the Autumn Archmage, Vossk of Sarangrave Reforged, who urged Prospero to host the summit.

Ward Little Boyar's Welcome.d: The motion took up an opportunity described in the Wind of Fortune "Outside the wall". The ward cost 20 wains of mithril and 60 crowns and needed three months of work once funded. Several citizens paid for it over the year. Yakov "Yasha" Bjelovuk gave mithril and most of the money after the Spring Equinox, and Farren Silver Streams added a crown. Triska Markova gave most of the mithril across several seasons, and Nikolai Yaropolk Borislav supplied the last two wains after the Winter Solstice. Once finished, the Little Boyar's Welcome was warded against the threats of Varushka's dark powers, and the taxation of Karov rose by six thrones a season.

Varushka.t: A Varushkan fortification is now protected against the dark powers that haunt the nation's lands, paid for mostly by Varushkan citizens, and Karov's taxes have risen.

Ward Little Boyar's Welcome.o: In Spring 387YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Karov's senator and seconded by Volodmartz's, to ward the walls of the Little Boyar's Welcome, a fortification in Duzekani, against supernatural threats.

Karov/Duzekani.t: The walls of the Little Boyar's Welcome in Duzekani are now warded against the supernatural threats of Varushka's dark powers.

Karov.t: Karov's senator proposed the ward, and its completion raised the territory's taxation by six thrones a season.

Warriors' Gate.d: Explorers mapped Warriors' Gate, a cold, flat tundra north of Suaq Fount. They found the frozen Lake of Sighs, Courtier's Wood, a carved trilithon dubbed the Gate of Winter and four pilgrim cairns. Armies cannot claim the region, but sites were found for Firebird Eorling's proposed Citadel of the Warm Hearth, which would anchor a claim. Two Blood-on-the-Snow regio, the Bloody Teeth and Treachers Dagger, were located, and a Wintermark mandate could turn the Hunt the Suaq Wastes venture against them. The Imperial Spymaster must choose to explore west, east or north next. Varushka and the Imperial Orcs pledged support, and the Whisper Gallery now offers a secret, criminal way to sabotage the effort.

Dawn.t: Dawnish adventurers pushed into Tsirku alongside the Winterfolk, and bold Dawnish captains may join the proposed hunt against Agramant's regio through the Hunt the Suaq Wastes venture.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction refers to orc warriors from the arid plains of Mareave, Grendel's territory at the time, learning to ski.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs Assembly pledged to learn from Varushka and Wintermark by a vote of 60-0, so their captains can now Adventure in Tsirku. For now, however, the nation remains focused on its highest calling of exploring the ancestors of septs outside the Empire.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: no Jotun presence was found in Warriors' Gate, and the fallen thane Wemba the Bloody is said to have broken when the Jotun claimed his hall in Atalaq.

Navarr.t: A single Navarr band, Powell Open-Skies' Open Skies, joined the scouts, and its members likened the Gate of Winter to Hercynia's Gate of Summer.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: no Thule presence was found in Warriors' Gate, though the eastern route towards Urdur may bring explorers into contact with them.

Varushka.t: Varushka's Assembly backed Wintermark's exploration by 208 votes to 30, opening the Adventure in Tsirku venture to its champions. A proposed mandate would rally Varushkans to help explore and exploit the wastes while recognising Wintermark's claim to Tsirku.

Wintermark.t: Winterfolk led the exploration of Warriors' Gate and shared their cold-weather expertise with the rest of the Empire. They now face choices over building the Citadel of the Warm Hearth, mandating a hunt against Agramant's regio and advising the Spymaster on the next direction of exploration.

Warriors' Gate.o: Winterfolk scouts, a band of Navarr and Dawnish adventurers made the first successful foray into Tsirku in Summer 388YE, mapping the region now called Warriors' Gate. The Empire was offered ways to build on this, including a proposed citadel, a hunt against Agramant's regio and a Varushkan mandate of support.

Otkodov/Urdur.t: Mentioned in passing: the ominous, rocky region east of Warriors' Gate may abut Urdur, making a Thule presence there more likely.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: Mentioned in passing: Warriors' Gate lies directly north of Suaq Fount.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: The Hunt the Suaq Wastes venture, based at the Hall of Hunters, has fewer beasts left to hunt. A proposed mandate would turn it against the Bloody Teeth or Treachers Dagger, though success might eventually end the venture's purpose.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: Mentioned in passing: the bleeding rocks at the new regio resemble the Bleeding Ice found in Tanikipari by the Shuttered Lantern three years earlier.

Tsirku/Warriors' Gate.t: Explorers mapped the region's Lake of Sighs, Courtier's Wood, Gate of Winter and pilgrim cairns, and located two Blood-on-the-Snow regio. They also identified sites where the Citadel of the Warm Hearth could be built to claim the region for the Empire.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the Gate of Winter reminded Navarr scouts of the Gate of Summer in Hercynia.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushkans call themselves cousins of the Suaq and Kallavesi.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction describes orcs from the arid plains of Mareave learning to ski in Tsirku.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: magicians cite Otkodov as an example of dangerous lands being rich, and the eastern route may border Urdur.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the western region of Tsirku may connect to the Sea of Snow, since great sea beasts must somehow reach the Grave of the Giants.

Sermersuaq.t: Sermersuaq is the gateway to Tsirku and suffers from monsters sent south from Agramant's regio. Destroying those regio would end the attacks, but the Smokehouse of Atalaq's provisions now go to explorers instead of boosting Sermersuaq's farms.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the wealth of the wild Barrens is cited as proof that dangerous places tend to be rich.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: one possible route of exploration heads west towards Tromsa into barren, windswept country.

Tsirku.t: The first region of Tsirku, Warriors' Gate, has been mapped, revealing landmarks, rare plants and Blood-on-the-Snow regio. Three routes onward now await the Spymaster's choice, and exploration after the Autumn Equinox will be harder.

Wasp nest.d: Hazelelponi's statement of principle passed by greater majority, the last use of this peerless kinship. With Eastring under the Druj, the Highborn and Navarr planned the Glade of Farewell, a weirwood memorial to be built and consecrated once a ravaged region is Imperial and uncorrupted. Samples of the Sephals Cauldron poison were brought to Anvil to find an antidote, which could then be applied through the Senate, the Gardens of High Chalcis or a suitable army. Other opportunities were the Micah's Stand wayhouse and a fortification for Peakedge Song. The briars have left the Garden of Glory, so its Keeper now receives twelve liao. The Assembly might seek to make peerless kinship permanent, at a cost.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: wounded Dawnish soldiers suggested the Barrens' shrine of hope as a model, and past kinship work had aided the Dawnish in the Barrens.

Druj.t: The Druj hold Eastring and East Ashes, where ghosts linger. They poisoned the Lower Tarn Valley, the Black Wind are eager to seize Imperial priests, and Peakedge Stead is feared to be their next target.

Highguard.t: Highborn priests and magisters led the effort to aid Navarr, bringing poison samples to Anvil and proposing a memorial glade and a fortification. This was their last chance to express peerless kinship, though they may seek to keep it permanently at a cost.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: earlier Highborn kinship work helped the Imperial Orcs in Skarsind understand the Ossium septs.

Navarr.t: The Navarr gained Highborn help with Therunin's restless dead, a plan to cure the poisoned Lower Tarn and a possible wayhouse and Keeper title for displaced Navarr in Reikos. Their herbalists also took over the abandoned Garden of Glory.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: earlier Highborn kinship work aided the Freeborn in Kahraman.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: past Highborn kinship work helped the Marches deal with threats in the Mournwold.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Zenith is cited as a place where the Druj once broke captured priests and turned them against the Empire.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: earlier Highborn work sought to increase understanding of the Ossium septs.

Wintermark.t: The Blood Cloaks were named as one of the few armies with the expertise to clear the Lower Tarn poison in a single season, if protected by Why Sulemaine Walked Away From The Baker.

Wasp nest.o: After the Highborn Assembly reaffirmed its peerless kinship with Navarr, Highborn priests went to Therunin to help lay its restless dead to rest. They found the worst-haunted region held by the Druj, and turned instead to new opportunities: a memorial glade, a cure for the poisoned Lower Tarn Valley, a Navarr wayhouse in Reikos and the defence of Peakedge Stead.

Brocéliande/Vale's Lament.t: The proposed Keeper of the Stand would be charged with striving to free Vale's Lament from the vallorn.

Reikos/Chalcis Mount.t: Micah's Stand could be built in Chalcis Mount before the Summer Solstice 387YE, creating the Keeper of the Stand title and boosting the herb yield of the Gardens of High Chalcis.

Therunin/East Ashes.t: Conquered East Ashes holds unquiet spirits and is a possible site for the Glade of Farewell, but only once it is liberated.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Eastring is haunted by many of the slaughtered dead but firmly Druj-held. Any priestly work must wait for its liberation, though the Glade of Farewell would at minimum lay its ghosts to rest.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are judged very unlikely to attack through the vallorn of Greenheart.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Imperial-held but poisoned valley could be cleansed if an antidote is found, through the Senate, the Gardens of High Chalcis or an army. Its abandoned Garden of Glory now yields twelve liao to its Keeper but remains under threat.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Peakedge Stead, its hospital and the new apothecary college are left undefended, and the Highborn urge a fortification built of white granite or weirwood.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: Mentioned in passing: the Garden of Glory lies on its edge, and the Highborn fear abominations could pour out of it.

Brocéliande.t: The proposed Keeper of the Stand would be charged with working to reclaim Vale's Lament from the vallorn.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the places where earlier Highborn kinship aided the Freeborn.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Valiant Pegasus is engaged in its liberation, and earlier Highborn kinship helped the Marches there.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as a haunted place whose ghosts give the Highborn their expertise with unquiet dead.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: earlier kinship work sought to increase understanding of the Ossium septs.

Reikos.t: Reikos could host the Micah's Stand wayhouse, and the Benefactor of High Chalcis could redirect the Gardens' herbs to cleanse Therunin, at the cost of the territory's herb yields while the work lasted.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: earlier Highborn kinship work with the Imperial Orcs took place there.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: its shrine of hope inspired the glade plan, and it is cited as a place where the Druj once turned captured priests.

Therunin.t: Therunin's war-haunted east, poisoned Lower Tarn Valley and vulnerable Peakedge Stead are the focus of the opportunities offered: a memorial glade, an antidote campaign and a possible fortification.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as a place where the Druj once broke captured priests and turned them against the Empire.

Watches from the Wall.d: The Wisdom Assembly (338-0) and League Assembly (312-0) endorsed the consecration. Holberg's residents then reported vivid dreams and unexplained dedications to Wisdom. Several opportunities followed. Until the end of the Winter Solstice 384YE, the Cardinal of Wisdom may enact a Focus of Wisdom mandate (25 liao) urging the faithful to solve a named problem. Reducing the Walls of Holberg would destroy the auras, but students proposed barbicans (100 wains of white granite, 200 crowns) raising its strength to 15,000. The Senate could trade one historical research capacity for an extra appraisal. Upgrading the Towerjacks to Engineer quality would cost 50 mithril and 100 crowns, which the Senate approved; this remains open until Spring Equinox 385YE. Holmauer Park's blight remains unresolved.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the orcs are cited as Holberg's relentless attackers for decades, justifying the proposed expansion of the city's defences.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard's great libraries are compared to Holberg's, and two Highborn visitors dreamed of being aboard a ship with Atun.

The League.t: The League's priests backed the consecration unanimously, and the Senate voted to upgrade the Towerjacks, one of the League's two armies, to Engineer quality. Proposals to strengthen Holberg's walls and to move civil servants to the city are also open.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's great libraries are noted as something Holberg lacks a rival to.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: a visiting boyar from Miekarova was the first to notice the second aura over the Holmauer Gate.

Watches from the Wall.o: Severin Teyhard von Holberg consecrated the gallery above Holberg's Holmauer Gate to Wisdom with true liao, backed without opposition by the Wisdom and League assemblies. A second, seemingly miraculous aura then settled on the gate itself, inspiring visionary dreams, spontaneous dedications to Wisdom and several new opportunities.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: The Holmauer Gate gallery became a consecrated, lit and painted gathering place for scholars, with a second aura over the gate beneath. Holmauer Park still suffers the Hag Queen's blight, which residents hope the new initiatives might address.

Holberg.t: The city gained two enduring auras of Wisdom, and its residents experienced visionary dreams and spontaneous dedications. Its walls can no longer be reduced without destroying the auras, though a costly upgrade to 15,000 strength has been proposed. The blight on Holmauer Park remains.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: a boyar visiting from Miekarova first remarked on the miraculous aura over the gate.

Watching my mistakes.d: The Wintermark Assembly had settled that former thralls could reweave their skeins, but many resistance fighters had survived through pacts with Blood-on-the-Snow. Four non-exclusive options, open only during the Winter Solstice, were set out: a Senate motion for sweeping magistrate investigations, costing Sermersuaq's military units two ranks for two seasons; a Synod investigation by the Silent Bell; a Conclave declaration sending the Shuttered Lantern to study the Howler's boons; or a Wintermark Assembly mandate sending priests to seek out offenders. Monsters from Agramant and Hayaak also roamed the territory. The proposed Hall of the Hunters (12 white granite, 3 thrones) would yield 9 mana and a monster-hunting paid work option.

Jotun.t: The Jotun have been driven from Sermersuaq, leaving behind their castles, thousands of cairns and the rune-carved stone markers that failed to keep the Howler's monsters out.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening story's Wintermark hunter bought her wolf-hound from a dog-training shop in Holberg.

Thule.t: The Thule warlocks gathered at Tanikipari were massacred by Hayaak's followers in Autumn 384YE, and the Griffon-King's monsters then scattered across Sermersuaq.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark is whole again but must decide how to deal with Winterfolk who made pacts with Blood-on-the-Snow; its Assembly could send priests to root them out and appoint a Banner-Bearer of Atkonaroq if the Hall of the Hunters is built.

Watching my mistakes.o: With the Jotun driven out of Sermersuaq, Wintermark faced the legacy of their rule: resistance fighters who had made pacts with Blood-on-the-Snow, and monsters from the Winter and Summer realms loose in the wilds. The Empire was offered several ways to root out the Whisperer's allies during the Winter Solstice, and a proposal to build a hunting hall in the Suaq Wastes.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Mentioned in passing: the respected Kallavesi magistrate Heorl Thunderspeaker, based in Sealtoq, could conduct any trials arising from a Wintermark Assembly mandate.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes.t: The Hall of the Hunters was proposed for the shore of Lake Atkonaroq in the Suaq Wastes, as a base for heroes hunting the monsters of Blood-on-the-Snow and Hayaak, producing 9 mana a season.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: Hayaak's army slaughtered the Thule warlocks gathered at Tanikipari in Autumn 384YE, and his monsters afterwards scattered across the territory rather than returning to the Summer realm.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: some Wintermarkers escaped the Jotun conquest of Sermersuaq by fleeing to Hahnmark.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the hound in the opening story was bought from a dog-training shop in Holberg.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: some Wintermarkers escaped the Jotun conquest of Sermersuaq by fleeing to Kallavesa.

Sermersuaq.t: Back under Imperial control, Sermersuaq faces possible investigations into cultists of Blood-on-the-Snow and is troubled by Winter and Summer monsters that a proposed Hall of the Hunters could keep at bay.

Watching you well.d: Following a unanimous Autumn Equinox 386YE direction from the Assembly of Nine, the Silent Bell questioned Suranni magicians rescued into the Empire and lawkeepers at the Suranni embassy in Sarvos. They described the disunited cult as made up of downtrodden members, diabolists, opportunists and murderous aberrants, the last likely being those freed from Axiom Prison by the Children of Wrecks. Most members see the Empire as an ally against the Dukes and have barely resisted the 384YE ban, which is punished with fines. The Bell outlined options for the Senate, Synod and Conclave to act, but warned that confronting the cult more effectively would likely provoke curses, kidnappings, subversion and violence.

The League.t: The League's Assembly of Nine commissioned the investigation unanimously, and League interest in the Black Plateau was answered with the finding that no connection to the Hand of Dumon could be found.

Watching you well.o: At the Assembly of Nine's request, the Silent Bell investigated the Hand of Dumon, a Suranni cult outlawed in the Empire, and reported on its nature, magic and aims, finding no link between the cult and the Black Plateau.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos is home to the Suranni embassy, whose lawkeepers told the Silent Bell that they are reluctant to execute aberrants, which led the Bell to conclude that aberrants made up most of those freed from Axiom Prison.

Watercolours in the rain.d: The scions raided the Brilliant Star after the Autumn Equinox, taking mithril and killing those who could not flee, including Verax of the Seventh Mist and most of their students. Its Day light now causes blistering illness. Tempest jade wards protect workers but production falls by four wains, to 20 a season, unless the Senate adds 5 thrones of upkeep, which would raise it to 28. The bourse seat gains a ministry trading tempest jade for splinterstars. Pride Assembly mandates are proposed: drawing armies home, freeing Proud congregations to become military units, or boosting art venues. Civilian commissions may receive cheaper labour, and national assemblies may call for art monuments.

Dawn.t: Dawnish knights-errant helped defend the Brilliant Star, and the Rose Towers would gain 108 extra rings at the Spring Equinox 386YE if the Pride mandate to celebrate art is enacted. Dawn's National Assembly may also call for a monument to its art.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Spires of Dusk, a horror the Druj left behind, could be remodelled into a memorial to the Hounds of Glory at reduced cost.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the threat of a Grendel assault on the coast meant the White Fountain garrison could send only a small force to retake the mine.

Highguard.t: A Highborn cataphract dedicated to Vigilance was among the mine's defenders. Imperial armies are credited with saving the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion from Cold Sun.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orc National Assembly could raise a statement of principle calling on citizens to design a monument to their art and culture in a named territory.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies destroyed Cold Sun's Ending Tide in Bregasland, then held by the Jotun.

Navarr.t: Navarr thorns fought to defend the Brilliant Star. Imperial armies are credited with protecting the Great Library of Hacynian in Hercynia.

The Brass Coast.t: The Azure Chorus at Braydon's Jasse and the Crimson Drummers of Madruga would each gain 108 extra rings if the art mandate is enacted. Imperial armies devastated Cold Sun's Fire Beacon in Segura.

The League.t: Congregations in Sarvos, Tassato and Temeschwar would each produce 36 extra rings under the art mandate, and Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato proposed an alternate Pride mandate. The League's assembly may also call for a monument.

Urizen.t: Urizen lost the Brilliant Star's benign light, Verax of the Seventh Mist and most of their students, and the chance to improve its ritual codification. Its armies would escape the draw-home mandate unless it passed by greater majority, and its assembly may call for a monument.

Varushka.t: Varushkan armies would only be affected by the draw-home Pride mandate if it passed by greater majority. Its National Assembly could also call for a monument to Varushkan art.

Watercolours in the rain.o: After Cold Sun's scions seized the Brilliant Star mithril mine in Tomari, its once-beneficial light became a permanent, dangerous bane that cuts production unless the Senate funds protection. The Pride Assembly's statements against Cold Sun also opened several proposed mandates to defend and celebrate Imperial art and culture.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: The Azure Chorus here would draw more visitors to its feasts and performances, gaining 108 rings, if the Pride art mandate passes.

Redoubt/Tomari.t: The Brilliant Star mine now glows with a harmful light, cutting output to 20 wains of mithril a season. A Senate-funded upkeep increase of 5 thrones would raise it to 28 wains, and splinterstars can be gathered from spent tempest jade wards.

Bastion.t: Without the Imperial armies, the scions might have destroyed the Grand Inspiration of the Way here. Any nation that calls for its own monument can no longer pledge support to that great work.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies destroyed the Ending Tide here.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies are credited with preventing the destruction of the Great Library of Hacynian here.

Kahraman.t: The Azure Chorus at Braydon's Jasse would see larger audiences and its title would gain 108 extra rings if the Pride art mandate is enacted.

Madruga.t: The Crimson Drummers of Madruga would draw more visitors, and the title would gain 108 extra rings, if the Pride art mandate is enacted.

Redoubt.t: The scions seized and permanently tainted the Brilliant Star here, killing those unable to flee. The White Fountain garrison sent a small force that retook the mine, but too late to prevent the looting.

Reikos.t: Remodelling the Spires of Dusk, left behind by the Druj, into a memorial to the Hounds of Glory would cost 20 crowns less if a Pride statement supports it.

Sarvos.t: Each congregation here would produce 36 extra rings next season if the art mandate is enacted, as the city hosts pilgrims seeking art and culture.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies devastated Cold Sun's Fire Beacon here.

Tassato.t: Each congregation here would produce 36 extra rings under the art mandate. Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato proposed an alternate Pride mandate.

Temeschwar.t: Each congregation here would produce 36 extra rings next season if the art mandate is enacted, as pilgrims come for art and culture.

Watered with fears.d: Having learned the Jotun military strategy, the Empire paired Rivers Run Red with a Winter curse that killed those who fell ill. Thousands of Imperials died, but two or three times as many Jotun fell, and more than half the remaining population of the Greensward perished. Outraged Marchers in the Mourn sent Mary Singer to Anvil to settle matters with the Marcher camp. Bloodcloak-aligned grimnir and apothecaries sent a delegation to question Imperial strategy, seeking Lofyn Ulfdottir, the authors of related Synod judgements and an audience with the Empress. The Jotun reportedly regard the strike as blasphemous, and the Feni of Alderly were also hard hit, raising fears they may turn on the Empire.

Jotun.t: Their armies lost thousands of soldiers to the curses, turning a military victory to ashes, and they are said to view the attack as blasphemous, which may hamper any future peace talks.

The Marches.t: Marchers in the Mourn, already enduring thralldom, now question whether the Empire has their interests at heart; regular visitors to Anvil face hostility there, and Mary Singer was sent to confront the Marcher camp.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: histories recall Wintermark and Jotun heroes occasionally fighting side by side against the Thule.

Wintermark.t: Grimnir and apothecaries gathering under the revived Bloodcloaks banner are troubled by the strategy and sent a delegation to Anvil to discuss Wintermark's place in Imperial warfare with its generals, priests and the Empress.

Watered with fears.o: At the Winter Solstice Imperial magicians turned the Mournwold into a killing ground with combined Spring and Winter curses, slaughtering Jotun soldiers but also killing a sixth of the territory's civilians. The carnage provoked anger among Mournwold Marchers, unease among Wintermark's healers and fury among the Jotun.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: The Feni said to live in Alderly's great forest were struck as hard as anyone, and if angered they might attack Imperials or stop harrying Jotun supply lines that pass the forest.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: The combined curses killed more than half of the remaining population of the Greensward.

Mournwold.t: The whole territory became a killing ground where a sixth of the civilian population died alongside thousands of soldiers, leaving Marcher resentment towards the Empire running high.

Wayfaring strangers.d: Peleus of Maykop sought Robert Von Holberg and the Ambassador to Axos, bringing a gift from the Grand Ilarch. Robert Stewart of the Forge and Furnace Fellowship came to settle the Tassatan Hills ilium dispute. If no plan emerged, labour costs would rise by three crowns per wain in Tassato from Winter 388YE, spreading to all League territories if the dispute was unresolved by the end of Spring 389YE. Anka Karass sought a private meeting with the Envoy to the Karass. The Marsh Lantern Spire asked the Magpies to remove a shroud from a cursed Druj fear artefact. The Wraith King's crew came to meet the Magpies. Beoraidh's maistirs staged the Battle of the Bay in the Anvil arena. Sebastião Duarte di Tassato offered covenstones for cursing Vellenka Vanyanova.

Druj.t: An Urizeni spire uncovered a cursed Druj artefact of fear in old ruins in Sarangrave. The Karass' long-feared betrayal turned out to be aimed at the Druj, aiding the Imperial raid on Druj-held Ulnak and Sanath.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Beoraidh's original arena was burned in an Imperial raid while the city was still under the Grendel banner.

Highguard.t: Highguard was one of three Imperial nations on the Bay of Catazar invited to field an eight-strong team in the Battle of the Bay against fighters from the Iron Confederacy and Morajasse.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs' raid with the Navarr on the Forest of Ulnak and the Salt Flats of Sanath succeeded only thanks to the Karass. Formerly enslaved Sannites among them had earlier derailed Beoraidh's overtures to the Empire, though negotiations have since smoothed matters.

Navarr.t: The Karass' assistance proved pivotal to the Navarr and Imperial Orc raid on the Forest of Ulnak and the Salt Flats of Sanath, though the Karass split from the rescue party along the way.

The League.t: League senators faced a Forge and Furnace Fellowship demand for redress over the Tassatan Hills, with strikes threatened first in Tassato and then across the League. Meanwhile a Tassatan merchant prince declared a vendetta against the Shadowed Torchbearer, and Robert Von Holberg was sought by an Axou emissary.

Urizen.t: The Marsh Lantern Spire, a new Urizeni settlement in Sarangrave, brought a cursed Druj artefact to the Magpies, and Urizen was invited to field a team in the Battle of the Bay.

Wayfaring strangers.o: Ahead of the Autumn 388YE summit, a series of foreign and Imperial visitors announced that they would come to Anvil seeking meetings. They included an Axou emissary, a mining guild threatening strikes in Tassato, the Karass, an Urizeni spire bearing a cursed Druj artefact, the crew of the Wraith King, Beoraidh gladiator maistirs and a feuding Tassatan merchant prince.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: The disputed Tassatan Hills ilium mine lies in the hills of Tassato Mestra. The Fellowship sought its return to the League, the 85 thrones from its auction, or other compensation.

Bay of Catazar.t: The maistirs of Beoraidh invited the friendly nations bordering the Bay of Catazar to compete in a gladiatorial tourney they named the Battle of the Bay.

Forest of Ulnak.t: Mentioned in passing: the Karass' part in the Imperial raid on the Forest of Ulnak drove interest in Anka Karass' visit.

Holberg.t: Holberg's senator had already paid the Forge and Furnace Fellowship 175 thrones in recompense. Holberg faced rising labour costs if the ilium dispute was not settled by the end of Spring 389YE.

Salt Flats of Sanath.t: Mentioned in passing: the Karass aided the Imperial raid on the Salt Flats of Sanath.

Sarangrave.t: A seer of the newly founded Marsh Lantern Spire uncovered Druj ruins in Sarangrave holding a shrouded artefact that radiates fear and would unleash a curse if destroyed carelessly.

Tassato.t: If Robert Stewart left unconvinced, labourers in Tassato would be encouraged to strike, adding three crowns per wain to new commissions from Winter 388YE. Tassato was also home to the merchant prince who declared a vendetta against the Shadowed Torchbearer.

We all stand.d: The serendipity enchantment helped Imperials meet locals, but it also helped those hostile to the Imperial Orcs find each other. The Golden Pyramid kept exploring, gaining resources each season. Talks over Beoraidh's docks stalled on steep tariffs. The Conclave disseminated Gift of the Wily Broker to the Black Sand Circle in exchange for Eye of Ruby and Sapphire.
