Proposals were raised for a cerulean mazzarine garden in Nadir, Tamazi fortifications in Eoradal and Fleisardh, and a Greater Apulian Way through Spiral. Both the Marcher and Freeborn assemblies sent farmers to help with Mareave's arid land. The Senate made the Bronze Bowls of the Three Seasons an Imperial Orc position. The Master of Rings commissioned Curstag's Way, linking Redoubt, Spiral and Mareave.

Grendel.t: The Tamazi pitched their proposed forts as protection against Grendel attack, while Golden Pyramid magicians made contact with former Grendel wizards of the Black Sand Circle in Beoraidh.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn members of the Golden Pyramid were among those seeking access to Beoraidh's docks.

Imperial Orcs.t: Tamazi orcs proposed fortifications and a Skouran embassy, and a Yerende orc proposed a cerulean mazzarine sinecure. The nation gained Marcher and Freeborn farming aid and was awarded the Bronze Bowls of the Three Seasons as a national position.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that farmers in Bregasland felt they had nothing to offer Mareave's arid grasslands.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed roadside rest stops in Spiral were to be patterned after Navarr wayhouses.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn assembly agreed to urge farmers, including Zemress islanders, to help make Mareave flower. This cost every Brass Coast congregation a rank of production, and the farmers expect recompense.

The League.t: Bishop Fabio's call for trade through Spiral inspired Leaguers to propose the Greater Apulian Way. The Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, commissioned Curstag's Way to connect Redoubt, Spiral and Mareave.

The Marches.t: The Marcher assembly agreed to send farmers to Mareave, drawing pious farmers away from Mitwold and Upwold. The farmers expect to be repaid for their efforts.

Urizen.t: Nightshadow spire architects co-devised the Greater Apulian Way and offered mithril if the Urizen assembly backed it. Urizen architects of the Golden Pyramid explored trade in Beoraidh.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is named as a likely market for Mareave's cerulean mazzarine.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark is named as a likely market for Mareave's cerulean mazzarine.

We all stand.o: In Autumn 386YE an Imperial Autumn enchantment over Mareave drew like-minded people together. Golden Pyramid magicians, Tamazi orcs, Marcher and Freeborn farmers, and League and Urizen builders pursued opportunities to develop the Empire's newest territory.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Golden Pyramid trade talks for Beoraidh's docks stalled over steep tariffs. The Black Sand Circle at Execution Hill traded Eye of Ruby and Sapphire for Gift of the Wily Broker.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: The Tamazi proposed converting Rucraic's Redoubt into the Storm Lords Sentinel, a fortification ready to serve as a Skouran embassy. They also eyed rebuilding a ruined aqueduct to bring fresh water.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: The Tamazi proposed High Mountain Home, a storm-warded mountain fortress meant to awe the Brine Turtles, but the opportunity has since expired.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Icarion's under-developed state raised building costs across Mareave. The Greater Apulian Way proposal would have removed that quality and placed an inn and warehouses near the old lighthouse ruins.

Mareave/Nadir.t: The Lazuline Bowl in central Nadir offers ideal conditions for cerulean mazzarine, and a sinecure creating a Lazuline Bonetender was proposed. It is illegal while the local orcs are still considered barbarians.

Spiral/Apulus.t: Apulus is the proposed site of the Greater Apulian Way great work, which would raise investment for Spiral's businesses.

Spiral/Screed.t: Mentioned in passing: the Black Plateau horror squatting in the centre of Screed is cited as the reason travel through Spiral is so hard.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the League's work on the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion is cited as why few Leaguers initially took up Fabio's call.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Freeborn farmers would travel to the far side of the Bay of Catazar to reach Mareave.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland's farmers are noted as believing they have nothing to offer arid Mareave.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: Feroz is cited as needing rebuilding, a reason some felt farmers should look closer to home.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the engineer Lucia Calumo di Apulian originally hails from Holberg.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is cited as needing rebuilding, a reason some felt farmers should look closer to home.

Mareave.t: Mareave lay under a serendipity enchantment that aided friends and foes alike. It became the focus of Golden Pyramid exploration, fortification and herb-garden proposals, Marcher and Freeborn farming aid, and a new trade road linking it to the Empire.

Mitwold.t: With Marcher farmers sent to Mareave, every congregation in Mitwold suffers a one-rank penalty for the season.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold is invaded, and its farmers have more pressing matters than Mareave.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Mazzar Tulk had lived her life in Ossium and Skarsind before travelling to Mareave.

Redoubt.t: Curstag's Way, commissioned by the Master of Rings, will connect Redoubt with Spiral and Mareave, reviving the old road route from Apulian to Redoubt.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a natural market for cerulean mazzarine and as one of Mazzar Tulk's former homes.

Spiral.t: Spiral was the site of the proposed Greater Apulian Way, with mithril-infused roadhouses to ease travel despite the Black Plateau. The Master of Rings commissioned Curstag's Way through the territory.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory appears only in the name of the Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar.

Upwold.t: With Marcher farmers sent to Mareave, every congregation in Upwold suffers a one-rank penalty for the season.

We are never ever getting back together.d: Rachensgrab yielded ten fleets, now being repaired in Sarvos, and two ritual texts, all held by Fleet Admiral Abel of Zenith Ascendant. Asavea remained at war with the Empire, and Jarm had severed ties. The Grendel embassy was completed. Salt Lord Kaliact of Spiral sent Speaker Curstag to Anvil to discuss renegotiating the peace treaty, and a Grendel navy anchored off Necropolis. The Vandersaar offered an Alivetti Market in Cigno, while the Gjullit family offered regular weirwood through altered or new docks. Three Lawkeeper knights came to work with the militia against the Hand of Dumon. Mathilda Fisher's terms for a Free Nation of Bregas were restated. The Senate had also amended tariffs on several foreign nations.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Lord Colwynn de Rondell of Dawn is named as Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy, and Jarrigk Orzel of Dawn as the Imperial Consul who met Mathilda Fisher.

Grendel.t: The Grendel faced Imperial sanctions even as their embassy was completed and Salt Lord Kaliact sought talks on the peace treaty. One of their navies was also anchored off Necropolis, and a Grendel in Nemoria bought the Temple of the Noble Virtues' idol of Prosperity.

Highguard.t: The National Assembly of Highguard was asked for a Statement of Principle on trading with the Grendel sailors in Necropolis, which would decide whether local businesses profited. Accalon of Felix's Watch also served as Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Pakt of the Imperial Orcs is named as Ambassador to Asavea, which is now at war with the Empire.

Jotun.t: Any treaty with Mathilda Fisher would require the Jotun to withdraw their armies from Bregasland and lose the Fishers' support. Harald Longaxe attended the Anvil meeting on behalf of Gudmundur Arason.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Gelert Ashborn of Navarr is named as Ambassador to Jarm, which has severed ties with the Empire.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn figured prominently. Esteban and Ezro were invited to the Grendel negotiations, some Freeborn plotted to steal the Scorrero Nets, and the Gjullit suggested new weirwood docks to serve a Brass Coast navy.

The League.t: Sarvos received the ten captured fleets and was named as the site of the proposed Vandersaar market, which League traders could use through a Trademaster. Lucia Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato served as Ambassador to the Commonwealth.

Thule.t: The Senate moved trade with the Thule first from sanctions and then to free trade as reparation for Thunderous Deluge, and the Empire was said to have secured significant change in Thule society.

Urizen.t: Urizen figures were central. Abel of Zenith Ascendant held the Rachensgrab spoils, Urizeni served as ambassadors to the Sarcophan Delves and Axos, and the Urizen encampment was suggested for the Grendel talks.

We are never ever getting back together.o: In the wake of the Rachensgrab raid, which shattered the international slave trade, this Wind of Fortune surveyed the Empire's foreign relations: the Liberty Pact's triumph, the hostility of Asavea and Jarm, an approach from the Grendel of Spiral, new Sarcophan trade offers, Suranni knights visiting Anvil and the Steward of Bregasland's terms for independence.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Mentioned in passing: the North Fens are not named specifically; the page discusses Bregasland as a whole under Mathilda Fisher.

Sarvos/Cigno.t: The Vandersaar proposed the Alivetti Market in Cigno, at an old villa with a decaying dock. It would need ten wains of weirwood, 20 crowns and three months to build, and would create a Trademaster able to buy ingots and measures.

Bay of Catazar.t: The Gjullit family proposed that the Senate could build entirely new docks anywhere along the Bay of Catazar to receive regular weirwood shipments, an offer the Senate had not yet taken up.

Bregasland.t: Mathilda Fisher still controlled Bregasland and sought a treaty making it an independent nation, with the Strong Reeds and the Jotun armies both withdrawing. An attempt by Marchers to assassinate her at Anvil had failed.

Necropolis.t: At least one Grendel navy anchored off Necropolis and its sailors frequented local taverns. If Highguard endorsed trading with them, Necropolis business owners would gain extra income before the Spring Equinox.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is listed among the nations whose tariffs the Senate amended the previous season.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Sejanus, the Senator for Redoubt, was invited to the negotiations with Salt Lord Kaliact's representatives.

Sarvos.t: The ten fleets taken at Rachensgrab were being repaired by the Sarvos Shipwrights Syndicate, but no Asavean merchants came to Sarvos's markets or the Cavabianca Dock.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra, the Senator for Segura, attended the meeting with Mathilda Fisher.

Spiral.t: Salt Lord Kaliact of Spiral had profited from a year of trade with the Empire and sent Speaker Curstag to Anvil to discuss renegotiating the peace treaty. The Spiral Envoy was among those invited.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Fleet Admiral Abel's name, Abel of Zenith Ascendant, is the only reference to Zenith.

We are the storm.d: Vesna declared the Empire the largest it had ever been after the Sarangrave victory. She called herself 'Ossium's Architect', having developed virgin Druj territory as a senator, and urged citizens to build Imperial homes across former Druj land for new taxes, bourse seats and hearths. She turned to the West, insisting Bregasland is Marcher because the Marchers made their homes there, while the Jotun fight for an ancient idea of the land. She announced she would march with her Iron Sparrows under The Drakes alongside Amberlain P Black and Bregasland's wardens, and invited others to join her. She also named and commended the generals who fought in the Sarangrave.

Druj.t: The Druj were cast as the defeated enemy in the East: Vesna hailed the taking of the Sarangrave as the first blow in a generation-defining war and urged that all former Druj land be settled with Imperial homes.

Jotun.t: Vesna denounced the Jotun presence in Bregasland, saying they fight to relive an ancient victory and are doomed to fail. She vowed that the Empire's enemies would burn if the Jotun did not leave.

Varushka.t: The Empress spoke as a Varushkan, invoking 'my own Varushka' and its tales of Bregasland. She commended generals of Varushkan armies such as the Golden Axe, Northern Eagle and Boyars Hasta for the Sarangrave victory.

We are the storm.o: In Winter 387YE Emperor Vesna addressed the whole Empire. She celebrated the victory that had made the Sarangrave Imperial, urged citizens to settle former Druj lands, and called on them to fight the Jotun in Bregasland.

Bregasland.t: Vesna claimed Jotun-held Bregasland as Marcher land. She announced that she and her Iron Sparrows would fight there under The Drakes beside Amberlain P Black and Bregasland's wardens, and called on others to join them.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Vesna cited her title 'Ossium's Architect' and her development of Ossium from virgin Druj land as proof that former Druj territory can be built into thriving Imperial land.

Sarangrave.t: The address celebrated the Empire's victory in the Sarangrave as historic, commended the generals who fought there, and pictured Urizeni hearths lighting the territory 'like a constellation of stars'.

We give the future to the winds.d: Asavean priests continue to blur their Golden Handed God with the Flame of Prosperity, so Boorra Talighar asked the Gatekeepers for true liao to consecrate the Temple of the High Flames before the Winter Solstice. Faraden will seek to renew its Jotun treaty in Summer 388YE, while the Iron Confederacy floats a Suranni invasion of Reinos. The Hakhandra offered granite and crowns for Yakholme Grange. The Blue Silk Scarf guild proposed a Delev guildhouse selling magical garb, which would bring them into contact with the Thule. Faraden favoured Astolat or Semmerholm over the Barrens, though Sansar merchants planned to visit the Dawnish at Anvil. The Cinders have gone ominously quiet.

Dawn.t: Earl Seraphine de Sarroi and Lady Cassandra du Creed drew Faraden interest in Dawnish wine and luxuries. Faraden preferred a market in Astolat or Semmerholm, but three Sansar merchants would come to Anvil to negotiate with the Dawnish camp.

Jotun.t: Faraden intended to renew its tithe-paying peace treaty with the Jotun in Summer 388YE. The Iron Confederacy, however, was discussing a Suranni invasion of Reinos to wipe out the Lasambrian septs.

The League.t: Faraden merchants were negotiating with the burghers of Holberg for a major enclave there, which remained the main focus of their trade ambitions in the Empire.

The Marches.t: The Marcher Assembly's welcome for Yakholme Grange delighted the Hakhandra, who pledged 15 wains of white granite and 45 crowns if it is commissioned and sent mooncheese to Sister Meredith's friars and monks. Some Faraden priests now hope to visit once it is built.

Thule.t: A Faraden guildhouse in Delev would inevitably bring Faraden wizards into contact with Thule merchants, a contact Mistress Karadragha herself is keen to secure.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Blue Silk Scarf's Celestial Caravan ritual is compared to the ritual known in Urizen lore as Ethereal Courier.

Varushka.t: After visiting the Great Hall of Fabric Arts, the Guild of the Blue Silk Scarf proposed a guildhouse ministry in Delev, creating a Blue Silk Weaver title. The Nekmelchida will hold back until a Great Market is built.

We give the future to the winds.o: Faraden's ambassador relayed a season of religious, military and trade news to the Empire. It included a covert priestly request for true liao to resist Asavean proselytising, confirmation that Faraden would keep its peace with the Jotun, and new trade openings in the Marches, Varushka and Dawn.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Dawnguard was among the western Barrens regions Faraden would prefer for any trading enclave in the territory.

The Barrens/Murderdale.t: Murderdale was named among the western Barrens regions Faraden found more attractive for a possible enclave.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: Saltmarsh was proposed for a Faraden market because of Dawn's planned port there, but that very prospect made it less appealing to the sea-wary Faraden.

Astolat.t: Mistress Karadragha suggested that Dawn and Faraden cooperate on a wine and luxury market in Astolat, along the planned Faraden trail, rather than in the Barrens.

Holberg.t: Faraden merchants continued negotiating with Holberg's burghers over a major enclave linked to Firewind Market, which would route caravans onward through Dawn.

Karov.t: Delev was proposed as the site of a Blue Scarf Guildhouse costing 12 weirwood, 8 mithril and 60 crowns, with the Faraden supplying the mithril. Faraden cloth merchants still await a Great Market there.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Delev Market's regular visitors from Otkodov are why a Faraden presence in Delev would lead to contact with the Thule.

Reinos.t: Faraden would keep paying tithes to the Jotun and Lasambrian jarls of Reinos under its peace treaty, while the Iron Confederacy mooted a Suranni invasion of the hills with covert Faraden support.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sea of Snow is not named; the only maritime note is Faraden's wariness of the sea, which makes a port-based Saltmarsh market less appealing to them.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm was put forward by the Faraden ambassador as a sensible, prosperous site for a joint Dawn–Faraden market along the planned Faraden trail.

The Barrens.t: Earl Seraphine pitched the Barrens as a frontier where a Faraden market would be the first of its kind. Most Faraden thought it too wild, though the Sansar family planned to talk with its people at Anvil.

We've been here forever.d: Eleonaris agreed to parley with Summer Archmage Solomon at a 7pm Friday reception in the Senate, where the Leonine Child would receive tribute. Her courtiers would then mingle across Anvil, on condition that no one asked for boons. Yaw'nagrah would meet Spring Archmage Fabienne Acoucher alone, saying the Empire could not be trusted to respect parley. Kaela offered Winter Archmage Emilia two non-military gifts. Ephisis declined a parley but sent traders to an open market. Azoth would receive Night Archmage Elyssiathain and give a gift to Ifan of the Darkwater Forge. Zakalwe offered to restore the Circlet of the Master Strategist but was puzzled by talk of a crystal crown lost in Brocéliande.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris praised the Golden Causeway proposed by the Lady of the Semmerlak, and Yaw'nagrah's message was delivered to a striding heading toward Ulvenholm.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Orrin, the Civil Service scribe who recorded Eleonaris's statement, is a Highguard scribe teased for 'Highborn nonsense'.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris cited the Empire's success in driving the Jotun out of Kahraman as one reason for her celebration.

Navarr.t: A small Navarr striding on the trod through Brocéliande was surrounded by handmaidens of the Green Mother. They were not attacked, and were made the bearers of Yaw'nagrah's demand to meet the Spring Archmage alone.

Urizen.t: Elyssiathain of Urizen, Archmage of Night, was to be received by Azoth for a formal parley. Zakalwe said he was pleased with how Urizen's magicians had used the Circlet of the Master Strategist and offered to restore its magic.

We've been here forever.o: After the Summer Solstice, six eternals answered the archmages' plenipotentiary messages and set out the terms, topics and times of their meetings at the Autumn Equinox. Eleonaris broke with custom by asking for a formal reception in the Imperial Senate.

Semmerholm/Ulvenholm.t: Mentioned in passing: Ulvenholm was the destination of the Navarr striding travelling north from Greenstead when Yaw'nagrah's handmaidens stopped it.

Brocéliande.t: Yaw'nagrah's handmaidens and a briar messenger stopped a Navarr striding in the vallorn-held forest, a reminder that the Conclave's enmity does not restrain eternals where the Empire does not hold sway. Zakalwe also denied knowing of any ancient crystal crown lost there.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr striding that met Yaw'nagrah's messenger was travelling toward Ulvenholm in Semmerholm.

Weak and idle theme.d: The Freeborn Assembly unanimously assured the Islanders that they faced no enslavement and claimed the rebels had refused refuge, a claim the Islanders doubted. The Pride Assembly unanimously condemned allowing slaves to be taken on Imperial soil, and its words resonated far more. Seguran Freeborn spoke of their people's role in banning slavery twice, including Emperor Ahraz's emancipation of orcs, perhaps foreshadowed in a past-life vision. With the Suranni already dragged back in chains, the Islanders proposed a mandate urging every Freeborn to aid enslaved people. If passed, the Freeborn would act at once to protect any slaves crossing the border. A wider version could reach every nation.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Zemress Islanders fled the threat of Grendel enslavement, and the story recalls a Freeborn shipwright drowned when the Grendel burnt the shipyards.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn across the Coast began questioning their national assembly's stance and taking pride in their history of abolition. A proposed mandate would have them rise at once to protect any slaves crossing the border.

Weak and idle theme.o: After the Iron Confederacy attacked and enslaved Suranni rebels sheltering in Feroz, the Zemress Islanders of Segura spread their outrage among the Freeborn, and conflicting Synod judgements left many questioning the Brass Coast's stance on slavery. The Wind offered a Synod mandate calling on Freeborn citizens to take up arms in defence of escaped slaves.

Feroz.t: The Iron Confederacy was allowed to bring armies into Feroz and enslave the Suranni rebels sheltering there in full view, and this sparked the controversy.

Kalino.t: Mentioned in passing: the Duke of Kalino and his forces are named as those who attacked the slaves' camp.

Segura.t: The Zemress Islanders settled in Segura carried their abolitionist concerns to their Seguran neighbours, some of whom shared them and helped shape the proposed mandate.

Weaving tangled nets.d: The Commonwealth questioned the Liberty Pact's future and imposed a -1 trade penalty at Volkavaar, Leerdam and newly opened Murolosch over Imperial trade at Radosmo. It also pressed for news of its magicians trapped in the Lyceum. The Granite Pillar, Rod and Shield and Golden Pyramid aided the Commonwealth and earned gifts of Soldier's Booze, Hero Stones and war ring schema. In Jarm, the Celestial Arch laid groundwork for a possible ceasefire summit, the Shuttered Lantern gathered intelligence, and the Sevenfold Path met the Convocation of Virtue. The Silver Chalice saved hundreds in Lantir, though some returned cursed. Containment failed, and the Senate could commission an appraisal to find further ways to help.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Asavean Plenum suggested to the Jarmish that Cold Sun might be related to Dawn and that Jarm might question the Empire about it.

Highguard.t: Thaumiel of Steeplechase Toll, Highguard's Ambassador to Jarm, was received briefly by Lord-Magister Trescher. Veterans of the Highborn army the Granite Pillar advised the Commonwealth generals and earned a seasonal gift of Soldier's Booze for their general.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Commonwealth soldiers are recalled as having fought and died alongside the Freeborn in the fall of Siroc.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: some members of Jarm's Convocation of Virtue first encountered the Way while visiting Sarvos on mercantile business.

Wintermark.t: Finn Pridetalker of Wintermark, as Ambassador to the Commonwealth, faced scepticism over the Radosmo trade and pointed questions about the Lyceum captives. Lofyn Bloodcloak's Cold Sun experience was welcomed, and cursed Silver Chalice members planned to meet at the Tree of Names in the Wintermark camp.

Weaving tangled nets.o: In Spring 388YE the Cold Sun incursion destroyed the small nation of Lantir and broke out of containment into Jarm, the Commonwealth and the neighbouring borderlands. Six Conclave orders and the Granite Pillar had offered aid to both rival powers, while diplomatic tensions over Imperial trade with Zemelslo continued.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar's orders had it hold a strategic defence of Astolat to resupply while sending officers to advise the Commonwealth.

Madruga.t: Mentioned in passing: the fall of Siroc is recalled as a battle where Commonwealth soldiers fought and died alongside the Freeborn.

Necropolis.t: Mentioned in passing: contact with Sarcophan pilgrims three generations ago is listed among the origins of Jarm's Convocation of Virtue.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: conversations held while visiting Sarvos on mercantile matters are cited as one way some Jarmish came to the Way.

Weight of the world.d: Vasili convinced sceptical locals, used to Druj domination, that the Empire meant to inspire rather than demean them. Two obstacles remained: the miasma and the conviction that the Druj would return. All Imperial armies had left Ossium. The Ketsov suggested a major fortification, or the Empire could permanently station an army or win a sustained defensive campaign. Pillars were located in the Galath Fields and Nearweald, and regions with pillars would be 20% easier for the Druj to conquer. The many orcs of Ossium could not become Varushkan. The Senate could declare them foreigners to work there or escort them to Skarsind. At the Summer Solstice the Senate declared them foreigners.

Dawn.t: Ser Ancél Watcher's Dawn Assembly mandate inspired troubadours and questing knights to scour Ossium's wilderness, and they found the miasma pillars in the Galath Fields and Nearweald.

Druj.t: The Druj are gone from Ossium, but locals are certain they will return and kill anyone who aided the Empire. Their lingering miasma pillars would make affected regions 20% easier for them to retake.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: orcs freed in recent raids on Grendel settlements are cited for comparison, as is the troubled release of former Grendel slaves at Sarvos.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: experience from the Reikos campaign informs the Empire's understanding of the miasma pillars.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Senate could have sent Ossium's orcs to Skarsind, potentially swelling the nation greatly, though it was unclear the Imperial Orcs wanted them. In the end the orcs were declared foreigners, and the Varushkan assembly welcomed Imperial Orc preachers to Ossium.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium's orcs were not deterred from moving to Skarsind by its proximity to the Jotun, an unknown threat they considered far less terrible than the Druj.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the League ceded Misericorde in Holberg to the Sand Fishers, and freed Grendel slaves were once left on the docks of Sarvos.

Thule.t: Thule armies in Ossium bring locals little comfort. The Ketsov are nervous of the Thule's reputed thirst for artisans, and the Thule are hoped to deal with the miasma pillar in their own lands.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan Assembly welcomed the Ketsov and all of Ossium who would be Varushkan, and Varushkan settlers are arriving. However, the egregore cannot accept orcs, and the locals' fear of the Druj hampers integration.

Weight of the world.o: In Summer 383YE, Vasili Zoryakovich Zverokaz's Pride mandate prepared the people of newly conquered Ossium to accept the Way. Ser Ancél Watcher's questers found two more Druj miasma pillars. Locals still feared that the Druj would return, and the Empire faced a choice over the territory's many non-Druj orcs.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers were evacuated to Misericorde to fish the Semmerlak and its shores.

Ossium/Bittershore.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bittershore's miasma pillar was found and destroyed during the invasion.

Ossium/Bonewood.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bonewood is the only part of Ossium where the Thule have spoken with local people.

Ossium/Galath Fields.t: Ser Ancél's questers found a Druj miasma pillar in the Galath Fields; until it is destroyed the region would be easier for the Druj to reconquer.

Ossium/Nearweald.t: A Druj miasma pillar was found in the Nearweald; it awaits destruction, and while it stands the region is more vulnerable to Druj conquest.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers were evacuated from Ossium to Misericorde in Holberg, a considerable sacrifice for its inhabitants.

Karov.t: Mentioned in passing: any overland migration of Ossium's orcs to Skarsind would have to pass through dangerous Karov.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan settlers come to Ossium from Karsk, and any orc migration to Skarsind would have to cross it.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan settlers are coming to Ossium from Miekarova.

Ossium.t: Pride preaching left the people receptive to the Way, but the miasma and fear of the Druj's return, with no Imperial army present, hold back integration. The Senate declared its orcs foreigners, which could let them work for the Ketsov and other Varushkans and speed the territory's growth.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of Otkodov have made little attempt to speak with Ossium's people outside the Bonewood.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: veterans of the Reikos campaign remember the miasma, and experience there suggests one pillar per region.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: freed Grendel slaves were once told to head for Skarsind from the docks of Sarvos, which did not end well.

Skarsind.t: Skarsind was proposed as a new home for Ossium's orcs, which could have filled the sparsely populated territory to overflowing. The Senate instead declared the orcs foreigners in Ossium.

Weird Goodbye.d: After Imperial heroes slew two Jotun warbands tracking the Artok, Big Icebarn was marked with Hirmok and Jotra and Little Icebarn with Hirmok and Pallas. The Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq, Liv Tidgaring, could send Big Icebarn raiding into Jotun Skallahn or Tromsa, or hunting monsters and beasts in Sermersuaq. The Keeper of the Runegrott, Derowen, could set Little Icebarn to mining or to building commissions. Big Icebarn went hunting, which would aid Wintermark units fighting monsters there and could continue if supported by a thousand strength. Little Icebarn went mining, adding four wains of mithril a season to the Pride for a year.

Jotun.t: The Jotun lost two warbands that had been tracking the Artok, and they escaped Big Icebarn being unleashed into Kalsea to distract their jarls, because it was sent hunting instead.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's title-holders chose how to use the two Artok. Their military units gained help against the monsters of Sermersuaq, and the nation gained extra mithril from the Pride of Ikka's Tears.

Weird Goodbye.o: In Winter 386YE the Cold Hand of Sarda icewalkers proposed tasks for the Icebarn twins, two Artok marked with runes after the Summer Solstice. Big Icebarn was sent to hunt the monsters of Agramant in Sermersuaq, and Little Icebarn was set to mine mithril at the Pride of Ikka's Tears.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: Little Icebarn was set to claw out ore from dangerous, inaccessible veins at the Pride of Ikka's Tears in Suaq Fount, increasing the mine's output by four wains of mithril a season for a year.

Sermersuaq.t: Big Icebarn was set to draw out and kill the monsters of Agramant in the Suaq wastes, easing the work of Wintermark units hunting there. It would only remain next season if they supported it with a thousand strength.

Skallahn.t: Skallahn was one of the Jotun territories where Big Icebarn could have been sent to distract the jarls and aid Wintermark raiders, but that option was not chosen.

Tromsa.t: Tromsa was one of the Jotun territories where Big Icebarn could have been sent to cause destruction and distraction, but the Artok was sent hunting in Sermersuaq instead.

Welly boots.d: The Jotun retreated in good order into Hordalant, without their usual promise to return. Mathilda Fisher fled west with a handful of loyal followers when the Empire turned south towards Kahraman, but Bushel Sykes stayed behind. Neighbours who sided with the invaders now face long Bregas grudges. The Marcher National Assembly could pass a mandate witnessing General Amberlain's oath that the Strong Reeds will never abandon Bregasland. The oath brings yeofolk support but carries harsh penalties if broken. The looted Breadbasket could be restocked for 15 thrones or handed to House Greywater. It could also be extended to Mournwold. Sykes has openly appeared at Ottery, creating a probable trap for General Asenath.

Jotun.t: The Jotun abandoned Bregasland in an orderly retreat into Hordalant and took Mathilda Fisher's cause with them, notably without any boast that they would return.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire turned its attention south towards Kahraman, which let Mathilda Fisher escape.

The Marches.t: The Marches regain Bregasland but face bitter local grudges and a looted Breadbasket. The National Assembly has the chance to bind the Strong Reeds to Bregasland by oath, to reward House Greywater, or to extend the Breadbasket to Mournwold.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar left Urizen with its work done, and General Asenath credited Urizen and Warcaster Aulus with the speed of her march to the Marches.

Welly boots.o: In Summer 385YE four Imperial armies, the Tusks, the Strong Reeds, the Bounders and the Highborn Granite Pillar, moved to retake Bregasland, only to find that the Jotun and Mathilda Fisher had already fled. The liberation left lingering grudges, a looted Breadbasket and several open opportunities for the Marches.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: Mathilda Fisher was cornered at Graven Rock, beaten and ripe for capture, before the Empire's shift south let her slip away.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Bushel Sykes rows Mathilda through the mists out of the Grey Fens as she escapes.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: Mentioned in passing: Larkin Pewter, a Landskeeper from the North Fens, offered an Autumn charm so the Strong Reeds' oath could be sworn by the Lictors.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: The Granite Pillar force-marched to Ottermire, and Bushel Sykes openly appeared at the Ottery fishing docks. A small Sentinel Gate conjunction there on the Saturday of the summit, assigned to General Asenath, has all the hallmarks of a trap.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland was retaken without a fight as the Jotun and the Fishers fled. Its Breadbasket was left looted, and neighbours who backed opposite sides now nurse grudges. Bushel Sykes remains at large.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun pulled back from Bregasland into Hordalant.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's attention turned south towards Kahraman, giving Mathilda Fisher the chance to flee.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: food to restock the Bregasland Breadbasket would be bought in Upwold and Mitwold.

Mournwold.t: Marchers proposed extending the Breadbasket to Mournwold as a great work costing 35 weirwood, 15 white granite and 100 crowns. It would share 1080 rings among the territory's farms, but would do nothing for its miners.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Mathilda's fur cloak was a gift from the Jarl of Tromsa, and Anagar had urged her to stay in Tromsa.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: food to restock the Bregasland Breadbasket would be bought in Upwold and Mitwold.

What did the deep say?.d: A sailor, sole survivor of a wrecked merchant crew, carried Siakha's message: a champion would meet the Archmage of Spring in the Hall of Worlds, not under parley, and the civil service warned this could be dangerous. Ephisis accepted parley with the Autumn Archmage to discuss trade, bringing other interested traders. Janon's troubadour-emissary accepted parley with Archmage of Night Elyssiathain Endsmeet to discuss boons and asked for Kahendrin Wordsmith. Barien will attend Archmage Solomon's feast with four Summer nobles and reward the best troubadours with a token. Tharim, tired of repeated requests, sent the herald Shackle; agents of his court will discuss its nature under parley and may bring 'gifts' for the Conclave.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: in the sailor's tale, a Grendel ship sank Cinque di Sarvos's vessel decades ago and left its crew in shark-infested water.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: a bosun's mate from Hahnmark, Hervis Rohansson, is recalled as one of the shipwrecked sailors killed by sharks in a story.

What did the deep say?.o: Following the Autumn Equinox, five eternals (Barien, Ephisis, Janon, Siakha and Tharim) publicly answered the plenipotentiary messages sent by the Archmages, most accepting formal parley at the coming summit. Siakha's reply came by way of a monstrous shark-like beast and explicitly refused parley.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: the doomed sailor Hervis Rohansson in Cinque's tale is said to have come from Hahnmark.

What regulates the wheel?.d: Two weeks before the Solstice, a conjunction of the Door, Lock and Key severed the Hall of Worlds from the Imperial regio. A Freeborn magician found the new portal nearby, and the civil service marked it with obsidian stones. Three days before the summit, a Dawnish coven found the regio no longer gave an extra rank of lore. It still speeds rituals, stays a strong regio linked to every territory, and works with the Citadel Guard. A powerful shroud now hides the regio, and the Grandmasters of the Unfettered Mind and Shuttered Lantern were asked to lead the investigation. Every Penumbral Veil and Vale of Shadows across the Empire collapsed, Leviathan moved his visits to midday, and Sung's rituals continued as normal.

Dawn.t: A Dawnish coven that arrived early at Anvil was the first to find the regio's empowering power gone while trying to enchant knights. Dawnish Semmerholm is where the Citadel Guard is stationed.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: news of the broken regio spread to people travelling through Casinea, the territory Highguard holds, and divinations on Casinea were floated as a possible source of clues.

Jotun.t: Every Jotun territory the Empire has maps of, Skallahn, Tromsa and Hordalant, now lies under the strange magnitude 30 shroud. So do the Jotun-held Bregasland and Liathaven.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Therunin, held by Navarr, is named among the territories now covered by the new magnitude 30 shroud.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the shrouds tied to the eternal Sung in Spiral, held by the League, were not affected by the collapse of other concealing magic.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: almost all of Otkodov, held by Thule, is reported to lie under the new magnitude 30 shroud.

Urizen.t: An Urizen seer, Aquillia, foresaw the crisis, and Urizen stargazers revealed the collapse of shrouds and the new shrouds over the Empire. Urizen magicians confirmed the regio still channels rituals through the Citadel Guard, with an unusually strong sense of connection to the army.

What regulates the wheel?.o: In the Winter of 387YE the Imperial regio at Anvil lost its power to empower rituals, the entrance to the Hall of Worlds moved away from it, and mysterious magnitude 30 shrouds settled over the Empire and its neighbouring territories. Meanwhile a celestial conjunction let covens of the same nation work together freely during the Winter Solstice.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland, held by the Jotun, is named among the territories bordering the Empire now covered by a magnitude 30 shroud of unknown origin.

Casinea.t: News of the regio's failure spread like wildfire to those travelling through Casinea to the summit. Some magicians suggested that rituals such as Dreams in the Witch House or Eye of the High Places performed on Casinea might give hints about what happened.

Hordalant.t: Hordalant, a Jotun territory the Empire has mapped, is now covered by the mysterious magnitude 30 shroud.

Liathaven.t: Liathaven, held by the Jotun, is named among the neighbouring territories now covered by the new magnitude 30 shroud.

Otkodov.t: Almost all of Thule-held Otkodov is reported to lie under the new magnitude 30 shroud.

Semmerholm.t: The Citadel Guard is stationed in Semmerholm. Magicians channelling rituals through the army may experience sensory phantoms of the territory, such as Dawnish wine, winter blossoms or glimpses of castles and woods.

Skallahn.t: Skallahn, a mapped Jotun territory, is now covered by the mysterious magnitude 30 shroud.

Spiral.t: The shrouds in Spiral connected to the eternal Sung survived intact while other large-scale concealing magic across the Empire was wiped away.

Therunin.t: Therunin is named among the territories now covered by the new magnitude 30 shroud that seems to blanket the Empire and its surroundings.

Tromsa.t: Tromsa, a mapped Jotun territory, now lies under the mysterious magnitude 30 shroud.

What shall we do now?.d: Ilarch Maxatios thanked Ambassador Fintan Nighthaven for a storm warning but questioned continued trade across the Bay of Catazar. The Khiklotu Khrysoú did not intend to reopen trade in Therunin. Repairs at Issyk's docks stalled over a Sarcophan investor, though Imperial ships would be welcome. Kantor would now offer Sable and Blackened Key instead of orichalcum. Maxatios condemned trade in Yellow Lotus and demanded details of the pact Fintan had vaguely mentioned. Grand Ilarch Keloparia confirmed Imperial students may study art at Maykop. Dancia Terricos thanked Gabriel Barossa for his letter. Enough priests took part that Solokha was secured, a diplomatic success, though no list of visitors could be compiled.

Druj.t: The Druj had overrun Therunin and held the popular agema Menoetius, and Axou watched the Empire's foray into the Sarangrave from Ipotavo, the citadel guarding Axos against them.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel were listed among the dangers making Axou trade across the Bay of Catazar increasingly hard to justify.

Navarr.t: With Therunin lost and talk of the Navarr goading the vallorn, the Khiklotu Khrysoú did not intend to reopen trade with the Navarr even if sovereignty were restored. The Navarr Ambassador Fintan Nighthaven also faced Axou irritation over his vague pact remarks.

The League.t: Former League general Gabriel Barossa received formal thanks from Dancia Terricos of Ipotavo for his letter, and League plays were said to be in demand in Issyk, where troupes were welcome to visit.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Axou had been warned of storms in the Urizen territory of Redoubt raised by the Children of Wrecks.

What shall we do now?.o: In Spring 387YE the Civil Service reported on relations with the Citadels of Axos, which were slowly warming but strained by trade risks, a vague Imperial reference to a pact, and the loss of Therunin. Imperial priests had also helped the Axou largely cleanse the haunted ruins of Solokha.

Bay of Catazar.t: Storms, the Grendel, the Children of Wrecks and an Asavean bounty made Axou merchants question continuing their risky trade across the bay, and Maxatios sought reassurance the problems would be dealt with.

Redoubt.t: The Imperial Ambassador's warning about storms in Redoubt raised by the Children of Wrecks prompted Axou concern about the safety of their trade routes.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: news of the Empire's foray into the Sarangrave reached Ipotavo, the citadel that guards Axos against the Druj.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: Axos once tried to invade Spiral in retaliation for the fall of Solokha, which they blamed on the Empire.

Therunin.t: With the Druj overrunning Therunin and all Imperial forces withdrawn, the Khiklotu Khrysoú traders, who escaped being trapped at Peakedge Stead, did not intend to reopen their trading post there.

What will be, was not.d: Raziel of the Shattered Tower, Edna of the Chantry and Bartimeus all had their mandates upheld. Weirwood and mithril at auction halved, other materials fell, and white granite and ilium were withheld entirely. Faraden traders added to the distrust by claiming the auction was rigged. White granite will stay off the auction until the Senate commissions the Cinderpath Exchange, and the Constitutional Court ruled that its title could only be appointed by the Bourse. Three proposals emerged: the Invisible Cord Brokerage for Navarr weirwood in Seren, the Clever Magpie ilium hall in Kalpaheim for Wintermark, and the Hand of Guerra refugee hostelry beside the Seminary of Zemress, inspired by Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial plan to fortify the southern coast against the Grendel is cited as one of the competing demands on white granite.

Highguard.t: Following their assembly's urging, Highborn citizens withheld their white granite until the Cinderpath Exchange is commissioned, which would also feed projects such as the Virtue's Rest. The Constitutional Court ruled that the Exchange's title would be appointed by congregation owners through the Bourse, not by the Highborn Assembly.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Brilliant Shore white granite source was ceded to the Imperial Orcs along with Skarsind.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun hold the Pride of Ikka's Tears and parts of Sermersuaq, which Wintermark hopes to see freed.

Navarr.t: Navarr brokers, aggrieved that two of their three great weirwood forests are Imperial resources, proposed the Invisible Cord Brokerage. It would gather weirwood for the betterment of the nation under a Broker appointed by herb garden owners.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn assembly upheld Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra's statement with a greater majority, urging pride and support for refugees. This led to a proposal for a Hand of Guerra hostelry and a Freeborn national title to promote abolitionism.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule were ceded the Stonefield Ice Caves and the Silver Peaks, once a Wintermark source of ilium.

Wintermark.t: The mandate reminded Wintermark that it alone has no Bourse seat and has lost its key resources. The Suaq proposed the Clever Magpie trading hall in Kalpaheim to buy ilium from across the north and bring it home.

What will be, was not.o: Following three upheld Synod mandates from the Winter Solstice, Imperial citizens began withholding materials from the public auction at Anvil and looking for ways to strengthen their own nations. No white granite reached the auction, and several national ministries were proposed in response.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: Mentioned in passing: the Silver Peaks were ceded to the Thule along with the Stonefield Ice Caves, costing Wintermark its starmetal and ilium source.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Palaces of the Cardinals would make the White City the equal in beauty of Timoj, adding to the demand for white granite.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: the Heartwood of the Great Vale is cited as an Imperial weirwood resource that Navarr brokers resent not controlling.

Madruga.t: A hostelry and office, the Hand of Guerra, was proposed beside the Seminary of Zemress in Calvos to help refugees. It would need a Senate commission or wayleave, 20 wains of white granite and 40 crowns.

Miaren.t: Miaren, home of the Golden Trees, was proposed as the site of the Invisible Cord Brokerage in Seren. It would cost 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns, and would cut eight wains of weirwood from the auction each season.

Sermersuaq.t: If the Clever Magpie were built and Sermersuaq were freed of the Jotun and returned to Wintermark, the ilium available to the hall would increase, up to an option for 10 rings.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind was ceded to the Imperial Orcs along with the Brilliant Shore, leaving Wintermark without a white granite source.

What's good for me.d: The Jarmish House of Princes extended its ultimatum but asked the Senate to reassure them and urge the Commonwealth towards diplomacy. If it did not, ties would be severed. The Thule invited the Ambassador to Otkodov to a caucus forum meeting and asked for 120 crystal mana. Asavean families warned the Cavabianca Docks would close unless the Empire raised a statue or made a statement supporting the Plenum. Mathilda Fisher and the Jotun asked the Empire to cede or abandon Bregasland. Salt Lord Kaliact began two fortifications in Spiral and will renegotiate Urizen support for the Citadel. The Suranni sought help capturing fleeing Hand of Dumon members, while the Hand begged the Conclave for sanctuary.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: a quoted Marches Assembly judgement recalls that the Marchers left Dawn.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: they are named as an enemy of the Thule alliance, whose Ossium garrison has fought them.

Grendel.t: Salt Lord Kaliact is building two fortifications in Spiral and will renegotiate the Urizen arrangement there. The North Mareave Trading Consortium is buying 50 wains each of weirwood and white granite at reduced prices, and Grendel are courting the Asavean granite trade for Dubhtraig.

Highguard.t: Highguard fleets would suffer a 1 rank trade penalty if the Senate agreed to the Suranni request. Unlike Freeborn and League ships, they would get no benefit from a reopened Robec.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Asavea, Ashborn Pakt, is of the Imperial Orcs.

Jotun.t: The Jotun back Mathilda Fisher's bid to complete the conquest of Bregasland and would recognise it as a free nation. Without a treaty, they would likely support her by invading Mitwold and Mournwold; meanwhile the Thule fight them in Sermersuaq.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the new Ambassador to Jarm, Gelert Ashborn, is Navarr and secured the extension of the Jarmish ultimatum.

The Brass Coast.t: Commonwealth zauberer have joined the Lyceum Schloss in Madruga. The Suranni proposal would mean a 1 rank trade penalty for Freeborn fleets, followed by a reopened Robec with a trade bonus; Fleet Master Ezro remains ambassador to the Grendel.

The League.t: Sarvos risks losing the Cavabianca Docks unless the Empire mends ties with the Asavean Plenum. A Jarmish break would cut mana to the Tassato Mana Exchange, and League fleets face the same Suranni penalty and potential Robec bonus as the Freeborn.

The Marches.t: Mathilda Fisher, whom the Marches Assembly has condemned, demands that the Empire cede the rest of Bregasland. Refusal is likely to bring a Jotun invasion of Mitwold and Mournwold.

Thule.t: The Thule maintain their military alliance, fighting in Sermersuaq and defending Ossium. They have booked Lashonar's caucus forum to discuss the campaigns with the Ambassador to Otkodov and to receive 120 crystal mana (or quintessence).

Urizen.t: Urizen in Spiral are building mithril nets into the Grendel fortifications, and Salt Lord Kaliact wants an offer for allowing them to keep supporting the Citadel. Urizen fleets would face the Suranni-related trade penalty, and Tarquinius Ankarien remains Ambassador to Axos.

Varushka.t: The Thule garrison in Ossium has defended the Varushkan territory against the Druj. The Thule have also finished consolidating the lands ceded to them under the Winter treaty.

Wintermark.t: Thule armies continue to fight beside Imperial forces liberating Sermersuaq from the Jotun. Eska Crowspeaker of Wintermark, as Voice of Liberty, holds the outcome of the Liberty Pact meeting.

What's good for me.o: The Summer Solstice 384YE foreign affairs Wind of Fortune set out the Empire's dealings with neighbouring and distant nations. It covered the Liberty Pact, Sarcophan trade, a Jarmish ultimatum, the Thule alliance, Mathilda Fisher's demand for an independent Bregasland, Grendel activity in Spiral and Mareave, and a Suranni request to help crush the Hand of Dumon.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: Imperial armies still hold Ottermire, which Mathilda Fisher intends to conquer unless the Empire cedes it or withdraws.

Bregasland/The Rushes.t: Imperial armies still hold the Rushes, which Mathilda Fisher intends to conquer unless the Empire cedes it or withdraws.

Miekarova/Mieriada.t: Mentioned in passing: the page notes only that the Thule have completed consolidation of Miekarovan lands ceded to them by the Winter treaty.

Ossium/Webwood.t: The Thule have completed their consolidation of the Webwood, ceded to them by the Senate in the Winter treaty.

Spiral/Apulus.t: The Salt Lord is building great walls and a fortified palace at Apullian, using mithril nets worked by Urizen. The North Mareave Trading Consortium's representative is also based here.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: A Grendel fortification is rising at the southern end of the Twilight Gate in Ossuary, magically accelerated and due before the Autumn Equinox.

Bay of Catazar.t: Sarcophan merchants trade throughout the Bay's ports, and the Commonwealth fleet has left it. The Suranni propose that magistrates along the Bay help capture fleeing Hand of Dumon members.

Bregasland.t: Mathilda Fisher and the Jotun hold three-fifths of the territory and intend to finish the conquest this season. They ask the Empire to cede the rest or withdraw its armies so an independent Bregasland can be agreed by treaty.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the page refers to the recent evacuation of Feroz, aided by the Muffled Oar ritual and Commonwealth ships, and notes the harsh treatment of the few people left under the Grendel.

Madruga.t: Commonwealth zauberer, including Professor Michael Enden of Volkavaar, have settled at the Lyceum Schloss and founded a popular battle-magic duelling club.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the North Mareave Trading Consortium, which backs the Mountains of the Moon raid, is buying weirwood and white granite from Imperial traders.

Miekarova.t: Mentioned in passing: the Thule have completed consolidation of lands ceded to them under the Winter treaty.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold faces a likely Jotun invasion if no treaty over Bregasland is secured with Mathilda Fisher.

Mountains of the Moon.t: Mentioned in passing: the North Mareave Trading Consortium is said to back Paymaster Muireall's plan to raid the Mountains of the Moon.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold faces a likely Jotun invasion if no treaty over Bregasland is secured with Mathilda Fisher.

Ossium.t: The Thule garrison here has fought off the Druj, the Thule have completed consolidation of the Webwood, and they want to discuss the Ossium campaign at the caucus forum.

Otkodov.t: The Thule invite the Ambassador to Otkodov, Yevgeny Katzev, and two companions to the caucus forum to coordinate the alliance's military campaigns.

Redoubt.t: The Senate commissioned an embassy with the Grendel at Cargo in Redoubt, but no progress has yet been made on it.

Sarvos.t: The Cavabianca Docks will stop trading after the Summer Solstice unless relations with the Plenum improve. The Asavean families suggest a statue of Balo of the Foam or Lord Isso; a larger one would add a third rank to the docks.

Segura.t: Segura borders the Suranni territory of Arbonne. Baroness Katerine asks that its magistrates and militia help Suranni law enforcement capture fleeing Hand of Dumon members.

Sermersuaq.t: Thule armies continue to fight alongside Imperial forces to liberate Sermersuaq from the Jotun, and the campaign is to be discussed at the caucus forum.

Spiral.t: Salt Lord Kaliact is raising two fortifications, sped by Autumn magic and due before the Autumn Equinox. She will renegotiate the Urizen arrangement there but promises no change before then.

Tassato.t: Mathilda Fisher's emissary came to the Imperial Consulate in Tassato. A break with Jarm would also reduce the mana available to the Tassato Mana Exchange.

When I met you.d: Eanna Glimmerwater offered to take up to ten unlineaged humans to a hidden lantern that can bring out merrow lineage. Miriam of Ezkiah's Legacy sought an ongoing commission of Mendicant Cassocks for the Voices of Virtue. Madoc First Sight sought mercenaries for retrieval deals, and Imma of Ehud's Strike sought victims of a curse from the Spring Equinox. Ash Markedford brought Summer hukkup for Marcher mummers. The Ketsov family planned to attend an Ossium meeting. Jarl Ustigar of Kierheim came to Anvil seeking a fitting death, which might aid peace with the Jotun. Other arrivals included Brez miners hungry for dark tales, Green Shield veterans, Bal Blueraven, and Milusa Velkovan with the Tyrant-Boyar's knife.

Dawn.t: Freeborn entrepreneurs planned to drag a captured mandowla to the Glory Square in the Dawnish camp, offering champions prizes for surviving in the ring with it. The Brez miners also intended to seek out quiet Dawnish firepits.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are blamed for destroying Glimmerwater's home in Eastring and for overrunning Ezkiah's Legacy's chapterhouse during their conquest of Reikos.

Highguard.t: Several Highborn visitors were expected. The surviving chapter of Ezkiah's Legacy sought a yearly commission of Mendicant Cassocks for Senator Solomon's Voices of Virtue, and Imma of Ehud's Strike sought those cursed at the Spring Equinox. A Highborn farmer from Sombregate also accompanied the hukkup parade.

Jotun.t: Jarl Ustigar of Kierheim, uncle to Queen Yrsa Jansdóttir and released from his duties, led a Kalsea delegation to Anvil seeking an honourable death. The visit came with gifts, and the yegarra ghodi Eirik the Golden was willing to discuss human spirituality among the Jotun.

Navarr.t: Eanna Glimmerwater planned to visit the Navarr market to offer unlineaged humans a chance to see the merrow lantern. Madoc of the First Sight striding sought mercenaries for dangerous retrieval deals.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the mysterious Brez miners intended to visit quiet firepits in the Urizen camp in search of stories of darkness.

Varushka.t: The Ketsov family planned to explain their withdrawal of support for the Burgher of Ketsov at an Ossium meeting in the Varushkan camp. Madoc First Sight was recruiting at The Glade there, and Milusa Velkovan brought the Tyrant-Boyar's knife to show Alderei the Fair.

Wintermark.t: Jarl Ustigar hoped to meet the Golden Jarl and Iron Jarl in the Wintermark camp, and asked the three traditions to bring tokens of food. Bal Blueraven and Green Shield veterans mourning their captain Torlin also sought Winterfolk there.

When I met you.o: Ahead of the Summer Solstice 387YE, a range of visitors sent word that they would come to Anvil seeking meetings. They included a merrow steading from Therunin, a dying Jotun jarl, Varushkan families and traders, and Freeborn showmen with a captured mandowla.

Casinea/Casfall.t: Travellers on the road from Casfall encountered Ash Markedford leading a rowdy parade of hukkup that had crashed marriage festivities at Sombregate.

Casinea/Greatwood.t: Freeborn entrepreneurs captured a mandowla in the Greatwood's predatory wilds, despite such beasts not being native to Casinea.

Skallahn/Bjarkey.t: Mentioned in passing: Bjarkey is not named directly; the page concerns Jarl Ustigar, long-time ruler of Kierheim and Skallahn.

Therunin/Eastring.t: The Glimmerwater merrow steading lies beside a Day regio in the Eastring bayou. It was ravaged by the Druj, and the steading now hides nearby with its lantern.

Volodmartz/Brez.t: A pair of odd miners from Brez, whose descriptions never quite agree, travelled to Anvil claiming to have been invited, to hear stories of dark places.

Casinea.t: A mandowla, not native to Casinea, was reportedly captured in the Greatwood, and a parade of Summer hukkup travelled the road from Casfall. Casinea's Senator Solomon inspired Ezkiah's Legacy to support the Voices of Virtue.

Ossium.t: Ketsov representatives travelled to and from Ossium and planned to attend a meeting on Ossium's welfare at Anvil. There they would explain withdrawing support for the Burgher of Ketsov.

Reikos.t: The chapterhouse of Ezkiah's Legacy was overrun when the Druj conquered Reikos, and only half a dozen members escaped. They rebuilt after Reikos was reclaimed.

Skallahn.t: Jarl Ustigar, who has ruled Kierheim and Skallahn with it for decades, has been released from his responsibilities. He came to Anvil seeking a fitting death.

Therunin.t: The Druj destruction of Therunin forced the Glimmerwater steading into hiding, though they saved their lineage-awakening lantern. A conjunction offered a route directly to their hiding place.

Volodmartz.t: Two strange travellers claiming to be miners from Brez in Volodmartz came to Anvil seeking tales of darkness and creeping dread.

When Spring comes.d: The Drakes, billeted in Mitwold, beat Cold Sun and then storm-borne shark heralds of Siakha, losing about 30 soldiers; the Wayford Wanderers were wiped out. Siakha then offered illegal boons to the Drakes and to Marcher ritualists, and Marcher fleets raiding the Jotun returned with double their plunder. In Bregasland, House Greywater felt snubbed. Three households stood accused of collaborating with the Fishers, and the magistrates asked the Senate to draw a line, send in the magistrates, or let violence run its course. Bushel Sykes was killed by Imperial citizens. Jack confirmed that Mournwold Orcs could bond as Marchers, a mandate to do so was proposed, and a conjunction to Hap the Soft's farm opened.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Siakha's messenger to the Drakes arrived dressed in Grendel colours but claimed to serve the Maelstrom, and was received only because the Empire remained at peace with the Grendel.

Imperial Orcs.t: Bloodcrow Knott's statement of principle reached Hap the Soft, who invited Knott and other Imperial Orc priests, perhaps including Bloodcrow Udoo, to visit Golden Hoof Farm through a Sentinel Gate conjunction.

Jotun.t: Marcher fleets raiding the Jotun's Gullet Shore were guided by Siakha's creatures to vulnerable Jotun ships, settlements and caravans. In Bregasland, the legacy of the Jotun-backed Fisher occupation fuelled bitter accusations of collaboration.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr soldiers helped with the Upwold harvest, and a Navarr messenger carried Hap the Soft's invitation to Bloodcrow Knott.

The Marches.t: The Marches endured shark attacks in Mitwold and dangerous tensions over collaboration in Bregasland, and were offered illegal boons by the enmity-bound eternal Siakha. The nation also learned that the Mournwold Orcs could join it through the egregore Jack.

When Spring comes.o: In Autumn 385YE the Marches faced several crises. Siakha's shark-like heralds ravaged Mitwold until the Drakes drove them off, Bregasland seethed with accusations of collaboration with Mathilda Fisher, and the egregore Jack confirmed that the Mournwold Orcs could become Marchers.

Bregasland/Grey Fens.t: The Droverbill clan of the south-eastern Grey Fens were accused of taking Fisher money to keep the Feni quiet and of refusing to help the Greywaters, and Joan Droverbill sat on the Council of Bregas.

Bregasland/North Fens.t: House Brawness, a large North Fens household, was accused of sheltering the Jotun, taking Fisher payment and guiding smaller households to cooperate, and Steward Aldith Brawness sat on the Council of Bregas.

Bregasland/The Rushes.t: The Clakes of Beandown were accused of informing for the Fishers in return for land and goats. A clash over stolen goats left three dead, and Rory Clake and two members of House Hiswen were arrested.

Mitwold/Golden Downs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Downs are named among the places where the Drakes met and gutted Siakha's shark creatures.

Mitwold/Oddmire.t: The Oddmire Allfriars escaped the worst of the shark attack on their match with the Wayford Wanderers, and Oddmire was among the places where the Drakes fought off the creatures.

Mournwold/Green March.t: At Golden Hoof Farm, Hap the Soft shunned the League questioner Graime and invited Imperial Orc priests to visit. A conjunction allows up to seven people to visit the farm at the coming summit.

Bregasland.t: Feuds over collaboration with Mathilda Fisher, the snubbing of House Greywater and the killing of Bushel Sykes left the territory close to violence. The Senate was asked to choose between drawing a line, sending in the magistrates, or letting the Bregas settle scores themselves.

Mitwold.t: Storm-borne shark heralds of Siakha attacked across Mitwold, burning farms and salting fields, but the Drakes held them off at the cost of about 30 soldiers and the Wayford Wanderers foot-the-ball team.

Mournwold.t: Young Mournwold orcs went out to work across the Marches. Jack confirmed they could bond to the nation, and a Synod mandate to welcome them as Marchers was proposed.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: a minority of Marchers asked why the Mournwold orcs could not all simply move to Skarsind.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: some Mitwolders grumbled that the Drakes should have been in Tromsa with the other armies hunting Mathilda Fisher.

Upwold.t: Upwold stayed largely quiet. Marchers, Mournwold orcs, Freeborn and Navarr soldiers worked the harvest together while fortifications and billeted armies fended off Cold Sun.

When all the land is in ruins.d: Navarr thorns, one Wintermark captain and Night-woven champions defended Greenstead and Eleri's Stead against miasma, husks, newly cunning ettercaps and heralds of Yaw'nagrah. Small steadings in the vallorn's heart were overrun, and the Broch was besieged. The surge was expected to grow, needing 2,000 to 5,000 force from the Slow the Vallorn action, or Imperial armies, to hold. Options included Dawnish and Highborn mandates, Llofir's aid in exchange for amity and Tamarbode, Tharim's aid at the cost of Navarr herbs and forests, help from the Great Forest orcs, evacuation or a fight to the end. The Dawn and Highguard mandates were enacted. The Conclave rejected Llofir, placing it under enmity, and accepted Tharim's aid.

Dawn.t: Ranae de Rondell enacted the Banners of Rucastle mandate, so Dawnish military units that help slow the vallorn earn extra rewards until the Winter Solstice 383YE.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj presence is given as the reason the route to Boar's Dell from Drycastle is far less feasible.

Highguard.t: Hazelelponi of the Shattered Tower enacted the Blade of the Pilgrims mandate. Highborn congregations accept a rank penalty for a year so their faithful add strength against the vallorn in Brocéliande.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; the page only compares the ettercaps and the vallorn's past slumber to events in Liathaven, which they hold.

Navarr.t: Navarr thorns and vates bore the brunt of the fighting and held Boar's Dell and Elerael, though steadings in the vallorn's heart fell. The national assembly was offered rival mandates to either evacuate Brocéliande or fight to the bitter end.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: a single Wintermark captain, Cadoc Artair Skölsson, joined the defence, and the Kallavesi mystic Tremont of Cundahl presented Llofir's arcane projections to the Conclave.

When all the land is in ruins.o: In Winter 382YE the vallorn of Brocéliande surged against the liberated regions of Boar's Dell and Elerael. Some three thousand Navarr held it back for the season, while the Empire weighed reinforcements, Synod mandates, eternal aid and even abandoning the territory.

Brocéliande/Black Boughs.t: The Broch came under concerted attack by husks and ettercaps and could only survive another season if at least 5,000 force was committed.

Brocéliande/Boar's Dell.t: Defenders at Greenstead kept the vallorn out of Boar's Dell this season, but the region remains under growing pressure.

Brocéliande/Elerael.t: Eleri's Stead and Elerael were held this season, though a steading there suffered a vallornspawn attack. Elerael would be the first region lost if fewer than 4,000 force is committed.

Brocéliande/Terunael.t: Mentioned in passing: the ruins of Terunael lie at the vallorn's heart, and some of the oldest husks may date from the city's fall.

Reikos/Tamarbode.t: Llofir, which infests Tamarbode, asked for the region's cession and amity in return for aid. The Conclave refused and placed it under enmity.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The Great Forest Encampment of Chief Vallack is here; a Winged Messenger from Therunin's senator could bring his orcs to Brocéliande.

Astolat.t: Under the enacted Dawnish mandate, noble houses and villages in Astolat are to support Dawnish champions who brave Brocéliande.

Brocéliande.t: The vallorn was held back from Boar's Dell and Elerael for the season, but smaller steadings in its heart were overrun, the Broch was besieged, and the surge was expected to intensify.

Casinea.t: Casinea's congregations are called on by the Highborn mandate to send their faithful against the vallorn, at the cost of a rank penalty for a year.

Hercynia.t: Because the Conclave accepted Tharim's aid, Hercynia's herb gardens each lose two random herbs and its forests two resources for a year. It was also named as a possible new home for evacuees.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: its ettercaps and the vallorn's earlier return to slumber there serve as comparisons, and Navarr magicians fighting in Liathaven may also use Tharim's heart's blood boon.

Miaren.t: Miaren's herb gardens and forests pay Tharim's price for his aid. Venomous weapons for the defence came from Honest Twyll's Gardening Supplies there.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: its recent addition to the trod network eases trod-walking, and it was a possible evacuation destination depending on the Senate.

Reikos.t: Reikos is the only practical route for an army to reach Elerael, and its congregations bear the Highborn mandate's penalty. Llofir's garden at Tamarbode lies here.

Semmerholm.t: Semmerholm offers the only safe route for an army to Boar's Dell. Its knights of Rucastle aided Greenstead, and its people are urged to support Dawnish champions.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: walking the trods through Sermersuaq is noted as difficult.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named; the only related point is that the Druj presence makes an approach via Drycastle much less feasible.

Therunin.t: Therunin's herb gardens and forests pay Tharim's price. The Great Forest orcs sheltering here offered to help but are troubled that the Holt of the Oak commission has lapsed.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: walking the trods through Druj-held Zenith is noted as difficult.

When all this was trees.d: Weary and depleted after seasons fighting Imperial forces around Dawnguard, the orcs raised a great camp in the Lower Tarn Valley. Their young chief and experienced council insist on keeping their own culture and faith, and they rebuffed approaches from Therunin guides. Their army needs 50 Thrones a season after the Winter Solstice and wants weirwood or mithril to rearm. It will defend Therunin against the Druj but commits to nothing else. They asked the Empire to cede the Upper Tarn Valley, Lower Tarn Valley or Eastring to their own law. Unidentified briars accompany them. Caerwyn Summercrow gave them 50 Thrones, but they remain in makeshift camps awaiting an answer on land.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the orcs' depleted numbers are blamed on seasons of fighting Imperial forces in and around Dawnguard in the Barrens.

Druj.t: The Great Forest orcs pointedly distance themselves from the Druj and their slave-keeping. Their warchief would fight alongside the Navarr if the Druj invaded Therunin.

Navarr.t: The Navarr of Therunin are hosting thousands of foreign orcs at their Senator's invitation. They are being asked to give up one of their northern regions, and they are the people the orcs' delegation wishes to speak to at Anvil.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: the Senate's earlier support for the Hierro clan orcs in Segura is cited as a precedent for funding the Great Forest army.

When all this was trees.o: In autumn 380YE the orcs of the Great Forest, formerly the Peytaht, left the Barrens and entered Therunin's Tarn Valley at the invitation of Therunin's Senator, Caerwyn Summercrow. They brought an army of around two thousand and most of their nation, after the Senate declared them foreigners rather than enemies at the Summer Solstice.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the orcs were worn down by several seasons of fighting Imperial forces in and around Dawnguard.

The Barrens/Hope's Rest.t: The Great Forest orcs' army and most of their nation left the Barrens through Hope's Rest on their way into the Tarn Valley.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Eastring is one of the three northern regions the orcs have asked the Empire to cede to their control.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's presence in Greenheart is noted as already reducing Navarr control of Therunin.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: The orcs' great camp was raised here, and they remain in makeshift camps. The region is also one of the three they have asked to be given.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's presence in Sweetglades is noted as already reducing Navarr control of Therunin.

Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley.t: The Upper Tarn Valley is one of the three northern regions the orcs have asked to be ceded to their own law.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the previous arrangement with the Hierro clan orcs in Segura is given as a model for Senate support of a foreign orc army.

The Barrens.t: The Great Forest orcs abandoned the Barrens, where they had fought Imperial forces, and may have brought with them briars suspected to be anarchists of Dourfell Keep.

Therunin.t: Therunin now hosts the Great Forest orcs and their army, and they have asked for one of its three northern regions under their own law. With the vallorn holding Sweetglades and Greenheart, ceding a region would leave the Empire only a single region short of losing the territory.

When peace was far away.d: Lord-Magister Anton Trescher wrote candidly that relations could thaw if the Empire respected Jarmish sovereignty, stayed out of the Lantir War and helped against the scions of Cold Sun. Imperial captains now trade at Radosmo in Zemelslo, which the Senate judged a sovereign nation under the Imperial Consul's remit. Zemelslo offered to buy 200 wains of weirwood at 20 crowns each for a navy. Jarm proposed that the Senate expand and concede its embassy in Cargo, garrisoning it with warwizards. The House of the White Palm asked the Apothecaries Guild for 200 drams each of marrowort and bladeroot in return for a herbal. Jarm refused further talk of the shield Measure.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn are cited as distant cousins of the people of Sarvos and the Brass Coast, and a Commonwealth castle in Highguard's Necropolis prompted Jarm's embassy proposal.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the people of Sarvos are cited as cousins to the Highborn, by way of comparison with Zemelslo's kinship to Jarm.

Urizen.t: Jarm proposed that the Senate expand and concede its embassy in Cargo and station elite warwizards there. The Civil Service warned that this would remove Imperial oversight and could leave a hostile Jarmish force inside Urizen if relations collapsed. The Urizeni ritual Ethereal Courier was also named as a way to send weirwood Bourse notes to Zemelslo's intermediary.

When peace was far away.o: In Winter 387YE the Civil Service reported on relations with the Principalities of Jarm, which remained at peace with the Empire but under embargo. Trade via the Jarmish protectorate of Zemelslo had opened, and Jarm made several offers, including a proposal to fortify and take full control of its embassy in Cargo.

Redoubt/Limus.t: The proposed Fortified Embassy commission in Limus would cost 30 mithril and 90 crowns and give the Walls of Cargo the Jarmish Warwizards quality, adding 1,000 strength to the defence if enemies threatened the region. It would require conceding the embassy to Jarm.

Necropolis.t: Jarm cited the Commonwealth castle built in Necropolis, across the river Couros from Cargo, as the reason it wanted a fortified embassy to protect Jarmish emissaries on the river.

Redoubt.t: Jarm proposed that its embassy in Cargo be expanded and conceded, with Jarmish battle-magicians helping to garrison the Walls of Cargo and guard shipping on the Couros against Commonwealth interests.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: its people are given as an example of folk who are cousins to the Highborn, likening this to Zemelslo's ties with Jarm.

When something is lost.d: The Night magic brought dreams of a phantasmal forest and friendlier encounters with heralds of Sung, Sadogua and Azoth, along with a mooted idea of following it with Spring and Winter enchantments. The Star Forged, enchanted with Find the Best Path, completed the work in Siroc Bayou and helped claim Crucible. The Drakes, carrying Clarity of the Master Strategist, seem to be still exploring it. Only four units escaped. Hakima advise going to look for them. Military units may take the Find the Drakes venture, with Freeborn, Navarr and Marcher units most effective, and any Marcher may support the effort. Eternal plenipotentiaries or a Conclave Order could also help.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Fay Baker of Dawn commanded one of the four units that emerged from Crucible, and Dawnish units can join the rescue only at reduced effectiveness.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs and Fire of the South left Madruga to campaign against the Jotun in Bregasland.

Navarr.t: Navarr's new army, the Star Forged, emerged muddied but triumphant after helping make Crucible truly Imperial, and Navarr units contribute fully to the rescue of the Drakes.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn territory of Madruga is now wholly Imperial but steeped in Night magic. Iñez i Azul-Mar i Riqueza led one of the escaped units, and Freeborn units are fully effective in the rescue.

The Marches.t: The Drakes, first army of the Marches under Alfred Houtman Fella, are lost in Crucible. That has sparked an outpouring of support, and any Marcher may now help bring them home.

When something is lost.o: In Autumn 388YE a potent Night enchantment settled over Madruga just as the Drakes and the Star Forged brought Siroc Bayou and Crucible into the Empire. The Star Forged emerged triumphant, but the six-thousand-strong Drakes vanished inside Crucible and now need rescuing.

Madruga/Crucible.t: Crucible was mapped and garrisoned enough to become truly Imperial, but it grows wilder the deeper one goes, and the Drakes are trapped somewhere inside awaiting rescue.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: The Star Forged emerged from Crucible into Lightsea, expecting to meet the Drakes there, and rescuers may lead the lost army back to it.

Madruga/Quiet Grasses.t: Mentioned in passing: named as a place that might benefit from follow-up Spring and Winter enchantments, and as a possible exit for the rescued Drakes.

Madruga/Siroc Bayou.t: The Drakes and Star Forged finished the Corsairs' work and brought the bayou into Imperial control, fighting phantasmal soldiers whose blows wounded only mind and spirit, though enigmas remain.
