Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs and Fire of the South had joined the campaign against the Jotun there.

Madruga.t: A Night enchantment fills Madruga with dreams of a marshy forest and more frequent visits from heralds of Night, while its last two regions came under Imperial control and the Drakes were lost within it.

Mitwold.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, lost Drakes soldiers remark that they are no longer in Mitwold.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Upwold led the Marcher outpouring of support for the missing Drakes.

When the ship comes in.d: Missionaries working with Bonewall Rek were well received in the Commonwealth, Asavea and Sarcophan, but less so in Jarm, where the Sumaah urged caution. No schism was expected. Asavean families arrived to use the new Cavabianca Dock but docked in Oran, insisting it should have been built there rather than in Sarvos. Axos kept paying high prices for liao. Rigia grew less welcoming. A Sumaah delegation landed at Crown's Quay to pursue an inquisition of Bonewall Rek and Cole. Faraden laid the i Tsagaan matter uneasily to rest. The Delves had a surplus of Cerulean Mazzarine. The Commonwealth remained frosty, and the Thule refused to recognise the new Ambassador.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: Faraden traders are said to be slowly becoming more common in western Dawn as stretches of the Blood Red Roads near completion.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire is technically at peace with the Druj, but it is unclear how long that will last given recent developments in Dawnguard, and there is no trade with them.

Grendel.t: The Commonwealth showed little interest in joining the Empire's campaign against the Grendel. Rumours spread of a Sarcophan agreement with the Grendel to keep access to Imperial ports, and of Sarcophan merchants reselling Imperial goods at a profit in Dubhtraig.

Highguard.t: Chesed of High House preached the new Doctrines to a Commonwealth congregation in Leerdam. The Faraden investigator concluded that Ephrael of Highguard's killing of Laodicia i Tsagaan was almost certainly provoked. A Sumaah delegation landed at Crown's Quay in Necropolis.

Navarr.t: The Great Forest orcs and their human allies remain in Navarri-held Therunin, though they and the Empire are now actively discussing a treaty.

The Brass Coast.t: An Asavean ship docked at Oran in Feroz, claiming the white granite docks were meant to be built there. The Freeborn welcome to Asavean visitors had already boosted local paradour owners, and Faraden traders are common on the Brass Coast.

The League.t: The newly completed Cavabianca Dock in Sarvos risks going unused because the Asavean families expected it in Oran. Meanwhile, the Lodge in Tassato has helped keep relations with Jarm cordial.

Thule.t: The Thule refused to recognise Ambassador Juha the Cavespider until the Empire builds an embassy in northern Varushka or lets the Varushkans appoint the title. They have not withdrawn their trade network offer or their interest in the Gildenheim Runeforge.

Urizen.t: The Urizen Assembly's call for Commonwealth soldiers to join the campaign against the Grendel met little interest, as Commonwealth critics accused the Empire of hypocrisy over slavery.

Varushka.t: The Thule will deal with the Varushkan warlock Juha but demand an embassy in northern Varushka or a Varushkan-appointed ambassador. Faraden traders are also appearing more often in southern Varushka.

When the ship comes in.o: In Summer 381YE, a Wind of Fortune reported that Imperial missionaries had spread the Doctrines of the Howling Abyss and the Ancestors to foreign followers of the Way. It also surveyed the Empire's relations and trade opportunities with Asavea, Axos, Jarm, Sumaah, Faraden, the Sarcophan Delves, the Commonwealth and the orc nations.

The Barrens/Dawnguard.t: Mentioned in passing: recent developments in Dawnguard are cited as casting doubt on how long the Senate will stay at peace with the Druj.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Asavean families' ship arrived on the Bay, and Sarcophan merchants are a common sight along its shores.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Faraden traders are a relatively common sight in Casinea.

Feroz.t: Members of the Heraclien and Ragnabe families docked at Oran rather than Sarvos, insisting their agreement placed the docks within sight of the temple there. A representative was expected at Anvil to speak to the Ambassador.

Necropolis.t: A Sumaah ship arrived at Crown's Quay, landing Tipoa the Insightful and an entourage bound for Anvil to pursue an inquisition into Bonewall Rek and Bonewall Cole.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named; the page only notes the Urizen Assembly's efforts to recruit Commonwealth soldiers for the campaign against the Grendel.

Sarvos.t: The Cavabianca Dock, built in the Sarvosan district of Caricomare for the Asavean white granite trade, may go unused unless the dispute over its intended location in Oran is resolved.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lodge in Tassato is cited as aiding relations with Jarm, and Faraden traders are common there.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: there is no trade with the Barrens orcs, and peace with the Druj looks uncertain after events in Dawnguard.

Therunin.t: The Great Forest orcs and their human allies remain in Therunin with no sign of leaving, though treaty discussions with the Empire are now under way.

Where do we go from here?.d: Following Naomi of Virtue's Rest's proposal of three great commissions, the Master of the Koboldi commissioned the Crucible of Fate, restoring and expanding the forges of Spire Calator near Mount Lutum, long home to ushabti artisans. The Urizen Assembly may now pass one of two competing mandates, emphasising function or form, to embrace the Crucible and end Zenith's despair. The koboldi built themselves quarters beneath the spire, and Adamant has asked the Conclave to decide by declaration of Concord whether they may stay. The Radix of Truth and Eye of the Heavens remain possible. Parts imported from the League earned every League business owner a share of 140 ingots.

Druj.t: The Druj's desolation of Zenith left it bereft of hope, and their marauders still roam there, but the Crucible offers Urizen a way to shed their awful legacy.

The League.t: League workshops, notably the Wunderkind of Holberg, supplied the cogs, gears and instruments for the Crucible, and every League citizen owning a business received a share of a one-off payment of 140 ingots.

Urizen.t: The Urizen Assembly can now choose between mandates championing function or form to embrace the Crucible of Fate and give Zenith a new destiny, while still able to pursue the Radix of Truth or Eye of the Heavens.

Where do we go from here?.o: Adamant's koboldi completed the Crucible of Fate in Zenith's Spire Calator, hastened by an Autumn ritual, giving the Urizen Assembly the chance to enact a mandate that would lift Zenith from being bereft of hope after the Druj desolation.

Zenith/Iteri.t: The page names no specific region; Spire Calator near Mount Lutum, site of the newly restored Crucible and the koboldi's hidden quarters, is the focus within Zenith.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wunderkind of Holberg are named as excelling at the fine clockwork parts imported for the Crucible.

Zenith.t: The Crucible of Fate stands complete in Zenith, and an Assembly mandate embracing it would end the territory's despair, though tortured souls, Druj marauders and realm monsters still remain to be dealt with.

Where five winds meet.d: Asavean warships that raided Meade had gathered in Faraden waters, where Asavean agents court anti-Imperial nobles. The Celestial Arch was sent to investigate the Asavean threat. Faraden merchants refused to pay the Ambassador's wain prices. The Tchemetzi family offered 75 Thrones or a Spring ritual text for 25 wains of weirwood. The Blue Silken Scarf sought gloaming through the City of Gold and Lead. Faraden musicians now visit the Azure Chorus, and an architect proposed a parador there. Mistress Karadragha floated a Faraden enclave in Holberg, offered a delegation to Anvil (matched by one to Asavea), and the Senate abrogated the Gloaming Road.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Asaveans are noted to have intervened militarily to aid the Grendel.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is named as one of the nations a Faraden caravan might trade with along the Blood Red Roads.

Jotun.t: Jotun lands separate the Empire from Faraden, and Jotun tariffs weigh on overland caravans. The Lasambrian Jotun invasion of Kahraman is noted as having ended in defeat for the orcs.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Owain Farkas of Navarr was briefly the last Overseer of the Gloaming Road before the title was abrogated and his bid returned.

The Brass Coast.t: Faraden performers now visit the Azure Chorus, earning the Azure Sutannir Mina i Yashum i Riqueza an extra 2 crowns a season. Erdene Bataguin asked the Freeborn assembly to welcome Faraden pilgrims and offered to design a parador there if it does.

The League.t: Mistress Karadragha asked whether the League would accept a Faraden trading enclave in Holberg. She suggested their priests might be consulted, and said it would make an Imperial enclave in Caitun easier to offer in return.

The Marches.t: The Asavean raid on Meade, launched from Faraden waters, is at the centre of the diplomatic dilemma facing the Marcher Ambassador Ebenezer. The Tchemetzi politely declined his offer to send Marcher landskeepers to Pelabuhan.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark is named as one of the nations a Faraden caravan might trade with on the way to Holberg.

Where five winds meet.o: Faraden's ambassador answered Imperial approaches on trade, delegations and a possible trading enclave, while the Empire weighed its response to the Asavean attack on Meade, which had been launched from Faraden waters. The Senate abrogated the Gloaming Road during the summit.

Holberg.t: Faraden expressed interest in establishing a trading enclave in the city of Holberg, pending the League's willingness.

Kahraman.t: With the Lasambrian Jotun invasion defeated, work was completed on securing Kahraman's roads, a project that used Faraden kamkrags and builders of the Bataguin family.

Mitwold.t: The Asavean surprise attack on Meade was repulsed, with one warship sunk and another damaged. Its origin in Faraden waters prompted the diplomatic questions on this page.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: Faraden superstition about the dangers of the Sea of Snows, including cambion whales, explains their wariness of trading by sea.

Segura.t: The Senate abrogated the Gloaming Road, ending the overland trade of Faraden mithril for gloaming through Segura.

Where the river rises.d: The flood killed perhaps two hundred people, injured twice as many and left many homeless, sick and hungry. Lord Rain's heralds lamented that his offer to spare all lives had been refused. The Cerevado Nets were wrecked, though the seat holder received eight rings of ilium this season, and every bridge except the Sobral Bridge was destroyed. This cut the Sunset Roads and stopped armies crossing between Madruga and Segura or Feroz. Madruga now has seven regions, and no one holds a usable map for scrying it. Fausta Ankarien guided the Silver Chalice to give aid, and the Conclave sent the Rod and Shield and the Unfettered Mind to explore the marshes. The Cerevado Nets remain unrepaired.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish difficulties in the Barrens are cited as a sign of the challenges the Freeborn will face in reclaiming Feroz.

Grendel.t: The Grendel forces in northern Siroc Plains were caught off guard by the floodwaters, which scattered their scouts and baggage trains from the siege of Oran. They still notionally hold the new marsh there, and their commander at Mora's Rock in Feroz shows no sign of surrendering.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the challenges the Imperial Orcs face in Mareave are given as an example of what awaits the Freeborn in Feroz.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sobral Bridge survived partly because it was reinforced for Imperial armies during the Lasambrian Jotun occupation of Segura, and Bregasland's marshes are used as a comparison.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: a liberated Therunin going to the Navarr is cited as an example of how certain it is that Feroz will be assigned to the Brass Coast.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn bore the cost of their own ritual: hundreds were killed, injured or displaced along the Scorrero, the Sunset Roads were severed and the Cerevado Nets were ruined. They must also decide whether to reclaim a Feroz left wrecked by Rahab, which is expected to be assigned to them.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's marshes are named as a comparison for the new marsh in Madruga.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the Varushkan experience in Ossium is cited as a sign of the challenges of reclaiming Feroz.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq's assignment to Wintermark is used as a comparison for Feroz, and Kallavesa's marshes are compared with the new Madrugan marsh.

Where the river rises.o: After Freeborn ritualists broke the banks of the Scorrero to cleanse the Blight from Madruga, the river flooded along its whole course, killing or injuring hundreds in Kahraman and Segura. In Madruga, the floodwaters transformed the southern Great Grasses and Siroc Plains into a strange, magic-infused marsh.

Feroz/Afarjasse.t: Afarjasse is back under Imperial control and still gives easy access to Segura despite the flood's disruption.

Feroz/Cazar Straits.t: Mentioned in passing: Spring magics worked by the Children of Wrecks here and in Free Landing may have made the sea rise to meet the flood.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: The Rivermouth Bridge linking Oranseri to Siroc Plains was destroyed, so armies can no longer cross between Feroz and Madruga.

Kahraman/Gambit.t: The floodwaters thundered through arid Gambit, flooding riverside villages and wrecking farms and their irrigation ditches.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: Floodwater ran down the hills, briefly making it hard for workers to reach the Damatian Cliffs, which were otherwise undisrupted. Rumours of Inacia's Trove drew treasure hunters to the riverbanks, but nothing was found.

Madruga/Calvos Sound.t: Calvos Sound remains under Imperial dominance, and the waters receded away from it to leave fertile, if strangely altered, grasslands nearby.

Madruga/Free Landing.t: Free Landing stays under the Children of Wrecks, whose Spring magics there may have helped the sea rise to meet the flood.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: The river on Lightsea's border with Siroc Plains burst its banks. The old Siroc Bridge still stands, but the shifting banks may yet wash it away.

Madruga/Torres.t: Torres remains under Imperial dominance, and the receding waters left fertile plains of unusual grasses and odd beasts to its south.

Segura/Burnish.t: The flood surged through Burnish, washing out riverside villages, ruining buildings and destroying farms and irrigation.

Segura/Lucksprings.t: Cerevado's waterfront was flattened and people died, the Cerevado Nets were left in tatters and the Cerevado Bridge was swept away, severing the Sunset Roads.

Segura/Sobral Grasses.t: Sobral was badly hit, with its people given only enough warning to flee, but the reinforced Sobral Bridge survived as the only remaining crossing of the Scorrero.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the swollen river between Lightsea and Siroc Plains now flows more swiftly than ever into the Bay of Catazar.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the new Madrugan marsh is likened to the marshes of Bregasland.

Feroz.t: Feroz largely escaped the flood, but losing the bridge between Oranseri and Siroc Plains cut it off from Madruga. Wrecked by Rahab and abandoned by the Freeborn, it will need major investment to rebuild, and Grendel and Children of Wrecks forces still hold regions there.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the new Madrugan marsh is likened to the marshes of Holberg.

Kahraman.t: The flooding began in Kahraman's mountains, and many riverside settlements were washed away before their priests received the warning. The Silver Chalice could offer aid here, and the Sobral Bridge still links the territory to Segura.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the new Madrugan marsh is likened to the marshes of Kallavesa.

Madruga.t: The Blight was washed away, but the southern Great Grasses and Siroc Plains became a steaming, magic-infused marsh, and the ruins of Siroc were swept away or sunk. The territory now has seven regions, cannot be scried with any existing map, and remains outside Imperial control.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs' challenges in Mareave are cited as a comparison for rebuilding Feroz.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the challenges the Varushkans faced in Ossium are cited as a comparison for rebuilding Feroz.

Segura.t: Segura took the brunt of the flood: the Cerevado waterfront was flattened, the Cerevado Nets were ruined and the Cerevado Bridge was lost, cutting the Sunset Roads off from the wider Empire. Only the Sobral Bridge still stands.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq's assignment to Wintermark is used as a comparison for the expected assignment of Feroz.

The Barrens.t: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish challenges in the Barrens are cited as a comparison for reclaiming Feroz.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: a liberated Therunin going to the Navarr is used as a comparison for Feroz's expected assignment.

Where the slow river flows.d: The original Jotun host withdrew west, leaving the Corazón, Escuta and Hierro in Mitwold. The Drakes, Tusks, Golden Sun, Valiant Pegasus, Green Shield and the Forte Fidelis garrison held a firm defensive line. At Wayford the Lasambrians were ambushed crossing the Meade. Wild Spring magic, linked to the Green Willow and the Rivers of Life curse, raised healing geysers that turned the fight into a brutal drowning melee until both sides withdrew. Barbarian casualties were roughly three times Imperial losses. The Corazón looted Meade and Wayford's football trophies. Stephen of Sarcombe was not seen, but he armed the heirs of Red Walder, whose raids brought Banditry to the Meadows and both Downs.

Dawn.t: Lord Daemon Mortére's Golden Sun held the line in Mitwold beside the Drakes and Dawnish knights joined the Wayford ambush. The Golden Sun also helped drive off the heirs of Red Walder when they attacked baggage trains and refugees.

Jotun.t: The Lasambrian-Jotun armies lost the Meadows and suffered heavy casualties at Wayford, yet still held Meade March and Oddmire and carried off much plunder. The Jarl-of-Jarls and many champions reportedly view Stephen of Sarcombe as a liability.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: many Lasambrians at Wayford were veterans of the plains of Segura and the hills of Kahraman, and their struggles on Segura's flat ground are recalled.

The Marches.t: Marcher armies, militia and the Forte Fidelis garrison defended Mitwold and reclaimed the Meadows, but Meade and Oddmire stayed in Jotun hands. Jim Moor's murder dented morale, and the heirs of Red Walder now raid the Marchers' own lands.

Wintermark.t: The Green Shield under Iron Osric fought with honour and led the only Imperial offensive, driving the Lasambrians from the Meadows and gaining a tenth of the way towards liberating Meade March. Wintermark heroes also fought among the Imperial captains.

Where the slow river flows.o: In Spring 388YE the Empire's armies held eastern Mitwold against the Lasambrian Jotun and, led by the Wintermark Green Shield, drove them out of the Meadows after a horrific battle at Wayford. The Jotun still held Meade March, including the city of Meade, and Oddmire.

Kallavesa/Wittal Grove.t: Mentioned in passing: the page cites the recent assault on Kierheim as having drawn the interest of the western Jotun.

Mitwold/Golden Downs.t: The Imperial armies gathered at the Golden Downs, which stayed in Imperial hands, but the region gained Banditry as Red Walder's heirs raided there.

Mitwold/Maiden Downs.t: The Maiden Downs remained under Imperial control but gained Banditry because of raids by the heirs of Red Walder.

Mitwold/Meade March.t: Meade March, including the city of Meade, stayed in Jotun hands and was thoroughly looted by the Corazón, though the Green Shield got a tenth of the way to liberating it. Heroes have the chance to fight at Meade Meadow to recover the stolen treasure, the Beater Cup and a healing spring.

Mitwold/Oddmire.t: Oddmire remained under Lasambrian-Jotun control and was among the places the Corazón plundered.

Mitwold/The Meadows.t: The Meadows saw the bloody Battle of Wayford and were fully reclaimed by the Empire, though the Corazón looted Wayford and the region gained Banditry from Red Walder's heirs.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes passed through the outskirts of Alderly on their way to Mitwold.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes crossed the Chalkdowns en route to the Golden Downs.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes marched through Green March out of Bregasland.

Reinos/Chaveiro.t: Mentioned in passing: news of the Iron Confederacy marching into Chaveiro spurred the Corazón to flee home with their loot.

Reinos/Corghosa.t: Mentioned in passing: Aitana Redondo, the jarl holding the stolen Beater Cup, comes from the hills of Corghosa.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes marched out of Bregasland to reach Mitwold, and the Green Shield aimed to drive the Jotun west towards it.

Fjorknae.t: The Lasambrians plan to ship their Meade plunder over the Sea of Snow to hire a large warband of Fjorknae orcs unless Imperial heroes recover it.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: some Lasambrian soldiers at Wayford were veterans of fighting in the hills of Kahraman.

Kallavesa.t: Mentioned in passing: the recent assault on Kierheim is cited as exposing a vulnerability that drew the western Jotun's interest.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold was the main battleground: the Empire reclaimed the Meadows and held both Downs, while Meade March and Oddmire remained under Jotun control and were plundered. Healing Spring rains promise a bumper harvest, but bandits backed by Stephen of Sarcombe now trouble the territory.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes marched through Green March, Alderly and the Chalkdowns, and Imperial efforts to bolster Marcher Pride and Loyalty had focused partly on the Mournwold.

Reinos.t: Mentioned in passing: the Corazón are eager to return to Reinos with their loot, news comes of the Iron Confederacy marching into Chaveiro, and the jarl holding the Beater Cup hails from Corghosa.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrians intend to ship their plunder across the Sea of Snow to entice the Fjorknae orcs.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: Lasambrian veterans of Segura's plains fought at Wayford, and their weakness on Segura's flat ground is cited.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: much of the metal in a Jotun supply cache in Meade March likely came from the mines of Skallahn.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: the plunder sled is built like those used by the natives of Tromsa.

Whispering wind.d: Some said the wind began on the coast of Feroz, others in the mountain passes of Kahraman. Its words were always the same: Jotun in Liathaven, Lasambrians in Segura, Grendel off the coast, a hard time to be Free Born, and a good time for all hakima to talk. The speaker promised to bring olives and signed off "Cande i Riqueza". The sender was probably a Freeborn magician or coven. No hakima council had met since Britta's death, when so many hakima died that some called them a spent force. By tradition any hakima may call a council, which was private, open only to hakima and kohan. Only the Freeborn heard the words, though gossip about the wind spread widely.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the wind's message lists "Grendel off the Coast" among the challenges facing the Freeborn.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named in the message, which deals only with the Brass Coast's troubles and its hakima.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the wind's message cites "Jotun in Liathaven" as one of the threats pressing on the Brass Coast.

The Brass Coast.t: Freeborn hakima were called by a speaking wind to their first council since Britta's death, a test of whether these magicians remain a force in the Coast at a hard time for the Free Born.

Whispering wind.o: In Winter 379YE a magical wind blew across the Brass Coast, whispering to the hakima a warning about the troubles facing the Coast and an invitation to a council at dusk on the first full day of the next summit at Anvil.

Feroz/Fontargenta.t: Fontargenta marked one end of the stretch of Feroz coast where the speaking wind was said to blow on-shore.

Feroz/Oranseri.t: Oranseri marked the other end of the coastline along which the wind was said to blow, whispering its invitation.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: Some said the wind raced down the mountain passes between Serra Briante and Serra Damata.

Kahraman/Serra Damata.t: Serra Damata was named as one side of the mountain passes through which some said the whispering wind descended.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page; the message refers only to Lasambrians in Segura and other threats to the Coast.

Feroz.t: Some said the whispering wind began in Feroz, blowing on-shore along the whole coast and carrying its message to the hakima.

Kahraman.t: Others claimed the wind came down from the mountains of Kahraman, racing through the passes to spread its call to council.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: the message warns of "Jotun in Liathaven" among the dangers facing the Freeborn.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: the message names "Lasambrians in Segura" as one of the challenges confronting the Brass Coast.

Whither the seed.d: Corey Wayfarer's Autumn Equinox 383YE mandate, passed 190-0, sought ways to lift the thirty-year curse. Five options surfaced. Niamh Swan's Rest proposed the Brokers Chain, a single commission with offices in Peakedge Stead, Treji and Seren to stockpile ritual potions. Drustan Brocs Guard recalled that the Jarmish prince Raina Telep of Hordoba may hold a Spring ritual text able to break such a curse. Gethin of Stars End Striding devised a magnitude 30 Spring arcane projection costing 90 rings of ilium. Urizen's Citadel Guard could let the ritual be cast from Anvil. Elin Quiet Words negotiated Kaela's aid, at the price of the Navarr renouncing Liathaven forever.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as having taken Zenith from Urizen, one reason the Citadel Guard is in such demand.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: noted as having gained Spiral from Urizen through a peace treaty.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: their bloody war with the Navarr for Liathaven, and their destruction of Elin's home there, explain why Kaela's price targets that territory.

Navarr.t: Navarr families in Brocéliande face withering births from their own curse, and the nation must now choose between costly routes to lift it, including the bitter option of abandoning Liathaven for Kaela's aid.

Urizen.t: Urizen's Citadel Guard could act as a focus, letting the Navarr break the curse from Anvil if it moved to Brocéliande, but the army is badly needed at home and its future is uncertain after territorial losses.

Whither the seed.o: After the Navarr's Wither the Seed curse on vallorn-held Brocéliande began to devastate the fertility of the Navarr living there, the Navarr Assembly urged the nation to find a way to lift it. Several possible routes emerged, each with its own heavy cost.

Liathaven/West Ranging.t: One of the two regions the Navarr still hold in Liathaven; if Kaela's mandate passed, her followers and grim legions would swiftly claim it, and the Navarr would be expected not to resist.

Liathaven/Westwood.t: Still under Navarr control, but would be claimed by Kaela's followers if the Navarr Assembly accepted her price and gave up Liathaven.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Peakedge Stead would house an office of the proposed Brokers Chain, so the network would depend on this region staying in Imperial hands.

Brocéliande.t: The curse saps the vallorn but steadily reduces births among the Navarr there, and every option raised aims to lift it from the territory before its thirty years run out.

Hercynia.t: Treji in Hercynia would host one of the three offices of the proposed Brokers Chain, a commission that has not yet been built.

Liathaven.t: Kaela's price for her aid is that the Navarr declare their vigil in Liathaven ended, after which her followers would move to claim the remaining Navarr regions there.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: Gethin, who devised the ilium-powered Spring arcane projection, lives at Stars End Striding in Miaren.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: noted as having been ceded to the Grendel by the Senate in a peace treaty.

Therunin.t: Peakedge Stead in Therunin would host one of the three offices of the proposed Brokers Chain, and losing it would break the whole network.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: noted as having fallen to the Druj, weakening Urizen and stretching the Citadel Guard.

Who benefits?.d: Phaleron offered a formal parley to Archmage of Day Skywise Gralka, open to every Urizen bonded to Menos. It also withdrew its earlier offers of an emissary and protection for the Anvil library. Lashonar opened the Caucus Forum for a meeting with the Hierro warchief. Cathan Canae demanded a parley on the Lion and Unicorn conflict, with specified Wintermark delegates and a representative of the Dawnish and Varushkan forces that invaded Ossium. Sorin rejected amity but sent a herald to question the Winter Archmage. Ephisis declined but prepared offers for the Autumn Archmage. Arhallogen's orc emissary at Lomaa refused any public meeting and said it would take 'the logical next step'.

Dawn.t: Cathan Canae required one person who could speak for the Dawnish and Varushkan forces that invaded Ossium to attend its parley armed.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: an Imperial clerk recoils at how the Druj kept prisoners in the Crawling Depths at Lomaa, and Ossium is described as a Druj territory invaded by Imperial forces.

Navarr.t: Arhallogen, the Queen of All Spiders, pointedly refused any public, formal meeting with any Navarr, and its emissary twisted its mouth at the very name.

Urizen.t: Phaleron invited every Urizen citizen bonded to the egregore Menos to its formal parley through a special portal from the Anvil regio. Urizen's Elyssiathain is named as Archmage of Night for the Lashonar meeting.

Varushka.t: Cathan Canae required a representative of the Varushkan and Dawnish forces that invaded Ossium to join its parley, which concerned the conflict between the Lion and the Unicorn.

Wintermark.t: Cathan Canae demanded three Wintermark delegates at its parley: a Suaq, a Kallavesi and a Steinr. One was to speak for the warriors, one for the senators and one for the magicians, and none could ever have championed Eleonaris or Jaheris.

Who benefits?.o: In the run-up to the Spring Equinox 383YE, six eternals answered plenipotentiary messages from the Imperial archmages. Phaleron, Lashonar and Cathan Canae arranged meetings, Sorin sent a herald instead, and Ephisis and Arhallogen declined to parley.

Ossium.t: An orc emissary of Arhallogen appeared in the civil servants' temporary offices at Lomaa to deliver its refusal and its warning of a 'logical next step'. Cathan Canae also sought a representative of the forces that invaded Ossium.

Who can you trust?.d: The scouting revealed that the Amber Scorpion sept, under the buruk tepel Taramid Skinwreath, was moving from Oerwealt into Ghul'thak Forest with its black lotus while Thule forces pursued it. A Sentinel Gate conjunction let Imperial heroes attempt to kill Skinwreath, carry the fragile plant home in its water-filled basin, seize sept treasures such as Black Wealt Wasps, and defeat Yaw'nagrah's heralds amid the Druj miasma. If the plant was recovered, the Military Council would choose between having an Imperial herbalist study it, which would kill it but yield one dose of powder, or entrusting it to the Karass rootwise. Two skirmishes were also offered: protecting Lenna Karass in Saltmarsh, and destroying a Thule-targeted day regio in Gloomsea.

Dawn.t: Many Dawnish nobles and banners joined the expedition to spy on the Thule, and a Druj warband slipped into the Dawnish-held Barrens to seize the Karass shaman Lenna Karass.

Druj.t: The Amber Scorpion sept was moving its black lotus, treasures and serfs under Taramid Skinwreath with the help of Yaw'nagrah's heralds, leaving it exposed to Imperial and Thule attack. A Druj raid also targeted Lenna Karass, apparently to punish the Karass for drawing close to the Empire.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: numerous Highborn citizens and banners are listed among those who spied on the Thule.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: several Navarr are listed among those who spied on the Thule, and Kaela's Gift is noted as extending into Therunin.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: a single League citizen is listed among those who spied on the Thule.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: three Marcher citizens, including one of the Mournwold Sappers, are listed among those who spied on the Thule.

Thule.t: Thule forces were hunting Druj black lotus plants in Ulnak, and an Imperial seizure of Skinwreath's lotus would leave them furious and likely to demand reparations, though it would not breach the treaty. Their warlocks also sought to use a Gloomsea day regio to locate the Sawscaled Vipers' plant.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: three Urizen citizens are listed among those who spied on the Thule.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: many Varushkans are listed among those who spied on the Thule, and the Amber Scorpion sept is noted as having once dwelt in Ossium before Varushka claimed it.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: a sizeable group of Wintermark citizens, many from Stormspire, are listed among those who spied on the Thule.

Who can you trust?.o: After nearly ten thousand Imperial scouts joined the Karass in spying on the Thule and Druj in the Forest of Ulnak, the Empire gained an unexpected chance to seize a Druj black lotus plant at the Fetid Heart in Ghul'thak Forest. Doing so would certainly provoke a major diplomatic incident with the Thule.

Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest.t: The Amber Scorpion sept moved into Ghul'thak Forest, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction to the Fetid Heart there offered the chance to kill Taramid Skinwreath and seize his black lotus under a Druj miasma.

Forest of Ulnak/Gloomsea.t: Thule-allied warlocks were heading for the Islet of Calm, a powerful day regio in Gloomsea, and Imperial magicians were offered a skirmish to destroy it with Wind of Mundane Silence and hide the evidence.

Forest of Ulnak/Oerwealt.t: Mentioned in passing: the Amber Scorpion sept's forces are reported to have moved out of Oerwealt into Ghul'thak Forest.

The Barrens/Saltmarsh.t: A Druj warband slipped into Saltmarsh to capture the young Karass shaman Lenna Karass, and the Envoy to the Karass was charged with intercepting it.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, which lets Imperial citizens choose a painless death, is noted as extending into Brocéliande.

Forest of Ulnak.t: The forest was the scene of the contest for black lotus plants, with the Thule pursuing the Amber Scorpion sept and Imperial heroes offered the chance to strike at the Fetid Heart and at a day regio.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold Sappers banner appears in the list of those who spied on the Thule.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: the Amber Scorpion sept is said to have once dwelt in Ossium before the Varushkans claimed it.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: thwarting the Gloomsea warlocks would stop the Thule taking a black lotus back to Otkodov.

The Barrens.t: A small Druj raiding band crossed into the Barrens to capture Lenna Karass. Saving her would lead the Karass to replace true vervain in their tribute with cerulean mazzarine.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift is noted as extending into Therunin.

Who counts the path untaken?.d: The Imperial feint on Kierheim drew Jotun armies back across the Kongegőr, but Imperial forces had already withdrawn, and the Jotun now know the bridge is vulnerable. Jarl Igya Olgafsdottir has called a hetjuveisla at Gull's Isle Hall, with Ingrid Talon-of-the-Mark responsible for engaging. The smidr Harald Fourforge wishes to discuss limits on magic in war and asks Vossk to choose attendees. After the Loyalty Assembly's writ and Wintermark's statement against evangelism, the Jotun responded warmly to a sample Peerless Kinship aura. A General Assembly mandate is proposed to consecrate a shrine, helped by a Sentinel Gate conjunction at the Summer Solstice.

Jotun.t: The Jotun armies retook Skallahn and guarded the Kongegőr, and their jarls are preparing to feast and negotiate with Imperial leaders at the hetjuveisla. Many ghodi and warriors were also deeply moved by the Loyalty aura.

The Marches.t: A major Jotun force was pulled away from the fighting in the Marches to defend the north, but enough remains to keep threatening Mitwold and Bregasland.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark has long had a close, if warlike, relationship with the Jotun. Its National Assembly's statement of principle reassured the Jotun that the Gull Isle Meeting Place would not be used for preaching.

Who counts the path untaken?.o: The Jotun swiftly retook the land the Empire had seized in Skallahn, and preparations moved forward for the hetjuveisla at Gull's Isle Hall and for a proposed Loyalty consecration of a shrine at the new Meeting Place.

Skallahn/Ulfrsmoor.t: Jarl Ottesen of Ulfrsmoor was impressed when the murder of her thralls was solved, and she recommended the smidr Harald Fourforge to attend the hetjuveisla.

Tromsa/Tromsdalen.t: The hetjuveisla is a Tromsdalen custom: both sides bring food, drink and bards, and a day must pass after the feast before violence resumes.

Bregasland.t: Bregasland remains conquered by the Jotun, who have kept enough force in the south to go on threatening it.

Hordalant.t: Mentioned in passing: Hordalant is not named on the page, which deals with the wider Jotun war and the Meeting Place on Gull Isle.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven is listed among the lands the Jotun have conquered, which they call Ashvale.

Mitwold.t: The Jotun invasion of Mitwold continues; although forces were drawn north, the orcs left enough behind to keep threatening it.

Skallahn.t: The land the Empire had claimed in Skallahn was retaken without real resistance after the Imperial retreat from Kierheim. The Jotun now recognise that the Kongegőr bridge is under threat.

Tromsa.t: The hetjuveisla being held at Gull's Isle Hall is a Tromsdalen tradition of hospitality that lets feuding warbands negotiate in good faith.

Who goes there?.d: Kay de Revoile planned to open a magical pouch in the Dawnish Glory Square. Endric of Lepidus sought musical settings of Elayne Silverlark's lyrics at the Navarr Song and Story Circle. Hahnmark's revived Strengths of the Deeps coven wanted advice from herb-garden owners on whether to use a Winter boon from the Hungry Wolf. Ale di Sarvos offered a strange tombola with prizes including White Granite. Lost Lore Steading urged that Navarr priests advise and scrutinise vates. Mystics of the Aviary of Ishal sought fellow mystics at the Tree of Names. The herald Archipelago asked Jackdaw Larksong to lead a team inside him to cure his indigestion.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: several members of the Strengths of the Deeps coven died in what they called a badly mishandled battle against the Druj, after which the coven stopped coming to Anvil.

Navarr.t: Lost Lore Steading called on the Navarr to scrutinise their vates more closely, urging priests to advise vates on their oaths and on dealings with eternals, though the idea met a mixed reception. Endric of Lepidus also planned to visit the Song and Story Circle in the Navarr camp to hear new settings of Silverlark's lyrics.

Wintermark.t: The Tree of Names in the Wintermark camp was chosen as a meeting place by the Hahnmark coven weighing a Winter boon, by mystics of the Aviary of Ishal discussing the future role of mystics, and by the tombola-running mountebanks.

Who goes there?.o: Several groups and individuals announced plans to come to Anvil for the Summer Solstice, each with business of their own. They included a Dawnish enchanter, a Highborn scholar, a Hahnmark coven, mountebanks, a Navarr steading, Wintermark mystics and a Summer herald seeking help.

Hahnmark.t: The Strengths of the Deeps coven had returned to their old hall at Gulnar's Deeps and begun clearing a neglected Winter regio. They held a boon from the Hungry Wolf that might benefit all Hahnmark, and sought counsel from the territory's herb-garden owners before deciding whether to use it.

Miaren.t: Lost Lore Steading in Miaren, known for valuing Vigilance and Wisdom, sent out a call for priests to advise the vates. Its artisans made eye-and-thorn tokens to mark the priests who take on that role.

Wide azure skies.d: The Grendel brought down the Blood River Colossi and Fleisardh's cliffs, opening the coast to the Golden Winds and Shamal navies. These landed the Black Eels, Bone Nautilus and Hamsin, the last backed by Asavean mercenaries paid by the Plenum. Outnumbered despite Day magic, ice giants of the Isjättens Väggar, Rucraic's Redoubt with the Ramparts of Ashlar and Skouran battle-engineers, the Imperial armies retreated and made a bloody stand in Clisearn. Local orcs began quietly supporting the defenders, and amethyst-sailed Grendel ships were sighted approaching. A Sentinel Gate opportunity at Ohwinn Scour offered chances to summon Iskanders Donjon, negotiate with or kill Scutt-Tadhg, rescue the Tholdie Rotary, kill Evdokia, and curse Fergus Konnaugh.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the toppling of the Colossi is said to be strategy rather than vandalism, since 'the Grendel are not the Druj'.

Grendel.t: Grendel forces retook Fleisardh with five armies and two navies, aided by Asavean mercenaries, and pressed halfway into Clisearn, though the Black Eels' indiscriminate raiding alienated local orcs.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Winter Sun and Seventh Wave lost Fleisardh but held stubbornly in Clisearn, winning quiet support and new recruits among Mareave's orcs, with opportunities to bind the Clisearn families to them.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks left Mareave for Spiral before the fighting.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Winds and Shamal navies sailed south from Redoubt to join the attack on Mareave.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the Brine Turtle negotiator Scutt-Tadhg's role is likened to that of a Wintermark mediator.

Wide azure skies.o: In Spring 388YE the Grendel, reinforced by two navies and fresh armies sailing from Redoubt, drove the Seventh Wave and Winter Sun out of Fleisardh and pushed halfway into Clisearn. Magical citadels, an enchanted fortress and Skouran mercenaries slowed but could not halt them.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel navies sailed through Beoraidh's waters on their way to Fleisardh.

Mareave/Clisearn.t: The Grendel pushed halfway into Clisearn, held back largely by the Isjättens Väggar, while local families began giving provisions to Imperial soldiers and the three families faced pressure to choose a side.

Mareave/Eoradal.t: Orcs of Eoradal came to watch the enchanted defenders of Rucraic's Redoubt, and a few would-be warriors quietly asked the Sannite about the Unshackled and the Empire.

Mareave/Fleisardh.t: Grendel ritual magic collapsed the Blood River Colossi and the coastal cliffs, poisoning the shore, and the Grendel drove the Imperial armies out of the region entirely.

Mareave/Icarion.t: Mentioned in passing: Grendel ships sailed past its cliffs, and its orcs came to view the sigils of Rucraic's Redoubt.

Mareave/Nadir.t: A frozen citadel rose in Nadir to support the Empire, and some local orcs came to view Rucraic's Redoubt and asked about joining the Unshackled.

Mareave/Sinfoyard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel navies sailed past the cliffs of Sinfoyard on their way south.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Spring storm clouds gathered above the bay as Winter faded.

Mareave.t: The Empire lost its hold on Fleisardh and the Grendel are halfway to conquering Clisearn, with both sides still locked in fighting as more Grendel ships approach.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel Golden Winds and Shamal navies set sail from Redoubt to reinforce Fleisardh.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks left Mareave bound for Spiral.

Wild blue yonder.d: After a three-day diplomatic silence, the Salt Lords resumed contact without an official response to Spiral becoming a League territory, though merchants hinted at fury and demanded Retribution. The Broken Shore Market and Spiral Envoy positions lapsed. Paymaster Muireall's enclave in southern Apstrus refused Imperial law and taxes, and might open a mountain route from Mareave. Her envoy was due at Anvil. Asavean warships destroyed the Sanctuary of the Justicars and Shantarim, saboteurs burned Sarvos's Cavabianca Docks, and privateers preyed on Liberty Pact shipping in the Bay of Catazar. Faraden ties improved, but a coming Faraden–Jotun meeting threatened overland trade through the Lasambrian Hills. A Freeborn family was rescued from Feroz.

Grendel.t: The Salt Lords were blindsided by Salt Lord Kaliact's defection and are said to want Retribution, while Paymaster Muireall's enclave rejected Imperial rule in Spiral and the Broken Shore Market stood empty. Speaker Morna denied that any Grendel ships were involved in the Asavean attacks.

Highguard.t: Grendel traders and sailors were welcomed in Necropolis under Brother Wildfyre's mandate, despite the Seventh Wave's warnings, and Highborn captains were encouraged to tell of clashes with Asavean pirates. Accalon of Felix's Watch was asked to host the Liberty Pact meetings.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Pakt of the Imperial Orcs was listed as Ambassador to Asavea.

Jotun.t: The Jotun were due to meet the Faraden at the Spring Equinox to renegotiate travel through the Lasambrian Hills. The Lasambrian Jotun reportedly wanted the Faraden to trade only with them, which could end overland Faraden–Imperial trade.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Cedric Gallows and Fintan Nighthaven of Navarr were named as ambassadors to the Iron Confederacy and Axos.

The Brass Coast.t: Suranni lawkeepers continued crossing into Segura after Hand of Dumon cultists, while Faraden trade into the Brass Coast stayed robust. The rescued Kanza family settled in Madruga, and Freeborn corsairs helped contain the Asavean privateers.

The League.t: Spiral was now a League territory, and Apulian traders courted their new fellow citizens. Asavean saboteurs burned the Cavabianca Docks in Sarvos, and Sarvosan captains fought the privateers in the Bay.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Thule appeared only in further reading on trade with Varushka and the Northern trade network.

Urizen.t: Abel of Urizen served as Ambassador to the Grendel and Ariadne as Ambassador to Jarm, while captains sailing from Redoubt helped hold back the Asavean privateers.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka appeared only in a further-reading link about trade opportunities with the Thule.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: Eska Crowspeaker of Wintermark was listed as Voice of Liberty.

Wild blue yonder.o: In Summer 385YE the Empire's foreign relations were in flux: the Grendel were quietly furious over Spiral's defection, Asavean warships and privateers struck at Imperial and Liberty Pact interests, and relations with Faraden kept improving. A Grendel breakaway enclave also refused to accept Imperial rule in Spiral.

Spiral/Apstrus.t: Paymaster Muireall's Grendel enclave in southern Apstrus refused Imperial law and taxes but avoided violence. With her mountaineering gear and experts, she might forge a route through the Apstrus mountains from Mareave.

Bay of Catazar.t: Asavean privateers preyed on Liberty Pact vessels in the Bay, enslaving crews and drowning officers, while Imperial captains largely contained them. Broken Shore merchants kept trading in Imperial ports around it.

Feroz.t: Governor Rahab continued his work in Feroz and reportedly prompted the Asavean raids. The temple delegate Marsail Cailc vanished, and the Kanza family were spirited out of the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull.

Madruga.t: Grendel navies remained moored off the coast, and the rescued Kanza family settled there with mixed feelings about the war with Asavea.

Mareave.t: Muireall's enclave on the Mareave border could open a mountain route from Mareave into Apstrus, letting Grendel forces bypass the Apulian Way. Her envoy came from the North Mareave Trading Consortium.

Necropolis.t: Broken Shore traders and Golden Winds sailors were welcomed in its hostels and inns under Brother Wildfyre's mandate, though the Seventh Wave confirmed that more than traders may be getting in. Captains based there helped contain the privateers.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov was named among the smaller neighbouring nations with outsized influence on the Empire.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: captains operating from Redoubt were among those containing the Asavean privateers.

Sarvos.t: Asavean 'merchant' ships set fire to the Cavabianca Docks, which were destroyed beyond repurposing, though the Sweetwater Springs helped stop the blaze reaching the city. Sarvosan captains also fought the privateers.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: priests of the Pride assembly crossed the Sea of Snow to study the Faraden faith.

Segura.t: Some Suranni merchants still traded overland into Segura, but most border crossers were lawkeepers hunting Hand of Dumon cultists.

Spiral.t: Spiral's new status as a League territory went officially unanswered by the Salt Lords, who are privately enraged. The Spiral Envoy title and the Broken Shore Market lapsed, and Muireall's enclave refused Imperial rule.

Wild is the wind.d: Faraden regretted the Empire's withdrawal from the Lasambrian Hills and cancelled a planned envoy. Caitun now offered mooncheese instead of orichalcum. The Hakhandra collected sixteen cattle from the Marches and proposed Yakholme Grange in Upwold, seeking Marcher Assembly support. Work could begin on the Faraden Quarter and Firewind Market in Holmauer, which would later allow caravanseri along trade routes. Muhnkhabat war wizards were due at Anvil. Joint preaching against Asavean influence narrowly failed. The Ember Blossoms declined to teach Imperials, and the Liege condemned the Cinders' attack on the Champion of Vigilance. Faraden also sought introductions to Axos, Skoura and Otkodov.

Dawn.t: Faraden expressed interest in a victuals market in Dawn, prizing its fine wines. Astolat and Semmerholm were named as possible caravanseri sites.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: Hakhandra visitors regretted lacking time to visit Mareave and Feroz to see the Empire's herds.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Faraden war-wizard delegation arrived in Casinea on its way to Anvil.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Hakhandra showed interest in the Great Northern Herd but had no time to visit Skarsind.

Jotun.t: Faraden resented paying Jotun tolls and had backed Imperial control of Reinos. The Muhnkhabat came to discuss collaboration against the Jotun and were narrowly dissuaded from attacking a Jotun outpost en route.

Navarr.t: Faraden traders passed through Miaren, which was named as a possible caravanseri site, and the Navarr roadwardens were credited with keeping Imperial roads safe.

The Brass Coast.t: Segura was the main Faraden entry point and home to the embassy, and both Segura and Kahraman could host caravanseri. The Ember Blossoms refused the Freeborn Assembly's suggestion that they train Imperials instead of being smuggled to Asavea.

The League.t: After Holberg's Chamber of Commerce chose the Iron option, work could begin on the Faraden Quarter and Firewind Market, overseen by a Firewind Prince chosen by League business holders. Tassato was a possible caravanseri site.

The Marches.t: The Hakhandra collected cattle from Ambassador Ebenezer, began seasonal gifts to him and proposed Yakholme Grange in Upwold. They asked the Marcher Assembly to state its position through a statement of principle.

Thule.t: Mistress Karadragha asked Imperial ambassadors to introduce Faraden to the diplomats of Otkodov, among others. The Civil Service advised caution.

Varushka.t: Faraden would welcome a fabric and clothing enclave in Delev if the Overseer of the Westward Road confirmed interest, but only after work began on Firewind Market.

Wild is the wind.o: The Civil Service's Summer 387YE report on Faraden covered trade, diplomacy and religion. It noted Faraden disappointment at the Imperial withdrawal from Reinos, set out new opportunities for Faraden markets and caravanseri, and reported a Faraden war-wizard delegation and an assassination attempt by the Cinders.

Holberg/Holmauer.t: Holmauer is the site of the planned Faraden Quarter and Firewind Market, costing 70 weirwood, 30 white granite and 300 crowns, with Faraden matching the effort.

Holberg/Misericorde.t: Despite concerns that Faraden might shun the Sand Fishers of Misericorde, they could profit by selling lumber to Faraden traders.

Astolat.t: Named as one of the territories where a Faraden caravanseri could be built once the Holberg quarter was complete.

Bregasland.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, a Marcher battle-mage resented Jotun attacks on her home, first in Mournwold and then in Bregasland.

Casinea.t: The Muhnkhabat war-wizard delegation reached Casinea in a receptive mood. It planned to present itself at Anvil to see Imperial war magic, the Hall of Worlds and the Sentinel Gate.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the Hakhandra regretted they had no time to visit Feroz on this trip.

Holberg.t: The Faraden Quarter and Firewind Market could now be built in Holmauer. Once complete, it would raise business investment, create the Firewind Prince and draw many more Faraden visitors.

Kahraman.t: Named as a possible site for a Faraden caravanseri along the trade route to Holberg.

Karov.t: Faraden suggested a fabric and clothing enclave in Delev, if Varushkan interest was confirmed, preferring to avoid the forests.

Mareave.t: Mentioned in passing: the Hakhandra regretted they had no time to visit Mareave on this trip.

Miaren.t: The Hakhandra travelled through Miaren on their way to the Marches, and it was named as a possible caravanseri site.

Mitwold.t: The Hakhandra visited Mitwold's cattle markets and hoped to buy its delicacies and livestock in future.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Jotun scouts were described tramping over the Mournwold, home to the Marcher wizard.

Otkodov.t: Faraden sought an Imperial introduction to the diplomats of Otkodov in order to open trade, which would have to pass through Imperial lands.

Reinos.t: The Empire's withdrawal from the Lasambrian Hills disappointed Faraden, which had hoped Imperial control would free its caravans from Jotun tolls. The planned envoy was cancelled.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named on the page beyond any link to the Icy Crag Tourney the Faraden wizards hoped to enter.

Segura.t: Most Faraden caravans entered the Empire through Segura, where the embassy receiving the Hakhandra's seasonal victuals stood. It was also a possible caravanseri site.

Semmerholm.t: Named as one of the territories where a Faraden caravanseri could be built.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Hakhandra regretted they could not visit Skarsind and the Great Northern Herd on this trip.

Tassato.t: The Hakhandra came through Tassato, which was named as a possible caravanseri site on the route to Holberg.

Upwold.t: The Hakhandra proposed Yakholme Grange in Stockland to make it the Empire's premier cattle market and raise farm investment. They wanted the Marcher Assembly's backing first because of religious tensions.

Wildest dreams.d: Donations, including from Mournwold orcs, funded the Black Canal between Meade and Sarcombe, but it stalled for want of white granite and weirwood. For a year, ministries commissioned in Sarcombe would cost less. The Chestnut Cartel proposed an Alder of Sarcombe sinecure. Clearing Alderly could support a fifth Marcher army after a year, which mattered because losing Bregasland left the four existing armies close to the limit of supply. Proposed commissions included New Longstwick Market, a deep lift at the Singing Caves and Green Iron Hill. Stephen of Sarcombe remained at large. In two conjunctions, the Bailiff of the Downs had to stop Little Robin reaching Liathaven, and the Master of Sarcombe Metal Market had to rescue Wise Maggie from Jotun raiders.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard traders are occasionally seen in Sarcombe's markets haggling for fine metals.

Jotun.t: Jotun forces held Bregasland and were massing in Liathaven, threatening the Mournwold and Mitwold. A raiding party under Jarl Hyglak the Quarrelsome hunted a Sarcombe metal merchant, and Jotun escorts awaited the traitor Little Robin.

The Brass Coast.t: Mentioned in passing: Brass Coast merchants are common visitors to Sarcombe, and Kahraman miners might be drawn to work the deep veins of the Singing Caves.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: merchants from Tassato frequent Sarcombe, which also offers markets for the fine goods of League cities.

The Marches.t: The Marches were offered a canal, new titles and ministries in the Mournwold, and a route to supporting a fifth army. However, with Bregasland lost, its four armies would begin to deteriorate if it lost one more region of Upwold or Mitwold, or two regions of the Mournwold.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan traders are occasionally seen in Sarcombe's markets buying fine metals.

Wildest dreams.o: Sarcombe in Southmoor grew in prosperity three years after receiving its charter, and the Marches were presented with several opportunities in the Mournwold: a canal to Meade, new civic offices, forest clearance, deeper mines and a green iron outpost. At the same time, Jotun threats linked to the traitor Stephen of Sarcombe were pressing on the territory.

Bregasland.t: Under Jotun control, Bregasland's fens no longer supported the Marcher armies. The Strong Reeds were harrying the Jotun and Mathilda Fisher, while Stephen of Sarcombe's people worked with the Fishers to sway the Bregas folk.

Kahraman.t: Mentioned in passing: Stephen of Sarcombe fought in the Kahraman campaign, leading forces at Rojota and ruining its roads, and Kahraman miners might be hired for the Singing Caves.

Liathaven.t: Jotun were massing in Liathaven once again, a raiding party slipped over the border from there into the Mournwold, and the traitor Little Robin was trying to reach it to pass on intelligence.

Mitwold.t: Meade was the planned terminus of the stalled Black Canal, and Jotun armies stood on Mitwold's threshold, with only the marshes of Oddmire between them and Meade. Losing a single region here would leave the Marcher armies without enough supply.

Mournwold.t: The Mournwold prospered around Sarcombe and was offered several opportunities: a canal, civic offices, the clearance of Alderly, deep mining and a green iron outpost. It also faced Jotun raids and the traitor Little Robin, and losing two of its regions would leave the Marcher armies without enough supply.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not named; the page refers only to occasional Varushkan traders in Sarcombe.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Tassato merchants are common visitors to Sarcombe, and its miners might be attracted to the deep veins of the Singing Caves.

Upwold.t: The presence of orc labourers on the canal raised eyebrows in Upwold, and losing a single Upwold region would leave all four Marcher armies without enough supply.

Will to survive.d: Whittle's friars, aided by liao donated to Whittle folk staying in Overton, began dedicating converts to Hatred, and hallowed weapons and consecrated campfires appeared across the Mournwold. A Statement of Principle backing Hatred of the Jotun, with a named priest providing 50 liao each season, would make every Mournwold region easier to retake by fostering resistance, though magistrates warned of possible condemnation for religious crimes. A rival statement denouncing Hatred, backed by 25 liao, would halt it but could push young Marchers to fight for the Jotun. The Drakes, Granite Pillar, Strong Reeds, Tusks and Winter Sun could use the "Into the Abyss" order while fighting in the Mournwold.

Jotun.t: Their newly conquered hold on the Mournwold faced Marcher resistance fuelled by Hatred, which could make every region easier for the Empire to retake, and Imperial armies could choose to fight them with an order that rejected the Jotun's rules of honourable engagement.

Will to survive.o: After the Mournwold fell to the Jotun, friars from the isolated village of Whittle began openly preaching Hatred as the secret of their long survival, spreading hallowed weapons and consecrations among Marchers and Imperial soldiers. The Synod was offered a choice to support or denounce the spread of Hatred, and several armies gained a new order.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: Mentioned in passing: Marcher-folk who yearned to stand on the hills of Freemoor again were described as grieving the fall of the Mournwold.

Mournwold.t: Now wholly under Jotun control, the territory became the centre of Whittle's preaching of Hatred, with hallowed weapons and consecrations spreading among its people and the soldiers fighting there. Depending on the Synod's choice, it would either become easier to retake or see more young Marchers take up arms for the Jotun.

Will you believe?.d: The Sumaah Houses of Virtue declared Timoj the true beacon of the faith and opened it to pilgrims. Their missionaries criticised the Synod over the Temple of Balo in Feroz, the Asavean shrines in Tassato, the Yaelian Schism, orc paragons and ancestor reverence. Proposed responses ranged from refutation and driving the missionaries out to appeasement and excommunicating Sumaah. Doing nothing would cost congregations in Sarvos, Tassato, Redoubt, Spiral and Necropolis 1 liao and 2 votes. Mandates for appeasement, Solas's 'not bound' position, 'Not a Trickle' and 'Hinder Us Not' all failed or were withdrawn. The Synod upheld Jorma's call for common ground, leaving the response to Sumaah, and the missionaries kept preaching.

Grendel.t: Grendel's congregations in Spiral were among those set to lose liao and Synod votes if the Sumaah missionaries went unchecked.

Highguard.t: Bastion's standing as the heart of the Way was directly challenged by Timoj, and orthodox Highborn congregations in Necropolis were judged especially receptive to the missionaries.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Navarr priests were among those favouring appeasement and recognising Sumaah as equal but separate.

The Brass Coast.t: The Sumaah cited the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz as proof of the Synod's laxity, while Freeborn priests were among those urging appeasement.

The League.t: The League's orthodox congregations in Sarvos and Tassato faced losses, the missionaries attacked Tassato's Asavean shrines, and Erasmo di Tassato's appeasement mandate was defeated or withdrawn.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Sumaah dismissed 'whatever it is the priests of the Marches preach' as non-doctrinal belief.

Urizen.t: Urizen's sword scholar sympathies made Redoubt's congregations receptive to questioning the Synod, and Solas's mandate denying any fixed heart of the Way failed or was withdrawn.

Will you believe?.o: Sumaah missionaries preached along the Empire's southern coast, denouncing the Imperial Synod and promoting Timoj over Bastion as the heart of the Way. At the Winter Solstice the Synod rejected several rival responses and backed Jorma Steelhail's mandate urging the Empire and Sumaah to seek common ground.

Bastion.t: The Sumaah urged the faithful to look to Timoj instead of Bastion, and the Synod's chosen mandate cast Timoj as Bastion's counterpart.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: nations along the Bay of Catazar were where the missionaries were expected to erode support for the Synod.

Feroz.t: The Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz were held up by Sumaah missionaries as examples of the Synod tolerating false religion.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold is not named on the page, though Marcher priests' preaching was derided by the Sumaah.

Necropolis.t: Congregations in Necropolis were to provide 1 less liao and 2 fewer Synod votes by the Spring Equinox if nothing were done.

Redoubt.t: Congregations in Redoubt were to provide 1 less liao and 2 fewer Synod votes by the Spring Equinox if the missionaries went unchecked.

Sarvos.t: Congregations in Sarvos were to provide 1 less liao and 2 fewer Synod votes by the Spring Equinox if nothing were done.

Spiral.t: Congregations in Spiral were to provide 1 less liao and 2 fewer Synod votes by the Spring Equinox if the missionaries went unchecked.

Tassato.t: The Asavean shrines around Tassato were attacked as idolatry, and its congregations faced losing 1 liao and 2 Synod votes each if nothing were done.

Willow and rain.d: With no Imperial armies in Therunin, the vallorn advanced from Greenheart and Sweetglades. A force of 25,000 was set to claim the Upper Tarn Valley by the Autumn Equinox. Cunning ettercaps, husks and abominations spread, and the miasma pooled in Morrow's lowlands. Ossegrahn warded Peakedge Stead for a second season, but only on condition that the Senate grant the Conclave a declaration of Remorse to remove Rivers Run Red and Mountain Remembers Its Youth from Imperial lore. If this failed, Peakedge Stead, the Houses of Healing and later Thornsong House would fall, and Ossegrahn would turn away from the Empire. Two conjunctions offered chances to strike at Druj remaining in Greenheart and Eastring.

Druj.t: The Druj held all of Therunin except the vallorn regions, but their armies withdrew and left the vallorn to run wild. Pockets of administrators, guards and treasure-seekers stayed behind, and one group worked with heralds of Arhallogen to cede Eastring to that eternal.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the closing of passes into Jotun lands along the western Empire is cited as a parallel to why the Druj might want Therunin made impassable.

Navarr.t: The Navarr who came home to fight the vallorn instead suffered defeat by the Druj and now faced the vallorn with no Imperial army to help them. The Navarr Assembly urged the people to harry and resist the Druj, but too few remained to make a difference.

Urizen.t: Vallorn miasma was confirmed pooling in northern Morrow, and sentinels clashed with vallornspawn in its foothills. High spires were mostly above the threat, but those in the lower valleys or travelling at ground level were endangered.

Willow and rain.o: In Summer 387YE the vallorn unleashed by the Druj in Therunin began to spread across the territory, with its miasma reaching into northern Morrow, while only Ossegrahn's protection kept Peakedge Stead alive. That protection would end unless his price was paid by the end of the Summer Solstice.

Morrow/Altis.t: There were a few clashes between sentinels and vallornspawn in the foothills of Altis as the miasma settled in the lowlands.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Sentinels clashed with vallornspawn in Peregro's foothills, though its higher spires were mostly out of the miasma's reach for now.

Therunin/East Ashes.t: East Ashes had been ravaged by Druj war and slaughter. There was speculation that the Druj were working on something in the east, possibly at the Docks at Feverwater or Mudlark's Haven, to hold the vallorn back.

Therunin/Eastring.t: Druj working with heralds of Arhallogen sought to create a profane site in Eastring's forests. Unless the Champion of Wisdom, Valens Leos, stopped them, the region and the Thimble would belong to Arhallogen by the Autumn Equinox.

Therunin/Greenheart.t: Abominations rose in Greenheart as the vallorn pressed outward. The Spear of the Seven, Corwyn Heartsbane, was called by Firstblade thorns to defeat Druj fleeing through the miasma with vallorn-born goods.

Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley.t: Poison tainted the Lower Tarn Valley's waters, and the vallorn spread there most slowly, though even the poison could not turn it back.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Lord Rain's briar wall and wooden guardians protected Peakedge Stead and the Houses of Healing. They would be destroyed, and their refugees killed, if the Conclave did not remove the two rituals by the end of the Summer Solstice.

Therunin/Sweetglades.t: Abominations rose in Sweetglades and began pushing into regions long since reclaimed from the vallorn.

Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley.t: The vallorn was marching on the Upper Tarn Valley with a strength of 25,000 and would claim it by the Autumn Equinox if nothing changed.

Brocéliande.t: Mentioned in passing: there may still be a chance to stop Therunin becoming another Brocéliande.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: Harwyn Eternal's Assembly statement lists Liathaven as long lost among Navarr's losses.

Morrow.t: The vallorn's miasma spread into northern Morrow's lowlands and vallornspawn clashed with sentinels in Peregro and Altis. The problem was contained for the moment, though poisoned air threatened the lower valleys.

Sarangrave.t: Mentioned in passing: Sarangrave is not named on the page, which concerns Druj activity in Therunin.

Therunin.t: With no Imperial armies present, the Druj held the territory while the vallorn rose out of Greenheart and Sweetglades and advanced on the Upper Tarn Valley. Only Peakedge Stead remained a refuge, and only while Ossegrahn's bargain held.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj destruction in Therunin is compared to how they once swept through Zenith like a burning plague.

Windfall.d: The egregores found the Apulians ambitious, competitive and fond of intrigue, and lightly attached to their Grendel faith, but questioned their loyalty after Kaliact betrayed her fellow Salt Lords. With no eligible League business owners in Spiral, the Constitutional Court ruled the Senator for Spiral title did not yet exist, and the election was scheduled for the Autumn Equinox. Imperial law barred recent voters elsewhere from voting there for up to twelve months. Kaliact wanted the territory renamed Apulian, which needs a Senate motion. The Legacy, producing 22 wains of mithril, awaits Senate allocation as an Imperial or League seat. The fortifications Ballaghadruh and the Apulian Palace, garrisoned mostly by Apulian Orcs, passed to the Senate's upkeep.

Grendel.t: Kaliact's followers, who have renounced the Salt Lords of Dubhtraig, were being judged as possible League citizens. They have stopped calling themselves Grendel and now use the name Apulians, and their Grendel faith was raised as a possible obstacle.

The League.t: The League's egregores were to decide at the summit whether to admit the Apulian Orcs. Meanwhile the four existing League senators could make the decisions that need the unanimous agreement of League senators, and League citizens could now move businesses into Spiral.

Urizen.t: Renaming Spiral to Apulian would tell the Urizen living there that any hope of the territory returning to their nation was over. The Apulians suggested working with the Urizen on a joint bid for the Legacy's mithril.

Windfall.o: After Salt Lord Kaliact's treaty let the Wolves of War take Spiral in a single season, the League egregores Harlequin and Innamorata weighed whether Kaliact's Apulian Orcs could join the League, setting a final decision for Saturday of the Summer Solstice summit. The Senate was left to settle the territory's name, its senator and the Legacy mithril mine.

Spiral/Ossuary.t: Ossuary holds the Legacy, a great mithril mine producing 22 wains each season. It was technically under Kaliact's control and awaited allocation by the Senate, and any mithril not allocated would be kept for the first person appointed to the seat.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not referred to directly in the text.

Holberg.t: The Senator for Holberg was one of the four League senators able to make the decisions that need all League senators to agree. Holberg business owners who move to Spiral cannot vote there until Spring 386YE.

Sarvos.t: It was unclear whether the people of Sarvos would welcome the orcs who had occupied their city. Sarvos business owners who move to Spiral cannot vote there until Summer 386YE, although congregation leaders could buy a business in Spiral and vote normally.

Spiral.t: Spiral became part of the League, but its Senator title was ruled not yet to exist, with an election set for the Autumn Equinox. Kaliact pressed to rename it Apulian, and the Senate took on upkeep of Ballaghadruh and the Apulian Palace.

Tassato.t: The Senator for Tassato could share in the decisions that need all League senators to agree, such as appointing the Steward of the Tassato Mana Exchange. Tassatan business owners who move to Spiral now could vote in its Autumn Equinox election.

Temeschwar.t: The egregores judged the Apulians every bit as ruthless as the Temeschwari. Temeschwar business owners who move to Spiral cannot vote there until Winter 385YE.

Winds and flames.d: The Liege Tchinua Ganbatar has favoured closer ties with the Empire since a coup in 384YE, and Mistress Singua Karadragha now serves as ambassador. High Lady Togene Altsanig opposes the Empire and appears to have Asavean allies. Many Faraden blame the Marches for the razing of Moonwater Hall. The Empire could commission a new Faraden trade enclave as a great work, costing 20 white granite, 20 weirwood and 120 crowns, which would raise business investment in the chosen territory by one. Several trade offers were also on the table: Faraden interest in weirwood at about two thrones a wain, an offer of 50 thrones for 25 wains from Pelabuhan, and a request for up to 150 iridescent gloaming from the Blue Silken Scarf guild.

Jotun.t: The Lasambrian Jotun of Reinos heavily tax Faraden caravans, and Faraden would welcome an Imperial attack or conquest of Reinos to open a direct land route and secure its own border.

The Brass Coast.t: A new Faraden trade enclave could be built anywhere in the Brass Coast, raising business investment there. Any boost to trade from a conquered Reinos would likely also raise taxation in the south-west.

The League.t: Tassato is one of the territories where a replacement Faraden trade enclave could be built, raising business investment there.

The Marches.t: Many Faraden blame the Marches for the destruction of Moonwater Hall, and a Marcher ambassador, Ebenezer, has drawn suspicion. Mournwold, Mitwold and Upwold are candidate sites for a new enclave.

Wintermark.t: Hahnmark and Kallavesa are candidate sites for a new Faraden trade enclave, though building in marshy Kallavesa may cost more labour.

Winds and flames.o: In Summer 386YE, Faraden relations with the Empire were broadly positive under the new Liege of the Five Winds, though some Faraden, led by High Lady Togene, resented the Marcher ambassador. Faraden sought a replacement for the destroyed Moonwater Hall and would welcome an Imperial move against Jotun-held Reinos.

Upwold/Tower March.t: The original Moonwater Hall stood near King's Stoke in Tower March until the Senate had it torn down in Spring 384YE, an act many Faraden still resent.

Hahnmark.t: A replacement Faraden trade enclave could be built here, raising business investment in the territory by one.

Kahraman.t: As Brass Coast land, Kahraman could host a new Faraden trade enclave that would raise business investment by one.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa could host the new Faraden enclave, though its marshy terrain may increase the labour cost.

Mitwold.t: Mitwold is a possible site for a replacement Faraden trade enclave that would raise business investment by one.

Mournwold.t: Mournwold is a possible site for a new Faraden trade enclave that would raise business investment by one.

Reinos.t: The Jotun tax Faraden caravans through Reinos, and Faraden would welcome an Imperial expeditionary force or conquest here. Conquest would open a direct land trade route to the Empire.

Sea of Snow.t: Mentioned in passing: it is described as the dangerous sea route that few Faraden attempt, and which a land route through Reinos would avoid.

Segura.t: As Brass Coast land, Segura could host a new Faraden trade enclave that would raise business investment by one.

Tassato.t: Tassato is a possible site for a replacement Faraden trade enclave that would raise business investment by one.

Upwold.t: Upwold was home to the original Moonwater Hall and is again a possible site for a new Faraden trade enclave.

Wise and measured.d: The Scions of Cavan were executed or fined into destitution after a lengthy trial, and Axos handed fugitive Disciples of Sulemaine back to Imperial magistrates. Navarr traders remain viewed with suspicion in Issyk and Kantor, though the Grand Council does not endorse closing those ports to them. Mistress Isephenia began studying the vallorn at the Great Library of Hacynian. Axos withdrew its queries about the Barossa School of Imperial Strategy. It insisted the orcs of Thornfen would be evicted and left to the Empire. The Civil Service will raise a motion confirming the Thornfen treaty, which Urizen may veto. Fintan Nighthaven's body was returned to Axos, the Rebuker of the Unwanted will be handed back at the Summer Solstice, and Pathfinder Brog's request for library access was declined.

Druj.t: The Druj grip over the Mallum is described as broken after the Empire captured Thornfen, and a Druj raid on the Shield of Ipotavo was intercepted, recovering the Axou relic the Rebuker of the Unwanted.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: in the opening fiction an Axou grandfather urges his granddaughter to study with a tutor at the House of Spirits and train in Highguard.

Navarr.t: Navarr traders are still unwelcome in Issyk and Kantor, the Scions of Cavan's plea to the Navarr went unanswered, and Fintan Nighthaven's remains were returned to Axos in line with his family's wishes.

The League.t: Axos withdrew its queries about the Barossa School of Imperial Strategy, accepting the Empire's concerns about military security, though an international college of war might be discussed later.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: Axou scholars at the Great Library are reviewing vallorn research gathered from Imperial and Thule sources.

Urizen.t: The Urizen assembly may veto the Senate's administrative motion confirming the treaty, as it would concede a region under Urizen control to Axos.
