Wintermark.t: Wintermark's 'Shacklebreaker' Thanmir Hrafnar, Imperial Ambassador to Axos, was credited with heading off a backlash over the Scions of Cavan and holds the recovered Rebuker of the Unwanted pending its return.

Wise and measured.o: In Spring 388YE the new Axou ambassador, Ilarch Kario Skopos of Solokha, reported cordial relations with the Empire after Ambassador Hrafnar's "wise and measured words" eased tensions over the executed Scions of Cavan. Axos reaffirmed it would evict the orcs of Thornfen once the Senate confirms the treaty ceding the region.

Sarangrave/Thornfen.t: Captured by the Empire with the help of the Axou army of Ipotavo, Thornfen is promised to Axos, which says it will evict the orcs living there and leave their fate to the Empire.

Sarangrave.t: With Thornfen captured, the treaty intends to cede Thornfen, the Tower of the Skink and Sephals to Axos, which plans a new citadel in Sarangrave, subject to a Senate motion.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: Fintan Nighthaven's remains were carried to Crown Quay and loaded onto a black-sailed Axou ship.

Wish you were here.d: The Fellowship of Purple Sails planned a nautical festival and lobbied the Fleetmaster for a new maritime sodality. Hamish, apprentice to Wind Lord Morath, landed at Sarvos under parley to meet Vossk and the Ambassador to the Grendel. The Stzena of Tears, who had spread an ominous ballad through Weirwater, came with a plaguewulf, possibly Dravec the Hunter, to speak with Varushkans. Others included a go-between for Holberg's Kleists, Kaisa of the Sewn Tongue inviting five to meet the Falconer, a Ketsov representative, trappers with a caged beast, Beoraidh's Diamant Drakes, Urizeni Stargazers, Ferozi corsairs, and Great Forest Orcs. Some herb garden owners suffered dreams of being hunted.

Dawn.t: The Stzena's Ballad of Leohanr Gildaryn, which mocks Weirwater's protector, was taken up by Dawnish singers. Charlie Stinger and the Diamant Drakes both planned to call at the Dawnish camp.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Stzena's ballad recalls Ser Emrys dying alone after fighting the Druj.

Grendel.t: Hamish, apprentice to the Wind Lord Morath, came under a flag of parley to speak privately with Vossk and the Ambassador to the Grendel. The Ferozi corsairs also wanted to discuss what the Grendel intervention over Feroz meant.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highborn benefactors helped found the Fellowship of Purple Sails, and citizens of Bastion and Casinea encountered some of the visitors.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: Bal Blueraven stayed near Pakaanan's Pass even after Skarsind was granted to the Imperial Orcs.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun breaking Pakaanan's Pass may have prompted Bal Blueraven to leave their hermitage.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr messenger carried Kaisa's invitation, and Navarr had facilitated the earlier meeting between the Great Forest Orcs and Wintermark.

The League.t: League merchants co-founded the Fellowship of Purple Sails, a go-between sought the Kleists of Holberg in the League camp, and the Diamant Drakes planned to visit the League first. Some League herb garden owners were troubled by hunting dreams.

The Marches.t: Beetle-studier Charlie Stinger sought romantic counsel, and Friar Aube Warren of Upwold came to the Marcher camp to discuss loyalty and the Silver Chase with Kennett the Mummer.

Urizen.t: Urizeni Stargazers headed for the Urizen camp to share celestial revelations with the Astral Arcanist Serenus Starsong, while Vossk of Zenith Ascendant was sought by the Grendel envoy.

Varushka.t: The Stzena of Tears came to negotiate on patronage with Varushka's senators, and the plaguewulf wished to speak with its wise ones about a ceremony to Zoria. A Ketsov representative also briefed prospective Burghers of Ketsov, and some Varushkan herb garden owners suffered hunting dreams.

Wintermark.t: Great Forest Orcs came to share stories with Wintermark and to discuss helping defend Kallavesa. A Kallavesi hermit sought Derowen of the Forge, and the possibly Wintermark Kaisa of the Sewn Tongue issued an invitation to meet the Falconer.

Wish you were here.o: Ahead of the Spring Equinox 387YE, a variety of visitors sent word that they would come to Anvil, among them a Grendel envoy under a flag of parley, the Stzena of Tears with a plaguewulf, orcs from Beoraidh, a Kallavesi hermit and Great Forest Orcs keeping a promise to Wintermark.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: The independent city of Beoraidh sent members of the Diamant Drakes, a gambling and gladiator venture, to forge closer ties with its northern neighbours.

Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass.t: Bal Blueraven left their hidden hermitage in the hills above Pakaanan's Pass after the Jotun broke the pass and it reopened.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: citizens of Bastion were surprised to see the purple-and-pink clad Beoraidh orcs travelling through.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Oligu Predborvana Ketsov had stayed in Casinea for two months awaiting the summit.

Feroz.t: The Wisdom sect Sular's Spyglass was based in Feroz, and the Malazine corsair siblings, who stayed behind after the evacuation, sought fellow Ferozi corsairs to discuss the Wharfage in Oran and the Grendel intervention.

Hercynia.t: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's statement welcomed the Great Forest Orcs who had settled in Hercynia.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the go-between Etienne di Sarvos sought representatives of the Holberg luminaries Lula and Bernhard Kleist on what may be building work.

Kallavesa.t: The Great Forest Orcs hoped to discuss how they might eventually help with Kallavesa's defences, and the hermit-artisan Bal Blueraven was Kallavesi.

Mareave.t: Orcs of the Diamant Drakes, now residents of independent Beoraidh in Mareave, travelled north seeking business connections in the Empire.

Ossium.t: A representative of the Ketsov family of Ossium came to brief candidates for Burgher of Ketsov on her family's current difficulties and hopes for the title.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: citizens of Redoubt saw the Beoraidh orcs wandering through.

Sarvos.t: A Grendel ship under a flag of parley landed the envoy Hamish at the docks of Sarvos, where magistrates confirmed his safe passage under Imperial law before letting him go under watch.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: Bal Blueraven spent part of each year in Sermersuaq.

Skarsind.t: The hermit Bal Blueraven, who stayed near Pakaanan's Pass after Skarsind went to the Imperial Orcs, left for Anvil once the pass was reopened.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: citizens of Spiral saw the Beoraidh orcs on their travels.

Therunin.t: Mentioned in passing: Savra and the Great Forest Orcs were weary after their retreat from Therunin.

Upwold.t: Friar Aube Warren, one of Upwold's great listeners, set out with a member of their community to discuss loyalty and the Silver Chase.

Weirwater.t: The Stzena of Tears demanded hospitality from travellers in northern Weirwater, spreading a ballad mocking the province's protector and saying it would not be safe from husks.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: Vossk of Zenith Ascendant was one of those the Grendel envoy asked to meet.

With a flower, with a flame.d: At the Winter Solstice, the Voices of the Unbound Storm raised a castle of ice and granite in Kalpamark, while the Sussivari Frost Coven and the Moon and Stars raised four castles of mist over fens and marshes in Bregasland and Kallavesa. The Penumbral Veil moved from Ossium and Semmerholm to Madruga and Kahraman. A star settled atop the White City's highest basilica after a vision of a veiled procession. Basileus Flint, Lashonar, Surut and Barien announced games, contests and bargains. Eternals recruited champions for a Summer tourney for the Icy Crag. Hayaak offered trials in the Forest of Affray via Axmure, and Meraud sought the Celestial Arch's help rescuing magicians at Kalino Tower.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish coven Moon and Stars helped raise castles of mist in Bregasland and Kallavesa, and the darkness over Semmerholm lifted. Dawn's Glory Square was named as the stage for Barien's preaching tournament and Meraud's contest, while the Forest of Affray trials ran through a regio in Axmure.

Highguard.t: Bastion witnessed a vast silent light show that ended with a glowing star resting atop the White City's highest basilica for the season. The Highborn magister Ahzrukhal son of Night was also named as Sadogua's sole champion for the Summer tourney.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: the Eternal Family of Navarr was among five candidates invited by Hayaak to form a team for his Forest of Affray trials.

The Brass Coast.t: The Penumbral Veil settled over the Freeborn territories of Madruga and Kahraman. Fleeing Suranni magicians were seeking sanctuary in southern Segura, and Meraud's Freeborn friends offered to help them across the border if they were rescued.

The Marches.t: Castles of mist were raised over the fens of the Rushes and Ottermire in Bregasland, adding magical fortifications to the Marcher territory.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Sejanus of Urizen was named as the surviving member of Adamant's team for the Summer tourney and was asked to find new companions.

Varushka.t: The inky black night skies that had hung over Ossium dissipated as the Penumbral Veil moved to the Brass Coast.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark magicians raised a castle of ice in Hahnmark and castles of mist in Kallavesa and Bregasland. Barien extended his challenge to the Ice Walkers to the Summer Solstice, and the Voices of the Unbound Storm were invited to Hayaak's trials.

With a flower, with a flame.o: A Spring 384YE Wind of Fortune reported new magical fortifications in Hahnmark, Bregasland and Kallavesa, shrouds shifting to the Brass Coast and a wondrous light show over Bastion. It also set out many eternal-led opportunities, including the contest for patronage of the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun and a conjunction to rescue fleeing Suranni magicians.

Bregasland/Ottermire.t: A castle of mist was raised over the fens of Ottermire.

Hahnmark/Kalpamark.t: The Voices of the Unbound Storm raised a great castle of ice and granite in the hills of Kalpamark.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: A castle of mist was raised over Kallavesa Marsh.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: A castle of mist was raised over the marshes of West Marsh.

Semmerholm/Axmure.t: A Summer regio in Axmure, opened by Barien, gave access to the Forest of Affray for those bearing Hayaak's token.

Astolat.t: Mentioned in passing: Astolat itself is not named, though the Glory Square 'of Dawn' was set as a venue for Barien's and Meraud's contests.

Bastion.t: A magical display of stars and veiled figures filled the night sky over Bastion, leaving a glowing star atop the White City's tallest basilica spire for the season.

Bregasland.t: Castles of mist were raised over the fens of the Rushes and Ottermire, fortifying the territory with magic.

Hahnmark.t: A great castle of ice and granite drawn from the Breath of Winter was raised in the hills of Kalpamark.

Kahraman.t: The Penumbral Veil now hung over Kahraman, shrouding the territory.

Kalino.t: Kalino Tower, a watchtower on the Brass Coast's southern border, was the destination of a conjunction in which Imperial magicians were asked to rescue renegade magicians from Arav's priesthood.

Kallavesa.t: Castles of mist were raised over West Marsh and Kallavesa Marsh by Wintermark and Dawnish covens.

Madruga.t: The Penumbral Veil now hung over Madruga, shrouding the territory.

Ossium.t: The inky black night skies that had covered Ossium dissipated.

Segura.t: Renegade Suranni magicians fleeing Arav's priesthood were trying to cross from Arbonne into the sanctuary of southern Segura.

Semmerholm.t: The black night skies over Semmerholm cleared, and a regio in Axmure became the route to the Forest of Affray for Hayaak's trials.

Without a plea for mercy.d: A year of Synod debate prompted by Severin's sermon produced many constitutional proposals but no immediate change. Eska Crowspeaker's upheld Wintermark statement led to mandates, raised by Severi Jarlmarison in Wintermark and Rafe in the General Assembly, letting idle priests exchange congregations for military units. Tiana i Zaydan i Riqueza's mandate to boost Freeborn raiders at Beoraidh and open an illegal raid on Kalino's slave camps won a majority, but the Throne's Custodian of Virtue power demanded a greater majority and it failed. Veikko Bondforger's condemnation of Almodin Oktístis left his idolatrous constructions unaddressed. Rykana's recognition as an exemplar of Wisdom has inflamed doubts about orcs in the Way, with dissent expected by Spring.

Grendel.t: The successful raid on Dubhtraig freed Grendel-held slaves, another plan to free slaves from Mareave is underway, and a failed Freeborn mandate would have strengthened units raiding Beoraidh.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn pilgrimage is cited as the source of a penalty on Freeborn units, and Bastion was proposed as the site of grand Cardinals' palaces.

Imperial Orcs.t: The recognition of Skywise Rykana, following Thrace, has brought to a head doubts over whether orcs can be exemplars under the Doctrine of Human Destiny and the law of idolatry, with dissent likely to surface at the Spring Equinox.

The Brass Coast.t: The Freeborn assembly praised the Dubhtraig raid and welcomed the freed slaves, but Tiana's mandate to free more slaves, including those in Kalino, failed after the Throne required a greater majority.

The League.t: A Tassato bishop's refusal to preach on Thrace sets the scene, and Almodin's idolatrous works, including Lorenzo's legacies of virtue and the Great Game casino at Temeschwar, still stand in League lands.

Urizen.t: Urizen is named among the nations where many of Almodin's dubious constructions still stand, and a national statement supporting Veikko could have had local effect.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Aleksandra's Watch in Karsk is the only Almodin project whose Asavean elements were removed, at great expense.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermark assembly backed Eska Crowspeaker's call for idle stormcrows to arm their congregations, and Severi Jarlmarison raised a mandate letting Winterfolk priests exchange congregations for military units at the Spring Equinox.

Without a plea for mercy.o: In Winter 382YE the fading influence of Severin von Holberg's encyclical left several Synod matters in play: Winterfolk priests urged to turn their congregations into fighting units, a Freeborn call to free more slaves, the idolatrous works of the Asavean Architect, and a brewing doctrinal crisis over orc exemplars.

Mareave/Beoraidh.t: Freeborn units joining the raid on Beoraidh after the Winter Solstice would have gained an extra rank, but the mandate was not upheld.

Bastion.t: Mentioned in passing: one proposal was to build grand palaces for the Cardinals in the city of Bastion as a modern wonder.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: the Pallas Docks in Cargo are listed among the constructions tainted by Almodin's idolatrous work.

Feroz.t: The failed Freeborn mandate would have let Imperial captains raid across the border from Feroz into Kalino to free slaves.

Kalino.t: The Iron Confederacy's slave camps in Kalino would have been the target of an illegal Spring raid, but the mandate creating that opportunity was not upheld.

Karsk.t: Mentioned in passing: Aleksandra's Watch in Karsk had its Asavean elements removed at great expense, unlike Almodin's other works.

Mareave.t: A plan to free slaves from Mareave is already underway, though the mandate to strengthen Freeborn raiders there failed.

Redoubt.t: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; it is linked only through Urizen, where many of Almodin's idolatrous constructions are said to stand.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: retaking Sermersuaq is cited by Eska Crowspeaker as a virtuous cause for armed congregations to fight for.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the orc preacher who confronts a League bishop over Thrace in the opening story comes from Skarsind.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: the Spiral Sword runeforge is among Almodin's commissions still bearing idolatrous imagery.

Tassato.t: Tassato is the setting of the opening story, where Bishop Camina is confronted for never preaching on Thrace and dismisses him as irrelevant to humans.

Temeschwar.t: The Great Game casino outside Temeschwar and Lorenzo's legacies of virtue retain Almodin's idolatrous statues and mosaics, with no plan yet to deal with them.

Wolf in summer.d: Shortly after the Spring Equinox, Sarvos, Temeschwar, Tassato and Holberg were all struck by a malaise. It left people lethargic, restless or aggressive, and brawls and ill-considered duels led to several deaths. An unusual heatwave with no wind and little rain made matters worse and raised fears of fire. Every mana site in League territories produced only half its usual crystalline mana, sending prices soaring, and several weak regio collapsed, one causing severe injuries. Divinations identified the curse, which must have been cast from within the Empire, through the Anvil regio or Winter regio in each territory. Who cast it was unknown, though some blamed Agramant. The effects faded after the Summer Solstice and did not recur.

Dawn.t: Mentioned in passing: a troupe leader in the story pours a Black Unicorn vintage white wine from Dawn.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: years of fighting the Druj are blamed for the dreadful state of Holberg's sewers, which worsened the heat there.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Jotun raids are noted as an added worry in Tassato, where low river levels raised fears about fighting fires.

The League.t: Every League city suffered the curse and the heatwave, and League magicians, from troupe dramaturgists to street mages, saw their mana sources halved until the Solstice, while the culprit remained unknown.

Wolf in summer.o: In Summer 379YE a ritual curse, Icy Maw Devours the Spark of Essence, fell on all four great League cities, halving the crystal mana produced in League territories and souring tempers during a sweltering heatwave until it faded after the Summer Solstice.

Holberg/Holfried.t: Those who could afford to were leaving Holfried for the Summer, seeking cooler climates away from the heat, failing sewers and the smell of the Morass.

Tassato/Tassato Mestra.t: Mentioned in passing: a mean little cellar in Tassato Mestra is cited as an example of how even humble mana sites were halved by the curse.

Tassato/Tassato Regario.t: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though the curse and heatwave affected Tassato as a whole.

Holberg.t: Holberg was hit especially hard, its war-neglected sewers and the stench of the Morass making the heat unbearable while its mana sites yielded only half their usual crystals.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos endured one of its worst summers on record, with people collapsing in the streets, drinking water being sold and brawls over crowded street tables, while its mana production was halved by the curse.

Tassato.t: In Tassato only the river kept the city from rioting, yet it fell to its lowest level since 296YE, exposing things better left submerged and raising fears that there would not be enough water to fight a major fire.

Temeschwar.t: Even usually mild Temeschwar saw soaring temperatures, and its mana sites, including well-kept forest estates, produced only half their normal crystals.

Words to make things right.d: After the Senate declared the Woods-that-fell Feni foreigners, diplomacy and trade cut the raiding but did not end it. The northern band left Southridge and headed north through Kalpamark. A Suaq grimnir, Kaukana, said he would speak for them at Anvil. In the Mournwold, the Marcher assembly's call to employ the southern band on farms failed. Some Feni now trade herbs for food instead, and the Alderly beater Dyl arranged for their representatives to meet the stewards. Neither band is hidden. An army ordered to do so could wipe them out for about fifty casualties, though not legally while they remain foreigners. An intercepted key would also let an army destroy the Alderly Feni this Autumn.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on this page, which deals with Feni troubles in Hahnmark and the Mournwold.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is listed among the territories where settlements were destroyed when the great sinkhole collapsed.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar is listed among the territories where settlements were destroyed by the sinkhole that displaced the Feni.

The Marches.t: Marchers bore the brunt of the southern band's raids, and the assembly's call to employ the Feni as harvest workers failed, though dialogue reduced the raiding. Marcher stewards were invited to meet Feni representatives at Anvil, while Marcher armies could legally destroy the Alderly Feni this season.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's diplomacy through the Sentinel Gate helped reduce raids in Hahnmark, though the northern band refused further talks and moved north. Leaders of the Mark were told to expect the Suaq grimnir Kaukana at Anvil claiming to speak for the Feni.

Words to make things right.o: In Autumn 382YE, the Woods-that-fell Feni, displaced by the great sinkhole, kept raiding for survival in Hahnmark and the Mournwold. Envoys arranged to come to Anvil to speak for them, and the Empire learned it could destroy both them and the Alderly Feni by force if it chose.

Hahnmark/Kalpamark.t: The northern Feni band moved fast along the major trod running north-east through Kalpamark, avoiding Kalpaheim and the larger halls while raiding slightly more often.

Hahnmark/Southridge.t: The Woods-that-fell sheltered in Southridge's gullies over the Summer Solstice, ambushing travellers. Six weeks ago they left northward, joined by some local Feni.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: The insular Alderly Feni were left exposed by an intercepted key that would let an army destroy their hidden settlement for about 120 casualties, if done this Autumn. Meanwhile the Alderly beater Dyl arranged for Woods-that-fell representatives to come to Anvil.

Mournwold/Chalkdowns.t: The southern band camped on the Chalkdowns, raiding for food and livestock. Local farms' offers of harvest work failed, and ex-Jotun orc farms bought off the raiders with tribute.

Mournwold/Freemoor.t: The people of Whittle formed a makeshift militia that lost no produce and drove off Feni raiders until they learned to avoid Whittle Hill.

Mournwold/Green March.t: Mentioned in passing: the Alderly Feni have occasionally raided Green March in the past.

Casinea.t: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on this page.

Hahnmark.t: The northern Woods-that-fell band, estimated at five hundred to eight hundred, raided halls and ambushed travellers on the roads to Kalpaheim before moving north. Any army there ordered to destroy them could break the band for about fifty casualties.

Miaren.t: Mentioned in passing: settlements in Miaren were destroyed when the great sinkhole collapsed.

Mournwold.t: The southern band stayed camped on the Chalkdowns, raiding for food, though the Bounders' presence and herb trading reduced the harm. An army here could destroy both Feni bands, including the Alderly Feni before their wards change at the new year.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: the grimnir Kaukana, who claims to speak for the Feni, hails from northern Sermersuaq.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: settlements in Temeschwar were destroyed when the great sinkhole collapsed.

Upwold.t: Mentioned in passing: the sinkhole destroyed settlements in Upwold, and the southern Feni band passed through it on its way to the Mournwold.

Workers in struggle.d: The civil service estimated the new Delver of the Depths title would yield 50 weltsilver, 20 tempest jade and 12 crystal mana each season. The scholar Peter of Hintown offered to explore the sinkhole's tunnels for 5 Thrones if invited. In Serra Briante, orcs stole four wains of mithril, cutting the Great Mine's yield to 18 wains this season, before it went to auction. The militia captured one orc and a herald serving an unnamed Summer eternal. A huge marshwalker, possibly linked to the Druj, attacked the Feverwater dredgers near Black Sails steading. Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar bought the naming rights, and Tobrytan Dunning sent Peter on his expedition.

Druj.t: The marshwalker attack on the Feverwater dredgers was suspected to be Druj work, since they are known to use such creatures and half the Feverwater lies in the Mallum.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are not named; the mithril heist is attributed only to an unidentified gang of orcs.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the orc thieves were thought to have fled into the mountains, possibly reaching Jotun-held Liathaven.

Navarr.t: The Navarr egregore reported a Sentinel Gate conjunction that let up to thirty citizens reach Black Sails steading, where a marshwalker had killed dredgers and threatened the steading.

The Brass Coast.t: The Great Mine of Briante lost four wains of mithril to an orc raid, and the Freeborn egregore offered a Sentinel Gate route for five people to help the Serra Briante militia investigate.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark's Tobrytan Dunning became Delver of the Depths and funded Peter of Hintown and his Winterfolk companions to explore the sinkhole beside New Dunhall.

Workers in struggle.o: In Autumn 381YE, three opportunities arose around Imperial resources: an expedition into the Northern Sinkhole, a mithril heist at the Great Mine of Briante, and a marshwalker attack on the Feverwater dredgers. The sinkhole was named "Lorenzo's Deep Pockets", and the new Delver of the Depths funded the expedition.

Hahnmark/Wood Heath.t: New Dunhall in Wood Heath was where the Delver of the Depths had to send a winged messenger authorising Peter of Hintown's expedition.

Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse.t: Mentioned in passing: the regular patrols from the garrison at Fort Braydon raised the question of how the orcs reached the mine and escaped unseen.

Kahraman/Serra Briante.t: The Great Mine in Serra Briante lost four wains of mithril to an orc heist, and its militia captured one orc and a Summer herald while investigating.

Hahnmark.t: Hahnmark, whose Dunhearth Hall lands were badly hit by the sinkhole, became the base for Peter of Hintown's authorised expedition into the newly named "Lorenzo's Deep Pockets".

Kahraman.t: Orcs raided mithril wagons from the Great Mine of Briante in Kahraman, stealing four wains and reducing the mine's output this season.

Liathaven.t: Mentioned in passing: the orc thieves were believed to have possibly fled into Jotun-held Liathaven.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is not named; the sinkhole is described only as lying in the north-western Empire.

Woven as a weapon.d: Graciana warned that the trods are a centuries-old, refined solution with no easy gains, and their effect cannot be measured with Day magic. She rejected tearing up the Empire's roads as economically ruinous. She proposed instead a wayhouse programme costing 300 wains of white granite, 100 of weirwood and 100 thrones, taking 18 months and two commissions. It would raise trod traffic by a tenth, enrich Navarr businesses and create five ministry wayhouses. A General Assembly mandate invoking the late Empress's call to pilgrimage could roughly double trod walkers for five years, at a cost in armies and taxes. Her third, riskier idea awaits Aquillian, who is forbidden from ritual magic.

Dawn.t: A proposed wayhouse at Rucastle in Semmerholm, beside Brocéliande, would bring Navarr-run ministry traffic into Dawnish land. If the pilgrimage mandate were endorsed, Dawn would lose a tenth of its taxation for five years, and an army if it can support more than two.

Highguard.t: The Highborn grey pilgrimage has already greatly boosted the trods and was the model for the proposed mandate. Highguard would be spared the mandate's losses of taxation and armies because its people already walk the trods.

Imperial Orcs.t: A wayhouse is proposed at Torfast in Skarsind, at the centre of the northern trade network. The Imperial Orcs would also face reduced taxation, and possibly a lost army, if the pilgrimage mandate passed.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: the opening story describes the Jotun as having been driven off the trod, and they hold Liathaven, where the proposals aim to aid Navarr travel and vallorn clearance.

Navarr.t: The appraisal concerns the Navarr's own ancient weapon against the vallorn. The wayhouse programme would enrich Navarr businesses and create five Navarr Imperial positions. A mass pilgrimage could let the Empire clear the vallorn hearts of Hercynia, Liathaven and perhaps Therunin, if enough armies were committed, while sparing Navarr its costs.

The League.t: The League would lose a tenth of its taxation, and an army if it can support more than two, under the proposed pilgrimage mandate. Tassato's La Redotta Rezia is cited as an example of a better-suited appraisal.

The Marches.t: A wayhouse is proposed at Sarcombe in the Mournwold to support trods into Liathaven. The Marches would face reduced taxation, and possibly a lost army, if the pilgrimage mandate were endorsed.

Urizen.t: The Urizen stargazer Aquillian Effugere is the only magician Graciana will trust with her unorthodox plan, but his conviction as a sorcerer may bar him legally. A proposed wayhouse at Peakedge Song could support trods towards Axos, and Urizen would bear the mandate's costs if it passed.

Woven as a weapon.o: The Senate commissioned Graciana i Lopez i Guerra to appraise ways of making the trod network more effective at depleting the vallorn. She identified two costly options, a major wayhouse-building programme and a Synod mandate for a mass pilgrimage, plus an untested idea blocked by Aquillian Effugere's sorcery conviction.

Brocéliande.t: The year-long campaign against the vallorn here inspired Graciana's experimental idea. Navarr businesses connected to Brocéliande would prosper from new wayhouses, with one proposed nearby at Rucastle.

Hercynia.t: Hercynia seconded the motion. The wayhouse programme would bring its businesses an estimated extra 1300 rings each season, and a mass pilgrimage could see its vallorn heart cleared completely.

Liathaven.t: Wayhouses would bring prosperity to Navarr businesses here, and three of the five planned ministry wayhouses would support travel to and from Liathaven. A mass pilgrimage could allow its vallorn heart to be cleared.

Miaren.t: Miaren, the territory already freed by destroying its vallorn heart, would gain less from the wayhouses because the Blood Red Roads already provide some of their benefits.

Mournwold.t: A substantial wayhouse is proposed at Sarcombe to support trods leading into Liathaven.

Semmerholm.t: A substantial wayhouse, operating as a ministry, is proposed at Rucastle, adjacent to Brocéliande.

Skarsind.t: A substantial wayhouse is proposed at Torfast, the centre point of the northern trade network.

Tassato.t: Mentioned in passing: an appraisal on profitably disposing of La Redotta Rezia is given as an example of a more suitable use of appraisal.

Therunin.t: Therunin proposed the appraisal. A ministry wayhouse is suggested at Peakedge Song, and a mass pilgrimage might even allow its vallorn heart to be cleared.

Write the lines.d: The Jotun ruled Sermersuaq harshly but did not lay it waste. The opportunities were: finishing the Smokehouse of Atalaq to support Wintermark's planned fourth, Suaq army (open until Autumn 384YE); completing the Jotun expansion of the Pride of Ikka's Tears and improving its supply route; renaming, remodelling or decommissioning Olgafsdottirshal and the Fortress of Kalant; and two Thule offers from Warlock Askja of Volham, a food-for-ilium trading hall at Wreck and five-year hunting rights, available only at the Winter Solstice. Jarl Ragnar the Dour was leading Ulfur and heralds towards Kalant to wreck the surrounding roads and bridges. Intercepting him fell to the Senator of Sermersuaq.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were cited as a contrast, a people who leave devastation behind and might have collapsed the mine out of spite.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun had collapsed the pass linking southern Sermersuaq to Skarsind.

Jotun.t: The Jotun's unfinished works and fortresses were left for the Empire to complete, rename or abandon, and renaming them was expected to be taken as a calculated insult. Meanwhile Jarl Ragnar of Peråsen led Ulfur and heralds of Cathan Canae towards the Fortress of Kalant.

Thule.t: Weakened by Hayaak's slaughter of their warlocks and short of food since the Dragons freed their slaves, the Thule offered ilium for food caravans through a trading hall at Wreck. They also offered up to 30 rings of ilium for five years of hunting rights in Suaq Fount and East Floes.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark was presented with the means to raise a fourth army rooted in Suaq tradition through the Smokehouse of Atalaq, and could rename the Jotun fortresses by statement of principle. It also had to weigh the Thule's offers of ilium for food and hunting rights.

Write the lines.o: After the Jotun withdrew from Sermersuaq, they left behind fortresses, a half-built smokehouse and an expanded mithril mine, and the Empire was offered several ways to use or remove them. The Thule also offered ilium for food and hunting rights, while a Jotun force advanced on the Fortress of Kalant.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: Wintermark can supply four armies only so long as it holds three territories and the consecrated Kallavesa Marsh.

Sermersuaq/East Floes.t: The Thule proposed a joint trading hall near Wreck in the East Floes to exchange food for ilium. They also sought hunting rights in this more populated region, and were willing to negotiate on it.

Sermersuaq/Sealtoq.t: Mentioned in passing: Sealtoq is not named; it is covered only as part of Sermersuaq generally.

Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks.t: The bloodied Thule armies retreated to the Silver Peaks. This is where the proposed food caravans would go and where the offered ilium would come from.

Sermersuaq/Stark.t: Stark holds the Jotun-built Fortress of Kalant. Jarl Ragnar's force was advancing on it to destroy the surrounding roads and bridges, which would confine the garrison to defending Stark alone.

Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount.t: Suaq Fount's Pride of Ikka's Tears could gain 5 wains of mithril a season for 200 thrones, and 2 more through an improved route to Atalaq. The Thule also offered 15 rings of ilium to hunt in the region.

Sermersuaq/Tanikipari.t: Tanikipari holds Olgafsdottirshal, the Jotun fortress some wished to rename or strip of Jotun symbols, while others wanted it kept, or decommissioned to save upkeep.

Hahnmark.t: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark was named as the soul of the Steinr tradition, as a comparison for Sermersuaq's place in Suaq identity.

Kallavesa.t: Kallavesa's swamps were consecrated to Pride with true liao by Rane Sherarding, and this is what allows Wintermark to support a fourth army. The territory was also described as the spiritual heart of the Kallavesi.

Otkodov.t: Otkodov's hunters, fishers and farmers struggled to feed newly freed people, which prompted the Thule offers of ilium for food. Any hunting-rights payment would be handed to the Ambassador to Otkodov.

Sermersuaq.t: Freshly reclaimed Sermersuaq faced a series of choices: completing the Jotun smokehouses and mine works, keeping, remodelling or abandoning two captured fortresses, and accepting or rejecting Thule trade and hunting proposals. A Jotun raid also threatened Kalant's roads and bridges.

Skallahn.t: Mentioned in passing: Skallahn is not named on the page and is connected only through the Jotun generally.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun collapsed the pass connecting southern Sermersuaq to Skarsind.

Tromsa.t: Mentioned in passing: Igya Olgafsdottir, architect of Olgafsdottirshal and Kalant, was named as the eldest child of the Jarl of Tromsa.

Write your own ending.d: The Seventh Wave hunted down tortured souls, Winter spirits and Druj guerrillas, so Zenith escaped lasting terror and its borders were secured. Miasma pillars still stood in Proceris, Iteri, Clypion and Lustri, denying all taxes until cleared by Senate motion or heroic stand. Sage Apollion of Tsark offered half the white granite for a Lustri fortification if the Empire swore never to enter Tsark. Prosperity priests found options to rebuild the Golden Cascade and three lost sinecures. An Autumn enchantment favoured those who moved resources to Zenith. The Senate's appraisal, led by Naomi of Virtue's Rest, proposed three follies offering Zenith a new arete. Three conjunctions dealt with tortured souls and miasma pillars.

Druj.t: Their armies were forced out of Lustri into the Sarangrave, where they were expected to resupply quickly, but their miasma pillars, tortured souls, cephalopods and lingering bands remained to torment Zenith.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's earlier warning to Tsark of an imminent Grendel attack was what persuaded Tsark to make its fortification offer.

Highguard.t: The Highborn Seventh Wave, urged on by the national assembly, rooted out the Druj legacy in Zenith. Highborn were invited to help lay tormented souls to rest at the Ring of Solace, and the proposed Radix of Truth would pay 200 herbs to Highguard's congregations for their stained glass.

The League.t: The proposed Crucible of Fate depends on finely made brass cogs from League workshops, and would bring a one-off payment of 140 ingots to League businesses if completed.

Urizen.t: Urizen regained Zenith but faced ruined spires, lost ushabti, reluctant refugees and miasma. Its assembly could endorse a new arete for the territory once one of Naomi's follies was built, and rebuilding the Golden Cascade would secure the Citadel Guard's supply.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is not named on this page, which concerns Zenith's restoration.

Write your own ending.o: After the Empire drove the Druj out of Zenith and the territory was returned to Urizen, Imperial efforts turned to restoring a land left ruined, stifled by miasma and bereft of hope. The page set out the territory's condition and a range of opportunities to rebuild it.

Morrow/Peregro.t: Mentioned in passing: the Halls of Knowledge, moved from Zenith to Peregro, were destroyed there by the Druj.

Zenith/Clypion.t: One of the four regions where Druj miasma pillars still stood, preventing any tax revenue from Zenith until they were cleared.

Zenith/Iteri.t: Miasma pillars still stood in Iteri, where the tortured souls Tibera and Gaiu were active. The region would host three of the proposed Eye of the Heavens observatories, or the Crucible of Fate at Spire Calator.

Zenith/Lustri.t: The Druj were driven from Lustri, but linked miasma pillars guarded by the tortured soul Aureli Major remained. Mount Kerion was identified as the site for the proposed Citadel of the Moon.

Zenith/Occursion.t: Its miasma pillar was destroyed at the Autumn Equinox, but Druj cephalopods were infesting its lakes. The region could host restored sinecures, two observatories and the Radix of Truth, and Tormented Souls had settled in the Ring of Solace's Day regio.

Zenith/Proceris.t: Proceris still had a miasma pillar, its waterways were infested by Druj cephalopods, and it had been flooded when the Golden Cascade was destroyed. The ruined Storm Vault there could be rebuilt alongside tempest jade workings.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: the Wunderkind of Holberg are named as excelling at the precision brass work the Crucible of Fate would need.

Morrow.t: Many Zenith refugees had settled in Morrow, its senator seconded the appraisal, and surviving illuminates were founding a new spire in its south-eastern mountains. A rebuilt Golden Cascade would ease food pressures there, while losing any region of Morrow without it would see the Citadel Guard decline.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not discussed directly on this page.

Redoubt.t: Zenith refugees had put down roots in Redoubt and were reluctant to return. A rebuilt Golden Cascade would ease food pressures there, while losing any region of Redoubt without it would see the Citadel Guard decline.

Sarangrave.t: The Druj armies driven out of Lustri fled into the Sarangrave to resupply, and the proposed Citadel of the Moon would guard Zenith's border against their return.

Sarvos.t: Mentioned in passing: Naomi's plan to give Zenith a new purpose was modelled on the approach used in Sarvos after the Hag Queen's curse.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: a rebuilt Golden Cascade would let Urizen supply the Citadel Guard even if it lost all access to Spiral.

Zenith.t: Liberated but devastated, Zenith remained stifled by miasma and bereft of hope. Opportunities were offered to clear the pillars, fortify Lustri, rebuild the Golden Cascade and lost sinecures, and commission a folly to define its new arete.

Written in salt.d: Axos freed its orc slaves under the Liberty Pact, but they have none of the rights of human citizens. They are forced into menial work and watched with suspicion, and diplomacy has only bred Axou resentment. The Imperial Orcs have few fleets, so a General Assembly or Assembly of the Nine mandate was proposed, sending a priest with 50 doses of liao to urge captains to offer passage. Captains doing so would earn reduced profits. Enough fleet strength could bring most or all of Axos's several thousand orcs to the Empire. This risked a diplomatic incident with the Axou. The Commonwealth meanwhile planned to rescue the orcs itself by the Spring Equinox. After the Winter Solstice, Skywise Gralka enacted the mandate.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of Axos are watched by the Axou for any sign of sympathy with the Druj.

Grendel.t: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of Axos are watched by the Axou for any sign of sympathy with the Grendel.

Imperial Orcs.t: The nation's reavers answered Skywise Gralka's statement but lacked the fleets to rescue the Axou orcs alone, so Gralka sought and later enacted a wider Synod mandate. Rescued orcs, who are city-dwellers with some magical knowledge, could offer an opportunity for the nation.

Written in salt.o: Imperial Orc reavers answering Skywise Gralka's call found the freed orcs of Axos living in dreadful conditions, but the nation lacked the ships to help them. The page proposed a Synod mandate urging Imperial fleet captains to carry them to the Empire before the Commonwealth did so itself, and Gralka later enacted that mandate after the Winter Solstice.

Skarsind.t: Imperial Orc reavers offered to escort rescued Axou orcs to Skarsind. If at least 10,000 fleet strength were committed, they would become a significant force there, comparable in impact to the Ossean septs.

Years of an inch and a step.d: Kerem's Summer Solstice mandate prompted many young Highborn to sell farms and businesses and take to the trods. At the Autumn Equinox every national assembly urged its citizens to feed, shelter and protect the pilgrims. As a result, every nation's farms and businesses lose 36 rings and its military units one rank for a season, while Highguard's losses stay at 72 rings and two ranks. All these penalties end by the Spring Equinox. The Highborn upheld three non-competing mandates: Shadrach's against false virtues and eternal worshippers, Yarona's casting pilgrims as guides to all human nations, and Dinah's, passed by the greatest majority, urging proselytising to foreigners.

Highguard.t: Highborn farms and businesses keep losing 72 rings and their military units two ranks for one more season before recovering, while the Assembly gave its grey pilgrims a missionary and inquisitorial mission, including a congregation penalty that reaches Highguard itself.

Imperial Orcs.t: The Imperial Orcs share the cost of supporting the pilgrims for a season, and Chainbreaker Snark proposed an alternative mandate for the Highborn Assembly urging pilgrims to convert travelling foreigners.

Navarr.t: The grey pilgrims take up part of the burden the Navarr have long carried against the vallorn, though Navarr also pays the season's support penalty and its congregations face the pilgrims' challenge under Yarona's mandate.

Urizen.t: Urizeni citizens reached out to aid the pilgrims and bear a season of reduced income and military strength, and as a human nation their congregations are subject to the one-rank penalty from Yarona's mandate.

Varushka.t: Varushka shares the season-long cost of supporting the pilgrimage, and as a human nation its congregations face a one-rank penalty while grey pilgrims question unorthodox beliefs there.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark bears the season's penalty to farms, businesses and military units for supporting the pilgrims, and its congregations are among those of all human nations hit by Yarona's mandate.

Years of an inch and a step.o: In Winter 382YE the costs of the Highborn pilgrimage to walk the trods against the vallorn, shared across the Empire after every national assembly urged support for the grey pilgrims, were set to ease within a season. The Highborn Assembly then passed three mandates defining the pilgrims' religious mission.

Bay of Catazar.t: Mentioned in passing: Suranni traders sailing the Bay of Catazar are cited as people the grey pilgrims should tell they worship false gods.

You belong with me.d: After years travelling the trods with stridings, many younger Great Forest Orcs no longer wished to return to the Barrens. Corey Wayfarer proposed a mandate that would see the Great Forest Steading founded in Miaren and the High Pines Steading in Hercynia. The orcs would pay for these themselves and could be hired to boost weirwood from the Golden Trees of Seren and the Heartwood of the Great Vale. Morwenna Winterbuilt proposed a sworn oath of welcome across all Navarr territories, invoking powerful hearth magic. Cautious guides offered a mandate ending the move towards integration. With no mandate, no steadings would be founded, though the orcs might make other requests later.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs once lived under Druj dominion, and news of the Druj defeat in Zenith was met with jubilation among them.

Imperial Orcs.t: Mentioned in passing: the would-be settlers hoped to learn more about the 'orcs of the Skarsind sept', and the out-of-character note says the Imperial Orc egregore cannot bond humans.

Navarr.t: The Navarr Assembly had to decide whether to welcome Great Forest Orc settlements beyond Therunin, a choice guides warned could lead to orcs asking to join the nation itself. An oath-sworn welcome would carry supernatural consequences if broken.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: news of the Druj defeat in Zenith was celebrated by the Great Forest Orcs.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: the out-of-character note cites the mora of Varushka as an example of a non-playable people.

Wintermark.t: Mentioned in passing: the out-of-character note cites the hylje and states the Great Forest Orcs could never join a nation so culturally unlike them as Wintermark.

You belong with me.o: Young Great Forest Orcs sheltering in Therunin asked the Navarr Assembly to endorse permanent settlements in Hercynia and Miaren, a step likely to lead to requests to join the Navarr nation. The Synod was offered a welcoming mandate, a stronger sworn welcome, or a cautionary mandate urging the orcs to move on.

Hercynia/Summersend.t: The proposed High Pines Steading would be built in Summersend, where orc woodworkers could be hired to increase weirwood from the Heartwood of the Great Vale.

Miaren/Serenael.t: The proposed Great Forest Steading would be built in Serenael, where hired orc expertise could boost weirwood from the Golden Trees of Seren.

The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht.t: The Senate had reassured the Great Forest Orcs of its intention to concede the Heart of Peytaht to them once the Barrens were secured, though such reassurances bind no future Senate.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Some mystically inclined Great Forest Orcs had taken up permanent residence at Peakedge Stead, studying medicinal techniques with the Navarr and Highborn.

Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley.t: The orcs living in the Upper Tarn Valley had grown familiar with the Highborn of Peakedge Song and Elerael, the example the would-be settlers hoped to follow elsewhere.

Hercynia.t: Young Great Forest Orcs sought Navarr endorsement to found the permanent High Pines Steading in Hercynia, near the Heartwood of the Great Vale.

Miaren.t: A second group of young orcs sought to found the permanent Great Forest Steading in Miaren, near the Golden Trees of Seren.

Skarsind.t: Mentioned in passing: the would-be settlers hoped to learn more about the 'orcs of the Skarsind sept'.

The Barrens.t: The Barrens remained the homeland most older Great Forest Orcs longed to return to, though many younger orcs now had little wish to go back there.

Therunin.t: Therunin remained the Great Forest Orcs' home-in-exile, where close bonds with their human neighbours had led some younger orcs to want to stay in the Empire permanently.

Zenith.t: Mentioned in passing: the Druj defeat in Zenith was greeted with widespread jubilation among the Great Forest Orcs.

You can't count on me.d: The Imperial Crown remained interdicted because its reconciliation was declared in an 'emergency session' with no legal standing. The Prefect would propose a Declaration of License, and if it failed the magistrates would seize and destroy the Crown. A Summer boon linked to Barien inspired crafting across the Mournwold and promised a trade boon. The Civil Service named Hammare 'Meathammer' Stenning Custodian of the Lost, and Harad of the High Path's Quiet Hall in Oakways was offered for Endowment. Tharim warded the Hall of Worlds while his image is displayed. Barien's heralds, Surut's agent and Zakalwe's strategy game awaited citizens. Dawn's Eastern Sky moved towards becoming a favoured army.

Dawn.t: Five Summer eternals stood ready to patronise the Eastern Sky under Dame Aurum de Castellan, and Cathan Canae offered her favour if a Synod mandate barred Dawnish generals from giving ground in defence. Barien's heralds would hold court at House du Lac, and Zakalwe invited six Dawnish strategists to a game.

Druj.t: A Penumbral Veil still hung over the Druj-held Barrens, and the Dripping Echoes of the Fen were raised in Ossium in case the Druj tried to reclaim the land.

Highguard.t: A new shroud was raised over the Highborn territory of Necropolis, frustrating any scrying into it.

Navarr.t: The late Navarr magician Harad of the High Path left his Quiet Hall in Oakways as a bequest. The Conclave could endow it to the Custodian of the Lost as a hospital, or to his niece Mathoni High Path in exchange for 5 measures of dragonbone each season.

The Brass Coast.t: New shrouds were raised over the Freeborn territories of Madruga and Segura. Barien's heralds also held a challenge scroll for Tono Shartha Riqueza.

The League.t: A Penumbral Veil continued to hang over the League territory of Sarvos.

The Marches.t: A Summer enchantment over the Mournwold inspired Marchers in crafting, cooking and brewing and promised a season of thriving trade. A Spring wall rose in Alderly, and Marchers were called to bring rough music against the stubborn ghosts of Greensward.

Thule.t: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Crown was recovered from the Thule by private collectors.

Urizen.t: The Custodian of the Lost carried on the legacy of Zenith's destroyed Spire of Twisting Shadows, and the Spire of the Seventh Mist pressed on with its campaign for access to the Brilliant Star mine. Zenith gained nightwoven fortifications and a Spring wall in Lustri while remaining veiled.

Varushka.t: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen rose in Drownbark Forest in Ossium to shield the Iron Helms against any Druj attempt to retake the land.

Wintermark.t: Fog fortifications were raised over Kallavesa Marsh and West Marsh. The Civil Service ruled that the Wintermark coven the Saque Magique could not hold the Custodian title and named Hammare 'Meathammer' Stenning instead.

You can't count on me.o: In Spring 385YE a round-up of magical incidents and opportunities was reported across the Empire. Highlights included a Summer enchantment over the Mournwold, the discovery that the Imperial Crown was still legally interdicted, and new magical fortifications and shrouds.

Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh.t: Magical fog fortifications were raised over Kallavesa Marsh.

Kallavesa/West Marsh.t: Magical fog fortifications were raised over West Marsh.

Miaren/Oakways.t: Harad's Quiet Hall, a wayhouse in idyllic woodland rich in dragonbone, awaited the Conclave's decision on whether it would become a hospital or pass to his niece's family.

Mournwold/Alderly.t: A great wall of branch and thicket was summoned from the Spring realm in Alderly.

Mournwold/Greensward.t: Greensward remained haunted, with stubborn ghosts gathered at Overton Ruins. Mary Overton called for Marchers to confront them with rough music through a Sentinel Gate conjunction.

Ossium/Drownbark Forest.t: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen rose in Drownbark Forest to shield the Iron Helms against the Druj.

Zenith/Lustri.t: A great wall of branch and thicket was summoned from the Spring realm in Lustri.

Kallavesa.t: Magical fog fortifications lay heavy over Kallavesa Marsh and West Marsh.

Madruga.t: A new shroud was raised over Madruga, blocking divination into the territory unless it is pierced.

Miaren.t: Harad's Quiet Hall in Oakways became a bequest the Conclave could endow, either as a hospital for magical maladies or to Mathoni High Path for its dragonbone.

Mournwold.t: A Summer enchantment linked to Barien filled the Mournwold with inspired craft, food and drink, promising a three-month boom in trade. The territory also gained magical fortifications, while ghosts lingered in Greensward.

Necropolis.t: A new shroud was raised over Necropolis, hindering any scrying into the territory.

Ossium.t: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen were raised in Drownbark Forest to protect the Iron Helms.

Sarvos.t: A Penumbral Veil continued to hang over Sarvos.

Segura.t: A new shroud was raised over Segura, blocking divination into the territory.

Semmerholm.t: Mentioned in passing: a statue honouring Eleonaris at the Golden Causeway in Semmerholm secured her favour for the Eastern Sky.

The Barrens.t: A Penumbral Veil still hung over the Barrens, frustrating Imperial scrying.

Zenith.t: Nightwoven fortifications strengthened Zenith's mists and a Spring wall rose in Lustri, while a veil remained over the territory. The legacy of its destroyed Spire of Twisting Shadows was clarified.

You could be happy.d: Herminius of the House of the Wanderer (General Assembly) and Tuuli (Wisdom Assembly) passed judgements calling citizens to act against the Druj threat to the eastern territories. Any national assembly bordering the Druj could enact a mandate encouraging citizens to walk the border. This raises the victory points the Druj need to claim a beachhead to 25, at a cost of five thrones in taxation from each protected territory. All four eligible assemblies enacted it. Separately, Amris Johan Merikovich's judgement urged the Iron Helms to abandon cruelty for dark magics and curses. The resulting mandate was discussed, but Anastasiya Lukashovna Volkov had the Eyes of Loyalty turned on it.

Dawn.t: The Dawnish Assembly enacted the border mandate, so Dawnish citizens patrol the Barrens against Druj incursion at a cost of five thrones in taxation.

Druj.t: Citizen patrols along the borders of Dawn, Navarr, Urizen and Varushka mean the Druj now need 25 victory points to claim a beachhead in those territories. The patrols do not harm their armies or affect regions they claim after a beachhead.

Highguard.t: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is listed among the territories the Druj have claimed over the last ten years.

Navarr.t: The Navarr Assembly enacted the border mandate, which protects Therunin once it is reclaimed and if it is assigned to Navarr, at a cost of five thrones in taxation.

The League.t: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is listed among the territories the Druj have claimed over the last ten years.

Thule.t: Varushka's border mandate does not extend to the Thule-held region of Webwood in Ossium, which remains without the citizen patrols.

Urizen.t: The Urizen Assembly enacted the border mandate, setting citizens to patrol both Morrow and Zenith at a combined cost of ten thrones in taxation.

Varushka.t: The Varushkan Assembly enacted the border mandate protecting Ossium. It also considered a mandate to turn the Iron Helms from cruelty to dark magics and curses, but the Eyes of Loyalty were turned on that mandate.

You could be happy.o: Following greater-majority Synod judgements urging vigilance against the Druj, the Dawnish, Navarr, Urizen and Varushkan Assemblies all enacted mandates sending citizens to patrol their borders with the Mallum. The Varushkan Assembly also had the chance to push the Iron Helms away from cruelty towards dark magic and curses, but the Eyes of Loyalty were turned on that mandate.

Ossium/Webwood.t: Because Webwood is held by Thule, the Varushkan border mandate does not extend to it, so it gains no protection from the citizen patrols.

Holberg.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the territories the Druj have laid claim to over the past decade.

Morrow.t: Urizeni citizens now patrol Morrow's border with the Druj, making a beachhead harder to claim, though the territory's taxation falls by five thrones.

Ossium.t: Still scarred by Druj devastation, Ossium is now patrolled by Varushkan citizens under their assembly's mandate. The Thule-held Webwood is not covered.

Reikos.t: Mentioned in passing: listed among the territories the Druj have laid claim to over the past decade.

The Barrens.t: Dawnish citizens now patrol the Barrens, where the Druj remain active, at a cost of five thrones in taxation. The territory was also where the Iron Helms executed the leaders of the Black Wind.

Therunin.t: With the Druj still active in Therunin, Navarr's mandate will see citizens patrol its border once it is reclaimed, if it is assigned to Navarr.

Zenith.t: Under the Urizen mandate, citizens patrol Zenith's border with the Druj, making a beachhead harder to claim, at a cost of five thrones in taxation.

You do it to yourself.d: Fintan Nighthaven's mandate (1594 to 367) rejected the false virtues behind "Death to the Druj", while Lenarius Ankarien's call to exterminate the Druj by any means narrowly failed (739 to 793). The Urizen and Vigilance Assemblies passed statements urging that the Druj legacy be scoured from Zenith. With Ossium liberated, the Barrens poised to fall and the Spires of Dusk taken, Lady Laudine of House duLac's wording would make the Druj war the priority for a year, whatever the sacrifice. Mael Donjeon's competing wording would refuse that priority and leave the Military Council and Senate free to agree terms with the Druj. Only one can be enacted. New answers would first need a statement of principle.

Druj.t: The Druj are described as uniquely cruel and now on the run. The Synod must choose whether the Empire pursues all-out victory over them or treats them as just one enemy, potentially open to negotiated terms.

Grendel.t: Under the Laudine mandate, talks with the Grendel could involve sacrifices for the sake of the Druj war. Under the Donjeon mandate, their navy and allies are cited as a greater threat, and Feroz and Spiral are noted as languishing under Grendel rule.

Jotun.t: The Wintermark campaign against the Jotun is described as honourable. Prioritising the Druj could mean sacrifices in that war, while the opposing view points out that the Jotun field more armies than the Mallum.

Navarr.t: Mentioned in passing: only against the Navarr does the Jotun war turn to savagery, with neither side able to tolerate the other's existence.

The Marches.t: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are said to honour the Marchers in their own way, and Jarl Kierheim's vow concerning the Jotun failure in the Mournwold is quoted.

Thule.t: The Thule are said to keep their word, and the costly peace with them has held. Under the Laudine mandate, talks with them could also involve sacrifices to focus on the Druj.

Urizen.t: The Urizen Assembly passed a statement urging Sword Scholars to scour the remnants of the Druj from Zenith. The opening story follows the Urizen sentinel Belisar and the scout Philamon, a veteran of Morrow and Zenith.

Varushka.t: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is cited as the first territory liberated from the Druj and now a thriving territory of Varushka.

Wintermark.t: The Wintermarkers are credited with leading an honourable campaign against the Jotun. Sermersuaq is cited as nearly lost for a generation, regained only through the Thule alliance.

You do it to yourself.o: Following the Winter Solstice 385YE Synod's decisive rebuke of the cry "Death to the Druj", the Empire faced the open question of what to do about the Druj. The civil service set out two competing General Assembly mandates: commit utterly to victory over the Druj, or treat them as only one threat among many.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as languishing under Grendel rule, part of the price of the Empire's focus on the Druj.

Morrow.t: Mentioned in passing: the scout Philamon is said to have fought in Morrow.

Mournwold.t: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Kierheim vows the Jotun will not make peace until all shamed by their failure in the Mournwold have passed on.

Ossium.t: Mentioned in passing: noted as the first territory liberated from the Druj and now a thriving part of Varushka.

Otkodov.t: Mentioned in passing: the northern lands under the Dragons of Otkodov are described as the price paid for the Thule alliance.

Sarangrave.t: Imperial spies have scouted the Sarangrave for its secrets and weaknesses, and raising a rebellion there is judged difficult but not impossible.

Sermersuaq.t: Mentioned in passing: cited as nearly lost for a generation and returned to Imperial rule only through the alliance with the Thule.

Spiral.t: Mentioned in passing: cited alongside Feroz as languishing under Grendel rule.

The Barrens.t: The Druj armies have been mauled and defeated here, and the territory looks set to fall to the Empire soon.

Zenith.t: The Druj have fled Zenith but left deep scars. The Urizen and Vigilance Assemblies passed statements urging citizens to root out the Druj legacy and stay watchful, though no military threat currently faces the territory.

You know the night.d: The Iron Helms, raised in Spring 381YE and famed for cruelty, were unleashed in the Mournwold with effective but disturbing results. Wintermark and the Freeborn had already passed mandates urging their soldiers to shun the Helms. Dawn, Highguard, Navarr and Urizen sided with Varushka. After Gralka's judgement, upheld 36 to 0, the Imperial Orc assembly could shun the Helms or permanently change the Summer Storm from relentless to heroic. It unanimously refused the Summer Storm change. The Varushkan assembly sent Bogdan Bogdanovich with a mandate urging all its soldiers to embrace their heritage. All Varushkan armies thereby stood with the Iron Helms, sharing their penalties when fighting alongside Wintermark and the Brass Coast, and each general gained one chance to update their army's quality.

Dawn.t: Dawn was counted among the nations standing with the Iron Helms and Varushka in the dispute over their cruel tactics.

Druj.t: Mentioned in passing: Empress Varkula's remark that high-minded ideals last only until the Druj are about to burn your house down is cited by Varushkans.

Highguard.t: Highguard was named among the nations that chose to stand with Varushka and the Iron Helms.

Imperial Orcs.t: Gralka's judgement condemning the Iron Helms' cruelty passed 36 to 0, opening mandates to shun the Helms and to make the Summer Storm heroic. The assembly unanimously refused to change the Summer Storm's quality.

Jotun.t: Mentioned in passing: Varushkans dismissed the Marches and Wintermark as nations bordering the Jotun that have never faced an enemy really trying.

Navarr.t: The Navarr sided with Varushka and were inspired to pass a mandate adopting similar tactics to the Iron Helms.

The Marches.t: The Marches were among the first nations to oppose the Iron Helms' tactics, drawing Varushkan scorn as high-minded farmers and hunters.

Urizen.t: Urizen narrowly backed Varushka, reportedly thanks to Zeno, and was inspired to pass a mandate adopting similar tactics.

Varushka.t: Varushka's assembly sent Bogdan Bogdanovich to urge all its soldiers to embrace their heritage, so every Varushkan army now stands with the Iron Helms and shares their penalties alongside Wintermark and the Brass Coast. Each general also gained a single chance to update their army's quality.

Wintermark.t: Wintermark had already enacted a mandate shunning the Iron Helms, and after Varushka's mandate all Varushkan armies now suffer penalties when fighting alongside Wintermark armies.

You know the night.o: Divisions over the brutal tactics of the Varushkan Iron Helms deepened in Winter 381YE, splitting the Empire's nations into rival camps and offering the Imperial Orc and Varushkan assemblies mandates to take sides. The Imperial Orcs declined to remake the Summer Storm, while Varushka chose to have all its soldiers embrace their heritage.

Mournwold.t: The Iron Helms were first unleashed in the Mournwold, where their cruel methods proved as effective as they were hard for many to stomach.

You'll recognise yourself.d: Supporters argued the Senate lacked ambition and time, and proposed a Master of Commissions title for la Volpe, subject to the Imperatrix's veto. Detractors, many from Highguard, called his works gauche and also condemned an Asavean architect's blasphemous works. They proposed a constitutional motion moving commissions to the Synod, an idea the constitutional court deemed constitutional in principle. Projects seeking his money were a dam in Madruga, cold-store caverns in Volodmartz, a pig farm at Graven, a taller Colossus near Tassato, a Therunin smithy and Holberg sausage distribution. Projects rejecting him were pilgrim hostels for Bastion, a Laroc arena (later superseded) and the Bleak Tower arboretum in Morrow. The opportunities remained open until the end of the Summer Solstice.

Dawn.t: Lady Larille de Rochemont proposed a magnificent new tournament arena at Laroc, appealing to two noble houses for support. It would aid Astolat's troubadours and let Dawn raise armies there faster, though this opportunity was later superseded.

Druj.t: The Druj invasion of Zenith had destroyed the Gardens of Pallas, scattering Urizeni herbalists as refugees into Morrow. Their past siege of Holberg was also recalled.

Highguard.t: Much of the opposition to la Volpe and the Asavean architect came from Highguard. Philemon of Fulmon's Bounty proposed pilgrim hostels for Bastion and refused any of la Volpe's money.

Navarr.t: The broker Cyfarth proposed a great cleaver-walled smithy in Peakedge Song to enrich Therunin's mines. Supporters of la Volpe derided the Navarr Dredgemaster of Feverwater as an indulgent sinecure.

The Brass Coast.t: The Galia family of Madruga sought la Volpe's backing for a great irrigation dam bearing the Butchers' symbols, which would yield a water-contract sinecure.

The League.t: La Volpe's growing fame was centred on the League, where Tassato residents proposed a taller rival Colossus and Holberg's Virtuous Company sought to spread Holberg sausage across the Empire under the Butchers' brand.

The Marches.t: The alders of Graven proposed a vast Blood Red Pig Farm to improve their bargaining position with local yeofolk, offering la Volpe an honorary citizenship if he funded it.

Urizen.t: Cyrus of the White Stair proposed restoring Morrow's Bleak Tower as an arboretum for refugee herbalists from Zenith. He sought Achilles of Damakan's Forge as benefactor rather than la Volpe.

Varushka.t: Boyar Petra of the Vale of Stars proposed fortifying the cold Star Caverns in Volodmartz as a food and herb store, extending his vale's protection over them.

You'll recognise yourself.o: As the fame of Lorenzo 'la Volpe' Macelliao von Temeschwar and his cleaver-adorned works spread, his supporters proposed making him a sole Master of Commissions while detractors urged the Senate to hand the power of commission to the Imperial Synod. A slate of possible commissions emerged, some courting his patronage and others pointedly refusing it.

Bregasland/Gravenmarch.t: The town of Graven proposed building the Blood Red Pig Farm on its northern edge to feed the town and supply its miners.

Madruga/Lightsea.t: The proposed Galia dam would lie thirty miles upriver from the coast at Lightsea, securing water for the family's farms.

Therunin/Peakedge Song.t: Cyfarth's proposed great smithy would stand on Peakedge Song's stable, mine-rich ground. Its walls could be carved as cleavers in la Volpe's honour.

Zenith/Iteri.t: The Druj had flooded the Gardens of Pallas in central Iteri, smashed their ushabti and burned their caretaker spires.

Astolat.t: A grand new arena at Laroc was proposed, which would bring liao and votes to Astolat's congregations and quicken the raising of Dawnish armies there. This opportunity was later superseded.

Bastion.t: Pilgrim hostels along the hoped-for Blood Red Roads were proposed, which would bring liao and Synod votes to Bastion's congregations. They would yield only half their benefit unless the roads reached the city.

Bregasland.t: Graven, Bregasland's largest town, proposed a huge pig farm and abattoir. It would supply the town and its miners and give its overseer access to weltsilver and green iron.

Feroz.t: Mentioned in passing: the Galia farms' grain and salted pork were unloaded weekly in Siroc.

Holberg.t: The Virtuous Company of Provisioners proposed expanding distribution of Holberg rations, bringing a bounty to every farm in Holberg. Rival food sellers accused them of seeking a monopoly.

Madruga.t: The Galia family proposed a great dam creating an artificial lake to irrigate their dry farms upriver from Lightsea.

Morrow.t: The ruined Bleak Tower, with its winter regio, was proposed for restoration as an arboretum. It would boost Morrow's herb gardens and give a custodian rare Heart's Blood each season.

Sarvos.t: Sarvos's Colossus was mocked by detractors. A rival statue near Tassato would cost the city some of the income its Colossus generated.

Segura.t: Mentioned in passing: la Volpe had once announced plans to extend the Blood Red Roads as far as Anduz in Segura.

Tassato.t: Residents proposed a larger, partly hollow Colossus of la Volpe on the Red Rock overlooking the Sapphire Stair. It would bring extra income to Tassato's businesses.

Temeschwar.t: Mentioned in passing: la Volpe is the Merchant Prince of Temeschwar, whose fame drove these proposals.

Therunin.t: A great smithy was proposed in Peakedge Song that would generate a bounty spread among all Therunin's mines.

Volodmartz.t: A plan to deepen and fortify the legendary Star Caverns in Marupa was proposed. The caverns would store food and herbs, and their overseer could buy bladeroot.

Zenith.t: Following the Druj conquest of Zenith, the Gardens of Pallas were destroyed and their herbalists fled as refugees to Morrow.

Your hand in mine.d: The Conscience of the Senate's motion sent Naomi to the rebels of Nesustak Forest. Three approaches, one to each sept, were driven off at bow-point, so she ruled out any commission, motion or judgement for now. Instead she found a conjunction at 14:00 on Sunday leading five citizens to the rebels' armed camp near the Bloodwater Marsh. She offered seven pieces of guidance, urged the envoys to go unarmed and aim only for further talks, and recommended Ser Guy of the Twisted Rose, Fausta Ankarien and Aspar. She advised against the Throne going. The Senate must choose the envoys. Unless something is done, the vallorn will destroy the rebels within three months.

Druj.t: The rebels threw off Druj rule and fear the Druj above all, while the vallorn the Druj unleashed in Sarangrave threatens to wipe them out. A failed meeting would hand the Druj more propaganda against the Empire among the septs still in Ulnak and Sanath.

Urizen.t: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named on the page; its only connection is its share in holding Sarangrave, the territory the rebels claim.

Your hand in mine.o: Naomi of Virtue's Rest, sent by Senate motion to appraise solutions to the Nesustak Forest rebels, failed to open talks but identified a single Sentinel Gate conjunction allowing five Imperial envoys to meet the rebels in Sarangrave.

Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh.t: The Sentinel Gate conjunction opens on the edge of the Bloodwater Marsh, close to the rebels' main camp. The Bloodwater Spears, one of the two leading rebel septs, are among those the envoys must understand.

Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest.t: The Nesustak rebels drove off Naomi's envoys but were saved from the Druj by the Gryphon's Pride. If nothing is done, the vallorn will obliterate them within three months.

Sarangrave.t: The rebel septs want Sarangrave for themselves and refuse to talk to the Empire. The one chance at diplomacy is a single meeting at their camp, while the Druj-unleashed vallorn closes in on them.
